stories.title: Lebanon confirms six killed in Israeli strikes despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry confirmed that Israeli air strikes killed six people and injured two others in southern Lebanon on April 24, despite an ongoing ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: China slaps export curbs on European firms over Taiwan arms sales
stories.summary: China imposed export restrictions on dual-use items targeting seven European entities, citing their involvement in arms sales to Taiwan. The curbs also prohibit foreign organizations and individuals from transferring China-originated dual-use goods to the named firms.

stories.title: Leaders of Colombia, Venezuela expected to discuss security at Caracas meeting
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro traveled to Caracas on Friday to meet Venezuelan counterpart Delcy Rodriguez. The two leaders, both under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, were expected to discuss bilateral security issues.

stories.title: Minister seeks details on reports of hijacking of tanker with Pakistani crew near Somali coast
stories.summary: Pakistan's Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry requested a detailed report on the reported hijacking of an oil tanker by pirates near the Somali coast. The vessel's crew reportedly includes 11 Pakistani nationals. The ministry said it is coordinating with the Foreign Office and Somali authorities.

stories.title: U.S. soldier charged with using classified intel to win $400K Polymarket bet on Maduro raid
stories.summary: U.S. Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke was charged with using classified intelligence to place approximately $400,000 in bets on the prediction market Polymarket regarding a raid on Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. Most bets were allegedly placed hours before missiles struck Caracas.

stories.title: Citizen taken into custody for likening Tarnol Railway Crossing to Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Police in Islamabad arrested a citizen for allegedly mocking the Tarnol Railway crossing by comparing it to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Middle East conflict. An FIR was registered under multiple sections including disobedience to a public servant's order.

stories.title: US justice department steps in on behalf of xAI in Colorado regulation case
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has intervened in a lawsuit filed by Elon Musk's xAI against a Colorado law regulating artificial intelligence systems. The department argued the state law violates the 14th Amendment's equal protection guarantee, setting up a conflict between state regulation and the Trump administration's push for a federal AI framework.

stories.title: Indigenous speakers booed at Anzac Day services as Ben Roberts-Smith attends Gold Coast event
stories.summary: Anzac Day commemorations in Melbourne and Sydney were disrupted by booing during Indigenous acknowledgement of country segments. One man was arrested at the Sydney dawn service at Martin Place. Separately, Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith, who faces five war crime murder charges he denies, attended the dawn service at Currumbin Beach on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: Israel reportedly agreed to, but did not implement US request to curb Gaza strikes
stories.summary: Hamas-run authorities reported that 13 people were killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza. Israel reportedly agreed to a US request to curb strikes in Gaza but did not implement the commitment. Tehran said no direct meeting with US officials was planned during the Islamabad talks.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed at least three people in Gaza on Friday, according to Palestinian health officials. The strike was reported from Cairo, with medics confirming the casualties.

stories.title: The Kashmir town trying to win back tourists after a deadly attack
stories.summary: One year after a deadly attack in Pahalgam, the town in Indian-administered Kashmir is struggling to revive its tourism industry. The slowdown has severely affected local livelihoods and the broader regional economy.

stories.title: As DJI duels Insta360, China sharpens global hardware edge amid US scrutiny
stories.summary: Shenzhen-based rivals DJI and Insta360 are intensifying competition across consumer drones and cameras, sharpening China's global hardware edge even as both companies face growing US regulatory scrutiny.

stories.title: Drones hit Kuwait border posts as Iraq orders investigation
stories.summary: Kuwait's military reported that two drones launched from Iraqi territory struck northern border posts on Friday, causing damage but no casualties. Iraq's prime minister ordered an investigation, and Baghdad condemned the attack during a call with Kuwaiti officials.

stories.title: Death toll from April 14 Russian strike on Dnipro rises to seven
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on April 14 has risen to seven after a 47-year-old man who was wounded in the attack died in the hospital.

stories.title: Did this tiny island’s Jewish community help win the Revolutionary War?
stories.summary: A historical account explores the role of the Jewish community on the Caribbean island of Sint Eustatius during the American Revolutionary War. Sephardic Jewish merchants were active participants in the island's thriving free port trade in the Atlantic world.

stories.title: Roommate arrested after body of University of South Florida doctoral student discovered
stories.summary: The body of Zamil Limon, a Bangladeshi doctoral student at the University of South Florida, was found on the Howard Frankland Bridge over Tampa Bay. His roommate, Hisham Abugharbeih, 26, was taken into custody. A second missing Bangladeshi USF doctoral student, Nahida Bristy, remains unaccounted for.

stories.title: Israel kills at least 12 Palestinians in Gaza amid ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least 12 Palestinians in Gaza, drawing condemnation from Hamas, which said the escalation demonstrated the international community's failure to uphold the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1521: 193 Ukrainian soldiers come home. The 73rd swap of the war.
stories.summary: On day 1,521 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, 193 Ukrainian soldiers were returned in the 73rd prisoner exchange. Ukrainian Commander Syrskyi stated that Ukrainian drones have been killing Russian troops faster than Moscow can replace them for four consecutive months.

stories.title: At post-Orbán EU summit, Zelenskyy proposed Europe build integrated air, missile, and drone defense
stories.summary: At a post-Orbán EU summit, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed that Europe build an integrated air, missile, and drone defense system. He thanked the EU for its 20th sanctions package against Russia and urged swift delivery of the first tranche of a €90 billion support package.

stories.title: US legal adviser says Iran war justified by Tehran's 'aggression' over decades
stories.summary: US State Department Legal Adviser Reed Rubinstein released a statement arguing that the war with Iran is justified by Tehran's "aggression" over decades. The statement came days before a deadline for President Trump to obtain congressional approval for the conflict.

stories.title: Iran seizes ship it says linked to US military
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced it seized a vessel named "Epamedons," alleging the ship had been collaborating with the US military. The IRGC said the vessel ignored warnings and committed violations, noting it had made multiple trips to US ports over the past six months.

stories.title: What to know about the Falkland Islands as US considers reassessing position
stories.summary: The United States may reassess its position on Britain's sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, according to an internal Pentagon email described by a U.S. official to Reuters. The review is reportedly being considered as potential punishment for Britain's lack of support regarding the Iran war.

stories.title: Opposition figure: Independent Belarusian attack on Ukraine unlikely despite militarization
stories.summary: A Belarusian opposition figure said that while Belarus is actively militarizing, reforming its mobilization system, and psychologically preparing its society for war, an independent Belarusian attack on Ukraine remains unlikely at present.

stories.title: Kuomintang gets the carrots, DPP the stick
stories.summary: Taiwanese President William Lai Ching-te had to cancel a visit to eSwatini after the Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar revoked overflight permission. The incident reflects growing pressure on Taiwan's diplomatic standing, with China offering incentives to the Kuomintang while penalizing the ruling DPP.

stories.title: Hasidic sect in northern Israel churns out child brides and covers up sex abuse — report
stories.summary: A Haaretz investigation reported that a Bratslav Hasidic community in Yavne'el, northern Israel, has been facilitating underage marriages and covering up sexual abuse. The report described a community-wide effort to prevent authorities from assessing the full scale of the problem.

stories.title: South Africa promises crackdown on xenophobic attacks after Ghana protests
stories.summary: South African authorities pledged on Friday to crack down on xenophobic attacks targeting Ghanaians and other foreign nationals. The announcement followed formal protests from Ghana after videos of violent incidents against its citizens circulated on social media.

stories.title: After years of vetoes, Ukraine expects first EU accession talks to open in weeks
stories.summary: Ukraine expects its first EU accession talks to open within weeks, according to trade negotiator Taras Kachka. He told Politico that Kyiv still views 2027 as a realistic target for closing the majority of negotiation chapters and drafting an accession treaty.

stories.title: China car giant BYD says it can thrive without US
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer BYD says it can thrive without access to the U.S. market, positioning itself to benefit from the global shift away from fossil fuels amid rising fuel prices.

stories.title: U.S. Floats Punishing NATO Members for Refusing to Join Iran War
stories.summary: An internal Pentagon email reportedly suggests the United States could punish NATO allies who refuse to participate in a potential conflict with Iran. Proposed measures include suspending Spain from the alliance and reviewing Britain's sovereignty claim over the Falkland Islands.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu says he was successfully treated for prostate cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced he was successfully treated for prostate cancer. He did not disclose when the treatment took place.

stories.title: Peruvian police raids property of former electoral chief amid irregularities in elections
stories.summary: Peruvian police raided the home of the country's former chief electoral official on Friday as part of an investigation into alleged irregularities in the April 12 general election. The official had resigned earlier in the week amid mounting criticism over delays in vote counting.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman apologises to Canada town for not reporting mass shooter
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman apologized to Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, after the company failed to report a banned ChatGPT account linked to 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, who later killed eight people in a mass shooting. The account had been flagged and banned over violent content concerns eight months before the attack.

stories.title: Trump administration pitching US companies to rebuild Gulf infrastructure hit by Iran
stories.summary: The Trump administration has been urging Gulf states including Kuwait, Bahrain, and the UAE to hire American engineering, manufacturing, and construction firms to rebuild infrastructure damaged by Iranian retaliatory strikes during the US-Israeli war against Iran.

stories.title: After days of crawling through Sumy pipes, Russia is now trying same tactic in Kupiansk
stories.summary: Russian forces are attempting to infiltrate Kupiansk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region by sending infantry through underground pipes, replicating a tactic previously used in the Sumy region.

stories.title: Teens in two states arrested over threat that shuttered Houston synagogue
stories.summary: Two teenagers were arrested in connection with a threat that forced the closure of Congregation Beth Israel, a synagogue in Houston, Texas. Angelina Han Hicks, 18, of Lexington, North Carolina, and an unnamed 16-year-old boy from Houston face charges related to a planned attack on the synagogue.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth blasts Europe, Asia for ‘free-riding’ on US Hormuz action
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth criticized European and Asian allies for 'free-riding' on American military action in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that the U.S. blockade of the strait, linked to the Iran war, is growing stronger each day.

stories.title: Putin may attend G20 summit in Miami after US invitation
stories.summary: The Kremlin said Russian President Vladimir Putin could attend the G20 summit in Miami in December after U.S. President Donald Trump suggested his attendance would be helpful. Trump also said expelling Russia from the G8 had been a mistake. Putin has not attended a G20 summit since 2019.

stories.title: Iran war leaves seafarers stranded in the Gulf
stories.summary: An Indian seafarer named Ankit Yadav and three fellow mariners have been stranded on a boat at an inland Iranian port for approximately two and a half weeks. The crew has been surviving on limited rations of tomatoes and potatoes as the Iran war disrupts shipping in the Gulf.

stories.title: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi to reach Pakistan tonight for talks with U.S.: report
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was expected to arrive in Pakistan for talks related to negotiations with the United States. A U.S. delegation was reportedly set to arrive in Islamabad on April 25 after an Iranian team established the framework for discussions.

stories.title: Child wounded in Bnei Brak missile strike dies after weeks in ICU
stories.summary: The city of Bnei Brak announced the death of Nesiah Karadi, a child who was fatally wounded by a cluster missile strike on the eve of Passover. She had been in intensive care for weeks following the attack on central Israel.

stories.title: Iran's FM Araghchi arrives in Pakistan ahead of planned US ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad, Pakistan, to discuss proposals for resuming peace talks with the United States. The White House confirmed that special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner would depart for Pakistan on Saturday to continue negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: Danish government talks deadlocked one month after election
stories.summary: Government formation talks in Denmark remain deadlocked one month after the parliamentary election. The stalemate is slowing decision-making as Denmark tries to manage a crisis in relations with the Trump administration over Greenland.

stories.title: Shabana Mahmood refuses to rule out sending back refused Afghan asylum seekers
stories.summary: UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has declined to rule out returning rejected Afghan asylum seekers to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan. She said she is closely monitoring discussions between Kabul and EU countries about a returns programme and indicated additional conversations on Afghan returns are taking place within Whitehall.

stories.title: 11-year old boy feared drowned after being swept away while swimming in open water line in Karachi
stories.summary: An 11-year-old boy named Zahid Mohammed Khan was feared drowned after being swept away while swimming in a Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation open water line in Karachi's Scheme-33 area. Rescue teams from Rescue 1122 and Edhi Foundation continued searching into the evening.

stories.title: Trump administration pitching US companies to rebuild Gulf infrastructure hit by Iran
stories.summary: The Trump administration is lobbying for US companies to secure contracts in the reconstruction of Gulf infrastructure damaged during the conflict with Iran. An Arab official described the push as appearing "a little tone-deaf."

stories.title: Russia vows to help Cuba withstand US 'blackmail and threats'
stories.summary: Russia declared solidarity with Cuba on Friday and pledged to continue providing humanitarian aid to the island nation. Moscow characterized Washington's actions toward Cuba as blackmail and threats, vowing to stand against U.S. pressure.

stories.title: US sending envoys to Pakistan, raising hopes of talks with Iran’s Araghchi
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad for diplomatic talks. The United States announced it would send envoys to Pakistan, raising the possibility of indirect engagement, though Tehran has not committed to direct talks with the US delegation.

stories.title: Mass wedding for 300 brides and grooms in central Gaza
stories.summary: A charity-sponsored mass wedding ceremony was held in Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, uniting 300 brides and grooms in a rare festive moment amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: US sanctions Chinese refinery over Iranian oil purchases
stories.summary: The Trump administration imposed new sanctions on Chinese refinery Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) for purchasing large volumes of Iranian crude oil. The US Treasury also sanctioned approximately 40 shipping companies and vessels linked to Iran's "shadow fleet" used to circumvent oil restrictions.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A weekly news quiz covers events from the week of April 18, including travel difficulties faced by Taiwan's president, a gathering of U.N. secretary-general candidates in New York, and Pope Leo's conclusion of a tour across Africa.

stories.title: Israel continues attacks on Lebanon despite extension of ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed six Hezbollah fighters in an exchange of fire near Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon, despite an extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russian forces strike fire station in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a fire and rescue station in a frontline settlement in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. The attack targeted civilian emergency infrastructure in the contested area.

stories.title: Ukraine’s “points-for-kills” procurement system has delivered 181,000 items to the front this year
stories.summary: Ukraine's Brave1 Market procurement system awards military units points for confirmed battlefield activity, which they can use to order equipment. The program has delivered 181,000 items to front-line forces this year, with 95% of drone units participating.

stories.title: Poland says it will challenge Mercosur trade deal in EU's top court
stories.summary: Poland announced it will file a legal challenge against the EU-Mercosur free trade agreement at the European Union's top court. Deputy Prime Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said Warsaw considers the deal harmful to Polish farmers.

stories.title: Human rights watch releases a new report detailing the quote “unrelenting persecution of Tigrayans”
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch published a report documenting what it calls ongoing persecution of Tigrayans nearly four years after the peace agreement between the Tigray People's Liberation Front and the Ethiopian government. The report notes hundreds of thousands of Tigrayans remain displaced and unable to return home.

stories.title: Iran to resume international flights from Tehran airport
stories.summary: Iran announced it will resume international flights from Tehran's airport, with the first routes serving Istanbul, Turkey, and Muscat, Oman.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrives in Islamabad ahead of US talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad, Pakistan, ahead of expected talks with the United States. Pakistani officials said Araghchi would meet senior Pakistani leaders to discuss regional developments and peace efforts as diplomatic activity surrounding the Iran conflict intensifies.

stories.title: High school senior identified as person killed in shooting at Lousiana mall
stories.summary: A 16-year-old high school senior, Martha Odom, was identified as the person killed in a shooting at a mall food court in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. She died from a gunshot wound to the chest after two groups exchanged gunfire on Thursday afternoon, leaving five others wounded.

stories.title: Putin may attend G20 summit in Miami after U.S. invitation: Kremlin
stories.summary: The Kremlin indicated that Russian President Vladimir Putin may attend the G20 summit in Miami in December following a U.S. invitation. Putin has not attended a G20 summit since 2019. President Trump has adopted a more conciliatory posture toward Russia during his second term.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth says US blockade on Iran ‘going global’
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the American blockade on Iran is expanding globally. He urged Iran to 'choose wisely at the negotiating table,' signaling continued pressure on Tehran.

stories.title: Trump says Iran preparing offer to meet US demands
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated in a Reuters interview that Iran is preparing a proposal aimed at addressing Washington's demands. The comments signal potential movement in ongoing negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: CJP says transferring judge back to SHC would render key constitutional ideals redundant
stories.summary: Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi, as chair of the Judicial Commission, opposed transferring Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro from the Islamabad High Court back to the Sindh High Court, arguing it would undermine constitutional principles of federalism and equitable representation.

stories.title: Trump to again end legal status of people who entered US with CBP One app
stories.summary: The Trump administration is moving again to end the temporary legal status of migrants who entered the United States through the Biden-era CBP One application. A judge had previously blocked an earlier attempt to terminate the program.

stories.title: EU just held its first summit without Orbán, and discovered his obstruction was covering deeper divisions
stories.summary: The European Union held its first summit without Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, revealing that deeper policy divisions among member states had long been masked by Orbán's well-known obstructionism. Diplomats privately acknowledged that conflicts previously attributed to Orbán were more broadly shared.

stories.title: Witkoff and Kushner headed to Pakistan for Iran talks
stories.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are headed to Pakistan for Iran ceasefire talks, where an Iranian delegation is already present. President Trump has signaled that Tehran may be prepared to offer concessions as signs of progress emerge.

stories.title: Pro-Russian forces’ victory in Bulgaria poses risks for Ukraine, but should not be overstated, analyst says
stories.summary: An analyst said the victory of pro-Russian forces led by Rumen Radev in Bulgaria creates additional challenges for Ukraine but cautioned that the threat should not be overstated. The political shift may complicate Bulgaria's stance on supporting Ukraine.

stories.title: Satellites at the center: Inside the Pentagon’s next-gen space architecture
stories.summary: The Pentagon is advancing a next-generation space architecture centered on satellites for data networking, missile tracking, and cyber resilience. Breaking Defense compiled reporting on the evolving role of satellite systems in US national security.

stories.title: PM Sanchez sidesteps Spain-U.S. dispute at NATO, brushing off reported Pentagon email
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez sidestepped a dispute with the United States while attending NATO proceedings. Reports emerged that the Pentagon was considering whether to suspend Spain from NATO, based on a U.S. Defence Department email cited by an unidentified American official.

stories.title: Indonesian UN peacekeeper dies of wounds suffered in Lebanon last month: UNIFIL
stories.summary: An Indonesian United Nations peacekeeper serving with UNIFIL in Lebanon has died from wounds sustained last month. His death brings the total number of peacekeepers killed since March 2 to six.

stories.title: WWF-Pakistan highlights 'potentially irreversible risks' of development work at Margalla foothills
stories.summary: WWF-Pakistan raised concerns about "potentially irreversible" ecological risks from development work at the foothills of Islamabad's Margalla Hills. The organization called for suspension of all proposed and ongoing activities pending a transparent environmental review, days after the Interior Ministry announced a 1,000-kanal park project.

stories.title: Petro becomes first president to visit Venezuela since Maduro abduction
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro traveled to Venezuela for a meeting with interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodriguez, marking the first presidential visit since the abduction of President Nicolás Maduro. Border security was a central topic of the discussions between the two leaders.

stories.title: Israeli PM Netanyahu reveals he had successful prostate cancer treatment
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed that doctors discovered a malignant prostate tumour at a very early stage and that he underwent successful treatment. He announced the news on the social media platform X.

stories.title: SBU releases exclusive footage of latest prisoner swap
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service released footage of Ukrainian defenders freed from Russian captivity in a prisoner exchange on Friday, April 24. The swap is part of ongoing efforts to secure the release of prisoners of war held by both sides.

stories.title: Pakistan secures 3 bids for spot LNG cargoes
stories.summary: Pakistan's state-run Pakistan LNG Limited secured three bids for spot LNG cargo deliveries between April 27 and May 8, ending a 28-month gap in such procurement. TotalEnergies, Vitol Bahrain, and OQ Trading submitted the lowest bids, ranging from $17.997 to $18.88 per million British thermal units.

stories.title: US sanctions hit China refinery, 40 shippers over Iran oil
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on a Chinese refinery and approximately 40 shipping vessels over their involvement in Iranian oil trade. The sanctions come as the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz heightens global energy tensions.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky visits Saudi Arabia for new security talks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Saudi Arabia for a second time in recent weeks to hold new security talks. The discussions are part of ongoing diplomatic efforts related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: Zelenskiy arrives in Saudi Arabia seeking security cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy arrived in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on Friday for his second visit in a month. Kyiv is seeking to strengthen security cooperation and promote its battle-tested military technology in the Middle East amid the ongoing Iran war.

stories.title: G7 ‘concerned’ at Russia and China’s nuclear build-up
stories.summary: The G7 Non-proliferation Directors Group issued a statement expressing concern over significant nuclear weapons build-up and modernization by Russia and China. The group reaffirmed support for the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons at a meeting whose results were published by the French foreign ministry.

stories.title: Russia says new EU sanctions will hurt developing countries
stories.summary: Russia warned on Friday that new European Union sanctions targeting its oil and gas exports would harm developing countries and the EU itself. Moscow promised retaliatory measures in response to the latest round of restrictions.

stories.title: Iran Foreign Minister Araghchi likely to reach Islamabad on April 24, Pakistani source says
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to arrive in Islamabad on April 24, according to Pakistani sources. A US logistics and security team is already in the capital in preparation for anticipated talks.

stories.title: Iranian FM Araghchi expected to arrive in Islamabad tonight, Pakistani sources say
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was expected to arrive in Islamabad on Friday with a small negotiating team, according to Pakistani sources. A second round of Iran-U.S. peace talks was also anticipated, with a U.S. logistics and security team already in the Pakistani capital. Iran's state media confirmed Araghchi would continue to Muscat and Moscow as part of a regional tour.

stories.title: First Ukraine made interceptor drones to hunt Shaheds. Now it’s firing them from a 1969 airplane.
stories.summary: Ukraine has begun launching interceptor drones from a 1969 Antonov An-28 transport plane to hunt Russian Shahed drones. Interceptor drones, which cost less than a used car each, now account for the destruction of one in three Russian aerial targets over Ukraine.

stories.title: Hormuz closure keeps Brent above $105 with outlook uncertain
stories.summary: Brent crude closed Friday at $105.33 per barrel, gaining nearly ten dollars over the week amid uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran conflict and the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The benchmark hit a weekly high of $107.40 on Thursday before pulling back.

stories.title: Qatar emir and Trump discuss Iran truce and maritime security
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and US President Donald Trump spoke by phone about the Iran ceasefire and maritime security concerns. The emir warned of risks to global shipping routes and supply chains and called for de-escalation.

stories.title: FAO and WMO warn extreme heat pushes global agriculture 'to the limit,' threatening one billion people
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Meteorological Organization published a joint report warning that escalating extreme heat events are pushing global agriculture to its limits. The report states the phenomenon threatens the health and livelihoods of over one billion people and causes the annual loss of 500 billion working hours in the agricultural sector.

stories.title: Ukraine underestimated ties with Global South, Ukrainian diplomat says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian diplomat acknowledged that Ukraine overestimated its partners' willingness to act decisively and underestimated the importance of building ties with countries in the Global South. The admission highlights a strategic diplomatic gap in Ukraine's outreach.

stories.title: El Niño set to return in mid-2026, UN warns of global climate impacts
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization warned Friday that the El Niño climate pattern is expected to return by mid-2026. The phenomenon could drive higher global temperatures and disrupt weather systems worldwide.

stories.title: Main suspect in Syria's Tadamon massacre arrested, ministry says
stories.summary: Syria's Interior Ministry announced the arrest of the main suspect in the 2013 Tadamon massacre, in which 288 civilians were killed. The massacre is considered one of the worst atrocities attributed to the former government of Bashar al-Assad.

stories.title: US veteran lost in Arizona’s wilderness for four days rescued by his own son
stories.summary: Vietnam war veteran Mark Young was rescued by his own son after spending four days lost in the Arizona wilderness with minimal supplies. Young battled dehydration and killed a rattlesnake while his children and others searched for him.

stories.title: Iran calls US seizure of ship ‘flagrant breach of international law’
stories.summary: Iran's mission to the United Nations has condemned the US seizure of the commercial vessel Touska, calling it a flagrant breach of international law. The ship was intercepted as part of Washington's naval blockade on Iranian ports and was reportedly carrying medical supplies including dialysis equipment.

stories.title: WATCH: Hezbollah uses ambulances to conceal terror activity, IDF footage reveals
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces released footage alleging that Hezbollah has used ambulances to conceal militant activity in Lebanon. The IDF stated that such use of medical equipment undermines protections granted to medical facilities under international law.

stories.title: Family under longest immigration detention of Trump’s term released
stories.summary: A US district judge in the western district of Texas ordered the release of a woman and her five children who had been held in immigration detention for over 10 months, the longest family detention under Trump's second administration. The family is connected to the suspect in the 2025 Colorado fire attack.

stories.title: President Zelensky, Saudi Crown Prince discuss three key areas of cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah to discuss three priority areas of cooperation between Ukraine and Saudi Arabia. Details of the specific cooperation areas were outlined during the talks.

stories.title: Moldova parliament votes to end energy state of emergency
stories.summary: Moldova's parliament voted to lift the country's energy state of emergency effective Saturday. The emergency had been imposed after Russian attacks in neighboring Ukraine destroyed a power line that supplied most of Moldova's electricity.

stories.title: Ukraine details its “deep strike center” – the coordination unit behind long-range drone operations on occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces disclosed details of its "deep strike center," the coordination unit responsible for planning and executing long-range drone operations against high-value Russian assets in occupied territories.

stories.title: 11-year-old girl from Bnei Brak dies of wounds from Iranian strike on Passover eve
stories.summary: Nesya Karadi, an 11-year-old girl from Bnei Brak in central Israel, died of wounds sustained when a cluster bomb submunition from an Iranian strike hit her family's home on April 1. She became the 21st victim of the Iran war.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP says ceasefire ‘meaningless’ in light of Israeli attacks
stories.summary: A Hezbollah member of parliament declared the ceasefire with Israel "meaningless" in light of ongoing Israeli attacks. Hostilities between Hezbollah and Israel resumed on March 2 when the group opened fire in support of Iran.

stories.title: China rejects Trump accusation intercepted Iran ship was 'gift'
stories.summary: China has rejected US President Trump's claim that the seized Iranian vessel was a "gift" to China. Beijing defended its trade ties with Iran as tensions escalated over the US interception and allegations of dual-use cargo aboard the ship.

stories.title: Sovereignty of Falklands rests with the UK, Britain tells the US
stories.summary: Britain's government reaffirmed that sovereignty over the Falkland Islands rests with the United Kingdom. The statement came after an internal Pentagon email suggested the U.S. could reassess its position on the Falklands to punish Britain for its stance on the Iran war.

stories.title: Putin’s approval rating falls to lowest since before Ukraine war, state pollster says
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin's approval rating has fallen to its lowest level since before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to Russia's state pollster. A government crackdown on internet access, messaging apps, and VPNs has fueled public frustration in recent months.

stories.title: Kushner, Witkoff to head to Islamabad for direct talks following initial Iranian refusal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is sending special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Islamabad, Pakistan, for direct talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi. The meeting follows an initial Iranian refusal to engage, according to US officials.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia cuts $200m in Met Opera House funding due to Iran war: Report
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has reportedly withdrawn $200 million in funding from New York's Metropolitan Opera House due to the economic impact of the Iran war on the kingdom. The Met's general manager confirmed the Saudi decision was linked to the conflict's financial toll.

stories.title: Can Europe help the Middle East resolve the war on Iran?
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondent Rory Challands reported from the EU summit held in Cyprus, where European leaders discussed potential roles for Europe in helping resolve the ongoing war involving Iran in the Middle East.

stories.title: Russian Platforms Label Pushkin, Gogol Classics Under ‘Drug Propaganda’ Law
stories.summary: Under a Russian law that took effect on March 1, literature, films, media, and online content deemed to promote narcotics must carry a warning label. The regulation has been applied to works by classic Russian authors including Pushkin and Gogol.

stories.title: Palestine Action defendants targeted Elbit's use of ‘deadly AI’, court hears
stories.summary: Six Palestine Action defendants are on trial at London's Woolwich Crown Court for criminal damage connected to a break-in at an Elbit Systems factory in Filton, near Bristol, in August 2024. The court heard that the activists targeted the Israeli arms company's use of artificial intelligence technology.

stories.title: Chornobyl employee, five National Guards still detained by Russia, plant chief says
stories.summary: The head of the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant reported that one plant employee and five National Guard servicemen who had been guarding the facility remain in Russian captivity. They were detained during Russia's occupation of the Chornobyl site.

stories.title: Mamdani vetoes school buffer zone bill; leading Jewish groups pan ‘profound failure’
stories.summary: New York state legislator Zohran Mamdani vetoed a bill that would have established buffer zones around schools, drawing criticism from leading Jewish organizations. New York City's mayor will allow a separate measure protecting houses of worship to become law, while a Long Island congressman proposed federal legislation to protect religious sites.

stories.title: US: Justice Department drops investigation into Fed Chair Powell
stories.summary: The US Justice Department closed its investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The decision removes a potential obstacle to the appointment of Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominee to lead the central bank.

stories.title: Report: Detainees in alleged plot against Russia’s internet regulator may belong to anti-censorship movement
stories.summary: Russia's FSB detained individuals allegedly plotting an attack against leaders of Roskomnadzor, the country's internet regulator. The Russian human rights group Department One concluded the detainees may be members of Alyi Lebed (Scarlet Swan), a movement opposing internet censorship in Russia.

stories.title: 'Information leakage to our adversaries': When prediction markets spiral out of control
stories.summary: A US Army soldier was indicted for allegedly using classified military intelligence to place winning bets on the capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. The case involves prediction markets such as Polymarket and Kalshi and is part of a growing pattern of insider trading on such platforms.

stories.title: Watch: 20,000 teddy bears highlight plight of missing Ukrainian children
stories.summary: An installation of 20,000 teddy bears was displayed in Washington, DC, with each bear representing one of the children Ukraine says have been abducted by Russia. The exhibit aimed to draw attention to the plight of missing Ukrainian children.

stories.title: US sanctions China-based oil refinery and 40 shippers over Iran oil
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced economic sanctions on a major China-based oil refinery and approximately 40 shipping companies and tankers involved in transporting Iranian oil. The measures target entities doing business with Iran as part of a broader campaign to curtail Iran's oil export revenues through secondary sanctions.

stories.title: Fire at Russian oil terminal enters 4th day as toxic smoke and ‘oil’ rains blanket port city
stories.summary: A fire at a marine terminal in Tuapse, Krasnodar Krai, Russia, burned for four days before emergency crews contained and extinguished the open flames by April 24. Some 276 personnel and 77 pieces of equipment were deployed as toxic smoke and oil residue affected the port city.

stories.title: Amid truce, Hezbollah attacks IDF in south Lebanon; troops kill 6 gunmen in Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: Hezbollah attacked Israeli Defense Forces in southern Lebanon despite an active truce, and IDF troops killed six gunmen in the town of Bint Jbeil. The IDF also struck buildings used to launch rockets at northern Israel shortly before President Trump announced a ceasefire extension, and an Israeli drone was downed over Tyre.

stories.title: How Gold and Regional Rivalries Drive the War in Sudan
stories.summary: The armed conflict in Sudan, now entering its fourth year, is being driven in part by competition over gold resources and regional rivalries. The war has produced what is described as the world's worst ongoing humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Netanyahu says he was successfully treated for prostate cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, 76, announced he had received successful treatment for early-stage prostate cancer discovered during a routine checkup. His annual medical report indicated the targeted treatment removed a malignant tumor with no remaining trace.

stories.title: Erdogan could be key go-between with Putin, says Crimean Tatar leader
stories.summary: Crimean Tatar leader Mustafa Dzhemilev suggested that Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan could serve as an effective intermediary with Russian President Vladimir Putin, both in broader peace negotiations and in efforts to secure the release of Ukrainian detainees.

stories.title: Space Force tasks a dozen companies for Golden Dome space-based interceptors
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force has tasked twelve companies with developing space-based interceptors for the Golden Dome missile defense program. The service aims to demonstrate an initial capability for orbital missile interceptors by 2028.

stories.title: Russian e-book platforms attach drug-harm labels to works by Pushkin, Gogol, and Bulgakov
stories.summary: Russian e-book and audiobook platforms have begun attaching drug-harm warning labels to works by classic authors including Alexander Pushkin, Nikolai Gogol, and Mikhail Bulgakov, according to the independent Russian outlet Verstka.

stories.title: South Africa vows crackdown on xenophobic attacks after Ghana protest
stories.summary: South Africa has pledged to take decisive action against perpetrators of xenophobic violence targeting foreign nationals. The commitment follows a formal protest from Ghana over incidents involving Ghanaian citizens in South Africa.

stories.title: Tanzania releases government-led inquiry into poll violence
stories.summary: A Tanzanian government-appointed commission released its report on violence during last year's elections. The inquiry was ordered by the president to investigate the circumstances surrounding the poll-related unrest.

stories.title: Netanyahu treated for early-stage prostate cancer, says he is in ‘excellent’ physical condition
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed that he was treated for early-stage prostate cancer. He said he delayed publishing his annual medical report to prevent Iran from using it as propaganda during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Russian animal rights activist dies weeks after 2 drunk men beat her, set dog on her
stories.summary: An animal rights activist in Omsk, Russia, died on April 23 after being beaten and attacked by a dog set on her by two intoxicated men the previous month, according to TASS citing law enforcement sources.

stories.title: Russia struck Ukraine’s railways 1,200 times in 2025 – more than the previous two years combined
stories.summary: Russia struck Ukrainian railway infrastructure more than 1,200 times in 2025, exceeding the total for the previous two years combined. Ukraine's rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia reported 17,300 rail sites hit since 2022, with 40 workers killed, as Russia increasingly targets trains directly.

stories.title: Resistance Imprisoned: A Spotlight on the Russians and Ukrainians Held by the Kremlin
stories.summary: A new exhibition in Strasbourg highlights the cases of Russian dissidents and Ukrainian civilians and soldiers currently imprisoned in Russia, drawing attention to political detention by the Kremlin.

stories.title: Israeli attacks on Lebanon may violate international law, UN warns
stories.summary: A United Nations report has warned that Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Hezbollah rocket attacks on Israel may have violated international humanitarian law. The report highlights potential breaches by both parties to the conflict.

stories.title: Iran: Neither war nor Peace, Ukraine’s Lifeline, Starmer: “Just a Scratch”?
stories.summary: A near-stalemate has emerged after approximately two months of asymmetric conflict between the United States and Iran. President Trump's public statements oscillated between aggressive rhetoric and expressions of optimism about a potential deal, including suggestions that Iran could hand over nuclear materials.

stories.title: Reality check: Israeli ambitions confront US dictates in Iran and Lebanon
stories.summary: Ceasefires involving Iran and Lebanon appear to have been imposed by the United States rather than negotiated by Israel, causing unease within the Israeli government. The dynamic highlights tensions between Israeli ambitions and US diplomatic directives in the region.

stories.title: Can Africa Follow Asia’s Development Model?
stories.summary: An economics writer known for analyzing Asian development models examines whether similar strategies could be applied to Africa, currently described as the fastest-growing continent.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi meets NATO, EU military chiefs to discuss Ukrainian forces urgent needs
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief General Oleksandr Syrskyi met with NATO Military Committee Chair Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone and EU Military Committee Chair General Seán Clancy to discuss the Ukrainian armed forces' most pressing operational needs.

stories.title: Ukraine to field 25,000 ground robots in push to replace soldiers for frontline logistics
stories.summary: Ukraine plans to deploy 25,000 ground robots for frontline logistics to reduce soldiers' exposure to danger. Ground robots completed over 9,000 frontline missions in March, tripling the November total, and last summer captured their first Russian position.

stories.title: Trump Justice Department adds firing squads for federal executions
stories.summary: The Trump administration's Justice Department announced plans to expand federal death penalty use and add firing squads, electrocution, and gas as execution methods alongside lethal injection. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said the move targets terrorists, child murderers, and those who kill law enforcement.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill eight across Gaza, including near hospital
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians across northern and southern Gaza on Friday. Artillery shelling hit a house near Kamal Adwan Hospital in the north, killing three, while a strike targeted a vehicle in al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis, in the south.

stories.title: Pentagon email floats suspending Spain from NATO, other steps over Iran rift, source says
stories.summary: An internal Pentagon email outlines punitive options against NATO allies perceived as unsupportive of U.S. operations in the war with Iran. Proposed measures include suspending Spain from NATO and reviewing the U.S. position on Britain's claim to the Falkland Islands, according to a U.S. official who spoke to Reuters.

stories.title: Suspected Nazi-looted Stradivarius reappears in France, says expert
stories.summary: A Stradivarius violin stolen by Nazi soldiers from a museum in Warsaw in 1944 has reportedly resurfaced in France. The instrument is now estimated to be worth approximately $13 million. An expert confirmed the reappearance of the suspected Nazi-looted instrument.

stories.title: Putin returns 'Iron Felix' Dzerzhinsky to Russia's spy school
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin has ordered Russia's Federal Security Service spy academy to be renamed after Felix Dzerzhinsky. Dzerzhinsky, known as "Iron Felix," founded the Soviet secret police and was the architect of the Red Terror following the 1917 revolution.

stories.title: Why is this game only legal across Australia one day a year?
stories.summary: Two-up, a coin-toss betting game historically played by Australian soldiers during World War One, is legal across Australia only on April 25, which is Anzac Day.

stories.title: US Air Force aims to double F-15EX Eagle fleet
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force announced plans to nearly double its F-15EX Eagle II fleet to 267 aircraft, significantly expanding the inventory of the advanced fighter platform.

stories.title: Gulf states in limbo as US-Iran crisis drags on
stories.summary: Analysts warn that Gulf states face uncertainty as the US-Iran crisis continues, with limited ability to influence Washington's decisions on war and peace. The prolonged standoff leaves the region in a precarious diplomatic position.

stories.title: Political scientist: Caution with word “victory” reflects maturing society
stories.summary: A political scientist observed that the declining use of the word "victory" in Ukrainian public discourse reflects a maturing society rather than disappointment. The shift indicates a more realistic approach to the ongoing war.

stories.title: CJP says granting transfer of judge from IHC to SHC would render key constitutional ideals redundant
stories.summary: Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi, as chairperson of the Judicial Commission, has opposed transferring Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro from the Islamabad High Court to the Sindh High Court, arguing it would undermine constitutional principles of federalism and equitable representation.

stories.title: Citizen taken into custody for likening Tarnol Railway Crossing to Strait of Hormuz: FIR
stories.summary: Police in Islamabad arrested a citizen for allegedly mocking the Tarnol Railway crossing by comparing it to the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial shipping route disrupted by the Middle East war. An FIR was registered under multiple sections including disobedience to public orders.

stories.title: US and EU sign critical minerals plan in push to loosen China’s grip on key materials
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic signed a memorandum of understanding on producing and securing critical minerals. The agreement aims to reduce Western dependence on China for materials essential to advanced manufacturing.

stories.title: US Air Force plans to boost stockpile of Lockheed’s stealth missile
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force plans to increase its stockpile of Lockheed Martin's stealth missiles. Military planners view the weapons as essential to preparedness for a potential future conflict with China.

stories.title: Michael B Jordan to take on big-screen adaptation of hit video game Battlefield
stories.summary: Actor and Oscar winner Michael B. Jordan is set to produce, and possibly star in, a film adaptation of the video game series Battlefield. Director Christopher McQuarrie is attached to helm the project.

stories.title: Rebuilding of Gaza healthcare system requires $10 billion: WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization estimates that rebuilding Gaza's healthcare system will require $10 billion. Israel's military campaign has devastated the sector, leaving hospitals and medical facilities severely damaged and laboratories only partially operational.

stories.title: After Independence Day, Israel faces its biggest test: Unity - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses internal divisions in Israel highlighted by an alternative Independence Day ceremony. The article argues that Israeli unity appears to be driven by crisis rather than peacetime solidarity.

stories.title: Forty years after nuclear disaster, Ukraine's Chornobyl plant is haunted by war
stories.summary: Ukraine's Chornobyl nuclear power plant, site of the 1986 disaster, continues to face threats from the ongoing war with Russia. A Russian strike drone hit the protective arc covering the damaged reactor last year, narrowly avoiding another catastrophe. The incident underscores the dangers posed by military operations near nuclear facilities.

stories.title: Why are campaigners concerned by Palantir's presence in the UK?
stories.summary: Israel-linked AI company Palantir is expanding its presence across British policing and healthcare sectors. Campaigners have raised concerns about the implications for privacy and surveillance in the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Will the US find that war damage and economic pain cannot bend Iran’s resolve?
stories.summary: An analysis examines whether sustained U.S. military and economic pressure can break Iran's resolve. Decades of sanctions have led Iran to build resilience into its economy and critical systems.

stories.title: Kosovo court jails three Serb separatists over 2023 Banjska attack
stories.summary: A Kosovo court has sentenced three Serb separatists for their roles in the 2023 attack on the village of Banjska. The assault led to a clash with police that killed one officer and three of the gunmen.

stories.title: Independence Day: Israel’s sirens signal danger, loss - and a wake-up call
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on Israel's Independence Day sirens, noting they now signal danger and loss alongside celebration. The author suggests adding a new siren tradition to remind citizens of the significance of their country.

stories.title: Israel says it killed six Hezbollah fighters in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military claimed it killed six Hezbollah fighters in the southern Lebanese village of Bint Jbeil during an exchange of fire near the border. The area had seen heavy fighting before a ceasefire took effect on 17 April. The claim could not be independently verified.

stories.title: Retired US Army Colonel discusses naval strategy in Hormuz
stories.summary: Retired US Army Colonel Joe Buccino, former communications director of US Central Command, discussed American naval strategy regarding the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM oversees US military operations across the Middle East, Central Asia, and South Asia.

stories.title: Trump administration to prioritise seeking death penalty, use firing squads
stories.summary: The Trump administration has announced plans to prioritize seeking the death penalty and permit the use of firing squads in federal executions. Capital punishment remains a divisive issue in the United States, with critics citing concerns about wrongful convictions.

stories.title: Zack Polanski calls for ‘nuance’ when discussing antisemitism in rebuke of PM
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski called for nuance in discussing antisemitism, accusing Prime Minister Keir Starmer of playing political games with the issue. Starmer had accused Polanski of downplaying recent antisemitic incidents as the Green Party faces scrutiny over members' comments.

stories.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy visits Saudi Arabia, Putin weighs G20 attendance
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited Saudi Arabia as part of a diplomatic offensive following the securing of an EU loan. Meanwhile, the Kremlin said Russian President Vladimir Putin may or may not attend the G20 summit in Miami in December.

stories.title: Sindh govt will fulfill its promise to rebuild Gul Plaza, CM Murad says
stories.summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah pledged to rebuild Gul Plaza in Karachi, a multi-storey shopping complex destroyed by an inferno that killed more than 70 people in January. Compensation cheques were distributed to affected shopkeepers.

stories.title: China adds 7 EU entities to export control list over Taiwan arms sales
stories.summary: China has added seven European Union entities to its export control list in response to arms sales to Taiwan. The designated entities are also prohibited from receiving Chinese-origin dual-use items through foreign organizations.

stories.title: Palestine Action defendants targeted Elbit's use of ‘deadly AI’, court hears
stories.summary: Three Palestine Action defendants—Zoe Rogers, Fatema Rajwani, and Jordan Devlin—told a UK court they targeted computers and drones at facilities linked to Israeli defense firm Elbit Systems. They said their actions were aimed at disrupting what they described as the company's use of AI-enabled weapons technology.

stories.title: US mulls lifting sanctions on the 'North Korea of Africa'
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering lifting sanctions on Eritrea as it seeks to expand US influence in the strategically important Red Sea region. Egypt is said to be facilitating talks between Washington and the East African nation, sometimes called the 'North Korea of Africa.'

stories.title: Drone attacks hit Dagestan, flights canceled at four airports
stories.summary: Drones struck the Russian region of Dagestan on Friday, April 24. Flights were subsequently canceled at airports in Dagestan, Ingushetia, Chechnya, and North Ossetia.

stories.title: Main suspect in Syria's Tadamon massacre arrested, ministry says
stories.summary: Syrian authorities arrested Amjad Yousef, the main suspect in the Tadamon massacre, in Hama province in western Syria. Yousef had been in hiding since the overthrow of President Bashar al-Assad in 2024.

stories.title: Who is Issam Buwaydani, ex-Syrian rebel leader detained by UAE?
stories.summary: Former Syrian rebel leader Issam Buwaydani, who headed Jaish al-Islam, was released after being detained by the United Arab Emirates for approximately one year. His detention and release highlight shifting relations between Syria and the UAE following the fall of Bashar al-Assad.

stories.title: UK Foreign Office closes unit tracking Israeli violations
stories.summary: The UK Foreign Office has closed a unit that tracked Israeli violations. Human rights lawyers and activists have raised concerns, saying the unit's materials were essential for holding Israel accountable.

stories.title: Three Kosovo Serbs jailed over deadly gun battle and monastery siege
stories.summary: A Kosovo court sentenced two Serb men to life imprisonment and a third to 30 years for the deadly 2023 attack in Banjska. The armed assault included a gun battle with police and a monastery siege in northern Kosovo.

stories.title: What the Iran-Iraq war taught today’s Iranian leaders - and why that matters
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the 1980–1988 Iran-Iraq war, launched by Saddam Hussein's invasion of Iran, shaped the Islamic Republic's current leadership and strategic thinking. The conflict lasted eight years and killed over one million people, profoundly influencing Iran's political and military institutions.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Faces Growing Human Displacement in Worsening Drought Crisis
stories.summary: The International Organisation for Migration reported that nearly 62,000 people have been displaced by drought in Somalia since the beginning of the year. More than six million people across five districts face hunger as the drought crisis worsens.

stories.title: Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei 'gravely wounded' but 'mentally sharp'
stories.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Iran's late Supreme Leader, is reported to be gravely wounded but remains mentally sharp. Senior Revolutionary Guards commanders have not visited him, though President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is also a heart surgeon, has been involved in his medical care.

stories.title: US has exhausted billions of dollars worth of weapons stockpile in war on Iran: NYT report
stories.summary: According to a New York Times investigation, the United States has expended billions of dollars' worth of weapons in its war on Iran, including over 1,200 Patriot interceptor missiles and roughly 1,100 long-range stealth cruise missiles originally built for a potential conflict with China.

stories.title: Space Force picks firms to develop Golden Dome’s space-based interceptors
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected multiple defense firms, including major contractors and startups, to develop space-based interceptor technologies for the Golden Dome missile defense program. The program's lead official has acknowledged concerns that the orbital defense system may prove unaffordable.

stories.title: How Israel targeted and killed Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed while reporting on an Israeli air strike in southern Lebanon during a 10-day ceasefire. The report details how Israeli forces targeted and struck her location.

stories.title: Trump's favourite field marshall: A profile of Asim Munir
stories.summary: Pakistan has positioned itself as a mediator or facilitator in peace talks between the United States and Iran. The article profiles Pakistani Army Chief General Asim Munir and his role in enabling the country's diplomatic positioning.

stories.title: President Trump should secure America’s nuclear future by taking weapons out of DoE
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Franklin C. Miller and Frank A. Rose argues that U.S. nuclear weapons management should be removed from the Department of Energy, contending the arsenal is too critical to national defense to remain housed within that agency.

stories.title: War, drought, aid shortfall to fuel hunger in 2026, global report says
stories.summary: A global report warns that war, drought, and aid shortfalls will fuel hunger in 2026. The report noted that acute hunger has doubled over the past decade, with two famines declared in 2025 for the first time in the report's history.

stories.title: Ukrainian strikes have wiped $25.5 billion off Russia’s war machine, Syrskyi says
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi said Ukrainian strikes have inflicted approximately $25.5 billion in damage to Russia's war capabilities. He stated that Ukrainian drones are now killing Russian troops faster than Moscow can replace them, a trend sustained for four consecutive months.

stories.title: Man found guilty over birds of prey dumped outside Hampshire village shop
stories.summary: James Kempster was found guilty in Hampshire, England, of possessing the bodies of a barn owl and a kestrel. His DNA was found on the dead birds of prey, which were left alongside 50 dead hares outside a volunteer-run shop in the village of Broughton.

stories.title: Pirates hijack oil tanker off the coast of Somalia
stories.summary: Pirates hijacked an oil tanker off the coast of Somalia in the Indian Ocean. Piracy in the region, once a major international concern, has seen a resurgence in recent years.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli attacks killed 2,491 since March
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Emergency Operations Centre reported that Israeli attacks killed 2,491 people and wounded 7,719 between 2 March and 24 April. The figures were released by Lebanon's National News Agency, citing the Ministry of Public Health.

stories.title: ‘No clear strategy’: how Trump went from shock and awe to wait and see in Iran
stories.summary: An analysis describes how the Trump administration's Iran strategy has shifted from initial shock-and-awe strikes and leadership targeting to sustained economic pressure. With negotiations stalled, U.S. allies reportedly see a lack of a clear long-term plan to end the conflict.

stories.title: Iran continuing to lay mines in Strait of Hormuz, US official says
stories.summary: A US official said Iran continues to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, President Donald Trump ordered the Navy to shoot and destroy any vessel suspected of mine-laying. Experts believe fewer than 100 mines have been placed so far.

stories.title: Zelensky: 193 defenders returning to Ukraine from Russian captivity
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that 193 Ukrainian service members are returning from Russian captivity as part of a prisoner exchange.

stories.title: EU approves 20th sanctions package against Russia and $105 billion loan to Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Union has approved its 20th sanctions package against Russia, targeting the country's oil and gas sector. The EU also approved a $105 billion loan to Ukraine, arriving just before the war-torn country was set to exhaust its financial reserves. Russia has vowed to retaliate.

stories.title: Trump sends Witkoff and son-in-law to Pakistan for Iran talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is sending envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner to Islamabad, Pakistan, for talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Vice President JD Vance and Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf are not expected to attend the discussions.

stories.title: Russian oil exports slump as Ukraine hammers ports and refineries
stories.summary: Russian oil exports are declining as Ukrainian strikes continue to hit Russian ports and refineries. Despite a US sanctions waiver, exports could fall to their lowest levels since 2023, according to sources.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister to embark on three-nation tour as US peace talks remain stalled
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi plans to visit Pakistan, Russia, and Oman to explore reopening stalled peace talks with the United States. A key Iranian demand is a permanent U.S.-Israeli commitment to cease attacks on Iran. Araghchi may also discuss a new arrangement for governing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman.

stories.title: Israeli settlers attack homes in Qusra near Nablus
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian homes in the town of Qusra, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Anti-settlement activist Abdul Azim Wadi reported that residents confronted the attackers, leading to clashes. The incident is part of ongoing settler violence targeting Palestinian communities in the West Bank.

stories.title: Venice Biennale Jury Excludes Russia and Israel From Awards Considerations
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale jury excluded both Russia and Israel from awards consideration. Both President Vladimir Putin and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu face active International Criminal Court warrants for alleged war crimes.

stories.title: El Nino set to return as early as May, impacting global weather patterns
stories.summary: The United Nations weather agency warned that El Niño conditions could return as early as May. The phenomenon is expected to shift global weather patterns, affecting rainfall, drought conditions, and temperatures worldwide.

stories.title: US envoys Witkoff, Kushner to depart Saturday for talks with Iran FM in Pakistan
stories.summary: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to depart Saturday for talks with Iran's foreign minister in Islamabad, Pakistan. The White House says Tehran requested an in-person meeting, and Vice President Vance is reportedly on standby to join if negotiations advance. The US is also said to be preparing new battle plans for the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Met Opera says Saudi partnership has fallen through
stories.summary: New York's Metropolitan Opera announced that its partnership with Saudi Arabia has collapsed. The development follows reports that Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund is also likely to end its support for LIV Golf.

stories.title: Czech military expert: Ukraine conducting highly skillful diplomacy in Middle East
stories.summary: A Czech military expert assessed that Ukraine is conducting skillful diplomacy in the Middle East. The analyst suggested this diplomatic engagement will yield significant positive consequences for Kyiv.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike killed at least three people in Gaza City, according to Palestinian health officials. The strike hit a crowded area near a bank where police were deployed. Gaza's interior ministry said the attack targeted a police patrol.

stories.title: Why the US Marine Corps wants a new anti-tank loitering munition
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps is seeking a new anti-tank loitering munition — a kamikaze-style drone — with a minimum range of approximately 15 miles. The system must be light enough for two dismounted Marines to carry on foot.

stories.title: Iranian delegation expected to arrive later tonight, Pakistani sources say
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to arrive in Islamabad with a small negotiating team for discussions. A US logistics and security team is already in the Pakistani capital, as a second round of US-Iran peace talks is anticipated.

stories.title: EU agency extends warning on flights to Mideast, including Israel, through May 1
stories.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has extended its warning on flights to the Middle East, including Israel, through May 1. The agency said it is too early to determine whether an extension of the Iran truce will lead to a sustained reduction in risk to civil aviation.

stories.title: A popular US theater is reviving a lost film by Israeli B-movie director Sam Firstenberg
stories.summary: Alamo Drafthouse theaters in five US cities will screen the 1989 action drama 'Riverbend' on April 29, directed by Israeli B-movie filmmaker Sam Firstenberg. The revival signals renewed interest in the director, whom critics have praised for his distinctive low-budget action films.

stories.title: The boatpeople basti who bothered a barrage
stories.summary: Armed police and bulldozers demolished a settlement near Taunsa Barrage in Punjab's Kot Addu district, displacing Mohana boatpeople of the River Indus from government land. The operation was carried out by the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority, with the site proposed for a Circuit House.

stories.title: China rejects US accusations over Taiwan travel disruption
stories.summary: China rejected U.S. accusations that it pressured African nations to block a planned trip by Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te, insisting its actions were legitimate diplomatic conduct.

stories.title: Inside the vortex: Why Israel keeps getting dragged into the Lebanese mud
stories.summary: Analysis explores why Israel continues to be drawn into prolonged military engagement in Lebanon. The piece examines the recurring pattern of IDF operations in Lebanese territory and the difficulty of disengagement.

stories.title: Was St. George really Palestinian?
stories.summary: An article explores the historical origins of Saint George, whose feast day is celebrated on 23 April in countries including England, Ukraine, and Ethiopia. The piece examines competing claims about where the saint actually came from, including the question of whether he was Palestinian.

stories.title: Activists break into Leicester factory owned by Israeli firm Elbit Systems
stories.summary: Activists from the group People Against Genocide broke into a factory in Leicester, England, owned by UAV Tactical Systems, a subsidiary of Israeli defense company Elbit Systems. The activists reportedly abseiled through the roof of the facility.

stories.title: Israeli police investigate after officers 'cut Palestinian flag' from skullcap
stories.summary: Israeli police launched an investigation after officers allegedly cut a Palestinian flag from the kippah of a British Israeli man in Israel. The man said he was detained after someone objected to his skullcap, which was embroidered with both Israeli and Palestinian flags.

stories.title: Police across the US worry officers are being misidentified as ICE, records show
stories.summary: Internal emails and memos obtained by the Guardian reveal that police departments across the United States are concerned that officers are being misidentified as immigration enforcement agents. Officials say the confusion, driven by the Trump administration's aggressive immigration crackdown, is interfering with police work and generating threats against officers.

stories.title: Benjamin Netanyahu reveals he was treated for early-stage cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu revealed he underwent successful prostate surgery a year and a half ago and was recently treated for a small early-stage cancerous spot found during routine monitoring. He said he delayed the disclosure to avoid giving propaganda opportunities to Iran and stated he is now in excellent condition.

stories.title: Ukraine is downing Shaheds with drones mounted on a 56-year-old An-28
stories.summary: Ukraine has adapted a 56-year-old Antonov An-28 aircraft by mounting drones on it to intercept Iranian-made Shahed drones used by Russia. The improvised approach offers a cost-effective alternative to using expensive air-to-air missiles launched from fighter jets.

stories.title: New head of UN peacekeeping force in DR Congo visits rebel-held Goma
stories.summary: James Swan, the new head of the UN peacekeeping force in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), visited rebel-held Goma. He welcomed progress on agreements concerning humanitarian access and judicial protection.

stories.title: Lebanon: 'Catastrophic' state of Israeli-occupied South
stories.summary: Jad Shahrour described conditions in Israeli-occupied southern Lebanon as "catastrophic," highlighting the humanitarian impact of the ongoing military presence in the region.

stories.title: Spain is 'reliable' Nato member, PM Sanchez says after reported US ouster threat
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez affirmed that Spain is a reliable NATO member after reports that the US Pentagon explored options to expel Spain over its refusal to support operations in the Middle East war against Iran.

stories.title: ‘Look, no hands’: China chases the driverless dream at Beijing car show
stories.summary: At the Beijing auto show, China's largest car manufacturers showcased autonomous driving technology as a major focus for future growth. With domestic EV sales slowing, Chinese automakers are investing heavily in AI-driven vehicles and expanding into overseas markets.

stories.title: DTEK: Energy workers restarted TPPs from scratch 17 times after shelling during heating season
stories.summary: Ukrainian energy company DTEK reported that its power engineers had to restart thermal power plants from scratch 17 times during the past heating season following Russian shelling attacks on energy infrastructure.

stories.title: EU to prepare blueprint for mutual assistance pact, amid NATO doubts
stories.summary: EU leaders meeting in Nicosia, Cyprus, directed officials to prepare a blueprint for activating the bloc's mutual assistance clause. The move comes amid growing doubts about US commitment to NATO and reflects European efforts to strengthen collective defense arrangements.

stories.title: US Justice Department drops criminal probe of Fed chair Jerome Powell
stories.summary: The US Justice Department announced on Friday that it has dropped its criminal probe into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The decision is expected to clear the way for the Senate confirmation of Powell's designated successor, Kevin Warsh.

stories.title: US has three aircraft carriers in the Middle East for first time since 2003
stories.summary: The US military has deployed three aircraft carriers simultaneously to the Middle East for the first time since 2003. The buildup accompanies a naval blockade on Iran's ports, with 34 vessels redirected as part of the operation amid a fragile regional truce.

stories.title: 193 Ukrainian troops freed from Russian captivity in major prisoner exchange
stories.summary: A total of 193 Ukrainian soldiers were freed from Russian captivity in a major prisoner exchange. The released troops included wounded personnel and defenders from five front-line sectors, with the United States and the United Arab Emirates serving as mediators.

stories.title: Anti-War Politician Boris Nadezhdin Eyes Run for State Duma
stories.summary: Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin announced plans to run for a seat in the State Duma. He told the newspaper Vedomosti that he would campaign on a platform of returning Russia to normal life.

stories.title: The US military wants a fleet of missile-killing laser drones
stories.summary: The U.S. military is renewing efforts to develop airborne directed energy weapons, specifically laser-equipped drones designed to intercept and destroy incoming missiles threatening American airspace.

stories.title: CENTCOM: US has redirected 34 ships in Strait of Hormuz to date
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that its forces have redirected 34 vessels in the Strait of Hormuz as part of an ongoing blockade targeting ships entering or exiting Iranian ports.

stories.title: Lockheed limbo in Lima? Firm says Peru is buying F-16s, but questions remain
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin has stated that Peru is purchasing F-16 fighter jets, but the deal's status remains uncertain. Peru's interim president indicated the agreement is on hold, while the U.S. Embassy in Lima maintains that at least part of the contract has already been signed.

stories.title: PM Sanchez rebuffs US idea of suspending Spain from NATO
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez rejected reports that the United States may seek to suspend Spain from NATO. The pushback came in response to suggestions that Washington was considering the move over Madrid's opposition to the war on Iran.

stories.title: Sanchez brushes off reported Pentagon email mulling suspending Spain's NATO membership
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declined to comment on a reported Pentagon email by policy adviser Elbridge Colby that raised the possibility of suspending Spain's NATO membership. The memo also reportedly suggested reconsidering U.S. support for the UK's Falkland Islands claim.

stories.title: Pakistan plans plastic reform but its informal recyclers hold the key
