stories.summary: Pakistan is considering plastic waste reforms, but the country's informal recycling sector—including child waste pickers in Karachi's Shireen Jinnah neighbourhood—plays a crucial and largely unrecognized role in the current recycling system.

stories.title: NRC chief: Norway should use wealth fund for aid due to oil rise
stories.summary: The head of the Norwegian Refugee Council suggested Norway should use its sovereign wealth fund to finance humanitarian aid, given rising oil revenues. Norwegian officials remain sensitive to criticism that the country profits from conflicts that drive up energy prices.

stories.title: Iran Peace Talks: Trump's unconventional diplomacy on display
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's unconventional diplomatic approach is shaping negotiations regarding an exit strategy from the Iran war. Analysts note that Trump will ultimately have the final say on any deal with Tehran.

stories.title: Lebanon under pressure to remove law boycotting Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon is facing pressure to repeal its longstanding law boycotting Israel amid US-led negotiations. The issue has become a point of diplomatic controversy during ceasefire and post-conflict discussions.

stories.title: Polish PM questions US loyalty in case of Russian attack: Report
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister publicly questioned US loyalty in the event of a Russian attack on a NATO ally. The remarks were made as EU leaders gathered in Cyprus to discuss the Middle East conflict and the alliance's next long-term budget.

stories.title: US weighs withdrawing diplomatic support for UK over Falklands
stories.summary: A leaked internal Pentagon email, confirmed by a U.S. official, revealed consideration of withdrawing American diplomatic support for the United Kingdom's claim to the Falkland Islands. The measure was reportedly part of retaliatory actions against NATO allies that did not support U.S. military operations in the war with Iran.

stories.title: Three carriers operate in Middle East for first time since 2003: CENTCOM
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command announced that three aircraft carriers — USS George H.W. Bush, USS Abraham Lincoln, and USS Gerald R. Ford — are simultaneously operating in the Middle East as part of Operation Epic Fury. This marks the first time since 2003 that three carriers have been deployed to the region concurrently.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz says no ‘immediate’ Ukraine EU membership, floats Kyiv joining meetings
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated there is no prospect of Ukraine's immediate accession to the European Union but proposed that Kyiv could participate in EU meetings without voting rights. Hungary's recent change of leadership had raised hopes for advancing Ukraine's membership bid.

stories.title: IDF orders evacuation of village in southern Lebanon after Trump announces extension of ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military ordered the evacuation of Deir Ammar in southern Lebanon after Hezbollah shot down an Israeli drone with a surface-to-air missile. The order came shortly after President Trump announced a three-week extension of the Lebanon ceasefire.

stories.title: Man claiming to be Ukrainian soldier crashes Russian university’s student recruitment call
stories.summary: A man claiming to be a Ukrainian serviceman crashed a video conference at Kuban State Agrarian University in which students were being urged to sign contracts with Russia’s Defense Ministry and go to

stories.title: Chornobyl at 40: Settlers and horses survive Russian drones, contamination
stories.summary: Forty years after the 1986 Chornobyl nuclear disaster in Ukraine, residents and researchers describe ongoing life in the exclusion zone. A radiation survivor, an elderly returnee, and a wildlife researcher detail challenges including contamination, Russian drone activity, and the presence of wild horses.

stories.title: Israeli military conducts artillery shelling and strikes in Southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military conducted artillery shelling in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli forces also carried out bombings in Al Bayyada and air strikes in Deir Aames and the Nabatieh district.

stories.title: Five games to go: The Premier League’s unpredictable season turns again
stories.summary: The English Premier League enters its final five matches with the title race still unsettled. Arsenal and Chelsea have experienced setbacks in a season marked by unpredictability, though the campaign appears to be trending toward a familiar conclusion.

stories.title: Keir Starmer suggests he will ban Iran's IRGC in 'next parliament'
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer indicated he would ban Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in the next parliament. He made the remarks during a visit to Kenton United Synagogue in London, which had been targeted in an arson attack.

stories.title: Nigeria: N1bn - Yahaya Bello Wins Defamation Suit Against Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan
stories.summary: The Kogi State High Court in Nigeria awarded former Governor Yahaya Bello N1 billion in damages in a defamation lawsuit he filed against Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, who represents the Kogi Central Senatorial District.

stories.title: Around 240 Indians claiming descent from biblical tribe arrive at Israel’s Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Approximately 240 Indians claiming descent from a biblical tribe arrived at Tel Aviv, Israel. They were welcomed by well-wishers with traditional Jewish songs and passed under a balloon arch in the colors of the Israeli flag.

stories.title: Africa: Ruto Urges Africa to Mobilise Domestic Capital, Warns Foreign Funding Delays Infrastructure Projects
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto called on African nations to mobilize domestic capital for infrastructure development, warning that dependence on foreign funding is slowing progress and undermining the continent's long-term development goals.

stories.title: Israeli army looting south Lebanon homes on 'crazy scale'
stories.summary: Israeli forces are reportedly looting homes in southern Lebanon on a large scale, according to a report. Senior Israeli military commanders and officers have allegedly failed to intervene to stop the looting.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth says US blockade on Iran 'going global'
stories.summary: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced the US blockade on Iran is expanding globally. He added that Tehran still has an opportunity to negotiate a deal with Washington.

stories.title: Tornado barrels through Oklahoma
stories.summary: A tornado struck the city of Enid in northern Oklahoma on Thursday, ripping roofs off homes and damaging power infrastructure. No fatalities were reported, but residents were trapped and extensive damage was recorded across the town of approximately 50,000 people.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Adjourns Yahaya Bello's Trial Until May 6
stories.summary: The Federal High Court in Abuja adjourned the money laundering trial of former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello until May 6 for continuation of proceedings.

stories.title: Famed Jewish conductor Michael Tilson Thomas dies at 81 of cancer
stories.summary: Renowned conductor Michael Tilson Thomas, descended from a Yiddish theater family in Los Angeles, has died at age 81 from cancer. He led symphonies around the world throughout his career, including performances in Israel.

stories.title: Pirate gangs prowl Bangladesh's Sundarbans forest
stories.summary: Pirate gangs have resurged in Bangladesh's Sundarbans mangrove forest, with their return fueled largely by poverty and debt. The armed groups, once thought subdued after mass surrenders a decade ago, again control the forest's river network and terrorize local populations.

stories.title: Netanyahu says he was successfully treated for prostate cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that he was successfully treated for early-stage prostate cancer. A malignant tumour was discovered during a routine medical checkup and was addressed in his annual medical report.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Breweries Quarterly Profit Up 26 Percent On Higher Revenue, Lower Finance Costs
stories.summary: Nigerian Breweries reported a 26 percent increase in quarterly profit, driven by a 7.7 percent rise in revenue to N413 billion. Strong sales of major brands, including Heineken lager, contributed to the growth.

stories.title: UK Palestine Action activist tells court sledgehammer attack on officer was ‘reasonable’
stories.summary: A Palestine Action activist on retrial for a 2024 raid on Israeli defense firm Elbit Systems' Bristol factory told a UK court that his sledgehammer attack on a police officer was a reasonable response. The defendant admitted the officer he struck was not actually harming anyone at the time.

stories.title: Italy forgoes $14 billion deficit spending on defense amid wobbling economy
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister announced that Italy will not pursue approximately $14 billion in deficit spending for defense, citing economic difficulties. The government is prioritizing energy costs and citizens' immediate needs over increased military investment.

stories.title: 40 years since the Chernobyl disaster
stories.summary: The 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster falls this Sunday. The UN says the 1986 accident affected more than 3.5 million people and contaminated nearly 50,000 square kilometres of land, remaining the worst nuclear disaster in history.

stories.title: DPM Dar, Iran FM exchange views on regional developments, Islamabad's diplomatic efforts in US-Iran war: FO
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar spoke by phone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi about the US-Iran ceasefire and regional developments. Dar emphasized the importance of sustained dialogue to advance regional peace. Pakistan's Foreign Office confirmed the exchange focused on Islamabad's ongoing diplomatic efforts regarding US-Iran engagement.

stories.title: Uganda: Ikon Awards Closes Submissions With a Surge in International Films
stories.summary: Uganda's iKON Awards, the country's largest film awards ceremony, closed submissions for its fourth edition with a notable increase in international film entries from across Africa and beyond.

stories.title: Changes to fire services law with tougher penalties set for public consultation
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities announced plans for a public consultation on amendments to the Fire Services Ordinance following the city's deadliest fire in decades. Proposed changes include mandatory six-monthly fire alarm inspections and tougher penalties for violations.

stories.title: Prince Harry visits Kyiv to back Ukraine and spotlight mine clearance
stories.summary: Prince Harry arrived in Kyiv on April 23, 2026, for a two-day unannounced visit to support Ukraine and draw attention to mine-clearance efforts in the country.

stories.title: Kenya: Kiambu 200-Acre Paradise Lost Land Battle Escalates As Family Claims Long-Term Ownership Since 1929
stories.summary: A family in Kiambu, Kenya, publicly defended their claim to the more than 200-acre Paradise Lost property, stating they have held possession since 1929. They accused unknown individuals of attempting to take over the land through allegedly fraudulent means.

stories.title: EU leaders discuss Iran crisis in Cyprus
stories.summary: European Union leaders meeting in Cyprus discussed the Iran crisis and pledged to intensify efforts to resolve Middle East conflicts. French President Emmanuel Macron stressed the urgency of restoring stability, as the U.S. criticized Europe for insufficient support in countering Iran.

stories.title: Milei reaffirms Falklands claim as US-Argentina alignment deepens with State Department visit
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei reaffirmed his country's sovereignty claim over the Falkland Islands during a visit to the U.S. State Department, citing "unprecedented progress." His remarks followed the leak of a Pentagon memorandum considering a review of U.S. diplomatic support for the UK's Falklands position.

stories.title: Former Nigeria striker Eneramo dies during match
stories.summary: Former Nigerian international striker Michael Eneramo, who earned 10 caps for the Super Eagles, died at age 40 after suffering a suspected cardiac arrest during a friendly match.

stories.title: Russia kills elderly couple in their home
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes on the coastal Ukrainian city of Odesa killed an elderly married couple when their home was hit early in the morning, damaging several apartment buildings. Separate drone attacks in the Kherson region killed two more people, including a 68-year-old man.

stories.title: Russia’s Central Bank Cuts Key Rate to 14.5%
stories.summary: It marks the eighth consecutive cut since borrowing costs were hiked to a two-decade high in 2024 to curb surging inflation.

stories.title: Why Are the Saudis Sitting Out the War With Iran?
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Saudi Arabia's decision to remain on the sidelines of the war with Iran may represent a missed opportunity. A more active Saudi role could strengthen Riyadh's influence and cement its position as a leading regional power.

stories.title: How Iran is wielding the Strait of Hormuz as leverage
stories.summary: Iran is leveraging its control over the Strait of Hormuz as a strategic bargaining tool amid signals from the United States about potential negotiations. Tehran is reportedly playing for time, banking on global dependence on Persian Gulf energy exports.

stories.title: Iran-Iraq Tanker War redux? Why the Strait of Hormuz crisis is different
stories.summary: Analysts are comparing the current crisis in the Strait of Hormuz to the 1980s Iran-Iraq Tanker War, which severely disrupted global shipping. However, experts note significant differences between the two situations in terms of geopolitical context and military dynamics.

stories.title: Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu says he received treatment for prostate cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed that he received radiation therapy for early-stage prostate cancer. His medical report indicated he is now in good health, and Netanyahu said he had delayed the announcement to avoid providing propaganda opportunities to Iran.

stories.title: US crackdown threat could shake out China’s ‘distillation’ AI copycats
stories.summary: The Trump administration has threatened action against Chinese AI companies accused of using 'distillation' techniques to replicate U.S. artificial intelligence models. White House science adviser Michael Kratsios warned that unauthorized distillation campaigns were enabling foreign entities, mainly in China, to produce competitive models. Analysts suggest the crackdown could eliminate weaker Chinese AI players within a year.

stories.title: Zelensky arrives in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in Saudi Arabia, where he will meet with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud.

stories.title: Lahore mother accused of killing her 3 children sent on 5-day physical remand
stories.summary: A woman in Lahore was placed on a five-day physical remand after being accused of killing her three children near Shah Jamal Colony. Police allege the murders were motivated by estrangement from her husband. The investigating officer sought the remand to recover evidence and conduct DNA and polygraph tests.

stories.title: French foreign minister Barrot voices concern about 'terrorist threat' in the Sahel
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot expressed concern about the spread of Islamist extremism in west Africa following talks with Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé. Jihadist violence that has plagued the Sahel for the past decade is now spreading into northern regions of coastal countries including Togo.

stories.title: US drops criminal probe of Fed chair Powell, likely clearing way for nominee Warsh
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department has ended its investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, according to U.S. Attorney Jeannine Pirro. The probe had focused on the Fed's building renovations and will now be handled by the Fed's inspector general. The closure removes a key obstacle to the Senate confirmation of Kevin Warsh as Powell's successor.

stories.title: Washington’s National Mall now holds 20,000 teddy bears — one for each Ukrainian child Russia abducted
stories.summary: Ukraine's ambassador to the United States placed 20,000 teddy bears on Washington's National Mall, each representing a Ukrainian child allegedly abducted by Russia. Only approximately 2,000 of those children have returned home.

stories.title: Starmer pledges to bring forward law proscribing Iran’s Revolutionary Guards
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged to introduce legislation proscribing Iran's Revolutionary Guards in the next parliamentary session in July. He made the announcement during a visit to a synagogue in north-west London, saying he wanted Britain's Jewish community to feel safe.

stories.title: Black Rain, Toxic Air and Bird Deaths: Russian Black Sea Town Reels From Refinery Strike
stories.summary: The scene in Tuapse has turned apocalyptic in recent days after strikes on a local oil refinery sparked major fires and caused an oil spill.

stories.title: Iranians bring music to sites devastated by US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Iranian musicians performed on city streets and at sites damaged by US-Israeli military strikes. The performances took place at locations across Iran that had been devastated during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister to visit Pakistan, indicating steps towards US talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is traveling to Islamabad with a delegation of officials, signaling steps toward resuming US-Iran talks. He is also expected to visit Moscow and Muscat after meeting Pakistani officials.

stories.title: Benjamin Netanyahu reveals he was treated for early-stage cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, 76, revealed he was treated for early-stage prostate cancer. He said he withheld the diagnosis to prevent Iran from using it as propaganda during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: 300-year-old Nazi-looted violin worth $10 million said to reappear in France
stories.summary: Experts believe a violin made by famed luthier Antonio Stradivari in 1719, valued at approximately $10 million, has resurfaced in France. The instrument was reportedly stolen by German soldiers from a Warsaw museum in 1944.

stories.title: Top US military official discusses ongoing blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Dan Caine provided updates on the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz during a press conference with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Caine praised the professionalism of the joint force maintaining operations against Iran.

stories.title: Burkinabé architect Francis Kere builds sustainable cultural centre in Senegal
stories.summary: Burkinabé-German architect Francis Kéré, the only African winner of the Pritzker Prize for architecture, is building a sustainable cultural centre in Senegal.

stories.title: Debris from downed drones found in two districts of Kyiv, says Klychko
stories.summary: Debris from downed Russian drones has been found in the Solomianskyi and Obolonskyi districts of Kyiv.

stories.title: Jean Lafaurie, 102 years old, still resisting
stories.summary: Jean Lafaurie, a 102-year-old French Resistance fighter and Dachau concentration camp survivor, continues to share his wartime experiences. On France's National Day of Remembrance for the Victims of Deportation, he issued a warning in defence of democracy and freedom, crediting prisoner solidarity with his survival.

stories.title: UK to end project tracking potential Israeli violations: Report
stories.summary: A UK Foreign Office unit responsible for logging potential Israeli war crimes in the Palestinian territories has been shut down amid funding cuts, according to a British newspaper report.

stories.title: PM reveals prostate cancer treatment, which he underwent without informing public
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, 76, disclosed he was treated for a malignant prostate tumour using radiation therapy. He said he withheld the diagnosis to prevent Iran from exploiting it as propaganda during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Nigeria sets up court martial over alleged 2025 coup plot
stories.summary: Nigeria has inaugurated a military court martial to try officers accused of involvement in a failed 2025 coup attempt. Authorities say the alleged plot could have ended decades of democratic governance in the country.

stories.title: US Navy authorised to target Iranian fast boats in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced that President Trump has authorized the US Navy to target Iranian fast boats operating in the Strait of Hormuz as part of the ongoing US-Iran confrontation.

stories.title: Warming El Nino set to return in mid-2026: UN
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization announced that the El Niño weather phenomenon is expected to return during the May-to-July 2026 window. Early indicators suggest it could be a strong event. The last El Niño episode pushed global temperatures to record highs.

stories.title: 'I wasn't in politics before and I'm not going to be after': Macron to quit politics in 2027
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced Thursday that he will leave politics in 2027 when his second presidential term ends. He said the most difficult challenge in his final year is balancing defense of his record with acknowledging shortcomings.

stories.title: Huawei, DeepSeek strengthen China’s AI self-reliance with collaboration on V4 model
stories.summary: Huawei announced that its newest Ascend 950PR and 950DT chips achieved immediate compatibility with DeepSeek's latest V4 AI model on the day of its release. The collaboration between the two Chinese firms highlights China's progress toward technological self-reliance amid U.S. restrictions on advanced semiconductor access.

stories.title: Papal Politics, Past and Present
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has clashed with U.S. President Donald Trump in a dispute that echoes historical tensions between the Vatican and political leaders. The confrontation reflects the Vatican's postwar tradition of peace advocacy, though past papal-political conflicts were often more dramatic.

stories.title: ‘Clear divide’ in military readiness for countries on NATO’s eastern flank: Report
stories.summary: A new report highlights a clear divide in military readiness among NATO countries on the alliance's eastern flank. The authors identified sustainment as a critical gap, citing deficiencies in maintenance capabilities and logistical limitations caused by poor transportation infrastructure in many Eastern Flank nations.

stories.title: EU could hit Israeli settlers with sanctions 'in coming days'
stories.summary: France's top diplomat indicated the European Union could impose sanctions on Israeli settlers in the coming days. The measures would respond to what the bloc considers illegal colonization of the West Bank and settler violence.

stories.title: In Odesa, injury toll from Russian attack increases to 17, with two fatalities
stories.summary: In Odesa, the number of casualties from the Russian attack has increased to 17, including 9 women and 8 men aged 18 to 83.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. in no rush but 'clock is ticking' for Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated the US is in no rush but warned that the "clock is ticking" for Iran. Trump, who on April 23, 2026, ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran, had previously ordered the US Navy to destroy any Iranian boat caught laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: “Make Iran Ungovernable” – Tracking Efforts To Destroy Iran’s Police Infrastructure
stories.summary: A Bellingcat investigation identified at least 80 police stations and law enforcement facilities, including Basij paramilitary infrastructure, damaged or destroyed during the first three weeks of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Experts said the strikes aim to degrade the Iranian regime's capacity to enforce domestic control.

stories.title: Four troops stranded without food at the front expose concealed failures – brigade commander fired
stories.summary: A Ukrainian brigade commander was fired after four troops were found stranded without food at front-line positions. The General Staff cited concealed logistics failures and lost positions in the Kupiansk sector as grounds for the dismissal.

stories.title: India-Pakistan ties 'not good', a year after Kashmir attack
stories.summary: A year after a deadly terror attack in Kashmir, India-Pakistan relations remain severely strained. Pakistan has since taken on a mediating role in efforts to end the war in Iran. Indian MP Dr Shashi Tharoor discussed India's perspective on Pakistan's peace push.

stories.title: US Secretary of War Hegseth: 'Iran will not have a nuclear weapon'
stories.summary: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth declared that Iran will not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon and announced a new phase in the conflict. He also provided updates on the US blockade of Iranian ships in the Strait of Hormuz and beyond.

stories.title: Burkinabé architect builds cultural centre in Dakar using sustainable material
stories.summary: Burkinabé-German architect Francis Kéré is constructing a cultural centre in Dakar, Senegal, using sustainable building materials. Kéré remains the only African architect to have won the Pritzker Prize, architecture's most prestigious award.

stories.title: Berlin culture minister resigns over irregular distribution of funds to fight antisemitism
stories.summary: Berlin's culture senator Sarah Wedl-Wilson resigned over the irregular distribution of €2.6 million in public funds intended for anti-antisemitism programmes. An audit found she had approved payments to groups that had not been fully vetted. She had previously dismissed a state secretary in her department over the affair.

stories.title: UEFA bans Benfica’s Prestianni for six games for verbally abusing Vinicius
stories.summary: UEFA suspended Benfica forward Matías Prestianni for six matches after finding him guilty of homophobic discriminatory conduct during a Champions League match against Real Madrid in February.

stories.title: Keir Starmer suggests he will ban Iran's IRGC in 'next parliament'
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer indicated he plans to ban Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in the next parliament. Speaking to the Jewish Chronicle, Starmer expressed concern about Iran-backed groups potentially carrying out antisemitic attacks in the UK.

stories.title: Netanyahu declared cancer-free after hiding diagnosis during Iran war
stories.summary: Netanyahu said the report was delayed for two months to avoid giving Iran an opportunity to exploit his medical condition for propaganda during the war.

stories.title: Chinese foreign minister and Thai prime minister agree to collaborate on fighting cyberscams
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister and Thai Prime Minister agreed to cooperate on combating cyberscams. China is Thailand's largest trading partner, and the two countries marked the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations last year.

stories.title: 4 tickets to World Cup final are listed on Fifa’s resale site for more than US$2 million each
stories.summary: Four tickets to the 2026 FIFA World Cup final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, were listed on FIFA's official resale marketplace for nearly $2.3 million each. FIFA does not control resale prices but charges a 15 percent fee to both buyers and sellers.

stories.title: China ramps up hunt for tax evaders, frames consumption levies as fiscal lifelines
stories.summary: Beijing is intensifying enforcement against tax evasion, with a focus on consumption taxes as a means of stabilizing local government finances hit by the property crisis. The State Taxation Administration publicized eight tax-violation cases spanning sectors including gold jewellery, alcoholic beverages, and refined oil across multiple regions.

stories.title: Why the future is fluid for middle powers in a sea of US-China rivalry
stories.summary: A leading Southeast Asian affairs scholar argues that middle powers are forming fluid coalitions to hedge against uncertainty driven by U.S.-China rivalry. Traditional U.S. allies are asserting greater autonomy, creating openings for smaller neutral states to diversify their international partnerships.

stories.title: China poised to send pandas to US before Trump’s planned visit
stories.summary: China is preparing to send giant pandas to the United States ahead of a planned visit by President Donald Trump. The panda loans are part of Beijing's longstanding diplomatic outreach known as Panda Diplomacy.

stories.title: ‘Silent suffering’: Why children in Gaza are losing their ability to speak
stories.summary: An estimated one million children in Gaza are in need of mental health support, according to reports. A growing number of children have lost the ability to speak due to severe psychological trauma caused by the conflict.

stories.title: Behind Nigeria's murky coup plot - the money, the prayers and a Nollywood arrest
stories.summary: The BBC has obtained court papers and spoken to sources close to an investigation into a coup plot in Nigeria. The documents reportedly reveal details about the plan's scope, including its financing, religious dimensions, and an arrest connected to the Nollywood entertainment industry.

stories.title: Florida officials investigate planned ‘Sloth World’ attraction after 31 sloths die in warehouse
stories.summary: Florida wildlife officials reported that 31 sloths imported from Guyana and Peru for a planned Orlando tourist attraction called 'Sloth World' died in a warehouse. An investigation found the animals perished from 'cold stun' in a facility that lacked power and running water.

stories.title: Israel launchws strikes on Lebanon in response to Hezbollah attack
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck Hezbollah targets in Lebanon in response to rocket fire on the northern border town of Shtula. The IDF stated the strikes were a direct retaliation for Hezbollah's attack.

stories.title: Japanese protest ‘frightening’ easing of decades-old arms export curbs
stories.summary: Protesters gathered in Tokyo on Friday to oppose Japan's decision to ease decades-old arms export restrictions. The new rules, announced by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government, permit the sale of lethal weapons overseas, marking a significant shift from Japan's post-war pacifist stance as it seeks to enter the global arms market.

stories.title: Israel 'prepares major assault on Gaza' amid Iran truce: report
stories.summary: Israel is reportedly preparing a major attack on the Gaza Strip amid a truce in the US-Israel war on Iran and in Lebanon

stories.title: Netanyahu says he was successfully treated for prostate cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed that he was successfully treated for early-stage prostate cancer. The 76-year-old said a malignant tumor was discovered during a routine checkup and targeted treatment removed it completely.

stories.title: Price monitoring committee claims transport fares remain unchanged
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Price Monitoring Committee, chaired by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, claimed transport fares remained unchanged and that chicken prices had returned to pre-Middle East conflict levels. However, the committee did not provide a fare breakdown despite reported sharp increases on public transport routes following recent petroleum price surges. Provincial governments have extended subsidies to goods transporters to help contain costs.

stories.title: The General Staff provides details on results of Neptune missile strike on defense facility in Taganrog
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed successful strikes by Ukrainian Neptune cruise missiles on the Atlant Aero defense facility in Taganrog, Russia.

stories.title: West Asia conflict could cause 120 bcm of LNG supply loss from 2026-2030, says International Energy Agency
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency warned that the West Asia conflict could result in 120 billion cubic metres of LNG supply losses between 2026 and 2030. LNG supply growth halted in March after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which cut combined Qatari and UAE LNG production by around 10 bcm for that month.

stories.title: Haitian PM says gang suppression force is making an impact in Port-Au-Prince
stories.summary: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé told the United Nations that security forces are gradually retaking areas of the capital, Port-au-Prince, from armed gangs. He said a gang suppression force deployed in the city is having a measurable impact.

stories.title: Indians forced to return home as Iran war rocks Gulf economy
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war has disrupted Gulf economies, forcing thousands of Indian workers in Gulf nations to leave their jobs and return to India. The mass return is now generating economic repercussions within India itself, and the future prospects of the displaced workers remain uncertain.

stories.title: A month after elections, Danish government talks remain in stalemate
stories.summary: Coalition talks in Denmark remain deadlocked one month after parliamentary elections. Caretaker Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has secured support only from left-wing parties, insufficient for a parliamentary majority, as the country works to address a diplomatic crisis with the Trump administration over Greenland.

stories.title: US Defense Secretary Hegseth: 'US blockade has gone global'
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that Operation Epic Fury, aimed at preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons, has entered a new phase. He said Iran now has an opportunity to pursue a peace deal. Hegseth confirmed the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz will be reinforced by a second aircraft carrier.

stories.title: UK position on Falklands will not change, No 10 says after leaked Pentagon memo
stories.summary: Downing Street insisted the UK's position on the Falkland Islands is 'resolute and unchanging' after a leaked Pentagon internal email proposed reassessing U.S. support for Britain's claim. The email reportedly linked the potential policy shift to Britain's lack of support for the Iran war. The UK government maintained that the defence relationship with the U.S. remains strong.

stories.title: US State Department offers $12m reward for leader of Iraqi armed group
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering a $12 million reward for information on the leader of Kataeb Sayyid al-Shuhada, an Iran-backed Iraqi armed group.

stories.title: REPLAY: Press briefing by US Defense Secretary
stories.summary: In a press briefing, U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that Operation Epic Fury has achieved decisive results in its effort to stop Iran's nuclear weapons development. He described a new phase offering Iran a chance at a peace deal and highlighted the expanding U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper dies of wounds in Lebanon
stories.summary: The UN peacekeeping mission in Lebanon confirmed that an Indonesian peacekeeper died from wounds sustained in a March 29 attack on his base. Separately, French President Emmanuel Macron, arriving at an EU summit in Cyprus, called on the European Union to intensify efforts to restore stability in the Middle East.

stories.title: Pentagon e-mail floats suspending Spain from NATO, other steps over Iran rift, source says
stories.summary: A Pentagon email reportedly proposed suspending Spain from NATO, among other measures, over disagreements related to the Iran conflict. However, the communication did not suggest that the United States would withdraw from the NATO alliance itself.

stories.title: Israel's 'peace' in Lebanon
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab commenting on Israel's actions in Lebanon during the ceasefire period.

stories.title: Israel wants peace…a piece of Lebanon
stories.summary: The New Arab/Al-Araby Al-Jadeed Cartoon of the Day by Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj.

stories.title: Africa: Strengthening Malaria Prevention Efforts in the Sahel #WorldMalariaDay
stories.summary: Malaria claimed an estimated 610,000 lives in 2024, according to the World Health Organization, with Africa accounting for 95% of global cases and deaths. Efforts are being strengthened to improve malaria prevention across the Sahel region, where children under five are disproportionately affected. The disease costs Africa approximately $12 billion annually in lost GDP.

stories.title: New Delhi criticises ‘poor taste’ Trump post calling India a ‘hellhole’
stories.summary: India's government criticized a social media post by US President Donald Trump that called the country a "hellhole" as being in poor taste. The diplomatic friction comes ahead of a planned visit to India next month by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who aims to ease recent tensions between the two nations.

stories.title: EU leaders want ‘mutual assistance pact’ plan, amid Trump’s Nato criticism
stories.summary: EU leaders have agreed to develop a blueprint for invoking the bloc's mutual assistance pact in the event of a foreign attack. The decision comes as Donald Trump's criticism of NATO intensifies, prompting European nations to explore how to collectively respond to security threats independently of the alliance.

stories.title: Pentagon’s Munitions Acceleration Council identifies 14 ‘critical’weapons for 2027
stories.summary: The Pentagon's Munitions Acceleration Council has designated 14 weapons systems as critical priorities for production by 2027. Acting Pentagon comptroller Jules "Jay" Hurst said defense contractors will be required to commit to agreed production ramp rates, with penalties imposed for failure to meet targets.

stories.title: ArianeGroup studying ballistic-missile production in Germany: Les Echos
stories.summary: French aerospace company ArianeGroup is studying the production of conventional ballistic missiles in Germany, according to Les Echos. The effort responds to growing European consensus on the need for deep-strike conventional ballistic missile capabilities amid expanding conflicts.

stories.title: 'The world bailed out the banks, no one is bailing out the children,' UNICEF says
stories.summary: UNICEF global spokesperson James Elder told FRANCE 24 that critical infrastructure relied upon by children in Lebanon has been targeted, leaving civilians with no sense of safety. He warned that humanitarian organizations including UNICEF face an existential funding crisis, lamenting the lack of international support for children compared to past financial bailouts.

stories.title: Starving soldiers of 14th Separate Mechanized Brigade: Joint Forces Task Force conducts full-scale investigation
stories.summary: Ukraine's Joint Forces Command launched a full-scale investigation into supply failures affecting soldiers of the 14th Separate Mechanized Brigade. The probe covers the entire chain of command of the 10th Army Corps following reports of starving troops at their positions.

stories.title: Inside the KKL-JNF shake-up led by its youngest chairman in decades
stories.summary: Eyal Ostrinsky, the youngest chairman of KKL-JNF in decades, took office on January 1 and has faced personal and national challenges, including the premature birth of his child and Iranian missile strikes on Israel.

stories.title: Pro-Palestinian activists break into suspected Elbit Systems drone factory
stories.summary: Pro-Palestinian activists broke into a factory in the United Kingdom that they identified as a suspected Elbit Systems facility. The activists alleged the site was manufacturing drones for Israel's military.

stories.title: Russian attack on Ukraine's Odesa kills married couple, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Odesa on April 24 killed an elderly married couple and wounded more than a dozen others, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Israel must stop pretending bond with US is 'unbreakable' before it's too late - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israeli leaders need to stop assuming the US-Israel bond is unbreakable and should create an advocacy group to better understand how Washington operates politically.

stories.title: Negotiations that enable Israel’s land-grabs
stories.summary: Since the Oslo Accords, periods of Israeli-Palestinian negotiations have coincided with continued expansion of illegal Israeli settlements and the loss of Palestinian land in the occupied territories.

stories.title: Nearly 1 in 4 Russians say they distrust Putin, highest share since start of full-scale war
stories.summary: Trust in Russian President Vladimir Putin has dropped to 71 percent, with nearly one in four Russians saying they distrust him, according to VTsIOM polling data. His approval rating fell to 65.6 percent, the lowest levels since the start of the full-scale war in Ukraine.

stories.title: US considers terror designation for Yemen’s Islah party
stories.summary: US reviews classifying Yemen’s Islah party as terrorist group, as reports cite UAE-linked lobbying and probe covering over 161 affiliated entities.

stories.title: Departments must communicate better, fire chief tells Tai Po blaze hearing
stories.summary: Hong Kong's fire services chief Andy Yeung acknowledged the need for better inter-departmental communication after an independent committee found officers took no action against possible safety breaches during renovations at Wang Fuk Court, where 168 people died in a fire.

stories.title: Death of the gatekeeper: Devil Wears Prada 2 depicts a revolution in the fashion world
stories.summary: The sequel to The Devil Wears Prada premiered in London, with an afterparty held at the National Gallery. Meryl Streep reprised her role as Miranda Priestly, a character inspired by Vogue editor Anna Wintour. The film explores how luxury fashion brands have shifted power away from once-dominant magazine editors.

stories.title: Chinese EV makers target global expansion at Auto China amid energy shock
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers are pivoting toward overseas markets amid weak domestic sales, using the Beijing Auto China show to showcase global expansion plans. Analysts note the Middle East energy crisis is acting as a catalyst for increased overseas EV deliveries.

stories.title: Cathay raises HK$2.08 billion after tapping public bond market for first time
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific Airways raised HK$2.08 billion (US$265.4 million) through its first public bond issuance in Hong Kong dollars. The three-year bonds carried a fixed interest rate of 3.78% and were sold primarily to professional investors.

stories.title: Iranian FM Araghchi to visit Pakistan in step towards US talks resumption
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is set to visit Islamabad as Pakistan hosts US-Iran talks aimed at resuming negotiations. Residents of the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi face road closures, halted courts, and economic disruption.

stories.summary: The European Union formally approved a loan to Ukraine and adopted its 20th sanctions package against Russia. Economists had warned that Ukraine could run out of funds by June without the disbursement.

stories.title: Arab, Muslim states slam Israeli raids on Jerusalem holy sites
stories.summary: Eight Islamic and Arab countries lambasted Israel for its violations targeting Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Save all living things: Europe’s 20th sanctions package still spares Russia’s nuclear war machine
stories.summary: The EU has sanctioned almost everything Moscow touches—except the one company running an occupied nuclear plant and building parts for Russian missiles.

stories.title: What’s been happening during the Lebanon ceasefire?
stories.summary: President Trump extended the Lebanon ceasefire by three weeks. However, Israel has faced accusations of using the truce period to advance its military objectives in the country.

stories.title: Pakistan repays $3.45 billion loan to UAE
stories.summary: Pakistan repaid a $3.45 billion loan to the United Arab Emirates after the UAE requested immediate return of the funds. The request came amid regional instability following the U.S.-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: US State Dept offers $10 mn reward for leader of Iraqi group
stories.summary: Al-Saraji has a seat within the Coordination Framework, the ruling Shia alliance that holds the parliamentary majority.

stories.title: Islamabad remains shut for heavy traffic amid uncertainty over U.S.-Iran talks
stories.summary: Authorities in Islamabad and Rawalpindi closed major roads and markets in VIP movement areas on April 19, 2026, restricting heavy traffic. The closures came amid uncertainty surrounding potential U.S.-Iran talks expected during the week.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Planning New POW Exchange, State Duma Lawmaker Says
stories.summary: A Russian State Duma lawmaker from United Russia said a new prisoner-of-war exchange between Russia and Ukraine is planned for Friday. The number of POWs involved was not disclosed.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Release Nearly 200 POWs Each
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine conducted a prisoner exchange involving nearly 200 POWs from each side. United Russia member Shamsail Saraliyev confirmed the swap would take place on Friday without disclosing exact numbers.

stories.title: Pentagon email floats suspending Spain from NATO, other steps over Iran rift, source says
stories.summary: A Pentagon email reportedly floated the option of suspending Spain and other countries deemed 'difficult' from important NATO positions over disagreements related to Iran. A U.S. official confirmed the existence of the email.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign minister expected in Pakistan, raising hopes for talks with US
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to travel to Islamabad, fueling optimism for a second round of US-Iran talks. Araghchi spoke by phone with Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir ahead of his arrival.

stories.title: South Africa's top envoy to Ghana summoned over attacks on foreigners
stories.summary: A Ghanaian national was confronted by South Africans in a viral clip and questioned about his immigration status.

stories.title: Firefighters extinguish blaze at Russian oil terminal after drone strikes sparked days-long fire
stories.summary: Firefighters in Krasnodar Krai have contained and extinguished the open blaze at the marine terminal in Tuapse, Russia, following days of fire sparked by drone strikes. Some 276 personnel and 77 pieces of equipment remain on scene for ongoing suppression work.

stories.title: Refugee crisis fuels measles and meningitis outbreaks in eastern Chad
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders warned that a dual outbreak of measles and meningitis is spreading across eastern Chad, fueled by overcrowded refugee camps housing people fleeing Sudan's civil war and compounded by limited healthcare access.

stories.title: China stealing US AI technology, accuses White House official
stories.summary: A White House official accused China of stealing US artificial intelligence technology, alleging that foreign entities are conducting "industrial-scale distillation campaigns" to acquire American tech. The accusation highlights growing tensions between Washington and Beijing over advanced technology competition.

stories.title: China's DeepSeek releases long-awaited new AI model
stories.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek released a new artificial intelligence model with significantly reduced costs, more than a year after its low-cost R1 reasoning model challenged U.S. competitors. The release comes amid intensifying U.S.-China rivalry over AI technology.

stories.title: Man, 32, jailed for life for rape and assault of Sikh woman in Walsall
stories.summary: John Ashby, 32, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 14 years at Birmingham Crown Court for the religiously aggravated rape and assault of a Sikh woman in Walsall. Ashby pleaded guilty to charges of rape, robbery, intentional strangulation, and religiously aggravated assault.

stories.title: Israeli demolishes civilian, heritage sites in Syria's Quneitra
stories.summary: Israeli demolitions and explosions hit civilian and heritage sites in Quneitra, raising fears of escalation in southern Syria

stories.title: U.S. says it does not object to Iran playing in World Cup but people with ties to IRGC won't be allowed
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department said it does not object to Iran's national team participating in the World Cup but indicated that individuals with ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps would be barred. President Trump stated his administration did not wish to penalize the athletes.

stories.title: Africa: Two-Thirds of Global Hunger Concentrated in 10 Conflict-Hit Countries
stories.summary: A major international report backed by UN agencies warns that two-thirds of people facing acute food insecurity globally are concentrated in just 10 conflict-affected countries, with hunger becoming increasingly entrenched in these nations.

stories.title: Chad: Algeria and Chad Cement Stategic Partnership With Raft of Bilateral Deals
stories.summary: Chad and Algeria have signed more than 30 bilateral agreements focused heavily on energy-sector economic cooperation. Chad's president described the deals as a shift from traditional friendship to a new-generation strategic partnership.

stories.title: Africa: Spat With Trump Distracts From Pope Leo's Africa Tour
stories.summary: Pope Leo visited Africa in his first trip to the continent, using the occasion to address broader global issues. However, observers noted that a public dispute with US President Trump overshadowed the visit, and many local concerns went unaddressed.

stories.title: China stages navy drill as US and Philippines embark on Balikatan 2026
stories.summary: China's People's Liberation Army Southern Theatre Command conducted naval drills in waters east of the Philippine island of Luzon, near Taiwan. The exercises appeared to be a response to the annual US-Philippines Balikatan 2026 military exercises taking place nearby.

stories.title: Two young men abducted, killed in Bannu’s Domel area
stories.summary: Two young men were abducted and killed by unidentified militants in the Domel area of Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Armed attackers opened fire on the men's vehicle when they failed to stop, killing one on the spot and fatally wounding the other.

stories.title: Syria arrests main suspect in civil war Tadamon massacre
stories.summary: Syrian authorities have arrested Amjad Yousef, the main suspect in the 2013 Tadamon massacre in Damascus.

stories.title: Thai court accepts case against 44 opposition figures over royal insult law
stories.summary: A Thai court accepted a case against 44 opposition figures charged under the country's royal insult law. The move is the latest setback for Thailand's liberal opposition, which was blocked from forming a government after winning the 2023 election.

stories.title: German man accused of live streaming child abuse in the Philippines
stories.summary: German prosecutors have charged a 46-year-old man from the Heidenheim district with serious sexual abuse of children via live streaming. He allegedly paid accomplices in the Philippines to abuse girls aged four to thirteen while he watched and directed remotely.

stories.title: China-Africa entrepreneurs summit calls for deepened cooperation
stories.summary: The inaugural China-Africa entrepreneurs summit was held at the African Union headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with participants calling for deeper economic cooperation between Chinese and African businesses.

stories.title: Kuwaiti army says border sites attacked by two drones from Iraq

stories.title: Up or down? War scrambles financial market signals
stories.summary: Global financial market signals have been disrupted by the war in the Middle East, with traditional asset correlations breaking down. Analysts warn that pre-conflict market patterns are unlikely to return within the next three to six months, complicating investor strategies.

stories.title: FSB says it foiled car bombing plot targeting leadership of Russia’s internet regulator
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service said it foiled a car bombing plot targeting senior officials at Roskomnadzor, Russia's federal internet and media regulator. The FSB announced the plot was uncovered on April 18, 2026, with details reported by the Interfax news agency.

stories.title: Tokyo workers encouraged to wear shorts to cut energy costs and keep cool
stories.summary: Tokyo metropolitan government officials are encouraging public servants to wear shorts during summer months to reduce air-conditioning use and lower electricity costs. The initiative builds on Japan's long-running Cool Biz energy-saving campaign, as officials cite rising energy costs linked to the US-Israel war on Iran and approaching summer heat.

stories.title: US mulls expelling Spain from Nato for failing to back war on Iran
stories.summary: A leaked Pentagon email suggests the US is considering measures to punish Spain for not supporting the war on Iran, potentially including expulsion from NATO. The proposed measures reportedly also include recognizing Argentine sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Balakliia; casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Balakliia in Ukraine's Kharkiv region with drones, killing one woman and wounding others.

stories.title: China to send giant pandas to Atlanta again
stories.summary: China announced plans to send giant pandas to Zoo Atlanta in the United States as part of its longstanding panda loan program. The initiative is widely regarded as a tool of Beijing's soft-power diplomacy.

stories.title: Israeli settlers cross into Syria and Lebanon calling for new settlements

stories.title: Syrian authorities arrest main suspect in 2013 Tadamon massacre
stories.summary: Ex-intelligence officer Amjad Youssef was seen shooting blindfolded civilians in a leaked video.

stories.title: FSB Shoots and Kills Man Suspected of Trying to Assassinate Roskomnadzor Officials
stories.summary: Russian authorities said the FSB shot and killed a man suspected of involvement in a plot to assassinate officials at Roskomnadzor, the country's internet regulator. Law enforcement characterized the alleged plot as a Ukrainian-orchestrated terrorist act aimed at disrupting Russia's information security.

stories.title: US charges two Chinese nationals over Myanmar crypto scam hub
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice charged two Chinese nationals in connection with a crypto scam hub operating out of Myanmar. The defendants allegedly oversaw "pig-butchering" schemes in which victims were lured into fraudulent online relationships and then defrauded of cryptocurrency.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon extend ceasefire as Trump seeks ‘best deal’ with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire while stating he was in no rush to reach a deal with Iran, seeking an "everlasting" peace agreement. The extension comes as broader US-Iran negotiations over the Middle East conflict continue without resolution.

stories.title: Middle Israel: Teach IDF soldiers harmony as fundamental Zionist value - opinion
stories.summary: IDF soldiers in Lebanon destroyed a statue of Jesus, prompting criticism. An opinion piece argued the incident reflects a broader problem and called for teaching harmony as a fundamental value within the Israeli military.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Joint Statement on the Fifth Joint Oversight Committee for the Peace Agreement Between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of Rwanda
stories.summary: The fifth Joint Oversight Committee meeting for the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda was held in Washington, DC. Participants included the US, DRC, Rwanda, Qatar, Togo as African Union mediator, and the AU Commission.

stories.title: Trump attack order highlights danger of Iran’s ‘mosquito fleet’
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the US military to target small Iranian boats deploying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting the threat posed by Iran's "mosquito fleet" of fast attack vessels. The fleet of small armed boats has been known to US officials for years, and weapons testers have regularly evaluated countermeasures against it.

stories.title: Trump turns time into a weapon as Iran war shifts to economic pressure phase
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly shifting its approach to Iran from military operations to economic pressure by extending the truce while tightening a blockade. The strategy aims to use time and economic attrition to influence Iran's decision-making.

stories.title: Amid Hormuz deadlock, Somalia 'blocks' Israel's Red Sea shipping
stories.summary: American forces receive 'shoot to kill' orders for Iranian boats in the Strait of Hormuz, while Somalia is moving to block Israeli access to the Bab al-Mandab

stories.title: US soldier allegedly bet on Maduro operation using intel
stories.summary: The US military launched strikes on Caracas on 3 January, arresting Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores and whisking them to New York

stories.title: Over 50 Central restaurants, shops join drive to boost spending, lure tourists
stories.summary: More than 50 restaurants and shops in Hong Kong's Central district have joined a "tourism everywhere" initiative organized by the Small and Medium Enterprises Association. The programme, running from May 1 through June, aims to boost local spending and attract tourists.

stories.title: Will China’s deal with Australian mining giant BHP boost yuan internationalisation?
stories.summary: Australian mining giant BHP agreed to adopt a yuan-denominated index for pricing iron ore with a major Chinese buyer, marking a breakthrough in Beijing's push for greater commodity pricing power. Analysts said the move challenges US dollar dominance but noted broader yuan internationalization efforts remain limited.

stories.title: Russia Develops ‘Anti-Aging Vaccine’ Targeting Cellular Aging
stories.summary: Russian researchers are developing what they describe as an 'anti-aging vaccine' targeting cellular aging processes. The project is part of broader efforts to expand domestic biotechnology research amid Russia's demographic decline and aging population.

stories.title: Pakistan military kills 22 in northwest clashes, child dead in crossfire
stories.summary: Pakistan's military reported that 22 militants were killed and a child died in crossfire during a joint security operation in the country's northwest. The military's media wing confirmed the operation involved an intense exchange of fire.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post published Shabbat candle lighting times for communities across Israel and the United States.

stories.title: With 3,000 containers stuck in Pakistan, Iran explores more land routes
stories.summary: Documents seen by Al Jazeera say Iran is seeking land transit for stranded sea cargo to bypass US blockade.

stories.title: Russian troops, warships in India soon? Why their new military pact matters
stories.summary: In a significant pact, India and Russia agree to the deployment of soldiers and warships on each other's soil during peace and wartime.

stories.title: Fleeing war in Sudan, refugees flock to Libya's Kufra province
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Sudanese refugees have fled the ongoing civil war between Sudan's regular army and the Rapid Support Forces, seeking shelter in Libya's southeastern Kufra province, roughly 250 kilometres from the Sudanese border. An estimated 40,000 to 60,000 Sudanese refugees now reside there, making Libya the second-largest host country after Chad.

stories.title: Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu treated for early-stage prostate cancer
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu disclosed that he underwent treatment for early-stage prostate cancer. A malignant tumour was successfully removed, and Netanyahu stated he is in excellent physical condition.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa kills 2, injures 14; residential buildings and cargo ship damaged
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Odesa on April 24 killed two people and injured 14 others, according to regional administration head Oleh Kiper. Residential buildings and a cargo ship were damaged in the strike.

stories.title: Britain should seek to rejoin EU, says civil servant who led Brexit department
stories.summary: Philip Rycroft, former permanent secretary of the UK's Department for Exiting the EU, has called for Britain to begin discussions about rejoining the European Union. Rycroft argued that Brexit's promises on economics and immigration have not been met, though he acknowledged that the process of rejoining could be lengthy and difficult.

stories.title: Iran war has drained US supplies of critical, costly weapons
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Iran conflict has significantly depleted Pentagon stockpiles of critical weapons, forcing the military to rush bombs, missiles, and other hardware to the Middle East. The drawdown highlights the strain on US defense supply chains from sustained operations in the region.

stories.title: Israeli settlers cross into Syria and Lebanon calling for new settlements
stories.summary: Groups of Israeli settlers briefly crossed into southern Syria and southern Lebanon this week, calling for the establishment of new Israeli settlements and the expansion of Israel's borders.

stories.title: Israeli forces raid town near Nablus in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces stormed and raided the town of Beit Furik, east of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, as part of nearly daily military operations in the area, according to the Wafa news agency.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper dies of wounds suffered in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Indonesian peacekeeper serving with the UN mission in Lebanon (UNIFIL) has died from wounds sustained in a March 29 attack on his base. French President Emmanuel Macron, arriving at an EU summit in Cyprus, called on the European Union to intensify efforts to help restore stability in the Middle East.

stories.title: How frustration at Cop stalemates inspires first global talks on phasing out fossil fuels
stories.summary: The world's first Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels conference opened in Santa Marta, Colombia, co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands. A coalition of 54 countries, subnational governments, and civil society groups aims to chart a path toward low-carbon energy, bypassing petrostate blockages at COP summits.

stories.title: Why are so many Colombians fighting for Ukraine?
stories.summary: A growing number of Colombian soldiers are fighting on Ukraine's front lines, drawn by comparatively high salaries and a sense of purpose. Reporters Gulliver Cragg and Catalina Gomez traveled through both Colombia and Ukraine to examine the motivations of these volunteers and the impact on their families back home.

stories.title: Tel Aviv set to choose new chief rabbi Sunday, with mayor said to favor Shas candidate
stories.summary:
After a nine year vacancy, a 64-member panel will choose a candidate, with Mayor Ron Huldai reportedly striking deal with powerful Haredi party to give his support 
The post Tel Aviv set to choose new

stories.title: Europe pushes for Lebanon-Israel role after Trump-led ceasefire
stories.summary: The Trump administration extended the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire by three weeks as Israeli violations reportedly continue. The European Union is considering a post-UNIFIL force for the region, while Lebanon has rejected proposed buffer zones.

stories.title: 22 terrorists killed in joint IBO in KP's Khyber, says military's media wing
stories.summary: Pakistan's military reported that 22 militants were killed in a joint intelligence-based operation in Khyber District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on April 21, 2026. The Inter-Services Public Relations said the militants belonged to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

stories.title: US Navy ordered to ‘shoot and kill’ alleged Iranian mine-laying boats amid ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has ordered the Navy to shoot and kill alleged Iranian mine-laying boats in the context of ongoing maritime interdiction operations. The number of intercepted vessels has been growing, and Hegseth stated the U.S. has "all the time in the world" to continue enforcement.

stories.title: Petro travels to Caracas to meet Delcy Rodríguez following failed Cúcuta summit
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro traveled to Caracas to meet Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez. The meeting marks the first official visit by a head of state since Rodríguez assumed power on January 5, following the US military capture of former president Nicolás Maduro on January 3.

stories.title: Ukraine’s new firms boom where missiles can’t reach
stories.summary: Year four of war, and Ukrainian business formation is accelerating—in sectors and cities the war can’t physically touch.

stories.title: Why China’s optical communications sector is the latest AI boom beneficiary
stories.summary: China's optical communications sector has surged amid the AI boom, with Shenzhen-listed Zhongji Innolight seeing its shares jump tenfold in the past year. Optical modules enabling ultra-fast data centre communications have created a new class of industrial companies on the mainland stock market.

stories.title: Pizzeria worker stabbed to death by teens on Independence Day after asking them not to use party spray
stories.summary:
Yemanu Binyamin Zelka, 21, dies of wounds sustained at Petah Tikvah Pizza Hut; 'Everyone loved him,' boss says; opposition MKs point finger at police under Ben Gvir
The post Pizzeria worker stabbed to

stories.title: Pentagon email floats suspending Spain from NATO over Iran rift
stories.summary: A Pentagon email has raised the possibility of suspending Spain from NATO over disagreements regarding Iran. President Trump has criticized NATO allies for not deploying their navies to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Chinese drone discovery sharpens focus on Asia’s undersea security race
stories.summary: A suspected Chinese underwater drone was recovered from Indonesian waters near the Lombok Strait, a key deepwater submarine transit route between the Pacific and Indian oceans. The discovery has intensified scrutiny of undersea surveillance competition across South and Southeast Asia. Beijing denied knowledge of the device.

stories.title: How long can Iran survive the US’s Hormuz blockade?
stories.summary: And just how long can the US hold out?

stories.title: Trump’s social media blitz divides advisers as Iran talks teeter
stories.summary: President Trump's social media messaging during Iran negotiations has divided his advisers, with officials saying his public statements are a key factor in the diplomatic impasse. The internal disagreement comes as talks between Washington and Tehran remain stalled.

stories.title: First female coach of top European men's football team faces backlash
stories.summary: Marie-Louise Eta has become the first woman to serve as head coach of a top-tier European men's football club, taking charge at Union Berlin in Germany's Bundesliga. Her historic appointment has been met with significant misogynistic backlash alongside recognition of the barrier she has broken.

stories.title: UK closes government unit tracking Israel's potential international law breaches
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has closed a government unit that had been monitoring Israel's potential breaches of international law. The closure follows the Labour government's decision to cut the overseas aid budget to 0.3 percent of gross national income.

stories.title: Africa: China's Ai Surge: What It Means for Africa's Digital Future
stories.summary: The article examines how China's state-guided AI strategy and the United States' capital-driven approach present opportunities for Africa's digital transformation. It argues Africa can draw lessons from both models to accelerate its own technological development.

stories.title: South Korean prosecutors seek 30-year jail term for ex-President Yoon in drone case
stories.summary: South Korean prosecutors have sought a 30-year prison sentence for former President Yoon Suk Yeol in a case related to a military drone incident. Yoon denies the charges, with his lawyers arguing he took no action that could provoke a military clash with North Korea.

stories.title: Number of amputees set to rise in Gaza as Israel blocks aid, NGO warns
stories.summary: Thousands of amputees cannot access care and are struggling with basic mobility.

stories.title: We had Amal Khalil by the grip of her hand
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed beneath a building struck by Israel. Her death highlights concerns about the collapse of international protections for journalists in conflict zones.

stories.title: Ukrainian soldiers left emaciated on frontline from lack of food and water
stories.summary: Ukraine's defence ministry dismissed a top military commander after photos of emaciated soldiers on the frontline surfaced on social media. The images, posted by soldier's wife Anastasiia Silchuk, showed four visibly malnourished men who had reportedly been deployed for months without adequate food or water supplies.

stories.title: Russia’s FSB tortured 9 Kherson residents for months, fabricated terrorism case against them; 1 died in custody
stories.summary: Nine residents of Kherson were detained by Russia's FSB in the summer of 2022 during the Russian occupation and charged with plotting assassinations of collaborationist officials. The defendants were reportedly tortured for months, one died in custody, and a Russian court sentenced the rest to 14 to 20 years in prison in January 2026.

stories.title: EU: War on Iran has negatively impacted European economy
stories.summary: EU Commissioner for Economy Valdis Dombrovskis said the US-Israel war on Iran has reduced the European Union's economic output by 0.2 to 0.6 percent. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and surging fuel prices are costing the EU approximately $584 million daily.

stories.title: Amjad Youssef, key suspect in Syria’s Tadamon massacre, detained
stories.summary: Amjad Youssef, accused of involvement in the Tadamon mass executions during the Syrian civil war, has been arrested following a security operation in Hama province, Syria.

stories.title: Amjad Youssef, key perpetrator of Tadamon massacre, arrested in Syria
stories.summary: Syrian authorities have detained Amjad Youssef, one of the main perpetrators of the April 2013 Tadamon massacre in Damascus. Leaked footage had previously shown Youssef shooting blindfolded detainees during the mass killings.

stories.title: US considers suspending Spain from NATO, reported internal email suggests
stories.summary: Pentagon email obtained by Reuters reveals US anger at Spain and the UK as Iran war tensions persist.

stories.title: Polish PM questions US loyalty in case of Russian attack, warns EU must be 'real alliance' - FT
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk questioned US reliability in the event of a Russian attack and urged the EU to become a 'real alliance.' He spoke at an informal EU summit in Cyprus where leaders also discussed the Middle East war, energy measures, and the bloc's long-term budget.

stories.title: Trump administration may expand refugee programme for white South Africans
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering expanding a refugee programme for white South Africans. The US president has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims of genocide against minority white Afrikaners in South Africa.

stories.title: Human Rights Watch calls on Lebanon to join International Criminal Court after Israeli forces kill journalist
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch has called on Lebanon to join the International Criminal Court's Rome Statute following the killing of Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil by Israeli forces. The organization urged a credible investigation into her death.

stories.title: Debris from downed drone falls in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district
stories.summary: Debris from a Russian drone intercepted over Kyiv fell in the Solomianskyi district, landing on a non-residential property and into a nearby body of water. No casualties were reported.

stories.title: China plans to invest billions on a robot army to run its power grid
stories.summary: China's State Grid Corporation has earmarked 6.8 billion yuan (US$1 billion) to deploy thousands of AI-powered robots across its power grid infrastructure. The robots will handle tasks ranging from inspecting remote substations to performing maintenance on ultra-high-voltage power lines.

stories.title: Michigan community ‘seeks answers’ to death of Chinese semiconductor researcher Wang Danhao
stories.summary: Community members and activists held a vigil at the University of Michigan for Wang Danhao, a Chinese semiconductor researcher who died by suicide after being questioned by US federal agents. About 30 people attended the event organized by peace advocacy group Code Pink, marking one month since his death.

stories.title: Explosions by Israeli forces in south Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Smoke rise above Khiam in southern Lebanon after Israel carries out explosions despite the ceasefire.

stories.title: US, Israel 'plan huge assault on Iran' as ceasefire hopes falter
stories.summary: The US military is reportedly preparing plans to destroy Iran's civilian infrastructure, while Israel has threatened to return the country "back to the Stone Age." The developments come as ceasefire hopes between the parties have faltered.

stories.title: Bill to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales set to fail
stories.summary: A bill to legalize assisted dying in England and Wales is expected to fail in Parliament. Supporters of the legislation have accused opponents in the House of Lords of deliberately blocking the measure from becoming law.

stories.title: Counterrevolution in Egypt: How Sisi broke the dream of a new republic
stories.summary: Egyptian writer Hossam el-Hamalawy has published a new book examining how the collapse of the Mubarak government in Egypt gave way to a new form of dictatorship under President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.

stories.title: Paris reportedly offers Athens a deal — 43 Greek Mirage 2000 jets for Ukraine, discounted Rafales in return
stories.summary: France has reportedly proposed that Greece transfer 43 Mirage 2000 fighter jets and spare parts to Ukraine in exchange for a discounted purchase of French-made Rafale aircraft, according to Le Figaro.

stories.title: Liberia: Press Union Warns of Shrinking Democratic Space
stories.summary: The Press Union of Liberia has warned that democratic norms and freedom of expression are being eroded under President Joseph Boakai's administration. The organization cautioned that recent developments risk undermining Liberia's democratic progress.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Chernobyl ‘liquidators’ return 40 years after disaster
stories.summary: Ukraine marked the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster in April 2026. Former clean-up workers, known as 'liquidators,' returned to the site for the commemoration.

stories.title: Border with Russia becomes front line, and enemy continues its assault, says Demchenko
stories.summary: Ukrainian State Border Guard Service spokesperson Demchenko stated that Ukraine's border with Russia has effectively become a front line, with active fighting and intense shelling involving aircraft, artillery, and drones ongoing along the border area.

stories.title: US soldier bet on Maduro capture on Polymarket
stories.summary: A U.S. Special Forces soldier involved in the operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro has been charged with wire fraud and other crimes. Prosecutors allege he used classified information about the mission to place bets on the prediction platform Polymarket, earning over $400,000.

stories.title: DoJ watchdog will investigate release of Epstein files – US politics live
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice's internal watchdog will investigate the agency's handling of records related to Jeffrey Epstein, including whether relevant documents were properly redacted. Separately, the Trump administration announced efforts to crack down on foreign exploitation of U.S. artificial intelligence models, singling out China.

stories.title: Key suspect in notorious Tadamon massacre during Syria civil war arrested
stories.summary: Amjad Youssef, a key suspect in the April 2013 Tadamon massacre in Damascus, has been arrested. He was wanted for his role in the mass killing of blindfolded civilians during the Syrian civil war.

stories.title: Liberia: Court Tosses Prosecution's Bail Challenge, Orders Samuel Jackson's Property Returned
stories.summary: Liberia's Criminal Court 'C' dismissed the prosecution's challenge to Samuel P. Jackson's bail bond, ruling that prosecutors missed the mandatory legal deadline to contest it. The court also ordered the return of personal property seized from Jackson's residence, deeming the continued confiscation unjustified.

stories.title: After losing her son, healthy British woman will legally end her life in Swiss clinic
stories.summary: A physically healthy British woman plans to end her life through euthanasia at a Swiss clinic following the loss of her son. The case has divided press opinion. Separately, a key oil pipeline from Russia to Germany has been suspended, with Russia citing technical reasons and German media suggesting political motivations.

stories.title: ‘It’s a tightrope’: why Europe faces a China dilemma over its wind power drive
stories.summary: At a wind energy expo in Madrid, European industry participants discussed the continent's push for energy security amid the US-Israel war on Iran. No Chinese companies operated exhibition booths, though Chinese participants networked from the sidelines. Analysts note Europe faces a dilemma over its reliance on Chinese supply chains for wind power development.
