stories.title: Liberia: UN Rights Office Warns Liberia's Anti-Corruption Drive Is Falling Short
stories.summary: The United Nations human rights office has warned that Liberia's anti-corruption efforts are falling short. The assessment, published in April 2026, highlights concerns about the effectiveness of the country's anti-corruption drive.

stories.title: Philippines' ex-president Duterte to face ICC trial for crimes against humanity
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court has confirmed charges of crimes against humanity against former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte for dozens of alleged extrajudicial killings. He will stand trial at The Hague.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Military Inaugurates General Court-Martial, Begins Trial of Coup Suspects
stories.summary: Nigeria's military has inaugurated a General Court-Martial to begin trying more than 30 officers accused of plotting a coup. The suspects were transported to the trial venue in a luxury bus. The proceedings follow detentions linked to an alleged coup plot against President Tinubu.

stories.title: NATO eyes Swedish-Canadian jet for AWACS role in shift away from Boeing
stories.summary: NATO is considering the Saab-Bombardier GlobalEye as a replacement for its Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft, marking a potential shift away from Boeing platforms. Political momentum behind the Swedish-Canadian jet for the AWACS surveillance role has been building among alliance members.

stories.title: Russians attack civilians with drones in Kherson region, two dead, three wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted drone attacks on civilians in Ukraine's Kherson region, killing two people riding a moped in a suburb of Kherson and wounding three others. The attacks have continued throughout the day.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister and Pakistani officials discuss ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held phone calls with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Field Marshal Asim Munir on Friday. The officials discussed developments related to ceasefire efforts, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency.

stories.title: Trump rules out striking Iran with nuclear weapon
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated he would not use nuclear weapons against Iran. This followed an earlier threat in which Trump warned that 'a whole civilisation will die tonight, never to be brought back,' before a ceasefire was reached.

stories.title: Ukrainian P1-Sun drones down 3,000-plus Shaheds in 2026 — at about $3,000 a piece
stories.summary: Ukrainian P1-Sun interceptor drones manufactured by Skyfall have shot down over 3,000 Russian Shahed drones in 2026 at a cost of approximately $3,000 per interception, according to Defense Ministry adviser Hanna Hvozdiar.

stories.title: Nato says 'no provision' to expel members after report US could seek to suspend Spain
stories.summary: An internal Pentagon email reportedly outlines options to punish allies over a perceived lack of support for Iran war.

stories.title: Trump administration may expand refugees programme for white South Africans
stories.summary: The Trump administration is considering expanding a refugee program for white South Africans. President Trump has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims of genocide being carried out against minority white Afrikaners.

stories.title: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei ‘gravely wounded’: NYT
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Iran's new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father, has been gravely wounded. Khamenei has not appeared in public since assuming the role and has communicated only through written statements. His absence has fueled speculation about his condition and whether he remains alive.

stories.title: Two injured in Mykolaiv region following Russian drone attack
stories.summary: Two people were injured in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region following a Russian attack using Shahed-type drones.

stories.title: First Bnei Menashe flight lands as Israel launches operation to complete community’s Aliyah
stories.summary: A flight carrying 240 immigrants from the Bnei Menashe community in northeastern India landed in Israel as part of the "Wings of Dawn" initiative. The operation aims to complete the community's Aliyah, with thousands more expected to arrive by 2030.

stories.title: Pentagon email floats suspending Spain from NATO, 'punishing' other allies over Iran war conduct
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez responded to reports of an internal Pentagon email discussing Spain's possible suspension from NATO over its conduct regarding the Iran war, stating that Spain acts on official documents and positions, not emails.

stories.title: After Meloni’s law change, Americans hope Italian supreme court ruling will open door to citizenship
stories.summary: Americans seeking Italian citizenship through distant ancestry face new obstacles after Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government enacted a law blocking such claims. The Italian supreme court is expected to issue a ruling that applicants hope will reopen the pathway. The law change also affects children of immigrants born in Italy.

stories.title: US gambling addiction is ‘out of control’ as betting markets boom, policy expert warns
stories.summary: A leading policy expert has warned that gambling addiction in the United States is spiraling "out of control" amid the rapid expansion of online gambling, prediction markets, and sports betting platforms. Harry Levant of the Public Health Advocacy Institute called for regulation comparable to that of alcohol or tobacco. Experts from around the world are set to gather in Boston to push for stricter industry oversight.

stories.title: Warner Bros.-Paramount deal advances
stories.summary: Paramount Skydance shareholders approved a buyout of Warner Bros. at $31 per share, advancing a potential merger of two major entertainment groups. Regulatory review is still required. The deal has faced opposition, particularly from Hollywood figures concerned about its impact on media plurality.

stories.title: Iran war shows ‘strategic value’ of AI for China’s military, PLA Daily says
stories.summary: China's official military newspaper, PLA Daily, urged the People's Liberation Army to accelerate AI integration, citing the US-Israeli campaign against Iran as evidence of a turning point in AI-driven warfare. The commentary highlighted that the Middle East conflict marked the first time AI was integrated across the full cycle of military operations, from intelligence analysis to target identification.

stories.title: Chinese girl insists on remaining by grandparents’ tombs; her nearby vigil moves many
stories.summary: A young girl in Liupanshui, Guizhou province in southwest China, refused to leave the tombs of her grandparents, who died within six months of each other. A viral video showed her lying in front of a tomb and occasionally eating cake. Her parents' efforts to persuade her to leave were unsuccessful.

stories.title: Australia awards contracts for counter-drone tech based on lasers, interceptors
stories.summary: Australia has awarded contracts for counter-drone technologies based on laser and interceptor systems. Both products are intended to be integrated into the Army's Land 156 command-and-control system designed to counter unmanned aerial threats.

stories.title: Hormuz standoff chokes 20% of oil supply
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are engaged in a tense standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 20% of global oil supply passes. Washington has emphasized ship seizures to demonstrate its ability to disrupt maritime traffic, while both sides contest control over demining and securing the waterway.

stories.title: Sleep loss, family worries, paperwork: the real top complaints in Ukrainian military therapy
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Ground Forces reported that over 70 percent of soldiers' consultations with military psychologists address fatigue, sleep loss, family concerns, and administrative issues rather than deep psychological trauma.

stories.title: Israeli military destroys houses in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military demolished houses in the town of Khiam in southern Lebanon, according to reports. The destruction occurred despite the announcement of a three-week extension to the Lebanon ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: In El Salvador, shackled prisoners watch their mass trial on a big screen
stories.summary: In El Salvador, more than one hundred alleged gang members sat shackled inside a mega prison watching their mass trial proceedings on a large screen. The defendants, with cuffed wrists and shackled ankles, viewed the court session that will determine their collective fate in San Salvador.

stories.title: Trump orders navy to shoot Iranian boats
stories.summary: President Donald Trump ordered the U.S. Navy to target Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating the military standoff between Washington and Tehran. Israel has also signaled readiness to resume bombing once it receives authorization from the United States. The situation appears to be moving closer to renewed conflict rather than a peace deal.

stories.title: Digested week:Iranian embassy trolls the most ‘powerfool’ man on the planet | Emma Brockes
stories.summary: Iran's diplomatic missions drew attention this week by publicly mocking U.S. President Donald Trump on social media amid the ongoing international crisis. The Iranian embassy's posts were noted for maintaining diplomatic decorum while poking fun at the American president.

stories.title: Americans don’t want Iranians killed. As long as they’re hipsters
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that American public sympathy for Iranian civilians has been shaped by viral images portraying Iranians as culturally familiar. The analysis draws parallels to how coverage of Ukrainian refugees similarly reflected selective empathy based on perceived similarity.

stories.title: Is Indonesia’s blasphemy law for religious protection or political purpose?
stories.summary: Indonesia's blasphemy law faces renewed scrutiny after former Vice-President Jusuf Kalla was reported to police over remarks linking past Muslim-Christian conflicts to beliefs about martyrdom. The complaint was filed by Christian complainants against one of Indonesia's most senior Muslim figures. Critics argue the case illustrates the law's vulnerability to politicized use.

stories.title: Syria arrests suspected leader of Tadamon massacre
stories.summary: Syrian security forces arrested Amjad Youssef, a former regime official suspected of leading the Tadamon massacre of an estimated 288 civilians under Bashar al-Assad's rule. He was captured in the countryside approximately 30 miles outside the city of Hama. Syria's interior ministry confirmed the arrest followed a carefully executed security operation.

stories.title: Klimkin: Most difficult EU accession negotiations to be with our neighbors
stories.summary: Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Pavlo Klimkin predicted that Ukraine's most difficult EU accession negotiations will be with its neighboring countries rather than other EU member states.

stories.title: Kremlin builds “hotbed of tension” narrative against Lithuania — ISW warns of groundwork for Baltic aggression
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reports that Moscow is using accusations against Lithuania and NATO regarding Kaliningrad Oblast to build a narrative justifying potential future military action against the Baltic states.

stories.title: Mass trial of MS-13 gang at CECOT prison
stories.summary: El Salvador has begun a mass trial of 486 alleged MS-13 gang members at the CECOT mega-prison, with prosecutors accusing them of thousands of murders and other crimes. The proceedings are part of President Nayib Bukele's crackdown under a state of emergency declared in 2022. Human rights organizations have raised concerns about due process violations, reports of torture, and over 500 prison deaths.

stories.title: Jewish Democrat Josh Shapiro tests political muscle in Pennsylvania’s midterms
stories.summary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, a moderate pro-Israel Jewish Democrat widely seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, is using the state's midterm elections to demonstrate his political strength in the key swing state.

stories.title: Israeli forces attack displacement center and shoot child in Beit Lahia, Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces attacked a displacement center in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza, with live ammunition on Friday, according to the Wafa news agency. A child was shot and wounded, and several others were injured by gunfire and shelling. Israeli forces also shelled areas near Gaza City and Khan Younis.

stories.title: Pakistan repays $3.45bn to UAE, confirms central bank
stories.summary: Pakistan's State Bank confirmed the country repaid $3.45 billion in deposits to the United Arab Emirates, with $1 billion going to the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development on April 23 and $2.45 billion repaid the previous week. The repayment was completed before the end-of-month deadline.

stories.title: Tanzania vows constitutional reform following post-election bloodshed
stories.summary: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan has pledged constitutional reform following post-election violence last year that left hundreds dead.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson slams ‘repulsive’ campaign against country club that barred Jewish toddler
stories.summary: Far-right commentator Tucker Carlson criticized the public backlash against a country club that reportedly barred a Jewish toddler. The segment included what observers described as coded references to Jews and discussions about inclusion initiatives.

stories.title: Liberia: Senate Passes Controversial U.S.$53 Million Supplementary Budget
stories.summary: The Liberian Senate passed a controversial US$53 million supplementary budget. Senator Dillon walked out of the session, citing procedural concerns about the process.

stories.title: Fuel crisis puts education of children with special needs at risk
stories.summary: In Karachi, children with special needs face disrupted access to education due to an ongoing fuel crisis. The article highlights Gul-e-Haya, a child from Hyderabad born with a congenital amputation, whose father struggles on minimum wage to provide specialized schooling. The fuel shortage is compounding transportation barriers for vulnerable families.

stories.title: China's Xpeng expects to start full-scale delivery of 'flying' cars in 2027
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle maker Xpeng announced it expects to begin full-scale delivery of its flying car products by 2027. The company also noted significant potential to deepen its cooperation with German automaker Volkswagen, which recently began mass-producing an EV model co-developed with Xpeng.

stories.title: Ex-SSP’s son booked for firing on FBR official in Karachi
stories.summary: In Karachi's Clifton area, Agha Sher, the son of former SSP Agha Asghar, was booked for allegedly shooting and injuring FBR inspector Shah Mir Lashari following a road accident. The suspect and an associate also reportedly assaulted the officer and his brother.

stories.title: Nigeria: 36 Serving Military Officers to Be Arraigned for Coup Plot Against President Tinubu
stories.summary: Thirty-six serving Nigerian military officers are set to be arraigned for allegedly plotting a coup against President Bola Tinubu. The officers are part of a larger group detained since 2025 in connection with the alleged plot, which was previously reported by Premium Times.

stories.title: Businessman shot dead in Carmel forest, police suspect criminal motive
stories.summary: A 58-year-old businessman was found shot dead in Israel's Carmel forest near Daliyat al-Carmel. Police suspect a criminal motive, noting the victim had been targeted in previous attempts on his life.

stories.title: ‘New’ Islamabad
stories.summary: Islamabad is undergoing plans for major urban redevelopment that could dramatically alter the city's character. Officials envision transforming the capital to resemble a mix of Manhattan and Shanghai while retaining the Margalla Hills' scenery. Critics warn the changes threaten to make the city more elitist and environmentally degraded.

stories.title: Environmental crisis in Russian city after drone attack on refinery
stories.summary: Residents of Tuapse, Russia, are raising concerns about environmental contamination following a fire at an oil refinery caused by a Ukrainian drone attack on the city.

stories.title: Trump says Lebanon ceasefire extended as Israel continues strikes
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the ceasefire in Lebanon following White House talks with Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors. The announcement came after Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed seven people, including a journalist, on the same day.

stories.title: A case for smaller provinces
stories.summary: The article discusses the case for creating smaller provinces in Pakistan to improve governance and administrative efficiency. It argues that the debate is often framed around ethnicity and political identity, which diverts from the core issue of governance failure. The piece points to India's experience of expanding its number of states as a model.

stories.title: 'A dangerous standoff' as Strait of Hormuz blockade continues
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are maintaining rival blockades of the Strait of Hormuz, creating what has been described as a dangerous test of wills between the two countries.

stories.title: Consequences of Russia’s strike on Odesa: Married couple killed; houses and merchant ship hit
stories.summary: A Russian nighttime strike on Odesa killed a married couple and damaged residential neighborhoods and a merchant ship in the port.

stories.title: US slaps sanctions on Cambodian senator suspected of controlling scam centres
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed sanctions on Cambodian Senator Kok An, a tycoon with ties to former leader Hun Sen, along with 28 associates, alleging they control scam compounds. Cambodia faces growing international pressure, including from China, to dismantle a cybercrime industry estimated at nearly US$20 billion annually.

stories.title: Russian diplomats denounce new EU sanctions, claim they are 'meaningless' without UN decision
stories.summary: Russian diplomats at Russia's mission to the European Union denounced newly imposed EU sanctions, calling them meaningless without a corresponding UN Security Council decision. The statement was reported by Russian news agencies.

stories.title: Iran, US to visit Islamabad with hopes of news US truce talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister and US envoys are scheduled to travel to Islamabad, Pakistan, on Saturday for a second round of ceasefire talks. The meeting follows earlier negotiations aimed at de-escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Iran FM to visit Islamabad with hopes of news US truce talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is set to visit Islamabad amid hopes of renewed US-Iran truce talks. The standoff between Washington and Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz blockade continues despite claims from President Trump about seeking a deal.

stories.title: Trump says wants 'best deal', Iran denies fractured leadership
stories.summary: President Trump expressed interest in reaching a deal with Iran, while Tehran denied claims that its leadership is fractured. The standoff between the US and Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz continues.

stories.title: HK Electric to cut May fuel charges, but warns of sharp future increase
stories.summary: HK Electric, one of Hong Kong's two electricity suppliers, announced a cut in fuel surcharges for May, reducing them by 4.4 HK cents per kilowatt-hour to 26 HK cents. However, the company warned that costs could rise significantly later in the year due to the Middle East conflict's impact on fuel prices.

stories.title: German prosecutors charge Ukrainian and Latvian with “agent activity for sabotage purposes”
stories.summary: German prosecutors charged a Ukrainian and a Latvian national with espionage-related sabotage after Bavarian police arrested them during a routine traffic stop on the A6 highway on April 12. Authorities seized a drone, GPS trackers, radios, and forged identification documents.

stories.title: Nepal: Mount Everest ice block obstructs large group of spring climbers
stories.summary: A large block of ice suspended above the Khumbu Icefall near Camp One on Mount Everest is blocking the route for spring climbers. The obstruction is too dangerous for either climbers or the specialist 'icefall doctors' who normally clear the path.

stories.title: Trump ally visits China, DeepSeek releases V4, EV earnings
stories.summary: US Senator Steve Daines, a Trump ally, will lead a bipartisan five-member Congressional delegation to Beijing and Shanghai starting May 1. The visit precedes a planned trip to China by President Donald Trump. Separately, Chinese AI company DeepSeek released its V4 model.

stories.title: India denounces ‘hellhole’ remark shared by Trump
stories.summary: India's Foreign Ministry rejected comments by US radio host Michael Savage, which were shared by President Donald Trump, calling them 'uninformed.' The remarks reportedly described India in derogatory terms, prompting an official diplomatic response from New Delhi.

stories.title: US justice department blocking Met police investigation into Mandelson, reports say – UK politics live
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice has reportedly refused to hand over key evidence from the Jeffrey Epstein files to London's Metropolitan Police. The refusal could delay Scotland Yard's criminal investigation into Peter Mandelson, a former UK business secretary and US ambassador.

stories.title: Ad astra
stories.summary: Two Pakistani candidates, Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, have been selected for China's manned space programme after completing multiple selection rounds. They will travel to China to begin training, with one eventually joining a Chinese mission as a payload specialist. The selectee would become the first foreign astronaut aboard China's space station.

stories.title: Global hunger report warns of rising malnutrition and famine risks
stories.summary: A global hunger report identified conflict as the leading driver of acute food insecurity, with nearly 150 million people worldwide facing severe food shortages. The report warned of rising malnutrition and increasing famine risks across conflict-affected regions.

stories.title: 107 Shaheds, 2 ballistic missiles. Russia’s overnight strike kills two in Odesa, hits a ship heading for port
stories.summary: Russia launched 107 Shahed drones and two ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight, killing two people and injuring 14 in the Odesa region. A civilian cargo vessel was struck, and energy infrastructure was hit across five oblasts, causing power outages.

stories.title: War update: 194 frontline clashes over past day, heavy fighting in Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 194 combat engagements with Russian troops on April 23. The heaviest fighting occurred in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors of the front line.

stories.title: Why is there a political deadlock in Lebanon?
stories.summary: Lebanon's government is seeking to compel Hezbollah to disarm as part of efforts to establish a state monopoly on weapons. The dispute over Hezbollah's armed status remains a central factor in the country's ongoing political deadlock.

stories.title: Trump keeps talking about Iran’s ‘nuclear dust’. What is it?
stories.summary: President Trump has repeatedly referenced Iran's "nuclear dust," a volatile and highly toxic substance capable of triggering a nuclear reaction. The term has featured in his public remarks amid ongoing tensions with Tehran.

stories.title: Eye on Africa: Fally Ipupa marks 20 years of career
stories.summary: Congolese music star Fally Ipupa is celebrating 20 years in the music industry with new albums and major concerts in Paris. He is recognized for modernizing Congolese rumba by blending it with R&B, pop, and urban sounds since his early career in Kinshasa.

stories.title: US soldier allegedly bet on Maduro operation using intel
stories.summary: US Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke, 38, of Fayetteville, North Carolina, has been charged with using classified information to place bets on the online prediction platform Polymarket. He allegedly earned over $400,000 by wagering on outcomes related to a US military operation targeting former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro in Caracas, an operation he helped plan.

stories.title: Eye on Africa: Migrants deported from US stuck in DRC
stories.summary: Fifteen migrants from Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru were deported from the United States and flown to the Democratic Republic of Congo. The deportees told AFP they endured a 27-hour flight in handcuffs and shackles before arriving in the DRC.

stories.title: Runway safety system did not activate before fatal Air Canada Express collision at LaGuardia: Report
stories.summary: A runway safety system failed to activate before a fatal collision involving an Air Canada Express aircraft at LaGuardia Airport in New York. Two pilots were killed and 39 people were hospitalized following the crash.

stories.title: Eye on Africa: Tanzania poll violence report
stories.summary: Tanzania's commission of inquiry into electoral violence released its report, acknowledging that hundreds of demonstrators were killed following the presidential election. The inquiry was commissioned by President Samia Suluhu, who was re-elected with 97.66% of the vote, but the opposition has rejected the report's findings.

stories.title: Stuffed toys in US capital symbolise displaced Ukrainian children
stories.summary: An installation of stuffed toys was displayed in Washington, D.C., to symbolize Ukrainian children reportedly forcibly relocated to Russia since the 2022 invasion. The display aimed to draw attention to the displacement of scores of Ukrainian minors.

stories.title: Gallup survey shows dip in private sector confidence in 2026
stories.summary: A Gallup Pakistan survey released in April 2026 shows a sharp decline in private sector confidence during the first quarter of the year. Based on responses from 510 businesses nationwide, the survey found broad deterioration across current performance, future expectations, and perceptions of national direction. Rising energy costs and regional geopolitical tensions were cited as key factors.

stories.title: Henderson’s winning bid to run harbour event space could boost Central’s access
stories.summary: Henderson Land Development, in a joint venture with concert organiser YW Company, won a tender to operate a 3.7-hectare harbourfront event space in Hong Kong's Central district. Experts say the arrangement could improve public accessibility and attract more visitors from surrounding commercial properties.

stories.title: Trump says Lebanon ceasefire extended as Israel continues strikes
stories.summary: President Trump announced a three-week extension of the Lebanon ceasefire after talks in Washington with Israeli and Lebanese envoys. Despite the extension, Israeli bombardment and fighting in southern Lebanon persisted, with strikes reported in areas including Bint Jbeil district.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon extend ceasefire as Iran peace talks stall
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire by three weeks, as announced by President Donald Trump during a meeting with ambassadors from both countries in Washington. The extension comes despite recent Israeli strikes in Lebanon and Hezbollah rocket fire. Separate US-Iran negotiations aimed at ending the broader Middle East conflict remain at a standstill.

stories.title: Food supply problems: Investigation launched in 14th Brigade, commander removed
stories.summary: Ukraine's Land Forces launched an investigation into food supply problems in the 14th Separate Mechanized Brigade. The brigade's commander was removed from his post, and the commander of the 10th Army Corps was dismissed and demoted.

stories.title: Baby twins attend their father’s funeral after Israeli settler attack
stories.summary: Palestinians in the occupied West Bank held a funeral for a 25-year-old father of twins who was shot and killed by Israeli settlers. His infant twin children were present at the burial ceremony.

stories.title: Israel’s Greatest Paradox with Micah Goodman - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Author Micah Goodman and host Noam discussed what they described as Israel's combination of radical individualism and fierce collectivism as a strategic asset. The conversation was presented as sponsored content.

stories.title: The Iran war is brewing a food crisis we must avert
stories.summary: An opinion piece warns that the US war on Iran, now approaching its third month, is threatening global food security as the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked. The closure has disrupted critical commodity flows, potentially putting millions worldwide at risk of food shortages.

stories.title: Pope Leo departs Equatorial Guinea after wrapping up 11-day trip to Africa
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV concluded an 11-day tour of Africa with an open-air mass in Equatorial Guinea attended by tens of thousands. The trip, his first major international journey, had been overshadowed by criticism from US President Donald Trump regarding the Pope's stance on Iran.

stories.title: Far-left author Peter Beinart’s ‘Being Jewish After the Destruction of Gaza’ wins PEN award
stories.summary: Author Peter Beinart won a PEN America Literary Award for nonfiction for his book 'Being Jewish After the Destruction of Gaza.' Beinart, who opposes Jewish statehood and has accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza, was recognized by the literary organization.

stories.title: South Korea police arrest man for posting AI photo of runaway wolf
stories.summary: South Korean police arrested a man for posting an AI-generated image of a runaway wolf. The fabricated photo had been widely circulated and prompted authorities to redirect their search operation based on the false information.

stories.title: US planning renewed military action against Iranian infrastructure should talks fail - CNN
stories.summary: CNN reported that the US is planning potential renewed military strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure should ceasefire talks fail. The option remains on the table as leverage to pressure Tehran into agreeing to a deal, consistent with earlier threats from President Trump.

stories.title: 11 granted bail in protest case
stories.summary: An Anti-Terrorism Court in Islamabad granted post-arrest bail to 11 suspects detained in connection with protests over the death of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Judge Abual Hasanat Mohammad Zulqarnain approved the bail applications and ordered the accused released against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each.

stories.title: Warner Bros. takeover by Paramount
stories.summary: Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders approved an $81 billion sale to Paramount, bringing properties including HBO Max, Harry Potter, and CNN under Paramount's umbrella. The deal still requires regulatory approval and has drawn criticism over potential effects on media plurality.

stories.title: Lebanon - Israel: Truce extended by three weeks
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire by three weeks following a meeting at the White House. Despite the extension, fighting continues as Hezbollah, which was not party to the talks, has launched rockets and drones while Israeli forces maintain operations in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills five in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday. In a separate incident in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, a 15-year-old was shot and killed by Israeli soldiers during a military raid, according to Palestinian health officials.

stories.title: In lead-up to Trump’s Beijing visit, China announces 2 pandas are headed to US zoo
stories.summary: China announced it will send two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, to Zoo Atlanta under a 10-year conservation agreement. The gesture comes weeks before US President Donald Trump's planned visit to Beijing, amid ongoing trade and security tensions between the two countries.

stories.title: Trump kill order highlights threat of Iran’s small, fast-attack boats
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to shoot Iranian gunboats accused of laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The directive highlights challenges posed by Iran's asymmetrical warfare strategy, which uses swarms of small, fast-attack boats to confront larger US naval vessels in the critical energy waterway.

stories.title: Feeling gloomy about the economy? The ‘vibecession’ has arrived in Australia – but experts are less worried
stories.summary: A poll indicates most Australians believe the country is in or approaching a recession, a sentiment economists do not fully share. Rising cost of living, accelerating inflation, and Reserve Bank interest rate hikes, compounded by the Iran conflict's economic effects, have fueled widespread economic pessimism.

stories.title: Russian attacks injure two in Dnipropetrovsk region, infrastructure damaged
stories.summary: Two people were injured after Russian forces carried out more than 10 attacks using drones and artillery across three districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. Infrastructure in the area was also damaged.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran, US seize ships
stories.summary: The US and Iran have each seized ships in the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating tensions. President Trump downplayed concerns over Iranian small boats while claiming Tehran cannot reach a deal due to internal leadership divisions, an accusation Iran has denied.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon extend ceasefire as Trump says ‘great chance’ for peace deal
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon extended their ceasefire for three weeks after officials from both sides met at the White House. US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a potential peace deal, though Israel and Hezbollah have each accused the other of violating the original truce.

stories.title: Parts of twin cities remain locked down despite uncertainty over US-Iran talks
stories.summary: District administrations in Rawalpindi and Islamabad have kept areas around Nur Khan Airbase locked down for five consecutive days amid uncertainty over expected US-Iran peace talks. Residents of several colonies near the old airport remain confined, and Metro Bus and electric bus services between the twin cities continue to be suspended.

stories.title: In Ivory Coast, Abidjan’s young people wage war on trash
stories.summary: In Abidjan, Ivory Coast, young volunteers are clearing rubbish-clogged drains in a working-class neighbourhood using shovels and rakes. The grassroots cleanup effort aims to address waste management problems in the city's streets.

stories.title: A new era and new leadership: The generals who are running Iran
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's son has been in hiding since US and Israeli forces bombed his father's compound on February 28. A new cohort of military generals has assumed leadership roles in governing Iran amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Ice block stalls hundreds of Everest climbers at base camp
stories.summary: A large unstable ice block, or serac, on the route between Everest base camp and camp one has forced hundreds of climbers and guides to delay their ascent. Nepal's department of mountaineering officials are assessing the route after deeming the formation too risky for passage.

stories.title: Pentagon said to float ways US can punish NATO allies for not helping fight Iran
stories.summary: An internal Pentagon email reportedly discussed measures to penalize NATO allies who have not assisted in the conflict with Iran. Options considered included suspending Spain and reviewing the US position on the United Kingdom's sovereignty claim over the Falkland Islands.

stories.title: US says Iran can play at 2026 World Cup but bars those with ‘IRGC ties’
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clarified that the United States has not barred Iran's national football team from competing in the 2026 World Cup. However, the US said individuals with ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps would not be permitted entry.

stories.title: Airwaves of Power: Why the Pentagon Should Shift to a Commercial-First Spectrum Model
stories.summary: An analysis argues the US Department of Defense should adopt a commercial-first electromagnetic spectrum model. The piece notes the military occupies prime mid-band frequencies for relatively low-throughput national security uses while spending heavily on asymmetric threats, such as firing million-dollar missiles at low-cost Iranian drones.

stories.title: Philippines pushes for South China Sea code by year end: ‘we owe it to the world’
stories.summary: The Philippines is pushing to finalize a South China Sea code of conduct by year's end as it chairs ASEAN. Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro emphasized the urgency at a Jakarta panel ahead of the 48th ASEAN summit in Cebu on May 8, where the global energy crunch will also top the agenda.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith to attend first Anzac Day service since war crime charges
stories.summary: Former Australian SAS soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, a Victoria Cross recipient, plans to attend an Anzac Day service in Queensland. It will be his first such commemoration since being criminally charged with five counts of the war crime of murder allegedly committed during service in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012.

stories.title: CM Bugti opens research centre in Balochistan to curb extremism
stories.summary: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti inaugurated the province's first research centre dedicated to countering violent extremism in Quetta. The Balochistan Centre of Excellence on Countering Violent Extremism was launched in the presence of Home Minister Mir Zia Langove and other officials. Additional Chief Secretary Muhammad Hamza Shafqaat briefed participants on the centre's objectives and future initiatives.

stories.title: Women speak of violence during childbirth in DR Congo
stories.summary: A viral video showing a doctor striking a young woman shortly after she gave birth in a Kinshasa hospital has sparked outrage across the Democratic Republic of Congo. The incident has drawn national attention to violence against women during childbirth in the country's healthcare facilities.

stories.title: 'No hardliners or moderates': Iran denies leadership is fragmented
stories.summary: Iranian President and parliamentary speaker both posted on social media that there are 'no hardliners or moderates' within the country's leadership, pushing back against US claims of internal divisions. The statements were a coordinated effort by senior officials to project unity.

stories.title: Russia spent 20 years hardening Ukraine by accident. Europe won’t get that gift.
stories.summary: An analysis argues that two decades of Russian hybrid pressure inadvertently strengthened Ukraine's resilience, enabling it to resist the 2022 invasion. The piece warns that NATO's eastern flank nations should assume they may face similar threats on a much shorter timeline.

stories.title: How the war in Iran is shifting from bombardment to a test of wills
stories.summary: President Trump's military campaign against Iran has shifted from intensive bombardment to a prolonged standoff at the mouth of the Persian Gulf. The conflict has become a costly test of wills between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Russia’s nighttime drone attack on Odesa leaves two dead, 15 injured
stories.summary: A Russian nighttime drone attack on Odesa struck residential buildings, killing two people and injuring 15 others.

stories.title: The story Tehran wants you to read
stories.summary: A new narrative about Iran's leadership is being promoted that mistakes continuity for genuine change, according to analysis. Critics say the framing echoes Tehran's own preferred messaging about its governance.

stories.title: Uproar as Israel kills Lebanese journalist amid peace talks
stories.summary: Lebanese leaders condemned an Israeli air strike that killed journalist Amal Khalil in southern Lebanon on Wednesday, calling it a war crime. Beirut has vowed to seek international justice. The strike coincided with a new round of ceasefire negotiations between Israel and Lebanon, overshadowing the diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Rubio says no objection to Iran playing in World Cup but people with ties to IRGC won’t be allowed
stories.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US has no objection to Iran's national team participating in the FIFA World Cup but will bar individuals with ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. A Trump envoy had earlier suggested replacing Iran with Italy in the tournament.

stories.title: Likud is no longer the largest party, according to latest Maariv mandates poll
stories.summary: According to a Maariv mandates poll, Israel's Likud party has lost its position as the largest party. Since the start of Operation Roaring Lion, Likud has lost three seats while Naftali Bennett's party has gained three, erasing a previous six-seat lead.

stories.title: Pentagon email floats suspending Spain from NATO: Report
stories.summary: An internal Pentagon email outlined options to punish NATO allies perceived as insufficiently supportive of US operations in Iran, including suspending Spain from the alliance and reviewing Washington's position on the UK's claim to the Falkland Islands, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Presence or Capacity? The Coast Guard Can Have Both Through Small Boat Stations
stories.summary: A proposal recommends reforming US Coast Guard small boat stations to better align their missions with national priorities. The article argues that while closing stations is politically difficult and leaving them unchanged is operationally inefficient, a new model could improve both coastal presence and operational capacity.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 910 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military estimates that Russia has lost approximately 1,323,460 personnel since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. In the most recent 24-hour period ending April 24, 2026, an estimated 910 additional Russian casualties were reported.

stories.title: Football fans not enthused by suggestion of Iran-Italy swap
stories.summary: US special envoy Paolo Zampolli suggested to President Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino that Iran be replaced by Italy at the upcoming US-hosted World Cup. Italian football fans and media responded with a mix of embarrassment and apathy. Italian media noted the idea carried a familiar ring from past controversies.

stories.title: Iran grants fee exemption on Hormuz passage for 'friendly' countries
stories.summary: Iran has granted fee exemptions for passage through the Strait of Hormuz to countries it considers friendly, including Russia. Iranian Ambassador to Moscow Kazem Jalali confirmed the exemptions, reported by Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.

stories.title: Kenya: Can Toxic Politics Trigger Violence? Kenya's Rising Risk of Election-Linked Unrest
stories.summary: An analysis from Capital FM in Nairobi warns that Kenya faces a rising risk of election-linked violence as political rhetoric intensifies. The country has a history of hostile political discourse preceding outbreaks of unrest.

stories.title: CJP Afridi openly opposes Judicial Commission of Pakistan meeting for judges’ transfer
stories.summary: Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi has formally opposed a scheduled Judicial Commission of Pakistan meeting convened to consider transferring five Islamabad High Court judges to other provincial high courts. In a letter to the commission, Afridi warned the move would set an undesirable precedent and erode public confidence in judicial independence.

stories.title: UK rights groups slam ‘authoritarian’ conviction of pro-Palestine activists
stories.summary: A UK court convicted pro-Palestine activists Ben Jamal and Chris Nineham, prompting condemnation from rights organizations including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, which warned the ruling would have a broader chilling effect on protest and free expression.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Israel launched new attacks on southern Lebanon hours after Trump announced a three-week ceasefire extension. Strikes targeted the towns of Touline, Khirbet Selm, and Majdal Zoun in the Tyre area, with artillery shelling also reported on the outskirts of Touline.

stories.title: Retail sales rise as British motorists stock up on fuel
stories.summary: The UK's Office for National Statistics reported that retail sales in Great Britain rose 0.7% in March, significantly exceeding forecasts of 0.1%. The increase was driven largely by motorists stockpiling fuel amid rapidly rising pump prices linked to the Iran war, with fuel purchases reaching their highest level since 2021.

stories.title: Trump rules out N-option amid Hormuz struggle
stories.summary: President Donald Trump ruled out using nuclear weapons in the conflict with Iran while claiming "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz and ordering the US Navy to destroy mine-laying vessels. A third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East as another Iranian tanker was seized in the Indian Ocean. A congressional effort to curb Trump's war powers was defeated.

stories.title: Ukraine: Russian strike on Odesa kills 2, hits hospitals and schools overnight
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Black Sea port city of Odesa overnight on April 23–24, 2026, killing at least two people and injuring more than a dozen. Ukrainian officials said the attack damaged hospitals and schools.

stories.title: Ukrainian married couple aged 75 killed in Russian attack on Odesa
stories.summary: A married couple, both aged 75, were killed in a Russian overnight attack on Odesa, Ukraine. Ukrainian officials reported that residential buildings and a bulk carrier vessel in the port were also struck during the assault.

stories.title: Why US interception of Iran tankers in Asian waters pose new risk to Asean neutrality
stories.summary: U.S. interceptions of Iranian-linked oil tankers in Asian waters are raising concerns about the impact on Southeast Asian neutrality. Analysts warn that countries including Malaysia, Indonesia, and Singapore face new risks from escalating U.S.-Iran maritime tensions near crucial sea lanes.

stories.title: Russia expands AI disinformation into cognitive warfare
stories.summary: Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation reported that Russia has expanded its use of deepfakes and AI-generated video into a full-scale cognitive warfare tool. The escalation represents a significant scaling-up of Moscow's disinformation operations.

stories.title: Israel retaliates against Hezbollah missile launch after ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched rockets toward Israel, saying the attack was in retaliation for an Israeli strike on the Lebanese village of Yater. Israel responded with retaliatory strikes against Hezbollah positions in Lebanon.

stories.title: David Rosen: Israel doesn’t adequately understand Christian relations
stories.summary: After an IDF soldier smashed a statue of Jesus in Lebanon, interfaith leader David Rosen stated that Israel lacks a coherent strategy for Christian relations. He called for improved education within Israel about modern Christian communities.

stories.title: Tokyo urges government workers to swap suits for shorts to counter energy costs
stories.summary: Tokyo authorities introduced new dress code rules allowing government workers to wear shorts to the office to reduce air conditioning use. The measure aims to cut energy costs as the Middle East conflict drives up energy prices globally.

stories.title: Reform UK asks steel bosses to draft ‘alternative strategy’ for industry
stories.summary: Reform UK's deputy leader Richard Tice met with steel industry bosses and commissioned them to draft an alternative steel strategy that would scrap net zero policies, positioning it as a rival to the Labour government's recent plans. The move is part of the party's effort to attract support in former Labour heartlands affected by decades of steel job losses.

stories.title: Register Now: Free Aliyah & Real Estate Meetings by Olim Advisors - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Olim Advisors is hosting free in-person meetings about Aliyah and real estate at six locations across New York and New Jersey between April 26 and May 3.

stories.title: India criticises ‘poor taste’ Trump post against immigrants
stories.summary: India's foreign ministry criticized a post by President Trump on Truth Social that shared comments calling India a "hellhole." The ministry described the remarks by conservative podcast host Michael Savage as "uninformed, inappropriate and in poor taste," ahead of a planned visit to India by Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

stories.title: Does Israel’s ‘Yellow Line’ violate the Lebanon ceasefire?
stories.summary: Israel has established a military zone inside southern Lebanon, which critics say may violate the Lebanon ceasefire agreement. The zone has drawn comparisons to the so-called "Yellow Line" Israel implemented in Gaza, raising concerns about a long-term territorial presence.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Trump says Lebanon and Israel agree to extend Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire by 3 weeks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire by three weeks. Israel said it struck a Hezbollah missile launcher in Lebanon that had fired into Israeli territory.

stories.title: UN General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock to visit India next week
stories.summary: UN General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock is scheduled to visit India next week. She will hold bilateral meetings with Indian government officials and meet the UN country team led by UN Resident Coordinator Stefan Priesner.

stories.title: What a Paramount-Warner Bros. merger could mean, including for coverage of Israel
stories.summary: A potential merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery would place CNN and CBS under the same corporate umbrella. Critics have raised concerns about media consolidation, while Paramount CEO David Ellison has pledged to maintain editorial independence.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Crackdown On Student Protesters Intensifies
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reports that Zimbabwean authorities have intensified a crackdown on student protesters opposing a proposed presidential term extension. The organization has called on the government to end attacks and respect freedom of expression.

stories.title: Ukrainian troops take two Russian soldiers prisoner in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 155th Separate Mechanized Brigade captured two Russian servicemen in the village of Hryshyne in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Trump says Navy Secretary Phelan was fired over shipbuilding conflicts
stories.summary: President Trump said he fired Navy Secretary John Phelan over conflicts related to shipbuilding programs. Sources indicated Phelan was removed for moving too slowly to implement reforms aimed at accelerating naval vessel construction.

stories.title: Embassy encourages Australia-based Iranians to volunteer to help war effort
stories.summary: Iran's embassy in Canberra posted messages on its website and Telegram channel encouraging Australia-based Iranians to register for a voluntary paramilitary campaign called "Janfada" to defend Iran against US forces. The recruitment drive has alarmed diaspora groups, and the Australian Federal Police are now examining the matter.

stories.title: Aboriginal children's book pulled over illustrator's Bondi attack comments
stories.summary: The University of Queensland Press pulled an Aboriginal children's book after its illustrator made controversial comments about the 2025 Bondi attack. Several writers subsequently cut ties with the publisher over the decision.

stories.title: Kenyan leader sparks uproar after  mocking Nigerians' spoken English
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto drew widespread criticism after claiming that Kenyans speak superior English compared to Nigerians, asserting that Nigerian-spoken English is difficult to understand. The remarks provoked backlash across both countries.

stories.title: US soldier allegedly used classified intel to win $400K Polymarket bet on Maduro raid
stories.summary: A 38-year-old US Army master sergeant who participated in an operation to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro allegedly used classified intelligence to win approximately $400,000 on the prediction market Polymarket. Prosecutors say the de facto leak endangered national security.

stories.title: South Korea and US in showdown over Coupang meddling, testing ties
stories.summary: South Korea's National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik condemned a letter from 54 U.S. Republican lawmakers alleging that Seoul was discriminating against e-commerce company Coupang, calling it interference in domestic affairs. The dispute is testing U.S.-South Korea diplomatic ties.

stories.title: 20,000 teddy bears in Washington highlight abducted Ukrainian children
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 teddy bears were displayed on the U.S. National Mall in Washington, D.C., to draw attention to Ukrainian children abducted since 2021. The installation aims to urge international action on the issue as Russia's war in Ukraine continues.

stories.title: Russian diplomats denounce new EU sanctions
stories.summary: Russian diplomats on April 24 condemned the latest European Union sanctions imposed over Moscow's invasion of Ukraine. They argued the measures lack United Nations legitimacy and infringe on the rights of third countries.

stories.title: A ‘final piano song’ offers closure as residents say goodbye to Wang Fuk Court homes
stories.summary: Residents of fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong's Tai Po district returned to their homes to retrieve belongings and say goodbye. The blaze at Wang Cheong House killed 81 of the 168 total victims and destroyed 63 percent of flats in that block.

stories.title: Russian drone strike hits Odesa, damaging homes and injuring civilians
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit a residential building in the Ukrainian city of Odesa during a nighttime attack, damaging homes and injuring civilians. Casualties were reported.

stories.title: Trump’s May 1 deadline: Can he continue war on Iran after that?
stories.summary: As the 60-day mark approaches on May 1, questions arise about whether President Trump can continue US military operations against Iran without congressional authorization, as required under the War Powers Act.

stories.title: Armenia marks 111th anniversary of Armenian genocide in Yerevan
stories.summary: Armenia commemorated the 111th anniversary of the Armenian Genocide on April 23–24, 2026, with marches and ceremonies in the capital Yerevan. Thousands of participants attended the events.

stories.title: US army developing plans to target Hormuz Strait if Iran truce deal shatters: Report
stories.summary: US military officials are developing contingency plans to target Iranian capabilities around the Strait of Hormuz, the southern Arabian Gulf, and the Gulf of Oman if the ceasefire with Iran collapses, according to CNN. Options include strikes on energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extended by three weeks after Oval Office meeting
stories.summary: The ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel has been extended by three weeks following a high-level meeting at the White House in the Oval Office.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 56 after Trump extended ceasefire?
stories.summary: On day 56 of the US-Iran conflict, the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was extended by three weeks following White House talks involving Israeli and Lebanese envoys. Trump announced the extension after negotiations in Washington.

stories.title: Shackled and shaved: El Salvador holds mass trial for hundreds of gang members
stories.summary: Hundreds of alleged Mara Salvatrucha gang members faced a mass trial at El Salvador's CECOT prison, accused of collectively carrying out more than 29,000 murders. Approximately 220 defendants appeared shackled and shaved during the proceedings.

stories.title: ‘Big shout-out’ to China’s environmental leadership from UN agency head
stories.summary: UN Environment Programme executive director Inger Andersen praised China's environmental leadership at a Regional Ecological Summit in Kazakhstan. She said UNEP relies significantly on China's contributions, including its funding for biodiversity conservation in the Global South.

stories.title: Fire brought under control at Russia's Tuapse oil terminal
stories.summary: Firefighters brought under control a fire at Russia's Tuapse oil refinery on the Black Sea coast on April 23. The blaze was caused by a Ukrainian drone attack, according to local officials.

stories.title: Unexpected love: Japan traditional dancer finds love at 60 with 26-year-old devoted protege
stories.summary: A 60-year-old traditional dancer in Japan's Ibaraki prefecture found love with a 26-year-old protege after two decades without a romantic relationship. The couple appeared on a Japanese television show but chose to keep their identities private.

stories.title: Editor's Notes: Milei’s torch should push Israel to think about its extra nine million
stories.summary: An editorial argues that Israel, built as a homeland for Jewish exiles, should do more to engage the broader global Jewish population. The piece uses Argentine President Milei's symbolic gesture as a prompt to reconsider outreach to an estimated nine million Jews outside Israel.

stories.title: Disgrace in Debel: A single incident undermines Israel’s reputation for tolerance - editorial
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was punished and a damaged statue replaced following an incident in Debel. The editorial argues the event should serve as a reminder of the standards of conduct expected of Israel and its military.

stories.title: DOJ charges soldier accused of betting $400,000 on Maduro removal
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice on April 23 charged a U.S. Army soldier who allegedly earned $400,000 by betting on the removal of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, using insider knowledge gained through his military role.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon extend ceasefire as Trump says ‘great chance’ for peace deal
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire by three weeks following a meeting of officials from both sides at the White House. US President Donald Trump said there was a "great chance" for a peace deal, despite mutual accusations of truce violations between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Africa: Largest Catch-Up Initiative Delivers Over 100 Million Childhood Vaccinations
stories.summary: The Big Catch-Up initiative, launched during World Immunization Week 2023, has delivered over 100 million vaccine doses to roughly 18.3 million children across 36 countries. About 12.3 million of those were 'zero-dose children' who had never received any vaccines. The initiative concluded in March 2026.

stories.title: Nigeria: Dangote to Partner Kenya, Uganda to Build Refinery in Tanzania
stories.summary: Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote has announced plans to partner with Kenya and Uganda to build a large-scale oil refinery in Tanzania. The project is intended to advance energy self-sufficiency and industrial growth across Africa.

stories.title: Baltic states say Europe cannot return to pre-war relations with Russia — Bloomberg
stories.summary: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania warned European partners that restoring normal relations with Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine is unrealistic and dangerous, according to Bloomberg. The Baltic states urged allies to maintain a firm stance toward Moscow.

stories.title: How fake AI victims are being used to provide rationale for attacking Iran
stories.summary: Fabricated AI-generated videos and images depicting fake female victims of Iran's government have been circulating widely online, being used as propaganda to build public support for military action against Iran.

stories.title: Latest Israeli strikes target southern Lebanese towns Touline, Khirbet Selm
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on the southern Lebanese towns of Touline and Khirbet Selm, with artillery shelling also reported near Touline. The strikes occurred just hours after US President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Venice Biennale jury excludes Israel, Russia from artist awards as EU threatens funding cut
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale jury announced it would exclude artists from countries whose leaders face International Criminal Court charges from consideration for awards. The decision affects both Israel and Russia.

stories.title: New secrets of human evolution unlocked in study of ancient DNA from Europe and Near East
stories.summary: Scientists analyzed 22,000 ancient genomes from Europe and the Near East, documenting hundreds of genetic changes driven by natural selection over the past 10,000 years. The study identified variants linked to conditions including celiac disease and multiple sclerosis.

stories.title: Hundreds of Congolese refugees voluntarily repatriated from Burundi
stories.summary: Hundreds of Congolese refugees residing at the Busuma camp in Burundi have been voluntarily repatriated to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

stories.title: Lebanese journalist recalls killing of colleague Amal Khalil
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Zeinab Faraj, speaking from her hospital bed in southern Lebanon, recounted the moment an Israeli airstrike killed her colleague, journalist Amal Khalil.

stories.title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire; Hong Kong actress’ second cancer shock: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump extended a ceasefire with Iran following a request from Pakistan's leadership. The extension came amid ongoing tensions, with Trump also claiming the interception of an unspecified item described as a 'gift from China.'

stories.title: Trump says US in no rush but ‘clock is ticking’ for Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the United States is in no rush regarding Iran but warned that "the clock is ticking." His remarks coincided with the arrival of a third U.S. aircraft carrier in the Middle East.

stories.title: China’s DeepSeek unveils latest models a year after upending global tech
stories.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek unveiled its latest model, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, approximately one year after its initial models disrupted the global tech landscape. The company claims the new model outperforms all rival open-source models in mathematics and coding benchmarks.

stories.title: Nearly half of Israelis oppose Trump's ceasefire extension with Iran
stories.summary: A survey conducted by the Israeli newspaper Maariv found that 42 percent of Israelis believe President Donald Trump's decision to extend a ceasefire with Iran was wrong. Twenty-eight percent supported the move, while 30 percent were unsure.

stories.title: US concerned about Chinese infrastructure in Argentina, US security official says
stories.summary: U.S. Undersecretary of State for Arms Control Thomas DiNanno expressed concern about Chinese-built infrastructure in Argentina during a press conference at the U.S. ambassador's residence in Buenos Aires on April 23.

stories.title: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire extended by 3 weeks, says Trump
stories.summary: President Trump announced a three-week extension of the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire following a White House meeting. The session was the second high-level negotiation between Israeli and Lebanese officials in a week.

stories.title: Revealed: UK oil refinery owner moved Russian loans to offshore subsidiary where sanctions did not apply
stories.summary: UK members of parliament are calling for an investigation into Essar Energy, owner of the Stanlow oil refinery in Cheshire, after reports it transferred loans from the sanctioned Russian state bank VTB to an offshore subsidiary in Mauritius, where sanctions did not apply. The revelations follow dock workers at Ellesmere Port refusing to unload Russian oil after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: One in 10 operations in England cancelled with less than 24 hours’ notice
stories.summary: A study of elective surgery at 91 NHS trusts in England found that roughly one in ten operations are cancelled within 24 hours of their scheduled date or postponed at the pre-operative appointment stage. Researchers estimated that nearly 40% of these cancellations could be avoided.

stories.title: Steve Rosenberg: Kremlin's tightening grip on internet fuels Russian discontent
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Steve Rosenberg reported that the Kremlin's tightening control over internet access across Russia is fueling public discontent. Russian citizens are drawing comparisons between current digital restrictions and Soviet-era censorship.

stories.title: America offers US$4 million bounty for arrest of Chinese money launderer
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering up to $4 million for information leading to the arrest of Chinese national Daren Li, 43, who fled the U.S. after being convicted of money laundering. Li was sentenced in absentia to 20 years in prison by a California federal court in February.

stories.title: Exchange of gunfire inside Mall of Louisiana leaves 1 person dead, 5 wounded
stories.summary: An exchange of gunfire inside the Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge left one person dead and five wounded. Two groups reportedly began arguing in the food court before shooting at each other.

stories.title: Mexico seeks to ease tensions over deaths of US officials in car crash
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum sought to de-escalate tensions with the United States on April 23 after two Americans died in a car crash in the northern state of Chihuahua. Sources identified the deceased as CIA officers working on an anti-narcotics operation.

stories.title: Bangladeshi YouTuber’s death sparks mourning amid Malaysia’s drink-driving crisis
stories.summary: Bangladeshi gaming YouTuber Muzahid Millad, known as Advance Gaming, was killed in a crash on Malaysia's Maju Expressway allegedly caused by a drink-driving Malaysian soldier. The 22-year-old's death has reignited public demands for stricter drink-driving laws in Malaysia.

stories.title: Nigeria: Kano Govt Prepares Wedding for 1,500 Couples - Official
stories.summary: The Kano State Government in Nigeria is preparing a mass wedding for 1,500 couples under its Marriage Social Welfare Initiative, known locally as 'Auren Gata.'

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya to Invest in Uganda Oil Refinery, Ruto Announces
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto announced that Kenya will invest in Uganda's oil refinery project. The move is aimed at strengthening regional energy cooperation and long-term infrastructure development in East Africa.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Asks Senate to Approve Another $516.3 Million Loan to Construct Roads
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve a $516.3 million loan to finance construction of the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway. The project is a flagship initiative under his Renewed Hope Agenda.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Tax Amnesty Warning As Deadline Looms for Zimbabweans
stories.summary: The Zimbabwe Revenue Authority urged taxpayers to take advantage of a voluntary disclosure programme before the June 30, 2026 deadline, warning that the tax amnesty window is closing.

stories.title: Nigeria: 12 of 416 Ngoshe Captives Escape From Boko Haram Terrorists
stories.summary: Twelve of the 416 residents abducted by Boko Haram from the town of Ngoshe in Gwoza local government area of northeastern Nigeria have escaped captivity, according to security sources.

stories.title: Tanzania: Dar es Salaam Leads As 518 People Reportedly Dead During Oct 29 Unrest
stories.summary: An independent commission of inquiry found that 518 people were killed during violence linked to Tanzania's October 29, 2025 general election. Dar es Salaam accounted for the highest number of deaths, with men making up the overwhelming majority of victims.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Targets Wheat Surplus in 2026 Amid Farmer Concerns Over Costs and Payments
stories.summary: Zimbabwe set an ambitious wheat production target for 2026 aimed at surpassing national demand. However, farmers warned that high costs and delayed government payments could undermine progress toward achieving a surplus.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump orders US to ‘shoot and kill’ boats laying mines in Hormuz strait; Israel-Lebanon truce extended
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the US military to shoot and kill small Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming total US control of the waterway despite Iran's seizure of two container ships. A report warned it could take months to fully clear the strait of mines. Separately, the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was extended.

stories.title: Israeli Ambassador to the US says Lebanon 'must recognise' Israeli presence
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador to the US Yechiel Leiter, leading negotiations with a Lebanese delegation at the White House, accused Beirut of failing to dismantle Hezbollah's infrastructure. He called on Lebanon to recognize Israel's presence and stated the root problem was Hezbollah.

stories.title: US-China AI race intensifies as DeepSeek releases 'reduced' cost model
stories.summary: Chinese AI company DeepSeek released a new model it says operates at drastically reduced costs and can process extra-long texts to complete complex tasks. The release intensifies the US-China AI competition after DeepSeek's earlier reasoning model challenged assumptions about American dominance in artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Budanov opposes legalizing weapons for civilians
stories.summary: Andriy Yermak, head of Ukraine's Presidential Office, spoke out against legalizing civilian weapons ownership. He argued that such a move could lead to greater problems for the country.

stories.title: Trump says US will not use nuclear weapon in Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared that the United States will not use nuclear weapons in any conflict with Iran, stating that nuclear weapons should never be used by any party.

stories.title: White House to host Lebanon-Israeli talks amid push for ceasefire extension
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to host Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors at the White House for talks aimed at extending a ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Venice Biennale jury excludes Russia and Israel from artist awards as EU threatens funding cut
stories.summary: Jurors at the 2025 Venice Biennale announced they would exclude artists from countries whose leaders face International Criminal Court charges from award consideration, effectively barring Russian and Israeli participants. The decision came as the European Union reportedly threatened to cut funding to the exhibition.

stories.title: US not against Iran's participation in World Cup, but ties to IRGC not allowed, Rubio says
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the U.S. does not oppose Iran's participation in the 2026 World Cup but said individuals tied to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps would not be permitted entry. His remarks followed reports that a Trump envoy had asked FIFA to replace Iran with Italy in the tournament.

stories.title: Hundreds of alleged MS-13 members tried at mass hearing in El Salvador mega-jail
stories.summary: Hundreds of alleged Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) gang members were tried in a mass hearing at an El Salvador mega-prison, accused of collectively committing over 29,000 murders. The mass trials are central to President Nayib Bukele's anti-gang campaign.

stories.title: Iranian cargo ship reaches port safely despite US efforts to seize it
stories.summary: An Iranian cargo ship carrying rice reached port safely after the United States reportedly attempted to seize it in the Oman Sea. Iran's semi-official Fars News Agency reported the vessel was escorted by naval units of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Ceasefire with Lebanon 'not 100 percent', Israel’s ambassador to the UN says
stories.summary: Israel's UN Ambassador Danny Danon said the ceasefire with Lebanon was "not 100 percent" following President Trump's announcement of a three-week extension. Danon stated that Israeli forces take action whenever they perceive a threat and must "retaliate" against Hezbollah rocket attacks.

stories.title: Actor felt ‘mocked’ by Rebel Wilson’s wife in Instagram post referencing Finding Nemo, court hears
stories.summary: Australian actor Charlotte MacInnes, who is suing Rebel Wilson for defamation, told a court she felt mocked by a social media post from Wilson's wife Ramona Agruma-Wilson. The Instagram post featured the animated character Dory from Finding Nemo and appeared to reference MacInnes's testimony. The defamation case stems from Wilson's social media posts about a sexual harassment complaint.

stories.title: Largest-ever ban on toxic chemicals in EU hit by ‘extremely frustrating’ delays
stories.summary: A report found that the European Commission's 2022 restrictions roadmap targeting 14 groups of hazardous substances, including toxic chemicals in children's nappies and PFAS "forever chemicals," has made poor progress after four years. Environmental groups called the Commission the chief roadblock to its own plans. Scientists described the delays as extremely frustrating.

stories.title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker 2026
stories.summary: Mozambique President Daniel Chapo met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, becoming the first African head of state to visit Xi in 2026 and the tenth national leader overall. US President Donald Trump is scheduled for a summit with Xi on May 14-15 in China. Russian President Vladimir Putin is also expected to visit before the end of June.

stories.title: Hamas terrorists significantly recovering capabilities during ceasefire - N12
stories.summary: An Israeli intelligence document obtained by N12 News indicates that Hamas is significantly rebuilding its military and civilian capabilities in Gaza during the ceasefire. The report alleges Hamas is avoiding commitments under the peace plan while strengthening its hold on the territory.

stories.title: Anthony Albanese accused of ‘caving to gas companies’ as Labor set to reject new export tax
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese faces criticism from Senator David Pocock for reportedly deciding against pursuing a new 25% tax on gas exports in the upcoming budget. Pocock accused the government of caving to gas industry pressure. The decision comes amid a global oil crisis and Albanese's efforts to secure domestic fuel supplies.

stories.title: India opens door to Sheikh Hasina extradition talks: a Delhi-Dhaka thaw?
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs confirmed on April 17 that it is conducting a formal review of Bangladesh's request for the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Hasina fled to India in August 2024 after her government was toppled by protesters. Observers caution that the review does not necessarily signal New Delhi's readiness to hand her over.

stories.title: Long Island father and teenage son arrested as cops probe swastika in school bathroom
stories.summary: A 15-year-old on Long Island was identified by police as having drawn a swastika in a school bathroom. When confronted, he told officers his father had provided him with explosive materials to build rockets, leading to the arrest of both father and son.

stories.title: US soldier allegedly made $400k on Polymarket betting on Maduro raid
stories.summary: US prosecutors allege a soldier used classified information about a military operation against Venezuelan President Maduro to place winning bets on the prediction market platform Polymarket, earning approximately $400,000. The case is part of a broader pattern of prediction market bets linked to US government actions.

stories.title: Huawei doubles down on autonomous driving, earmarking US$11.7b for autopilot training
stories.summary: Huawei Technologies plans to invest up to 80 billion yuan (US$11.7 billion) over five years to expand computing power for training and testing its semi-autonomous driving systems. The investment aims to enhance reliability of vehicles using the Huawei Qiankun ADS autopilot system. The Shenzhen-based company seeks to broaden its customer base in China's smart driving market.

stories.title: Ukraine says drone operators can down targets from thousands of kilometres away
stories.summary: A Ukrainian lawmaker disclosed that he had operated a drone interceptor from outside Ukraine, demonstrating that Ukrainian drone operators can engage targets from thousands of kilometres away. The claim highlights advances in remote warfare capabilities used in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iran uses fast boats to seize container ships in Strait of Hormuz, challenging US blockade
stories.summary: Iran used fast-attack boats to seize two container ships near the Strait of Hormuz, challenging the U.S. naval blockade in the area. U.S. President Trump had previously dismissed Iran's fast-attack vessels as not posing a significant threat.

stories.title: Israeli 'violations' of Temple Mount spark backlash from Muslim, Arab states
stories.summary: Eight Arab countries issued a joint statement condemning Israel's actions at Jerusalem's Temple Mount and other holy sites. They characterized the moves as provocations and violations of international law, sparking backlash from Muslim and Arab states.

stories.title: Could thousands of US ‘hellscape’ drone boats mess with PLA plans for Taiwan?
stories.summary: Taiwanese analysts broadly welcomed a US Navy plan to deploy thousands of uncrewed surface vessels across the Indo-Pacific by 2030, saying it could complicate Beijing's military planning regarding Taiwan. However, they cautioned that unless Taipei advances its own stalled drone fleet programs, the direct benefit to Taiwan may be limited due to US production and logistics challenges.

stories.title: US soldier charged with making $400,000 on Maduro removal bets
