stories.summary: Pentagon personnel have used a Google Gemini-based tool on the GenAI.mil platform to create approximately 100,000 AI agents for use on unclassified Defense Department networks. The agents are designed to handle data processing and automate routine online tasks for DOD staff.

stories.title: EU Hits Russia With 20th Sanctions Package
stories.summary: The European Union imposed its 20th sanctions package on Russia. Brussels also approved a €90 billion loan to Ukraine after Hungary and Slovakia withdrew their vetoes blocking the measure.

stories.title: Washington’s One-Dimensional Chess in the Horn of Africa
stories.summary: The Trump administration is pursuing an effort to lift sanctions on Eritrea, a move critics say reflects a lack of coherent US strategy in the Horn of Africa. Analysts characterize the approach as one-dimensional and lacking clear strategic justification for the policy reversal.

stories.title: Reza Pahlavi splattered with red liquid in Berlin
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran's ousted shah, was splattered with red liquid during an appearance in Berlin where he called on Europeans to support the Iranian people. The alleged perpetrator was detained by authorities.

stories.title: Thousands call on UK ministers to cut ties with US tech giant Palantir
stories.summary: More than 200,000 people signed petitions urging the UK government to end public contracts with US tech company Palantir, citing concerns about its role in the NHS, police, military, and councils, as well as its links to US immigration enforcement and the Israeli military.

stories.title: Bangladesh measles crisis deepens as child deaths reach 194
stories.summary: Bangladesh reported 194 child deaths from measles in an outbreak that began on March 15, with suspected cases exceeding 28,000. The government launched a nationwide vaccination campaign targeting 18 million children in response to the worst measles outbreak in decades.

stories.title: More than 6 million Somalis face hunger amid climate shocks and conflict
stories.summary: Approximately 6.5 million people in Somalia face severe hunger driven by drought, failed rains, and ongoing armed conflict, with children at particular risk of acute malnutrition.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teenager in occupied West Bank raid
stories.summary: A Palestinian teenager was killed after Israeli forces shot him with live ammunition during a raid in the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian media reports. He died in hospital from a gunshot wound to the shoulder.

stories.title: Russian court labels LGBTQ+ media project Parni Plus an ‘extremist’ organization
stories.summary: A court in Russia's Oryol Region designated the LGBTQ+ media project Parni Plus an "extremist" organization, ruling in favor of a Justice Ministry lawsuit against the outlet.

stories.title: Iran receives first revenue from Strait of Hormuz tolls: Official
stories.summary: Iran has begun collecting its first revenue from tolls imposed on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported that Parliament's security commission approved the toll plans in March.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes kill three in south Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed three people on the Shoukine road in Lebanon's Nabatieh district and wounded two others, including a child, in the village of Yater, despite a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. The attacks occurred hours before a second round of Lebanese-Israeli talks mediated by the US in Washington.

stories.title: Dozens of Mexican mafia members arrested in California crackdown
stories.summary: Federal authorities arrested more than two dozen members and associates of the Mexican Mafia in a crackdown across southern California, primarily in Orange County. A total of 43 people were indicted on charges including murder, kidnapping, extortion, and drug trafficking.

stories.title: Unspecified threats temporarily close Houston synagogue and Jewish day school
stories.summary: A synagogue and a Jewish day school in Houston, Texas, were temporarily closed due to unspecified threats. The Jewish Federation of Greater Houston said it did not believe there was a broader risk to the local Jewish community.

stories.title: Syria carrying out arrests of Palestinians linked to Assad regime, rights orgs. claim
stories.summary: Rights organizations report that Syrian authorities are arresting Palestinians linked to the former Assad regime. The Action Group for Palestinians of Syria said at least 14 men were detained from camps and neighborhoods including Khan Al-Shih, Jaramana, Rukn al-Din, and the town of al-Hameh.

stories.title: South Africa court halts return of ex-Zambian president's remains, again
stories.summary: A South African court blocked the repatriation of former Zambian president Edgar Lungu's remains, halting plans for a state funeral and extending a dispute that has persisted for nearly 10 months.

stories.title: China has ‘deliberate, industrial-scale campaigns’ to steal US AI models, White House says
stories.summary: The White House accused China of conducting deliberate, industrial-scale campaigns to steal US artificial intelligence models. Administration officials said they would collaborate with the private sector to counter foreign-led AI model distillation efforts.

stories.title: Is Ethiopia bracing for war?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that the ongoing war in Iran has temporarily delayed an escalation of tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea, though renewed armed conflict between the two countries remains a possibility.

stories.title: Decapitating cartels? Mexico leans into ‘kingpin strategy’ but at a cost
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has authorized military operations targeting cartel leaders under a renewed "kingpin strategy," reportedly under pressure from the United States. The approach has drawn scrutiny over its broader security costs.

stories.title: Italy slams Trump envoy proposal of taking Iran’s place in World Cup 2026
stories.summary: Italian officials rejected a proposal by a Trump administration envoy suggesting Italy's national football team replace Iran at the 2026 World Cup. Fans in Italy also responded with little enthusiasm to the idea.

stories.title: The future of Israeli tech: Insights from Yaniv Golan
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Conference, tech entrepreneur Yaniv Golan discussed artificial intelligence, deep tech, and the challenges Israeli startups face in adapting to a rapidly evolving AI-driven market.

stories.title: Virgina court blocks new congressional maps two days after state votes in favor
stories.summary: A Virginia court blocked newly approved congressional redistricting maps just two days after state voters approved them. Republicans accused Democrats of hypocrisy, citing their previous opposition to partisan gerrymandering.

stories.title: Trump claims US has total control over strait of Hormuz after Iran seizes two container ships
stories.summary: President Trump claimed the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, but Iranian commandos seized two container ships and a US report warned mine clearance could take six months, casting doubt on that assertion.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth Is America’s New Secretary of Pestilence
stories.summary: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has moved to reverse vaccine mandates within the US military. Critics argue the policy change undermines military readiness by exposing service members to preventable diseases.

stories.title: Trump says King Charles’ visit could ‘absolutely’ repair US-UK ties
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told the BBC that King Charles' upcoming four-day state visit to the United States could help repair strained US-UK relations, with tensions over the Iran war and the Jeffrey Epstein scandal looming over the trip.

stories.title: Iranian delegation 'forbidden' from raising nuclear issues in US talks - report
stories.summary: An Iranian delegation heading to talks with the United States was reportedly forbidden from raising nuclear issues. The order allegedly came from officials close to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei as the negotiation team was preparing to depart.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz expresses displeasure at lack of functional early weather warning systems in GB
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed displeasure at non-functional early weather warning systems in Gilgit-Baltistan, particularly for glacial lake outburst floods. He ordered an inquiry during a review meeting on pre-monsoon strategy and climate preparedness.

stories.title: Abidjan’s young people wage war on trash
stories.summary: A group of young volunteers in a working-class neighbourhood of Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, is cleaning rubbish-clogged drains using shovels and rakes in a grassroots effort to improve local sanitation.

stories.title: Border guards destroy Russian drone launch site in southern direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian border guards destroyed a Russian FPV drone launch position in the southern sector of the front line, eliminating a site used to operate first-person-view attack drones.

stories.title: Is an 'Islamic NATO' emerging as a counterweight to Israel?
stories.summary: An analysis examines whether Israel's military campaigns and territorial ambitions since 2023 are driving regional Muslim-majority states toward a new collective security and defence alignment, sometimes described as an "Islamic NATO."

stories.title: ACLU, Amnesty lead 120 rights groups issuing US World Cup ‘travel advisory’
stories.summary: A coalition of over 120 rights organizations, including the ACLU and Amnesty International, issued a travel advisory for visitors to the United States ahead of the 2026 World Cup, citing what they called deteriorating human rights conditions. The White House dismissed the advisory as "scare tactics."

stories.title: Ukrainian pilots now down Shaheds thousands of kilometers away – including from other countries
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone operators can now down Russian Shahed drones from thousands of kilometers away, including from locations outside Ukraine such as Kyiv, Lviv, or abroad. This reduces their exposure to strikes and electronic warfare.

stories.title: Department of Air Force picks bidders for nuclear microreactors, assigns locations
stories.summary: Supporters say the program could enhance national security by strengthening DoD’s energy sources. Critics, meanwhile, have argued that ANPI’s benefits are illusory, and come with too much cost and ris

stories.title: Report: Mother of Russia’s presidential administration chief receives large sum by lending to defense company
stories.summary: An investigation by Russian outlet iStories found that Tatyana Yezhevskaya, mother of Presidential Administration chief Anton Vaino, lent 450 million rubles to defense company group Sfera in March 2022 and collected 525 million rubles in repayment with interest the following year.

stories.title: Kuwait releases journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin after acquittal
stories.summary: Kuwaiti-American journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin has been released from prison in Kuwait after being acquitted of all charges. The 41-year-old was arrested on 2 March while visiting family, reportedly for sharing images on social media related to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Trump’s navy secretary ousted over dispute about shipbuilding
stories.summary: John Phelan firing caused by poor relationship with Pete Hegseth and slow movement on shipbuilding, sources sayThe Trump administration fired its top naval official on Wednesday in a move unrelated to

stories.title: Iranian ex-shah's son says talks with Tehran are 'appeasement'
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran's ousted shah, stated Thursday that any negotiations with Tehran's clerical leadership constitute "appeasement." His remarks come amid the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Sweden says may ration fuel as Iran war threatens economy
stories.summary: Sweden's government warned it may need to ration fuel in the coming months as the war involving Iran in the Middle East significantly impacts the country's economy. The potential disruptions are linked to conflict-related pressures on global energy supplies.

stories.title: Ukraine deserves full membership because it defends EU in reality, not symbolically — Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky argued that Ukraine deserves full European Union membership, stating that the country is defending Europe at the cost of Ukrainian lives and should receive more than symbolic support.

stories.title: Journalist detained in Kuwait acquitted of ‘spreading false information’, says press monitor
stories.summary: Committee to Protect Journalists says Ahmed Shihab-Eldin was found innocent after 52 days in detentionMiddle East crisis – live updatesA Kuwaiti-American journalist, who had been detained in Kuwait, h

stories.title: Huge chunk of glacier blocks Everest route in peak climbing season
stories.summary: Sherpas cannot prepare the route to the world's highest peak because a huge block of ice is in the way.

stories.title: Iran’s exiled crown prince splashed with red liquid after railing against ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran's exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi was splashed with what police described as tomato juice by a protester in Berlin after he publicly opposed ceasefire efforts. The protester was detained by German police. Pahlavi was reportedly snubbed by the German government during his visit.

stories.title: Indonesia Says It Will Buy 150M Barrels of Russian Oil Amid Global Shortage
stories.summary: Indonesia announced plans to purchase 150 million barrels of Russian oil amid a global supply shortage. Approximately 20–25% of Indonesia's crude imports normally transit the Strait of Hormuz from the Middle East.

stories.title: Lebanon to seek ceasefire extension in US-hosted talks with Israel
stories.summary: The United States will host a second meeting between Lebanese and Israeli envoys on April 24. Lebanon seeks an extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah during the Washington-hosted talks.

stories.title: Chechnya’s ruler promotes energy drink brand named after his teenage son
stories.summary: Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov is promoting a new energy drink brand called "K13," named after his 18-year-old son Adam Kadyrov, according to the independent Russian outlet Verstka.

stories.title: 'The future is peace': A story of brotherhood across a divided land
stories.summary: Israeli entrepreneur Maoz Inon, whose parents were killed in the October 7, 2023 attacks, and Palestinian activist Aziz Abu Sarah, who lost a brother during the first intifada, have forged a close friendship. They co-authored a book titled "The Future is Peace" recounting their shared journey and vision for reconciliation in the Holy Land.

stories.title: Slovakia says getting Russian oil from repaired Ukraine pipeline
stories.summary: Slovakia confirmed it is again receiving Russian oil through the repaired Druzhba pipeline crossing Ukraine. The pipeline had been at the center of a dispute involving Ukraine, the EU, Hungary, and Slovakia.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei awake, aware, but IRGC commanders actually running Iran - report
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's new supreme leader, remains mentally sharp and is receiving handwritten updates. However, IRGC commanders are reportedly the ones actually running the country's day-to-day operations.

stories.title: Israeli-US war on Iran drives costs up, forcing aid cuts worldwide
stories.summary: Norwegian Refugee Council Secretary General Jan Egeland warned that the Israeli-US war on Iran is driving up global costs and forcing humanitarian organizations to scale back operations. He cited doubled diesel costs for the organization's 1,500 vehicles as an example of the impact on relief work.

stories.title: Lockheed Martin CEO sees Trump’s Pentagon as ‘golden opportunity’ for growth
stories.summary: Jim Taiclet spoke in earnings call as company expands contracts with the US government amid the Iran warLockheed Martin’s CEO has called the Trump administration a “golden opportunity” for the company

stories.title: Russian attack on Dnipro: Injury toll rises to 13, three killed
stories.summary: A Russian nighttime drone attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed three people and injured at least 13 others, with the casualty toll rising as rescuers worked through the aftermath.

stories.title: Is the tide turning for Ukraine in war with Russia? – The Latest
stories.summary: With the EU approving a €90bn loan for Ukraine, a surprise visit from Prince Harry, and data suggesting Russian troops made almost no territorial gains in March – are there reasons for optimism in Kyi

stories.title: Foreign Office unit tracking Israel’s potential breaches of international law closes due to cuts
stories.summary: Exclusive: Officials warn department will also lose access to database of 26,000 verified incidents due to cutsThe Foreign Office unit tracking potential breaches of international law by Israel in Gaz

stories.title: Dutch gov't ups Jewish security amid massive rise in antisemitic attacks
stories.summary: The Dutch government has increased security funding for Jewish schools, institutions, and events amid a sharp rise in antisemitic attacks, structurally allocating €1.3 million per year since 2025.

stories.title: Rosalinda González Valencia, alias ‘La Jefa’
stories.summary: Rosalinda González Valencia, known as "La Jefa," served as a key financial operator for Mexico's Jalisco Cartel New Generation (CJNG), helping build it into one of Mexico's most powerful criminal organizations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s MoD and European Commission agree on funding for new defense technologies
stories.summary: At the Ukraine–EU Business Summit in Brussels, the European Commission and Ukraine's Ministry of Defense signed a Declaration of Cooperation on funding investments in advanced and breakthrough defense technologies.

stories.title: Michael Tilson Thomas, award-winning conductor and composer, dies aged 81
stories.summary: Renowned artist, who won 12 Grammys, died at home after being diagnosed with an aggressive type of brain cancerSign up for the Breaking News US email to get newsletter alerts in your inboxMichael Tils

stories.title: 3 SHOs suspended, probe ordered after 4 killed in alleged drone strike in Khairpur
stories.summary: Four civilians were killed in an alleged drone strike in Saeed Khan Lakho village in Sindh's Khairpur district, Pakistan. Three station house officers were suspended, and Sindh's home minister and inspector general ordered investigations into the incident.

stories.title: Nigeria: We Won't Reverse Our Reforms - Oyedele
stories.summary: Nigeria's Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele declared that the federal government will not reverse its current economic reforms, stating that policy reversals will not define the country's economic management.

stories.title: Southern US wildfires force residents to flee: ‘I don’t know if I have a house standing or not’
stories.summary: Fires that spread during drought in Georgia and Florida have blanketed cities hundreds of miles away in smokeSign up for the Breaking News US email to get newsletter alerts in your inboxWildfires tear

stories.title: Nigeria: Governors Back State Police Framework
stories.summary: Nigeria's governors, through the Nigeria Governors' Forum, endorsed a State Police Framework ahead of proposed constitutional amendments and backed the federal government's proposed 12-year continuous basic education plan.

stories.title: 12 Russian FSB officers killed as Ukrainian drones hit “dirty war” command post in occupied Donetsk
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes reportedly hit a Russian FSB command post in occupied Donetsk, killing 12 FSB officers. A Ukrainian commander said the facility had been coordinating recruitment, sabotage operations, and actions targeting civilians in occupied areas.

stories.title: PM meets astronomers selected for China's space mission, hopes it will 'usher in era of space research'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met astronomers Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud in Islamabad after their selection for China's manned space programme. Sharif called the mission a source of national pride and expressed hope it would launch a new era of space research in Pakistan.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike enemy targets in occupied territories, damaging missile depot, fuel train
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a missile and artillery depot and a logistics storage facility near the temporarily occupied settlement of Sartana in Donetsk region during overnight operations on April 23.

stories.title: Slovenia says it will air Palestinian documentaries instead of this year’s Eurovision
stories.summary: Slovenia announced it will broadcast Palestinian documentaries instead of participating in the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna. It is among five countries that withdrew from the contest; only Iceland and the Netherlands among the boycotting nations plan to air the competition.

stories.title: Mozambique: Mozambique Launches Long-Acting Injectable Prep
stories.summary: Mozambican health authorities launched a long-acting injectable PrEP against HIV in Maputo on Wednesday. The medication can reduce the risk of HIV infection by more than 99 percent.

stories.title: Israel charges two air force soldiers over alleged Iran espionage
stories.summary: Israel has charged two air force technicians with espionage for Iran, including aiding the enemy during wartime and transferring sensitive military information. The charges were announced jointly by the Israeli military, Shin Bet, and police. One suspect is accused of direct contact with a foreign agent.

stories.title: Watch: U.S. extended sanctions waiver on Russian oil purchase after request from over 10 countries
stories.summary: The United States extended a sanctions waiver on Russian oil purchases following requests from more than ten countries.

stories.title: Why Do Many Western Defense Tech Firms Struggle in Ukraine?
stories.summary: Michael Kofman joined Ryan at a live event earlier this year to discuss the performance of American defense technology in Ukraine and why it often falls short. They examine the challenges of fielding

stories.title: Israel appoints first special envoy to Christian world after scandals strain ties
stories.summary: Israel has appointed George Deek, former envoy to Azerbaijan and a member of the Arab Christian community, as its first special envoy to the Christian world. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said the appointment reflects the importance Israel places on relations with Christian communities globally.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz crisis: Iran threatens to open Pandora's Box through chaos - analysis
stories.summary: Iran's actions in the Strait of Hormuz have triggered a broader crisis, raising unforeseen strategic and diplomatic issues that extend beyond previous negotiations over a deal with Tehran.

stories.title: Is China's economy insulated from Iran war shock?
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving the US and Israel against Iran has triggered a major global energy crisis. China, the world's second-largest economy, has so far appeared largely shielded from the most severe economic consequences of the disruption.

stories.title: AvtoVAZ starts monthly car subscription program for its Lada lineup
stories.summary: Russia's state-owned automaker AvtoVAZ launched a long-term monthly vehicle subscription program called "Lada Legko" for its Lada car lineup. The program offers an alternative to traditional car ownership for Russian consumers.

stories.title: Clearing Hormuz Strait mines could take six months: Report
stories.summary: A report indicates that clearing mines from the Strait of Hormuz could take up to six months even after hostilities end and any blockade is lifted. The finding underscores the lasting disruption to the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Iranian Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi splashed with red substance in Berlin after criticizing ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi was splashed with a red substance, reportedly tomato juice, during an appearance in Berlin after he criticized a ceasefire. Police arrested the suspect immediately; Pahlavi was not injured.

stories.title: Somalia: Lafta Gareen-Aligned Forces Move Into Gedo, Heightening Political Tensions
stories.summary: Hundreds of fighters loyal to former South West state president Abdiasis Lafta Gareen have entered parts of Somalia's Gedo region near Dolow, according to witnesses and officials. The troop movement risks escalating an ongoing political standoff in southern Somalia.

stories.title: Lebanon leaders accuse Israel of war crime after journalist killed
stories.summary: Lebanese leaders accused Israel of committing a war crime after an airstrike in southern Lebanon killed journalist Amal Khalil, a 42-year-old reporter for the Lebanese daily Al-Akhbar. The Israeli military said it was reviewing the incident. Rescuers and the newspaper confirmed Khalil's death.

stories.title: Prince Harry arrives in Kyiv in a show of support
stories.summary: Prince Harry arrived in Kyiv in a show of support for Ukraine at a time when global attention has shifted toward the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: US-Israeli war on Iran will push 30 million back into poverty, UN warns
stories.summary: The UNDP has warned that a US-Israeli military campaign against Iran could push 30 million people back into poverty. The chief concern is disruption to fuel and fertiliser supplies caused by a potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which would severely impact global crop yields.

stories.summary:

stories.title: PM meets astronauts selected for China's space mission, hopes it will 'usher in era of space research'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met astronauts Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, who were selected for China's manned space program. Sharif expressed hope the mission would usher in a new era of space research for Pakistan.

stories.title: US weapons supplies continue, but more air defense systems needed – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that the United States continues shipping weapons to Ukraine but said there remains a significant shortage of air defense systems. He called for additional deliveries to strengthen Ukraine's defensive capabilities.

stories.title: Israel signs $200m munitions deal with Elbit for 'busy decade'
stories.summary: Israel signed a $200 million deal with defense contractor Elbit Systems for aerial munitions. Officials described the purchase as part of preparations for what they called a "busy decade" ahead.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland President Heads to UAE On Visit
stories.summary: Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi Irro departed from Hargeisa for Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on Thursday. The presidency described the trip as a private visit.

stories.title: ‘Hellhole on the planet’: Trump reposts critique targeting India, China over birthright citizenship
stories.summary: Former President Trump reposted comments by conservative author Michael Savage criticizing India and China over birthright citizenship. Savage characterized the policy as a loophole enabling chain migration from those countries.

stories.title: Journalist recalls Israeli strike killing Amal Khalil in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Zainab Faraj recounted the final moments of fellow journalist Amal Khalil, who was killed in an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon. The account highlights the dangers faced by media workers covering the conflict in the region.

stories.title: Kuwait releases journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin after acquittal
stories.summary: Kuwaiti-American journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin was released from custody in Kuwait following his acquittal. He had been arrested in early March 2026 after posting social media images related to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Warner Bros shareholders approve Paramount’s takeover
stories.summary: Warner Bros shareholders have voted to approve a takeover by Paramount. Regulatory scrutiny is expected from authorities in both Washington and London, who will examine the merger's potential market impact before it can proceed.

stories.title: It’s a Russian truck massacre as more Ukrainian drones surge into the logistical zone
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones are increasingly striking Russian logistical targets, hitting trucks deep in the Russian rear to disrupt supply lines feeding front-line regiments.

stories.title: Russia’s Justice Ministry refuses to accept mandatory ‘foreign agent’ reports from pro-Kremlin blogger
stories.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry is reportedly refusing to accept mandatory foreign-agent reports from Roman Alekhin, a pro-Kremlin blogger whom Russian authorities themselves designated a foreign agent. Alekhin disclosed the refusal publicly.

stories.title: Amal Khalil: The fearless journalist, killed by Israel, who embodied southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil, a veteran correspondent for Al-Akhbar, was killed by Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. She was widely remembered for decades of reporting on Israeli occupation and was described as generous and brave by colleagues.

stories.title: Protest at RAF Fairford over UK's role in US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: The Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, the Stop the War Coalition, and the Fairford Movement announced a protest at RAF Fairford over the UK's role in the US-Israeli war on Iran. The demonstration is scheduled for the following Saturday outside the base.

stories.title: Defense Forces thwart Russian attempt to seize Bochkovе in Kharkiv sector
stories.summary: Ukraine's 16th Army Corps repelled a Russian attempt to capture the settlement of Bochkove in the Kharkiv sector. Ukrainian servicemen demonstrated how they prevented Russian forces from seizing the position in the area.

stories.title: South Africa's president suspends police chief after court charges
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa suspended national police chief Fannie Masemola following court charges, citing the critical importance of the role in the country's fight against crime.

stories.title: UK: Health data volunteered by 500,000 people to Biobank charity listed for sale on Alibaba in China
stories.summary: The British government is investigating how health data from approximately 500,000 volunteers to the UK Biobank charity appeared listed for sale by three vendors on China's Alibaba e-commerce platform. The data had originally been donated for medical research purposes.

stories.title: Warner Bros investors back US$110 billion merger with Paramount Skydance
stories.summary: Warner Bros Discovery shareholders voted on Thursday to approve a proposed US$110 billion merger with Paramount Skydance. However, investors cast an advisory vote against executive compensation packages tied to the deal, including a potential payout of up to US$887 million for CEO David Zaslav. The merger still requires regulatory approval.

stories.title: EU formally approves €90bn Ukraine loan and 20th sanctions package against Russia
stories.summary: EU leaders finalized a €90 billion loan for Ukraine on Thursday, ending a diplomatic deadlock in time for summit talks in Cyprus that will include Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The bloc also approved a 20th package of sanctions against Russia. Leaders are expected to discuss responses to surging energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: US Marine Corps, Navy join forces to combat insufficient amphibious fleet size
stories.summary: The two services will work together to boost the country's amphibious fleet size and availability after the readiness rate of its ships dropped in 2025.

stories.title: US Marine Corps, Navy joins forces to combat insufficient amphibious fleet size
stories.summary: The US Marine Corps and Navy announced they will collaborate to increase the country's amphibious fleet size and availability. The decision follows a decline in readiness rates for amphibious ships in 2025.

stories.title: Exclusive: UK's Aviva Investors bought $108m of Israeli government bonds in January sale
stories.summary: UK-based Aviva Investors purchased approximately $108 million in Israeli government bonds during a January sale, making it one of the largest international buyers. The asset management arm of the insurance giant subsequently reduced its stake quietly.

stories.title: As Iran saps US focus, the troop math for monitoring a Ukraine peace deal looks grim
stories.summary: Military planners face significant challenges in assembling sufficient troops to monitor a potential Ukraine ceasefire, as the US conflict with Iran diverts attention and resources. The proposed monitoring coalition has also not resolved what rules of engagement its forces would operate under once a ceasefire takes effect.

stories.title: Women speak of violence experienced during childbirth in DR Congo
stories.summary: A viral video showing a doctor striking a young woman shortly after she gave birth in a Kinshasa hospital has sparked outrage across the Democratic Republic of Congo. Women have come forward to describe violence they experienced during childbirth in the country.

stories.title: Israel's supreme court hears petitions on Oct 7 state inquiry
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court on Thursday heard petitions seeking to compel the government to establish a state inquiry into the security and intelligence failures that led to the 7 October attacks.

stories.title: Israel supreme court hears petitions on Oct 7 state inquiry
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court examined petitions seeking to compel the government to establish a formal state inquiry into the security failures that led to the October 7 attacks.

stories.title: Iran executes another 'political prisoner', NGO says
stories.summary: Iran executed a man convicted of membership in the banned opposition group MEK and collaboration with Israel. An NGO described the executed individual as a "political prisoner."

stories.title: EU leaders gather in Cyprus as Middle East tensions shape summit agenda
stories.summary: EU leaders convened in Cyprus for a summit shaped by Middle East tensions, with the island's proximity to Israel and Lebanon and its close regional ties placing geopolitical developments at the center of discussions.

stories.title: Israel committed war crime by killing journalist, Lebanon says
stories.summary: Lebanon's government accused Israel of committing a war crime after a Lebanese journalist was killed in a targeted Israeli strike in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Tanzania poll violence claimed 518 lives: government enquiry
stories.summary: A government-appointed commission in Tanzania reported that 518 people were killed in violence surrounding the country's October general election. The official figure is far lower than opposition estimates, which put the death toll in the thousands.

stories.title: Russia's claims of full control over Luhansk region are untrue — Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected Russian claims of having captured over 700 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory and gaining full control of the Luhansk region. Zelensky stated that these assertions do not correspond to reality.

stories.title: US military board, seize another ship in international waters
stories.summary: The Pentagon released video showing US soldiers descending from helicopters to board and seize a ship in international waters. No further details on the vessel's origin or cargo were provided in the initial report.

stories.title: Trump says Navy will ‘shoot and kill’ boats laying mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated on Thursday that the Navy would shoot and destroy small boats attempting to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The threat is directed at Iran and follows Trump's repeated claims that Iran's larger naval vessels have been neutralized as part of ongoing US pressure on Tehran.

stories.title: ADB deepens Pakistan engagement with $3.67bn commitments, targets fiscal reform and minerals
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank committed $3.67 billion to Pakistan in 2025, a 22 percent increase from the previous year. New areas of engagement include the mineral sector, alongside continued support for fiscal reform and public-sector lending.

stories.title: US-Kuwaiti journalist held in Kuwait over social media posts acquitted, lawyers say
stories.summary: Kuwaiti-American journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin has been acquitted in Kuwait of charges including spreading false information. He had been arrested after reposting social media images related to the Iran war.

stories.title: Shadow of failed 1983 agreement haunts new Israeli-Lebanon talks
stories.summary: Lebanon is preparing to resume direct negotiations with Israel, but the talks are shadowed by the failed May 17, 1983 agreement that was signed but never implemented. President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam face opposition from Hezbollah, which has rejected compromise and issued veiled threats against Lebanon's leadership.

stories.title: Ukraine’s new “Khmarinka” drone copies Russia’s Molniya – cheap, catapult-launched, 50 km strike range
stories.summary: Ukrainian General Chereshnya delivered the first 150 units of the new "Khmarinka" drone — a cheap, catapult-launched system with a 50 km strike range modeled on Russia's Molniya — to frontline brigades. The drone is expected to be listed on Ukraine's Brave1 defense marketplace.

stories.title: Every 1ºC of global warming avoided could halve number of world heritage sites exposed to major disruption: Unesco
stories.summary: A UNESCO global assessment found that every 1°C of global warming avoided could halve the number of World Heritage sites, Biosphere Reserves, and Global Geoparks exposed to major disruption by century's end. The report warned that inaction could push natural systems in over one-quarter of sites past critical tipping points by 2050.

stories.title: Lebanon Latest: Israel attacks kill journalist and target first responders
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed a journalist and targeted first responders while a fragile ceasefire remained in place. The attacks drew condemnation from Lebanese officials.

stories.title: Lebanon to seek ceasefire extension in U.S.-hosted talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon plans to seek an extension of the U.S.-mediated ceasefire with Israel during upcoming talks hosted by the United States. Despite a significant reduction in violence, Israeli troops have seized a self-declared buffer zone in southern Lebanon and sporadic attacks continue.

stories.title: Why Iran war is the surest sign that the US is in decline
stories.summary: Chinese state media and analysts are increasingly characterizing the US military campaign against Iran as evidence of declining American global dominance. The Communist Party newspaper People's Daily published a critique on Thursday accusing Washington of shifting from an international rule-builder to a "predatory hegemon," warning this would undermine US prosperity and influence.

stories.title: Internal Israeli debate and the costs to Diaspora Jewry - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's exercise of military force in self-defense has, in some instances, generated backlash against Jewish communities outside Israel. The article examines how internal Israeli debates carry consequences for Diaspora Jewry worldwide.

stories.title: President: Ukraine expects to receive first tranche of EU loan in late May or early June
stories.summary: Ukraine expects to receive the first tranche of the EU's €90 billion loan in late May or early June. Ukrainian officials said they have been working to unlock the loan and implement the 20th package of EU sanctions against Russia.

stories.title: US to ‘shoot and kill’ Iranian boats laying mines in Hormuz, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the US Navy to shoot and destroy any boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, the US announced it had intercepted another tanker carrying Iranian oil. Trump also commented on alleged infighting within Iran's leadership.

stories.title: BP board suffers triple climate rebellion from shareholders
stories.summary: At BP's first annual general meeting under new leadership, more than 50% of voting shareholders opposed the company's plans to scrap its existing climate reporting. Shareholders also voted against replacing in-person annual meetings with online-only events, delivering a triple rebuke to the board on climate-related resolutions.

stories.title: UN might keep presence in south Lebanon once UNIFIL mandate ends, says official
stories.summary: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix indicated that the UN may maintain a presence in southern Lebanon after the UNIFIL mandate expires. He noted that Beirut has clearly expressed its desire to retain a UN presence in the area.

stories.title: Trump orders US Navy to destroy boats laying mines in Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the US Navy to shoot and destroy any vessel laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz. He posted that mine sweepers were already clearing the strait. The directive was aimed at increasing pressure on Iran to reopen the crucial sea passage.

stories.title: Pakistan Minister, U.S. envoy discuss efforts for 2nd round of U.S.-Iran talks
stories.summary: A Pakistani minister met with the U.S. envoy to discuss diplomatic efforts aimed at facilitating a second round of U.S.-Iran negotiations. The meeting reflects intensified engagement to bring Tehran and Washington back to the negotiating table.

stories.title: UK to pay for French officers to deport asylum seekers from war-torn countries
stories.summary: The United Kingdom will fund 200 French officers to detain and deport asylum seekers from 10 nationalities under a new £660 million UK-France agreement. A removal site in Dunkirk will hold people from countries including Eritrea, Afghanistan, Iran, and Sudan who are attempting Channel crossings in small boats.

stories.title: Warner Bros Discovery vote to approve $110bn merger with Paramount Skydance
stories.summary: Warner Bros Discovery shareholders voted overwhelmingly on Thursday to approve a $110 billion merger with Paramount Skydance, parent company of CBS News. However, they rejected proposed executive compensation packages, including a $550 million payout for outgoing CEO David Zaslav. The merger still requires government approval and faces a potential lawsuit.

stories.title: Three men guilty of repeatedly raping woman on Brighton beach in ‘predatory, callous’ attack
stories.summary: Three men were found guilty at Hove Crown Court of repeatedly raping a woman on Brighton beach. The attack occurred in the early hours of October 4 after the victim became separated from friends during a night out. One man filmed the assault while the other two carried it out.

stories.title: More than 1,600 candidates in May local elections make major pro-Palestine pledge
stories.summary: More than 1,600 candidates running in May local elections in the UK have signed a pledge organized by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign. The pledge commits them to support Palestinian rights if elected.

stories.title: IRGC‑linked Tasnim warns of risks to undersea cables below Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC-linked Tasnim news agency warned of risks to undersea communications cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz, amid broader concerns about attacks on data infrastructure in conflict zones including the Red Sea.

stories.title: South Africa coal phase-out delay could cause 32,000 deaths: report
stories.summary: Climate rights groups warned that delaying the closure of South Africa's coal-fired power plants could cause up to 32,000 preventable deaths between 2026 and 2050.

stories.title: Take action over officials in Kyrgyzstan ‘helping Russia evade sanctions’, MPs and peers say
stories.summary: More than 20 British MPs and peers have urged the UK foreign secretary to impose sanctions on Kyrgyz officials allegedly facilitating Russian sanctions evasion. They specifically cited Kyrgyzstan's role in hosting infrastructure for the ruble-pegged cryptocurrency A7A5, calling for personal sanctions against three top Kyrgyz officials.

stories.title: Sumud flotilla marks biggest Gaza aid effort as fleet doubles
stories.summary: The Gaza-bound Sumud Flotilla is assembling in Italy with a fleet that has officially surpassed last year's size as additional vessels join the civilian aid mission. It is described as the biggest Gaza aid flotilla effort to date.

stories.title: New Paris exhibition showcases work of US photographer and war reporter Lee Miller
stories.summary: The Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris is hosting a major retrospective exhibition of American photographer and war reporter Lee Miller. The show traces Miller's career across New York, Paris, Cairo, and London, highlighting her work capturing pivotal moments with what curators describe as rare sensitivity and audacity.

stories.title: Ukraine launches reciprocal strikes against Russia’s energy sector, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is conducting reciprocal strikes against Russia's energy sector in response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. The strikes are targeting facilities deemed critical to Russia's operations.

stories.title: PPP opposes proposed park project at Margalla’s foothills
stories.summary: Pakistan's PPP opposed a government proposal to build a park on 1,000 kanal at the foothills of the Margalla Hills in Islamabad. The project was announced following a meeting on CDA issues chaired by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

stories.title: After collapse and controversy, Adelaide writers’ week has a new director: ‘I don’t envy anyone in this position’
stories.summary: Rosemarie Milsom, founder and director of the Newcastle Writers Festival, has been appointed the new director of Adelaide Writers' Week. She replaces Louise Adler following the festival's collapse after the board disinvited Palestinian-Australian author Randa Abdel-Fattah over past comments about Israel and Zionism.

stories.title: Beijing’s emphasis on security weighing on US firms’ optimism: AmCham China
stories.summary: The American Chamber of Commerce in China reported that US firms acknowledged improvements in China's regulatory environment and greater openness. However, long-standing concerns over market access and Beijing's emphasis on national security continue to dampen business optimism. Expectations for President Trump's upcoming visit to China remain muted.

stories.title: Trump claims US has 'total control' over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump claimed on his TruthSocial platform that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, stating it was "sealed up tight" until Iran agrees to a deal. He also alleged infighting between hardliners and moderates within Iran's leadership.

stories.title: Series of terrorist attacks orchestrated by Russia thwarted at high schools in Kirovohrad and Odesa regions
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service and National Police thwarted a series of planned terrorist attacks at high schools in the Kirovohrad and Odesa regions. Authorities said the attacks were orchestrated by Russia.

stories.title: Who was Amal Khalil, the Lebanese journalist killed by Israel?
stories.summary: Amal Khalil, a veteran Lebanese journalist, was killed in an Israeli strike and is being mourned nationwide. She was known for decades of fearless reporting from southern Lebanon.

stories.title: EXCLUSIVE: Lockheed exits Navy trainer aircraft competition
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin has withdrawn from the US Navy's Undergraduate Jet Training System competition. The remaining competitors for the trainer aircraft contract are Sierra Nevada Corporation, Boeing, and Textron subsidiary Beechcraft in partnership with Leonardo.

stories.title: Nigerian artist Eniwaye Oluwaseyi explores memory, identity in Paris show
stories.summary: Nigerian artist Eniwaye Oluwaseyi is presenting a double exhibition titled "Buried roots up in the air" in Paris and Luxembourg. The show features multi-layered compositions exploring personal memories, belonging, identity, and cultural roots.

stories.title: Trump, his ‘low IQ’ slur, and the right’s race obsession
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump used the phrase "low IQ person" to attack Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson and House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries, both prominent Black figures. The insult carries racial overtones in the United States and drew widespread attention.

stories.title: Bedlam erupts in Supreme Court as pro-government activists try to force their way into Oct. 7 inquiry hearing
stories.summary: Pro-government activists attempted to force their way into an Israeli Supreme Court hearing on petitions demanding a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks. Demonstrators chanted "Judge the judges" outside. The judges indicated they may delay a ruling until after the election.

stories.title: 9 killed in armed attack at mining site in Balochistan’s Chagai
stories.summary: Unidentified gunmen attacked a copper and gold mining site operated by National Resources Limited in Chagai district, Balochistan, killing at least nine people. Security forces, including the Frontier Corps, responded and launched a clearance operation in the area.

stories.title: Photo of migrant family separation in US scoops World Press prize
stories.summary: A photograph by Carol Guzy of ZUMA Press and iWitness for the Miami Herald won the 2025 World Press Photo of the Year Award on Thursday. The image depicts the moment US Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers arrested an Ecuadoran man named Luis after a court hearing, as his family desperately clung to him.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz directs that transport nationwide be gradually shifted to EVs
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed a gradual nationwide shift of transport to electric vehicles during a meeting on energy security. He noted that government measures had averted an energy crisis despite global disruptions linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Exploding shells may turn the Apache helicopter into a drone hunter
stories.summary: The US Army is exploring the use of exploding proximity-fused shells fired from Apache helicopters to counter small drones. The concept originated from a soldier's proposal and aims to incorporate lessons learned from drone warfare in Ukraine and conflicts involving Iran.

stories.title: US says forces boarded tanker carrying Iranian oil
stories.summary: The US Defense Department announced its forces boarded a vessel in the Indian Ocean that was transporting Iranian oil. The action came as an Iranian official said Tehran had collected its first proceeds from tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: How Iran war has triggered soaring cost of medicines
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war has caused the cost of medicines to surge in multiple countries. Pharmacists report that prices of painkillers have more than quadrupled in some locations.

stories.title: Restrictions deepen for Palestinians in Iraq, impacting cooking
stories.summary: Palestinians in Iraq, many originating from villages near Haifa as well as Jaffa, Nablus, and Jerusalem, face deepening restrictions that are affecting daily life including access to cooking supplies.

stories.title: 7-year-old girl critically injured by Iranian missile is discharged from hospital
stories.summary: A seven-year-old girl critically injured by an Iranian missile strike on the Israeli city of Arad on March 21 has been discharged from the hospital. She underwent a series of surgeries and will continue recovery at home.

stories.title: Tennessee police investigate after finding bones believed to be from three children
stories.summary: Memphis, Tennessee police discovered human remains believed to belong to three children aged approximately three to seven in a wooded area. The police chief said the remains had likely been there for several years and did not match any local missing persons reports. An investigation is underway.

stories.title: Virginia court blocks redistricting map approved by voters in win for GOP
stories.summary: A Virginia court on Wednesday blocked a voter-approved congressional redistricting map that Democrats had hoped would help them gain seats in midterm elections. The state attorney general vowed to appeal. President Trump had previously pushed Republicans to pursue redistricting efforts in states including Texas.

stories.title: EU approves massive loan to help Ukraine after Hungary lifts its veto
stories.summary: The European Union approved a major loan package on Thursday to support Ukraine's economic and military needs for the next two years, after Hungary lifted its veto. The EU also adopted a new round of sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine. The decisions were finalized ahead of summit talks in Cyprus.

stories.title: Lebanon to seek ceasefire extension in US-hosted talks with Israel
stories.summary: The United States is hosting a second round of talks between Lebanese and Israeli envoys on Thursday, with Lebanon seeking an extension of the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire set to expire Sunday. Israeli strikes killed at least five people including a journalist the previous day. Israeli forces maintain a self-declared buffer zone in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Fifa World Cup: Italy underwhelmed by Trump envoy’s suggestion they should replace Iran
stories.summary: US special envoy Paolo Zampolli suggested to President Trump and FIFA head Gianni Infantino that Italy should replace Iran at this year's US-hosted FIFA World Cup. The proposal was met with mixed reactions in Italy, with fans expressing embarrassment and apathy, and Italian media noting the idea felt familiar.

stories.title: DOD completes $1B investment in L3Harris missile unit
stories.summary: The US Department of Defense has completed a $1 billion investment in L3Harris Technologies' solid-rocket-motor business. L3Harris will retain an 80% stake in the unit, which is transitioning to become a publicly traded company.

stories.title: The Israel-Lebanon truce is a turning point - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece characterizes the truce between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon as a significant turning point. The author argues that additional measures are needed to reduce Hezbollah's influence in the broader region.

stories.title: Europe cancels thousands of flights amid Middle East fuel shock
stories.summary: Soaring fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict are forcing European airlines to cancel thousands of flights and raise ticket prices. Airlines in Germany have grounded parts of their fleets, while fares in France are rising. The energy crisis threatens to disrupt summer travel plans across the continent.

stories.title: Trump envoy asks FIFA to replace Iran with Italy at World Cup
stories.summary: A U.S. envoy to President Donald Trump asked FIFA to replace Iran with Italy at the upcoming World Cup, according to a report by the Financial Times.

stories.title: SSU drones damage three oil tanks at Russian Gorky pumping station
stories.summary: Drones from the Security Service of Ukraine's Special Operations Center 'A' struck the Gorky oil pumping station in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region on the night of April 23, damaging three oil storage tanks.

stories.title: Iran’s new internet litmus test ensures only pro-regime voices will be heard online, experts warn
stories.summary: Iran partially rolled back internet restrictions, but experts warn the regime's new filtering system serves as a tool to amplify pro-government propaganda to Western audiences while silencing dissenting voices.

stories.title: Inside China, artificial intelligence is a snake eating its own tail
stories.summary: AI researchers in China are encountering "model collapse," a phenomenon where artificial intelligence models trained on their own synthetic outputs degrade over successive generations. The issue highlights growing challenges in China's AI development ecosystem.

stories.title: Fire at Novokuybyshevsk: Ukraine targets the chemical inputs behind Russia’s explosives production
stories.summary: Ukraine struck the Novokuybyshevsk industrial complex in Russia for the second reported time since October 2025, targeting chemical facilities linked to explosives production. The previous drone strike had shut down primary processing at the site.

stories.title: 2 IDF aircraft mechanics charged with spying for Iran, leaking fighter jet info
stories.summary: Two IDF aircraft mechanics serving at Tel Nof Airbase have been charged with spying for Iran. The pair allegedly sent a diagram of an aircraft engine and photos of an aviation instructor to an Iranian handler, in one of the most serious recent espionage incidents.

stories.title: Iran economy looks set to withstand US naval blockade, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts say Iran's economy appears capable of withstanding the US naval blockade in the near term. The closure of Iranian ports is expected to take weeks or months to significantly impact the economy, contrary to claims of immediate collapse.

stories.title: Libya oscillates between cooperation and illusion
stories.summary: For the first time, representatives from both sides of Libya's political divide are participating in Flintlock, a U.S.-led multinational military exercise, raising questions about whether this signals progress toward reunification.

stories.title: UN warns Libya at 'critical' crossroads amid deepening divisions
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that Libya is at a "critical" crossroads, facing deep political fragmentation, economic distortions, and delayed elections that threaten the country's stability.

stories.title: AI startup Cursor with Pakistani co-founder set for $60bn deal with SpaceX
stories.summary: AI code-generation startup Cursor, co-founded by Pakistani-born Sualeh Asif, has reportedly secured a $60 billion acquisition deal with Elon Musk's SpaceX. SpaceX announced it obtained the right to acquire Cursor later this year, positioning itself in the competitive AI-assisted coding market.

stories.title: Samsung workers rally in South Korea, demanding higher pay, threatening to strike
stories.summary: Samsung's labor union, representing approximately 74,000 workers in South Korea, held a rally demanding higher pay and threatened to strike. The union argued the company had not offered adequate compensation despite strong financial performance.

stories.title: Multi-sourcing, MOSA, and producibility form next-level defense acquisition reform
stories.summary: A defense policy analysis argues the Pentagon should embrace multi-sourcing, Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA), and producibility principles to reform defense acquisition. The recommendation calls for moving away from proprietary products toward multi-sourced, competitive programs to build more resilient supply chains.

stories.title: Turkey opts for silence on von der Leyen remarks to avoid straining EU ties
stories.summary: Turkey chose not to respond publicly to remarks by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen that characterized Ankara as a negative influence, opting for restraint after Brussels issued a clarification amid economic and strategic considerations.

stories.title: Nigel Clarke: “Preserving fiscal sustainability must be Africa’s priority” [Interview]
stories.summary: In an interview, Nigel Clarke argued that preserving fiscal sustainability must be Africa's top priority as the continent's economies face imported inflation, dependence on international markets, and structural vulnerabilities from a crisis not of their making.

stories.title: Autonomous weapons will be 'key part' of US warfare: Joint Chiefs chairman
stories.summary: Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine stated that autonomous weapons systems will be a key component of future US military operations. The Pentagon is exploring autonomous technology for drones and command-and-control functions, though members of Congress have raised concerns about oversight.

stories.title: Woman in occupied Ukraine jailed 14 years for buying Kyiv war bonds
stories.summary: A woman in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, was sentenced to 14 years in prison after the FSB caught her purchasing Ukrainian war bonds worth approximately $3,600 through a mobile app.

stories.title: ‘The world’s most impossible job’: Who will lead the United Nations next?
stories.summary: Four candidates vying to succeed António Guterres as United Nations secretary-general pledged on Wednesday to revitalize the organization through reform while upholding peacekeeping and development principles. The next leader, who will take office at the start of next year, faces the challenge of restoring the credibility of an institution whose global influence has significantly declined.

stories.title: Mexico reopens famed pyramids under heavy police presence after deadly shooting
stories.summary: Mexico's Teotihuacan archaeological site reopened on Wednesday under heavy police presence following a shooting two days earlier in which a gunman killed a Canadian woman and wounded 13 others at the Pyramid of the Moon. Fewer tourists than usual visited the site. The incident has raised scrutiny of security at Mexico's cultural sites ahead of its co-hosting of the World Cup.

stories.title: Senate Democrats challenge Russian oil waiver—Moscow revenues hit two-year high
stories.summary: U.S. Senate Democrats challenged a Treasury Department waiver on Russian oil, noting that Moscow's oil revenues have reached a two-year high. A Delaware senator questioned the Treasury Secretary on the policy's effects using March export data.

stories.title: How Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was pursued and killed by Israel
stories.summary: New details have emerged about how Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was pursued and killed by Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. Khalil was a veteran correspondent for the daily newspaper Al-Akhbar.

stories.title: KSE-100 plunges below 170,000-mark as bears maintain control of PSX
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell over 2,700 points, dropping below 170,000 to 168,828 during intraday trading on Thursday. The decline was driven by bearish sentiment linked to stalled US-Iran talks and rising oil prices amid Middle East uncertainty.

stories.title: Lebanese journalist killed in Israeli attack had spoken of death threat
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil, 43, was killed in an Israeli attack on Wednesday in southern Lebanon. Khalil, who worked for al-Akhbar newspaper, had previously reported receiving a death threat from an unidentified Israeli phone number warning her to leave the area. Media rights groups have condemned the killing.

stories.title: At least 10 killed in Pakistan mining project attack: officials
stories.summary: Approximately 40 militants on motorcycles and other vehicles attacked a mining project site operated by Pakistani company NRL in the Darigwan area of Chagai district, Balochistan, on April 22. At least 10 people were killed in the assault, according to officials.

stories.title: Investigators Search Dagestan Government Offices Over Illegal Permits Linked to Flood Damage
stories.summary: Investigators searched government offices in Dagestan over allegedly illegal construction permits linked to flood damage. The floods, caused by heavy rainfall in late March and early April, killed at least seven people and displaced over 6,200.

stories.title: Lebanese PM says no deal with Israel without troop withdrawal
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam stated that no agreement with Israel is possible without a full withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon, calling the occupation non-negotiable.

stories.title: ‘Solutions, not slogans’: Gaza holds first election in 21 years
stories.summary: The city of Deir el-Balah held Gaza's first local election in 21 years amid widespread war damage. Residents participating in the vote called for practical solutions rather than slogans.

stories.title: Makan Nasiri, the only child still missing from the school bombed in Iran
stories.summary: Iranian authorities have told the parents of seven-year-old Makan Nasiri that the search for his remains has been closed after nearly seven weeks. He is the only child still missing from a school bombing in Iran.

stories.title: Iran says won't reopen Hormuz if U.S. upholds naval blockade
stories.summary: Iran declared it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the US maintains its naval blockade. Despite a truce pausing strikes in the region, both sides continue exerting economic pressure over the crucial trade route.

stories.title: Iran: Daily life shadowed by war, scarcity and fear
stories.summary: A U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports aims to pressure Tehran's government, but ordinary Iranians are bearing the brunt of the effects, facing growing exhaustion from scarcity and the broader conflict.

stories.title: Dr Samah Jabr on what the Palestinian psyche can teach the world
stories.summary: Palestinian psychiatrist Dr. Samah Jabr discussed psychological warfare and the intersection of geopolitics and mental health in the context of the Palestinian experience.

stories.title: Slovakia’s Fico will skip Moscow’s parade but still lay flowers in the Kremlin
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico announced he will skip Moscow's 9 May Victory Day parade but will still visit the Kremlin to lay flowers at its wall. Fico characterized the visit as a "pilgrimage for peace," maintaining his position as one of the EU's most openly pro-Russian leaders.

stories.title: Iranian monarchist leader Reza Pahlavi hit with paint in Berlin
stories.summary: Exiled Iranian monarchist leader Reza Pahlavi was struck with a bucket of paint by a demonstrator as he left a press conference in Berlin, Germany.

stories.title: Defects – not jumping tourists – caused deadly Xinjiang bridge collapse: report
stories.summary: Chinese authorities in Xinjiang concluded that construction defects, management failures, and legal violations caused the deadly Jiangjun Bridge collapse at Xiata Scenic Area in Yili last August, not tourist behavior. The incident killed five people and injured 24 when the suspension bridge tilted.

stories.title: China targets greener AI data centres, heavy industry in push to meet 2030 climate goals
stories.summary: China issued an 18-point policy document aimed at reducing carbon emissions across strategic sectors, including energy-intensive AI data centers, steel, and chemicals. The guidelines are part of Beijing's push to meet its 2030 climate targets amid energy price volatility linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Infiltration from Within: Israelis recruited to spy for enemy countries
stories.summary: An investigation has detailed cases of Israelis recruited to spy for enemy countries, exposing intelligence failures. The report covers espionage incidents from early security breaches through the October 7 attacks and the war with Iran.

stories.title: War in Lebanon: Most people 'are severely traumatised', CARE country director says
stories.summary: CARE's country director for Lebanon, Michael Adams, told FRANCE 24 that the ceasefire in Lebanon remains very fragile, with ongoing violations undermining public confidence. He described widespread displacement, with many people living in streets, cars, parks, or stadiums, and said most of the population is severely traumatized by the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers looting homes in Lebanon on large scale, report says
stories.summary: A report alleges that Israeli soldiers have been looting civilian homes in southern Lebanon on a large scale, taking items including motorbikes, televisions, and furniture, with little accountability.

stories.title: Syrskyi: Defense Forces liberate more than 480 square kilometers from Russian forces since February
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Ukrainian Defense Forces have liberated more than 480 square kilometers of territory from Russian forces since early February.

stories.title: Iran principlists call for ships to be seized in Straight of Hormuz: Press review
stories.summary: Iranian principlist political figures are calling for the seizure of ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, a seven-year-old child was reported killed in an Israeli strike on a school in Minab, Iran.

stories.title: KSA–Turkey rail line planned linking holy cities to Istanbul
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and Turkey are advancing plans for a railway connecting the holy cities of Makkah and Medina to Istanbul, with the route passing through Jordan and Syria.

stories.title: What Orban's exit means for the future of EU-Israel relations
stories.summary: The defeat of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is seen as a strategic setback for Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, raising questions about the durability of Israel's alliances within the European Union.

stories.title: Iran tightens control of Hormuz after US calls off renewed attacks
stories.summary: Iran seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz, tightening control over the strategic waterway after US President Donald Trump announced an indefinite halt to attacks. There were no signs of peace talks restarting between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: US hosts talks as Lebanon seeks ceasefire extension with Israel
stories.summary: The United States hosted talks as Lebanon sought to extend a US-mediated ceasefire with Israel, set to expire on Sunday. While violence has significantly decreased, attacks in southern Lebanon have continued.

stories.title: Pentagon denies reported assessment that de-mining Hormuz will take six months
stories.summary: The Pentagon denied a Washington Post report, based on a classified congressional briefing, estimating that de-mining the Strait of Hormuz could take six months. Iran claims it has begun collecting transit tolls from shipping in the strait.

stories.title: EU approves US$106 billion loan to Ukraine after Hungary lifts veto
stories.summary: The European Union approved a loan package of approximately $106 billion (€90 billion) to support Ukraine's economic and military needs over the next two years, after Hungary lifted its veto. A new round of sanctions against Russia was also adopted, having been delayed for months by Hungarian and Slovak opposition.

stories.title: Israel kills five in Lebanon as Beirut seeks 'truce' extension
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed five people in Lebanon, including veteran journalist Amal Khalil, despite an existing ceasefire. Beirut condemned the attacks as war crimes and sought an extension of the truce.

stories.title: Lebanese village replaces IDF-gifted Jesus statue with replica of crucifix smashed by soldier
stories.summary: Residents of a Lebanese village, assisted by an Italian UNIFIL battalion, replaced an IDF-gifted Jesus statue with a replica of the original crucifix that had been broken by an Israeli soldier.

stories.title: Israel quietly pushes plans for another West Bank settlement
stories.summary: Israel is moving to reopen the dismantled Ganim settlement in the occupied West Bank, part of a broader effort to quietly accelerate settlement expansion in the territory.

stories.title: Pope Leo stresses importance of dialogue on Africa trip
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV visited four African countries, calling for peace, unity, and dialogue. He criticized war, corruption, and inequality, urging leaders to prioritize the well-being of their people.

stories.title: Pope Leo stressed importance of dialogue on Africa trip
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV visited four African countries, calling for peace, unity, and dialogue while criticizing war, corruption, and inequality. He urged leaders across the continent to prioritize the welfare of their people.

stories.title: Pope Leo's Africa trip pushes peace and unity
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV visited four African countries, calling for peace, unity, and dialogue. During the trip, he criticized war, corruption, and inequality, urging African leaders to prioritize the welfare of their populations.

stories.title: Iran war pushing more than 30 million back into poverty: UN
stories.summary: The UN's development chief warned that the war involving Iran is pushing more than 30 million people back into poverty due to fuel and fertilizer shortages caused by the conflict.

stories.title: Hong Kong airport’s revenue ‘expected to grow by up to 10%’ despite Mideast war
stories.summary: Hong Kong International Airport expects revenue growth of up to 10% this year despite disruptions from the Iran war, according to Airport Authority CEO Vivian Cheung. She aims to position the facility as an alternative aviation hub as Middle Eastern airports face conflict-related flight cancellations.

stories.title: Dutch prosecutors seek 30-year sentence for alleged Syrian torturer
stories.summary: Dutch prosecutors have requested a 30-year prison sentence for a Syrian man accused of torturing and raping prisoners while serving as a member of a militia linked to the Assad regime.

stories.title: Duterte to face ICC trial after judges confirm murder charges
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court confirmed murder charges as crimes against humanity against former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, paving the way for a trial related to his anti-drug campaign.

stories.title: Iran economy looks set to withstand US naval blockade
stories.summary: Analysts assess that while the US naval blockade of Iran will reduce the country's oil output in the coming weeks, it is unlikely to cripple Iran's broader economy.

stories.title: Voting underway in key Indian states of West Bengal, Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Voting began Thursday in India's West Bengal and Tamil Nadu states, with tens of millions casting ballots. In West Bengal, the first phase covered 152 of 294 assembly constituencies. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP is seeking to gain ground in these opposition-held states.

stories.title: In Dnipro, death toll after Russian strike climbs to three, with 10 injured
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the city of Dnipro killed three people and injured ten others, with the death toll climbing after the initial attack.

stories.title: Protester hurls red fluid at Reza Pahlavi during Germany visit
stories.summary: Exiled former Iranian crown prince Reza Pahlavi was splashed with red fluid by an activist during a visit to Berlin, Germany.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Substitutes Close to U.S.$5 Billion Worth of Imports in Nine Months
stories.summary: Ethiopia's Industry Minister Melaku Alebel reported that the country substituted approximately $4.85 billion worth of imports with locally produced goods over the past nine months, marking a milestone in its industrial transformation.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Prime Minister Abiy Receives Djibouti Foreign Minister, Discusses Bilateral Cooperation
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed hosted Djibouti's Foreign Minister Abdoulkader Houssain Omar in Addis Ababa for discussions on bilateral cooperation between the two neighboring nations.

stories.title: Africa: Prime Minister Abiy Pledges Ethiopia's Commitment to Sharing Ai Experience Across Africa
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed reaffirmed Ethiopia's commitment to sharing its artificial intelligence experience with other African nations and strengthening continental partnerships in emerging technology.

stories.title: As US-Iran war chokes Hormuz, can Central Asia’s ‘Middle Corridor’ rise to the rescue?
stories.summary: The conflict between the US-Israel coalition and Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, prompting interest in Central Asia's "Middle Corridor" as an alternative trade route. The Trans-Caspian International Transport Route connects China to Europe via Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey.

stories.title: China can offer Gulf states more than just a security umbrella
stories.summary: The Iran war has severely disrupted Gulf states' security architecture and economic stability, with Iranian strikes hitting ports, energy terminals, and airports across the region. The article argues China can offer Gulf states more than a security umbrella as the Strait of Hormuz faces sustained disruptions.

stories.title: EU approves €90 billion Ukraine loan and 20th Russia sanctions package as Hungary’s veto falls
stories.summary: The European Union approved a €90 billion loan to Ukraine and adopted its 20th sanctions package against Russia after Hungary dropped its veto. The first tranche is expected in May or June, with funds earmarked for weapons procurement, budget support, and energy defense.

stories.title: Russian e-commerce group urges prime minister to phase in 22% VAT on imported goods through 2029
stories.summary: A Russian e-commerce industry group urged Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin to phase in a new 22% VAT on imported goods gradually through 2029, rather than imposing it all at once.

stories.title: Latin America's largest investment bank targets Uruguay as regional hub after acquiring local HSBC unit
stories.summary: Brazilian investment bank BTG Pactual is awaiting regulatory approval from Uruguay's Central Bank to begin local operations following its $175 million acquisition of HSBC Uruguay, agreed in July 2025. The bank plans to use Uruguay as a regional hub, with operations expected to start gradually in the second half of 2026.

stories.title: How has Hezbollah shifted its battle tactics?
stories.summary: Hezbollah has reportedly shifted its weapons and battle tactics in its ongoing conflict, though specific details of the changes remain under analysis.

stories.title: UK and France strike new £662m small boats deal
stories.summary: The United Kingdom and France signed a three-year agreement worth £662 million to combat illegal small-boat Channel crossings. The deal includes deploying at least 50 riot-trained police officers to address violence and hostile crowds at departure points.

stories.title: Russia’s Culture Ministry denies distribution license for film about woman who leaves North Korea
stories.summary: Russia's Culture Ministry denied a distribution license for the film 'Hana Korea,' which tells the story of a woman who leaves North Korea, according to its Russian distributor U Films.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval for Fresh $516m Loan
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu submitted a request to the Senate seeking approval to borrow an additional $516.3 million in external loans. The purpose of the fresh borrowing was not detailed in the initial report.
