stories.title: Tochytskyi: Ukraine expects more countries to join Special Tribunal agreement soon
stories.summary: Ukrainian diplomat Tochytskyi stated that several additional countries are expected to join the Enlarged Partial Agreement on a Special Tribunal for Russia before the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers meets in Chisinau. Ukraine also hopes the European Union will join as a separate institution.

stories.title: UK undershoots annual borrowing target by £700m
stories.summary: The UK government borrowed a net £132 billion for the financial year ending March, undershooting the Office for Budget Responsibility's forecast of £132.7 billion by £700 million. However, analysts warn the ongoing conflict with Iran is likely to erode Chancellor Rachel Reeves's fiscal headroom in coming months.

stories.title: Lebanon to confront Israel over demolition of homes in occupied areas since ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanon plans to confront Israel over the large-scale demolition of homes in occupied areas of southern Lebanon following a ceasefire with Hezbollah. The Israeli army says the destroyed buildings were used as Hezbollah outposts, but residents, Lebanese officials, and UN peacekeepers warn the widespread demolitions could leave displaced civilians with nowhere to return.

stories.title: French Cup: Nice reach final after victory at Strasbourg
stories.summary: OGC Nice defeated Strasbourg 2–0 in the French Cup semi-final, with striker Elye Wahi scoring both goals. Nice, currently 15th in Ligue 1, will face Lens in the final at the Stade de France on 22 May.

stories.title: US tells Israel ceasefire with Iran set to end on Sunday, Israeli media reports
stories.summary: Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported that the United States informed Israel that the ceasefire with Iran will expire on Sunday. According to the report, President Trump is seeking concrete understandings with Tehran rather than open-ended negotiations.

stories.title: Trump revives election fraud claims after Virginia redistricting defeat
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed without evidence that a Virginia vote on congressional redistricting had been "rigged" after Republicans lost the closely watched election. The assertion revived Trump's familiar pattern of alleging election fraud following unfavorable results.

stories.title: Mysterious death of Jackson Stacker near Byron Bay referred to homicide squad
stories.summary: The New South Wales coroner has referred the 2021 death of Melbourne man Jackson Stacker, found near Byron Bay with two stab wounds to the chest, to the homicide squad. Coroner Teresa O'Sullivan raised concerns about the early police investigation, which the family argues prematurely concluded he killed himself.

stories.title: Italian man convicted of trafficking Singaporean Tinder date for Dubai sex work
stories.summary: A court convicted Italian national Achraf Arjaouy, 31, of human trafficking for deceiving a Singaporean woman he met on Tinder into sex work in Dubai. Arjaouy had posed as a wealthy pilot from Qatar. The victim's identity is protected by a gag order.

stories.title: US Navy Secretary Phelan fired by Pentagon, source says
stories.summary: The Pentagon confirmed that U.S. Navy Secretary John Phelan has been removed from his position. His departure comes just weeks after the U.S. Army's top general was also ousted from his post.

stories.title: MTR Corp unveils HK$300 million wheelset centre, boosting efficiency by 80%
stories.summary: Hong Kong's MTR Corporation unveiled a new HK$300 million Integrated Wheelset Maintenance Centre at the Ho Man Tin siding, set to open in the coming months. The automated facility can process 1,500 wheelsets annually, reducing maintenance time from over three days to approximately 10 hours.

stories.title: Can Chinese scientists bring Nasa’s ‘space spider’ dream to life?
stories.summary: Scientists at the Shenyang Institute of Automation in northern China say they have developed key technologies similar to NASA's cancelled SpiderFab project, which envisioned spider-like robots constructing large structures in orbit from carbon-fibre materials. The Chinese team built components using carbon-fibre composites.

stories.title: ‘Innate kindness’ of Chinese people moves British granny, 74, travelling solo across country
stories.summary: A 74-year-old British grandmother named Gill, who has visited 72 countries solo, received widespread assistance from Chinese citizens during a solo trip across China. The story began when a university student from Hezhou in Guangxi Province met Gill while volunteering in Phuket, Thailand.

stories.title: Mapped: the elections that could deliver ‘unprecedented’ losses for Labour
stories.summary: Data analyzed by the Guardian indicates Labour is on track for historically low vote-share results in England's council elections and devolved parliament elections in Wales and Scotland on 7 May. Reform, the Greens, and nationalist parties are expected to make significant gains, increasing pressure on Labour leader Keir Starmer.

stories.title: Iran, Hezbollah ceasefires need enforcement, not just declarations, to sustain calm  - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that ceasefires involving Iran and Hezbollah require active enforcement mechanisms rather than mere declarations to sustain calm. It notes the Trump administration is combining ceasefire diplomacy with economic pressure on Iran while Israel faces ongoing threats from Hezbollah on its northern border.

stories.title: Pentagon removes top Navy official amid military shake-up
stories.summary: US Secretary of the Navy John Phelan departed his post with immediate effect, the Pentagon announced Wednesday, without providing a reason. His removal is part of a broader shake-up of senior military officials under President Donald Trump during the ongoing unresolved conflict with Iran.

stories.title: In Algerian desert, Sahrawi refugees still dream of independent homeland
stories.summary: Sahrawi refugees living in the Aousserd camp near Tindouf in southern Algeria continue to demand independence for Western Sahara. Residents say decades of exile have not weakened their resolve.

stories.title: South Africa: Cape Town Battles Flooding After Heavy Rains - South African News Briefs - April 23, 2026
stories.summary: Cape Town, South Africa, experienced significant flooding following heavy rains, prompting emergency response efforts across the city.

stories.title: Iran tightens grip on Strait of Hormuz after Trump calls off attacks
stories.summary: Iran has tightened its control over the Strait of Hormuz following President Trump's decision to call off military attacks. The U.S. Navy continues to maintain its blockade of Iran's maritime trade routes.

stories.title: Thursday briefing: ​Why the US president is losing support from crucial allies
stories.summary: A newsletter analysis notes that US President Donald Trump faces declining support from key allies amid an escalating foreign conflict and a deepening cost-of-living crisis at home. His poll ratings have reached a second-term low, though more than a third of Americans still approve of his performance.

stories.title: Leading California governor candidates spar in debate as topsy-turvy race heats up
stories.summary: Six candidates for California governor clashed in a debate over homelessness and the cost-of-living crisis, the first since former congressman Eric Swalwell exited the race following sexual assault and misconduct allegations. No clear frontrunner has emerged in the wide-open race to succeed outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom.

stories.title: Spain provides Ukraine with 100 VAMTAC armored vehicles and artillery shells
stories.summary: Spain is providing Ukraine with 100 VAMTAC armored tactical vehicles along with a shipment of 155-millimeter artillery ammunition to support Ukrainian defense efforts.

stories.title: More bookings, shorter trips: Chinese adjust to higher fuel prices for Labour Day break
stories.summary: Analysts report that Chinese tourist bookings for the five-day Labour Day holiday are up roughly 8–10 per cent year on year despite higher global fuel prices linked to the ongoing conflict. Travelers are expected to prefer shorter domestic trips to offset increased transport costs.

stories.title: Taiwan minister makes rare visit to disputed South China Sea island
stories.summary: Taiwan's Minister Kuan Bi-ling made a rare visit to Taiping Island in the disputed South China Sea, observing coast guard drills. The island is also claimed by China, the Philippines, and Vietnam.

stories.title: Trump considering plan to send Afghan refugees who helped US to Congo - NYT
stories.summary: The New York Times reports the Trump administration is considering a plan to send Afghan refugees stranded in Qatar, many of whom assisted US operations, to the Democratic Republic of Congo. AfghanEvac President Shawn VanDiver criticized the proposal as moving people from one major refugee crisis to another.

stories.title: Telegram founder Pavel Durov says he received summons in Russia addressed to 'suspect'
stories.summary: Telegram founder Pavel Durov disclosed that he received a criminal summons in Russia at a former address identifying him as a "suspect" in an unspecified case. The summons was sent to an old address in Moscow.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills five Palestinians in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed five Palestinians, including three children, in the northern Gaza Strip on Wednesday. Health officials and medics in Gaza confirmed the casualties.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers looting civilian property in southern Lebanon: Report
stories.summary: According to a Haaretz report based on military testimonies, Israeli soldiers have been looting civilian property including motorcycles, televisions, and furniture from homes and businesses in southern Lebanon. The report states senior and junior commanders are aware but have not taken effective disciplinary action.

stories.title: Bennett doubles down on mandatory haredi enlistment, blames current gov't for lack of IDF soldiers
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett reiterated his support for mandatory enlistment of ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) men into the IDF. Speaking on Radio 103FM, Bennett blamed the current government for soldier shortages and said draft evasion is costing soldiers' lives.

stories.title: Democrats up in Virginia, but US voters may pay price for redistricting war
stories.summary: Political experts warn that an unprecedented wave of tit-for-tat congressional redistricting across U.S. states could lead to a surge in gerrymandering. Democrats are currently polling ahead in Virginia.

stories.title: Can fish hook voters in India’s West Bengal elections?
stories.summary: In India's West Bengal elections, campaigners from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party canvassed with fish in hand to appeal to local voters in a region where fish is a cultural staple.

stories.title: South Africa: Durban Shops Close As Locals Protest Against Immigrants
stories.summary: In Durban, South Africa, shops closed as local residents protested against immigrants, with reports of foreign nationals being attacked. Police commander Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi said he would meet protest leaders to address the situation.

stories.title: Nigeria: As Foreign Aid Declines, Can Pension Funds Fill Nigeria's Health Financing Gap?
stories.summary: Nigeria's pension fund assets grew 20% in 2025, reaching over ₦27 trillion, but remain heavily concentrated in government securities. Analysts are exploring whether these funds could help fill the country's health financing gap as foreign aid declines.

stories.title: Nigeria: Retired General, Five Others Plead Not Guilty to Coup Charges, Court Adjourns Bail Hearing
stories.summary: A retired Nigerian general and five other men pleaded not guilty to 13 coup-related charges before the Federal High Court in Abuja. The court adjourned the bail hearing.

stories.title: Protesters stabbed at London rally against war on Iran
stories.summary: Multiple individuals were stabbed during a protest in London against a potential war on Iran. Videos circulating online show several people with apparent knife wounds sustained during the rally.

stories.title: Iran Foreign Minister tells South Korea envoy of 'US-Israeli crimes'
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with a South Korean special envoy in Tehran and detailed what he described as US-Israeli violations during recent military operations against Iran. Araghchi urged countries to take a firm stance condemning the attacks.

stories.title: AI-driven Hong Kong stock inflows from mainland China slow as investor options multiply
stories.summary: Mainland Chinese investors have slowed purchases of Hong Kong-listed shares via the Stock Connect system in 2026, with southbound inflows reaching about US$30 billion so far, lagging behind 2025's record US$180 billion. BNP Paribas attributes the slowdown to expanding AI investment opportunities available in mainland markets.

stories.title: US intercepts three Iranian oil tankers in Asian waters, sources say
stories.summary: The US military intercepted at least three Iranian-flagged oil tankers in Asian waters near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka, redirecting them away from their positions, according to shipping and security sources.

stories.title: South Sudan: As Civil War Reignites in South Sudan, So Too Does a Battle Over Aid
stories.summary: Fighting has reignited in South Sudan's civil war, raising renewed concerns about the humanitarian situation. Aid access and the relationship between civilian populations and humanitarian workers remain critical issues in the conflict.

stories.title: Libya: UN Mission Chief Laments Lack of Progress Towards National Renewal
stories.summary: The UN Special Representative for Libya told the Security Council that Libyan political leaders have failed to make progress on implementing a roadmap toward national elections and unified institutions.

stories.title: Sudan: The Best Efforts to Reduce Violence in Sudan Today Are Not Led By Diplomats
stories.summary: A report highlights that locally grounded peacebuilding efforts in Sudan, rather than diplomat-led initiatives, are proving most effective at reducing violence. These community-based approaches are described as relatively inexpensive with proven results.

stories.title: Sudan: Restrictions On Humanitarian Work in Tawila Locality, North Darfur, Sudan
stories.summary: The Darfur Network for Human Rights reported that the Rapid Support Forces have imposed strict restrictions on humanitarian organizations operating in Tawila camp in North Darfur, Sudan. The RSF communicated the restrictions through official letters sent directly to field organizations.

stories.title: Pilot’s selfie led to mid-air collision in F-15K fighter jet, says South Korea’s air force
stories.summary: South Korea's air force apologized for a 2021 mid-air collision between two F-15K fighter jets, after auditors found that pilots had been taking selfies and filming during the flight. One pilot was suspended from flying duties and ordered to repay a portion of the approximately $600,000 in damages.

stories.title: Poland does not rule out delays in delivery of weapons purchased from U.S.
stories.summary: Poland has acknowledged that delays in the delivery of US military equipment, linked to the situation in the Middle East, may also affect Polish defense procurement schedules.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: US and Iran in blockade stalemate as Washington’s navy secretary leaves office ‘immediately’
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards released footage showing the seizure of two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, citing maritime violations. Meanwhile, a blockade stalemate persists between the US and Iran, and the US Navy secretary departed his post effective immediately, according to the Pentagon.

stories.title: Trump says eight Iranian women won't be executed, Iran disputes entire account
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran agreed not to execute eight women protesters as a sign of respect for him, while Iranian officials denied any such executions had been planned and accused Trump of spreading falsehoods.

stories.title: Euro, yuan unlikely to match US dollar as global currencies, Daniel Gros says
stories.summary: Daniel Gros, director of the Institute for European Policymaking at Bocconi University, argued that neither the euro nor the Chinese yuan is likely to displace the US dollar as the dominant global currency. He analyzed structural tensions in EU-China economic relations and drew comparisons between the euro's trajectory and the yuan's prospects.

stories.title: Lebanon accuses Israel of targeting journalist killed in air strike
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister accused Israel of war crimes after an Israeli airstrike killed a journalist. IDF attacks on Red Cross vehicles also prevented rescue teams from reaching the site of the strike.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin can meet Zelenskiy only to agree final conflict arrangements
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russian President Putin can only meet Ukrainian President Zelenskyy for the purpose of finalizing conflict agreements, setting a narrow precondition for any summit.

stories.title: Pope Leo 'using more politics than he should' amid US-Iran war, say Trump supporters
stories.summary: Pope Leo has publicly criticized President Donald Trump's actions against Iran on multiple occasions. The exchanges have escalated into a public dispute on social media between the two leaders, drawing criticism from Trump supporters who say the Pope is overstepping into politics.

stories.title: Islamic militants kill 11 people, burn homes in late-night attack in Nigeria
stories.summary: Islamic militants killed 11 people and burned homes in a late-night attack in Nigeria. The assault is part of a broader and longstanding security crisis affecting Africa's most populous country.

stories.title: Opinion: Why Iran will not surrender
stories.summary: Middle East politics writer Soumaya Ghannoushi argues that modern Middle Eastern history shows a recurring pattern in which external military pressure generates resistance rather than submission, applying this framework to Iran's current posture.

stories.title: ‘Apprenticeship penalty’ on benefits forces young people from poorer UK families to quit
stories.summary: A UK welfare rule known as the "apprenticeship penalty" is causing young people from disadvantaged families to abandon job training. When a 16-year-old begins an apprenticeship, they are classified as an independent worker, triggering the loss of their parents' child benefit and universal credit elements—up to £340 per week.

stories.title: Czech journalists threaten to strike over plan to scrap licence fees
stories.summary: Journalists at Czech public broadcasters have threatened to strike over the government's plan to replace household licence fees with direct state funding. Critics, including the journalists, say the proposal by Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's government would undermine the independence of public television and radio.

stories.title: How Southeast Asia’s aviation hubs are capturing traffic amid Iran war
stories.summary: Southeast Asian airlines including Singapore Airlines, Cathay Pacific, and Korean Air are experiencing increased demand for European routes as travelers avoid Middle Eastern hubs disrupted by drone and missile attacks linked to the Iran war. The region's aviation sector is pivoting to serve as alternative transit hubs to offset tourism losses.

stories.title: Body of journalist for pro-Hezbollah daily pulled from rubble of home struck by IDF
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it targeted a building in its southern Lebanon security zone to which it claimed militants had fled after an earlier strike on a vehicle. The body of journalist Amal Khalil, who worked for a pro-Hezbollah daily, was pulled from the rubble. A photographer accompanying her suffered a head wound.

stories.title: Argentina truckers and farmers plan talks to resolve Quequen port protest
stories.summary: Argentine truckers blocking access to the Quequen port over demands for higher freight rates have agreed to meet with farmers in the coming days to resolve the dispute. Julian Kristansen, chair of the Necochea city council's transportation committee, confirmed the planned talks.

stories.title: Deaths of CIA agents in Mexico spark sovereignty row with White House
stories.summary: The deaths of CIA agents during an operation to dismantle a drug lab in northern Mexico have triggered a sovereignty dispute between Mexico and the United States. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum stated her government was not informed of the foreign operatives' involvement, calling it a breach of security protocols.

stories.title: Bullrich arrives in Uruguay criticising cannabis legalisation and calling for tougher security policy
stories.summary: Argentine Senator Patricia Bullrich visited Montevideo to participate in a conference organized by the Manantiales Foundation. During her visit, the former security minister under President Javier Milei criticized Uruguay's cannabis legalization policy and called for tougher security measures to reduce the country's homicide rate.

stories.title: Trump envoy seeks to 'replace Iran with Italy' in World Cup: FT
stories.summary: According to the Financial Times, an Italian envoy to President Trump asked him to replace Iran with Italy in the upcoming FIFA World Cup as a gesture to repair relations with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

stories.title: CPJ 'outraged' over Israeli targeting of Lebanese journalists
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned Israel for striking Lebanese journalists Amal Khalil and Zeinab Faraj while they were reporting near the southern village of Bint Jbeil. The pair were hit in al-Tayri after sheltering in a building following an initial strike on a nearby civilian vehicle.

stories.title: Israel kills journalist and wounds another in south Lebanon targeted attack
stories.summary: Israel killed journalist Amal Khalil and wounded photographer Zeinab Faraj in a 'double-tap' airstrike in southern Lebanon. The two were covering events near the border at the time of the attack.

stories.title: Belarus follows Russia in imposing mobile web restrictions, says CCD
stories.summary: Belarus has imposed new restrictions on mobile internet access, including a 30 GB monthly data cap and artificial throttling of speeds, according to the Centre for Contemporary Democracy (CCD). The measures follow a similar pattern of digital controls previously adopted by Russia.

stories.title: Israeli strikes wound journalist, trap another under rubble in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon on Wednesday wounded one journalist and trapped another under rubble. Rescuers were temporarily unable to reach the trapped journalist due to ongoing Israeli fire, according to Lebanon's health ministry and press advocates.

stories.title: European airlines cut flights and raise fares as Iran conflict fuels jet fuel crisis
stories.summary: Lufthansa Group announced the cancellation of 20,000 short-haul flights from its summer schedule through October due to soaring jet fuel prices linked to the Iran conflict. The cuts represent the most significant scheduling reduction by a European airline, reflecting a broader trend reshaping the continent's aviation sector.

stories.title: University of Queensland Press cancels children’s book over illustrator’s post on ‘Zionist framing’ of Bondi attack
stories.summary: University of Queensland Press cancelled a children's book by Indigenous poet Jazz Money after illustrator Matt Chun described victims of the Bondi beach terror attack as "affluent beneficiaries of imperialism." Several prominent Australian authors, including Evelyn Araluen and Melissa Lucashenko, said they would no longer work with the publisher.

stories.title: Senator Lindsey Graham speaks to Trump, Hegseth on 'way forward' in Iran conflict
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina spoke with President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth about the 'way forward' in the Iran conflict. Graham also warned other countries against assisting Iran's oil distribution efforts.

stories.title: Alibaba opens Qwen app to outside partners with China Eastern Airlines tie-up
stories.summary: Alibaba has partnered with China Eastern Airlines to integrate flight booking capabilities into its Qwen AI app. The collaboration allows users to search, purchase tickets, select seats, and check in through a single natural-language chat interface, marking the app's first external partnership beyond Alibaba's own ecosystem.

stories.title: Trump administration explores Spirit rescue as Iran war fuel shock hits airlines
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly exploring a rescue plan for struggling airline Spirit as heightened tensions with Iran and potential fuel supply shocks put additional financial pressure on carriers with thin margins.

stories.title: Turkey trying to revive Russia-Ukraine negotiations, Erdogan tells NATO chief
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte during a meeting in Ankara that Turkey is working to revive negotiations between Russia and Ukraine and bring together the leaders of the two warring sides.

stories.title: Argentina arrests Colombian linked to 2025 assassination of senator Uribe
stories.summary: Argentine authorities arrested a Colombian man linked to a woman convicted for the murder of Colombian senator and presidential hopeful Miguel Uribe. The arrest took place in Argentina, according to officials who announced it on Wednesday.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Lebanon meets Israel in Washington to request truce extension
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli delegations met in Washington on Thursday to discuss extending a ceasefire that is due to expire within days. Beirut plans to request a one-month extension of the truce during the negotiations.

stories.title: Buried but not out, Iran’s ballistic missile threat weathers US-Israeli strikes intact
stories.summary: The Israeli military assesses that Iran still possesses hundreds of missile launchers and approximately 1,000 ballistic missiles, many stored underground and not destroyed by recent US-Israeli strikes. Tehran is reportedly working to rebuild its weapons stockpile.

stories.title: Israel destroys 428 housing units in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military demolished 428 housing units in southern Lebanon over a three-day period despite a ceasefire being in effect. An additional 50 units were damaged during the same period, according to Lebanon's National Council for Scientific Research.

stories.title: Film on Manila hostage crisis sparks debate over ‘secondary trauma’ in Hong Kong
stories.summary: A Hong Kong film titled Beyond Hostage Crisis, adapted from the 2010 Manila hostage crisis that killed eight Hongkongers, has sparked debate over potential secondary trauma. Starring Hong Kong Film Awards best actress Fish Liew Chi-yu, the film opened in Malaysia in April and is set for Hong Kong release on May 28.

stories.title: German Parliament speaker targeted in Signal app phishing attack: Report
stories.summary: Germany's Bundestag speaker was reportedly targeted in a phishing attack via the Signal messaging app. German intelligence services have attributed the attack to Russia.

stories.title: Lebanon PM accuses Israel of war crimes, claims IDF targeted journalists
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of committing war crimes by targeting journalists in southern Lebanon. The Israeli Defense Forces said reports of injured journalists were under review and denied preventing rescue teams from reaching the area.

stories.title: Ukrzaliznytsia remains Ukraine’s largest employer – Opendatabot
stories.summary: Ukraine's state railway company JSC Ukrzaliznytsia has been ranked the country's largest employer for the fifth consecutive year, according to Opendatabot. The company employs nearly 170,000 people.

stories.title: US intercepts 3 Iranian tankers near India, Malaysia, Sri Lanka amid Hormuz tensions
stories.summary: The US military intercepted at least three Iranian-flagged tankers in waters near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka, redirecting them as part of Washington's naval blockade on Iranian trade. The action comes amid ongoing tensions over Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz, nearly two months into the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Iran says won't reopen Hormuz as long as US blockade remains
stories.summary: Iran declared it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the U.S. blockade on Iranian ports and vessels remains in place. Tehran insists the American blockade violates the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Eretz Nehederet searches for light at the end of the bomb shelter in season finale
stories.summary: The Israeli comedy show Eretz Nehederet completed its season finale, with the cast reflecting on a season that ran from late February through April during which they repeatedly had to take shelter in bomb shelters.

stories.title: 600 families seek second visit as residents return to worst-hit Wang Fuk Court tower
stories.summary: Approximately 600 families from Hong Kong's fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court have requested a second visit to retrieve belongings from their flats. Residents of the most severely affected tower recounted harrowing escapes, while some criticized the time limits imposed on household visits and called for accountability over the deadly blaze.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox Jews burn Israeli flags to protest national day
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters burned Israeli flags and displayed anti-Zionist banners in West Jerusalem during demonstrations against Israel's national day celebrations.

stories.title: Trump claims ‘rigged’ Virginia vote as court moves to block map redraw
stories.summary: President Donald Trump alleged without evidence that a Virginia redistricting referendum was "rigged" after voters approved a congressional map favoring Democrats. A county judge moved to block the measure, which could help Democrats flip up to four Republican-held House seats.

stories.title: China’s Canton Fair defies global trends as overseas customers flock to buy robots, drones
stories.summary: China's Canton Fair saw strong attendance from overseas buyers, with robotics, drone, and new energy pavilions reaching capacity shortly after opening. Foreign visitors live-streamed new technology products and purchased samples on the spot, reflecting growing international demand for Chinese tech exports.

stories.title: US downplays Iran's seizure of European vessels
stories.summary: The United States downplayed Iran's seizure of two European-owned vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian forces also targeted a third ship in the waterway on Wednesday, underscoring Tehran's ability to disrupt maritime traffic two months into the conflict.

stories.title: US Centcom says 31 vessels have been redirected as part of blockade on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command announced that 31 vessels have been redirected or ordered to return to port as part of Washington's naval blockade on Iran. Centcom stated that most of the redirected ships were oil tankers.

stories.title: Gaza: Children among five killed in Israeli strike in Beit Lahia
stories.summary: Five Palestinians, including three children, were killed in an Israeli airstrike that targeted civilians near Al-Qassam mosque in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza.

stories.title: US intercepts Iran oil tankers in Asian waters as demining of Hormuz expected to take months
stories.summary: The US Navy is intercepting Iranian oil tankers in Asian waters, operating away from the Strait of Hormuz due to the threat of mines. The Pentagon estimates demining operations in the Hormuz waterway could take up to six months.

stories.title: Suspected Boko Haram militants kill 20 in northeast Nigeria attacks
stories.summary: Suspected Boko Haram militants on motorbikes attacked two villages in northeast Nigeria, killing at least 20 people, according to a local official in Maiduguri.

stories.title: Due to aircraft shortage, Russia returns worn-out equipment to service — intelligence
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reports that Russia is returning worn-out small aviation aircraft to service due to equipment shortages caused by international sanctions.

stories.title: Trump envoy seeks to replace Iran with Italy in upcoming World Cup - Financial Times
stories.summary: A Trump administration envoy is reportedly seeking to replace Iran with Italy in the upcoming FIFA World Cup, according to the Financial Times. Iran had previously said it would decide on participation only after FIFA responded to its request to relocate matches from the U.S. to Mexico.

stories.title: Israeli attacks on journalists constitute 'war crimes', Lebanese Prime Minister says
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of committing war crimes by systematically targeting journalists in southern Lebanon. He said strikes on reporters during their professional duties and obstruction of rescue teams constitute clear violations of international law.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz cannot be opened due to ceasefire breaches
stories.summary: Iran's chief negotiator stated that violations by the United States and Israel make it impossible to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing breaches of the US-Iran ceasefire as justification for maintaining closure of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Thai hotels woo Asian guests with curated stays as Iran war keeps Europeans away
stories.summary: Thai hotel chains such as Centara are shifting their offerings to cater to Asian travelers as the US-Iran war deters European tourists. Resorts on islands like Koh Samui are introducing curated experiences and regionally tailored amenities.

stories.title: Six suspected Nigerian coup plotters plead not guilty as court adjourns trial
stories.summary: Six former Nigerian security officials accused of plotting the violent overthrow of President Bola Tinubu's government pleaded not guilty in an Abuja court. The trial was adjourned to April 27.

stories.title: UN leadership candidate Grynspan vows peacemaking and reform
stories.summary: Former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan, a candidate to lead the United Nations, pledged to prioritize peacemaking if selected. She warned that trust in the world body is declining and that time is running out to restore it.

stories.title: China’s dark compute power could be 6,000 times higher than current estimates
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology reported 1,882 exaflops of domestic AI computing power, a figure over 6,000 times higher than previous public estimates. Experts suggest this points to a vast 'dark pool' of undisclosed compute capacity.

stories.title: China live-streams expose minors undergoing harsh training designed for ‘rebellious youth’
stories.summary: Chinese state media reports reveal that teenagers at youth correction centers marketed for 'rebellious youth' are subjected to beatings and sexual assault off camera. Live-streams show the minors expressing gratitude in camouflage uniforms, but investigations have prompted calls for better oversight.

stories.title: Iran latest: Trump has ‘no time frame’ to end war as world waits for peace talks
stories.summary: The White House stated that President Trump has set 'no time frame' for ending the war with Iran as negotiations remain stalled. Global attention is focused on the Strait of Hormuz amid an ongoing energy crisis, while the status of Trump's extended ceasefire remains uncertain.

stories.title: Hundreds of Hezbollah terrorists killed in 24 hours before Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, IDF reveals
stories.summary: The Israeli military revealed that hundreds of Hezbollah fighters were killed in the 24 hours preceding the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire. Among those killed was Ali Reza Abbas, commander of a Hezbollah unit operating in the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil.

stories.title: Iran releases video of IRGC seizing ship in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) released footage purporting to show its forces seizing a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel kills five, including three children, in north Gaza
stories.summary: At least five people, including three children, were killed in an Israeli airstrike near Al-Qassam Mosque in Beit Lahia in northern Gaza. Several others sustained serious injuries in the attack.

stories.title: Dutch prosecutors seek 30-year sentence for alleged Syrian torturer
stories.summary: Dutch prosecutors in The Hague demanded a 30-year prison sentence for a Syrian man accused of torturing and raping prisoners while serving in a militia that supported former President Bashar al-Assad's government.

stories.title: Russia launches digital service to attract foreign specialists due to labor shortage — CCD
stories.summary: Russia has launched a digital service designed to attract foreign specialists to address its ongoing labor shortage. The initiative follows similar past efforts that failed, and analysts have noted this project also faces significant risk of failure.

stories.title: Iran seizes pair of container ships, in first since start of war with US and Israel
stories.summary: Iranian forces seized two European-owned container ships in the Strait of Hormuz and targeted a third vessel, according to a UK maritime agency. The White House said the seizures did not violate the truce because the ships were not American or Israeli.

stories.title: Travel scheme could allow Hong Kong, Macau yachts to sail to 6 Greater Bay Area ports
stories.summary: A forthcoming cross-border travel scheme will permit yachts from Hong Kong and Macau to sail independently to approximately six designated ports in the western waters of China's Greater Bay Area. According to a Guangdong provincial government document, the policy could be finalized as early as this summer, with recommended leisure routes through the Pearl River Delta and nearby waters.

stories.title: White House denies Trump setting a timeline for receiving Iran proposal
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that President Donald Trump has not set a timeline for receiving a proposal from Iran. She added that the ceasefire was extended because Iran needs to 'get their act together.'

stories.title: EU moves to start drafting Montenegro accession treaty
stories.summary: European Union member states agreed to begin drafting an accession treaty for Montenegro, advancing the country into a new phase of its EU membership process.

stories.title: Israel army returns dozens of Israeli settlers who entered Syria
stories.summary: The Israeli military intercepted and returned dozens of Israeli settlers who had crossed the border into Syria. Members of the group known as the Pioneers of Bashan had previously entered Syrian territory on multiple occasions.

stories.title: Interpol issues red notice for Lyari gangster Wasiullah Lakho
stories.summary: Interpol issued a red notice for Lyari gangster Wasiullah Lakho, who is reportedly hiding abroad and wanted by Karachi police. The notice was requested by Pakistani authorities through Interpol's secretariat in Lyon, France.

stories.title: Smuggled chicken discovery hints at Cambodian shortages amid Thai border conflict
stories.summary: Plastic bags filled with rotting chicken from a smugglers' boat washed ashore in Thailand, suggesting supply shortages inside Cambodia as formal trade between the two countries has collapsed amid their ongoing border conflict. Illicit cargo flows of Thai oil, fruit, meat, and consumer goods have surged, while Cambodian citizens maintain a boycott of Thai businesses.

stories.title: Iran war live: Israel kills Lebanese journalist; Tehran-US talks stalled
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon on Wednesday killed at least five people, including Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil.

stories.title: US Senate rejects latest bid to curb Trump’s war powers
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate voted down a resolution to limit President Trump's authority to wage war on Iran by a margin of 51 to 46. It was the fifth failed attempt to curb Trump's war powers. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer accused Trump of making 'empty promises' to end the conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky holds meeting on Ukraine's memory policy and honoring national heroes
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held a meeting focused on strategic issues related to Ukraine's memory policy and the honoring of national heroes.

stories.title: Second French soldier dies of wounds after attack on UN force in Lebanon
stories.summary: French Chief Corporal Anicet Girardin has died from wounds sustained on April 18 during an attack on the United Nations peacekeeping force in Lebanon. He is the second French soldier to die as a result of the incident.

stories.title: French soldier dies of wounds after attack on UN force in Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that a second French soldier died from wounds sustained in an attack on United Nations peacekeepers in Lebanon the previous week. Macron attributed the attack to Iran-backed Hezbollah.

stories.title: War update: 127 clashes since morning, Pokrovsk direction remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 127 combat engagements with Russian troops since the start of the day, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk direction in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: He wasn't guilty but delays left this man jailed for five years without trial
stories.summary: Rasheed Wasiu was detained at age 17 during a Nigerian security crackdown on protests against police brutality. Despite not being found guilty, he spent five years in jail without trial due to systemic delays in the justice system.

stories.title: Mamdani administration won’t use a codified antisemitism definition, representative says
stories.summary: New York City's Mamdani administration announced it will not use a codified definition of antisemitism, after discarding the IHRA definition. Separately, the NYPD said 'kill Zionists' graffiti does not necessarily constitute a hate crime.

stories.title: Trump ballroom deal shields donor identities, limits conflict safeguards, contract shows
stories.summary: A contract related to a Trump ballroom deal includes provisions that restrict the disclosure of donor identities and limit conflict-of-interest safeguards, according to details revealed in the agreement.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills journalist Amal Khalil in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Al-Akhbar journalist Amal Khalil was killed by an Israeli airstrike on the town of al-Tiri in southern Lebanon. She was trapped under rubble alongside fellow journalist Zeinab Faraj following the strike.

stories.title: Colombian sent from US to Congo says she faces pressure to risk danger back home
stories.summary: A Colombian woman deported from the United States to the Democratic Republic of Congo under a new agreement with the Trump administration said she is being pressured to return to Colombia despite facing dangers there. She spoke from Dakar about her situation.

stories.title: EU unblocks €90 billion Ukraine loan after Hungary row
stories.summary: The European Union unblocked a EUR 90 billion loan to Ukraine after resolving a dispute with Hungary. Budapest had held up the decision while awaiting the resumption of Russian oil deliveries through the Druzhba pipeline via Ukraine.

stories.title: Pentagon says navy secretary is leaving, marking another top leader’s departure
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that Navy Secretary John Phelan is departing the administration effective immediately. His exit follows the firing of the Army's top officer by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the previous week, marking another high-level departure from Pentagon leadership.

stories.title: Zelensky appoints Ukraine's Ambassador to Kingdom of Bahrain
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed Oleksandr Balanutsa as Ukraine's Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary Ambassador to the Kingdom of Bahrain.

stories.title: South American migrants deported to DRC say facing pressure to return home
stories.summary: South American migrants deported to the Democratic Republic of the Congo report facing pressure to return to their home countries. Rights advocates have accused the Trump administration of using third-country deportations to intimidate asylum seekers.

stories.title: Iran, Russian oil waivers extended after requests from vulnerable countries, says Bessent
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Bessent announced that oil sanctions waivers for Iran and Russia have been extended following requests from vulnerable countries. Bessent disputed estimates that Iran gained more than $14 billion from the sanctions relief, calling such figures "a myth."

stories.title: Los Angeles school board votes to set limits on classroom screen time
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Unified School District board voted 6-0 to impose daily and weekly limits on classroom screen time for students in the upcoming school year. The resolution also restricts device use during passing periods, lunch, and recess, and blocks YouTube on district devices for elementary and middle school students.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 3 in Lebanon, Beirut to seek truce extension
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed three people in Lebanon, prompting Beirut to seek an extension of the existing truce. Israel called on the Lebanese government to cooperate against Iran-backed Hezbollah ahead of scheduled talks.

stories.title: EU unblocks $134b Ukraine loan after Hungary row
stories.summary: EU ambassadors approved the disbursement of a €90 billion loan to Ukraine after Hungary lifted its veto, which had been linked to a dispute over oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline. The loan is critical for Kyiv's finances as US support has largely been cut off.

stories.title: Billionaire Justin Sun sues Trump family crypto venture
stories.summary: Crypto billionaire Justin Sun filed a lawsuit in San Francisco federal court against World Liberty Financial, a Trump family-backed cryptocurrency platform, alleging fraud. Sun claims he invested $45 million in the platform's WLFI token starting in October 2024 and was subsequently blocked from withdrawing his assets.

stories.title: Russia to stop Kazakh oil flows to German PCK refinery via Druzhba
stories.summary: Russia announced it will halt the supply of Kazakh crude oil through the Druzhba pipeline to Germany starting May 1, according to Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak. The decision forces the PCK refinery near Berlin to find alternative crude sources.

stories.title: City firms bank on ‘savvy’ advertising campaign to push Brits towards investing
stories.summary: UK financial firms launched a government-endorsed advertising campaign costing up to £50 million, featuring a CGI squirrel, to encourage British savers to move money out of cash and into investments. The initiative is part of Chancellor Rachel Reeves' broader effort to boost financial risk-taking amid concerns that risk-averse consumer behavior is stifling UK economic growth.

stories.title: China praises blocking of Taiwan President's Africa trip, Taipei defiant
stories.summary: China praised the blocking of a planned Africa trip by Taiwan's president through denial of airspace access. The incident marks the first time a Taiwanese president has had to cancel an entire foreign trip for this reason, signaling a new Chinese pressure tactic.

stories.title: US Navy secretary steps down, Pentagon announces
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that U.S. Secretary of the Navy John C. Phelan is leaving his post effective immediately. No explanation was provided for the sudden departure. Undersecretary Hung Cao will serve as acting Navy secretary.

stories.title: Iran appreciates Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between Tehran and Washington
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei expressed appreciation for Pakistan's mediation efforts between Tehran and Washington aimed at ending the Middle East war. He did not comment on a ceasefire extension announced by the United States.

stories.title: Moscow region in Russia most protected by air defense — expert
stories.summary: Russia faces a shortage of anti-aircraft missiles and is redeploying air defense systems between regions to counter Ukrainian strikes, according to a military expert. The Moscow region remains the most heavily defended area in the country.

stories.title: Palestinian man shot dead amid settler attack on West Bank town near Ramallah
stories.summary: A Palestinian man was shot dead during an Israeli settler attack on the West Bank town of Deir Dibwan near Ramallah. The IDF confirmed the settler raid but said its troops did not fire at local Palestinians. Israeli suspects were handed to police, who opened an investigation but made no arrests.

stories.title: Hezbollah supporters defiant after sons killed fighting Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah supporters in Lebanon remain defiant after losing family members in the ongoing conflict with Israel. Lebanese authorities report that more than 2,400 people have been killed in the fighting.

stories.title: 'Inaccurate reports': CENTCOM denies media allegations of ships breaking Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command denied media reports that several ships had broken through the Strait of Hormuz blockade, calling the allegations inaccurate. CENTCOM provided details of U.S. military interceptions and orders directing vessels to turn back.

stories.title: Two Israel Air Force technicians charged with spying for Iran - KAN
stories.summary: Two Israeli Air Force technicians are set to be charged with espionage for Iran, according to Israeli broadcaster KAN. The pair allegedly leaked sensitive military documents during Operation Roaring Lion.

stories.title: Top ministers quit after Peru’s president postpones F-16 fighter jet deal
stories.summary: Top ministers in Peru resigned after President postponed a deal to purchase F-16 fighter jets. The Trump administration warned Peru against pulling out of the agreement, calling it a sign of 'bad faith' negotiations.

stories.title: Hezbollah says attacks on Israeli troops respond to truce violations
stories.summary: Hezbollah stated that its attacks on Israeli soldiers and vehicles in Qantara on Wednesday were carried out in response to alleged violations of the 10-day ceasefire. The group said the strikes were its third operation of the day. Israel has previously accused Hezbollah of breaching the ceasefire but has not commented on the latest attacks.

stories.title: US visa system ‘rolls out red carpet’ for Chinese spies, congressional hearing told
stories.summary: At a U.S. congressional hearing, senators alleged that America's visa system facilitates Chinese espionage and the theft of military and commercial secrets. Republican Senator Ashley Moody of Florida said the system effectively rolls out the "red carpet" for spies as Washington and Beijing compete over AI and advanced technologies.

stories.title: Trump envoy seeks to replace Iran with Italy at World Cup, says report
stories.summary: A U.S. special envoy to President Donald Trump has asked FIFA to replace Iran with Italy in the upcoming World Cup, according to the Financial Times. The effort reportedly aims to repair relations between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni after tensions arose over Trump's criticism of Pope Leo XIV regarding the Iran conflict.

stories.title: US downplays Iran's seizure of European vessels, Hormuz brinkmanship continues
stories.summary: The U.S. downplayed Iran's seizure of European vessels as brinkmanship over the Strait of Hormuz continues. The financial impact of U.S. and Iranian blockades is becoming apparent, with Gulf states seeking access to U.S. dollars amid disrupted trade routes near Musandam, Oman.

stories.title: Erdogan: Turkey trying to revive Russia-Ukraine negotiations
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that Turkey is actively engaged in efforts to bring Russia and Ukraine back to the negotiation table for peace talks.

stories.title: Free sale of weapons to other countries impossible during active phase of war — Budanov
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence chief Budanov stated that free arms sales to other countries are not possible during the active phase of the war. He noted Ukraine can only sell weapons it has in sufficient supply, such as naval drones and UAV models considered outdated for current operations.

stories.title: Germany's Merz: Climate protection must not hold economy back
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that climate protection policies must not hold back the economy. He warned that the public would not accept measures leading to deindustrialization, arguing they would hinder progress and innovation.

stories.title: Trump’s top Navy official out, with US still locked in war with Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of the Navy John Phelan departed his post immediately, with no explanation from the Pentagon. His removal follows the recent ouster of top Army general Randy George and two other senior officers. The shakeup comes while the United States remains engaged in an unresolved conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Four dead in Russia, Ukraine after exchange of drone strikes
stories.summary: Drone strikes exchanged between Russia and Ukraine killed four people as both sides intensified long-range attacks amid stalled diplomatic talks. Moscow and Kyiv have been launching nightly swarms of explosive-laden drones at each other.

stories.title: Over 62,000 Lebanon housing units estimated to be damaged, destroyed in Israel attacks
stories.summary: An estimated 62,000 housing units in Lebanon have been damaged or destroyed by Israeli attacks since March 2. The strikes have killed more than 2,400 people and displaced over one million, according to local assessments.

stories.title: Peru ministers quit after president delays F-16 fighter jet purchase
stories.summary: Peruvian Defense Minister Carlos Diaz and Foreign Minister Hugo de Zela both resigned on Wednesday following interim President Jose Balcazar's decision to postpone a purchase of F-16 fighter jets from the United States.

stories.title: Body of journalist for pro-Hezbollah paper pulled from rubble of building hit by IDF
stories.summary: The body of journalist Amal Khalil was recovered from the rubble of a building struck by the Israeli military in Lebanon. The head of Lebanon's journalists union reported that a photographer accompanying Khalil suffered a head wound. The IDF said it targeted a building to which militants had fled.

stories.title: Lebanese journalist Zeinab Faraj wounded in Israeli air strike, stable after surgery
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Zeinab Faraj was wounded in an Israeli air strike and trapped for over an hour alongside colleague Amal Khalil before a Red Cross team evacuated her. The ambulance carrying Faraj came under fire and was hit by multiple bullets during the evacuation. Faraj underwent surgery and is reported in stable condition.

stories.title: Trump envoy seeks to replace Iran with Italy in World Cup, report says
stories.summary: A top envoy to U.S. President Donald Trump asked FIFA to replace Iran with Italy in the upcoming World Cup, according to the Financial Times. The proposal is reportedly aimed at mending ties between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni after a diplomatic rift over the Pope and the Iran war.

stories.title: Inside Tesla’s hidden supply chain: how a Chinese town shapes the modern world
stories.summary: Huangyan, an industrial district in Taizhou, Zhejiang province, China, is a major hub for plastic components and moulding equipment central to global manufacturing. The town's producers have long dominated this supply chain, supplying parts for Tesla and other automakers as well as household goods.

stories.title: Two more arrested on suspicion of plotting arson attack on Jewish venue
stories.summary: UK counter-terrorism police arrested two more men, aged 19 and 26, in Watford in connection with an alleged conspiracy to commit arson at a site connected to the Jewish community. Nine people have now been arrested in total in the investigation.

stories.title: All-rounder Mohammad Nawaz under scrutiny for alleged recreational drug use
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board investigated all-rounder Mohammad Nawaz after reports he tested positive for recreational drug use during the T20 World Cup. His contract to join Surrey for England's T20 Blast reportedly fell through as a result.

stories.title: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil, working for a Lebanese outlet, was killed in an Israeli air strike. Her body was recovered from rubble after the attack. Lebanon's health ministry accused Israel of targeting the house where Khalil and journalist Zeinab Faraj had taken shelter, while the Israeli military denied targeting journalists.

stories.title: Negotiations on Ukraine cannot wait until war in Iran ends — Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky warned that negotiations on Ukraine cannot wait until the war in Iran concludes, calling any delay a "big risk." He said the Iranian conflict has diverted international attention from Russia's ongoing aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: A lost film by Israeli B-movie director Sam Firstenberg gets a new life
stories.summary: Israeli-raised B-movie director Sam Firstenberg, known for cult films "American Ninja" and "Breakin' 2: Electric Boogaloo," is experiencing a career revival after a previously lost film was rediscovered and given new release.

stories.title: Sheinbaum weighs sanctions on Chihuahua state after CIA agents died after drug lab raid in Mexico
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she is considering sanctions against the government of Chihuahua state for allowing CIA agents to participate in a drug laboratory raid without federal approval. The operation led to the deaths of CIA agents, and Sheinbaum insisted all U.S. security collaboration must be authorized by Mexico's federal government.

stories.title: US says it is awaiting ‘unified’ Iranian position, amid reports of fractured leadership
stories.summary: The U.S. said it is waiting for a unified Iranian negotiating position amid reports of fractured leadership in Tehran. The White House offered no timeline for extending the U.S.-Iran truce, while Israeli media reported the deadline is Sunday. A source close to President Trump said he wants to exhaust all options before resuming military force.

stories.title: Pentagon says John Phelan out as Navy secretary
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that John Phelan is no longer serving as U.S. Navy Secretary. Spokesperson Sean Parnell confirmed the departure but the Pentagon provided no official reason for the move.

stories.title: China bought zero H200 chips ‘as of today’, says Lutnick as he cites ‘delicate balance’ with Xi
stories.summary: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testified before the Senate Appropriations Committee that China has purchased zero H200 advanced chips. Lutnick said President Trump is striking a "delicate balance" on technology transfers given his relationship with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, though senators expressed skepticism about the administration's approach.

stories.title: Navy Secretary Phelan leaving post immediately, Pentagon says
stories.summary: Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced that Navy Secretary John Phelan departed his post effective immediately. The sudden move was unexpected, and no explanation was provided by the Pentagon for the abrupt timing of his removal.

stories.title: Former Gaza hostages visit wounded soldiers before Independence Day
stories.summary: Former Hamas hostages Avinatan Or, Alon Ohel, and Guy Gilboa-Dalal visited wounded Israeli soldiers at the Rabin Medical Center-Beilinson Campus ahead of Israel's Independence Day. The three had been treated at the same facility after their release from captivity in Gaza.

stories.title: From paint to planes, Iran war lifts costs, darkens outlooks
stories.summary: The war involving Iran is driving up costs across multiple industries, from paint manufacturing to aviation. Investors and economists are monitoring whether companies can continue to absorb the financial shock of the conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky on sanctions against Russia: It is not about number of packages, but their quality
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that EU sanctions against Russia should be judged by their effectiveness and speed of implementation rather than the number of packages adopted.

stories.title: Second French peacekeeper dies after ambush blamed on Hezbollah
stories.summary: French peacekeeper Anicet Girardin became the second French soldier killed in Lebanon since hostilities escalated on 2 March, dying after an attack blamed on Hezbollah.

stories.title: Trump sets no deadline for Iran proposal, White House says
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that President Donald Trump has not set a deadline for receiving a proposal from Iran. Trump extended a ceasefire on Tuesday, with the White House saying the president will determine how long it remains in effect.

stories.title: Trial opens after Nigeria charges six over 2025 coup plot
stories.summary: A trial has opened in Nigeria after six men were charged with plotting a coup, including a planned attack on the presidential villa in 2025. Separately, a new investigation suggests foreign fighters, including Colombians, have been supporting one faction in the Sudan conflict.

stories.title: UK to pay France another £660m to curb Channel crossings
stories.summary: The UK government agreed to pay France £660 million over three years to reduce Channel crossings by asylum seekers. The deal, to be signed by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, includes funding for a riot squad and a 40% increase in enforcement, intelligence, and military officers to target smuggling gangs.

stories.title: China weathered Trump's tariffs - but the Iran war is taking a toll
stories.summary: The US-Iran war is straining China's export-driven economy, putting pressure on factory orders, production costs, and employment as the Middle East conflict disrupts global trade.

stories.title: How Iran and the United States Are Planning Their Next Moves
stories.summary: Analyst Karim Sadjadpour discussed the strategic calculations of both Iran and the United States following the extended ceasefire and the continued U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: What Happens if the U.S.-Iran Cease-Fire Collapses?
stories.summary: An analysis examines the fragility of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire and potential consequences if it collapses. Despite President Trump's extension of the truce, the agreement remains precarious.

stories.title: Zelensky calls EU loan matter of survival for Ukraine
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky described a proposed EUR 90 billion loan from the European Union as a matter of "life and surviving" for Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran war disrupting food aid for world’s hungriest, UN warns
stories.summary: The United Nations has warned that the Iran war is disrupting emergency food aid deliveries to the world's hungriest populations. Food shipments are currently stuck at ports in Oman and Kenya due to the conflict's impact on supply routes.

stories.title: Turkiye making efforts to revive Russia-Ukraine talks, says Erdogan
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan discussed efforts to revive Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations during a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Kyiv has requested that Ankara host a leaders-level meeting with Russia. Erdogan stated that Turkey is actively engaged in bringing both sides back to the negotiation table.

stories.title: Watch: Tamil Nadu and West Bengal to decide their fate tomorrow | Above the Fold | 22.04.2016
stories.summary: A news segment covered upcoming assembly elections in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, along with updates on the Iran-Israel conflict, a court ruling in the 2006 Malegaon blast case, and a revisit to Pahalgam one year after an attack.

stories.title: Gulf allies have requested financial support, US Treasury Secretary says
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Gulf and Asian allies have requested currency swap lines from the United States to manage energy shocks and economic fallout from the Middle East war.

stories.title: Firm tracks tanker movements despite US blockade of Iranian ports
stories.summary: Energy analytics firm Vortexa recorded 34 movements of sanctioned and Iranian-linked tankers in the Persian Gulf in the week following the imposition of a US naval blockade. Six outbound tankers were confirmed carrying approximately 10.7 million barrels of Iranian crude.

stories.title: How the US-Iran war is costing China
stories.summary: The BBC examines the economic costs the US-Iran war is imposing on China, including disruptions to trade and energy supply, alongside potential political opportunities for Beijing.

stories.title: President: Ukrainian military personnel sent to London for conference on reopening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Ukrainian military officials traveled to London to participate in a conference focused on strategies for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. President Zelensky confirmed the delegation's participation.

stories.title: Hungary Drops Veto on Massive EU Loan to Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungary dropped its veto on a major EU loan package to Ukraine after the reopening of the Druzhba pipeline resolved Budapest's final objection. The move clears the way for the financial aid to proceed.

stories.title: Twenty killed in suspected Boko Haram attack in Nigeria
stories.summary: At least 20 people were killed in a suspected Boko Haram attack in northeastern Nigeria. The assault is part of an escalating wave of violence by Boko Haram and its Islamic State-affiliated splinter group ISWAP, which have intensified attacks on military bases and villages in the region.

stories.title: EU unveils plan to tackle energy crisis
stories.summary: The European Union unveiled plans to protect households and businesses from an energy crisis triggered by the war with Iran. The bloc reported spending an additional €24 billion on energy imports due to higher prices since the conflict began and urged greater investment in renewable energy.

stories.title: Iran negotiator says reopening Hormuz ‘impossible’ amid ceasefire breaches
stories.summary: Iran's lead negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared on social media that reopening the Strait of Hormuz is impossible while ceasefire violations continue. He cited an ongoing maritime blockade and what he termed Zionist aggression across multiple fronts as obstacles to any agreement.

stories.title: One US team, two wars. Zelenskyy says Ukraine can’t wait for Iran to close
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN that pausing Ukraine peace talks until the US war with Iran concludes would be a "big risk." He described the EU's €90 billion loan as essential for Ukraine's survival.

stories.title: US halts $637 million cash shipment bound for Iraq after militia strikes, sources say
stories.summary: The United States halted a $637 million cash shipment destined for Iraq in response to strikes by Iran-backed militias. The move is intended to pressure the Iraqi government over the activities of those armed groups.

stories.title: Zelensky on renewed talks: Ukraine ready for meetings in any format, at any time
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine is prepared for peace talks in any format and at any time. He identified Turkey and Middle Eastern countries as priority locations for negotiations between Ukraine, the United States, and Russia.

stories.title: Israeli forces fire tear gas at funeral of Palestinians killed by settlers
stories.summary: Israeli forces used tear gas during a funeral in the occupied West Bank for two Palestinians who had been killed by settlers at a school.

stories.title: Israeli settler shoots, kills man in West Bank's Deir Dibwan
stories.summary: Israeli settlers shot and killed 25-year-old Awda Atef Awawdeh in the West Bank town of Deir Dibwan. The killing is the latest incident of Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied territory.

stories.title: Pakistan Gambled on Mediation
stories.summary: Pakistan's efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran face growing risks as talks between Washington and Tehran falter. Islamabad confronts increasing political and economic consequences from its mediating role.

stories.title: US Army seeks ‘last mile’ robot for medevac and resupply
stories.summary: The US Army is seeking an unmanned ground vehicle capable of transporting wounded personnel for medical evacuation and resupply missions without causing further harm to casualties.

stories.title: Trump must consider terms for Iranian people in potential deal, expert warns - interview
stories.summary: Author Roya Hakakian, who fled Iran as a teenager, warned that any US deal with Iran must consider terms benefiting the Iranian people. She cautioned that watching two major militaries fail to topple the regime could have a devastating effect on Iran's domestic opposition movement.

stories.title: With ciggies in short supply, Gaza smokers turn to dried jute
stories.summary: Amid severe shortages of cigarettes in Gaza, residents have resorted to smoking dried jute as a substitute. The improvised alternative reflects the dire conditions faced by people in the territory seeking any brief escape from hardship.

stories.title: Czech public broadcaster unions issue strike warning over government's funding revamp
stories.summary: Unions at Czech Television and Czech Radio issued a strike warning on Wednesday over proposed government reforms to the state broadcasters' funding model. The unions view the planned changes, including scrapping the licence fee, as a threat to the broadcasters' editorial independence.

stories.title: Red Cross vehicle carrying wounded journalist comes under fire in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanese health authorities reported that Israeli forces struck a house in at-Tiri sheltering journalists Zeinab Faraj and Amal Khalil after an initial attack. A Lebanese Red Cross ambulance attempting to evacuate the wounded was subsequently obstructed and fired upon, including being hit with a stun grenade.

stories.title: Tracking ships under fire in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's top negotiator declared it is "not possible to reopen" the Strait of Hormuz, accusing the United States of "blatant violations" of the US-Iran ceasefire. Ships in the strait continue to face dangerous conditions.

stories.title: US in talks to resettle 1,100 Afghans in Congo, group says
stories.summary: The Trump administration is in discussions with the Democratic Republic of Congo to resettle approximately 1,100 Afghans who have been stranded in Qatar while awaiting U.S. visas, according to an advocacy organization working on their behalf.

stories.title: In Gaza, first local vote in years offers gauge of Hamas popularity
stories.summary: Municipal elections are being held in the Palestinian territories, offering the first local vote in years and a potential measure of Hamas's popularity in Gaza. The polls represent the fifth municipal elections in the West Bank since 2005.

stories.title: School's out in Iran: No phone, no internet, no classes
stories.summary: Schools across Iran have closed due to the ongoing war, with classes conducted via television and the national intranet. Children without laptops or smartphones are unable to participate, and the country remains largely cut off from the global internet.

stories.title: FY27 budget request negates need for INDOPACOM spending wishlist: Commander
stories.summary: INDOPACOM Commander Admiral Samuel Paparo indicated that the fiscal year 2027 budget request addresses Pacific defense needs, reducing the necessity for a separate spending wishlist. The Department of Defense plans to allocate $12 billion for the Pacific Deterrence Initiative next year.

stories.title: Israel's furthest north communities welcome baby born during Independence Day
stories.summary: Tal and Kirish Akrish welcomed their third son at Ziv Medical Center in northern Israel, marking the first birth at the facility's maternity ward since the war began over a month ago. The family resides in one of Israel's northernmost communities.

stories.title: Ukraine says it is ready joining multinational mine-clearing operation in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Ukraine announced its readiness to join a multinational mine-clearing operation in the Strait of Hormuz, with two Ukrainian vessels crewed by personnel who have completed training and passed NATO interoperability assessments.

stories.title: Sexual violence in the West Bank emerges as tool to intimidate Palestinians
stories.summary: Reports document systematic sexual violence and harassment by Israeli soldiers and settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, described as a tool to intimidate and displace the population.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times, causing damage
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Nikopol, Kryvyi Rih, and Synelnykiv districts of Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times using artillery, aerial bombs, and drones, causing damage across the area.

stories.title: Can a divided EU become a united voice against Israeli aggression?
stories.summary: The European Union faces growing internal debate over its relationship with Israel, its largest trading partner, amid calls for a unified stance on the conflict.

stories.title: Lebanon accuses Israel of blocking attempt to rescue journalist after bomb strike
stories.summary: Lebanon accused Israel of blocking rescue efforts after an Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon wounded journalist Zeinab Faraj and left journalist Amal Khalil trapped under rubble for hours. Israel's military denied preventing rescue teams from reaching the area.

stories.title: Warner Bros and Paramount merger could reshape US media landscape
stories.summary: A proposed merger between Warner Bros and Paramount is under regulatory scrutiny in the United States, with concerns about its impact on the media landscape and the role of foreign investment in funding the deal.

stories.title: Israel’s death penalty law deepens injustice for Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel enacted a new death penalty law that critics say deepens an apartheid-like legal framework imposed on Palestinians under occupation. Analyst Fadel Abdulghany argues the legislation entrenches systemic injustice against the Palestinian population.

stories.title: Algeria bookshop reopens after being shut by police over event
stories.summary: An Algerian bookshop reopened days after police raided it and forced its closure over a book-signing event by author Fatma Oussedik. The incident has renewed concerns about censorship and restrictions on free expression in Algeria.

stories.title: Instagram Star’s Appeal to Putin Sets Off a War of Words, from State TV to the Opposition
stories.summary: Russian-born Instagram personality Viktoria Bonya posted a viral message to President Putin about the struggles of ordinary Russians, sparking heated debate across state television and opposition circles.

stories.title: Iran murals project defiance in war with US
stories.summary: Murals projecting defiance against the United States have appeared across Iran's urban landscape amid the ongoing war. The displays build on a longstanding tradition of murals and banners as tools of public messaging in Iran.

stories.title: Syrian minorities refused asylum in Europe as rejections surge
stories.summary: EU asylum approval rates for Syrian nationals have dropped sharply following the fall of Bashar al-Assad's government. Critics warn that the surge in rejections is premature, as Syria remains unstable and unsafe for returning refugees.

stories.title: EU prepares finalisation of Ukraine loan and new Russia sanctions, Cyprus says
stories.summary: EU ambassadors in Brussels approved on Wednesday the disbursement of a €90 billion loan to Ukraine and a new sanctions package against Russia after Hungary lifted its veto. Cyprus, holding the EU's rotating presidency, confirmed the decision and said formal sign-off was expected by Thursday.

stories.title: ‘Hungry all the time’: US Navy deny food shortages after grim photos emerge
stories.summary: The US Navy denied claims of food shortages aboard warships maintaining the blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, after photos showing mostly empty food trays circulated online with reports that sailors were "hungry all the time."

stories.title: Lebanon hopes for extension of ceasefire at Washington meeting
stories.summary: Lebanon's government is seeking an extension of the 10-day US-mediated ceasefire with Israel, set to expire on April 26, during meetings in Washington. The ceasefire has provided a temporary halt to hostilities.

stories.title: Inquiry clears Bristol school of antisemitism for postponing Jewish MP’s visit
stories.summary: An independent inquiry into Bristol Brunel Academy found no evidence of antisemitism after the school postponed a visit by Jewish Labour MP Damien Egan. The review concluded the visit was delayed over safeguarding concerns rather than external influence.

stories.title: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian man in West Bank shooting
stories.summary: Israeli settlers shot and killed 29-year-old Palestinian Odeh Atef Odeh Awawdeh in Deir Dibwan, east of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank. According to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, settlers surrounded the town and opened fire with live ammunition; Awawdeh was shot in the back and died at Ramallah Medical Complex.

stories.title: Trump among recipients of Israel Prize for ‘special contribution to the Jewish people’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is among the recipients of Israel's annual Israel Prize for "special contribution to the Jewish people." He is expected to receive the award during his next visit to Israel, alongside artists, researchers, and educators honored at the ceremony.

stories.title: Mexico’s Sheinbaum demands answers over CIA agents in Chihuahua
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum demanded an explanation after CIA officers were found to have participated in a drug raid in the state of Chihuahua without the federal government's knowledge.
