stories.title: High Anti-Corruption Court refuses to dismiss charges against Tymoshenko
stories.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court denied a defense motion to dismiss charges against Member of Parliament Yulia Tymoshenko. The ruling allows the case to proceed.

stories.title: Israel bombs Gaza police checkpoint after gang members attacked
stories.summary: Israel bombed a police checkpoint in Gaza after gang members were reportedly attacked there. Hamas said it would soon respond to proposals for the second phase of a ceasefire, though talks have proven difficult.

stories.title: No delegation from Iran visits Islamabad, state television says, as talks speculation grows
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that no delegation from Iran had traveled to Islamabad for potential talks with the United States. Pakistani officials have been on standby for days awaiting possible negotiations, but no Iranian official has confirmed participation.

stories.title: WATCH: US intercepts 'stateless sanctioned' vessel in Indo-Pacific area, enforcing Iran sanctions
stories.summary: The Pentagon confirmed the US military boarded the stateless vessel M/T Tifani in the Indo-Pacific, which was tied to Iranian smuggling activity. The operation was part of global maritime enforcement efforts to disrupt illicit networks and enforce Iran sanctions.

stories.title: In a first, Ukraine’s drone force launches interceptor drone from USV to destroy Shahed
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone force achieved a first by launching an interceptor drone from an uncrewed surface vessel to destroy a Russian Shahed kamikaze drone. Experts say this new sea-air integration capability could significantly complicate Russia's use of kamikaze drones against Ukrainian targets.

stories.title: Role of US officials killed in crash in Mexico under scrutiny
stories.summary: Two U.S. officials died in a car crash in Mexico following a Mexican-led operation to destroy a clandestine drug laboratory. The circumstances and roles of the officials involved are now under scrutiny.

stories.title: Lamine Yamal, Carlos Alcaraz among winners at Laureus World Sports Awards
stories.summary: The Laureus World Sports Awards ceremony was held in Madrid. FC Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and tennis star Carlos Alcaraz were among the winners.

stories.title: Eurovision 2026: Over 1000 artists call for boycott for ‘normalising’ Israel’s genocide
stories.summary: Over 1,000 artists, including Brian Eno, Macklemore, and Sigur Rós, have called for a boycott of Eurovision 2026, accusing the broadcaster of normalizing Israel's actions and drawing comparisons to its response to Russia.

stories.title: Iran war fuel hike adds $130 to long-haul flight cost, study says
stories.summary: A study found that fuel price increases linked to the Iran conflict are adding approximately $130 to long-haul flight costs. European airlines are bracing for a difficult spring and summer travel season as a result.

stories.title: Rabbi who became mascot for Gaza genocide honoured by Israel on independence day
stories.summary: Rabbi Avraham Zarbiv, known for filming himself destroying Palestinian homes in Gaza, has been chosen to light a torch at Israel's national independence day ceremony, one of the country's highest civilian honors.

stories.title: 11 countries want Ukraine’s drone defense technology: three Gulf states already signed 10-year deals
stories.summary: Eleven countries have expressed interest in acquiring Ukraine's battlefield-validated drone defense technology, including interceptor drones designed to shoot down attack UAVs. Three Gulf states have already signed 10-year deals for the systems.

stories.title: Nigeria charges six people with treason over Independence Day coup plot
stories.summary: Nigerian authorities charged six people with treason over an alleged coup plot. Suspicions first emerged in October 2025 when an Independence Day parade was cancelled.

stories.title: Israeli settlers kill two Palestinians, including student, in Ramallah school attack
stories.summary: Israeli settlers opened fire near a school in al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, killing two Palestinians, including a student. The Palestinian health ministry reported four others were wounded in the attack.

stories.title: Russia and North Korea Celebrate Joining of First Road Bridge
stories.summary: Russia and North Korea celebrated the completion of their first road bridge connecting the two countries. The crossing is scheduled to open for traffic in the summer and is designed to handle up to 300 vehicles and 2,850 people daily.

stories.title: Iran decides to continue negotiations with U.S. following Trump's latest threats — Axios
stories.summary: Iran decided to continue negotiations with the United States after Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered a last-minute return to the negotiating table, according to Axios. A US delegation led by Vice President J.D. Vance traveled to Islamabad for talks aimed at ending the war.

stories.title: Why speculation about China arming Iran is way off base
stories.summary: An analysis argues that speculation about China arming Iran in the ongoing conflict is unfounded, contending that Beijing would have nothing to gain from fueling the war.

stories.title: Number of Hong Kong school leavers seeking education elsewhere hits 14-year low
stories.summary: The number of Hong Kong secondary school leavers studying abroad fell to a 14-year low of 2,671 in 2025, a 13 percent drop from 2024. An expert attributed the decline to increased competition from mainland Chinese students enrolling in Hong Kong universities.

stories.title: Hormuz crisis forces Japan, South Korea to rethink strategy
stories.summary: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has prompted Japan and South Korea to reassess their strategic reliance on maritime trade routes for essential goods, including food and fuel supplies.

stories.title: What are Japan, South Korea learning from Hormuz disruption?
stories.summary: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has alarmed Japan and South Korea, exposing their heavy dependence on maritime trade routes for critical imports including food and fuel.

stories.title: Beware scam messages offering ships safe transit through Hormuz Strait, says security firm
stories.summary: A security firm warned the shipping industry about scam messages offering safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Unknown actors have been demanding that shipping companies pay transit fees in cryptocurrency in exchange for passage clearance.

stories.title: US held secret talks with Cuba
stories.summary: Cuba and the United States confirmed that officials held talks on the island on April 10 amid ongoing tensions over the U.S. energy blockade on the Caribbean nation. Cuba identified lifting the blockade as a key priority in the discussions.

stories.title: Ukraine’s new exoskeleton has no electronics, no power supply, and takes 2 minutes to put on
stories.summary: Ukraine has developed a new exoskeleton for frontline soldiers that is purely mechanical, requiring no electronics or power supply. The device can be put on in two minutes, making it well-suited to electronic warfare conditions.

stories.title: Jet fuel prices flying sky high
stories.summary: The war in Iran is driving jet fuel prices sharply higher, putting pressure on airlines and raising concerns about potential fuel shortages. France and other European countries are seeking solutions, including alternative fuel sources, to prevent supply disruptions in the aviation sector.

stories.title: 'Nothing to go back to' - BBC reports from Lebanon's 'Yellow Line'
stories.summary: Israel has established a military zone it calls the "Yellow Line," extending roughly 10 kilometers north of its border with Lebanon. The buffer zone has displaced Lebanese residents from their homes in the area.

stories.title: Olly Robbins revelas "constant pressure"
stories.summary: Former senior British Foreign Office official Olly Robbins told a parliamentary committee he faced "constant pressure" from the Prime Minister's office to expedite Peter Mandelson's appointment as ambassador to the United States. Robbins said Number 10 showed a "dismissive attitude" toward security vetting, amid reports that independent officials recommended denying Mandelson clearance over past links to Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: German Gurdwara violence: Four injured in clash; police launch probe
stories.summary: A violent clash at a Gurdwara in Germany on April 19 left four people injured, prompting a major police security response. Authorities launched an investigation after footage of the unrest inside the premises spread on social media.

stories.title: Settlers raise Israeli flag at al-Aqsa in latest raid on mosque
stories.summary: Israeli settlers and soldiers raised Israeli flags at the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound and other sites occupied by the army to mark Israel's Independence Day, in the latest raid on the holy site.

stories.title: Ukraine family get cancer and bomb news on same day
stories.summary: A Ukrainian family received their baby's cancer diagnosis on the same day their home in Ukraine was struck by Russian drones, compounding personal and wartime crises.

stories.title: London Tube strike set to cause travel chaos for commuters
stories.summary: London Underground staff are set to stage two 24-hour walkouts this week, expected to cause significant disruption for commuters across the city.

stories.title: Young doctor shot dead near Karachi’s Mehran Hotel
stories.summary: A young doctor, Dr. Sarang Memon, was fatally shot near Karachi's Mehran Hotel on Monday night in a suspected targeted attack. He was traveling in a rickshaw with his wife when armed suspects in a car intercepted and fired upon them before fleeing.

stories.title: ECP halts Senate by-election for Murad Saeed’s vacant seat
stories.summary: Pakistan's Election Commission halted the Senate by-election for the seat vacated by PTI leader Murad Saeed and issued a stay order. A petition challenged the legality of the de-notification process, arguing Saeed had never taken the oath of office.

stories.title: Iran signals new military options amid talks uncertainty
stories.summary: Iran has indicated it possesses additional military capabilities it could deploy if hostilities resume, while sending mixed signals about its participation in upcoming talks in Pakistan. Internal divisions within Iran's leadership have surfaced, particularly regarding policy on the Strait of Hormuz, as the US prepares to send its vice president to Islamabad.

stories.title: Former Hong Kong trade office chief contesting UK local elections for Reform
stories.summary: Lee Sheung-yuen, a former director of Hong Kong's Economic and Trade Offices in Jakarta and Bangkok, is running for a seat on London's Ealing Council representing the Reform UK party. He left Hong Kong government service in 2023.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ holds talks with DP World on rebuilding Gaza, FT says
stories.summary: Trump's Board of Peace held talks with Dubai-based DP World about rebuilding Gaza. Discussions focused on a potential partnership for DP World to handle logistics operations in the territory.

stories.title: Nigeria charges six people with ‘terrorism’, treason over 2025 coup plot
stories.summary: Nigerian authorities have charged six military officers with terrorism and treason over an alleged plot to overthrow President Bola Tinubu in 2025.

stories.title: Iran’s World Cup participation depends on team’s safety in the US: Minister
stories.summary: Iran's Sport Minister Ahmad Donyamali said the national team is preparing for the FIFA World Cup but may not travel to the US-hosted tournament unless player safety can be guaranteed.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers and settlers kill 11 Palestinians across Gaza, West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers and settlers killed 11 Palestinians across Gaza and the West Bank. In Hebron, a 16-year-old was struck and killed by a vehicle escorting an Israeli minister.

stories.title: Makeshift pistol from Israel's War of Independence to be displayed at Ha'emek Museum for first time
stories.summary: A makeshift pistol built during Israel's 1948 War of Independence will be displayed at Ha'emek Museum for the first time. The weapon was constructed by 16-year-old Uzi Aharoni in Kibbutz Gvat's blacksmith shop to defend the settlement.

stories.title: A bitter reflection on Independence Day as Israel celebrates its 78th anniversary - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on Israel's 78th Independence Day, expressing concern about the state of its liberal democratic character. The author argues that a change in leadership is needed in the upcoming general election.

stories.title: 1.5 million more Russian soldiers would have to die to take rest of Donetsk Oblast — Ukraine’s UN ambassador
stories.summary: Ukraine's UN ambassador cited casualty-per-territory statistics suggesting Russia has lost approximately 254 soldiers per square kilometer in Donetsk Oblast. At that rate, taking the rest of the region would require an estimated 1.5 million more Russian casualties.

stories.title: US House votes to extend temporary protections for Haitian immigrants
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed bipartisan legislation to extend Temporary Protected Status for Haitian immigrants. The measure pushes back against President Donald Trump's efforts to end the program.

stories.title: IAF pilot reveals he considered recording keepsakes for his family during Operation Roaring Lion
stories.summary: An Israeli Air Force pilot revealed he considered recording farewell messages for his family during Operation Roaring Lion. Despite the emotional weight, he remained focused on completing the mission.

stories.title: Jewish anti-Zionist group files ‘genocide’ claim against FedEx over Israel deliveries
stories.summary: The French Jewish Union for Peace filed a legal claim against FedEx, alleging the company delivered parts for F-35 aircraft used in bombing raids in Gaza. FedEx denied it transports weapons.

stories.title: Hong Kong aiming to curb illicit fuel trade with tougher penalties: source
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Security Bureau proposed tougher penalties for illicit fuel trade, including fines up to HK$1 million and one year in prison for buyers. Maximum penalties for sellers would increase to HK$3 million and longer jail terms under the proposed amendments.

stories.title: Germany and Italy reject push by EU allies to end association deal with Israel
stories.summary: Germany and Italy rejected calls by Spain, Slovenia, and Ireland to suspend the EU's trade association agreement with Israel. Belgium described Israeli conduct as "unacceptable" and pushed for a partial suspension.

stories.title: Denmark to receive first SAMP/T NG air-defense system in 2028
stories.summary: Denmark is set to receive its first SAMP/T New Generation air-defense system in 2028. Copenhagen selected the European-made system in September over the American Patriot missile defense platform.

stories.title: Guinea Bissau's Djabi seriously injured in stabbing
stories.summary: Midtjylland midfielder Alamara Djabi of Guinea-Bissau was seriously injured in a stabbing in Denmark. His club confirmed he is in stable condition.

stories.title: Lebanon seeks truce extension in Thursday talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon is seeking to extend its truce with Israel ahead of new talks scheduled in Washington on Thursday. Attacks and home demolitions continue in Israeli-occupied areas of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Nigeria's $2B energy bailout tests President Tinubu reforms
stories.summary: Nigeria approved roughly $2 billion to clear power sector debts under President Tinubu's reform agenda. Analysts say the move could stabilize electricity supply but warn that deeper structural issues in the energy sector remain unaddressed.

stories.title: Nigeria's $2B power bailout tests Tinubu reforms
stories.summary: Nigeria approved approximately $2 billion to clear power sector debts. Analysts say the bailout may stabilize electricity supply but leaves deeper structural problems in the energy sector unresolved.

stories.title: Myanmar president seeks peace talks by July 31, 2 rebel groups reject offer
stories.summary: Myanmar's military-backed President Min Aung Hlaing called for peace talks with opposition armed groups by July 31. Two key rebel groups rejected the offer, and the country's civil war continues five years after his coup.

stories.title: Dozens of Israelis Briefly Detained, Questioned at Moscow Airport
stories.summary: Dozens of Israeli citizens were briefly detained and questioned by security officials at a Moscow airport. Russian media reported that some passengers were questioned regarding the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Trump says he does not want to extend ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump told CNBC he does not want to extend the ceasefire with Iran, saying the US is in a strong negotiating position. Washington has expressed confidence that talks with Iran will proceed in Pakistan.

stories.title: Shipping traffic through Hormuz remains mostly halted
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains largely halted, with only three ships passing in the past 24 hours. Iran has maintained restrictions on the waterway in response to a US blockade of Iranian ports, despite a pause in hostilities.

stories.title: Israel honors fallen soldiers on Remembrance Day as US-Iran talks begin in Islamabad
stories.summary: Israel observed Remembrance Day honoring fallen soldiers as US-Iran negotiations began in Islamabad, Pakistan. The Jerusalem Post provided a news roundup covering the day's top developments.

stories.title: Teenager pleads guilty to arson attack on synagogue in London
stories.summary: A 17-year-old British boy from Brent, north-west London, pleaded guilty at Westminster magistrates court to arson not endangering life after an attack on Kenton United Synagogue on Saturday night. The teenager has not been publicly named due to his age.

stories.title: Kremlin forcing big firms to join ‘witch-hunt’ against internet rebels, claims report
stories.summary: Researchers report that major Russian companies, including banks and web platforms, are being compelled by the Kremlin to collect data on users employing VPN tools to access blocked websites. The advocacy group RKS Global described the effort as a "witch-hunt" against citizens circumventing internet controls.

stories.title: EU court finds Hungary's anti-LGBTQ legislation violates bloc's rules
stories.summary: The European Court of Justice ruled on Tuesday that Hungary's 2021 anti-LGBTQ legislation violates EU rules. The decision presents an early challenge for Hungary's new leader Peter Magyar, who won a landslide election on April 12, ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year hold on power.

stories.title: SSU drones strike Samara oil terminal, which processes Urals crude for export
stories.summary: Ukrainian Security Service drones struck the Samara line-production dispatch station in the town of Prosvet, Samara region, Russia, causing a major fire. The facility processes Urals crude oil for export.

stories.title: Two men guilty of murdering woman in drive-by shooting at London church
stories.summary: Two men were found guilty of murdering Michelle Sadio, 44, in a drive-by shooting outside the River of Life Pentecostal church in Willesden, north London, on December 14, 2024. Sadio was among approximately 100 mourners at a wake when the shooting occurred, injuring two others.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Coordinated attacks and evictions in Gaza, West Bank
stories.summary: Palestinian deaths in Gaza and settler violence across the West Bank continued to surge in the past week, with coordinated attacks and evictions reported in both territories.

stories.title: South Korea's Lee says claim that Minister leaked classified intel is 'absurd'
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung dismissed as "absurd" claims that Unification Minister Chung Dong-young leaked classified intelligence. South Korean media reported the United States curtailed some intelligence sharing on North Korea after Chung publicly discussed a previously unconfirmed uranium enrichment facility.

stories.title: Tigray restores regional parliament, stoking fears of conflict with Addis Ababa
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) announced the restoration of a regional parliament in Ethiopia's Tigray region. The move has alarmed observers who fear it could reignite conflict between the TPLF and the Ethiopian federal government.

stories.title: Shot by Israeli forces, Hala, 18 and Mohammad, 13 fight for their lives
stories.summary: An 18-year-old woman in Gaza and a 13-year-old boy in the West Bank are fighting for their lives after being shot in the head by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Navy tests long-range JDAM, striking out to 200 nautical miles
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy tested modified long-range Joint Direct Attack Munitions launched from F/A-18E Super Hornets in back-to-back trials, striking targets at distances up to 200 nautical miles. The JDAM modifications were developed by Boeing to extend the weapon's range significantly beyond its standard capability.

stories.title: Taiwanese leader Lai postpones Africa trip after 3 nations revoke overflight permission
stories.summary: Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te postponed a trip to eSwatini, Taiwan's sole African diplomatic partner, after three nations revoked overflight permission. Taipei blamed the denials on pressure from Beijing, marking the first such last-minute delay for a Taiwanese leader.

stories.title: Iran executes man over burning of mosque during January protests: report
stories.summary: Iran executed a man convicted of burning a mosque during nationwide anti-government protests earlier this year. The protests were met with what has been described as the largest crackdown in the Islamic Republic's history.

stories.title: Hezbollah to bury fighters killed in war with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah is holding mass funerals in southern Lebanon for 44 fighters killed during the war with Israel. The ongoing ceasefire has allowed the group to retrieve and bury the remains.

stories.title: Four contenders for UN secretary-general face live hearings; others may join race
stories.summary: Four candidates are facing live hearings for the position of UN secretary-general to replace António Guterres. Contenders include IAEA chief Rafael Grossi and former Costa Rican president Rebeca Grynspan, with others potentially joining the race.

stories.title: PAA extends airspace ban for Indian aircraft until May 24
stories.summary: The Pakistan Airport Authority extended its airspace ban on Indian-registered aircraft and Indian airlines until May 24, 2026. The restriction, covering both the Karachi and Lahore flight information regions, marks a year of flight restrictions on Indian aviation.

stories.title: France and Lebanon share 'cultural, religious and political links, dating back to the 19th century'
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron hosted Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam in Paris, underscoring longstanding cultural, religious, and diplomatic ties between France and Lebanon dating to the 19th century. Analysts note that France's traditional mediating role in Lebanese affairs has diminished due to regional realignments and strained relations with Israel.

stories.title: Last remaining perpetrators of Rwandan genocide return to villages
stories.summary: Thirty-two years after the Rwandan genocide, the country is reintegrating its last remaining convicted perpetrators into communities where they committed their crimes. Many of those being released have served full 30-year prison sentences. Authorities face the challenge of resettling these individuals in a society that has undergone profound transformation.

stories.title: US positive on Iran deal but talks still uncertain as ceasefire end nears
stories.summary: The United States has expressed optimism about reaching a deal with Iran, but negotiations remain uncertain as the current ceasefire deadline approaches. A Pakistani source indicated President Trump might attend a signing ceremony in person or virtually if an agreement is reached.

stories.title: US positive on Iran deal but talks still uncertain as ceasefire end nears
stories.summary: The United States expressed confidence that peace talks with Iran would proceed in Pakistan, while a senior Iranian official said Tehran was considering participation. Significant hurdles remain as a ceasefire between the two countries nears expiration.

stories.title: Russian forces fire on Donetsk region 1,354 times
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 1,354 attacks on the Donetsk region over the past 24 hours, damaging 30 civilian facilities.

stories.title: Palestinian teenager killed by Israeli minister convoy car
stories.summary: An Israeli security convoy linked to Settlement Minister Orit Strook struck and killed a Palestinian teenager near Hebron as the youth was heading to school.

stories.title: Spain, Ireland, Slovenia push EU to suspend Israel pact
stories.summary: Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia are pressing the European Union to discuss suspending its trade agreement with Israel, citing alleged rights abuses in Gaza and breaches of international law.

stories.title: With tariffs stalled, Trump’s China policy drifts
stories.summary: President Trump's China policy has stalled amid paused tariff actions, causing confusion among US officials and leading to contradictory decisions within the administration.

stories.title: Contenders to head crisis-wracked UN face live grillings
stories.summary: Four candidates competing to become the next UN secretary-general are facing live public hearings on April 21 and 22 as the organization grapples with multiple crises.

stories.title: Pakistan races against time to get Iran back to US talks as truce end nears
stories.summary: Pakistan is working urgently to bring Iran back to negotiations with the United States as the ceasefire deadline approaches, but US escalations are complicating mediation efforts, according to analysts.

stories.title: Nepal restarts Gulf work permits after Iran conflict halted labor migration
stories.summary: Nepal has resumed issuing work permits for Gulf countries after the Iran conflict disrupted labor migration to the region. Approximately 75% of Nepali workers abroad are based in the Middle East, and remittances account for over a quarter of Nepal's $42 billion economy.

stories.title: Japan’s new arms export rules trigger Chinese warning against ‘moves towards militarism’
stories.summary: Japan's cabinet approved a major overhaul of arms export rules, scrapping long-standing restrictions rooted in post-war pacifism. China expressed "serious concern," warning against moves toward militarism. The changes could enable sales of lethal equipment previously banned.

stories.title: Requests for US legal aid linked to Palestine activism far surpass pre-2023 levels
stories.summary: Palestine Legal reported that requests for legal assistance related to Palestine activism in the U.S. remain far above pre-2023 levels, logging 1,131 requests in 2025. While down from a record 2,184 in 2024, the figure represents a 300% increase over any year before Israel's war in Gaza.

stories.title: Economist Justin Lin urges West to adopt ‘Eastern wisdom’ as China moves up value chain
stories.summary: Former World Bank chief economist Justin Lin Yifu rejected Western claims of Chinese "overcapacity" as a double standard. Speaking in Hong Kong, he urged advanced economies to adopt "Eastern wisdom" rather than protectionism in response to China's rise in hi-tech industries.

stories.title: ‘Blood only begets blood’: Why these bereaved Oct. 7 families still choose coexistence
stories.summary: Some bereaved families of October 7 Hamas attack victims are working alongside Palestinian peace activists to advocate for political change and coexistence, despite facing a hostile public atmosphere in Israel.

stories.title: US forces intercepted ‘gift from China’ to Iran, Donald Trump says
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that American forces intercepted a ship carrying items he described as a "gift from China" destined for Iran. The claim came as a two-week ceasefire was set to expire, with Trump suggesting Tehran had been restocking supplies with Beijing's assistance.

stories.title: FedEx faces French 'genocide' complaint over Israel cargoes
stories.summary: FedEx is facing a legal complaint in France alleging complicity in genocide in Gaza. The complaint claims the company shipped aircraft parts to Israel used in F-35 fighter jet operations.

stories.title: In bellicose Memorial Day speeches, leaders vow to keep fighting; Netanyahu heckled
stories.summary: Israeli leaders delivered combative Memorial Day speeches vowing to continue fighting. Prime Minister Netanyahu was heckled by a protester when he claimed to have brought back all hostages from Gaza, while the defense minister threatened Hezbollah's leader.

stories.title: Mossad agent killed abroad significantly influenced Iran war, Barnea reveals
stories.summary: Mossad chief David Barnea revealed that an agent identified only as "M." was killed abroad and had significantly influenced the course of the Iran war. Barnea did not disclose the agent's identity, the timing, or the specific location of the death.

stories.title: Mossad agent ‘Mem,’ who died in 2023, contributed to Iran war success, spy chief reveals
stories.summary: Israel's Mossad chief revealed that an agent known as "Mem," who died in 2023 when a boat capsized on Italy's Lake Maggiore during a reported meeting between Israeli and Italian spies, contributed to successes in the Iran war.

stories.title: Mass trial for 486 alleged MS-13 gang members begins in El Salvador
stories.summary: A mass trial for 486 alleged members of the MS-13 gang began in El Salvador. The defendants are collectively accused of committing more than 47,000 crimes, including murder.

stories.title: Chad announces deployment of troops to Haiti to help tackle gangs
stories.summary: Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Deby announced the deployment of 1,500 troops to Haiti as part of a UN-backed security force. The mission aims to help combat gang violence in the Caribbean nation.

stories.title: EU credibility is on the line over Israel, says Spanish foreign minister
stories.summary: Spain's foreign minister warned that the EU's credibility is at risk without a unified stance on Israel, urging consistency with the bloc's approach toward Russia.

stories.title: Three ships including an Iranian vessel attempt Hormuz transits
stories.summary: Three ships, including an Iranian vessel, attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Of the other two ships, one is flagged to Gambia and the other has no identifiable flag or owner.

stories.title: China’s CRRC drops bid for Lisbon metro deal as EU finds ‘billions’ in subsidies probe
stories.summary: Chinese railway manufacturer CRRC withdrew from a Lisbon metro contract after a European Commission investigation found the company benefited from foreign subsidies that allowed it to underbid competitors. A Polish firm was awarded the contract instead, with the EU citing harm to its internal market integrity.

stories.title: Tai Po blaze probe: temporary removal of fireproof windows ‘complied with rules’
stories.summary: A Hong Kong Labour Department official told an inquiry into the deadly Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court that the temporary removal of fireproof windows from emergency passages complied with occupational safety protocols. The inquiry also heard that a department officer had misled residents about the regulatory scope of renovation materials' fire resistance.

stories.title: Buffer zone: How Israel is tightening its grip on south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel is consolidating control over southern Lebanon through the demolition of villages and creation of a buffer zone demarcated by a so-called Yellow Line. The measures continue despite the ceasefire, signaling Israel's intent to maintain a long-term military presence in the area.

stories.title: State tells High Court there is no basis to move up deadline in Gaza press-access case
stories.summary: Israel asked the High Court to maintain its May deadline in a case concerning foreign journalists' access to Gaza. The state argued that ongoing military operations and incomplete processes justify keeping the current timeline.

stories.title: Report: Russia opens negligence case after pacifist blogger is found hanged in prison solitary confinement cell
stories.summary: Russian authorities opened a criminal negligence case after pacifist blogger Vegan Khristolub Bozhiy was found hanged in a solitary confinement cell at a prison in the Voronezh region. Sources close to the blogger reported the death to Russian Telegram channels SotaVision and Ostorozhno Novosti.

stories.title: Trump says recovering Iran uranium ‘will be a long and difficult process’
stories.summary: President Trump stated that recovering uranium from Iran will be a long and difficult process, signaling expectations of protracted negotiations on the nuclear issue.

stories.title: Iran-US war: Four scenarios for what’s next as talks stumble
stories.summary: Analysts outlined four potential scenarios for the US-Iran conflict as the ceasefire nears expiration and negotiations over a possible deal remain uncertain.

stories.title: Biographies of Bulgakov and Vysotsky to be labeled under Russia’s drug ‘promotion’ law
stories.summary: Biographical books about Russian poet Vladimir Vysotsky and writer Mikhail Bulgakov will be labeled under Russia's law banning drug "propaganda," according to state news agencies RIA Novosti and TASS.

stories.title: EU to warn against early nuclear exits in effort to address energy crisis
stories.summary: The European Commission is set to caution EU member states against prematurely shutting down nuclear power plants as Europe grapples with an energy crisis exacerbated by the Iran war. The draft plan also includes measures to cut electricity taxes and scale up clean energy technologies.

stories.title: World’s top condom maker to raise prices by up to 30% over Iran war impact
stories.summary: Malaysia-based Karex, the world's largest condom manufacturer, announced plans to raise prices by 20 to 30 percent due to supply chain disruptions caused by the Iran war. CEO Goh Miah Kiat said rising freight costs and shipping delays have reduced customer stockpiles, driving a surge in demand.

stories.title: Full suspension of trade relations with Israel requires EU unanimity
stories.summary: Germany on Tuesday blocked EU efforts led by Spain and Ireland to suspend the bloc's cooperation agreement with Israel over its conduct in Gaza, Lebanon, and the West Bank. Berlin called the proposed suspension "inappropriate." Any full suspension of EU-Israel trade relations requires unanimous agreement among all member states.

stories.title: Canadian military aims to show it can go it alone in the Arctic
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has pledged that Canada will develop the capability to defend its Arctic territory independently, without relying on outside assistance. The Canadian military is undertaking efforts to demonstrate self-sufficiency in Arctic operations.

stories.title: Singer Dua Lipa helped raise funds for a pickup truck for Ukrainian military medics
stories.summary: Singer Dua Lipa helped raise funds through a Service95 event in London, organized with Driving Ukraine, to purchase a pickup truck for Ukrainian military medics. The vehicle was delivered to Ukraine's First Separate Medical Battalion.

stories.title: Man detonates grenade in Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring five police officers
stories.summary: Five police officers were injured in the Synelnykove district of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region when a heavily intoxicated man detonated a grenade. The suspect has been detained.

stories.title: Why we must demand accountability from Meta over Palestine
stories.summary: Meta is accused of monetizing Israeli settlement activity and violence against Palestinians while suppressing Palestinian voices on its platforms. Jalal Abukhater calls for accountability from the social media company over its content moderation policies.

stories.title: Trump's 'Board of Peace' held talks with DP World over Gaza reconstruction
stories.summary: Members of President Trump's Board of Peace communicated with Emirati company DP World about managing supply chains, humanitarian aid, and logistics for Gaza reconstruction. Discussions included warehousing, tracking systems, and security for goods entering the besieged territory.

stories.title: Starmer admits should never have named Mandelson as US envoy
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer admitted it was a mistake to appoint Peter Mandelson as the UK's envoy to the United States, citing connections to the Jeffrey Epstein scandal. The admission has deepened a political crisis and intensified calls for Starmer's resignation.

stories.title: Apple's veteran John Ternus named as new CEO
stories.summary: Apple announced that CEO Tim Cook will step down on September 1 after nearly 15 years, transitioning to the role of executive chairman. John Ternus, the company's hardware chief, will succeed him as CEO. Under Cook's leadership, Apple's market value grew by more than $3.6 trillion.

stories.title: Hidden office, fractured bone: violent resistance behind China’s record food safety fine
stories.summary: China's State Administration for Market Regulation imposed a record 3.6 billion yuan (US$528 million) fine on seven major e-commerce and food-delivery platforms operated by PDD Holdings, Meituan, JD.com, Alibaba, and ByteDance. Regulators uncovered a network of unlicensed "ghost" bakeries, along with evidence of a hidden office and violent resistance during the investigation.

stories.title: Ukraine struck Russian Samara oil terminal, which produces the Urals export grade of crude oil
stories.summary: Ukraine's SBU Alfa unit struck Russia's Samara oil terminal overnight on April 21, damaging five 20,000-cubic-meter crude oil tanks. The facility produces Russia's Urals export grade of crude oil.

stories.title: From super powder to super power: can Chinese plasma mill give it key tech edge over US?
stories.summary: A new facility in Guangdong province, described as the world's largest precision powder mill, was unveiled in China. The mill reportedly uses technology ten times more efficient than older methods to produce micron-scale "super powders" at industrial scale, materials critical for advanced military applications such as stealth jets and hypersonic missiles.

stories.title: Russia bombed the pipeline. Hungary blocked the loan. Ukraine is about to pay for both to unblock.
stories.summary: Russia bombed a pipeline while Hungary blocked a loan, leaving Ukraine facing the costs of resolving both issues. Kyiv's financing through 2027 depends on an oil deal, a veto lift, and a Brussels vote all occurring within the same week.

stories.title: Israeli minister's convoy hits and kills Palestinian boy in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: A vehicle in the security convoy of Israeli settlement minister Orit Strock struck and killed 16-year-old Palestinian Mohammad Majdi al-Jaabari near Hebron in the occupied West Bank on April 21, 2026. The teenager was riding his bicycle when the incident occurred on Route 60.

stories.title: Former Ura.ru editor sentenced to 5 years in prison for buying police reports from his uncle
stories.summary: A court in Yekaterinburg sentenced Denis Allayarov, a former editor at the Russian news agency Ura.ru, to five years in prison on bribery charges for purchasing police reports from his uncle. The independent outlet Mediazona reported the verdict.

stories.title: What was the Iran nuclear deal Trump dumped in search of ‘better’ terms?
stories.summary: The article examines the 2015 JCPOA nuclear agreement with Iran, from which President Trump withdrew the US in 2018, calling it "the worst deal ever" and seeking stronger terms.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 21 – The shekel’s remarkable strength
stories.summary: The Israeli shekel has shown strong performance against the US dollar. Times of Israel tech editor Sharon Wrobel discussed the currency's resilience along with recent disruptions in air travel.

stories.title: What course will Bulgaria’s new leader Rumen Radev take?
stories.summary: Rumen Radev, a former general and ex-president, won Bulgaria's latest election. He has pledged to combat corruption and pursue dialogue with Russia.

stories.title: 'Lame excuse': British papers not convinced by PM Starmer's Mandelson defence
stories.summary: British newspapers widely criticized Prime Minister Keir Starmer's defense before the House of Commons regarding the Peter Mandelson vetting scandal. Broadsheets and tabloids alike expressed skepticism about his explanations. Separately, former French Prime Minister Gabriel Attal faced questions about a potential conflict of interest.

stories.title: Mass trial for nearly 500 alleged gang members in El Salvador
stories.summary: Nearly 500 alleged gang members are facing a mass trial in El Salvador.

stories.title: Zhukov appointed advisor to head of National Police
stories.summary: Yevhenii Zhukov, former head of Ukraine's Patrol Police Department, has been appointed advisor to the head of the National Police of Ukraine.

stories.title: UN maritime agency urges help for seafarers stranded in Hormuz
stories.summary: The head of the International Maritime Organization appealed for assistance for approximately 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz since US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. The waterway normally carries about one-fifth of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.

stories.title: Iran crisis costs France up to 6 billion euros, says minister
stories.summary: France's government estimates the Iran crisis is costing the country between four and six billion euros due to energy price shocks and increased borrowing costs. Officials announced plans for targeted support measures and a spending freeze to manage the economic impact.

stories.title: Terrorists without finance means no more terror, lawyer for some Oct. 7 victims argues - interview
stories.summary: Attorney Gideon Fisher outlined an emerging legal strategy of targeting terrorist financing through civil litigation on behalf of October 7 massacre victims. The approach aims to cut off funding to terrorist organizations while providing a potential path for victim compensation.

stories.title: U.S. positive on Iran deal but talks still uncertain as ceasefire end nears
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is seeking an agreement with Iran to prevent further oil price spikes and stock market disruption, while insisting Iran cannot retain the means to develop nuclear weapons. Talks remain uncertain as the ceasefire deadline approaches.

stories.title: Sino Land-led consortium clinches Kam Sheung Road Phase Two with US$1.7 billion investment
stories.summary: A consortium led by Sino Land and Great Eagle Holdings, alongside China Overseas Land & Investment and China Merchants Land, won the tender for the Kam Sheung Road Station Phase Two development in Hong Kong. The group plans to invest more than HK$13 billion (US$1.7 billion) in residential projects.

stories.title: Hong Kong property investment soars on lower funding costs, rising demand
stories.summary: Hong Kong's commercial property market attracted US$1.6 billion in investment in the first quarter of 2025, a 41 per cent increase year-on-year, according to property consultancy JLL. Rising demand for office, retail, and hotel assets was driven by improving liquidity, with further inflows expected from global investors seeking alternatives amid the US-Israel-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Midtjylland footballer Alamara Djabi seriously injured after stabbing in Denmark
stories.summary: Midtjylland midfielder Alamara Djabi, 19, was stabbed and seriously injured over the weekend in Herning, Denmark, where the Danish Superliga club is based. The club confirmed the former Benfica academy product is in stable condition.

stories.title: EU announced funding shortfall for Ukraine in 2027
stories.summary: EU Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis announced that the €90 billion EU loan covers two-thirds of Ukraine's financial needs for 2026–2027. However, the remaining third of funding is secured only through 2026, leaving a gap for 2027.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: U.S. positive on Iran deal but talks still uncertain as ceasefire end nears
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned they would target any vessel attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without permission. The threat comes amid ongoing US-Iran tensions as a ceasefire deadline nears and negotiations over a potential deal remain uncertain.

stories.title: Exclusive: Inside Hezbollah’s battle for Bint Jbeil and Khiam
stories.summary: Hezbollah maintained control of the southern Lebanese towns of Bint Jbeil and Khiam despite weeks of Israeli bombardment and encirclement attempts. Sources close to Hezbollah said the towns' survival exposed the limits of Israeli firepower and highlighted the strategic advantage of the terrain for defenders.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria-South Africa Navies Deepen Ties On Maritime Security
stories.summary: The Nigerian and South African navies strengthened their maritime security partnership during inaugural Naval Staff Talks held at Naval Base Simon's Town in Cape Town, South Africa.

stories.title: Donald Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ held talks with DP World over Gaza reconstruction: report
stories.summary: A report indicates that Donald Trump's "Board of Peace" held discussions with Dubai-based DP World regarding the reconstruction of Gaza. Global institutions have estimated the rehabilitation cost at approximately $70 billion after two years of Israeli bombardment destroyed four-fifths of the territory's buildings.

stories.title: A legacy of love and service: Remembering Ariel Sosnov
stories.summary: The article pays tribute to Ariel Sosnov, whose partner was killed in combat. Sosnov's loved one continues a mission of service through a nonprofit organization dedicated to spreading kindness and hope.

stories.title: EU optimistic over approval of €90bn loan for Ukraine following Orbán defeat – Europe live
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas expressed optimism about approving a €90 billion loan for Ukraine following a shift in Hungary's government. German Foreign Minister Joseph Wadephul called the change in Budapest "a breath of fresh air" and urged Hungary to drop its blockade of Ukraine-related policies.

stories.title: Tim Cook to step down as Apple CEO after 15 years in the job
stories.summary: Apple announced that Tim Cook will step down as CEO in September after 15 years, with hardware engineering chief John Ternus named as his successor. Separately, a think tank report showed renewable energy exceeded one-third of global electricity generation in 2025 for the first time.

stories.title: Pakistan halts $1.5bn Sudan arms deal after Saudi objection
stories.summary: Pakistan has suspended a $1.5 billion arms deal with Sudan after Saudi Arabia withdrew its financing for the agreement. The decision came amid Saudi pressure and a shifting strategy regarding regional conflicts.

stories.title: Iran rejects US 'talks under threat' as ceasefire extended
stories.summary: Iran rejected what it called US "talks under threat" even as the ceasefire was extended. Prospects for diplomacy remain uncertain, with both sides balancing pressure and the risk of renewed escalation.

stories.title: Iran rejects US 'talks under threat' as ceasefire deadline nears
stories.summary: Iran has rejected what it characterizes as negotiations conducted under threat from the United States, with only one day remaining before a ceasefire between the two countries expires. Both sides face the risk of renewed military escalation if diplomacy fails.

stories.title: Israel's conduct in Lebanon totally unacceptable, says Belgium's foreign minister
stories.summary: Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot condemned Israel's conduct in Lebanon as "totally unacceptable" ahead of an EU foreign ministers' meeting in Luxembourg. Prevot called for condemning both Hezbollah's initial attacks and Israel's "disproportionate and indiscriminate response," and urged at least a partial suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement.

stories.title: Zelensky signs law on integration of Ukraine’s and EU’s energy markets
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a law on April 20 implementing European Union legislation to integrate Ukraine's and the EU's energy markets. The law had been adopted by parliament on April 7.

stories.title: Nigeria charges six people with treason for plan to overthrow president
stories.summary: Nigerian authorities charged six people, including a retired major general and a serving police inspector, with terrorism and treason over an alleged coup plot to overthrow President Bola Tinubu. All six defendants are in custody.

stories.title: Apple switches CEO: What it means for the iPhone maker
stories.summary: Apple announced that hardware engineer John Ternus will become CEO, succeeding Tim Cook. The leadership transition raises questions about the $4 trillion company's strategy on artificial intelligence.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel's Remembrance Day ceremony begins at Mt. Herzl
stories.summary: Israel's Remembrance Day ceremony was held at Mount Herzl in Jerusalem. Prime Minister Netanyahu honored fallen soldiers and victims, saying the pain of their loss never fades.

stories.title: ‘Immediate results’ versus ‘the long game’: Iran and the US face off
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are pursuing divergent negotiating strategies—Washington seeking immediate results and Tehran playing a longer game—ahead of expected talks this week.

stories.title: EU plans to provide Ukraine with the first tranche of a 90-billion-euro loan in late May or early June
stories.summary: EU Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said the first tranche of the €90 billion loan for Ukraine will be disbursed in late May or early June 2026. He indicated there are no technical delays in the preparation process.

stories.title: Victor Wembanyama unanimously named NBA Defensive Player of the Year
stories.summary: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama was unanimously named the NBA Defensive Player of the Year, receiving all 100 first-place votes. He became the first player to achieve a unanimous selection for the award since its inception in 1983.

stories.title: A history of Israel’s invasions of Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel has invaded Lebanon on multiple occasions since 1948. Most recently, Israel has declared plans to reoccupy large areas of southern Lebanon, continuing a decades-long pattern of military intervention in its northern neighbor.

stories.title: Ex-UK official says he felt pressure over Mandelson from PM’s office
stories.summary: A former senior UK Foreign Ministry official testified that he faced "constant pressure" from Prime Minister Keir Starmer's office to expedite the appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador to the United States. The controversy centers on Mandelson's known ties to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: First Thing: Vance to lead US delegation in Pakistan if Iran agrees to talks
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance is expected to travel to Islamabad to lead the American delegation if Iran agrees to further negotiations, as the current ceasefire deadline approaches. He would be accompanied by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

stories.title: UN working on Hormuz 'evacuation plan' amid US-Iran deadlock
stories.summary: International Maritime Organization chief Arsenio Dominguez announced that the UN is drafting an evacuation plan for hundreds of ships in the Strait of Hormuz amid the US-Iran standoff. The plan can only be carried out once conditions are deemed safe.

stories.title: How a U.S.-Iran deal over Hormuz unravelled
stories.summary: No substantive article content was provided beyond the headline referencing the unraveling of a US-Iran deal over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: South Korean police seek arrest warrant for Hybe founder Bang after travel request
stories.summary: Seoul Metropolitan Police requested an arrest warrant for Bang Si-hyuk, founder of K-pop entertainment company Hybe, through the Seoul Southern District Prosecutors' Office. Bang is accused of fraudulent stock trading in violation of South Korea's Capital Markets Act. Hybe is the company behind globally popular groups including BTS.

stories.title: Initial Iranian, US delegations landed in Islamabad, Pakistani source tells Arab outlets - report
stories.summary: Initial Iranian and US delegations reportedly arrived in Islamabad, Pakistan, for negotiations, according to a Pakistani source cited by Arab media outlets. However, Iranian state media denied the report, claiming no delegation had left Tehran as of Tuesday morning.

stories.title: Trump’s Federal Reserve chair pick to face lawmakers at key confirmation hearing – US politics live
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominee to chair the Federal Reserve, faces a Senate confirmation hearing. Warsh must clear the hearing to succeed Jerome Powell, whose term ends on May 15.

stories.title: The Shreveport shooting shows how Black women and children are at a higher risk of domestic violence
stories.summary: Eight children were shot and killed in Shreveport in the deadliest U.S. mass shooting in nearly two years. The gunman was the father of seven of the victims and the cousin of another; three additional people, including two mothers of his children, were injured.

stories.title: ‘We were terrified they were going to kill us’: fishers who survived US boat strike speak out
stories.summary: An Ecuadorian fishing crew aboard the vessel Don Maca described being struck by a U.S. vessel in the Pacific Ocean during what they say was a routine swordfish and albacore fishing operation. The crew members say the incident occurred as part of the Trump administration's campaign against alleged narcoterrorists.

stories.title: SCMP’s ‘original’ finance reporting honoured at State Street Institutional Press Awards
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post received six honours at the State Street Institutional Press Awards Asia-Pacific 2025, which recognized outstanding institutional finance reporting. Veteran journalist Enoch Yiu was given the Outstanding Contribution to Institutional Journalism Award. The competition drew a record 246 submissions from eight economies.

stories.title: China confronts Middle East supply shock, as State Council mulls energy strategy
stories.summary: China's State Council, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, convened a high-level session to review the country's energy security strategy amid a shipping crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. Beijing designated energy security as a pillar of national stability as disruptions threaten to become a long-term economic liability.

stories.title: Arrests in Nigeria after abduction of local monarch 'held for ransom'
stories.summary: Authorities in Nigeria made arrests following the abduction of a local monarch who was seized from his palace on Saturday. The kidnappers are believed to be holding him in a forest for ransom.

stories.title: Trump, GOP stockpile $1.2 billion in cash ahead of midterms
stories.summary: President Trump and the Republican Party have amassed $1.2 billion in campaign funds ahead of the midterm elections. The fundraising surge comes as polling suggests Trump's 2024 electoral coalition is weakening.

stories.title: Iraq-Syria border crossing reopens for first time in over a decade
stories.summary: The Rabia-Yarubiyah border crossing between Iraq and Syria reopened for the first time in over a decade. The crossing had been closed since the Syrian civil war began in 2011.

stories.title: Lebanon’s Christians support displaced amid ceasefire uncertainty
stories.summary: Lebanese Christian communities are providing support to people displaced by conflict as authorities work to extend the country's ceasefire. Many residents continue to face deep uncertainty about their security and future amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: Hezbollah to hold mass funerals for fighters killed in Israel's war on Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it would hold mass funerals in southern Lebanon for 44 of its fighters killed during Israel's six-week war on Lebanon. The burials follow a 10-day ceasefire announced by President Trump, though Hezbollah has not disclosed its total casualties.

stories.title: Middle East: Doubts grow over US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Iran's delegation had not yet departed for scheduled peace talks with the United States in Islamabad as of Tuesday, according to Iranian state television. U.S. Vice President JD Vance was reportedly en route to Pakistan, but Iran had not confirmed its attendance.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Charges Retired General, Others Over Alleged Failed Coup
stories.summary: Nigerian authorities have charged a retired general and others in connection with an alleged failed coup. The 13 charges include treason, terrorism, money laundering, and terrorism financing.

stories.title: New MONUSCO chief makes first field visit to eastern DRC
stories.summary: James Swan, the new UN Special Representative for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, began his first field visit to eastern DRC since assuming leadership of the MONUSCO peacekeeping mission.

stories.title: Malawi: Fuel Crisis Turns Critical - Malawi Runs Dry As Government Admits Empty Reserves and Cash Shortage
stories.summary: Malawi is experiencing a severe fuel crisis after government spokesperson Shadric Namalomba confirmed the country has completely exhausted its fuel reserves. The shortage is compounded by a cash shortage affecting resupply efforts.

stories.title: Nigeria: It's Unfair for Atiku to Call Jonathan an Inexperienced Leader - Onuesoke
stories.summary: Nigerian commentator Chief Sunny Onuesoke criticized former Vice President Atiku Abubakar for describing former President Goodluck Jonathan as an inexperienced leader, calling the characterization unfair.

stories.title: The counterterrorism czar without a counterterrorism plan
stories.summary: Renewed Iranian threats against U.S. targets have drawn attention to the fact that White House counterterrorism adviser Sebastian Gorka has yet to produce his long-promised counterterrorism doctrine. The absence of a formal plan has raised questions about the administration's preparedness.

stories.title: Afghans displaced by Pakistan conflict survive in tent camps
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Afghan civilians have been displaced by fighting along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and are now surviving in makeshift tent camps. The conflict has created a growing humanitarian crisis for the displaced population.

stories.title: Israeli strikes level homes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces fired artillery near Kunin in southern Lebanon's Bint Jbeil district despite an active ceasefire, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli forces also demolished homes and buildings across the south, reportedly booby-trapping residences in Beit Lif, Shamaa, Biyyada, and Naqoura before leveling them.

stories.title: Twelve people injured in Kharkiv region due to Russian strikes
stories.summary: Twelve people were injured in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine over a 24-hour period on April 20 as a result of Russian strikes.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Government Urges Nurses to End Strike As Talks Begin
stories.summary: The Zimbabwean government urged striking nurses to return to work as negotiations began over low wages and poor working conditions in public hospitals.

stories.title: Trump’s madman diplomacy isn’t working on Iran
stories.summary: CATO Institute analyst Benjamin Giltner argues that President Trump's application of "madman theory" diplomacy toward Iran is proving ineffective. Giltner contends that Trump's misapplication of the pressure strategy is compounding challenges in the U.S.-Iran standoff.

stories.title: Israel hindering Gaza aid access despite court ruling, says NGO
stories.summary: A non-governmental organization accused Israel of obstructing aid access to Gaza despite a court ruling mandating it. According to the NGO, Israel has continued to block the entry of humanitarian aid valued at millions of dollars.

stories.title: Is China a winner of the Iran war or facing economic risks?
stories.summary: China's economy has outperformed expectations despite disruptions from the Iran war. However, analysts note the country still faces weak domestic demand and structural economic risks that could undermine growth.

stories.title: EU’s top court finds Hungary’s anti-LGBTQ+ law in breach of key values
stories.summary: The European Court of Justice ruled that Hungary's 2021 anti-LGBTQ+ law, which bans content about LGBTQ+ people from schools and primetime television, is discriminatory and breaches fundamental EU democratic values. The ruling presents an early test for Hungary's incoming government.

stories.title: Senior RSF commander defects to Sudan army in major blow to paramilitaries
stories.summary: A senior Rapid Support Forces commander defected to the Sudanese army as the country's civil conflict enters its fourth year. The defection may signal emerging fractures within the paramilitary RSF.

stories.title: Popemobile child clinic yet to reach Gaza one year after Francis's death
stories.summary: A charity is still awaiting an entry permit to bring the late Pope Francis's converted popemobile into Gaza for use as a children's medical clinic. The initiative was one of Francis's final wishes before his death over a year ago, but Israeli restrictions have blocked its delivery.

stories.title: Amnesty highlights erosion of civil liberties in Pakistan
stories.summary: Amnesty International's annual report, released in London, warned that the world faces an unprecedented human rights crisis. The organization accused Pakistani authorities of weaponizing cybercrime and anti-terrorism laws to silence dissent and pulling advertisements from critical newspapers.

stories.title: Amnesty International warns of 'predatory world order' in grim rights report
stories.summary: Amnesty International released a report warning that the world faces a "perilous new era" characterized by states' "predatory" behavior driving an "anti-rights" international order.

stories.title: Iran war creating worst energy crisis ‘in history,’ says International Energy Agency
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency declared that the Iran war has created the worst energy crisis in history. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz combined with energy disruptions from the Ukraine war is driving up costs, including jet fuel prices affecting travelers.

stories.title: Hong Kong seeks to seize HK$56.5 million, 17 companies from jailed Jimmy Lai
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government applied to the High Court to confiscate HK$56.5 million (US$7.2 million) from jailed media entrepreneur Jimmy Lai's bank accounts and seize shares in his 17 companies. Lai was sentenced to 20 years in prison under the national security law for conspiracies related to foreign sanctions and inciting public hatred.

stories.title: UK police say 17-year-old boy charged over arson attack on London synagogue
stories.summary: UK police charged a 17-year-old boy in connection with an arson attack on a London synagogue. A 19-year-old was also arrested but not yet charged. The incident is part of a string of arson attacks targeting Jewish-linked sites in London.

stories.title: Japan approves scrapping a ban on lethal weapons exports in a change of its postwar pacifist policy
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's Cabinet approved new guidelines scrapping a longstanding ban on lethal weapons exports, marking a significant shift from Japan's postwar pacifist policy. The decision clears the final regulatory hurdles for Japan's arms sales abroad.

stories.title: Premium for mainland China shares erodes – or flips – as capital flows to Hong Kong
stories.summary: The valuation gap between mainland China-listed A shares and Hong Kong-listed H shares of dual-listed companies has narrowed significantly, with the Hang Seng AH Premium Index falling below 120 from a high of 157.89 in February 2024. The shift reflects global investors re-rating China's technology companies and increasing capital flows into Hong Kong.

stories.title: Two Arab citizens, including young mother, killed in separate shootings
stories.summary: Two Arab citizens of Israel were killed in separate shooting incidents. A 27-year-old woman was found with a gunshot wound in southern Israel, and her brother was detained. Hours later, a man was killed in Kafr Qasim in a suspected blood feud.

stories.title: One dead as Austrian trolleybus crashes into supermarket
stories.summary: One person, a 55-year-old local passer-by, was killed when a trolleybus crashed into a supermarket in Austria, according to a police statement.

stories.title: Hong Kong braces for 9-degree temperature drop, thunderstorms later this week
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Observatory forecast squally thunderstorms and a nine-degree Celsius temperature drop later in the week as a cold front approaches the South China coast. Temperatures are expected to fall to 21 degrees Celsius on Friday following a period of unseasonably hot weather.

stories.title: In Rostov region, drones attack railway facilities near military unit, halting train traffic
stories.summary: On the night of April 21, drones struck railway infrastructure in Russia's Rostov region near a military unit, halting train traffic in the area.

stories.title: Pakistan receives $1bn from Saudi Arabia as second tranche of $3bn deposit
stories.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan confirmed receipt of a $1 billion deposit from Saudi Arabia on April 20, 2026, constituting the second tranche of a $3 billion agreement. The first tranche of $2 billion was transferred the previous week, following Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's diplomatic visit to Riyadh.

stories.title: Japan loosens arms export rules in break from post-WW2 pacifism
stories.summary: Japan announced a major loosening of its arms export rules, breaking from its post-World War II pacifist policies. The changes clear the way for Japan to sell weapons to more than a dozen countries.

stories.title: Iran warns of immediate response as US ceasefire nears expiration
stories.summary: Iran warned of an immediate response as a two-week ceasefire with the United States nears its Wednesday expiration. Both countries have accused each other of violating the ceasefire terms.

stories.title: After 11 years, Hadar Goldin's  family marks Remembrance Day with closure
stories.summary: The family of Lt. Hadar Goldin marked Remembrance Day with a sense of closure for the first time after his remains were returned from Gaza following over 11 years. His sister spoke about the significance of the moment on Israeli radio.

stories.title: Clean electricity meets all new demand, curbing fossil fuels, says Ember
stories.summary: Energy think tank Ember reported that clean electricity generation met all new global power demand in 2025, beginning to curb reliance on coal and gas. Despite this milestone, Ember warned that global warming continues at a rapid pace.

stories.title: Germany's foreign minister urges Iran to take 'extended hand' of US and join talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged Iran to engage in constructive talks with the United States in Islamabad, Pakistan. He noted that US Vice President Vance was prepared to travel to Islamabad and called on Iran to accept the offer for the sake of its people.

stories.title: Ukrainian defense tech is in demand worldwide — German minister Pistorius
stories.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius stated at the Hannover Messe that Ukrainian defense technologies are in high demand worldwide. He urged partner nations to continue paying attention to Ukraine's defense-tech sector.

stories.title: Labor to tighten child NDIS eligibility to curb spending as Queensland MP warns change is ‘failing kids’
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government announced plans to tighten NDIS eligibility rules for children under 18 and introduce mandatory character checks for service providers to curb spending on the approximately $50 billion program. Health Minister Mark Butler faces backlash from state counterparts, including Queensland, over the changes.

stories.title: Kevin Warsh: Trump’s ideal choice to push Fed to cut interest rates
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, a former Wall Street banker and Federal Reserve governor, faces a Senate confirmation hearing for the role of Fed chair. His nomination is complicated by President Trump's unprecedented public attacks on the central bank's independence.

stories.title: ‘Uber for nurses’: gig-work apps lobby to deregulate healthcare, report finds
stories.summary: A report from the AI Now Institute found that billion-dollar tech platforms are lobbying U.S. states to deregulate gig-work nursing apps. The report warns that the growing use of AI staffing technology in healthcare comes at the expense of workers' rights, protections, and pay.

stories.title: China worker gains envy after winning 7-day ‘rain leave’; boss also offers cash subsidies
stories.summary: An employee at Changsha-based spicy snack company Mala Wangzi in Hunan province, southern China, won seven days of paid "rain leave" through a company raffle, allowing her to stay home when it rains. The unusual prize went viral online and sparked widespread envy among Chinese internet users.

stories.title: Air Defense forces shoot down 116 of 143 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 116 of 143 Russian drones launched against Ukraine since the evening of April 20.

stories.title: Lahore High Court grants bail to Falak Javed in Azma Bokhari video case
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court granted post-arrest bail to PTI social media activist Falak Javed and co-suspect Muhammad Shafiq in a case involving the alleged circulation of a fake video of Punjab Information Minister Azma Bukhari. Justice Shehram Sarwar Chaudhry set bail at surety bonds of one million rupees. The case was registered by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency.

stories.title: Hungary’s anti-LGBTQ law breaches EU rules as court ruling hailed as ‘historic’
stories.summary: The European Court of Justice ruled that Hungary's 2021 anti-LGBTQ legislation breached EU rules, including provisions on the bloc's fundamental values. The European Commission, 16 member states, and the European Parliament brought the case, which has been called the largest human rights case in EU history.

stories.title: US in talks with DP world on Gaza logistics under Trump’s Board of Peace plan - Financial Times
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported that the US is in talks with DP World regarding logistics operations in Gaza under Trump's Board of Peace plan. Gaza's reconstruction is estimated to cost around $70 billion after Israeli bombardment destroyed roughly four-fifths of the territory's buildings.

stories.title: EU pushes to limit carry-on bag fees
stories.summary: European lawmakers are considering rules that would require airlines to offer free cabin baggage on flights across the continent. Industry representatives have warned the measure could lead to higher overall costs for consumers.

stories.title: Apple's Tim Cook steps down: John Ternus names as new CEO
stories.summary: Tim Cook announced he will step down as Apple CEO effective September 1, ending a 15-year tenure marked by significant growth in profits and market value. John Ternus, Apple's head of hardware engineering, has been named as his successor.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon to hold news talks
stories.summary: The United States will host talks between Israel and Lebanon at the State Department in Washington on Thursday at the ambassadorial level. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated the goal is to end hostilities and Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon, though Hezbollah has rejected the negotiations.

stories.title: EU hosts Palestinian peace conference
stories.summary: More than 60 countries sent representatives to Brussels for an EU-hosted Palestinian peace conference focused on stability, security, and long-term peace. The EU's top diplomat said the bloc would assess member states' willingness to take individual measures against Israel, as Spain pushed to suspend the EU-Israel cooperation agreement.

stories.title: Civil groups file case against Mali over Wagner Group abuses
stories.summary: Three civil society groups filed a case before the African Union's human rights court on Monday alleging abuses in Mali committed by Malian armed forces and the Russian mercenary Wagner Group.

stories.title: Pakistan prepares for potential talks
stories.summary: Iran's delegation had not departed for scheduled peace talks with the United States in Islamabad as of Tuesday, according to Iranian state TV. U.S. Vice President JD Vance was reportedly heading to Pakistan, but Iran had not confirmed its participation in the negotiations.

stories.title: Doubt surrounds potential US-Iran talks
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire is set to expire on Wednesday, with uncertainty remaining over whether Iran will attend a new round of talks in Islamabad. Key issues including control of the Strait of Hormuz remain unresolved, and President Trump has renewed threats of military action if no agreement is reached.

stories.title: IEA: War on Iran is causing biggest energy crisis in history
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency has warned that the conflict involving Iran, the United States, and Israel has triggered the worst global energy crisis in history. Disruptions to oil and gas flows through the Strait of Hormuz are straining worldwide supply chains.

stories.title: Three people injured and educational institution destroyed in Sloviansk due to enemy FAB strikes
stories.summary: Russian airstrikes using guided aerial bombs struck Sloviansk in Ukraine's Donetsk region, destroying an educational institution and injuring three people.

stories.title: Suppose Iran didn’t exist
stories.summary: An opinion piece uses a hypothetical scenario of Iran's nonexistence to examine the geopolitical motivations of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump regarding Iran. The article references historical and cultural dimensions of Iran's significance. No specific new developments are reported.

stories.title: Spain, Slovenia, Ireland push EU to debate Israel pact suspension
stories.summary: Spain, Slovenia, and Ireland have jointly written to EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas urging a formal debate on suspending the EU's association agreement with Israel. The three governments cited alleged human rights violations by Israel.

stories.title: No time for allies
stories.summary: A commentary discusses Pakistan's role as mediator in the US-Iran peace talks hosted in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, noting that domestic affairs have been sidelined amid the high-stakes negotiations. The article highlights the tensions involved in facilitating dialogue between distrustful adversaries while the world faces the risk of broader war.

stories.title: Jurors set to hear opening statements in Harvey Weinstein’s rape retrial in New York
stories.summary: Opening statements began in Harvey Weinstein's rape retrial in New York. An accuser alleges the former film mogul forced himself on her in 2013 during what she describes as a previously consensual relationship. Weinstein is already imprisoned for a separate sexual assault conviction.

stories.title: Japan escapes worst of magnitude 7.7 quake but experts warn of potential bigger one
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of northeast Japan on Monday, causing limited damage. The Japan Meteorological Agency issued a special advisory warning of a slightly elevated risk of a magnitude 8 or stronger earthquake in the coming days, citing a 1 per cent chance of a megaquake.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ holds talks with DP World on Gaza
stories.summary: Trump's "Board of Peace" initiative held discussions with Dubai-based logistics firm DP World regarding aid supply chains and reconstruction projects in Gaza. The territory faces an estimated $70 billion rebuilding challenge.

stories.title: No Iranian delegation has departed for Pakistan yet, report says
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that no Iranian delegation had yet departed for Pakistan to participate in talks with the United States. State media dismissed reports suggesting otherwise, stating that neither a main nor subsidiary delegation had left for Islamabad.

stories.title: Execution law entrenches 'horrific Israeli racism' say activists
stories.summary: Activists have condemned a new Israeli execution law as entrenching racism against Palestinians. More than 9,500 Palestinian prisoners are currently held in Israeli prisons, including 86 women and 350 children.

stories.title: US ‘restricts intelligence sharing with South Korea’ after minister identified suspected nuclear site
stories.summary: The United States has reportedly restricted intelligence sharing with South Korea after Unification Minister Chung Dong-young publicly identified Kusong as a suspected North Korean uranium enrichment site. The facility had not previously been officially confirmed alongside the known nuclear sites at Yongbyon and Kangson.

stories.title: Car said to belong to minister’s security detail strikes and kills Palestinian teen
stories.summary: A vehicle belonging to an Israeli minister's security detail struck and killed 16-year-old Palestinian Mohammad Majdi al-Ja'abari near Hebron in the occupied West Bank. The teen was riding his bicycle when hit. Minister Ben Gvir's office said he was not at the scene and claimed the teenager entered the road at a red light.

stories.title: Burn treatment for Gaza children threatened by Israeli restrictions
stories.summary: Medical treatment for children with burn injuries in Gaza is under threat due to Israeli restrictions on the entry of supplies and personnel. The limitations are hampering healthcare access for injured minors in the besieged territory.

stories.title: Russian forces attack power facility in Chernihiv region; 54,000 customers without power
stories.summary: A Russian attack damaged a power facility in the Nizhyn district of Ukraine's Chernihiv region, leaving approximately 54,000 customers without electricity.

stories.title: Ben-Gurion, Epilogue - Sponsored Content
