stories.summary: Several Israel Defense Forces officers have been charged with embezzling millions of shekels while serving in classified IDF units. Authorities say the stolen funds and bribes were laundered using cryptocurrency.

stories.title: Kyiv shooting death toll rises to 7, mayor says
stories.summary: The death toll from a shooting in Kyiv rose to seven, according to the city's mayor. Seven additional people, including a child, remain hospitalized after being wounded in the attack.

stories.title: PSX plunges over 1,700 points amid Middle East tensions
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index fell by over 1,700 points, or 1 percent, on Monday amid uncertainty over the Middle East conflict and the status of U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Former Afghanistan cricketer Shapoor Zadran battles life-threatening disease
stories.summary: Former Afghanistan national cricket team pace bowler Shapoor Zadran is being treated at a hospital in India for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), a rare and life-threatening immune system disorder.

stories.title: Trump: Israel 'never talked me into a war with Iran'
stories.summary: President Trump insisted that Israel did not push him into war with Iran, citing the October 7 attacks and his longstanding belief that Iran must never possess nuclear weapons as the reasons for his decision.

stories.title: Biggest party in Romanian coalition set to demand PM's resignation, political crisis looms
stories.summary: Romania faces a potential political crisis as the largest party in the ruling coalition is set to demand Prime Minister Bolojan's resignation. The four-party pro-European coalition, formed 10 months ago to counter far-right gains, has repeatedly clashed over reform measures.

stories.title: Approximately 300,000 children missed during year’s 2nd nationwide polio campaign
stories.summary: Pakistan's second nationwide anti-polio campaign of the year fell short of its target by approximately 300,000 children. Over 44.7 million children out of a goal of more than 45 million were vaccinated, according to the National Emergency Operations Centre.

stories.title: Israel condemns soldier’s desecration of crucifix in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the foreign minister, and the military condemned the desecration of a crucifix by an Israeli soldier in the Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon. A photo showed the soldier using an axe to smash a sculpture of Jesus on the cross.

stories.title: Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Russian schools, universities, and kindergartens have spent billions of rubles on drones since start of full-scale war
stories.summary: According to Novaya Gazeta Europe, Russian schools, universities, and kindergartens have collectively spent 16 billion rubles on drones and drone training kits since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The spending reflects a broad integration of drone technology into Russia's educational system over four years.

stories.title: Israel army warns Lebanese against returning to south
stories.summary: The Israeli army warned Lebanese civilians against returning to southern Lebanon, citing Hezbollah activities in the area that it said violated the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills 80-year-old Palestinian academic and former hijacker in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in Tyre, southern Lebanon, killed 80-year-old Palestinian academic Maha Abu Khalil. She was an early member of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

stories.title: Russian forces attempting to open new front sector on Orikhiv axis – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Russian troops intensified assault operations near Shcherbaky and Pavlivka on the Orikhiv axis, according to Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn. The attacks aim to expand the front line and open a new sector in the area.

stories.title: Israel at a crossroads: Choosing between decline and a renewed vision for Israel - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion article argues that Israel faces critical decisions as inequality, emigration trends, and debates over national identity intensify. The piece frames the country as being at a crossroads between decline and a renewed national vision.

stories.title: Palestinians not welcome as Israel marks Memorial Day
stories.summary: Israel marked its annual Memorial Day for fallen soldiers, but critics noted that Palestinian casualties are excluded from the commemorations. Detractors argue the observance reinforces a one-sided narrative of sacrifice.

stories.title: Ukraine named three banks to lease equipment to defense industry at 5% annual rate
stories.summary: Ukraine designated three banks to lease equipment to its defense industry at a 5% annual interest rate. The financing mechanism aims to address practical constraints limiting the pace at which Ukraine can scale up domestic arms production.

stories.title: Russian Oil Is Too Big to Ignore, Kremlin Says
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov asserted that Russian oil remains too significant for global markets to ignore. He described Russia as a responsible and important player in global energy markets.

stories.title: Lebanon Latest: Israel establishes ‘yellow line’ in south
stories.summary: Israel has established a so-called 'yellow line' in southern Lebanon amid a fragile ceasefire with Hezbollah. Al Jazeera reported on the evolving situation along the border area.

stories.title: US military blockade redirected 27 vessels since blockade
stories.summary: US Central Command reported that the US military has redirected 27 vessels since imposing its blockade around the Strait of Hormuz, ordering them to turn around or return to Iranian ports.

stories.title: The battle for Bint Jbeil: Israel's war on south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces sought to take control of southern Lebanon and establish a buffer zone, with Bint Jbeil emerging as a key strategic and symbolic battlefield in the campaign.

stories.title: 'Hierarchy of sovereignty': Israel claims authority over 'which Lebanese areas are inhabitable'
stories.summary: Nadim Houry of the Arab Reform Initiative argued that Israel's "Yellow Line doctrine" in Lebanon, Gaza, and Syria functions as a military tool for territorial control rather than a legitimate security measure. He said the practice undermines ceasefire agreements and international law.

stories.title: Argentinian union talk with two Palestinian terrorists cancelled after police action
stories.summary: A planned event in Argentina featuring two Palestinian individuals released in a hostage deal was canceled after police intervention. Jewish organizations filed legal complaints that prompted authorities to act, stopping the appearance before it took place.

stories.title: Over 40% of European Jews experienced antisemitism last year, survey finds
stories.summary: A Jewish Agency survey found that over 40 percent of European Jews experienced antisemitism in the past year. Nearly half reported feeling unsafe in their countries, though European Jews expressed stronger connection to their Jewish communities compared to North American Jews.

stories.title: Iranian FM spokesman says ceasefire ‘violated’ by US in shipment seizure
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei accused the United States of violating the ceasefire by seizing an Iranian shipment. Tehran characterized the seizure as a breach of the truce terms.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP calls for Lebanese president to withdraw from Israel talks
stories.summary: Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah called on Lebanese President Aoun to withdraw from direct negotiations with Israel. Fadlallah said Hezbollah wants the ceasefire to continue and urged a return to national consensus on Lebanon's best path forward.

stories.title: Two arrested over attempted arson attack at synagogue in London
stories.summary: Two people were arrested in London in connection with an attempted arson attack on Kenton United Synagogue. The incident is the latest in a series of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites across the British capital in recent weeks.

stories.title: No movement of equipment or troop buildup near border in Belarus, SBGS spox says
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service reported no movement of military equipment or troop buildups near the border on Belarusian territory. The statement indicates no current signs of a threat from the Belarus direction.

stories.title: Polish FM says IDF soldiers ‘admit to war crimes,’ setting up clash with Sa’ar
stories.summary: Polish Foreign Minister accused IDF soldiers of admitting to war crimes, prompting Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar to call the claims "baseless" and indicative of "profound ignorance." The exchange set up a diplomatic clash between Warsaw and Jerusalem.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda's Energy Sector Commits to Raising 50,000 Female Engineers
stories.summary: Uganda's energy sector held a summit in Kampala on April 15, committing to a goal of raising 50,000 female engineers in the country.

stories.title: Malawi: Flood Disaster Spirals As Malawi Seeks K48.8 Billion to Avert Deepening Humanitarian Crisis
stories.summary: Malawi is seeking approximately $27.89 million (K48.84 billion) in emergency funding after devastating floods left tens of thousands homeless, destroyed farmlands, and crippled critical services.

stories.title: Israel restores West Bank settlement, as minister demands occupation of Gaza
stories.summary: The Israeli government restored a West Bank settlement and agreed to rebuild three settlements dismantled in 2005. Defence Minister Israel Katz and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich attended a ribbon-cutting ceremony, while a minister called for the occupation of Gaza.

stories.title: US Army wants doctrine for landing helicopters on Arctic ice
stories.summary: The US Army Corps of Engineers' research and development division is working to develop doctrine for landing helicopters on Arctic ice, seeking to challenge longstanding assumptions about the risks of operating on frozen lakes.

stories.title: Iran's foreign minister holds call with Pakistan ahead of new round of talks
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke by phone with Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar ahead of a fresh round of US-Iran talks. The call took place as Pakistan played a mediating role in the negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Iran’s President stresses importance of diplomacy while noting distrust of US
stories.summary: Iran's president emphasized the importance of diplomacy in reducing tensions with the United States while acknowledging deep distrust of Washington. He stated that every rational and diplomatic path should be pursued.

stories.title: Africa: How the Mideast Crisis Is Deepening Hunger Far Beyond the Front Lines
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warns that conflict spillover from the Middle East crisis is driving up food prices in parts of Asia and Africa, stressing the need to keep humanitarian supply chains open to prevent millions more from falling into food insecurity.

stories.title: Two arrested over attempted arson attack at synagogue in London
stories.summary: British police arrested two people in connection with an attempted arson attack on a synagogue in north London over the weekend. Counter-terrorism officers are investigating possible links between the incident and a series of recent attacks on Jewish targets potentially connected to Iran.

stories.title: ‘Israel never talked me into the war with Iran,’ Trump says
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Israel did not persuade him to go to war with Iran, characterizing the decision as his own. The remarks come as the war struggles to gain public support amid a growing energy crisis.

stories.title: Trump: Iran deal to be signed 'today,' as negotiators en route to Islamabad
stories.summary: President Trump announced that a deal with Iran would be signed "today" in Pakistan, saying Vice President JD Vance and the US negotiating team were en route to Islamabad. Trump reiterated that Iran giving up nuclear weapons capability was a non-negotiable demand.

stories.title: Kash Patel sues the Atlantic for $250m over article alleging misconduct – US politics live
stories.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit against The Atlantic and reporter Sarah Fitzpatrick over an article alleging misconduct. Patel's lawyers described the piece as a malicious and defamatory hit piece.

stories.title: Signs of panic in UK over Hormuz blockade, as govt summons banks
stories.summary: The UK government summoned banks amid growing panic over the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade has sparked fears of inflation across Europe and North America as trade disruptions continue.

stories.title: Pakistan, Egypt conclude 2-week long counter-terrorism exercise: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan and Egypt concluded a two-week joint counter-terrorism military exercise called Thunder-II at the Special Operations School in Cherat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The exercise focused on enhancing interoperability in counter-terrorism drills and techniques.

stories.title: Ukraine dismisses ‘encirclement’ claims: Russian troops held far from Sumy
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials dismissed Russian claims of encircling positions in the Sumy region, stating that Russian forces hold only settlements directly along the border. All attempts by Russian troops to push deeper into Ukrainian territory have been repelled.

stories.title: Australia signals greater defense investment, but is urgency still lacking?
stories.summary: Australia has signaled increased defense investment, but analysts say the pace of capability acquisition needs to accelerate. One analyst noted that while developments are positive, faster movement is needed to meet emerging security challenges.

stories.title: Bangladesh faces telecom shutdowns from West Asia fuel crisis
stories.summary: Bangladesh's telecom operators warned that continued operations, including data centres, cannot be sustained without fuel amid a supply crisis linked to disruptions in West Asia. The Association of Mobile Telecom Operators issued the alert about potential service shutdowns.

stories.title: Robot beats human half-marathon world record
stories.summary: A robot won a half-marathon race held in Beijing on April 19, finishing in 50 minutes and 26 seconds — nearly seven minutes faster than the human world record for the distance.

stories.title: 'When the killer cooks': Viral image shows Israeli soldier cooking in southern Lebanese home
stories.summary: A viral image showed an Israeli female soldier cooking inside a home in Bint Jbeil, in southern Lebanon's Nabatiye governorate. A Lebanese journalist described the photo as an "insult to people's memory and dignity."

stories.title: Prediction platform Polymarket in talks to raise funds at up to $15bn valuation
stories.summary: Online prediction platform Polymarket is in talks to raise $400 million at a valuation of up to $15 billion. The company has seen surging volumes from bets placed on Middle East conflict events, some of which raised insider-trading concerns.

stories.title: Liberia: Incumbency Power and the Shrinking Space for Dissent
stories.summary: Liberia, while praised for maintaining electoral continuity since its civil war, faces growing concerns over shrinking space for political dissent and the expanding use of incumbency power.

stories.title: Ukrainian partisans cut power to Russian GRAU arsenal supplying Kharkiv front
stories.summary: Ukrainian partisan forces reportedly severed power supply to a Russian GRAU arsenal that supports operations on the Kharkiv front. The action targeted logistics infrastructure sustaining Russian forces in the area.

stories.title: Scientists, authorities divided over fate of stranded whale in Baltic Sea
stories.summary: A humpback whale named Timmy has been stranded off Germany's Baltic coast since late March, sparking debate between rescuers and marine biologists. A privately funded rescue mission is underway, but scientists say the whale has no chance of survival.

stories.title: F/A-XX fighter downselect coming in August: CNO
stories.summary: US Chief of Naval Operations announced that the F/A-XX sixth-generation fighter contract competition will be narrowed to Northrop Grumman and Boeing, with a downselect decision expected in August.

stories.title: Russian regional authorities say Ukrainian drone strike on oil refinery caused petroleum spill off coast
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on the Tuapse oil refinery on April 16 caused a petroleum spill off the coast, according to Krasnodar Region authorities. The incident affected waters near the refinery in southern Russia.

stories.title: 40 Hong Kong tour groups safe after magnitude 7.5 quake strikes Japan
stories.summary: About 40 Hong Kong tour groups in Japan, including groups in the northeast and Hokkaido, were reported safe after a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck off Japan's northeast coast on Monday, triggering tsunami warnings.

stories.title: Iran’s targeting of our THAAD/TPY-2 radars is a ‘big freaking deal’
stories.summary: CSIS analyst Tom Karako warned that Iran's targeting of US THAAD and TPY-2 radar systems represents a serious operational concern. He emphasized that achieving operational success matters more than the cost per interceptor round.

stories.title: NDIS infiltrated by organised crime gangs using intimidation and threats of violence against Australians
stories.summary: Australia's Criminal Intelligence Commission warned parliament that organised crime gangs have infiltrated the National Disability Insurance Scheme, using the A$50 billion program to launder money and hide assets. A review recommended better data use and mandatory provider registration.

stories.title: Pakistan engages IFC for investors in installation of 10m smart meters across all Discos
stories.summary: Pakistan signed an agreement with the International Finance Corporation to advise on bringing private investors into a rollout of 10 million smart electricity meters across all distribution companies. The initiative was first announced by the Ministry of Energy in October 2025.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on Tuapse refinery, two Russian landing ships, oil depot
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on the Tuapse oil refinery, two Russian large landing ships, an oil depot, and ammunition storage facilities. The attacks represent renewed Ukrainian operations targeting Russian military and energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Ceasefire at risk after US seizes Iranian ship, Iran shuns peace talks
stories.summary: A US-Iran ceasefire appeared in jeopardy after the US seized an Iranian cargo ship that attempted to breach a naval blockade near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran vowed retaliation and refused to join new peace talks, accusing Washington of not being serious about diplomacy.

stories.title: Eight children killed in US domestic violence shooting
stories.summary: A man shot and killed eight children — seven of them his own — in Shreveport, Louisiana, in a domestic violence incident spanning three locations. Two women were also seriously injured. It was the deadliest US mass shooting in more than two years.

stories.title: Japan on high alert for 'huge' second quake after issuing tsunami warning
stories.summary: Japan's meteorological agency issued a tsunami warning after a significant earthquake and cautioned that another, stronger quake could strike within the next week.

stories.title: Russia tried to kill Ukraine’s most public Shahed analyst — with four superspeed jet-powered Shaheds
stories.summary: Russia attempted to kill a prominent Ukrainian analyst who publicly tracks Shahed drone operations, using four jet-powered Shahed variants. Reports indicate that approximately 20% of Russian Shahed drones are now manually piloted.

stories.title: Africa’s shifting security map: Ten years on, a continent under strain
stories.summary: Over the past decade, political violence across Africa has nearly doubled, driven by civil wars, jihadist attacks, local conflicts, and government crackdowns affecting millions of people.

stories.title: Hormuz traffic at standstill as US vessel seizure widens risk
stories.summary: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz came to a standstill after the US Navy seized an Iranian vessel following a brief reopening of the waterway. The seizure marked the first such action by US forces and widened the risk of further disruption to global maritime trade.

stories.title: Ugandan military reports rescue of some 200 hostages from ADF militants in eastern DRC
stories.summary: Ugandan and Congolese military forces jointly rescued approximately 200 hostages from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The operation targeted the Islamist militant group, which has been active in the region.

stories.title: Watch: Islamabad tightens security ahead of possible US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Islamabad authorities tightened security measures across the Pakistani capital ahead of a possible second round of direct talks between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: CNO denies reports of poor food service aboard Navy vessels
stories.summary: US Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle denied reports that sailors aboard Navy vessels stationed in the Middle East were experiencing food shortages or poor food service.

stories.title: Iranian support for US action hangs on Trump’s next moves, an Iranian expert warns - interview
stories.summary: Human rights activist Nazanin Afshin-Jam MacKay told The Jerusalem Post that Iranian public support for U.S. involvement depends on President Trump's next policy moves. She discussed the international community's potential role in challenging Iran's Islamic regime.

stories.title: Iran executes two men convicted of links to Israel’s spy agency
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of having links to Israel's intelligence agency, the Mossad. The men were also found guilty of "moharebeh," a capital offense under Iranian law meaning waging war against God.

stories.title: Unpacking the 2026 Venice Biennale controversies and highlights
stories.summary: The 2026 Venice Biennale has drawn controversy over Russia's return to the international contemporary art exhibition, as well as the continued participation of Israel and the United States, prompting politicized backlash.

stories.title: Kash Patel sues the Atlantic over bombshell story detailing allegations of misconduct
stories.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit in Washington, D.C., against The Atlantic over a story alleging excessive drinking and unexplained absences. The magazine has stood behind the reporting by national security journalist Sarah Fitzpatrick.

stories.title: Mediazona reports Israeli passengers held 5 hours at Moscow airport without food, water, or bathroom access
stories.summary: At least 40 passengers arriving on a flight from Tel Aviv were held by security officials for five hours at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport on April 19, according to the independent Russian outlet Mediazona. The Israeli and dual Israeli-Russian passport holders were denied food, water, and bathroom access during the detention.

stories.title: 45,000 homes damaged in Tehran from war, with some repaired
stories.summary: Authorities in Tehran reported that 45,000 housing units were damaged in the city due to the war. Officials said most units require only minor repairs, while residents who lost their homes would be provided alternatives.

stories.title: Anti-Western activist Kemi Seba seeks asylum in South Africa
stories.summary: Pan-African and pro-Russian activist Kemi Seba has applied for political asylum in South Africa, where he is currently detained for breaching immigration laws, according to his lawyer.

stories.title: Ethiopia: EU Resumes Budgetary Support to Ethiopian Government
stories.summary: The European Union has resumed budget support to Ethiopia with an initial allocation of 140 million euros, more than five years after cutting payments over human rights concerns during the northern Ethiopia war.

stories.title: Namibia: Police Allegedly Assault 31 Boys
stories.summary: Nine police officers in Otjiwarongo, Namibia, are alleged to have assaulted 31 boys from Karundu Secondary School in February, but no arrests have been made.

stories.title: How to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An analysis discusses the diplomatic and military frameworks needed, along with creative approaches, to reopen the Strait of Hormuz amid the current U.S.-Iran standoff.

stories.title: Ukrainian commander confirms new strike on Tuapse oil refinery
stories.summary: Commander Robert Brovdi of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces confirmed a new drone strike on an oil refinery in Tuapse, located in Russia's Krasnodar region. The facility had been targeted previously in recent days.

stories.title: Japan records 80cm tsunami after powerful 7.4-magnitude quake: JMA
stories.summary: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck off northern Japan's Iwate prefecture, triggering a tsunami warning. An 80-centimetre tsunami wave was recorded at Kuji port, and Japan's Meteorological Agency warned of waves up to three metres.

stories.title: Gambia: All Hands On Deck to Obtain National Identity Cards
stories.summary: In The Gambia, voter registration is set to end on May 31, but insufficient capacity to issue national identity cards is undermining the process, with some political parties reportedly establishing irregular attestation operations near registration centres.

stories.title: 'Anatomy of a Cry': Crystal Murray on teen fame and going indie
stories.summary: French-American musician Crystal Murray discussed her new EP "Anatomy of a Cry" and her transition to becoming an independent artist after moving to London. The interview also covered new releases by Massive Attack, Foo Fighters, and Fally Ipupa.

stories.title: Gulf diplomacy intensifies amid Iran-US ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Gulf states intensified diplomatic efforts to secure an Iran-US ceasefire and prevent further regional escalation. The diplomacy aimed to protect regional interests as talks between Washington and Tehran remained uncertain.

stories.title: Mother and six children killed in explosion and fire at Pennsylvania home
stories.summary: A mother and six children, aged three to eleven, were killed in an explosion and fire at a home in Lamar Township, Clinton County, Pennsylvania, on Sunday. Firefighters confirmed seven people were trapped but could not enter the engulfed building.

stories.title: US Navy wants helicopter sonar that can detect subs – and mines
stories.summary: The US Navy is exploring development of a dual-purpose helicopter sonar system capable of detecting both submarines and mines, replacing the current approach of using separate technologies for each mission.

stories.title: Outrage over Israeli soldier's vandalism of Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier vandalized a statue of Jesus in Lebanon, prompting the Israeli military to say it views the incident with "great severity." The US ambassador called for "swift" consequences against the soldier involved.

stories.title: Trump says he has ‘no problem’ meeting Iran’s leaders as future of peace talks in doubt
stories.summary: President Trump said he had "no problem" meeting Iran's leaders as his negotiating team, led by Vice President Vance, headed to Islamabad. Iran stated "no decision" had been made on sending a delegation, while Pakistan deployed 20,000 police for security.

stories.title: Africa: After COP30, What's Next for the Fossil Fuel Phaseout?
stories.summary: Following mixed results on a fossil fuel phaseout at COP30, attention is shifting to the Santa Marta conference hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, which aims to push governments toward concrete just-transition and tax reform plans.

stories.title: U.S., allied forces kick off combat drills with Philippines despite Washington's focus on Iran
stories.summary: The United States and the Philippines launched large-scale annual combat drills despite Washington's focus on tensions with Iran. This year's exercises have expanded to include forces from Japan, France, and Canada, all of which have signed visiting forces agreements with Manila.

stories.title: Israel’s Lebanon move raises doubts over gas, Hezbollah and  the 2022 maritime deal - analysis
stories.summary: Israel's establishment of a new buffer zone in southern Lebanon reflects its long-term security strategy focused on countering Hezbollah. Analysts say the move raises questions about the viability of the 2022 Israel-Lebanon maritime agreement and the future of offshore gas development in the area.

stories.title: Odesa City Council deputy Ivanytskyi found dead
stories.summary: Odesa city council deputy Oleksandr Ivanytskyi was found dead on the morning of April 20 in the city's Prymorskyi district. No further details about the circumstances of his death were immediately available.

stories.title: South Georgia/Falklands Stamps to honor 100th Anniversary of Queen Elizabeth II birth
stories.summary: The postal authorities of South Georgia, the Falkland Islands, and other British Overseas Territories will issue commemorative stamps on April 21, 2026, marking the centenary of Queen Elizabeth II's birth.

stories.title: Israel flattening civilian buildings in southern Lebanon during truce, say commanders
stories.summary: Israeli forces have continued systematically demolishing civilian buildings in southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire that began 10 days earlier, according to Israeli army commanders quoted by Haaretz.

stories.title: UK universities paid security firm to monitor pro-Palestine students and academics: Report
stories.summary: A joint investigation by Al Jazeera and Liberty Investigates found that 12 British universities paid security firm Horus Security, run by former military intelligence officials, approximately £440,000 since 2022 to monitor students and academics, including those expressing solidarity with Palestine.

stories.title: Destruction of Jesus statue should serve as moral wake-up call for IDF, Israel
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier's vandalism of a Jesus statue in Lebanon has drawn criticism and renewed calls for the IDF to address problematic conduct. Commentators argue the incident undermines Israel's claims of protecting Christians and minorities.

stories.title: Israel's history of destroying Christian, Muslim religious sites
stories.summary: The vandalism of a Jesus statue in Lebanon by an Israeli soldier renewed scrutiny over the destruction of Christian, Muslim, and other religious sites across Gaza, the West Bank, and southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Circus Tiger Jumps Into Crowd After Safety Barrier Collapses in Rostov-on-Don
stories.summary: A tiger leaped into the audience at a circus in Rostov-on-Don, Russia, after the safety barrier around the performance ring collapsed. Three tigers and two trainers were in the ring at the time of the incident.

stories.title: Ukrainian pork enters Vietnam, Philippines, and Singapore as EU loses Asian ground
stories.summary: Ukrainian pork exports have entered the markets of Vietnam, the Philippines, and Singapore, gaining ground as EU producers lose share in Asia. Domestically, carrot prices in Ukraine surged 13% in one week, highlighting infrastructure gaps in the agricultural sector.

stories.title: Over 3,300 people have died in Iran during war: Iran’s Forensic Chief
stories.summary: Iran's Forensic Medicine Organization chief reported that over 3,300 people have died in Iran during the ongoing war. Of the dead, 2,875 were male and 496 were female, with 383 being children aged 18 or under. No breakdown between civilian and security force casualties was provided.

stories.title: China’s Huawei debuts AI glasses to challenge Meta, Alibaba and Rokid in crowded arena
stories.summary: Huawei Technologies launched its first AI-enabled smart glasses, priced from 2,499 yuan ($367) and weighing 35.5 grams, entering competition with Meta, Alibaba, and Rokid in the growing smart eyewear market. The glasses are powered by Huawei's self-developed chip.

stories.title: ‘Hormuz moment’ could herald decline of US dominance: Citic Securities analysts
stories.summary: Citic Securities analysts suggest the US-Iran shipping standoff in the Strait of Hormuz could mark a turning point that accelerates America's strategic retreat and reshapes the global economic order, as Washington faces a dilemma over the critical waterway.

stories.title: Macron meets Tusk to discuss possible Polish role in French nuclear deterrence
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk met in Gdansk to discuss defence cooperation, including Poland's potential contribution to French nuclear deterrence. The talks come amid growing European security concerns over Russian threats and uncertainty about US NATO commitments.

stories.title: Thousands urge Israeli media to skip state Independence Day ceremony, air civilian alternative
stories.summary: Thousands of people have backed a campaign urging Israeli media outlets to skip the official state Independence Day ceremony and instead broadcast a civilian-organized alternative. The initiative was started by Yotam Kipnis, a resident of Kibbutz Be'eri who lost both parents and other relatives in the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Iran executes 2 over Israel spy links, opposition rejects claim
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad Masoum Shahi and Hamed Validi on charges including "enmity against God" and cooperation with hostile groups linked to Israel. Iranian opposition groups rejected the espionage claims against the two men.

stories.title: Philippines, US launch drills near Taiwan, test readiness under real-world conditions
stories.summary: The Philippines and the United States launched joint military exercises near Taiwan to test operational readiness under real-world conditions. Philippine armed forces chief Romeo Brawner said the drills aimed to reaffirm the bilateral alliance and their shared responsibility for regional security.

stories.title: Tiger walks into audience at Russian circus after safety net collapses
stories.summary: A tiger escaped into the audience during a circus performance in Rostov-on-Don, Russia, after a protective safety net around the ring collapsed. The incident occurred while three tigers and two trainers were in the performance ring.

stories.title: Around 20% of Shahed drones equipped with real-time control from Russia – defense minister's advisor
stories.summary: An adviser to Ukraine's defense minister reported that approximately 20% of Russian-deployed Shahed-type attack drones are now equipped with real-time control capabilities. These drones are operated via networks based on Russian territory.

stories.title: Cloud over US-Iran talks: What are the key sticking points?
stories.summary: President Trump announced a new round of talks with Iran as a fragile ceasefire brokered by Pakistan raised the stakes. Key sticking points between Washington and Tehran continue to cloud the prospects for a deal.

stories.title: Hong Kong watchdog warns of undeclared gluten in Marks and Spencer yoghurt
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Centre for Food Safety warned consumers with gluten allergies to avoid a Marks & Spencer vanilla Greek yoghurt product after undeclared gluten was found. The affected 500g batch, imported by Alf Retail Hong Kong Limited, has a use-by date of May 12.

stories.title: Russia arrests German woman in alleged bomb plot
stories.summary: Russian authorities arrested a German woman in southern Russia, alleging she carried a homemade bomb as part of a Ukrainian-directed plot to attack a security services facility. Russia has made numerous similar arrests throughout its war with Ukraine.

stories.title: Philippines, US and allies start military exercises testing 'real‑world' readiness
stories.summary: Philippine and US forces launched the annual Balikatan military exercises on April 20, including maritime strike drills on a Philippine island near Taiwan. The exercises, running through May 8, are the largest yet, with Australia, Canada, France, New Zealand, and Japan participating.

stories.title: NHIndustries inks contract for NH90 Block 2 study in support of future tech
stories.summary: NHIndustries signed a contract to conduct a Block 2 study for the NH90 helicopter, aimed at developing multiple upgrade options aligned with the operational requirements of NATO and participating nations.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks to raise its global standing in push for Middle East peace
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a mediator between Iran and the United States, working to facilitate a second round of peace talks in Islamabad. Islamabad hopes to boost its diplomatic standing and attract economic benefits from its peacemaking role.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Tuapse port kills one
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on Russia's Black Sea port of Tuapse started a fire and killed at least one person, Russian officials reported on Monday. The attack came only hours after a blaze from a similar strike on April 16 had been extinguished.

stories.title: IDF probes soldier over inciting patches on uniform, amid growing backlash
stories.summary: The IDF opened a probe into a soldier photographed in the West Bank wearing uniform patches with slogans calling for violence. The army reiterated its ban on non-military symbols amid growing backlash over troops wearing religious and political insignia.

stories.title: Mossad, Shin Bet, IDF announce joint bust of global Iranian terror network, including in Azerbaijan
stories.summary: Israel's Mossad, Shin Bet, and IDF jointly announced the dismantling of a global Iranian terror network with operations including in Azerbaijan. Top Iranian operatives from the IRGC Intelligence Unit 4000 who led the network were killed during the recent Israeli-US war against Iran.

stories.title: For Germany, the plot thickens toward a US-optional nuclear deterrent
stories.summary: Guest author Karl-Heinz Kamp argues that European discussions on nuclear deterrence independent of the United States must be expanded to include more European states. The debate centers on Germany's interest in a potential US-optional nuclear deterrent framework.

stories.title: Israel flattening civilian buildings in southern Lebanon during truce, say commanders
stories.summary: Israeli operatives told Haaretz that Israel is demolishing civilian buildings, including homes and schools, in southern Lebanon near the Litani River during the truce. Commanders described the strategy as modeled on the destruction carried out in Gaza.

stories.title: Zelensky to discuss return of Oschadbank funds with Hungary's PM-elect Magyar
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy announced plans to discuss the return of seized Oschadbank funds with Hungary's incoming prime minister, Peter Magyar. Hungarian authorities confiscated the funds from Ukrainian state bank cash-in-transit vehicles in early March.

stories.title: Space Force’s 15-year vision calls for more personnel, simulators and survivability
stories.summary: The US Space Force released a 15-year vision document addressing the future of space warfare, calling for increased personnel, more simulation capabilities, and enhanced survivability of space assets.

stories.title: Sri Lanka’s Tamil parties seek sustained Indian push to realise spirit of Indo-Lanka Accord
stories.summary: Sri Lanka's Tamil political parties have called on India to maintain sustained diplomatic pressure to implement the devolution provisions of the Indo-Lanka Accord. India's Vice-President reportedly assured Tamil leaders that India's position on devolution remains unchanged. Provincial council elections were also discussed with Sri Lankan officials.

stories.title: Israel army warns Lebanese against returning to south
stories.summary: Israel's military warned Lebanese civilians against returning to dozens of villages in southern Lebanon, citing alleged Hezbollah ceasefire violations. Thousands of displaced residents had already begun returning since a truce took effect on Friday.

stories.title: Iran-US ceasefire talks: Nuclear program remains sticking point
stories.summary: A senior Iranian source told Reuters that differences over Iran's nuclear program remain a key obstacle in US-Iran peace talks as a two-week ceasefire nears expiration. Tehran said its missile program and defensive capabilities are not open to negotiation.

stories.title: Bulgaria’s pro-Kremlin ex-president wins election, Russia and EU welcome victory
stories.summary: Pro-Russian former President Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party won Bulgaria's parliamentary election with 44.7 percent of the vote, potentially shifting the EU and NATO member closer to Moscow and ending years of political instability that produced eight elections in five years.

stories.title: Lebanese former minister: Israel has destroyed villages since ceasefire
stories.summary: Ali Hassan Khalil, a top aide to Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, said Israel had destroyed whole or parts of 39 villages in southern Lebanon since a ceasefire with Hezbollah was agreed. The former finance minister and Amal movement member called the actions "a clear war crime."

stories.title: Israel army says established 'Yellow Line' in Lebanon, as in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel's military announced it established a "Yellow Line" demarcation in southern Lebanon, similar to the one separating its forces from Hamas-controlled areas in Gaza. Israel also said it struck a militant cell operating near the line during a 10-day ceasefire with Lebanon.

stories.title: US seizes Iranian-flagged cargo ship
stories.summary: The United States seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship near the Strait of Hormuz after it attempted to breach a US naval blockade. Iran vowed retaliation, casting doubt on planned peace talks between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran-US: European stocks slide as oil jumps on Hormuz tensions
stories.summary: Oil prices surged and European stock markets fell amid escalating tensions over the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The market turmoil reflected growing concerns about the impact of the US-Iran conflict on global energy supplies.

stories.title: Qatar facing 'strategic shock' in energy, influence crisis in wake of Iran war
stories.summary: Qatar endured approximately 700 Iranian missile and drone strikes aimed at US military bases on its soil during the recent conflict with Iran. While no civilian deaths were reported, the attacks inflicted severe economic damage, creating what observers describe as a strategic shock to the Gulf state's energy sector and regional influence.

stories.title: Consider Beijing’s 10-point plan, Taiwan business leaders urge ruling DPP
stories.summary: Several Taiwan business leaders urged the ruling Democratic Progressive Party to consider Beijing's new 10-point plan for boosting cross-strait exchanges, arguing it could help struggling sectors. The DPP accused the business groups of helping China use commerce to exert political pressure.

stories.title: Bulgaria's Kremlin-friendly ex-president set for landslide election win
stories.summary: Pro-Russian former President Rumen Radev is projected to win Bulgaria's election by a wide margin, according to official results. The victory could end years of weak coalition governments in Sofia and sideline the country's long-dominant political forces.

stories.title: Nigerian wins global prize for trying to save bats in a country that shuns them
stories.summary: Nigerian ecologist Iroro Tanshi won a global prize for her efforts to conserve bat species in Nigeria, where many people associate bats with witchcraft. Her work challenges cultural stigma to protect the animals' ecological role.

stories.title: Tight security in Islamabad as US-Iran talks set to go ahead
stories.summary: Security forces locked down Islamabad as Pakistan prepared to host a new round of US-Iran negotiations. Tight security measures were implemented across the Pakistani capital ahead of the talks.

stories.title: Kyiv shooting death toll rises to 7, mayor says
stories.summary: A Kyiv resident wounded in the April 18 shooting in the Holosiivskyi district died in the hospital, bringing the confirmed death toll to seven, Mayor Vitali Klitschko announced.

stories.title: One killed, several injured as Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Zaporizhzhia, killing one person and injuring four others. No additional details about the type of weapon used were immediately provided.

stories.title: 'Situation is dire' for displaced people in Lebanon, journalist says
stories.summary: A senior journalist in Lebanon described dire conditions for displaced people returning home after the ceasefire, with thousands of homes destroyed and over a million displaced. Lebanese are closely watching US-Iran peace talks, as Tehran has used Lebanon as leverage in negotiations.

stories.title: In contested seas, autonomy has to think ahead, not just steer
stories.summary: A sponsored article discusses the growing importance of predictive autonomy software for unmanned maritime systems operating in contested environments, where missions extend farther from base and communications become less reliable.

stories.title: Gaza death toll rises
stories.summary: Medical sources in Gaza reported that the death toll from the Israeli offensive since October 7, 2023, has risen to 72,553, with 172,296 wounded. Since a ceasefire on October 11, an additional 777 people have been killed and 2,193 injured.

stories.title: As the Hormuz crisis exposes ‘fragile’ global supply chains, how will China respond?
stories.summary: China's National Development and Reform Commission head Zheng Shanjie outlined strategies to safeguard economic security amid Strait of Hormuz disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, warning of mounting external risks and the need to reinforce strategic reserves.

stories.title: Israel demolishes south Lebanon homes as talks to happen 'soon'
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued demolishing homes and structures across southern Lebanon's border area, destroying dozens of towns and villages in occupied territory. The demolitions proceeded even as talks were expected to take place "soon."

stories.title: India in ‘extremely high’ doping risk bracket: Athletics Integrity Unit
stories.summary: The Athletics Integrity Unit ranked India in the "extremely high" doping risk bracket, placing it among the top two countries for anti-doping rule violations in athletics between 2022 and 2025.

stories.title: Turkey to train 200 Nigerian special forces soldiers under new defence deal
stories.summary: Nigeria and Turkey have signed a defence agreement under which Turkey will train 200 Nigerian special forces soldiers to help combat Nigeria's 17-year jihadist insurgency.

stories.title: Mining China’s ‘Little Red Book’ for Open Source Gold
stories.summary: Bellingcat examines the difficulties of conducting open-source intelligence research within China, where major Western platforms like Facebook, Google, and YouTube are blocked. Chinese-owned social media platforms that remain accessible are strictly regulated and monitored in real time using artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Iran executes two men accused of involvement in ‘spy network linked to Israel’, judiciary news outlet reports
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad Masoum Shahi and Hamed Validi, accusing them of belonging to a spy network linked to Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. Authorities said the two had received training abroad, including in Iraq's Kurdistan region.

stories.title: War on Iran: Why Egypt cannot afford to take sides
stories.summary: Egypt is seeking to position itself as a mediator in the US-Iran conflict rather than taking sides. Cairo aims to present itself as an ally of Gulf Cooperation Council states while avoiding direct involvement in a war it cannot afford.

stories.title: War on Iran: Why Egypt cannot afford to take sides
stories.summary: Egypt is seeking to position itself as a mediator in the US-Israeli war on Iran rather than taking sides in the conflict. Analysts say Cairo cannot afford direct involvement and aims to present itself as a credible ally to Gulf Cooperation Council states.

stories.title: As IDF maintains hold on south Lebanon, residents of over 50 villages told to stay away
stories.summary: The IDF maintained its hold on southern Lebanon during a truce, telling residents of over 50 villages to stay away. Lebanese President Aoun said he chose to negotiate with Israel "to save" his country.

stories.title: Israel re-opens West Bank settlement evacuated 20 years ago
stories.summary: Israel reopened the Sa-Nur settlement in the occupied West Bank, which had been evacuated 20 years ago under the 2005 disengagement policy. Far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the re-establishment "cancels the shame" of the withdrawal.

stories.title: Ukrainian Navy on Black Sea oil spill: Russia using technical fleet without oversight
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Navy suggested that a major oil spill in the Black Sea near the Russian resort city of Anapa may have resulted from Russia's use of technically outdated vessels from its so-called shadow fleet, operating without proper oversight.

stories.title: What we know about the US capture of Iranian vessel near Hormuz
stories.summary: The US military released video showing the capture of an Iranian-flagged vessel near the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump said the ship attempted to breach the US naval blockade in the area.

stories.title: Can Saudi Arabia and Turkey reshape regional air power?
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran and Washington's inability to manage its spillover are pushing Saudi Arabia and Turkey toward deeper defense cooperation. The two regional powers are exploring joint efforts to reshape regional air power capabilities.

stories.title: State indicts Kafr Kassem man over alleged role in Gaza smuggling scheme
stories.summary: Israeli authorities indicted a man from Kafr Kassem for allegedly playing a central role in smuggling prohibited goods into Gaza. The prosecution says the scheme operated between August and December 2025 and generated significant financial proceeds.

stories.title: Carney says Canada’s strong economic ties to US are ‘weakness’ to be corrected
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a video address that Canada's heavy economic dependence on the United States has become a vulnerability. He outlined efforts to diversify trade by attracting new investment and pursuing deals with other countries.

stories.title: U.S. funding helps Cyprus upgrade military bases for its role as a regional safe haven
stories.summary: The United States European Command is funding a new heliport at Cyprus's Evangelos Florakis naval base, located about 142 miles from Lebanon's coast. The facility will accommodate large transport helicopters such as Chinooks for evacuating civilians from regional conflict zones.

stories.title: Vote rigging at Wang Fuk Court went unchecked before deadly fire, inquiry hears
stories.summary: A public inquiry into Hong Kong's deadly Wang Fuk Court fire heard that authorities and homeowner representatives took no proactive steps to address long-standing proxy vote rigging at the subsidised housing estate, which allegedly enabled certain committee members to maintain power.

stories.title: Why Spain’s outreach to China offers a viable model for Europe
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's fourth visit to Beijing in four years highlights Spain's sustained engagement with China, which some view as diverging from the EU's de-risking approach but may represent a broader shift in European strategy amid US-China rivalry.

stories.title: Sudan war fuels child hunger crisis
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war, now in its fourth year, has displaced millions and pushed parts of the country toward famine. Aid agencies warn that children are disproportionately affected as food shortages intensify and humanitarian funding declines.

stories.title: Sudan war enters fourth year as child hunger crisis deepens
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war has entered its fourth year, displacing millions and pushing parts of the country toward famine. Aid agencies warn that children are disproportionately affected as food shortages worsen and humanitarian funding declines.

stories.title: US Air Force wants better infrared jammers for its combat rescue helicopters
stories.summary: The US Air Force is seeking improved infrared countermeasure systems for its HH-60W combat rescue helicopters. Air Force Materiel Command noted the aircraft, recently used to rescue downed pilots in Iran, currently lacks adequate infrared jamming capability.

stories.title: Gaza's Deir al-Balah holds first elections in 20 years
stories.summary: The city of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza held its first elections in 20 years. While the city sustained less damage than other parts of the Gaza Strip during the war, it has still been significantly affected by the conflict.

stories.title: Sybiha hails Baltic states' decision to bar Fico's plane from flying to Moscow
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha thanked Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania for denying Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico permission to fly through their airspace en route to Moscow. The Baltic states blocked the transit in opposition to Fico's planned visit to Russia.

stories.title: Two terrorists killed, police constable martyred in Lakki Marwat
stories.summary: Two militants were killed and one police constable died in a gunfight during a targeted security operation in a forested area near Khundan in Lakki Marwat district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Police acted on intelligence that Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan fighters were hiding in the area.

stories.title: Iran says it has ‘no plans’ for negotiations with the US
stories.summary: Iran declared it has "no plans" to enter into negotiations with the United States, casting doubt on the prospect of diplomatic talks amid the ongoing conflict between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war live: Iran accuses U.S. of ceasefire breach, vows to 'soon respond' after U.S. destroyer hits cargo ship
stories.summary: Iran accused the United States of breaching ceasefire terms after a U.S. destroyer struck an Iranian cargo ship and announced it does not currently plan to attend scheduled Monday talks with Washington.

stories.title: Iraq’s ruling Shia bloc races to choose PM as US, Iran watch
stories.summary: Iranian Quds Force commander Ismail Qaani visited Baghdad at the request of Prime Minister al-Sudani as Iraq's ruling Shia parliamentary bloc faced internal divisions over selecting a new prime minister. Both the US and Iran are closely watching the process.

stories.title: Are insider traders making millions from the Iran war?
stories.summary: A BBC investigation found significant spikes in trading activity shortly before US President Trump made certain public announcements, raising concerns about possible insider trading linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 20 – ToI reports from new Lebanon ‘forward defense area’
stories.summary: The Times of Israel reported from a new Israeli "forward defense area" in southern Lebanon, describing a security zone being established on the northern border for the first time in 26 years. The report also covered IDF assessments of the Iran arena.

stories.title: After 'ceasefire, Iran's streets and strategy await next stage
stories.summary: In conversations across Tehran following the ceasefire, a prevailing sentiment has emerged that the outcome of Iran's conflict with the US and Israel should not be diminished through negotiations. Iranians are preparing for what they see as the next stage of the confrontation.

stories.title: US and Mexican officials assigned to cartel case killed in car accident
stories.summary: Two US officials and two Mexican officials were killed in a car accident in the northern Mexican state of Chihuahua on Sunday. The group was conducting an operation to destroy clandestine drug laboratories in the municipality of Morelos.

stories.title: Israel talks aim to end hostilities, occupation, Lebanese president says
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated that planned talks with Israel aim to end hostilities and the Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon. He appointed former ambassador to Washington Simon Karam to lead the Lebanese negotiating delegation.

stories.title: Is Vietnam becoming more like China?
stories.summary: Vietnam's lawmakers unanimously elected Communist Party chief To Lam as the country's president. Analysts are debating whether Vietnam is moving toward a political model resembling that of Chinese President Xi Jinping's consolidated leadership.

stories.title: Is To Lam's Vietnam turning into Xi Jinping's China?
stories.summary: Vietnam's National Assembly unanimously elected Communist Party chief To Lam as president, consolidating his power over both the party and the state. Analysts are debating whether Vietnam is moving toward a political model resembling China's centralized system under Xi Jinping.

stories.title: 'US military leverage a risky tactic': Bombs, military escalation will not bring Iran 'to the table'
stories.summary: Former US Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense Jim Townsend argued that military escalation alone will not bring Iran to the negotiating table. He said meaningful progress in US-Iran talks depends on mediation, incremental trust-building, and extending fragile ceasefires.

stories.title: FSB Arrests German Woman in Alleged Ukrainian Bomb Plot
stories.summary: Russia's FSB announced the arrest of a German woman accused of plotting a bomb attack on a law enforcement facility. The agency claimed she was recruited by a Central Asian national allegedly working for Ukrainian security services.

stories.title: Billion-dollar tariff refund process kicks off in US
stories.summary: US businesses began applying for tariff refunds after the Supreme Court ruled that President Trump had exceeded his authority in imposing them. Meanwhile, oil prices surged after Iran threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting supply chains.

stories.title: Woman arrested in US for trafficking arms to Sudan for Iran
stories.summary: Shamim Mafi, a resident of Woodland Hills in the Los Angeles area, was arrested in the United States on charges of trafficking arms to Sudan on behalf of Iran.

stories.title: China threatens EU firms over cybersecurity plans targeting Chinese companies
stories.summary: China's commerce ministry warned the European Commission in a 30-page document that it would impose reciprocal measures against EU firms if proposed cybersecurity regulations penalize Chinese companies such as Huawei and ZTE.

stories.title: EXCLUSIVE: Hanwha, Magnet Defense partner to build MUSVs, robotic shipyards
stories.summary: Hanwha and Magnet Defense are signing a Memorandum of Understanding to collaborate on building a 38-meter medium uncrewed surface vessel (MUSV) and developing robotic shipyard capabilities.

stories.title: Los Angeles woman arrested on Iranian arms trafficking charge
stories.summary: U.S. authorities arrested Los Angeles resident Shamim Mafi on charges of brokering arms sales between Iran and the Sudanese Armed Forces. The alleged transactions included drones, bombs, bomb fuses, and millions of rounds of ammunition.

stories.title: Pope Leo criticises exploitation by world’s ‘authoritarians’ during Angola trip
stories.summary: Pope Leo, the first American pope, criticized global authoritarians and the exploitation of people by the wealthy during a Mass in Saurimo, Angola, near the Democratic Republic of Congo border. The remarks are part of a forceful speaking style adopted during his four-nation Africa tour, which has drawn criticism from US President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Oil depot in Sevastopol on fire for third day in Kozacha Bay area – social media
stories.summary: An oil depot in the Kozacha Bay area of Russian-occupied Sevastopol continued burning for a third consecutive day after being struck by drones on the night of April 18. Reports of the ongoing fire circulated on social media.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: UN Welcomes Progress On Talks Between DR Congo, M23 Armed Group
stories.summary: MONUSCO, the UN peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo, welcomed progress after Kinshasa and M23 rebels agreed during talks in Switzerland to ease humanitarian aid deliveries and release prisoners within 10 days.

stories.title: Watch: ‘Stop this war and rein in Netanyahu’: Spanish Prime Minister
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister called for an end to the war and urged the international community to rein in Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

stories.title: Nigeria: APGA Bans Sharing of Cash, Items During Primaries
stories.summary: Nigeria's All Progressives Grand Alliance banned the sharing of cash and items during party primaries. Officials were also prohibited from wearing campaign materials or accepting gifts from aspirants.

stories.title: Somalia: Turkey Pledges Direct Support to Somalia in Fight Against Militant Groups
stories.summary: Turkey formally announced for the first time that it will directly support Somalia's fight against armed groups, particularly Al-Shabaab and ISIS. The pledge was made by Turkish officials in Ankara.

stories.title: Botswana: Boko Rallies Party Around Faith and Unity
stories.summary: Botswana's National Front celebrated its 60th anniversary at a gala dinner in Gaborone. Party president and national President Duma Boko delivered an address focused on unity, economic reform, and the country's future.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Police Destroy Al-Shabaab Extortion Checkpoint in Lower Shabelle Operation
stories.summary: Somalia's police counter-terrorism command conducted an operation in the Lower Shabelle region, destroying an Al-Shabaab extortion checkpoint. A local militant leader was killed during the planned raid.

stories.title: Malawi: UN Report Exposes Deep-Rooted Corruption Rot Undermining Malawi's Governance
stories.summary: A United Nations assessment has exposed deep-rooted corruption, procurement scandals, and political interference undermining governance in Malawi. The report warned that selective accountability is steadily weakening the country's institutions.

stories.title: Africa: Africa's Job Crisis Deepens As Growth Lags Behind Exploding Population, World Bank Warns
stories.summary: The World Bank warned that economic growth across Africa is not keeping pace with rapid population expansion. The organization highlighted that millions of young people entering the workforce each year face a deepening jobs crisis.

stories.title: India's 'wells of death': Gravity-defying stuntmen become social media phenomenon
stories.summary: Stunt performers in India race cars and motorbikes at high speed along the vertical walls of cylindrical arenas known as "wells of death." The gravity-defying shows attract large crowds of young Indians and have become a viral social media phenomenon.

stories.title: UN survey says economic growth momentum weakening in Asia-Pacific developing countries
stories.summary: A United Nations report found that economic growth in Asia-Pacific developing countries slowed to 4.6 percent in 2025 and is projected to decline further to 4 percent in 2026. The slowdown is attributed to disruptions from the Middle East conflict affecting energy prices and supply chains.

stories.title: China's Xi urges normal passage in Strait of Hormuz in call with Saudi crown prince
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged that normal traffic through the Strait of Hormuz be maintained during a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Xi also called for an immediate and comprehensive ceasefire in the region.

stories.title: EU praises ‘extremely constructive’ early talks with incoming Hungarian government – Europe live
stories.summary: The European Commission praised early discussions with Hungary's incoming government led by Péter Magyar as "extremely constructive," describing them as a good start toward unblocking funds for the Hungarian people.

stories.title: Amy Winehouse’s father Mitch loses high court battle against her friends
stories.summary: Mitch Winehouse, father of the late singer Amy Winehouse, lost a high court claim against two of his daughter's friends over the auctioning of items once owned by the singer. The judge threw out the case against stylist Naomi Parry and friend Catriona Gourlay.

stories.title: Israeli officials attend Sa-nur settlement reestablishment ceremony
stories.summary: Israeli officials attended a ceremony marking the reestablishment of the Sa-Nur settlement in the West Bank. Samaria Regional Council Chairman Yossi Dagan, who was evacuated from Sa-Nur during Israel's 2005 disengagement, was among 16 families who moved into the settlement on Sunday.

stories.title: Russian drone hits home of Defense Ministry adviser 'Flash'
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Ministry adviser Serhii Beskrestnov, known by the call sign "Flash," reported that Russian forces targeted his home with a jet-powered drone in what he described as an assassination attempt.

stories.title: Starmer expected to lead Labour into next election, says minister, but warns there are ‘no certainties’ amid Mandelson scandal – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced parliamentary pressure over the appointment of Peter Mandelson as Britain's ambassador to Washington. Reports indicated Mandelson failed security vetting checks, and questions arose over whether Starmer was informed of the concerns before the appointment.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack on Tuapse Port Kills 1
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on the Tuapse oil port in southern Russia killed one person. The attack marked the second strike to damage the strategic oil export facility in less than a week.

stories.title: U.S. security agency is using Anthropic's Mythos despite blacklist: Report
stories.summary: A U.S. security agency is reportedly using Anthropic's Mythos AI system despite the company being on a blacklist. Anthropic, the NSA, and the Department of Defense have not commented on the report.

stories.title: Terrorist involved in February suicide attack among two killed in Bannu IBO: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed two militants, including one linked to a February suicide attack, during an intelligence-based operation in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The military's ISPR said the operation targeted members of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

stories.title: Russia’s FSB says it thwarted a bomb attack on a law enforcement facility, detaining a German woman it says was acting on orders from Ukrainian intelligence
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service said it prevented a planned bomb attack on a law enforcement facility in Stavropol Krai. The FSB detained a German woman born in 1969 whom it accused of acting on orders from Ukrainian intelligence.

stories.title: South Korea-US tensions flare over ‘intelligence leak’ claims, Pyongyang policy
stories.summary: Tensions between South Korea and the United States emerged after Unification Minister Chung Dong-young publicly identified a suspected North Korean uranium-enrichment site at Kusong. Washington viewed the remark as a disclosure of sensitive intelligence and reportedly reduced intelligence-sharing with Seoul in response.

stories.title: Senior UAE scholar says US bases are 'a burden and not a strategic asset'
stories.summary: Prominent Emirati academic Abdulkhaleq Abdulla, who has ties to UAE leadership, called for closing US military bases in the country. He argued the bases are "a burden and not a strategic asset," saying the UAE has demonstrated it can defend itself.

stories.title: Oil prices rise and markets fall after US seizure of ship hits Iran peace deal hopes
stories.summary: Oil prices rose sharply, with Brent crude climbing 4.8 percent to $94.69 per barrel, while European stock markets fell after the US seizure of an Iranian vessel undermined hopes for a peace deal. Fears mounted that the Strait of Hormuz could remain closed for an extended period, pushing UK gas prices higher.

stories.title: Iranian woman arrested in US for allegedly trafficking arms to Sudan
stories.summary: U.S. authorities arrested Iranian national Shamim Mafi on charges of brokering arms sales to Sudan's defence ministry on behalf of Iran. The case involves alleged trafficking of weapons in violation of international arms restrictions.

stories.title: Japan tsunami alert issued following powerful earthquake off northern coast – follow latest
stories.summary: A magnitude-7.5 earthquake struck off Japan's Sanriku Coast, prompting tsunami warnings and evacuation orders for affected areas on Honshu. Australian officials in Japan are urgently monitoring the situation and stand ready to provide consular assistance to Australian citizens.

stories.title: Russia’s 20% windfall tax breaks Putin’s promise—again
stories.summary: Russia imposed a 20% windfall tax on major corporations despite earlier assurances against such measures. The decision came as oil prices reached a four-year high, with Moscow opting for compulsory taxation over voluntary oligarch donations.

stories.title: Electric car sales soar 51% in mainland Europe as Iran war drives up fuel prices
stories.summary: Electric vehicle sales in continental Europe surged 51 percent in March, with 224,000 new EVs registered, driven partly by rising petrol and diesel costs linked to the Iran war. Over the first quarter, 500,000 EVs were registered, a 33.5 percent increase year on year, according to New AutoMotive and E-Mobility Europe data.

stories.title: Russia claims Ukraine-linked bomb plot foiled, German woman arrested
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) announced it had arrested a German woman found carrying a bomb in her backpack. The FSB alleged she was involved in a plot orchestrated by Ukraine.

stories.title: Two more Israelis charged in Iran spy case amid expanding online recruitment drive
stories.summary: Two additional Israeli citizens have been charged in connection with an espionage case linked to Iranian intelligence. Authorities say Iranian handlers have been using social media and messaging platforms to recruit Israeli nationals in an expanding online campaign.

stories.title: Russian governor fires regional agriculture minister over livestock disease outbreak and other complaints
stories.summary: Novosibirsk Governor Andrei Travnikov dismissed regional agriculture minister Andrei Shindelov following a livestock disease outbreak and other complaints. The dismissal was announced by the regional government's press service.

stories.title: A match made in opposition: Venezuela’s Machado courts Spain’s right wing
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has been building ties with right-wing political figures in Spain. Analysts note that while the political rivals of Venezuelan President Maduro and Spanish PM Sánchez share economic policy positions, they diverge on social issues.

stories.title: Iran talks in doubt as Tehran vows to boycott Islamabad meeting
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister ruled out attending a second round of negotiations with the United States in Islamabad, casting doubt on the diplomatic process. Washington had already sent a delegation to the Pakistani capital for the planned talks.

stories.title: ‘I never knew my father’: Avichai Ayubi on loss, Israel’s orphaned generation, and moving forward
stories.summary: Avichai Ayubi spoke about growing up without his father, who died five months before Avichai was born. His story highlights the experiences of Israel's orphaned generation and the lasting impact of loss on families of fallen soldiers.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Donetsk region more than 1,200 times in one day
stories.summary: Russian troops carried out 1,222 attacks on Ukraine's Donetsk region in a single day, damaging 14 civilian structures. Preliminary reports indicated no casualties from the barrage.

stories.title: What is real?  Iran’s conflicting messages & Trump’s confusing stance
stories.summary: Analyst Shir Perets examined the contradictory signals emerging from Iran and the United States regarding ongoing Middle East tensions. The discussion focused on conflicting reports about the status of US-Iran engagement and broader regional dynamics.

stories.title: Quarter of a million people could lose job by middle of 2027 as UK ‘flirts with recession’, analysis says
stories.summary: Analysis from leading accounting firms warns that approximately 250,000 people in the UK could lose their jobs by mid-2027 as Britain "flirts with recession." Business confidence has been shattered by the economic fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran, prompting Chancellor Rachel Reeves to summon bank chiefs for crisis talks.

stories.title: Mainland Chinese to make 980,000 inbound trips to Hong Kong for Labour Day break
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Immigration Department estimates that mainland Chinese visitors will make approximately 980,000 inbound trips during the Labour Day holiday, a 7 percent increase from the previous year. Authorities have stepped up crowd control, transport, and tourism measures, and plan to enforce environmental regulations around the clock at popular camping sites.

stories.title: Despite cost of living hikes, Israelis are eating more beef, veal
stories.summary: Israel's Agriculture Ministry reported that annual per capita consumption of bovine meat reached 20.2 kilograms last year, a 7 percent increase from the previous year. The rise came despite ongoing cost-of-living pressures, with purchases expected to spike further around Independence Day.

stories.title: Mozambique looks to China for industrial boost
stories.summary: Mozambican President Daniel Chapo is visiting China on his first state visit since taking office in 2025. He is touring key industrial hubs as Mozambique seeks Chinese manufacturing support to accelerate infrastructure development.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russian port, killing 1 and setting oil refinery on fire
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Russian port city of Tuapse overnight on April 20, killing one person and injuring another, according to Krasnodar Krai Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. A fire erupted at the seaport and transport infrastructure was damaged.

stories.title: Kremlin says it hopes Iran talks continue for the good of the Gulf and global economy
stories.summary: The Kremlin expressed hope that negotiations involving Iran would continue to avoid further escalation and negative consequences for the Gulf region and global economy. Moscow said it is not acting as a mediator but stands ready to assist if needed.

stories.title: US urges contractor to evacuate workers from Kuwait and Iraq over worries of Iran-backed attacks
stories.summary: The US State Department urged defense contractor V2X to evacuate its employees from Kuwait and Iraq, warning they could be targeted by Iran-backed militias. V2X personnel were stationed at US military bases in Kuwait and at facilities in Iraq including Erbil.

stories.title: ByteDance profit plunges on AI push as TikTok Shop powers overseas growth: reports
stories.summary: ByteDance, TikTok's parent company, reported a more than 70 percent drop in net profit in 2025 due to heavy investment in artificial intelligence, according to Chinese media. Overseas revenue surged nearly 50 percent, driven partly by TikTok Shop, significantly outpacing roughly 20 percent revenue growth in China.

stories.title: Death toll from attack in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district rises to seven – Klitschko
stories.summary: The death toll from the April 18 shooting in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district rose to seven after another wounded victim died in the hospital, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

stories.title: Russian blogger posts AI video of herself as Spider-Man fighting pro-Kremlin TV host and officials
stories.summary: Russian blogger Viktoria Bonya posted an AI-generated video on Instagram depicting herself as Spider-Man fighting pro-Kremlin TV host Vladimir Solovyov, blogger Artemy Lebedev, and State Duma deputy Vitaly Milonov.

stories.title: Ghana: No Premature Declarations or Campaigns - - NDC Tells Aspirants
stories.summary: Ghana's National Democratic Congress warned party members against prematurely declaring their candidacies for upcoming internal elections. The party said such actions could lead to disqualification from the contests.

stories.title: Philippine army kills at least 10 Maoist rebels during battles on Negros
stories.summary: Philippine Army forces killed at least 10 New People's Army Maoist guerrillas in gun battles near Toboso on Negros island in the central Philippines. Army spokesman Colonel Louie Dema-ala said the toll could be as high as 19. The clashes targeted remnants of the NPA as part of the decades-old counterinsurgency campaign.

stories.title: Iran ‘is our war,’ says UK lawmaker Greg Smith — contrary to PM Starmer’s claims
stories.summary: UK Conservative lawmaker Greg Smith, the new head of the Conservative Friends of Israel, declared the Iran conflict is Britain's war, contradicting Prime Minister Keir Starmer's position. He criticized the Labour government's handling of the US-Israel conflict with Iran amid rising antisemitism in Britain.

stories.title: Israel under fire over appointment of ambassador to Somaliland
stories.summary: More than a dozen countries have condemned Israel's appointment of a diplomatic envoy to Somaliland, the breakaway region of Somalia. Critics warn the move could destabilize the Horn of Africa.

stories.title: The 3.00 squeeze: Why the surging shekel is a threat to Israel’s economy
stories.summary: The Israeli shekel has strengthened significantly against the US dollar, approaching the 3.00 exchange rate. Exporters are struggling with rising costs, and analysts warn Israel's economic competitiveness faces immediate risk without government intervention.

stories.title: Radical settler group to stage march by Gaza border to ‘renew Jewish hold on Gaza Strip’
stories.summary: The radical Israeli settler group Nachala announced plans to march near the Gaza border to promote Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip. The event has received support from a Likud member of Knesset who asserted a right to settle throughout the Land of Israel including Gaza.

stories.title: Pakistan’s military chief takes lead on US-Iran talks in diplomatic blitz
