stories.summary: Pakistan's military chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, played a leading role in mediating between the United States and Iran during talks held on April 11. Munir was one of two Pakistani mediators involved in the diplomatic effort.

stories.title: EU highlights backing for Palestinians amid Iran War
stories.summary: European Union officials publicly reaffirmed support for the Palestinian Authority and the two-state solution as the US-Israeli war with Iran diverted international attention from Gaza. Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot emphasized the need to maintain diplomatic focus on Palestinian statehood.

stories.title: Iran vows retaliation for 'maritime piracy' after US seizes ship
stories.summary: Iran threatened retaliation after accusing the United States of seizing an Iranian cargo ship, calling the action "maritime piracy." Tehran said the seizure breached the ceasefire agreement, further escalating tensions in Gulf waters.

stories.title: Russia kills teenager in drone strike on Chernihiv, injuring 4 others
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted a large-scale drone strike on the Ukrainian city of Chernihiv overnight on April 19, killing a teenager and injuring four others. The attack was reported by Chernihiv regional administration head Vyacheslav Chaus.

stories.title: ‘Technofascism’: Critics accuse Palantir of pushing AI war doctrine
stories.summary: Critics have labeled Palantir Technologies' approach as "technofascism" following the publication of CEO Alexander Karp's book, The Technological Republic. The book advocates for Western hard power built on software and advances an AI-driven military doctrine.

stories.title: Ukraine’s interior minister orders probe into police who fled during Kyiv shooting
stories.summary: Ukraine's Internal Affairs Minister Ihor Klymenko ordered an internal investigation into the conduct of police officers during the April 18 shooting attack in Kyiv that killed multiple people. The probe focuses on officers who reportedly fled the scene.

stories.title: Drones attack Sevastopol, air defense systems were active near Belbek airfield – media
stories.summary: Air defense systems were activated near the Belbek airfield in Russian-occupied Sevastopol during an evening drone attack. Residents reported hearing machine-gun fire and anti-aircraft artillery explosions across multiple districts.

stories.title: Little faith in south Lebanon that ceasefire will last
stories.summary: Civilians in the southern Lebanese city of Sour expressed doubt that the ceasefire with Israel will hold. Residents reported ongoing hardships and a struggle to survive amid continued uncertainty about security conditions.

stories.title: China’s Xi Jinping says Strait of Hormuz should be open in call with Saudi crown prince
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for the Strait of Hormuz to remain open during a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, according to state broadcaster CCTV. It was reportedly the first time Xi called for the reopening of the waterway, which has been repeatedly blockaded since US-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28.

stories.title: Two young men set to be charged with spying for Iran
stories.summary: Two young men in Israel are set to be charged with espionage on behalf of Iran. One suspect, a 19-year-old, reportedly maintained contact with an Iranian handler and agreed to undergo training in an Arab country despite threatening messages sent to his family.

stories.title: Latvia and Lithuania bar Slovak prime minister’s plane from their airspace on route to Moscow for May 9 parade
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico confirmed that Latvia and Lithuania refused to allow his government plane to transit their airspace for a planned trip to Moscow to attend Russia's May 9 Victory Day military parade.

stories.title: Trump says he will consider advice from Pakistan's Munir on Hormuz blockade, Pakistani source says
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told Pakistan's army chief General Asim Munir in a phone call that he would consider Pakistan's advice regarding the Strait of Hormuz blockade. A Pakistani security source said Munir argued the blockade was an obstacle to peace talks with Iran.

stories.title: US military says it killed three people in latest Caribbean boat strike
stories.summary: U.S. Southern Command reported that American forces killed three men in a strike on a boat in the Caribbean on Sunday. The military described the individuals as illicit drug smugglers.

stories.title: Russia arrests German woman over bomb plot it says is linked to Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia announced the arrest of a German woman found carrying a homemade bomb in her backpack, alleging she was part of a Ukrainian-linked plot to attack a security services facility in southern Russia. The arrest is among dozens Russia has made during the four-year war, mostly of its own citizens, on allegations of working for Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel announces exposure of Iranian terror network targeting Israelis abroad
stories.summary: Israel announced the dismantling of an Iranian terror network that was planning attacks against Israelis abroad. Arrests were made in Azerbaijan in connection with planned attacks on a synagogue and an embassy, while ringleaders were killed during the Iran war.

stories.title: UK arrests 2 teens as ‘thugs for hire’ after latest arson attack on London synagogue
stories.summary: UK Metropolitan Police arrested two teenagers as suspected "thugs for hire" following the latest arson attack on a London synagogue. The arrests bring the total to 15 in connection with six separate incidents over recent months, with police noting pressure from hostile states.

stories.title: Anger as Israeli soldier smashes Jesus statue in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army confirmed that one of its soldiers vandalized a statue of Jesus Christ in southern Lebanon, prompting widespread anger. The incident drew condemnation from Lebanese civilians and religious communities.

stories.title: Free webinar: Managing your Israeli property remotely in uncertain times - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored webinar is being offered on managing Israeli property remotely during uncertain times. The session will cover operations, risks, and decision-making for property owners abroad.

stories.title: Report: Russian courts treat the number 666 as a symbol of a banned ‘extremist’ movement
stories.summary: Russian courts have begun fining residents for posting images featuring the number 666, treating them as propaganda for the "International Satanism Movement," which Russian authorities have designated an extremist organization, according to state news agency RIA Novosti.

stories.title: The economy amid the US-Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan faces significant balance-of-payments pressure in April 2026, with $4.8 billion in debt repayments due including $3.5 billion to the UAE and a $1.3 billion maturing Eurobond. The State Bank of Pakistan holds approximately $16.38 billion in foreign reserves amid economic strain from the US-Iran war.

stories.title: The EU must not wait till Israel starts executing Palestinians
stories.summary: Calls have intensified for the European Union to cancel the EU-Israel Association Agreement. Advocates cite Israeli violations of the agreement's human rights clause and urge immediate action rather than waiting for further escalation.

stories.title: Russians shell railway infrastructure in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck railway infrastructure facilities in Ukraine's Kharkiv region overnight on April 20. No casualties were reported in the attack.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson's claims against actress are 'malicious concoctions', Australian court hears
stories.summary: Actress Rebel Wilson faces a defamation lawsuit in an Australian court over claims she made about a co-star from her film The Deb. The opposing legal team described Wilson's allegations, which involved an incident at a Bondi bath, as malicious fabrications.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer under pressure over Mandelson's appointment as ambassador
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a parliamentary crisis over the appointment of Peter Mandelson as Britain's ambassador to Washington. Mandelson reportedly failed security vetting checks, and questions have mounted over whether Starmer knew about the security concerns before the appointment was made.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in the air as high-seas ship seizure reignites Hormuz tensions
stories.summary: Pakistan proceeded with preparations for a second round of US-Iran talks as a tenuous ceasefire neared expiration, despite rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The US Navy attacked and seized the Iranian-flagged cargo vessel Touska, which it said had tried to evade a blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Rumen Radev, pro-Russia ex-pilot who wants to give Bulgaria wings
stories.summary: Former fighter pilot Rumen Radev's party won Bulgaria's eighth parliamentary election in five years on Sunday. The 62-year-old ex-president has advocated for dialogue with Russia while acknowledging the benefits of EU membership. He has positioned himself as a champion of Bulgaria's poorest citizens amid the country's prolonged political instability.

stories.title: Peace talks clouded by uncertainty after US seizes Iranian ship
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and Iran escalated on Monday after the U.S. seized an Iranian cargo ship that allegedly attempted to breach a naval blockade. Iran vowed retaliation and stated it would not participate in a planned second round of negotiations. The developments raised concerns that the existing ceasefire between the two countries could collapse.

stories.title: Algeria opens new oil and gas bids as Middle East war strains markets
stories.summary: Algeria launched a new round of international bids for hydrocarbon exploration and production concessions on Sunday. The move aims to boost energy investment as global markets face disruption from the ongoing war in the Middle East.

stories.title: India and China wall off border rows to focus on trade and security
stories.summary: India and China held their first bilateral consultations focused exclusively on the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in New Delhi, signaling a cautious diplomatic reset. Analysts say the two countries are increasingly separating their border disputes from expanding cooperation on trade, security, and multilateral diplomacy.

stories.title: Ceasefire at risk after US seizes Iranian ship, Iran shuns peace talks
stories.summary: A US-Iran ceasefire appeared at risk after the US Navy seized an Iranian-flagged ship and Iran declined to participate in peace talks. Washington had hoped to begin negotiations in Pakistan before the two-week ceasefire expired.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry says US not serious about pursuing diplomacy
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry accused the United States of not being serious about diplomacy, citing alleged violations of their two-week ceasefire. Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei pointed to the US seizure of an Iranian cargo ship and the ongoing naval blockade as evidence.

stories.title: Second round in Islamabad: Who are the main US-Iran negotiators?
stories.summary: A second round of US-Iran negotiations is set to take place in Islamabad, though the talks remain uncertain. The article profiles the key figures from both the American and Iranian sides who have driven the diplomatic process so far.

stories.title: US captures Iranian ship Touska amid mediation efforts: All we know
stories.summary: US forces seized the Iranian cargo ship Touska, claiming it was attempting to evade the American naval blockade. Iran condemned the action as "piracy." The incident occurred amid ongoing mediation efforts between the two countries.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF strikes ready-to-fire Hezbollah launcher in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces carried out a strike on what it identified as a ready-to-fire Hezbollah rocket launcher in southern Lebanon. The IDF also issued warnings to civilians in the area, advising them not to move south of specified villages due to continuing military operations against Hezbollah.

stories.title: China ‘Superdad’ uses salary, loans to build ‘marathon Dream Home’ for 300 deprived kids
stories.summary: Bai Jian, a 52-year-old physical education teacher in Anshan, Liaoning province, has adopted nearly 300 parentless children over the past three decades. He rents a large property called Dream Home to house 20 to 30 children at a time, funded by his salary and loans. The children include orphans and others who were abandoned.

stories.title: Oil refinery on fire following drone attack in Tuapse
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a large fire at the tank farm of an oil refinery in Tuapse, Krasnodar Krai, Russia, during a nighttime attack.

stories.title: The bike that could save billions
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs in Pakistan are prompting discussion about electric motorcycles as a potential alternative for delivery workers and commuters. The article examines the financial barriers, including high upfront costs, that prevent widespread adoption of electric bikes.

stories.title: What does the US and Iran’s ‘fight-talk’ dynamic mean before their ceasefire expires?
stories.summary: The US Navy destroyer USS Spruance fired on the Iranian-flagged cargo ship Touska in the Gulf of Oman after its crew reportedly ignored orders to halt. The incident near the Strait of Hormuz raised conflict risks, though analysts say both Washington and Tehran have shown reluctance to prolong the war.

stories.title: British universities paid security firm to ‘spy’ on pro-Palestine students
stories.summary: An investigation found that British universities hired Horus, a security firm led by former military intelligence officials, to monitor pro-Palestine student protesters. The surveillance was carried out during a wave of campus activism.

stories.title: Red Zone sealed again ahead of possible Islamabad Talks 2.0
stories.summary: Islamabad's Red Zone and Extended Red Zone were sealed to all traffic ahead of expected second-round talks between US and Iranian delegations. Public and heavy transport were suspended, and alternate traffic plans were issued for residents of the capital.

stories.title: Ireland plans “generous” payout to send 16,000 Ukrainian refugees home — The Times
stories.summary: Ireland's migration minister Colm Brophy announced plans to end state-provided accommodation for approximately 16,000 Ukrainian refugees within 12 months. The government intends to offer a financial returns package described as generous to encourage voluntary departures.

stories.title: ‘Their legacy commands us’: IDF chief marks Remembrance Day with call for unity, resolve
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir delivered remarks on Israel's Remembrance Day, honoring fallen soldiers and calling for national unity. This marks the third Remembrance Day observed since the October 7 massacre.

stories.title: France summons Elon Musk over X probe
stories.summary: French authorities summoned Elon Musk for an interview in connection with a probe related to his social media platform X. Officials have not disclosed the location or timing of the scheduled interview.

stories.title: How China's chip expansion puts pressure on global rivals
stories.summary: U.S. restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports have pushed China to develop its own chip manufacturing ecosystem. While China still trails at the cutting edge, its expanding production of competitive-enough chips is increasingly powering segments of the global economy.

stories.title: How China is reshaping the global chip industry
stories.summary: U.S. restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports have driven China to develop its own chip ecosystem. Although China still trails at the cutting edge, its domestically produced semiconductors are increasingly powering segments of the global economy.

stories.title: Death toll in occupied West Bank from Israeli attacks rises
stories.summary: Since Israel's war on Gaza began in October 2023, Israeli army and settler attacks have killed at least 1,151 Palestinians and wounded over 11,885 across the occupied West Bank. More than 23,000 Palestinians have been arrested during the same period, with over 9,560 held in Israeli jails as of April 2026.

stories.title: Intelligence shows how two large Russian landing ships were hit in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Prymary special unit, part of the Main Intelligence Directorate, carried out strikes on two Russian large landing ships stationed in occupied Crimea. Intelligence documentation confirmed the successful hits on both vessels.

stories.title: Zelenskyy puts March price tag on Russian oil hits — $2.3bn in one month
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil infrastructure cost Russia at least $2.3 billion in revenue during March alone. He pledged to continue the targeting campaign against Russian energy assets.

stories.title: ‘Worst I’ve seen’: forest fires rage across Thailand, Mekong region
stories.summary: Severe forest fires are burning across Laos, Myanmar, and Thailand, producing dangerous smoke levels and a public health crisis, particularly in northern Thailand's Chiang Mai. Dry season conditions have created tinderbox environments, leaving overstretched firefighters battling widespread blazes across the Mekong region.

stories.title: The ugly Israeli
stories.summary: The Italian magazine L'Espresso published a cover story featuring an Israeli soldier-settler filming a distraught Palestinian woman, depicting harassment that occurs frequently in occupied Palestinian territories. The cover provoked widespread accusations of antisemitism.

stories.title: Remembering Daniel – with Rabbi Doron Perez - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: As Israel marks Yom HaZikaron, Aviva Klompas interviewed Rabbi Doron Perez about his son Captain Daniel Perez, who was killed on October 7 while defending Israel's border. The conversation focuses on remembrance and honoring the fallen.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones kill man in southern Russian city: governor
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes killed a man in a city in southern Russia, according to the regional governor. Earlier in the week, a 14-year-old girl and a young woman were also killed in drone attacks in the same area.

stories.title: Volyn foresters and Latvian volunteers lay “Forest of Remembrance” for engineer killed in 2023 shelling
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Latvian foresters planted a memorial forest in Ukraine's Volyn region honoring Bohdan Kostiuchyk, an engineer killed in a 2023 shelling, along with all fallen foresters. A companion memorial forest is planned in Latvia the following week.

stories.title: Magnitude 7.5 earthquake strikes northern Japan; tsunami warning issued
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck northern Japan, prompting authorities to issue a tsunami warning. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced the establishment of a crisis management team in response to the quake.

stories.title: Ukraine claims attack on Russian warships in occupied Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence claimed a successful attack on two large Russian landing ships in Sevastopol Bay in Russian-occupied Crimea. The strikes targeted vessels stationed in the strategically important naval port.

stories.title: US Navy seizure of Iranian ship casts doubt on fresh ceasefire talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy's seizure of an Iranian-flagged cargo ship cast doubt on President Donald Trump's announcement that American negotiators would travel to Pakistan on Monday for further talks with Iran. The fragile ceasefire between the two nations is set to expire by Wednesday. Iran has not confirmed whether it will attend the negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine reaches security deal with India — Zelenskyy says documents being finalized
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine has reached a security cooperation arrangement with India, with documents currently being finalized. The development followed a briefing from NSDC Secretary Rustem Umerov on April 19.

stories.title: This Yom HaZikaron, keep their memory alive through a Chumash with their stories - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored initiative offers a Chumash that honors fallen IDF soldiers with tributes, biographies, and Torah commentaries on each page. Donors contributing $360 or more receive the Chumash, and an additional copy is gifted to an injured soldier.

stories.title: Why Israel cannot defeat Hezbollah
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Israel has been unable to defeat Hezbollah despite over two years of military operations under Prime Minister Netanyahu. The assessment suggests Israel's military strategy in Lebanon has reached its limits despite repeated promises of total victory.

stories.title: Weather tracker: temperatures in Spain and Brazil well above late April norm
stories.summary: Temperatures in Spain are expected to reach well above seasonal averages this week, with Madrid forecast at 30°C and Seville at 34°C due to warm air from North Africa. Parts of Brazil are also experiencing unusually high temperatures in the high 30s, while storms are forecast in southern Africa.

stories.title: Bulgaria Kremlin-friendly ex-president wins parliamentary majority
stories.summary: Former Bulgarian president Rumen Radev, who has called for renewing ties with Russia and criticized the EU, secured an absolute parliamentary majority in Sunday's elections based on near-complete results. Bulgaria, the EU's poorest member, has held eight elections since 2021 following anti-corruption protests that toppled former Prime Minister Boyko Borissov's government.

stories.title: ‘We wasted a lot of lives’: CIA spymaster’s caution over past Iran intervention resurfaces from beyond the grave
stories.summary: A documentary about Peter Sichel, a former CIA station chief in Berlin who died in 2025, includes his reflections on the human costs of past US interventions in Iran and the Middle East. Sichel, a Jewish refugee from Nazi Germany, acknowledged that many lives were wasted through such operations.

stories.title: Japan warship’s Taiwan Strait voyage reignites China tensions
stories.summary: China issued a "strong protest" after the Japanese destroyer JS Ikazuchi transited the Taiwan Strait en route to military exercises in the Philippines. The passage occurred on the anniversary of the 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki, which ceded Taiwan to Japan. Beijing called the 14-hour voyage a "deliberate provocation."

stories.title: The fallout
stories.summary: The US-Iran war is expected to have lasting security, economic, and diplomatic consequences globally. Damage to energy infrastructure and disrupted oil shipments have driven up energy prices, affecting countries well beyond the Middle East.

stories.title: Bulgaria's former President Radev takes strong lead in election
stories.summary: Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party led Sunday's parliamentary election with 44.59% of votes after 32% were counted. The former fighter pilot and ex-president, who opposes military support for Ukraine, stepped down from the presidency in January to run. The election followed mass protests that forced out the previous government in December.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz sets crisis talks to tackle energy price impact
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced crisis talks to address the impact of rising energy prices. Merz stated that while the market situation is tense, Germany's energy supply remains secure.

stories.title: Russians attack Kryvyi Rih, two districts of Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving six injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 20 strikes using drones, aerial bombs, and artillery against Kryvyi Rih and the Nikopol and Synelnykove districts of Dnipropetrovsk region. Six people were wounded in the attacks.

stories.title: UK's Starmer to face grilling from MPs over Mandelson scandal
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced parliamentary questioning on Monday over a scandal involving Peter Mandelson, a long-time associate of Jeffrey Epstein. Mandelson was appointed Britain's ambassador to the United States in late 2024 despite reportedly failing security checks. The controversy has intensified calls for Starmer to resign amid declining public support.

stories.title: Bulgaria: Pro-Russia Rumen Radev wins ‌election
stories.summary: Rumen Radev's new center-left party, Progressive Bulgaria, won an absolute majority in the country's eighth general election in five years. Both Russia and the European Union sent congratulations to the pro-Russia leader following his victory.

stories.title: Bulgaria: Pro-Russia Rumen Radev on course to win election
stories.summary: Rumen Radev's new center-left party, Progressive Bulgaria, is projected to win Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years. Radev's pro-Moscow stance has raised concerns in Brussels about the country's foreign policy direction.

stories.title: China warns joint US, Philippines and Japan drills risk regional trust
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry warned on Monday that joint military exercises among the United States, the Philippines, and Japan risk undermining mutual trust among regional countries. The remarks came in response to the annual joint drills hosted by the Philippines and the U.S., which this year also involve Japanese forces.

stories.title: Inside war-hit Sudan’s only functioning hospital curing tropical diseases
stories.summary: A report highlights the last functioning hospital in Sudan treating tropical diseases amid the ongoing civil war. Sudan's health ministry says 37 percent of the country's health facilities are out of service as the conflict enters its fourth year.

stories.title: Minns doubles down on ‘rational’ anti-protest law despite NSW’s highest court ruling it unconstitutional
stories.summary: New South Wales Premier Chris Minns defended his government's anti-protest legislation as "rational and proportionate" after the state's highest court ruled it unconstitutional. The Greens and protest advocates criticized his response as an "extraordinary attack" on the judiciary.

stories.title: China presses IMF for quota reform, better surveillance of advanced economies
stories.summary: People's Bank of China governor Pan Gongsheng urged the IMF to oppose protectionism and defend multilateralism at the fund's 53rd International Monetary and Financial Committee meeting. China pressed for IMF quota reform and improved surveillance of advanced economies amid rising trade restrictions and the Middle East conflict's impact on energy and food security.

stories.title: War update: 206 frontline clashes over past day, fiercest fighting in Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: A total of 206 combat engagements were recorded along the frontline on April 19 between Ukrainian Defense Forces and Russian troops. The most intense fighting occurred in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: U.S. military strike on alleged drug boat kills 3 in Caribbean Sea
stories.summary: The U.S. military conducted a strike on a boat it accused of transporting drugs in the Caribbean Sea, killing three people aboard the vessel.

stories.title: Can a US-governed ‘Pax Silica’ hub turn Philippines into a chip powerhouse?
stories.summary: The United States plans to build a 4,000-acre economic security zone in the Philippines as part of the Pax Silica initiative to counter China's dominance in critical technologies. The hub would operate under US common law on Philippine soil and be designated the first "AI-native investment acceleration hub" under the framework.

stories.title: Myanmar military regime widens sanitary towel ban, claiming rebels use them for first aid
stories.summary: Myanmar's military regime expanded its ban on distributing sanitary towels, claiming resistance fighters use them for first aid. Activists condemned the policy as gender-based violence that violates women's rights amid the civil war that has raged since the 2021 military coup.

stories.title: Iran says 'no decision' on whether to attend next round of US talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Tehran has not yet decided whether to attend the next round of talks with the United States. He stated that no plans or decisions regarding further negotiations have been made.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Govt Warns Against Illegal Use, Conferment of Ambassadorial Titles
stories.summary: Nigeria's government issued a warning against the illegal use and conferment of ambassadorial titles. The relevant ministry stated that improper use of such titles is considered a criminal offense.

stories.title: Iran says not attending talks, US team 'en route' to Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran maintained it would not attend ceasefire talks with the US in Pakistan, citing unresolved issues. Meanwhile, the US negotiating team was reported to be en route to Pakistan for the planned discussions.

stories.title: US-Iran tensions escalate as Strait of Hormuz blockade continues
stories.summary: Iran announced it has no plans to attend negotiations with the United States in Pakistan, as the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remains a major point of contention. Tensions between Washington and Tehran continue to escalate over the blockade.

stories.title: Nigeria: Terrorists Attack Military Base in Kwara
stories.summary: Terrorists attacked a military base in Kwara state, Nigeria, seizing eight operational motorcycles and a gun truck. Intelligence sources and local residents confirmed the details of the raid.

stories.title: Gaps over Iran's nuclear work remain, missile programme not negotiable with US, senior Iranian source says
stories.summary: A senior Iranian source told Reuters that significant gaps remain between Iran and the United States over Iran's nuclear programme. Tehran has declared its missile programme and defensive capabilities non-negotiable and said the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz undermines diplomacy.

stories.title: Round two?
stories.summary: Pakistan's federal capital Islamabad is preparing to host a potential second round of high-level diplomatic engagements related to Middle East peace efforts. Security plans and logistical arrangements are being put in place following the prime minister's three-nation tour and the defence chief's visit to Iran.

stories.title: Palestinian children protest against siege on their school
stories.summary: Palestinian children staged a protest against Israeli settlers and soldiers who have been blocking the only safe route to their school. The demonstrations took place in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: China voices concern over US seizure of Iranian cargo ship
stories.summary: China expressed concern over the US forced interception of an Iranian-flagged cargo ship, urging all parties to abide by the ceasefire agreement. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesman called on those involved to avoid further escalation near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russian drone strike hits residential building in Velykyi Burluk, three injured
stories.summary: Three people were injured overnight on April 20 when Russian drones struck a residential building in Velykyi Burluk, Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Bulgaria’s new Orbán? Ex-president Radev’s anti-Ukraine party wins country’s eighth election in five years
stories.summary: Former Bulgarian president Rumen Radev's party won the country's eighth parliamentary election in five years. Radev opposes sending weapons to Ukraine and has called for pragmatic relations with Moscow.

stories.title: Baltic nations brace for impact of Iran war delaying US weapons shipments
stories.summary: Baltic nations using U.S.-supplied HIMARS systems are concerned that the conflict between the United States and Iran could delay ammunition deliveries. The potential shortages have raised questions about whether Washington would permit the Baltic states to use non-Lockheed Martin rockets in the launchers.

stories.title: Delays, rising costs hit Asia’s trade as Gulf crisis spills beyond oil
stories.summary: Malaysia's busiest container port began refusing Middle East-bound cargo unless shipping lines guarantee prompt pickup, reflecting the Gulf crisis's growing impact on Asian trade. Longer transit times, missed sailings, and sharply higher insurance premiums are disrupting regional logistics chains beyond the oil sector.

stories.title: Tensions escalate over Strait of Hormuz, Iran says "no plans" to join talks
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remained closed on Monday amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran. Washington said talks were due to resume, but Tehran stated it had no plans to participate in negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli army investigates soldier seen striking Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military is investigating a soldier photographed striking a statue of Jesus with a sledgehammer in southern Lebanon. The IDF confirmed the image circulating on social media is authentic and said the incident is being viewed with "great severity."

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defenses down 113 out of 142 Russian drones in overnight attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 113 of 142 drones launched by Russia since the evening of April 19. The remaining drones were not neutralized during the overnight attack.

stories.title: Iran executes two men convicted of espionage for Mossad and plotting attacks
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad Masoum Shahi and Hamed Validi after convicting them of espionage for Israel's Mossad and plotting attacks inside Iran. The two were accused of receiving training abroad as part of a spy network.

stories.title: Why Hong Kong property recovery sceptics miss the bigger picture
stories.summary: Hong Kong's property market outlook has improved significantly over the past year. Morgan Stanley's prediction of a 10 percent rise in secondary home values, initially considered a non-consensus call in January, now aligns with most industry forecasts. The office market outlook has also shifted.

stories.title: EU Parliament press Norway to boost Ukraine aid from energy profits; Stoltenberg cites existing support
stories.summary: Members of the European Parliament called on Norway to direct its surging oil and gas revenues toward supporting Ukraine, with a Greens lawmaker proposing a windfall tax on energy company Equinor. Former NATO chief and Norwegian FM Jens Stoltenberg pointed to Norway's existing support contributions.

stories.title: Can US blockade Iranian-linked ships anywhere in the world?
stories.summary: Legal experts are debating whether the United States can lawfully blockade Iranian-linked ships in international waters. One expert noted that for a blockade to be considered legal, it must be both enforceable and actively enforced.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,050 over past day
stories.summary: Russia's cumulative combat losses in Ukraine have reached approximately 1,319,270 personnel from February 24, 2022, to April 20, 2026, according to Ukrainian military figures. An estimated 1,050 Russian troops were lost in the past day alone.

stories.title: The Strokes highlight destroyed Gaza and Iran universities at Coachella
stories.summary: The American rock band The Strokes used their Coachella performance to display images of universities destroyed in Gaza and Iran. The on-stage visuals drew attention to the impact of US-Israeli military operations on educational institutions.

stories.title: Pakistan Medical Association warns of surge in hepatitis cases on World Liver Day
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical Association warned of rising hepatitis and liver disease cases on World Liver Day, noting Pakistan has the highest global burden of Hepatitis C. Approximately 37,000 deaths occur annually in the country from liver complications including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

stories.title: New drought-resistant wheat variety named after October 7 victim
stories.summary: Israel's Volcani Institute named a new drought-resistant wheat variety after Yakov Inon, an agronomist who served as a consultant to the institute. Inon and his wife Bilha were killed by Hamas at Moshav Netiv Ha'asara on October 7.

stories.title: Tsunami warning issued in Japan after magnitude-7.5 quake hits northeast
stories.summary: A magnitude-7.5 earthquake struck off Japan's Sanriku Coast, prompting tsunami warnings for parts of northeast and northern Japan. Residents evacuated to higher ground, and fishing boats left ports to avoid incoming waves. The event revived memories of the devastating 2011 earthquake and tsunami disaster.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson accused in court of trying to paint actor as ‘money grabbing opportunist’ as defamation trial begins
stories.summary: A defamation trial began in court with actor Charlotte MacInnes accusing Rebel Wilson of hiring a private investigator and publishing false information online to portray her as a "money grabbing opportunist." Wilson denies the allegations and claims MacInnes told her about an uncomfortable situation with a producer.

stories.title: Iran's president highlights importance of diplomacy while stressing distrust of US, IRNA reports
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that all rational and diplomatic paths should be used to reduce tensions with the US, while emphasizing that vigilance and distrust toward Washington remain essential. A two-week ceasefire is set to expire on Wednesday.

stories.title: Strong 7.5 earthquake hits off Japan, tsunami warning issued
stories.summary: A 7.5-magnitude earthquake struck off northern Japan on Monday, prompting tsunami warnings in the region from Japan's Meteorological Agency. The tremor was powerful enough to shake large buildings as far away as Tokyo, located hundreds of kilometers from the epicenter.

stories.title: US strike on alleged drug boat in Caribbean kills 3
stories.summary: A U.S. military strike on a suspected drug-smuggling boat in the Caribbean killed three people. The incident is part of a broader military campaign against cartels that has killed at least 180 people since last year, drawing criticism over its legality.

stories.title: China’s trade with Iran, Gulf states plunges as Strait of Hormuz crisis hits energy flows
stories.summary: China's trade with Iran and Gulf states fell sharply in March as Strait of Hormuz restrictions tightened amid the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. Chinese imports from Iran dropped 48 percent year on year, while exports to Iran plunged 90 percent. Exports to eight Persian Gulf economies declined 57 percent.

stories.title: Beersheba woman killed, eight-year-old severely injured in domestic stabbing attack
stories.summary: A woman was fatally stabbed and an eight-year-old child was severely injured in a domestic attack in Beersheba, Israel. Police arrested the woman's husband on suspicion of murder and opened an investigation.

stories.title: Israel’s new automatic Roem howitzer used for first time in combat
stories.summary: Israel deployed its new Roem howitzer in combat for the first time. The fully automated artillery system can fire six to eight rounds per minute and has an effective range of up to 40 kilometers.

stories.title: Washington’s approach raises doubts, Araghchi tells Pakistan over phone
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar by phone that Washington's approach shows 'ill will' and a lack of seriousness, citing repeated breaches of trust including US military actions during negotiations.

stories.title: The F-35 Is a Masterpiece Built for the Wrong War
stories.summary: The F-35 program's total projected lifetime cost exceeds two trillion dollars, making it the most expensive Major Defense Acquisition Program in U.S. history. The United States plans to purchase thousands of the aircraft. Critics argue that while the fighter jet is technologically advanced, its high cost and slow production rate make it ill-suited for large-scale conflict scenarios.

stories.title: Water worries grip KP farmers amid Indus Treaty concerns
stories.summary: Farmers in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Dera Ismail Khan district are expressing concern over potential disruptions to water supplies linked to the Indus Waters Treaty with India. Experts warn that reduced river flows could worsen food insecurity and affect irrigation and electricity generation at Tarbela and Mangla dams.

stories.title: Tuapse burns again: drones hit the port city three days after the last fire was put out
stories.summary: Ukraine's GUR military intelligence "Prymary" unit struck two Russian landing ships and a Podlet-K1 radar in occupied Sevastopol on April 19. Separately, Ukrainian drones hit the Russian port city of Tuapse, killing one person and starting a fire at the seaport.

stories.title: Israeli gunfire injures two Palestinians in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and wounded a young Palestinian man with live fire in Kafr Qud village, west of Jenin, in the occupied West Bank. In a separate incident, another Palestinian was shot during an Israeli raid in Nablus.

stories.title: Ukraine pushing for Special Tribunal at PACE spring session
stories.summary: Ukraine's delegation to the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe is pushing for the establishment of a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine during PACE's spring plenary session beginning April 20 in Strasbourg.

stories.title: Forces target terrorist positions on Peshawar outskirts
stories.summary: Security forces including police, army, Frontier Corps, and the Counter-Terrorism Department conducted a joint operation against Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan militants in the Hassan Khel area on the outskirts of Peshawar and Kohat. Officials reported that several militants were eliminated and their hideouts destroyed.

stories.title: UK PM to face grilling from MPs today over Mandelson scandal
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces questioning from MPs over a scandal involving Peter Mandelson, a long-time associate of Jeffrey Epstein who reportedly failed a security vetting process in late 2024. Opposition leaders have called on Starmer to resign, while ministers say he was unaware of Mandelson's clearance status.

stories.title: Unicef decries water suppliers’ killing in Gaza
stories.summary: UNICEF condemned the killing of two civilian water truck drivers by Israeli troops in northern Gaza. The Israeli military claimed its forces fired on what it described as two armed terrorists approaching along the Yellow Line.

stories.title: Turkey, Syria, Jordan unveil Gulf-Europe rail corridor as Ankara pushes alternative trade routes
stories.summary: Turkey, Syria, and Jordan announced plans for a Gulf-to-Europe rail corridor running from European ports through Turkey and Syria into Jordan, creating a continuous land bridge to Gulf markets as Ankara pursues alternative trade routes.

stories.title: Bulgaria's Kremlin-friendly former president Radev wins parliamentary election
stories.summary: Former Bulgarian president Rumen Radev won a parliamentary majority in Sunday's elections according to near-complete results released Monday. Radev, who has advocated renewing ties with Russia and criticized the EU, called the outcome a "victory of hope."

stories.title: Iran executes two men accused of planning attacks with Israel’s Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad Masoum Shahi and Hamed Validi, who were convicted of collaborating with Israel's Mossad. The two men were found guilty of working with hostile groups and receiving training abroad to plan attacks inside Iran.

stories.title: Kuwait detains journalist amid crackdown on war coverage
stories.summary: Kuwaiti authorities detained US-Kuwaiti journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin, who has not been seen publicly since March 2. He faces charges of spreading false information and harming security. The Committee to Protect Journalists and a UN rapporteur have called for his immediate release.

stories.title: 'Unprecedented since 1999': Radev secures absolute majority with reformist and eurosceptic coalition
stories.summary: Political scientist Dr. Petia Gueorguieva of New Bulgarian University noted that Rumen Radev's parliamentary majority is unprecedented since 1999. She said Radev united a diverse electorate spanning pro-reform citizens and Eurosceptic, economically vulnerable groups. While Bulgaria remains in the EU and NATO, the result carries implications for the country's geopolitical positioning and political stability.

stories.title: Kenya: Chaos in Haiti As Civilians Attempt to Block Departure of Kenyan Police Officers
stories.summary: Haitian civilians in central Haiti attempted to block the departure of Kenyan police officers serving in the Kenya-led Multinational Security Support Mission. Residents feared that the withdrawal would expose communities to renewed gang violence as the mission winds down operations.

stories.title: Russian drone hits infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck an infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, causing damage to nearby residential buildings.

stories.title: Lebanon restores lifelines as Israel extends demolition
stories.summary: Lebanon's military reopened the Qasmiyeh bridge and a key road in the south destroyed by Israeli strikes, restoring a vital link for civilians. Meanwhile, Israel continued demolitions and pushed deeper into Lebanese territory to establish a buffer zone amid a fragile 10-day truce.

stories.title: Video: US attacks and seizes Iranian cargo ship near Hormuz
stories.summary: US naval forces attacked and seized the Iranian-flagged container ship Touska near the Strait of Hormuz, disabling its engine room before boarding. Washington cited blockade enforcement, while Iran called the seizure unlawful.

stories.title: Israel attacks Kfarkela in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck what it described as a ready-to-fire launcher in the Kfarkela area of southern Lebanon overnight, despite an ongoing ceasefire agreement in the country.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A morning briefing summarized rising US-Iran tensions over maritime control, stalled diplomacy, and military actions, with Pakistan attempting to broker peace as the ceasefire expiration nears and escalation risks remain high.

stories.title: Israel army probes image of soldier hitting Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army opened an investigation into a photograph showing a soldier damaging a statue of Jesus in southern Lebanon. A military spokesman stated that the act does not align with IDF values.

stories.title: Iran and the Indispensable Broker: How Pakistan Outmaneuvers India on the World Stage
stories.summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense pact in Riyadh in September 2025, formalizing decades of bilateral security cooperation. The agreement is seen as part of Pakistan's longstanding pattern of leveraging diplomatic relationships to maintain outsized geopolitical influence despite economic challenges, including reliance on International Monetary Fund bailouts.

stories.title: US releases video of forces seizing Iranian ship
stories.summary: The United States intercepted an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf as part of its naval blockade. President Donald Trump confirmed the seizure, and the US military released video footage of the operation.

stories.title: Hinglaj Mata festival draws nearly 300,000 Hindu pilgrims in Balochistan
stories.summary: The three-day annual Hinglaj Mata festival concluded in Balochistan, drawing nearly 300,000 Hindu pilgrims to the historic temple. Security arrangements, medical camps, and round-the-clock aid were provided, and officials called for religious harmony and unity.

stories.title: U.S. Navy seizes Iranian-flagged ship near Strait of Hormuz, Tehran vows swift response
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy seized an Iranian-flagged ship near the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first interception since Washington imposed a blockade on Iranian ports the previous week. Iran vowed a swift response to the seizure.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 52 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: On day 52 of US-Israeli military operations against Iran, diplomatic talks in Islamabad were thrown into uncertainty. Iran vowed retaliation after US marines captured an Iranian cargo ship near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Assault on vessel overshadows preparation for round two of US-Iran dialogue
stories.summary: An incident involving a vessel in the Sea of Oman has overshadowed preparations for a second round of US-Iran talks expected to take place in Islamabad. Iran has signaled reluctance to attend, citing what it calls Washington's excessive demands, while heavy security measures have been imposed across Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

stories.title: UN Security Council to discuss Russia’s attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: The United Nations Security Council is scheduled to convene on Monday to discuss recent Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Iran says 95 percent of airport infrastructure still operational
stories.summary: Iran reported that approximately 95 percent of its airport infrastructure remains intact and operational, though about 20 aircraft have sustained serious damage, according to Fars news agency.

stories.title: Bulgaria: Pro-Russian Radev takes lead in early vote count
stories.summary: Exit polls from Bulgaria's eighth election in five years show former president Rumen Radev's new left-leaning, pro-Russian party with a significant lead. Radev, a former fighter pilot, stepped down as Bulgaria's president in January.

stories.title: Nigeria: Foreign Travel Advisories: Nigeria Should Invoke Reciprocity
stories.summary: A Nigerian opinion piece questions whether the country should invoke reciprocity regarding foreign travel advisories, noting that countries issuing warnings about Nigeria also face significant street crime and organized violence.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria to Send 200 Special Forces to Türkiye for Training - Minister
stories.summary: Nigeria's Defence Minister, retired Gen. Christopher Musa, announced that 200 Nigerian Special Forces personnel will be deployed to Türkiye for training under a newly reached bilateral agreement.

stories.title: Nigeria: FCT Teachers Resume Strike Today, Halt School Resumption
stories.summary: Primary and secondary school teachers in Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory have resumed an indefinite strike, halting school resumption across all public schools in the territory.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - Total Shutdown As Enugu West Zone Endorses Tinubu, Mbah for Second Term
stories.summary: Residents of Enugu West Senatorial District in Nigeria have endorsed President Bola Tinubu and Governor Peter Mbah for second terms in the 2027 elections, citing positive policy impacts on the region.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rising Truck Volumes At Rusumo Pile Pressure On Infrastructure
stories.summary: Daily truck crossings at Rwanda's Rusumo border post have doubled to over 600 in three years, making it one of the country's busiest trade corridors and straining existing infrastructure.

stories.title: Rwanda: What Drives Your Water Bill? Inside Rura's Tariff System, Consumer Protection
stories.summary: Rwandan officials say limited public understanding of how water tariffs are determined remains a key challenge, even as the country has made progress in expanding access to clean water under regulator Rura's tariff system.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: ceasefire under pressure and talks in doubt as Iran threatens to ‘retaliate’ to US seizure of ship
stories.summary: Iran threatened to retaliate after the US seized the Iranian-flagged vessel M/V Touska, with Tehran reportedly refusing to participate in new peace talks and accusing Washington of violating the ceasefire. US Central Command released footage showing Marines from the USS Tripoli rappelling onto the cargo ship by helicopter.

stories.title: Vietnam and Philippines trust Japan. Why doesn’t Indonesia?
stories.summary: An annual survey shows trust in Japan as a security partner varies significantly across Southeast Asia. The Philippines and Vietnam rank Tokyo highly due to Chinese territorial pressure, while Indonesia remains wary given its longstanding commitment to non-alignment.

stories.title: Is Malacca Strait at risk from Hormuz ‘chain reaction’ after warning from Iranian adviser?
stories.summary: An adviser to Iran's supreme leader warned of a potential "chain-reaction response" affecting critical global shipping lanes, including the Malacca Strait in Southeast Asia, after Iran declared another full closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The threat raised concerns about disruptions to major trade routes.

stories.title: Shipping channels unaffected  by Hormuz tensions
stories.summary: Despite tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, shipping activity at Pakistan's ports remains unaffected. Oil tankers, including Pakistan National Shipping Company vessels MT Sargodha, MT Shalimar, and MT Lahore, continue to deliver crude oil and petroleum fuel to Karachi port.

stories.title: Two FC men martyred in Bannu attack
stories.summary: Two Frontier Constabulary personnel were killed by militants in Kuram Garhi, Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, while shopping at a local market. The attackers arrived on a motorcycle and fled the scene. Security forces launched a search operation afterward.

stories.title: Pfizer, Amgen among 22 strategic firms eyeing Hong Kong expansion: source
stories.summary: Pfizer, Amgen, and 20 other strategic enterprises from sectors including fintech, cloud computing, and aerial transport are planning to open or expand offices in Hong Kong. The companies are set to sign agreements with Hong Kong's Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises.

stories.title: Kyiv region attacked by Russian drones, damage, injuries reported
stories.summary: Russian strike drones targeted Kyiv region, damaging homes in the Brovary district and injuring one person.

stories.title: Iran ensures safe passage through Hormuz, Iranian envoy says
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Moscow, Kazem Jalali, told Russian newspaper Vedomosti that Iran ensures safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz under a new legal regime and that US and Israeli attacks had failed to achieve regime change.

stories.title: Russia launches 142 drones at Ukraine overnight – homes near Kyiv damaged, one hospitalized
stories.summary: Russia launched 142 drones at Ukraine overnight on April 20, damaging residential homes in Kyiv Oblast and Kharkiv Oblast. Four civilians were injured, and one person was hospitalized.

stories.title: Only one-fifth MNAs attended 26th NA session
stories.summary: Only 66 out of 333 members of Pakistan's National Assembly attended all sittings during the 26th session held between March 30 and April 8. Fifty-one members, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Nawaz Sharif, and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, did not attend any sitting.

stories.title: Second cancer shock for Hong Kong actress Kristal Tin. How does disease strike?
stories.summary: Hong Kong actress Kristal Tin, 48, disclosed that cancer cells were found in her lymph nodes, more than a year after being diagnosed with early-stage lung cancer. The former TVB actress won a best lead actress theatre award in 2024.

stories.title: Pakistan ready for multi-day US-Iran talks, but Tehran unsure about joining
stories.summary: Pakistan has offered to host a second round of US-Iran negotiations, but Iranian officials have not yet confirmed their participation as a ceasefire deadline approaches.

stories.title: Addressing markup consumer prices
stories.summary: Pakistan's sales tax system, designed as a value-added tax to document the economy and collect revenue across supply chains, continues to have significant gaps. Wholesalers and retailers remain largely outside the tax net despite the system being in place for over 25 years.

stories.title: Focus on outflows and inflows
stories.summary: Pakistan's interior minister disclosed that Pakistani businessmen have moved billions of dollars abroad over the past three to four years. Business leaders cite policy inconsistency, misgovernance, and lack of trust as reasons for capital flight.

stories.title: Why SMEs struggle to access capital
stories.summary: Pakistan's small and medium enterprise sector comprises over 7.1 million businesses employing more than 25 million people. Despite this scale, SMEs continue to face significant challenges in accessing capital needed for growth and sustainability.

stories.title: US military releases video of marines seizing Iranian ship
stories.summary: The US military released video showing marines boarding and seizing an Iranian-flagged ship near the Strait of Hormuz as part of an ongoing naval blockade enforcement operation.

stories.title: Mykolaiv attacked by Russian drones, houses, cars, power lines damaged
stories.summary: Russian drone attacks on Mykolaiv damaged residential buildings, cars, and power lines in the city.

stories.title: Indonesian rights body says soldiers killed 12 civilians in Papua. Military denies claim
stories.summary: Indonesia's National Human Rights Commission reported that 12 civilians, including women and children, were shot dead during a military operation against separatist rebels in central Papua province. The Indonesian military denied knowledge of the deaths, while dozens of others reportedly sustained serious injuries.

stories.title: At least 25 killed in firecracker factory blast in India
stories.summary: An explosion at a firecracker factory in Tamil Nadu state, India, killed at least 25 people. The majority of the victims were female workers.

stories.title: Washington and Iran quarrel over status of talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: The United States and Iran issued conflicting accounts regarding the status of diplomatic talks held in Pakistan. The dispute emerged as the economically vital Strait of Hormuz remained largely closed to shipping traffic.

stories.title: 'I feel like we failed' to bring Gaza hostages home, Rachel Goldberg-Polin tells CBS's 60 Minutes
stories.summary: Rachel Goldberg-Polin, mother of a former Gaza hostage, told CBS's 60 Minutes she feels she 'failed' to bring hostages home alive, though she acknowledged the effort ultimately resulted in their return.

stories.title: Iran not planning to attend talks with US in Pakistan
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Tehran is not currently planning to attend US talks in Pakistan, citing the ongoing US naval blockade of Iranian ports as a significant obstacle, just days before the ceasefire expires.

stories.title: Iran executes two men accused of involvement in 'spy network linked to Israel', report says
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad Masoum Shahi and Hamed Validi, convicted of cooperating with Israel's Mossad intelligence service and planning attacks inside Iran. The men were accused of belonging to a spy network and receiving training abroad, including in Iraq's Kurdistan region.

stories.title: China’s armed police mull riot control without human contact at all
stories.summary: Chinese People's Armed Police Force engineers published a study outlining scenarios for using autonomous machines instead of human officers for urban riot control. The concept envisions deploying roadblocks and robotic systems to manage crowd unrest without direct human contact.

stories.title: China influencer builds house for girl who claims to be raising sisters alone amid family drama
stories.summary: Chinese influencer Chen Jiajun, known online as Super Btai, built a house for 18-year-old Aji in Guizhou province after she claimed to be raising her sisters alone. He later discovered some of her hardship claims were exaggerated.

stories.title: From grief to action: Ensuring the sacrifices of Israel’s fallen are not in vain - editorial
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post editorial on Israel's Remembrance Day calls for ensuring the sacrifices of fallen soldiers are not in vain and urges action to prevent similar losses in the year ahead.

stories.title: Report: Iran stands firm on demands for a truce in Lebanon, frozen assets
stories.summary: Ebrahim Azizi, head of Iran's parliamentary National Security Committee, told Al Jazeera that Iran will continue talks with the US but insists on a truce in Lebanon and the release of frozen assets as preconditions.

stories.title: British PM to face angry MPs calling for his resignation amid Mandelson-Epstein scandal
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces calls to resign from opposition MPs over his appointment of a US envoy linked to the Mandelson-Epstein scandal. He is expected to address Parliament to explain the decision.

stories.title: The Strokes use Coachella set to denounce US foreign intervention
stories.summary: The Strokes used their Coachella set to denounce US foreign intervention, displaying a montage of world leaders whose death or removal the CIA has been proven or suspected of involvement in. The statement addressed American actions in countries including Iran and Palestine during their performance of the 2016 song Oblivius.

stories.title: South Africa: Mop-Up Operations Begin After Cape Storms - South African News Briefs - April 20, 2026
stories.summary: Mop-up operations have begun in South Africa's Cape region following severe storms. Authorities are working to address the damage caused by the weather events.

stories.title: As barbed wire blocks kids from class, Palestinians stage ‘Freedom School’
stories.summary: Palestinian children from Umm al-Khair in the occupied West Bank organized a 'Freedom School' protest after settlers erected a barbed-wire fence blocking their access to school.

stories.title: To stay or to go? No good options for Lebanon’s displaced
stories.summary: Residents of southern Lebanon face the choice of staying home amid security threats or fleeing and risking deeper poverty, as displacement continues to affect the region.

stories.title: US, Mexican officials assigned to cartel case killed in car accident
stories.summary: MEXICO CITY, April 19 - Two U.S. officials and two Mexican officials assigned to combat cartel operations died in a car accident in the northern Mexican state of Chihuahua on Sunday, a U.S. Embassy sp

stories.title: Moroccans rally in rabat against Israel death penalty law
stories.summary: Thousands of demonstrators marched in Rabat, Morocco, on Sunday to denounce a new Israeli law that would permit the execution of Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. Protesters also reaffirmed their support for the Palestinian cause.

stories.title: Kenya: 'Everything Is On the Table' - Oburu On Pre-2027 Coalition Talks With UDA
stories.summary: ODM leader Oburu Oginga stated that "everything is on the table" in ongoing coalition negotiations with Kenya's ruling United Democratic Alliance ahead of the 2027 General Election. The talks come amid emerging cracks in the broad-based government arrangement.

stories.title: Kenya: Oburu Oginga Warns Against 'Reckless Tax Removal' Amid Fuel Price Pressure
stories.summary: ODM leader Oburu Oginga has cautioned against what he called the "reckless removal of taxes" in Kenya as pressure mounts on the government to further reduce fuel prices despite recent partial relief measures.

stories.title: Kenya: 'He Is Not the Pope' - Oburu Escalates Clash With Sifuna, Says Raila Was 'Fed Up' With Him
stories.summary: ODM leader Oburu Oginga has intensified the party's internal conflict with Secretary General Edwin Sifuna, stating that Sifuna "is not the Pope" and insisting on party discipline amid a dispute over Sifuna's potential removal from office.

stories.title: Kenya: NACADA Seizes Sh4.1mn Ethanol Haul in Runda Crackdown
stories.summary: Kenya's National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse seized illicit ethanol valued at over Sh4.1 million during a targeted operation in Runda Estate, Westlands Sub-County, Nairobi.

stories.title: Authorities urge evacuation of children from Kherson suburbs amid intensified shelling
stories.summary: Authorities in the Kherson community are urging parents to evacuate children from dangerous suburban areas as Russian shelling intensifies in the region.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Debunks Hidden Spending Claims, Clarifies World Bank Report
stories.summary: Nigeria's Minister of State for Finance Taiwo Oyedele has dismissed reports alleging hidden spending and federation revenue diversion, describing them as misinterpretations of the World Bank Nigeria Development Update.

stories.title: Nigeria: Enugu West Endorses Tinubu, Mbah As Nnamani Dismisses One Term Promises
stories.summary: Political leaders in Nigeria's Enugu West Senatorial District have endorsed President Tinubu and Governor Mbah for second terms. Former Senate President Ken Nnamani cautioned voters against trusting one-term promises from rival candidates.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu's Govt Planning to Reintegrate Repentant Terrorists Into Society - ADC Alleges
stories.summary: Nigeria's African Democratic Congress has alleged that the Tinubu administration is planning to reintegrate individuals it described as "repentant terrorists" back into society.

stories.title: Nigeria: ADC Slams Govt Over Plan to Reintegrate 800 'Repentant Terrorists'
stories.summary: The African Democratic Congress in Nigeria has criticized a reported government plan to reintegrate nearly 800 repentant terrorists into communities, warning it could undermine counterinsurgency efforts and endanger traumatized populations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Dismisses 'Hidden Spending' Claims, Says World Bank Report Misinterpreted
stories.summary: Nigeria's Finance Ministry has responded to allegations of hidden spending by stating that FAAC deductions reflect legitimate fiscal obligations. Officials say ongoing reforms are improving transparency and revenue distribution.

stories.title: Nigeria: El-Rufai Raises Alarm Over Alleged Plot to Tarnish His Reputation
stories.summary: Former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai has alleged a coordinated plot to tarnish his reputation following a report linking him to an alleged attack on a prosecution witness in Nigeria.

stories.title: Nigeria: Muslims Challenge Southwest Power Imbalance, Say 'No Muslim Candidate, No Vote'
stories.summary: Muslim groups in southwestern Nigeria are demanding greater political representation, noting that no Muslim currently serves as governor in any of the region's five states. They have adopted a "no Muslim candidate, no vote" stance.

stories.title: Nigeria: Sokoto, Unicef Forge Strategic Front Against Child Malnutrition
stories.summary: Sokoto State's health ministry and primary healthcare agency, in collaboration with UNICEF's Sokoto Field Office, have handed over critical nutrition supplies to the state government to treat thousands of children suffering from acute malnutrition.

stories.title: Nigeria: Delays, Referrals and Risk - What a Doctor's Death Reveals About Nigeria's Maternal Care Gaps
stories.summary: The death of a doctor in Nigeria has raised questions about post-delivery monitoring and the availability of intensive care services at facilities managing high-risk pregnancies, highlighting gaps in the country's maternal healthcare system.

stories.title: Video: Band closes Coachella festival set with Gaza and Iran visuals
stories.summary: The Strokes closed their Coachella festival set with a large-screen visual montage referencing US foreign interventions, CIA-backed government overthrows, and the ongoing conflicts in Iran and Gaza.

stories.title: The German refugees who found shelter in Yugoslavia
stories.summary: Historian Marie Janine Calic has documented the stories of Germans who fled to Yugoslavia after the Nazis seized power in 1933. The research sheds light on the refugees who found shelter in the Balkan country during that era.

stories.title: Nigeria: Inside the Growing Bird Strike Crisis Affecting Nigeria's Aviation Sector
stories.summary: Recurring bird strikes at Nigerian airports are exposing environmental and operational gaps in the country's aviation sector. The incidents are testing aviation safety systems across multiple airports.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's PM Abiy Ahmed Renews Call for Sea Access
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed reiterated his country's determination to secure direct sea access. Ethiopia is closely watching the port of Assab in neighboring Eritrea, located near the Ethiopian border.

stories.title: China’s Hesai adds colour to lidar as EV makers race to level up in self-driving tech
stories.summary: Shanghai-based Hesai Group, the world's largest vehicle lidar sensor manufacturer, unveiled a 6D full-colour lidar platform that detects colour to improve object identification for autonomous driving. The technology aims to enhance ranging and small-target detection capabilities.

stories.title: Uganda: Veteran Journalist Joe Nam Shot Dead in Kampala
stories.summary: Veteran journalist Joe Nam was shot dead by unknown assailants in Kampala, Uganda. Police confirmed the killing but have not yet identified the perpetrators.

stories.title: NBC poll: Trump approval at 37 percent as war divides voters
stories.summary: An NBC News poll found US President Donald Trump's approval rating has dropped to 37 percent, with 67 percent of respondents disapproving of his handling of the war with Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Denies 'Hidden Spending' Claims, Says World Bank Report Misinterpreted
stories.summary: Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Finance has denied claims of hidden spending and diversion of federation revenue, saying the allegations stem from a misinterpretation of findings in the latest World Bank Nigeria Development Update.

stories.title: Nigeria: Fela's Music Catalogue Not for Sale, Remains Family Property - Femi Kuti
stories.summary: Grammy-nominated musician Femi Kuti stated that the music catalogue of his late father, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, is not for sale. He affirmed that the works remain the exclusive property of the Kuti family.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland Pushes Back Against Foreign Stance, Reaffirms Sovereignty
stories.summary: The government of Somaliland has reaffirmed its sovereignty in response to a joint statement by several foreign ministers. Hargeisa stated that its status is grounded in facts and international law.

stories.title: Body of 32-year-old man found floating off Hong Kong park
stories.summary: A 32-year-old man with a history of mental illness was found dead floating in waters near Tsing Yi Northeast Park in Hong Kong. Firefighters recovered the body, and police said the cause of death will be determined by autopsy.

stories.title: Asia growth forecasts slashed as Iran war and tariffs threaten supply chains
stories.summary: International organizations have cut Asia-Pacific growth forecasts for 2025, citing rising costs from the US-Israel war on Iran and trade uncertainty threatening global supply chains. China posted better-than-expected first-quarter growth of 5 percent, providing some regional resilience.

stories.title: Portrait of a nation at war: ‘I am just too exhausted to care’
stories.summary: The current war has supplied no glue to hold the country together, and most Americans are just watching and worrying.

stories.title: Iran’s lesson for China, record-breaking Hong Kong Sevens: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: The article compiles weekend coverage including analysis of Iran's low-cost 358 missile effectiveness against U.S. assets, the Hong Kong Sevens rugby tournament results, and developments around the Strait of Hormuz closures.

stories.title: Hamas officials claim terror group ready to hand over small weapons, rifles to Gazan police - NYT
stories.summary: Two Hamas officials told The New York Times that the group's latest proposal involves surrendering thousands of small weapons and rifles used by its police and security agencies to a Gazan police force.

stories.title: Trump says US destroyer hit Iran cargo ship trying to evade blockade
stories.summary: The Iranian-flagged cargo ship, which had sailed from Malaysia, ignored warnings to stop, says the US president.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un oversees ballistic missile tests
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw ballistic missile tests and expressed satisfaction with the results. Kim described the tests as validation of years of work by a specialized missile warhead research group.

stories.title: UK condemns North Korean missile launches testing warheads containing cluster munitions
stories.summary: The United Kingdom condemned North Korea's ballistic missile launches on April 19, which tested warheads containing cluster munitions, calling them a breach of UN Security Council resolutions that destabilize regional peace and security.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo - Fresh Attacks Reported After New Round of Peace Talks
stories.summary: Drone and artillery attacks have been reported in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo despite new peace commitments made between AFC/M23 and the Congolese government during talks in Switzerland on April 17.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Denies Alleged Hidden Spending, Diversion of Federation Revenue
stories.summary: Nigeria's Federal Government has denied allegations of hidden spending and diversion of federation revenue, saying the claims reflect a misunderstanding of the country's fiscal system.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amnesty, CSOs Flay NBC Over Directive to Broadcasters
stories.summary: Amnesty International, civil society organizations, and former Nigerian Vice President Atiku Abubakar have criticized a recent advisory from the National Broadcasting Commission, calling it an attempt to stifle free speech and silence media dissent.

stories.title: New Zealand declares emergency in Wellington as record rainfall triggers flash floods
stories.summary: New Zealand declared a state of emergency in Wellington after record rainfall triggered flash flooding overnight. Residents in low-lying areas were urged to evacuate, and the national weather service issued its highest-level red warning indicating a threat to life.

stories.title: What is really happening in northern Nigeria
stories.summary: An analysis of northern Nigeria's security situation attributes the violence to an adaptive insurgency rather than a US-led conspiracy or a targeted 'Christian genocide.'

stories.title: Israeli forces demolishing towns in Lebanon buffer zone, report says
stories.summary: A Haaretz report states Israeli forces are systematically demolishing civilian homes, public buildings, and schools in a buffer zone in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire with Hezbollah. Contractors are reportedly being paid per structure destroyed.

stories.title: US captures Iranian cargo ship that tried to evade Hormuz blockade as new round of talks is prepared
stories.summary: The US Navy fired on and boarded the Iranian-flagged cargo ship M/V Touska in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, marking the first naval seizure since Washington imposed a blockade on Iranian ports a week earlier. Iran called the operation an "act of piracy" and vowed retaliation, casting doubt on a second round of peace talks planned for Monday in Islamabad.

stories.title: Video: Israeli soldier destroys Jesus statue in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: A photo of an Israeli soldier using a jackhammer to destroy a statue of Jesus on a cross in the Maronite Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon has gone viral, sparking widespread condemnation online.

stories.title: Bolivia runoff consolidates fragmentation: ruling party keeps two regions, opposition governs the rest
stories.summary: Runoff elections in five Bolivian departments on Sunday consolidated a fragmented political landscape. President Rodrigo Paz's Patria coalition retained only two of nine governorships nationwide, while seven were won by various opposition forces.

stories.title: Oil jumps over 4 percent after US seizes Iranian ship
stories.summary: Crude oil prices rose over 4 percent after the US seized an Iranian vessel near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has reimposed control over the strait, through which roughly 20 percent of global oil exports previously flowed.

stories.title: WSJ: UAE discusses economic lifeline with US officials
stories.summary: The UAE has opened discussions with US officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, about establishing an economic safety net in case the Iran conflict worsens, according to The Wall Street Journal.

stories.title: Low-cost ‘paper antenna’ paves way for large-scale 5G upgrade on Chinese warships: study
stories.summary: Chinese researchers developed a flexible 5G millimetre-wave antenna made from photo paper, reducing material costs by over 95 percent. The technology, designed for shipborne communications, could enable large-scale 5G adoption on Chinese naval vessels.

stories.title: Arrests fuel fears among Madagascar’s gen Z protesters that new regime no better than one they overthrew
stories.summary: Four Gen Z activists were arrested in Madagascar on April 12 after participating in a protest demanding the military regime set an election date. The detentions have fueled fears among young people that the junta, which seized power after large-scale Gen Z demonstrations last year, may prove no better than the government it replaced.

stories.title: Ukraine police chief: 9,000 officers fighting on front lines out of 100,000
stories.summary: National Police of Ukraine chief Ivan Vyhivskyi stated that over 100,000 officers currently serve in the force, with approximately 9,000 deployed to fight on the front lines.

stories.title: Netanyahu says conflict with Iran could shift at any moment
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the war with Iran is 'not over' and said the situation could shift at any moment, speaking alongside Argentine President Javier Milei at a joint news conference.

stories.title: Outrage after Israeli soldier desecrates statue of Jesus Christ in Lebanon
stories.summary: A photograph showing an Israeli soldier using a jackhammer to destroy a statue of Jesus Christ in the village of Debel in southern Lebanon has provoked widespread international condemnation.

stories.title: Tai Po fire probe: member alleges rigged proxy votes in management committee election - as it happened
stories.summary: A public inquiry into the deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong, heard testimony from witness Kong Cheung-fat, who alleged irregularities involving proxy votes during a management committee election. Kong was re-elected to the owners' corporation committee in September 2024, when former chairman Tang Kwok-kuen was voted out.
