stories.title: Ukraine pushes for Europe to build defense system against ballistic weapons
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Europe must develop its own defense system against ballistic weapons and that Ukraine is already in discussions with several countries on building such a system. The announcement was made on April 19 from Kyiv.

stories.title: Iran war escalates as Houthis threaten to sever Saudi oil exports
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement threatened to blockade the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean, potentially cutting off Saudi Arabia's remaining oil export route. The escalation followed Iranian drone attacks against US Navy vessels in the Strait of Hormuz after diplomatic efforts to end the conflict appeared to collapse.

stories.title: North Korea again tests cluster munitions in launch observed by Kim and his daughter
stories.summary: North Korea conducted a new cluster munitions test observed by leader Kim Jong Un and his daughter. Analysts suggest the Iran war, in which cluster munitions were used against Israeli cities, may have prompted the demonstration.

stories.title: Germany's Merz, Brazil's Lula stress close European-Brazilian cooperation
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva called for closer ties between Brazil and the European Union at the opening of the Hanover industrial fair on April 19. Both leaders emphasized the importance of European-Brazilian economic cooperation.

stories.title: Moscow continues nuclear cooperation with Tehran, report says
stories.summary: Russia continues developing the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant in Iran and is expanding industrial, energy, and space research cooperation with Tehran, according to former Russian International Affairs Council director Andrei Kortunov.

stories.title: Tehran warns conflict could resume at any moment
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that the conflict could escalate at any moment and said Tehran does not trust its adversaries, while affirming Iran is engaged in negotiations but prepared to act.

stories.title: LA woman arrested on charge of helping Iran traffic weapons to Sudan
stories.summary: An Iranian national and US permanent resident was arrested in Los Angeles on charges of brokering arms sales between Iran and Sudan, including drones, bombs, bomb fuses, and millions of rounds of ammunition.

stories.title: World weighs fate of Middle East ceasefire after US seizes Iranian cargo ship
stories.summary: Efforts toward a lasting Middle East ceasefire face uncertainty after the US seized an Iranian cargo ship. Iran has stated it would retaliate soon, raising doubts about the prospects for sustained peace negotiations.

stories.title: Iran rebuffs Trump announcement of new peace talks, state media reports
stories.summary: Iran rejected President Trump's announcement of new peace talks, according to the official IRNA news agency. Iranian state media cited excessive U.S. demands as the reason for refusing to engage in the proposed negotiations.

stories.title: Louisiana father kills 7 of his children and another child in shooting at house — police
stories.summary: A father in Louisiana shot and killed seven of his own children and one other child at a house. The children ranged in age from 3 to 11; their mother was critically injured. The gunman was killed by police after a chase.

stories.title: Oil prices surge amid mixed signals on US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged more than 7 percent as the US and Iran offered conflicting accounts regarding the status of ceasefire negotiations, increasing market uncertainty.

stories.title: LAX authorities arrest Iranian national attempting to traffic arms to Sudan for Islamic regime
stories.summary: Federal authorities arrested Shamim Mafi, a 44-year-old Iranian national, at Los Angeles International Airport on charges of arms trafficking. She allegedly attempted to smuggle drones, bombs, and millions of rounds of ammunition to Sudan on behalf of the Iranian government.

stories.title: ‘Like charcoal’: Wang Fuk Court residents sift through ashes for belongings
stories.summary: Residents of Wang Sun House in Hong Kong's fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court estate in Tai Po began returning under government supervision for three-hour sessions to retrieve belongings. Residents described blackened interiors and widespread ash, recovering items including bikes, figurines, and paintings from the scorched flats.

stories.title: Hong Kong reasserts role as safe haven in global finance amid Middle East turmoil
stories.summary: Amid the ongoing US-Israeli military conflict with Iran, Hong Kong is positioning itself as a safe-haven destination for global capital, gold investment, and property. Analysts suggest the seven-week Middle East conflict could redefine the city's role as an international financial center, with property demand holding firm despite global turmoil.

stories.title: India officials push for regional energy hub in Sri Lanka
stories.summary:
Indian officials called for the swift implementation of a proposed regional energy hub in Sri Lanka at the start of bilateral talks in Colombo on Sunday.
The planned oil hub in the northeastern port o

stories.title: China’s C919 sees delivery delays in 2026, with 3 units shipped in 3 months
stories.summary: Deliveries of China's domestically built C919 narrowbody airliner by the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (Comac) appear to be falling behind schedule, with only three units shipped to Chinese carriers in the first quarter of 2026. Observers cite engine supply issues, though analysts say Comac's focus on quality over speed is prudent.

stories.title: Fire destroys 1,000 ‘stilt’ homes in Malaysia’s Sabah, displacing thousands
stories.summary: A massive fire in Sandakan district, Sabah state, Malaysia, destroyed approximately 1,000 stilt homes in a coastal "water village" on Sunday, displacing thousands. The affected area housed some of Malaysia's poorest residents, including indigenous and stateless communities living in closely packed wooden structures built over water.

stories.title: Two officers suspended in Ukraine over claims they fled Kyiv shooting
stories.summary: Two Ukrainian police officers were suspended after video showed them fleeing the scene of a shooting in Kyiv. The footage captured the officers standing near a person on the ground before running as gunshots rang out.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Iran would have achieved nuclear bomb if Israel had not attacked over past 15 months
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Iran would have developed a nuclear weapon had Israel not carried out attacks over the past 15 months. He made the remarks during a meeting with torchlighters for Israel's 78th Independence Day ceremony, calling such a scenario a threat to the Jewish people.

stories.title: Syrskyi: Development of Military Law Enforcement Service's potential proves its effectiveness as combat component
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi stated that the Military Law Enforcement Service has proven its effectiveness as both a law enforcement and combat component of the armed forces. He emphasized that the VSP's expanded capabilities go beyond its traditional control and response functions.

stories.title: South Korea targets India, Vietnam in ‘co-prosperity’ push for trade and tech
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung began a six-day trip to India and Vietnam aimed at strengthening trade, technology, and strategic partnerships with the Global South. Lee arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for meetings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and business leaders before continuing to Vietnam.

stories.title: Why the Northern Metropolis needs more than one big push
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government faces growing pressure to advance the Northern Metropolis project, announced in 2021, with less than 15 months remaining in its current term. The megaproject aims to develop 30,000 hectares near the mainland China border into an innovation and technology hub to drive economic growth and housing supply.

stories.title: Security beefed up as Islamabad prepares for foreign delegations’ arrival amid anticipation of US-Iran talks
stories.summary:
Islamabad’s Red Zone was closed for traffic as the capital braces to welcome foreign delegations, police said on Sunday, with alternate traffic plans issued to facilitate citizens.
“Due to the arrival

stories.title: IDF warns southern Lebanese residents not to return amid truce, hits Hezbollah rocket launcher
stories.summary: The Israeli military warned residents of southern Lebanon not to return to their homes during the truce and struck a Hezbollah rocket launcher. Separately, Iran's envoy to Russia said Tehran ensures safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Eight children killed in Louisiana mass shooting, US police say
stories.summary: Eight children, aged one to 14, were killed in a mass shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana, according to local police. The gunman was fatally shot by officers following a car chase.

stories.title: US Navy destroyer fires on cargo vessel attempting to sail to Iranian port
stories.summary: The US Navy destroyer USS Spruance fired multiple rounds from its 5-inch MK 45 gun into the engine room of the Iranian-flagged cargo vessel Touska to disable its propulsion. The ship had been attempting to sail to an Iranian port in defiance of the US blockade, according to US Central Command.

stories.title: China woman returns to hometown to raise 60,000 venomous snakes, earns US$146,000 annually
stories.summary: A woman surnamed Qin from Guilin in southern China's Guangxi province has drawn widespread online attention for raising over 60,000 venomous snakes, including more than 50,000 five-step snakes. Born in 1995, she returned to her village after university to help her father and now earns over one million yuan (approximately US$147,000) annually.

stories.title: What’s behind the US army’s decision to raise enlistment age to 42?
stories.summary: The US Army has raised its maximum enlistment age to 42 in an effort to address persistent recruitment shortfalls in recent years.

stories.title: At least 170 soldiers killed, 54 disabled due to war over past year, Defense Ministry reports
stories.summary: Israel's Defense Ministry reported that at least 170 soldiers have been killed and 54 disabled due to war over the past year. The number of bereaved families in Israel now exceeds 59,000, with a significant increase since the Hamas attack on October 7.

stories.title: Iran says it will defend ports, ships amid tensions
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned the United States against threatening Iranian ports and ships, calling Washington's demands irrational. Speaking with his Pakistani counterpart, Araghchi said Iran would use all its capacities to protect its national security and interests.

stories.title: Israeli army says photo of soldier damaging Jesus statue is authentic
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that a widely circulated photograph showing a soldier damaging a statue of Jesus in southern Lebanon is authentic. The military announced it has opened an investigation into the incident, which sparked outrage on social media.

stories.title: US says it seized Iranian ship that tried to break blockade; Tehran vows to retaliate
stories.summary: US forces seized an Iranian-flagged ship that allegedly attempted to break the naval blockade near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran accused the US of 'armed piracy' and vowed retaliation, while the UK warned of miscalculation risks in the strait.

stories.title: Tehran warns of ‘significant costs’ if pressure continues
stories.summary: Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref warned that restricting Iran's oil exports would carry "significant costs" for global energy markets. Writing on X, Aref stated that security in the Strait of Hormuz is not free and called for an open oil market for all nations.

stories.title: European Commission believes elections in Hungary serve as warning for allies of Trump and Putin
stories.summary: Executive Vice-President of the European Commission Teresa Ribera stated that the election defeat of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is a warning for conservative European leaders who may be tem

stories.title: In 45-minute phone call with Pezeshkian, PM Shehbaz reaffirms Pakistan’s commitment to advancing regional peace
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone for 45 minutes with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to advancing regional peace. The call came after U.S. President Trump confirmed American officials were headed to Islamabad for another round of talks with Iran, following inconclusive direct U.S.-Iran negotiations held there on April 11–12.

stories.title: ‘We’re Catholic first’: Sunday mass attendees weigh in on Trump’s feud with Pope Leo
stories.summary: Catholic churchgoers in the Atlanta area expressed mixed reactions to the ongoing rhetorical conflict between President Donald Trump and Pope Leo. Congregants at the Catholic Church of Saint Monica in Duluth, Georgia, weighed their religious faith against political loyalties.

stories.title: Israeli military publishes map of new deployment line in Lebanon, bringing dozens of villages under its control
stories.summary: The Israeli military published a map showing its new deployment line inside Lebanon, bringing dozens of mostly abandoned villages under Israeli control. The map was released days after a U.S.-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah took effect following the first direct Israeli-Lebanese talks in decades on April 14.

stories.title: China warns strong El Nino this year may worsen global fossil fuel crisis
stories.summary: Chinese government scientists warned that a strong El Niño event expected this year could increase global fossil fuel demand, compounding price pressures from the ongoing Iran crisis. The climate phenomenon can cause droughts or extreme flooding, potentially forcing hydropower stations to reduce output and raising reliance on fossil fuels.

stories.title: Asia’s EV revolution shifts into overdrive with Iran war oil shock
stories.summary: Rising oil prices driven by the conflict in Iran are accelerating electric vehicle adoption across Asia. Consumers and businesses in countries including Nepal are increasingly turning to EVs, with early adopters citing insulation from fuel price volatility as a key advantage.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran may skip talks as tensions rise over US ship seizure
stories.summary: Iran may skip a new round of US talks brokered by Pakistan amid rising tensions following the US seizure of an Iranian ship near the Strait of Hormuz, hours after President Trump announced sending negotiators to Islamabad.

stories.title: Ukraine agrees on ten-year defense deals with three Gulf states, receives interest from 11 more countries – Zelensky

stories.title: Outrage after photo shows Israeli soldier smashing Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: A photograph circulated on social media showing an Israeli soldier using a jackhammer to destroy a statue of Jesus in southern Lebanon. The image provoked widespread condemnation online, with critics highlighting what they called Western silence on Israeli attacks against religious symbols and sites.

stories.title: Australia news live: ‘weeks’ to restore production at Geelong refinery after blaze, Viva says; Chalmers warns of ‘big risks’ to inflation and growth
stories.summary: Australia's Viva Energy said it would take weeks to restore production at its Geelong refinery following a fire. Meanwhile, Treasurer Jim Chalmers warned of inflation and growth risks as global oil prices surged nearly 8% amid fading hopes for a peace deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli soldier filmed smashing Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: An image of an Israeli soldier using a jackhammer to destroy a statue of Jesus on a cross went viral after being shared on social media. The statue was reportedly located in Debel, a Maronite Christian village in southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces have maintained positions since launching operations on March 2.

stories.title: Israeli military publishes map of south Lebanon territory under its control
stories.summary: The Israeli military published a map showing territory it controls in southern Lebanon, encompassing dozens of mostly abandoned villages. Israel is establishing a buffer zone intended to prevent Hezbollah attacks on its northern border.

stories.title: Vance will lead US team to Iran talks in Pakistan: White House
stories.summary: The White House announced that Vice President JD Vance will lead a U.S. delegation to Pakistan for talks with Iran. The current U.S.-Iran ceasefire is scheduled to expire on April 22.

stories.title: Israeli forces wound boys in Hebron, man shot near Jenin
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and wounded two teenage boys near Hebron and a young man near Jenin in the occupied West Bank. Seventeen-year-old Mahab Balal sustained a serious head wound in the Ras al-Joura area and required emergency surgery. Another boy, Youssef Mansieh, was hit by shrapnel in the head.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Iran vows response after US destroyer fires on cargo ship
stories.summary: Iran vowed military retaliation after a U.S. destroyer fired on an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman as it attempted to evade a U.S. naval blockade. Tehran's military command condemned the attack as "armed piracy" and warned of an imminent response.

stories.title: India has splurged billions on metro trains. But where are the commuters?
stories.summary: India has invested billions of dollars in metro rail systems across multiple cities, but ridership remains well below projections. Experts attribute the low usage to inadequate last-mile connectivity and high fares.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of ceasefire breach, vows retaliation over ship attack
stories.summary: Iran's joint military command accused the United States of violating a ceasefire by firing on an Iranian commercial vessel traveling from China to Iran in the Gulf of Oman. A spokesperson for Khatam al-Anbiya condemned the attack as "armed piracy" and warned that Iran's armed forces would retaliate.

stories.title: 'They told me he was dead': Children born near Kenyan army base learn truth about UK soldier dads
stories.summary: A DNA and legal project has identified the biological fathers of 20 children born near a British military base in Kenya. The fathers are UK soldiers who had been stationed at the base.

stories.title: FBI Director Kash Patel 'paranoid' he is next to be fired from Trump administration - report
stories.summary: Patel's fears come after several prominent figures were fired from the Trump administration, including former US Army chief of staff Randy George and former attorney-general Pam Bondi.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Izium with MLRS, three civilians injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the city of Izium in the Kharkiv region using a multiple launch rocket system (MLRS), injuring three civilians.

stories.title: ABF poised to reveal result of Primark and food business demerger plan
stories.summary: Associated British Foods is expected to announce whether it will proceed with a demerger separating Primark from its food businesses, including Kingsmill and Twinings. Retail analysts suggest the split would make strategic sense given challenging conditions in both the fashion and food sectors.

stories.title: Tehran has not decided whether to join new talks with U.S. in Pakistan: Iranian state media
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Tehran has not decided whether to participate in a new round of U.S.-Iran negotiations in Pakistan. Fars News Agency cited a source stating that the lifting of a U.S. blockade on Iranian ports is a precondition for Iran's participation.

stories.title: Art on trial - a sculptor's arrest highlights new extremes for censorship in China
stories.summary: Chinese sculptor Gao Zhen was arrested and retroactively punished for artworks created 15 years ago, alarming international rights groups. The case highlights an intensifying climate of censorship and artistic repression in China.

stories.title: Police scrap plan for officers to join audience of contentious right-wing talk show
stories.summary: Israeli police canceled a plan to send approximately 70 officers to join the studio audience of Channel 14's "The Patriots," a right-wing talk show. The force was also ordered to address a complaint filed against the channel's pundits.

stories.title: Zelensky announces new security agreements with partners
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is preparing new security cooperation agreements with international partners, with signings expected the following week. No specific countries or details of the agreements were disclosed.

stories.title: Woman charged in US with trafficking arms to Sudan for Iranian government
stories.summary: U.S. federal prosecutors charged Shamim Mafi, a 44-year-old Iranian national and Woodland Hills, California resident, with brokering arms sales to Sudan on behalf of Tehran. She was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport and allegedly facilitated the sale of Iranian-manufactured drones, bombs, and ammunition.

stories.title: Iranian ship seized by US Navy after attempting to pass through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy seized an Iranian ship named TOUSKA after it attempted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. According to President Trump, the vessel was given a warning before a U.S. Navy ship engaged it.

stories.title: Religious scholar Engineer Muhammad Ali Mirza survives attack in Jhelum
stories.summary: Religious scholar Engineer Muhammad Ali Mirza survived an attack by an unidentified gunman outside the Quran & Sunnat Research Academy in Jhelum, Pakistan. The attacker was killed in retaliatory firing. Mirza had previously survived assassination attempts in 2021 and earlier in 2025.

stories.title: Louisiana mass shooting: Eight of 10 victims are children, police say; suspect shot dead
stories.summary: A gunman killed eight children, ages one to 14, and wounded two others in a domestic-related mass shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana, on Sunday. The suspect was fatally shot by police following a vehicle chase after fleeing the scene.

stories.title: Trump says US representatives heading to Islamabad, will be ‘there tomorrow evening for negotiations’ with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that U.S. representatives were heading to Islamabad for a second round of negotiations with Iran. Trump warned that if Iran does not accept what he called a fair deal, the U.S. would strike Iranian power plants and bridges.

stories.title: Hapoel Tel Aviv heads to Euroleague quarterfinals
stories.summary: Hapoel Tel Aviv advanced to the Euroleague basketball quarterfinals despite losing to Monaco. Meanwhile, Maccabi Tel Aviv shifted its focus to the Israeli domestic league, and Hapoel Jerusalem returned to action with a victory.

stories.title: Bulgaria's pro-Russian former president takes strong lead
stories.summary: Exit polls indicate former Bulgarian president Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria coalition leads the country's parliamentary election but may fall short of a governing majority. The vote, marked by low turnout, is Bulgaria's eighth election in five years amid persistent political fragmentation and instability.

stories.title: Global leftists rally in Spain hoping to spark resurgence against far right
stories.summary: Thousands of left-leaning political figures and activists gathered in Barcelona, Spain, over the weekend to discuss strategies for countering the rise of far-right movements globally. Topics included reforming the UN Security Council and taxing billionaires.

stories.title: Zelenskyy slams oil sanctions relief for Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized the easing of oil sanctions on Russia, claiming it provides Moscow with approximately $10 billion in resources. Zelenskyy stated that revenue is directly converted into new military strikes against Ukraine.

stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Ukraine's long-range strikes caused an estimated $2.3 billion in losses to Russia's oil sector in March 2026. The strikes targeted Russian oil infrastructure as part of Ukraine's ongoing campaign against Russian energy assets.

stories.title: Russian attacks kill at least two as Ukraine strikes a Russian drone factory
stories.summary: A large-scale nighttime drone strike on Chernihiv in northern Ukraine killed a 16-year-old boy and wounded four others, according to local military officials. Separately, Ukrainian forces struck a Russian drone manufacturing facility. At least two people were reported killed in Russian attacks overall.

stories.title: Israel says to use 'full force' in Lebanon despite truce if soldiers face threat
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel would use "full force" in Lebanon if its soldiers face threats, despite the existing truce. Katz reiterated plans to demolish houses along the border as part of establishing a security zone in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Rumen Radev looks set to win Bulgarian Parliamentary election
stories.summary: Exit polls from Bulgaria's parliamentary election indicate former president Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party leading with approximately 37% of the vote. This is more than double the nearest competitor's share, though Radev will likely need coalition partners to form a government.

stories.title: Trump cannot settle for uranium removal in efforts to remove Iran’s nuclear threat - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that President Trump should not settle for uranium removal alone in negotiations with Iran, asserting that Iran's nuclear and missile programs remain unresolved threats. The piece contends that the U.S.-Israel military campaign has made progress but that key dangers require further urgent action.

stories.title: IDF says photo of soldier destroying Jesus statue in Lebanon is genuine, vows action
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces confirmed that a photograph showing a soldier destroying a statue of Jesus in Lebanon is genuine. The military said it views the incident with "great severity" and pledged to handle it through the chain of command and help restore the statue.

stories.title: KP CM Afridi says conveyed to Imran that if he gives go-ahead, ‘we will be in Islamabad the next day’
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi told a rally in Mardan that he informed imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan of his readiness to lead supporters to Islamabad. Khan reportedly instructed him to consult allied political leaders before any action.

stories.title: Iranian American woman arrested in Los Angeles for alleged arms trafficking
stories.summary: Shamim Mafi, a 44-year-old Iranian American woman from Woodland Hills, California, was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport on Saturday night. Federal prosecutors allege she trafficked weapons to contacts in Africa, including Sudan, on behalf of the Iranian government.

stories.summary: U.S. Central Command released video showing a guided-missile destroyer firing on the Iranian-flagged ship Touska near the Strait of Hormuz. The incident marks a significant escalation in U.S.-Iran maritime tensions in the region.

stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announced an investigation into an alleged incident in which a soldier smashed a Jesus statue in the Maronite Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon. stories.summary: Israel has stated it will use "full force" in Lebanon if its soldiers face threats, despite an existing truce. The military has been ordered to demolish any structures or roads found to be booby-trapped in the area.

stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called for a comprehensive overhaul of police response protocols, recruitment, and training after a terrorist attack on April 18 in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district. stories.summary: Pakistan and Qatar are in advanced discussions for the supply of at least four LNG cargoes, which would transit through the Strait of Hormuz. The talks follow disruptions to Pakistan's LNG imports and growing domestic electricity shortfalls ahead of summer.

stories.title: Pakistan pledges to mediate for ‘lasting peace’ in region
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reaffirmed Islamabad's commitment to mediating regional tensions after a phone call with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Sharif said Pakistan is ready to facilitate diplomatic efforts aimed at easing the ongoing crisis and securing regional stability.

stories.title: Eight people remain in hospital after Kyiv shooting, mayor says
stories.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Sunday that eight people, including a child, remain hospitalized after a shooting in the Ukrainian capital that killed six people.

stories.title: New petition asks High Court to freeze Gofman appointment as Mossad chief
stories.summary: A new petition was filed with Israel's High Court seeking to block Maj.-Gen. Roman Gofman's appointment as Mossad chief. The petition cites alleged flaws in the vetting process and serious allegations connected to the Elmakayes affair.

stories.title: CoE secretary general responds to deadly Kyiv shooting, urges end to violence
stories.summary: Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset responded to the April 18 terrorist attack in Kyiv, which killed six people, urging an end to violence.

stories.title: UK police investigating Iran link to arson attacks on Jewish sites in London
stories.summary: UK Metropolitan Police counterterror officers are investigating whether a series of arson attacks on synagogues and other Jewish sites in London are linked to Iranian proxies. The fires also targeted a Persian-language media company. No injuries have been reported, but the UK's chief rabbi said British Jews face a campaign of violence and intimidation.

stories.title: Salah scores in Merseyside derby as Liverpool win to boost European hopes
stories.summary: Mohamed Salah scored Liverpool's opening goal in the Merseyside derby against Everton, while Virgil van Dijk netted an injury-time winner to secure the victory and strengthen Liverpool's pursuit of European competition qualification.

stories.title: Charges against PM’s top aides could be dropped as prosecution fails to extradite Einhorn
stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors told a court that the refusal of witness Einhorn to return to Israel from Serbia could lead to the collapse of a witness intimidation case against two aides to Prime Minister Netanyahu—Jonatan Urich and Ofer Golan. Charges against the defendants may be dropped due to the failed extradition effort.

stories.title: Eight children killed in Lousiana mass shooting - NBC
stories.summary: Eight children were killed and ten total were shot in a mass shooting in Louisiana stemming from a domestic dispute, according to NBC. The victims ranged in age from 1 to 14.

stories.title: IDF establishes position in Ait a Shaab, former Hezbollah stronghold
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces established a new military position in Ait a Shaab in southern Lebanon, a village previously considered a Hezbollah stronghold. Journalists visited the site with IDF personnel.

stories.title: How Milei brought Judeo-Christian civilization home to Jerusalem - comment
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei signed the Isaac Accords with Israel during his visit to Jerusalem. The agreement is framed as promoting freedom and democracy, drawing on Milei's stated inspiration from Jewish tradition.

stories.title: Netanyahu claims that Israel is fighting a ‘battle of civilisation’ against Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu characterized the conflict with Iran as a "battle of civilization against barbarism" during a visit by Argentine President Javier Milei. Netanyahu said Israel and the United States are jointly confronting what he called Iran's tyranny and its threat to global stability.

stories.title: Ukraine asks Turkey to arrange Zelensky-Putin meeting with Erdogan and Trump
stories.summary: Ukraine has asked Turkey to help organize a meeting between President Zelensky and Russian President Putin, potentially with the participation of Turkish President Erdogan and U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: Israeli ministers celebrate re-establishment of Sa-Nur West Bank settlement
stories.summary: Israeli government ministers celebrated the re-establishment of Sa-Nur, a West Bank settlement. Sa-Nur is one of four former settlements recently approved for reconstruction by the Israeli government, roughly two decades after settlers were evacuated from the sites.

stories.title: Did the US misjudge Iran? A military strategist answers
stories.summary: Military strategist Bryan Clark analyzed whether the United States misjudged Iran's capabilities and intentions. Clark discussed shifting war aims and escalation risks, questioning whether Iran now poses a greater threat to the U.S. than previously assessed.

stories.title: Israel wins 3 medals in European Judo Championships, including gold for Raz Hershko
stories.summary: Israeli judoka Raz Hershko, an Olympic silver medalist, won gold at the European Judo Championships, her second continental title and fifth consecutive medal at the event. Israel won a total of three medals at the tournament.

stories.title: Republican senator criticizes Trump’s ‘holy war’ with Pope Leo
stories.summary: Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana publicly criticized President Donald Trump's ongoing feud with Pope Leo XIV, calling it a "holy war" and a distraction. Kennedy, a longtime Trump supporter and ally of the MAGA movement, made the remarks during a Fox News interview on Saturday.

stories.title: France and Greece to renew defence pact for another five years
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron will travel to Greece next week to renew a bilateral defence pact for another five years, a Greek government official confirmed on Sunday. The renewal comes against the backdrop of the ongoing war in Iran and broader European security concerns.

stories.title: Iran says final deal still far off as Hormuz Strait shuttered
stories.summary: Iran stated that a final deal with the United States remains far off as the Strait of Hormuz remains shuttered. A two-week ceasefire between the two sides is set to expire on April 22 unless renewed.

stories.title: Allies fear a rushed US-Iran framework deal could backfire, leaving technical deadlock
stories.summary: U.S. allies have expressed concern that Washington may rush into a superficial framework deal with Iran that could backfire. They worry such an agreement could lock in unresolved issues and entrench deeper technical deadlocks in negotiations.

stories.title: Donald Trump says U.S. officials will be in Pakistan ‘for negotiations’
stories.summary: President Trump announced U.S. officials would travel to Pakistan for negotiations, reiterating an offer to Iran and threatening to destroy Iranian power plants and bridges if the deal is rejected.

stories.title: Trump says US representatives heading to Islamabad, will be ‘there tomorrow evening for negotiations’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that U.S. representatives were heading to Islamabad for a second round of negotiations with Iran, warning that the U.S. would destroy Iranian power plants and bridges if Tehran rejected the deal.

stories.title: Pakistan tightens security in Islamabad ahead of U.S.-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan heightened security in Islamabad ahead of a second round of U.S.-Iran talks, with President Trump confirming that American negotiators would arrive on Monday, April 21, 2026, to resume discussions on ending the war with Iran.

stories.title: Iran replenishes launchers at higher rate than pre-war, guards commander says
stories.summary: The commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards Aerospace Force said Sunday that Iran now replenishes and updates its missile and drone launchers faster than before the war with the U.S. and Israel. The statement was reported by Iranian outlet Nournews.

stories.title: Iran to resume international flights from Mashhad airport on April 20
stories.summary: Iran announced the resumption of international flights from Mashhad airport on April 20, after Iranian airports had been closed since the outbreak of war with Israel and the United States on February 28.

stories.title: Israeli forces burn homes in south Lebanon town
stories.summary: Israeli forces set fire to homes in the southern Lebanese town of Qantara, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The incident was reported from Marjeyoun district amid ongoing tensions despite a fragile ceasefire reached days earlier.

stories.title: Pope Leo prays at Catholic shrine in Angola that was a centre of African slave trade
stories.summary: Pope Leo visited the Sanctuary of Mama Muxima in Angola, a Catholic shrine located at a historic hub of the African slave trade under Portuguese colonial rule. The American pope reflected on the "sorrow and great suffering" endured by Angolans over centuries. The site became a major pilgrimage destination after reported Marian apparitions around 1833.

stories.title: Antalya forum: Sybiha raises alarm over Russia recruiting African mercenaries
stories.summary: At the Antalya Diplomacy Forum, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha raised concerns about Russia recruiting mercenaries across Africa during bilateral meetings with representatives of African nations.

stories.title: Turkey’s FM accuses Israel of using security ‘as an excuse to occupy more land’
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's government of using security concerns as a pretext to expand territorial control. Fidan specifically alleged Israel is attempting to create permanent facts on the ground in Lebanon while U.S.-Iran negotiations are ongoing.

stories.title: Culture Minister Miki Zohar questioned by police in Histadrut corruption probe
stories.summary: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar was questioned by police as part of a corruption investigation involving the Histadrut labor union. Zohar, a member of Prime Minister Netanyahu's Likud party, is the latest figure interrogated in a probe into an alleged bribery network linking the union, municipalities, and government officials.

stories.title: Iran says final deal still far off as Hormuz Strait shuttered
stories.summary: Iran stated that a final deal remains far off as a temporary ceasefire nears expiration. Tehran declared the Strait of Hormuz — through which a fifth of global oil and LNG transits — open after a ceasefire was agreed to halt Israel's war with Iran-allied Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Reservists Party vows to form Zionist government, discusses potential alliance with Gantz
stories.summary: Israel's Reservists Party announced efforts to form a Zionist government and disclosed ongoing talks about a potential alliance with Benny Gantz's Blue and White party ahead of the 2026 elections.

stories.title: Iran rejects second round of talks, cites ‘excessive’ US demands
stories.summary: Iran has refused to participate in a second round of negotiations with the United States, accusing Washington of excessive demands, shifting positions, and maintaining a naval blockade that Tehran considers a breach of the ceasefire. The announcement was reported by Iran's state news agency IRNA.

stories.title: WATCH: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meets with President of Argentina Javier Milei
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with Argentine President Javier Milei during Milei's visit to Israel. A key announcement during the visit was the planned launch of a new direct El Al flight route between Israel and Argentina.

stories.title: Trump again threatens Iran as he orders negotiators to Pakistan
stories.summary: President Trump announced he is sending a delegation led by Vice President JD Vance to Pakistan on Monday for ceasefire talks with Iran, which expire Wednesday. Trump again threatened strikes on Iranian infrastructure if no deal is reached.

stories.title: Hamas rebuffs ‘trap’ disarmament plan as Israeli violations stall ceasefire process
stories.summary: Hamas rejected a US-backed "Board of Peace" proposal calling for the group's disarmament, describing it as a "trap" aimed at sparking civil war in Gaza. Palestinian sources told Middle East Eye that Hamas cited ongoing Israeli violations of the first phase of the ceasefire as justification.

stories.title: Iran and Israel: From friends to enemies
stories.summary: Israel and the United States have been engaged in armed conflict with Iran since February 28. The article traces the historical arc of Israeli-Iranian relations, which shifted from a period of cooperation and friendship to the current open hostilities.

stories.title: Civil resistance activists detained in Manchester over alleged plan to raid high-end stores
stories.summary: UK police arrested seven members of the activist group Take Back Power in Salford, Greater Manchester, on suspicion of conspiracy to steal from high-end stores. The group, which campaigns for higher taxes on the super-rich, said the arrests took place during a training session. Six women and one man were detained.

stories.title: Ukraine FM: Ukraine asked Türkiye to host Zelenskyy-Putin talks — but “Putin is hiding”
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Ukraine has asked Turkey to host direct talks between President Zelensky and Russian President Putin. Sybiha noted that Turkish President Erdoğan and U.S. President Trump could also participate, but stated that Putin has not agreed to the meeting.

stories.title: Magyar announces renewed cooperation following talks with European Commission
stories.summary: Péter Magyar, Hungary's incoming prime minister, announced renewed cooperation with the European Commission following technical meetings in Brussels. He said his government would work with the EU to unblock frozen funds allocated to Hungary.

stories.title: Another attempted arson attack at Jewish site in London, charity says
stories.summary: The Community Security Trust reported an attempted arson attack at a synagogue in north London, the latest in a series of arson incidents targeting Jewish sites across the British capital in recent weeks.

stories.title: Intemperate Trump brings chaos and confusion to Iran talks
stories.summary: The U.S. announced it would send officials to Islamabad for further talks with Iran just 24 hours after Iran again closed the Strait of Hormuz. The decision signals to Tehran that its control over the strategic waterway remains a powerful bargaining asset. Analysts note Trump's unpredictable diplomatic style has reinforced Iran's resolve to act cautiously.

stories.title: Israel 'preparing attacks on Iran energy infrastructure'
stories.summary: Israel is reportedly preparing to strike Iranian energy infrastructure ahead of a possible resumption of US-Iran negotiations. The reported planning raises concerns about escalation during a sensitive diplomatic period.

stories.title: Israel publishes map of s. Lebanon territory under its control
stories.summary: The Israeli army published a map showing the territory it controls in southern Lebanon, with soldiers deployed and instructed to destroy what Israel identifies as Hezbollah infrastructure in the area.

stories.title: Ukraine police chief resigns after officers allegedly fled deadly shooting
stories.summary: Ukraine's police chief resigned after officers allegedly fled the scene of a deadly shooting. The officers involved have been suspended, and authorities have launched an investigation into their conduct.

stories.title: Allies fear a rushed US-Iran framework deal could backfire, leaving technical deadlock - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis warns that Washington risks locking in a superficial framework agreement with Iran covering nuclear issues and sanctions relief, which could then face months or years of technically complex follow-on negotiations that may stall.

stories.title: UN warns that 22 million at risk in Yemen amid funding shortages
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that 22 million people in Yemen are at risk due to funding shortages. Aid organizations have been forced to scale back vital programs, with children particularly affected by reduced access and increased humanitarian needs.

stories.title: US energy chief says Iran talks progressing, predicts ‘nice end’ to conflict
stories.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated on Fox News that negotiations with Iran are progressing behind the scenes and predicted a positive outcome. Wright praised President Trump's negotiating approach, describing him as a creative negotiator who applies pressure.

stories.title: Head of Patrol Police Zhukov resigns after terrorist attack in Kyiv
stories.summary: Yevhenii Zhukov, head of Ukraine's Patrol Police Department, resigned following the terrorist attack in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district on Saturday.

stories.title: Syria must shift from aid to development, minister says
stories.summary: Syria's Social Affairs Minister Hind Kabawat called for a shift from emergency humanitarian aid to long-term development to address widespread poverty. She warned about significant funding gaps hindering the transition.

stories.title: Israel’s symbolic strikes on bridges and high-rises show limits of military power - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines Israel's strikes on bridges and high-rises in Gaza and Lebanon, arguing these are largely symbolic actions that reveal the limits of Israeli military power as Hezbollah and Hamas maintain influence in both regions.

stories.title: Allies back Starmer as Mandelson’s Epstein links leave the UK leader fighting for his job
stories.summary: Senior UK Cabinet ministers rallied behind Prime Minister Keir Starmer amid a crisis over his appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador to the United States. Mandelson reportedly failed security checks, and his ties to the late Jeffrey Epstein have fueled controversy. Starmer faced Parliament on Monday to defend his leadership.

stories.title: Trumps sends delegation to Pakistan for possible new round of Iran war talks
stories.summary: A U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance, envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner is returning to Islamabad, Pakistan, for possible talks aimed at ending the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported Tehran has not decided to send negotiators while the naval blockade persists. President Trump repeated threats against Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Israeli attacks on healthcare across Iran, Lebanon and Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has carried out attacks targeting healthcare infrastructure in Iran, Lebanon, and Gaza. Details on specific facilities and casualties remain limited in the initial report.

stories.title: Weary Iranians expect no postwar respite under entrenched regime
stories.summary: Iranian citizens expressed concern that a potential agreement with the United States could strengthen the ruling regime rather than improve their lives. Many fear their rights will be further eroded while the war's impact on the economy and infrastructure persists.

stories.title: What would it take for the Iran-US talks to succeed?
stories.summary: Political scientist Mohsen Milani and former White House official Elisa Ewers discussed the prospects and obstacles facing ongoing US-Iran negotiations, examining what conditions could lead to a successful outcome.

stories.title: War update: 84 clashes on front line since morning, most fights in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 84 clashes along the front line since the morning, with the heaviest Russian activity concentrated in the Pokrovsk direction.

stories.title: Bulgaria: Pro-Russian Radev leading after parliamentary vote, exit polls show
stories.summary: Exit polls following Bulgaria's eighth parliamentary election in five years show former President Rumen Radev's new pro-Russian, left-leaning party in a commanding lead. Radev, a former fighter pilot, stepped down as president in January.

stories.title: Albanese slams Israeli army as ‘depraved’ after abuse of child
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese called the Israeli military "the most depraved army" after footage emerged showing soldiers abusing a child in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills man in central Gaza as genocide death toll reaches 72,551
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike on Salah al-Din Street northeast of Nuseirat camp in central Gaza killed Ayman Khaled Abu Hasna, 38, and wounded several others. Medics at Al-Awda Hospital confirmed the death. Gaza health officials report the cumulative Palestinian death toll has reached 72,551.

stories.title: Hamas rebuffs ‘trap’ disarmament plan as Israeli violations stall ceasefire process
stories.summary: Hamas rejected a U.S.-backed disarmament proposal, calling it a "trap," citing Israel's failure to implement the first phase of an existing ceasefire agreement. Sources said Hamas also raised concerns over security arrangements in Gaza. The stalled ceasefire process has been marked by continued Israeli military operations, including strikes in Khan Younis.

stories.title: Female IDF soldiers required to wear long pants at Jerusalem Marathon during heat wave
stories.summary: Female IDF soldiers were ordered to wear long pants during the Jerusalem Marathon despite a heat wave, while male soldiers wore shorts. The incident drew criticism over religious coercion in the military. The IDF denied a dress code difference and said it would investigate.

stories.title: Spanish Prime Minister calls for EU to break Association Agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called on the European Union to suspend its Association Agreement with Israel, arguing that a government violating international law cannot be an EU partner.

stories.title: Israel to use full force in Lebanon if soldiers 'face threat'
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz threatened to order the Israeli army to use full force in Lebanon if its soldiers face any threats, despite a 10-day ceasefire being in effect.

stories.title: Met Police investigate potential Iran links to London arson attacks
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating potential Iranian links to a series of arson attacks in the city. The most recent incident targeted Kenton United Synagogue, a Jewish site in northwest London, causing minor damage.

stories.title: Israel is missing a NIS 180 billion growth engine - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlights that Arab citizens remain underrepresented in Israel's business sector, particularly in higher-paying, higher-quality roles. The article estimates this underrepresentation costs the Israeli economy approximately NIS 180 billion in unrealized growth.

stories.title: Mass shooting rampage in Louisiana leaves eight children dead and others wounded
stories.summary: At least eight children, aged 18 months to 14 years, were killed in a mass shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana. Two women were shot in the head but survived, and a young boy was injured jumping from a roof. The suspect was fatally shot by police.

stories.title: There is already certain level of competition on global stage for Ukraine's attention, opportunities to cooperate – Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that multiple countries are competing for Ukraine's attention and cooperation on the global stage, reflecting Kyiv's growing international agency and appeal as a partner.

stories.title: Argentina's Milei lands in Israel to open embassy in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Far-right Argentine President Javier Milei arrived in Israel to open an Argentine embassy in Jerusalem and participate in Israeli Independence Day celebrations.

stories.title: Israel unveils new military occupation line inside southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel published a map showing a new military deployment line extending 5 to 10 kilometres inside southern Lebanon, placing dozens of villages under its control. The move came days after a US-backed ceasefire with Hezbollah took effect, indicating Israel intends to maintain a buffer zone beyond its border.

stories.title: From Sudan to Gaza, becoming 'Singapore' means choosing to comply
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Khalid Albaih examines how nations such as Sudan and Gaza are pressured to emulate Singapore's model of compliance in exchange for stability. The article references Iranian missile strikes on Abu Dhabi in February 2026 as evidence of the limits of political submission.

stories.title: 8 children between 1 and 14 killed in Louisiana mass shooting, police say
stories.summary: Eight children were killed in a domestic-related mass shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana, on Sunday. The victims ranged in age from one to about 14 years old, according to Shreveport police spokesperson Chris Bordelon.

stories.title: 8 children killed after shootings in Louisiana, police say
stories.summary: A gunman in Shreveport, Louisiana, killed eight children ranging in age from one to about 14 in domestic-related shootings at multiple homes on Sunday. Two adults were also shot. The suspect fled in a stolen car and was fatally shot by police following a chase.

stories.title: Jesy Nelson issues plea over stolen car containing twins’ medical equipment
stories.summary: Former Little Mix singer Jesy Nelson appealed for help after her black Land Rover was stolen from her driveway in Brentwood, Essex, at approximately 3 a.m. on Sunday. The vehicle contained essential medical equipment for her twin children. Nelson offered a £10,000 reward for information.

stories.title: Countries that ignored Ukraine before are now competing for meetings — Ukrainian FM after Antalya forum
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha noted a shift in diplomatic engagement at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum, stating that countries that previously ignored Ukraine are now actively seeking meetings.

stories.title: War on Iran: Mediators push ceasefire extension as deal hopes fade
stories.summary: Mediators are working to extend the ceasefire between Iran and the United States ahead of a Wednesday deadline, with sources telling Middle East Eye that progress has been made on key issues but major gaps remain. Pakistan is hosting the mediation talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: The US-Iran negotiations in Pakistan: More talk, less action on critical issues - analysis
stories.summary: A new round of negotiations between the United States and Iran is taking place in Pakistan. Key issues, including control and security of the Strait of Hormuz, remain unresolved despite ongoing dialogue.

stories.title: Religious cleric Engineer Muhammad Ali Mirza survives attack in Jhelum
stories.summary: Religious cleric Engineer Muhammad Ali Mirza survived an attack by an unidentified gunman outside the Quran & Sunnat Research Academy in Jhelum, Pakistan. The attacker, who carried a 9mm pistol, was killed in retaliatory fire. Mirza has survived multiple prior assassination attempts.

stories.title: Russian FPV drone hits multi-story building in Kherson, leaving one injured
stories.summary: A Russian first-person-view drone struck a multi-story residential building in the Korabelnyi district of Kherson, injuring at least one person.

stories.title: Kamala Harris accuses Netanyahu of dragging US into Iran war
stories.summary: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu of dragging the United States into the war with Iran, saying it was not what the American people wanted. She also described the conflict as a distraction from the Epstein files.

stories.title: Life in Donbas: 'If we give up, there will be nothing left'
stories.summary: The Russian army continues advancing on the Ukrainian town of Kostiantynivka in Donbas, aiming to occupy the entire region. Despite the threat, residents continue to live and resist in the area.

stories.title: Eight children killed in Louisiana shooting, gunman fatally shot by police
stories.summary: A shooting in Louisiana linked to a domestic violence incident left eight children dead and two others injured. The gunman was fatally shot by responding police officers. The community is reported to be in shock.

stories.title: Kiryat Shmona residents protest Lebanon ceasefire outside US embassy in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Residents of Kiryat Shmona in northern Israel protested the Lebanon ceasefire outside the US embassy in Jerusalem. The municipality went on strike, closing its education system and non-essential services, accusing the government of abandoning the border city that has faced repeated Hezbollah attacks.

stories.title: IDF reveals Forward Defense Line in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military revealed a Forward Defense Line in southern Lebanon, stating it is operating south of the line to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and prevent threats to communities in northern Israel.

stories.title: Spain urges EU to end Israel agreement over human right violations
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced plans to formally ask the European Union to suspend its association agreement with Israel, citing breaches of international law in Gaza and Lebanon. He made the announcement at a rally, arguing Israel is an unsuitable EU partner.

stories.title: IMF withdraws previous scenario for Ukraine. New outlook is much more gloomy — but not without silver lining
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund revised its baseline assumptions for Ukraine, withdrawing its previous economic scenario in favor of a more pessimistic outlook, though some positive elements remain.

stories.title: Police patrol chief quits over ‘shameful’ response to Kyiv shooting
stories.summary: Ukraine's police patrol chief Yevhen Zhukov resigned after two officers were filmed fleeing the scene of a shooting in Kyiv that killed at least six people and injured over a dozen. Zhukov, citing his combat experience, called the officers' response unacceptable and said resignation was the right course of action.

stories.title: Spain urges EU to end agreement with Israel over violations
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez urged the European Union to end its association agreement with Israel, stating that Israel violates international law in the Palestinian territories and Lebanon and therefore cannot be an EU partner.

stories.title: Israel’s 10 Days of Awe: From Yom HaShoah to Yom HaAtzmaut - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: An article explores Israel's national commemorative period from Yom HaShoah to Yom HaAtzmaut, reflecting on how days of mourning are observed when historical traumas feel connected to present events.

stories.title: Syrskyi holds meeting with commanders of unmanned systems units
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi held a meeting with commanders of the Armed Forces' unmanned systems units to discuss operations involving drone warfare.

stories.title: Why do we pray? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A discussion piece explores the nature and purpose of prayer, examining whether it is directed toward God or others, and how prayer intersects with politics, identity, and belonging.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran talks to take place Tuesday, threatens ‘NO MORE MR. NICE GUY!’
stories.summary: President Trump announced that US-Iran talks would take place on Tuesday and threatened to attack Iranian bridges and power plants if Tehran does not agree to demands. Iran remained undecided on sending a delegation to Pakistan, and Iranian speaker Ghalibaf mocked Trump's naval blockade.

stories.title: Gaza Freedom Flotilla rocked by sexual misconduct allegations against senior member aboard ship
stories.summary: The Gaza Freedom Flotilla has been shaken by allegations of sexual misconduct against a senior member aboard one of its ships, prompting an investigation into the claims.

stories.title: Newly published documents belonging to Israel's first prime minister reveal eerily relevant message
stories.summary: Newly published documents from Israel's first prime minister, David Ben-Gurion, reveal his early recognition that front lines reaching population centers would make the home front a critical component of warfare.

stories.title: Ciao UFO takes top prizes at Hong Kong Film Awards as Sons of the Neon Night glows
stories.summary: At the 44th Hong Kong Film Awards, sci-fi drama Ciao UFO won best film and best director for Patrick Leung Pak-kin. Dystopian crime thriller Sons of the Neon Night took home eight prizes from 12 nominations, making it the ceremony's biggest winner. The event was held at the Cultural Centre in Tsim Sha Tsui.

stories.title: How To Rebuild Jewish Systems - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A discussion examines the future of Jewish thought and how Jews worldwide should reconsider Zionism after October 7th, featuring David Hazony, Director of the Z3 Institute.

stories.title: Kuwait detains journalist amid Gulf crackdown on war reporting
stories.summary: Kuwaiti authorities detained US-Kuwaiti journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin, who has not been seen publicly for six weeks since visiting family in Kuwait. He has been charged with spreading false information and harming national security. The Committee to Protect Journalists reported the detention amid a wider Gulf crackdown on war reporting.

stories.title: Russia’s war on culture: Moscow has struck 1,723 Ukrainian heritage sites since 2022
stories.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, Moscow's forces have struck 1,723 Ukrainian cultural heritage sites, including churches and libraries, according to a new tally documenting the destruction.

stories.title: Will the ceasefire last? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A discussion between analysts examines the outcomes of the war with Iran and whether the ceasefire will hold, assessing what was achieved militarily and diplomatically and what challenges remain ahead.

stories.title: Drone footage shows huge Malaysian coastal village fire
stories.summary: A large fire destroyed approximately 1,000 homes in a coastal village in Malaysia's Sabah state, displacing thousands of residents. Drone footage captured the scale of the devastation.

stories.title: Will Conservative Judaism survive? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A discussion featuring rabbis from Sinai Temple in Los Angeles explores the future and distinctive characteristics of Conservative Judaism in the United States.

stories.title: Mines in the Strait of Hormuz: How dangerous are they?
stories.summary: Iran announced it has placed naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz to discourage independent maritime traffic. The development raises questions about the danger posed by the mines and the feasibility of clearance operations.

stories.title: From Erbil to Rojhilat: A new Kurdish political alignment emerges - opinion
stories.summary: After decades of internal division, several Iranian Kurdish political groups have formed a new coalition based in Erbil, with potential strategic implications for the broader region.

stories.title: Russians strike residential neighborhood in Zaporizhzhia, leaving one injured
stories.summary: A Russian attack struck a residential neighborhood in Zaporizhzhia, injuring a woman during a daytime assault on one of the city's districts.

stories.title: Australia's most decorated serviceman vows to fight war crime charges
stories.summary: Former Australian special forces soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, the country's most decorated living serviceman, vowed to fight five charges of war crime murder related to alleged unlawful killings in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012. He was granted bail on Friday following a high-profile arrest.

stories.title: Is Israeli-Palestinian peace still possible? with Ittay Flescher - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A conversation with Ittay Flescher examines whether Israeli-Palestinian peace remains achievable, considering devastating losses on both sides and debating whether hope is naive or necessary in the current environment.

stories.title: Is Japan’s treaty-day Taiwan Strait warship transit a new flashpoint with China?
stories.summary: The Japanese destroyer JS Ikazuchi transited the Taiwan Strait on Friday, spending 14 hours in the waterway on the anniversary of the 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki, which ceded Taiwan to Japan. China's PLA Eastern Theatre Command tracked the passage, and the transit has heightened tensions between Tokyo and Beijing.

stories.title: Thousands of Parisians evacuated as WW2 bomb detonated
stories.summary: Thousands of residents in Paris were evacuated from a 450-meter radius while authorities detonated an unexploded World War II bomb found in the city.

stories.title: Traffic restored on Karakoram Highway following landslide as heavy rainfall lashes GB
stories.summary: The Karakoram Highway in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, was reopened to light traffic after a landslide near Lachi in Kohistan blocked the route for nearly 20 hours. Heavy rainfall triggered landslides across the region, and the Astore Valley road remained blocked.

stories.title: Iran says final deal still far off as Strait of Hormuz remains closed
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between parties in the Iran conflict is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22, 2026, unless renewed, with Tehran saying a final agreement remains distant while the Strait of Hormuz stays closed.

stories.title: Pro-Russian Fico complains Latvia and Lithuania blocked his flight to Moscow for Putin’s 9 May parade
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said Latvia and Lithuania blocked his flight to Moscow, where he planned to attend President Putin's May 9 Victory Day parade. Fico vowed to find an alternative route and pledged to block EU sanctions against Russia.

stories.title: European allies fear US may strike rushed deal with Iran — Reuters
stories.summary: European allies expressed concern that an inexperienced U.S. negotiating team may pursue a hasty framework agreement with Iran, which could deepen rather than resolve existing disputes, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Israeli army says soldier killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced that a soldier was killed in southern Lebanon. The death brings the total Israeli army fatalities in the six-week conflict between Israel and Hezbollah to 15.

stories.title: “This is just like Putin”: WWII bunker that once documented Nazis opens museum of Russia’s war against Ukraine
stories.summary: A World War II-era bunker in Berlin that once documented Nazi activities has opened a new museum exhibition focused on Russia's war against Ukraine, featuring a destroyed Ukrainian volunteer van among its displays.

stories.title: Satellite images reveal Israel expanding Gaza military sites
stories.summary: Satellite imagery shows Israel constructing what appear to be permanent military bases inside the Gaza Strip. The expansion comes as US-backed reconstruction plans for Gaza have stalled.

stories.title: Iran not sending negotiating team to Pakistan due to US blockade
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that Tehran has not confirmed whether it will send a negotiating team to Pakistan for talks with the United States, citing the ongoing US naval blockade as the key obstacle.

stories.title: Smotrich urges PM to order the IDF to ‘prepare for the full occupation’ of Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich urged Prime Minister Netanyahu to order the IDF to prepare for full military occupation of the Gaza Strip. Smotrich also repeated his call for rebuilding Israeli settlements in Gaza. A separate Likud minister praised the reestablishment of a West Bank settlement evacuated in 2005.

stories.title: Trump sending US delegation for Iran talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: President Trump announced a U.S. delegation will travel to Pakistan on Monday for another round of talks with Iran, as a fragile ceasefire nears its Wednesday expiration. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported Tehran has made no decision to send negotiators as long as a U.S. naval blockade remains in place.

stories.title: 'No more Mr. Nice Guy!': Trump says Iran committed 'serious' ceasefire violation, still wants deal
stories.summary: President Trump declared Iran committed a 'serious' ceasefire violation but said he still wants a deal. A White House official confirmed Vice President JD Vance, envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner would head to Pakistan for talks.

stories.title: Authorities open criminal proceedings in Kyiv over alleged official negligence by police during terrorist attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement opened a criminal case in Kyiv investigating alleged negligence by police officers during their response to a terrorist attack on April 18.

stories.title: Israeli drone‑detection start-up scores major US commercial breakthrough
stories.summary: Israeli start-up Tondo Smart, founded by IDF Unit 8200 graduates, achieved a major U.S. commercial breakthrough with a drone-detection system that monitors and manages low-altitude airspace, commercializing Israeli defense-derived technology.

stories.title: Why is Russia’s threat from Belarus not about Kyiv this time?
stories.summary: Belarus is reportedly constructing new roads and calling up reservists, raising concerns about a potential military threat from Belarusian territory, though analysts suggest the objective may not be directed at Kyiv this time.

stories.title: Syria 'foils' cross-border attack by Assad remnants, Hezbollah
stories.summary: Syrian authorities said they foiled a cross-border attack by arresting members of a cell allegedly linked to Hezbollah and remnants of the Assad regime who were planning a sabotage operation.

stories.title: Labor accused of ignoring anti-racism plan as documents reveal repeated pleas to take action
stories.summary: Australia's federal Labor government has been accused of failing to act on a national anti-racism plan nearly 18 months after receiving recommendations from the human rights commission. Documents released to the Senate showed no progress on the strategy, despite repeated pleas from the race discrimination commissioner.

stories.title: You can’t topple Iran without fighting the IRGC - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion piece argues that while military action may weaken Iran's government, the absence of a viable opposition force means the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps must be directly confronted to achieve regime change.

stories.title: Sviderskyi: MLE creates security “buffer” between front line and rear
stories.summary: Ukraine's Military Law Enforcement Service monitors the movement of personnel, weapons, and equipment between the combat zone and rear areas, creating a security buffer to prevent unauthorized transport of dangerous items.

stories.title: Syria says it foiled Hezbollah-linked cross-border attack planned from area near Israel
stories.summary: Syria's interior ministry announced it foiled a cross-border missile attack planned by a Hezbollah-linked cell operating from Quneitra province, which borders Israel. The ministry did not specify the intended target of the planned strike.

stories.title: Iran’s entrepreneurs vexed as internet blackout chokes ability to earn and run firms
stories.summary: Iranian entrepreneurs report severe economic hardship due to a prolonged internet blackout imposed during the war. A Tehran interior designer said she was forced to sell valuables, while a Paris-based business owner reported a sharp drop in orders from Iranian clients.

stories.title: DRC government, AFC/M23 rebels agree to ease humanitarian access
stories.summary: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel coalition reached progress on a protocol covering humanitarian access, judicial protection, ceasefire oversight, and the release of prisoners.

stories.title: US animal rights activists clash with police over Wisconsin dog breeder
stories.summary: Approximately 1,000 animal welfare activists attempted to enter the Ridglan Farms beagle breeding and research facility in Blue Mounds, Wisconsin, on Saturday. Police used rubber bullets and pepper spray to disperse the crowd and arrested the group's leader. It was the second such attempt in recent months.

stories.title: Israeli settlers burn Palestinian home, car in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian property in the West Bank, burning a home and a car. In separate incidents, settlers stole 150 sheep from a Palestinian farmer and injured an elderly Palestinian woman.

stories.title: More than 18,000 patients wait to leave Gaza
stories.summary: More than 18,000 patients in the Gaza Strip are waiting for medical evacuation, but only a few hundred have been allowed to leave for treatment despite ceasefire commitments to facilitate such evacuations.

stories.title: “Rusty Dagger” built for Ukraine reportedly cleared F-16 integration testing
stories.summary: A cruise missile known as "Rusty Dagger," designed specifically for Ukraine, has reportedly passed F-16 integration testing. The affordable weapon could soon be deployed on Ukraine's F-16 fighter jets.

stories.title: ISW: Russia likely plans to exploit European telecom loopholes for Shahed guidance — as it already does near Poland, Romania, Belarus
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russia likely plans to exploit European telecom network loopholes to guide Shahed drones. Ukraine's Defense Ministry adviser said Russia uses SIM cards from Rostelecom subsidiary T2, which switch to neighboring countries' networks when Ukrainian signals are blocked.

stories.title: Trump threatens to ‘blow up whole country’ if Iran does not sign deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told Fox News he would 'blow up the whole country' if Iran does not sign a peace deal. Trump said Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner would lead talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Damascus claims to arrest more Hezbollah-linked cell members behind plot to kill rabbi
stories.summary: Syrian state media reported the arrest of additional members of a Hezbollah-linked cell in Damascus accused of plotting to assassinate Rabbi Michael Khoury near the Maronite Church in the Bab Touma neighborhood on April 11.

stories.title: DR Congo, AFC/M23 group agree to facilitate aid, release prisoners within 10 days
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 group agreed on Sunday to facilitate humanitarian aid deliveries and release prisoners within 10 days. The AFC/M23 has seized large areas of eastern DR Congo since 2021.

stories.title: DRC government, M23 rebels commit to protect civilians, aid deliveries
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's government and M23 rebels agreed during talks in Switzerland to protect civilians and facilitate aid deliveries. The two sides also advanced a protocol for monitoring the ceasefire.

stories.title: Former US vice president Harris accuses Netanyahu of dragging Trump into Iran war
stories.summary: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu of drawing President Trump into the war with Iran. Harris said Americans do not want war and that US servicemen have been put at risk. Netanyahu has repeatedly denied the accusation.

stories.title: Islamabad police impose traffic restrictions ahead of further talks
stories.summary: Islamabad police announced traffic restrictions and a 'red zone' closure due to visiting foreign delegations, signaling that a new round of U.S.-Iran talks may resume in Pakistan's capital.

stories.title: Turkey 'optimistic' Middle East ceasefire will be extended
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan expressed optimism that the Middle East ceasefire between the U.S.-Israel coalition and Iran would be extended before its Wednesday expiration, saying no one wants to see the war continue.

stories.title: What to know about US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump accused Iran of violating the ceasefire and announced plans to send US negotiators to Pakistan for further talks. Tensions center on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route.

stories.title: Canada Research Chair chemist Janusz Pawliszyn joins Chinese university
stories.summary: Janusz Pawliszyn, a 71-year-old Canada Research Chair chemist and fellow of the Royal Society of Canada, has joined Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou, China. He has supervised over 110 graduate students and nearly 200 postdoctoral researchers during his career.

stories.title: Rescuers show how they extinguished Shostka fire under threat of further Russian attacks
stories.summary: Rescuers from Ukraine's State Emergency Service extinguished fires in Shostka, Sumy region, caused by a Russian drone attack on the night of April 19, working despite ongoing threats of additional strikes.

stories.title: Iran claims it replenishes missile launchers faster than before Operation Roaring Lion - report
stories.summary: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander claimed Iran is replenishing its missile launchers faster than before Operation Roaring Lion. Separately, an Israeli report said the security establishment located missile launchers aimed at Israel, ready to fire if no Lebanon ceasefire was reached.

stories.title: Russia plans to move 114,000 of its citizens into occupied regions of Ukraine, skipping cities it destroyed
stories.summary: Russia plans to resettle approximately 114,000 of its citizens into occupied regions of Ukraine, excluding heavily destroyed cities such as Bakhmut, Avdiivka, Marinka, and Vuhledar from its reconstruction plans.

stories.title: North Korea launches ballistic missiles as UN warns of nuclear advances
stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles from its Sinpo area toward its eastern waters, with each traveling approximately 140 kilometers, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. The launches came days after the IAEA warned of Pyongyang's advancing nuclear capabilities.

stories.title: As Israel approaches 78th Independence Day, its population stands at 10.244 million
stories.summary: Israel's population stands at 10.244 million as it approaches its 78th Independence Day. Approximately 76% are Jews and 'others,' while 21.1% are Arabs. Over the past year, 177,000 were born, 48,000 died, and 21,000 immigrated.

stories.title: Oklahoma principal who disarmed gun-wielding intruder crowned prom king
