stories.summary: Former al-Qaeda member Aiman Dean claimed on X that the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire is actually linked to the Iran situation. He alleged that Tehran has been using the demand for a Lebanon ceasefire as a reason to avoid serious engagement in negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy calls for joint efforts to set up Hormuz  mission
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called for joint international efforts to establish a mission ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. He offered Ukraine's wartime experience securing Black Sea shipping lanes as a potential contribution.

stories.title: As China’s biotech firms shift gears, can AI floor the accelerator?
stories.summary:
A quarter featuring multiple eye-popping deals is no longer unusual for China’s pharmaceutical industry – in fact, it may soon be considered a slow season.
In recent months, companies including CSPC P

stories.title: Uruguayan court rejects injunction against offshore seismic prospection, allowing exploration to continue
stories.summary: A civil court in Montevideo dismissed an injunction filed by social organizations and fishing industry unions against offshore seismic prospection in Uruguay's exclusive economic zone. The ruling allows French company Viridien (CGG Services) to continue hydrocarbon exploration on a block assigned to oil major Chevron.

stories.title: Global oil market hit by 500 million barrel loss amid Iran war
stories.summary: The war on Iran has removed approximately 500 million barrels of crude from the global market, the largest energy supply disruption in modern history, according to analytics firm Kpler. Reuters reported the loss was equivalent to nearly a month of US oil demand or more than a month's supply for all of Europe.

stories.title: Pope Leo slams AI abuse after Trump’s Jesus post
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV criticized the misuse of artificial intelligence, warning that replacing reality with AI-generated simulations risks fueling polarization, conflict, fear, and violence. His remarks followed a controversial AI-generated image of Jesus posted by U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: US Navy denies reports of food shortages on warships
stories.summary: The US Navy denied reports of food shortages aboard the aircraft carriers USS Abraham Lincoln and USS Tripoli, calling the claims "incorrect." A Navy official said routine menu adjustments were made to improve operational endurance during the confrontation.

stories.title: India-flagged vessels start sailing out of Hormuz
stories.summary: India-flagged vessels have begun sailing out of the Strait of Hormuz. Most of the ships are carrying crude oil critical to India's energy supply needs.

stories.title: Hormuz open only under ceasefire conditions, Iran says
stories.summary: Iran's Defence Ministry spokesperson Brigadier General Reza Talaei-Nik said the Strait of Hormuz is open only under ceasefire conditions and on a temporary basis. He added that military vessels affiliated with hostile forces are barred from passage and the strait could be closed again if conditions change.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions aimed at Colombian fighters in Sudan
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on five companies and individuals on April 17 for allegedly recruiting former Colombian military personnel to fight for a paramilitary group in Sudan.

stories.title: Police detain Russian agent for preparing strike on air defense positions in Odesa region
stories.summary: The Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) has detained a woman who, allegedly on orders from Russia's FSB, was preparing coordinates for a new series of missile and drone strikes on the Odesa region.

stories.title: Japan warned of ‘hellish summer’ as energy fears mount
stories.summary: Japan is hoping further US-Iran talks will ease tensions in the Middle East and help reopen the Strait of Hormuz permanently, but there is also mounting anxiety over what a failure could mean for the

stories.title: Lebanon president says ceasefire should move to permanent agreements
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called on Friday for the existing ceasefire in Lebanon to be transformed into "permanent agreements." Speaking in Beirut, Aoun did not specify whether he was referring to a prospective peace deal with Israel or broader regional arrangements.

stories.title: Oil tankers make dash towards Hormuz strait as Iran says vital waterway is open
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister declared the Strait of Hormuz fully open to commercial shipping on April 17. Oil tankers began moving toward the vital waterway following the announcement.

stories.title: Lebanese man removes Israeli flag from castle in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: A Lebanese man returning to southern Lebanon removed an Israeli flag from Beaufort Castle, also known as Qalaat al-Shaqif, in the country's south.

stories.title: Jewish groups urge Trump to prioritize Americans held in Iran during ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Several Jewish and human-rights organizations, including the AJC, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, the Foley Legacy Foundation, the Raoul Wallenberg Center, and United Against Nuclear Iran, urged President Trump to prioritize the release of Americans detained in Iran during ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: US midwestern states at risk of severe thunderstorms, weather agency warns
stories.summary: The U.S. National Weather Service warned that severe thunderstorms and tornadoes could affect midwestern states from Wisconsin to Oklahoma on Friday. Approximately 26 million people were placed under tornado watches. Tornadoes had already battered towns across the central U.S., causing debris and property destruction.

stories.title: Polish town’s new ‘information center’ denies murders of Jews by local Poles in 1941
stories.summary: A new "information center" in the Polish town of Jedwabne denies that local Poles murdered Jewish residents in 1941. The family of a Jewish survivor of the Jedwabne massacre is seeking removal of the installation, which they describe as a "denial museum."

stories.title: Iran says it did not agree to halt uranium enrichment indefinitely
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official said Iran did not agree to halt uranium enrichment indefinitely, calling enrichment one of the most prominent points of contention with Washington. The official warned that Trump's statements could derail ongoing US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: IDF officers in southern Lebanon claim they were not informed of ceasefire deal - N12
stories.summary: IDF officers stationed in southern Lebanon reportedly said they were not informed in advance of the ceasefire deal with Lebanon. The ceasefire, announced by US President Donald Trump on Thursday, took effect at midnight Israel time between Thursday and Friday.

stories.title: Significant differences remain between Iran-US, including on nuclear issues, senior Iranian official says
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that significant differences remain between Iran and the United States on reaching a deal to end the war, including on nuclear issues. The official added that keeping the Strait of Hormuz open is conditional on U.S. adherence to ceasefire terms.

stories.title: In Malaysia, unlicensed street photography becomes focus of crackdown
stories.summary: While many Europeans are considering putting long-haul flying on the back burner as jet fuel costs and airfares climb, those with a trip already booked for Malaysia may need to watch out if ambling ar

stories.title: Pope condemns use of AI to fuel 'polarisation, conflict, fear and violence'
stories.summary: Pope Leo condemned the use of artificial intelligence to fuel polarization, conflict, fear, and violence. The remarks highlighted how the AI industry's reliance on cobalt extraction disproportionately burdens Africa with environmental and human costs.

stories.title: Russian drone with warhead retrieved from Dnipro River in Kyiv
stories.summary: In Kyiv, police explosives experts recovered a Russian drone equipped with a warhead from the Dnipro River.

stories.title: No sirens reported in Israel for over 24 hours after ceasefire
stories.summary: No air raid sirens have sounded in Israel for over 24 hours following the ceasefire, with the last alert early Friday near the Lebanon border determined to be a false alarm. Prior to the ceasefire, sirens regularly sent residents to shelters across major cities including Jerusalem and Tel Aviv.

stories.title: Oil prices fall, Wall Street hits record as Iran reopens Hormuz
stories.summary: Oil prices fell approximately 9% and Wall Street hit record highs after Iran announced the Strait of Hormuz was reopened for commercial tankers. The S&P 500 rose 1.2% and the Dow Jones gained about 870 points, as oil returned to price levels seen in the early days of the Iran war.

stories.title: Pope Leo and Trump, the battle for America’s soul
stories.summary: A dispute has emerged between Pope Leo and U.S. President Donald Trump, with Trump accusing the pope of catering to the radical left. The article examines the political and ideological clash over American values.

stories.title: Ghalibaf says Trump’s 'false' claims won’t help in negotiations
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf dismissed recent claims by US President Donald Trump as "false," stating that the US did not win the war through lies. Ghalibaf warned that the Strait of Hormuz would not remain open if the US blockade of Iranian ports continues.

stories.title: French court rules antisemitism not a motive in nanny’s poisoning of Jewish family
stories.summary: A French appeals court ruled that antisemitism was not a motivating factor in the poisoning of a Jewish family by their Algerian nanny. The ruling came despite the caretaker's statements to police referencing the family's Jewish identity and perceived wealth and power.

stories.title: ByteDance, Tencent step up AI talent battle amid reported departure of DeepSeek researcher
stories.summary: ByteDance, Tencent, and other major Chinese tech firms are intensifying competition to recruit top artificial intelligence talent. Guo Daya, a lead researcher on DeepSeek's R1 model, reportedly left to join ByteDance's Seed AI development team. The moves highlight growing sensitivity around AI hiring in China's tech sector, which is also drawing researchers from Silicon Valley.

stories.title: Japan ditches decades of arm export curbs as US reliability wavers
stories.summary: Japan is preparing to relax its long-standing arms export restrictions, with cabinet approval of revisions to the Three Principles on the Transfer of Defence Equipment and Technology expected next week. Analysts say the changes aim to bolster Japan's domestic defence industry and deepen security partnerships, as confidence in U.S. reliability as a security partner diminishes.

stories.title: Why China is urgently looking to North Africa as the energy crisis rolls on
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the war in Iran has pushed China to urgently pursue energy partnerships in North Africa. Beijing is looking to fast-track projects in Algerian oilfields, Moroccan battery factories, and Egypt's industrial base. The goal is to create a Mediterranean hub as a strategic backup for its green-energy supply chain.

stories.title: China family buries luxury car as offering, prompting government reprimand, public apology
stories.summary: In Liaoyang, Liaoning province, a family buried a Mercedes-Benz S450L as a funerary offering during an elderly relative's funeral on April 9. A viral video of the burial sparked public outrage over legal violations and environmental concerns. Local government officials issued a reprimand, and the family publicly apologized.

stories.title: Trump thanks Gulf states for their ‘tremendous’ support
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump thanked Gulf states for what he called their "tremendous" support, as Iran fully opened the Strait of Hormuz. Trump described the development as a potentially great day for the world.

stories.title: Temporary truce: On U.S.-Israel ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: A ceasefire between the United States, Israel, and Iran has been announced, with calls for it to hold across all fronts. The truce aims to de-escalate the broader conflict in the region.

stories.title: In final moments before truce, Israeli strike kills Lebanese man's family
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in Tyre, southern Lebanon, killed 13 members of Hassan Abu Khalil's family in the final minutes before a ceasefire took effect. Abu Khalil was the sole survivor after his family had endured six weeks of war.

stories.title: Sea of Azov on brink of ecological disaster as Russia planning mass jellyfish harvest
stories.summary: The National Resistance Center has warned that the Sea of Azov is facing a potential environmental disaster, as Russian authorities are preparing a large-scale jellyfish harvest.

stories.title: Answering the call: The overlooked Jewish role in America’s revolution - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlighted the historical contributions of Jewish merchants, artisans, and professionals to the American Revolution, including supplying goods, raising funds, and joining local militias.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelensky calls for joint efforts to set up Hormuz mission
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called for joint international efforts to establish a security mission in the Strait of Hormuz, stating that political decisions alone cannot address the waterway's security challenges.

stories.title: New ‘information center’ in Polish town denies murders of Jews by local Poles in 1941
stories.summary: A new information center in a Polish town is denying the murders of Jews by local Poles in 1941. The center was inaugurated with a ribbon-cutting ceremony promoted by right-wing Polish activist Wojciech Sumlinski.

stories.title: 2 US soldiers injured in brown bear attack during training exercise in Alaska
stories.summary: Two U.S. Army soldiers were injured in a brown bear encounter during a land navigation training exercise in Arctic Valley, part of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson's training area in Anchorage, Alaska. The incident occurred on Thursday, and both soldiers were receiving medical care as of Friday.

stories.title: Russian police chief’s son accused of raping sleeping woman during livestream
stories.summary: The son of a district police chief in Yakutsk, Russia, has been accused of raping a sleeping woman while livestreaming the assault on the Bigo Live platform and collecting viewer donations.

stories.title: Watch: Fuel truck leaves trail of fire on road in Syria
stories.summary: A burning fuel tanker was filmed driving through the centre of Hasakah, Syria, leaving a trail of fire along the road. Eyewitnesses captured the incident.

stories.title: UN aid chief warns of possible ‘full-scale famine’ in South Sudan
stories.summary: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher warned that South Sudan is at risk of sliding into full-scale famine and collapse. The statement highlights the severity of the humanitarian crisis in the country.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth compares media to Pharisees, ancient Jewish sect derided by Christians
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth compared the media to the Pharisees, an ancient Jewish sect often derided in Christian tradition. The remarks echoed a similar 2019 comment by then-Indiana mayor Pete Buttigieg about Mike Pence.

stories.title: Lebanon president says ceasefire should move to permanent agreements
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called for the ceasefire to transition into permanent agreements, asserting that Lebanon is no longer a card in anyone's game or an arena for others' wars.

stories.title: Lebanese joy at returning to homes in the south mixed with horror at ruins of war
stories.summary: Lebanese residents began returning to southern Lebanon after a truce with Israel, crossing a makeshift bridge over the Litani River. Children flashed victory signs from cars, but families faced bombed-out ruins and difficult conditions upon arrival.

stories.title: Shock therapy: war forces oil-addicted Asia to finally go green
stories.summary: Rising oil prices driven by the Iran war are accelerating solar energy adoption across Asia, particularly in Thailand. Thai company Wayso reports surging demand for rooftop solar panel installations. The conflict has achieved what years of climate summits could not, making renewable energy an economic necessity for the region.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran says US blockade of ports must end as strait opens
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people forcibly displaced by Israeli attacks on Lebanon used the first day of a ceasefire to return home. Separately, Tehran called for an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports as the Strait of Hormuz reopened.

stories.title: Trump rejects idea that Iran could charge tolls on Strait of Hormuz: ‘Nope. No way. No.’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump rejected the idea that Iran could charge tolls on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the USS Gerald Ford returned to the Middle East as a third US aircraft carrier headed to the region, and Trump insisted Iran's uranium would be sent to the US despite Iranian denials.

stories.title: Ukraine, US discuss expanding Reconstruction Investment Fund capabilities
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko and DFC CEO Ben Black discussed expanding the capabilities of the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund during bilateral talks.

stories.title: Lenfilm to produce series based on book by Russia’s Investigative Committee chief
stories.summary: Russia's Lenfilm studio announced it will produce a multi-part television series based on a book by Alexander Bastrykin, head of Russia's Investigative Committee.

stories.title: EU could release jet fuel stocks if Hormuz disruption persists
stories.summary: The European Union indicated it could release jet fuel stockpiles if disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz persists. An EU spokesperson said Iran's announcement of the strait's reopening had not changed current contingency plans.

stories.title: US to recover uranium from Iran at a ‘leisurely pace’, Trump tells Reuters
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told Reuters that the United States would recover uranium from Iran at a "leisurely pace," referring to "nuclear dust" and stating it would be retrieved "very soon."

stories.title: World Cup 2026: Fans to pay $150 for train ticket to stadium
stories.summary: Transportation costs for World Cup fans traveling to US stadiums could be more than 10 times higher than regular fares. Local officials and FIFA bosses are trading blame for the increased prices while

stories.title: Iran denies claim that US will retrieve enriched uranium, says removal of material 'not an option'
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official denied U.S. claims that Iran would hand over enriched uranium, calling the removal of the material "not an option." The official also told Reuters that significant differences remain in negotiations to end the war.

stories.title: Amid truce with Israel, Aoun says Lebanon to now seek ‘permanent agreements’
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said Lebanon will seek "permanent agreements" following the ceasefire with Israel. Aoun stated that negotiating with Israel is not a sign of weakness, while urging an IDF withdrawal from Lebanese territory.

stories.title: War update: 118 clashes on frontline, Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk axes hottest
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 118 attacks on Ukrainian positions along the frontline, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors of the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Russian TV host and blogger deletes Instagram post criticizing corruption in Russia
stories.summary: Russian TV host and blogger Aiza deleted an Instagram post in which she criticized corruption in Russia. The video, published on April 14, is no longer accessible.

stories.title: Mine threat in parts of Hormuz not fully understood, US navy advisory says
stories.summary: A U.S. Navy advisory issued on April 17 warned that the mine threat in parts of the Strait of Hormuz is not fully understood. The advisory recommended that ships consider avoiding the affected areas.

stories.title: Ships crossing Hormuz need IRGC OK, unfreezing of assets part of deal, Iran official says
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official said all ships may transit the Strait of Hormuz but must coordinate passage with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The official also confirmed that unfreezing Iranian financial assets was part of the broader deal.

stories.title: Myanmar cuts ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi’s sentence, frees former president
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government reduced the prison sentence of former leader Aung San Suu Kyi by one-sixth as part of a broader amnesty. The 80-year-old Nobel laureate had been serving a 27-year sentence on charges her allies described as politically motivated following the 2021 coup.

stories.title: White House and Anthropic CEO discuss working together amid Mythos AI fears
stories.summary: White House staff and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met on Friday to discuss potential collaboration, following a prior dispute between the Pentagon and the AI firm over model usage. The meeting comes amid growing concerns that Anthropic's latest AI model could be exploited to enhance cyberattacks. The discussions suggest efforts to rebuild trust between the administration and the company.

stories.title: Magyar unlikely to fully reverse Hungary's Ukraine policy – expert
stories.summary: An expert assessed that a potential change in Hungary's political leadership under Peter Magyar may improve relations with Ukraine somewhat, but a full reversal of Budapest's Ukraine policy remains unlikely.

stories.title: He made jazz under air raids - and built an Indian city's music scene
stories.summary: KC Sen, a war correspondent and jazz bandleader, shaped Kolkata's music scene by organizing and performing jazz during air raids in India. His work as an impresario helped build the city's cultural landscape.

stories.title: School shooting in Zakarpattia: 15-year-old suspect charged with attempted murder
stories.summary: A 15-year-old suspect has been formally charged with attempted murder after opening fire at a school in Chop, in Ukraine's western Zakarpattia region.

stories.title: Spain's Sanchez says Venezuela's Machado declined to meet him
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado declined an offered meeting with him and his government during her visit to Spain. Machado reportedly said she did not consider the meeting opportune at this time.

stories.title: Nordic leaders welcome Iran’s statement on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The leaders of Finland, Norway, Sweden, and Denmark jointly welcomed Iran's announcement regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The Nordic leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts to achieve lasting solutions to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iraq resumes southern oil exports after month-long halt due to Hormuz disruption
stories.summary: Iraq resumed southern oil exports on Friday after a month-long halt caused by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The Malta-flagged tanker Agios Fanourios I anchored off Iraq's southern terminals to load approximately two million barrels of Basra crude.

stories.title: BBC Russia reports shadow fleet vessel likely caused Black Sea oil spill near Russian coast
stories.summary: The Russian-flagged vessel Sofia was likely responsible for a large oil spill discovered near Anapa on Russia's Black Sea coast, according to BBC Russia, identifying it as a shadow fleet vessel.

stories.title: 'Drone sanctions' inflict noticeable losses on Russia but don't halt war financing – expert
stories.summary: An expert noted that Ukraine's sustained drone strikes on Russian economic infrastructure are inflicting significant damage but have not yet undermined Moscow's ability to finance the war.

stories.title: Trump says Israel is banned from bombing Lebanon
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Israel is banned from bombing Lebanon and said the United States would handle the Hezbollah situation through its own appropriate measures.

stories.title: Watch: Constitution Amendment Bill, part of delimitation package, defeated
stories.summary: India's Lok Sabha defeated a Constitution Amendment Bill on women's parliamentary quotas that was part of a broader delimitation package. Separately, Sri Lanka's Power and Energy Minister resigned, and Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz is 'open' but tracking shows few ships moving
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz open, but vessel-tracking data showed minimal shipping traffic. U.S. President Donald Trump acknowledged Tehran's announcement but stated the American naval blockade would remain in place until a peace deal is finalized.

stories.title: Truce in effect as Trump says Israel ‘prohibited’ from bombing Lebanon
stories.summary: A truce between Israel and Hezbollah took effect in Lebanon, with U.S. President Donald Trump stating Israel was prohibited from bombing Lebanon. The Lebanese Army warned southern residents not to return home immediately, citing continued Israeli acts of aggression.

stories.title: Australian former soldier gets bail on Afghanistan war crime charges
stories.summary: Australia's most decorated living military veteran was released on bail from a Sydney prison ten days after being charged with war crimes allegedly committed during service in Afghanistan.

stories.title: U.S.-Iran tension will not deter Haj pilgrims, say officials
stories.summary: Indian officials said U.S.-Iran tensions would not deter Haj pilgrims, with the first batch scheduled to depart from various Indian embarkation points on April 18.

stories.title: Russian drone strike hits warehouses near Kherson, sparks fire
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a drone attack on warehouse facilities in Zelenivka, a suburb of Kherson, on April 17, sparking a fire that spread to a nearby house.

stories.title: US judge blocks Justice Department bid to seize voter data in Rhode Island
stories.summary: A US federal judge blocked the Justice Department's attempt to seize voter data in Rhode Island. The ruling marks another legal setback for the Trump administration, which has sought access to state voter records ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz 'completely open' and Iran will 'never close' it again, Trump announces
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran announced that the Strait of Hormuz is fully reopened to all commercial vessels. President Trump declared Iran would never close the waterway again, linking the reopening to the Lebanon ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Sri Lanka repatriates survivors of U.S. torpedo attack on Iranian ship
stories.summary: Sri Lanka repatriated 238 Iranian sailors, including 32 survivors of a U.S. torpedo attack on an Iranian ship in the Indian Ocean.

stories.title: Chinese manufacturers recalibrate overseas expansion plans in wake of Iran war
stories.summary: Chinese manufacturers are recalibrating overseas expansion plans in response to the Iran war's disruption of global trade. Companies like a toy factory operator in Vietnam are adjusting strategies as they seek new markets amid narrowing domestic profits and expanding production capacity.

stories.title: IDF says elite unit took control of key position in southern Lebanon minutes before ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces said an elite unit captured the "Christophani Ridge," a key position in southern Lebanon, minutes before the ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Trump seeks ‘resolution’ of his $10bn lawsuit against IRS, spurring concern
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is seeking a resolution to his $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. Critics have raised concerns that Trump could negotiate his own settlement through a Justice Department under his control.

stories.title: Russia’s Leningrad Region to deploy mobile fire groups at critical sites to counter drone attacks, staffed by reservists
stories.summary: Russia's Leningrad Region announced plans to deploy mobile fire groups staffed by reservists at industrial facilities and critical infrastructure to counter drone attacks, according to Governor Alexander Drozdenko.

stories.title: ‘Dystopian’ Iran war bets spark US crackdown on prediction markets
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers raised concerns over prediction market wagers on the U.S.-Israel war against Iran, citing risks of insider trading and erosion of public trust. The controversy has prompted calls for a crackdown on such platforms.

stories.title: China calls passage of Japanese warship through Taiwan Strait a 'provocation'
stories.summary: China condemned the transit of Japanese destroyer JS Ikazuchi through the Taiwan Strait as a provocation. Chinese military naval and air forces tracked and monitored the vessel throughout its passage on April 17.

stories.title: Lula and Sanchez seal progressive alliance in Barcelona and call for front against global far right
stories.summary: Brazilian President Lula da Silva and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez held a bilateral summit at Barcelona's Pedralbes Palace, signing cooperation agreements. Both leaders displayed alignment and framed their alliance as a progressive front against the global far right.

stories.title: Russian forces massing on southern outskirts of Myrnohrad – military
stories.summary: Russian troops are massing personnel and equipment on the southern outskirts of Myrnohrad in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, according to Ukrainian military officials.

stories.title: Iran declares Hormuz "fully open" until ceasefire ends; Trump insists on keeping Iranian port blockade
stories.summary: Iran announced the Strait of Hormuz will remain fully open to merchant shipping until the U.S.-Iran ceasefire expires, effectively ending a nearly seven-week blockade. The announcement triggered a nearly 10% drop in oil prices and relief across global markets.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia and US discuss keeping Strait of Hormuz open, Saudi state news agency
stories.summary: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed efforts to ensure the Strait of Hormuz remains open and to consolidate the Lebanon ceasefire, according to Saudi state news agency SPA.

stories.title: Russia approves 10-year statute of limitations for privatization cases, with exceptions for anti-corruption and ‘extremism’ grounds
stories.summary: Russia's government submitted a bill to the State Duma on April 16 establishing a maximum 10-year statute of limitations for privatization cases. The legislation includes exceptions for cases involving anti-corruption and extremism grounds.

stories.title: Israel says military operation against Hezbollah ‘still not complete’
stories.summary: Israel stated that its military operation against Hezbollah in Lebanon is "still not complete" despite the ceasefire. Israeli officials warned that displaced residents returning to southern Lebanon might need to evacuate again if fighting resumes.

stories.title: Hong Kong is ageing, but the real question is where people age
stories.summary: Hong Kong faces an increasingly urgent aging population challenge, with long hospital waits and chronic shortages in long-term care. Policymakers and researchers are debating where residents age and whether the city's healthcare and social care systems can remain sustainable.

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump claim on deal to surrender nuclear material stockpiles
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry rejected U.S. President Donald Trump's claim that Tehran had agreed to hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, stating the material would not be transferred anywhere.

stories.title: US is leading G20 initiative to ensure fertilizer access, sources say
stories.summary: The United States is leading a G20 initiative urging coordinated action with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank to ensure global fertilizer access. The effort responds to disruptions in food trade supply chains caused by the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Svyrydenko discusses Ukraine's key defense needs with U.S. Congress members
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko met with members of the Ukraine Caucuses in the U.S. Congress during a visit to Washington. Discussions focused on Ukraine's key defense needs and increasing pressure on Russia.

stories.title: Argentina’s Milei to arrive in Israel on Sunday, his third trip in last three years
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei is scheduled to arrive in Israel on Sunday for his third visit in three years. He will meet Prime Minister Netanyahu at the Western Wall, having previously described Israel as a strategic ally.

stories.title: Ukraine Has a Plan to Build Back Better
stories.summary: Ukraine is developing reconstruction plans aimed at rebuilding in an environmentally, socially, and geopolitically sustainable manner following the extensive damage caused by the war.

stories.title: Russian billionaire says drone attacks affect nitrogen fertiliser trade
stories.summary: Russian billionaire Andrei Melnichenko, founder of fertilizer producer EuroChem, said that recent drone attacks are significantly disrupting Russia's nitrogen fertilizer industry and affecting trade in the sector.

stories.title: Unicef says Lebanon ceasefire ‘must hold’
stories.summary: UNICEF welcomed the Lebanon ceasefire after 46 days of conflict, reporting that at least 172 children were killed, 661 injured, and more than 415,000 displaced during the hostilities.

stories.title: Iran says Hormuz Strait open after Lebanon deal, Trump expects Iran deal ‘soon’
stories.summary: Iran announced the Strait of Hormuz would reopen following a Lebanon ceasefire deal, while President Trump said he expects a broader Iran deal "soon." Trump noted that the U.S. military blockade of ships sailing to Iranian ports remained in place.

stories.title: Russia’s economic reserves ‘largely exhausted,’ development minister says
stories.summary: Russian Economic Development Minister Maxim Reshetnikov stated that the country's economic reserves have been largely exhausted. He cited a strong ruble, high interest rates, labor shortages, and budget constraints as contributing factors to increasingly difficult economic conditions.

stories.title: Spain signs deals with Brazil as Sanchez builds anti-Trump bloc
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva held their first bilateral summit, signing 15 agreements covering critical minerals, telecommunications, and AI. The leaders are seeking to build an alliance to counter U.S. President Donald Trump's policies.

stories.title: Lead prosecutor on investigation into former CIA director no longer on case
stories.summary: Federal prosecutor Maria Medetis Long has left the investigation into former CIA Director John Brennan after expressing reservations about the case. Brennan led the CIA when it assessed that Russia acted to boost Donald Trump in the 2016 election.

stories.title: Zambia: Democratic Senators Press State Department on Conditioning HIV Aid on Economic Concessions
stories.summary: U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Chris Coons, and Brian Schatz sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressing concern over reports that the State Department may condition HIV/AIDS treatment and economic aid to Zambia on economic reforms favorable to American businesses.

stories.title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open after Lebanon truce; Trump says blockade to continue
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz open to commercial vessels following a Lebanon ceasefire, while U.S. President Donald Trump stated that the naval blockade against Iran would remain in force until a broader deal is reached.

stories.title: India drops proposal to mandate national ID app on smartphones after pushback
stories.summary: India's government has dropped a proposal that would have required smartphone manufacturers including Apple and Samsung to pre-install the Aadhaar biometric identification app. The Unique Identification Authority of India had previously asked the IT ministry to pursue mandatory pre-installation with leading phone makers.

stories.title: Air Canada temporarily suspends some flights to New York and other locations
stories.summary: Air Canada temporarily suspended flights from Toronto and Montreal to New York's JFK airport due to rising fuel prices. The move reflects broader airline industry concerns as aviation fuel costs climb amid the ongoing U.S.-Israel war with Iran, despite a fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Zelensky warns Belarus against joining war, cites Venezuela as cautionary example
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Belarus against entering the war, noting increased military activity in Belarus. He referenced Venezuela as a cautionary example of the consequences of such involvement.

stories.title: Zelensky after Syrskyi's report: Russia once again tries to drag Belarus into its war
stories.summary: President Zelensky reported, following a briefing by Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi, that Russia is again attempting to draw Belarus into the war against Ukraine. He cited road construction toward Ukraine and the establishment of artillery positions in Belarusian territory.

stories.title: Trump says Iran peace deal could be reached ‘soon’ after Tehran reopens Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: Iran announced the Strait of Hormuz was reopened to commercial shipping during the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, and President Trump suggested a peace deal could come soon. However, Iranian officials cautioned that serious differences between Tehran and Washington remain unresolved.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1514: From Belarus border roads to Black Sea silence — Ukraine strikes deep while bracing for new pressure
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy called for Ukraine to reduce dependence on Western air defense by scaling up domestic missile production. The US warned NATO's eastern flank of delayed weapons shipments as the Iran war drains European stockpiles. A private-sector group in Kharkiv Oblast downed its first jet-powered Shahed drone.

stories.title: Lebanon president says country is no longer a pawn amid Israel ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun pledged to preserve Lebanon's sovereignty and freedom, declaring the country would no longer serve as a proxy or battleground in others' conflicts amid the ceasefire with Israel.

stories.title: Iran says its enriched uranium 'not going to be transferred'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated that Iran's enriched uranium stockpile would not be transferred anywhere, directly contradicting President Trump's claim that the U.S. would obtain the nuclear material.

stories.title: London insurers launch $1.2b war cover for Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: London-based insurers have launched $1.2 billion in war-risk coverage for shipping transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The ongoing conflict has significantly driven up insurance costs underpinning the global freight industry.

stories.title: First deportees from US arrive in Congo capital, sources say
stories.summary: The first migrants deported from the United States under a recent bilateral agreement arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo's capital early on Friday. Their arrival was confirmed by one of the deportees, a lawyer in contact with the group, and airport sources in Kinshasa.

stories.title: Decisions on Hormuz shape future conflicts – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that international decisions regarding the Strait of Hormuz will affect global shipping security and influence the behavior of aggressive actors in future conflicts. He called for united international efforts to address threats in the strait.

stories.title: PM, Erdogan emphasise importance of utilising ‘window of opportunity’ for lasting regional peace
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum. Both leaders emphasized utilizing the current diplomatic window to advance lasting regional peace amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.

stories.title: British police investigate security incident near London’s Israeli embassy
stories.summary: British police are investigating a security incident near the Israeli embassy in London. The embassy issued a statement confirming that all staff members were safe.

stories.title: NYC judge declines to dismiss case in 1979 disappearance of Jewish boy Etan Patz
stories.summary: A New York City judge declined to dismiss charges against Pedro Hernandez in the 1979 disappearance of six-year-old Etan Patz, setting the stage for a third trial in the decades-old case.

stories.title: Kremlin says Europe's drone cooperation with Ukraine shows its growing involvement in the war
stories.summary: The Kremlin accused European countries of deepening their involvement in the Ukraine war, citing Russia's Defence Ministry warnings about Ukrainian drone production sites across Europe and Britain. Moscow framed European drone cooperation with Kyiv as evidence of escalating continental engagement in the conflict.

stories.title: Donetsk was Russia’s safe rear. Now AI drones hunt its supply trucks.
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes are targeting Russian supply trucks in the Donetsk region using AI-guided drones, degrading Russian air defenses and leaving wide areas of Russia's rear defenseless against further aerial attacks.

stories.title: Winner Jerusalem Marathon 2026: A marathon of resilience in Israel’s capital
stories.summary: The 2026 Jerusalem Marathon proceeded after the Lebanon ceasefire and a security assessment allowed the event to go forward. Organizers framed the race as a demonstration of resilience in Israel's capital.

stories.title: Europe looks to secure shipping in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A coalition led by France and the United Kingdom announced readiness to lead an international naval mission to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. However, deployment of the force is not expected before the conclusion of the Iran war.

stories.title: As Strait of Hormuz reopens, Europe looks to secure shipping
stories.summary: A coalition led by France and the UK announced readiness to lead an international mission to secure shipping through the reopened Strait of Hormuz, though deployment would not occur until the Iran war concludes.

stories.title: Kremlin denies Putin is cut off from bad news after blogger's criticism goes viral
stories.summary: The Kremlin denied on Friday that President Vladimir Putin is shielded from negative information, responding to a viral accusation by a celebrity blogger. The blogger alleged that senior officials were not telling Putin the truth about Russia's domestic problems.

stories.title: Pro-Palestinian Tufts University graduate targeted by Trump admin returns to Turkey
stories.summary: A pro-Palestinian Tufts University PhD student whose visa was revoked over an anti-Israel op-ed has returned to Turkey after being held for weeks in the U.S. and having the case dropped.

stories.title: Will the ceasefire in Lebanon hold?
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel are holding their first direct talks in decades as both sides work to maintain the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Army pushes industry to share costs as GE seeks more funding for ITEP testing
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is urging defense industry partners to share development costs for the Improved Turbine Engine Program, as GE seeks additional government funding for testing. Maj. Gen. Clair Gill emphasized the Army's preference to focus spending on long-term procurement rather than bearing all development expenses.

stories.title: Trump says US to recover uranium from Iran, meet for further negotiations 'very soon'
stories.summary: President Trump said the U.S. would recover enriched uranium from Iran and meet for further negotiations 'very soon.' Iran's nuclear program is believed to possess more than 900 pounds of uranium enriched up to 60 percent, a major sticking point in talks.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Dnipro, three districts of Dnipropetrovsk region more than 40 times since morning, leaving one dead and 12 injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Dnipro and three districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 40 times in a single day, killing one person and injuring 12 others. The Dnipro, Nikopol, and Synelnykove districts were targeted.

stories.title: Pakistan raises $500m through Eurobond after 4-year hiatus
stories.summary: Pakistan raised $500 million through a Eurobond issuance, marking its return to international capital markets after a four-year absence. The three-year bond was issued under the country's Global Medium-Term Note Programme, coming one day after receiving $2 billion in assistance from Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Displaced family reunited with grandfather in Lebanon’s Tyre
stories.summary: A displaced family was reunited with their grandfather in the southern Lebanese city of Tyre following the conflict.

stories.title: More than 38,000 women, girls killed in Gaza war by end of 2025, UN says
stories.summary: The UN Women agency estimated that over 38,000 women and girls were killed in Gaza between October 2023 and December 2025 as a result of Israeli military operations. The total death toll recorded by Gaza's health ministry now exceeds 72,000.

stories.title: Iran Says Strait of Hormuz Is ‘Completely Open’
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to shipping, but uncertainty remains over whether the strategic waterway is truly accessible without conditions attached.

stories.title: Hungary's Magyar starts early EU talks to unblock funds
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced he would begin talks with EU officials in Budapest to unblock funds frozen by the bloc. The funds had been withheld due to disputes between the EU and Magyar's predecessor over rule-of-law concerns.

stories.title: Colombia's Petro will travel to Caracas next week
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro announced he will travel to Caracas on April 24 to meet with Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodríguez. The visit comes amid ongoing diplomatic engagement between Bogotá and the Venezuelan government.

stories.title: UN warns South Sudan at risk of ‘full-scale famine’ as fighting intensifies
stories.summary: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher warned that South Sudan faces the risk of full-scale famine as fighting intensifies and humanitarian needs grow across the country.

stories.title: Israel lifts wartime restrictions nationwide, authorizes Independence Day ceremonies
stories.summary: Israel lifted wartime restrictions nationwide and authorized Independence Day ceremonies. The IDF, Culture and Sports Minister Miki Zohar, and Defense Minister Israel Katz made the announcement on Friday.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran war victory boast has echoes of Bush’s ill-fated ‘mission accomplished’ claim
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed major sticking points with Iran have been resolved ahead of peace talks, but analysts have drawn comparisons to President George W. Bush's 2003 'mission accomplished' declaration during the Iraq War. Some of Trump's assertions about progress have been questioned.

stories.title: Russians shell Kherson region since morning, leaving four injured
stories.summary: Russian shelling of Ukraine's Kherson region injured four people over the course of the day. Ukrainian authorities initiated criminal proceedings in response to the attacks.

stories.title: Arizona judge backs key Republican election official in voting board fight
stories.summary: An Arizona judge ruled in favor of Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap, granting his office greater authority over elections. The decision could have significant implications for Arizona, a key battleground state that has faced disputes fueled by election conspiracy theories.

stories.title: ICJ 80th Anniversary: Antonio Guterres calls for law to be respected
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, speaking at The Hague to mark the 80th anniversary of the International Court of Justice, warned that international law is disintegrating before the world's eyes and called for it to be respected.

stories.title: Lockheed Martin nabs $105M ground system contract to support next-gen GPS
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin received a $105 million contract to upgrade its ground system supporting next-generation GPS IIIF satellites. The upgrade would allow Lockheed's AEP system to replace RTX's troubled OCX ground control program.

stories.title: Iran, Magyar, Mythos & the Pope
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz fully open for commercial trade, effectively ending a nearly seven-week blockade of the critical shipping lane. In response, President Trump imposed a U.S. blockade on Iranian ports, vowing to maintain it until a peace deal is finalized.

stories.title: Air Force unit executes test of Anduril’s semiautonomous combat drone
stories.summary: A U.S. Air Force unit conducted a test of Anduril's YFQ-44A, a semiautonomous jet-powered combat drone. The aircraft is designed to potentially fly alongside piloted fighter jets in future operations.

stories.title: Average of 47 women and girls killed daily during Gaza war, UN says
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that an average of 47 women and girls were killed daily during the Gaza war. More than 38,000 women and girls were killed in Gaza between October 2023 and December 2025, according to the UN figures.

stories.title: Iran to impose fees on ships permitted to cross Strait of Hormuz, negotiator says
stories.summary: Iran announced it will impose fees on commercial ships permitted to cross the Strait of Hormuz, according to the ISNA news agency. Negotiator Mahmoud Nabavian linked the waterway's opening to the Lebanon ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz open for commercial vessels after Lebanon deal
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi announced that the Strait of Hormuz was open to all commercial vessels for the remaining ceasefire period following a truce accord in Lebanon. It was unclear whether he referred to the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire or the earlier Iran-U.S. truce that began April 8.

stories.title: War update: 40 combat engagements on front line since morning, Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions remain most active
stories.summary: Since the start of the day, Russian forces launched 40 combat engagements along the front line in Ukraine. The Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions in eastern Ukraine saw the heaviest activity.

stories.title: World Cup fans will have to pay $150 for NY stadium train ticket, officials say
stories.summary: Officials announced that a roundtrip train ride between New York and Meadowlands stadium will cost World Cup fans $150 for the 58-kilometer journey, compared to the normal fare of $12.90.

stories.title: Spain's far-right Vox party secures first regional coalition deal with conservatives
stories.summary: Spain's far-right Vox party and the conservative People's Party reached a preliminary coalition agreement to govern the Extremadura region. The deal is the first of three regional coalitions being negotiated and could test the right-wing alliance's ability to challenge the ruling Socialists nationally.

stories.title: Euromaidan Press is one of 45 medias to receive support within the Ukraine Resilient Media Initiative
stories.summary: Euromaidan Press was selected as one of 45 Ukrainian media outlets to receive support through the Ukraine Resilient Media Initiative.

stories.title: Trump says ‘no sticking points at all,’ predicts deal with Iran could come in days
stories.summary: President Trump predicted a deal with Iran could come within days, claiming there are no sticking points. However, both U.S. and Iranian officials indicated that significant gaps remain between the two sides.

stories.title: New roads and artillery positions: Zelenskyy warns of military buildup in Belarus near Ukraine border
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky warned of a Russian military buildup in Belarus near the Ukrainian border, citing new roads and artillery positions detected by intelligence. Kyiv has communicated through diplomatic channels to Minsk that it is prepared to defend itself.

stories.title: US Congress extends controversial surveillance power under FISA for 10 days
stories.summary: The U.S. Congress extended surveillance authority under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) for 10 days, a measure long criticized for allowing intelligence agencies to collect citizen data without a warrant.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to share defense technologies and experience with Sweden – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky expressed Ukraine's readiness to share defense technologies and battlefield experience with Sweden. He emphasized interest in a long-term partnership and expanded cooperation in the defense-industrial sector.

stories.title: World reacts to Strait of Hormuz reopening amid US-Iran conflict
stories.summary: Politicians and industry leaders welcomed the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway whose traffic disruption had caused global oil prices to spike during the U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: When death becomes a statistic: Necropolitics in the age of moral silence
stories.summary: The article examines the concept of 'necropolitics,' analyzing how modern power structures reduce human casualties to statistics and collateral damage across conflict zones from the Middle East to sub-Saharan Africa.

stories.title: Tennessee advances ‘Judea and Samaria’ bill, sends measure to governor
stories.summary: The Tennessee state legislature advanced the 'Recognizing Judea and Samaria Act,' sending it to the governor. The bill would prohibit Tennessee state agencies from using the term 'West Bank' in official documents and products.

stories.title: Lebanon president says country no longer 'arena for anyone's wars'
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun declared in his first post-ceasefire speech that Lebanon is no longer an 'arena for anyone's wars.' He said Lebanon had reclaimed its decision-making sovereignty for the first time in nearly half a century.

stories.title: US Marine Corps releases video showcasing new Medium Landing Ship design
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps released a video showcasing the design of its new Medium Landing Ship. The vessel is intended to transport troops, equipment, and supplies to shorelines without requiring established port infrastructure.

stories.title: Significant differences remain between Iran-US, including on nuclear issues, senior Iranian official says
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that significant differences remain between Iran and the United States, particularly on nuclear issues. The official added that keeping the Strait of Hormuz open is conditional on U.S. adherence to ceasefire terms.

stories.title: Fighting instructions, acquisition reform and Iran: What we expect from Sea Air Space 2026
stories.summary: A preview of the 2026 Sea Air Space conference highlights expected discussions on Navy fighting instructions, acquisition reform, and the impact of the Iran conflict on naval strategy and procurement.

stories.title: Umerov, Indian FM discuss frontline situation, prospects for peace negotiations
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council Secretary Rustem Umerov met with Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar. They discussed the frontline situation in Ukraine and prospects for peace negotiations.

stories.title: Explainer-What's in the Lebanon ceasefire deal and will it hold?
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a US-backed ceasefire to halt fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah. The deal is intended to facilitate broader US-Iran negotiations but allows Israeli forces to maintain positions inside southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Your Investments: Can you attain financial freedom in Israel?
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post column examined financial independence strategies for residents of Israel. The piece was published ahead of Israeli Independence Day and focused on personal investment and financial planning.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A news quiz covers events from the week of April 11, including Hungary's elections, President Trump's remarks about the pope, and the war in Sudan entering its fourth year.

stories.title: Pakistan escorted Iranian negotiators home from peace talks amid concerns of Israeli attack, sources say
stories.summary: Pakistan's air force escorted Iranian negotiators home from inconclusive peace talks with the United States in Islamabad, deploying roughly two dozen jets and an airborne surveillance system. The operation was launched after Iranian officials expressed concerns that Israel might attempt to target their delegation.

stories.title: Trump says 'no sticking points' remain in Iran talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told AFP that there were 'no sticking points' remaining in peace negotiations with Iran and that a deal was 'very close.' His comments came as a ceasefire took effect in Lebanon and Tehran declared the Strait of Hormuz open to commercial shipping.

stories.title: EU to announce fourth element of security guarantees for Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Union plans to announce a fourth element of security guarantees for Ukraine on April 21 at a Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Luxembourg. The meeting will also address additional pressure on Russia.

stories.title: Shipping firms seek clarifications before crossing Hormuz
stories.summary: Shipping companies are seeking clarification on conditions for crossing the Strait of Hormuz, including the potential presence of mines and any requirements imposed by Iran.

stories.title: First loaded Iranian oil tankers exit Gulf since U.S. blockade: Kpler
stories.summary: Three Iranian oil tankers—the Deep Sea, Sonia I, and Diona—all under U.S. sanctions, passed through the Strait of Hormuz on April 15, 2026, according to tracking firm Kpler. The vessels had loaded crude at Iran's Kharg Island between April 2 and 9.

stories.title: Oil prices drop more than 10% and US stocks soar after Iran reopens Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Global oil prices dropped more than 10 percent and U.S. stock markets surged after Iran announced the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump welcomed the move but said the U.S. naval blockade would remain until a deal is reached.

stories.title: Two Israeli films to premiere at Tribeca in June
stories.summary: Two Israeli films — 'The Future to Come' by director Ruthy Pribar and 'Moishe Badhan' by Gidi Dar and Shuli Rand — have been selected to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival in New York in June.

stories.title: Two radars blinded, drone controls hit, ammo depots struck: Ukraine’s overnight campaign targets Russia’s command network
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck two Russian radar systems — a Nebo-M in Belgorod Oblast and a Podlyot in Rostov Oblast — as part of a multi-day campaign targeting Russia's command and surveillance network. Ammunition depots and drone control sites were also hit.

stories.title: What has Trump said ahead of possible US-Iran talks and what could it mean?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted statements claiming Iran would relinquish nuclear material and keep the Strait of Hormuz open ahead of possible U.S.-Iran negotiations. Details and conditions of any prospective deal remain unclear.

stories.title: Iran declares Hormuz open as Lebanon ceasefire begins
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz open to shipping as a ceasefire began in Lebanon. U.S. President Trump stated that Israel is 'prohibited' from attacking Lebanon under the truce arrangement.

stories.title: Zelensky imposes sanctions on 130 Russian military commanders, religious figures
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed decrees imposing sanctions on 130 Russian military commanders and religious figures. The targeted commanders are involved in missile attacks on Ukraine, while the religious figures are accused of justifying Russian aggression.

stories.title: Air Force secretary eyes multi-year deals for satellites, aircraft
stories.summary: U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink is pursuing multi-year procurement deals for satellites and aircraft. Pentagon officials are seeking congressional authorization to buy weapon systems through long-term contracts covering munitions, aircraft production, and spacecraft production.

stories.title: A new, forceful Pope Leo steps onto the world stage
stories.summary: Pope Leo adopted a forceful speaking style during a four-nation Africa tour, sharply denouncing war and inequality. His remarks drew repeated criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump, who called him 'terrible,' apparently in response to the pope's criticisms of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Fifteen South American people deported from the US arrive in DR Congo
stories.summary: Fifteen South American nationals deported from the United States arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are the first deportees sent to the DRC under a recently agreed arrangement between Washington and Kinshasa.

stories.title: UN chief welcomes Hormuz reopening, urges full freedom of navigation
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres welcomed Iran's agreement to stop blocking the Strait of Hormuz. His spokesman called it a step in the right direction and urged full restoration of international navigational rights in the waterway.

stories.title: The Iran War Comes for the ‘King of Chemicals’
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict in Iran is severely disrupting the chemical industry, an obscure but critically important sector. The war's impact on chemical supply chains is causing widespread economic consequences.

stories.title: Inside Kharg Island, Iran’s oil lifeline under threat
stories.summary: Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export terminal, faces heightened scrutiny as the U.S. maintains a blockade of Iranian ports. Reports focus on the impact on civilians living on and near the island.

stories.title: Kosovo approves troop contribution for Gaza stabilization force
stories.summary: Kosovo's parliament unanimously approved sending demining and security units to an international stabilization force being assembled for Gaza. Officials said the contribution mirrors the NATO support Kosovo received during its own post-war period with Serbia.

stories.title: After Lebanon truce, Iran says Hormuz ‘completely open’; US maintains naval blockade
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz 'completely open' following the Lebanon ceasefire, but the U.S. maintained its naval blockade and said mine-clearing operations were underway. Oil prices fell sharply, while shipping firms and the EU warned the situation remained unstable.

stories.title: IDF to continue to attack Hezbollah in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces indicated it will continue operations against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire. The military considers the Litani River an indefinite security line in case Lebanon cannot guarantee Hezbollah's disarmament.

stories.title: Without Chinese help, it will take years for Iran to have thousands of missiles
stories.summary: Analysts assess that without Chinese assistance, Iran would need years to rebuild a stockpile of thousands of missiles. Iran reportedly lost hundreds of billions in assets, and a U.S. deal calls for the removal of its 60% enriched uranium.

stories.title: IDF expects Hamas to enter disarmament process soon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces stated that it expects Hamas to enter a disarmament process in the near future. However, Hamas has not yet begun disarming, and it remains uncertain whether the group will follow through.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister: strait of Hormuz now ‘completely open’ to commercial vessels
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to commercial vessels, sending oil prices lower. Simultaneously, a new 10-day truce in Lebanon entered its first full day, while President Trump claimed Iran had agreed to suspend its nuclear program.

stories.title: Nearly 900 Rohingya refugees dead, missing in shipwrecks in 2025: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that nearly 900 Rohingya refugees were dead or missing in shipwrecks in 2025. The figure represents more than one in seven of the estimated 6,500 Rohingya who attempted sea crossings during the year.

stories.title: Police say no evidence found of reported gang-rape in Epsom
stories.summary: Surrey police said they found no evidence supporting reported claims of a gang-rape in Epsom that had triggered protests in the town. Officers continue to investigate a report that a woman in her 20s was raped by a group of men on April 11 after leaving a nightclub.

stories.title: Rachel Reeves to raise windfall tax on low-carbon electricity generators
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves plans to raise the windfall tax on low-carbon electricity generators to help limit household energy bills. The levy, introduced in 2022, targets excess profits from older renewable energy and nuclear plants that benefited from high electricity prices following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Lebanese prime minister vows full control of Beirut, restricting arms to state forces
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam announced that his government would take full control of the Beirut Governorate and restrict weapons to legitimate state forces. He described the decision as irrevocable and aimed at safeguarding citizens' safety and property.

stories.title: France denies entry to Palestinian human rights defender
stories.summary: France denied entry to Shawan Jabarin, general director of the Palestinian human rights organization Al-Haq. Jabarin had been invited to brief French officials on Israel's human rights record in Palestine.

stories.title: ‘Performative’ Berlin donor conference for Sudan causes backlash
stories.summary: A donor conference on Sudan held in Berlin drew criticism from activists and commentators over the lack of Sudanese representation. Concerns were also raised about which states were invited to participate in the conference.

stories.title: TotalEnergies workers strike in France over fuel prices
stories.summary: Workers at TotalEnergies in France went on strike over fuel prices. The company said seven stations, representing about 4 percent of its sites, were affected by the industrial action.

stories.title: Zelensky: EU loan unlock could fund expansion of Ukraine’s combat aviation
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine is preparing to expand its combat aviation with Swedish-made Gripen fighter jets. He stated that unblocking a European financial package for Ukraine would provide the necessary funding for the acquisition.

stories.title: Israeli drone strike kills one in south Lebanon on first full day of truce, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed one person in southern Lebanon on the first full day of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire. The strike occurred shortly before President Trump announced the U.S. had banned Israel from further bombing in Lebanon.

stories.title: Nearly 900 Rohingya refugees dead, missing in shipwrecks in 2025: UN
stories.summary: The UN refugee agency reported that nearly 900 Rohingya refugees were dead or missing due to shipwrecks in the Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal during 2025. Spokesman Babar Baloch disclosed the figures at a press briefing in Geneva.

stories.title: Israel says military operation against Hezbollah ‘still not complete’
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel's military operation against Hezbollah in Lebanon is still not complete. He warned that displaced residents returning to southern Lebanon could face renewed evacuations if fighting resumes.

stories.title: Iran war: France and UK to lead ‘defensive’ force for Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: France and the United Kingdom announced plans to lead a multinational defensive naval force to ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and French President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the initiative during international talks in Paris, emphasizing it would deploy only after lasting regional peace is achieved.

stories.title: Bullied for speaking Ukrainian, taken to camps, threatened with conscription: 19 children evacuated from Russian occupation
stories.summary: The organization Bring Kids Back UA evacuated 19 children from Russian-occupied territory in Ukraine. The children reportedly faced bullying for speaking Ukrainian, forced attendance at camps, and threats of conscription.

stories.title: 日本訪問中のNATO大使ら 米軍横須賀基地を視察
stories.summary: NATO ambassadors from 30 countries currently visiting Japan toured the U.S. Navy base in Yokosuka on April 17, inspecting a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier and discussing the U.S.-Japan alliance's role in Indo-Pacific security.

stories.title: US to recover uranium from Iran at a 'leisurely pace', Trump tells Reuters
stories.summary: President Trump told Reuters the U.S. would work with Iran to recover its enriched uranium at a 'leisurely pace,' describing plans to excavate material and bring it to the United States. He also referenced retrieving 'nuclear dust' very soon.

stories.title: Army’s HADES spy plane on track for first delivery later this year
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's HADES high-altitude spy plane is on track for its first delivery later this year. Flight testing of the first prototype is scheduled to begin this summer.

stories.title: India fails to pass bill to boost women’s representation after delimitation row
stories.summary: India's parliament failed to pass a constitutional amendment bill aimed at boosting women's representation through a 33% quota. Opposition parties accused Prime Minister Modi's BJP government of using the quota plan as a pretext for redrawing electoral boundaries through delimitation.

stories.title: Israel prohibited from 'bombing Lebanon any longer,' warns Trump
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Israel that it is prohibited from continuing to bomb Lebanon. Trump also confirmed that the United States plans to engage with Lebanon separately.

stories.title: Hours after ceasefire, a lifeline to south Lebanon reopens
stories.summary: A key route into southern Lebanon reopened hours after a ceasefire took effect between Israel and Hezbollah. Tens of thousands of displaced people are hoping to return home following the cessation of hostilities.

stories.title: Tens of thousands return to south Lebanon after ceasefire, defying Israeli warnings
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of displaced Lebanese residents began returning to southern Lebanon after a ceasefire took effect at midnight, defying Israeli warnings. Israel said its forces remain positioned south of the Litani River to monitor Hezbollah activity.

stories.title: Russian Stocks Slip After Iran Says Strait of Hormuz ‘Completely Open’ for Duration of Ceasefire
stories.summary: Russian energy stocks fell after Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz fully open for the duration of the ceasefire. Rosneft shares dropped over 4%, while Gazprom Neft fell nearly 3%, and Lukoil and Tatneft each declined more than 2%.

stories.title: Green Party strategist reveals plan for local elections and slams 'sectarian' claims
stories.summary: The UK Green Party launched its campaign for local elections scheduled for May 7. Elections coordinator Faaiz Hasan outlined the party's strategy and rejected what he called 'sectarian' accusations against the party.

stories.title: Zelensky: Conflict in Iran poses risks to Ukraine’s weapons supply
stories.summary: President Zelensky warned that the conflict in Iran poses risks to the supply of weapons to Ukraine. He noted that European partners are prepared to help find alternative solutions to address potential disruptions.

stories.title: Pope urges Cameroon to reject violence at mass that draws 120,000 people
stories.summary: Pope Leo urged Cameroonians to reject violence and show generosity during a mass attended by approximately 120,000 people in the port city of Douala. The event was the largest gathering of his four-nation Africa tour, held at Japoma Stadium under heavy security.

stories.title: Ukraine’s private-sector air defense groups downed their first jet Shahed — Russia’s drone that flies at 300+ km/h
stories.summary: A private-sector air defense group in Kharkiv Oblast shot down a jet-powered Shahed drone, which flies at speeds exceeding 300 km/h, marking the first such interception by a civilian enterprise. The network has expanded from 13 to 19 enterprises since March, integrated into Ukraine's Air Force command.

stories.title: UK: Footage used in Palestine Action trial contains 'perceived gaps', court hears
stories.summary: In a UK trial involving Palestine Action activists who raided an Elbit Systems factory in Bristol, a police officer testified that CCTV footage contained 'perceived gaps.' The officer described the company's surveillance system as 'not fit for purpose.'

stories.title: 9 firms win orbital AMTI deals, Space Force says
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force announced that nine firms have been awarded contracts for orbital Air and Missile Tracking Integration (AMTI) capabilities. The Space Force did not disclose when the contracts were awarded or the individual dollar values.

stories.title: Nigeria: Offa Bank Robbery - Saraki Denies Fresh Charges, Alleges Political Plot
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Senate President Bukola Saraki has denied involvement in the 2018 Offa bank robbery after fresh criminal charges were filed by the Kwara State Government. Saraki described the charges as politically motivated and an abuse of judicial process.

stories.title: Questions raised over whether £3.8m government grant awarded to Wrexham AFC was lawful
stories.summary: Questions have been raised about whether a £3.8 million UK government grant to Wrexham AFC, co-owned by Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, was lawfully awarded. The club received the stadium redevelopment grant without a contract or completed state aid assessment and has received £18 million in total taxpayer funding.

stories.title: Fallen idol: French singer Patrick Bruel accused of rape, sexual assault
stories.summary: French singer and actor Patrick Bruel, a longtime household name in France, faces charges of sexual assault and rape. Multiple accusations have emerged against the former teen heartthrob, while some members of his fanbase have publicly defended him.

stories.title: Iran opens Strait of Hormuz for remaining period of ceasefire, Iran’s Foreign Minister announces
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced the opening of the Strait of Hormuz to all vessels for the remaining duration of the ceasefire. The move follows the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire in Lebanon.

stories.title: Report: Russia’s aviation regulator asks Transport Ministry to ban power bank use on flights
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Air Transport Agency has asked the Transport Ministry to ban the use of power banks on aircraft. The request followed an incident on a Ural Airlines flight in which a power bank caught fire mid-flight.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Long ‘road to peace’ begins, as Trump says Israel ‘PROHIBITED’ from bombing Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu spoke of a long 'road to peace' as a 10-day ceasefire with Lebanon largely held. President Trump declared Israel 'prohibited' from bombing Lebanon, though Lebanese media reported an Israeli strike on a motorcycle.

stories.title: Canada T20 World Cup game under ICC scrutiny after corruption claim
stories.summary: The International Cricket Council is investigating Cricket Canada over match corruption allegations, including Canada's eight-wicket loss to New Zealand at the T20 World Cup in Chennai. The probe followed allegations highlighted in a Canadian Broadcasting Corporation documentary.

stories.title: Army exploring refueling requirement for Cheyenne II MV-75: Official
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is exploring how to develop an aerial refueling capability for the MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotor. Maj. Gen. Clair Gill, PAE of Maneuver Air, said the Army needs to solve its own logistical resupply challenges in the air since it currently lacks organic refueling assets.

stories.title: Supreme court sides with oil and gas firms in Louisiana coastal damage fight
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 8-0 in favor of oil and gas companies, including Chevron, in lawsuits over coastal land damage in Louisiana. The procedural decision grants the companies a new hearing in federal court after a state jury had ordered Chevron to pay over $740 million for coastal cleanup.

stories.title: EU to restore Syria relations, strengthen trade and security ties, document shows
stories.summary: The European Union plans to relaunch formal political contacts with Syria and pursue closer economic and security ties, according to a document seen by Reuters. The move marks a significant policy shift after years of frozen relations between Brussels and Damascus.

stories.title: LHC upholds govt’s policy abolishing free electricity units for power sector employees
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court upheld the Pakistani federal government's policy to monetize free electricity units previously provided to officers of the Water and Power Development Authority and power distribution companies. Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains ruled the benefit was a non-statutory perk that could be lawfully altered.

stories.title: 'Totally unfair' that EU countries making money on energy crunch: Former EU commissioner Breton
stories.summary: Former EU Internal Market Commissioner Thierry Breton criticized EU countries profiting from the energy crisis as "totally unfair." Breton, who helped drive the Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act, was among five figures subjected to U.S. travel bans, which he likened to McCarthyism.

stories.title: US Congress passes 10-day extension of surveillance law amid Republican infighting
