stories.title: China slams Japan for sending warship through Taiwan Strait
stories.summary: China condemned Japan for sending a warship through the Taiwan Strait, calling it a "deliberate provocation." Beijing lodged a formal protest with Tokyo, days after Japan announced its troops would join a major U.S.-Philippine military exercise for the first time.

stories.title: US warns Europe about delays in weapons deliveries due to war with Iran - Reuters
stories.summary: American officials informed European counterparts that some previously signed arms supply contracts will face delays due to the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: What we know about the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon. Details of the agreement's specific terms and enforcement mechanisms are still emerging.

stories.title: Russia is pulling strategic reserves to prop up a failing offensive, HUR says — and 20,000 troops is less than one month of its own losses
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence directorate (HUR) reports that Russia is deploying strategic reserves to sustain a failing offensive in Donetsk Oblast. Moscow missed its self-imposed April deadline to capture three cities in the region and has reportedly set a new target of September, while losing approximately 20,000 troops per month.

stories.title: Richard Desmond loses £1.3bn damages battle over national lottery licence
stories.summary: Media tycoon Richard Desmond lost his claim for up to £1.3 billion in damages from the UK Gambling Commission over its decision to award the national lottery licence to Allwyn. Mrs Justice Smith dismissed the case in a high court judgment that criticized failings by Desmond's legal team. Desmond has vowed to appeal.

stories.title: Turkey-Syria-Jordan deal revives historic Middle East railway
stories.summary: Turkey, Syria, and Jordan have agreed to modernize their railway networks, aiming to establish a transport corridor connecting Southern Europe to the Persian Gulf within five years.

stories.title: Prosecutors in a Minnesota county charge ICE agent with assault
stories.summary: Prosecutors in a Minnesota county have charged a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent with assault. The officer allegedly pointed a gun at two people in another vehicle along a highway.

stories.title: House approves short-term extension of surveillance law in blow to Republicans’ long-term plan – US politics live
stories.summary: The US House of Representatives voted to extend a controversial warrantless surveillance law through April 30 after 20 Republicans joined House Democrats to defeat longer-term renewal proposals of five years and 18 months.

stories.title: First Thing: Trump announces 10-day ceasefire in Lebanon after ‘excellent conversations’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire in Lebanon, to be followed by a meeting between Israeli and Lebanese leaders. The deal aims to facilitate progress toward a broader peace agreement between the US and Iran. The Lebanese army warned displaced residents against returning south due to intermittent shelling after the ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Asian airlines face ‘major headwind’ from jet fuel costs, forcing flight changes
stories.summary: Asian airlines are reducing flights, raising fares, and adjusting routes as the Iran war drives jet fuel prices sharply higher. Analysts note the region is particularly vulnerable because many Asian economies depend on Middle East fuel supplies, and some carriers lack hedging protections against sudden price spikes.

stories.title: Tai Po fire: owners’ group repeatedly protested against use of flammable materials
stories.summary: A public inquiry in Hong Kong heard that the owners' corporation of Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po had repeatedly urged renovation contractors to use fire-resistant materials before the city's deadliest fire in decades. Chairman Tony Tsui said residents were unable to compel contractor Prestige Construction to comply due to the absence of statutory requirements.

stories.title: Palestinians observe Prisoner’s Day amidst 83% increase in number of prisoners since October 2023
stories.summary: Palestinians marked Prisoner's Day as over 9,600 Palestinians, including 350 children, remain held in Israeli prisons, according to the Wafa news agency. Approximately half are detained without charge or trial. The number of Palestinian prisoners has risen 83% since October 2023.

stories.title: Australian soldier accused of war crimes in Afghanistan granted bail
stories.summary: An Australian court granted bail to former soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, who has been charged with murdering unarmed prisoners during operations in Afghanistan. Roberts-Smith, a Victoria Cross recipient, faces allegations stemming from a 2020 military report that uncovered torture and summary executions by Australian elite units.

stories.title: Residents report explosions in Crimea, strike documented near airfield at Cape Khersones – social media
stories.summary: Explosions were reported in occupied Crimea from the evening of April 16 into the night of April 17. A powerful strike was documented near the airfield at Cape Khersones, close to Sevastopol.

stories.title: Report: Apple warns Russian iPhone users that unofficial Telegram client Telega contains malicious code
stories.summary: Apple has reportedly warned iPhone users in Russia that Telega, an unofficial Telegram client, contains malicious code, according to the Telegram news channel Ostorozhno Novosti.

stories.title: Give theatre choreographers and movement directors their own awards, says union group
stories.summary: Equity's Choreographers and Movement Directors Network called for major theatre awards to create dedicated categories for choreographers and movement directors, arguing these artists are undervalued. The statement followed last weekend's Olivier Awards, where Fabian Aloise won best theatre choreographer for Evita at the London Palladium.

stories.title: Iranian women footballers have 'hope for future' in Australia
stories.summary: Seven members of Iran's national women's football delegation sought asylum in Australia after being labeled "traitors" in Iran for refusing to sing the national anthem.

stories.title: Russian businesses warn AI regulation bill would raise costs and restrict access to advanced technology
stories.summary: Major Russian companies and business associations have warned that a proposed bill on state regulation of artificial intelligence could raise costs and restrict access to advanced technology if passed in its current form.

stories.title: Lebanese return to devastated south as fragile 10-day truce takes hold
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of displaced Lebanese residents began returning to devastated areas in southern Lebanon as a fragile 10-day truce between Israel and Lebanon took effect. Hezbollah warned it has its "finger on the trigger" in case of Israeli violations of the temporary ceasefire.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz to meet President Erdogan, attend diplomacy forum on third leg of tour today
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and attend the Antalya Diplomacy Forum as part of a tri-nation tour. He will participate in a leaders' panel on managing global uncertainties and present Pakistan's perspective.

stories.title: Chinese ministry focuses on car standards to put industry in global driving seat
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology announced plans to accelerate the development of automotive technical standards over the next five years. Officials told state broadcaster CCTV in Beijing that the initiative aims to position China as a global rule-setter in the next-generation vehicle market.

stories.title: Soldier kills guard escorting him back to his unit in St. Petersburg, then is detained again
stories.summary: A Russian soldier who had fled his unit killed one of the military police guards escorting him back to his base in St. Petersburg. He was subsequently detained again, according to Russia's federal Investigative Committee.

stories.title: Canada T20 World Cup game in India under ICC scrutiny amid corruption claim
stories.summary: Canada's T20 World Cup match against New Zealand in India is under ICC scrutiny following corruption allegations against officials within Canadian cricket's governing structure.

stories.title: Russians strike port in Izmail, damaging production buildings and railway facilities
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the port in Izmail, Ukraine, on the night of April 17, damaging production buildings and railway facilities.

stories.title: As ceasefire holds, displaced Lebanese trickle home to find out what remains
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese civilians lined up to cross the destroyed Qasmiyeh Bridge over the Litani River after the Lebanese army bulldozed a new path. Returning residents expressed determination to stay on their land as the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon held.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia sign agreement to extend $3bn deposit
stories.summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed an agreement to extend a $3 billion deposit from the Saudi Fund for Development with the State Bank of Pakistan. Earlier in the week, Saudi Arabia also pledged an additional $3 billion in deposits and extended an existing $5 billion facility for three more years.

stories.title: 'Older women are in demand by younger men': Papers discuss dating trends
stories.summary: A press review covering multiple topics noted reactions to the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, UK food shortages linked to trade disruptions described as stemming from "Trump's war," and remarks attributed to US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The review also discussed contemporary dating trends involving age-gap relationships.

stories.title: Hong Kong authorities use drones to help raid illegal slaughterhouse in Yuen Long
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department used drones to raid an illegal slaughterhouse in Kam Tin, Yuen Long. Officers arrested the 67-year-old operator and seized 7.4 kilograms of goat meat and offal valued at approximately HK$3,000. The unlicensed premises were allegedly used to keep and slaughter goats for sale.

stories.title: Saudi wealth fund sells football club Al-Hilal
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund sold a 70 percent stake in football club Al-Hilal to Kingdom Holding Company. The deal was valued at 1.4 billion Saudi riyals.

stories.title: Australia scrambles to secure energy as war on Iran fuels uncertainty
stories.summary: Australia, which is heavily dependent on imported oil, is scrambling to secure energy supplies amid uncertainty driven by the ongoing war involving Iran. Officials are pursuing quick fixes ranging from regional diplomacy to measures such as free train rides to reduce fuel consumption.

stories.title: Spain announces it will not broadcast Eurovision due to Israel’s participation
stories.summary: Spain's public broadcaster RTVE announced it will not air the Eurovision Song Contest due to Israel's participation. This marks the first time Spain has declined to broadcast the event since it began participating in 1961.

stories.title: This Prisoners' Day, WB's mothers fear children may return dead
stories.summary: Palestinian Prisoners' Day this year focuses on administrative detention and legislation permitting the execution of prisoners. Mothers in the West Bank have expressed fears that their detained children may not return alive.

stories.title: Israeli settlers raid homes of displaced Palestinian communities near Jericho
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked homes of displaced Palestinian Bedouin families and chased shepherds in the Balqa area north of Jericho in the occupied West Bank, according to Wafa news agency. The families had previously been displaced in July 2025. OCHA reported over 1,700 Palestinians displaced by settler violence as of March 31.

stories.title: Countries to discuss Hormuz mission for when conflict ends
stories.summary: France and Britain are chairing a meeting in Paris of approximately 40 countries to discuss a potential multinational mission to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz once conditions allow, signaling allied readiness to the United States.

stories.title: China’s space station crew to ‘maximise opportunities’ with extra month in orbit
stories.summary: China's Tiangong space station crew aboard Shenzhou-21 will extend their mission by approximately one month, state broadcaster CCTV reported. The three astronauts launched from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre on October 31 and were originally scheduled to return at the end of this month after a six-month stay.

stories.title: Irfan Nooruddin: 'Much to be gained by having more women in India's highest parliamentary body'
stories.summary: Scholar Irfan Nooruddin of Georgetown University's School of Foreign Service discussed the potential benefits of increasing women's representation in India's highest parliamentary body. He framed institutional reform as a reconfiguration of incentives within India's federal democracy.

stories.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang warns Huawei chips for DeepSeek AI models would be ‘horrible’ for US
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warned on the Dwarkesh Podcast that if Chinese AI startup DeepSeek optimized its models on Huawei Technologies chips, it would be a detrimental outcome for the United States. Huang said China could become superior to the US if future AI models are built on Chinese technology standards rather than the American tech stack.

stories.title: ‘Fire Roses’: China only all-female cremation team challenges stereotypes, reshapes mortality views
stories.summary: A five-member all-female cremation team known as the Fire Roses operates at Beijing's Babaoshan Funeral Home, making it the only such team in China. Formed in 2022 with an average age of 28, the group works in extreme heat while challenging gender stereotypes in the funeral industry.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa region: Port equipment and homes damaged, nature reserve on fire
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a large-scale overnight drone attack on Ukraine's Odesa region, damaging port equipment, transport infrastructure, and residential buildings. A nature reserve in the area was also set on fire.

stories.title: Dubai says first flying taxi station completed
stories.summary: Dubai announced the completion of its first flying taxi station. Commercial operations using the aerial vehicles are expected to begin by the end of 2026.

stories.title: Turkey, Pakistan could become Israel's new enemy, analyst says
stories.summary: Israeli analyst Boaz Golani, writing in the daily Maariv, suggested that Turkey or Pakistan could emerge as Israel's next major adversary as Iran's role diminishes. The analysis points to shifting regional dynamics amid discussions about the end of the war on Iran.

stories.title: Victoria Beckham defends parenting amid rift with son Brooklyn
stories.summary: Victoria Beckham publicly defended her parenting amid reports of a rift with her eldest son Brooklyn, who reportedly criticized his parents in recent months.

stories.title: Myanmar frees over 4,000 prisoners in annual tradition
stories.summary: Myanmar's new president announced the release of over 4,000 prisoners as part of an annual amnesty tradition, calling for stability and reconciliation. Those freed include former President Win Myint.

stories.title: Pakistani prime minister welcomes ceasefire announcement
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif welcomed the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, crediting U.S. President Donald Trump's diplomatic efforts. Sharif reaffirmed Pakistan's support for Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity. The prime minister is currently on a diplomatic tour of the Middle East.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes fire station in Sumy region
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a fire and rescue station in Ukraine's Sumy region on the evening of April 16, damaging the building. No further details on casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: Prince Harry and Meghan meet survivors of Bondi Beach attack on final day of Australia trip
stories.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle met survivors of the Bondi Beach attack on the final day of their visit to Australia. Among those they spoke with was Elon Zizer, 40, who survived multiple gunshot wounds sustained while shielding his children.

stories.title: World Anti-Doping Agency targets India’s performance-enhancing drugs production
stories.summary: World Anti-Doping Agency chief Witold Banka visited New Delhi to address India's role as the largest global producer of performance-enhancing drugs. WADA is seeking cooperation with Indian agencies including the Central Bureau of Investigation to disrupt supply chains of doping substances.

stories.title: Religious war?
stories.summary: This article is an opinion piece analyzing the doctrinal justifications behind the attack on Iran. It suggests that supporters of "Greater Israel" within the U.S. administration pursued the conflict as a perceived religious obligation, framing the attack as part of a broader strategic sequence.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith’s comrades say he ordered them to execute unarmed civilians, court documents show
stories.summary: Australian soldiers told prosecutors they executed unarmed civilians at the orders of, or in complicity with, former SAS corporal Ben Roberts-Smith, according to a statement of facts filed in a New South Wales local court. Roberts-Smith, a Victoria Cross recipient, faces five charges of war crime murder allegedly committed during his service in Afghanistan.

stories.title: Australia refines its defense strategy and investment plan
stories.summary: The Australian government outlined a goal for defense spending to reach 3 percent of GDP by 2033–34 as part of a refined defense strategy and investment plan.

stories.title: Turning tides: Most Democrats voted to block aid to Israel
stories.summary: A majority of U.S. Senate Democrats voted in favor of bills to block weapons and bulldozer funding to Israel. However, the votes fell short of the threshold needed to pass the legislation.

stories.title: Europe leads postwar security talks
stories.summary: French and British leaders are chairing a meeting of approximately 40 countries focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz. The talks come as another round of US-Iran negotiations could take place as soon as this weekend, according to President Trump.

stories.title: Lebanon: Mass displacement after weeks of strikes
stories.summary: Following six weeks of Israeli strikes that displaced over one million people in Lebanon—roughly one-fifth of its population—some residents began moving back toward the south despite Lebanese army warnings. Private organizations have stepped in to provide aid as the country grapples with both the conflict's aftermath and a pre-existing economic crisis.

stories.title: War-delayed marathon-less Jerusalem Marathon takes over capital amid ceasefire
stories.summary: Jerusalem held a delayed marathon event during the ceasefire period, though the full marathon was canceled due to weather conditions. Freed hostage Rom Braslavski helped kick off the 10-kilometer race in the Israeli capital.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks minibus in Kherson
stories.summary: On the morning of April 17, a Russian drone struck a route minibus in the Dniprovskyi district of Kherson. The attack targeted a civilian vehicle in the city.

stories.title: BBC in Iran: 'Tehran does not think it has lost this war'
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Lyse Doucet reports from Tehran that Iranian leaders seek resolution to longstanding tensions with the United States but are unwilling to accept a deal on Washington's terms. Iranians broadly want an end to the animosity, though the government does not view itself as having lost the conflict.

stories.title: Polls find PM’s bloc far from majority, but most say Zionist opposition also falls short
stories.summary: Recent Israeli polls show Prime Minister Netanyahu's governing bloc falling short of a parliamentary majority, while the Zionist opposition also lacks enough support. A Channel 12 survey found that even coalition voters believe not enough has been done to help those financially affected by the war.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz 'open' following start of Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon took effect at midnight, with Iran subsequently declaring the Strait of Hormuz open for shipping. The Lebanese army reported Israeli violations of the truce.

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defenses down 147 out of 172 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted or jammed 147 of 172 Russian drones launched overnight. Impacts from a ballistic missile and 20 strike UAVs were recorded across eight locations in Ukraine.

stories.title: Tycoon Pan Shiyi slams China property ‘Ponzi’ as Evergrande boss pleads guilty
stories.summary: Property tycoon Pan Shiyi publicly criticized China's real estate development model as a "Ponzi scheme" in a WeChat post from the United States. His remarks came days after China Evergrande founder pleaded guilty in a fraud trial. Evergrande's 2021 collapse, involving over US$300 billion in debt, triggered a systemic property crisis.

stories.title: US-China tensions simmer, economy outperforms, Auto China begins
stories.summary: The US-China trade war continued this week as US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told lawmakers Washington is finalizing a multinational agreement on trade and critical minerals to reduce China's dominance over vital resources. Greer also sought a larger budget for trade investigations and suggested steps to reduce US farmers' dependence on Chinese orders.

stories.title: Will South Korea’s ‘Goldilocks’ missile dent China’s Middle East arms ambitions?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest South Korea's combat-proven, interoperable surface-to-air missiles could challenge China's efforts to sell defense systems in the Middle East. The US-Israel war on Iran has driven surging demand for air defense systems among Persian Gulf states seeking protection against Iranian aerial threats.

stories.title: Hectic diplomacy
stories.summary: Pakistani civil and military leaders are conducting shuttle diplomacy across multiple capitals to prevent the U.S.-Iran ceasefire from collapsing. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif visited Saudi Arabia and Qatar before heading to Turkey, as the international community watches efforts to stabilize the Middle East.

stories.title: Hong Kong Observatory issues amber rainstorm signal, warns of hail, violent gusts
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory issued an amber rainstorm warning on Friday afternoon and warned residents of potential hail and violent gusts as severe thunderstorms approached the city. The amber signal, the lowest tier in the three-level rainstorm warning system, was issued at 4:35 p.m.

stories.title: Sindh High Court sets aside conviction in sexual assault case
stories.summary: The Sindh High Court set aside a conviction in a sexual assault case involving a juvenile victim, citing failures by both the investigating officer and the victim's father that created reasonable doubt. The court criticized the lack of sensitivity in the investigation and the prosecution's handling of the case.

stories.title: Statue of Theodor Herzl vandalized in central Israel days before Independence Day
stories.summary: A statue of Theodor Herzl in central Israel was vandalized days before Independence Day. Investigators found that the vandals sawed off the bronze legs of the approximately seven-meter-tall statue in an apparent attempt to topple it.

stories.title: War update: 132 clashes on frontline over past day, fiercest fighting in Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Russian forces engaged in 132 combat clashes along the front lines on April 16. The fiercest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Overshadowed by Iran, Gaza stuck between war and peace
stories.summary: The conflict in Gaza has receded from international attention amid the war in Iran. Despite a six-month ceasefire, efforts to reach a lasting resolution to the Gaza conflict have stalled.

stories.title: After US rescues airmen in Iran, commando opens up about IDF’s own daring extractions
stories.summary: Following a U.S. operation rescuing airmen in Iran, a reservist combat medic from the IDF's Unit 669 helicopter rescue squad described the unit's rapid-response extraction missions. The commando detailed battlefield conditions and the mental toll of life-saving operations in two books chronicling his service.

stories.title: Policeman martyred, another wounded in Manghopir attack
stories.summary: A policeman was killed and another wounded in an armed attack in Karachi's Manghopir area. The West Zone DIG ruled out terrorism, attributing the attack to robbers attempting to evade arrest near Hub Canal. Sindh's chief minister ordered the immediate arrest of the perpetrators.

stories.title: Trump calls Russian mass strike on Ukraine “terrible”
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump described Russia's large-scale air attack on Ukraine on April 16 as "terrible." The comment came after widespread strikes across multiple Ukrainian regions.

stories.title: Trump hints at Islamabad trip if Iran deal is finalised
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump suggested he may visit Islamabad if a deal with Iran is finalized. Meanwhile, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Qatar's Emir in Doha, and Pakistan's military chief visited Tehran to meet Iran's parliament speaker, as Pakistan-led diplomacy gains global attention.

stories.title: Hong Kong to scrap fax messaging between police and fire services for emergencies
stories.summary: Hong Kong Security Secretary Chris Tang Ping-keung pledged to replace fax-based communications between police and fire services with a digital system and increase emergency call centre phone lines. The announcement followed an inquiry into a deadly November fire in Tai Po that revealed callers waited up to 15 minutes to be transferred.

stories.title: Yom HaZikaron: Stand with the Widows and Orphans of the Fallen - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Israel's annual Yom HaZikaron memorial day honored fallen soldiers and their families. The observance called attention to the ongoing needs of widows and orphans of those killed in service.

stories.title: France nears rocket artillery decision, plans ballistic missile by 2035
stories.summary: French defense leaders have prioritized acquiring a new rocket artillery system for land forces. France also plans to develop a ballistic missile capability by 2035.

stories.title: Moran Zaga: The Gulf states react to humiliation by Iran
stories.summary: Gulf states including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, which had pursued diplomatic stability with Tehran, are reassessing their approach after being adversely affected by Iran. Analyst Moran Zaga writes that these wealthy nations now face pressure to reconsider how they address the Iranian threat.

stories.title: India: Modi plan for women's quota in parliament fails vote
stories.summary: India's parliament voted down a constitutional amendment bill that would have added hundreds of seats and established a 33% women's quota in the Lok Sabha. Opposition parties accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP government of using the quota proposal as cover for redrawing the electoral map.

stories.title: India: Parliament votes on women's quota, delimitation amid opposition row
stories.summary: India's Modi government pushed key bills through Parliament that could redraw parliamentary seats and introduce a women's quota. Opposition parties raised objections, questioning the government's intentions behind the legislative push.

stories.title: Pakistan-flagged tanker first crude carrier to exit Hormuz with cargo since US curb
stories.summary: A Pakistan-flagged tanker, Shalamar, became the first crude carrier to exit the Strait of Hormuz with cargo since a US blockade began. The vessel carried approximately 450,000 barrels of crude loaded in the UAE.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1513: Russia kills 16 Ukrainian civilians overnight as Patriot crews ration interceptors
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed 16 Ukrainian civilians overnight as Ukrainian Patriot air defense crews reportedly rationed interceptor missiles. Separately, Austria joined an international tribunal examining Russian aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Prominent lawyer Raza Kazim passes away at 96
stories.summary: Raza Kazim, a prominent Pakistani lawyer, philosopher, and founder of the Sanjan Nagar Institute of Philosophy and Arts, passed away in Lahore at the age of 96. Born in Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh, he was active in the Indian Congress movement and later the Muslim League before joining the Pakistan Communist Party.

stories.title: Juvenile ID rule for MDCAT leaves parents fuming
stories.summary: Pakistan's Medical and Dental Council now requires candidates under 18 to obtain a Nadra-issued Juvenile Registration Card with biometric verification to sit the MDCAT-2026 exam. Parents and candidates have raised concerns about added costs, long queues, and the short validity of the cards, with around 200,000 aspirants potentially affected.

stories.title: G-7 finance chiefs push for ‘lasting peace’ in Middle East, warn of war’s economic damage
stories.summary: G-7 finance ministers called for a lasting peace in the Middle East while warning of the economic damage caused by ongoing conflict. The officials also discussed continued support for Ukraine and efforts to develop supply chains alternative to China for rare minerals.

stories.title: US military in Libya: Pursuing unity, or pressuring Russia?
stories.summary: Libya is hosting the U.S.-led Flintlock military exercise for the first time, with soldiers from both sides of the divided country participating. The exercise is driven by security concerns, economic interests, and competition with Russia.

stories.title: Macron expresses concern that Israel-Lebanon ceasefire 'already undermined'
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron expressed support for the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announced by President Trump but voiced concern that it may already be compromised by ongoing military operations. He called for the safety of civilian populations on both sides.

stories.title: Democrats move to impeach Hegseth over Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. House Democrats introduced six articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging an unauthorized war on Iran and abuse of power. The resolution, led by Rep. Yassamin Ansari of Arizona, is unlikely to pass given the Republican majority in the House.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,000 over past day
stories.summary: Russia's total estimated combat losses in its full-scale war against Ukraine have reached approximately 1,316,070 personnel as of April 17, 2026. Ukrainian officials reported around 1,000 Russian troops killed or wounded in the preceding 24 hours.

stories.title: Trump-Meloni relationship turn sour
stories.summary: The relationship between Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and US President Donald Trump has reportedly deteriorated. Meloni, once considered one of Trump's closest European allies, has fallen out of favor partly due to her criticism of the Iran war and her opposition to Trump's public disagreement with the Pope.

stories.title: Europe faces looming jet fuel shortage: 'Six weeks of fuel left', energy boss warns
stories.summary: Europe and Asia face a severe jet fuel shortage as the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, with one energy executive warning that Europe has approximately six weeks of fuel remaining. Rising costs have already prompted airlines worldwide to raise ticket prices, and widespread flight cancellations are possible ahead of the summer travel season.

stories.title: Pope blasts 'tyrants' ravaging the world
stories.summary: Pope Leo continued a four-nation tour of Africa, traveling to Douala, Cameroon's main port city, where the Vatican expected around 600,000 people to attend Mass. Days after being criticized on social media by US President Trump, the Pope spoke out against war during a visit to Cameroon's largest anglophone city.

stories.title: IDF uses Ro'em self-propelled howitzer artillery for first time in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces deployed the Ro'em self-propelled howitzer in southern Lebanon for the first time, declaring the firing an operational success. The military said the operation also helped develop new artillery fire responses for use in combat.

stories.title: France, UK host talks on securing Hormuz
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Keir Starmer chaired a meeting of approximately 40 non-belligerent countries in Paris to discuss securing the Strait of Hormuz. The strait's closure by both an Iranian blockade and a retaliatory US blockade has triggered what is described as the worst oil price shock in history.

stories.title: Netanyahu's coalition struggles to close gap against opposition for third week - poll
stories.summary: A recent poll shows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition continues to trail the opposition for a third consecutive week. Within the opposition bloc, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! party lost one seat to the Democrats, though no major shift occurred between the broader blocs.

stories.title: What Magyar's election win means for Hungary's economy and Europe
stories.summary: Peter Magyar's centre-right Tisza party won a landslide victory in Hungary over longtime Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's nationalist government. Magyar has pledged to repair Hungary's confrontational relationship with the European Union, potentially unlocking EU funding for both Hungary and Ukraine. Voters cited the stagnating economy as a key factor.

stories.title: Myanmar pardons over 4,000 prisoners, including deposed president
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government pardoned over 4,000 prisoners, including deposed President Win Myint. A lawyer for ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi said her jail sentence has been reduced. Such amnesties are customary in Myanmar around the country's New Year in April.

stories.title: Pakistan, Italy to combat cultural heritage smuggling
stories.summary: Pakistan and Italy are establishing a bilateral cooperation mechanism to combat smuggling of cultural heritage. The framework includes a liaison channel between Pakistan's FIA and Italy's Carabinieri TPC unit, along with intelligence sharing, specialized training, and technology transfer.

stories.title: Lebanon army reports number of ceasefire violations
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel took effect on Friday, though the Lebanese army reported several alleged violations in the southern border region. US President Trump announced the deal and invited both countries' leaders to the White House, which would mark the first high-level Lebanese-Israeli meeting in decades.

stories.title: Albanese’s visits to key allies have borne early fruits of fuel and fertiliser but ‘resilience’ is on the budget agenda
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's recent diplomatic visits to Singapore and Malaysia have yielded early results in securing fuel and fertiliser supplies. The trips come amid growing recognition that Australia is vulnerable to global disruptions, with resilience measures expected to feature prominently in the upcoming budget.

stories.title: Israel carries out 'massive' demolition in south Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli army carried out a large-scale demolition in the southern Lebanese town of Khiam in the Marjayoun district, hours after the ceasefire with Lebanon took effect, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: “Storm a treeline? Better to just take it apart with a Vampire” — drone battalion commander on how war changed in 2026
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone battalion commander using the call sign "Rumyn" described how warfare has evolved in 2026, with drone technology expanding the effective kill zone from 3 kilometers to significantly greater distances. He noted this shift reduces the need for traditional infantry assaults on fortified positions.

stories.title: Celebrate Israel at 78: Free game connecting Jewish hearts to the homeland - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: SparkIL released a free printable game to celebrate Israel's 78th Independence Day. The game is designed to foster conversation and connection to Israel among Jewish communities.

stories.title: Cameroon sees mass turnout for Pope Leo XIV visit as he calls for peace
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an open-air Mass before thousands of faithful at Bamenda's airfield in Cameroon on April 16, calling for a "decisive change of course" towards peace in the country.

stories.title: Iran war’s big winners: Wall Street, weapons firms, AI and green energy
stories.summary: Analysts note that Wall Street, weapons manufacturers, artificial intelligence firms, and green energy companies are experiencing a boom amid the ongoing Iran war. The broader global economic outlook for 2026, however, is described as grim if the conflict continues.

stories.title: Iran war exposes cost of Asia’s fossil fuel reliance
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving Iran is exposing the vulnerability of fossil-fuel-dependent Asian economies. Bangladesh has been forced into costly spot market LNG purchases, while Pakistan's solar expansion has reduced its fuel import costs. Analysts are urging a faster global transition to clean energy.

stories.title: Tens of thousands return to southern Lebanon: Report
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of displaced Lebanese citizens began returning to southern Lebanon following the ceasefire deal with Israel, despite warnings from the Lebanese army against returning due to continued Israeli attacks.

stories.title: Celebrate Israel with ChaiFlicks: A year of entertainment for just $48 - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jewish streaming service ChaiFlicks is offering a promotional annual subscription for $48 to mark Israeli independence celebrations. The platform features films and shows from Israel and around the world.

stories.title: Pakistan oil tanker becomes first to exit through Hormuz since US blockade began
stories.summary: A Pakistan-flagged tanker, the Shalamar, became the first vessel to exit the Strait of Hormuz with a crude cargo since a US blockade began on Monday. The Aframax-class vessel carried approximately 450,000 barrels of crude loaded at Das Island in the United Arab Emirates, passing south of Iran's Larak Island into the Gulf of Oman late Thursday.

stories.title: NA panel seeks review of high taxes on mobile phones
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance expressed concern over high taxes on mobile phones and directed the Tax Policy Office to report on the existing taxation structure. Committee chair Naveed Qamar noted that income tax on phones was effectively functioning as a sales tax, affecting affordability.

stories.title: Russian strike hits Dnipro, damages transport facility
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro, sparking a fire and damaging a transport facility, according to local authorities. No further details on casualties were immediately released.

stories.title: Will Bulgaria's election change the country's course?
stories.summary: Bulgaria will hold its eighth parliamentary election in five years on April 19. Former President Rumen Radev, who has taken pro-Russian stances in the past, is projected to win on a platform of fighting corruption.

stories.title: Indonesia’s Surabaya bans absentee fathers from public services for dodging child support
stories.summary: The Indonesian city of Surabaya in East Java bars men who fail to pay court-ordered child support from accessing public services. First introduced in 2023, the initiative has been applied to more than 8,000 men as divorce rates rise and single mothers struggle to collect support payments.

stories.title: How to Counter the Houthis Without Strengthening Them
stories.summary: An analysis argues the United States should avoid repeating past mistakes if drawn into military action in Yemen against the Houthis, officially known as Ansar Allah. Previous US-backed Saudi and Emirati campaigns from 2015 onward devastated civilians and paradoxically strengthened Houthi power. The piece recommends integrating force within a broader political and economic strategy.

stories.title: Govt admits up to seven hours of power outages
stories.summary: Pakistani Power Minister Awais Leghari confirmed six to seven hours of load shedding, nearly three times higher than previously announced. He attributed the shortfall of approximately 3,400 megawatts to a sudden demand surge, disrupted LNG imports linked to the Middle East crisis, and reduced water discharges.

stories.title: Lebanon truce takes effect as damaged Qasmiyeh bridge reopens
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel took effect on Friday. The Lebanese army reopened a single lane on the Qasmiyeh Bridge in southern Lebanon, a key crossing linking Tyre to the wider region that had been damaged by Israeli strikes.

stories.title: British PM Starmer faces calls to quit over Mandelson vetting
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces calls to resign over the appointment of Peter Mandelson as envoy to the United States, despite Mandelson's reported ties to China, Russia, and Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: Congo's Sassou-N'Guesso sworn in to fifth presidential term
stories.summary: Denis Sassou-N'Guesso was sworn in on Thursday to a fifth term as president of the Republic of the Congo.

stories.title: Kurdish political groups cautiously back Iraq conscription bill
stories.summary: Kurdish political groups in Iraq's Kurdistan Region have offered cautious support for a proposed military conscription bill in Baghdad. Responses remain mixed due to historical grievances and current economic pressures in the region.

stories.title: A week into Iran ceasefire, Israelis try to snap back as expected, but fear return to war
stories.summary: One week into a ceasefire in the Iran conflict, Israeli civilians are returning to normal routines after spending weeks in bomb shelters. Residents express resilience but also fear a resumption of hostilities amid uncertainty about the conflict's outcome.

stories.title: Reeling from war after synagogue wrecked, Iran’s Jews staying loyal to regime
stories.summary: A synagogue in Tehran was damaged during weeks of U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran, though its Torah scrolls reportedly survived unharmed. Iran's small Jewish community is holding an event honoring slain Iranians, expressing loyalty to the Iranian regime despite the destruction.

stories.title: Azov units disrupting Russian supply routes around Donetsk with drone strikes
stories.summary: Units of Ukraine's Azov Brigade, part of the National Guard's 1st Corps, are using attack drones to disrupt Russian supply routes around Donetsk. The operations target logistics networks and strike positions deep behind Russian lines.

stories.title: Winning in the Donbas: What Russia’s 2014–2015 Campaign Reveals About Modern War
stories.summary: An analysis of Russia's 2014–2015 Donbas campaign examines the continued relevance of land forces in modern warfare. The piece notes that the US-Israeli decapitation and airpower-centric campaign against Iran has not achieved strategic goals, raising questions about potential US ground force commitment amid a fragile ceasefire and naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Haiti hunger crisis deepens as almost 6 million face acute food insecurity
stories.summary: Nearly 6 million people in Haiti are expected to face acute food insecurity in the coming months, according to a new assessment published on April 16. Gang violence, mass displacement, and economic strain continue to drive a deepening humanitarian crisis in the Caribbean nation.

stories.title: Hong Kong to strengthen police coordination in animal abuse cases
stories.summary: Hong Kong's conservation officers will increase coordination with police for joint operations to investigate suspected animal abuse on private premises. The move follows an ombudsman's report that found existing investigation procedures ineffective in handling such cases.

stories.title: Europe has capacity to clear mines in Hormuz Strait, French Defence Minister says
stories.summary: French Defence Minister Catherine Vautrin stated that European countries including Belgium, the Netherlands, and France have mine clearance capabilities that could help secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Discussions on escort services for ships were set to take place in Paris.

stories.title: Vietnamese airline to lease up to 10 C909 jets in boost for Chinese aircraft maker
stories.summary: Vietnamese budget carrier VietJet Air agreed to lease up to 10 Chinese-made C909 regional jets through SPDB Financial Leasing, a subsidiary of Shanghai Pudong Development Bank. The deal boosts manufacturer Comac's efforts to compete internationally with Airbus and Boeing.

stories.title: Ukrainian marines strike Russian boats on Dnipro, neutralize 15 troops
stories.summary: Fighters from Ukraine's 40th Separate Marine Brigade used drones to attack two Russian boats attempting to cross the Dnipro River, neutralizing 15 enemy troops. The strikes targeted Russian waterborne movement along the river.

stories.title: Palestinian Prisoner’s Day: What happened in Palestine on April 17, 1971?
stories.summary: Palestinians marked Prisoner's Day on April 17, commemorating the date in 1971 significant to the prisoner rights movement. Nearly 10,000 Palestinian men, women, and children are currently held in Israeli prisons, with roughly a third detained without charge or trial.

stories.title: Sudan’s Prime Minister: This is the path out of the horrors of war
stories.summary: Sudanese Prime Minister Kamil Idris outlined his government's vision for ending the country's civil war, rebuilding infrastructure, and restoring civilian rule. His statement addressed both domestic and international audiences as Sudan's conflict continues.

stories.title: Malaysian man among 8 dead in Indonesian helicopter crash
stories.summary: A private Airbus H130 helicopter crashed in dense forest on Indonesia's Borneo island in West Kalimantan province, killing all eight people on board, including a Malaysian national. The aircraft, owned by Matthew Air Nusantara, lost contact shortly after departing from an oil plantation.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'I Was a Rubber Stamp, Not Decision Maker,' Diezani Tells UK Court
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke told a UK court that she served as a "rubber stamp" rather than a decision maker. She stated that contracts passed through multiple agencies before reaching her desk.

stories.title: Lebanese civilians force past barriers to reach southern Lebanon despite IDF warnings
stories.summary: Lebanese civilians who had fled northward during Israel's war with Hezbollah are pushing past barriers to return to southern Lebanon despite IDF warnings. Social media videos show crowds attempting to cross via a central bridge over the Litani River.

stories.title: Minister defends Starmer amid Mandelson revelations, saying vetting decision ‘utterly unacceptable’ – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Cabinet Office minister Darren Jones ordered an urgent review after revelations that the Foreign Office ignored security vetting advice regarding Lord Mandelson. Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to resign over the matter.

stories.title: Elderly man stabbed in the leg by attacker with knife in Sheung Wan
stories.summary: An 80-year-old man was stabbed in the leg and elbow by a knife-wielding attacker near Cosco Tower on Wing Lok Street in Hong Kong's Sheung Wan district. He was taken to Queen Mary Hospital for treatment. Police are searching for the suspect and the motive remains unknown.

stories.title: Australia did not receive US request to join operations against Iran
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said his country received no new US requests to participate in military operations against Iran. The statement responded to President Trump's criticism that Australia was "not there" regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: World Athletics blocks 11 athlete transfer requests to Turkiye
stories.summary: World Athletics rejected 11 athlete transfer requests to Türkiye, involving athletes from Kenya, Nigeria, and Jamaica. The governing body cited concerns over what it characterized as a government-backed recruitment drive by Türkiye.

stories.title: IAEA probing power loss at Zaporizhzhia NPP on Thursday
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency is investigating a temporary external power outage at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant that occurred on Thursday evening. The Russian-occupied facility has repeatedly faced power disruptions during the war.

stories.title: Burkina Faso dissolves more than 100 NGOs and civil society groups
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military government under Ibrahim Traoré has dissolved more than 100 NGOs and civil society organizations. Amnesty International condemned the move as a flagrant attack on basic rights.

stories.title: Harry and Meghan meet Bondi shooting survivors
stories.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle met survivors of the Bondi shooting on the fourth day of their visit to Australia. The couple paid tribute to the 15 people killed in the attack.

stories.title: Hong Kong-flagged oil tanker passes through Strait of Hormuz in test of US blockade
stories.summary: A Hong Kong-flagged oil tanker, AVA 6, passed through the Strait of Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman, appearing to test the U.S. blockade targeting vessels near Iranian ports. The tanker had departed from a UAE port and transited the strait on Thursday, according to Chinese maritime data firm Mingkun Technology.

stories.title: Myanmar frees Win Myint, cuts Aung San Suu Kyi’s prison term in broad-ranging amnesty deal
stories.summary: Myanmar freed former president Win Myint and reduced the prison sentence of former leader Aung San Suu Kyi as part of a broad amnesty releasing 4,335 prisoners. Win Myint had been detained since the 2021 military coup. The pardons were announced by the office of newly installed president Min Aung Hlaing.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: UN chief calls for Israel-Lebanon ceasefire to be ‘fully’ respected as it comes into effect
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire to be fully respected as it came into effect. The 10-day truce pauses fighting between Israel and Hezbollah that has killed over 2,100 Lebanese people and displaced more than 2.1 million.

stories.title: Mamdani’s wife Rama Duwaji apologizes for using slurs online as a teenager
stories.summary: Rama Duwaji, wife of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, apologized for using slurs on social media as a teenager. She did not address separate controversies involving social media posts related to Palestinian militants and October 7.

stories.title: Could the US withdraw from NATO?
stories.summary: The article examines the possibility of a US withdrawal from NATO, exploring the implications such a move could have for the transatlantic military alliance.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 49 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 49 of the US-Iran conflict, celebrations erupted across Lebanon as a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect, opening the door to negotiations on a longer-term Israel-Lebanon agreement.

stories.title: Russian strike on Chernihiv energy facility leaves 6,000 without power
stories.summary: A Russian strike on critical energy infrastructure in Chernihiv on the night of April 17 left approximately 6,000 residents without power. The attack sparked fires in the northern Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Lebanese officials had ‘good’ meeting with IMF, finance minister says
stories.summary: Lebanese officials held what Finance Minister described as a "good" meeting with the International Monetary Fund. Lebanon reaffirmed its commitment to working toward an IMF lending programme.

stories.title: Lebanese officials had 'good' meeting with IMF, finance minister says
stories.summary: Lebanese Finance Minister Yassine Jaber said on April 16 in Washington that his government had productive meetings with the International Monetary Fund this week. Lebanon remains committed to working toward an IMF lending program.

stories.title: Young South Sudanese models ‘take up space’ in quest to showcase talent
stories.summary: Young South Sudanese models aspire to walk international runways but face barriers including social conservatism and a lack of structural support for the fashion industry in their country.

stories.title: 7 arrested in crackdown on party rooms offering copyright-infringing karaoke sets
stories.summary: Hong Kong customs arrested seven people in an operation targeting party rooms offering karaoke sets with copyright-infringing songs. The operation, code-named "Magpie," involved over 100 officers who raided 14 party rooms, a bar, and two residences, seizing 28 suspected illegal devices.

stories.title: China woman sweeps wrong tomb, boy does homework at police station, courier ‘feeds’ village
stories.summary: During China's Tomb Sweeping Festival in April, a woman in Guangdong province discovered her family had been visiting the wrong grave for two years after being informed by a man from another village. The story is among several quirky anecdotes from daily life in China.

stories.title: US tech firms successfully lobbied EU to keep datacentre emissions secret
stories.summary: An investigation found that Microsoft and other U.S. tech companies successfully lobbied the European Union to keep environmental data from their datacentres secret. A confidentiality clause adopted nearly verbatim from industry demands was added to EU rules in 2024, hindering public scrutiny of datacentre emissions.

stories.title: Woman stranded in Dusseldorf after return UK flight blocked over Home Office admin error
stories.summary: Liza Tobay, a German woman who has lived in the UK for 15 years, was stranded in Düsseldorf after the Home Office mistakenly red-flagged her settled status. She was separated from her two-year-old daughter in Edinburgh while traveling with her six-year-old son.

stories.title: New test range opens for the startup-war era
stories.summary: A new 400,000-acre test range opened in Georgia, United States, designed to bring together startup companies, new technologies, and military operators in support of defense innovation.

stories.title: 10-day ceasefire deal between Israel and Lebanon takes effect
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has taken effect. U.S. President Donald Trump said he expected Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun to visit the White House within days.

stories.title: Trump administration attempts to deport Iranian media commentator Yousof Azizi
stories.summary: The Trump administration is seeking to deport Iranian media commentator Yousof Azizi from the United States. He is accused of having belonged to a group that supports Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Trump administration attempts to deport Iranian media commentator Yousof Azizi
stories.summary: The Trump administration said on April 16 it was attempting to deport Iranian academic and media commentator Yousof Azizi, alleging he lied on his visa application. A Muslim advocacy group criticized the detention as a crackdown on Iranian voices during the ongoing Iran war.

stories.title: Moldova, separatist Transdniestria make no progress on settlement
stories.summary: Talks between Moldova and its separatist Transdniestria region ended without progress on April 16 in Chisinau. The breakdown comes as Moldova continues pursuing European Union membership by 2030.

stories.title: US Senate vote shows why Israel must prioritize military independence - editorial
stories.summary: A U.S. Senate vote has prompted discussion about Israel's need to prioritize military independence. The editorial argues that self-reliance in defense is essential to ensuring Israel can uphold its security commitments on its own terms.

stories.title: Inside Israel’s prison system
stories.summary: As Palestinians marked Prisoners' Day, more than 9,600 Palestinians remained detained in Israeli prisons. The report examines conditions inside Israel's prison system.

stories.title: Iran women football players thank Australian government for protection
stories.summary: Two Iranian women's football players who stayed in Australia after the Asian Cup have thanked the Australian government for providing protection. They expressed a desire to rebuild their lives in safety.

stories.title: Israeli ambassador meets with France’s Marine Le Pen, extending outreach to Europe’s far-right
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to France held an unannounced meeting with Marine Le Pen in Paris, confirmed by the Israeli embassy to French outlet Le Parisien. The topics discussed were not disclosed, and the meeting represents continued Israeli outreach to European far-right leaders.

stories.title: ‘Vengeance for all’: How Iran’s Lego videos won narrative war against Trump
stories.summary: Iranian creators produced viral Lego-style videos that analysts say effectively targeted divisions in US politics during the Iran conflict. The videos are described as high-quality yet inexpensive to produce.

stories.title: Why are anti-war protests in the West muted on Iran?
stories.summary: Despite widespread global opposition to the Iran war, anti-war protests in Western countries have been notably smaller than those seen during the Gaza and Ukraine conflicts. Analysts attribute the muted response to fatigue, fear, and disillusionment.

stories.title: Hong Kong school to close in 2029 over Primary One enrolment shortfall
stories.summary: CCC Cheung Chau Church Kam Kong Primary School in Hong Kong will close in the 2029–30 academic year after failing to enroll enough Primary One pupils and not submitting a required survival plan. It will be the first of 15 under-enrolled schools barred from running subsidized P1 classes from September.

stories.title: 'The world is being ravaged by a handful of tyrants': Pope Leo XVI
stories.summary: Pope Leo XVI, during a visit to Cameroon, condemned world leaders for manipulating religion to justify war, stating that "the world is being ravaged by a handful of tyrants."

stories.title: What we know about the ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has taken effect, with Iran-backed Hezbollah expressing support for the truce. Negotiations between the United States and Iran continue alongside the ceasefire.

stories.title: 'Allies, not vassals': How Meloni's break with Trump became a political moment for Italy
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni faced a public rebuke from U.S. President Donald Trump over disagreements regarding the pope, Iran, and a defence deal with Israel. The rupture, building since the outbreak of the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, may serve Meloni's political interests ahead of Italy's 2027 elections.

stories.title: Congo’s Sassou Nguesso sworn in for fifth term
stories.summary: Denis Sassou Nguesso has been sworn in for a fifth term as president of the Republic of Congo, extending his decades-long hold on power in the Central African nation.

stories.title: Conference League: Strasbourg stun Mainz to reach historic semi-finals
stories.summary: RC Strasbourg overcame a two-goal deficit to defeat Germany's Mainz and reach the Europa Conference League semi-finals for the first time. Ivorian midfielder Abdoul Ouattara scored the equaliser as the Alsatian club advanced before their home crowd at the Meinau stadium.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces destroy Russian ground drone in Chasiv Yar
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces detected and destroyed a Russian Impuls-M ground-based robotic system in the city of Chasiv Yar in the Donetsk region. The incident highlights the growing use of unmanned ground vehicles in the conflict.

stories.title: ‘Safe haven’: Iranian soccer players who sought asylum in Australia thank supporters
stories.summary: Two Iranian women's soccer players, Fatemeh Pasandideh and Atefeh Ramezanisadeh, who sought asylum in Australia after the Asian Cup, thanked supporters and said they hope to continue their sporting careers in their new home.

stories.title: Poll: 62 percent of Israelis think war on Iran will restart
stories.summary: A poll published by Israeli daily Maariv found that 62 percent of Israelis believe the war on Iran will restart in the near future. Twenty-four percent thought fighting would not resume, while 14 percent were unsure.

stories.title: A Tale of Two Sisters
stories.summary: The article tells the story of Grace and Carol, two sisters in their eighties who became unexpected roommates after being displaced by war.

stories.title: Cameroon: Pope Leo Excoriates 'Tyrants' Waging War Instead of Peace
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned leaders waging war instead of pursuing peace, describing them as "tyrants" destroying the world. His remarks, which escalated his criticism of global violence, reportedly drew anger from U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: Senegal: The Goethe-Institut Opens its New Building in Dakar
stories.summary: The Goethe-Institut has opened a new building in Dakar, Senegal, designed by architect Francis Kéré. The structure features sustainable design using local earth-based materials blended with contemporary architectural elements.

stories.title: Two more Democrats qualify for California debate stage after Swalwell exits
stories.summary: Former California Attorney General Xavier Becerra and San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan qualified for next week's California gubernatorial primary debate after Representative Eric Swalwell, facing sexual assault allegations, dropped out of the race.

stories.title: Trump calls war on Iran a ‘little diversion’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump described the war on Iran, which has killed more than 2,000 people, as a "little diversion" during public remarks.

stories.title: Australian ex-soldier Roberts-Smith granted bail in Afghan war crimes case
stories.summary: Former Australian soldier Ben Roberts-Smith has been granted bail in a war crimes case. He faces accusations of murdering five people during military operations in Afghanistan.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'Since Buhari Completed His Eight Years, Tinubu Too Must Complete His Own' - Presidency
stories.summary: Nigeria's presidency has stated that President Tinubu, from Lagos in southern Nigeria, should be allowed to complete his term, just as former President Buhari from northern Nigeria completed his eight years in office.

stories.title: Myanmar’s junta chief-turned civilian president commutes all death sentences
stories.summary: Myanmar's junta leader Min Aung Hlaing, recently installed as civilian president, issued a blanket order commuting all death sentences. The military junta had resumed executions after overthrowing Aung San Suu Kyi's government in a 2021 coup. Critics describe the transition as a civilian rebranding of military rule.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Orders Arrest of Former Humanitarian Minister Farouq, Top Official Over Fraud Charges
stories.summary: A Nigerian court has ordered the arrest of former Humanitarian Affairs Minister Sadiya Farouq and a co-defendant after they failed to appear for arraignment on fraud charges.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda Signs Medicines Deal With Swiss Drug Maker
stories.summary: Rwanda has signed an agreement with Swiss pharmaceutical company Sandoz Group AG to ensure a stable supply of essential medicines. The deal covers antibiotics, cancer treatments, and other critical drugs.

stories.title: China’s energy mismatch
stories.summary: This article discusses China's food security vulnerabilities amid global supply disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and extreme weather. While China has sufficient staple grain supplies, Beijing acknowledged structural challenges including a weak processing industry and a lack of high-quality crop varieties.

stories.title: Ceasefire in Lebanon widely welcomed, Trump says may be 'historic day'
stories.summary: The 10-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel was widely welcomed internationally, with supportive statements from Egypt, Syria, Jordan, the Gulf Cooperation Council, and Iran. Tehran praised Pakistan's mediation efforts, and President Trump called it a potentially historic day.

stories.title: 699 children killed in Ukraine since start of full-scale war
stories.summary: Since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, 699 children have been killed and 2,457 have been injured, according to Ukrainian authorities.

stories.title: Trump says Iran has agreed to hand over its enriched uranium supply
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran has agreed to hand over its enriched uranium supply. He also announced a 10-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel beginning April 16.

stories.title: Netanyahu rejects demand by Hezbollah for full Israeli army withdrawal
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to a temporary ceasefire with Lebanon but rejected Hezbollah's demand for a full Israeli military withdrawal, stating Israel would maintain a security presence in Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Europe tests ‘third way’ on Hormuz without the US, Israel and Iran. Will it work?
stories.summary: France and Britain are convening a summit of more than 30 nations in Paris to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz without the involvement of the U.S., Israel, or Iran. Europe, while insisting it is not a party to the conflict, is contending with soaring energy prices and diverted munitions from Ukraine. China is among the Asian nations involved.

stories.title: US releases details of Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, Israel preserves right to self-defense
stories.summary: The United States has published details of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire agreement, which preserves Israel's right to self-defense. Both countries acknowledge that Hezbollah's activities must be curtailed and that only Lebanon's official security forces are authorized to carry weapons.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: 18 Dead After Commuter Omnibus Explodes on Bulawayo-Beitbridge Highway
stories.summary: At least 18 people died after a commuter minibus burst into flames on the Bulawayo-Beitbridge highway near Gwanda tollgate in Zimbabwe, according to police.

stories.title: China’s 3-satellite surveillance network, Hong Kong’s inflation surge: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: China released radar images confirming a three-satellite geosynchronous surveillance network, raising U.S. military concerns about tracking capabilities. Separately, Hong Kong experienced an inflation surge. These were among the South China Morning Post's top seven stories of the week.

stories.title: Africa: UN Peacekeeping Missions Under Strain As Funding Cuts and New Threats Grow
stories.summary: UN peacekeeping missions across Africa face growing strain from funding cuts and emerging threats including drone warfare. Operations in the Central African Republic and the disputed Abyei region are among those affected by shrinking resources.

stories.title: France arrests suspect over 1982 attack on Jewish restaurant
stories.summary: French authorities arrested Mahmoud Khader Abed Adra in connection with a 1982 attack on a Jewish restaurant. The suspect, sought for over four decades, was surrendered by Palestinian authorities.

stories.title: 10-day ceasefire deal between Israel, Lebanon takes effect
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he expected Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun to visit the White House within days, which would mark the first-ever meeting between the leaders of Israel and Lebanon. A 10-day ceasefire between the two countries has taken effect.

stories.title: Italy’s opposition leader, whose father is Jewish, backs PM in split with Trump over Israel and pope
stories.summary: Italian opposition leader Elly Schlein, whose father is Jewish, publicly backed Prime Minister Meloni's split with the Trump administration over Israel and the pope. Schlein stressed her opposition to the Iran war and supported the suspension of the Italy-Israel defense agreement.

stories.title: Hezbollah lawmaker demands end to Israeli attacks under ceasefire deal
stories.summary: Hezbollah lawmaker Ibrahim al-Moussawi said the ceasefire agreement must include a complete halt to Israeli hostilities across Lebanon. He stated the deal was reached under Iranian pressure, Pakistani efforts, and Saudi cooperation.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth reads fake Bible verse from Pulp Fiction
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth read aloud a prayer at an event that was drawn from a misquoted version of Ezekiel 25:17, a passage famously altered in the film Pulp Fiction.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith granted bail after being charged with five counts of war crime murder
stories.summary: Former Australian SAS corporal Ben Roberts-Smith, a Victoria Cross recipient, was granted bail from Silverwater prison after being charged with five counts of war crime murder. The charges relate to the alleged killing of unarmed civilians during his service in Afghanistan.

stories.title: US officials tell European countries to expect weapons delivery delays, sources say
stories.summary: U.S. officials have informed several European countries, including those in the Baltic region and Scandinavia, to expect delays in weapons deliveries. The specific causes and scope of the delays have not been publicly detailed.

stories.title: Celebrations in Lebanon as 10-day ceasefire with Israel begins
stories.summary: Celebratory gunfire was heard in Beirut as a 10-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel took effect. However, the Lebanese military reported violations of the truce shortly after it began.

stories.title: Cuba’s president says island does not wish for US aggression, but ready to fight
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel declared at a rally commemorating the 65th anniversary of the revolution's socialist declaration that Cuba does not seek U.S. military aggression but is prepared to defend itself. Hundreds attended the event amid what Díaz-Canel described as an extremely challenging moment.

stories.title: Trump says it is important for Pope to understand Iran is a global threat
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated it is important for the Pope to understand that Iran poses a global threat. The remarks come amid ongoing tensions between Trump and the Pope, who has been an outspoken critic of the war with Iran.

stories.title: Australia's most decorated living soldier granted bail over war crime charges
stories.summary: Ben Roberts-Smith, described as Australia's most decorated living soldier, has been granted bail while facing war crime charges. His lawyers argued he would be unable to properly prepare his defense from prison.

stories.title: How Israel’s war upended daily life in Lebanon
stories.summary: Residents of Beirut described how the Israeli military campaign against Lebanon has severely disrupted daily life across the country.

stories.title: Australia fuel watch tracker: check current petrol and diesel prices, service station outages and shipments – in charts
stories.summary: The Australian federal government has released fuel reserves, cut fuel excise taxes, and rolled out a national fuel security plan amid a fuel crisis. A tracking tool monitors petrol and diesel prices, service station outages, and fuel shipments across the country.

stories.title: US oil floats to top as Asia looks for Middle Eastern alternatives amid Iran war
stories.summary: Asian refiners, led by buyers in Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and Thailand, are increasingly purchasing U.S. crude oil to replace Middle Eastern supply disrupted by the Iran conflict. At least 60 million barrels of U.S. Gulf grades were bought for May loading as the region seeks alternatives.

stories.title: 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire may be extended by mutual agreement, US says
stories.summary: The United States said the 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon may be extended by mutual agreement of both parties. Officials indicated the pause is intended to enable negotiations toward a permanent security and peace agreement.

stories.title: Trump official defends seeking identities of Jews at Penn for campus antisemitism probe
stories.summary: A US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission official defended efforts to collect information on Jewish students at the University of Pennsylvania as part of a campus antisemitism probe, while critics warned against compiling lists of Jews.

stories.title: 10-day ceasefire between Israel, Lebanon takes effect
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect on Friday after being announced by U.S. President Donald Trump. Israel's attacks in Lebanon since March 2 have killed more than 2,100 people and displaced over 1.2 million, according to Lebanese authorities. Trump said he was trying to arrange the first-ever meeting between the Israeli and Lebanese leaders.

stories.title: Trump says he may go to Islamabad if Iran deal reached
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that he may travel to Islamabad if a deal with Iran is reached. Trump expressed an optimistic tone about the prospects for an agreement with Iran.

stories.title: US House votes to defy Trump, extend Haitians' temporary protections
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives voted to extend Temporary Protected Status for approximately 350,000 Haitians living in the United States, defying President Trump's immigration enforcement agenda. A handful of Republican members joined Democrats to pass the measure.

stories.title: Ukraine reports 957 new tuberculosis cases in March
stories.summary: Ukraine recorded 957 new tuberculosis cases in March 2026. The ongoing war has strained the country's public health infrastructure.

stories.title: WATCH: 'Not fringe youth': Hundreds of Israelis protest West Bank settler violence in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Hundreds of Israelis protested settler violence against Palestinians in a Tel Aviv demonstration. Activist Oded Papourish, injured in the West Bank village of Kusra, said settler violence relies on complicity from Israeli law enforcement.

stories.title: Tai Po probe: owners’ urged contractor for more fire-resistant materials ‘in vain’
stories.summary: At Hong Kong's inquiry into the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, testimony indicated that the owners' corporation had urged the contractor to use more fire-resistant materials but was unsuccessful. A former management committee chairman and a construction worker were set to testify on Friday.

stories.title: Pope Leo slams 'those who manipulate religion' for war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV issued a strong condemnation of leaders who manipulate religion to justify war, in remarks widely seen as directed at the Trump administration's biblical invocations regarding the US-Israeli war on Iran. He made the comments during a visit to Cameroon.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions Nicaragua government officials, others for alleged seizure of US property
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on five individuals and seven companies operating in Nicaragua's gold sector, including two sons of the country's co-presidents. The sanctions target alleged seizure of U.S. property in Nicaragua.

stories.title: Turkey, Pakistan could become Israel's new enemy, analyst says
stories.summary: Israeli analyst Boaz Golani wrote in Maariv that Turkey and Pakistan could become Israel's new adversaries, arguing the war on Iran has diminished Tehran's military capabilities and shifted regional dynamics.

stories.title: US to delay weapons deliveries to some European countries due to Iran war, sources say
stories.summary: The United States plans to delay weapons deliveries to several European countries, including nations in the Baltic region and Scandinavia, due to the ongoing war in Iran, according to anonymous sources.

stories.title: Report: Telegram works without a VPN for some users in Russia, but reason is unknown
stories.summary: On the evening of April 16, some Telegram users in Russia reported that the blocked messaging app was functioning without a VPN for several hours. The independent Russian outlet iStories documented the reports, though the reason for the restored access remains unknown.

stories.title: Israeli envoy to UN: ‘If we feel threatened, we will react'
stories.summary: Israel's UN Ambassador Danny Danon warned that Israel would react if it feels threatened, following the 10-day ceasefire with Lebanon. He said it was too early to confirm whether direct Israeli-Lebanese meetings would take place.

stories.title: Trump says Iran deal 'very close,' may go to Pakistan to sign
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said a deal with Iran is "very close" and suggested he may travel to Pakistan to sign it. Trump praised Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir for their role in brokering talks with Tehran.

stories.title: China warns of food security risks as Iran war threatens global supplies
stories.summary: China warned that its food supply could be vulnerable to global price spikes caused by extreme weather and the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. While staple grain stocks remain sufficient, Beijing identified structural weaknesses including a weak processing industry and insufficient high-quality crop varieties.

stories.title: Lebanese officials had 'good' meeting with IMF: finance minister
stories.summary: Lebanon's finance minister reported that government officials held productive meetings with the International Monetary Fund this week. Lebanon remains committed to working toward an IMF lending programme.

stories.title: Despair rises, trust in leadership falls for most Israelis after US-Iran ceasefire agreement - poll
stories.summary: A poll of Israeli citizens found rising despair and declining trust in leadership following the U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement, with most respondents expressing pessimism and fatigue and expecting the conflict to continue.

stories.title: ‘Trump forced Israel into a ceasefire’ with Lebanon
