stories.summary: Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Dan Caine announced that the US military will pursue vessels in the Pacific Ocean that are supporting Iran, including dark fleet ships carrying Iranian oil. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth was present at the Pentagon briefing.

stories.title: The Man Who Represents Post-Clerical Iran
stories.summary: The rise of Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr in Iran's political hierarchy signals the consolidation of a new type of post-clerical state. His ascent represents a shift in the nature of Iranian governance away from traditional clerical leadership.

stories.title: Starlink outage hit drone tests, exposing Pentagon’s growing reliance on SpaceX
stories.summary: A global Starlink satellite network outage last August disrupted U.S. Navy unmanned surface vessel tests off the coast of California, halting operations. The incident exposed the Pentagon's growing dependence on Elon Musk's SpaceX for critical military communications.

stories.title: Philippines corruption scandal suspect Zaldy Co arrested in Prague, Marcos says
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced that Zaldy Co, a former congressman implicated in a corruption scandal involving flood control projects, was arrested by authorities in Prague, Czech Republic. Efforts are under way to repatriate Co to the Philippines, where the case has sparked widespread public outrage.

stories.title: Iran war exposes weakened state of Britain's armed forces - explainer
stories.summary: An analysis of Britain's armed forces revealed their weakened state amid the Iran conflict. British Prime Minister Keir Starmer defended his government's record, stating he had implemented the largest sustained increase in military spending since the Cold War.

stories.title: 10-day Lebanon-Israel ceasefire announced by Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 10-day ceasefire set to begin at 21:00 GMT on Thursday. The truce is intended to enable negotiations toward a longer-term security arrangement.

stories.title: Israel tells Ukraine too late to seize Russian grain ship as it left Haifa — report
stories.summary: Reports indicate Israel informed Ukraine it was too late to seize a Russian grain ship allegedly carrying stolen Ukrainian grain after the vessel departed Haifa. Israeli authorities reportedly knew about the ship for two weeks before its arrival, potentially violating sanctions.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire as US pushes broader deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire beginning Thursday at 5 p.m. EST. Trump said the agreement followed discussions with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun aimed at advancing broader peace efforts.

stories.title: Lebanon's president refuses talks, Iran stockpiles cause concern
stories.summary: Lebanon's president reportedly refused to engage in talks, while concerns grew over Iran's stockpiling activities. The developments were highlighted in the Jerusalem Post's news roundup covering key regional security issues.

stories.title: Younger Americans, those informed by social media more antisemitic — poll
stories.summary: A new poll found that younger Americans and those who get news primarily from social media hold more antisemitic views. The survey also found that half of Democrats agreed with white supremacist Nick Fuentes's statement about US policy toward Israel.

stories.title: EU welcomes Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, urges respect for sovereignty
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen welcomed the 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon mediated by US President Trump. The EU urged full respect for Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.title: UAE to resume in-person schooling as Iran ceases attacks
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced plans to resume in-person schooling following Iran's cessation of attacks. The Gulf state had previously canceled International Baccalaureate exams in March due to the conflict.

stories.title: Rescue operations completed in Odesa after building struck three times by Russian drones
stories.summary: Emergency rescue operations concluded in Odesa after a high-rise residential building was struck three times by Russian drones over a two-day period. The building sustained two hits within 24 hours and an additional strike the day before.

stories.title: Three arrested after attempted arson at Iran International parent company office in London
stories.summary: Three individuals were arrested in London following an attempted arson attack on the office of Iran International's parent company in Wembley. An ignited container was thrown at the building on Wednesday, but no damage or injuries were reported.

stories.title: Foreign journalists push Israel's High Court to speed up ruling on Gaza access
stories.summary: Foreign journalists petitioned Israel's High Court of Justice to expedite a ruling on media access to Gaza. If a conditional order is granted, the Israeli state would be required to formally justify why journalists should not be permitted entry into the territory.

stories.title: Iran halts petrochemical exports until further notice
stories.summary: Iran announced it is halting petrochemical exports until further notice to prioritize domestic supply and prevent shortages of raw materials.

stories.title: ‘We're asking for our husbands' salaries’: The plight of soldiers' widows in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: In Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo, widows of fallen Congolese soldiers are living in a makeshift camp under plastic sheeting after fleeing Goma when M23 rebels captured the North Kivu capital in January 2025. The women are demanding access to their late husbands' pensions.

stories.title: Apple TV accused of whitewashing genocide after announcing new Israeli series
stories.summary: Apple TV faced online criticism after announcing a new Israeli series titled "Unconditional." Social media users accused the streaming platform of helping normalise Israel's image amid its ongoing military operations in the Middle East and North Africa region.

stories.title: South Africa arrests activist Kemi Seba, wanted by Benin for 'inciting rebellion'
stories.summary: South African police arrested pan-African and pro-Russian activist Kemi Seba, who is wanted by Benin for allegedly backing an attempted coup and inciting rebellion. Authorities in Pretoria have launched extradition proceedings to transfer him to Benin.

stories.title: Venezuela, Russia step up crude shipments, India benefits
stories.summary: Venezuela and Russia have increased crude oil shipments amid a global energy crisis caused by the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. India is reportedly the primary beneficiary, absorbing most of the additional supply from both countries.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill 17 across Ukraine in worst attack of 2026
stories.summary: Russian drone and missile strikes killed at least 17 people across Ukraine in what officials described as the worst such attack of 2026. Separately, a major Ukrainian drone attack on the Russian Black Sea port of Tuapse killed two people.

stories.title: Can Iran circumvent the US blockade? Routes and risks explained
stories.summary: Tehran is exploring alternative routes to maintain oil exports as the US blockade targets Iranian ports and shipping lanes near the Strait of Hormuz. The analysis examines the feasibility and risks of circumventing the American naval restrictions.

stories.title: Republicans block bid to halt Trump’s Iran war in House vote
stories.summary: Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked a Democratic-led resolution to halt President Trump's military campaign against Iran without congressional approval. The measure failed by a 214–213 vote, following a similar effort stopped in the Senate the previous day.

stories.title: Report: FSB unit linked to Navalny poisoning now controls Russia’s internet
stories.summary: According to a report by independent Russian outlet The Bell, the FSB's Second Service has taken control of Russia's internet infrastructure. The unit, previously linked to the poisoning of Alexei Navalny, is reportedly behind the blocking of WhatsApp and Telegram and a crackdown on VPNs.

stories.title: Germany’s TKMS, Spain’s Navantia to explore Spanish-based submarine production
stories.summary: Germany's TKMS and Spain's Navantia signed a memorandum of understanding to explore submarine production based in Spain. The two naval defense companies will assess whether closer industrial cooperation can make joint projects more efficient and cost-effective.

stories.title: At court’s behest, Ben Gvir agrees to reevaluate refusal to promote police detective
stories.summary: Following a court directive, Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir agreed to reevaluate his refusal to promote Chief Superintendent Ruti Hauslich within the police. The detective's attorney accused Ben Gvir of interfering in appointments to serve his political agenda.

stories.title: Israel escalates attacks on medics in Lebanon with deadly ‘quadruple tap’
stories.summary: The Lebanese health ministry reported that Israeli forces have killed 91 healthcare workers in Lebanon, including through repeated "quadruple tap" strikes targeting rescue teams responding to initial airstrikes. The ministry accused Israel of showing "total disregard" for international law protecting medical personnel.

stories.title: Russian blogger thanks Kremlin for watching her address to Putin, tells TV Rain she is ‘not with’ them
stories.summary: Russian blogger Victoria Bonya thanked the Kremlin for acknowledging her video address to President Vladimir Putin. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the address had been seen. Bonya later told TV Rain she is "not with" them.

stories.title: How did Israel's air defences perform against Iran's missiles?
stories.summary: An analysis assessed that Israel's multilayered air defense systems, while largely effective against Iranian missiles, showed signs of strain as the war extended and Iran adapted its tactics.

stories.title: Luhansk Court Jails Polish Man 13 Years for Fighting for Ukraine
stories.summary: A court in Russian-occupied Luhansk sentenced Polish national Krzysztof Flaczek, 47, to 13 years in prison for fighting on Ukraine's side. He was captured in November 2024 near the city of Chasiv Yar, according to Russia's Prosecutor General's Office.

stories.title: Teachers protest as Turkey buries school shooting victims
stories.summary: Teachers across Turkey staged protests after two school shootings killed a total of ten people. Authorities cracked down on social media and launched investigations into the attacks, which have shocked the nation.

stories.title: No date set for US-Iran talks, as Pakistan pushes to keep diplomacy alive
stories.summary: Pakistan's prime minister and army chief are traveling to meet key players involved in the US-Iran conflict in an effort to sustain diplomatic channels. No date has been set for direct US-Iran talks.

stories.title: Trump set to invite Israel and Lebanon leaders for White House talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced he will invite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to the White House for talks focused on achieving peace between the two countries.

stories.title: Either Russia’s air defense doesn’t work, or NATO is launching drones, says Russia’s Shoigu
stories.summary: Russia's Nikolai Shoigu suggested that either Russian air defenses are failing or NATO is launching drones into Russian territory. He invoked Article 51, which pertains to the right of self-defense under international law.

stories.title: Israeli court gives Ben-Gvir 10 days to explain why he blocked police officer's promotion
stories.summary: An Israeli court ordered National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir to explain within 10 days why he blocked a police officer's promotion. The order followed a day-long High Court session in which Ben-Gvir's legal team defended against petitions seeking his removal from office.

stories.title: High Court stops short of ousting Ben-Gvir, limits his influence in police matters
stories.summary: Israel's High Court declined to remove National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from office but significantly narrowed his authority over police affairs. The ruling allows Ben-Gvir to remain in his position while limiting the scope of his operational influence over the Israeli police.

stories.title: Lebanon and Syria – are deals possible? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that even a modest security arrangement between Lebanon and Syria could serve as a foundation for more substantive diplomacy over time.

stories.title: Pope lashes out at foreigners who exploit Africa
stories.summary: Pope Francis spoke forcefully during his visit to conflict-affected Cameroon, criticizing foreign actors who exploit Africa. The pontiff's remarks were unusually direct for the visit.

stories.title: Russia charges journalist and former TV producer with inciting terrorism over social media comments
stories.summary: Russian authorities have charged journalist and former television producer Kapitolina Averina with publicly inciting terrorism over social media comments. She has been held in a pretrial detention center in the Kaluga region since February 2026, according to Sever.Realii.

stories.title: President Zelensky honoured in the Netherlands for Ukraine’s fight for freedom
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was honored in the Netherlands for Ukraine's fight for freedom. The Roosevelt Foundation stated that Zelensky and Ukrainians are battling for the security of all of Europe.

stories.title: FM monitors ship with stolen grain, stays in contact with Israel
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is tracking the vessel Abinsk, which entered Israel's port of Haifa carrying wheat from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories. The ministry said it remains in constant contact with Israeli authorities regarding the shipment of allegedly stolen grain.

stories.title: US general clarifies Iranian ports under blockade, not Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A US general clarified that the American military is blockading Iranian ports specifically, not the entire Strait of Hormuz. The clarification addressed confusion about the scope of US naval operations in the region.

stories.title: Iran, US narrow differences after Pakistani mediation but splits remain: Senior Iranian official
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official said that US-Iran negotiations mediated by Pakistan have narrowed differences but significant splits remain. Key unresolved issues include Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile and the duration of proposed nuclear restrictions.

stories.title: Column | Lost in rhetoric
stories.summary: The article discusses how U.S. President Trump's rhetoric on Iran reflects a broader coarsening of global political discourse.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire, Trump says
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 10-day ceasefire starting Thursday at 5 PM EST, following calls with Israeli PM Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun. Trump did not mention Hezbollah in his statement.

stories.title: Trump says Israel agrees to 10-day Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel agreed to a 10-day ceasefire in Lebanon, with US President Trump inviting Israeli PM Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun to the White House for further talks. The announcement came amid continued violence, including strikes that killed a paramedic in Nabatieh.

stories.title: Zelenskyy receives international prize honouring his and Ukraine’s courage and resilience
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy received the International Four Freedoms Award, honoring his and Ukraine's courage and resilience amid the ongoing conflict with Russia.

stories.title: The Army is now relevant to the Pacific. Congress should budget accordingly.
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the U.S. Army has spent years restructuring itself for a potential conflict with China in the Pacific theater. The piece calls on Congress to align its budgeting with the service's evolving requirements for Pacific-focused weapons systems and capabilities.

stories.title: Drone attacks in Zaporizhzhia region kill one, injure another
stories.summary: Russian drone attacks struck two districts in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing one person and injuring another. The strikes targeted civilian areas in the southeastern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Danish Refugee Council warns 4 million more face displacement as aid drops
stories.summary: The Danish Refugee Council warned in Geneva that over four million people worldwide are projected to be newly displaced by the end of next year. The organization cited declining donor support for life-saving humanitarian aid as a key driver of the crisis.

stories.title: 'Lebanon is being held hostage to Hezbollah acting at Iran's behest'
stories.summary: Hezbollah drew Lebanon into war with Israel in early March 2025 and continues fighting despite setbacks suffered in 2024. Analysts are questioning whether the Lebanese government can succeed in disarming the Iran-backed militant group.

stories.title: Burkina Faso junta dissolves dozens of civil society groups
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's ruling military junta dissolved dozens of civil society organizations. Territorial Administration Minister Emile Zerbo said the dissolutions enforce existing regulations and warned non-compliant groups of legal penalties.

stories.title: Israeli shekel hits 30-year high against dollar
stories.summary: The Israeli shekel reached a 30-year high against the US dollar, driven by a resilient economy and positive growth outlook. The currency strengthened despite ongoing risks from the war with Iran and increased defense spending.

stories.title: Next chief executive Simon Wolfson paid record £7m last year
stories.summary: Next chief executive Simon Wolfson received a record pay package exceeding £7 million last year, with potential earnings of up to £9.27 million this year after the retailer increased his basic salary and bonuses. The company cited "sustained outperformance" and raised profit guidance by £8 million for the year to January 2027.

stories.title: Lebanon, Hezbollah, Israel: Negotiations at gunpoint
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab depicting the dynamics of negotiations between Lebanon, Hezbollah, and Israel as taking place under the threat of force.

stories.title: India-Zambia talks on critical minerals stall over mining rights: sources
stories.summary: Talks between India and Zambia over critical mineral mining rights have stalled over disagreements on mining access. Sources said New Delhi is attempting to restart discussions, but the situation remains uncertain.

stories.title: US missile defences may take years to rebuild after Iran war
stories.summary: An analysis found that US and allied missile defense systems may take years to rebuild after thousands of interceptors were deployed to counter Iranian attacks during the six-week conflict.

stories.title: Gaza’s war amputees short of prostheses under Israeli restrictions
stories.summary: In Gaza City, 14-year-old Fadel al-Naji lost both legs in an Israeli drone strike in September, while his 11-year-old brother lost an eye in the same attack. War amputees in Gaza face severe shortages of prosthetic devices due to Israeli restrictions on supplies entering the territory.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF kills three Hamas commanders in Gaza strikes this week
stories.summary: The IDF announced it killed three Hamas commanders in strikes on Gaza during the week. According to the military, the commanders were actively involved in rebuilding Hamas's military capabilities and planning imminent attacks against Israeli forces.

stories.title: Soviet 14th Army’s heirs just became persona non grata in Moldova
stories.summary: Moldova declared personnel linked to the legacy of the Soviet 14th Army as persona non grata. The decision by Chișinău targets individuals associated with the Russian-backed military presence in the breakaway Transnistria region along the Dniester River.

stories.title: Hegseth warns US ready to resume fighting ‘with more power than ever’ if Tehran spurns deal
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that Washington is prepared to resume military operations against Iran "with more power than ever" if Tehran rejects a deal. Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine announced the US Navy will actively pursue vessels serving Iranian interests worldwide.

stories.title: Pope Leo to hold peace meeting in Cameroon amid Trump attacks
stories.summary: Pope Leo held a peace meeting in Cameroon and urged the country's government to combat corruption and resist undue influence from the wealthy and powerful. The visit took place amid ongoing tensions with the Trump administration.

stories.title: Vance criticised for ‘inaccurate’ claim that Gaza aid is highest in five years
stories.summary: Gaza's Government Media Office condemned US Vice President JD Vance's claim that humanitarian aid entering the Strip is at its highest level in five years, calling his remarks "inaccurate and misleading" and bearing "no relation to reality."

stories.title: PM Shehbaz meets Qatar emir, stresses importance of de-escalation, dialogue amid regional situation
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Doha, emphasizing the need for de-escalation and dialogue amid regional tensions. The meeting was part of Sharif's official visits to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Türkiye from April 15 to 18.

stories.title: Senate Democrats move to stall Trump’s ‘absurd’ bid to install new Fed chair
stories.summary: Senate Democrats moved to delay the confirmation hearing of Kevin Warsh, Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, calling the bid "absurd." Democratic lawmakers on the banking committee urged Republican leadership to postpone the hearing while the Fed faces criminal investigations.

stories.title: In tough times, Russians are turning to witchcraft
stories.summary: Demand for crystal balls and protective amulets in Russia more than doubled in 2025 as Russians increasingly turn to witchcraft and occult practices during difficult times.

stories.title: IHC expresses displeasure over cutting of trees in Islamabad in violation of previous orders
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court expressed displeasure over continued tree cutting in the federal capital despite injunction orders issued on January 15 and April 8. Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro warned authorities of contempt proceedings if violations by the Capital Development Authority continued.

stories.title: Zionist militia frequently contacted Nazi Germany, Israeli documents reveal
stories.summary: Declassified Israeli documents reported by Haaretz reveal that the Stern Gang, a Zionist militia active during the British Mandate period, maintained frequent contacts with Nazi Germany. The files shed further light on the historical relationship between the group and Hitler's government.

stories.title: A Warning from Auschwitz
stories.summary: Sylvan Adams led a call against rising antisemitism at the March of the Living event at Auschwitz. He warned that failure to act risks creating a new generation of survivors.

stories.title: Epsom church minister condemns ‘intimidating’ protest over alleged gang-rape
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters gathered in Epsom, Surrey, to demand information from police about suspects in an alleged gang-rape of a woman in her 20s outside Epsom Methodist church. The church's minister, Rev. Catherine Hutton, condemned the demonstration as "intimidating."

stories.title: Bulgaria's pro-Russian former president leads election race on anti-graft ticket
stories.summary: Former Bulgarian president and pro-Russian figure leads the country's upcoming election race, campaigning on an anti-corruption platform. In rural southern Bulgaria, voters like farmer Nikolay Vasiliev expressed frustration with persistent graft and a stagnant economy that revolving governments in Sofia have failed to address.

stories.title: Syria takes control of all bases where US forces were deployed
stories.summary: The final convoy of US soldiers and equipment departed Qasrak air base in the northeastern Hasakah governorate, completing the US military withdrawal from Syria. Syrian authorities have assumed control of all bases previously occupied by American forces.

stories.title: US military fully withdraws from Syria after 10 years
stories.summary: The last remaining US military personnel and equipment exited Syria via Jordan after a decade-long presence, completing the full American withdrawal. Syrian authorities moved to take control of the final US-held base.

stories.title: London mayor dodges Nakba march dispute between police, orgs
stories.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan's office declined to weigh in on a dispute between police and organizations over policing of a Nakba march, stating that protest policing is an operational matter for the Metropolitan Police.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopian Editor Seized From Addis Standard Newsroom By Unidentified Men
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists has called on Ethiopian authorities to locate and free Addis Standard managing editor Million Beyene, who was seized by unidentified men from his newsroom in Addis Ababa on Wednesday.

stories.title: Gaza’s war amputees short of prostheses under Israeli restrictions
stories.summary: Gaza has nearly 5,000 war amputees, approximately a quarter of whom are children. Israeli restrictions are limiting access to prosthetic limbs for those injured in the conflict.

stories.title: MEP: Hungary stands to gain from Ukraine’s EU accession
stories.summary: A member of the European Parliament argued that Hungary stands to gain economically from Ukraine's accession to the EU. The MEP noted that EU history shows all member states have benefited when neighboring countries joined the bloc.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone forces claim 16-target overnight strike – Iskander bases, air defenses, and a Rubikon workshop
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces claimed to have struck 16 Russian military targets overnight in an operation spanning Crimea, Donetsk, and Zaporizhzhia. Targets included Iskander missile bases, air defense systems, and a Rubikon workshop, coordinated through a newly established deep strike center.

stories.title: Lebanon president had phone call with Trump, thanked him for 'efforts' towards ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun spoke by phone with U.S. President Donald Trump, thanking him for efforts toward securing a ceasefire with Israel. Aoun had previously rejected a U.S. request to speak directly with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

stories.title: Current account posts surplus of $1.07bn in March
stories.summary: Pakistan recorded a current account surplus of $1.07 billion in March 2026, up from $231 million in February, according to the State Bank of Pakistan. Finance adviser Khurram Schehzad called it the third consecutive monthly surplus of 2026 and among the strongest monthly outcomes on record.

stories.title: 3 arrested after attempted arson at London Persian media office
stories.summary: Three people were arrested in London following an attempted arson at the office of a Persian-language media outlet. Police are investigating the incident amid growing concerns over threats to journalists critical of the Iranian government.

stories.title: Russia escalates internet crackdown, says curbs are temporary
stories.summary: The Kremlin acknowledged on Tuesday that internet restrictions have disrupted daily life for many Russians but described them as temporary security measures. Authorities shut down mobile internet in Moscow for nearly three weeks in March, citing the risk that Ukrainian drones could use cellular networks to guide attacks. Regular mobile internet blackouts have also occurred in other parts of the country.

stories.title: Space-based missile defense may cost too much for Golden Dome’s 12-figure spending plan
stories.summary: Questions have emerged about the affordability of space-based missile defense systems proposed under the Golden Dome program, which carries a 12-figure spending plan. The program's czar has acknowledged uncertainty about whether the ambitious technology can be produced at a manageable cost.

stories.title: RFK Jr once cut penis off ‘road-killed raccoon’ in New York, new book reveals
stories.summary: A new book reveals that Robert F. Kennedy Jr., now U.S. health secretary, described in a 2001 diary entry cutting the penis off a road-killed raccoon on a New York highway to "study" later, with his children present in the car.

stories.title: Trump says Israel and Lebanon agree to temporary ceasefire
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire beginning Thursday. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam welcomed the announcement of the temporary truce.

stories.title: Israel says it’s West’s defender, but cares little for European critics
stories.summary: Israel has positioned itself as a defender of Western interests, but its expanding military operations and strained relations with traditional European allies have deepened international criticism and diplomatic isolation.

stories.title: Turkey launches internet crackdown ahead of funerals for shooting victims
stories.summary: Turkey launched an internet crackdown ahead of funerals for victims of a recent shooting in the southern province of Kahramanmaras. The incident was the second such attack in the country within a week.

stories.title: Jet fuel shortage: Why Iran war could ground flights in Europe
stories.summary: Tensions around the Strait of Hormuz are threatening jet fuel supplies to Europe, raising the prospect of flight disruptions and groundings as the summer travel season begins.

stories.title: PA said to extradite to France key suspect in 1982 Paris antisemitic terror attack
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority reportedly extradited Hicham Harb to France in connection with the 1982 attack on the Jo Goldenberg restaurant in Paris, which killed six people. Harb, suspected of leading the gunmen, had been arrested by PA forces in September.

stories.title: Lebanon's Aoun rejects call with Netanyahu as Israel severs last bridge to the south
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun rejected a proposed phone call with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu even as Israel destroyed the last operational bridge over the Litani River in southern Lebanon. The Israeli army was reportedly preparing for a ceasefire set to begin Thursday evening.

stories.title: Iran says talks with US remain inconclusive, denies truce extension
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei denied reports of an agreement with the United States to extend a temporary ceasefire, stating that negotiations between the two countries remain unresolved.

stories.title: Thousands of bees swarm southern Israel
stories.summary: Thousands of bees have been documented swarming the southern Israeli city of Netivot. Residents have been recording and sharing footage of the unusual swarm event.

stories.title: Millionaires fund last-ditch attempt to save humpback whale stranded in Germany
stories.summary: A rescue effort is under way in Germany's Baltic Sea to save a male humpback whale nicknamed Tommy (originally Timmy) that has repeatedly become stranded near Timmendorfer Strand. The operation is funded by millionaires but has drawn criticism from experts who say it is unlikely to succeed and could further harm the 12-tonne animal.

stories.title: Combined attack on Kyiv: casualties rise to 62, four killed
stories.summary: A combined Russian military attack on Kyiv resulted in four deaths and injured a total of 62 people. The casualty toll rose as rescue operations continued in the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Europe has 'maybe six weeks of jet fuel left', energy boss warns
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency warned that Europe may have only about six weeks of jet fuel reserves remaining. The agency's energy chief cautioned that flight cancellations could follow if fuel supplies from the Gulf region continue to be blocked.

stories.title: WATCH: US ready to restart combat if no Iran deal reached, Hegseth says
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the United States is prepared to resume combat operations if no deal is reached with Iran. Hegseth directly addressed Iranian leadership, stating that American military capabilities far exceed Iran's and warning that Washington is closely monitoring Tehran.

stories.title: Army making ‘significant headway’ in ATI aviation overhaul
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has divested nearly 60 percent of its Apache D model helicopters over the past year as part of its Aviation Transformation Initiative overhaul, according to Col. Tim Jaeger, director of Army aviation at the G3/5/7. Officials described the restructuring as making "significant headway."

stories.title: No date set for second round of US-Iran talks, FO says
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said no date has been set for a second round of US-Iran talks. He noted that nuclear issues are among subjects under discussion and emphasized that Pakistan would not comment on the negotiating positions of either party, citing the importance of trust and secrecy.

stories.title: On the Radar: A Border Dispute Creates Criminal Opportunity
stories.summary: A Colombia-Ecuador trade dispute is fueling contraband activity along their shared border. Separately, Peru's upcoming election highlights the state's struggle to contain crime, while illegal mining linked to cocaine trafficking is expanding in Costa Rica.

stories.title: Syria says has taken over all bases previously hosting US forces
stories.summary: Syria announced it has taken control of all military bases that previously hosted U.S. forces deployed as part of the anti-Islamic State group coalition in the country.

stories.title: Syria takes over northeast base after int'l coalition pullout
stories.summary: Syrian government forces took control of the Qasrak base in the northeast after US-led international coalition forces withdrew. Kurdish forces in the area are integrating into the Syrian state as the government expands its territorial control.

stories.title: Hamas bomber, PFLP commander exchanged for Oct. 7 hostages to speak at Argentina trade union HQ
stories.summary: Hamas operative Osman Bilal and PFLP commander Nader Sadaqa, released in exchange for October 7 hostages, are scheduled to speak at an Argentine trade union headquarters. The event organizer, Action for Palestine, listed the two as 'Palestinian activists and former prisoners.'

stories.title: Turkiye to hold funerals for school shooting victims
stories.summary: Turkey held funerals for victims of recent school shootings. The article references past mass violence incidents, including a 2014 attack near the University of California, Santa Barbara.

stories.title: Hong Kong leader John Lee, EU officials meet to discuss trade, cooperation
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee met with EU officials, including EU Office head Ambassador Harvey Rouse, to discuss trade and cooperation opportunities. Both sides emphasized multilateralism amid rising global tensions and market instability.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lassa Fever Death Triggers Emergency Response in Oyo
stories.summary: The Oyo State Government in Nigeria activated emergency response measures after a 44-year-old woman died from Lassa fever at the University College Hospital in Ibadan.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: At Least 18 Dead After Commuter Omnibus Catches Fire, Explodes Along Bulawayo-Beitbridge Highway
stories.summary: At least 18 people died after a commuter omnibus caught fire and exploded along the Bulawayo-Beitbridge Highway in Zimbabwe, according to the Zimbabwe Republic Police.

stories.title: Pope Leo: The world is being 'ravaged by a handful of tyrants'
stories.summary: Pope Leo XVI, during a visit to Cameroon, declared that the world is being "ravaged by a handful of tyrants." He criticised global leaders for spending billions on warfare while neglecting resources for healing, education, and reconstruction.

stories.title: Hero of 2022 battles will now command defense of five oblasts on Ukraine’s Eastern Front
stories.summary: Ukraine appointed a new commander for its Eastern Front, responsible for the defense of five oblasts. The officer, recognized for heroism during the 2022 battles, assumed leadership of an Operational Command overseeing operations in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Kenya: Supreme Court Clarifies Definition and Role of Local Tribunals
stories.summary: Kenya's Supreme Court ruled on an appeal filed by the National Assembly regarding the legal framework governing local tribunals. The court overturned an earlier appellate court judgment, clarifying the definition and role of such tribunals.

stories.title: Burundi: Mystery Shrouds Death of Burundi Information Minister
stories.summary: Burundian Minister for Media and Communication Gabby Bugaga was found dead on the morning of Thursday, April 16. The circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear.

stories.title: LIV Golf chief: Tour will continue despite Saudi funding doubts
stories.summary: LIV Golf's CEO stated that the 2026 season will proceed as planned despite reports questioning the continuation of Saudi funding. The league intends to push ahead with its schedule and global events.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kigali's Industrial Exports Reach $290 Million
stories.summary: Industries within the Kigali Special Economic Zone exported processed goods worth approximately $290 million in 2025. Rwandan authorities are advancing expansion preparations for Phase III and Phase IV of the zone.

stories.title: US strike on Pacific vessel kills three
stories.summary: The US military released footage on Wednesday showing its latest strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean, which killed three people aboard.

stories.title: Arrest in Bolivia Signals Transnational Expansion of Colombian Gangs
stories.summary: Bolivian police arrested Jorge Isaac Campaz Jiménez, alias "Mapaya," leader of the Colombian criminal group Espartanos, in Santa Cruz, Bolivia on April 6. The arrest indicates the transnational expansion of Colombian criminal organizations from the Pacific coast into other South American countries.

stories.title: Nigeria: Police Extradite Fugitive to UK Over Murder, Drug Trafficking
stories.summary: Nigeria's police force extradited Matthew Chukwuemeka Adebiyi to the United Kingdom. He is wanted for alleged involvement in murder and drug trafficking.

stories.title: Nigeria: I'm Not Desperate to Be Nigeria's President, Obi Insists
stories.summary: Former Anambra State governor and 2023 Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi stated that he is not desperate to become Nigeria's president but rather wants to see the country function as a stable nation.

stories.title: Sudan: Tragic Toll After Three Years of War - Over 150,000 Dead and 14 Million Displaced
stories.summary: The war in Sudan, which began on April 16, 2023, has killed over 150,000 people and displaced 14 million over three years. The Sudanese Armed Forces have recaptured large parts of Khartoum, including Omdurman and Bahri, and established their base in Port Sudan.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nasarawa Governor Names Preferred APC Successor
stories.summary: Nasarawa State Governor Sule announced his preferred successor for the All Progressives Congress (APC) during a meeting with political appointees at Government House in Lafia, Nigeria.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP: Lebanon's direct negotiations with Israel a 'grave error'
stories.summary: Hezbollah lawmaker Hussein Hajj Hassan called Lebanon's decision to hold direct negotiations with Israel a "grave error" and urged Beirut to halt what he described as a series of useless concessions to Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Archbishop of Canterbury backs pope’s calls for peace amid Trump feud
stories.summary: Archbishop of Canterbury Sarah Mullally expressed solidarity with Pope Leo XIV's calls for peace amid his public dispute with U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump had objected to the Pope's comments suggesting a "delusion of omnipotence" was fueling the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran.

stories.title: India plans parliament expansion for women; opposition cries foul
stories.summary: India's government proposed expanding parliament by roughly two-fifths to increase women's representation, with Prime Minister Modi calling it a historic step. Opposition parties criticized the plan, arguing it would disproportionately benefit the ruling party. The bill seeks to fast-track implementation of a 2023 law.

stories.title: NSW electric buses, trains and light rail services to run entirely on renewable energy from 2027 in $1.9bn deal
stories.summary: The New South Wales government announced a $1.9 billion, seven-year contract with Snowy Energy to power all electric buses, trains, and light rail services with renewable energy starting July 2027. It will be the first time all public transport operations in the state run under a single renewable energy agreement.

stories.title: Wall Street seems to have decided the recession risk is over. Can the Australian market do the same?
stories.summary: Wall Street has recovered strongly despite ongoing global economic concerns, with stocks hitting record highs. Analysts say U.S. markets may have "run ahead" of fundamentals, while Australia's ASX 200 recovery has been more modest, partly due to the country's reliance on fuel imports amid the global energy shock.

stories.title: Zelensky receives Four Freedoms Award in Netherlands
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky received the international Four Freedoms Award in Middelburg, the Netherlands. The award was presented to Zelensky and the people of Ukraine in recognition of their defense of fundamental freedoms.

stories.title: Six African athletes blocked from transfers to Turkey
stories.summary: World Athletics rejected applications from 11 elite athletes, including six from Africa, to switch nationality to Turkey, determining the requests were part of a coordinated government recruitment strategy using lucrative contracts.

stories.title: Fuel shortages loom as Strait of Hormuz crisis threatens global economy
stories.summary: Rising energy costs and dwindling petroleum product availability are being felt globally as the Strait of Hormuz crisis threatens fuel supplies. IEA head Birol warned of "two big problems": soaring prices and shrinking access to key petroleum products.

stories.title: Drones Russia thought were unjammable just met US LEONIDAS microwave weapon
stories.summary: The U.S. LEONIDAS microwave weapon system was reportedly used against Russian fiber-optic guided drones previously considered resistant to electronic jamming. These UAVs had posed a threat to logistics infrastructure up to 50 kilometers behind front lines.

stories.title: Russia Resumes Daytime Flights to Israel
stories.summary: Russia has resumed daytime flights to Israel under new guidance effective until at least May 15. Russian carriers may operate flights to Israeli airports between 7 a.m. and 1 a.m. Moscow time.

stories.title: NY governor pushes to double funding for protection against hate crimes
stories.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul proposed an additional $35 million in funding to protect organisations targeted by hate crimes, doubling current levels. She also backed legislation to establish buffer zones around houses of worship.

stories.title: Iran halts petrochemical exports until further notice
stories.summary: Iran halted petrochemical exports until further notice after Israeli strikes disrupted key production hubs. The decision aims to stabilize domestic supply as the US naval blockade continues to pressure Iranian trade and revenue.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Patriot crews are rationing missiles mid-attack — Ukraine’s Air Force confirms  interceptor missile shortage
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Air Force spokesman confirmed that stocks of Patriot interceptor missiles are critically depleted. Air defense crews have been forced to ration interceptors during active Russian missile attacks, as Patriots are the only system capable of countering Russian ballistic missiles.

stories.title: AJK police arrest suspected RAW agent in Rawalakot
stories.summary: Azad Jammu and Kashmir police arrested a suspected agent of India's Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) in Rawalakot. AJK Inspector General Liaqat Ali Malik said the suspect had been blackmailed into working for the Indian intelligence agency through a Facebook-based handler.

stories.title: Antisemitism and apology for terrorism 'already illegal in France': Is Yadan Law 'really necessary?'
stories.summary: France is debating the Yadan Bill, a proposed law targeting antisemitism. Economist Renaud Foucart of Lancaster University analyzed the legislation, identifying tensions between combating antisemitism, preserving freedom of expression, and the potential political instrumentalization of legal tools. He acknowledged the legitimacy of concerns about antisemitism in France but warned the bill risks overreach.

stories.title: Israel appoints first non-resident ambassador to Somaliland
stories.summary: Israel appointed its first non-resident ambassador to Somaliland, the self-declared independent region in the Horn of Africa. Somalia's internationally recognized government in Mogadishu condemned the diplomatic move.

stories.title: Will China arm Iran during the ceasefire?
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said China has directly assured Washington it will not supply weapons to Iran during the current Middle East ceasefire. The assurance came as the U.S. increased pressure on Tehran to accept a broader peace deal brokered by Pakistan.

stories.title: Lebanon buries paramedics killed in Israeli 'triple-tap' strikes
stories.summary: Lebanon held funerals for at least three paramedics killed in what were described as Israeli "triple-tap" strikes. The attacks also wounded several other emergency responders, contributing to the rising death toll in Lebanon.

stories.title: Ukraine’s executives were most optimistic since the invasion. Oil had other plans.
stories.summary: A survey of Ukrainian business executives had shown the highest optimism since Russia's 2022 invasion, but rising oil prices quickly changed conditions. The survey results no longer reflect the current economic situation facing Ukrainian businesses.

stories.title: Injury toll from Russian attack on Odesa rises to 26, nine killed
stories.summary: At least nine people were killed and 26 injured in an overnight Russian attack on Odesa on April 16. Reports indicated that additional people remained missing following the strikes on the southern Ukrainian port city.

stories.title: Head of Palestinian rights group Al-Haq barred from entering France
stories.summary: Shawan Jabarin, head of Palestinian human rights organisation Al-Haq, was barred from entering France, where he had been scheduled to attend briefings at the French parliament, foreign ministry, and the Council of Europe.

stories.title: China asks Iran to ensure freedom of navigation through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: China urged Iran to ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz amid an energy crisis worsened by a U.S. blockade preventing ships from carrying oil and gas from Iranian ports. China is Iran's largest oil importer and a close ally.

stories.title: The immense cost of Iran's nuclear program
stories.summary: Iran maintains that its nuclear program serves peaceful civilian purposes, including energy production. However, analysts point to figures and statistics that suggest the program's scope extends beyond stated civilian aims.

stories.title: Novaya Gazeta’s Dmitry Muratov: ‘Cruelty Has Become a Form of Patriotism’
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Novaya Gazeta editor Dmitry Muratov continues to live in Moscow despite mounting pressure and attacks targeting him and his newspaper. He described cruelty as having become "a form of patriotism" in Russia.

stories.title: US can intercept any Iran-linked ship globally, Caine says
stories.summary: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine stated that U.S. forces can intercept any Iranian-flagged vessel or any ship providing material support to Iran anywhere globally. He noted that operations extend across multiple areas of responsibility, including the Pacific under the command of Adm. Samuel Paparo.

stories.title: Iran to execute first woman prisoner linked to January protests as regime executions surge
stories.summary: Iran is set to execute Bita Hemmati, the first woman prisoner sentenced to death in connection with the January protests. Hemmati and three others were convicted of 'collusion' and 'propaganda,' but human rights advocates say the charges are baseless, citing secretive proceedings and state-televised interrogations.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy successfully test fires locally developed anti-ship ballistic missile: ISPR
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy successfully test-fired an indigenously developed ship-launched anti-ship ballistic missile, striking its target at extended range. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the test as a demonstration of preparedness and precision-strike capability.

stories.title: Why India's SMEs are suffering from Hormuz Strait crisis
stories.summary: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz amid Middle East conflict is disrupting India's small and medium enterprises, particularly in Kerala's spice trade hub and the ceramics manufacturing center of Morbi.

stories.title: How the Hormuz Strait crisis is squeezing India's SMEs
stories.summary: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is affecting India's small and medium enterprises, particularly in Kerala's spice trade hub and the ceramics manufacturing center of Morbi in Gujarat.

stories.title: Report: Russian Ka-52 pilot who posted farewell video is alive and has gone AWOL
stories.summary: Russian Ka-52 helicopter pilot Alexei Zemtsov, a senior lieutenant who runs a pro-war Telegram channel with over 170,000 subscribers, posted a farewell video suggesting he intended to take his own life. Subsequent reports indicate he is alive and has gone absent without leave.

stories.title: Turkiye’s Roketsan eyes top 10 exporter rank amid Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Turkey's missile manufacturer Roketsan is aiming to become a top-10 global defence exporter. The company's growth has been driven by rising demand amid ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and beyond.

stories.title: At least 17 people killed in Russia’s deadliest attack on Ukraine this year
stories.summary: Russia launched its deadliest attack on Ukraine this year, killing at least 17 people and injuring more than 100 using nearly 700 drones and dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles. Nine people died in Odesa, four in Kyiv including a 12-year-old boy, three in Dnipropetrovsk region, and one in Zaporizhzhia oblast.

stories.title: The limits of Israel's quest for regional dominance
stories.summary: An analysis examined how three years of multi-front warfare across the Middle East have revealed the limits of Israel's ability to achieve regional dominance through military power alone.

stories.title: Russian strike damages DTEK facility in Kyiv, energy worker injured
stories.summary: A DTEK energy company production facility in Kyiv was damaged during a large-scale Russian strike. At least one energy worker was injured in the attack on the Ukrainian capital's infrastructure.

stories.title: Hegseth says US is ‘locked and loaded’ to finish job of destroying Iran energy grid
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Iran's energy infrastructure is "not destroyed yet" and the U.S. is "locked and loaded" to finish the job. He called on Tehran to accept a nuclear deal as a naval blockade of Iranian ports began this week.

stories.title: After three years of war, Sudan army and RSF locked in military impasse
stories.summary: After three years of fighting, the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces remain locked in a military stalemate as the war enters its fourth year. Neither side has achieved a decisive victory, and the humanitarian crisis continues to worsen.

stories.title: US: Hegseth reads fake Bible verse from Pulp Fiction during Pentagon sermon
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth read a fictional Bible verse adapted from a monologue in Quentin Tarantino's film Pulp Fiction during a sermon at the Pentagon. The passage is not from the actual Bible.

stories.title: How the US military could clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the U.S. military could clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz using drones, explosive-laden robots, and helicopters. The report notes that while these technologies reduce risk, de-mining crews could remain vulnerable to Iranian attacks during clearance operations.

stories.title: Military conflict cannot resolve problems: PM Modi on West Asia, Ukraine after talks with Austria Chancellor
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated after talks with Austria's chancellor that India and Austria agree military conflict cannot resolve problems, referencing the situations in West Asia and Ukraine.

stories.title: Doping is a ‘big problem’ in India, global anti-doping body chief says
stories.summary: The head of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) has described doping as a major problem in India. WADA is targeting India's performance-enhancing drug production industry, which it identifies as the world's largest.

stories.title: Turkiye launches internet crackdown ahead of funerals for shooting victims
stories.summary: Turkish authorities detained 83 people and blocked hundreds of social media accounts over posts praising two school shootings that occurred on consecutive days. The attacks killed nine people, including eight children aged 10–11 and their teacher, and wounded 29 others. Funerals for victims were being held.

stories.title: Trump says Lebanese-Israeli leaders will speak
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said Israeli and Lebanese leaders would speak, as he sought to create "breathing room" between the two countries after more than six weeks of war between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah.

stories.title: French man convicted of killing Israeli woman in 2011 shot dead in Paris
stories.summary: Two helmeted assailants on a scooter shot and killed a French man in Paris who had previously been convicted of killing an Israeli woman in 2011. The attackers opened fire at close range and fled the scene within seconds.

stories.title: US to blockade Iran ports 'as long as it takes': Hegseth
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth declared at a Pentagon press conference that the US will maintain its blockade of Iranian ports for "as long as it takes." He threatened renewed airstrikes on Iranian infrastructure and energy facilities if Tehran does not agree to a deal.

stories.title: What does Japan’s role in a US-Philippine military drill mean for Taiwan?
stories.summary: Japan announced its largest-ever participation in the annual Balikatan military exercise with the Philippines, deploying approximately 1,400 Self-Defence Forces personnel, warships, aircraft, and Type 88 anti-ship missiles. Analysts say the counter-landing and missile defense drills signal Japan's priorities in deterring Beijing in a potential Taiwan contingency.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit worries, tariffs tested, diaspora drama: 7 US-China relations reads
stories.summary: A roundup of recent U.S.-China relations developments highlights uncertainty surrounding a Trump-Xi summit, ongoing tariff disputes, and diaspora-related tensions. Experts noted the summit preparations have been compressed and disjointed due to the Middle East war and Trump's decision-making style.

stories.title: Frenchman who killed woman in Tel Aviv hit-and-run in 2011 shot dead in Paris
stories.summary: Eric Robic, a Frenchman involved in a 2011 hit-and-run in Tel Aviv that killed 25-year-old Pilates instructor Lee Zeitouni, was shot dead by two men on a motor scooter in a Parisian suburb. Robic and accomplice Claude Khayat had fled to France after the incident.

stories.title: Experts say death penalty law discriminatory and drastic, but not necessarily doomed
stories.summary: Legal experts in Israel have described a new death penalty law as discriminatory and constitutionally flawed but not necessarily destined to be struck down. Some analysts suggest its extreme language may be intended to provoke a confrontation with the judiciary for political purposes.

stories.title: Hegseth says US to keep Iran port blockade in Hormuz, ready for new attacks
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that the United States will maintain its naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz. Washington urged a diplomatic resolution but declared it is prepared to resume military strikes if necessary.

stories.title: Building New Lives in Israel - One Story at a Time
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post and Nefesh B'Nefesh launched 'Aliyah Stories,' a video series profiling individuals who have immigrated to Israel. The program highlights personal accounts of people building new lives in the country.

stories.title: Smoke Plume Rises Above Krasnodar Oil Depot After Ukraine and Russia Trade Deadly Barrages
stories.summary: A large smoke plume rose over an oil depot in Russia's Krasnodar region following an exchange of strikes between Ukraine and Russia. Authorities in Krasnodar reported that a woman and a teenage girl were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on the port town of Tuapse.

stories.title: Smoke Plume Rises Above Krasnodar Oil Refinery After Ukraine and Russia Trade Deadly Barrages
stories.summary: Authorities in Krasnodar Krai reported that a woman and a teenage girl were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on the port town of Tuapse. A smoke plume was observed rising above the Krasnodar oil refinery amid mutual strikes between Ukraine and Russia.

stories.title: Unmanned Systems Forces hit 16 Russian targets overnight, including Iskander bases
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck 16 Russian military targets overnight on April 16. The targets included air defense systems, Iskander missile launch sites, and fuel storage depots across multiple locations.

stories.title: ECP directs MQM-P to hold intra-party elections by October 15
stories.summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan directed the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan to hold intra-party elections by October 15. A three-member ECP bench headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja issued the directive after the party's counsel sought a 90-day extension.

stories.title: French billionaire Bollore sparks turmoil at top publisher Grasset
stories.summary: Dozens of authors publicly criticized French billionaire Vincent Bolloré after Olivier Nora, the longtime head of publishing house Grasset, departed abruptly on Tuesday after 26 years. Reports indicate Nora was dismissed by Bolloré following a disagreement over a book. The controversy follows similar upheavals at other Bolloré-owned media outlets across France.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon peace talks: Future negotiations depend on 'confidence-building measures'
stories.summary: Former Pentagon official Bilal Y. Saab discussed Israel-Lebanon peace prospects, describing Lebanon's government as reform-oriented and resistant to external interference. He identified Hezbollah as the central challenge, given its entrenched role across political, military, and economic spheres. Saab advocated a gradualist strategy combined with nation-building efforts rather than abrupt confrontation.

stories.title: South African opposition politician gets jail term for gun offence
stories.summary: South African opposition politician Julius Malema received a jail sentence after being convicted in October of unlawful possession of an assault rifle and firing it at a 2018 rally.

stories.title: Author Ece Temelkuran finds solidarity in her 'Nation of Strangers'
stories.summary: Turkish author and journalist Ece Temelkuran has published a new book titled "Nation of Strangers," exploring the experiences of exiles, migrants, and refugees. The work examines the existential and physical realities of displacement and reflects on what it means to lose one's home morally, spiritually, and politically.

stories.title: Body found in Jerusalem identified as woman who went missing 17 years ago
stories.summary: A body found in a storage unit in Jerusalem has been identified as Ruth Abramov, a woman who went missing in 2008. A 70-year-old suspect was briefly detained and released; the circumstances of her death remain under investigation.

stories.title: Eisenkot visits illegal settlement outpost, site of severe assault against Israeli lawyer
stories.summary: Former IDF Chief of Staff and Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot visited the illegal settlement outpost of Shuvael in the northern West Bank, where a severe assault against an Israeli lawyer had occurred. Peace Now urged him not to ignore settler violence during the visit.

stories.title: Trump says Israel, Lebanon leaders to hold talks on April 16
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump announced that Israeli and Lebanese leaders would hold talks on April 16. Lebanon was drawn into the broader Middle East war on March 2 after the pro-Tehran group Hezbollah attacked Israel.

stories.title: Russian forces push to advance and entrench in Donetsk region's Hryshyne – military
stories.summary: Russian forces are attempting to expand their presence and establish fortified positions in Hryshyne, a settlement in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. Ukrainian military officials reported ongoing efforts to repel the Russian advance in the area.

stories.title: Volunteers in Russia rescue oil-soaked birds as new petroleum slick hits Black Sea coast
stories.summary: Volunteers in Anapa, Russia, are rescuing birds contaminated by a new petroleum spill along the Black Sea coast. Rescue worker Goar Avanesova told Russian outlet Podyom that the substance differs from the oil that washed ashore in the previous year's incident.

stories.title: Lebanon's Aoun will not hold call with Netanyahu in near future, Lebanese officials say
stories.summary: Three Lebanese officials told Reuters that President Joseph Aoun will not hold a phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the near future, despite U.S. President Donald Trump's suggestion that the two leaders would speak. The Lebanese embassy in Washington reportedly informed the U.S. administration of this position before a call between Aoun and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday.

stories.title: FRANCE 24 report: Lebanon’s displaced turn to private aid groups as state support struggles
stories.summary: Thousands of families displaced by ongoing conflict in Lebanon are searching for temporary shelter as government aid remains limited. Private aid organizations are stepping in to address the gap in support. FRANCE 24 correspondents reported from Beirut on the growing reliance on non-state assistance.

stories.title: Afghan women’s rights advocates urge Melania Trump to support girls facing Taliban restrictions
stories.summary: More than 100 Afghan women's rights advocates have sent a letter to US First Lady Melania Trump, requesting her support in restoring education and freedoms for women and girls living under Taliban restrictions in Afghanistan.

stories.title: REPLAY: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth leads press conference on Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Thursday that the United States will blockade Iranian ports "as long as it takes" and threatened renewed strikes if Tehran does not agree to a deal. Speaking at a Pentagon press conference, Hegseth warned that Iran could face bombs targeting infrastructure, power, and energy facilities if it "chooses poorly."

stories.title: IMF managing director meets Aurangzeb, hails Pakistan’s reform progress, macroeconomic stability
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva met Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb at the IMF–World Bank Spring Meetings 2026 in Washington and commended Pakistan's continued progress on economic reforms and macroeconomic stability under the Fund's programme.

stories.title: Report: Russia’s Gosuslugi government portal blocks access for users with VPN enabled
stories.summary: Russia's Gosuslugi government services portal has begun blocking access for users inside Russia who have VPN software enabled, according to Russian independent outlet Verstka. The move was reported on April 16.

stories.title: Russia toughens restrictions on VPNs amid internet crackdown
stories.summary: Russia has tightened restrictions on virtual private networks used to bypass state censorship, according to state and independent media reports on Wednesday. VPN usage has surged in Russia in recent years as authorities have blocked critical news sites, Western services, and social media platforms. The new measures aim to further limit Russians' ability to access restricted online content.

stories.title: Lebanon's Aoun will not hold a call with Israel's Netanyahu in the near future: officials
stories.summary: Three Lebanese officials told Reuters that President Joseph Aoun will not hold a phone call with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu in the near future. The Lebanese embassy in Washington informed the US administration of this position before a call between Aoun and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

stories.title: Iran war exposes weakened state of Britain’s armed forces
stories.summary: A report examines the weakened state of Britain's armed forces as exposed by the Iran conflict. The analysis details the scale of decline in British military capabilities and assesses the country's current defense readiness.

stories.title: France releases Russian shadow fleet tanker after Marseille court imposes fine
stories.summary: France released the Deyna, a tanker linked to Russia's shadow fleet, from the port of Marseille after a court imposed a fine. The vessel departed on April 16 and is heading toward international waters.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Tuapse port kills two children, governor says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Tuapse port killed two children, according to the regional governor. Russia's defense ministry reported that 207 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight.

stories.title: Russian telecom companies agree to freeze expansion of international network links to curb VPN use, RBC reports
stories.summary: Approximately 20 Russian telecommunications companies that own international network links to Europe have agreed to a moratorium on expanding that capacity, according to RBC. The freeze is aimed at curbing VPN usage by Russian citizens seeking to bypass internet restrictions.

stories.title: Lebanon 'not aware' of any upcoming contact with Israel: official source
stories.summary: A Lebanese official source stated that Lebanon is not aware of any planned or upcoming contact with Israel and has not been informed of any through official channels.

stories.title: EU working on jet fuel plan as Iran crisis threatens air travel
stories.summary: The European Union is developing a plan to secure jet fuel supplies as the Iran crisis threatens disruptions to air travel. The initiative aims to ensure that existing refining capacity across the bloc is fully utilized and maintained.

stories.title: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth attacks press coverage of war on Iran
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth criticised press coverage of the ongoing US military campaign against Iran, accusing media outlets of misrepresenting the conflict.

stories.title: Russian missiles and drones bombard Ukraine at night, killing at least 16 people
stories.summary: Russia launched its deadliest attack of 2026 on Ukraine overnight, striking Kyiv and other cities with missiles and drones. At least 16 people were killed, including a 12-year-old child in Kyiv, and more than 50 were injured.

stories.title: He flew from Peru to Moscow for work. Russia took his passport and sent him to Ukraine.
stories.summary: A Peruvian national who traveled to Moscow for work reportedly had his passport confiscated by Russian authorities and was coerced into fighting in Ukraine. The account adds Latin America to the growing list of regions affected by Russia's global military recruitment practices.

stories.title: Give officials more power to probe suspected animal cruelty cases: watchdog
stories.summary: Hong Kong's ombudsman recommended granting conservation officers the power to enter private residences to investigate suspected animal cruelty cases. The watchdog described current enforcement procedures as ineffective, noting less than 1 percent of reported cases lead to prosecutions, and called for stronger penalties against illegal animal traps.

stories.title: Death toll rises to three after overnight Russian strike on Dnipro, 13 hospitalized
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian overnight strike on the city of Dnipro rose to three, with 13 people hospitalized. The attack targeted the central Ukrainian city during nighttime hours.

stories.title: Joan Nathan knew her Catholic relative died in the Holocaust. A new project added detail
stories.summary: Renowned Jewish cookbook author Joan Nathan's family history, including details about a Catholic relative who died in the Holocaust, has been further documented through the Histories and Mysteries project of the Ackman and Ziff Family Genealogy Institute in Manhattan.

stories.title: Russian Central Bank Governor Warns of Unprecedented Labor Shortage
stories.summary: Russian Central Bank Governor Elvira Nabiullina warned of an unprecedented labor shortage in the country during an economic forum in Moscow. She described the shortage as a new reality facing both the Russian government and businesses.

stories.title: Iraq revives idea for compulsory service to 'rebalance' army
stories.summary: Iraq's government has revived a proposal for compulsory military service aimed at rebalancing the army's sectarian composition. The idea has been pushed before, particularly by Sunni political factions seeking greater representation in the armed forces.

stories.title: FINDING A FUEL WE CAN AFFORD
stories.summary: The article describes the impact of a rapid spike in crude oil prices on everyday Pakistanis, with Dubai crude reportedly doubling from $71 to $146 per barrel in 14 days. The price shock was linked to the US-Israeli-Iran conflict and the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Can Iran legally impose tolls on the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Iran has argued it is not bound by the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea in asserting its authority over the Strait of Hormuz. The legal debate centers on whether Iran can impose tolls on vessels transiting the critical waterway.

stories.title: Pope Leo decries world ruled by ‘tyrants’ after Trump attacks
stories.summary: Pope Leo XVI, speaking during a visit to Cameroon, denounced a world ruled by tyrants and called for a decisive change of course away from conflict and exploitation of resources.

stories.title: 'They are champions at lying': Ex-defense official warns against US-Iran nuclear deal
stories.summary: A former Israeli defense official has cautioned against pursuing a nuclear deal with Iran, citing concerns over Tehran's credibility. The debate centers on Iran's stockpile of approximately 450 kilograms of enriched uranium accumulated since 2018, according to the official.

stories.title: Kyiv hit by deadly missile attack amid shortage of interceptors
stories.summary: A deadly missile attack struck Kyiv as Ukraine faces a critical shortage of ballistic missile interceptors. The lack of air defence capabilities left the capital exposed to the Russian strike.

stories.title: Russia trying to seize border villages in Sumy region for 10 days – military spokesperson
stories.summary: Russian forces have been attempting to seize border villages in Ukraine's northeastern Sumy region for 10 consecutive days, according to a Ukrainian military spokesperson. Residents of the targeted settlements had already been evacuated before the offensive began.

stories.title: Can Japan’s US$10b energy shield oust China’s influence in Southeast Asia?
stories.summary: Japan pledged US$10 billion in energy support to Southeast Asian nations, a move analysts describe as a strategic effort to counter China's regional influence amid disruptions to global oil markets caused by the Iran war. However, some observers questioned its impact given Southeast Asian countries' tendency toward strategic hedging.

stories.title: 170 soldiers added to list of Israel’s fallen since last Memorial Day
stories.summary: Israel added 170 soldiers to its official list of fallen since the last Memorial Day, along with 54 veterans who died from service-related injuries. The total number of fallen since 1860 now stands at 25,644, and wartime guidelines may require pre-recorded memorial ceremonies.

stories.title: Germany-Israel divide deepens after Merz criticism
stories.summary: Relations between Germany and Israel have deteriorated further after Israeli Finance Minister sharply criticized German Chancellor Merz's stance on Israel's settlement policy, highlighting a growing diplomatic estrangement.

stories.title: Germany, Israel see growing divide after criticism of Merz
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister sharply criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's views on Israel's settlement policy, highlighting a growing rift in German-Israeli relations.

stories.title: Pope Leo blasts the 'tyrants' ravaging Earth with war and exploitation on Cameroon visit
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned "a handful of tyrants" ravaging the world with war during a visit to Cameroon's separatist western region, where a years-long conflict has killed thousands. He called for global military spending to be redirected toward healthcare and education.

stories.title: Trade tensions make rest of world less keen to invest in US and China, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey by Allianz Trade found that U.S.-China trade tensions have reduced global companies' willingness to invest in either country, with the U.S. nearly twice as unpopular. Investment intention toward China dropped from 53 percent to 24 percent of respondents year-on-year.

stories.title: Why the US must prioritize Hezbollah in the Iran deal - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the United States should prioritize addressing Hezbollah's role as part of any nuclear negotiations with Iran. The piece frames the talks as a broader regional security test affecting both Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Beirut said to balk as Trump pushes for 1st-ever call between leaders of Lebanon and Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun reportedly told US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that he would not speak with Israeli PM Netanyahu, insisting on a ceasefire before any direct talks. Cross-border fighting between Israel and Lebanon continued in full force.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teenager, seize body
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed Palestinian teenager Muhammad Rayyan northwest of Jerusalem, according to local authorities. The military also seized the teenager's body following the incident.

stories.title: In Cameroon, Pope Leo assails ‘tyrants ravaging’ world amid Trump row
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered forceful remarks in Cameroon criticizing world leaders who spend billions on wars, calling them "tyrants ravaging" the world. His comments came after U.S. President Donald Trump attacked him on social media. The Pope also addressed the nearly decade-long conflict in Cameroon's anglophone regions.

stories.title: EU working on jet fuel plan as Iran crisis threatens air travel
stories.summary: The European Union is developing contingency plans for jet fuel supply as the Iran crisis threatens to disrupt air travel. Airlines have warned of potential shortages ahead of the summer travel season due to war-related supply chain disruptions.

stories.title: School shooting in Zakarpattia: Police search for parents of ninth-grade student
stories.summary: A ninth-grade student opened fire at a school in Ukraine's western Zakarpattia region, injuring another student. Police are searching for the shooter's parents, and the student is currently refusing to communicate with psychologists.

stories.title: India plans more seats for women in parliament, links it to ‘delimitation’
stories.summary: India's ruling BJP has linked implementation of a law reserving 33 percent of parliamentary seats for women to the completion of a delimitation exercise that would redraw constituency boundaries.

stories.title: Iran war: What has the war done to the cost of humanitarian aid?
stories.summary: The war on Iran has driven up the cost of humanitarian aid globally, with supply disruptions and soaring prices threatening vulnerable populations. Aid agencies describe the situation as a race against time, including in Afghanistan where the UN World Food Programme distributes emergency supplies.

stories.title: Pakistan continues to insist Lebanon part of current MidEast ceasefire deal even as US, Israel deny
stories.summary: Pakistan has continued to assert that Lebanon is included in the current Middle East ceasefire agreement, a claim denied by both the United States and Israel. US Vice President JD Vance stated publicly that no such promise regarding Lebanon was ever made during negotiations.

stories.title: US military says strike on vessel in Eastern Pacific kills three
stories.summary: The U.S. military said it struck a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Wednesday, killing three people. The strike is part of the Trump administration's ongoing maritime operations, which have drawn condemnation from human rights advocates.

stories.title: Middle East crisis tests African economies [Business Africa]
stories.summary: The IMF now expects African economic growth to slow to 4.3% this year as the war in the Middle East poses new threats to the continent's economies. Analysts note that regional planners now have better tools to absorb economic shocks compared to past crises.

stories.title: Government approves 5-year, billion-shekel plan to develop Golan, give it its 1st city
