stories.summary: U.S. Central Command reported that ten vessels attempting to sail from Iran were turned back within the first 48 hours of a naval blockade, with no Iranian-origin ships successfully passing through.

stories.title: US Senate foils effort to nix Israel arms sale, but 75% of Dems vote to block it
stories.summary: The US Senate voted down resolutions by Senator Bernie Sanders to block arms sales to Israel, including bulldozers and bombs. However, roughly 75% of Democratic senators voted in favor of blocking the sales, signaling a significant shift in the party's stance toward Israel.

stories.title: Several killed in Russian strikes across Ukraine, many more injured
stories.summary: Russian missile and drone strikes hit the Ukrainian cities of Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro, killing several people including a 12-year-old child. Many more were injured across the targeted areas.

stories.title: Somalia: Israel Appoints First Ambassador to Somaliland After Recognition
stories.summary: Israel appointed its first ambassador to Somaliland, deepening diplomatic ties approximately four months after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Israel's formal recognition of Somaliland as an independent state.

stories.title: Macau finance minister steps down for ‘personal reasons’
stories.summary: Macau's Secretary for Economy and Finance Tai Kin-ip resigned for personal reasons, effective Thursday, after serving since December 2024. China's State Council approved his removal, and Chief Executive Sam Hou-fai will temporarily assume the duties until a replacement is appointed.

stories.title: Nigeria: TIME100 - Dangote, Trump, XI, Others Make 2026 Global Influential List
stories.summary: Nigerian business magnate Aliko Dangote, founder of the Dangote Group, has been named to the TIME100 list for 2026 in the "Titans" category. He is the only Nigerian on this year's list.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lassa Fever Fatality Rate Rises in Nigeria As Cases Fall
stories.summary: Nigeria's Lassa fever case fatality rate has risen to 24.8 percent, up from 18.8 percent during the same period in 2025, despite a decline in the overall number of infections.

stories.title: Russian agents detained in Dnipro and Odesa for arson and sabotage – SBU
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) and National Police detained two Russian agents in Dnipro and Odesa accused of carrying out arson attacks and acts of sabotage.

stories.title: Australia, Malaysia share 'deep concern' over situation in the Middle East
stories.summary: Australia and Malaysia issued a joint statement expressing deep concern over the Middle East conflict and its impact on regional energy supply and prices. The two countries pledged to strengthen energy supply chain resilience together.

stories.title: Rwanda: Defence Minister Warns Against Violence Targeting Genocide Survivors
stories.summary: Rwanda's Defence Minister Juvenal Marizamunda issued a warning against acts of violence targeting survivors of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

stories.title: China’s Wang Yi calls on Iran to ensure freedom and safe passage through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called on Iran to guarantee freedom and safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz during a phone call with Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday. The diplomatic effort comes as a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports intensifies global energy disruptions and Tehran has effectively closed the critical waterway.

stories.title: Trump says first Israel-Lebanon talks in decades will happen Thursday
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Israeli and Lebanese leaders will speak on Thursday for the first time in approximately 34 years, seeking what he described as 'breathing room' between the two countries.

stories.title: Nigeria drops terrorism charges against ex-justice minister: lawyer
stories.summary: Nigerian authorities have withdrawn terrorism financing charges against former Justice Minister Abubakar Malami, according to his lawyer.

stories.title: More than a dozen killed in Russian attacks on Kyiv, other Ukrainian cities
stories.summary: Russian missile and drone strikes on residential buildings killed more than a dozen people across Ukraine overnight into Thursday, including at least two children. The attacks hit Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro, and injured dozens of civilians. The assaults continued a pattern of near-daily Russian bombardments of Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: NSW’s highest court strikes down anti-protest law introduced in wake of Bondi beach terror attack
stories.summary: The New South Wales Court of Appeal ruled an anti-protest law introduced after the Bondi beach terror attack unconstitutional. The law had granted police powers to restrict marches, including at an anti-Herzog rally. The challenge was brought by three activist groups: Blak Caucus, Palestine Action Group, and Jews Against the Occupation.

stories.title: Future of the NHS, saviour of the high street? High hopes for health hub in a Barnsley shopping centre
stories.summary: Medical services in Barnsley have been relocated from the district general hospital to a purpose-built outpatients centre in the Alhambra shopping centre, occupying a former Wilko store. The health hub allows patients to access eye tests, mole examinations, and consultant appointments in a retail setting. The move aims to improve healthcare access while boosting high street footfall.

stories.title: Mozambique: Interns Promise to End Strike If Government Pays Their Allowances
stories.summary: Medical interns from UNIZAMBEZE University in Beira, Mozambique, have been demonstrating outside the Health Ministry in Maputo. They vowed to continue their strike until the government pays allowances owed for the past 10 months.

stories.title: Russia pummels Ukraine with drone and missile strikes, killing at least 12
stories.summary: Russian missile and drone strikes killed at least 12 people across Ukraine, according to local authorities. Six people died in attacks on the southern port city of Odesa, as reported by the city's military administration head Sergiy Lysak. Additional fatalities were recorded in Kyiv and Dnipro.

stories.title: Malaysia pumps up police action at border petrol stations to curb subsidised fuel leaks
stories.summary: Malaysia deployed police to dozens of petrol stations along its borders with Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, and Brunei to prevent subsidized fuel from being smuggled out. Authorities classified 36 stations as hotspots and 55 as high-risk, linking the enforcement to a global energy crunch triggered by the Iran war.

stories.title: US deploys additional troops to Middle East as Hormuz blockade enters third day - report
stories.summary: The United States has reportedly deployed additional military forces to the Middle East as a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz enters its third day. The deployment includes the USS George H.W. Bush carrier strike group with approximately 6,000 personnel and around 4,200 Marines.

stories.title: Sudan: 'Sudan Is an Atrocities Laboratory', UN Aid Chief Tells Berlin Conference
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from across the world met at a conference in Berlin on Wednesday to discuss aid for Sudan. The UN's aid chief described Sudan as "an atrocities laboratory" as the country enters a fourth year of war with deepening humanitarian needs.

stories.title: Sudan: Women Victims of Sudan's War Bear Scars of 'Indescribable' Violence
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war, now in its fourth year, has been described by the United Nations as the world's worst humanitarian crisis for women and girls. Sexual violence has reportedly been used as a weapon of war, notably by paramilitary forces fighting the Sudanese army.

stories.title: Trump says Israel and Lebanon leaders will speak Thursday
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said Israeli and Lebanese leaders would speak on Thursday as Washington seeks to ease hostilities after their first direct talks in decades. Since Hezbollah attacked Israel on March 2, Israeli strikes have killed over 2,000 people and displaced more than a million in Lebanon, with Israeli ground forces also entering the country.

stories.title: Mark Mobius, pioneering emerging-market investor and China bull, dies at 89
stories.summary: Mark Mobius, widely known as the father of emerging markets investing and among the first fund managers to invest in Hong Kong and mainland China, died at age 89. He was based in Dubai in recent years and remained active through his firm, managing the Mobius Emerging Opportunities Fund.

stories.title: World Bank launches ‘Water Forward’ programme to tackle global water stress
stories.summary: The World Bank and other major development lenders launched the "Water Forward" initiative in London on April 15, aiming to improve secure water access for one billion people over the next four years.

stories.title: Japan pledges $10bn to help Asian countries deal with oil crisis
stories.summary: Japan has pledged $10 billion in aid to help Asian nations cope with fallout from the ongoing oil crisis. The amount is roughly equivalent to a year's worth of crude oil imports by ASEAN countries.

stories.title: First IMF program review scheduled for June – Finance Ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's Finance Ministry announced that the first review of the country's program with the International Monetary Fund is scheduled for June 2026. A successful review would release approximately $686 million to Ukraine.

stories.title: The fluff stops here: Beijing’s battle against the green wall ‘snowstorm’
stories.summary: Beijing residents are preparing for the annual seasonal release of willow and poplar catkins, which create a "snowstorm" of fluffy seeds across the city each spring. The catkins carry bacteria, pollen, and dust, triggering respiratory and skin issues for residents.

stories.title: Victorian fuel prices could spike by 20c a litre due to Geelong refinery fire, experts warn
stories.summary: Experts warn that a major fire at Viva Energy's oil refinery in Geelong, Victoria, could cause fuel prices to rise by up to 20 cents per litre. Some petrol stations may experience short-term outages as refinery output slows. Analysts say the impact should be temporary and national fuel supplies are unlikely to be significantly affected.

stories.title: US launches fifth strike on alleged Pacific drug boat in a week, killing three
stories.summary: The U.S. military carried out its fifth strike on an alleged drug-trafficking vessel in the Eastern Pacific in one week, killing three people on Wednesday. U.S. Southern Command said it targeted a vessel operated by designated terrorist organizations, bringing the total killed in such strikes to at least 177.

stories.title: Trump says Israel and Lebanon’s leaders will speak on Thursday
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Israeli and Lebanese leaders will speak directly on Thursday for the first time in 34 years, in an effort to ease tensions between the two countries.

stories.title: War on Iran 'can be over very soon', Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump said the US-Israel war against Iran could end soon, as Washington considers extending the ceasefire window beyond two weeks. Pakistan's army chief and interior minister traveled to Tehran after direct US-Iran talks in Islamabad collapsed on Saturday.

stories.title: White House offers no hint of Iran war cost as it seeks military funding surge
stories.summary: The White House has not disclosed the cost of the war with Iran while seeking a military funding surge from Congress. The war's expenses remain an open and contentious question on Capitol Hill.

stories.title: White House offers no hint of Iran war cost as it seeks military funding surge
stories.summary: White House budget director Russell Vought said on April 15 he could not estimate the cost of the U.S. war with Iran while defending President Trump's request for a $1.5 trillion annual military budget. Bipartisan lawmakers criticized the Pentagon's lack of financial accountability.

stories.title: Ukraine says it is employing new integrated drone-infantry warfare system
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defence Ministry announced on April 15 that it is deploying a new combat model integrating drone warfare with infantry operations. The ministry pointed to successes in retaking territory from Russian forces in southern Ukraine.

stories.title: Hopes grow for a breakthrough in US-Iran talks as Pakistan mediates
stories.summary: Pakistani sources report a major breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations concerning Iran's nuclear programme, with Pakistan playing a central mediating role in the talks held in Islamabad.

stories.title: FIFA president Infantino says Iran will participate in World Cup 'for sure' despite war
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino stated that Iran will participate in the upcoming US-hosted World Cup despite the ongoing war between the two countries, emphasizing the importance of Iran's inclusion in the tournament.

stories.title: Mykolaiv Territorial Defense troops test Wolly remote fire control module
stories.summary: Territorial Defense forces in the Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv are testing the Wolly remotely controlled fire module, which allows operators to engage targets from a significant distance from the firing position.

stories.title: Hungary’s youth-led revolution is a wake-up call for Israel’s opposition
stories.summary: Youth-led protests are challenging Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule amid economic difficulties. Observers draw parallels to potential opposition movements in Israel, though analysts note Israel's political landscape is more complex.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill three, including child, as drones and missiles hit Kyiv
stories.summary: Russia launched overnight drone and missile attacks on Kyiv, killing three people including a 12-year-old boy and a 35-year-old woman. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed the casualties as air alerts were triggered across the capital. The strikes came amid months of intensifying near-daily bombardments of Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Democrats clash with US Energy Secretary over Iran war and gas prices
stories.summary: A Democratic congresswoman confronted U.S. Energy Secretary during a congressional hearing, accusing him of being out of touch regarding the Iran war's impact on gas prices.

stories.title: US Senate Republicans block latest bid to rein in Trump’s Iran war powers
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate voted 52-47 on April 15 to block a war powers resolution aimed at constraining President Trump's authority over military operations in Iran. Senate Republicans prevented the measure from advancing.

stories.title: How South Korea plans to use the Iran crisis to spur a renewables revolution
stories.summary: South Korea is leveraging the energy crisis triggered by the Iran war to accelerate its transition to renewable energy, particularly solar power. In the farming village of Guyang-ri, a one-megawatt solar installation generates roughly 10 million won in monthly net profit, funding communal meals and strengthening community bonds.

stories.title: US warns that buyers of Iranian oil could be hit with sanctions
stories.summary: The United States warned that buyers of Iranian oil could face sanctions as Washington enforces its maritime blockade on Iran. The move aims to further tighten economic pressure on Tehran.

stories.title: US targets Iran's oil transportation infrastructure with sanctions
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department announced on April 15 new sanctions targeting Iran's oil transportation infrastructure. The measures were imposed on more than two dozen individuals, companies, and vessels involved in Iranian oil shipments.

stories.title: US envoy Waltz appears to torpedo Bachelet as next UN leader
stories.summary: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz appeared on April 15 to undermine former Chilean President Michelle Bachelet's candidacy to lead the UN. Waltz said he shared a U.S. senator's concerns about her fitness for the position.

stories.title: Shepherds without borders: In biblical Israel’s war zone, flocks traversed contested lands
stories.summary: A study of 3,000-year-old animal teeth from Tel Hazor in Israel's Upper Galilee found that livestock herds moved between the ancient kingdoms of Israel and Aram, suggesting borders between warring states were more permeable than previously thought.

stories.title: Israeli military continues to strike Hezbollah amid Lebanon peace talks, Netanyahu says
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on April 15 that military strikes against Hezbollah were continuing, including operations near the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil. The statement came amid growing pressure for an Israel-Lebanon ceasefire.

stories.title: PM says Israel ready for Iran war resumption, while US gears for another round of talks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu declared Israel's readiness to resume war against Iran, while the White House indicated a second round of US-Iran talks would likely take place in Islamabad. A Pakistani delegation arrived in Tehran to prepare as the US maintains a port blockade on Iran.

stories.title: Hamas plans to use Iran, Lebanon negotiations to avoid disarmament, gain control of Gaza's BoP
stories.summary: Security establishment sources warn that Hamas is exploiting Israel's focus on Hezbollah in Lebanon and US engagement on the Iran front to avoid disarmament and gain control of Gaza's border crossings.

stories.title: African Catholics recoil at Trump's spat with Pope Leo
stories.summary: African Catholics have expressed displeasure over U.S. President Donald Trump's public dispute with Pope Leo. Trump had previously drawn criticism on the continent for derogatory remarks about African nations and cuts to foreign aid.

stories.title: White House denies US requested ceasefire, says new talks may happen in Pakistan
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt denied on April 15 that the U.S. had requested a ceasefire with Iran. She said discussions about a possible second round of U.S.-Iran talks, potentially in Pakistan, were ongoing and productive.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel winner Mohammadi ‘critical’ after heart attack
stories.summary: Jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi is in critical condition after suffering a heart attack last month, her foundation warned. Her family and legal team were allowed a second in-person visit at her prison in northern Iran, where they observed significant deterioration in her physical state.

stories.title: Tai Po fire probe: resident recalls deaths of 3 family members, domestic helper
stories.summary: An evidential hearing into a deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong's deadliest blaze in decades, continued for its 13th day. More residents and senior engineering staff are set to testify before a committee chaired by Justice David Lok Kai-hong.

stories.title: US won’t renew sanction waivers for Iranian and Russian oil, says Bessent
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the United States will not renew sanction waivers that had allowed certain purchases of Iranian and Russian oil without penalty.

stories.title: Israeli attacks prevent Lebanese from burying their dead in ancestral lands
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes in Lebanon have prevented displaced residents from returning to bury their dead in ancestral lands. In Beirut, brothers Ali and Wael Sabbagh stood before the ruins of their family home of over 50 years.

stories.title: Russia warns drone plans for Ukraine are pulling Europe deeper into war
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry warned on April 15 that European plans to increase drone supplies to Ukraine are drawing those countries deeper into the conflict. Moscow characterized the expanded military support as escalatory.

stories.title: Israel, U.S. goals 'identical'; prepared for any scenario: Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel and US goals are 'identical' and that Israel is prepared for any scenario. He said Israeli forces were close to overcoming Bint Jbeil, a key Hezbollah stronghold in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Platoon commander explains how Ukraine’s 123rd Territorial Defense Brigade adapts ground drones for frontline needs
stories.summary: Members of Ukraine's 123rd Territorial Defense Brigade are adapting unmanned ground vehicles to meet operational demands on the front lines.

stories.title: Health of jailed Iran Nobel winner 'critical': supporters
stories.summary: Jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi is in critical health following a heart attack last month, according to her supporters.

stories.title: Pakistan expecting ‘major breakthrough’ tied to Iran’s nuclear programme
stories.summary: A source told Al Jazeera that Pakistan expects an imminent breakthrough linked to Iran's nuclear programme, as Islamabad continues mediating between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky, Italian PM pledge defence, drone cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Italian Prime Minister pledged cooperation on defence and drone technology. No concrete details of the agreement were announced.

stories.title: Colombia court orders Petro government to return emergency funds
stories.summary: Colombia's Constitutional Court ordered President Gustavo Petro's government on April 15 to return funds collected during an economic emergency that the court had ruled unconstitutional.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Israel and Lebanon leaders to hold talks Thursday
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that Israeli and Lebanese leaders would hold talks on Thursday, following a high-level face-to-face meeting in Washington on Tuesday. The Washington meeting was the first direct negotiation between Israel and Lebanon since 1993. The talks were mediated by the United States.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz meets Saudi crown prince in Jeddah; Dar says avenues to further enhance cooperation discussed
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation. Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, who attended the meeting, described it as focused on deepening the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia partnership.

stories.title: Iran offers proposal allowing ships to exit Oman side of Hormuz free of attack, source says
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly proposed allowing commercial ships to transit freely through the Omani side of the Strait of Hormuz without risk of attack, as part of ongoing negotiations with the United States aimed at preventing renewed conflict, according to a source briefed by Tehran.

stories.title: Democrats file articles of impeachment against Hegseth for ‘high crimes and misdemeanors’
stories.summary: House Democrats filed six articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of high crimes and misdemeanors. The charges reference the attack on Iran without congressional authorization and deadly strikes on suspected drug smuggling boats. The action comes amid growing scrutiny of the Trump administration's foreign military operations.

stories.title: When the ‘Dubai dream’ goes wrong - podcast
stories.summary: A podcast examines the case of British businessman Albert Douglas, who was imprisoned in Dubai after a failed attempt to flee the UAE. Douglas alleges he endured years of court proceedings, imprisonment, and mistreatment. The report highlights a broader pattern of foreign nationals being detained in Dubai's opaque legal system.

stories.title: China beats expectations with 5% growth in first GDP release since Iran war
stories.summary: China's GDP grew 5 percent year on year in the first quarter of 2026, beating market expectations of 4.86 percent despite disruptions from the U.S.-Israel war in Iran. Analysts said the figures indicate China remains on track to meet its full-year growth target without near-term stimulus.

stories.title: Fire at Australian refinery fuels petrol shortage fears amid global oil crisis
stories.summary: A fire broke out at Viva Energy's Geelong refinery in Victoria, Australia, one of the country's two operating oil refineries, with flames reaching 60 meters. Authorities said petrol production could be affected more than diesel and aviation fuel, raising supply concerns amid the global oil crisis. No injuries were reported.

stories.title: Israeli forces fire stun grenades at journalists in occupied Nablus
stories.summary: Video footage shows Israeli forces firing stun grenades at journalists covering an Israeli military raid in the occupied West Bank city of Nablus.

stories.title: Kremlin says US has rejected its proposal that Russia take Iranian uranium stocks
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman said on April 15 that the United States had rejected Russia's proposal to take custody of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile. Moscow had offered the measure as a potential step toward resolving the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: 2 arrested for trying to torch London synagogue in what cops call an antisemitic attack
stories.summary: British police arrested a 47-year-old woman and a 46-year-old man for attempting to set fire to a Reform synagogue in London. The suspects threw two bottles of suspected flammable material at the temple, which did not ignite, and police classified the incident as an antisemitic attack.

stories.title: Sonia Sotomayor apologizes to Brett Kavanaugh in US supreme court justice spat
stories.summary: Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor publicly apologized to Justice Brett Kavanaugh after criticizing him at an event in Kansas over his opinion backing roving ICE immigration raids in California. The unusual public apology highlighted deepening divisions within the court. Sotomayor had taken issue with Kavanaugh's concurring opinion from September.

stories.title: At least 16 reported dead from heavy rains in Hispaniola
stories.summary: Days of torrential rainfall across northwest Haiti and the neighboring Dominican Republic have killed at least 16 people. Civil protection agencies and local media reported the deaths on April 15.

stories.title: NATO chief, Kyiv allies vow not to lose sight of Ukraine
stories.summary: NATO's secretary general and allied leaders of Ukraine-supporting nations vowed on April 15 not to lose focus on Ukraine's defense. The statement came amid growing fears that international support for Kyiv is waning.

stories.title: US pushes for global signatories for ‘trade over aid’ initiative
stories.summary: The Trump administration is urging countries worldwide to sign a 'trade over aid' initiative that would dismantle the global aid system in favor of trade and investment. Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordered US diplomats to issue the call to action via a cable to all embassies.

stories.title: U.S. Senate Republicans block latest bid to rein in Trump Iran war powers
stories.summary: US Senate Republicans blocked the latest Democratic effort to restrict President Trump's war powers regarding Iran. The resolution failed to advance in the chamber.

stories.title: Ukraine and Germany to establish coordination committee on mineral resources
stories.summary: Ukraine and Germany signed a memorandum of cooperation on geology and mineral resource management. The agreement provides for the creation of a joint coordination committee on mineral resources.

stories.title: Would more drastic measures help Philippines bring down fuel prices?
stories.summary: Fuel prices in the Philippines are among the world's hardest hit by the Iran war, prompting consumer groups to urge bolder government action including tighter pump price controls. Economists say more realistic options include tax relief, targeted subsidies, and transport support rather than direct price controls.

stories.title: By voicing their needs, Chinese women are normalising them
stories.summary: A Chinese film depicting a young woman's painful gynecological examination has sparked public discussion about women's healthcare experiences. The scene highlights how Chinese women are increasingly voicing their needs and normalizing conversations about female health issues.

stories.title: Growing discontent as 36 Democrats back Bernie Sanders’ bid to block arms sales to Israel
stories.summary: More than 36 Senate Democrats supported Senator Bernie Sanders' effort to block U.S. arms sales to Israel, reflecting growing unease over Prime Minister Netanyahu's policies and conflicts in Gaza and Iran. The resolutions were defeated by Republican opposition. The vote highlighted rising dissent within the Democratic Party on military aid to Israel.

stories.title: Senate Republicans back Trump military sales to Israel
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate blocked two resolutions on Wednesday that would have halted approximately $450 million in military sales of bombs and bulldozers to Israel. Senate Republicans voted to support the Trump administration's arms transfers. The measures had been introduced to restrict weapons sales to the longtime U.S. ally.

stories.title: Pentagon holds talks with US automakers to boost weapons production
stories.summary: Senior Pentagon officials met with top US automaker and manufacturer executives to discuss expanding weapons and military supply production, according to the Wall Street Journal. The talks reflect the Trump administration's push to involve American manufacturers more in defense production.

stories.title: Syria begins loading Iraqi oil shipments for re-export
stories.summary: Syria has begun loading its first tanker of Iraqi crude oil at the port of Baniyas for re-export, after Gulf oil exports were disrupted. Damascus is retaining some of the oil supplies for domestic power generation.

stories.title: Trump says Israeli and Lebanese leaders will speak today
stories.summary: President Trump announced that Israeli and Lebanese leaders will speak on Thursday, expressing hope for 'breathing room' between the two countries but stopping short of announcing a ceasefire. Separately, Hezbollah continued firing at Israel, and Iran said it arrested four alleged Israeli spies.

stories.title: Israeli support for Iran attack slumps, shows survey
stories.summary: A survey shows Israeli public support for the attack on Iran has declined, with only 57% of respondents believing Prime Minister Netanyahu's decision to launch the operation was primarily driven by strategic security considerations.

stories.title: Why US funding for Israel’s Iron Dome is losing support on both sides of the aisle
stories.summary: Bipartisan support for US funding of Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system is eroding. Progressive Democrats, fiscal conservatives, and liberal Zionists have each developed distinct reasons to question continued funding since the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Ukraine kill three, including a 12-year-old child
stories.summary: Russian strikes hit Kyiv's Podilskyi and Obolonskyi districts, killing three people including a 12-year-old child and causing fires and damage to residential buildings.

stories.title: Netherlands to spend $370 million on drones for Ukraine
stories.summary: The Netherlands announced it will spend $370 million on drones for Ukraine. The drones will be manufactured in both the Netherlands and Ukraine.

stories.title: Why China jobseekers use dating apps for work, recruitment sites for matchmaking
stories.summary: Young Chinese jobseekers are turning to dating apps to find work, while some use recruitment platforms for matchmaking, as youth unemployment among those aged 16–24 has remained above 16 percent since July. Many report applying for hundreds of positions daily with minimal responses.

stories.title: The next frontier: China maps seabed resources as Japan races to tap rare earths
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Natural Resources published its first atlas mapping seabed chemical elements in the country's eastern waters, based on two decades of marine geological surveys. The map charts the location and concentration of dozens of elements in seabed sediments, as Japan also races to exploit undersea rare earth resources.

stories.title: Logistics corridor to Falklands via Uruguay: former Kirchnerist diplomat denounces untracked flight
stories.summary: A former Argentine Kirchnerist diplomat flagged a Royal Air Force A400M transport aircraft that flew between Mount Pleasant base in the Falkland Islands and Montevideo's Carrasco airport on April 12. The aircraft reportedly switched off its transponder during its return leg to the islands, making it invisible to civilian tracking systems.

stories.title: White House offers no hint of Iran war cost as it seeks military funding surge
stories.summary: White House budget director Russell Vought told U.S. lawmakers on Wednesday that the administration does not have a cost estimate for military operations against Iran. The admission came as the White House seeks a surge in military funding without providing Congress a projected price tag for the conflict.

stories.title: Bernie Sanders’ effort to block US weapons sales to Israel fails in Senate
stories.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders led his fourth effort to block U.S. weapons sales to Israel, including bombs and bulldozers, but the Senate rejected the resolutions. Thirty-six Democrats supported the measures, reflecting growing appetite within the party to impose limits on military transfers to Israel. The Republican majority and some Democrats voted against the resolutions.

stories.title: CDF Munir visits Iran alongside delegation as part of mediation efforts, holds meeting with FM Araghchi
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Tehran as part of mediation efforts between Iran and the United States. He was accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and held meetings with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Pakistan's ISPR described the visit as focused on de-escalation.

stories.title: US sanctions Iranian oil shipping network run by son of Ali Shamkhani
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury imposed sanctions on an Iranian oil shipping network linked to the son of Ali Shamkhani. The network had previously been targeted in July 2025, when 115 sanctions were issued against the group.

stories.title: YouTube suspends pro-Iran channel posting Lego-style clips
stories.summary: YouTube suspended a channel run by the pro-Iran group Explosive Media, which posted Lego-style animated clips mocking US President Trump. The group's war propaganda videos continue to circulate on other platforms.

stories.title: Russian forces destroy historic wooden school in occupied Mariupol – city council
stories.summary: Russian forces demolished the Gogol wooden school, a historic landmark built in 1911, in occupied Mariupol, according to the city council.

stories.title: High Court weighs petitions urging Ben Gvir’s ouster, but seems hesitant to back them
stories.summary: Israel's High Court of Justice heard petitions calling for the removal of National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir but appeared reluctant to mandate his ouster. Judges indicated a preference for reviving a compromise to curb his interference in law enforcement, though the Attorney General warned that approach had already failed.

stories.title: Tunisia to broaden access to annual Jewish pilgrimage
stories.summary: Tunisia announced it will broaden access to the annual Jewish pilgrimage at the Ghriba synagogue on Djerba island. Festivities will remain indoors as the community gradually recovers from a deadly 2023 attack on the site.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims 39 attacks on Israeli targets over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed responsibility for 39 attacks on Israeli targets over a 24-hour period, including strikes on Israeli settlements and troops along the Lebanon-Israel boundary.

stories.title: Police stop Palestinians hiding in truck trying to enter Israel
stories.summary: Israeli police discovered approximately 70 Palestinian men hidden inside a garbage truck at a West Bank checkpoint attempting to enter Israel. The incident highlights growing desperation following a ban on Palestinian work permits.

stories.title: Georgia man charged over attacks that killed DHS worker and another woman
stories.summary: An Atlanta man has been charged in a series of attacks on Monday that killed two women and left a man in critical condition. One victim was identified as Lauren Bullis, a Department of Homeland Security employee who was walking her dog. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued a statement about the killings, which authorities described as random.

stories.title: Counter-terrorism police investigate attempted arson attack on London synagogue
stories.summary: British counter-terrorism police launched an investigation on April 15 into an attempted arson attack on a synagogue in north London. The incident is the latest targeting the capital's Jewish community.

stories.title: Canton Fair under Middle East cloud, but sets records, as high costs hit China’s exporters
stories.summary: The Canton Fair opened in Guangzhou amid rising Middle East tensions that are affecting global trade and increasing costs for Chinese exporters. Domestic exporters and foreign buyers at the fair assessed the potential ripple effects of geopolitical shocks on supply chains and shipping.

stories.title: Iran war live: Pakistan in push for new round of US-Iran peace negotiations
stories.summary: Since March 2, Israeli attacks on Lebanon have killed at least 2,167 people and injured more than 7,000, as Pakistan pushes for a new round of US-Iran peace negotiations.

stories.title: Combined attack on Ukraine: air defense downs 20 missiles, 349 drones
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a combined attack on Ukraine on April 15, firing 21 missiles and 361 strike drones. Ukrainian air defenses downed or suppressed 20 missiles and 349 drones between 09:00 and 22:00.

stories.title: Norway to lift ban on wealth fund investments in Syrian bonds
stories.summary: Norway will lift its ban on its $2.2 trillion sovereign wealth fund investing in Syrian government bonds, while simultaneously imposing a new prohibition on purchasing Iranian debt.

stories.title: 3 killed in KP’s Bajaur as mortar shells fired from across Afghan border: security sources
stories.summary: Two children and a woman were killed and three others injured in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, when mortar shells fired from across the Afghan border struck a house in Kitkot village. Pakistani security sources blamed the Afghan Taliban for the unprovoked attack, saying it was linked to attempts to infiltrate Fitna al Khawarij militants into Pakistan.

stories.title: Pakistan considering buying LNG on spot market to offset supply disruptions caused by Iran war: petroleum minister
stories.summary: Pakistan is considering purchasing liquefied natural gas on the spot market to offset supply disruptions caused by the Iran conflict, according to Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik. Qatar's force majeure declaration forced Pakistan toward costly spot purchases, with prices surging to $20–$30 per mmBtu. Islamabad prefers government-to-government deals to avoid steep premiums.

stories.title: War update: 133 combat clashes on front since dawn
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 133 attacks on Ukrainian defensive positions since dawn, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector, where 33 assaults were recorded.

stories.title: Hermes hit as war deters shoppers from Dubai to Paris
stories.summary: Hermès reported first-quarter sales below forecasts as the US-Iran war reduced consumer spending in the Middle East and dampened tourism to Europe. Luxury mall sales in Gulf states reportedly dropped around 40% in March.

stories.title: Man goes on trial accused of attempting terrorist attack at London's Israeli embassy
stories.summary: A man armed with two knives and carrying a "martyrdom note" went on trial in London accused of attempting a terrorist attack at Israel's British embassy. Prosecutors said the defendant wanted to send a message about "the killing of children."

stories.title: US says destroyer turned back Iranian cargo vessel under Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: The guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance forced an Iranian-flagged cargo ship leaving Bandar Abbas to turn back under the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command said this was the 10th vessel turned around since the blockade began three days ago.

stories.title: Kuwait detained US-Kuwaiti journalist over war posts, CPJ says
stories.summary: Kuwaiti authorities detained U.S.-Kuwaiti journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin, who has not been seen for six weeks, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists. The detention occurred amid a broader crackdown by Gulf nations on individuals filming or posting footage related to the Iran war.

stories.title: White House offers no hint of war cost, seeks military funding
stories.summary: The White House has not disclosed the costs of the US military campaign against Iran, while President Trump seeks a $1.5 trillion defense budget. The lack of transparency has drawn bipartisan scrutiny in Congress.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses security and support for Ukraine with Italian President
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Italian President Sergio Mattarella to discuss European and Middle Eastern security issues. Zelensky thanked Italy for its ongoing support of Ukraine, including assistance to its energy sector.

stories.title: China threat used to convince Congress of need to bolster US military capabilities
stories.summary: U.S. military leaders briefed Congress on financial year 2027 readiness, citing Chinese military threats including PLA invasion rehearsals and live-fire exercises near Taiwan. Vice Chief of Naval Operations James Kilby emphasized the need for combat-ready naval forces in the Indo-Pacific.

stories.title: Israeli security cabinet weighs Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet discussed a possible ceasefire with Lebanon, according to senior officials cited by Reuters. Israeli and Lebanese envoys held rare talks in Washington, while Prime Minister Netanyahu said Israeli forces were close to overcoming the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil.

stories.title: Explainer-Why is Sudan at war, and what is the impact?
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war entered its fourth year on April 15, overshadowed by other regional conflicts despite creating what the United Nations calls the world's worst humanitarian crisis. The war has produced massive displacement and widespread hunger with no end in sight.

stories.title: Watch: Delimitation controversy & Bihar’s first BJP CM | Above the Fold | 15.04.2026
stories.summary: India's INDIA opposition bloc, led by AICC President Mallikarjun Kharge, announced united opposition to the Delimitation Bill. Separately, Samrat Choudhary was sworn in as Bihar's first BJP Chief Minister. The death toll from a power plant explosion in Sakti, Chhattisgarh, rose to 16.

stories.title: Russian blogger’s video address to Putin draws 20 million views and 1 million likes on Instagram
stories.summary: A video by Russian blogger Victoria Bonya addressing President Vladimir Putin has amassed more than 20 million views and one million likes on Instagram.

stories.title: Russian strike on Odesa high-rise leaves one dead, six wounded
stories.summary: A Russian strike on a residential high-rise building in Odesa killed one person and wounded six others.

stories.title: Israel bombs homes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military bombed buildings in the Bint Jbeil district of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Israeli artist adopts classical motifs to frame contemporary trauma in new exhibit
stories.summary: The Israel Museum is exhibiting 'Yudith Levin: Break of Dawn,' spanning 50 years of the Israeli artist's work. The pieces employ classical motifs to address personal and national trauma, from her brother's 1956 military death to the October 7 Hamas attack.

stories.title: 11 nations urge ‘coordinated’ economic support amid Mid-East war
stories.summary: Eleven nations issued a joint call for coordinated economic support amid the Middle East war, warning of threats to global energy security, supply chains, and financial stability.

stories.title: London police launch probe after ‘attempted arson attack’ on synagogue, amid rising ani-Semitism
stories.summary: London police launched an investigation after two bottles, believed to contain petrol, were thrown at a synagogue in what authorities described as an attempted arson attack. The bottles did not ignite. The incident occurred amid rising anti-Semitism in the UK.

stories.title: Russia’s Defense Ministry publishes list of European drone manufacturers, and a Kremlin official calls them potential military targets
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry published lists of European companies it claims are involved in producing strike drones for Ukraine. A Kremlin official subsequently described those manufacturers as potential military targets.

stories.title: Netherlands to invest €248 million in drones for Ukraine
stories.summary: Dutch Defense Minister Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius announced a €248 million investment in drones for Ukraine during a Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting. The commitment is part of the Netherlands' ongoing military support for Kyiv.

stories.title: US imposes new sanctions on Iran’s oil shipping network
stories.summary: The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control announced new sanctions targeting Iran's oil shipping network, covering two dozen individuals, companies, and vessels linked to a network run by Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pledged continued efforts to disrupt Iran's oil smuggling operations.

stories.title: Kuwaiti faces UK court over bid to attack Israeli embassy
stories.summary: A Kuwaiti migrant is facing charges in a UK court for allegedly planning an attack on the Israeli embassy in London. The suspect reportedly stated he wanted to take action to stop the war, referencing the conflict in Gaza.

stories.title: Pakistan Keeps Pushing for Peace
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a mediator in U.S.-Iran tensions following an initial round of talks held in Islamabad. The first negotiation session did not produce a deal, but Pakistan is seeking to remain involved in future diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: US Senate Republicans block latest bid to rein in Trump Iran war powers
stories.summary: US Senate Republicans voted 52-47 to block a resolution aimed at curtailing President Trump's war powers regarding the Iran conflict. The vote reflected continued Republican support for Trump's war policy more than six weeks after hostilities began.

stories.title: Top British private Jewish school closing amid funding challenges
stories.summary: A prominent British private Jewish school is closing due to financial pressures, including a new value-added tax on independent school fees. Enrollment shifts toward Haredi institutions have also contributed to the school's funding challenges.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel to expand Lebanon buffer zone, continue strikes on Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to expand the buffer zone in southern Lebanon, including extending it eastward. He said the expansion was intended to assist Druze communities and that strikes on Hezbollah would continue.

stories.title: Air Force kicks off AMTI program with competition for first ‘increment’
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force has launched the Advanced Moving Target Indication (AMTI) program with a competition for its first operational increment. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink stated that contract awards for the initial satellites capable of tracking aircraft from space will be issued shortly.

stories.title: ECP issues delimitation schedule for long-delayed local govt elections in Punjab
stories.summary: Pakistan's Election Commission issued a delimitation schedule for union councils in Punjab, a key step toward holding long-delayed local government elections. The seven-step timeline aims to complete the delimitation exercise by August 10, after which the ECP can announce the election date.

stories.title: Zelensky summarizes results of UDCG meeting
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky summarized the outcomes of the latest Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting. Allied nations announced new support packages focused on air defense, drones, and logistics, and confirmed contributions to joint defense programs.

stories.title: Russians will surrender to robots. Russian robots won’t.
stories.summary: A report examines a historic first involving Russian forces surrendering to robotic ground systems on the battlefield. However, communications and navigation challenges remain significant obstacles to broader adoption of roboticized ground assault capabilities. Russian-operated robots have not demonstrated the same willingness to surrender.

stories.title: Apple TV releases 'Unconditional' drama series trailer
stories.summary: Apple TV announced the trailer for 'Unconditional,' an eight-episode thriller produced by Keshet International. The series stars Liraz Chamami and newcomer Talia Lynne Ronn, with its premiere scheduled on Israel's Keshet 12 channel.

stories.title: Quad summit plan turns uneasy as India pushes ahead without top leaders: sources
stories.summary: India is planning to host a Quad foreign ministers' meeting that could be framed as a leaders-level discussion, after its 2025 rotating chairmanship ended without a leaders' summit. The move comes amid diplomatic tensions, with top leaders from other Quad nations not expected to attend.

stories.title: Qatar emir, Trump discuss Hormuz tensions and regional escalation
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and US President Donald Trump discussed maritime security and energy market stability amid tensions over the Strait of Hormuz. The emir called for intensified international efforts to prevent further regional escalation.

stories.title: U.S., Iran consider extending ceasefire by two weeks – Bloomberg
stories.summary: According to Bloomberg, the United States and Iran are considering extending their ceasefire by two weeks beyond its April 21 expiration date. The extension would allow additional time for negotiations toward a potential broader peace agreement.

stories.title: US Navy destroyer intercepts Iranian-flagged vessel trying to skirt blockade
stories.summary: A U.S. Navy destroyer intercepted an Iranian-flagged vessel attempting to circumvent the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command confirmed that no vessels have successfully broken through the blockade since it began on Monday.

stories.title: China doubles ‘AI for science’ computing scale in 2 months using no US chips
stories.summary: China brought its largest AI computing cluster for scientific research into operation in Zhengzhou, Henan province, doubling the number of domestically produced AI accelerator chips in just two months. The chips were made by Sugon, affiliated with the Chinese Academy of Sciences, using no US-made components.

stories.title: Iran ups threats over naval blockade, but still talking to U.S.
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi hosted a Pakistani delegation led by army chief Asim Munir in Tehran on April 15. Iranian state television reported the visit was intended to relay a new U.S. message and discuss a second round of U.S.-Iran talks.

stories.title: Russian drone kills 1, wounds 6 in strike on apartment building in Odesa region
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a nine-story apartment building in the Odesa region on April 15, killing one person and wounding six others. Odesa regional military administration head Oleh Kiper confirmed the casualties.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi in critical condition, supporters say
stories.summary: Supporters of jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi said her health has become critical after she suffered a heart attack last month. Her family and lawyers, granted a second prison visit, reported a sharp deterioration in her physical condition.

stories.title: US Air Force debuts operational AI wargame system
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force declared operational a new AI-powered wargaming system called WarMatrix during an event in late March. The system is designed to enhance wargaming capabilities while keeping human judgment central to the decision-making process.

stories.title: Gray whales, once rare in San Francisco Bay, dying there at alarming rates
stories.summary: A study published in Frontiers in Marine Science found that gray whale deaths in San Francisco Bay have increased in recent years, primarily due to collisions with vessels on busy shipping routes. The whales, which historically rarely lingered in the bay during their migration between Mexico and the Arctic, have been appearing there more frequently.

stories.title: France seeks release of 86-year-old French widow detained by ICE
stories.summary: France is seeking the release of 86-year-old Marie-Therese Ross, a French widow of a U.S. military veteran, who was detained by ICE agents in Alabama on April 1 for overstaying her 90-day visa. She is currently held at a federal immigration detention facility in Louisiana.

stories.title: PM Svyrydenko attends U.S.-Ukraine Forum in Washington
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko began a working visit to Washington, D.C., accompanied by a government delegation. She attended the U.S.-Ukraine Forum to discuss bilateral cooperation.

stories.title: Kanye West postpones France concert after minister's block call
stories.summary: American rapper Kanye West postponed a concert scheduled in Marseille, France, after a French minister called for the event to be blocked. West maintained the postponement was his own decision.

stories.title: Australia news live: Chris Bowen says Geelong refinery fire ‘not great timing’; Canavan defends Coalition’s hardline immigration plan
stories.summary: A major fire broke out at the Viva oil refinery in Corio, near Geelong, Australia, prompting shelter-in-place warnings for nearby residents due to smoke. Energy Minister Chris Bowen said the facility was still producing diesel and jet fuel at reduced capacity while the blaze continued to burn.

stories.title: UN experts condemn Israeli strikes on Lebanon, UN rights body says
stories.summary: United Nations experts condemned Israeli strikes on Lebanon earlier in April as illegal aggression and an indiscriminate bombing campaign, according to the UN Human Rights Council. The condemnation was issued on Wednesday.

stories.title: US Senate rejects bid to halt war on Iran without congressional approval
stories.summary: The US Senate voted 52–47 against a Democratic-led resolution to halt the US-Israeli war on Iran without congressional authorization. Republican Senator Rand Paul was the sole GOP supporter, while Democrat John Fetterman was the only member of his party to oppose it. It was the fourth failed attempt at such a resolution.

stories.title: Air Force Secretary doubles down on space-based radar bet amid key aircraft losses in Iran
stories.summary: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink has reaffirmed the service's commitment to developing space-based radar capabilities following the loss of E-3 radar aircraft during operations in Iran, designated Epic Fury. The E-3's planned replacement program is not receiving additional funding despite the operational gaps created by the aircraft losses.

stories.title: Gaza civil defence says toddler among 10 killed in Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Gaza's civil defense agency reported that 10 people, including a toddler, were killed in Israeli strikes. A spokesman said four people died, including a child, in a strike targeting a police vehicle in Gaza City.

stories.title: Reeves gives more energy bill support to businesses as Iran war pushes up costs
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves expanded the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme to cover 10,000 energy-intensive businesses, up from the original 7,000, offering bill reductions of up to 25%. The move responds to rising energy costs driven by the Middle East conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Dollar falls below three shekels for first time in over 30 years, annual inflation rate declines
stories.summary: The US dollar fell below three Israeli shekels for the first time in over 30 years, while Israel's annual inflation rate declined. The head of Israel's Manufacturers' Association warned that the strong shekel posed a risk to the country's economy.

stories.title: Why North Korea is rekindling China relations
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un signaled a diplomatic pivot back toward China, saying his country places 'the greatest value' on ties with Beijing. The shift came during Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi's first visit to North Korea since 2019, where he met Kim and North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui.

stories.title: US envoy Waltz touts ‘America first’ policy, budget cuts in Senate swipe at UN
stories.summary: US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz touted $570 million in UN budget cuts and 3,000 job reductions during Senate testimony, while criticizing the organization's inability to address conflicts in Ukraine and Iran or counter China's influence.

stories.title: Out-of-control blaze at one of Australia’s two remaining oil refineries in Geelong
stories.summary: An out-of-control fire erupted at the Viva oil refinery in Corio, Geelong, on Wednesday night after an explosion in the Mogas unit. The refinery supplies roughly half of Victoria's fuel and 10% of Australia's national supply. Fire Rescue Victoria responded around 11:15 p.m., and the blaze remained uncontained by Thursday morning.

stories.title: Iran offers proposal allowing ships to exit Oman side of Hormuz free of attack, source says
stories.summary: Iran proposed allowing ships to exit through the Oman side of the Strait of Hormuz without being attacked. The Iran war has caused the largest-ever disruption to global oil and gas supplies due to interference with traffic through the strait.

stories.title: Hamas rejects JD Vance's claim that more humanitarian aid entering Gaza after ceasefire
stories.summary: Hamas rejected US Vice President JD Vance's claim that more humanitarian aid was entering Gaza following the ceasefire. Vance made the assertion at a Turning Point USA event after being heckled by audience members over civilian casualties.

stories.title: Magyar’s Big Plans for Budapest
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming leader Péter Magyar has outlined plans to address corruption, reduce the influence of the previous administration, and lessen the country's dependence on Russia as he prepares to take office in Budapest.

stories.title: Ukraine to create drone-assault units – Defense Ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry announced plans to create drone-assault units that integrate unmanned aerial systems with ground forces. The new formations are intended to enhance battlefield effectiveness by combining drone capabilities with infantry operations.

stories.title: UN nuclear chief urges strict Iran checks in any deal to end war
stories.summary: IAEA Director General urged strict verification measures in any US-Iran deal to end the war, warning against creating an 'illusion' of oversight over Tehran's nuclear program.

stories.title: Lyse Doucet: Under fragile ceasefire, Iranians wonder if US deal can be done
stories.summary: The BBC's chief international correspondent Lyse Doucet reports from Iran, where a fragile ceasefire is in place and diplomatic efforts are under way to negotiate a deal with the United States and prevent a return to war.

stories.title: Two billion dollars pledge for Sudan
stories.summary: International donors pledged nearly $2 billion in aid for Sudan, marking three years since the outbreak of war in the country. The pledges were announced during a donor event focused on the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Could the EU’s alliance with Israel soon change?
stories.summary: A European Union petition is on track to trigger a formal review of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, potentially signaling a shift in the bloc's diplomatic relationship with Israel.

stories.title: China says it will 'resolutely support' Cuba against U.S. pressure
stories.summary: China declared it will "resolutely support" Cuba against U.S. pressure, amid escalating tensions following U.S. President Donald Trump's warning that Cuba "is ready to fall."

stories.title: London police launch probe after 'attempted arson attack' on synagogue
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police launched an investigation after an attempted arson attack on a synagogue in Finchley. The incident occurred amid a broader rise in antisemitic violence in the area.

stories.title: Israel appoints first ambassador to Somaliland
stories.summary: Israel has appointed its first ambassador to Somaliland, months after becoming the first country to formally recognise the territory—a move that drew widespread international condemnation.

stories.title: Iranian proposal offers ships safe passage on Omani side of Hormuz, source says
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly proposed allowing ships safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz on the Omani side. The offer is contingent on Washington agreeing to free hundreds of tankers and ships that have been stuck since the war began.

stories.title: Israeli military chief says plans approved for continued strikes in Iran, Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military chief Eyal Zamir announced approved plans for continued strikes in both Iran and Lebanon. He said joint US-Israeli operations had significantly weakened Iran's defensive capabilities and warned of further strikes if needed, while noting ongoing ground operations in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Shares in Allbirds surge after maker of wool sneakers announces pivot to AI
stories.summary: Allbirds, the wool sneaker company once valued at $4 billion, announced it is rebranding as "NewBird AI" and pivoting from footwear to artificial intelligence. The announcement sent the company's shares surging 582% in mid-day trading, a dramatic reversal for a stock that had lost 99% of its value in recent years.

stories.title: Child victims of online sexual abuse in UK inadequately protected, review finds
stories.summary: A review by His Majesty's Chief Inspector of Constabulary found that UK police forces are failing to adequately protect child victims of online sexual abuse due to insufficient funding. Chief Inspector Michelle Skeer warned that referrals have increased by two-thirds annually and the situation risks worsening without greater investment and coordination.

stories.title: China moves to block entrance to disputed South China Sea shoal, images show
stories.summary: Satellite images show China has positioned four fishing boats, a naval or coast guard vessel, and a new floating barrier near a disputed South China Sea shoal, as the Philippines sends its own coast guard and fisheries vessels to support Filipino fishermen in the area.

stories.title: Police: Remote mining of residential areas increasing in Kherson
stories.summary: Police in Kherson reported an increase in remote mining of residential areas by Russian forces. The most commonly used munitions are "Peliustky" and "Prianyk" anti-personnel mines, which are being scattered across civilian neighborhoods.

stories.title: 96% of Russia’s record March casualties were caused by drones — so the UK is sending its biggest package of the year
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced its largest military aid package of the year for Ukraine, including over 120,000 drones, hundreds of thousands of artillery rounds, and thousands of air defense missiles. UK Defense Secretary John Healey made the announcement at a 43-nation arms coordination meeting in Berlin. Drones reportedly caused 96% of Russia's record March casualties.

stories.title: Bonus In Brief: Choke Point: The Risks and Realities of America’s Iran Blockade
stories.summary: On April 13, the U.S. military initiated a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports, following failed negotiations between American and Iranian officials in Islamabad. President Trump announced the blockade on April 12 after talks broke down. Experts are assessing the blockade's enforceability, strategic implications, and potential impact on the global economy.

stories.title: UK defense official met Ramallah governor who held meetings with released terrorists
stories.summary: A senior British Ministry of Defence adviser for the Middle East met with Ramallah Governor Laila Ghannam, a senior Palestinian Authority official. The governor had previously held meetings with released Palestinian prisoners.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia on cusp of severing ties with LIV Golf: Report
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is reportedly on the verge of ending its involvement with LIV Golf, walking away from an estimated $5 billion investment. The Public Investment Fund governor cited the US war on Iran as accelerating pressure to reposition the kingdom's investments.

stories.title: Two arrested over attempted arson attack on synagogue in north London
stories.summary: A 47-year-old woman and a 46-year-old man were arrested in the Watford area on suspicion of arson endangering life following an attempted attack on a synagogue in Finchley, north London. The Metropolitan Police described the incident as an antisemitic hate crime. Both suspects remain in custody.

stories.title: US says optimistic about reaching peace deal with Iran
stories.summary: The White House expressed optimism about reaching a peace deal with Iran, saying a second round of negotiations would "very likely" take place in Islamabad. Washington said it felt positive about the prospects for an agreement.

stories.title: Zelensky: Italy interested in drone deal
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Italy has expressed interest in Ukraine's drone defense experience. The announcement suggests potential cooperation between the two countries on drone technology.

stories.title: Iran sought Lebanon’s inclusion in ceasefire, Hezbollah official says
stories.summary: A senior Hezbollah source told Al Jazeera that Iran pushed for Lebanon's inclusion in the current ceasefire agreement during talks held in Islamabad. The source added that Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz could serve as leverage to pressure the US and Israel into accepting a Lebanon ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran military says it will block Red Sea if US blockade of Hormuz continues
stories.summary: Iran's military threatened to block the Red Sea if the U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues. Maritime data indicated that several ships departing Iranian ports had managed to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Nine killed, 13 wounded after school shooting in Turkiye’s second school shooting in 2 days
stories.summary: A teenager opened fire at a school in Kahramanmaras province in southern Türkiye, killing nine people and wounding 13. It was the second school shooting in the country in two consecutive days, according to Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci.

stories.title: Ukraine robot combat unit says it launched over 100 attacks on Russia’s forces
stories.summary: A Ukrainian ground robot combat unit, the NC-13 company within the 3rd Assault Brigade, reported carrying out over 100 attacks on Russian forces along the front lines. The operations included eliminating enemy personnel using remotely controlled combat machines, following President Zelensky's recent praise of the new tactic.

stories.title: WSJ: Europe is quietly building a NATO fallback in case the US steps back
stories.summary: European nations are quietly developing a NATO fallback plan in case the United States reduces its security commitments. Germany's Chancellor Merz reportedly concluded that President Trump was prepared to abandon Ukraine, prompting Berlin to help build a broader European defense coalition.

stories.title: Security cabinet said to weigh one-week Lebanon ceasefire amid US pressure
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet is reportedly weighing a one-week ceasefire in Lebanon amid US pressure. Washington said it did not ask Israel to halt operations against Hezbollah but would welcome a truce as part of broader Lebanon negotiations. The IDF chief declared southern Lebanon a 'kill zone' for militants.

stories.title: Space Force 2040: 30,000 satellites, ‘thousands’ more Guardians
stories.summary: U.S. Space Force Chief of Space Operations Gen. Chance Saltzman outlined an Objective Force plan projecting a need for approximately 30,000 satellites and thousands of additional Guardians by 2040. Classified portions of the plan address requirements for orbital warfare and electronic warfare capabilities.

stories.title: Russian military strikes energy facility in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an energy facility in the Nizhyn district of Ukraine's Chernihiv region. Details on the extent of damage and casualties were not immediately specified.

stories.title: Top Israel court hears petitions to oust far-right minister
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court heard petitions to remove far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from office. The petitions accuse Ben-Gvir of undermining the independence of the police.

stories.title: AeroVironment launches new multifunctional drone variant
stories.summary: AeroVironment unveiled the MAYHEM 10, a new multifunctional drone variant within its Switchblade family. The system is designed as a multifunctional launch platform capable of deployment from various platforms.

stories.title: Dubai’s landmark Burj Al Arab hotel will shut for 18-month refurbishment amid tourism decline
stories.summary: Dubai's Burj Al Arab hotel will close for an 18-month refurbishment. The closure comes as tourism in the region has declined due to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

stories.title: IMF advises Pakistan to phase out fuel subsidies, broaden tax base for medium-term sustainability
stories.summary: The IMF advised Pakistan to phase out fuel subsidies, address contingent liabilities, and broaden its tax base for medium-term fiscal sustainability, projecting the country's fiscal deficit at around 3.2 percent of GDP.

stories.title: K-Electric appoints Shaheryar Chishti as new board of directors chairman
stories.summary: K-Electric announced that Shaheryar Chishti has been appointed as the new chairman of its board of directors, following elections held at an extraordinary general meeting on April 2, 2026, in Pakistan.

stories.title: NATO加盟の30か国の大使らが来日 “異例の規模”の訪問団
stories.summary: Ambassadors from 30 NATO member states arrived at Tokyo's Haneda Airport on a dedicated flight for what is described as an unusually large-scale delegation visit. The group will meet with Japanese ministers through May 17 to strengthen cooperation, with China's military buildup as a key concern.

stories.title: 13-year-old boy kills 4, wounds 20 in latest Turkey school shooting
stories.summary: A 13-year-old boy carried out a school shooting in Turkey, killing a teacher and three students and wounding 20 others. The attacker also died in the incident, making it the latest in a series of school shootings in the country.

stories.title: IDF combat engineers blowing up 'endless' amount of Hezbollah terror infrastructure - interview
stories.summary: An IDF combat engineering battalion commander described ongoing operations to destroy Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon. Lt.-Col. "R" of battalion 603 characterized the volume of Hezbollah tunnels and fortifications encountered as "endless."

stories.title: Russians attack Odesa, nine-story building reportedly hit
stories.summary: The Russian military attacked the city of Odesa, with preliminary reports indicating a nine-story residential building was hit. The strike is part of ongoing Russian bombardment of Ukrainian urban areas.

stories.title: Russian air defenses are collapsing. Now Ukrainian warplanes can hit harder.
stories.summary: The Ukrainian air force struck a Russian drone storage site in Russian-held Donetsk using warplanes, taking advantage of the reported degradation of Russia's air defense systems. The method of the strike reportedly signals growing Ukrainian air capabilities.

stories.title: Could the US oil blockade snuff out the Cuban cigar?
stories.summary: Since January, the Trump administration has imposed an oil blockade on Cuba, cutting off foreign oil supplies to the island and raising concerns about the survival of Cuba's cigar industry amid the deepening economic crisis.

stories.title: 'L’Abuso': Real Italian magazine cover of Israeli settler sparks online storm
stories.summary: Italian weekly magazine L'Espresso sparked a diplomatic dispute after publishing a cover titled "L'Abuso" ("The Abuse") featuring a photo of an armed Israeli settler pointing a smartphone at a distressed Palestinian woman. Israel's ambassador to Italy condemned the cover as "manipulative."

stories.title: CDF Munir arrives in Iran alongside delegation for ‘ongoing mediation efforts’: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir arrived in Tehran alongside Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi as part of ongoing mediation efforts between the U.S. and Iran, according to Pakistan's ISPR.

stories.title: Gaza civil defence says toddler among 10 killed in Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed at least 10 people, including a toddler, according to the Palestinian civil defence and health ministry.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz arrives in Saudi Arabia on first leg of regional tour
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on the first stop of a regional tour that will also include visits to Qatar and Türkiye from April 15 to 18.

stories.title: Guterres urges end to arms flow as Sudan war enters fourth year
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for an end to the flow of weapons into Sudan on the third anniversary of the country's war, pleading with international actors to halt arms transfers fueling the conflict.

stories.title: US Senate rejects another war powers resolution to limit Trump on Iran
stories.summary: The US Senate rejected a war powers resolution aimed at limiting President Trump's authority regarding military action against Iran. It was the fourth such vote to fail, and the first since Trump threatened to destroy Iranian civilisation.

stories.title: Hormuz traffic remains at a trickle as US blockade of Iranian ports appears to hold
stories.summary: Ship tracking data shows maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains minimal as the US naval blockade of Iranian ports appears to hold. The US military reportedly has some 10,000 personnel deployed to enforce the blockade.

stories.title: Shekel breaks below 3 to the dollar in first since 1995; exporters warn of economy risk
stories.summary: The Israeli shekel broke below 3 to the US dollar for the first time since 1995, driven by optimism over a potential Iran deal and a Lebanon truce. Israeli exporters warned the currency's strength poses risks to the economy, while the Bank of Israel has not intervened.

stories.title: Zelensky and Meloni discuss joint drone production
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni discussed joint drone production between Ukraine and Italy. Italy expressed interest in cooperating with Ukraine on manufacturing unmanned systems.

stories.title: Netanyahu, Hungary’s PM-elect Peter Magyar hold first call, pledge continued close ties
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar held their first phone call, pledging to maintain close bilateral ties. Magyar invited Netanyahu to a ceremony marking 70 years since the 1956 Hungarian Uprising, while Netanyahu invited Magyar to a government-to-government meeting in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Ukraine retakes 50 sq km of territory in March, army chief says
stories.summary: Ukraine's army chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Ukrainian forces regained control of nearly 50 square kilometers of territory from Russia during March, building on gains made since the start of the year.

stories.title: Pakistani army chief in Tehran amid bid to restart US talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief traveled to Tehran for high-level talks aimed at helping revive negotiations between Iran and the United States, as diplomatic efforts in the region intensify.

stories.title: Pakistan army chief in Tehran to advance next round of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief traveled to Tehran to help facilitate the next round of US-Iran negotiations. Pakistani mediators expressed optimism about achieving a breakthrough regarding Iran's nuclear programme, according to Al Jazeera sources.

stories.title: MPs vote against social media ban for under-16s a second time
stories.summary: The UK House of Commons voted 256 to 150 against a proposal to ban under-16s from social media, rejecting a Lords amendment to the children's wellbeing and schools bill. The prime minister separately summoned tech executives to demand stronger action on internet safety.

stories.title: At 15, He Became One of Russia’s Youngest Political Prisoners. He Now Faces New Charges.
stories.summary: Arseny Turbin, who became one of Russia's youngest political prisoners at age 15, is now facing new criminal charges. His mother publicly expressed fear for his life amid the ongoing legal proceedings.

stories.title: Sudan's forgotten war: three years on, humanitarian catastrophe has no end in sight
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war has entered its fourth year, having displaced over 11 million people and killed tens of thousands. The conflict remains deadlocked with no viable path to peace, while civilians are trapped in ongoing violence and deprivation.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war ‘very close to being over’ as US blockades Iranian ports
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said the war with Iran is "very close to being over" as the U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Back-channel talks between the two sides have reportedly made progress in narrowing gaps toward a potential deal.

stories.title: Four injured in Kherson region today, including child
stories.summary: Four civilians, including a child, were wounded in the Kherson region of Ukraine as a result of Russian shelling. The attacks targeted areas within the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Israeli security cabinet discusses possible Lebanon ceasefire, senior official says
