stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet met on April 15 in Jerusalem to discuss a possible Lebanon ceasefire, more than six weeks into its war with Hezbollah. The conflict escalated out of the broader U.S.-Israeli military engagement with Iran.

stories.title: Lebanon says over 2,100 killed since Israeli attacks resumed
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that at least 2,167 people have been killed and 7,061 wounded since Israel resumed military operations across the country on March 2.

stories.title: War on Iran 'can be over very soon' Trump says, as backchannel diplomacy resumes
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated the war on Iran "can be over very soon" as backchannel diplomatic efforts resumed. Trump also claimed that neither Saudi Arabia nor China objected to the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iranian convict returns home after French detainees Freed
stories.summary: Iranian national Mahdieh Esfandiari returned to Iran after being released from detention in France, following Tehran's release of two French citizens in a prisoner exchange.

stories.title: Erdogan says Turkey working to extend Iran ceasefire, continue talks
stories.summary: Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said Ankara is working to extend the ceasefire between the United States and Iran, ease tensions, and ensure the continuation of diplomatic talks. Erdogan expressed cautious optimism despite ongoing stumbling blocks in negotiations.

stories.title: Russians strike Zaporizhzhia for second time today, explosion reported
stories.summary: Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, was struck by Russian forces for the second time in one day, with an explosion reported in the city. No immediate details on casualties or damage were provided.

stories.title: Pope Leo visits Cameroon with message of peace amid attacks from Trump
stories.summary: Pope Leo visited Cameroon delivering a message of peace, amid criticism from US President Donald Trump. Trump attacked the pope over his calls for peace and his criticism of the US war on Iran.

stories.title: Limits of ceasefire
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, which took effect on April 8, lacks a legal framework grounded in international law and risks becoming merely a temporary pause between escalations without substantive conflict resolution.

stories.title: Frank Gardner: Why China keeps cropping up in Iran war stories
stories.summary: BBC Security Correspondent Frank Gardner examines China's growing relevance to the US-Iran conflict in the Gulf region, exploring how the world's second-largest economy factors into the ongoing war.

stories.title: Trump says Xi told him that China is not sending weapons to Iran
stories.summary: President Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping told him that China is not sending weapons to Iran. Trump also confirmed he will visit Beijing on May 14–15 for a summit with Xi.

stories.title: Sudan: Three Years On, 'Sudan remains a test the world is failing' - UN Coordinator
stories.summary: On the third anniversary of Sudan's civil war, the UN Emergency Relief Coordinator described Sudan as the world's largest humanitarian crisis. The UN response has been severely hampered by underfunding, with the coordinator stating the world is "failing" Sudan.

stories.title: Attempted arson attack a bid to scare British Jews, says leader of London synagogue
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are searching for two suspects who approached Finchley Reform Synagogue after midnight on April 15 wearing dark clothing and balaclavas. They allegedly threw a brick and two suspected petrol bottles at the building. Police are treating it as an antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: Boosting military spending by slashing welfare is not the answer, senior Labour figures warn Reeves
stories.summary: Senior Labour figures in the UK warned Chancellor Rachel Reeves against funding increased military spending by cutting welfare programs. The debate intensified after a former NATO secretary general criticized what he called "corrosive complacency" on defence funding.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon peace talks: Future negotiations depend on 'confidence-building measures'
stories.summary: Analyst Bilal Y. Saab described Lebanon as being at a crossroads during Israel-Lebanon peace discussions. He said Lebanon's government is committed to reform but faces the central challenge of Hezbollah, which operates across political, military, and economic domains.

stories.title: Israeli triple-tap strike kills three paramedics in Lebanon, officials say
stories.summary: Lebanese officials condemned the killing of three paramedics in a triple-tap Israeli airstrike in Lebanon. One of the paramedics had previously been featured in a BBC report. The Lebanese government described the incident as a "flagrant crime."

stories.title: Serbia's president tells military to create units armed with attack drones
stories.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić ordered the military to establish units equipped with attack drones as part of efforts to modernize the country's armed forces. Serbia is seeking to move beyond its obsolete Soviet-era military technology.

stories.title: Can Trump get a better Iran deal than Obama?
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran over Tehran's nuclear program have resumed after years of failed diplomacy and 40 days of military conflict. President Donald Trump has claimed he can secure a better deal than the 2015 agreement reached under President Barack Obama, which collapsed after the U.S. withdrawal.

stories.title: Suspect accused of planting pipe bombs on eve of January 6 faces new charges
stories.summary: Brian Cole Jr., 30, of Woodbridge, Virginia, faces two additional felony counts in a new indictment related to planting pipe bombs near the Republican and Democratic national committee headquarters on the eve of the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack.

stories.title: Arab Barghouti says rights groups must do more for Palestinian prisoners
stories.summary: Arab Barghouti, son of imprisoned Palestinian leader Marwan Barghouti, called on international human rights organizations to take stronger action against what he described as Israel's abuse of Palestinian prisoners.

stories.title: Hopes rise for renewed talks as U.S. military says Iran blockade is in force
stories.summary: Regional officials reported that the United States and Iran reached an in-principle agreement to extend a two-week ceasefire, set to expire on April 22, to allow further diplomatic negotiations. The U.S. military confirmed that its naval blockade of Iran remains in effect.

stories.title: UN experts condemn Israeli strikes on Lebanon as ‘illegal aggression’
stories.summary: UN human rights experts condemned Israel's military operations in Lebanon as "illegal aggression" and an "indiscriminate bombing campaign." Over 250 people were killed in Israeli strikes on April 8, described as the heaviest bombardment since fighting with Hezbollah resumed on March 2.

stories.title: Drone strike hits Iranian Kurds, one killed: exiled group
stories.summary: A drone strike hit an Iranian Kurdish group in Iraq's Kurdistan region, killing one person. Authorities blamed Iran-backed militias, marking the first such attack since the US-Israel-Iran ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Putin Demands Answers as Russia’s Economy Undershoots Expectations
stories.summary: President Putin publicly called for urgent measures to revive Russia's economic growth, marking his second complaint about economic underperformance within a month as output fell short of expectations.

stories.title: Iran weighs pausing its Hormuz shipping to avoid derailing talks
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly considering a pause in its shipping activities through the Strait of Hormuz to avoid undermining ongoing diplomatic talks with the United States. However, the situation remains fluid, as Iran's Revolutionary Guards could instead challenge the U.S. naval blockade.

stories.title: Sudan’s Forgotten War Enters Its Fourth Year
stories.summary: Sudan's war, now in its fourth year, is described as the world's worst humanitarian crisis. Aid organizations warn the conflict threatens to destabilize the wider region.

stories.title: Reeves tells Americans Trump’s Iran war is a ‘mistake’
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves publicly called President Trump's war on Iran a "mistake" at an event in Washington on April 15. She said the conflict had destabilised the global economy and damaged living standards worldwide, marking a sharpening of British criticism.

stories.title: Lithuania’s top administrative court overturns entry ban on Russian rapper Morgenshtern
stories.summary: Lithuania's Supreme Administrative Court overturned an entry ban on Russian rapper Alisher Morgenshtern, as reported by Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT.

stories.title: The AI images Trump can’t get enough of
stories.summary: President Trump has repeatedly shared AI-generated images on social media depicting himself in various roles, including as a king, footballer, and alongside Jesus. The posts have drawn criticism from both sides of the political spectrum.

stories.title: No peace, no normalization: What Lebanon really wants - analysis
stories.summary: Lebanon, which until recently boycotted Israel and designated it an enemy state, is now actively seeking direct talks with Israel, raising questions about Beirut's shifting diplomatic posture amid ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Russian Websites Begin Blocking VPN Users as Internet Controls Tighten
stories.summary: Several major Russian websites, including the e-commerce platform Ozon and streaming service Kinopoisk, have begun blocking users who access their services via VPNs, displaying "access denied" messages as part of tightening internet controls in Russia.

stories.title: Russia’s Leningrad Region shot down 243 Ukrainian drones in the first 3 months of 2026, governor says
stories.summary: The governor of Russia's Leningrad Region reported that 243 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the region during the first three months of 2026, highlighting the expanding geographic reach of Ukrainian drone operations.

stories.title: Over 40 Palestinians arrested in Syria without gov't explanation
stories.summary: Syrian authorities detained over 40 Palestinians in a series of arrests. The Syrian Ministry of Interior has not provided any explanation for the detention campaign.

stories.title: Iran used Chinese spy satellite to attack US bases in Gulf: Report
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reportedly used a Chinese spy satellite, purchased for approximately $36.6 million in a renminbi-denominated deal, to target US military bases in the Gulf, according to reports.

stories.title: US high school principal tackles and disarms gunman as students flee, dramatic video shows
stories.summary: Pauls Valley High School Principal Kirk Moore tackled and disarmed a former student who opened fire in the school lobby in Oklahoma on April 7. Moore was shot in the leg but subdued the gunman until law enforcement arrived. Newly released video captured the incident.

stories.title: Space Force’s 2040 vision: a larger force to contend with larger Chinese, Russian threats
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force has outlined a vision for 2040 that includes a significantly expanded force to counter growing threats from China and Russia. Officials speculate the U.S. could operate approximately 30,000 satellites by that time, more than double the current number.

stories.title: Around the world, residential institutions for people with disabilities are being shut down. In Russia, reform has stalled.
stories.summary: A new analysis by the think tank To Be Precise examines Russia's residential institutions for people with disabilities, finding that reform efforts have stalled despite international trends toward deinstitutionalization and years of pressure from nonprofits.

stories.title: Will the Gulf ever be the same? Trump, Iran and the Arabian Peninsula
stories.summary: Iran's ability to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for one-fifth of global oil and gas, has exposed the vulnerability of Arabian Peninsula monarchies. The situation has forced major powers to the negotiating table.

stories.title: Top Israel court hears petitions to oust far-right minister
stories.summary: Israel's High Court heard petitions to remove far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir from office. The petitions allege he undermined police independence amid deepening political tensions in Israel.

stories.title: Eight Palestinians killed by Israeli military in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed eight Palestinians and wounded 29 others in Gaza over a 24-hour period, in what the health ministry described as ceasefire violations. Since the ceasefire was agreed in October, 765 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli strikes, bringing the overall Gaza death toll above 72,000 since October 2023.

stories.title: Foreign media group slams Israel’s military over AI image of journalist killed in Lebanon strike
stories.summary: An international media association accused the Israeli military of circulating an AI-generated image depicting slain Lebanese journalist Ali Shoeib in Hezbollah fatigues. Shoeib and two other journalists were killed in an Israeli strike in Lebanon on March 28.

stories.title: ‘Paradigm-shifting’ $1.5T defense budget to enable multiyear contracts: OMB director
stories.summary: Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought defended using the reconciliation process to fund $350 billion in defense spending within President Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion military budget. He said the approach would prevent funds from being held up during the regular appropriations process.

stories.title: Nigeria orders probe and defends deadly airstrike in insurgent-held Jilli
stories.summary: Nigeria ordered a full independent investigation into a military airstrike on a market in the insurgent-held town of Jilli that left at least 200 people feared dead. The government defended the operation, stating it targeted Islamist militants based in the area.

stories.title: Swedish power plant targeted by pro-Russian group in 2025, government says
stories.summary: The Swedish government disclosed that a pro-Russian cyber group attempted to disrupt operations at a Swedish thermal power plant in 2025. Stockholm said Russian hybrid attacks against Sweden have become more frequent and serious.

stories.title: Trump needs a better Iran deal than Obama’s – but faces major hurdles
stories.summary: Analysts note that any future U.S.-Iran deal negotiated by President Trump faces the challenge of appearing stronger than the 2015 Obama-era agreement and more favorable than terms available before hostilities began. A second round of talks may take place in Islamabad.

stories.title: Syrian authorities discover Hezbollah arms smuggling tunnel, warehouses near Lebanon border
stories.summary: Syrian authorities uncovered a Hezbollah-operated tunnel linking Syria and Lebanon that was used for weapons smuggling. A large shipment of improvised explosive device components destined for Lebanon was also seized nearby.

stories.title: Lebanon ceasefire 'imminent' as Pakistan army chief visits Iran
stories.summary: Sources told The New Arab that a ceasefire in Lebanon was expected imminently as Pakistan's army chief visited Tehran to mediate US-Iran talks. The diplomatic push coincided with broader negotiations aimed at de-escalation.

stories.title: Russia Agrees to Pay Damages for Azerbaijan Plane Crash That Killed 38
stories.summary: Russia and Azerbaijan issued a joint statement in which Russia agreed to pay damages for a plane crash that killed 38 people. The statement formally acknowledged the crash resulted from an unintentional strike by a Russian air defense system in Russian airspace.

stories.title: Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces strike petrochemical plant in Bashkortostan – commander
stories.summary: The commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces confirmed a strike on a petrochemical plant in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan, Russia. The facility produces aviation fuel, components for aviation kerosene, and synthetic rubber.

stories.title: Fisa surveillance vote sparks fierce debate as Congress splits on warrantless monitoring
stories.summary: A debate is underway in Congress over the reauthorization of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which permits warrantless surveillance and is set to expire next week. A coalition of progressive Democrats and far-right Republicans is pushing for reforms against bipartisan opposition.

stories.title: Navy MQ-4C Triton suffers Class A mishap
stories.summary: A U.S. Navy MQ-4C Triton unmanned surveillance aircraft suffered a Class A mishap, indicating major damage or total loss. It remains unclear whether the aircraft was brought down by enemy fire or experienced a mechanical failure.

stories.title: Countries pledge $1.5bn for Sudan crisis as war enters fourth year
stories.summary: International donors pledged $1.5 billion to address the Sudan crisis as the war entered its fourth year. The UN Secretary-General called for an end to the conflict, while Khartoum's government rejected the international conference, characterizing it as a "colonial tutelage approach."

stories.title: ECP moves to hold local govt polls in 42 cantonment boards across the country
stories.summary: Pakistan's Election Commission announced it is moving to hold local government elections across 42 cantonment boards by August 8, with Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja chairing consultations on the schedule.

stories.title: Numbers Russia doesn’t publish: $216 billion in energy losses, 50% drop in timber exports, and no way back
stories.summary: Internal Russian assessments reportedly acknowledge that international sanctions have cost the country approximately $130 billion between 2022 and 2025. Broader estimates suggest Russia's energy losses total around $216 billion, with timber exports declining by roughly 50 percent.

stories.title: Four dead after Turkiye's second school shooting in two days
stories.summary: An eighth-grade student carried out a shooting at a school in Turkey, killing four people. The student concealed firearms belonging to their father in a backpack to carry out the attack. This was Turkey's second school shooting in two days.

stories.title: More than £1bn pledged for Sudan as humanitarian crisis deepens
stories.summary: International donors pledged more than £1 billion at a conference in Berlin on April 15 to address Sudan's humanitarian crisis. The pledges exceeded the funding target but prospects for a ceasefire in the three-year conflict remain distant, with 34 million people requiring assistance.

stories.title: US claims no vessels moved through under Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: US Central Command stated that no ships entered or exited Iranian ports during the first 48 hours of its Strait of Hormuz blockade, with nine vessels ordered to turn back. Iran's Fars news agency disputed the claim, reporting that a supertanker had passed through toward Imam Khomeini Port.

stories.title: China plans $2 billion investment in Egypt aluminium complex
stories.summary: China announced plans for a $2 billion investment in an aluminium complex in Egypt. The investment comes as Gulf-based producers face uncertainty due to the Iran war and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Partners must provide $60B in defense aid to Ukraine this year – Rutte
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte called on partner countries to provide Ukraine with $60 billion in defense assistance in 2025, in addition to funds expected from the European Union under a joint loan mechanism.

stories.title: Russia and Azerbaijan say they have settled all issues related to the 2024 AZAL plane crash, including compensation
stories.summary: The foreign ministries of Russia and Azerbaijan issued a joint statement announcing a settlement of all issues related to the December 2024 Azerbaijan Airlines plane crash, including compensation arrangements.

stories.title: PSX gains nearly 2,900 points amid hopes of US-Iran talks reviving
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index surged nearly 2,900 points, or 1.74 percent, to close at 168,519.94 amid optimism that a second round of U.S.-Iran peace talks may proceed, potentially in Islamabad.

stories.title: Pope Leo, attacked again by Trump, flies to Cameroon on Africa tour
stories.summary: Pope Leo departed for Cameroon as part of a 10-day tour of four African countries, where he is expected to call for peace in the conflict affecting Cameroon's English-speaking regions. The visit comes amid renewed criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump directed at the pope.

stories.title: Iran war pushes Israel-Turkey rift into more dangerous phase - analysis
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war has intensified the strategic rift between Israel and Turkey, with competing claims over deterrence and regional credibility escalating an already damaged relationship into a sharper confrontation.

stories.title: Regime change is the only viable endgame in Iran - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that regime change is the only viable strategy for Iran, contending that Western approaches to Tehran have repeatedly failed to produce lasting results while the Iranian government faces a deepening domestic crisis.

stories.title: Rival of Druze leader Hikmat al-Hiri gunned down in Suweida
stories.summary: A rival of pro-Israel Druze leader Hikmat al-Hijri was shot and killed in the city of Suweida, Syria. Local sources described the incident as a failed kidnapping attempt.

stories.title: US accuses Cuba of supporting Russia—weeks after letting a sanctioned Russian tanker break its own blockade
stories.summary: A U.S. State Department report formally accused Cuba of enabling the recruitment of Cuban citizens into Russia's armed forces. The report was submitted to Congress approximately two weeks after the Trump administration allowed a sanctioned Russian oil tanker to pass through its blockade of Cuba.

stories.title: Germany just committed to hundreds of Patriot missiles for Ukraine
stories.summary: Germany committed to supplying hundreds of Patriot missile interceptors to Ukraine. Berlin is also funding the production of long-range strike drones within Ukraine as part of its expanded military support.

stories.title: Sudan: 'Presence Vs Absence' At Berlin Conference, Disputes Over Civilian Representation, and Exclusion of Warring Parties
stories.summary: The Third International Conference on Sudan opened in Berlin with approximately 40 political and civilian figures participating, while Sudan's warring parties — the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces — were excluded. The conference aims to mobilize international support for peace and humanitarian aid delivery. Disputes arose over civilian representation.

stories.title: Haifa court extends detention of Israel Police officer suspected in gold bars theft
stories.summary: A Haifa court extended the detention of an Israel Police officer and his brother suspected of stealing gold bars worth hundreds of thousands of shekels.

stories.title: Putin says Russia’s GDP contraction in first 2 months of year is due to seasonal factors
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin stated at a government meeting that Russia's GDP decline in the first two months of the year was caused by seasonal factors rather than structural economic problems.

stories.title: RTX modifies Growler’s next-gen jammer to work from land or sea
stories.summary: RTX's Raytheon division has adapted the Next Generation Jammer technology from the Navy's EA-18G Growler for use on land and sea platforms. The Raytheon Surface Electronic Attack System is designed to generate non-kinetic effects to protect high-value assets from adversary targeting.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Conference Kicks Off in Berlin - Hopes to Raise Over $1 Billion
stories.summary: The Berlin conference on Sudan aimed to raise over $1 billion in humanitarian aid. UN special envoy Pekka Haavisto called the gathering a crucial step toward delivering aid and ending the war, describing it as an opportunity to push for a humanitarian truce.

stories.title: Examining the Cracks and the Cement in the Sino-Russian Relationship
stories.summary: Authors John Stanko and Spenser Warren revisited their 2024 analysis of tensions in the Sino-Russian relationship that could lead to armed conflict. Two years after their original article on Russian threat perception and nuclear strategy regarding China, they assessed whether new friction points have emerged in the partnership.

stories.title: Iran arrested 35 members of alleged 'Zionist spy cell', regime's intelligence ministry claims
stories.summary: Iran's Intelligence Ministry claimed it arrested 35 members of an alleged "Zionist spy cell" linked to Mossad, seizing explosives and firearms across several provinces in what the regime described as a counterterrorism operation.

stories.title: After criticizing the pope, Trump slams Italy's Meloni over Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly criticized Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni over her stance on the Iran conflict, telling an Italian newspaper she lacked courage and had let Washington down. The remarks followed Trump's earlier criticism of the pope.

stories.title: Masked men hurl firebombs at London synagogue in attempted arson attack
stories.summary: Masked individuals threw firebombs at Finchley Reform Synagogue in London in an attempted arson attack. Neither bottle ignited and no damage was caused, according to the Metropolitan Police and the Community Security Trust.

stories.title: The Iran war's lasting impact on the Middle East
stories.summary: Analysts assess that the US-Iran war, with no clear victor, has accelerated shifts in Middle East geopolitics. The conflict has weakened longstanding assumptions about power dynamics, deterrence, and regional security.

stories.title: Germany, the UK warn the Iran war distracts from Ukraine and oil price rises help Russia
stories.summary: Germany's defense minister warned at the Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting in Berlin that Russia benefits from the Iran conflict in the Middle East. He cited rising oil prices as filling Moscow's war funding, cautioning that the Iran situation risks distracting from Ukraine support. The UK echoed similar concerns.

stories.title: Russia’s “medical equipment” holding makes photodiodes for Iskander missiles. Most of it is still outside sanctions
stories.summary: An investigation exposed the eighth holding company under Russia's Rostec conglomerate, revealing that a firm officially categorized as a medical equipment manufacturer produces photodiodes used in Iskander missiles. Most of the holding's activities reportedly remain outside the scope of international sanctions.

stories.title: Germany to supply Patriot missiles, IRIS-T systems, EUR 300M for long-range drones to Ukraine – Pistorius
stories.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius announced that Germany will supply Patriot missiles and IRIS-T air defense systems to Ukraine, along with €300 million allocated for long-range drone capabilities.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill three paramedics in Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes on the town of Mayfadoun killed three paramedics and wounded six others in a series of attacks. Rescue teams dispatched to aid the initial victims were themselves targeted in successive strikes.

stories.title: Palestinian leader Marwan Barghouti facing ‘escalating abuse’ in Israeli jails
stories.summary: Jailed Palestinian leader Marwan Barghouti has been attacked three times in recent weeks in Israeli prison, including an incident where guards allegedly set a dog on the 66-year-old. His lawyer warned he faces immediate risk of further abuse.

stories.title: Iran issues warnings as Trump says war 'is almost over'
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that the commander of Iran's joint military command threatened to block all exports and imports across the Persian Gulf, Sea of Oman, and Red Sea if the U.S. does not lift its blockade on Iranian ports. President Trump meanwhile stated the war "is almost over."

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Govt Reiterates Rejection of the Berlin Conference - Pro-Army Voices Call Out 'Selectivity'
stories.summary: The Sudanese government reiterated its rejection of the Third International Conference on Sudan held in Berlin, calling it a violation of sovereignty. Pro-army voices criticized the conference's participant selection as biased, describing it as an exercise in colonial-style tutelage.

stories.title: 11 finance ministers, stung by Iran war’s economic damage, call for full ceasefire
stories.summary: Finance ministers from 11 countries, including the UK, EU member states, Australia, Japan, and New Zealand, issued a joint statement calling for a full ceasefire in the Iran conflict. The UK minister cited the need to avoid responses that increase costs for households.

stories.title: Iran’s economy could collapse within three months thanks to blockade, experts suggest
stories.summary: Experts suggest Iran's economy could collapse within three months due to a blockade. Analysts noted that Iranian authorities have previously threatened to block regional ports if denied access to their own.

stories.title: ‘You’re bombing children’: JD Vance heckled over Gaza, Iran at Turning Point event
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance was heckled over Gaza and Iran policy at a Turning Point USA event, with attendees shouting about the bombing of children. Vance said he understood young people's opposition to US wars but deflected responsibility to former President Joe Biden.

stories.title: UN experts urge member states to suspend Israel arms transfers
stories.summary: UN human rights experts urged member states to suspend arms transfers to Israel, citing its April 8 bombardment of Lebanon as "a blatant violation of the UN Charter."

stories.title: Afghans comb riverbed in search of gold dust
stories.summary: In eastern Afghanistan's Kunar province, hundreds of men are digging in the rocky bed of the Kunar River near the Pakistani border, searching for gold dust as an alternative income source amid low wages in the country.

stories.title: Knesset legal adviser blasts media bill’s legislative process, urges committee change
stories.summary: Knesset legal adviser Sagit Afik criticized the legislative process surrounding a media bill, saying proceedings at a special panel failed to meet basic legal requirements. She demanded the bill be returned to the economics committee after legal advisers were silenced during proceedings.

stories.title: US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz: What do the numbers show?
stories.summary: Marine tracking data shows ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has slowed dramatically due to blockade measures by both the United States and Iran. The critical waterway normally handles a significant share of global oil and gas transit.

stories.title: Iran threatens to shut down Red Sea shipping unless US lifts naval blockade
stories.summary: Iran's joint military command threatened on April 15 to block all shipping across the Persian Gulf, Sea of Oman, and Red Sea unless the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports. Commander Ali Abdollahi said Iran would act to defend its sovereignty and interests.

stories.title: Rutte at Ramstein: NATO allies need $60 billion more for Ukraine in 2026
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte stated at a Ramstein meeting that allied nations supporting Ukraine need to increase defense aid by an additional $60 billion in 2026. The call came during discussions on sustaining long-term military assistance to Kyiv.

stories.title: Fedorov at UDCG meeting: Ukraine now intercepts 80% of missiles, 90% of drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian Digital Transformation Minister Mykhailo Fedorov reported at a UDCG meeting that Ukraine now intercepts nearly 80% of incoming cruise missiles and 90% of attack drones, reflecting significant air defense improvements.

stories.title: Iraq-bound tanker sails into Gulf after second attempt at Hormuz
stories.summary: An Iraq-bound oil tanker successfully navigated the Strait of Hormuz on its second attempt, becoming the first crude carrier to head westward since the U.S. naval blockade on Iran's ports took effect.

stories.title: Is Iran beating the US at its own propaganda game?
stories.summary: Iran condemned YouTube's ban on a pro-Iranian group that had been producing Lego-style AI-generated propaganda videos. The incident highlighted the ongoing information war between Iran and the United States across social media platforms.

stories.title: UAE's Burj Al Arab to close for 18 months refurbishment after Dubai tourism drop-off
stories.summary: Dubai's Burj Al Arab hotel will close for 18 months of refurbishment following a decline in tourism to the emirate. The drop in visitor numbers was linked to the impact of Iranian attacks in the region.

stories.title: Sudan: From Genocide to Countless Acts of Solidarity - Documenting Three Years of War in Sudan
stories.summary: Three years into Sudan's conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, the country remains divided and partitioned among warring parties and allied armed groups. Mediation efforts have shown few signs of breakthrough, with indications pointing toward further regional escalation.

stories.title: Hezbollah says ceasefire possible ‘soon’ as talks continue
stories.summary: Hezbollah spokesperson Ibrahim al-Mousawi said efforts led by Iran and regional actors could lead to a ceasefire in Lebanon "soon." Senior Lebanese officials confirmed discussions are under way, noting any ceasefire's duration would likely depend on the US-Iran ceasefire holding.

stories.title: Feinberg should create a DRPM for drones
stories.summary: Rebecca Grant of the Lexington Institute has called on Pentagon leadership, specifically Steve Feinberg, to establish a dedicated resource and program management framework for drone programs. The proposal comes in response to the rapid expansion of U.S. military drone initiatives, which Grant argues lack a unified management structure.

stories.title: Iran used Chinese spy satellite to target US bases, FT reports
stories.summary: China denied a Financial Times report alleging it helped Iran target US military bases using spy satellites, calling the leaked documents cited in the report "disinformation."

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Cameroon on second leg of African tour
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Yaoundé, Cameroon, on the second leg of his African tour after spending two days in Algeria. His Algeria visit was marred by two suicide attacks and a diplomatic dispute with U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Trump says he asked Xi not to give Iran weapons
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he sent a letter to Chinese President Xi Jinping asking China not to supply weapons to Iran, and that Xi responded indicating China was not doing so.

stories.title: Russia launches more than 300 drones, missiles at Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russia launched 324 drones and three ballistic missiles at Ukraine in an overnight barrage beginning the evening of April 14, 2026, according to Ukraine's air force.

stories.title: Belgium seizes arms shipment sent from Britain to Israel
stories.summary: Belgium seized a shipment of arms being transported from Britain to Israel. Brussels has banned aircraft carrying military equipment destined for Israel from stopping in the country or using Belgian airspace.

stories.title: Israel to build new settlements on private Palestinian land
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved the construction of new settlements on land previously owned by Palestinians who were forcibly expelled. Several of the recently approved settlement sites are located on private Palestinian property.

stories.title: Israel’s High Court hears petitions to oust Ben-Gvir
stories.summary: Israel's High Court heard petitions seeking the removal of far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir from his position. The legal challenge centers on allegations regarding his conduct in office.

stories.title: Israel destroys over 1,000 homes a day in Lebanon, report finds
stories.summary: A report found that Israeli attacks on Lebanon destroyed over 1,000 homes per day during just over a month of war. Tens of thousands of housing units were partially or completely destroyed, with most of the damage concentrated in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Nigeria drops terrorism financing charges against ex-justice minister
stories.summary: Nigeria dropped terrorism financing charges against former Justice Minister Abubakar Malami. Malami was considered one of the most influential cabinet members during former President Muhammadu Buhari's administration.

stories.title: Baku marks Holocaust Remembrance Day, highlights rescue of 55,000 Jews
stories.summary: A Holocaust Remembrance Day event in Baku highlighted Azerbaijan's role in rescuing approximately 55,000 Jews during World War II. Speakers also addressed current regional tensions, including those involving Iran.

stories.title: Trump posts image of Jesus hugging him amid row with pope over Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted an apparently AI-generated image on social media showing Jesus embracing him on April 15. The post came two days after he deleted a separate image that drew criticism for appearing to compare himself to Jesus.

stories.title: Israel plans to divide south Lebanon as Beirut seeks ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel is pursuing plans to divide southern Lebanon as Lebanese authorities seek a ceasefire. Israel's primary objective remains disarming Hezbollah, while Beirut maintains that disarmament will take time and should be achieved through political means.

stories.title: Kharkiv region expands mandatory evacuation zone for families with children
stories.summary: The Kharkiv Region Defense Council expanded the mandatory evacuation zone for families with children to include 23 additional settlements in the Kupiansk district amid ongoing security threats.

stories.title: Netanyahu sees Lebanon as his last chance for a ‘win’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly focusing on Lebanon as an opportunity for a military success after setbacks in Gaza and against Iran. Analysts view the Lebanese front as his remaining avenue for a political victory.

stories.title: Russia pledges further oil supplies to Cuba after dispatching crude cargo
stories.summary: Russia dispatched a crude oil cargo to Cuba and pledged to continue providing energy assistance to the island nation.

stories.title: Israel says 'no plan' for imminent ceasefire in Lebanon after Iran-linked report
stories.summary: Hezbollah-linked Lebanese outlet Al Mayadeen reported that a potential ceasefire in Lebanon could last one week and expire simultaneously with the temporary US-Iran ceasefire. Israel said it had no plan for an imminent ceasefire in Lebanon.

stories.title: Marwan Barghouti suffers repeated assaults in Israeli custody
stories.summary: Palestinian leader Marwan Barghouti has been repeatedly assaulted while held in solitary confinement in Israeli prison, according to rights groups. The reports highlight ongoing concerns about his treatment in custody.

stories.title: Pakistan's army chief lands in Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir arrived in Tehran and was welcomed by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Munir had previously mediated US-Iran talks in Islamabad that ended on Sunday, and his delegation traveled to Iran to help narrow remaining gaps between the two sides.

stories.title: Sudan: Washington's Asymmetry of Interests in Sudan
stories.summary: After three years of civil war in Sudan, 700 civilians have been killed by drone strikes from warring factions since the start of the year alone. Two-thirds of Sudan's population face acute food insecurity, and 70 percent live at or below the World Bank's $2-per-day poverty threshold. Washington's engagement has been criticized as inconsistent.

stories.title: Pope Leo says world needs to hear message of peace after Trump attacks
stories.summary: Pope Leo, during a flight from Algeria to Cameroon on his Africa tour, called for a message of peace and coexistence after US President Donald Trump attacked him on social media for a second time in one week.

stories.title: Subcontinent might see subdued monsoon as ‘super El Niño’ expected this year: weather expert
stories.summary: A Pakistan Meteorological Department spokesperson warned that a 'super El Niño' is expected to develop by late August or September, potentially suppressing the subcontinent's summer monsoon season.

stories.title: After Hungary’s Orban loses, Czech FM says Prague will remain ‘advocate’ for Israel
stories.summary: Czech Foreign Minister Petr Macinka affirmed Prague would remain an advocate for Israel following the electoral defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban. Macinka said he was reopening discussions about moving the Czech embassy to Jerusalem, regardless of EU opinion.

stories.title: U.S. Believes Cuba Helped Russia Recruit Soldiers to Fight in Ukraine – Axios
stories.summary: According to a report cited by Axios, U.S. intelligence assesses that Cuban authorities knowingly tolerated or facilitated the recruitment of Cuban nationals to serve in the Russian armed forces fighting in Ukraine. The report references "significant indicators" of Havana's involvement.

stories.title: 'The Boys' faces boycott as star Tomer Capone’s past in Israeli army resurfaces
stories.summary: Actor Tomer Capone, who stars in Amazon's 'The Boys,' faces boycott calls after a 2016 interview resurfaced in which he described his service in the Israeli military, including violence against Palestinians.

stories.title: On Israel’s Holocaust Remembrance Day, Zelensky criminalizes antisemitism in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a law criminalizing antisemitism in Ukraine on Israel's Holocaust Remembrance Day. The legislation makes hate crimes against Jews punishable by up to eight years in prison.

stories.title: Constable martyred after unknown assailants open fire on polio team in Balochistan’s Dera Murad Jamali
stories.summary: A police constable named Farhan Bashir was killed in Dera Murad Jamali, Nasirabad district, Balochistan, after unknown armed men on motorcycles opened fire on security personnel escorting a polio vaccination team.

stories.title: Israeli army strikes south of Beirut as Hezbollah launches rockets at Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military conducted airstrikes south of Beirut while Hezbollah launched rockets at 10 areas in northern Israel, marking continued cross-border hostilities between the two sides.

stories.title: Portugal, unlike Spain, rejects separate European army
stories.summary: Portugal's defense minister stated that the country opposes creating a separate European army, instead favoring the strengthening of armed forces within NATO. This position contrasts with neighboring Spain, which has supported the concept of an independent European military force.

stories.title: Report: Putin secretly authorized jailing of Russians without trial for opposing war in Ukraine
stories.summary: The human rights project Department One reported that on March 8, 2022, President Putin secretly authorized security officials to detain Russian citizens and foreigners in pretrial detention centers without court orders for opposing the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting begins in Berlin
stories.summary: The 34th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group convened in Berlin at the defense minister level, bringing together NATO member states to coordinate military support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Hamas rejects US-led disarmament plan, demands changes to proposal
stories.summary: Hamas rejected a US-led disarmament plan put forward by the Board of Peace, demanding changes to the proposal and accusing the mediator of pro-Israel bias.

stories.title: Why has Italy’s Giorgia Meloni suspended a defence pact with Israel?
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni suspended a bilateral defence pact with Israel, marking a significant policy reversal by one of Israel's closest European allies. While the immediate practical impact is limited, the decision represents an unprecedented diplomatic shift.

stories.title: Germany not taking part in Iran war but feeling its effects, says minister
stories.summary: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said at the IMF spring meetings in Washington that although Germany is not participating in the war on Iran, the conflict is directly harming the country's economic growth. He called for diplomacy with Tehran.

stories.title: Kyiv chief rabbi on Holocaust remembrance: ‘We must not live inside it' - interview
stories.summary: Kyiv Chief Rabbi Markovitch spoke with The Media Line on Holocaust Remembrance Day, reflecting on the responsibility of remembrance while cautioning against being consumed by the trauma of the past.

stories.title: European Commission to invest EUR 1.07B in defense projects, including cooperation with Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Commission announced a €1.07 billion investment in 57 new defense projects under the 2025 European Defense Fund, including initiatives to strengthen cooperation with Ukraine's defense industry.

stories.title: Peace activist, 91, walks across Ireland in protest against US military stopovers
stories.summary: Lelia Doolan, a 91-year-old Irish peace activist, completed a 220-kilometer walk across Ireland on April 15, arriving at parliament in Dublin. She called on the government to bar U.S. military flights from using Shannon Airport, arguing the stopovers violate Irish neutrality.

stories.title: Why is Ben Gvir rising in the polls while Smotrich can’t keep his head above water?
stories.summary: Israeli polls show Itamar Ben Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party climbing to around 10 seats, while Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism party struggles to pass the electoral threshold. The two far-right parties ran together in 2022 but have since diverged in public support.

stories.title: When vitiligo is seen but not understood
stories.summary: This article is sponsored content discussing vitiligo, a chronic autoimmune disorder that destroys pigment-producing skin cells. It highlights that public awareness of the condition in Hong Kong remains limited, leading to misunderstanding and social stigma for those affected.

stories.title: Prominent Palestinian prisoner Marwan Barghouti assaulted three times in a month, family says
stories.summary: The family of prominent Palestinian prisoner Marwan Barghouti alleged he was physically assaulted three times in one month while in Israeli detention. The Israeli Prison Service denied the allegations, calling them "false and baseless."

stories.title: France puts mobile corps command to the test in major war scenario
stories.summary: France conducted a major exercise testing its mobile corps command post, designed to keep commanders close to the engagement zone. A senior general said the forward command structure enables direct contact with divisions during operations.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Robotic arms + satellite refueling | Iran war costs | Unmasking shadow fleets…from space
stories.summary: A defense industry briefing covered developments including robotic arms and satellite refueling technology, the financial costs of the Iran conflict, and the use of space-based capabilities to identify shadow fleet vessels.

stories.title: St. Petersburg facial recognition system mistakes rock musician for Ukrainian journalist wanted in Russia
stories.summary: Police at Moscow Station in St. Petersburg detained rock musician Dmitry Galyanskikh, frontman of the band Svoboda vazhnee mody, after a facial recognition system misidentified him as Ukrainian journalist Dmytro Gordon, who is wanted in Russia.

stories.title: 'Frightening milestone': Saudi Arabia hits 2,000 executions since King Salman took power
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has carried out 2,000 executions since King Salman assumed power, according to rights monitors. The kingdom's use of the death penalty has increased fivefold despite Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's promises of reform and modernization.

stories.title: Ukraine’s factories are getting second life: Germany launches “Industrial Ramstein”
stories.summary: Germany launched an "Industrial Ramstein" initiative in Berlin aimed at integrating Ukrainian factories into European supply chains, giving Ukraine's industrial sector new economic partnerships.

stories.title: Ukraine broaches ‘stolen’ Russian grain cargo on call with Israel
stories.summary: Ukraine raised the issue of Russian seizure of Ukrainian grain during a call with Israel, claiming that Russia has stolen 15 million tonnes of Ukrainian grain since the start of the war.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia pledges additional $3 billion support to Pakistan
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia pledged an additional $3 billion in financial support to Pakistan at a crucial time as Islamabad prepares to repay $3.5 billion owed to the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: IMF chief hopes US-Iran ceasefire leads to durable peace
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva expressed hope that the US-Iran ceasefire would lead to a durable peace. Speaking at the IMF/World Bank spring meetings in Washington, she said discussions focused on supporting countries affected by the energy shock caused by the war.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian radar systems, drone depots, logistics hubs
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces struck multiple Russian military targets on April 14–15, including radar systems, drone depots, logistics hubs, and personnel concentrations in Russia and occupied Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Can Japan’s arms industry gain from Trump trust loss?
stories.summary: Japan announced plans to expand its defence exports amid shifting global alliances. The move comes as some countries reassess arms procurement strategies in light of reduced trust in US reliability under the Trump administration.

stories.title: Israeli security cabinet to discuss possible Lebanon ceasefire: senior official
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet convened on April 15 to discuss a possible ceasefire with Lebanon amid its ongoing war with Hezbollah. Senior Hezbollah official Ibrahim al-Moussawi told Reuters that diplomatic efforts by Iran and regional states could produce a ceasefire soon.

stories.title: There's nothing inevitable about Sudan's war
stories.summary: As Sudan's civil war enters its fourth year with no resolution in sight, commentators argue the conflict is not inevitable. Writer Yassmin Abdel-Magied urged against despair and called for continued engagement.

stories.title: Gulf states begin gradual recovery as Iran-US truce holds
stories.summary: Gulf states are beginning a gradual economic recovery as the US-Iran truce holds. However, disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and a collapse in tourism continue to take a heavy toll on the region's economies.

stories.title: Russian programmer gets 13-year prison sentence for treason after FSB held him in isolation and assets disappeared from his crypto wallet
stories.summary: A court in Irkutsk sentenced Russian programmer Vadim Nekrashchuk to 13 years in a high-security penal colony on treason charges. Reports indicate the FSB held him in isolation and assets disappeared from his cryptocurrency wallet during his detention.

stories.title: Chinese national given one year in prison for smuggling ants out of Kenya
stories.summary: A Chinese national, Zhang Kequn, was sentenced to one year in prison in Kenya after being arrested in March while attempting to smuggle more than 2,000 live ants to China.

stories.title: Cocaine and Gold: The Battle to Protect Costa Rica’s Corcovado National Park
stories.summary: Cocaine trafficking in Costa Rica is increasingly intertwined with illegal gold mining inside Corcovado National Park. Park rangers face growing challenges in protecting natural resources due to a lack of operational support and funding.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Raid Ipob Hideout, Rescue Kidnap Victim After N2 Million Ransom
stories.summary: Nigerian Army troops rescued a kidnap victim in Uzo-Uwani local government area of Enugu State and subsequently raided a hideout linked to the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) in Ezeagu local government area.

stories.title: Reeves tells Americans she does not know why they launched Iran war – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves told an American audience she does not understand why the U.S. launched the war on Iran and said she is not convinced the conflict has made the world safer. Her remarks came amid ongoing tensions between Britain and the United States over Middle East policy.

stories.title: Mediators push to extend US-Iran ceasefire, though both sides deny reports
stories.summary: A US official denied reports that Washington had formally agreed to extend the ceasefire with Iran, telling The Jerusalem Post that no such commitment had been made, even as mediators pushed for a prolongation.

stories.title: From Yaoundé to Bamenda, Cameroonians await Pope Leo XIV’s visit
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV is visiting Cameroon from April 15 to 18, with stops planned in Yaoundé, Douala, and Bamenda. The visit to Bamenda is notable as the Northwest region has experienced a socio-political crisis for a decade. He will be the third pope to visit Cameroon.

stories.title: Iran warns US naval blockade threatens ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran warned that the ongoing US naval blockade in the Persian Gulf threatens the ceasefire between the two countries. Tehran stated it would halt all trade in the Gulf if the US continues to block Iranian vessels.

stories.title: Sudan enters fourth year of war as officials lament 'abandoned crisis'
stories.summary: Sudan entered its fourth year of war on April 15, with officials describing it as an "abandoned crisis" overshadowed by the Middle East conflict. Some 13 million people have been displaced, and the country faces what is called the world's largest humanitarian challenge.

stories.title: London police probe attempted arson at synagogue
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating an attempted arson attack on a synagogue in Finchley. The incident is being treated as an antisemitic hate crime amid a broader rise in such incidents.

stories.title: North Korea boosting ability to make nuclear arms: UN watchdog
stories.summary: The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency said during a visit to Seoul that North Korea is showing a "very serious increase" in its ability to produce nuclear weapons, with rapid expansion of operations at the Yongbyon nuclear site confirmed.

stories.title: US sending 10,000 more troops to Middle East despite Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: The United States is deploying an additional 10,000 troops to the Middle East this month, according to The Washington Post, despite an active ceasefire between the US and Iran.

stories.title: US blockade of Iranian ports 'fully implemented'
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced it successfully stopped six ships from leaving Iranian ports during the first 24 hours of its naval blockade. CENTCOM said more than 10,000 troops, over a dozen warships, and dozens of aircraft are participating in the operation.

stories.title: Nine killed in second Turkish school shooting in two days
stories.summary: A school shooting in Turkey killed eight students and one teacher, according to Interior Minister Mustafa Cifci. It was the second deadly school attack in the country in two consecutive days.

stories.title: Live: Reports of possible Israel-Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet convened at 8 p.m. local time on April 15 to discuss a possible ceasefire with Lebanon. Senior Hezbollah official Ibrahim al-Moussawi said diplomatic efforts by Iran and regional states could yield a ceasefire soon.

stories.title: Another flight attendant detained in Dubai over Iran war WhatsApp message
stories.summary: A 32-year-old Emirates cabin crew member was detained in Dubai after privately sharing a WhatsApp photo taken during Iranian attacks on the UAE. The campaign group Detained in Dubai said the man was unaware of restrictions on posting war-related footage.

stories.title: Army introduces MV-75 as Cheyenne II, won’t commit to first flight, production dates
stories.summary: The US Army officially designated its next-generation armed reconnaissance aircraft as the Cheyenne II, based on the MV-75 platform. Maj. Gen. Clair Gill declined to commit to specific timelines for the aircraft's first flight or production milestones.

stories.title: Finance minister meets with US commerce secretary, briefs IMF official on war’s impact on Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met with the US commerce secretary in Washington to discuss bilateral economic ties and briefed an IMF official on the Middle East conflict's economic impact on Pakistan during the World Bank-IMF Spring Meetings.

stories.title: Ukraine's Anti-Corruption Court allows Tymoshenko to travel abroad for event in Zagreb
stories.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court granted Batkivshchyna party leader Yulia Tymoshenko permission to travel abroad to attend an international event in Zagreb, Croatia.

stories.title: Will the ceasefire last? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored discussion analyzed the outcomes of the US-Iran war and the prospects for the current ceasefire. The segment examined what was achieved, what was not, and potential next steps.

stories.title: Kenya: Pressure Mounts On Ruto To Address Rising Costs
stories.summary: Kenya's United Alternative Government opposition group has called on President William Ruto to convene a special parliamentary sitting within seven days to address record-high fuel prices and a deepening fuel crisis.

stories.title: ‘Privilege for none’: Pakistan calls for abolition of UNSC veto power, rejects new permanent seats
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad called for the abolition or severe restriction of the UN Security Council veto power and opposed any expansion of permanent membership during Intergovernmental Negotiations on UNSC reform.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Govt Drops Terrorism Financing Charges Against Malami, Son
stories.summary: The Nigerian government has dropped terrorism financing charges against former Attorney General Abubakar Malami and his son, though prosecutors will continue to pursue other charges filed against them in the case.

stories.title: Pope Leo stresses message of peace and unity despite another Trump attack
stories.summary: Pope Leo, speaking during a flight from Algeria to Cameroon on his 10-day Africa tour, called for a message of peace, coexistence, and dialogue between communities. His remarks came after President Trump attacked him for a second time on social media. The first American-born pope urged respect for all people.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Nurses Announce Plans For Nationwide Strike
stories.summary: Zimbabwean nurses announced plans for a nationwide strike from April 20 to 22, stating that concerns they raised with the government the previous month had been ignored.

stories.title: Israeli security cabinet to discuss possible Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli security cabinet was set to convene on Wednesday night to discuss a possible ceasefire in Lebanon. The Israeli military had renewed evacuation orders for a large area of southern Lebanon as bombing and clashes with Hezbollah continued.

stories.title: Suspicion surrounds death of US influencer Ashly Robinson in Zanzibar
stories.summary: U.S. lifestyle influencer Ashly Robinson died on April 9 while vacationing in Zanzibar, Tanzania, with her boyfriend Joe McCann. Local officials have withheld McCann's passport, though police have not named him as a suspect. The circumstances of her death have drawn widespread suspicion on social media.

stories.title: Somalia: Puntland Launches Operations Against Islamic State Fighters in Somalia's Bari Region
stories.summary: Security forces in Somalia's semi-autonomous Puntland region launched large-scale military operations against Islamic State-linked fighters in the Bari region, according to officials in Mogadishu.

stories.title: Bennett names 23-year-old reservist activist Yonatan Shalev to party slate
stories.summary: Israeli politician Naftali Bennett added 23-year-old reservist activist Yonatan Shalev to his party slate. Shalev's Shoulder to Shoulder movement endorsed Bennett as the leader who can reform Israel.

stories.title: Sudan enters 4th year of civil war as UN official says ‘world has failed’ to meet crisis
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war entered its fourth year with tens of thousands killed and over 10 million displaced. A UN official said the world has failed to adequately respond to the crisis involving fighting between the army and a militia allegedly backed by the UAE.

stories.title: ADL reports ‘systemic failure’ to protect Instagram users from antisemitic content
stories.summary: The Anti-Defamation League released a report describing a systemic failure by Instagram to protect users from antisemitic content. ADL head Jonathan Greenblatt said the platform is becoming a hub for hate, especially after it ended its fact-checking program.

stories.title: Turning point: Russia is now losing more soldiers in Ukraine each month than it recruits
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense minister stated that Russia is now losing more soldiers each month in Ukraine than it can recruit, describing the development as a turning point in the conflict.

stories.title: ‘Don’t lose sight of Ukraine,’ Nato chief tells European allies – Europe live
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte urged European allies at a Berlin meeting of defence ministers not to lose sight of the Ukraine conflict and to boost military backing for Kyiv to $60 billion in 2026. The meeting included officials from key supporters including Germany and Britain.

stories.title: After three years of war, Sudan in focus at Berlin donor talks
stories.summary: International donors convened in Berlin to raise more than $1 billion in humanitarian aid for Sudan, where a civil war now in its third year has displaced millions and created a severe humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: 'War on women and girls' : Sexual violence the 'blueprint and strategy' of Sudan's brutal civil war
stories.summary: As Sudan's civil war enters its fourth year, reports detail how the conflict has evolved into a systematic campaign of sexual violence against women and girls, used as a weapon of war. UN Women officials call for accountability, sustained international attention, and direct support to women-led organizations responding to the crisis.

stories.title: Big US banks rake in near $50bn profit as Iran war shakes markets
stories.summary: Six major U.S. banks, including Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and JP Morgan, reported nearly $50 billion in combined first-quarter profits. The earnings jump was driven by increased demand for trading services as investors reacted to stock market turbulence caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: In Iran, the conflict is unresolved. But in the US, Israel is losing the war
stories.summary: While many Israelis view the conflict with Iran as an existential fight, American public opinion has soured on both the war and Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu continues to rely on President Trump's support amid shifting US sentiment.

stories.title: Amazon enters agreements for nine Australian renewable projects to power datacentres
stories.summary: Amazon signed power agreements for nine new renewable energy projects in New South Wales and Victoria, Australia, including wind, solar, and battery installations. The deals will nearly double the company's renewable energy sourcing in Australia from 430MW to nearly 1GW as it powers its datacentre operations.

stories.title: Yellen says ‘no alternative’ to dollar, urges US-China cooperation for sake of the world
stories.summary: Former U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen, speaking at the HSBC Global Investment Summit in Hong Kong, warned against economic decoupling between the United States and China. She argued there is no alternative to the dollar and said China's export-driven growth and resulting trade surplus have created serious global conflicts.

stories.title: Conflicting reactions to direct talks with Israel underscore Lebanon’s deep internal rift
stories.summary: Direct talks between Lebanon and Israel drew conflicting reactions within Lebanon, highlighting deep internal divisions. Hezbollah rejected negotiations outright, while opposing political factions expressed cautious support. Many Lebanese remain skeptical the talks will succeed.

stories.title: 'If we don't divide the land we're heading to apartheid': Ex-head of Israel's Shin Bet
stories.summary: Former Shin Bet director Ami Ayalon told FRANCE 24 that Israel risks moving toward apartheid unless it agrees to divide the land with the Palestinians. He stressed the limits of military power against Iran and said Middle East stability requires a negotiated agreement with the Palestinian people.

stories.title: Trump threatens to fire Fed chair Jerome Powell amid pressure campaign
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell if he remains in the role past the end of his tenure in May. Trump also intensified a criminal investigation into renovations of the Fed's headquarters as the White House pushes his nominee, Kevin Warsh, to take charge.

stories.title: Russian losses exceed mobilization rate as Ukraine increases battlefield pressure – DM Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Fedorov stated that Russia's battlefield losses have reached record levels, now exceeding the country's monthly mobilization rate, increasing pressure on Moscow's war effort.

stories.title: Sudan: Ranking Member Shaheen, Senators Booker, Coons, Merkley, Van Hollen Statement on the Third Anniversary of the Sudan Civil War
stories.summary: U.S. Senators Shaheen, Booker, Coons, Merkley, and Van Hollen issued a statement marking the third anniversary of the Sudan civil war, urging all parties to take immediate action to end the suffering of the Sudanese people.

stories.title: Sinlaku rips through Northern Mariana Islands as strongest tropical cyclone this year
stories.summary: Super Typhoon Sinlaku struck the Northern Mariana Islands, flipping cars, toppling utility poles, and damaging roofs with fierce winds and heavy rain. More than 1,000 people sheltered across Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. No deaths have been reported so far.

stories.title: Sudan enters fourth year of war as officials lament 'abandoned crisis'
stories.summary: Sudan entered the fourth year of its civil war, with officials describing it as an "abandoned crisis" and the world's largest humanitarian challenge in terms of displacement and hunger.

stories.title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif embarks on three-nation visit to discuss bilateral, regional issues
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif embarked on a three-nation visit covering Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Qatar to discuss bilateral and regional issues, including participation in the Fifth Antalya Diplomacy Forum.

stories.title: Starmer says 'won't yield' to Trump's Mideast war threats
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer rejected pressure from US President Donald Trump to join military action against Iran, even as Trump threatened consequences for a bilateral trade deal, deepening tensions between London and Washington.

stories.title: Xi Jinping calls China-Russia ties 'precious' in current international context
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping described China-Russia ties as "precious" during a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Beijing, emphasizing the enduring significance of the bilateral friendship treaty in the current international context.

stories.title: Russian villagers petition to oust local council head over livestock seizure protests
stories.summary: Residents of Kozikha village in Russia's Novosibirsk Region collected 268 signatures on a petition requesting that the regional governor dismiss village council head Nina Chistyakova for losing public trust, following disputes over livestock seizure protests.

stories.title: Israeli army 'using Gaza tactics' while razing southern Lebanon villages
stories.summary: According to a Haaretz report, the Israeli army is employing tactics similar to those used in Gaza while demolishing villages in southern Lebanon. The military is also building new outposts in Lebanon, suggesting plans for a long-term presence.

stories.title: Camp Mystic official says she still hasn’t reported flood deaths to Texas agency
stories.summary: The medical officer for Camp Mystic, a Christian summer camp in Texas where 27 girls and counselors died in a flood last year, testified she has still not reported the deaths to the state health agency. Mary Liz Eastland, a member of the family that owns the camp, appeared in court as the state reviews the camp's application to reopen.

stories.title: Turkey rocked by two mass school shootings in two days, at least nine killed
stories.summary: Turkey experienced two mass school shootings in two days. In the second incident, in Kahramanmaraş province, a gunman killed eight students and a teacher before taking his own life. Dozens were wounded across both attacks.

stories.title: 254 soldiers per square kilometer: price Russia is paying to move front line
stories.summary: Reports indicate Russia is sustaining approximately 254 soldier casualties per square kilometer of front-line advancement in Ukraine, while Ukraine claims to intercept 90% of Russian attack drones.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer says ‘not going to yield’ to Trump’s Mideast war threats
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer told parliament he would not yield to U.S. pressure to join the war against Iran, stating it was not in the UK's national interest. President Trump had threatened to alter a U.S.-UK trade deal in response to Britain's refusal to participate in the conflict.

stories.title: Trump warns US-UK trade deal ‘can always be changed’ with relations in ‘sad state’
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to alter the U.S.-UK trade deal, saying he gave Britain a better deal than necessary and that relations are in a "sad state" because the UK refused to support the U.S. war on Iran. The deal had previously reduced tariffs on British cars, aluminium, and steel.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces regain control of nearly 50 km² in March – CinC Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Ukrainian defense forces regained control of nearly 50 square kilometers of territory in March, even as Russian forces intensified offensive operations across most of the front line.

stories.title: Russia launches over 300 drones, missiles at Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russia launched over 300 drones and missiles at Ukraine in overnight attacks, targeting port infrastructure in southern Ukraine. At least seven people were wounded in the strikes.

stories.title: Russia repeats offer to take Iran's enriched uranium
stories.summary: Russia has reiterated its offer to take custody of Iran's enriched uranium as a potential solution amid stalled peace talks between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: ‘Erosion of a country’s future’: What has the war cost Sudan?
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war, which began three years ago, has devastated civilian infrastructure and displaced millions. The conflict has caused widespread destruction across the country and pushed large segments of the population into severe hardship.

stories.title: Trump: Xi will give me a 'big, fat, hug' for opening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that China was pleased with his move to permanently open the Strait of Hormuz. Trump claimed President Xi Jinping agreed not to send weapons to Iran. Tuesday marked the first full day of a US blockade of the strait.

stories.title: Trump doubles down in criticising Pope Leo over Iran
stories.summary: Pope Leo criticized U.S. President Donald Trump's threat to destroy Iranian civilization, calling it unacceptable. The pope had also previously declined to join Trump's proposed "Board of Peace" initiative for Gaza. Trump responded by publicly doubling down on his criticism of the pontiff.

stories.title: Children killed in Lebanon as Israeli strikes hit homes far from front lines of war with Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit homes far from the front lines of the war with Hezbollah in Lebanon, killing children. The Israeli military did not deny child casualties but stated it targeted Hezbollah facilities and militants.

stories.title: Raytheon secures $3.7B deal with Ukraine for German-funded Patriot interceptors
stories.summary: Raytheon secured a $3.7 billion contract to supply PAC-2 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, funded by Germany. The exact missile quantity and delivery timeline were not disclosed. The deal comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urges partner nations to make new air-defense commitments.

stories.title: Does Viktor Orbán’s defeat signal a wider backlash against ‘the forces of darkness’?
stories.summary: Opposition leader Péter Magyar won a stunning electoral victory over Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán on April 12, 2026. The result is seen as a boost for liberal democracy in Europe, though analysts caution against expecting similar outcomes in other upcoming European elections.

stories.title: Burj Al Arab closes for restoration after Iran war debris damage
stories.summary: Dubai's Burj Al Arab hotel has closed for restoration after sustaining damage from drone debris linked to the Iran war. The conflict has also disrupted tourism and air travel in the emirate.

stories.title: Russian Law Enforcement Busts $13.2Bln Tax Evasion Operation
stories.summary: Russian law enforcement dismantled a tax evasion operation involving thousands of shell companies that generated more than $13.2 billion in fraudulent deductions.

stories.title: Israel and Hezbollah continue attacks after Israel-Lebanon talks in US
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon while Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel, one day after rare direct negotiations between Israeli and Lebanese officials took place in the United States.

stories.title: Politico: Fico is first in line for Orbán’s disruptor crown — but Brussels has four more leaders to worry about
stories.summary: Politico reported that Slovak PM Robert Fico threatened to veto Ukraine's €90 billion loan, while Czech leader Andrej Babiš demanded a carveout. Italian PM Giorgia Meloni, Bulgarian President Rumen Radev, and Slovenian politician Janez Janša were also cited as potential disruptors of EU consensus.

stories.title: What's behind Israeli attacks along Lebanon's Litani River?
stories.summary: Israel is advancing plans to remove Lebanese homes and residents from the area between the Litani River and the Israeli border to create a buffer zone. The zone is considered strategically significant in the broader Middle East conflict involving Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: What's behind Israel's attacks along Lebanon's Litani River?
stories.summary: Israel is advancing operations along Lebanon's Litani River to remove homes and residents between the river and the Israeli border, aiming to create a buffer zone in a strategically important area of the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky meets Norway’s Crown Prince, thanks for €9 billion in support for Ukraine
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Norway's Crown Prince Haakon and thanked Norway for allocating €9 billion in support for Ukraine this year. The leaders also discussed long-term defense-sector cooperation.

stories.title: Russia ready to help China with energy ahead of Putin’s visit, says foreign minister
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met Chinese President Xi Jinping on April 15 and signaled Moscow's readiness to assist China with energy supplies ahead of President Vladimir Putin's planned visit to Beijing.

stories.title: Ant smuggler sentenced to a year in jail by Kenyan court
stories.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced Chinese national Zhang Kequn to one year in prison and fined him for attempting to smuggle more than 2,200 ants out of Kenya through Nairobi airport. The insects were destined for China, part of a lucrative trade in which individual ants can sell for about $100 each.

stories.title: Iran sees hundreds of thousands of jobs lost due to war
stories.summary: Iran has experienced hundreds of thousands of job losses after six weeks of war. Destroyed industrial facilities have halted production across multiple sectors, severely affecting Iranian workers.

stories.title: Iran: Hundreds of thousands of jobs lost due to war
stories.summary: After six weeks of war, Iran is experiencing growing job losses as destroyed industrial facilities have halted production across multiple sectors, with Iranian workers bearing the brunt of the economic damage.

stories.title: Economy will be slower this quarter because of Iran war, US Treasury chief says
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the economy would slow this quarter due to the war on Iran but predicted a rebound. He noted that oil prices did not yet appear to be significantly affecting inflation expectations.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz departs on official visits to Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Qatar
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed Islamabad for Jeddah, beginning a series of official visits to Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Qatar from April 15 to 18, where he is expected to meet top leadership including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman.

stories.title: Germany to provide further $30 million in aid to Sudan in 2026
stories.summary: Germany announced it will provide an additional $30 million in aid to Sudan in 2026. The ongoing war in Sudan has caused widespread hunger and displaced millions of people.

stories.title: Every 27 minutes, someone is killed in Sudan’s war
stories.summary: Over the three years of Sudan's civil war, an average of 53 people have been killed daily, equating to roughly one death every 27 minutes. The statistic underscores the devastating human toll of the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Erdogan pushes to extend US-Iran ceasefire despite tensions
