stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced that Turkey is working to extend a ceasefire between the United States and Iran and to keep peace talks on track. He also criticized Israeli military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Italian magazine cover of Israeli settler sparks diplomatic backlash
stories.summary: An Italian magazine cover depicting an armed Israeli settler grinning at a Palestinian woman triggered a diplomatic backlash from Israel. The image provoked sharp criticism from Israeli officials.

stories.title: Trump says the Iran war is ‘close to over’. Is he just out of options?
stories.summary: President Trump claimed in a Fox News interview that the six-week-old U.S. war with Iran is nearing its end. Analysts said the statement reflects Trump's desire to break a military deadlock and ease domestic political pressure during a two-week ceasefire, with a deal still considered possible.

stories.title: Kenya fuel prices surge amid global oil crisis and domestic controversy
stories.summary: Kenya announced a sharp rise in fuel prices, with diesel recording its largest increase on record despite a recent tax cut, driven by a global oil crisis and domestic policy disputes.

stories.title: What was agreed in the Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington?
stories.summary: Israel continued conducting deadly airstrikes on Lebanon even as rare US-brokered talks between Israeli and Lebanese representatives began in Washington, raising doubts about the prospects for meaningful negotiations.

stories.title: US-Iran talks: What’s the latest on mediation efforts?
stories.summary: US-Iran mediation efforts have stalled in Islamabad, with Tehran rejecting American preconditions on its nuclear programme. Disputes over sanctions relief and control of the Strait of Hormuz remain key obstacles to a deal.

stories.title: Netanyahu claims to have prevented an Iranian-wrought second Holocaust. If only we could be so sure
stories.summary: In his Holocaust Remembrance Day address, Prime Minister Netanyahu claimed to have prevented Iran from developing nuclear weapons, likening the threat to a second Holocaust. Critics questioned whether such certainty is warranted given the unresolved status of Iran's nuclear programme.

stories.title: Chinese tanker retreats twice from US’ Hormuz blockade in 48 hours
stories.summary: A fully laden Chinese tanker, the Rich Starry, turned back twice in 48 hours from the U.S. naval blockade of traffic leaving Iranian ports after departing the United Arab Emirates. Analysts said the incident illustrates how Chinese commercial vessels are assessing risks, with no country's ships receiving special treatment.

stories.title: Year-long IDF closure said to bolster settler violence by only barring Palestinians’ allies
stories.summary: The Israeli military imposed a year-long closed military zone near the West Bank village of Duma. Critics say the closure is selectively enforced, barring Palestinian allies and activists while settlers continue to assault villagers.

stories.title: Nine dead after Turkey's second school shooting in two days
stories.summary: A student killed nine people and wounded 13 in a school shooting in Kahramanmaras, Turkey. It was the second school shooting in the country in two days, raising widespread alarm.

stories.title: Four dead after Turkey's second school shooting in two days
stories.summary: A student carried out a shooting at a school in Kahramanmaraş, Turkey, killing four people and wounding 20. It was the second school shooting in the country in two days.

stories.title: Israel boxes Paris out of Lebanon talks, halts arms buys as French disconnect grows
stories.summary: Israel has excluded France from Lebanon ceasefire negotiations and halted arms purchases from Paris. Israeli officials called France irrelevant and accused it of undermining security, while a French official denied the claims.

stories.title: China’s CATL to invest US$4.4 billion in mining arm to secure EV battery supply chain
stories.summary: China's CATL, the world's largest EV battery manufacturer, announced plans to invest 30 billion yuan (US$4.4 billion) to establish a mining subsidiary. The new arm will manage existing mining assets and pursue mineral projects domestically and abroad to secure the company's battery supply chain.

stories.title: What people in Lebanon are saying about talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese citizens expressed mixed reactions to the country's first direct talks with Israel in decades. Public opinion in Lebanon remains divided over the diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: UK to provide Ukraine with 120,000 drones in biggest ever package
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced its largest-ever drone package for Ukraine, pledging to deliver at least 120,000 drones during 2025.

stories.title: Nigeria: Group, Traditional Rulers Abolish 'Money Woman' Practice, Free 57 Victims in Cross River Community
stories.summary: In Cross River State, Nigeria, a group working with traditional rulers abolished the "Money Woman" practice and freed 57 victims. Approximately 6.2 million naira was mobilized to secure the initial release of affected women.

stories.title: Farmers owning under 12 acres eligible for new federal subsidy scheme
stories.summary: Pakistan's federal government announced a subsidy programme for farmers owning less than 12 acres of land, aimed at mitigating the adverse impact of the global energy crisis, with registration available through the Pakistan Asaan Khidmat application.

stories.title: What are Iran’s $100bn in frozen assets and where are they held?
stories.summary: Iran is seeking the release of approximately $100 billion in frozen assets held abroad as part of ongoing negotiations with the United States. Tehran says the funds could help rebuild its war-damaged economy.

stories.title: Berlin gets a front-row seat to German weapons’ performance in Ukraine
stories.summary: Germany and Ukraine signed a bilateral agreement on sharing battlefield performance data from German-made weapons systems used in Ukraine, including the Panzerhaubitze 2000, RCH-155 artillery, and the IRIS-T air-defense system. The arrangement gives Berlin direct insight into how its equipment performs in combat.

stories.title: Paris art enthusiast wins €1m Picasso painting in €100 charity raffle
stories.summary: Ari Hodara, a 58-year-old software engineer from Paris, won a Picasso painting worth more than €1 million in a €100 charity raffle. He initially suspected it was a hoax when notified by Christie's auction house. The 1941 work by the Spanish master was the raffle's grand prize.

stories.title: Activist flotilla heads to Gaza from Spain
stories.summary: A flotilla of approximately 40 boats departed from Barcelona, Spain, heading toward Gaza in an attempt to break Israel's naval blockade and deliver humanitarian aid to the territory.

stories.title: Army names its first tiltrotor aircraft: Cheyenne II
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has named its first tiltrotor aircraft the Cheyenne II. The name honors the Cheyenne tribe, whose members have served in every major U.S. war, and references a previously cancelled helicopter program.

stories.title: US officials claim China is ‘hoarding’ oil. What does the data say?
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China of "hoarding" oil and undermining global energy security during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. However, import and inventory data suggest Beijing is facing its own supply pressures as the conflict continues, complicating Washington's claims.

stories.title: Montparnasse Tower: Paris's most unpopular landmark gets a facelift
stories.summary: Paris's Montparnasse Tower, a 1973 skyscraper widely criticized for clashing with the city's historic skyline, is set to undergo a major renovation. Construction is expected to begin in the summer and continue until at least 2030.

stories.title: Russia’s prosecutor general says warrantless access to phone data would aid law enforcement but raises constitutional concerns
stories.summary: Russian Prosecutor General Alexander Gutsan told the upper house of parliament that warrantless access to mobile phone data would significantly aid law enforcement, while acknowledging the proposal raises constitutional concerns.

stories.title: Comptroller pans government for failing to plan for air travel turbulence during war
stories.summary: Israel's state comptroller criticized the government for failing to plan for air travel disruptions during wartime. The report found consumers paid inflated ticket prices and recommended conditioning aid to airlines on prioritizing national interests.

stories.title: Trump says he asked China's Xi not to give Iran weapons
stories.summary: President Trump told Fox Business that he sent a letter to Chinese President Xi Jinping asking him not to supply weapons to Iran. Trump said Xi responded by denying that China was providing arms to Tehran.

stories.title: The underground architecture that has sustained Iran’s military capacity in the face of US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Iran's underground military architecture on Qeshm Island, featuring buried facilities beneath coastal settlements and trade infrastructure, has helped sustain its military capacity during 42 days of intense US-Israeli attacks before a fragile two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Rattled by Trump, US allies eye Japan’s biggest arms opening since WWII
stories.summary: Japan is preparing its most significant easing of arms export restrictions since World War II, drawing interest from allies ranging from Poland to the Philippines. The policy shift comes as US partners seek to diversify defense supply chains amid uncertainty over American commitments under President Trump.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses Drone Deal, Special Tribunal with Norway’s Storting President
stories.summary: President Zelensky met with Storting President Masud Gharahkhani and Norwegian political party leaders to discuss a drone procurement deal, the establishment of a special tribunal for Russian aggression, and broader support for Ukraine.

stories.title: UN watchdog warns North Korea is boosting nuclear weapons capacity
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, speaking in Seoul, warned that North Korea has made very serious advances in its nuclear weapons capacity, including the probable addition of a new uranium enrichment facility. Enriching uranium provides an alternative path to weapons-grade material beyond reprocessing plutonium.

stories.title: Iran's foreign ministry says ceasefire extension reports are unconfirmed
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said reports of an extension to the US-Iran ceasefire are unconfirmed. The Associated Press had earlier reported that mediators were moving closer to extending the truce, which is set to expire on April 22.

stories.title: Trump doubles down in criticising Pope Leo over Iran
stories.summary: President Trump escalated his criticism of Pope Leo over the pontiff's statements regarding the Iran conflict. The remarks followed Pope Leo's warning about the risk of democracies sliding into "majoritarian tyranny."

stories.title: Canada, UK, Australia and Japan urge end to Lebanon hostilities
stories.summary: The United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and Japan jointly called for an urgent ceasefire in Lebanon. The countries condemned attacks that killed UN peacekeepers and warned of a worsening humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Australia books Indian national for alleged sexual assault of woman seated next to him on flight
stories.summary: An Indian national was charged in Australia with the alleged sexual assault of a woman seated next to him on a Singapore-to-Perth flight. Australian Federal Police said the woman was moved to another seat after reporting the incident to cabin staff.

stories.title: Russia-linked hackers compromised scores of Ukrainian prosecutors’ e-mail accounts, data shows
stories.summary: Russia-linked hackers compromised at least 284 email inboxes belonging to Ukrainian prosecutors between September 2024 and March 2026, according to newly revealed data.

stories.title: Iran used Chinese spy satellite to target US bases: Media
stories.summary: Iran reportedly used a Chinese spy satellite to capture images of Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on March 13, 14, and 15, using the intelligence to target U.S. military installations in the region.

stories.title: Olive Growing in Palestine: Roots of resistance in occupied land
stories.summary: The book "Olive Growing in Palestine" examines how Palestinian farmers navigate agricultural survival under Israeli settler-colonial conditions, offering a detailed study of land use and resistance in the occupied territories.

stories.title: At least 9 dead in Turkey’s second school shooting in 2 days
stories.summary: A 14-year-old student shot and killed nine people, including eight fellow pupils and one teacher, and wounded 13 others at a middle school in Kahramanmaraş province in southeastern Turkey. Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci said six of the wounded were in critical condition. It was Turkey's second school shooting in two days.

stories.title: Strikes hit Sloviansk and Sumy as Russia pounds Ukrainian cities
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Ukrainian city of Sloviansk with a FAB-1500 bomb, destroying civilian buildings. Repeated drone attacks also ignited major fires in the industrial zone of Sumy.

stories.title: 168 children killed by Israel's strikes in Lebanon
stories.summary: According to reporting on civilian casualties, at least 168 children were among more than 2,100 people killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon during six weeks of renewed warfare between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah. The report highlighted an 11-year-old boy and his cousin killed while playing soccer.

stories.title: Russia spends $130 billion to circumvent sanctions over four years of war – intelligence
stories.summary: Intelligence reports indicate Russia has spent approximately $130 billion between 2022 and 2025 on efforts to circumvent Western sanctions, including procuring banned goods needed for its war effort.

stories.title: Hong Kong police intercept Maserati, arrest 2 over suspected money laundering
stories.summary: Hong Kong police intercepted a Maserati on Sai Yeung Choi Street South in Mong Kok and arrested a man and woman in their twenties in connection with a suspected money laundering case. Officers from the New Territories North regional headquarters searched the vehicle during the operation.

stories.title: Why Israel’s Post-Oct. 7 Security Doctrine Has Failed
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's post-October 7 security strategy—seeking to eliminate rather than manage threats across Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran—has not achieved its objectives.

stories.title: Analysts doubt Iran war will prompt China stimulus, tip ‘solid’ first-quarter GDP growth
stories.summary: Analysts said the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and the competing blockades of the Strait of Hormuz are likely to overshadow China's first-quarter economic performance. Most observers expect Beijing to adopt a wait-and-see approach, with little likelihood of immediate stimulus measures to meet its annual growth target.

stories.title: EU budget chief pitches collaboration and bonds on Hong Kong leg of Asia tour
stories.summary: EU Budget Commissioner Piotr Serafin, visiting Hong Kong on his first Asia tour, said the European Union would remain open to capital from mainland China and Hong Kong despite its de-risking strategy. He expressed interest in financial collaboration with Hong Kong, particularly in green bonds, calling the city a bridge to Asia.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon talks: US Rubio hails 'historic opportunity' even amid challenges
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel held their first direct diplomatic talks in decades on Tuesday in Washington, following weeks of war between Israel and Hezbollah. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the meeting a "historic opportunity" but cautioned that an immediate breakthrough agreement was not expected.

stories.title: Pope heads to Cameroon with message of peace for conflict zone
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV departed Algeria on Wednesday for a four-day visit to Cameroon, where he plans to travel to areas affected by a nearly decade-long separatist conflict in the country's English-speaking regions. He is expected to deliver a message of peace.

stories.title: Dembele sends PSG past wounded Liverpool into Champions League semis
stories.summary: Paris Saint-Germain advanced to the Champions League semi-finals after Ousmane Dembélé scored twice in a 2-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Tuesday. The result gave the defending champions a 4-0 aggregate win over the two legs.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drones Reportedly Target Petrochemical Plant in Bashkortostan
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Sterlitamak Nitrogen-Hydrogen Plant in Bashkortostan, which produces ammonia, nitrogen-based fertilizers, and chemical components used in jet fuel.

stories.title: Kanye West postpones France concert after minister's block call
stories.summary: US rapper Kanye West postponed his concert in Marseille, France, on Tuesday after reports that France's interior minister sought to block the performance. The move was linked to West's previous anti-Semitic remarks.

stories.title: Israel & Hezbollah trade fire a day after historic talks in Washington
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon overnight into Wednesday, a day after the first round of direct Lebanese-Israeli diplomatic talks in Washington. Smoke was visible over the coastal city of Tyre. Southern Lebanon continues to face frequent attacks even as bombardment of Beirut has eased since a deadly strike that killed over 350 people the previous week.

stories.title: Ukraine’s “furious” drones hit Russia’s tire rubber supply chain 1,300+ km away
stories.summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Sterlitamak petrochemical plant in Russia's Bashkortostan region, over 1,300 km from the front lines. The facility produces synthetic rubber for Russia's tire industry and reportedly lacked air defenses.

stories.title: Mediators move to extend US-Iran ceasefire, Trump says talks could resume soon
stories.summary: President Donald Trump indicated that talks with Iran could resume soon and result in a deal, while US forces enforcing a blockade turned back vessels leaving Iranian ports. Vice President JD Vance, who led earlier negotiations in Pakistan that ended without a breakthrough, expressed optimism about progress.

stories.title: India's aviation boom hits turbulence amid Iran war
stories.summary: India's rapidly expanding aviation sector is facing disruptions from the Middle East conflict involving Iran, including longer flight routes and higher fares that expose vulnerabilities in the country's airline industry.

stories.title: Americans’ views of China improve ahead of Trump-Xi summit: Survey
stories.summary: A Pew Research Centre survey found that 27 percent of Americans now hold a favorable view of China, a 6-percentage-point increase since 2025. The shift comes ahead of a planned summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: US shuts down Iran’s maritime trade despite optimism for more talks
stories.summary: The United States effectively shut down Iran's maritime trade through the Strait of Hormuz blockade, despite growing optimism that negotiations could resume. President Trump indicated talks with Tehran on ending the war could restart within the week.

stories.title: Attorney for suspect in attack at Sam Altman’s home says he was in midst of ’mental health crisis’
stories.summary: The public defender for the suspect accused of throwing an incendiary device at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's home said her client has autism and was experiencing an "acute mental health crisis" at the time of the incident.

stories.title: Mediators move closer to extending US-Iran ceasefire, AP reports
stories.summary: The Associated Press reported that mediators have moved closer to extending the US-Iran ceasefire before its April 22 expiration. Regional officials said both parties gave an in-principle agreement to extend the truce to allow further diplomacy on Iran's nuclear programme and the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Zelensky announces deals for PAC-2 missiles, IRIS-T launchers after Europe talks
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced new agreements for the supply of PAC-2 interceptor missiles and additional IRIS-T launchers following talks in Germany and Norway. Both countries also pledged further contributions to the PURL initiative.

stories.title: As world focuses on Iran, Israel ‘engineering starvation policy’ in Gaza
stories.summary: International attention on the US-Iran conflict has overshadowed conditions in Gaza, where restrictions on logistics have caused severe shortages of fuel, food, and medicine for Palestinian civilians.

stories.title: China calls U.S. claims of military pressure on Taiwan a 'distortion'
stories.summary: China rejected U.S. assertions that it is applying military pressure on Taiwan, calling the claims a distortion. Beijing has recently increased military operations around Taiwan, which it considers part of its sovereign territory.

stories.title: Pope Leo lands in Cameroon with message of peace as separatists announce 3-day truce
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Cameroon on Wednesday as part of an 11-day apostolic journey across Africa. Separatist groups in the English-speaking western regions declared a three-day ceasefire to allow the pontiff to visit the conflict-affected area.

stories.title: North Korea is boosting nuclear weapons capacity: IAEA chief
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated that North Korea is expanding its nuclear weapons capacity, estimating Pyongyang holds a few dozen warheads. He cited increased activity including the operation of a light water reactor and activation of facilities beyond the Yongbyon nuclear complex.

stories.title: Xi meets Russian FM as leaders flock to China over Middle East war
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in Beijing as multiple world leaders, including Spain's PM and Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince, visited China amid the Middle East war. Lavrov said Moscow could compensate for China's energy shortages caused by disrupted Strait of Hormuz shipping.

stories.title: 'At every single step there is death and danger': The struggle to get food in Sudan
stories.summary: On the third anniversary of the war in Sudan, which has killed tens of thousands, an aid worker from one of the few remaining NGOs described widespread starvation and the extreme dangers of delivering food. She also highlighted how Sudanese civilians have organized to support one another.

stories.title: Labor to boost defence spending by $53bn over next decade – but plan still short of Donald Trump’s demands
stories.summary: Australia's Labour government plans to increase defence spending by A$53 billion over the next decade, bringing it to about 2.4% of GDP. Defence Minister Richard Marles will unveil the national defence strategy, though the spending level remains below the 3.5% of GDP urged by U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: Given history of ceasefires, it’s no surprise US-Iran truce is fraying
stories.summary: The ceasefire in the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran is fraying, reflecting historical patterns in which truces fail because they address only battle-related violence without resolving underlying causes of conflict. Analysts note that pauses without a shared endgame often reset the battlefield rather than leading to lasting peace.

stories.title: Estonia raids combat-vehicle funds to buy more drones, air defenses
stories.summary: Estonia's defense minister announced the reallocation of combat-vehicle funds toward purchasing more drones and air-defense systems. The decision was driven by lessons learned from Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike petrochemical plant in Russia, sparking fire
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an industrial zone in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan, on the morning of April 15, according to regional head Radiy Khabirov. The attack sparked a fire at the site, though several drones were reportedly intercepted.

stories.title: Over 80% nations got loans from China in the last two decades
stories.summary: A report indicates that over 80% of nations have received loans from China over the past two decades. Chinese banks have lent approximately $200 billion to U.S.-based projects and initiatives, making the United States the largest recipient of Chinese lending.

stories.title: Kazakhstan hires Chinese firm to replace Shell and Eni as Ukrainian strikes hit Russia’s pipeline
stories.summary: Kazakhstan hired a Chinese construction firm to replace Shell and Eni at a key gas field, reportedly prompted by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil pipeline infrastructure that disrupted operations.

stories.title: US eases sanctions on state-run Venezuelan banks
stories.summary: The United States eased sanctions on state-run Venezuelan banks, a move that will facilitate dollar-denominated transactions for those institutions.

stories.title: U.S. shuts down Iran's maritime trade despite optimism for more talks
stories.summary: The United States has moved to shut down Iran's maritime trade amid the ongoing conflict. However, officials from Pakistan, Iran, and Gulf states indicated that U.S. and Iranian negotiating teams could return to Pakistan later this week for further talks.

stories.title: Iran military warns will block Red Sea if US naval blockade continues
stories.summary: Iran's military warned it would block trade through the Red Sea, the Gulf, and the Sea of Oman if the U.S. naval blockade continues. The head of Iran's military central command said continued blockade actions against Iranian vessels would constitute a violation of the ceasefire.

stories.title: Drones target military-linked petrochemical site in Russia’s Bashkortostan
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones targeted a petrochemical facility in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan, a major center of Russia's chemical industry. The site is reportedly associated with the production of components used in military equipment.

stories.title: At least nine people killed in Turkiye’s second school shooting in two days
stories.summary: A school shooting in the south-central Turkish province of Kahramanmaraş killed eight students and a teacher, according to the interior minister. It was the second mass school shooting in Turkey in two days.

stories.title: Yemen's Hodeidah braces for attacks amid US-Israel-Iran standoff
stories.summary: Yemen's port city of Hodeidah is bracing for potential Israeli and U.S. airstrikes amid the broader U.S.-Israel-Iran standoff. Renewed threats of targeting maritime assets with missiles or drones are raising fears of retaliatory attacks on the city.

stories.title: Pakistan PM tours Gulf, Turkey as Saudi gives $3bn boost
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif began a tour of Gulf states and Turkey aimed at reviving U.S.-Iran talks. Saudi Arabia pledged $3 billion to help Pakistan manage an upcoming UAE debt repayment.

stories.title: North Macedonian synagogue hit by arson in country’s 1st antisemitic attack since Holocaust
stories.summary: A synagogue in Skopje, North Macedonia, was targeted in an arson attack, described as the country's first antisemitic incident since the Holocaust. The attack occurred in a country with approximately 200 Jewish residents.

stories.title: Trump doubles down in criticising Pope Leo over Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump reiterated criticism of Pope Leo XIV on Truth Social, urging the Pope to acknowledge Iran's killing of protesters and stating that an Iranian nuclear weapon is "absolutely unacceptable." The Pope had previously condemned Trump's war and immigration policies.

stories.title: EU unveils age-check app amid efforts to better protect children online
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced that an EU-developed age-verification app is ready for deployment to help protect children online. Five EU countries, including France and Italy, have been testing the app as Brussels faces pressure to implement stronger safeguards amid moves by member states to ban social media for minors.

stories.title: Stephen Kapos: The Holocaust survivor who leads pro-Palestine protests
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Stephen Kapos, who survived Nazi-occupied Hungary as a child, has become a prominent pro-Palestine protest leader. He shared his experiences of hiding his identity to avoid Nazi detection during an interview.

stories.title: Senior UAE, Iran officials discuss de-escalation in rare call
stories.summary: Senior UAE and Iranian officials held a rare phone call to discuss regional de-escalation. UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke with Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf about ways to reduce tensions amid the U.S.-Iran war.

stories.title: Nigerian with 'natural explosiveness' aiming for NFL spot
stories.summary: Nigerian athlete Uar Bernard, noted for his physical attributes described as "natural explosiveness," is seeking to be drafted by an NFL team this month.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla sets sail from Barcelona in bid to break Israeli blockade
stories.summary: A flotilla of dozens of boats departed Barcelona on Wednesday aiming to deliver aid to Gaza by breaking Israel's naval blockade. A similar attempt last year involving about 50 boats was intercepted by the Israeli navy, resulting in the arrest and expulsion of crew members including activist Greta Thunberg.

stories.title: FM Lavrov Pledges Energy Support to China After Meeting With Xi
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and pledged continued energy cooperation, describing bilateral ties as playing a stabilizing role in world affairs.

stories.title: Iran details maritime losses from US, Israeli attacks in IMO report
stories.summary: Iran submitted a formal document to the International Maritime Organization's Legal Committee detailing what it describes as severe maritime and civilian losses caused by U.S. and Israeli military attacks.

stories.title: UNHCR chief calls for 'urgent' support to Lebanon during war
stories.summary: UNHCR chief Barham Salih called on the international community to provide urgent support to Lebanon, where a fifth of the population has been displaced by Israel's war. He made the appeal after meeting Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.

stories.title: Hegseth skips Ukraine weapons meeting again — third-tier Pentagon official sent instead
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth skipped another Ukraine weapons coordination meeting; a third-tier Pentagon official attended instead. Over 50 defense ministers were expected to participate virtually on April 15.

stories.title: Asian Cup 2027 draw in Saudi Arabia moved to May 9 over Iran war
stories.summary: The draw for the 24-team 2027 AFC Asian Cup, scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia, was postponed from its original date to May 9 due to the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Can Iran’s small, fast-attack boats challenge US Navy in Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Chinese analysts suggest Iran's small, fast-attack boats could challenge U.S. blockade operations in the Strait of Hormuz despite heavy losses suffered by Iran's navy during the opening weeks of the U.S.-Israeli offensive. The U.S. launched a naval blockade on Monday after peace talks in Pakistan failed over the weekend.

stories.title: Tai Po blaze: Hong Kong official defends refusing mainland Chinese firefighters’ help
stories.summary: A Hong Kong fire services official defended the decision to decline help from mainland Chinese firefighters during the deadly Tai Po blaze, citing concerns about their ability to adapt to the local environment and communicate effectively with Hong Kong counterparts. Deputy Chief Fire Officer Sunny Wong testified on the 12th day of a public evidential hearing.

stories.title: Why Southeast Asian nations are hesitant to join major US-Philippine Balikatan drills
stories.summary: The annual U.S.-Philippine Balikatan military exercises are beginning this month without participation from any Southeast Asian neighbor. Analysts say ASEAN members are hesitant to join because participation could be perceived as taking sides in the strategic rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

stories.title: GE warns ITEP engine program needs ‘little bit more money’ for testing in FY27 budget
stories.summary: GE Aerospace warned that the Improved Turbine Engine Program needs additional funding to complete qualification testing after the president's fiscal year 2027 budget request eliminated ITEP funding entirely.

stories.title: US says Iran's shipping 'completely halted' in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States announced it has completely halted Iran's shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, blocking all of Iran's maritime trade. Tehran is reportedly seeking alternative routes for its exports.

stories.title: Up to 60 explosions reported in Chernihiv region over past 24 hours, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 33 strikes on populated areas in Ukraine's Chernihiv region over 24 hours, resulting in 59 explosions. Two people were wounded and damage was reported at multiple locations.

stories.title: Butch Ware: How the US legacy of slavery led us to Trump’s America
stories.summary: Historian Rudolph "Butch" Ware discussed the legacy of American slavery and its connections to the modern political landscape under the Trump administration. He addressed myths about abolition and the enduring structures of white supremacy.

stories.title: Anger in Lebanon as Israel launches deadly strikes despite diplomatic drive
stories.summary: Israel launched deadly strikes on Lebanon even as diplomatic efforts continued, sparking anger among Lebanese. Hezbollah lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said negotiating with Israel was wrong and warned of internal division.

stories.title: Eyal Weizman: How Israel is engineering genocide and ethnic cleansing
stories.summary: Eyal Weizman, founder of Forensic Architecture, discussed his research agency's use of spatial investigation to document state violence and human rights abuses. He traced what he describes as an architecture of occupation dating back to 1948 across Gaza and the West Bank.

stories.title: Sudan enters 4th year of war as ‘abandoned crisis’ grows
stories.summary: Sudan entered its fourth year of civil war on Wednesday, with fighting between the military and paramilitary forces having displaced 13 million people. The conflict, described as the world's largest humanitarian crisis, is being called an "abandoned crisis" as the Middle East war diverts international attention.

stories.title: US V-P Vance heckled in anti-war protest at University of Georgia
stories.summary: Vice President J.D. Vance was heckled by anti-war protesters during a visit to the University of Georgia. Vance invoked World War II to defend the U.S. bombing campaign against Iran in response to criticism from Pope Leo.

stories.title: Humanoid robots box and perform at Hong Kong AI and robotics fair
stories.summary: Hong Kong's InnoEX 2026 fair showcased humanoid robots capable of boxing, playing music, and performing rescue operations, highlighting China's efforts to integrate intelligent machines into everyday life.

stories.title: Between bombs and talks: What is Israel's endgame in Lebanon?
stories.summary: Lebanon remains caught between Israel's military operations and political demands, Hezbollah's refusal to disarm, and the Lebanese government's limited capacity to intervene. The situation reflects competing and largely unachievable objectives from multiple parties.

stories.title: Scottish leadership quits Your Party over autonomy row
stories.summary: Twelve members of Your Party's Scotland leadership resigned, citing what they described as a dismissive attitude from the UK-level branch toward Scottish autonomy within the party structure.

stories.title: Double standards? Why Iran’s nukes are scrutinised, Israel gets a pass
stories.summary: Israel maintains a policy of nuclear ambiguity regarding its own weapons capability, while Iran's nuclear programme faces intense international scrutiny. The disparity in treatment has drawn accusations of double standards.

stories.title: PSX gains 4,300 points amid hopes of US-Iran talks reviving
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index surged over 4,300 points during intraday trading on Wednesday, driven by optimism that US-Iran peace talks would proceed to a second round, potentially hosted in Islamabad.

stories.title: Sri Lanka repatriates 238 stranded Iranian sailors: Minister
stories.summary: Sri Lanka repatriated 238 Iranian sailors, including 32 rescued from the frigate IRIS Dena, which was attacked on March 4 near Sri Lanka, and 206 from the IRIS Bushehr. Deputy Defence Minister Aruna Jayasekara confirmed the sailors departed on April 14, 2026.

stories.title: Iran offers limited internet in rare move to stem economic losses from war
stories.summary: Iran restored limited internet service in a rare wartime concession aimed at reducing economic losses from the ongoing conflict. The service reportedly does not appear to be available to private individuals.

stories.title: Sanctioned tanker turns back to Strait of Hormuz, day after Gulf exit
stories.summary: A sanctioned tanker reversed course back toward the Strait of Hormuz one day after exiting the Gulf. President Trump announced the Hormuz blockade on April 12, 2026, following the failure of U.S.-Iran peace talks held over the weekend in Islamabad.

stories.title: No diapers: Gaza's infants face growing hygiene crisis
stories.summary: In the Gaza Strip, diaper prices have surged from roughly $3 to over $30 per pack, making basic infant hygiene products unaffordable for most families and deepening a humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: 1 Killed in Fire at Kazan Gunpowder Plant
stories.summary: One person was killed in a fire at the Kazan Gunpowder Plant in Tatarstan, which produces artillery ammunition and gunpowder for small arms. The fire broke out on Tuesday night.

stories.title: Russian attacks on energy sector cause outages in five regions
stories.summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure caused power outages affecting consumers in five Ukrainian regions as of the morning of April 15.

stories.title: How Israel and the US are losing the broader battle against Iran
stories.summary: An analysis examines how Israel and the United States are struggling to translate tactical military victories against Iran, including assassinations of key Iranian leaders, into broader political gains in their ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Malaysia’s content creators battle AI abuse as deepfakes, scam ads spread online
stories.summary: Experts at the Freedom Film Network's International Conference on Film & Society in Kuala Lumpur warned that AI-generated deepfakes, cloned voices, and scam advertisements are harming content creators in Malaysia. Researchers and advocates from across Southeast Asia discussed the threats at the event.

stories.title: One hurt as Hezbollah fires over 40 rockets at northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired over 40 rockets at northern Israel, injuring one person. The Israeli military reported hitting over 200 targets in Lebanon over the previous day.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone forces count their air defense kills by the fortnight — 12 in the first two weeks of April alone
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone force commander Robert Brovdi released video documenting the destruction of 12 Russian air-defense systems in the first two weeks of April, including Tor-M1 units near Mariupol and Luhansk and a Pantsir-S1 in Donetsk Oblast.

stories.title: Jockey Club invested HK$1 billion into basketball betting, will use it for football now
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Jockey Club invested approximately HK$1 billion and hired 180 staff to develop a basketball betting system, but the Hong Kong government halted plans for its rollout. About HK$400 million had already been spent on preparatory work. The operator now plans to repurpose the infrastructure for football betting.

stories.title: Ukraine seeks clarification from Israel over Russian ‘shadow fleet’ ship docking in Haifa
stories.summary: Ukraine's embassy in Israel expressed deep concern after a Russian vessel linked to Moscow's so-called shadow fleet docked in the port of Haifa. Kyiv said the shipment may violate international law and Ukrainian territorial sovereignty.

stories.title: Deadly Israeli strikes hit Gaza’s Al‑Shati camp and Al‑Shifa Hospital
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit Gaza's Al-Shati refugee camp and the area around Al-Shifa Hospital despite an existing ceasefire, killing at least 11 Palestinians in renewed violence.

stories.title: Republicans struggle to highlight Trump’s cuts as Americans see little effect on Tax Day – US politics live
stories.summary: Republicans hoped Trump's 2025 tax cuts would resonate with voters on Tax Day, but many Americans reportedly have not noticed a difference. Separately, President Trump threatened to roll back a U.S.-UK trade deal amid disagreements over Washington's Middle East policy.

stories.title: Pakistan officials visit Tehran as Iran-US talks gain momentum
stories.summary: Pakistani officials traveled to Tehran to help arrange a new round of Iran-US peace talks before a two-week ceasefire is set to expire on April 22.

stories.title: Trump floats new peace talks as hopes grow for end to Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump suggested that a second round of peace talks with Iran could be held in Pakistan later this week, even as tensions persist over the ongoing American naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: FM Sybiha to Israeli counterpart: Importing grain from occupied Ukrainian territories unacceptable after Russian vessel docks in Haifa
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha raised concerns with Israeli counterpart Gideon Saar about a Russian vessel carrying what Kyiv says is stolen Ukrainian grain that docked at an Israeli port. Sybiha called the import of goods from occupied Ukrainian territories unacceptable.

stories.title: Ship ‘spoofing’ in Strait of Hormuz may compound confusion
stories.summary: Experts identified a new pattern of ship "spoofing" — vessels falsifying their location data — in waters around the Strait of Hormuz following the U.S. blockade. The deceptive activity may compound navigational confusion in the already tense waterway.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia pledges $3bn fresh deposit, extends $5bn facility through 2028
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia pledged an additional $3 billion in deposits for Pakistan and extended its existing $5 billion facility through 2028, as announced by Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb in Washington. Pakistan also faces pressure from a $3.5 billion loan repayment due to the UAE.

stories.title: Erdogan says Turkey working to extend Iran ceasefire, continue talks
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced that Ankara is working to extend the ceasefire between the United States and Iran and ensure the continuation of negotiations. He also criticized Israel's attacks on Lebanon as harmful to peace prospects.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Condemns Berlin Conference As Devastating War Enters Fourth Year
stories.summary: Sudan's government condemned a Berlin donor conference as "surprising and unacceptable" interference as war between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces enters its fourth year. Millions remain displaced amid widespread hunger.

stories.title: Ramadan TV: Six things we learned from the 2026 season
stories.summary: The 2026 Ramadan television season featured 81 series, including the Egyptian-produced drama "Ashab El-Ard" set in Gaza. The season remains the biggest TV event in the Arab world with the highest viewership.

stories.title: Rev. Munther Isaac: Israel is fighting Palestinian Christians
stories.summary: Rev. Munther Isaac has accused Israel of actively targeting Palestinian Christians in Jerusalem by restricting worship and undermining their presence in the city.

stories.title: China’s Xi Jinping tells Vietnamese counterpart they should ‘jointly oppose unilateralism’
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping told Vietnamese leader To Lam that the two countries should jointly oppose unilateralism and protectionism. The remarks came during a meeting in Beijing amid heightened energy concerns linked to the Iran conflict. Xi called for safeguarding global free trade and stabilizing supply chains.

stories.title: A shipment of Austrian timber and its tortuous new route to Qatar
stories.summary: A shipment of Austrian spruce timber destined for Qatar's construction industry has been forced onto a lengthy alternative route due to the Iran war. The conflict has disrupted previously routine shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to Doha.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Trump not considering extending ceasefire with Iran, says 'deal is preferable'
stories.summary: President Trump stated he is not considering extending the ceasefire with Iran, expressing a preference for a negotiated deal. He suggested significant developments could unfold within two days.

stories.title: Bilawal to launch Phase-II of Solar Home Systems project today
stories.summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah are inaugurating the second phase of the Solar Home Systems project in Larkana, Sindh, aimed at providing solar energy to deserving households.

stories.title: 700 killed in Sudan drone strikes as humanitarian crisis deepens: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that nearly 700 civilians have been killed in drone strikes in Sudan since January 2026, underscoring the escalating toll as the civil war enters its fourth year.

stories.title: Scottish Labour leader calls claim he tried to do Reform deal a ‘desperate lie’
stories.summary: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar denied claims by Reform UK's Scotland leader Malcolm Offord that Sarwar offered to make a deal with Reform to keep the SNP out of power. Sarwar called the allegation a "desperate lie" and said there had been no backroom contacts with the party.

stories.title: No, south Lebanon towns haven’t disappeared from Apple Maps
stories.summary: Social media claims that Apple intentionally removed southern Lebanese towns from its Maps app in connection with the Israel-Lebanon conflict are false. Apple stated the locations were never indexed and that the coverage gaps predate the current war.

stories.title: How long can China hold out if Trump chokes off Iran’s oil? - analysis
stories.summary: Analysts assess that China can temporarily offset the loss of Iranian crude by tapping strategic stockpiles and sourcing alternatives, but the U.S. naval blockade targeting Iran's oil exports is increasingly being used as leverage against Beijing.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz to depart today on official visits to Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Qatar
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed Islamabad for official visits to Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Qatar from April 15–18, accompanied by a high-level delegation, according to the Foreign Office.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to direct negotiations after 'productive' talks: U.S.
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to enter direct negotiations after Israeli and Lebanese envoys held over two hours of talks in a session mediated by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

stories.title: Iran seeking dialogue, not war, President Pezeshkian says
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran seeks dialogue rather than war and that U.S. attempts to force Iran's surrender would fail. He questioned the legal justification for attacks on civilians, schools, and hospitals.

stories.title: US-Iran peace talks could resume in next two days, Trump says | First Thing
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said U.S.-Iran peace talks could resume in Islamabad within two days. A Pakistani official expressed optimism but suggested the timeline might be longer. Separately, Israel and Lebanon held their first direct negotiations in over three decades in Washington.

stories.title: Hong Kong leader vows reforms to boost safety, national security after Tai Po fire
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee pledged systemic governance reforms in public security following a deadly fire in Tai Po. Beijing's top official overseeing Hong Kong, Xia Baolong, said individuals with "ulterior motives" had exploited the blaze to stir social unrest and called for heightened vigilance.

stories.title: Lightelligence on track with IPO plans as China’s AI photonics race gathers pace
stories.summary: Shanghai-based Lightelligence, which produces silicon photonic computing chips, is advancing its IPO plans after passing its Hong Kong listing hearing. The company is the first globally to achieve large-scale deployment of hybrid optical-electronic computing. The listing comes amid intensifying U.S.-China semiconductor competition.

stories.title: ‘Psychological torture’: outcry over conditions at ICE desert detention camp
stories.summary: Detainees at Camp East Montana, a large tent-based ICE detention facility in west Texas, described harsh conditions including near-freezing temperatures, constant dust, leaking tarps, and what they called psychological torture. The facility houses immigration detainees amid ongoing U.S. enforcement operations.

stories.title: Missile strike on Dnipro: 19 wounded remain hospitalized, 13 in intensive care
stories.summary: Nineteen people remain hospitalized in Dnipro following a Russian missile strike on the afternoon of April 14, with 13 of them in intensive care.

stories.title: After 3 years of conflict, gold is the driving force behind Sudan's civil war
stories.summary: On the third anniversary of Sudan's civil war, journalist Roula Merhej spoke to Africanews about how gold and other economic factors have become central driving forces behind the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Trump’s push to cut interest rates has echoes of ‘banana republic’, says Yellen
stories.summary: Former U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen criticized President Donald Trump's push to lower interest rates, comparing the approach to that of a "banana republic." She warned that reducing rates to cut debt service costs on the U.S.'s $39 trillion debt could lead to uncontrolled inflation.

stories.title: Kanye West postpones Marseille concert after French authorities say they’ll seek ban
stories.summary: Kanye West postponed a planned concert in Marseille, France, after French authorities announced they would seek to ban the event. The artist, who has a history of antisemitic remarks, said he did not want to put fans in a difficult position.

stories.title: UK’s largest housebuilder to buy less land, in blow to Labour’s homes target
stories.summary: Britain's largest housebuilder, Barratt Redrow, announced plans to significantly reduce land purchases, citing the impact of the Iran war on mortgage rates and construction costs. The company cut its plot approval target to 7,000–9,000, down from previous guidance of 10,000–12,000, putting pressure on Labour's housebuilding goals.

stories.title: Short-term gains for China from US-Iran war may turn to longer-term pain
stories.summary: Beijing may be gaining short-term diplomatic advantages from the U.S.-Iran war, but analysts warn the conflict poses longer-term risks to China's energy security and economy. The war delayed a planned Trump visit to Beijing, disrupting what China's foreign minister had predicted would be a "big year" for bilateral relations.

stories.title: US doesn’t ‘have time for Ukraine’ because of Iran war: Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that the United States does not "have time for Ukraine" because of the Iran war. He said deliveries of U.S. arms to Ukraine have become "a big problem" as Washington's attention shifts to the Middle East.

stories.title: Another U.S. strike on suspected drug boat in the eastern Pacific kills four
stories.summary: The U.S. military carried out another strike on a suspected drug-trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific, killing four people. The cumulative death toll from such operations has reached 175 since they began in early September.

stories.title: Canada, Britain, Australia, Japan call for ‘urgent end to hostilities in Lebanon’
stories.summary: Canada, Britain, Australia, and Japan jointly called for an urgent end to hostilities in Lebanon, where Israeli attacks have killed more than 2,000 people since March.

stories.title: Immigrants should think of themselves as Americans first: Vance
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance urged immigrants to identify as Americans first. He cited his father-in-law, an Indian immigrant, as someone who contributed to the U.S. without asking Vance to act specifically in the interest of his country of origin.

stories.title: Israeli forces number Palestinian women’s hands during Jenin invasion
stories.summary: Israeli forces marked dozens of Palestinian women with numbers on their hands during the ongoing invasion of the Jenin refugee camp in the occupied West Bank. Approximately 40,000 Palestinians have been forcibly expelled from Jenin and other northern West Bank camps.

stories.title: Report: only a rise in rival party support could push Putin to ease Russia’s internet restrictions
stories.summary: An independent Russian political newsletter reported that Vladimir Putin might ease Russia's internet restrictions only if rival political parties gain significant support ahead of upcoming parliamentary elections.

stories.title: Trump dismisses concern Iran war will derail China trip: interview
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed concerns that the war on Iran would disrupt his planned visit to Beijing to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping. In a Fox Business interview, Trump said he had exchanged letters with Xi, asking China not to supply weapons to Iran.

stories.title: IMF cuts growth outlook, warns world already drifting toward more adverse scenario
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund lowered its global growth forecast, warning that conditions are drifting toward a more adverse scenario. Under its worst-case outlook, the global economy nears recession with oil prices averaging $110 per barrel in 2026 and $125 in 2027.

stories.title: Chinese steelmakers coordinate response to EU’s carbon-linked import imposts
stories.summary: China's major steelmakers are coordinating efforts to adjust export strategies and compliance systems in response to the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which took full effect this year. The CBAM imposes carbon-linked costs on imports. Industry officials noted that China's indirect steel exports to the EU include significant high-value-added products.

stories.title: Five injured in Kharkiv region over past 24 hours from Russian strikes
stories.summary: Five people were injured in Russia's Kharkiv region on April 14 as a result of Russian strikes over a 24-hour period.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 15 — Hezbollah rockets continue to pummel Israel’s north
stories.summary: Hezbollah continued rocket attacks on northern Israel following the first direct Israel-Lebanon talks in Washington, D.C. A health reporter described conditions along the Israeli border as the Iranian-backed group intensified its strikes.

stories.title: St. Petersburg woman detained in Russia on charges of offending religious believers over Easter bread photo
stories.summary: Russian authorities in St. Petersburg detained a 20-year-old woman on charges of offending religious believers, reportedly in connection with a photograph involving Easter bread shared on social media.

stories.title: Expanding permanent category with veto critical to real reform of UNSC: India
stories.summary: India emphasized that expanding the permanent membership category with veto power is essential for meaningful United Nations Security Council reform. New Delhi reiterated its position that it deserves a permanent seat on the council.

stories.title: Israel and South Korea 'resolve dispute' over President Lee’s controversial Holocaust comments
stories.summary: South Korea's Foreign Minister confirmed that Israel accepted Seoul's explanation regarding President Lee's controversial remarks about the Holocaust, resolving a diplomatic dispute triggered by the president's social media post.

stories.title: Liberia: Infrastructure Gaps Threaten Harper Port's Trade Potential
stories.summary: The Port of Harper in Maryland County, Liberia, is struggling to establish itself as a viable trade hub due to persistent infrastructure and operational constraints, even as West Africa's maritime sector expands.

stories.title: Japan plans US$10 billion support to help Asia secure oil: ‘we are mutually dependent’
stories.summary: Japan announced a financial framework worth approximately US$10 billion to help Asian nations procure energy resources and bolster stockpiles amid rising Middle East tensions. Funding will be channeled through state-backed institutions including Japan Bank for International Cooperation and Nippon Export and Investment Insurance.

stories.title: Israeli military attacks kill at least eight people in Gaza in one day
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes killed at least eight people and wounded 29 across the Gaza Strip in a 24-hour period. Gaza's health ministry reported a total of 72,344 Palestinians killed since the war began, with 765 killed since the October 11 ceasefire.

stories.title: Coalition in London vows Nakba march despite police rejection
stories.summary: The Palestine Coalition in London announced it will proceed with a planned Nakba commemoration march despite police rejecting the proposed route.

stories.title: Israel, Iran, and the US: The uncertain ceasefire and nuclear standoff
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Dispatch podcast discussed the uncertain ceasefire dynamics involving Israel, Iran, and the United States, along with the broader nuclear standoff and its implications for daily life in Israel.

stories.title: Italy suspends long-standing defence agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italy suspended the renewal of a 20-year defence agreement with Israel amid recent tensions between the two countries. The decision reflects growing diplomatic friction over ongoing regional conflicts.

stories.title: What you need to know about Israel’s ambassador to the US
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador to the U.S. Yechiel Leiter held talks with his Lebanese counterpart. Critics have raised concerns about Leiter's suitability as a negotiator in the diplomatic process.

stories.title: Pope’s visit raises hopes for peace in cameroon’s anglophone region
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV's upcoming visit to Cameroon's conflict-affected anglophone region is raising cautious hopes for peace among residents and leaders who have called for an end to years of violence.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at Russia’s oldest gunpowder plant, injuring several
stories.summary: A fire broke out at the Kazan Gunpowder Plant in Tatarstan on April 14, causing partial structural collapse and injuring several people. Authorities attributed the blaze to a technical malfunction.

stories.title: Italian papers united as PM Meloni faces off with Trump
stories.summary: Italian front pages rallied behind Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni as she confronted US President Donald Trump. The press review also highlighted war robots capturing Russian positions in Ukraine for the first time, the Sudan war entering its fourth year, and the World Press Photo awards.

stories.title: Haitian factory workers protest for higher wages as oil prices surge
stories.summary: Hundreds of factory workers protested in Haiti's capital on Tuesday, demanding a higher minimum wage as the conflict in Iran drives up global oil prices and increases living costs.

stories.title: France’s Ekitike to miss World Cup after Liverpool Champions League injury
stories.summary: Liverpool striker Hugo Ekitike was stretchered off during a Champions League match against Paris Saint-Germain. The France international will miss the upcoming World Cup due to the injury sustained in the defeat.

stories.title: Nazareth woman charged with spying for Iran
stories.summary: A woman from Nazareth, identified as Shomua Abu Abed, was charged with spying for Iran. She allegedly surveilled the Haifa oil refinery, IDF military bases, and a former Israeli official in exchange for payment.

stories.title: Toddler among 10 killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
stories.summary: Gaza's civil defence agency reported that 10 people, including a toddler, were killed in separate Israeli strikes in northern Gaza on Tuesday. The violence persists despite a ceasefire that took effect on October 10, with Israel and Hamas each accusing the other of violations.

stories.title: China tests submarine cable cutter at 3,500-metre depth
stories.summary: China's research vessel "Haiyang Dizhi 2" completed a deep-sea mission that included testing a device capable of cutting underwater structures such as submarine cables at a depth of 3,500 metres. The test used a deep-sea electro-hydrostatic actuator. The Ministry of Natural Resources confirmed the mission concluded on Saturday.

stories.title: Sri Lanka repatriates 238 Iranian sailors stranded after US torpedo attack
stories.summary: Sri Lanka repatriated 238 Iranian sailors who had been stranded after a US attack on the Iranian vessel Iris Dena. The attack reportedly killed 104 people aboard the ship.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks to shield Gulf states as US-Iran talks set to resume
stories.summary: Pakistan is preparing to host a second round of U.S.-Iran negotiations while its mediators work to shield Gulf monarchies from the conflict. Pakistani mediation has facilitated confidence-building phone calls between Iranian and U.S. officials. The outcome depends largely on whether the talks produce substantive progress.

stories.title: War and Peace: Israel brings Lebanon to negotiating table as airstrikes rain down on Beirut
stories.summary: Former Lebanese Foreign Minister Farès Boueiz described the ongoing Israeli-Lebanese talks as an exploratory stage rather than a breakthrough. He noted a fundamental misalignment: Lebanon seeks an immediate ceasefire and implementation of UN Resolution 1701, while Israel is pursuing full political peace and normalization of relations.

stories.title: Number of injured in Cherkasy drone attack rises to four
stories.summary: Four people were injured in the central Ukrainian city of Cherkasy following an attack by Russian drones.

stories.title: Winning without victory: Why the real war with Iran starts now-opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that while active hostilities between the U.S. and Iran may have subsided, the broader strategic competition between the two countries is far from resolved.

stories.title: Pope to urge peace in Cameroon's conflict zone
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to arrive in Cameroon on Wednesday as part of an African tour, following suicide attacks in Algeria on his first day. He will meet President Paul Biya before traveling to a conflict zone in the English-speaking region, where separatists have fought the Cameroonian army for nearly a decade.

stories.title: Israeli forces launch large-scale raids, demolitions in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted large-scale raids across the occupied West Bank, arresting dozens of Palestinians and carrying out house searches and demolitions. Operations took place in Ya'bad and Zububa near Jenin, along with other locations.

stories.title: Peru candidate demands vote annulment as count tightens
stories.summary: Peruvian right-wing presidential candidate Rafael Lopez Aliaga rallied supporters in Lima on Tuesday, demanding authorities annul the first-round election results over fraud allegations. He is in a tight three-way contest for second place in Sunday's vote; the runner-up will face conservative frontrunner Keiko Fujimori in a June presidential run-off.

stories.title: China cements Russia ties as both win from US war
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said after meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing that Russia can help compensate for energy supply shortfalls caused by the Iran war, including disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Lavrov described Chinese-Russian ties as "unshakeable."

stories.title: Frenchman scoops up 1 million euro Picasso painting in Paris raffle
stories.summary: A 59-year-old Parisian software engineer named Ari Hodara won a Picasso painting valued at 1 million euros in a non-profit raffle held at Christie's auction house in Paris on Tuesday. The draw selected from 120,000 tickets sold at 100 euros each, with proceeds funding Alzheimer's disease research.

stories.title: Lebanese 'cautiously optimistic' as talks with Israel unfold in Washington
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to direct negotiations following talks in Washington on Tuesday, which US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called a "historic opportunity" for peace. Lebanon's ambassador to the United States, Nada Hamadeh Moawad, called for a ceasefire during the discussions.

stories.title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker 2026
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met multiple world leaders this week, including Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, Vietnamese leader To Lam, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, and Abu Dhabi's crown prince. U.S. President Donald Trump postponed his China trip to May 14–15 due to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: US lets Russian oil waiver expire—but the holes remain
stories.summary: The United States allowed a waiver on Russian oil sanctions to expire, reimposing restrictions. However, analysts question whether the renewed sanctions will effectively curtail Russian oil revenues given existing enforcement gaps.

stories.title: U.S. eases sanctions on Venezuela central bank
stories.summary: The United States eased sanctions on Venezuela's central bank, though specific details of the relief measures were not immediately available.

stories.title: Israeli army issues new evacuation call to south Lebanon residents
stories.summary: Israel's military issued a new evacuation order for residents of south Lebanon on Wednesday as it continued its offensive against Hezbollah militants. The order came one day after direct talks were held in Washington between the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to the United States.

stories.title: US scraps deadline for Holocaust-looted art claims, paving way for new restitution efforts
stories.summary: President Trump signed legislation expanding the 2016 HEAR Act governing Holocaust-looted art restitution claims. The law removes the previous deadline for claims and bars current artwork holders from using certain legal defenses such as switching courts.

stories.title: Hungary for change
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party faced defeat in Hungary's recent elections after 16 years in power. Far-right allies from across Europe and Latin America traveled to Budapest to support Orbán's bid for a fifth term, but their efforts were unsuccessful.

stories.title: After three years of war, exiled Sudanese find their place in Kenya
stories.summary: Wednesday marks three years since the start of Sudan's civil war, which has displaced 14 million people, with roughly 4 million fleeing the country. Kenya's capital Nairobi has become a hub for Sudanese refugees as well as political and armed groups connected to the conflict.

stories.title: Israel demolishes UNESCO-protected shrine in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces demolished at least nine religious sites in southern Lebanon's border villages through controlled explosions, including a shrine with UNESCO-protected status.

stories.title: Russian forces drop FAB-1500 on Sloviansk, injuring one and destroying historic landmark
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the central part of Sloviansk in Donetsk Oblast with a FAB-1500 aerial bomb, injuring one person and destroying a historic landmark.

stories.title: Israeli drone strike kills two in Lebanon's Tyre
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike on the Tyre-Beirut highway in eastern Lebanon killed two people on Wednesday, according to Lebanese media reports.

stories.title: Back to the table?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump ordered a blockade of Iranian shipments through the Strait of Hormuz shortly after high-level U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without a formal agreement. The move aims to pressure Tehran into accepting terms presented by Vice President J.D. Vance during the Islamabad discussions.

stories.title: US urges IMF, World Bank to abandon climate finance goals
stories.summary: The Trump administration is pressuring the World Bank and International Monetary Fund to abandon clean energy development goals. Separately, Russia pledged to compensate for any shortfall in Chinese oil supplies caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, while crude prices fell on hopes of renewed peace talks.

stories.title: Uganda: Law Society Rejects Seven-Year Term Proposal, Warns of Constitutional Crisis
stories.summary: The Uganda Law Society opposed proposals to extend political terms from five to seven years, warning the move could undermine democratic principles and trigger a constitutional crisis.

stories.title: Art Basel Hong Kong, other events drive 14% year-on-year rise in March tourist arrivals
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Tourism Board reported a 14 percent year-on-year increase in visitor arrivals in March, driven by events including Art Basel Hong Kong and ComplexCon. First-quarter arrivals reached 14.31 million, up 17 percent year-on-year. The board cautioned that the U.S.-Israel war with Iran could introduce volatility.

stories.title: Iran citizen held in France over pro-Palestine comments returns home
stories.summary: Iranian citizen Mahdieh Esfandiari, detained in France over pro-Palestine comments, has returned to Iran. Her release came one week after Iran freed two French citizens who had been held on espionage charges.

stories.title: Haiti gangs under pressure but adapting to crackdown: UN report
stories.summary: A United Nations report found that Haitian gangs are under increased pressure but are adapting to the ongoing security crackdown. Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, has faced a deep and prolonged security crisis.

stories.title: Trump says no need to extend Iran ceasefire, predicts ‘an amazing two days ahead’
stories.summary: President Trump said there was no need to extend the Iran ceasefire, predicting "an amazing two days ahead." CENTCOM confirmed the naval blockade on Iran was fully implemented after 36 hours, while the IAEA chief called for detailed nuclear oversight in any deal.

stories.title: Israeli jailers assaulted Marwan Barghouti three times in a month, lawyer says
stories.summary: Palestinian political prisoner Marwan Barghouti was violently assaulted three times in one month by Israeli prison guards, according to his lawyer. The attacks occurred while he was in solitary confinement at Megiddo and Ramon prisons in northern and southern Israel.

stories.title: Sliver of hope
stories.summary: Reports indicate the U.S. and Iran may hold another round of negotiations, possibly in Pakistan, following earlier talks. President Trump signaled openness to further meetings. Pakistan and other intermediaries have been actively working to prevent a collapse in the diplomatic process.

stories.title: Kenya fuel prices rise sharply despite reduction in tax due to Iran war
stories.summary: Diesel prices in Kenya rose by a record margin despite a reduction in value-added tax, with the increase attributed to the broader impact of the Iran war on global energy markets.

stories.title: Jaishankar speaks to Israeli counterpart Gideon Sa'ar over ‘different aspects’ of West Asia crisis
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar spoke by phone with Israeli counterpart Gideon Sa'ar about various aspects of the West Asia crisis. The call came amid efforts by the U.S. and Iran to arrange a fresh round of negotiations following the collapse of initial talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: North Korea boosting ability to manufacture nuclear arms, IAEA chief warns
stories.summary: IAEA Director General warned that North Korea is rapidly expanding its ability to manufacture nuclear weapons. The agency reported a significant increase in operations at North Korea's Yongbyon nuclear reactor complex.

stories.title: Strong China-Russia relations are stabilising force in a ‘turbulent’ landscape: Xi Jinping
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Beijing and characterized strong China-Russia relations as a stabilizing force amid global turbulence. Xi urged deeper "all-around cooperation" and called for reinvigorating the authority of the United Nations.

stories.title: Pakistani delegation heads to Iran with US message on new talks
stories.summary: A Pakistani delegation departed for Iran carrying a message from the United States to Tehran, aimed at facilitating planning for a second round of direct talks between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war 'close to over' amid ongoing Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared the conflict with Iran is nearing its end while the U.S. military continues enforcing a full port blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan is reportedly pushing for new negotiations between the parties.

stories.title: Are US-Singapore relations under pressure as public trust declines?
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters gathered at Singapore's Hong Lim Park to denounce the U.S. military's actions, reflecting declining public trust in Washington across Southeast Asia. The demonstration, which required government permission, came amid regional backlash over the U.S.-led war on Iran.

stories.title: War update: 212 clashes on front lines in past day
stories.summary: Ukrainian military officials recorded 212 combat engagements between Ukrainian and Russian forces along the front lines on April 14.

stories.title: Chinese‑built satellite in Iranian hands tracked US bases - report
stories.summary: A report reveals that Iran secretly acquired a Chinese-built spy satellite, the TEE-01B, enabling it to monitor US military bases across the Middle East during the recent conflict, including air and naval facilities.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims rocket attack on northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed responsibility for rocket barrages targeting the Israeli settlements of Metula, Kfar Giladi, and Kiryat Shmona in northern Israel.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Defends Airstrikes On Border Market, Orders Probe Into Civilian Casualties
stories.summary: Nigeria's government defended airstrikes on a border market while ordering a full investigation into reported civilian casualties resulting from the military operation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nine Killed in Fresh Attack As Fear Grips Benue Communities
stories.summary: Nine residents were killed in an attack in Edikwu Ankpali, Apa Local Government Area of Benue State, Nigeria, as renewed violence deepens insecurity and prompts community demands for urgent government action.

stories.title: Anti-encroachment operation triggers violent backlash from villagers in Islamabad
stories.summary: An anti-encroachment operation by Islamabad's Capital Development Authority in Noorpur Shahan's Noori Bagh Mohallah triggered violent clashes. At least eight policemen were injured, two vehicles were torched, and police used teargas and pellets against resisting villagers.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan in a Week Issue #29
stories.summary: The Ayin Network published its 29th weekly briefing on Sudan, summarizing major developments amid the country's ongoing devastating war.

stories.title: South Africa: How the Education Department Plans to Keep Pregnant Learners in School
stories.summary: South Africa's Department of Basic Education proposed draft regulations to prevent the quiet expulsion of pregnant learners, including mandatory reporting laws and academic protections, though legal advocates warn schools still push expecting teens out.

stories.title: Palestinian leader Barghouti endures ‘violent’ assaults in Israeli prisons
stories.summary: Palestinian leader Marwan Barghouti has reportedly endured violent assaults in Israeli prisons, according to recent reports. Last year he sustained broken ribs and head injuries during an attack while in custody.

stories.title: Russian drones strike port infrastructure in Odesa region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region using attack drones, continuing a pattern of targeting the area's logistical facilities.

stories.title: No peace, no normalization: What Lebanon really wants - analysis
stories.summary: Analysts are examining why Lebanon, which previously boycotted Israel and labeled it an enemy, is now actively pursuing direct talks. The key issues remain achieving peace and the question of normalization between the two countries.

stories.title: The human cost of the war in Sudan, three years on
stories.summary: Three years after the eruption of conflict in Sudan in 2023, the BBC reports the humanitarian toll has been staggering, with massive displacement and widespread suffering across the country.

stories.title: Mpox cases rise to 25 as two more test positive in Sindh
stories.summary: Two more mpox cases were confirmed in Sindh province, Pakistan — one in Karachi and one in Khairpur — raising the provincial total to 25 with nine deaths in 2026. Khairpur is the current hotspot with 18 confirmed cases.

stories.title: State officials among 9 people arrested over deadly stampede at Haiti citadel
stories.summary: Nine people, including five police officers and two state officials, were arrested in connection with a deadly stampede at Haiti's UNESCO-listed Citadelle, a historic fortress.

stories.title: Israel’s spy chief addresses criticism about the war with Iran
stories.summary: Mossad chief David Barnea publicly addressed criticism of Israel's war with Iran, characterizing it as a war "of necessity." His comments come amid ongoing debate about Israel's military operations against Iranian targets.

stories.title: Petition seeks probe of Channel 14, calling it ‘pure poison capsule’ undermining court
stories.summary: An Israeli organization filed a petition seeking a police investigation into Channel 14, a pro-government media outlet. The petition cited inflammatory comments by the channel's pundits, including alleged calls for physical intimidation of Supreme Court justices.
