stories.title: US controls chips in the AI race, but China controls the scoreboard
stories.summary: A strategic analysis suggests China is gaining an advantage in AI competition not through building the most powerful models but through dominance in AI inference and deployment. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's remarks about inference workloads and compute revenue were cited as reflecting a dynamic China has already recognized.

stories.title: First time to Iraq's Kirkuk governor post for Turkmen since 2003
stories.summary: A Turkmen politician has been appointed governor of Kirkuk province in Iraq for the first time since 2003. Kirkuk, located roughly 250 kilometers northeast of Baghdad, is an oil-rich and multi-ethnic disputed territory.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,010 troops, four MLRS in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military estimates that Russian forces lost approximately 1,010 troops and four multiple-launch rocket systems in a single 24-hour period. Cumulative Russian combat losses since February 2022 are estimated at roughly 1,313,970 personnel.

stories.title: Iceland and Poland tip special tribunal for Russia’s aggression to 17 — the minimum needed for a formal vote
stories.summary: Iceland and Poland formally confirmed support for a special tribunal to address Russia's aggression against Ukraine, bringing the total number of backers to 17—the minimum needed for the Council of Europe to table the agreement for a formal vote in mid-May.

stories.title: ‘Food is unifying’: How Lebanon’s migrants are feeding the war-displaced
stories.summary: Migrant communities in Lebanon are helping feed people displaced by the ongoing war in the country. Often marginalized in Lebanese society, these migrants are stepping in to fill gaps left by the state in providing food assistance.

stories.title: Labor lashes Coalition immigration plan as Usman Khawaja calls policy ‘appalling’
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke criticized Opposition Leader Angus Taylor's proposal to prioritize immigration from liberal democracies, saying it would fundamentally change the nation's character. Cricket star Usman Khawaja called the policy "appalling," arguing it would discriminate against Muslims.

stories.title: South Korea secures 270 million barrels of oil from suppliers unaffected by Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: South Korea secured supplies of over 270 million barrels of crude oil from sources unaffected by the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Officials said the amount covers more than three months of the country's oil needs.

stories.title: Arab voices cautiously back Israel-Lebanon talks, blast Hezbollah’s role in war
stories.summary: Arab commentators have expressed cautious support for the Israel-Lebanon direct talks while criticizing Hezbollah's role in the war. Journalist Tony Boulos wrote on social media platform X that he hopes the process will lead to a fair peace agreement.

stories.title: Senate panel flags massive smuggling, tax evasion, revenue losses
stories.summary: A Pakistani Senate panel raised alarms over widespread smuggling and tax evasion, particularly in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Senators reported smuggled diesel sold cheaply in Quetta and open cultivation of cannabis and opium in Qila Abdullah valley.

stories.title: US alleges well-known Mexican human rights activist works for drug cartel
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on a prominent Mexican human rights activist, alleging he worked on behalf of a powerful drug cartel. The activist had for years accused Mexico's armed forces of human rights abuses.

stories.title: Lahore lawyers demand end to Imran’s solitary confinement
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court Bar Association and Lahore Bar Association jointly condemned the solitary confinement of PTI founding chairman and former Prime Minister Imran Khan, demanding an end to his isolation.

stories.title: Ukraine downs 309 of 324 Russian drones in overnight attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 309 of 324 drones launched by Russian forces during an overnight attack beginning on the evening of April 14, according to Ukrainian military officials.

stories.title: Families across Sudan endure years of displacement, hunger, loss
stories.summary: More than nine million people remain displaced in Sudan, while nearly 29 million face acute hunger. Families across the country continue to endure years of conflict-driven displacement and food insecurity.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts thousands of Sikh pilgrims for 2026 baisakhi rites
stories.summary: Pakistan welcomed approximately 2,300 Sikh pilgrims from India for Baisakhi 2026 celebrations at Gurdwara Panja Sahib in Hasan Abdal, located about 45 kilometres from Islamabad.

stories.title: Why Booz Allen is Partnering With One of the World’s Most Important VC Firms
stories.summary: Booz Allen Hamilton and Andreessen Horowitz announced a new partnership aimed at bridging Silicon Valley's technology ecosystem with U.S. government and national security needs. The collaboration addresses venture capital's growing role in defense and the challenges of delivering technology to government agencies.

stories.title: Why Booz Allen is Partnering With One of the World’s Most Important VC Firms
stories.summary: Booz Allen Hamilton and Andreessen Horowitz announced a partnership aimed at integrating Silicon Valley technology into US national security and defense. The collaboration highlights venture capital's growing role in government technology adoption and the persistent challenges of deploying commercial innovations within government agencies.

stories.title: Sour note: China criticises local governments for ‘imprudent’ spending
stories.summary: China's central government publicly criticized several local authorities, including Zhaojue county in Sichuan province, for imprudent fiscal spending. The county, formerly ranked among China's poorest, allegedly used transfer payments to fund tourism projects. The criticism is part of a campaign urging officials to adopt proper standards of governance.

stories.title: India’s nuclear breakthrough lights path to energy independence
stories.summary: Indian scientists achieved criticality at the Kalpakkam prototype fast breeder reactor in Tamil Nadu, marking a significant milestone in India's nuclear energy program. The breakthrough advances India's ability to harness its thorium reserves, which represent roughly 25 percent of global deposits, moving toward greater energy self-reliance.

stories.title: US destroyer interdicts two oil tankers attempting to leave Iran, official says
stories.summary: A U.S. Navy destroyer intercepted two oil tankers attempting to leave Iran on April 14, one day after the American naval blockade on Iranian ports went into effect.

stories.title: China, Spain call for closer ties amid  ‘crumbling’ world order
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, with both leaders calling for closer Europe-China ties. Xi said the international order is 'crumbling,' while Sanchez emphasized countering threats to multilateralism.

stories.title: Video: Palestinian child killed after Israeli strike targets police car
stories.summary: Three-year-old Yahya al-Malah and four other Palestinians were killed in an Israeli airstrike targeting a police car in Gaza City on Tuesday. Nine bystanders were also wounded, some critically.

stories.title: North Korea rapidly expanding nuclear weapons capability, UN watchdog warns
stories.summary: IAEA head Rafael Grossi warned that North Korea has made "very serious" progress in its nuclear weapons production capability, with a rapid rise in activity at its main nuclear complex. Pyongyang is estimated to have assembled about 50 nuclear warheads, though experts question its ability to miniaturize them for long-range missiles.

stories.title: US Treasury chief Bessent says US growth may exceed 3% or 3.5% this year despite Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent projected that American economic growth could exceed 3 or 3.5 percent in 2026 despite the Iran war. He dismissed reduced global growth forecasts by the IMF and World Bank as an overreaction.

stories.title: Two children among six killed in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least six Palestinians, including two children, in separate strikes across the Gaza Strip, violating the US-brokered ceasefire. A police vehicle was targeted in Gaza City, killing four people and wounding nine.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 47 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 47 of the U.S.-Iran conflict, President Donald Trump signaled a possible second round of negotiations with Iran in the coming days. The development comes amid the ongoing military standoff between the two nations.

stories.title: Ukraine remains Norway's top foreign policy priority – PM Stoere
stories.summary: Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre affirmed that Ukraine remains Norway's top foreign policy priority. The two countries are deepening cooperation in defense and other sectors.

stories.title: US hosts ‘rare’ direct talks between Lebanon and Israel
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted the first direct talks in decades between Israeli and Lebanese envoys in Washington. Foreign ministers from 17 countries urged both sides to seize the opportunity to end the conflict.

stories.title: Alon-Lee Green: 'There are millions of Palestinians living under Israeli military rule for decades'
stories.summary: Alon-Lee Green, National Director of the Israeli-Palestinian grassroots movement Standing Together, argued that Israel's military campaigns are strategically ineffective and morally corrosive. He called controversial new death penalty legislation a discriminatory law that targets only Palestinians and does not apply to Israeli settlers in the West Bank.

stories.title: Silent Killers, Not Signals: Why States Use Poison in Assassinations
stories.summary: Reports that Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny's death was caused by epibatidine, a toxin derived from a South American frog, have renewed attention on state use of poisons in assassinations. The article notes that the erosion of norms against assassinations and chemical weapons increases the likelihood of future poison-based killings, citing operations targeting Iranian leadership and nuclear scientists.

stories.title: Brazil blacklists China’s BYD, how batteries might get a quality upgrade: 7 EV reads
stories.summary: Tesla regained the global top spot in pure electric vehicle sales in Q1, overtaking China's BYD for the first time since late 2024. Separately, Brazil has blacklisted BYD. The roundup covers developments in the EV and battery industries over the past two weeks.

stories.title: Trump eyes round two of Islamabad talks within days
stories.summary: The Trump administration signaled a possible second round of talks with Iran within days as diplomatic efforts intensify. Separately, China warned that a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz would aggravate confrontation in the region.

stories.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills woman, damages homes, business
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the city of Zaporizhzhia killed one woman and damaged residential buildings, a business, and a parking area.

stories.title: Malaysian man jailed in Singapore for raping, robbing Filipino helper
stories.summary: A 24-year-old Malaysian man, Harvin Velanggany, was sentenced in Singapore to eight years in jail and six strokes of the cane for raping a 32-year-old Filipino domestic worker in the Rochor area. He also stole money from the victim. The assault occurred on May 26, 2024, on the worker's day off.

stories.title: IDF troops uncover anti-tank launcher in southern Lebanon, strike Hezbollah targets
stories.summary: Israeli forces uncovered an anti-tank launcher during operations in southern Lebanon and struck Hezbollah targets. The military activity continues as Israeli and Lebanese officials hold direct talks in Washington.

stories.title: World Bank could provide up to $127 billion in funds for countries hit by war, president says
stories.summary: The World Bank announced it could mobilize up to $127 billion in funding to support countries affected by the war. The bank's president indicated that a prolonged conflict would require the institution to seek additional resources.

stories.title: The Demise of Strategic Planning in Israel
stories.summary: The article examines the decline of strategic planning in Israel following Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack and subsequent conflicts in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran. It argues that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has progressively undermined Israel's strategic decision-making by surrounding himself with compliant officials, including the defense minister and heads of Mossad and Shin Bet.

stories.title: Israeli air attacks kill at least nine in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least nine people in southern Lebanon. Five died in the town of Ansariyah, while four bodies were recovered in the Qadmus area, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: In Indonesia, leaked plan for US military overflights triggers sovereignty row
stories.summary: A leaked defense document revealed plans to grant the U.S. military broad overflight access to Indonesian airspace, sparking a domestic backlash amid Washington's war on Iran. Analysts say the proposal, reportedly discussed following a February meeting, raises concerns about President Prabowo Subianto compromising Indonesia's strategic independence.

stories.title: Report: Hezbollah storms Israeli military position in Lebanon, attempt thwarted
stories.summary: The Israeli army reportedly thwarted an attempt by Hezbollah to storm a military position in southern Lebanon, according to Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth. An Israeli battalion commander said forces are working to establish a buffer zone in the area.

stories.title: Trump turns on Meloni, saying she lacks ‘courage’ over US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: President Trump publicly rebuked Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, saying she lacked "courage" in her response to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. The sharp criticism targeted one of Trump's closest European allies.

stories.title: Uzbek chess grandmaster Sindarov sets up world title match with Gukesh
stories.summary: Uzbek chess grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov won the Candidates Tournament with a round to spare. He will face reigning world champion Gukesh of India in a world title match.

stories.title: Sudan slams Berlin donor conference as ‘unacceptable’ as devastating war enters fourth year
stories.summary: Sudan's government condemned a donor conference hosted by Germany in Berlin as "surprising and unacceptable," accusing organizers of meddling in its internal affairs without consulting Khartoum. The conference coincides with the war between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces entering its fourth year.

stories.title: Iran used Chinese spy satellite to target US military bases in Middle East – report
stories.summary: According to a Financial Times report, Iran purchased a Chinese spy satellite in late 2024 and used it to monitor U.S. military bases in the Middle East. The IRGC reportedly directed the satellite to surveil the bases before and after Iranian missile and drone strikes.

stories.title: Uganda: I Don't Want to Hear Corruption Again in Parliament - Museveni Warns NRM MPs
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni issued a stern warning to National Resistance Movement members of parliament against corruption, vowing decisive action against both those who take and offer bribes.

stories.title: Haaretz: Israel demolishing villages in Lebanon 'just like Gaza'
stories.summary: Israeli forces have been demolishing villages in southern Lebanon using methods similar to those employed in Gaza, according to a Haaretz report citing Israeli soldiers. Bulldozers have reportedly been used to raze villages near the border to clear space for military outposts.

stories.title: US Vice-President Vance says mistrust between US and Iran cannot be solved overnight
stories.summary: Vice President J.D. Vance acknowledged that deep mistrust between the United States and Iran cannot be resolved quickly. He indicated that talks aimed at ending the Iran war could resume in Pakistan within the next two days.

stories.title: Nuba Mountains, a fragile refuge on Sudan's front line
stories.summary: The self-governed Nuba Mountains region, situated between Sudan and South Sudan, is contending with frontline war dynamics while hosting hundreds of thousands of refugees it lacks the resources to adequately support.

stories.title: Nuba Mountains: a fragile refuge on Sudan's frontline
stories.summary: The Nuba Mountains, a self-governed region between Sudan and South Sudan, are hosting hundreds of thousands of refugees while contending with the pressures of Sudan's ongoing war and severely limited resources.

stories.title: Sudan: After Three Years of Conflict, Sudan Faces a Deeper Health Crisis
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported that three years of war in Sudan have created the world's largest humanitarian and displacement crisis, with devastating consequences for the population's health.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Enters Political Uncertainty As Parliament Term Expires
stories.summary: Somalia's 11th parliament saw its four-year term expire on Tuesday, pushing the country into political uncertainty amid ongoing tensions over elections and proposed constitutional changes in Mogadishu.

stories.title: Sudan: At Least 245 Child Casualties in Sudan in the First 90 Days of 2026
stories.summary: UNICEF reported that at least 245 children were killed or injured in Sudan during the first 90 days of 2026, with drone attacks accounting for nearly 80 percent of all child casualties.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Cherkasy injures at least three people
stories.summary: At least three people were injured in the central Ukrainian city of Cherkasy during an overnight Russian drone attack.

stories.title: Iran used Chinese spy satellite to target US bases, report says
stories.summary: Iran secretly acquired a Chinese spy satellite, the TEE-01B, built and launched by Chinese company Earth Eye Co, according to the Financial Times. The satellite, obtained by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in late 2024, gave Iran the capability to target US military bases across the Middle East.

stories.title: In Annaba, Pope Leo XIV hails Algeria’s small Catholic flock and Saint Augustine
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass at the Basilica of Saint Augustine in Annaba, Algeria, highlighting the country's small Catholic community and the legacy of Saint Augustine during a symbolic visit.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Chamisa Claims 'Fake News' As Activists Accuse Him of Selling Out
stories.summary: Former Citizens Coalition for Change leader Nelson Chamisa in Zimbabwe pushed back against accusations from opposition activists that he had "sold out the struggle for democracy," calling the claims a propaganda campaign of fake news.

stories.title: China’s Xi meets Russian FM Lavrov, calls relations with Moscow ‘precious’
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Beijing, describing China-Russia relations as "precious." Their discussions covered the ongoing Iran war and other regional concerns.

stories.title: Congress removes deadline for Holocaust-looted art claims, opening door to more restitution
stories.summary: The US Congress removed the sunset clause deadline from a 2016 law governing claims for Holocaust-looted art, enabling further restitution cases. Watchdog groups had argued that owners of looted works were deliberately hiding them until the deadline passed.

stories.title: Ukraine says Russian ship carrying stolen grain docked at Haifa, asks Israel to detain it
stories.summary: Ukraine asked Israel to detain a Russian ship carrying allegedly stolen Ukrainian grain that docked at the port of Haifa. Ukraine's Foreign Minister told Israeli counterpart Sa'ar that illegal trade in stolen goods must not be permitted.

stories.title: Iran says $270bn war loss must be compensated, as fresh talks with US loom
stories.summary: Iran has demanded $270 billion in compensation for war damages caused by U.S. and Israeli attacks on its critical infrastructure. The claim comes as fresh negotiations between Tehran and Washington are expected to begin.

stories.title: Russian attack on Dnipro sparks fire, woman injured
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Dnipro caused a fire in an administrative building and injured one woman in the central Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Ambassadors meet for historic talks in US amid deeply fraught Lebanon-Israel tensions
stories.summary: Lancaster University professor Simon Mabon characterized the Lebanon-Israel conflict as defined by layered, overlapping sovereignties rather than a conventional state-to-state dispute. He noted that while the Washington talks between Israeli and Lebanese officials appear historically significant, the central issue is Israel's confrontation with Hezbollah, a hybrid political and militant group, rather than the Lebanese state.

stories.title: Ambassadors meet for historic talks in US amid deeply fraught Lebanon-Israel tensions
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors held historically significant talks in the United States amid ongoing tensions between the two countries. Analysts caution the negotiations involve complex, overlapping sovereignty issues and should not be treated as conventional diplomacy.

stories.title: Pakistan PM Sharif to depart for Saudi Arabia official visit today
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed Islamabad for an official visit to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, accompanied by a high-level delegation. The visit is part of ongoing Pakistani diplomatic efforts aimed at facilitating US-Iran peace talks.

stories.title: Trump will head to Beijing amid warming trend in sentiment about China at home
stories.summary: A Pew Research Centre survey conducted in March found that positive American views of China have nearly doubled since 2023, ahead of a planned summit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in May. However, a majority of Americans still view China as a competitor rather than a partner.

stories.title: Chinese create ‘wealthy’ online personas by buying exotic ‘lifestyle photos’ warned of legal risks
stories.summary: An online industry in China allows users to purchase luxury lifestyle photographs for as little as one yuan to create fake wealthy personas on social media. The images, sold on e-commerce platforms, feature travel, gourmet dining, and leisure activities, and authorities have warned of potential legal risks.

stories.title: ‘Field of Dreams stuff’: will Leeds finally get its trams after decades of promises?
stories.summary: Leeds, in northern England, has discussed plans for a tram system for decades, dating back to abandoned proposals in the 1980s and 1990s. Local officials and residents remain divided over whether the long-promised transit project will finally be realized.

stories.title: When defense becomes political: Iron Dome's falling US congressional support - editorial
stories.summary: A growing number of progressive US lawmakers have voiced opposition to continued American funding for Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system. Some critics argue the system has emboldened Israel to carry out military operations against other countries.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: US claims blockade has ‘completely halted economic trade’ into Iran, as Trump hints at return to talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: The US military claims its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has completely halted economic trade into Iran. President Trump indicated that US-Iran peace talks could resume in Pakistan within days. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed for Saudi Arabia to facilitate ongoing diplomacy.

stories.title: Sydney judge overturns bail conditions limiting anti-Herzog protester from entering CBD
stories.summary: A Sydney judge overturned bail conditions imposed on Siena Hopper, a 25-year-old protester with no criminal history who was arrested during demonstrations against Israeli President Isaac Herzog. The Downing Centre local court ruled it was not reasonable to bar her from the City of Sydney except for work or court appearances.

stories.title: KKL-JNF unveils new photographs of Forest of the Martyrs to mark Holocaust Remembrance Day
stories.summary: KKL-JNF released new photographs of the Forest of the Martyrs near Jerusalem to mark Holocaust Remembrance Day. Chairman Eyal Ostrinsky described the forest as a living testament to the Jewish and Zionist spirit.

stories.title: US Democrats will try, and try again, to rein in Trump’s Iran war powers
stories.summary: US Senate Democrats plan to vote as soon as Wednesday on a resolution to limit President Trump's war powers regarding the Iran conflict. Party leaders vowed to continue bringing up such resolutions as long as the war persists.

stories.title: In first for an Israeli, Avdija leads Portland to NBA playoffs with 41 points
stories.summary: Israeli basketball player Deni Avdija scored 41 points to lead the Portland Trail Blazers into the NBA playoffs, marking a first for an Israeli player. Portland will face the San Antonio Spurs in the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.

stories.title: Sri Lanka repatriates 238 stranded Iranian sailors
stories.summary: Sri Lanka repatriated 238 Iranian sailors stranded in the country after one of their warships, the IRIS Dena, was torpedoed by a US submarine off Sri Lanka's coast on March 4. The sailors, including 32 rescued from the frigate and 206 from the IRIS Bushehr, departed on Tuesday.

stories.title: Ukraine showcases Borodianka reconstruction in Germany as model for large-scale recovery
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Oleksii Kuleba met German Federal Minister Verena Hubertz in Berlin to present the reconstruction of Borodianka as a model for large-scale recovery efforts across Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine showcases Borodianka reconstruction in Germany as model for large-scale recovery
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Oleksii Kuleba met German Federal Minister Verena Hubertz in Berlin to present the reconstruction of Borodianka as a model for large-scale recovery efforts in Ukraine.

stories.title: Mossad says Israel will keep trying to topple Iran’s government
stories.summary: Mossad chief David Barnea stated that Israel will continue covert operations aimed at toppling Iran's government, even as the U.S. pursues new peace negotiations with Tehran. He acknowledged that Israeli and U.S. bombardment of Iranian military and nuclear sites had not been sufficient to end Iran's clerical-led rule.

stories.title: US military claims maritime superiority after Iran blockade enforcement
stories.summary: US Central Command declared it has achieved "maritime superiority" in the Middle East, stating its blockade of Iranian ports was fully implemented within 36 hours. Admiral Brad Cooper said US forces had halted all sea trade going in and out of Iran.

stories.title: US, Iran may resume talks this week despite port blockade
stories.summary: Signs emerged that the US and Iran may resume diplomatic talks this week despite the ongoing US naval blockade of Iranian ports. The prospect of renewed engagement helped calm global oil markets.

stories.title: US military says blockade of Iran ports ‘completely’ halts economic trade
stories.summary: US Central Command reported that more than 10,000 armed forces personnel, along with warships and aircraft, are enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports that has completely halted the country's economic trade.

stories.title: Victoria left without limits on political donations after high court rules laws unconstitutional
stories.summary: Australia's High Court unanimously ruled that a section of Victoria's electoral act governing political donation caps is unconstitutional. The decision leaves the state with no limits on donations or disclosure requirements. New legislation would need to be introduced urgently before Victoria's November election.

stories.title: Lavrov offers Russia energy to China amid US blockade
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov offered to supply energy to China to offset shortages caused by the US blockade of Iranian ports. Speaking after meeting President Xi Jinping, Lavrov said Russia could help cover the resource deficit for China and other cooperating countries.

stories.title: King Charles to head to US to woo Trump and restore 'closest of friendships'
stories.summary: King Charles is scheduled to visit the United States later in April for a state visit that includes tea and a private meeting with President Donald Trump. The British government hopes the monarch's diplomatic engagement can help mend strained relations between the UK and the US amid tensions linked to the war in Iran.

stories.title: Trump clashes with Pope Leo again, says Iran must not get nuclear bomb
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump addressed Pope Leo on social media, insisting Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon. Trump cited Iranian government killings of protesters, escalating a public dispute with the pontiff.

stories.title: Ben and Jerry’s founder wants Magnum to sell brand; conglomerate says it’s not for sale
stories.summary: Ben & Jerry's co-founder Ben Cohen has called on Magnum's parent conglomerate to sell the Ben & Jerry's brand, accusing the company of stifling social activism. The parent company has stated the brand is not for sale.

stories.title: Several turtles found dead along Balochistan seashore
stories.summary: Multiple dead turtles — including loggerhead, green, and olive ridley species — have been found along the Balochistan coast over the past 20 days, according to WWF-Pakistan. The deaths are attributed to entanglement in fishing gear near Gwadar.

stories.title: In a first, KP govt moves to register Kalash marriages
stories.summary: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government introduced the Kalash Marriage Bill 2026 in the provincial assembly to formally register marriages within the Kalash community, a minority of over 4,000 people in Chitral district's remote valleys.

stories.title: College that pioneered Holocaust studies and birthed Yiddish Book Center to close
stories.summary: Hampshire College, which pioneered Holocaust studies and gave rise to the Yiddish Book Center, announced it will close at the end of 2026 after 61 years. The college cited declining enrollment and mounting debt; the Yiddish Book Center will not be affected.

stories.title: Prabowo’s Russian Roulette
stories.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto visited Moscow and also signed a defense agreement with the United States. The dual engagements highlight Indonesia's balancing act between major global powers.

stories.title: Could the Middle East conflict dent turnout at Hong Kong Rugby Sevens?
stories.summary: Attendance at the Hong Kong Rugby Sevens tournament may be affected by the Middle East conflict, as disrupted flight routes and higher fuel costs have led to softer hotel bookings. The three-day event traditionally draws tens of thousands of overseas visitors.

stories.title: Justice denied: why families of apartheid victims are still searching for answers
stories.summary: In South Africa, families of apartheid-era victims continue to seek justice nearly 30 years after the Truth and Reconciliation Commission hearings began. In June 1985, activists Fort Calata, Matthew Goniwe, Sicelo Mhlauli, and Sparrow Mkonto were intercepted by security police on a road near Cradock and never returned home.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran war 'very close' to ending amid ceasefire deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the US-Iran war is "very close" to ending, with peace talks between Washington and Tehran expected to resume on Thursday amid an ongoing ceasefire deal.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Central Bank Governor Highlights Ethiopia's Financial Reforms At IMF-World Bank Meetings
stories.summary: National Bank of Ethiopia Governor Eyob Tekalign presented Ethiopia's financial sector reform agenda at a Capacity Development Talk held alongside the IMF/World Bank Spring Meetings 2026 in Washington.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda Launches 'Nutrition for All' Campaign to Combat Rising Child Malnutrition
stories.summary: The Ugandan government launched its 'Nutrition for All' campaign to address rising child malnutrition, with health experts and development partners warning of the scale of the crisis across the country.

stories.title: Mozambique: Mozambique Relies On Rwanda's Troops to Fight Terrorism - What Happens If They Leave?
stories.summary: Rwanda has threatened to withdraw its troops from Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province, where they have been helping fight an Islamist insurgency. The potential departure could significantly alter Mozambique's security landscape.

stories.title: Sudan: World Failing Sudan As War Enters a Fourth Year, UN Relief Chief Warns
stories.summary: UN agencies warned that Sudan remains the world's largest humanitarian and displacement crisis, with over 11 million people displaced and tens of thousands killed. UN Relief Chief called for an end to the war as it approaches its three-year mark.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Peace Talks Open As Violence Shifts to Remote Highlands
stories.summary: Peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo's government and M23 rebel delegates opened in Geneva. Fighting in eastern DRC has shifted to remote highland areas that are difficult to access, despite repeated ceasefire efforts.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Drone Strikes Have Killed Nearly 700 Civilians in Three Months, UN Says
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that drone strikes in Sudan have killed nearly 700 civilians in three months. UN aid chief Tom Fletcher said the international community has failed Sudan as the conflict between the army and paramilitary groups enters its fourth year.

stories.title: Iran enrichment limits subject to political decision, IAEA says
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said any moratorium on Iran's uranium enrichment would be determined through political negotiations, not technical assessments. His remarks came as US-Iran talks continue, with reports of discussions on enrichment limits.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudanese Communities Are Rebuilding Under Fire. Will Berlin Back Them?
stories.summary: Civil society groups in Sudan are working to rebuild communities amid ongoing conflict. Advocates are urging international donors meeting in Berlin to provide sustained, open-ended support for local organizations.

stories.title: Over 400,000 Ukrainians live in northern Poland, Consul General says
stories.summary: Approximately 420,000 Ukrainian citizens currently reside in four voivodeships in northern Poland — West Pomeranian, Pomeranian, Kuyavian-Pomeranian, and Warmian-Masurian — according to Ukraine's Consul General in the region.

stories.title: South Korea jails US YouTuber Johnny Somali for kissing ‘comfort women’ statue
stories.summary: American YouTuber Johnny Somali, whose real name is Ramsey Khalid Ismael, was sentenced to six months in prison by a Seoul court for kissing a statue commemorating Korean wartime sex slaves. The 25-year-old had previously gained notoriety for provocative stunts in South Korea and Japan.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel agree to direct negotiations after ‘historic’ Washington talks
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon held their first high-level direct negotiations since 1993 during a meeting in Washington on April 14. The talks are being described as a historic step toward potential peace between the two countries.

stories.title: South Korea jails American YouTuber for public nuisance
stories.summary: A South Korean court jailed American YouTuber Johnny Somali for public nuisance after he sparked outrage by kissing a statue memorializing World War Two-era sex slaves.

stories.title: Trump hints Iran talks could resume this week as US port blockade continues
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump signaled that negotiations with Iran could resume within the week. The UN Secretary General said a restart of talks was "highly probable," even as the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.

stories.title: Why Did China Buy Up the World’s Ports?
stories.summary: China has pursued extensive investments in ports worldwide, focusing less on acquiring sovereign control and more on securing its own strategic supply chain security.

stories.title: Cheap Drones Complicate the Gulf’s AI Boom
stories.summary: The proliferation of inexpensive drones is complicating the Gulf region's push to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure. Analysts note that protection of AI assets is becoming inseparable from ensuring access to them.

stories.title: Chinese rocket force scientist Major General Feng Yufang dies aged 63
stories.summary: Major General Feng Yufang, a leading missile scientist with China's PLA Rocket Force and a member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, died on April 13 at age 63. State media reported he died of illness after a career spanning nearly 40 years in military equipment research.

stories.title: Israel strikes 76 areas in Lebanon, 21 killed
stories.summary: Israeli air and artillery attacks struck 76 cities, towns, and areas across Lebanon on Tuesday, killing 21 people and injuring 29, according to Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health. The total death toll in Lebanon has surpassed 2,089 since the escalation began on March 2, 2026.

stories.title: US Navy forces eight Iran-linked tankers to turn back
stories.summary: US naval forces have compelled eight Iran-linked oil tankers to reverse course since Monday as part of the blockade on Iranian ports, according to The Wall Street Journal. All tankers complied with radio instructions, and no boardings were necessary.

stories.title: Israeli legal advocay group files ICC case against Spanish PM over exports to Iran
stories.summary: Israeli legal advocacy group Shurat HaDin filed a case at the International Criminal Court against Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, accusing his government of exporting components used for military purposes by Iran and its proxies.

stories.title: China rejects US criticism, urges 'end to military operations' in Middle East
stories.summary: China pushed back against US criticism, with a Chinese embassy spokesperson blaming global fuel shortages on Middle East instability rather than Beijing's actions. The spokesperson called for an immediate halt to military operations in the region.

stories.title: Congo to receive first group of deportees from US this week, sources say
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is set to receive more than 30 deportees from the United States this week, according to four sources who spoke to Reuters. The move represents Washington's use of agreements with African governments to accelerate migrant removals.

stories.title: ‘Show patriotism through concrete actions,’ Xia Baolong tells Hong Kong businesspeople
stories.summary: Xia Baolong, director of Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, urged Hong Kong businesspeople to drive economic development by investing in innovation and the Northern Metropolis project. He also accused people with "ulterior motives" of politicizing the deadly Tai Po fire to stir social unrest.

stories.title: US destroyer interdicts two oil tankers attempting to leave Iran, official says
stories.summary: A US destroyer intercepted two oil tankers attempting to leave Iran as part of President Trump's blockade of Iranian ports. The blockade aims to pressure Iran regarding its closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Dutch PM meets with Trump to discuss Ukraine and war in Middle East
stories.summary: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten met with US President Donald Trump in Washington to discuss the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East.

stories.title: Britain’s King Charles to charm Trump on state visit overshadowed by US-UK rift
stories.summary: Britain's King Charles is set to visit the United States on April 27 for a four-day state visit, during which he will have tea and a private meeting with President Trump. The trip, marking the 250th anniversary of U.S. independence, carries added significance amid a U.S.-UK rift over the Iran war.

stories.title: US Centcom says blockade enforced on ships of all nations
stories.summary: US Central Command stated that the blockade on Iranian ports is being enforced impartially against vessels of all nations. US Navy guided-missile destroyers are among the assets carrying out the operation in Iranian coastal waters.

stories.title: US-Iran mistrust cannot be solved overnight, but progress being made, says Vance
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance described US-Iran talks held in Islamabad as unprecedented, noting that meetings at that level had not occurred between the two countries in 47 years. He acknowledged that mutual mistrust cannot be resolved quickly but said progress is being made.

stories.title: UK, Canada, others call for 'urgent end to hostilities' in Lebanon
stories.summary: Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, and several other countries issued a joint statement calling for an urgent end to hostilities in Lebanon. They warned of a worsening humanitarian crisis and stressed that civilians and infrastructure must be protected.

stories.title: US president says war on Iran 'very close to over'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told Fox News he believes the war on Iran is "very close to over," saying he thinks Tehran wants to negotiate a deal. Trump added that without US military action, Iran would have obtained a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: US navy blocks Iranian oil tankers leaving port, officials say
stories.summary: A US Navy destroyer intercepted two oil tankers attempting to leave Iran's Chabahar Port and ordered them to turn around as part of the maritime blockade, according to a US official cited by Reuters. The tankers were among six merchant vessels referenced by US Central Command.

stories.title: Hormuz blockade: shipping industry slams transit fees as 20,000 seafarers still stranded
stories.summary: The International Chamber of Shipping denounced proposed transit tolls in the Strait of Hormuz following the U.S. blockade, calling them a threat to freedom of navigation. The organization noted that approximately 20,000 stranded seafarers remain the shipping community's primary concern.

stories.title: Ukraine to produce drones in Norway, Oslo says
stories.summary: Norway and Ukraine announced strengthened bilateral defence cooperation that will include producing Ukrainian drones in Norway. The Norwegian government confirmed the agreement on Tuesday.

stories.title: US threatens action on Chinese vessels carrying Iran oil
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the United States will prevent China from accessing Iranian oil, stating that Chinese tankers could be blocked in the Strait of Hormuz. Bessent called Beijing an "unreliable global partner" for continuing to purchase Iranian oil.

stories.title: Ex-congressman Eric Swalwell faces second sexual assault probe
stories.summary: Lonna Drewes, a software entrepreneur, has accused former US Congressman Eric Swalwell of drugging and sexually assaulting her in 2018. This marks the second sexual assault probe involving Swalwell.

stories.title: US forces kill 4 people in latest strike on vessels in eastern Pacific
stories.summary: US forces carried out a deadly strike on vessels in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing four people. The incident marked the fourth such lethal US strike in the eastern Pacific within four days.

stories.title: Meta launches sixth annual Sharing Memories Holocaust remembrance project
stories.summary: Meta launched the sixth edition of its annual Sharing Memories project in partnership with the non-profit Our 6 Million to amplify Holocaust survivors' voices as the number of living witnesses continues to decline.

stories.title: Vance says Trump seeking ‘grand bargain’ with Iran
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said President Trump is seeking a "grand bargain" with Iran that would normalize economic relations if Tehran changes course. Speaking at a Turning Point USA event in Georgia, Vance emphasized that preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon remains the core US policy.

stories.title: War spurs EU plan for electricity tax cuts, faster shift from fossil fuels, draft shows
stories.summary: The European Union is drafting plans to reduce electricity taxes and accelerate the transition from fossil fuels to offset the energy impact of the Iran war. The measures aim to reduce consumer exposure to soaring oil and gas prices caused by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: ‘Echoes the dark times’: Recent deadly antisemitism features heavily at March of the Living
stories.summary: The annual March of the Living featured prominently the impact of recent deadly antisemitic attacks. Survivors of contemporary massacres, including the daughter of a man killed in the Bondi Beach attack, joined Holocaust survivors at the event.

stories.title: US to allow waiver on Iran oil to expire, administration sources say
stories.summary: The U.S. administration plans to allow a waiver on Iranian oil sanctions to expire, according to administration sources. The decision comes alongside the existing U.S. blockade on shipments from Iranian ports.

stories.title: Western officials consider Budanov effective negotiator - Bloomberg
stories.summary: According to Bloomberg, Western officials regard Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, as an effective negotiator in peace talks with Russia.

stories.title: Tai Po probe: woman trapped in blaze died after 999 call not passed to fire department
stories.summary: A judge-led panel investigating Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades, which killed 168 people at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, heard testimony that a 999 emergency call was not relayed to the fire department. Representatives from the Fire Services Department and police testified during the 12th day of hearings.

stories.title: Issachar Dov Spiegel pronounced dead after Netanya drowning, brother still missing
stories.summary: Issachar Dov Spiegel was pronounced dead following a drowning incident in Netanya, Israel. His brother remains missing. Rescue operations are being led by the Lehava unit under the Central District Command, with assistance from ZAKA volunteers and special units.

stories.title: US military says 4 killed in fourth ‘drug boat’ strike in a week
stories.summary: The U.S. military confirmed a fourth strike on an alleged drug-trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific within a week, killing four people. U.S. Southern Command released aerial footage of the strike, and the cumulative death toll from the operations continues to rise.

stories.title: Malaysian police recall overflowing cash, gems in 1MDB raid on Najib-linked condo
stories.summary: Malaysian police testified in the High Court about discovering 71 luggage bags overflowing with cash and jewellery worth hundreds of millions of ringgit during a 2018 raid on a luxury condominium at Pavilion Residences in Kuala Lumpur, linked to the 1MDB investigation involving former PM Najib Razak.

stories.title: Zhang Kai: why I left Yale for China at the peak of my career in life science
stories.summary: Professor Zhang Kai, a leading cryo-electron microscopy scientist, left positions at Yale University and Cambridge to return to China. Unlike many returning scientists who remain silent about their reasons, Zhang has spoken openly about his decision and his ambitions in the field.

stories.title: Sheinbaum vows to ‘defend Mexicans at every level’ amid anger at Trump over migrant deaths
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has pushed back against the Trump administration following the deaths of Mexican citizens in US custody and Washington's energy blockade on Cuba. Sheinbaum pledged to defend Mexicans while maintaining a measured diplomatic approach to offset US tariff threats.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon hold direct talks for first time in decades
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon held their first direct talks in decades, resulting in an agreement to begin formal negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon talks unlikely to yield much until Iran undergoes fundamental change
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese officials held direct talks in Washington, with Beirut seeking a ceasefire and Jerusalem seeking the disarmament of Hezbollah. Analysts suggest neither goal is likely achievable as long as Iran continues to support its Lebanese proxy.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 10 in northern Gaza, including toddler, civil defence says
stories.summary: Gaza's civil defence agency reported that Israeli strikes in northern Gaza killed 10 people on Tuesday, including a toddler. Among the attacks, a strike on a police vehicle in Gaza City killed four people. The violence continued despite a ceasefire agreement reached on October 10.

stories.title: US military says it killed four more people in a boat strike in the eastern Pacific
stories.summary: The US Southern Command announced it killed four people in a boat strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Tuesday, claiming without evidence that they were narco-terrorists. This was the third deadly attack on vessels in the region in four days, bringing the total killed since September to 174.

stories.title: US DoJ files for overturning January 6 convictions for far-right groups’ members
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice filed motions to overturn seditious conspiracy convictions of members of the Proud Boys and Oath Keepers for their roles in the January 6, 2021, siege of the US Capitol. The motions were signed by Jeanine Pirro, the Trump-appointed US attorney for the District of Columbia.

stories.title: UN chief says highly probable Iran talks will restart
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated on April 14 that negotiations with Iran could resume in Pakistan within the next two days. UN Secretary-General António Guterres indicated it is highly probable that the Iran talks will restart.

stories.title: UN’s Guterres says highly probable Iran talks will restart
stories.summary: U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said Tuesday that it is highly probable that talks to end the Iran war will restart. He indicated the United Nations had received signals suggesting negotiations would resume.

stories.title: Jailed witness reveals Duterte plotted to oust Philippines’ Marcos
stories.summary: A jailed witness named Ramil Madriaga testified before the Philippine House Committee on Justice that former President Rodrigo Duterte discussed removing President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. from office and even considered assassination. The allegations emerged during impeachment hearings into Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio.

stories.title: KMT chief shows way forward to avoid blind confrontation with Beijing
stories.summary: KMT chairman is positioning the party as a pragmatic alternative to the ruling DPP in Taiwan, advocating engagement rather than confrontation with Beijing. The DPP government under President William Lai has faced criticism over concessions on Taiwan's semiconductor industry under U.S. pressure.

stories.title: 250 missing after migrant boat sinks in Indian Ocean
stories.summary: A migrant boat sank in the Indian Ocean, leaving approximately 250 people missing. The United Nations said the trawler reportedly went down due to heavy winds, rough seas, and overcrowding.

stories.title: Russia’s major mobile carriers warn users to disable VPN for apps to work properly
stories.summary: Russia's major mobile carriers, including leading operators, warned users that official company apps may malfunction when a VPN is active, according to a report by RIA Novosti on April 14.

stories.title: India to host Foreign Minister-level meetings of BRICS and Quad in May
stories.summary: India confirmed it will host foreign minister-level meetings of both BRICS and the Quad in May. The announcement followed a social media post by U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor indicating that Secretary of State Marco Rubio would visit India in May.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel agree to direct negotiations after Washington talks
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to continue direct negotiations following US-mediated talks in Washington on Tuesday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the meeting a historic opportunity. Hezbollah opposed the talks and fired rockets at northern Israeli towns as the meeting began.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill 11, including two children, in day of strikes on Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on northern Gaza killed 11 people, including a three-year-old and a 14-year-old child, during a day of attacks on the territory.

stories.title: China AI robot restaurant analyses diners’ faces, tongues to recommend health-focused dishes
stories.summary: Restaurants in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, are using AI robots to cook up to 100 dishes, handle ordering, serving, and cleaning. One establishment in Xihu district employs eight robots that perform 60 percent of kitchen work, sparking debate on social media about automation in the food industry.

stories.title: Former chief executive of Russia’s main satellite manufacturer placed under house arrest on fraud charges
stories.summary: A court in Krasnoyarsk placed Nikolai Testoedov, former chief executive of ISS Reshetnev, Russia's primary satellite manufacturer, under house arrest on fraud charges.

stories.title: ‘Unreliable partner’: China has been hoarding oil during Middle East war, says US Treasury’s Bessent
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China of hoarding oil during the ongoing Middle East conflict, calling Beijing an "unreliable partner." Bessent said he had raised the issue directly with Chinese officials.

stories.title: My grandfather, the Nazi: A German historian helps families unravel forebears’ crimes
stories.summary: German historian Johannes Spohr, after discovering his own grandfather's role in the Holocaust, now offers workshops helping families uncover their forebears' involvement in Nazi crimes. His work confronts specific family histories within a broader culture of remembrance in Germany.

stories.title: Arson suspect recruited by Russia detained in Lutsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service and National Police detained a young man in the western city of Lutsk who was allegedly recruited by Russian intelligence to carry out an arson attack inside Ukraine.

stories.title: Kanye West postpones Marseille concert as France considers blocking him from performing
stories.summary: US rapper Kanye West announced he is postponing his planned concert in Marseille, France. The decision came after reports that French Interior Minister Bruno Retailleau was seeking to block the performance due to West's past antisemitic remarks.

stories.title: Fertiliser shortages due to Iran war are a key worry for developing world, UN agency says
stories.summary: The head of the United Nations trade agency said fertiliser shortages caused by the Iran war are a pressing concern for developing countries. The agency also warned that gains from rising oil and gas prices for developing-world producers are likely to be short-lived.

stories.title: Middle East live: Trump says Iran talks may resume as Israel, Lebanon open direct track
stories.summary: President Trump said US-Iran peace talks could resume this week, while Israel and Lebanon agreed to launch direct negotiations. The parallel diplomatic developments signal movement on two key Middle East fronts, though ongoing violence underscores the fragility of the process.

stories.title: Cops detain 70 Palestinians hiding in garbage truck while trying to enter Israel
stories.summary: Israeli police detained 70 Palestinians who were hiding inside a garbage truck attempting to enter Israel through a West Bank checkpoint. The Israeli driver of the vehicle was arrested for the apparent smuggling attempt.

stories.title: Haiti’s Culture Ministry fires workers over citadel stampede that killed 25
stories.summary: Haiti's Culture Ministry fired workers in connection with a stampede at the citadel that killed 25 people. At least nine individuals, including police officers and ministry employees, have been arrested.

stories.title: Six ships turned around as part of Strait of Hormuz blockade, US military says
stories.summary: The US military reported that six ships have been turned back as part of a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade targets vessels traveling to or from Iran.

stories.title: Jewish food writer Joan Nathan discovers her relative’s martyrdom and full Holocaust history
stories.summary: Jewish food writer Joan Nathan uncovered details about a relative's martyrdom during the Holocaust, bringing her family's wartime history into sharper personal focus.

stories.title: Irish government majority cut as two lawmakers quit over fuel protests
stories.summary: Two lawmakers supporting the Irish government withdrew their backing on Tuesday over the coalition's response to public demonstrations against surging fuel prices. The departures reduced the government's parliamentary majority to five seats.

stories.title: Russian artist dies by suicide in jail after arrest over online comment, acquaintances say
stories.summary: An artist from Russia's Far East reportedly died by suicide in a pretrial detention center after being arrested over an online comment he had made the previous year, according to acquaintances who spoke to the independent outlet Mediazona.

stories.title: Call to check tech trends when drafting policies after basketball betting U-turn
stories.summary: Hong Kong observers called on authorities to consider technological developments when drafting policies, after the government suspended plans for basketball betting over concerns about prediction market gambling platforms. Officials warned that betting on sports events through such platforms is illegal for Hong Kong residents.

stories.title: Japan’s Narita Airport expansion revives row over forced land sales
stories.summary: Narita International Airport's operator is considering compulsory land acquisition from farmers to build a planned third runway. The move recalls the violent clashes of the 1960s when forced land purchases for the original airport construction sparked confrontations between police and residents.

stories.title: Which countries are most vulnerable as US imposes its own blockade in Persian Gulf?
stories.summary: Asian and European economies face significant vulnerability from the U.S. blockade on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz following the collapse of U.S.-Iran talks. A report by Japanese investment bank Nomura identified Asian economies as the most exposed to disruptions at this critical energy chokepoint.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says war ‘close to over’ as Hormuz blockade continues
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated the war with Iran is "close to over" and suggested a second round of talks could be held in Pakistan, while the US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.

stories.title: In a first, Libya’s rival forces take part in joint US-led military exercises
stories.summary: Libya's rival military forces participated together in joint U.S.-led military exercises for the first time. Libya has been divided between competing factions since 2014.

stories.title: French investigators raid Elysee palace in contracts probe: Source
stories.summary: French investigators raided the Elysee Palace as part of a probe into government contracts. Further details about the scope and targets of the investigation were not immediately available.

stories.title: BBC reports ‘serious malpractices’ continued at Taunsa hospital months after it was linked to HIV outbreak
stories.summary: A BBC investigation found that serious malpractices persisted in the children's ward of Taunsa Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Punjab, Pakistan, months after the facility was linked to an HIV outbreak among children in late 2024. Secret filming by BBC Eye Investigations reportedly showed children's lives were still being put at risk despite Punjab authorities' promises of a crackdown.

stories.title: Zelensky warns that large-scale air attack can take place overnight
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that a large-scale Russian air attack could take place overnight, urging vigilance among defense forces and the population.

stories.title: Unheeded lessons from the US warship nearly sunk by an Iranian mine
stories.summary: Analysis of past incidents, including the near-sinking of a US warship by an Iranian mine, highlights an ongoing and often overlooked threat posed by underwater weapons. Experts warn that institutional memory about such risks remains inadequate.

stories.title: Delcy Rodriguez calls for a ‘Venezuela free of sanctions’ amid US detente
stories.summary: Venezuelan President Delcy Rodriguez called for a "Venezuela free of sanctions" amid a diplomatic détente with the United States, saying limited sanctions relief has been insufficient to stabilize the country's troubled economy.

stories.title: Trump says Iran talks could resume over next two days, NY Post reports
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said peace talks with Iran could resume within two days and indicated negotiations would likely return to Pakistan's capital, Islamabad. Pakistan's army chief has been serving as a mediator in the process.

stories.title: Former Ekho Moskvy editor-in-chief charged with ‘undesirable organization’ violations, Mediazona reports
stories.summary: A Moscow court received an administrative charge against Alexei Venediktov, former editor-in-chief of the shuttered Russian radio station Ekho Moskvy, for alleged violations related to an 'undesirable organization,' according to Mediazona.

stories.title: Ukraine and Norway sign defense partnership declaration
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre signed a declaration on defense partnership during a meeting in Oslo, formalizing closer military cooperation between Ukraine and Norway.

stories.title: High Court to hear petitions on Wednesday calling for Ben Gvir to be fired from gov’t
stories.summary: Israel's High Court is set to hear petitions calling for the dismissal of far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir from the government. The attorney general supports his removal, saying he overstepped his powers, while Prime Minister Netanyahu has opposed the effort.

stories.title: Lebanese and Israeli envoys to meet as Israel presses war on Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli envoys are set to meet in Washington amid ongoing Israeli military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. The talks come one week into a fragile ceasefire between the United States, Israel, and Iran, with Pakistan mediating broader efforts to end the wider conflict.

stories.title: Russian army strikes Kharkiv with guided aerial bomb, causing fire
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv with a guided aerial bomb on Tuesday, igniting a fire at the impact site. Details on casualties were not immediately available.

stories.title: UN says Haiti powerful gang expansion halted but threat persists
stories.summary: A UN expert report said anti-gang operations in Haiti, supported by drone strikes and self-defence groups, have slowed the expansion of powerful armed groups in Port-au-Prince. However, progress remains uneven as gangs continue to adapt amid the country's prolonged security crisis.

stories.title: Three years of messages at once - a chronicle of Sudan's war pours in as trapped reporter's phone turns on
stories.summary: As Sudan's civil war enters its fourth year, journalist Mohamed Suleiman received three years of accumulated messages when his phone was turned on, documenting the scale of devastation and loss in the country.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon hold rare talks in Washington, DC, amid Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese officials held their first direct talks in Washington, DC, occurring against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran war. US officials indicated that more time is needed to advance the discussions.

stories.title: China terms U.S. blockade of Strait of Hormuz 'dangerous and irresponsible' move
stories.summary: China condemned the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz as a "dangerous and irresponsible" move. Beijing also denied providing military aid to Iran and warned of retaliatory measures if President Trump increases tariffs against China based on allegations of assisting Tehran.

stories.title: UK to call for end to Sudan bloodshed at Berlin talks on third anniversary of war
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper will urge Sudan's warring factions to cease hostilities at a major conference in Berlin on the third anniversary of the war. The UK plans to double its aid as 19 million people face acute hunger. Analysts doubt the summit will produce a breakthrough amid Saudi-UAE tensions.

stories.title: Higher-income households benefited most from Help to Buy, thinktank finds
stories.summary: An analysis by the UK's Institute for Fiscal Studies found that higher-income households benefited most from George Osborne's Help to Buy mortgage schemes, launched in 2013 by the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government. The IFS concluded the schemes had little effect on social mobility despite being aimed at improving home ownership access.

stories.title: Chiang Mai’s New Year revelry hit by smog and war-related price spikes
stories.summary: Persistent wildfires in northern Thailand have caused severe air pollution around Chiang Mai, forcing three provinces to declare emergencies. The smog has obscured views at landmarks like Doi Suthep temple and harmed tourism. Businesses are also affected by war-related price increases linked to the conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: The Take: Who is keeping the fight alive in Sudan’s war?
stories.summary: The report examines the ongoing civil war in Sudan, now in its third year, exploring the actors sustaining the conflict and the toll it has taken on the country.

stories.title: Trump turns on Italy’s Meloni, ‘shocked’ by criticism, lack of courage
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni reportedly criticized U.S. President Donald Trump over his decision to go to war with Iran and his public attacks on Pope Leo. Trump responded by expressing shock at Meloni's remarks, accusing her of lacking courage.

stories.title: Trump’s son, Eric, to join father on state visit to China
stories.summary: Eric Trump and his wife Lara will join President Donald Trump on a state visit to China. Critics noted that Trump had previously criticized then-Vice President Joe Biden when his son Hunter accompanied him on a trip to China.

stories.title: Paratroopers show how they destroy enemy in Sloviansk direction
stories.summary: Fighters from Ukraine's 81st Separate Slobozhanska Airmobile Brigade demonstrated operations against Russian forces in the Sloviansk sector, using unmanned drone systems to destroy enemy equipment and personnel despite logistical challenges.

stories.title: Red Cross makes first aid shipments into Iran since start of war
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross delivered its first shipment of medical supplies and other humanitarian aid into Iran on April 12, marking the organization's first aid delivery since the start of the war.

stories.title: Ceasefire not included: Lebanon begins historic 'exploratory' talks with Israel
stories.summary: The Trump administration hosted Lebanese and Israeli diplomats in Washington on Tuesday for the first direct talks between the two countries in over three decades. A ceasefire was not on the agenda, and Hezbollah had no representation at the meeting. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio presided over the discussions.

stories.title: Health of boy thrown from Tate Modern takes ‘sad step backwards’, family say
stories.summary: The family of a French boy thrown from the 10th-floor balcony of the Tate Modern gallery in London in August 2019 said his recovery has suffered a setback following surgery in January. The child was six years old when attacker Jonty Bravery carried out the assault.

stories.title: US must adjust to Iran’s use of commercial satellite photos, Space Command says
stories.summary: US Space Command has acknowledged that Iran is effectively using commercial satellite imagery despite CENTCOM's declaration of space superiority. Officials say the US military must adapt to Tehran's growing exploitation of commercially available space-based intelligence.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it launched drones at Israeli military in occupied Golan Heights
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it launched a squadron of drones targeting Israeli military positions in the occupied Golan Heights late Tuesday, striking an artillery site in Za-oura and a battalion headquarters in Odem. The attack coincided with US-mediated Israeli-Lebanese talks in Washington.

stories.title: Xi calls for closer ties with Spain in face of global 'chaos'
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for strengthened ties with Spain during talks at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, citing global instability. Xi urged both nations to deepen communication, build mutual trust, and cooperate to oppose what he described as the world's regression to "the law of the jungle."

stories.title: Around 250 people feared missing after boat capsizes in Andaman Sea: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that approximately 250 people, including children, are feared missing after a trawler carrying Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals capsized in the Andaman Sea. The vessel departed from Teknaf in southern Bangladesh bound for Malaysia and reportedly sank due to heavy winds, rough seas, and overcrowding.

stories.title: Russians attack industrial infrastructure facility in Zaporizhzhia region, causing fire
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an industrial infrastructure facility in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, causing a fire. Details on casualties were not immediately reported.

stories.title: Russian missile kills five in Ukraine's Dnipro, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike killed five civilians in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, according to Ukrainian officials. Infrastructure Minister Oleksiy Kuleba said the victims were driving on a road in their cars when they were struck.

stories.title: Ukraine asks Israel to detain Russian ship carrying stolen grain that docked in Haifa
stories.summary: Ukraine's foreign ministry asked Israel to detain a Russian ship carrying allegedly stolen Ukrainian grain that docked in Haifa, stating that illegal trade in stolen goods must not be permitted. Separately, Pakistan's finance chief said Islamabad would not abandon US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine asks UN Security Council to hold meeting over escalation of Russian attacks
stories.summary: On Tuesday, Ukraine formally requested that the UN Security Council convene a meeting in response to escalating Russian attacks and increasing civilian casualties across the country.

stories.title: Pope Leo issues warning on democracy after Trump criticism
stories.summary: Pope Leo issued a letter from the Vatican on April 14 warning that democracies risk sliding into "majoritarian tyranny." The statement came two days after U.S. President Donald Trump attacked the pontiff on social media.

stories.title: News live: ‘really dangerous time’ for global economy as Australians pay price for Middle East conflict, Chalmers says
stories.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers warned that the global economy faces a dangerous period following the IMF's forecast of slower growth, higher inflation, and elevated fuel prices potentially lasting through 2027. Chalmers said the IMF is sounding the alarm about severe recession scenarios linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Amid focus on Strait of Hormuz, experts sound warning on Yemen’s Houthis and Red Sea
stories.summary: Foreign policy experts warned that while attention is focused on the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen's Houthi forces pose an additional threat in the Red Sea. Iran and its proxies could leverage multiple maritime choke points during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: IMF chief: Rapid economic recovery possible if war ends soon
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said the global economy could recover rapidly if the Iran war ends within weeks but warned conditions would deteriorate if fighting continues through summer. The IMF, World Bank, and International Energy Agency plan biweekly calls to assess disruptions to global energy markets.

stories.title: Is the US trying to pressure China with Hormuz blockade?
stories.summary: Analysts say the US naval blockade of Iranian ports is not aimed at pressuring China to intervene with Iran but rather at demonstrating American maritime supremacy over the Strait of Hormuz. The US Navy has deployed at least 15 ships to enforce the blockade, which began Monday.

stories.title: Knesset finance panel approves nearly NIS 100M in additional funds for Haredi schools
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset finance committee approved nearly 100 million shekels in additional funding for ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) schools. Opposition party Yesh Atid criticized the move, accusing beneficiaries of prioritizing institutions that do not teach the core curriculum.

stories.title: Drone attack on Cherkasy: Injury toll rises to 14, one child  killed
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the central Ukrainian city of Cherkasy killed one child and injured at least 14 people. The casualty toll rose as rescue operations continued.

stories.title: FBI arrests California man shot by ICE on ‘assault’ charges
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Carlos Ivan Mendoza Hernandez, 36, in California on charges of assaulting a federal officer. Mendoza Hernandez was shot by ICE agents on April 7 in Patterson, California, sustaining more than six bullet wounds including one to the face. The Department of Homeland Security has been accused of making false and misleading statements about the incident.

stories.title: Iran may opt to abide by US blockade in hopes of a deal, experts say
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Iran may choose to comply with the US naval blockade in the short term, hoping to secure a diplomatic deal. Iranian oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz had reached up to 1.5 million barrels per day, but Brent crude prices have remained relatively contained amid cautious market optimism.

stories.title: Pope Leo issues warning on democracy after Trump criticism
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV issued a public letter warning about threats to democracy following criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump. The Pope cautioned that without proper foundations, democracy risks becoming "majoritarian tyranny" or a facade for domination by economic and technological elites.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon Hold Rare U.S.-Mediated Peace Talks on Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon participated in rare U.S.-mediated peace talks focused on Hezbollah and a potential cease-fire. However, observers noted that without direct involvement from Hezbollah, implementing any cease-fire agreement would be difficult.

stories.title: UCLA gynecologist pleads guilty to 13 sexual abuse charges and is sentenced to 11 years in prison
stories.summary: Former UCLA gynecologist James Heaps pleaded guilty to 13 felony sexual abuse charges involving multiple patients and was sentenced to 11 years in prison. Heaps had been convicted and sentenced in 2023, but an appeals court overturned the original verdict after finding he was denied a fair trial.

stories.title: Explosion occurs at Kazan Gunpowder Plant in Russia
stories.summary: A powerful explosion occurred at a state-owned gunpowder plant in the Kirovsky district of Kazan, Russia. Authorities reported casualties, though specific numbers were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Talks with Israel ‘productive’, says Lebanese ambassador
stories.summary: Lebanese Ambassador to the US Nada Hamadeh Moawad described Tuesday's US-mediated talks with Israel in Washington as productive. She called for a ceasefire, humanitarian relief, the return of over one million displaced people, and reaffirmed Lebanon's full sovereignty over its territory.

stories.title: How Pakistan outmanoeuvred India in Iran war diplomacy with China’s help
stories.summary: After more than 20 hours of negotiations in Islamabad, US Vice President J.D. Vance confirmed that Washington and Tehran failed to reach a deal, with Iran rejecting US terms on its nuclear programme. Pakistan's role as host highlighted its growing diplomatic influence, aided by Chinese support, in outmaneuvering India on Iran war diplomacy.

stories.title: Canada was once a dream destination for Indian students. Is that changing?
stories.summary: Indian students are increasingly reconsidering Canada as a study destination due to tighter immigration rules, rising costs, and heightened visa risks.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills five in Gaza City
stories.summary: Five civilians were killed and several others injured in an Israeli air strike on the al-Shati camp in Gaza City on Tuesday, according to the Wafa news agency. Earlier the same day, four Palestinians, including a toddler, were killed in Israeli shelling targeting a police vehicle in Gaza City.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Cherkasy, killing 8-year-old boy, injuring 12 people
stories.summary: Russian strike drones attacked Cherkasy region in the evening, killing an eight-year-old boy in the regional center and injuring 12 others. The attack targeted the city of Cherkasy.

stories.title: Woman among four more Iranians sentenced to death over protests: NGOs
stories.summary: Four more Iranians, including one woman, have been sentenced to death in connection with anti-government protests, according to NGOs. The accused were charged with throwing concrete blocks at security forces from a residential building.

stories.title: Trump says Italian PM Meloni lacks ‘courage’ on Iran war: report
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump publicly criticized Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni for refusing to join the U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, telling Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera he was "shocked" by her lack of courage. The remarks came a day after Meloni condemned Trump's criticism of Pope Leo XIV over the pontiff's calls for peace in the Middle East.

stories.title: The Israeli town on the frontline with Hezbollah
