stories.summary: BBC correspondent Nick Beake reported from Metula, an Israeli town on the Lebanese border surrounded on three sides by Lebanon, highlighting its position on the frontline with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Sudan to mark third anniversary of civil war
stories.summary: Sudan is approaching the third anniversary of its civil war, a conflict that has killed tens of thousands and displaced approximately 12 million people. Separately, Pope Leo XIV is continuing his tour of Africa, visiting Algeria's St. Augustine Basilica before heading to Cameroon.

stories.title: Synagogue targeted in first such arson attack in modern N. Macedonian history
stories.summary: Two men were captured on alleged surveillance footage climbing a fence and dousing a synagogue with an accelerant in North Macedonia. Police recovered a fuel canister at the scene and documented fire damage. It is described as the first arson attack on a synagogue in modern North Macedonian history.

stories.title: Canada faces calls to rescind planned cuts to refugee healthcare scheme
stories.summary: Health workers and rights advocates in Canada are urging the government to reverse planned co-payments for refugee healthcare, set to take effect on May 1, arguing the changes would amount to a de facto denial of care for refugees.

stories.title: Two arms brokers on trial in UK for missiles and fighter jet deals with Libya and Sudan
stories.summary: Two arms brokers went on trial in London on April 14, accused of arranging illegal deals to supply ex-Soviet surface-to-air missile systems to South Sudan and fighter jets to Libya during its civil war, according to British prosecutors.

stories.title: 'War is development in reverse' UNDP chief tells France 24
stories.summary: The UNDP warned that the war in Iran could push more than 32 million people worldwide into poverty through energy disruption, food price increases, and weaker economic growth, even if hostilities ended immediately. The IMF also downgraded its global economic outlook under multiple conflict-duration scenarios.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran talks could resume over the next two days, ‘we’re more inclined’ to go to Pakistan
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that US-Iran talks could resume within two days and indicated a preference for holding them in Pakistan. Trump praised Pakistan's leadership, suggesting Islamabad as the likely venue for continued negotiations.

stories.title: Despite Israeli firepower, Netanyahu struggles for political gains in Iran war
stories.summary: More than six weeks into the war with Iran, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has struggled to convert military operations into political gains. The conflict was intended to deliver a defining victory over Tehran but has yet to yield the expected results.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills six in Gaza, including two children, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli fire killed six people in Gaza, including two children, according to medics. No further details on the specific location or circumstances of the strikes were provided.

stories.title: Drone attacks in Sudan kill two, injure 56, MSF says
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières reported on April 14 that five drone attacks carried out by the Sudanese Armed Forces in the Darfur region killed two people and wounded 56 others.

stories.title: US says it won’t renew temporary ease on Iran oil sanctions that expires Sunday
stories.summary: The United States announced it will not renew a temporary easing of oil sanctions on Iran that is set to expire Sunday. The decision aims to maintain maximum pressure on Tehran following a brief relaxation intended to stabilize energy prices amid the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: On Iran, China Softens Its Approach
stories.summary: China has adopted a notably restrained posture during the Strait of Hormuz crisis involving Iran and the United States. Analysts say Beijing's relative silence reflects a domestic policy shift in its approach to the conflict.

stories.title: Europe excludes US from plan to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: European countries are drafting a plan for a broad international coalition, excluding the US, Israel, and Iran, to reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war ends. French President Macron said the mission would exclude "belligerent" countries and could include mine-clearing operations.

stories.title: Fujimori heads toward Peru runoff as vote count enters third day
stories.summary: Conservative candidate Keiko Fujimori is set to advance to a presidential runoff in Peru as the vote count entered its third day on April 14. A former Lima mayor and a center-left candidate are in a tight contest for second place.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon hold first direct talks since 1993
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon have agreed to launch direct negotiations for the first time since 1993. A U.S. statement confirmed both sides committed to talks at a time and place still to be determined.

stories.title: Turkey’s war of words, and its boundaries - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines Turkey's escalating rhetoric against Israel, noting the gap between President Erdogan's strong verbal condemnations and the prospect of actual military action such as an invasion.

stories.title: Norway to lift ban on wealth fund investments in Syrian bonds, document shows
stories.summary: Norway's $2.2 trillion Government Pension Fund Global plans to lift its ban on investing in Syrian bonds, according to a document. The decision marks a significant step in Syria's reintegration into global financial markets.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1511: Merz and Zelenskyy seal landmark defense deal as Germany pledges hundreds of Patriot missiles
stories.summary: On day 1,511 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a landmark defense deal in which Germany pledged hundreds of Patriot missiles to bolster Ukraine's air defenses.

stories.title: Israeli attack kills several people in Gaza refugee camp
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit the Shati refugee camp in Gaza, killing several people. Video footage showed victims being rushed to a nearby medical facility.

stories.title: Harvey Weinstein rape retrial begins in New York
stories.summary: The retrial of Harvey Weinstein on a third-degree rape charge began Tuesday in New York, after a mistrial was declared last June when the jury foreman refused to return to deliberations. Weinstein is accused of raping actress Jessica Mann and will remain imprisoned for other convictions regardless of this verdict.

stories.title: Tunisia broadens access to annual Jewish pilgrimage to Africa’s oldest synagogue
stories.summary: Tunisia is broadening access to the annual Jewish pilgrimage to the Ghriba synagogue on the island of Djerba, Africa's oldest synagogue. Organizers announced a gradual return to normal after the event was scaled down following a deadly 2023 terrorist attack at the site.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to direct negotiations, says US
stories.summary: The US State Department announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to launch direct negotiations following a trilateral meeting in Washington. Lebanon called for a ceasefire and humanitarian measures, while Israel expressed commitment to resolving issues through dialogue.

stories.title: Missiles, drones, weapons production, and aid: 10 agreements signed by Ukraine and Germany
stories.summary: During President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's visit to Germany, Ukraine and Germany signed 10 agreements covering missiles, drones, weapons production, and aid. The Ukrainian Defense Ministry signed contracts with Raytheon for PAC-2 missiles and with Diehl Defence for IRIS-T systems.

stories.title: Aid groups use land routes to deliver humanitarian relief to Iran
stories.summary: International humanitarian organizations announced on April 14 that they had begun delivering emergency relief to Iran via overland routes. These are among the first aid deliveries since U.S.-Israeli strikes began in late February.

stories.title: Hundreds missing after Rohingya refugee boat capsizes in Andaman Sea: UN
stories.summary: A boat carrying Rohingya refugees capsized in the Andaman Sea, leaving approximately 250 people, including children, feared missing, according to the United Nations and the International Organization for Migration.

stories.title: Hormuz mission talks to focus on sanctions, work with industry: Source
stories.summary: Britain and France are leading discussions on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including possible financial sanctions on Iran if it continues to block the waterway. The talks, reported from Paris on April 14, will also address working with industry to resume shipping.

stories.title: Zelenskyy flew to Oslo to lay groundwork for joint project. Drone Deal is next step
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Oslo to lay the groundwork for a joint defense project with Norway. The visit resulted in the signing of a joint declaration, with a drone procurement deal expected as the next step.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister suspended a defence cooperation agreement with Israel, citing the current geopolitical situation. The pact, which is renewed every five years, will remain on hold indefinitely.

stories.title: US appeals court blocks contempt case over Trump deportation flights
stories.summary: A US appeals court blocked a contempt case against the Trump administration related to its decision to proceed with two deportation flights in 2025, halting a probe into potential contempt of court.

stories.title: 100 bereaved families ask coalition MKs to skip cemetery speeches on upcoming Memorial Day
stories.summary: Approximately 100 bereaved Israeli families have asked coalition members of the Knesset to refrain from delivering speeches at cemeteries on the upcoming Memorial Day, urging lawmakers not to turn grave sites into political platforms.

stories.title: How US blockade on Iran will worsen energy crisis
stories.summary: The US military blockade of Iranian ports has taken effect, disrupting global energy markets. Analysts warn the blockade will deepen energy supply concerns worldwide as Iranian oil exports are cut off.

stories.title: Russian missile kills five civilians in Ukraine’s Dnipro, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed five civilians, officials said. More than two dozen others were injured, with at least 10 hospitalized in severe condition.

stories.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1pc on Mideast war, warns world economy could be ‘thrown off course’
stories.summary: The IMF cut its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, down from 3.3% projected in January, citing the impact of the Middle East war on commodity markets and prices. The revision was announced in the IMF's World Economic Outlook during its spring meetings in Washington.

stories.title: US could return to Islamabad for additional negotiations with Iran in next two days, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump told the New York Post the US is "more inclined" to return to Islamabad for additional negotiations with Iran within the next two days, following the breakdown of earlier talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: LPG shortage from Iran war fuels labour exodus from major Indian cities
stories.summary: An LPG shortage linked to the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz blockade is causing hardship in Indian cities, including New Delhi, where families struggle to access cooking fuel. The crisis is driving a labour exodus from major urban centres.

stories.title: From Lithuania to Jerusalem, a Holocaust survivor shares his story with diplomats
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Clevs shared his wartime experiences from Lithuania with diplomats at an event in Jerusalem organized by Zikaron Basalon and the Anti-Defamation League. Clevs recounted memories from when he was eight years old during the Holocaust.

stories.title: Pope Leo's visit revives priest's hopes for peace in anglophone Cameroon
stories.summary: Pope Leo's visit to Cameroon has revived hopes for peace in the country's anglophone regions. A Catholic priest, Rev. Killian Ndonui Nshamikara, was kidnapped by armed rebels in western Cameroon in January and held for ransom exceeding $25,000.

stories.title: SECP grants Buy Now Pay Later licence to Alibaba-owned Koko Tech Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistan's Securities and Exchange Commission has granted a Buy Now Pay Later licence to Alibaba-owned Koko Tech Pakistan. The SECP described the entry of the Alibaba-backed firm as a significant milestone for Pakistan's digital financial ecosystem.

stories.title: YouTube bans viral pro-Iran AI-generated LEGO videos trolling Trump
stories.summary: YouTube removed viral AI-generated LEGO-style videos produced by an Iran-linked group called Explosive Media that ridiculed the US war effort in Iran and mocked President Trump. The videos, which attracted hundreds of millions of views, are part of an ongoing online propaganda exchange between US and Iranian-aligned actors.

stories.title: Top Russian and Chinese envoys meet in Beijing to discuss Iran, Ukraine and Taiwan
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met in Beijing on Tuesday to discuss the Iran war, Ukraine, and Taiwan. A Chinese readout noted growing global turmoil, in an implicit criticism of Washington, as Beijing stepped up its Iran war diplomacy.

stories.title: LPG shortage from Iran war fuels labour exodus from major Indian cities
stories.summary: An LPG shortage linked to the Iran war is reportedly driving migrant workers out of major Indian cities. Long queues at railway stations indicate a reverse migration of labor, though the Indian government denies the trend.

stories.title: Germany and Ukraine establish two joint ventures for interceptor drones and unmanned ground systems
stories.summary: During Ukrainian-German government consultations in Berlin on April 14, German company Quantum Systems announced two new joint ventures under the "Build with Ukraine" initiative. The ventures will focus on interceptor drones and unmanned ground systems.

stories.title: Estonia watched Ukraine for four years. Now it’s spending €500 million on lessons
stories.summary: Estonia announced plans to invest €500 million in defense improvements based on lessons learned from observing four years of warfare in Ukraine. The spending is aimed at preparing the Baltic nation for future security challenges.

stories.title: Israeli-Lebanese negotiations 'largely symbolic and performative', Middle East expert says
stories.summary: Aaron David Miller of the Carnegie Endowment for Peace told FRANCE 24 that the Israeli-Lebanese talks in Washington are "largely symbolic and performative." He noted that none of the participants have authority to negotiate and that implementing the desired outcomes is not feasible.

stories.title: Italy suspends defense agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italy announced the suspension of its defense cooperation agreement with Israel. The decision represents a significant shift for Rome, which has long maintained close ties with Israel and has been regarded by the Trump administration as a key European partner.

stories.title: Pope Leo, after Trump's attack, honours saint in Algeria who decried wars
stories.summary: Pope Leo traveled to Annaba, Algeria, on April 14 to pay homage to St. Augustine of Hippo, the ancient theologian born there who inspired the pontiff to become a priest. The visit followed a social media attack on the pope by U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: Twin suicide attacks rock Algeria during Pope’s visit, source says
stories.summary: Twin suicide attacks struck Algeria during Pope Leo's visit. Authorities have not yet established any link between the attacks and the papal trip.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italy suspended its defence cooperation agreement with Israel. A diplomatic source said maintaining the deal had become "politically difficult" amid ongoing Middle East conflicts.

stories.title: US Centcom says no ships passed through first day of US Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: US Central Command stated that no ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz during the first 24 hours of the US blockade, with over 10,000 service members and more than a dozen warships enforcing the operation. The blockade began after ceasefire talks with Iran collapsed.

stories.title: US, Iran may resume talks this week despite port blockade
stories.summary: A proposal has been shared with Washington and Tehran to send their delegations back for peace talks, with a possible resumption of US-Iran negotiations as early as this week despite the ongoing port blockade.

stories.title: White House wants Pentagon to demo nuclear space power by 2031
stories.summary: The Trump administration released its National Initiative for American Space Nuclear Power, calling on the Pentagon and NASA to demonstrate nuclear power capabilities in space by 2031. The plan includes parallel design competitions intended to advance both military and civilian space-based nuclear energy systems.

stories.title: FIFA faces pressure to call on Trump to stop ICE raids at 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: The Athletic reported that FIFA president Gianni Infantino is receptive to a proposal asking US President Trump to impose a moratorium on ICE immigration raids at venues during the 2026 World Cup, which the US is co-hosting.

stories.title: Why are global views of the US getting worse?
stories.summary: The report discusses the declining global perception of the United States, linking it to the launch of a war against Iran and years of worsening international views of the nation.

stories.title: Norwegian Kongsberg’s answer to mass Russia’s Shahed attacks: mast, camera, and 70 mm rocket
stories.summary: Norwegian defense company Kongsberg has developed an anti-drone system using a mast-mounted camera and 70 mm rockets designed to counter mass drone attacks like Russia's Shahed strikes. The system has been mounted on a Ukrainian armored vehicle for deployment.

stories.title: PM takes president into confidence on US-Iran talks, briefs him on upcoming visits to Saudi Arabia, Turkiye
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif briefed President Asif Ali Zardari on all aspects of the US-Iran dialogue hosted in Islamabad and on upcoming visits to Saudi Arabia and Turkey. Pakistan hosted direct US-Iran talks over the weekend, the highest-level engagement between the two nations since 1979.

stories.title: Six ships turned around as part of Strait of Hormuz blockade, US military says
stories.summary: US Central Command reported that six merchant vessels complied with US Navy instructions to turn around and re-enter an Iranian port on the Gulf of Oman as part of the Strait of Hormuz blockade. CENTCOM said no ships made it past the blockade.

stories.title: Lebanese and Israeli envoys to meet as Israel presses war on Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese envoys are scheduled to meet in Washington on Tuesday as Israel continues its military campaign against Hezbollah. The diplomatic meeting is overshadowed by conflicting agendas, with Israel ruling out a ceasefire and demanding that Beirut disarm the Iran-backed group.

stories.title: Day of mourning declared in Dnipro for victims of rocket attack
stories.summary: The city of Dnipro declared April 15 a day of mourning following a deadly morning rocket attack by Russian forces. The strike killed multiple residents of the central Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Israeli ambassador to US: Israel, Lebanon united in liberating Lebanon from Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, said after meeting Lebanese ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad in Washington that Lebanon no longer wants to be "occupied" by Hezbollah. The two sides also discussed border demarcation and long-term security cooperation.

stories.title: Florida surgeon indicted after removing liver instead of spleen
stories.summary: A Florida surgeon, Thomas Shaknovsky, 44, was indicted by a grand jury in Tallahassee on a manslaughter charge after removing a patient's liver instead of his spleen during an August 2024 operation. The patient, 70-year-old William Bryan of Alabama, died on the operating table.

stories.title: Pakistan PM headed to Riyadh and Ankara amid prospect of new US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is traveling to Riyadh and Ankara as diplomatic efforts continue around the US-Iran conflict. President Trump indicated that ceasefire talks could resume in Pakistan within two days.

stories.title: Australia gets new military leaders, including first female army chief
stories.summary: Australia announced new senior military leadership appointments, including Lieutenant General Susan Coyle as the country's first female army chief. Coyle is scheduled to assume her new role in July.

stories.title: The algorithm of speed: How Matan Ivri is rewriting the Israeli record books
stories.summary: Israeli runner Matan Ivri broke the national 1,500-meter record at a competition held at Stanford University, finishing in 3:38.15 minutes. Ivri won his heat in a highly competitive field.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Gaza police car kills child
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike struck a police vehicle in Gaza City, killing at least four people, including a three-year-old child.

stories.title: Widows of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine are using AI to ‘resurrect’ their husbands
stories.summary: Widows of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine are increasingly using AI tools to digitally animate photographs and videos of their deceased husbands, according to BBC News Russian. Using old photos, wedding footage, and selfies, generative AI creates short clips in which the dead appear to move, smile, and speak.

stories.title: IMF cuts global growth forecast during Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: The IMF cut its global growth forecast and raised its inflation projection to 4.4 percent, up 0.6 percentage points, citing surging oil, gas, and fertiliser costs linked to the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Morocco: Court upholds sentences for Senegalese AFCON attendees
stories.summary: A Moroccan court upheld prison sentences for 18 Senegalese football fans charged with a pitch invasion during the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. The ruling was made on appeal.

stories.title: Israeli, Lebanese envoys hold historic summit in Washington to discuss peace deal
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors held a two-hour meeting in Washington, mediated by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, to discuss a framework for a peace deal. Hezbollah launched attacks on Israel as the talks began.

stories.title: Cuba's top destinations deserted, without power or fuel under US sanctions
stories.summary: Cuba's top tourism destinations, including areas near the Zapata Swamp, are largely deserted and suffering from power and fuel shortages under US sanctions. The eco-tourism sites that once attracted hundreds of thousands of visitors annually are now largely inactive.

stories.title: Czech coorporation is maintaining Russia’s tank and artillery lines — investigation
stories.summary: An investigation has revealed that a Czech industrial group continued maintaining Russian tank and artillery supply lines despite publicly announcing its departure from Russia after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence cooperation deal with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced on Tuesday that Italy will suspend the automatic renewal of its defence cooperation agreement with Israel. Meloni cited the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East as the reason for the decision.

stories.title: House Democrats call for commission led by JD Vance to oust Trump
stories.summary: House Democrats, led by Representative Jamie Raskin, proposed creating a commission to work with Vice President JD Vance to remove President Trump from office under the 25th Amendment. The measure followed Trump's statements about annihilating Iran and a social media post depicting himself as Jesus.

stories.title: How war in Gulf reveals the ‘cut corners’ on British defence
stories.summary: Experts and commentators highlighted how the Iran war has exposed significant shortcomings in British defence capabilities. With army personnel halved since the Cold War, the UK's ambitions for global military deployment do not match its actual readiness, as illustrated by delays in deploying HMS Dragon to Cyprus.

stories.title: Zelensky Says Kyiv Seized a Russian Position With Drones and Robots. Is This a Game Changer?
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy announced that Kyiv's forces captured a Russian position using drones and ground robots. Military experts said the operation illustrates how unmanned systems are already transforming tactics and strategy in the war.

stories.title: Hungary Turns a New Page
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán conceded defeat in the April 12 parliamentary election after his Fidesz party lost its majority, ending his 16-year rule. The center-right Tisza party, led by Péter Magyar, won a projected two-thirds supermajority on promises to tackle corruption and align Hungary more closely with Europe.

stories.title: Naqvi calls on businessmen to bring back ‘20-30pc’ of wealth to Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi urged the business community at a Federation House ceremony in Karachi to repatriate 20-30% of their wealth held abroad ahead of the upcoming budget. He said the government would facilitate investment and that the process could be completed online.

stories.title: Fed nominee Warsh’s financial disclosures point to assets well over $100m
stories.summary: Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh's financial disclosures reveal assets well over $100 million, which are expected to be a central focus of his upcoming Senate confirmation hearing next week.

stories.title: Shelling in Kherson region kills one, wounds 11 over day
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Kherson region, Russian shelling over the course of a day killed one person and wounded 11 others. Law enforcement authorities have opened pre-trial investigations into the attacks.

stories.title: Israeli ambassador: Lebanon wants to be liberated from Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, stated that Lebanon expressed a shared desire to be liberated from Hezbollah's influence during talks in Washington.

stories.title: Lebanon: Debate over fake 'plot' to overthrow government
stories.summary: Debate has erupted in Lebanon over unverified claims that Israel's bombing of Beirut thwarted a coup plot against the Lebanese government. The controversy highlights deep domestic divisions as Israel-Lebanon negotiations get under way.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon united in liberating Lebanon from Hezbollah, Israeli ambassador to US says
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the U.S., Yechiel Leiter, said the Lebanese government expressed during U.S.-brokered talks that it no longer wants to be "occupied" by Hezbollah. He reported discussions about a long-term vision including clearly delineated borders between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Aid groups bidding to boost relief shipments into Iran
stories.summary: International aid organizations are working to increase humanitarian relief shipments into Iran, but efforts have been complicated by closures of air and sea routes due to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Hundreds of asylum seekers moved from hotels to army barracks, Home Office announces
stories.summary: The UK Home Office announced it has closed eleven asylum seeker hotels across England, Scotland, and Northern Ireland and moved approximately 350 claimants to Crowborough military camp in East Sussex. The Refugee Council criticized the decision, calling military sites unsuitable and more expensive than hotels.

stories.title: Nearly 700 reported killed in Sudan drone strikes this year: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that nearly 700 civilians were killed in drone strikes in Sudan during the first three months of 2025. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher released the figures one day before the third anniversary of the war's start.

stories.title: Florida Jewish community says kaddish for children killed in Holocaust
stories.summary: A Conservative synagogue in Florida held a program called "Remember a Child" to recite kaddish for children killed in the Holocaust. At least a third of the approximately 150-family congregation participated in the memorial observance.

stories.title: Lebanon-Israel talks conclude in Washington
stories.summary: The first round of direct talks between Lebanon and Israel concluded in Washington, according to Lebanese state news. The discussions took place amid reports of continued Israeli military operations inside Lebanon.

stories.title: War didn’t stop Ukraine from building economic footprint in West Africa
stories.summary: Despite the ongoing war, Ukraine has expanded its economic presence in West Africa, including exporting flour to Ghana. The trade activity demonstrates Kyiv's efforts to maintain commercial relationships during wartime.

stories.title: Italian PM says suspends renewal of defence agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced the suspension of Italy's defence agreement with Israel, which covers military equipment exchange and technology research. The move came the same day President Trump criticized Meloni in Corriere della Sera for refusing to support the U.S.-led campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Trump Always Skips the Hard Part
stories.summary: An analysis argues that U.S. President Trump's approach to dealmaking on foreign policy lacks follow-through on difficult implementation details, potentially increasing the risk of further conflict.

stories.title: Over-sold and under-delivered: Israel’s Netanyahu faces ceasefire backlash
stories.summary: Polls indicate growing Israeli public frustration with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over a military campaign against Iran that many feel did not achieve a decisive victory, prompting backlash over ceasefire terms.

stories.title: Israeli troops fully surround Bint Jbeil in Lebanon offensive
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced its troops have fully surrounded the town of Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon, marking a significant advance in the ground offensive. Three Hezbollah fighters were captured, and Israel reported striking areas in Adshit al-Qusayr.

stories.title: State Duma Passes VAT Exemption for Food Industry to Ease Wartime Tax Burden
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma has passed legislation granting a VAT exemption for the food industry. If signed into law, the measure would partially reverse a January tax reform that raised the standard VAT rate from 20% to 22% and lowered the income threshold for small businesses required to pay it.

stories.title: Germany will pay for “hundreds” of Patriot missiles for Ukraine as strategic partnership signed
stories.summary: Germany signed a strategic partnership with Ukraine that includes funding for hundreds of Patriot missiles. Berlin will also provide IRIS-T air-defense launchers, invest in deep-strike capabilities, and jointly develop mid-range drones with Kyiv.

stories.title: About 250 missing after boat carrying Rohingya refugees capsizes in Andaman Sea
stories.summary: Approximately 250 people are missing after a trawler carrying Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals capsized in the Andaman Sea, according to the UN's refugee and migration agencies. The overcrowded vessel departed Teknaf in southern Bangladesh bound for Malaysia and sank due to harsh weather conditions.

stories.title: In parliament, Polish MP calls Israel ‘new Third Reich,’ waves Israeli flag with swastika
stories.summary: Polish far-right MP Konrad Berkowicz drew outrage in parliament by calling Israel the "new Third Reich" and displaying an Israeli flag altered with a swastika. Israel's embassy condemned the display as "antisemitic horror."

stories.title: German pro-Israel activist, granddaughter of Nazis, warns: 'Antisemitism is threat to democracy'
stories.summary: German activist Karoline Preisler, granddaughter of a Nazi soldier and a well-known counter-protester at pro-Palestinian rallies, warned in an interview with Walla that antisemitism poses a threat to democracy.

stories.title: Drones, Iran war escalating horror as Sudan war enters fourth year
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that hundreds of people have been killed by drone strikes in Sudan over the past three months as the war enters its fourth year. A medical charity also reported two additional deaths in the Darfur region.

stories.title: Iran war escalation could trigger global recession, IMF warns
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that further escalation of the Iran war could trigger a global recession, with the UK facing the sharpest impact among G7 nations. The IMF cut its 2026 growth forecasts based on the economic damage from the Middle East conflict so far.

stories.title: Antisemitic violence at record high for Jews outside Israel
stories.summary: A new report by Tel Aviv University, released as Israel marks Holocaust Remembrance Day, documents record-high levels of antisemitic violence against Jews living outside Israel. The study found surging cases of severe attacks against Jews in Western countries in 2025.

stories.title: Canada allocates Lebanon $40m in humanitarian aid
stories.summary: Canada announced $40 million in humanitarian aid for Lebanon through international organizations. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand reiterated support for Lebanon's sovereignty and condemned Israeli attacks during a call with her Lebanese counterpart.

stories.title: Kremlin says internet curbs are temporary, will be lifted once security threat passes
stories.summary: The Kremlin acknowledged that internet restrictions imposed in Russia have caused disruption to many citizens. Officials stated the curbs are temporary and will be lifted once the perceived security threat has passed.

stories.title: Nigeria police arrest 33-member gang over Kwara church abductions
stories.summary: Nigerian police arrested a 33-member gang in connection with church abductions that took place in Kwara state in November. The arrests were announced from the capital, Abuja.

stories.title: Orbán’s loss won’t stop Russian influence campaigns, but it shows they’re beatable
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán's electoral defeat in Hungary demonstrates that Russian influence campaigns, while growing in scope, can be overcome. Analysts say the result exposes both the reach and the limitations of Russian hybrid-warfare tactics in European democracies.

stories.title: Netanyahu, officials lay wreaths after siren marking Holocaust Remembrance Day
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other Israeli officials laid wreaths during a siren marking Holocaust Remembrance Day at a memorial ceremony in Israel.

stories.title: Video: UN chief Antonio Guterres says talks on Iran war likely to restart
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated it is "highly probable" that negotiations to end the US-Israel war on Iran will resume, while emphasizing the importance of ongoing diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Redefining mobile artillery for a faster, more lethal fight
stories.summary: A sponsored report highlights the battlefield role of mobile howitzer systems, emphasizing the importance of domestic manufacturing to ensure supply availability for artillery platforms.

stories.title: What will it take? Israel-Lebanon talks open as fighting continues
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese envoys appeared together publicly for what may be the first time, meeting under U.S. auspices in Washington. The Lebanese government has been increasingly vocal in calling on Hezbollah to disarm, while the U.S. has an interest in restraining Israel to advance broader negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: Europe Is Looking for Its Own Hormuz Fix
stories.summary: European nations are exploring military and diplomatic options to address the disruption caused by the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. While Europe possesses relevant military capabilities, there is limited political appetite for direct involvement in the conflict.

stories.title: Put nuclear reactors in space within a few years, White House tells Pentagon
stories.summary: The White House has directed the Pentagon to deploy nuclear reactors in space within the next few years. The initiative is part of broader Trump administration efforts to expand the use of nuclear power.

stories.title: Imran’s sisters manage to reach Adiala jail but still denied meeting with ex-premier
stories.summary: Sisters of incarcerated former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan reached Adiala jail but were denied a meeting with him. Aleema Khan told media that police typically prevent them from reaching the facility, while the jail administration tells courts the family did not arrive.

stories.title: Russian court sentences actor to 8 years in prison in absentia over ‘false information’ about military
stories.summary: A Moscow court sentenced Russian actor Artur Smolyaniov in absentia to eight years in prison for spreading what authorities called "false information" about the Russian military, as reported by Mediazona.

stories.title: Israel attacks areas in southern Lebanon amid talks in Washington
stories.summary: Israel continued launching air strikes on multiple areas in southern Lebanon, including the town of Haneen and outskirts of Tyre, while direct talks between Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors were ongoing in Washington.

stories.title: The Price Israel Is Paying for Its Wars
stories.summary: An analysis examines the cumulative toll of Israel's multi-front military engagements on its armed forces, economy, and relationship with the United States.

stories.title: Kremlin says it is glad Hungary's Magyar seems ready for 'pragmatic dialogue' with Russia
stories.summary: The Kremlin expressed satisfaction that Hungarian Prime Minister-elect Peter Magyar appears ready for pragmatic dialogue with Russia. Moscow said it would base its position on the specific steps taken by Magyar's incoming government.

stories.title: Swastika shown in Polish parliament during March of the Living
stories.summary: During the March of the Living on Tuesday, a Polish member of parliament displayed a swastika in the Polish parliament and described Israel as a "New Third Reich."

stories.title: Ukraine and several third countries join renewed EU sanctions against Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine and several third countries have formally joined the latest round of European Union sanctions targeting Russian entities imposed last month.

stories.title: Further Iran-US peace talks 'highly probable', says UN secretary general
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said it is "highly probable" that US-Iran ceasefire negotiations will resume. He also described the direct Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington as important for creating conditions for change.

stories.title: US-Iran peace talks could resume in next two days, Trump says
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran peace talks could resume in Islamabad within two days, President Trump said Tuesday, praising Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir as a "fantastic" mediator. The statement followed an initial round of ceasefire talks held in the Pakistani capital over the preceding weekend.

stories.title: Moscow court declares Microsoft’s Russian subsidiary bankrupt
stories.summary: A Moscow arbitration court declared Microsoft's Russian subsidiary bankrupt on April 14 and initiated liquidation proceedings, according to court documents.

stories.title: Gulf states weigh UN complaint against Iraq over militia attacks
stories.summary: Several Gulf states are considering filing a complaint with the UN Security Council against Iraq over attacks carried out by Iran-backed militias during the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Keep Humans in the Loop
stories.summary: A policy discussion argues that while artificial intelligence has a role in military targeting decisions, proper human oversight and safeguards are essential to its responsible use.

stories.title: China now the ‘good guy’ on AI as Trump takes ‘wild west’ approach, MPs told
stories.summary: A former UN adviser told a House of Commons committee that China is now more supportive of global AI governance efforts than the United States. Prof Dame Wendy Hall said the Trump administration's deregulatory approach has created a "wild west" environment driven by profit-hungry companies.

stories.title: Beyond the headlines: Implications of a Matzah shortage - opinion
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post opinion column discusses the broader societal implications of a matzah shortage in Israel, offering a perspective on everyday life beyond headline news.

stories.title: Who is Uganda's army chief and what did he say about Turkey?
stories.summary: Uganda's military chief drew sharp criticism from Turkey after making statements demanding a Turkish bride and threatening to sever diplomatic ties with Ankara.

stories.title: No ships ‘make it past US blockade’ in Hormuz strait in first day: Pentagon
stories.summary: US Central Command said no ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz during the first 24 hours of the US blockade, contradicting earlier reports of vessels breaking through. President Trump suggested US-Iran talks could resume within two days.

stories.title: School shooting in Turkey leaves 16 wounded, governor says
stories.summary: A teenager opened fire at a high school in Sanliurfa province in southeastern Turkey on Tuesday, wounding at least 16 people including students and teachers. Governor Hasan Sildak confirmed the attacker killed himself after the shooting.

stories.title: Video shows drone exploding in northern Israel
stories.summary: Video footage captured a drone exploding in Nahariya, a city in northern Israel located approximately 10 kilometres from the Lebanese border.

stories.title: Trump’s son Eric to join father’s state visit to China
stories.summary: Eric Trump and his wife Lara will accompany U.S. President Donald Trump on his state visit to China scheduled for May 14–15. A spokeswoman for the Trump family organization said Eric, who manages his father's business empire, would attend in a personal capacity, potentially contributing to U.S.-China business relations.

stories.title: Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt to hold talks on Iran conflict
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey are meeting in Turkey this week to discuss tensions related to the Iran conflict. This is the third such meeting among the four nations on regional affairs.

stories.title: Auckland council backs sanctions probe over Israel war crimes
stories.summary: Auckland Council in New Zealand voted on Tuesday to explore sanctioning companies linked to Israel's illegal occupation of Palestinian territory, citing concerns over war crimes.

stories.title: Ukraine may receive first tranche of €90 billion EU loan by end of Q2 2026 – European Commission
stories.summary: The European Commission indicated that key elements of a €90 billion credit support package for Ukraine have been prepared, with the first tranche potentially disbursed by the end of the second quarter of 2026.

stories.title: New accuser says Eric Swalwell sexually assaulted her in 2018
stories.summary: A woman named Lonna Drewes publicly accused California Democratic Congressman Eric Swalwell of drugging and sexually assaulting her at a Beverly Hills hotel in 2018. Drewes, who was working as a model at the time, made the allegations at a press conference on Tuesday.

stories.title: Somalia reports hit on al-Shabab with ‘international support’
stories.summary: Somalia's military reported killing al-Shabab fighters with the support of an international partner that carried out air strikes against the armed group.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence cooperation deal with Israel
stories.summary: Italy suspended its defence cooperation agreement with Israel, ending military training collaboration between the two countries. A Defence Ministry source confirmed that one consequence is the cessation of joint military training programs.

stories.title: Novaya Gazeta Editor Charged in Privacy Investigation
stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta editor Oleg Roldugin was arrested following a police raid on the newspaper's Moscow office. He faces charges in a privacy-related investigation.

stories.title: Brazil demands rare earths be processed at home as US and China compete
stories.summary: Brazil announced it will require foreign partners to process rare earth minerals domestically as a condition for accessing its reserves. Senior industry ministry official Leonardo Durans said the policy reflects a matured negotiating position, a move that could reshape competition between Chinese and Western firms for Brazil's resources.

stories.title: Violent assault on Jewish student in Berlin not antisemitic in motive, appeals court rules
stories.summary: A Berlin appeals court ruled that a violent assault on a Jewish student was not antisemitic in motive. The court also reduced the attacker's prison sentence to two years and six months.

stories.title: Sudan: 3 babies born into war every minute amid dire conditions
stories.summary: The UN reported that three babies are born every minute in conflict-hit Sudan, where newborns face severe risks due to under-equipped healthcare facilities, food shortages, and frequent displacement.

stories.title: UN raises alarm about Iran war causing fertiliser shortages for developing countries
stories.summary: The head of the UN's International Trade Centre warned that the Strait of Hormuz blockade is causing fertiliser shortages that threaten food security in developing countries, even as oil and gas can potentially be sourced elsewhere.

stories.title: Nearly 700 civilians reported killed in drone strikes since January amid Sudan’s civil war: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that nearly 700 civilians have been killed in drone strikes across Sudan since January as the country's civil war continues. Near-daily drone attacks have severely disrupted life throughout the country.

stories.title: Almost half of Sudan's lifesaving kitchens have closed in last six months
stories.summary: Nearly half of Sudan's lifesaving community kitchens have closed over the past six months as the humanitarian crisis deepens three years into the war. International governments are meeting in Berlin to address the worsening situation.

stories.title: Trump says Iran talks may renew; Mossad chief: Our mission isn’t over until regime falls
stories.summary: President Trump gave contradictory accounts about the pace of US-Iran negotiations while suggesting talks may resume. Separately, Mossad chief David Barnea stated that Israel's mission would continue until the Iranian regime falls.

stories.title: Russian attack on Dnipro: 12 seriously injured
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Tuesday afternoon left 22 people hospitalized, with 12 in serious condition, according to regional authorities.

stories.title: Reeves arrives at IMF with little leeway to prove its UK downgrade wrong
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves arrived at the IMF facing forecasts that the Iran war's impact will make Britain the worst-affected G7 economy. The IMF downgraded UK growth projections by 0.5 percentage points for the current year, the sharpest cut among G7 nations.

stories.title: Sudan War: UN officials sound alarm on humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: As Sudan's civil conflict nears its three-year mark, UN officials are warning of a dire humanitarian crisis. The alarm comes as global attention remains largely focused on the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Airlines urge EU to step in as Iran war chokes jet fuel supply
stories.summary: An industry group warned that Europe could face a systemic jet fuel shortage within three weeks as the Iran war disrupts supply chains. Airlines are urging the European Union to intervene to address the crisis.

stories.title: Iran war wreaks havoc on global economy and could spark recession, says IMF
stories.summary: The IMF warned that the war on Iran has "abruptly darkened" the global economic outlook and could trigger a worldwide recession if prolonged. The fund downgraded most growth forecasts, projecting 3.1 percent global growth this year, down from 3.4 percent.

stories.title: Russia slows internet crackdown as voter anger hits Putin rating
stories.summary: Russia has eased its internet crackdown as public dissatisfaction grows, with trust in President Vladimir Putin reaching its lowest level since the start of the Ukraine war in early March.

stories.title: Idling Shadow Fleet Tankers Threaten Baltic Security and Environment, Experts Warn
stories.summary: Dozens of shadow fleet tankers are idling in the Baltic Sea after being unable to load cargo from Ukrainian-damaged Russian oil terminals. Experts warn the stationary vessels pose risks to undersea cables and the marine environment.

stories.title: Meta 'financially enabling' Israeli settler violence against Palestinians, report says
stories.summary: A report by 7amleh, the Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media, alleges that Meta is financially enabling incitement against Palestinians by allowing settler-affiliated Israeli accounts to generate revenue despite content that violates the platform's own policies.

stories.title: Rising antisemitism signals risk of second Holocaust, WJC Israel President warns at Auschwitz
stories.summary: World Jewish Congress Israel President Sylvan Adams warned at Auschwitz that rising antisemitism risks a second Holocaust. Adams said he had previously believed antisemitism had been pushed to the margins of modern life.

stories.title: It is time for a ceasefire in Sudan and a new way forward
stories.summary: An opinion piece calls for a ceasefire in Sudan, arguing that the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces cannot determine the country's future alone and that all political actors and citizens must be included.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli forces near border
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed on Tuesday that it fired rockets at Israeli soldiers and vehicles south of Khaim and targeted Israeli military infrastructure in Karmiel. The group also said it shelled Israeli forces in Qouzah and targeted a military drone over Tyre.

stories.title: French minister seeks to ban Kanye West concert in Marseille over anti-Semitic remarks
stories.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez is seeking to ban a planned June concert by Kanye West in Marseille due to the rapper's anti-Semitic remarks. The potential cancellation reflects French authorities' response to West's controversial public statements.

stories.title: Foreign secretary Misri reaches Berlin for India-Germany Foreign Office consultations
stories.summary: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri arrived in Berlin for India-Germany Foreign Office consultations. Discussions are expected to cover trade, investment, defence, security, technology, green energy, and regional matters of mutual interest.

stories.title: Gaza's premature babies and the parents they never knew
stories.summary: Palestinian parents described the pain of separation after their premature babies were evacuated from Gaza to receive medical care abroad during the war, leaving families divided across borders.

stories.title: Trump accuses ally Meloni of lacking courage for not joining attacks on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump criticized Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni for not joining the U.S. attack on Iran, calling her lacking in courage. Italy simultaneously suspended its defence agreement with Israel amid growing domestic pressure over the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Why and how is US blockading Iranian ports in Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: The U.S. under President Donald Trump initiated a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz targeting Iranian ports. The move aims to restrict maritime traffic entering and leaving Iran, though its practical implications remain under scrutiny.

stories.title: Iran war wipes out global oil demand growth in 2026: IEA
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency reported that the Iran war has wiped out projected global oil demand growth for 2026. The IEA described the conflict's impact as the biggest oil supply disruption in history.

stories.title: Ukraine agrees new €4 billion cooperation package with Germany – DM Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukraine and Germany signed a €4 billion defense cooperation package covering air defense reinforcement, long-range strike capabilities, and joint drone production, announced by Ukrainian Defense Minister Fedorov.

stories.title: Russian missile strike on Dnipro kills 5, wounds 22
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike on the city of Dnipro killed five people and wounded 22, according to regional military administration head Oleksandr Ganzha.

stories.title: Former NATO chief targets PM Starmer, warning UK's security in 'peril'
stories.summary: Former NATO Secretary General George Robertson is set to publicly criticize UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, warning that Britain's national security is "in peril" due to political complacency and under-investment in defence.

stories.title: Wealthy Middle East residents are house-hunting in Europe to escape war
stories.summary: Wealthy residents of the Middle East are increasingly looking to purchase property in Europe as the ongoing war has shaken confidence in the region's stability. The conflict has undermined some Middle Eastern cities' reputations as safe havens.

stories.title: Russia works on giving Putin legal pretext to invade any country with Russian citizens in it
stories.summary: Russia is pursuing legal changes that would give President Putin a formal pretext to intervene militarily in any country with Russian citizens. The framework reportedly classifies "Russophobia" as an official justification for Russian intervention abroad.

stories.title: How a Russian ship under sanctions delivered armoured vehicles to Mali
stories.summary: A Russian cargo ship currently under international sanctions delivered dozens of armoured military vehicles to Mali via the port of Conakry, Guinea, in late March. The delivery highlights ongoing Russian military support to Mali despite sanctions.

stories.title: Britain’s national security ‘not safe’, says former NATO head
stories.summary: Former NATO head George Robertson accused UK ministers of "corrosive complacency" in a speech declaring Britain's national security is "not safe." The remarks target the current government's approach to defence spending.

stories.title: Trump: Iran talks could resume over next two days, NY Post reports
stories.summary: President Trump told the New York Post that US ceasefire talks with Iran could restart in Pakistan within two days after previous negotiations led by Vice President JD Vance broke down last week.

stories.title: U.S., Iran may meet again in Islamabad for second round of talks by next week: Report
stories.summary: Contacts are ongoing between the United States and Iran for a possible second round of talks in Islamabad, with reports suggesting negotiations may resume before the two-week ceasefire expires on April 21.

stories.title: Chinese tanker passes through Strait, Mossad chief vows Iran regime change
stories.summary: A Chinese tanker passed through the Strait of Hormuz, and Mossad chief David Barnea publicly vowed regime change in Iran, according to a Jerusalem Post news roundup.

stories.title: IDF soldiers wounded by Hezbollah terrorists, as weapons found in Lebanon home
stories.summary: IDF soldiers were wounded in an engagement with Hezbollah operatives in Lebanon. The IDF returned fire and killed three attackers, while weapons were discovered in a Lebanese home.

stories.title: Sudan: Iran war prompts 'massive' food, fuel price rises; drones kill hundreds of civilians in 2026
stories.summary: German charities report that food and fuel prices in war-torn Sudan have risen 70–80% amid broader Middle East unrest and the Iran conflict. Drone strikes have killed hundreds of Sudanese civilians, and international donors gathered in Berlin on the third anniversary of Sudan's war.

stories.title: Karishma Patel: What it was like inside the BBC amid Israel's genocidal war on Gaza
stories.summary: Former BBC journalist Karishma Patel left the broadcaster over what she described as editorial double standards in its coverage of the Israel-Gaza war. She detailed an atmosphere she characterised as 'Orwellian' in the BBC newsroom.

stories.title: First direct Lebanon-Israeli talks in decades 'historic' opportunity, says Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the first direct Lebanon-Israel talks in decades a "historic opportunity" as ambassadors from both countries met at the State Department in Washington.

stories.title: Recon battalion commander speaks about heroism of his soldiers
stories.summary: The commander of the 132nd Separate Reconnaissance Battalion of Ukraine's 7th Rapid Response Corps described his soldiers' missions during operations in Russia's Kursk region and in Ukraine's Donetsk region, where they defeated numerically superior enemy forces.

stories.title: After three years of war, what is the situation like in Sudan?
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war, now in its third year, has displaced millions of people and caused thousands of deaths, with no clear end to the violence in sight.

stories.title: Gideon Levy: Reporting on the Intifada changed how I see Israel
stories.summary: Israeli journalist Gideon Levy discussed how reporting on the Intifada fundamentally changed his perspective on Israel and the occupation of Palestinian territories. He has spent decades documenting conditions in the occupied lands.

stories.title: Germany jails Chinese student in Pelicot-like rape case
stories.summary: A Munich court sentenced 28-year-old Chinese student Zhongyi J. to over 11 years in prison for repeatedly drugging, raping, and filming his unconscious girlfriend. The court confirmed at least seven assaults, with videos stored on a hard drive, in a case compared to France's Pelicot rape case.

stories.title: IMF warns Middle East war driving up financial stability risks
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that the ongoing Middle East war is increasing global financial stability risks, driving up inflation, tightening markets, and straining private credit and AI-sector borrowers.

stories.title: 1:5 kill ratio: Ukraine inflicts heavy Russian losses using drones, says Finnish president
stories.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb, speaking during a visit to Washington, stated that Ukraine is achieving a roughly 1-to-5 kill ratio against Russian forces through effective use of drones. Stubb said Ukraine is in a stronger military position than at any previous stage of the conflict.

stories.title: Underground art, literally: War takes Tel Aviv museum’s tours to the basement
stories.summary: The Tel Aviv Museum of Art has moved its guided tours to basement galleries, including a New Objectivity exhibit rehung in dressing rooms, as the war forces cultural institutions underground.

stories.title: What does the blockade mean for oil prices?
stories.summary: The United States launched a naval blockade of maritime traffic at Iranian ports, raising concerns about global oil supply disruptions and potential price increases in energy markets.

stories.title: Kyiv strikes back: Ukraine names its new 1,400 km drone after month in winter which Russia hits hardest
stories.summary: Ukraine has unveiled a new long-range drone named "Sichen," meaning January in Ukrainian — the winter month when Russian attacks are most intense. The drone has a reported range of 1,400 kilometers.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon talks a rare historic moment amid hopes of conflict resolution
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors held rare direct talks in Washington, a tentative step toward broader negotiations to end hostilities involving Hezbollah. U.S. President Trump declared that Hezbollah must be eliminated while also signaling possible new peace talks with Iran as early as this week.

stories.title: Iyad el-Baghdadi: Israel as an ethno-nationalist state, won't last beyond the 2030s
stories.summary: Author and activist Iyad el-Baghdadi discussed the long-term viability of Israel as an ethno-nationalist state, arguing it may not survive in its current form beyond the 2030s. He also examined whether a Palestinian state remains feasible.

stories.title: Hossam el-Hamalawy: How has Israel's war on Gaza weakened Sisi's rule?
stories.summary: Egyptian activist Hossam el-Hamalawy discussed how Israel's war on Gaza has affected President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi's rule in Egypt. He also addressed the broader context of political change in Egypt since the revolution that toppled Hosni Mubarak.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia asks US to end Hormuz blockade amid worries of possible Houthi retaliation - WSJ
stories.summary: Saudi officials have asked the United States to end its naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to The Wall Street Journal. Riyadh is concerned that Iran could retaliate through allied forces such as the Houthis elsewhere in the region.

stories.title: 16 wounded in Turkey school shooting; gunman dead
stories.summary: A former student opened fire at a school in Turkey, wounding 16 people before dying. The attacker was identified as having previously attended the targeted school.

stories.title: Washington-Vatican feud deepens as JD Vance says pope should 'stick to matters of morality'
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance escalated a feud between Washington and the Vatican by suggesting Pope Leo XIV should focus on moral and church matters rather than commenting on US foreign policy, after the pope criticised the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Lebanese, Israeli ambassadors begin direct talks in US
stories.summary: The Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to the United States met in Washington for their countries' first direct talks in decades, mediated by the US.

stories.title: Russia’s State Duma passes first reading of bill allowing military to operate abroad to protect Russian citizens
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma passed the first reading of a bill that would authorize the Russian military to operate extraterritorially to protect Russian citizens abroad, as reported by state agencies TASS and RIA Novosti.

stories.title: Zelensky, Merz seal 10 new agreements to boost Ukraine-Germany cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz signed ten new cooperation agreements during their meeting, covering multiple areas of bilateral partnership.

stories.title: Spain probes CAF over role in Israeli settlement rail project
stories.summary: Spanish authorities are investigating railway manufacturer CAF over its alleged involvement in a Jerusalem light rail project that connects illegal Israeli settlements in occupied East Jerusalem.

stories.title: Mustafa Barghouti: Palestinians will 'die here and not leave'
stories.summary: Mustafa Barghouti, general secretary of the Palestinian National Initiative, responded to US President Donald Trump's plan to expel Palestinians from Gaza. He also described accelerating ethnic cleansing in the occupied West Bank amid rising settler violence.

stories.title: The Israeli town on the frontline with Hezbollah
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Nick Beake visited Metula, an Israeli town bordered on three sides by Lebanon, reporting on conditions for residents living on the frontline with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Bulls take charge as KSE-100 rallies 5,000 points
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index surged over 5,000 points on Tuesday, recovering partially after shedding more than 6,000 points the previous day amid market fears over inconclusive Iran-US peace talks and potential supply disruptions.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill six in Gaza, including two children
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, including two children, putting further strain on the US-brokered ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes drone production, military support deal with Germany
stories.summary: Ukraine and Germany signed a deal in which Germany gains access to Ukraine's advanced drone technology in exchange for additional military support in Ukraine's war against Russia.

stories.title: How much has the US-Israel war on Iran cost so far?
stories.summary: The five-week US-Israel war on Iran has generated enormous costs, with each side presenting significantly different estimates of the financial and material damage inflicted.

stories.title: SAM Ukraine built in secret is now standing in plain sight
stories.summary: Ukraine has revealed a domestically built surface-to-air missile system that was previously developed in secret. Spain contributed to the project, and the system's design was influenced by the IRIS-T air-defense platform.

stories.title: Norman Finkelstein: Will Israel manipulate Trump?
stories.summary: Political analyst Norman Finkelstein discussed the trajectory of Israeli policy toward Palestinians, arguing that Israel and the Trump administration would continue plans to displace Palestinians from the territory between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.

stories.title: Husband of US woman missing in Bahamas released, says he will keep looking
stories.summary: Brian Hooker, the husband of US woman Lynette Hooker who went missing in the Bahamas earlier this month, was released from custody after being detained and questioned by authorities. He stated he would continue searching for his wife.

stories.title: Report: Major Russian platforms begin restricting services for users with VPN enabled
stories.summary: Major Russian internet platforms have started restricting access for users connecting through VPNs, according to the Telegram channel Ostorozhno Novosti. The move signals an escalation in Russia's efforts to control online access and circumvention tools.

stories.title: Iran less likely to compromise in US talks as its isolation grows, analyst warns
stories.summary: The collapse of U.S.-Iran negotiations is raising doubts about the durability of the current ceasefire, with analysts warning Iran's growing isolation makes compromise less likely.

stories.title: High Court petition seeks to block Gofman’s Mossad appointment over Elmakayes affair
stories.summary: A petition was filed before Israel's High Court seeking to block the appointment of Gofman as Mossad chief, citing the Elmakayes affair. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had approved the appointment ahead of a scheduled June 2 start date.

stories.title: ‘Blindsided’: US farmers strained as fertiliser costs surge on Iran war
stories.summary: US farmers are facing surging fertiliser and diesel costs after US-Israeli strikes on Iran prompted Tehran to block the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting critical supply shipments during peak planting season for crops including corn and soybeans.

stories.title: Magyar’s first visit to Warsaw may help revive Visegrád Group’s role in EU – Czaputowicz
stories.summary: Former Polish Foreign Minister Jacek Czaputowicz suggested that Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar's planned first foreign visit to Warsaw could signal alignment with Donald Tusk's Civic Coalition and help revive the Visegrád Group's role within the EU.

stories.title: Pakistan working to set second round of US, Iran talks: Sources
stories.summary: Pakistani officials are working to arrange a second round of US-Iran peace talks and to extend the current ceasefire beyond its deadline. Islamabad is serving as a mediating venue for the negotiations.

stories.title: WATCH: Daughter of Holocaust survivor robbed in Hadera, suspect arrested
stories.summary: Police in Hadera, Israel, arrested a 30-year-old suspect in connection with the robbery of a daughter of a Holocaust survivor. The suspect was taken to a police station for questioning.

stories.title: Russian journalist charged with unauthorized access to computer data as part of a group
stories.summary: Russian journalist Oleg Roldugin, a columnist for the independent outlet Novaya Gazeta, has been charged with unauthorized access to computer data as part of a group. The outlet itself reported the charges against its staff member.

stories.title: Russia Introduces Helium Export Controls Amid Global Shortage
stories.summary: Russia has introduced export controls on helium amid a global shortage. Russia ranks as the world's third-largest helium producer, behind Qatar and the United States.

stories.title: Woman among four more Iranians sentenced to death over protests
stories.summary: An Iranian court sentenced four more people, including a woman, to death in connection with protests that took place in January. International rights groups have warned of escalating repression in the country.

stories.title: Ukraine just gave Germany’s AI something no simulation ever could: real war
stories.summary: German Chancellor Merz and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy signed a major defense technology agreement described as the most consequential in Europe. The deal involves integrating real battlefield data from Ukraine into Germany's AI defense systems.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit shaped by uncertainty, not strategy: experts
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are preparing for a summit in the coming weeks, with planning including a possible visit to Beijing's Temple of Heaven and a military parade. Experts noted the compressed and disjointed preparation process, shaped by the Middle East war and Trump's preference for last-minute decisions.

stories.title: A peek into munitions spending, and a chat with Sweden’s DefMin
stories.summary: The latest episode of The Break Out podcast covers large-scale munitions spending amounting to billions of dollars for missile procurement and features a discussion with Sweden's Defense Minister on Stockholm's security priorities.

stories.title: 2 policemen injured as residents protest against anti-encroachment drive in Islamabad
stories.summary: Two police officers were injured in Islamabad's Noorpur Shahan area after residents protesting a Capital Development Authority anti-encroachment operation torched two CDA vehicles, prompting authorities to deploy tear gas and additional police.

stories.title: School shooting in Turkiye leaves 16 wounded
stories.summary: A 19-year-old former student wounded 16 people in a shooting at a high school in Türkiye before taking his own life as police attempted to apprehend him.

stories.title: Why Pakistan is looking to Saudi Arabia, China for UAE repayment
stories.summary: Pakistan is looking to Saudi Arabia and China to help it repay a loan owed to the United Arab Emirates, drawing on its longstanding bilateral ties with both Riyadh and Beijing.

stories.title: Zelensky rejects “EU light” and “NATO Light,” insists on full membership
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine will not accept reduced "EU light" or "NATO light" membership options, insisting on full membership in both organizations.

stories.title: Russia opens criminal case against woman near St. Petersburg over Easter bread photo
stories.summary: Russia's Investigative Committee for the Leningrad Region has opened a criminal case against a woman from the Murino district near St. Petersburg over a photo she posted online featuring an Easter bread loaf.

stories.title: US-based Credo Tech snaps up Israeli maker of silicon chips for up to $1.3 billion
stories.summary: US-based Credo Technology Group is acquiring Israeli company DustPhotonics, backed by entrepreneur Avigdor Willenz, in a deal valued at up to $1.3 billion. DustPhotonics develops silicon photonics technology for high-speed data transfer in AI applications.

stories.title: US, Iranian teams could return to Islamabad for peace talks this week: Sources
stories.summary: Sources indicate that US and Iranian delegations could return to Islamabad for peace talks as early as the end of this week. A specific date has not yet been confirmed by either side.

stories.title: Infected blood scandal compensation to rise
stories.summary: The UK government allocated an additional £1 billion in compensation for victims of the infected blood scandal, described as the biggest treatment disaster in NHS history. Payments include an extra £35,000 each for former pupils of Treloar school who were experimented on without their knowledge.

stories.title: United Airlines CEO reportedly pitched merger with American, sparking competition fears
stories.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby reportedly pitched a merger with American Airlines during a meeting with President Donald Trump in late February. The proposed combination of the world's two largest carriers has sparked competition concerns from critics.

stories.title: Wadah Khanfar: The more the US interferes, the more they are hated
stories.summary: Wadah Khanfar, founder of the Al-Sharq Forum and former Al Jazeera director general, discussed the Gaza conflict, the prospect of regional war, and growing Arab frustration over the situation in the Palestinian territories.

stories.title: Italy’s PM: Defence agreement with Israel suspended
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced that Italy has suspended the automatic renewal of a defence cooperation agreement with Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan's diplomatic gamble: How an unlikely peacemaker emerged
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as an unlikely mediator, brokering a ceasefire and hosting historic US-Iran talks. However, analysts warn the country faces a difficult balancing act between rival alliances if no lasting agreement is reached.

stories.title: Israeli ambassador to Germany condemns Bezalel Smotrich’s tirade against chancellor
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to Germany, Ron Prosor, publicly condemned far-right Israeli cabinet member Bezalel Smotrich for a verbal attack on German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Smotrich had made references to the Nazi regime, which Prosor said "erodes the memory of the Holocaust."

stories.title: Italy's Meloni suspends defence cooperation deal with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni suspended Italy's defence cooperation deal with Israel amid tensions over the Middle East war and Israeli strikes on Lebanon.

stories.title: Gaza shoe display in Amsterdam appears to appropriate Holocaust imagery ahead of Yom Hashoah
stories.summary: A pro-Palestinian nonprofit displayed shoes in Amsterdam's Dam Square to commemorate Palestinian children killed in the Gaza war. The display drew criticism for appearing to appropriate Holocaust imagery ahead of Yom Hashoah.

stories.title: China says policy to improve relations with India remains unchanged
stories.summary: China has stated that its policy of improving relations with India remains unchanged, amid ongoing tensions over Beijing's practice of publishing Chinese names for regions in Arunachal Pradesh, which India has consistently rejected.

stories.title: EagleNXT deepens buying spree in Israel with $10m. investment in ThirdEye Systems
stories.summary: U.S.-based EagleNXT invested $10 million in Israeli firm ThirdEye Systems as part of a broader acquisition strategy. Plans include a joint venture in Texas to help ThirdEye enter the North American market.

stories.title: ‘Bizarre’ lack of urgency in putting UK on war footing, says defence review co-author
stories.summary: Fiona Hill, co-author of Britain's strategic defence review and former White House adviser on Russia, criticized Prime Minister Keir Starmer for a "bizarre" lack of urgency in putting the UK on a war footing. Her remarks echoed concerns from former NATO chief George Robertson about "corrosive complacency" in defence planning.

stories.title: Italy's Meloni suspends defence cooperation deal with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni suspended a defence cooperation deal with Israel, reflecting deteriorating ties between previously close allies. Meloni's right-wing government, once one of Israel's closest European partners, has recently criticized Israeli attacks on Lebanon that killed hundreds.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian drone storage site near Donetsk airport with SCALP missiles
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces used French-made SCALP cruise missiles to strike a Russian drone storage facility near Donetsk Airport, targeting a site used to house strike unmanned aerial vehicles.

stories.title: Vance says progress made with Iran as sides weigh second round of talks
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance said on Fox News that significant progress was made in talks with Iran and that the next step was up to Tehran. Both sides are weighing whether to hold a second round of negotiations.

stories.title: Rubio hosts Israeli, Lebanese envoys as talks begin in Washington
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors in Washington on Tuesday for the first direct peace talks between the two countries in decades. The discussions represent a significant diplomatic development between the long-time adversaries.

stories.title: Antisemitic attacks in 2025 led to highest number of fatalities in 30 years, study finds
stories.summary: A Tel Aviv University study found that 2025 saw the highest number of fatalities from antisemitic attacks in over 30 years, with 20 people killed. The violence, including a deadly attack at a Hanukkah celebration in Australia, continued a spike that began after Hamas's October 7, 2023, attacks.

stories.title: Naledi Pandor on the fight to isolate Israel
stories.summary: Former South African Minister of International Relations Naledi Pandor discussed South Africa's decision to bring a case against Israel at the International Court of Justice, alleging genocide in Gaza. South Africa filed the case earlier in 2024.

stories.title: Historic but not enough? Colombia’s Gustavo Petro defends cocaine seizures
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro has overseen record-level cocaine seizures, but questions remain whether the historic interdiction volumes will be sufficient to reduce pressure from the United States.

stories.title: In Iran conflict, Tehran and Washington fight with new weapons
