stories.summary: The conflict between Iran and the United States has featured new weapons on both sides, including upgraded Iranian missiles with extended range and American drones modeled on Iranian designs. The war is functioning as a real-world testing ground for these munitions.

stories.title: Roy Casagranda on the US' long history of coups and wars in the Middle East
stories.summary: Professor Roy Casagranda of Austin Community College discussed the United States' history of coups and military interventions in the Middle East over the past century, examining patterns of American involvement in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Defense Forces strike Russian air defense assets in Belgorod region, occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck three Russian radar stations and a surface-to-air missile system in Russia's Belgorod region and occupied Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Wisden laments India’s ‘Orwellian’ control of world cricket
stories.summary: The latest edition of Wisden Cricketers' Almanack has criticised what it calls India's 'Orwellian' political interference in global cricket administration, highlighting Indian dominance of the International Cricket Council's leadership.

stories.title: China’s Xi says rule of law must be upheld for Middle East peace
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that the rule of law must be upheld to achieve peace in the Middle East. Beijing is seen as playing a behind-the-scenes role in encouraging Iran toward a peace deal with the United States.

stories.title: Mossad chief Barnea: Iran mission incomplete until it results in regime change
stories.summary: Outgoing Mossad chief David Barnea publicly stated for the first time that the agency's mission regarding Iran remains incomplete until it results in regime change in Tehran.

stories.title: With no one to say Kaddish for many children killed in the Holocaust, a US synagogue steps up
stories.summary: Dozens of families at Temple Beth El in West Palm Beach, Florida, have adopted the memory of child victims of the Holocaust who have no surviving relatives to say Kaddish for them, creating a new form of remembrance.

stories.title: ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’: Why a documentary on Russia resonated with the world - opinion
stories.summary: A documentary about opposition to President Vladimir Putin has drawn international attention, with commentators drawing parallels between repression in modern Russia and the fear that pervaded Soviet society under Joseph Stalin.

stories.title: Israel wants to 'separate Hezbollah from Lebanon' in US talks
stories.summary: Israel has stated its goal of separating Hezbollah from the Lebanese state as direct talks with Lebanon began in Washington. However, reaching common ground remains difficult as Israel continues military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Twin suicide attacks rocked Algeria Monday during Pope's visit
stories.summary: Twin suspected suicide attacks struck the city of Blida, southwest of Algiers, on Monday during Pope Leo's visit to Algeria. The incidents have heightened security tensions in the country.

stories.title: A Russian Defense Ministry institute is testing drugs and munitions on human subjects
stories.summary: An investigation by the outlet Proekt, summarized by Agentstvo, reports that Russia's Institute for Experimental Military Medicine, part of the Defense Ministry, has been conducting trials of munitions and medical substances on volunteer servicemen.

stories.title: Trump turns on Italy’s Meloni, says he is ‘shocked’ by her
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly criticized Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in an interview with Corriere della Sera, saying he was "shocked" by her. Meloni, previously a strong Trump supporter, had criticized his decision to go to war with Iran and denounced his criticism of Pope Leo as "unacceptable."

stories.title: UK’s armed forces are in a sad state – and they have only themselves to blame
stories.summary: Critics, including former NATO Secretary General George Robertson, have accused the UK Ministry of Defence of institutional complacency and failure to learn from past mistakes. Robertson accused Prime Minister Keir Starmer of lacking willingness to make necessary defence investments.

stories.title: Zimbabwe pacer Blessing Muzarabani banned for 2 PSL editions over ‘failure to honour commitments’
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board has banned Zimbabwe fast bowler Blessing Muzarabani from the next two editions of the Pakistan Super League for failing to honour agreed-upon commitments to the tournament.

stories.title: ‘Debased himself’ and risking Australia’s reputation: Liberals torn up about Taylor’s Trumpian immigration plan
stories.summary: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor unveiled a hardline immigration policy that drew criticism from refugee advocates and some within his own Liberal Party. Former Howard-era minister Amanda Vanstone warned against turning immigration into heavy-handed law enforcement.

stories.title: Dinner for few: Australians eating out less as fuel crisis deals biggest blow to consumer confidence since Covid
stories.summary: Australian consumer confidence has fallen sharply due to rising fuel prices linked to the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran. Households are cutting back on dining out and choosing cheaper menu options, in what experts describe as "cautious consumption" reminiscent of pandemic-era behavior.

stories.title: IMF Warns of Mounting Economic Pressures for Sub-Saharan Africa Amid Global Instability
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund's latest World Economic Outlook warns of mounting economic pressures for Sub-Saharan Africa. The IMF cites escalating conflict in the Middle East as a threat to the region's already fragile recovery.

stories.title: Threat of Russia’s space nuclear weapon ‘forced us to prepare,’ Space Command head says
stories.summary: U.S. Space Command conducted a wargame focused on the threat posed by a potential Russian nuclear weapon deployed in space. The exercise involved participation from dozens of private-sector companies. SPACECOM's commander stated the threat compelled the military to undertake preparedness measures.

stories.title: DRC: Dozens gather for 'standing parliament' in Kinshasa
stories.summary: In Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, dozens of people gathered at an informal 'standing parliament.' Some observers believe President Félix Tshisekedi may be using such gatherings to build support for constitutional changes allowing a third term.

stories.title: Hegseth announces ‘major’ defence partnership with Indonesia
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a major defense partnership with Indonesia covering military training and cooperation.

stories.title: Zelenskyy hails Magyar’s win over Orbán as ‘the victory of light over darkness’ in Hungary – as it happened
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised Péter Magyar's election victory over Viktor Orbán's party in Hungary, calling it a victory of "light over darkness." German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the result would have implications for support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Russian army strikes Dnipro with missile, leaving four killed and 25 injured
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed four people and injured 25, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Why are the US, Iran arguing over duration of uranium enrichment ban?
stories.summary: Negotiations between the US and Iran have stalled over the duration of a uranium enrichment ban. Washington reportedly seeks a 20-year halt, while Tehran has offered five years, highlighting a major gap in the talks.

stories.title: Comprehensive migrant agreement at centre of Syria-UK talks
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is seeking a comprehensive migrant agreement with Syria, modeled on a similar deal signed with the Iraqi government in August of the previous year.

stories.title: Brazil's former spy chief detained by ICE agents in US
stories.summary: Alexandre Ramagem, Brazil's former spy chief, was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in the United States. Ramagem had been sentenced to 16 years in prison in Brazil for plotting a military coup but had already fled the country.

stories.title: Twin suicide attacks rocked Algeria during Pope's visit
stories.summary: Two suspected suicide attacks struck the city of Blida, Algeria, during a visit by Pope Leo XIV. Authorities are investigating the incident.

stories.title: ‘We are a stable, predictable country’: Spanish PM Sanchez in Beijing
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, where both leaders emphasized respect for international law and a shared sense of justice, with Sánchez portraying Spain as a stable and predictable partner.

stories.title: Defense and economy: Ukraine and Germany sign cooperation documents
stories.summary: Ukraine and Germany signed two cooperation agreements covering defense and economic matters during intergovernmental consultations.

stories.title: Toddler among four killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: Four people, including a toddler, were killed in an Israeli airstrike in northern Gaza on Tuesday. The civil defence said the strike targeted a police vehicle in Gaza City, with several others injured.

stories.title: Kremlin says Russia’s internet restrictions will be lifted once the need for them disappears
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia's internet restrictions would be lifted once the government determines the "necessity" for them has ended, without specifying a timeline.

stories.title: High school shooting in Turkiye wounds 16; attacker dead
stories.summary: A 19-year-old former student opened fire at his former high school in Sanliurfa province in southeastern Türkiye, wounding 16 people including students, before killing himself. Special security forces were deployed and the wounded were taken to a hospital in Siverek district.

stories.title: Kuwait detaining journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin after social media posts
stories.summary: Kuwaiti authorities have detained award-winning journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin over social media posts. Rights groups say his detention reflects a broader crackdown on online speech in the region amid the Iran war.

stories.title: Colombia approves culling plan as Escobar’s Hippos become environmental threat
stories.summary: Colombian authorities have approved a plan to cull dozens of hippos descended from animals originally imported by drug lord Pablo Escobar in the 1980s. The rapidly growing population has become a threat to local communities and native wildlife.

stories.title: Russian weapon Ukraine cannot intercept is now hitting civilian water supplies
stories.summary: Russian forces bombed the dam supplying drinking water to Kharkiv, Ukraine. Ukrainian authorities say the weapon used cannot currently be intercepted by Ukraine's air defenses.

stories.title: US fires more judges including those blocking deportations
stories.summary: The Trump administration has fired multiple U.S. immigration judges, including those who had blocked deportations of pro-Palestinian students, according to the judges' union.

stories.title: US blockade of Iran ports irresponsible and dangerous, China says
stories.summary: China condemned the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports as "irresponsible and dangerous." Beijing, the largest buyer of Iranian oil, warned that the blockade undermines an "already fragile ceasefire" between the U.S. and Iran.

stories.title: Russian troops drop six guided aerial bombs on one of largest reservoirs in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped six guided aerial bombs on the dam of the Pechenihy Reservoir, one of the largest reservoirs in Ukraine's Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Vedomosti reports over 50% of Russia’s library holdings could be seized under literal reading of ‘foreign agent’ and ‘undesirable’ laws
stories.summary: The head of Russia's Eksmo-AST publishing group warned that over 50% of Russia's library holdings could be subject to seizure under a literal interpretation of the country's "foreign agent" and "undesirable organizations" laws, as reported by Vedomosti.

stories.title: Nigeria slashes import duties to fight rising cost of living
stories.summary: Nigeria announced it will cut import duties on a range of goods starting July 1. The measure is aimed at easing rising living costs and supporting businesses across the country.

stories.title: 'Race to the border' as Islamic State and JNIM clash in Niger
stories.summary: Islamic State and the al-Qaeda affiliate JNIM clashed for the first time inside Niger, expanding their confrontations beyond the tri-border area with Mali and Burkina Faso. The fighting is spreading toward the border region between Niger, Nigeria, and Benin as both groups compete for resources and recruits.

stories.title: Iran war: US blockade of Hormuz tests China's restraint
stories.summary: China, the largest buyer of Iranian oil, is assessing the impact of a US naval blockade of Iran's ports and shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts are examining whether the escalation could draw Beijing into the broader conflict.

stories.title: Global federation lauds ‘professionalism’ of Pakistan’s air traffic controllers amid airspace disruptions
stories.summary: The International Federation of Air Traffic Controllers' Associations praised the professionalism of Pakistan's air traffic controllers amid recent airspace disruptions, according to a letter from the federation's Asia-Pacific vice president shared by the Pakistan Airports Authority.

stories.title: Russia’s Oil Export Revenue Surged in March, IEA Says
stories.summary: Russia's oil export revenue surged to $19 billion in March, according to the International Energy Agency, marking a sharp reversal from February when revenues hit their lowest level since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Hollywood stars speak out against Paramount-Warner deal
stories.summary: Hundreds of Hollywood figures, including Jane Fonda, Joaquin Phoenix, and Bryan Cranston, signed an open letter opposing a proposed deal in which Paramount would acquire the historic Warner Bros. studio.

stories.title: New trial over soccer legend Maradona's death begins in Argentina
stories.summary: A new trial began in Buenos Aires on Tuesday over the 2020 death of Argentine soccer legend Diego Maradona. Seven members of his medical team face charges of negligent homicide, nearly a year after a previous trial was declared a mistrial.

stories.title: 'No time to waste': Magyar vows new era in Hungary after ousting Orban
stories.summary: Hungarian election winner Péter Magyar promised a "new era" in politics after his landslide victory over Viktor Orbán's party. He pledged to restore democratic standards and unblock European Union funds, likely anchoring Budapest in the EU mainstream.

stories.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast on Iran war
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund cut its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1 percent, down from the 3.3 percent projected in January, citing disruptions from the war in the Middle East. US growth was also revised lower due to the conflict's effects on commodity markets and prices.

stories.title: At Auschwitz, Diaspora Jews who lived through terror march alongside Holocaust survivors
stories.summary: At the annual March of the Living at Auschwitz, Diaspora Jews who experienced antisemitic persecution in recent years marched alongside Holocaust survivors. Organisers noted it was the deadliest year for Diaspora Jews in three decades.

stories.title: Italy suspending defense agreement with Israel amid Mideast conflict, PM Meloni says
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced the suspension of Italy's defence agreement with Israel amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. An EU petition to reassess ties with Israel has gathered over one million signatures.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian port damages Panama-flagged vessel, officials say
stories.summary: Russian drones attacked Ukraine's Izmail port in the southern Odesa region overnight, damaging a civilian Panama-flagged vessel. Ukrainian officials reported the strike on Tuesday.

stories.title: US officials underwhelmed by French far-right's plans for economy
stories.summary: U.S. officials who met leaders of France's far-right National Rally party were underwhelmed by their economic plans, according to two diplomatic sources. The reaction is a setback for the party's efforts to present itself as a credible manager of the euro zone's second-largest economy ahead of next year's election.

stories.title: White supremacist pleads guilty to Tennessee civil rights center arson
stories.summary: Regan Prater, a man linked to white supremacist movements, pleaded guilty to setting a fire that destroyed an office at the Highlander social justice center in Tennessee. He also admitted to attempting to aid Hezbollah by providing personally identifying information. Sentencing is set for September.

stories.title: Hamas rejects Gaza disarmament plan, Palestinian official says
stories.summary: A Palestinian official told the BBC that Hamas has rejected a Gaza disarmament plan and will not resume negotiations until Israel fully meets its existing commitments.

stories.title: McDonald's, Iran and the pope: Trump's bizarre press conference
stories.summary: President Donald Trump held a press conference during which he received a DoorDash delivery from McDonald's in the Oval Office. He spoke about the Iran conflict and his dispute with Pope Leo during the event.

stories.title: Xi Jinping’s meeting with Abu Dhabi crown prince highlights Gulf turn towards China
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and proposed a four-point plan for Middle East stability. The meeting underscores Beijing's intensifying diplomatic engagement in the Gulf amid the Iran crisis.

stories.title: French investigators target Élysée palace in events company contracts probe
stories.summary: French financial and anti-corruption investigators raided the Élysée Palace on Tuesday as part of a probe into contracts awarded to the events company Shortcut Events. The investigation examines why the firm was chosen to host important state events for more than two decades.

stories.title: Russians strike Dnipro, leaving 15 people wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro in central Ukraine, wounding 15 people in the attack.

stories.title: UK steel exports to EU at risk as bloc doubles tariffs and halves quotas
stories.summary: The European Union plans to double tariffs and halve duty-free quotas on steel imports starting in July, reducing quotas by 47%. While aimed at curbing Chinese imports, the move could also harm UK steel exports to the bloc.

stories.title: JD Vance defends Trump amid spat with Pope Leo: ‘Stick to matters of morality’
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance defended President Trump in his dispute with Pope Leo, telling the pontiff to "stick to matters of morality" and leave U.S. policy to the president. The pope had criticized the White House over the Iran war.

stories.title: US, Iranian teams could return to Islamabad for 2nd round of peace talks this week: sources
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiating teams may return to Islamabad later this week for a second round of peace talks, after the first direct discussions between the two countries since 1979 ended without a breakthrough or a breakdown over the weekend.

stories.title: Report: Russia’s customs service starts imposing higher duties on goods from ‘unfriendly’ countries
stories.summary: Russia's customs service has begun imposing higher import duties on goods originating from countries Moscow deems "unfriendly," even when those goods enter through the Eurasian Economic Union, according to Forbes Russia.

stories.title: Palestinian Authority blames Israel for death of released Palestinian terrorist in Egypt
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority, through its WAFA news agency, attributed the death of released Palestinian prisoner Amour in Egypt to alleged medical neglect during his years in Israeli detention, stating a long illness worsened under those conditions.

stories.title: Druzhba pipeline partially repaired by end of April — enough to function, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the Druzhba oil pipeline would be partially repaired and operational by the end of April. He also signaled readiness to reset ties with Hungary following Péter Magyar's election victory.

stories.title: Understanding the Illegality of Trump’s Iran Threats
stories.summary: The conflict between the U.S. and Iran has become a testing ground for advanced weapons systems on both sides. Iran has deployed upgraded extended-range missiles, while the U.S. has used drones inspired by Iranian designs.

stories.title: Inside the rise of Project Maven and AI warfare [Book excerpt]
stories.summary: Katrina Manson's book "Project Maven" details how a Marine colonel and his team helped launch the U.S. military's pioneering artificial-intelligence program, Project Maven, which has become central to the Pentagon's push to integrate AI into modern warfare.

stories.title: France expects Hungary's new leadership to lift veto on aid to Ukraine – French FM Jean-Noël Barrot
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said France expects Hungary's incoming leadership under Péter Magyar to lift the country's veto on EU aid to Ukraine. Barrot characterized the defeat of Viktor Orbán as Putin losing his "Trojan horse" in the European Union.

stories.title: Italy halts automatic renewal of defense agreement with Israel amid Middle East conflicts
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced that Italy would suspend the automatic renewal of its defense cooperation agreement with Israel, citing the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East as the reason.

stories.title: OPEC: Middle East oil production plummets due to Iran war
stories.summary: OPEC has reported a significant drop in Middle East oil production since the start of the Iran war. The decline is documented in a new OPEC report assessing the conflict's impact on regional output.

stories.title: Jerusalem ceremony recognizes four Jews who rescued other Jews during Holocaust
stories.summary: A ceremony in Jerusalem honoured four Jews who risked their own lives to rescue fellow Jews during the Holocaust. The B'nai B'rith-KKL-JNF citation recognised their heroism during World War II.

stories.title: With memorial siren wailing, Israel remembers Holocaust victims in shadow of war tensions
stories.summary: Israel held its annual Holocaust Remembrance Day ceremony at Yad Vashem without a public audience due to ongoing fighting with Hezbollah and a ceasefire with Iran. The March of the Living took place in Poland, with most Israelis unable to attend.

stories.title: Naval chief says Pakistan stands ready to deter any aggression, vows ‘befitting response’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, speaking at a Pakistan Air Force cadet graduation in Risalpur, stated that Pakistan's armed forces stand ready to deter any aggression and deliver a befitting response, referencing the May 2025 conflict with India.

stories.title: Why India walked away from its bid to host COP33
stories.summary: India has quietly withdrawn its bid to host the COP33 UN climate conference, reversing a pledge made by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2023. Experts are analyzing the factors behind New Delhi's decision.

stories.title: Sudan’s war still misunderstood after three years
stories.summary: April 15, 2026, marks three years since the war in Sudan erupted. The conflict, which began as a power struggle between rival military factions, remains widely misunderstood despite its prolonged devastation.

stories.title: The €35 billion Hungary lost while Orbán picked fights with Brussels
stories.summary: Hungary risks losing approximately €35 billion in EU funds, with €2 billion already forfeited and a key deadline approaching in August, due to ongoing disputes between Budapest and Brussels.

stories.title: Greenpeace warns of potential ‘catastrophic’ collapse at defunct Chernobyl nuclear power station
stories.summary: Greenpeace warned of a potential catastrophic collapse at the defunct Chernobyl nuclear power station in Ukraine. The environmental group said that despite repair works, the confinement function of the facility's safety shell could not be fully restored.

stories.title: Kuwait detains journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin over social posts
stories.summary: Kuwaiti authorities detained journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin over social media posts, raising concerns about press freedom amid the ongoing Iran war.

stories.title: New Mossad chief backs Gaza occupation and once 'used' a teenager in operation
stories.summary: Roman Gofman, described as a Netanyahu loyalist, has been appointed as Israel's new Mossad chief. Questions have been raised about his integrity, including allegations that he used a teenager in an intelligence operation earlier in his career.

stories.title: France, Germany, Netherlands, and Italy resist fast-track EU membership for Ukraine, Politico reports
stories.summary: France, Germany, the Netherlands, and Italy oppose fast-tracking Ukraine's EU membership, according to Politico. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy rejected any reduced "EU-lite" membership option during a Berlin press conference with German Chancellor Merz.

stories.title: Can Pakistan juggle US-Iran mediation with Saudi defence commitments?
stories.summary: Pakistan is attempting to simultaneously mediate between the US and Iran while maintaining its defence commitments to Saudi Arabia. Pakistani officials and analysts say both roles can coexist, though the balancing act presents significant challenges.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks hospital in central Kherson, injuring four staff members
stories.summary: Russian forces used a drone to attack a hospital in central Kherson, Ukraine, injuring four staff members. Separately, a 62-year-old resident was wounded when explosives were dropped from a drone onto a car.

stories.title: Philippines rejects China’s claim it ‘staged’ cyanide evidence at disputed shoal
stories.summary: The Philippine military rejected China's claim that Manila staged evidence of cyanide use near a contested reef in the South China Sea. The dispute centers on the BRP Sierra Madre, a grounded warship serving as a Philippine military outpost, where Filipino officials accused Chinese fishermen of deploying cyanide.

stories.title: Rolls-Royce modern AE Engines power the future of Army aviation – and more
stories.summary: Rolls-Royce is supplying its AE engine family to several U.S. military platforms, including the MV-75 Future Long Range Assault Aircraft and the MQ-25 Stingray unmanned aerial refueling drone, as part of efforts to modernize Army aviation and broader defense capabilities.

stories.title: Russia hands Crimea’s main detention center to FSB
stories.summary: Russia has transferred control of Crimea's main detention center to the FSB, reversing a concession made to the Council of Europe in 2005. Detention facilities in Crimea are already operating at 103% capacity.

stories.title: Israel ‘wants to reach peace and normalisation with Lebanon’
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar stated that Israel seeks to achieve peace and normalisation with Lebanon, signaling diplomatic intentions as broader regional tensions continue.

stories.title: Will Europe's airports run out of jet fuel?
stories.summary: The head of French energy group TotalEnergies warned that European airports could face a jet fuel shortage in the coming weeks or months if the situation at the Strait of Hormuz does not improve.

stories.title: Trump pick to lead Federal Reserve has assets worth over $100m, disclosures indicate
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, submitted financial disclosures indicating he holds assets worth over $100 million. The filings are required for his Senate confirmation process to replace current Fed Chair Jerome Powell.

stories.title: Lebanon-Israel talks: 'A significant and symbolic step'
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli representatives met in Washington on Tuesday for their first direct diplomatic talks in decades. The meeting follows more than a month of war between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Gulf allies turn to Ukraine, UK, and Asia as ammunition runs low
stories.summary: After six weeks of repeated Iranian attacks, Gulf states are seeking to replenish their ammunition and defense systems from Ukraine, the United Kingdom, and Asian suppliers rather than relying solely on the United States.

stories.title: Two ships from Iran ports pass Hormuz Strait despite US blockade
stories.summary: At least two ships using Iranian ports passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday despite the U.S. military blockade, according to maritime tracking data from Kpler. The incidents raise questions about the effectiveness of the American naval blockade.

stories.title: Intimacy coordinator Paloma Garcia Martens on 'respecting people's humanity on set'
stories.summary: An analysis argues that U.S. President Trump's threats to destroy Iranian bridges and power plants would violate international law. The piece warns such actions could expose American service members to prosecution.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone revolution is transforming the landscape of the ground war - analysis
stories.summary: Ukraine has become a leading innovator in drone technology and unmanned ground vehicles during its ongoing ground war, driven by battlefield necessity. Analysts compare its advances to Israel's drone development programs.

stories.title: Nigerian airstrike hits market in northeast Yobe state
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel began direct talks in Washington on Tuesday, marking a rare diplomatic engagement between two parties technically at war since 1948.

stories.title: Pope makes first papal visit to Algeria
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran has served as a real-world testing ground for new weapons systems. Both sides have deployed upgraded munitions, including extended-range Iranian missiles and American drones inspired by Iranian designs.

stories.title: ICRC delivers the first batch of emergency relief to Iran
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross delivered 171 metric tonnes of emergency relief supplies to the Iranian Red Crescent Society. The shipment, one of the first cross-border humanitarian deliveries to Iran in six weeks, is intended to assist more than 25,000 people.

stories.title: Who wants what from Israel-Lebanon talks?
stories.summary: Italy's government, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, suspended its defence cooperation agreement with Israel after Rome accused Israeli forces of firing warning shots at a convoy of Italian UN peacekeepers in Lebanon.

stories.title: US-sanctioned tankers pass Strait of Hormuz despite US blockade, data shows
stories.summary: Tracking data shows that U.S.-sanctioned tankers have passed through the Strait of Hormuz despite the American naval blockade. The tanker and its parent company are sanctioned by Washington for dealings with Iran.

stories.title: Shanghai Gigafactory has potential to construct humanoid robots: Tesla China president
stories.summary: Tesla's China president Allan Wang Hao said the company's Shanghai Gigafactory, its largest production base, has the potential to manufacture humanoid robots in the future. He described the facility's efficiency and capability as a possible "golden key" to mass-producing the technology.

stories.title: IMF warns ‘unprecedented’ energy crisis could trigger global recession as Australia prepares for G20 fuel talks
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that the U.S.-Israel war on Iran risks creating an unprecedented energy crisis that could push the global economy toward recession. Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers is preparing to attend IMF spring meetings and G20 fuel talks in Washington.

stories.title: Will the next round of US-Iran talks bring peace or more confrontation?
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiating teams could return to Islamabad for a second round of talks as early as this week, following 21 hours of negotiations that ended without a deal. Analysts say a limited settlement remains possible despite a deep deficit of trust between the two sides.

stories.title: IMF cuts China’s GDP growth forecast to 4.4% as Iran war pressures global economy
stories.summary: The IMF lowered China's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.4%, citing shocks from the US-Israeli war in Iran. The global growth projection was also cut to 3.1%, down 0.2 percentage points from the January estimate.

stories.title: How a feud with Pope Leo could hurt Trump at home
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has entered a public dispute with Pope Leo XIV over the war on Iran, immigration, and the intervention in Venezuela, raising concerns that the clash could alienate religious conservative voters ahead of US midterm elections.

stories.title: Russian drone hits commercial ship flying Liberian flag
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a commercial ship flying a Liberian flag as it traveled along a maritime corridor designated for grain transport.

stories.title: How the sewers under Nazi-occupied Ukraine gave rise to unexpected Holocaust heroes
stories.summary: A newly published war memoir by Ignacy Chiger documents how Jews survived in the sewers beneath Nazi-occupied Ukraine. The account raises questions about the Judenrat's communal responsibility versus allegations of complicity during the Holocaust.

stories.title: West Asia conflict threatens to push 2.5 million people in India into poverty: UNDP report
stories.summary: A UNDP report warns that the West Asia conflict could push up to 2.5 million people in India into poverty, a significant increase from an earlier estimate of around 400,000.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government has suspended the automatic renewal of a defence cooperation agreement with Israel, freezing military training and research ties in light of the current Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Ex-Senator Savelyev Jailed 10 Years for Conspiring to Murder Business Partner
stories.summary: Former Russian senator Dmitry Savelyev was sentenced to 10 years in prison for conspiring to murder his jailed business partner Sergei Ionov. Prosecutors alleged Savelyev paid $100,000 in August 2023 to arrange the killing.

stories.title: Bahamas police release Michigan man questioned after wife disappeared from their boat
stories.summary: Bahamian police released Brian Hooker, a Michigan man, without charges after questioning him about the disappearance of his wife Lynette from their boat. Hooker told authorities she fell overboard and was carried away by strong currents. He had been in custody since April 8.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence cooperation deal with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced the suspension of a defence cooperation agreement with Israel that covers military training and research. The Israeli Foreign Ministry downplayed the decision, saying it would have no impact on security.

stories.title: Hamas to reject disarmament in Cairo meeting as Zikim reopens
stories.summary: Hamas is expected to reject disarmament demands at a Cairo meeting with the Board of Peace over phase two of the ceasefire. Meanwhile, Gaza's Zikim crossing reopened for the first time in 40 days.

stories.title: Zelensky announces upcoming news regarding PURL program following conversation with Rutte
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy announced forthcoming updates on the PURL program following a conversation with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. The program enables Ukraine to purchase missiles for Patriot air defense systems from the United States.

stories.title: Malaysians urged to tighten their belts as Iran war fallout starts to bite
stories.summary: Malaysia's government has urged citizens to prepare for prolonged economic belt-tightening as the fallout from the Iran war disrupts global energy markets. The full impact is expected to hit by June, after domestic fuel subsidies and gas production buffers are exhausted.

stories.title: India cricket slammed for ‘Orwellian’ control of global game by Wisden
stories.summary: The UK-based Wisden Cricketers' Almanack has criticised the Board of Control for Cricket in India for what it describes as an unhealthy and politicised dominance over the global game, calling India's control 'Orwellian.'

stories.title: US is negotiating an Iran deal that would buy time, again
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly pursuing negotiations with Iran aimed at reaching a deal that would buy time rather than achieve a comprehensive resolution. This approach mirrors a historical pattern in U.S.-Iran diplomacy of seeking incremental agreements.

stories.title: Iran remains an obstacle to the ‘Greater Israel’ project
stories.summary: Iran continues to pose a significant obstacle to Israeli expansion in the Middle East. Israel's inability to defeat Iran is described as a major setback for its broader regional ambitions.

stories.title: How much will US Hormuz blockade hurt Iran, and does Tehran have an escape?
stories.summary: Iran earned approximately $5 billion in oil exports over the past month while restricting passage through the Strait of Hormuz for most other vessels. A potential US blockade of the strait could jeopardize that revenue stream.

stories.title: Who profits most from a US-Israel-Iran stalemate?
stories.summary: An analysis examines which actors stand to gain most from a prolonged US-Israel-Iran stalemate. The piece suggests that the resulting instability may serve certain strategic interests rather than being merely an unintended consequence of policy failures.

stories.title: Around 90 detained in New York City protest over US arms sales to Israel
stories.summary: Approximately 90 protesters were detained by police in New York City during demonstrations calling for a halt to US arms sales to Israel, with detainees including whistleblower Chelsea Manning and members of the anti-war group Jewish Voice for Peace.

stories.title: Magyar’s victory: what it unlocks for Ukraine—and where it stops short
stories.summary: Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar has the parliamentary majority to rewrite the constitution but has signaled limits to the changes he intends to pursue, including on Ukraine-related policy.

stories.title: Nigeria: Ex-Oil Minister Alison-Madueke Denies Bribery Charges in UK Court
stories.summary: Former Nigerian petroleum minister Diezani Alison-Madueke denied bribery and corruption charges in a UK court. She told the court she neither solicited nor received illicit payments during her time in office.

stories.title: How many ships have passed the Strait of Hormuz and how many were attacked?
stories.summary: Ship-tracking data indicates that 279 vessels have transited the Strait of Hormuz since the war on Iran began, with 22 of those ships attacked during the period.

stories.title: New Paris exhibit explores borders, from walls to algorithms
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel are set to hold their first direct diplomatic talks in decades in Washington on Tuesday, following more than a month of war between Israel and Hezbollah. The Israeli government has been described as mostly ambivalent toward the talks' outcome, though that stance may be shifting.

stories.title: Smotrich refers to Nazis as he brands Germany 'hypocrites' over Israeli settler criticism
stories.summary: Israeli far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich invoked Nazi-era references while calling Germany hypocritical over its criticism of Israeli settlements. His remarks responded to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's concerns about what Merz described as de facto annexation in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Iranian delegation claims it was 'under attack' en route to Islamabad, regime is re-arming - report
stories.summary: An Iranian delegation reportedly claimed it came under attack while traveling to Islamabad, Pakistan. Iranian regime sources stated they do not trust the United States and are actively preparing militarily for a potential future conflict.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence agreement with Israel as Lebanon attacks stoke tensions
stories.summary: Lebanon is approaching its first direct diplomatic talks with Israel in decades with "very cautious optimism," according to reports from Beirut. The Washington talks follow more than a month of war between Israel and Hezbollah that has severely impacted Lebanon.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 14 – Lebanon and Israel get talking, with shared goal to disarm Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel held direct talks in Washington, their first in decades, with a shared stated goal of disarming Hezbollah. The discussions took place on Holocaust Remembrance Day amid ongoing Iranian negotiations and regional tensions.

stories.title: Russians strike Dnipro, five people wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro, injuring five people in the attack.

stories.title: Nearly 700 reported killed in Sudan drone strikes this year
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that nearly 700 civilians have been killed in drone strikes in Sudan since January 2025. The ongoing civil war has created what the UN describes as the world's largest humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: US begins Iran port blockade, oil prices ease on hopes for dialogue
stories.summary: The United States imposed a blockade on Iran's ports, though oil prices eased on hopes that diplomatic dialogue might resume. The blockade has angered Tehran and added uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global shipping route.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel talks set to begin in Washington
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel began direct talks in Washington, marking a rare diplomatic engagement between the two countries, which have been technically at war since 1948.

stories.title: French minister seeks ban of Kanye West concert in Marseille
stories.summary: France's Interior Minister Laurent Nunez is seeking to ban US rapper Kanye West from performing at Marseille's Velodrome stadium on June 11. The move follows West's widely criticized antisemitic remarks and expressions of admiration for Adolf Hitler.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon talks: How motivated is Netanyahu to find a deal?
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government suspended Italy's defence cooperation agreement with Israel after Italian UN peacekeepers in Lebanon were reportedly targeted by Israeli warning shots. The incident has stoked tensions between Rome and Jerusalem.

stories.title: 'Very cautious optimism' as Israel-Lebanon talks set to begin
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel held their first direct diplomatic talks in decades in Washington on Tuesday. The discussions come amid ongoing conflict between Israel and the Hezbollah militant group, with the two countries technically at war since 1948.

stories.title: Hong Kong retiree gets 1 year in jail for seditious social media comments
stories.summary: A 61-year-old Hong Kong retiree, Raymond Chong Wai-man, was sentenced to one year in prison under the domestic national security law for publishing 53 seditious Facebook posts. The posts, made between March 2024 and November 2025, denigrated central and local authorities.

stories.title: Iran says a 'lack of goodwill' from the US blocked deal
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told France that a lack of US goodwill and maximalist positions blocked a deal during negotiations in Islamabad. He warned that continued military pressure would deepen regional instability.

stories.title: Should China be worried as Japan starts replacing helicopters with drones?
stories.summary: Japan's latest defense budget allocates 11.1 billion yen for five wide-area unmanned aerial vehicles to replace some attack helicopters. Chinese media outlets and analysts have warned that the drone procurement could be viewed as a hostile move.

stories.title: China’s edge over US in AI world models: abundant data, faster deployment, executive says
stories.summary: A Chinese AI executive claims China holds an advantage over the US in AI world models due to abundant data and faster deployment enabled by integration with the country's industrial base. World models simulate 3D environments and are expected to advance robotics and autonomous vehicles.

stories.title: What to know about the US blockade of Iran’s ports
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced a full blockade of Iran's southern coastline, targeting the country's port access. The blockade represents a significant escalation in the ongoing U.S.-Iran confrontation.

stories.title: Petition filed against incoming Mossad director over lack of ‘trustworthiness’
stories.summary: A petition has been filed against incoming Mossad director Roman Gofman, alleging he exploited a teenager for an army intelligence operation and showed no remorse. The petitioner argues these actions disqualify Gofman from leading the agency.

stories.title: Defense forces launch massive night attack on Crimea, substation hit in Melitopol
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces launched a large-scale overnight attack on Russian-occupied Crimea, with explosions reported near Simferopol, Feodosia, and Kerch. A substation was also hit in Melitopol in occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast.

stories.title: US prosecutors say OpenAI firebomber was trying to kill boss Sam Altman
stories.summary: U.S. federal prosecutors charged Daniel Moreno-Gama, 20, of Texas with attempting to kill OpenAI CEO Sam Altman by throwing a Molotov cocktail at his San Francisco home. Authorities said he possessed an anti-AI document.

stories.title: Thousands gather in Krakow to honor Holocaust survivors at March of the Living
stories.summary: Thousands of people gathered in Krakow, Poland, for the annual March of the Living ceremony to honor Holocaust survivors and promote education about resilience and combating hatred.

stories.title: ‘Blindsided’: US farmers strained as fertiliser costs surge on war
stories.summary: U.S. farmers face surging fertilizer costs driven by the Iran war and related disruptions to global supply chains. The price increases are hitting a key political support base for President Donald Trump.

stories.title: WATCH: Knesset holds annual ‘Every Person Has a Name’ ceremony on Holocaust Remembrance Day
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset held its annual "Every Person Has a Name" ceremony on Holocaust Remembrance Day, during which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other officials read aloud the names of family members they lost in the Holocaust.

stories.title: How a Norwegian pastor helped Jews pray in secret during the Holocaust
stories.summary: During the Holocaust, a Norwegian pastor in Trondheim helped members of the local Jewish community practice their faith in secret, forming a notable bond with the community's rabbi.

stories.title: Aurangzeb says ‘all options on table’ to replace UAE’s $3.5bn loan, weighs strategic fuel reserve
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the country is considering Eurobonds, loans from other nations, and commercial debt to replace a $3.5 billion loan facility from the UAE. He also noted the Middle East war has prompted Pakistan to consider building a strategic petroleum reserve.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia 'urging US to drop Hormuz blockade': report
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is reportedly pressuring the United States to lift its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade is also being challenged by US-sanctioned ships attempting to pass through the waterway.

stories.title: Zelensky in Syria: A new security actor in a crowded battlefield
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Syria, introducing a new security dynamic in a region where Turkey is the dominant player and Russia retains a military presence. The outreach adds a layer of geopolitical competition to Syria's already complex landscape.

stories.title: Who controls the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: A US move to block the Strait of Hormuz has escalated tensions over control of the vital waterway. The action has intensified debate over who governs access to the strait and under what conditions.

stories.title: War pushes seven in 10 Sudanese into poverty: UN official says
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that 70 percent of Sudan's population has been pushed into poverty by the war between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces. The conflict continues to drive a severe humanitarian crisis and widespread hunger.

stories.title: Sudan three years on: A generation shaped by war & displacement
stories.summary: As Sudan's civil war enters its fourth year, thousands of children remain displaced amid worsening hunger and collapsing public services. The crisis has received limited global attention despite its scale.

stories.title: Fresh diplomatic push seeks to restart US-Iran negotiations
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts are underway to restart US-Iran negotiations before a ceasefire deadline expires. Disputes over nuclear terms and the use of pressure tactics remain key obstacles.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel hold rare talks as fighting rages in Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel's ambassadors to the US held rare direct talks in Washington on Tuesday, with Beirut insisting on a ceasefire. The talks occurred as Israeli forces continued fighting around Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel to hold talks as fighting rages in Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel's ambassadors to Washington are set to hold rare talks in the US capital on Tuesday. The meeting comes as fighting continues in the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil, with Beirut pushing for a ceasefire.

stories.title: Holocaust Remembrance Day: Honoring victims and celebrating Jewish resilience
stories.summary: Yom Hashoah, Holocaust Remembrance Day, was observed with commemorations featuring personal objects, letters, and artifacts that highlight the lives lost during the Holocaust.

stories.title: IPL switch leads to two-year PSL ban for Zimbabwe’s Muzarabani
stories.summary: Zimbabwean cricketer Blessing Muzarabani has received a two-year ban from the Pakistan Super League after switching from Islamabad United to India's Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.

stories.title: Russians strike Kryvyi Rih infrastructure again, causing fire
stories.summary: Russian forces struck infrastructure in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk region, for the second time within hours, causing a fire at the impact site.

stories.title: “We will provide the loan one way or another” — Brussels moves on €90B Ukraine package
stories.summary: The European Commission is targeting the second quarter of 2026 for the first disbursement from a €90 billion loan package for Ukraine. Three legal documents must still be finalized before funds can be released.

stories.title: Italy suspends defence agreement with Israel
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced the suspension of Italy's defence cooperation agreement with Israel, pausing military equipment deals and joint research. Meloni cited current conditions as the reason for halting the agreement's automatic renewal.

stories.title: Haiti: Several police arrested over stampede which killed 25
stories.summary: Haitian authorities have arrested several individuals, including five police officers, in connection with a stampede that killed 25 people at a former military citadel in the north of the country.

stories.title: Russian man who survived 2 months adrift in the Sea of Okhotsk is sentenced to forced labor in relatives’ deaths
stories.summary: A court in Ulan-Ude, Russia's Buryatia region, convicted Mikhail Pichugin in connection with the deaths of two relatives and sentenced him to three years of forced labor. Pichugin had previously survived two months adrift in the Sea of Okhotsk.

stories.title: US-Philippines ties enter ‘more mature’ phase with planned fuel depot
stories.summary: The United States is planning to build a fuel depot in the southern Philippines to support humanitarian and maritime security missions, marking what observers describe as a more mature phase in the US-Philippine alliance in the Western Pacific.

stories.title: Cameroon separatists to pause fighting ahead of Pope visit
stories.summary: Separatist groups in Cameroon's Anglophone regions announced a temporary ceasefire ahead of an upcoming visit by the Pope, citing responsibility, restraint, and respect for human dignity as reasons for the pause in fighting.

stories.title: Sixteen injured in rare Turkey school shooting in Siverek district
stories.summary: An 18-year-old former student opened fire at Ahmet Koyuncu Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in the Siverek district of Şanlıurfa province, Turkey, on April 14, 2026. Sixteen people were injured in the rare school shooting.

stories.title: Turkey school shooting wounds 16, attacker dead
stories.summary: A former student opened fire at a school in Şanlıurfa, Turkey, wounding 16 people including students and teachers. The attacker killed himself as police responded to the scene.

stories.title: Hegseth right to mock Royal Navy, says ex-army chief as he backs claims over military underfunding – UK politics live
stories.summary: Former British Army chief Richard Barrons backed former NATO head George Robertson's criticism of UK military underfunding, saying British forces are "too small and undernourished for the world that we now live in." The comments came amid broader debate about UK defence spending priorities.

stories.title: Fighting continues near Mariine: Tregubov says Russian forces have advanced into Sumy region
stories.summary: Russian troops advanced near the village of Myropillia in Ukraine's Sumy region, though fighting continues in the Mariine area. Ukrainian spokesperson Tregubov stated that Russian forces have not reached Novodmytrivka.

stories.title: 'AI tsunami is here': Israel must invest in AI to stay competitive - opinion
stories.summary: Professor Lior Rokach, selected to join a UN panel monitoring artificial intelligence, urged Israel to increase investment in AI to maintain competitiveness. Rokach described the current moment as an "AI tsunami" requiring immediate action.

stories.title: Russia’s parliament approves bill imposing fines for depicting churches without crosses
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma committee on constitutional legislation approved a bill imposing fines for depicting religious buildings without their traditional symbols, such as churches shown without crosses.

stories.title: Russia and UAE minister call for immediate ceasefire in Gulf
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan held a phone call Tuesday urging an immediate ceasefire in the Gulf. They discussed the aftermath of the failed US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad.

stories.title: Trump’s genocidal threat to Iran and an elusive deal
stories.summary: The article discusses US President Trump's threats against Iran and the challenges of reaching a diplomatic agreement amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: U.S.-Iran tensions persist as diplomacy struggles to keep pace
stories.summary: Efforts to arrange a second round of US-Iran talks are underway, but escalating threats around the Strait of Hormuz continue to endanger a fragile ceasefire. The tensions are also rattling global markets.

stories.title: How the Negev desert became Israel's unlikely global tech powerhouse
stories.summary: Israel's Negev desert region is emerging as a global technology hub, hosting developments in cybersecurity and climate technology. The area is being transformed into an international laboratory for innovative solutions.

stories.title: Israel leads in tech innovation, not in gender inclusion - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that despite Israel's global leadership in technology innovation, the country significantly lags in gender inclusion within its tech sector.

stories.title: Breaking barriers: Israeli women expand opportunities in STEM and hi-tech
stories.summary: A report highlights efforts by Israeli women to expand opportunities in STEM fields and the hi-tech sector, focusing on initiatives aimed at breaking barriers and increasing female representation in technology industries.

stories.title: Middle East war revs up electric car demand in Asia
stories.summary: Electric vehicle sales surged across Southeast Asia as consumers sought to avoid fuel price spikes driven by the Middle East war. Vietnamese EV maker VinFast and Chinese manufacturers have benefited from the shift as crude oil shipments to Asian nations declined sharply.

stories.title: 'Pipe dream': Turkey's plan to redraw Middle East energy routes after Iran
stories.summary: Turkey is exploring plans to reroute Middle East energy flows in the wake of the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Proposed pipelines from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Turkmenistan could position Turkey as a regional energy hub, though analysts remain skeptical.

stories.title: Zelenskyy in Berlin: Germany pledges air defense, long-range weapons and ammunition in new aid packages
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, where the two signed defense cooperation agreements. Germany pledged new aid packages including air defense systems, long-range weapons, drones, and ammunition.

stories.title: PSX recovers over 4,000 points during intraday trade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index surged over 4,100 points during intraday trading on Tuesday, recovering from a 6,600-point drop the previous day that was triggered by panic-selling amid inconclusive Iran-U.S. peace talks.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills 1 in Lipetsk Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on the city of Yelets in Russia's Lipetsk region killed one person and hospitalized four others with injuries.

stories.title: Nigeria: Karauye - Gang Violence Puts Katsina Metropolis On Edge
stories.summary: Gang violence in the Katsina metropolis of northern Nigeria continues to put residents on edge despite repeated government and security pledges to address the problem. Cases of gang-related crime remain rampant in the state.

stories.title: Survivors ask why Nigeria bombed busy market in effort to target jihadist group
stories.summary: Survivors and observers are questioning the Nigerian military's justification for an airstrike on Jilli market near the Borno-Yobe state border that killed as many as 200 people, many of them civilians. The military described the Saturday attack, which targeted a jihadist group, as a "precision airstrike."

stories.title: Nigeria: Akande Tells President to Impose Consequences On Security, Military Chiefs Who Don't Deliver
stories.summary: Former Nigerian presidential spokesperson Laolu Akande called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to impose consequences on underperforming security and military chiefs. Akande warned that continued failures undermine public confidence and national security.

stories.title: Nigeria: Again, Court Adjourns El-Rufai's Bail Ruling
stories.summary: A Kaduna State High Court in Nigeria has adjourned a bail ruling in the corruption case brought by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission against former governor Nasir El-Rufai.

stories.title: Senegal: Digital Radicalisation in Senegal - Early Warning of an Evolving Terror Threat
stories.summary: A report by the Institute for Security Studies warns that jihadist digital radicalization is a growing threat in southeastern Senegal. It recommends integrating the digital dimension into the country's terrorism prevention strategies.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia President Meets Chinese Delegation to Boost Security, Trade Ties
stories.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud met a senior Chinese delegation in Mogadishu to discuss security, peace, and trade, aiming to strengthen bilateral relations between Somalia and China.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gov Lawal Approves 120-Day Intervention Plan for Zamfara Education
stories.summary: Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal approved a 120-day Rapid Intervention Action Plan to address critical failures in the state's education sector. The plan targets systemic issues plaguing schools across Zamfara in northern Nigeria.

stories.title: Former Donetsk separatist official detained in St. Petersburg on charges of discrediting the Russian military
stories.summary: Russian authorities detained Alexander Vaskovsky, a former official of the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic and Telegram blogger, in St. Petersburg on April 13 on charges of discrediting the Russian military.

stories.title: Dozens detained in New York City protest over US arms sales to Israel
stories.summary: Dozens of protesters were detained by police in New York City on Monday during demonstrations against U.S. arms sales to Israel. The demonstrators called for an end to American military support for Israel.

stories.title: Anger at ‘bloody unacceptable’ efforts to end Sudan’s war as conflict enters fourth year
stories.summary: The UN's top official in Sudan, Denise Brown, criticized the international community's response to the country's civil war as "unacceptable" on the eve of the conflict's third anniversary. The war has displaced 14 million Sudanese and is described as the world's largest humanitarian crisis, with tens of thousands missing.

stories.title: War, AI, and innovation: Inside the new world order – from the editor
stories.summary: An editorial discussed how artificial intelligence, shifting global alliances, and modern warfare are reshaping geopolitics. Topics covered included AI-driven conflict, energy security, and broader societal impacts.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces pull back to prepared lines near Myropilske as Russia claims ground in three Sumy villages
stories.summary: Russian forces advanced near three settlements in Ukraine's Sumy Oblast as Ukrainian troops pulled back to prepared defensive lines near Myropilske. Russian military recruitment reportedly fell 20% in the first quarter of 2026, while confirmed Russian deaths rose to 25,000.

stories.title: Secretive Bilderberg group just met – but who knows what global elite said?
stories.summary: The 72nd meeting of the Bilderberg group was held over the weekend at the Salamander hotel in Washington, DC. The secretive policy conference brought together prime ministers, military leaders, tech billionaires, and investment company heads behind a security cordon.

stories.title: ‘Nothing but tree skeletons’: record-breaking wildfires devastate US cattle country
stories.summary: Record-breaking wildfires scorched more than a million acres across Nebraska's Great Plains this spring, devastating cattle country. Rising temperatures and extreme drought drove the fires, obliterating annual acreage-burned records in a single month.

stories.title: China hits out at ‘dangerous and irresponsible’ US blockade of Iran’s ports
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry condemned the US naval blockade of Iranian ports as 'dangerous and irresponsible,' calling for an immediate ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, warning that the action could escalate regional tensions.

stories.title: Rheinmetall and Destinus to combine forces in new missile systems joint venture
stories.summary: German defense firm Rheinmetall and aerospace company Destinus have announced a joint venture to develop new missile systems. Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger stated the partnership aims to expand Europe's industrial base for modern defense systems.

stories.title: Global oil demand to plunge amid disruptions caused by war on Iran: IEA
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency warned that global oil demand is set to plunge due to disruptions caused by the war on Iran. The IEA's report on demand destruction followed statements that unnamed countries have been hoarding oil stocks.

stories.title: 24 settlements hit in Kharkiv region: one woman killed, 20 injured over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian attacks hit 24 settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region over a 24-hour period on April 13, killing one woman and injuring 20 other people.

stories.title: Hegseth announces 'major' defence partnership with Indonesia
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a major defense partnership with Indonesia aimed at boosting military cooperation and stability in the Indo-Pacific region.

stories.title: Israel’s ambassador to Germany assails Smotrich for attack on chancellor
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador to Germany Ron Prosor rebuked Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich for telling German Chancellor Friedrich Merz "you will not force us into ghettos again." The rare diplomatic criticism came after Merz voiced concerns about Israeli policy on Holocaust memorial day.

stories.title: UK’s finance minister criticises Washington as Hormuz disruption fuels economic worries
stories.summary: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves criticized Washington over the war with Iran, expressing frustration at the lack of a clear US exit strategy. She warned the Strait of Hormuz disruption is worsening economic conditions for the UK.

stories.title: Reform activist suspended over racist and antisemitic comments remains election agent
stories.summary: A Reform UK activist named Adam Mitula, previously suspended over racist and antisemitic comments, has been named as election agent for three of the party's candidates in the Tameside area of Manchester ahead of May 7 local elections. Mitula confirmed his suspension as a party member "pending investigation" in February.

stories.title: Liberia: Airport Revolt Brewing - Unpaid Workers Threaten to Shut Down Monrovia's Domestic Airport As Salary Arrears Spark Anger and Corruption Questions
stories.summary: Workers at the James Spriggs Payne Airport in Monrovia, Liberia, are threatening to shut down operations over months of unpaid salaries. The dispute has raised questions about leadership and financial accountability within the Liberia Airport Authority.

stories.title: Detention of journalist in Kuwait raises questions about crackdown on freedom of speech
stories.summary: Journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin, a US-born Kuwaiti national, was arrested in Kuwait on March 3 after reporting on a friendly fire incident involving a US Air Force aircraft. The Committee to Protect Journalists raised concerns about the detention as part of a broader crackdown on press freedom in the Middle East during the US-Israel war with Iran.

stories.title: Swedish, Polish firms invest in TNT plants to quench Europe’s ammo thirst
stories.summary: Swedish firm Swebal is building a new factory capable of producing more than 4,000 metric tons of TNT annually, as Swedish and Polish companies invest in ammunition production to address Europe's growing demand. Russia is estimated to produce approximately 50,000 tons of TNT per year.

stories.title: Woman killed, 5 injured as Ukrainian drones strike Russia
stories.summary: A woman was killed when Ukrainian drones struck the city of Yelets in Russia's Lipetsk region, according to Governor Igor Artamonov. Five other people were reported injured in the attacks.

stories.title: Ice hockey coach admits to faking COVID certificate to enter China Olympics
stories.summary: A Swiss ice hockey coach admitted to using a fake COVID-19 certificate to gain entry to the Olympic Games in China. The revelation raises questions for Swiss Ice Hockey ahead of hosting the World Championships in May.

stories.title: China's Xi says rule of law must be upheld for Middle East peace
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for upholding the rule of law as essential for Middle East peace. Xi criticized the US-Israel war on Iran while deepening strategic ties with the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Sixteen injured after ex-student opens fire at high school in Turkey
stories.summary: A former student opened fire at a high school in southeastern Turkey, injuring sixteen people including students and teachers.

stories.title: What we know about US-hosted talks between Israel and Lebanon
stories.summary: Officials from Lebanon and Israel met in the United States on Tuesday for talks. The US-hosted discussions mark a rare direct diplomatic engagement between the two countries.

stories.title: US, Iran negotiating teams could return to Islamabad this week after talks stall - report
stories.summary: A source reported that a proposal has been shared with both the US and Iran to send their negotiating teams back to Islamabad this week. The move follows the stalling of talks that failed to produce a deal over the weekend.

stories.title: Public universities admit 65 non-local DSE pupils last year, a fivefold jump since 2022
stories.summary: Hong Kong's public universities admitted 65 non-local students with Diploma of Secondary Education qualifications last year, a fivefold increase since 2022, while local DSE-qualified admissions fell by 5 percent over the same period.

stories.title: Cameroon's Catholics fear papal visit could pay political dividends for President Biya
stories.summary: Some Catholics in Cameroon have expressed concern that the anticipated papal visit could be leveraged by longtime President Paul Biya to improve his public image, coming six months after deadly protests following his contested re-election.

stories.title: Moscow student gets 10 days in jail for throwing shoe at Lenin’s sarcophagus
stories.summary: A Moscow court sentenced an 18-year-old college student to 10 days in jail after he struck Vladimir Lenin's sarcophagus and threw a shoe at it during a visit to the mausoleum on Red Square.

stories.title: Liberia: CDC Rejects Weedor Nomination, Warns of Electoral Risk - Unveils Parallel Elections Team
stories.summary: Liberia's opposition Congress for Democratic Change has rejected the nomination of Jonathan K. Weedor as chairman of the National Elections Commission, calling the move dangerous and a breach of public trust, and has announced a parallel elections team.

stories.title: Kenya: MPs Raise Alarm Over Rise of Political Gangs Ahead of 2027 General Election
stories.summary: A Kenyan parliamentary committee has raised alarm over the growing use of organised political gangs, warning that the trend poses a serious national security threat ahead of the 2027 general election.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon direct talks in the US: All to know
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon held their first direct talks since 1993, brokered by the United States. Hezbollah's rejection of the process threatens to undermine the diplomatic effort.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone regiment takes out Russian fuel tanker, logistics hub deep in occupied Donetsk, Melitopol, Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Raid drone regiment struck Russian logistics targets in occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast, including a fuel tanker. Additional overnight drone strikes hit Melitopol and caused explosions across Russian-occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Iran slams US blockade as ‘grave violation of sovereignty’
stories.summary: Iran condemned the U.S. naval blockade as a grave violation of its sovereignty. President Trump warned that any Iranian boats challenging the blockade would be destroyed.

stories.title: War pushes poverty in Sudan to 70 percent, UN warns
stories.summary: A senior United Nations official has warned that nearly 70 percent of Sudan's population is now living in poverty, almost double pre-war levels, as ongoing conflict continues to devastate the country's economy and social fabric.

stories.title: Russian court sentences former senator to 10 years in prison for attempted murder of business partner
stories.summary: A Russian court sentenced former senator Dmitry Savelyev to 10 years in a high-security penal colony for the attempted murder of his former business partner Sergei Ionov, as reported by Mediazona.

stories.title: Prosecutors demand copy of Shin Bet head’s letter on PM’s inability to testify
stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors demanded a copy of a letter from the Shin Bet security service head regarding Prime Minister Netanyahu's inability to testify publicly. The letter reportedly warns that Iranian agents could exploit a public appearance to harm Netanyahu.

stories.title: South Korea warns Hormuz tensions to prolong energy and supply shocks
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung warned that escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz will prolong disruptions to global energy supplies and supply chains. He called for urgent diversification of energy supply routes.

stories.title: Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey pleads not guilty to new rape charges
stories.summary: Ghanaian footballer Thomas Partey has pleaded not guilty to two new rape charges in a court proceeding.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan's War On Women - Sexual Violence Support Needs Quadruple As Abuse Becomes War Blueprint
stories.summary: UN Women has warned that sexual violence has become a defining feature of Sudan's war as it enters its fourth year, with support needs for survivors quadrupling. The agency called for accountability, protection of women and girls, and increased funding for women-led response efforts.

stories.title: Central Africa: Aid, Movements Hindered in South Kivu Highlands
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch has reported that warring parties in the South Kivu highlands of the Democratic Republic of Congo are hindering humanitarian aid delivery and threatening the protection of civilians.

stories.title: Iran slams YouTube ban on pro-Iranian group’s Lego-style AI videos
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned YouTube's removal of AI-generated Lego-style videos produced by a pro-Iranian group. A ministry spokesman said the ban was intended to suppress information about the war on Iran.

stories.title: Residents of Iraqi Kurdistan in despair: 'We weren't at war with anyone'
stories.summary: Residents of Iraqi Kurdistan have endured approximately 700 drone and missile attacks targeting US positions and Kurdish interests over a month and a half. A civilian was killed in a drone attack blamed on Iran just 24 hours before a ceasefire. Residents expressed devastation at being caught as indirect victims of the US-Iran war.

stories.title: BP hails ‘exceptional’ trading as oil prices soar in Iran war
stories.summary: BP expects to report "exceptional" oil trading earnings driven by volatile energy markets caused by the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Citi analysts upgraded BP's profit forecast by 20 percent to $2.6 billion for the first quarter despite flat oil and gas production.

stories.title: Who still reads Holocaust stories? A publisher sees shifting trends after October 7
stories.summary: A Dutch publisher focused on Holocaust memoirs reports declining demand for such works amid rising antisemitism and changing consumer patterns. The shift has intensified since the events of October 7.

stories.title: Asia’s energy supply at breaking point as US blockades Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States imposed a naval blockade on the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Iran into accepting a deal to end the ongoing Iran war. The move has threatened Asia's energy supply, with peace talks stalled and no timeline for resuming oil flows. Iran responded by threatening all ports in the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Nigeria: Six Months Enough to Tackle Insecurity If FG Is Serious - Ndume
stories.summary: Nigerian Senator Ali Ndume, representing Borno South, stated that the country's insecurity could be decisively tackled within six months if the federal government demonstrates sufficient commitment.

stories.title: Liberia: 'You'll Be Defeated' - CDC Chairman Janga Kowo Warns Boakai-Led Government
stories.summary: Janga Kowo, chairman of Liberia's opposition Congress for Democratic Change, warned that the ruling Unity Party under President Boakai has failed the Liberian people and predicted it will be voted out in the 2029 elections.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon envoys meet in US for historic Hezbollah disarmament talks
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors met in Washington, D.C., for talks on disarming Hezbollah and advancing a peace framework, with the United States serving as mediator focused on ensuring Israel's long-term security.

stories.title: EU to cut funding for Chinese inverters as quiet offensive replaces grandstanding
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen approved a plan in March to block EU funds from going to clean technology projects using Chinese-made inverters. Chinese companies, led by Huawei Technologies, are estimated to control over 220 gigawatts of Europe's installed solar capacity through these power electronics devices.

stories.title: Horse swept away in a fast-moving flood in Illinois rescued after eight hours
stories.summary: A horse named Troy was rescued in Illinois after being swept from a barn by floodwaters and stranded approximately 600 feet from shore in Coon Creek, about 60 miles northwest of Chicago. Marengo fire and rescue crews built a makeshift raft to bring the horse safely to shore after an eight-hour operation.

stories.title: Kazakh sovereign fund issues Central Asia’s first panda bond in ‘milestone’ sale
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's sovereign wealth fund, Samruk-Kazyna, sold 3 billion yuan (US$440 million) in panda bonds on China's interbank market, marking Central Asia's first yuan-denominated debt issuance. The sale comes as global investors seek safe havens amid geopolitical uncertainties including the Iran war.

stories.title: Love and compassion in China: Moroccan student saves drowning woman, long-ago pen pals reunite
stories.summary: Ayoub Fadil, a 21-year-old Moroccan student at Hangzhou Dianzi University in Zhejiang province, rescued a drowning woman from Jinsha Lake on April 6. Local residents and authorities in Hangzhou hailed him as a hero and presented him with an award for his actions.

stories.title: World leaders and Israeli officials mark Holocaust Remembrance Day with calls to fight antisemitism
stories.summary: World leaders and Israeli officials marked Holocaust Remembrance Day with statements calling for continued efforts against antisemitism. Some Israeli public figures chose to address current events in connection with the commemoration rather than issuing standalone statements.

stories.title: Sanctioned tankers transit Strait of Hormuz amid US blockade
