stories.summary: The Chinese-owned tanker Rich Starry became the first US-sanctioned vessel to transit the Strait of Hormuz and exit the Persian Gulf since the American blockade began. The passage tests US enforcement of its restrictions on Iranian-linked shipping.

stories.title: Ukraine spent a year beating wartime inflation. A different war just reversed it.
stories.summary: Ukraine's fuel costs surged 23% in March as the Middle East war drove prices above central bank forecasts, reversing a year of progress against wartime inflation and putting a potential rate hike on the table.

stories.title: Ukraine was beating inflation. Then oil prices rose.
stories.summary: Ukraine's fuel costs surged 23% in March as the Middle East conflict pushed oil prices above the central bank's forecast. A potential interest rate hike is now under consideration to address rising inflation.

stories.title: Russians kill one and wound three in Donetsk region over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian forces killed one civilian and wounded three others in Ukraine's Donetsk region over a 24-hour period on April 13.

stories.title: Nigeria: Northern Leaders Raise Concerns Over Rising Attacks
stories.summary: Northern Nigerian leaders have voiced concern over rising terrorist attacks in the region, noting that violence persists despite the presence of a special US military security assistance team.

stories.title: Pakistan launches medical tourism initiative under Special Investment Facilitation Council
stories.summary: Pakistan formally launched a National Medical Tourism Initiative under the Special Investment Facilitation Council, announced during the 30th annual conference of the Pakistan Association of Plastic Surgeons in Islamabad.

stories.title: Police officers among seven arrested over deadly Haiti stampede
stories.summary: Police officers are among seven people arrested in connection with a deadly stampede at Haiti's Laferrière Citadel on Saturday that killed 25 people. An investigation into the cause of the incident is underway.

stories.title: Australia touts first GMLRS artillery rocket assembled Down Under
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin's Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System (GMLRS) artillery rocket has been assembled in Australia for the first time. The rocket is a flagship project of Australia's Guided Weapons and Explosive Ordnance Enterprise, which aims to build domestic strike weapon manufacturing capability.

stories.title: Israeli settlers storm Al-Aqsa mosque under Israeli forces’ protection
stories.summary: Approximately 120 Israeli settlers entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in occupied East Jerusalem on Tuesday under the protection of Israeli forces. The Jerusalem Governorate reported the incursion.

stories.title: Harry and Meghan mix charity and business on Australia visit
stories.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are visiting Australia, combining charity engagements with business activities, while questions have been raised about whether local taxpayers are covering any policing costs for the visit.

stories.title: Colombia approves plan to cull roaming hippos linked to Pablo Escobar
stories.summary: Colombian officials authorized a plan on Monday to cull dozens of hippos roaming freely in a central region of the country. The animals, which threaten villagers and displace native species, descend from hippos originally brought to Colombia by drug lord Pablo Escobar.

stories.title: US and Iran keep talking as Trump's blockade takes effect
stories.summary: President Trump said Iran "badly" wants to make a deal as the US blockade of Iranian ports took effect Monday and a fragile ceasefire held. High-stakes talks between the US and Iran in Islamabad had ended without agreement over the weekend.

stories.title: Colombia's Petro walks back 100% tariffs on Ecuadorean goods
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro reversed a previous announcement and said Colombia would not impose 100 percent tariffs on imports from Ecuador. The trade ministry had announced the tariffs the prior week.

stories.title: Ex-Nigeria oil boss denies £2M bribe claims in London court
stories.summary: Former Nigerian oil minister Diezani Alison-Madueke testified before a London court, denying allegations that she accepted approximately £2 million in bribes while serving in office.

stories.title: Fujimori leads chaotic Peru vote as election officials arrested over delays
stories.summary: Conservative candidate Keiko Fujimori led Peru's first round of presidential voting on Sunday amid widespread logistical failures that delayed polling center openings. Police raided the headquarters of the National Office of Electoral Processes and detained an election official over the delays.

stories.title: Standing with Our Soldiers - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Institute of Justice provides free legal aid to Israel Defense Forces soldiers. The organization describes itself as the only group offering such services.

stories.title: 'Shocking attack': Italian press reacts to Trump's feud with pope
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted and later deleted an AI-generated image depicting himself as a Jesus-like figure, drawing widespread criticism. The incident occurred amid his escalating feud with Pope Leo, who has criticized the US-Israeli strikes on Iran as inhumane. Italian press reacted strongly to the confrontation.

stories.title: Around 100 pro-Palestinian protesters detained at New York demo
stories.summary: Around 100 pro-Palestinian demonstrators were detained at a protest in New York City. The protesters demanded an end to US arms sales to Israel amid the Gaza war, strikes on Iran, and a broader crackdown on pro-Palestinian activism.

stories.title: 'Total dehumanisation': French former hostages in Iran give interview
stories.summary: French citizens Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris gave their first television interview after returning to France following nearly four years of detention in Iran on espionage charges. The pair described their experience in captivity and how they sustained hope during imprisonment.

stories.title: Air defense downs missile and 114 drones launched by Russia since evening
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted one guided missile and 114 drones launched by Russia in an attack that began on the evening of April 13.

stories.title: Sudan drone strikes kill nearly 700 in three months as civil war reaches grim milestone
stories.summary: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher reported that nearly 700 civilians have been killed by drone strikes in Sudan in the first three months of the year. The civil war, now in its third year, has killed tens of thousands and displaced more than 11 million people.

stories.title: China's exports slow amid surging costs brought on by Iran war
stories.summary: China's export growth slowed to 2.5% year-on-year in March, down sharply due to disruptions from the war in Iran. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has driven up material costs, squeezing profit margins for Chinese factories.

stories.title: Gunman at Turkey high school wounds 16 before killing himself
stories.summary: An 18-year-old former student armed with a shotgun opened fire at a vocational high school in Siverek, Sanliurfa province, in southeastern Turkey on Tuesday, wounding 16 people. The victims included 10 students, four teachers, a canteen employee, and a police officer. The attacker killed himself after being cornered by police, according to Governor Hasan Sildak.

stories.title: Sirens halt Israel for Holocaust Remembrance Day as antisemitism surges
stories.summary: Israel observed Holocaust Remembrance Day on 14 April 2026 with a nationwide two-minute silence, while ceremonies at the Yad Vashem memorial took place amid growing concern over a global rise in antisemitic incidents.

stories.title: War on Iran: Why the Islamabad talks failed
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, ended without a breakthrough. Analysis suggests the talks were characterized by the Trump administration attempting to impose demands rather than engage in genuine negotiation.

stories.title: China calls US blockade of Iranian ports ‘dangerous and irresponsible’
stories.summary: China condemned the US blockade of Iranian ports as "dangerous and irresponsible." Spokesperson Guo Jiakun warned the action risks deepening regional instability and threatening maritime security despite the temporary ceasefire.

stories.title: The Gulf’s Phoney Ceasefire
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab titled "The Gulf's Phoney Ceasefire," commenting on the current regional situation.

stories.title: When the Bolsheviks said ‘nyet’
stories.summary: Pakistan hosted landmark talks between Iran and the United States last week. The article traces the historical colonial backdrop involving Britain's imperial activities across the Middle East and South Asia, contextualizing the current diplomatic efforts within a longer geopolitical trajectory spanning two World Wars and numerous regime changes.

stories.title: Russia’s Lavrov visits China as US pressures Iran with Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov visited China as the United States maintained its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Both Russia and China have criticized the US-Israel military campaign against Iran, which is an ally of both nations.

stories.title: Live on Sunday: Declaration of Independence at the Kotel - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A gathering at the egalitarian section of the Western Wall in Jerusalem is planned for Sunday. Jews from Israel and abroad will read Israel's Declaration of Independence to affirm shared values.

stories.title: War update: 125 combat engagements on frontline over past day
stories.summary: A total of 125 combat engagements between Ukrainian Defense Forces and Russian troops were recorded along the front line on April 13.

stories.title: UN warns 8 million in Asia-Pacific risk poverty if Iran war drags on
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that more than 8 million people across the Asia-Pacific could be pushed into poverty if the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continue. The UN forecasts job losses, inflation, and food insecurity, with the poorest nations most exposed to the oil supply shock.

stories.title: Xi calls on Spain to jointly resist ‘law of the jungle’ in a turbulent world
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met visiting Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez in Beijing on Tuesday, calling on both nations to resist "the law of the jungle" and defend multilateralism. Both sides condemned US-Israel military actions on Iran and criticized the US blockade of Iranian ports. Sanchez is on his fourth visit and a five-day trip to China.

stories.title: Nepal’s trekking trade looks east as Iran war disrupts Western tourist flow
stories.summary: Nepal's tourism industry is experiencing a sharp decline in Western visitors during the peak spring trekking season due to travel disruptions linked to the Iran war. Arrivals from the Americas and Europe dropped by nearly 25 percent and 19 percent respectively in March. Operators are pivoting toward Asia-Pacific markets to offset the losses.

stories.title: It’s far from over
stories.summary: The United States and Iran held hours-long negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, over the weekend but ended without a public breakthrough. International media reactions were mixed, with some declaring the talks a failure and others viewing them as a potential starting point for further dialogue.

stories.title: Made lot of progress, ball in Iran’s court: Vance
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance said significant progress was made during the 21-hour marathon talks with Iran in Islamabad but stated the ball was now in Tehran's court. Washington indicated that Tehran refused to relinquish its right to enrich nuclear fuel, preventing an agreement.

stories.title: Foreign Minister Sybiha urges to unblock the €90 billion loan as Brussels waits for Magyar to take office
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha urged EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas to unblock the €90 billion loan for Ukraine following Viktor Orbán's electoral defeat in Hungary. The transition to incoming leader Péter Magyar is not expected until May.

stories.title: China Evergrande’s billionaire boss pleads guilty to fraud
stories.summary: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty to charges including fundraising fraud at a court in Shenzhen, China. The former steelworker turned billionaire expressed remorse during trial proceedings following the collapse of the world's most indebted property developer.

stories.title: Israel envoy protests Japanese TV commentator’s remarks about Kushner’s Jewish identity
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to Japan and the Simon Wiesenthal Centre condemned a Japanese political commentator for remarks on a morning news programme suggesting Jared Kushner should not be involved in Iran negotiations because he is Jewish. Kushner had joined Vice-President J.D. Vance and envoy Steve Witkoff in Islamabad for talks on ending the US-Israel-Iran war.

stories.title: Seven arrested in Haiti as stampede toll revised to 25
stories.summary: Seven people were arrested in Haiti after a stampede at the Citadelle Henri during a traditional festival. The death toll from the incident was revised to 25, with exceptionally large crowds reported at the event.

stories.title: DSE citizenship exam tests students on social awareness and national principles
stories.summary: Approximately 50,300 Hong Kong students sat the citizenship and social development paper for the Diploma of Secondary Education exams on Tuesday. The exam covered the "One Country, Two Systems" principle and contemporary topics including e-commerce and online influencers. Educators noted shifts in the paper's content compared to previous years.

stories.title: World faces food ‘catastrophe’ if Strait of Hormuz disruption persists: FAO
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization warned that continued disruption of the Strait of Hormuz could trigger a global food catastrophe. The FAO said global agriculture is highly vulnerable to waterway blockages, risking surging commodity prices and food inflation.

stories.title: What hopes for Lebanon-Israel talks as Hezbollah urges cancellation?
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli representatives are scheduled to meet in Washington on Tuesday for US-mediated talks aimed at ending the war in Lebanon. Hezbollah has rejected the negotiations, stating it will not abide by any resulting agreements and calling for their cancellation.

stories.title: US naval blockade begins as Trump vows will destroy Iran boats that approach
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned that any Iranian fast-attack vessels approaching the US maritime blockade of Iran would be destroyed. The US naval blockade on vessels entering and departing Iran took effect at 1400 GMT on Monday.

stories.title: Blow hot, blow cold
stories.summary: Following the departure of U.S. and Iranian delegations from Islamabad without a deal, President Donald Trump posted aggressive statements on social media. The article notes that Trump's threatening rhetoric risks undermining ongoing behind-the-scenes diplomatic efforts to resolve the U.S.-Iran dispute.

stories.title: 'No glimmer of hope': Little optimism among Lebanon's displaced as talks with Israel begin
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli delegations are set to hold US-mediated talks in Washington on Tuesday to negotiate an end to the conflict in Lebanon. Hezbollah has declared it will not honor any agreements from the negotiations and has demanded their cancellation.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Trump vows U.S. will sink any Iran boats that challenge blockade
stories.summary: President Donald Trump vowed that the U.S. military would sink any Iranian boats challenging its naval blockade. Iran responded with threats against ports in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, raising the prospect of a direct military confrontation.

stories.title: Russian drones hit civilian and port infrastructure in Odesa region, causing damage
stories.summary: Russian drones struck civilian and port infrastructure in Ukraine's southern Odesa region overnight on April 14, causing damage.

stories.title: Two ships from Iran ports pass Hormuz Strait despite US blockade
stories.summary: Two ships departing from Iranian ports passed through the Strait of Hormuz despite a U.S. military blockade. Separately, Lebanon and Israel are scheduled to meet in the United States for truce negotiations.

stories.title: Pakistan pitches new US-Iran talks, as Lebanon, Israel to meet
stories.summary: Pakistani officials proposed hosting a second round of US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad. Separately, Lebanese and Israeli representatives are scheduled to meet in the United States amid ongoing hostilities.

stories.title: Pakistan Medical Association demands halt to law allowing technicians to practise independently
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical Association warned that the Allied Health Professionals Council Act creates a dangerous legal loophole by allowing medical technicians to practice independently without supervision, calling it "legalised quackery."

stories.title: Election Commission issues fresh schedule for assembly elections in GB
stories.summary: The Gilgit-Baltistan Election Commission issued a revised schedule for assembly elections, with nomination papers accepted from April 16 to 20 and polling set for June 7, 2026. Local government elections are scheduled for June 14.

stories.title: Russia is quietly expelling anyone in occupied Luhansk who didn’t take a Russian passport
stories.summary: Russian authorities deported 570 residents of occupied Luhansk Oblast in 2025 for not holding Russian passports. Reports indicate deportation lists are maintained in every local municipality across the occupied territory.

stories.title: Israeli envoy calls Italian magazine antisemitic over settler violence coverage
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to Italy accused the Italian magazine L'Espresso of antisemitism over its front-page coverage of Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank. The ambassador faced online mockery following the remarks.

stories.title: HSBC says Iran war is hitting confidence as businesses warn over economic risks
stories.summary: HSBC's Lebanon-born CEO Georges Elhedery expressed concern at a Hong Kong conference about the Iran war's impact on global economic confidence. The bank's chair identified oil-driven inflation as a major challenge, lifting inflation and depressing growth worldwide.

stories.title: China turns to central Asia as US blockade in Hormuz chokes global energy flows
stories.summary: Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang is traveling to Turkmenistan for a three-day visit to attend the groundbreaking of the fourth phase of the Galkynysh gas field and a bilateral cooperation meeting. The visit reflects China's push to secure Central Asian energy supplies as the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts global shipping routes.

stories.title: Russian forces strike energy facilities in Mykolaiv region, leaving three settlements without power
stories.summary: Russian Shahed-131/136-type drones hit energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, knocking out power to three settlements.

stories.title: How Iran, suffering under sanctions, diversified its economy
stories.summary: The article examines how Iran diversified its economy while enduring prolonged international sanctions. While sanctions have significantly damaged Iran's economy, they have not broken it, with Tehran finding ways to adapt.

stories.title: Russia is using deported Ukrainian children as negotiating leverage, Foreign Minister told UN envoy
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha told a UN envoy that Russia is erasing the identities of deported Ukrainian children and using them as leverage in negotiations. Up to 300,000 children remain unaccounted for.

stories.title: Taylor’s Trumpian immigration pitch is aimed at fighting One Nation – but puts Australia’s identity at stake
stories.summary: Australian Coalition leader Peter Dutton's immigration policy pitch draws comparisons to Trump-era rhetoric, aimed at countering voter losses to Pauline Hanson's One Nation party. The approach marks a shift from previously bipartisan support for Australia's multicultural identity.

stories.title: Alarm raised over health of PTI’s jailed leaders
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf raised alarm over the deteriorating health of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, citing declining eyesight due to prolonged detention and restricted medical access. The party also demanded specialized care for detained leader Ejaz Chaudhry.

stories.title: Dozens arrested in NYC during protests against US support for Israel
stories.summary: Dozens of people were detained in New York City during protests against US arms sales to Israel. Among those arrested was Chelsea Manning, who called for an end to US military support for Israel.

stories.title: No deal, no calm: Iranians settle into a war of endurance
stories.summary: Iranians are adjusting to prolonged conflict following the collapse of high-stakes negotiations in Islamabad. The Pakistan-mediated talks had aimed to stabilize a temporary ceasefire but ended without agreement.

stories.title: Malaysia races to go green as Iran war squeezes oil supply
stories.summary: Malaysia's deputy prime minister announced the country is accelerating its renewable energy transition in response to the energy crisis caused by the Iran war. Iran's near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted approximately 25 percent of global seaborne oil trade and nearly a fifth of global liquefied natural gas exports.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: ‘Master of the house’ says Ben-Gvir as Al-Aqsa opens
stories.summary: Nine-year-old Ritaj Rihan was among multiple Palestinians killed in ongoing Israeli attacks on Gaza. Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir declared himself "master of the house" as Al-Aqsa Mosque was opened to settlers.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 820 over past day
stories.summary: Russia's estimated total combat losses in Ukraine from February 24, 2022 to April 14, 2026 have reached approximately 1,312,960 personnel, with 820 casualties reported over the past day.

stories.title: Bahamas police release Michigan man after his wife vanishes at sea
stories.summary: Bahamian police released a Michigan man who had been arrested in connection with his wife's disappearance at sea. He was initially questioned as a witness before being taken into custody.

stories.title: CAF chief open to corruption probe as Senegal-Morocco row deepens
stories.summary: Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe said he welcomes an independent inquiry into CAF governance, as tensions escalate between Senegal and Morocco over the decision to reassign hosting of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations to Morocco.

stories.title: Heathrow airport traffic surges as war diverts global flights
stories.summary: London's Heathrow Airport reported a 10 percent surge in transit passengers in March as the U.S.-Iran war closed major Middle Eastern airspace, rerouting global flights through Europe. Total passenger numbers rose 6.9 percent to 6.65 million.

stories.title: Govt and Google join hands to arm youth with artificial intelligence skills
stories.summary: The Pakistani government and Google launched "AI Seekho 2026," a free nationwide initiative to equip young developers and professionals with artificial intelligence and vibe coding skills, in collaboration with Telenor and Innovista.

stories.title: U.S., Iran leave door open to dialogue after tense Islamabad talks
stories.summary: The United States and Iran concluded tense negotiations in Islamabad without a deal but left open the possibility of continued dialogue. Despite significant obstacles, both sides were reported to have reasons to consider de-escalation.

stories.title: The Bromine Chokepoint: How Strife in the Middle East Could Halt Production of the World’s Memory Chips
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has exposed a vulnerability in the global semiconductor supply chain related to bromine, a raw material used to produce hydrogen bromide gas for chip etching. While attention has focused on helium shortages from Qatar's offline Ras Laffan facility, analysts warn bromine disruption could pose a greater threat to memory chip production.

stories.title: The Bromine Chokepoint: How Strife in the Middle East Could Halt Production of the World’s Memory Chips
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war with Iran and an unstable ceasefire have exposed vulnerabilities in the global semiconductor supply chain, particularly concerning bromine. Bromine is a key raw material for producing semiconductor-grade hydrogen bromide gas used in chip etching, and disruption in the Middle East threatens memory chip production worldwide.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed as vehicle crashes in south Lebanon; 10 hurt in clash with Hezbollah
stories.summary: IDF Sergeant Major (res.) Ayal Uriel Bianco, 30, was killed when a military vehicle crashed in south Lebanon. Separately, 10 Israeli soldiers were injured in a clash with Hezbollah, which continued sporadic rocket fire on northern Israel.

stories.title: What the naval blockade of Iran might look like
stories.summary: U.S. Navy destroyers could enforce a potential naval blockade of Iran by using radar systems to monitor and track vessel traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills four in Gaza amid truce talks in Cairo
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike killed at least four Palestinians near a school in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza on Monday, as mediators met Hamas leaders in Cairo to bolster the fragile U.S.-brokered ceasefire. Separately, Israeli forces targeted a key town in south Lebanon.

stories.title: Deployment of Russian EW systems near Narva may signal potential plans to strike Baltic states, expert says
stories.summary: An expert warns that Russia's deployment of electronic warfare systems near Narva, combined with claims about Baltic states' airspace being used for Ukrainian drone attacks, may signal Kremlin preparations for escalation toward the Baltic states.

stories.title: Guterres calls Islamabad talks ‘positive step’ despite no deal
stories.summary: UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called recent U.S.-Iran talks hosted by Pakistan a "positive and meaningful step" while warning there is no military solution to the conflict. He announced he is sending special envoy Jean Arnault to Islamabad for further consultations.

stories.title: Chinese tanker sanctioned by US crosses Strait of Hormuz despite blockade
stories.summary: The US-sanctioned Chinese tanker Rich Starry crossed the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the first vessel to exit the Gulf since the US blockade began. The tanker was carrying methanol loaded at a UAE port.

stories.title: Ukraine has enough weapons to defend itself for the first time in history, Zelenskyy says — and wants to sell that expertise abroad
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has sufficient weapons to defend itself against Russia for the first time in its history, crediting drones with reshaping the battlefield. He also expressed interest in expanding government-to-government arms exports.

stories.title: Police arrest Hariri crime family members in raid for extortion, using explosives
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested members of the Hariri crime family on charges of extortion and use of explosives. The suspects allegedly extorted residents in the Samaria region of the West Bank, demanding payments totaling millions of shekels.

stories.title: Sweden calls for reduced reliance on US military support
stories.summary: Swedish Defence Minister Pal Jonson called for Northern Europe to reduce its military dependence on the United States. His remarks followed President Trump's comments about reassessing NATO commitments.

stories.title: US blockade of Hormuz puts ceasefire to test
stories.summary: The U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz intensified tensions with Iran despite a ceasefire and peace talks in Islamabad. President Trump claimed Iran's navy was "obliterated," while NATO allies refused to join the blockade and Iran warned no Gulf port would be secure.

stories.title: Tactical Success, Strategic Failure? Washington Walks the Path to Defeat in Iran
stories.summary: An analysis questions the strategic objectives of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran six weeks after its launch. Critics argue the Trump administration failed to articulate a clear political end-state and repeatedly shifted its stated goals as military operations produced unintended consequences.

stories.title: US V-P Vance says ball now in Iran’s court on peace talks
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance stated that Iran must now respond to peace overtures, emphasizing that preventing Iran from developing a nuclear weapon remains a non-negotiable condition in any negotiations.

stories.title: Russian drone hits high-rise building in Kharkiv
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a multi-storey residential building in the Shevchenkivskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine.

stories.title: UN chief says ‘all parties’ must respect freedom of navigation in Hormuz
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General called on all parties to respect freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz following U.S. President Donald Trump's imposition of a blockade on the strait on April 13.

stories.title: Efforts afoot for second round of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan, regional capitals, and major powers are actively pursuing a second round of U.S.-Iran talks. Officials said a ceasefire extension is the immediate priority, with Tehran favoring Islamabad as the venue for further negotiations.

stories.title: Prediction markets boom raises concerns as Hong Kong calls off basketball bets
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government halted plans for legalized basketball betting as cryptocurrency-based prediction markets surge in popularity. Observers warned that Hong Kong residents using these unregulated platforms could be violating gambling laws and face risks of reneged payouts and unregulated contract disputes.

stories.title: Strategy Without Hubris: How China Rose by Managing America’s Reaction
stories.summary: A new book by Oriana Skylar Mastro, published by Oxford University Press, examines how China expanded its economic, military, and diplomatic power over three decades without triggering early containment by the United States. The work explores why the US-China rivalry deepened only gradually despite significant shifts in relative power.

stories.title: Singapore’s Hormuz stance, Manila-Hong Kong housing gap: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: Singapore's refusal to negotiate with Iran over access to the Strait of Hormuz triggered a backlash from Malaysian politicians who viewed the stance as lecturing. The story was among seven Asia-focused highlights selected by the South China Morning Post covering the past week's developments.

stories.title: IMF, World Bank, IEA urge countries to stop hoarding energy supplies, imposing export controls
stories.summary: The IMF, World Bank, and IEA jointly urged countries to stop hoarding energy supplies and imposing export controls. The three institutions' leaders pledged to coordinate their responses to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Man charged after Molotov cocktail attack on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home
stories.summary: Daniel Moreno-Gama was charged after a Molotov cocktail attack on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's home. The FBI said he was carrying a self-authored anti-AI document when arrested.

stories.title: Man charged after Molotov cocktail attack on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's home
stories.summary: A Texas man was charged with throwing a Molotov cocktail at the home of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and attempting to set fire to OpenAI's headquarters. The incident occurred on April 13.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Ambassador to Canada meets with Mayor of Toronto
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ambassador to Canada, Andrii Plakhotniuk, met with Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow to discuss bilateral matters.

stories.title: Trump deletes image of himself as Jesus as feud with pope dismays US Catholics
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump deleted a social media image depicting himself as Jesus following backlash from religious leaders who called it blasphemous. The controversy compounded dismay among American Catholics over Trump's verbal attacks on Pope Leo XIV, the first American pope to lead the Catholic Church.

stories.title: Australia ‘deeply invested’ in Hormuz access, defence minister says
stories.summary: Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said Canberra is "deeply invested" in maintaining open access through the Strait of Hormuz. Australia is working with France and the UK but stopped short of supporting the US blockade.

stories.title: Neo-Nazi pleads guilty to trying to give Hezbollah intel on Israeli officials in US
stories.summary: A self-identified neo-Nazi in the United States pleaded guilty to attempting to provide Hezbollah with intelligence on Israeli officials in the US. He also admitted to setting a fire that destroyed an office at a historic social justice center in Tennessee.

stories.title: Spain seeks closer China links amid global tensions
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on 14 April 2026, seeking to strengthen political and trade ties between Spain and China amid heightened global tensions.

stories.title: Video: Fidan says Israel seeking to declare Turkey as a ‘new enemy’
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Israel is seeking to designate Turkey as a "new enemy," describing it as an evolving state strategy under Prime Minister Netanyahu's government.

stories.title: Australia news live: Hanson claims credit for Taylor’s immigration plans; Jactina Allan says Coalition stance ‘straight out of the Donald Trump playbook’
stories.summary: Sydney is set to receive its first new Roman Catholic Cathedral in more than a century, as part of a 7.7-hectare precinct in the northern suburb of Waitara. Irish architect Niall McLaughlin will lead the design for the Diocese of Broken Bay, covering more than two dozen parishes.

stories.title: China quietly profits from US AI boom despite Washington’s tech curbs: research
stories.summary: Research by Oxford Economics found that China is quietly benefiting from America's AI-driven data-centre spending boom despite Washington's technology restrictions. Roughly $2 trillion in U.S. data-centre projects are planned or under way, with up to three-quarters of costs tied to equipment flowing through Asian supply chains.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 46 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 46 of the US-Iran conflict, the United States initiated a blockade of Iranian ports. President Trump indicated that a diplomatic deal with Tehran remains possible.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: US blockade of strait of Hormuz begins as Hezbollah urges Lebanon to pull out of talks with Israel
stories.summary: The U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz began as Hezbollah urged Lebanon to withdraw from talks with Israel. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung warned of prolonged disruption to global energy and raw materials markets, while Vice President Vance accused Iran of economic terrorism.

stories.title: Military expert: Russia using two new drafting schemes – via detention centers and universities
stories.summary: A military expert reports that Russia is expanding conscription efforts by introducing new drafting mechanisms through pre-trial detention centers and higher education institutions to find manpower for the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Vance: Lot of progress made in talks toward ‘grand deal,’ but ball in Iran’s court
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said significant progress was made in talks toward a "grand deal" with Iran but that the next steps rest with Tehran. Reports indicate the US sought a 20-year enrichment freeze while Iran offered 5-10 years, which Trump rejected.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits south Lebanon homes as sirens sound in northern Israel
stories.summary: An Israeli air raid on the southern Lebanese town of Bafliyeh damaged multiple homes and caused injuries. Simultaneously, air-raid sirens sounded in northern Israeli towns after a suspected drone infiltration from Lebanon was detected.

stories.title: Hong Kong tram operator launches real-time app, pledges no fare rise this year
stories.summary: Hong Kong Tramways launched a mobile app providing real-time tram arrival information and pledged not to raise fares this year. The operator installed over 400 RFID sensors along its 30-kilometre route to support the new service.

stories.title: US and Iran mull second meeting in bid to revive ceasefire talks
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are considering a second round of meetings to revive ceasefire negotiations after talks held the previous weekend failed to produce a breakthrough.

stories.title: China dismisses Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Sun Weidong
stories.summary: China dismissed Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Sun Weidong in a sudden move linked to the country's ongoing anticorruption campaign, which has led to a wave of high-level removals.

stories.title: The Sea of Azov: Ukraine’s loss but hardly Russia’s gain
stories.summary: The large steel plants along Ukraine's coast of the Sea of Azov have been reduced to unrestorable ruins since Russia's full-scale invasion, diminishing the strategic value of the area.

stories.title: NATO states refuse to join naval blockade of Iran – Reuters
stories.summary: NATO allies announced on Monday they would not support U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to impose a naval blockade on Iranian ports, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Nearly 100 arrested at New York protest over arms sales to Israel
stories.summary: About 90 protesters were arrested in Manhattan after blocking traffic during a demonstration against US arms sales to Israel and the war on Iran. The protest was led by Jewish Voice for Peace and included prominent figures such as Chelsea Manning.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war highlights: Trump vows to destroy Iranian warships that get near U.S. blockade
stories.summary: President Trump vowed to destroy Iranian warships approaching the U.S. naval blockade. Meanwhile, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said a ceasefire between the United States and Iran was holding and that efforts to reach a broader agreement were continuing.

stories.title: China: Evergrande property developer founder pleads guilty
stories.summary: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty in a Chinese court after the property development giant, once China's largest, defaulted on most of its liabilities and payments in 2021.

stories.title: Sergeant Major Ayal Uriel Bianko killed in southern Lebanon, IDF announces
stories.summary: The IDF announced that Sergeant Major Ayal Uriel Bianco, a 30-year-old reservist from Katzrin serving in the 188th Brigade, was killed during combat in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Magyar's landslide victory over Orbán 'showed the limits of right-wing populism in Europe'
stories.summary: Peter Magyar won a landslide election victory over Hungary's long-serving Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Analyst Ian Bond of the Centre for European Reform characterized the result as illustrating the limits of right-wing populism in Europe, with implications for EU cohesion and Ukraine policy. Bond cautioned that political change in Hungary would likely be partial and contested.

stories.title: Why Indonesia’s Prabowo is in Russia – and what he needs from Putin
stories.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto traveled to Moscow seeking affordable oil as global prices surged following the U.S.-Israel war on Iran and the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The visit comes amid fears that millions of Indonesians could be pushed into poverty by the deepening energy crisis.

stories.title: High Court clash exposes IDF manpower crisis, gov't stalling on haredi draft - editorial
stories.summary: Israel's High Court held a hearing that highlighted the IDF's growing manpower shortage. Criticism is mounting over government delays in enforcing conscription of ultra-Orthodox (haredi) men into military service.

stories.title: Japan-based China nurse criticised for posting work clips, raising privacy, ethics concerns
stories.summary: A Chinese nurse working at a Tokyo hospital faced backlash from both Chinese and Japanese internet users for allegedly posting patients' personal and medical information on social media. The woman, identified online as "Zhaozhaozzz," has roughly 21,000 followers and shared videos described as immersive nursing vlogs.

stories.title: Vance says next step in negotiations up to Iran, US has all the cards with blockade in effect
stories.summary: Vice President Vance said the next step in US-Iran negotiations is up to Tehran, noting the US holds leverage through its naval blockade. He indicated the Iranian delegation needed to return to Tehran to obtain approval from senior leadership.

stories.title: Sudan: World Leaders Need to Act On Ongoing Atrocities
stories.summary: At a Berlin conference marking the third anniversary of the Sudan war, Human Rights Watch called on world leaders to take action on ongoing atrocities, protect civilians, and hold abusers accountable.

stories.title: IDF eases home front limits in parts of north, tightens rules elsewhere amid Iran truce
stories.summary: The Israeli military eased home-front restrictions in parts of northern Israel, allowing educational activities in bomb shelters along the Lebanese border. Simultaneously, a cap of 5,000 on gatherings was reintroduced in the Jerusalem area and southern regions amid an Iran-related truce.

stories.title: South Africa: Cape Town Officers Attacked During Athlone Arrest - South African News Briefs - April 14, 2026
stories.summary: Police officers in Cape Town's Athlone neighborhood were attacked while carrying out an arrest, according to South African news reports.

stories.title: Trump: Blockade needed to stop Iran blackmailing the world
stories.summary: President Donald Trump confirmed that a US blockade of Iran's ports began on Monday. Trump said the measure is necessary to prevent Iran from using leverage to pressure the international community.

stories.title: Avenging angel risked her life to try to save Warsaw’s Jews — and lived to write about it
stories.summary: An updated English translation of Vladka Meed's 1948 Yiddish memoir, "On Both Sides of the Wall," has been published. The book recounts her experiences with the Jewish resistance against the Nazis in wartime Warsaw.

stories.title: Asia’s stock markets surge, oil falls on hopes for US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Stock markets across Asia surged and oil prices fell after President Trump suggested Iranian officials are open to a deal, offering relief to global markets amid the US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Tuesday briefing: What needs to be done to tackle child poverty in the UK
stories.summary: A UK analysis found that more than one-fifth of children from the austerity generation live in poverty. The article examines the impact of welfare cuts introduced after the 2008 financial crisis under then-Chancellor George Osborne, which removed an estimated £37 billion from the welfare system by 2021.

stories.title: Palestinian groups launch legal bid to shed light on Australian arms export permits to Israel
stories.summary: Three Palestinian human rights groups — the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights, Al-Haq, and Al Mezan — launched a legal bid in Australia to compel Defence Minister Richard Marles to disclose whether the government approved Israel-bound military export permits. The groups argue such permits could violate international law.

stories.title: Ukrainian water polo team handed technical loss for refusing to play Russia
stories.summary: Organizers of the 2026 Water Polo World Cup in Malta awarded a technical defeat to Ukraine's national team after it refused to play against the Russian team competing under a neutral designation.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel to hold rare direct talks in Washington despite Hezbollah opposition
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli envoys are scheduled to meet in Washington on Tuesday for the first direct face-to-face talks between the two countries in decades, mediated by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The Lebanese militant group Hezbollah has opposed the negotiations, warning it will not abide by any resulting agreements.

stories.title: US energy chief warns oil prices may peak in coming weeks
stories.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright warned that oil prices could peak in the coming weeks due to ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. He said prices should ease once the US-Iran conflict ends and energy flows resume.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief urges Lebanese government to cancel Washington talks with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem urged the Lebanese government to cancel planned Washington talks with Israel. Hundreds of Hezbollah supporters protested on April 10–11, 2026, accusing Prime Minister Nawaf Salam of being aligned with Israel.

stories.title: Founder of China's Evergrande pleads guilty to fraud
stories.summary: Hui Ka Yan, founder of China's Evergrande — once the country's biggest real estate firm with a stock market valuation exceeding $50 billion — pleaded guilty to fraud charges.

stories.title: Nigeria: Ex-Oil Minister Diezani Denies All Six Bribery Counts in UK Trial
stories.summary: Former Nigerian petroleum minister Diezani Alison-Madueke denied all six bribery counts at London's Southwark Crown Court, telling the jury she never abused her office or accepted bribes under the UK Bribery Act.

stories.title: Sanctioned Chinese tanker transits Hormuz despite US blockade
stories.summary: A US-sanctioned Chinese tanker, Rich Starry, transited the Strait of Hormuz despite the American naval blockade, becoming the first tanker to exit the Gulf since the blockade began. The vessel carried approximately 250,000 barrels of methanol loaded in the UAE.

stories.title: Indonesia, US sign ‘major’ defence cooperation agreement
stories.summary: Indonesia and the United States signed a major defence cooperation agreement. The deal follows reports that Washington has been seeking overflight access in Indonesian airspace for US military aircraft.

stories.title: Israeli strike damages hospital in south Lebanon, casualties reported
stories.summary: An Israeli strike damaged Tebnin Governmental Hospital in southern Lebanon, with casualties reported. Lebanese officials say more than 2,000 people have been killed in southern Lebanon since Israeli operations began on 2 March.

stories.title: Mozambique: Terrorists Do Not Occupy Any Towns, Says Chapo
stories.summary: Mozambican President Daniel Chapo announced that Islamist terrorists operating in the northern province of Cabo Delgado do not currently occupy any towns in the province.

stories.title: Tanzania: Tanzania Suspends Jambo TV for Querying Inquiry Into Post-Election Killings
stories.summary: Tanzanian authorities imposed a 90-day suspension on Jambo TV over its YouTube and Instagram posts questioning an inquiry into post-election killings. The Committee to Protect Journalists has urged an immediate reversal of the suspension.

stories.title: Israel says 154 soldiers injured in Lebanon as talks aim to curb attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported 154 soldiers wounded in southern Lebanon fighting since the previous Thursday, including 34 in serious condition. Lebanese Culture Minister Ghassan Salameh described talks in Washington as a preparatory step toward halting military attacks.

stories.title: Holidays take a hit as UK cost of living fears and Iran war bite
stories.summary: UK consumers cut back on travel spending for the first time in five years in March amid rising cost-of-living concerns linked to the Iran war. Overall consumer card spending rose only 0.9 percent year on year, down from 1 percent in February, according to Barclays data.

stories.title: ‘Huge’ increase in kennelling and vet spending by police after XL bully ban
stories.summary: Police spending on kennels and veterinary care in England and Wales has more than tripled since the XL bully dog ban took effect in 2024. Data obtained from 22 police forces via freedom of information requests showed average per-force spending rose from £137,400 in 2022-23 to £423,136 in 2024-25, with some forces reporting nearly 500% increases.

stories.title: Three babies born into Sudan war every minute, charity warns
stories.summary: Save the Children warned that three babies are being born every minute in Sudan amid the ongoing war, with newborns facing conditions the charity described as unacceptable for any child.

stories.title: Hong Kong lawyer faces new charges after second victim accuses him of indecent assault
stories.summary: Hong Kong barrister Simon So Shun-yan faces additional charges of common assault and indecent assault after a second victim came forward. The 32-year-old, admitted to the bar in 2018, was already facing accusations from a former pupil over alleged incidents nine years ago.

stories.title: Sudan: Top UN Aid Official Warns of 'Abandoned Crisis' As War Enters Fourth Year
stories.summary: The UN's top humanitarian official in Sudan warned that as the war enters its fourth year, civilians continue to face killings, displacement, and widespread sexual violence, calling it an "abandoned crisis" requiring urgent action.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Opens Investigation After Deadly Airstrike Kills Dozens in Market
stories.summary: Nigeria opened an investigation after military airstrikes targeting jihadists in the northeast killed dozens of people at a market, according to local residents and NGOs.

stories.title: US funding for Iron Dome air defense system no longer enjoying bipartisan support
stories.summary: US funding for Israel's Iron Dome air defense system is facing growing opposition from progressive lawmakers who argue Israel does not need the assistance. The funding had previously enjoyed broad bipartisan support in Congress.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader asks Lebanon to cancel April 14 meeting with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah supporters protested against planned talks between Lebanon and Israel, with demonstrators branding the Lebanese prime minister a "Zionist." Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem called on Lebanon to cancel the April 14 meeting scheduled in Washington.

stories.title: Ukraine eases procurement rules for testing innovative weapons in combat
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers approved new procurement rules allowing the Defense Ministry to purchase innovative weapons for testing under real combat conditions.

stories.title: Founder of China’s Evergrande Group Hui Ka-yan pleads guilty in fraud trial
stories.summary: Hui Ka-yan, founder and former chairman of China Evergrande Group, pleaded guilty to charges including embezzlement of corporate assets and corporate bribery at the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court. The trial took place on Monday and Tuesday, with a judgment to be issued at a later date.

stories.title: What is really behind South Korea’s row with Israel?
stories.summary: At least 26 South Korean tankers are reportedly stranded near the Strait of Hormuz, which analysts say motivated President Lee Jae Myung's diplomatic confrontation with Israel last week. The dispute erupted after Lee commented on footage appearing to show Israeli soldiers pushing a body from a rooftop.

stories.title: Netanyahu hails blow dealt to Iran as Israel commemorates Holocaust
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu invoked the Holocaust to justify Israel's military actions against Iran, stating that without Israeli intervention, sites like Natanz could have become synonymous with horror comparable to Auschwitz.

stories.title: Super Typhoon Sinlaku bears down on Northern Mariana Islands, Guam
stories.summary: Super Typhoon Sinlaku is approaching the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam. Though the slow-moving storm is weakening, authorities warn it will still bring dangerous conditions to the region.

stories.title: How Iran Helped Bring Ronald Reagan to Power
stories.summary: This article examines how Iran's 1979-1981 hostage crisis influenced US domestic politics, particularly Ronald Reagan's rise to the presidency. The piece notes the crisis dominated headlines at the time and left a lasting impression on Donald Trump.

stories.title: Can Hong Kong, target of the most US sanctions, become China’s quantum gateway?
stories.summary: Hong Kong, which has over 300 entities blacklisted by Washington, is pursuing ambitions to become an international technology hub and a gateway for China's quantum technology development. The government says U.S. sanctions will not deter its plans, which include deepened partnerships with the mainland through the cross-border Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong initiative.

stories.title: Iran tries to cosy up to Europe to increase pressure on US
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi briefed French and German foreign ministers on the offer Tehran had been willing to make regarding its enriched uranium stockpile and the Strait of Hormuz during the Islamabad talks. The diplomatic outreach aims to capitalize on the transatlantic split and increase pressure on Washington.

stories.title: Hezbollah rejects Israel-Lebanon talks in Washington as Rubio joins
stories.summary: Hezbollah rejected Israel-Lebanon negotiations in Washington as "futile," urging Lebanon to confront Israeli attacks instead. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was expected to join the discussions between Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors.

stories.title: Dublin’s National Concert Hall scraps fundraiser for Israel’s MDA, sparking outcry
stories.summary: Dublin's National Concert Hall cancelled a fundraising event for Israel's Magen David Adom, sparking criticism. The head of MDA's local branch said the cancellation reinforced perceptions of Ireland as hostile toward Jewish causes.

stories.title: Pezeshkian: Iran will negotiate only within framework of international law
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told French President Macron that "unreasonable" US demands prevented a deal during recent talks in Pakistan. Pezeshkian said Iran will continue negotiations only within the framework of international law.

stories.title: Malaysia’s Anwar douses row over diesel supplied to Philippines
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim denied allegations that Malaysia's national oil company Petronas supplied diesel to the Philippines. Anwar clarified that the shipment was handled by foreign commodity company Vitol, which has an agreement to transport and sell oil to the Philippines through Malaysian waters.

stories.title: No Strait answer: Can international law stay afloat in Hormuz?
stories.summary: President Trump announced a US Navy blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, effective Monday evening, after 21 hours of inconclusive US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad produced no agreement. Vice President Vance confirmed the talks ended without a deal.

stories.title: UN says world ignoring repeated atrocities in Sudan
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that the world is ignoring repeated atrocities in Sudan. The UN estimates at least 6,000 people died in the first three days of a recent assault, with the true death toll unknown.

stories.title: US officials say Islamabad talks created framework for future negotiations
stories.summary: US officials said talks in Islamabad with Iran, while not producing a breakthrough, established a framework for continued negotiations, according to The Atlantic. A new round of talks could take place as early as Thursday, with Islamabad and Geneva under consideration as venues.

stories.title: Double defeat for Vance as failed Iran talks and Orban’s exit bruise US vice-president
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance left Pakistan after 21 hours of failed negotiations with Iran in Islamabad without reaching a deal. Separately, Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán lost power, dealing Vance a second setback as the U.S. had sought to keep Orbán in office.

stories.title: IMF, World Bank, IEA urge countries to stop hoarding energy supplies, imposing export controls
stories.summary: The IMF, World Bank, and IEA called on countries to stop hoarding energy supplies and imposing export controls. IEA Executive Director Birol described the conflict as having caused the worst global energy disruption ever, with over 80 oil and gas facilities damaged across West Asia.

stories.title: Two Ukrainian postage stamps receive international recognition
stories.summary: Two Ukrainian postage stamps, "Taxes. Army. Victory" and "Melitopol Is Ukraine!" received awards at international stamp competitions.

stories.title: Canada calls on Israel to stop attacks on Lebanon after citizen’s death
stories.summary: Canada called on Israel to stop attacks on Lebanon after confirming the death of a Canadian citizen in the country's south. Canada's foreign minister urged a return to diplomacy and expressed support for efforts toward a lasting solution.

stories.title: Iran war to boost Ukraine inflation, central bank chief says
stories.summary: Ukraine's central bank chief said the US-Iran war is expected to increase inflation in Ukraine. The central bank has scheduled meetings for the following week to assess the conflict's full economic impact.

stories.title: AP: Another round of US-Iran talks could be held 'as early as Thursday'
stories.summary: The Associated Press reported that a new round of US-Iran negotiations could occur as early as Thursday. Officials said both sides agreed in principle to resume talks, with Islamabad and Geneva being considered as possible venues.

stories.title: Video: Netanyahu says Trump administration reports to him daily regarding Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Trump administration briefs him daily on Iran. He noted that Vice President JD Vance called him after leaving Islamabad to detail the weekend talks with Iran that failed to produce a deal.

stories.title: Democrats to force Senate vote on curbing Trump’s war powers
stories.summary: US Senate Democrats announced plans to force another vote to limit President Trump's authority to wage war against Iran. Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said it would be the fourth such effort since the conflict began, though previous attempts were blocked by Republicans.

stories.title: Holocaust survivor Tsili Wenkert speaks on reunion with released hostage grandson, Omer
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Tsili Wenkert spoke about her reunion with her grandson Omer, a released hostage. She described seeing his smile in the hospital as confirmation of her belief in his survival.

stories.title: China’s imports surge in March as exports soften amid Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: China's export growth softened to 2.5 percent year on year in March while imports surged, as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz from the Iran war pushed up transport, commodity, and energy costs. Analysts said China was likely to weather the impact better than other countries due to its large domestic market and manufacturing base.

stories.title: Canada’s Carney secures majority government with special election wins
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney secured a parliamentary majority for his Liberal government through special election wins on Monday. Carney said the majority would help him deal more effectively with the trade war initiated by U.S. President Donald Trump and would likely allow him to govern without facing an election for years.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran ‘wants to work a deal’ as US blocks Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed Iran "wants to work a deal," saying he had received calls from the "right people" without identifying them. The statement came as the US moved to block the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US military kills two men in new strike on vessel in eastern Pacific
stories.summary: The US military killed two men in a strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean. The attack brings the death toll from US strikes on vessels in the Pacific and Caribbean to at least 170 since September.

stories.title: Man charged with attempted murder after attack on OpenAI CEO Altman’s home
stories.summary: A 20-year-old Texas man was charged with attempted murder after an arson attack on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's residence in San Francisco. He faces potential life imprisonment.

stories.title: Trump deletes meme depicting him as Jesus, refuses to apologize amid feud with pope over Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump deleted a social media meme depicting him as Jesus, claiming he mistook it for a Red Cross image. The incident occurred amid an ongoing dispute with the pope over the US-Iran war.

stories.title: Anti-war protesters arrested in New York urging end to Israel weapon sales
stories.summary: Police in New York arrested approximately 100 anti-war protesters during a sit-in demonstration demanding an end to US arms sales to Israel.

stories.title: Crans-Montana mayor says unaware of six-year safety lapse before Swiss bar fire that killed 41
stories.summary: Crans-Montana Mayor Nicolas Feraud said he was unaware that safety inspections had not been conducted for six years at a Swiss ski resort bar where a fire during New Year celebrations killed 41 people. Prosecutors are investigating the blaze, and nine individuals, including Feraud, are under criminal investigation.

stories.title: Dublin’s National Concert Hall scraps fundraiser for Israeli emergency service, igniting outcry
stories.summary: Dublin's National Concert Hall cancelled a fundraiser for an Israeli emergency service that was scheduled for May 11. The event was to feature a play with testimonies from survivors and first responders of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel.

stories.title: Russia renews offer to receive Iran’s enriched uranium
stories.summary: The Kremlin reiterated its willingness to receive Iran's enriched uranium as part of a potential US-Iran agreement. Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the offer remains on the table but has not yet been acted upon.

stories.title: Asia air travel faces turbulence as Iran war exposes jet fuel vulnerability
stories.summary: Jet fuel shortages and surging prices are forcing flight cancellations across the Asia-Pacific following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the U.S.-Iran conflict. The squeeze intensified after the United States began controlling oil shipments through the strait following failed peace talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Pope pledges to keep speaking against war, Trump draws outrage for AI Jesus-like image of self
stories.summary: Pope Leo pledged to continue speaking out against war, while President Trump drew criticism for posting an AI-generated image on Truth Social that resembled a depiction of Jesus. Trump later said the image was meant to portray him as a doctor.

stories.title: Shenzhen’s new party boss has taken the wheel but can he deliver ahead of Apec?
stories.summary: Jin Lei, the new Communist Party chief of Shenzhen, faces his first major test as the city prepares to host the APEC leaders' summit in November. Beijing is seeking to use the forum to promote cooperation in areas like artificial intelligence and showcase Shenzhen's tech-driven potential.

stories.title: US military says it killed two people in another boat strike in eastern Pacific
stories.summary: The US military announced it killed two people in a vessel strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Monday, claiming the targets were involved in narco-trafficking operations. As with most of the military's statements on dozens of strikes conducted in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean Sea, no evidence was provided to support the claim.

stories.title: Uber faces second driver sexual assault trial following $10 million verdict
stories.summary: Uber faces a second trial over allegations of driver sexual assault following a previous $10 million verdict. The case will serve as a bellwether for the ride-share company, which faces more than 3,300 similar lawsuits.

stories.title: Russians set up command headquarters for military unit in hospital in Skadovsk — ATESH
stories.summary: The ATESH partisan movement reported that Russian military forces in the temporarily occupied Kherson region established a command headquarters inside a closed hospital in Skadovsk.

stories.title: US, Iran leave door open to dialogue after tense Islamabad talks
stories.summary: Despite failing to reach a deal in Islamabad, both the US and Iran left the door open to further dialogue. Vice President Vance's post-talks remarks suggested additional exchanges of some kind would continue.

stories.title: Malaysian bust spotlights shadow fleet oil trade in Southeast Asia
stories.summary: Malaysian authorities intercepted two tankers off Penang during an alleged illegal transfer of more than 700,000 litres of diesel. The bust highlights the ongoing shadow fleet oil trade in Southeast Asia, which has persisted despite the paralysis of legitimate shipping routes caused by the Iran war.

stories.title: Brussels must resist ‘passive’ role in US-China trade war, EU chamber urges
stories.summary: The European Union Chamber of Commerce in China urged Brussels to avoid becoming a passive recipient of U.S.-China trade negotiations in a report released Tuesday. The chamber called on the EU to take the lead in discussions affecting European interests while urging Beijing to avoid blanket export controls.

stories.title: Colombia to control hippo population linked to drug lord Pablo Escobar through euthanasia
stories.summary: Colombia plans to control its feral hippo population, descended from animals imported by drug lord Pablo Escobar, through euthanasia. Officials warn that without intervention, the hippo population could grow to as many as 1,000 by 2035.

stories.title: Dominican Republic rains force 30,000 to evacuate, 3 reported dead
stories.summary: Torrential rains in the Dominican Republic have forced approximately 30,000 people to evacuate their homes, with three deaths reported. Weather systems have lingered over the Caribbean nation for more than a month, delivering heavy rainfall across much of its northern region.

stories.title: Middle East war live: US-sanctioned tanker passes Strait of Hormuz despite Trump's blockade
stories.summary: A Chinese tanker under US sanctions passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to shipping data, hours after President Donald Trump vowed to block the strategic chokepoint entirely. Separately, Hezbollah urged Lebanon to withdraw from upcoming direct talks with Israel scheduled in Washington.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Hungary’s new leader says he would ask Putin to end the killing in Ukraine
stories.summary: Péter Magyar, Hungary's new leader after defeating Viktor Orbán in a landslide, said he would speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin if contacted and would ask him to end the killing in Ukraine. Magyar also plans to review and potentially renegotiate Hungary's Russian energy contracts.

stories.title: Florida teenager charged with sexually assaulting and killing stepsister Anna Kepner on cruise ship
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy, Timothy Hudson, has been charged with murder and aggravated sexual abuse in connection with the death of his 18-year-old stepsister Anna Kepner aboard a Carnival cruise ship on 6 November. Kepner's body was found concealed under a bed. The case details became public after a court seal was lifted in a Miami federal court.

stories.title: Officials seek to temper expectations as Israel, Lebanon envoys set to hold historic meeting
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors were set to hold a rare direct meeting in Washington to discuss a possible ceasefire. However, officials tempered expectations, noting Israel has shown no interest in a truce until Hezbollah is disarmed.

stories.title: Chinese man, 32, suffers stomach pain, discovers thermometer swallowed as child still inside him
stories.summary: A 32-year-old man surnamed Wang from Wenzhou, Zhejiang province, China, went to hospital with stomach pain and discovered a mercury thermometer he had swallowed as a child approximately 20 years ago was still lodged in his duodenum.

stories.title: Two Customs officers arrested for allegedly replacing 400kg of seized silver with lead
stories.summary: Two Pakistani Customs preventive officers were arrested for allegedly swapping 400 kilograms of seized silver bullion with lead during official transport from Quetta to the Pakistan Mint in Lahore. A criminal case has been registered and both officers are in custody.

stories.title: How an oath by Buchenwald survivors is being used to fuel anti-Israel protests
stories.summary: A pro-Palestinian group called "Kufiyas in Buchenwald" was blocked from demonstrating outside the former Nazi concentration camp ahead of Yom Hashoah. The planned protest reignited debate over the use of the site's legacy in anti-Israel activism.

stories.title: Lavrov tells Iran conflict has ‘no military solution’
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi that the conflict has no military solution and reaffirmed Moscow's willingness to help resolve the crisis diplomatically. Araghchi briefed Lavrov on recent US-Iran talks in Pakistan that ended without an agreement.

stories.title: Israeli troops fire tear gas at Palestinian schoolchildren in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli troops fired tear gas at Palestinian schoolchildren in the West Bank. The children had been holding an open-air class as a sit-in to demand access to their school when the tear gas was deployed.

stories.title: Minister says Pakistan ‘committed’ to repay US$3 billion loan from UAE
stories.summary: Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the country is committed to repaying a $3 billion loan from the United Arab Emirates and is considering financing from countries and banks. Pakistan failed to roll over the debt with the UAE for the first time in seven years, adding pressure amid soaring oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: UN chief says 'all parties' must respect freedom of navigation
stories.summary: The UN Secretary-General called on all parties to respect freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas supplies transit. The waterway has become a key flashpoint in the US-Iran standoff.

stories.title: Vance says talks with Iran made progress, defends shipping blockade
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said talks between Washington and Tehran held in Islamabad yielded significant progress, calling the meeting a historic high-level engagement. He also defended the administration's decision to blockade Iranian shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: PTCL says repair work on submarine cable to begin from Tuesday, internet users may face service degradation in evening hours
stories.summary: Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited announced that repair work on one of its submarine internet cables would begin on April 14 and could last until April 20. PTCL warned that users may experience service degradation during evening hours throughout the maintenance period.

stories.title: Iran demands compensation from five regional countries over war damage
stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador Amir Saeid Iravani demanded compensation from Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, and Jordan, accusing them of breaching international obligations and causing losses to Iran during the conflict.

stories.title: Canada's ruling party supports visa-free travel with Ukraine
stories.summary: Canada's ruling Liberal Party passed a resolution at its convention supporting visa-free short-term travel for Ukrainian citizens to Canada.

stories.title: Emerging economies in focus at IMF World Bank meetings
stories.summary: Global financial policymakers are convening in Washington for the IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings this week. The gatherings take place against the backdrop of economic disruption caused by the ongoing Iran war, which has added fresh uncertainty to the global economic outlook.

stories.title: In meeting with WB vice president, Aurangzeb calls for enhanced technical support for debt management
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met World Bank Vice President Jorge Familiar Calderon in Washington and requested enhanced technical support and training for Pakistan's Debt Management Office. Aurangzeb is attending the IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings 2026, participating in over 50 high-level gatherings from April 13 to 18.

stories.title: US and Iran keep talking as Trump's blockade takes effect
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said Iran "badly" wants a deal as the US naval blockade took effect on Monday and a fragile ceasefire held. High-stakes talks between the US and Iran in Islamabad, Pakistan, ended without an agreement.

stories.title: Japan’s bid to avert Trump tariffs draws fire over climate impact of US projects
stories.summary: Japan's pledge to invest 5.7 trillion yen ($35.6 billion) in US infrastructure projects to avoid Trump administration tariffs has drawn criticism from environmental groups. They warn the projects could generate greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to about 20 percent of Japan's annual total.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says Tehran wants deal amid US blockade in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran accused the United States of committing piracy as Washington maintains a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. Thousands rallied in Tehran against the blockade while Trump claimed Iran wants a deal.

stories.title: Dialogue between US, Iran still alive after Islamabad talks ended
stories.summary: A source involved in US-Iran talks in Islamabad said the two sides came "very close" to an agreement, reaching roughly 80 percent consensus before encountering issues that could not be resolved on site. Dialogue between the parties reportedly remains active.

stories.title: Italy rallies round pope as Trump attack tests ties with Meloni
stories.summary: Italian political and church leaders rallied behind Pope Leo on Monday after U.S. President Donald Trump publicly attacked the pontiff. The dispute put Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in a difficult position as she sought to balance Italy's close relationship with the Vatican against her alliance with Trump.

stories.title: US positions warships in region as it moves to enforce naval blockade of Iran
stories.summary: US Central Command positioned warships to enforce a naval blockade of Iran, warning that vessels attempting to enter or leave Iranian ports without authorization are subject to capture. CENTCOM told seafarers details of enforcement are still being finalized.

stories.title: Zelensky presents awards to defense industry workers on Ukrainian Weaponsmith Day
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy presented state awards to defense industry employees on Ukrainian Weaponsmith Day, recognizing their contributions to the country's military production efforts.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills three in Gaza following new ceasefire talks
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed three people outside a school in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, according to medics, as new ceasefire negotiations were underway. The Israeli military did not immediately comment on the strike.

stories.title: Hospital at centre of child HIV outbreak caught reusing syringes in undercover filming
stories.summary: Undercover footage from a hospital in Pakistan at the centre of a child HIV outbreak shows staff injecting patients without gloves and reusing syringes, though the hospital's head has refused to acknowledge the footage as genuine.

stories.title: Lebanon seeks peace, but Hezbollah needs to be convinced first
stories.summary: The Lebanese government is entering peace negotiations but holds limited leverage over Hezbollah, which operates largely independently of state authority.

stories.title: Deadline passes for US blockade of Strait of Hormuz, Iran threatens to retaliate against Gulf neighbours
stories.summary: The deadline for the U.S. military blockade of the Strait of Hormuz passed with no sign of the waterway reopening, and oil prices surged sharply. Iran threatened to retaliate against its Gulf neighbours after weekend talks on ending the war collapsed.

stories.title: Israel says troops fighting Hezbollah surrounded key Lebanon town
stories.summary: Israel's 98th Division has completed the encirclement of Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon and begun an assault on the town, according to the Israeli military's Arabic-language spokesman Colonel Avichay Adraee.

stories.title: Jerusalem Post conference returns to New York against backdrop of regional tension
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post conference convened in New York, bringing together international speakers to discuss security, economic, and geopolitical challenges and opportunities facing Israel and the Jewish people amid regional tensions.

stories.title: Hungary vote removes Ukraine's staunchest foe in EU
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, long considered Ukraine's strongest critic in the EU, was defeated in Sunday's election by opposition leader Péter Magyar. Ukraine welcomed the result, which could unblock a €90 billion EU loan Kyiv needs to fund its war with Russia, though Magyar has not been an outspoken ally of Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump says Iranian ‘fast-attack’ ships that come close to US blockade will be eliminated
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that Iranian "fast-attack" ships approaching the U.S. blockade near the Strait of Hormuz would be eliminated. He compared the planned response to how the U.S. military deals with suspected drug boats in the Caribbean and Pacific.

stories.title: ‘Little progress’ in stopping drug drones at HMP Manchester, watchdog says
stories.summary: England and Wales Chief Inspector of Prisons Charlie Taylor reported that HMP Manchester has made very little progress in stopping drones from delivering drugs into the facility. Broken windows remain unfixed and security measures to prevent contraband deliveries to gangs have not been installed.

stories.title: US Navy should rely on allies to boost maritime industrial base, report says
