stories.summary: A new report recommends that the U.S. Navy increase reliance on allied nations to strengthen the American maritime industrial base as the service expands its presence in the Middle East.

stories.title: Starmer’s ‘corrosive complacency’ on defence has put UK in peril, says ex-Nato chief
stories.summary: Former NATO Secretary General George Robertson criticized UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's defense policy, accusing the government of "corrosive complacency" that has put Britain in peril. Robertson, who authored the government's strategic defence review, said the Iran war should serve as a wake-up call to address military underfunding.

stories.title: Russia offers to take in Iran's enriched uranium
stories.summary: Russia has offered to receive Iran's enriched uranium, though recent talks between Iran and the United States over the weekend failed to produce an agreement to end the ongoing conflict that has caused thousands of deaths and significant global economic disruption.

stories.title: Drone attack on truck in Sumy region kills driver
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a truck with a drone in the Hlukhiv community of Ukraine's Sumy region, killing the 39-year-old driver.

stories.title: Trump’s lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein story dismissed for now
stories.summary: A Florida judge dismissed Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over a story about a letter allegedly sent to Jeffrey Epstein. The court ruled that Trump failed to meet the "actual malice" standard required for public figures in defamation cases.

stories.title: Iran executed at least 1,639 in 2025, more hangings feared: NGOs
stories.summary: Iran executed at least 1,639 people in 2025, a 6% increase over the 975 executions carried out in 2024, according to a joint report by Norway-based Iran Human Rights and Paris-based Together Against the Death Penalty. The figure included 48 women.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader urges Lebanon’s government to pull out of Israel talks
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem called on Lebanon's government to withdraw from planned talks with Israel in Washington, DC, claiming the negotiations are designed to pressure Hezbollah into disarming.

stories.title: Vance: Lots of progress made in Pakistan talks, there could be ‘a grand deal’ but ball is in Iran’s court
stories.summary: Vice President Vance said significant progress was made in US-Iran talks in Pakistan and suggested a "grand deal" is possible. Iran reportedly offered to suspend uranium enrichment for five years, while the US sought a 20-year halt. A US energy official warned oil prices may rise until Hormuz traffic resumes.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine’s defense industry can produce millions of FPV drones annually
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine's defense industry has the capacity to produce millions of first-person-view (FPV) drones per year.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine’s defense industry can produce millions of FPV drones annually
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine's defense industry now has the capacity to produce millions of first-person-view drones per year.

stories.title: Sylvan Adams addresses pre-Holocaust Remembrance Day gathering in Krakow
stories.summary: Canadian-Israeli philanthropist Sylvan Adams addressed a pre-Holocaust Remembrance Day gathering in Krakow, Poland. He urged attendees to focus not only on how Jews perished but also on how Jewish life endures.

stories.title: Ukraine is becoming a space power
stories.summary: Ukraine's main intelligence directorate has completed at least two space launches since February 2022, according to a Ukrainian lawmaker, signaling the country's growing capabilities in the space domain.

stories.title: UN maritime chief says no country has right to close Hormuz
stories.summary: The head of the United Nations maritime agency declared that no country has the legal right to close the Strait of Hormuz. The statement came as access to the critical waterway remained blocked six weeks after the eruption of the Iran war.

stories.title: EU doubles steel tariffs to 50% to curb surge of cheap Chinese imports
stories.summary: EU lawmakers and member states agreed to double tariffs on foreign steel imports to 50% to protect European industry from cheap Chinese imports. The deal also reduces duty-free import volumes by 47%. EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic warned that global overcapacity threatens Europe's industrial base.

stories.title: US says it will intercept, divert or capture ships leaving Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced it would intercept, divert, or capture ships departing Iranian ports, with enforcement beginning at 10 p.m. Singapore time on April 13. The measures represent a significant escalation of the U.S. blockade against Iran.

stories.title: Energy prices rise despite Jones Act suspension by Trump
stories.summary: Shipping costs have risen more than 10 percent over the past month amid the US-Israel military campaign against Iran, even after President Trump suspended the Jones Act to ease energy supply constraints.

stories.title: First US-Iran talks in decades end without deal but dialogue ‘still alive’
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials concluded their highest-level direct talks in decades in Islamabad without reaching a breakthrough, though sources said dialogue remains open. Key issues included the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear program, and international sanctions.

stories.title: Dozens arrested at anti-Israel protest in NYC calling to block sale of US bombs
stories.summary: Dozens of protesters led by Jewish Voice for Peace were arrested in New York City after attempting sit-ins at the offices of Democratic Senators Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand. They demanded the senators block a roughly $600 million US bomb sale to Israel.

stories.title: Zelensky announces talks with European officials on joint air defense system
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine will hold talks with European partners this week on establishing a joint air defense system.

stories.title: UN experts slam attacks on Gaza shelters, forced displacement in West Bank
stories.summary: A panel of UN experts documented attacks by Israeli forces on shelters in Gaza and acts of violence by Israeli settlers against displaced Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Red Cross calls consecutive strikes in Lebanon 'gravely concerning'
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross expressed grave concern over consecutive attacks on medical workers in Lebanon. A deadly strike hit a Red Cross centre on Monday, one day after a Red Cross volunteer was killed in a separate incident.

stories.title: To compete with China, US needs to rebuild rare earth talent from the ground up
stories.summary: Experts say the US effort to reduce dependence on China for rare earths and critical minerals faces significant talent and workforce challenges. Eroding industrial expertise, a weak education pipeline, and inconsistent long-term strategy could hinder US ambitions in the mining sector.

stories.title: Dozens arrested in New York as protesters demand US blocks sale of bombs to Israel
stories.summary: Nearly 100 protesters led by Jewish Voice for Peace were arrested in Manhattan during a demonstration demanding Senators Schumer and Gillibrand block a US bomb sale to Israel. The protest cited Israel's intensifying military operations in Lebanon and the US-Israel campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Over 80 years after fleeing the Nazis, a survivor moves to Israel, finally home
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Penina Zeitchik immigrated to Israel more than 80 years after fleeing the Nazis. On her first Holocaust Remembrance Day in Israel, she planned to gather her grandchildren to share her family's wartime experiences.

stories.title: Why is Trump picking a fight with the pope?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump launched a verbal attack on Pope Leo XIV, suggesting the pontiff was elected because he is American. Trump also posted an AI-generated image depicting himself as Jesus, which was later removed.

stories.title: Tankers turn back at Hormuz as crude jumps over 4% on US blockade
stories.summary: Two oil tankers reversed course near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday after the U.S. naval blockade on Iranian ports took effect, according to MarineTraffic data. Brent crude rose 4.4% to $99.36 per barrel and WTI climbed 2.6% to $99.08, as reported by Bloomberg.

stories.title: French court jails Lafarge ex-CEO for funding IS in Syria
stories.summary: A French court sentenced former Lafarge CEO to prison and fined the cement company over €1 million for financing Islamic State and other armed groups in Syria. The payments were made to keep Lafarge's Syrian plant operational between 2013 and 2014.

stories.title: Blue-and-white skates to hockey gold in Bulgaria
stories.summary: Israel's national ice hockey team won gold at the 2026 IIHF World Championship Division II Group B in Bulgaria. The team completed the tournament with a perfect 5-0 record.

stories.title: Venezuela expands Chevron operations in Orinoco Belt following hydrocarbon reform
stories.summary: Venezuela's government signed an agreement at the Miraflores presidential palace in Caracas expanding U.S. oil company Chevron's operations in the country's Orinoco Belt. The deal follows recent hydrocarbon reforms that opened Venezuela's energy sector to private and foreign investment.

stories.title: French cement giant Lafarge guilty of financing ISIL in Syria
stories.summary: French cement company Lafarge and eight former employees were found guilty by a French court of financing the Islamic State group during its presence in Syria.

stories.title: Military expert: Russia moving toward North Korea-style controlled internet
stories.summary: A military expert assessed that Russia is gradually moving toward a restricted internet model, sometimes called "Cheburnet," similar to North Korea's approach. The model involves limiting access to external resources and strengthening internal oversight of online information.

stories.title: Soviet power nearly erased Ukraine’s Easter. What’s being rebuilt exists almost nowhere else in Europe
stories.summary: Traditional spring ritual games, nearly eradicated during the Soviet era, were revived in central Kyiv for Easter. Such customs have survived intact only in Ukraine, Lithuania, and parts of Serbia.

stories.title: Pakistan has the world’s attention. Now it must focus inwards
stories.summary: Pakistan played a key diplomatic role in brokering a temporary ceasefire between the United States, Israel, and Iran amid escalating tensions that threatened a wider regional conflict. Islamabad leveraged backchannel engagement and balanced competing alliances to bring the adversaries to the table.

stories.title: BBC joins paramedics on duty in Lebanon after Israeli strikes
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Hugo Bachega accompanied paramedics working in Nabatieh, a city in southern Lebanon left largely abandoned following Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Hungary's next PM would pick up if Putin calls and tell him to stop Ukraine war
stories.summary: Hungary's prospective next prime minister, Péter Magyar, said he would answer a call from Russian President Vladimir Putin and urge him to stop the war in Ukraine, though he would not initiate the call himself. Russia has offered what it called "pragmatic" relations.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran calling United States, wants to make deal 'very badly'
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran has been contacting the United States and wants to make a deal "very badly." He declined to specify consequences if no agreement is reached by the end of the current ceasefire but warned it "won't be pleasant" for Tehran.

stories.title: Donald Trump vows U.S. will sink any Iran boats that challenge blockade
stories.summary: The US military announced a blockade of ships entering or departing Iranian ports, effective Monday, but as the deadline passed there was no confirmation the measure had taken effect or that any interceptions had occurred. President Trump vowed to sink any Iranian boats that challenged it.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1510: For first time, Ukraine captured Russian position without deploying any infantry
stories.summary: For the first time in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukrainian forces captured a Russian position without deploying infantry, on day 1,510 of the conflict. Separately, Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule in Hungary ended as Peter Magyar's Tisza party won a two-thirds supermajority.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly panel approves bill setting minimum marriage age at 18 for both males and females
stories.summary: A Punjab Assembly standing committee approved the Child Marriage Restraint Bill 2026, setting the minimum legal marriage age at 18 for both males and females. Some committee members, including the chairperson, expressed reservations.

stories.title: Israel kills three Palestinians in separate Gaza strikes
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Gaza on Monday killed at least two Palestinians, according to officials at Nasser hospital. A third Palestinian was reported killed in a separate strike elsewhere in Gaza.

stories.title: Philippines accuses China of using cyanide to poison South China Sea atoll
stories.summary: The Philippines accused China of deploying cyanide at a South China Sea atoll, warning the substance could damage marine ecosystems and weaken the reef structure supporting a grounded Philippine warship.

stories.title: Nigerian airstrike at village market is latest in which civilians have been killed
stories.summary: A Nigerian military airstrike hit a village market, with more than 200 people feared dead. The incident is the latest in a series of strikes in which the Nigerian military has struck civilian targets while pursuing Islamist militants and armed groups.

stories.title: U.S. Military Imposes Blockade on Iranian Ports in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. military imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz. The action lacks international backing and risks undermining Washington's already fragile ceasefire with Tehran.

stories.title: Ukraine’s USFs hit Russian chemical plant in Cherepovets
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck a chemical plant in Cherepovets, Russia. The facility produces components used in the manufacture of explosives.

stories.title: Israeli army bulldozes buildings in south Lebanon: Report
stories.summary: The Israeli army bulldozed several buildings and landmarks in the southern Lebanese town of Naqoura in the Tyre district, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency. The demolitions occurred as Israel continued its ground invasion in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Orban’s paradox: A friend of Israel, a challenge for Jews - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines the paradox of outgoing Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who combined ultra-nationalist and illiberal domestic policies with consistent diplomatic support for Israel throughout his tenure.

stories.title: Trump vows US will 'eliminate' any Iranian ships defying blockade
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned that any Iranian vessels breaching the newly enforced U.S. naval blockade would be "immediately eliminated." The statement came after Pakistan-brokered peace talks failed to produce an agreement on the conflict in Iran.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief demands Lebanon back out of ‘futile’ planned talks with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem demanded Lebanon withdraw from US-brokered negotiations with Israel scheduled in Washington, calling them futile. He vowed Hezbollah would never surrender and threatened to capture Israeli soldiers amid ongoing fighting.

stories.title: War in Iran could accelerate global energy transition
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict in Iran has highlighted the vulnerabilities of countries dependent on Middle Eastern fossil fuels. Former Uruguayan Energy Secretary Ramon Mendez argued that a rapid shift to renewable energy is achievable, citing Uruguay's success in sourcing 98% of its electricity from low-carbon sources.

stories.title: Aron Heller: 1.5 million-strong Jewish band of brothers
stories.summary: Author Aron Heller spoke on Israel's Holocaust Remembrance Day about the estimated 1.5 million Jewish servicemembers who fought against Nazi forces during World War II, the subject of his book "Zaidy's Band."

stories.title: Military expert: Escalation possible in Middle East after April 15
stories.summary: A military expert warned that the security situation in the Middle East could deteriorate after mid-April, citing an increase in U.S. military presence in the region as a contributing factor.

stories.title: Foreign Ministry holds Holocaust Remembrance Day ceremony for Righteous Among the Nations
stories.summary: Israel's Foreign Ministry held a Holocaust Remembrance Day ceremony honoring the Righteous Among the Nations. The event took place beside a wall inscribed with the names of foreign diplomats who risked their lives to rescue Jews during the Holocaust.

stories.title: WATCH: Survivor recounts how he held on to hope, as Knesset Speaker marks Holocaust Remembrance Day
stories.summary: A Holocaust survivor recounted his experiences during an event held as part of the Zikaron BaSalon framework in Israel. The program provides intimate, home-based alternatives to formal Holocaust Remembrance Day ceremonies, with Knesset Speaker marking the occasion.

stories.title: 'We have been in exile': Norway government back to old quarters 15 years after Breivik bomb
stories.summary: Fifteen years after far-right extremist Anders Behring Breivik detonated a bomb that damaged Norway's government quarter in Oslo, the prime minister celebrated the return of several ministries to the redeveloped area on Monday. Officials described the period away as a time of exile.

stories.title: Iran denies charging toll for Indian tankers transiting Hormuz strait
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to India denied that Indian tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz had paid tolls to Tehran. The statement came after U.S. President Donald Trump vowed to block passage for vessels making payments to Iran.

stories.title: NATO allies refuse to join Trump’s Strait of Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: NATO allies refused to participate in the U.S.-led blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Instead, the allied nations called for the vital waterway to be reopened to international shipping.

stories.title: Judges fired after blocking deportation of pro-Palestinian students
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice terminated six immigration judges, including Roopal Patel and Nina Froes, who had ruled against the Trump administration in deportation cases involving pro-Palestinian university students Rümeysa Öztürk and Mohsen Mahdawi.

stories.title: Israel presses assault on Lebanon border town ahead of US-hosted talks
stories.summary: Israeli forces launched an assault on a key town in southern Lebanon to dislodge Hezbollah fighters on Monday. The military operation came on the eve of rare U.S.-hosted talks between Israeli and Lebanese government envoys in an effort to address the conflict.

stories.title: Bernie Sanders vows to push resolution to block US weapons to Israel
stories.summary: US Senator Bernie Sanders announced plans to introduce a resolution in the Republican-controlled Senate to block American weapons transfers to Israel, a move that could highlight shifting Democratic positions on the issue.

stories.title: Netanyahu rebukes Europe as Israel commemorates Holocaust in shadow of Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu criticized Europe during Holocaust Remembrance Day, accusing the continent of "deep moral weakness" while asserting Israel defends it. President Herzog called for national unity, eulogizing a fallen soldier whose grandmother survived Bergen-Belsen.

stories.title: Bahrain summons Iraqi ambassador over drone attacks
stories.summary: Bahrain summoned Iraq's ambassador in response to ongoing drone attacks attributed to pro-Iranian groups based in Iraqi territory. Several Gulf countries and Jordan had previously issued a joint statement demanding Baghdad take immediate action to halt the attacks.

stories.title: Ukraine has built new defense industry in four years – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has built an entirely new defense industry over the past four years of conflict.

stories.title: J Street says Israel should pay out-of-pocket if it wants US weapons
stories.summary: U.S. pro-Israel advocacy group J Street stated that Israel should pay for American weapons with its own funds rather than relying on U.S. taxpayer money. The shift reportedly followed widespread public opposition to taxpayer-funded arms transfers.

stories.title: Israel loses Hungary as key EU ally as Viktor Orban exits power - analysis
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán's departure from power following Hungarian elections has cost Israel a key ally within the European Union. Analysts note Israel now faces a significantly different European diplomatic landscape without Orbán's reliable support.

stories.title: France's Macron to hold talks with Venezuelan opposition leader Machado
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron held talks on Monday with Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado in Paris. The meeting signals continued French engagement with Venezuela's political opposition.

stories.title: After US-Iran talks in Islamabad, PM Shehbaz says ‘full efforts’ ongoing to resolve conflict
stories.summary: Following US-Iran talks held in Islamabad, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said a ceasefire remains in place and that efforts to resolve outstanding issues are ongoing. He described hosting the negotiations as a historic moment.

stories.title: Estonia’s Orthodox church that declared independence from Russia is still run by Moscow, intelligence report says
stories.summary: Estonia's internal security service reported in 2025 that the Estonian Christian Orthodox Church's name change and new statutes were cosmetic reforms. The agency found that Moscow Patriarch Kirill's oversight departments continue to direct the church's activities despite its declared independence from Russia.

stories.title: Wife of Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez charged with corruption
stories.summary: Begoña Gómez, wife of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, has been formally charged with corruption following a years-long investigation. Judge Juan Carlos Peinado opened the probe in April 2024 into whether Gómez exploited her position. The case adds to several corruption investigations surrounding Sánchez's family and allies.

stories.title: Drone strikes on Moscow serve as pressure tool against Russia, expert says
stories.summary: An expert assessed that Ukrainian drone strikes on Moscow and other Russian targets are designed as a pressure tool, deliberately hitting economically sensitive sites to inflict significant financial losses on Russia.

stories.title: 'Very difficult for me': Actress Hana Laszlo decides to not carry Independence Day torch
stories.summary: Israeli actress Hana Laszlo decided not to carry the Independence Day torch after facing controversy. Critics objected to statements she allegedly made critical of IDF activities during the Israel-Hamas war.

stories.title: Colombia to cull hippo population founded by drug lord
stories.summary: Colombia plans to cull its invasive hippo population, originally introduced by drug lord Pablo Escobar in the 1980s. The animals have become a tourist attraction but pose significant challenges for local authorities and residents.

stories.title: Hundreds of Lufthansa flights cancelled as pilots strike again over pay
stories.summary: Lufthansa cancelled hundreds of flights on Monday as pilots launched another strike over pay disputes. The walkout follows a previous pilots' strike at the German airline in mid-March.

stories.title: There is 'continued engagement with Iran', US official says
stories.summary: A U.S. official confirmed continued engagement between Washington and Tehran, with forward motion toward reaching an agreement. The statement came as the U.S. military began a blockade of Iranian ports and Iran threatened retaliation against Gulf neighbors following the collapse of talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Putin fortifies his family’s home. Seven new missile towers went up in single day
stories.summary: Seven Pantsir air-defense missile systems were installed in a single day at Russian President Vladimir Putin's residence near Valdai, bringing the total number of such systems at the site to 27. Ukraine has not struck the location to date.

stories.title: High Court orders IDF to allow women in Armored Corps tanks by November 2026
stories.summary: Israel's High Court ordered the IDF to allow women to serve in Armored Corps tanks by November 2026. The military had twice delayed a pilot program during wartime, but justices ruled there is a legal obligation to provide equal combat-role opportunities.

stories.title: Donald Trump deletes AI image of himself as Jesus after attacking Pope Leo
stories.summary: President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image depicting himself as Jesus Christ healing the sick while attacking Pope Leo on social media. He deleted the image Monday after backlash from Christian and Catholic supporters, claiming he thought it depicted him as a doctor.

stories.title: What impact will the Iran war have on the wedding industry?
stories.summary: The UK wedding industry is assessing the economic impact of the conflict with Iran. Rising fuel prices are putting pressure on supply chains, though vendors say they are prepared to absorb higher costs.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel ushers in Holocaust Remembrance Day under shadow of Iran threat
stories.summary: Israel marked Holocaust Remembrance Day on Monday evening with a prerecorded official state ceremony at the Yad Vashem Holocaust museum and memorial site in Jerusalem. The commemoration took place under the shadow of the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Trump says he won't apologize to Pope Leo after criticism
stories.summary: President Donald Trump refused to apologize to Pope Leo XIV after criticizing the pontiff's opposition to the war in Iran. Trump claimed a deleted social media post depicting him as Jesus was meant to show him as a doctor. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called Trump's remarks "unacceptable."

stories.title: US to enforce blockade in Gulf of Oman, Arabian Sea, note to seafarers says
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command issued a notice to seafarers announcing enforcement of a blockade in the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea east of the Strait of Hormuz. The measures apply to all vessel traffic regardless of flag, according to the notice seen by Reuters.

stories.title: Islamist militants raid Nigerian army base, kill commander and six soldiers
stories.summary: Islamist militants on motorbikes attacked a Nigerian army base near the northeastern border with Chad late on Sunday. The raid killed the base commander and six other soldiers, according to military sources in Maiduguri.

stories.title: Pope Leo pays his respects at Algeria-France war monument
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Algeria to begin an 11-day tour of four African countries. He visited a monument commemorating the Algeria-France war and promoted Christian-Muslim coexistence.

stories.title: Hezbollah rejects Lebanon’s direct negotiations with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem called on the Lebanese government to cancel a planned meeting between Lebanese and Israeli representatives in Washington, describing direct negotiations as pointless. Lebanon's foreign minister said Beirut intended to use the talks to press for a ceasefire.

stories.title: Belgium and Spain just committed €1 billion each to Ukraine. Here’s what they buy
stories.summary: Belgium and Spain each pledged €1 billion in military aid to Ukraine. Belgium's contribution includes additional F-16 fighter jets for Kyiv's air force.

stories.title: Russian drone strike leaves four people injured in Kherson
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the city of Kherson injured four people, three of whom are reported to be in moderate condition.

stories.title: Actress Hana Laszlo backs out of lighting torch at Independence Day ceremony
stories.summary: Israeli actress Hana Laszlo withdrew from lighting a torch at the Independence Day ceremony after facing criticism from some bereaved parents. The backlash stemmed from her signing a petition the previous year calling to end the conflict in Gaza.

stories.title: Israeli troops fire tear gas at Palestinian kids in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli troops fired tear gas at Palestinian schoolchildren and adults in the West Bank who were holding an open-air class as a sit-in to demand access. The incident occurred during what participants described as a peaceful demonstration.

stories.title: PMD predicts rainfall in upper parts of country from April 16 to 19
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast rain, windstorms, and thunderstorms across the country's upper regions from April 16 to 19, affecting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.title: Trump doubles down in Pope feud, refuses to apologise
stories.summary: Former U.S. President Donald Trump refused to apologize after publicly attacking Pope Leo XIV, calling him "weak." The exchange marked an escalation in a public feud between Trump and the new pontiff.

stories.title: EU hands Hungary’s new leader 27 conditions. One of them is unlocking €90 billion for Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Union presented 27 conditions to Hungary's new leadership, including the release of approximately €90 billion in funding for Ukraine. The remaining conditions address anti-corruption reforms and the reversal of decisions from the Orbán era that were found to violate EU rules.

stories.title: Bahamas police again question US man over disappearance of wife at sea
stories.summary: Police in the Bahamas continued questioning US citizen Brian Hooker over the disappearance of his wife Lynette, who he claims fell overboard from their dinghy. Family members have expressed doubt about Hooker's account of the incident.

stories.title: Sloviansk under day-long attack by Russian drones
stories.summary: Russian FPV drones attacked the town of Sloviansk in Ukraine's Donetsk region throughout the day on April 13. The sustained strikes damaged a multi-story residential building in the town.

stories.title: Donald Trump 'hasn't read the psychology of Iranians well at all', military expert says
stories.summary: Former British Military Intelligence officer Philip Ingram told FRANCE 24 that President Trump has misjudged Iranian psychology, arguing that Iran will not capitulate. Ingram said Trump faces a choice between maintaining the blockade with its global economic consequences or resuming a bombing campaign.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader asks Lebanon to cancel meeting with Israel in Washington
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem urged Lebanon to cancel a planned meeting with Israel scheduled for the following day in Washington. In a televised address, Qassem reiterated Hezbollah's rejection of direct negotiations with Israel, calling for a "historic and heroic stance" against the talks.

stories.title: US House committee to investigate Eric Swalwell over sexual assault allegations
stories.summary: The US House Ethics Committee opened an investigation into Democratic Congressman Eric Swalwell over allegations of sexual misconduct, including toward an employee. The announcement came a day after Swalwell dropped out of the California governor's race amid reports of sexual assault.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief urges Lebanese government to cancel US-Israel talks
stories.summary: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem called on Lebanon's government to cancel a scheduled meeting between Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors in Washington, describing the talks as pointless. Lebanon's foreign minister said Beirut would use the face-to-face negotiations to press for a ceasefire.

stories.title: Trump says Iran wants ‘peace deal’ but insists on ‘no nukes’
stories.summary: Donald Trump stated that Iran wants to reach a peace deal "very badly" following the conclusion of talks in Islamabad, which ended without an agreement. Trump insisted that any deal must ensure Iran does not acquire nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Israelis war-weary but most oppose Iran ceasefire, poll suggests
stories.summary: A poll of Israelis indicates that while war fatigue is widespread, a majority oppose a ceasefire with Iran. Most respondents said they did not believe Hezbollah or Iran had been significantly weakened by weeks of Israeli and US military strikes.

stories.title: Israel slams South Korean leader for comparing IDF activity to the Holocaust
stories.summary: Israel condemned South Korean President Lee Jae Myung for sharing a post comparing IDF activity to the Holocaust. Jerusalem accused the South Korean leader of trivializing the massacre of Jews on the eve of Holocaust Remembrance Day.

stories.title: Russia calls for joint food reserves with BRICS to counter Middle East crisis risks
stories.summary: Russia proposed creating joint food reserves with fellow BRICS members and former Soviet neighbours to counter risks to global food security from the Middle East conflict. The initiative was announced by a senior Russian security official, citing the country's position as the world's largest wheat exporter.

stories.title: Philippines accuses Chinese fishermen of dumping cyanide in South China Sea
stories.summary: The Philippines accused Chinese fishermen of dumping cyanide in the South China Sea, alleging the poison was used to kill fish and deprive Filipino troops stationed in the area of food supplies. Beijing rejected the accusation, calling it a "farce."

stories.title: Lebanon will need '1 billion dollars just to keep humanitarian situation afloat', minister says
stories.summary: Lebanese Social Affairs Minister Hanin Sayyed told FRANCE 24 that Lebanon will need approximately $1 billion over 12 months to maintain basic humanitarian conditions amid ongoing Israeli attacks and ground invasion, which have caused mass displacement across the country.

stories.title: High Court says IDF must implement equal opportunity for women in combat roles
stories.summary: Israel's High Court ruled that the IDF must implement equal opportunity for women in combat roles, including infantry and armored units. The petitions, originally filed in 2020, were brought by female candidates and service members seeking equal access to elite unit screening.

stories.title: Turkey says NATO should reset ties with Trump at next summit, prepare for future
stories.summary: Turkey called on NATO allies to use the upcoming July summit in Ankara to reset relations with U.S. President Donald Trump. Ankara also urged the alliance to prepare for a potential reduction in U.S. involvement in NATO.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran again expressed interest in deal after US naval blockade begins
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran expressed renewed interest in a deal after the U.S. began a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Trump warned that Iranian ships attempting to cross the blockade would be "eliminated" and stated that non-Iranian vessels could transit the Strait of Hormuz freely.

stories.title: IDF kills Hamas terrorist involved in building collapse which killed 21 soldiers
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces killed Hamas operative Yousef Ibrahim Mahmoud Basheti, who was involved in a January 2024 building collapse in Gaza that killed 21 IDF soldiers. Basheti had been part of a group that fired anti-tank missiles at buildings where Israeli soldiers were operating.

stories.title: Magyar backs €90B loan opt-out, opposes Ukraine’s fast-track EU accession
stories.summary: Hungarian opposition leader Peter Magyar of the Tisza party supports Hungary's right to opt out of the EU's €90 billion loan for Ukraine. He also opposes Ukraine's fast-track accession to the European Union.

stories.title: Plans to change HS2 train size could reduce capacity and speed in north, says expert
stories.summary: A review of the original HS2 train order in the United Kingdom could result in fewer seats and slower services north of Birmingham, according to a senior government and rail industry figure. The £2 billion order for 54 high-speed trains, being built by Alstom and Hitachi, is under review as HS2 Ltd seeks to cut costs.

stories.title: French court rules cement giant Lafarge guilty of funding Syria ‘terrorism’
stories.summary: A French court found cement company Lafarge guilty of funding terrorism during the Syrian civil war. The company was fined and several executives, including former CEO Bruno Lafont, were sentenced to prison for payments totaling $6.54 million made to jihadist groups including Islamic State between 2013 and 2014.

stories.title: Volunteers step in to support aging Holocaust survivors in Tel Aviv, Jaffa - interview
stories.summary: The Amcha Institute supports approximately 220 Holocaust survivors in the south Tel Aviv and Jaffa area. All are elderly individuals who were referred to the program through social services. Volunteers provide assistance to help meet their daily needs.

stories.title: Brazil’s former spy chief who fled country arrested by ICE agents in US
stories.summary: Alexandre Ramagem, Brazil's former spy chief under ex-President Jair Bolsonaro, was arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents. Ramagem had fled Brazil after being sentenced to 16 years in prison for his role in plotting a military coup.

stories.title: Flag, anthem restrictions dropped for Russian, Belarusian swimmers
stories.summary: International sports-governing bodies have eased restrictions on Russian and Belarusian swimmers, lifting bans on displaying national flags and playing anthems at competitions. The move signals a broader relaxation of sanctions imposed on athletes from both countries.

stories.title: President Herzog to award Argentina's Javier Milei with Presidential Medal of Honor
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced plans to award Argentine President Javier Milei the Presidential Medal of Honor. The medal recognizes individuals who have made exceptional contributions to Israel or humanity through their talent or service.

stories.title: India, Oman discuss ways to boost trade, investments
stories.summary: India and Oman discussed expanding bilateral trade and investment. India agreed to reduce tariffs on Omani products including dates, marbles, and petrochemical items under a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement.

stories.title: Why the US-Iran ceasefire is no path to peace
stories.summary: Analysis argues that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire represents only a fragile pause rather than a path to lasting peace. The truce was driven by rising costs and strategic pressure around the Strait of Hormuz in a conflict with no clear endgame.

stories.title: Turkey concerned about any new Iran-US rules for Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Turkey's foreign minister expressed concern on Monday about any new regulations proposed by Iran or the United States for transit through the Strait of Hormuz. He also noted difficulties with proposals to reopen the waterway using an international force.

stories.title: Ukraine’s forces strike Russian logistics in occupied Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Raid regiment of the Unmanned Systems Forces struck Russian military logistics deep inside occupied Zaporizhzhia region. The operation employed domestically produced drones to target supply lines in temporarily occupied territory.

stories.title: French court jails Lafarge former CEO for funding IS in Syria
stories.summary: A French court fined cement company Lafarge over $1.3 million and sentenced its former CEO to six years in prison for paying protection money to the Islamic State group and other jihadist organizations to maintain business operations in war-torn Syria.

stories.title: Judge drops Trump’s US$10 billion Epstein report lawsuit against WSJ, Murdoch
stories.summary: A federal judge in Florida dismissed President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over a story about Trump's ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Judge Darrin P. Gayles ruled Trump failed to demonstrate the article was published with malicious intent but allowed the president to file an amended complaint.

stories.title: Is it realistic for US Navy to counter-block Iran’s Hormuz Strait blockade?
stories.summary: Confusion remains over how the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will be enforced and how American forces would respond to challenges. The blockade was announced after US-Iran peace talks failed over the weekend.

stories.title: Hungary will be "a tough partner, but a partner" on Ukraine, expert says
stories.summary: Analyst Lukáš Macek of the Jacques Delors Centre told FRANCE 24 that Hungary's new government under Peter Magyar is expected to stop blocking aid for Ukraine and will be "a tough partner, but a partner" on the issue of Ukrainian accession to the EU.

stories.title: How the Strait of Hormuz became Iran's most powerful weapon
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the Strait of Hormuz has become Iran's most powerful strategic leverage point. The current war has allowed Tehran to test its ability to control the waterway for the first time, and Iran is unlikely to relinquish that advantage.

stories.title: Five years after Belarus’ stolen election, Ukraine is still catching up on Tsikhanouskaya
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held his first presidential-level meeting with Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya in January 2025. However, two months later, a promised visit by Tsikhanouskaya to Kyiv and the appointment of a special envoy have yet to materialize.

stories.title: Netanyahu meets Holocaust survivors chosen to bear torches at Remembrance Day ceremony
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife met with Holocaust survivors selected to bear torches at the upcoming Holocaust Remembrance Day ceremony. Netanyahu described the annual meeting as an extraordinarily moving tradition and praised the survivors as "giants of the spirit."

stories.title: No infantry: For first time, Ukraine captured Russian position using only drones and robots
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces captured a Russian position for the first time using only drones and robotic systems without deploying infantry. Such unmanned systems reportedly conducted 22,000 missions over a three-month period.

stories.title: Court convicts man of aggravated rape, child abuse in Gedera home invasion
stories.summary: A court in Israel convicted a man of aggravated rape and child abuse following a home invasion in the city of Gedera. The attacker entered the victim's second-floor apartment through the balcony in the early morning hours and overpowered her inside.

stories.title: Kremlin says it hopes for pragmatic ties with new Hungarian leadership after Orban defeat
stories.summary: The Kremlin said Monday it hoped to maintain "highly pragmatic ties" with Hungary's new leadership after Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, a close Russian partner, lost to opposition leader Peter Magyar in parliamentary elections.

stories.title: Hungarians look to a changed future after pro-EU Magyar’s election landslide win
stories.summary: Peter Magyar's pro-EU Tisza party won a landslide victory in Hungary's elections, defeating Viktor Orbán. Supporters hope the new government will strengthen the rule of law and unlock billions in frozen EU funds.

stories.title: Indian workers protest over rising living cost
stories.summary: Factory workers in the Indian city of Noida staged protests over rising living costs, with demonstrations turning violent. Police scaled up enforcement in the area to manage the unrest.

stories.title: Iran resumes rail services on routes damaged by war
stories.summary: Iran resumed rail services on routes damaged during nearly 40 days of fighting, with reconstruction work underway on war-damaged infrastructure.

stories.title: Red Cross calls consecutive Lebanon strikes 'gravely concerning'
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross called consecutive Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon "gravely concerning." The attacks targeted a Red Cross centre and killed a medic, prompting deep concern over the safety of medical workers in the conflict zone.

stories.title: U.S. aware of Iran’s capabilities, says Iran Envoy Mohammad Fathali
stories.summary: Iran's envoy Mohammad Fathali stated that the United States is aware of Iran's military capabilities and accused Washington of making "unlawful" demands during the failed peace talks.

stories.title: St. Petersburg to Restore Imperial Stables Following Decades of Neglect
stories.summary: St. Petersburg authorities plan to restore the Konnyushennoye Vedomstvo, an imperial stables complex established under Peter the Great to house royal horses, carriages, and support personnel. The site has suffered decades of neglect.

stories.title: Ukraine repositions troops to strengthen defense near Myropilske in Sumy region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces repositioned troops to new defensive positions near Myropilske in the Sumy region. The military said the move was made to preserve personnel amid ongoing combat operations.

stories.title: Estonia to halt $587M Infantry Fighting Vehicle buy in favor of drones, air defense
stories.summary: Estonia announced it will halt a $587 million purchase of infantry fighting vehicles in favor of investing in drones and air defense systems. Defense Minister Hanno cited the diminishing battlefield utility of heavy equipment as the reason for not replacing CV90s over the next decade.

stories.title: Moscow bar worker faces criminal case for placing Easter bread under hookah bowl
stories.summary: Russia's Investigative Committee opened a criminal case against a Moscow bar employee for "offending the religious feelings of believers." The worker had placed an Easter bread loaf beneath a hookah bowl and posted images on social media.

stories.title: Trump admin fires judges who blocked deportations of pro-Palestinian activists
stories.summary: The Trump administration fired two immigration judges who had blocked deportations of pro-Palestinian student activists. Judge Roopal Patel had stopped the deportation of Tufts student Rümeysa Öztürk, and Judge Nina Froes had halted the removal of Columbia student Mohsen Mahdawi.

stories.title: Vance’s bad week: vice-president risks becoming face of two Trump foreign policy failures
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance faced setbacks on two foreign policy fronts, with the fall of Viktor Orbán's government in Hungary and the failure of nuclear talks with Iran. The developments raised questions about the administration's diplomatic strategy.

stories.title: Military defense attorney indicted over alleged sex offenses against 10 soldiers and recruits
stories.summary: An Israeli military defense attorney identified as Dvir was indicted on 10 counts of alleged sex offenses against soldiers and recruits. The charges include rape, attempted rape, indecent acts by force, and multiple counts of indecent acts.

stories.title: 3 cops martyred, 5 injured as assailants open fire on police vehicle in GB’s Diamer
stories.summary: Three police officers were killed and five others, including a deputy superintendent, were injured when unknown assailants opened fire on a police vehicle in Gilgit-Baltistan's Diamer district. The officers were returning from destroying poppy crops in Thor village.

stories.title: Lafarge Trial: Cement firm fined, former CEO jailed
stories.summary: A French court fined cement manufacturer Lafarge $1.3 million for making payments to the Islamic State group and other jihadist organizations to keep its factory operating in Syria during the civil war. The company's former CEO received a prison sentence.

stories.title: Canada's Carney set to win majority government in special elections
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and his Liberal Party were projected to win a parliamentary majority in Monday's elections. A majority government would allow Carney to advance his legislative agenda amid growing global uncertainty and trade tensions with the United States.

stories.title: Pope Leo says he is not afraid of Trump after US president’s broadside
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly attacked Pope Leo XIV as "terrible," prompting the pontiff to respond that he has "no fear" of the administration and will continue denouncing war. The dispute centers on the pope's criticism of the US-Israeli war in Iran and US immigration policies.

stories.title: Israeli military says surrounded key Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it had completely surrounded the strategic southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil amid fierce fighting with Hezbollah. The encirclement represents a significant development in Israel's ground operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: RBC reports Russia’s government approves criminal penalties for illegal cryptocurrency circulation, with sentences of up to 7 years in prison
stories.summary: Russia's government commission approved amendments to the Criminal Code imposing criminal penalties of up to seven years in prison for illegal cryptocurrency circulation. The Russian business outlet RBC reported the decision on April 13, citing sources.

stories.title: Colombia to cull up to 80 hippos descended from Pablo Escobar zoo
stories.summary: Colombian officials authorized a plan to cull up to 80 feral hippos descended from animals brought to the country by Pablo Escobar in the 1980s. Environment Minister Irene Vélez said other control methods, including neutering and relocation, had proven too expensive and unsuccessful.

stories.title: Nearly 270,000 public services identified in Ukraine – Ministry of Digital Transformation
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation reported that nearly 270,000 public services have been identified through a nationwide screening. These services are delivered by approximately 15,000 entities at both central and local government levels.

stories.title: US expected to start naval blockade of Iranian ports after deadline passes
stories.summary: The United States was expected to begin a naval blockade of Iranian ports on Monday evening after a deadline passed. US Central Command said the blockade would apply to any ships entering or departing Iranian ports or coastal areas, escalating the six-week-old US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Why did Pakistan deploy soldiers, fighter jets to Saudi Arabia?
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed military personnel and fighter jets to Saudi Arabia, reinforcing its 2025 defense pact with Riyadh. The deployment comes amid the broader conflict involving the U.S. and Israel against Iran.

stories.title: Hungary, Israel share 'special relationship,' Prime Minister-elect Peter Magyar says
stories.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister-elect Peter Magyar described the relationship between Hungary and Israel as special. He emphasized Israel's importance as an economic partner and expressed his intention to pursue a pragmatic bilateral relationship.

stories.title: Israel says troops fighting Hezbollah surrounded key Lebanese town
stories.summary: Israel said its troops fighting Hezbollah had surrounded a key town in southern Lebanon, marking a significant advance in its ongoing invasion of the country.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Velykyi Burluk in Kharkiv region: one killed, three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone strike on the settlement of Velykyi Burluk in Kupiansk district, Kharkiv region. The attack killed one person and injured three others.

stories.title: Jewish Israelis, by large margin, support continued fighting Hezbollah; Arabs don’t
stories.summary: A poll found that approximately 80% of Israeli Jews support continuing military operations against Hezbollah, even if it causes friction with Washington, amid the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. Arab citizens of Israel largely opposed the continuation of fighting.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills three in Gaza following new ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Israeli fire killed three people in Gaza during a period of renewed ceasefire negotiations. Medics reported that the strike hit a group of men outside a school in Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Holocaust survivor, 92, makes aliyah to Israel nine decades after Kindertransport - interview
stories.summary: Helen Hesse Charash, a 92-year-old Holocaust survivor born in Hamburg, Germany, has immigrated to Israel nearly nine decades after being saved by the Kindertransport. Her father, an attorney, was barred from practicing law beginning in April 1933.

stories.title: Nowhere to hide: Iran war spotlights military challenges posed by space-based remote sensing
stories.summary: The US-Iran war has highlighted military challenges posed by space-based commercial remote sensing. Planet, a satellite imagery company, instituted a 14-day delay on releasing imagery of Iran, nearby military bases, Gulf States, and existing conflict zones.

stories.title: Russian Swimmers Allowed to Compete Under National Flag After Restrictions Dropped
stories.summary: World Aquatics has restored full membership rights to Russia and Belarus, permitting swimmers from both countries to compete under their national flags and anthems for the first time since restrictions were imposed.

stories.title: Turkey says Iran, US ‘are sincere’ about ceasefire
stories.summary: Turkey said both Iran and the United States are "sincere" about pursuing a ceasefire in the ongoing conflict. Ankara joined diplomatic efforts to mediate, despite being a vocal critic of Israel's military actions.

stories.title: Israel seeking to declare Turkey ‘new enemy’, says Ankara’s top diplomat
stories.summary: Turkey's top diplomat accused Israel of seeking to declare Turkey a "new enemy." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to confront Iran and its regional allies.

stories.title: Cameroon separatists declare three-day ceasefire for papal visit
stories.summary: A separatist alliance in Cameroon's English-speaking regions declared a three-day ceasefire to allow civilians and visitors safe passage during an upcoming visit by Pope Leo XIV to the country.

stories.title: Ghana says France is open to engaging on slavery reparations
stories.summary: Ghana said France expressed willingness to discuss reparations for transatlantic slavery following talks between Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama and French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris last week.

stories.title: Starmer announces talks to address the Strait of Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Starmer announced talks to be held this week, co-hosted with France, aimed at finding a diplomatic resolution to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: In Pacific Ocean, Super Typhoon Sinlakua bears down on group of remote US islands
stories.summary: Super Typhoon Sinlakua is expected to make landfall on Tuesday in the Northern Mariana Islands, bringing destructive winds, heavy rain, and flooding. The National Weather Service warned of potentially lengthy power outages. Guam, a US territory with about 170,000 residents and American military installations, is also under threat.

stories.title: Meta accused of monetising Israeli extremist platforms
stories.summary: A report by digital rights group 7amleh accused Meta of monetizing content from Israeli settler platforms while excluding Palestinians from monetization programs. The report highlights alleged disparities in the company's content policies.

stories.title: Peace was within reach. Then came the missiles. Will it be different this time?
stories.summary: Before the Islamabad talks, Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi publicly stated that peace between the US and Iran was "within reach," citing Tehran's agreement on uranium enrichment limits and IAEA verification. Subsequent missile strikes derailed those prospects.

stories.title: How Orban's loss could damage the British right
stories.summary: Former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's ouster from power has raised questions about the future of his trans-national right-wing network centered in Budapest. Analysts suggest the development could weaken allied movements, including elements of the British right such as Nigel Farage's Reform UK.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian strike on Bohodukhiv rises to four
stories.summary: The casualty toll from a Russian attack on the city of Bohodukhiv in Kharkiv region rose to four. Medical personnel are treating the injured, including a 7-year-old boy and an elderly man.

stories.title: US blockade of Iranian ports explained in two minutes
stories.summary: BBC security correspondent Frank Gardner provided a brief explanation of how the US naval blockade of Iranian ports is intended to operate.

stories.title: Polish PM hopes Hungary opposition victory ends asylum for ex-ministers
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he hoped Hungary's opposition election victory would end the political asylum granted to two former Polish ministers in Hungary, allowing them to be returned to face justice.

stories.title: EU: No peace possible while “Lebanon is in flames”
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen warned that peace efforts are impossible while Lebanon is under attack. She cited the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Israeli strikes on Lebanon as threats to regional stability.

stories.title: Hezbollah explosive drone injures at least eight IDF soldiers in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: A Hezbollah explosive drone struck Israeli Defense Forces soldiers in southern Lebanon, injuring at least eight. The wounded soldiers were evacuated to a hospital for further medical treatment.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson criticises UK ban on Palestine Action
stories.summary: American commentator Tucker Carlson criticized the UK government's ban on Palestine Action, alleging Israeli political pressure influenced the decision. Hundreds of people have been arrested in London in connection with the group's activities.

stories.title: War update: 53 combat engagements on front line since morning, Pokrovsk direction remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 53 Russian combat engagements along the front line since the morning. The Pokrovsk sector remained the most active area, with the heaviest Russian pressure concentrated there.

stories.title: What are the pros and cons of Trump’s Iranian naval blockade?
stories.summary: Analysis examines the potential effectiveness and drawbacks of President Trump's naval blockade of Iranian ports. The blockade aims to pressure Tehran but raises questions about whether it can achieve U.S. strategic objectives.

stories.title: Ukraine built Areion on Neptune’s backbone — and it can now be launched from almost anywhere
stories.summary: Ukraine developed the Areion missile system, building on the Neptune anti-ship missile platform. The new weapon is mobile enough to be launched from a trailer and is described as having cruise-missile-like strike capability.

stories.title: Israelis oppose Iran ceasefire, divided over whether to respect it: Poll
stories.summary: A poll found that a majority of Israelis oppose a ceasefire with Iran, with only 41% saying Israel should respect a ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: NATO allies refuse to join Trump's Strait of Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: NATO allies declined to participate in President Trump's naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Allied nations proposed instead to intervene in the waterway after the U.S.-Iran war concludes.

stories.title: Kremlin won’t congratulate Hungary’s new opposition leader, citing ‘unfriendly country’ status it ignored when congratulating Orban
stories.summary: The Kremlin announced it will not congratulate Peter Magyar, Hungary's incoming leader, on his parliamentary election victory, citing Hungary's "unfriendly country" status. Moscow had previously congratulated outgoing Prime Minister Viktor Orbán despite the same designation.

stories.title: Pope says he will continue to speak out against war after Trump attack
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV said he would continue speaking out against war following criticism from US President Donald Trump. The pontiff stated he did not want to enter a debate with Trump and said the Gospel's message should not be "abused."

stories.title: Chilean copper miner Codelco, contractors fined after deadly mine collapse
stories.summary: Chilean state copper miner Codelco was fined by labor authorities following a deadly collapse at its El Teniente mine. Three contractors whose workers were killed or injured received heavier sanctions, according to inspection records obtained by Reuters.

stories.title: US military eyes high-energy ‘laser dome’ for domestic air defense
stories.summary: The US military is pursuing high-energy laser weapons for domestic air defense, potentially creating a "laser dome" system. The effort responds to the growing threat posed by low-cost weaponized drones.

stories.title: French company Lafarge found guilty of paying $6.54 million to jihadists in Syria
stories.summary: A French court convicted cement company Lafarge and sentenced former CEO Bruno Lafont to six years in prison for paying $6.54 million to Islamic State in Syria between 2013 and 2014. Eight former employees were implicated in the case.

stories.title: Report: Kazakhstan raises Kazakh language bar for residency permits to B2, Russians say
stories.summary: Russians who relocated to Kazakhstan report that the country has raised its language requirement for residency permits. Applicants now reportedly must demonstrate Kazakh language proficiency at the B2 level, up from previous requirements.

stories.title: Bahrain summons Iraqi envoy as pro-Iranian attacks persist in Gulf
stories.summary: Bahrain summoned Iraq's ambassador over continuing drone attacks by pro-Iranian groups based in Iraq, which have persisted despite a ceasefire. Several Gulf countries and Jordan had previously demanded Baghdad act to stop the attacks.

stories.title: Military shows how it carries out operation to liberate Stepnohirsk in Zaporizhzhia
stories.summary: Fighters from Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate, together with other Defense Forces units, are conducting operations to liberate and clear the settlement of Stepnohirsk in the Zaporizhzhia sector. The military released footage showing the comprehensive operation.

stories.title: Senior IDF intel. officer: In minutes, we devastated Hezbollah, killing hundreds of terrorists
stories.summary: A senior IDF intelligence officer stated that Israeli strikes on April 8 killed approximately 250 Hezbollah fighters and targeted key command centers across Lebanon. The officer said total Hezbollah losses have exceeded 1,400.

stories.title: ‘Liberated’: Hungarian youths celebrate Viktor Orban’s defeat
stories.summary: Crowds gathered in central Budapest early Monday to celebrate the electoral defeat of nationalist Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who held power for 16 years. Young Hungarians danced, sang, and tore down government billboards, describing a feeling of liberation after the opposition's resounding victory.

stories.title: EU launches critical minerals procurement platform to cut China dependence
stories.summary: The European Union launched the critical minerals section of its energy and materials procurement platform on Monday, aimed at reducing dependence on China by aggregating purchases from regional buyers. The platform is part of the EU's RESourceEU strategy announced in December to develop supply chains for rare earths and other strategic minerals.

stories.title: YouTube removes pro-Iran channel producing anti-Trump videos
stories.summary: YouTube suspended the account of Explosive Media, also known as Akhbar Enfejari, a pro-Iran channel that produced anti-Trump content. The platform cited violations of its spam, deceptive practices, and scams policies.

stories.title: Palestinian family jailed after reporting settler attacks
stories.summary: A Palestinian family in the West Bank was jailed after reporting attacks by Israeli settlers. The incident highlights growing concerns about impunity for settler violence in the occupied territory.

stories.title: PSX sheds 6,600 points after Trump announces Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell 6,600 points, or 3.95%, closing at 160,591 on Monday after US-Iran peace talks collapsed and President Trump ordered a blockade of Iranian ports. The benchmark had opened around 161,000, down sharply from its previous close of 167,191.

stories.title: Hongkonger arrested on suspicion of underage sex and scamming girls of HK$33,000
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested a 36-year-old unemployed man on suspicion of having underage sex and defrauding teenage girls of more than HK$30,000 in a compensated dating scam. The suspect allegedly posed as a customer and had sex with a 15-year-old victim at a Yuen Long hotel.

stories.title: Russians attempt to intensify their offensive in Pokrovsk agglomeration — Defense Forces
stories.summary: Russian troops are attempting to intensify their offensive in the Pokrovsk agglomeration in eastern Ukraine. Ukrainian defense units report they are holding back the pressure and destroying Russian assault groups despite the difficult situation.

stories.title: Iran executed at least 1,639 in 2025, more hangings feared: NGOs
stories.summary: NGOs report that Iranian authorities executed at least 1,639 people in 2025, a figure among the highest in decades. Organizations warn that further executions may increase in the wake of the war against the U.S. and Israel.

stories.title: Global Jewish population is 15.8 m., almost half live in Israel, CBS reveals
stories.summary: Israel's Central Bureau of Statistics reported that the global Jewish population stands at approximately 15.8 million, with nearly half residing in Israel. In 1939, before World War II, the global Jewish population was 16.6 million, with only 3% living in Israel.

stories.title: Britain will not back blockade of Strait of Hormuz, PM Starmer says
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the United Kingdom would not support the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and would not be drawn into the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump's naval blockade raises economic pressure on Iran
stories.summary: The United States has imposed a naval blockade aimed at halting most of Iran's oil exports, cutting off Tehran's primary source of hard currency and raising questions about whether the pressure will lead to renewed negotiations or further escalation.

stories.title: US maritime restrictions increase economic pressure on Iran
stories.summary: The United States imposed naval restrictions aimed at halting most of Iran's oil exports, targeting Tehran's main source of hard currency. The measures are intended to increase economic pressure on Iran amid uncertainty over whether it will return to negotiations.

stories.title: Fitch affirms Pakistan’s credit rating at ‘B-’
stories.summary: Fitch Ratings affirmed Pakistan's long-term foreign currency issuer default rating at 'B-' with a stable outlook. The agency cited progress on fiscal consolidation and macroeconomic stability measures aligned with Pakistan's IMF program, along with rebuilt foreign exchange reserves.

stories.title: Turkish FM makes bold claims against Israel, Iran ceasefire hanging by a thread
stories.summary: Turkey's foreign minister made claims against Israel, while an Iran ceasefire appeared fragile. The report was part of the Jerusalem Post's daily news roundup.

stories.title: Ukraine and NATO are building new kind of wartime procurement
stories.summary: Ukraine and NATO are developing a new wartime procurement framework to accelerate defense acquisitions. The Alliance has backed the initiative with financial support.

stories.title: Iran releases assets of women’s football captain in Australia asylum row
stories.summary: Iran released the frozen assets of women's football captain Zahra Ghanbari, one of six players who had sought asylum in Australia. Ghanbari subsequently reversed her asylum decision and returned to Iran.

stories.title: Russia uses hybrid air defense systems due to shortage of 'Pantsir' systems — 'Flash'
stories.summary: Due to shortages of Pantsir surface-to-air missile systems, Russia has begun deploying hybrid air defense solutions. These include ground-based launchers adapted to fire air-to-air missiles, according to Ukrainian intelligence source Flash.

stories.title: Starmer says ‘highly fragile’ ceasefire with Iran should include Lebanon – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer described the ceasefire with Iran as "highly fragile" and said it should encompass Lebanon. He also stated that international cooperation would be needed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran ships nearing Hormuz blockade will be ‘immediately eliminated’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned that Iranian ships approaching a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz would be "immediately eliminated." Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu expressed full support for the blockade and rejected reports of a rift with Washington, emphasizing U.S. demands that Tehran halt its nuclear enrichment program.

stories.title: FM Lavrov Plans 2-Day China Visit This Week
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov is scheduled to visit China for two days this week. He is expected to discuss the wars in Iran and Ukraine with Chinese counterpart Wang Yi.

stories.title: Developer of Ukraine’s Ruta missiles just partnered with Rheinmetall to build Europe’s answer to HIMARS
stories.summary: Ukrainian developer of the Ruta missile system has partnered with German defense company Rheinmetall to build a European counterpart to the U.S. HIMARS rocket launcher. Rheinmetall aims to scale the system across NATO member states.

stories.title: At least one woman wounded by Hezbollah rocket barrage launched towards Nahariya, MDA confirms
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched a barrage of rockets toward the Israeli city of Nahariya, wounding at least one woman. Magen David Adom reported that six rockets were intercepted, but a seventh struck a residence, injuring the woman inside.

stories.title: Judge dismisses Trump’s lawsuit against Wall Street Journal and Murdoch
stories.summary: A Florida judge dismissed Donald Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over a report alleging Trump sent a lewd drawing to Jeffrey Epstein in 2003. The judge ruled the complaint failed to demonstrate actual malice, though Trump was given two weeks to refile.

stories.title: Mark Ruffalo and Emma Thompson among 1,000+ signatories on open letter opposing Paramount’s Warner buyout
stories.summary: Over 1,000 film and TV industry figures, including Mark Ruffalo, Emma Thompson, Joaquin Phoenix, and Kristen Stewart, signed an open letter opposing Paramount's pending acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. The signatories argued the merger would prioritize a small group of powerful stakeholders over the broader public good.

stories.title: Pakistan making efforts to revive failed US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's foreign ministry is working to bring the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table before the truce expires on April 21. The effort follows the collapse of talks held in Islamabad.

stories.title: Ex-Nigerian oil minister denies taking bribes
stories.summary: Former Nigerian oil minister Diezani Alison-Madueke denied taking bribes at proceedings in the United Kingdom. She is accused of living a lavish lifestyle at UK properties paid for and refurbished by industry figures.

stories.title: Trump and Vance showed Europe’s far right how to weaponize Ukraine. Don’t expect them to stop.
stories.summary: The article examines how U.S. President Trump and Vice President Vance have influenced Europe's far-right movements by using Ukraine as a political tool. It argues that Ukraine has been reduced to rhetoric benefiting a MAGA-European far-right alignment.

stories.title: Israel reports 1,000 antisemitic incidents worldwide, 20 killed in past year
stories.summary: Israel reported approximately 1,000 antisemitic incidents worldwide over the past year, with 20 people killed. More than 300 incidents were recorded in the United States, with over 130 each in the United Kingdom and France.

stories.title: Explainer: What does a US naval blockade of Iran mean for oil flows?
stories.summary: The US naval blockade of Iran's ports would remove approximately two million barrels of Iranian crude oil per day from global markets, significantly tightening supply.

stories.title: Trump is returning to a war with Iran that offers no easy victory for anyone
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict presents no clear path to victory for either side. Analysts draw parallels between Trump's current position and the challenges Israel faced during its operations in Gaza.

stories.title: Dangerous super typhoon barreling toward group of remote US islands
stories.summary: Super Typhoon Sinlaku is expected to make landfall Tuesday in the Northern Mariana Islands, a group of remote U.S. territories in the western Pacific. The National Weather Service warned of destructive winds, widespread heavy rain, and flooding from the dangerous storm.

stories.title: Nigeria: Wike-Backed Faction Renovates PDP National Secretariat Ahead of Resumption
stories.summary: The faction of Nigeria's Peoples Democratic Party backed by FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has begun renovating the party's national secretariat, Wadata Plaza, ahead of a planned resumption of activities.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'Leave Our Son Alone' - Amupitan's Kinsmen Tell 'Distractors'
stories.summary: Community members from Ayetoro Gbede in Nigeria's Kogi State urged critics to stop calling for the resignation of INEC Chairman Prof. Joash Amupitan, asking that he be allowed to carry out his duties without interference.

stories.title: How the Army is preparing to bring its first tiltrotor aircraft online
stories.summary: The US Army is preparing to bring its first tiltrotor aircraft, the MV-75, into service, aiming to acquire capabilities other military branches have had for years while avoiding the troubled reputation of the V-22 Osprey.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nerc Unveils New Mini-Grid Regulation to Boost Rural Electrification
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Electricity Regulatory Commission introduced a new regulatory framework for mini-grid development and operation, aimed at improving electricity access in underserved rural communities.

stories.title: Nigeria: Insurgents Reportedly Kill Colonel, Other Soldiers in Borno
stories.summary: Insurgents reportedly killed a colonel and other soldiers in an attack in Nigeria's Borno State. Military authorities have not yet issued an official statement regarding the incident.

stories.title: Bankova, Budapest, and Bunnies
stories.summary: The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest published by War on the Rocks, curates commentary and analysis from Ukrainian media covering politics, daily life, and public debate. The latest edition addresses developments related to Kyiv, Budapest, and domestic Ukrainian discourse.

stories.title: Video: Trump says he isn't 'a big fan' of Pope Leo
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters he is not "a big fan" of Pope Leo. Trump accused the pope of being tolerant of Iran possessing a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: Despite Gaza ceasefire, antisemitism rates higher in several countries, TAU report says
stories.summary: A Tel Aviv University report found that antisemitism rates remain elevated in several countries despite the Gaza ceasefire. The post-ceasefire environment in 2025 was more hostile to Jews compared to the period before the October 7 massacre, even in countries that saw a decline from 2024 levels.

stories.title: Ghana: Football Player Killed in Highway Robbery, Ghana Police Confirms
stories.summary: Ghana Police confirmed that a Berekum Chelsea football player was killed in a highway robbery attack near Ahyiresu in the Ashanti Region.

stories.title: Trump says Iranian ships that come close to US blockade will be eliminated
stories.summary: President Trump warned on Truth Social that Iranian ships approaching the U.S. naval blockade would be "immediately eliminated." He stated that 158 Iranian navy ships had already been destroyed, with only small "fast attack ships" remaining.

stories.title: AFU thwarts Russian attempts to set up pontoon crossing in Lyman direction
stories.summary: In the Lyman sector, Ukraine's Signum unmanned systems battalion destroyed an enemy vehicle and prevented Russian forces from establishing a pontoon crossing. The action thwarted Russian attempts to set up the crossing in the Lyman direction.

stories.title: Israeli forces fire teargas at schoolchildren holding West Bank sit-in
stories.summary: Israeli forces fired teargas at Palestinian schoolchildren staging a sit-in in the occupied West Bank after settlers blocked access to their school. The incident occurred on the first day pupils were due back in class after more than 40 days. The Israeli military said it had dispersed an "unusual gathering."

stories.title: Will Orbán’s defeat in Hungary be a turning point for Europe? – The Latest
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule in Hungary ended after the opposition Tisza party, led by Péter Magyar, won a landslide election victory. Orbán conceded quickly, describing the result as "painful but unambiguous." Attention now turns to how Magyar will reshape Hungary's relations with the EU and NATO.

stories.title: Israelis oppose Iran truce, divided over whether to respect it
stories.summary: A poll found that nearly two-thirds of Israelis oppose the ceasefire with Iran. Public opinion is divided on whether Israel should respect the truce or resume military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Russia’s Easter “ceasefire” stopped Shaheds for a day — and nothing else
stories.summary: Russia declared an Easter ceasefire but Ukraine reported 10,721 violations across the front lines. Ukrainian authorities said Russian forces shot four Ukrainian prisoners of war near Veterynarne in Kharkiv Oblast after the truce formally began, while Shahed drone attacks paused for only one day.

stories.title: Chinese Workers Protest Unpaid Wages in Russia’s Far East
