stories.summary: Around 200 Chinese employees of Russian-Chinese contractor Petro-Hehua marched through Komsomolsk-na-Amure in Russia's Far East on Sunday, demanding unpaid wages.

stories.title: U.K. will not back blockade of Strait of Hormuz, says PM Starmer
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the UK would not support the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Starmer noted that British minesweepers were in the region but said their mission was focused on keeping the strait open for navigation.

stories.title: Iranian passenger plane destroyed in US strikes on Mashhad International Airport - report
stories.summary: Reports indicated that US strikes on Mashhad International Airport in Iran destroyed an Iranian passenger aircraft. The United States has not officially claimed responsibility for the strike.

stories.title: Deadline passes for US blockade of Hormuz, Iran threatens to retaliate against Gulf neighbours
stories.summary: The U.S. military blockade of ships leaving Iranian ports began on Monday after peace talks between the warring sides collapsed in Pakistan. Iran's military warned it would treat the blockade as an act of piracy. Oil prices surged as the Strait of Hormuz disruption continued.

stories.title: Future Hungarian PM Magyar makes first statements on EU’s €90 billion loan for Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar made his first statements regarding the European Union's €90 billion loan for Ukraine. The loan had previously been blocked by outgoing Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's government.

stories.title: Lebanon Latest: Talks scheduled as Israeli strikes continue
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon have pushed the death toll past 2,000. Ceasefire talks are being scheduled, but divisions among the parties involved are deepening.

stories.title: Israel seeks to declare Turkiye ‘new enemy’, says FM Fidan after Netanyahu’s remarks on Erdogan
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan accused Israel of seeking to declare Türkiye a "new enemy" after remarks by Prime Minister Netanyahu about President Erdoğan. Fidan said the shift toward framing Türkiye as a threat is becoming an Israeli state strategy, following tensions over the conflict in the region.

stories.title: Russian troops strike Bohodukhiv: Two people injured, homes damaged
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out drone strikes on the city of Bohodukhiv in the Kharkiv region, injuring two women. Ten private houses were damaged in the attack.

stories.title: Ex-UK PM Boris Johnson criticises ‘timidity’ over Ukraine after visit for film
stories.summary: Former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson criticized Western "timidity" in supporting Ukraine after a 72-hour documentary trip that took him to frontline areas near Zaporizhzhia. He insisted Ukraine can win the war but that allies are failing to honor their pledges.

stories.title: Nigerian Air Forces launches investigation into deadly airstrike in Yobe state
stories.summary: Nigeria's Air Force has launched an investigation into a Sunday airstrike in Yobe state that allegedly killed dozens of civilians in the country's northeast.

stories.title: ‘No time to waste’: Pro-EU Magyar vows ‘new era’ in Hungary after ousting Orban
stories.summary: Peter Magyar's pro-EU Tisza party won a two-thirds parliamentary majority in Hungary's elections, ousting long-serving Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Magyar pledged a "new era" and said the country had been "plundered and ruined" under his predecessor.

stories.title: The US blockade of Iran is a gamble. Will it work?
stories.summary: The United States military has imposed a blockade aimed at cutting off Iran's vital trade routes. Questions persist about whether the strategy will achieve its intended objectives or prove counterproductive.

stories.title: Poland’s premier hails Hungary vote as blow to authoritarian rule
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Hungary's election results demonstrate that Europe is not inevitably headed toward authoritarian rule. The center-right Tisza party ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year hold on power.

stories.title: Moscow Warns of ‘Perfect Storm’ for EU After Orbán’s Defeat in Hungary
stories.summary: The Kremlin responded in measured terms to the election defeat of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, while other Russian officials and pro-Kremlin commentators used the result to criticize EU member states opposed to Moscow.

stories.title: French cement maker convicted of financing terror groups to keep its Syria plant working
stories.summary: A French court fined cement maker Lafarge more than €1 million and sentenced its former CEO to six years in prison for paying nearly €5.6 million to Islamic State and other armed groups in Syria between 2013 and 2014. The payments were made to keep the company's Syrian plant operational during the civil war.

stories.title: HASC chair: Trillion-dollar defense budgets are the ‘new normal.’ Reconciliation is less certain.
stories.summary: House Armed Services Committee Chair stated that trillion-dollar defense budgets are becoming the "new normal" for the United States. However, achieving those levels through the budget reconciliation process remains uncertain, particularly for the administration's military space priorities.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks police vehicle in Sumy region, leaving one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a police vehicle in the town of Bilopillia in the Sumy region with a drone. One law enforcement officer was injured in the attack.

stories.title: Gambling on death: Polymarket and the dark rise of war betting
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran war has become the first major conflict traded in real time on prediction markets such as Polymarket. Evidence of insider trading on war-related bets is already emerging.

stories.title: Ukraine launched two rockets into space from its territory during war, plans to make own space force
stories.summary: Ukraine announced it launched two rockets into space from its own territory during the ongoing war and plans to establish its own space force. A Ukrainian lawmaker highlighted the country's missile defense and hypersonic strike capabilities.

stories.title: The Pentagon wants a 188 percent bump for missile procurement. Can industry deliver?
stories.summary: The Pentagon's fiscal year 2027 budget request includes $70.5 billion for munitions, representing a 188 percent increase in missile procurement funding. Analysts anticipate the Department of Defense will distribute spending across multiple years and pursue multiyear procurement contracts to help industry scale up production capacity.

stories.title: Iran war: Talks collapse is bad news for ordinary Iranians
stories.summary: US-Iran diplomatic talks have collapsed, raising uncertainty about prospects for a negotiated resolution. Internal challenges within Iran further complicate the outlook for any future agreement.

stories.title: US blockade of Iran ports begins
stories.summary: The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports officially began on Monday at 1400 GMT after a deadline set by President Trump passed. The blockade followed the collapse of weekend peace talks with Tehran, though non-Iranian vessels will be allowed through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UK: Six Palestine Action activists stand trial over Elbit Systems break-in
stories.summary: Six Palestine Action activists are standing trial in the United Kingdom on criminal damage charges. The charges relate to a break-in at a factory owned by Elbit Systems, Israel's largest weapons manufacturer.

stories.title: Pakistan PM Sharif says 'full effort' still on to resolve conflict
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that full efforts continue to resolve the conflict between the United States and Iran. His comments came a day after talks between the two sides in Islamabad concluded without an agreement.

stories.title: Hungarians look to changed future after pro-EU Magyar's election landslide
stories.summary: Hungarians awoke to a political upheaval on Monday after Péter Magyar's centre-right opposition won a landslide election victory, ousting long-serving PM Viktor Orbán. Magyar pledged a sweeping anti-corruption drive and stronger judicial independence to help unlock frozen EU funds. Local markets surged on the news.

stories.title: The Telegraph deletes story falsely claiming Erdogan threatened to invade Israel
stories.summary: The UK's Telegraph newspaper deleted an article that falsely claimed Turkish President Erdogan had threatened to invade Israel. The story reportedly relied on statements Erdogan made two years earlier, taken out of context.

stories.title: Pro-EU Hungarian PM-elect Magyar vows to bring in 'new era'
stories.summary: Hungary's premier-elect Péter Magyar pledged to usher in a "new era" after his pro-EU election victory over Viktor Orbán. EU leaders from Madrid to Helsinki hope the result will help unify the bloc as it faces hybrid warfare from Moscow, tensions with Washington, and economic pressure from Beijing.

stories.title: US-Vatican feud over Iran: Pope Leo pushes back on Trump's criticism
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV pushed back on Monday against President Donald Trump's criticism of the Vatican's stance on the U.S.-Israel war in Iran, saying the Church's appeals for peace are rooted in the Gospel. His comments came as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz appeared to halt and oil prices resumed climbing following Trump's blockade announcement.

stories.title: Less pomp, more cosplay: Prince Harry and Meghan’s ‘faux royal’ Australian tour
stories.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are set to arrive in Sydney on Tuesday for a four-day Australian visit. The tour includes promotional events, a children's hospital visit, a women's homeless service, and a war memorial, with Harry also making a solo trip to Canberra.

stories.title: Drone attack in Kherson region kills woman, injures another
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack in the Kherson region killed an 89-year-old woman in the village of Osokorivka. A 65-year-old man in the city of Kherson was also injured in the strike.

stories.title: Middle East war boosts London Heathrow airport traffic
stories.summary: London's Heathrow Airport reported a 10 percent increase in transit passengers during March. The rise was driven by Gulf countries closing their airspace due to the U.S.-Iran war, rerouting travelers through the UK hub.

stories.title: Two killed in Ukraine despite Easter ceasefire, governor says
stories.summary: Two people were killed and one injured by Russian troops in Ukraine's frontline Donetsk region before the expiry of an Orthodox Easter ceasefire, according to a local official. The deaths occurred despite the truce intended to mark the holiday.

stories.title: US says to blockade Iran ports: What could be the consequences?
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced it would begin a blockade of all Iranian ports on Monday after peace talks between the warring sides collapsed in Pakistan. Iran's military warned it would treat any such action as piracy, raising concerns about a major escalation in the conflict.

stories.title: Electoral earthquake: Hungary vote triggers setback for Putin and Trump
stories.summary: Hungarian voters ousted Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power, electing pro-European challenger Péter Magyar in a landslide. The result dealt a significant blow to Orbán's global far-right alliances, including his close ties with U.S. President Trump and Russian President Putin.

stories.title: Massive Attack frontman arrested in London for backing banned anti-Israel group
stories.summary: Massive Attack frontman Robert Del Naja was arrested in London for supporting Palestine Action, which the UK has proscribed as a terrorist organization. Del Naja described the arrest as "farcical authoritarian overreach" at a protest event.

stories.title: Israel presses assault on Lebanon border town ahead of US-hosted talks
stories.summary: Israeli troops launched an assault on a key town in southern Lebanon to seize it from Hezbollah fighters on the eve of rare talks between Israeli and Lebanese envoys in Washington. Lebanon's foreign minister said Beirut would use the face-to-face negotiations to press for a ceasefire.

stories.title: Turkish FM: Israel trying to ‘declare Turkey the new enemy’ after Iran
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan accused Israel of trying to portray Turkey as its new enemy following the Iran conflict. Fidan alleged that both Israeli government and opposition lawmakers are pursuing a coordinated strategy against Ankara.

stories.title: Gaza ‘heading towards famine’ as bread shortages deepen amid Israeli curbs
stories.summary: Gaza is facing deepening bread shortages and growing risk of famine amid Israeli restrictions on supplies. Residents in areas including the Nuseirat refugee camp are queuing for hours to receive food from charity kitchens.

stories.title: Mark Dixon: “We must declare the Economic World War on Russia”
stories.summary: Businessman Mark Dixon argued that the West should declare an "Economic World War" against Russia. He contended that existing economic tools have never been used at full power despite four years of Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Iranian crude returns to India after seven years as tankers dock at key ports
stories.summary: Iranian crude oil shipments arrived at Indian ports for the first time in seven years under a one-month exemption allowing the sale of Iranian oil already in transit. The measure was intended to ease global supply disruptions and contain rising prices.

stories.title: The 10-point plan to wage the Economic World War—to harm Russia and help Ukraine
stories.summary: A 10-point plan was proposed to intensify economic warfare against Russia in support of Ukraine. The plan warns that Russia's financial strength could tip the global balance between democracy and autocracy.

stories.title: UWC president congratulates Péter Magyar on election win, calls for unity
stories.summary: Paul Grod, president of the Ukrainian World Congress, congratulated Péter Magyar and Hungary's Tisza Party on their election victory. The UWC characterized the result as a setback for Russia's destabilization strategy in Europe.

stories.title: Almost all Russian staff pulled from Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant
stories.summary: Russia has withdrawn almost all of its staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, according to the head of Russia's atomic energy agency Rosatom. The withdrawal was announced on Monday amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Iranian railroads damaged by air strikes repaired, says state TV
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that rail infrastructure damaged by U.S.-Israeli air strikes in five provinces has been repaired. Rebuilt lines include routes connecting Tehran to Tabriz and Tabriz to Mashhad.

stories.title: Turkey says NATO should reset ties with Trump at next summit, prepare for future
stories.summary: Turkey called on NATO to reset its relationship with the Trump administration at its next summit. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte acknowledged Trump's frustrations while noting that most European nations have contributed to the US war effort in Iran.

stories.title: Trump says Iranian ships will be ‘eliminated’ as US naval blockade begins
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned that Iranian ships approaching the American naval blockade of Iranian ports would be "eliminated." Iran characterized the blockade as Trump's retaliatory measure against the global economy.

stories.title: Russia’s KRONA just entered testing. Ukraine and its allies need to move faster
stories.summary: Russia's Kalashnikov Group has entered testing of its KRONA anti-drone system, which features two types of guidance. The article urges Ukraine and its allies to accelerate countermeasure development in response.

stories.title: 'Israel cannot live without hostility': Turkey warns Israel may target it next
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned that Israel may target Turkey next, stating that Israel cannot exist without hostility. His remarks followed President Erdogan's sharp escalation of rhetoric threatening possible military action against Israel.

stories.title: Anas Sarwar asks voters in Scotland to give Labour five years to ‘fix SNP’s mess’
stories.summary: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar appealed to voters to give Labour five years to address issues left by the SNP, pledging more housing, tax cuts, and a smaller public sector. Recent polls place Scottish Labour third or fourth behind the SNP, Reform, and the Scottish Greens ahead of May elections.

stories.title: What does a US naval blockade of Iran mean for oil flows?
stories.summary: The US military announced it would block shipping traffic in and out of Iran's ports starting Monday at 10am ET, following the failure of US-Iran peace talks held in Islamabad. The blockade would remove roughly two million barrels per day of Iranian oil from global markets.

stories.title: Ghanaian Premier League player Dominic Frimpong killed during attack on team bus
stories.summary: Ghanaian Premier League winger Dominic Frimpong, 20, of Berekum Chelsea was killed during a suspected armed robbery attack on the team's bus. Ghana's football association confirmed the death.

stories.title: Ukraine seeks security cooperation with Iraq and African nations - Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is pursuing security cooperation with Iraq and several African nations. He indicated that Kyiv is in active communication with nine countries on security matters.

stories.title: Ben-Gvir says he feels like he 'owns' Al-Aqsa during raid
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said he felt like he "owns" the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound during a visit. His remarks were followed by Jewish worshippers performing rituals at the site that are considered illegal under the longstanding Status Quo agreement.

stories.title: Bahrain summons Iraqi charge d'affaires over attacks launched from Iraq
stories.summary: Bahrain summoned Iraq's chargé d'affaires in Manama over drone attacks allegedly launched from Iraqi territory against Bahrain and other Gulf states. Bahrain delivered a formal protest and warned it reserves the right to take measures to protect its security.

stories.title: Khakassia governor says residents backed Stalin monument after vote drew 2% of population
stories.summary: Residents of Russia's Khakassia republic voted in favor of erecting a monument to Soviet leader Joseph Stalin in Abakan's Victory Park. Governor Valentin Konovalov announced the result after a public vote organized by the Public Chamber, though only about 2% of the population participated.

stories.title: US moves to block Iranian ports as Tehran threatens retaliatory strikes on Gulf hubs
stories.summary: The United States moved to implement a blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran peace talks collapsed. Pakistan, which mediated the negotiations, continued diplomatic efforts as a two-week ceasefire remained in place.

stories.title: Russia is now using one Shahed to distract — and second to kill crew shooting it down
stories.summary: Russia has adopted a new tactic of deploying one Shahed drone as a decoy to distract Ukrainian air defense crews while a second drone targets the crew. The approach exploits vulnerabilities among Ukraine's mobile drone-hunting teams.

stories.title: Could Trump’s Hormuz blockade derail China summit with Xi Jinping?
stories.summary: Analysts warn that President Trump's threatened blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could complicate his planned summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping by forcing Beijing into a political dilemma over energy security and its relationship with Iran.

stories.title: French cement giant guilty of financing IS and other militant groups in Syria
stories.summary: A Paris court found French cement giant Lafarge guilty of financing the Islamic State and other militant groups in Syria. The company reportedly paid approximately $6.5 million to jihadist organizations to keep its cement plant operational during the Syrian war.

stories.title: Trump’s threat to blockade Hormuz: Why it’s the latest major escalation
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz represents a major escalation that could undermine the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Global markets slide as Donald Trump orders Strait of Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Global financial markets declined after US President Donald Trump ordered a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions following the breakdown of US-Iran peace talks.

stories.title: European security 'risks becoming more regionalised' if NATO falls apart, military expert warns
stories.summary: Military expert Jean-François Bélanger of the Royal Danish Defence College warned that European security risks becoming regionalized if NATO were to collapse. He told FRANCE 24 that NATO's strength lies in aggregating different threat perceptions among its members, and a standalone European army could fracture rapid resource mobilization.

stories.title: Oil jumped 8% as Trump’s Hormuz blockade undid the ceasefire crash
stories.summary: Global oil prices surged 8% following President Trump's naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, reversing a previous ceasefire-driven decline. Negotiations collapsed in Pakistan, and the blockade replaced the truce, ending a brief window of relief for Russia's war-related oil revenues.

stories.title: Kremlin Repeats Offer to Take Iran’s Highly Enriched Uranium
stories.summary: The Kremlin reiterated its offer to take custody of Iran's highly enriched uranium amid stalled negotiations. Talks between Iran and the United States over the weekend failed to produce a deal.

stories.title: Hungary’s PM-elect Magyar sends warm overture to China, vows fair play for firms
stories.summary: Hungary's prime minister-elect Peter Magyar extended a diplomatic overture to China, calling it one of the world's most powerful countries and expressing openness to mutual high-level visits with Beijing.

stories.title: Will Orban's defeat in Hungary lead to EU sanctions on Israel?
stories.summary: The electoral defeat of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán removes a key EU-level shield that had helped Israel avoid European sanctions. However, divisions within the EU and uncertainty about incoming leader Peter Magyar's policies mean concrete action remains unclear.

stories.title: World Bank chief sounds alarm about looming jobs crisis even after war ends
stories.summary: World Bank President Ajay Banga warned that developing economies are on track to generate only about 400 million jobs over the next 10 to 15 years, leaving an 800-million-job deficit for the 1.2 billion people expected to reach working age in that period.

stories.title: Iran denies charging toll for Indian tankers transiting Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to India denied that Tehran has charged tolls for Indian tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The denial followed threats by President Trump to block passage for vessels making payments to Iran.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Derhachi in Kharkiv region, wounding at least five
stories.summary: A Russian strike hit the town of Derhachi in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, wounding at least five people. Two of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.

stories.title: Far-right MK apologizes, deletes post criticizing Trump over Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli far-right lawmaker Zvika Fogel of Otzma Yehudit apologized and deleted a social media post criticizing President Trump over the Iran war. Prime Minister Netanyahu reportedly told lawmakers to "choose your words carefully."

stories.title: Pressed by Russian Drones, Ukraine Turns to Ground Robots
stories.summary: Ukraine is increasingly deploying ground-based robots for both logistics and combat operations as Russian drone attacks intensify. The shift toward unmanned ground vehicles represents an adaptation by Ukrainian forces to counter persistent aerial threats on the battlefield.

stories.title: Kremlin says Russia will maintain ‘pragmatic’ ties with Hungary under new government
stories.summary: The Kremlin said Russia expects to maintain "pragmatic" contacts with Hungary's new government after Péter Magyar's Tisza Party won parliamentary elections. The statement signals Moscow's intent to preserve diplomatic ties despite the change in Hungarian leadership.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia renew drone strikes after Easter truce
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia resumed drone strikes following the expiration of an Easter truce. Ukrainian authorities reported that an infrastructure facility was hit in the central-eastern Dnipropetrovsk region.

stories.title: Armed gangs behind killings, kidnappings in Nigeria
stories.summary: Armed gangs continue to carry out killings and kidnappings in northern Nigeria's Sokoto State. Separately, the Tigray People's Liberation Front accused Ethiopia's government of violating the Pretoria peace agreement that ended the 2020–2022 war, a conflict that killed hundreds of thousands.

stories.title: Ukraine just X-rayed Russia’s $100,000 drone — and found components from China, Taiwan, and Switzerland
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces disassembled and analyzed a Russian drone valued at approximately $100,000, finding components sourced from China, Taiwan, and Switzerland. The report notes that only the European Union has sanctioned the factory producing the drone.

stories.title: Israel steps up strikes on Lebanon and Hezbollah attacks continue as talks loom
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon have killed more than 160 people since Friday as the military continues its campaign against Hezbollah. The escalation comes despite an existing US-Iran ceasefire and ahead of anticipated diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Pakistan eyes narrow window to resuscitate US-Iran talks after breakdown
stories.summary: Marathon peace talks between the United States and Iran ended without agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan is seeking a narrow window to revive negotiations as the fragile ceasefire faces growing strain.

stories.title: 4 policemen injured in militant attack on polio team in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary: Four police officers were injured in a militant attack on a polio vaccination team in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The injured officers were taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.

stories.title: Turkey pushes for larger role in Europe’s defense as Trump questions NATO
stories.summary: Turkey's defense minister urged European allies not to exclude Ankara from EU defense initiatives, warning that doing so would cause more damage than a U.S. troop withdrawal from the continent. The push comes as President Trump's questioning of NATO commitments prompts European nations to reassess their defense posture.

stories.title: Middle East War: Iran threatens Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman
stories.summary: Iran's military has warned that no ports in the Persian Gulf or Gulf of Oman will be safe if its own ports are threatened. The statement followed a US military announcement of a blockade targeting all Iranian ports and coastal areas.

stories.title: Ghana's Partey denies two new counts of rape
stories.summary: Ghanaian footballer Thomas Partey, aged 32, pleaded not guilty to two new counts of rape at Southwark Crown Court in London.

stories.title: Airstrike in Nigeria kills dozens, civilians feared among victims
stories.summary: A military airstrike hit a market in northeastern Nigeria, killing at least 56 people and injuring 14, according to a UN report. Local residents and rights groups say civilians were among the victims.

stories.title: US-Iran talks on long-term deal doomed as long as both sides insist they won the war
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran negotiations on a long-term deal remain stalled as both sides claim victory in the recent conflict. Iran seeks major concessions on nuclear and Hormuz issues, while Washington refuses to make concessions to a country it recently bombed.

stories.title: Israel kills three people in Gaza following new ceasefire talks
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza as mediators were meeting with Hamas leaders to strengthen the existing ceasefire. The strike occurred amid renewed diplomatic efforts to stabilize the truce.

stories.title: Israeli kills three people in Gaza following new ceasefire talks
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza as mediators met with Hamas leaders to reinforce the ceasefire. The strike came amid ongoing diplomatic efforts involving multiple regional actors.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV pushes back as Donald Trump criticism escalates
stories.summary: US-born Pope Leo XIV responded to President Donald Trump's public criticism by stating that the Vatican's calls for peace regarding the US-Israeli war in Iran are rooted in the Gospel. The pope said he does not fear the Trump administration.

stories.title: As Antisemitism spikes, JWed.com sees more Jewish marriages with a record 4,100 - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Jewish dating service JWed.com reported a record 4,100 marriages amid a spike in antisemitism. The platform serves observant and traditional Jewish singles seeking committed relationships.

stories.title: Slovakia's Fico ready to cooperate with Hungary's new prime minister
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico congratulated Hungary's incoming leader Peter Magyar and offered "intensive cooperation." Fico also expressed gratitude to outgoing Prime Minister Viktor Orbán following the major election upset.

stories.title: Starmer, Macron say UK and France to discuss ‘multinational mission’ to safeguard Hormuz
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Starmer and French President Macron announced discussions on a multinational naval mission to safeguard the Strait of Hormuz. Macron described the effort as strictly defensive and separate from the U.S. blockade, while Starmer confirmed the UK would not join Trump's operation.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Iran ceasefire could end at any moment, we back Trump’s blockade
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu warned that the Iran ceasefire could end at any moment and expressed support for Trump's naval blockade. The IDF said it remains on heightened alert, while Netanyahu cited disagreements over Hormuz and enriched uranium as reasons the U.S. walked away from talks.

stories.title: Australia appoints woman to lead its army for the first time
stories.summary: Australia announced that Lieutenant General Susan Coyle will become the first woman to serve as chief of army, effective July. She currently holds the role of chief of joint capabilities and will replace Lieutenant General Simon Stuart. The appointment comes as Australia's military works to increase female representation amid harassment allegations.

stories.title: Russian airstrikes on Riasne in Kharkiv region wound two
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the village of Riasne in the Kharkiv region with guided aerial bombs, injuring two women. One of the women is in critical condition.

stories.title: US to start Hormuz blockade amid renewed Israeli threat to Iran
stories.summary: The United States announced plans to blockade Iranian ports following the collapse of peace talks in Islamabad. The move comes alongside renewed Israeli threats to resume bombing campaigns against Iran.

stories.title: With Joint Innovation Outpost, Army ‘operationalized an acquisition cell’
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has established the Joint Innovation Outpost (JIOP) to provide a permanent acquisition and industry experimentation capability for the XVIII Airborne Division. Rather than one-off efforts, JIOP is designed to create an enduring process, with officials hoping to expand the model across the broader Army.

stories.title: Cold Response 2026: NATO holds Arctic drills to test readiness against Russia
stories.summary: NATO conducted large-scale military exercises called Cold Response 2026 in the Arctic, simulating a Russian invasion. Thousands of soldiers, armoured vehicles, ships, and helicopters operated in sub-zero conditions to test alliance readiness and signal deterrence to Moscow.

stories.title: Lebanon: Red Cross teams inspect wreckage after Israeli airstrikes damage ambulances
stories.summary: On April 13, 2026, Lebanese Red Cross teams inspected ambulances damaged by Israeli airstrikes in the coastal city of Tyre. Rescue crews also cleared debris in the nearby village of Maaroub.

stories.title: A third of Holocaust survivors in Israel living in poverty, study finds
stories.summary: A study found that roughly one-third of Holocaust survivors in Israel are living in poverty. An Israeli mental health charity has received thousands of calls from survivors since the Iran war began, with many reporting feelings of loneliness and helplessness.

stories.title: Why Beijing isn’t panicking over Hungarian PM Viktor Orban’s stunning election defeat
stories.summary: Peter Magyar's Tisza Party won a landslide victory in Hungary's parliamentary elections, ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule. Chinese analysts suggest the political transition is unlikely to dramatically alter Hungary-China ties or broader China-EU relations.

stories.title: US-Iran war: Is Pakistan a real peacemaker?
stories.summary: Pakistan has been credited with mediating between the United States and Iran, but Islamabad faces questions about its credibility given its ongoing conflict with Afghanistan and domestic crackdowns on opposition figures.

stories.title: Trump family dealings may forever break taboo on US presidents profiting from office
stories.summary: Reports highlight the expanding business ventures of the Trump family during his second term, particularly in the Middle East. The dealings represent a significant departure from past presidential norms of avoiding the appearance of profiting from public office.

stories.title: UK murder of 3 girls by teenager should have been prevented, says inquiry
stories.summary: A UK public inquiry concluded that the 2024 murders of three girls at a Taylor Swift-themed dance event in Southport, England, by teenager Axel Rudakubana should have been prevented. The inquiry found a fundamental failure by state bodies to recognize the threat he posed.

stories.title: Millions of people in Sudan surviving on one meal a day as food crisis deepens, NGOs say
stories.summary: Aid organizations report that millions of people in Sudan are surviving on one meal a day as the country's food crisis deepens. The ongoing war has caused widespread hunger and displaced millions across the country.

stories.title: Voyager is fortifying the U.S. Defense supply chain
stories.summary: Voyager is working to strengthen the U.S. defense supply chain by supporting Pentagon efforts to bolster the domestic defense industrial base.

stories.title: Cop martyred, 4 injured in attack on Hangu police team en route to provide security for polio drive
stories.summary: A police constable was killed and four officers were injured when attackers opened fire on a law enforcement team in Hangu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The officers were en route to provide security for a polio vaccination campaign on its first day, running April 13–19.

stories.title: Ankara says Israel seeks to declare Turkey 'new enemy'
stories.summary: Turkey's top diplomat accused Israel of attempting to designate Turkey as its next adversary. The foreign minister stated that Israel "cannot live without an enemy" and is now targeting Ankara after the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Enemy strike hits area near freight train locomotive in Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: In the Dnipropetrovsk region, railway workers halted a commuter train and evacuated passengers during a morning air threat. An enemy strike subsequently hit near a freight train locomotive in the area.

stories.title: Trump's framing of war as Iran's barbarism vs civilised West is a huge lie
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that two conceptual fallacies underpin the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran: the portrayal of Iran as a barbaric nation and the framing of the United States as a representative of Western civilization.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's UN Envoy, Jimoh Ibrahim, to Deliver Keynote Address At Iias 10th Anniversary
stories.summary: Nigeria's Ambassador to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, is scheduled to deliver a keynote address titled "The Nigerian Project Revisited: Crisis, Continuity, and Possibility" at the IIAS 10th anniversary event.

stories.title: Nigeria: ADC Crisis - What Lawyers Say About INEC's Decision On David Mark, Nafiu Bala Factions
stories.summary: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission withdrew recognition from rival factions claiming leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress party, citing a Court of Appeal ruling. Legal experts weighed in on the implications of INEC's decision regarding the David Mark and Nafiu Bala factions.

stories.title: Nigeria: Terror Attacks Intensify in Western Zamfara - What We Know So Far
stories.summary: Terror attacks have intensified in western Zamfara State, Nigeria, a region bordering Niger, Kebbi, and Sokoto States, all of which have also experienced renewed attacks by armed bandits.

stories.title: Iran carried out highest number of executions in decades
stories.summary: Human rights organizations report that Iran carried out its highest number of executions in decades. NGOs warn that additional executions may follow in the aftermath of anti-government protests that swept the country.

stories.title: Australia appoints first female army chief
stories.summary: Australia has appointed Major General Susan Coyle as its first female army chief, effective July. Coyle joined the Australian Army at age 17.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia, Afreximbank Deepen Push for African Self-Reliance and Economic Cooperation
stories.summary: Ethiopia and the African Export-Import Bank held high-level engagements in Addis Ababa focused on advancing Africa's economic self-reliance and strengthening continental cooperation in response to global economic pressures.

stories.title: Taiwan industries cheer Beijing’s 10-point plan to boost cross-strait ties
stories.summary: Taiwanese industry groups welcomed Beijing's 10-point plan to promote cross-strait economic exchanges. Taiwan's main opposition Kuomintang party expressed relief that the measures focused on economic and livelihood issues rather than politically sensitive topics.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill three Palestinians in Gaza, arrest dozens in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed three Palestinians in Gaza and arrested dozens in the occupied West Bank. The actions coincided with meetings between Palestinian groups and mediators from Egypt, Turkey, and Qatar in Cairo to discuss the fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Liberia: China Envoy Lauds Construction of Monrovia Super Mall
stories.summary: China's Ambassador to Liberia, H.E. Yin Chengwu, praised the grand opening of the Monrovia Super Mall as a symbol of growing investor confidence and deepening China-Liberia trade relations.

stories.title: Is Trump’s new naval blockade 3D chess or grasping at straws?
stories.summary: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports was set to begin at 10 a.m. Eastern Time following the collapse of weekend peace talks in Islamabad. Observers remain divided on whether the move represents a strategic escalation or desperation.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s Mirror star Keung To fined HK$2,200 for driving offences
stories.summary: Hong Kong singer Keung To of the boy band Mirror was fined HK$2,200 for careless driving, running a red light, and failing to display a probationary sign on his vehicle.

stories.title: Trump says ‘not a big fan’ of Pope Leo after his anti-war message
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland that he is "not a big fan" of Pope Leo XIV, after the pontiff urged world leaders to end the war in the Middle East during a speech at St Peter's Basilica. Trump called the American-born pope "very liberal."

stories.title: Pakistan steps up push to end polio with second nationwide campaign
stories.summary: Pakistan launched its second nationwide polio vaccination campaign of 2025 on Monday, aiming to immunize over 45 million children under five. More than 400,000 health workers will go door to door across all provinces, territories, and Islamabad through April 19, also administering Vitamin A supplements.

stories.title: US blockade of Iran will be major military endeavor, experts say
stories.summary: Experts said the announced U.S. blockade of Iran would constitute a major military undertaking. The U.S. military has not yet disclosed basic operational details, including how many warships would be deployed to enforce the blockade.

stories.title: At least six killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: At least six people were killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon. Israel has indicated it is close to taking over the major town of Bint Jbeil, with peace talks in the U.S. pending.

stories.title: China calls reports it supplied weapons to Iran 'baseless smears'
stories.summary: China denied reports that it had supplied or planned to supply weapons to Iran, calling the allegations baseless smears. Iran is a key economic partner for Beijing.

stories.title: Brazil’s Lula, 80, livestreams workouts before election against rival half his age
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, has been livestreaming workout videos ahead of the October presidential election to demonstrate his fitness. Lula is expected to face Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, nearly half his age, in what would be his seventh presidential campaign.

stories.title: Iran executed at least 1,639 people in 2025, most since 1989: NGOs
stories.summary: According to Norway-based Iran Human Rights and Paris-based Together Against the Death Penalty, Iran executed at least 1,639 people in 2025, averaging more than four hangings per day. The organizations described the figure as an absolute minimum, marking the highest annual total since 1989.

stories.title: Russian court extends Azerbaijani diaspora leader’s prison term to 24 years
stories.summary: A court in Yekaterinburg sentenced Shahin Shykhlinski, head of the Azerbaijani diaspora in Russia's Urals region, to nine years in a maximum-security prison for violence against a law enforcement officer. The sentence extends his total prison term to 24 years.

stories.title: Military: Russian forces near Vovchansk attempt assaults in small groups
stories.summary: Russian troops near Vovchansk, Lyptsi, and Vovchanski Khutory in the Kharkiv region continued attempting to advance using small assault groups. Ukrainian military officials said these efforts have been unsuccessful.

stories.title: Tourists to Australia would have social media accounts vetted under Trumpian Coalition plan
stories.summary: Australia's opposition Coalition, led by Angus Taylor, proposed vetting the social media accounts of tourists and visa applicants as part of a hardline immigration policy. The plan would also end Australia's non-discriminatory immigration program and accelerate rejection of certain visa applications.

stories.title: As a global Warring States era begins, China must plan for the future
stories.summary: Chinese strategic analysts are increasingly framing global politics as entering a "Warring States" era of intensified great-power competition. Commentators argue China's future influence will depend less on economic power and more on presenting a coherent political vision.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE updates: Trump says doesn't care if Iran comes back to talks
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced it would begin a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports and coastal areas on Monday. President Trump stated he did not care whether Iran returned to negotiations.

stories.title: Philippines accuses China of poisoning disputed waters
stories.summary: The Philippines' National Security Council accused China of poisoning disputed waters around Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands. The alleged poisoning reportedly began last year near vital shipping lanes in an area believed to be rich in minerals.

stories.title: US blockade of Strait of Hormuz is ‘easy enough for them to do’ but at what cost?
stories.summary: Analysts say the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could give Washington strategic leverage over Iran but warn it risks undermining the ceasefire and deepening the global energy crisis. US Central Command said the blockade targets ships entering or departing Iranian ports.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Moving forward without democracy
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military leader Ibrahim Traoré has publicly rejected a return to democracy. An opposition alliance formed in exile is pushing for democratic restoration, but Traoré retains a firm grip on power.

stories.title: South Korean president’s Holocaust remarks spark Israel outcry
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung sparked a diplomatic dispute with Israel by comparing Israeli military actions against Palestinians to the Holocaust. Israel condemned the remarks, and the comments also drew criticism within South Korea.

stories.title: Netanyahu says US Vice President briefed him on Iran talks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said US Vice President JD Vance called to brief him on the Iran negotiations after departing Islamabad, where weekend talks had collapsed without an agreement.

stories.title: Spain reopens embassy in Tehran following US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Spain reopened its embassy in Tehran following a US-Iran ceasefire. The Spanish ambassador said the reopening was intended to support peace efforts from every possible quarter.

stories.title: What Pakistani jets in Saudi Arabia mean for Gulf security in Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed an air force contingent to a base on Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast while simultaneously mediating US-Iran talks. Analysts say the defensive deployment could deter Iran from attacking Saudi energy infrastructure if hostilities resume.

stories.title: Trump's framing of war as Iran's barbarism vs civilised West is a huge lie
stories.summary: A commentary by Peter Oborne challenges the US-Israeli framing of the Iran war as a clash between Iranian barbarism and Western civilization, arguing this flawed narrative has led to strategic miscalculations against Tehran.

stories.title: Europe failed the test of the Shoah. Is it failing again to confront absolute evil? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Europe is failing to confront what the author describes as absolute evil, drawing parallels between the continent's response to the October 7 attack and its historical failures during the Holocaust.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV lands in Algeria for first-ever visit by a pontiff
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Algeria for the first-ever papal visit to the country. The trip aims to promote Christian-Muslim coexistence amid global conflict and to honour St. Augustine, the locally born figure who inspired the Pope's religious spirituality.

stories.title: These are the 20 people killed in Israel by Iranian ballistic missile attacks
stories.summary: Twenty people were killed in Israel by Iranian ballistic missile attacks during 40 days of fighting. Victims included an entire family in Haifa, three teenage siblings in Beit Shemesh, several immigrants, and two foreign workers.

stories.title: Cement company Lafarge found guilty in Syria terrorism financing case
stories.summary: A French court found cement company Lafarge guilty of financing armed groups during the Syrian civil war. The case centered on payments made to keep the company's Syrian operations running amid the conflict.

stories.title: Spring flooding cuts road access to 136 communities in one Russian region, inundates 142 homes in another
stories.summary: Spring flooding inundated 142 homes and 306 residential plots in Russia's Altai Krai, with the number of flooded homes more than doubling in two days. In another Russian region, floodwaters cut road access to 136 communities.

stories.title: Ghanaian winger Dominic Frimpong killed at age of 20 in attack on team bus
stories.summary: Ghanaian footballer Dominic Frimpong, a 20-year-old winger for Berekum Chelsea, was killed during an armed robbery on the team bus on Sunday. Six masked gunmen wielding assault rifles blocked the road as the team returned from a Ghana Premier League match against Samartex.

stories.title: Kenya: 26 Kenyans Arrested in India Over Sh500mn Gold Smuggling
stories.summary: Twenty-nine Kenyans have been arrested in India after being found in possession of gold worth over 500 million Kenyan shillings, in what authorities describe as a smuggling operation.

stories.title: Russian forces intensifying offensive in Sumy region – Tregubov
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesman Trehubov reported that Russian forces have intensified offensive operations near the border in Ukraine's Sumy region. The troops are attempting to expand their zones of control with short-distance advances.

stories.title: Cop martyred, 4 injured in attack on police team in Hangu
stories.summary: A police constable was killed and four officers injured when attackers opened fire on a police team providing security for polio vaccination workers in Hangu district's Thall tehsil, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the first day of a nationwide campaign running April 13–19.

stories.title: U.S. Waiver on Russian Oil Expires as Extension Remains Uncertain
stories.summary: A U.S. waiver allowing certain transactions involving Russian oil has expired, and it remains uncertain whether Washington will grant an extension. Asian countries dependent on Middle Eastern energy supplies have been lobbying for the waiver's renewal.

stories.title: Luxury brands face profits squeeze as Iran conflict shrinks Dubai Mall sales
stories.summary: Luxury brands reported sales declines of 30 to 50 percent at the Mall of the Emirates in Dubai during March. The drops were attributed to the ongoing Iran conflict, which has reduced consumer traffic and spending in the region.

stories.title: Israel approves appointment of new intelligence agency chief
stories.summary: Israel approved the appointment of Roman Gofman as the new chief of its intelligence agency. Gofman is set to begin the role in June 2026, succeeding current director David Barnea.

stories.title: Israel is trying to change Jerusalem’s religious identity
stories.summary: Israel is accused of undermining the longstanding Status Quo arrangements at holy sites in Jerusalem. Critics say the moves aim to establish full Israeli control over Muslim and Christian religious life in the city.

stories.title: China says open Strait of Hormuz crucial for global interests as Trump blockade looms
stories.summary: China called for the Strait of Hormuz to remain open to international trade and energy shipments as President Trump announced a naval blockade targeting the chokepoint. Beijing's foreign ministry said maintaining safe passage serves the common interests of the international community.

stories.title: Victory Giant joins IPO push by China’s circuit-board makers amid AI frenzy
stories.summary: Victory Giant Technology, a printed circuit board supplier to Nvidia, launched bookbuilding in Hong Kong on Monday for an IPO seeking to raise up to HK$17.49 billion. The listing reflects growing investor interest in China's PCB manufacturers as global demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure drives expansion across the chip supply chain.

stories.title: 4 ways the war in Iran has weakened the US in the great power game
stories.summary: Analysis identifies four ways the US conflict with Iran has weakened America's position in great power competition. The war has strained US alliances while enabling China and Russia to advance their regional influence.

stories.title: France, Spain's anti-Israel bias pushes Israel-Europe relations to new low
stories.summary: Israel's relations with Europe have reached a new low amid diplomatic disputes with France and Spain. The deterioration accelerated after Prime Minister Netanyahu's far-right coalition government took office.

stories.title: MoS Margherita attends mourning ceremony for late Iranian leader Ayatollah Khamenei
stories.summary: Italy's Minister of State Margherita attended a mourning ceremony on Sunday, April 12, 2026, organized by the Iranian embassy to mark the 40th day since the death of Ayatollah Khamenei. The Chehelum ceremony was held to pay respects to the late Iranian leader.

stories.title: Ships with Iran oil anchor off India as Trump announces blockade
stories.summary: Several ships carrying Iranian oil have anchored off India's coast as the Trump administration announces a naval blockade targeting Iranian maritime traffic. Questions remain about how the blockade will affect any existing waivers on Iranian oil imports to India.

stories.title: Battles intensifying near Kupiansk as Russia trying to regain foothold across Oskil River – military
stories.summary: Fighting has intensified on the outskirts of Kupiansk as Russian forces attempt to regain a foothold across the Oskil River. Ukrainian military officials said the situation inside the city remains relatively calm but assault operations on its edges have resumed.

stories.title: PSX sheds over 3,500 points after Trump announces Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell over 3,500 points during intraday trading on Monday after President Trump ordered a blockade of Iranian ports, with the index hitting an intraday low of 161,638 before partially recovering.

stories.title: Slovakia's Fico ready to cooperate with Hungary's new Prime Minister
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico expressed readiness to cooperate with Hungary's new prime minister. Under Fico, Slovakia has maintained close ties with Hungary, with both countries maintaining warm relations with Moscow and opposing EU sanctions while continuing purchases of Russian oil and gas.

stories.title: Russia’s FSB and Investigative Committee charge 3 Telegram channel operators with stock market manipulation
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service said it disrupted a stock market manipulation scheme run by three Russian citizens through Telegram channels. The individuals allegedly used the channels to manipulate securities traded on the Moscow Exchange.

stories.title: Australia appoints Lt. Gen. Susan Coyle as first woman to lead its Army
stories.summary: The Australian government announced that Lieutenant General Susan Coyle will become the country's first female Chief of Army in July. Coyle currently serves as chief of joint capabilities and will assume the new role as part of a broader military leadership reshuffle.

stories.title: Southport attack: ‘catastrophic’ failures by multiple agencies contributed to atrocity, public inquiry finds – live updates
stories.summary: A UK public inquiry found that "catastrophic" failures by multiple agencies and the "irresponsible" behavior of his parents contributed to Axel Rudakubana's attack in Southport in summer 2024, which killed three young girls at a dance workshop. Rudakubana had exhibited violent behavior and expressed murderous thoughts from age 13.

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon, clashes with Hezbollah ahead of talks
stories.summary: Israel launched new airstrikes on Lebanon and clashed with Hezbollah forces in the southern town of Bint Jbeil ahead of scheduled Israeli-Lebanese negotiations in Washington on Tuesday.

stories.title: Heavy Russian armor limited by ‘kill zone,’ infantry losses being replenished, military spox says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian military spokesman said Russian forces in some front-line sectors are primarily replacing personnel losses rather than building up troop numbers. Heavy armor is being used in a limited capacity due to the constraints of modern warfare.

stories.title: Asian messaging apps surge 60% in Russia as Telegram faces restrictions, Kommersant reports
stories.summary: Asian messaging apps saw a 60% surge in monthly active users in Russia during March, according to MTS AdTech research cited by Kommersant. The increase coincided with mounting restrictions on Telegram in the country.

stories.title: UK and France plan naval mission over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The UK and France announced plans to co-host talks on a potential multinational naval mission in the Strait of Hormuz. French President Emmanuel Macron described it as a strictly defensive deployment to protect maritime traffic, separate from the warring parties.

stories.title: Tear gas fired at Indian workers demanding higher wage as living costs rise
stories.summary: Factory workers in Noida, a suburb of India's national capital, protested to demand higher wages as living costs rise globally, partly driven by the ongoing Iran war. Police responded by firing tear gas at the demonstrators.

stories.title: Iran says train service resumed on routes damaged by strikes during war
stories.summary: Iranian authorities announced the resumption of train services on routes damaged by Israeli strikes during the war. The IDF had previously said it targeted specific rail sections to prevent Iran's Revolutionary Guards from moving weapon systems.

stories.title: Haiti declares three days of national mourning for 25 killed in stampede
stories.summary: Haiti's government declared three days of national mourning after at least 25 people were killed in a stampede at the Laferrière Citadel, a major tourist site in northern Haiti. The incident occurred during an annual celebration at the historic landmark.

stories.title: Ghanaian footballer killed after armed attackers open fire at team bus
stories.summary: A Ghanaian football team was attacked by masked gunmen wielding assault rifles as its bus returned from a match. One player was killed in the shooting.

stories.title: South Korea, Poland to upgrade ties as Donald Tusk calls Seoul key ally after U.S.
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk agreed to upgrade bilateral ties, with Tusk calling Seoul a key ally after the United States. The two nations plan to expand defense industry cooperation under a $44.2 billion framework pact signed in 2022.

stories.title: Trump says US will blockade strait of Hormuz after Iran peace talks fail | First Thing
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the US will blockade the Strait of Hormuz after peace talks with Iran failed, with US Central Command stating the blockade would begin Monday. Separately, Viktor Orbán was defeated in Hungary's parliamentary elections.

stories.title: Russian offensive pressure unchanged during “Easter ceasefire”, Ukrainian military says
stories.summary: The Ukrainian military said the intensity of combat on the front line did not decrease during Russia's declared Easter ceasefire. Russian forces reportedly used certain periods during the pause to rotate and regroup their units.

stories.title: US military to begin blockade of Iranian ports on Monday
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced it would begin a blockade of all Iranian ports on Monday after talks between American and Iranian delegations in Islamabad failed, with President Trump blaming Iran's refusal to abandon its nuclear ambitions. Vice President JD Vance left the negotiations without an agreement.

stories.title: Poland withdraws from treaty banning antipersonnel mines, will use them to defend against Russia
stories.summary: Poland withdrew from the Ottawa Treaty banning antipersonnel mines on February 20, 2026, and announced plans to renew manufacturing of such weapons. Poland had ratified the treaty in 2012 and completed destruction of its domestic antipersonnel mine stockpile in 2016. The move is intended to bolster defenses against Russia.

stories.title: Report: Russia builds 27 air defense positions around Putin’s residence
stories.summary: At least 27 air defense positions have been constructed around Russian President Vladimir Putin's residence at Valdai in the Novgorod Region, according to an April 12 report by RFE/RL's Russian service.

stories.title: South Africa: Thyspunt Recommended for Eskom's New Nuclear Power Station
stories.summary: A draft environmental scoping report has recommended Thyspunt, a coastal site in South Africa's Eastern Cape, as the most viable location for Eskom's new nuclear power station. However, a heritage protection order on the site could complicate the approval process.

stories.title: How the US-Iran talks in Islamabad unfolded
stories.summary: Pakistan hosted US-Iran talks in Islamabad, leveraging its diplomatic ties with the Gulf states, the United States, and China. The negotiations drew international attention as Pakistan facilitated discussions that other mediators had been unable to arrange.

stories.title: French court jails Lafarge ex-CEO for funding IS in Syria
stories.summary: A French court fined cement company Lafarge and sentenced its former CEO to several years in prison for paying protection money to jihadist groups during the Syrian civil war. The long-running case addressed the company's operations in Syria amid active conflict.

stories.title: French firm Lafarge found guilty of financing jihadists in Syria
stories.summary: A Paris court found French cement company Lafarge guilty of financing the Islamic State and other jihadist groups in Syria. The company was charged with paying protection money to keep its Syrian plant operational.

stories.title: Aurangzeb arrives in Washington for IMF, World Bank spring meetings
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb arrived in Washington to attend the IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings 2026, scheduled from April 13 to 18, where he plans to hold meetings with global financial leaders on Pakistan's reform agenda.

stories.title: How would a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz work? Here are some possibilities
stories.summary: The United States is set to impose a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz beginning April 13. Analysts are examining how the U.S. military could enforce restrictions on maritime traffic through the strategically vital waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to the open ocean.

stories.title: South Africa: Local Firms Lead Charge As SA Secures R890 Billion in Investment Pledges
stories.summary: South Africa's sixth Investment Conference secured a record R890 billion in investment pledges, with local firms leading the commitments. The event highlighted domestic companies' confidence in the country's economic prospects.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed at least three Palestinians near a school in Deir el-Balah in central Gaza while mediators continued negotiations with Hamas on a US-brokered ceasefire deal. Over 750 Palestinians have been killed since the deal began.

stories.title: Pope Leo: I am not afraid of Trump administration
stories.summary: Newly installed Pope Leo stated he is not afraid of the Trump administration. The pontiff emphasized that his anti-war statements are not directed at any specific individual.

stories.title: Ukraine signals readiness for dialogue with Hungary
stories.summary: Ukraine signaled its readiness to establish dialogue with Hungary's incoming leadership following recent elections. Kyiv expressed willingness to build good-neighborly relations with Budapest's new government.

stories.title: More than 200 birds found dead or injured on Russia’s Black Sea coast after oil spill
stories.summary: More than 200 birds were found dead or injured on Russia's Black Sea coast near Anapa on April 11–12 following an oil spill. The Krasnodar Region operational headquarters confirmed the toll.

stories.title: IDF: Within a few days, there won't be major fights left in Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF stated it expects major fighting in southern Lebanon to conclude within a few days. Limited engagements may continue against remaining Hezbollah forces that have not withdrawn north of the Litani River.

stories.title: Sticker shock: LA residents alarmed by price of 2028 Olympics presale tickets
stories.summary: Presale tickets for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics drew complaints from local residents in southern California and Oklahoma City over high prices and unexpected service fees. LA28 had reserved ticket lottery slots for residents in areas hosting events.

stories.title: ‘Common ignorance’: how China took the lead in global efforts to govern AI’s future
stories.summary: At the inaugural Hong Kong Global AI Conference at the University of Hong Kong, experts said governments, industry, and the public share a "common ignorance" about AI's trajectory. Alibaba policy lead Fu Hongyu noted that China is now at the forefront of global efforts to establish AI governance frameworks.

stories.title: Southport attack blamed on ‘catastrophic’ failures by agencies and killer’s ‘irresponsible’ parents
stories.summary: A public inquiry led by Sir Adrian Fulford concluded that the Southport attack by Axel Rudakubana resulted from catastrophic failures by multiple state agencies and his parents' irresponsible conduct. The report condemned a culture of agencies passing responsibility and ignoring warning signs over many years.

stories.title: Israel could act against Syria after Iran war, Turkish foreign minister says
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned that Israel could take military action against Syria after the Iran war concludes. He identified reconstruction, internal stability, and potential Israeli aggression as Syria's most pressing challenges.

stories.title: ‘The rat gnawed at my toes’: Rodent infestation overruns Gaza’s displaced
stories.summary: Displaced Palestinians in Gaza City are facing a severe rodent infestation in their tent encampments. A 63-year-old diabetic woman was bitten by a rat while sleeping without initially realizing it due to nerve damage.

stories.title: Iran’s army says US plan to blockade Hormuz ‘amounts to piracy’
stories.summary: Iran's military condemned a planned US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, calling restrictions on maritime navigation and transit in international waters illegal and tantamount to piracy.

stories.title: Trump lambasts Pope Leo XIV, extending feud over Iran war with first American pontiff
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV, the first American pontiff, has become an outspoken critic of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28. President Trump escalated a public feud with the pope over his anti-war stance.

stories.title: France open to engaging on slavery reparations, says Ghana
stories.summary: Ghana said France expressed openness to discussions on reparations for transatlantic slavery following a meeting between Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama and French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris. Ghana's Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa confirmed Macron's willingness to engage on the issue.

stories.title: Israeli forces fire tear gas near Palestinian schoolchildren
stories.summary: Israeli forces fired tear gas toward Palestinian schoolchildren attempting to walk to school in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Ukraine’s defense intelligence reveals components used in Russia’s Knyaz Veshchy Oleg reconnaissance drone
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (DIU) published an interactive 3D model detailing the components of Russia's Knyaz Veshchy Oleg reconnaissance drone. The information was released on the War & Sanctions portal's Components in Weapons section.

stories.title: Millions of people in Sudan surviving on one meal a day: NGOs
stories.summary: NGOs report that millions of people across war-torn Sudan are surviving on just one meal a day as the country's food crisis deepens and threatens to spread to additional regions.

stories.title: What does a US naval blockade of Iran mean for oil flows? - explainer
stories.summary: After US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad ended without a deal, President Trump ordered a naval blockade targeting the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts are examining the potential impact on global oil flows and energy markets.

stories.title: REPLAY: Pope Leo XIV delivers remarks as he opens trip in Algeria
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV began a landmark visit to Algeria on Monday, calling for forgiveness in a speech honoring victims of Algeria's war of independence from France. The trip was overshadowed by the US-Israeli war in Iran and a public attack on the pope by President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Russian drone strike on ambulance in Sumy region wounds 3 medical workers, regional official says
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck an ambulance in the Hlukhiv community of Ukraine's Sumy region overnight on April 12, wounding three medical workers. Regional military administration chief Oleh Hryhorov reported the attack and published photos of the damaged vehicle.

stories.title: Report: Russian Orthodox patriarch interrupts Easter service to thank Putin for transferring icons from state museum
stories.summary: Patriarch Kirill interrupted the Russian Orthodox Easter service at Moscow's Cathedral of Christ the Savior to thank President Vladimir Putin for transferring two icons from the Tretyakov Gallery to the church. The incident was reported by Russian investigative outlet Agentstvo.

stories.title: French cement-maker Lafarge found guilty of financing jihadists in Syria
stories.summary: A Paris court found French cement-maker Lafarge, now owned by Switzerland's Holcim, guilty of financing the Islamic State group and other jihadist organizations to keep a plant operating in northern Syria during the civil war.

stories.title: Pope Leo says has 'no intention to debate' with Trump
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV told reporters aboard the papal plane en route to Algeria that he had "no intention to debate" with President Trump after the US president criticized the pontiff's comments on the US-Iran war. Leo stated his message remains focused on promoting peace.

stories.title: United Kingdom highlights close relationship with Chile in defense and security
stories.summary: Chilean Defense Minister Fernando Barros inaugurated the United Kingdom pavilion at a defense event alongside UK Ambassador David Concar and British military officials, underscoring bilateral defense and security ties between the UK and Chile.

stories.title: The digital euro: Europe’s bid for financial sovereignty
stories.summary: The European Central Bank's digital euro initiative aims to reduce Europe's dependence on US payment giants Visa and Mastercard. The vulnerability of this reliance was highlighted when US sanctions on International Criminal Court judges blocked their bank card use even on European soil.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 13 – Trump plays chicken with Iran over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without a deal, and the Trump administration moved to blockade Iranian ports near the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Israel-Lebanon talks are scheduled in Washington, and Hungary's longtime leader Viktor Orbán suffered an electoral defeat.

stories.title: Nigeria: Electricity Generation Improved to 4300mw From 3951mw - FG
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government announced that electricity generation rose from 3,951 MW to 4,300 MW between March 28 and April 10. The improvement represents an increase of roughly 350 MW in national power output.

stories.title: Oil rises above $100 per barrel amid announced U.S. naval blockade of Iran
stories.summary: Oil prices rose above $100 per barrel on Monday as the US Navy prepared to block maritime traffic to and from Iran through the Strait of Hormuz. The move could significantly limit Iranian oil exports and further tighten global supply.

stories.title: Russia spent $130 billion extra on sanctioned goods since 2022 — and it still couldn’t find replacements for some of them, Latvia says
stories.summary: Latvia's intelligence service estimates that Russia has spent $130 billion extra on sanctioned goods since 2022 but has still failed to find replacements for some items. The agency assesses that President Putin likely receives sanitized economic reports, reducing the impact of sanctions pressure.

stories.title: More than 100 Chinese workers march through Russian city to protest unpaid wages
stories.summary: More than 100 Chinese workers marched through the streets of Komsomolsk-on-Amur on April 12 to protest unpaid wages, later staging a sit-in along Pervostroiteley Avenue.

stories.title: Hong Kong school hits back at filmmaker in row over Italian festival screening
stories.summary: The supervisor of Hong Kong's Ying Wa Girls' School accused the director and distributor of the documentary "To My Nineteen-Year-Old Self" of defaming the school's principal. The dispute centers on a planned screening at an Italian film festival and marks an escalation in the ongoing controversy.

stories.title: Malawi: Flood Aftermath Bites - Thousands Return to Ruins As Government Shuts Evacuation Camps
stories.summary: Thousands of displaced Malawians are being forced to leave evacuation camps after devastating floods, returning to ruined homes with little support. The government has begun shutting down camps despite residents facing uncertain futures and the challenge of rebuilding from almost nothing.

stories.title: US to blockade Iran after talks fail to yield a deal
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced on April 12 that it would begin a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports and coastal areas on Monday, after weekend talks in Pakistan failed to produce a deal. The move jeopardizes a fragile two-week ceasefire in the U.S.–Iran conflict.

stories.title: Starmer says UK will not support US blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced that Britain would not support the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. France, Spain, Turkey, and China also criticized or condemned the American plan.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali PM Marks 66th Anniversary of National Army, Hails Security Gains
stories.summary: Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre attended a ceremony marking the 66th anniversary of the Somali National Army's founding. He emphasized the importance of building a strong and disciplined military to protect national sovereignty and highlighted recent security gains.

stories.title: How a UK military college sought to distance itself from ban on Israelis
stories.summary: Emails revealed that the head of a UK military college asked a military official to ensure the government took public ownership of a ban on Israeli nationals, seeking to distance the institution from the controversial policy.

stories.title: South Sudan: Don't Diminish the UN Peacekeeping Mission in South Sudan
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is set to debate renewing the UNMISS peacekeeping mission in South Sudan as civilians face ongoing risks of atrocities. Human Rights Watch urged the council not to diminish the mission, which is mandated to protect civilians, support the peace process, and facilitate humanitarian access.

stories.title: Red Zone, key roads in Islamabad to remain closed
stories.summary: Islamabad's capital police announced the complete closure of the Red Zone and surrounding areas, restricting entry to official vehicles only. Traffic from Kashmir Chowk toward Serena Chowk and Srinagar Highway was shut down. Commuters were advised to use alternate routes through Club Road and Kashmir Chowk.

stories.title: Starmer says UK will not join Trump's blockade of Iran's ports
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated that Britain will not participate in the US-led blockade of Iran's ports. British minesweepers and anti-drone assets will continue operating in the region as efforts intensify to reopen key shipping lanes.

stories.title: Turkey says Iran and US ‘sincere’ on ceasefire despite failed talks
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said both Iran and the United States remain sincere about pursuing a ceasefire despite the collapse of Pakistan-mediated talks. Fidan said Ankara continues to engage with all sides and raised concerns about growing Gulf tensions.

stories.title: Oil surge as Trump says to blockade Hormuz after Iran talks fail
stories.summary: The US military announced it will begin blockading all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports and coastal areas on Monday, after weekend talks failed to produce a deal to end the war with Iran. The move jeopardizes a fragile two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Study suggests Russia could conquer Baltic states in 90 days
stories.summary: A study suggests Russia could potentially conquer the Baltic states — NATO members Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania — within 90 days, though opinions among officials and analysts differ on whether Russia has the appetite for such an attack.

stories.title: FSB takes control of 7 Russian jails, including Lefortovo and St. Petersburg’s Shpalerka
stories.summary: Seven Russian pretrial detention centers, including Moscow's Lefortovo and St. Petersburg's Shpalerka, have been transferred from the Federal Penitentiary Service to FSB control, according to Russia's EGRUL corporate registry.

stories.title: On the ground: Pope Leo arrives in Algiers to start Africa tour
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Algiers on Monday for the first-ever papal visit to Algeria, beginning an 11-day tour of four African nations including Cameroon, Angola, and Equatorial Guinea. The US-born pope aims to promote Christian-Muslim coexistence and honor St. Augustine, who was born in the region.

stories.title: US, China seen as top AI beneficiaries in new growth forecast from ‘Doctor Doom’ economist
stories.summary: Economist Nouriel Roubini, known as "Doctor Doom" for predicting the 2008 financial crisis, forecast that AI and other technological advances could push US economic growth to 4% by 2030 and potentially 10% within 25 years. He identified the US and China as the top beneficiaries of AI-driven growth.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry lifts advisory urging citizens to avoid travel to Hungary
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lifted its advisory urging citizens to avoid travel to Hungary. The decision reverses a previous recommendation against visiting the neighboring country.

stories.title: Firefighters prioritised tackling blaze over rescues, Tai Po probe hears
stories.summary: A public inquiry into Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades heard that firefighters prioritized controlling the blaze over evacuating residents due to its unprecedented scale. Four Fire Services Department officers testified about the initial response to the 43-hour inferno at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po last November.
