stories.title: Beijing’s 10 measures to boost cross-strait ties
stories.summary: Beijing announced 10 measures aimed at boosting cross-strait ties between mainland China and Taiwan. The document was translated from Chinese to English and published for reference purposes.

stories.title: ‘The perception is Carney is a wartime leader’: why Canada’s PM could secure a majority
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is positioned to secure a majority government as his Liberal party is expected to win key byelections and attract defections from rival parties. Analysts attribute his momentum to public demand for stability amid tensions triggered by US President Trump's actions.

stories.title: Bikes, books and ambitions: how Zhang Xue and Zhang Xuefeng inspire a generation in China
stories.summary: Chinese social media mourned the death of education influencer Zhang Xuefeng, who had over 30 million followers, in late March. Simultaneously, motorcycle brand ZXMOTO founder Zhang Xue gained attention after an international racing victory. Both self-made figures resonated with public sentiment in China.

stories.title: How the Pentagon Can Manage the Risks of AI Warfare
stories.summary: An analysis examines the challenges the Pentagon faces in managing risks associated with AI-enabled warfare, emphasizing that warfighters must trust the technology for it to be effectively adopted in military operations.

stories.title: Strikes on alleged drug boats kill 5, leave 1 survivor in eastern Pacific, says U.S. military
stories.summary: U.S. Southern Command said it carried out strikes on alleged drug trafficking boats along known smuggling routes in the eastern Pacific Ocean. The strikes killed five people and left one survivor.

stories.title: Millions in war-ravaged Sudan surviving on one meal a day, say NGOs
stories.summary: NGOs report that millions of people in war-ravaged Sudan are surviving on just one meal a day. Residents in North Darfur and South Kordofan states have resorted to eating leaves and animal feed amid a deepening food crisis.

stories.title: As US military set to blockade Iranian ports, Tehran says move ‘amounts to piracy’
stories.summary: US Central Command announced it would block all ships entering and exiting Iranian ports but would not obstruct Strait of Hormuz traffic bound for non-Iranian destinations. Tehran condemned the blockade as an act of piracy.

stories.title: Malaysia faces energy emergency amid Trump’s Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Malaysia faces a potential energy emergency following President Trump's announcement of a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts say the escalation in the US-Israel war on Iran could accelerate Malaysia's energy crisis, with the government having already flagged June as a critical supply pressure point.

stories.title: Japan’s rural rail crisis hits new low as JR East cuts toilet paper service
stories.summary: JR East, one of Japan's largest rail operators, has stopped providing toilet paper at a growing number of unmanned rural stations as a cost-cutting measure. The decision highlights the financial pressures facing Japan's rural rail services and has drawn frustration online.

stories.title: French parliament debates bill on return of artworks looted during colonial era
stories.summary: France's National Assembly is debating draft legislation to facilitate the return of artworks and artifacts looted during the colonial era. The bill, previously backed by the Senate, could address restitution requests from countries including Mali, Algeria, and Benin.

stories.title: March of the Living: Holocaust survivors stand tall against surge of world-wide antisemitism
stories.summary: Holocaust survivors participated in the March of the Living, standing against a global surge of antisemitism. A small group of elderly survivors, many of whom were children during World War II, flew from Israel despite ongoing Hezbollah rocket fire targeting civilians.

stories.title: US blockade of Iran would worsen global energy crisis, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts warn that a US blockade of Iranian ports would exacerbate the global energy crisis. Although the US military says the blockade would target only Iranian ports, experts say the economic ripple effects would be felt worldwide.

stories.title: Middle East war will leave UK households £480 worse off this year, says thinktank
stories.summary: The Resolution Foundation warned that higher energy prices resulting from the Iran war could leave UK households approximately £480 worse off this year. The thinktank cited rising gas, electricity, and petrol costs as key drivers of diminished living standards.

stories.title: Netanyahu in southern Lebanon: A first since the start of the war
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made his first visit to southern Lebanon since fighting began against Hezbollah on March 2. He declared that Israel had eliminated the threat of an invasion by the Iran-backed Lebanese Shiite movement.

stories.title: Rwanda: What to Know About 21 Politicians Remembered for Opposing Genocide
stories.summary: Rwanda held its annual ceremony on April 13 honoring 21 politicians killed for opposing the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. The event concludes the country's national mourning week each year.

stories.title: Trump’s Hormuz blockade risks piling pain on Asia allies, China
stories.summary: President Trump's announced blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could severely impact Asian economies, including key U.S. allies and China. Analysts warn that in a worst-case scenario, oil prices could surge to as high as $170 per barrel due to disrupted energy flows.

stories.title: Hong Kong expands heat stress monitoring to better protect outdoor workers
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Labour Department expanded heat stress monitoring to include data from 10 sites using newly added Hong Kong Observatory stations. The move aims to provide more accurate local heat readings and issue timely warnings to protect outdoor workers.

stories.title: Europe must wean off ‘addiction’ to US military, Swedish DefMin says
stories.summary: Swedish Defense Minister Pål Jonson said Europe must reduce its reliance on US military capabilities. He noted that defense cooperation between Sweden and the United States has not been affected by recent political tensions between the allies.

stories.title: Oil prices surge as Trump vows to block the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US crude oil prices surged nearly 8% to approximately $104 per barrel amid concerns over a potential US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran exported around 1.85 million barrels of crude per day through the strait in March.

stories.title: Russian tanks and IFVs rarely reach the contact line — Ukraine’s 20 km kill zone stops them cold, spokesman says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian military spokesman said Russian tanks and infantry fighting vehicles rarely reach the front line because they are destroyed within a roughly 20-km kill zone. He noted that lighter vehicles such as quad bikes and motorcycles still manage to get through but do not constitute serious military hardware.

stories.title: Pakistan sending troops to Saudi Arabia may could shift tide in war against Iran - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines how Pakistan sending troops to Saudi Arabia could shift dynamics in the war against Iran. The deployment could increase pressure on Tehran but also bring Saudi Arabia closer to a country that has expressed hostile positions toward Israel.

stories.title: Trump orders blockade of Hormuz strait after Iran talks fail
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the US Navy to blockade the Strait of Hormuz after peace talks with Iran broke down in Pakistan over Iran's refusal to abandon its nuclear ambitions. Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned they controlled traffic in the waterway and would trap any challenger in a "deadly vortex."

stories.title: Trump move to blockade Hormuz risks complicating ties with China
stories.summary: China called for calm and restraint from all sides in response to President Trump's threat to blockade the Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran talks failed. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said keeping the waterway safe and unimpeded serves the international community's common interest.

stories.title: Trump calls Pope Leo ‘terrible’ in unusual direct attack on church leader
stories.summary: President Trump called Pope Leo XIV "terrible" in an unusually direct attack on a church leader. The pontiff had criticized Trump's war in Iran and his immigration policies.

stories.title: Trump attacks Pope Leo, calling him ‘terrible’ for foreign policy and ‘weak’ on crime
stories.summary: President Donald Trump publicly criticized Pope Leo XIV, calling him "terrible" on foreign policy and "weak" on crime. The remarks followed the pontiff's criticism of Trump's military campaign in Iran and his administration's immigration crackdown.

stories.title: War in the Mideast: Israel, Lebanon gear up for talks
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam announced efforts to halt the Israel-Hezbollah war ahead of planned trilateral talks in Washington on Tuesday involving Lebanese, Israeli, and US officials. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told troops in southern Lebanon that the fight was far from over.

stories.title: 'Love has triumphed': Hungarian papers react to Orban loss in historic elections
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán suffered a historic defeat in Hungary's parliamentary elections. Other major stories included Pope Leo XIV's visit to Algeria, the appointment of Susan Coyle as head of the Australian army, and Union Berlin hiring the Bundesliga's first female coach.

stories.title: Flood threat looms over Chitral valley as summer approaches
stories.summary: Residents and experts in Pakistan's Chitral valley are urging construction of protective bulwarks along the 400-kilometer Chitral River as summer flooding season approaches. Over the past two decades, the region from Broghil Valley to Arandu on the Pak-Afghan border has experienced increasing flood intensity driven by global warming and rapid glacial melt.

stories.title: Watch: Netanyahu: We have thwarted the threat of invasion from Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel has thwarted the threat of invasion from Lebanon. No further details were provided in the report.

stories.title: Climate war shock
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israel war against Iran has disrupted global energy supplies, particularly through the Strait of Hormuz, which handles roughly 20 percent of global oil transit. The conflict has created a systemic economic shock and threatens to derail climate goals, as scientists warn the window to limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius is closing by 2030.

stories.title: Protesters rally in Paris against ‘liberty-killing’ anti-Semitism bill
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters gathered in Paris to oppose a proposed French law aimed at combating what legislators describe as renewed forms of anti-Semitism. Demonstrators characterized the bill as a threat to civil liberties.

stories.title: 'Turkey is the new Iran': The growing threat Erdogan poses to Israel - analysis
stories.summary: Middle East expert Yoni Ben Menachem warned that Turkish President Erdogan is building a structured plan to create a new Sunni axis that could replace Iran's regional role. The analysis describes Turkey as a growing strategic threat to Israel.

stories.title: US begins naval blockade of Iran, Israel 'surrounds' Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: President Trump's naval blockade of Iranian ports officially began after the Monday deadline passed. The U.S. military announced it would enforce the blockade at the Strait of Hormuz while allowing non-Iranian vessels to transit.

stories.title: Iran says will keep control of Hormuz amid 'illegal' US blockade
stories.summary: An Iranian Armed Forces spokesperson stated that US restrictions on vessels in international waters were illegal and amounted to piracy. Iran vowed to maintain control over the Strait of Hormuz despite the US blockade.

stories.title: Five settlements in Kharkiv region come under enemy fire over past day, casualties reported
stories.summary: Five settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region came under Russian strikes on April 12, resulting in casualties. The attacks targeted civilian areas across the region.

stories.title: At least 30 people dead following tragic stampede at Haiti fort
stories.summary: A stampede at the Citadelle Laferrière, a mountaintop fortress near Milot in northern Haiti, killed at least 25 to 30 people and injured dozens. The incident occurred on April 11 when crowds gathered for traditional festivities at the UNESCO heritage site.

stories.title: Lapid lashes out at opposition rivals for ‘fleeing’ Knesset, fight against Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid criticized rival opposition figures for what he called fleeing the Knesset and abandoning the fight against Prime Minister Netanyahu's government.

stories.title: Fashion brands in Lahore ‘ignore’ labour rights violations in textile recycling sector
stories.summary: A study by the Labour Education Foundation and the Netherlands-based organization Arisa found widespread labour rights violations in Lahore's textile recycling sector. The report highlights that major fast fashion brands promoting recycling as a sustainability measure remain largely unaware or unaccountable for exploitative conditions in their supply chains.

stories.title: High-stakes diplomacy
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without a deal but also without a breakdown, with both delegations returning to their capitals for consultations. A fragile ceasefire remains in place and backchannel communication is expected to continue. For Pakistan, hosting the negotiations represented a significant diplomatic achievement.

stories.title: An end on horizon?
stories.summary: Following the announcement of a two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, crude oil prices fell about 15 percent to roughly $96 per barrel. Analysts had warned that continued hostilities and Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could push prices significantly higher. Uncertainty remains over future oil market behavior.

stories.title: 2025 toll of Diaspora Jews killed in antisemitic attacks was highest in three decades
stories.summary: A Tel Aviv University study found that the number of Diaspora Jews killed in antisemitic attacks in 2025 was the highest in three decades. Australia and Canada recorded their highest-ever yearly totals of antisemitic incidents.

stories.title: US blockade of Iran will be major military endeavour, say experts
stories.summary: Military experts say the U.S. naval blockade of Iran will require a major operational commitment. They warn it could provoke fresh retaliation from Tehran and strain an already fragile ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Trump’s Hormuz blockade may target China along with Iran
stories.summary: The US announced a blockade targeting ships calling at Iranian ports after weekend peace talks ended without a deal. US Central Command said the action would begin Monday at 10am New York time, though vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to non-Iranian ports would not be affected. Analysts noted the blockade could also pressure China, a major buyer of Iranian oil.

stories.title: A nation under two pressures
stories.summary: Pakistan faces a potential double crisis as the Iran-U.S.-Israel conflict drives up oil prices while weather forecasts predict monsoon rainfall 22 to 26 percent above normal. Experts warn of likely heavy flooding in 2026, compounding economic stress from geopolitical disruptions and volatile global energy markets.

stories.title: 3 satellites to track all? Chinese radar images confirm US military fears
stories.summary: China released radar satellite images of a Japanese-flagged oil tanker, the Towa Maru, near the Spratly Islands in the South China Sea. The images, taken from 35,800 km above, marked the first public demonstration of a capability that confirms US military concerns about Chinese satellite tracking of vessels.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV begins landmark Algeria visit with call for 'forgiveness'
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV began a landmark visit to Algeria on Monday, calling for forgiveness while paying tribute to victims of the country's 1954–1962 war of independence from France. The visit, the first by a pope to the Muslim-majority nation, was partly overshadowed by US President Trump's public criticism of the pontiff's stance on the Iran war.

stories.title: War update: 107 combat clashes on frontline over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces recorded 107 combat engagements with Russian forces along the frontline on April 12. The clashes occurred across multiple sectors of the front.

stories.title: Long, winding road
stories.summary: Talks between U.S. and Iranian delegations in Islamabad concluded on Sunday without a breakthrough after beginning on Saturday. The two-week truce facilitated by Pakistan appears to be holding following 40 days of war sparked by U.S.-Israeli aggression against Iran. An immediate return to hostilities does not appear imminent.

stories.title: What Iran is saying about US plan to blockade ports
stories.summary: Iran's military condemned US plans to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, calling the move an act of piracy. Tehran has vowed to maintain control over its waters in the face of the proposed restrictions.

stories.title: French lawmakers set to push bill criminalising speech on Israel
stories.summary: French lawmakers are advancing a bill that would criminalize certain forms of speech related to Israel. Nearly 700,000 people have signed a petition opposing the proposed legislation, with protesters rallying under the slogan that supporting Palestine is not a crime.

stories.title: IDF says close to capturing Hezbollah’s historic Bint Jbeil stronghold
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it is close to capturing Bint Jbeil, a historic Hezbollah stronghold in southern Lebanon, claiming over 100 Hezbollah operatives have been killed in the fighting. Officials estimated the operation would take several more days to complete.

stories.title: China's exports set to lose momentum as Iran war undercuts AI-driven boom
stories.summary: China's export growth is expected to lose momentum as the Iran war undercuts an AI-driven trade boom. Exports were forecast to have risen 8.6 percent year-on-year in dollar terms, according to a Reuters poll.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Super Typhoon Sinlaku threatens Mariana Islands
stories.summary: Super Typhoon Sinlaku is threatening the Mariana Islands in the western Pacific, including the U.S. territories of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. The rapidly strengthening storm originated over Micronesian waters and intensified into a super typhoon, bringing destructive winds and flooding risk.

stories.title: Keir Starmer defends plan for closer alignment with EU rules
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer defended plans to align more closely with certain EU rules, stating that a stronger relationship with Europe serves British interests amid international turmoil over the Iran war. He addressed criticism that the approach amounted to integration by stealth, noting that changes would require parliamentary legislation.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 87 out of 98 Russian drones during nighttime attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 87 of 98 Russian drones launched during an overnight attack on April 13.

stories.title: Cuba sent doctors. Washington sent a destroyer.
stories.summary: The US naval blockade is affecting Cuba, where decades of medical solidarity—including sending doctors abroad—are being undermined. The blockade's impact extends beyond Iran, threatening the small island nation's humanitarian outreach programs.

stories.title: Refugee in my own city: Surviving Tehran’s bombing, with my cat for company
stories.summary: A Tehran resident identified as Sana continues to live in the Iranian capital despite relentless US bombing during the ongoing war. She remains with her cat, clinging to moments of normalcy amid the destruction.

stories.title: Mideast war a 'big problem' for EU competitiveness: Former Italian prime minister Enrico Letta
stories.summary: Former Italian Prime Minister Enrico Letta warned that the war in the Middle East poses a significant challenge to EU competitiveness, particularly through its impact on energy costs. He said many recommendations from his 2024 report on the EU Single Market remain unimplemented, and fragmentation continues to raise costs.

stories.title: Iran war prompts European rethink on energy security: How can the EU become more independent?
stories.summary: The war in Iran has exposed Europe's continued energy vulnerability despite efforts to reduce reliance on Russian supplies. Disruptions to liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have driven EU inflation to 2.5% in March, largely due to soaring energy costs.

stories.title: Cuba’s President warns U.S. against attacking island or trying to depose him
stories.summary: Cuban President warned the United States against attacking the island or attempting to depose him. Tensions between Cuba and the U.S. remain elevated, though both sides have acknowledged that talks are taking place without sharing details.

stories.title: Ghanaian footballer Dominic Frimpong killed in armed attack on team bus
stories.summary: Ghanaian footballer Dominic Frimpong of Berekum Chelsea was killed when armed robbers attacked the Ghana Premier League team's bus as it traveled home after a match.

stories.title: Why Singapore’s property slowdown is the envy of the rest of Asia
stories.summary: Singapore faces significant vulnerability to the energy shock from the Iran conflict, as imported natural gas generates roughly 95% of the city-state's electricity. Nomura ranked Singapore the fourth most vulnerable Asian economy to the crisis based on fossil fuel dependence and Gulf energy imports.

stories.title: CORPORATE WINDOW: A clear goal with unclear execution
stories.summary: Despite Pakistan's strengthened diplomatic standing through strategic neutrality amid global trade and energy disruptions, the country has struggled to convert that position into tangible economic gains. Analysts argue Pakistan should pursue strategic conversion of its diplomatic capital into investment, exports, and long-term economic resilience.

stories.title: 'I like his brother more': Trump slams Pope Leo over Iran nuclear issue, left-wing policies
stories.summary: President Trump criticised Pope Leo XIV over his stance on Iran's nuclear program and left-wing policies. Trump claimed the pope was elected only because he was American and could "deal with" the US president.

stories.title: China’s Tibet mega dam: safety and quality are ‘top priorities’
stories.summary: Chinese Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing said the mega dam under construction on the Yarlung Tsangpo river in Tibet must prioritize ecological integrity and safety. The facility will be the world's largest hydropower project. India has expressed concerns about potential water shortages and ecological damage downstream.

stories.title: Australia appoints female army chief for the first time in history
stories.summary: Australia appointed Lieutenant General Susan Coyle as its first female army chief. Coyle has held several senior command roles over a nearly 40-year military career.

stories.title: Mentally ill son who killed mother detained indefinitely at psychiatric hospital
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court ordered Wong Chun-kit to be detained indefinitely at a psychiatric hospital after he killed his mother, believing she was a "monster lizard." Two psychiatrists recommended the hospital order on charges of manslaughter by diminished responsibility and preventing lawful burial.

stories.title: Haiti: At least 25 dead in stampede at UNESCO Citadelle Laferrière fortress
stories.summary: A stampede at the Citadelle Laferrière near Milot in northern Haiti on April 11 killed at least 25 people. Crowds had gathered at the UNESCO-listed mountaintop fortress for traditional festivities when the deadly crush occurred.

stories.title: Russian forces strike 13 settlements in Kherson region over past day, leaving two injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck 13 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region over the past 24 hours, wounding two people.

stories.title: Four officials hurt as Afghan residents clash with police in Islamabad
stories.summary: A police search operation targeting Afghan residents in Islamabad's Sarai Kharboza area turned violent, injuring four officers. Authorities arrested 23 people, who now face terrorism charges. An FIR alleges that a suspect named Mubeen led a group that abducted a police official and set a building on fire.

stories.title: PTI optimistic about progress as US, Iran talks end without deal
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf stated that although U.S.-Iran talks concluded in Islamabad without a final agreement, most key points had already been agreed upon. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said only a few issues remain unresolved and urged optimism about continued diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Gas supply to power sector may double amid LNG shortfall
stories.summary: Pakistan's government is planning to at least double domestic gas supply to the power sector by month's end, potentially diverting gas from households, CNG stations, and fertilizer production to offset an LNG shortfall and prevent severe loadshedding and tariff hikes.

stories.title: Pope Leo begins 10-day Africa tour as Trump attacks Church leader
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV began a 10-day tour of Africa amid an ongoing public dispute with President Trump. More than 20% of the world's Catholics live on the African continent, according to Vatican statistics.

stories.title: Iran’s underground Air Force base had been hit earlier in the war
stories.summary: Previously unreported U.S. strikes hit an underground Iranian Air Force base at the end of March during the ongoing conflict. Details of the attack only emerged after the fact, revealing a significant strike on Iran's concealed military infrastructure.

stories.title: Pope sees ‘moral obligation’ to protect Lebanese
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV expressed solidarity with the people of Lebanon, saying there was a moral obligation to protect them. Lebanese authorities report more than 2,000 people killed in Israeli strikes over the preceding six weeks. The Pope made the remarks at St. Peter's Square following his Regina Coeli prayer.

stories.title: Can a New Bridge Finally Save the Pentagon’s Best Ideas?
stories.summary: An analysis examines the Pentagon's historical challenges in transitioning innovative ideas into operational capabilities, citing Admiral Hyman Rickover's 1953 development of the first naval nuclear propulsion system near Idaho Falls as a model of aggressive innovation.

stories.title: Can a New Bridge Finally Save the Pentagon’s Best Ideas?
stories.summary: An analysis explores how the US Department of Defense can better bridge the gap between innovative ideas and fielded capabilities, drawing on historical examples such as Admiral Hyman Rickover's development of naval nuclear propulsion in the 1950s.

stories.title: China, the Iran war and the chemical suddenly stoking global supply fears
stories.summary: China has reportedly decided to halt sulphuric acid exports starting in May, compounding supply fears alongside the collapse of US-Iran peace talks. Economists warned the move could drive up prices and disrupt global mining and fertiliser supply chains with few available alternatives.

stories.title: Russia loses 960 troops, one air defense system in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: According to Ukrainian military figures, Russian forces lost approximately 960 personnel in a single day, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, to about 1,312,140. One Russian air defense system was also destroyed.

stories.title: UK shelves Chagos Islands deal following lack of support from Trump
stories.summary: The UK government has shelved a deal to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, citing the lack of US support. Legislation was reportedly set to expire in parliament. The islands host the strategically important US-UK military base at Diego Garcia.

stories.title: ‘The rat gnawed at my toes’: Rodent infestation overruns Gaza’s displaced
stories.summary: Displaced Palestinians in Gaza are facing a severe rodent infestation in displacement camps. Residents report nightly rat attacks in their tents, and authorities warn of a worsening public health crisis. One 63-year-old woman in Gaza City was hospitalised after rodents bit her feet.

stories.title: Splash and crash: Thailand celebrates Songkran as energy crisis deepens
stories.summary: Thailand's annual Songkran water festival proceeded across Bangkok on Monday despite a deepening energy crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The three-day celebration drew a surge of tourists to the country, whose economy has been struggling with rising fuel and commodity prices.

stories.title: Over 7,600 Israelis treated in hospitals since conflict began, health ministry says
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported that 7,693 people have been admitted to hospitals since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran, with 104 still hospitalised. Of those currently in hospital, two are in critical condition and 13 in serious condition. Some injuries were indirect, including people hurt while reaching shelters.

stories.title: World powers urge US, Iran to uphold truce, return to talks
stories.summary: Pakistan on Sunday urged the United States and Iran to uphold their ceasefire after talks in Islamabad failed to break the deadlock. The EU, Oman, and Australia also called on both sides to extend the truce and return to negotiations. The conflict escalated after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Russians carry out 456 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, one person injured
stories.summary: Russian occupying forces carried out 456 strikes on 28 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over 24 hours, injuring one woman in the Zaporizhzhia district.

stories.title: Easter truce between Ukraine and Russia ends
stories.summary: An Easter truce between Ukraine and Russia ended after lasting 32 hours, from 4:00 p.m. GMT+1 on April 11 to the end of the day on April 12. The ceasefire had been observed to mark the Orthodox Easter holiday.

stories.title: Iran restores key rail links after US-Israeli strikes disrupted transport
stories.summary: Iran restored rail connections between Tehran, Tabriz, and Mashhad after a four-to-five-day suspension caused by US-Israeli strikes, according to IRNA. A Tehran-Tabriz-Van service to Turkey also resumed using repaired tracks. The disruption followed US threats to target Iranian transport infrastructure.

stories.title: Iran ‘will not bow to any threats’, Ghalibaf declares
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led negotiations with the United States in Pakistan, declared that Iran will not yield to threats. His remarks followed U.S. President Donald Trump's order of a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran called control over the strait non-negotiable and demanded full sanctions relief.

stories.title: A Closed Strait of Hormuz Risks a Global Food Security Crisis
stories.summary: Analysts warn that a closure of the Strait of Hormuz could trigger a global food security crisis by disrupting supplies of urea, a nitrogen fertilizer critical for staple grain production. Urea, derived from natural gas, is a key agricultural input transported through the waterway.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 45 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 45 of the US-Iran conflict, the United States moved to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, marking the latest escalation after peace deal negotiations failed.

stories.title: In Pakistan talks, Iran saw a US trying to dictate, not negotiate
stories.summary: During US-Iran talks held in Islamabad, Pakistan, both sides reportedly entered negotiations believing they held the advantage. Iran perceived the US as attempting to dictate terms rather than negotiate in good faith.

stories.title: Who is Yechiel Leiter, Israel’s US envoy leading talks with Lebanon?
stories.summary: Yechiel Leiter, Israel's ambassador to the United States, is leading Israeli negotiations with Lebanon. Leiter has far-right political ties and has drawn attention for contentious rhetoric during the Lebanese peace talks.

stories.title: Why restraint matters in managing public perceptions
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance and Iranian Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf arrived in Islamabad for talks amid heightened public expectations stoked by extensive media coverage and billboards. By Sunday, framing of the negotiations as a decisive moment had outpaced actual developments, as the talks ended without a deal.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Zaporizhzhia, residents report explosions
stories.summary: Residents of Zaporizhzhia city reported explosions as hostile drones targeted the area.

stories.title: Orban’s defeat in Hungary has ripple effect for Trump, US conservatives
stories.summary: The electoral defeat of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is seen as having ripple effects for US President Donald Trump and American conservatives. Trump had been an outspoken supporter of Orbán's nationalist governance.

stories.title: Iran says 77 historic sites damaged in strikes on Tehran
stories.summary: Iranian officials reported that 77 historical buildings, palaces, and museums in Tehran were damaged by US-Israeli strikes, according to IRNA. About 90 percent of the damage was described as minor, while 10 percent was serious. Affected sites include Qajar-era landmarks such as Farrokhabad Palace and Ishratabad Palace.

stories.title: Oil price tops $100 a barrel after US-Iran talks fail and Trump orders strait of Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Oil prices surged above $100 a barrel after U.S.–Iran talks ended without agreement and President Trump ordered a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. Navy is targeting Iranian vessels and ships that have paid tolls to Iran for passage through the strait to cut off Iranian oil exports.

stories.title: Regime Change in Iran, Underpants Gnomes, and the Phase II Problem
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the US and Israeli goal of regime change in Iran through the ongoing war has stalled due to a lack of clear strategy. As a ceasefire pauses combat and failed talks lead to a planned Strait of Hormuz blockade, the regime-change objective remains unrealized.

stories.title: Nigeria: NAF Jet Kills Over 200 Civilians
stories.summary: A Nigerian Air Force airstrike on a weekly market along the Borno-Yobe border reportedly killed over 200 people, mostly traders, drawing condemnation from civil society organizations and security experts.

stories.title: Africa: Checkmating Traoré's Anti-Democracy Incitement in Africa
stories.summary: Commentators have raised concerns about Burkina Faso leader Ibrahim Traoré's anti-democracy incitement in Africa, calling for efforts to uphold popular will and counter the spread of military dictatorship on the continent.

stories.title: Nigeria: Killings Under-Reported, Security Crisis Deepening - Gbenga Hashim
stories.summary: Former Nigerian presidential candidate Gbenga Hashim warned that killings across parts of Nigeria are being under-reported and that the country's security crisis continues to deepen.

stories.title: Nigeria: Conviction of Terrorists Will Give Hope to Victims - U.S., CSOs, Lawyer
stories.summary: The United States, civil society organizations, and a senior lawyer praised the conviction and sentencing of Boko Haram terrorists to life imprisonment by Nigeria's Federal High Court in Abuja, calling it a step toward justice for victims.

stories.title: Malawi: Child Sexual Abuse Crisis' in Malawi - Government Moves to Enhance Law Enforcement and Response Systems
stories.summary: Malawi's Ministry of Gender, Children, Disability and Social Welfare announced urgent measures to address what it described as a child sexual abuse crisis, including enhanced law enforcement and response systems.

stories.title: Nigeria: Mixed Reactions As Govt Cuts Duties On Pharmaceutical Products, Rice, Cars, Others
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government approved a 2026 fiscal policy reducing import tariffs on pharmaceutical products, rice, cars, and other goods, drawing mixed reactions from stakeholders.

stories.title: Malawi: Witchcraft Killings Surge - 11 Elderly Slaughtered in Four Months As Fear Grips Malawi
stories.summary: Eleven elderly people have been killed in Malawi over witchcraft accusations in the first four months of 2025, prompting alarm over a deepening human rights crisis.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Eyes Free Trade Agreement With India to Boost Exports
stories.summary: Kenya is exploring a Free Trade Agreement with India to boost exports and address a widening trade imbalance between the two countries.

stories.title: Spanish PM Sanchez heads for fourth China visit, risks annoying Trump
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is preparing his fourth visit to China, signaling his determination to maintain an independent foreign policy. The trip risks further straining relations with US President Trump.

stories.title: Trump says US spending on Nato under ‘serious examination’
stories.summary: President Trump said US spending on NATO is under "very serious examination," criticising the alliance for insufficient support during the war involving Iran. Trump questioned the value of US membership, saying allied nations had not reciprocated American defence commitments.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: US blockade of Iran’s ports to begin later today as Trump says he doesn’t care about further talks
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command announced a naval blockade of all Iranian Gulf ports beginning at 10 a.m. ET on Monday, effectively seizing control of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump stated he was indifferent to further negotiations with Iran after weekend talks collapsed.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amid Erratic Power Supply, Adelabu Says He Has Delivered On Two-Week Pledge
stories.summary: Nigerian Power Minister Adebayo Adelabu claimed improved electricity generation between March 28 and April 10, 2026, despite ongoing erratic power supply complaints across the country.

stories.title: Nigeria: Supreme Court Overrules Court of Appeal On Receiver's Powers in Nestoil, Neconde Legal Tussle
stories.summary: Nigeria's Supreme Court overruled the Court of Appeal in the legal dispute involving Neconde Energy Limited, Nestoil Limited, FBN Quest Merchant Bank, and FBN Trustees, reinstating senior advocates as counsel in the case.

stories.title: Kenya: DCI Arrests Prime Suspect in Brutal Murder of RIAT College Student in Kisumu
stories.summary: Detectives in Kisumu West, Kenya, recovered the decomposing body of a 21-year-old RIAT College student from Riat Forest and arrested the prime suspect. She had been reported missing after a suspected abduction on April 5, 2026.

stories.title: South Sudan: Both Sides Blocking Aid, Displacing Civilians
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that both sides in South Sudan's conflict are blocking humanitarian aid and displacing civilians, calling for secure humanitarian access.

stories.title: Kenya: 16 Killed in 12 Hours As 30 Road Accidents Recorded Nationwide
stories.summary: At least 16 people were killed and 61 injured in 30 road accidents recorded across Kenya within a 12-hour period, according to the Traffic Department.

stories.title: Peter Magyar: former Fidesz insider who vowed to dismantle Orban system 'brick by brick'
stories.summary: Péter Magyar, a 45-year-old former Fidesz insider, led his Tisza party to a decisive victory in Hungary's elections on Sunday, ending 16 years of rule by Viktor Orbán's party. Magyar has pledged to fight corruption and rebuild Hungary's strained relationships with the European Union and NATO.

stories.title: Gaza's land looters turn destruction into opportunity for profit
stories.summary: Displaced Gazans are struggling to recover land and homes seized in their absence amid widespread destruction and the collapse of law enforcement. Reports indicate that some individuals have exploited the chaos to seize properties for profit.

stories.title: Yuan’s ‘golden window’ is open, former PBOC governor says as US dollar credibility teeters
stories.summary: Former People's Bank of China governor Zhou Xiaochuan said faltering confidence in the U.S. dollar has created a "golden window of opportunity" for China to promote international use of the yuan. Zhou attributed shifts in the international monetary system to U.S. policy choices, including broad tariff applications.

stories.title: Zelensky congratulates Magyar on his victory in elections in Hungary
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky congratulated Péter Magyar and his TISZA party on winning Hungary's parliamentary elections.

stories.title: Girl, 13, looked up punishment for running someone over after hitting cyclist in stolen car, court hears
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl appeared in a Victorian children's court in Australia charged with multiple offenses, including allegedly swerving a stolen car toward members of the Jewish community and hitting a cyclist. Police told the court she searched online for the punishment for running someone over after the incident.

stories.title: Iran executed over 1,600 people in 2025, most since 1989, rights groups say
stories.summary: Rights groups reported that Iran executed over 1,600 people in 2025, the highest number since 1989, averaging four to five executions daily. The Iran Human Rights organisation warned that if the regime survives the current war, executions could be used even more extensively.

stories.title: Lebanon PM says he’s working to get Israeli troops to withdraw
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister stated he is working to secure the withdrawal of Israeli troops from southern Lebanon. Israel has said the ceasefire in its broader conflict with Iran does not extend to operations against Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russia resumes night attacks: 12,000 people without electricity after enemy strike in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: A Russian strike on an energy facility in Ukraine's Chernihiv district left more than 12,000 consumers without electricity during resumed nighttime attacks.

stories.title: Trump calls Pope Leo 'terrible' in public attack after pontiff's anti-war message
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly attacked Pope Leo XIV, calling the US-born pontiff "terrible for foreign policy" and "a very liberal person." Trump's remarks followed Leo's suggestion that a "delusion of omnipotence" was fueling the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: IRGC: Military vessels approaching Hormuz constitute 'breach of ceasefire'
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned that the approach of military vessels toward the Strait of Hormuz would constitute a ceasefire violation and would be met with a "firm and harsh" response. The IRGC said civilian shipping remains permitted under regulated conditions. The statement followed US CENTCOM's transit of destroyers through the strait.

stories.title: Impact of Middle East war on Hong Kong’s aviation hub status ‘relative’: experts
stories.summary: Aviation experts said the Middle East conflict's impact on Hong Kong's status as a transit hub would depend on the war's duration. Surging fuel prices have triggered passenger flight cuts. Analysts noted Hong Kong faces competition from Singapore, Japan, South Korea, and China's Greater Bay Area.

stories.title: Budget deficit for two months exceeds annual target in Russia — intelligence
stories.summary: According to intelligence reports, Russia's federal budget deficit for January–February 2026 reached $69.9 billion, nearly double the Finance Ministry's earlier estimate of $43.3 billion.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia restores East-West pipeline, Manifa output after Hormuz disruption
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia announced it restored full pumping capacity through its East-West pipeline to approximately 7 million barrels per day after disruptions caused by the Iran conflict. Output from the Manifa oil field, previously reduced by about 300,000 barrels per day, has also been restored.

stories.title: In broadside, Trump slams ‘weak’ pope who ‘thinks it’s OK’ for Iran to have a nuclear bomb
stories.summary: President Trump publicly attacked Pope Leo XIV, calling him "weak" and accusing him of thinking it is acceptable for Iran to possess nuclear weapons. Trump urged the pontiff to "stop catering to the Radical Left." The remarks follow the pope's repeated calls for an end to Middle East hostilities.

stories.title: US military to begin blockade of Iranian ports on April 13
stories.summary: The US military announced it will begin enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports on April 13. Officials stated that vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to and from non-Iranian ports will not be impeded.

stories.title: Donald Trump launches extraordinary attack on Pope Leo calling him ‘weak’ and ‘terrible’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump sharply criticized Pope Leo XIV in social media posts and follow-up remarks, calling the U.S.-born pontiff "weak," "terrible," and "a very liberal person." Trump suggested the pope should "stop catering to the Radical Left" in an unprecedented public attack on the leader of the Catholic Church.

stories.title: Ben-Gvir expands gun access to Caesarea, home of Sara and Yair Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir expanded gun access to additional locations including Caesarea, where members of Prime Minister Netanyahu's family reside. Other newly included areas are Arad, Rosh Pinna, and communities in the Upper Galilee.

stories.title: US Senator calls Trump’s attack on pope ‘abhorrent’
stories.summary: US Senator Mark Kelly criticised President Trump's public remarks about Pope Leo XIV, calling them "abhorrent." Kelly, a Catholic, said the president's Iran policies have led to casualties and accused Trump of attacking anyone to protect himself.

stories.title: Hungary: Peter Magyar's election heralds thaw in EU ties
stories.summary: Péter Magyar's election victory in Hungary signals a potential thaw in relations between Budapest and the European Union. Magyar succeeds Viktor Orbán, who led Hungary for 16 years and maintained close ties with Russia, and has pledged to repair relations with Brussels.

stories.title: Hungary: Orban's ouster heralds thaw in EU ties
stories.summary: Hungarian voters ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule by electing pro-EU candidate Péter Magyar, signaling a potential shift in Hungary's relations with Brussels and a move away from its Russia-friendly foreign policy.

stories.title: China restaurant owner rejects fame after being overwhelmed by growing number of customers
stories.summary: A chicken pot restaurant in Foshan, Guangdong province, went viral in China after its owner rejected the attention from sudden fame. At its peak, over 200 groups of customers waited more than three hours. The owner's reaction reflected the "lying flat" attitude popular among Chinese youth.

stories.title: No illusions: Iranian people return to frontlines of dealing with regime - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that while stopping bombing in Iran is a necessary step, lasting change requires addressing the Iranian regime itself. The piece contends that no deal can produce meaningful results as long as the current government remains in power.

stories.title: Asia braces for gas shortages after Iran talks collapse
stories.summary: Asian energy buyers are bracing for deeper gas supply shortages after US-Iran talks in Islamabad collapsed without a deal. Gas shipments to China fell approximately 30 percent over the past month compared with a year earlier, reflecting growing strain on regional energy supplies linked to Strait of Hormuz tensions.

stories.title: Tributes pour in for legendary Indian singer Asha Bhosle
stories.summary: Indian singer Asha Bhosle died at the age of 92 and will be cremated with full state honours. Tributes have been pouring in from across the country and beyond.

stories.title: Fidesz MEP László attributes loss to low turnout of 'undecided voters' and EU 'economic stagnation'
stories.summary: Fidesz MEP András László attributed the party's election loss to low turnout among undecided voters and broader economic stagnation affecting governing parties across Europe. He accused Hungary's opposition of running a "filthy and hate-filled campaign" focused on personalities rather than policy substance.

stories.title: Easter truce between Ukraine and Russia ends
stories.summary: An Easter truce between Ukraine and Russia has ended. Russia's defence ministry accused Kyiv of nearly 2,000 violations during the ceasefire period.

stories.title: Monday briefing: Hungary chooses Péter Magyar over Viktor Orbán
stories.summary: Péter Magyar's Tisza party defeated Viktor Orbán's Fidesz in Hungary's elections on Sunday, ending 16 years of Fidesz rule. Orbán conceded defeat within hours of polls closing, marking a significant political shift expected to reshape Hungary's relations with the EU, the United States, and Russia.

stories.title: ‘Terrible for foreign policy’: Trump attacks Pope Leo after peace appeal
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV, the first US-born pope, has become a vocal critic of the US-Israeli war on Iran. President Trump responded by publicly attacking the pontiff over his peace appeals, calling him detrimental to foreign policy.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson slams UK's Palestine Action ban, calls Keir Starmer 'enslaved'
stories.summary: American commentator Tucker Carlson condemned the British government's ban on the direct action group Palestine Action in a BBC interview. Carlson criticised Prime Minister Keir Starmer, calling him "enslaved," and questioned whether Starmer made the decision independently.

stories.title: Trump: ‘I don’t care’ if Iran comes back to negotiations
stories.summary: President Trump expressed indifference toward renewed Iran negotiations, blaming Tehran's nuclear ambitions for the collapse of talks. He announced a US naval blockade of Iran, signaling an escalation in pressure on Tehran.

stories.title: Australia pledges US$1.7 million in aid after Cyclone Maila kills 11 in Pacific
stories.summary: Australia pledged A$2.5 million (US$1.7 million) in aid to Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands after Tropical Cyclone Maila caused floods and landslides that killed 11 people. Foreign Minister Penny Wong allocated A$1 million for Papua New Guinea and A$1.5 million for the Solomon Islands.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amnesty International Condemns Killings of Civilians in Military Airstrike
stories.summary: Amnesty International condemned a Nigerian military airstrike that accidentally killed more than 100 civilians.

stories.title: Nigeria: Civilians Feared Killed As NAF Airstrike Hits Border Market
stories.summary: A Nigerian Air Force airstrike hit a border market, with NAF spokesperson Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame describing the strikes as precision bombings targeting terrorists along the Jilli axis. Civilian casualties are feared.

stories.title: Nigeria: Over 1,100 People Kidnapped in Northern Nigeria in Four Months - Amnesty
stories.summary: Amnesty International reported that at least 1,100 people were kidnapped in northern Nigeria within three months, warning of worsening insecurity and government failure to protect citizens.

stories.title: From generation to generation: Holocaust and Oct. 7 meet in intimate salon memorials
stories.summary: The Zikaron BaSalon memorial program has grown to over two million participants worldwide, bringing together Holocaust survivors and families affected by the October 7 attack. Former hostages and their relatives are learning from survivors how sharing personal stories can aid rehabilitation.

stories.title: Is Gout Gout faster than Usain Bolt? Australian sprinter sets sights on Jamaican great’s 200m record
stories.summary: Australian sprinter Gout Gout, 18, ran 19.67 seconds in the 200 meters at the Australian championships in Sydney, breaking the 20-second barrier. His coach Di Sheppard suggested there is no limit to his potential, drawing comparisons to Usain Bolt's 200m record.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland MP Urges Elon Musk's X to Recognize Somaliland Identity
stories.summary: A Somaliland lawmaker in Hargeisa called on Elon Musk and the social media platform X to include the Republic of Somaliland in its identity verification system, citing a lack of digital recognition for Somaliland users.

stories.title: Two men indicted in Tel Aviv for illegal firearms, carjacking tools possession
stories.summary: Two men were indicted in Tel Aviv for illegal firearms possession and possessing carjacking tools. Police conducted an independent investigation that uncovered evidence of deliberate preparation for criminal activity using multiple means.

stories.title: Kenya: From Turkana to Tana River - Kenya's Climate Crisis Drives Hunger, Displacement and Loss
stories.summary: Communities across Kenya's arid northern counties, including Turkana, Wajir, Marsabit, Garissa, Mandera, and Tana River, face worsening hunger and displacement as climate change forces residents to travel longer distances for water and pasture.

stories.title: Video: Participants demand action from leaders as Flotilla sets sail
stories.summary: International participants in the Global Sumud Flotilla held a press conference before setting sail toward Gaza. Activists from countries including Germany and Malaysia acknowledged limitations of civilian aid efforts but said they aimed to counter government inaction regarding Palestinian humanitarian needs.

stories.title: Kenya: Police Dismantle 'Tokyo Mafias' Gang in Nairobi, 10 Suspects Arrested in Makadara Raid
stories.summary: Police in Nairobi dismantled a criminal gang known as the 'Tokyo Mafias' operating in the Makadara area, arresting ten suspects during a targeted security operation.

stories.title: Activists announce ‘Freedom Fleet 2’ to Gaza from European ports
stories.summary: Pro-Palestinian groups announced that a large flotilla called "Freedom Fleet 2" is preparing to sail from European ports, including Marseille and Barcelona, toward Gaza. Organisers said the initiative aims to challenge the blockade, deliver humanitarian aid, and draw global attention to conditions in Gaza.

stories.title: South Africa: Can the Democratic Alliance Transform Fear Into Hope Before 2029 Elections?
stories.summary: Ahead of South Africa's 2029 elections, the Democratic Alliance faces the challenge of addressing voter concerns over crime, corruption, unemployment, and infrastructure failures that are driving disillusionment with politics.

stories.title: Australia appoints first female army chief in ‘historic’ reshuffle of military top brass
stories.summary: Australia announced Lieutenant General Susan Coyle as its first female Chief of Army, effective July. Coyle, currently chief of joint capabilities, will replace Lieutenant General Simon Stuart. The appointment is part of a broader defense force leadership reshuffle as the military seeks to increase female representation.

stories.title: Over 6,500 wounded in Lebanon, death toll climbs amid relentless Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli strikes have killed at least 2,055 people and wounded 6,588 others since March 2. Israeli bombing and raids continue across southern Lebanon. The conflict has displaced approximately 1.1 million people, representing 20 percent of Lebanon's population.

stories.title: Sudan: Civilian Death Toll From North Darfur Drone Attack On Wedding Procession Rises to 58
stories.summary: A drone attack on a wedding procession in Kutum, North Darfur, Sudan, has killed at least 58 civilians, including 17 children, with dozens more injured. Markets have closed and movement has halted as bombardments continue.

stories.title: China’s tea-drink shops thirst for profits as price wars dry up prospects
stories.summary: China's tea-drink market, valued at an estimated 370 billion yuan ($54.2 billion) annually, faces intense price competition threatening to push out thousands of small operators. The market's boom-to-bust cycle illustrates the broader challenge of sustaining profitability in mainland China's consumer sectors.

stories.title: Ukrainian team of veterans and civilians in wooden wheelchairs takes part in Paris Marathon
stories.summary: A Ukrainian team of seven war veterans and civilians participated in the 2026 Paris International Marathon, completing the 42-kilometer course in wooden wheelchairs they built during rehabilitation in Lviv.

stories.title: Shipping halts in Hormuz after US blockade announcement
stories.summary: Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz halted immediately following the US naval blockade announcement, according to Lloyd's List. Some vessels already transiting the strait turned back. Shipping had been operating at reduced levels over the weekend before flows stopped entirely.

stories.title: Defence chief says Australian ships ‘ready, capable’ as Albanese calls on US and Iran to reopen strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called for the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and free navigation for all countries, expressing disappointment at the failure of U.S.–Iran talks. Australia's defence chief said Australian naval ships were ready and capable of assisting if needed.

stories.title: 'Leo should get his act together': Trump attacks Pope over Iran comments
stories.summary: President Trump publicly criticised Pope Leo XIV after the pontiff called for an end to the war with Iran and warned against a "delusion of omnipotence." Trump called the pope "weak on crime" and "terrible for foreign policy" in a social media post, also claiming credit for Leo's election.

stories.title: Viktor Orban ousted after 16 years as Hungarians flock to pro-EU rival
stories.summary: Early election results in Hungary showed Viktor Orban's nationalist Fidesz party losing to a pro-EU opposition rival after 16 years in power, amid public frustration with economic stagnation.

stories.title: Hormuz oil crisis hits China; a family of dentists: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: The Middle East conflict's disruption of the Strait of Hormuz has affected China's transport and manufacturing sectors with reports of cancelled orders. Separately, the UAE withdrew $3.5 billion from Pakistan following its role in Iran war mediation. The compilation also covers Japanese military drills focused on deterring China.

stories.title: Iran executed 'at least 1,639 people' in 2025, highest number since 1989
stories.summary: Iran Human Rights and Together Against the Death Penalty reported that Iran executed at least 1,639 people in 2025, the highest figure since 1989, averaging over four executions daily. The groups warned that executions could increase further following January protests and amid the ongoing conflict triggered by the U.S. and Israel.

stories.title: Once inspired by Viktor Orban, Hungary’s Peter Magyar unseats long-serving PM in landmark election
stories.summary: Péter Magyar defeated long-serving Prime Minister Viktor Orbán in Hungary's landmark election, which saw record voter turnout. The result is expected to shift Hungary's alignment away from Russia and unsettle right-wing political circles in Europe.

stories.title: Iran war could plunge 32 million into poverty, says United Nations
stories.summary: A United Nations Development Programme report warns that the Iran war's economic fallout could push more than 32 million people worldwide into poverty. The UNDP cited a "triple shock" of rising energy costs, food price increases, and weaker economic growth, with developing countries expected to be hit hardest.

stories.title: Swalwell suspends California governor bid amid sexual assault allegations
stories.summary: U.S. Congressman Eric Swalwell suspended his campaign for California governor amid sexual assault allegations. Multiple Democratic lawmakers and dozens of former staffers called on him to leave Congress. Swalwell apologized for past mistakes in judgment while pledging to fight what he called false allegations.

stories.title: Reactions to PM Orban's likely defeat in Hungary's election
stories.summary: Partial results from Hungary's national election indicated that the centre-right opposition Tisza party was on track to win, potentially ending Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule. Orbán, a nationalist leader backed by US President Donald Trump and Russia, appeared headed for defeat.

stories.title: Israel PM formally appoints new Mossad chief
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu formally appointed Roman Gofman as the new head of Mossad. Gofman is a military officer with no prior intelligence background and is viewed as supportive of Netanyahu's nationalist agenda.

stories.title: U.S. military says it will start blockade of all ships going to and from Iran on Monday
stories.summary: US Central Command announced it will begin a full maritime blockade of all ships traveling to and from Iranian ports on Monday. The blockade will apply impartially to vessels of all nations across Iranian ports on the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman.

stories.title: No commander to oversee firefighters as flames blocked access, Tai Po probe hears
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades held its 11th hearing on Monday. The blaze at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po killed 168 people. Four senior firefighters who served as commanders during the incident are set to testify, with prior sessions focusing on deactivated safety systems.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires rocket barrages at northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it launched rocket barrages at northern Israeli towns including Kiryat Shmona and Doviv, citing Israeli ceasefire violations and continued attacks on southern Lebanese villages. The group reported dozens of attacks targeting military positions and infrastructure. Israeli media said two elite paratrooper soldiers were wounded in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump says he ‘doesn’t care’ if Iran returns to talks
stories.summary: President Trump told reporters he is unconcerned about whether Iran returns to negotiations, saying "I don't care." Speaking at Joint Base Andrews, Trump confirmed a blockade of Iranian ports would take effect at 14:00 GMT and described the ceasefire as "holding well."

stories.title: Malaysia seizes US$1.37 million worth of diesel in illegal fuel transfer off Penang
stories.summary: Malaysia's Maritime Enforcement Agency detained two tankers off Penang for allegedly conducting an illegal ship-to-ship transfer of approximately 700,000 litres of diesel. The seizure was valued at US$1.37 million. Malaysia has intensified its crackdown on fuel smuggling amid regional shortages linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Asian markets fall as oil surges past $100 after talks collapse
stories.summary: Asian stock markets fell and oil prices surged past $100 per barrel after US-Iran talks collapsed and Washington ordered a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 0.84 percent and South Korea's Kospi fell 1.83 percent. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 8.56 percent to $104.84 per barrel.

stories.title: Amid fierce global competition, China launches national plan to boost AI education
stories.summary: China launched a national "AI+ Education" action plan to integrate artificial intelligence across all levels of its education system, from primary schools to lifelong learning. The Ministry of Education and four other bodies issued the mandate amid intensifying global competition in advanced technologies.

stories.title: Israeli minister storms Al Aqsa Mosque again amid restrictions on worshippers
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in occupied East Jerusalem on Sunday under heavy police protection. Palestinian officials condemned the incursion amid ongoing restrictions on worshippers' access to the site.

stories.title: UN force in Lebanon says Israeli tank rammed its vehicles in south
stories.summary: The United Nations peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon (UNIFIL) reported that an Israeli tank rammed its vehicles. Israeli soldiers also fired warning shots in the area, striking and damaging clearly identifiable UNIFIL vehicles.

stories.title: After Trump’s blockade announcement, IRGC says will view military vessels approaching Hormuz as ceasefire breach
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps warned that any military vessels approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be treated as a ceasefire violation following President Trump's blockade announcement. The IRGC stated the strait remains under Iranian naval control and is open only to non-military vessels.

stories.title: Peru's presidential election delayed as voting chaos forces extension
stories.summary: Peru's presidential election was extended into Monday after logistical problems disrupted voting across the country. Electoral authorities were forced to delay results in a crowded race featuring 35 candidates, amid widespread public frustration over crime and corruption.

stories.title: Trump lambasts Pope Leo XIV, extending feud over Iran war with first American pontiff
stories.summary: President Trump publicly criticised Pope Leo XIV, the first American pope, escalating a feud over the pontiff's repeated calls to end the war in the Middle East. The remarks came as US and Israeli strikes on Iran continued.

stories.title: Stampede at Haitian mountaintop fortress kills at least 25 people and injures dozens
stories.summary: A stampede at a mountaintop fortress in Haiti killed at least 25 people and injured dozens more. The Haitian National Police opened an investigation to determine the exact cause of the incident.

stories.title: Netanyahu backs Gofman as new Mossad chief, praises military record
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appointed Roman Gofman as the new head of the Mossad intelligence agency. Netanyahu praised Gofman's military record, describing him as bold and creative.

stories.title: High Court releases names of Israeli brothers indicted for selling AI-generated info. to Iran
stories.summary: An Israeli court released the names of two Israeli brothers indicted for selling mostly false, AI-generated information to Iranian contacts. The brothers were charged last month and reportedly received tens of thousands of shekels in exchange.

stories.title: Some of Swalwell's fellow Democrats urge him to quit Congress amid sexual assault allegations
stories.summary: US Representative Eric Swalwell, a leading candidate for California governor, faced growing calls from fellow Democrats to resign from Congress. The pressure follows accusations of sexual assault, which Swalwell has denied.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills paramedic, says Lebanese Red Cross – as it happened
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck what it said was a rocket launcher positioned in the Jouaiyya area of southern Lebanon. The Lebanese Red Cross reported that an Israeli strike killed a paramedic during the same period of operations along the border.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Lebanon war to continue amid talks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that military operations in southern Lebanon will continue, including inside the designated "security zone." Netanyahu spoke after visiting near the border and receiving an operational briefing. Israeli airstrikes have persisted in areas such as Bint Jbeil, though strikes near Beirut have eased.

stories.title: European leaders fete Hungarian opposition’s victory over Orban as win for democracy
stories.summary: European leaders, including officials from Spain, Poland, France, and the EU, celebrated Peter Magyar's opposition victory over Viktor Orban in Hungary as a win for democracy and European unity. Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid wished Magyar well, while Prime Minister Netanyahu, who had effectively endorsed Orban, did not comment.

stories.title: Trump says US gas prices may remain high through November midterm election
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump acknowledged that American gasoline prices may remain elevated through the November midterm elections. The statement was a rare recognition of the political consequences stemming from his decision to launch military action against Iran.

stories.title: US Senator says Trump’s Iran policy fuelling inflation
stories.summary: US Democratic Senator Patty Murray criticised President Trump's Iran policies, saying they are contributing to rising inflation in the United States. Murray said Trump's decision to start a "costly foreign war" was a major factor behind surging prices, contradicting his promises to lower costs.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump announces blockade of Strait of Hormuz on Monday
stories.summary: President Trump announced a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian ports beginning Monday, after ceasefire talks collapsed in Pakistan. Oil prices surged on the news, and both the U.S. and Iran traded blame for the breakdown in negotiations amid rising regional tensions.

stories.title: ‘Not a fan’: Trump launches extraordinary attack on Pope Leo as rift deepens over war
stories.summary: President Trump sharply criticized Pope Leo XIV in social media posts and remarks to reporters, calling him "a very liberal person" and saying he was not doing a good job. Trump suggested the Pope should "stop catering to the Radical Left," deepening a rift between the two leaders over the ongoing war.

stories.title: EU tests of China’s C919 speed up as pilots stay in Shanghai ‘permanently’: sources
stories.summary: European Union Aviation Safety Agency technicians and pilots have established a permanent presence in Shanghai to conduct checks and flight tests on China's C919 airliner. The certification process for the domestically built aircraft, which aims to compete with Boeing and Airbus, has shown steady progress in recent months.

stories.title: Trump considers limited operation against Iran in response to failed Islamabad negotiations - WSJ
stories.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, President Trump is considering a limited military operation against Iran following the failed round of negotiations held in Islamabad.

stories.title: Lebanon says at least five dead as Israel pounds country’s south
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck targets in southern Lebanon, killing at least five people. The Israeli military accused Hezbollah of using a hospital compound in the town of Bint Jbeil for military purposes.

stories.title: Oil prices surge past $103 a barrel after US announces blockade of Iran
stories.summary: Oil prices surged past $103 per barrel following the United States' announcement of a naval blockade targeting Iran. Asian stock markets declined as the blockade threat introduced fresh turmoil into global financial markets.

stories.title: Hong Kong increasingly seen as a safe haven in troubled world
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Hong Kong is increasingly positioned as a safe haven amid global disruptions including the Russia-Ukraine war and the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran. The city's stability is seen as attractive as trade routes, energy supplies, and security alliances are being reshaped by geopolitical upheaval.

stories.title: Massive Attack frontman Robert Del Naja among 500 arrested at Palestine Action protest
stories.summary: Massive Attack frontman Robert Del Naja was among approximately 500 people arrested at a protest in London's Trafalgar Square on Saturday against the ban on Palestine Action. Del Naja was detained on suspicion of showing support for a proscribed organisation while holding a sign reading "I Oppose Genocide, I Support Palestine Action."

stories.title: Viktor Orban concedes ‘painful’ defeat to conservative Peter Magyar in Hungary polls
stories.summary: Nationalist leader Viktor Orban conceded defeat to conservative challenger Peter Magyar in Hungary's parliamentary elections after 16 years in power. With two-thirds of precincts counted, Magyar's party was projected to win approximately 137 of 199 seats. Trump had endorsed Orban ahead of the vote.

stories.title: Judge lifts gag order on names of brothers charged last month in Iran spy case
stories.summary: An Israeli court lifted a gag order revealing Meir and Yosef Nahum as the brothers charged in an Iran espionage case. The pair allegedly provided Iranian agents with AI-generated fake military information in exchange for over $32,000.

stories.title: South Korea includes foreign residents with ‘close ties’ to citizens in state relief plan
stories.summary: South Korea announced that some foreign residents with "close ties" to citizens will be eligible for government cash relief ranging from 100,000 to 600,000 won. The payments are part of a supplementary budget designed to offset high fuel costs caused by the prolonged Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Eric Swalwell quits California governor race after sexual assault allegations
stories.summary: Democratic Congressman Eric Swalwell suspended his campaign for California governor after multiple sexual assault and misconduct allegations from a former staff member and at least three other women. The San Francisco Chronicle reported that the former staffer accused Swalwell of assaulting her twice when she was too inebriated to consent.

stories.title: Saudi summons Iraq ambassador over ‘attacks’ from its territory: State media
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia summoned Iraq's ambassador over allegations that attacks targeting Gulf states may have been launched from Iraqi territory, marking the latest such accusation.

stories.title: Geopolitical tensions may bolster Hong Kong office demand as Gulf capital looks east
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Hong Kong's office market could benefit as Gulf investors seek stable financial hubs amid the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran. The geopolitical disruption may drive demand for premium office space in Hong Kong's core business districts as capital from the Middle East looks eastward for diversification.

stories.title: China woman unhappy with salary takes 5-hour nap at work to show boss ‘You get what you pay for’
stories.summary: A woman in Shangqiu, Henan province, China, went viral on social media after taking a five-hour nap at work to protest what she considered an inadequate salary. Her boss reportedly threatened to fire her. The incident resonated with online audiences amid broader discussions about workplace dissatisfaction in China.

stories.title: Elusive deal: On the Iran-U.S. ceasefire talks
stories.summary: The United States and Iran concluded ceasefire talks without reaching a final agreement. Commentators have urged both sides to continue diplomatic engagement to end the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Kremlin planning to cut support for agricultural sector amid budget crisis, intel reports
stories.summary: Intelligence reports indicate the Kremlin is planning to reduce state support for Russia's agro-industrial sector amid a growing budget deficit, despite previously designating agriculture as a strategic priority.

stories.title: US to begin enforcing Strait of Hormuz blockade from Monday morning, CENTCOM announces
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that enforcement of a naval blockade around the Strait of Hormuz will begin Monday morning. CENTCOM stated the blockade will be applied impartially to vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas.

stories.title: US military threatens to blockade all Iranian ports starting on Monday
stories.summary: The US military announced it will blockade all Iranian ports beginning Monday. US Central Command stated that vessels will still be permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz to and from non-Iranian ports.

stories.title: From toilet paper to travel: why inflation could soon hit Hongkongers hard
stories.summary: Economists and business leaders warned that Hong Kong faces a wave of imported inflation from the world's highest petrol and diesel prices caused by the Middle East war's oil crisis. Analysts said the impact on inflation would be more immediate than effects on growth, with repercussions expected in the third and fourth quarters.

stories.title: Uruguay hosts DEA summit that warns of new drug trafficking routes in South America
stories.summary: Uruguay hosted the DEA's 2nd Regional Coordination Meeting of the Southern Cone Division on April 9–10 in Montevideo. Representatives from Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and the United States discussed strengthening cooperation against drug trafficking and transnational organized crime, including emerging trafficking routes across South America.

stories.title: ‘No other way’: Mid-East prepares for more fighting as Iran peace talks fail
stories.summary: Following the failure of US-Iran talks in Islamabad, countries across the Middle East are preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities as the two-week ceasefire's future remains uncertain.

stories.title: Russia–Ukraine Easter truce expires amid mutual accusations of violations
stories.summary: A 32-hour Easter truce between Russia and Ukraine expired on Monday, with both sides accusing each other of thousands of violations along the roughly 1,200-kilometer front line. Despite a brief reduction in air and missile strikes, drone and artillery activity continued throughout the ceasefire period.

stories.title: Shin Bet chief reportedly tells court PM can’t testify at trial over danger to life
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet chief reportedly told a court that Prime Minister Netanyahu cannot testify at his trial due to danger to his life, claiming Iranian agents might exploit his testimony. A government watchdog noted that the previous Shin Bet head had refused a similar request from the prime minister.

stories.title: DHS investigating claim about Swalwell nanny filed by conspiracy theorist
stories.summary: The Manhattan district attorney's office opened a criminal investigation into a sexual assault allegation against Congressman Eric Swalwell, reportedly committed in New York in 2024. Separately, conspiracy theorist Joel Gilbert filed claims with DHS accusing Swalwell of immigration law violations related to a nanny.

stories.title: Gaza-bound aid flotilla sets sail symbolically, delays international waters departure due to weather conditions
