stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla departed Barcelona symbolically on Sunday en route to Gaza but delayed its voyage into international waters due to adverse weather. Coordinator Thiago Avila said the mission would proceed in phases, with possible further delays along the route.

stories.title: Japan to welcome 30 Nato envoys as Trump rattles US allies
stories.summary: Japan will host 30 NATO ambassadors this month for talks on China's regional influence, Russia's war in Ukraine, and the evolving global security landscape. The visit reflects deepening ties between Japan and the transatlantic alliance amid growing concerns about Washington's reliability as a security partner.

stories.title: Iran war live: US military says it will block Iranian traffic in Hormuz
stories.summary: US Central Command announced a blockade of Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, set to begin at 14:00 GMT. Iran warned the move would lead to further increases in fuel prices.

stories.title: Political turmoil in Indian border state as nine million lose voting rights
stories.summary: Nine million voters have been removed from electoral rolls in India's West Bengal state, raising concerns about voter exclusion and electoral fairness.

stories.title: 'Game on’: How Iran can exact a toll in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An analysis describes how Iran could leverage its geographic position along the Strait of Hormuz to impose tolls and exert control over oil tanker traffic, including requiring clearance codes and payments routed through Omani banks linked to Tehran.

stories.title: Peru closes a troubled election day and begins a lengthy count with outcome uncertain
stories.summary: Peru's election day closed after a ten-hour voting period marred by logistical failures that forced a one-hour extension. Fifteen voting centers in Lima could not be set up, leaving approximately 63,300 voters unable to cast ballots.

stories.title: What can the IDF learn from Ukraine about emerging Hezbollah FPV threat? - comment
stories.summary: Hezbollah is increasingly deploying first-person-view explosive drones against IDF forces, adopting tactics observed in Ukraine's battlefield. Analysts say the trend raises concerns about Israel's preparedness for this evolving aerial threat.

stories.title: Australia news live: Albanese says Australia ‘hasn’t been asked’ to help blockade strait of Hormuz; Labor defends fuel security ads
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated that Australia has not been asked to participate in the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. He called for a resumption of US-Iran negotiations, citing the massive global economic impact of the standoff.

stories.title: The US-Iran ceasefire appears to be holding. What next?
stories.summary: High-level talks between the United States and Iran held in Islamabad ended without a formal agreement after 21 hours of negotiations. US Vice President JD Vance announced at an early-morning press briefing that no deal had been reached. Despite the inconclusive outcome, a ceasefire between the two sides appears to be holding.

stories.title: Oil tops $100 after US-Iran talks collapse
stories.summary: Following the collapse of US-Iran negotiations, oil prices surged past $100 a barrel. Brent crude futures reached $102.60, while US crude hit a session high of $105.25, according to Reuters.

stories.title: War update: 91 clashes on frontline, 7,696 ceasefire violations recorded since truce begins
stories.summary: A total of 91 combat clashes were recorded along the frontline, with 7,696 ceasefire violations logged since the truce began. Russian forces have broadly adhered to ceasefire terms but continue operations in certain areas, particularly using drones.

stories.title: Number of phishing cases drops in Hong Kong but victims lose more money
stories.summary: Hong Kong police reported that the number of phishing scam cases dropped by more than half last year, but total financial losses doubled to HK$110 million. A phishing simulation found that more than one in eight employees clicked malicious email links.

stories.title: Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran after talks collapse
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is reportedly considering restarting limited military strikes on Iran and enforcing a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz after talks in Pakistan ended without agreement. A broader bombing campaign is also under review but is considered less likely due to escalation concerns.

stories.title: Iran says talks were ‘two steps away’ from a deal before US ‘intransigence’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said negotiations with the United States in Islamabad were close to producing a memorandum of understanding before collapsing. Tehran blamed shifting US demands and what Araghchi described as Washington's intransigence for the failure.

stories.title: After talks fail, IDF planning for return to war, Trump mulls strikes on Iran — reports
stories.summary: Reports indicate the Israeli Defense Forces are preparing for a possible return to war following the failure of negotiations, while the US has signaled that ending Iran's nuclear program and its support for proxy groups were non-negotiable demands during the talks.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner beats Alcaraz in Monte Carlo final to reclaim top spot in tennis rankings
stories.summary: Italy's Jannik Sinner defeated Spain's Carlos Alcaraz 7-6(5), 6-3 in the Monte Carlo Masters final, claiming his first clay-court Masters title and reclaiming the world number one ranking. The victory marked Sinner's fourth consecutive Masters 1000 title and eighth overall.

stories.title: Two soldiers moderately hurt by Hezbollah rocket fire in southern Lebanon on Sunday — IDF
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were moderately injured by Hezbollah rocket fire in southern Lebanon on Sunday, according to the IDF. The troops were hospitalized for shockwave-related injuries from the rocket impact.

stories.title: Iranian hopes dashed as US talks fail after weeks of war
stories.summary: Iranian civilians expressed disappointment after US-Iran negotiations failed to produce a deal, with weeks of bombardment having taken a heavy toll on the population.

stories.title: Iran navy chief mocks Trump Hormuz blockade threat as ‘ridiculous’
stories.summary: Iran's navy commander Shahram Irani dismissed US President Trump's threat to blockade the Strait of Hormuz as "ridiculous" following the breakdown of US-Iran talks. He stated that Iranian naval forces are monitoring all US military movements in the region.

stories.title: Trump orders naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz after failed US-Iran talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump ordered a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz beginning Monday after US-Iran ceasefire talks in Pakistan collapsed without agreement. The announcement raised concerns about further disruption to global energy supplies and international shipping routes.

stories.title: Trump's blockade threat raises risks and leaves predicaments unchanged
stories.summary: The US blockade of Iran has evolved into a test of endurance between Iran's ability to withstand strikes and Washington's willingness to bear the war's costs. Analysts say the strategy raises risks without resolving underlying tensions.

stories.title: Bangladesh government starts China outreach, to send 20-member delegation this week
stories.summary: Bangladesh's government is initiating outreach to China by sending a 20-member delegation this week. China is involved in several major projects in Bangladesh, including the Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration Project.

stories.title: IMF warns Strait of Hormuz might never be back to normal
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that shipping disruption at the Strait of Hormuz may not fully recover, drawing parallels to the Bab al-Mandab strait, where traffic has not returned to normal since the first Houthi attacks.

stories.title: Dar briefs Turkish, Saudi, Egyptian FMs on Islamabad Talks, reaffirms support for diplomacy and dialogue
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar briefed the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey on the concluded US-Iran talks held in Islamabad, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to supporting diplomatic efforts and dialogue.

stories.title: 'Civilisation will die' remarks brought Iran to bargaining table: Trump
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump claimed his remarks about the potential destruction of Iranian civilization helped bring Iran to the negotiating table, attempting to justify the comments by noting Iran's longstanding "death to America" rhetoric.

stories.title: After Trump’s Hormuz blockade announcement, IRGC says will view military vessels approaching strait as ceasefire breach
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps warned that any military vessels approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be treated as a ceasefire violation following President Trump's blockade announcement. The IRGC stated the strait remains under Iranian naval control but is open to non-military vessels.

stories.title: US to enforce maritime blockade on Iranian ports from April 13
stories.summary: US Central Command announced it will begin enforcing a maritime blockade on Iranian ports starting 13 April at 1500 GMT. The move follows President Donald Trump's directive after US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without a deal.

stories.title: IDF Merkava tank rammed UNIFIL vehicles on two occassions on Sunday, UN force claims
stories.summary: UNIFIL reported that an Israeli Defense Forces Merkava tank rammed its vehicles on two occasions in southern Lebanon on Sunday. The UN force also said IDF troops fired warning shots near its positions, raising concerns about peacekeeper safety and freedom of movement.

stories.title: Lebanon PM says working to achieve Israeli troop withdrawal
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister said he is working toward achieving a withdrawal of Israeli troops from Lebanese territory. Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes have killed 2,055 people, including 165 children and over 80 health workers.

stories.title: Hungary's 'return to Europe: Peaceful revolution' embraces new path away from Russia and autocracy
stories.summary: Péter Magyar is set to become Hungary's new prime minister after winning a supermajority in elections widely seen as a civic awakening. Analysts and politicians describe the result as a turn away from autocracy and a restoration of Hungary's democratic trajectory within Europe.

stories.title: Nigerian airstrike hits market, 200 feared dead in northeast Yobe state
stories.summary: At least 200 people are feared dead after Nigerian military jets struck a village market in northeast Yobe state on Saturday night while pursuing Islamist militants, according to a local councillor and residents in Maiduguri.

stories.title: Ukrainian marine returns home after four years in Russian captivity
stories.summary: Ukrainian marine Yevhenii Demchuk returned home to Ukraine after spending four years in Russian captivity as part of a prisoner exchange. Demchuk is from the village of Lvove in the Kherson region.

stories.title: Trump vows to blockade Strait of Hormuz after Iran peace talks stumble
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. will blockade the Strait of Hormuz and begin destroying mines he said Iran had placed in the waterway. The announcement followed the failure of U.S.-Iran peace talks to reach agreement on Tehran's nuclear program.

stories.title: What an ancient Chinese map reveals about global history and modern power: Sheng-Wei Wang
stories.summary: Scholar Sheng-Wei Wang discusses her research into an ancient Chinese world map, arguing it suggests Chinese explorers mapped the world before the European Age of Discovery. She also examines how Eurocentric historical narratives continue to shape modern power dynamics.

stories.title: Peru presidential run-off looms as Fujimori leads troubled vote
stories.summary: Peru's Keiko Fujimori led first-round presidential voting on Sunday but fell well short of the 50 percent threshold needed to avoid a runoff. Far-right candidate Rafael Lopez Aliaga emerged as her nearest rival. The election was marred by logistics problems, police raids, and allegations of fraud.

stories.title: DIG orders inquiry after video, purportedly showing armed robbery on Karachi bridge, goes viral
stories.summary: In Karachi, East DIG Dr Farrukh Ali ordered an inquiry after a viral video purportedly showed 10–12 armed robbers looting commuters on a bridge in Shah Faisal Colony at night. Police in Korangi and Malir were directed to investigate and register an FIR.

stories.title: Trump's incendiary rhetoric fuels 'chaos and confusion', driving NATO allies toward self-reliance
stories.summary: Alexandre Vautravers of the Geneva Centre for Security Policy said President Trump's confrontational rhetoric is pushing NATO allies toward greater military self-reliance. He noted that Europe is entering a phase of cautious autonomy as the US becomes an increasingly unpredictable alliance partner.

stories.title: These are people Israel killed in Lebanon on a single day
stories.summary: On Wednesday, April 8, Israeli strikes across Lebanon killed more than 350 people in a matter of minutes, marking one of the deadliest single days of the conflict.

stories.title: At least 100 people killed in ‘mistaken’ air force attack on Nigerian market
stories.summary: A Nigerian military airstrike hit a village market in Yobe State near the Borno State border, killing at least 100 people. The strike was reportedly targeting jihadist insurgents in the epicenter of the northeast insurgency.

stories.title: Hamas position on disarmament to be determined this week, source tells 'Post'
stories.summary: A source told the Jerusalem Post that Hamas's position on disarmament is expected to be determined this week. During a recent Israeli security cabinet meeting, several ministers called for military action against central Gaza camps if Hamas refuses to disarm.

stories.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir visits flashpoint Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir visited the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem's Old City, one of the most sensitive religious sites in the region, sacred to both Judaism and Islam.

stories.title: US threatens to ‘vigorously prosecute’ Iran oil sanctions breaches
stories.summary: Acting Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche warned that the US Department of Justice will "vigorously prosecute" anyone involved in buying or selling sanctioned Iranian crude oil. He stated the DOJ fully supports President Trump and the military.

stories.title: Roman Gofman approved as new Mossad director, PMO confirms
stories.summary: The Israeli Prime Minister's Office confirmed Major General Roman Gofman as the new Mossad director. Gofman, currently serving as the prime minister's military secretary, will replace David Barnea on June 2.

stories.title: Ukraine’s USFs hit over 24,000 pieces of Russian military equipment in 10 months
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces have struck more than 24,000 pieces of Russian military equipment in the 10 months since their establishment. The force operates drones and other unmanned platforms as part of Ukraine's armed forces.

stories.title: 200 feared dead after Nigerian air strike hits market in northeast Yobe state
stories.summary: An estimated 200 people are feared dead after Nigerian military aircraft struck a village market in Yobe state while pursuing Islamist militants. Nigeria's Air Force confirmed striking Boko Haram fighters in the Jilli axis in neighbouring Borno state but did not mention hitting a market.

stories.title: Abuse allegations against lead Democrat shake race for California governor
stories.summary: US Representative Eric Swalwell, a leading Democratic candidate in the California governor's race, faces calls to resign following media reports detailing sexual assault allegations against him.

stories.title: Trump orders US naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump ordered a U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz after Iran refused to make concessions on its nuclear program during negotiations.

stories.title: Iran president urges US to abandon 'totalitarianism' negotiating position
stories.summary: Iran's president called on the United States to abandon what he described as a "totalitarianism" negotiating stance, saying a deal is achievable if Washington respects Iranian rights. He praised parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf's role in negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia accuse each other of Easter truce violations
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia accused each other of violating an Easter ceasefire, with Ukraine recording 2,299 violations including shellings and drone strikes. Russia's Defence Ministry accused Kyiv of nearly 2,000 breaches.

stories.title: Approximately 120 Holocaust survivors made aliyah during Gaza war, but numbers dropping
stories.summary: Approximately 120 Holocaust survivors immigrated to Israel during the Gaza war, though overall numbers are declining. The Aliyah Ministry attributed the decrease to the growing difficulty of relocating at an advanced age.

stories.title: Military tax revenue rises 27.5%, budget receives over UAH 43B in Q1
stories.summary: In the first quarter of 2026, Ukrainians paid 43.5 billion hryvnias in military tax, an increase of 27.5% or 9.4 billion hryvnias compared to the same period in 2025. The revenue supports Ukraine's defense budget.

stories.title: Gov’t secretary claims chief of staff Zamir backs haredi draft bill at High Court, IDF denies
stories.summary: Israeli Government Secretary Yossi Fuchs claimed that IDF Chief of Staff Zamir supports a proposed bill on haredi (ultra-Orthodox) military draft. IDF sources denied the claim, stating they strongly oppose the legislation put forward by Bismuth.

stories.title: Hungary’s Orban concedes landmark defeat to center-right opposition
stories.summary: Hungary's Viktor Orban conceded defeat to the center-right, pro-EU Tisza party in parliamentary elections. The result could reshape European political dynamics and weaken Orban's ties with leaders including Putin, Trump, and Netanyahu.

stories.title: Nigerian artisans preserve handwoven fabric amid rising global demand
stories.summary: Nigerian artisans continue to hand-weave traditional aso-oke fabric, resisting mechanisation as global demand for the textile grows in international fashion markets.

stories.title: Could the Iran war pose lasting risks to global food security?
stories.summary: The United Nations has warned that the ongoing conflict involving Iran could pose lasting risks to global food security, with impacts potentially extending well beyond the duration of hostilities.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s military secretary Roman Gofman approved to serve as next Mossad chief
stories.summary: Roman Gofman, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's military secretary, has been approved as the next Mossad chief. His five-year term is set to begin in June. Gofman was previously involved in a controversial online influence operation using a minor.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in Islamabad yield no conclusion. Will the war resume?
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran talks held in Islamabad ended without a conclusion after extended negotiations. Pakistan, which hosted the discussions, urged both sides to maintain the existing two-week ceasefire while considering next steps.

stories.title: Three killed as armed men attack Pakistan Coast Guards in Arabian Sea
stories.summary: Armed men attacked Pakistan Coast Guards in the Arabian Sea, killing three personnel. The incident occurred in Balochistan, a region experiencing ongoing insurgency where armed groups frequently target security forces.

stories.title: Israel to mark Holocaust remembrance, but ceremonies disrupted by Iran war
stories.summary: Israel is set to mark Holocaust Remembrance Day, but ceremonies have been disrupted by the ongoing war with Iran. Despite a pause in Iranian missile strikes and relaxed safety regulations, Yad Vashem confirmed there would be no live ceremony.

stories.title: Israel’s Ben Gvir says he feels like the 'owner' of Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir visited the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem and declared he feels like its "owner," calling for expanded access for Jewish worshippers. The visit came days after Israel reopened the site to Palestinian worshippers following a month-long closure.

stories.title: History of flotilla campaigns to end Israel’s siege of Gaza
stories.summary: A flotilla of approximately 70 boats has departed from Spain with the goal of breaking Israel's naval blockade on Gaza. The effort follows a history of similar campaigns that have faced Israeli interceptions at sea.

stories.title: High turnout: Over 74% of voters cast ballots in Hungary
stories.summary: Voter turnout in Hungary's parliamentary elections exceeded 74% by 5:00 p.m. local time on Sunday, with over 5.5 million people casting ballots. The high participation marked significant public engagement in the vote.

stories.title: Why Viktor Orban’s Fidesz Party Lost
stories.summary: In Hungary's recent elections, an opposition coalition defeated Viktor Orbán's ruling Fidesz party in a result widely seen as unexpected. The outcome has drawn comparisons to political dynamics in the United States, with observers noting potential lessons for the Democratic Party and implications for allies of former President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Why Viktor Orban’s Fidesz Party Lost
stories.summary: An analysis of Hungary's parliamentary elections examines why Viktor Orban's Fidesz party lost to Peter Magyar's opposition, drawing lessons for US Democrats and warnings for allies of former President Trump.

stories.title: What’s next for the US-Iran peace process after talks end without a deal?
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran concluded in Pakistan without a deal. Sources in Islamabad indicated that some progress was made during the talks, leaving open the possibility of future diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Hezbollah rocket hits remains of 1,500-year-old Byzantine church in Nahariya
stories.summary: A Hezbollah rocket struck a structure in Nahariya, Israel, that housed the remains of a 1,500-year-old Byzantine church. The Israel Antiquities Authority said the modern protective building was damaged but the ancient mosaic floor remained intact.

stories.title: IDF kills Hamas terrorists involved in hostage-taking on October 7
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it killed Hamas operatives involved in hostage-taking during the October 7 attack. Among those killed was Ali Sami Mohammad Shakra, identified as a Nukhba unit commander who participated in the abduction of several hostages including Hersh Goldberg-Polin.

stories.title: Netanyahu appoints army general as new Mossad chief
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has appointed Major General Roman Gofman as the next director of the Mossad. Gofman, who has a background in the armoured corps rather than intelligence, will replace outgoing director David Barnea on June 2, 2026.

stories.title: From achievement in Iran to diplomacy, and back to pressure - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis notes differing emphases among Israeli and US leaders following the Iran talks: Prime Minister Netanyahu focused on military capability, US Vice President JD Vance highlighted commitments, and President Trump escalated pressure on Iran.

stories.title: “The initiative is in the hands of Tehran, not Washington”
stories.summary: Defence analyst Mushahid Hussain Syed stated that the US-Iran conflict cannot be resolved through military force, arguing that the diplomatic initiative currently rests with Tehran rather than Washington.

stories.title: First lady urges public cooperation as nationwide anti-polio campaign begins April 13
stories.summary: Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto Zardari urged public cooperation ahead of a nationwide anti-polio vaccination campaign beginning April 13. The week-long drive aims to vaccinate over 45 million children under five across all provinces and regions.

stories.title: Hezbollah rocket hits Byzantine-era church in Nahariya, damages protective infrastructure
stories.summary: A Hezbollah rocket struck a Byzantine-era church in the Israeli city of Nahariya, damaging protective infrastructure around a restored mosaic. The mosaic, originally destroyed by Persians in 614 CE, had been painstakingly restored by the Israel Antiquities Authority and opened to the public in 2022.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts power restrictions on Monday, but only for industrial customers
stories.summary: Ukraine's grid operator Ukrenergo announced power restrictions for Monday, April 13, affecting industrial consumers across all regions from 4:00 p.m. to midnight. Household consumers are not expected to face rationing.

stories.title: Iran war cost about NIS 35 billion in budgetary expenses, Finance Ministry says
stories.summary: Israel's Finance Ministry estimated the Iran war cost approximately NIS 35 billion in budgetary expenses over a 40-day campaign, with defence costs alone accounting for an estimated NIS 22 billion.

stories.title: The infant Lebanese girl who was killed by an Israeli strike at her father’s funeral
stories.summary: Seven-year-old Aline Saeed was severely injured and her infant sister killed in an Israeli airstrike on their family home in the village of Srifa in southern Lebanon. The strike occurred on the first day of a US-Iran ceasefire, during her father's funeral; Israeli strikes killed over 350 people across Lebanon.

stories.title: 'No other way': Mideast prepares for more fighting as talks fail
stories.summary: Civilians across the Middle East expressed anxiety after peace talks between the United States and Iran collapsed in Pakistan. Residents in the region voiced concern about the prospect of further military escalation.

stories.title: How shaky is the Iran-US ceasefire?
stories.summary: The ceasefire between the United States and Iran remains fragile, with uncertainty over whether the truce will lead to a lasting peace agreement or a resumption of hostilities.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of violating Putin’s Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged accusations of violating a 32-hour Easter ceasefire declared by President Vladimir Putin, which was meant to last from Saturday afternoon through Sunday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had agreed to observe the truce but warned of possible violations. The mutual accusations came as Orthodox Christians in both countries marked the holiday.

stories.title: Is Iran's nuclear threat completely removed or imminently deadly? - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines whether Iran's nuclear threat has been fully eliminated or remains a danger, arguing that the US-led war was not primarily driven by the nuclear issue despite shifting public messaging from US and Israeli leaders.

stories.title: Iran says goodwill steps advanced US talks, dismisses Trump threats
stories.summary: Iran's senior negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Tehran's goodwill gestures helped advance negotiations with the United States. He dismissed recent threats from U.S. President Donald Trump, stating they would not alter Iran's stance in the talks.

stories.title: In Kharkiv region, bomb disposal experts destroy over 40 WWII-era munitions
stories.summary: Explosive ordnance disposal teams from Ukraine's State Emergency Service recovered and destroyed 43 World War II-era munitions in the Kharkiv region. The operation addressed lingering dangers from decades-old unexploded ordnance.

stories.title: UN says Israeli tank rammed peacekeeper vehicles in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) reported that an Israeli Merkava tank rammed its clearly marked peacekeeping vehicles twice on Sunday in southern Lebanon. UNIFIL also said Israeli soldiers fired warning shots near its personnel during the past week, with one landing a metre from a peacekeeper.

stories.title: ‘Feels like a blessing’: On Orthodox Easter, Christians flock back to the Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: During a ceasefire between Israel and Iran, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem reopened to the public for Orthodox Easter. Christians from various denominations returned to the site, believed to enshrine Jesus's tomb, with cautious celebration.

stories.title: Nigeria: Over 100 civilians killed in airstrike described as ‘mistake’ by rights groups
stories.summary: Over 100 civilians were killed in a Nigerian airstrike that rights groups have described as a mistake. Dozens of injured victims were taken to a hospital in Geidam for treatment.

stories.title: Pope says he is 'closer than ever' to Lebanese people
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV expressed solidarity with the people of Lebanon, saying he is "closer than ever" to them. The pope has spoken out against war multiple times in recent weeks.

stories.title: South Africa coalition party elects Cape Town mayor as leader
stories.summary: South Africa's Democratic Alliance elected Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis as the party's new leader on Sunday. The DA, the second-largest party in the ruling coalition, aims to leverage public discontent to broaden its support ahead of upcoming local elections.

stories.title: Military air strikes kill dozens of people in northeast Nigeria, Amnesty International says
stories.summary: Military air strikes hit a village in northeastern Nigeria on Saturday, killing dozens of people, according to Amnesty International. Nigeria's air force initially said it had targeted a known terrorist logistics hub but later announced an investigation following reports of civilian casualties.

stories.title: Move to expel Democrat Eric Swalwell from Congress gains steam
stories.summary: A growing bipartisan group in Congress is calling for the expulsion of Democratic Representative Eric Swalwell following reported allegations of sexual assault and rape, which he denies. Separately, Republican Representative Tony Gonzales of Texas faces scrutiny over an affair with a staffer who died by suicide. Swalwell may face an expulsion vote before he can resign.

stories.title: Arab pressure reins in Hezbollah protests ahead of Israel-Lebanon talks
stories.summary: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have pressured Hezbollah-allied Lebanese parliament speaker to halt protests ahead of Israel-Lebanon negotiations. The demonstrations failed to dissuade Prime Minister Nawaf Salam from proceeding with Washington-backed talks.

stories.title: Russia ready to supply gas to the EU if it has a surplus, says reports
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia is prepared to supply natural gas to the European Union if it has a surplus. However, Peskov also noted that Europe would find alternative gas sources even without Russian supply.

stories.title: WATCH: Netanyahu, Defense Minister Katz visit IDF troops in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz visited IDF troops deployed in southern Lebanon. Katz announced that the operation to disarm Hezbollah in southern Lebanon has been named "Silver Plow."

stories.title: What Iran refused in ceasefire talks that sank a deal
stories.summary: US-Iran ceasefire talks in Pakistan concluded without a deal, with an American official telling reporters that significant gaps remained between the two sides. The official said the parties "were really not close to an agreement."

stories.title: Pope says he is ‘closer than ever’ to Lebanese people
stories.summary: Pope Francis expressed solidarity with the people of Lebanon, saying he is "closer than ever" to them. He emphasized a moral obligation to protect Lebanese civilians and called on all warring parties to pursue peace.

stories.title: John Mearsheimer to New Arab: US-Israel post-war relation 'sour'
stories.summary: Political scientist John Mearsheimer told The New Arab that the U.S.-Israel relationship is likely to become "sour" in the post-war period. The ongoing U.S.-Israel war on Iran is raising questions about the future direction of American foreign policy in the Middle East.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu, in south Lebanon, says threat of invasion by Hezbollah removed
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited troops in southern Lebanon, declaring that Israeli forces had eliminated the threat of a Hezbollah invasion. The visit occurred two days before scheduled trilateral talks between Lebanon, Israel, and the United States in Washington. Netanyahu stated that military operations continue within the security zone in Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran talks yielded progress on ‘most points’ but no nuclear agreement
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said talks with Iran held in Islamabad yielded progress on "most points" but failed to secure an agreement on Tehran's nuclear program. Trump warned that Washington would move to blockade the Strait of Hormuz following the breakdown in negotiations.

stories.title: Unexploded drone munition safely disposed of in Finland
stories.summary: Finnish Armed Forces and police safely detonated an unexploded drone component found in a remote area of the municipality of Iitti, Finland. The disposal operation was carried out without incident.

stories.title: UK rules out role in Hormuz blockade, backs navigation coalition
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has ruled out participating in any blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Financial Times. London opposes imposing fees on vessels transiting the waterway and is working with France and other partners to form a coalition protecting freedom of navigation.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills infant girl in south Lebanon during father’s funeral
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon killed an infant girl who was not yet two years old. The strike reportedly occurred while the child's father was attending a funeral.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. to start blockading the Strait of Hormuz immediately
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an immediate naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, ordering the Navy to interdict all vessels that have paid tolls to Iran. Trump stated that no one paying what he called an "illegal toll" would have safe passage on international waters.

stories.title: No need for hard stares as Paddington: The Musical triumphs at Olivier awards
stories.summary: Paddington: The Musical dominated the Olivier Awards ceremony at London's Royal Albert Hall, winning seven prizes including best new musical. James Hameed, who voices and puppeteers Paddington, won best actor in a musical. Rachel Zegler, Rosamund Pike, and Paapa Essiedu were also recognised.

stories.title: British minister says ‘disappointing’ no breakthrough in Iran war talks
stories.summary: British Health Secretary Wes Streeting described the lack of a breakthrough in US-Iran peace talks as disappointing. He characterized earlier social media comments by US President Donald Trump as incendiary.

stories.title: Israeli lawmaker taunts Trump with apparent call to attack Iran
stories.summary: Israeli lawmaker Zvika Fogel, chair of the Knesset's National Security Committee and a member of the far-right Jewish Power party, publicly urged US President Donald Trump to seemingly attack Iran. Fogel stated: "Donald, if you have to shoot, shoot. Don't quack."

stories.title: Rescuers dig through rubble after deadly Israeli strikes in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Rescue teams are searching through rubble in southern Lebanon after Israeli airstrikes killed at least 13 people in the latest wave of attacks on the region.

stories.title: Trump says US will blockade strait of Hormuz after Iran peace talks fail
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the US would begin blockading the Strait of Hormuz following the failure of peace talks with Iran in Pakistan. Trump also repeated threats to strike Iranian water treatment facilities, power plants, and bridges if Tehran does not abandon its nuclear weapons programme. Iran warned the blockade would breach the existing ceasefire.

stories.title: Russians attack evacuation convoy with drones, kill own prisoners in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked an evacuation convoy with drones in Chasiv Yar, Donetsk region, killing wounded soldiers, including their own prisoners, during a declared ceasefire. The attack targeted a group being evacuated from the front lines.

stories.title: UK: Streeting says 'disappointing' no breakthrough in Iran talks
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting called it "disappointing" that no breakthrough was reached in the US-Iran talks. He also criticized Trump's use of "provocative, incendiary" language, particularly threats regarding Iran's civilization.

stories.title: Lebanese govt politically present, operationally absent': PM accuses Israel of violating int'l law'
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister accused Israel of violating international law amid ongoing Israeli military operations across Lebanon. Spokesperson Jad Shahrour of the Samir Kassir Foundation highlighted the fragmentation of international narratives and the humanitarian toll on civilians. The Iran-US ceasefire does not extend to Lebanon, which remains an active conflict zone.

stories.title: Dozens feared dead in air strike on village in northeastern Nigeria
stories.summary: Amnesty International reports that a military airstrike struck a market in Jilli village in northeastern Nigeria, killing more than 100 people. The attack targeted a civilian area, raising concerns about the use of force.

stories.title: Trump orders US Navy to block Hormuz Strait after Iran talks fail
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to blockade the Strait of Hormuz after ceasefire talks with Iran in Pakistan failed to produce a deal. Trump said the US is working to clear the strait of mines and reopen it to all shipping.

stories.title: Iran says Hormuz open to civilian vessels, warns military ships
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open to civilian vessel traffic in compliance with international law. The IRGC warned that any military ships approaching the waterway would be "dealt with severely."

stories.title: CENTCOM using underwater drones to clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US Central Command is deploying underwater drones to clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway's closure remains a key sticking point in US-Iran ceasefire talks, with Iran estimated to possess between 2,000 and 6,000 naval mines.

stories.title: Israel’s far-right minister visits flashpoint Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, a far-right politician, visited the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem. Ben-Gvir stated he was seeking to expand access to the site for Jewish worshippers, a move considered provocative by Palestinians.

stories.title: West Asia war hit Nepal’s remittance economy, says FM Shishir Khanal
stories.summary: Nepal's Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal stated that the 2026 West Asia war has negatively affected Nepal's remittance economy. He expressed hope the ceasefire would hold and said Prime Minister Balendra Shah plans to visit India.

stories.title: Civilians feared killed after reports of air strike on Nigerian market
stories.summary: Reports indicate that an airstrike struck a village market in Nigeria, with civilians feared killed. The Nigerian Air Force has not addressed the allegations that the strike hit the market while targeting militants.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine trade accusations of Orthodox Easter ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of violating a 32-hour ceasefire declared for Orthodox Easter. Both sides reported over a thousand drone and shelling attacks just hours after the truce began on Saturday in their four-year war.

stories.title: Hungarian parliamentary elections: voter turnout exceeded 66%
stories.summary: By 3:00 p.m. local time on Sunday, voter turnout in Hungary's parliamentary elections reached 66.01%, with nearly 5 million people having cast ballots. Turnout continued to climb through the afternoon.

stories.title: Iran warns any military ships nearing Strait of Hormuz would breach ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned that any military vessels approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be treated as a breach of the two-week ceasefire with the United States. The Guards said Iran's navy maintains control and "smart management" of the strategic waterway while keeping it open for non-military traffic.

stories.title: Peruvians vote in crowded presidential race as runoff looms
stories.summary: Peruvians voted on Sunday in a first-round presidential election featuring more than 30 candidates. The crowded field follows years of political turmoil that have eroded public confidence in institutions, making a runoff likely.

stories.title: Iran 'retains nuclear capabilities' despite weeks of bombardment
stories.summary: Despite weeks of sustained US and Israeli strikes, Iran reportedly retains nuclear capabilities. Surviving infrastructure and stockpiles of enriched uranium continue to give Iran leverage in ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Hezbollah denies link to cell accused of planning Damascus attack
stories.summary: Hezbollah denied any connection to a cell accused of planning an attack in Damascus, stating it conducts no activity in Syria.

stories.title: Britain could adopt single market rules without MPs’ vote as part of UK-EU reset
stories.summary: British ministers are planning new legislation that could allow the UK to adopt EU single market rules without a full parliamentary vote. The move is part of Prime Minister Keir Starmer's push for closer ties with the European Union following the Iran war. The proposal for "dynamic alignment" is expected to face opposition from critics.

stories.title: Maliki sidelined after election of new Iraqi president
stories.summary: Former Iraqi Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki's prospects for winning the premiership have diminished following the election of a new Iraqi president. Deep divisions within the ruling Coordination Framework contributed to Maliki's sidelining.

stories.title: New Gaza aid flotilla sets sail from Spain, trying again to break Israeli blockade
stories.summary: A new Gaza-bound aid flotilla called the Global Sumud Flotilla departed from Barcelona, Spain, aiming to establish a humanitarian corridor to the Gaza Strip. Previous flotilla attempts have been intercepted by Israel.

stories.title: Iran - Enemies of the Straights: Former NATO General discusses US blockade threats
stories.summary: Former French Air Force General and ex-NATO Supreme Allied Commander Transformation Jean-Paul Palomeros discussed US threats to blockade the Strait of Hormuz. The analysis focused on the strategic and military implications of a potential American naval blockade targeting Iran.

stories.title: Police launch appeal after woman raped by several men outside Surrey church
stories.summary: Surrey Police launched an appeal after a woman in her 20s was raped by several men outside a church in Epsom after leaving the Labyrinth nightclub between 2am and 4am on Saturday.

stories.title: Iran: Trump vows US naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump vowed to impose a US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to "blow to hell" any Iranian who fires at US vessels in the waterway.

stories.title: Hungary election live: Polls in Hungary close in tightly fought election after 16 years under Viktor Orbán
stories.summary: Polls closed in Hungary's tightly contested election after 16 years of Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's rule. Opposition challenger Péter Magyar had been leading in polls in a race with potential implications for Europe, the US, and Russia.

stories.title: IDF says Hamas terrorists who abducted, held hostages were killed in Gaza strike
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it struck a Hamas cell in central Gaza that was planning an imminent attack on troops. The IDF stated the cell included operatives involved in abducting and holding hostages. Hamas authorities reported seven people killed in the strike.

stories.title: WATCH: In burned-out Be’eri homes, Magen 48 prepares local responders for future attacks
stories.summary: In the fire-damaged community of Be'eri, the organization Magen 48 is training local first responders to defend their communities until military reinforcements arrive, preparing for potential future attacks.

stories.title: How Iran's universities became a target of US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: On 6 April, an explosion struck Sharif University of Technology, one of Iran's leading engineering institutions, damaging multiple buildings including an artificial intelligence center. No casualties were reported. The university is widely regarded as a top engineering school in West Asia.

stories.title: Hamas to meet Egyptian mediators over alleged Gaza truce violations by Israel
stories.summary: Hamas is set to meet with Egyptian mediators to discuss alleged Israeli violations of the Gaza ceasefire. Violence has continued in the Palestinian territory despite the truce.

stories.title: Stampede at historical fort in Haiti kills at least 30, culture minister confirms
stories.summary: A stampede at the Citadelle Henri, a historic fortress in Haiti, killed at least 30 people on Saturday. Culture Minister Emmanuel Menard confirmed the deaths, noting that many of the victims were young visitors and that injured survivors were receiving medical care.

stories.title: Be’eri begins demolishing homes destroyed on October 7, choosing life over ruins
stories.summary: Kibbutz Be'eri, located near the Gaza border, began demolishing two neighborhoods destroyed during the October 7 attack. The community, which lost more than 100 residents, started with a home belonging to the Gat family as part of efforts to rebuild.

stories.title: Saudi summons Iraq envoy over drone threat claims
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia summoned Iraq's ambassador after accusing armed groups of launching drones from Iraqi territory toward the kingdom and other Gulf states. The Saudi foreign ministry called on Iraq to deal "responsibly" with the escalating threats.

stories.title: China offers incentives to Taiwan following opposition leader’s visit
stories.summary: Following a visit to China by Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, Beijing unveiled 10 new incentive measures for Taiwan including easing tourist restrictions and facilitating food sales. Cheng met Chinese President Xi Jinping and discussed peace and reconciliation.

stories.title: Syria begins to rehabilitate Conoco gas field near Deir ez Zor
stories.summary: Syria has begun rehabilitating the Conoco gas field near Deir ez-Zor, preparing the associated gas pipeline for a return to service. The work includes extensive demining and infrastructure repairs.

stories.title: China sets up new county in Xinjiang near PoK, Afghan border
stories.summary: China established a new county named Cenling in Xinjiang near the borders of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Afghanistan. It is the third new county created by Beijing in the predominantly Muslim Uyghur region in just over a year.

stories.title: US lawmakers split on party lines over negotiations’ failure to end Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers divided along party lines following the failure of US-Iran negotiations. Republicans, led by former UN ambassador Nikki Haley, called on President Trump to "finish the job," while leading Democrats warned against resuming hostilities.

stories.title: Trump declares US Navy to begin blockading Strait of Hormuz ‘effective immediately’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to begin blockading the Strait of Hormuz "effective immediately," directing it to stop all ships entering or leaving the waterway. Reports indicate approximately 60 percent of the IRGC navy's Hormuz patrol fleet remains intact.

stories.title: Nigerian airstrike targeting jihadists reportedly kills at least 100 civilians
stories.summary: A Nigerian air force strike targeting jihadist rebels in northeast Yobe state hit a market, killing over 100 people according to Amnesty International. Officials confirmed a misfire had occurred but provided no further details.

stories.title: Israeli Olympic medalist Peter Paltchik on failure, pain, comeback, ahead of Jerusalem Marathon
stories.summary: Israeli Olympic judo medalist Peter Paltchik discussed career setbacks, his Olympic journey, and the role of mental resilience ahead of the Jerusalem Marathon.

stories.title: Ceasefire? Israel’s Budget. Jewish Terrorism. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored discussion examines questions around the ongoing ceasefire, Israel's budget, and issues of extremist violence, asking who may have won the war and who is negotiating on Iran's behalf.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla aims to break Israeli blockade
stories.summary: A flotilla of approximately 30 boats plans to depart from Barcelona carrying medical aid and other supplies in an effort to break Israel's blockade of Gaza.

stories.title: Iran’s ex-foreign minister blames talks’ failure on US push to ‘dictate’ terms
stories.summary: Iran's former foreign minister attributed the failure of US-Iran talks to Washington's attempt to dictate terms, arguing that no negotiations with Iran can succeed on such a basis.

stories.title: Why does Judaism have denominations? with Zev Eleff - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored discussion with Zev Eleff explores the origins and meanings of Judaism's various denominations, including Orthodox, Conservative, Reform, and Reconstructionist traditions.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF kills Hezbollah terrorists responsible for fallen soldier in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced it killed two Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon who were responsible for the death of an Israeli soldier. One was killed during an initial firefight on Tuesday and the second in a follow-up operation.

stories.title: In pictures: VP Vance gets cordial send-off as Islamabad Talks conclude
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran direct talks in Islamabad concluded without an agreement after extended negotiations. U.S. Vice President JD Vance held a press conference acknowledging "substantive discussions" before both delegations departed Pakistan.

stories.title: Hezbollah denies link to cell accused of Damascus attack plan
stories.summary: Hezbollah denied any connection to a cell accused by Syrian authorities of planning an attack in Damascus. The group called the accusations "false and fabricated" and urged Syria to conduct a thorough investigation.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 55 attacks since start of day, most in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 55 attacks on Ukrainian defense positions since the start of the day, with the heaviest activity concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors of the front line in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Woman, 19, killed in Essex dog attack named as Jamie-Lea Biscoe
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman named Jamie-Lea Biscoe was killed in a dog attack at a property in Leaden Roding, Essex. A 37-year-old man from Dunmow was arrested on suspicion of being in charge of a dangerously out-of-control dog and has been bailed until July.

stories.title: Revisiting Osirak: the airstrike that shocked the world - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored segment revisits Operation Opera, Israel's 1981 airstrike on Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor, examining the historical questions the operation raises in the context of current events.

stories.title: Iran war has cost Israel $11.5 billion in budgetary expenses, Finance Ministry says
stories.summary: Israel's Finance Ministry reported that the war with Iran has cost the country approximately $11.5 billion in budgetary expenses. Iran has estimated its own war losses at $145 billion, while U.S. expenditure estimates are roughly comparable to Israel's.

stories.title: The battle over the word ‘Zionism’ - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored discussion examines the contested meaning and significance of the word "Zionism," exploring its historical weight, burden, and connection to Jewish identity.

stories.title: Erdogan threatens military action against Israel, MK calls him a 'megalomaniacal dictator'
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan warned that Turkey could take military action against Israel if necessary, drawing comparisons to past Turkish interventions in Nagorno-Karabakh and Libya. An Israeli Knesset member responded by calling Erdogan a "megalomaniacal dictator."

stories.title: Israeli forces raid West Bank cities as Ben-Gvir storms al-Aqsa
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted raids across multiple West Bank cities, injuring and detaining several people. The operations coincided with far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir storming the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Iranian authorities remain defiant, urge supporters to stay in streets
stories.summary: Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led Iran's delegation at peace talks, stated that the US delegation failed to gain Iran's trust. Ghalibaf's remarks came as Iranian authorities urged their supporters to remain in the streets.

stories.title: Did Iran lose the war? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored analysis examines whether Iran lost the war, noting that US and Israeli strikes inflicted serious damage on Iran's military and nuclear infrastructure while questioning whether the impact was sufficient to produce lasting regional change.

stories.title: Cuba’s president warns US against attacking island or trying to depose him
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned the United States against any military attack on Cuba or attempts to depose him, saying in an NBC interview that an invasion would be costly and destabilizing for regional security.

stories.title: What is really happening with Zionism among Jews today? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored segment features Mimi Kravetz of the Jewish Federations of North America discussing recent JFNA poll data that indicates a surge in Zionist identification among Jews today.

stories.title: IDF says it raided hospital used by Hezbollah in terror group’s Bint Jbeil stronghold
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it raided a hospital in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, that was allegedly being used by Hezbollah. The IDF reported fierce clashes as troops advanced into the town and said soldiers killed a Hezbollah fighter responsible for killing an Israeli soldier the previous week.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia executes seven people in a day for drug trafficking
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia executed seven people in a single day for drug trafficking offenses. The individuals executed included five Saudi citizens and two Jordanian nationals.

stories.title: Seven ways America can win the ceasefire and end the war
stories.summary: An analysis argues that US President Donald Trump needs to take decisive steps to secure regional peace, framing the effort partly as a strategic move ahead of upcoming midterm elections.

stories.title: Iran leaders say 'couldn't trust US' at failed Islamabad talks
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the US failed to earn Iran's trust during negotiations held in Islamabad. The talks ended without an agreement between the two sides.

stories.title: Trump says US will begin 'blockading' the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that the US Navy would immediately begin blockading the Strait of Hormuz, preventing ships from entering or leaving. He also stated that the US would interdict any vessel in international waters that had paid a toll to Iran for passage through the critical waterway.

stories.title: Video: Severe flooding closes schools in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Saudi Arabian authorities ordered schools to close after severe flooding struck parts of the country. Video footage showed the extent of the flooding that prompted the closures.

stories.title: Israel’s Ben Gvir says he feels like the 'owner' of Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
stories.summary: Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem and said he feels like its "owner." The visit came days after the site was reopened to Palestinian worshippers following weeks of closure.

stories.title: Economic shock of Mideast war to cast shadow over IMF meeting
stories.summary: The IMF and World Bank announced plans to raise their global inflation forecasts due to the economic impact of the war in the Middle East. The revised projections were expected to feature prominently in upcoming institutional meetings.

stories.title: Irish police clear fuel protesters from central Dublin after days of gridlock
stories.summary: Irish police cleared fuel protesters from central Dublin after days of gridlock. Ireland has experienced a 20 percent rise in diesel prices since the US-Israeli war on Iran began.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson says Iran war Trump's 'single biggest mistake' in BBC interview
stories.summary: Conservative commentator Tucker Carlson called the Iran war President Trump's "single biggest mistake" in a BBC interview. Carlson had previously described Trump's remarks about opening the Strait of Hormuz as "evil" on his podcast.

stories.title: Putin Says Ready to Help Peace Efforts in Call With Iran President
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with Iran's president, expressing readiness to assist peace efforts. Separately, U.S.-Iran talks failed to produce a deal to end the Middle East conflict, though no immediate return to hostilities followed.

stories.title: At least two members of Quetta’s Hazara community killed in firing incident
stories.summary: At least two members of Quetta's Hazara community were killed and three others injured when unidentified gunmen on motorcycles opened fire on their vehicle. Police in Pakistan's Balochistan province described the incident as a targeted killing near the Hazarganji vegetable market.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia trade Easter truce breach barbs
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia accused each other of violating an Orthodox Easter truce thousands of times, with both sides trading allegations of widespread breaches.

stories.title: Center for Study of Occupation: Russians moving military equipment en masse from Berdiansk area to northern Donetsk region
stories.summary: The Center for Study of Occupation reported that Russian forces are relocating large quantities of military equipment from the Berdiansk area to the northern part of Donetsk region. The movement suggests a potential redeployment of assets along the front line.

stories.title: IRGC threatens to trap 'enemies' in 'deadly vortex' in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded to US President Trump's announced naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, warning that enemies would become "trapped in a deadly vortex" if they made a wrong move. The IRGC said all traffic in the strait is under full control of Iran's armed forces.

stories.title: Iran believes they hold the cards amid 'dysfunction & chaos in US national security decision-making'
stories.summary: Former State Department Middle East negotiator Aaron David Miller, now a Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, assessed that Iran perceives an advantage amid what he describes as dysfunction in US national security decision-making. He characterized the ongoing negotiations involving Iran, Israel, and Lebanon as driven by tactical necessity rather than a coherent diplomatic strategy.

stories.title: Trump threatens China with 'staggering' tariffs if it helps Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened China with a 50 percent tariff if it provides military assistance to Iran. In a Fox News interview, Trump also warned against allowing Iran to profit from oil sales and said he could target Iran's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Votes for populist parties in May elections will put NHS at risk, Streeting says
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting warned that voting for populist parties in May's local and devolved elections could endanger the NHS, calling the founding principles of the health service more threatened than at any time since 1948.

stories.title: Interest in EVs surges in Europe as fuel prices jump after Iran war
stories.summary: Interest in electric vehicles has surged across European markets including the UK, Germany, France, and Spain since the start of the Iran war, driven by rising fuel prices. Online marketplaces reported large increases in EV inquiries.

stories.title: US-Iran talks: What prevented a deal and what's next?
stories.summary: The United States and Iran concluded 21 hours of direct talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, without reaching a deal to end the war. The outcome casts uncertainty over a fragile two-week ceasefire between the two sides.

stories.title: Mixed signals from Washington cloud intentions for future of Iran war, experts tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Experts told the Jerusalem Post that mixed signals from Washington are obscuring U.S. intentions regarding the Iran conflict. Former U.S. Ambassador to Oman Marc Seivers suggested that neither diplomatic talks nor the ceasefire indicate an American withdrawal from the war.

stories.title: At least 200 killed in airstrikes in northeast Nigeria
stories.summary: Military airstrikes in Nigeria's northeastern Yobe state killed at least 200 people as air force jets targeted Boko Haram jihadists. Local residents and Amnesty International reported the civilian casualties.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia restores full capacity on East-West oil pipeline to 7 million bpd after attacks
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia restored full capacity on its East-West oil pipeline to 7 million barrels per day following earlier attacks. The pipeline has served as Saudi Arabia's only route for crude exports.

stories.title: ‘There is no rule of law’: High Court justices rail at failure to enlist Haredim
stories.summary: Israel's High Court of Justice rebuked the government and police for failing to enforce the drafting of ultra-Orthodox men into the military. Justices accused the government of deliberately delaying action to buy time before reinstating broad exemptions from military service.

stories.title: Trump announces Strait of Hormuz blockade after US-Iran peace talks end
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, directing the US Navy to enforce it. The declaration followed the conclusion of US-Iran peace talks in Pakistan, which ended without a deal.

stories.title: US arrests Iranian family tied to 1979 Iran hostage crisis at US embassy
stories.summary: U.S. authorities arrested Seyed Eissa Hashemi, the son of Masoumeh Ebtekar, who served as spokeswoman for the Islamist militants who seized the U.S. Embassy in Tehran during the 1979 hostage crisis.

stories.title: Lubinets to appeal to UN and Red Cross over shooting of Ukrainians during ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukraine's parliamentary human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets announced he will appeal to the United Nations and the International Committee of the Red Cross. The appeal concerns the reported execution of four Ukrainian prisoners of war and an evacuation team during the Easter truce.

stories.title: Justice Ministry says legal aid opened nearly 2,500 cases for Holocaust survivors over past year
stories.summary: Israel's Justice Ministry reported that its legal aid services opened nearly 2,500 cases for Holocaust survivors over the past year. About 1,500 cases involved stipends and grants, while roughly 1,000 dealt with civil legal matters.

stories.title: Global Sumud Flotilla sets sail from Barcelona for Gaza
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla, described as the largest ever, departed from Barcelona's port bound for Gaza. Thousands of people gathered at the port to see the flotilla off.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla backed by Greenpeace falters on departure date due to storm
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla's 39 vessels departing from Moll de la Fusta Port in Barcelona were forced to delay their direct route to Gaza due to storm conditions, instead diverting to another port. The flotilla is backed by Greenpeace.

stories.title: FIFA rejects Iran’s request to relocate World Cup games amid US-Israel war
stories.summary: FIFA rejected Iran's request to relocate its World Cup matches away from the United States despite repeated appeals. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed the decision, stating FIFA would not move Iran's fixtures.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV urges immediate ceasefire as Israel-Hezbollah clashes rage
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV called for an immediate ceasefire as clashes between Israel and Hezbollah continue, urging all parties to respect international law and protect civilians.

stories.title: Trump says US to blockade ships crossing Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared that the US Navy would immediately blockade the Strait of Hormuz, stopping ships from crossing the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Drone tech's impact on warfare: From tactical drones to high-precision missiles
stories.summary: Defense technology expert Menachem Landau discussed the growing role of drones and precision missiles in modern warfare, highlighting U.S.-Israeli collaboration in reshaping military strategies.

stories.title: Texas Congressman presents bill to designate CAIR a terror org., revoke NGO status, over Hamas ties
stories.summary: Texas Congressman Chip Roy introduced a bill to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) a terrorist organization and revoke its NGO status, citing CAIR's listing as an unindicted co-conspirator in the 2007 Holy Land Foundation terrorism financing trial.

stories.title: US Navy to blockade Strait of Hormuz ‘effective immediately,’ Trump says
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that the US Navy would blockade the Strait of Hormuz effective immediately. In a social media post, Trump warned that any Iranian forces firing on US assets or civilian vessels would face decisive military retaliation.

stories.title: Live: Polls close in crucial Hungary election, turnout reaches record high
stories.summary: Hungary held elections on Sunday with record-high voter turnout, posing the biggest electoral challenge yet to Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. His main rival, centre-right candidate Peter Magyar, sought to unseat the long-serving leader. Orbán campaigned aggressively, warning that his defeat could draw Hungary into the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defense goes private: businesses can now buy point coverage for their own sites
stories.summary: Ukraine has introduced a policy allowing private businesses to purchase and operate their own air-defense systems to protect specific sites. A fragment of a privately developed system is already operational amid continued Russian strikes on infrastructure.

stories.title: Over 3.5 million square meters of roads repaired in Ukraine this year
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities reported that 3.5 million square meters of road surface on national highways were repaired in 2026. The effort reflects ongoing infrastructure maintenance despite the continuing conflict.

stories.title: Iran says time for US to decide ‘whether it can earn our trust’ after talks
stories.summary: Following inconclusive US-Iran talks in Islamabad, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said it is now time for the United States to decide whether it can earn Tehran's trust. Ghalibaf led the Iranian delegation and cited past conflicts as reasons for Iran's distrust.

stories.title: Trump says points agreed to in talks 'don't matter' due to Iran's 'nuclear ambitions'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that points agreed upon in U.S.-Iran talks "don't matter" because of Iran's nuclear ambitions, vowing that Iran will never obtain a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: ‘This likely isn’t over’: Journalists, analysts react to ‘stalemate’ in US-Iran talks
stories.summary: After 21 hours of talks in Islamabad, US and Iranian delegations departed without reaching an agreement. US Vice President JD Vance acknowledged the failure, while both sides had been observing a two-week ceasefire brokered with Pakistan's diplomatic involvement.

stories.title: US appeals court rules Mahmoud Khalil deportation case can continue
stories.summary: A U.S. appeals court ruled that the deportation case against Mahmoud Khalil may proceed. Separately, the Trump administration reportedly dismissed two immigration judges who had blocked the deportation of two pro-Palestine international students.

stories.title: Gaza war: Sumud flotilla aims to again break Israeli blockade
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla is preparing to send approximately 30 boats carrying humanitarian supplies from Barcelona toward Gaza in another attempt to break Israel's naval blockade of the territory.

stories.title: Noga Erez tells Coachella she’s ‘heartbroken’ about situation at home
stories.summary: Israeli indie musician Noga Erez, the first Israeli artist to perform at the Coachella music festival in California, told the audience she was "heartbroken" about the ongoing war situation at home.

stories.title: Several cities nix Independence Day parties due to shaky Iran truce, Hezbollah war
stories.summary: Several Israeli cities canceled large-scale Independence Day celebrations due to the fragile ceasefire with Iran and the ongoing war with Hezbollah. Local officials recommended holding smaller ceremonies, with one mayor saying celebrating as usual would be detached from reality.

stories.title: Hamas to meet Egyptian mediators over Israeli truce violations
stories.summary: A Hamas delegation is set to meet Egyptian mediators to discuss outstanding provisions of the first phase of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, as well as Israel's continued near-daily attacks on the territory.

stories.title: At least 30 dead in stampede at Haiti’s historic Citadelle Laferriere
stories.summary: At least 30 people died in a stampede at Haiti's Citadelle Laferrière, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Authorities said the fortress was packed with visitors ahead of an annual celebration.

stories.title: Trump floats naval blockade of Iran, Islamabad talks fail
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post's news roundup covered President Trump's proposal for a naval blockade of Iran and the failure of U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks held in Islamabad.

stories.title: Trump says US military is 'locked and loaded' to 'finish up' Iran
stories.summary: President Trump declared on Truth Social that the U.S. military is "locked and loaded" to "finish up" Iran and announced plans to blockade all ships entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump orders blockade of Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced via social media on Sunday that the US Navy would begin an immediate blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, barring ships from entering or leaving. He further ordered the interdiction of any vessel in international waters that had paid transit tolls to Iran.

stories.title: Seven new towers equipped with Pantsir systems built around Putin's residence in Valday
stories.summary: In March 2026, seven new towers equipped with Pantsir air defense systems were constructed around Russian President Vladimir Putin's residence in Valday. The installations bolster the site's aerial defenses.

stories.title: Ex-CIA director calls for ousting Trump: ‘25th amendment was written with him in mind’
stories.summary: Former CIA Director John Brennan called for President Trump's removal under the 25th Amendment, describing Trump as "clearly unhinged" after his volatile remarks about destroying Iranian civilization during the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Easter prayer fiasco, resolved too late, shows Christians still treated as afterthought
stories.summary: A dispute over Christian access to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem during Easter was resolved only after the controversy had already caused harm. Prime Minister Netanyahu subsequently claimed credit for protecting worshippers at the site.

stories.title: Bennett's 'repair team' reveals the lesson he learned from Lapid, his own scars - analysis
stories.summary: A recent Lazar Research poll showed former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's party at 24 seats, one behind Likud's 25, with the opposition bloc holding a projected 61-seat majority in the Knesset.

stories.title: Hong Kong, mainland China sign ‘milestone’ MOU on promoting digital economy
stories.summary: Hong Kong and mainland China signed a memorandum of understanding to promote the digital economy, covering areas including artificial intelligence and cross-boundary data flows. The MOU was signed by Hong Kong's innovation secretary and a deputy director of the Cyberspace Administration of China.

stories.title: 'Undeterred’: Hungarian investigative journalist faces threats and espionage accusations from Orbán
stories.summary: Budapest-based investigative journalist Szabolcs Panyi, who works for VSquare and Direkt36, reported on alleged ties between Hungary's political leadership and Russian state actors. In response, Prime Minister Viktor Orbán publicly accused Panyi of espionage. Panyi contends that Orbán uses false conspiracy narratives to discredit independent journalism.

stories.title: Trump says US will 'blockade all ships entering or leaving Hormuz'
stories.summary: President Trump announced that U.S. forces would begin blockading all vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, and instructed the Navy to interdict ships that have paid tolls to Iran.

stories.title: Sweden detains dry cargo ship en route from Russia
stories.summary: Sweden detained the Panamanian-flagged bulk carrier Hui Yuan on April 12 on suspicion of violating environmental laws. The Swedish coast guard's aircraft reportedly recorded the vessel dumping coal residues into the sea while en route from Russia.

stories.title: 13 killed in Lebanon as Israel threatens more attacks
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed five people in the town of Qana, bringing the total Lebanese death toll to 2,020. Prime Minister Netanyahu vowed further strikes despite ongoing peace negotiations.

stories.title: Police clear Irish fuel protesters from several locations
stories.summary: Irish police cleared fuel protesters from several locations across the country. The Irish cabinet is scheduled to meet on Sunday to receive an update on ongoing talks aimed at resolving the fuel crisis.

stories.title: Anthony Albanese urges Israel to stop Lebanon attacks that intensified during Middle East ceasefire
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese urged Israel to halt its attacks on Lebanon, expressing concern over intensified military operations targeting Beirut and southern Lebanon. He also called on Hezbollah to cease reprisals and confirmed Australia's military surveillance aircraft would remain deployed in the region.

stories.title: How a Chinese company said it used AI to track US bomber movements over Iran
stories.summary: Chinese geospatial intelligence firm MizarVision published a report claiming to use AI analysis to track U.S. KC-135 and KC-46 aerial refueling tanker movements during Operation Epic Fury over Iran. The firm said it identified links between tanker activity and strike patterns against Iranian targets.

stories.title: Post-Orban Hungary would not expose Israel to more EU pain, though support may ebb
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that a potential post-Orbán Hungarian government led by a center-right rival would be unlikely to significantly increase EU pressure on Israel, though Budapest's level of diplomatic support for Jerusalem may gradually decline.

stories.title: Hacking women's political underrepresentation, Dutch-style
stories.summary: In recent Dutch local elections, 504 women won seats, aided by a "Vote for a Woman" campaign that boosted preferential votes. Despite the record number, women remain underrepresented in Dutch local politics.

stories.title: Control of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran’s uranium stockpiles were sticking points
stories.summary: The meeting between U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance and Iranian counterpart Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Pakistan represented the highest-level direct engagement between the two countries since 1979. Control of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's uranium stockpiles were identified as key sticking points in the negotiations.

stories.title: China announces partial resumption of ties with Taiwan
stories.summary: China announced the partial resumption of previously suspended ties with Taiwan, including direct flights to mainland Chinese cities and the import of Taiwanese aquaculture products.

stories.title: Planeloads of negotiators and too little time: US and Iran’s 21 hours of talks
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations held 21 hours of talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, but failed to reach a deal on Iran's nuclear program and related disputes. Both sides flew in large teams of negotiators, though the compressed timeframe limited prospects for resolving the decades-long standoff, now complicated by the Strait of Hormuz crisis and compensation demands.

stories.title: One dead and several injured after mass shooting at Chick-fil-A in New Jersey
stories.summary: At least six people were shot, one fatally, at a Chick-fil-A restaurant on Route 22 in Union Township, New Jersey, on Saturday night. The Gun Violence Archive listed the incident as the 100th mass shooting documented in the US this year. No suspect or motive details have been released.

stories.title: Irish police clear Dublin blockade staged by fuel price protesters
stories.summary: Irish police cleared a blockade of Dublin's O'Connell Street staged by farmers and hauliers protesting fuel prices. Mounted units and hundreds of officers peacefully removed trucks and tractors on Sunday, potentially ending six days of demonstrations that disrupted the capital.

stories.title: Gulf states on edge as US-Iran talks in Islamabad end without deal - analysis
stories.summary: Gulf states are growing uneasy after U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without an agreement. Analysts note the Gulf feels some of its concerns are being addressed and that many regional actors want negotiations to continue.
