stories.title: Two supertankers U-Turn in Hormuz as US-Iran talks break down
stories.summary: Two supertankers made U-turns in the Strait of Hormuz as U.S.-Iran talks broke down. The specific reasons behind the vessels' abrupt course changes have not been confirmed.

stories.title: Pakistan gambles on Iran-US talks and comes up short - analysis
stories.summary: Analysts say Pakistan's decision to host the U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad reflected its ambition to assume greater regional diplomatic responsibility, though the negotiations ultimately ended without an agreement.

stories.title: Palestinians condemn storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by Israel’s Ben-Gvir
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in occupied Jerusalem under security protection. Palestinian leaders condemned the visit as a provocation.

stories.title: Israeli bombardment kills infant in Lebanon during father’s funeral
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the village of Srifa in south Lebanon killed an infant and other relatives of seven-year-old Aline Saeed during her father's funeral. The strike occurred on the first day of a U.S.-Iran ceasefire that many in Lebanon had hoped would extend to their country.

stories.title: How Iran's universities became a target of US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Approximately 30 Iranian universities were struck during U.S.-Israeli military operations. Iranian academics and students described the attacks as an effort to undermine Iran's sovereignty and technological autonomy. Iran's science minister inspected damage at Shahid Beheshti University in Tehran.

stories.title: Post-war recalibration: Why Israel must rethink Syria approach - analysis
stories.summary: Analysts argue Israel should reassess its approach to Syria, noting that since December 8, 2024, Syrians have demonstrated a desire to rebuild their country and pursue peace, despite ongoing challenges.

stories.title: Putin says he is ready to help mediate peace efforts
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian by phone that he is prepared to help mediate a political and diplomatic settlement to achieve lasting peace in the Middle East.

stories.title: Ahead of Holocaust Remembrance Day, 111,000 survivors living in Israel
stories.summary: Ahead of Holocaust Remembrance Day, Israel's Central Bureau of Statistics reported that 111,000 Holocaust survivors live in Israel. Over a quarter are older than 90, and two-thirds are women. The global Jewish population has not yet recovered to its 1933 level.

stories.title: Impunity by design: How the IDF, settlers repress Palestinians in the West Bank - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the Israeli military regime in the occupied West Bank systematically enables settler violence and soldier abuses against Palestinians through a structure of institutional impunity.

stories.title: Trump escalates Gulf crisis with order for total blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered the Navy to immediately begin a total blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, blocking all maritime traffic entering or leaving the waterway. He also directed the interception of any vessel that has paid a toll to Iran.

stories.title: Reservist soldier fatally shoots Palestinian amid alleged rock-throwing near Ramallah
stories.summary: An Israeli reservist soldier fatally shot a Palestinian near Ramallah during an alleged rock-throwing incident. Separately, settlers were filmed stealing sheep and using pepper spray against Palestinians in the South Hebron Hills, and Duma's mayor accused settlers of throwing a Molotov cocktail into a children's bedroom.

stories.title: US-Iran peace talks end without deal as delegations leave Pakistan
stories.summary: US-Iran peace talks ended without an agreement after 21 hours of negotiations in Pakistan, with both delegations departing Islamabad. Each side blamed the other for the failure to resolve a conflict that has killed thousands and disrupted the global economy.

stories.title: Talks ended without deal due to 'excessive demands' made by U.S.: Iran
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei attributed the failure of US-Iran talks to excessive American demands. He affirmed that Iran remains committed to using all tools, including diplomacy, to protect its national interests.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Zolochiv in Kharkiv region; two people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the village of Zolochiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region on the morning of April 12. Two people were injured in the attack.

stories.title: ‘Pakistan opened door to dialogue’: Islamabad becoming a direct mediator, say US scholars
stories.summary: American scholars have highlighted Pakistan's growing diplomatic role following the intensive US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad. US Vice President JD Vance praised Pakistan's efforts despite the talks ending without an agreement.

stories.title: At least 30 dead in stampede at Haiti’s historic Laferriere Citadel
stories.summary: At least 30 people were killed in a stampede at Haiti's historic Laferrière Citadel in the country's northern countryside on Saturday, April 12. Authorities warned the death toll could rise.

stories.title: Israel 'reprimands' Spain over blowing up of Netanyahu effigy
stories.summary: Israel formally reprimanded Spain after an effigy of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was set on fire in the Spanish town of El Burgo. Netanyahu is wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes in Gaza.

stories.title: 🔴 Middle East war live: Trump says US will begin 'blockading' Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the US would begin blockading the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route. The move comes amid the ongoing US-Iran crisis.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims attack on Israeli military vehicle in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it launched a drone attack on an Israeli military vehicle carrying a command crew in Taybeh in the occupied West Bank. The group also said it fired multiple drones at the Kiryat Shmona barracks in northern Israel.

stories.title: First-ever life-size Vivekananda statue in U.S. unveiled in Seattle
stories.summary: A life-size statue of Swami Vivekananda was unveiled in Seattle, marking the first such statue in the United States. The event coincided with ICCR Day celebrations and is part of India's cultural diplomacy efforts.

stories.title: Man charged with murder of Finbar Sullivan in Primrose Hill
stories.summary: Oliuwadamilola Ogunyankinnu, 27, was charged with the murder of 21-year-old Finbar Sullivan, who was fatally stabbed in Primrose Hill, north London, on April 7. The suspect is scheduled to appear in court on Monday.

stories.title: Lessons from the Iran war
stories.summary: Analysis of the recent conflict involving Iran highlights shifts in modern warfare over the preceding six weeks, suggesting the nature of military engagement is evolving significantly.

stories.title: ‘Blown to hell’: Trump announces US blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a sweeping naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical oil transit chokepoints. The order directs the U.S. Navy to block all ships attempting to enter or leave the strait, risking a deepening global crisis.

stories.title: Collapse of US-Iran talks heightens fears of prolonged energy shock
stories.summary: The collapse of US-Iran peace talks has raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to global energy markets. Oil tankers remain stranded in the Gulf, and analysts expect oil prices and borrowing costs to rise as the standoff continues.

stories.title: Trump was watching a UFC fight in Miami while Iran talks collapsed
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump was attending a UFC fight in Miami at the time the U.S.-Iran negotiations in Islamabad collapsed. It was unclear whether the president had been informed of the talks' failure before he entered the arena.

stories.title: Atesh partisans hit Russia’s shrinking locomotive fleet – one engine at a time
stories.summary: The Atesh partisan network claims to have targeted locomotives belonging to Russian Railways. Atesh says a shortage of operational locomotives within the Russian rail system makes each destroyed engine increasingly difficult to replace.

stories.title: Yaakov Levitan Was Preparing a Hanukkah Celebration. Then the Attack Began. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Yaakov Levitan, a father of four and prominent member of Sydney's Jewish community, was among 15 people killed in a terror attack during a Hanukkah celebration. He was remembered at a Yom Hazikaron ceremony organized by Masa.

stories.title: US, Iran fail to agree on peace deal
stories.summary: Iran's Parliamentary Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran presented forward-looking proposals during talks in Islamabad but that the US failed to earn the Iranian delegation's trust. US Vice President JD Vance confirmed that 21 hours of negotiations ended without a peace deal.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia accuse each other of breaching Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged accusations of violating an Easter ceasefire. The Kremlin stated Russia would not extend the truce unless Kyiv accepted Moscow's conditions.

stories.title: Stalemate diplomacy: US-Iran talks fail as both sides resist major concessions - analysis
stories.summary: US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended in stalemate as both sides refused major concessions. Iran sought an end to the Lebanon war before engaging on other issues, while the US prioritized reopening the Strait of Hormuz to focus negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme.

stories.title: After Iran talks falter, the big question is 'what happens next?'
stories.summary: Negotiations between Iran and the United States in their latest round of talks failed to produce a breakthrough after 21 hours of discussion, leaving 47 years of mutual hostility unresolved.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire talks: What are the key sticking points?
stories.summary: Talks between the United States and Iran revealed deep disagreements during a two-week ceasefire, with key sticking points prolonging uncertainty about a lasting agreement.

stories.title: Ten police officers wounded in drone attack on Novooleksandrivka in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Novooleksandrivka in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region wounded ten police officers and one civilian.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda at 32 - Memory, Unity, and the Power of Intentional Leadership
stories.summary: Rwanda began its annual commemoration of the 1994 genocide on April 7, marking 32 years since the tragedy that claimed more than 800,000 lives in 100 days.

stories.title: Sudanese refugees in CAR: humanitarian situation is disastrous
stories.summary: The humanitarian situation for Sudanese refugees in the Central African Republic remains dire despite declining international attention. Approximately 2.3 million people — 35 percent of the CAR's population — live in extreme vulnerability.

stories.title: Netanyahu says war with Iran 'not over yet', attacks Erdogan
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that the war with Iran is "not over yet" and claimed "historic achievements" in the conflict. He also publicly attacked Turkish President Erdogan in a social media post.

stories.title: Nine foreign airlines plan to resume Tel Aviv routes this week, amid US-Iran truce
stories.summary: Nine foreign airlines, including Etihad, Ethiopian, and Hainan, plan to resume flights to and from Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv during the U.S.-Iran truce, according to Israel's airport authority.

stories.title: PM calls petitions for Ben Gvir’s ouster ‘unconstitutional,’ as minister prays on Temple Mt.
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu called legal petitions seeking National Security Minister Ben Gvir's removal "unconstitutional" ahead of a High Court hearing. Ben Gvir again visited the Temple Mount/Al-Aqsa compound, breaching the site's status quo arrangements.

stories.title: Iranian officials say 3,375 killed in US-Israel attacks
stories.summary: Iran's Forensic Medicine Organisation reported that 3,375 people have been identified as killed in U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran, including 2,875 men and nearly 500 women.

stories.title: Donald Trump and Marco Rubio watch UFC fights in Miami as peace talks with Iran fail
stories.summary: President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio attended a UFC event at the Kaseya Center in Miami on Saturday night, as US-Iran peace talks were failing in Islamabad. Family members including Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr. were also present alongside UFC chief Dana White.

stories.title: Why China is looking to Central Asia as Middle East grows riskier
stories.summary: The ongoing war in Iran is reshaping global energy flows and forcing reassessments of supply chain vulnerabilities, particularly for China. Beijing is increasingly looking to Central Asia as an alternative energy source as the Strait of Hormuz faces sustained disruption risks.

stories.title: China says it will resume some ties with Taiwan including more direct flights
stories.summary: China's Taiwan Work Office announced plans to resume some cross-strait ties, including exploring a communication mechanism between the Communist Party and Taiwan's Kuomintang Party and facilitating imports of Taiwanese aquaculture products that had been previously banned.

stories.title: Progress hailed as Hong Kong, Shanghai link digital authentication systems
stories.summary: Hong Kong and Shanghai linked their digital authentication systems during the first annual meeting of the Working Group on Shanghai and Hong Kong Digital Cooperation. Five mainland Chinese enterprises also established operations in Hong Kong as part of the deepening partnership.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia restores full pumping capacity to East-West pipeline
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia announced it has restored full pumping capacity to its East-West pipeline, returning output to 7 million barrels per day.

stories.title: Arrest made over 2019 shooting death of 18-year-old whose body was found in pit
stories.summary: Israeli police made an arrest in connection with the 2019 shooting death of 18-year-old Eviatar Azarzar from Bnei Brak. His body was found in a pit in Ramat Hasharon after a three-week search. More suspects are expected to be detained.

stories.title: AI on the battlefield
stories.summary: The article examines the use of artificial intelligence in warfare, drawing parallels to US drone "signature strikes" in Pakistan's Waziristan region during the Obama administration, which used early AI-assisted surveillance to identify targets.

stories.title: Ireland police remove farmers, blockades protesting fuel price rises
stories.summary: Irish police dismantled a blockade on Dublin's O'Connell Street set up by fuel protesters who had disrupted much of Ireland for six days. Clashes also occurred in Galway as the government prepared to approve cost-cutting measures aimed at ending the crisis over soaring fuel prices.

stories.title: 2,000 violations in 15 hours: what Russia’s Easter truce looked like from the front
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff documented approximately 2,000 ceasefire violations by Russian forces within 15 hours, before Easter Sunday had officially begun. The data underscores the scale of breaches during Russia's self-declared unilateral Easter truce.

stories.title: A ceasefire won't stop Iran's military industry-analysis
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that a potential ceasefire with Iran would not halt its military industry. Periods of reduced conflict could allow Iran to clandestinely reorganize, restock, and expand its weapons procurement capabilities.

stories.title: Iranians rally outside US embassies worldwide, urge continued pressure on Tehran
stories.summary: Iranian expatriates rallied outside US embassies in multiple countries, urging Washington not to reach agreements with Tehran. Protesters called on American policymakers to maintain pressure on the Iranian government.

stories.title: Who is running US foreign policy? Varsha Gandikota and Jeremy Scahill
stories.summary: Journalist Jeremy Scahill and analyst Varsha Gandikota-Nellutla discussed who shapes U.S. foreign policy and who stands to benefit from the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Saudi says pipeline, energy facilities restored after attacks
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia announced that the East-West pipeline and energy facilities damaged during Iranian attacks have been repaired and restored to full operational capacity.

stories.title: Vance leaves Pakistan after Iran talks fail to reach a deal
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance departed Pakistan after US-Iran talks in Islamabad failed to produce a deal. Key unresolved issues included Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz, though Iranian media suggested talks may continue.

stories.title: Blue city, red state battle: Kansas City feuds over ‘colonial’ police system
stories.summary: Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas described the city's police governance structure as a "colonial system," criticizing it as anti-Black and anti-immigrant. Kansas City, a Democratic-led city in Republican-controlled Kansas, does not have local control over its police force, and reform efforts have been blocked by state Republicans.

stories.title: ‘I didn’t want to be on medication the rest of my life’: veteran runs psilocybin retreats for PTSD before FDA approval
stories.summary: Army ranger veteran Jesse Gould, who developed PTSD after three combat deployments in Afghanistan, now runs psilocybin retreats for fellow veterans. Researchers say psilocybin may help treat traumatic symptoms, but urge caution as several US states expand access ahead of potential FDA approval.

stories.title: Trump faces a dilemma in the aftermath of failed US-Iran peace talks: Chinese analysts
stories.summary: Chinese analysts say the failure of U.S.-Iran peace talks in Islamabad leaves President Trump facing a dilemma over whether to resume military strikes. The Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program were central issues during the 21 hours of negotiations.

stories.title: US-Iran talks failed over Hormuz, Lebanon and nuclear programme
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran negotiations held in Islamabad collapsed over disagreements regarding Lebanon, the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran's nuclear program. U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Iran had rejected what he called a "final" offer.

stories.title: Celin Dion to perform 16 concerts in Paris
stories.summary: Singer Celine Dion will perform 16 concerts in Paris beginning in September, marking her return to live performance after a lengthy break caused by a rare health condition. The concert series is expected to generate hundreds of millions of euros for the French capital, and authorities have warned fans about potential ticket scams.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia accuse each other of hundreds of ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia have accused each other of hundreds of ceasefire violations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukrainian forces would respond "symmetrically" to any Russian attacks.

stories.title: Israeli army raids across the occupied West Bank overnight
stories.summary: The Israeli military conducted overnight raids across multiple locations in the occupied West Bank. No further details on casualties or arrests were immediately provided.

stories.title: Indian music legend Asha Bhosle dies aged 92
stories.summary: Indian playback singer Asha Bhosle, one of Bollywood's most celebrated voices, has died at age 92 in Mumbai. The two-time Grammy nominee had been hospitalized with extreme exhaustion and a chest infection. Her career defined Bollywood music through the 1970s and 1980s.

stories.title: Iran states that agreement with U.S. not reached due to “two or three" key issues
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said disagreements over "two or three" key issues prevented the US and Iran from concluding an agreement during talks held in Islamabad, Pakistan.

stories.title: 380 Wang Fuk Court households seek second visit to collect belongings
stories.summary: About 380 households from Hong Kong's fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court housing estate in Tai Po have requested a second visit to retrieve belongings. Authorities notified over 1,730 families from seven towers about scheduled retrieval sessions between April 20 and May 4.

stories.title: Ben Gvir visits Al-Aqsa Mosque complex, says 'I feel like the owner'
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir visited the Al-Aqsa Mosque complex in occupied Jerusalem and said he felt "like the owner." Jordan's foreign ministry condemned the visit as a violation of the Status Quo agreement governing the site.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 12 – As US de-mines Strait of Hormuz, traffic status still murky
stories.summary: U.S. forces are working to clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz, though the status of shipping traffic through the waterway remains uncertain. The briefing also covered the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, IDF operations in southern Lebanon, and strikes on Gaza.

stories.title: WATCH: Seventeen haredi protesters arrested during anti-draft protests in Jerusalem, Tel Hashomer
stories.summary: Seventeen ultra-Orthodox (haredi) protesters were arrested during anti-military-draft demonstrations in Jerusalem and Tel Hashomer. Protesters attempted to block vehicles by lying in roads and directed hostile chants at police officers.

stories.title: At least 30 killed in crush at historic fortress in Haiti
stories.summary: At least 30 people, many of them young, died in a crush at Citadelle Laferrière, a 19th-century mountaintop fortress in northern Haiti. Dozens more were injured or reported missing at the popular tourist site, according to Nord department civil protection chief Jean Henri Petit.

stories.title: CIA reportedly used Pegasus software for deception op during rescue of airman in Iran
stories.summary: The CIA reportedly used NSO Group's Pegasus spyware to conduct a deception operation during the rescue of a downed American airman in Iran, sending fake messages to Iranian officials and IRGC operatives claiming the officer had already been recovered.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE updates: Iran says talks ended without deal due to 'excessive demands' made by U.S.
stories.summary: Iran stated that US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without a deal due to what Tehran described as excessive American demands. US Vice President JD Vance departed Pakistan after the negotiations failed to produce an agreement.

stories.title: No power outages scheduled in Ukraine today
stories.summary: No electricity consumption restrictions were scheduled in any region of Ukraine on Sunday, April 12.

stories.title: Sri Lankan authorities seal state-run coal procurement firm's headquarters amid alleged irregularities
stories.summary: Sri Lankan authorities sealed the headquarters of a state-run coal procurement firm amid allegations of irregularities. An audit report cited procedural violations including altered tender deadlines and alleged favoritism toward certain suppliers.

stories.title: Israeli energy minister calls for bombing Lebanese civilian infrastructure
stories.summary: Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen called for bombing civilian infrastructure in Lebanon, including sites linked to the Lebanese state. Cohen, a member of Israel's Security Cabinet, expressed skepticism about ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Dar urges US, Iran to uphold commitment to ceasefire as talks conclude without deal
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar urged the United States and Iran to maintain their ceasefire commitment after 21-hour marathon talks in Islamabad concluded without a deal. Pakistan offered to continue facilitating dialogue between the two sides.

stories.title: Bennett announces former gov’t CEOs as first two members to join party list ahead of elections
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett announced Keren Terner and Liran Avisar Ben-Horin as the first two members of his party list ahead of upcoming elections. Terner previously led the Communications Ministry and Avisar Ben-Horin headed both the Finance and Transportation Ministries.

stories.title: Rabbi reportedly target of Hezbollah plot in Syria, Damascus arrests five
stories.summary: Syrian authorities in Damascus arrested five people over an alleged Hezbollah plot to target Rabbi Michael Khoury in Syria, according to reports from KAN and Radio Free Syria.

stories.title: ‘You cannot lose if you do not have a goal’: the viral wisdom of ‘Don Tzu’
stories.summary: A satirical piece contrasts the ancient military wisdom of Chinese strategist Sun Tzu with humorous modern aphorisms attributed to a figure called "Don Tzu," emphasizing careless decision-making.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia Exchange Accusations Over Easter Truce Violations
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged accusations of violating an Easter truce, with Ukraine's military recording nearly 2,300 violations and Russia reporting almost 2,000 breaches as of Sunday morning.

stories.title: US and Iran fail to reach a deal after peace talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: The United States and Iran concluded peace talks in Islamabad on Sunday without reaching a deal to end their conflict. A fragile two-week ceasefire remains in doubt as both sides blamed each other for the breakdown, with little progress reported on core disputes.

stories.title: Islamabad talks: U.S. and Iran fail to reach agreement after 21 hours, Vance departs Pakistan
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance departed Pakistan after 21 hours of talks with Iran failed to produce an agreement. Vance praised Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir as hosts.

stories.title: Ghalibaf says US 'failed to gain the trust of the Iranian delegation'
stories.summary: Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, a member of the negotiating team, stated on social media that the US failed to gain the trust of the Iranian delegation. He cited past experiences from two previous wars as the basis for Iran's distrust.

stories.title: Russian forces shell 19 settlements in Sumy region; casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled 19 settlements in Ukraine's Sumy region more than 70 times over the past 24 hours, resulting in casualties among the local population.

stories.title: Israeli floor gymnasts share podium with gold and bronze at Croatia World Cup
stories.summary: Israeli gymnasts Artem Dolgopyat and Noam Berkovich won gold and bronze respectively in the floor exercise at the Gymnastics World Cup event in Osijek, Croatia.

stories.title: Pakistan to continue facilitating U.S.-Iran talks, says Ishaq Dar; urges ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stated that Pakistan would continue facilitating US-Iran dialogue and urged both sides to maintain the ceasefire. The Pakistan-brokered talks were the first direct high-level engagement between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

stories.title: High Court allows broader anti-war protests over weekend, criticizes state over repeated delays
stories.summary: Israel's High Court of Justice ruled to permit broader anti-war protests over the weekend. The court criticized the state for repeatedly seeking delays in the proceedings.

stories.title: War with Iran exposes Israel's critical energy vulnerabilities
stories.summary: The war with Iran exposed critical vulnerabilities in Israel's energy infrastructure, underscoring the need for the country to better secure its power sources against wartime disruptions.

stories.title: Sumud aid flotilla departs Spain for Gaza to break Israeli blockade
stories.summary: A flotilla of approximately 30 boats carrying medical aid and other supplies departed from Barcelona, Spain, bound for Gaza to attempt to break the Israeli blockade. The Global Sumud Flotilla is organized by the same group whose previous attempt with roughly 40 boats was halted by the Israeli military in October.

stories.title: Shelly Kittleson kidnapping prompts journalists to leave Iraq
stories.summary: The kidnapping of journalist Shelly Kittleson has prompted foreign journalists to leave Iraq. Only around 10 foreign journalists reportedly remain in Baghdad amid increased kidnappings and deteriorating security conditions.

stories.title: Jinnah Convention Centre turns into media hub for US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Islamabad's Jinnah Convention Centre served as a media hub during the US-Iran talks, hosting over 50 foreign journalists. Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar noted that visa-on-arrival was offered to foreign press covering the event.

stories.title: Lighting the torch: The survivors at the heart of Israel’s Holocaust Memorial Day ceremony
stories.summary: Israel's Holocaust Memorial Day ceremony will feature eight survivors in key roles during the state event scheduled for Monday evening. The annual ceremony commemorates victims of the Holocaust.

stories.title: War update: 120 clashes and 2,299 ceasefire violations recorded on front lines
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 120 combat clashes with Russian troops and 2,299 ceasefire violations along front lines over the past 24 hours as of April 12.

stories.title: How talks broke down in Islamabad, with both sides blaming each other
stories.summary: Peace talks between the US and Iran broke down in Islamabad, with both sides assigning blame. US Vice President JD Vance met with Pakistani Prime Minister during the negotiations. Iran said progress depended on American seriousness and good faith.

stories.title: Despite war cancellations, Holocaust survivors from Israel to join March of the Living
stories.summary: Around a dozen Holocaust survivors aged 90 to 100 from Israel will travel to Poland to participate in the March of the Living, even though most Israeli delegates were forced to cancel due to the war. Former hostages will light a torch during the event.

stories.title: FBI arrests former SOCOM employee for leaking classified information to journalist
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Courtney Williams, 40, of Wagram, North Carolina, a former US Special Operations Command employee. Williams was indicted by a federal grand jury on charges of transmitting classified national defense information to unauthorized individuals, including a journalist.

stories.title: Iran's new Supreme Leader is reportedly recovering from severe wounds
stories.summary: Reuters reported that Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is recovering from severe and disfiguring wounds sustained in the airstrike that killed his father, Ali Khamenei. Mojtaba Khamenei has not been seen publicly since his appointment.

stories.title: Why Cantopop star Hins Cheung’s new mentor role has polarised Hong Kong fans
stories.summary: Hong Kong Cantopop singer Hins Cheung has divided his fan base by taking on a mentor and volunteer role in the Security Bureau's youth rehabilitation program. The controversy stems from his previous perceived alignment with the city's social movement supporters.

stories.title: Haiti: More than 30 killed in stampede at historical fort
stories.summary: A deadly stampede occurred during an annual celebration at the Citadelle Laferrière, a UNESCO-listed fort in Haiti. More than 30 people were killed at the historic site, which is a symbol of Haitian independence.

stories.title: Russian forces shell four settlements in Kharkiv region, causing damage
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled four settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region on April 11, causing damage to local infrastructure.

stories.title: Wes Streeting attacks Trump’s ‘outrageous’ Iran war rhetoric
stories.summary: British Health Secretary Wes Streeting called President Donald Trump's rhetoric on Iran "incendiary, provocative and outrageous" and described the failure of US-Iran peace talks as disappointing. He stressed that successful future negotiations remain in everyone's interest.

stories.title: Lebanon protests talks with Israel
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon are set to begin negotiations in Washington on Tuesday. Israel is pressing Lebanon's government to take responsibility for disarming Hezbollah, a demand widely viewed as nearly impossible and one that analysts warn could risk pushing Lebanon into civil war.

stories.title: Hungarians vote in landmark election closely watched by EU, Russia, US
stories.summary: Voters in Hungary cast ballots in a closely watched election. Opinion polls showed Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party trailing Peter Magyar's center-right Tisza opposition party by 7–9 percentage points, with Tisza polling at approximately 38–41%.

stories.title: Asha Bhosle: The sound of Bollywood dies aged 92
stories.summary: Indian playback singer Asha Bhosle has died at the age of 92. Her voice became iconic in Bollywood, serving as the soundtrack for generations of Indian audiences.

stories.title: War of words: China and the US battle it out for the loyalty of African hearts and minds
stories.summary: The United States and China are waging an information war across Africa to influence the continent's young, media-savvy population. US Army-affiliated publications and Chinese outlets have published articles designed to portray each other negatively.

stories.title: Celestial craftsmanship: discoveries from China Sanxingdui uveil secrets of meteorite axe
stories.summary: Chinese researchers at the Sanxingdui archaeological site in Sichuan province revealed that ancient inhabitants forged an axe-like tool from a meteorite, adding to 13 known meteorite artifacts in China and highlighting the site's distinct regional culture.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks killed 26 healthcare workers: Iranian media
stories.summary: Iranian state media outlet Mehr News Agency reported that US-Israeli attacks on Iran killed 26 healthcare workers and wounded 118 others during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Pakistan deploys 13,000 troops and fighter jets to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed 13,000 troops and fighter jets to Saudi Arabia to enhance joint military coordination and operational readiness between the two countries' armed forces, aimed at supporting regional and international security and stability.

stories.title: UK woman biker in armoured gear arrives in Karachi to break ‘stereotypes’
stories.summary: British-Pakistani adventure biker Gul-i-Afshan Tariq arrived in Karachi, Pakistan, as part of a solo motorcycle journey aimed at breaking cultural stereotypes. She was welcomed at the Quaid-i-Azam House Museum alongside local women bikers.

stories.title: UK expresses disappointment over negotiations stalling
stories.summary: British Health Secretary Wes Streeting expressed the UK's disappointment that US-Iran talks in Islamabad stalled without a breakthrough. He added that diplomatic efforts remain worthwhile despite the setback.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says key oil pipeline back to full capacity after attacks
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced the East-West oil pipeline has been restored to full pumping capacity at approximately 7 million barrels per day following earlier attacks on the infrastructure.

stories.title: Study detects high prevalence of rabies virus in Karachi’s street dogs
stories.summary: A study published in an international journal found high prevalence of rabies virus among street dogs in Karachi, Pakistan, with most cases linked to the Korangi and Malir areas. Researchers called for expanded vaccination programs and improved stray dog population management.

stories.title: IDF confiscates 200 pipe bombs, numerous IEDs from weapons manufacturing lab in West Bank
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces confiscated 200 pipe bombs and numerous improvised explosive devices from a weapons manufacturing laboratory in the West Bank. The military said the lab had been operational since before the start of its counterterrorism operations in the area.

stories.title: JD Vance says talks failed due to Iran’s refusal to give up nuclear programme
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance blamed the failure of marathon US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad on Iran's refusal to abandon its nuclear weapons program. Iranian delegates countered that Washington must do more to earn their trust for future talks to succeed.

stories.title: Legendary Bollywood singer Asha Bhosle dies aged 92
stories.summary: Indian playback singer Asha Bhosle has died at the age of 92. Over a career spanning seven decades, Bhosle recorded more than 12,000 songs in multiple Indian languages.

stories.title: More than 500 people arrested at London rally for Palestine Action
stories.summary: More than 500 people were arrested at a pro-Palestine rally held at Trafalgar Square in London. Protest organisers accused the UK government of complicity in what they described as genocide in Gaza.

stories.title: Benin election favours continuity amid al-Qaeda attacks, poverty
stories.summary: Benin held its presidential election on Sunday, with Finance Minister Romuald Wadagni favored to succeed outgoing President Patrice Talon. Nearly eight million voters were eligible to cast ballots amid concerns about voter apathy and ongoing jihadist threats in the north.

stories.title: US judges fired after blocking deportations of pro-Palestinian students
stories.summary: Multiple U.S. immigration judges were fired after issuing rulings that blocked deportations of pro-Palestinian students. The dismissals mark a departure from prior norms, as it was rare for immigration judges to be terminated before President Trump returned to office.

stories.title: At least 30 dead in stampede at Haiti’s historic Laferriere Citadel
stories.summary: At least 30 people died in a stampede at the historic Laferrière Citadel in Haiti. Authorities have warned that the death toll could continue to rise.

stories.title: Israel launches fresh attacks on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel launched heavy attacks across multiple locations in southern Lebanon on Sunday. Strikes on Tefahta, Maaroub in Tyre, and Qana killed at least 24 people, according to Al Jazeera and Lebanon's National News Agency. Raids were also reported in Bazourieh, Qalila, Bafliyeh, and Qlawiya.

stories.title: Russians injure 15 people in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Russian forces wounded 15 civilians in Ukraine's Donetsk region over a 24-hour period on April 11.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Iran's negotiating delegation departed Pakistan after US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without agreement. US Vice President JD Vance also left the city. The marathon negotiations, lasting over 20 hours, broke down over disputes including Iran's nuclear programme and control of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: New era of Pak-Iran ties
stories.summary: An analysis highlighted Pakistan's role in facilitating direct engagement between the US and Iran, describing Islamabad's diplomatic efforts as demonstrating credibility, balance, and strategic patience in brokering dialogue between the two adversaries.

stories.title: Trump orders 'immediate' US naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered an immediate US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to "blow to hell" any Iranian who fires at US Navy or other "peaceful" vessels transiting the waterway.

stories.title: US and Iran fail to reach deal, Vance leaves Pakistan
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance departed Islamabad after the United States and Iran failed to reach an agreement to end the ongoing war between the two countries.

stories.title: Fine imposed on marriage halls for one-dish policy breach in Sargodha
stories.summary: Authorities in Sargodha, Pakistan, fined marriage halls a total of Rs200,000 for violating the government's one-dish policy at wedding events. The assistant commissioner conducted surprise inspections and warned of strict enforcement.

stories.title: Netanyahu effigy blown up in Spanish town festival; Israel summons envoy
stories.summary: During an Easter festival in a Spanish town, an effigy of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was blown up in a traditional event known as the "Burning of Judas." Israel summoned Spain's envoy and accused Spanish leadership of incitement.

stories.title: First contact
stories.summary: An editorial assessed the significance of the first direct US-Iran negotiations held in Islamabad, Pakistan. Reports indicated possible Israeli reduction of attacks on Lebanon and the release of frozen Iranian assets, though sticking points including the Strait of Hormuz remained unresolved.

stories.title: Partisans sabotage key transit hub for Russian military cargo to Zaporizhzhia front
stories.summary: Agents of the ATESH partisan movement sabotaged a diesel locomotive near the Likhovskaya railway station in Russia's Rostov region. The station serves as a key transit hub for Russian military cargo heading toward the Zaporizhzhia front in Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran and Strait of Hormuz: A lone battle for control
stories.summary: An analysis examined Iran's strategic leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping chokepoint. The piece noted that international straits have historically served as flashpoints and bargaining tools during conflicts between littoral states and external powers.

stories.title: ‘Too powerful for the public’: Inside Anthropic’s bid to win the AI publicity war
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic announced it had developed a model called Claude Mythos but withheld its public release, citing catastrophic cybersecurity risks. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent convened major bank leaders to discuss the model. Critics have suggested the announcement may be a publicity strategy to attract investment.

stories.title: US media emphasises rarity of direct US-Iran talks
stories.summary: US media outlets emphasized the historic rarity of direct diplomatic contact between Washington and Tehran as senior officials met face-to-face. CNN noted that the US delegation was led by Vice President JD Vance in what was described as one of the few such engagements in nearly half a century.

stories.title: Polls open in Benin presidential election, finance minister a favourite
stories.summary: Benin held its presidential election on Sunday, with Finance Minister Romuald Wadagni considered the strong favorite after overseeing a decade of economic growth despite jihadist attacks in the country's north.

stories.title: U.S., Iran talks extend into second day as strait showdown deepens
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials held direct face-to-face talks extending into a second day in Pakistan, with Islamabad participating alongside both delegations. In a departure from past practice, the two sides negotiated directly rather than through shuttle mediators.

stories.title: India: Legendary playback singer Asha Bhosle dies at 92
stories.summary: Indian playback singer Asha Bhosle, one of the world's most prolific recording artists with approximately 11,000 songs, has died at the age of 92. She was among the most celebrated voices in Bollywood history.

stories.title: Latest exchange of prisoners of war between Russia and Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine conducted a latest exchange of prisoners of war. Ukraine's military documented 469 Russian violations of the 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire. Governors in Russia's Kursk and Belgorod regions reported Ukrainian drone strikes that injured five people.

stories.title: Italy's Crippa wins Paris marathon as Ethiopia's Demise sets new women's record
stories.summary: Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa won the Paris Marathon on Sunday with a personal best time in a closely fought men's race. Ethiopia's Shure Demise set a new women's course record with a dominant victory.

stories.title: Pro-Palestinian rally in London: Over 500 arrested
stories.summary: London police arrested more than 500 pro-Palestinian protesters on Saturday during a demonstration supporting the banned group Palestine Action. The UK government designated Palestine Action a terrorist organization in July, but that designation is currently being challenged in court.

stories.title: Clay cylinders found in Iraq bear writings of Babylonian king who besieged Jerusalem, study reveals
stories.summary: Researchers translating clay cylinders discovered in Iraq found inscriptions attributed to Babylonian King Nebuchadnezzar. The texts appear to align with descriptions in the Book of Daniel depicting the king boasting about construction projects from his palace roof in Babylon.

stories.title: US and Iran end 21-hour ceasefire talks without agreement before Vance departs Pakistan
stories.summary: The United States and Iran ended 21 hours of face-to-face talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, without reaching an agreement. Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation, said negotiations failed after Iran refused American terms to refrain from developing nuclear weapons. The status of a fragile two-week ceasefire remains unclear.

stories.title: UN agency chiefs seek end to war rules violations in Middle East
stories.summary: Heads of multiple UN agencies issued a joint statement demanding an end to impunity for international humanitarian law violations in the Middle East, six weeks into the US-Israeli war on Iran. The UN Inter-Agency Standing Committee stressed that rules of war must be respected.

stories.title: Iran-US: Talks ended after 21 hours without reaching agreement
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance announced that 21 hours of US-Iran peace talks held in Pakistan ended without a deal to end the war. Both sides blamed each other for the failure of the negotiations.

stories.title: Bennett names 2 female ex-senior officials as 1st members of party’s electoral slate
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett named two women as the first members of his party's electoral slate: Keren Terner, former Finance Ministry director-general, and Liran Avisar Ben-Horin, former Communications Ministry director-general.

stories.title: UK halts Chagos Islands handover after US opposition
stories.summary: Britain halted its planned handover of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius following US President Donald Trump's criticism of the deal. The legislation underpinning the sovereignty transfer has been shelved, leaving indigenous Chagossians in uncertainty.

stories.title: Colleague Skill: AI job fears in China set off viral spread of supposed ability harvester
stories.summary: An open-source AI project designed to harvest human skills into reusable digital formats has gone viral in China. The project gained traction as a meme among young Chinese workers facing growing job insecurity amid rapid AI development.

stories.title: AI pessimism is a luxury the Global South cannot afford
stories.summary: The article argues that AI pessimism is a luxury developing nations cannot afford, citing policies like Digital Ethiopia 2030 and Pakistan's National AI Policy 2025 that treat AI as a practical tool for improving healthcare, education, agriculture, and disaster management.

stories.title: 'Out-blockade Iran': Trump floats Hormuz naval blockade in post after Islamabad talks fail
stories.summary: Following the collapse of US-Iran talks in Islamabad, President Trump shared an article suggesting the US Navy could impose a complete naval blockade on the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Iran.

stories.title: Russians attack ambulance with drone in Sumy region at night, three medics injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked an ambulance with a drone overnight in the Hlukhiv community of Ukraine's Sumy region, injuring three medics.

stories.title: Benin finance minister expected to coast to presidential election win
stories.summary: Benin's long-serving finance minister Romuald Wadagni is widely expected to win the presidential election held on Sunday in Cotonou. His candidacy is bolstered by strong economic growth and the lack of a credible opponent, though concerns persist over jihadist threats in the country's north.

stories.title: China boosts ties with Taiwan after opposition leader visits
stories.summary: China announced it would resume flights between Taiwan and additional mainland cities, while also easing bans on Taiwanese food imports and television shows, in a move to strengthen cross-strait ties after an opposition leader's visit.

stories.title: China should abandon threats against Taiwan, US diplomat says
stories.summary: A senior US diplomat called on China to abandon threats against Taiwan. Despite the absence of formal diplomatic ties, the United States remains Taiwan's most important arms supplier and international backer.

stories.title: Easter truce between Russia and Ukraine falters
stories.summary: Ukraine accused Russia of nearly 470 ceasefire violations during an Orthodox Easter truce, including air strikes, drone attacks, and shelling. The 32-hour ceasefire was proposed by Ukrainian President Zelensky and ordered by Russian President Putin. Both sides exchanged 175 prisoners of war each.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,070 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,311,180 personnel as of April 12, 2026, including 1,070 casualties over the past day.

stories.title: What happened in 40 days of war on Iran
stories.summary: A summary of 40 days of conflict involving Iran details the attacks, damage, and civilian toll resulting from the war, highlighting the people caught in the crossfire.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 44 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations held in Islamabad on day 44 of the conflict ended without a deal. Both sides blamed each other for the failure to reach an agreement.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine accuse each other of violating Orthodox Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine each accused the other of violating an Orthodox Easter ceasefire. The truce was established while US-led settlement negotiations have been paused due to the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine accuse each other of violating Orthodox Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged accusations of violating an Orthodox Easter ceasefire. The temporary truce was established as U.S.-led settlement negotiations have been suspended amid the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: New Russian space launch vehicle undergoing final tests, top official says
stories.summary: A senior Russian space official said a new two-stage launch vehicle is undergoing final tests. The rocket, capable of placing payloads of up to 17 metric tonnes in orbit, is intended to replace the Zenit rocket series.

stories.title: Riyadh, Doha to provide $5bn lifeline to Islamabad
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and Qatar are set to provide Pakistan with $5 billion in financial support to bolster its foreign exchange reserves. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb departed for Washington to attend IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings amid regional tensions.

stories.title: Israel kills 18 in Lebanon, West Bank and Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least 18 people across Lebanon, Gaza, and the occupied West Bank on Saturday. Eight were killed near Sidon in south Lebanon, while an Israeli settler shot dead a Palestinian man in the West Bank.

stories.title: Forget Hong Kong and Singapore, Philippines housing is least affordable: survey
stories.summary: A Gallup survey found the Philippines has the world's highest share of residents reporting housing affordability difficulties at 55 percent, followed by Sri Lanka at 54 percent and Myanmar at 49 percent, surpassing traditionally expensive cities like Hong Kong and Singapore.

stories.title: Semiconductor leap: China looks to next-gen ‘2D chip’ with 1,000-fold growth speed
stories.summary: Chinese scientists announced development of a wafer-scale 2D semiconductor growth method that is 1,000 times faster than existing techniques. The advance could help overcome physical limitations of current chip technology amid surging demand driven by AI applications.

stories.title: How China’s fake Titanic sank like a stone – and became a symbol of local excess
stories.summary: A life-size replica of the Titanic, conceived by Chinese entrepreneur Su Shaojun in 2014, has become a symbol of local excess after the ambitious project failed. The venture was inspired by the success of James Cameron's 1997 film, which grossed over $200 million in China.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in Pakistan end without breakthrough
stories.summary: Marathon negotiations between the United States and Iran in Islamabad ended early Sunday without a breakthrough. The two sides failed to bridge differences over nuclear issues, the Strait of Hormuz, and sanctions relief.

stories.title: New evidence further implicates US missiles in strikes that killed 21 civilians in Iran
stories.summary: New evidence has further implicated U.S. missiles in strikes on Iran that killed 21 people, including at least five children, according to Iranian officials.

stories.title: Manhattan district attorney investigates four sexual assault claims against California's Swalwell
stories.summary: The Manhattan district attorney is investigating four sexual assault claims against California Representative Eric Swalwell. Swalwell denied the accusations as "absolutely false," but several leading Democrats have urged him to withdraw from the California governor's race.

stories.title: US and Iran fail to reach agreement to end war – JD Vance
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance announced that the United States and Iran failed to reach an agreement to permanently end the ongoing war between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran says more than 2,000 children wounded in US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Iran's emergency department head Jafar Miadfar reported that more than 2,000 children were wounded in US-Israeli attacks on Iran, including 124 under age five. About 5,000 women were also injured, with attacks concentrated in Tehran, Khuzestan, Lorestan, Isfahan, Kermanshah, and Ilam provinces.

stories.title: Pope rails at ‘delusion of omnipotence,’ use of Christian language to justify war
stories.summary: During a prayer service, Pope Francis criticized the "delusion of omnipotence" and the use of Christian language to justify war. He called for negotiations and lamented that religious rhetoric was being used to support violence.

stories.title: Costa Rica receives first group of deported migrants under third-country agreement with US
stories.summary: Costa Rica received its first group of migrants deported from the United States under a third-country deportation agreement signed between San José and Washington in March. The migrants are nationals of countries other than Costa Rica.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia trade accusations of Orthodox Easter truce violations
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia accused each other of thousands of violations of an Orthodox Easter truce as the war enters its fifth year. The brief ceasefire had been agreed upon by Presidents Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky, underscoring the fragility of diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Trump’s 80th birthday bash to feature UFC fight at White House
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a UFC fight will be held on the White House grounds to celebrate his 80th birthday on June 14. The event was originally considered for July 4, coinciding with the 250th anniversary of US independence.

stories.title: Iran delegation leaves Pakistan after failed US talks
stories.summary: Iran's negotiating delegation, including Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, departed Pakistan after over 20 hours of talks with the US ended without a deal. US Vice President JD Vance also left Islamabad.

stories.title: Ukrainian air defense downs rare Russian drones Knyaz Veshchiy Oleg and Izdeliye-54
stories.summary: An anti-aircraft missile division of Ukraine's 67th Separate Mechanized Brigade shot down two rare Russian drone models, the Knyaz Veshchiy Oleg and the Izdeliye-54.

stories.title: Trump says it makes ‘no difference’ to him if Iran, US reach deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated it makes "no difference" to him whether the U.S. and Iran reach a deal. He also expressed frustration with NATO allies for remaining on the sidelines during the conflict.

stories.title: At least 30 feared dead in crush at Haitian tourist site
stories.summary: At least 30 people are feared dead after a crush at a tourist event in Haiti. Haiti's prime minister said the incident occurred at a gathering attended by many young people.

stories.title: US-Iran peace talks end without agreement, delegations leave Pakistan
stories.summary: US-Iran peace talks held in Islamabad, Pakistan, concluded without an agreement, and both delegations departed. The US Vice President stated that Iran declined to accept American terms, which included a commitment not to develop nuclear weapons.

stories.title: US-Iran peace talks end without agreement, Vance leaves Pakistan
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance departed Pakistan after peace talks with Iran ended without an agreement. Vance said Iran chose not to accept American terms, citing shortcomings in the negotiations.

stories.title: Among Magyar's supporters, "one word keeps coming up: hope"
stories.summary: Hungary's opposition leader Péter Magyar is challenging incumbent Prime Minister Viktor Orbán in what observers describe as a direct contest between the two figures. Reporting from Budapest, journalists noted that Magyar's supporters frequently cited hope as a driving motivation for their support.

stories.title: Iran says ‘diplomacy never ends’ as consultations continue
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei stated that diplomatic efforts will continue despite the stalled talks with the United States, saying "diplomacy never ends." He added that consultations with Pakistan and other neighbouring countries would proceed.

stories.title: Beijing pledges better Taiwan air and travel links after KMT leader’s mainland China trip
stories.summary: Beijing announced 10 measures to improve cross-strait relations after Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun concluded a mainland visit that included a meeting with Xi Jinping. The measures include restoring direct flights and easing travel restrictions to Taiwan.

stories.title: Hungarians vote in record numbers in election that could oust Orban, rattle Russia
stories.summary: Hungarian voters turned out in record numbers for parliamentary elections that could unseat Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Voting for the 199-seat Parliament opened at 6 a.m. and was scheduled to close at 7 p.m.

stories.title: Israel and Turkey trade accusations as tensions widen over Syria and Gaza
stories.summary: Israel and Turkey exchanged accusations amid rising tensions over Syria and Gaza. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's display of a map excluding the Palestinian West Bank heightened concerns about Israel's territorial claims.

stories.title: Macron urges Iranian president to restore security in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron urged Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to use ongoing negotiations in Islamabad to achieve de-escalation and restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Bunker busters and a Burger King: a visual guide to US military bases on British soil
stories.summary: The US-Iran war has drawn attention to approximately 15 American military installations located across the British countryside. Many of these sites carry Royal Air Force names but are effectively under US operational control, secured behind heavily guarded perimeters.

stories.title: Australia urges US, Iran to resume talks after stalemate
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong urged the United States and Iran to maintain their ceasefire and resume negotiations after talks in Islamabad ended without agreement. She warned that any escalation would increase the human toll and further damage the global economy.

stories.title: Thousands protest government and Iran war in Tel Aviv, exceeding court-ordered limits
stories.summary: An estimated 2,000 people protested against the Israeli government and the Iran war at Habima Square in Tel Aviv, double the court-permitted number. Additional protests took place in Jerusalem and Haifa. Heavy police were present but no violence or arrests were reported.

stories.title: Ukraine’s USFs eliminate over 82,000 Russian troops in 10 months
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces reported eliminating more than 82,000 Russian military personnel in the ten months since the unit was established within the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

stories.title: Minister warns Malaysia will enter ‘critical period’ for fuel supply by June
stories.summary: Malaysia's Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah warned the country will face a critical fuel supply period by June and July due to the global shortage linked to the Middle East conflict. The government is exploring alternative raw materials to address the shortfall.

stories.title: US intelligence indicates China preparing weapons shipment to Iran: CNN
stories.summary: US intelligence indicates China is preparing weapons shipments to Iran, according to CNN. Beijing is reportedly planning to route the deliveries through third countries to conceal their origin.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in Pakistan end after 21 hours with no deal; US negotiators leave
stories.summary: US-Iran talks in Pakistan ended after 21 hours without a deal. Vice President JD Vance said Iran refused to disavow its nuclear weapons capability, while Iran cited disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz as another key sticking point.

stories.title: Russians kill Ukrainian evacuation team and execute four prisoners during “ceasefire”
stories.summary: Near Huliaipilske in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Russian forces reportedly killed a Ukrainian evacuation team using FPV drones during a declared ceasefire. Four Ukrainian prisoners were also allegedly executed near Veterinarne in the Kharkiv region.

stories.title: US-Iran negotiations under way, Trump says Strait of Hormuz being cleared
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations continued in Islamabad as President Trump claimed the Strait of Hormuz was being cleared of mines. Two US warships reportedly transited the strait, and shipping data showed three supertankers departing the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Three wounded in Grand Central Station machete attack, Mamdani confirms
stories.summary: Three people were wounded in a machete attack at Grand Central Station in Manhattan. In a separate incident Saturday evening, one person was killed and several wounded in a shooting at a Chick-fil-A in Union Township, New Jersey.

stories.title: Chinese firm slammed for using ex-employee’s data to create ‘AI human’ to continue working
stories.summary: A game company in Shandong province, China, drew controversy after reportedly using a former employee's personal data to create an AI-powered digital worker that continued performing HR tasks after the employee resigned.

stories.title: ‘Your photos will be deleted’: Apple users warned over ‘nasty’ iCloud storage scam
stories.summary: Fraudsters are targeting Apple users with scam emails falsely claiming their iCloud storage is full or that photos will be deleted. The messages trick recipients into clicking malicious links designed to steal banking and personal details.

stories.title: ‘We’re trapped’: despair for sellers as Iran war knocks confidence in UK housing market
stories.summary: Estate agents across the UK report that the Iran war has undermined confidence in the housing market, with rising mortgage costs creating widespread fear among buyers and sellers. Canterbury is among the cities affected, with the spring selling season disrupted by economic uncertainty linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Video: No breakthrough after 21 hours of Iran nuclear talks, says Vance
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance said US-Iran negotiations ended without progress after more than 21 hours of talks in Islamabad. Vance stated the core US demand was a firm Iranian commitment not to pursue nuclear weapons or the capability to rapidly build one.

stories.title: Pauline Hanson says convicted rapist employed by One Nation has been sacked
stories.summary: Australian Senator Pauline Hanson confirmed she has sacked One Nation campaign manager Sean Black, who was convicted of rape in 2018. The party had previously rehired Black in 2020 after he served his sentence, drawing criticism from Coalition MPs.

stories.title: Ireland clears refinery blockade as fuel protests trigger nationwide shortages
stories.summary: Irish authorities used force to reopen the country's only refinery after days of fuel protests over rising petrol prices caused nationwide shortages and threatened emergency services operations.

stories.title: Israel cannot afford to maintain illusions about the Lebanese state - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that Israel cannot sustain illusions about the Lebanese state, contending that military force without a supporting diplomatic framework risks becoming a strategic trap in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran says negotiations with US stalled after differences on three key issues
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said negotiations with the United States ended without agreement after differences emerged on three key issues. Officials said both sides reached understanding on some points but remained divided on the unresolved matters.

stories.title: Penny Wong calls failed peace talks between US and Iran ‘disappointing’ and urges resumption
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong called the failed U.S.-Iran peace talks in Pakistan "disappointing" and urged both sides to maintain the ceasefire and resume negotiations. The talks, described as the highest-level direct U.S.-Iran engagement in decades, collapsed after a marathon 21-hour first session without securing a deal or reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Middle East war live: US failed to gain Tehran's trust, Iranian negotiator says
stories.summary: Iran's Parliamentary Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran presented forward-looking initiatives during talks in Islamabad but accused the US of failing to earn Tehran's trust. US Vice President JD Vance confirmed that 21 hours of peace talks ended without producing a deal to end the war.

stories.title: Iran says 'unrealistic to expect deal' in single round of talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said it was unrealistic to expect a deal with the US in a single round of talks. He noted the two sides remained divided on two to three important issues and that progress depends on both sides' seriousness and good faith.

stories.title: Pakistan urges US and Iran to uphold ceasefire, continue talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar urged the US and Iran to maintain the ceasefire and continue negotiations. He said Pakistan would continue facilitating dialogue between the two sides in the coming days.

stories.title: In Philippines, LPG price shock reaches bottom of beloved beef stew bowls
stories.summary: In the Philippines, the war in the Middle East has driven liquefied petroleum gas prices to nearly double, impacting small food businesses. Vendors of pares, a traditional Filipino beef stew, are struggling to manage soaring fuel costs.

stories.title: Pakistan urges US and Iran to uphold ceasefire after talks end
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called on the United States and Iran to uphold their ceasefire agreement after talks between the two sides concluded in Pakistan.

stories.title: No power outages planned across Ukraine on Sunday – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national energy company Ukrenergo announced that no electricity consumption restrictions were planned for any region of the country on Sunday, April 12.

stories.title: Hyundai spearheads foreign EV comeback push in China with Ioniq brand
stories.summary: Hyundai Motor launched the Ioniq brand tailored for Chinese consumers as part of a renewed push into China's electric vehicle market. The South Korean carmaker, which reversed a six-year sales decline in 2025, is building the brand around local technologies and partnerships.

stories.title: US and Iran fail to reach peace deal after marathon talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: US-Iran talks held in Pakistan ended without a peace deal. Vice President JD Vance said Iran refused to accept US terms, while Iran stated it did not expect an agreement from the first round of negotiations.

stories.title: What could come after a rules-based world order?
stories.summary: Analysis examines whether the rules-based international order established after World War II is collapsing, citing the US-Israel war on Iran as a key indicator. The piece explores what alternative global frameworks might emerge.

stories.title: ‘A dream come true’: helpers flock to Disneyland for free trip given as thanks
stories.summary: Hong Kong Disneyland and the Li Ka Shing Foundation distributed 5,000 free tickets to domestic workers from the Philippines, Indonesia, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Thailand. Hundreds of recipients arrived early to enjoy the theme park.

stories.title: Musician performs inside melting glacier to highlight climate crisis
stories.summary: Swiss musician To Athena performed inside a cave within a melting glacier in the Alps to draw attention to ice loss caused by the climate crisis. The performance aimed to highlight the accelerating effects of global warming on alpine glaciers.

stories.title: Oil tankers exit Strait of Hormuz amid fragile US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Three supertankers carrying oil exited the Strait of Hormuz during the fragile US-Iran ceasefire, according to shipping data. The movements come amid a global energy crunch linked to tensions in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: ‘A house of cards’: how did Wireless festival get it so wrong on Kanye West?
stories.summary: The Wireless music festival faced major fallout after announcing Ye, formerly Kanye West, as its 2026 headliner. Sponsors including Pepsi and Diageo withdrew, UK Jewish groups threatened protests, and Prime Minister Keir Starmer criticized the booking, which industry experts called a calculated risk with broad implications for the festival sector.

stories.title: Why did US-Iran talks end without an agreement in Pakistan?
stories.summary: High-level US-Iran talks held in Pakistan — the first direct diplomatic engagement in years — ended without an agreement. The two sides were unable to reach terms to resolve their conflict despite extended negotiations.

stories.title: Israel PM says war succeeded in ‘crushing’ Iran nuclear, missile programmes
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu claimed the war succeeded in crushing Iran's nuclear and missile programmes. He spoke as Iranian and US officials held talks in Pakistan aimed at ending the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Twelve Ukrainian defenders from Azov and Kara-Dag brigades return from Russian captivity
stories.summary: Twelve Ukrainian servicemembers were released from Russian captivity, including eleven from the 1st National Guard Corps Azov Brigade and one from the Kara-Dag brigade.

stories.title: Iran in no hurry to resume negotiations, ball in America’s court, local media says
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that Tehran is "in no hurry" to resume negotiations and considers the "ball in America's court." Iran warned that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz would not change unless Washington agrees to what Tehran considers a reasonable deal.

stories.title: London police arrest 523 people at protest over Palestine Action ban
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested 523 people at a protest against the ban on Palestine Action. The demonstration was the first since a High Court ruling in February declared the group's designation as a terrorist organisation unlawful.

stories.title: 'We need real peace': Easter truce fails to lift grim mood in war-torn Ukraine
stories.summary: In Kharkiv, Ukraine, Easter celebrations were subdued as residents anticipated a resumption of fighting after a weekend truce. Ukrainians expressed skepticism that the temporary ceasefire would lead to lasting peace.

stories.title: Tasnim: No change in Hormuz until US agrees to ‘reasonable’ deal
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that the Strait of Hormuz situation will remain unchanged unless the US agrees to what Iran considers a reasonable deal. Key disputes centered on Iran's claim to control the strait and its refusal to surrender its enriched uranium stockpile.

stories.title: Axios: Hormuz control, uranium stockpile key disputes in US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Axios reported that the main disputes in US-Iran negotiations were Iran's claim to control the Strait of Hormuz and its refusal to give up its enriched uranium stockpile. Talks in Islamabad ended without an agreement after failing to bridge these differences.

stories.title: Controversial Hong Kong documentary pulled from Italian film festival
stories.summary: The Hong Kong documentary To My Nineteen-Year-Old Self was withdrawn by distributor Golden Scene from the Far East Film Festival in Udine, Italy, following a dispute among stakeholders. The distributor said it reserved all legal rights to protect its reputation.

stories.title: What an Israeli bomb shelter can teach about fear, patience, and survival - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on the experience of sheltering during conflict in Israel, describing how time spent in a bomb shelter can offer lessons in fear management, patience, and survival.

stories.title: Drone, unexploded warhead crash in Finland
stories.summary: A drone carrying an unexploded warhead crashed in Finland. Ukrainian drones have recently been knocked off course by Russian electronic interference.

stories.title: UN Watch demands democracies explain election of human rights abusers to UN positions
stories.summary: UN Watch called on democratic nations to explain why human rights-abusing states continue to be elected to UN bodies, citing the UN Economic and Social Council's recent nomination of Iran to the Committee for Program and Coordination.

stories.title: Hungarians vote in landmark election closely watched by EU, Russia, US, Israel
stories.summary: Hungarians voted in a closely watched election as Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, in power since 2010, faced voter discontent over a stagnant economy. Opposition challenger Péter Magyar led in polls, though the outcome remained uncertain. An Israeli diplomat endorsed Orbán on X before deleting the post.

stories.title: Time to act on stalled proposal toughening child abuse penalties, lawmakers say
stories.summary: Hong Kong lawmakers urged authorities to strengthen penalties for child abuse, noting that protection laws for minors have not been updated since 1995. A review found that only one of 13 serious child abuse cases resulted in a jail term near the 10-year maximum.

stories.title: Does Iran’s wartime resilience offer any lessons for Taiwan?
stories.summary: Iran's ability to sustain military operations despite heavy US-Israeli attacks has prompted debate in Taiwan about its own wartime resilience. Taiwanese officials and analysts said the island could endure a conflict with mainland China only by shifting toward more integrated and survivable defense systems.

stories.title: Doubts about Trump strain Southeast Asia’s US-China balancing act
stories.summary: A survey on Southeast Asian attitudes shows growing unease about both China's influence and US leadership under President Trump, complicating the region's longstanding strategy of balancing between the two powers. Confidence in ASEAN's institutional capacity is also weakening.

stories.title: Israel reprimands Spain over blowing up of Netanyahu effigy in decades-old ceremony
stories.summary: Israel reprimanded Spain after an effigy of Prime Minister Netanyahu was blown up during a traditional local ceremony. Past editions of the event have featured effigies of other world leaders including Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Fars: Iran has no plans for further talks after failed negotiations
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported that Tehran has no plans for another round of negotiations with the United States. A source close to the Iranian delegation said the American team was "looking for an excuse" to leave the talks.

stories.title: How was the U.S.-Iran ceasefire deal reached?
stories.summary: The article examines how a two-week US-Iran ceasefire was negotiated and how Pakistan became involved as a mediator in the Islamabad talks. It also explores Israel's negative reaction to the negotiations and assesses the chances of the talks succeeding.

stories.title: Iran media: Talks end with no deal over ‘excessive’ US demands
stories.summary: Iran's Press TV reported that negotiations in Islamabad ended without agreement, citing US "excessive demands" as the cause. Key disputes included the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear rights, and other unresolved issues.

stories.title: Vance says US seeks firm Iranian pledge on nuclear program
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance said the US is seeking an "affirmative commitment" from Iran not to pursue nuclear weapons or the means to rapidly develop one. He noted that Iran's enrichment facilities had been destroyed but said Washington needs a fundamental commitment of will from Tehran.

stories.title: Vance says US made ‘final offer’ as proposal remains on table
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance said the US presented its "final and best offer" during talks with Iran in Islamabad, adding the proposal remains on the table. The US delegation left without an agreement after more than 20 hours of negotiations led by Vance in coordination with President Trump.

stories.title: 'Unreasonable demands': Talks pause as Iran calls for US flexibility
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency said the outcome of negotiations depends on the US changing what Tehran described as "unreasonable demands," with the Strait of Hormuz among key unresolved issues. Both delegations paused talks to consult expert teams on draft texts, with Pakistan mediating.

stories.title: Watch JD Vance’s full remarks after US-Iran talks end without deal
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance departed Pakistan after US-Iran talks concluded without a deal. Vance said Tehran chose not to accept what Washington described as its "final and best offer."
