stories.title: US delegation leaves Pakistan without reaching Iran deal
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance confirmed the US delegation left Pakistan without reaching an agreement with Iran following more than 20 hours of negotiations in Islamabad.

stories.title: US vice president says talks end without agreement
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance said he was returning to the US without a deal after more than 20 hours of negotiations with Iran in Islamabad. He thanked Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the army chief for their mediation efforts.

stories.title: Pope Leo slams ‘delusion of omnipotence’ stoking US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: Pope Leo denounced the "delusion of omnipotence" driving the US-Israeli war on Iran during an evening prayer service at St. Peter's Basilica. His remarks came as US-Iran negotiations began in Pakistan and a fragile ceasefire held in the region.

stories.title: Iran, US fail to reach agreement in marathon talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations held in Pakistan ended without an agreement after hours of marathon talks. US negotiators departed the country following the failure to reach a deal.

stories.title: Iran must not charge tolls in Strait of Hormuz, UN maritime chief says
stories.summary: The head of the International Maritime Organization said in an interview with Al Jazeera that Iran must not impose tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, calling on the international community to reject such measures.

stories.title: Manhattan District Attorney investigates sexual assault claims against Swalwell
stories.summary: The Manhattan District Attorney's office is investigating sexual assault allegations against US Representative Eric Swalwell of California. Swalwell denied the claims, noting they emerged ahead of the June primary in the California governor's race.

stories.title: U.S. warships transit Strait of Hormuz in mine clearance operation
stories.summary: US warships transited the Strait of Hormuz as part of a reported mine clearance operation. Iran "strongly rejected" Washington's claims that US vessels entered the strait, with military spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari denying the transit on state television.

stories.title: How Hungary's knife-edge election could impact the US and Russia
stories.summary: Hungary faces a closely contested election that could affect relations with the United States and Russia. The BBC's Europe Editor Katya Adler reported from Felcsút, the home town of Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

stories.title: Quds Force chief links ceasefire to broader regional groups
stories.summary: Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani said Iran's "resistance front" — including Hezbollah, the Houthis, and allied groups — is "stronger and more cohesive than ever" amid ongoing US and Israeli diplomatic efforts. He said pressure on these groups would not weaken them.

stories.title: As Turkey reportedly seeks to jail them, Israeli leaders blast Erdogan for ‘massacring Kurds’
stories.summary: Israeli leaders sharply criticized Turkish President Erdogan after reports that Turkey is seeking to prosecute Israeli officials. Prime Minister Netanyahu accused Erdogan of accommodating Iran's proxies, while other Israeli ministers issued personal attacks against the Turkish leader.

stories.title: Trump says Iran talks 'make no difference', attends UFC fight in Miami
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said it "makes no difference" to him whether a deal is reached with Iran while negotiations continued in Islamabad. He made the remarks before attending a UFC event in Miami, where he was seen speaking briefly with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

stories.title: Iran chose 'not to accept our terms', US VP Vance says after negotiations
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance announced that Iran declined to accept American terms after 21 hours of negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan. The breakdown followed intensive diplomatic efforts mediated by Pakistan.

stories.title: Campaign against Iran not over, existential threats removed: Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that the campaign against Iran is not over but claimed that existential threats from Iran, Syria, Yemen's Houthis, Hezbollah in Lebanon, and Hamas in Gaza have been removed.

stories.title: Ship traffic rises in Hormuz as US-Iran talks continue in Islamabad
stories.summary: At least 16 ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, the highest level since the ceasefire began, according to NBC News. Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers also transited the waterway as US-Iran talks continued in Islamabad.

stories.title: Turkey seeking nearly 5,000 years in prison for Netanyahu over October Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Turkey is seeking nearly 5,000 years in prison for Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and 34 other officials over the October Gaza flotilla incident. Defense Minister Katz and National Security Minister Ben Gvir are also among those charged.

stories.title: Netanyahu next to Middle East map: ‘We strangled them and have more to do’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, standing beside a map of the Middle East, stated that Israel had "strangled" its adversaries and had more to accomplish. He referenced six countries he said had sought to threaten Israel.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in Pakistan fail to yield deal, end after 21 hours; US negotiators leave
stories.summary: US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended without a deal after approximately 21 hours of negotiations. Vice President Vance said Iran refused American terms on its nuclear program, while Iranian media blamed Washington's "excessive demands" for the breakdown.

stories.title: Maduro’s capture sparked outrage, confusion – and a Chinese migration wave to Venezuela
stories.summary: Two months after the U.S. captured and forcibly extradited former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro, a wave of Chinese migrants has begun relocating to Venezuela seeking business opportunities. Some are returning residents who had fled during Maduro's tenure, while others are new arrivals drawn by the changing political landscape.

stories.title: US, Iran search for breakthrough in Islamabad as talks stretch into third round
stories.summary: Direct talks between US and Iranian delegations, mediated by Pakistan, stretched into a third round in Islamabad on Sunday. Expert-level committees covering economic, military, legal, and nuclear issues exchanged written texts at the Serena Hotel.

stories.title: Iran says Islamabad talks involved extensive exchanges on key issues
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said negotiations in Islamabad involved extensive exchanges of texts and messages between Iranian and US teams. Key issues discussed included the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program.

stories.title: Netanyahu presented Iran attack plan to former US presidents, former secretary of state claims
stories.summary: Former US Secretary of State John Kerry claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu presented Iran attack plans to Presidents George W. Bush, Barack Obama, and Joe Biden, all of whom declined. Trump reportedly agreed to the plan.

stories.title: Marathon US-Iran talks end in failure as Vance cites nuclear arms as key sticking point
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance announced that marathon negotiations with Iran in Islamabad, Pakistan, ended without an agreement after 21 hours of talks. Vance identified Iran's nuclear weapons program as the central sticking point and characterized the failure as detrimental to both nations.

stories.title: New relief for households being considered as Albanese government warns of ‘long tail’ from Iran war
stories.summary: The Australian government under Prime Minister Albanese is considering additional household relief measures in next month's federal budget amid economic fallout from the Iran war. Infrastructure Minister Catherine King acknowledged that the U.S.-Iran peace talks represented the best chance of lowering fuel prices but signaled further assistance may be needed.

stories.title: Fighting in Lebanon intensifies with strikes and missile fire
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck the town of Qounine and areas near Halta farm in southern Lebanon, according to Al Jazeera Arabic. Hezbollah responded by firing missiles at Israeli troop positions near Bint Jbeil, Khiam, and Rashaf in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Why securing Hong Kong’s economic future is a cultural question
stories.summary: Hong Kong is undergoing an economic transition, experiencing growth in family offices and its role as an offshore renminbi hub. Officials and analysts argue the city needs to strengthen its cultural infrastructure to attract talent, lure back diaspora members, and draw high-spending tourists, in line with China's 15th five-year plan.

stories.title: London police arrest 212 people at protest over Palestine Action ban
stories.summary: London police arrested 212 people during a protest against the UK government's ban on Palestine Action. The group was banned by lawmakers in 2025 after its members broke into a Royal Air Force base.

stories.title: Russian regional officials say Ukraine attacked Kursk, Belgorod regions
stories.summary: Governors of Russia's Kursk and Belgorod border regions reported on April 11 that Ukrainian drones attacked targets in both regions, injuring five people.

stories.title: Netanyahu says campaign against Iran ‘not over,’ touts ‘historic achievements’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said the campaign against Iran is "not over" and cited "historic achievements" in recent military and diplomatic efforts. Opposition leaders countered that war goals remain unfulfilled.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges end to 'madness of war' as US, Iran start talks
stories.summary: Pope Leo issued an appeal from Vatican City urging world leaders to end the "madness of war" as senior U.S. and Iranian officials met in Pakistan on April 11 to discuss ending their six-week conflict.

stories.title: Russian listed by Memorial as political prisoner goes on hunger strike
stories.summary: A former Moscow district official, listed by the Memorial human rights organization as a political prisoner, declared a dry hunger strike in a Russian prison, refusing both food and water over what he says are politically motivated charges.

stories.title: China family creates AI clone to comfort elderly mum after only son dies in car accident
stories.summary: A family in Shandong province, China, hired an AI technology team led by Zhang Zewei from Jiangsu province to create a digital clone of their son after he was killed in a car accident. The AI replica chats online with his elderly mother to help her cope with the loss of her only child.

stories.title: Palestinians appalled as Israel approves settlements in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israel approved 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank, drawing strong condemnation from Palestinians who expressed fear of further land loss. The decision deepens tensions over Israeli settlement expansion in the territory.

stories.title: Macron, Erdoğan discuss war in Ukraine, Middle East situation
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron held a phone call with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. The two leaders discussed Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine and the broader situation in the Middle East.

stories.title: Empty tankers heading to US to load up with oil and gas, says Trump
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump stated that empty tankers are heading to the United States to load oil and gas, amid the worst disruption to global energy supplies in history caused by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: India refuses to criminalise marital rape. This new series shines a light on it
stories.summary: India's Supreme Court declined to criminalize marital rape. The Indian television series Chiraiya has drawn millions of viewers and sparked widespread social media discussion about consent and misogyny.

stories.title: Israel reprimands Spanish diplomat over detonation of Netanyahu effigy
stories.summary: Israel formally reprimanded Spain's top diplomat in Tel Aviv after an effigy of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was publicly detonated in Spain, calling the incident a provocation.

stories.title: Evening update
stories.summary: Fourteen hours of ceasefire talks between US and Iranian delegations in Islamabad ended without agreement, with negotiations set to resume on Sunday, according to Iranian media. In London, Metropolitan Police arrested over 500 people at a Trafalgar Square protest against the proscription of Palestine Action.

stories.title: Singapore’s robotaxi drive revs up with help from Chinese AV leaders
stories.summary: Singapore is advancing its robotaxi program with assistance from Chinese autonomous vehicle companies. Test vehicles, which are left-hand-drive Chinese models, currently operate with safety officers on board in northern Singapore. The goal is fully driverless operation, similar to services already running in Beijing, Shenzhen, San Francisco, and Los Angeles.

stories.title: Iran war live: Vance says no deal reached, US has made ‘best, final offer’
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad ended without a deal, with Vice President JD Vance saying the US had made its "best, final offer." Iranian media accused the US of looking for an excuse to leave the talks and said the "ball is in America's court."

stories.title: Russian drone attack sets residential building on fire in Druzhkivka
stories.summary: A Russian FPV drone struck a five-storey residential building in Druzhkivka, Donetsk region, on the evening of April 11, causing a fire. The city is located in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Iranian media: peace talks to continue on Sunday after no agreement reached
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported that US and Iranian delegates in Islamabad failed to reach an understanding after their latest round of negotiations. Talks are scheduled to continue on Sunday. Journalists noted very few details have leaked from the sensitive ceasefire discussions.

stories.title: US warships transit Strait of Hormuz in mine clearance operation: Centcom
stories.summary: Two US Navy warships transited the Strait of Hormuz as part of a mine clearance operation targeting mines laid by Iran, according to US Central Command. The transit is the first since the US-Israeli war on Iran began. President Trump stated Washington had started "clearing out" the strategic waterway, which carries a fifth of global crude oil.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it fired on Israeli military in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it fired missiles at Israeli army positions near Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon. The attack followed reported Israeli air strikes across southern Lebanon on Saturday, pushing the total Lebanese death toll past 2,000 since the conflict began.

stories.title: The moral barometer: Iran uses its people as live targets, as America values every life - opinion
stories.summary: This opinion piece argues that Iran uses its own civilians as targets while the United States values every life. It contrasts what the author describes as civilized democracy against a regime that tortures its people.

stories.title: Over 500 protestors in London arrested over Palestine Action ban, says Met police
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested 523 people at a Trafalgar Square protest on Saturday demanding the UK lift its ban on Palestine Action. It was the first mass demonstration since the High Court ruled the group's proscription as a terrorist organisation unlawful. UK Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood has been granted approval to appeal the ruling.

stories.title: Bilawal terms Islamabad Talks ‘biggest achievement so far’ in efforts for US-Iran de-escalation
stories.summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari described US-Iran talks taking place in Islamabad as the "biggest achievement so far" in de-escalation efforts. Pakistan brokered a two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran ahead of the negotiations. Bilawal made the remarks during an interview with Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Supertankers exit Gulf via Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran talks begin, data shows
stories.summary: Shipping data showed supertankers exiting the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran talks began, with crude oil expected to arrive at Malaysia's Malacca port by April 21.

stories.title: US-Iran peace negotiations end after 14 hours but disagreements remain, says Iran
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that the third round of US-Iran talks in Islamabad ended with serious disagreements remaining. Iranian sources described US demands during the 14-hour negotiations as "excessive." Iran's government said both delegations continued exchanging messages after the session concluded Saturday.

stories.title: War update: 101 clashes on frontline, 469 violations of ceasefire recorded
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukrainian positions 101 times in one day, with 469 violations of the ceasefire recorded after 16:00, according to Ukrainian military reports.

stories.title: Iraqi Parliament elects Nizar Amedi as country’s new president
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament elected Nizar Amedi as the country's new president. Iraq must now select a new prime minister, a closely watched process.

stories.title: On the record and off the court: Meet the only Jewish player on the NCAA championship team
stories.summary: Harrison Hochberg, the only Jewish player on the University of Michigan's NCAA championship basketball team, discussed celebrating Passover during the Final Four, confronting antisemitism, and honoring his grandfather's legacy.

stories.title: We spoke to the man making viral Lego-style AI videos for Iran. Experts say it's powerful propaganda
stories.summary: An individual creating AI-generated Lego-style videos promoting Iranian narratives has gained viral attention online. Experts describe the content as highly sophisticated propaganda that goes beyond typical low-quality AI-generated material.

stories.title: Pakistan sends military force, fighter jets to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed a military force and fighter jets to King Abdulaziz Air Base in Saudi Arabia's eastern province. The Saudi defence ministry confirmed the deployment is intended to strengthen a joint defence cooperation agreement between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran war lands 'triple blow' to flood-ravaged Sri Lankans
stories.summary: Sri Lanka faces compounded crises as the Iran war disrupts economic conditions in a country already reeling from devastating floods and a prolonged economic downturn.

stories.title: UNICEF says humanitarian aid ‘critical’ in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: UNICEF official Elias Diab called for a ceasefire in Lebanon, warning that hospitals in hard-to-reach areas of the south are cut off from the rest of the country. UNICEF said its teams are delivering medical supplies, safe water, and hygiene kits to overwhelmed health facilities and isolated families in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Australia news live: government ad campaign urges drivers to minimise fuel use as supply crisis persists
stories.summary: The Australian government launched an advertising campaign urging drivers to minimize fuel consumption amid a global supply crisis linked to the US-Israel conflict with Iran. The "Every little bit helps" campaign spans TV, digital, and billboard formats as part of a four-tier national fuel security plan.

stories.title: US liberal zionist advocacy group backs blocking aid to Israel, including for defence
stories.summary: J Street, a US liberal Zionist advocacy group, announced it will support ending all American aid to Israel, including funding for defensive systems such as Iron Dome. Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has also called for blocking defensive-system funding after voting against an amendment to cut $500 million in US aid to Israel.

stories.title: Hezbollah | Ayatollah’s allies in Lebanon
stories.summary: Despite Israeli operations that killed Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024 and a ground offensive in Lebanon, Hezbollah has continued firing hundreds of rockets and drones at Israeli forces over more than 40 days.

stories.title: Man arrested for allegedly damaging US military aircraft in Shannon airport
stories.summary: A man in his 40s was arrested at Shannon Airport in County Clare, Ireland, after allegedly entering an unauthorized area and damaging a US Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane. He was detained on suspicion of criminal damage and remains in police custody.

stories.title: Relatives seek FO’s help to ascertain fate of family members believed to be killed by missile debris in Kuwait
stories.summary: Relatives of Waqas Ahmed, a Pakistan-origin man missing in Kuwait along with his family, have written to Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs seeking help to confirm whether the family was killed by missile debris following an interception incident.

stories.title: Libya signs first unified state Budget in more than a decade
stories.summary: Libya signed its first unified state budget in more than a decade. The oil-producing country has been divided since a 2014 civil war led to the creation of two rival administrations.

stories.title: London police arrest 212 people at protest over Palestine Action ban
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested 212 people at a Trafalgar Square protest opposing the UK government's ban on the Palestine Action group. The demonstration followed a High Court ruling in February that the ban designating the group as a terrorist organization was unlawful. UK Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood has been granted approval to appeal that ruling.

stories.title: IRGC warns military vessels attempting to cross Hormuz of ‘strong response’
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned that any military vessel attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz would face a "strong response." The IRGC said only non-military vessels would be permitted through the channel under specific regulations. Iran denied US claims that two American warships had crossed the strait.

stories.title: Fury beats Makhmudov in heavyweight boxing comeback, then calls out Joshua
stories.summary: Tyson Fury defeated Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous points decision in his heavyweight boxing comeback. After the fight, Fury issued a public call-out to Anthony Joshua.

stories.title: US-Iran talks move to third round as Trump claims ‘no difference’ to him if deal reached
stories.summary: US-Iran talks entered a third round in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Iranian media describing the negotiations as potentially the "last opportunity" to find common ground. President Trump said it made "no difference" to him whether a deal was reached, insisting Washington had already won.

stories.title: Trump: ‘Regardless of what happens, we win’ in Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told reporters that the US wins "regardless" of the outcome of Iran negotiations, claiming the US had "totally defeated" Iran. He also said the US was clearing mines from the Strait of Hormuz, after the military reported two ships transited the channel — a claim Iran denied.

stories.title: Two US Navy destroyers begin clearing mines in Strait of Hormuz – CNN
stories.summary: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers began mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz, according to CNN. The operation targets mines in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Teams of experts from Iran, US exchange written texts after in-person talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Expert-level delegations from Iran and the United States exchanged written texts during in-person nuclear, military, legal, and economic discussions at the Serena Hotel in Islamabad. Negotiations continued as part of talks held during a two-week ceasefire in the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: IDF soldier severely injured in operational accident in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli Defense Forces soldier was severely injured in an operational accident in Gaza. The soldier was evacuated to a hospital for treatment, and his family was notified of the incident.

stories.title: US President Trump says US ‘wins’ regardless of how Iran talks go
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the United States would "win regardless" of the outcome of ongoing negotiations with Iran, speaking to reporters outside the White House on Saturday.

stories.title: Iran and US top officials launch negotiations in Pakistan
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations launched negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, though the two sides remained far apart on key issues including sanctions and Lebanon. The talks are aimed at resolving the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Map of Israel used by Netanyahu in speech suggests annexation of West Bank completed
stories.summary: During a televised address by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a map displayed behind him showed the occupied West Bank incorporated within the borders of the state of Israel, suggesting completed annexation.

stories.title: Five arrested as Syria says it foiled Hezbollah-linked plot to kill Damascus rabbi
stories.summary: Syrian authorities said they foiled a Hezbollah-linked plot to assassinate a rabbi in Damascus, arresting five suspects. The ministry stated the suspects attempted to plant a bomb near the target's home and had received specialized military training abroad.

stories.title: Price monitoring committee directs Sindh govt to take corrective measures against rising fares in Karachi
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Price Monitoring Committee directed the Sindh government to address rising public transport fares in Karachi. This came despite Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah's earlier announcement of a province-wide fare freeze following negotiations with transporters amid global fuel price increases.

stories.title: UN demands accountability for violations of rules of war in Middle East
stories.summary: United Nations agency leaders called for accountability over violations of the rules of war in the Middle East. They expressed particular concern about the disproportionate impact on women, children, and other vulnerable populations.

stories.title: Ukraine preparing active engagement with European partners – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is maintaining constant contact with the United States and preparing for intensified cooperation with European partners. He emphasized advancing negotiations and strengthening security guarantees.

stories.title: Trump says US forces are ‘clearing’ Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that American forces are clearing the Strait of Hormuz, reiterating claims that the US military has destroyed Iran's navy and air force. The strait is a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments.

stories.title: Iraqi parliment appoints Kurdish Nizar Amedi as new president
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament elected Kurdish politician Nizar Amedi as the country's new president. Amedi is a member of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), a party considered friendly to Iran, which could have broader implications for Iraqi politics.

stories.title: Gaza civil defence says Israeli strikes kill seven
stories.summary: Gaza's civil defense reported that Israeli strikes killed seven people despite an October 10 ceasefire, as both Israel and Hamas continued to accuse each other of violating the truce.

stories.title: Tel Aviv: Israeli protestors rally against wars in Iran and Lebanon
stories.summary: Approximately 800 Israeli demonstrators rallied in Tel Aviv against the wars in Iran and Lebanon, accusing Prime Minister Netanyahu of attempting to derail the ceasefire with Iran.

stories.title: Irish police move to break blockade of oil refinery by protesters angry at fuel prices
stories.summary: Irish police moved to clear protesters blockading the Whitegate oil refinery, Ireland's only refinery, amid demonstrations over surging fuel prices. A senior government minister described the situation as a "very dangerous economic moment" for the country.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1508: Ukraine leads drone war but runs out of time to share blueprint
stories.summary: On day 1,508 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, 182 Ukrainian prisoners were returned from Russian captivity ahead of Easter. The article also examines Ukraine's lead in drone warfare technology and the challenges of sharing its operational blueprint.

stories.title: Irish police chief denounces oil refinery blockade
stories.summary: Ireland's police chief denounced a blockade of an oil refinery that protesters have maintained since Tuesday over rising petrol and diesel prices linked to the Middle East war.

stories.title: Sudanese man charged in UK over migrant deaths
stories.summary: A Sudanese man arrested Friday in England has been charged in connection with a French investigation into the deaths of four migrants attempting to cross the English Channel.

stories.title: Death toll of shooting in Afghanistan's Herat hits 11
stories.summary: The death toll from a shooting in western Afghanistan's Herat province rose to 11 on Saturday after gunmen targeted civilians at a picnic spot.

stories.title: Zelensky: We hope to continue prisoner exchanges in near future
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an evening address that Ukraine hopes to continue prisoner exchanges with Russia in the near future.

stories.title: Pope condemns ‘delusion of omnipotence’ causing US-Iran war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned what he called the "delusion of omnipotence" driving the US-Israel war on Iran during an evening prayer service at Saint Peter's Basilica. He called for an end to war and the display of power.

stories.title: Colombia retaliates with 100% tariffs on Ecuador
stories.summary: Colombia imposed 100% retaliatory tariffs on Ecuadorian goods amid an ongoing trade war. Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa has criticized Colombian President Gustavo Petro over drug trafficking and illegal mining along their shared border.

stories.title: WATCH: Netanyahu says that Israel's campaign in Iran is 'not over yet'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel's military campaign in Iran is 'not over yet.' He claimed the Iranian regime is seeking a ceasefire and facing internal leadership conflicts.

stories.title: Mourners bid farewell to Lebanese state security personnel killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Mourners attended funeral services for Lebanese state security personnel killed in an Israeli airstrike on Lebanon.

stories.title: Hezbollah slams planned Lebanese talks with Israel as strikes kills 10
stories.summary: Hezbollah condemned planned Lebanese talks with Israel as Israeli strikes killed 10 people. Hezbollah lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said the talks deepen domestic divisions at a time when Lebanon needs unity against Israeli aggression.

stories.title: Russian artillery strike on Kherson injures four, including minor
stories.summary: A Russian artillery strike on the city of Kherson injured four people, including a 14-year-old boy who was hospitalized. The attack targeted the southern Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Iranian media: new round of talks may be ‘last opportunity’ for agreement with US
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that the third round of trilateral negotiations between Iran, the United States, and Pakistan has begun in Islamabad. The agency described the current round as potentially the last opportunity to reach a ceasefire framework.

stories.title: Sex assault claims against California governor hopeful Eric Swalwell under investigation
stories.summary: The Manhattan District Attorney's office confirmed it is investigating sexual assault allegations against US Congressman Eric Swalwell, a leading Democratic candidate for California governor. A former district office employee accused him of two nonconsensual sexual encounters in 2019 and 2024.

stories.title: Death toll from Israeli strike in Lebanon’s Tafahta rises to 13
stories.summary: The death toll from an Israeli air strike on Tafahta in southern Lebanon rose to 13, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. NNA reported a wave of Israeli attacks across multiple towns in southern Lebanon on Saturday.

stories.title: Several Gazans said killed in IDF strikes; soldier seriously hurt in operational accident
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it struck operatives in Gaza who were planning attacks against troops. Separately, an Israeli soldier was seriously injured in an operational accident and hospitalized.

stories.title: “Diplomacy is not an event, it’s a process, it takes time.”
stories.summary: A former Pakistani diplomat urged realistic expectations for the US-Iran talks being held in Islamabad. The diplomat emphasized that diplomacy is a prolonged process rather than a single event.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP slams planned Lebanese talks with Israel as strikes kill 10
stories.summary: A Hezbollah-affiliated member of the Lebanese parliament criticized planned Lebanese negotiations with Israel as Israeli strikes killed 10 people. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has expressed willingness to engage in direct talks with Israel.

stories.title: Iran-US negotiations underway in Pakistan, US says Strait of Hormuz being 'cleared'
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations held direct negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, for the first time since 1979, aimed at ending a six-week conflict. President Trump said the US military had begun clearing mines from the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges world leaders to reject war and negotiate peace
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV called on world leaders on Saturday to reject war as a means of resolving disputes and to pursue peace through negotiation.

stories.title: Iraqi parliament elects new president
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament elected Kurdish politician Nizar Amedi as the country's new president, ending months of political deadlock over the position.

stories.title: Iran says talks with US move to expert level – CNN
stories.summary: US-Iran trilateral talks in Islamabad moved to the expert level, according to Iranian officials cited by CNN. The negotiations, also involving Pakistan, continued as the sides worked toward a broader agreement.

stories.title: French police find naked boy, 9, locked in father’s van since 2024
stories.summary: French police in the village of Hagenbach rescued a nine-year-old boy found naked and locked inside his father's utility van, where he had reportedly been confined since 2024. The child was hospitalized and the father detained.

stories.title: Has Israeli society become conditioned to permanent war?
stories.summary: Opinion polls in Israel indicate public opposition to ending the war against Iran, raising questions about whether Israeli society has grown accustomed to prolonged conflict.

stories.title: Washington officials say 21 dead canines that washed ashore were foxes, solving local mystery
stories.summary: Authorities in Skagit County, Washington, determined that 21 dead canines that washed ashore on Guemes Island were foxes legally used as bait in fishing operations, resolving a local mystery.

stories.title: Iranian delegation meets Pakistan’s Sharif ahead of peace talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: An Iranian delegation met with Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in Islamabad ahead of peace talks between Iran and the United States.

stories.title: UK crime agency charges Sudanese man after four die in Channel boat crossing
stories.summary: Britain's National Crime Agency charged a 27-year-old Sudanese man with endangering life after four migrants died during a small boat crossing of the English Channel from France to the United Kingdom earlier in the week.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least 18 people across southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon have killed at least 18 people. Lebanon's Health Ministry reports that more than 2,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks since March 2.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia swap 175 servicemen each ahead of Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 prisoners of war each on Saturday ahead of a ceasefire marking Orthodox Easter. Officials from both countries confirmed the swap as the temporary truce was set to begin.

stories.title: Iranian military ‘strongly’ denies US claim two ships passed through Hormuz
stories.summary: A spokesperson for Iran's military headquarters denied US Central Command's claim that American warships transited the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM had reported that two US vessels passed through the strait to clear sea mines laid by Iran. Iran's statement asserted that control over vessel passage remains with the Iranian Armed Forces.

stories.title: Over 60 drone and artillery strikes hit Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving one civilian injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched over 60 drone and artillery strikes on two districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring one civilian.

stories.title: Families gather to mourn victims of deadly shooting in Afghanistan
stories.summary: Dozens of mourners gathered in Afghanistan to pray for the victims of a shooting at a picnic spot in the western city of Herat that killed at least 11 people.

stories.title: Watch: A halt to the war, including in Lebanon, has been part of the ceasefire deal: Iran Foreign Ministry
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry stated that a halt to the war, including the conflict in Lebanon, has been part of the ceasefire deal under discussion.

stories.title: White House says in-person talks with Iran ‘ongoing’
stories.summary: A senior White House official confirmed that face-to-face talks between the US and Iran are ongoing in Islamabad, Pakistan, extending late into the evening. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with US Vice President JD Vance during the negotiations. Iranian state media reported that two rounds of talks had already taken place.

stories.title: US warships transit Strait of Hormuz in mine clearance op
stories.summary: Two US warships began mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday. The operation coincided with the start of US-Iran peace talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: Pakistan deploys fighter jets to Saudi Arabia under defence pact
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed fighter jets to Saudi Arabia under a defense pact after Iranian strikes hit key Saudi energy infrastructure and killed a Saudi national.

stories.title: UN demands accountability for war crimes in Middle East
stories.summary: UN agency chiefs demanded an end to impunity for widespread violations of international law in the Middle East. The statement on Saturday called for accountability for war crimes committed in the region.

stories.title: Pope Leo says 'enough of war!' in fiery speech
stories.summary: Pope Leo delivered a forceful speech condemning the war in the Middle East, calling for an end to the conflict. It was described as his strongest condemnation of the violence to date.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Israel wants ‘true peace pact’ with Lebanon, campaign in Iran 'not over'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel seeks a lasting peace deal with Lebanon. He also declared that Israel's military campaign against Iran is 'not over,' while noting what he called 'historic achievements.' The remarks came during ongoing US-Iran ceasefire talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks persist despite Kremlin’s Easter ceasefire, Ukrainian forces say
stories.summary: Ukraine reported 469 violations of Russia's Kremlin-declared 32-hour Easter ceasefire, including continued drone strikes on Odesa and Kherson. A Ukrainian military officer confirmed that Russian drone attacks persisted after the ceasefire took effect on Saturday.

stories.title: Iran’s deputy FM says Tehran has ‘upper hand’ in talks with US
stories.summary: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi stated that Tehran entered negotiations with the United States from a position of strength, asserting that the war on Iran has failed.

stories.title: Two patrol officers killed in Russian shelling in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Two Ukrainian patrol officers, Ihor Lisytsyn and Ihor Radzyminskyi, were killed on April 11 in the Donetsk region by Russian shelling.

stories.title: Hezbollah supporters demonstrate to protest Lebanon’s talks with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah supporters gathered outside the Lebanese Prime Minister's office in Beirut to protest the government's decision to negotiate directly with Israel. Hezbollah and the Amal Movement reportedly urged supporters not to hold demonstrations to preserve stability. Prime Minister Nawaf Salam postponed a planned trip to the US citing domestic instability.

stories.title: Nigeria terror trial: Nearly 400 terror suspects convicted
stories.summary: A mass terror trial in Nigeria resulted in 386 convictions of Islamist militants. The country continues to face an insurgency involving extremist groups including Boko Haram.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran peace talks under way as Trump claims US has begun clearing mines in strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US-Iran peace talks began in Islamabad with Pakistan acting as mediator, while President Trump claimed the US had started clearing mines from the Strait of Hormuz. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated Israel remains committed to fighting Iran. The UK announced it will host a Strait of Hormuz meeting next week to restore free maritime movement.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. forces are ‘clearing’ Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump stated that American forces are "clearing" the Strait of Hormuz, posting the claim as senior U.S. and Iranian officials began talks on April 11, 2026, in Islamabad with Pakistani mediation.

stories.title: US says Navy destroyers working to de-mine Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that Navy destroyers are conducting mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz, with additional forces expected in coming days. Iranian outlets dismissed the claim as 'fake news.' President Trump claimed that all of Iran's mining boats had been destroyed.

stories.title: Buffets, baristas, but no briefings: A journalist’s account of covering Islamabad Talks
stories.summary: Hundreds of journalists gathered at Islamabad's convention centre, converted into a media hub for the US-Iran peace talks, but were largely confined to waiting as negotiations took place behind closed doors at a separate location.

stories.title: US says two naval ships ‘transited’ Strait of Hormuz for mine-clearing
stories.summary: The United States said two naval ships transited the Strait of Hormuz for mine-clearing operations. Control of the strait remains a key issue in ongoing US-Iran negotiations being held in Islamabad.

stories.title: Pakistan sends fighter jets to Saudi Arabia amid fragile US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed fighter jets to Saudi Arabia under a mutual defence pact amid a fragile US-Iran ceasefire. The deployment comes as Islamabad hosts US-Iran ceasefire talks.

stories.title: Iranian media: Third session of US-Iran talks to be held tonight
stories.summary: Iranian state TV reported that a third session of US-Iran peace negotiations would take place in Islamabad on Saturday evening. The second session had concluded earlier that day in Pakistan, following a two-week ceasefire agreement reached between Iran and the US.

stories.title: US agreed to unfreeze Iranian assets, sources tell Al Jazeera
stories.summary: Sources close to the Iranian delegation told Al Jazeera that the United States agreed to release frozen Iranian assets ahead of the talks in Pakistan. This concession addresses one of Iran's demands outlined in its 10-point plan prior to ceasefire negotiations. The White House has not commented on the reported agreement.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes oil depot, pumping station, and ammo dumps in Russia and occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces struck an oil depot, an oil pumping station, three ammunition depots, and concentrations of Russian personnel in occupied Ukrainian territories and inside Russia on and around April 11.

stories.title: Iran installing roadblocks in front of buried nuclear facility entrances - report
stories.summary: The Institute for Science and International Security analyzed satellite imagery showing Iran installing roadblocks in front of entrances to its underground nuclear facility in Isfahan.

stories.title: Israel will continue to fight Iran, Netanyahu says
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed that Israel will continue fighting against what he called Iran's regime and its proxies. Netanyahu, who faces an International Criminal Court warrant for alleged war crimes in Gaza, also accused Turkish President Erdogan of aiding Iran. The statement came amid ongoing US-Iran ceasefire talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: US continues ‘extravagant’ demands in talks, says Iran state TV
stories.summary: Iran's state TV reported that the United States is pressing 'extravagant' demands during peace negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan. Iran's Tasnim news agency said the Strait of Hormuz remains a key point of disagreement. Iran is also insisting on preserving military gains made during the conflict.

stories.title: Hungary PM Viktor Orban’s birthplace turns into a battleground for his survival
stories.summary: Hungary holds elections on April 12 amid widespread public discontent over the cost of living and allegations of cronyism. The vote is being closely watched as a potential challenge to Prime Minister Viktor Orban's hold on power in his birthplace region.

stories.title: Best drone tech in world is in Ukraine. But it’s running out of time to export it, says UK defense chief
stories.summary: A UK defense chief stated that Ukraine possesses the world's best drone technology but faces time pressure to export it. Ukraine's drone capabilities have drawn significant international interest.

stories.title: Russian attacks leave three killed, eight injured in Kherson region
stories.summary: Russian attacks on the Kherson region on April 11 killed three people and injured eight others, including a trolleybus driver who later died of critical wounds in hospital.

stories.title: Israel will fight on ferociously:  It will hunt down its enemies, not be hounded by them - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that Israel would pursue aggressive military action against its enemies rather than return to containment policies that prioritized restraint and diplomacy.

stories.title: US appeals court extends deadline to halt White House ballroom construction
stories.summary: A US appeals court extended the deadline for halting construction of a ballroom at the White House. Judges questioned the Trump administration's argument that completing the project is necessary for national security.

stories.title: Death toll in Lebanon surpasses 2,000
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that at least 2,020 people have been killed and 6,436 wounded in Israeli strikes since March 2. The death toll in Lebanon has now surpassed 2,000.

stories.title: Orthodox Christian pilgrims flock to Jerusalem for Holy Fire ceremony
stories.summary: Orthodox Christian pilgrims attended the annual Holy Fire ceremony in Jerusalem amid a heightened police presence. Several Palestinian Christians were reportedly detained during the procession. Attendance was limited due to the fragile ceasefire with Iran.

stories.title: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian during raid on occupied West Bank village
stories.summary: Israeli settlers killed a Palestinian during a raid on a village in the occupied West Bank. The incident occurred days after Israel approved 34 new illegal settlements in the territory.

stories.title: First glimpse in years— wife barely recognizes Ukrainian soldier after weight loss in Russia’s captivity
stories.summary: A Ukrainian soldier was barely recognized by his wife after significant weight loss during captivity in Russia. The family was reunited following his release.

stories.title: UK police arrest over 200 at London demonstration for Palestine Action support
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested over 200 people at a demonstration in support of Palestine Action. The arrests came as the UK government appealed a court ruling against a ban on the group. Protesters said they would defy the order, arguing legal changes did not affect their principles.

stories.title: Nigeria convicts 386 Islamist militants in mass trials
stories.summary: Nigeria convicted 386 Islamist militants in mass trials held in the capital Abuja this week, the country's Attorney General announced on Friday, April 11. The proceedings represent one of the largest batches of militant convictions in recent Nigerian history.

stories.title: DM Fedorov discusses defense cooperation priorities with Norwegian counterpart
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov met with Norwegian Defense Minister Tore Sandvik to discuss defense cooperation priorities.

stories.title: Iranian rabbi describes Israel’s destruction of a Tehran synagogue
stories.summary: An Iranian rabbi reported that one of Tehran's few remaining synagogues was destroyed in an Israeli military strike. The rabbi described being informed of the destruction of the religious site in the Iranian capital.

stories.title: Direct talks begin between US, Iran delegations in Islamabad: state media
stories.summary: Direct negotiations between US and Iranian delegations began in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Pakistani mediation. The US side is led by Vice President JD Vance, joined by Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, while Iran's delegation is headed by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The talks follow a two-week halt in US-Israeli military operations against Iran.

stories.title: LIVE: Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov – heavyweight boxing match
stories.summary: Heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury faced Arslanbek Makhmudov in a boxing match held in London. The event featured a full main card with live coverage and analysis.

stories.title: Ukraine can play useful role in Strait of Hormuz, Britain says
stories.summary: Britain's armed services minister said Ukraine could play a useful role in international efforts to secure the Strait of Hormuz, praising Ukrainian drone technology as among the best in the world. The statement was made in Kyiv on April 11.

stories.title: Iranian state media reports: US-Iran talks over, more likely held tonight or tomorrow
stories.summary: The first phase of US-Iran talks in Islamabad concluded, with delegations exchanging written texts to confirm agreements reached. Pakistan pushed to extend negotiations for at least another day, but had not yet succeeded in doing so.

stories.title: Watch: Who is Amit Kshatriya, the mind behind NASA’s Moon programme?
stories.summary: Indian-American scientist Amit Kshatriya serves as NASA's Associate Administrator overseeing the Artemis programme, which aims to return humans to the Moon. He advanced through engineering and leadership roles at NASA, contributing to missions including Artemis I, and now plays a central role in planning future Moon and Mars exploration.

stories.title: Iranian spokesperson accuses US media of double standards
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei accused the US media of double standards, alleging that elements within the US policy and media space recommended assassinating Iranian negotiators if talks failed. He criticized what he called the normalization of extortion through threats of violence.

stories.title: SSU releases exclusive footage of latest prisoner exchange
stories.summary: The Security Service of Ukraine released footage of Ukrainian prisoners freed from Russian captivity during a prisoner exchange conducted on Saturday, April 11.

stories.title: Northern Israel hit with barrage of Hezbollah rockets, drones, one building damaged
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched a barrage of rockets and five drones into northern Israel, with one building in Shlomi sustaining minor damage. Magen David Adom emergency teams responded to the incident.

stories.title: Bilawal terms Islamabad Talks ‘biggest achievement so far’ in de-escalation efforts between US, Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan People's Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari described the US-Iran talks in Islamabad as the "biggest achievement so far" in de-escalation efforts. Speaking to Al Jazeera, he noted that Pakistan brokered a two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran that enabled the negotiations to take place.

stories.title: French man charged with keeping nine-year-old son locked in van since 2024
stories.summary: French police rescued a malnourished nine-year-old boy who had been locked in his father's van since 2024 in the village of Hagenbach in eastern France, near the Swiss and German borders. A neighbour alerted authorities after hearing sounds of a child coming from the vehicle. The father has been charged.

stories.title: Americans weigh in on the Iran war, gas prices and their fears
stories.summary: After six weeks of war with Iran that jolted global energy markets, Americans are grappling with the conflict's impact on fuel prices and the broader economy. A fragile ceasefire is in place, but public anxiety persists over potential escalation and economic consequences.

stories.title: US military says two of its warships passed through Hormuz to remove mines
stories.summary: The US military said two warships passed through the Strait of Hormuz as part of a mission to remove sea mines placed by Iran. CENTCOM Admiral Brad Cooper said they were establishing a safe passage to restore the free flow of commerce through the vital waterway.

stories.title: Israel kidnaps three people in latest raid on south Syria
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted raids in southern Syria and abducted three civilians, escalating ground incursions in the area.

stories.title: Gaza families mourn loved ones killed in overnight Israeli air strikes
stories.summary: Families in Gaza mourned relatives killed in overnight Israeli air strikes. At least seven people were killed, and families gathered outside a Gaza hospital over the bodies of the deceased.

stories.title: Iran: a mediator on the mediations
stories.summary: Gavin Lee interviewed Oliver McTernan, Director of Forward Thinking, about the current situation involving Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, and Pakistan's mediating role. The discussion focused on ongoing diplomatic efforts and regional tensions.

stories.title: U.S. and Iran envoys meet Pakistani PM as negotiations get under way
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and US Vice President JD Vance each met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad as negotiations between the US and Iran got under way. Both delegations arrived at the venue for talks aimed at addressing the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Trump 'praises Allah again' in post boasting Iran's destruction
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted a message invoking praise to Allah while boasting about destruction inflicted on Iran. It was the second time Trump used the phrase, having previously done so when demanding Iran open the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukrainian General Staff: Ceasefire regime introduced at front for Easter holidays
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi, on orders from President Volodymyr Zelensky, directed Ukraine's Defense Forces to observe a ceasefire on land, sea, and air during the Easter holiday period.

stories.title: US-Iran talks hit ‘stalemate’ over Strait of Hormuz, FT reports
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad hit a stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Financial Times. Closed-door talks resumed after a dinner break, following an initial round that lasted just under two hours.

stories.title: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian in raid on West Bank village
stories.summary: Israeli settlers killed a 23-year-old Palestinian during a raid on a village in the occupied West Bank. The incident occurred amid a broader surge in settler violence across the territory.

stories.title: Police arrest protesters opposing Palestine Action ban in London
stories.summary: London police arrested protesters demonstrating against the UK government's ban on Palestine Action. The direct-action group was proscribed as a terrorist organisation by British authorities in July 2025.

stories.title: Amnesty calls for funds for Sudan as war nears 3rd anniversary
stories.summary: Amnesty International called on global governments to increase funding for Sudan as the country's war approached its third anniversary. NGOs reported being unable to assist desperate populations due to severe funding cuts.

stories.title: Five more killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed at least five people in Tefahta, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Additional air strikes hit the towns of Seddiqine, Tibnin, and Dibbine. Earlier attacks on Nabatieh city killed 10 people, including three emergency workers.

stories.title: U.S. official denies report Washington agreed to unfreeze Iran assets
stories.summary: A US official denied reports that Washington had agreed to unfreeze Iranian assets as part of negotiations. Iran had previously stated that any permanent ceasefire agreement must include the unfreezing of sanctioned assets and an end to Israel's military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iranian source says US has agreed to unfreeze Iranian funds, Washington denies it
stories.summary: An Iranian source claimed the United States has agreed to unfreeze Iranian funds as a sign of seriousness in reaching a deal during talks in Pakistan. Washington denied the claim. The dispute emerged as US-Iran negotiations were underway in Islamabad.

stories.title: Tankers exit Gulf via Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran talks begin
stories.summary: Three supertankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran talks began in Islamabad. The transit signaled a possible easing of the blockade following the US-Iran ceasefire and ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Trump says empty tankers heading to U.S. to load up with oil and gas
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed that empty tankers were heading to the United States to load oil and gas. The statement came as senior US and Iranian officials met on April 11, 2026, in Islamabad with Pakistani intermediaries for ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: US authorities launch new effort to uncover birth tourism schemes
stories.summary: The Trump administration launched a Birth Tourism Initiative, directing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents nationwide to investigate networks that allegedly help pregnant foreign nationals enter the US to secure citizenship for their children. The effort was outlined in an internal ICE email reviewed by Reuters.

stories.title: Ukraine proposes Norway access to its drone war secrets
stories.summary: Ukraine offered its NATO partners access to battle-proven drone warfare technology ahead of a Ramstein meeting. The proposal positioned Ukraine as bringing both requests and valuable military capabilities to the table.

stories.title: Russian forces carry out 50 attacks since start of day, fiercest fighting in Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors
stories.summary: Russian troops launched 50 attacks on Ukrainian positions since the start of the day, with the most intense fighting reported in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors.

stories.title: Vigil held in Madrid for victims of Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Dozens of people gathered in Madrid, Spain, for a vigil honoring victims of Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon. The demonstration expressed solidarity with those affected by the strikes.

stories.title: Israel lashes out at South Korean leader over Palestine posts
stories.summary: Israel criticized South Korean President Lee Jae Myung after he highlighted the treatment of Palestinians and called on Israeli leaders to reflect on their actions.

stories.title: From Vilna to Eretz Yisrael: One Holocaust survivor's journey to Israel
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Dov Levin escaped the Kovno Ghetto in Lithuania, fought as a partisan, and crossed war-torn Europe alone to reach Israel. He documented his journey from Vilna through loss and resilience.

stories.title: Gaza fibreglass homes aim to offer more 'dignity' for displaced
stories.summary: Aid workers in Gaza began constructing fibreglass homes to provide shelter and dignity for displaced families. Nearly two million people in the territory remained in dire humanitarian conditions.

stories.title: Ceasefire brings some relief for Iranians but economic outlook remains grim
stories.summary: Economic activity in Tehran's Grand Bazaar has increased somewhat following a ceasefire, but vendors report that sales remain sluggish. Iranians expressed some relief at the halt in hostilities, though the broader economic outlook remains bleak.

stories.title: Iraq parliament elects Kurdish politician Nizar Amedi as president
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament elected Kurdish politician Nizar Amedi as the country's new president after he secured 227 votes. The election ended five months of political deadlock, and Amedi pledged an 'Iraq First' agenda.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine trade drone strikes ahead of Easter truce
stories.summary: Russia launched at least 160 drones at Ukraine ahead of a proposed Orthodox Easter truce, killing four people in eastern and southern regions. Both sides exchanged drone strikes as tensions persisted despite the planned ceasefire.

stories.title: Artemis II: Space race heats up with China
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission marks the first time in over 50 years that humans have ventured near the Moon, intensifying the space competition between the United States and China over lunar exploration ambitions.

stories.title: Young Palestinian man shot dead in Israeli settler attack
stories.summary: A 23-year-old Palestinian man, Ali Majed Hamadneh, was shot dead by Israeli settlers during an attack on the village of Deir Jarir, east of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank. Armed settlers, reportedly under Israeli army protection, opened fire on residents.

stories.title: Iraq elects Kurdish politician Nizar Amidi as president amid war fallout
stories.summary: The Iraqi parliament elected Kurdish politician Nizar Amedi as the country's new president on Saturday, amid ongoing regional instability from the wider war.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz leverage looms over US-Iran talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials held their first direct talks since 1979 in Islamabad, Pakistan. Negotiations centered on the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil transit route, which remained a key point of contention between the two sides.

stories.title: Macron tells Iranian president ceasefire must be ‘fully respected’ and include Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron spoke with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and urged that the US-Iran ceasefire be fully respected and extended to include Lebanon. Macron also called on Iran to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukraine could play useful role in Strait of Hormuz, UK minister says
stories.summary: A UK minister suggested that Ukraine, with its advanced drone technologies, could contribute to international security efforts in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Fuel tankers regain access to Irish oil refinery
stories.summary: Fuel tankers regained access to an Irish oil refinery after demonstrations over high fuel prices disrupted traffic on several roads. The price increases were linked to the impact of the US-Israeli war against Iran.

stories.title: US clearing out Strait of Hormuz, Trump claims as Iran threatens to attack unauthorized ships
stories.summary: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers passed through the Strait of Hormuz in what officials described as a freedom-of-navigation mission. President Trump claimed the US was clearing the strait, while Iran threatened to attack unauthorized vessels.

stories.title: Ukraine’s general who lost Siversk just said what few commanders ever admit
stories.summary: A Ukrainian general publicly acknowledged the loss of the city of Siversk, making a rare admission of battlefield defeat. The statement drew attention for its unusual candor among military commanders.

stories.title: 'The Last Cedar of Lebanon': A play exploring war’s lasting scars
stories.summary: Playwright Aïda Asgharzadeh's latest work, The Last Cedar of Lebanon, examines how war and geopolitical upheaval affect individuals across generations. The play follows her earlier acclaimed production Persian Dolls, which explored dissidence and exile between Iran and France.

stories.title: US and Iran hold talks in Islamabad as Pakistan seeks to broker peace deal
stories.summary: Senior U.S. and Iranian officials held direct face-to-face peace talks in Islamabad on April 11, mediated by Pakistan, marking the highest-level meeting between the two countries since 1979. U.S. Vice President JD Vance led the American delegation, while Iran's parliamentary speaker headed the Iranian side.

stories.title: Kuwait reports no threats in airspace in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Kuwait's Centre for Government Communication reported no airspace threats in the past 24 hours as US-Iran peace talks continued in Islamabad. Earlier in the week, Kuwait reported Iranian attacks that damaged power, desalination, and oil facilities.

stories.title: Iran moves to impose Strait of Hormuz fees under new law
stories.summary: Iran's parliament advanced a new law to impose transit fees in rials on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. US President Trump warned against the move.

stories.title: What are the main talking points at the US-Iran negotiations in Pakistan?
stories.summary: Key issues at the US-Iran negotiations in Pakistan include Iran's demand for a ceasefire in Lebanon, where Israeli attacks have killed nearly 2,000 people. The talks in Islamabad aim to address broader regional conflict dynamics beyond the direct US-Iran war.

stories.title: At 78, is Israel really an independent state? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece questioned Israel's independence at age 78, reflecting on the experience of spending Passover in bomb shelters and debating the meaning of freedom under such conditions.

stories.title: Iranian president says delegation ‘a staunch guardian of Iran’s interests’
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian expressed support for Iran's negotiating delegation in Islamabad, stating they would defend national interests with courage. He pledged that regardless of the outcome, his government would continue serving the Iranian people.

stories.title: Fire engulfs Russia’s strategic rear: Ukraine hit fuel, ammo, and drone command all in one night
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck Russian fuel depots, ammunition stores, and a drone command center in a single overnight operation. The attacks were aimed at degrading frontline coordination and disrupting Russian logistics networks.

stories.title: A shattered covenant: Israel’s lone soldiers and the broken promise of care
stories.summary: An article examined the case of Joshua Boone, a lone soldier who served 748 days in the Gaza war, raising questions about whether Israel fulfilled its duty of care to soldiers who served on its behalf.

stories.title: US state department revokes green cards of three Iranian nationals it links to regime
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department revoked the green cards of three Iranian nationals with family ties to Iranian military and regime officials. Federal agents arrested the three, including the son of an Iranian revolutionary linked to the 1979 hostage crisis.

stories.title: US and Iran hold direct talks in Pakistan to end war
stories.summary: Senior US and Iranian officials met in Islamabad for the highest-level direct talks between the two nations in 50 years. Vice President JD Vance, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner met with Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with Pakistan's army chief present.

stories.title: Witkoff and Kushner join Vance for first in-person talks with Iran
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance, envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner represented the US in face-to-face peace talks with Iran in Islamabad, the first such meeting since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The three-way negotiations included Pakistan and aimed to end the six-week war.

stories.title: IDF and Hezbollah trade strikes, rockets as Israel and Lebanon gear up for direct talks
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported striking over 200 targets in Lebanon in a single day, with two soldiers wounded in south Lebanon combat. Hezbollah launched rockets and drones in response, as 10 Lebanese were reported killed. Both Israel and Lebanon were preparing for direct talks.

stories.title: In new war with Israel, Hezbollah defies notion that it was crippled
stories.summary: Hezbollah has demonstrated continued military capability in renewed fighting with Israel, defying assessments that the group had been significantly weakened. Lebanese and Israeli military officials report the group now largely relies on makeshift, low-cost drones.

stories.title: Djibouti president wins election with 97.8% of vote, state media says
stories.summary: Djibouti's President Ismael Omar Guelleh won re-election with 97.8% of the vote, according to state media on Saturday. The victory gives him a sixth term, extending his 27-year rule over the strategically located East African nation.

stories.title: Britain shelves handover of Chagos Islands, which host military base, after Trump criticism
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has shelved its plan to hand over the Chagos Islands, which host a joint US-UK military base on Diego Garcia. The decision follows criticism from US President Donald Trump, who in January called the deal an act of "great stupidity" by London.

stories.title: Watch: Global oil crisis: Why is India’s transport sector far more exposed than China’s?
stories.summary: A comparison of India and China reveals sharply different vulnerabilities to the Middle East-driven oil price surge of nearly 67% in one month. China's rapid adoption of electric vehicles has reduced its transport sector's fossil fuel dependence, while India remains overwhelmingly reliant on petrol and diesel.

stories.title: Russia-Ukraine Orthodox Easter ceasefire begins
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to observe a temporary ceasefire for Orthodox Easter. The truce took effect as US-led diplomatic efforts to negotiate a lasting end to the war remained stalled.

stories.title: Lubinets reports on health condition of Ukrainians released from Russian captivity
stories.summary: Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets reported on the health of seven Ukrainian men released from Russian captivity. The men had been abducted by Russian forces in 2022 from the Kharkiv, Kyiv, Kherson, and Donetsk regions.

stories.title: US V-P J.D. Vance emerges as Trump’s Iran closer, a task fraught with risk
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance is leading negotiations with Iran in Islamabad, positioning himself as a key diplomatic figure in the Trump administration. A successful outcome could bolster his international credibility ahead of a potential 2028 presidential bid, though the task carries significant risks.

stories.title: US military begins clearing Strait of Hormuz, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump announced that the U.S. military has begun clearing the Strait of Hormuz. Reports on Saturday confirmed the presence of U.S. Navy ships operating in the strait.

stories.title: Iran's new Supreme Leader has severe and disfiguring wounds, sources say
stories.summary: Sources report that Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei sustained severe facial disfigurement and significant leg injuries in an attack on the Supreme Leader's compound in central Tehran. Three sources confirmed the extent of his wounds.

stories.title: Iraq’s militia state: Shelly Kittleson’s kidnapping exposes who runs Baghdad
stories.summary: Journalist Shelly Kittleson's kidnapping in Baghdad highlighted the influence of Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) over the country's governance. Since October 2023, PMF-affiliated forces have conducted attacks against US personnel and positions in Iraq.

stories.title: Machete-wielding man killed by police in New York’s Grand Central station
stories.summary: A man armed with a machete attacked passengers at New York's Grand Central station, wounding three elderly victims. Police fatally shot the attacker, and authorities said they were continuing to investigate the incident.

stories.title: U.K. pauses its plan to cede Chagos Islands after U.S. opposition
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has paused its plan to hand over the Chagos Islands following US opposition. Under the existing deal, Britain would retain control of the strategically important Diego Garcia military base on a 99-year lease preserving US operations there.

stories.title: Beirut airport remains operational despite Israeli bombings
stories.summary: Beirut's airport remains operational despite nearby Israeli airstrikes, functioning at reduced capacity through close coordination with international parties and security guarantees.

stories.title: ‘Stepping stone toward durable peace’: PM Shehbaz meets US VP Vance as Islamabad Talks commence
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met US Vice President JD Vance in Islamabad for talks aimed at achieving durable peace in the region and potentially ending the war against Iran. Vance was accompanied by Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes before temporary ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes before a temporary Orthodox Easter ceasefire that began on Saturday. The Kremlin ordered a 32-hour truce starting at 4 PM Moscow time, one week after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed a holiday halt to hostilities.

stories.title: Russians attack minibus and car with drones in Kherson, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a minibus and a private car with drones in Kherson, Ukraine, injuring three people. Both public and private transport were targeted in the attack.

stories.title: Americans weigh in on the Iran war, gas prices, their fears
stories.summary: Reuters interviewed 16 Americans across Indiana, New York, California, Georgia, and Colorado about their views on the Iran war. Respondents shared concerns about gas prices and personal fears amid rapidly shifting news and political divisions.

stories.title: US-Iran officials meet in Islamabad as Tehran outlines terms for talks - report
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials met in Islamabad with Pakistani mediators facilitating the discussions. Tehran outlined its red lines, including demands regarding control of the Strait of Hormuz, the release of frozen assets, and a regional ceasefire.

stories.title: Israel army says hit over 200 Hezbollah targets in last 24 hours
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported striking over 200 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon within 24 hours, sending smoke over border villages. The strikes coincided with the start of U.S.-Iran peace talks, though Tehran stated it would not negotiate until Israel stops its bombing campaign in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran, US top officials meet face-to-face
stories.summary: Senior U.S. and Iranian officials met face-to-face in Pakistan on Saturday for direct negotiations. The talks came days after a fragile two-week ceasefire was announced, as the conflict—now in its seventh week—has killed thousands and disrupted global markets.

stories.title: Explosion incident near Serbian gas pipeline shows signs of Russian provocation – military expert
stories.summary: An explosion incident near the Balkan Stream gas pipeline in Serbia is suspected to be a Russian intelligence provocation ahead of Hungary's election. Military experts noted the amount of explosives found would have been insufficient to disable the pipeline, which carries Russian gas to Serbia and Hungary.

stories.title: Iran pays tribute to schoolchildren victims at truce talks
stories.summary: The Iranian delegation at the Islamabad truce talks paid tribute to dozens of schoolchildren killed in a US bombing of a school in the town of Minab.

stories.title: Three wounded in stabbing attack at New York’s Grand Central subway station
stories.summary: A man stabbed three people on a subway platform at New York City's Grand Central station before being shot by police. The three victims were hospitalized in stable condition, while the suspect was reported in critical condition.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Swap Hundreds of Prisoners Ahead of Easter Truce
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged 175 servicemen each in a prisoner swap facilitated by the United Arab Emirates ahead of an Easter truce. The Russian Defence Ministry confirmed the exchange.

stories.title: Israel says it attacked more than 200 sites in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it struck more than 200 Hezbollah sites in Lebanon over 24 hours and vowed to continue targeting Hezbollah infrastructure in the south. The Lebanese health ministry reported 10 people killed, including three emergency workers in Nabatieh.

stories.title: Vance joins Iranians in Islamabad for peace talks overshadowed by mutual mistrust
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance joined Iranian officials in Islamabad for peace talks marked by deep mutual mistrust. The two sides remain far apart on key issues, including the status of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: In Ethiopia, fuel prices overshadow this year's Easter celebrations
stories.summary: Millions of Ethiopians marked Good Friday in Addis Ababa amid chronic fuel shortages and rising commodity costs linked to the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: From allies to adversaries: US-Iran relations since 1979
stories.summary: The United States and Iran, adversaries since the 1979 Islamic revolution and embassy hostage crisis in Tehran, are set to hold talks in Islamabad. The negotiations aim to end more than a month of war in the Middle East as a fragile ceasefire holds amid deep mutual mistrust.

stories.title: CNN: China preparing to supply weapons to Iran, US says
