stories.summary: US intelligence indicated that China was preparing to supply air defence systems to Iran, potentially through third countries, according to CNN. The reports emerged as high-stakes US-Iran negotiations were underway in Islamabad.

stories.title: Hungry Fury ‘light and lean’ for heavyweight comeback fight with Makhmudov
stories.summary: Tyson Fury weighed in lighter than his previous bout for his heavyweight comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov, though he still came in three pounds heavier than his opponent.

stories.title: Christians return to Jerusalem’s Holy Sepulchre as Israel eases restriction
stories.summary: Orthodox Christians celebrated the Holy Fire ceremony at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem after Israel eased access restrictions. The event marked a return of worshippers to the site for Easter observances.

stories.title: Suspect arrested after Molotov cocktail attack at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home
stories.summary: San Francisco police arrested a 20-year-old suspect for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's home in the North Beach neighborhood and making threats near the company's headquarters. The incendiary device was thrown at approximately 4:12 AM, and the suspect was detained about an hour later.

stories.title: 300 convictions: Nigeria sees mass trial for terrorism suspects
stories.summary: A court in Abuja, Nigeria, convicted more than 300 terrorism suspects over a four-day mass trial.

stories.title: Aurangzeb departs for US to participate in IMF-WB meetings
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb departed for Washington, DC, on Saturday to attend the World Bank and IMF Spring Meetings 2026, scheduled for April 13–18. He is expected to participate in over 50 high-level engagements amid heightened global economic uncertainty.

stories.title: Zelensky: 182 Ukrainians return from Russian captivity
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the return of 182 Ukrainians from Russian captivity, including 175 military personnel and 7 civilians. The release was carried out as part of a prisoner exchange.

stories.title: Shin Bet chief said to downplay Jewish terrorism in West Bank as ‘friction’
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet chief reportedly downplayed settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank, characterizing it as friction rather than terrorism. The unit tasked with countering such attacks was said to be in crisis, with former security officials calling for urgent action.

stories.title: Trump says 'sea mines' in Strait of Hormuz are remaining Iranian threat
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Iran's remaining threat consists of sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump announced the US would begin clearing the strait, criticizing other nations including China, Japan, South Korea, France, and Germany for not undertaking the effort themselves.

stories.title: Fish and vegetarianism major flashpoints in India’s West Bengal election
stories.summary: In India's West Bengal state, fish and vegetarianism have become major campaign issues ahead of elections on April 23 and 29. Fish holds deep cultural significance for Bengalis, and the debate has turned the dietary staple into a political flashpoint.

stories.title: Russian Memorial human rights NGO labeled 'extremist'
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court designated the human rights organization Memorial as "extremist," a move experts describe as a new level of domestic repression.

stories.title: Israel blows up building in Tulkarm as settler rampage continues
stories.summary: Israeli forces demolished a building in the Tulkarm refugee camp in the occupied West Bank. The operation occurred amid an escalation of settler attacks across the West Bank, with arrests and injuries reported.

stories.title: Nearly 400 sentenced in Nigeria for links to militant Islamists
stories.summary: Courts in Nigeria sentenced nearly 400 individuals with links to militant Islamist groups, handing down penalties ranging from five years to life imprisonment in mass trials.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire: Can pressure, incentives, and risks deliver a final deal
stories.summary: US-Iran ceasefire negotiations continued amid questions about whether pressure and incentives could produce a final deal. Factors including Vice President Vance's team, US midterm politics, energy market risks, and Tehran's pursuit of sanctions relief shaped the talks.

stories.title: Ukrainian civilians abducted, tortured in Russian prisons
stories.summary: Russia has held thousands of Ukrainian civilians in detention for years in violation of international humanitarian law. Families have sought their release, some for more than a decade.

stories.title: US and Iranian delegations holding direct talks in same room
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations engaged in direct negotiations in the same room in Islamabad, with Pakistani mediators present. The main delegations were expected to remain for one day, with lower-level diplomatic talks continuing afterward.

stories.title: John Kerry says Netanyahu lobbied for Iran strike for decades
stories.summary: Former US Secretary of State John Kerry stated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had lobbied multiple US presidents for decades to strike Iran. Kerry said Donald Trump was the only president to agree to such action.

stories.title: Russians drop FAB-250 on central Kramatorsk, wounding 10
stories.summary: The Russian military carried out an airstrike on central Kramatorsk on Saturday morning, dropping a FAB-250 bomb that injured 10 people. The strike hit the city center of the Donetsk region city.

stories.title: Lebanon mourns security forces killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Lebanon held funeral ceremonies for 13 members of its State Security agency who were killed in an Israeli strike. The event drew public mourning across the country.

stories.title: Syria says busts cell planning attack on 'religious figure'
stories.summary: Syrian authorities announced the arrest of five suspects accused of plotting a bomb attack against a religious figure in Damascus. Officials alleged the cell had links to Hezbollah and that the suspects had received military training abroad.

stories.title: Pakistan Defense Minister deletes anti-Israel post from X after diplomatic backlash
stories.summary: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif deleted a post on X that accused Israel of genocide after facing diplomatic backlash. Israeli officials had condemned the language as inflammatory and offensive.

stories.title: In pictures: Iran, US delegations accorded warm welcome upon arrival in Pakistan
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance arrived at Nur Khan Air Base in Pakistan on Saturday and was received by Pakistani Deputy PM Ishaq Dar, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. An Iranian delegation led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf also arrived in Islamabad for historic talks.

stories.title: Hungary votes Sunday: what could change if Viktor Orbán loses to Péter Magyar—and what may not
stories.summary: Hungary held national elections on April 12, with voters choosing between Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's 16-year incumbency and challenger Péter Magyar. Magyar's own record on Ukraine remained ambiguous despite his opposition positioning.

stories.title: Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has severe and disfiguring wounds, sources say
stories.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father as Iran's Supreme Leader, reportedly sustained severe facial and leg injuries in the February 28 air strike that killed former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

stories.title: Russia held them for years —Ukraine just brought home 182 prisoners, including Mariupol’s defenders
stories.summary: Ukraine secured the return of 182 prisoners from Russian captivity, including defenders of Mariupol. Among those released was a man who had been abducted while traveling to visit his father.

stories.title: US and Iran begin negotiations in Islamabad
stories.summary: Iranian and US delegations began formal negotiations in Islamabad, according to Iranian media. Iran's ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, questioned whether the US was negotiating in good faith and stated the talks aimed to end what he called an illegal war against Iran.

stories.title: Why the Nato alliance is not as likely to dissolve as Trump makes it seem
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the NATO alliance is more resilient than U.S. President Trump's rhetoric suggests, noting that mutual strategic dependencies between the United States and Europe sustain the partnership despite political tensions.

stories.title: Chinese crystal ‘paves way’ for GPS-free thorium clock navigation
stories.summary: Scientists in Xinjiang, China, developed the world's first crystal capable of producing ultraviolet light at 145.2 nanometres, a wavelength needed for future thorium nuclear clocks. Published in Advanced Materials, the fluorinated borate compound could enable ultra-precise portable clocks for navigation without GPS in submarines and deep-space probes.

stories.title: US-Iran talks begin in Pakistan; Tehran demands control of Hormuz, truce in Lebanon
stories.summary: US-Iran talks began in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Tehran demanding control over the Strait of Hormuz and a truce in Lebanon. US Vice President Vance warned that the American negotiating team would not be receptive if Iran attempted to exploit the process.

stories.title: Writing through war: Helping Israelis process trauma across generations - opinion
stories.summary: An Israeli writer described using writing as a means to process trauma during more than two years of conflict. The author reflected on how putting experiences into words provided comfort and clarity amid ongoing upheaval.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine will respond in kind if ceasefire is violated
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine would adhere to the ceasefire but would respond in kind to any violations. His remarks signaled Ukraine's commitment to the truce while maintaining a posture of readiness.

stories.title: Inside trauma: How AI is helping Israelis see the invisible wounds of war
stories.summary: Researcher Tal Pasternak Magnezi created AI-generated images to illustrate the psychological trauma experienced by Israelis affected by war. The project aims to visualize the often invisible symptoms of conflict-related trauma.

stories.title: 19-year-old woman dies after being attacked by a dog in Essex
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman died after being attacked by a dog at a property in Essex, England. Police arrested a 37-year-old man on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control causing injury resulting in death.

stories.title: Mexico seeks to curb reliance on US gas
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced plans to use hydraulic fracturing to reduce Mexico's dependence on US natural gas amid the Iran war. She characterized the approach as sustainable extraction, but affected communities continue to oppose fracking due to environmental and health concerns.

stories.title: Pakistan sends fighter jets to Saudi Arabia under defence pact
stories.summary: Pakistani fighter jets arrived in Saudi Arabia to bolster joint defence cooperation under a bilateral pact. The deployment follows recent regional attacks and coincides with ongoing US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Letters of love and survival: A Holocaust love story preserved at Yad Vashem
stories.summary: Yad Vashem has preserved letters exchanged by a young Orthodox Jewish couple in Hungary during the Holocaust. Their correspondence sustained them through forced labor, ghettos, escapes, and months in hiding.

stories.title: Erdogan and Macron discuss US-Iran ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and French President Emmanuel Macron discussed the US-Iran ceasefire talks in a phone call. Macron called on all parties to respect the ceasefire, including in Lebanon, and to uphold freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Pakistan's PM says he 'appreciated Iran's engagement'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed appreciation for Iran's engagement after meeting an Iranian delegation that included Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Sharif's office said Pakistan intended to continue its role as a mediator to promote regional and global peace.

stories.title: Global growth to suffer due to Middle East war: World Bank chief
stories.summary: World Bank President Ajay Banga warned that the Middle East war will have cascading effects on the global economy, even if the US-announced ceasefire holds. He estimated global growth could drop by 0.3 to 1 percentage point depending on the conflict's duration, with inflation potentially rising by 200 to 300 basis points.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire pauses war - nuclear, Hormuz, and Lebanon issues remain
stories.summary: A tentative US-Iran ceasefire has paused active hostilities, but major issues including Iran's nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz, and Lebanon remain unresolved. Israelis have expressed security concerns while Americans focus on disengagement.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi visits Southern Operational Zone, coordinates defense efforts
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief General Oleksandr Syrskyi visited the Southern Operational Zone to coordinate defense efforts with unit commanders. The visit focused on planning an effective active defense strategy in the region.

stories.title: Israel kills seven people in Gaza in new attack targeting police
stories.summary: At least seven people were killed in an Israeli airstrike targeting Palestinian police personnel in Gaza. The attack has been described as the latest violation of the ceasefire in the territory.

stories.title: US, Iran hold separate talks with Pakistan's PM ahead of negotiations
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials held separate meetings with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday ahead of formal negotiations. International media later reported that the two sides also began direct talks in the afternoon, amid a fragile ceasefire and continued fighting in Lebanon.

stories.title: US-Iran talks on ending war begin in Pakistan
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations began talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, to address the ongoing conflict. The negotiations are being mediated by Pakistan. Details of the agenda have not yet been disclosed.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine begin 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine began a 32-hour ceasefire on Saturday to mark Orthodox Easter, after President Vladimir Putin ordered the truce following a proposal by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Kyiv warned it would respond immediately to any Russian violations during the pause in fighting.

stories.title: Al Jazeera’s Diplomatic Editor outlines key issues in US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Al Jazeera's diplomatic editor James Bays outlined key sticking points ahead of the US-Iran meeting in Pakistan. The report identified unresolved issues expected to challenge negotiators as both sides prepared to engage.

stories.title: Dan Bilzerian, who says Judaism is ‘terrible’ and wants to ‘kill Israelis,’ runs for Congress
stories.summary: Social media influencer Dan Bilzerian announced a run for the US Congress. Bilzerian has made derogatory statements about Judaism and Israel and has declined to answer whether Adolf Hitler was antisemitic, while also minimizing the Holocaust to his 30 million followers.

stories.title: Tories would reinstate two-child benefit cap to fund defence, says Badenoch
stories.summary: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch announced plans to reinstate the two-child benefit cap and redirect savings toward what she called the biggest peacetime rearmament programme in British history. She criticized the current government for a lack of military readiness exposed by recent global events.

stories.title: US agrees to unfreeze Iranian funds in Qatar: report
stories.summary: The United States has reportedly agreed to unfreeze Iranian assets held in Qatar and other countries. The decision is linked to security arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Reiterated demand for Hasina extradition with India: Bangladesh Foreign Minister Rahman
stories.summary: Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman said Dhaka reiterated its demand for the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from India. Rahman indicated more meetings are planned ahead of PM Tarique Rahman's visit, while also discussing regional cooperation amid the West Asia crisis.

stories.title: Phone-a-friend: Mapping PM Shehbaz, DPM Dar’s call-a-thon leading up to the US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Since the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran on February 28, Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy PM Ishaq Dar conducted extensive phone diplomacy with Gulf, Iranian, and Western counterparts. Islamabad positioned itself as a diplomatic bridge between Washington and Tehran to facilitate ceasefire efforts.

stories.title: Israeli spy firm Black Cube involved in Cyprus corruption probe
stories.summary: Israeli private intelligence firm Black Cube, founded by former Israeli intelligence operatives, confirmed its involvement in a sting operation targeting officials and private interests in Cyprus. A senior aide to Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides resigned in January after a video surfaced showing him discussing investment projects.

stories.title: Boris Johnson visits Defense Forces positions in Zaporizhzhia sector of front
stories.summary: Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson visited positions held by Ukraine's 65th Brigade on the Zaporizhzhia sector of the front line.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Could Zimbabwe's Constitutional Changes Take It Back to the Mugabe Era?
stories.summary: Proposed constitutional changes in Zimbabwe could extend President Emmerson Mnangagwa's rule and alter leadership selection processes. Critics warn the amendments could push the country toward a one-party state reminiscent of the Robert Mugabe era by weakening democratic checks.

stories.title: In pictures: JD Vance greeted warmly by country’s leadership on arrival
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance was greeted upon arrival at Nur Khan Air Base by Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. Vance and his delegation are in Pakistan for historic talks with Iran's leadership.

stories.title: Video: JD Vance meets with Pakistani PM ahead of Iran talks
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad ahead of anticipated negotiations with Iran. The meeting took place as US officials prepared for possible direct talks with Iranian counterparts.

stories.title: Aurangzeb, Saudi counterpart discuss ‘strong bilateral relationship’, economic cooperation
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb saw off Saudi counterpart Mohammed bin Abdullah Al-Jadaan at Islamabad International Airport following a productive visit. The two ministers discussed bilateral relations and economic cooperation, with Aurangzeb expressing eagerness to meet again at the upcoming World Bank–IMF Spring Meetings in Washington.

stories.title: US intelligence indicates China preparing weapons shipment to Iran, CNN reports
stories.summary: According to a CNN report, U.S. intelligence suggests China is preparing to ship shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missile systems to Iran.

stories.title: US intelligence indicates China preparing weapons shipment to Iran, CNN reports
stories.summary: US intelligence indicates China is preparing to ship shoulder-fired anti-air missile systems to Iran, according to a CNN report. The potential weapons transfer could escalate the ongoing conflict and further complicate diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran.

stories.title: US Vice President JD Vance arrives in Islamabad for ‘make-or-break’ talks with Iran
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance and his delegation arrived in Islamabad for talks with Iran's leadership during a two-week ceasefire halt. The US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28, and Pakistan brokered a temporary ceasefire on April 8. The conflict had spread across the Middle East and disrupted global economies.

stories.title: Pope rejects US claim that God has picked a side in the Iran war
stories.summary: Pope Francis rejected the notion that God has chosen a side in the Iran war, without naming specific individuals. His remarks followed repeated comments from US President Donald Trump suggesting divine support for America's position in the conflict.

stories.title: Drone strike kills man in Nikopol
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes hit the city of Nikopol in Ukraine, killing a 67-year-old man.

stories.title: Iran's supreme leader has severe and disfiguring wounds: report
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is reportedly recovering from severe and disfiguring injuries sustained in an airstrike that killed his father. Questions are growing over his capacity to lead the country.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill 10 in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed 10 people on Saturday, according to the Lebanese health ministry. Three of the strikes hit Nabatieh city, killing three emergency workers. The ministry condemned what it called Israel's systematic targeting of emergency personnel.

stories.title: Man arrested on suspicion of murder after death of 21-year-old in Primrose Hill
stories.summary: Metropolitan Police arrested a 27-year-old man on suspicion of murder in connection with the fatal stabbing of 21-year-old Finbar Sullivan in Primrose Hill, north-west London. A second man, aged 25, was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. Sullivan was stabbed on Tuesday evening and pronounced dead at the scene.

stories.title: US push to counter hackers draws industry deeper into offensive cyber debate
stories.summary: The White House is expanding the market for offensive cyber capabilities, increasingly involving private-sector companies in that ecosystem. Policy boundaries governing the use of such tools remain unclear.

stories.title: Pakistani fighter jets land in Saudi Arabia as part of defence pact
stories.summary: Pakistani fighter jets and support aircraft landed at King Abdulaziz Air Base in Saudi Arabia under a bilateral defence pact signed in September. The Saudi defence ministry said the deployment aimed to strengthen military coordination and enhance operational readiness between the two countries.

stories.title: Makeshift Gaza university offers chance to resurrect academic studies
stories.summary: A makeshift, solar-powered university has been established in Gaza to provide academic opportunities for students affected by the war. The facility aims to help students resume their studies despite widespread destruction and limited resources.

stories.title: Lebanese, Israeli ambassadors hold call, set date for talks
stories.summary: The Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors to the United States held a phone call and agreed to meet in Washington on Tuesday for direct talks. The diplomatic engagement comes as Israel continues deadly military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: ‘A perfect mission’: NASA celebrates as Artemis II astronauts return to Earth
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission concluded as all four astronauts returned to Earth and were recovered after splashdown. The crew members were able to walk unassisted upon reaching the recovery ship. NASA hopes to land astronauts on the lunar surface as early as 2028.

stories.title: Democrats urged to reclaim anti-war identity amid Trump’s assault on Iran
stories.summary: Following President Trump's threat on Truth Social to destroy Iranian civilization, Democrats called for his removal from office and debated reclaiming an anti-war stance. Progressives within the party see the US-Iran conflict as an opportunity to reorient American foreign policy away from military interventionism.

stories.title: Workers at LA stadium threaten World Cup strike amid anger over ICE
stories.summary: The Unite Here hospitality union, representing about 2,000 workers at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, threatened to strike during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The union demanded improved working conditions and urged FIFA to prevent Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents from operating near matches.

stories.title: ‘A big deal’: the military drills showing Tokyo’s growing focus on deterring China
stories.summary: Japan participated in the annual US-Philippine Salaknib military exercise on Luzon island, involving over 7,000 American and Philippine soldiers. Analysts described Tokyo's involvement as significant, reflecting Japan's expanding role in regional security groupings oriented toward deterring China.

stories.title: Russian forces attack two districts in Dnipropetrovsk region over 10 times, causing damage
stories.summary: The Russian military launched more than 10 drone and artillery strikes on two districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region since Friday evening, causing damage to the area.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange 175 prisoners of war each
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged 175 prisoners of war and seven civilians each on Saturday in a swap facilitated by the United Arab Emirates. The exchange marked a rare instance of cooperation between the two warring nations.

stories.title: US officials claim Iran unable to find mines it laid in strait of Hormuz, report says
stories.summary: US officials told the New York Times that Iran cannot locate all the mines it laid in the Strait of Hormuz because the explosives were dropped erratically and may not have been properly marked. Reopening the strait, a chokepoint for roughly one-fifth of global oil supply, is a primary US demand to end the war.

stories.title: ‘I wished for death’: Sexual violence in Israel’s prisons is an ‘organised state policy’
stories.summary: Palestinian former detainees have provided testimonies alleging systematic sexual violence, including rape, inside Israeli prisons such as Sde Teiman detention facility, describing the abuse as an organized policy approved at senior levels of Israeli leadership.

stories.title: Gucci shoes worth HK$11,000 stolen from shopping centre restroom in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong police are investigating the theft of a pair of Gucci shoes worth HK$11,000 from a restroom at Times Square shopping centre in Causeway Bay. The 48-year-old victim had purchased the shoes from the store and left them in the restroom, returning to find only the empty shoebox.

stories.title: US denies agreeing to unfreeze Iranian assets
stories.summary: A White House official denied reports that the United States agreed to unfreeze Iranian assets held in Qatar and other foreign banks, contradicting claims by a senior Iranian source cited by Reuters.

stories.title: Who is Iran's Chief negotiator Ghalibaf?
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf is leading a 70-member Iranian delegation in negotiations with the United States in Pakistan. A prominent non-clerical political figure in Iran, Ghalibaf has been tasked with securing an end to the war on terms acceptable to Tehran.

stories.title: Iran is prepared for a war lasting six months, but constraints will come from its population, China
stories.summary: Analysts assess that Iran is prepared to sustain a war lasting up to six months, but faces constraints from its own population and its relationship with China. If Iranian citizens come to believe the government is prolonging the conflict unnecessarily, public sentiment could turn against the authorities.

stories.title: Tel Aviv kindergarten director and husband arrested for sexual offenses against children
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a Tel Aviv kindergarten director and her husband on suspicion of committing sexual offenses against children at their unlicensed facility, following multiple complaints from parents.

stories.title: Russians booby-trap another street in Kherson
stories.summary: Russian forces have been recorded laying anti-personnel mines on another street in the Ukrainian city of Kherson, continuing a pattern of booby-trapping civilian areas.

stories.title: US to demand freeing of American detainees in Iran as part of Islamabad negotiations - report
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that the US delegation led by Vice President JD Vance plans to demand the release of American detainees held in Iran as part of the Islamabad negotiations. The priority level assigned to this demand remains unclear.

stories.title: World leaders push to save Iran talks amid Israel’s attacks in Lebanon
stories.summary: World leaders are working to preserve US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad as Israeli attacks in Lebanon threaten to derail the negotiations. President Trump's ceasefire with Iran appears at risk as discussions begin in Pakistan. The diplomatic efforts come amid heightened regional tensions.

stories.title: Can a lasting deal emerge from the Islamabad talks?
stories.summary: Analyst Shahir Shahidsaless writes that US President Donald Trump is the decisive factor in whether the Islamabad talks between the US and Iran can produce a durable agreement. A key test is whether Washington can pressure Israel to halt its strikes on Lebanon.

stories.title: Artemis II crew seen on recovery ship after moon mission return
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew was observed aboard a US Navy recovery ship after returning from a mission around the Moon. The four astronauts were assisted across the ship's deck following their splashdown.

stories.title: JD Vance meets Pakistani PM
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad amid ongoing US-Iran negotiations. It remained unclear whether the talks with Iran would be conducted face-to-face or indirectly through Pakistani mediators.

stories.title: Vaccine coverage gaps spur Bangladesh’s deadly measles outbreak
stories.summary: Bangladesh is experiencing its worst measles outbreak in years, with at least 143 deaths—mostly children—and over 12,000 suspected cases since March 15. Gaps in vaccine coverage have been identified as a key driver of the outbreak's severity.

stories.title: Drone targeted Shelly Kittleson, US diplomats at Baghdad airport
stories.summary: A drone crashed near US diplomats at Baghdad International Airport during an escort operation for freed American journalist Shelly Kittleson. Washington condemned the attack as part of an escalating pattern of strikes targeting US personnel in Iraq.

stories.title: China to join Pakistan-hosted US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: China announced it will join Pakistan-hosted peace talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad. Pakistan has been urging Tehran to drop preconditions and engage directly in negotiations.

stories.title: China targets middlemen in renewed crackdown on ‘hidden’ corruption
stories.summary: China's Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate jointly issued a judicial interpretation detailing how criminal law can be applied to corrupt middlemen. The guidance refines criteria for prosecuting intermediaries involved in bribery, targeting what authorities call "new and hidden forms of corruption."

stories.title: Russian forces shell seven settlements in Kharkiv region, killing one and wounding another
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled seven settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region over the past 24 hours, killing one person and wounding another.

stories.title: IDF removes clip of Passover song slammed as ‘medley of contempt’ for women in military
stories.summary: The Israeli military removed a Passover song clip produced by its rabbinate after widespread criticism that the song demeaned women in the military. The IDF stated the publication did not follow its guidelines.

stories.title: US agrees to unfreeze Iranian assets in foreign banks
stories.summary: A senior Iranian source told Reuters that the United States agreed to unfreeze Iranian assets held in foreign banks. Tehran characterized the move as a sign of Washington's seriousness during the Islamabad negotiations, linking the funds to safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US, Iran sit down for talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met US Vice President JD Vance in Islamabad as peace talks aimed at ending the expanding Middle East war commenced. The US delegation was set to meet Iranian officials later in the day, with Pakistan serving as host and mediator.

stories.title: Israel in row with South Korean leader over Palestinian abuse concerns
stories.summary: South Korean President expressed disappointment that Israel has not reflected on international criticisms regarding its treatment of Palestinians, sparking a diplomatic row between Seoul and Jerusalem.

stories.title: Thais celebrate new year despite fuel price shocks delaying travel
stories.summary: Thai travelers faced significantly higher fuel costs for holiday journeys home during new year celebrations, driven by surging fuel prices. Despite inflated fares, many at Bangkok's Mo Chit Two bus station said the opportunity to visit family made the extra expense worthwhile.

stories.title: US, Iran teams in Pakistan for peace talks but doubts emerge over Lebanon, sanctions
stories.summary: Senior U.S. and Iranian delegations gathered in Islamabad, Pakistan, on April 11 for negotiations aimed at ending their six-week-old conflict. However, Tehran cast doubt on the talks' progress by demanding prior commitments regarding Lebanon and sanctions relief before formal discussions could begin.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine set to begin Easter truce
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine are set to begin an Easter truce, with the Kremlin announcing that Defence Minister Andrei Belousov and army chief Valery Gerasimov have been instructed to cease hostilities in all directions during the period. The temporary halt in fighting applies across the front lines of the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Ten Indian nationals indicted in U.S. for visa fraud conspiracy
stories.summary: Ten Indian nationals have been indicted by a US federal grand jury on one count of conspiracy to commit visa fraud. The charges relate to a scheme involving staged armed robberies at convenience stores designed to facilitate fraudulent visa applications.

stories.title: Revamped Iranian leadership wary ahead of US peace talks
stories.summary: Iran's reconstituted senior leadership is reportedly cautious but inclined to pursue a truce and engage in peace talks with the United States.

stories.title: Revamped Iranian leadership wary ahead of US peace talks
stories.summary: Iran's revamped senior leadership is approaching US peace talks in Islamabad with caution but apparent willingness to pursue the truce. Analysts note reasons to believe Tehran's leadership wants to continue negotiations. The talks follow a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE updates: Vance warns Iran 'not to play us' ahead of Islamabad talks, Iran says 'lacks trust' with U.S.
stories.summary: The Iranian delegation arrived in Islamabad for peace talks with the United States, while US Vice President JD Vance was en route. Vance warned Iran 'not to play us,' and Iran's delegation expressed a lack of trust with the US. The talks are the first direct engagement since strikes began six weeks ago.

stories.title: Iranian vice president says US must avoid 'Israel First' agenda
stories.summary: Iranian Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref stated that the US must avoid an "Israel First" agenda during the Islamabad negotiations. He warned that prioritizing Israeli interests over American ones would result in no deal and a stronger Iranian defensive posture.

stories.title: German court upholds ban on protest against Israel’s ‘genocide’ at Buchenwald memorial
stories.summary: A German court upheld a ban on a pro-Palestinian protest planned at the Buchenwald Holocaust memorial site. The activist group "Kufiyas in Buchenwald" was ordered to hold its Sunday vigil in the nearby city of Weimar instead.

stories.title: Russian forces kill one civilian and wound three in Donetsk region over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian attacks in Ukraine's Donetsk region killed one civilian and wounded three others over the past 24 hours. The casualties resulted from ongoing Russian aggression targeting the region.

stories.title: Israel says ceasefire with Hezbollah not on the table
stories.summary: Israel announced it will not discuss a ceasefire with Hezbollah during upcoming talks with Lebanese diplomats in the United States. Israeli warplanes struck the towns of Jibchit, Kfar Sir, and Mayfadoun in southern Lebanon, killing at least three people in the Nabatieh district.

stories.title: Video: ‘Crucial talks’ says Al Jazeera reporter at US-Iran meeting venue
stories.summary: Officials from Iran and the United States began negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Pakistani officials serving as mediators in what observers described as crucial talks.

stories.title: Foreign Secretary Misri wraps up U.S. visit with talks to deepen nuclear ties, explore LPG exports
stories.summary: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri concluded a US visit focused on deepening bilateral nuclear ties and exploring US LPG exports to India. US Ambassador Sergei Gor stated Washington's readiness to cooperate on civil nuclear energy, coal gasification, and LPG trade.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP says Lebanon-Israel talks are 'blatant violation' of constitution
stories.summary: Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah condemned planned direct negotiations between Lebanon's government and Israel in Washington, calling them a violation of Lebanon's constitution and national pact. He warned the talks would deepen domestic divisions amid ongoing Israeli military operations.

stories.title: Still in shock, Beirut tries to heal after deadly Israeli attacks
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Hugo Bachega reported from Beirut, where residents are coping with the aftermath of deadly Israeli strikes earlier in the week. The attacks left parts of the Lebanese capital reeling.

stories.title: Can the Iran-US ceasefire produce a lasting deal?
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between Iran and the United States is being tested as analysts assess whether President Trump can pressure Israel to stop military strikes on Lebanon. The outcome is seen as critical to any lasting agreement emerging from the Islamabad talks.

stories.title: UK to hold off on deal ceding Chagos Islands amid US opposition
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has paused legislation to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands in the Indian Ocean to Mauritius, following opposition from the United States, which operates the Diego Garcia military base on the archipelago.

stories.title: Public holiday extended in Pindi; markets, fuel stations along key roads closed
stories.summary: Rawalpindi's district administration declared Saturday a public holiday due to security arrangements for the US-Iran dialogue taking place in nearby Islamabad. Markets and fuel stations along key roads were closed, extending earlier holiday declarations on April 9 and 10. Emergency departments and hospitals remained operational.

stories.title: Unearthing peace: ancient China gravesite reveals significance of broken weapons
stories.summary: Archaeologists in Shaanxi province, northwest China, uncovered a Western Zhou dynasty (1046–771 BC) gravesite containing individuals buried with deliberately broken weapons. Researchers announced the findings in mid-March, interpreting the custom as reflecting a yearning for peace among those acquainted with conflict.

stories.title: Turtle found dead after apparent fall in Hong Kong’s Wong Tai Sin
stories.summary: A 10-centimeter turtle was found dead after apparently falling from a height at No. 185 Hammer Hill Road in Hong Kong's Wong Tai Sin district. Police were alerted by a security guard on Saturday afternoon. In Hong Kong, animal cruelty is punishable by up to three years in jail and a HK$200,000 fine.

stories.title: PPP, Jamaat members clash with blows, kicks in Karachi City Council
stories.summary: A violent brawl erupted during a Karachi City Council session between members of the ruling Pakistan Peoples Party and opposition Jamaat-i-Islami over a seating dispute. Councillors exchanged punches, kicks, and hurled chairs at each other. The council passed 13 resolutions after JI staged a walkout.

stories.title: Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors hottest, 173 clashes reported in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 173 combat engagements with Russian troops along front lines over the past 24 hours on April 10. The Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors experienced the heaviest fighting.

stories.title: UK shelves Chagos Islands deal after Trump's criticism
stories.summary: The United Kingdom shelved legislation to transfer the Chagos Islands to Mauritius following criticism from US President Donald Trump. The islands host the Diego Garcia military base, which positions US bomber aircraft within range of Iran and requires UK authorization for use.

stories.title: An Orban loss in Hungary’s election could be the turning point Putin fears
stories.summary: Hungary's legislative elections on Sunday are being closely watched in Moscow, as PM Viktor Orban has been Russian President Putin's closest EU ally. A victory by Peter Magyar's opposition Tisza party could undermine Kremlin influence within the European Union.

stories.title: Inside the Sudanese army coalition split over Iran and the Muslim Brotherhood
stories.summary: Sudanese General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan condemned Iranian strikes under pressure from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Western nations, exposing a split within Sudan's army coalition over ties to Iran and the Muslim Brotherhood.

stories.title: Turkey, Somalia to start first offshore drilling project at Somalian coast
stories.summary: A Turkish drilling ship docked at the port of Mogadishu on Friday to begin Somalia's first offshore oil drilling project, a joint venture announced by both Turkey and Somalia.

stories.title: CM Sindh okays Rs9.98bn Phase-II of Karachi Safe City Project
stories.summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah approved Phase-II of the Karachi Safe City Project at an estimated cost of Rs9.98 billion. Work is expected to begin next month, with over 2,300 smart cameras to be installed across Karachi, excluding district Central. Authorities are also exploring expanding the surveillance network to other Sindh cities.

stories.title: Iranian delegation reaches Islamabad for peace talks with U.S. as world waits for deal to end conflict
stories.summary: Iran's delegation, led by Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Araghchi, arrived in Islamabad for peace talks with the United States. Iran's semi-official news agency reported that negotiations would not begin until preconditions were met. The talks aim to reinforce a fragile ceasefire and end hostilities.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine to begin Orthodox Easter truce
stories.summary: Russia declared a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire starting Saturday afternoon, and Ukraine said it was ready to reciprocate. However, Russian drone strikes killed at least two people in the Ukrainian port city of Odesa overnight, just hours before the truce was due to begin.

stories.title: Trump shares video of brutal Florida killing allegedly by Haitian immigrant
stories.summary: US President Trump shared a video on social media of a fatal attack at a Florida gas station convenience store, allegedly committed by a Haitian immigrant. The female clerk was killed outside the store, and the suspect was arrested the same day.

stories.title: Voices from the Arab press: Internal Arab fractures amid Iran war
stories.summary: Arab media outlets published a range of opinions and analyses highlighting internal fractures within the Arab world caused by the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: US President Trump projects cautious optimism ahead of Iran talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed cautious optimism ahead of indirect talks with Iran in Islamabad, noting his team of JD Vance, Steve, and Jared Kushner. Trump acknowledged the diplomatic process remains fragile while avoiding predictions about outcomes. The remarks came as he boarded Air Force One on Friday evening.

stories.title: Islamabad keyed up for ‘make-or-break’ talks
stories.summary: US-Iran dialogue is set to begin in Islamabad after a last-minute hurdle involving Israeli strikes in Lebanon was eased, with Tehran having conditioned its participation on a ceasefire there. Pakistan's backchannel diplomacy helped broker the talks, with an Iranian delegation and a US team led by Vice President Vance converging on the Pakistani capital. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called the negotiations a decisive moment for peace.

stories.title: Iran unable to find mines in Strait of Hormuz, US says
stories.summary: The United States claims Iran has been unable to locate and clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz, preventing the full reopening of the vital waterway. The mines were reportedly laid during the conflict, and Iran's difficulty in finding them has hampered efforts to restore normal shipping traffic through the critical oil transit route.

stories.title: Landlords of 5,557 subdivided homes seek 3-year grace period to fix flats
stories.summary: Landlords of 5,557 subdivided housing units across 1,370 flats in Hong Kong have applied for a three-year grace period to meet new size, safety, and hygiene requirements. Hong Kong Housing Secretary Winnie Ho said the units represent about 5% of all subdivided homes, mostly located in Yau Tsim Mong district.

stories.title: Explosives found near pipeline in Serbia probably ‘Russian provocation’, says expert
stories.summary: Approximately 4 kilograms of explosives found near the Balkan Stream gas pipeline in Kanjiža, Serbia, were likely insufficient to destroy the infrastructure, according to a former Ukrainian major general. The expert concluded the incident was probably a Russian intelligence provocation aimed at influencing Hungary's upcoming election.

stories.title: Foreign Minister Araghchi says Iran enters talks with 'complete distrust'
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told German counterpart Johann Wadephul that Iran enters the US talks with "complete distrust," citing previous American "betrayals of diplomacy." Araghchi pledged to fight for Iranian national interests and rights during the negotiations.

stories.title: Israel refuses ceasefire with Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israel refused to discuss a ceasefire with Hezbollah ahead of scheduled talks with Lebanon in Washington on Tuesday. Lebanese authorities report Israeli strikes have killed more than 1,950 people, including over 350 on the first day of the US-Iran ceasefire alone.

stories.title: Six wounded in Kherson region over past 24 hours in Russian attacks
stories.summary: Six civilians were injured in the Kherson region of Ukraine over the past 24 hours due to Russian attacks. The casualties resulted from ongoing Russian aggression targeting the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance arrived in Islamabad with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for peace talks with Iran. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf were received at Nur Khan Air Base by Pakistani officials including Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Army Chief Syed Asim Munir.

stories.title: Iran’s Mojtaba Khamenei suffers severe, disfiguring wounds, insiders report
stories.summary: Sources report that Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is recovering from severe, disfiguring injuries sustained in an airstrike that killed his father at the start of the war. He assumed the supreme leader role following his father's death.

stories.title: US says Iran lost track of mine locations spread in Strait of Hormuz, complicating reopening - NYT
stories.summary: The United States reports that Iran has lost track of the locations of naval mines it deployed in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the New York Times. The mines were laid by small boats without clear records of their placement, making the critical waterway nearly impossible to transit safely.

stories.title: US negotiators to leave Pakistan after Iran peace talks fail
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials held face-to-face talks in Pakistan — described as the most significant direct diplomatic engagement since 1979 — but US negotiators left after the peace talks failed to produce an agreement.

stories.title: US and Iran hold highest-level talks in decades in Pakistan
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials held face-to-face talks in Pakistan, marking the most significant diplomatic engagement between the two countries since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

stories.title: US–Iran talks begin in Pakistan amid uncertainty over Lebanon
stories.summary: Iran and the United States are scheduled to hold peace talks in Pakistan, though the two sides remain far apart on key demands. The negotiations take place amid significant uncertainty over the situation in Lebanon.

stories.title: Germany funds armored medevac fleet for Ukraine as one vehicle survives triple drone strike
stories.summary: Germany delivered five Mediguard armored medical evacuation vehicles to Ukraine's National Guard. One previously deployed unit survived three drone strikes with its crew uninjured, demonstrating the vehicle's protective capability.

stories.title: US intel said to assess Iran can recover underground launchers, fire thousands of missiles
stories.summary: US intelligence assessments indicate Iran could recover underground missile launchers and rebuild its capacity to fire thousands of ballistic missiles during the current truce. CNN separately reported that China is preparing to ship air defense systems to Iran.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s Cathay Pacific and HK Express cut some flights as jet fuel prices rise
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways announced it will cancel about 2% of its flights between mid-May and late June, mainly on regional routes plus some services to Australia, South Asia, and South Africa. The cuts are driven by surging jet fuel prices linked to the ongoing Middle East war. Budget arm HK Express is also affected.

stories.title: Hong Kong regulator urged to expand stablecoin rules after cautious roll-out
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority granted its first two stablecoin licences to HSBC and a Standard Chartered-led joint venture. Industry figures urged the regulator to loosen restrictions further, saying the cautious rollout of only two licences fell short of market expectations.

stories.title: High hopes
stories.summary: Pakistan is hosting US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad after brokering a two-week truce between the two nations. A security blanket has been placed over the federal capital and Rawalpindi for the high-stakes negotiations. The talks aim to transform the fragile ceasefire into a longer-term peace agreement amid deep mutual mistrust.

stories.title: Tver hears blasts, Krasnodar burns: Ukraine’s drones reach deep into Russian rear
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck deep into Russian territory overnight, with drone debris igniting a fire at an oil depot in Krymsk, Krasnodar Krai. Approximately 80 firefighters were deployed and contained the blaze by morning. Explosions were also reported in Russia's Tver region.

stories.title: Trump likes to back winners. Hungary’s upcoming election will test his clout
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has endorsed candidates in Hungary's upcoming election, breaking with the tradition of avoiding overt involvement in other nations' domestic politics. The vote is seen as a test of Trump's international political influence.

stories.title: McDonald’s CEO blames mother’s etiquette training for awkward burger bite in video
stories.summary: McDonald's CEO Chris Kempczinski attributed his awkward on-camera burger-eating style to his mother's etiquette advice about not talking with a full mouth. The February taste-test video drew widespread online mockery, prompting him to record another eating video.

stories.title: Air defense downs 133 of 160 Russian drones launched overnight
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 133 of 160 Russian drones launched in an overnight attack beginning on the evening of April 10. The drones were part of a large-scale Russian aerial assault on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: UN: Civilian casualties in Ukraine rose 49% in March, with small drones killing more people than any other weapon
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that civilian casualties in Ukraine rose 49% in March compared to February, with 211 civilians killed. Small drones were the deadliest weapon, responsible for 66 deaths — a 70% increase over March 2025.

stories.title: Hins Cheung to lead arrested 2019 Hong Kong protesters on mainland exchange trips
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Security Bureau launched a rehabilitation project for approximately 7,000 young people arrested during the 2019 anti-government protests. Cantopop singer Hins Cheung will lead participants on exchange trips to mainland China. Security Secretary Chris Tang said the project has been running for two years.

stories.title: Middle East war to cut growth, deliver cascading impact, World Bank chief says
stories.summary: The World Bank warned that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East is expected to reduce economic growth and produce cascading effects across the region. The institution also cautioned governments against establishing energy subsidies they cannot sustain financially.

stories.title: Iran, US delegations to start negotiations in Pakistan
stories.summary: A US government plane carrying top officials landed in Islamabad on Saturday for peace talks with Iran aimed at permanently ending the six-week-old war that has killed thousands across the Middle East. The negotiations mark a significant diplomatic effort hosted by Pakistan.

stories.title: At least seven Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out early-morning strikes in Gaza, hitting civilians in Bureij refugee camp and launching drone attacks on a tent in Khan Younis, killing at least seven Palestinians.

stories.title: Russian strikes in Sumy region injure 23 over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian strikes in Ukraine's Sumy region injured 23 people over the past 24 hours. The casualties resulted from ongoing Russian military aggression targeting the northeastern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Can World Bank and IMF leaders rescue a global economy on the brink?
stories.summary: The World Bank and IMF Spring Meetings beginning April 13 in Washington will address the economic fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran. The article questions whether the nearly 200 member countries can collectively counter the economic disruption caused by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: 2,500-year-old infant mass grave cracks open enigma of biblical-era baby burials
stories.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered a 2,500-year-old mass grave containing the remains of dozens of infants under age two in a water reservoir at an ancient Judean town, shedding light on biblical-era burial practices.

stories.title: Over 100,000 rally at Budapest megaconcert in call to vote out Hungary’s Orban on Sunday
stories.summary: Over 100,000 people rallied at a megaconcert in Budapest calling for the ouster of Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ahead of Hungary's Sunday election. Opposition leader Péter Magyar is considered the most credible challenger to Orbán's 16-year rule.

stories.title: PTI hails Pakistan’s role in bringing Iran, US to negotiating table
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf praised Pakistan's role in facilitating dialogue between Iran and the United States aimed at a negotiated settlement to the Middle East crisis. The party said the diplomatic effort reflects founder Imran Khan's philosophy of prioritizing peace over conflict and resolving disputes through dialogue.

stories.title: North Korean leader Kim backs China’s push for multipolar world in talks with Foreign Minister
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un expressed support for China's vision of a multipolar world during talks with China's Foreign Minister. Kim emphasized strengthening ties between North Korea and China in the current geopolitical climate and outlined Pyongyang's stance on regional and international issues.

stories.title: Hong Kong proposes mandatory renovation briefings to combat bid-rigging
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities proposed a legal amendment to the Building Management Ordinance requiring property owners to attend mandatory briefings on major renovation projects before voting on procurement. The measure, announced by Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak, aims to curb bid-rigging following a deadly fire in Tai Po.

stories.title: Middle East conflict derails Gilgit-Baltistan trophy hunting programme
stories.summary: Gilgit-Baltistan's 2025-26 trophy hunting programme suffered an estimated Rs250 million loss as permits for Markhor, blue sheep, and Himalayan ibex went unused due to the Middle East war. The cancellations were triggered by law-and-order concerns and regional tensions affecting international hunter participation during the November-to-April season.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court halts deportation of Afghans awaiting resettlement abroad
stories.summary: The Peshawar High Court temporarily restrained Pakistani law enforcement from deporting an Afghan family whose UNHCR-facilitated asylum case for resettlement in a third country is pending. The court issued notices to the interior ministry and other respondents. The petitioner is a former serviceman of the Afghan government ousted in 2021.

stories.title: Albanese didn’t return with shiploads of diesel. That doesn’t mean his Singapore visit wasn’t a success
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese visited Singapore to secure assurances on refined fuel supplies amid disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict. While he did not return with immediate diesel shipments, the visit yielded commitments that could prove significant if fuel supply constraints worsen.

stories.title: Russian military loses 1,440 soldiers and three air defense systems in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian forces lost 1,440 soldiers and three air defense systems in the past 24 hours of fighting in Ukraine. Total Russian combat losses since the February 2022 invasion have reached approximately 1,310,110 personnel as of April 11, 2026.

stories.title: Over 2,200 Indian Sikh pilgrims arrive for Baisakhi festival
stories.summary: Around 2,238 Sikh pilgrims from India arrived in Pakistan to participate in Baisakhi festivities, with grand arrangements and tight security at Nankana Sahib and Hasanabdal. More than 2,800 visas were issued to Indian pilgrims, and over 8,000 Sikhs worldwide were expected to attend. The Kartarpur Corridor remained closed from the Indian side.

stories.title: Pakistan calls for 'constructive talks' as delegations arrive in Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistan's foreign ministry confirmed the arrival of the US delegation in Islamabad for peace talks with Iran, calling for constructive negotiations. Vice President JD Vance, envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner represented the US side, while Iran's delegation included Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

stories.title: Is Iran Trump’s Suez crisis, or just a passing thunderstorm?
stories.summary: An opinion piece compares the US war on Iran to Britain's 1956 Suez crisis, suggesting America's global standing could suffer lasting damage. The analysis questions whether the conflict represents a pivotal decline or a temporary disruption for US influence in the Middle East.

stories.title: The winners from China’s growing intercity football rivalries may surprise you
stories.summary: The Jiangsu City Football League, known as the Su Super League, begins its 2026 season in eastern China's Jiangsu province. The amateur intercity tournament has generated significant public enthusiasm, with rivalries between cities like Suzhou and Yangzhou drawing widespread attention.

stories.title: China warns university students to beware of well-paid jobs offered by foreign spies
stories.summary: China's Ministry of State Security warned university students to be wary of well-paid job offers that may serve as fronts for foreign espionage recruitment. The warning came ahead of a record graduation season, with the agency citing examples of postings offering high pay for remote data processing as potential intelligence-gathering traps.

stories.title: Trump's Iran threats renew debate over war crimes, illegal orders
stories.summary: President Trump's threats against Iran have reignited debate in the United States over war crimes and the legality of military orders. The discussion centers on whether certain proposed actions could constitute violations of international law and whether service members could refuse illegal orders.

stories.title: Starmer says Nato in America’s ‘interests’ as Gulf tour ends
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, concluding a three-day Gulf tour in Doha, insisted that NATO serves America's interests and described it as a defensive alliance. His comments followed US President Trump's threats to withdraw from NATO after allies refused to join the Iran war. Starmer said Britain is building a 30-nation coalition to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran delegation to meet Pakistan PM Sharif ahead of talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Iran's negotiating delegation, led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad ahead of high-stakes talks with the United States. The Iranian team also met Pakistan's army chief and foreign minister. Pakistan is serving as a central mediator in the negotiations during a temporary ceasefire.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills at least six at Gaza police checkpoint, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike struck a police checkpoint in Bureij camp in central Gaza on Saturday, killing at least six people and injuring several others, according to medics in Cairo.

stories.title: Israel rejects ceasefire with Hezbollah ahead of Lebanon talks next week
stories.summary: Israel has rejected a ceasefire proposal with Hezbollah ahead of scheduled talks in Washington next week. Israeli military operations in Lebanon continue, while Iran has insisted that any ceasefire agreement must include Tehran.

stories.title: Israeli drone attack kills Palestinians near Gaza mosque
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike near a mosque in central Gaza killed at least six Palestinians. The attack took place in the central part of the territory.

stories.title: Conscientious objections to war rise sharply in US
stories.summary: The Centre on Conscience and War reported a 1,000 percent surge in calls to its GI Rights Hotline from US service members seeking information on conscientious objector status. Over 80 new cases were filed in March alone, nearly double the typical annual total. Many callers cited the bombing of a school in Iran as a turning point.

stories.title: China plans to deliver air defense systems to Iran in coming weeks, US intelligence reveals - CNN
stories.summary: US intelligence reports indicate China is planning to deliver air defense systems to Iran within the coming weeks. According to CNN, China intends to use third countries to conceal the shipments amid rising regional tensions.

stories.title: 'Iran has put up a demand that Lebanon should be included in the ceasefire'
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations arrived in Islamabad for negotiations to end the six-week-old Middle East war. In a last-minute complication, Iran demanded that Lebanon be included in any ceasefire agreement, according to France 24's correspondent in Pakistan.

stories.title: Police reportedly forming new unit to tackle Iran spying cases
stories.summary: Israeli police are reportedly establishing a new major crimes unit to handle Iran-linked espionage cases, coordinated with the Shin Bet security agency. The unit is being created based on the assessment that Iranian espionage activities will persist, with financial incentives identified as the primary motive for those recruited.

stories.title: Iran enters talks in 'good faith', cites distrust of US as talks begin in Islamabad
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that Tehran entered the Islamabad negotiations in good faith despite deep mistrust of the United States, according to IRNA. Ghalibaf, leading Iran's delegation, cited Washington's failure to honor past commitments and said any agreement would require guarantees against repeated violations.

stories.title: Vaccine gaps fuel Bangladesh’s deadly measles crisis
stories.summary: Bangladesh is experiencing its worst measles outbreak in 20 years, with at least 143 deaths—mostly children—and over 12,000 suspected cases since March 15. Vaccination gaps are identified as the primary driver of the crisis. Families from rural areas are rushing to hospitals in Dhaka seeking treatment.

stories.title: Drone attack damages dozens of buildings in Odesa, two killed and two injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack struck a residential area in the Ukrainian city of Odesa, killing two people and injuring two others. The strikes damaged dozens of buildings in the area.

stories.title: Video: Vance arrives in Pakistan for talks with Iran
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance landed in Pakistan to hold talks with Iranian officials. The negotiations in Islamabad are aimed at reaching a deal to end the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills 13 security personnel in  Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the southern Lebanese city of Nabatiyeh killed at least 13 State Security personnel. The attack came amid fierce cross-border fighting despite planned ceasefire talks between Israel and Lebanon. The UN warned of a looming food crisis as Lebanon's war death toll approached 1,900.

stories.title: Diesel price cut by Rs135; petrol sees drop of Rs12
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a Rs135 per litre cut in diesel and Rs12 per litre cut in petrol prices, effective for the week ending April 17. The reductions were attributed to easing global oil prices following a two-week US-Iran ceasefire. High-speed diesel dropped 26 percent to Rs385.54 per litre.

stories.title: Tighter civil service disciplinary rules risk becoming excessive: union head
stories.summary: The head of Hong Kong's Federation of Civil Service Unions, Leung Chau-ting, warned that proposed tighter disciplinary rules for civil servants risk becoming excessive. The Civil Service Bureau plans to revise regulations to address underperforming workers, including stricter rules on withholding salaries during suspensions.

stories.title: Top US officials land in Pakistan for talks with Iran
stories.summary: Senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Islamabad for talks with Iran. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the negotiations as "make or break" during a temporary ceasefire. Pakistan provided extensive security for the Iranian delegation, including AWACS aircraft, electronic warfare planes, and fighter jet escorts.

stories.title: Israel bombs Lebanon towns as Hezbollah targets army base
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck the towns of Jebchit and Kfarsir in southern Lebanon. A separate Israeli air strike on a residential building in Mayfadoun in the Nabatieh district killed three people. Hezbollah responded by firing missiles at the Yaara barracks of the Israeli army in northern Israel.

stories.title: Enemy attack on Lubenskyi district in Poltava region kills one, injures another
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Lubenskyi district of Ukraine's Poltava region, killing one person and injuring another in the attack.

stories.title: Ceasefire & Peacetalks, Hungary 'False Flags' & Final Rallies
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued escalating threats against Iran during the week, demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. His remarks, delivered in unfiltered language including on Easter Sunday at the White House, preceded the announcement of ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: How the Gulf conflict recast risks for Asian investors in Dubai
stories.summary: Asian digital entrepreneurs and investors who used Dubai as a base for global expansion are reassessing risks after the US-Israel war on Iran exposed vulnerabilities. Disruption around the Strait of Hormuz raised concerns about liquidity, credit, and market confidence for businesses from India, China, and Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Iran’s supreme leader has disfiguring facial wounds and may have lost a leg, sources say
stories.summary: Sources close to Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei report he sustained severe, disfiguring facial wounds and may have lost a leg. US intelligence reportedly believes he lost the limb on the first day of the war. Sources say he remains mentally sharp and continues decision-making through audio conferencing with officials.

stories.title: After AIPAC-backed primary loss, Malinowski endorses rival who accuses Israel of genocide
stories.summary: Former US Congressman Tom Malinowski endorsed progressive candidate Analilia Mejia after losing an AIPAC-backed primary. Mejia has accused Israel of genocide. The pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC has dismissed criticism that its attack ads inadvertently helped the progressive candidate win.

stories.title: Iran’s delegation carries photos and bags of children killed in Minab to Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran's delegation arrived in Islamabad carrying photos and bags belonging to children killed in US strikes on Minab on February 28. The delegation, led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, is in Pakistan to negotiate a ceasefire with the United States.

stories.title: Russian strikes on residential buildings in Sumy injure 14 in one day
stories.summary: Russian strikes on residential buildings in the Ukrainian city of Sumy injured 14 people over the course of a single day. The attacks targeted civilian infrastructure in the city.

stories.title: US delegation arrives in Islamabad for Iran talks, Pakistan sets up media hub
stories.summary: A plane carrying the US negotiating delegation for talks with Iran arrived in Islamabad. Pakistan set up a media center at the Jinnah Convention Centre to support press coverage of the talks. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the facility includes high-speed internet, workstations, and live broadcast areas.

stories.title: South Korea’s president hits back at Israel in row over ‘disturbing’ video
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung accused Israel of failing to address allegations of rights abuses after Israel criticized him for sharing a social media video purportedly showing Israeli soldiers abusing a Palestinian child. Israel's foreign ministry had accused Lee of amplifying disinformation.

stories.title: Trump officials unveil plans for gilded, triumphal Washington arch
stories.summary: Trump administration officials unveiled plans for a gilded triumphal arch to be built in Washington, DC. The structure would feature a towering winged figure flanked by two eagles and guarded by four lions. President Trump called it the "greatest and most beautiful triumphal arch" in the world.

stories.title: China café sets ‘entry rules’ that ban littering, discarding black stockings, stealing tiny turtles
stories.summary: A café called Yi Nan Ping in Qingzhou Ancient City, Shandong province, China, went viral for posting an oversized notice listing unusual entry rules. The banned behaviors include littering, discarding black stockings, and stealing tiny turtles from the café's pond.

stories.title: Iran retains thousands of missiles, ability to reactivate launchers - report
stories.summary: A report indicated that Iran retains thousands of ballistic missiles and the ability to reactivate damaged launchers, contradicting US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's earlier claim that Iran's missile capability had been "depleted and decimated." US officials expressed concern that Iran may use the ceasefire period to rearm.

stories.title: Concerns after satellite provider restricts Iran images following US pressure
stories.summary: US-based satellite imagery provider Planet Labs announced it is indefinitely restricting coverage of Iran and parts of the Middle East following pressure from the United States, raising concerns about reduced transparency in the region.

stories.title: Live: US delegation arrives in Pakistan for peace talks with Iranian officials
stories.summary: A U.S. government plane carrying senior American officials landed in Islamabad, Pakistan, on Saturday for peace talks with Iranian counterparts. The negotiations aim to permanently end the six-week-old war between Washington and Tehran, a conflict that has killed thousands across the Middle East.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 1,953 in Lebanon, health ministry says
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli strikes have killed at least 1,953 people and wounded 6,303 others since March 2. Officials said 357 people died in a single day of attacks on Wednesday, with many remains still unidentified. Israeli and Lebanese envoys held a phone call as diplomatic contacts continued alongside the fighting.

stories.title: FAA, Pentagon sign agreement on deploying anti-drone laser system near Mexico
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration and the Pentagon signed an agreement enabling deployment of a high-energy laser counter-drone system along the U.S. southern border with Mexico. The agreement was announced on Friday in Washington.

stories.title: CNN: China may supply air defences to Iran, US intelligence says
stories.summary: US intelligence indicates China is preparing to deliver air defense systems to Iran in the coming weeks, according to a CNN report citing three sources. Beijing may route shipments through third countries to conceal their origin. The systems are expected to include shoulder-fired MANPADS anti-air missiles.

stories.title: Explainer-Why are people talking about the 25th Amendment to the US Constitution?
stories.summary: Some Democratic lawmakers have discussed invoking the 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution to remove President Donald Trump from office. The discussions were prompted by Trump's profanity-laced threats to destroy Iran's civilization.

stories.title: South Korean President clashes with Israel over 'despicable' video
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung clashed with Israel's foreign ministry after sharing a 2024 video showing Israeli soldiers throwing a body from a rooftop in the occupied West Bank. Israel accused Lee of presenting an old incident as current. Lee responded that global criticism reflects concerns over human rights violations.

stories.title: Malaysia detains masseuses from China offering ‘extra services’
stories.summary: Malaysian immigration officers raided two massage parlours in Johor suspected of offering sexual services, detaining 21 foreign workers from China and a local man believed to be the manager. The businesses had publicly advertised standard massage services but were alleged to be involved in immoral activities employing undocumented foreign workers.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills six Palestinians at Gaza checkpoint, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit a police checkpoint in the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza, killing at least six people and injuring several others. It was unclear whether all victims were police members. The Israeli military did not immediately comment on the strike.

stories.title: Zebras, wealth and power: Hungary’s election tests Orbán’s grip on power
stories.summary: Hungary is heading into an election that represents the most significant challenge yet to long-serving Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's hold on power. Corruption scandals, including drone footage of a lavish estate with exotic animals such as zebras, and a surging opposition movement have intensified scrutiny of his government.

stories.title: State failing to learn lessons of Southport attack, say victims’ lawyers
stories.summary: Lawyers representing victims of the July 2024 Southport attack in the United Kingdom say the government is failing to learn lessons from the incident, with violence-obsessed young people still posing a serious threat. A report by Judge Sir Adrian Fulford, due for release on Monday, is expected to criticize failures by multiple agencies, including the counter-terrorism programme Prevent.

stories.title: The war over Omagh’s gold: the £21bn mine plan tearing a community apart
stories.summary: A public inquiry is set to reopen on Monday in Omagh, County Tyrone, concerning a proposed gold mine estimated at £21 billion, first proposed nine years ago. The plan has deeply divided the local community, with residents such as retired social worker Fidelma O'Kane becoming heavily involved in opposing the mining company's project.

stories.title: SUVs are making Britain’s potholes worse, say scientists
stories.summary: British scientists and engineers have linked the increasing prevalence of SUVs to accelerated road deterioration and worsening potholes across the United Kingdom. Research indicated that hundreds of thousands of drivers purchased heavier vehicles partly to navigate already-damaged roads, compounding the problem further.

stories.title: Who is Vietnam’s new Prime Minister Le Minh Hung?
stories.summary: Vietnam's National Assembly elected Le Minh Hung as the country's new prime minister. Born in 1970, Hung is Vietnam's youngest premier since 1955 and is characterized as a technocrat with economic training rather than a provincial political figure. Analysts view his appointment as a deliberate bet on competence over seniority.

stories.title: ‘Cancelling orders’ in China: how Hormuz oil crisis is hitting transport, manufacturing
stories.summary: Manufacturers across China are facing supply and pricing volatility as the Strait of Hormuz has repeatedly opened and closed amid the US-Iran conflict. Soaring oil prices have driven up costs for processed fuel and petroleum-based raw materials critical to China's manufacturing sector. Industry sources say a fragile two-week ceasefire is unlikely to restore pre-conflict stability.
