stories.title: US, Iran set for peace talks but doubts emerge over Lebanon, sanctions
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are reportedly preparing for peace negotiations, though skepticism has emerged regarding issues related to Lebanon and sanctions. President Trump posted on social media that Iranians' sole reason for being alive is to negotiate a deal.

stories.title: US V-P Vance leaves for Islamabad, Iran demands measures as ‘make-or-break’ talks near
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance departed for Islamabad ahead of negotiations with Iran, while Tehran demanded preconditions be met before talks could proceed. President Trump posted on social media that the only reason Iranians were alive was to negotiate a deal.

stories.title: Michigan rabbi whose synagogue was attacked slams leftist senate candidate’s response
stories.summary: A rabbi at Temple Israel in suburban Detroit criticized Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for invoking the war in Lebanon in connection with an attack on the synagogue. Rabbi Jen Lader called El-Sayed's statement offensive, saying it undermined his earlier condemnation of the incident.

stories.title: Dan Bilzerian wants to ‘kill Israelis,' thinks Judaism is ‘terrible,’ and is running for Congress
stories.summary: Social media figure Dan Bilzerian, who is running for Congress, made inflammatory remarks about Israelis and Judaism. In an interview with TMZ, he denied being antisemitic and questioned the term "antisemitism," claiming it has been "hijacked to only talk about Jews."

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 43 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 43 of the US-Iran conflict, senior Iranian officials arrived in Islamabad, Pakistan, for ceasefire negotiations with the United States. The talks aim to address the ongoing hostilities between the two countries.

stories.title: Argentine court orders environmental studies over HIF plant in Uruguay
stories.summary: A federal court in Concepción del Uruguay, Argentina, ordered environmental studies and requested information from Uruguayan agencies regarding a green hydrogen plant planned by multinational HIF Global in Paysandú, Uruguay. The ruling accepted a lawsuit against the Uruguayan state and HIF Global, creating new bilateral tensions reminiscent of the early-2000s Botnia pulp mill dispute.

stories.title: Two Ukrzaliznytsia officials in Kyiv suspected of UAH 4.4M embezzlement in equipment procurement case
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement issued suspicion notices to two deputy directors of a Ukrzaliznytsia (Ukrainian Railways) branch in Kyiv over alleged embezzlement during locomotive equipment procurement. The scheme reportedly caused losses exceeding 4.4 million Ukrainian hryvnias.

stories.title: US team heads to Iran talks in Pakistan with low expectations
stories.summary: A U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance departed for Islamabad on Friday for weekend talks with Iran, though expectations were low. Both sides accused each other of violating commitments made to secure the temporary ceasefire.

stories.title: Sex, Nazism and rock ‘n’ roll: Why rockers love to goose step in the gaslights
stories.summary: A new book by music historian Daniel Rachel, titled "This Ain't Rock 'n' Roll," examines the use of Nazi symbols by rock and pop icons from David Bowie to John Lennon. The work explores the cultural and provocative role of Third Reich imagery in popular music history.

stories.title: Colombia raises Ecuador tariffs to 100% as trade tensions escalate
stories.summary: Colombia announced it would raise tariffs on imports from neighboring Ecuador to 100%, up from 30%, matching Ecuador's tariff increase from the previous day. The escalating trade dispute reflects deepening diplomatic tensions between the two South American nations.

stories.title: Iran parliament speaker posts images of children killed in US strike ahead of talks
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted images on X showing portraits of children killed in a US missile strike, placing their photos on airplane seats as he flew to Pakistan for peace talks. A preliminary US military investigation found outdated intelligence likely led to the February 28 strike on a school in Iran, which killed more than 165 children.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. will have Strait of Hormuz 'open fairly soon'
stories.summary: President Trump stated the US would have the Strait of Hormuz open "fairly soon." Tehran's blockade of the strait since the Iran war began has caused the worst disruption to global energy supplies in history.

stories.title: Pakistan ambassador speaks to Al Jazeera on eve of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's ambassador to the United States said that weeks of intensive diplomatic efforts preceded the US-Iran talks. The ambassador told Al Jazeera that all sides have expressed a shared commitment to the negotiation process.

stories.title: From Harbin to Hollywood: The tale of two talented Jewish sisters in China's 'Ice City'
stories.summary: The city of Harbin in northeastern China, once home to a thriving Jewish community, preserves its Jewish heritage through music and cultural memory. The story focuses on the legacy of the Schoenfeld sisters, two talented Jewish musicians who lived in the city.

stories.title: Romanian secret police trailed a Jewish photographer in the ’80s. Those files are now a film
stories.summary: Romanian filmmaker Radu Jude created a short documentary based on secret police surveillance files tracking Jewish American photographer Edward Serotta during his travels in communist Romania in the 1980s. Serotta only recently discovered the extent of the surveillance.

stories.title: Pakistan’s prime minister calls US-Iran talks ‘make or break’
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the upcoming US-Iran ceasefire talks in Islamabad as a critical turning point. He characterized the negotiations as "make or break" for resolving the conflict.

stories.title: UAE pulls US$3.5 billion from Pakistan after Iran war mediation
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates withdrew a US$3.5 billion deposit from Pakistan's central bank, equivalent to roughly 21 percent of the country's foreign exchange reserves. The withdrawal came days before Pakistan helped secure a ceasefire in the Iran war. Pakistan's foreign ministry described it as a routine financial transaction amid Emirati criticism of Islamabad's mediation role.

stories.title: Report: Iran missile capability persists, damaged launchers could be recovered
stories.summary: Iran retains thousands of ballistic missiles despite significant damage to its launch infrastructure, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials. About half of Iran's missile launchers have been destroyed, damaged, or buried, but many could potentially be repaired or recovered from underground facilities.

stories.title: Several airlines to reinstate flights to Israel in coming weeks
stories.summary: Greek carrier Blue Bird is set to resume flights to Israel on Sunday, becoming the first foreign airline to return since airspace was largely closed following the start of Operation Roaring Lion. Several other airlines plan to reinstate Israeli routes in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine set to begin Orthodox Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia declared a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire beginning Saturday at 4:00 PM Moscow time through the end of Sunday, and Ukraine indicated readiness to reciprocate. The temporary pause comes as US-led diplomatic efforts to end the four-year war continue to falter amid ongoing strikes and battlefield tensions.

stories.title: Longtime US congressman Eliot Engel, whose defeat augured surge in anti-Israel sentiment, dies at 79
stories.summary: Former US Congressman Eliot Engel of New York has died at age 79. AIPAC eulogized the Jewish lawmaker as a "steadfast friend of the pro-Israel community," while fellow New York Democrats remembered him as a champion of the Bronx.

stories.title: New Zealand’s North Island braces for Cyclone Vaianu with thousands ordered to evacuate
stories.summary: Thousands of residents on New Zealand's North Island were ordered to evacuate on Saturday ahead of Cyclone Vaianu, which was forecast to bring winds up to 130 km/h and heavy rain on Sunday. Authorities warned of potential coastal flooding and landslides, with the storm expected to pass west of the Chatham Islands on Monday.

stories.title: Temple Israel rabbi slams Michigan Senate candidate for ‘offensive’ remarks on synagogue attack
stories.summary: Rabbi Jen Lader of Temple Israel in suburban Detroit criticized Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for suggesting that an attack on the synagogue could be understood through the lens of Israeli military actions. Lader called the remarks offensive.

stories.title: UN: Lebanon shelters overcrowded amid mass displacement crisis
stories.summary: UN officials reported that shelters for displaced people in Lebanon are severely overcrowded as Israeli evacuation orders drive mass displacement. Nearly half of Lebanon's public schools are serving as reception centers. Up to 1.2 million people have been displaced, with approximately 250,000 crossing into Syria, according to UNHCR.

stories.title: US-Iran direct talks hours away, first since strikes began 6 weeks ago
stories.summary: Direct US-Iran peace talks are set to begin in Islamabad, the first since strikes began six weeks ago. The US delegation is led by Vice President JD Vance, while Iran's team is headed by Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Araghchi. Deep mistrust overshadows the negotiations aimed at reinforcing a fragile two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Experts warn of ‘hasbara’ and disinformation in digital battle over Palestine
stories.summary: A panel of researchers, activists, and digital media experts discussed the role of propaganda, artificial intelligence, and media narratives in shaping perceptions of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The discussion focused on disinformation tactics and their impact on public discourse surrounding Palestine.

stories.title: Suspect arrested after Molotov cocktail attack at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home
stories.summary: A suspect was arrested after a Molotov cocktail attack at the home of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Threats were also reportedly made outside OpenAI's headquarters. Details about the suspect's identity and motive were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Belarusian mercenary captured in Sumy region
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 47th Separate Mechanized Brigade Magura captured a Belarusian mercenary fighting for Russian forces in Ukraine's Sumy region. The detention highlights the involvement of foreign fighters in Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Israeli strikes hit south Lebanon, Hezbollah claims attacks in north Israel
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted the towns of Toul and Jebchit in southern Lebanon amid continued cross-border hostilities. Hezbollah said it fired missiles at the northern Israeli towns of Kiryat Shmona, Metula, and Misgav Am, and struck Israeli military infrastructure in Safed. The group also claimed a drone strike on Israeli soldiers in the southern Lebanese town of Shamaa.

stories.title: Former Gaza hostage Rom Braslavski faces online attacks after criticizing Gal Hirsch
stories.summary: Former Gaza hostage Rom Braslavski faced online attacks after criticizing the selection of Brigadier General (res.) Gal Hirsch to light a torch at Israel's Independence Day ceremony. Braslavski called the choice "a slap in the face" to hostage families.

stories.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz to reopen ‘soon’ as US, Iran head to talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen "soon" as American and Iranian delegations prepared for talks. Trump said Washington would not accept Iran's imposition of a de facto toll system on the critical waterway.

stories.title: White House opted against televised address about Iran ceasefire, US officials say
stories.summary: The White House considered but ultimately decided against having President Donald Trump deliver a nationally televised address about his ceasefire deal with Iran. Some aides and advisers privately expressed concern about potentially overselling the still-nascent agreement, according to three U.S. officials.

stories.title: Asia’s ‘panicked farmers’ brace for a looming rice crisis post-Iran war
stories.summary: Farmers across Southeast Asia are facing spiking fuel and fertilizer costs driven by the Middle East war, threatening rice production in one of the world's largest growing regions. In Thailand, some farmers are leaving harvest-ready crops in the ground because processing costs have become prohibitive. Tens of millions of smallholders are struggling to afford diesel and crop nutrients.

stories.title: US Jewish authors slam Jewish Book Council’s bias toward ‘Israeli and Zionist voices’
stories.summary: Forty-two US Jewish authors signed an open letter criticizing the Jewish Book Council for allegedly favoring Israeli and Zionist voices in its programming after October 7. The writers argued the emphasis gives a false impression that Jewish literature is inherently Zionist.

stories.title: Israel won't discuss Hezbollah truce in talks with Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, confirmed that Israel agreed to begin formal peace negotiations with the Lebanese government, with which it has no diplomatic relations. However, Israel refused to discuss a truce with Hezbollah as part of those talks.

stories.title: Tasnim: 71-member Iranian delegation joins US negotiations
stories.summary: Iran's 71-member delegation arrived in Islamabad for negotiations with the United States, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency. The delegation includes the main negotiating team, technical committees, expert teams, media representatives, and protocol and security personnel.

stories.title: Israel says it will not negotiate ceasefire with Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador to the United States Yechiel Leiter said Israel agreed to formal peace negotiations with Lebanon under US auspices but refused to discuss a ceasefire with Hezbollah. Leiter described Hezbollah as "the main obstacle to peace" and rejected direct engagement with the group.

stories.title: Three more countries interested in Ukraine’s drone defense experience – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Oman, Bahrain, and Kuwait have expressed interest in learning from Ukraine's experience in drone defense. The announcement highlights growing international attention to Ukraine's counter-drone capabilities developed during its ongoing conflict with Russia.

stories.title: Antisemitism is returning – and the world is silent, again - opinion
stories.summary: A UK opinion piece raised concerns about rising antisemitism globally, citing British Prime Minister Keir Starmer's statements suggesting a confrontation with Iran is not Britain's concern. The commentary questioned whether Western nations are willing to learn from historical failures to confront hatred.

stories.title: Security researchers find 213 vulnerabilities in Russia’s state-backed messaging app Max
stories.summary: Security researchers discovered 213 vulnerabilities in Max, Russia's state-backed messaging application, through a bug bounty program. The findings were announced by Positive Technologies CTO Alexei Batyuk at the Svyaz-2026 exhibition in Russia.

stories.title: US, Lebanon request Israel pause attacks against Hezbollah prior to talks - report
stories.summary: The United States and Lebanon reportedly requested that Israel pause its attacks against Hezbollah ahead of planned diplomatic talks. The request was said to be under review by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Lebanon confirmed that the US would mediate the negotiations.

stories.title: Vance en route, Iranian delegation touches down for Islamabad talks
stories.summary: An Iranian delegation arrived in Islamabad on Friday night ahead of negotiations with the United States, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance and his team were en route to Pakistan. The talks follow a two-week halt in the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which began on February 28. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif brokered the pause in fighting.

stories.title: Was Penang ‘robbed’ from Kedah? Malaysian states face off in sovereignty row
stories.summary: The Malaysian states of Penang and Kedah are engaged in a sovereignty dispute rooted in colonial-era history. British merchant Francis Light took possession of Penang island in 1786 on behalf of the British East India Company. The row centers on whether the island was legitimately ceded or effectively taken from the Kedah sultanate.

stories.title: China has mapped out a third new county in Xinjiang. Why?
stories.summary: China has established a third new county in Xinjiang, named Cenling, located in the southwestern part of the region near the Karakoram Range. The county sits along key transport routes linking China to Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Central and South Asia. Analysts say the move reflects Beijing's focus on governance and security along its western borders.

stories.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs12 per litre, HSD by Rs135
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a reduction of Rs135 per litre in high-speed diesel prices and Rs12 per litre in petrol prices. The new rates of Rs385 for HSD and Rs366 for petrol took effect from Saturday. Sharif said targeted fuel subsidies introduced during the Middle East crisis would continue.

stories.title: Lebanon says first contact with Israel held ahead of U.S.-brokered talks
stories.summary: Lebanon announced that it held its first direct contact with Israel ahead of U.S.-brokered negotiations. No further details about the substance or outcome of the contact were immediately available.

stories.title: Iran wanted to negotiate with US V-P J. D. Vance. They got their wish
stories.summary: Iran sought direct negotiations with US Vice President J.D. Vance, viewing him as one of the most anti-war figures in President Donald Trump's inner circle. The talks materialized as part of broader diplomatic engagement between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Amid echoes of war, these survivors will light Yom Hashoah torches in pre-recorded ceremony
stories.summary: Israel's Yad Vashem Holocaust memorial announced that this year's Yom Hashoah torch-lighting ceremony, themed "The Jewish Family During the Holocaust," will be broadcast as a pre-recorded program rather than a live event. No reason was given for the change.

stories.title: Court sentences man who set fire to military vehicles to seven years in prison in Sumy region
stories.summary: A court in Ukraine's Sumy region sentenced a man to seven years in prison for setting fire to two vehicles belonging to military personnel.

stories.title: Helpful analysts predict China property recovery now, soon and much later
stories.summary: China's property market continues to struggle, with homeowners who purchased since the late 2010s sitting on significant losses. Analysts offer divergent timelines for a potential recovery, ranging from imminent to years away. Sales briefly picked up around Spring Festival in cities like Chongqing, but buyer offers remain well below sellers' expectations.

stories.title: Rahat resident indicted for smuggling goods into Gaza Strip, aiding enemy during wartime
stories.summary: Israeli authorities indicted a 34-year-old resident of Rahat, Nasser Mustafa, for smuggling goods into the Gaza Strip and aiding the enemy during wartime. The Southern District Attorney's Office said the smuggling was coordinated with an IDF reserve officer.

stories.title: One dead, 27 injured as bus carrying British tourists crashes in Spain’s La Gomera island
stories.summary: A bus carrying British tourists crashed on the island of La Gomera in Spain's Canary Islands, killing one person and injuring 27. La Gomera is a popular destination for visitors from northern Europe.

stories.title: How gossip spread in ancient China before advent of printing when newspapers reported on scandals
stories.summary: Ancient China had informal information networks that spread gossip and scandal long before printing became widespread. During the Eastern Han dynasty, the imperial Censorate was established to monitor official conduct. Censors, teahouses, street tabloids, and stage stations formed an interconnected system for circulating news about the powerful.

stories.title: Firmly oppose the targeting of civilians and infrastructure in West Asia conflict, says Jaishankar
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, attending an Indian Ocean Rim ministers' conference in Mauritius, stated India firmly opposes the targeting of civilians and infrastructure in the West Asia conflict. The conference was overshadowed by the ongoing U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and related peace talks.

stories.title: Artemis II safely splashes down in Pacific Ocean, concluding 10-day moon mission
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II capsule splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California, completing a 10-day moon mission covering 694,392 miles. The four astronauts traveled deeper into space than any humans before them.

stories.title: Trump's peace board faces cash crunch as Gaza plan stalls
stories.summary: Trump's Board of Peace has reportedly received contributions from only three donors, with total funds currently under $1 billion, stalling plans to rebuild Gaza.

stories.title: Russia's two largest car manufacturers report deepening crisis – intelligence
stories.summary: Russia's two largest automakers, KamAZ and AvtoVAZ, are experiencing a deepening crisis that official rhetoric about industrial resilience can no longer conceal, according to intelligence reports. The difficulties reflect broader economic pressures facing Russia's manufacturing sector.

stories.title: Molotov attack on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home leads to arrest
stories.summary: A 20-year-old man was arrested in San Francisco for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's North Beach residence and making threats outside the company's headquarters. The incendiary device was thrown at approximately 4:12 a.m. on Friday. The suspect was detained about an hour later.

stories.title: Lebanon heads to historic Israel talks with few hopes except to staunch bloodshed
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called for historic direct talks with Israel after a month of war that displaced more than a million Lebanese and caused extensive destruction in Beirut. The negotiations are viewed with limited optimism, with the primary goal being to halt the bloodshed.

stories.title: UK police arrest Sudanese man after four die in Channel boat crossing
stories.summary: British police arrested a 27-year-old Sudanese man on suspicion of endangering life after four migrants died during a small boat crossing of the English Channel from France to Britain this week.

stories.title: Multiple people face charges, including murder, in California fireworks blast
stories.summary: Multiple people have been charged with murder in connection with a fatal fireworks-warehouse explosion near Esparto, California, about an hour from Sacramento. The blast at a 5,000-square-foot warehouse on July 1 killed seven people and injured two others, sparking a massive fire and leading to the cancellation of local Fourth of July celebrations.

stories.title: In meeting with Saudi finance minister, PM emphasises ‘strong commitment’ to expanding cooperation in all spheres
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed bin Abdullah al Jadaan in Islamabad on Friday. Sharif emphasized Pakistan's commitment to expanding cooperation with Saudi Arabia in trade, investment, and economic development. Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar also attended the meeting at PM House.

stories.title: RMIT drops misconduct case against student who accused university of being ‘complicit in Gaza genocide’
stories.summary: RMIT University in Australia dropped a misconduct case against student Gemma Seymour, who had accused the institution of complicity in genocide in Gaza due to its Sir Lawrence Wackett Defence and Aerospace Centre's ties to weapons companies. Seymour had faced potential suspension over a social media video calling for the centre to be shut down.

stories.title: Palestinian youths injured in Israeli West Bank raids
stories.summary: Israeli forces wounded a 21-year-old Palestinian man with rubber-coated metal bullets during a military raid in Birzeit, north of Ramallah. Another young man was detained after being injured by live fire during a separate raid on Al-Arroub refugee camp in the West Bank.

stories.title: Japan’s Middle East oil habit gets an Iran war reality check
stories.summary: Japan's heavy dependence on Middle Eastern oil, with over 95 percent of its crude sourced from the region and routed through the Strait of Hormuz, has been exposed by the Iran war. A two-week ceasefire offered temporary relief by reopening the strait to tanker traffic. Analysts say the crisis revealed energy security vulnerabilities Tokyo cannot easily address.

stories.title: Iran war live: US negotiators due to arrive in Pakistan for ceasefire talks
stories.summary: US negotiators are due to arrive in Pakistan for ceasefire talks with Iran. Separately, Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli attacks since March 2 have killed 1,953 people and wounded 6,303 others.

stories.title: Iran speaker demands Lebanon truce, release of assets ‘before negotiations’
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary speaker demanded a truce in Lebanon and the release of frozen Iranian assets as preconditions before entering negotiations. The demands were made shortly after US Vice President J.D. Vance departed for peace talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: Israeli strike on government building kills Lebanese officers
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit a government building in the southern Lebanese town of Nabatieh, killing at least 13 people. The dead included Lebanese officers, according to reports.

stories.title: US team heads to talks with Iran in Pakistan with low expectations
stories.summary: A US negotiating team headed to Pakistan for talks with Iran amid low expectations. White House officials expressed skepticism the talks could immediately reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides accusing each other of breaking ceasefire commitments.

stories.title: US intel said to assess Iran still has thousands of ballistic missiles, can recover launchers
stories.summary: US intelligence assesses that Iran still possesses thousands of ballistic missiles and could recover damaged launchers, according to reports. Separately, Hezbollah launched overnight rocket attacks on Israeli communities near the Lebanese border. Trump's Board of Peace denied any funding constraints for Gaza commitments.

stories.title: Historic Vance-Ghalibaf talks must bridge deep distrust
stories.summary: Potential face-to-face talks between US Vice President JD Vance and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf would represent the highest-level direct engagement between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The discussions must overcome decades of deep mutual distrust.

stories.title: Invaders strike high-rise in Sumy with drone, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a high-rise residential building in the Ukrainian city of Sumy using a drone, resulting in casualties. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure in the northeastern Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Trump: US will have Strait of Hormuz ‘open fairly soon’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters the US would have the Strait of Hormuz open "fairly soon," ahead of ceasefire talks in Islamabad. Iran had closed the strait since the start of US-Israeli military operations in the region, disrupting roughly 20 percent of global oil transit.

stories.title: The president who threatened to end a civilization is supposed to guarantee Ukraine’s survival
stories.summary: An analysis argued that the US war with Iran has diverted diplomatic resources and depleted interceptor missile stockpiles that were intended to underpin security guarantees for Ukraine.

stories.title: Brazil announces US partnership to intercept weapons, drug trafficking
stories.summary: Brazil announced a new partnership with the United States to intercept illicit weapons and drug trafficking. President Lula's government said it had seized 1,168 illegal arms imported from the US over the past 12 months.

stories.title: Colombia responds to Ecuador’s tariff hike with 100-percent import tax
stories.summary: Colombia imposed a 100-percent import tax on Ecuadorian goods in retaliation for Ecuador's tariff increases. The escalation comes amid cross-border tensions over illicit drug flows and the fate of former Ecuadorian politician Jorge Glas.

stories.title: California: Eric Swalwell staffers quit after new sexual assault allegations
stories.summary: Several staffers for California gubernatorial candidate Eric Swalwell resigned and prominent supporters withdrew backing after new sexual assault allegations were published by the San Francisco Chronicle and reported on CNN.

stories.title: Estonia says detaining Russia's tankers in Baltic Sea is too risky
stories.summary: NATO member Estonia announced it will not detain Russian "shadow fleet" vessels in the Baltic Sea. A senior Estonian commander said seizing Western-sanctioned oil tankers could provoke a military response from Moscow, making the action too risky.

stories.title: Trump’s Board of Peace denies reports of funding shortages
stories.summary: Trump's Board of Peace denied reports of funding shortages, stating all funding requests have been met "immediately and in full." A Reuters report had claimed the board received only a fraction of the $17 billion pledged for rebuilding Gaza.

stories.title: Arriving in Pakistan, Iran’s top negotiator demands US accept ‘preconditions’ before talks start
stories.summary: Iran's top negotiator arrived in Islamabad and demanded the US accept preconditions before formal talks begin. President Trump countered that Iran has "no cards" and insisted the Strait of Hormuz would reopen "with or without them."

stories.title: Netanyahu requests delay in his corruption trial testimony
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu requested a delay in testimony for his ongoing corruption trial, which had been scheduled to resume on April 12.

stories.title: Iran has ‘goodwill but no trust in US’ ahead of ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran is ready for a ceasefire deal if the US seeks a genuine agreement and recognizes Iran's rights. He added that Iran would bring "goodwill" but "no trust in the US" to the talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court stays repatriation of Afghan family whose asylum case for resettlement in a third country is pending
stories.summary: The Peshawar High Court issued a temporary order barring law enforcement agencies from repatriating an Afghan family whose asylum case for third-country resettlement through UNHCR is pending. The petition was filed by a former serviceman of the previous Afghan government who fled Afghanistan with his family in 2021. The court sought replies from the federal interior ministry and other respondents.

stories.title: Watch Artemis II astronauts hurtle home from moon towards splashdown
stories.summary: The four Artemis II astronauts were returning to Earth after completing the first crewed lunar voyage in over 50 years. Their Orion capsule executed a final thruster firing to adjust its course ahead of splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California.

stories.title: Iran has 'no cards' beyond Strait of Hormuz control, says Trump ahead of talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Ahead of talks in Islamabad, U.S. President Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran has "no cards" beyond its control of the Strait of Hormuz, stating that Iran's only option is to negotiate.

stories.title: Russian investigative journalist is placed in pre-trial detention
stories.summary: A Russian court ordered the pre-trial detention of Oleg Roldugin, an investigative journalist for the independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta. Roldugin had been arrested the previous day in Moscow.

stories.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs12 per litre, diesel by Rs135
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a reduction in diesel prices by 135 rupees per litre and petrol by 12 rupees per litre, effective Saturday. He said targeted fuel subsidies introduced during the Middle East-related fuel crisis would continue.

stories.title: JD Vance dispatched to negotiate Iran peace with few cards to play
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance arrived in Islamabad to negotiate a peace deal with Iran, facing Iranian negotiators emboldened by their control of the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts described the assignment as difficult given Vance's prior opposition to Middle East wars and the administration's urgency to reopen shipping lanes.

stories.title: 'Game on’: How Iran can exact a toll in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Analysts described how Iran could formalize control over the Strait of Hormuz by requiring transit fees and clearance codes for tankers passing through its territorial waters. A potential US-Iran peace deal in Pakistan could institutionalize this arrangement for global shipping.

stories.title: 'Game on’: How Iran can exact a toll in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Analysts examined how Iran could leverage control over the Strait of Hormuz to impose costs on international shipping amid its conflict with the United States. The analysis suggested that if US sanctions on Iran were lifted, shipping companies might willingly pay transit fees given elevated oil and freight prices.

stories.title: ‘No money’: Trump’s Board of Peace faces cash crunch, stalling Gaza plan, sources say
stories.summary: Trump's Board of Peace is facing a funding shortage that is stalling plans for Gaza, with only three out of ten expected contributing countries having provided funds.

stories.title: US, Lebanon ask Israel to ‘pause’ attacks on Hezbollah
stories.summary: The Lebanese government and the Trump administration reportedly asked Israel to pause its attacks on Hezbollah ahead of direct negotiations set for next week. The request followed the deadliest Israeli strikes since the war began, which killed over 350 people on Wednesday.

stories.title: France’s Macron talks war, peace and basketball with Pope Leo
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican, where they discussed efforts to end the war in the Middle East. Both leaders have called for dialogue to resolve the conflict in the region.

stories.title: Hezbollah rocket attack damages 1,500-year-old Israeli church
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched a rocket barrage at northern Israel, striking and damaging a 1,500-year-old Byzantine church in the coastal city of Nahariya.

stories.title: Israel rejects ceasefire talks with Hezbollah but agrees to negotiating with Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel refused to engage in ceasefire talks directly with Hezbollah but agreed to begin formal peace negotiations with the Lebanese government. Israel's ambassador to the US announced the agreement following a call with Lebanese and US ambassadors, with an initial meeting set for Tuesday.

stories.title: 22 of Russia’s 30 most popular Android apps monitor whether users have VPN enabled, study finds
stories.summary: A study by RKS Global found that 22 of Russia's 30 most popular Android apps monitor whether users have a VPN service enabled. The findings were first reported by Russian business outlet The Bell on April 10.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court stays repartiation of Afghan family whose asylum case for resettlement in a third country is pending
stories.summary: The Peshawar High Court temporarily barred Pakistani law enforcement from repatriating an Afghan family whose asylum case for resettlement in a third country through the UN refugee agency is pending. The family fled Afghanistan in 2021.

stories.title: Over 200 hectares in Khmelnytskyi region transferred to state from Russian and Belarusian owners
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Khmelnytskyi region, 209 hectares of land previously owned by Russian and Belarusian citizens have been transferred to Ukrainian state ownership since the beginning of the full-scale invasion.

stories.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home targeted in Molotov cocktail attack
stories.summary: Police reported that a suspect threw a Molotov cocktail at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's residence in San Francisco before dawn and fled the scene on foot.

stories.title: US loans 8.5m barrels of SPR oil in second batch since Iran war
stories.summary: The United States released 8.5 million barrels of oil from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve as loans, the second such release since the Iran war began. The move aims to stabilize global oil markets affected by the conflict.

stories.title: 'Make or break': What to know about US-Iran talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: US-Iran ceasefire talks mediated by Pakistan are set to begin in Islamabad on Saturday. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the negotiations as a critical moment, with the key deliverable being the willingness of all parties to agree to meet again.

stories.title: Iran war leaves crisis-scarred countries counting the cost
stories.summary: The war in Iran is causing economic repercussions in crisis-affected countries including Sri Lanka, where fuel prices rose 35%. Tour operators in Colombo reported business declines of nearly a third as the conflict disrupted economic recovery efforts across South Asia.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran on Hormuz tolls as frozen traffic spurs Japan to release more oil
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump warned Iran against imposing tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Japan moved to release additional oil reserves as vessel traffic through the strait remained disrupted.

stories.title: Pentagon, FAA sign agreement on deploying anti-drone laser system near Mexico
stories.summary: The Pentagon and FAA signed an agreement to deploy an anti-drone laser system near the US-Mexico border. The FAA had previously conducted testing of the laser system in New Mexico.

stories.title: US jury indicts 10 Indians for visa fraud conspiracy involving staged robberies at convenience stores
stories.summary: A U.S. federal grand jury in Boston indicted 10 Indian nationals on conspiracy to commit visa fraud charges involving staged armed robberies at convenience stores, allowing store clerks to falsely claim crime-victim status on immigration applications.

stories.title: Key facts about Sunday's election in Hungary and possible outcomes
stories.summary: Hungary is holding a parliamentary election on Sunday that is drawing close international attention from the European Union, the United States, and Russia. The vote is considered a landmark event in the central European nation's politics.

stories.title: US inflation surges as effects of the Iran war show in prices
stories.summary: US consumer prices recorded their largest monthly increase since the post-pandemic inflation crisis in 2022, driven in part by economic effects of the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine tips drone war in its favor
stories.summary: Ukraine has gained an advantage in the drone war by rapidly innovating its drone technology. Reports indicate Ukraine is now beginning to match Russia's ability to scale production as well.

stories.title: Vocational schools new front in China’s strategy to support businesses’ global expansion
stories.summary: China is expanding vocational education programs for international students from Southeast Asia, Africa, and other regions as part of a strategy to support Chinese businesses' global expansion. Hebei Software Institute in Baoding has established multiple overseas-oriented programs training students in factory operations and supply chain management.

stories.title: Iranian delegation arrives in Islamabad for talks with US
stories.summary: A senior Iranian delegation arrived in Islamabad, Pakistan, to hold talks with US officials.

stories.title: Islamabad on lockdown ahead of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistani authorities deployed more than 10,000 military and police personnel across Islamabad ahead of the arrival of US and Iranian delegations for negotiations.

stories.title: 1,000 km from front line: Special Operations Forces strike oil rigs in Caspian Sea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces destroyed two Lukoil drilling platforms on the Caspian Sea shelf, approximately 1,000 km from the front lines. The deep-strike operation was carried out on the night of April 10 and footage of the destruction was released.

stories.title: White House opted against announcing Iran ceasefire on TV, fearing it may not last
stories.summary: The White House reportedly decided against having Trump announce an Iran ceasefire on television over concerns it might not hold. The White House denied the report, calling it "fake news" and saying the idea was never discussed with the president.

stories.title: Israeli strike in south Lebanon kills 10 security personnel
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck the city of Nabatiyeh in south Lebanon, hitting near the government complex and the State Security office. The state-run National News Agency reported a series of heavy strikes that killed 10 security personnel.

stories.title: In photos: Pakistan prepares to host US-Iran ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Pakistan is preparing to host US-Iran ceasefire talks in Islamabad on April 10, 2026. Pakistani troops escorted motorcades carrying US security officials to the venue, while digital screens across the capital displayed news of the peace talks.

stories.title: Streaming services unveil Holocaust Memorial Day 2026 programming
stories.summary: Streaming services announced special programming for Holocaust Memorial Day 2026. A highlight includes a new edition of Zikaron BaSalon, an intimate project in which Holocaust survivors share their personal stories.

stories.title: ‘World doesn’t have a plan B’: Bilawal stresses need for US-Iran talks to lead to peaceful resolution of conflict
stories.summary: Former Pakistani Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari told Sky News that the world lacks a "plan B" if U.S.-Iran talks scheduled in Islamabad fail, stressing the need for negotiations to achieve a peaceful resolution to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Next Ramstein meeting to take place on April 15
stories.summary: The next meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group in the Ramstein format is scheduled for April 15. Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius discussed preparations for the gathering.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel and US hold three-way-call, agree to meeting on Tuesday
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel made direct contact for the first time through a three-way phone call that included their ambassadors in Washington and the US ambassador to Lebanon. Both sides agreed to hold a US-mediated meeting on Tuesday at the State Department, as part of diplomatic efforts aimed at securing a ceasefire.

stories.title: China’s next growth engine? An AI-powered intelligence dividend
stories.summary: As China prepares its 15th five-year plan, policymakers are looking to artificial intelligence and AI agents as a potential new growth engine. The country faces a fading demographic dividend and intensifying industrial competition. The focus is shifting from growth speed to productivity gains through scaled AI deployment.

stories.title: Pope Leo slams Iran war, says 'God does not bless any conflict'
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV criticized the Iran war during a gathering of bishops in Iraq, stating that God does not bless any conflict. The pontiff expressed hope for peace while intensifying his condemnation of the ongoing hostilities.

stories.title: Wyoming man who injured wolf, taped its mouth shut and then killed it receives probation
stories.summary: Cody Roberts, 44, of Wyoming received an 18-month probation sentence for injuring a gray wolf with a snowmobile, taping its mouth shut, displaying it at a bar, and then killing it. The judge in Pinedale, Wyoming, also imposed fines but no jail time. The case drew widespread public outrage over the treatment of the animal.

stories.title: EU ‘strongly condemns’ authorisation of record number of new Israeli settlements in West Bank
stories.summary: The European Union strongly condemned Israel's decision to authorize 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank, the largest number approved by the Israeli cabinet at once. EU spokesperson Anouar El Anouni called the settlements illegal under international law, saying they severely undermine prospects for peace.

stories.title: Muslims hold first Friday prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque after reopening
stories.summary: Thousands of Muslim worshipers performed Friday prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem after it reopened following a 40-day closure imposed by Israel. The reopening drew large crowds to the holy site.

stories.title: California governor candidate Eric Swalwell accused of sexual assault by former staffer in new report – US politics live
stories.summary: California U.S. Representative Eric Swalwell, a candidate for governor, has been accused of sexual assault by a former staffer, according to a Politico report. Multiple staffers resigned from his gubernatorial campaign just before the accusation became public.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces shot down Shahed drones in West Asian countries during Iran war
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukrainian forces shot down Iranian-made Shahed drones in West Asian countries during the Iran war. He emphasized the effort was not a training exercise but part of building a functional modern air defence system for partner nations.

stories.title: The Iran war ceasefire: A guide for the informationally perplexed - opinion
stories.summary: Analysis examines whether the US and Israel have achieved their objectives in the Iran war and what the ceasefire means. The commentary highlights the difficulty of reaching clear conclusions in today's complex information environment.

stories.title: Iran says talks with US will begin once ‘preconditions are accepted’
stories.summary: Iran's delegation, led by parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, arrived in Islamabad ahead of peace talks with the US. Iranian officials stated that ceasefire negotiations would begin once their preconditions are accepted. Araghchi also reiterated the necessity for Lebanon to be included in discussions.

stories.title: Ukrainians and Russians doubt 32-hour Easter truce will lead to lasting peace
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials urged Russia on Friday to extend a ceasefire announced for Orthodox Easter weekend and resume peace talks. However, residents in both Kyiv and Moscow expressed doubt that the 32-hour truce would lead to a lasting resolution of the war.

stories.title: Trump tariff refund tool will go live on April 20, US Customs says
stories.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection announced that its tariff refund filing tool, called CAPE, will go live on April 20. The first phase will handle straightforward and recent import entries, with more complex refund cases addressed later. The move follows a February U.S. Supreme Court ruling that struck down certain duties.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Ambassador to EU believes U.S. remains ally of Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ambassador to the EU, Vsevolod Chentsov, stated that the United States remains an ally of Ukraine despite recent tensions between Kyiv and Washington. The ambassador's remarks come after months of strained relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Former Russian defence official is jailed for 19 years for corruption
stories.summary: A Russian military court sentenced former deputy defence minister Pavel Popov to 19 years in prison for corruption on Friday. The verdict was reported by state news agency RIA.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1507: Russia offers the ceasefire it already rejected from Ukraine — Zelenskyy says the real battle is for Donbas
stories.summary: On day 1,507 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia announced a unilateral Easter ceasefire days after rejecting an identical offer from Kyiv. President Zelenskyy warned that withdrawing from Donbas would open an unobstructed Russian path to Kharkiv and Dnipro. Ukraine's Special Operations Forces struck two Russian oil platforms in the Caspian Sea, nearly 1,000 km from the front lines.

stories.title: France accelerates shift to electric power amid global energy price surges
stories.summary: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced measures to reduce France's dependence on fossil fuels and accelerate a shift to electric power. The move follows a spike in global oil and gas prices caused by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Aid convoy heads from Turkey to Iran
stories.summary: The Turkish Red Crescent dispatched an aid convoy from Turkey to Iran, including four trucks carrying 48 tonnes of humanitarian supplies. The shipment contained emergency shelters for displaced families, hygiene kits, and first-aid materials.

stories.title: Moscow court orders arrest of Novaya Gazeta journalist on personal data charges
stories.summary: A Moscow court ordered the arrest of Oleg Roldugin, a journalist at the independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta, on charges of illegally using personal data.

stories.title: Brazil and US launch joint action to fight organized crime
stories.summary: Brazil and the United States announced a joint initiative to combat organized crime, involving data integration between Brazil's federal tax authority and US Customs and Border Protection. The announcement was made on Friday from São Paulo and Brasília.

stories.title: Where Do the Gulf States Go From Here?
stories.summary: The U.S. war with Iran has severely disrupted the economic model of Gulf states. The article examines the challenges facing Gulf countries as they reassess their strategic and economic positions in the aftermath of the conflict.

stories.title: Russia adds grandson of Soviet writer Alexei Tolstoy to ‘foreign agent’ registry
stories.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry added Ivan Tolstoy, a philologist and grandson of Soviet writer Alexei Tolstoy, to its registry of "foreign agents."

stories.title: China, Russia rally behind Cuba as US squeezes Havana in deepening crisis
stories.summary: China and Russia publicly backed Cuba's government amid increasing U.S. pressure on Havana. Russia's deputy foreign minister visited Cuba, while Beijing signaled willingness to strengthen diplomatic support. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China would support Cuba in safeguarding its sovereignty against external interference.

stories.title: Power outage schedules to be in effect on Saturday morning across all regions
stories.summary: Hourly electricity outage schedules were imposed across all regions of Ukraine on Saturday, April 11, affecting all categories of consumers.

stories.title: US presses Iran as talks gear up in Pakistan under fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad to lead negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the more than month-long Middle East conflict. The talks, expected to begin Saturday in the Pakistani capital, are taking place during a two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan. President Trump pressed Iran to meet U.S. demands ahead of the discussions.

stories.title: U.S.-Iran Peace Talks May Collapse Before They Even Begin
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran peace talks hosted in Islamabad face the risk of collapse before formally beginning. Tehran is demanding new conditions for dialogue, while Israel continues military strikes on Lebanon.

stories.title: Russia’s Security Council deputy chairman serves as editor-in-chief of new social studies textbooks for grades 9–11
stories.summary: Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, served as editor-in-chief of new social studies textbooks for Russian students in grades 9 through 11, as announced by Deputy Education Minister Olga Koludarova.

stories.title: Mali backs Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara
stories.summary: Mali's Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop announced on Friday that Mali supports Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara. Mali joins a growing number of African countries endorsing Rabat's proposal to resolve the 50-year conflict with the Algeria-backed Polisario Front.

stories.title: US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad: What to expect?
stories.summary: US and Iranian delegations are scheduled to meet in Islamabad, Pakistan, for peace talks aimed at ending six weeks of war between the two countries. Pakistan is serving as the host and mediator for the negotiations.

stories.title: The Iran War’s Agriculture Shock Isn’t Over Yet
stories.summary: Despite a ceasefire agreement in the U.S.-Iran conflict, disruptions to global energy and fertilizer supply chains persist. Vital agricultural input flows remain trapped, extending the war's shock to global food production.

stories.title: Worker who allegedly set fire to California warehouse compares self to Luigi Mangione
stories.summary: Chamel Abdulkarim, 29, has been charged with felony and state arson counts after allegedly setting fire to a Kimberly-Clark paper products warehouse in Ontario, California, destroying nearly $600 million in property. Authorities said Abdulkarim compared himself to Luigi Mangione in a message to co-workers after the fire.

stories.title: Report: Russia considers 20% windfall tax on corporate profits earned in 2025
stories.summary: Russian authorities are reportedly considering imposing a 20 percent windfall tax on corporate profits earned in 2025, according to the Interfax news agency.

stories.title: Withdrawing from Donbas would give Russia a free path to Kharkiv and Dnipro, Zelenskyy warns
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warned that a withdrawal from Donbas would give Russia a direct path to Kharkiv and Dnipro. He noted that building replacement fortifications would take up to 18 months and could not match the protection of the urban terrain Ukraine currently holds.

stories.title: US immigration appeals board decides Mahmoud Khalil can be deported
stories.summary: A US immigration appeals board ruled that former Columbia University student Mahmoud Khalil can be deported. His lawyers noted that the removal decision cannot be carried out while his federal case is still ongoing.

stories.title: Crispin Odey drops £79m libel claim against FT over sexual misconduct allegations
stories.summary: Former hedge fund manager Crispin Odey dropped his £79 million libel claim against the Financial Times over its reporting of sexual misconduct allegations. The FT published accounts from 20 women in 2023 alleging assault and harassment spanning five decades. Odey's lawyers said he was forced to accept the newspaper would likely succeed in its public interest defense.

stories.title: Direct Israel-Lebanon talks set for Tuesday in DC; US said pressing Israel for ceasefire
stories.summary: Direct Israel-Lebanon talks are scheduled for Tuesday in Washington, DC, with the US reportedly pressing Israel to agree to a ceasefire. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and President Trump reportedly held a tense call on Lebanon, with Netanyahu concerned the US might declare a unilateral truce with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Israeli army claims 180 Hezbollah fighters killed on Wednesday
stories.summary: The Israeli army claimed to have killed at least 180 Hezbollah fighters in strikes on Wednesday that hit 100 targets simultaneously across Lebanon, including Beirut, the Bekaa Valley, and southern Lebanon. The Lebanese health ministry reported the death toll exceeded 350 people, marking the deadliest day of attacks since the war began.

stories.title: Gunmen kill at least four people at Afghanistan picnic spot
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a picnic site near the village of Deh Mehri in Herat province, Afghanistan, killing at least four people. Officials confirmed the attackers opened fire on civilians at the location.

stories.title: Prince Harry sued for defamation by Sentebale charity he co-founded
stories.summary: Prince Harry is facing a defamation lawsuit filed by Sentebale, the charity he co-founded. A spokesperson for Harry said he categorically rejects the libel claim, calling it offensive and damaging.

stories.title: Russian forces launch nearly 50 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region, causing damage
stories.summary: On April 10, Russian forces carried out nearly 50 attacks, including drone strikes and artillery bombardments, on the Nikopol and Synelnykove districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, causing damage.

stories.title: Trump: Iranians only alive to negotiate, have no cards but 'short-term extortion' with Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Iranians have no leverage other than short-term extortion through blocking the Strait of Hormuz. He asserted they are only alive to negotiate, as US-Iran talks approached.

stories.title: Russia adds Stanford University to registry of ‘undesirable’ organizations
stories.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry added Stanford University to its registry of "undesirable" organizations, making it at least the 19th Western educational institution to receive such a designation in recent years.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia move towards potential peace deal, Bloomberg reports
stories.summary: Bloomberg News reported on Friday that Ukraine and Russia are moving toward a potential deal to end the war, citing a top aide to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.

stories.title: Working through war: Six ways Israelis can stay calm amid constant threat
stories.summary: An article offered six suggestions for Israelis to manage stress while working during ongoing security threats. The guidance addressed coping with the constant threat environment during the conflict.

stories.title: When comfort is off the table, Israelis find new ways to cope under fire
stories.summary: Israelis have been developing new emotional coping strategies during the ongoing conflict, including yoga, art workshops, online communities, and dark humor. The approaches serve as alternative support systems amid persistent security threats.

stories.title: Starmer calls Pakistan PM to emphasise importance of ‘lasting' ceasefire
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer spoke with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to express support for Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to facilitate US-Iran ceasefire talks. Both leaders agreed on the importance of sustaining the ceasefire to create conditions for lasting regional peace and stability.

stories.title: Trump's peace board faces cash crunch, stalling Gaza plan, sources say
stories.summary: Trump's Board of Peace is facing funding shortfalls that are stalling plans for Gaza, with sources saying funding has remained under $1 billion. The Iran war has exacerbated existing financial difficulties for the initiative.

stories.title: Russian drone hits apartment building in Sumy, woman injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a multi-story apartment building in the Ukrainian city of Sumy on April 10, injuring a woman.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon are expected to hold talks. What do we know?
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese officials are expected to meet in Washington next week to discuss ongoing tensions. The talks come as US President Donald Trump seeks to calm weeks of Israeli fighting with Iran-backed Hezbollah that has threatened to derail a fragile US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Vance heads to Islamabad, says Trump gave him ‘some pretty clear guidelines’ on Iran talks
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance departed for Islamabad on Friday to lead an American delegation for talks with Iranian representatives. The negotiations follow a two-week pause in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, which began with strikes on February 28, 2026. Pakistan facilitated the ceasefire after an appeal by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

stories.title: Israel strike kills 13 members of Lebanon state security
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the Nabatieh Government Complex in Lebanon killed 13 members of Lebanon's state security, the largest number of Lebanese government personnel killed at once since the war began. Lebanon's general directorate of state security condemned the attacks targeting military personnel and civilians on Lebanese soil.

stories.title: Macron undermined Israel and defied the US, then asked for a Lebanon role - comment
stories.summary: An analysis argued that France undermined Israel and defied the US, then sought a role in Lebanon peace talks. The commentary concluded that Paris failed to earn the trust needed to broker negotiations.

stories.title: Can Iran negotiations lead to peace?
stories.summary: Former Iranian and US diplomats discussed the prospects for ongoing negotiations to end the war in Iran. The conversation explored whether diplomatic efforts could realistically lead to a peace agreement.

stories.title: Vice President JD Vance: US ready to negotiate but warns Iran not to ‘play’
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance warned Iran not to negotiate in bad faith ahead of ceasefire talks in Islamabad mediated by Pakistan. Vance said the US is ready to extend an open hand if Iran negotiates in good faith, but threatened consequences otherwise. President Trump also warned of retaliation if talks fail.

stories.title: New tensions emerge before US-Iran war ceasefire talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: New tensions have emerged ahead of US-Iran ceasefire talks set to take place in Pakistan. An Iranian official stated that preconditions for negotiations have not yet been met, while President Trump renewed threats of military attacks.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A news quiz covers events from the week of April 4, including Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's preparations for elections, President Trump's threats against Iran, and a visit by Taiwan's opposition leader to China.

stories.title: Baltic states reject Russian claims of providing airspace for Ukrainian strikes
stories.summary: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania issued a joint statement through their foreign ministers rejecting Russian accusations that the Baltic states allowed their territories and airspace to be used for drone attacks against Russia.

stories.title: Dubai limits foreign flights until May 31, letters show, hitting Indian airlines hardest
stories.summary: Dubai International Airport announced it will limit foreign carriers to one round trip per day until May 31. The restrictions are expected to disproportionately affect Indian airlines.

stories.title: High fertiliser prices mean more soybeans for farmers – and greater reliance on China
stories.summary: Rising fertilizer prices, driven partly by disruptions from Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the broader Middle East conflict, are pushing U.S. farmers toward planting soybeans over corn. Dairy farmer Jeff Winton in upstate New York stopped planting corn in 2022 due to spiking input costs. The shift increases American agricultural reliance on China as a major soybean buyer.

stories.title: Pakistan PM: Ceasefire talks beginning tomorrow will be ‘make or break’
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that ceasefire talks between US and Iranian leadership would commence the following day in Islamabad. Sharif described the negotiations as a make-or-break moment for achieving a permanent ceasefire and called it a historic occasion for resolving issues through dialogue.

stories.title: Pentagon, Lockheed Martin agree to $4.7 billion PAC-3 interceptor deal
stories.summary: The Pentagon and Lockheed Martin agreed to a $4.7 billion deal for PAC-3 missile interceptors. Lockheed Martin discussed in January a goal of increasing annual PAC-3 production from approximately 600 to 2,000 interceptors over seven years.

stories.title: Romford boy, 16, charged with murder of Eghosa Ogbebor, 14, in south London
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy from Romford has been charged with the murder of 14-year-old Eghosa Ogbebor, who was fatally shot near Woolwich Dockyard train station in south-east London. The Metropolitan Police said another 16-year-old was arrested on suspicion of murder and remains in custody.

stories.title: Additional anti-drone defenses installed in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Ministry specialists from the State Special Transport Service are installing additional anti-drone defenses in frontline areas of the Donetsk region.

stories.title: IRGC commander, Iranian FM Araghchi clash over negotiating team before US-Iran talks - report
stories.summary: Reports indicated a clash between IRGC Commander-in-Chief Ahmad Vahidi and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi over control of the negotiating team ahead of US-Iran talks. Vahidi reportedly sought to limit the authority of Araghchi and parliament speaker Ghalibaf.

stories.title: WATCH: Rocket hits parking lot in Safed as Hezbollah keeps firing at northern Israel
stories.summary: A Hezbollah rocket directly struck a parking lot in Safed in northern Israel, with the IDF confirming it was a direct hit rather than shrapnel. Over 30 rockets were fired at northern Israel on Friday.

stories.title: After years of war with Russia, Ukraine's farmers are hit by Iran conflict
stories.summary: Ukrainian farmer Mykola Maliienko in Malopolovetske is planting 100 fewer hectares of corn this spring due to rising fertiliser costs linked to the war in Iran. The conflict's economic ripple effects are hitting agricultural exports from central Ukraine to Europe.

stories.title: Russia’s Internet crackdown is drawing criticism from state-sanctioned ‘opposition’ parties. It’s all part of Kremlin-approved campaign messaging.
stories.summary: At the New People party congress in St. Petersburg in early March, Kremlin official Alexander Kharichev read a message from President Putin amid large-scale mobile internet disruptions in Moscow. State-sanctioned opposition parties have begun criticizing Russia's internet crackdowns as part of Kremlin-approved campaign messaging.

stories.title: Lebanon: Death toll from Israeli strikes on Wednesday rises to 357
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that the death toll from Israeli strikes on Wednesday rose to 357. The bombardment was described as the heaviest since the latest wave of Israeli attacks on Lebanon began six weeks ago.

stories.title: Israel approves 34 new West Bank settlements: report
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet approved the establishment of 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank, according to the watchdog Peace Now and Israeli media. The decision was reportedly taken secretly in early April, adding to 68 settlements already approved since Prime Minister Netanyahu's government took power in 2022.

stories.title: Pakistan Walks a Tightrope on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan is hosting U.S.-Iran peace talks in Islamabad while simultaneously maintaining a security partnership with Saudi Arabia. The balancing act reflects Islamabad's complex diplomatic position between rival regional powers.

stories.title: Iranians sceptical, afraid ahead of talks on ending war
stories.summary: Many Iranians express scepticism and fear ahead of talks aimed at ending the war, with some wanting regime change but feeling threatened by apocalyptic rhetoric from the U.S. president.

stories.title: In pictures: Sikh pilgrims arrive in Pakistan from India to celebrate Baisakhi festival
stories.summary: The first group of Sikh pilgrims arrived in Pakistan from India via the Wagah border to celebrate the Baisakhi harvest festival. Pakistan issued visas to 2,800 Indian Sikh pilgrims, with the main ceremony scheduled for April 14 at Gurdwara Panja Sahib in Hasan Abdal.

stories.title: Exclusive: What the Lebanese government wants from talks with Israel
stories.summary: The Lebanese government is seeking to establish a new negotiation format that would give it equal standing in discussions about Lebanon's future. A Lebanese delegation is scheduled to meet Israeli officials in Washington next week, amid pressures from Israel, Iran, and the US.

stories.title: UK police arrest man after four die during Channel crossing attempt
stories.summary: UK authorities arrested a Sudanese man after four people died during an attempted Channel crossing. The National Crime Agency said the suspect was detained on suspicion of endangering another person.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces hit key enemy sites in occupied areas and inside Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck multiple logistical and other key Russian military facilities overnight on April 10, targeting occupied areas and sites inside Russia to reduce Russian offensive capabilities.

stories.title: French man charged with locking son in van for more than a year
stories.summary: A French man has been charged with locking his son in a van for more than a year. The boy was found malnourished, naked, lying next to human excrement, and unable to walk, according to prosecutors.

stories.title: UK to convene more talks on Strait of Hormuz next week
stories.summary: Britain announced plans to convene another round of talks with allies next week on reopening the Strait of Hormuz without paying tolls to Iran. Discussions may include coordinated sanctions and efforts to secure the release of ships held in the strait.

stories.title: Russia’s An-series military transports were designed in Kyiv — and Moscow’s leaked documents show 143 of its 368 military Antonovs need urgent repair
stories.summary: Leaked internal documents from Russia's Aviaremont repair plant reveal that 143 of Russia's 368 military Antonov transport aircraft need urgent repair. The facility has spent all its government contract advances, cannot source parts for the Ukrainian-designed aircraft, and was borrowing money to pay wages as of January 2026.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer and Trump discussed military options for Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and US President Donald Trump discussed military options for keeping the Strait of Hormuz open. UK Defence Secretary John Healey said they are pursuing both diplomatic and military plans.

stories.title: “Cultural propagandists” – Ukraine sanctions five Russian participants in the Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Ukraine sanctioned five Russian participants in the Venice Biennale, labeling them cultural propagandists. Those sanctioned include the daughter of a Rostec arms executive appointed as pavilion commissioner and a Putin envoy who described the war as an important historical moment.

stories.title: The Charisma Wars
stories.summary: An analysis explores the growing importance of personal charisma over policy substance in global politics. The piece examines how political leaders worldwide increasingly rely on personality-driven appeal.

stories.title: Over 100,000 Muslim worshipers at Al-Aqsa in first Friday prayers after Jerusalem holy sites reopen
stories.summary: Over 100,000 Muslim worshipers attended Friday prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque on Jerusalem's Temple Mount after holy sites reopened. The mosque and other Muslim, Christian, and Jewish holy sites had been largely closed to the public due to safety restrictions amid Iranian missile fire.

stories.title: Exclusive: What the Lebanese government wants from talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and President Joseph Aoun are seeking to keep Lebanon safe while distancing the country from Iran in upcoming talks with Israel. The negotiations aim to address Lebanon's security concerns amid the ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin envoy's US visit does not mean Ukraine talks have resumed
stories.summary: The Kremlin stated on April 10 that a visit to the United States by President Vladimir Putin's special investment envoy should not be interpreted as a resumption of negotiations over a potential peace deal in Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister: Lebanon must be included in ceasefire deal
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Lebanon must be included in any US-Iran ceasefire deal. He made the remarks in a phone call to Iran's envoy to Lebanon, condemning Israel's ongoing strikes on the country.

stories.title: US Navy ends USS Boise submarine overhaul after price tag soars
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy terminated a maintenance overhaul of the submarine USS Boise after costs escalated beyond the initial $1.2 billion budget set when work began in 2024. The decision reflects ongoing challenges with rising costs in naval vessel maintenance.

stories.title: Details of U.S. troops based in Europe as Trump mulls removing some
stories.summary: President Donald Trump has discussed with advisers the possibility of withdrawing some U.S. troops stationed in Europe. Reuters reported the deliberations, citing a senior White House official on April 10.

stories.title: Russia stepping up assaults across frontline, 61 combat clashes reported
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 61 combat clashes against Ukrainian positions, with the heaviest fighting reported in the Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk, Huliaipole, Northern Slobozhanshchyna, and Kursk sectors of the front line.

stories.title: UN rights chief condemns ‘unrelenting pattern of killings’ conducted with 'impunity' in Gaza
stories.summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk condemned the ongoing killing of Palestinians in Gaza despite an alleged ceasefire. Turk described an unrelenting pattern of killings reflecting disregard for Palestinian lives enabled by impunity.

stories.title: US pushes to renew ties with Peru ahead of uncertain election
stories.summary: As Peru heads into the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, the United States is intensifying efforts to strengthen influence in the major copper-producing nation. Washington's push comes as China has become an increasingly important strategic partner for Peru.

stories.title: Russia sentences former deputy defense minister to 19 years in prison and strips him of his general rank
stories.summary: A Moscow military court sentenced former Deputy Defense Minister Pavel Popov to 19 years in a maximum-security prison on April 10 for embezzling 25.8 million rubles from the Patriot military park. He was also stripped of his general rank.

stories.title: Russia Designates Stanford University as ‘Undesirable’
stories.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry designated Stanford University as an "undesirable" organization, making the California-based institution at least the 19th Western university or educational program to receive the label in the past five years.

stories.title: Jewish-owned Israeli restaurant vandalized in Munich; police suspect antisemitic motive
stories.summary: A Jewish-owned Israeli restaurant called Eclipse Grillbar was vandalized in Munich, Germany. Investigators believe pyrotechnic devices were thrown into the establishment, breaking several windows. Police suspect an antisemitic motive; no arrests have been made.

stories.title: Reform UK local election candidate was twice disciplined by Tories over ‘racist comments’
stories.summary: A Reform UK candidate standing in upcoming English council elections was previously disciplined twice by the Conservative Party over alleged racist comments. Derek Bullock was disowned by the Tories in 2023 after allegedly using a racial slur. Another Reform candidate was found to have shared Covid conspiracy theories.

stories.title: Moscow residents receive notifications warning of mobile internet restrictions
stories.summary: Residents of several Moscow neighborhoods received official notifications on April 10 warning of mobile internet restrictions imposed for stated "security purposes."

stories.title: Starmer says NATO in US's 'interests' as Gulf tour ends
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer defended NATO as being in America's interests during a visit to the Gulf region. His remarks came amid renewed criticism of the alliance by US President Donald Trump and threats of a US withdrawal.

stories.title: Trump: Only reason Iranians are alive ‘is to negotiate’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Iranians have "no cards" and stated "the only reason they are alive is to negotiate." The remarks came as a ceasefire between the US and Iran hung in the balance ahead of peace talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: Is the US-Iran ceasefire already doomed?
stories.summary: Analysts are assessing whether the US-Iran ceasefire talks are likely to fail. Even if negotiations do not produce a formal deal, observers suggest a return to full-scale war may still be avoided.

stories.title: OIC condemns Israeli approval of 34 new West Bank settlements
stories.summary: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation condemned Israel's approval of 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank. The Palestinian Presidency's office called the plan a flagrant violation of international law.

stories.title: The Fight Over the Future of Meat
stories.summary: An article examines the global competition over the future of meat production and alternative proteins. It draws a parallel with the U.S. losing the electric vehicle race to China, warning that a similar dynamic could emerge in the food sector.

stories.title: In March, 572 hectares of farmland cleared under compensation program
stories.summary: Under a Ukrainian state compensation program, mine action operators cleared 572 hectares of agricultural land in March to make farmland safe for use again.

stories.title: California coffee chain faces backlash after pledge to remove Pride flags
stories.summary: Philz Coffee, a San Francisco-based chain with locations across California, is facing backlash after announcing plans to remove Pride flags from its stores. A petition with 4,000 signatures criticized the decision, saying the company built its success in part on support from the LGBTQ+ community.

stories.title: Pope urges dialogue and condemns 'collateral damage' in war for 'self-interest'
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned the spread of violence through sacred places in the Christian East ahead of US-Iran ceasefire talks in Pakistan. In posts on X, he said no cause could justify the shedding of innocent blood and called for dialogue.

stories.title: Remaining in Nato is in best interests of US, says Keir Starmer
