stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said it is in the best interests of the United States to remain in NATO, pushing back against President Trump's threats to leave the alliance. Speaking at the end of a Gulf trip focused on the Iran ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Starmer also urged European members to increase their contributions.

stories.title: Ex-Deputy Defense Minister Pavel Popov Jailed 19 Years on Corruption Charges
stories.summary: Former Deputy Defense Minister Pavel Popov was sentenced to 19 years in prison on corruption charges. His arrest in August 2024 was part of a broader military shake-up that included the dismissal of Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and criminal investigations against senior officials.

stories.title: Labour MPs propose specialist sexual offences courts to help trials backlog
stories.summary: Labour MPs in the UK proposed amendments to the government's courts bill, calling for specialist sexual offences courts with fixed trial dates to address the trials backlog. The amendments aim to block broader government plans to reduce eligibility for jury trials in England and Wales.

stories.title: Shin Bet chief 'downplaying' settler terror surge in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that Shin Bet chief David Zini has been downplaying a surge in settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank, characterizing them as friction. Former Israeli security leaders have warned of escalating settler violence.

stories.title: Former IS group child ‘fighters’ jailed in Iraq seek repatriation to France
stories.summary: Three French men who were taken to Syria as children by jihadist parents and forced to work for the Islamic State group are seeking repatriation from Iraq. They are among thousands of IS-affiliated detainees transferred from Syria to Iraqi custody earlier this year.

stories.title: One dead and 27 injured after bus with British passengers crashes in Canary Islands
stories.summary: A man died and 27 people were hospitalized after a bus carrying British passengers veered into a ravine on the GM-2 highway near San Sebastián de La Gomera in the Canary Islands. The crash occurred at 1:15 p.m. local time on Friday while the tour group was being transported for a boat excursion.

stories.title: Prince Harry sued for defamation by charity he co-founded
stories.summary: Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, is being sued for defamation by Sentebale, the African charity he co-founded. The charity filed papers in London's High Court naming Harry and former trustee Mark Dyer as defendants. The legal action follows Harry's resignation as patron and a public dispute with the charity's chair.

stories.title: Trump threatens new strikes on Iran if talks fail
stories.summary: President Trump warned that US warships are being reloaded with weapons to strike Iran if ceasefire talks in Pakistan fail. He stated the military would use them "very effectively" if no deal is reached.

stories.title: Syria FM backs Hezbollah disarmament, condemns Israel occupation
stories.summary: Syria's foreign minister expressed support for the disarmament of Hezbollah and condemned Israel's military strikes on Lebanon. He also blamed Iran for the devastation Syria has experienced.

stories.title: Israeli settlers repeatedly try to sacrifice animals at al-Aqsa
stories.summary: There has been a reported increase in attempts by Israeli settlers to sacrifice animals at the al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem. The incidents have fueled concerns about a potential takeover of the Muslim holy site.

stories.title: Defense forces strike two drilling rigs in Caspian Sea
stories.summary: On the night of April 10, the Ukrainian Armed Forces struck two drilling platforms on the Caspian Sea shelf, targeting infrastructure allegedly supplying Russian military forces.

stories.title: War in numbers: US hit tens of thousands of targets in Iran, but capabilities remain
stories.summary: The Pentagon reported striking over 13,000 targets in Iran during Operation Epic Fury, including missiles, launchers, navy ships, and factories. Despite the heavy US bombardment, Iran's military firing capabilities reportedly remained steady.

stories.title: Man arrested after four die trying to cross Channel in small boat
stories.summary: A 27-year-old Sudanese national was arrested by National Crime Agency investigators on suspicion of endangering life after four people — two men and two women — died during a small boat Channel crossing on Thursday. The victims were swept away by currents while attempting to board a dinghy off the French coast.

stories.title: Experts warn ‘damage already done’ to food production from Hormuz closure
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization warned that damage to global food production from the Strait of Hormuz closure has already been done. FAO chief economist Maximo Torero said recovery would be long and uneven even if the strait reopened immediately, due to disrupted fertiliser supplies.

stories.title: Concerns raised about motorbike tourist trail after death of British teenager in Vietnam
stories.summary: A 19-year-old British gap-year student, Orla Wates from Surrey, died after falling off a motorcycle and being struck by a truck on the Ha Giang loop in northern Vietnam. The incident has heightened safety concerns about the popular but rugged mountain trail, which locals describe as unpredictable and congested.

stories.title: Back from the brink in Iran? Not while Palestine, Lebanon burn
stories.summary: An analysis argued that lasting peace in the Gulf and broader Middle East cannot be achieved without addressing the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and Israeli actions in Lebanon. The piece contended that the Greater Israel project poses a threat to regional stability.

stories.title: World Food Programme warns Lebanon facing food security crisis due to Iran war
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that Lebanon faces a food security crisis linked to the Iran conflict. Many traders reported having less than one week of essential food stocks remaining.

stories.title: Police investigating after explosive devices damage Israeli restaurant in Munich
stories.summary: Police in Munich are investigating after explosive devices damaged an Israeli restaurant owned by Jewish proprietors. Authorities are examining whether the attack was motivated by antisemitism.

stories.title: Palestinian shot dead during Israeli settler attack on occupied West Bank village
stories.summary: A Palestinian was shot and killed during an Israeli settler attack on a village in the occupied West Bank. The incident occurred as former Israeli security chiefs warned that government-sponsored settler violence had spiraled out of control.

stories.title: UAE hands Bahrain financial lifeline as Iran war shocks economy
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it would provide up to 20 billion Emirati dirhams in liquidity to Bahrain to stabilize its finances. The financial lifeline comes as the Iran war has delivered shocks to the Bahraini economy.

stories.title: Doctors’ leader claims new reduced pay offer killed chances of ending strikes in England
stories.summary: Dr. Jack Fletcher, a leader of resident doctors in England, accused government ministers of undermining a potential deal to end strikes by suddenly reducing their pay offer. The dispute has led to a 15th round of strikes by resident doctors, disrupting NHS services this week.

stories.title: Ukrainians sceptical as Russia’s Putin orders Easter truce
stories.summary: Russia announced a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire beginning Saturday afternoon, following a proposal originally made by Kyiv. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine was willing to reciprocate, but Ukrainian citizens expressed skepticism about Russia's commitment to honoring the truce.

stories.title: When Washington came to Pakistan: a brief history
stories.summary: Pakistan is hosting talks between Iran and the United States in Islamabad on Saturday, April 11, after brokering a ceasefire in the Middle East conflict. The delegations include U.S. Vice President JD Vance and Iranian Foreign Ministry officials.

stories.title: Ukraine’s presidential office chief says peace deal with Russia is close
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's presidential office, told Bloomberg he does not expect a peace settlement with Russia to take long. Budanov is a key participant in the ongoing peace negotiations.

stories.title: Starmer and Trump talked military options to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated that he and US President Donald Trump discussed military capabilities and options to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blocked amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: TotalEnergies says Saudi refinery offline after strikes
stories.summary: French energy company TotalEnergies reported that a Saudi Arabian refinery went offline following strikes. Saudi Arabia produces around 10 million barrels of crude oil per day, most of which transits through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin envoy's U.S. visit does not mean Ukraine talks have resumed
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that the visit of Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev to the United States does not constitute a resumption of negotiations over the Ukraine conflict. Peskov clarified that Dmitriev is not negotiating a settlement regarding Ukraine.

stories.title: Government simplifies public procurement rules to protect critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers approved amendments to public procurement regulations to streamline processes for protecting critical infrastructure. The changes aim to improve community preparedness for wartime challenges.

stories.title: New Israeli app tracks disaster victims in real time, speeds emergency response
stories.summary: Israeli developer Shmuel Fitoussi created an app that tracks disaster victims in real time by connecting live data entry to resident profiles, improving emergency coordination and response times.

stories.title: Israeli settlers turn Passover into celebration of ethnic cleansing
stories.summary: Palestinians displaced by Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank reported the destruction of their communities. Settlers were reported to have celebrated the forced expulsions of Palestinian residents during the Passover holiday.

stories.title: Israeli military: Lebanon fired 30 rockets, reservist seriously injured
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported that 30 rockets were fired from Lebanon toward northern Israel. A reservist officer was seriously wounded and a soldier lightly injured in a drone attack in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy rescues 18 crew members, including foreign nationals, of merchant vessel in Arabian Sea operation
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy rescued 18 crew members, including nationals of China, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Vietnam, and Indonesia, from the merchant vessel MV Gold Autumn in the North Arabian Sea. The ship was located approximately 370 kilometers off Pakistan's coast following a distress call.

stories.title: Chimpanzees in Uganda locked in vicious 'civil war', say researchers
stories.summary: Researchers report that the Ngogo chimpanzee community in Uganda has been engaged in an intense intra-group conflict for the past eight years, splitting a once close-knit group.

stories.title: African space council chief wins top award
stories.summary: Tidiane Ouattara, head of the African space council, received the Aerospace Innovation Award in recognition of his contributions to advancing space science and technology across Africa.

stories.title: From battlefields to data centres: The US-Iran war in the age of AI
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israel war with Iran in 2026 has highlighted how AI has transformed modern warfare, blurring the line between military and civilian infrastructure. Data centers, software engineers, and civilian technologies have become both enablers of military power and vulnerable targets.

stories.title: Navy to mothball USS Boise, capping off years of maintenance challenges
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy announced it will mothball the submarine USS Boise after years of persistent maintenance challenges. Officials described the decision as part of a broader data-driven initiative to optimize the overall composition and readiness of the Navy's fleet.

stories.title: 'Trump harbors an unexplained sympathy for Vladimir Putin', Ukrainian analyst says
stories.summary: Ukrainian analyst Peter Zalmayev of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative questioned why President Trump has not pressured Russia to end its war in Ukraine, despite brokering a ceasefire with Iran. He suggested Trump harbors an unexplained sympathy for Russian President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Russia’s Black Sea oil hub resumes loading amid sustained Ukrainian drone campaign
stories.summary: One berth has resumed crude oil loading at Russia's largest Black Sea export hub, though the full recovery timeline remains uncertain amid an ongoing Ukrainian drone campaign targeting the facility.

stories.title: Netanyahu removes Spain from Gaza coordination centre over ‘hostility’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu removed Spain from a Gaza coordination centre, accusing Madrid of waging a diplomatic war against Israel. The move reflects escalating tensions between Israel and Spain over the conflict.

stories.title: Kuwaiti army says Iran attacked National Guard facilities, injuring personnel
stories.summary: Kuwait's army reported that Iran fired seven drones into Kuwaiti airspace over 24 hours, targeting National Guard-linked facilities and injuring personnel. Iran's Revolutionary Guard denied launching missiles at any country during ceasefire hours.

stories.title: Israel: Hezbollah rocket from Lebanon strikes Safed, injuring several people
stories.summary: Emergency services responded in Safed on April 10 after a Hezbollah rocket fired from Lebanon struck the northern Israeli city, injuring several people. Crews treated casualties and secured the area.

stories.title: Trump’s war and Melania’s Epstein statement, with US editor Betsy Reed – The Latest
stories.summary: Melania Trump made a public statement at the White House denying any relationship with Jeffrey Epstein or Ghislaine Maxwell and calling on Congress to hold public hearings with Epstein's victims. The announcement came as political attention had been focused on the US-Iran war and concerns about the fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Four men deported by US to Eswatini have right to see lawyer, court rules
stories.summary: Eswatini's supreme court ruled that four men deported by the US to the southern African country have the right to see a local lawyer. The men, from Cambodia, Cuba, Vietnam, and Yemen, were sent to Eswatini in July despite having no connection to the country and had been denied in-person legal counsel for nine months.

stories.title: Friday recap: key events from the day in the US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran will not negotiate with the US until Israeli strikes on Lebanon halt and Iran's blocked assets are released. Israeli attacks on Lebanon continued, with 14 people killed in strikes on the Nabatieh governorate.

stories.title: British PM Starmer says Trump’s Iran rhetoric is contrary to UK values
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer criticised President Trump's rhetoric on Iran as contrary to UK values. Britain also declared it would not accept tolls imposed by the U.S. or Iran on passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: SSU warns of possible provocations, terrorist attacks, and sabotage over Easter
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SSU) has warned citizens of possible provocations, terrorist attacks, and sabotage during the Easter holiday period. The agency urged the public to remain vigilant and follow safety guidelines.

stories.title: Novaya Gazeta says security forces have no complaints against its editorial office after 13-hour search
stories.summary: The independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta reported that security forces who searched its Moscow offices on April 9 for 13 hours found no complaints against the editorial office or its website. The newspaper communicated the outcome to readers via a newsletter.

stories.title: Meme Wars
stories.summary: The article examines how President Trump has upended traditional norms of diplomatic communication, with other countries adopting similar unconventional approaches. The shift involves the use of memes and informal rhetoric in international relations.

stories.title: Chinese, Taiwanese will unite, Xi tells Taiwan opposition leader
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in Beijing, expressing confidence that Chinese and Taiwanese people would unite. Cheng is the first KMT leader to visit China in a decade, a move that has sparked debate in Taiwan.

stories.title: Hamas delegation to hold Cairo talks with Board of Peace envoy
stories.summary: A Hamas delegation is holding talks with Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov in Cairo. The negotiations come as Gaza marks six months of a frequently violated ceasefire.

stories.title: UK doctor suspended for sending Islamophobic messages about Gaza to colleague
stories.summary: A UK medical tribunal suspended doctor Cindy Nonoo-Cohen for sending Islamophobic messages to a colleague who had circulated a petition in support of Gaza. The tribunal described the comments as deplorable.

stories.title: Nigeria’s aso-oke weaving tradition gains global spotlight
stories.summary: The town of Iseyin in southwestern Nigeria has become a hub for weaving aso-oke, a traditional handmade Yoruba fabric, as the centuries-old craft gains increasing international recognition.

stories.title: Milei to light Israel celebration torches with 'genocidal' rabbi
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei plans to light torches for Israel's Independence Day celebration alongside a rabbi accused of advocating for and participating in the destruction of Gaza.

stories.title: ‘We thought Beirut was going to collapse’: recounting the deadliest day of the war with Israel
stories.summary: Israel launched unannounced strikes on Beirut and other parts of Lebanon on Wednesday, killing more than 300 people and wounding at least 1,000 in the deadliest day of the renewed conflict. Residents, lawyers, doctors, and aid workers described widespread chaos and destruction.

stories.title: Lebanon gripped by uncertainty over Iran-US ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanon faces heightened uncertainty following recent Israeli attacks, with the UN describing conditions as a "perfect storm." Direct talks between Lebanon and Israel are being considered to address the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Iranian parliament speaker says no talks until Lebanon ceasefire and assets released
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf announced via X that Iran will not engage in peace talks with the US until Israeli strikes on Lebanon cease and Iran's frozen assets are released. He called Lebanon and the Resistance Axis inseparable from any ceasefire.

stories.title: WFP warns Lebanon facing food security crisis due Israeli war
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that Lebanon faces a food security crisis due to the Israeli military campaign. Lebanon's Ministry of Economy said the country's food stocks are sufficient for only three to four months.

stories.title: Survivors of Epstein’s abuse accuse Melania Trump of ‘shifting burden’ on to victims
stories.summary: More than a dozen survivors of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse accused First Lady Melania Trump of shifting the burden onto victims after she called for Congress to hold public hearings. The survivors noted they had already demonstrated courage by coming forward, filing reports, and providing testimony.

stories.title: Girl, 9, in a critical condition with meningococcal infection after holiday in Japan
stories.summary: A nine-year-old girl from Hong Kong is in critical condition in the paediatric intensive care unit of Princess Margaret Hospital in Kwai Chung after contracting invasive meningococcal infection. She developed symptoms after visiting Japan during the Easter holiday. Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection has contacted other members of her tour group as a precaution.

stories.title: How Iran Hawks Are Viewing the Cease-Fire
stories.summary: Former National Security Adviser John Bolton discussed the US-Iran ceasefire from a hawkish perspective, expressing the view that President Trump should have continued military operations rather than agreeing to halt the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes two Russian oil platforms in the Caspian Sea, nearly 1,000 km from the front
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck two Russian oil platforms in the Caspian Sea, approximately 1,000 kilometers from the front lines. Kyiv stated the platforms supply fuel and lubricants to Russian military forces, classifying them as legitimate military targets.

stories.title: FM on Easter ceasefire: Ukraine ready to respond in kind, details pending
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Ukraine is prepared to observe an Easter ceasefire on a reciprocal basis. He stated that Ukraine is waiting to see where and when the ceasefire takes effect before responding.

stories.title: JD Vance expects ‘positive’ US-Iran war talks as he departs for Pakistan
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said he expected positive outcomes from upcoming US-Iran talks as he departed for Pakistan. Vance stated that President Trump had provided clear guidelines and that progress depended on Iran negotiating in good faith.

stories.title: Dagestan Was Already Facing an Infrastructure Crisis. Then Came the Floods.
stories.summary: Dagestan, a republic in Russia's North Caucasus, is experiencing its worst flooding in over a century. The disaster has compounded existing infrastructure challenges in the region.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF destroys Hezbollah rocket launcher that fired from inside school in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it destroyed a Hezbollah rocket launcher that had been positioned inside a school in Lebanon, condemning the group's use of civilian infrastructure for military purposes.

stories.title: US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad face massive hurdles
stories.summary: Analyst Ali Vaez warned that upcoming US-Iran talks face significant obstacles due to a deep deficit of trust between the two sides. The negotiations are set to take place in Islamabad, Pakistan.

stories.title: In pictures: Heavy security in Islamabad ahead of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Islamabad was placed on red alert ahead of U.S.-Iran peace talks, with more than 10,000 police and security personnel deployed throughout the capital. The military is supervising the multi-tiered security arrangement, assisted by Rangers, Islamabad Police, and Punjab Police.

stories.title: Israel excludes France from talks with Lebanon, sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Israel has excluded France from upcoming talks with Lebanon, with an Israeli official stating that France's conduct over the past year led Israel to view it as an unfair mediator.

stories.title: European countries boost Russian LNG imports by 17% as Middle East war cuts Qatar shipments, Financial Times reports
stories.summary: European imports of liquefied natural gas from Russia's Yamal LNG facility rose 17 percent in the first quarter of 2026, reaching five million tons, according to the Financial Times citing analytics firm Kpler. The increase came as the Middle East war disrupted Qatari LNG shipments.

stories.title: DIA centralizes AI efforts with Digital Modernization Accelerator
stories.summary: The Defense Intelligence Agency established a new Digital Modernization Accelerator to centralize its artificial intelligence efforts. DIA Chief AI Officer Maj. Gen. Robert Kinney urged his team to move with urgency, emphasizing the competitive pressure driving the agency's modernization push.

stories.title: U.S., Iran prepare for ceasefire talks as Netanyahu authorises negotiations with Lebanon
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are preparing for ceasefire talks in Pakistan, while Israel and Lebanon are expected to begin separate negotiations at the State Department in Washington. Both diplomatic tracks could advance broader ceasefire efforts across West Asia.

stories.title: Seyed Hossein Mousavian: Could the Islamabad talks end 48 years of hostility between the US and Iran?
stories.summary: Former Iranian diplomat Seyed Hossein Mousavian examined whether the Islamabad talks could end 48 years of US-Iran hostility. He noted the two-week ceasefire followed 40 days of military confrontation involving Iran, the US, and Israel.

stories.title: Beirut hospitals overwhelmed, survivors recount carnage scenes
stories.summary: Beirut hospitals were overwhelmed with casualties the day after intense Israeli strikes on Lebanon's capital that marked the deadliest day in over five weeks of renewed war between Israel and Hezbollah. Survivors recounted scenes of carnage as medical facilities struggled to cope with the surge of wounded.

stories.title: France's drone minehunters target Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: France has deployed drone-equipped minehunting ships to help clear naval mines from the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has declared are placed across a large section of the passage. A French company developed the mine-hunting vessel, which uses high-performance drones to detect and destroy underwater mines.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts hurtle home from moon toward splashdown
stories.summary: The four Artemis II astronauts were returning to Earth on Friday aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft after completing the first crewed moon voyage in over half a century. The 10-day mission was concluding with a planned splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California following atmospheric re-entry.

stories.title: Netanyahu requests delay in his corruption trial testimony, citing security developments
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu requested a two-week delay in his corruption trial testimony, citing classified security developments. The trial had previously been suspended during the Iran war.

stories.title: US and Iran prepare for ceasefire talks as Netanyahu authorises negotiations with Lebanon
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiators prepared for high-level ceasefire talks as their existing truce remained fragile, with Israel and Hezbollah continuing to exchange fire and Iran maintaining control over the Strait of Hormuz. Reporting came from Doha, Qatar, where diplomatic efforts were underway.

stories.title: 'We can provide more durable cooperation with Gulf countries', Ukraine defence industry chief says
stories.summary: Ihor Fedirko, CEO of the Ukrainian Council of Defence Industry, said Kyiv is pursuing durable cooperation with Gulf states on drone defence technology, a partnership accelerated by the Middle East war. He stated Ukraine can produce nearly $55 billion in weaponry annually and aims to reach $10 billion in exports within five years.

stories.title: Inside the Iran war decision making: NYT describes how Trump chose to go to war
stories.summary: A New York Times report detailed how President Trump decided to go to war with Iran, weighing his instincts against the deep concerns of Vice President Vance and a pessimistic intelligence assessment. The report outlined the internal deliberations within the administration leading up to the conflict.

stories.title: Israel expels Spanish representatives from Gaza humanitarian relief centre
stories.summary: Israel announced the expulsion of Spanish representatives from the Civil-Military Coordination Center in Kiryat Gat, which oversees humanitarian aid delivery to Gaza. Prime Minister Netanyahu said the decision followed Spain's criticism of Israeli soldiers.

stories.title: Cloud of uncertainty over US-Iran talks in Pakistan as sides trade accusations
stories.summary: Scheduled US-Iran talks in Pakistan were clouded by uncertainty on Friday, with no confirmation of negotiators' arrivals and both sides accusing the other of failing to implement the ceasefire. President Trump expressed displeasure over Iran's handling of the Strait of Hormuz, while Tehran demanded Israeli strikes on Lebanon also fall under the agreement.

stories.title: Honorary consul in Monaco: Ukraine’s reconstruction already underway
stories.summary: Ukraine's honorary consul in Monaco said the principality will serve as a hub for investment in Ukraine's reconstruction, a process already underway. The total cost of reconstruction is currently estimated at approximately $588 billion.

stories.title: At Least 2 Killed in Blast at Fireworks Warehouse in North Ossetia-Alania
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in an explosion at a fireworks warehouse in Vladikavkaz, the capital of North Ossetia-Alania in southern Russia. Local authorities reported a powerful blast in the city center, with an increasing number of people hospitalized with injuries.

stories.title: France's Macron talks war, peace and basketball with Pope Leo
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV and French President Emmanuel Macron held their first meeting at the Vatican on Friday, discussing the Iran war and Middle East crisis resolution. Macron also presented the pope with a signed French national basketball team jersey among his gifts.

stories.title: UK campaign backs Abu Sittah as GMC moves to overturn acquittal
stories.summary: A UK campaign was launched to defend Dr. Ghassan Abu Sittah after the General Medical Council moved to appeal a tribunal ruling that had cleared him. The allegations were linked to his exposure of Israeli actions during the Gaza conflict.

stories.title: China’s Li Qiang urges faster industrial AI adoption at meeting with Moonshot AI founder
stories.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Moonshot AI founder Yang Zhilin at a high-level symposium on economic resilience and growth. Li urged faster adoption of artificial intelligence in China's industrial and manufacturing sectors. The meeting reflects Beijing's push to accelerate digital transformation of its economy.

stories.title: Tripoli zoo reopens to offer Libyans rare respite from violence
stories.summary: Tripoli's zoo in Libya reopened after a 17-year closure caused by the country's prolonged conflict. The facility, originally shut for renovations, was unable to reopen due to ongoing violence.

stories.title: At the impossible table: The diplomatic maze awaiting the world in Islamabad
stories.summary: Islamabad is hosting high-stakes peace negotiations between the United States and Iran, with U.S. Vice President JD Vance leading the American delegation. The talks aim to establish a lasting settlement to the ongoing U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: ‘Anti-Israel obsession’: Israel boots Spanish representatives from Gaza ceasefire HQ
stories.summary: Israel removed Spanish representatives from the Gaza ceasefire coordination centre. Foreign Minister Sa'ar said Spain had lost its ability to serve as a useful actor, while Netanyahu vowed consequences for countries waging a diplomatic war against Israel.

stories.title: PMDC expresses ‘deep concern’ at suspected suicide of medical student in Mirpurkhas
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council expressed deep concern over the suspected suicide of a 21-year-old third-year medical student in Mirpurkhas. The student's family has accused a teacher and fellow students of harassment prior to her death.

stories.title: Inflation rises in US amid Iran war, Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: A US government report showed inflation rising amid the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Gasoline prices increased by 21.2 percent in March, with petrol remaining above $4 per gallon despite a truce.

stories.title: Pakistan takes rare global stage in US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan is taking on a prominent diplomatic role by hosting U.S.-Iran talks expected to begin on April 11, marking a rare turn on the global stage for Islamabad.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian interceptors downed Iran drones in the Middle East
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukrainian interceptor systems shot down Iranian drones in the Middle East. He noted that 228 Ukrainian military experts had previously been deployed to the region.

stories.title: Russia dismissed Ukraine’s Easter truce offer – then declared its own days later
stories.summary: Russia rejected Ukraine's proposal for an Easter ceasefire but then announced its own days later. A similar Russian-declared ceasefire the previous year was reportedly violated more than 2,000 times.

stories.title: EU airline industry warns of fuel shortages if Strait of Hormuz stays closed
stories.summary: The trade body representing European airports warned that continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz could lead to aviation fuel shortages within three weeks across the EU airline industry.

stories.title: From the Nile to the Euphrates: Inside Israel's expansionist ambitions
stories.summary: The article examines the concept of "Greater Israel," noting that Israel has never officially defined its borders while some settlers and government ministers advocate for territorial expansion based on biblical boundaries.

stories.title: Iran war is defeat for US, John Mearsheimer tells Arab Centre DC
stories.summary: Experts at the Arab Center in Washington assessed that the US is losing its war with Iran, warning of escalating risks to global stability and domestic political consequences for the administration.

stories.title: Labor’s planned gambling ad limits have influencer ‘blind spots’, experts warn
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government faces criticism over its proposed partial ban on gambling advertising, with experts and crossbench senators warning of blind spots regarding influencers, podcasters, and social media platforms. Independent Senator David Pocock said the gambling industry is adept at quickly pivoting to exploit new mediums.

stories.title: China banks buffer against AI contagions as US sweats over Anthropic’s Mythos
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell reportedly held urgent talks over cybersecurity concerns related to Anthropic's latest AI model, Mythos. Experts warned of potential economic damage in the hundreds of billions of dollars. Chinese banks, meanwhile, were said to be taking a more cautious approach, prioritizing financial stability.

stories.title: Spain Is the Friend That the United States Needs
stories.summary: The article argues that Spain has been a valuable ally to the United States during the Iran war and in broader geopolitical matters, sometimes acting more effectively in defense of US interests than Washington itself.

stories.title: Starmer faces reckoning over his support for Trump's illegal war on Iran
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces political backlash over his support for US military operations against Iran, with Labour potentially facing losses in local elections. US Air Force assets have been operating from RAF Fairford in England.

stories.title: Hungary: Is Viktor Orban Russia's 'Trojan horse' in the EU?
stories.summary: Hungary holds legislative elections on Sunday, with Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin under scrutiny. His frequent meetings with Putin, opposition to EU aid for Ukraine, and reported live briefings to the Kremlin on EU summits have drawn criticism within the bloc.

stories.title: Hungary vote: Rising opposition threatens Orban’s grip on power
stories.summary: Hungary's Sunday election could reshape EU dynamics, as opinion polls show the centre-right opposition Tisza party, led by Peter Magyar, with a strong lead over Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Orbán's illiberal governance since 2010 has made Hungary the only EU state classified as "partly free" by Freedom House.

stories.title: Budanov: Ukraine moves closer to agreement with Putin
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's Presidential Office and chief negotiator with Russia, said he sees progress toward a possible peace agreement with the Kremlin. Budanov suggested that resolving the war may not take much time.

stories.title: Opposition supporters call for change ahead of Benin presidential election
stories.summary: Opposition candidate Paul Hounkpè of the Cowry Forces for an Emerging Benin party used his final campaign days ahead of Benin's presidential election to highlight his differences with the current administration.

stories.title: China telecoms face US exit risk as FCC deepens crackdown on data centres
stories.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission announced it is considering measures to bar Chinese telecom carriers from operating data centres in American territory. Analysts said the restrictions could ultimately force Chinese telecoms operators, including China Mobile, out of the US market. The move represents an escalation in Washington's multi-year crackdown on Chinese technology.

stories.title: Macron meets pope, gives him basketball jersey
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron presented Pope Leo XIV with a signed French national basketball team jersey during their first meeting at the Vatican. The two leaders discussed the conflict in the Middle East, and Macron was expected to invite the pope to visit France.

stories.title: Meron Rapoport: Why Iran could be the one to finally kill Netanyahu’s career
stories.summary: Following President Trump's announcement of a ceasefire with Iran, analyst Meron Rapoport argued that a US-Iran deal could undermine Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's political legacy, making him potentially more dangerous in response.

stories.title: Taiwan’s Political Crisis Is a Security Nightmare
stories.summary: Taiwan is experiencing a political crisis that has paralyzed government functions, frozen critical budgets, and eroded public trust. The gridlock is raising security concerns for the island amid ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Ukraine talking with Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain on security
stories.summary: Ukraine has been engaging with Oman, Kuwait, and Bahrain on security cooperation. Ukraine also deployed more than 200 experts to the Middle East, where they successfully intercepted Iranian long-range Shahed drones.

stories.title: Relentless airstrikes on Beirut's residential areas 'remind Lebanese that Israel is enemy as well'
stories.summary: Dr. Randa Slim of the Middle East Institute argued that Israeli airstrikes on residential areas in Beirut cannot credibly be framed as targeted operations against Hezbollah. She characterized them as indiscriminate violence causing widespread civilian casualties and described the events as a critical inflection point in Lebanese public opinion.

stories.title: Fourteen more killed by Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Eight members of Lebanon's security forces were killed in an Israeli airstrike on Nabatieh, and six civilians died in a strike on a car wash in Jbaa in southern Lebanon. The attacks occurred despite a ceasefire agreement signed days earlier.

stories.title: Iran war: Rifts in regime bigger threat to ceasefire
stories.summary: As the United States and Iran prepare for high-stakes negotiations, analysts point to internal fractures within Iran's regime as a potentially greater threat to any ceasefire agreement than external pressures.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone makers visit Paris looking for co-production deals
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone manufacturers traveled to Paris to seek co-production partnerships with French defense firms. Oleksandr Kamyshin, a Ukrainian official, promoted a mutually beneficial model, emphasizing lessons learned from the ongoing conflict that could support French industry and economy.

stories.title: Airline pilots fear retribution over refusing to fly in Middle East, aviators' group says
stories.summary: Airline pilots have raised safety concerns about flying over the Middle East during the ongoing Iran conflict. An aviators' group reports that pilots fear retribution from their airlines for refusing high-risk assignments in the region.

stories.title: High Court rules 1,000 allowed at Tel Aviv anti-government protest Saturday, 150 in Haifa
stories.summary: Israel's High Court ruled that up to 1,000 people could attend an anti-government protest in Tel Aviv on Saturday and 150 in Haifa. The court cited the Iran ceasefire and the absence of a concrete security warning in allowing the demonstrations.

stories.title: Ukraine gains advantage on battlefield thanks to drones – ISW
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reported that Ukrainian forces have gained a battlefield advantage over Russian troops through superior drone use. This advantage is likely helping halt Russia's advance and supporting recent Ukrainian counterattacks.

stories.title: Ukraine : Russian drone attacks hit Sumy and Odesa as Easter truce looms
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes hit the Ukrainian cities of Sumy and Odesa, injuring at least two people and damaging homes and energy infrastructure. The attacks came as Russian President Putin proposed a brief Easter ceasefire.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine Plan Easter Eve Prisoner Exchange on Saturday
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine are planning a prisoner-of-war exchange on Easter Eve, Saturday. The two sides carried out a similar POW exchange over the Orthodox Easter holidays the previous year.

stories.title: Orest Mandzii appointed head of Ukraine's State Customs Service
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers appointed Orest Mandzii as the new head of the State Customs Service.

stories.title: Man arrested after baby killed in suspected dog attack in Yorkshire
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man was arrested after a three-month-old baby girl died in a suspected dog attack in Dormanstown, Redcar, Yorkshire. Cleveland police responded to reports of concern for the child's welfare on Thursday afternoon. A woman was also treated for an arm injury from a dog bite.

stories.title: Iran-linked ships drive traffic through Strait of Hormuz, ship tracking data shows
stories.summary: Despite a two-week US-Iran ceasefire, ship tracking data shows that most vessels currently sailing through the Strait of Hormuz are linked to Iran, indicating limited resumption of broader commercial traffic.

stories.title: Anger as swifts’ nesting holes in Derbyshire rail viaduct ‘blocked up’
stories.summary: Campaigners say swift nesting holes in the Chapel Milton viaducts in Derbyshire were sealed during a £7.5 million Network Rail refurbishment. Nature groups warned that returning swifts could die trying to access their blocked ancestral nesting sites on the edge of the Peak District.

stories.title: Israel expels Spain from US's CMCC in Kiryat Gat over 'obsessive anti-Israel bias'
stories.summary: Israel expelled Spain from the US-led Civil-Military Coordination Center in Kiryat Gat, citing what it called Spain's "obsessive anti-Israel bias." Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said the move was coordinated with the United States.

stories.title: Pakistan sets modest goal for US-Iran summit: A deal to keep talks going
stories.summary: US-Iran talks opened in Islamabad, Pakistan, with mediators setting a modest initial goal of sustaining dialogue. Pakistani hosts focused on keeping negotiations alive amid deep divisions between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Fuel-price protesters cause chaos in Ireland and spread to Norway
stories.summary: Fuel-price protests linked to the Middle East conflict caused significant disruptions in Ireland and spread to Norway. Hauliers, farmers, and other groups blocked motorways and brought parts of Dublin to a standstill on the fourth consecutive day of action.

stories.title: British drone flew over Lebanon hours before and after Israeli massacre
stories.summary: A Royal Air Force MQ-9B Protector drone flew over Lebanon from RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus on the same day Israel launched strikes killing over 300 people, including 18 in Baalbek in the Beqaa Valley, according to flight-tracking data analyzed by Middle East Eye.

stories.title: Wizz Air, Bluebird to resume Tel Aviv flights, while major carriers push off return
stories.summary: Bluebird Airlines plans to become the first European carrier to resume Tel Aviv flights with service to Athens on April 12, following the Iran ceasefire. Wizz Air intends to gradually restart Tel Aviv flights beginning April 25, while major carriers continue to delay.

stories.title: China will not tolerate independence for Taiwan, Xi Jinping tells island's opposition leader
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping told Taiwan's opposition leader that China "won't tolerate" independence for Taiwan during talks on cross-strait relations. Military tensions around the island have been rising.

stories.title: Xi sells 'peace' message to Taiwan opposition ahead of Trump visit
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Taiwan's opposition leader, promoting "peaceful development" of cross-strait relations. Analysts suggest the talks were also aimed at softening Washington's stance on Taiwan ahead of a visit by U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: Ukraine races to harden water systems as Russia prepares its next winter campaign
stories.summary: Ukraine is working to reinforce its water infrastructure ahead of an anticipated Russian winter campaign. Moscow has previously targeted Ukrainian energy systems with strikes aimed at disrupting civilian services during cold months.

stories.title: Fire can be seen from 20 kilometers away: Pumping station on fire in Russia's Volgograd region after attack
stories.summary: A pumping station on the Volgograd–Tikhoretsk oil product pipeline in Russia's Volgograd region caught fire overnight following an attack. The blaze was reportedly visible from approximately 20 kilometers away.

stories.title: Space Force programs supporting Golden Dome see big FY27 budget boost
stories.summary: US Space Force programs supporting the Golden Dome missile defense initiative are receiving significant budget increases in the fiscal year 2027 proposal. Missile warning and tracking programs and the Space Data Network, which transmits space sensor data to ground, air, and sea-based forces, are among those seeing major boosts.

stories.title: European airports could face jet fuel shortages within three weeks
stories.summary: Airports Council International Europe warned EU Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas that European airports could face jet fuel shortages within three weeks if oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz are not restored. The shortages could disrupt summer holiday air travel.

stories.title: Ukraine in talks with Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain on security cooperation, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy announced that Ukraine is in talks with Oman, Kuwait, and Bahrain on security cooperation, including sharing drone defense expertise and technology.

stories.title: Middle East producers prepare for oil export resumption via Hormuz, sources say
stories.summary: Middle East oil producers are reportedly preparing to resume exports through the Strait of Hormuz, with Saudi Aramco allegedly asking clients to submit nominations for cargo loadings.

stories.title: Russia Eyes Management of Cuba’s Industrial Production
stories.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov visited Havana and met with Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel on Thursday. The meeting addressed Russia's interest in managing aspects of Cuba's industrial production.

stories.title: Kimbanguism: The church shaping faith and politics in DR Congo
stories.summary: Kimbanguism, a Christian religious movement founded in the Democratic Republic of Congo, continues to play a significant role in shaping both faith and politics in the country.

stories.title: The high-stakes diplomacy that led to Pakistan hosting US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Pakistan brokered U.S.-Iran peace talks by leveraging critical minerals, cryptocurrency agreements, and CIA cooperation. Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir played a central role in facilitating the diplomatic breakthrough in Islamabad.

stories.title: Vance expects ‘positive’ Iran talks as he heads to Islamabad
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that President Trump provided "clear guidelines" for negotiations with Iran as Vance headed to Islamabad, Pakistan, expressing expectations for "positive" outcomes from the talks.

stories.title: Pakistan's defence minister calls Israel 'curse for humanity' in deleted post
stories.summary: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif called Israel "evil" and a "curse for humanity" in a post on X that was later deleted. The post appeared hours before US and Iranian delegations arrived in Islamabad for Pakistan-mediated peace talks.

stories.title: Ukraine faces months of diplomatic and military pressure, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy warned that the spring and summer months would be difficult for Ukraine, facing pressure both on the battlefield and diplomatically to end the war.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts hurtle home from moon toward splashdown
stories.summary: The four Artemis II astronauts were returning to Earth aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft after completing the first crewed lunar voyage in over 50 years. The crew was headed for a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California, concluding a 10-day mission.

stories.title: Human rights groups decry US plan for Guantánamo camp for Cuban migrants
stories.summary: Eighty-five US and international human rights organizations sent a joint letter to Congress opposing the Trump administration's plans to establish a migrant camp at Guantánamo Bay for Cubans fleeing a potential humanitarian crisis. The plan was announced by a US military general.

stories.title: Mapping the attacks on the Gulf since the US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Critical oil and gas infrastructure across the Gulf has been targeted in suspected Iranian strikes in the hours following the announcement of a US-Iran ceasefire on Wednesday.

stories.title: Kremlin sources say Russia is no longer ruling out defeat for Orban’s party in Hungary elections
stories.summary: Kremlin-connected sources told Meduza that Moscow is no longer ruling out a defeat for Viktor Orban's Fidesz party in Hungary's April 12 elections.

stories.title: Sudan: Three Years of War in Sudan Have Shattered Water and Health Services: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reports that three years of war in Sudan have devastated essential water and health services across the country. The WHO's representative in Sudan described it as the largest humanitarian crisis in the world.

stories.title: Zelensky names facts indicating that Putin does not want peace
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy cited Russia's refusal to hold leader-level meetings, opposition to foreign troops along the line of contact, and statements about Donbas as evidence that President Putin does not genuinely want peace.

stories.title: Dressed for school, returned in a shroud: Israeli forces kill Palestinian girl in class
stories.summary: Nine-year-old Ritaj Abdulrahman Rihan was killed by Israeli fire while attending class in a Gaza City school on 9 April 2026. She was reportedly solving a math problem when the strike hit her classroom.

stories.title: Kudus World Cup return in doubt after injury setback
stories.summary: Ghana forward Mohammed Kudus faces doubts over his availability for the World Cup after Tottenham confirmed the player may need surgery for a quadriceps injury.

stories.title: From critic to negotiator: JD Vance to spearhead US efforts in Iran ceasefire talks
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance traveled to Pakistan to lead ceasefire negotiations with Iran on behalf of President Donald Trump. Vance, a known skeptic of foreign military interventions, faces the challenge of converting a fragile ceasefire into a lasting peace agreement.

stories.title: From battlefields to data centres: The US-Iran war in the AI age
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has increasingly involved data centres, software engineers, and civilian technologies as both military enablers and targets. The article examines how Operation Epic Fury, the February 2026 joint U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran, demonstrated AI's transformative role in modern warfare.

stories.title: Missing Tourists Found Dead in Kamchatka
stories.summary: A group of missing tourists was found dead in Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. Regional authorities also located and rescued five survivors who showed signs of severe frostbite.

stories.title: Missing Tourists Found Dead on Kamchatka Peninsula
stories.summary: Regional authorities on Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula found missing tourists dead. Five survivors were located and rescued with signs of severe frostbite.

stories.title: Tai Po blaze: no fire risk checks done for HK$336 million estate renovation
stories.summary: A Hong Kong public inquiry revealed that fire authorities did not conduct a fire risk assessment for the HK$336 million renovation project at Wang Fuk Court before a deadly blaze struck the housing estate. Sam Keung Sai-ming of the Fire Services Department confirmed no special attention was paid to fire hazards at residential estates undergoing large-scale maintenance.

stories.title: Vance warns Iran not to ‘play’ the US as he departs for peace talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance warned Iran not to "play" the United States as he departed for peace talks in Islamabad, Pakistan. Iranian delegations reportedly arrived in the city, which was placed under lockdown. Israel is not represented at the negotiations.

stories.title: Stefano Gabbana has resigned as Dolce & Gabbana chair, filing shows
stories.summary: Stefano Gabbana resigned as chairman of Dolce & Gabbana, according to a corporate filing. Reports indicated the designer was also considering options for his approximately 40 percent stake in the company ahead of negotiations with bank lenders.

stories.title: For full occupation of Donbas, Putin needs to sacrifice up to 1 million lives – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy stated that a full Russian occupation of Donbas would cost between 300,000 and one million lives. He affirmed that Ukraine will not withdraw its forces from the region.

stories.title: Hezbollah calls on Lebanese government to stop offering 'free concessions' to Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem called on the Lebanese government to stop offering "free concessions" to Israel ahead of planned talks in Washington. His message was broadcast on Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Manar TV.

stories.title: Russian Space Forum: South Africa shares spatial ambitions and aims for the moon
stories.summary: South Africa shared its space ambitions, including lunar aspirations, at the first Russian Space Forum held in Moscow on Thursday.

stories.title: Charges filed against Rahat man for smuggling goods into Gaza during war
stories.summary: An Israeli man from Rahat has been charged with smuggling goods into Gaza during the war. Two IDF officers are also under investigation for trafficking cigarettes and other items, which prosecutors say aided Hamas.

stories.title: U.S. Vice-President Vance sets off to Pakistan to lead talks with Iran as war's ceasefire remains shaky
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance departed for Pakistan to lead negotiations with Iran as the war's ceasefire remains fragile. Vance has historically been skeptical of foreign military interventions and open-ended overseas conflicts.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank upgrades Pakistan’s economic growth rate to 3.5pc
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank upgraded Pakistan's GDP growth forecast to 3.5 percent for FY2026 and 4.5 percent for FY2027, up from 3.1 percent in FY2025. The ADB cited recovering manufacturing and increased investment but warned of downside risks from global economic uncertainty linked to the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Are ships able to pass through the Strait of Hormuz yet?
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains highly restricted despite the US-Iran ceasefire, with few vessels passing through due to mine threats and ongoing political tensions.

stories.title: Islamabad locked down ahead of high-stakes US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistani authorities locked down parts of Islamabad ahead of high-stakes negotiations between the United States and Iran scheduled for Saturday. The U.S. delegation, led by Vice President JD Vance, arrives following weeks of conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Nigeria: 61 Bodies Recovered After Niger Attack
stories.summary: Sixty-one bodies have been recovered in Niger State, Nigeria, following an attack. Residents said the corpses were found in surrounding bushes days after victims were abducted.

stories.title: Dutch police urge victims of 'international sextortion campaign' to come forward
stories.summary: Dutch police have called on victims of an international sextortion campaign to come forward. Authorities say dozens of women and girls across multiple countries were coerced into performing degrading sexual acts on camera.

stories.title: Israel threatens healthcare as it continues to attack Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel has been accused of targeting healthcare infrastructure as it continues military operations in Lebanon, threatening medical services in the country.

stories.title: Why Iran could be the one to finally kill Netanyahu’s career
stories.summary: Analyst Meron Rapoport argues that a potential deal between Tehran and Washington could devastate Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's political legacy. The analysis suggests this dynamic makes Netanyahu particularly dangerous in the current moment.

stories.title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy urges Russian oil sanctions to be reimposed after Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for the reimposition of oil sanctions on Russia following the Iran ceasefire. The United States had previously eased some Russian oil sanctions to address surging energy costs caused by the West Asia war.

stories.title: Exiled cartoonists give voice to Iran's silenced millions
stories.summary: Exiled Iranian cartoonists are using satire to give voice to millions of silenced citizens inside Iran. Artists have historically used satirical work to circumvent the threat of persecution throughout the country's turbulent history.

stories.title: China-North Korea thaw gathers pace as Kim Jong-un says ties have reached a new level
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Pyongyang on Friday, declaring bilateral relations had reached new heights. Wang's visit, his first to North Korea since 2019, included conveying greetings from President Xi Jinping. Both sides pledged to deepen strategic coordination and practical cooperation.

stories.title: Russia suffers ‘record’ soldier casualties as Ukraine ups drone production
stories.summary: Russia is reportedly experiencing record soldier casualties amid its war in Ukraine, while recruitment numbers are declining and territorial gains are diminishing. Ukraine has simultaneously increased its drone production capabilities.

stories.title: ‘Neither war nor peace’: What Gaza looks like six months into ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Six months after an October 2025 ceasefire agreement in Gaza, the situation remains unstable with continued attacks, insufficient humanitarian aid, and deepening regional conflicts contributing to ongoing instability.

stories.title: Budanov: Wars are not won without people, drones can not fight for us
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, stated that drones alone cannot win the war against Russia and emphasized that human personnel remain essential to military success.

stories.title: Meloni warns Iran's plan to charge for passage through Strait of Hormuz could disrupt global trade
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned that Iran's plan to charge for passage through the Strait of Hormuz could disrupt global trade. Deputy PM Matteo Salvini said Italy would not deploy naval vessels to patrol the area without UN authorization.

stories.title: Under the fog of ceasefire: Competing narratives over the peace talks
stories.summary: FRANCE 24's media show examined competing narratives over whether the US-Iran ceasefire includes Lebanon. The US and Israel say it does not, while Iran and mediator Pakistan insist it does. Guests included Al-Monitor editor-in-chief Joyce Karam and former Reuters correspondent Barry Malone.

stories.title: Not total victory, but a new reality: How Israel reshaped its war with Iran
stories.summary: Israel did not achieve all its stated war aims against Iran but emerged with its adversary significantly weakened. Analysts say the regional balance of power has shifted in Israel's favor, creating a new strategic reality.

stories.title: Iranian hackers leak ex-Israeli army chief's documents, photos
stories.summary: Iran-linked hackers claimed to have leaked over 19,000 files, images, and documents belonging to former Israeli army chief Herzi Halevi in a cyberattack attributed to Iranian-affiliated groups.

stories.title: Smotrich: 'Establishing settlements destroys idea of Palestinian state in our heartland'
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said establishing settlements undermines the possibility of a Palestinian state. He made the remarks at a ceremony for a new settlement called Maoz Tzur in the Binyamin region of the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Gaza father searches for his children’s remains in the rubble for years
stories.summary: A father in the Al Bureij refugee camp in Gaza survived an Israeli airstrike but lost four of his children. He has spent years searching through rubble for their remains.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts hurtle home from moon toward splashdown
stories.summary: The four Artemis II astronauts were returning to Earth aboard their Orion spacecraft after completing the first crewed moon voyage in over 50 years. They were headed for a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California.

stories.title: Weaponising sexual violence under Israel's death penalty law
stories.summary: A new report documents sexual violence and coercion against Palestinians held in Israeli detention facilities. The findings raise concerns about impunity and the implications of Israel's expanded death penalty law.

stories.title: In photos: First Friday prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque since start of Iran war
stories.summary: Palestinian worshippers performed Friday prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem for the first time in 40 days, following a two-week ceasefire in the US-Israel war on Iran that began on 28 February. Israel had barred Palestinian access during the conflict.

stories.title: Will Cheng Li-wun’s meeting with Xi Jinping temper cross-strait ties?
stories.summary: Communist Party leader Xi Jinping and Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun met in Beijing on Friday in the first talks between sitting leaders of the two parties in nearly a decade. Observers said the meeting signaled a revival of cross-strait engagement and a step toward stability, despite the KMT's opposition status in Taiwan.

stories.title: My Word: Beyond the 'Four Questions' - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion column discusses Iranian rocket and shrapnel strikes that have hit Jerusalem, including areas near sites sacred to Muslims, arguing that Iran's attacks are indiscriminate in their targeting.

stories.title: Fuel depot on fire for third day after drone attack in Feodosia – satellite images
stories.summary: Satellite images show a fuel depot in Feodosia, in Russian-occupied Crimea, burning for a third consecutive day after a Ukrainian drone strike on the night of April 8.

stories.title: Japanese tankers head towards Hormuz Strait as more ships gather
stories.summary: Japanese tankers Mayasan and Yakumosan began sailing eastward from waters off Ras Tanura in Saudi Arabia late on April 9, heading toward the Strait of Hormuz as more vessels gathered in the area.

stories.title: Middle Israel: What comes after NATO? The fall of the Western alliance's era - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that NATO and the broader Western alliance have lost strategic direction and cohesion. The author contends the alliance is effectively defunct and calls for a new security framework to replace it.

stories.title: ‘For Trump, this is seen as an unmitigated failure, this war’
stories.summary: Analyst Omar Rahman characterized the ongoing war as "an unmitigated failure" from President Trump's perspective, reflecting criticism of the conflict's progress and outcomes.

stories.title: US should judge UK on its actions in Gulf, not on Trump’s social posts, says defence secretary
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey said Britain's actions in the Gulf should be the basis for US judgment of the UK's value as an ally, rather than President Trump's social media posts. Prime Minister Starmer recently discussed keeping the Strait of Hormuz open with Trump and met leaders in Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Could the Islamabad talks end 48 years of hostility between the US and Iran?
stories.summary: US-Iran peace talks are taking place in Islamabad, Pakistan, during a two-week ceasefire pause. Uncertainty remains over whether the negotiations represent genuine diplomacy or merely an opportunity for both sides to replenish weapons stockpiles.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces shot down Shahed drones in Mideast amid Iran war, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky revealed that Ukrainian forces used domestically developed interceptor drones to shoot down Iranian Shahed drones in the Middle East during the Iran war. Ukraine provided the assistance in exchange for weapons, fuel, and money.

stories.title: Jewish leader of UK’s Green Party calls to end trade, diplomatic ties with Israel
stories.summary: Zack Polanski, the Jewish leader of the UK's Green Party, called for ending trade and diplomatic ties with Israel. He also urged Britain to block the US from using British airspace for strikes on Iran and to disentangle the two countries' militaries.

stories.title: Trump’s $1.5T defense budget to weather harsh scrutiny on Capitol Hill
stories.summary: President Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget faces difficult scrutiny in Congress. Operations in Iran, upcoming midterm elections, and Republican intraparty politics are expected to complicate the budget's legislative path.

stories.title: Singapore, Australia vow uninterrupted fuel supply amid global energy shock
stories.summary: Singapore and Australia pledged on Friday to maintain uninterrupted fuel and gas supplies amid Middle East-driven energy market disruptions. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese offered additional LNG supplies, while both sides are working toward a legally binding agreement on essential energy supplies.

stories.title: Airline pilots fear retribution over refusing to fly in Middle East, aviators’ group says
stories.summary: Airline pilots from Lebanon to India have expressed concerns about potential sanctions or retribution if they refuse to fly routes through the Middle East conflict zone, according to an aviators' group.

stories.title: In exchange for giving up nuclear weapons, Ukraine was supposed to receive NATO membership, Zelensky says
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine was supposed to receive NATO membership in exchange for giving up its nuclear weapons. He described the security guarantees Ukraine received instead as "an unfair game and a major mistake."

stories.title: US inflation soars in March as war on Iran drives economy into uncertainty
stories.summary: US consumer prices rose 0.9% in March and 3.3% year-over-year, the largest monthly spike in nearly two years, according to new CPI data. The increase reflects the economic impact of the US-Israel conflict with Iran, including disruptions from Iran's blockage of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: India says deeply concerned by reports of civilian casualties in Lebanon
stories.summary: India's foreign ministry expressed "deep concern" over civilian casualties in Lebanon, two days after Israeli bombardments killed more than 300 people. Israel had invaded Lebanon in pursuit of Hezbollah after the group fired into Israel in support of Iran.

stories.title: New Kai Tak Hospital to open in 2 phases starting in October
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hospital Authority announced that the new 2,400-bed Kai Tak Hospital on Shing Cheong Road in Kowloon Bay will begin admitting patients in phases starting October. The facility, the city's largest public hospital with 500,000 square metres of floor area, will take over services from Queen Elizabeth Hospital.

stories.title: Lahore-bound Shalimar Express derails near Sheikhupura; rail traffic suspended
stories.summary: The Lahore-bound Shalimar Express derailed near Sheikhupura, Pakistan, causing the suspension of rail traffic on the Faisalabad–Lahore section. No injuries or casualties were reported, and a relief train from Lahore was dispatched to restore the derailed coach to the tracks.

stories.title: Lebanon says ceasefire must be in place before Israel talks
stories.summary: A senior Lebanese official told the BBC that Lebanon will only participate in talks with Israel if a ceasefire is already in effect, setting a precondition for any negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Alibaba’s HappyHorse tops Seedance, offering glimpse into China’s race for AI talent
stories.summary: Alibaba's newly developed HappyHorse 1.0 video generation model has overtaken ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 as the top-ranked AI video tool on a benchmark evaluation site. The model was developed by the Innovation Business Unit under Alibaba's newly formed Token Hub and was still in internal beta testing.

stories.title: Russia strikes apartments in Konotop, Sloviansk, and Odesa, wounding three women
stories.summary: Russian forces struck residential buildings in Konotop, Sloviansk, and Odesa overnight, wounding three women in Sloviansk. Russia deployed Shahed, Gerber, and Italmas drones across nine Ukrainian regions, hitting targets in Sumy and Odesa oblasts.

stories.title: The Golden Dome’s missing layer: On-orbit logistics for a resilient missile defense
stories.summary: A sponsored analysis argues that building on-orbit servicing capabilities into the Golden Dome missile defense constellation's architecture is essential for sustaining resilient space-based missile defense over time.

stories.title: Russia has no war goal and Putin is a “Punchinello,” says ex-DNR “governor” who vowed to exterminate Ukrainians
stories.summary: Pavel Gubarev, a former self-proclaimed governor of the Donetsk People's Republic and ex-neo-Nazi paramilitary figure, has publicly stated that Russia has no clear war goal and called President Putin a "Punchinello." He now faces an administrative case for criticizing the Russian military.

stories.title: Iran’s Hormuz toll threat lays bare Asia’s energy vulnerability
stories.summary: Iran's threat to impose tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz has raised alarm across Asia, which depends heavily on Middle Eastern energy supplies. Nearly a fifth of global oil passes through the waterway. Analysts warn the chokepoint could be used as political leverage rather than governed by international rules.

stories.title: Holocaust survivors in Tel-Aviv need your support now more than ever - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: As Holocaust Remembrance Day approaches, the Jaffa Institute is seeking support for Holocaust survivors in Tel Aviv who need food, care, and assistance.

stories.title: Nigeria: Full List of African Referees Selected for 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA confirmed seven African referees have been selected to officiate at the 2026 World Cup. The full list of chosen officials was published by Nigerian outlet Vanguard.

stories.title: Uganda: UPDF Hosts U.S. Army War College Delegation On Military Transformation, Regional Security
stories.summary: The Uganda Peoples' Defence Forces hosted a delegation from the United States Army War College in Kampala. Discussions focused on military transformation, regional security, and defense cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: Budanov on cooperation with Verkhovna Rada: Dialogue should be systematic
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, stated that dialogue with members of the Verkhovna Rada, Ukraine's parliament, will continue on a systematic basis.

stories.title: Kenya: Athletics Legend Treated to Game Drive Ahead of Guest Appearance At SOYA Awards
stories.summary: The Kenya Tourism Board hosted Ethiopian marathon legend Haile Gebrselassie on a game drive at Nairobi National Park on April 10, 2026. The visit preceded his guest appearance at the 22nd Sports Personality of the Year Awards (SOYA) held that evening at Uhuru Gardens in Nairobi.

stories.title: Kenya: High Court Extends Orders Blocking State Interference in Nairobi Hospital Management
stories.summary: Kenya's High Court extended conservatory orders preventing the government from interfering with the management of The Nairobi Hospital. The ruling comes amid an ongoing legal dispute over governance at the private health facility.

stories.title: Kenya: Kitutu South Residents Protest Alleged Boundary Encroachment By Nyaribari Chache Leaders
stories.summary: Residents of Kitutu Chache South constituency in Kisii, Kenya, staged protests over alleged boundary encroachment by leaders from neighboring Nyaribari Chache constituency. Tensions have risen between residents of the two constituencies.

stories.title: Kenya: U.S. Based Investor Charles Hill Jr Moves to High Court to Halt 'Unlawful' Criminal Case Over Sh4.5bn Loan
stories.summary: U.S.-based investor Charles Hill Jr filed a petition in Kenya's High Court seeking to halt criminal proceedings against him related to a 4.5 billion Kenyan shilling loan, arguing the charges are unlawful and violate his constitutional rights.

stories.title: Schoolgirl among five killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
stories.summary: A Palestinian schoolgirl was among five people killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza. Media workers also mourned an Al Jazeera reporter killed during what is nominally a ceasefire period.

stories.title: Nigeria: Navy Dismantles 12 Illegal Refineries, Recovers 531,500 Litres of Stolen Crude
stories.summary: The Nigerian Navy dismantled 12 illegal oil refineries and recovered 531,500 litres of stolen petroleum products during Operation Delta Sentinel in the first quarter of 2026. The operation involved over 183 missions and resulted in 18 arrests linked to crude oil theft and maritime crimes.

stories.title: Putin’s approval rating falls below 70%, its lowest since before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia's state-run VTsIOM polling center recorded Vladimir Putin's approval rating falling below 70%, its lowest level since before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

stories.title: Tehran reacts to US-Iran ceasefire deal with hope and scepticism
stories.summary: A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire between the US and Iran has halted military operations and reopened the Strait of Hormuz. However, Iranians remain in limbo amid soaring inflation and fears that the conflict could resume.

stories.title: Malaysia’s Anwar on Singapore’s Hormuz stance: ‘that’s their affair’
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim responded to Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's stance against negotiating for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz by saying it was Singapore's affair. Anwar reaffirmed Malaysia's independent foreign policy while emphasizing strong neighborly ties and refusing to overlook causes of regional instability.

stories.title: Who are Araghchi and Ghalibaf, Iranian duo set to lead US ceasefire talks in Islamabad?
stories.summary: Direct US-Iran negotiations are set to begin in Islamabad on Saturday, the first since the Pentagon launched Operation Epic Fury six weeks ago. Vice-President J.D. Vance will lead the US delegation alongside envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Iran's team will be led by parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

stories.title: Portugal to join agreement on Special Tribunal for Russia’s crimes against Ukraine – FM Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced that Portugal will become the 15th country to join the agreement establishing a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Pakistan tightens security in Islamabad ahead of US-Iran negotiations
stories.summary: Pakistan tightened security across Islamabad ahead of US-Iran negotiations. A US Air Force C-130 aircraft carrying an advance security and tactical team landed at Nur Khan Air Base on Thursday to prepare for the American delegation's arrival.

stories.title: ‘Everyone wants a spaceplane’: More countries eye on-orbit protection for satellites
stories.summary: A new report indicates that France, Germany, India, and Japan are pursuing spaceplane capabilities to provide on-orbit protection for their satellites. These nations aim to develop technologies similar to those already fielded by the United States and China.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief sworn in as President
stories.summary: Myanmar's military junta chief was sworn in as president in a transition that democracy watchdogs criticized as a superficial rebranding of military rule. Observers described the move as an unconvincing civilian disguise for continued military governance.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill over 300 people in Lebanon since yesterday
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least 303 people and injured 1,150 others in Lebanon within a 24-hour period, according to Lebanon's Disaster Risk Management Unit. The total death toll since the offensive began has reached 1,888 with 6,092 wounded. Israel also issued new forced evacuation orders for Beirut's Dahiyeh district.

stories.title: Why China’s green energy strategy may shield it from the Iran war oil shock
stories.summary: China's green energy transition is being tested by the US-Israeli conflict in Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which handles about 20 percent of global oil and gas supplies. Analysts say China's shift toward renewables, outlined in its 15th five-year plan, may help insulate it from the oil shock.

stories.title: How the Army is developing its C2 plans
