stories.summary: Joseph Welch, the US Army's PAE C5ISR official, discussed the Army's command-and-control development plans in an interview on the Pentagon Buzz podcast with Mark Pomerleau.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: No substantive content was available for this article.

stories.title: Syrian defector 'Caesar' says govt rehabilitating 'Assadists'
stories.summary: Syrian defector Farid al-Madhhan, known as "Caesar," criticized Syria's current government for rehabilitating figures associated with the former Assad regime. He accused authorities of appointing individuals linked to the previous government to official positions.

stories.title: US, Iran set for crunch Pakistan talks in bid to rescue truce
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiators are set to meet in Pakistan for talks aimed at rescuing a fragile ceasefire. Disputes over Lebanon and the Strait of Hormuz have threatened to collapse the agreement.

stories.title: Lego-style memes troll Trump after fragile US-Iran truce
stories.summary: A Lego-style video circulating online lampoons US President Donald Trump over the fragile US-Iran truce, declaring that "Iran won." The meme went viral following the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer and Trump discussed military options for Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and U.S. President Donald Trump discussed potential military options for securing the Strait of Hormuz. French President Emmanuel Macron has separately raised the idea of a European-led effort to protect the strategic waterway, though only after the current war concludes.

stories.title: Céline Dion's concerts set to give Paris multimillion-euro boost
stories.summary: Céline Dion's 16 Paris concert dates this autumn are expected to generate hundreds of millions of euros for the French capital. Revenue is anticipated from ticket sales, hotel and restaurant bookings, and retail spending as international fans travel to see the performer.

stories.title: Budanov urges public to “grow up” in sharp remarks on draft evaders and anti-TRC sentiment
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, Head of Ukraine's Office of the President, sharply criticized draft evaders and opponents of Territorial Recruitment Centers, calling on Ukrainian society to "grow up" and accept wartime responsibilities.

stories.title: Protests erupt across US over Iran war threat, Lebanon massacre
stories.summary: Large protests erupted across cities and towns in the United States in response to President Trump's threat to annihilate Iran and Israel's large-scale bombing campaign in Beirut and Lebanon.

stories.title: ‘Closer to a break than ever’: Can NATO survive if Trump pulls the US out?
stories.summary: The war involving Iran has deepened divisions within the transatlantic alliance, raising questions about NATO's future viability should the United States withdraw from the organization under President Trump.

stories.title: Parashat Shmini: Guarding a pure heart
stories.summary: This article is a religious commentary on Parashat Shmini, exploring the Hebrew concept of timtum—spiritual blockage or emotional dullness—and its connection to dietary laws in Jewish tradition.

stories.title: Judge rules slain hostage’s family may use his sperm with a surrogate
stories.summary: A Beersheba family court ruled that the family of Yotam Haim, a hostage abducted to Gaza who was mistakenly killed by Israeli troops after escaping Hamas captivity, may use his sperm with a surrogate. The court found he had expressed an "unequivocal" desire to have children.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The article provides Shabbat candle lighting times for communities in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Israel slams Pakistan Minister Khawaja Asif for ‘outrageous’ comments
stories.summary: Israel condemned remarks by Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif, who called Israel "evil" and a "curse for humanity" in a social media post. Israel described the comments as outrageous.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: U.S. Vice-President Vance sets off to Pakistan to lead talks with Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance departed for Pakistan to lead negotiations with Iran in Islamabad. Meanwhile, air raid alerts sounded across Israel, including Tel Aviv and Ashdod, following rocket fire from Lebanon.

stories.title: Chinese, Taiwanese will unite, Xi Jinping tells Taiwan Opposition leader
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping told visiting Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun that Chinese and Taiwanese people will unite. The visit, the first by a sitting KMT leader in a decade, has sparked debate in Taiwan, with critics accusing Cheng of being too accommodating toward Beijing.

stories.title: Islamabad prepares to host US-Iran negotiations as Trump casts doubt on ceasefire | First Thing
stories.summary: Pakistan deployed its army in Islamabad ahead of US-Iran negotiations set to begin Saturday. The fragile ceasefire showed further strain as Trump accused Iran of failing to uphold promises on the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran claimed Israeli attacks on Lebanon violated the truce.

stories.title: Israel pledges 'talks under fire' as Lebanon death toll at 303
stories.summary: Israel announced it would begin ceasefire negotiations with Lebanon in the coming days in Washington. Prime Minister Netanyahu stressed that Israeli attacks on Lebanon would continue even as talks proceed, with the Lebanese death toll reaching 303.

stories.title: Cuban president defiant despite Trump pressure to resign
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel has vowed to resist US pressure to resign as President Trump escalates threats against Havana and tightens an oil blockade on the island.

stories.title: Donald Trump's tenuous Iran exit plan isn't healing Republican rifts exposed by the war
stories.summary: Former U.S. Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, a one-time Trump supporter turned critic, called for President Trump's removal through the 25th Amendment. The article examines divisions within the Republican Party exposed by the U.S. approach to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russia will unlikely fully cover budget deficit despite sanctions relief
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy said Russia is unlikely to fully cover its budget deficit despite a temporary easing of oil sanctions, suggesting the relief will be insufficient to close Moscow's fiscal gap.

stories.title: Starmer says he discussed military options for Strait of Hormuz with Trump
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he discussed military capabilities and logistics for moving vessels through the Strait of Hormuz with US President Donald Trump. Starmer indicated the UK is assembling a coalition of countries pursuing both diplomatic and military options during his visit to the Middle East.

stories.title: Telegram founder says WhatsApp reads users’ messages and shares them with third parties
stories.summary: Telegram founder Pavel Durov accused Meta's WhatsApp of reading users' messages and sharing them with third parties, calling WhatsApp's encryption claims possibly "the biggest fraud in history."

stories.title: ‘We felt death’: Survivors recount Israel’s massacre in Beirut
stories.summary: Survivors in Beirut recounted Israeli air strikes that hit densely populated areas on a Wednesday afternoon. Rescue efforts involved pulling bodies from rubble across multiple locations in Beirut's southern suburbs, the Beqaa governorate, and southern villages.

stories.title: Iran sets 'preconditions' ahead of ceasefire talks as Vance warns Tehran not to 'play' US
stories.summary: Iranian and U.S. delegations headed to Islamabad on Friday for ceasefire negotiations, but deep disagreements threatened to derail the talks. Iran stated it would only begin negotiations if Washington accepted its preconditions, while Vice President JD Vance warned Tehran not to "play" the United States.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks damaged more than 125,000 civilian sites in Iran, Red Crescent says
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society reported that US-Israeli attacks have damaged more than 125,630 civilian sites across Iran. Of those, 23,500 are commercial centers and 339 are medical facilities, according to the organization's head, Pirhossein Kolivand.

stories.title: Zelensky explains why Ukrainian strikes on Russia become more effective
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy stated that Ukrainian strikes on Russian targets have grown more effective due to improved technology and new operational strategies.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strikes Kill 1 in Volgograd Region
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes killed one person in Russia's Volgograd region. Russia's Defense Ministry reported intercepting 57 Ukrainian drones in the region between Thursday night and early Friday morning.

stories.title: Senegal's PM Sonko accuses US President Trump of 'destabilising' the world
stories.summary: Senegalese Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko publicly criticized U.S. President Donald Trump over the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. Sonko called Trump a "man of chaos" and accused him of destabilizing the world.

stories.title: ‘High risk’: US V-P Vance tasked by Trump to lead Iran talks
stories.summary: US Vice-President J.D. Vance has been tasked by President Trump to lead negotiations with Iran in Islamabad, Pakistan. The high-stakes talks represent one of the most significant moments of Vance's political career.

stories.title: Gaza families still unable to bury dead six months into ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Approximately 10,000 Palestinians remain missing in Gaza six months into a ceasefire, believed to be buried under the rubble of buildings destroyed during Israel's military campaign. Families are still unable to recover and bury their dead.

stories.title: Trump slams right-wing commentators who oppose Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump criticized right-wing commentators who opposed the Iran war, after they accused him of abandoning his anti-war campaign promises.

stories.title: Pakistan allows visa-free boarding, offers visa on arrival for Islamabad Talks delegates
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar announced that airlines have been instructed to allow visa-free boarding for delegates traveling to Islamabad for U.S.-Iran peace talks. Foreign delegations from both countries are expected in the Pakistani capital for negotiations aimed at ending hostilities, following a two-week Pakistan-brokered ceasefire.

stories.title: Telegram blocking rate in Russia reaches 95%
stories.summary: Data from the international research project OONI indicates that Telegram blocking rates in Russia reached 95% by the morning of April 10, as reported by the independent Russian outlet Agentstvo.

stories.title: Indictment filed against Jerusalem resident for spying on behalf of Iran, contacting foreign agent
stories.summary: Israeli authorities filed an indictment against Jerusalem resident Lachovitz on charges of espionage for Iran. Prosecutors allege he continued cooperating with an Iranian-linked contact even after becoming aware of the connection to Tehran.

stories.title: Protester says they are willing to close Ireland down over fuel costs
stories.summary: Protesters in Ireland threatened to shut down the country over rising fuel costs. Irish authorities announced that the military would be deployed to remove vehicles blocking critical infrastructure.

stories.title: US summons Iraqi ambassador over drone strike on diplomatic facility in Baghdad
stories.summary: The United States summoned Iraq's ambassador following a drone strike on a US diplomatic facility in Baghdad. Washington demanded that Iraq take measures to dismantle Iran-aligned militia groups operating within its borders.

stories.title: Canadian mother held by ICE with daughter, 7, speaks out on families ‘suffering greatly’ in detention
stories.summary: Canadian citizen Tania Warner and her seven-year-old daughter Ayla were released after nearly three weeks of detention by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Texas facilities described as unsafe and degrading. Warner spoke out about families still suffering in detention.

stories.title: Chinese firms in Hungary face a post-election reckoning – no matter who wins
stories.summary: Chinese firms operating in Debrecen, Hungary, face growing local opposition ahead of Sunday's general election. Protesters have targeted a mega-factory built by battery giant CATL, with banners reading "Chinese, go home" displayed near the railway station. A protest was planned for Saturday, the day before the vote.

stories.title: Two major energy facilities in Odesa region heavily damaged in Russian attack
stories.summary: Two major energy facilities in Ukraine's Odesa region sustained significant damage during a Russian drone attack overnight on April 10.

stories.title: Kenya: Unexpected Ally Stepping Up Against Sexual Assault in Kenyan Slums - Landlord Standfirst
stories.summary: In Kenyan slums, landlords have emerged as unexpected allies in efforts to combat sexual assault. The initiative highlights community-based approaches to addressing gender-based violence in informal settlements.

stories.title: Africa: Kenya Approves Defence Pact With France, As Paris Shifts Focus From West Africa
stories.summary: Kenya's National Assembly ratified a bilateral defence agreement with France, reflecting Paris's strategic pivot from its traditional partnerships in West Africa toward anglophone African nations.

stories.title: Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire, Zelensky agrees
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky agreed. Zelensky had proposed an Easter truce for over a week, accusing Moscow of responding to his earlier calls with drone attacks on Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Not just about Gaza: the Muslim voters turning from Labour to the Greens
stories.summary: In Newcastle, some Muslim voters are shifting support from Labour to the Greens ahead of local elections, driven partly by Labour's stance on the war in Gaza. Campaigning also shows concerns about the far right, climate change, and cost of living among voters.

stories.title: Kommersant reports UniCredit abandons plan to sell its Russian subsidiary, will wind down operations instead
stories.summary: Italy's UniCredit has abandoned plans to sell its Russian subsidiary and is now considering a full wind-down of operations in Russia, according to the Russian business daily Kommersant.

stories.title: Middle East crisis has given Iran new way to resist nuclear limits, say former US-Iran envoys
stories.summary: Former U.S.-Iran negotiators who worked on the 2015 JCPOA nuclear deal said the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran and Tehran's subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz have given Iran new leverage to resist pressure on its nuclear programme. They warned Iran now sees Hormuz as a tool to balance its power asymmetry with the U.S.

stories.title: Hungary election campaigns enter final stretch as Orbán fights to remain in power – Europe live
stories.summary: Hungary's parliamentary election campaigns are in their final days ahead of Sunday's vote, with opposition Tisza party leader Péter Magyar challenging Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Magyar rallied supporters in Hatvan and warned against complacency as some voters remain undecided.

stories.title: Ukraine's winter preparations: Shmyhal outlines six key energy priorities
stories.summary: Ukraine's First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal convened an emergency response headquarters meeting focused on preparing Ukraine's energy sector for the upcoming winter, outlining six key priorities.

stories.title: ‘We felt death’: Survivors recount Israel’s massacre in Beirut
stories.summary: Survivors in Beirut recounted their experiences during Israeli strikes on the city on 8 April 2026. Residents described searching through rubble as the attacks devastated neighborhoods and shattered civilian lives.

stories.title: Russia deploying strategic reserve troops to frontline – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy reported that Russia is deploying troops from its strategic reserve to the frontline in Ukraine, increasing its troop presence in the conflict zone.

stories.title: Jerusalem man indicted for passing information to Iranian agent
stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors indicted Jerusalem resident Moshe Lachovitz for passing information to an Iranian agent. He allegedly photographed locations in Ra'anana, where former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett resides, in exchange for cryptocurrency payments.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader calls for ‘reconciliation’ after meeting Xi
stories.summary: KMT leader Cheng Li-wun met Chinese President Xi Jinping and called for reconciliation between Taiwan and China. She emphasized shared cultural heritage and indicated she would seek to slow Taiwan's military build-up.

stories.title: Zelensky suggests Russia sought looser oil sanctions to sell Lukoil assets in Europe
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy suggested that Russia may have sought looser oil sanctions to facilitate the sale of Lukoil's European assets.

stories.title: Will Israel and Lebanon start ceasefire talks?
stories.summary: Israel and Hezbollah continued exchanging attacks on Friday, though at a reduced intensity. Prospects for formal ceasefire negotiations between the two sides remain uncertain.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree to Easter Ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter this weekend, marking a rare pause in the conflict that has lasted more than four years.

stories.title: Lebanon to attend Washington ceasefire talks, says truce needed for broader deal
stories.summary: Lebanon confirmed it will attend ceasefire talks in Washington with US and Israeli representatives, though the exact date has not been set. A senior Lebanese official said Beirut's position is that a ceasefire must be a precondition for any broader deal with Israel.

stories.title: Alla Pugacheva fan festival in Moscow canceled after civic activist files complaint with prosecutors
stories.summary: A fan festival dedicated to Russian singer Alla Pugacheva was canceled in Moscow after Vitaly Borodin, head of the Federal Project on Security and Anti-Corruption, filed a complaint with prosecutors seeking to ban the event.

stories.title: Iran war is huge success for Israel - but it is not a victory, yet - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's military campaign against Iran has achieved significant results but falls short of outright victory, contending that political leaders misled the public by promising quick, purely military solutions.

stories.title: White House warned staff not to engage in insider trading amid war with Iran
stories.summary: The White House issued a directive warning staff against insider trading amid the war with Iran. The warning followed a surge of suspicious trading activity on prediction markets, oil futures, and stocks.

stories.title: Zelensky warns of mounting pressure on Ukraine before autumn
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy warned that Ukraine will face intensifying political and military pressure until September, while pledging that the country's national interests will be protected.

stories.title: Nigeria: Atiku's Aide Faults Tinubu Over Plateau Visit, Lagos Engagements
stories.summary: An aide to Nigerian opposition figure Atiku Abubakar criticized President Bola Tinubu's governance approach, including his visit to Plateau state and engagements in Lagos. The aide argued that presidential leadership requires greater presence and responsiveness.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Army Land Forces Chief Meets Partners to Boost Joint Operations
stories.summary: The commander of the Somali National Army's land forces met in Mogadishu with officials from the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia and allied countries. Discussions focused on strengthening security cooperation and accelerating joint operations against militant groups.

stories.title: Iran's Khamenei says does not seek war, will not renounce rights
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated that Iran does not seek war but will not renounce its rights. Khamenei, who was likely wounded in the strike that killed his father, has not been seen in public since assuming the leadership role.

stories.title: Vedomosti reports Belgorod governor set to resign and join Russia’s Economic Development Ministry
stories.summary: Belgorod Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov is reportedly set to resign and may be appointed deputy minister at Russia's Economic Development Ministry under Minister Maxim Reshetnikov, according to the Russian business daily Vedomosti.

stories.title: Tanzania: MPs Seek Road Financing Shift
stories.summary: Members of Parliament in Tanzania have called for a shift in road financing policy, citing inadequate funding, poor connectivity, and unequal resource allocation. Lawmakers in Dodoma argued these constraints hinder economic growth and service delivery.

stories.title: Israel strikes residential areas, destroys homes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted residential areas in southern Lebanon, destroying homes and displacing large numbers of people. The United Nations warned that Lebanon is experiencing not only a displacement crisis but also a rapidly developing food security emergency.

stories.title: Lviv to host Defense Tech Valley 2026 on Sept 16-17
stories.summary: The city of Lviv will host the Brave1 Defense Tech Valley 2026 conference on September 16–17. The event is billed as Ukraine's largest defense technology gathering, bringing together manufacturers, investors, and international partners.

stories.title: US urges citizens to reconsider travel to Nigeria over security risks
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department issued an updated travel advisory urging American citizens to reconsider travel to Nigeria. The advisory cited elevated risks of terrorism, civil unrest, and kidnapping across the country.

stories.title: Fear, anxiety grip Iranians ahead of US talks: ‘I’m scared of war starting again’
stories.summary: Ordinary Iranians expressed fear and skepticism ahead of planned U.S.-Iran negotiations hosted by Pakistan. Citizens described feeling caught between a government they say does not understand peace and threats from American President Trump.

stories.title: TotalEnergies says Saudi refinery shut down after attacks
stories.summary: French energy company TotalEnergies shut down a major refinery on Saudi Arabia's eastern Gulf coast after it was damaged during the Middle East conflict. The Satorp refinery is a joint venture between TotalEnergies and Saudi Aramco. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry confirmed multiple recent attacks on its oil and gas sites.

stories.title: Ukrainian experts down Shahed drones across Middle East, Zelensky says
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukrainian specialists successfully intercepted Iranian-made drones, including jet-powered models, in several Middle Eastern countries.

stories.title: German transgender far-right extremist arrested in Czech Republic
stories.summary: Czech authorities arrested Marla-Svenja Liebich, a German transgender far-right extremist. German media report that Liebich was formerly a member of the neo-Nazi group Blood and Honour.

stories.title: Poland: "Frog Patrol" saves thousands of amphibians during migration
stories.summary: Volunteers near Warsaw, Poland, have organized a seasonal 'Frog Patrol' to help thousands of frogs and toads safely cross roads during their spring migration. The effort aims to protect local amphibian breeding grounds from traffic-related deaths.

stories.title: US-Iran talks leave Gulf states on edge about the price of peace
stories.summary: Gulf Cooperation Council states are watching U.S.-Iran negotiations in Pakistan with deep anxiety after being struck by Iranian drones and missiles during the conflict. China and Russia vetoed the GCC's bid for UN Security Council approval of defensive measures to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump ‘reaping bitter fruit’ of thinking Iran intervention as easy as Venezuela, says former diplomat
stories.summary: Former U.S. ambassador John Feeley said President Trump mistakenly believed the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro offered a model for toppling Iran's regime. Feeley argued Trump was emboldened by the Venezuela operation when he decided to attack Iran in February.

stories.title: ‘Illegal’ forest service overhaul risks causing ‘chaos’ across US public lands, union claims
stories.summary: Union leaders warned that a restructuring of the U.S. Forest Service under the Trump administration will close all regional offices overseeing 193 million acres of public land. Workers are being forced to decide whether to relocate or resign, which the union says risks causing chaos across public lands.

stories.title: ’He’s mentally unstable’: Iranian American in Congress condemns Trump’s war and pushes for his removal
stories.summary: US Representative Yassamin Ansari, an Iranian American Democrat, called for President Trump's removal from office over the war in Iran, calling him "mentally unstable." She argued the conflict has further entrenched the Iranian regime rather than weakening it.

stories.title: Move over, Hercules: China’s new Y-30 aims to outmuscle America’s best transport aircraft
stories.summary: China's new Y-30 medium-lift transport aircraft, developed by Shaanxi Aircraft Industry Corporation, conducted its maiden test flight in December. Chinese military publications claim the four-engine turboprop will surpass the U.S. C-130J Super Hercules in most performance metrics.

stories.title: Foreigners flock to China spas to enjoy unique cultural baths amid rise of wellness tourism
stories.summary: Foreign tourists have been visiting Chinese spa centres and bathhouses, drawn by 24-hour operations offering hot springs, food, entertainment, and affordable prices. The trend reflects a growing interest in wellness tourism in China.

stories.title: Dolce & Gabbana says co-founder Stefano Gabbana has quit as chair
stories.summary: Dolce & Gabbana announced that co-founder Stefano Gabbana resigned as chair effective January 1, described as part of a governance evolution. Gabbana, who holds a 40% stake, is reportedly considering options for his shares ahead of talks with lenders.

stories.title: French MEP cleared in drugs probe amid pro-Palestine speech row
stories.summary: French prosecutors dropped a drugs investigation into MEP Rima Hassan, a pro-Palestine activist. Criticism had grown over her arrest, which followed a social media post referencing a 1972 attack.

stories.title: World Food Programme warns Lebanon facing food security crisis due to Iran war
stories.summary: The UN World Food Programme warned that Lebanon is facing a food security crisis as the Iran war disrupts supply chains. WFP country director Allison Oman said food prices are soaring and becoming increasingly unaffordable for displaced populations.

stories.title: Zelensky dismisses ‘buffer zone’ threat in Vinnytsia region
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy dismissed claims about Russia creating a buffer zone specifically along Transnistria in the Vinnytsia region, stating that Russia aims for a buffer zone along its entire border and Belarus's but currently lacks the capacity.

stories.title: 'Stupid people': Trump attacks Tucker Carlson, Candace Owens, Alex Jones, Megyn Kelly over Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump attacked conservative media figures Tucker Carlson, Candace Owens, Alex Jones, and Megyn Kelly over their criticism of his Iran policy. Trump accused them of supporting Iran's pursuit of nuclear weapons and called them "nutjobs" with "Low IQs."

stories.title: France and Pakistan condemn ‘Lebanon ceasefire violations’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy PM Ishaq Dar and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot condemned ceasefire violations in Lebanon during a phone call. Both officials emphasized the importance of full implementation of the ceasefire, following an Israeli air strike campaign that killed over 200 people.

stories.title: With all quiet on the Iran front, Israel turns its sights on Hezbollah
stories.summary: Following the ceasefire with Iran, Israel expanded military operations in Lebanon despite an existing truce with Tehran. The US is working to contain the fallout, while the trajectory of fighting on Israel's northern front remains unclear.

stories.title: The political system of Cuba is not on the table in any dialogue with the U.S.: Juan Carlos Marsan
stories.summary: Cuban Ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan stated that Cuba's political system is not subject to negotiation in any dialogue with the United States. Cuba is facing a severe economic crisis driven by fuel shortages, U.S. sanctions, prolonged blackouts, and disruptions to daily life.

stories.title: Ukraine to fix Druzhba pipeline this spring, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine will complete repairs to the Druzhba oil pipeline this spring under a deal with the EU, but warned Kyiv cannot guarantee transit safety against potential Russian strikes.

stories.title: North Korea, China agree to deepen cooperation in talks between Foreign Ministers
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi traveled to Pyongyang for his first visit to North Korea in seven years. During talks with his North Korean counterpart, the two sides agreed to deepen bilateral cooperation.

stories.title: Six months into ‘ceasefire’, Gaza suffers under persistent Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Six months after a US-brokered ceasefire was announced, Gaza continues to suffer persistent Israeli attacks. Over 72,000 people have been killed and 172,000 injured, with aid groups documenting ongoing violations of the truce agreement.

stories.title: New Patriot missiles delivered to Ukraine, Zelensky confirms
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukraine has received new Patriot air defense missiles from international partners, continuing the supply of the system.

stories.title: Dmitriev arrives in Washington as Russia’s sanctions clock ticks toward April 11, Reuters reports
stories.summary: Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev arrived in Washington as a 30-day US waiver on Russian oil sanctions approaches its April 11 expiration. Peace deal discussions are also reportedly on the agenda, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Victim of ‘disgusting paedophile’ serving Australia’s longest sentence for child sex abuse tells of ‘lost decades’
stories.summary: A woman testified in an Australian court about decades of harm caused by William "Rob" Gilfillan, a former high school PE teacher at Traralgon high school in Gippsland. Gilfillan was found guilty of indecent assault and sexual penetration of minors and is already serving Australia's longest sentence for child sex abuse.

stories.title: Spain calls on Iran to negotiate in 'good faith'
stories.summary: Spain's Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares urged his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi to negotiate in good faith during US-Iran talks in Islamabad. Albares also asked Iran to halt missile activities as part of broader diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Moscow will not abandon Cuba and plans to help with energy: Russian diplomat
stories.summary: A Russian diplomat stated that Moscow will not abandon Cuba and plans to assist with the island's energy needs. Russia has been working to strengthen ties with Cuba, echoing the close relationship the two countries had during the Soviet era.

stories.title: Somalia, the Islamic State group's new front line in Africa
stories.summary: Islamic State fighters have established a stronghold in Somalia's Puntland region, using its mountainous terrain as a base for wider operations in Africa. Local authorities launched a major offensive, driving jihadists from villages into cave positions amid ongoing clashes and casualties.

stories.title: Residents trapped indoors as area sealed under tight security
stories.summary: Residents in Rawalpindi and Islamabad faced severe movement restrictions as authorities sealed roads near Nur Khan Airbase and surrounding neighborhoods with containers and barbed wire ahead of U.S.-Iran talks. Areas including Shah Khalid Colony and Gulzar-e-Quaid were effectively locked down.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Politician Arrested for Allegedly Providing False Intelligence to Embassies
stories.summary: Nigerian former lawmaker Mr. Gebi, who served in the 7th House of Representatives, was arrested by the State Security Service on April 3. He is accused of allegedly providing false intelligence to foreign embassies.

stories.title: Satellites alone don’t explain Iran’s nine-fold jump in strike accuracy — InformNapalm says Russian SOF doctrine does
stories.summary: An InformNapalm analysis attributes Iran's rapid improvement in missile strike accuracy—from 3% to 27%—not solely to satellite data but to Russian special operations forces doctrine linking reconnaissance to fire coordination.

stories.title: India finalising agreement to supply oil, gas to Mauritius amid West Asia crisis: Jaishankar
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said India is finalizing an agreement to supply oil and gas to Mauritius amid disruptions caused by the West Asia crisis. Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz has halted shipping and driven global oil prices sharply higher.

stories.title: War update: 163 clashes on frontline over past day, hottest fighting in Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka sectors
stories.summary: On April 9, Ukrainian and Russian forces engaged in 163 combat clashes along the frontline. The heaviest fighting occurred in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors, with increased Russian activity also reported in the Huliaipole sector.

stories.title: Gladio: NATO’s secret cold war operation in Italy
stories.summary: After World War II, NATO established a clandestine network in roughly ten European countries to counter the spread of communism during the Cold War. In Italy, the covert operation was code-named Gladio and remains one of Europe's most significant state secrets and political scandals.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire deal shows strain ahead of talks with oil flows squeezed
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire deal showed signs of strain ahead of formal talks scheduled for April 11 in Islamabad, Pakistan, with oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remaining squeezed.

stories.title: Ceasefire holds, but Strait of Hormuz remains at a standstill
stories.summary: A fragile ceasefire is in place between the U.S., Israel, and Iran, but maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains nearly halted. Growing evidence suggests Iran's Revolutionary Guard has laid mines in the strait, deterring shipping companies from transiting the waterway.

stories.title: Gaza marks 6 months of ceasefire. Does it offer lessons for the Iran war?
stories.summary: Friday marked six months since Gaza's ceasefire took effect between Israeli forces and Hamas-led militants, largely overshadowed by the fragile Iran war ceasefire. Major challenges remain, including disarming Hamas, deploying an international stabilisation force, and beginning reconstruction in the territory.

stories.title: Iran demands Lebanon truce, asset unfreeze ahead of talks
stories.summary: Iran is demanding a truce in Lebanon and the unfreezing of its assets as preconditions ahead of ceasefire talks with the US. Pakistan's capital, Islamabad, is preparing to host the Iranian and US delegations for the negotiations.

stories.title: Islamabad prepares for Iran-US delegations as talks set to begin
stories.summary: Pakistan's capital Islamabad is preparing to host Iranian and US delegations for ceasefire negotiations. Security and logistical arrangements are being finalized as both sides prepare for the talks.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Cyclone Maila batters Solomon Islands with 115mph winds
stories.summary: Severe Tropical Cyclone Maila struck the Solomon Islands with sustained winds of 115 mph and gusts up to 160 mph, causing widespread damage in Western, Choiseul, and Isabel provinces. The Australian Bureau of Meteorology called it the strongest cyclone recorded this far north in the Solomon Sea.

stories.title: Nigeria: Jihadists kill army general and soldiers in attack on Borno state base
stories.summary: Unidentified jihadists attacked a military base at Benisheikh, approximately 75 kilometres from Maiduguri, the capital of Borno state in northeast Nigeria. The attackers overran the base and torched vehicles before soldiers repelled the raid, according to military sources.

stories.title: Hong Kong awards stablecoin licences to HSBC, StanChart-led group in long-awaited roll-out
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority issued the city's first stablecoin issuer licences to HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture led by Standard Chartered. The licences follow the enactment of Hong Kong's Stablecoin Ordinance eight months ago as the city pursues its ambition to become a global digital asset hub.

stories.title: Confusion over Melania Trump's bizarrely-timed Jeffrey Epstein disavowal
stories.summary: Hungary's opposition leader Péter Magyar is challenging Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ahead of Sunday's election. Separately, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump held a press conference at the White House to deny ties to Jeffrey Epstein, raising questions about whether it was intended to divert attention from the Iran war.

stories.title: A new dawn?
stories.summary: The article is an opinion piece discussing Iran's confrontation with the United States in the context of a broader historical struggle. It draws parallels to anti-colonial movements and notes that even if the ceasefire collapses, Tehran has achieved a strategic milestone.

stories.title: Opposition bloc continues to hold 61 seat majority as Bennett's party gains on Likud - poll
stories.summary: An Israeli opinion poll showed the opposition bloc maintaining a 61-seat majority, with former PM Naftali Bennett's party gaining ground on the ruling Likud. Opposition leader Yair Lapid said the results demonstrate that reality is prevailing over attempts at political messaging.

stories.title: Xi holds landmark Taiwan meeting, Iran war ceasefire, GDP update
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in Beijing, the first such meeting between leaders of the Communist Party and Taiwan's main opposition in nine years. Xi expressed confidence in closer cross-strait ties, while Cheng emphasized a message of peace across the Taiwan Strait.

stories.title: China's Xi hosts Taiwan opposition leader in Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in Beijing, marking the first meeting between leaders of the Chinese Communist Party and Taiwan's main opposition party in nine years. The meeting focused on cross-strait relations, with Xi expressing confidence in closer ties between mainland China and Taiwan.

stories.title: Russian nighttime drone attack in Odesa region leaves energy and port infrastructure damaged
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukraine's Odesa region overnight with drones, damaging port and energy infrastructure and causing disruptions to the electricity supply.

stories.title: CNIC not moveable property; can’t be blocked, impounded or attached: Lahore High Court
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court ruled that Pakistan's computerized national identity card (CNIC) is not movable property and cannot be blocked, impounded, or attached by civil courts as a coercive measure. Justice Tanveer Ahmad Sheikh issued the ruling at the Multan Bench in a case involving CNIC blocking ordered by a civil court.

stories.title: Ukraine destroys S-300V and drone command post in coordinated Zaporizhzhia strike
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces destroyed a Russian S-300V air defense system and a drone command post in the Zaporizhzhia region through a coordinated multi-phase operation involving drones and the Ukrainian Air Force.

stories.title: Hezbollah attacks towns in northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched rocket attacks targeting towns in northern Israel, including Kiryat Shmona, Metula, and Misgav Am. The group said in a Telegram statement that attacks would continue until Israeli-American aggression against Lebanon stops.

stories.title: Attacking Lebanon
stories.summary: The opinion piece discusses uncertainties surrounding U.S.-Iran negotiations, particularly regarding Lebanon. On the day a Pakistan-brokered truce was announced, Israel launched strikes on Lebanon that reportedly killed over 200 people and caused significant infrastructure damage.

stories.title: トランプ大統領 NATOへの不満示す 駐留米軍の一部撤退も議論か
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted messages on social media expressing dissatisfaction with NATO over its response to the Iran situation. Reuters reported that Trump discussed the possible partial withdrawal of American troops stationed in European NATO member countries.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 113 out of 128 Russian drones since yesterday evening
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 113 out of 128 Russian drones launched since the previous evening. Enemy strikes were recorded at six locations across the country.

stories.title: How Starlink is helping Iranians evade wartime internet blackout
stories.summary: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service is helping Iranians bypass a wartime internet blackout despite being illegal in Iran. Starlink receivers have been smuggled into the country and sold on the black market.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya, Morocco Ink 11 Deals to Unlock Trade and Investment
stories.summary: Kenya and Morocco signed 11 bilateral agreements in Nairobi aimed at boosting trade and investment across sectors including agriculture, health, education, and the blue economy.

stories.title: Families search for missing after Israel massacre in Lebanon
stories.summary: Families in Lebanon are searching for missing relatives following a large-scale Israeli attack. Witnesses and survivors described indiscriminate strikes that killed entire families, raising serious concerns about proportionality under international law.

stories.title: Former Iranian FM Kharazi dies from wounds following airstrike, state media says
stories.summary: Former Iranian Foreign Minister Kamal Kharrazi died from wounds sustained when his home was struck on April 1 during US-Israeli operations dubbed Roaring Lion and Epic Fury, according to Iranian state media.

stories.title: From Kyiv’s skies to the Gulf: Ukraine trades drone war expertise for diesel and interceptors
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy stated that Ukrainian specialists shot down Iranian-made Shahed drones in multiple Middle Eastern countries. Kyiv has also opened security talks with Oman, Kuwait, and Bahrain, trading drone warfare expertise for diesel and interceptors.

stories.title: Another mpox case of ‘local transmission’ appears in Karachi
stories.summary: Karachi reported its second suspected case of locally transmitted mpox, with the patient hospitalized at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital. Separately, the city's East district recorded its first dengue death of the season, as authorities continue efforts to contain the mpox outbreak in Khairpur.

stories.title: ‘An abomination’: the Lancashire town kicking up at stink from reopened landfill
stories.summary: Residents of Fleetwood, Lancashire, are protesting a persistent foul smell from the reopened Transwaste landfill site, saying the odour is causing illness and severely affecting their quality of life.

stories.title: Iran banks to resume full operations tomorrow
stories.summary: Iran's Bank Coordination Council announced that all bank branches across the country, including headquarters units in Tehran, will resume full operations starting Saturday. The reopening follows disruptions caused by the ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Iran ceasefire: Not an off-ramp for the US but a life-saving ejection seat
stories.summary: A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire between Iran and the United States has taken effect following weeks of conflict. Iran is described as having single-handedly checked the war-making capabilities of both the US and Israel, marking a significant shift in regional power dynamics.

stories.title: Argentina’s Milei to light torch at Israel’s 78th Independence Day ceremony
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei has been invited to light a torch at Israel's 78th Independence Day ceremony, with Israeli officials citing his strong support for Israel and efforts against antisemitism.

stories.title: Takeaways from Cheng Li-wun’s press conference about meeting with Xi Jinping
stories.summary: KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun held a press conference in Beijing following her historic meeting with Xi Jinping, highlighting the need for peace across the Taiwan Strait. She expressed hope of inviting Xi to Taiwan if the KMT wins the 2028 election.

stories.title: Russians carry out 810 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, leaving one killed, nine injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 810 strikes on 42 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over a 24-hour period, killing one person and injuring nine others.

stories.title: “It will be very difficult for us until September” – Zelenskyy on possible paths for peace talks
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy warned that the period through September will be very difficult for Ukraine, citing an August US political deadline. He outlined two possible Russian paths forward: escalation or peace negotiations.

stories.title: Cutting fuel to Australia ‘won’t happen’, says Singapore PM, as Albanese secures pledge from our largest petrol source
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese secured a pledge from Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to maintain fuel supplies amid the international crisis. The two countries signed an agreement to continue exchanging refined fuels and liquefied natural gas to ensure mutual energy security.

stories.title: Pakistani women drive a fifth of Senate agenda: Free and Fair Election Network
stories.summary: A report by Pakistan's Free and Fair Election Network found that female senators contributed about 20 percent of the regular plenary agenda during the 23rd parliamentary year, slightly exceeding their proportional representation. The report covered the 2025–2026 parliamentary year and noted that women's legislative contributions spanned economy, security, and taxation issues.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills one in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the town of Hanawya in southern Lebanon killed one person and injured another, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The Israeli army also destroyed residential areas in Aita al-Shaab, and three areas in the Tyre district were hit by Israeli artillery.

stories.title: Pakistan emerges as a key international player as it mediates between US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a key mediator between the US and Iran, leveraging its close ties with both Tehran and Washington. Previous intermediaries had drawn criticism from Iran during the conflict, giving Islamabad a unique diplomatic position.

stories.title: Is China about to launch a rocket from South China Sea international waters?
stories.summary: China plans to launch a Jielong-3 rocket from a converted barge in international waters of the South China Sea, demonstrating a more flexible maritime launch capability. The solid-fuelled rocket is scheduled to lift off on Saturday, according to leaked schedules on Chinese social media.

stories.title: The Future Soldier Loadout: Smarter Gear or Dead Weight?
stories.summary: A discussion featuring three former U.S. servicemembers turned industry leaders examines the next generation of soldier-carried technology. The conversation addresses how frontline capabilities blending human and machine systems may evolve over the next decade and the constraints involved.

stories.title: The Future Soldier Loadout: Smarter Gear or Dead Weight?
stories.summary: A podcast episode featuring three former U.S. military servicemembers turned industry leaders examines the future of soldier equipment and technology. The discussion focuses on next-generation systems that integrate human and machine capabilities and the constraints shaping their development over the next decade.

stories.title: The Future Soldier Loadout: Smarter Gear or Dead Weight?
stories.summary: A discussion featuring three former U.S. servicemembers turned industry leaders examined how next-generation soldier equipment may evolve over the next decade. The conversation focused on emerging technologies that blur the line between human and machine on the battlefield and the constraints shaping their development.

stories.title: Russian attacks over past day leave nine injured, including one child, in Kherson region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck 35 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region using drones, artillery, and aircraft over the past day, injuring nine people including one child.

stories.title: Nigeria general killed as troops repel Borno base attack
stories.summary: Jihadists attacked a military base in northeast Nigeria's Borno state, killing several soldiers including a brigadier general. Officials said it was the second killing of a high-ranking Nigerian military officer in five months.

stories.title: Starmer says he is ‘fed up’ with Trump and Putin’s impact on UK energy costs
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he is "fed up" with the impact of Donald Trump's Middle East actions and Vladimir Putin's conduct on UK energy costs. He called for a plan to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to stabilise household and business energy bills.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a 32-hour ceasefire to mark Orthodox Easter, as broader diplomatic efforts remain stalled. Both Moscow and Kyiv signaled the short truce amid mounting war pressures.

stories.title: Hormuz traffic plummets as Iran asserts control
stories.summary: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained well below 10 percent of normal volumes despite a U.S.-Iran ceasefire, as Tehran warned vessels to stay within its territorial waters. Hundreds of tankers remain trapped inside the Gulf since the war began on February 28, cutting global oil supply by an estimated 20 percent.

stories.title: US considers new crackdown on Chinese telecom companies
stories.summary: The United States is considering a new crackdown on Chinese telecommunications companies, with China Mobile, China Telecom, and China Unicom among the firms potentially targeted.

stories.title: Iran’s supreme leader says does not seek war in written message
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a written message stating that Iran does not seek war. Khamenei has not appeared in public since being appointed to the position.

stories.title: PM, Bilawal agree ‘national harmony need of hour’
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari agreed in a phone call that national harmony is essential to meet current challenges. Bhutto-Zardari congratulated the prime minister on Pakistan's mediation role in bringing the United States and Iran to the negotiating table.

stories.title: US forces to remain deployed near Iran until  ‘real’ agreement reached, says Trump
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that American military ships, aircraft, and personnel would remain deployed near Iran until a lasting peace agreement is reached. He warned of a major escalation if Iran failed to comply but expressed confidence that a deal would be finalized.

stories.title: Gaza media office rejects Board of Peace claim that 602 trucks entered Thursday
stories.summary: Gaza's Government Media Office disputed a claim by the US-led Board of Peace that 602 trucks entered Gaza on Thursday. The office said verified data showed only 207 trucks entered, including 79 aid trucks, calling the Board of Peace statement inaccurate and inconsistent with field realities.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,130 troops, 45 artillery systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russia lost 1,130 troops and 45 artillery systems in the past day fighting against Ukraine. Total Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,308,670 personnel.

stories.title: Tears of joy mark reopening of Jerusalem holy sites after 41 days
stories.summary: Jerusalem's holy sites, including the Al Aqsa Mosque compound, reopened after 41 days of closure following a truce with Iran. Worshippers from Muslim, Christian, and Jewish faiths expressed deep emotion, though tensions flared when police dispersed Muslims at Al Aqsa to allow access for Jewish visitors.

stories.title: Myanmar’s coup leader Min Aung Hlaing sworn in as president
stories.summary: Myanmar's coup leader Min Aung Hlaing was sworn in as president. He pledged to enhance international relations and strengthen ties with ASEAN after the 2021 coup plunged the country into prolonged instability and conflict.

stories.title: Moscow lifts ban on Pakistani potatoes
stories.summary: Russia lifted its ban on potato imports from Pakistan, permitting shipments from Punjab to enter the Russian Federation effective April 8. The ban was lifted after Pakistan submitted pest status records and laboratory reports confirming the absence of identified pests and pathogens.

stories.title: Malaysian business lobby says working from home will hurt city profits, faces backlash
stories.summary: A Malaysian business association faced public backlash after warning that expanded work-from-home arrangements would harm urban businesses. Critics accused the group of prioritizing city-centre profits over the government's plan to reduce fuel consumption and manage rising subsidy costs ahead of a civil service remote-work rollout starting April 15.

stories.title: Report: Over 6,400 Iranian attacks launched since the start of the war
stories.summary: Anadolu Agency reported that Iran launched a total of 6,413 missiles and drones across the region since the war began in late February. Attacks continued during the first two days of the ceasefire, with 151 recorded. Targets included the UAE, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Lawmakers’ schemes outpace sluggish uplift spending
stories.summary: Pakistan's government spent only 41.5 percent of its Public Sector Development Programme budget in the first nine months of the fiscal year, while parliamentarians' own constituency schemes saw roughly 70 percent utilization in just four months. The PSDP had already been cut by 90 billion rupees to fund fuel subsidies.

stories.title: Disperse to Survive: The Logic of French Forward Deterrence
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron delivered a nuclear deterrence speech outlining a new doctrine of "forward deterrence." For the first time, he offered to deploy French Strategic Air Forces to other European countries, proposing to disperse nuclear-capable assets across the continent similarly to how strategic submarines operate in the oceans.

stories.title: Disperse to Survive: The Logic of French Forward Deterrence
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron delivered a nuclear deterrence speech outlining a new doctrine of "forward deterrence," offering for the first time to deploy French Strategic Air Forces to allied European countries. The proposal aims to disperse French nuclear capabilities across the continent as a survival and deterrence strategy.

stories.title: China healthcare stocks outgain Hong Kong market as Middle East roils global investments
stories.summary: China's healthcare stocks listed in Hong Kong have outperformed the broader market as investors seek safe havens amid global volatility driven by the Middle East conflict. The Hang Seng Healthcare Index surged roughly 13 percent since March 23, compared to about 6 percent for the benchmark Hang Seng Index.

stories.title: Pakistan steps up diplomacy as Lebanon strikes strain ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan pledged to support both Iran and the United States in reaching a peaceful settlement as Israeli strikes on Lebanon threatened to derail upcoming negotiations. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief reviewed mediation efforts and arrangements for the Islamabad talks.

stories.title: Xi meets Taiwan opposition chief, expresses ‘full confidence’ in China-Taiwan unity
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang leader Cheng Li-wun in Beijing, expressing confidence in China-Taiwan unity and reiterating opposition to Taiwanese independence. The visit, the first by a KMT leader in a decade, provoked controversy in self-ruled Taiwan.

stories.title: Tel Aviv airport reopens but airfares again skyrocket as foreign carriers stay away
stories.summary: Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion Airport reopened, but airfares surged as most foreign carriers have not resumed service. Israeli travelers face high summer travel costs due to limited flight availability and soaring jet fuel prices linked to the regional war.

stories.title: Why US-Iran ceasefire has not led to Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: Despite a U.S.-Iran ceasefire, the Strait of Hormuz has not fully reopened to commercial shipping. Tehran says the strait is open, but passage still requires coordination with Iran's military forces.

stories.title: Zelensky on ceasefire: Russia has chance not to resume strikes after Easter
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called on Russia not to resume military strikes after the Easter holiday, saying people need a holiday free from threats and real progress toward peace.

stories.title: Kenya: MPs Blame Weak Laws, Police Failures for Stalling Drug Abuse War
stories.summary: A Kenyan parliamentary committee criticized security agencies and regulators for failing to address alcohol and drug abuse effectively. Lawmakers accused segments of the police of enabling the drug trade due to weak enforcement and legal gaps.

stories.title: Vladislav Inozemtsev: A collapse is not imminent
stories.summary: Economist Vladislav Inozemtsev discussed Russia's oil revenues, the impact of Ukrainian strikes, and argued that despite economic pressures, a Russian collapse is not imminent and the war will ultimately be decided on the ground.

stories.title: Iran’s Other Front: The War Over the Internet
stories.summary: Following Israeli and American strikes on Iranian military installations, Iran's government deliberately shut down nearly all domestic internet access, causing a 98 percent collapse in traffic. The blackout reflected Tehran's long-standing approach of treating free internet access as a state-controlled privilege.

stories.title: Iran’s Other Front: The War Over the Internet
stories.summary: Following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, the Iranian government shut down nearly all internet traffic, causing a 98 percent collapse within hours. The deliberate communications blackout reflects Tehran's longstanding practice of controlling internet access as a tool of state power during crises.

stories.title: Capital on high alert ahead of US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Islamabad was placed on red alert ahead of U.S.-Iran peace talks, with more than 10,000 police and security personnel deployed across the city. Multi-tier security arrangements are being supervised by the military, assisted by paramilitary Rangers and police forces from Islamabad and Punjab.

stories.title: Iranians pay tribute to slain supreme leader weeks after killing
stories.summary: Thousands of Iranians rallied in tribute to former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed on the first day of the war with the United States and Israel. Participants also expressed criticism of ceasefire talks expected to take place in Pakistan.

stories.title: Israeli military says Hezbollah launched missile at Israel, triggering sirens
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported that Hezbollah launched a missile at Israel, triggering air-raid sirens. The attack follows Israel's heaviest bombardment of Lebanon during the war, which occurred on April 8.

stories.title: Iran’s chief foreign affairs strategist dies after US-Israeli air strike injuries
stories.summary: Kamal Kharrazi, head of Iran's Council of Foreign Relations and former foreign minister, has died from injuries sustained in US-Israeli air strikes. The same attack on April 1 killed his wife. Kharrazi was a key adviser to both the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and his successor Mojtaba Khamenei.

stories.title: John Spencer: US can force open Strait of Hormuz if it decides to
stories.summary: US military expert John Spencer discussed the feasibility of the US forcibly reopening the Strait of Hormuz if necessary. The analysis came as a ceasefire with Iran took effect and questions arose about what the joint US-Israeli campaign achieved.

stories.title: Australian War Memorial amends Ben Roberts-Smith display after former soldier charged with war crimes
stories.summary: The Australian War Memorial updated the display for former SAS corporal Ben Roberts-Smith in its Hall of Valour after he was charged with five counts of the war crime of murder. The revised plaque now references the war crime charges and the ongoing legal process.

stories.title: Partisans scout Russian military unit in Rozdolne, Crimea
stories.summary: Ukrainian partisan forces conducted reconnaissance on a Russian military unit stationed in the settlement of Rozdolne in temporarily occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Melania Trump denies connection to Epstein case, calls accusations ‘baseless lies’
stories.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump denied any connection to the Jeffrey Epstein case, calling the accusations baseless lies. She called for Congress to hold a public hearing centered on survivors and claimed the allegations against her were financially and politically motivated.

stories.title: Pakistan’s defense minister calls Israel ‘cancerous’ ahead of US-Iran talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistan's Defense Minister Khawaja Asif called Israel "cancerous" and criticized it as a state created on Palestinian land, days into Pakistan-brokered ceasefire talks. Israeli PM Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Sa'ar denounced the remarks, which were later deleted.

stories.title: Kuwait condemns drone attacks on vital facilities, Iran denies involvement
stories.summary: Kuwait condemned drone attacks on its vital facilities, calling them a violation of its sovereignty and attributing them to Iran and its proxies. Iran denied involvement in the strikes, which occurred on a Thursday evening.

stories.title: Gulf states rethink security in light of US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Gulf states are reassessing their security partnerships following the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, which turned American bases on Gulf soil into targets for Iranian retaliation. The nations face the challenge of rebuilding economies while contending with an emboldened Tehran and its remaining missile capabilities.

stories.title: Occupiers train students in military skills and carry out covert mobilization in Mariupol
stories.summary: In Russian-occupied Mariupol, Russian forces are reportedly training students in military skills and conducting covert mobilization efforts among the local population.

stories.title: A new generation of Jewish leaders is rethinking what comes next - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: An 18-month fellowship program is convening a new generation of Jewish leaders across North America. The initiative aims to explore community needs through the lens of Jewish texts and ideas amid growing global complexity.

stories.title: White House warned staff against betting on Iran war, report says
stories.summary: The White House sent a staff-wide email warning employees not to exploit their positions to place bets on prediction markets related to the Iran war. The warning came shortly after President Trump announced a sudden pause in strikes on Iran. More than $760 million in oil futures activity was reported around that period.

stories.title: Djibouti: Djibouti Election Unfolds at Strategic Shipping Chokepoint
stories.summary: Djibouti held a presidential election expected to extend President Ismail Omar Guelleh's 27-year rule. The strategically located country hosts major foreign military bases and sits along a key global shipping route affected by regional conflict.

stories.title: Ecuador raises tariffs on Colombia to 100% from 50%
stories.summary: Ecuador announced it is raising tariffs on imports from neighboring Colombia to 100%, up from 50%. The Ecuadorian government cited Colombia's alleged failure to implement agreed-upon border security measures as justification.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts hurtle home from Moon toward Pacific splashdown
stories.summary: The Artemis II crew is heading back to Earth after completing the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years. The astronauts are preparing for re-entry and a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast on Friday, marking the most critical phase of the 10-day mission.

stories.title: Rocket hits building in northern Israel: Report
stories.summary: A rocket struck a building in Misgav Am in northern Israel, according to the Israeli Broadcasting Authority. The Israeli Home Front Command had activated sirens in the area due to the threat of rocket and missile launches from Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump says optimistic on Iran despite Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: President Trump expressed optimism about prospects with Iran despite ongoing Israeli strikes on Lebanon, describing Iran's leaders as more reasonable than their public rhetoric suggests.

stories.title: Israel seeks Lebanon talks after bombardments threaten Iran truce
stories.summary: A senior Israeli official indicated that Israel was preparing to scale down military operations in Lebanon and pursue diplomatic talks, as continued bombardments threatened to undermine the fragile truce with Iran.

stories.title: Lebanon reeling as Israeli strikes continue after 300 killed yesterday
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon following a day in which more than 300 people were reported killed. Rocket sirens sounded in northern Israel as calls to extend a regional ceasefire went unheeded.

stories.title: Cheng hopeful to invite Xi Jinping to Taiwan if the KMT wins 2028 election – as it happened
stories.summary: KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun met Communist Party chief Xi Jinping in Beijing on Friday, the first such meeting between leaders of the two parties since 2016. Both leaders emphasized peace across the Taiwan Strait, and Cheng expressed hope of inviting Xi to Taiwan if the KMT wins the 2028 presidential election.

stories.title: Dmitriev arrives in US for talks with Trump representatives – Reuters
stories.summary: Kirill Dmitriev, a special envoy of Russian President Vladimir Putin, traveled to the United States to hold meetings with senior members of the Trump administration, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Jewish leader of UK’s Green Party calls to end trade, diplomatic ties with Israel
stories.summary: Adrian Ramsay's co-leader of the UK Green Party, Adrian Polanski, who is Jewish, called for ending trade and diplomatic ties with Israel during his party's local election campaign.

stories.title: Tyson Fury insists he’s ‘still got it’ ahead of Makhmudov comeback fight
stories.summary: Former heavyweight champion Tyson Fury announced a comeback fight against Russian-born fighter Arslanbek Makhmudov. Fury insisted he remains competitive and expressed interest in a future bout with Anthony Joshua.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 42 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire between the US and Iran took effect on day 42 of US-Israeli attacks on Iran. However, disputes over the scope of the truce are fueling continued regional tensions.

stories.title: PIA fleet expansion on the cards
stories.summary: Arif Habib, chairman of the consortium that owns Pakistan International Airlines, said PIA currently has 30 aircraft with 18 operational and plans to double the fleet to 60 aircraft. Five to six planes require repair and maintenance before they can return to service.

stories.title: Trump says Iran should not charge fees to tankers going through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran should not impose fees on oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Media reports had suggested Iran was considering charging a toll for vessels passing through the critical waterway.

stories.title: Spain is failing the West and weakening Europe's diplomatic hand  - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial criticized Spain, a NATO member, for underfunding collective defense, obstructing allied operations, downgrading relations with Israel, and restoring ties with Tehran, arguing these actions weaken Europe's diplomatic credibility.

stories.title: IDF dropped 18,000 bombs during Iran war
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force dropped 18,000 bombs during the Iran war as part of approximately 1,000 waves of aircraft sorties. US Central Command reported striking over 13,000 targets during the conflict.

stories.title: ‘Irresponsible failure’: Google, Meta, Snap and Microsoft slam EU over child sexual abuse law lapse
stories.summary: The European Parliament blocked the extension of a temporary law allowing tech companies to scan for child sexual exploitation material on their platforms. Google, Meta, Snap, and Microsoft criticized the decision, while experts warned the legal gap could sharply reduce reports of abuse.

stories.title: Welcome to Y’all Street: bullish Dallas aims to steal New York’s financial crown
stories.summary: Dallas, Texas, is positioning itself as a rival to New York's financial dominance, attracting major banks including Goldman Sachs, which is building a $700 million campus for over 5,000 staff. The city is leveraging looser regulations and lower taxes to draw financial institutions.

stories.title: US travellers mistakenly think China ‘happy funeral’ celebrating longevity is trendy eatery
stories.summary: American YouTuber Ludwig and a friend, while on a motorcycle journey across China from Guangdong to Inner Mongolia, mistook a traditional Chinese "happy funeral" banquet celebrating a long life for a trendy restaurant. Local attendees gave the travelers an unexpected warm welcome.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump casts doubt on Iran war ceasefire over continued closure of strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump cast doubt on the US-Iran ceasefire over Iran's continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz, while Israel and Hezbollah continued exchanging strikes. Islamabad was placed on strict lockdown as Pakistan prepared to host historic US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Australia fuel watch tracker: check current petrol and diesel prices, service station outages and shipments – in charts
stories.summary: Australia is experiencing a fuel crisis as Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts oil shipments, causing service station outages and elevated petrol and diesel prices. The federal government has released fuel reserves, cut fuel excise taxes, and launched a national fuel security plan.

stories.title: Israeli army hits residential areas in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck residential areas in the town of Ayta ash Shab in southern Lebanon. Simultaneously, the Israeli Home Front Command activated sirens in northern Israel over the threat of rocket and missile fire from Lebanon.

stories.title: Energy prices may take ‘months’ to normalise, despite ceasefire: Analysts
stories.summary: Analysts say energy prices may take months to return to normal despite the US-Iran ceasefire, as markets require a predictable and stable flow of cargo through the Strait of Hormuz before stabilizing.

stories.title: US Republicans block attempt to rein in Trump’s war powers over Iran campaign
stories.summary: US Senate Republicans blocked a Democratic effort to reassert congressional authority over President Trump's war powers regarding the Iran campaign. Democrats have begun openly discussing impeachment after Trump's statement that "a whole civilization will die."

stories.title: Fisherman catches Chinese drone; Iran war’s lessons for China: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: An Indonesian fisherman reportedly caught a Chinese underwater drone near a strategic waterway leading to Australia. The incident was among several highlighted stories covering Hong Kong, mainland China, and the broader Asia-Pacific region.

stories.title: Council of Europe's Committee against Torture points to problems in Ukraine’s psychiatric and social care institutions
stories.summary: The Council of Europe's Committee for the Prevention of Torture (CPT) published findings highlighting problems in Ukraine's psychiatric hospitals and social care institutions, including unequal living conditions, staff shortages, and over-reliance on medication-based treatment.

stories.title: UN condemns drone strike on Sudan wedding, calls for end to hostilities
stories.summary: The United Nations condemned a drone strike that killed 30 people at a wedding in North Darfur state, Sudan. Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric called for an end to hostilities.

stories.title: Undeterred by war, foreign students at universities learned what it means to be Israeli
stories.summary: Despite ongoing missile fire during the conflict with Iran, many international students at Israeli universities chose to remain. Students described adapting to routines of moving between classrooms and safe rooms during attacks.

stories.title: As ceasefire halts fighting, Iran war becomes a battlefield for votes
stories.summary: As a ceasefire halted fighting in the Iran war, Israeli domestic politics intensified ahead of upcoming elections. Prime Minister Netanyahu's political standing may not have improved as much as hoped, and rivals are positioning to capitalize.

stories.title: South Korean youth hooked on easy access to drugs online
stories.summary: Drug trafficking in South Korea has increasingly shifted online, with teenagers and young adults purchasing illegal substances through platforms like Telegram and the dark web. Buyers pay with bitcoin and receive instructions for collecting their orders at designated pickup locations.

stories.title: Hong Kong government must guard against exploitation of diesel subsidy, experts warn
stories.summary: Hong Kong announced a two-month, HK$3-per-litre diesel subsidy totaling HK$1.8 billion to help the transport sector cope with record-high oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict. Industry leaders and lawmakers warned the government to guard against fuel companies exploiting the relief measure through discount manipulations.

stories.title: 2 years on: China proves its ‘desert wheat farms’ are not a hoax
stories.summary: A wheat-growing project launched two years ago on the fringes of the Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang, China, has continued to survive repeated sandstorms. The initiative aims to combat desertification and strengthen national food security by cultivating crops in sandy terrain.

stories.title: Xi tells Taiwan opposition leader people on both sides of strait are Chinese in rare meeting
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang chair Cheng Li-wun in Beijing, the first such high-level contact between China and Taiwan's opposition in a decade. Xi declared that people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait are Chinese. The visit has sparked controversy in Taiwan.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Sentences More Terror Suspects to 60, 40 Years Imprisonment
stories.summary: A special court in Abuja, Nigeria, sentenced scores of defendants to prison terms of up to 60 years for alleged involvement with Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP).

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Govt Counters U.S. Advisory Warning Citizens Against Travel to Nigeria
stories.summary: The Nigerian government pushed back against a U.S. State Department travel advisory warning American citizens against traveling to Nigeria due to insecurity. The advisory also urged non-essential U.S. embassy officials to leave the country.

stories.title: Cameroon: Empty Cooking Pots, Rising Hunger in Cameroon
stories.summary: The World Food Programme reported that millions of people in Cameroon are suffering from rising hunger driven by conflict, displacement, and climate shocks. WFP and other humanitarian organizations are stretching limited budgets to provide support.

stories.title: Palestinian journalist describes losing prosthetic eye in Israeli prison
stories.summary: Palestinian journalist Muath Amarne reported that his prosthetic eye fell out due to an untreated infection while he was held in Israeli detention.

stories.title: Take down bird feeders this summer to cut spread of avian disease, says RSPB
stories.summary: The RSPB advised UK bird lovers to remove seed and nut feeders between May and October to reduce the spread of avian diseases such as trichomonosis. The parasitic disease has caused significant declines in greenfinch populations and spreads more easily when birds cluster at feeders in warmer months.

stories.title: Kuwait blames Iran for drone strike, Iran denies responsibility
stories.summary: Kuwait has accused Iran and its proxies of carrying out a drone attack on Kuwaiti territory on Thursday night. Iran has denied any responsibility for the strike.

stories.title: South Sudan: South Sudan's New Cybercrime Law Ramps Up Threat of Jail for Journalists
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists called on South Sudan's authorities to reform a new cybercrimes law that punishes defamation with up to five years in prison, criminalizes speech on broad grounds, and lacks protections for whistleblowers and public interest reporting.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Declares War On Nairobi Cartels, Undermining County Progress
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto declared a crackdown on cartels operating in Nairobi, pledging to end the protection of powerful interests that he said were undermining public welfare and the county's progress.

stories.title: Starmer, Trump discussed opening Strait of Hormuz, Downing Street says
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and U.S. President Donald Trump discussed plans to restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz as quickly as possible, Downing Street confirmed, following a U.S. ceasefire with Iran.

stories.title: In Yes!, Israeli director Nadav Lapid skewers his country’s ‘moral abyss’ after Oct. 7
