stories.summary: Israeli director Nadav Lapid's satirical film "Yes!" critiques what he calls Israel's "moral abyss" following October 7. Lapid acknowledged the film may be difficult for many Diaspora Jews but said he stands by his convictions.

stories.title: Trump posts graphic video of woman’s killing in Florida
stories.summary: President Donald Trump posted a graphic surveillance video on Truth Social showing a woman being killed in Fort Myers, Florida, by a man described as an undocumented Haitian immigrant. The post was seen as an attempt to redirect public attention toward immigration amid questions about the Iran war and other controversies.

stories.title: This Was the First War Against AI
stories.summary: The war on Iran has highlighted geopolitical miscalculations related to the current artificial intelligence technology race. The conflict is described as the first war fought against AI capabilities.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims 35 attacks in response to Israel's assault on Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it carried out 35 attacks targeting Israeli settlements, forces, vehicles, and military sites in response to heavy Israeli strikes on Lebanon. Since March 2, Hezbollah has conducted over 1,500 attacks on Israel, while Israeli operations have killed nearly 1,900 people across Lebanon in the same period.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader meets Xi Jinping in Beijing
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun traveled to Beijing and met with Chinese President Xi Jinping, becoming the party's first sitting leader to visit China in a decade.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires missile at southern port of Ashdod as IDF strikes launchers in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired a missile at the southern Israeli port city of Ashdod, triggering sirens in Tel Aviv due to falling interceptor debris. A home in Misgav Am was also hit by a rocket. The IDF struck Hezbollah launchers in Lebanon in response.

stories.title: Enemy delivers mysterious shipping containers to Berdiansk Port for second week straight, says Andriushchenko
stories.summary: According to adviser Petro Andriushchenko, Russian forces have been using military tractors and trucks to transport shipping containers of unknown contents from the Port of Rostov-on-Don to the occupied Port of Berdiansk for a second consecutive week.

stories.title: Army general and several soldiers killed in attack on military base in Nigeria's northeast
stories.summary: Jihadist fighters attacked a military base in northeast Nigeria, killing several soldiers including a brigadier general. It marks the second killing of a high-ranking Nigerian officer in five months.

stories.title: South Korea appoints envoy to Iran to ensure safety of vessels in the region
stories.summary: South Korea's Foreign Ministry appointed Chung Byung-ha as a special envoy to Iran to address the safety of South Korean vessels in the region. Twenty-six vessels linked to Seoul remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz due to Iranian restrictions.

stories.title: Jardine Matheson to exit Swire’s Taikoo Place, consolidate offices in Central: sources
stories.summary: Jardine Matheson is vacating its remaining office space in FWD Tower at Taikoo Place in Hong Kong and consolidating staff at Jardine House in Central. The move reflects a broader trend of companies returning to Hong Kong's core business district, where demand for premium office space has been rising.

stories.title: US Republicans block bid to rein in Trump Iran war powers
stories.summary: U.S. House Republicans blocked a Democratic effort to end American attacks on Iran and curb President Trump's war powers on April 9.

stories.title: Sara Duterte leads early 2028 Philippine presidential poll as rivals struggle to unite
stories.summary: A survey by Manila-based pollster WR Numero found Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio leading the prospective 2028 presidential race with 36 percent support. This is despite her father's detention at The Hague, a collapsed alliance with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and ongoing impeachment proceedings before the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Could Trump be forced out of office? – podcast
stories.summary: Calls emerged from both the political left and right to invoke the 25th Amendment to remove President Donald Trump from office, despite his securing a temporary ceasefire with Iran. The Guardian's podcast examined the various constitutional mechanisms Congress could use to remove a sitting president.

stories.title: ‘Nobody’s in charge’: is power sharing still working in Northern Ireland?
stories.summary: Northern Ireland marks the 28th anniversary of the Good Friday Agreement amid widespread concerns about feuding political parties and deteriorating public services. While the 1998 accord ended the Troubles and established lasting peace, public faith in the Stormont power-sharing government has eroded.

stories.title: Man who allegedly claimed partner died in ‘crash with kangaroo’ in NT charged with murder
stories.summary: A 33-year-old man near Tennant Creek in Australia's Northern Territory was charged with murdering his 27-year-old partner after allegedly telling police she died in a car crash with a kangaroo. Police found the woman dead with visible facial injuries in a vehicle on an outback highway.

stories.title: Russia's Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire, expects Ukraine to do the same
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a ceasefire over a two-day Orthodox Easter period and called on Ukraine to reciprocate, the Kremlin said on April 9.

stories.title: Ukraine installs nearly 500 MW of energy storage systems – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's state grid operator Ukrenergo reported that nearly 500 megawatts of energy storage capacity had been installed across Ukraine's energy system as of early April.

stories.title: Attacks cut Saudi oil output and East-West pipeline flow, state news agency says
stories.summary: Attacks on Saudi energy facilities reduced the kingdom's oil production capacity by approximately 600,000 barrels per day and cut East-West pipeline throughput by about 700,000 bpd, according to Saudi state news agency SPA.

stories.title: US military bases in Gulf 'useless' after Iranian strikes, experts say
stories.summary: Middle East experts argue that at least a dozen US military sites across the Gulf region have been so severely damaged by Iranian retaliatory strikes that they now create more vulnerabilities than benefits. The New York Times previously described the bases as "all but uninhabitable."

stories.title: UK's Starmer says Iran conflict shows Britain must take a new path
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the Iran conflict must serve as a turning point for Britain, pledging to strengthen the country's economy and military to address what he called a more volatile and dangerous world.

stories.title: US summons Iraq envoy over attacks by Iran-backed groups
stories.summary: The US State Department summoned Iraq's ambassador to condemn attacks by Iran-backed armed groups against American interests in Iraq during the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: UK PM Keir Starmer visits Gulf to shore up ‘fragile’ US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited Doha as part of a Gulf tour, where he discussed efforts to support and sustain the fragile US-Iran ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Russian special envoy Dmitriev in US, meeting Trump administration members, sources say
stories.summary: Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev is in the United States meeting Trump administration officials to discuss a Ukraine peace deal and U.S.-Russia economic cooperation, according to sources familiar with the visit.

stories.title: Pakistan prepares for U.S.-Iran talks with anxiety
stories.summary: Pakistan is preparing with unease for upcoming diplomatic talks between the United States and Iran, amid regional tensions over the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Peace is a common wish, Xi Jinping tells Taiwan’s opposition leader Cheng Li-wun
stories.summary: Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping met with Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in the first meeting between sitting leaders of the two parties in nine years. Both sides emphasized peace, development, communication, and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire shows strain ahead of talks with oil flows squeezed
stories.summary: The two-week US-Iran ceasefire showed further signs of strain on Friday, one day before the two sides were scheduled to negotiate in Pakistan. Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain disrupted.

stories.title: 650 Iranian missiles fired, 24 killed, and 10,800 Israeli strikes: The war in numbers
stories.summary: During the Iran war, Iran fired approximately 650 missiles at Israel, killing 24 people—all civilians—most of whom were outside bomb shelters. Israel conducted over 10,800 strikes, while the US struck more than 13,000 targets.

stories.title: Why Japanese firm’s tie-up with Ukrainian drone maker sparks concerns in Russia
stories.summary: Russia formally protested a proposed investment by a Japanese company in a Ukrainian drone manufacturer, with Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko raising concerns in a meeting with Japan's ambassador to Moscow. Analysts suggest Moscow fears Tokyo may be moving toward closer defense cooperation with Kyiv and potentially lifting its long-standing ban on weapon exports.

stories.title: Islamabad prepares to host historic negotiations between Iran and the US
stories.summary: Pakistan's capital Islamabad was placed under strict lockdown with army deployments and a public holiday declared ahead of historic US-Iran peace negotiations. The talks proceeded despite the increasingly precarious state of the US-Iran ceasefire and Israel's continued bombardment of Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel continues assault on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel continued air strikes across Lebanon, with the latest recorded in the southern town of Babliyeh. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed strikes would continue "wherever necessary." Since hostilities began in March, nearly 1,900 people have been killed and over 6,000 wounded in Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel plans talks with Lebanon as violence imperils Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu authorized direct negotiations with Lebanon aimed at disarming Hezbollah and establishing formal relations between the two countries. Netanyahu stressed there was no ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, which have technically been at war since 1948.

stories.title: Tai Po probe: fire department to propose law changes, tougher penalties to boost safety
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades at a Tai Po housing estate, which killed 168 people in November, held its 10th day of hearings. The Fire Services Department's handling of shutdown notices for fire safety systems is under scrutiny, and the department plans to propose legislative changes and tougher penalties.

stories.title: Shipping in Strait of Hormuz at a standstill despite US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz has come to a standstill despite the US-Iran ceasefire, with Washington and Tehran each accusing the other of failing to honor the terms of the truce agreement.

stories.title: Kuwait condemns drone attacks, Iran denies involvement
stories.summary: Kuwait condemned drone attacks targeting vital facilities in the country on Thursday evening. Iran denied any involvement in the strikes.

stories.title: Greens say Australia should step up pressure on Israel over ‘disastrous, illegal, immoral war’ on Lebanon
stories.summary: Australia's Greens party called on the federal government to pressure Israel to stop strikes on Lebanon, including cancelling weapons contracts. The call came as former Prime Minister Tony Abbott separately suggested Australia should send troops to support US forces in the Middle East.

stories.title: Russia plans to open four more embassies in African countries to increase its influence
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov announced plans to open four additional embassies in African countries, aiming to expand Russia's political and ideological influence on the continent.

stories.title: Middle East live: Vance heads to Pakistan for Iran talks as Israeli assault on Lebanon tests truce
stories.summary: US Vice-President J.D. Vance departed for Pakistan to lead mediated talks with Iran aimed at resolving the Middle East war, as massive Israeli strikes on Lebanon tested the fragile US-Iran ceasefire. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu separately authorized direct negotiations with Lebanon, expected to take place in Washington the following week.

stories.title: Asian economies face ‘formidable test’ as Middle East conflict drags on: ADB
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank projected that developing Asia's GDP growth will slow to 5.1 percent this year from 5.4 percent in 2025 due to the ongoing Middle East conflict. The ADB warned that impacts from the US-Israeli war on Iran would ripple through manufacturing, tourism, and other industries across the region.

stories.title: Ethiopia army base used to support Sudan paramilitary: report
stories.summary: A Yale University report found that an Ethiopian military base near the Sudanese border has been providing support to Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

stories.title: WATCH: IDF strikes Hezbollah launchers following missile barrage on Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces struck 10 Hezbollah rocket launchers in Lebanon following a missile barrage targeting Israeli territory. The IDF had earlier warned of a possible increase in rocket launches from Lebanon extending beyond border areas.

stories.title: Trump weighs pulling some US troops from Europe amid NATO strains, official says
stories.summary: President Trump has discussed with advisers the possibility of withdrawing some U.S. troops from Europe, reportedly frustrated by NATO allies' reluctance to help secure the Strait of Hormuz and the lack of progress on acquiring Greenland.

stories.title: Trump, Starmer discuss reopening of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Trump and British Prime Minister Starmer discussed plans to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway carrying approximately one-fifth of global oil consumption. Restoring navigation through the strait is a key component of the US-Iran ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Netanyahu greenlights Israel-Lebanon talks in Washington amid ceasefire tensions
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon are set to hold talks in Washington amid escalating tensions over continued Israeli strikes in Lebanon and growing concerns about the fragile US-Iran ceasefire. Heavy fighting, rising casualties, and disputes over the scope of the truce have complicated regional security efforts.

stories.title: Lava bursts forth as Hawaii’s Kilauea volcano erupts
stories.summary: Kilauea volcano on Hawaii's Big Island erupted on Thursday, sending lava fountains over 200 meters into the air. The eruption produced 3.6 million cubic yards of lava, prompting the closure of Hawaii Volcanoes National Park.

stories.title: Attack on Saudi Arabian pipeline wiped out 10 percent of kingdom's oil export capacity
stories.summary: Attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline knocked out approximately 700,000 barrels per day of oil capacity, representing roughly 10 percent of the kingdom's current exports, according to the Saudi energy ministry.

stories.title: Russia’s internet regulator bans site that tracks which VPNs still work in the country
stories.summary: Russia's internet regulator Roskomnadzor banned the "VPN Traffic Light" website, which tracked which VPN services still functioned within the country. The decision was made on April 6, with blocking implemented on April 9.

stories.title: Trump says Iran doing 'poor job' of letting oil through Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Trump accused Iran of doing a "very poor job" of allowing oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and said Tehran was breaching the terms of the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Scientists stunned as chimpanzees turn on friends in killing spree
stories.summary: Researchers studying the Ngogo chimpanzee community in Uganda's Kibale National Park documented how a stable group that had been observed for two decades fractured and descended into years of deadly intra-group violence.

stories.title: ‘No offensive role’ for Australia as clock ticks towards first US-Iran talks since war
stories.summary: US Vice-President J.D. Vance is traveling to Islamabad, Pakistan, for the first round of direct US-Iran talks aimed at ending the Middle East war. The negotiations, set for Saturday morning local time, mark the most significant high-level face-to-face US-Iran contact since 1979.

stories.title: Putin declares ceasefire in Ukraine for Orthodox Easter
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared a ceasefire in Ukraine for Orthodox Easter, covering a two-day period, and called on Ukraine to reciprocate.

stories.title: Thousands of electric vehicles recalled in Australia due to battery fire risk
stories.summary: Hyundai issued a recall in Australia for nearly 5,000 electric vehicles due to a battery management software fault that could cause fires while the cars are recharging or parked. The local recall is part of a global action involving more than 100,000 vehicles.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says Iran attacks have affected oil production
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reported that Iranian attacks on the kingdom's energy infrastructure killed one person and impacted oil production capacity.

stories.title: Commercial areas, tony seafront neighborhoods among parts of Beirut hit in Wednesday’s wave of strikes
stories.summary: Intensive Israeli airstrikes hit commercial districts and seafront neighborhoods in Beirut that had traditionally been spared from conflict. The IDF said Hezbollah had redeployed assets to those areas of the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Russian ministers arrive in Dagestan after flooding kills six, displaces thousands
stories.summary: Three Russian ministers arrived in Dagestan on April 9 to oversee the emergency response to flooding that has killed six people and prompted the evacuation of thousands in the Caucasus region.

stories.title: UN envoy meets Iran’s deputy minister and visits bombed sites in Tehran
stories.summary: UN envoy Jean Arnault met Iran's deputy minister and visited bombed sites in Tehran. He also met representatives of the Iranian Red Crescent Society.

stories.title: Solid-state battery firms in China and US line up IPOs as oil prices lift EV appeal
stories.summary: Three solid-state battery developers in China and the United States are pursuing initial public offerings amid elevated oil prices and growing demand for energy-efficient technology. China's Qingtao Energy filed for a Hong Kong listing, Beijing WeLion began pre-listing preparations for Shenzhen, and US-based Factorial is also advancing toward an IPO.

stories.title: Why Trump’s Hormuz rebuke won’t derail South Korea’s ‘very strong’ alliance with US
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly rebuked South Korea for refusing to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz, adding strain to the 70-year alliance. Analysts said the relationship would likely withstand the pressure, citing deep institutional military ties and broad support for the alliance in both countries.

stories.title: Can a ‘community with a shared future’ prevail over zero-sum rivalry?
stories.summary: A forthcoming summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, rescheduled for May, highlights two competing visions for global order. Trump postponed the original April meeting due to the war on Iran, and a swift resolution to the conflict before the summit appears unlikely.

stories.title: In written message, Iran supreme leader says Tehran does not seek war but will not renounce legitimate rights
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written message that Tehran does not seek war with the United States and Israel but will not renounce its legitimate rights. The message coincided with 40 days since his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was assassinated on February 28.

stories.title: US Democrats fail in bid to curb Trump’s Iran war powers
stories.summary: U.S. House Republicans blocked a Democratic attempt to curb President Trump's war powers regarding Iran.

stories.title: Thailand snatches US$260 million from cross-border scammers in ‘decisive’ crackdown
stories.summary: Thailand's Anti-Money Laundering Office seized assets worth 8.3 billion baht (US$260 million) linked to transnational cyber scam operations based in Cambodia. The latest seizure included cash, vehicles, and bank deposits, bringing total confiscated assets in the widening probe to more than 20 billion baht.

stories.title: Iran's Supreme Leader says does not seek war in written message
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated in a message broadcast on state television that Iran does not seek war, declaring the country will nonetheless protect its legitimate rights.

stories.title: Democratic National Committee panel rejects measure singling out AIPAC for criticism
stories.summary: The Democratic National Committee's Resolutions Committee rejected a measure that specifically singled out AIPAC for criticism. Instead, the panel advanced a broader resolution condemning "dark money" in politics without naming specific organizations.

stories.title: UK tracked 3 Russian subs carrying out alleged covert operation in British waters
stories.summary: The United Kingdom, alongside Norway and other allies, tracked three Russian submarines conducting a suspected covert operation in the North Atlantic within British waters.

stories.title: Public outrage as Chinese man takes part in matchmaking event while wife goes to toilet
stories.summary: A man in Bengbu, Anhui province, China, sparked online outrage after joining a matchmaking event and claiming to be single while his wife had briefly gone to the bathroom. The incident occurred during a popular matchmaking event called "Auntie Wang's Matchmaking," and the man was exposed on the spot.

stories.title: White House warned staff against market bets amid war on Iran: Report
stories.summary: The White House sent a staff-wide email on March 24 warning government employees against improperly leveraging their positions to place bets in futures markets. The warning came one day after President Trump posted on Truth Social that he would order a delay in attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Filmmaker accuses school of ‘blatantly lying’ in row over documentary screening
stories.summary: Hong Kong filmmaker Mabel Cheung Yuen-ting accused Ying Wa Girls' School of "blatantly lying" about arrangements for screening her award-winning coming-of-age documentary at an Italian film festival. The dispute escalated after the school distanced itself from the screening.

stories.title: Lebanese man describes the loss of his family in Israeli attacks
stories.summary: A Lebanese man from the southern city of Tyre described returning home to find his family killed in an Israeli air strike on March 6. Since the start of March, Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed over 1,700 people and wounded nearly 6,000.

stories.title: Law enforcement officers expose criminal group that earned about UAH 10M per month from drug trafficking from EU
stories.summary: Ukrainian police dismantled a transnational drug trafficking network that smuggled narcotics from the European Union into Ukraine. The five-member criminal group was earning approximately 10 million Ukrainian hryvnias per month from the operation.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky meets Hungarian minority as Orban faces key election
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with members of Hungary's ethnic minority community in western Ukraine's Zakarpattia region. The visit comes as Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán faces a key domestic election.

stories.title: Is oil crisis just the start of economic pain for Hongkongers?
stories.summary: Hong Kong bus company operator Martin Lau of ABC Touring Car Company described mounting losses from surging fuel prices, saying he has tried reducing services and performing his own fleet repairs. The situation reflects broader economic pressures facing Hong Kong's transport sector amid the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Israel a ‘curse for humanity,’ says Pakistan Defense Minister
stories.summary: Pakistan's Defense Minister Khawaja Asif called Israel a "curse for humanity" and "cancerous" while Islamabad positions itself as a mediator in ceasefire talks between the US, Israel, and Iran. The remarks drew sharp criticism from Israeli officials.

stories.title: India proposes new rules to regulate news and political posts on social media
stories.summary: India's government proposed new regulations to govern news-related and political content on social media, which would grant authorities greater power over posts shared by podcasters and influencers.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s Likud takes hit in polls, which show most Israelis oppose Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: New Israeli polls show Prime Minister Netanyahu's Likud party losing support, while a majority of Israelis oppose the Iran ceasefire. A Channel 12 survey found 79% of respondents support continued military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Dozens of states condemn attacks on UN peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: On April 9, dozens of states issued a joint statement at the United Nations condemning attacks on UN peacekeepers in Lebanon and calling for greater protections, following the deaths of three Indonesian soldiers serving in the peacekeeping mission.

stories.title: US: Pentagon must restore journalists' access, judge says
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge ruled that the Pentagon has not complied with court orders requiring it to restore journalists' access to the building. New rules have prevented reporters from entering without an escort.

stories.title: Israel seeks peace talks with Lebanon ‘as soon as possible’ as world condemns Tel Aviv’s bombardment amid US-Iran truce
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered ministers to begin direct talks with Lebanon, pushing for Hezbollah's disarmament. Lebanon stated it wants a ceasefire declared before negotiations begin. At least 300 people were killed and over 1,000 wounded in Israeli strikes on Lebanon on Wednesday.

stories.title: Can Japan regain shipbuilding might with US$6.3 billion funding plan?
stories.summary: Japan is advancing an investment plan of up to 1 trillion yen (US$6.3 billion) to revitalize its shipbuilding industry, which has lost ground to China's dominant sector. Analysts cautioned that funding alone cannot overcome challenges including higher costs, labor shortages, and years of lost capacity.

stories.title: How the cost of holidays, food and clothes is rising - despite the Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Despite a ceasefire with Iran, consumer costs in the UK continue to rise, with fuel prices already surging and increases expected in flights, mortgages, and food prices.

stories.title: Iran war live: Israeli attacks on Lebanon threaten US-Iran ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that "time is running out" as Israeli military attacks on Lebanon threaten to derail ongoing US-Iran ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: ‘Sold us illusions’: Opposition accuses Netanyahu of failing war goals, backs Lebanon talks
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leaders accused Prime Minister Netanyahu of failing to achieve stated war goals following the Iran ceasefire, saying he "sold illusions" to the public. Some opposition figures expressed support for negotiations with Lebanon regarding Hezbollah disarmament.

stories.title: Ukrainian USFs wipe out Russian Tor-M1 air defense system in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's 1st Separate Center of the Unmanned Systems Forces destroyed a Russian Tor-M1 surface-to-air missile system in occupied territory of the Donetsk region. The strike marks the ninth Tor-M1 system destroyed in nine days.

stories.title: Iran ‘doing a very poor job’ of allowing oil through Strait of Hormuz, Trump says
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized Iran on social media for doing what he called a "very poor job" of allowing oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump stated that Iran's restrictions violate the terms of their agreement.

stories.title: Israel wants to start peace talks with Lebanon ‘as soon as possible’, says Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel wants to begin peace talks with Lebanon as soon as possible. He indicated the negotiations would include demands for the disarmament of Hezbollah.

stories.title: Video shows explosion over Erbil in suspected drone interception
stories.summary: Video footage captured an explosion in the sky above Erbil in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, in what is suspected to be a drone interception.

stories.title: PML-N lawmaker submits resolution in PA, calls for nominating CDF Munir, PM Shehbaz, DPM Dar for Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: A PML-N lawmaker submitted a resolution in Pakistan's Punjab Assembly calling for the nomination of CDF Asim Munir, PM Shehbaz Sharif, and DPM Ishaq Dar for the Nobel Peace Prize, citing their diplomatic efforts amid Iran-Israel-U.S. tensions.

stories.title: News live: Tony Abbott calls for Australia to join war in Middle East; Queensland MP Jimmy Sullivan found dead
stories.summary: Former Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott called for Australia to join the war in the Middle East in support of allied nations. Separately, the IMF warned that the Iran war would permanently scar the global economy even if a durable peace deal is reached.

stories.title: War update: 134 clashes on frontline, heaviest fighting in Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk sectors
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 134 attacks on Ukrainian defensive positions along the frontline. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors, with increased Russian activity also reported in the Huliaipole sector.

stories.title: Ecuador hikes tariffs to 100-percent in feud with neighbour Colombia
stories.summary: Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa raised tariffs to 100 percent on Colombian imports, accusing Colombian President Gustavo Petro of failing to take effective measures against drug trafficking. The move escalates an ongoing diplomatic feud between the two neighboring South American nations.

stories.title: Trump, Starmer discuss need for 'practical plan' on Hormuz: UK
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and US President Donald Trump discussed the need for a practical plan to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Iran ceasefire. The strait is a critical maritime chokepoint for global oil transit.

stories.title: EU demands explanation from Hungary on alleged information sharing with Russia
stories.summary: The European Union demanded an explanation from Hungary after reports that Foreign Minister Peter Szijjártó shared EU information with Russia. The allegations have heightened tensions between Budapest and Brussels.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires missile at southern city of Ashdod; debris from interception triggers sirens in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired a missile at the southern Israeli city of Ashdod, with debris from its interception triggering sirens in Tel Aviv. No injuries were reported. Separately, Pakistan's defense minister called Israel a "curse for humanity," drawing condemnation from Jerusalem.

stories.title: Israel approves dozens of new settlements in West Bank, watchdog says
stories.summary: An Israeli watchdog group reported that Israel has approved the establishment of dozens of new Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank. The approvals come amid a rise in settler attacks on Palestinians across the territory.

stories.title: Putin announces "Easter ceasefire"
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a temporary ceasefire in the war against Ukraine to coincide with Orthodox Easter celebrations.

stories.title: Uganda: France, EU Commit Shs735bn to Rehabilitate Nalubaale and Kiira Dams
stories.summary: France and the European Union have committed 735 billion Ugandan shillings toward rehabilitating Uganda's Nalubaale and Kiira hydropower dams in Jinja. The investment aims to boost the country's clean energy capacity.

stories.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says ‘we seek compensation, not war’
stories.summary: Iranian state television broadcast a message from new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stating that Iran does not seek war. Khamenei indicated that Tehran is instead pursuing compensation for damages sustained during recent hostilities.

stories.title: Former Iranian foreign minister dies from attack wounds
stories.summary: A former Iranian foreign minister died from wounds sustained during US-Israeli military strikes earlier in the month, according to Iranian media reports. No further details about the individual's identity were provided in the initial report.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel will continue to strike Hezbollah ‘wherever necessary’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared that Israel will continue striking Hezbollah "wherever necessary." The Israeli military confirmed it was conducting ongoing ground operations in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Spreading Islamist insurgency dominates Benin's presidential campaign
stories.summary: Benin's presidential campaign is being dominated by concerns over a spreading Islamist insurgency, with cross-border raids from militant groups increasingly threatening the West African nation's stability.

stories.title: Ceasefire or no ceasefire, the Middle East's reshuffling is not yet done
stories.summary: Despite both Israel and Iran having incentives to end hostilities, analysts note the two sides lack common ground for a lasting resolution. The broader geopolitical reshuffling across the Middle East remains ongoing even as ceasefire discussions continue.

stories.title: Nigerian army general killed in overnight assault on base, military says attack repelled
stories.summary: Islamist militant groups Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province launched coordinated overnight attacks on multiple locations in Borno state, northeastern Nigeria. An army general and several soldiers were killed, though the military said the attacks were ultimately repelled.

stories.title: Rutte names four countries “holding back” Ukraine’s NATO membership
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte publicly identified four countries that are blocking Ukraine's path to NATO membership, though the specific nations were not detailed in the report.

stories.title: Trump weighs pulling some US troops from Europe amid NATO strains, official says
stories.summary: President Trump has discussed with advisers the option of withdrawing some U.S. troops stationed in Europe, according to a senior White House official. The deliberations come amid escalating tensions between Trump and NATO allies.

stories.title: Artemis II crew to return home as Nasa lays out steps for safe splashdown
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew is preparing to return to Earth following a historic 10-day lunar flyby mission. The Orion capsule will re-enter the atmosphere at nearly 24,000 mph before splashing down off the coast of San Diego, California.

stories.title: Greenland prime minister rebuffs Trump remarks as NATO tensions rise
stories.summary: Greenland's prime minister rejected recent remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump, who referred to the territory as a "big, poorly run, piece of ice." The exchange comes amid rising tensions within NATO.

stories.title: A toll for using Hormuz would be a ‘dangerous precedent’, says UN’s shipping agency
stories.summary: The United Nations' International Maritime Organization warned that Iran's proposal to charge a toll for passage through the Strait of Hormuz would set a "dangerous precedent." Iranian officials had raised the toll idea amid the broader ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: Sudan drone strike kills 32, including children, in North Darfur
stories.summary: A drone strike on an RSF-controlled town in Sudan's North Darfur state killed at least 32 civilians, including women and children. The attack targeted the town amid the ongoing armed conflict between the Sudanese military and the Rapid Support Forces.

stories.title: Editor's Notes: Why Americans turned to Al Jazeera instead of CNN or Fox during Iran war - comment
stories.summary: A commentary examines how Al Jazeera became the most-watched English-language news channel covering the Middle East during the Iran war. The piece attributes this shift to Western media outlets reducing their regional coverage, leaving a gap filled by the Qatar-funded network.

stories.title: Top EU diplomat calls for urgent cessation of hostilities in Lebanon
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called for an urgent cessation of hostilities in Lebanon and urged all parties to respect the US-Iran ceasefire agreement. She also demanded full freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz in line with international law.

stories.title: IMF expects to provide vulnerable economies hit by Iran war up to $63 billion
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund announced it expects to provide up to $63 billion to vulnerable economies affected by the Iran war. Low-income energy-importing countries with limited fiscal space have been disproportionately impacted by the crisis.

stories.title: Police in Venezuela block protesters calling for higher wages, pensions
stories.summary: Venezuelan police blocked protesters in demonstrations calling for higher wages and pensions. The protests reflect persistent cost-of-living pressures in Venezuela following the US-led removal of former President Nicolás Maduro in January.

stories.title: With Iran ceasefire set, IDF chief declares Hezbollah main front
stories.summary: Israeli military chief Zamir declared Hezbollah the main front following the US-Iran ceasefire agreement. He stated that Iran is now "much weaker" than before the war, signaling a strategic shift in Israel's military priorities toward Lebanon.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire: Uncertainty over what’s next
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran has paused active hostilities, though significant unresolved issues remain. Analysts note that questions persist regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Israeli strikes in Lebanon, and Iran's remaining military capabilities.

stories.title: US judge rules Pentagon has violated his order in press access case
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Paul Friedman ruled that the Pentagon violated his earlier order by failing to restore press credentials, and he directed the return of passes to seven New York Times reporters. The ruling stems from a lawsuit the Times filed against the Trump administration over restrictive new press access policies.

stories.title: Austria demands Israel stop attacking civilian targets in Lebanon
stories.summary: Austria demanded that Israel cease attacks on civilian targets in Lebanon. Austrian officials also called for the protection of their personnel serving in a United Nations peacekeeping force deployed in the country.

stories.title: US judge orders Pentagon to restore press access to credentialled reporters
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge in Washington ruled that the Pentagon has been defying a court order requiring it to restore press access to credentialled reporters. District Judge Paul Friedman ordered the Department of Defense to comply with his earlier ruling, which sided with The New York Times and other news organizations challenging access restrictions.

stories.title: Judge bars Trump administration from nixing protected status for Ethiopians
stories.summary: A US federal judge blocked the Trump administration from terminating Temporary Protected Status for Ethiopian nationals. The ruling represents a legal setback for the administration's broader efforts to roll back immigration protections for various groups.

stories.title: Liberia: In U.S.$6.2m Corruption Trial
stories.summary: The US$6.2 million corruption trial of former Liberian Finance Minister Samuel D. Tweah Jr. and four other ex-officials entered a tense phase in court. Defense cross-examination of a Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission official exposed disputes over investigative standards and evidence handling.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to truce for Orthodox Easter
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a truce with Ukraine for Orthodox Easter, set to last from Saturday afternoon on April 11 through Easter Sunday. The ceasefire marks a rare pause in hostilities.

stories.title: Attack on Saudi Arabian pipeline wiped out 10 percent of kingdom's oil export capacity
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry detailed the impact of Iranian strikes on the kingdom's oil infrastructure, reporting that a pipeline attack eliminated 10 percent of its oil export capacity. The statement described multiple targets hit during the conflict.

stories.title: A new US anti-Zionist PAC endorses candidates who believe Jews were behind 9/11
stories.summary: A newly founded US political action committee called AZAPAC has endorsed candidates who promote the conspiracy theory that Jews were responsible for the September 11 attacks. The PAC was founded by a self-described libertarian who has referred to Israel as the "synagogue of Satan."

stories.title: Russia adds 2 suspects in killing of Chechen woman to federal wanted list
stories.summary: Russia's Interior Ministry added Karina Iminova and Said-Khamzat Baisarov to its federal wanted list in connection with the killing of Aishat Baimuradova, a woman from Chechnya, according to the SK SOS Crisis Group.

stories.title: At Beirut hospital, grieving families identify mangled bodies after Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Grieving families gathered at a Beirut hospital to identify victims following Israeli strikes across Lebanon on April 8. More than 250 people were killed in the bombardment.

stories.title: In ‘Yes!,’ Israeli director Nadav Lapid skewers the country’s ‘moral abyss’ after Oct. 7
stories.summary: Israeli director Nadav Lapid's film "Yes!" has entered limited US theatrical release nearly a year after premiering at the Cannes Film Festival. The film is sharply critical of Israel's conduct after October 7, though it has also faced boycotts from pro-Palestinian activists.

stories.title: Russia declares federal emergency in 2 regions amid severe flooding
stories.summary: Russian Emergency Situations Minister Alexander Kurenkov declared a federal state of emergency in Dagestan and Chechnya on April 9 following severe flooding in both regions.

stories.title: Ukrainian border guards wipe out Russian infantry in Belgorod direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian border guards from the Strix unmanned systems unit destroyed Russian infantry forces in the Belgorod direction and struck a mobile Russian fire group along with its crew using drone systems.

stories.title: Melania says her piece about Epstein – doth the lady protest too much?
stories.summary: First Lady Melania Trump made a public appearance at the White House to deny any relationship with Jeffrey Epstein, putting one of President Trump's political liabilities back in the spotlight amid the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: Germany's Merz: we do not want NATO to split over U.S.-Iran war
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated he does not want NATO to split over the U.S.-Iran war. He downplayed reported threats by U.S. President Donald Trump to withdraw troops from NATO countries perceived as not contributing sufficiently to the alliance.

stories.title: Reservist rabbi who called to ‘flatten’ Gaza will be honored at state Independence Day event
stories.summary: Israel plans to honor reservist rabbi and rabbinic judge Avraham Zarbiv, who previously called to "flatten" Gaza, at an official Independence Day ceremony. Zarbiv, also a bulldozer operator, was selected alongside other figures including an amputee soldier and Argentina's president.

stories.title: Netanyahu authorises direct talks with Lebanon 'as soon as possible'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu authorized direct talks with Lebanon as soon as possible, as Beirut advocated for a temporary ceasefire. U.S. Vice President Vance was set to lead negotiations in Islamabad.

stories.title: Lebanon’s hospitals may run out of vital medical supplies within days, says WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned that Lebanon's hospitals may run out of vital medical supplies within days. Israel continued bombing targets in Lebanon on April 9, compounding the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Putin orders Easter ceasefire, calls on Ukraine to follow
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared an Easter ceasefire from 4:00 p.m. on April 11 through the end of April 12 and called on Ukraine to reciprocate, the Kremlin announced on April 9.

stories.title: Russia’s Justice Ministry identifies 196 active members of Memorial movement, now banned as ‘extremist’
stories.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry identified at least 196 people as active members of the International Memorial movement, which Russia's Supreme Court has designated an extremist organization.

stories.title: Russian Orthodox patriarch opens Easter-week sermon by congratulating worshippers on January holiday; Patriarchate scrubs the error
stories.summary: Russian Orthodox Patriarch Kirill mistakenly opened his Holy Thursday sermon on April 9 by congratulating worshippers on Epiphany, a January holiday. The Patriarchate subsequently removed the error, as reported by journalist Ksenia Luchenko.

stories.title: Hot in the city: Energy crisis tests Singapore's air-con addiction
stories.summary: Rising energy prices, driven partly by heavy reliance on Gulf oil, are acutely affecting Asian nations. Singapore faces particular strain as the crisis tests the city-state's dependence on energy-intensive air conditioning.

stories.title: Democrats in US slam Pam Bondi for refusing to appear for Epstein hearing
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers criticized former Attorney General Pam Bondi for refusing to appear at a congressional hearing related to Jeffrey Epstein. The lawmakers warned that a congressional subpoena compelling her testimony remains in effect.

stories.title: Will Netanyahu Derail the Iran War Cease-Fire?
stories.summary: Israel's continued military offensive in Lebanon is threatening the fragile ceasefire in the broader Iran conflict, raising questions about whether Prime Minister Netanyahu's actions could derail the truce.

stories.title: Will Trump’s Iran war ‘loyalty test’ spell the end of Nato?
stories.summary: A Chinese analyst suggested the U.S.-Israel war on Iran could reduce NATO to a largely nominal alliance, though an outright dissolution remains unlikely. President Trump has intensified criticism of NATO allies, accusing them of free-riding on American security commitments.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strike on oil pumping station in Russia’s Krasnodar Krai
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck the Krymskaya oil pumping station in Russia's Krasnodar Krai on the night of April 9, according to Ukraine's General Staff.

stories.title: Starmer and Trump discuss need for opening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and US President Donald Trump discussed the need for a practical plan to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Iran ceasefire. The UK is working to convene partners to agree on restoring freedom of navigation in the waterway.

stories.title: US military bases in Gulf 'useless' after Iranian strikes, experts say
stories.summary: Middle East experts argued that at least a dozen US military bases across the Gulf region have been so severely damaged by Iranian retaliatory strikes that they now pose more vulnerabilities than strategic benefits. The New York Times previously described the bases as "all but uninhabitable."

stories.title: Putin signs law criminalizing denial of Nazi genocide of Soviet people during World War II
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin signed a law making it a criminal offense to deny or approve what Russia describes as the Nazi genocide of the Soviet people during World War II, or to insult the memory of its victims.

stories.title: Partial easing of U.S. sanctions fails to boost Russia’s oil shipments – intel
stories.summary: Despite a temporary easing of U.S. sanctions, Russia was unable to increase oil shipments through its seaports in March 2026, according to intelligence reports.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1506: Russia races to triple drone army as Ukraine strikes oil artery feeding Black Sea port
stories.summary: On day 1,506 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia is racing to field 165,000 drone operators by year's end, according to Ukraine's commander-in-chief. Ukrainian forces struck the Krymskaya oil station and destroyed a ninth Russian Tor-M1 air defense system in nine days, while President Zelenskyy accused Washington of ignoring evidence that Moscow shared US base coordinates with Iran.

stories.title: Law enforcement officer carried unconscious from Novaya Gazeta newsroom during search
stories.summary: Masked law enforcement officers conducted searches at the Moscow newsroom of Novaya Gazeta, during which a man was carried out unconscious, according to RTVI and the Telegram channel Ostorozhno Novosti.

stories.title: Hospitals in Beirut struggle to deal with casualties after Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Hospitals in Beirut are struggling to treat a surge of casualties resulting from Israeli military attacks on the city and surrounding areas. Doctors have warned of a worsening humanitarian crisis as vital medical supplies run critically low.

stories.title: Chilean Air Force conducts first-ever aerial refueling of US F-35 fighters
stories.summary: The Chilean Air Force completed its first-ever aerial refueling of two U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II fighters. The operation marks a milestone in military interoperability between Chile and the United States.

stories.title: CAF President Motsepe rejects Senegal’s corruption claim amid AFCON fallout
stories.summary: Confederation of African Football President Patrice Motsepe rejected corruption allegations made by Senegal's government. The accusations followed a dispute over the awarding of the Africa Cup of Nations title to Morocco.

stories.title: ‘Nothing short of horrific’: World reacts to Israeli ‘carnage’ in Lebanon
stories.summary: Global leaders reacted with condemnation after Israel launched its heaviest air assault on Lebanon since the conflict with Hezbollah began on March 2, killing more than 250 people. The strikes came hours after a U.S.-Iran truce brokered through Pakistani diplomatic efforts, even as Hezbollah had paused its own attacks.

stories.title: NATO’s Rutte told allies Trump wants Hormuz commitments within days, diplomats say
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte informed allies that U.S. President Donald Trump wants commitments regarding the Strait of Hormuz within days, according to diplomats. Rutte met with Trump on April 8 amid growing tensions within the alliance over the Iran war.

stories.title: Middle East crisis is pushing China to deepen Latin America ties
stories.summary: The war in Iran and resulting disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and global energy markets are pushing China to deepen strategic ties with Latin America, as Beijing seeks to diversify its supply routes and reduce dependence on unstable regions.

stories.title: Afrika Bambaataa, hip-hop pioneer, dies aged 67
stories.summary: Afrika Bambaataa, the Bronx-born rapper, DJ, and founder of the Universal Zulu Nation who helped bring hip-hop to the mainstream, died at age 67 in Philadelphia from complications related to cancer.

stories.title: Worried by hits on Iran nuclear sites, must never happen again: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, who is running for UN Secretary General, expressed concern about strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, saying such attacks must never happen again. He acknowledged that war has returned to multiple parts of the world.

stories.title: Zelensky warns: Leaving Donbas would open door to Russian assault on Kharkiv, Dnipro
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that withdrawing from the Donetsk region would not constitute a compromise and could enable Russia to launch assaults on Kharkiv and Dnipro.

stories.title: Democrats ramp up calls to remove Trump over his Iran threats
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers intensified calls to remove President Trump from office following his threats to destroy Iran, marking a shift from the restraint Democrats had previously exercised regarding discussions of presidential removal.

stories.title: Rafah crossing restrictions derail Palestinian student’s academic dreams
stories.summary: A Palestinian medical student's academic aspirations have been disrupted by restrictions at the Rafah border crossing linked to the ongoing war in Gaza. The closure has prevented students from accessing educational opportunities outside the territory.

stories.title: Italy pledges emergency funds to reopen rail, motorway after landslide on key Adriatic corridor
stories.summary: Italy declared a state of emergency and pledged millions in funding after a major landslide severed rail and motorway links along a key north-south Adriatic transport corridor. The government moved quickly to limit disruption and begin restoration efforts.

stories.title: Trump again chides NATO for failing to back US operations in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump again criticized NATO for failing to support U.S. military operations in Iran. His remarks followed a tense private meeting at the White House with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

stories.title: 'Iran will not forfeit its rights': Statement attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei read on state TV
stories.summary: A statement attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei was read on Iranian state television declaring that Iran will not forfeit its rights, is not seeking war, and considers all resistance fronts a unified entity.

stories.title: Will ASEAN Welcome Myanmar Back Into Its Fold?
stories.summary: The official appointment of Myanmar coup leader Min Aung Hlaing as president is expected to prompt debate within ASEAN about whether to re-engage with Myanmar's military government.

stories.title: Hourly power outage schedules to be in effect in all regions on Friday
stories.summary: Scheduled hourly electricity outages will be imposed across all regions of Ukraine on Friday, April 10, affecting all categories of consumers throughout the entire day.

stories.title: IMF expects to provide vulnerable economies hit by Middle East war up to $50 billion
stories.summary: The IMF announced it may need to provide between $20 billion and $50 billion in immediate financial assistance to countries economically affected by the Middle East war. Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva cited spillover effects including food insecurity from disrupted transport and supply chains.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. military to stay deployed near Iran until 'real agreement' reached
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that American military forces would remain deployed near Iran until a 'real agreement' is reached, adding that the military was preparing for potential further action.

stories.title: US to host Israel-Lebanon meeting to discuss ceasefire talks
stories.summary: The US State Department announced it will host a meeting next week between Israeli and Lebanese officials to discuss ongoing ceasefire negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Netanyahu: ‘No ceasefire in Lebanon’, Israel open to peace talks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that no ceasefire is in effect in Lebanon, while indicating Israel remains open to peace negotiations. The declaration comes amid continued Israeli military operations in Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Netanyahu corruption trial to resume on Sunday after Israel eases war restrictions
stories.summary: The Jerusalem District Court confirmed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial will resume on Sunday, after emergency wartime restrictions imposed during the conflict with Iran were lifted. A defense witness is expected to testify at the hearing.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir discuss Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir discussed Pakistan's mediation efforts between the United States and Iran. Both expressed satisfaction with de-escalation achieved so far and urged all parties to maintain peace and a ceasefire.

stories.title: Update from the Battlefield: Drones, Distance, and Diminishing Returns for Russia
stories.summary: Analyst Michael Kofman discusses the current state of the Russia-Ukraine war following a recent frontline visit. The conversation covers how drone warfare has created a dispersed kill zone, why Russian infiltration tactics have yielded limited gains, and how the war in Iran is beginning to influence the conflict.

stories.title: Update from the Battlefield: Drones, Distance, and Diminishing Returns for Russia
stories.summary: Analyst Michael Kofman discussed the evolving state of the Russia-Ukraine war, noting how drone warfare has transformed frontline combat into a dispersed contest. He also examined how Russian infiltration tactics are yielding diminishing returns and how the Iran war is beginning to influence the conflict.

stories.title: Gaza journalists mourn Al Jazeera’s Wishah, killed by Israel
stories.summary: Al Jazeera journalist Wishah was killed by Israeli forces in Gaza, prompting mourning among fellow journalists. Wishah is the latest in a series of Al Jazeera reporters killed in Gaza since the war began in October 2023.

stories.title: Hamas not expected to okay disarmament offer by Saturday deadline, but talks ongoing
stories.summary: Hamas is not expected to accept a disarmament proposal by the Saturday deadline set by the Board of Peace, though negotiations continue. Sources involved in the talks say progress is being made and a response could come shortly after the deadline passes.

stories.title: Red Cross 'outraged' by 'death and destruction' in Lebanon
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross expressed outrage at the widespread death and destruction across Lebanon on Wednesday as Israel carried out a massive wave of airstrikes throughout the country.

stories.title: Rutte Defends NATO’s Iran War Response Amid Trump’s Ire
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte publicly defended the alliance's response to the Iran war following a tense White House meeting with President Trump, who has criticized NATO allies over their lack of support for U.S. operations.

stories.title: Russian troops attack Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 60 times since morning, leaving two injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 60 attacks on the Nikopol, Synelnykove, and Pavlohrad districts of Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring two people.

stories.title: Ukraine hits oil-pumping station on route to Russia’s biggest Black Sea export port, triggering fire
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Krymskaya oil-pumping station, which supplies crude to Russia's largest Black Sea export port at Novorossiysk, triggering a fire at the facility.

stories.title: Ukraine: Russia's Putin declares Easter ceasefire
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared an Easter ceasefire in the war against Ukraine during the Orthodox holiday period. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy responded that Ukraine would "act accordingly" during the announced truce.

stories.title: British man appears in court charged with being member of al Shabaab
stories.summary: A British man appeared in a London court charged with membership in al-Shabaab, the Somali militant group. He is accused of having trained and fought as a commando with the organization in Somalia more than 15 years ago.

stories.title: Vladimir Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire with Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared a 32-hour ceasefire in Ukraine for the Orthodox Easter weekend, ordering forces to halt from Saturday afternoon through Sunday. The announcement followed an earlier call from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for a pause in fighting.

stories.title: Inside America: How Iran’s regime built a decades-long influence network inside the United States
stories.summary: An investigation detailed how the Islamic Republic of Iran has spent 47 years building a network of institutions inside the United States designed to shape policy influence in Washington aligned with the regime's interests.

stories.title: Nigeria begins trial of 500 terrorism suspects
stories.summary: Nigeria has begun mass terrorism trials of approximately 500 suspects across 13 courtrooms in Abuja under heavy security, amid a surge of violence across the country.

stories.title: Ex-CENTCOM Chief: IRGC running Iran can make concessions without regime change - interview
stories.summary: Former US CENTCOM Commander General Kenneth McKenzie discussed the Iran conflict in an interview, suggesting that an IRGC-led Iranian government could potentially make concessions without requiring full regime change.

stories.title: Khamenei says Tehran ‘astonished the world’ during US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: In a televised statement, Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Tehran "astonished the world" during the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Khamenei declared that Iran will demand compensation for damages inflicted during the conflict.

stories.title: Budanov confirms that partners asked Ukraine not to strike Russian oil terminals
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov confirmed that international partners had asked Ukraine not to strike Russian oil terminals. Budanov stated that Ukraine has its own national interests to consider.

stories.title: Iran: Strait of Hormuz open with restrictions
stories.summary: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister announced that the Strait of Hormuz remains open but with restrictions, requiring ships to coordinate passage with Iranian naval forces. The waterway is a critical global shipping route for oil exports.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says operational activities halted at several energy sites
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia announced that operational activities have been halted at several energy sites following attacks on its facilities. A Saudi official told the state news agency that the strikes have reduced supply and slowed recovery efforts.

stories.title: Russia hands Ukraine 1,000 war dead
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged the bodies of deceased soldiers on Thursday. Russia returned 1,000 war dead to Ukraine as part of the exchange process.

stories.title: Masked security agents raid Russian newspaper in Moscow and arrest journalist
stories.summary: Masked security agents raided the Moscow offices of Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's leading independent newspapers. Russian state media reported that a prominent journalist was arrested during the operation.

stories.title: Israel to hold direct talks with Lebanon, Netanyahu says
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israel would hold direct talks with Lebanon, following a wave of Israeli airstrikes on Wednesday that killed 303 people across Lebanon, according to Lebanese health officials.

stories.title: What just happened? Breaking down the ceasefire
stories.summary: The United States and Iran reached a ceasefire agreement after weeks of escalating tensions, though analysts question whether the deal represents genuine de-escalation or merely a temporary pause in hostilities.

stories.title: High fuel prices spur interest in EVs
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs driven by the war in Iran are increasing consumer interest in electric vehicles, as observed at the New York Auto Show. Meanwhile, financial markets saw a relief rally lose momentum as a fragile Iran ceasefire entered its second day.

stories.title: Halt to Iran attacks means Netanyahu’s corruption trial will resume on April 12
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial is set to resume on April 12 following a halt to Iran-related hostilities. Netanyahu denies charges of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust that were filed in 2019.

stories.title: Russian special envoy in US to meet Trump administration officials
stories.summary: Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev is in the United States meeting Trump administration officials to discuss a Ukraine peace deal and U.S.-Russia economic cooperation. The visit coincides with an upcoming decision on whether to extend sanctions relief on Russian oil, expiring April 11.

stories.title: Russian shelling damages fire station in Donetsk region
stories.summary: A fire and rescue station in Mykolaivka, Donetsk region, was damaged by Russian shelling.

stories.title: Watch: Dramatic visuals of high-speed car chase in California
stories.summary: A high-speed police chase in Southern California ended when sheriff's deputies used a 'grappler' device, causing the vehicle to crash into a home in Jurupa Valley. The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene.

stories.title: Erdogan tells Iran president talks should aim for lasting peace
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in a phone call to use upcoming Pakistan-brokered talks between Iran and the US to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region.

stories.title: Explainer: Can the US and Iran bridge their differences in talks?
stories.summary: The United States and Iran remain deeply divided on key issues as they consider potential negotiations. Significant gaps persist between the two sides on matters central to any comprehensive agreement.

stories.title: Sindh govt constitutes high-level committee to ‘ensure execution’ of Gul Plaza inferno’s inquiry report
stories.summary: The Sindh government in Pakistan formed a high-level committee to implement the findings of an inquiry report into the Gul Plaza fire in January, which killed more than 70 people. The blaze took nearly two days to extinguish and partially collapsed the building.

stories.title: Russia returns bodies of 1,000 soldiers to Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged the bodies of fallen soldiers, with Red Cross observers present to oversee the transfer. Russia returned 1,000 deceased soldiers to Ukraine as part of the repatriation process.

stories.title: Poll finds 60% of Americans have unfavorable view of Israel, up sharply since 2022
stories.summary: A Pew Research Center poll found that 60 percent of Americans now hold an unfavorable view of Israel, a sharp increase since 2022, while 56 percent of US Jews expressed little or no confidence in Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Israel to reopen Karish offshore platform following ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel instructed energy company Energean to resume operations at the Karish offshore natural gas platform in the eastern Mediterranean following the ceasefire agreement with Iran.

stories.title: Judge says ‘No case, no ruling’ in Credit Suisse – Simon Wiesenthal Center settlement dispute
stories.summary: A judge declined to issue a ruling in a dispute between Credit Suisse and the Simon Wiesenthal Center related to a 1990s settlement over Holocaust victims' assets held by Swiss banks and their predecessor institutions.

stories.title: Strikes on Russian oil terminals strengthen Ukraine's position in negotiations – Budanov
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov said that strikes on Russian oil terminals strengthen Ukraine's negotiating position and predicted that Russia would present significant new proposals at the next round of talks.

stories.title: IDF tells Knesset panel new Iranian regime even more extreme
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces briefed a Knesset panel that Iran's new leadership, dominated by Revolutionary Guards figures, is more extreme than its predecessor, while officials indicated fighting with Iran could soon resume.

stories.title: Melania Trump says she did not have relationship with Jeffrey Epstein
stories.summary: First Lady Melania Trump publicly denied having had a relationship with the late Jeffrey Epstein or his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell. She delivered the statement at the White House and called on Congress to hold a hearing with survivors of Epstein's abuse.

stories.title: Pakistan bridging proposal salvaged Iran talks before US deadline expired — officials
stories.summary: Officials revealed that a Pakistani bridging proposal salvaged US-Iran talks before a US deadline expired, with sources indicating both Trump's urgency for a deal and Iran's acceptance of a proposal different from the one it publicly released.

stories.title: US defense official overseeing AI reaped millions selling xAI stock after Pentagon entered agreement with company
stories.summary: Pentagon official Emil Michael, who oversees the Defense Department's AI efforts, earned up to $24 million from selling stock in Elon Musk's xAI company after the Pentagon entered an agreement with the firm. Ethics experts say federal law prohibits officials from taking actions that benefit their own financial interests.

stories.title: Israel army warns that Hezbollah may expand fire 'in the coming hours'
stories.summary: The Israeli military warned citizens that Hezbollah projectile launches, typically confined to northern border areas near Lebanon, could expand to other parts of Israel in the coming hours, urging public vigilance.

stories.title: Lebanon seeks Pakistan’s support for ending Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam called Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to request Pakistan's support in ending Israeli strikes on Lebanon. PM Shehbaz condemned Israel's ongoing aggression and expressed condolences over the thousands of lives lost.

stories.title: Iranians pay tribute to slain supreme leader weeks after killing
stories.summary: Thousands of Iranians rallied on Thursday to pay tribute to slain Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei weeks after his killing, with many expressing criticism of the upcoming US-Iran peace talks expected to take place in Pakistan.

stories.title: US has let in 4,499 refugees since October - all but three were South African
stories.summary: Since October, the United States has admitted 4,499 refugees, nearly all of whom were South African. The Trump administration has prioritized Afrikaners, a white minority group it claims faces persecution; South Africa has disputed that characterization.

stories.title: Brazil on track to fill China beef export quota by May as prices hit all-time high
stories.summary: Brazil is on track to exhaust its annual beef export quota to China by early May. Cattle prices hit a nominal record of R$365 per arroba, rising 12.5% over the past year, as Beijing's import restrictions pushed South American exporters to seek alternative markets.

stories.title: IMF chief warns that Iran war will slow global economic growth
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director warned that the war on Iran is darkening the global economic outlook, regardless of whether a fragile ceasefire holds.

stories.title: Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire in Ukraine after Kyiv proposes same
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a ceasefire in Ukraine for the Orthodox Easter weekend, following a similar proposal from Kyiv for a pause in hostilities.

stories.title: High Commissioner Vikram Doraiswami awarded Freedom of the City of London
stories.summary: India's High Commissioner to the U.K., Vikram Doraiswami, was awarded the Freedom of the City of London. He described his time in London as transformative for bilateral relations, including the conclusion of the India-U.K. Free Trade Agreement.

stories.title: German leader says he does not want Nato to 'split' over war on Iran
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed concern about NATO unity fracturing over the war on Iran, amid reports that the US could penalize alliance members that did not assist and reward those that did.

stories.title: Due to blocking of European funds, we carry out preparations for next winter using internal resources – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Ukraine is preparing for the next winter heating season using only domestic resources because European funding has been blocked. The lack of access to European funds has forced reliance on internal capacities.

stories.title: Why is Hezbollah a sticking point in the Iran ceasefire?
stories.summary: Hezbollah, the Lebanese armed group allied with Tehran, remains a central obstacle in ceasefire negotiations between the US and Iran, as Israel continues to carry out military operations against the group.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills girl student in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed a young female student while she attended a class held in a tent in Beit Lahiya, northern Gaza Strip, according to Palestinian health and education officials on April 9.

stories.title: Ukraine and Syria tighten relations
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Syria in a move described as strategically motivated by considerations regarding Russia, which was previously a key supporter of the Syrian state.

stories.title: Israel's Deadly Ceasefire in Lebanon
stories.summary: Despite a ceasefire announcement between the US and Iran, Israeli bombing continues in Lebanon, and prospects for the disarmament of Hezbollah remain distant.

stories.title: Israel says peace talks with Lebanon to begin ASAP, rejects calls for truce first
stories.summary: Israel announced that peace talks with Lebanon would begin as soon as possible, with Prime Minister Netanyahu saying disarming Hezbollah would be the focus, while rejecting international calls for a truce before negotiations start.

stories.title: UK says it deployed military to deter Russian submarines from attack on undersea cables
stories.summary: The United Kingdom said it deployed Royal Navy assets to deter Russian submarines from attacking undersea cables. British officials stated Russia was exploiting the distraction of the Middle East crisis to conduct covert operations.

stories.title: Iran rules out restrictions on enrichment programme: nuclear energy chief
stories.summary: Iran's nuclear energy chief Mohammad Eslami stated that Iran will not accept restrictions on its uranium enrichment programme, asserting that enemies' efforts, including the recent war, have failed to force concessions.

stories.title: We prepare drafts of new defense agreements with Middle Eastern countries – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that Ukraine is preparing drafts of new defense cooperation agreements with countries neighboring Iran in the Middle East. Details of the specific countries and agreement terms were not disclosed.

stories.title: Scale of Beirut destruction revealed after wave of Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Satellite and ground-level imagery revealed extensive destruction across Beirut following Israel's large-scale airstrikes on Tuesday, with the full scope of damage becoming visible as smoke cleared from affected neighborhoods.

stories.title: Hezbollah lawmaker says group rejects direct talks between Lebanon and Israel: Report
stories.summary: Hezbollah lawmaker Ali Fayyad reiterated the group's rejection of any direct negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, responding to Netanyahu's announcement that he had ordered his cabinet to begin talks with Beirut.

stories.title: Russia brands Nobel-winning rights group Memorial an extremist movement
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court designated the Nobel Peace Prize-winning human rights group Memorial as an "extremist" movement. Memorial said the ruling marked a new phase of state oppression in Russia.

stories.title: Iran says it ‘would be dumb’ for US to let Netanyahu kill diplomacy
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned the United States against allowing Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to undermine diplomatic efforts, responding implicitly to US Vice President JD Vance's remarks regarding Israel's attacks on Lebanon.

stories.title: On the Radar: Do Crackdowns Work?
stories.summary: InSight Crime's weekly roundup reports that a co-founder of Mexico's CJNG cartel pleaded guilty, Ecuador sought European assistance to combat crime, and US strikes targeted trafficking routes, though the cocaine trade continues to adapt.

stories.title: At least 4 dead, 38 rescued during attempted channel crossing from France to U.K.
stories.summary: At least four migrants died and 38 were rescued during an attempted English Channel crossing from France to the United Kingdom. The migrants were swept away by dangerous currents while trying to board a 'taxi-boat.'

stories.title: UK Defense Ministry says 3 Russian submarines conducted suspicious activity near undersea cables in North Atlantic
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence reported that three Russian submarines were detected conducting suspicious activity near critical undersea cable infrastructure in the northern Atlantic Ocean.

stories.title: ‘I live alone and I can’t run’: Elderly from the north turn social welfare hot potato
stories.summary: The Tzalir Fund evacuated approximately 1,200 elderly residents from northern Israel's frontline communities, housing them in five hotels, but its funding is set to expire on April 15, raising concerns about continued care.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon to begin direct talks on Hezbollah disarmament and peace, Netanyahu declares
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israel and Lebanon will begin direct negotiations focused on Hezbollah's disarmament and establishing peaceful relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran’s Hormuz tolls would set a dangerous precedent, says global shipping watchdog
stories.summary: Iran's proposal to charge tolls for passage through the Strait of Hormuz has drawn criticism from global shipping authorities, who called it a dangerous precedent.
