Iranian control over the strait was reportedly one of Tehran's conditions during ceasefire negotiations with the United States.

stories.title: Israel to ramp up production of Arrow interceptors
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to increase production of its Arrow interceptor missile system. The decision preceded a US-Iran ceasefire that has proven fragile and did not prevent Israel from continuing to strike targets in Lebanon.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks civilian car in Ruska Lozova, killing one person
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a civilian vehicle in Ruska Lozova in the Kharkiv district on April 9, killing one man. The attack targeted a car in the settlement.

stories.title: ‘Forgetting the people’: Iranians fear regime will become more brutal after ceasefire
stories.summary: Kurdish Iranian opposition figure Kako Aliyar warned that a premature end to the war could embolden Iranian authorities to become more repressive domestically. Many Iranians fear the regime will intensify crackdowns following the ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran war doubles Russia’s main oil revenue to $11.5 billion in April, Reuters calculations show
stories.summary: Russia's oil revenue roughly doubled to $11.5 billion in April, according to Reuters calculations, as the Iran war disrupted global energy markets. The Kremlin stated that demand for Russian energy remains high amid the ongoing crisis.

stories.title: Sidelined by Trump’s truce with Iran, Israel pummels Lebanon – then agrees to talks
stories.summary: Following the US-Iran ceasefire that sidelined Israel's broader war goals, Israeli forces escalated attacks on Lebanon before agreeing to US-brokered peace talks. Critics of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have called the situation a strategic failure that has weakened Israel's position with Washington.

stories.title: Iranians rally nationwide to honour late leader Ali Khamenei
stories.summary: Thousands of Iranians gathered in cities across the country to honor the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, whose assassination reportedly marked the beginning of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Nadra warns of penalties for those who delay obtaining, renewing identity documents
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) warned citizens of additional fees and penalties for delaying the obtaining or renewal of identity documents, noting that essential services linked to CNICs could be disrupted.

stories.title: Russia criminalises denial of ‘Soviet genocide’ by Nazis during World War II
stories.summary: Russia formally designated Nazi crimes against the Soviet population during World War II as genocide and criminalized their denial after President Putin signed amendments to the criminal code. Authorities have also proposed converting a former Gulag museum into one focused on Nazi crime victims.

stories.title: War update: 64 clashes on front line since morning, heaviest fighting continues in Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 64 Russian attacks on their positions since the morning along the front line. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions, with increased Russian activity also noted in the Huliaipole direction.

stories.title: UK says three Russian submarines tracked during ‘covert’ operation
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence disclosed that the Royal Navy tracked three Russian submarines during a covert operation near British waters but found no evidence that Russia had damaged undersea infrastructure.

stories.title: Who profits off Iran war? Strait of Hormuz toll talk fuels outrage
stories.summary: The White House issued contradictory statements within the same press conference regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz, first celebrating its reopening and then calling on Iran to reopen it. The confusion reflects five weeks of unclear messaging about the ceasefire deal's actual terms.

stories.title: Zohran Mamdani on 100 days as New York mayor
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani reflected on his first 100 days in office, discussing priorities including childcare, housing, combating bigotry, the Iran conflict, and the future direction of the Democratic Party.

stories.title: Artemis II moon mission unifies politically divided Americans in wonder
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission, the first crewed lunar voyage in over 50 years, has generated widespread public enthusiasm across the United States. The mission has drawn attention from Americans across political divides, providing a moment of shared national pride.

stories.title: Thousands of Iranians rally in memory of late supreme leader Khamenei
stories.summary: Thousands of Iranians rallied to commemorate the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. A state funeral has not yet been held due to the ongoing Middle East conflict.

stories.title: EU police smash ring smuggling Vietnamese to Europe
stories.summary: European law enforcement dismantled a smuggling ring that transported Vietnamese nationals to Europe. The network handed migrants to a Kurdish-Iraqi group that arranged their passage to Britain via small boats.

stories.title: China denies reports of support to Iran's military during war with U.S.
stories.summary: China's Defence Ministry denied reports that Beijing provided military support to Iran during its conflict with the United States. Spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang stated that China has maintained an objective and impartial stance on the Iran issue.

stories.title: UK accuses Russia of covert submarine operation threatening undersea cables
stories.summary: The UK accused Russia of conducting a covert submarine operation that threatened undersea cables, involving an Akula-class submarine and two GUGI surveillance submarines. British Defence Secretary John Healey said allied forces tracked the deployment across every mile of its route.

stories.title: Texas Democrat Talarico faces tough test with Black voters in Senate race
stories.summary: Texas state Representative James Talarico won the Democratic nomination for US Senate with support from white college-educated Democrats and Latino voters. His prospects in the November general election may depend on gaining stronger support from Black voters.

stories.title: Wednesday death toll from Israeli attacks in Lebanon rises to 303
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that the death toll from Israeli attacks across Lebanon on Wednesday rose to 303, following a massive wave of strikes throughout the country.

stories.title: A man with conviction: Boy George posts support for Israel on X
stories.summary: British musician Boy George posted messages of support for Israel on the social media platform X. He also recently defended singer Lady Gaga after a clip surfaced of her expressing love for Israel during a concert.

stories.title: Expert warns Orbán may resort to provocations to hold power in Hungary election
stories.summary: An expert warned that Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán may resort to provocations, declare a state of emergency, or engage in electoral fraud to retain power ahead of upcoming elections in Hungary.

stories.title: Continued IDF ops. in Lebanon will ruin Iran peace talks in Islamabad, Iranian officials claim
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister Saeed Khatibzadeh warned that continued IDF operations in Lebanon could undermine Iran peace talks in Islamabad. He also stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open to civilian ships that coordinate with Iranian authorities.

stories.title: Over 1 million Sudanese refugees in Chad face drastic aid cuts, UN says
stories.summary: The UN warned that over one million Sudanese refugees in Chad face drastic cuts to life-saving aid, including food and water. Two UN agencies stated that donors need to fill a funding shortfall exceeding $400 million.

stories.title: Navy selects Leidos, Defense Unicorns to test software prototypes for ships
stories.summary: The US Navy selected Leidos and Defense Unicorns to test software prototypes for ships under an other transaction agreement. The companies will conduct testing in a lab-based environment.

stories.title: Wild chimpanzees recorded waging ‘civil war’ with coordinated attacks between two groups
stories.summary: A study documented what researchers describe as the first observed instance of a unified chimpanzee community turning on itself, with coordinated attacks between two factions of the Ngogo group in Uganda's Kibale National Park, first noticed by primatologist Aaron Sandel in 2015.

stories.title: Nearly 30,000 property damage claims filed since start of Operation Roaring Lion
stories.summary: Nearly 30,000 property damage claims have been filed since the start of Israel's Operation Roaring Lion. The Israeli Tax Authority reported that 65 compensation teams are operating nationwide to assist civilians whose homes and property were damaged.

stories.title: UK should bin Israel trade deal, impose sanctions: Polanski
stories.summary: UK Green Party Leader Zack Polanski called on the British government to cancel its trade agreement with Israel and impose sanctions following Israeli attacks on Lebanon that killed hundreds.

stories.title: British Navy Says It Tracked Russian Submarines Surveying Undersea Cables in North Atlantic
stories.summary: British Defence Secretary John Healey said the Royal Navy tracked Russian submarines surveying undersea cables in the North Atlantic over a period lasting more than a month.

stories.title: JD Vance under scrutiny after Pentagon summons Vatican envoy
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance faced scrutiny after reports emerged that a Pentagon official summoned a Vatican envoy, reportedly warning that the US could act freely and urging support for Pope Leo.

stories.title: Kremlin says Russia has right to defend itself from 'piracy' after report of warship escort near UK
stories.summary: The Kremlin asserted Russia's right to defend itself from what it called piracy after reports that a Russian navy frigate escorted UK-sanctioned tankers through the English Channel. The statement came in response to a report by Britain's Telegraph newspaper.

stories.title: India election roll overhaul sparks anger as key states vote
stories.summary: India's election commission faces criticism over a Special Intensive Revision drive that removed millions of voters from electoral rolls in several states. Opposition leaders allege the overhaul disproportionately affects marginalized and minority communities and have threatened legal action.

stories.title: Zelensky comments on Vance’s statement about “haggling over a few square kilometers”
stories.summary: President Zelensky responded to U.S. Vice President JD Vance's remarks about "haggling over a few square kilometers," stating that Vance is not directly participating in negotiations between Ukraine, the United States, and Russia.

stories.title: Lebanon seeks ceasefire before talks with Israel: Report
stories.summary: A Lebanese official told AFP that Lebanon is seeking a ceasefire with Israel before beginning peace talks. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said he instructed officials to begin negotiations with Lebanon, including the disarmament of Hezbollah.

stories.title: Trump’s Recipe for Accelerated U.S. Decline
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the combination of erratic US militarism and increased defense spending under the Trump administration risks accelerating America's long-term strategic decline.

stories.title: Trump blasts NATO after closed-door Rutte meeting
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump publicly criticized NATO following a closed-door meeting with Secretary General Mark Rutte. Trump revived previous remarks about Greenland and raised questions about the United States' ongoing commitment to the alliance.

stories.title: The Iran war balance sheet: wins, losses, and undecideds - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis assessed the strategic wins and losses for both Israel and Iran during their recent conflict. The piece noted that while the outcome remains unclear, a definitive winner is expected to emerge over time.

stories.title: Trump’s tariff threat on European cars escalates global trade tensions
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to impose a 20% tariff on all cars imported from the European Union unless the bloc removes its tariffs and trade barriers on U.S. goods, further escalating global trade tensions.

stories.title: Jawad's ordeal: A Gaza toddler's trauma after Israeli torture
stories.summary: A report details the alleged detention and abuse of a Gaza toddler named Jawad by Israeli forces. The child reportedly spent 10 hours in detention, resulting in significant trauma. His father remains in Israeli custody.

stories.title: Novaya Gazeta journalist detained in Moscow on suspicion of illegally using personal data
stories.summary: Oleg Roldugin, managing editor of the independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta, was detained in Moscow on suspicion of illegally using personal data. He was being questioned by law enforcement, according to Russian state media RIA Novosti.

stories.title: Pink to host 2026 Tony awards: ‘It’s the honor of an entire lifetime’
stories.summary: Singer Pink has been announced as the host of the 2026 Tony Awards ceremony, scheduled for June 7 at Radio City Music Hall in New York. The three-time Grammy winner will be making her debut as emcee of the event.

stories.title: “Will not be tolerated” – UK exposes Russian spy submarine operation targeting its undersea cables
stories.summary: The UK revealed that a Russian Akula-class decoy submarine and two GUGI mini-submarine carriers operated covertly north of Britain before the Royal Navy intervened, exposing what officials described as a spy operation targeting undersea cables.

stories.title: US Democrats warn Trump that Iran ceasefire must apply to Lebanon
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers in the US urged the Trump White House to ensure that any ceasefire agreement with Iran also covers Lebanon, warning that continued Israeli bombing there could reignite a broader regional war.

stories.title: Sidon residents recall horror of Israeli strikes after Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Residents of the southern Lebanese city of Sidon described the devastation following Israeli airstrikes that flattened a religious complex, as they surveyed the destruction after a US-Iran ceasefire was announced.

stories.title: Macron set for first meeting with Pope Leo amid calls for peace in Middle East
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is meeting Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican on Friday, their first face-to-face encounter. The meeting comes as the Pope has criticised U.S. President Trump's conduct during the Iran war, and Macron has called for a negotiated end to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Iran nuclear chief says enrichment cannot be stopped, calls US-Israel actions ineffective
stories.summary: Iran's nuclear chief declared that the country's uranium enrichment program cannot be stopped, dismissing U.S. and Israeli efforts to curtail it as ineffective.

stories.title: Israel’s attacks on Lebanon should not be happening, says Keir Starmer
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, during a Middle East visit, said Israel's continued attacks on Lebanon should not be happening. In a Guardian article, he called for the Iran conflict to serve as a catalyst for strengthening Britain's security resilience with European allies.

stories.title: Does a US-Iran ceasefire mean the end of the war?
stories.summary: Following a ceasefire deal between the United States and Iran, military strikes have slowed but tensions persist, raising questions about whether the agreement will hold or eventually collapse.

stories.title: In pictures: Security beefed up in Islamabad ahead of highly anticipated US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Islamabad's Red Zone was placed under heightened security and local holidays declared in the twin cities ahead of U.S.-Iran talks hosted by Pakistan. VVIP protocol under the Blue Book was extended to both delegations, with police and paramilitary forces deployed under strict guidelines.

stories.title: Had Bush and Blair been punished for Iraq war crimes, Iran might have been spared
stories.summary: A commentary by Peter Oborne draws parallels between the 2003 Iraq invasion and the current US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, arguing that accountability for earlier war crimes might have prevented the present conflict.

stories.title: Dozens of states condemn attacks on UN peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: Dozens of countries and the European Union issued statements condemning attacks on United Nations peacekeepers in Lebanon. The condemnations followed the killing of three Indonesian UNIFIL soldiers, with signatories calling for stronger protections for peacekeeping personnel.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders 'direct negotiations with Lebanon under fire'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered direct negotiations with Lebanon to proceed without pausing military operations. An Israeli official confirmed that talks would take place while bombardment of Lebanon continues.

stories.title: LA28 Olympics opens ticket sales globally after record local demand
stories.summary: The LA28 Olympic organizing committee opened ticket sales to international buyers after setting a record for domestic ticket sales, surpassing all previous Olympic Games in local demand.

stories.title: Iran says massive Israeli strikes in Lebanon render peace talks with US ‘meaningless’
stories.summary: Iran stated that massive Israeli strikes in Lebanon have rendered its peace talks with the United States meaningless, while President Trump reportedly urged Netanyahu to scale back attacks to prevent the truce from collapsing. The Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded.

stories.title: IMF warns of looming inflation crisis on back of US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned of a growing inflation crisis driven by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has disrupted oil and natural gas markets and damaged refineries and energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Floods in Russia’s Dagestan have affected thousands. Experts say the disaster reflects not just extreme weather, but deep infrastructure failures.
stories.summary: Flooding in Russia's Dagestan republic affected more than 6,200 people, with the hardest-hit areas including Makhachkala, Kaspiysk, and the Khasavyurtovsky and Derbentsky districts. Experts said the disaster reflects deep infrastructure failures in addition to extreme weather.

stories.title: Lebanon's hospitals may run out of vital medical supplies within days, says WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned that Lebanese hospitals may run out of vital medical supplies within days. Israel continued bombing targets in Lebanon on Thursday, following its largest attacks of the war the previous day.

stories.title: Moscow Police Raid Novaya Gazeta’s Newsroom
stories.summary: Moscow police raided the newsroom of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta. The search is reportedly linked to a criminal investigation alleging the newspaper illegally obtained and used personal information.

stories.title: Is Trump's ceasefire a trick for escalation? A pessimist's view
stories.summary: Columnist K. Al Hroub questioned whether the Trump administration's ceasefire efforts may serve as cover for military escalation. The piece noted that U.S. military buildup has accelerated even as diplomatic rhetoric dominates media coverage.

stories.title: ‘Mental breakdown’: oil tanker workers stuck in Gulf for six weeks are reaching their limit
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Gulf after six weeks due to Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz. Crew members on oil tankers report severe mental health strain and say conditions remain too unsafe to sail through the strait.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu calls for talks with Lebanon ‘as soon as possible’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said his government is prepared to begin negotiations with Lebanon as soon as possible, with a focus on disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations.

stories.title: Zelensky names condition for halting strikes on Russian oil refineries
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries are a direct response to Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. He indicated Ukraine would halt such strikes if Russia stopped targeting Ukrainian energy facilities.

stories.title: Iran’s envoy deletes post on delegation arrival in Islamabad for US talks
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Pakistan reportedly deleted a social media post about the Iranian delegation's arrival in Islamabad for upcoming talks with the United States. An embassy official declined to confirm whether the envoy was expected to arrive on April 9.

stories.title: As US and Iran talk truce, Israel digs in for a 'forever war' - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis described Israel's establishment of buffer zones in Gaza, Syria, and Lebanon as a strategic shift following the October 7, 2023 attacks. The approach places Israel in what the article characterizes as a semi-permanent state of war even as U.S.-Iran truce talks proceed.

stories.title: China’s dual-use ambitions could severely threaten America’s force posture
stories.summary: An op-ed by Heritage Foundation analysts Brent Sadler and Allen Zhang warns that China's dual-use technology ambitions, particularly in maritime infrastructure, pose a growing threat to America's military force posture. The authors argue the Pentagon must expand monitoring beyond dual-use technology to include maritime assets.

stories.title: Venezuela police tear gas protesters calling for pay and pension rises
stories.summary: Police in Caracas fired tear gas at thousands of protesters marching toward the presidential palace to demand pay raises and pension increases. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez had announced wage increases on May 1 without specifying the amount, amid widespread poverty-level salaries in Venezuela.

stories.title: UK says Russia ran submarine operation over cables and pipelines
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey disclosed that Russia conducted a submarine operation over cables and pipelines in the Atlantic. Healey stated there is no evidence of damage to British infrastructure.

stories.title: Why Gulf states turned to Ukraine for defence deals
stories.summary: Gulf states have pursued defense agreements with Ukraine as part of a broader strategy to diversify their security partnerships. The deals reflect a long-term shift in Gulf security infrastructure beyond traditional alliances, coinciding with Ukraine's diplomatic outreach.

stories.title: IDF's 98th Division gains control over Hezbollah-ridden town in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF's 98th Division reportedly gained control of a town in southern Lebanon described as a Hezbollah stronghold. Israeli media, citing IDF estimates, reported that several dozen Hezbollah fighters, including Radwan Force operatives, were present in the town.

stories.title: The Lebanese civilians killed in Israel's massacre
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on April 8, 2026, marked the heaviest single day of bombing in Lebanon, killing more than 200 people including a doctor, journalists, and students, despite a US-announced two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Calls to invoke the 25th Amendment after Trump's Iran threats 'useless'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's threat to destroy "a whole civilisation" in Iran has prompted renewed calls to invoke the 25th Amendment, drawing bipartisan condemnation. However, observers note that the constitutional mechanism remains politically unviable despite declining presidential approval ratings.

stories.title: 'Trump abandoned us': ceasefire sparks anger, fear, division among Iranians
stories.summary: Iranians are sharply divided over the two-week ceasefire and possible peace plan between the US and Israel on one side and Iran on the other. Reactions range from relief to anger and fear after five weeks of armed conflict, according to interviews conducted by FRANCE 24 Observers inside Iran.

stories.title: No peace in the Middle East until Israeli state is dismantled
stories.summary: Op-ed columnist Ghada Karmi argued that Israel has fueled wars, displacement, and global crises since its founding in 1948. The piece questioned what benefits, if any, the Israeli state has provided to the world.

stories.title: Kenya disputes UN probe accusing Haiti mission of sexual abuse
stories.summary: Kenya disputed a United Nations report containing substantiated allegations of sexual abuse by members of a UN-backed anti-gang mission in Haiti. The force is staffed predominantly by Kenyan police officers.

stories.title: 'Not buying it': Nearly half of Israelis say Israel and US did not win Iran war, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll conducted by Walla and Maariv found that nearly half of Israelis do not believe Israel and the United States won the war against Iran. The survey revealed broad dissatisfaction with the war's outcome and mixed views on political leadership.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia lacks forces to capture Kostiantynivka and Druzhkivka by end of April
stories.summary: President Zelensky assessed that Russian forces lack sufficient strength to capture Kostiantynivka and Druzhkivka in Donetsk Oblast by the end of April. He described the situation in the Pokrovsk sector as difficult but stable.

stories.title: Lidl to open 50 UK stores in year ahead – and its first pub
stories.summary: German-owned retailer Lidl plans to open 50 new stores across the United Kingdom in the coming year, creating nearly 2,000 jobs, as it seeks to surpass Morrisons as Britain's fifth-largest supermarket. The company is also building its first pub in east Belfast.

stories.title: UK tracked Russia submarines in alleged Atlantic ‘covert’ operation: defence secretary
stories.summary: Britain announced it tracked and deterred three Russian submarines during an alleged month-long covert operation in UK waters in the North Atlantic near undersea cables and pipelines. Defence Secretary John Healey said there was no evidence of damage to subsea infrastructure. The operation was conducted jointly with Norway and other allies.

stories.title: As Trump claims victory, Iran emerges bruised but powerful with leverage over Hormuz - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that despite sustaining damage from U.S. military action, Iran retains significant strategic leverage through its control over the Strait of Hormuz. Middle East scholar Fawaz Gerges characterized the conflict as a grave strategic miscalculation by the Trump administration with unintended regional consequences.

stories.title: Israel’s Lebanon strikes kill 203, sparking global calls to extend U.S.-Iran truce
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon killed at least 203 people, prompting global calls to extend the U.S.-Iran truce to cover Lebanese territory. Washington stated that the Lebanon conflict was not included in the ceasefire, and Israel indicated it had no intention of halting operations.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Israel wants to start peace talks with Lebanon 'as soon as possible'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced he has instructed his cabinet to begin direct peace talks with Lebanon as soon as possible, with negotiations to focus on disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations.

stories.title: Air France extends Middle East flight suspensions to May 3
stories.summary: Air France extended suspensions of its Middle East flight operations through May 3. A source indicated the airline made the decision to extend suspensions before the US-Iran ceasefire was announced.

stories.title: Nato chief: Member countries are ‘doing everything’ Trump is asking
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in a Washington speech that nearly all NATO member countries are responding to President Trump's requests to strengthen the military alliance, despite some initially being slow to act.

stories.title: With a switch of a letter in DNA ‘dark matter,’ Israeli scientists change sex of mouse
stories.summary: Researchers at Bar-Ilan University in Israel used CRISPR gene-editing technology to alter the Enh13 genetic switch controlling the Sox9 gene, causing chromosomally female (XX) mice to develop as males, with potential implications for understanding genetic mutations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Indabo Residents in Kano Call for More Health Workers to Ensure Round-the-Clock Phc Services
stories.summary: Residents near Indabo Primary Healthcare Centre in Kano, Nigeria, are calling for additional health workers to provide round-the-clock services, citing risks to pregnant women and other patients who cannot access care after dark.

stories.title: Russians shell Zolochiv in Kharkiv region, injuries, damage reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the settlement of Zolochiv in the Bohodukhiv district of Ukraine's Kharkiv region on April 9. Two women and three children were injured, and damage to the area was reported.

stories.title: IMF strikes staff-level deal with Sri Lanka on $700m in funding
stories.summary: The IMF reached a staff-level agreement with Sri Lanka to unlock approximately $700 million in funding, contingent on board approval. The deal supports Sri Lanka's recovery from its worst economic crisis, which led to a 2022 debt default and a $2.9 billion IMF bailout programme.

stories.title: Fighting between Sahel-based jihadist rivals spills into Niger
stories.summary: Al Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates in West Africa clashed inside Niger for the first time, according to a statement from one of the groups. Analysts said the fighting signals an intensification of the jihadist rivals' years-long competition in the Sahel region.

stories.title: Republicans block Democrats’ push to curb Trump’s war powers over Iran
stories.summary: House Democrats attempted to pass a resolution limiting President Donald Trump's war powers regarding Iran using a unanimous consent procedure. Republican pro forma speaker Chris Smith blocked the effort by not recognizing Democratic lawmakers on the floor. The resolution was expected to fail but reflected growing unease in Congress over the open-ended conflict.

stories.title: Hormuz at near standstill as Iran warns ships to keep to its waters
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has slowed to a near standstill as Iran warned vessels to remain in its designated waters. Japanese shipping firm Mitsui O.S.K. Lines is among companies affected by confusion over the impact of the two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire on navigation.

stories.title: Gaza border kibbutz redirects donations to help war-torn north
stories.summary: Kibbutz Nirim, located on the Gaza border and which lost seven residents on October 7, announced it would redirect incoming donations to assist communities in war-affected northern Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan declares Islamabad holidays ahead of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan declared public holidays in Islamabad ahead of U.S.-Iran talks expected to take place in the capital. Enhanced security measures are being implemented in preparation for the high-level diplomatic negotiations.

stories.title: Italy says EU should consider pausing budget rules if Iran crisis persists
stories.summary: Italy's government suggested the European Union consider pausing its budget rules if the crisis stemming from the Iran conflict persists. Rome is preparing to lower its GDP growth estimates for 2026.

stories.title: Russia detains former Radio Free Europe freelance journalist on treason charge
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service detained a former Radio Free Europe freelance journalist on suspicion of treason. Authorities accused the journalist of passing information to Ukrainian intelligence services.

stories.title: The Iran Cease-Fire Has Only Divided the War
stories.summary: The ceasefire between the United States and Iran has failed to end the broader fighting and has instead complicated the conflict. Disagreements over the scope of the truce, particularly regarding Lebanon, have divided the parties involved.

stories.title: Rawalpindi board postpones matric exams scheduled for April 10
stories.summary: The Rawalpindi Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education postponed matric examinations at 64 centres scheduled for April 10, citing heightened diplomatic activity in Islamabad during U.S.-Iran talks. Exams in other districts of Rawalpindi Division were to continue as scheduled.

stories.title: Ukraine ensures fuel security with Middle East agreements, Zelensky says
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that Ukraine has reached agreements with several Middle Eastern countries to secure annual volumes of oil and petroleum products. He described the deals as part of efforts to ensure Ukraine's fuel security.

stories.title: 'President Trump, do not betray the Iranian people!' - comment
stories.summary: A commentary argued that while a ceasefire may halt bombing, it leaves Iran's government free to intensify repression against its own citizens. The piece urged President Trump not to abandon the Iranian people.

stories.title: MEPs raise alarm about possible Russian meddling in Hungary’s elections
stories.summary: Members of the European Parliament urged European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to investigate possible Russian interference in Hungary's upcoming elections. MEPs cited concerns about disinformation and voter intimidation on behalf of Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's ruling party, days before the vote.

stories.title: Humanitarian situation in Sudan at ‘catastrophic levels’, says NGO
stories.summary: The NGO Humanity & Inclusion reported that the humanitarian situation in Sudan has reached catastrophic levels, with people with disabilities facing extreme challenges amid ongoing war and crisis.

stories.title: “If we don’t hit them in the face, they will hit us and won’t feel what war is” – Zelenskyy on Ukraine’s energy strikes
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine will continue striking Russian energy infrastructure until Moscow ceases its attacks on Ukraine's energy sector. He framed the strikes as a necessary deterrent to make Russia feel the consequences of war.

stories.title: Russia’s oil and gas revenues fall 45% in first quarter as budget deficit exceeds full-year target
stories.summary: Russia's oil and gas revenues fell 45.4 percent in the first quarter of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, according to the Finance Ministry. The federal budget deficit has already exceeded the full-year target within three months.

stories.title: Houthi leader calls ceasefire with US a ‘major victory’ for Iran
stories.summary: Ansar Allah leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi described the Pakistan-brokered truce between the US and Iran as a great victory for Tehran and the Iranian-aligned axis of resistance, speaking on Al Masirah TV.

stories.title: Iran rules out restrictions on enrichment programme: chief
stories.summary: Iran's nuclear chief rejected any restrictions on the country's uranium enrichment program ahead of talks with the United States. Iranian officials stated that demands from Washington and Israel to limit enrichment "will not come true."

stories.title: Saudi Arabia executes two Shia citizens from Eastern Province
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia executed two Shia citizens, Mustafa Ali al-Subaiti and his nephew Ali Hassan al-Subaiti, from the Eastern Province on Monday. Authorities alleged the two were involved with a foreign terror group.

stories.title: How Ukraine Benefited from Trump’s Iran War
stories.summary: Ukraine has benefited from the Iran war as multiple countries have sought military deals with Kyiv. The conflict has increased global demand for defense partnerships, positioning Ukraine as an attractive partner for arms agreements.

stories.title: Lebanon thought there was a ceasefire - then Israel unleashed deadly blitz
stories.summary: Israel stated that Lebanon is not covered by the ceasefire agreement between the US and Iran, and subsequently launched deadly strikes on Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Can Africa’s informal economy become the continent’s next investment frontier? {Business Africa}
stories.summary: An investment firm is working to formalize Africa's large informal economy by converting unreported consumer activity into verifiable, high-growth investment portfolios. Separately, Kenya faces a housing deficit of two million units despite 5.7% growth in its real estate sector.

stories.title: How the Iran conflict might change defense investments in the Gulf
stories.summary: The Iran conflict is expected to reshape defense investment patterns in Gulf states. Middle East Bureau Chief Agnes Helou discussed the war's implications and interviewed the CEO of SCOPA in the Middle East Defense Digest.

stories.title: 'Endless fears': Even if fighting stops, the damage to Iran's children will endure
stories.summary: The BBC gathered testimony from parents and aid workers in Iran describing the psychological toll of the ongoing conflict on children, highlighting fears that the damage will persist long after fighting ends.

stories.title: Russia’s Supreme Court Designates Nobel Prize-Winning Memorial as ‘Extremist’
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court designated the Nobel Prize-winning human rights organization Memorial as an extremist group. The court justified the ban by characterizing Memorial's activities as "markedly anti-Russian."

stories.title: What Happens Inside Israel’s Detention System
stories.summary: Human rights organizations, UN investigators, and Israeli legal groups have reported that torture of Palestinian detainees is part of a systematic practice within Israel's detention system.

stories.title: Kenya: Oburu Odinga Condemns Attack On Vihiga Senator, Calls for Swift Investigation
stories.summary: Kenya's Orange Democratic Movement, through Oburu Odinga, condemned a physical attack on Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and called on authorities to investigate the incident promptly.

stories.title: Memorial Human Rights Center suspends all work in Russia after Supreme Court designates movement ‘extremist’
stories.summary: The Memorial Human Rights Center announced it is suspending all work inside Russia as of April 9. The decision followed Russia's Supreme Court designating the International Memorial public movement an extremist organization.

stories.title: China hopes ‘relevant parties’ can grasp chance at peace in Iran war
stories.summary: China called on relevant parties to seize the opportunity for peace amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran. The statement came after US President Donald Trump vowed to maintain American military assets in the Middle East.

stories.title: Israeli military attacks town on Lebanon’s southern border
stories.summary: Israeli troops attempted to besiege the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil, approximately 5 km from the Israeli border. Hezbollah reported clashes with Israeli forces in the area, and Israel expanded forced displacement orders covering 14 percent of Lebanon.

stories.title: Uganda: Butabika Director - Uganda Lacking Secure Forensic Psychiatry Ward
stories.summary: Dr. Juliet Nakku, Executive Director of Butabika National Referral Hospital in Kampala, Uganda, revealed that the country lacks a secure forensic psychiatry ward.

stories.title: Zelensky signals imminent trilateral talks to end Ukraine war, format still unclear
stories.summary: President Zelensky indicated that a trilateral meeting aimed at ending the war in Ukraine is expected in the near future. The format of the talks has not yet been finalized.

stories.title: 'Everything begins with intelligence': Three wars rewriting the rules of modern warfare
stories.summary: An analysis examined how conflicts in Israel, Ukraine, and Taiwan are redefining modern warfare. The piece highlighted intelligence and emerging technologies as central drivers reshaping military strategy across all three theaters.

stories.title: Uganda: Unicef Condemns Brutal Attack At Ggaba School
stories.summary: UNICEF's representative to Uganda, Dr. Robin Nandy, condemned a violent attack at Ggaba School in Kampala, part of a pattern of attacks targeting children across the country.

stories.title: India’s Assam and Kerala states hold legislative assembly elections
stories.summary: India's Assam and Kerala states held legislative assembly elections, with voting also taking place in the federal territory of Puducherry. West Bengal and Tamil Nadu are scheduled to vote later in the month.

stories.title: Israel bombed Gaza on 36 of the past 40 days while the war raged in Iran
stories.summary: Israel bombed Gaza on 36 of the past 40 days during the war with Iran, killing 107 people, approving only 8 percent of medical evacuations, and allowing just 20 percent of aid trucks to enter.

stories.title: Russia opens criminal case against comedian and screenwriter for violating ‘foreign agent’ rules
stories.summary: Russian authorities opened a criminal case against comedian and screenwriter Semyon Slepakov for failing to comply with obligations under Russia's foreign agent law. The Moscow Prosecutor's Office said the case was initiated based on its own investigation.

stories.title: Four dead after migrant dinghy sinks in English Channel off northern France
stories.summary: A small boat carrying approximately 30 migrants sank in the English Channel off the coast of northern France, killing four people. Two men and two women died after being swept away by strong currents near Boulogne. At least 42 other passengers were rescued by emergency services.

stories.title: Between 'victory' and uncertainty: What ceasefire means for Iran
stories.summary: A ceasefire narrative of "victory" quickly took hold in Iran following the truce, but many Iranians remain uncertain whether the agreement will lead to lasting peace. Questions persist about the country's strategic direction after the conflict.

stories.title: Spain condemns Israeli attacks on Lebanon, reopens Tehran embassy
stories.summary: Spain publicly condemned Israeli military strikes on Lebanon and announced the reopening of its embassy in Tehran. The move positions Spain as one of the most outspoken Western critics of Israel's military operations in the region.

stories.title: Al Jazeera’s Mohammed Wishah, killed by Israeli strike, laid to rest
stories.summary: Mourners gathered in Gaza for the funeral of Al Jazeera Mubasher journalist Mohammed Wishah, who was killed in an Israeli strike.

stories.title: Russia condemns Israeli attack on Lebanon, calls for immediate ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia's foreign ministry strongly condemned Israeli strikes on Lebanon and called for an immediate ceasefire that should extend to Lebanon, warning that the attacks threaten to derail emerging negotiations.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Over 1K Bodies
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged the remains of over 1,000 fallen personnel. The transfer occurred as officials on both sides indicated progress toward a significant prisoner-of-war exchange agreement.

stories.title: Bodies of 1,000 fallen returned to Ukraine
stories.summary: The bodies of 1,000 fallen individuals were returned to Ukraine as part of ongoing repatriation efforts. Russian authorities identified the remains as belonging to Ukrainian servicemembers.

stories.title: Security officers raid Novaya Gazeta’s Moscow offices
stories.summary: Masked security service officers raided the Moscow offices of Novaya Gazeta, the independent Russian newspaper reported. The raid is connected to ongoing legal proceedings against the publication.

stories.title: Majority of US adults have negative view on Israel, Netanyahu, Pew Research finds
stories.summary: A Pew Research Center survey found that a majority of U.S. adults hold negative views of Israel and Prime Minister Netanyahu. While most Republicans and Republican-leaning individuals still view Israel favorably, the share with unfavorable opinions has risen sharply since the previous year.

stories.title: Almodóvar, Travolta and Bardem lead 2026 Cannes lineup
stories.summary: The 2026 Cannes Film Festival lineup features major directors including Pedro Almodóvar, Steven Soderbergh, and Ron Howard premiering new work. Stars such as Javier Bardem, John Travolta, Michael Fassbender, and Kristen Stewart are also set to appear at the festival.

stories.title: Why the U.S.-Iran ceasefire is on a shaky ground | Explained
stories.summary: The ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran faces uncertainty due to serious differences between the two sides' interpretations of its terms. Analysts are examining the divergent American and Iranian versions of the deal.

stories.title: Al Jazeera, media rights group RSF condemn killing of journalist in Israeli strike on Gaza
stories.summary: Al Jazeera and Reporters Without Borders condemned the killing of a journalist in an Israeli airstrike on Gaza. RSF reported that more than 220 journalists have been killed by Israeli forces in Gaza since October 2023.

stories.title: How Israel is sowing sectarian strife in its war on Lebanon
stories.summary: A report alleged that Israel's military strategy in Lebanon is deliberately exacerbating sectarian divisions among the country's religious communities. The war has reportedly caused significant demographic shifts across Lebanese regions.

stories.title: UN: Over 1,000 aid workers killed in past 3 years, most in Gaza
stories.summary: A United Nations report found that more than 1,010 humanitarian aid workers were killed between 2023 and 2025, with over 560 deaths occurring in Gaza and the West Bank. Sudan, South Sudan, Ukraine, and the Democratic Republic of Congo also saw significant losses, nearly tripling the 377 killed from 2020 to 2022.

stories.title: Greenland hits back at Trump amid Nato tensions: ‘we’re not ‌some piece of ‌ice’
stories.summary: Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen pushed back against U.S. President Trump's characterization of the Arctic island as a 'big, poorly run piece of ice,' asserting that Greenland is a proud nation. Trump's comments came amid strained NATO relations over the Iran war.

stories.title: Government approves 34 new settlements as it acts to deepen hold on West Bank
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet approved 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank in a single decision, the largest number approved at one time by any Israeli government, bringing the current government's total to 103.

stories.title: Moldova formally exits Russia’s post-Soviet CIS as Sandu signs withdrawal decrees
stories.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu signed decrees formally completing the country's withdrawal from Russia's post-Soviet Commonwealth of Independent States. The move follows a parliamentary vote on April 2 approving the exit.

stories.title: Israeli cabinet 'secretly approves record number' of new West Bank settlements
stories.summary: Israel's cabinet secretly approved 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank in a single decision, according to i24NEWS. This brings the total approved by the current government to over 100, amid the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: Iran sees jihad, the West sees geopolitics - and that gap is dangerous - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argued that Western strategy toward Iran has failed to account for Tehran's ideological motivations rooted in jihad, creating a dangerous gap between how Iran and Western governments perceive the conflict.

stories.title: Israel orders Lebanese in south Beirut to flee ahead of possible attack
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings for residents of south Beirut ahead of possible strikes, following bombardment the previous day that killed more than 250 people and injured over 1,000.

stories.title: Britain exposes clandestine Russian operation in North Atlantic
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey revealed details of a covert Russian operation in the North Atlantic. He warned Russia of serious consequences if it continues to threaten British underwater infrastructure.

stories.title: Caught between wars: Gaza residents wait for someone to change their fate
stories.summary: Residents of Gaza are caught between the broader war involving Iran and their own unresolved conflict. Gazans continue to wait for a resolution to their predicament amid the ongoing regional hostilities.

stories.title: Israel approves largest West Bank settlement expansion on record
stories.summary: Israeli ministers reportedly approved 34 new settlements in the occupied West Bank in a covert decision earlier this month. The expansion is described as the single-largest settlement approval in Israeli history.

stories.title: Iran’s ‘jihad of knowledge’ was never about its people - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that Iran's Islamic Republic weaponized scientific research and higher education for regime purposes while undermining its own universities and leaving ordinary citizens to bear the consequences.

stories.title: Iran’s nuclear agency chief says its right to ‘enrich uranium is necessary’ for U.S. talks
stories.summary: The head of Iran's nuclear agency stated that the country's right to enrich uranium is a necessary condition for upcoming talks with the United States. The negotiations are scheduled to take place in Islamabad, Pakistan's capital.

stories.title: The 'final blow' doctrine: How Trump is rewriting the rules of American power - analysis
stories.summary: The article analyzes how senior US officials Pete Hegseth, Marco Rubio, and Mike Waltz used the Iran conflict to reshape American military doctrine. It examines what it calls a "final blow" approach and discusses Israel's central role in this new model of US power projection.

stories.title: Israeli military says it has killed nephew of Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it killed a nephew of Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue striking Iran-backed Hezbollah targets wherever necessary, a day after major Israeli airstrikes hit Lebanon.

stories.title: De-Hamasification: The ideological war Israel isn't fighting - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel is not adequately pursuing ideological deradicalization efforts against Hamas in Gaza. The author contends that deradicalization should be treated as an active component of the war effort rather than a post-war project.

stories.title: WHO: Lebanon’s hospitals may run out of medical supplies in days
stories.summary: The WHO warned that Lebanon's hospitals could run out of vital medical supplies, including bandages, antibiotics, and anaesthetics, within days following mass casualties from large-scale Israeli strikes on Wednesday.

stories.title: Between two camps: Iran war forces the Arab world to pick a side - opinion
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving Iran is forcing Arab states to choose sides, in what analysts describe as a war that could determine the Middle East's next geopolitical alignment.

stories.title: Debt, defense, and disruption: The true cost of Israel's multi-front war - analysis
stories.summary: A mid-2026 analysis examines the economic toll of Israel's multi-front war, focusing on rising debt, increased defense spending, and broader economic disruption. The assessment highlights the strain on Israel's war-affected economy.

stories.title: JD Vance’s claims about Orbán, the EU and Hungary fact-checked
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance visited Budapest and praised Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, claiming the EU had attempted to "destroy" Hungary's economy. Fact-checkers noted Hungary is a net recipient of EU funds, contradicting Vance's characterization of Brussels' actions.

stories.title: UK navy foiled Russian submarines surveying undersea cables, defence minister says
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey revealed that a Royal Navy warship and P8 patrol aircraft tracked and deterred three Russian submarines surveying undersea infrastructure in the North Sea over a month-long operation. The submarines were forced to abandon their activity and flee the area.

stories.title: Lebanon must be covered by ceasefire agreement, French foreign minister says
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot stated that the ceasefire agreement between Iran and the United States must extend to cover military operations in Lebanon. Barrot also condemned what he described as massive Israeli strikes on Lebanon carried out the previous day.

stories.title: Settlers storm Al-Aqsa as Israel lifts holy site restrictions
stories.summary: Israeli settlers entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem after Israel lifted restrictions on the holy site. The access changes followed a fragile ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Traffic falls on major Sydney and Melbourne roads as fuel crisis sees Australians cut back on driving
stories.summary: Road traffic on major Sydney and Melbourne highways has declined significantly as rising fuel prices lead Australians to reduce driving. New South Wales government data shows key Sydney thoroughfares recording up to 20% fewer weekend trips amid the ongoing fuel crisis.

stories.title: Woman with three deadly diseases has ‘remarkable’ recovery after cell therapy
stories.summary: A 47-year-old woman with three life-threatening autoimmune diseases experienced a "remarkable" recovery after receiving cell therapy at University Hospital Erlangen in Germany. The treatment reset her immune system after nine previous treatments had failed to produce lasting results.

stories.title: ‘Inherently dangerous and unnecessary’: NT buses will soon be patrolled by armed officers
stories.summary: The Northern Territory government in Australia announced that armed Police Public Safety Officers will begin patrolling public transit in Darwin and Palmerston. First Nations legal groups and politicians warned the policy would disproportionately affect Indigenous people.

stories.title: Hormuz toll debate: China experts propose ‘innovative’ solutions as impasse persists
stories.summary: Chinese experts have proposed tying potential Strait of Hormuz transit tolls to oil prices or using China-issued digital tokens for settlements, as international debate over toll collection in the strategic waterway continues unresolved.

stories.title: Paul Hounkpè, the moderate challenger facing favourite Wadagni in Benin vote
stories.summary: Paul Hounkpè of the Cowry Forces for an Emerging Benin party is the sole opposition candidate in Benin's presidential election, positioning himself as a moderate challenger against the ruling bloc's favored candidate.

stories.title: Polish F-16s intercept Russian reconnaissance aircraft in Baltic Sea
stories.summary: Polish F-16 fighter jets intercepted a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance aircraft over the Baltic Sea on April 8. The Russian plane was operating with its transponder turned off during the mission.

stories.title: Can Istanbul rival Dubai? Turkey looks to woo investors as Iran war reshapes region
stories.summary: Turkish officials are offering incentives to Gulf firms unsettled by the Iran war, positioning Istanbul as a potential rival to Dubai as a regional business hub, though significant obstacles remain.

stories.title: UK says it deployed military to deter Russian submarines from attack on undersea cables
stories.summary: The United Kingdom deployed military assets to deter Russian submarines suspected of threatening undersea cables. Norway's defense ministry confirmed it contributed a P-8 maritime patrol aircraft and a frigate to the joint operation.

stories.title: Foolproof security arranged for foreign guests, Naqvi assures US envoy ahead of US‑Iran talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi assured US Ambassador Natalie Baker that comprehensive security arrangements were in place for foreign dignitaries ahead of US-Iran talks in Islamabad. Pakistan is hosting the in-person negotiations following a two-week ceasefire announced between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Israeli attacks on Lebanon aimed to undermine ceasefire, critics say
stories.summary: More than 250 people have been killed in Israeli air strikes on Lebanon since a ceasefire was declared, with critics arguing the attacks were aimed at undermining the truce.

stories.title: US had hottest March on record as nation faced ‘unprecedented’ heat
stories.summary: The continental United States recorded its hottest March in 132 years of federal weather records, according to NOAA data. The month's temperatures exceeded normal levels by a wider margin than any other month in recorded history for the lower 48 states. Forecasters warn a potentially super-strength El Niño could further increase global temperatures.

stories.title: Russia returns bodies of 1,000 fallen Ukrainian servicemembers; Ukraine returns 41 fallen Russian servicemembers
stories.summary: Russia transferred the bodies of 1,000 fallen Ukrainian servicemembers to Ukraine, while Ukraine returned the remains of 41 fallen Russian servicemembers. Russian State Duma deputy Shamsail Saraliyev confirmed the exchange.

stories.title: Trump sending US VP Vance to Pakistan for Iran talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he is sending Vice President JD Vance and other negotiators to Islamabad, Pakistan, for talks with Iran beginning Saturday. The White House confirmed the diplomatic mission as ceasefire efforts continued.

stories.title: Has Iran’s 10-point plan changed, as JD Vance claims?
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance claimed that Iran's 10-point peace plan had changed, fueling uncertainty as US officials offered conflicting interpretations of the proposal to permanently end hostilities.

stories.title: He Fought Terrorists for 12 Hours. Then the Real Battle Began. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Institute of Justice provides free legal aid to wounded Israeli soldiers returning from war, with over 22,000 soldiers having come home with injuries.

stories.title: Israel’s pounding of Lebanon is ‘deeply damaging’: British Foreign Secretary
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper described Israel's ongoing bombardment of Lebanon as deeply damaging. She called for Lebanon to be included in the US-Iran ceasefire agreement to prevent further escalation.

stories.title: Lebanon declares day of mourning after over 250 killed in Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Lebanon declared a national day of mourning on Thursday after Israeli strikes on Wednesday killed more than 250 people and injured over 1,000 across the country. Israel continued bombing additional targets in Lebanon on Thursday, threatening to undermine President Trump's truce from the outset.

stories.title: Hungary election: Voters want new EU approach, but tough Ukraine stance, poll shows
stories.summary: A poll conducted ahead of Hungary's election found that most voters want at least minor changes to the country's relationship with the European Union. The survey also revealed skepticism toward financial support for Ukraine, with voters prioritizing domestic issues.

stories.title: Hungary election: Voters want new EU approach, but tough on Ukraine, poll shows
stories.summary: A poll ahead of Hungary's upcoming election found that most voters want at least some changes to the country's relationship with the European Union. However, respondents expressed skepticism toward financial support for Ukraine and prioritized domestic issues.

stories.title: Iran war: Tehran claims victory but people fear what's next
stories.summary: A tenuous truce has taken hold in Iran after more than a month of bombing by the U.S. and Israel. While Tehran has claimed victory, Iranians fear the surviving but weakened regime will intensify domestic repression.

stories.title: Rescuers search for survivors in Lebanese capital amid new Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Rescue teams searched for survivors beneath destroyed buildings in Beirut on Thursday as Lebanon observed a national day of mourning. The search followed Israeli strikes across Lebanon that killed more than 200 people, with ongoing operations amid continued military activity.

stories.title: Russia’s Supreme Court designates Memorial an ‘extremist’ organization, banning its activities in the country
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court declared the Nobel Prize-winning human rights organization Memorial an extremist organization and banned its activities in the country. The court acted on a lawsuit filed by the Justice Ministry, claiming Memorial's activities were "anti-Russian."

stories.title: Pakistan PM forms crisis team to deal with effects of West Asia conflict on economy
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister formed a crisis management team to address the economic fallout from the conflict in West Asia. The National Coordination and Management Council is tasked with managing financial, economic, and trade-related policy measures.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in Islamabad: Who is involved and why it matters
stories.summary: Pakistan is set to host US-Iran talks in Islamabad after President Donald Trump announced a two-week ceasefire just before a self-imposed deadline expired. The negotiations follow back-channel diplomacy led by Pakistan, with Iran having submitted a 10-point proposal to the United States.

stories.title: Ukraine aims to store at least 13.2 bcm of gas ahead of winter – Shmyhal
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal stated that Ukraine aims to store at least 13.2 billion cubic meters of natural gas in underground facilities before the next winter heating season. He described this level as the critically necessary minimum.

stories.title: Kremlin states Putin did not decide on Easter truce
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that President Vladimir Putin has not yet made a decision on a possible Easter truce in the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran, Saudi FMs hold first call since start of conflict, discuss ways to reduce tensions
stories.summary: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi held their first phone call since Tehran launched strikes against Gulf neighbors. The two officials discussed the latest regional developments and ways to reduce tensions following the announcement of a two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Lebanon PM seeks support from Pakistan for inclusion in ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam called Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to seek confirmation that the US-Iran ceasefire includes Lebanon, following Israeli strikes that killed more than 250 people in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran war: Catalyst for a renewable energy push?
stories.summary: The US-Israel war with Iran has caused one of the largest global energy shocks in decades, disrupting oil and gas supplies particularly for Asian economies. Energy prices have surged worldwide. Climate activists argue the disruption should accelerate the transition to renewable energy sources.

stories.title: In pictures: Israeli strikes pummel Lebanon, putting US–Iran ceasefire at risk
stories.summary: Israel launched its heaviest coordinated air assault on Lebanon since the US-Iran war began, killing over 200 people. The strikes have put the Pakistan-brokered ceasefire between the United States and Iran at risk, with conflicting claims about whether Lebanon was covered by the truce.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns Israeli aggression against Lebanon in ‘strongest terms’, says it undermines peace efforts
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office issued a strong condemnation of Israel's ongoing military attacks on Lebanon, citing loss of civilian lives and destruction of infrastructure. Islamabad warned that the Israeli operations violate international law and undermine regional peace efforts.

stories.title: For Asia, US-Iran ceasefire offers little relief – and much uncertainty
stories.summary: The two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire reopened the Strait of Hormuz and eased global energy fears, but analysts say the time-limited truce offers Asian economies little long-term relief. The agreement is tied to ongoing negotiations and temporary safe-passage arrangements rather than a settled regional order.

stories.title: Israel launches fresh strikes on Lebanon after huge attacks jeopardise truce
stories.summary: Israel launched additional airstrikes on targets in Lebanon on Thursday, following attacks that killed more than 250 people — the largest Israeli bombardment of Lebanon during the conflict. The strikes have put the Middle East ceasefire brokered by the US and Iran in serious jeopardy.

stories.title: Russian director Andrei Zvyagintsev’s new film selected for Cannes main competition, Variety reports
stories.summary: Russian director Andrei Zvyagintsev's new film "Minotaur" has been selected for the main competition at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, running May 12–23. The selection was reported by entertainment trade outlet Variety.

stories.title: Netanyahu corruption trial to resume on Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's corruption trial, which began in 2020, will resume on Sunday after Israel lifted the state of emergency imposed during the war on Iran, allowing the judicial system to return to normal operations.

stories.title: Slamming Israel at Michigan rallies, Hasan Piker boosts Senate candidate Abdul el-Sayed
stories.summary: Far-left streamer Hasan Piker held rallies at Michigan universities supporting Democratic Senate candidate Abdul el-Sayed, delivering sharp anti-Israel rhetoric to cheering crowds.

stories.title: Evictions in East Jerusalem surge as Palestinians lose court fight against far-right group
stories.summary: Dozens of Palestinian families in the Silwan neighborhood of East Jerusalem have been evicted from their homes as the far-right group Ateret Cohanim claims trusteeship over land belonging to pre-state Jewish owners, with more evictions expected.

stories.title: US warns citizens to reconsider Nigeria travel on safety grounds
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department urged American citizens to reconsider travel to Nigeria due to safety concerns and authorized the voluntary departure of non-emergency embassy staff on security grounds.

stories.title: Russian forces attack car with drone in Zaporizhzhia district; two people injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone attacked a civilian car in the village of Yurkivka in the Zaporizhzhia district, injuring two people. The strike targeted a vehicle in the area.

stories.title: Push to end Israeli strikes on Lebanon to save Iran-US ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed at least 203 people, prompting sharp condemnations from several countries. Multiple nations demanded that Lebanon be included in the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, with diplomatic pressure mounting to halt the attacks.

stories.title: Israel dismisses calls to add Lebanon to US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel rejected international demands to include Lebanon in the US-Iran Gulf ceasefire and vowed continued strikes against Hezbollah. The Lebanese health ministry reported at least 203 people killed and 1,000 wounded in the latest Israeli attacks on Lebanon.

stories.title: Iranians rally to mark 40-day mourning for slain supreme leader Khamenei
stories.summary: Mourners across Iran held ceremonies marking the 40th day since the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed at the start of the Iran war. In Tehran, participants wearing black rallied from Jomhouri Eslami Square to the neighbourhood of Khamenei's former office.

stories.title: Promised in 2023. Grounded in Belgium. Norway’s F-16s still haven’t reached Ukraine.
stories.summary: Norwegian F-16 fighter jets promised to Ukraine in 2023 remain grounded in Belgium and have not been delivered. A Western advisor stated the aircraft were urgently needed during the winter and their absence may have cost lives.

stories.title: #Lebanon: Scenes of destruction day after ‘terrifying’ Israeli #strikes
stories.summary: Lebanon declared a national day of mourning on Thursday following Israel's largest attack of the war on its neighbour. The strikes caused widespread destruction in Beirut and killed more than 250 people, according to Lebanon's civil defence service.

stories.title: Netanyahu corruption trial to resume after Iran halt
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial is set to resume after proceedings were paused during the Iran conflict. The ceasefire has allowed the judicial system to return to normal operations.

stories.title: Three Palestinians, including a child, injured by Israeli military in West Bank raids
stories.summary: Three Palestinians, including a child hit by rubber-coated bullets, were injured during an Israeli military raid in the Umm al-Sharayet neighborhood south of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent Society.

stories.title: Taking stock of Iran war after 40 days of conflict
stories.summary: After 40 days of conflict, the Iran war has caused significant damage to Iranian infrastructure and military capabilities, even as Tehran claims victory. The Trump administration has suggested Iran underwent regime change, but Iranian leadership remains in place. A fragile ceasefire between Iran and the United States is now the focus of global attention.

stories.title: India hit by Middle East war: Millions face gas shortages
stories.summary: India faced severe cooking gas shortages after Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz during the Middle East conflict, disrupting LPG imports on which nearly 1.5 billion people depend. Long queues formed at distribution centres in major cities, driving many to the black market. The conflict also endangered nearly ten million Indians living and working in Gulf countries.

stories.title: France unveils rearmament boost to face Russia threat, global instability
stories.summary: France announced plans to increase explosive drone stockpiles by up to 400 percent by 2030 as part of new draft legislation. The rearmament push follows warnings from France's top military commanders that the country must prepare for a potential clash with Russia within the coming years and that NATO needs to accelerate weapons production.

stories.title: Zelensky on €90 billion loan: Meloni is strong leader, and her voice is important for Ukraine
stories.summary: President Zelensky praised Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni as a strong leader whose voice is important for Ukraine, in the context of discussions about a proposed €90 billion loan.

stories.title: Russia’s Federal Budget Deficit Blows Past Annual Target in Just 3 Months
stories.summary: Russia's federal budget deficit exceeded its full-year target within the first three months of the fiscal year. The shortfall was driven by a sharp decline in energy tax revenues and a double-digit increase in government spending.

stories.title: Fragile Iran truce brings brief relief to African markets
stories.summary: The truce between the United States, Israel, and Iran has provided temporary relief to African markets that were strained by the conflict. Economists caution that underlying economic vulnerabilities may limit the duration of any market rebound.

stories.title: Fact check: Orban points to Ukraine over pipeline bomb
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán suggested that explosives found near a gas pipeline in Serbia were evidence of Ukrainian sabotage. However, Serbia's intelligence chief publicly disputed Orbán's claim.

stories.title: Southeast Asia trusts the EU more, but Brussels still has work to do
stories.summary: A survey indicates that Southeast Asian nations increasingly view the European Union as a trusted counterbalance to U.S.-China rivalry. Analysts note that Brussels needs to deepen political engagement to convert growing goodwill into substantive strategic influence in the region.

stories.title: Head of IMF says Iran war will permanently scar global economy even if peace is reached
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that the Iran war will permanently damage the global economy even if a durable peace deal is reached. Speaking as the ceasefire appeared fragile, she said scarring effects from the conflict would result in slower global growth and a lasting hit to living standards worldwide.

stories.title: How can Beijing prepare for Trump’s ‘drunken boxing’ style before he meets Xi in China?
stories.summary: Chinese analysts are studying U.S. President Donald Trump's abrupt policy swings—particularly the Iran crisis and subsequent ceasefire—as Beijing prepares for a planned high-stakes visit by Trump next month. Observers in China describe his negotiating approach as unpredictable "split" or "drunken boxing" style governance.

stories.title: Son of British couple detained in Iran calls on Starmer to press for their release
stories.summary: Joe Bennett, son of detained British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, urged Prime Minister Keir Starmer to press for their release from Tehran's Evin prison. The couple was arrested on espionage charges during a trip to Iran in January of last year and has been held for 15 months.

stories.title: Lebanon calls for direct talks with Israel
stories.summary: The Lebanese government called for direct talks with Israel following the heaviest Israeli strikes on Lebanon in six weeks, which killed more than 250 people on Wednesday.

stories.title: BTS battle torrential rain to kick off $1bn world tour
stories.summary: K-pop group BTS launched their world tour, expected to gross $1 billion, in Goyang, South Korea, performing through torrential rain during the opening concert.

stories.title: The victims of Israel's 'Black Wednesday' attack on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon on what has been called "Black Wednesday" killed hundreds of people in a matter of minutes. Reports indicate that civilians and children were among the majority of casualties.

stories.title: Hackers say they obtained at least 19,000 files from ex-Israeli army chief Halevi's phone
stories.summary: An Iran-aligned hacking group called the Handala Hack Team claimed it obtained over 19,000 sensitive files from the personal phone of former Israeli army Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi in a years-long cyber operation.

stories.title: Who was Mohammed Wishah, Al Jazeera correspondent Israel killed?
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondent Mohammed Wishah was killed by Israeli forces. Colleagues described him as a mentor who fostered relationships among journalists, resolved conflicts, and offered guidance.

stories.title: Iran to let no more than 15 vessels a day pass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran announced it will allow no more than 15 vessels per day through the Strait of Hormuz under the ceasefire deal with the US. The strait, which carries about a fifth of global oil supplies, had been largely shut since the war began.

stories.title: How the Army could spend nearly $19 billion in RDT&E funding
stories.summary: The US Army's research, development, test, and evaluation budget of nearly $19 billion is largely allocated to major programs. Key recipients include the Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft, THAAD missile defense, hypersonic weapons, counter-drone technology, and M-SHORAD air defense systems.

stories.title: Holy sites reopen in Jerusalem’s Old City after over a month of closure
stories.summary: Holy sites in Jerusalem's Old City reopened after more than a month of closure, with Muslim worshipers gathering at Al-Aqsa for dawn prayers and extended Ramadan hours maintained for Jewish visitors to the Temple Mount.

stories.title: Benin faces uneven race for president
stories.summary: Benin's presidential race pits ruling-bloc-backed Finance Minister Romuald Wadagni, who has held the post for a decade, against sole opposition candidate Paul Hounkpè, a former culture minister regarded as a moderate.

stories.title: Gaza: Selling handmade dolls to survive and bring joy to children
stories.summary: Shireen al-Kurdi, a 36-year-old displaced Palestinian mother of five in Gaza, is earning a limited income by making handmade crochet dolls and selling them at affordable prices to bring joy to children amid the conflict.

stories.title: This Isn’t a 1970s Oil Shock
stories.summary: The Iran war has disrupted global energy markets, but analysts note the current situation differs from the 1970s oil shocks. The modern global energy system is structured differently and is considered more fragile than during previous crises.

stories.title: The Pentagon claims ‘we control the sky’ over Iran. Experts say the air war isn’t that simple.
stories.summary: Pentagon claims of air superiority over Iran are being challenged by defense experts who say the term is being misapplied. Analysts argue the characterization obscures ongoing dangers that have resulted in US aircraft being downed and damaged.

stories.title: Gaza mourns Al Jazeera reporter Mohammed Wishah killed iin Israeli drone strike
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondent Mohammed Wishah was killed in an Israeli drone strike that hit his car west of Gaza City. Residents of Gaza mourned the journalist following the attack.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills girl student in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: A young female student was killed by Israeli fire in Gaza while attending class in a tent, according to medics. The incident underscores deteriorating conditions for children in the territory under a fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz, raising fears over mined waterway
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday in response to Israeli attacks on Lebanon. As of early Thursday, no tanker traffic had been reported passing through the waterway, raising concerns about potential mine threats.

stories.title: Pro-Iranian hacking group Handala claims breaching ex-IDF chief Halevi's phone
stories.summary: A pro-Iranian hacking group called Handala claimed it breached the phone of former IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi. The group published footage allegedly showing Halevi in meetings with senior Arab officials, including representatives from Qatar and Jordan.

stories.title: Zelensky believes negotiations between Ukraine, US, and Russia to resume
stories.summary: President Zelensky said the U.S. has shifted its focus to the Middle East, causing trilateral talks with Russia to be postponed. He expressed confidence that the negotiation process between Ukraine, the United States, and Russia will resume.

stories.title: Israel’s bombing of Lebanon after US-Iran ceasefire prompts condemnation
