stories.summary: Israel launched devastating strikes on Lebanon hours after the US-Iran ceasefire was announced, killing more than 200 people including in densely populated areas. The bombardment drew widespread international condemnation, including from the International Committee of the Red Cross, amid efforts to preserve the fragile truce.

stories.title: Deported to Eswatini: Cambodian refugee questions controversial US policy
stories.summary: Pheap Rom, a Cambodian refugee who held U.S. permanent resident status since 1985, was deported and is now detained in Eswatini, raising questions about controversial U.S. deportation policies.

stories.title: Nato briefed that Trump wants immediate commitments from allies to secure Hormuz
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte briefed member states that the US wants concrete commitments within days to help secure the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump had expressed frustration with NATO over insufficient support in the Iran war.

stories.title: Africa: Afreximbank Supports Dangote Group As It Targets U.S.$100 Billion Annual Revenue By 2030
stories.summary: Afreximbank announced its support for the Dangote Group as the Nigerian conglomerate aims to expand operations and grow its annual revenue to $100 billion by 2030.

stories.title: Ukraine's parliament forms commission to probe actions threatening economic security
stories.summary: Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada passed a resolution establishing a temporary investigation commission to probe actions by officials that may threaten the country's economic security.

stories.title: Pentagon’s ouster of Anthropic opens doors for small AI rivals
stories.summary: The Pentagon's removal of Anthropic from defense AI contracts has created opportunities for smaller artificial intelligence startups in the defense sector. These companies are now receiving interest from military generals, combatant commanders, and major investors.

stories.title: Is the world economy heading towards stagflation?
stories.summary: Economists are debating whether the global economy is heading toward stagflation, a combination of stagnant growth and rising inflation.

stories.title: Israeli settlers storm Al-Aqsa Mosque compound after reopening
stories.summary: Israeli settlers entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem shortly after the site reopened following an extended closure.

stories.title: Did Israel attack Lebanon to spoil Iran war ceasefire?
stories.summary: Israel launched large-scale strikes on densely populated areas in Lebanon, killing more than 200 people. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed the attacks targeted Hezbollah members. The strikes drew widespread international condemnation and raised questions about whether they were intended to undermine ceasefire negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: Iran’s engagement removed doubts about Vance’s participation in Islamabad talks
stories.summary: The White House confirmed Vice President JD Vance's participation in US-Iran talks in Islamabad after Iran signaled its willingness to engage directly at the highest diplomatic level. President Trump had initially suggested Vance might not travel due to security concerns before the announcement was reversed.

stories.title: What is Iran’s Strait of Hormuz protocol and will other nations accept it?
stories.summary: Iran announced plans to impose a tax on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to fund reconstruction efforts. The proposal has already drawn international pushback from other nations.

stories.title: The economic cost of US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Analysis focuses on the economic costs of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran and its broader financial impact.

stories.title: Russian troop activity is particularly high: Syrskyi visits Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi visited the Pokrovsk sector, where Russian troop activity has been particularly high. Ukrainian defense forces repelled 260 Russian attacks in that sector over the past week.

stories.title: Michigan Democrats, Jewish leaders uneasy over Senate candidate’s alliance with Hasan Piker
stories.summary: Michigan Democratic leaders and Jewish community figures expressed concern over Senate candidate Abdul el-Sayed's alliance with streamer Hasan Piker, who held rallies at two Michigan universities, deepening divisions over radical voices in US politics.

stories.title: NTV pundit says he left Russia after FSB agents threatened him at home
stories.summary: Victor Olevich, a political analyst who appeared as an American affairs expert on Russia's state-controlled NTV channel, said he fled Russia after FSB agents threatened him at his home. He disclosed the incident on Facebook.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in Pakistan: Who’s attending, what’s on the agenda?
stories.summary: The US and Iran are holding negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, seeking a diplomatic off-ramp to the conflict. Deep mutual mistrust and regional tensions threaten to undermine the talks.

stories.title: Russian lawmakers say Telegram ban makes it harder to communicate with constituents
stories.summary: Russian lawmakers from several parties told the business daily Vedomosti that a ban on Telegram is hindering their ability to communicate with constituents and fellow party members.

stories.title: Has US achieved its war objectives in Iran?
stories.summary: The United States entered its conflict with Iran with key objectives of preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and degrading its military arsenal. Analysis examines whether those goals have been met.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran war widens rift with European nationalists once viewed as MAGA allies
stories.summary: The US-led war on Iran has widened a rift between the Trump administration and European nationalist leaders. Italy's Giorgia Meloni refused to allow US use of an air base for Iran strikes, and France's Marine Le Pen criticized the war's goals as erratic.

stories.title: UK to call for toll-free Strait of Hormuz, wants Lebanon in ceasefire deal
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper plans to call for toll-free shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, opposing Iran's push to control the waterway. Cooper also stated that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Lebanese govt bans non-state weapons in capital Beirut
stories.summary: The Lebanese government ordered security forces to restrict weapons in Beirut to state control, reinforcing a ban on Hezbollah's armed presence in the capital. The decision came after Israeli strikes on the city.

stories.title: As US and Iran talk truce, Israel digs in for a ‘forever war’
stories.summary: Israel is reportedly seizing additional territory from neighboring states as it prepares for an extended conflict, even as the United States and Iran pursue truce negotiations.

stories.title: Iran announces alternative routes for ships travelling through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran announced alternative shipping routes for vessels traveling through the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran had effectively blocked the critical waterway since early March, causing global energy prices to spike.

stories.title: The deadliest 10 minutes in decades: Lebanese reel from Israeli strikes that killed hundreds
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck over 100 targets across Lebanon in approximately 10 minutes, killing hundreds in one of the deadliest attacks since Lebanon's civil war ended in 1990. Beirut residents, including those in the central Barbour neighbourhood, described buildings destroyed by bombs. Lebanese officials said civilians were the primary casualties.

stories.title: China sidelined: EU shelves rare strategy debate as Middle East crisis takes priority
stories.summary: The European Commission postponed a scheduled strategic debate on China, originally planned as part of an internal "China week," to focus on the escalating Middle East crisis. The meeting would have been the first discussion on Beijing among all 27 EU commissioners under the current leadership.

stories.title: China’s yuan settlements hit record, and the Iran conflict is looking like a catalyst
stories.summary: Transactions through China's Cross-border Interbank Payment System have reached record levels, with analysts attributing the surge partly to rising demand for yuan settlement in oil trade amid Middle East tensions. Standard Chartered's chief economist for Greater China called the conflict a catalyst for the trend.

stories.title: Israeli arrested in Iranian plot to assassinate former PM Naftali Bennett
stories.summary: Israeli authorities arrested a 22-year-old Israeli citizen suspected of involvement in an Iranian plot to assassinate former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett. The suspect was allegedly tasked with gathering intelligence, including photographing the Haifa port and missile impact sites.

stories.title: Lebanon Latest: Israel kills hundreds in one day
stories.summary: Israel launched a wave of air strikes across Lebanon killing hundreds of people in a single day, despite an active US-Iran ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Philippines unveils new coast guard command in disputed South China Sea
stories.summary: The Philippines unveiled a new coast guard command in the disputed South China Sea. The newly established district headquarters, previously overseen from Palawan, will cover approximately 68,000 square kilometers of contested waters.

stories.title: US asks allies to pitch plans within days to secure Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States asked allied nations to submit plans within days for securing the Strait of Hormuz. The request was made during discussions between American and NATO officials at the White House.

stories.title: More than 250 people killed in Israel’s largest airstrike on Lebanon — Reuters
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out their most extensive airstrikes on Lebanon since the start of the war with Hezbollah, killing at least 254 people and wounding more than 1,100 others, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Dollar struggles to rebound amid fragile US-Iran truce
stories.summary: Currency markets remained cautious as a fragile U.S.-Iran truce and ongoing Israel-Hezbollah tensions weighed on investor sentiment. The U.S. dollar struggled to recover, with the Japanese yen also affected by the uncertainty.

stories.title: Israel’s deadly strikes in Lebanon spark outrage, condemnation from rights bodies
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on densely populated areas across Lebanon drew condemnation from international humanitarian organizations. The International Committee of the Red Cross expressed outrage at the widespread death and destruction caused by the attacks.

stories.title: China throws the switch on battery buildout ‘equal to 10 times US capacity in 2025’
stories.summary: Major Chinese battery manufacturers, including CATL and Gotion High-tech, announced plans to add over 600 gigawatt-hours of new energy storage production capacity in early 2026. That figure represents roughly ten times the total installed capacity across the United States in 2025.

stories.title: Retirement age rising in Ukraine as labor market increasingly relies on pensioners – lawmaker
stories.summary: Ukraine's retirement age is effectively rising due to stricter insurance record requirements and labor market shifts driven by the ongoing war. Labor shortages have led to a growing reliance on working pensioners, according to a Ukrainian lawmaker.

stories.title: Lebanon's civilian population caught in Israel-Hezbollah conflict with no exit - analysis
stories.summary: Lebanese civilians remain caught between Israeli strikes and Hezbollah activity, with Lebanon excluded from the US-Iran ceasefire. Displaced residents face continued vulnerability with no clear path to safety or resolution.

stories.title: What to know about the Strait of Hormuz under the ceasefire
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains uncertain despite the US-Iran ceasefire announcement. The fragility of the truce has been the primary reason vessels are holding back from transiting the waterway.

stories.title: China’s role in the Iran-US ceasefire reflects its strategic distance
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran was announced on April 7, brokered through Pakistani mediators after Iran delivered a 10-point proposal. Iranian officials credited a last-minute intervention by China for securing Tehran's acceptance of the deal.

stories.title: First Thing: Ceasefire in peril as Israel assaults Lebanon and Iran blocks oil tankers
stories.summary: The two-week ceasefire in the Iran conflict faced collapse as Iran and mediator Pakistan insisted it covered Lebanon, while Israel and the United States disagreed. Israel intensified bombing in Lebanon, and Iran halted the passage of oil tankers through the Gulf, citing alleged Israeli ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Researchers propose ‘rewilding’ Europe’s borderlands to repel enemies
stories.summary: A new report proposes restoring wetlands and peat bogs along Europe's border regions to serve as natural barriers against potential military incursions. Researchers say the "rewilding" approach could simultaneously bolster defense and contribute to climate resilience.

stories.title: Donald Trump blasts NATO after closed-door meeting with Mark Rutte
stories.summary: President Donald Trump criticized NATO allies during a closed-door meeting with Secretary General Mark Rutte over their refusal to support the US war against Iran. The confrontation raised concerns that Trump might seek to withdraw the United States from the nearly eight-decade-old alliance.

stories.title: Africa: Afreximbank Delivers Strong FY2025 Results - With Total Assets And Contingencies Base Of Us$48.5 Billion
stories.summary: The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) reported strong financial results for fiscal year 2025, with total assets and contingencies reaching $48.5 billion.

stories.title: Trump says US military to stay around Iran, threatens action if Tehran fails to comply with deal
stories.summary: President Trump declared on Truth Social that the US military would remain deployed near Iran, threatening action if Tehran fails to comply with their deal. Iran responded that it would be "unreasonable" to proceed with talks after Israel's strikes on Lebanon on April 8.

stories.title: Haifa man suspected of making explosives to ‘harm’ ex-PM Bennett on Iranian orders
stories.summary: Israeli security services arrested a 22-year-old man from Haifa on suspicion of manufacturing and testing explosives intended to harm former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett. The suspect allegedly acted on Iranian orders, receiving payment and recruiting three accomplices.

stories.title: Summer school programs to be extended after weeks of wartime closures
stories.summary: Israel's Education Ministry announced that summer school programs for elementary students will be extended by three weeks and expanded through sixth grade. The move follows weeks of wartime school closures, with a separate catch-up plan for middle school students to address learning gaps caused by the Iran conflict.

stories.title: EU should join forces with Ukraine and others to create military bloc to deter Russia, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on the EU to form a military bloc with Ukraine and other nations to deter Russia, citing concerns over potential U.S. withdrawal from NATO.

stories.title: Global energy crisis is ‘the mother of all crises’: Turkish energy minister
stories.summary: Turkey's energy minister told Al Jazeera that the global energy crisis is the most significant of current crises, highlighting Turkey's role as a regional energy hub due to its geographic location and investments.

stories.title: UN chief warns Israeli strikes on Lebanon pose ‘grave risk’ to US-Iran truce: Spokesman
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General warned that Israeli strikes on Lebanon pose a "grave risk" to the US-Iran truce. Lebanon's health ministry reported 182 deaths and 890 wounded from Israeli strikes on April 8.

stories.title: Trump threatens to resume Iran war, throws ceasefire into chaos
stories.summary: Trump administration officials contested elements of the ceasefire with Iran, including whether the truce extends to Lebanon, where Israeli strikes killed more than 250 people on Wednesday. The disputes have thrown the ceasefire's scope into question.

stories.title: Fury vs Makhmudov: All you need to know about the heavyweight boxing bout
stories.summary: Tyson Fury announced his return from retirement to face heavyweight Arslanbek Makhmudov in a bout scheduled at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.

stories.title: Track current petrol and diesel prices, service station outages and shipments – Australia's fuel crisis in charts
stories.summary: Australia is experiencing a fuel crisis driven by Iran's continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz, with hundreds of service stations running empty and prices rising sharply. The federal government has released fuel reserves and cut excise taxes in response to supply disruptions.

stories.title: Rising oil prices: Are we heading for a recession?
stories.summary: Crude oil prices continued rising on Thursday amid signs that the US-Iran ceasefire is fragile. Economist Ilian Mihov of INSEAD warned that supply shortages from the conflict could affect economic activity more severely than price increases alone, and that central banks face difficult policy calculations regarding a potential global recession.

stories.title: FSB Arrests Former Radio Liberty Reporter in Far East Russia
stories.summary: Russia's FSB arrested a former Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reporter in the country's Far East. Local and independent media identified the detained man as Alexander Andreyev.

stories.title: Kenya disputes UN report on rape allegations against its Haiti personnel
stories.summary: Kenya's foreign minister disputed a United Nations report alleging that Kenyan personnel deployed in Haiti committed acts of rape involving children, stating that the accusations were investigated and found to be unsubstantiated.

stories.title: Russia sees China's WeChat, Douyin as models for its homegrown Max messenger
stories.summary: Russia is looking to China's WeChat and Douyin platforms as models for developing its domestic Max messenger application. The Kremlin views a platform economy integrating e-commerce and banking services as a key tool for stimulating its slowing economic growth.

stories.title: Why US-Iran truce may not end high airfares and flight disruptions
stories.summary: Airlines have largely halted flights in the Gulf region following six weeks of conflict in the Middle East, with Air France extending suspensions until May 3. Despite the US-Iran ceasefire, elevated fuel costs and route disruptions are expected to keep airfares high and schedules uncertain.

stories.title: China deploys new battlefield AI in command tent. It outsmarts everyone
stories.summary: China's military has reportedly deployed an artificial intelligence agent designed to assist battalion-level commanders during operations. The AI system was tested in a simulated amphibious assault scenario, where it demonstrated the ability to process battlefield information faster than human counterparts.

stories.title: Aftermath of Russian strikes on Balabyne in Zaporizhzhia: School and more than 100 houses damaged
stories.summary: On the morning of April 9, Russian forces struck settlements in the Kushuhum community of Zaporizhzhia district, damaging a school identified as the Prestige educational institution and more than 100 residential buildings in the village of Balabyne.

stories.title: In pictures: Hundreds gather as Al Aqsa Mosque reopens after weeks-long shutdown
stories.summary: Al Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem reopened on Thursday after a 40-day closure imposed by Israel. Hundreds of Palestinian Muslim worshippers entered the Al-Haram al-Sharif compound at dawn, with many visibly emotional as they returned to the holy site.

stories.title: Funeral held for Al Jazeera’s Wishah killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: A funeral was held in Gaza for Al Jazeera journalist Mohammed Wishah, killed in an Israeli strike. More than 260 journalists have been killed by Israel in Gaza since October 2023.

stories.title: Italy working to restore freedom of navigation in Hormuz: Meloni
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated that Italy is working to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it vital for European Union trade. Meloni urged restraint regarding Iran and ruled out early Italian elections.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Lebanon 'grave violation' of ceasefire, Iran minister tells BBC
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister told the BBC that Israeli strikes in Lebanon constitute a grave violation of the ceasefire, urging the US to choose between pursuing war or honoring the truce.

stories.title: Iran estimates war losses at up to $145 billion after weeks of fighting
stories.summary: Iran estimated its total war losses at up to $145 billion following weeks of fighting with the US and Israel. Open-source intelligence assessments point to heavy military damage, significant casualties, and widespread economic disruption.

stories.title: Millions vote in Assam, Kerala as India begins series of state elections
stories.summary: Millions of voters cast ballots in state elections in Assam and Kerala, the first of four key Indian state contests scheduled for the month. The elections are being watched as a gauge of public sentiment toward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling coalition amid Middle East conflict-related fuel pressures.

stories.title: Russia's oil revenues hit highest level since 2022 – media
stories.summary: Russia's oil export revenues have reached their highest level since June 2022, driven by rising global oil prices and increased shipment volumes, according to media reports.

stories.title: Al Jazeera condemns killing of journalist in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: Al Jazeera condemned the killing of its journalist Mohammed Wishah in an Israeli strike in Gaza. The Israeli military claimed Wishah was a Hamas operative, an allegation the Qatar-based network has denied.

stories.title: Hamada ElKept brings Gaza's sleepless reality to the world
stories.summary: Palestinian artist Hamada ElKept discussed his work exploring themes of displacement, survival, and the loss of everyday life in Gaza. His art aims to convey the daily reality facing Gaza's population to international audiences.

stories.title: Tanzania: MPs Push for Fuel Tax Relief
stories.summary: Members of Parliament in Tanzania urged the government in Dodoma to reduce levies on fuel imports to address rising fuel prices worsened by the ongoing Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Zelensky: US ignores evidence that Russia helps Iran strike American bases in Middle East
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the United States is ignoring evidence that Russia is assisting Iran in striking American military bases in the Middle East, alleging Washington places undue trust in Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 9 – All sides claim war victory. They can’t all be right
stories.summary: Times of Israel editor David Horovitz analyzed the current cessation of hostilities in a daily briefing, examining how multiple parties in the conflict each claim victory. The briefing explored the events leading to the ceasefire and potential next steps for the involved sides.

stories.title: Police hunting man who stole 2 Pokemon cards worth HK$250,000 from store
stories.summary: Hong Kong police are searching for a man who stole two rare Pokémon trading cards valued at a combined HK$250,000 (US$31,917) from Light TCG, a shop on Granville Road in Tsim Sha Tsui. The suspect posed as a customer, grabbed the cards, and fled toward Chatham Road South.

stories.title: Nova Poshta branch destroyed by drone attack in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: A Nova Poshta postal branch in the village of Novomykolaivka, Zaporizhzhia region, was destroyed overnight by a Russian strike drone. No casualties were reported in the attack.

stories.title: Lebanon declares national day of mourning after Israel kills 203
stories.summary: Lebanon declared a national day of mourning after Israeli strikes killed 203 people. Egypt, Italy, Qatar, and other countries denounced the attacks, while Iran insisted that any ceasefire must also cover Lebanon.

stories.title: IMF strikes staff-level deal with Sri Lanka on $700 million in funding
stories.summary: The IMF reached a staff-level agreement with Sri Lanka on approximately $700 million in funding, acknowledging the country's economic reforms while noting its significant exposure to the effects of the Iran war.

stories.title: 'Sheer terror rained from the sky': Arab Reform Initiative Executive Director Nadim Houry
stories.summary: Arab Reform Initiative Executive Director Nadim Houry described the chaos during Israel's strikes on Beirut, where approximately 100 targets were hit in just ten minutes. Houry said the attacks on Lebanon could stop immediately if President Trump pressured Prime Minister Netanyahu by threatening to cut US weapons supplies to Israel.

stories.title: 36 hours of chaos: The scramble for a ceasefire in Iran
stories.summary: A fragile two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran was reached after 36 hours of intensive negotiations. President Trump had set a deadline threatening strikes if Iran did not reopen navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: IDF says it killed Hezbollah chief’s secretary as some 70 rockets fired from Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced it killed a secretary to the Hezbollah chief as approximately 70 rockets were fired from Lebanon toward Israeli border towns. No injuries or damage were reported. The IDF stated that some 3,000 projectiles have been launched from southern Lebanon since March 2, accusing Beirut of failing to disarm Hezbollah.

stories.title: China tankers join line to test Hormuz exit and US-Iran truce
stories.summary: Chinese tankers have joined a line of vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz to test the US-Iran truce. A successful crossing is not yet guaranteed, as several ships have turned back at the last moment.

stories.title: EU aviation regulator extends warning to avoid Middle East airspace until 24 April
stories.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency extended its advisory for airlines to avoid Middle Eastern and Gulf airspace until 24 April. The warning was previously set to expire on 10 April and was updated due to ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: Thousands of Iranians rally in memory of late supreme leader Khamenei
stories.summary: Thousands of Iranians rallied across multiple cities, including Tehran, Urmia, and Gorgan, to pay tribute to the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Khamenei was killed in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Iran war after ruling for nearly four decades.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says U.S. military to stay deployed near Iran until 'real agreement' reached
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire showed signs of unravelling as Israel bombarded Lebanon and Washington contradicted some of Iran's conditions for ending the war. President Trump announced that US military forces would remain deployed near Iran until a formal agreement is reached.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages reported in five regions due to enemy attacks
stories.summary: As of the morning of April 9, power outages caused by enemy strikes and artillery shelling affected electricity users across five regions of Ukraine, according to grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: Man arrested in Greece over plot to kill Russian activist and political adviser in Lithuania
stories.summary: A 55-year-old man suspected of orchestrating a plot to kill a Russian activist and political adviser in Lithuania was arrested in Thessaloniki, Greece, according to the Lithuanian outlet Delfi.

stories.title: High Court asked to enforce return order in Ras Ein al-Auja case after state misses deadline
stories.summary: Petitioners have asked Israel's High Court of Justice to enforce its ruling in the Ras Ein al-Auja case after the state missed a court-imposed deadline to report on measures enabling displaced residents to return to the area.

stories.title: Spain reopens Iran embassy amid criticism of Lebanon strikes
stories.summary: Spain reopened its embassy in Tehran and condemned Israeli strikes on Lebanon as illegal. The Spanish government called for peace amid rising tensions across the Middle East.

stories.title: Cannes 2026 Palme d’Or picks include Iran’s Farhadi, Spain’s Almodovar
stories.summary: The 2026 Cannes Film Festival announced 21 directors competing for the Palme d'Or, including Iran's Asghar Farhadi and Spain's Pedro Almodóvar. Major Hollywood studios are expected to be largely absent from the festival on the French Riviera in May.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone forces destroy 9th Tor-M1 in 9 days in occupied Donetsk Oblast
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone units destroyed a ninth Russian Tor-M1 air defense system in occupied Donetsk Oblast over a nine-day period. Ukraine's Special Forces command identified the Tor-M1 as a priority target because Russia uses it to protect frontline positions.

stories.title: A day in the life of a 19-year-old in ICE detention: ‘I feel that this nightmare is not going to end’
stories.summary: A 19-year-old asylum seeker from the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been detained at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas for over four months. She has reportedly lost 20 pounds and suffers daily headaches while awaiting resolution of her case.

stories.title: Man charged with US firebomb plot is linked to group whose leaders back violence against Palestinians
stories.summary: A man charged with plotting to firebomb a pro-Palestine activist's home in the United States has been linked to the JDL 613 Brotherhood. The group's leaders have voiced support for violence against Palestinians and platformed a convicted terrorist who fundraises for a violent settler movement in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Taiwan should learn from mainland AI, KMT head Cheng Li-wun says
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun visited the Shanghai headquarters of Meituan during a trip to mainland China, where she met CEO Wang Xing. Cheng stated that Taiwan could learn from how the mainland applies artificial intelligence, particularly in platforms like Meituan's delivery and services operations.

stories.title: Nepal issues arrest warrant for former PM Deuba in graft probe
stories.summary: Nepal has issued an arrest warrant for former Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba in a corruption probe. This follows the earlier arrests of former PM K.P. Sharma Oli and ex-Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak over the deadly crackdown on anti-corruption protests in September.

stories.title: Indonesian activists target Myanmar’s president in genocide case against him
stories.summary: Indonesian human rights activists filed a genocide complaint with Indonesia's Attorney General's Office against Myanmar's newly elected President Min Aung Hlaing. The complaint accuses the former military chief of genocide against the Rohingya, including mass rape, forced eviction, killings, and arson.

stories.title: Trump’s abrupt Iran reversal exposes limits of his leverage
stories.summary: President Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran, stepping back from threats against the country after a 40-day war that disrupted global energy markets. Critics questioned the effectiveness of his negotiating approach, while Trump claimed victory despite unresolved tensions.

stories.title: Why Israel’s attacks on Lebanon could cripple US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire faces strain as the US and Israel excluded Lebanon from the agreement, with Israeli strikes on Lebanon raising fears of broader regional conflict.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon leave more than 200 dead and 1,000 wounded
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on Beirut, Tyre, and the southern village of Abbassiyeh in Lebanon killed at least 203 people and wounded more than 1,000, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The overall death toll from Israeli attacks since early March has surpassed 1,500.

stories.title: Drone Debris Kills Man in Village Near Novorossiysk
stories.summary: Falling drone debris killed a man in a village near Novorossiysk in Russia's Krasnodar region. Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 69 Ukrainian drones across multiple regions between Monday night and Tuesday morning.

stories.title: Russian forces fired on Chernihiv region 32 times over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the Chernihiv region 32 times over the 24-hour period on April 8, resulting in 42 reported explosions across the area.

stories.title: US court expedites Anthropic’s legal battle with Department of War
stories.summary: A US court expedited Anthropic's legal battle with the Department of War after the Pentagon labeled the AI startup a supply chain risk. Anthropic had sought a stay of action in the case.

stories.title: More than 3,000 Iranians killed during war, medical body says
stories.summary: Iran's forensic authority reported that more than 3,000 people have been killed across the country since the war began on 28 February. Officials said 40 percent of the dead required forensic work for identification.

stories.title: Sudan: Prime Minister Reaffirms Government of Hope's Commitment to Strengthening Civilian Protection
stories.summary: Sudan's Prime Minister Kamil Idris reaffirmed the Government of Hope's commitment to strengthening the protection of civilians amid the country's ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Hamas operative posing as journalist killed in Gaza strike, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it killed Muhammad Samir Muhammad Washah in a strike in Gaza, identifying him as a Hamas operative posing as a journalist. The IDF described him as a key figure in Hamas's rocket and weapons production operations.

stories.title: Russia’s FSB detains former RFE/RL correspondent on treason charges
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service detained a resident of Chita on suspicion of treason, identifying the suspect as a former freelance correspondent for Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty's Russian service, according to state news agency TASS.

stories.title: No let-up in Israeli attacks on Lebanon as US-Iran ceasefire teeters
stories.summary: Israel bombed targets in Lebanon on Thursday, killing more than 250 people in the largest Israeli strikes of the war, threatening the US-Iran ceasefire. In Islamabad, Pakistan, authorities locked down areas around the Serena Hotel ahead of anticipated peace talks between American and Iranian delegations.

stories.title: DeCarlos Brown Jr, alleged killer of Ukrainian refugee in US, ruled incompetent to stand trial
stories.summary: DeCarlos Brown Jr, the alleged killer of a Ukrainian refugee in the United States, has been ruled incompetent to stand trial. The August 2025 murder case became a political rallying point for the US right wing.

stories.title: France calls Hungary a traitor as recordings reveal Szijjártó fed Lavrov closed EU summit intel
stories.summary: France accused Hungary of betrayal after recordings emerged showing Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó sharing closed EU summit intelligence with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Szijjártó allegedly offered to transmit EU documents via Hungary's embassy in Moscow and coordinated efforts to obstruct sanctions.

stories.title: Drones attack oil pipeline facility in Krasnodar region, Russia
stories.summary: On the night of April 9, drones attacked the Krymskaya Line Production and Dispatch Station, a key oil pipeline facility in Russia's Krasnodar region.

stories.title: Israeli military kills young man and child in Gaza
stories.summary: The Israeli military shot and killed a young man in Khan Younis and a child named Ritaj Abdul Raouf Rihan in Beit Lahia in the northern Gaza Strip on Thursday. The child was reportedly attending classes inside a school tent when she was killed.

stories.title: White House knew about Pakistan’s ceasefire post on X before it was sent
stories.summary: The White House had reviewed and approved Pakistan's social media post about the ceasefire on X before it was published. Behind-the-scenes coordination preceded the public announcement.

stories.title: The ten minutes that shook Beirut: Israel's massacre in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes struck Beirut within a span of minutes, killing more than 250 people and overwhelming hospitals. The attack marked the deadliest single day in Lebanon since the Israeli military campaign began.

stories.title: Polisario Front celebrates 50 years of Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic
stories.summary: The Polisario Front marked the 50th anniversary of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic with a military parade held in a refugee camp near Tindouf, Algeria, reaffirming Western Sahara's independence movement.

stories.title: The Strait of Hormuz is closed again. Could the Iran-US truce fail at any moment?
stories.summary: Iran reclosed the Strait of Hormuz, straining the fragile ceasefire agreed with the United States just days earlier. Analysts said the move would not necessarily trigger renewed war, but noted that Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon remained a destabilizing wildcard.

stories.title: US to remain key ally of Asean despite Iran war fallout: diplomat
stories.summary: Former U.S. diplomat Ambassador Daniel Kritenbrink argued that the United States remains a dependable ally and central partner for Southeast Asian nations despite the economic fallout from the Iran war. Energy-importing ASEAN economies have been severely affected by the conflict's disruption to Middle Eastern oil supplies.

stories.title: NASA’s lunar success sharpens focus on China’s 2030 crewed landing goal
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission sent four astronauts past the moon's far side, setting a new deep-space record and advancing plans for a 2028 lunar landing. The achievement has intensified focus on China's goal of landing astronauts on the moon by 2030.

stories.title: US-Iran truce should extend to Lebanon, EU's top diplomat says
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called for the US-Iran ceasefire to be extended to Lebanon and urged Hezbollah to disarm. Kallas said Israeli strikes that killed hundreds in Lebanon were putting the truce under severe strain.

stories.title: German AfD party will expel from its ranks a Chechen who advocates for Germany’s “unity” with Russia
stories.summary: Germany's AfD party announced plans to expel Chechen-born influencer Murad Dadaev after reports surfaced that he met officials linked to Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, trained with a Kalashnikov, and gifted a Wehrmacht swastika dagger during a trip to Chechnya.

stories.title: US Army veteran charged with leaking classified information to journalist
stories.summary: A US Army veteran has been charged with leaking classified information to a journalist. The leaked material was used for a book alleging drug trafficking, murder, and corruption at a military base.

stories.title: Trump’s administration trying to sell war ‘wins’ to a sceptical US public
stories.summary: The Trump administration is attempting to present the war with Iran as a success, but faces skepticism from the American public regarding the conflict's outcomes.

stories.title: Iran’s economy was weak before the war, now it’s worse
stories.summary: Iran's economy, already weakened before the war, has deteriorated further amid the conflict. The central bank introduced a new 10-million rial banknote in mid-March as a sign of galloping inflation.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia, killing 1 person
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Krasnodar region overnight on April 9, killing one person, according to regional governor Veniamin Kondratiev.

stories.title: Russians launch more than 100 strikes on Sumy region; one woman injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched over 100 strikes on 36 settlements across 18 territorial communities in Ukraine's Sumy region between the mornings of April 8 and April 9. One woman was reported injured.

stories.title: Iran cannot ‘hijack’ strait of Hormuz with shipping tolls, says Yvette Cooper – UK politics live
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper stated that Iran cannot impose shipping tolls on the Strait of Hormuz, calling it an international transit route protected by the law of the sea. She declined to confirm reports of a Russian warship escorting sanctioned Russian vessels through the English Channel.

stories.title: Ugandan man admits 'human sacrifice' kindergarten stabbings
stories.summary: A man in Uganda has admitted to killing four young children in a stabbing attack at a kindergarten, describing it as a "human sacrifice." The attack has shocked the nation.

stories.title: Bitten by snakes 200 times – on purpose: US man’s quest to help deliver new antivenom
stories.summary: Tim Friede, a 58-year-old American, has subjected himself to approximately 200 intentional venomous snakebites over nearly 20 years to build immunity that could help develop a universal antivenom. His efforts aim to address rising snakebite deaths, which researchers link partly to climate change increasing human-snake encounters.

stories.title: China authorities probe ‘national-level bullying’ of diving icon Quan Hongchan amid toxic fan culture
stories.summary: Chinese authorities launched a major investigation into organized cyberbullying targeting Olympic diving champion Quan Hongchan. The probe follows malicious online attacks that included derogatory comments about her appearance and questioned her championship legitimacy.

stories.title: Four people die in Channel small-boat sinking
stories.summary: Four people — two men and two women — died after a small migrant boat sank in the English Channel off the coast of Boulogne, France. The victims were swept away by strong currents while attempting to board a dinghy. At least 42 others were rescued.

stories.title: Saudi and Iranian foreign ministers hold first call since start of war
stories.summary: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan held a phone call with Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi, marking the first official contact between the two countries since Iran struck Gulf neighbours in retaliation for US-Israeli attacks. The call focused on de-escalation efforts.

stories.title: Alarm raised over outbreak of mpox in Khairpur
stories.summary: Experts at Karachi's Aga Khan University Hospital raised alarm over an mpox outbreak in Khairpur, Sindh, where seven newborn babies were confirmed infected and four died. They urged healthcare providers and policymakers to treat the outbreak as an immediate public health concern.

stories.title: Iran-linked hackers leak photos of ex-IDF chief Halevi’s work and family life
stories.summary: An Iran-linked hacking group called Handala claimed to have obtained 19,000 confidential images and videos from former IDF chief Halevi. The leaked materials reportedly include footage from previously undisclosed meetings as well as personal family photos.

stories.title: 'Ketamine Queen' sentenced to 15 years in death of 'Friends' star Matthew Perry
stories.summary: Jasveen Sangha, dubbed the "Ketamine Queen," was sentenced to 15 years in prison in Los Angeles for her role in supplying the ketamine dose that killed actor Matthew Perry in 2023. Sangha had pleaded guilty to five felony drug counts after admitting to running an illegal narcotics operation from her North Hollywood home.

stories.title: Russia building a 165,000-strong drone army. We cannot afford to stop — Syrskyi says
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi stated that Ukrainian drone units have neutralized more Russian personnel than Moscow has recruited for four consecutive months. Intelligence data indicates Russia aims to build a 165,000-strong drone force, tripling its unmanned troop numbers by year's end.

stories.title: Facts vs. influencers: Is the 'Dubai dream' really over?
stories.summary: Debate has emerged among Dubai residents over the impact of the Iran war on life in the emirate. Some insist daily life continues normally, while others claim the so-called "Dubai dream" has ended. The reality remains contested.

stories.title: Commuters in Karachi pay grudgingly as govt’s call to freeze fares ignored
stories.summary: Public transport commuters in Karachi continue to pay inflated fares despite a Sindh government directive to freeze prices in exchange for a fuel subsidy. Bus owners and operators of minibuses, rickshaws, and other vehicles have widely ignored the order amid optimism over potential fuel price reductions following the US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Chart shows Iran may have put sea mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Semiofficial Iranian news agencies ISNA and Tasnim published a chart suggesting Iran's Revolutionary Guard placed sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz during the conflict. The release appears intended to pressure the United States as the two-week ceasefire remains uncertain and further negotiations are expected in Pakistan.

stories.title: US-Iran truce hangs in balance as war flares in Lebanon
stories.summary: The two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran faced immediate strain as Israel launched a major bombardment of Lebanon, killing at least 182 people and wounding nearly 900. Tehran threatened to resume hostilities, while Israel maintained its operations against Hezbollah were separate from the truce.

stories.title: Pentagon called in Vatican’s top US diplomat over Pope’s anti-war remarks, media reports
stories.summary: The Pentagon summoned the Vatican's top U.S. envoy over anti-war remarks made by Pope Leo XIV. Sources described the meeting as a "bitter lecture" directed at the papal representative.

stories.title: US–Iran ceasefire: Has Iran’s regime emerged weakened or reinforced?
stories.summary: Following the US-Iran ceasefire, both President Trump and Iran claimed victory after approximately 40 days of war. Iran sustained significant damage to its infrastructure and military capabilities, raising questions about whether the regime has been weakened or reinforced by the conflict.

stories.title: 'We are not broken': French nationals freed from Iran welcomed by President Macron
stories.summary: Two French nationals detained in Iran were freed and received by President Emmanuel Macron at the Elysée Palace in Paris on Wednesday.

stories.title: Major automakers unveil new electric vehicles at NYC International Auto Show
stories.summary: Major automakers showcased new electric vehicles at the New York International Auto Show. The ongoing Middle East conflict has boosted consumer interest in EVs, with automakers reporting rising sales in early 2026.

stories.title: Israel's pounding of Lebanon is 'deeply damaging', UK foreign minister says
stories.summary: UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper called Israel's strikes on Lebanon "deeply damaging." French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot also condemned the "massive strikes" and insisted Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Tehran residents welcome ceasefire but voice concerns
stories.summary: Residents in Tehran welcomed the two-week ceasefire agreement reached with the United States after roughly 40 days of conflict but expressed concerns about its durability. The US and Iran have committed to beginning peace consultations in Islamabad, Pakistan.

stories.title: Netanyahu faces mounting criticism as Israel’s war goals in Iran remain unmet
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces growing domestic criticism after failing to achieve stated war goals against Iran, including regime change and halting uranium enrichment. International opinion of Israel has declined further, with a majority of Americans now holding a negative view of the country.

stories.title: Israel reopens Al-Aqsa Mosque as it extends settler raid hours
stories.summary: Israeli authorities reopened Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem after an unprecedented closure lasting more than 40 days. Over 3,000 Palestinian worshippers performed dawn prayers at the site. Israel simultaneously extended hours for settler visits to the compound.

stories.title: Red Zone sealed as capital prepares for high-stakes Iran-US talks
stories.summary: Authorities in Islamabad and Rawalpindi declared two local holidays and sealed the capital's Red Zone ahead of planned US-Iran peace talks. A hotel within the restricted area was reserved for the delegations, and comprehensive security measures were implemented.

stories.title: One person killed and three others injured in Kharkiv region due to Russian strikes
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Kharkiv region, one person was killed and three others were injured over the past 24 hours on April 8 as a result of Russian strikes.

stories.title: IDF kills Hezbollah chief's secretary in Beirut, strikes crossings and weapons sites
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it killed Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem's secretary in a strike on Beirut. The IDF also reported overnight strikes on two key crossings used by Hezbollah to move operatives and weapons across the Litani River.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Beirut kill at least 182 and wound hundreds
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit busy commercial and residential districts in central Beirut late Wednesday, killing at least 182 people and wounding 890, according to Lebanon's health ministry. Rescue crews spent the night searching through rubble for survivors.

stories.title: Israeli military says it killed nephew of Hezbollah chief in Beirut
stories.summary: Israel's military announced it killed Ali Yusuf Harshi in Beirut, identifying him as the nephew and close adviser of Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem. The military claimed Harshi played a central role in managing and securing Qassem's office.

stories.title: Shaky ceasefire unlikely to stop cyberattacks from Iran-linked hackers for long
stories.summary: Cybersecurity analysts warn that the uncertain US-Iran ceasefire is unlikely to halt cyberattacks from Iran-linked hackers for long, as Tehran-allied groups are expected to continue digital operations regardless of the truce's outcome.

stories.title: Energy crisis as catalyst
stories.summary: The article examines how the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israeli war on Iran caused an immediate energy crisis in Pakistan, with petrol prices surging 20 percent and LNG shipments collapsing. It argues the crisis should catalyze Pakistan's long-delayed energy transition.

stories.title: ‘Unacceptable’: European countries slam IDF strikes on Hezbollah amid US-Iran truce
stories.summary: The United Kingdom, France, and Italy condemned Israeli military strikes on Hezbollah targets in Lebanon carried out during the US-Iran truce. The UK called the attacks "deeply troubling," France deemed them "unacceptable," and Italy condemned bombings on civilian populations.

stories.title: Trump says US military to stay deployed near Iran until ‘real agreement’ is reached
stories.summary: President Trump stated that the US military will remain deployed near Iran until a "real agreement" is reached. The fragile truce between Iran and the United States is showing signs of unravelling.

stories.title: France accuses Hungary of ‘betrayal of solidarity’ over leaked call with Russian foreign minister – Europe live
stories.summary: France accused Hungary of a betrayal of solidarity after a leaked call between Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó and Russia's foreign minister revealed an apparent offer to share documents about Ukrainian EU accession. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán rejected claims of close ties to Moscow.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit set for limited trade-focused agenda
stories.summary: The upcoming US-China presidential summit will focus on trade issues rather than investment, according to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Greer cautioned against premature discussions on investment programs, reflecting ongoing reluctance to lift all economic constraints between the two countries.

stories.title: France mulls fallback tank for delayed MGCS program in defense update
stories.summary: France is considering an alternative tank program due to delays in the joint Franco-German Main Ground Combat System (MGCS) project. The delay stems from Germany's decision to pursue development of new Leopard 3 tanks separately.

stories.title: Will Philippine ex-president Duterte stand trial at the ICC, and for how long?
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court is expected to decide by April 28 whether former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte will stand trial on charges of crimes against humanity related to his war on drugs. Observers predict proceedings could take years even if the trial moves forward. Duterte was surrendered to the ICC in March.

stories.title: Several people reported killed in fresh Israeli attacks on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed multiple people, with Israel claiming it killed a close aide to Hezbollah's leader. The attacks threatened the fragile US-Iran truce and placed Lebanon under severe strain.

stories.title: The war on Iran: Nobody won, everyone paid
stories.summary: Analysts assess that the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran failed to achieve its stated objectives. Iran sustained significant damage, while Gulf states also bore substantial economic costs from the conflict.

stories.title: Can global supply chains recover from the Iran war?
stories.summary: The war involving Iran has disrupted global supply chains, particularly affecting the flow of critical raw materials used in manufacturing, aviation, and technology sectors.

stories.title: War and peace
stories.summary: The opinion piece celebrates Pakistan's role in brokering the US-Iran ceasefire, describing it as a historic diplomatic achievement that came after President Trump threatened to destroy Iranian civilization if his deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was not met.

stories.title: Russians injure six residents of Donetsk region
stories.summary: Russian strikes injured six residents of Ukraine's Donetsk region over a 24-hour period on April 8, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Who can claim victory if Iran ceasefire holds? An early winner is China
stories.summary: China is being credited with helping persuade Iran to agree to the ceasefire deal announced by the US and Iran. Beijing's role as a mediator has bolstered its status as a regional diplomatic power, though analysts note Iran was already inclined toward the agreement.

stories.title: Iran's Jews: Israel strike of synagogue attack on 'anti-Zionism'
stories.summary: Iran's Jewish community distanced itself from Zionism following an Israeli strike on a synagogue. A Jewish shopkeeper in Tehran stated that Iranian Jews identify as Iranians first and reject actions taken in the name of Zionism.

stories.title: Italian prime minister suggests suspending EU spending rules over Iran war
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni proposed that the EU consider temporarily suspending its fiscal spending rules if the Iran war and resulting energy crisis worsen. She compared the potential response to measures taken during the Covid pandemic.

stories.title: Pakistan’s envoy to US acknowledges China’s quiet but persuasive role in Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's ambassador to Washington, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, acknowledged China's quiet but persuasive diplomatic role in facilitating the US-Iran ceasefire. He described the breakthrough as the result of weeks of intense diplomatic effort underpinned by trust from all parties.

stories.title: Oil price rises as markets question durability of Middle East ceasefire
stories.summary: Oil and gas prices rose on Thursday while Asian stock markets retreated amid doubts about the durability of the US-Iran ceasefire. Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon and mutual threats of resumed military action between Washington and Tehran fueled market uncertainty.

stories.title: Trump threatens to renew war if Iran doesn’t comply with ‘real agreement’
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to renew military action against Iran if it does not agree to a "real agreement." US forces will remain in the region ahead of peace talks in Pakistan, while uncertainty over Lebanon and the Strait of Hormuz threatens the fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Costa Rica designates IRGC, Hezbollah, Hamas, Houthis as terrorist organizations
stories.summary: Costa Rica officially designated the IRGC, Hezbollah, Hamas, and the Houthis as terrorist organizations. The government said the decision aligns with Costa Rica's international commitments to combating terrorism and its financing.

stories.title: Israel accepts direct talks with Lebanon 'under fire'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announced Thursday that he ordered his cabinet to open direct talks with Lebanon aimed at disarming Hezbollah and establishing peace, even as hostilities continue.

stories.title: Uncertainty over US-Iran talks as Israel strikes Lebanon
stories.summary: Uncertainty surrounds the upcoming U.S.-Iran talks in Pakistan despite confirmed participation from both sides. Deadly Israeli strikes on Lebanon have strained the fragile ceasefire and complicated diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Iran team heads to Pakistan as Lebanon hit by Israel massacre
stories.summary: An Iranian negotiating team departed for Pakistan for high-stakes talks with the United States as Lebanon reeled from a deadly Israeli bombardment. The diplomatic efforts come amid escalating tensions across the Middle East.

stories.title: Their finest hour
stories.summary: The article credits Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir for brokering the US-Iran ceasefire. The diplomatic effort averted President Trump's threat to "wipe out an entire civilisation" if Iran did not surrender.

stories.title: Turkish, Italian defense firms team up to produce unmanned surface vessels for Italy
stories.summary: Turkish firm Havelsan and Italian companies VN Maritime and Piloda Defence have partnered to produce unmanned surface vessels for Italy. The consortium is targeting the signing of its first purchase order in the first half of 2026.

stories.title: Australian spy plane operators in Middle East not sharing intel with US for offensive operations, defence boss says
stories.summary: Australia extended the deployment of its E-7 Wedgetail surveillance aircraft in the Middle East. Defence chief Admiral David Johnston confirmed that Australian personnel are filtering intelligence to ensure no information is shared with the United States for offensive military operations, while continuing to share defensive threat data.

stories.title: Japanese band One OK Rock cancels Hong Kong concerts in May, no specific reason given
stories.summary: Japanese rock band One OK Rock cancelled its Hong Kong concerts scheduled for early May, citing unforeseen circumstances. The cancellation followed a similar move in March when the band dropped its Shanghai show. The concerts were part of the band's Detox Asia Tour 2026.

stories.title: China’s energy storage tech exports: a buffer against the Iran war oil shock?
stories.summary: China's exports of energy storage equipment, including inverters, are rising as the US-Israeli war in Iran drives global demand for energy independence. Chinese inverter exports surged 57 percent year-on-year to $1.66 billion in the first two months of 2026.

stories.title: Citic tops Asia-Pacific banking fees as mainland China and Hong Kong IPOs surge
stories.summary: China's Citic Securities ranked as the top investment banking fee earner in Asia-Pacific excluding Japan in the first quarter of 2026. Total regional fees reached $5.3 billion, down 5 percent year-on-year, as equity market gains were offset by weaker debt and M&A activity.

stories.title: Nigeria: Power DisCos Miss Revenue Targets Amid Efficiency Concerns
stories.summary: Nigeria's power distribution companies missed revenue targets, receiving electricity worth ₦336.43 billion but billing only ₦268.20 billion and collecting just ₦204.74 billion, raising concerns about operational efficiency.

stories.title: Boat capsize incident off Italy: Most of missing Pakistanis were ‘in Umrah pilgrims’ guise’
stories.summary: Most Pakistani migrants who went missing in a boat capsize off Italy had reportedly left Pakistan posing as Umrah pilgrims, while others used visit visas for Azerbaijan, Egypt, and Uganda. They had traveled through various routes to Libya before attempting the sea crossing. Pakistan's FIA has been tasked with collecting data on the missing individuals.

stories.title: Fears Middle East ceasefire at risk after Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 182 people
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit commercial and residential areas of central Beirut on Wednesday, killing at least 182 people and wounding 890, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The strikes have raised fears that the Middle East ceasefire could collapse.

stories.title: Ukraine’s veterans’ theatre turns war wounds into catharsis
stories.summary: In Kyiv, wounded Ukrainian veterans, soldiers' wives, and widows participate in a theatre programme where they workshop ideas and stage plays about their wartime experiences, using performance as a form of catharsis.

stories.title: Uganda: Govt Publishes List of Licensed Labour Export Firms
stories.summary: Uganda's government published a list of licensed labor export firms as State Minister Balaam Barugahara warned young people against fraudulent recruitment schemes run by traffickers and unlicensed agents.

stories.title: Haiti postpones voter registration for first election in a decade, no new dates given
stories.summary: Haiti's CEP electoral council postponed voter registration that was scheduled to begin on April 1 for the nation's first presidential election in a decade. No new dates were announced, with the council saying it would provide updated timelines shortly.

stories.title: On Truth Social, die-hard MAGA supporters start to turn on Trump
stories.summary: Following the fragile two-week US-Iran ceasefire, media reports highlight growing criticism of President Trump from formerly loyal supporters on Truth Social who are questioning his claims of victory. International press coverage has widely challenged the narrative that the ceasefire represents a US success.

stories.title: War update: 164 combat engagements between Ukraine's Defense Forces and Russian troops on frontline over past day, Pokrovsk sector most active
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces recorded 164 combat engagements with Russian troops along the frontline on April 8, with the Pokrovsk sector seeing the most activity.

stories.title: Record animal sacrifice attempts at Al-Aqsa prompt status quo fears
stories.summary: Israeli settlers made a record number of attempts to smuggle animal sacrifices into Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem. Observers describe the incidents as the most significant escalation at the site since 1967, raising concerns about changes to the status quo.

stories.title: Djibouti Vote: Guelleh poised to extend 27-year rule
stories.summary: Djibouti's President Ismail Omar Guelleh, who has ruled for 27 years, held his final campaign rally ahead of Friday's presidential election. He faces a divided and largely silenced opposition and is widely expected to win reelection in the strategically located Horn of Africa nation.

stories.title: Iran's IRGC opens ranks to children as young as 12
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced a programme opening its ranks to children as young as 12. An IRGC official in Tehran said the children would be assigned tasks including patrolling and manning checkpoints.

stories.title: Islamofascism: The word that launders war crimes, from Iran to Palestine
stories.summary: An opinion article argues that the term "Islamofascism," originally coined in the post-9/11 era, is being revived to justify Western military actions in the Middle East, including operations in Iran and Palestine.

stories.title: Iran announces alternative routes in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran announced it would temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz as part of the two-week ceasefire with the United States, including alternative shipping routes through the waterway.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian man near Tubas
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a 28-year-old Palestinian man, Alaa Khaled Muhammad Subaih, near the village of Tayasir east of Tubas in the occupied West Bank. The shooting occurred after residents confronted an Israeli settler attack near the village, and the victim's body was withheld by Israeli forces.

stories.title: President of Madagascar declares state of emergency over fuel supply concerns
stories.summary: Madagascar's president declared a state of emergency over concerns about fuel and energy supply disruptions affecting the Indian Ocean island nation.

stories.title: Senegal protesters rally over cost of living and debt crisis
stories.summary: Protesters in Dakar, Senegal, including workers, union members, and opposition supporters, rallied on Wednesday against the rising cost of living and the country's ongoing debt crisis.

stories.title: Pakistan’s return: Mediator or West Asia asset?
stories.summary: Pakistan's role in mediating the US-Iran ceasefire has drawn mixed reactions across India and the broader South Asia strategic community, with observers expressing both surprise and unease about Islamabad's rising diplomatic profile in the region.

stories.title: Russian attack on Balabyne: Injury toll rises to four, one dead
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Balabyne in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region killed one person and injured four others.

stories.title: Police arrest Michigan man after wife's Bahamas disappearance
stories.summary: Bahamian authorities arrested a Michigan man after his wife went missing at sea over the weekend during a trip to the Bahamas. Search and rescue efforts for the woman have been called off.

stories.title: China says Lebanon sovereignty 'should not be violated' after Israel strikes
stories.summary: China's Foreign Ministry stated that Lebanon's sovereignty "should not be violated" following Israeli strikes on the country. Spokesperson Mao Ning urged restraint and called for a de-escalation of the regional situation.

stories.title: South Africa: High Costs and Cheap Imports Threaten Local Sugar Farmers
stories.summary: South Africa's sugar industry faces a dual threat from high domestic production costs—driven by expensive fuel, fertilizer, and diesel—and an influx of cheap, heavily subsidized sugar imports undercutting local small-scale farmers.

stories.title: ‘I’m broken-hearted’: father pays tribute to student, 21, stabbed in Primrose Hill
stories.summary: Finbar Sullivan, a 21-year-old film student, was fatally stabbed in Primrose Hill park in north London on Tuesday evening. His father described him as a loving young man who had gone to the park to use a new camera. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

stories.title: PM hopes US-Iran ceasefire will become permanent
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed hope that the temporary US-Iran ceasefire would become permanent, thanking China, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt, and Qatar for supporting the peace effort. The government is considering observing a "Thanksgiving Day" to mark Pakistan's diplomatic role.

stories.title: What do Americans think of Trump's 'insane' military budget?
stories.summary: The Trump administration has proposed multiple military budget requests, the largest being $1.1 trillion, with an additional $200 billion earmarked for the war on Iran. Public opinion on the spending levels is under debate.

stories.title: Lahore High Court rules unrelated individuals can’t challenge acquittals
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court ruled that a private individual with no direct connection to a criminal case lacks legal standing to challenge an acquittal. Chief Justice Aalia Neelum upheld an objection against a petition challenging the acquittal of PM Shehbaz Sharif and his son Hamza in a money laundering case.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 99 out of 119 drones launched by Russia overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 99 of 119 drones launched by Russian forces in an overnight attack beginning the evening of April 8.

stories.title: Spain to reopen its embassy in Tehran
stories.summary: Spain announced it is reopening its embassy in Tehran to support peace efforts during the US-Israeli war on Iran. Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares said he instructed the Spanish ambassador to return to the Iranian capital.

stories.title: Once ‘Ultra-MAGA’, Trump supporters fume about Iran on Truth Social
stories.summary: Supporters of President Trump on his Truth Social platform are expressing unease and anger over the administration's approach to Iran. The discontent is notable among users who previously identified as strong Trump backers.

stories.title: US urged to end Ukraine war after Iran truce
stories.summary: Ukraine called on the United States to apply the same "decisiveness" used in the Iran ceasefire to pressure Russia into ending its invasion. The Kremlin also signaled hope for a new round of peace talks, while the US vice president called the Ukraine conflict the "hardest to solve."

stories.title: Thousands of Palestinians pray at Al-Aqsa Mosque after Israel’s 40-day ban
stories.summary: Approximately 3,000 Palestinian worshippers performed morning prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem after Israel lifted a 40-day ban on access to the site.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill seven in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed seven people and wounded others in the town of Abbasiya in Tyre, southern Lebanon. The strikes also targeted key bridges and infrastructure, largely cutting southern Lebanon off from the rest of the country.

stories.title: 15 nations plan to help restore traffic through Hormuz: Macron
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that approximately 15 countries are planning to help restore maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Iran ceasefire. The first ships have crossed the strait, but major shipping lines remain cautious, and hundreds of vessels are still stranded after a month-long blockade cut traffic by 95 percent.

stories.title: Iran has been bloodied, but it is winning against the US-Israel axis
stories.summary: Despite sustaining heavy human and material losses during the US-Israeli military campaign, Iran has survived the conflict. Some analysts frame Iran's endurance as a strategic outcome against the US-Israel axis.

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau on edge after activist's killing
stories.summary: The death of activist Vigario Luis Balanta in Guinea-Bissau, whose body showed signs of extreme violence, has sparked protests and accusations against the country's military rulers, raising concerns about repression and media freedom.

stories.title: French minister condemns Israeli blitz on Lebanon, says it undermines truce efforts
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot condemned Israeli strikes on Lebanon as "intolerable," saying they undermine the US-Iran ceasefire. He called for Lebanon to be included in any truce while also insisting that Hezbollah must disarm.

stories.title: World Bank cuts Middle East growth forecast after energy sector turmoil
stories.summary: The World Bank cut its 2026 growth forecast for Middle East economies following disruptions caused by the US-Israel war against Iran, including the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and destruction of energy infrastructure. The announcement came shortly after President Trump declared a two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Campaigners demand action to break UK’s ‘addiction’ to herbicides
stories.summary: Campaigners in the UK are calling for action to address what they describe as an addiction to herbicides, noting that glyphosate use has risen tenfold over 30 years. The practice of spraying glyphosate on wheat before harvest originated with Scottish farmers in the 1980s and has since spread globally.

stories.title: China strengthens oversight of state-owned assets overseas amid global tensions
stories.summary: China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission established a new department to oversee foreign investments by state-owned enterprises. The bureau will guide SOEs in international operations amid an increasingly turbulent geopolitical environment.

stories.title: China team introduced plant-based photosynthesis in sick animals. They recovered
stories.summary: Chinese scientists developed plant-based, light-activated nanoparticles that can be introduced into animal cells to boost energy production and restore cellular functions. When tested in rats and rabbits with degenerative conditions, the photosynthetic nanoparticles improved health and lifespan.

stories.title: Iranian minister to US: 'You cannot have a cake and eat it at the same time'
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister, Saeed Khatibzadeh, criticised the United States for seeking a ceasefire while its ally Israel carried out strikes on Lebanon that killed over 250 people. Tehran conveyed this message directly to Washington.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,040 troops, 64 artillery systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces lost approximately 1,040 troops and 64 artillery systems in a single day of fighting in Ukraine, bringing total estimated Russian personnel losses since February 2022 to roughly 1,307,540.

stories.title: India says it won’t host UN climate talks in 2028
stories.summary: India has withdrawn its offer to host the UN Climate Conference of the Parties (COP33) in 2028, according to two government officials. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had originally proposed hosting the summit in 2023, and the reason for the withdrawal was not immediately clear.

stories.title: Trump blasts CNN, New York Times over circulating ‘fake’ Iran plan
stories.summary: President Trump accused CNN and The New York Times of reporting on a fabricated ten-point plan related to the Iran negotiations. In a Truth Social post, he claimed the reports were undermining the peace process.

stories.title: Israeli military says it has killed nephew of Hezbollah chief
stories.summary: Israel's military announced it struck and killed Ali Yusuf Harshi, the personal secretary and nephew of Hezbollah Secretary General Naim Qassem, in a strike in the Beirut area on April 8. The military described Harshi as a close adviser who played a central role in managing Qassem's office.

stories.title: Rats spread across Gaza's camps, threatening children
stories.summary: Rat infestations are spreading across displacement camps in Gaza, increasingly entering tents where families sleep. The rodents pose a growing health threat, particularly to children living in the camps.

stories.title: “Incapable to proceed”: man who killed Ukrainian refugee Iryna Zarutska ruled incompetent
stories.summary: DeCarlos Brown, accused of fatally stabbing Ukrainian refugee Iryna Zarutska on a Charlotte, North Carolina train, has been ruled mentally incompetent to stand trial. The finding stalls death penalty proceedings that had been backed by President Trump.

stories.title: Trump declares end to Iran’s uranium enrichment
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared that Iran will no longer enrich uranium and announced plans for the US and Iran to jointly "dig up and remove" nuclear material buried by US strikes. Trump also threatened 50 percent tariffs on nations supplying weapons to Tehran.

stories.title: Argentine MPs approve Milei-backed bill to allow mining in glaciers
stories.summary: Argentina's lower house of parliament approved a bill backed by President Javier Milei permitting mining in glacier regions. Environmentalists and scientists have warned the legislation threatens water resources in frozen areas of the Andes mountains. The law takes effect upon publication in the official gazette.

stories.title: Nigeria: U.S. Extends Hostile Acts Towards Nigeria, Tells Americans Not to Visit Country
stories.summary: The United States issued a travel advisory warning Americans against visiting Nigeria, amid concerns that Washington may be attempting to pressure Nigeria into accepting a U.S. military base on its territory.

stories.title: BBC at the site of Israeli air strikes in Beirut
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit Beirut, killing at least 182 people and wounding 890 others, according to figures released by the Lebanese health ministry.

stories.title: “They trust Putin”: Zelenskyy says US ignored proof of Russia-Iran military cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alleged that Russia shared U.S. base coordinates with Iran and that Washington ignored the evidence because it trusts President Putin. He noted that Trump envoys visited Moscow five times without traveling to Kyiv.

stories.title: Islamabad takes centre stage, to host high-stakes US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Islamabad is set to host direct US-Iran negotiations beginning Friday, following a Pakistan-brokered two-week ceasefire. US Vice President J.D. Vance and Iran's foreign minister will lead their respective delegations, though the truce has shown signs of strain after Israeli strikes in Lebanon.

stories.title: Bus driver killed, 16 injured in 2 separate crashes on Hong Kong highway
stories.summary: A bus driver was killed and 16 people were injured in two separate multi-vehicle crashes on Hong Kong's San Tin Highway within two hours. The incidents involved a total of eight vehicles, and the injured were transported to North District Hospital.

stories.title: War in Middle East fails to dent remittances in March
stories.summary: Pakistan received $3.8 billion in remittances in March, a 17 percent increase over February despite the ongoing Middle East conflict. The State Bank of Pakistan reported that inflows from Middle Eastern countries experienced positive growth, partly attributed to Ramadan.

stories.title: Russian forces strike settlement in Zaporizhzhia region, leaving one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a settlement in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia district, injuring one woman.

stories.title: Trump: US military will stay deployed near Iran until Tehran complies with ceasefire deal
