stories.summary: President Trump stated on Truth Social that US military forces will remain deployed near Iran until Tehran fully complies with the ceasefire deal. He warned that if compliance fails, military action would resume on a larger scale.

stories.title: Trump says US forces to stay near Iran, ready for ‘next conquest’
stories.summary: President Trump stated that US forces will remain deployed near Iran and signaled readiness for further military action. Ongoing Israeli attacks in Lebanon continued to cast doubt on fragile ceasefire efforts.

stories.title: Gingle Wang’s rise to the top, apps that help fight jet lag: 7 Lifestyle highlights
stories.summary: The article highlights lifestyle stories trending in China and Taiwan, including the career rise of Taiwanese actress Gingle Wang and apps designed to combat jet lag.

stories.title: As Trump claims victory, Iran emerges bruised but resilient, with leverage over Hormuz
stories.summary: Despite US claims of victory, Iran retains missile capabilities and uranium stockpiles following the conflict. Gulf states have pressed for guarantees of maritime freedom through the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran maintains strategic leverage.

stories.title: What is Strategic Rivalry? Why Should We Care?
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the United States' key strategy documents since the 2017 National Security Strategy have used terms like "great power competition" without adequately addressing the concept of strategic rivalry. The piece notes that interstate rivals have caused roughly 80 percent of history's wars, with rivalries having only a coin-toss chance of ending peacefully.

stories.title: What is Strategic Rivalry? Why Should We Care?
stories.summary: The article examines the concept of strategic rivalry and its relevance to US national security, noting that interstate rivals have caused approximately 80 percent of historical wars. It critiques US strategy documents since 2017 for using vague terms like great power competition without fully addressing the dynamics of rivalry.

stories.title: China’s Unitree to debut cheapest humanoid robot globally on Alibaba site: sources
stories.summary: Chinese robotics company Unitree plans to launch its R1 humanoid robot on Alibaba's AliExpress marketplace, targeting markets including North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore. The R1 is described as the company's cheapest humanoid model and was previously launched in mainland China.

stories.title: Kenya: Police Warn of Traffic Disruptions in CBD As Ruto Plans Day-Long Activities
stories.summary: Kenya's National Police Service issued a traffic advisory warning of temporary disruptions in Nairobi's Central Business District ahead of President William Ruto's planned day-long activities, including an inaugural address at City Hall.

stories.title: Classification of Russia's crimes against journalists should be carried out in four categories – IMI director
stories.summary: The director of the Institute of Mass Information stated that since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, at least 428 editorial offices have been affected by Russian crimes. He proposed classifying these crimes against journalists into four categories.

stories.title: UK Foreign Minister says Israeli assault on Lebanon 'deeply damaging'
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper described Israel's attacks across Lebanon as "deeply damaging" and called for Lebanon to be included in the ceasefire. She warned that continued Israeli escalation could destabilise the entire region.

stories.title: Trump’s abrupt Iran reversal exposes limits of his leverage
stories.summary: President Trump's acceptance of a ceasefire with Iran is being viewed by some analysts as a reversal that exposes the limits of his negotiating leverage, following a pattern of taking extreme positions before backpedaling.

stories.title: Iran’s Asymmetric Counterair Campaign: Attacking the U.S. Air Force’s Nests and Eggs
stories.summary: On March 27, Iranian drones and missiles struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, destroying a U.S. E-3 Sentry airborne command aircraft and damaging multiple KC-135 tankers. An earlier Iranian attack that month had already damaged five KC-135s at the same base, marking unprecedented hits against these aircraft types.

stories.title: Iran’s Asymmetric Counterair Campaign: Attacking the U.S. Air Force’s Nests and Eggs
stories.summary: On March 27, Iranian drones and missiles struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, destroying a US E-3 Sentry airborne command aircraft and damaging multiple KC-135 tankers. An earlier Iranian attack in March had already damaged five KC-135s at the same base, marking unprecedented hits against these aircraft types.

stories.title: Indian oil minister to visit Qatar from Thursday
stories.summary: India's oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri will visit Qatar on 9–10 April amid disruptions to India's LPG supply caused by the regional conflict. The visit follows the announcement of a US-Iran ceasefire, though Israeli strikes on Lebanon continue.

stories.title: FAO food commodities prices up in March; concern with energy and fertilizer costs
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization reported that global food commodity prices rose in March for the second consecutive month. The increase was driven largely by higher energy prices linked to the escalating conflict in the Near East, with concerns also raised about rising fertilizer costs.

stories.title: NATO 約30か国の大使 今月中旬に日本を訪問する方向で調整
stories.summary: Ambassadors from approximately 30 NATO member countries are coordinating a visit to Japan in mid-month. The unusually large delegation aims to strengthen NATO's ties with the Indo-Pacific region amid China's growing military capabilities.

stories.title: Why North Korea’s Kim may shake hands with Trump again despite missile tests
stories.summary: North Korea conducted a series of weapons tests, including cluster munitions and radar-evading systems, ahead of the upcoming US-China summit. Analysts suggest China may use the summit to facilitate renewed talks between North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and US President Donald Trump.

stories.title: France’s Macron urges US, Iran to respect ceasefire in Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron urged the United States and Iran to respect the ceasefire in Lebanon. However, both Israel and the U.S. have stated that Lebanon was not included in the ceasefire agreement with Iran.

stories.title: Three life terms for Kashmir’s Aasiya Andrabi fit India’s ‘broader pattern’
stories.summary: A court in India sentenced 64-year-old Kashmiri activist Aasiya Andrabi to three life terms. Legal experts say the conviction was primarily based on speech-related offences and reflects a broader pattern of harsh sentencing in Kashmir.

stories.title: More Chinese banks claw back bonuses, cut salaries despite mixed profit recovery
stories.summary: Several major Chinese banks, including state-owned Bank of China, have reclaimed performance-based bonuses from employees amid economic sluggishness and government scrutiny. Bank of China recovered 47.18 million yuan from 4,630 individuals in 2025, according to annual reports.

stories.title: Paratroopers destroy Russian D-30 howitzer in Myrnohrad, Donetsk region
stories.summary: Drone operators from the 25th Separate Sicheslav Airborne Brigade of Ukraine's Armed Forces destroyed a Russian D-30 howitzer near Myrnohrad in the Donetsk region using unmanned aerial systems.

stories.title: Lebanon must be included in US-Iran ceasefire deal, Yvette Cooper to say
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper is set to tell City leaders in London that Lebanon must be included in the US-Iran ceasefire deal. Her remarks come as Israel intensifies bombing of Lebanon and US Vice President Vance has stated Lebanon is not part of the agreement.

stories.title: Lebanese PM declares day of mourning after ‘unprecedented’ wave of IDF strikes
stories.summary: Lebanon's prime minister declared a national day of mourning after Israeli strikes killed at least 182 people. The IDF said it targeted hundreds of Hezbollah operatives, with strikes hitting both Beirut's southern suburbs and central areas, some without warning.

stories.title: Power consumers to bear Rs10.6bn extra burden
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Electric Power Regulatory Authority approved an additional Rs10.57 billion burden on electricity consumers through a Rs1.42 per unit fuel cost adjustment for April bills. The net impact is slightly lower than March, as it replaces a higher Rs1.63 per unit charge.

stories.title: Iranian delegation to reach Islamabad Thursday, Iran's ambassador to Pakistan says
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, announced that an Iranian delegation would arrive in Islamabad on Thursday night for talks aimed at resolving the conflict with the US and Israel. The talks are based on 10 points proposed by Iran.

stories.title: Russia plans to restrict international calls for citizens — intelligence
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reports that Russian authorities plan to restrict incoming international calls from designated "unfriendly" countries to ordinary citizens without prior subscriber consent, and to introduce mandatory labeling of such calls.

stories.title: Russia plans to restrict international calls for citizens — intelligence
stories.summary: Russian authorities plan to block incoming international calls from designated "unfriendly" countries unless subscribers provide prior consent, and to introduce mandatory labeling for such calls.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1505: Ukraine and Croatia break ground on underground drone factory
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that Hungary has been sharing intelligence with Iran. The report emerged as U.S. Vice President Vance traveled to Budapest to campaign alongside Hungarian leadership. Separately, Ukraine and Croatia broke ground on an underground drone factory.

stories.title: Iranian envoy set to arrive in Pakistan's capital on Thursday
stories.summary: An Iranian delegation is expected to arrive in Islamabad on Thursday at the invitation of Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to Iran's ambassador Reza Amiri Moghadam. The delegation will engage in talks with the US based on 10 points proposed by Iran.

stories.title: UK says Lebanon must be included in ceasefire deal
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper stated that the US-Iran ceasefire must include Lebanon, where Israeli strikes killed at least 254 people on Wednesday. Cooper also demanded Iran cease mining and drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Senegal: A Decade of Unresolved Climate Displacement
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch has called on Senegal to develop a national planned relocation policy, citing a decade of unresolved climate-related displacement affecting communities in the country.

stories.title: Iran war day 41: What’s happening in Lebanon, Middle East and beyond?
stories.summary: Lebanon declared a national day of mourning after Israeli attacks killed at least 254 people in a single day. The strikes marked one of the deadliest episodes since the conflict began.

stories.title: 10,000 suspected fake football jerseys seized in HK$64 million customs crackdown
stories.summary: Hong Kong customs seized approximately 10,000 suspected counterfeit football jerseys and other goods worth an estimated HK$64 million ahead of the World Cup finals. Three people were arrested during the 19-day operation code-named Dawnbreaker, which targeted cross-boundary transshipment.

stories.title: Philippines expands South China Sea footprint with permanent Thitu Island base
stories.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard opened its first dedicated command center on Thitu Island in the Spratly chain, a disputed area of the South China Sea. The new district headquarters, previously managed from Palawan, will cover approximately 68,000 square kilometers of contested waters.

stories.title: Russian government uses 'whitelists' during internet restrictions to promote players loyal to the authorities – intelligence
stories.summary: Russian authorities are reportedly using internet "whitelists" — registers of sites that remain accessible during connectivity restrictions — to favor businesses loyal to the government, turning a technical tool into an instrument of economic coercion and market redistribution.

stories.title: Israel renews attacks on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel launched renewed air strikes on southern Lebanon in what reports described as the deadliest wave of attacks since the war on Iran began. At least 250 people were killed and over a thousand wounded across Lebanon.

stories.title: Pakistan plays major role trying to mediate an end to Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a key mediator between the United States and Iran, helping broker the two-week ceasefire agreement. Islamabad, which maintains ties with both Tehran and Washington, is set to host further peace talks over the weekend.

stories.title: Russian drones damage substation in Odesa region, Ukrainian officials say
stories.summary: Russian drones damaged a power substation in Ukraine's southern Odesa region on Wednesday. Moscow's forces also repeatedly attacked areas in eastern Ukrainian regions, killing one person, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Quirky China: haunted house auctioned 3 times, lift serves only 1 floor, ‘mouse run’ at eatery
stories.summary: A series of quirky viral stories from China includes a reportedly haunted flat in Chengdu auctioned for the third time, a lift that serves only one floor, and a mouse spotted on a sushi conveyor belt at a restaurant.

stories.title: For Gulf states, Hormuz uncertainty casts shadow over US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Gulf states are concerned that a US-Iran ceasefire deal could give Iran leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy route. Experts say the uncertainty around Hormuz is complicating regional diplomatic calculations.

stories.title: From Khamenei’s death to the 'Islamabad Accords': Ceasefire leaves unanswered questions - editorial
stories.summary: Former Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is dead and Iran's ballistic missile infrastructure has been significantly degraded, but the Iranian regime survived. The ceasefire, described as the "Islamabad Accords," leaves major unanswered questions about the conflict's resolution.

stories.title: America’s Pro-War Elites Must Be Held Accountable
stories.summary: The article argues that American proponents of military action in Iran should be held accountable for what the author characterizes as a disastrous intervention. It calls for scrutiny of pro-war elites in the US policy establishment.

stories.title: Netanyahu fails to address Israel’s failure to achieve war goals in Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu issued a statement on the U.S.-Iran ceasefire but did not address Israel's failure to achieve its stated war objectives. Reporting from Jerusalem, FRANCE 24 noted those goals included regime change in Iran, destruction of Iran's ballistic missile capabilities, and elimination of the nuclear threat.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Red Cross ‘outraged’ as Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 254 people; Trump says US military to remain in region
stories.summary: The Red Cross expressed outrage after Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed 254 people, as President Trump announced the US military would remain deployed in the region. UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper called for Lebanon's inclusion in any ceasefire and demanded toll-free shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Thursday briefing: ​What difference will the ceasefire in the Middle East make, and will it hold?
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran was announced Tuesday, just an hour before Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. However, unresolved disputes and competing interpretations of the deal threaten to pull the region back toward crisis.

stories.title: Australia eyes new fuel supply from US, Mexico and Asia as diesel prices spike to record high
stories.summary: Australia is seeking alternative fuel supplies from the US, Mexico, and Asian neighbors as diesel prices hit record highs amid Middle East disruptions. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese traveled to Singapore to secure ongoing refined fuel shipments, while energy officials said supplies were secure until mid-May.

stories.title: Russia tempts energy-starved South Asia with 40% discounts on US-sanctioned LNG
stories.summary: Russia is offering liquefied natural gas from US-sanctioned facilities to South Asian buyers at roughly 40 percent below spot prices. The offers are being routed through little-known intermediary companies based in China and Russia, according to sources familiar with the negotiations.

stories.title: Greek PM says tolls for ships to cross Hormuz would be unacceptable, a risk to freedom of navigation
stories.summary: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said it would be unacceptable for ships to pay tolls to transit the Strait of Hormuz, as Iran has suggested. He warned that such a move would set a dangerous precedent for freedom of navigation.

stories.title: Ceasefire threatened as Israel expands Lebanon strikes, Iran closes strait again
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire came under immediate threat as Israel expanded military strikes into Lebanon and Iran responded by closing the Strait of Hormuz again. The White House demanded the strait be reopened and sought to keep planned peace talks on track.

stories.title: Nigeria: Trump Links CNN's Ceasefire Report to Unknown Nigerian Outlet
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump alleged that a controversial report on the Iran-US ceasefire originated from a "fake news site" in Nigeria, drawing the country into a dispute over CNN's coverage of the ceasefire.

stories.title: Nigeria: Plateau Killings - Victims Laid to Rest
stories.summary: The death toll from the Palm Sunday attack on the Anguwan Rukuba community in Jos North, Plateau State, Nigeria, has risen to 33. Some victims were laid to rest on Tuesday.

stories.title: Protesters gather outside US embassy in Tel Aviv ahead of Iran ceasefire announcement
stories.summary: Protesters organized by the Peace Partnership coalition gathered outside the US embassy in Tel Aviv ahead of the Iran ceasefire announcement. Demonstrators called for an end to the war, chanting that conflict would not bring freedom to anyone in the region.

stories.title: Shaky US-Iran ceasefire in doubt, as Israel pounds Lebanon
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire appeared shaky as Iran and the United States laid out sharply contrasting agendas ahead of talks scheduled for April 11, while Israel continued to strike targets in Lebanon.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire: Why Tehran wants to charge ships for crossing the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: As part of a 10-point proposal to end hostilities with the United States and Israel, Iran is seeking continued control over the Strait of Hormuz, including the authority to charge ships up to $2 million each for passage. Tehran says the revenue would fund reconstruction of infrastructure damaged during the conflict.

stories.title: PSG take control of Champions League semi-finals tie with win against Liverpool
stories.summary: Paris Saint-Germain defeated Liverpool 2-0 at home in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final. Désiré Doué scored in the 11th minute and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia added a second in the 65th minute. PSG dominated possession at 74 percent and registered 18 shots.

stories.title: Israel’s ‘ice orphans’: Survival, legacy, and the battle for hockey gold in Sofia
stories.summary: Israel's national ice hockey team competed in a tournament in Sofia, Bulgaria, in a sport with a small but dedicated following in the country.

stories.title: Trump warns ‘shooting’ could start again as fragile Iran truce is tested by Lebanon violence
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned on his Truth Social platform that the US military would remain deployed around Iran and threatened to resume "shooting" if Tehran does not fully comply with the recently reached deal. The statement came as a fragile US-Iran truce faced growing uncertainty.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with 'bigger and better' attacks if no deal reached
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared on Truth Social that American military forces would remain deployed near Iran until a "real agreement" is fully complied with, threatening further military action if no deal is reached.

stories.title: Xi: senior officers must ‘stay pure’ to meet Chinese military’s centenary goal
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged senior People's Liberation Army officers to deepen ideological rectification and maintain political loyalty to the Communist Party. The directive follows a sweeping anti-corruption campaign within the military ahead of the PLA's centenary in 2027.

stories.title: Kenya: Rights Group Warns of Mass Action If Govt Fails to Act On Fuel Quality Concerns
stories.summary: The Mtetezi Grassroots Economic Justice Movement in Kenya has threatened nationwide protests if the government fails to act against Energy Cabinet Secretary Opiyo Wandayi over allegations of substandard fuel imports entering the country.

stories.title: Abandoned Battle of Britain control tower to become a home for holidaymakers … and six species of bat
stories.summary: A derelict Battle of Britain-era RAF watch office in the New Forest, Hampshire, has received planning permission for conversion into a holiday retreat. The Landmark Trust's £700,000 project will create a four-bedroom home that accommodates both visitors and six resident bat species.

stories.title: Mozambique: World Bank Accused of Using Outdated Statistics
stories.summary: Mozambican Finance Minister Carla Louveira has accused the World Bank of relying on outdated statistics in its latest report on Mozambique's economic situation.

stories.title: Man rescued after two weeks trapped in collapsed Mexico mine
stories.summary: Mexican military divers rescued a man who had been trapped for nearly two weeks in a flooded gold mine in Sinaloa, Mexico.

stories.title: Trump slams NATO over Iran after meeting Rutte, renews Greenland threat
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte and expressed disappointment that NATO member states had not supported the US war effort against Iran. Trump also renewed his rhetoric regarding Greenland.

stories.title: US-Iran truce should apply to Lebanon, Australian Prime Minister says
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the US-Iran ceasefire should also apply to Lebanon, according to the Associated Press.

stories.title: Rwanda: Genocide Case Against Widow of Ex-Rwandan President Remains in the Balance
stories.summary: A French court has postponed its ruling on whether to dismiss genocide allegations against Agathe Habyarimana, the widow of former Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana. A decision is now expected on 6 May, after 18 years of investigation.

stories.title: Sudan: 'Sudan Army Detains, Tortures Civilians in Ethnic Targeting Campaign' - HRW
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that Sudanese Armed Forces-affiliated security and military forces have arbitrarily detained, tortured, and ill-treated civilians in areas under their control across Khartoum, El Gezira, El Gedaref, and Red Sea State. The group said the violations may amount to war crimes and crimes against humanity.

stories.title: Government turns down in situ redevelopment proposal by over 400 Tai Po fire victims
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Housing Bureau rejected a proposal by over 400 displaced residents of the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po for in situ partial redevelopment. Officials said rebuilding on the original site would take too long and carried too many uncertainties to serve as a viable long-term housing solution.

stories.title: Africa: Over 1,000 Humanitarians Have Been Killed in Three Years, Security Council Hears
stories.summary: The UN Security Council heard that at least 326 humanitarian workers were killed in the line of duty across 21 countries in 2025, bringing the three-year total to over 1,010. The International Red Cross warned that "we are losing our humanity in war."

stories.title: Man fighting for life after alleged hammer attack by woman he knew in Sydney hospital
stories.summary: A 46-year-old woman was charged with grievous bodily harm after allegedly striking a 63-year-old male patient in the head with a hammer at Sydney's Royal Prince Alfred hospital. Police said the woman knew the victim, who is now fighting for his life.

stories.title: UN chief says Israeli attacks on Lebanon pose 'grave risk' to truce efforts
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that Israel's ongoing assault on Lebanon poses a grave risk to the US-Iran ceasefire deal. His spokesperson called on all parties to immediately cease hostilities.

stories.title: Al-Aqsa reopens after Israel's closure since start of war on Iran
stories.summary: Israel reopened Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem to Muslim worshippers after weeks of total closure dating back to late February. The closure had barred access throughout Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr, marking the longest such restriction since 1967.

stories.title: US and Iran may have to talk 'as guns are firing'
stories.summary: The US scrambled to salvage its ceasefire with Iran after deadly Israeli strikes on Lebanon and an unclaimed attack on an energy facility on Iran's Lavan Island threatened to collapse the agreement. The Trump administration and Iran appeared to be negotiating terms in real time under Pakistani mediation.

stories.title: Hundreds search for wolf that escaped from zoo in South Korea
stories.summary: A male wolf escaped from O-World theme park zoo in Daejeon, South Korea, prompting a local school closure and a search involving over 300 firefighters, police, and military personnel. The wolf, born in 2024, remained at large as of Thursday.

stories.title: ‘Malaysia won’t be lectured’: Singapore’s refusal to negotiate over Hormuz creates waves
stories.summary: Singapore's refusal to negotiate with Iran over access to the Strait of Hormuz drew criticism from Malaysian politicians, who accused Singapore of lecturing them on the issue. Tehran had largely shut the strait—which handles about a fifth of global oil and gas shipments—in retaliation for US and Israeli military strikes.

stories.title: UN condemns Israeli strikes on Lebanon, calls casualty reports 'appalling'
stories.summary: The United Nations condemned a massive wave of Israeli strikes across Lebanon on Wednesday, calling reports of hundreds of casualties, including civilians, "appalling." The strikes came just hours after the U.S.-Iran ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: US-Iran truce enters second day as war flares in Lebanon
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire entered its second day amid escalating violence in Lebanon, where Israel launched its heaviest bombardment yet. The truce between the US, Israel, and Iran remained fragile.

stories.title: George Clooney calls Donald Trump’s ‘a whole civilization will die tonight’ threat to Iran a war crime
stories.summary: George Clooney accused U.S. President Donald Trump of committing a war crime by threatening Iran that 'a whole civilization will die tonight.' Clooney made the remarks during a speech to approximately 3,000 high school students in Cuneo, Italy. The White House dismissed the criticism, mocking Clooney's acting career.

stories.title: Hong Kong receives 90 reports of people stuck in lifts after voltage dip
stories.summary: A technical fault between Hong Kong's two power providers caused a brief voltage dip on Thursday, leading to roughly 90 reports of people trapped in lifts within 30 minutes. Several hospitals on Hong Kong Island were affected, requiring resets of medical equipment.

stories.title: Consumers urged to ‘completely avoid’ UK-caught cod as population plunges
stories.summary: The Marine Conservation Society urged consumers to "completely avoid" UK-caught cod, warning that populations have reached dangerously low levels. The advisory was issued despite existing zero-catch recommendations, as part of the charity's Good Fish Guide for sustainable seafood choices.

stories.title: Is one of America’s top AI-robot scholars about to join China’s tech talent pool?
stories.summary: Su Hao, an American-based scholar with dual doctorates in mathematics and computer science specializing in AI for robotics, has appeared on Fudan University's faculty list in Shanghai as a PhD supervisor. The appointment signals a potential gain for China's efforts to recruit top global AI talent.

stories.title: Volkswagen tests China’s appetite for locally developed EVs
stories.summary: Volkswagen plans to launch three new electric vehicle models in mainland China over the next two weeks, developed using technology from Chinese firms. The German automaker is seeking to remain competitive in the world's largest car market amid fierce domestic competition in the EV segment.

stories.title: US did not agree that ceasefire with Iran would cover Lebanon, V-P Vance says
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance stated in Budapest that the ceasefire with Iran was intended to cover Iran and U.S. allies, not Lebanon, clarifying the American position on the scope of the agreement.

stories.title: Palestinian killed by Israeli fire amid series of reported West Bank settler attacks
stories.summary: A Palestinian man was killed by Israeli fire near Tayasir in the occupied West Bank. The Israeli military said a soldier on leave shot the individual during clashes between Palestinians and settlers over a new wildcat outpost.

stories.title: Sounds of silence: Israeli sports return, but minus fans who define them
stories.summary: The Israel Soccer League resumed play across the country but in largely empty stadiums, creating an atmosphere compared to the COVID-19 pandemic era of 2020.

stories.title: JD Vance says US 'never made that promise' on Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said Washington never assured Iran that the ceasefire would cover Lebanon, calling it a "legitimate misunderstanding." His remarks came after Israeli strikes across Lebanon killed over 250 people and injured more than 1,160.

stories.title: U.S. court declines to block Pentagon's Anthropic blacklisting for now
stories.summary: A U.S. court declined to immediately block the Pentagon's blacklisting of AI company Anthropic. Anthropic alleges that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth overstepped his authority by designating the company a national security supply-chain risk.

stories.title: Russian propaganda spreads more than 500 fake publications portraying Ukraine as 'terrorist state' – SPRAVDI
stories.summary: According to Ukraine's SPRAVDI center, Russian information outlets have disseminated more than 500 fabricated publications promoting the narrative that Ukraine is a "terrorist state," leveraging topics such as strikes on Russian territory and accusations against Baltic nations.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl captures terrifying moment Israel bombed Beirut
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl in Beirut captured footage on Snapchat of the moment Israeli forces began bombing the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Reza Pahlavi says Iranians still 'need to topple regime'
stories.summary: Iranian crown prince Reza Pahlavi said Iranians still need to topple the regime, arguing that the reported succession of killed Supreme Leader Khamenei's son Mojtaba as Iran's new leader contradicts President Trump's claims of achieving regime change.

stories.title: Chinese researcher's death after questioning in US prompts anger in Beijing
stories.summary: A Chinese semiconductor researcher was found dead after what Beijing described as "hostile questioning" by US law enforcement, prompting anger from Chinese officials and the public.

stories.title: South Korean activists howl with rage as escaped wolf faces death
stories.summary: A male wolf born in 2024 escaped from O-World zoo at a theme park in Daejeon, South Korea, on Wednesday and remained at large on Thursday. A nearby school closed over safety concerns as hundreds of emergency and military personnel conducted a search of surrounding areas.

stories.title: Lufthansa cabin crew to strike on April 10, union says
stories.summary: Germany's Lufthansa cabin crew union announced a strike beginning just after midnight on April 10 and lasting until 10 p.m. that day.

stories.title: Hong Kong to roll out subsidies, fee waivers for transport sector as fuel costs soar
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities plan to introduce short-term subsidies and fee waivers to support the transport sector as oil price fluctuations driven by the Middle East conflict and global energy crisis push up fuel costs. The measures are expected under a new government task force established to respond to the crisis.

stories.title: Trump lashes out at Nato, alliance chief says US president 'clearly disappointed'
stories.summary: President Trump criticized NATO on Truth Social after a closed-door meeting with Secretary General Mark Rutte in Washington, claiming the alliance was absent when needed. Rutte described the conversation as "very frank" and acknowledged Trump was "clearly disappointed." Trump also referenced Greenland.

stories.title: Israeli settler wounded by rock, Palestinian shot by IDF soldier, in West Bank altercation
stories.summary: An Israeli settler was wounded by a rock and a Palestinian was shot by an off-duty IDF soldier near Tayasir village in the occupied West Bank. The military said soldiers were dispatched after Palestinians reportedly threw rocks at Israeli settlers.

stories.title: Nearly 5,000 South African Afrikaners take up Trump refugee offer
stories.summary: Nearly 5,000 white South African Afrikaners have entered the United States under a refugee program created by President Trump, which was based on unfounded claims that the minority faces persecution in South Africa.

stories.title: Long Island architect pleads guilty to 'Gilgo Beach' serial killings
stories.summary: Long Island architect Rex Heuermann pleaded guilty on Wednesday to killing eight women in attacks dating back to the 1990s, resolving the long-unsolved 'Gilgo Beach' serial killer case after DNA evidence led to his 2023 arrest.

stories.title: When war feels next door
stories.summary: An oil rig worker from West Bengal, India, describes living in Kuwait as the U.S.-Israel-Iran war escalates nearby, facing fear, uncertainty, and limited options for returning home.

stories.title: Inside the situation room: How did Netanyahu pitch the Iran war to Trump? - report
stories.summary: A report described how Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu made a "hard sell" to President Trump for attacking Iran, presenting options for a new Iranian leader to replace the current regime. The pitch reportedly took place in a situation room briefing.

stories.title: Partisans carry out sabotage on railway and disrupt Russian supply lines in Kupiansk sector
stories.summary: Agents of the partisan movement ATESH carried out two simultaneous sabotage operations on a railway section between Stary Oskol and Urazove in the Kharkiv region, disrupting Russian military supply lines serving the Kupiansk sector.

stories.title: Turkish convoy condemns ‘lawless aggression’ of the US and Israel
stories.summary: Hundreds of vehicles drove through Istanbul, Turkey, in a convoy protesting what participants described as lawless aggression by the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Trump weighs punishing certain NATO countries over lack of Iran war support, reports say
stories.summary: Reports indicate President Donald Trump is considering punishing certain NATO member countries for insufficient support of the U.S. war effort in Iran, potentially by relocating American troops out of those nations.

stories.title: Middle East live: Hezbollah says it fired rockets at Israel in response to ‘violation of ceasefire’
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it fired rockets toward Israel on Thursday, citing Israeli violations of the U.S.-Iran truce agreement. Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for Israeli attacks in Lebanon. The ceasefire appeared increasingly fragile as hostilities continued on multiple fronts.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill four, including Al Jazeera journalist, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip on April 8 killed four people, including an Al Jazeera journalist, according to local health authorities and the Qatari news network.

stories.title: Dilemma over crossings as fate of Hormuz ships remains uncertain
stories.summary: Only three ships attempted to cross the Strait of Hormuz on April 8, reflecting uncertainty despite the announcement of a two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran.

stories.title: Thai men sign up for military, driven by prospect of steady pay amid sluggish economy
stories.summary: Voluntary military enlistment in Thailand has risen steadily over the past five years, with some districts filling annual conscription quotas entirely from willing volunteers. Analysts attribute the trend to the appeal of steady pay amid a sluggish economy, despite recent lethal border clashes with Cambodia.

stories.title: US man arrested in case of Michigan woman's disappearance in Bahamas
stories.summary: A US man was arrested in connection with the disappearance of Michigan woman Lynette Hooker in the Bahamas. Her husband had told authorities she fell overboard from a small boat and was swept out to sea by strong currents.

stories.title: FBI arrests ex-Fort Bragg employee over alleged classified leak to journalist
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Courtney Williams, a 40-year-old former employee at Fort Bragg linked to military special operations, on charges of leaking classified information to a journalist. FBI Director Kash Patel announced the arrest on Wednesday. The journalist was reportedly investigating deaths and drug use at the U.S. military base.

stories.title: Shippers seek clarity as Iran still controls Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted as Iran maintains control of the waterway. Indian vessels are awaiting government clearance, with more than 25 India-bound ships still stuck.

stories.title: Key Indian state polls begin in test for Modi's party
stories.summary: State assembly elections have begun in a key Indian state, serving as a test for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party as it seeks to expand into regions where it has historically struggled.

stories.title: Israel hammers Lebanon with strikes, killing and wounding scores on deadliest day of war
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit commercial and residential areas in central Beirut without warning on Wednesday, hours after a ceasefire was announced in the US-Israeli war with Iran. Lebanon's civil defence reported 254 people killed and over 1,100 wounded across the country, making it the deadliest day of the conflict.

stories.title: Syria condemns Israeli assault on Lebanon
stories.summary: Syria's Foreign Ministry condemned Israel's assault on Lebanon, calling the strikes a clear violation of international law and the UN Charter. The ministry demanded an immediate ceasefire and urged the international community to confront Israeli violations.

stories.title: Shippers seek clarity on Hormuz passage as Iran issues fresh warnings
stories.summary: Iran declared that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed to vessels without a permit, despite the ceasefire with the United States, leaving shippers seeking clarity on passage rules.

stories.title: U.S. did not agree that ceasefire would cover Lebanon, Vance says
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance stated that the United States did not agree that the ceasefire with Iran would extend to Lebanon. Vance said Israel had agreed to show restraint in Lebanon but provided no details.

stories.title: As Trump claims victory, Iran emerges bruised but powerful with leverage over Hormuz
stories.summary: Following nearly six weeks of war and a U.S.-Iran ceasefire, analysts say Iran retains significant leverage through its control of the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining influence over global energy markets despite sustaining damage in the conflict.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims attacks on Israel in response to 'ceasefire violations'
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it fired rockets toward northern Israel in response to what it called Israeli ceasefire violations. The rocket attacks followed a large-scale Israeli bombing campaign across Lebanon that killed over 250 people, launched hours after the US-Iran ceasefire was agreed.

stories.title: Italy summons Israeli ambassador after shots fired at UN in Lebanon
stories.summary: Italy summoned the Israeli ambassador on April 8 to demand an explanation after Israeli forces fired shots at an Italian convoy serving with a United Nations mission in Lebanon. Italy's foreign minister warned that Israeli forces had no authority to target Rome's troops.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill four, including Al Jazeera journalist, Gazan medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed four people, including Al Jazeera correspondent Muhammad Washah, according to Gazan health authorities. The strike targeted a vehicle Washah and another Palestinian were driving along a coastal road in Gaza City.

stories.title: Uruguay considers relocating HIF Global's green hydrogen megaplant to ease tensions with Argentina
stories.summary: Uruguay is considering relocating HIF Global's green hydrogen and synthetic fuels megaplant within the department of Paysandú to ease diplomatic tensions with Argentina. The project, estimated at $5.385 billion in its final phase, would be the largest private investment in Uruguay's history.

stories.title: Netanyahu left with vague promises, no clear victories after another war ends without a decisive win
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu emerged from the US-Iran ceasefire process without clear victories, as President Trump moved toward negotiations with Tehran that could potentially fund Iranian rearmament. The outcome followed Israeli military campaigns in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran that did not deliver decisive results.

stories.title: ‘Talks were almost dead’: Pakistan’s last-ditch effort to secure Iran war truce
stories.summary: Pakistan mounted a last-ditch overnight diplomatic effort to prevent the collapse of mediation talks between the United States and Iran, ultimately securing a temporary ceasefire and bringing both sides into direct negotiations.

stories.title: US Senate to vote on resolution to curb Trump’s Iran war powers
stories.summary: The US Senate is preparing to vote on a resolution to curb President Trump's war powers regarding Iran. Trump's Republican allies in Congress have so far almost unanimously backed his policies.

stories.title: US Senate to vote on resolution to curb Trump's Iran war powers
stories.summary: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer announced that U.S. lawmakers will vote next week on a resolution to halt the Iran war and require President Trump to seek congressional approval for further military action.

stories.title: Cultural clashes, ‘unruly crowds’ at Japan’s cherry blossom parties stir overtourism debate
stories.summary: Japan's cherry blossom season has intensified the country's overtourism debate after the conservative Sankei newspaper accused foreign visitors of misbehaving during hanami parties. The report prompted renewed calls for tourists to respect local customs amid broader concerns about managing large numbers of visitors.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s global future depends on diverse talent
stories.summary: A commentary argues that Hong Kong's status as a global hub depends on maintaining diversity in its talent pipeline. Concerns have been raised that the overwhelming majority of applicants under key admission schemes come from mainland China, raising questions about the city's international competitiveness.

stories.title: IMF, World Bank and UN food agency say war is increasing food prices, insecurity
stories.summary: The World Bank, IMF, and UN World Food Programme warned that rising oil, natural gas, and fertilizer prices caused by the Middle East war will drive up global food prices and worsen food insecurity.

stories.title: Russian airline Azimuth nearing bankruptcy – intelligence
stories.summary: Russian airline Azimuth is reportedly nearing bankruptcy, according to intelligence sources. The airline's financial deterioration reflects broader pressures on Russia's aviation sector.

stories.title: Trump criticizes NATO over Iran in meeting with Rutte
stories.summary: During a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, President Donald Trump criticized the alliance for not supporting the US and Israel during attacks on Iran. Rutte responded that a large majority of European countries had fulfilled their obligations.

stories.title: Protesters outside Israeli embassy in London condemn assault on Lebanon
stories.summary: Protesters blocked roads outside the Israeli embassy in London to condemn Israel's military strikes on Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran announces alternative routes to Hormuz Strait, local media reports
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced alternative navigation routes for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz due to the risk of sea mines. The notice advised all ships to follow the new routes to ensure maritime safety.

stories.title: Latin America faces fertilizer vulnerability; IICA and TFI agree joint plan amid Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: The Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture and the US-based Fertilizer Institute announced a joint plan to secure fertilizer supply across the Americas. The partnership responds to logistical disruptions and price volatility caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israel-Iran war.

stories.title: Singapore raises air-con temperatures in public spaces to save energy amid fuel crisis
stories.summary: Singapore's government announced measures to reduce electricity consumption in public facilities, including setting air-conditioning to 25 degrees Celsius or higher. The Ministry of Sustainability and Environment cited the need to bolster energy resilience as the Middle East conflict tightens global energy supplies.

stories.title: ​A respite: On the two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: An editorial urged the United States not to allow Israel to undermine the two-week ceasefire agreement reached between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Mining revolution: China’s 500-tonne ‘underground carrier’ tunnels a kilometre to mine ore
stories.summary: China has developed a 500-tonne boring machine called "Gangtie Jiliang" (Steel Backbone), described as the world's first capable of excavating full-face shafts exceeding 1,000 metres deep in hard rock. The machine measures 8.1 metres wide and is designed for deep underground mining operations.

stories.title: China woman, 89, climbs from 27th to 21st floor of building to escape locked bedroom goes viral
stories.summary: An 89-year-old woman in Beijing climbed from the 27th to the 21st floor on the exterior of her residential building after accidentally locking herself in her bedroom. A cleaner and security guard spotted her clinging to air-conditioner rails and called police for rescue.

stories.title: Sirens sound in Israel after launch detected from Lebanon
stories.summary: Air raid sirens sounded in northern Israel after a launch was detected from Lebanon. The incident followed Israeli military strikes across Lebanon, including intense bombardment of Beirut, despite a two-week ceasefire deal between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Al Jazeera slams killing of journalist in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: Al Jazeera condemned the killing of its correspondent Mohammed Wishah in an Israeli strike in Gaza, calling the attack deliberate rather than random. The network said the strike was intended to intimidate the journalist.

stories.title: Nato chief says Trump ‘clearly disappointed’ by US allies’ refusal to join Iran war
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said President Trump was "clearly disappointed" that US allies refused to join the war against Iran, following a closed-door meeting in Washington. Rutte declined to say whether Trump raised the possibility of withdrawing from NATO over the issue.

stories.title: Wealthy nations slashed development aid in 2025 for second year in row, debt group says
stories.summary: A debt monitoring group reported that wealthy nations cut development aid in 2025 for the second consecutive year, possibly by record amounts, ahead of official data from the OECD.

stories.title: 5 killed, several injured in rain-related incidents in Punjab, KP
stories.summary: Heavy rains and storms across Pakistan's Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces killed at least five people and injured several others, with deaths caused by roof collapses and related incidents in Bhakkar, Sargodha, and Mohmand.

stories.title: Explainer: What we know about US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump reversed his threats to strike Iranian civilian infrastructure on Tuesday evening, leading to a ceasefire agreement. Details of the arrangement between Washington and Tehran remain under scrutiny.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran talks will be held behind closed doors
stories.summary: President Trump announced that U.S.-Iran negotiations would be conducted privately, with talks expected to begin on April 10. He told ABC News the process would move quickly.

stories.title: Kremlin waging propaganda campaign marking 12th anniversary of so-called “DPR” – CCD
stories.summary: Russia launched a large-scale propaganda campaign in occupied Donetsk to mark the 12th anniversary of the self-proclaimed 'Donetsk People's Republic.' The Center for Countering Disinformation noted that Russia is concealing the role of Russian militants and special forces who entered the region in 2014 to seize administrative buildings.

stories.title: US VP JD Vance says Lebanon is not part of the US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that Lebanon is not covered by the ceasefire agreement reached between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad, Rawalpindi for April 9 and 10; essential services to remain operational
stories.summary: District administrations in Islamabad and Rawalpindi declared local holidays on April 9 and 10. Essential services, including those of the Capital Development Authority, will remain operational.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire unlikely to cause major fuel price drop: Hong Kong economists
stories.summary: Hong Kong economists said the two-week US-Iran ceasefire is unlikely to significantly reduce fuel prices without a permanent end to the conflict. Simon Lee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong's Shenzhen Finance Institute cited continuing volatility and uncertainties in the situation.

stories.title: China biotech flow picks up as Everest seals US$250 million deal
stories.summary: Shanghai-based Everest Medicines agreed to a US$250 million deal to acquire a Singapore company holding rights to 14 chronic-disease treatments across the Asia-Pacific region. The investment was backed by sovereign wealth funds from Singapore and the UAE alongside Chinese state-backed investors.

stories.title: Report: Nearly half of Russia’s embassy staff in Hungary may have ties to intelligence services
stories.summary: An investigation by Russian independent outlet Agentstvo found that nearly half of Russia's 47 embassy staff members in Hungary may have ties to intelligence services. Fifteen employees were confirmed to have such connections, while six more are suspected, based on analysis of leaked data spanning several years.

stories.title: Lebanon ceasefire 'will continue to be discussed', US Press Secretary says
stories.summary: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said Lebanon's inclusion in the ceasefire 'will continue to be discussed' between President Trump, Prime Minister Netanyahu, and other parties. Pakistan, which mediated the US-Iran deal, claimed the two-week pause would extend to Lebanon, but conflicting accounts have emerged.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi police arrest 375 people of various nationalities over footage, disinformation
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi police arrested 375 individuals of various nationalities for sharing footage and disinformation. The crackdown is part of a broader Gulf-state effort to control content related to Iran's recent attacks.

stories.title: Israel launches fresh assault on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel launched air strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs at dawn on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported. The attacks followed a massive wave of Israeli strikes across Lebanon that killed at least 254 people, coming just hours after the US-Iran ceasefire was announced.

stories.title: Iran-US truce on brink as Israel pounds Lebanon, Tehran warns of escalation
stories.summary: The two-week truce between Iran and the United States was under severe strain as Israel launched heavy strikes on Lebanon and Tehran threatened renewed hostilities. Lebanese authorities reported at least 182 people killed and nearly 900 wounded. Both Iran and the United States claimed victory despite the escalating violence.

stories.title: Newly created Polymarket accounts win big on well-timed Iran ceasefire bets
stories.summary: A group of newly created accounts on prediction market Polymarket made well-timed bets on a US-Iran ceasefire shortly before it was announced Tuesday, earning hundreds of thousands of dollars. The bets were placed despite few public signals that a deal was imminent.

stories.title: US, Iranian delegations expected in Pakistan on Friday; White House says first round of talks to be held on Saturday
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that U.S. and Iranian delegations will arrive in Pakistan on Friday for peace talks. Iran's President Pezeshkian confirmed Tehran's participation. The White House said the first round of negotiations would be held Saturday.

stories.title: Iran vows to ‘punish’ Israel over Lebanon strikes and ceasefire breach
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Al Jazeera that Tehran will 'punish Israel' for what it described as violations of the ceasefire and attacks on Lebanon. Fars news agency reported that Iran is preparing a military response to the alleged breaches.

stories.title: China-backed solar project powers up in Laos amid Iran war energy shock
stories.summary: China completed the initial phase of a 1-gigawatt solar power project in northern Laos, the country's first large-scale mountainous photovoltaic installation. The project was connected to the grid on Tuesday and is expected to generate about 1.65 billion kilowatt-hours annually amid global energy disruptions.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump threatens action if Tehran fails to comply with deal
stories.summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk described Israel's attacks on Lebanon as horrific, noting they came shortly after a ceasefire agreement had been reached between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Ukrainian paratroopers destroy multiple Russian shelters on Kupiansk axis
stories.summary: Paratroopers from Ukraine's 77th Separate Air Assault Brigade conducted operations on the Kupiansk axis, destroying multiple Russian shelters along with enemy personnel. The unit is part of the 7th Rapid Response Corps of Ukraine's Air Assault Forces.

stories.title: North Korea tests electromagnetic weapon and carbon fibre bomb: state media
stories.summary: North Korea conducted weapons tests over three days from Monday to Wednesday, including trials of an electromagnetic weapon system and a carbon fibre bomb. The tests, overseen by General Kim Jong-sik, were reported by the state-run Korean Central News Agency amid heightened geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Russia’s agricultural oversight agency blames government missteps and harsh weather for livestock disease outbreak
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance (Rosselkhoznadzor) attributed a livestock disease outbreak in the Novosibirsk region to government missteps, an atypical strain of pasteurellosis, and harsh weather. The explanation came in response to a formal inquiry from Communist Party State Duma member Yuri Sinelshchikov.

stories.title: Trump threatens to renew war if Iran doesn’t comply with ‘real agreement’
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to renew military action against Iran if Tehran does not comply with a "real agreement." Meanwhile, Iranian media reported the IRGC released a map guiding ships around mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Hezbollah claimed rocket fire on northern Israel, accusing Israel of breaching the truce.

stories.title: Ecuador recalls ambassador to Colombia in latest diplomatic stir
stories.summary: Ecuador recalled its ambassador to Colombia for consultations after comments by Colombian President that Quito characterized as interference in Ecuadorean affairs. Ecuador's foreign minister announced the diplomatic move on Wednesday.

stories.title: Nearly 200 arrests in Turkey after attack on Israeli consulate
stories.summary: Turkish authorities arrested 198 people with suspected links to ISIS across 34 provinces following an attack on the Israeli consulate in Turkey.

stories.title: Trump announces 50% tariffs on nations supplying Iran with weapons
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced immediate 50 percent tariffs with no exemptions on imports from countries supplying military weapons to Iran. The announcement came in a social media post just hours after the US agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Tehran.

stories.title: Chechen leader says his forces will not fight for Iran because it is also striking Arab allies
stories.summary: Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov declared that his forces would not fight on Iran's behalf in its conflict with the United States and Israel, citing Iran's strikes against Arab allies as a reason.

stories.title: Israel offered to check itself in Lebanon strikes to promote Iran ceasefire, VP Vance claims
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance claimed Israel offered to restrain its strikes in Lebanon to help advance the Iran ceasefire. Vance clarified that Iran mistakenly believed Lebanon was covered by the ceasefire, but that it was not included in the agreement.

stories.title: Trump weighs punishing certain NATO countries over lack of Iran war support - report
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering punishing certain NATO countries for declining to support the US war effort in Iran. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte acknowledged that some alliance members were tested by Washington's criticism and fell short.

stories.title: CAF’s Motsepe welcomes corruption probe after Senegal dispute
stories.summary: Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe said he would welcome a corruption investigation after meeting Senegalese officials in Dakar. Senegal had called for a probe after CAF stripped it of the 2025 AFCON hosting rights and awarded them to Morocco.

stories.title: ‘Israel must be restrained for US-Iran ceasefire to hold’
stories.summary: Former US counterterrorism official Joe Kent warned that Israel could sabotage the US-Iran ceasefire, arguing that Israel must be restrained for the truce to hold.

stories.title: Falling global oil prices increase pressure on Russia – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that falling global oil prices, triggered by a ceasefire announcement in the Middle East, are a positive signal for markets and increase sanctions pressure on Russia's economy.

stories.title: Australia news live: shadow defence minister claims Trump threatened to ‘escalate in order to de-escalate’ in Middle East
stories.summary: Australia's shadow defence minister James Paterson said Iran did not want to see Trump follow through on threats to escalate in order to de-escalate in the Middle East. Paterson expressed reluctance to accept Iran's claim that Lebanon was included in the ceasefire deal.

stories.title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on countries supplying Iran with weapons
stories.summary: President Trump announced that countries supplying Iran with military equipment would face immediate 50 percent tariffs on all goods entering the United States, with no exemptions. China and Russia, both accused of aiding Iran's military buildup, have denied recently providing weapons.

stories.title: Israel pounds Lebanon with heaviest airstrikes of war as Hezbollah pauses attacks
stories.summary: Israel launched its heaviest airstrikes on Lebanon since the conflict began, targeting over 100 Hezbollah command centers and military sites in Beirut, the Bekaa Valley, and southern Lebanon. The strikes killed 112 people and wounded 837, even as Hezbollah paused attacks under a U.S.-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Russian man who joked his way onto ‘foreign agent’ list gets suspended sentence
stories.summary: A Russian court sentenced Marat Nikandrov, a Moscow Region resident who was designated a foreign agent in 2023 after submitting his own application, to eight months on a suspended sentence with a one-year probationary period, according to business outlet RBC.

stories.title: The sticking points in the US-Iran ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Ongoing US-Iran ceasefire talks face sticking points including long-standing disagreements between Tehran and Washington that predate the recent conflict.

stories.title: Vance to lead US negotiators at first round of Islamabad talks with Iran on Saturday
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance will lead US negotiators at the first round of talks with Iran in Islamabad on Saturday. Vance said Tehran had a 'legitimate misunderstanding' about Lebanon's inclusion in the truce, while Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf accused the US of violating understandings.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ceasefire paves way to diplomacy and ending war
stories.summary: President Zelensky said the United States' shift toward diplomacy in the military conflict involving Iran, combined with a ceasefire, creates additional opportunities to end ongoing conflicts and strengthen international security.

stories.title: Seven-year-old killed by drone debris in southwest Iran
stories.summary: A seven-year-old girl was killed in Shushtar, Khuzestan province, in southwest Iran after debris from a drone intercepted by Iranian air defenses struck her location. Six members of her family were also reported injured in the incident.

stories.title: Hungary’s foreign minister offered to send Russia EU document in leaked audio
stories.summary: Leaked audio revealed Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto offering to send a European Union document to his Russian counterpart, telling him he was at Russia's disposal whenever needed.

stories.title: Italy summons Israeli ambassador after shots fired at UN in Lebanon
stories.summary: Italy summoned the Israeli ambassador after Israeli forces fired warning shots at an Italian UN logistics convoy traveling from Shama to Beirut in Lebanon. The convoy was about 2 kilometers from its departure point when the shots were fired.

stories.title: Russian forces attack energy facility in Odesa region
stories.summary: On the evening of April 8, Russian forces used drones to strike an energy facility in Ukraine's Odesa region.

stories.title: Ministers unveil ‘right to try’ plan to help disabled people find work
stories.summary: The UK government introduced legislation allowing disabled people to try work or volunteering without automatically triggering a benefit reassessment. Campaigners welcomed the move but warned it does not sufficiently address hostile workplace conditions.

stories.title: ‘Excessive’ financial risks threaten survival of many English universities, report warns
stories.summary: A report by the Higher Education Policy Institute warns that many English universities face excessive financial risks, including high borrowing levels and rapid student enrollment expansion, threatening not only their own survival but the broader higher education sector.

stories.title: Dutch trial of Syrian man accused of torture during war begins
stories.summary: The trial of Syrian national Rafiq Al Q began in the Netherlands on charges of committing war crimes, including torture, during the Syrian civil war. The defendant claimed that the nine victims, witnesses, and Dutch authorities are 'conspiring against him.'

stories.title: US ignoring evidence Russia is helping Iran because it trusts Putin, says Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alleged the U.S. has ignored evidence that Russia is helping Iran target American bases in the Middle East because Washington trusts Vladimir Putin. He said he had tried to alert the White House to Moscow-Tehran military collaboration.

stories.title: AI fuels global trade growth as China-US flows shift, McKinsey finds
stories.summary: A McKinsey & Company report found that AI-linked goods, including semiconductors, graphics cards, and servers, accounted for roughly one-third of global trade growth last year. Global trade grew 6.5 percent, outpacing the broader world economy, as geopolitical tensions shifted China-U.S. trade flows.

stories.title: Iran says US must choose between ceasefire and continued war
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi demanded the United States choose between upholding the ceasefire or continuing war through Israel, saying both cannot coexist. He wrote on Telegram that the situation in Lebanon is being closely monitored and that 'the ball is in America's court.'

stories.title: 'Ceasefire not holding': US and Iran may have to talk 'as guns are firing'
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire appeared to falter as Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Iranian strikes on Gulf targets jeopardized the agreement. US officials moved to shore up the shaky deal, with reports suggesting the two sides may need to negotiate even as hostilities continue.

stories.title: 'Talks were almost dead': Pakistan's last-ditch effort to secure Iran war truce
stories.summary: Pakistan played a critical last-ditch role in mediating the US-Iran ceasefire, involving direct contact with top officials on all sides. A Pakistani source said the hardest part was convincing Iran to accept a truce without preconditions.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces hold line in Chasiv Yar, prevent enemy advance toward Kostiantynivka – military
stories.summary: Ukrainian troops continue to defend Chasiv Yar, successfully preventing Russian forces from advancing toward the nearby city of Kostiantynivka.

stories.title: Democrats push vote to halt US military action in Iran
stories.summary: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced his party would seek passage of a resolution to halt further US military action in Iran during Thursday's congressional session. Democrats plan to seek approval by unanimous consent, though as the minority party they may face procedural obstacles from the Republican presiding officer.

stories.title: Most Israeli schools to open on Thursday as Home Front Command updates guidelines
stories.summary: Israel's Home Front Command announced that most schools across the country will reopen on Thursday at 6 a.m., with previous limits on public gatherings canceled following the ceasefire.

stories.title: White House confirms U.S.–Iran talks this weekend
stories.summary: The White House announced that Vice President JD Vance and senior U.S. negotiators will travel to Pakistan this weekend for talks with Iran aimed at securing a lasting ceasefire.

stories.title: UN: Israeli fire, Hezbollah IED killed peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: A UN investigation found that Israeli fire and a Hezbollah improvised explosive device were responsible for the deaths of three UN peacekeepers in Lebanon last month. The UN called for those responsible to be held accountable.

stories.title: Netanyahu says ‘finger on trigger’ to resume war any time; opposition accuses him of strategic debacle
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu insisted Israel was not caught off-guard by the US-Iran truce and said his 'finger is on the trigger' to resume war at any time. Opposition leaders accused him of a strategic debacle, while Netanyahu said Iran's enriched uranium would be removed by agreement or resumed fighting.

stories.title: Jewish families and a rabbi ask to join lawsuit to block Oklahoma Jewish charter school
stories.summary: Several Jewish families and a rabbi in Oklahoma have asked to join a lawsuit seeking to block what would be the country's first publicly funded Jewish charter school. The plaintiffs argue the state school board cannot be trusted to defend secular education laws.

stories.title: ‘Deeply concerned’ Australia says Lebanon should be included in Middle East ceasefire
stories.summary: Australia led a joint statement with Brazil, Colombia, Indonesia, Jordan, Sierra Leone, and the UK calling for Lebanon's inclusion in the Middle East ceasefire. Israel carried out its largest attack on Lebanon since the Hezbollah war began, killing at least 254 people and wounding 837.

stories.title: Israel backs US-Iran ceasefire but Netanyahu's war goals remain unfulfilled
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu responded in a muted fashion to the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, contrasting with more triumphal statements from Washington and Tehran. Netanyahu's stated war objectives against Iran remain unachieved despite the truce.

stories.title: Israeli strikes hit multiple areas in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted the areas of Beit Yahoun, al-Jumaijmah, and Majdal Selm in southern Lebanon, according to ground reports.

stories.title: Iranian FM says US must choose between ceasefire, supporting Israeli action against Hezbollah
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed that ceasefire terms explicitly include Lebanon, demanding the US choose between upholding the truce and supporting Israeli operations against Hezbollah. Both President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu have denied Lebanon's inclusion.

stories.title: Chile exposes smuggling ring that shipped US$917m in stolen copper to Chinese buyers
stories.summary: Chilean authorities dismantled a smuggling ring that shipped an estimated $917 million worth of stolen copper to Chinese buyers over five years. The network trucked stolen metal to the northern port city of Iquique and disguised shipments as scrap cargo bound for China.

stories.title: Iran war: is the US shifting away from its strategy of precision strikes?
stories.summary: The article examines whether the U.S. and Israel are shifting away from precision strikes in their war against Iran, noting the targeting of Iran's South Pars gas field and the broader implications for warfare, geopolitics, and energy security.

stories.title: Ukrainian interceptor drones destroy over 33,000 enemy UAVs in March – Defense Minister
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Minister reported that Ukrainian interceptor drones destroyed more than 33,000 Russian unmanned aerial vehicles in March 2026, doubling the previous month's total.

stories.title: Americans question Trump’s instinct on Iran war
stories.summary: American public opinion is divided over President Donald Trump's instinct-driven approach to managing the conflict with Iran. Polls suggest significant disagreement on whether to trust the president's strategy.

stories.title: UN says its envoy is in Iran to support ‘durable’ end to conflict
stories.summary: A personal envoy of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres arrived in Iran as part of a regional tour to support efforts toward a comprehensive and durable resolution to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Crown Prince Pahlavi tells Iranians ceasefire is ‘not a time for despair' but 'belief in victory'
stories.summary: Exiled Iranian Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi urged Iranians to view the ceasefire not as a moment of despair but as evidence that the Iranian regime has suffered a major defeat.

stories.title: Relief at truce gives way to alarm as Israel pounds Lebanon and Iran hits neighbours
stories.summary: Despite both the United States and Iran declaring victory following the ceasefire, their main disputes remained unresolved. Alarm grew as Israel continued strikes on Lebanon and Iran struck neighboring countries.

stories.title: Pakistan expresses concern at storming of Kuwait’s consulate in Basra
stories.summary: Pakistan expressed concern over the storming and vandalism of Kuwait's consulate in Basra, Iraq, calling the act inconsistent with diplomatic norms and international law and urging a thorough investigation.

stories.title: Trump meets NATO’s Rutte as US weighs exit over lack of Iran war support
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte as the administration weighed a possible exit from the alliance over members' lack of support for the Iran war. Reports indicated Trump was also considering withdrawing U.S. troops from some NATO countries.

stories.title: Universities may allow one-time reduction of up to 3pc in MDCAT passing marks to fill vacant seats: PMDC
stories.summary: Pakistan's Medical and Dental Council announced that universities may allow a one-time reduction of up to three percent in MDCAT passing marks to fill vacant seats for the 2025–26 academic session, following a parliamentary committee recommendation.

stories.title: JD Vance says Iran would be ‘dumb’ to let talks collapse over Lebanon
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that Iran had a 'legitimate misunderstanding' about whether Lebanon was included in the ceasefire agreement with the United States. Vance warned that Iran would be 'dumb' to allow negotiations to collapse over the Lebanon issue.

stories.title: Trump and Netanyahu broke Iran’s empire, now they must win at Hormuz - comment
stories.summary: An analysis notes that Iran lost its proxy forces, missiles, and nuclear infrastructure during the conflict but discovered significant leverage through its ability to close the Strait of Hormuz, which carries a fifth of global oil supply.

stories.title: Trump administration signals it is mulling NATO withdrawal after Iran war
stories.summary: The Trump administration has signaled it is considering withdrawing from NATO following the Iran war. President Trump criticized European partners for refusing to contribute military forces to the US-led campaign against Iran.

stories.title: At least 182 killed as Israel strikes central Beirut after saying Iran truce doesn't apply there
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported 182 people killed in Israeli strikes on Wednesday, the highest single-day death toll in the Israel-Hezbollah conflict. Israel struck central Beirut and other areas as a U.S.-Iran ceasefire took effect, with Iran and the U.S. disputing whether Lebanon was covered by the deal.

stories.title: Iran shuts Strait of Hormuz again, threatens to abandon ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran has shut the Strait of Hormuz again and warned it will withdraw from a ceasefire with the United States if Israeli strikes on Lebanon continue.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of ‘reneging’ on ceasefire terms over Lebanon
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei accused the United States of reneging on the ceasefire terms regarding Lebanon. He cited White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt's statement that Lebanon is not included in the two-week agreement, and pointed to Pakistan's assertion that the deal was meant to cover Lebanon.

stories.title: Macron welcomes US-Iran ceasefire and urges Lebanon’s inclusion
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire, calling it 'very good news.' Macron also urged that Lebanon be included in the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Cease-Fire Confusion Over Lebanon
stories.summary: Disputes over the terms of the US-Iran ceasefire agreement have emerged concerning Lebanon, with disagreements about what was actually agreed upon. The confusion threatens to unravel the broader deal before formal talks can proceed.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Israel ready to 'return to battle' against Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that Israel still has objectives to complete against Iran and is ready to 'return to battle' at any moment. His remarks came despite the ceasefire agreed upon the previous day between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Afghanistan, Pakistan agree to avoid escalation: China
stories.summary: China, Afghanistan, and Pakistan held a week of informal meetings in Urumqi, Xinjiang, from April 1 to 7, according to Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning. Afghanistan and Pakistan agreed to avoid escalation in their conflict during the talks.

stories.title: High Court postpones joint protest and Kotel hearings to Friday, resets filing deadlines
stories.summary: Israel's High Court postponed hearings on joint protest petitions and Western Wall access cases to Friday, resetting filing deadlines. The petitions involve wartime restrictions on anti-war demonstrations and limits on worshippers at the Kotel.

stories.title: Iran’s shattered economy means any success in war may be fleeting
stories.summary: Iran's economy has been severely damaged by the recent conflict, with officials estimating that the country's biggest industries could take years to recover.

stories.title: Asia’s flood of cheap Ozempic generics opens gates to weight-loss abuse
stories.summary: Following the expiration of the semaglutide patent in India and China on March 20, a flood of cheap generic versions of Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy weight-loss drugs has entered Asian markets, raising concerns about potential abuse.

stories.title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on countries that supply Iran with weapons
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to impose 50 percent tariffs on countries that supply Iran with weapons. Analysts questioned the legal authority for such tariffs and described the threat as potentially unenforceable.

stories.title: Devastation in Beirut after Israeli strikes reduce homes to rubble
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit Beirut hours after the US-Iran ceasefire was announced, reducing homes to rubble. Residents in the Lebanese capital searched through the destruction for survivors.

stories.title: UN rights chief says Lebanon killings ‘nothing short of horrific’
stories.summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk described the scale of killing and destruction in Lebanon, where at least 254 people died in Israeli attacks, as 'nothing short of horrific.'
