He said the carnage occurring within hours of the Iran ceasefire agreement 'defies belief' and stressed obligations under international humanitarian law.

stories.title: Airline and travel industries see no immediate relief from Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Airline and travel industries reported no immediate relief from the US-Iran ceasefire, as analysts projected it could take months for jet fuel supply chains to recover from the industry's worst crisis in years.

stories.title: Vance says Ukraine conflict has been 'hardest' to solve
stories.summary: US Vice President J.D. Vance described the Ukraine conflict as the hardest to resolve, expressing disappointment with European political leadership for what he characterized as insufficient interest in solving the conflict.

stories.title: US dispatching negotiating team for Iran talks, Tehran signals willingness to hand over uranium
stories.summary: The White House confirmed that Vice President JD Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner will participate in upcoming US-Iran negotiations. Tehran has signaled willingness to hand over enriched uranium as part of a deal.

stories.title: What to know about Israel’s strikes on Lebanon amid US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel launched a massive bombardment on Lebanon the day after the United States and Iran reached a ceasefire agreement. The strikes raised questions about whether Lebanon was covered by the truce.

stories.title: Leaked recordings suggest Szijjártó offered sensitive EU accession document to Russia
stories.summary: Leaked audio recordings suggest Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó offered to share a document related to Ukraine's EU accession process with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

stories.title: US ceasefire with Iran sets diplomatic clock for Trump as war powers deadline nears
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran has set a diplomatic deadline that coincides with the approaching 60-day limit under America's War Powers Resolution for waging war without congressional authorization. The outcome remains uncertain if diplomacy fails.

stories.title: 'Pakistani military calling the shots: Has connections with IRCG, very good relationship with Trump'
stories.summary: Ali Vaez of the International Crisis Group argued that the U.S.-Iran war has shifted power within Iran toward hardline actors, particularly the Revolutionary Guard. From Tehran's perspective, survival against overwhelming military force constitutes a form of victory.

stories.title: JD Vance to lead Iran ceasefire negotiations in Pakistan, White House says
stories.summary: The White House announced that Vice President JD Vance will lead US negotiations with Iran in Pakistan. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt also indicated that Iran has signaled willingness to hand over its highly enriched uranium to the United States.

stories.title: QatarEnergy and Chevron join Shell in Uruguay's offshore oil exploration
stories.summary: QatarEnergy and Chevron have joined Shell as non-operating partners in offshore hydrocarbon exploration blocks off Uruguay's coast, as announced by state energy company Ancap. Their entry reinforces international interest in Uruguay's frontier offshore petroleum potential.

stories.title: Iran to approach peace talks with US with caution, Iranian ambassador to UN says
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations said Tehran would approach the upcoming peace talks with the United States cautiously. He added that the conflict would affect the future legal regime governing the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: He's Australia's most decorated soldier. Now he's at the centre of a historic war crimes case
stories.summary: Ben Roberts-Smith, Australia's most decorated living soldier, is at the centre of a historic war crimes case. Historians describe the proceedings as unprecedented for Australia and extraordinary on a global scale.

stories.title: JD Vance to lead US delegation in Iran talks
stories.summary: The White House announced that Vice President JD Vance will lead the US delegation in talks with Iran, set to begin Friday in Islamabad. The team is expected to include special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

stories.title: Wars impose deep and prolonged economic costs on countries, IMF research finds
stories.summary: Research published by the International Monetary Fund on April 8 found that wars cause an average output decline of roughly 7% over five years in affected countries. The IMF noted that economic scars from armed conflict persist for more than a decade.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz: is a Trump‑Iran joint venture really possible?
stories.summary: Control of the Strait of Hormuz has become the central issue in U.S.-Iran negotiations. President Trump suggested a possible "joint venture" with Iran to safeguard the waterway, attempting to bridge Tehran's push for dominance and Washington's insistence on open passage.

stories.title: Trump has found his Iran off-ramp – but at what cost?
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire has been characterized as an off-ramp for President Trump, though analysts warn the domestic and international consequences of the war will be felt for years.

stories.title: How international media covered Pakistan’s defining role in the US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: International media covered Pakistan's role in brokering the US-Iran ceasefire, with The Independent noting the significant diplomatic optics for Islamabad. The deal came shortly before a deadline set by US President Donald Trump, after PM Shehbaz urged both sides toward negotiations.

stories.title: ‘People are afraid’: Lebanese reeling after Israel’s devastating attacks
stories.summary: Lebanese civilians expressed fear and confusion as Israeli strikes devastated parts of the country. Lebanon's inclusion in the US-Iran ceasefire remains contested between the parties involved.

stories.title: Satellite images show fuel storage tanks at oil terminal on fire in Feodosia following Ukrainian strikes
stories.summary: Satellite imagery confirmed a large-scale fire at fuel storage tanks at the Marine Oil Terminal in Russian-occupied Feodosia, Crimea, following Ukrainian drone strikes.

stories.title: Report: Hungary offered Iran intel on Hezbollah pager attack by Israel
stories.summary: A report revealed that Hungary offered Iran intelligence about Israel's 2024 Hezbollah pager attack in Lebanon. A transcript of a call two weeks after the operation raised concern among Western officials about Budapest's ties to Tehran despite its outwardly pro-Israel stance.

stories.title: Iran attacked Kuwait, UAE after strikes on its oil facilities: State TV
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that Iran attacked Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates following US-Israeli strikes on Iranian oil facilities. The Lavan refinery on a small Gulf island, which processes Iran's highest quality export crude, was among the facilities targeted.

stories.title: Iran re-closes Strait of Hormuz after Israeli strikes in Lebanon, putting ceasefire at risk
stories.summary: Iran suspended tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz shortly after its ceasefire with the United States took effect, responding to continued Israeli strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon. The closure jeopardizes the truce and risks deepening the global energy crisis.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz says US, Iranian delegations will be coming to Pakistan on Friday for talks
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that delegations from the United States and Iran would arrive in Pakistan on Friday for peace talks. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian confirmed Tehran's participation in the Pakistan-offered negotiations following a conversation with PM Shehbaz.

stories.title: ‘Heinous crime’: Al Jazeera condemns Israeli killing of journalist
stories.summary: Al Jazeera condemned what it called a 'heinous crime' after an Israeli drone strike killed its journalist Mohammed Wishah in Gaza.

stories.title: US military says it’s ready to resume fighting if diplomacy fails
stories.summary: The U.S. military signaled it is prepared to resume combat operations against Iran if diplomatic efforts fail. A military official also claimed that Tehran's missile program has been functionally destroyed.

stories.title: Turkish intelligence played a role securing US-Iran ceasefire, media says
stories.summary: Turkish media reported that Turkey's National Intelligence Organization played a role in facilitating the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. The agency reportedly worked to maintain open communication channels between the parties involved.

stories.title: Explainer: What the US, Iran, Israel and Pakistan have said about the ceasefire
stories.summary: The United States, Israel, and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire mediated by Pakistan. U.S. and Iranian officials are expected to hold talks on Friday to discuss terms for a long-term settlement.

stories.title: The One Thing That Terrifies Donald Trump
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that Iran identified a key vulnerability for President Donald Trump during the US-Iran conflict: the impact of hostilities on financial markets. A market downturn linked to the war reportedly created significant political pressure on the administration.

stories.title: Energy crisis not over despite relief rally
stories.summary: Oil prices dropped and stock markets rallied following the announcement of a two-week U.S.-Israel-Iran ceasefire. However, analysts warn the energy crisis is far from over, as damage to regional infrastructure means oil and gas production may take years to recover to pre-war levels.

stories.title: Macron welcomes home two French nationals freed after years in Iran jail
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed home Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris, two French nationals freed after being held in Iran since 2022 on espionage charges. The pair had been detained for nearly four years.

stories.title: White House says NATO ‘failed’ to back war on Iran
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt accused NATO allies of failing to support the US-led war on Iran, saying the alliance had been 'tested and failed.' Her remarks came during a meeting between President Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at the White House.

stories.title: Afghanistan, Pakistan agree to avoid escalation during China-hosted talks: Beijing
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan agreed to avoid escalation in their armed conflict during a week of China-hosted informal meetings held in Urumqi, Xinjiang, from April 1 to 7. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the three delegations engaged in frank and pragmatic discussions.

stories.title: Israel launches most violent strikes on Beirut since start of war
stories.summary: Israel launched what has been described as the most violent air strikes on Beirut since the start of the war. The strikes occurred as Iran-backed Hezbollah claimed it was close to achieving a "historic victory."

stories.title: Taiwan Opposition leader says China visit to sow 'seeds of peace'
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun visited China as the first KMT leader to do so in a decade, hoping to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping. She described the trip as an effort to sow seeds of peace, though the visit sparked debate within Taiwan.

stories.title: Shahar Cohen: ‘My life’ comic laughs about ‘managing the war’ with Nescafe in hand
stories.summary: Israeli comedian and content creator Shahar Cohen discussed life in wartime, drawing humor from his experiences of 'managing the war' as depicted through his popular Israeli and American characters.

stories.title: What is in Iran's 10-point ceasefire agreement plan?
stories.summary: Iran released a 10-point ceasefire agreement plan, but according to a New York Times report citing a US official, the terms in Iran's version do not match those seen by President Trump.

stories.title: The Energy Crisis Won’t End Right Away (Even if the Iran War Does)
stories.summary: Experts warn that even if the US-Iran ceasefire holds, the energy disruptions caused by the conflict will take months to resolve. The war's impact on global energy supplies and markets is expected to persist well beyond any immediate diplomatic resolution.

stories.title: Marta Kos welcomes adoption of important laws in Ukraine
stories.summary: EU Commissioner Marta Kos praised Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada for adopting legislation tied to reforms, citing the country's commitment to its path toward European Union membership.

stories.title: Israel Opposition leaders slam Netanyahu over ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid sharply criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the ceasefire with Iran, calling it an unprecedented political disaster. Lapid said Israel was excluded from decision-making on matters central to its national security.

stories.title: School to reopen across most of Israel Thursday as wartime restrictions eased
stories.summary: Schools are set to reopen across most of Israel on Thursday as wartime restrictions are eased. Restrictions remain in place in northern Israel due to the ongoing threat of Hezbollah rockets, and the IDF warned that rocket fire could still target central and southern areas.

stories.title: ‘Everything will be worse’: Ceasefire leaves some Iranians fearful of greater crackdown
stories.summary: Some Iranian citizens expressed fear that the ceasefire could embolden the Islamic Republic's government to intensify domestic crackdowns. Meanwhile, residents of Gulf states voiced concern about a possible return to hostilities between Iran and the US.

stories.title: NA opposition leader extends ‘unconditional support’ to govt for Middle East peace efforts
stories.summary: Opposition Leader in Pakistan's National Assembly, Mehmood Khan Achakzai, offered unconditional support to the government's Middle East peace efforts. He responded to Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar's request for the opposition to defer a planned protest scheduled for Thursday.

stories.title: Success or surrender? Iran ceasefire exposes rift in Trump’s Maga movement
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire has exposed divisions within Trump's MAGA movement, with some supporters praising the deal and others calling it a betrayal. The Strait of Hormuz remained closed on Wednesday, and Israel launched major strikes on Lebanon despite the truce.

stories.title: Negotiators face huge task to close gaps in rival Iran peace proposals
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiators are working to bridge significant gaps between a 15-point American proposal and a 10-point Iranian counterproposal for a peace deal. The BBC's diplomatic correspondent reports the two plans remain far apart on key issues.

stories.title: Netanyahu: A ‘ceasefire with Iran will not include Hezbollah’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared that the US-Iran ceasefire 'will not include Hezbollah,' in his first public remarks following the agreement. The statement underscored Israel's intent to continue operations against the Lebanese militant group.

stories.title: WATCH: Netanyahu claims Israel was not surprised at last second with Trump's ceasefire
stories.summary: Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that Israel was not caught off guard by President Trump's ceasefire announcement with Iran, claiming the move was coordinated between the two nations.

stories.title: IDF announces St.-Sgt. Touvel Yosef Lifshiz killed in combat in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF announced that Staff Sergeant Touvel Yosef Lifshiz, aged 20, from Beit She'an, was killed in combat in southern Lebanon. He served in the 13th Battalion of the Golani Brigade.

stories.title: Loss of Ukraine means end for Europe – Lithuanian colonel
stories.summary: A Lithuanian colonel warned that a Russian victory in Ukraine could embolden further attacks on European countries and urged the EU to increase its support for Kyiv.

stories.title: Beijing Prefers Peace to Force on Taiwan
stories.summary: Beijing has signaled a preference for peaceful approaches over military force regarding Taiwan. Chinese officials and analysts have framed potential conflict over the island as a tragedy to be avoided rather than a strategic opportunity to be seized.

stories.title: Ukraine’s interceptor drones just set record, as industry has crossed threshold
stories.summary: Ukraine's interceptor drone program has set a new record for shooting down Iranian-made Shahed drones. The country's defense industry is paying drone companies per Shahed destroyed, a model that appears to be yielding results.

stories.title: 5 Unanswered Questions on the U.S.-Iran Cease-Fire
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire faces significant unresolved issues that could undermine its durability. Key questions remain about the terms and implementation of the fragile truce.

stories.title: US-Iran truce: ‘Sensitive behind-the-scenes conversations’ paved way for Pakistan-brokered ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ambassador to France, Mumtaz Zahra Baloch, described the US-Iran ceasefire as a moment of recalibration rather than outright victory for either side. She noted that both Washington and Tehran are constructing competing narratives to maintain political legitimacy. The ambassador emphasized the deal reflects survival dynamics rather than a conventional military outcome.

stories.title: Uganda man says he killed 4 children as human sacrifices in bid to get wealthy
stories.summary: A 39-year-old dual Ugandan-American citizen, Christopher Okello Onyum, admitted in a Ugandan court to stabbing four children to death at a kindergarten, claiming he believed the killings as human sacrifices would make him wealthy.

stories.title: JD Vance says Europe has not made sufficient efforts to end war in Ukraine
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance stated that the United States is disappointed with European leaders, saying they have not made sufficient efforts to help end the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Afghanistan, Pakistan agree to avoid escalation: China
stories.summary: Following a week of discussions hosted by China, Afghanistan and Pakistan agreed to end hostilities and avoid further escalation in their conflict. China described the talks as 'pragmatic and frank.'

stories.title: Italy rules out sending ships to patrol Hormuz Strait without U.N. mandate
stories.summary: Italian Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini announced on April 8 that Italy will not deploy ships to patrol the Strait of Hormuz following the U.S.-Iran ceasefire unless authorized by a United Nations mandate.

stories.title: Norwegian Nobel Committee condemns Russia’s treatment of rights group Memorial
stories.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee condemned Russia's efforts to criminalize Memorial, the human rights organization that co-received the 2022 Nobel Peace Prize. Moscow has sought to designate Memorial as an extremist organization.

stories.title: Can ceasefire hold? US-Iran truce tested before talks start
stories.summary: A ceasefire between the United States and Iran was reached in the final hours before further escalation, following roughly five and a half weeks of conflict. Both sides have claimed victory, though the truce remains fragile and untested ahead of formal negotiations. Observers suggest the war may reshape global perceptions of both nations.

stories.title: World reacts to ‘brutal’ Israeli attacks on Lebanon amid US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli attacks on Lebanon killed at least 254 people and wounded 1,165 others, according to Lebanon's Civil Defence. The strikes drew international condemnation and occurred amid the newly announced US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: US V-P Vance says Ukraine conflict has been ‘hardest’ to solve
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance described the Ukraine conflict as the "hardest" to resolve. On April 8, Kyiv called on the United States to pressure Russia into ending its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel was not informed of US-Iran ceasefire plan until late stages of discussion - report
stories.summary: Israel was reportedly not informed of the US-Iran ceasefire plan until its late stages, according to the Wall Street Journal. A US official said President Trump called Prime Minister Netanyahu shortly before the announcement.

stories.title: France plans 36 billion euro boost to rearmament, nuclear deterrent expansion
stories.summary: France announced plans to increase defense spending by 36 billion euros through 2030 under an updated military planning law. The boost will expand the country's nuclear arsenal and increase missile and drone stocks, driven by security pressures from conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East and uncertainty over U.S. NATO commitments.

stories.title: 'Ketamine Queen' jailed for 15 years over Matthew Perry overdose death
stories.summary: Jasveen Sangha, a British-American drug dealer known as the "Ketamine Queen," was sentenced to 15 years in prison on Wednesday for selling the ketamine that caused actor Matthew Perry's fatal overdose. Sangha reportedly boasted about supplying drugs to an elite circle of Hollywood clients.

stories.title: Trump says US will work closely with Iran, discuss sanctions
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced on April 8 that the United States will work closely with Iran and that the two countries are discussing tariff and sanctions relief. The statement followed the announcement of a two-week ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Trump administration's claims of victory in Iran 'really quite hollow', analyst says
stories.summary: Barbara Slavin of the Stimson Center said the Trump administration's claims of victory in the Iran conflict are "really quite hollow." She noted that while the U.S. can pause attacks temporarily, the administration is seeking a way to end the war and declare success.

stories.title: Russian forces carry out nearly 40 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region since, leaving four people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 40 attacks on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, striking the Nikopol and Synelnykove districts with drones and artillery and injuring four people.

stories.title: First ships through Strait of Hormuz since ceasefire: Monitor
stories.summary: The first commercial ships transited the Strait of Hormuz following the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. Approximately 800 vessels remain stranded in the Gulf awaiting passage.

stories.title: Unsanctioned France cricket team plays international tournament amid 'high' legal risks
stories.summary: France Cricket, which lost its official governing status on January 1, fielded a senior men's team at a ranked international tournament in Portugal. France's sports ministry warned the participation was illegal, and legal experts said organizers face potential civil and criminal liability.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel ready to 'return to battle at any moment' against Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Israel ready to resume military operations against Iran despite the U.S.-Iran truce. Lebanon's civil defense service reported 254 people killed in Israeli strikes across Lebanon on Wednesday.

stories.title: European leaders welcome ceasefire, say it should include Lebanon
stories.summary: Britain and France welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire and called for it to include Lebanon. Both European nations had sought to lead the political process to reopen the Strait of Hormuz after US President Trump criticized European countries for not supporting the war effort.

stories.title: Lapid accuses Netanyahu of achieving 'worst result' in Iran war, 'selling lies' to the US
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid accused Prime Minister Netanyahu of achieving the 'worst result' in the Iran war and 'selling lies' to the United States. Lapid claimed Israel had no influence on the ceasefire agreement or the negotiations that produced it.

stories.title: 5 killed, 22 injured in rain-related incidents in Punjab, KP
stories.summary: Heavy rains and storms across Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over 24 hours killed at least five people and injured 22 others. Roof collapses caused casualties in Bhakkar, Khanewal, Muzaffargarh, and Sargodha, according to Rescue 1122 officials.

stories.title: Iranians breathe a ‘ceasefire’ sigh of relief as all sides claim victory
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran expressed both relief and skepticism following the announcement of a ceasefire between the US and Iran. While celebrations took place, many Iranians voiced doubts about the truce's durability.

stories.title: Russia seeks to restore Soviet Union – Lithuanian colonel
stories.summary: A Lithuanian colonel stated that Russia seeks to restore control over former Soviet territories, calling the capture of Ukraine critically important to that ambition.

stories.title: ‘Unhinged, insane’: US lawmakers call for Trump’s removal via 25th Amendment
stories.summary: Democratic U.S. lawmakers intensified calls to remove President Trump from office by invoking the 25th Amendment, describing his conduct as "unhinged." The push continued despite Trump's announcement of a last-minute ceasefire agreement with Iran.

stories.title: Hungary's Tisza party seen winning two-thirds majority in parliament, Median projection shows
stories.summary: A projection from polling agency Median shows Hungary's opposition Tisza party is on track to win a two-thirds parliamentary majority in Sunday's election. Such a result would allow the party to amend the constitution and key laws needed to unlock EU funds.

stories.title: Turkey’s Roketsan opens new production facilities, delivers missiles to armed forces
stories.summary: Turkey's Roketsan opened new production facilities and delivered missiles to the Turkish armed forces. CEO Murat Ikinci described the facilities as the largest defense industry investments in the history of the Turkish Republic.

stories.title: Iran says Lebanon must be included in ceasefire deal
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Israel's war against Hezbollah in Lebanon must end as part of any ceasefire agreement with the US, contradicting Israeli statements excluding Lebanon from the deal.

stories.title: Democrats and die-hard pro-Israel voices skewer Iran ceasefire, as Republicans back Trump
stories.summary: Republican lawmakers praised the US-Iran ceasefire as a diplomatic success for President Trump, while Democratic lawmakers and pro-Israel voices criticized the agreement, calling it a defeat.

stories.title: As US claims victory, Iran emerges bruised but with leverage over Hormuz
stories.summary: Despite U.S. claims of victory in the Iran conflict, Tehran retains significant leverage through its control of the Strait of Hormuz. The ceasefire has locked in the position of Iran's entrenched government as a key power broker in the region.

stories.title: Relief in financial markets after Iran ceasefire – but it is far from absolute | Richard Partington
stories.summary: Financial markets rallied and oil prices dropped following the announcement of a two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire. However, conflicting messages from Tehran and Washington over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz kept the situation volatile after weeks of energy crisis.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at Rio de Janeiro Olympic Park
stories.summary: Around 60 firefighters and 20 fire trucks responded to a fire at the Velodrome in Rio de Janeiro's Olympic Park early on Wednesday. The blaze was reported by the state's military fire department.

stories.title: Russia says some in EU are helping election rivals of Hungary's Orban
stories.summary: Russia's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that some political forces within the European Union were working against Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's re-election bid and trying to assist his opponents.

stories.title: White House says Trump’s ‘red line’ against Iran nuclear enrichment remains
stories.summary: The White House announced that Vice President JD Vance will lead the US negotiating team for talks with Iran, set to take place in Pakistan on Saturday. Press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that Trump's opposition to Iranian nuclear enrichment remains a firm position.

stories.title: Since beginning of full-scale invasion, 147 media workers killed, and 28 journalists still in captivity – NUJU
stories.summary: The National Union of Journalists of Ukraine reported that 147 media workers have been killed since Russia's full-scale invasion began, and 28 journalists remain in captivity.

stories.title: Iran continues to target Gulf countries despite ceasefire announcement
stories.summary: Iran continued pressuring Gulf countries despite the ceasefire announcement, with demands including control over the Strait of Hormuz and the withdrawal of U.S. combat troops from the region. Reporting from Doha indicated these demands are unlikely to be acceptable to Gulf states.

stories.title: Nearly 5,000 S.African Afrikaners take up Trump refugee offer
stories.summary: Nearly 5,000 white South African Afrikaners have entered the United States under a refugee program launched by President Donald Trump, based on unsubstantiated claims of persecution against the minority group.

stories.title: In Iran, Trump faces the limits of American power | Analysis
stories.summary: Analysts assessed that the US-Israeli war on Iran failed to achieve its declared objectives and instead reinforced Iran's standing as a major regional power in West Asia, particularly in the Persian Gulf, highlighting the limits of American power.

stories.title: Middle East ceasefire threatens to unravel as Israel assaults Lebanon and Iran blocks oil tankers
stories.summary: The two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire appeared at risk on Wednesday as Israel intensified bombing in Lebanon and Iran halted oil tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and Pakistan, which brokered the truce, asserted Lebanon was included in the deal, while Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu disagreed.

stories.title: ‘Ketamine Queen’ gets 15 years in jail for selling Matthew Perry the drugs that killed him
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge sentenced 42-year-old Jasveen Sangha to 15 years in prison for selling actor Matthew Perry the ketamine that caused his fatal overdose in 2023. She is the third defendant sentenced among five who pleaded guilty.

stories.title: Netanyahu says ceasefire with Iran does not apply to Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that any ceasefire with Iran will not extend to Hezbollah and that Israeli forces will continue attacking the group in Lebanon.

stories.title: Report: Kaliningrad cancels Victory Day military parade
stories.summary: Kaliningrad has canceled its Victory Day military parade scheduled for May 9, according to multiple sources cited by local outlet Novy Kaliningrad.

stories.title: Trump says ‘no enrichment’ of uranium in Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared that Iran must not enrich uranium and threatened immediate 50 percent tariffs on countries supplying military weapons to Iran, with no exemptions.

stories.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again after Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Iran re-closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to Israeli strikes on Lebanon, less than 24 hours after agreeing to a ceasefire with the US that had reopened the critical shipping route. The Israeli attacks killed at least 254 people and wounded 1,165.

stories.title: 'Wait-mode drones' can remain dangerous for more than one day – Defense Ministry advisor 'Flash'
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Defense Ministry advisor known as 'Flash' warned that loitering or wait-mode drones can remain dangerous for over 24 hours in power-saving mode. The drones are increasingly used on both front lines and rear areas.

stories.title: Cricket NSW says David Warner aware of ‘seriousness’ of drink-driving charges
stories.summary: Former Australian cricket opener David Warner, 39, was charged with drink-driving after allegedly recording more than twice the legal blood-alcohol limit during a random breath test in Sydney. Cricket New South Wales said Warner was aware of the seriousness of the charges and is due in court on May 7.

stories.title: Iran war: who gained ground, who lost influence
stories.summary: The war involving Iran has reshaped regional power balances beyond the Persian Gulf, with some states gaining leverage and others losing influence, while civilians bear the heaviest toll.

stories.title: US V-P Vance says Trump is ‘impatient’ about progress on Iran
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that President Trump is "impatient" about the pace of progress on Iran and has instructed his negotiating team to "work in good faith" during ceasefire talks.

stories.title: A Russian children’s dance group won a competition after performing a routine set to Putin’s speech announcing the war against Ukraine
stories.summary: A Russian children's dance group from Shebekino, Belgorod region, won the grand prize at Sochi's Crystal Magnolia festival in late March for a routine performed to Vladimir Putin's speech announcing the war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Iran’s enriched uranium will be removed, by agreement or in resumed fighting
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Iran's enriched uranium will be removed either through agreement or resumed military operations. He said the campaign against Iran was coordinated with the US and that the fight against Hezbollah would continue.

stories.title: Ukraine renews attacks on Russian energy sites - what has been hit?
stories.summary: Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian energy facilities in recent weeks as peace negotiations have stalled. The strikes target energy infrastructure across Russia.

stories.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again as Israel pounds Lebanon, air defense systems go off in Tehran
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again and air defense systems were activated in Tehran and Alborz province less than 24 hours after the ceasefire announcement with the U.S. and Israel. Correspondents in Tehran described the events as early signs of the truce's fragility.

stories.title: Trump backs Israel, says Lebanon a ‘separate skirmish’ after ceasefire
stories.summary: Following Israeli strikes on Beirut, President Donald Trump said Lebanon is not covered by the US-Iran ceasefire, describing the conflict there as a 'separate skirmish.' Trump expressed support for Israel's military operations.

stories.title: Africa: Governments Push for Increased Local Control of Africa's Gold
stories.summary: Ghana's government is increasing local ownership in the gold sector, taking over Gold Fields Ltd.'s Damang mine on April 18 after declining to renew its lease and restricting bids to Ghanaian-owned companies.

stories.title: How Trump’s promise to ‘wipe out’ Iran could backfire on US power
stories.summary: Amid escalating tensions, analysts are examining whether President Trump's threat to 'wipe out' Iran could undermine US strategic power and credibility on the global stage.

stories.title: Democrats renew push to curb Trump’s Iran war as calls to use 25th amendment mount
stories.summary: More than 70 Democratic U.S. lawmakers called for invoking the 25th Amendment to remove President Trump from office amid the Iran war. Democratic leaders also pledged to renew efforts to pass war powers resolutions to curb Trump's military actions.

stories.title: 'Ketamine Queen' sentenced to 15 years in death of 'Friends' star Matthew Perry
stories.summary: A Los Angeles drug dealer known as the "Ketamine Queen" was sentenced to 15 years in prison for her role in supplying the ketamine that caused actor Matthew Perry's fatal overdose.

stories.title: Trump's 'Apocalypse Now' is a busted flush. Iran has proved it and China knows it
stories.summary: Analysts suggest the fate of the US-Iran ceasefire depends on developments at the Strait of Hormuz and whether Israel continues its military operations in Lebanon. The situation has raised questions about the durability of the truce.

stories.title: Russian Preschools to Roll Out Patriotic Lessons This Fall
stories.summary: Russian authorities announced that patriotic lessons called "Kind Games," focused on "spiritual and moral values," will be introduced in preschools beginning this fall.

stories.title: Beijing Is Trying to Break U.S. Narratives Over Taiwan
stories.summary: Beijing held a key meeting with Taiwan's opposition in an effort to present an alternative model of cross-strait stability. The engagement is part of China's broader strategy to counter U.S. narratives regarding Taiwan.

stories.title: California sheriff who seized ballots ordered to halt election investigation
stories.summary: The California Supreme Court ordered Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco to pause his investigation into alleged election fraud after he seized over half a million 2025 election ballots. Attorney General Rob Bonta argued the sheriff had no authority over election materials.

stories.title: USF strike Russian Tor-M2 air defense system and drone depots in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's 413th Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment struck a Russian Tor-M2 surface-to-air missile system along with drone depots and a pre-flight preparation site in Russian-occupied areas of Donetsk region.

stories.title: From spiralling war to ceasefire: How Pakistan emerged as peacemaker between US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan emerged as a key intermediary between the United States and Iran, helping secure a temporary ceasefire across the Middle East including Lebanon. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that the two-week truce would be followed by peace talks hosted in Islamabad.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Al Jazeera journalist in Gaza City
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on a vehicle in Gaza City killed Al Jazeera Mubasher correspondent Mohammed Wishah. His death brings the number of Palestinian journalists killed since October 2023 to 262.

stories.title: Alleged Syrian militia member tells trial he did not torture prisoners
stories.summary: A Syrian man accused of crimes against humanity appeared before Dutch judges in The Hague on Wednesday. He denied torturing or beating prisoners while allegedly serving as a member of a pro-government militia under former president Bashar al-Assad's regime.

stories.title: France plans $53.6 billion boost to rearmament, nuclear deterrent expansion
stories.summary: France announced plans for a $53.6 billion boost to its defense capabilities, including an expansion of its nuclear deterrent arsenal and increased stocks of missiles and drones.

stories.title: How Pakistan Helped Secure a Cease-Fire in Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan helped broker the U.S.-Iran ceasefire and has offered to host subsequent peace talks. Analysts note the truce remains fragile despite Islamabad's diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: How Pakistan secured ‘biggest diplomatic win in years’ with Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan played a central role in brokering the U.S.-Iran ceasefire after more than two weeks of negotiations. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Pakistani officials pursued intensive diplomacy that analysts describe as Islamabad's biggest diplomatic achievement in years.

stories.title: ‘A lot of work to do’ to reopen Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated that significant work remains to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Iran ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Trump meets NATO chief as Iran war strains alliance
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump hosted NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at the White House on Wednesday as the war with Iran has strained relations among alliance members. The meeting took place amid a broader crisis within NATO over the US approach to the conflict.

stories.title: Evangelicals amplify Trump’s religious framing of Iran war
stories.summary: Evangelical Christian leaders in the United States have amplified President Trump's religious framing of the Iran war, casting the conflict as a struggle between good and evil.

stories.title: Russia says it welcomes Iran ceasefire, hopes US will now resume Ukraine talks
stories.summary: Russia welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire and expressed hope that Washington would now resume peace talks on Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also welcomed the ceasefire announcement.

stories.title: Absence of conscription poses threat to EU’s defense capabilities, says Lithuanian colonel
stories.summary: A Lithuanian colonel argued that the absence of conscription in EU member states poses a significant threat to Europe's collective defense capabilities and called for expanding defense industry capacity across the bloc.

stories.title: Army Data Operations Center is open for requests
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's Data Operations Center announced it is accepting requests to support divisions by handling data tasks. The center aims to relieve operational data teams so they can focus on their commanders' priorities.

stories.title: Starmer says UK wants to help with opening of Hormuz strait on Gulf visit
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited an airbase in Taif, Saudi Arabia, and said Britain has a role in helping reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian reports indicated the key shipping route had closed again hours after the ceasefire announcement.

stories.title: ‘It’s not AI, it’s real’: shock as RSPCA releases images of 250 dogs found at property
stories.summary: The RSPCA recovered more than 250 dogs from a single property at an undisclosed location in the UK, with 87 taken in by the RSPCA and the remainder by the Dogs Trust. The charity denied allegations that the disturbing images were generated by artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 254, injure 1,165: Civil Defense
stories.summary: Lebanon's Civil Defense reported that Israeli strikes killed 254 people and injured 1,165 across the country. Beirut recorded the highest casualties with 92 deaths and 742 injuries, while southern suburbs saw 61 killed and 200 wounded.

stories.title: Ecuador recalls its ambassador from Colombia over Jorge Glas comments
stories.summary: Ecuador recalled its ambassador from Colombia following comments related to former Vice President Jorge Glas. The move reflects growing tensions between Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa and Colombian President Gustavo Petro.

stories.title: Bangladesh FM in India, most senior visit since 2024 uprising
stories.summary: Bangladeshi Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman met Indian counterpart Subrahmanyam Jaishankar in New Delhi on Wednesday, marking the most senior Dhaka visit since the 2024 uprising that toppled Sheikh Hasina. Issues including extradition, trade, water sharing, and border security were on the agenda.

stories.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad for April 9 and 10; essential services to remain operational
stories.summary: The Islamabad district administration declared local holidays on April 9 and 10 in the federal capital. Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon announced that essential services, including the Capital Development Authority and Islamabad Capital Territory Administration, would remain operational.

stories.title: How we got here: Inside Pakistan’s backchannel diplomacy that led to the US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan conducted weeks of quiet backchannel diplomacy between the United States and Iran, facilitating communication through hours-long calls and privately refined proposals. These largely unseen efforts culminated in the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on Wednesday.

stories.title: Five weeks of devastation: Counting the cost across the Mideast
stories.summary: Five weeks of war across the Middle East have killed thousands of people and destroyed key infrastructure, military bases, and residential buildings throughout the region.

stories.title: Poland detains third suspect over arson attack on Czech factory
stories.summary: Poland detained a third suspect in connection with an arson attack on an optics and drones factory in the Czech Republic last month. A special services spokesman confirmed the arrest on Wednesday.

stories.title: War update: 43 clashes on front lines; Pokrovsk sector sees fiercest battles
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 43 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front lines, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector of the Donetsk region.

stories.title: A defiant Hasan Piker boosts Michigan Senate candidate Abdul el-Sayed in rallies taking on Israel
stories.summary: Leftist Twitch streamer Hasan Piker rallied support for Michigan Senate candidate Abdul el-Sayed at events critical of Israel. Leading Democrats have called on the party to distance itself from Piker.

stories.title: Britain breaks solar energy record twice as UK’s biggest solar farm gets approval
stories.summary: Britain set consecutive solar energy records on Monday and Tuesday, with solar farms across England, Wales, and Scotland generating up to 14.4 GW of electricity during sunny spring weather. The previous record of 14 GW was set in July of the prior year.

stories.title: ‘Why my child?’: Yemen’s Taiz mourns sniper’s killing of teen
stories.summary: A teenager was killed by a suspected Houthi sniper while heading to school in the city of Taiz, Yemen. The incident has sparked grief and outrage among local residents.

stories.title: Air defences activated in Tehran after ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that air defenses were activated in Tehran despite the two-week ceasefire agreement between the US and Iran, signaling early strains in the truce.

stories.title: Turkey detains 10 suspects over Istanbul gun attack outside Israeli consulate: Media reports
stories.summary: Turkish authorities detained 10 suspects in connection with a gun attack outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. Officials have not yet disclosed a motive for the assault.

stories.title: How NATO’s Air Defense Future Is Unfolding
stories.summary: Analyst Shaan Shaikh revisits his 2024 framework outlining three potential directions for NATO air and missile defense development. The reassessment comes amid ongoing alliance tensions and active conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East that have reshaped the defense landscape since his original analysis.

stories.title: How NATO’s Air Defense Future is Unfolding
stories.summary: Analyst Shaan Shaikh revisited his 2024 assessment of three potential directions for NATO air and missile defense development. The reassessment comes amid ongoing alliance tensions and conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East two years after the original analysis.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires at North, fragment falls in open area, no injuries
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired projectiles toward northern Israel, with fragments landing in an open area and causing no injuries. Iran had also launched missiles at Israel hours after President Trump announced a two-week ceasefire.

stories.title: Lebanon: Reopening main Syria border crossing closed over Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon reopened the Masnaa border crossing with Syria after it was closed due to Israeli threats. The crossing is a key trade route and has been restored under tight security measures.

stories.title: Iran shuts Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for Israeli strikes on Hezbollah - report
stories.summary: Iran's navy reportedly shut down the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for Israeli strikes on Hezbollah, warning that any vessel attempting to transit would be targeted and destroyed.

stories.title: Zelensky, welcoming Iran de-escalation, says Ukraine ready for ceasefire with Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the US-Iran de-escalation and said Ukraine was ready for a ceasefire with Russia, stating Kyiv would "respond in kind" if Moscow ceased its strikes.

stories.title: Thailand confirms three deaths from vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Thailand confirmed three Thai crew members died when their cargo vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Twenty other crew members were rescued by the Omani navy following the incident.

stories.title: Iran Strait of Hormuz warning adds to shipping uncertainty
stories.summary: BBC Verify analysis shows that only a few vessels have crossed the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Iran ceasefire deal was announced, reflecting continued uncertainty for international shipping through the critical waterway.

stories.title: Major reaction to news of Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: The United States and Iran confirmed a two-week ceasefire following mediation by Pakistan. The agreement prompted widespread international reaction on April 8.

stories.title: Pope Leo praises Iran war ceasefire after criticising Trump’s threat
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV praised the US-Iran ceasefire after having previously criticized President Trump's threats against Iran. The pope urged continued negotiations to achieve a permanent end to the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine follows established procedure and deadlines in nominating ICC candidate, says Mudra
stories.summary: Deputy Head of Ukraine's Presidential Office Iryna Mudra stated that Ukraine followed established procedures and deadlines in nominating a candidate to the International Criminal Court, noting that a selection committee identified two candidates on April 8.

stories.title: Counting the cost of the Iran war in Iraqi Kurdistan
stories.summary: Waves of drone and missile strikes during the US-Iran war caused significant economic damage across Iraqi Kurdistan, disrupting commerce and deepening political tensions between the Kurdistan Regional Government in Erbil and the central government in Baghdad.

stories.title: What does the US-Iran ceasefire mean for the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Uncertainty remains over operations through the Strait of Hormuz following the two-week ceasefire between the United States, Israel, and Iran. The strategic waterway's status is a key concern for global energy markets and shipping.

stories.title: Bloomberg: Russia’s weekly oil export revenue reaches highest level since June 2022
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported on April 8 that Russia's weekly oil export revenue reached its highest level since June 2022, driven by rising prices and increased shipment volumes.

stories.title: Rohingya activist urges Muslim world to oppose Myanmar junta
stories.summary: Rohingya activist Yasmin Ullah called on the Muslim world to oppose Myanmar's military junta after filing a genocide complaint in Indonesia against the country's president-elect over the persecution of the Rohingya people.

stories.title: Why ceasefire deal with US has unsettled Iran's hardliners
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran has opened the possibility of direct negotiations but has angered hardliners within Iran's leadership, according to BBC News Persian's Kasra Naji.

stories.title: Anthropic says its latest AI model can expose weaknesses in software security
stories.summary: Anthropic announced that its unreleased AI model, Claude Mythos, has identified thousands of previously unknown software vulnerabilities in commonly used applications. The company formed an alliance with cybersecurity specialists to strengthen defenses and is withholding wide distribution of the model.

stories.title: Watch: Fire damages roof of Rio's Olympic velodrome
stories.summary: A fire damaged the roof of the Olympic velodrome in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Approximately 80 firefighters and 20 fire trucks responded to the blaze. The state military fire department confirmed no injuries were reported.

stories.title: Russia says it welcomes Iran ceasefire, hopes U.S. will now resume Ukraine talks
stories.summary: Russia welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire agreement and expressed hope that the United States would now resume negotiations on the Ukraine conflict. Kremlin spokesman said Russia supported the decision not to proceed further with armed escalation.

stories.title: Settlers establish first outpost within Jerusalem city limits
stories.summary: Jewish settlers established the first settlement outpost within the municipal boundaries of Jerusalem. In recent days, dozens of extremists from the encampment have carried out attacks on residents of two nearby Palestinian villages.

stories.title: Civilians under fire by gangs in Gaza: What happened in Maghazi?
stories.summary: Armed men raided the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza, reportedly with support from the Israeli army. Civilians in the camp came under fire during the operation.

stories.title: Fearing loss of control, Israel reluctantly backs US-Iran ceasefire but keeps Hezbollah fight out of it
stories.summary: Israel expressed reluctant support for the US-Iran ceasefire but insisted that its fight against Hezbollah in Lebanon remains outside the scope of the truce. Israel's key objective is to prevent the US from making significant concessions to Iran.

stories.title: Report: Russian military recruiters pressure underage college students to pledge future enlistment
stories.summary: Reports indicate that military recruiters in Russia's Krasnodar Krai are pressuring underage college students to sign pledges committing to future enlistment with the Defense Ministry, according to the student rights project Molnia.

stories.title: A pause, not an end: What the two-week ceasefire with Iran really means - opinion
stories.summary: Analysts describe the two-week Iran ceasefire as a pause rather than a resolution. Washington views the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz as a strategic achievement, while Iran gains temporary breathing room.

stories.title: Trump claims victory in Iran — but is this really a win?
stories.summary: President Trump has claimed total victory over Iran following the ceasefire announcement, though no formal terms have yet been negotiated. Analysts and observers have questioned whether the outcome constitutes a genuine win for the United States.

stories.title: Jet fuel supplies to take 'months' to recover from war: IATA
stories.summary: The International Air Transport Association warned that jet fuel supplies could take months to recover even after the Iran ceasefire, citing significant refinery damage caused during the conflict.

stories.title: Bowen: Ceasefire means respite for civilians, but it might not last long
stories.summary: A ceasefire in the Middle East has provided temporary relief for civilians, but BBC international editor Jeremy Bowen notes that the war and its consequences are reshaping the region, and a lasting peace deal remains uncertain.

stories.title: Israeli attack kills Al Jazeera journalist Mohammed Wishah in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed Al Jazeera Mubasher correspondent Mohammed Wishah west of Gaza City while he was driving on a main road.

stories.title: Egypt farmers face crisis as Hormuz disruption drives costs up
stories.summary: Egyptian farmers are facing a growing crisis as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz drive up fertiliser and energy costs, raising fears of a broader food crisis across the country.

stories.title: Lebanon PM welcomes US-Iran ceasefire as Israeli strikes hit Beirut
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam expressed optimism about de-escalation following the US-Iran ceasefire deal, even as Israeli strikes continued to hit targets in Beirut.

stories.title: Beirut doctor reports 'massive influx of casualties'
stories.summary: A doctor at Beirut's largest public hospital reported a massive influx of casualties following Israel's wave of air strikes on Lebanon. Safa Bleik, a medical coordinator with Médecins Sans Frontières, said emergency rooms were receiving large numbers of wounded, including children with shrapnel injuries.

stories.title: Netherlands not planning to bar Kanye West over antisemitic outbursts
stories.summary: The Dutch government said it is not planning to bar rapper Kanye West from the Netherlands despite his history of antisemitic remarks and a ban imposed by the United Kingdom.

stories.title: PSX gains 14,000 points amid investor glee over US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index surged approximately 14,138 points, or 9.32 percent, closing at 165,811 on Wednesday as investors reacted to the US-Iran ceasefire announcement. Trading was temporarily suspended after the index initially jumped over 8 percent shortly after opening.

stories.title: Iraq’s Pro-Iran Groups Aren’t Going Anywhere
stories.summary: Pro-Iran militia groups in Iraq remain deeply embedded in the country's most powerful political and security networks. Analysts assess these groups are unlikely to diminish in influence despite broader regional developments.

stories.title: Iran signals possible ceasefire withdrawal amid reports of strikes
stories.summary: Iran signaled it may withdraw from the ceasefire agreement with the United States, citing what it views as Israeli violations. Iran's IRGC reported downing an Israeli drone over Fars province, and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted.

stories.title: Trump halts Iran attacks after talks with PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir; US, Iran reach ceasefire agreement
stories.summary: Pakistan announced that the United States and Iran, along with their allies, agreed to an immediate ceasefire including in Lebanon, and invited delegations to Islamabad on April 10 for further talks. The breakthrough followed engagement by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir.

stories.title: Russia Summons Japan’s Ambassador Over Ukraine Drone Deal
stories.summary: Russia summoned Japan's ambassador after Terra Drone Corporation, a Japanese firm, announced a strategic investment in Kharkiv-based Amazing Drones, a Ukrainian company that develops and manufactures interceptor drones.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on two oil depots in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its defense forces struck oil depots in the occupied Crimean cities of Feodosiia and Hvardiiske during overnight operations on April 8.

stories.title: First ships pass through Strait of Hormuz since ceasefire: monitor
stories.summary: Two ships — the Greek-owned bulk carrier NJ Earth and the Liberia-flagged Daytona Beach — passed through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran agreed to reopen the waterway as part of the US-Iran ceasefire deal, according to maritime monitor MarineTraffic.

stories.title: Tehran raises Israeli ceasefire breaches during Pakistan talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi raised allegations of Israeli ceasefire violations during talks with Pakistani mediators, warning that Iran may withdraw from the ceasefire agreement if breaches continue.

stories.title: India welcomes ceasefire, stresses dialogue and diplomacy
stories.summary: Government calls for de-escalation and unimpeded navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, does not acknowledge Pakistan’s role in U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks

stories.title: Russia’s defense ministry says drone forces commanders may discharge student recruits after 1 year but are not required to
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed that commanders of drone forces units have the authority to discharge contract servicemembers after one year but are not obligated to do so, according to an official response reviewed by a legal rights organization.

stories.title: At least 89 killed, over 800 wounded in latest Israeli attacks on Lebanon: Health ministry
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported at least 89 people killed and over 800 wounded in the latest wave of Israeli attacks on Lebanon, according to figures shared with Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Kurdistan Region of Iraq hopes ceasefire brings end to drone, missile attacks
stories.summary: The Kurdistan Region of Iraq expressed hope that the ceasefire would end drone and missile attacks. Since the war began, Tehran directed its allied militias in Iraq to target the region, including US forces stationed there.

stories.title: Is conditional ceasefire a victory for US or Iran?
stories.summary: Both the US and Iran have claimed victory following a conditional ceasefire. Iran stated it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and said its military gains would be consolidated in upcoming negotiations.

stories.title: Pakistan takes on role of peacemaker, but it comes with risks - analysis
stories.summary: Pakistan assumed a mediating role in the Iran ceasefire alongside Turkey, Qatar, and China. Analysts note the risks involved and question whether Pakistan can sustain the trust needed for lasting peace.

stories.title: From Drug Dealer to the Sinaloa Cartel’s Highest-Ranking Woman
stories.summary: U.S. prosecutors targeted the Sinaloa Cartel's inner circle in the late 2010s, during which Guadalupe Fernández Valencia rose as a key figure managing northbound narcotics shipments and southbound cash flows for the organization.

stories.title: 'Islamic bomb': The secret Pakistani scheme to make Iran a nuclear power
stories.summary: Pakistani nuclear scientist Abdul Qadeer Khan, who was monitored by Israel's Mossad, sought to transfer nuclear technology to Iran as part of a scheme to create an "Islamic bomb" to challenge Western power.

stories.title: Starmer heads to Gulf, welcomes Iran war truce
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer traveled to the Gulf region to support the Iran ceasefire, with a focus on securing key shipping routes and promoting regional stability.

stories.title: Oil prices plunge, stocks surge against backdrop of Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Oil prices dropped sharply and Wall Street's major indexes surged more than two percent following the announcement of the US-Iran ceasefire. However, oil prices remain significantly higher than pre-war levels due to the risk of resumed hostilities.

stories.title: Ben Gurion Airport to fully reopen as Israel lifts flight restrictions after ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel announced it will fully reopen Ben Gurion Airport and lift flight restrictions following the ceasefire. Israeli carriers El Al, Israir, and Arkia are preparing to expand operations, though foreign airlines are expected to wait for further clarity on the truce.

stories.title: Nobel Prize Committee condemns Russian move to criminalise rights group
stories.summary: The Nobel Prize Committee condemned Russia's move to criminalize the human rights group Memorial, which co-won the 2022 Nobel Peace Prize for documenting human rights abuses in Russia.

stories.title: Trump: Lebanon not part of ceasefire
stories.summary: President Donald Trump confirmed in a PBS interview that Lebanon was excluded from the US-Iran ceasefire deal. Trump described Israel's continued military operations in Lebanon as a "separate skirmish" and indicated he accepted Israel's ongoing strikes.

stories.title: Guadalupe Fernández Valencia, alias ‘La Patrona’
stories.summary: Guadalupe Fernández Valencia, known as "La Patrona," became one of the highest-ranking women within Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking organizations in the Western Hemisphere.

stories.title: China's Foreign Minister to visit North Korea between April 9 and 10
stories.summary: Beijing has worked to draw Pyongyang back into its orbit, after the COVID-19 pandemic froze exchanges and as North Korean leader Kim Jong ‌Un shored up relations with Moscow, sending troops and weapon

stories.title: Five minors tried in Sweden over Iran dissident murder plot
stories.summary: Five teenagers went on trial in Sweden over an alleged plot to assassinate an Iranian dissident researcher. Prosecutors have alleged links between the suspects and organised crime networks.

stories.title: EU welcomes US-Iran ceasefire, urges efforts to create lasting agreement
stories.summary: European Union leaders welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire, describing it as "a step back from the brink." They urged efforts to establish a lasting agreement and called for the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Kuwait reports damage at oil facilities, power stations after Iranian drone attack
stories.summary: Kuwait's interior ministry reported severe material damage to oil facilities, power stations, and water desalination plants following an Iranian drone attack. Fires broke out at several of the targeted sites operated by Kuwait Petroleum Corporation.

stories.title: WP: Hungary is sharing intelligence with Iran, while Vance flies to Budapest to back its leader amid election campaign
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that Hungary has been sharing intelligence with Iran. Vice President JD Vance traveled to Budapest to support Hungarian leader Viktor Orbán during an election campaign.

stories.title: More than 15 countries planning to facilitate Strait of Hormuz access, Macron says
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said approximately 15 countries were planning to facilitate the resumption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement followed the US-Iran ceasefire, which included provisions for reopening the waterway that normally carries a fifth of global oil supply.

stories.title: Five things to watch amid the ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: Key issues to monitor following the Iran ceasefire include the situations in Lebanon and Iraq, the role of Vice President JD Vance, domestic US political fallout, and the details of Iran's proposed 10-point plan.

stories.title: Yair Lapid: ‘Netanyahu led us into a strategic debacle,’ sold lies to the Americans
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid delivered a televised address accusing Prime Minister Netanyahu of leading Israel into a "strategic debacle" and deceiving both Israeli citizens and American partners regarding the Iran war.

stories.title: St. Petersburg Court Jails Former Members of Youth Activist Group Vesna
stories.summary: A St. Petersburg court convicted former members of the youth activist group Vesna on charges including extremism and spreading "war fakes," sentencing them to varying prison terms.

stories.title: 'Political disaster': Fury in Israel at Trump's Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leaders criticised Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the terms of the US-brokered Iran ceasefire, accusing him of failing to achieve Israel's stated war objectives.

stories.title: US man pleads guilty to murdering 7 women and admits he killed another
stories.summary: Rex Heuermann, a 62-year-old Long Island architect, pleaded guilty to murdering seven women and admitted to killing an eighth in the long-unsolved Gilgo Beach serial killings. He will be sentenced to life in prison without parole at a later date.

stories.title: Iran struck Saudi oil pipeline hours after ceasefire: Report
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps struck Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline with missiles and drones hours after the ceasefire agreement, according to Reuters. The pipeline is currently Saudi Arabia's sole crude oil export route, and damage is being assessed.

stories.title: Power cuts to be in effect in all regions of Ukraine this evening
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities announced scheduled power cuts across all regions of the country, to be in effect from 7:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.

stories.title: Trump’s EPA chief Zeldin gives keynote speech at climate-denying group’s event
stories.summary: U.S. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin delivered the keynote speech at a conference hosted by the Heartland Institute, a group known for denying climate science. The Heartland Institute previously compared climate advocates to the Unabomber in a 2012 billboard campaign.

stories.title: Hegseth’s Divine War
stories.summary: Experts told a news outlet that U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is using the military to promote Christian nationalism. The characterization followed Hegseth's references to divine providence when discussing the U.S. military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Hegseth claims Iran ‘begged’ for ceasefire after US and Tehran agree to two-week pause
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed Iran "begged" for the ceasefire during his first Pentagon press briefing since the war began 40 days earlier. Hegseth said Iran's weapons factories had been reduced to rubble and its military rendered ineffective for years.

stories.title: Why Trump Mishandled Iran
stories.summary: Analysis suggests President Donald Trump's approach to the Iran conflict was shaped by following other world leaders or personal instinct rather than relying on U.S. intelligence officers and policy experts.

stories.title: UK ban on Ye sparks criticism as Starmer stays silent over US threats to destroy Iran
stories.summary: The UK Home Office banned US rapper Ye, formerly Kanye West, over past antisemitic remarks. Critics noted Prime Minister Keir Starmer's silence regarding US threats to destroy Iran while acting swiftly on the rapper's entry ban.

stories.title: Israel's attacks on Beirut 'much bigger than anything we've seen in this war or the previous one'
stories.summary: Independent journalist Rania Abouzeid described Israel's attacks on Beirut as far exceeding anything seen in the current or previous wars. Strikes have expanded beyond the southern suburbs to crowded, mixed residential areas filled with displaced people, with hospitals overwhelmed by casualties.

stories.title: US forces will be ‘hanging around’ Middle East after Iran ceasefire, Hegseth says
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said American forces will remain in the Middle East after the Iran ceasefire to enforce the agreement. Despite the U.S. military's air campaign, Iran has maintained a defiant posture.

stories.title: Delta CEO braces flyers for higher fares amid surge in oil prices tied to Iran war
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian warned passengers to expect higher fares due to surging oil prices linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. The airline projected a $2 billion increase in fuel costs for the current quarter but forecast 10% revenue growth amid strong passenger demand.

stories.title: Ethiopian police arrest human trafficking ring responsible for 3,000 victims
stories.summary: Ethiopian police arrested members of a human trafficking network that had been under investigation since 2018. The ring recruited approximately 3,000 young victims from Ethiopia, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti, Kenya, and Somalia seeking to migrate to Europe through Libya.

stories.title: Lebanon: How Hezbollah is rising from the ashes
stories.summary: Hezbollah has regrouped following the 2024 war in Lebanon, acquiring new weapons and commanders while adopting a guerrilla strategy. Reports indicate Israeli forces have struggled to adapt to the group's revamped military approach.

stories.title: How Pakistan managed to get the US and Iran to a ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan conducted backchannel diplomatic talks that led to a temporary ceasefire between the United States and Iran after weeks of military conflict between the two nations.

stories.title: Norway's Telenor faces lawsuit for giving junta data from its customers in Myanmar
stories.summary: A Swedish non-profit filed a class action lawsuit against Norwegian telecommunications company Telenor, alleging it endangered customers in Myanmar by sharing their data with the military junta. Telenor said it had no real choice in the matter.

stories.title: Hungary robbed $82 million from Ukraine’s state bank, now it has fabricated subtitles on a toilet-office joke video to justify it
stories.summary: Hungary allegedly seized $82 million from Ukraine's state bank and then fabricated subtitles on a private video to justify the action. The altered video falsely included a reference to corruption money that was never spoken.

stories.title: Hegseth: Iran ‘begged’ for ceasefire, claims ‘historic victory’
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth publicly claimed a decisive military victory over Iran following the announcement of a ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Japan is sending engineers to Ukraine’s frontline — and they’re coming back with $2,500 weapon
stories.summary: Japan is sending engineers to frontline areas in Ukraine, where they are working with a Ukrainian drone startup producing weapons at roughly $2,500 each. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are reportedly monitoring the venture closely.

stories.title: Iran Conflict Threatens Armenia-Azerbaijan Progress
stories.summary: Analysts warned that the U.S. military campaign against Iran could undermine diplomatic progress between Armenia and Azerbaijan. The Iran conflict risks destabilizing a region where Trump's administration had previously brokered a peace accord.

stories.title: Israel pounds Lebanon with heaviest air strikes of the war
stories.summary: Israel carried out its heaviest air strikes on Lebanon since the conflict with Hezbollah began, even as the Iran-aligned group paused attacks on northern Israel and Israeli troops in Lebanon. The bombardment came during a two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Heavy rains kill 3, injure 17 across Punjab
stories.summary:
LAHORE: Heavy rains and storms in Punjab over the past 24 hours have left three people dead and 17 others injured, rescue officials said on Wednesday.
In Bhakkar, two separate roof-collapse incidents

stories.title: PSX gains close to 14,000 points amid investor glee over US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange’s (PSX) benchmark index KSE-100 surged by almost 14,000 points during intraday trade on Wednesday as investors reacted to the positive developments of a ceasefire between t

stories.title: Trump says Lebanon not included in US-Iran ceasefire amid Israeli assault
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Lebanon was not included in the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, describing the ongoing Israeli military operations in Lebanon as a "separate skirmish." Israel continued strikes across Lebanon, killing dozens after the regional truce was announced.

stories.title: Europe should learn from Ukrainian troops and fight “smartly”, says Colonel Idzelis
stories.summary: Lithuanian Colonel Idzelis urged European militaries to learn from the Ukrainian army's combat experience, arguing that a high-tech approach focused on minimizing soldier casualties is essential for defending against Russian infantry tactics.

stories.title: Pakistan PM urges restraint amid Israeli ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urged all parties to exercise restraint following Israel's wave of attacks on Lebanon and Iranian threats to respond, calling for the two-week ceasefire to be respected so diplomacy can proceed.

stories.title: Ceasefire changes little for shipping in strait of Hormuz, experts say
stories.summary: Shipping analysts said the U.S.-Iran ceasefire will bring only a limited increase in traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, as vessels still need Iranian permission to transit. Tehran warned that any ship attempting passage without authorization would be "targeted and destroyed."

stories.title: Govt removes acting Ogra chairman amid oil supply challenges, pricing controversies
stories.summary: ISLAMABAD: In the middle of oil supply challenges and pricing controversies, the government on Wednesday removed acting chairman of the Oil & Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) and appointed an offic

stories.title: Israel Katz: Attacks struck 'hundreds' of Hezbollah fighters, threatens leader
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz claimed the latest strikes on Lebanon killed hundreds of Hezbollah fighters, calling it the group's largest blow since the 2024 exploding pager attack. Katz also threatened Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem.

stories.title: Scottish Labour pledges £30m to top up artists’ income to a living wage
stories.summary: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar pledged £30 million to provide artists and musicians in Scotland with a living wage, modeled on a similar basic-income scheme in Ireland. The proposal would be part of a broader overhaul of arts funding ahead of next month's Holyrood election.

stories.title: In phone call with PM Shehbaz, Pezeshkian confirms Iran’s participation in Islamabad talks
stories.summary: Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian has confirmed Tehran’s participation in Pakistan-offered peace talks with the United States in Islamabad to finalise a peaceful settlement to their conflict, the Prime

stories.title: BAE Systems trials low-cost counter drone solution for Eurofighter Typhoon
stories.summary: BAE Systems has conducted an internally funded air-to-surface trial of a low-cost counter-drone solution designed for the Eurofighter Typhoon. The company said the test reflects its commitment to investing in advanced capabilities required by its customers.

stories.title: Discussed ways to build strong future of India-U.S. ties: U.S. envoy Gor on meeting with Trump
stories.summary: ‘We discussed President Donald Trump's unwavering determination to bring global stability’ said the U.S. Ambassador

stories.title: Casualties mount from Israeli attacks on Lebanon, including 10 killed at funeral, and three girls
stories.summary: Israel's latest attacks on Lebanon caused mass casualties, including at least 10 people killed in a strike on a funeral in the eastern town of Shmestar. Beirut hospitals were inundated with wounded, and the American University of Beirut Medical Center appealed for blood donations.

stories.title: France to increase defense spending by $42 billion, mulls new tank effort
stories.summary: France has announced plans to boost defense spending by $42 billion. Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin indicated the country is considering an interim tank solution, likely based on a KNDS Germany or KNDS France platform, as part of a broader effort to strengthen armored capabilities.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran won’t enrich uranium, will give up uranium, while US lifts sanctions
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran agreed not to enrich uranium and would surrender its uranium stockpile, while the US would lift sanctions. However, there was no indication Tehran accepted such terms, and Iran's military continued missile and drone operations.

stories.title: French pair held in Iran says not 'broken' after return to France
stories.summary: French nationals Cécile Kohler, 41, and Jacques Paris, 72, returned to Paris on Wednesday after nearly four years of detention in Iran. President Emmanuel Macron greeted them at the Élysée Palace, and the pair said they would speak about the conditions of their imprisonment.

stories.title: Trump halts Iran attacks after talks with PM Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir; US, Iran reach ceasefire agreement
stories.summary: Pakistan on Wednesday announced that the Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States of America, along with their allies, had agreed to an immediate ceasefire, including in Lebanon, effective immed
