stories.title: Hegseth: US achieved 'decisive victory' in Iran, claims Mojtaba Khamenei disfigured
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared a decisive American victory in Iran and claimed that Mojtaba Khamenei had been disfigured. He expressed hope the ceasefire would hold and thanked Israel for its role.

stories.title: Hegseth hails Iran 'victory' as confusion remains over ceasefire deal
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared a decisive military victory over Iran and claimed Tehran's missile program has been functionally destroyed. However, the two sides presented vastly different interpretations of the two-week ceasefire agreement's terms.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Leopard 2A6 reportedly hit Russian T-72B3 at 5.5 km — this may be longest kill in this war
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Leopard 2A6 tank reportedly struck a Russian T-72B3 at a distance of 5.5 kilometres, potentially making it the longest confirmed tank kill of the Russia-Ukraine war.

stories.title: Hezbollah pauses attacks under US-Iran ceasefire: Sources
stories.summary: Hezbollah paused its attacks under the US-Iran ceasefire, according to sources. However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the truce does not include Lebanon.

stories.title: Germany suspends military approval for long stays abroad for men under 45
stories.summary: Germany suspended the requirement for men under 45 to obtain military approval for extended stays abroad. The regulation had largely gone unnoticed until it was reported by a German newspaper.

stories.title: Hormuz crisis pushes Arab states toward MENA transport corridor
stories.summary: Turkey and Saudi Arabia launched a land-based transport corridor to maintain regional trade during the Strait of Hormuz crisis. Syria and Jordan have also reached separate transit agreements.

stories.title: Israel pounds Beirut as Lebanon left out of ceasefire deal
stories.summary: Lebanon's government reported that Israeli strikes on April 8 killed dozens and wounded hundreds across the country, with Beirut experiencing its most violent bombardment since the start of the war with Hezbollah. The attacks continued despite a two-week ceasefire deal between the U.S. and Hezbollah's backer, Iran.

stories.title: Huge strategic defeat for the US? There is now a two-week ceasefire but hard questions remain
stories.summary: The US-Iran two-week ceasefire raised questions about Washington's strategic position, as Tehran's 10-point peace plan was accepted as the baseline for negotiations. Analysts viewed this as a significant concession by the United States.

stories.title: Report: War veteran set to replace Belgorod Region governor as Putin prepares leadership change
stories.summary: Belgorod-based outlet Pepel reported that Major General Alexander Shuvaev, currently deputy governor of Irkutsk Region, is set to replace Vyacheslav Gladkov as acting governor of Belgorod Region following Gladkov's expected resignation.

stories.title: Iranian official threatens to 'punish' Israel for Lebanon attacks
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official threatened to "punish" Israel for its attacks on Lebanon, calling them a violation of the ceasefire terms. Iran's Fars news agency reported that Tehran is preparing a military response to the Israeli assault.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry to appoint ambassador for prisoners of war
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced it would introduce a new ambassador-at-large position dedicated to prisoners of war on April 9.

stories.title: Israeli attacks hit nine Beirut neighbourhoods: Report
stories.summary: Al Jazeera Arabic reported that Israel's latest wave of air strikes on Beirut hit nine separate neighbourhoods across the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Palestinian children's charity closes in wake of Israeli pressure
stories.summary: Defence for Children International – Palestine announced its closure after more than 30 years of operations, citing continued Israeli restrictions that made its work impossible. The organization had focused on protecting the rights of Palestinian children.

stories.title: How did Pakistan broker a temporary truce between Iran and the US?
stories.summary: Pakistan brokered a temporary truce between the US and Iran, with President Trump acknowledging that Islamabad "knows the country better than most." Negotiations between the two sides are set to begin in Islamabad on Friday.

stories.title: Israel launches 100 air strikes in 10 minutes across Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel carried out approximately 100 air strikes across Lebanon within a 10-minute span, described as an unprecedented wave of coordinated attacks on the country.

stories.title: Film show: Gus Van Sant returns with absurdist thriller
stories.summary: Director Gus Van Sant's new film "Dead Man's Wire" is an absurdist thriller starring Bill Skarsgård and Colman Domingo, inspired by a true 1970s kidnapping. Robert Aramayo received a BAFTA for portraying campaigner John Davidson, who has Tourette's syndrome.

stories.title: Trump says he will work with Iran for 'very productive regime change, there will be no enrichment'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the US would work with Iran on what he described as regime change, asserting there would be no uranium enrichment and that buried nuclear materials would be removed.

stories.title: Vance warns Iran ceasefire hinges on good faith talks
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that the US-Iran ceasefire depends on Iran's willingness to negotiate in good faith, emphasizing that President Trump is seeking a genuine diplomatic deal.

stories.title: France to target Russia's 'shadow fleet' with tougher penalties for ships sailing under false flag
stories.summary: France plans to double jail terms for owners and operators of ships sailing under false flags, targeting Russia's so-called shadow fleet. The measure is part of a draft update to France's military planning law aimed at vessels suspected of transporting Russian oil in violation of Western sanctions.

stories.title: Iran, US both claim victory, but did they actually concede ground?
stories.summary: Both the United States and Iran have claimed victory following their ceasefire agreement, but apparent concessions made by each side could become obstacles during upcoming negotiations scheduled to take place in Islamabad, Pakistan.

stories.title: Lebanese man scours home bombed by Israel for mementos of his slain family
stories.summary: In Tyre, southern Lebanon, Hussein Saleh has been returning daily to the site of his destroyed home to search for belongings of his wife, daughter, and six other relatives killed in an Israeli strike. The visits have continued for about a month.

stories.title: Benin finance minister Wadagni seeks his own mandate in election
stories.summary: Benin Finance Minister Romuald Wadagni is the strong favorite in Sunday's presidential election in Cotonou. The longtime technocrat is seeking his own mandate amid ongoing jihadist attacks in the country's north.

stories.title: Hegseth touts US ‘victory’ over Iran as Tehran hails its own ‘historic’ win
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared a total military victory over Iran, while Tehran simultaneously claimed its own "historic" win, with both sides issuing competing victory narratives amid the ceasefire.

stories.title: Delight and disappointment as Celine Dion fans in battle for tickets
stories.summary: Tickets for Celine Dion's upcoming run of shows in Paris went on sale, with some fans securing spots while many others were left disappointed. A general sale begins Friday, and Dion announced six additional shows.

stories.title: Airlines see no immediate relief despite Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Airlines continue to face months of disruption despite the Iran ceasefire, as jet fuel supplies remain constrained by refinery damage sustained during the conflict.

stories.title: Gaza residents struggle to buy bread amid flour shortage
stories.summary: Residents of Gaza are facing severe flour shortages, with long queues forming outside bakeries and some waiting for hours. A lack of small-denomination currency has compounded the difficulty, and digital payment options remain inaccessible to many in the enclave.

stories.title: Beirut hospitals 'overwhelmed' by victims of latest Israeli attack, doctors plea for help
stories.summary: The Beirut Doctors Syndicate reported that hospitals across the Lebanese capital are overwhelmed with casualties from Israel's latest air strikes. Syndicate head Elias Challala called on all doctors to report to hospitals to help treat the large number of injured.

stories.title: Israel strikes central Beirut without warning
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck central Beirut without prior warning following the US-Iran ceasefire, killing dozens and wounding hundreds, according to Lebanese officials.

stories.title: Timor-Leste is vulnerable to ‘infiltration by foreign organized crime’, president José Ramos-Horta says
stories.summary: Timor-Leste President José Ramos-Horta warned that the nation is vulnerable to infiltration by foreign organized crime. Australian federal police confirmed they are providing support to Timorese law enforcement, including deploying digital forensic and cyber experts in December 2025 to address threats from online scam centers.

stories.title: ‘Non-survivable’: heatwaves are already breaching human limits, with worse to come, study finds
stories.summary: A new study analyzing six extreme heatwaves between 2003 and 2024 found that when temperature, humidity, and the body's cooling ability are considered, all events created potentially deadly conditions for older people. Researchers warn humans are more vulnerable to rising temperatures than previously understood.

stories.title: Cuts to NDIS to be focus of Labor’s quietly launched ‘razor gang’ ahead of May budget
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government established an NDIS Sustainability Taskforce within the health department to identify cost-cutting options for the $52 billion National Disability Insurance Scheme. The taskforce, led by former Treasury official Anthea Long, will advise ahead of the May federal budget.

stories.title: When it comes to Trump, Albanese’s tactic has been don’t buy-in and don’t bite back. Why has that changed?
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese shifted from his usual restrained approach toward U.S. President Donald Trump after Trump threatened mass bombings of bridges and power plants. Albanese reportedly judged that this rhetoric crossed a new threshold requiring a public response.

stories.title: Shell oil trading profits soar amid Iran war but Qatar strikes hit gas output
stories.summary: Shell is expected to report significantly higher oil trading profits in the first quarter of 2025 due to market volatility caused by the Iran crisis. However, strikes in Qatar have reduced the company's gas output. Earnings at Shell's renewable energy division are projected between $200 million and $700 million.

stories.title: Why the US-Iran ceasefire is seen as a failure for Donald Trump
stories.summary: Analysts assessed that the United States emerged as the strategic loser in the five-week conflict with Iran despite military superiority, with gains limited to a fragile two-week ceasefire and conditional passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan mediated the ceasefire agreement reached just before President Trump's deadline.

stories.title: After two years, Israel still withholds Walid Daqqa's body
stories.summary: Israel has withheld the body of deceased Palestinian prisoner Walid Daqqa for two years. His family and supporters continue to demand its return.

stories.title: Gunmen kill 60 in northwest Nigeria, locals and humanitarian groups say
stories.summary: Gunmen killed at least 60 people in attacks across at least 10 villages in northwestern Nigeria's Kebbi and Niger states, according to local clergymen and a humanitarian report.

stories.title: Nigeria begins mass trial of 500 terrorism suspects
stories.summary: Nigeria began a mass trial of approximately 500 terrorism suspects, addressing a longstanding issue in which individuals accused of terror-related offenses were held without prosecution for extended periods.

stories.title: Did America lose yet another war?
stories.summary: An analysis examined the US war on Iran in the context of past American military conflicts, drawing parallels with previous engagements that critics have characterized as failures.

stories.title: Iran's IRGC says it downed Hermes 900 drone over Fars province
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC announced it shot down a Hermes 900 drone over the city of Lar in Fars province. The IRGC warned that any US or Israeli aircraft in Iranian airspace would be considered a ceasefire violation and would receive a decisive response.

stories.title: Survey finds 60 percent of Americans view Israel unfavourably following Iran war
stories.summary: A survey found that 60 percent of Americans now view Israel unfavorably following the Iran war, with support declining across party lines. The poll indicated even young Republicans are increasingly turning against Israel.

stories.title: North Korea fires two rounds of ballistic missiles: Seoul military
stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles in two rounds on Wednesday, South Korea’s military said, after reporting an “unidentified projectile” was launched from the Pyongyang area the

stories.title: CAF’s Motsepe to visit both Senegal and Morocco amid AFCON fallout
stories.summary: Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe plans to visit both Senegal and Morocco amid a dispute over the Africa Cup of Nations title. Senegal is appealing a decision to strip its AFCON title and award it to Morocco.

stories.title: Lebanon displaced share stories at theatre turned refuge
stories.summary: Families displaced by the war in Lebanon have found shelter at a theatre in Beirut. In addition to providing a roof, the venue has given residents the opportunity to take the stage and share their personal stories of displacement.

stories.title: Lebanon's health minister: 'Hundreds' killed and wounded in last wave of Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Minister Rakan Nassereddine reported hundreds killed and wounded in the latest Israeli strikes on Beirut and other areas. Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned the attacks, and Lebanon's Red Cross deployed 100 ambulances in response.

stories.title: Lithuanian colonel outlines scenarios for Russian aggression against Baltic States
stories.summary: Lithuanian Colonel Linas Idzelis outlined four possible scenarios for Russian aggression against the Baltic states, following Russian threats over allegations that Baltic nations provided airspace for Ukrainian strikes on Russian ports.

stories.title: Nigeria: At least 20 killed in attack, residents say
stories.summary: An attack in northern Nigeria killed at least 20 people according to residents and humanitarian workers, though authorities placed the official death toll at three. The incident occurred in an area plagued by kidnapping gangs and Islamist militants.

stories.title: In a war with no winners, Netanyahu looks like the biggest loser
stories.summary: As the U.S. and Iran agreed to a fragile two-week ceasefire, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced criticism from opponents who characterized Israel's conflict with Iran as a strategic failure. Years of Israeli diplomatic pressure for a war against Iran yielded few tangible gains.

stories.title: Iran doubles down on executions amid US-Israeli war
stories.summary: Iran has executed 14 individuals in recent weeks, continuing its use of capital punishment despite the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against the country.

stories.title: How Pakistan emerged as the peacemaker between the US and Iran
stories.summary:
Pakistan has emerged as a key intermediary between Iran and the United States to secure a temporary ceasefire and host negotiations to end the war in the Middle East.
On Wednesday, Prime Minister Sheh

stories.title: France to ramp up drone stocks by 400 percent to face Russia threat
stories.summary: France announced plans to increase its stockpiles of explosive drones by up to 400 percent by 2030 under new defense plans unveiled on Wednesday. The accelerated rearmament is a response to what Paris considers a growing military threat from Russia.

stories.title: As US, Israel, Iran claim victory, Pakistan wins the meme war
stories.summary: Following Pakistan's role in brokering the Iran ceasefire, Pakistanis celebrated widely on social media, sharing memes as the United States, Israel, and Iran each claimed victory.

stories.title: Iran celebrates ceasefire amid critical war losses, says it 'forced America to accept its demands'
stories.summary: Iranian officials celebrated the ceasefire while acknowledging critical losses from the war, claiming that Iran had forced the United States to accept its demands.

stories.title: Israeli attacks across Lebanon kill dozens hours after Iran-US ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel's military carried out what it described as its largest coordinated strike across Lebanon since renewing its war on the country, killing dozens just hours after the US-Iran ceasefire was announced. The Lebanese health ministry confirmed the casualties.

stories.title: Empty ships and shut wells: Why the Iran war oil crisis is not over yet
stories.summary: The US-Iran war removed hundreds of millions of barrels from global oil markets, leaving ships empty and oil wells shut. Analysts warn the oil crisis is far from over despite the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Ethiopia renews tenure of Tigray regional leader
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed extended the mandate of Tigray's interim regional administrator by one year, raising questions about elections that had been scheduled for June in the northern region.

stories.title: Macron welcomes home French pair freed after years in Iran jail
stories.summary: France welcomed home two nationals who had been detained in Iran for three and a half years. President Emmanuel Macron described their release as the end of a prolonged ordeal.

stories.title: IDF launches largest airstrikes yet against Hezbollah, despite truce with Iran
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched its largest air strikes yet against Hezbollah targets in Lebanon despite the US-Iran truce, killing dozens in Beirut. Israel rejected Pakistan's assertion that the Iran ceasefire extended to Lebanon, while the IDF said the operation had been planned weeks earlier.

stories.title: Schools to gradually reopen after ceasefire, with uneven rollout across Israel
stories.summary: Some Israeli cities began resuming school classes following the ceasefire, while others delayed reopening. Home Front Command guidelines remained unchanged, leading to an uneven rollout across the country.

stories.title: Ukraine and Croatia are building underground drone factory to kill Chinese supply chain
stories.summary: Ukraine and Croatia signed a joint production agreement to build drones in an underground factory on Ukrainian soil. The deal between General Cherry and ORQA aims to localise drone component manufacturing and reduce reliance on Chinese supply chains.

stories.title: How have MENA states reacted to Iran-US ceasefire?
stories.summary: Gulf and regional states broadly welcomed the Iran-US ceasefire as a step toward de-escalation. Several governments urged a lasting peace while raising concerns about the situation in Lebanon.

stories.title: As 2-week ceasefire takes hold, Pentagon touts ‘decisive military victory’
stories.summary: A two-week ceasefire has taken effect following U.S. military operations against Iran. Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine stated that the Pentagon destroyed Iran's defense industrial base, claiming it would take years for Iran to reconstitute those capabilities.

stories.title: UK's Starmer heads to the Gulf to discuss Strait of Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer traveled to the Gulf on Wednesday to discuss ensuring the permanent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz with regional leaders. The visit followed the announcement of a US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Oil prices plunge, stocks surge on US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Oil and gas prices dropped sharply while global stock markets surged after the US-Iran ceasefire led to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, easing energy supply fears.

stories.title: Did US really secure 'overwhelming military victory' in Iran?
stories.summary: France 24 examined U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's claim of a decisive military victory over Iran and the functional destruction of Tehran's missile program. Analysts questioned whether the U.S. achieved a strategic victory despite its military campaign, noting uncertainty about the full extent of damage to Iranian capabilities.

stories.title: Hungary and Russia Agreed to Strengthen Economic and Cultural Ties in December Cooperation Plan – Politico
stories.summary: Politico reported that Hungary and Russia agreed in December to strengthen economic and cultural ties through a cooperation plan, as Hungary approaches elections in which Prime Minister Viktor Orbán faces accusations of foreign interference.

stories.title: Iran attacks two cities in Bahrain despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran launched drone attacks on two cities in Bahrain despite a declared ceasefire, with explosions reported near the Bahraini capital on Wednesday morning.

stories.title: Russian court sentences 6 members of opposition movement Vesna to up to 12 years in prison
stories.summary: A St. Petersburg court sentenced six members of the Russian opposition movement Vesna to prison terms of up to 12 years in a general-regime penal colony, as reported by local media outlet Bumaga.

stories.title: Lavan refinery blaze continues hours after US-Iran ceasefire agreement
stories.summary: A fire continued burning at an oil refinery on Iran's Lavan Island hours after the US-Iran ceasefire agreement took effect, with large plumes of black smoke visible from the facility.

stories.title: 'Unlawful' war on Iran: 'Use of force by the United States never justified'
stories.summary: Professor Marc Weller of Chatham House argued that the U.S. use of force against Iran constitutes an unlawful act of aggression. He said threats directed at civilian infrastructure represent clear violations of international humanitarian law and warned of an erosion of the international order.

stories.title: ‘Ketamine Queen’ to be sentenced over Matthew Perry’s death
stories.summary: Jasveen Sangha, dubbed the "Ketamine Queen," faces sentencing for supplying the drugs that led to actor Matthew Perry's death. She could receive more than six decades in prison.

stories.title: JD Vance criticizes Zelenskyy and Ukraine in Hungary on visit campaigning for Viktor Orban
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance criticized EU leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a visit to Hungary, where he campaigned for Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ahead of elections. The Kremlin voiced its approval from Moscow.

stories.title: Polish firm teams with Northrop, ST Engineering to tap Poland’s massive ammo spending
stories.summary: A Polish defense firm has partnered with U.S.-based Northrop Grumman and Singapore's ST Engineering to compete for Poland's large-scale ammunition contracts. Global defense companies are seeking to capture multibillion-dollar opportunities in eastern and central Europe for equipping ground forces.

stories.title: Anger and surprise in Israel after US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli politicians, commentators, and analysts expressed anger and surprise at the US-Iran ceasefire agreement. Many in Israel criticized the deal as a "complete failure" of stated war objectives.

stories.title: New Zealand defense minister to help shepherd military-integration push with Australia
stories.summary: New Zealand Defense Minister Chris Penk is leading efforts to deepen military integration with Australia. Penk is the first New Zealand defense minister to have previously served in both the New Zealand and Australian armed forces.

stories.title: AFCENT awards Kraus Hamdani $270M for solar-powered, long-endurance drones
stories.summary: U.S. Air Forces Central Command has awarded Kraus Hamdani Aerospace a $270 million contract for solar-powered, long-endurance drones. The company's K1000ULE platform set endurance records with a three-day flight and has been demonstrated in multiple military exercises across several areas of responsibility.

stories.title: Ukrainian intelligence  called it “the last Russian railway ferry in the Kerch Strait still afloat” — now it’s out of action too
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence said it destroyed the Slavyanin, described as the last operational Russian railway ferry in the Kerch Strait, using a drone strike on the night of April 5-6. The vessel had been transporting fuel, weapons, and ammunition to occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Israeli closure of Al-Aqsa ‘selective’, ‘discriminatory’
stories.summary: Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem has been closed to Muslim worshippers for over a month, with critics describing Israel's closure policy as selective and discriminatory.

stories.title: US and Israel set out ambitious, vital war goals; as of the ceasefire, none have been achieved
stories.summary: An analysis concluded that neither the United States nor Israel achieved their stated war goals by the time the ceasefire took effect. President Trump hailed only a tactical victory while facing the challenge of negotiating final terms with an emboldened Iranian regime within two weeks.

stories.title: France: French former prisoners in Iran describe detention conditions
stories.summary: Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris, two French nationals released from Iran after nearly four years in detention, described the "daily horror" of their imprisonment upon returning to France on Wednesday. They expressed hope despite their ordeal.

stories.title: Israel pounds Lebanon with 100 strikes in 10 minutes
stories.summary: Israel carried out approximately 100 airstrikes across Lebanon within a span of ten minutes on Wednesday, including targets in Beirut. Hundreds of casualties were reported.

stories.title: REPLAY: Hegseth claims Iran suffered 'devastating military defeat'
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth held a press conference declaring a decisive military victory over Iran and claiming Tehran's missile program has been functionally destroyed. The briefing followed the announcement of a two-week ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: From Evin Prison to a dash through wartime Iran: How French couple’s four-year ordeal ended
stories.summary: French nationals Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris returned to France on Wednesday after more than three and a half years in Tehran's Evin Prison, enduring a perilous journey through wartime Iran. Iran characterized their release as a prisoner swap, while France has distanced itself from U.S.-Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: South Africa to lay legendary Albert Mazibuko to rest
stories.summary: South Africa is preparing to lay to rest Albert Mazibuko, a founding member of the Grammy Award-winning group Ladysmith Black Mambazo, who died at age 77 after a short illness.

stories.title: Diplomacy pays off: A timeline of events leading up to the ceasefire between US and Iran
stories.summary: Backchannel diplomatic efforts by Pakistan appear to have finally paid off, as the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire after weeks of escalating hostilities triggered by US-Israeli s

stories.title: ‘Stone Age’ to ‘Golden Age’: How the final hours before the truce unfolded
stories.summary: Intense last-minute diplomacy preceded the announcement of a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran. The final hours featured escalatory threats alongside frantic negotiations to secure the truce.

stories.title: Indian embassy in Iran asks citizens to ‘expeditiously exit’, hours after ceasefire announcement
stories.summary: The Indian embassy also said that citizens’ exit must be in coordination with the embassy, and shared emergency numbers

stories.title: Scenes of chaos, destruction as Israel bombards Lebanon
stories.summary: Video footage captured widespread chaos and destruction in Beirut as the Israeli military carried out extensive bombing attacks across the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to reciprocate with ceasefire: Zelensky addresses Russia following truce between U.S. and Iran
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine is prepared to reciprocate with a ceasefire if Russia halts its attacks. He also praised the U.S.-Iran ceasefire in the Middle East as the right decision.

stories.title: Defeat from the jaws of victory: Israel reacts to Trump’s Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli analysts and officials reacted with frustration to the US-Iran ceasefire brokered by President Trump, with some assessing that Iran emerged from the confrontation both intact and strategically stronger than before.

stories.title: No truce in Lebanon as Israel bombs Beirut, south
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck several dense commercial and residential areas in central Beirut without warning on Wednesday afternoon, hours after a ceasefire had been announced in the broader U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran. No truce was observed in Lebanon.

stories.title: In Gaza, the daily search for bread is becoming more desperate
stories.summary: Millions of people in Gaza are struggling to secure bread and other basic food supplies amid Israel's ongoing military operations and blockade of the territory.

stories.title: Xi Jinping backs services sector to power China’s next growth phase
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping signaled a renewed focus on China's services sector, calling for a demand-driven and technology-led strategy to reshape growth and create jobs. The remarks were delivered at a two-day conference on the sector that concluded Wednesday.

stories.title: Ex-NATO general: 'I was worried my former colleagues would become war criminals overnight.'
stories.summary: Former NATO General Michel Yakovleff told France 24 he feared former colleagues could become war criminals if ordered to carry out what he described as unlawful destruction of infrastructure, as U.S. President Trump had threatened before the ceasefire. Yakovleff called the Middle East war pointless and doubted Trump would resume hostilities.

stories.title: One in eight Britons left UAE amid Iran war: report
stories.summary: A report found that one in eight British residents in the UAE departed during Iranian strikes. Some may return now that a ceasefire is in effect.

stories.title: Kyiv calls for Ukraine ceasefire after Iran truce
stories.summary: Ukraine called on the United States to pressure Russia into a ceasefire, citing the Iran truce as evidence of Washington's ability to broker peace agreements.

stories.title: Will the Iran war permanently fragment Trump's MAGA base?
stories.summary: Analysts are examining whether the US-Israeli war on Iran could permanently fracture Donald Trump's MAGA coalition, as the issue exposes deep divisions within his political base.

stories.title: Who is Asim Munir and why are Trump and Iran praising him?
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir emerged as a significant diplomatic figure after both US President Donald Trump and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi praised his role in brokering the two-week ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Tai Po blaze: no fire safety system checks before firm sent 85 shutdown notices
stories.summary: A Hong Kong inquiry heard that a fire services company acted as a rubber stamp, submitting 85 shutdown notices for a housing estate's hose reel system without conducting on-site inspections. The Tai Po estate, Wang Fuk Court, was struck by one of Hong Kong's deadliest blazes in decades.

stories.title: DIU disables Russians’ last railway ferry in Kerch Strait
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Intelligence special forces disabled Russia's last operational railway ferry in the Kerch Strait, further disrupting Russian logistics to occupied Crimea.

stories.title: The Kremlin’s crackdown on VPNs is escalating. Here’s what Meduza readers in Russia have to say about it.
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry, reportedly acting on FSB or Kremlin instructions, is preparing new restrictions on VPN services, including measures to limit app purchases, raise fees on international traffic, and potentially penalize VPN use. Meduza surveyed readers in Russia about the impact.

stories.title: Nigeria faces deadly heatwave as fuel costs skyrocket
stories.summary: Nigeria is experiencing a severe heatwave in Lagos, compounded by skyrocketing fuel costs and widespread reliance on generators, leaving millions struggling with health risks and power challenges.

stories.title: Cameroon 'military contractors' killed in Russia-Ukraine war - BBC confirms leaked message
stories.summary: The BBC confirmed leaked messages indicating that Cameroonian nationals working as military contractors were killed in the Russia-Ukraine war. Cameroon's government has generally avoided commenting on its citizens' involvement in the conflict.

stories.title: US war on Iran: Lucas makes case for 'discussions & dialogue over renewing violence & confrontation'
stories.summary: Professor Scott Lucas of University College Dublin described the U.S.-Iran ceasefire as a recalibration rather than a resolution. He argued the ceasefire emerged from the limits of military escalation, with Iran leveraging resilience and regional positioning to strengthen its diplomatic hand.

stories.title: While West watches Middle East, Russia quietly secured foothold in world’s second-largest graphite producer
stories.summary: Russia has quietly secured a foothold in the world's second-largest graphite-producing country, gaining access to cobalt, rare earths, and a key Indian Ocean shipping route while global attention focused on the Middle East.

stories.title: Why won't FIFA ban Israel: Palestine's football fight
stories.summary: Palestine has intensified its campaign to ban Israel from FIFA after a report found anti-discrimination policy breaches by the Israeli football association.

stories.title: Chile’s far-right government rips up plan for memorial at Pinochet torture site
stories.summary: Chile's far-right government reversed plans to establish a memorial at the former Colonia Dignidad compound, a site linked to torture under the Pinochet dictatorship. The settlement was founded by ex-Nazi Paul Schäfer, who held as many as 300 people in an isolated enclave. The reversal of the expropriation has left victims without resolution.

stories.title: China’s Zhipu AI open-sources flagship model, raises prices to narrow gap with US rivals
stories.summary: Chinese AI company Zhipu AI open-sourced its flagship model GLM-5.1 and raised API prices by 10 percent. This marked Zhipu's second price increase in 2025 as the company shifts toward monetizing advanced AI capabilities amid intensifying competition with US rivals.

stories.title: Ray Dalio says US-China ties are critical as world enters dangerous new era
stories.summary: Billionaire investor Ray Dalio called the US-China relationship the most critical factor for global well-being, speaking at an event in Shanghai. He warned that poor relations could cause catastrophic damage as the war on Iran shakes the world order and the two countries' leaders prepare to meet.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Doubling down on C-UAS; Hypersonic flight; Could AI help the Navy build hulls faster?
stories.summary: Recent defense industry developments include increased investment in counter-drone systems, advances in hypersonic flight technology, and exploration of AI applications to accelerate U.S. Navy hull construction.

stories.title: Kremlin Welcomes Iran Ceasefire Deal
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov welcomed the Iran ceasefire deal, stating that the warring parties should pursue their interests through diplomatic negotiations rather than military action.

stories.title: Russians transfer military equipment through Mariupol toward Huliaipole, says Andriushchenko
stories.summary: According to Mariupol mayoral adviser Petro Andriushchenko, Russian forces have been observed moving military equipment and personnel through occupied Mariupol toward the town of Huliaipole in the Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Leaked documents show Hungary agreed to Russian teachers, energy deals, and circus cooperation with Moscow. Magyar calls it outright betrayal
stories.summary: Leaked documents revealed that Hungary and Russia signed a 12-point cooperation plan covering education, energy, and cultural exchanges, including provisions for Russian teachers. Opposition leader Péter Magyar called it a betrayal.

stories.title: World Athletics postpones Doha Diamond League amid US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: World Athletics postponed the Doha Diamond League event originally scheduled for May 8 to June 19, citing the ongoing US-Israeli military conflict with Iran. Organizers said the rescheduled date is contingent on improved conditions.

stories.title: Ukraine hit Crimea’s key fuel hub and struck deep into Luhansk Oblast — while clearing more air defenses across the occupied south
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Feodosiia Marine Oil Terminal in Crimea, causing a fire visible over 20 kilometres away and confirmed by NASA satellite data. Separate strikes in Luhansk Oblast destroyed Russian Buk-M3, Tor-M2, and Zoopark-1M air defense systems.

stories.title: Breaking Defense expands editorial staff, with Ben Watson joining as production editor
stories.summary: Breaking Defense has expanded its editorial team by hiring Ben Watson as production editor. Watson will oversee newsletters, social media, and special editorial projects for the defense-focused news outlet.

stories.title: Report: Armed men in masks break up self-organization festival in Russia
stories.summary: Armed men in masks raided and shut down a self-organization festival on its opening day in the Siberian city of Tyumen, Russia, according to the independent Russian outlet 7×7.

stories.title: Madagascar declares state of emergency over energy situation due to Iran war
stories.summary: Madagascar declared a state of emergency over its energy situation as supply disruptions caused by the war involving Iran began affecting daily life and the functioning of public services across the island nation.

stories.title: Can Philippines become critical minerals powerhouse with help from US, Japan?
stories.summary: The United States and Japan aim to transform the Philippines into a critical minerals powerhouse to reduce reliance on China. However, analysts from the Centre for a New American Security warned that Manila's lack of comprehensive reforms and persistent corruption could undermine the effort.

stories.title: Both sides claim victory after US, Iran agree to 11th-hour truce
stories.summary: Both the United States and Iran claimed victory following an eleventh-hour truce agreement. Iran characterized the deal as a "crushing defeat" for the U.S., while President Trump declared it a "total victory" for the American side.

stories.title: Gulf States welcome ceasefire deal between US, Israel, and Iran, demand end to all attacks
stories.summary: Gulf states welcomed the ceasefire agreement between the United States, Israel, and Iran, calling for an end to all hostilities even as Iranian missile and rocket attacks on Gulf facilities continued.

stories.title: Daily Quiz | On the Rwandan genocide
stories.summary: A daily quiz commemorates the 1994 Rwandan genocide, marked on April 7, during which close to a million people were killed over approximately 100 days. The quiz covers events leading to the genocide.

stories.title: Ethiopia: PM Abiy Extends Tenure of Tigray Region Interim Chief Administrator By One Year
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed extended the appointment of Lieutenant General Tadesse Worede as Chief Administrator of the Tigray Interim Administration for one additional year, effective April 9, 2026.

stories.title: How Pakistan brokered a US-Iran ceasefire, and what's next
stories.summary: Pakistan brokered a two-week ceasefire between the United States, Israel, and Iran, marking a significant diplomatic achievement for Islamabad. The temporary truce halts hostilities but faces uncertain prospects for a lasting resolution.

stories.title: German, Japanese, and Swiss machines are inside Russia’s missile factories. None are sanctioned
stories.summary: An investigation found that German, Japanese, and Swiss precision machines are being used inside Russian missile factories, including in Iskander missile production. None of the machine manufacturers are currently sanctioned.

stories.title: As war premiums hit groceries, China deals give Africa room to breathe
stories.summary: The partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran disrupted global oil supplies, pushing Brent crude above $100 per barrel and driving up grocery prices worldwide. China's trade deals with African nations provided some economic relief to the continent amid rising war-related premiums.

stories.title: Verkhovna Rada calls on partners to strengthen nuclear safety and increase pressure on Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada adopted an appeal to foreign parliaments, governments, the UN, and the IAEA on the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster, calling on the international community to strengthen nuclear safety measures and increase pressure on Russia.

stories.title: Mumbai’s historic dock quietens as fuel crisis chokes fishing trade
stories.summary: Fishing boats at Mumbai's historic Sassoon Dock have been idled as surging diesel costs linked to the broader fuel crisis cripple the city's fishing trade and threaten the livelihoods of its maritime workers.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. will help with 'traffic buildup' in Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had said hours earlier that safe passage through the Strait will be possible “via coordination with Iran’s Armed Forces and with due consideration of technical

stories.title: Russia’s Supreme Court chief says Russian courts are the best place to seek justice
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court chief Igor Krasnov argued in a published article that foreign judicial systems cannot guarantee impartiality, asserting that Russian courts are the most reliable venue for seeking justice.

stories.title: Oil dives below $100, stocks jump after two-week ceasefire agreed
stories.summary: Oil prices slid, stocks and bonds surged, while the safe-haven dollar was knocked back on Wednesday, as ​a two-week Middle East ceasefire brought some relief to markets on hopes for a resumption of oi

stories.title: World leaders hail Iran truce as stocks rally, oil prices tumble
stories.summary: World leaders welcomed the two-week US-Iran truce and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, prompting a stock market rally and falling oil prices. France and Spain called for the ceasefire to be extended to cover Israel's conflict with Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Reaffirms Neutrality in Middle East Conflict After Iran Criticism
stories.summary: Kenya reaffirmed its neutral stance on the escalating Middle East conflict after facing criticism from the Iranian government.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Easter Road Crashes Fall but Death Toll Rise - Police
stories.summary: Zimbabwe police reported that road traffic accidents during the 2026 Easter holiday declined compared to last year, but the death toll increased.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Protests UN Report On Haiti Mission, Says No Rape Complaints Were Filed
stories.summary: Kenya's Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi formally protested a UN report on the Haiti mission, writing to Secretary-General António Guterres that the report failed to reflect findings clearing Kenyan personnel of rape allegations during their deployment.

stories.title: Namibia: Namibia Urged to Strengthen Child Health As Preventable Deaths Continue, Says Unicef
stories.summary: UNICEF country representative Samuel Ocran urged Namibia to strengthen child health services, warning that thousands of newborns continue to die in their first days of life from preventable causes.

stories.title: South Africa: Schreiber Welcomes Approval of Revised White Paper On Citizenship
stories.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber welcomed Cabinet's approval of the Revised White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection.

stories.title: Lesotho: Passport Crisis in Lesotho
stories.summary: Lesotho's government suspended passport services, but desperate citizens continue to queue at offices in Maseru amid a growing passport crisis.

stories.title: Floods kill dozens as heavy rains hit Angola
stories.summary: Torrential rains in Angola have killed approximately 40 people, with several others still reported missing according to authorities.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian DJs Association Bans Members From Playing Burna Boy's Songs Over Altercation With DJ Tunez
stories.summary: Nigeria's DJs Association banned its members from playing songs by artist Burna Boy following a reported physical altercation between the musician and DJ Tunez.

stories.title: 49% of Russians still read Telegram channels despite blocking, Levada poll finds
stories.summary: A Levada Center poll found that 49% of Russians continued reading Telegram channels despite the platform being effectively blocked in the country, with 20% accessing the channels daily or multiple times per day.

stories.title: Trump says US won 'total and complete victory' after ceasefire deal with Iran, AFP reports
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told AFP on Tuesday that the United States had achieved a "total and complete victory" after agreeing to a two-week ceasefire deal with Iran.

stories.title: Does the Iran ceasefire include Lebanon? Here's what we know
stories.summary: Uncertainty persists over whether Lebanon is included in the US-Iran ceasefire. Israel continues strikes on Lebanese territory, and conflicting positions from involved parties have left the question unresolved.

stories.title: Republic of Altai Introduces Fines for Refusing to Hire War Veterans
stories.summary: The Republic of Altai in Russia introduced fines for companies with more than 100 employees that refuse to hire veterans of the conflict in Ukraine, under a law requiring at least 1.2% of their workforce to be comprised of such veterans.

stories.title: Despite ceasefire, Iran claims refinery hit, launches wave of attacks against UAE, Kuwait
stories.summary: Despite the ceasefire, Iran reported a refinery was struck and launched retaliatory attacks against the UAE and Kuwait. The first two ships traversed the Strait of Hormuz after its reopening, while Vice President Vance warned the truce remains fragile.

stories.title: Kenya: Stateless At Home - Kenyan Somalis Struggle to Reclaim Citizenship From Refugee Records
stories.summary: Kenyan Somalis in the Garissa area are struggling to reclaim their citizenship after being registered as refugees, with some individuals like Amina Saida having been brought to the Dadaab refugee camp near the Somali border as young children.

stories.title: Fragile ceasefire lifts markets as Trump threatens 50% tariffs on Iran arms suppliers
stories.summary: Global markets rallied following the US-Iran ceasefire announcement, but US President Trump simultaneously threatened 50 percent tariffs on countries supplying weapons to Iran. Tehran warned it might withdraw from the agreement if Israeli attacks on Lebanon continued, and passage through the Strait of Hormuz remained restricted.

stories.title: North Africa: Over 180 Feared Dead in Crossings From Africa as Mediterranean Death Toll Nears 1,000 in 2026
stories.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that over 180 people are feared dead or missing in recent Mediterranean shipwrecks involving crossings from North Africa, bringing the total death toll in 2026 close to 1,000.

stories.title: Hezbollah urges displaced not to return ahead of Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Hezbollah urged displaced Lebanese residents not to return to their homes in southern Lebanon, the Bekaa Valley, or Beirut's southern suburbs until a formal ceasefire in Lebanon is officially declared, as fighting with Israel continues.

stories.title: Russian drone strike damages port infrastructure in Izmail
stories.summary: Port infrastructure in the Ukrainian city of Izmail, located on the Danube River, was damaged during a Russian drone attack carried out overnight on April 8.

stories.title: Israel weighs expanding Ben-Gurion flights after Iran ceasefire announcement
stories.summary: Israeli carrier Arkia Airlines announced plans to resume its full flight schedule from Ben-Gurion Airport by May 3 following the Iran ceasefire, though it cautioned that operations remain dependent on the evolving security situation.

stories.title: Washington pushes allies to match tougher China chip curbs under new bill
stories.summary: A new US bill, the Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls in Hardware (Match) Act, introduced by Representative Michael Baumgartner, seeks to tighten restrictions on China's access to advanced chipmaking equipment. Washington aims to bring allies including the Netherlands and Japan into closer alignment on export controls.

stories.title: As France pulls gold from the US, how can China develop into the next global gold hub?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest China should seize a strategic window to develop into a global gold hub as France repatriates gold reserves from the United States. Beijing could leverage policy stability and Hong Kong's fintech strengths amid growing de-dollarisation concerns under President Trump's administration.

stories.title: Starmer hopes to establish key diplomatic role for Britain as he heads to the Gulf
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer embarked on a three-day trip to the Gulf region to discuss diplomatic efforts supporting the US-Iran ceasefire and address the impact of the conflict on the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Residents report explosions in three Russian regions, ammunition arsenal targeted – media
stories.summary: Residents of Russia's Moscow, Vladimir, and Yaroslavl regions reported at least three simultaneous explosions on April 7. Reports suggest an engineering munitions arsenal may have been among the targets struck.

stories.title: Turkish intelligence aided ceasefire efforts between US and Iran, officials say
stories.summary: Turkey's intelligence agency MIT helped facilitate the US-Iran ceasefire by maintaining communication channels with Washington, Tehran, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps, working to prevent miscalculations between the parties.

stories.title: In Germany, a woman bites a railway worker to get through closing doors
stories.summary: A 36-year-old woman in Munich, Germany, bit a 29-year-old railway station worker on the arm while trying to board a train through closing doors at Pasing station. The worker sustained a visible wound but was not seriously injured and continued working.

stories.title: Attack in Bahrain injures two despite US, Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Two people were injured and homes damaged in Bahrain's Sitra district after shrapnel fell from an intercepted Iranian drone, despite the announced US-Iran ceasefire. Bahrain's Interior Ministry confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Will the ‘No Kings’ protest be a defining moment in Trump’s second term? | In Focus Podcast
stories.summary: Journalist Anisha Dutta says the anti-war sentiment across America was a key factor that led to protesters turning out in the millions

stories.title: What is Iran’s 10-point conditions for ceasefire and negotiations
stories.summary: Iran said that the plan called for continued Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz, acceptance of enrichment, lifting of all primary and secondary sanctions against the Islamic Republic

stories.title: What we know about the Iran ceasefire - and what we don't
stories.summary: President Trump accepted an Iranian ceasefire proposal as a basis for peace talks, potentially indicating significant US concessions. Key details of the agreement and its implementation remain unclear.

stories.title: Three Thai crew killed in Hormuz attack as ships remain stranded
stories.summary: Three crew members aboard a Thai-flagged vessel attacked in the Strait of Hormuz last month have died, Thailand's foreign minister confirmed. Twenty other crew were rescued by Oman's navy, while nine Thai vessels remain stranded in the waterway.

stories.title: Thailand confirms deaths of 3 cargo ship crew in Gulf attack
stories.summary: Thailand's foreign minister confirmed three Thai crew members died when the Thai-flagged cargo ship Mayuree Naree was struck by Iran on March 11 while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The attack occurred after Iran effectively closed the strait in response to US-Israeli strikes on Iranian targets.

stories.title: Don't be fooled: This war is not US versus Iran, it's Israel against America
stories.summary: Protests against the US-Iran war took place near the Iranian embassy in Baghdad, with demonstrators denouncing both President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. The article argues the conflict is primarily driven by Israeli interests.

stories.title: Rwanda fights farmland loss with satellites
stories.summary: Rwanda is deploying satellite technology to monitor and protect agricultural land in its capital from urban development encroachment, as the country grapples with being Africa's most densely populated nation.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran threats look like self-incrimination for potential war crimes
stories.summary: Legal analysts have raised concerns that President Trump's threats against Iran, including targeting civilian infrastructure, could constitute self-incrimination for potential war crimes. The laws of war prohibit the destruction of civilian infrastructure as a means of coercing a government.

stories.title: Russians attack 19 settlements in Chernihiv region over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled 19 settlements in Ukraine's Chernihiv region over the past day, with authorities recording 30 separate attacks and 57 explosions.

stories.title: Israel backs Trump’s two-week pause on Iran strikes, says Lebanon excluded
stories.summary: Israel expressed support for President Trump's two-week pause on strikes against Iran while excluding Lebanon from the arrangement. Iran announced that negotiations for a permanent peace deal would begin on April 10 in Islamabad, Pakistan.

stories.title: In pictures: Iranians celebrate as ceasefire with US eases tensions
stories.summary:
The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, with both sides claiming victory.
