stories.title: Watch: When will fuel prices go down?
stories.summary: The BBC's Nick Marsh examined whether fuel prices will decline following the announcement of a ceasefire between the United States and Iran, exploring the potential impact on global fuel costs.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE updates: U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement 'big day for world peace', says Trump
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a ceasefire that includes Iran guaranteeing safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz for two weeks if attacks are halted. President Trump called it a 'big day for world peace.' Israel stated the ceasefire does not include Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran thanks Pakistan for its efforts in reaching talks with U.S.
stories.summary: Iran expressed gratitude to Pakistan for its diplomatic efforts in facilitating talks with the United States. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif invited both Iranian and American delegations to Islamabad for further negotiations.

stories.title: Iranian hackers' targeting of US critical infrastructure has escalated since start of war, U.S. says
stories.summary: US officials reported that Iranian hackers have escalated cyberattacks targeting American critical infrastructure since the start of the war. In some cases, hackers altered display data and extracted device project data from compromised systems.

stories.title: Macron greets French detainees back in Paris after ‘terrible ordeal’ in Iran
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed Cecile Kohler and Jacques Paris back to Paris after nearly four years of detention in Iran on espionage charges. The two French nationals arrived at Charles de Gaulle Airport and were greeted by Macron at the Elysee Palace.

stories.title: Russia plans to create buffer zone in Vinnytsia region — Palisa
stories.summary: Oleh Palisa, deputy chief of Zelenskyy's office, said Russia is considering establishing a buffer zone in Ukraine's Vinnytsia region from the direction of Moldova's unrecognized Transnistria territory but currently lacks sufficient forces to implement the plan.

stories.title: Russia supplies Iran with cyber support, spy imagery to hone attacks, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence assessed that Russia has been providing Iran with cyber support and satellite spy imagery to improve its military targeting capabilities. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed a specific incident detailed in the assessment.

stories.title: Tanzania: Public Warned Over Unsafe Meat Practices
stories.summary: Health authorities in Zanzibar, Tanzania, urged the public to follow proper animal slaughter procedures to prevent diseases that could pose serious risks to human health.

stories.title: Israel says battle in Lebanon continues despite Iran war truce
stories.summary: Israel renewed its strikes in southern Lebanon and urged residents in parts of Beirut to evacuate on Wednesday, after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu insisted the US-Iran truce does not exte

stories.title: Iran deal ‘total and complete victory’ for US, Trump tells news agency
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump described the ceasefire deal with Iran as a "total and complete victory" for the United States. The statement followed the agreement on a two-week ceasefire between the two nations.

stories.title: On India’s updated climate pledges
stories.summary: India announced revised Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement, prompting analysis of its existing climate mitigation efforts and the challenge of balancing developmental costs with climate commitments.

stories.title: Sweden tries five minors over Iranian dissident murder plot
stories.summary: Sweden is prosecuting five minors over a plot to murder Iranian dissident Arvin Khoshnood. Khoshnood stated he believes the attack was ordered at the behest of Iranian authorities.

stories.title: Madagascar declares state of emergency over severe fuel shortages linked to Iran war
stories.summary: Madagascar declared a state of emergency due to severe fuel shortages linked to the Iran conflict, with the presidency citing concerns that the shortages could trigger public disorder.

stories.title: U.S., Iran agree to two-week ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan mediated a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, with all parties and their allies agreeing to an immediate halt to hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon. Islamabad announced it will host direct talks between the two sides on April 10.

stories.title: Co-founder of Jalisco New Generation drug cartel pleads guilty
stories.summary: Érick Valencia Salazar, a co-founder of Mexico's Jalisco New Generation drug cartel, pleaded guilty in the United States. He was among 29 alleged drug lords extradited from Mexico to face U.S. charges.

stories.title: Trump finds his off-ramp with Iran, but the causes of war remain unresolved
stories.summary: The two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran provided President Trump a diplomatic off-ramp, but analysts note that the fundamental divides between Washington and Tehran remain as sharp as they were in February when hostilities began.

stories.title: The body continues: In war, dance becomes a way to survive
stories.summary: Choreographers Bosmat Nossan and Roni Chadash created new works for the Batsheva Ensemble exploring dance as a means of survival and resilience during wartime in Israel.

stories.title: Israel backs Trump's two-week pause on Iran strikes, says Lebanon excluded
stories.summary: Israel expressed support for U.S. President Donald Trump's two-week pause on strikes against Iran, while stating that Lebanon would be excluded from the arrangement. Israel also backed U.S. efforts to neutralize Iran's nuclear, missile, and alleged terrorism threats to the U.S., Israel, and neighboring Arab states.

stories.title: What we know about the two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week provisional ceasefire, coming more than a month after coordinated US-Israeli military operations against Iran. The truce is conditional, with further negotiations expected.

stories.title: US lawmakers divided over Trump’s Iran ceasefire, reflecting foreign policy unease
stories.summary: US lawmakers reacted along partisan lines to President Trump's announcement of a temporary ceasefire with Iran. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Trump was 'desperately searching for any sort of exit ramp,' while others offered varying assessments of the move.

stories.title: PLA troops facing Taiwan Strait and Japan simulate response to nuclear attack
stories.summary: The People’s Liberation Army division responsible for the East China Sea and the Taiwan Strait carried out a decontamination exercise amid targeting of Iranian nuclear facilities by the United States

stories.title: Cameroon Says 16 of Its Citizens Were Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine
stories.summary: Cameroon's government announced that 16 Cameroonian nationals were killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine, based on a list provided by the Russian Embassy in Yaoundé.

stories.title: Israel army ‘regrets’ damage to Tehran synagogue, says targeted senior commander
stories.summary: The Israeli military expressed regret over damage to a synagogue in Tehran, stating it had been targeting a senior military commander in the area. Iran maintains a small Jewish community, though many members left the country following the 1979 Islamic revolution.

stories.title: US support group for interfaith Jewish families guts staff amid funding crisis
stories.summary: The U.S. nonprofit 18Doors, which supports interfaith Jewish families, reduced its staff from 15 to four employees amid a funding crisis linked to shifting charitable giving patterns since October 7 toward Israel and antisemitism causes.

stories.title: Iran war shows Trump not ‘reliable ally’ for UK, says Ed Davey – UK politics live
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey argued that the Iran conflict demonstrates the UK cannot rely on Donald Trump as a dependable ally, describing the situation as a 'classic Donald Trump cycle of destruction.'

stories.title: ‘Tireless and courageous diplomacy’: World reacts to Islamabad-brokered US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: World leaders reacted to the US-Iran ceasefire brokered by Pakistan, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif inviting delegations from both countries to Islamabad on April 10 for further negotiations. Pakistan had been conducting behind-the-scenes diplomacy with key regional players.

stories.title: Turkey detains 10 suspects over Istanbul gun attack outside Israeli consulate
stories.summary: Turkish authorities detained 10 suspects in connection with a gun attack outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, including two wounded attackers who are being questioned in hospital.

stories.title: Sybiha welcomes ceasefire in Middle East: 'Time to show determination to compel Moscow'
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha welcomed the U.S.-Iran ceasefire and called on the international community to demonstrate similar determination in compelling Moscow to end hostilities in Ukraine.

stories.title: Russia’s Central Election Commission says candidates can campaign on Telegram
stories.summary: Russia's Central Election Commission told the newspaper Vedomosti that political candidates are legally permitted to campaign on Telegram, affirming their right to choose their own methods of outreach.

stories.title: Israel says Iran ceasefire does not include Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military announced it would continue operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, stating that the ceasefire agreement reached between Iran, the US, and Israel does not extend to the conflict in Lebanon.

stories.title: US ‘third-country’ deportees deal sparks backlash in DRC
stories.summary: A U.S. agreement to deport individuals to the Democratic Republic of the Congo as a third country has provoked backlash within the DRC.

stories.title: Liberal judge Chris Taylor wins election to Wisconsin supreme court – US politics live
stories.summary: Liberal judge Chris Taylor won the Wisconsin Supreme Court election, giving Democratic-backed justices a 5-2 majority on the court. Separately, in a special House election in northwest Georgia's conservative-leaning district formerly held by Marjorie Taylor Greene, the Republican candidate prevailed.

stories.title: Israel strikes southern Lebanon after US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck the Tyre and Nabatieh areas in southern Lebanon just hours after the announcement of a US-Iran ceasefire, signaling that Israel does not consider Lebanon covered by the truce.

stories.title: Pro-regime Iranians celebrate ceasefire
stories.summary: Supporters of Iran's Supreme Leader celebrated in the streets of Tehran following the announcement of a two-week ceasefire with the US and Israel. US President Donald Trump claimed 'regime change' had already occurred in Iran, though hardliners remain in power and anti-regime voices continue to face suppression.

stories.title: Italy rules out Hormuz naval deployment without UN mandate
stories.summary: Italy ruled out deploying naval vessels to the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Iran ceasefire unless a United Nations-led mission is established. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini confirmed the deployment is not under consideration.

stories.title: Iran ceasefire: What happens next?
stories.summary: The United States and Iran reached a two-week ceasefire deal less than two hours before President Trump's deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Negotiations toward a more permanent peace agreement are now set to take place during the ceasefire period.

stories.title: Africa: Gender Quotas Cannot Stand Alone - Political Parties Must Lead
stories.summary: [Liberian Observer] Across Africa, the surge of women excelling in politics and public leadership has been largely propelled by gender quotas, primarily enacted through legislation. Countries like Sie

stories.title: UK house prices fall in March amid uncertain impact of Middle East conflict
stories.summary: UK house prices fell 0.5% in March according to Halifax data, pushing the average home price back below £300,000 to £299,677. The decline was attributed to uncertainty surrounding the Middle East conflict, rising energy costs, and their knock-on effects on mortgage rates and the broader economy.

stories.title: Is Lebanon part of the Iran war ceasefire?
stories.summary: Iran and Pakistan assert that Lebanon is included in the US-Iran ceasefire, while Israel denies this and continues military strikes on Lebanese territory, creating confusion over the truce's scope.

stories.title: UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain report attacks despite Iran-US ceasefire
stories.summary: The UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain reported military strikes across the Gulf region just hours after the US and Iran announced a two-week ceasefire, raising questions about the truce's enforcement.

stories.title: Israel’s war on Lebanon: What exactly is the ‘Dahieh Doctrine’?
stories.summary: The "Dahieh Doctrine" is an Israeli military strategy named after Beirut's southern suburb of Dahieh, involving disproportionate force against civilian areas and infrastructure. It has been condemned for its application in Gaza and Lebanon.

stories.title: Oil posts biggest crash since 1991—but the Gulf ceasefire has two versions
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices dropped 15% in the largest crash since 1991 following the Gulf ceasefire announcement, though conflicting versions of the agreement emerged and reports indicated missiles continued to fly, with Iran reportedly imposing fees on Strait of Hormuz passage.

stories.title: NATO chief Mark Rutte set for Trump talks as US-Iran truce begins
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte was set to meet with President Trump as the U.S.-Iran truce took effect. Rutte, described as a "Trump whisperer," has played a central role in allied efforts to manage relations with the U.S. president.

stories.title: Both sides claim victory after US, Iran agree to a two-week ceasefire
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire barely an hour before President Trump's deadline to attack the country, prompting global relief. Both Tehran and Washington claimed victory following the announcement ending the more than month-long conflict.

stories.title: US and Iran agree to provisional ceasefire as Tehran says it will reopen strait of Hormuz | First Thing
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week conditional ceasefire that includes a temporary reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu endorsed the US-Iran deal but stated it does not cover Israeli military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, where Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,500 people.

stories.title: Global markets rally, oil drops below $100 after US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Global financial markets rallied and oil prices fell approximately 15% below $100 per barrel after the announcement of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, with Asian markets showing particularly strong gains in early trading.

stories.title: Fuel depot on fire after shelling in Feodosia – social media
stories.summary: A fuel depot in Feodosia, in Russian-occupied Crimea, caught fire following shelling during the night of April 8, according to social media reports.

stories.title: Kimberly-Clark toilet paper warehouse in California destroyed by fire; employee arrested
stories.summary: A Kimberly-Clark toilet paper warehouse in California was destroyed by fire, and an employee was arrested in connection with the incident. Analysts warned that the destruction could lead to toilet paper supply problems in the region.

stories.title: Oil prices fall after ceasefire deal as questions over Hormuz Strait linger
stories.summary: Oil prices dropped sharply and Asian and European equity markets rebounded following the US-Iran two-week ceasefire agreement. Questions remain about the long-term future of the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil and natural gas transits. Pakistan's adoption of solar power has partially shielded it from the war's energy shock.

stories.title: PSX gains over 12,000 points amid investor glee over US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index surged over 12,000 points—an 8.15 percent gain and the largest single-day rally in absolute terms in PSX history—following the announcement of a US-Iran ceasefire. Trading was temporarily suspended per exchange regulations.

stories.title: Ukraine importing necessary volumes of fuel – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Ukraine is importing necessary fuel volumes, with supply operations continuing through cooperation with European partners and Middle Eastern countries.

stories.title: US and Iran reach ceasefire deal with both sides claiming victory
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire on Tuesday, just 90 minutes before a deadline President Trump had set for strikes on Iranian civilian infrastructure. The deal, brokered by Pakistan, pauses a six-week conflict that killed thousands and triggered a global energy crisis.

stories.title: ISW: Russians “weaponizing civilian harm as an intentional tool of war” by pervasively employing human safari tactics
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russian forces are systematically targeting civilians, citing two FPV drone strikes on civilian buses in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on April 7 as part of a documented pattern the UN has classified as crimes against humanity.

stories.title: Network Rail worker wins race harassment case after EDL leaflet left in locker
stories.summary: Network Rail worker Parmjit Bassi won a race harassment case after colleagues placed an anti-Islam English Defence League leaflet in his locker. Bassi, who is not Muslim, was also falsely accused of a knife attack by co-workers. An employment tribunal found the incident constituted racial harassment.

stories.title: 'Political disaster': Israeli leaders lash out over ceasefire, split on who’s to blame
stories.summary: Israeli political leaders clashed over the ceasefire with Iran, with opposition figure Yair Lapid blaming Prime Minister Netanyahu for strategic damage and Otzma Yehudit MK Zvika Fogel criticizing President Trump for backing down.

stories.title: India's digital census prompts fear of hidden agendas
stories.summary: India has launched a fully digital census using millions of enumerators and allowing self-reported data. Critics fear the process could be exploited for political manipulation in the world's most populous country.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire: 'Still unclear what is to be negotiated'
stories.summary: President Trump added confusion to the ceasefire terms by telling AFP the US had a 15-point proposal for upcoming negotiations, contradicting his earlier reference to Iran's 10-point plan. Talks between the two sides are set to take place within the two-week ceasefire window.

stories.title: Shipping remains halted in Hormuz despite Iran-US ceasefire
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted despite the US-Iran ceasefire, as companies and the Norwegian Shipowners' Association cite ongoing security concerns and uncertain conditions preventing vessels from resuming transit.

stories.title: Vance praises Orbán on Ukraine during his ‘unprecedented’ Hungary visit – Europe live
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance visited Budapest and praised Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's role in peace efforts during what was described as an unprecedented visit. Vance also criticized EU and UK energy policies in a speech at a private school in the Hungarian capital.

stories.title: Declarations of victory in Iran after ceasefire agreed with US
stories.summary: Iranian state media hailed the two-week ceasefire agreement with the US and Israel as a victory, calling it 'yet another retreat' by President Trump. Declarations of triumph were widespread across Iranian media following the deal's announcement.

stories.title: Gulf countries report attacks despite Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Several Gulf states reported being targeted by Iranian strikes despite the ceasefire between Iran, the US, and Israel. Qatar and the UAE said missiles were intercepted, sirens sounded in Saudi Arabia, and two people were injured in Bahrain by falling debris.

stories.title: 'Clearly insane', 'not well', 'stunning': Papers discuss Trump's rhetoric
stories.summary: International newspapers scrutinized President Trump's mental health following his threat to wipe out Iranian civilization, with headlines describing his rhetoric as 'clearly insane' and 'stunning.' Coverage also touched on developments in the Epstein investigation.

stories.title: Russians attack 17 settlements in Kharkiv region, leaving two civilians injured over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces struck 17 settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region on April 7, injuring two civilians.

stories.title: Colombia's Petro calls for economic emergency, fresh financing law
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro announced plans to submit an economic emergency decree and a new tax reform bill to Congress to balance the country's 2026 budget. The announcement was made on Tuesday evening in Bogotá.

stories.title: Hungary's Orban plays on energy price fears in re-election bid
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has centered his re-election campaign on energy policy, promising to maintain energy subsidies and keep prices low amid a global energy crisis. He has continued purchasing Russian gas, making Hungary one of only two EU nations exempt from the bloc's policy to reduce dependence on Russian imports.

stories.title: China probes ‘malicious’ cyberbullying of teen diving champion Quan
stories.summary: Chinese authorities launched an investigation into online cyberbullying targeting Quan Hongchan, a three-time Olympic gold medalist in diving, after the teenager faced toxic abuse about her appearance and reportedly considered quitting the sport.

stories.title: Trump stops bombing Iran after conversations with PM Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir; Iran, US agree to two-week ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan announced that the United States and Iran, along with their allies, agreed to an immediate ceasefire including in Lebanon. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif credited conversations with both sides and invited delegations to Islamabad on April 10 for further peace talks.

stories.title: ‘Biggest diplomatic win in years’: Pakistan’s quiet role in US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Diplomatic observers told Dawn that more than two weeks of largely unseen Pakistani mediation preceded the US-Iran two-week ceasefire agreement. Islamabad activated diplomatic channels across multiple capitals shortly after the conflict erupted on February 28.

stories.title: Mozambique: They Were Not Asked. Now They Are Asking Parliament To Stop
stories.summary: [Redactor] Mozambique's Tobacco Control Bill is poised for a plenary vote with no impact study, half a day of public consultation, and the voices of nearly one million people completely absent from th

stories.title: Nigeria: World Bank to Nigeria - Save Oil Windfall for Rainy Day, Rebuild Fiscal Buffers
stories.summary: [This Day] Abuja -- The World Bank has prescribed some policy responses for Nigeria in the wake of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, including fiscal discipline, rebuilding fiscal buffers, and

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader Cheng Li-wun makes rare China visit
stories.summary: Kuomintang leader Cheng Li-wun made a rare visit to mainland China, calling for reconciliation and unity with Beijing at a memorial for Taiwan's founding father in Nanjing. Taiwan's ruling Democratic Progressive Party criticized the visit and urged China to cease its aggression.

stories.title: Online fuel subsidy portal shuts down due to ‘hacking attempts’ in Karachi
stories.summary: In Karachi, Sindh's online fuel subsidy portal for motorcyclists was temporarily shut down due to repeated hacking attempts. Excise Minister Mukesh Kumar Chawla said the system was restored after being secured. Approximately 3,000 bikers had applied for the Rs 2,000 subsidy.

stories.title: Voices of America
stories.summary: An opinion piece critiques former US President Trump's rhetoric on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, referencing Senator Bernie Sanders' characterization of Trump's statements as those of 'a dangerous and mentally unbalanced individual' and his call for Congress to end the war.

stories.title: Airlines warn jet fuel shortages may persist for months
stories.summary: The International Air Transport Association warned that global jet fuel shortages could persist for months even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens, due to continued disruptions to Middle East refining capacity affecting airline operating costs.

stories.title: India’s space ambition set to soar after Artemis II moon mission’s success
stories.summary: As Nasa’s Artemis II crew loops around the moon, the mission involving four astronauts from the US and Canada is set to reignite India’s ambition to grow its space sector and launch future lunar missi

stories.title: China ZXMOTO founder revokes ‘not getting a cent’ from government remark after controversy
stories.summary:
The founder of the Chinese motorcycle brand ZXMOTO, Zhang Xue, has stoked controversy after saying his company did not take “a single cent” from the government.
His comments sparked accusations that C

stories.title: China’s DeepSeek adds expert chatbot mode ahead of much-awaited V4 release
stories.summary:
DeepSeek has introduced new “instant” and “expert” modes to its chatbot, the most significant update to its user interface since the Hangzhou-based start-up gained global recognition.
The changes come

stories.title: As more nations seek counterspace chops, GPS jamming also rises: Report
stories.summary: The Secure World Foundation's annual report found that more nations are pursuing counterspace capabilities, while GPS jamming incidents are increasing globally. The report also identified a growing trend toward deploying 'bodyguard' satellites designed to shadow and defend high-value military and intelligence satellites from adversary attacks.

stories.title: Celebrations across the Middle East after Iran-US two-week truce
stories.summary: Celebrations erupted across multiple Middle Eastern countries following the announcement of a two-week US-Iran truce. The coming negotiations will determine whether the temporary ceasefire can lead to a lasting peace agreement.

stories.title: EU mass deportation plan likened to ICE-style enforcement
stories.summary: Critics warn that a proposed EU mass deportation plan could mirror US Immigration and Customs Enforcement tactics, including expanded detention, family separation, and offshore processing hubs, raising significant human rights concerns.

stories.title: Hegseth declares ‘decisive military victory’ in Iran, says U.S. is ‘hanging around’ to enforce ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared a "decisive military victory" over Iran and said American forces would remain in the region to enforce the ceasefire. The chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff reported more than 13,000 strikes on Iran since the war began.

stories.title: US, Iran ceasefire will bring 'relief' but unclear 'what the future holds'
stories.summary: Middle East specialist Myriam Benraad of the University of Exeter said the US-Iran two-week ceasefire will bring relief to the international community and the Iranian population. However, she noted that contradictory messages from the White House create uncertainty about what longer-term peace negotiations will yield.

stories.title: Russian strikes leave 4,500 consumers without electricity in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Russian strikes on two settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region cut electricity to approximately 4,500 consumers on the evening of April 7.

stories.title: ‘A step back from the brink’: European leaders welcome US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: European leaders welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire deal, calling it "a step back from the brink," and urged the permanent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The two-week conditional ceasefire, brokered by Pakistan, was agreed Tuesday, but Israel said it would continue operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: With threat to wipe out Iran’s civilisation, Trump’s rhetoric goes beyond bluster
stories.summary: President Trump's threat to wipe out Iran's civilization represented an escalation in rhetoric that went beyond previous statements. His advisers characterized the increasingly extreme language as a negotiating tactic aimed at pressuring Tehran into a deal.

stories.title: Doctors’ strike timed to cause havoc over Easter break, says NHS England chief
stories.summary: NHS England chief executive Sir Jim Mackey accused resident doctors of deliberately timing their six-day strike to coincide with the Easter holiday period to maximize disruption. Mackey said hospitals struggled to fill rotas because many replacement staff were already on leave during the holiday break.

stories.title: Shift to electric
stories.summary: An editorial argues that the Israel-Iran conflict's disruption of LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, including Qatar's force majeure declaration on gas plants, exposes Pakistan's vulnerability to geopolitical shocks due to its dependence on imported cooking fuels.

stories.title: DR Congo: Uncertainty over the release of FARDC soldiers by M23
stories.summary: In March, AFC/M23 announced the liberation of 5,000 soldiers from the armed forces of the DRC but their transfer to Kinshasa has yet to happen.

stories.title: US, Israel and Iran agree to 2-week ceasefire as Trump pulls back on threats
stories.summary: Iran, the United States, and Israel reached a two-week ceasefire on Wednesday as President Trump withdrew his threats to destroy Iranian civilization. The agreement came just hours before Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face attacks on its infrastructure.

stories.title: Israel says war on Lebanon continues despite Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military declared it will continue operations in Lebanon despite the Iran ceasefire, with spokesperson Colonel Avichay Adraee stating the truce does not cover the Lebanese front and warning residents to evacuate areas south of the Zahrani River.

stories.title: Netanyahu backs Iran truce; opposition blames him for ‘diplomatic disaster’
stories.summary: Prime Minister Netanyahu endorsed the two-week US-Iran ceasefire tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Opposition leader Yair Lapid accused him of a diplomatic disaster, saying Israel failed to secure vital demands and faces lasting strategic damage.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 146 out of 176 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defence Forces intercepted 146 of 176 unmanned aerial vehicles launched by Russia against Ukraine beginning on the evening of April 7.

stories.title: Ceasefire wins Trump instant gratification but Iran can enter talks with stronger hand
stories.summary: The US-Iran two-week ceasefire allowed President Trump to claim victory with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, but analysts note Iran enters peace talks in a stronger position. Tehran retains its enriched uranium stockpile and has demonstrated its capacity to inflict economic pain on the US.

stories.title: Ukraine’s greatest philosopher visited this estate. Russia burned it down 242 years later
stories.summary: The Donets-Zakharzhevskyi estate in Velykyi Burluk, Kharkiv region — a protected architectural monument once visited by Ukrainian philosopher Hryhorii Skovoroda — was destroyed by fire on April 7 after two Russian drone strikes. No casualties were reported.

stories.title: Sealed Gul Plaza fire probe report handed over to Sindh govt
stories.summary: Justice Agha Faisal of the Sindh High Court handed over the sealed Gul Plaza Judicial Commission report to the Sindh government regarding the January 17 fire in Karachi that killed more than 70 people.

stories.title: Reform UK to block visas for Ghana, Nigeria, Jamaica over slavery reparations
stories.summary: A row has erupted after Nigel Farage’s party, Reform UK, unveiled plans to refuse visas to nationals from countries pursuing compensation for the transatlantic slave trade, drawing sharp criticism fro

stories.title: Oil drops below $100 following ceasefire announcement
stories.summary: Brent crude fell 13.8% to $94.25 per barrel and US WTI dropped 15.4% to $95.52 after President Trump announced a two-week ceasefire with Iran linked to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. European diesel prices also declined sharply.

stories.title: HSBC’s HK$5 billion headquarters opens in Hong Kong in 1986 – SCMP archive
stories.summary:
This article was first published on April 8, 1986.
Billion dollar brilliance
by Staff Reporters
The new $5.2 billion headquarters of the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corpn was formally opened last ni

stories.title: Don't drink the Sparta Kool-Aid. Israel is hurting from Iran war
stories.summary: Israel is experiencing growing economic pressure as a result of its involvement in the war with Iran, yet Israeli public opinion, media outlets, and political leaders continue to support further military escalation, according to commentary by Abed Abou Shhadeh.

stories.title: China enforces new security rules to defend supply chains from global threats
stories.summary: China enacted an 18-point regulation on March 31 elevating supply-chain security to a national-security matter. The rule empowers officials to punish entities deemed to threaten China's access to vital resources or the free flow of goods. The full text was published in mid-April as Beijing faces a volatile global trade environment.

stories.title: Lebanon excluded from ceasefire as Israeli strikes continue
stories.summary: Lebanon has been excluded from the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, with Israel explicitly stating the truce does not extend to its military operations there. Israeli strikes on Lebanese territory continued after the ceasefire announcement.

stories.title: Adopting e-mobility
stories.summary: An editorial supports Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's framing of electric mobility as a strategic necessity amid rising energy prices and regional instability, arguing that transport electrification is essential for climate-vulnerable Pakistan beyond the current crisis.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire deal: What are the terms, and what’s next?
stories.summary: President Trump cited Iran's 10-point plan as a basis for further peace negotiations under the ceasefire deal, potentially signaling progress toward a longer-term resolution of the conflict.

stories.title: Google adds Gemini crisis features amid lawsuit over user's death
stories.summary: Google announced new crisis-response features for its Gemini AI chatbot, including a redesigned "Help is available" prompt that activates when conversations indicate potential mental health distress. The update comes as the company faces a lawsuit related to a user's death.

stories.title: Russian army strikes 30 settlements in Sumy region over past day, leaving one killed and three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked 30 settlements in Ukraine's Sumy region over the past day, killing one person and wounding three others.

stories.title: Japan’s ‘imperialist forces’ divided Taiwan from mainland, KMT’s Cheng Li-wun says
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun visited Sun Yat-sen's mausoleum in Nanjing on Wednesday and blamed Japanese "imperialist forces" for separating Taiwan from mainland China. She cited Taiwan's colonization by Japan after China's defeat in the 1895 Sino-Japanese War as the origin of the division.

stories.title: Spain welcomes Iran-US ceasefire, criticises US role
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire but criticized Washington for triggering the conflict, stating Spain would not applaud those who "set the world on fire just because they turn up with a bucket."

stories.title: Myanmar’s food security in crisis as fuel, fertiliser shortages threaten fragile economy
stories.summary: Myanmar faces a deepening food-security crisis as fuel shortages prevent farmers from operating tractors at the start of planting season. Disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have also caused fertiliser shortages. A quarter of Myanmar's population already lacks sufficient food amid civil war and runaway inflation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Groups Warn Nigeria 'On Brink of Collapse' Over Insecurity, Economic Strain
stories.summary: [Premium Times] The groups said the country is "on the brink of collapse" amid rising insecurity, widening inequality and declining public confidence in public institutions.

stories.title: War update: 170 clashes on frontline over past day, Russian forces intensifying assaults in three sectors
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces recorded 170 combat engagements with Russian troops along the frontline on April 7, with Russian forces intensifying assaults in three sectors.

stories.title: Trump acknowledges China help in Iran ceasefire deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump acknowledged China's role in facilitating a two-week ceasefire with Iran that includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Negotiations between the US and Iran are set to begin in Islamabad, Pakistan, on Friday. Iran has separately called for China to serve as a guarantor of regional peace.

stories.title: Iraq's oil exports hindered by large tanker shortages
stories.summary: Iraq is struggling to resume full oil export capacity due to a shortage of large tankers, even as Iran has provided assurances that shipments through the Strait of Hormuz will not be disrupted.

stories.title: Police arrest man on suspicion of stealing personal data of 56,000 patients
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested a man working for a Hospital Authority contractor on suspicion of stealing personal data from more than 50,000 patients. The arrest followed an investigation by the privacy watchdog and police into a large-scale data leak involving over 56,000 patients.

stories.title: Israel attacks kill 254 in Lebanon despite US-Iran truce
stories.summary: Israel carried out its heaviest bombardment of Lebanon since the start of the war between Hezbollah and Israel, killing 254 people and injuring 1,165 despite the US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Israel launches major attack on Lebanon, despite US-Iran truce
stories.summary: Israel launched its heaviest bombardment of Lebanon since hostilities with Hezbollah began, striking targets across the country despite the recently announced US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict paused: two-week truce secures Hormuz route
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire shortly before a deadline set by President Trump for military strikes, easing global tensions and reopening the Strait of Hormuz to maritime traffic.

stories.title: India to receive first Iranian oil shipment in seven years
stories.summary: India is set to receive its first Iranian crude oil shipment in seven years after the US temporarily eased sanctions to address supply shortages. Indian Oil Corporation purchased the cargo, which is en route aboard the tanker Jaya.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Kherson region leave four civilians killed, 21 injured over past day
stories.summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region on April 7 killed four civilians and injured 21 others, including one child.

stories.title: James Swan steps in as new MONUSCO chief in DR Congo
stories.summary: James Swan has officially taken office as the new head of the UN mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo, MONUSCO.

stories.title: Intelligence report warned of Iran’s ‘persistent threat’ to US as White House downplayed the risk

stories.summary: Crude oil prices fell by as much as 15% following the announcement of the US-Iran ceasefire plan, while global stock markets rallied. However, prices remain significantly higher than pre-war levels.
