stories.title: US and Canadian astronauts capture global attention with Artemis II moon flight
stories.summary: HOUSTON, April 7 - The voyage of four astronauts to the far side of the moon has given the world a glimpse of America at its best, offering a respite from global despair and displeasure over U.S-led c

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith to remain in jail after bail hearing over war crimes charges
stories.summary: Former Australian SAS soldier and Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith will remain in jail for at least a week after his legal team declined to apply for bail following his arrest on five war crimes murder charges. A bail review hearing is scheduled for April 17 at Downing Centre local court in Sydney.

stories.title: Araghchi says Iran will halt fire if attacks stop, thanks Pakistan
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would halt military operations if attacks on Iran cease. He thanked Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and military chief Asim Munir for their mediation efforts.

stories.title: Protesters break into Kuwaiti consulate in Iraq’s Basra after rocket attack kills three
stories.summary: BASRA, Iraq, April 7 - Protesters stormed the Kuwaiti consulate in the Iraqi city of Basra, police sources said on Tuesday, after a rocket attack fired from the direction of Kuwait killed three people

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Warns Against Genocide Denial, Historical Distortion
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame warned against genocide denial and historical distortion, emphasizing that the facts of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi are well-documented and cannot be erased.

stories.title: Matt Canavan’s ‘economic revolution’ is little more than a populist mirage – and Australians would pay the price | Patrick Commins
stories.summary: Australian Nationals leader Matt Canavan proposed an "economic revolution" focused on locally manufactured goods to address the high cost of living. Critics argue the plan is a populist approach that would raise consumer prices by forcing Australians to purchase more expensive domestically produced products.

stories.title: French arms exports to Israel ‘a continuous pipeline of military hardware’
stories.summary: A new report by two pro-Palestinian organizations alleges that French arms exports to Israel constitute a "continuous pipeline of military hardware" throughout the war in Gaza. France has maintained that its military equipment exports to Israel were solely for defensive purposes or intended for re-export. The report claims French firms and transport hubs bypassed public scrutiny.

stories.title: Trump says Iran uranium will be ‘taken care of'
stories.summary: President Trump told AFP that Iran's enriched uranium would be "perfectly taken care of" under the ceasefire deal, describing the outcome as a "total and complete victory" and saying he would not have agreed otherwise.

stories.title: Billionaire Gina Rinehart says ‘I don’t understand’ arrest of Ben Roberts-Smith over alleged war crimes
stories.summary: Australian billionaire Gina Rinehart publicly questioned the justification for prosecuting former SAS soldier Ben Roberts-Smith over alleged war crimes, saying she did not understand the cost and time spent investigating former soldiers. Roberts-Smith, a Victoria Cross recipient, was charged with five counts of war crime murder.

stories.title: Intelligence report warned of Iran's 'persistent threat' to US as White House downplayed the risk
stories.summary: Multiple U.S. intelligence agencies warned that Iran poses a "persistent threat" to U.S. military personnel, government officials, Jewish and Israeli institutions, and Iranian dissidents, even as the White House downplayed the risk.

stories.title: Iran portraying ceasefire as 'victory against the United States and Israel'
stories.summary: FRANCE 24 reported from Tehran that Iranian state media is framing the ceasefire agreement with the United States as a victory against both the U.S. and Israel. Despite heavy losses including strikes on infrastructure, assassinations of senior leaders, and civilian casualties, Iran's messaging emphasizes that the Islamic Republic's survival constitutes success.

stories.title: Fars details Iran’s 10-point plan for US talks
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported details of Tehran's 10-point plan for talks in Islamabad, including a commitment not to pursue nuclear weapons, an end to attacks on Iran and allied groups, possible U.S. troop withdrawal, and restricted Strait of Hormuz passage under Iranian rules.

stories.title: US ceasefire allows negotiations on Iran’s ‘workable’ 10-point plan
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a two-week ceasefire with Iran, creating space for negotiations based on Tehran's 10-point proposal, which Iran has described as a workable framework for ending hostilities.

stories.title: How Pakistan helped secure a fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan played a key diplomatic role in brokering the fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran, leveraging its historic ties with Tehran. Despite these connections, reaching an agreement was not guaranteed.

stories.title: Oil prices plunge and stocks jump after Trump announces conditional ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude oil fell roughly 15% to around $93 a barrel following the announcement of a conditional U.S.-Iran ceasefire and Iran's pledge to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under its military's management. Stock markets rallied as the deal was reached just over an hour before Trump's deadline to escalate military action against Iran.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Rights Group Warns of Intimidation At Constitution Hearings Despite High Turnout
stories.summary: The Zimbabwe Human Rights Commission raised concerns about intimidation and restricted participation during public hearings on proposed constitutional amendments, despite reporting strong public turnout across the country.

stories.title: Kenyan private sector slips back into contraction amid Middle East fallout
stories.summary: Kenya's private sector contracted in March for the first time since August 2025, with companies reporting lower output and fewer new orders. The downturn is attributed to weaker purchasing power and disruptions linked to the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Palestinian girl who lost arm in Israeli missile attack on Gaza arrives in UK
stories.summary: Ten-year-old Mariam Sabbah, a Palestinian girl who lost her arm during an Israeli missile strike on Gaza, arrived at London's Heathrow airport for specialist medical treatment. She was accompanied by her mother, Fatma Salman, and two brothers. The UK became the destination after President Trump halted visitor visas for Palestinians.

stories.title: Treat jailed drug dealers like radical extremists, says prisons watchdog
stories.summary: Charlie Taylor, HM Chief Inspector of Prisons for England and Wales, called for jailed drug dealers to be isolated from the general prison population, similar to how radical extremists are managed. Taylor said major dealers currently live "consequence-free" in prisons and should face regular searches and stricter behavioral monitoring.

stories.title: UK opening new oil and gas fields would imperil global climate goals, experts say
stories.summary: Senior climate experts warned that opening new oil and gas fields in the UK's North Sea would undermine international climate targets and encourage developing nations to expand their own fossil fuel extraction. The UK government faces pressure from the oil industry, the Conservative Party, Reform UK, and some trade unions to approve new drilling.

stories.title: Iran says it is ready for anything after Trump warns ‘whole civilisation will die’
stories.summary: “No threat is beyond our preparedness and intelligence,” says Iranian first vice-president.

stories.title: Following Pakistan’s request, Trump agrees to suspend attacks if Iran opens Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Following a request by Pakistan, US President Donald Trump said early on Wednesday he had agreed to suspend the bombing of Iran for two weeks if Tehran completely reopened the vital Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: ‘Cautious optimism’ in Asia after US, Iran agree to ceasefire, reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: Asian markets responded positively to President Trump's announcement of a two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, which included Tehran's agreement to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump described a 10-point proposal from Iran as "workable," providing relief as a deadline for military action had been approaching.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits ambulance in south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike targeted an ambulance in the town of Qlaileh near Tyre in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanese media reports. Lebanese health officials said Israeli forces have repeatedly struck medics and rescue crews during the conflict.

stories.title: ICE says it shot man who tried to ram officers with car
stories.summary: April 7 - ICE officers shot and wounded a man in California on Tuesday after the suspect tried to ram one of them with his vehicle, the acting director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said

stories.title: Associated Press reports discrepancy in Iranian ceasefire texts on enrichment
stories.summary: The Associated Press reported a discrepancy between Persian and English versions of Iran's ceasefire proposal, noting the Persian text includes "acceptance of enrichment" while the English version omits it. The reason for the difference was not immediately clear.

stories.title: UN chief welcomes ceasefire, urges path to lasting peace
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres welcomed the two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire and called on all parties to comply with international law. His personal envoy, Jean Arnault, is in the region to support diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Rwanda: 'Speaking Helps Us Heal' Says Rwandan Survivor On Genocide Anniversary
stories.summary: Rwanda began its annual commemoration of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. Survivor Godelieve Mukasarasi, who has spent over three decades helping women raped during the genocide and children born of sexual violence, emphasized that speaking about the past aids healing.

stories.title: Kenya: Seizure of 2,000 Ants At Nairobi Airport Highlights the Hidden Scale of Insect Trafficking
stories.summary: Kenyan authorities seized over 2,000 garden ants at Nairobi's main international airport in 2026, highlighting a growing insect trafficking problem driven by demand for exotic pets in Europe and Asia. In 2025, four men were sentenced for attempting to smuggle more than 5,000 ants out of the country.

stories.title: Iran reports strikes on bridges, key highway and railways
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it struck bridge segments that were utilised by the Iranian armed forces transporting weapons.

stories.title: AP: Iran, Oman to charge fees for Hormuz passage under ceasefire
stories.summary: Under the Pakistan-mediated ceasefire deal, Iran and Oman will be permitted to charge fees on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the Associated Press reported. Iran reportedly plans to use the revenue for reconstruction.

stories.title: US politicians react to Trump’s Iran ceasefire with caution, relief
stories.summary: Republican hawks in the U.S. Congress expressed scepticism about entering talks with Tehran, while Democratic lawmakers welcomed the truce and called for accountability regarding the conflict's conduct.

stories.title: Israeli shelling reported in south Lebanon after ceasefire remarks
stories.summary: Israeli forces shelled the town of Baraachit in southern Lebanon, Al Jadeed TV reported, following statements from Netanyahu's office that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire excludes the Lebanon front. Pakistan's prime minister disputed this, saying the deal covers Lebanon.

stories.title: SSU detains engineer at defense plant in Dnipropetrovsk region for spying for Russians
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service counterintelligence directorate detained an engineer at a strategic defense plant in the Dnipropetrovsk region for spying on behalf of Russia's FSB and military intelligence (GRU).

stories.title: Iranians commemorate victims of Minab school strike
stories.summary: Iranians held commemorations for the 168 victims of a U.S. strike on a girls' school in Minab, Iran, mourning the casualties of the attack.

stories.title: Trump branded ‘crazy’ over apocalyptic Iran threats
stories.summary: President Trump's apocalyptic threats toward Iran drew widespread criticism, with some former allies publicly questioning his judgment. His extreme language prompted a range of critics to raise concerns about his rhetoric.

stories.title: Iran violates ceasefire agreement hours after Trump announces truce
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council accepted the two-week ceasefire but stressed the broader war had not ended, in what was characterised as a violation of the agreement's terms hours after Trump announced the truce.

stories.title: Tropical Cyclone Vaianu may bring life-threatening winds to New Zealand, forecasters warn
stories.summary: Tropical Cyclone Vaianu, a Category 3 storm with winds exceeding 150 km/h, is moving south of Fiji toward New Zealand. MetService issued strong wind watches for the entire North Island, warning of potentially life-threatening winds and heavy rain later in the week.

stories.title: Petrol prices rise again as Albanese government warns Iran war ceasefire won’t make fuel cheaper
stories.summary: Australian petrol prices rose again as wholesale diesel prices hit new record highs amid the Iran conflict. Energy Minister Chris Bowen cautioned Australians against expecting the U.S.-Iran ceasefire to lower fuel costs, as fuel tankers continued to increase their charges.

stories.title: World welcomes US-Iran ceasefire, urges lasting peace in the Middle East
stories.summary: Multiple countries welcomed the two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire and praised Pakistan for its role in facilitating the truce, while urging both sides to commit fully to the agreement.

stories.title: Malaysian corruption watchdog secures arrest warrant for tycoon Daim’s sons
stories.summary: Malaysia's anti-corruption agency secured arrest warrants for two sons of former finance minister Daim Zainuddin after they repeatedly failed to appear for questioning about their family's wealth. The Daim family has been the subject of a years-long investigation into alleged abuse of power and corruption linked to former Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.

stories.title: Israel says Iran ceasefire agreement doesn’t include war in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu said his government supports the U.S. ceasefire with Iran but maintains it does not apply to the ongoing conflict with Hezbollah in Lebanon. Israel said the truce is contingent on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Banga defends World Bank’s role on Trump’s Board of Peace
stories.summary: World Bank chief says it is seeking to play a constructive role in aiding Gaza’s recovery from war.

stories.title: Full text of Iran's National Security Council statement on ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council released a statement claiming victory and outlining its 10-point plan, confirming that negotiations with the United States would take place in Islamabad, Pakistan.

stories.title: Asia shows interest in Ukraine's maritime defence expertise, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: KYIV, April 7 - The Ukrainian military is participating in consultations on the Strait of Hormuz, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday, adding that Ukraine's maritime defence expertise is als

stories.title: Turkey to race ahead of EU on battery storage amid fossil fuel crisis
stories.summary: Turkey has approved more than 33 gigawatts of battery storage capacity since 2022, surpassing any EU member state, according to climate think tank Ember. By comparison, European leaders Germany and Italy each have only 12–13 GW of planned and operational capacity, highlighting a shift in the clean energy transition.

stories.title: How China’s tax crackdown on undeclared overseas income is targeting retail investors
stories.summary: Chinese tax authorities have begun contacting individuals to verify accuracy of declared income, including overseas earnings. The crackdown is targeting retail investors with undeclared foreign income, prompting some to settle outstanding taxes on overseas trading activities.

stories.title: National support group for interfaith Jewish families guts staff amid funding crisis
stories.summary: 18Doors, a U.S. nonprofit supporting interfaith Jewish families, cut its staff from 15 to 4 amid a funding crisis. A board member said the budget shortfall stemmed from philanthropic funding shifting its focus toward Israel.

stories.title: Explainer: What is in Iran’s 10-point ceasefire plan and will the US agree to it?
stories.summary: The United States and Iran reached a two-week ceasefire agreement barely an hour before President Trump's deadline to escalate strikes on Iran. Tehran agreed to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The deal followed diplomatic efforts involving Pakistan's leadership, with China also believed to have exerted influence over Tehran.

stories.title: Madagascar declares state of emergency over energy situation due to Iran war
stories.summary: Local ⁠media in Madagascar reported widespread fuel ‌shortages

stories.title: Economic Security Bureau of Ukraine foils procurement abuses at defense enterprise
stories.summary: Ukraine's Economic Security Bureau filed an indictment against a former official of a state-owned defense-industrial enterprise, accusing him of abuse of office related to procurement irregularities.

stories.title: White House says ceasefire creates opening for long-term peace
stories.summary: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt credited President Trump and the U.S. military for creating conditions for the ceasefire, saying core objectives had been exceeded within 38 days and that the Strait of Hormuz had been reopened.

stories.title: Mussolini’s summer villa on Italian coast to be a cultural space
stories.summary: The former summer residence of Italian fascist dictator Benito Mussolini in the Adriatic coastal town of Riccione will be converted into a cultural community space. The local council spent approximately US$1.3 million to acquire Villa Mussolini, which the Mussolini family purchased in 1934. Exhibitions on history promoting democratic values are planned.

stories.title: Iran claims ‘historic victory,’ says US accepted terms ahead of talks
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council declared a "historic victory," claiming the U.S. accepted the framework of its 10-point proposal that includes non-aggression guarantees, Strait of Hormuz control, sanctions relief, U.S. troop withdrawal, and reparations.

stories.title: Iran ceasefire deal gives Trump a way out of war - but at a high cost
stories.summary: The two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran may have significantly shifted global perceptions of American power and diplomacy, raising questions about the long-term costs of the agreement for U.S. credibility.

stories.title: UN probe blames Israeli fire, Hezbollah IED for peacekeeper deaths in Lebanon
stories.summary: A UN investigation found that one peacekeeper in Lebanon was killed by an Israeli tank projectile, while two others died from an improvised explosive device most likely placed by Hezbollah. The preliminary findings assigned responsibility to both Israeli forces and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Could Philippines’ declining literacy affect its status as help desk hub?
stories.summary: The Philippines' call center industry, which employs over a million workers and generates billions in revenue, faces a potential threat from declining literacy rates. While artificial intelligence poses one challenge, analysts warn that an education system producing insufficiently skilled graduates could undermine the country's status as a global customer service outsourcing hub.

stories.title: Trump announces US pause on Iran strikes for two weeks
stories.summary: President Trump announced a two-week suspension of U.S. bombing of Iran, linking the ceasefire to Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz. He cited talks with Pakistani leaders and called Iran's 10-point proposal a workable basis for negotiations.

stories.title: Trump: US to ‘suspend bombing’ of Iran for 2 weeks while talks held on ‘longterm peace’ deal
stories.summary: President Trump announced a two-week "double-sided ceasefire" with Iran contingent on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan's prime minister said it was effective immediately and included Lebanon, which Netanyahu disputed. Iran and Israel continued attacks after the announcement.

stories.title: Pope Leo calls Trump’s threat against Iran ‘truly unacceptable’
stories.summary: It is rare for the pope to respond directly to a world leader.

stories.title: Netanyahu says US-Iran ceasefire ‘does not include Lebanon’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed the U.S. decision to suspend strikes on Iran but stated that the ceasefire does not extend to Lebanon, where Israel continues operations against Hezbollah.

stories.title: U.S. disrupts Russian military-run DNS hijacking network, Justice Department says
stories.summary: U.S. Justice Deartment said that the ‌GRU used routers ​to facilitate hijacking operations against worldwide ⁠targets, including individuals in military, government and critical ‌infrastructure sector

stories.title: Tai Po probe: fire contractor admits never conducting on-site checks due to ‘busy’ schedule
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, Hong Kong, which killed 168 people, began its second round of hearings. Chung Kit-man, director of Victory Fire Engineering, the estate's fire service equipment contractor, admitted he never conducted on-site checks due to being too busy.

stories.title: Iraqi armed group says it will release abducted US journalist, says she must leave Iraq immediately
stories.summary: The Iran-aligned Iraqi armed group Kataib Hezbollah announced it would release US journalist Shelly Kittleson, who was abducted in Baghdad. The group stated she must leave Iraq immediately.

stories.title: Woman charged over Singapore crash that killed Indonesian girl in Chinatown
stories.summary: A 38-year-old woman in Singapore was charged with two counts of driving without due care and attention after an accident in Chinatown that killed a six-year-old Indonesian girl and severely injured her mother. The woman cannot be named due to a gag order and faces potential imprisonment if convicted.

stories.title: DHS says US could stop processing international travellers at some airports in ‘sanctuary cities’
stories.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security said it could stop processing international travelers at some airports in so-called sanctuary cities. The move was being considered as Congress remained deadlocked over DHS funding.

stories.title: French Foreign Minister Barrot hopes Trump does not go ahead with threat against Iran
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said he hoped US President Trump would not follow through on his latest threats against Iran. The statement was made as tensions escalated over the Strait of Hormuz deadline.

stories.title: Iran lists demands as Trump pulls back from catastrophic attacks
stories.summary: Iran declared victory in the weeks-long conflict triggered by U.S. and Israeli military strikes and presented a 10-point plan aimed at permanently ending hostilities.

stories.title: US, Israel, Iran agree two-week truce, Tehran lists demands
stories.summary: The U.S., Israel, and Iran agreed to a two-week truce after weeks of conflict sparked by U.S. and Israeli strikes. Iran claimed victory and presented a 10-point plan for permanently ending the war.

stories.title: Germany's young men do not need permit for foreign travel, ministry said
stories.summary: Germany's defense ministry clarified that young men will not need prior permission to travel abroad despite the country's new military service law. The ministry said it would issue a blanket exemption to avoid unnecessary bureaucracy.

stories.title: Iranian hackers' targeting of US critical infrastructure has escalated since start of war, US says
stories.summary: April 7 - Iranian hacking campaigns targeting equipment used across multiple U.S. critical infrastructure sectors are escalating in response to hostilities, U.S. cybersecurity, law enforcement and int

stories.title: Ukraine sees growth in new truck sales – Ukrautoprom
stories.summary: According to industry group Ukrautoprom, sales of new commercial vehicles in Ukraine rose by 23 percent in March 2026, indicating growth in the country's truck market.

stories.title: Top Australian soldier charged with war crimes to remain in jail after bail hearing
stories.summary: Former Australian special forces soldier Ben Roberts-Smith has been charged with five counts of the war crime of murder and will remain in jail after a bail hearing. The charges carry a potential penalty of life in prison.

stories.title: Middle East live: Netanyahu says US-Iran ceasefire does not include Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire reached late Tuesday does not include Lebanon. The last-minute diplomatic effort was led by Pakistan and halted planned American strikes on Iran. Formal talks between the parties are scheduled to begin in Islamabad on Friday.

stories.title: Trump branded ‘crazy’ over apocalyptic Iran threats
stories.summary: Even some former allies have called for the 79-year-old Republican's removal from office after a series of outlandish and sometimes expletive-riddled social media posts

stories.title: Hong Kong to set up company this year to fast-track San Tin tech hub as firms eye move
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities plan to establish a company this year to accelerate development of the San Tin Technopole innovation hub near the mainland border. Permanent Secretary Kevin Choi Kit-ming said firms have already expressed interest in relocating there, and measures to enable cross-border data and biological sample transfers may be introduced soon.

stories.title: Iraqis celebrates US-Iran ceasefire as two-week halt in war begins
stories.summary: Celebrations broke out across Iraq following the announcement of a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, as Iraqis welcomed the halt in hostilities.

stories.title: Climate activist Greta Thunberg slams Trump’s threats against Iran
stories.summary: Climate activist Greta Thunberg criticised President Trump's threats against Iran. Polls indicate that young Americans are increasingly sceptical of foreign military intervention, including the war on Iran.

stories.title: 'Europe is a bit of a mess', Donald Trump Jr. tells panel in Bosnia
stories.summary: Donald Trump Jr. visited Bosnia's Serb Republic in a trip widely seen as a show of support for ousted pro-Russian leader Milorad Dodik. During a panel in Banja Luka, he criticized the European Union.

stories.title: Vatican aid convoy to southern Lebanese town forced back by bombardment
stories.summary: A Vatican-organized humanitarian aid convoy heading to a besieged Christian town in southern Lebanon was forced to turn back on Tuesday due to bombardment in the area. The convoy had been arranged through the Vatican's embassy in Beirut.

stories.title: Russia positions itself as 'major space power' in countries across Asia, Africa, and Latin America – CCD
stories.summary: Russia is promoting itself as a major space power across Asia, Africa, and Latin America through its network of "Rossotrudnichestvo" agencies and "Russian Houses," according to a report by the CCD.

stories.title: Japan’s deportation drive strikes fear into asylum seekers, foreign residents
stories.summary: Japan forcibly deported a record 318 foreign nationals under escort in 2025, a 30 percent increase from the previous year, as part of the government's Zero Illegal Foreign Residents Plan. Rights groups warn the intensified deportation drive is deepening fear among asylum seekers and long-term foreign residents.

stories.title: Chinese youth are embracing Ching Ming with cultural confidence
stories.summary: Young people in China are increasingly embracing the Ching Ming Festival, a traditional occasion for honoring deceased family members and ancestors. The observance, which involves sweeping tombstones, burning incense, and offering food, is seeing renewed interest amid a broader trend of cultural confidence among Chinese youth.

stories.title: Oil prices slide, stocks surge as Trump announces two-week Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Oil prices fell and global stock markets surged after Trump announced the two-week Iran ceasefire, as investors anticipated the possible resumption of oil and gas flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Kyiv lays out how ‘Russian satellites help Iran in war’
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence assessed that Russian satellites conducted detailed imagery surveys of military facilities across at least 11 Middle Eastern countries, including U.S. bases, between March 21 and 31. Iran subsequently struck several of the mapped targets, according to the assessment reported by Reuters on day 1,505 of Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Singapore says no negotiations for Hormuz safe passage; transit is ‘right, not privilege’
stories.summary: Singapore's Foreign Affairs Minister Vivian Balakrishnan stated that Singapore will not negotiate for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, asserting that transit through international waterways is a legal right, not a privilege. He was responding to a parliamentary question about whether Singapore would engage Iran or consider paying a toll for its vessels.

stories.title: Tributes after British teenager dies while visiting Vietnam
stories.summary: British teenager Orla Wates died in a road accident while visiting Vietnam. Her mother remembered her as 'beautiful, independent and very funny.'

stories.title: Iran says talks with US will begin in Pakistan’s Islamabad on Friday
stories.summary: Iran announced that negotiations with the United States would begin on Friday in Islamabad, Pakistan, based on Tehran's 10-point proposal, which includes demands for control over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Portugal says U.S. uses Azores base on condition no civilian infrastructure targeted
stories.summary: LISBON, April 7 - Portugal said it had authorised 76 landings by U.S. aircraft at the Lajes air base in the Azores and 25 overflights of its territory since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran,

stories.title: Iran agrees to open Strait of Hormuz for two-week US ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran would agree to a ceasefire on the condition that U.S. attacks against Iran are halted, and confirmed Tehran's willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz during the two-week truce.

stories.title: Ancient China lavish toilet routines: nobles used silk, Empress Cixi had 28 maids to serve her
stories.summary: The article discusses elaborate toilet customs in ancient China's imperial court, where even basic hygiene became a display of status and ritual. While commoners used leaves or pebbles, nobles used silk for personal cleaning. Empress Cixi reportedly had 28 maids attending to her bathroom needs.

stories.title: Indonesian fisherman nets surprise catch – a Chinese underwater drone
stories.summary: An Indonesian fisherman discovered a Chinese underwater drone near the Lombok Strait, a key deepwater passage between Bali and Lombok leading toward Australia. The strait is closely monitored by the United States and Australia as one of few routes accommodating submarine transits at operational depth.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz asks Trump to extend deadline for two weeks; requests Iran to open Hormuz for corresponding period
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif asked US President Donald Trump to extend by two weeks the deadline he set for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and reach a deal with Washington. The appeal came hours before the deadline, after Trump warned of wider bombing of Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Democrats call on Republicans to prioritise patriotic duty over party loyalty and stop Trump’s ‘madness’
stories.summary: US House Democrats called on Republicans to prioritize patriotic duty over party loyalty and halt what they termed President Trump's 'madness' after he threatened to decimate an entire civilization. Trump had given Iran until 8pm ET to end its Strait of Hormuz blockade or face destruction of bridges and power plants.

stories.title: Fuel prices could keep rising for months after Hormuz reopens, US EIA says
stories.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration warned that fuel prices could continue rising for months even after the Strait of Hormuz reopens. The agency expects uncertainty around future supply disruptions to keep oil prices above pre-conflict levels through the rest of 2026.

stories.title: Republican wins Georgia runoff election to replace Marjorie Taylor Greene
stories.summary: Republican Clay Fuller won the Georgia special runoff election to replace former Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene in the conservative-leaning northwest Georgia congressional district. Fuller, who supports the war in Iran, defeated Democrat Shawn Harris, who opposed it. The Associated Press called the race as results from rural counties came in.

stories.title: Ukraine lawmakers inch forward with IMF-linked bill for strained budget
stories.summary: Ukraine's parliament passed one of several tax reform bills on April 7 as part of conditions set by the International Monetary Fund. Additional votes were expected the following day as Kyiv works to secure critical financing for its strained budget.

stories.title: Trump suspends Iran bombing for two weeks, after apocalyptic threats
stories.summary: President Trump suspended planned military strikes on Iran for a two-week period, linking the pause to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement followed earlier threats of mass destruction against the country.

stories.title: Court sentences Russian agent who attempted to derail a Ukrzaliznytsia train to up to 15 years in prison
stories.summary: A court in Ukraine sentenced a Russian intelligence agent to 15 years in prison with property confiscation. The agent was apprehended in May 2025 in the Kyiv region while attempting to derail a Ukrzaliznytsia freight train.

stories.title: New research institute to ramp up efforts as Hong Kong pursues ‘AI for all’
stories.summary: Hong Kong is establishing the Hong Kong Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Institute to pursue an "AI for all" strategy. Permanent Secretary Kevin Choi Kit-ming said the institute would prioritize integrating locally developed AI to strengthen government capabilities and ensure benefits reach all residents and sectors.

stories.title: Iran says talks with US to begin Friday in Islamabad
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Security Council announced that negotiations with the United States would begin Friday, April 10, in Islamabad, Pakistan. Iran submitted a 10-point proposal to Washington via Pakistani intermediaries covering Strait of Hormuz transit, sanctions relief, and withdrawal provisions.

stories.title: USTR Greer says US-Mexico-Canada pact talks may run past July 1 deadline
stories.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said negotiations to rebalance the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement are likely to continue past the July 1 deadline. The Trump administration will attempt to resolve as many issues as possible before that date.

stories.title: China and Russia veto UN resolution on protecting Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: China and Russia vetoed a UN Security Council resolution aimed at protecting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The council voted 11 in favor, with two against and two abstentions.

stories.title: China and Russia veto UN resolution on protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: China and Russia vetoed a United Nations Security Council resolution aimed at protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The council voted 11 in favor, with two vetoes and two abstentions among its 15 members.

stories.title: New Zealand asks US to send fuel tankers to Pacific to alleviate pressure caused by Iran war
stories.summary: New Zealand Foreign Minister Winston Peters met U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington and requested that the U.S. send fuel tankers to the Pacific. Peters emphasized the significant economic and fuel supply pressures the Iran war has placed on New Zealand and Pacific island nations.

stories.title: White House confirms two-week suspension of strikes on Iran
stories.summary: The White House confirmed that the United States has agreed to suspend all bombing and military attacks on Iran for a two-week period as part of the ceasefire arrangement.

stories.title: U.S. and Iran Agree to 2-Week Cease-Fire
stories.summary: The United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, with the announcement coming less than two hours before President Trump's deadline for escalated military action was set to expire.

stories.title: Trump announces 'double sided ceasefire' between US, Iran following Pakistani proposal
stories.summary: President Trump announced a "double sided ceasefire" between the US and Iran following a proposal from Pakistan. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had urged both sides to implement a two-week ceasefire to allow diplomacy to conclude the war.

stories.title: Cambodia has a new law targeting scams, but is it just another ‘paper reform’?
stories.summary: Cambodia's parliament approved the country's first law targeting scam centers, following international pressure over an industry estimated to generate up to US$19 billion annually. Analysts warn the law may be ineffective unless authorities pursue the officials and networks that have long enabled trafficking of an estimated 200,000 workers into fraud compounds.

stories.title: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani will seek to dismiss fraud case in US
stories.summary: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani will ask a US judge to dismiss a civil fraud case brought by the SEC. Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani were charged in November 2024 with orchestrating a bribery scheme involving Indian government officials to benefit Adani Green Energy.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russians try to scale up their 'safari' against our people
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russian forces of escalating brutal drone strikes targeting Ukrainian civilians, describing the attacks as a "safari" against the Ukrainian people.

stories.title: Iranian 10 point proposal ‘workable basis’, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump described Iran's 10-point proposal as a "workable basis" for negotiations. He said he agreed to suspend strikes on Iran after consultations with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, conditional on Iran immediately reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukrainian military take part in consultations on situation in Strait of Hormuz – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that Ukrainian military personnel are taking part in international consultations regarding the future operation of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Dar says Israeli attack on Iran set off ‘dangerous developments’ that ‘severely damaged’ peace process
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar told the Senate that an Israeli attack on Iran triggered developments that severely damaged the peace process between Washington and Tehran. Pakistan has positioned itself as a facilitator in those negotiations ahead of Trump's deadline for Iran.

stories.title: Trump says he has agreed to suspend 'bombing and attack of Iran' for two weeks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a two-week suspension of bombing and military attacks on Iran, as diplomatic efforts continue.

stories.title: Trump says he has agreed to two-week ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump announced he has agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran. He stated he expects a broader agreement to be finalized and completed during the ceasefire period.

stories.summary: Former soldier charged with five war crime murders. Follow updates liveGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastCyclone-hammered reefs can take many years to recover, study findsStor

stories.title: Donald Trump says he has agreed two-week ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: US president says on social media he agreed to suspend attack for two weeks, subject to Iran opening the strait of Hormuz, ahead of self-imposed deadlineMiddle East crisis – live updatesSign up for th

stories.title: Trump agrees to pause attacks on Iran if Strait of Hormuz opens
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced he would extend his threatened deadline to strike Iran by two weeks, contingent on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping.

stories.title: Qatar says four wounded, including a child, by missile debris
stories.summary: Qatar's interior ministry reported that four people, including a child, were injured by falling debris after Qatari air defenses intercepted Iranian missiles. The debris struck a home in the Muriykh residential area in western Doha.

stories.title: Ukraine to discuss security cooperation with European partners in coming weeks – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine will engage with European partners in the coming weeks on joint arms production and coordination of security actions.

stories.title: Trump will pursue stability with China’s Xi in May meeting, USTR Greer says
stories.summary: US Trade Representative Greer said President Trump will pursue stability with Chinese President Xi Jinping at a May meeting. Washington is seeking to ensure continued access to China's rare earth minerals.

stories.title: Shelly Kittleson freed after being held hostage by Iraqi militia
stories.summary: American journalist Shelly Kittleson was freed from captivity after being held hostage by the Iraqi militia Kataeb Hezbollah, which released a video of her shortly after her release.

stories.title: Iraq's Kataeb Hezbollah airs Shelly Kittleson propaganda video
stories.summary: The Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah released a propaganda video of American journalist Shelly Kittleson hours after she was reportedly freed from captivity in Iraq.

stories.title: American journalist Shelly Kittleson released, say Iraqi officials
stories.summary: American journalist Shelly Kittleson was released in Iraq after being abducted on March 31. The Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah announced it had decided to free her.

stories.title: A Lebanese seafarer caught in a double-whammy amid the West Asia war
stories.summary: Hundreds of merchant ships are stranded in the Gulf, unable to navigate the Strait of Hormuz amid the broader West Asia conflict. A Lebanese seafarer's situation highlights the dual impact of the crisis on civilian maritime workers.

stories.title: US Jewish groups denounce Trump’s threat that a ‘whole civilization will die’ in Iran
stories.summary: Multiple US Jewish organizations denounced President Trump's threat that a "whole civilization will die" in Iran. The head of the JCPA stated that Jewish communities understand the gravity of leaders calling for populations to be wiped out.

stories.title: On India’s updated climate pledges
stories.summary: India announced revised Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement, prompting analysis of how the country balances its climate mitigation commitments with its developmental needs and costs.

stories.title: Iran urges youth to form human chains to protect power plants
stories.summary: Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard called on young people to form human chains around bridges and power plants to protect critical infrastructure. The Guard warned that Iran would "deprive the U.S. and its allies of the region's oil and gas for years."

stories.title: Russian intelligence spies on EU, US,and Ukrainian citizens via hacked routers – SSU
stories.summary: The Security Service of Ukraine, working with the FBI, Polish counterintelligence, and EU law enforcement, conducted a joint cyber operation to disrupt Russian GRU intelligence activities that used hacked routers to spy on citizens in the EU, US, and Ukraine.

stories.title: Preliminary UN probe blames Israel and likely Hezbollah for peacekeeper deaths
stories.summary: A preliminary United Nations investigation attributed the deaths of Indonesian peacekeepers in southern Lebanon to Israel and likely Hezbollah in two separate incidents. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the killings "unacceptable."

stories.title: 'We must reject division:' UN chief marks 32 years since start of Rwandan genocide
stories.summary: Rwanda on Tuesday marked 32 years since the genocide that massacred more than a million people in the space of just one hundred days.

stories.title: Trump announces two-week ceasefire as Iran agrees to reopen Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: President Trump declared a two-week ceasefire in the US-Iran conflict, making the suspension of military operations conditional on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz to maritime traffic.

stories.title: 'Hard to unseat the king': Iran's control of Hormuz may not be end of petrodollar
stories.summary: Experts suggest that while Iran can maintain control of the Strait of Hormuz, displacing the US dollar's dominance in global oil trade will prove far more difficult. The strait, through which roughly 20 percent of global energy passes, has become the focal point of the conflict.

stories.title: Watch: Iranians form human chains on bridges, near power plants as Trump threatens to unleash ‘hell’
stories.summary: Iranians formed human chains across several cities on Tuesday, gathering on bridges and around power plants as US strikes on Iran intensified and President Trump's deadline to unleash "hell" approached.

stories.title: Trump: US to ‘suspend bombing’ of Iran for 2 weeks as talks held on ‘longterm peace’ deal
stories.summary: President Trump announced a two-week "double sided ceasefire" with Iran while talks proceed on a long-term peace deal. Israel is also part of the ceasefire, though Iran launched missile attacks on the Jerusalem area. The pause is conditional on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump agrees to suspend attack on Iran for two weeks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump agreed to suspend planned military strikes against Iran for a two-week period as part of a provisional ceasefire arrangement between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Pakistan requests two-week extension for talks as Trump's Iran deadline nears
stories.summary: Pakistan formally requested a two-week extension for diplomatic talks as President Trump's deadline threatening destruction of Iranian civilization approached. The White House confirmed Trump was aware of Islamabad's request.

stories.title: Afghanistan, Pakistan hold 'useful' peace talks in China, says Kabul
stories.summary: Afghanistan and Pakistan held peace talks in China, which Kabul described as "useful." The discussions followed a conflict that broke out between the two South Asian neighbors in October 2025.

stories.title: Russia's fourth-largest oil refinery halts operations after Ukrainian drone attacks – CCD
stories.summary: The Nizhny Novgorodnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, the country's fourth-largest, halted operations after Ukrainian drone strikes. The facility suspended production following the attack.

stories.title: Talking peace: why mediation still matters in a world at war
stories.summary: Amid the ongoing war in West Asia, discussions about mediation as a conflict-resolution tool have gained renewed prominence. Analysts point to historical precedents where individuals and states facilitated agreements between conflicting parties alongside the evolution of international dispute-resolution conventions.

stories.title: French nationals freed from detention in Iran, returning to France, Macron says
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that French nationals Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris were freed from detention in Iran and were returning to France. The two had been held for over three years on espionage charges.

stories.title: World held hostage by reliance on fossil fuels, Christiana Figueres warns – and climate health impacts are ‘mother of all injustices’

stories.title: What we know about Pakistan’s proposed Iran war pause
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reported that diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Israeli war on Iran are making progress. Islamabad has positioned itself as a mediator in the conflict.

stories.title: Russia's Sheskharis terminal halts oil loading after drone attack – Reuters
stories.summary: Crude oil exports from Russia's Sheskharis terminal at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk were suspended after a major Ukrainian drone attack caused a fire. Reuters reported the halt in loading operations.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz calls on nation to contribute to fuel conservation, austerity drive
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urged the nation to contribute to fuel conservation and austerity measures in response to the global fuel crisis stemming from the US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began February 28. Markets nationwide except in Sindh were ordered to close by 8pm.

stories.title: Iranian musician stages protest at power station over Trump threats
stories.summary: Iranian musician Ali Ghamsari staged a symbolic protest performance outside the Damavand power station in Iran, responding to US President Trump's threats against Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Turkish, Pakistani foreign ministers hold call on efforts to end Iran war: Report
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan spoke by phone with Pakistani Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar on Tuesday to coordinate diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: US seeks to deport Kilmar Ábrego García to Liberia despite new Costa Rica deal

stories.title: China, Russia veto UN resolution to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Russia and China vetoed a UN Security Council resolution to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Pakistan and Colombia abstained. The Bahrain-drafted resolution received 11 votes in favor after six rounds of revisions.

stories.title: As missile barrage on Iran continues, what is it teaching China about US war resilience?
stories.summary: Whether the US-Israeli war on Iran wraps up quickly or drags on, the repercussions will be felt for years, reshaping warfare, geopolitics and energy security as well as how the world sees the United S

stories.title: Kanye West barred from UK over antisemitic history, causing music festival cancellation
stories.summary: Rapper Kanye West was barred from entering the United Kingdom due to his history of antisemitic statements, leading to the cancellation of a music festival appearance. West had offered to meet British Jewish leaders to express remorse.

stories.title: Djibouti and the Horn of Africa: new front in the war on Iran
stories.summary: Djibouti, which has built its economy by hosting military bases from multiple world powers, is emerging as a new strategic front in the broader conflict involving Iran and the Horn of Africa.

stories.title: Trump condemned over threat that Iran's 'civilisation will die'
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General expressed deep concern over President Trump's statement that Iran's "civilisation will die," made as the US president pressured Tehran to finalize a deal ending hostilities.

stories.title: Russian airstrikes damage hospital Kherson region, patients evacuated
stories.summary: Russian airstrikes damaged a medical facility in Stepanivka, Kherson region, Ukraine, that housed patients requiring specialized care. Patients were evacuated following the attack.

stories.title: Exclusive: Staff in Karim Khan's office write in support of his return to ICC
stories.summary: A group of staff in ICC Prosecutor Karim Khan's office, claiming to represent the "silent majority," wrote a letter supporting his return to the International Criminal Court and urging respect for judicial findings regarding his alleged misconduct.

stories.title: Iran warns region and beyond as tension builds ahead of US ultimatum
stories.summary: Iran issued warnings to countries in the region and beyond as tensions escalated ahead of a US ultimatum. President Trump had threatened to destroy every bridge and power plant in Iran.

stories.title: Dubai dog lovers revel regardless of Mid-East war
stories.summary: A dog festival called Barkfest took place in Dubai, with attendees largely unaffected by the ongoing war in the Gulf region. Revellers at the event paid little attention to the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Gunfight near Israeli consulate in Istanbul recalls Turkey's past militant attacks
stories.summary: An attacker was killed in a gunfight with police outside the building housing the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on April 7. Turkish authorities and Reuters witnesses confirmed the incident, which recalled past militant attacks in Turkey.

stories.title: A whole civilisation will die, says Trump ahead his Iran deadline
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened that "a whole civilisation will die" ahead of his deadline for Iran, having previously stated the US military could bomb Iran's bridges, power plants, and other civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Pope Leo slams Trump's 'unacceptable' threat to Iranians
stories.summary: Pope Leo publicly condemned President Trump's threats to obliterate Iran, stating that such remarks raise serious questions about morality and international law.

stories.title: Kuwait, Bahrain push preemptive measures, close bridges as Iran threatens transport infrastructure
stories.summary: Kuwait ordered citizens to stay near protected areas overnight, while Bahrain closed the King Fahd Causeway linking it to Saudi Arabia. Both Gulf states took preemptive measures as Iran threatened regional transport infrastructure.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks ambulance in Kherson, injuring three medics
stories.summary: Russian forces used a drone to strike an emergency medical team in Kherson's Dniprovskyi district, injuring three healthcare workers. The attack targeted an ambulance responding to calls in the area.

stories.title: Pakistan appeals to Trump to extend deadline, Iran to reopen Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif appealed to President Trump to extend his military deadline against Iran, citing progress in diplomatic efforts. Sharif also urged Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iranian hackers' targeting of US critical infrastructure has escalated since start of war, US says
stories.summary: U.S. authorities reported that Iranian hackers have escalated cyberattacks on American critical infrastructure since the start of the conflict. Targeted sectors include government services, water and wastewater systems, and energy facilities.

stories.title: US soldier’s wife released after arrest by ICE agents at military base

stories.title: To beat Cambodia’s scam gangs, US must work with China – not blame it

stories.title: Passover and Song of Songs: What spring teaches us about freedom
stories.summary: A reflection ties the Jewish holiday of Passover and the biblical Song of Songs to themes of freedom and renewal in spring. The piece notes that Israel's hiking trails are quieter than usual amid the current security situation.

stories.title: After fleeing past Hezbollah fighting, some Israelis on northern border vow to stay
stories.summary: Some Israeli residents along the northern border with Lebanon are returning to their homes after being displaced by Hezbollah rocket attacks since October 2023. Residents of communities near the border, including Manara, have vowed to stay despite the ongoing threat.

stories.title: Voloshyn: Russians kill 9 civilians, injure 49 injured in one day in southern regions
stories.summary: Russian strikes on southern Ukrainian regions killed 9 civilians and injured 49 others, including a child, in a single day. Ukrainian official Voloshyn reported that Russian forces targeted residential buildings, civilian infrastructure, and transport.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strikes kill five, including child and parents at home, Russian officials say
stories.summary: Russian officials reported that Ukrainian drone strikes killed five civilians, including a 12-year-old boy and his parents, in Russian-controlled southeastern Ukraine on April 7. A school in the area was also struck.

stories.title: US-Iran mediation efforts via Pakistan continue, but strikes on Saudi Arabia may derail effort, say sources
stories.summary: Mediation efforts between the United States and Iran continued through Pakistan, but Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia threatened to derail the dialogue. Sources said the next three to four hours were critical for the future of negotiations.

stories.title: PMDC to hold exam for medical students seeking transfer to Pakistani institutions on May 16
stories.summary: Pakistan's Medical and Dental Council announced a National Equivalence Board exam on May 16 for medical students affected by the US-Israeli war on Iran who are seeking transfer to Pakistani institutions. The computer-based exam assesses students who partially completed education abroad.

stories.title: Russia supplies Iran with cyber support, spy imagery to hone attacks, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Ukraine's intelligence assessment alleges that Russia has provided Iran with cyber support and detailed satellite imagery of military facilities to help Tehran target US forces in the region.

stories.title: Protesters in Iraq swarm Kuwaiti consulate after deadly rocket attack
stories.summary: Crowds of protesters stormed the Kuwaiti consulate in the southern Iraqi city of Basra following a deadly rocket attack. The demonstrators expressed anger over the incident.

stories.title: Iranians brace for possible devastation as Trump’s deadline looms
stories.summary: Iranians across the country are bracing for potential devastation as President Trump's military deadline approaches. Anxiety is widespread amid threats of US-led strikes on civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Several people evacuated as rain causes flooding in parts of Peshawar
stories.summary: Rescue personnel evacuated at least 65 people from Peshawar's Sardar Colony as continued rainfall caused flooding across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Mohmand district. Heavy rains also struck parts of Punjab, with the ongoing spell claiming several lives across KP, Punjab, and Balochistan.

stories.title: US lawmakers call to remove Trump after 'civilization will die' threat against Iran
stories.summary: Several US lawmakers invoked the 25th Amendment and called for President Trump's removal from office after he threatened that Iran's "civilization will die." The amendment allows for the ousting of a president deemed mentally or physically incapacitated.

stories.title: How is the US-Israel war on Iran affecting Russian-Iranian relations?
stories.summary: Moscow has benefitted from rising oil prices resulting from the US-Israeli war on Iran, complicating Russian-Iranian relations as Tehran faces sustained military pressure from Washington and its allies.

stories.title: Only virtual talks, no new investment push before Xi-Trump summit: Greer

stories.title: Libyan financier enabled ‘$300m in loans’ for Haftar’s Tripoli offensive
stories.summary: A report revealed that a Libyan financier facilitated approximately $300 million in loans to fund Khalifa Haftar's 2019 military offensive on Tripoli. The Libyan public was left burdened with unpaid debts, and key figures have faced no accountability.

stories.title: São Paulo stock exchange reverses losses and closes higher on US-Iran negotiation signals
stories.summary: The São Paulo stock exchange reversed its losses in the final minutes of trading and closed Tuesday with a slight gain of 0.05%, lifted by President Donald Trump's statement that he is in "heated nego

stories.title: Trump warns ‘whole civilisation will die’ in Iran if Tehran does not heed his ultimatum
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned on Truth Social that "a whole civilisation will die" in Iran if Tehran does not comply with his ultimatum. Tehran reported that U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iranian infrastructure were already under way.

stories.title: Iranians 'form human chains' at power plants: state media
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that citizens and senior officials formed human chains around power plants in a show of national solidarity amid US President Trump's threats to destroy Iran's infrastructure.

stories.title: Iran positively reviewing Pakistan’s request for a two-week ceasefire: Report
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran is positively reviewing Pakistan's request for a two-week ceasefire. The diplomatic effort comes amid escalating tensions over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Zaporizhzhia region with drones and airstrikes, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck settlements in the Zaporizhzhia district using drones and airstrikes. Three people were wounded as a result of the attacks throughout the day.

stories.title: Trump says he is in "heated negotiations" with Iran hours before Hormuz ultimatum expires
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said Tuesday he is in "heated negotiations" with Iran just hours before his ultimatum for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face massive attacks on its civilian infras

stories.title: US hits military targets on Iran’s Kharg Island, Vance says no change to strategy
stories.summary: The United States struck military targets on Iran's Kharg Island, according to Vice President JD Vance, who said there was no change to U.S. strategy. A U.S. official stated the strikes did not impact oil infrastructure on the island.

stories.title: Pakistan PM seeks two-week extension to Trump's deadline on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif publicly requested that President Trump extend his deadline on Iran by two weeks to allow diplomacy to proceed. Sharif also urged Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for the same period as a goodwill gesture.

stories.title: Palestinians queue for hours in pouring rain to get bread
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza were seen waiting in line for hours in heavy rain to obtain bread as food shortages in the territory continue to worsen.

stories.title: ‘Policy of abuse’: Women march in Cuba against US energy blockade
stories.summary: Women in Cuba marched against the US energy blockade in government-led protests. Demonstrators called on Washington to allow oil shipments to reach the island.

stories.title: Antimicrobial resistance threatens the lives of millions on the African continent
stories.summary: In tonight's edition, as leaders  gathered for the “One Health” summit in France, antimicrobial resistance emerges as a bigger killer in Africa than malaria, HIV or TB. Also, a woman seeking care was

stories.title: Trump warns 'whole civilisation will die' in Iran if ultimatum expires
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned on his Truth Social platform that "a whole civilisation will die" in Iran if his ultimatum expires without compliance. Trump added, "I don't want that to happen, but it probably will."

stories.title: ‘Pre-admission of genocide’: Politicos blast Trump over threat to destroy ‘a whole civilisation’ in Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened on Truth Social that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" if Iran does not agree to open the Strait of Hormuz and reach a deal. Pakistani politicians condemned the rhetoric as a "pre-admission of genocide."

stories.title: The HH-60W helped rescue a pilot in Iran. Here’s why the Air Force might not buy more.
stories.summary: The HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopter was used in a recent pilot rescue operation in Iran. The Air Force sought to cap procurement at 75 aircraft in fiscal year 2023, but Congress has pushed back against limiting the fleet.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson urges US officials to oppose Trump’s plan to target Iranian civil infrastructure
stories.summary: Conservative commentator Tucker Carlson publicly urged U.S. officials to oppose President Trump's plan to target Iranian civilian infrastructure, calling the remarks 'evil.' Trump dismissed Carlson as 'a low-IQ person.'

stories.title: Russia's Black Sea's Sheskharis terminal halts loadings after drone attack, sources say
stories.summary: Crude oil exports from Russia's Sheskharis terminal at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk were suspended on April 7 after a large drone attack caused a fire. Two sources familiar with the situation confirmed the halt in loadings.

stories.title: Reuters reports Russia’s NORSI refinery halts operations after Ukrainian drone strike
stories.summary: Russia's NORSI oil refinery in Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod Region, suspended operations after sustaining damage from a Ukrainian drone strike in the early hours of April 5, according to Reuters sources.

stories.title: Will Trump Attack or TACO?
stories.summary: A deadline was set giving Tehran four hours to accept a ceasefire deal with the United States, with the alternative being US strikes on Iranian civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Russia delays lunar missions as US marks historic flight
stories.summary: Russia postponed the launch of three lunar missions, according to the Interfax news agency, setting back its lunar exploration program. The delay came as the United States celebrated a historic crewed flight around the moon.

stories.title: Russia and China block UN resolution on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Russia and China vetoed a UN Security Council resolution concerning the Strait of Hormuz. The resolution had received support from 11 of the 15 council members despite being watered down to avoid vetoes.

stories.title: Iran has attacked Saudi Arabia’s Jubail petrochemical complex, IRGC says
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it attacked Saudi Arabia's Jubail petrochemical complex. Iran stated the strike was in retaliation for attacks on petrochemical plants connected to its South Pars gas field.

stories.title: Pope Leo slams Trump’s threat that Iran’s ‘civilisation will die’
stories.summary: Pope Leo condemned US President Donald Trump's remarks that Iran's "civilisation will die," calling the threats "unacceptable" and raising concerns about morality and international law.

stories.title: Mediterranean migrant deaths mounting towards 1,000 in 2026: UN
stories.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that migrant deaths in the Mediterranean Sea are approaching 1,000 in 2026, marking one of the deadliest starts to a year since records began.

stories.summary: As Donald Trump threatened to wipe out an entire civilisation in Iran ahead of his latest deadline for Tehran to open up the Strait of Hormuz, Qatar's foreign ministry official warned that the world w

stories.title: Two women injured and home damaged in Chernihiv region village after Russian attack
stories.summary: Two elderly women were injured and homes on two streets were damaged in a Russian drone attack on a village in the Novobilouska community of Ukraine's Chernihiv region.

stories.title: No military objective justifies destruction of a society’s infrastructure, UN chief says
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed deep concern over statements suggesting an entire civilization could face consequences for political and military decisions. His remarks followed Trump's warning that 'a whole civilization will die tonight' if Iran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said no military objective justifies wholesale destruction of a society's infrastructure.

stories.title: French couple leave Iran after over three years in detention
stories.summary: French citizens Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris are expected to arrive in France on Wednesday after being released from house arrest in Iran. The pair had been detained for over three years.

stories.title: Pro-Iran group says will release US journalist kidnapped in Iraq
stories.summary: The Iran-aligned Iraqi armed group Kataib Hezbollah announced it would release abducted US journalist Shelly Kittleson, who was kidnapped in Baghdad in late March. The group said she must leave Iraq immediately upon release.

stories.title: Afghanistan, Pakistan held 'useful' peace talks, Kabul says
stories.summary: Afghanistan and Pakistan held what Kabul described as useful peace talks following clashes between the Afghan Taliban and Pakistani forces that reignited in February. Pakistan accuses Afghanistan of harboring hostile militants, a charge Kabul denies. China has offered to mediate between the two sides.

stories.title: FIFA opens disciplinary probe against Spanish FA after Islamaphobic chants
stories.summary: FIFA opened a disciplinary investigation into the Spanish Football Association following Islamophobic chants during a match against Egypt. Barcelona and Spain forward Lamine Yamal publicly condemned the chants from home supporters.

stories.title: Massive fire engulfs oil storage tanks near Baghdad
stories.summary: A large fire broke out at oil storage tanks in Nahrawan, near Baghdad, Iraq. Video footage showed intense orange flames and thick black smoke rising from the facility, which held so-called 'black oil.'

stories.title: Trump's 'rhetoric itself could create a norm' for others to terrorise entire populations
stories.summary: Negah Angha, a visiting fellow at King's College London and former senior advisor at the US State Department and National Security Council under Biden, told FRANCE 24 that aggressive US rhetoric toward Iran risks establishing a precedent other countries could follow, potentially causing emotional and humanitarian crises in Iran and surrounding nations.

stories.title: Russian forces launch nearly 60 attacks on Dnipro region, four killed and 24 wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 60 attacks on Ukraine's Dnipro region, targeting the Nikopol, Kryvyi Rih, and Pavlohrad districts. Four people were killed and 24 others were wounded throughout the day.

stories.title: ‘No end in sight’ if Trump acts on threat to destroy Iran infrastructure
stories.summary: Experts warn that if Donald Trump follows through on threats to destroy Iranian infrastructure, the conflict could escalate indefinitely. Analysts say Iran would likely respond with additional attacks, further destabilizing the broader Middle East region.

stories.title: Trump to pursue stability with China’s Xi in May meeting, USTR Greer says
stories.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said President Trump will seek stability in a planned May meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Greer stated the U.S. is 'not looking for a massive confrontation' and characterized the bilateral relationship as stable.

stories.title: US Navy seeks 1,200% increase in Tomahawk missile procurement for 2027
stories.summary: The US Navy is requesting $3 billion to purchase Tomahawk cruise missiles for fiscal year 2027, representing a 1,200% increase in procurement. The request aims to replenish stockpiles depleted during the ongoing Iran war.

stories.title: US judge rejects bid by Swiss Bank UBS to limit its liability for Nazi-linked crimes
stories.summary: A U.S. judge rejected Swiss bank UBS's attempt to expand a 1999 settlement of $1.25 billion to cover newly discovered ties between Nazi officials and Credit Suisse. The ruling means UBS may face additional liability for Nazi-linked financial crimes.

stories.title: Efforts to facilitate talks between US and Iran ongoing, Pakistani sources say
stories.summary: Pakistani sources told Reuters that mediation efforts to facilitate talks between the United States and Iran are ongoing. A senior security official warned that Iran's strike on Saudi industrial facilities linked to US firms threatened to derail negotiations and could draw Pakistan in under its defense pact.

stories.title: Iranians form human chains across bridges, at power plants
stories.summary: Iranians across the country formed human chains on bridges and in front of power plants. The demonstrations were a show of solidarity amid rising tensions over threatened U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Iranians form human chains at bridges and power plants
stories.summary: Iranian authorities encouraged civilians to form human chains at bridges and power plants across the country. The gatherings came after U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iranian civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: How US-Israeli war gave Iran all the cards in the Middle East
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the U.S.-Israeli military campaign has strengthened Iran's strategic position in the Middle East. Tehran has established control over the Strait of Hormuz and reportedly united much of the Arab world behind its cause.

stories.title: US journalist in Iraq freed one week after kidnapping by Kataeb Hezbollah
stories.summary: U.S. freelance journalist Shelly Kittleson was released by the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah roughly one week after being kidnapped in Baghdad, Iraq. She was reportedly ordered to leave the country immediately upon her release.

stories.title: Ukraine’s deep-strike drone program has one bottleneck: tiny jet engine made by three European companies
stories.summary: Ukraine's long-range drone strike program is constrained by a shortage of small jet engines produced by only three European manufacturers. Current European production stands at roughly 200 engines per month, far short of the thousands Ukraine requires.

stories.title: Russia, China veto UN resolution on reopening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Russia and China vetoed a United Nations Security Council resolution calling for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain's Foreign Minister Al Zayani said the failed resolution 'sends the wrong signal to the world.'

stories.title: How AI is being used to target Palestinians
stories.summary: An investigation examines how artificial intelligence and emerging military technologies are being deployed to identify and target Palestinians in conflict zones. The report also explores how Palestinians are leveraging technology for their own purposes.

stories.title: Casualties from Russian attack in Pryluky rise to 15
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian attack on Pryluky in Chernihiv Oblast has risen to 15, including one minor.

stories.title: Are war crimes being committed in the Middle East war?
stories.summary: The UN and other organizations warned that ongoing US and Israeli strikes on Iran's critical infrastructure could constitute war crimes. The warnings came Tuesday as threats of further attacks escalated.

stories.title: Commonwealth leaders vow to keep seeking reparations after Reform UK plan to halt visas
stories.summary: Politicians warn party’s pledge to ‘punish’ countries seeking justice for slavery will harm and isolate BritainCommonwealth politicians say they will not back down from seeking reparations as UK publi

stories.title: Russian attacks on Ukraine's southeast kill seven, hit city bus
stories.summary: Russian attacks on two cities in southeastern Ukraine on Tuesday killed seven people and injured more than two dozen, including a strike that hit a city bus. Ukrainian officials accused Moscow of escalating strikes rather than agreeing to a proposed Easter ceasefire.

stories.title: Kuwait is asking citizens to stay home as a ‘precautionary measure’
stories.summary: Kuwait's interior ministry instructed citizens to remain home between midnight and 6 a.m. local time as a precautionary measure. The advisory comes amid heightened regional tensions related to the U.S.-Iran confrontation.

stories.title: 'At your service': Hungary's Orban offered help to Putin, Bloomberg reports
stories.summary: A Bloomberg report citing a phone call transcript revealed that Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán offered to help Russian President Vladimir Putin "in any way," including hosting a summit in Budapest to settle the Ukraine war. The offer was reportedly made last year.

stories.title: French couple leave Iran after more than three years in jail
stories.summary: French nationals Cecile Kohler and Jacques Paris have departed Iran after spending more than three years imprisoned there. French President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the couple is on their way home.

stories.title: US remarks on NATO are pushing Europe to seek alternative security options, Spain says
stories.summary: Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares said that recent US complaints about NATO allies and threats to leave the alliance are pushing European countries to explore alternative security arrangements.

stories.title: Your router could be Russian spy — Ukraine and FBI just exposed how Moscow did it
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities and the U.S. FBI jointly exposed a Russian operation that compromised home internet routers to conduct espionage. The hackers used the compromised routers to steal passwords and other sensitive data.

stories.title: Zimbabwe launches new bank notes aimed at boosting confidence in local currency
stories.summary: Zimbabwe launched upgraded banknotes on Tuesday as part of an effort to boost public confidence in its local currency. Officials appealed to national pride during the rollout.

stories.title: Video: Historic building in Ukraine up in flames after Russia drone attack
stories.summary: A two-storey historic building in eastern Ukraine was engulfed in flames after being struck by a Russian drone. The attack damaged the building's infrastructure, as shown in video footage of the incident.

stories.title: An 'eerie still' in Tehran amid Trump's apocalyptic threats
stories.summary: Reporting from Tehran, a journalist described an 'eerie still' in the Iranian capital as residents awaited the expiration of Trump's ultimatum. Trump had warned that a 'whole civilization will die tonight' if Iran failed to reach a deal.

stories.title: Israel detects another wave of missiles launched from Iran
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported detecting another wave of missiles launched from Iran toward Israeli territory. Israel said its defensive systems were operating to intercept the incoming threats.
