stories.title: French nationals return home following Iran prison release
stories.summary: French nationals Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris returned home after being released from Iran's Evin prison in November. The pair had been detained for more than three years.

stories.title: Pakistan has repaid $1.43 billion in debt, including Eurobond due April 8, adviser says
stories.summary: Pakistan repaid $1.43 billion in external debt, including a $1.3 billion Eurobond maturing on April 8, paid on schedule and in full, according to Finance Adviser Khurram Schehzad. An additional $126.125 million in coupon obligations on other Eurobonds was also met.

stories.title: HMS Dragon docks in eastern Mediterranean after problems with water systems
stories.summary: The Royal Navy destroyer HMS Dragon docked in the eastern Mediterranean for maintenance after experiencing problems with its water systems. The Type 45 destroyer had been deployed to reinforce security around RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus after the base was struck by a drone.

stories.title: The Iran War Is Exposing Iraq’s Weaknesses
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is exposing Iraq's vulnerabilities, as Baghdad struggles to maintain control over much of its own territory amid the conflict.

stories.title: What we know about the shooting by Istanbul’s Israeli consulate
stories.summary: Gunmen opened fire near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, Turkey, sparking a gun battle with Turkish police. Details about casualties and the attackers' identities are still emerging.

stories.title: Iraq's Kataib Hezbollah to release abducted American journalist Shelly Kittleson
stories.summary: Iraq's Kataib Hezbollah announced it would release kidnapped American journalist Shelly Kittleson. Kittleson is a U.S.-based freelance reporter who had covered multiple conflicts in the Middle East and contributed to the news site Al-Monitor.

stories.title: Experts weigh two options to complete Khmelnytskyi NPP — MoE Shmyhal
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Shmyhal said experts are evaluating two options to complete the construction of two power units at the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant. A decision on the most optimal approach is pending.

stories.title: Wireless festival cancelled after Kanye West banned from entering UK
stories.summary: The Wireless music festival in London was cancelled after the artist Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, was banned from entering the UK. His electronic travel authorization was blocked by officials amid outcry over his past antisemitic remarks.

stories.title: Long Island town must pay $19M for blocking construction of Chabad synagogue
stories.summary: A U.S. judge ruled that Old Westbury, a town on Long Island, New York, must pay $19 million for blocking construction of a Chabad synagogue. The court found that a 2001 local ordinance unconstitutionally discriminated against the free exercise of religion.

stories.title: French couple allowed to leave Iran after more than three years in detention
stories.summary: French nationals Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris departed Iran after more than three years of detention on espionage charges. They left at dawn with the French ambassador, traveling to Azerbaijan, according to sources.

stories.title: Iraqi armed group releases abducted US journalist Shelly Kittleson
stories.summary: The Iraqi armed group Kataib Hezbollah released abducted U.S. journalist Shelly Kittleson in Baghdad. The group said her release was conditional on her leaving Iraq immediately.

stories.title: Russian Crude Oil Selling at 13-Year High
stories.summary: On April 2, Russian Urals crude sold for $116.05 per barrel from the Baltic port of Primorsk and $114.45 per barrel from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, according to Bloomberg, marking a 13-year high.

stories.title: Tehran synagogue destroyed as US-Israeli strikes kill over a dozen
stories.summary: A synagogue in Tehran was destroyed during a wave of overnight strikes attributed to U.S. and Israeli forces. The attacks reportedly killed over a dozen people.

stories.title: Army’s top brass condemns attacks on Saudi Arabia as ‘unnecessary escalation’: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's military leadership, led by Field Marshal Asim Munir, condemned attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure as an "unnecessary escalation" amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, according to ISPR. The 274th Corps Commanders' Conference also acknowledged government efforts to end the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: French nationals leave Iran after more than three years in detention
stories.summary: Two French nationals, Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris, left Iran on Tuesday after more than three years of detention on espionage charges. They had been under house arrest at the French embassy in Tehran since their release from prison in November, as US-Israeli strikes on Iran began in late February.

stories.title: Russia reportedly supplying Iran with spy imagery of US and Israeli targets
stories.summary: A Ukrainian intelligence report alleges that Russia has been supplying Iran with satellite imagery of U.S. and Israeli targets in the Gulf region. Moscow reportedly also provided Tehran with a detailed list of 55 Israeli energy infrastructure targets.

stories.title: Israel army 'regrets' damage to Tehran synagogue
stories.summary: The Israeli military expressed regret over collateral damage to the Rafi Niya synagogue in Tehran caused by an overnight airstrike. The IDF said the strike targeted a senior Iranian commander at the Khatam al-Anbiya emergency headquarters.

stories.title: Only IDF is capable of disarming Hamas, senior INSS researcher tells 'Post'
stories.summary: A senior researcher at Israel's Institute for National Security Studies told the Jerusalem Post that only the IDF can disarm Hamas. Meanwhile, representatives from the Gaza Board of Peace met with Hamas in Cairo to discuss amendments to a disarmament proposal.

stories.title: Shots fired outside Israel’s Istanbul consulate, 2 police officers wounded
stories.summary: Three suspects were neutralized outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul after opening fire, according to media reports. Two Turkish police officers were wounded in the incident.

stories.title: One attacker dead, two injured in gunfight outside Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: One attacker was killed and two were injured in a gunfight outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. Two police officers were also injured, and a source confirmed no Israeli diplomat was present in the city at the time.

stories.title: Afghanistan brands China peace talks with Pakistan ‘useful’
stories.summary: Afghanistan's foreign minister described China-brokered peace talks with Pakistan as 'useful.' Kabul expressed hope that minor disagreements over interpretation would not hinder progress in the negotiations.

stories.title: Why is Ukraine attacking Russian refineries amid a global oil crisis?
stories.summary: Ukraine has been targeting Russian oil refineries amid a global energy crisis following the US attack on Iran. The strikes intensified after the US temporarily waived sanctions on Russian oil in March, raising Ukrainian concerns about Russian economic gains.

stories.title: Trump warns a 'whole civilization will die tonight' if a deal with Iran isn't reached
stories.summary: President Trump warned that a 'whole civilization will die tonight' if Iran failed to meet his deadline, which included reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responded by urging young people to form human chains around power plants and other potential targets.

stories.title: Europe's future on the ballot? Hungary's Orban in tight re-election race
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance campaigned in Budapest for far-right Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who trails in polls ahead of Sunday's general election. European observers noted the unusual intervention by the United States in a European election, using rhetoric aligned with Russia's talking points.

stories.title: Republicans silent as Democrats call on US cabinet to oust Trump over Iran
stories.summary: US House Democrats called for the invocation of the 25th Amendment to remove President Trump from office over his threats against Iran, which they characterized as threats to commit war crimes. Congressional Republicans remained largely silent on the matter.

stories.title: Stork warning: woman gives birth midair on Jamaica-to-New York flight
stories.summary: A woman gave birth during a Caribbean Airlines flight from Kingston, Jamaica, to New York's JFK airport on Saturday. The newborn's nationality is yet to be determined.

stories.title: American journalist released a week after being kidnapped in Iraq
stories.summary: US journalist Shelly Kittleson was released approximately one week after being kidnapped from a Baghdad street. She had been held by the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah, which stated she must leave Iraq.

stories.title: Israel refrains from striking Lebanese-Syrian border crossing after mediation efforts, source says
stories.summary: The Israeli military refrained from striking a key border crossing between Syria and Lebanon after both countries pressed the United States on the need to keep it open. A Lebanese source familiar with the matter disclosed the development on Tuesday.

stories.title: Starmer urged to limit US access to UK bases after ‘dangerous’ Trump threats
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced pressure from Liberal Democrats, Greens, and some Labour MPs to limit US access to British airbases after Trump's threats against Iran. Downing Street has allowed US forces to use UK bases only for defensive missions, ruling out involvement in strikes on civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: UK blocks rapper Kanye West from entry over anti-Semitism and Nazi support
stories.summary: The United Kingdom barred American rapper Kanye West from entering the country over past anti-Semitic remarks and expressions of support for Nazism. British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said it was concerning that London's Wireless Festival had booked West.

stories.title: The Iran War’s Widening Impacts in the Middle East and North Africa
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is generating ripple effects across the Middle East and North Africa, with Gulf Arab states, Iraq, and Jordan suffering direct attacks from Iran. Israel has intensified bombing in Lebanon and expanded its ground invasion in the south in response to Hezbollah attacks, while broader regional impacts continue to spread.

stories.title: The Iran War’s Widening Impacts in the Middle East and North Africa
stories.summary: The war with Iran has produced ripple effects across the Middle East and North Africa, with Gulf Arab states, Iraq, and Jordan suffering direct attacks. Israel has intensively bombed parts of Lebanon and expanded its ground invasion in the south in response to Hezbollah attacks.

stories.title: Why Trump's latest Iran threats could constitute war crimes
stories.summary: Legal analysts argued that President Trump's threats to destroy Iran's civilian infrastructure could constitute war crimes under international law. The threats raised legal risks for US military personnel and heightened humanitarian concerns.

stories.title: UAE in 'deep regret' over UN Security Council failure to pass Hormuz resolution
stories.summary: The UAE expressed "deep regret" after the UN Security Council failed to pass a resolution on ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The UAE called for an international framework to counter Iran's threats to global commerce.

stories.title: Russia’s internet regulator blames Rostelecom network fault for widespread outages
stories.summary: Russia's internet regulator Roskomnadzor attributed widespread outages affecting banks, telecom operators, and other online services on the evening of April 6 to a fault on Rostelecom's backbone network, as reported by the St. Petersburg outlet Fontanka.

stories.title: Airline pilots must be given final say on flying in war zones, aviators’ group says
stories.summary: An international aviators' group called for airline pilots to be given the final decision on whether to fly through active conflict zones. The group also urged airlines to recognize the mental and emotional strain that conflict zone operations place on flight crews.

stories.title: Ukrainian parliament passes law extending military levy for three years after martial law
stories.summary: Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada passed a law extending the military levy for three years beyond the end of martial law. The government bill was adopted at both first reading and in full.

stories.title: Lebanon vs Hezbollah: A standoff between state sovereignty and Iranian influence - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that despite being significantly weakened by Israeli military and covert operations, Hezbollah remains too powerful for the Lebanese government to control. The group's ties to Iran continue to challenge Lebanon's state sovereignty.

stories.title: Far-right settlers track assaults on Palestinians in West Bank
stories.summary: A far-right Israeli settler group has been documenting attacks on Palestinian communities in the occupied West Bank. The group's records include names of villages targeted, mosques burned, and properties damaged.

stories.title: Will Trump prosecute Israeli reporter over Iran rescue leak?
stories.summary: President Trump threatened legal action over a leak related to an Iran rescue operation. Attention has focused on an Israeli journalist reportedly close to Prime Minister Netanyahu as a possible source of the disclosed information.

stories.title: Army operations center is trying to solve battlefield data problems in real time
stories.summary: The US Army has established a 180-day task force operating as an operations center to test solutions for battlefield data-sharing problems in real time.

stories.title: Petrol pump owners, dealers demand increase in commission proportionate to recent price hikes
stories.summary: Pakistani petrol pump owners' and dealers' associations demanded an increase in commission proportionate to recent fuel price hikes, warning they would shut down outlets nationwide if margins were not raised to eight percent of the invoice price from the current fixed Rs8 per litre.

stories.title: Iran calls on young people to form human chains around power plants as Trump deadline looms
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said 14 million people declared readiness to defend the country as officials called on young people to form human chains around power plants. The mobilization came as Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached.

stories.title: Charity cleared after false claims online over migrant welcome project
stories.summary: UK charity City of Sanctuary was cleared of wrongdoing after a watchdog found that viral online allegations about its migrant welcome project in schools were misleading and false. The claims had subjected the organization to widespread social media attacks.

stories.title: US journalist Shelly Kittleson to be released after kidnap in Iraq, militia says
stories.summary: The Iran-linked Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah announced the release of kidnapped US journalist Shelly Kittleson, stipulating that she must leave Iraq immediately as a condition of her freedom.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Leopard took 52 hits and kept going. This is armor upgrade that made it possible
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Leopard tank survived 52 hits in combat thanks to extensive armor upgrades. The modifications reportedly transformed the vehicle into something closer to a fortified position than a standard tank.

stories.title: How Israel's death penalty law codifies killing under apartheid
stories.summary: Israel's death penalty law has drawn criticism for what observers describe as discriminatory application and arbitrary enforcement targeting Palestinians under occupation.

stories.title: Karachi Kings captain David Warner charged with drink-driving in Sydney: reports
stories.summary: Former Australian cricketer and Karachi Kings captain David Warner was charged with mid-range drink-driving after being pulled over in Sydney. The 39-year-old allegedly returned a positive breath test after stopping short of a random testing site.

stories.title: Trump: “Whole civilization will die tonight” if Iran refuses deal
stories.summary: US President Trump warned that 'an entire civilization will perish' tonight if Iran refuses a deal, calling the moment one of the most important in world history.

stories.title: Two children among seven dead in fresh Ukraine, Russia strikes
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged deadly long-range drone and missile strikes that killed seven people, including two children. Both sides have escalated such attacks in recent months.

stories.title: Iran deploys Legos and social media trolling in war for public opinion
stories.summary: Iranian embassies have turned to social media humor and props, including Legos, to counter U.S. threats over the Strait of Hormuz. One embassy joked that Tehran 'lost the keys' to the strait, while another quoted Mark Twain to mock President Trump.

stories.title: Russia confirms deaths of 16 Cameroonians fighting in Ukraine war, Yaounde says
stories.summary: Cameroon announced that Russian authorities confirmed the deaths of 16 Cameroonian nationals who had been fighting on Russia's side against Ukraine. This marks the first time Cameroon's government has publicly addressed the involvement of its citizens in the war.

stories.title: Ben-Gvir tours Temple Mount, urges expanded access for worshippers amid Iran war restrictions
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir visited the Temple Mount and called for expanded access for worshippers during wartime restrictions. He also criticized the Israeli High Court's approval of larger protests.

stories.title: Kataib Hezbollah say they will release abducted US journalist
stories.summary: Kataib Hezbollah, an Iraqi armed group, announced plans to release an abducted American journalist. Iraqi sources indicated the journalist, Kittleson, was taken to a location south of Baghdad reportedly to deter US airstrikes on the group's stronghold.

stories.title: Why JD Vance joined Pakistan’s last-ditch US-Iran mediation efforts
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance joined backchannel mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as an intermediary. Iran is reportedly seeking indirect diplomatic engagement through the vice president.

stories.title: Iran war: Russia and China veto UN resolution to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Russia and China vetoed a UN Security Council resolution to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with 11 votes in favor and abstentions from Pakistan and Colombia. The vote occurred hours after President Trump threatened that a "whole civilization will die tonight" if Iran does not comply with his 8pm deadline.

stories.title: Russian drones strike snack manufacturer’s warehouse in Pavlohrad overnight
stories.summary: Russian drones struck a warehouse complex belonging to the international Star Brands snack manufacturer in Pavlohrad, Dnipropetrovsk region, during an overnight attack on April 7.

stories.title: Iran war: Which countries are allowed through Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Iran has designated a set of 'friendly countries' permitted to send vessels through the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing war, a blockade, and escalating threats over the critical waterway.

stories.title: UK veterans ‘forced to resign’ for being gay launch legal action against MoD
stories.summary: Two UK veterans, Steven Stewart and Mark Shephard, launched legal action against the Ministry of Defence over the LGBT Financial Recognition Scheme. Both were effectively forced to resign from the military due to their sexuality and argue the compensation scheme is "structurally unfair."

stories.title: Two firms picked as finalists for contract to outsource Army pilot training
stories.summary: Two companies have been selected as finalists for a contract to outsource US Army pilot training. The contract award is still planned for September despite concerns raised by lawmakers.

stories.title: WHO halts Gaza medical evacuations after worker killed
stories.summary: The WHO announced it is halting medical evacuations from Gaza until further notice after one of its workers was killed. The organization said the incident is under investigation.

stories.title: Mediation efforts halt Israeli strike on Lebanon-Syria crossing
stories.summary: The Israeli military halted a planned strike on a key border crossing between Syria and Lebanon after both countries urged the United States to keep the crossing open. Mediation efforts led to the decision to refrain from the attack.

stories.title: Bell, M1 advance to final phase of Army’s Flight School Next competition
stories.summary: Bell and an M1 Abrams-related competitor have advanced to the final phase of the U.S. Army's Flight School Next competition. Army technical evaluation team members will fly each aircraft to verify they meet the Aviation Center of Excellence's standards.

stories.title: Israeli military issues warning for vessels in a maritime area in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued a warning to all vessels in the maritime area between Tyre and Ras Naqoura off the Lebanese coast. Ships were ordered to immediately sail north of Tyre, signaling a likely imminent military operation.

stories.title: After fleeing past Hezbollah fighting, some Israelis on northern border vow to stay
stories.summary: Some Israeli residents along the northern border who fled Hezbollah rocket attacks starting in October 2023 have returned to their homes despite ongoing fighting. Residents described returning as soon as basic utilities were restored.

stories.title: Pakistan's efforts to end West Asia war approaching ‘critical’ stage: Iran's envoy
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, said Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to help end the West Asia conflict are reaching a critical stage. He stated that Iran prioritizes diplomacy but insists any negotiated outcome must ensure a permanent resolution.

stories.title: Iran judiciary urges courts to 'speed up' execution verdicts
stories.summary: Iran's judiciary has directed courts to accelerate execution verdicts. Human rights organizations have warned of a surge in hangings of political prisoners, which they link to the ongoing US-Israeli war.

stories.title: UN Security Council fails to approve resolution on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The UN Security Council failed to approve a Bahraini-drafted resolution on protecting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. China and Russia vetoed the measure, which received 11 votes in favor out of the 15-member council.

stories.title: Why Energy Has Become a Foreign-Policy Weapon
stories.summary: Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has highlighted the growing use of energy infrastructure as a tool of leverage in great-power competition. The move underscores how critical waterways can be weaponized in geopolitical conflicts.

stories.title: Top university says US-Israel attack targeted Iran’s progress, AI learning
stories.summary: A top Iranian university accused the United States and Israel of targeting Iran's academic institutions and AI research capabilities in recent strikes. Iran condemned what it called systematic attacks on civilian sites, including academic hubs, as critical infrastructure sustained heavy damage.

stories.title: US denies nuclear plan as deadline on threat to Iran ‘civilisation’ looms
stories.summary: The White House denied that the United States is considering the use of nuclear weapons against Iran. The denial came amid rising fears prompted by comments from President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance regarding the conflict with Tehran.

stories.title: Artemis crew snap historic Earthset photo and call space station on way home
stories.summary: The Artemis II astronauts captured a historic "Earthset" photograph showing Earth dropping below the lunar horizon during their return journey. The crew also communicated with the International Space Station. The image was a deliberate homage to the iconic Earthrise photo taken during the Apollo 8 mission in 1968.

stories.title: UK government urged to act over proposed illegal Israeli settlement
stories.summary: A group of 32 former UK ambassadors and high commissioners urged the British government to act against the proposed E1 Israeli settlement in the West Bank. They said the planned 3,400-home settlement would divide the West Bank and destroy Palestinian viability, calling on ministers to threaten action against companies bidding for the project.

stories.title: Russian oil prices hit 13-year high amid Strait of Hormuz closure
stories.summary: Russian Urals crude loaded at the Baltic port of Primorsk reached $116.05 per barrel on April 2, its highest price since 2013, according to Bloomberg citing Argus Media data. The spike comes amid the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Houthis hold Gulf states from joining US attacks with Bab el-Mandeb Strait trump card - interview
stories.summary: Analysts suggest the Houthis' threat to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait may be deterring Gulf states from joining US military operations against Iran. Yemen expert Inbal Nissim-Louvton discussed the strategic implications.

stories.title: Ukraine’s RBS 15 anti-ship missile reportedly made its combat debut — and it flies 2 meters above water
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Navy released footage of an RBS 15, a Swedish-made anti-ship cruise missile, being launched from a mobile ground platform against Russian targets. The strike reportedly marks the weapon's combat debut in the conflict.

stories.title: Russians attack bus in Nikopol district again, injuries reported
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked a passenger bus in Ukraine's Nikopol district for the second time in one day, injuring five people.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Israel shifting ‘balance of power’ with Iran strikes
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel is shifting the balance of power through intensified strikes on Iran. Netanyahu characterized the military campaign as a broader strategic effort against Iranian targets.

stories.title: Iran-backed Iraqi armed group release kidnapped US journalist
stories.summary: An Iran-backed Iraqi armed group released an American journalist who had been kidnapped in Baghdad the previous week. The group agreed to free the journalist as a goodwill gesture toward Iraq's outgoing prime minister, according to an Iraqi official.

stories.title: ‘Dangerous escalation’: Pakistan condemns Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia’s energy facilities
stories.summary: Pakistan condemned Iranian missile and drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's energy facilities in the Eastern Region, calling the attacks a dangerous escalation that undermines regional peace and stability.

stories.title: In glitzy interwar Warsaw, truth meets fiction as 2 young women hunt for missing mentor
stories.summary: Author Judy Batalion's novel "The Last Woman of Warsaw," released April 7, is set in interwar Warsaw and follows two young women searching for their missing mentor. The book highlights the Jewish diversity of cosmopolitan Warsaw through a blend of historical truth and fiction.

stories.title: Drones from Iraq targeted area near US base in northeast Syria
stories.summary: An overnight drone attack originating from Iraq targeted an area in northeast Syria near a base hosting US forces, according to a military source. No further details on casualties or damage were immediately provided.

stories.title: Gunman killed, 2 wounded in shootout outside Israel’s Istanbul consulate
stories.summary: A gunman was killed and two others wounded in a shootout with police outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. Turkish Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci said the assailants traveled from Izmit and one was affiliated with an unspecified organization. Two police officers were lightly injured.

stories.title: Gunmen attack building housing Israeli Consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked the building housing the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. Turkish officials noted that no Israeli diplomats were present, as Israel had previously withdrawn its diplomatic staff from missions in Turkey amid security concerns and deteriorating bilateral relations.

stories.title: First Nation asks court to block Alberta referendum on seceding from Canada
stories.summary: The Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation in Alberta filed a court challenge to block a proposed referendum on the province's secession from Canada. The First Nation argued the separatist push would violate their treaty rights and called it "consummately irresponsible."

stories.title: Can Starmer maintain ‘defensive strikes’ stance as Trump escalates threats on Iran?
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces growing pressure to maintain his stance that U.S. use of UK bases is limited to "defensive" strikes on Iranian military targets. President Trump's threats to bomb civilian infrastructure in Iran are straining the UK's distinction between defensive and offensive operations.

stories.title: Why is the West pretending Iran is winning the war against Israel, the US? - opinion
stories.summary: Western analysts' assessments of the Iran-US-Israel war have been questioned by commentators who argue that Iran's military situation has deteriorated significantly despite narratives suggesting otherwise.

stories.title: Situation on Kharg Island 'under control' following US strikes: Report
stories.summary: Iran's Mehr News Agency reported that the situation on Kharg Island is under control following US strikes, with no damage found to oil infrastructure. The United States said it targeted military installations on the island, which is a key Iranian oil export hub.

stories.title: Ukraine keeps hitting same Russian oil terminal — and it’s getting worse every night
stories.summary: Ukraine has been conducting repeated strikes against a Russian oil terminal in the Baltic region. The systematic attacks are reportedly causing escalating damage to a key Russian oil export facility.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank to support Pakistan’s solar transition, power sector reforms
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank is expected to provide financial and technical support for Pakistan's transition to solar power with battery energy storage systems. ADB officials discussed integrated planning, digitization, and data governance in Pakistan's power sector during meetings in Islamabad.

stories.title: Russia confirms 16 Cameroonian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
stories.summary: Russia confirmed that 16 Cameroonian soldiers were killed while fighting in the war in Ukraine. No details were provided about how the Cameroonian nationals came to be serving with Russian forces.

stories.title: French nationals released from Iran, returning to France, Macron says
stories.summary: French President Macron announced that French nationals Cecile Kohler and Jacques Paris have been released from Iran and are returning to France. They had been held in Iran's Evin Prison for over three years before an initial release in November 2025.

stories.title: ‘Admission Is Now a One-Way Ticket’: Kremlin Escalates Crackdown on Western Universities
stories.summary: The Kremlin is intensifying pressure on Russian students enrolled at foreign universities designated as "undesirable" organizations by Moscow. Thousands of Russian students currently attend such institutions abroad.

stories.title: Fire erupts near industrial site in Saudi Arabia after Iranian strikes
stories.summary: A suspected Iranian missile strike sparked a large fire near an industrial complex in Saudi Arabia. Details about the extent of damage to the industrial site were not immediately available.

stories.title: ‘No impact’ of Middle East conflict on remittances from Gulf countries so far: finance minister
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told the National Assembly that remittances from Gulf Cooperation Council countries have not yet been affected by the Middle East conflict. He noted that 40 to 50 percent of Pakistan's remittances originate from GCC nations.

stories.title: Iran's Kuwait ambassador urges Gulf to work on averting 'tragedy'
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Kuwait called on Gulf states to work together to avert a 'tragedy' as a deadline set by US President Trump for Iran approached on Tuesday evening.

stories.title: Ukraine: Several killed as Russia strikes bus, other targets
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia and Russian-occupied territories killed at least five people, including a 12-year-old boy. Separately, Russian strikes hit a bus and other targets in Ukraine, killing several people. Ukraine has been pushing for a ceasefire during Orthodox Easter.

stories.title: Why Viktor Orban wants energy prices at the heart of Hungary’s elections
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has centered his campaign for Sunday's parliamentary elections on cheap energy and opposition to EU support for Ukraine. An alleged plot to sabotage a Russian gas pipeline into Hungary—dismissed by opponents as a "false flag"—may boost his campaign.

stories.title: Russia revises launch timeline for Luna-28, Luna-29, and Luna-30 spacecraft
stories.summary: Russia has revised the launch schedule for its Luna-28, Luna-29, and Luna-30 lunar spacecraft, according to the business daily Kommersant, citing a presentation by Russian Academy of Sciences Vice President Sergei Chernyshev.

stories.title: Israeli military asks people in Iran to refrain from using trains; railway movement stopped in Masshad
stories.summary: The Israeli military posted a warning on its Persian-language X account urging people in Iran to avoid using trains. Railway services were subsequently halted in the Iranian city of Mashhad.

stories.title: White House denies it is considering using nuclear weapons in Iran
stories.summary: The White House denied it is considering using nuclear weapons against Iran amid the ongoing conflict. The denial followed comments by Vice President JD Vance that many interpreted as hinting at potential nuclear weapon use.

stories.title: Ukraine unleashes machine gun-toting drones into the Black Sea
stories.summary: Ukraine has deployed machine gun-equipped drones in the Black Sea, according to both Ukrainian and Russian sources. The adaptation represents a new use of drone technology in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns storming of Al Aqsa Mosque by Israeli occupation forces
stories.summary: Pakistan strongly condemned the storming of the Al Aqsa Mosque compound in East Jerusalem by Israeli forces. The condemnation followed far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's entry into the mosque's courtyards.

stories.title: Train driver killed, two critically injured as French TGV collides with truck
stories.summary: A TGV high-speed train collided with a truck at a level crossing between Bethune and Lens in the Pas-de-Calais region of northern France. The train driver was killed and two people were critically injured in the accident.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes hit Iran's Kharg island: media
stories.summary: US and Israeli forces struck Iran's Kharg Island, the country's primary oil export terminal. The strikes came as President Trump intensified threats against Iran.

stories.title: Details of the $1.5 trillion defense budget request, and a key lawmaker’s take on the F-35
stories.summary: The U.S. administration submitted a $1.5 trillion defense budget request. The proposal and a key lawmaker's assessment of the F-35 program were featured on the defense podcast The Break Out.

stories.title: Trump Is Attacking Iranians, Not Just Iran
stories.summary: U.S. strikes on Iranian infrastructure are reportedly causing significant harm to ordinary Iranian civilians. The destruction of key infrastructure has raised concerns about the humanitarian toll on the broader population beyond military targets.

stories.title: Artemis II crew takes historic photo of Earth setting behind moon
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew captured a photograph of Earth setting behind the Moon, evoking Apollo 8's iconic 1968 "Earthrise" image. The White House described the photo as "Humanity, from the other side."

stories.title: ‘We still deserve due process,’ says Cambodian man deported by US to Eswatini
stories.summary: Pheap Rom, a Cambodian man deported by the United States, said he was sent to prison in Eswatini despite having completed his U.S. sentence. He was among 15 deportees sent to the African kingdom, and said he would have accepted deportation to Cambodia instead.

stories.title: Iran attacked Saudi Arabia's Jubail petrochemical complex, IRGC says
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it attacked Saudi Arabia's Jubail petrochemical complex. The strike followed President Trump's ultimatum demanding Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday night.

stories.title: Africa: Afreximbank to Avail U.S.$10 Billion Under Its Gulf Crisis Response Programme
stories.summary: The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) approved a US$10 billion Gulf Crisis Response Programme to shield African and Caribbean economies from the economic shocks caused by the escalating conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Africa: Afreximbank Dominates the 2026 IFLR Africa Awards With a Triple Win, Retaining Key Awards
stories.summary: The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) won three categories at the 2026 IFLR Africa Awards, which recognize innovative cross-border financial transactions and the institutions driving them across the continent.

stories.title: Pro-Iran hackers have disrupted some industrial-control systems, US says
stories.summary: US cyber and intelligence agencies reported that pro-Iran hackers have disrupted some industrial control systems in the United States. The hackers targeted federal and local governments, water systems, and energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Death toll from strikes on Kherson rises to four
stories.summary: The death toll from Russian strikes on the Korabelny district of Kherson, Ukraine, has risen to four.

stories.title: Current oil and gas crisis worse than 1973, 1979, 2002 put together: IEA chief
stories.summary: International Energy Agency chief said the current oil and gas crisis is worse than those of 1973, 1979, and 2002 combined. He warned that developing nations face the greatest risk from higher energy prices.

stories.title: From first intercept to 10,000 combat intercepts: Iron Dome turns 15-analysis
stories.summary: Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system has reached its 15th anniversary, having completed over 10,000 combat intercepts since its first operational use. The system is widely credited with reshaping Israel's national security doctrine.

stories.title: Three gunmen open fire on police outside Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Three gunmen opened fire on police outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, Turkey. Turkish officers shot and killed one assailant; two policemen and two attackers were wounded, according to Turkish officials.

stories.title: Shootout outside Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: A gunman was killed and two other assailants were wounded in a shootout with police outside the Israeli consulate building in Istanbul on April 7. Two police officers sustained light injuries. The intended target of the attack was not immediately confirmed.

stories.title: Chechen Court Declares Separatist Group in Exile ‘Terrorist’ Organization
stories.summary: A court in Chechnya has designated the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, an unrecognized separatist state that existed de facto from 1991 to 2000, as a terrorist organization.

stories.title: West Asia conflict: Why has Iran called for ‘human chains’ to counter U.S.?
stories.summary: Iran has called for the formation of civilian human chains as a defensive measure against potential U.S. strikes. The move follows U.S. President Donald Trump's threat to target Iranian infrastructure, including bridges and power plants, if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened.

stories.title: Iran’s other would-be WMD program lies in ruins following strikes by Israel and the US
stories.summary: Joint strikes by Israel and the United States have destroyed facilities linked to Iran's non-nuclear weapons of mass destruction program. Former CIA Iran analyst Jim Lamson noted the WMD sites appeared to be a lower priority for coalition war planners compared to other targets.

stories.title: Iran war jeopardises US global leadership, warns Italian minister
stories.summary: Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto warned that the U.S. war on Iran jeopardizes American global leadership. Crosetto expressed concern about the potential for nuclear escalation, calling it "madness."

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon's bridges, threatens key border crossing
stories.summary: Israel intensified strikes across Lebanon, targeting bridges and residential areas. Israeli forces also threatened the Al-Masnaa border crossing, a key link between Lebanon and Syria.

stories.title: Human skull discovered during Easter egg hunt near Los Angeles
stories.summary: A human skull was discovered during an Easter egg hunt at DeForest Park in Long Beach, California, on Sunday. Authorities launched an investigation after a family found the remains at approximately 5 p.m.

stories.title: JD Vance accuses EU of ‘interference’ as he visits Hungary to help Orbán win election
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance traveled to Budapest to support Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ahead of Sunday's parliamentary elections. Vance accused the European Union of "blatantly interfering" in Hungary's vote, calling it one of the worst examples of foreign election interference.

stories.title: White House denies it is considering using nuclear weapons in Iran
stories.summary: The White House denied that the United States is considering using nuclear weapons against Iran. The denial followed days of escalatory rhetoric from President Trump, including a claim that 'a whole civilization will die' if Iran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russia confirms deaths of 16 Cameroonians fighting in Ukraine war
stories.summary: Russia has confirmed the deaths of 16 Cameroonian nationals who were fighting on its side in the war in Ukraine. Cameroon's diplomatic note did not specify how the men came to be enlisted or provide details on when, where, or how they died.

stories.title: At least 30 Indian fishermen repatriated from Sri Lanka return home
stories.summary: At least 30 Indian fishermen detained in Sri Lanka have been repatriated and returned home to India. The treatment and detention of fishermen remains a longstanding point of contention in India-Sri Lanka bilateral relations.

stories.title: US strikes Kharg Island military targets, American official confirms to 'Post'
stories.summary: US forces struck military targets on Iran's Kharg Island, including air defense systems, a US official confirmed. Kharg Island is a critical hub for Iran's oil exports.

stories.title: IDF says it has ‘completed deployment’ to anti-tank defensive line in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announced the completed deployment of an anti-tank defensive line in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah rocket fire wounded two people in northern Israel, while the IDF reportedly delayed strikes on a Lebanon-Syria border crossing following US intervention. The elite 98th Division was mobilized to the area.

stories.title: Report: Russian marketplaces begin blocking users who connect via VPN
stories.summary: Russian online marketplaces Wildberries and Ozon, along with grocery retailer VkusVill, have begun restricting access for users connecting through popular VPN services, according to the newspaper Izvestia.

stories.title: Aftermath of a rescue: wreckage of aircraft at site of US mission in Iran
stories.summary: Wreckage of two U.S. C-130 planes and two helicopters was found at a site near Shahreza in Iran's Isfahan province following a U.S. rescue mission. Personnel cleared the desert site near the farming community of Parzan, which had previously been largely spared from the U.S.-Israeli conflict.

stories.title: Russian forces destroy 1830s Dontsi-Zakharzhevski estate in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces destroyed the Dontsi-Zakharzhevski estate, an architectural landmark dating to the 1830s, in Ukraine's Kharkiv region. The historic site was hit directly, causing a fire that led to its destruction.

stories.title: Chinese construction workers in Israel: 'I’d rather be bombed than live in poverty'
stories.summary: Chinese construction workers in Israel are choosing to remain on job sites despite ongoing airstrikes and conflict. Many cite higher wages as the primary reason for staying rather than evacuating.

stories.title: Israeli forces beat elderly Palestinian woman to death
stories.summary: Israeli forces reportedly beat 68-year-old Palestinian woman Sabriya Shamasneh to death during a raid on her home near Qalqiya in the occupied West Bank on April 7, 2026. Soldiers allegedly struck her with their rifles.

stories.title: Russian airline drew almost no tourists on subsidized Moscow-Pyongyang route
stories.summary: Russian airline Nordwind, which received approval in July 2025 to operate direct flights between Moscow and Pyongyang, has failed to attract tourists on the subsidized route, the business daily Kommersant reports.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran: ‘A whole civilisation will die tonight’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump warned Iran that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The threat came as a deadline set by Trump for Iran's compliance approached.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills at least 10 near Gaza school as ceasefire strains
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed at least 10 people and wounded others outside a school sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza on Monday. The strike came after clashes between Palestinians and an Israeli-backed militia at the school, further straining the fragile U.S.-backed ceasefire.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Will deal be struck before Trump's deadline?
stories.summary: President Trump warned that "a whole civilization will die" in Iran if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his midnight deadline. Vice President Vance stated the U.S. has unused tools against Iran without providing specifics. Prospects for a deal remained uncertain.

stories.title: Lebanon health ministry says 1,530 killed since 2 March
stories.summary: Lebanon's Ministry of Health reported that Israeli strikes have killed 1,530 people in Lebanon since March 2, including 102 women, 130 children, and 57 medical personnel. An additional 4,812 people have been wounded during the same period.

stories.title: Trump says Iran’s ‘whole civilization’ will die tonight as Iran stops direct talks with US
stories.summary: Iran officially severed all direct communications with the United States following President Trump's threat. It remained unclear whether the two nations would resume direct talks before Trump's 8 p.m. EST deadline on Tuesday.

stories.title: US hits military targets on Iran’s Kharg Island
stories.summary: The United States carried out strikes against military targets on Iran's Kharg Island, a key oil export hub. Vice President JD Vance stated the operation did not represent a shift in overall U.S. strategy toward Iran.

stories.title: With his 'Stone Age' threat to Iran, Trump has unleashed a new age of savagery
stories.summary: An opinion article characterized President Trump's threat to bomb Iran "back to the Stone Age" as an escalation of rhetorical savagery. The piece criticized Trump's approach to the Iran conflict as historically illiterate.

stories.title: Iran will plunge Middle East into 'darkness' if Trump escalates war
stories.summary: A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran is prepared to plunge the Middle East into darkness if the US escalates its military campaign. Iran stated it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for "empty promises" and warned of retaliation against regional energy infrastructure.

stories.title: ‘A whole civilization will die tonight,’ Trump says as Iran defies deal
stories.summary: President Trump issued a stark warning as Iran refused to comply with a proposed deal, stating that "a whole civilization will die tonight." A former U.S. State Department legal advisor said the remarks could plausibly be interpreted as a threat to commit genocide.

stories.title: Italian energy giant ENI announces gas discovery off Egypt coast
stories.summary: Italian energy company ENI announced a gas discovery off the coast of Egypt. The find comes as Egypt faces energy supply challenges linked to the ongoing US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine’s robot army is exploding in size: from 67 units to 167 in four months
stories.summary: Ukraine's fleet of frontline military robots grew from 67 to 167 units over four months. The robotic units completed approximately 9,000 missions in a single month.

stories.title: Preventing an Iranian Bomb Is Only Getting Harder
stories.summary: Analysts warn that Iran's nuclear program is becoming harder to contain as the regime grows more isolated, suspicious, and less cautious under evolving leadership. Iran's leverage over the Strait of Hormuz further complicates diplomatic efforts to prevent nuclear weapons development.

stories.title: Democrats outraged at Trump’s Iran post: ‘A threat to commit a war crime’
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers condemned President Trump's Truth Social post threatening to annihilate Iranian civilization if Tehran ignored his deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Critics called the statement "a threat to commit a war crime," noting it provided direct evidence of intent to violate international law.

stories.title: From 9pm shutdowns to remote work: Egypt cuts fuel amid power crisis
stories.summary: Egypt introduced energy conservation measures including 9 p.m. shutdowns and expanded remote work to cope with fuel shortages. The measures were linked to disruptions caused by the US-Israel military conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Bahamas police search for US woman who reportedly fell off boat
stories.summary: Bahamian police are searching for a US woman who reportedly fell from a dinghy on Saturday night. Her husband told authorities she was swept out to sea.

stories.title: Oil slick from bombed Iranian ship threatens protected wetland
stories.summary: An oil slick from the Iranian drone carrier Shahid Bagheri, struck by a U.S. warplane near the Strait of Hormuz, is threatening the Hara mangrove forest, a protected wetland home to migrating birds and endangered turtles. The spill poses risks to coastal communities in the Gulf.

stories.title: Student claiming RMIT is ‘complicit in genocide’ in social media post faces misconduct action
stories.summary: An RMIT University student in Australia faces potential suspension after posting a video on social media accusing the institution of being "complicit in genocide" in Gaza. The university said the video publicly identified the location of its defence and aerospace research centre, which is not normally published.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith is back in court, now as a defendant. His case reminds us that there are laws even amid war
stories.summary: Former Australian soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, a Victoria Cross recipient, is back in court as a defendant. His earlier defamation trial produced extensive public evidence of alleged war crimes, and the case highlights legal accountability for conduct during armed conflict.

stories.title: Saudi petrochemical complex hit after barrage targets country’s east
stories.summary: A Saudi petrochemical complex in the country's east was struck by a barrage of projectiles. The attack came hours after similar industrial installations in Iran were hit, indicating an escalation of tit-for-tat strikes in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine to have access to EU funds despite delay in final approval of loan, says Barrot
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot stated that the European Commission will work to ensure Ukraine has access to EU funds even if final approval of a planned loan is delayed beyond the end of April.

stories.title: Pentagon investigators blocked from using 'War Department' in official documents
stories.summary: The Pentagon's inspector general warned in an April 1 memo that investigators cannot use the term 'War Department' in official court filings. The designation may be used as a secondary name on letterhead but not in legal documents.

stories.title: Did US Military Strikes Impact Caribbean Drug Trafficking?
stories.summary: US military strikes in the Caribbean have disrupted certain drug trafficking routes, but traffickers have already adapted their operations. Venezuela remains a significant node in the cocaine trade despite the interventions.

stories.title: India’s nuclear leap: Why its fast breeder reactor success matters
stories.summary: India achieved a milestone with its fast breeder reactor, advancing toward reducing the country's dependence on imported uranium. The reactor represents India's most advanced nuclear energy technology to date.

stories.title: Italy set to sign off on Turkish TB3 drone order within months, says Baykar CEO
stories.summary: Baykar CEO announced that Italy is expected to finalize an order for Turkish-made TB3 drones within months. The deal would make Italy the first European country outside Turkey to operate the TB3 platform.

stories.title: Trump: ‘A whole civilization will die tonight’ if ultimatum for Iran to open Hormuz expires
stories.summary: President Trump warned Iran that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" as an 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached. The IRGC threatened to cut off oil and gas supplies to the US and its allies for a year, while Iranian President Pezeshkian said he and millions of Iranians were ready to sacrifice their lives.

stories.title: One gunman killed and two injured in shooting at Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: A gunman was killed and two others were wounded by Turkish police during a shooting near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. The consulate has been unstaffed for approximately two and a half years, with no Israeli diplomats present in Turkey.

stories.title: Russia has shifted to a year-round conscription system. Here’s what that means for the country’s young men.
stories.summary: Russia has transitioned from seasonal to year-round military conscription, replacing its traditional spring and autumn draft cycles. Restrictions on draft-eligible men are being imposed more frequently, enforcement is tightening, and the risk of deployment to combat zones remains significant.

stories.title: Doctors in England begin six-day strike after rejecting government’s pay and workforce deal
stories.summary: Junior doctors in England began a six-day strike after rejecting the government's pay and workforce deal. The British Medical Association has conducted several rounds of industrial action over pay since 2023.

stories.title: Armed attack on Israeli consulate in Istanbul leaves several injured
stories.summary: An armed attack targeted the Israeli consulate building in Istanbul. One attacker was killed and two others were wounded and neutralized by Turkish police. Two police officers sustained injuries in the incident.

stories.title: Vance openly supports Russia’s favorite European ally in Budapest, while accusing Ukraine in meddling Hungarian elections
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance traveled to Budapest to meet with Hungarian leadership, openly expressing support for Hungary, which critics describe as Russia's closest European ally. Vance also accused Ukraine of meddling in Hungarian elections.

stories.title: LHC grants post-arrest bail to Canadian scholar in cybercrime case
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court granted post-arrest bail to Canadian-Pakistani scholar Hamza Ahmad Khan, who was charged under Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act for allegedly making anti-state social media posts.

stories.title: Achakzai suggests formation of ‘national government’ to build political consensus
stories.summary: Pakistani opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai proposed forming a national government to build political consensus, speaking during a National Assembly debate on the Iran situation. He said the current coalition system had collapsed.

stories.title: Iran allows 2 French former detainees to leave country
stories.summary: France secured the release of two former detainees, Cecile Kohler and Jacques Paris, from Iran after three and a half years of detention. President Macron confirmed they departed Iranian territory from French diplomatic premises where they had been sheltered since their prison release.

stories.title: Suspect in space? Analysis finds 75 ‘unusual’ moves by Chinese satellites in nearly 10 years
stories.summary: A study by the Center for Strategic and International Studies identified 75 unusual maneuvers by Chinese satellites in geostationary orbit over nearly a decade. The analysis suggests the movements may indicate potential military and intelligence-related missions conducted by a small number of Chinese spacecraft.

stories.title: The War Will End With a Hormuz Toll Booth
stories.summary: Analysts suggest the conflict with Iran may conclude with Iran retaining some form of control over the Strait of Hormuz. The key challenge for diplomats will be negotiating terms that make Iranian oversight of the waterway acceptable to international shipping and regional actors.

stories.title: Trump agrees to suspend bombing of Iran for 2 weeks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the United States would pause its bombing campaign in Iran for two weeks, calling it a “double-sided ceasefire” requested by Pakistani mediators in a las

stories.title: US and Iran near brink of escalation as Trump deadline for deal looms
stories.summary: The United States and Iran neared a major escalation as President Trump's deadline for Tehran to accept a deal approached. Trump threatened to destroy Iran's civilization if it failed to comply by 8pm EST, while Pakistan intensified mediation efforts.

stories.title: Iranian-linked drone attack kills Kurdish couple in northern Iraq
stories.summary: An Iranian-linked drone strike killed a Kurdish couple in northern Iraq. Iranian-backed militias have launched more than 500 attacks on the Kurdistan region since late February.

stories.title: Gaza's Palestinians divided over Iran's region-wide ceasefire
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza are divided over Iran's proposed region-wide ceasefire. Reported conditions include ending wars in Gaza and Lebanon along with broader security and economic arrangements.

stories.title: South Sudan: South Sudan Speaker Summons MPs for Emergency Sitting Amid Threats of Her Removal
stories.summary: South Sudan's parliament speaker Jemma Nunu Kumba summoned all MPs and government ministers to an emergency sitting as political pressure mounted over efforts to remove her from office.

stories.title: 'US, Israeli citizens not welcome': Wave of antisemitic incidents hit Rio de Janeiro on Passover
stories.summary: A wave of antisemitic incidents occurred in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, during Passover, with reports of hostility directed at US and Israeli citizens. StandWithUs Brazil called for the legal adoption of the IHRA definition of antisemitism.

stories.title: Croatia finally landmine-free 30 years after war, but wounds remain
stories.summary: Croatia has been declared free of landmines 30 years after the wars that accompanied the disintegration of Yugoslavia. The United Nations had previously estimated that as much as one-fifth of Croatian territory was affected by mines.

stories.title: Uganda: Opposition Unveils Alternative Budget, Warns of 'Illusion' of Economic Growth
stories.summary: Uganda's parliamentary opposition released an alternative budget for the 2026/27 financial year, warning that the country's reported economic growth conceals deep fiscal strain and declining capacity to deliver public services.

stories.title: Erdogan condemns 'treacherous attack' in Istanbul
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the shooting near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul as a "treacherous attack." Erdogan vowed to continue fighting all forms of terrorism and to prevent provocations from undermining Turkey's security.

stories.title: South Africa: Dr Delay - Apartheid-Era Chemical Weapons Head Wouter Basson to Face Disciplinary Hearing
stories.summary: Dr. Wouter Basson, the former head of apartheid-era South Africa's secret chemical and biological warfare programme, will face a disciplinary hearing before the Health Professions Council of South Africa.

stories.title: Russia supplies Iran with satellite data on U.S. military bases in Middle East
stories.summary: Russia reportedly provided Iran with satellite imagery of military facilities and key sites across 11 Middle Eastern countries. The images were gathered during at least 24 Russian satellite reconnaissance missions conducted in the final ten days of March.

stories.title: Amid Iran war, 53 of Israel's future scientists showcase projects in Jerusalem contest
stories.summary: Fifty-three young Israeli scientists presented research projects at a competition in Jerusalem as part of National Science Week, continuing the 29th annual Young Scientists and Developers contest despite the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Sri Lanka introduces fuel subsidies for economic relief amid West Asia war
stories.summary: Sri Lankan President Dissanayake announced that Indian PM Modi agreed to supply petrol and diesel. Sri Lanka has also begun talks with Russia to obtain gas, coal, fuel, and fertilizer amid disruptions from the West Asia conflict.

stories.title: Heat, costs, shortages: US faces limits in deciding next actions in Iran - report
stories.summary: A J.P. Morgan paper estimated Iran could generate $70–90 billion annually if allowed to charge tolls in the Strait of Hormuz. Reports also noted the US faces logistical constraints including extreme heat and supply shortages in planning further military action against Iran.

stories.title: Mum of twins who says home was bombed in Lebanon speaks to BBC
stories.summary: A Lebanese mother of twins told the BBC her home was bombed during Israel's military operations in Lebanon. More than one million people in Lebanon have been displaced since Israel expanded its ground offensive in the country.

stories.title: Iran's Jewish community condemns US-Israeli attack on synagogue
stories.summary: Iran's Jewish community condemned the destruction of a synagogue in Tehran caused by US-Israeli strikes. The community spoke out as the strikes intensified and casualties continued to rise.

stories.title: Ukraine's attack drone fleet faces a mini jet engine supply crunch
stories.summary: European specialist manufacturers of mini jet engines are ramping up production and investment to address a looming supply shortage. The crunch threatens to slow Ukraine's deep-strike drone program at a critical stage of its war with Russia.

stories.title: Russia supplies Iran with cyber support, spy imagery to hone attacks, says Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine has accused Russia of providing Iran with cyber support and spy imagery to improve Iranian attack capabilities. European leaders reportedly raised the issue with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio during a G-7 meeting in March.

stories.title: Row over ‘virtual gated community’ AI surveillance plan in Toronto neighbourhood
stories.summary: Residents of Toronto's wealthy Rosedale neighbourhood are debating a proposal to install Flock AI-powered licence plate-scanning cameras to combat rising property crime. Critics have described the plan as creating a "virtual gated community." Break-ins in the area occur at more than double the city average.

stories.title: 1.1 million displaced in Lebanon as Israeli assault intensifies
stories.summary: More than 1.1 million people have been displaced in Lebanon as Israel expands its military operations. Hezbollah has continued its attacks amid the escalating Israeli assault.

stories.title: Iran President says 14 million Iranians, including himself, have volunteered to sacrifice their lives in war
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian claimed on social media that 14 million Iranians, including himself, have volunteered to sacrifice their lives. The statement came ahead of a U.S. deadline threatening strikes on Iranian infrastructure over the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader arrives in China on ‘journey of peace’
stories.summary: Taiwan opposition leader Cheng Li-wun arrived in China on April 7 at the invitation of President Xi Jinping, calling the visit a "journey of peace." The trip comes as Beijing continues its push for the self-ruled island to come under its control.

stories.title: France's Sarkozy says 'innocent' at trial over Libya funding
stories.summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy declared his innocence at an appeals trial on charges that he sought Libyan financing for his 2007 presidential campaign. Sarkozy is accused of receiving funds from Libya in exchange for helping improve Tripoli's international image.

stories.title: Carnival fever hits Lagos as locals celebrate Afro-Brazilian heritage
stories.summary: The centuries-old Fanti Carnival returned to Lagos, Nigeria, celebrating the city's Afro-Brazilian heritage with colorful festivities reflecting historical cultural ties between Nigeria and Brazil.

stories.title: ‘Paper tiger’: what’s behind Donald Trump’s renewed Greenland threat?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump renewed threats to take control of Greenland while escalating tensions with European allies. Trump derided NATO as a "paper tiger" and threatened to withdraw the U.S. from the transatlantic alliance. Analysts say the move deepens fractures between Washington and its European partners.

stories.title: The Orphan Pearl: How a blockade of Kharg Island could bring Iran to its knees - opinion
stories.summary: Analysts highlight Kharg Island's strategic importance as the hub handling virtually all of Iran's crude oil exports, noting that a blockade of the island could severely undermine Iran's economic stability.

stories.title: Qatar warns of 'uncontrollable escalation' in region amid war
stories.summary: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari called on all parties involved in the Iran war to find a resolution. He warned of an 'uncontrollable escalation' in the region.

stories.title: Fuel supply shortages hit one in five petrol stations in France
stories.summary: Fuel shortages affected nearly one in five petrol stations across France amid surging global oil prices. The French government attributed the situation to logistical strains and heavy demand at discounted outlets. Road blockades emerged as frustration grew among households and businesses.

stories.title: Is Israel redefining Jerusalem's religious status quo?
stories.summary: Israel has closed Muslim and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem amid the Iran war. The unprecedented restrictions have raised concerns about upending the city's longstanding religious status quo.

stories.title: Vietnam elects Communist Party chief To Lam as President, echoing China's power structure
stories.summary: Vietnam's National Assembly unanimously elected Communist Party chief To Lam as president for a five-year term, consolidating his control over both the party and the state in a structure echoing China's governance model.

stories.title: Trump: 'A whole civilisation will die tonight'
stories.summary: Airstrikes hit two bridges and a train station in Iran on Tuesday as President Trump warned "a whole civilisation will die tonight" if Tehran does not meet his deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials urged young people to form human chains to protect power plants.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly in ‘severe’ condition, unable to govern Iran
stories.summary: Reports citing a US-Israeli diplomatic memo indicate that Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in severe condition and unable to govern from Qom. The memo also suggests Tehran may be preparing to bury his father alongside others, possibly including Mojtaba himself.

stories.title: WHO suspends Gaza medical evacuations after contractor killed by Israeli troops
stories.summary: The World Health Organization suspended medical evacuations from Gaza after an Israeli military strike killed a contractor. The Israeli military stated its troops fired on a vehicle they believed posed an immediate threat.

stories.title: Trump on Iran: ‘A whole civilisation will die tonight’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump escalated threats against Iran, warning that "a whole civilisation will die tonight." Democratic lawmakers criticized Trump's rhetoric, calling his statements "sick" and "genocidal."

stories.title: Politico: U.S. expands list of targets in Iran to avoid war crimes charges
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly expanding its list of potential Iranian targets to include energy facilities that serve both civilian and military purposes. The move is aimed at reducing the risk of war crimes allegations in any future strikes.

stories.title: ECP dismisses MQM-P request for 2-month extension in intra-party elections case
stories.summary: Pakistan's Election Commission dismissed MQM-P's request for a two-month extension for party chairman Dr. Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui to appear in a case regarding the party's overdue intra-party elections.

stories.title: King Fahd Causeway, linking Saudi Arabia to Bahrain reopens after attack threats
stories.summary: The King Fahd Causeway connecting Saudi Arabia and Bahrain reopened after an hours-long closure prompted by an Iranian ballistic missile attack that targeted Saudi Arabia and may have damaged energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Tehran synagogue damaged by missile strike according to Iranian media reports
stories.summary: A missile strike damaged the Rafi Niya Synagogue near Palestine Square in central Tehran, according to Iranian media reports and footage circulated on social media.

stories.title: South Sudan President Salva Kiir fires parliament speaker and deputy
stories.summary: South Sudan's President Salva Kiir dismissed parliament speaker Jemma Nunu Kumba and her deputy. Kumba, a member of the ruling SPLM party, had served as speaker of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly since 2021.

stories.title: IDF admits Tehran synagogue was ‘collateral damage’ in strike on Iran commander
stories.summary: The Israeli military acknowledged that damage to Tehran's Rafi Niya synagogue was collateral from a strike targeting a senior Iranian commander. Video from the site showed rescuers recovering what appeared to be Hebrew scripture from the rubble.

stories.title: 1 attacker killed, two hurt in gun battle with police outside unstaffed Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: One attacker was killed and two brothers were wounded in a gun battle with Turkish police outside Israel's unstaffed consulate in Istanbul. The assailants traveled from Izmit, and authorities linked one to a terror group that "exploits religion," possibly alluding to ISIS.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘new, reasonable’ Iran is neither new nor reasonable, and he knows it
stories.summary: An analysis piece argued that President Trump's characterization of a "new, reasonable" Iran does not reflect reality while the regime retains power and its nuclear ambitions. The article also noted Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's perceived lack of empathy in the crisis.

stories.title: Noga Erez to play Coachella, despite haters, war and canceled flights
stories.summary: Israeli singer Noga Erez is set to perform at the Coachella festival despite the ongoing conflict and canceled flights. Erez and her partner, musician Ori Rousso, have been sharing updates from the road while awaiting the rest of their band.

stories.title: Fanti Carnvial in Lagos showcases cultural bridge between Nigeria and Brazil
stories.summary: The annual Fanti Carnival in Lagos, Nigeria, is one of West Africa's most prominent cultural festivals, blending Nigerian traditions with Brazilian and Cuban influences to showcase centuries-old Afro-Brazilian heritage.

stories.title: When Satellite Imagery Goes Dark: New Tool Shows Damage in Iran and the Gulf
stories.summary: Bellingcat has launched a new tool to track damage across Iran and the Gulf amid limited access to open-source imagery of the ongoing conflict. An Iranian internet blackout is severely restricting the flow of photos, videos, and digital communications from within the country.

stories.title: Chinese memory giants to gain market share via lower prices, expanded capacity: analysts
stories.summary: Chinese memory chipmakers are leveraging price advantages exceeding 15 percent and expanding production capacity to gain market share during an AI-driven global memory "super cycle." Analysts say Chinese manufacturers are particularly competitive in the price-sensitive general-purpose server and consumer markets.

stories.title: Sybiha: Russian disinformation is Moscow’s acknowledgment of Ukraine’s success in Gulf states
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha characterized Russian disinformation campaigns as evidence that Moscow recognizes Ukraine's growing diplomatic influence in the Gulf states. He said Russia's own efforts to undermine Ukraine's position in the region have failed.

stories.title: 'Free and on ​their ‌way ⁠to France': Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris released by Iran, says Macron
stories.summary: French President Macron announced that Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris were freed from Iranian detention and returning to France after three and a half years. The two French nationals had been imprisoned on espionage charges and were released in November.

stories.title: France warns US strikes on Iran infrastructure would break international law
stories.summary: France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot warned that US strikes on Iran's civilian infrastructure would violate international law. Speaking hours before Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Barrot cautioned such attacks would trigger dangerous escalation.

stories.title: Ringleader of suspected human trafficking network arrested in Ethiopia
stories.summary: Authorities in Ethiopia arrested Yetbarek Dawit, the alleged ringleader of a suspected human trafficking network. He is accused of operating a multi-million-dollar operation that used torture to extort money from victims.

stories.title: Trump tells Iran: 'A whole civilization will die tonight'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump escalated threats against Iran, stating "a whole civilisation will die tonight" in an effort to pressure Tehran into striking a deal. The remarks came as a US-imposed deadline on Iran approached.

stories.title: #MeToo movement brings wave of harassment claims across Colombia
stories.summary: A wave of sexual harassment allegations has emerged across Colombia following accounts by female journalists. Reporter Juanita Gómez described being forcibly kissed by a senior colleague while on assignment for Caracol television in 2015. The allegations have reached as far as the Colombian government.

stories.title: Australian and IPL cricket great David Warner charged with drink-driving
stories.summary: Former Australian and IPL cricketer David Warner, 39, was charged with drink-driving. Warner retired from international cricket in 2024 but continues to play in T20 franchise leagues.

stories.title: Turkish police shoot three gunmen in clash outside Israel's Istanbul consulate
stories.summary: Turkish police killed one gunman and severely wounded two others in a firefight outside Israel's consulate in Istanbul. The two surviving attackers are brothers who traveled from Izmit, and one is reportedly linked to a religiously motivated terror group.

stories.title: Doctors in England begin six-day strike after rejecting government's pay and workforce deal
stories.summary: Doctors in England began a six-day strike after rejecting the government's pay and workforce deal. The government subsequently withdrew a pledge to fund 1,000 additional specialty training posts that had been contingent on acceptance of the agreement.

stories.title: The Gulf’s Wartime Unity Is Unraveling
stories.summary: Gulf states are experiencing growing divisions over the ongoing conflict with Iran. Some members are pushing for military escalation, while others are advocating diplomatic restraint, fracturing the wartime consensus in the region.

stories.title: US lawmaker pushes to impeach Hegseth over Iran war
stories.summary: A US Democratic lawmaker has introduced an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, citing alleged war crimes and constitutional violations. The impeachment bid faces significant political obstacles.

stories.title: ‘Iranians reject idea that US will bring stability’
stories.summary: Iranian public sentiment reportedly rejects the notion that US military intervention will bring stability to the region. The sentiment reflects broader opposition within Iran to American involvement amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: China opens its flour market to Ukraine as Kazakh producers pay for using Russian wheat
stories.summary: China has opened its flour market to Ukrainian producers. In the same week, Beijing blocked Kazakh flour producers from using Russian wheat in their products.

stories.title: Iran reports US-Israeli strikes on bridges, highway and railway
stories.summary: Iran reported that US-Israeli strikes hit key bridges in Qom and Kashan and a highway connecting Tabriz to Tehran. The infrastructure strikes targeted critical transportation links amid ongoing military operations.

stories.title: Trump's deadline approaches, Russia caught with Iran
stories.summary: As President Trump's stated deadline for Iran approaches, Russia faces diplomatic complications due to its ties with Tehran. The situation is adding pressure to Moscow's balancing act between its Iranian relationship and broader geopolitical interests.

stories.title: Dozens killed as Angola flood death toll rises
stories.summary: The death toll from severe flooding in Angola continues to rise, with dozens killed. President Lourenço described recovery efforts as a "race against the clock" to locate those still affected.

stories.title: ING Terminates Sale of Russian Business
