stories.summary: Dutch bank ING canceled the planned sale of its Russian business unit after concluding there was no realistic prospect the buyer would obtain the necessary regulatory approvals.

stories.title: Russian forces strike residential area in Kherson: Three dead, five wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a residential area in Kherson's Korabelnyi district, killing three people and wounding five others.

stories.title: Israel targets railways and infrastructure, at least nine killed
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit a residential building in Shahriar, killing at least nine people and injuring 15, and struck the Yahya Abad railway bridge in Kashan, killing two. US President Donald Trump separately threatened to attack Iranian civilian infrastructure if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Turkey opposes Ukraine proposal to ship LNG through Bosphorus
stories.summary: Turkey rejected a Ukrainian proposal to ship liquefied natural gas through the Bosphorus strait, citing security risks. Ankara instead offered to supply gas to Ukraine through existing pipeline routes via Bulgaria and Romania.

stories.title: Shorebird from Australia spotted over 7,400 km away on island in Andamans: Expert
stories.summary: A tagged shorebird from Australia was spotted over 7,400 kilometers away on Narcondam Island in India's Andaman archipelago. An expert from the Bombay Natural History Society said it was the first recorded re-sighting of a tagged bird on the island.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza school kill 10 as health crisis deepens under siege
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit a school sheltering displaced people near Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, killing 10. The Palestinian health ministry warned of a catastrophic medical crisis as Israel continues attacks and restricts humanitarian aid.

stories.title: ‘Caught unawares’: France put to the test by the US-Israeli war in the Middle East
stories.summary: France is seeking to define its diplomatic role amid the US-Israeli military campaign in the Middle East. President Emmanuel Macron convened a national defence council meeting as Paris attempts to limit its exposure to the escalating crisis.

stories.title: How Israel’s invasion of southern Lebanon created a humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: Israel's military operations in southern Lebanon have displaced approximately 1.2 million people, roughly one-fifth of the country's population. The humanitarian crisis has intensified over the past month as the invasion expanded.

stories.title: US, IDF strikes hit Iranian rail and Kharg Island; Israel faces ongoing missile attacks
stories.summary: US and Israeli forces struck Iranian railway infrastructure and targets on Kharg Island. Israel continued to face missile attacks, including Hezbollah rocket fire in the north and Iranian cluster munitions hitting central Israel. Reports of damage to a Tehran synagogue were under review.

stories.title: ‘Get a grip’: How Iranian embassies mocked Trump’s vulgar threat
stories.summary: Iranian embassies around the world launched a coordinated social media campaign mocking President Trump's profanity-laden threat against Iran. The diplomatic trolling effort was a direct response to Trump's escalatory rhetoric.

stories.title: DR Congo: Fighting between army and M23 rebels leave civilians at breaking point
stories.summary: Fighting between Congolese soldiers backed by local armed groups and M23 rebels allegedly supported by Rwanda continues in Fizi territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. New recruits are joining armed groups while civilians are caught in the crossfire.

stories.title: Soaring costs, fuel shortage fears drive Pakistan to electric motorbikes
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs and supply fears linked to Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz are driving a surge in electric motorbike sales across Pakistan. Retailers in Rawalpindi and other cities report sales increases of up to 70 percent.

stories.title: In Albania, teens at German school discover tribal code of honor that saved Jews in WWII
stories.summary: Students at the Refik Veseli Schule in Albania learned about "besa," an Albanian tribal code of honor that mandated protection of strangers fleeing persecution during World War II. The school is named for an Albanian recognized as Righteous Among the Nations for saving Jews.

stories.title: ToI closes its Arabic- and Persian-language sites
stories.summary: The Times of Israel closed its Arabic- and Persian-language websites. The outlet cited the ease of online translation tools and a strategic decision to focus on original English-language content.

stories.title: Russia says Middle East war opens new export opportunities
stories.summary: Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said the Middle East war is creating opportunities for Moscow to expand global exports of energy, raw materials, and food. He noted that rising oil prices are boosting state revenues as geopolitical tensions reshape supply chains.

stories.title: Gunmen attack building housing Israeli Consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Three gunmen attacked police outside a building housing the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on Tuesday, sparking a gunfight. One attacker was killed and the two others were captured with injuries, according to Turkish officials.

stories.title: Gunfire heard near Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Gunfire was reported near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. A local Jewish community member told the Jerusalem Post that the consulate has been closed for two years and is likely unstaffed.

stories.title: Armed Forces of Ukraine regain control of section in Kharkiv region between Ambarne and Milove, says Tregubov
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recaptured a small section in the Kharkiv region between the villages of Ambarne and Milove, according to spokesperson Tregubov. Meanwhile, Russian troops continue active operations in the Lyman and Kupiansk sectors.

stories.title: Exiled for a drawing: The Russian father and daughter who stood up to Putin
stories.summary: In March 2022, twelve-year-old Maria Moskaleva drew an anti-war picture at her school in western Russia protesting the offensive in Ukraine. Her father was imprisoned for "discrediting" the Russian army after supporting her. The two fled Russia and are now refugees in Strasbourg, France.

stories.title: Iran calls for young people to form human chains to protect power plants
stories.summary: Iranian officials urged young people to form human chains around power plants as airstrikes pounded Tehran on Tuesday. The call came hours before the expiration of President Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating strikes on its infrastructure.

stories.title: US reportedly strikes Iran's Kharg Island
stories.summary: The United States carried out strikes on what it described as military targets on Iran's Kharg Island, according to Axios citing a senior US official. Kharg Island is a critical hub for Iran's crude oil exports.

stories.title: Settlers erect outpost in East Jerusalem, attack Palestinian locals
stories.summary: Extremist Israeli settlers erected an outpost in East Jerusalem and attacked Palestinian residents in a nearby hamlet, injuring four people. Four individuals were arrested, and the IDF briefly detained then released two Israelis suspected of beating a Palestinian family in the West Bank.

stories.title: California 'architect' of 19th century native American genocide, 'US govt 'funded' most of killing'
stories.summary: UCLA History Professor Benjamin Madley argues that the destruction of California's Indigenous populations between 1846 and 1873 meets the legal criteria for genocide. His research contends the U.S. government funded most of the killing, challenging narratives attributing the demographic collapse primarily to disease or displacement.

stories.title: Fresh strikes hit Kharg Island as Trump threatens to kill "a whole civilization" tonight
stories.summary: The United States and Israel struck Iran's Kharg Island, the country's main oil export terminal, on Tuesday. The strikes came hours before President Trump's deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face massive attacks on power plants and bridges.

stories.title: Passover candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: Passover candle lighting times were published for communities across Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Gunman killed in shootout outside Israel's Istanbul consulate
stories.summary: A gunman was killed and two others were wounded in a shootout with Turkish police outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on Tuesday.

stories.title: Israel is 'systematically' killing Lebanese healthcare workers
stories.summary: Former Lebanese Health Minister Firas Abiad accused Israel of systematically killing healthcare workers in Lebanon, stating that medical personnel have been targeted in what he described as brazen attacks.

stories.title: One dead as train travelling 99mph collides with lorry in France
stories.summary: A train traveling at 99 mph collided with a lorry in northern France, killing the train driver. The lorry driver has been taken into custody.

stories.title: Why Donald Trump now needs a ‘forever war’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted an expletive-laden ultimatum on Truth Social directed at Iran, demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and threatening strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges. The post drew widespread attention for its tone and content.

stories.title: Israel's attacks devastate over a fifth of Lebanon farmland
stories.summary: Israel's military operations have damaged over one-fifth of Lebanon's farmland, severely disrupting food production and driving sharp increases in food prices across the country.

stories.title: Iran Guards threaten long-term energy disruption for US allies if ‘red lines’ crossed
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned it could disrupt oil and gas supplies to the United States and its allies if Washington crosses Tehran's declared red lines. The Guards said their response would extend beyond the region and target energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Under airstrikes, Iran defiant on eve of Trump's ceasefire deadline
stories.summary: Iran and Israel traded attacks on Tuesday as Tehran refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or accept a ceasefire deal ahead of a deadline set by U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump had threatened to have Iran "taken out" if his demands were not met.

stories.title: Dear or peril? War on Iran enters its most decisive phase
stories.summary: The conflict between the United States and Iran has reportedly entered a critical phase, though specific new developments were not detailed in the available text.

stories.title: Russian forces strike administrative buildings in Chernihiv region; casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck administrative buildings in Novhorod-Siverskyi and Pryluky in Ukraine's Chernihiv region, resulting in casualties.

stories.title: Chilean woman accused of Pinochet-era kidnaps loses extradition battle
stories.summary: Adriana Rivas, a Chilean woman accused of kidnappings during the Pinochet era, lost her extradition battle in Australia. Rivas had moved from Chile to Australia in the 1970s, where she worked as a nanny and cleaner.

stories.title: What’s Iran’s 10-point peace plan that Trump says is ‘not good enough’?
stories.summary: Iran presented a 10-point peace plan to address the ongoing conflict, but President Trump dismissed it as "not good enough." As Trump's deadline approached, prospects for a ceasefire appeared unlikely.

stories.title: Iran says it struck energy and industrial infrastructure in Israel, UAE and Kuwait
stories.summary: Iran's military announced it conducted drone attacks on petrochemical and energy infrastructure in southern Israel near Dimona, as well as targets in the UAE and Kuwait. The strikes included a US Navy repair facility in Jebel Ali port and were described as retaliation for attacks on Iranian energy sites.

stories.title: Australian soldier charged with war crimes in Afghanistan
stories.summary: Australian soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, one of the country's most decorated military veterans, was charged on Tuesday with murdering unarmed prisoners captured during operations in Afghanistan.

stories.title: Taiwanese opposition leader to meet China’s Xi in a test of diplomatic skill
stories.summary: Kuomintang leader Cheng Li-wun traveled to China for a meeting with President Xi Jinping. The visit is seen as a significant test of diplomatic skill that could affect the party's prospects in upcoming Taiwanese elections.

stories.title: South Africa: Missing Helicopter Found With Occupants Unharmed
stories.summary: South African police located a helicopter that went missing on Monday with four occupants, including the pilot. All individuals were found alive and unharmed, according to the South African Police Service.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF kills Hezbollah anti-tank terrorists operating from southern Lebanon mosque
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it killed Hezbollah anti-tank operatives who were operating from a mosque in southern Lebanon. Additional Hezbollah fighters were also killed, and weapons including explosives and firearms were seized.

stories.title: Chinese embassy in US confirms death of semiconductor researcher Wang Danhao
stories.summary: The Chinese embassy in Washington confirmed that semiconductor researcher Wang Danhao died by suicide at the University of Michigan after being questioned by US federal law enforcement. Embassy spokesperson Liu Pengyu said the US had "overstretched" national security concerns, subjecting Chinese students and scholars to unwarranted scrutiny.

stories.title: Drone strikes minibus in Nikopol: Three dead, injury toll climbs to 16
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a city minibus in Nikopol, Ukraine, killing three people. The total number of casualties from the attack has risen to 16.

stories.title: Pezeshkian says ready to die for Iran as official urges youth to form human chains near targets
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian declared he is ready to die for Iran as Trump's deadline to reach a deal on the Strait of Hormuz approaches. An Iranian official also urged young people to form human chains near potential strike targets.

stories.title: Israel kills 11 Palestinians in Gaza, Ben-Gvir storms Al-Aqsa
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed 11 Palestinians in Gaza, including in an attack on a school sheltering displaced people. Separately, Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir raided the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in East Jerusalem.

stories.title: Trump threatens to take out Iran in 'one night' as deadline looms
stories.summary: President Trump said Monday he could take out Iran "in one night," threatening to destroy all of the country's power plants and bridges if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his Tuesday 8 pm ET deadline. Iran had rejected a proposed 45-day ceasefire and called for a permanent end to the war.

stories.title: Iran ‘does not forget its friends’ as Malaysia ships pass Hormuz amid selective access
stories.summary: Iran permitted Malaysia-linked vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz while restricting other shipping, highlighting Tehran's use of the strategic waterway as diplomatic leverage. Analysts noted the move underscored close Iran-Malaysia political ties and drew scrutiny over sanction-sensitive oil trade.

stories.title: Australia’s most decorated soldier Ben Roberts-Smith arrested over alleged war crimes in Afghanistan
stories.summary: Ben Roberts-Smith, 47, Australia's most decorated living soldier, was arrested at Sydney Airport and charged with five counts of war crime murders related to the killing of unarmed civilians during deployments in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012.

stories.title: NYT: Ukraine attacks Russian oil ports to cut into Iran’s war profits
stories.summary: Ukraine escalated drone strikes on Russian oil ports in the Baltic region, which handle approximately 40% of Russia's crude exports. The attacks aimed to reduce Russian oil revenues that have reportedly doubled due to the disruption of Iranian exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Turkey probes shooting near Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Turkey's justice minister announced an investigation into the shooting near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, assigning three prosecutors to the case. Officials noted no Israeli diplomats are currently based at the consulate or at the embassy in Ankara.

stories.title: Government shutdown enters eighth week as Johnson faces GOP revolt over DHS funding deal – US politics live
stories.summary: The US partial government shutdown entered its eighth week with Congress on recess until April 13, as House Speaker Johnson faced a Republican revolt over DHS funding. President Trump reiterated threats to destroy Iran's infrastructure if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his Tuesday evening deadline.

stories.title: Diamer-Bhasha Dam protesters call off sit-in, reopen Karakoram Highway
stories.summary: Protesters blocking the Karakoram Highway in the Diamer district of Pakistan's Diamer-Bhasha Dam area ended their sit-in after negotiations with the district administration. Stranded vehicles and passengers began moving following restoration of traffic.

stories.title: Syrian children face deadly legacy of mine-contaminated land
stories.summary: Children across Syria continue to be killed and injured by landmines and unexploded ordnance left over from years of conflict, particularly in villages and farmlands contaminated with deadly explosives.

stories.title: Ukrainian duo indicted in Romania for setting incendiary traps at Nova Post office — allegedly on Russia’s orders
stories.summary: Romanian prosecutors indicted two Ukrainian nationals for allegedly planting incendiary parcels at a Nova Post office in Bucharest. The sabotage plot is reportedly linked to Russian intelligence services.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 27 attacks on Chernihiv region, damaging energy infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 27 strikes on Ukraine's Chernihiv region over a 24-hour period, causing 67 explosions and damaging energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Videos capture shooting near Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Videos circulating online captured the sound of gunfire during a shooting incident near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, Turkey. The footage documented the armed confrontation in the vicinity of the diplomatic building.

stories.title: Russia’s Baltic port resumed shipments two days ago. Ukraine just struck it again.
stories.summary: On April 7, Ukrainian forces struck a Russian Baltic port for a second time, just two days after it had resumed oil shipments. The attack is part of a broader Ukrainian campaign targeting Russia's major oil export infrastructure.

stories.title: Viktor Orbán told Putin ‘I am at your service’ in October phone call
stories.summary: A phone call transcript reported by Bloomberg revealed Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán told Russian President Vladimir Putin "I am at your service" during an October call. The revelation drew fresh scrutiny of Budapest's ties to the Kremlin as US Vice President JD Vance arrived in Hungary.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks on Iran are ‘clear and obvious war crimes’
stories.summary: Critics have characterized ongoing US and Israeli military operations against Iran as violations of international law, warning that the conflict risks undermining the rules-based global order.

stories.title: Whale that swam 32km up Washington river is found dead
stories.summary: A grey whale that swam approximately 32 kilometers up a river in Washington state was found dead. Researchers believe the whale may have traveled inland in search of food or because it was ill.

stories.title: Elbit to start delivering drones to Romania, signs Greece deal
stories.summary: Israel's Elbit Systems is preparing to begin drone deliveries to Romania and has signed a deal to supply rocket launchers to Greece, expanding its European defense contracts.

stories.title: War in Ukraine: Cameroon confirms death of 16 nationals enlisted in Russian army
stories.summary: The Cameroonian government published the names of 16 Cameroonian citizens who died while fighting alongside the Russian military in Ukraine.

stories.title: Oil hovers near $110 as Trump deadline on Hormuz looms
stories.summary: Oil prices hovered near $110 per barrel as a deadline set by US President Donald Trump for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached. Brent crude traded around $108.82 while US West Texas Intermediate briefly surged above $116, a four-week high.

stories.title: Student Kills Teacher in Knife Attack at Perm Region School
stories.summary: The fatal knife attack occurred at School No. 5 in Dobryanka, a town of about 30,000 people in Russia's Perm region. A student killed a teacher in the incident.

stories.title: Trump threatens ‘complete demolition’ of Iran as deadline nears
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened the complete demolition of Iran as his stated deadline for Tehran approached. Regional officials were engaged in urgent diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions.

stories.title: India kicks off crucial state elections for Modi’s BJP amid Iran war turmoil
stories.summary: India began state elections in Assam and Kerala on Thursday, with West Bengal and Tamil Nadu voting later in the month. The campaigns have been shaped by concerns over potential energy price increases and the safety of Indian migrant workers in the Middle East amid the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Harry Styles announces jazz, pop, indie and electronic artists for his Meltdown festival
stories.summary: Harry Styles announced the lineup for the 2025 Meltdown festival at London's Southbank Centre, featuring artists spanning jazz, pop, indie rock, and electronic music. Styles will perform a solo concert on June 16 at the Royal Festival Hall alongside his Wembley Stadium dates.

stories.title: Explainer: Why Trump’s Iran threats are raising war crimes concerns
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's threats against Iran have raised concerns about potential war crimes. However, analysts suggest Trump may not face any legal consequences for his statements or actions.

stories.title: Ethiopia: PM Abiy, Lt. Gen. Tadesse Convene As Tigray Admin Term Nears End
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed met with Lieutenant General Tadesse Werede in Addis Ababa as the term of the Tigray Regional Interim Administration approaches its end. The discussions focused on reviewing the administration's annual performance report.

stories.title: Can Africa tackle the oil shock from the Iran war?
stories.summary: African nations are working to secure alternative oil and gas supplies as the ongoing war involving Iran disrupts energy exports from the Middle East, threatening the continent's energy security.

stories.title: Malawi: Inside the K5 Billion Amaryllis Cash-Out - Collins Magalasi At the Centre of the Operation
stories.summary: Malawi's Financial Intelligence Agency faces scrutiny for failing to act on controversial cash withdrawals totaling K5 billion from the sale of Amaryllis Hotel. The matter is now under parliamentary investigation, with Collins Magalasi identified as a central figure.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike at least 30% of the oil storage tanks in Ust-Luga, says CCD
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck at least 30% of the oil storage tanks at the Russian Baltic port of Ust-Luga, according to Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF strikes Shiraz petrochemical site, releases footage of attacks on Iranian air defenses
stories.summary: The Israeli military released footage of strikes on a petrochemical facility in Shiraz, Iran, which it said produced key missile-related chemical components. The IDF also published video showing attacks on Iranian air defense systems.

stories.title: Russian court designates Chechen Republic of Ichkeria a ‘terrorist organization,’ bans its units across Europe
stories.summary: A court in Grozny, Russia, designated the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria a terrorist organization and banned its activities within Russia.

stories.title: Africa: AU Shares Sorrow at Death of Ambassador Konjit Sinegiorgis of Ethiopia
stories.summary: African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf expressed condolences over the death of Ethiopian Ambassador Konjit Sinegiorgis. She was recognized as a pioneering figure in Ethiopia's foreign service and a dedicated Pan-Africanist.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Ambush, Kill University Student in Plateau
stories.summary: Gunmen ambushed and killed a 300-level university student in Dum Village, Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State, Nigeria.

stories.title: Tanzania: TMA Issues a Weather Alert Warning of Heavy Rainfall, Floods in Coastal Regions
stories.summary: The Tanzania Meteorological Authority issued a three-day weather alert warning of heavy rainfall and potential flooding in several coastal regions, including Dar es Salaam.

stories.title: Members of neo-Nazi ‘active clubs’ join combat events at secretive Virginia compound
stories.summary: Members of neo-Nazi "active clubs" from Texas, Tennessee, and Pennsylvania have been traveling to a secretive compound in Lynchburg, Virginia, to participate in riot-style combat training events with other white nationalist groups. Participants included a licensed school teacher and a former police officer.

stories.title: Rwanda: Experts On Why Genocide Ideology Continues to Spread Abroad
stories.summary: Experts warn that the ideology behind the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi continues to spread across the Great Lakes region and among Rwandan diaspora communities. Propagation occurs through social media, digital platforms, and networks linked to perpetrators and their descendants.

stories.title: Manlio Graziano: 'Europe still needs the US but they know they cannot trust Americans anymore'
stories.summary: Geopolitics professor Manlio Graziano argued that the US remains a superpower but no longer functions as "leader of the free world," citing strategic failures from Vietnam to Afghanistan. He said Europe still needs the US but can no longer fully trust American commitments.

stories.title: China starts work on solar plant built under extreme conditions, amid global energy crisis
stories.summary: China broke ground on a 50-megawatt concentrated solar power plant in Dangxiong County, Tibet, at an altitude of 4,550 metres, making it the world's highest-altitude parabolic trough solar thermal facility. The project includes a 400-megawatt photovoltaic system and is expected to be fully operational by 2027.

stories.title: Israel tells Iranians their lives are at risk if they use trains as Trump deadline looms | First Thing
stories.summary: Israel warned Iranian civilians their lives would be at risk if they used railways on Tuesday, as President Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached. Trump had threatened to bomb Iran's power plants and bridges if no deal was reached.

stories.title: Australia's most decorated soldier Ben Roberts-Smith arrested over alleged war crimes
stories.summary: Ben Roberts-Smith, described as Australia's most decorated living soldier, has been arrested over alleged war crimes related to the killing of unarmed civilians during his military deployment in Afghanistan.

stories.title: NGO on Gaza: 'We don’t share the same definition of ceasefire'
stories.summary: An airstrike in central Gaza killed ten people despite a fragile ceasefire established last October. NGO Première Urgence Internationale said millions of Palestinians in both Gaza and the West Bank still require basic humanitarian assistance as global attention has shifted toward the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Vinicius hails Lamine Yamal for condemning anti-Muslim fan chants
stories.summary: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior praised FC Barcelona's Lamine Yamal for publicly condemning anti-Muslim chants by football fans, expressing hope that their joint stand will protect future players from similar abuse.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Protests sweep West Bank after death penalty law
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes on densely populated areas in Gaza have escalated, with children among the injured and civilians killed. Protests have also spread across the occupied West Bank following the passage of a new death penalty law.

stories.title: Iran targets Saudi petrochemical site as Israel strikes Shiraz facility
stories.summary: Iran attacked a petrochemical complex in Jubail, Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, according to Iran's Fars news agency, marking a significant escalation. Separately, the Israeli military struck a petrochemical facility in Shiraz, southwestern Iran, claiming it produced nitric acid.

stories.title: ‘Dying of thirst’: Inside Gaza’s al-Mawasi water crisis
stories.summary: Residents of al-Mawasi in Gaza are facing a severe water crisis, with families describing daily hardship as shortages of clean drinking water continue to worsen under ongoing siege conditions.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: UN Security Council to vote on Strait of Hormuz resolution
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is set to vote on a resolution concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that the strait has undergone what it called irreversible strategic changes.

stories.title: Between war and regime oppression, Iran trapped by trauma cycle
stories.summary: The ongoing war on Iran has worsened a pre-existing mental health crisis in the country, compounding decades of psychological trauma caused by living under repressive governance, according to author Tara Kangarlou.

stories.title: Turkish police shoot three gunmen in clash outside Israel's Istanbul consulate
stories.summary: Turkish police shot three gunmen in a clash outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul. Turkey's interior minister said one of the attackers had links to the Islamic State group.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages reported in 15 regions due to shelling and severe weather
stories.summary: As of the morning of April 7, power outages affected 170 settlements across nine Ukrainian regions due to severe weather. Russian shelling caused additional outages in seven more regions, according to grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills Child and Parents in Vladimir Region
stories.summary: In addition to the three family members killed in the Ukrainian drone strike in Russia's Vladimir region, a second child—a girl—survived but was hospitalized with burns, according to regional authorities.

stories.title: Trump’s blunders in Iran have made Russia the big winner. But Ukraine is fighting back.
stories.summary: An updated analysis examines how U.S. policy missteps regarding Iran have strategically benefited Russia five weeks into the conflict. The report also assesses Ukraine's counter-moves and unexpected developments that emerged during the period.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strike kills family of 3, including 12-year-old, in Russia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike killed two adults and their 12-year-old child in the Alexandrovsky District of Russia's Vladimir region, according to Governor Alexander Avdeyev.

stories.title: UK government caps student loan interest rates at 6% from September
stories.summary: The UK government announced a cap of 6% on interest rates for plan 2 and plan 3 student loans in England and Wales, effective from September. Ministers acted after criticism that higher inflation linked to global conflict was driving up graduate repayments significantly beyond original loan amounts.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Govt Begins Mass Trial of Suspected Terrorists in Abuja
stories.summary: The Nigerian government has begun mass trials of suspected terrorists at the Federal High Court headquarters in Abuja. Thirteen courtrooms were simultaneously handling terrorism cases on Tuesday.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Awaits Arrival of Turkish Oil Drilling Ship in Landmark Energy Move
stories.summary: Somalia is preparing for the arrival of the Turkish-owned drilling vessel Cagri Bey, expected in Mogadishu starting April 9. The move marks a landmark step in Somalia's offshore energy exploration efforts.

stories.title: Malawi: Chakwera Spits Fire - 'My Silence Is Not Weakness'
stories.summary: Former Malawian President Lazarus Chakwera delivered a rare public warning, stating that his habitual calmness and restraint should not be mistaken for political weakness.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes 'completely destroy' synagogue in Tehran
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes completely destroyed the Rafi-Nia Synagogue in central Tehran, according to footage released by Iran's IRNA news agency. The building was reduced to rubble in the attack on the Iranian capital.

stories.title: How US, Israel are waging a war on Iranian culture, education
stories.summary: Iranian officials have accused the United States and Israel of targeting Iranian cultural and educational institutions, claiming the strikes aim to undermine Iranian national identity.

stories.title: India moves closer to nuclear fuel self-reliance
stories.summary: India's domestically designed Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam achieved criticality, a key milestone toward nuclear fuel self-reliance. Prime Minister Modi said the development supports India's goal of expanding nuclear power capacity from 8 to 100 gigawatts by 2047.

stories.title: Donald Trump has repeatedly delayed deadlines for Iran, but suggests Tuesday’s is final
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly pushed back deadlines for Iran but has indicated that a Tuesday deadline is final. Trump stated he is not concerned about committing war crimes with his planned military attacks on Iran.

stories.title: 1 attacker dead after gunmen open fire outside Israeli consulate in Istanbul
stories.summary: Three gunmen opened fire on police outside a building housing the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on Tuesday, killing one attacker and resulting in the capture of two others. Two Turkish police officers sustained minor injuries. The assailants carried long-barrelled weapons and had reportedly traveled to Istanbul from elsewhere.

stories.title: Ben Gvir raids Al-Aqsa as Israel plans to reopen mosque to settler incursions
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir raided Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem on Monday while Muslims remain barred from entry. Israeli police are planning to reopen the site to allow up to 150 settlers at a time to resume daily incursions, drawing widespread Palestinian criticism.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 7: Crunch time for talks with Iran as Trump threatens Tuesday night strikes
stories.summary: US President Trump threatened Tuesday night strikes on Iran as diplomatic efforts intensified. Separately, a downed US airman was rescued from Iranian territory as talks on a potential deal with Tehran continued.

stories.title: Five policemen injured in IED attack targeting police patrol in Lakki Marwat
stories.summary: At least five policemen were injured in Lakki Marwat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, when an IED fitted to a motorcycle exploded as a police patrol passed on the Bannu-DI Khan section of the Indus Highway. Authorities attributed the attack to Fitna-al-Khawarij, the state's term for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

stories.title: Vedomosti reports Kremlin is weighing removal of Belgorod region governor ahead of September elections
stories.summary: Russian business daily Vedomosti reported, citing sources close to the presidential administration, that the Kremlin is considering removing Belgorod Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov before regional elections scheduled for September 2026.

stories.title: Easter faith and defiance in Lebanon under Israeli fire
stories.summary: Lebanese communities marked Easter under continued Israeli fire, baking, praying, and remaining on their land despite displacement and destruction. Residents expressed determination to preserve traditions amid fears of permanent loss.

stories.title: Artemis II moon crew flies farther than humans have ever gone before
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew flew farther from Earth than any humans in history during a six-hour flyby of the moon's far side. The four astronauts observed meteor impact flashes on the darkened lunar surface during the rare survey.

stories.title: One assailant killed, two wounded after shooting outside Istanbul's Israeli consulate
stories.summary: One attacker was killed and two were wounded in a shooting outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on Tuesday; no diplomats were present at the time. Two police officers sustained minor injuries. Turkey's interior ministry said the dead gunman was affiliated with a designated terror group.

stories.title: Artemis II crew start trip home after milestone-rich lunar flyby
stories.summary: The Artemis II crew completed their lunar flyby and began their return journey to Earth on Tuesday. The astronauts gathered celestial observations including views of little-known lunar craters, a solar eclipse, and meteor strikes that scientists hope will yield new discoveries.

stories.title: Cape Town mums patrol streets amid surge in violence
stories.summary: In Cape Town, South Africa, a group of mothers has formed neighborhood watch patrols to protect their community amid a surge in gang-related violence. The South African government deployed 2,200 soldiers alongside police across five provinces for one year to combat gangs and organized crime.

stories.title: Iranian missile strike damages cars and street in Israel
stories.summary: Video footage from Ramat Hasharon in Israel shows damaged sidewalks and an overturned car resulting from an Iranian missile strike on the city.

stories.title: Shmyhal inspects power facility damaged by Russian attacks
stories.summary: Ukraine's First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal visited a power generation facility that had been damaged by Russian strikes.

stories.title: Nigeria: Itsekiri Youths Call for Careful Management of Pipeline Surveillance Contracts in Niger Delta
stories.summary: The Itsekiri Youths for Good Governance urged Nigeria's federal government to ensure careful management and oversight of pipeline surveillance contracts in the Niger Delta to maintain safety and operational efficiency.

stories.title: What must happen for the US and Iran to reach a peace deal?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump extended his deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Tuesday evening, his third extension since the conflict began on February 28. Analysts noted significant gaps between the two sides, including a trust deficit, the absence of a guarantor, and disagreements over Israel's role.

stories.title: Singapore set to be hit by global energy crisis as it unveils countermeasures
stories.summary: Singapore announced a package of measures to help households and businesses cope with rising energy costs driven by the Middle East conflict. Analysts said the city-state's economy would inevitably be affected by the global energy crunch, though it is better positioned than neighboring Southeast Asian countries.

stories.title: Russians strike minibus in Nikopol: Three dead, 12 wounded
stories.summary: A Russian military drone struck a minibus in Nikopol, Ukraine, killing three people and wounding 12 others.

stories.title: Trump says can take out Iran 'in one night' as deadline ticks closer
stories.summary: President Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran on Monday, saying the "entire country can be taken out in one night" as his deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached. Iran had rejected a 45-day ceasefire proposal and demanded a permanent end to the war.

stories.title: Tanzania: Government Orders Swift Recovery for Traders After Simu 2000 Fire
stories.summary: Tanzanian Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba ordered immediate measures to restore business activities after a fire destroyed market stalls at the Simu 2000 complex in Sinza Ward, Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam.

stories.title: ‘US-Israel playing Russian roulette with security of the region’
stories.summary: Analysts have warned that joint US-Israeli military operations in the Middle East are recklessly endangering regional security and risk triggering a wider conflict.

stories.title: Student stabs teacher to death outside school in Russia
stories.summary: A 17-year-old student stabbed a teacher to death outside a school in Dobryanka, a city in Russia's Perm Krai, approximately 60 kilometers from the city of Perm.

stories.title: Middle East War: Trump ramps up threats against Iran
stories.summary: As the conflict in the Middle East enters its second month, U.S. President Donald Trump is escalating threats against Iran. On Monday he warned that the entire country could be 'taken out' on Tuesday.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia kill three civilians each in tit-for-tat drone attacks
stories.summary: Drone attacks by both Ukrainian and Russian forces each killed three civilians in a single day of tit-for-tat strikes. The attacks came one day after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy renewed his offer for an Easter ceasefire.

stories.title: Chinese logistics firms shift away from Middle East as war raises costs
stories.summary: Chinese logistics companies are reducing operations in the Middle East due to rising costs from the ongoing conflict. Firms are redirecting resources to Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Americas.

stories.title: At least 133 injured in Israel over past 24 hours: Report
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported that 133 people were injured across the country over the past 24 hours from continued Iranian retaliatory strikes.

stories.title: Iran strikes disrupt Saudi-Bahrain bridge, hit petrochem site
stories.summary: Authorities temporarily closed the King Fahd Causeway between Saudi Arabia and Bahrain on Tuesday after Iranian missiles struck Saudi Arabia's largest petrochemical complex. The strikes disrupted operations at the major industrial site.

stories.title: Taiwan’s gender row boxer Lin takes bronze medal at Asian championships
stories.summary: Taiwanese boxer Lin Yu-ting won a bronze medal at the Asian championships in her first competitive bout since a gender eligibility dispute overshadowed her Olympic gold medal victory.

stories.title: Air India CEO steps down early as losses mount
stories.summary: Air India CEO Campbell Wilson is stepping down before his term was set to expire in 2027, as the airline continues to face mounting financial losses. He will remain in the role until a successor is appointed.

stories.title: Germany works to clarify new rules on fighting-age men leaving country
stories.summary: Germany's defense ministry is working to clarify a provision in an updated military service law requiring men aged 17 to 45 to obtain permission before leaving the country for more than three months. The law took effect in January but went largely unnoticed until a local newspaper report highlighted it.

stories.title: Three killed in shooting near Israeli consulate in Turkiye’s Istanbul
stories.summary: Three people were killed and two police officers injured in a shooting near the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, Turkey. Authorities launched an investigation into the incident.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda Turns to Homegrown Apps for Faster Services
stories.summary: Ugandan government institutions are increasingly adopting locally developed digital applications as part of the country's digital transformation. Innovation hubs are creating new opportunities for youth in the technology sector.

stories.title: Ethiopia: PM Abiy Meets Tigray Interim Chief Administrator to Assess Annual Report
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed held talks with Tigray Interim Chief Administrator Lieutenant General Tadesse Worede to review the region's annual performance report and discuss key findings.

stories.title: US is ‘using Mexico as a garbage sink’ leading to ‘toxic crisis’, UN expert says
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Marcos Orellana warned that Mexico faces a "toxic crisis" due to pollution from imported US waste and dangerous pesticides, calling the country a "garbage sink." He cited lax environmental standards and insufficient oversight as enabling pollutants to accumulate and harm Mexican communities' health.

stories.title: Wisconsin votes in supreme court race amid threat of midterm election attacks
stories.summary: Wisconsin voters went to the polls on Tuesday to elect a state supreme court judge replacing retiring conservative Justice Rebecca Bradley. The race could further strengthen the liberal majority on the bench ahead of midterm elections in the key swing state.

stories.title: Trump’s New Cyber Strategy Is Catnip for Beijing
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the Trump administration's new offensive cyber strategy, intended to restore deterrence, may instead benefit Beijing. Critics contend that emphasizing offensive cyber operations could prove counterproductive against China's capabilities.

stories.title: Beyond Russian oil, China also increases appetite for Ukrainian wheat flour
stories.summary: China signed a protocol with Ukraine to allow imports of Ukrainian wheat flour, broadening agricultural trade between the two countries. The agreement was signed by China's ambassador to Ukraine, Ma Shengkun, and Ukrainian officials. The move underscores Beijing's pragmatic diplomacy as it simultaneously increases energy imports from Russia.

stories.title: From tech PhD to China Taoist priest, Zhang Gaocheng inspires a new generation
stories.summary: Zhang Gaocheng, a 74-year-old Taoist priest and deputy director of the Taoist Association of China, gained social media attention for his academic background and life advice resonating with younger Chinese. He came into the spotlight after attending the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.

stories.title: Qatar LNG ships appear to abort bid to exit Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Qatar's liquefied natural gas tankers appeared to abandon attempts to exit the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has restricted transit through the waterway since U.S. and Israeli military strikes began.

stories.title: No Russian ships or boats present in Azov-Black Sea region, says Pletenchuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian Navy spokesperson Pletenchuk reported that no Russian ships or boats were present in the waters of the Azov-Black Sea region.

stories.title: Kenya: ODPP Boosts Prosecutors' Capacity to Tackle Terror Financing in Weeklong Training
stories.summary: Kenya's Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions launched a weeklong training program to strengthen prosecutors' capacity to investigate and prosecute terrorism financing cases linked to extremist networks.

stories.title: Outpaced by the US, China’s military places selective bets on artificial intelligence
stories.summary: China is making selective investments in military artificial intelligence applications, with a Taiwan-based analyst noting that Beijing may have surpassed the United States in AI capabilities for drone swarms. Overall, however, the US maintains a broader lead in military AI development.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran threat deepens fears of wider war as mediation efforts continue
stories.summary: US President Trump escalated threats against Iran, describing scenarios of devastating military strikes, while also signaling cautious support for Pakistan's mediation efforts to prevent a full-scale conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Rwanda: Genocide - Some of the Places That Faced Most Vicious Massacres
stories.summary: Rwanda is commemorating the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, in which over one million people were killed in approximately 100 days. The remembrance highlights some of the sites where the most brutal massacres occurred.

stories.title: Antonio Guterres ‘alarmed’ by Donald Trump rhetoric on Iranian energy plants: UN spokesperson
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed alarm over Donald Trump's rhetoric regarding Iranian energy plants. As the West Asia conflict entered its second month, Guterres stressed the need for dialogue and diplomacy to reach a peaceful resolution.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes destroy buildings in northern Iran
stories.summary: Video footage shows widespread destruction in Pardis, a city in northern Iran, following strikes. The Israeli military confirmed it bombed targets in Iran on April 7.

stories.title: Gaza genocide death toll surpasses 72,312 as Israeli continues attacks
stories.summary: The Palestinian health ministry reported that at least 72,312 people have been killed and 172,134 wounded in Gaza since October 7, 2023. In the past 24 hours, hospitals received 10 bodies and 44 wounded individuals. Since the October 2025 ceasefire, at least 733 more have been killed.

stories.title: Train driver killed, two critically injured as TGV train collides with truck in north of France
stories.summary: The driver of a TGV high-speed train was killed and 13 people were injured when the train struck a truck at a level crossing in the Pas-de-Calais region of northern France on Tuesday morning.

stories.title: Nigeria Christian group disputes army rescue claim in Kaduna church attack
stories.summary: A Christian group in Nigeria is disputing the Nigerian army's claim that it rescued victims during a deadly church attack in Kaduna state. The disagreement has raised tensions in the region.

stories.title: Weizmann Institute helps map Moon’s shadowy sources of ice
stories.summary: Scientists from Israel's Weizmann Institute and U.S. institutions are collaborating to map ancient ice deposits at the Moon's poles. The research supports NASA's Artemis program priorities, including ice sampling for a potential lunar water supply.

stories.title: Schools set to partially reopen Sunday, subject to IDF guidelines
stories.summary: Israeli schools are set to partially reopen on Sunday in lower-risk areas, subject to IDF security guidelines. Students will alternate between in-person and remote learning, with 30 to 50 percent attending classes at a time where shelters are available.

stories.title: Iran defiant on eve of Trump’s ceasefire deadline, refuses to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of a ceasefire deadline set by U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump had demanded Tehran reopen the strait by midnight GMT on April 7.

stories.title: France's Sarkozy says 'innocent' at trial over Libya funding
stories.summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy declared his innocence at an appeals trial on Tuesday, rejecting charges that he sought Libyan financing for his 2007 presidential campaign in exchange for helping improve Tripoli's international image.

stories.title: Russian forces carry out 60 strikes on Sumy region; one man injured
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted 60 strikes on 23 settlements across 14 territorial communities in Ukraine's Sumy region between the mornings of April 6 and April 7. One man was injured.

stories.title: 'Moving moment' as Artemis II crew flies farther than humans have ever gone before
stories.summary: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission flew past the far side of the moon on Monday, traveling deeper into space than any humans before them. The rare flyby revealed the lunar surface under cosmic bombardment and was described as a "moving moment" at mission control in Houston.

stories.title: Hungary’s foreign minister says JD Vance’s visit signals ‘golden age’ of Hungarian-US relations – Europe live
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance arrived in Budapest for a two-day visit and was welcomed by Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó. Szijjártó described the visit as signaling a "golden age" in Hungarian-U.S. relations. Hungarian opposition leader Péter Magyar responded by saying no foreign country should interfere in Hungarian elections.

stories.title: Iranian missile fragments hit several locations in central Israel following interception
stories.summary: Iranian missile fragments struck several locations in central Israel after interception by air defenses. Sirens sounded at approximately 9:10 a.m., and initial reports suggested the missile carried a cluster munitions warhead.

stories.title: Israeli-US air strikes in Iran’s Alborz kill 18, including children
stories.summary: Israeli-US air strikes on residential areas in Iran's Alborz province killed at least 18 people, including two children. The province's deputy governor confirmed the death toll and said 24 others were injured in the attacks, according to Iran's Fars news agency.

stories.title: Ukraine hits major oil terminal in southern Russia in drone strike
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's marine terminal in southern Russia on Monday, damaging a mooring point and igniting four oil tanks, according to the Russian defence ministry. Ukraine's military said it targeted a different terminal in the port of Novorossiysk.

stories.title: “We expect more nonsense”: Sybiha warns of Russian fakes targeting Ukraine’s Gulf defence role
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha warned of Russian disinformation campaigns targeting Ukraine's developing defense ties with Gulf states. Sybiha said the fake narratives are evidence of Moscow's strategic failures.

stories.title: Oil prices seesaw after Trump says Iran can be ‘taken out’ in one night
stories.summary: Oil prices fluctuated sharply on Tuesday after President Trump said Iran could be "taken out" in one night. Brent crude rose to $111 a barrel before dipping to around $109.40. The IMF chief warned of inflation and slower growth linked to the crisis.

stories.title: France high-speed rail collides with truck, killing train driver
stories.summary: A French TGV high-speed train traveling from Dunkirk to Paris collided with a truck carrying military equipment at a level crossing in Bully-les-Mines in northern France on Tuesday. The train driver was killed, two people were critically injured, and 11 others sustained lesser injuries. The train was carrying 243 passengers.

stories.title: Resident doctors begin longest strike yet as Streeting accuses BMA of hypocrisy over pay – UK politics live
stories.summary: Resident doctors in the UK began their longest strike yet in a dispute over pay. Health Secretary Wes Streeting and the British Medical Association exchanged accusations over responsibility for the collapse of negotiations.

stories.title: USA striker Patrick Agyemang’s World Cup in doubt after stretcher exit
stories.summary: U.S. men's national team striker Patrick Agyemang faces doubt over his World Cup participation after being stretchered off following an awkward fall during an English Championship match. The player appeared emotional as he left the pitch.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 77 of 110 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 77 of 110 drones launched by Russian forces against Ukraine since the evening of April 6.

stories.title: Liberia: President Boakai Extends Mandatory Firearms Registration
stories.summary: Liberian President Joseph Boakai signed Executive Order No. 162, extending the mandatory registration of civilian-held firearms across the country.

stories.title: Nigeria: Police Arrest Suspected Killers of Three Officers in Taraba, Recover Stolen Firearms
stories.summary: Police in Taraba State, Nigeria, arrested suspects allegedly involved in the killing of three police officers in Donga Local Government Area. Stolen service firearms from the deceased officers were also recovered.

stories.title: Trump's Tuesday deadline: Will he really ‘bomb Iran into the Stone Age’?
stories.summary: International press coverage examined whether President Trump would follow through on his threat to bomb Iran's energy infrastructure if it does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz before his Tuesday deadline. Coverage also touched on Australia's arrest of war crimes suspect Ben Roberts-Smith and reports of a secret military base in Somaliland linked to U.S., UAE, and Israeli interests.

stories.title: Israel warns Iranians their lives will be at risk if they use trains as Trump deadline looms
stories.summary: Israel warned Iranian citizens to avoid using the country's railways on Tuesday ahead of Trump's deadline, citing safety risks. The warning, posted in Farsi on social media by the Israeli military, came after Trump threatened to destroy Iran's bridges and power plants if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UNSC to vote on Hormuz resolution ahead of Trump deadline
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is set to vote on a Bahrain-drafted resolution on the Strait of Hormuz, coordinated with the GCC and Jordan, ahead of a US deadline for Iran to reopen the waterway. The resolution demands Iran cease attacks on commercial ships and encourages coordinated defensive measures.

stories.title: Nigeria: NiMet Forecasts 3-Day Sunshine, Cloudiness Across Nigeria
stories.summary: Nigeria's Meteorological Agency forecast sunshine and cloudiness across the country from Monday to Wednesday.

stories.title: What is the US telling its Pacific allies by moving missiles to use in the Iran war?
stories.summary: The Pentagon has relocated nearly its entire inventory of JASSM-ER long-range cruise missiles from the Pacific theater to the Middle East for use in the Iran conflict. Analysts say the move suggests possible U.S. arms supply constraints and signals to Indo-Pacific allies and adversaries that Washington's strategic priorities currently lie elsewhere.

stories.title: Iran arrests 85 accused of sharing intelligence with ‘enemy’
stories.summary: Iranian authorities arrested 85 people across 25 provinces accused of gathering and transmitting intelligence to hostile actors. Security forces dismantled what they described as an enemy network, seizing electronic equipment including Starlink devices, weapons, and ammunition.

stories.title: Traders across Punjab want early closure timings for Cantts, DHA too
stories.summary: Traders across Punjab, Pakistan, have called on authorities to uniformly enforce the government's 8pm business closure policy in all areas, including cantonments and Defence Housing Authority zones, without discrimination.

stories.title: Ben Gvir raids Al-Aqsa as Israel plans to reopen mosque to settler incursions
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in East Jerusalem. Palestinian authorities warned that an Israeli proposal to admit equal numbers of Palestinians and Israelis to the site risks entrenching division at the holy compound.

stories.title: ‘Remarkable resilience’ in Iran as Trump deadline looms
stories.summary: With hours remaining before President Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, France 24's correspondent in Tehran reported tension among ordinary Iranians. However, many citizens displayed what was described as "remarkable resilience," continuing to show support for the government despite the ongoing war and threat of further strikes.

stories.title: Albanese brings forward Singapore trip and speaks with China in bid to shore up petrol shipments to Australia
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese moved up a planned trip to Singapore, Australia's largest source of petrol imports, to secure fuel shipments amid the Middle East conflict. Diesel prices are rising again and petrol prices have stopped falling despite a recent government cut to the fuel excise.

stories.title: ‘Military action is not an effective means to pursue nonproliferation’
stories.summary: Observers have raised concerns about strikes on nuclear facilities in Iran, warning that military action risks radioactive contamination and is not an effective tool for pursuing nonproliferation goals.

stories.title: Trump steps up Iran threats as deadline approaches
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to destroy every bridge and power plant in Iran within four hours unless Tehran met his demands, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Trump set a deadline of Tuesday 8 p.m. New York time for Iran to comply.

stories.title: Has US war on Iran killed the 'Gulf moment'?
stories.summary: The ongoing US war on Iran has raised questions about the future of Gulf states' rising global influence. Analysts are debating whether the conflict undermines the political, economic, and cultural ascendancy of the UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia on the world stage.

stories.title: Trump’s Board of Peace gives Hamas disarmament deadline
stories.summary: The Trump administration's Board of Peace issued a disarmament deadline to Hamas. Representatives from the Board of Peace and Hamas were expected to meet in Cairo on April 7.

stories.title: Ukraine scores 9 out of 100 on the reform plan that decides its EU future
stories.summary: Three months into a reform plan that will determine Ukraine's EU accession prospects, the country has scored only 9 out of 100 possible points. The plan sets 10 priorities over one year for EU membership progress.

stories.title: US, Israel, Iran agree two-week ceasefire
stories.summary: President Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran after threatening to "wipe out a civilisation" if Tehran failed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by midnight GMT.

stories.title: Trump says US to stop 'bombing and attack of Iran' for two weeks
stories.summary: President Trump warned he would "wipe out a civilisation" if Iran failed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by a midnight GMT deadline. He subsequently announced a two-week suspension of bombing and attacks on Iran.

stories.title: Only the president 'knows what he will do on Iran': White House
stories.summary: The White House stated that only President Trump knows what actions he will take regarding Iran. Trump had previously threatened to 'wipe out a civilisation' if Iran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by midnight GMT.

stories.title: Trump threatens 'whole civilisation will die' if no Iran deal
stories.summary: President Trump threatened that Iran's 'whole civilisation will die' if a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is not reached by Tuesday night. US-Israeli strikes had already targeted key Iranian roads and bridges.

stories.title: US-Israel strikes hit Iran as Tehran defies Trump's deadline
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes continued to hit Iran on Tuesday as Tehran showed no sign of backing down ahead of Trump's deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The war continued to rage across the broader region.

stories.title: NASA’s record-breaking crew Earth-bound after trip around Moon
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew is returning to Earth after a lunar flyby mission. The Lockheed Martin-built Orion capsule came within an estimated 6,545 kilometers of the moon's surface, setting a record.

stories.title: Trump and Hegseth invoke God and religion in Iran war press conference
stories.summary: President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth invoked religious themes during a press conference on the Iran war. Trump stated he believes God supports the U.S. effort, while Hegseth compared a rescued airman's story to the resurrection of Jesus.

stories.title: Who will blink first? Trump wants talks to end war, but Iran won’t bow easily to pressure
stories.summary: Tensions between the U.S. and Iran remain high as President Trump pushes for negotiations to end the war while Iran resists pressure. The gap between American demands and Iranian expectations raises concerns the conflict could escalate significantly.

stories.title: PTCL forces subscribers to buy internet package or lose landline in Karachi
stories.summary: PTCL is replacing copper wire infrastructure with fibre optic cables in Karachi, including in Defence Housing Authority areas. Residents report being told they must purchase PTCL internet packages or lose their existing landline connections.

stories.title: Galactic lunacy
stories.summary: The article discusses humanity's long fascination with the moon, touching on cultural myths, the origin of the term 'lunatic,' and the moon's gravitational effect on tides. It references Yuri Gagarin's 1961 orbit of Earth as a milestone in space exploration.

stories.title: War update: 150 combat engagements on front line over past day, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors remain most active
stories.summary: A total of 150 combat engagements were recorded along the front line on April 6. The Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors remained the most active areas of fighting.

stories.title: Iran rejects 45-day ceasefire proposal
stories.summary: Iran rejected a proposed 45-day ceasefire, stating it wants a permanent end to the conflict rather than a temporary halt to hostilities.

stories.title: A new oil shock accelerates return to nuclear power
stories.summary: Rising oil prices from the Middle East conflict are accelerating a global return to nuclear power. The responses of Japan and Taiwan to the energy crisis are expected to influence other nations' stances on nuclear energy.

stories.title: Six weeks in, US-Israel war on Iran becomes battle of endurance
stories.summary: Six weeks into the US-Israeli war on Iran, the conflict has evolved into a prolonged battle of endurance. Developments include a high-risk US special forces operation inside Iranian territory and mounting military pressure around the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Tight rope act
stories.summary: Pakistan is navigating a difficult balancing act domestically and internationally amid an ongoing regional conflict. Islamabad has been central to negotiations but faces challenges due to its fragile economic situation and an unpopular government. Continued hostilities risk destabilizing the country's position further.

stories.title: Iran releases on bail Japan national jailed amid antigovernment protests
stories.summary: Iran has released on bail a Japanese national who had been jailed amid antigovernment protests. The individual is believed to be Shinnosuke Kawashima, the Tehran bureau chief for Japanese public broadcaster NHK.

stories.title: Synagogue in Tehran ‘completely destroyed’ in US-Israeli attack
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes destroyed a synagogue in Tehran, with reports indicating at least 15 people were killed across Iran overnight. The attack prompted widespread outrage.

stories.title: Trump’s lesson from risky rescue: Threaten to go harder at Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump renewed his threat to bomb Iran and its leaders following a risky rescue operation that freed two American troops. Trump has signaled an escalation in military pressure against Tehran.

stories.title: Lebanese firefighters respond to aftermath of Israeli strike
stories.summary: Lebanese firefighters responded to the aftermath of an Israeli strike on the southern city of Maarakeh. Video footage showed crews working to extinguish fires caused by the attack.

stories.title: Russians attack four districts of Dnipropetrovsk region since yesterday evening, leaving one dead and five injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck Kryvyi Rih, Nikopol, Pavlohrad, and Synelnykove districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 10 times using drones since Monday evening. An 11-year-old boy was killed and five others were wounded.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill five in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon killed at least five people. Lebanon's National News Agency reported three killed in Ma'raka and two in Tayr Dibba, as Israeli warplanes and artillery intensified bombardment across multiple towns in the south.

stories.title: For Gulf states, geography is both a generous and treacherous patron
stories.summary: The blockage of the Strait of Hormuz is causing severe economic consequences for Gulf states including the UAE and Qatar, which rely on energy exports and serve as international air traffic hubs. Rising fuel prices are being felt globally, and expatriates and affluent residents in the region are reportedly leaving.

stories.title: Trump’s threats
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump held a press conference on Monday offering both threats against Iran and hints of a possible negotiated solution. The event followed inflammatory social media posts targeting Iran. Much of the presser focused on a mission inside Iran in which two American troops were reportedly rescued.

stories.title: Lawmakers call for fuel subsidies, citing loss-making bus service amid oil price spike
stories.summary: Hong Kong lawmakers urged the government to provide fuel subsidies and approve fare increases for non-franchised bus companies as rising oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict drive up operating costs. A coach operator's failed attempt to cut services was cited as a sign of broader problems in the transport sector.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei unconscious in Qom as questions grow over who leads Iran today - report
stories.summary: A diplomatic memo cited by The Times reports that Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei is unconscious and in severe condition in Qom, unable to participate in decision-making. The report deepens uncertainty over who is currently governing Iran.

stories.title: Russia loses 980 troops, two air defense systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost 980 troops in one day, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses to approximately 1,305,470 personnel since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. Two Russian air defense systems were also destroyed.

stories.title: Dam protest  paralyses Karakoram Highway
stories.summary: Protesters affected by the Diamer-Bhasha Dam project blocked the Karakoram Highway for six days near Chilas and Thore in Diamer, cutting land connectivity between Gilgit-Baltistan and the rest of Pakistan and stranding hundreds of passengers.

stories.title: Iran calls for ‘human chains’ around its power plants before US deadline
stories.summary: Iran urged young citizens to form human chains around power plants ahead of President Trump's Tuesday 8 p.m. EDT deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian President said 14 million people had volunteered to fight. Trump has threatened to bomb all of Iran's power plants and bridges if the deadline is not met.

stories.title: What is driving the Houthis’ decision-making on joining the Iran war
stories.summary: Internal debate within Yemen's Houthi movement is shaping their stance on joining the broader Iran war. Two factions have emerged: one favoring caution and another pushing for commitment to their allies.

stories.title: Most in Asean prefer China over US as partner in poll, Trump cited as biggest concern
stories.summary: An annual survey by the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute found that most Southeast Asians would choose China over the United States as a strategic partner if forced to pick. Analysts attributed the shift to geopolitical and trade uncertainties driven by Washington's policies but cautioned against viewing it as a zero-sum contest, noting ASEAN seeks to diversify partnerships.

stories.title: WHO suspends Gaza ops after contract worker killed
stories.summary: The World Health Organization suspended all operations in Gaza, including medical evacuations, after a contract worker was killed. The suspension remains in effect until further notice.

stories.title: Death toll rises to 11 in Balochistan as rain lashes much of country
stories.summary: At least 11 people have died in rain-related incidents in Balochistan, Pakistan, with five fatalities in Qila Abdullah and Kakar Khurasan districts. Heavy rains and thunderstorms continued across 30 of the province's 41 districts, with flooding expected in the Kabul River and urban areas.

stories.title: The Hidden System Turning Chinese Tech Companies into Military Suppliers
stories.summary: Chinese robotics firm Unitree, which signed a 2022 pledge not to weaponize its machines, holds over 60 percent of the global quadruped robot market. An investigation reveals how Chinese tech companies are being drawn into military supply chains despite public commitments against weaponization.

stories.title: The Hidden System Turning Chinese Tech Companies into Military Suppliers
stories.summary: Chinese robotics firm Unitree Robotics, which signed a 2022 pledge alongside Boston Dynamics not to weaponize robots, held over 60 percent of the global quadruped robot market by 2023. An investigation examines a hidden system that has turned Chinese technology companies into military suppliers despite public commitments otherwise.

stories.title: The Hidden System Turning Chinese Tech Companies into Military Suppliers
stories.summary: Chinese robotics firm Unitree, which signed a 2022 pledge not to weaponize its machines, holds over 60 percent of the global quadruped robot market. An investigation highlights hidden systems that channel Chinese tech companies into military supply roles.

stories.title: The Hidden System Turning Chinese Tech Companies into Military Suppliers
stories.summary: An investigation reveals that Chinese tech companies, including Hangzhou-based Unitree Robotics, are being drawn into military supply chains despite public pledges against weaponization. Unitree, which holds over 60 percent of the global quadruped robot market, signed an open letter in 2022 alongside firms like Boston Dynamics pledging not to weaponize their machines.

stories.title: Russians carry out 788 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region, injuring three people
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 788 strikes targeting 43 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, injuring three people.

stories.title: Jailed PTI leaders urge multiparty moot on Middle East war
stories.summary: Jailed PTI leaders urged the party to convene a multiparty conference on the escalating Middle East conflict, while JUI-F chief Fazlur Rehman separately called for an in-camera parliamentary session to clarify Pakistan's position on the crisis.

stories.title: Filipino farmers leave crops to rot as fuel prices drive up cost of harvest
stories.summary: Filipino farmers in the northern province of Benguet are leaving vegetables to rot in the fields rather than harvesting at a loss. Rising oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict have driven up costs for labor, transportation, and packing, making it economically unviable for growers like 57-year-old Romeo Wagayan to bring crops to market.

stories.title: 6 takeaways from Trump’s news conference on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump set a deadline of 8 p.m. Washington time on April 7 for Iran to agree to a ceasefire during a press conference. He offered few details on the war's direction while maintaining both threats and openness to negotiation.

stories.title: How Pakistan’s solar boom is shielding it from worst of Iran war crisis
stories.summary: Approximately a quarter of Pakistani households have adopted solar panels, helping insulate millions of families from the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing Iran war. The solar boom is reducing Pakistan's vulnerability to global fuel disruptions.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 39 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: On day 39 of US-Israeli attacks on Iran, President Trump's strict deadline approached while Tehran dismissed his threats as 'delusional.' Iran has shown defiance in the face of continued military pressure.

stories.title: Video: Fires erupt at Saudi Arabia’s Jubail industrial hub after missile attack
stories.summary: Fires erupted at Saudi Arabia's Jubail Industrial City after Iranian missile strikes on Monday. Saudi Arabia's defense ministry said air defenses intercepted seven ballistic missiles targeting the Eastern region, but debris fell near energy facilities at the major petrochemical hub.

stories.title: Why Turkey will be a key regional powerbroker after Iran war
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Turkey is positioned to become a key regional powerbroker following the Iran war. How Ankara wields its influence could determine whether the Middle East moves toward stabilization or further fragmentation.

stories.title: Pauline Hanson says she won’t ‘abandon’ Ben Roberts-Smith as Greens argue ‘no one should be above the law’
stories.summary: Australian One Nation leader Pauline Hanson said she would not "abandon" Ben Roberts-Smith following his arrest on five war crime murder charges related to service in Afghanistan. The Australian Greens countered that "no one should be above the law." Prime Minister Anthony Albanese declined to comment on the arrest.

stories.title: Nearly 18 percent of French petrol stations face fuel shortages
stories.summary: Around 18 percent of petrol stations across France experienced fuel shortages on Tuesday. Junior energy minister Maud Bregeon attributed the disruptions to TotalEnergies' decision to cap retail fuel prices below competitors, driving higher demand at certain stations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Dangote Refinery Ships 17 Petrol Cargoes to African Countries As Global Supply Tightens
stories.summary: Dangote refinery owner Aliko Dangote said the facility has shipped 17 petrol cargoes to African countries as global supply tightens due to disruptions from the Iran war.

stories.title: Israeli strikes leave 15 more dead in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon on Sunday killed at least 15 people, including a local Christian political party official. Israel launched a ground invasion in southern Lebanon in March after Hezbollah entered the Middle East war on Iran's side.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: 'The Foolishness in Attending to Voice Dissent' - Zanu-PF Blames Opposition for Public Hearings Chaos
stories.summary: Zanu-PF Treasurer Patrick Chinamasa accused Zimbabwe's opposition of causing chaos during public hearings on Constitutional Amendment Bill number 3, stopping short of calling the hearings a ruling party event.

stories.title: Middle East war will kickstart renewables boom: IEA chief
stories.summary: International Energy Agency executive director Fatih Birol said the Middle East war will accelerate a boom in renewable energy adoption. Birol indicated the transition to renewables can happen very soon as the conflict disrupts traditional energy markets.

stories.title: Rocket fragments fall in five Israeli cities, local media reports
stories.summary: Rocket fragments fell in at least five cities in central Israel following Iran's latest ballistic missile attack. Loud explosions were reported over Tel Aviv linked to interception activity, while Israeli Army Radio said a cluster munition was fired toward Eilat.

stories.title: Israel threatens Iran’s trains, railways before Trump’s deadline expires
