stories.summary: Israel threatened to target Iran's railway infrastructure ahead of President Trump's deadline. The King Fahd Causeway linking Saudi Arabia and Bahrain was briefly closed amid escalating tensions over Iranian infrastructure threats.

stories.title: Israeli strikes target Iran’s petrochemical facilities
stories.summary: US and Israeli airstrikes targeted Iranian civilian and energy infrastructure, including the South Pars petrochemical complex and multiple airports near Tehran. IRGC and Quds Force officials were assassinated, and over 15 Iranian citizens were killed. Iran retaliated, striking Haifa and US bases in Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Almost 26,000 Ukrainian Armed Forces personnel undergo advanced training in Germany – General Staff
stories.summary: Approximately 26,000 Ukrainian Armed Forces personnel have undergone advanced training in Germany since mid-2022, coordinated through the Multinational Special Training Command, according to Ukraine's General Staff.

stories.title: Iran envoy says Pakistan mediation nearing ‘critical’ stage
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, said Islamabad's mediation efforts to halt the US-Israeli war on Iran are entering a 'critical, sensitive' stage. He described Pakistan's diplomatic push as 'positive and productive.'

stories.title: Closing the Air and Missile Defense Gap in the Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: During a 12-day war between Iran, Israel, and the United States, the U.S. military expended 100 to 150 upper-tier missile interceptors—approximately 25 percent of its total stockpile. The analysis highlights growing air and missile defense gaps in the Indo-Pacific as assets are consumed in Middle East operations.

stories.title: Closing the Air and Missile Defense Gap in the Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: During last summer's 12-day war involving Iran, Israel, and the United States, the U.S. military expended approximately 100 to 150 upper-tier missile interceptors — about 25 percent of its total stockpile. The experience has highlighted significant air and missile defense gaps that need to be addressed in the Indo-Pacific theater.

stories.title: Trump lashes out at ‘paper tiger’ NATO while re-upping Greenland claim
stories.summary: President Trump criticized NATO as a paper tiger during a press conference and renewed his claim over Greenland. He also expressed dissatisfaction with non-NATO allies South Korea, Australia, and Japan for not providing support.

stories.title: Iranian media: Jewish synagogue destroyed in US-Israeli strike
stories.summary: A synagogue in Tehran was destroyed after a US-Israeli strike targeted a nearby residential building, according to Iran's Mehr news agency. The blast severely damaged surrounding structures due to narrow streets. Video from Press TV showed rescue workers searching through rubble.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts 7 missiles; debris falls near energy facilities
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia announced on Tuesday that it intercepted and destroyed seven ballistic missiles targeting its Eastern Region. The defense ministry reported that debris from the intercepts fell near energy facilities in the area.

stories.title: Opposition chides, govt defends increase in oil prices
stories.summary: Pakistan's opposition lawmakers in the National Assembly criticized a sharp increase in petroleum prices, while the government defended the hike citing rising international oil prices linked to the US-Israel-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Trump seizes on rescue of downed airman to recast unpopular Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump used the successful rescue of a downed US airman in Iran to recast public perception of the five-week-old war. He emphasized the operation's cinematic elements to project military strength and command of the conflict.

stories.title: Iran judiciary chief calls to fast-track cases tied to ‘enemy collaboration’
stories.summary: Iran's judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei called for expedited prosecutions of individuals accused of aiding the country's adversaries amid ongoing US-Israeli strikes. He urged authorities to accelerate verdicts, including executions and asset confiscation.

stories.title: Partners provide Ukraine with medical humanitarian aid worth UAH 31M in March – Ministry of Health
stories.summary: Ukraine received medical humanitarian aid worth approximately 31 million hryvnias from international partners during March, according to the Ministry of Health.

stories.title: Iran’s Anti-Access and Area Denial Strategy Is Cruder Than China’s But Still Dangerous
stories.summary: An analysis examines Iran's anti-access and area-denial strategy in the Persian Gulf, including its effective closure of shipping routes and continued Houthi missile threats. The piece argues that these capabilities pose serious challenges to U.S. forces, including a Marine expeditionary unit considering entry into the Gulf.

stories.title: Iran’s Anti-Access and Area Denial Strategy Is Cruder Than China’s But Still Dangerous
stories.summary: Analysts assess that Iran's anti-access and area-denial strategy in the Persian Gulf, while less sophisticated than China's, poses significant dangers to U.S. forces. Closed shipping routes are increasing costs, Gulf partner nations face continued pressure, and Houthi missile launches underscore that the approaches to the battlefield are themselves contested zones.

stories.title: Russia’s drone hits Nikopol bus mid-route: 3 dead, 12 injured at city-centre stop
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a bus mid-route in the Ukrainian city of Nikopol, killing three people and injuring 12 at a city-center stop. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha called the attack deliberate terror against civilians.

stories.title: UN expected to vote on watered-down Hormuz resolution on Tuesday
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is expected to vote Tuesday on a resolution to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The resolution has been significantly weakened after China, a veto-wielding member, opposed provisions authorizing the use of force.

stories.title: Gwadar Port activity revives as Malaysian ship docks
stories.summary: A Malaysian cargo vessel, MV Riva Glory, docked at Pakistan's Gwadar Port carrying 14,629 metric tonnes of transhipment cargo, marking a boost in the port's commercial activity.

stories.title: AJK voter registration deadline extended
stories.summary: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir Election Commission extended the voter registration deadline from April 7 to April 13 for the upcoming 2026 Legislative Assembly elections, covering 33 constituencies across 10 AJK districts and 12 refugee constituencies in Pakistan.

stories.title: Reform UK would stop visas for people from countries seeking slavery reparations
stories.summary: Reform UK announced it would stop issuing visas to people from any country demanding compensation from the UK for the transatlantic slave trade. Party home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf called the reparations demands "insulting," saying "the bank is closed and the door is locked."

stories.title: Taiwanese opposition leader Cheng Li-wun begins ‘journey of peace’ in Shanghai
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun departed for Shanghai leading a 14-member delegation on a six-day visit to mainland China. A planned meeting with Communist Party leader Xi Jinping has drawn scrutiny in Taipei. Cheng said she hoped to make the Taiwan Strait safer amid rising cross-strait tensions.

stories.title: Occupiers unable to restore their air defense system in time after strikes by Ukraine's Defense Forces in Crimea — partisans
stories.summary: Partisan sources report that Russian forces in temporarily occupied Crimea are unable to quickly restore their air defense systems following strikes by Ukraine's Defense Forces, leaving gaps in their defensive capabilities.

stories.title: Saudi-Bahrain causeway closed after Trump threatens to blow up Iran’s infrastructure
stories.summary: Authorities suspended traffic on the King Fahd Causeway linking Saudi Arabia and Bahrain as a precautionary measure amid fears of Iranian strikes targeting Saudi Arabia's eastern province. The closure followed US President Trump's threats to strike Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: India's top court hears challenges to ruling on women's entry into temple
stories.summary: India's Supreme Court is hearing challenges to its earlier ruling on women's entry into a temple. Legal experts say the decision will significantly affect women's religious freedoms in India.

stories.title: Trump renews criticism of Japan, South Korea for not helping US in Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump renewed criticism of Japan and South Korea for not supporting American military efforts in the Iran war. He noted that U.S. troops are stationed in both countries to protect them from North Korea.

stories.title: Minnesota deny Rodriguez has rare muscle wasting condition
stories.summary: Minnesota United denied rumors that midfielder James Rodriguez is suffering from a potentially life-threatening muscle-wasting condition.

stories.title: Report: 40,000 Filipinos unable to take Middle East jobs amid war
stories.summary: More than 40,000 Filipino workers set to depart for jobs in Israel, Lebanon, and Gulf countries have been unable to leave due to the ongoing war and limited flight availability, according to the Philippine Daily Star. Many are staying in temporary accommodation in Manila or have returned to home provinces.

stories.title: Trump's threatened destruction of Iranian infrastructure could be a war crime, legal experts say
stories.summary: Legal experts warned that President Trump's threat to bomb Iranian bridges and power plants could constitute a war crime under international humanitarian law. Trump said Monday he was "not at all" concerned about the risk of committing war crimes in carrying out the strikes.

stories.title: Police notify two Russian servicemen of crimes during occupation of Bucha
stories.summary: Ukrainian National Police investigators notified two Russian servicemen of suspicion for attempted murder and torture of civilians during the temporary occupation of Bucha in the early stages of the war.

stories.title: Senator says targeting Iran civilians would be ‘black mark’ on US military
stories.summary: US Senator Mark Kelly warned that striking civilian infrastructure in Iran could violate international law and damage the reputation of the US military. Kelly called threats to target power plants and other non-military sites illegitimate, saying such orders with no valid military purpose would likely breach the laws of armed conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine, Sweden strengthen cultural cooperation during wartime
stories.summary: Ukraine's Vice Prime Minister Tetiana Berezhna met with Sweden's Culture Minister Parisa Liljestrand to strengthen cultural cooperation between the two countries during wartime.

stories.title: Can small nuclear reactors solve Europe's energy woes?
stories.summary: Debate continues in Europe over whether small modular nuclear reactors can help meet the continent's energy goals. Supporters see them as a key solution, while critics argue they represent a costly distraction from other energy strategies.

stories.title: Can small modular nuclear reactors solve Europe's energy woes?
stories.summary: Proponents argue that small modular nuclear reactors are essential for meeting Europe's energy and climate goals. Critics counter that the technology is a costly distraction that will not resolve the continent's energy challenges.

stories.title: Final death toll 12 in Russian petrochemical plant accident
stories.summary: Rescue operations concluded five days after a large fire at a Russian petrochemical plant, with the final death toll confirmed at 12. The company owning the facility announced the completion of search efforts on Tuesday.

stories.title: Australia charges ex-soldier Roberts-Smith with Afghan war crimes
stories.summary: Australia has charged former soldier Ben Roberts-Smith with war crimes related to the conflict in Afghanistan. The charges follow Roberts-Smith's failed defamation case against journalists who reported he was involved in the murders of unarmed Afghan men.

stories.title: Bangladesh launches measles vaccination drive as child death toll passes 100
stories.summary: Bangladesh launched an emergency measles-rubella vaccination drive in partnership with the United Nations after more than 100 children died in the country's worst measles outbreak in years. Over 900 cases have been confirmed since March, driven by declining vaccination rates.

stories.title: Decorated Australian soldier faces 5 murder charges in Afghan war crime probe
stories.summary: Australian Federal Police arrested a 47-year-old former soldier, widely identified as Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith, on five counts of murder. The charges relate to the alleged killing of unarmed prisoners during service in Afghanistan and follow a sweeping war crimes investigation.

stories.title: Iran says US-Israeli projectile has struck a synagogue in Tehran
stories.summary: A US-Israeli projectile struck a synagogue in Tehran, causing extensive damage, according to video released by Iran's Mehr News Agency. Iranian authorities confirmed the strike hit the religious site in the capital.

stories.title: Draft resolution on Hormuz revised ahead of vote
stories.summary: The UN Security Council scheduled a vote for Tuesday on a revised draft resolution aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The resolution, originally submitted by Bahrain, was amended twice after opposition from Russia and China over language authorizing 'all necessary means,' which can include military action.

stories.title: Doctors warn of spinal cord damage as ‘neck-hanging exercise’ trends among China youth
stories.summary: A trend called the "neck-hanging exercise" has emerged among young people in China, involving hanging by the head from trees to relieve cervical spine pain. According to the 2024 China Cervical Spine Health White Paper, over 200 million people in China suffer from cervical spine disorders, with more than 40 percent of patients under 30. Doctors have warned the practice risks spinal cord damage.

stories.title: Malaysia-owned commercial vessel passes Hormuz
stories.summary: One of seven Malaysian-owned commercial vessels previously stranded in the Strait of Hormuz has been granted safe passage, Malaysia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced. The outcome followed diplomatic engagement, including a call between Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

stories.title: US shouldn't negotiate with Iran until it realizes how badly it's losing - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that Tehran's refusal to accept an interim ceasefire arrangement reflects the regime's belief that time will rescue it from a deteriorating position, and recommends the US delay negotiations until Iran recognizes the extent of its losses.

stories.title: Wang Fuk Court briefing to give residents answers before decisions are made: minister
stories.summary: Hong Kong's home affairs minister assured residents of the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court that an upcoming briefing will address their concerns before key decisions are made. Over 300 homeowners petitioned for a general meeting with interim administrator Hop On Management, a Chinachem Group subsidiary appointed by the government.

stories.title: Australia's most-decorated living soldier arrested over alleged war crimes
stories.summary: Ben Roberts-Smith, Australia's most-decorated living soldier, has been arrested over alleged war crimes. He denies all wrongdoing and previously lost a landmark defamation case related to the alleged murders.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Israel threatens entire Iran train network; Trump says he is ‘not at all’ worried about possible war crimes
stories.summary: The Israeli military warned Iranian citizens to stop using trains, citing danger to their lives, as it threatened Iran's entire rail network. U.S. President Donald Trump said he was not concerned about potential war crimes from planned attacks on Iran as his deadline for a deal approached.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson to Trump: ‘No president should mock Islam'
stories.summary: Political commentator Tucker Carlson criticized US President Donald Trump for mocking Islam in a social media post, calling it an 'intentional desecration of beauty and truth.' Trump had threatened destruction of Iran's energy and transport infrastructure and signed off with 'Praise be to Allah.'

stories.title: UN expected to vote on watered-down Hormuz resolution that omits military action
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is expected to vote on a revised Strait of Hormuz resolution after China blocked language authorizing the use of military force. The watered-down proposal now urges only 'defensive' measures to ensure safe passage for ships.

stories.title: Far Right Jewish West Bank activists publish document summarizing attacks on Arab population
stories.summary: Far-right Jewish activists in the West Bank published a document summarizing attacks they have carried out against Arab residents in West Bank villages. The document was sent to security officials alongside a poster condemning IDF Major General Avi Bluth.

stories.title: US lawmaker says strikes on infrastructure would be 'war crime'
stories.summary: Democratic Senator Chris Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, warned that President Trump's threat to strike civilian infrastructure in Iran could constitute war crimes. Murphy said targeting energy facilities and bridges would kill tens of thousands of innocent Iranians.

stories.title: Brazil's free cooking gas program threatened by energy price spike ahead of election
stories.summary: Surging energy prices in Brazil threaten a government program providing free cooking gas to approximately 50 million people. Fuel distributors, resellers, and analysts warned the program could be undermined six months ahead of a presidential election.

stories.title: Dangote refinery exports surge amid disruptions linked to the Iran war
stories.summary: Nigeria's Dangote refinery, Africa's largest, has increased exports of fuel and fertilizer to African countries experiencing supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Why Real Madrid tie could make or break Kane's Ballon d'Or hopes
stories.summary: Real Madrid's upcoming match against Harry Kane's team could be pivotal for his Ballon d'Or candidacy. Despite being Europe's leading goalscorer, questions remain about whether Kane needs a major trophy to win the award.

stories.title: Canada's Vizsla Silver confirms nine dead workers after abduction at Mexican mine
stories.summary: Canadian mining company Vizsla Silver confirmed on Monday that nine of its ten workers abducted in late January in Concordia, Sinaloa, Mexico, are dead. The workers had been taken from the company's operations in the Mexican state.

stories.title: Russian plant 'Kremniy El' still not resumed production after strike by Defense Forces – partisans
stories.summary: The Bryansk-based Russian plant Kremniy El has not resumed production after being struck by Ukrainian Defense Forces on March 10 and is operating in emergency recovery mode with production halted, according to partisan sources.

stories.title: トランプ大統領 軍と共同で記者会見【ノーカット動画】
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump held a joint press conference with military officials at the White House. He reiterated a deadline for attacking Iran's energy facilities and criticized NATO as a paper tiger, also naming Japan, Australia, and South Korea for not providing assistance.

stories.title: Moon crater named after Artemis commander’s dead wife
stories.summary: A crater on the Moon has been named after Carroll Taylor Wiseman, the late wife of Artemis mission commander Reid Wiseman. Mrs. Wiseman died of cancer in 2020.

stories.title: Hong Kong property launch sees brisk sales as buyers unfazed by Trump’s Iran warning
stories.summary: Hong Kong's La Mirabelle I residential project in Tseung Kwan O saw brisk sales in its second round, with 72 of 168 units sold by noon despite escalating Middle East tensions. Flats were priced between HK$5.93 million and HK$8.99 million with maximum discounts of 15 per cent.

stories.title: What’s behind sudden thaw as North, South Korea exchange warm words?
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret over drone incursions into North Korea, prompting a warm response from Kim Yo-jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. She welcomed his remarks as a wise move, raising hopes for easing tensions on the Korean peninsula.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia President Attends Rally Backing One-Person-One-Vote Elections in Southwest
stories.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud attended a rally in Baidoa where women from the Southwest region expressed support for introducing one-person-one-vote elections in the country.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader makes first China visit since 2016
stories.summary: Taiwan opposition leader Cheng Li-wun traveled to China, marking the first such visit by a major Taiwanese opposition figure since 2016. She said she accepted an invitation from Chinese President Xi Jinping and hopes to serve as a "bridge for peace."

stories.title: Cameroon: Cameroon's Biya Appoints Son Vice President, Head of Armed Forces
stories.summary: Cameroon's President Paul Biya appointed his son, Franck Emmanuel Biya, as Vice President, Head of the Armed Forces, and Minister Delegate at the Ministry of Defence, consolidating executive and military authority within the family.

stories.title: Nigeria: Relief for Nigeria's Oil Sector As Seplat Workers Halt Strike Action
stories.summary: Senior workers at Seplat, one of Nigeria's most prolific energy companies, called off a strike action that could have negatively impacted the country's efforts to increase oil production.

stories.title: Nigeria: Only 10.5% Women in Nigeria Have Formal Jobs - World Bank
stories.summary: A World Bank gender data report found that only 10.5 percent of employed women in Nigeria held wage or salaried positions in 2025, highlighting continued disadvantages for women in the country's formal labour market.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lagos Moves to Decongest Correctional Centres and Upgrade Facilities, Frees 43 Inmates
stories.summary: Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu approved the release of 43 inmates from correctional centres across the state as part of efforts to decongest custodial facilities. This follows the release of 91 inmates in December 2025.

stories.title: Nigeria: After 13 Years, Court Moves to Fast-Track N1.4bn Subsidy Fraud Case
stories.summary: Justice Ismail Ijelu of the Lagos State High Court directed Nigeria's EFCC to conclude its prosecution within three months in the 13-year-old N1.4 billion oil subsidy fraud case against Nadabo Energy Limited and its managing director Abubakar Ali Peters.

stories.title: Nigeria: TCN to Begin Upgrade of Alaoji-Onitsha Transmission Line
stories.summary: Nigeria's Transmission Company of Nigeria, in partnership with the African Development Bank, has begun implementing plans to reconstruct and upgrade the 138-kilometer Alaoji-Onitsha 330kV transmission line, including land acquisition and right-of-way clearing.

stories.title: Nigeria: Again, OPEC Snubs Nigeria, Raises Output Quota for Saudi Arabia, Others
stories.summary: OPEC+ adjusted crude oil output quotas for key producers including Saudi Arabia but again excluded Nigeria from production increases, as the group works to stabilise the global oil market.

stories.title: Rwanda: What Happened On April 7, 1994 As Genocide Against the Tutsi Began
stories.summary: An article in Rwanda's New Times recounts the events of April 7, 1994, when years of genocidal ideology and systemic discrimination erupted into the Genocide against the Tutsi, which claimed over one million lives in 100 days.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amid Deepening Poverty, Govt, States' Revenue Surges 14.2 Percent in 2026
stories.summary: Nigerian federal, state, and local government revenue from the Federation Account Allocation Committee rose 14.2 percent in the first two months of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, even as household poverty indicators continued to worsen.

stories.title: Rwanda: 32 Years Later, Rwanda Remembers
stories.summary: Rwanda commemorated the 32nd anniversary of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. President Kagame lit the Flame of Hope, a symbolic torch that will burn for 100 days to reflect the duration of the genocide.

stories.title: ‘It’s heartbreaking’: resident doctors in England face halt on new training posts
stories.summary: Resident doctors in England face uncertainty after the withdrawal of additional specialty training posts promised during negotiations between the British Medical Association and the government. Up to 4,500 posts were pledged over three years to help doctors progress, but a deadlock over strike action has halted new placements.

stories.title: Some might pay: Noel Gallagher guitar used to write Oasis’s second album to be auctioned
stories.summary: A signed acoustic guitar that Noel Gallagher used to write Oasis's second album, (What's the Story) Morning Glory?, will be auctioned at Sotheby's. The instrument from the bestselling British album of the 1990s is expected to fetch up to £60,000.

stories.title: Calls grow for government to automatically release child trust funds at 21
stories.summary: Calls are growing in the UK for the government to automatically release child trust funds when recipients turn 21. An estimated £1.5 billion in the state-funded savings accounts, set up for children born between September 2002 and January 2011, remains unclaimed.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s Coming Food Crisis
stories.summary: Southeast Asia faces a growing food crisis, with Myanmar expected to be the most severely affected country in the region.

stories.title: Iran rejects ceasefire as Trump says entire country can be ‘taken out’
stories.summary: Iran rejected a ceasefire proposal from the United States as President Trump threatened to "rain hell" on Tehran. Trump warned of strikes unless Iran agreed to a deal that includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Slump in F&B sector over Easter break as 28% of Hongkongers leave city
stories.summary: About 2.12 million Hong Kong residents left the city during the first four days of the Easter break, a 14.34 per cent increase year-on-year. The mass outflow significantly affected the local food and beverage sector, while mainland Chinese visitor arrivals rose 16.13 per cent.

stories.title: IRNA: Iran submits response to US proposal via Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran has delivered its response to a US proposal aimed at ending the war through Pakistan as an intermediary, state news agency IRNA reported. Tehran reportedly rejected a temporary ceasefire, instead calling for a permanent end to hostilities along with sanctions relief and security guarantees.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Marks April 6 Anniversary With Renewed Calls to End War and Restore Civilian Rule
stories.summary: Sudanese political parties and civil forces marked the seventh anniversary of the April 6, 2019 sit-in outside the General Command in Khartoum. They renewed calls for an immediate end to the ongoing war and a return to civilian rule.

stories.title: Africa: How the Middle East War Is Impacting Humanitarian Aid to Africa
stories.summary: Disrupted trade routes caused by the war in the Middle East have delayed the delivery of medicines and other humanitarian aid to crisis zones in Africa, including Sudan and Mali.

stories.title: Anti-war protest held outside US Embassy in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Israeli left-wing activists protested outside the US Embassy in Tel Aviv on Monday, calling for an end to the ongoing war with Iran. The demonstration followed escalating regional tensions after US and Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28 prompted retaliatory missile attacks.

stories.title: As aircraft losses mount, Pentagon wants a software fix to see through the fog of war
stories.summary: The U.S. Defense Department is seeking software upgrades to improve how older aircraft identify each other and process data amid mounting aircraft losses. The initiative aims to enhance situational awareness and reduce friendly-fire risks in complex combat environments.

stories.title: Taxi driver arrested for demanding HK$85 ‘highway toll’ from undercover officers
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested a 31-year-old taxi driver on Lantau Island for demanding approximately HK$85 as a fraudulent highway toll from undercover officers. The arrest was part of a crackdown on taxi violations, with officers posing as passengers on a route from Hong Kong Disneyland Resort to the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge checkpoint.

stories.title: Trump’s threat to strike Iran’s power plants looms
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on social media that Tuesday would be 'power plant day,' signaling a potential escalation of strikes targeting Iran's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Sikorski comments on hints about Ukraine's involvement in TurkStream incident
stories.summary: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski expressed skepticism about the explosives incident near the TurkStream pipeline, suggesting the alleged mining could politically benefit Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ahead of Hungary's parliamentary elections.

stories.title: US says over 13,000 targets struck in Iran
stories.summary: US Central Command said its forces have struck more than 13,000 targets in Iran during the war under Operation Epic Fury, and damaged or destroyed over 155 Iranian vessels. The operations involve nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, submarines, F-35 fighter jets, and B-52 bombers.

stories.title: UAE retaliates against Iran, Bali’s spate of murders: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post highlighted seven major Asia stories from the past week. Key developments included the UAE retaliating against Iran by squeezing its economic lifelines and a series of murder cases in Bali raising safety concerns about the Indonesian island.

stories.title: Global stocks slip, oil climbs above $110 amid Hormuz uncertainty
stories.summary: Global stock markets declined while oil prices rose amid tensions over the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude climbed to $110.19 per barrel and US West Texas Intermediate reached $113.31, as investors weighed the risk of escalation ahead of President Trump's deadline for Iran.

stories.title: ‘Why would Iran agree to a ceasefire given US and Israeli track record?’
stories.summary: Political analyst Trita Parsi stated that Iran's rejection of a US-proposed ceasefire deal should not be surprising, citing the track record of the United States and Israel as reasons Tehran would decline such an agreement.

stories.title: Iran's peace proposal calls for end to Israeli strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon - NYT
stories.summary: According to The New York Times, Iran's peace proposal calls for a complete end to attacks rather than a temporary ceasefire, including a halt to Israeli strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon and the lifting of all sanctions against Tehran.

stories.title: Filipino taxi driver suspended after overcharging K-pop star Soobin in Cebu
stories.summary: A Filipino taxi driver in Cebu has been suspended after attempting to overcharge K-pop group TXT member Soobin in a fare scam. The incident, revealed through the group's channels and reported by South Korean media outlet JTBC, sparked backlash in both South Korea and the Philippines.

stories.title: Trump threatens jail for reporter who revealed Iran airman rescue
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to jail a reporter who revealed details about the rescue of a downed U.S. airman in Iran. The specific media outlet or journalist Trump was referring to was not identified.

stories.title: Spanish politicians clash over request to move Picasso’s Guernica
stories.summary: A dispute has erupted between Spain's Madrid and Basque regional governments over a request to temporarily move Picasso's Guernica to the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao for the 90th anniversary of the bombing of the Basque town. The painting has hung in Madrid's Reina Sofía museum since 1992, and previous relocation requests have been refused.

stories.title: Did Ukraine finally hit Russia’s new Black Sea Fleet flagship?
stories.summary: Ukraine reportedly struck what may be Russia's new Black Sea Fleet flagship, continuing a campaign of increasingly powerful drone attacks aimed at destroying remaining Russian naval assets in the Black Sea.

stories.title: UN says 1.1 million displaced in Lebanon amid conflict
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that more than 1.1 million people have been displaced in Lebanon, representing nearly one-fifth of the country's population. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said approximately 137,000 displaced people are living in shelters, while most others are staying with host communities with limited access to basic services.

stories.title: Blasts heard in Damascus as Israeli defences intercept missiles, report says
stories.summary: Explosions were heard in Damascus and surrounding areas as Israeli air defenses intercepted missiles fired from Iran, according to Syrian state television. No immediate details on damage or casualties were reported.

stories.title: Trump says reopening Hormuz must be in Iran ceasefire deal
stories.summary: President Trump stated on April 6 that reopening the Strait of Hormuz was "a very big priority" and must be included in any ceasefire agreement with Iran.

stories.title: Frankfurt cinema declines to participate in Jewish film festival, drawing backlash
stories.summary: The Astor Film Lounge cinema in Frankfurt declined to participate in a Jewish film festival, drawing criticism from the local Jewish community, which called the decision a 'devastating societal signal.' The cinema cited financial reasons, but a Jewish NGO called the explanation a pretext.

stories.title: Houthis claim joint attack with Iran, Hezbollah on Israel targets
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed a joint military operation with Iran's Revolutionary Guard and Lebanon's Hezbollah targeting sites in southern Israel. Military spokesman Yahya Saree said the attack used cruise missiles and drones against targets in the Umm al-Rashrash area.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says he stands by ceasefire proposal to Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy reaffirmed on Monday his ceasefire proposal to Russia, which is contingent on Moscow halting all attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Rescue operations ongoing in Tehran after strike hits residential area
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society reported that rescue workers are conducting relief operations in Tehran after a US-Israeli air strike hit a residential area. Video showed rescuers searching through rubble of collapsed buildings and assisting injured residents.

stories.title: Japan confirms release of second citizen held in Iran
stories.summary: Japan confirmed the release on bail of a second Japanese national detained in Iran, believed to be the Tehran bureau chief of public broadcaster NHK. The individual had been detained by Iranian authorities since January 20 and was released on April 6 local time.

stories.title: WSJ: No deal likely before Trump deadline expires
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the gap between Washington and Tehran is unlikely to be bridged before President Trump's deadline expires, citing US officials. Trump has grown less optimistic privately about reaching a deal, and strikes could be ordered as early as Tuesday evening.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader makes rare visit to China
stories.summary: Taiwanese opposition leader and Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun arrived in China on Tuesday for a six-day visit aimed at improving cross-strait relations. Despite having previously advocated for Taiwan's independence, Cheng is now working to build ties with Beijing.

stories.title: U.S.-Israeli strike kills Iran Guards intelligence chief
stories.summary: Major General Majid Khademi, described as the intelligence chief of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, was killed in a joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike at dawn. He is among several senior IRGC figures killed since the start of the conflict.

stories.title: Bahrain urges residents to take cover amid missile alert
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry urged residents to take cover after sirens were activated following reports of incoming fire. The warning follows repeated missile and drone attacks on Bahrain since the start of the war in February, as the country hosts US military assets.

stories.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping calls for new energy system amid global shock
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for accelerated development of a new energy system to ensure energy security, as global fuel prices surge following the US-Israeli attack on Iran. Xi emphasized strengthening domestic energy capacity, including hydropower expansion.

stories.title: Venezuela's government, opposition may cooperate to safeguard US assets
stories.summary: Venezuela's government and political opposition are reportedly seeking to coordinate legal efforts to protect the country's U.S.-based assets. The move follows Washington's recognition of interim President Delcy Rodriguez, raising questions about legal representation in American courts.

stories.title: JD Vance backs Viktor Orban ahead of high-stakes Hungary parliamentary elections
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance traveled to Hungary on Monday to express support for Prime Minister Viktor Orban ahead of closely contested parliamentary elections. Vance said discussions would cover bilateral ties, European affairs, and Ukraine, and he planned to deliver a speech on U.S.-Hungary relations.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith arrested: former Australian soldier to be charged with five war crime murders in Afghanistan
stories.summary: Former Australian soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, the country's most decorated living veteran, was arrested at Sydney airport on war crime charges. He faces allegations of five murders of unarmed civilians during service in Afghanistan. Roberts-Smith previously lost a defamation lawsuit against newspapers that published the allegations.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent coordinating airstrikes on Kramatorsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service counterintelligence detained a Russian agent in the Donetsk region who had been coordinating airstrikes targeting the city of Kramatorsk.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent coordinating airstrikes on Kramatorsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) counterintelligence detained a Russian agent in the Donetsk region who was coordinating airstrikes targeting the city of Kramatorsk.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump’s Iran ultimatum enters final 24 hours amid escalation fears
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump expanded military threats against Iran to include power plants and bridges as his deadline for a ceasefire deal entered its final 24 hours. Tehran had rejected a 45-day ceasefire proposal, and Trump warned the country could be destroyed in a single night.

stories.title: Florida governor signs law letting state officials blacklist groups as terror organizations
stories.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a law allowing state officials to designate groups as terror organizations. Free speech and Muslim advocacy groups opposed the legislation, raising concerns about free speech and due process, while DeSantis framed it as a tool to combat extremism.

stories.title: WHO suspends medical evacuations from Gaza following death of contractor in 'security incident'
stories.summary: The WHO suspended medical evacuations from Gaza after an individual contracted to provide services to the organization was killed during a security incident. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed the suspension following the contractor's death.

stories.title: ICBC and CCB lead China’s 6 biggest banks in US$61 billion dividend payout
stories.summary: China's six largest state-owned banks, led by ICBC and China Construction Bank, plan to distribute over 420 billion yuan (US$61 billion) in dividends for 2025. The record-high payouts aim to attract investors seeking stable income as they rotate into defensive assets amid low interest rates.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted 7 missiles, debris falls near energy facilities
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry announced that air defenses intercepted and destroyed seven ballistic missiles launched toward the country's Eastern Region. Debris from the intercepts reportedly fell near energy facilities in the area.

stories.title: Blasts heard near Erbil airport in Iraqi Kurdistan
stories.summary: Local authorities in Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan, reported blasts heard near the city's airport. A separate deadly drone incident struck a civilian area in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

stories.title: Hormuz war pushing millions into poverty, warns Bahrain Foreign Minister
stories.summary: Bahrain's foreign minister warned that the war near the Strait of Hormuz is pushing millions of people into poverty. Traffic through the strait has declined by more than 90% since the onset of the war with Iran. The UN has warned the disruption could send 45 million people worldwide into acute hunger.

stories.title: Hamas given until week’s end to accept disarmament proposal — sources
stories.summary: Hamas has been given until the end of the week to accept a disarmament proposal as part of President Trump's reconstruction plan for Gaza. A diplomat from a mediating country indicated that both Hamas and Israel are unlikely to cooperate with the plan being advanced by envoy Mladenov.

stories.title: China cuts cost of military-grade infrared chips to as little as a few dozen USD
stories.summary: Researchers at China's Xidian University have developed a method to manufacture military-grade infrared chips using conventional techniques, potentially reducing costs to as little as a few dozen U.S. dollars. Mass production is planned by year's end, with applications for smartphone cameras and self-driving vehicles.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills 10 at Gaza school shelter, WHO halts evacuations after aid worker death
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike killed at least 10 people near a school sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza, straining a fragile U.S.-backed ceasefire. The World Health Organization suspended medical evacuations from Gaza after a contracted aid worker was killed.

stories.title: ‘They want to create a rift’: Israeli attacks deepen Lebanon fissures
stories.summary: Lebanon is growing increasingly divided as escalating Israeli bombardment and a ground invasion deepen internal fissures and worsen a displacement crisis across the country.

stories.title: IAEA says strikes near Iran nuclear power plant ‘must stop’
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency called for an end to strikes near an Iranian nuclear power plant, which has been targeted four times since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began. The IAEA warned that continued attacks near the facility pose serious safety risks.

stories.title: Accused Pinochet agent turned Bondi nanny Adriana Rivas to be extradited to Chile
stories.summary: Adriana Rivas, a former Sydney nanny accused of serving as an agent under Chile's Pinochet dictatorship, will be extradited to Chile after losing a seven-year legal battle. Rivas, now in her 70s, is accused of participating in the disappearances of seven people in 1976 and denies allegations of aggravated kidnapping.

stories.title: Israel orders evacuation of 41 towns in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army ordered residents of 41 towns in southern Lebanon to evacuate and move north of the Zahrani River. The directive accompanies ongoing military operations that have cleared large areas of southern Lebanon of residents.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted seven missiles, debris falls near energy sites
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry said it intercepted and destroyed seven ballistic missiles launched toward its Eastern Region, with debris falling near energy facilities. Damage assessments are underway. The kingdom has faced repeated missile and drone attacks since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Trump news at a glance: president’s deadline for Iran and threats against civilian targets loom
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump expanded threats against Iran to include power plants and bridges as his deadline for a deal neared. Tehran rejected a 45-day ceasefire proposal, with Trump warning the country could be 'taken out in one night' if it failed to comply.

stories.title: Trump says Vance, Witkoff, Kushner talking with intermediaries in Pakistan; Iran could be ‘taken out’ on Tuesday
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned on Monday that Iran could be "taken out" in a single night, potentially as soon as Tuesday, ahead of a deadline for Tehran to agree to a ceasefire. Trump demanded Iran forswear nuclear weapons and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Vice President JD Vance and other officials were reportedly talking to intermediaries in Pakistan.

stories.title: Hungary’s Orbán has long annoyed the European Union. Now some hope he faces defeat
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán faces a challenge in the April 12 election from an opponent seeking to mend ties with the European Union. Orbán has long used EU rules to block key initiatives and secure additional funding, with some critics calling him a 'Trojan horse' within the bloc.

stories.title: Trump says Iran could be ‘taken out’ on April 7, Hegseth says major strikes to come
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran could be "taken out" on April 7 and described a weekend operation to recover a downed U.S. airman from Iran. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth indicated that major strikes were forthcoming if Trump's deadline passed without a deal.

stories.title: Ukraine Energy Support Fund receives EUR 3.2M in March
stories.summary: The Ukraine Energy Support Fund received EUR 3.2 million in contributions during March 2026, bringing cumulative donations to the fund to EUR 1.854 billion.

stories.title: India's high-growth economy gets a Middle East oil shock
stories.summary: India's economy is facing significant headwinds as the war involving Iran has triggered a triple energy shock. The country's currency, stock markets, and growth projections have all been negatively affected by rising Middle East oil disruptions.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills at least 10 near Gaza school as ceasefire strains
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike near a school housing displaced Palestinians in Gaza killed at least 10 people and wounded several others on Monday. The attack is the latest violence threatening the fragile U.S.-backed Gaza ceasefire deal, according to health officials.

stories.title: Nigeria Christian group disputes army rescue claim in Kaduna church attack
stories.summary: A Nigerian Christian group in Kaduna state disputed the army's claim that it had rescued 31 people abducted by armed men in northern Kaduna. The group maintained that the victims remained in captivity despite the military's assertions.

stories.title: NGO slams Greek shippers over deliveries to Israel
stories.summary: An NGO criticized Greek shipping companies for facilitating deliveries to Israel, claiming that between May 2024 and December 2025, at least 57 covert crude oil shipments transported approximately 47 million barrels of oil from Turkey to Israel.

stories.title: Judge says Lil Nas X police battery charges to be dismissed if he completes treatment program
stories.summary: A judge in Los Angeles allowed rapper Lil Nas X to enter a mental health diversion program that could lead to dismissal of four felony charges for allegedly attacking police officers. If he completes the treatment program and obeys all laws for two years, the charges will be dropped.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly committee calls for abolishing colonial-era law that ‘criminalises poverty’
stories.summary: A Punjab Assembly committee in Lahore, chaired by Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan, reviewed Section 55(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. The committee declared the colonial-era provision effectively criminalizes poverty by allowing warrantless arrests and recommended its abolition.

stories.title: Riots over Star Ferry fare increase kill 1 as 1,800 arrested – SCMP archive
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post republished archival articles from April 8, 1966, covering riots in Hong Kong's Kowloon and New Kowloon districts sparked by a Star Ferry fare increase. One person was killed and approximately 1,800 were arrested as mobs stoned vehicles, set fires, and clashed with police.

stories.title: China ‘sexual intelligence godmum’ returns, paper robots for ancestors, mum goes bald tutoring son
stories.summary: Chinese online influencer Zhou Yuan, known as the 'Godmother of sexual intelligence,' has resurfaced online after being banned earlier this year. Based in Hunan province, she reportedly earned 24 million yuan (US$3.5 million) selling courses teaching women to enhance their sexual appeal before her account with 200,000 followers was banned in January.

stories.title: Iran UN envoy says Trump remarks ‘incite terrorism’
stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador Amir Saeed Irvani accused US President Donald Trump of inciting terrorism in a letter to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. Irvani also characterized US and Israeli strikes on civilians and infrastructure as war crimes and state terrorism, warning that inaction could undermine international law.

stories.title: WHO suspends Gaza ops after contract worker killed
stories.summary: The World Health Organization suspended its operations in the Gaza Strip after a contract worker was killed. Israel has been accused of consistently violating the ceasefire that took effect on October 10 in Gaza, with over 700 Palestinians reportedly killed since then.

stories.title: Pro-government rallies continue in Iran as officials call for protests
stories.summary: Pro-government rallies continued across Tehran, with demonstrators gathering in public squares waving Iranian flags and expressing support for the government. Iran's deputy minister of youth and sports, Alireza Rahimi, called on citizens to form human chains at power plants nationwide to protest US threats against Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Rules of war must be respected in words and action, ICRC president says
stories.summary: The president of the International Committee of the Red Cross urged governments to respect the rules of war in both words and actions. The statement followed U.S. President Donald Trump's escalating rhetoric against Iran, including threats to rain "hell" on Tehran.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims attacks as Israeli strikes kill 3 in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed its fighters targeted Israeli soldiers and tanks with rockets and drones in the Lebanese towns of Aainata and Markaba, and struck Israeli positions near Kiryat Shmona and Sasa. Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed three people in Tayr Debba in the Tyre district. At least two others were wounded in a strike on a house in Maarakah.

stories.title: Report: 15 Americans wounded in Iranian drone strike on Kuwait base
stories.summary: Fifteen American personnel were wounded in an Iranian drone strike on the Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait, according to CBS News. Most of the injured have reportedly returned to duty. The base, located about 37 kilometres from the Iraqi border, serves as a key hub for US military operations in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy reiterates truce offer ahead of Orthodox Easter
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy renewed his offer to Russia for a mutual ceasefire on strikes against energy infrastructure ahead of Orthodox Easter on April 13. Zelenskyy said the proposal was conveyed to Russia through the Americans but acknowledged Moscow was unlikely to accept. Separately, Australian police arrested an army reservist for joining the war.

stories.title: IMF warns Iran war will raise prices, slow global growth
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that the war on Iran will drive higher inflation and slower global economic growth, even if the conflict ends quickly. The IMF is expected to downgrade its global growth forecast and raise its inflation outlook in its upcoming projections.

stories.title: ESF among 8 international school operators that failed to meet non-local student targets
stories.summary: Eight international school operators in Hong Kong, including the English Schools Foundation, failed to meet government-mandated targets for admitting non-local students this academic year. ESF said it had been increasing non-local student proportions since the pandemic but noted reaching mandated levels could take several years.

stories.title: Olympic cyclist Rohan Dennis says he never wanted to hurt wife Melissa Hoskins and attacks media’s ‘false narrative’
stories.summary: Olympic cyclist Rohan Dennis posted on social media denying allegations of abuse against his wife Melissa Hoskins, who was fatally struck by his car in 2023. Dennis accused journalists of creating a false narrative and stated he has always been against any form of abuse against women.

stories.title: Trump threatens jail for reporter who revealed Iran airman op
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened imprisonment for a reporter who revealed details of an operation involving a US airman in Iran. A US fighter jet was shot down over Iran on Friday, and several media outlets reported that one of the two airmen onboard had been successfully recovered.

stories.title: General Atomics CCA drone wingman prototype crashes in California
stories.summary: A General Atomics prototype drone built for the U.S. Air Force's collaborative combat aircraft program crashed in California. The company reported a mishap occurred shortly after takeoff.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei being treated for ‘severe’ condition in Qom, unable to govern Iran — report
stories.summary: Reports indicate that Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's supreme leader, is being treated for a severe condition in Qom and is unable to participate in governance. Separately, the UN Security Council is expected to vote Tuesday on a revised Hormuz resolution, and Israel approved a plan to partially reopen schools.

stories.title: IMF chief says Iran war means 'all roads' lead to higher prices
stories.summary: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said the war on Iran means all roads lead to higher prices and slower growth. The Fund is expected to release multiple scenarios in its upcoming World Economic Outlook, due for publication on April 14.

stories.title: Why high fuel costs could accelerate the Philippines’ EV boom
stories.summary: Record fuel prices in the Philippines, driven by the war in Iran and a national energy emergency, are pushing consumers toward electric and hybrid vehicles. Filipino motoring journalist James Deakin highlighted the growing cost burden, as Vietnamese EV manufacturers eye the Philippine market.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump warns of attacks as Hormuz deal deadline nears
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said American forces are conducting more strikes on Iran than on any previous day since the war began, as a deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches.

stories.title: Russian attacks cause power outages across border communities in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Russian attacks damaged power infrastructure in the Novhorod-Siverskyi and Koriukivka districts of Ukraine's Chernihiv region, causing power outages across most border communities in the area.

stories.title: Trump says April 7 deadline to make a deal with Iran is final
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared his April 7 deadline for a deal with Iran is final. He acknowledged an Iranian peace proposal as significant but stated it was not sufficient to meet his demands.

stories.title: Zelensky says Ukraine proposed energy truce to Russia through U.S. intermediaries
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv transmitted a proposal to Moscow through American intermediaries for both sides to cease strikes on each other's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: North Korea leader’s sister says Seoul’s regret sending drones ‘wise behaviour’
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret to Pyongyang over drones that were sent into North Korea earlier this year, calling the actions "irresponsible." North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's sister responded by characterizing Seoul's expression of regret as "wise behaviour."

stories.title: Trump: US has plan to destroy every bridge and power plant in Iran Tuesday night if no deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the US has a plan to destroy every bridge and power plant in Iran on Tuesday night if no deal is reached. Iran dismissed the remarks as baseless threats from a delusional president. Trump described Iran's truce offer as significant but insufficient.

stories.title: Zelensky on new diplomatic agreements: Ukraine is sought-after partner
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Ukrainian diplomacy is working to reestablish a permanent presence in Syria and deepen cooperation with regional countries. The government is also pursuing new security agreements with international partners.

stories.title: Kuwait says six injured after Iranian attack on residential area
stories.summary: Kuwait reported six people were injured after Iranian retaliatory strikes hit a residential area. Gulf nations including Kuwait have sustained damage from Iran's strikes since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks in late February, sparking a regional war.

stories.title: Iran conveys to Pakistan its rejection of US ceasefire proposal: report
stories.summary: Iran has communicated its rejection of a U.S. ceasefire proposal to Pakistan, which is serving as an intermediary. Tehran's response included 10 clauses demanding a permanent end to the war, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, sanctions relief, and reconstruction. U.S. President Trump had set a Tuesday deadline for a deal.

stories.title: Trump's Hormuz deadline looms but Asian nations have already struck deals with Iran
stories.summary: As President Trump's deadline on the Strait of Hormuz approaches, several Asian nations have already struck energy deals directly with Iran. Countries in the region moved to secure agreements given their heavy economic reliance on Middle Eastern energy supplies.

stories.title: Hong Kong hospital uses VR tour to ease children’s fears ahead of operations
stories.summary: Hong Kong Children's Hospital in Kowloon Bay introduced a virtual reality program to help ease children's fears before surgery. Guided by a panda character, the VR tour allows young patients to explore the operating theatre and make choices about their anesthesia experience.

stories.title: ‘New’ Bangladesh-India ties will avoid ‘mistakes of the past’: Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir
stories.summary: Bangladesh Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir stated that renewed Bangladesh-India relations should avoid past mistakes. He recommended more frequent exchanges at the level of political parties and officials to address difficult issues and prevent misunderstandings between the two countries.

stories.title: Russia says Ukraine damaged CPC terminal on the Black Sea with drones
stories.summary: Russia accused Ukraine of using drones to attack the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's Black Sea terminal, which handles approximately 1.5% of global oil supply. Moscow reported damage to the single point mooring, loading infrastructure, and four large storage tanks.

stories.title: Israel rescuers say four bodies recovered from Iran strike site
stories.summary: Israeli rescue teams recovered four bodies from an Iranian strike site. The victims were identified as two men and two women, all Israeli civilians from the same family, according to the military.

stories.title: Russian bank apps, telecom services, and Rostelecom home internet go down in widespread outages
stories.summary: Banking apps, telecom services, and Rostelecom home internet experienced widespread outages across Russia on the evening of April 6. The Russian outage-tracking service Sboi.rf reported disruptions affecting banks, satellite companies, and other organizations, with the cause not immediately determined.

stories.title: Russian grain ship believed sunk in Ukrainian drone attack is found and towed to shore, TASS says
stories.summary: A Russian grain ship carrying wheat, previously believed sunk in the Sea of Azov after a Ukrainian drone attack, was found and towed to shore, according to TASS. The death toll from the attack rose to three.

stories.title: Fake Australian, Chinese and Brazilian police stations: BBC goes inside a seized scam compound
stories.summary: Thai military forces seized the Royal Hill casino compound in Thailand in December, revealing it had been operating as a scam center with fake police stations impersonating Australian, Chinese, and Brazilian law enforcement.

stories.title: Little sign of breakthrough as Trump's Iran deadline nears
stories.summary: As President Trump's Tuesday deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches, there are few signs of a diplomatic breakthrough. Trump finds himself in a delicate political position as the final hours tick down.

stories.title: Second ex-staffer accuses Texas lawmaker of sending sexually explicit messages
stories.summary: A second former female staffer has accused Texas Republican Congressman Tony Gonzales of sending sexually explicit messages. Gonzales ended his re-election bid in March after admitting to an affair with a different aide. The San Antonio Express-News first reported the new allegations.

stories.title: Media: Drones attack major chemical plant in Voronezh region
stories.summary: On April 6, a group of drones struck the Minudobreniya chemical plant, one of the largest in Russia's Voronezh region. The facility produces fertilizers and is a major industrial site in the area.

stories.title: Over 60% of Argentines disapprove of Milei amid economic and social crisis
stories.summary: Multiple polls show that over 60% of Argentines now disapprove of President Javier Milei, marking his lowest approval since taking office in December 2023. The decline is driven by persistent high inflation, rising unemployment, business closures, and corruption scandals involving his inner circle.

stories.title: Down the rabbit hole: Trump offers dark Iran warnings after Easter bunny act
stories.summary: President Trump held a press conference after the White House Easter egg roll, during which he discussed the Iran war and issued warnings about the conflict. The event drew attention for its juxtaposition of holiday festivities with stark statements about ongoing military operations.

stories.title: Iraq could restore oil exports to pre-war level within a week if Hormuz reopens, Basra Oil chief says
stories.summary: The head of Iraq's state-run Basra Oil Company said Iraq could restore crude oil exports to approximately 3.4 million barrels per day within a week if the Iran war ends and the Strait of Hormuz reopens.

stories.title: Oil prices slip back as some ships pass Hormuz gauntlet
stories.summary: Oil prices dipped slightly as some commercial vessels resumed transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Turkey's transport minister reported that a third Turkish-owned ship had successfully crossed the war-affected strait, contributing to the easing of prices.

stories.title: Ukraine drones spark blaze at Russia’s Sheskharis oil terminal, sources say
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal, sparking a fire. The attack is part of Ukraine's intensified aerial campaign targeting Russian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine proposes energy truce to Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky proposed an energy truce to Russia, offering to halt attacks on Russian energy infrastructure if Moscow stops targeting Ukraine's energy sector. The proposal was conveyed to Russia through American intermediaries.

stories.title: Trump boasts about 'subterfuge' in operation to rescue US airman in Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said the US operation to rescue a downed American airman in Iran relied on 'subterfuge,' including spreading false information to thin out Iranian forces searching for the pilot.

stories.title: Air Chief Marshal visits the U.S. to boost defence ties
stories.summary: India's Air Chief Marshal visited the United States to strengthen defence ties between the two countries. The visit is part of a series of high-level exchanges reflecting growing strategic convergence between India and the U.S.

stories.title: Taiwan to ship oil from Saudi Red Sea ports
stories.summary: Taiwan announced plans to ship oil from Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports. The Middle East supplied nearly 70 percent of Taiwan's oil imports in 2025, with Saudi Arabia alone accounting for almost 29 percent.

stories.title: ‘I’m very upset’: Trump says US tried to arm Iranian protesters, but guns were diverted
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the US attempted to supply weapons to Iranian protesters, but the arms were diverted. Trump initially blamed Kurdish groups for taking the guns and warned that a certain group of people would pay a big price for the diversion.

stories.title: NATO’s generals warn of war by 2029. Europe won’t be ready until 2035.
stories.summary: NATO military leaders have warned that a major war could occur by 2029, but European nations are not expected to be defense-ready until 2035. Analysts describe the gap between the threat timeline and the readiness timeline as a critical vulnerability window.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russian attack on Odesa kills three, including child, and injures 18
stories.summary: A nighttime Russian attack on the city of Odesa killed three people, including a child, and wounded 18 others, according to President Zelensky.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu ousts top aide after he allegedly made racist remarks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed his chief of staff, Ziv Agmon, after leaked comments in which Agmon allegedly referred to Jews of Moroccan descent as "baboons" and disparaged members of Netanyahu's Likud party. Ido Norden has been named as Agmon's successor.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz: are France and Germany just out to ‘manage their irrelevance’?
stories.summary: France and Germany have intensified diplomatic efforts to contain fallout from the Middle East oil crisis linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Analysts say the European push is more about damage control than a genuine leadership bid, given both nations' security dependence on the United States.

stories.title: Watch: Israel confirms U.S.-Israeli strikes kill Iran Guards intelligence chief
stories.summary: Israel's Defence Minister confirmed that a joint U.S.-Israeli strike in Tehran killed Majid Khademi, the intelligence chief of Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps. Iran condemned the attack as a "terrorist attack" and blamed both Israel and the United States. The killing is the latest in a series of strikes targeting senior Iranian leadership since late February.

stories.title: Trump threatens to take out Iran in 'one night' if no deal before deadline
stories.summary: President Trump has threatened to destroy Iran 'in one night' if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy route, before his self-imposed Tuesday deadline.

stories.title: 'They're animals': Trump doubles down on threat to destroy Iran's critical infrastructure
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump reiterated threats to destroy Iran's critical infrastructure, dismissing suggestions that such actions could constitute war crimes. He used dehumanizing language to describe Iranian leaders.

stories.title: Iran rejects latest ceasefire proposal as Trump deadline approaches
stories.summary: Iran rejected the latest U.S. ceasefire proposal as President Donald Trump's deadline approaches. Trump's deadline centers on Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately one-fifth of the world's oil is shipped during peacetime.

stories.title: What US rescue of shot down pilot means for Hormuz, Kharg, potential invasions in Iran - analysis
stories.summary: Analysts are examining whether the successful US rescue of a shot-down pilot in Iran could increase the likelihood of President Trump approving a ground invasion of the Strait of Hormuz area or Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal.

stories.title: News live: Trump says Australia ‘didn’t help’ with Iran war; ‘increasing’ cyclone threat for Queensland
stories.summary: President Trump criticized Australia, Japan, and South Korea for not assisting with the Iran conflict. Separately, Australia's Bureau of Meteorology warned that Tropical Cyclone Maila has an increasing chance of hitting far north Queensland this weekend, weeks after Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle struck the same area.

stories.title: Trump says Iran can be taken out in one night, reveals details on fighter pilots' rescue mission
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to unleash devastating strikes on Tehran if Iran did not agree to a deal by Tuesday to reopen traffic through a vital global energy shipping route. He claimed Iran could be 'taken out in one night' and disclosed details of the fighter pilot rescue mission.

stories.title: Trump operating in a 'carnival framework' that allows rule-breaking in domestic and foreign policy
stories.summary: FRANCE 24 discussed President Trump's mixed messaging during the Iran conflict with Lisa Gaufman of the University of Groningen. Gaufman, author of "The Trump Carnival," described Trump as operating within a "carnival framework" that enables rule-breaking in both domestic and foreign policy.

stories.title: Trump says US could charge for Strait of Hormuz passage amid Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Washington has a 'concept' for charging tolls on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, framing the US as the 'winner' of the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: ‘No objectives being met’: Lapid, opposition slam Netanyahu for war conduct, lack of strategy
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu's conduct of the war, saying no objectives are being met. Lapid, who initially supported Netanyahu at the conflict's outset, stated he could no longer maintain that position.

stories.title: Iran 'objecting to any kind of ceasefire', diplomat says
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Armenia, Khalil Shirgolami, said Tehran is objecting to any ceasefire proposals floated by the Trump administration, arguing the US lacks the battlefield position to impose preconditions.

stories.title: California county records sixth person bitten by rattlesnake in just under a month
stories.summary: A sixth person was bitten by a rattlesnake in southern California's Ventura County in under a month, with two fatalities reported in the region so far. Warmer spring temperatures are believed to be bringing rattlesnakes onto trails earlier than usual. The latest victim was bitten near California State University Channel Islands.

stories.title: Israel to sell PULS systems to Greece for $750 million
stories.summary: Israel has agreed to sell its PULS rocket artillery systems to Greece in a deal worth approximately $750 million. The agreement includes dozens of launchers and rockets, reflecting deepening defense ties between the two countries in the Eastern Mediterranean.

stories.title: Nine policemen sentenced to death in India over Covid custody killings
stories.summary: A court in India sentenced nine policemen to death for the custody killings of a father and son who died in jail in 2020 after being arrested on suspicion of breaching Covid lockdown rules.

stories.title: Russia provided Iran with list of Israeli energy targets, Ukrainian intelligence finds - exclusive
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reportedly found that Russia provided Iran with a categorized list of Israeli energy targets, divided into three tiers based on strategic importance.

stories.title: Why is Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant being attacked?
stories.summary: Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant has come under attack, prompting the World Health Organization to warn of 'catastrophic' risks should radioactive material be released from the facility.

stories.title: Protesters swarm US embassy in Tel Aviv, demanding end of wars
stories.summary: Protesters gathered outside the US embassy in Tel Aviv, demanding an end to the wars involving Iran and Lebanon. The demonstration reflected growing public pressure over the ongoing regional conflicts.

stories.title: Former Russian governor gets 14-year prison sentence for taking bribes tied to border fortifications
stories.summary: A court in Kursk sentenced former regional Governor Alexei Smirnov to 14 years in a maximum-security prison and fined him 400 million rubles for accepting bribes connected to border fortification contracts.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers fire tear gas at Palestinian youth during raid in Hebron
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted a raid on the Muslim Youth Association in the West Bank city of Hebron, firing tear gas at Palestinian youth during the operation.

stories.title: General Atomics pauses drone wingman flight tests after crash
stories.summary: General Atomics paused flight tests of its drone wingman prototype after a crash. The company is competing for the U.S. Air Force's collaborative combat aircraft program.

stories.title: Iran, U.S. Reject Cease-Fire Proposals
stories.summary: Both Iran and the United States rejected cease-fire proposals as tensions escalated. President Trump issued a 24-hour ultimatum for Tehran to agree to a peace deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face massive military strikes against Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Government simplifies modernization of aviation to combat Shahed-type drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers has simplified procedures for modernizing aircraft to counter Iranian-designed Shahed-type drones, streamlining the re-equipping process for the country's aviation forces.

stories.title: Israel attacks Iran's South Pars gas field again
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes struck two petrochemical plants in Iran's South Pars gas field complex, marking the second time Israel has targeted the key energy site since the war began. The previous attack on March 18 prompted Iranian retaliatory strikes on regional energy infrastructure. Pakistan has offered public transport subsidies to cushion the impact of the energy crisis.

stories.title: Four members of the Gershovitz family identified as victims of Haifa missile attack
stories.summary: Four members of the Gershovitz family were identified among the victims of a missile attack on the Israeli city of Haifa. The dead include veteran acting teacher Lena Ostrovsky Gershovitz, her husband Vladimir, son Dimitri, and his wife Lucille Jane.

stories.title: Unpacking viral theories: Censorship, Mojtaba missing, and death hoaxes
stories.summary: Analysts examined viral claims circulating online related to Israel and the war, including censorship allegations, rumors about Mojtaba Khamenei's disappearance, and death hoaxes. The report debunked several of the most widely shared theories.

stories.title: Ogra, PSO come under fire for poor monitoring of oil stocks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority and Pakistan State Oil faced criticism in Islamabad for inadequate online monitoring and automation of petroleum stock and supply data. The cabinet committee responded by deciding to activate law enforcement and investigation agencies to monitor retail petroleum outlets and counter hoarding.

stories.title: Hormuz closure divides the fortunes of Middle Eastern oil states
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected Middle Eastern oil-producing states differently depending on their geographic positions. Countries with alternative export routes have fared better than those dependent on transit through the strait.

stories.title: F-15s assassinated Khamenei, now hunting Iran ballistic missiles, Air Force base chief tells 'Post'
stories.summary: The chief of Israel's Hatzerim Air Force Base revealed that F-15 fighter jets were used in the operation that killed Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei and are now being deployed to hunt Iranian ballistic missile crews despite ongoing air defense threats.

stories.title: Murmansk governor confirms Russian general killed in An-26 crash in Crimea
stories.summary: Murmansk Governor Andrei Chibis confirmed that Lieutenant General Alexander Otroshchenko was among those killed when an An-26 military transport plane crashed in Russian-occupied Crimea on March 31. There were no survivors.

stories.title: Russia jails former Kursk governor in Ukraine incursion-linked graft probe
stories.summary: A Russian court sentenced former Kursk Governor Alexei Smirnov to prison after finding him guilty of accepting bribes from companies contracted to build fortifications along the Ukraine border, in a graft case linked to Ukraine's incursion into the region.

stories.title: 2 dead, including pregnant woman, in Russia flooding
stories.summary: Two people, including a pregnant woman, died in flooding in the Derbent district of Dagestan, Russia, according to the TASS news agency citing the republic's emergency medicine center.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts reach farther from Earth than any humans in history
stories.summary: The four astronauts aboard NASA's Artemis II Orion capsule surpassed the Apollo 13 distance record while looping around the moon, traveling more than 250,000 miles from Earth.

stories.title: Netanyahu said to ask Trump not to move forward with Iran ceasefire at this stage
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly asked President Trump not to proceed with a ceasefire with Iran at this stage. Netanyahu raised the issue while congratulating Trump on the rescue of the downed US airman, and Israel's cabinet was told a truce with Iran would not halt its ground operation in Lebanon.

stories.title: Russian shelling of Dnipropetrovsk region leaves ten people injured
