stories.title: Bombing of Iran's pharma producers threatens patients' lives
stories.summary: Ongoing US and Israeli airstrikes on Iranian pharmaceutical and medical facilities are disrupting access to essential medications. Doctors and activists warn that thousands of patients are being denied critical medical treatment as a result.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Ukraine's Odesa kills three, regional governor says
stories.summary: Russia launched a drone attack on the Ukrainian Black Sea port city of Odesa overnight on Monday, killing three people including a child. The regional governor reported damage to infrastructure, residential buildings, and administrative buildings.

stories.title: Polymarket criticized over ‘disgusting’ bets on fate of pilots on US jet shot by Iran
stories.summary: Polymarket, an online betting platform, stopped accepting wagers on when US warplane crew members shot down by Iranian forces would be rescued after criticism from Democratic Representative Seth Moulton. The Massachusetts congressman and Iraq war veteran condemned the bets as disgraceful.

stories.title: US Army wants new grenade launcher, ammunition to be able to destroy drones
stories.summary: The US Army is seeking prototype submissions for a new grenade launcher and specialized ammunition capable of destroying drones. The solicitation calls for 16 weapons, fire control systems, and approximately 25,000 rounds of ammunition.

stories.title: South Korea to send ships to Saudi Red Sea port to avoid Hormuz
stories.summary: South Korea announced plans to send five ships to the Saudi Arabian Red Sea port of Yanbu to establish alternative oil supply routes, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing tensions in the waterway.

stories.title: Israel says it killed leader of IRGC Quds Force undercover unit
stories.summary: Israel's military spokesperson announced the assassination of Asghar Barkeri, identified as the leader of an undercover unit within the IRGC Quds Force. Iran has not commented on the claim.

stories.title: UK police arrest protesters outside base linked to US jet downed in Iran
stories.summary: British police arrested protesters outside RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, a US military base in the UK. Analysts believe an F-15E fighter jet shot down over Iran was likely based at the facility.

stories.title: Woman killed and three others wounded in Kherson due to shelling by Russian forces
stories.summary: Russian troops shelled the Korabelnyi district of Kherson on the morning of April 6, killing an older woman and wounding three other women.

stories.title: DR Congo agrees to take deportees from the US
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo agreed to accept deportees from the United States beginning this month. Congolese authorities have not disclosed how many deportees they will receive.

stories.title: Russia listed Ivory Coast as a “promising country” for influence operations — then ran four anti-Ukraine campaigns there in five months
stories.summary: Leaked documents from a Russian influence network called "The Company," analyzed by France 24, reveal that Moscow identified Ivory Coast as a target and conducted four anti-Ukraine disinformation campaigns there within five months in 2024.

stories.title: China Signals Readiness to Extend Visa-Free Regime for Russians
stories.summary: China signaled its readiness to extend a visa-free regime for Russian citizens. Beijing had lifted visa requirements for Russians in a one-year trial program allowing 30-day visa-free visits.

stories.title: Pakistan’s peace plan a ‘critical opportunity’ for US-Iran talks ahead of Trump deadline
stories.summary: Pakistan proposed an immediate ceasefire plan ahead of President Trump's Tuesday deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The plan was brokered through contacts between Pakistani army chief Asim Munir, US Vice President J.D. Vance, and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

stories.title: Iranian Kurds deny receiving US weapons to arm Iran's protesters
stories.summary: Several Iranian Kurdish party leaders denied receiving US weapons after President Trump claimed Washington sent guns to Iranian protesters through the Kurds. PJAK senior figure Siamand Moeini explicitly rejected the claim.

stories.title: Two separate Israeli espionage cases uncover Iran-linked activities in Jerusalem, Ashkelon
stories.summary: Israeli authorities uncovered two separate espionage cases in Jerusalem and Ashkelon involving suspects linked to Iranian intelligence, including explosive material production and digital recruitment operations.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Triggers Fire at Key Russian Black Sea Oil Terminal – Reports
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack reportedly started a fire at a key Russian oil terminal on the Black Sea. The strike targeted infrastructure critical to Moscow's energy revenues amid surging global oil prices linked to the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Iran executes man over attack on military site during January protests, Mizan reports
stories.summary: Iran executed a man in connection with an attack on a military site during January protests, according to the Mizan news agency. Three other individuals linked to the same incident had already been executed.

stories.title: Ukraine Hits Major Oil Terminal in Southern Russia – Moscow
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Sheskharis oil terminal in southern Russia, the latest in a series of attacks on energy infrastructure. The strike comes as global oil prices have surged amid the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: “There are no small literatures”: an American scholar on Ukraine’s battle for culture and truth
stories.summary: American scholar Andrew Giarelli discussed Ukraine's struggle to preserve its culture and convey the truth about the war, arguing that simply showing atrocities does not effectively move audiences and exploring alternative approaches.

stories.title: Why KMT leader’s planned visit to Beijing is under scrutiny in Taiwan
stories.summary: KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun is set to depart for mainland China on a six-day trip, with reports of a possible meeting with Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping in Beijing. The visit, the first high-level KMT-CCP encounter in a decade, is drawing scrutiny in Taiwan over cross-strait implications.

stories.title: Russians use “cannon fodder attacks” to hide problems from command, says paratrooper
stories.summary: A Russian paratrooper stated that Russian army units conduct so-called "cannon fodder attacks" to conceal operational problems from higher command and attempt to resolve them independently.

stories.title: Zambia: Government declares fuel supply situation an emergency
stories.summary: The Zambian government declared its fuel supply situation an emergency as the ongoing war in the Middle East continues to drive up global fuel prices.

stories.title: The US could still try to play the ethnic card in Iran
stories.summary: Analysts examine the possibility of the United States exploiting ethnic divisions within Iran as a strategic tool, concluding that historical precedent and current geopolitical conditions make such an approach unlikely to succeed.

stories.title: Jobless young Palestinians trapped as Israel holds Gaza’s economy hostage
stories.summary: In Gaza, approximately 80 percent of young Palestinians are unemployed as the Israeli blockade continues to cause widespread economic collapse, leaving the population struggling to meet basic needs.

stories.title: Israel strikes Iran's petrochemical complex at Asaluyeh, defence minister says
stories.summary: Israel struck Iran's largest petrochemical complex at Asaluyeh, according to Defence Minister Israel Katz. Explosions were reported at the South Pars facility, though Iran's Tasnim agency said the main Pars petrochemical company was not damaged.

stories.title: ‘Smell’ of war comes to St Petersburg as Ukraine hammers Russian refineries
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck oil facilities at Pokrovsk and Ust-Luga on Russia's Baltic Sea coast, targeting refineries in a campaign to reduce Russian energy revenues. Residents of St. Petersburg reportedly noticed the effects of nearby attacks.

stories.title: South Korea says ‘credible intelligence’ indicates Kim Jong Un’s daughter is his successor
stories.summary: South Korea's National Intelligence Service assessed that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's teenage daughter has been designated as his successor. The NIS cited credible intelligence, including a recent public display of the daughter driving a tank, as evidence of her positioning.

stories.title: WHO worker among seven killed by Israel in Gaza bombing
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit a UN vehicle carrying WHO staff in Gaza, killing a WHO worker and at least six other Palestinians. The attack occurred amid ongoing ceasefire violations.

stories.title: How US operation to rescue air officer from Iran unfolded
stories.summary: The US military conducted two raids to rescue an American service member whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran. President Trump confirmed the operation and the recovery of the air officer.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russians launch more than 2,800 drones and 1,350 guided bombs at Ukraine over past week
stories.summary: President Zelensky reported that Russian forces launched more than 2,800 attack drones, nearly 1,350 guided bombs, and over 40 missiles of various types at Ukraine over the past week.

stories.title: Improving neighbourly relations: US-Mexico border authorities close the door
stories.summary: President Trump has escalated rhetoric against Mexico, branding it a narco-state and threatening unilateral military action over drug trafficking and illegal immigration. Correspondents report from the Mexican side of the border on conditions amid tightened US-Mexico border enforcement.

stories.title: Murmansk Governor Confirms Russian Navy General’s Death in Crimea Plane Crash
stories.summary: The governor of Murmansk confirmed that a Russian Navy general was among the 29 people killed when an Antonov An-26 military transport plane crashed into a cliff near Sevastopol, Crimea, on March 31.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills two medical workers in south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike directly targeted a medical crew in Haris, in southern Lebanon's Bint Jbeil district, killing two medics and seriously injuring a third, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: In closing airspace to US, Europe opens an existential debate over Nato
stories.summary: Several European nations refused to support Washington's campaign to unblock the Strait of Hormuz, with some closing their airspace to US military operations. President Trump warned the US could leave NATO unless allies aligned with his Iran policy, prompting NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte to plan a stabilizing visit to Washington.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Ukraine’s Odesa kills three, Regional Governor says
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Odesa killed three people, according to the regional governor. Odesa, Ukraine's largest port and a key logistics hub for grain exports, has faced escalating Russian strikes as the war enters its fifth year.

stories.title: He was once a migrant himself. Now he jailed for stealing Ukrainian flag and smashing car — because he hated that refugees “take our jobs”
stories.summary: A Lithuanian court sentenced a rideshare driver to 90 days in jail for stealing a Ukrainian flag and vandalizing a car selected because of its Ukrainian license plates. The driver, himself a former migrant, expressed resentment toward refugees.

stories.title: Iranian missile attack on Israel's Haifa kills four
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck the city of Haifa in northern Israel on Sunday, killing at least four people. Iran said the attack was carried out in retaliation for continued Israeli strikes on Iranian territory.

stories.title: Israel ramps up Arrow interceptor production amid reports of depleted stockpile
stories.summary: Israel's Defense Ministry signed a deal with Israel Aerospace Industries to substantially increase production of Arrow interceptor missiles. Defence Minister Katz denied reports that Israel's interceptor stockpile had been depleted during the war with Iran.

stories.title: German mayors call for night-time ban on robot lawnmowers to protect hedgehogs
stories.summary: German mayors have called for a nationwide ban on nighttime use of robot lawnmowers to protect hedgehogs and other small nocturnal animals. Studies show the devices' blades pose serious risks to wildlife active between dusk and dawn, especially hedgehogs that curl up rather than flee.

stories.title: Singapore’s Shanmugam on deported blogger Amos Yee: ‘I wish the Americans had kept him’
stories.summary: Singapore's Home Affairs Minister K. Shanmugam said he wished the US had kept Amos Yee, a blogger and convicted child sex offender deported back to the city-state. Yee, listed among the "worst of the worst criminal aliens" by the US Department of Homeland Security, was deported on March 19.

stories.title: UAE says the use of Hormuz must be guaranteed in any US-Iran deal
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates stated that any US-Iran ceasefire deal must guarantee freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and address Tehran's nuclear program, missiles, and drones to avoid further regional instability.

stories.title: Kenya: Abdullahi, Kipkorir Call for Private Sector Arrests Amid Probe On Off-Spec Fuel
stories.summary: Kenyan lawyers Ahmednassir Abdullahi and Donald Kipkorir called on the government to arrest private-sector figures implicated in a fuel cartel scandal involving off-specification fuel, arguing accountability should extend beyond public officials.

stories.title: “Aggression cannot be normalized through sport”: Ukraine wins landmark chess ruling at CAS
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Russia cannot hold chess tournaments in occupied Ukrainian territory. Moscow announced it would ignore the ruling, which could lead to a three-year suspension from FIDE.

stories.title: Malawi: Malawi Earns Global Acclaim for SRH Gains
stories.summary: Malawi has received global recognition for progress in adolescent sexual and reproductive health, with new evidence ranking it among Africa's top performers. However, experts warn that deep-rooted challenges could undermine these gains.

stories.title: Živković: UNDP supports removal of over 1 million tons of debris in Ukraine
stories.summary: UNDP official Živković stated that the United Nations Development Program has supported the removal of over one million tons of debris in Ukraine caused by Russian attacks, calling debris clearance a key recovery challenge.

stories.title: North Korea working on carbon-fibre ICBM for multi-warhead delivery, Seoul says
stories.summary: South Korea's intelligence agency reported that North Korea is developing a carbon-fibre intercontinental ballistic missile capable of delivering multiple warheads. In March, North Korea conducted a ground test of a solid-fuel rocket engine believed to be linked to the new ICBM program.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Launches First Offshore Oil Drilling Campaign
stories.summary: The Somali federal government officially launched its first offshore oil drilling campaign, which officials described as carrying major economic and geopolitical significance.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Defense Minister Visits Army Positions Outside Baidoa City
stories.summary: Somali Defense Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi and army commander Brigadier General Ibrahim Mohamed Mahmoud visited military positions outside the southwestern city of Baidoa.

stories.title: Nigeria: Police Express Concern Over Masked Security Personnel Protecting Vips
stories.summary: Nigerian police expressed concern over masked security personnel protecting VIPs, warning that such practices threaten public safety and undermine trust, accountability, and inter-agency collaboration.

stories.title: Qatar’s LNG tankers idle across Asia as export plant stays shut
stories.summary: Qatari liquefied natural gas tankers are sitting idle across Asian waters, including east of Singapore, after a major export facility remained shut down.

stories.title: Iran warns of ‘more devastating’ response as strikes kill 34
stories.summary: Tehran vowed a more devastating response after US-Israeli strikes killed at least 34 people in Iran, warning of escalation if President Trump follows through on threats to target civilian infrastructure ahead of a Tuesday deadline.

stories.title: IDF Nahal Brigade kills Hezbollah terrorists responsible for murdering four soldiers
stories.summary: The IDF's Nahal Brigade killed Hezbollah operatives responsible for the deaths of four Nahal Reconnaissance Battalion soldiers — Captain Noam Madmoni, Staff-Sergeant Ben Cohen, Staff-Sergeant Maxsim Entis, and Staff-Sergeant Gilad Harel — who were killed the previous week.

stories.title: EV battery tech gives Ukraine’s fixed-wing drones a 46% range boost — and a Buk-M1 scalp
stories.summary: Ukraine's PAWELL fixed-wing drone extended its range from 30 km to 197 km by incorporating electric-vehicle battery technology. The drone destroyed a Russian Buk-M1 air defense system and struck an ammunition depot, with developers targeting a 400 km range next.

stories.title: Kurdish Iranian groups deny receiving guns from US following Fox report
stories.summary: Kurdish Iranian opposition groups denied receiving weapons from the United States following media reports, amid concerns that such claims could provoke further Iranian drone and missile attacks against them.

stories.title: Somalia set for 'historic' first offshore oil drilling
stories.summary: Somalia is preparing for its first offshore oil drilling operation, described as historic. A Turkish government-owned drilling ship is expected to arrive in Somali waters later this week.

stories.title: Saudi oasis town adjusts to life in the firing line
stories.summary: A Saudi oasis town is adjusting to being in the line of fire amid the broader regional conflict. The presence of U.S. military forces in Saudi Arabia has been a source of contention.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Christian party official in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on an apartment in Ain Saadeh, east of Beirut, killed a local official from a Christian political party on Sunday, deepening internal Lebanese divisions over Hezbollah as Israel expands its targeting.

stories.title: Nigeria: Bandits Kill Police Officer, Burn Health Centre in Katsina Communities
stories.summary: Bandits attacked communities in Katsina State, Nigeria, killing a police officer and burning a primary healthcare centre in Sayaya town. The attackers also looted and set fire to several shops during the early morning raid.

stories.title: Has Trump confirmed Iran’s claim that protesters were US-armed?
stories.summary: President Trump stated that the US sent weapons to Kurdish Iranian opposition groups during January protests in Iran. The claim appeared to confirm allegations previously made by Tehran about foreign-armed demonstrators.

stories.title: ‘Not the Cairo we know’: Energy shock from Iran war dims Egypt nights
stories.summary: Egypt is experiencing an energy crisis linked to the war in Iran, leading to early business closures and dimmed lighting in Cairo. Critics say the measures are disproportionately affecting workers and businesses in the informal economy.

stories.title: Russians attack Chernihiv region with drones; two people injured
stories.summary: In a village in the Mryn community of Chernihiv region, Russian drone attacks injured two people and damaged civilian homes and vehicles.

stories.title: Iran threatens Bab al-Mandeb closure: How would that affect world trade?
stories.summary: Iran has threatened to close the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Analysts warn that a simultaneous closure of both Bab al-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz could block approximately a quarter of global energy supplies.

stories.title: Is Trump the president who lost Asia to China?
stories.summary: Amid the ongoing crisis, Beijing is increasingly viewed by some Asian nations as a less risky partner compared with the United States under President Trump's leadership, raising questions about shifting geopolitical influence in the region.

stories.title: Sweden to provide Ukraine with Tridon Mk2 air defense systems to combat “suicide drones”
stories.summary: Sweden announced a €400 million allocation to supply Ukraine with Tridon Mk2 air defense systems designed to counter Shahed-type drones. The systems can fire up to 300 rounds per minute and have a range of 12 kilometers.

stories.title: Bitcoin ticks up even as Trump’s Iran war threats cloud markets
stories.summary: Bitcoin showed relative stability compared with other asset classes even as U.S. President Trump's threats related to the Iran war created uncertainty across global financial markets.

stories.title: Iran says US airman rescue may have been cover to 'steal enriched uranium'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry alleged that a US operation to rescue a downed F-15E airman may have been a cover to steal enriched uranium. Iran's military called the operation a failed deception and escape mission.

stories.title: SBU general who ran Russia’s Kherson filtration ops dies
stories.summary: Former SBU major general Lyapkin, who oversaw Russian filtration operations in occupied Kherson Oblast, was killed on March 17, 2026, while fighting on the Russian side.

stories.title: Hong Kong restaurant revenues drop over Easter break as departures outnumber arrivals
stories.summary: Hong Kong restaurants saw a 6 to 7 percent revenue decline over the Easter weekend despite a 15 percent increase in mainland Chinese tourists. Approximately 1.7 million local residents departed Hong Kong during the holiday, a trend industry leaders described as the new normal.

stories.title: EU Ambassador finds Shahed UAV debris during walk in Kyiv forest
stories.summary: EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarína Mathernová discovered debris from a Russian Shahed-type drone while walking in a forest near Kyiv.

stories.title: Thailand PM calls for energy saving as Middle East conflict drives price surge
stories.summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul urged the public to conserve energy by working from home and carpooling amid surging oil prices driven by the Middle East conflict. He warned that Thailand's heavy reliance on imported oil and gas leaves the country highly exposed to the crisis.

stories.title: Mauritius: Slavery - 'The Gravest Crime Against Humanity'
stories.summary: The United Nations passed a resolution on March 25, 2026, affirming chattel slavery and the trafficking of Africans as "the gravest crime against humanity" and calling for reparatory justice. The resolution was supported by 123 countries, while 52 abstained.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran ramps up attacks after Trump warning; Israeli strike kills 25 in Iran
stories.summary: Iran launched a barrage of missile and drone strikes hitting Israel, Kuwait, and the UAE on April 6. An Iranian presidential spokesperson stated the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only after Iran receives compensation for war damages. An Israeli strike killed 25 people in Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan offers ‘two-phased’ truce deal to end US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan presented a two-phased ceasefire proposal to end the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. Tehran is reviewing the plan but has rejected reopening the Strait of Hormuz as part of any temporary ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Israeli rescuers search for missing in building strike by Iranian missile, two dead
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck a building in Israel, killing at least two people. Israel's Magen David Adom emergency service reported four wounded, including a 10-month-old baby with a head injury.

stories.title: Oil smugglers, hoarders in Thailand worsen supply crisis as Anutin warns of tough times
stories.summary: Oil smuggling, hoarding, and underground stockpiling in Thailand have worsened a fuel supply crisis as diesel prices hit a record high of about 50 baht per liter. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul warned conditions would deteriorate further given the country's dependence on fuel imports.

stories.title: Katz, IDF: We assassinated IRGC intelligence chief Majid Khademi
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz and the IDF confirmed they assassinated IRGC Intelligence Organization chief Majid Khademi in strikes targeting Iran's Islamic regime.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Bridge Day’ threat: Can a last-ditch ceasefire plan work?
stories.summary: Mediators Pakistan, Turkey, and Egypt proposed a 45-day ceasefire plan to avert further escalation before a US 'Bridge Day' deadline. Iran has expressed reluctance to accept the terms.

stories.title: Iraq urges customers to send oil loading plans after Hormuz exemption
stories.summary: Iraq's state oil marketer asked customers to submit crude oil lifting schedules within one day after reports that Iran granted transit exemptions through the Strait of Hormuz for Iraqi shipments.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 6: Court, MKs battle over wartime restrictions on protests vs. prayers
stories.summary: Israeli political correspondent Sam Sokol discussed tensions between Israel's High Court and Knesset members over wartime restrictions on protests and prayers, including backlash to a court order permitting an anti-war rally.

stories.title: Real Madrid vs Bayern Munich: Champions League – team news, start, lineups
stories.summary: Real Madrid hosted Bayern Munich at home for the first leg of their UEFA Champions League quarterfinal. Both clubs entered the match as reigning domestic league champions.

stories.title: At least 45 dead, including 23 children, in North-West Pakistan in rain-related incidents
stories.summary: At least 45 people, including 23 children, died in rain-related incidents across northwest Pakistan. The Provincial Disaster Management Authority forecast continued rainfall across the region through April 9.

stories.title: Why did Iran war not affect China’s energy security so far?
stories.summary: China has so far insulated its energy security from the Iran war by diversifying its energy sources and consumption patterns, reducing dependence on any single supplier in the Middle East.

stories.title: Russians attack energy facility in Odesa region; DTEK reports severe damage
stories.summary: An energy facility in the Odesa region sustained severe damage during a Russian attack on the night of April 6. Energy company DTEK reported the damage.

stories.title: Iran rejects deadlines, any immediate move to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Tehran rejected any immediate move to reopen the Strait of Hormuz despite an approaching US deadline. Pakistan's army chief mediated between US and Iranian officials over a proposed framework to end the five-week-old war.

stories.title: Free Trade Is Dead in Washington
stories.summary: A bipartisan shift in Washington has moved US trade policy away from free trade principles, with both parties increasingly focused on countering China. The trend extends beyond the Trump administration's tariff actions to reflect a broader consensus in Congress.

stories.title: Man from Bedouin town Segev Shalom stabbed to death in nearby Ofakim; 5 arrested
stories.summary: Marei al-Dabari, 36, from the Bedouin town of Segev Shalom was stabbed to death in nearby Ofakim in a suspected inter-family clash. Five suspects were arrested. Arab Israeli homicide victims in 2026 have risen 30 percent compared to the same period in 2025.

stories.title: ‘A surrender to special interests’: alarm as Utah shields fossil-fuel companies
stories.summary: Utah has enacted legislation making it nearly impossible for residents to hold fossil fuel companies legally accountable for climate-related damages. Critics say the law prioritizes polluters' profits over public health. Other states are expected to pursue similar measures.

stories.title: AI at war l What to know about Project Maven
stories.summary: Project Maven, a U.S. Department of Defense artificial-intelligence program, has been used to accelerate the targeting and firing process in sustained American air strikes, streamlining the military's kill chain.

stories.title: 4.7-magnitude earthquake off Lebanon coast felt in northern Israel
stories.summary: A 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Lebanon, west of Tyre, and was felt in northern Israel, including the city of Nahariya. No injuries or damage were reported.

stories.title: China moves to expand role in Iran war diplomacy; U.S. seems sceptical
stories.summary: China, together with Pakistan, put forward a five-point diplomatic proposal aimed at ending the conflict in West Asia, seeking backing from Gulf nations and opposing a UN move concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Washington has expressed skepticism about Beijing's mediation efforts.

stories.title: Kenya: Turkana Disarmament - 26 Firearms Surrendered As Community Cooperation Grows
stories.summary: Twenty-six firearms were surrendered during an ongoing disarmament exercise in Turkana County, Kenya. Authorities noted growing community cooperation with the voluntary disarmament campaign in the region.

stories.title: Nigeria: Low Spending - Manufacturers Shun Dealers, Now Deal Directly With Consumers
stories.summary: Nigerian manufacturers are increasingly bypassing dealers and selling directly to consumers in response to prolonged low consumer spending. The shift reflects the sustained pressure on supply chains caused by declining purchasing power.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike hits building near Iran’s capital, at least 25 killed
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck a building near Tehran and targeted the Sharif University of Technology in the Iranian capital, killing at least 25 people. Israel's military confirmed it had completed a wave of strikes against targets in Tehran.

stories.title: Nigeria: 33 Banks Now Bigger, Stronger
stories.summary: Thirty-three Nigerian deposit money banks raised a combined N44.65 trillion through a recapitalisation exercise led by the Central Bank of Nigeria. The regulator framed the capital-base upgrades as essential for economic stability amid a complex global financial landscape.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Frigate Admiral Grigorovich, launching its air defense missiles at drones in Russia’s primary Black Sea port (VIDEO)
stories.summary: Ukraine struck the Russian frigate Admiral Grigorovich while it was launching air defense missiles at drones at Russia's primary Black Sea port. The vessel is known for carrying missiles used in strikes on Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Nigeria: New Tax Law - Nrs Takes Over Collection of Mineral Royalties
stories.summary: The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has assumed responsibility for collecting mineral royalties from mining operators across the country, following the enactment of a new tax law transferring the function to the agency.

stories.title: Nigeria: Us-Iran Conflict - Man Outlines Measures to Mitigate Effect On Nigerian Manufacturers
stories.summary: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) warned that escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pose severe risks to Nigeria's manufacturing sector. The association outlined urgent measures to mitigate effects on industry operators, including supply-chain and energy-cost disruptions.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz Sharif ‘deeply’ concerned after 3 Pakistani nationals injured in UAE amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed concern after three Pakistani nationals were injured at Khor Fakkan port in the UAE during a missile interception. Gulf states including the UAE have faced attacks amid Iran's retaliatory campaign against the US-Israeli military operations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Easter Tragedy - Herders, Terrorists Kill 16 in Benue, Kaduna
stories.summary: At least 16 people were killed in separate attacks by herders and armed groups in Benue and Kaduna states during Easter celebrations in Nigeria. The violence prompted calls for strengthened security measures in the affected communities.

stories.title: Back in Berlin - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: This is a sponsored content piece about two friends traveling to Berlin to research their family histories during World War II. It is not a conflict or security news article.

stories.title: Trump accused of ‘threatening possible war crimes’ in Iran post | First Thing
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump faced sharp criticism, including from Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer, after threatening to destroy Iran's power plants and bridges in a social media post. Iran's parliament speaker responded by warning that such actions would set the entire region ablaze.

stories.title: Are Iraqi militias crossing into Iran to support Iran's war effort? - analysis
stories.summary: Analysis examines reports that Iraqi militia forces may be crossing into Iran to support the IRGC's war effort, potentially serving as reinforcements or being used to enforce order in peripheral areas of Iran.

stories.title: Floods kill 3 in Russia, thousands evacuated after dam wall breaks in Dagestan
stories.summary: Three people died and approximately 4,000 were evacuated after a dam wall broke in Russia's Dagestan republic following heavy rain. Around 2,000 homes in the Derbent region on the Caspian Sea were flooded, and searches continued for missing persons.

stories.title: Israel destroys southern Lebanon towns, hits ‘safe’ areas around Beirut
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched new strikes on southern Lebanon towns and areas around Beirut designated as safe zones, deepening the humanitarian crisis in the country.

stories.title: Protecting water supply systems: UNDP describes its work in Ukraine
stories.summary: The United Nations Development Program is working in Ukraine to protect water supply and sanitation systems, applying global expertise to address war-related damage to critical infrastructure.

stories.title: In photos: Aftermath of Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Photographs documented widespread destruction across Beirut neighborhoods including Bir Hassan and Jnah following Israeli strikes on April 6, 2026, amid the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Was Trump ignorant to the realities of Netanyahu’s promised ‘easy’ war on Iran?
stories.summary: The article examines whether the Trump administration was misled by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's assurances of an easy war against Iran. Senior U.S. officials reportedly believe Netanyahu overpromised when he pitched expanded military operations during a December meeting at Mar-a-Lago.

stories.title: FM Lavrov Urges U.S. to Abandon ‘Language of Ultimatums’ and Negotiate Peace With Iran
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov urged the United States to abandon the "language of ultimatums" and negotiate peace with Iran during a phone call with his Iranian counterpart. He also called on the U.S. to halt what he termed illegal attacks on civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Russia launches 141 drones across Ukraine, kills mother and toddler in Odesa
stories.summary: Russia launched 141 drones across Ukraine overnight, striking northern, southern, and eastern regions. The attack killed three people in Odesa, including a two-and-a-half-year-old girl, and left roughly 10,000 consumers without power in Chernihiv Oblast.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike kills Iran Guards intelligence chief
stories.summary: A joint U.S.-Israeli strike killed the head of intelligence of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as confirmed by the IRGC on Monday.

stories.title: Intelligence head of Iran's Revolutionary Guards killed in strike
stories.summary: Israel and the US confirmed that strikes killed Majid Khademi, the head of intelligence for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Iran says it has formulated diplomatic response to US, to announce in due course
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei announced that Tehran has formulated a diplomatic response to the US regarding the proposed 'Islamabad Accord,' which envisions an immediate ceasefire and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel approves increased production of Arrow missile interceptors for second time this year
stories.summary: Israel's ministerial committee approved a rapid increase in Arrow missile interceptor production for the second time this year, aiming to replenish stocks depleted during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: US, Iran and mediators make push for 45-day ceasefire, Axios reports
stories.summary: The United States, Iran, and mediators are pursuing a 45-day ceasefire as the first phase of a potential deal that could lead to a permanent end to the war, according to an Axios report.

stories.title: Nigeria troops rescue 31 abducted Easter worshippers in Kaduna attack
stories.summary: Nigerian military forces rescued 31 worshippers who were abducted during Easter church services in Kaduna state. The attack also left several people dead.

stories.title: Severe Tropical Cyclone Maila could hit far north Queensland three weeks after Narelle tore through
stories.summary: Australia's Bureau of Meteorology warned that Severe Tropical Cyclone Maila could strike far north Queensland's Cape York region, potentially over the weekend. The area was already hit by Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle just three weeks earlier. The storm's exact path and intensity remain uncertain.

stories.title: Liberia: 'We Are No Longer Prisoners of Fear but Carriers of Victory', Bishop Quire Declares
stories.summary: Bishop Samuel J. Quire Jr. delivered an Easter sermon at the Stephen Trowen Nagbe Memorial United Methodist Church in Monrovia, Liberia. He declared congregants "carriers of victory" rather than "prisoners of fear."

stories.title: Israeli strike hits Beirut's southern suburbs
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit Beirut's southern suburbs on Monday, with smoke seen billowing from the area. The district has been largely emptied of residents following repeated Israeli strikes and forced evacuation orders.

stories.title: Iraq urges customers to send oil loading plans after Hormuz exemption, document shows
stories.summary: Iraq has urged its oil customers to submit loading plans after receiving an exemption related to the Strait of Hormuz closure. A resumption of Iraqi oil exports could help boost Iran's production, which collapsed in March.

stories.title: ‘Not the Cairo we know’: Energy shock from Iran war dims Egypt nights
stories.summary: Egypt imposed early-closing orders on shops and cafes in Cairo to curb soaring energy costs stemming from the US-Israel war on Iran. Shops must now close by 9 PM on weekdays and 10 PM on weekends, with a brief extension expected for Coptic Easter holidays.

stories.title: Cairo goes dark as Egypt struggles to cope with fall out from Iran war
stories.summary: Egypt imposed a month-long early-closing order for shops in Cairo due to soaring fuel costs linked to the fallout from the Iran war. Shops must now close at 9 p.m. on weekdays and 10 p.m. on weekends.

stories.title: Nigeria: In Nigeria's Maiduguri, a Doctor Has a Simple Cure for Adapting to Extreme Heat
stories.summary: A doctor in Maiduguri, northeastern Nigeria, is promoting tree planting and fruit cultivation as a practical measure to help residents adapt to extreme heat while also providing affordable nutrition.

stories.title: Defiant Iran ramps up attacks after Trump warning
stories.summary: Iran intensified missile and drone attacks following a warning from U.S. President Donald Trump. Israel, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates each reported being hit by barrages of Iranian missiles and drones.

stories.title: In Odesa, injury toll after Russian attack climbs to 15, with three fatalities
stories.summary: The injury toll from an overnight Russian attack on Odesa rose to 15 people, with 13 hospitalized and three fatalities confirmed.

stories.title: Opinion: Has US war on Iran killed the 'Gulf moment'?
stories.summary: This opinion piece examines whether the US war on Iran has undermined the rising geopolitical influence of Gulf states such as the UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia, whose power rested on deep integration within the global economy.

stories.title: While Trump hails ‘daring’ airman rescue in Iran, Chinese experts count US wins and losses
stories.summary: Chinese military analysts assessed that the US rescue of a downed F-15E crew member in Iran demonstrated Washington's comprehensive capability for high-risk operations. The airman was recovered after the fighter jet was shot down over southern Iran during the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Liberia: Petrol Products Prices Hiked
stories.summary: The Liberian government announced a new price ceiling for petroleum products effective April 4, 2026, raising gasoline and diesel prices in response to global and local market fluctuations.

stories.title: Liberia: FIFA Issues Final Warning to Liberia Over Halted LFA Election
stories.summary: FIFA has issued a final warning to Liberia over third-party interference in the Liberia Football Association's electoral process, after a court injunction halted the association's elections. The world governing body expressed deep concern about what it called undue judicial interference.

stories.title: Africa: Middle East Crisis Pushes Buyers to Nigeria, Other African Producers
stories.summary: Global energy analysts predict that Nigeria and other oil-producing African countries stand to benefit from the ongoing Middle East conflict as buyers seek alternative crude oil sources.

stories.title: Nigeria: Easter - 27 Killed in Kaduna, Benue, Katsina Attacks
stories.summary: At least 25 people were killed in attacks by bandits on communities in Benue and Kaduna states in Nigeria during the Easter period. The violence struck multiple locations across the two states.

stories.title: Iran accuses UN nuclear watchdog of inaction, warns of risk from attacks
stories.summary: Iran's atomic energy chief Mohammad Eslami accused the IAEA of inaction, warning that silence emboldens attacks on nuclear facilities. He said the Bushehr nuclear power plant had been targeted four times, with the latest attack killing a staff member.

stories.title: Nigeria: INEC Suspends Voter Revalidation Exercise
stories.summary: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has directed all Resident Electoral Commissioners to suspend publicity and preparations for the voter revalidation exercise nationwide. The commission instructed officials to await further directives before proceeding.

stories.title: Tuen Mun bus operator cuts services amid soaring fuel prices, warns of closure
stories.summary: Hong Kong bus operator ABC Touring Car Company, serving Tuen Mun commuters, announced service cuts and warned of possible closure due to fuel costs more than doubling since late February. The company said soaring oil prices linked to the Iran conflict had pushed it to the brink of financial collapse.

stories.title: Iran war: South Korea aims to bypass Hormuz, send ships to Saudi port for oil
stories.summary: South Korea plans to send five Korean-flagged ships to Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu to establish alternative oil supply routes, bypassing the disrupted Strait of Hormuz. Iran has effectively closed the strait amid the US-Israeli war, threatening South Korea's oil imports, which depend on the Middle East for about 70 percent of supply.

stories.title: Small UK firms’ energy bills set to more than double due to Iran war
stories.summary: Thousands of small and medium-sized UK businesses face energy bills more than doubling due to sharp increases in heating oil costs driven by the war in Iran. About 7% of small and medium firms rely on heating oil, which has more than doubled in price in recent weeks.

stories.title: China’s Absence Draws America Deeper Into Risky Wars
stories.summary: The article argues that the absence of China as a global counterweight is drawing the United States into riskier military interventions, encouraging overreach in its foreign engagements.

stories.title: Renowned China university apologises for mini-film depicting career man, family-focused woman
stories.summary: Shanghai Jiao Tong University apologised and withdrew a mini-film celebrating its 130th anniversary after it drew accusations of gender bias. The video depicted a male graduate pursuing a career while a female graduate focused on family life.

stories.title: War update: 120 clashes on front lines, most battles occur in Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors
stories.summary: On April 5, Ukrainian Defense Forces recorded 120 combat clashes with Russian forces along the front lines, with the highest concentration of fighting in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Emergency jabs after 100 children die of suspected measles in a month in Bangladesh
stories.summary: Over 100 people, mostly children, have died from suspected measles in Bangladesh since mid-March. Authorities launched emergency vaccination campaigns in response to the outbreak.

stories.title: Trump’s Strait of Hormuz ultimatum: threat or tactic?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump issued an ultimatum giving Iran until Tuesday evening Eastern Time to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face attacks on key infrastructure. Analysts and lawmakers are divided on whether the deadline signals imminent military action or is a high-stakes pressure tactic.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Warm March in US leaves snowpack critically low
stories.summary: A historically warm March across the United States has left mountain snowpack at critically low levels in the American West, threatening water supplies for millions. Concerns about wildfire risk are growing. Meanwhile, a rare tropical cyclone has formed on the other side of the Pacific.

stories.title: Explosives found by pipeline to Hungary: PM Orban clams sabotage
stories.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić reported that army and police found two backpacks containing explosives near a gas pipeline to Hungary on Sunday. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán called an emergency meeting in response, claiming sabotage.

stories.title: Middle East conflict has no easy answers, only hard choices
stories.summary: An analysis suggests the US-Israel conflict with Iran fits a pattern of wars that begin with confident declarations but encounter prolonged, complex realities. Regional actors are hedging their positions, and the conflict shows no signs of nearing resolution.

stories.title: World Cup qualification earns Iraq coach Arnold a hero’s welcome in Sydney
stories.summary: Iraq coach Graham Arnold received a celebratory welcome from Iraqi fans upon arriving in Sydney, Australia, following a successful World Cup qualification campaign.

stories.title: AI is rewiring the world's most prolific film industry in India
stories.summary: Film studios across India are adopting artificial intelligence at an unprecedented scale, producing fully AI-generated movies, using AI-powered dubbing to release titles in multiple languages, and re-editing older films to generate additional revenue.

stories.title: Kuwait says six injured after Iranian attack on residential area
stories.summary: An Iranian attack on a residential area in northern Kuwait injured six people on Monday. Kuwait's military said its air defenses were working to intercept incoming Iranian missiles and drones.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: 15 dead in israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on south Beirut, Lebanon, killed at least 15 people and wounded 39 on Sunday.

stories.title: Defense Ministry recognizes IAF Maj. (res.) Asaf Dagan as fallen soldier after PTSD-related suicide
stories.summary: Israel's Defense Ministry officially recognized IAF Major (res.) Asaf Dagan as a fallen soldier after his PTSD-related suicide. The recognition followed a prolonged campaign by his family to acknowledge the psychological toll of his military service.

stories.title: Hamas rules out disarmament before Israel meets ceasefire terms
stories.summary: Hamas military spokesman Abu Obeida ruled out disarmament in Gaza before Israel fulfills first-phase ceasefire obligations. He also expressed support for Iran's strikes on Israel and accused mediators of pressuring Palestinian factions while ignoring Israeli violations.

stories.title: Up to 1.2 million people forced to flee as Israel pummels Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military attacks on Lebanon have displaced nearly 1.2 million people, with many families forced to flee for the second time in recent months.

stories.title: In Chernihiv region, Russians strike energy infrastructure overnight and this morning; most districts without power
stories.summary: Russian strikes on energy infrastructure in Chernihiv region overnight and into the morning of April 6 left most districts without electrical power.

stories.title: Downed US airman said to have directed strikes on Iranian positions from hiding place
stories.summary: A downed US F-15E airman reportedly directed strikes on Iranian positions from a hiding location during a 14-hour period before rescue contact was established, according to US officials.

stories.title: Head of Iran's Revolutionary Guards' intelligence organisation announced as dead, state media reports
stories.summary: Iranian state media announced the death of Majid Khademi, head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' intelligence organization, without providing additional details.

stories.title: World Cup 2026: DRC celebrates the Leopards’ historic qualification
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's national football team, the Leopards, qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It marks only their second World Cup appearance, following their sole prior participation in 1974 when the country was known as Zaire.

stories.title: US president Donald Trump warns Tehran to reopen Hormuz or face "hell"
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face severe consequences. Iran and the United States received a draft proposal on Sunday calling for a 45-day ceasefire and the reopening of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Iran struck US forces relocated on Kuwait's Bubiyan island, military spokesperson says
stories.summary: Iran's military said it struck US forces on Kuwait's Bubiyan island with drones, targeting satellite equipment and munitions. Spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari said US forces had relocated there from Arifjan camp after repeated Iranian strikes.

stories.title: Iraqis give rousing welcome to coach behind historic World Cup return
stories.summary: Iraqi supporters gathered in large numbers in Sydney to welcome national team coach Graham Arnold back to Australia after securing a historic World Cup qualification.

stories.title: U.S., Iran and mediators make push for 45-day ceasefire, Axios reports
stories.summary: The United States, Iran, and mediators are pursuing a two-phased deal that would begin with a 45-day ceasefire, during which negotiations for a permanent end to the war would take place, according to an Axios report.

stories.title: ISW: Ukraine at Huliaipole and Oleksandrivka keeps disrupting Russian spring offensive across the theater
stories.summary: According to the Institute for the Study of War, Ukrainian counterattacks near Huliaipole and Oleksandrivka have forced Russian naval infantry to redeploy, disrupting Russia's planned spring offensive across multiple sectors of the front.

stories.title: Israeli rescuers search for missing in building struck by missile, 2 dead
stories.summary: Israeli rescue teams searched for missing people in a seven-story building that suffered a direct missile hit, killing at least two and injuring four others. The strike tore through parts of the structure.

stories.title: Anxious days, sleepless nights for young Iranians in Hong Kong as war rages on
stories.summary: Iranian nationals living in Hong Kong are experiencing severe anxiety as the conflict in the Middle East continues. Young Iranians in the city report sleepless nights and constant monitoring of news as they await word from family members in Iran.

stories.title: Russians hit energy infrastructure in Kyiv region, Slavutych left without power
stories.summary: A Russian strike on energy infrastructure in the Kyiv region knocked out power to the city of Slavutych.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Donald Trump threatens to hit Iran power plants
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed the intelligence chief of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Iran defied threats from U.S. President Donald Trump, who warned he would devastate Iranian civilian infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers given Temple-themed board game ahead of Passover
stories.summary: Israeli reservists created and distributed a Temple-themed board game called 'From Egypt to Jerusalem' to fellow soldiers ahead of Passover, featuring religious and military imagery with players advancing toward Jerusalem.

stories.title: Ukraine repairs 2.7 million sq m of roads – Svyrydenko
stories.summary: First Deputy Prime Minister Svyrydenko reported that Ukraine has repaired 2.7 million square meters of damaged roads since the start of 2026, with roughly half of repairs on international highways completed.

stories.title: Ukraine takes back 480 sq km near Oleksandrivka as Russia pushes for Dnipropetrovsk “buffer zone” – Syrskyi says
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi reported that Ukrainian forces recaptured approximately 480 square kilometers and 12 settlements in the Oleksandrivka direction since late January, following his visit to the front lines.

stories.title: Families fleeing Israeli attacks take refuge in Lebanon’s mountains
stories.summary: Over one million people have been displaced across Lebanon as Israel escalated its military campaign with air raids and a ground invasion, forcing families to seek refuge in mountainous areas.

stories.title: Testing out alternative oil routes
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran has disrupted global energy supplies, prompting exploration of alternative oil shipping routes. President Trump's April 1 address failed to calm oil markets as escalating tensions with Iran crushed ceasefire hopes.

stories.title: Railways fares to remain unchanged for three months after govt subsidy in Punjab
stories.summary: Pakistan's federal government will pay approximately Rs6 billion to Pakistan Railways to offset increased operational costs from recent diesel price hikes. The subsidy will keep passenger fares and freight charges unchanged for three months through June 30.

stories.title: Ukraine and Syria to reopen embassies as trade hits ninefold surge since September
stories.summary: Ukraine and Syria agreed to reopen embassies in Kyiv and Damascus after bilateral trade surged ninefold since September 2025. The announcement followed President Zelenskyy's visit to Damascus.

stories.title: Iran rejects ceasefire proposal, wants permanent end to war
stories.summary: Iran rejected a ceasefire proposal for a temporary truce, stating through the state-run IRNA news agency that it demands a permanent end to the war with the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Airstrikes kill more than 34 in Iran as Trump's deadline looms
stories.summary: More than 34 people were killed in airstrikes on Iran as President Trump's deadline for Tehran approached. Simultaneously, both Iran and the US reportedly received a Pakistan-brokered plan to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Yemen’s civilians fear fallout after Houthis enter Iran war
stories.summary: Civilians in Sanaa, Yemen, are facing growing fears of air strikes and rising prices as Houthi involvement in the broader regional conflict with Iran draws the country deeper into war.

stories.title: Trump says US armed Iranian dissidents via Kurds, Kurdish groups deny claim
stories.summary: Former President Donald Trump claimed the US armed Iranian dissident groups through Kurdish intermediaries. Kurdish groups denied the claim, while Iran cited it as evidence that January protests were Western-backed.

stories.title: Nigerian army rescues 31 held after Easter church attack
stories.summary: The Nigerian army rescued 31 hostages following a gunmen attack on a church during Easter celebrations. Five civilians were killed in the attack, and their bodies were recovered at the scene.

stories.title: Could China's adoption of electric vehicles shield it from the energy crisis?
stories.summary: With crude oil prices near $110 per barrel due to the war in Iran and the Hormuz Strait closure, consumers worldwide face rising fuel costs. China's rapid adoption of electric vehicles, which now account for over half of new car sales, may partly shield the country from the energy crisis.

stories.title: New UK farm inheritance tax rule will cause ‘significant challenges’, say accountants
stories.summary: A new UK inheritance tax regime affecting farms and family businesses valued at £2.5 million or more took effect on April 6. Accountants warned the levy, first announced by the government in October 2024, will present significant challenges for those affected.

stories.title: Russia sends grain supplies to crisis-hit Egypt amid Iran war
stories.summary: Russia sent grain supplies to Egypt, which faces a crisis as the US-Israeli war on Iran has disrupted essential energy and crude oil shipments, particularly from Kuwait and other Gulf states.

stories.title: Can palm biodiesel provide quick relief for Malaysia amid Iran war?
stories.summary: Malaysia faces pressure to expand palm-based biodiesel use as the Iran war drives up fuel costs, but observers say high infrastructure costs and slow implementation limit its potential for quick relief. The government's fuel subsidy bill could reach 4 billion ringgit per month due to rising global energy prices.

stories.title: Hungarian elections, academia’s greatest chancer, and Easter-inspired satire
stories.summary: Ahead of Hungary's elections, the satirical Two-Tailed Dog Party is campaigning on promises of free beer and anti-corruption measures. Separately, French police apprehended an academic who fabricated a prestigious award and then bestowed it upon himself.

stories.title: No easy way out
stories.summary: An analysis argues the US is increasingly mired in a difficult war against Iran, now in its second month. Iran's resilience and control over the Strait of Hormuz have given it leverage over global energy markets, while the US faces growing international isolation with no allied support beyond Israel.

stories.title: Three people, including child, killed in Odesa in overnight Russian attack
stories.summary: A massive Russian strike on Odesa on the night of April 6 killed three people, including a child, in the southern Ukrainian port city.

stories.title: Iran threatens to restrict Bab el-Mandeb Strait after Trump warnings
stories.summary: After U.S. President Trump threatened Iran with a Tuesday deadline to open the Strait of Hormuz, Iran responded by threatening to restrict the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

stories.title: Orthodox Christians in Gaza mark Palm Sunday with church service
stories.summary: Palestinian Orthodox Christians gathered at St. Porphyrios Greek Orthodox Church in Gaza City to hold a Palm Sunday service.

stories.title: Unsustainable rise
stories.summary: Pakistan's health minister warned the country could become the world's fourth most populous nation within five years, with a current population exceeding 255 million growing by roughly 6.2 million annually. The commentary calls for urgent political action on population planning.

stories.title: Corporate hopes amid global tensions
stories.summary: Pakistani business leaders see recent diplomatic gains as potentially beneficial for the country's global standing and economic relief. The Pakistan Business Council's CEO urged long-term, investment-friendly policies over populist relief measures amid global volatility.

stories.title: Iran’s top university bombed as US, Israel intensify attacks; 34 killed
stories.summary: US and Israeli strikes hit a top university in Tehran, killing at least 34 people. Iran accused President Trump of inciting war crimes and vowed to respond in kind to attacks on its infrastructure.

stories.title: Arab American Heritage Month in US begins amid war, racism
stories.summary: National Arab American Heritage Month began in the United States during a period of regional conflict and rising concerns about racism, making community solidarity particularly significant for Arab Americans.

stories.title: Russian forces lose 940 invaders in war against Ukraine in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russian forces lost approximately 940 personnel in the past 24 hours, bringing estimated total Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, to about 1,304,490.

stories.title: Reservist airman who died by suicide in 2024 recognized as fallen soldier, family says
stories.summary: Israel's Defense Ministry recognized combat navigator Maj. (res.) Asaf Dagan, who died by suicide in 2024, as a fallen soldier and PTSD combat casualty, after his family campaigned for acknowledgment.

stories.title: Iraq’s PMF says US-Israeli raids hit two bases
stories.summary: The Popular Mobilisation Forces in Iraq reported that simultaneous US-Israeli strikes hit PMF intelligence headquarters in the Nineveh and Salah al-Din governorates.

stories.title: Replacement of Ice Patrol HMS Protector in the Works?
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence confirmed that capabilities for a future ice patrol ship are being developed to replace HMS Protector. Defence Minister Luke Pollard disclosed the plans in response to a parliamentary written question from MP Andrew Rosindell.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader to make ‘peace’ visit to China, first in 10 years
stories.summary: A Taiwanese opposition leader is planning to visit China in what is being described as a peace trip, marking the first such high-level opposition visit in approximately ten years.

stories.title: Iran and US receive draft proposal for 45-day ceasefire as attacks continue
stories.summary: The United States and Iran received a draft framework for a 45-day ceasefire, though Tehran rejected any immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. On the same day, US and Israeli forces struck targets in Iran, killing over 25 people, while Iran responded with missile fire on Israel and Gulf Arab states.

stories.title: India sends emergency relief supplies to flood and earthquake-hit Afghanistan
stories.summary: India dispatched emergency humanitarian relief supplies to Afghanistan following floods and an earthquake. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India remains committed to assisting the Afghan people during the crisis.

stories.title: Supr­eme Court to resume Imran’s review plea hearing in Rs10bn libel case tomorrow
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court will resume hearing on April 7 a review petition filed by PTI founder Imran Khan in a Rs10 billion defamation case brought by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. A bench headed by Justice Ayesha A. Malik will take up the petition, which had stayed trial court proceedings in Lahore.

stories.title: More than 40 trapped underground after strike on coal mine in Russian-controlled Luhansk region
stories.summary: More than 40 people were trapped underground after a strike hit a coal mine in the Russia-controlled Luhansk region of eastern Ukraine. A Moscow-installed official blamed the attack on Ukrainian forces.

stories.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, burn house, tents and vehicles near Nablus
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians in al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, burning a house, two tents, and three vehicles. Two Palestinians were hospitalized after the assault.

stories.title: Students of US universities in Iraqi Kurdistan fearful and lost
stories.summary: Iran warned it might target American-linked universities in Iraq's Kurdistan region, causing widespread fear among students and staff at US-affiliated institutions there.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 38 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: On day 38 of US-Israeli military operations against Iran, tensions escalated further after President Trump posted a threat on Truth Social demanding Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Drone attack hits high-rise and homes in Odesa, casualties reported
stories.summary: A massive Russian drone attack struck residential areas in two districts of Odesa, hitting a high-rise building and homes. Casualties were reported.

stories.title: More foreign marques face a do-or-die moment as Chinese buyers shun petrol cars
stories.summary: Several international car brands face potential exit from mainland China as losses mount from falling sales amid Chinese consumers' shift away from petrol vehicles. Analysts say brands selling fewer than 1,000 units monthly cannot cover manufacturing costs in the world's largest auto market.

stories.title: Lebanon’s Christians mark Easter in solidarity with war-hit south
stories.summary: Christians in Lebanon marked Easter in solidarity with communities in the war-affected south, where villages remain caught in fighting between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Chinese AI rivals clash over Anthropic’s OpenClaw exit amid global token crunch
stories.summary: Chinese tech companies are publicly clashing over opportunities created by US startup Anthropic's withdrawal of its Claude AI models from the open-source tool OpenClaw. The dispute comes amid a global crunch in computational power driven by surging demand for AI tokens from AI agent applications.

stories.title: Iran, US receive plan to end hostilities, immediate ceasefire, source says
stories.summary: Pakistan brokered a framework plan exchanged with Iran and the United States proposing an immediate ceasefire followed by reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with a comprehensive agreement to be finalized within 15-20 days.

stories.title: British MPs under fire for promoting Malik Riaz’s Dubai project: report
stories.summary: Three Pakistani-origin British MPs—Labour's Naz Shah and Afzal Khan, and independent Ayoub Khan—attended promotional events for a Dubai property project owned by Pakistani tycoon Malik Riaz Hussain and his son. Both Riaz figures are barred from the UK and face investigation in Pakistan, according to The Sunday Times.

stories.title: Diamer-Bhasha Dam land-affected people block Karakoram Highway
stories.summary: Protesters affected by Diamer-Bhasha Dam land acquisition blocked the Karakoram Highway at multiple locations in Diamer district, Gilgit-Baltistan. The "Huqooq Do, Dam Banao" movement threatened a long march to the dam's construction site if their demands for land rights were not met.

stories.title: Sindh flags Tarbela delays, warns of Kharif water crisis
stories.summary: The Sindh provincial government warned of an imminent water crisis for the kharif crop season due to persistent delays in Tarbela Dam infrastructure work by Wapda. Sindh Irrigation Minister Jam Khan Shoro wrote to the federal water resources minister noting that projects approved by IRSA in 2022 remain unfinished past their June 2025 deadline.

stories.title: IMF asks Pakistan to remove fuel price distortions amid subsidy pressures
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund urged Pakistan to eliminate distortions in petroleum pricing despite having accepted the government's Rs152 billion fuel subsidy cap. The subsidy was introduced amid a global energy price surge linked to the US-Israel attacks on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel says 163 injured in past 24 hours amid Iran, Hezbollah attacks
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported 163 people were hospitalized over 24 hours due to injuries from Iranian and Hezbollah attacks. An 82-year-old man seriously injured in an Iranian ballistic missile strike underwent surgery.

stories.title: AirAsia X hikes ticket prices by 40%, cuts capacity by 10% as Iran war hits fuel costs
stories.summary: Malaysia-based AirAsia X raised ticket prices by up to 40 percent and cut about 10 percent of its flights to offset soaring fuel costs caused by the Iran war. Average jet fuel costs have surged significantly, prompting the Southeast Asian low-cost carrier to also increase fuel surcharges by about 20 percent.

stories.title: Iran military says U.S. rescue operation used abandoned airport in southern Isfahan
stories.summary: Iran's military claimed it foiled a U.S. rescue operation at an abandoned airport in southern Isfahan province. Spokesman Ebrahim Zolfaghari of the Khatam Al-Anbiya central command said the operation was conducted under the pretext of recovering a downed aircraft's pilot.

stories.title: Iran executes man over attack on military site during January protests, Mizan
stories.summary: Iran executed Ali Fahim, the fourth person put to death over an alleged attempt to storm a military facility during January protests. A fifth defendant linked to the same case is believed to face execution in coming days.

stories.title: Nigerian worshippers celebrate Easter under tight security after deadly attack
stories.summary: Christians in Jos, central Nigeria, celebrated Easter Sunday Mass under heightened security following a shooting approximately one week earlier that killed around 30 people.

stories.title: Has US war on Iran killed the 'Gulf moment'?
stories.summary: This opinion piece analyzes whether the US-led war on Iran has undermined the geopolitical rise of Gulf Cooperation Council states, whose influence depended on strategic integration within the global economy.

stories.title: Enemy strike in Chernihiv region leaves over 10,000 without power
stories.summary: A Russian attack damaged an energy facility in the Novhorod-Siverskyi district of Chernihiv region, leaving over 10,000 people without electricity.

stories.title: The Age of Unlearning: How Democracies Lost Their Grip on Strategic Time
stories.summary: An analysis argues that U.S. strategic capacity has eroded through bureaucratic cuts and political incentives favoring short-term thinking over long-term planning. The piece cites the temporary elimination of the Pentagon's Office of Net Assessment, a Cold War-era body designed for long-range comparative assessments, as emblematic of this decline.

stories.title: The Age of Unlearning: How Democracies Lost Their Grip on Strategic Time
stories.summary: The article examines how the United States has progressively lost its capacity for long-term strategic thinking due to bureaucratic cuts and political incentives favoring short-term action. The temporary elimination of the Pentagon's Office of Net Assessment is cited as emblematic of this trend.

stories.title: Pakistan breaching temperature thresholds set for 2030
stories.summary: Pakistan is already breaching extreme temperature thresholds intended for 2030, according to a Pakistan Meteorological Department report. The country recorded its second-highest average nighttime minimum temperature on record during March, despite its minimal contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions.

stories.title: 1 in 3 Hong Kong commercial laundry operators at risk of closure as oil prices soar
stories.summary: Up to one-third of Hong Kong's commercial laundry operators face closure due to soaring fuel costs, with industrial diesel prices surging more than 190 percent from late February to early April. Some operators have been forced to reject new orders and freeze hiring.

stories.title: Artemis II approaches historic lunar loop for first Moon flyby since 1972
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew entered the Moon's gravitational influence, approaching a historic lunar flyby — the first crewed Moon flyby since Apollo 17 in 1972 — and is expected to set a distance record from Earth.

stories.title: How a perilous US rescue mission in Iran nearly went off course
stories.summary: A U.S. rescue mission in Iran nearly went off course when two MC-130 aircraft carrying approximately 100 special operations forces into Tehran experienced mechanical failures during the perilous operation.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz stays sticking point as ceasefire remains elusive
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains a central sticking point as ceasefire efforts between the US-Israel coalition and Iran stall. Iran demands war damage payments before reopening the strait, while the US threatened further strikes on Iranian infrastructure. China and Russia called for a ceasefire.

stories.title: 'Hit by both sides': US war on Iran threatens Iraq's 'careful strategy of multi-alignment'
stories.summary: Chatham House's Dr. Renad Mansour warned that the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is undermining Iraq's long-standing strategy of multi-alignment between Tehran and Washington. Iraq's ability to remain neutral is diminishing as the conflict threatens political and economic stability across the Middle East.

stories.title: Sharpening Signals and Reducing Noise for Better Defense Budgets
stories.summary: A policy article in an 11-part series by the Potomac Institute for Policy Studies examines how defense budget debates and economic statecraft should be better integrated into U.S. national security strategy. The piece argues that military power depends on sound economic foundations and budgetary decisions.

stories.title: Sharpening Signals and Reducing Noise for Better Defense Budgets
stories.summary: The article, part of a series by the Potomac Institute for Policy Studies and War on the Rocks, examines how the United States should improve defense budget processes. It argues that debates over defense spending and economic statecraft are integral to military power, not a distraction from warfighting.

stories.title: Kuwait oil facilities, HQ damaged by Iran drone strikes
stories.summary: Iranian drone strikes damaged Kuwait Petroleum Corporation facilities and its headquarters building, which also houses Kuwait's Oil Ministry.

stories.title: Young Palestinian man stabbed to death in Negev
stories.summary: A 36-year-old Palestinian man from Shaqib al-Salam, a Bedouin town in southern Israel, was fatally stabbed in Ofakim city in the Negev on Sunday night. The killing raised the 2026 death toll among Palestinian citizens of Israel to 77.

stories.title: UAE responds to drone incident near du telecom building in Fujairah
stories.summary: Authorities in Fujairah, UAE, responded to an incident involving a drone that approached a du telecommunications building. Officials said the drone came from the direction of Iran. No injuries were reported.

stories.title: Enemy strikes school in Chernihiv region with FPV drones
stories.summary: Russian FPV drones struck a school in Semenivka, Chernihiv region, causing damage to the facility.

stories.title: China’s electric truck revolution: powerful painkiller for the Iran war?
stories.summary: Sales of electric heavy-duty trucks in China are surging, partly driven by the Iran war's impact on fossil fuel prices. In regions like Xinjiang, Shanxi, and Inner Mongolia, electric truck adoption is accelerating as companies seek alternatives to expensive diesel fuel.

stories.title: Track current petrol and diesel prices, service station outages and shipments – Australia's fuel crisis in charts
stories.summary: Australia is facing a fuel crisis as Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts oil shipments, causing hundreds of service stations to run empty and fuel prices to rise sharply. The federal government has released fuel reserves and cut fuel excise taxes in response.

stories.title: Remove madman who has executive office, former White House official on Trump
stories.summary: Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci called for President Trump's removal from office, invoking the 25th Amendment. Scaramucci described Trump as a "mad man" unfit for the executive office.

stories.title: Iran executes man over alleged attack on military site during January protests
stories.summary: Iran executed Ali Fahim, the fourth person put to death over an alleged attempt to storm a military facility during January protests. A fifth defendant is believed to face the same punishment in coming days.

stories.title: Russia says it downed 148 Ukrainian drones in three hours
stories.summary: Russia's military reported that air defense units downed 148 Ukrainian drones within three hours on April 6. Emergency crews worked to restore power to nearly half a million households affected by outages linked to the aerial attacks.

stories.title: US, Iran discuss potential two phase deal including 45-day ceasefire - Axios
stories.summary: The US and Iran are discussing a potential two-phase deal including a 45-day ceasefire, according to Axios. Negotiations are being conducted through Pakistani, Egyptian, and Turkish mediators, with communication between US envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

stories.title: Occupiers in TOT Donetsk region push “military-historical tourism”
stories.summary: Occupation authorities in the temporarily occupied territory of Donetsk region announced plans to develop "military-historical tourism" in the area.

stories.title: North Korean silence on Iran signals openness to US talks: Seoul’s spy agency
stories.summary: South Korea's National Intelligence Service reported that North Korea has refrained from sending weapons or supplies to Iran since the conflict began on February 28. Seoul's spy agency assessed that Pyongyang is distancing itself from Tehran to preserve the possibility of engagement with the United States.

stories.title: Trump makes foul-mouthed threat to Iran after US airman is rescued
stories.summary: President Trump renewed threats of air strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges following the rescue of a U.S. airman from Iranian territory, using explicit language in his warning.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's Army Rescues 31 Hostages After Church Attack
stories.summary: The Nigerian army rescued 31 hostages after an attack on a church during Easter celebrations in northwestern Kaduna state, a region that has struggled with violence for years.

stories.title: Steph Curry returns from injury with 29 points but Warriors lose to Rockets
stories.summary: Golden State Warriors guard Steph Curry returned from a nine-week injury absence, scoring 29 points, but the Houston Rockets defeated the Warriors 117-116 in San Francisco.

stories.title: Search for 81-year-old hiker missing in Tuen Mun enters third day
stories.summary: An 81-year-old mainland Chinese hiker surnamed He went missing on Hong Kong's MacLehose Trail Section 10 on Saturday while hiking with his wife.
