stories.summary: Multiple fires broke out at the Borouge petrochemical plant in Abu Dhabi after debris from aerial interceptions fell on the facility. Operations were immediately suspended pending a damage assessment. No injuries were reported.

stories.title: Iran executes two men for breaking into a military base during January’s protests
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad-Amin Biglari and Shahin Vahedparast, who were convicted of breaking into a military base during January's anti-government protests. Authorities said the men attempted to steal weapons and military equipment.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 37 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the rescue of a US crew member who had been missing after Iran shot down an American fighter jet on day 37 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim cluster missile attack on Israel’s Ben Gurion airport
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces claimed responsibility for a cluster missile strike targeting Israel's Ben Gurion airport in Jaffa, according to the group's military spokesman.

stories.title: Over 100,000 sq km of Ukrainian land still potentially dangerous due to mines – Presidential Office
stories.summary: Ukraine's Presidential Office reported that over 100,000 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory remain potentially hazardous due to landmines and unexploded ordnance from the ongoing war.

stories.title: Tehran says Islamabad talks depend on terms
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied rejecting Islamabad as a venue for U.S.-Iran negotiations, stating that Tehran's participation depends on the terms and conditions offered. Pakistan has been facilitating diplomatic efforts between the two sides.

stories.title: CONFLICT: BOMBING TRUST
stories.summary: Ali Larijani, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, was killed in an Israeli airstrike on March 17, 2026. The latest round of US-Israeli military strikes on Iran began while Tehran was engaged in nuclear negotiations with Washington.

stories.title: Aid groups warn Iran war is hindering food and medicine from reaching millions
stories.summary: The United Nations described the Iran war's impact on supply chains as the most significant disruption since COVID-19, with shipment costs rising up to 20% and widespread delays as goods are rerouted away from conflict zones.

stories.title: Hong Kong rescuers search for man, 81, who went missing on hike in Tuen Mun
stories.summary: Hong Kong rescue teams are searching for an 81-year-old man surnamed He who went missing while hiking along Section 10 of the MacLehose Trail near Tai Lam Chung Reservoir in Tuen Mun. Authorities found one of his shoes roughly 20 hours into the operation after he became separated from his wife on Saturday.

stories.title: Fewer Russian drones last night. That’s when Ukraine starts watching the skies more carefully
stories.summary: After recent massive Russian drone attacks involving up to 542 drones, Russia launched 93 drones against Ukraine overnight on April 4–5. Analysts noted the dip may precede a surge attack or reflect a diversion of drone supplies to Iran.

stories.title: Crew member from downed US fighter jet rescued in 'miraculous' operation, says Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that American forces recovered a second airman downed in Iran, describing the rescue as miraculous and one of the most daring in US history. Iranian media reported that five people were killed in strikes carried out during the operation.

stories.title: Trump warns of ‘hell’ as Iran fights back
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened Iran with severe consequences, urging Tehran to negotiate or reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian missiles struck near military headquarters in Tel Aviv, while U.S. and Israeli forces bombed petrochemical facilities and the Bushehr nuclear plant. The WHO reported over 4.3 million displaced and 116 attacks on healthcare facilities.

stories.title: Intercepted call reveals Russian commanders threatening troops over refusal to attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence intercepted a call in which a Russian commander threatened subordinates with reprisals for refusing to carry out an attack, highlighting reported discipline problems within Russian forces.

stories.title: Israel says 108 hospitalised with war injuries in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported 108 people were hospitalised over the past 24 hours with conflict-related injuries tied to fighting with Iran and Hezbollah. A total of more than 6,800 people have been treated for war-related injuries since fighting began on February 28.

stories.title: Indonesia lays to rest peacekeepers killed in Lebanon, Prabowo condemns attacks
stories.summary: Three Indonesian UN peacekeepers killed in two separate explosions in southern Lebanon last week were laid to rest in their hometowns. President Prabowo condemned the attacks. The peacekeepers, serving with the UN Interim Force in Lebanon, died on March 29 and 30 amid ongoing conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Nine killed in US strikes in Iran’s Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province
stories.summary: At least nine people were killed and eight wounded in US strikes in Iran's Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, according to Fars news agency. Casualties were reported in Koh Siah in Kohgiluyeh County and in the Vazg and Kakan areas of Boyer-Ahmad County.

stories.title: US successfully rescues second airman deep behind enemy lines in Iran, Trump confirms
stories.summary: US officials confirmed to Axios that a specialized commando unit with heavy air support successfully rescued the second airman from deep inside Iran following the downing of an American fighter jet.

stories.title: Erdogan, Rutte discuss Ukraine, Iran wars, preparations for NATO summit
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte held a phone call to discuss the wars in Ukraine and Iran as well as preparations for an upcoming NATO summit.

stories.title: NYT: US destroyed malfunctioning planes during Iran rescue mission
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that two US transport planes malfunctioned during a rescue mission in Iran and were ordered destroyed to prevent seizure. The operation aimed to recover crew members of a US F-15E shot down over Iran.

stories.title: Hong Kong-listed CaoCao hails fleet-first strategy as China’s robotaxi race gathers pace
stories.summary: Hong Kong-listed CaoCao, a Geely-backed ride-hailing company, plans to deploy 100,000 autonomous vehicles by 2030 as part of a fleet-first robotaxi strategy. CEO Gong Xin described the approach as a closed-loop model integrating vehicle manufacturing, autonomous driving technology, and fleet management.

stories.title: Bahrain says Bapco fire extinguished after Iranian attack
stories.summary: A fire at a Bapco energy company warehouse in Bahrain, caused by an Iranian attack, has been extinguished, according to Bahrain News Agency. Emergency teams responded to the blaze, and authorities had sounded sirens urging residents to take precautions.

stories.title: ‘From big renovation to big burial’: Wang Fuk Court residents return to mark Ching Ming
stories.summary: Displaced residents of Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong, returned to the fire-ravaged estate on Ching Ming Festival to mourn loved ones lost in the November 26 blaze. The inferno, Hong Kong's deadliest fire since 1948, killed 168 people and spread across seven of the estate's eight towers.

stories.title: Aid groups warn Iran war is hindering food and medicine supply, suffering set to deepen
stories.summary: Aid organizations warned that the conflict with Iran and attacks on the Strait of Hormuz have severed vital supply routes, driving up fuel prices and disrupting food and medicine deliveries across the region.

stories.title: ‘Miraculous’: US rescues second pilot downed in Iran, Trump confirms
stories.summary: President Trump confirmed the rescue of a second US pilot downed over Iran. Iran claimed it shot down another American aircraft involved in the rescue operation of the F-15 fighter crew.

stories.title: Israel says it hit 120 Iranian air defense systems in 24 hours
stories.summary: The Israeli military said its air force struck more than 120 targets across central and western Iran over 24 hours, including air defense systems, ballistic missile sites, UAV production facilities, and missile infrastructure linked to the IRGC.

stories.title: White House official criticizes media over Trump hospitalisation rumours
stories.summary: White House communications director Steven Cheung criticized media and social media users for circulating unverified claims that President Trump had been hospitalized, though he did not cite specific examples.

stories.title: Russian drone attack sparks fires in Odesa, two injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Odesa caused fires and injured two people. The strikes targeted areas within the city, causing damage to local structures.

stories.title: Tai Po fire hearings reveal broken promises to Hongkongers
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating the deadly Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong completed its first round of hearings. The inquiry revealed widespread fragmentation of responsibility among parties involved in the estate's management and highlighted failures in government monitoring and enforcement.

stories.title: Murder suspect caught hiding in IDF base weeks after the killing
stories.summary: Israeli police apprehended a murder suspect hiding at an IDF military base weeks after the killing. The victim was a 32-year-old Rehovot resident stabbed outside a Tel Aviv club in February.

stories.title: Iran is using North Korean weapons against Israel, US, expert tells Fox News - report
stories.summary: Security expert Bruce Bechtol of Angelo State University told Fox News that Iran is using North Korean-supplied weapons in its conflict against Israel and the United States, describing North Korea as the seller and Iran as the buyer.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky fears Iran war may lead to less support to fight Russia’s invasion
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed concern that a prolonged US-Israeli conflict with Iran could reduce American support for Ukraine. In an interview in Istanbul, he emphasized Ukraine's critical need for more Patriot air defence systems to counter Russian missile and drone attacks.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone operators destroy Russian Solntsepyok flamethrower system in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 129th Separate Heavy Mechanized Brigade used drones to destroy a Russian Solntsepyok heavy flamethrower system near Dvorichna in the Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Fair Work Agency’s priorities criticised days before its launch
stories.summary: The UK's new Fair Work Agency, a cornerstone of Labour's Employment Rights Act launching Tuesday, faces criticism after the government asked it to reduce the regulatory burden on business. Unite's leader warned the directive risks undermining the agency's mandate to enforce minimum wage, holiday pay, and modern slavery laws.

stories.title: China’s long-delayed skyscraper, Goldin Finance 117, nears completion amid property woes
stories.summary: Goldin Finance 117, a skyscraper in Tianjin, China, is nearing completion after nearly a decade of construction dormancy. Workers recently began installing a diamond-shaped crown atop the 596-metre tower. The project's revival comes amid China's ongoing property market struggles.

stories.title: IRGC says it destroyed US aircraft tracking crew of downed fighter jet in Isfahan
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it destroyed a US aircraft in southern Isfahan province that was tracking the crew of a downed American F-15E fighter jet. The IRGC said Iranian forces targeted the "enemy bird," though few details were provided.

stories.title: Trump must 'reign down hell' on Islamic regime, make his ultimatum on Iran count - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial called on President Trump to follow through on his 48-hour ultimatum to Iran, arguing that Israel's public has shown resilience and deserves decisive action rather than shifting deadlines.

stories.title: Hong Kong economy showed resilience in first quarter of 2026, Paul Chan says
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan reported that the city's economy showed resilience in the first quarter of 2026 despite Middle East conflict-driven market volatility. He attributed the performance to steady growth in mainland China's economy.

stories.title: Balochistan fixes price of Iranian petrol at Rs280
stories.summary: The Balochistan provincial government, under Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti, fixed the price of Iranian smuggled petrol at 280 Pakistani rupees per litre. Officials announced that the fuel would be sold only within Balochistan and would not be permitted to leave the province.

stories.title: Rains in KP, Punjab kill six amid new spell forecast
stories.summary: Rain and windstorms killed at least six people across Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces in Pakistan, including four deaths in KP's Khyber district. The Met office warned of a fresh spell of rain and thunderstorms due to a western disturbance entering Balochistan and KP.

stories.title: Trump says US officer rescued, injured but ‘will be fine’
stories.summary: President Trump confirmed the rescue of a US weapons systems officer, identified as a colonel, whose F-15E fighter jet was shot down over Iran. Trump said the officer sustained injuries but is expected to recover fully.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump says F-15 crew member missing in Iran is ‘safe’ after ‘dozens of aircraft’ sent to recover him
stories.summary: President Trump announced that a second U.S. crew member from an F-15 fighter jet downed over Iran was rescued after dozens of aircraft were deployed. Iranian media reported that the Revolutionary Guards destroyed a U.S. aircraft searching for the missing pilot in the southern Isfahan region.

stories.title: Why war on Iran threatens to unleash unrest in South Asia
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the Iran war is threatening economic stability across South Asia, with Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Pakistan particularly vulnerable due to their dependence on Middle Eastern fuel and Gulf remittances. Rising energy and food costs risk pushing these IMF-dependent economies to the brink.

stories.title: Ukraine boosts farm equipment compensation to 40% for farmers in war-affected areas
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers increased compensation for Ukrainian-made farm equipment to 40% for agricultural producers operating in frontline and combat-affected areas, up from previous support levels.

stories.title: Iran says ‘brotherly’ Iraq’s ships can use Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's military announced that Iraq is exempt from shipping restrictions imposed on the Strait of Hormuz, which have disrupted global energy flows for weeks. The exemption could release as much as three million barrels per day of Iraqi oil cargoes onto global markets.

stories.title: Nearly 100 NSW service stations fined $1,100 each over misleading petrol prices amid fuel shortage crackdown
stories.summary: Ninety-three service stations in New South Wales, Australia, were fined $1,100 each for misrepresenting fuel prices during the country's fuel crisis. Inspectors visited approximately 1,800 stations in a two-week compliance operation, with most violations found in regional areas.

stories.title: In Estonia, rumors are circulating that the city of Narva wants to secede and join Russia. Is it true?
stories.summary: Online rumors have circulated claiming residents of Narva, an Estonian city bordering Russia, want to secede and join Russia. The reports are being examined amid broader concerns about Russian influence in border regions of the Baltic states.

stories.title: Does the Estonian city of Narva really want to join Russia?
stories.summary: The Estonian border city of Narva, located adjacent to Russia, has been the subject of online rumors claiming some residents wish to secede and join Russia. The report examines the veracity of those claims.

stories.title: 'People's Republic' rumors: Does an Estonian city really want to join Russia?
stories.summary: Online rumors have circulated claiming residents of Narva, an Estonian city bordering Russia, want to secede and join Russia. The reports examine what is actually occurring in the city on Europe's eastern frontier.

stories.title: Israeli forces blow up residential buildings in Lebanon township
stories.summary: Israeli forces demolished residential buildings in the Naqoura region of southern Lebanon, causing widespread destruction. The operations also included the destruction of surveillance cameras near the headquarters of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL).

stories.title: Middle East War live: Rescued crew member from downed US fighter jet 'safe and sound,' says Trump
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that U.S. forces successfully recovered a crew member from a downed American fighter jet in Iran, describing it as one of the most daring rescue operations in U.S. history. The recovery came as Iran launched missiles and drones at Israel and Kuwait early Sunday.

stories.title: Satellite firm says it’s indefinitely withholding Iran war images at US request
stories.summary: Satellite imaging firm Planet Labs informed clients it is shifting to case-by-case "managed distribution" of imagery from the Iran conflict at the request of the US government, expanding on a 14-day delay imposed in March.

stories.title: Trump’s unpopular war on Iran
stories.summary: Polling indicates that a majority of Americans oppose the US-Israel military campaign against Iran, making it one of the most unpopular conflicts at its outset in recent US history.

stories.title: At Easter vigil, Pope Leo urges world not to grow numb to war
stories.summary: Pope Leo led the Easter vigil Mass at St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City on Saturday night. He urged the world's Catholics not to become numb to ongoing wars and to actively work for peace.

stories.title: Fire reported at Bahrain site after Iranian strike
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry said civil defense teams responded to a fire at a facility caused by an Iranian attack. No immediate details on casualties or the extent of damage were provided.

stories.title: Trump weighs broader cabinet shake-up as Iran war pressure grows
stories.summary: President Trump is considering a broader cabinet reshuffle as the Iran war drives down his approval ratings to 36 percent, according to a Reuters/Ipsos survey. This represents the lowest approval figure of his current presidential term.

stories.title: Syria closes border crossing after Israeli threat
stories.summary: Syria closed the Jdeidet Yabous border crossing after Israel threatened to conduct raids on the Lebanese side. Syrian customs official Mazen Alloush said the crossing serves only civilian movement and has no military purpose.

stories.title: IRNA: Strike on petrochemical hub kills 5, wounds 170
stories.summary: Iranian state media agency IRNA reported that airstrikes on the Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Economic Zone in Khuzestan province killed at least five people and wounded approximately 170 others. The facility is a major hub in Iran's petrochemical sector near the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Trump, Israel pressure Iran ahead of deadline, as hunt goes on for missing US crew member
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict entered its sixth week with little prospect of peace talks. President Trump and Israel continued pressuring Tehran as the search for a missing American crew member went on, amid low public support for the war shown in polls.

stories.title: Iran's use of cluster munitions against Israel may be a war crime - Human Rights Watch
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch said Iran's use of cluster munitions in populated areas of Israel may constitute a war crime. Researcher Patrick Thompson stated the weapons pose a foreseeable and long-lasting danger to civilians.

stories.title: Hong Kong tourists choose safety, affordability with trips to mainland China
stories.summary: Rising fuel surcharges linked to the U.S.-Israel attack on Iran are prompting Hong Kong travelers to choose mainland China destinations accessible by high-speed rail instead of international air travel. Travelers report significantly lower costs for domestic rail trips compared to flights.

stories.title: Rescue ongoing for downed F-15E crew member still inside Iran, official says
stories.summary: A US government official told Al Jazeera that a crew member from the downed F-15E fighter jet had been located inside Iran but had not yet been extracted. The official described a fierce firefight during the ongoing rescue effort.

stories.title: Syrskyi discusses counter-drone measures and military training with airborne assault units
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi met with sergeants and soldiers of airborne assault units to discuss counter-drone measures, military training needs, frontline challenges, and supply issues.

stories.title: India turns to ‘trusted friend’ Russia for oil, LNG supply as Iran war energises ties
stories.summary: Russia offered to increase energy supplies to India amid the global crisis caused by the Iran war, reinforcing bilateral ties. Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov indicated Moscow was prepared to ramp up oil and LNG deliveries to New Delhi.

stories.title: Asian countries assure Australia ‘normal supply’ of fuel will continue as Albanese focuses on averting shortages
stories.summary: Australia's federal government secured reassurances from Asian trading partners including Singapore, South Korea, Malaysia, and Japan that normal fuel supply would continue despite disruptions from the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Al Jazeera: Second crew member of downed F15 located
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the second crew member from a US F-15E fighter jet downed over Iran's Khuzestan province was located amid heavy fighting. One crew member had been rescued earlier while search operations continued for the second.

stories.title: Downed US airman found after ‘heavy firefight’ in Iran
stories.summary: The second crew member of a U.S. F-15E fighter jet downed over Iran was rescued after a heavy firefight, President Trump announced. Trump said the U.S. military deployed dozens of aircraft in a multi-hour search and rescue operation to recover the airman.

stories.title: Fired US general says soldiers deserve 'leaders of character'
stories.summary: Former US Army Chief of Staff General Randy George, removed by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, issued a farewell letter stating that soldiers deserve "leaders of character" and urged officers to remain focused on their mission.

stories.title: Drone attacks damage Kuwait power, water plants
stories.summary: Iranian drone attacks caused serious material damage to two electricity and water distillation plants in Kuwait, knocking out two power-generating units. No casualties were reported. The strikes followed earlier drone attacks on Kuwait's Shuwaikh Oil Sector Complex.

stories.title: How can Beijing attract top-tier Chinese AI professionals based abroad?
stories.summary: Beijing is being urged to improve strategies for attracting top Chinese AI professionals working abroad, as the U.S. increasingly integrates artificial intelligence into military and national security systems. Rising geopolitical tensions are forcing Chinese researchers at U.S. institutions to confront difficult career choices.

stories.title: China executes Frenchman convicted in 2010 for drug trafficking
stories.summary: China executed Chan Thao Phoumy, a 62-year-old French national born in Laos, who had been convicted of drug trafficking and sentenced to death in 2010.

stories.title: Israel Police investigating after human remains found in ocean off coast of Herzliya
stories.summary: Israeli police are investigating after human bones were discovered in the sea off the coast of Herzliya. The remains were found by Tel Aviv District Marine Police following a tip from citizens.

stories.title: Two more detained over arson attack on Czech defence factory
stories.summary: Czech police and prosecutors announced the detention of two more suspects in connection with an arson attack on an optics and drone factory in the Czech Republic last month.

stories.title: Russia carries out 14 massive combined attacks during winter – Ihnat
stories.summary: In addition to daily air strikes on Ukraine, Russia carried out 14 large-scale combined attacks over the winter period, according to Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat.

stories.title: US satellite imagery firm Planet Labs announces blackout on Middle East war pics
stories.summary: US satellite imagery company Planet Labs announced an indefinite blackout on imagery of the Middle East at the request of the US government, restricting public access to commercial satellite photos of ongoing conflicts in the region.

stories.title: Iran attacks Kuwait, Israel after Trump sets deadline for deal
stories.summary: Iran launched missiles and drones at Israel and Kuwait after President Trump issued a 48-hour deadline for Tehran to negotiate or face severe consequences. Both Kuwait and Israel activated air defenses in response to the attacks, which are part of a broader war sparked by earlier U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Iran orders asset seizures for 100 accused of 'supporting enemy abroad'
stories.summary: Tehran's Prosecutor's Office ordered the seizure of assets and freezing of bank accounts of more than 100 individuals accused of supporting the enemy abroad, including staff of Iran International and Manoto news channels, which Tehran accuses of ties to Israel.

stories.title: Iran warns of 'big surprise' for US, Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian security official warned of a "big surprise" for the United States and Israel, saying Tehran is operating according to its plans. The official dismissed US targeting claims as evidence of failed American military operations.

stories.title: Observatory warns of thundery showers amid Ching Ming Festival in Hong Kong
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory warned of intense thundery showers approaching the city during the Ching Ming Festival, as a trough of low pressure brought a band of storms from the seas south of Hong Kong.

stories.title: Houthis claim joint attacks with Iran, Hezbollah targeting Ben Gurion Airport
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi group announced joint military operations with Iran and Hezbollah targeting Ben Gurion Airport in Israel. Spokesman Yahya Saree said the attacks involved a ballistic missile and several drones aimed at Lod Airport and military targets in southern Israel.

stories.title: Trump administration files emergency motion to resume ballroom work, citing security issues
stories.summary: The Trump administration filed an emergency motion to resume construction work in the White House ballroom after Judge Richard Leon's ruling halted the project. Officials argued the decision left the executive mansion "open and exposed," posing grave national security risks to the president and staff.

stories.title: Japan-linked tanker clears Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A second Japan-linked vessel, the Indian-flagged LPG tanker Green Sanvi operated by Mitsui OSK Lines, transited the Strait of Hormuz after being stranded in the Gulf since the war began. The tanker was among 45 Japan-linked ships stuck in the region due to passage restrictions.

stories.title: Syrian-Lebanese border closed after IDF issues evacuation notice - report
stories.summary: The IDF issued an evacuation notice for areas near the Syrian-Lebanese border, prompting closure of the crossing. The military stated the action was due to Hezbollah's alleged use of the crossing for military purposes and weapons smuggling.

stories.title: Man charged with impaired driving after after hitting Louisiana crowd celebrating Lao New Year
stories.summary: At least 15 people were injured when an alleged drunk driver struck pedestrians at a Lao New Year parade in New Iberia, Louisiana, on Saturday. Some injuries are reported to be serious. Louisiana State Police charged the man with driving while impaired, 18 counts of first-degree negligent injuring, and careless operation.

stories.title: U.S. revokes green cards and visas of several Iranian nationals connected to Tehran government
stories.summary: The United States has revoked green cards and visas of several Iranian nationals identified as having connections to the Tehran government.

stories.title: Ukraine extradites foreign fighter who fought for Russia to Azerbaijan
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement extradited to Azerbaijan a native of Hajigabul who had participated in combat operations alongside Russian military units during the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Israeli forces destroy 17 UN peacekeeper cameras in south Lebanon, says UN official
stories.summary: A United Nations official reported that Israeli forces destroyed 17 UN peacekeeper surveillance cameras in southern Lebanon, with a UN spokeswoman stating the cameras appeared to have been damaged by some form of laser technology.

stories.title: Iran says Iraqi ships can pass Strait of Hormuz as transits tick up
stories.summary: Tehran announced that Iraqi ships will face no restrictions transiting the Strait of Hormuz, praising Iraq's stance against the United States as overall transit volume through the waterway has increased.

stories.title: Why does Trump want to pull out of NATO?
stories.summary: An explainer examines the Trump administration's questioning of NATO's founding principles and membership structure. It covers NATO's origins, recent alliance tensions, U.S. financial contributions, and the legal complexities of a potential American withdrawal.

stories.title: WSJ: Trump administration weighs targeting Iran energy sites
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that senior Trump administration aides have discussed targeting Iranian energy facilities and bridges as legitimate military targets. President Trump publicly pledged to bomb Iran, while legal experts questioned whether such strikes meet the standard of tangible military advantage.

stories.title: Ex-IAEA chief warns of 'ball of fire' in region, urges 'madman' Trump be stopped
stories.summary: Former IAEA chief Mohamed ElBaradei urged Gulf nations and the United Nations to act following President Trump's 48-hour ultimatum to Iran. He warned that escalation could turn the region into a "ball of fire" and called for intervention to prevent further conflict.

stories.title: ‘Don’t bomb’: Israelis call for ending Iran war
stories.summary: Hundreds of Israeli protesters gathered in Tel Aviv on April 4, calling on their government to end military operations against Iran and opposing further escalation of the conflict.

stories.title: Lebanon evacuates border crossing amid Israeli threats
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities evacuated the General Security Centre and its database at the Al-Masnaa border crossing with Syria after Israel threatened to target the site. Hundreds of transport trucks and drivers remain stranded in the border area.

stories.title: Small protests in Israel call for ending Iran war
stories.summary: Hundreds of Israelis gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday to protest the war against Iran and demand the government end the military campaign.

stories.title: Iran adds Israeli power stations to target list, report says
stories.summary: Iran's armed forces added two major Israeli power stations to their target list, according to Tasnim news agency. The decision followed reports that Israel is preparing to strike Iranian energy facilities, reflecting an escalating cycle of threats against energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Russian propaganda spreading narratives portraying Ukraine as “terrorist state” over strikes on Russian facilities
stories.summary: Russian information outlets have escalated narratives labeling Ukraine a "terrorist state" following Ukrainian strikes on oil terminals and refineries in Ufa and other Russian facilities. The campaign aims to shape international perceptions of Ukraine's military operations on Russian territory.

stories.title: How China is transforming Hong Kong into a strategic hub
stories.summary: Hong Kong is developing its first five-year plan modeled on mainland China's approach to long-term economic planning. The initiative represents a significant departure from the city's traditional laissez-faire economic model and reliance on market forces.

stories.title: Second American crewman from downed fighter jet rescued in commando raid inside Iran
stories.summary: US forces conducted a commando raid inside Iran to rescue the second crew member from a downed American fighter jet. Separately, Kuwait reported Iranian drone attacks on oil and power infrastructure, and a Palestinian was reportedly seriously injured in a settler attack.

stories.title: US satellite firm Planet Labs announces blackout on war on Iran images
stories.summary: US satellite imaging company Planet Labs announced it will indefinitely withhold imagery of the Iran conflict, stating the decision followed a request from the US government.

stories.title: China not targeting US West Coast with ultra-large underwater drones: lead scientist
stories.summary: China's unmanned submersibles are now the world's largest, with models approaching 20 metres in length displayed at military parades and a classified variant exceeding 40 metres detected by satellite imagery at a naval installation. The lead scientist denied the vessels target the U.S. West Coast.

stories.title: Public outrage as China traveller at pet-friendly hotel receives text recommending dog meat eateries
stories.summary: A pet-friendly hotel in Guizhou province, China, faced public backlash after sending a guest traveling with a puppy an official message recommending local dog meat restaurants as attractions. The incident sparked fierce criticism on Chinese social media.

stories.title: IDF Northern Command chief admits Israel overestimated damage to Hezbollah after 2024 war
stories.summary: IDF Northern Command chief Major General Rafi Milo acknowledged in recorded remarks that Israel overestimated the damage inflicted on Hezbollah during the 2024 war. Officials estimate Hezbollah still possesses tens of thousands of rockets.

stories.title: Georgia extends aid for Ukrainian refugees by three months
stories.summary: Georgia extended medical services and financial assistance for Ukrainian refugees residing in the country by an additional three months. The decision continues support for Ukrainian citizens who have been living continuously in Georgia.

stories.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner could visit Ukraine, Kyiv says
stories.summary: Ukrainian presidential aide Kyrylo Budanov said U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner could visit Kyiv in April. The potential trip comes amid efforts to revive peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, which stalled following the outbreak of war in the Gulf.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to make deal or face ‘Hell’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Iran to reach a deal or face severe consequences. The threat followed a strike near an Iranian nuclear power plant that prompted evacuations, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have hit a commercial ship in Bahrain allegedly linked to Israel.

stories.title: Ro Khanna | Exploring the new middle
stories.summary: Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna outlines a political vision blending elements of America First nationalism with progressive welfare policies. He advocates for state-supported manufacturing development and working-class investment while calling for moderation in the tech sector.

stories.title: Dancing through the crackdown: The satirical song soundtracking post-Khamenei Iran
stories.summary: London-based Iranian artist Naz released a satirical song on social media amid celebrations following the reported death of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. The song gained traction as Iranian regime forces reportedly opened fire on citizens celebrating in the streets.

stories.title: Mohammad Ishaq Dar | At the global high table
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, a close confidant of the Sharif family, is leading a diplomatic reboot. His efforts include restarting ties with Bangladesh and pursuing mediation roles in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Thailand’s US$7 billion fishing industry sinks as Iran war hits fuel costs
stories.summary: Thailand's fishing industry, valued at approximately $7 billion, has been severely impacted by surging diesel prices caused by Iran's restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz. Half of the country's fishing fleet has reportedly been docked due to unaffordable fuel costs.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump confirms rescue of US officer, says ‘we got him’
stories.summary: Iran reported that US-Israeli airstrikes on the Mahshahr Petrochemical Zone killed five people and wounded 170. Separately, President Trump confirmed the rescue of a US officer shot down over Iran.

stories.title: War update: 128 clashes on front line, Ukrainian forces neutralize over 110 invaders in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces reported 128 combat engagements with Russian troops on April 4. Russian forces were most active in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions, with Ukrainian forces neutralizing over 110 invaders in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: Nigeria launches manhunt after abductions by bandits in northwest Zamfara
stories.summary: Nigerian security forces launched a manhunt after a large group of bandits abducted residents from villages in northwest Zamfara state. Police described it as one of the region's largest recent attacks.

stories.title: US arrests relatives of slain Iranian general Soleimani, rescinds residency permits
stories.summary: The niece and grandniece of Iranian General Qassem Soleimani were arrested in the United States after their residency permits were rescinded. Soleimani was killed in a U.S. drone strike in Iraq in January 2020.

stories.title: Syrskyi discusses priority needs under PURL program with NATO commander
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi spoke by phone with NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich. They discussed stable weapons supplies and Ukraine's priority needs under the PURL program.

stories.title: Slovak PM says EU should drop sanctions on Russian oil and gas to boost energy security
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico called on the European Union to drop sanctions on Russian oil and gas imports and restore flows through the Druzhba pipeline. He argued these steps, along with ending the war in Ukraine, were needed to address Europe's energy crisis exacerbated by the war in Iran.

stories.title: Bomb allegedly left at US base by Alen Zheng was built inside 2 Pepsi bottles
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors revealed that a bomb placed outside MacDill Air Force Base's visitors center in Florida on March 10 was constructed inside two 2-litre cherry Pepsi bottles. Alen Zheng, 20, of Land O'Lakes, Florida, is accused of planting the device, which did not detonate.

stories.title: Cops violently disperse protesters at Tel Aviv anti-war rally, after court raised attendance cap
stories.summary: Israeli police forcibly dispersed anti-war protesters at a rally in Tel Aviv after a court raised the permitted attendance cap. Detained activists reported police prevented them from reaching shelters during a missile attack.

stories.title: Russian strike on market in Ukraine kills five, wounds 25
stories.summary: A Russian strike on a market in Ukraine killed five people and wounded 25, including a 14-year-old girl reported to be in critical condition.

stories.title: US says it arrested relatives of slain Iran general Soleimani
stories.summary: U.S. authorities announced the arrest of individuals they identified as relatives of slain Iranian General Qasem Soleimani. Two of Soleimani's daughters denied that the detained women were related to the deceased IRGC commander.

stories.title: Israel says will strike Lebanon-Syria border crossing
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it would strike an area near the main border crossing between Syria and Lebanon. Residents in the vicinity were urged to evacuate.

stories.title: Delegation led by Witkoff and Kushner may visit Ukraine after Easter – Budanov
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov said a U.S. delegation led by White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner is expected to visit Kyiv after Easter, around April 12.

stories.title: Israel claims over 200 strikes on Iran and Hezbollah targets
stories.summary: The Israeli military claimed it conducted over 200 air strikes over a weekend targeting sites in Iran and Lebanon. Strikes in Iran reportedly hit air defense systems, ballistic missile production facilities, and an IRGC weapons storage site. In Lebanon, targets included Hezbollah weapons depots, launch positions, and the headquarters of its elite Radwan Force.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson, Mamdani must accept Israel cannot exist without being a Jewish state - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion article argues that Tucker Carlson and Zohran Mamdani should accept that Israel's existence is inherently tied to its identity as a Jewish state. The piece contends that Jews have historically lacked a permanent homeland elsewhere.

stories.title: UAE arrests flight attendant over war image in ongoing Dubai crackdown
stories.summary: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates arrested a British flight attendant in Dubai over posting a war-related image. The detention is part of a broader crackdown in the UAE on social media content related to the regional conflict, raising concerns about civil liberties.

stories.title: Zohran Mamdani: What side of the Muslim world are you on? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlights the silence of New York politician Zohran Mamdani on the Iranian regime, contrasting his stance with global Muslim leaders who have spoken out against Tehran. The commentary questions his position within broader Muslim-world politics.

stories.title: UAE condemns ‘acts of vandalism’ at its embassy in Damascus
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates condemned riots and acts of vandalism at its embassy and the residence of its head of mission in Damascus, Syria. Protesters had gathered outside the embassy, with some chanting anti-Israel slogans. The UAE called on Syria to protect the embassy and hold perpetrators accountable.

stories.title: Relatives of Iran's late Gen. Qassem Soleimani arrested: U.S.
stories.summary: The United States revoked the green cards and visas of several Iranian nationals connected to Tehran's government, including relatives of slain Iranian General Qassem Soleimani, and arrested them.

stories.title: UAE condemns ‘riots, acts of vandalism’ at its embassy in Damascus
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates condemned riots and vandalism at its embassy in Damascus, Syria. The unrest was linked to Israel's passage of a law imposing the death penalty on Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages on Sunday
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that no electricity supply restrictions are planned for Sunday, April 5.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was killed and another seriously wounded in what the Israeli military described as a friendly fire incident in southern Lebanon. The army confirmed the incident occurred on a Friday.

stories.title: Caught in the crossfire: The American highschoolers who stayed behind to help amid the Iran war
stories.summary: Approximately 60 American high school students chose to remain in Israel during the Iran war rather than return home. The teens joined agricultural nonprofit Hiburim B'Haklaut to assist farmers affected by the conflict.

stories.title: Explosion rocks Sudan’s capital; police blame war-era landmine
stories.summary: An explosion in the Burri neighbourhood of eastern Khartoum, Sudan, was caused by a war-era landmine that detonated after residents set fire to waste in the area, according to Sudanese police.

stories.title: UAE condemns pro-Palestine protests targeting its embassy in Syria
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine protesters in Damascus targeted the UAE embassy, with dozens gathering outside and some chanting "the Zionist embassy." The demonstrations reflected anger at the UAE's perceived support for Israel. The UAE condemned the protests directed at its diplomatic mission in Syria.

stories.title: PM says disbursement of funds for public transport, freight operators has begun through digital wallets
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that relief funds for public transport and freight vehicle operators have begun disbursement through digital wallets. He chaired a meeting reviewing petroleum reserves and government measures to provide relief during the ongoing crisis.

stories.title: Israeli measures tighten grip on Hebron’s Ibrahimi Mosque
stories.summary: Israeli authorities have intensified security measures at the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron, with restrictions reportedly resembling those applied at Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem. The tightened controls affect Palestinian worshippers' access to the site.

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's 'helpless, nervous, unbalanced' threats
stories.summary: Iran's central military command rejected a threat from U.S. President Donald Trump to destroy Iranian infrastructure if Tehran did not accept a peace deal within 48 hours. General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi dismissed the ultimatum as "helpless, nervous, unbalanced" and warned that "the gates of hell" would open in response.

stories.title: Three workers wounded in strike on North Rumaila oil field in southern Iraq
stories.summary: A drone strike hit an equipment storage facility at the North Rumaila oil field in southern Iraq, wounding three workers. Iraqi engineers said the strikes had no impact on operations at the giant Rumaila oilfield.

stories.title: At least 12 persons, including eight of one family, killed in Afghan quake
stories.summary: An earthquake in Afghanistan killed at least 12 people, including eight members of one family. Five homes were destroyed and 33 others significantly damaged across the provinces of Kabul, Panjshir, Logar, Nangarhar, Laghman, and Nuristan, affecting 40 families.

stories.title: Zelensky meets with Patriarch Bartholomew
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew in Istanbul. They discussed the plight of Ukrainian children affected by Russian aggression and the development of the Orthodox church in Ukraine.

stories.title: The man who became one of India's greatest stage queens
stories.summary: Chapal Bhaduri became one of Bengal's most celebrated stage queens, performing female roles in traditional Indian theater. His prominence faded as women entered the stage and audiences shifted their attention.

stories.title: After October 7, containment is dead: Israel must redraw its borders - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that after the October 7 attack, Israel's previous strategy of containment has failed and the country must redraw its borders with neighboring territories.

stories.title: Anti-war protests held across Israel under wartime gathering limits
stories.summary: Anti-war protests took place across Israel under wartime gathering restrictions. Demonstrators carried signs opposing the war, with about 200 people gathering at Horev Junction in Haifa.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes as Zelenskyy goes to Turkiye
stories.summary: Russia launched 286 drones at Ukraine overnight, with Ukrainian air defenses intercepting 260 of them, according to the Ukrainian Air Force. The strikes occurred as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Turkey.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon’s Tyre after issuing evacuation warnings
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on the southern Lebanese city of Tyre after issuing evacuation warnings. Tens of thousands fled the city, though around 20,000 residents remained, including 15,000 displaced from surrounding villages. Attacks also targeted Tyre's port and Beirut's southern suburbs.

stories.title: What next for the struggling rural mothers in China who helped to build AI?
stories.summary: Thousands of rural women in China's southwestern Guizhou province performed data-labeling work that helped train autonomous driving AI systems. Based in the mountainous city of Tongren, where incomes are less than half of Beijing's, these workers now face an uncertain future as the industry evolves.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Sumy with drones, leaving one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kovpakivskyi district of Sumy, Ukraine, using unmanned aerial vehicles. A 52-year-old man was injured and two cars were damaged in the attack.

stories.title: Two more detained over attack on Czech drone maker accused of making arms for Israel
stories.summary: Czech authorities detained two additional foreign suspects in connection with a March 20 arson attack on a factory used by drone manufacturer LPP Holding. The company, which supplies Ukraine, denied any collaboration with Israel's Elbit Systems.

stories.title: Bilawal stresses political unity amid economic crisis triggered by US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari called for political unity in Pakistan in response to the economic crisis caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Speaking at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh on the 47th death anniversary of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, he praised Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi for participating in national consultations.

stories.title: Erdogan assures of continued support from Turkey for negotiations between Ukraine and Russia
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan pledged Turkey's continued support for negotiations between Ukraine and Russia, stating the region needs greater peace and stability.

stories.title: How bankers, bureaucrats and bystanders sustain Israel's genocide in Gaza
stories.summary: An analysis examines how financial institutions, government officials, and broader systemic actors contribute to sustaining military operations in Gaza. The piece highlights drone warfare, technology supply chains, and political silence as enablers of the ongoing violence.

stories.title: Iran conflict to forefront of UK religious and political leaders’ Easter messages
stories.summary: Religious and political leaders in the United Kingdom are centering their Easter messages on the conflict in the Middle East involving Iran. Archbishop of Canterbury Dame Sarah Mullally plans to call for peace and an end to violence in her first Easter sermon, while the Prime Minister urged Britons to choose community over division.

stories.title: China’s growing North Africa presence a structural challenge for Europe
stories.summary: China has accelerated investments across North Africa in 2026, expanding Belt and Road Initiative frameworks as the US-Israeli war with Iran disrupts Gulf shipping routes. With the Strait of Hormuz largely blocked to container traffic, Beijing is diversifying energy sources, posing a structural challenge to European influence in the region.

stories.title: Houthis claim joint operation with Iran targeting Israel sites
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed it conducted a joint military operation with Iran's Revolutionary Guard, the Iranian army, and Hezbollah targeting sites in Israel, including Ben Gurion Airport. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said the attack involved a ballistic missile and several drones.

stories.title: Russia evacuates 198 more staff from Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, agencies report
stories.summary: Russia's state nuclear company Rosatom evacuated an additional 198 staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday. The evacuation was reported by Russian news agencies amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Slovak PM Fico calls on EU to lift sanctions and resume dialogue with Russia after conversation with Hungarian PM Orban
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico, after talks with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, called on the European Union to lift sanctions on Russian oil and gas imports and restore supplies through the Druzhba pipeline.

stories.title: German males under 45 may need military approval for long stays abroad
stories.summary: Germany is considering a law requiring males under 45 to obtain military approval before extended stays abroad. Officials noted that travel approvals would generally be granted, and enforcement mechanisms for violations remain unclear.

stories.title: UAE condemns ‘acts of vandalism’ after anti-Israel riot at its embassy in Damascus
stories.summary: Protesters in Damascus attempted to storm the UAE embassy during demonstrations against an Israeli death penalty law, with some calling it the "Zionist embassy." A guard was seen kissing and hoisting a Palestinian flag while detaining a man who had flown it on the building. The UAE condemned the incident as "acts of vandalism."

stories.title: US arrests relatives of top Iranian commander assassinated in 2020 strike on Baghdad
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department announced the arrest of Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter, the niece and grandniece of slain Iranian general Qassem Soleimani, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked their lawful permanent resident status. Soleimani was killed in a U.S. drone strike in Baghdad in January 2020.

stories.title: Explosion hits pro-Israel centre in the Netherlands
stories.summary: An explosion struck a pro-Israel center run by Christians for Israel in the Dutch town of Nijkerk. No injuries were reported in the blast.

stories.title: Russian strike on Ukraine market kills five, wounds 25
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a covered market in the eastern Ukrainian city of Nikopol on Saturday, killing five people and wounding 25 others.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine rallies sweep Syria amid Gaza genocide and Israeli occupation
stories.summary: Pro-Palestinian protests took place across Syria, with demonstrators expressing anger over Israeli military operations in Gaza and Israeli occupation of southern Syrian territory, including the Golan Heights.

stories.title: From diplomacy to bombs: Western nihilism fueled Iran’s expansion - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece contends that decades of Western diplomatic engagement misjudged Iran's ideological ambitions, contributing to conditions that led to a war the West was unprepared to fight.

stories.title: Sudan: 'We Watched Them Die Before Our Eyes' - Sudan Health Workers Helpless Amid Medical Shortages
stories.summary: Health workers in Sudan's South Kordofan state report being unable to save patients due to severe medical supply shortages amid ongoing violence. A key maternity hospital faces overwhelming patient numbers with critically limited resources, as tens of thousands flee the region.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Iran, warning of severe consequences if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to make a deal before 'all hell reigns', hunt goes on for US pilot
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social giving Iran 48 hours to reach a deal, threatening severe consequences. A search continues for a missing US pilot.

stories.title: Sudan: WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Urges the World Not to Ignore the Sudan Crisi
stories.summary: World Health Organization Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged the international community not to ignore the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Sudan.

stories.title: FO rejects ‘misleading, unfounded’ commentary regarding financial deposits from UAE
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office rejected claims about financial deposits from the United Arab Emirates as "misleading and unfounded," calling the matter a routine transaction. A senior Pakistani official had said Islamabad would return $3.5 billion in debt to the UAE, funds originally extended in 2019 to stabilize Pakistan's balance of payments.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to make a deal as search continues for missing US pilot
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump gave Iran a 48-hour deadline to negotiate a deal, as American and Iranian forces continued searching for a downed U.S. airman. Trump warned Tehran would face severe consequences if it did not comply.

stories.title: Russia’s internet regulator orders outlets to delete reports linking bank disruptions to its website-blocking activity
stories.summary: Russia's federal internet regulator Roskomnadzor ordered Russian media outlets to delete reports linking a widespread disruption at major Russian banks on April 3 to the agency's own website-blocking activities.

stories.title: How will Pakistan deal with the fallout from Iran war?
stories.summary: The ongoing war in the Middle East is deepening Pakistan's economic crisis. Islamabad faces growing pressure to manage the diplomatic and financial fallout from the regional conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Russian missile strike hits Sumy region, two civilians injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a missile strike on the Popivka community in Ukraine's northeastern Sumy region, injuring two civilians.

stories.title: Dozens gather outside Presidential Administration in Moscow to submit petitions against messaging app blocks and mobile internet shutdowns
stories.summary: Dozens of people gathered outside the Presidential Administration building in Moscow to submit petitions protesting the blocking of messaging apps and shutdowns of mobile internet access in Russia.

stories.title: Siberian regional TV releases video of ‘grateful farmers’ who lost livestock to government seizures, but journalists identify participants as local officials
stories.summary: OTS, a television channel owned by Russia's Novosibirsk regional government, aired a video featuring supposedly grateful farmers who lost livestock to government seizures. Journalists identified the participants as local officials rather than actual farmers.

stories.title: China executes French national convicted in 2010 for drug trafficking
stories.summary: China executed a French national who had been sentenced to death in 2010 for drug trafficking. France's foreign ministry expressed its "consternation" at the execution.

stories.title: Trump: Iran faces ‘all hell’ if it doesn’t make a deal or open Hormuz in 48 hours
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran it faces "all hell" if it does not agree to a deal or reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours. A U.S. defense official said Israel is awaiting American approval to strike Iranian energy sites.

stories.title: Indonesia receives bodies of peacekeepers killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Indonesia received the bodies of its peacekeepers who were killed in southern Lebanon. Foreign Minister Sugiono called for a thorough United Nations investigation into the circumstances of their deaths.

stories.title: US takes relatives of Qassem Soleimani captive after revoking residency status
stories.summary: The United States detained Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter, relatives of slain Iranian commander Qassem Soleimani, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked their green cards. They are now in the custody of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

stories.title: For Trump, the cost of Iran war is rising
stories.summary: At least six U.S. KC-135 tanker aircraft were reportedly damaged in two Iranian missile and drone attacks on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. The U.S. has also lost at least 12 MQ-9 Reaper drones since the war with Iran began, according to some reports.

stories.title: Russia begins emergency hepatitis A vaccination in flood-hit region as more than 30 people are poisoned by drinking water
stories.summary: Russia's consumer health watchdog launched an emergency hepatitis A vaccination campaign in flood-affected areas of Dagestan after more than 30 people were poisoned by contaminated drinking water.

stories.title: Zelensky, Erdogan agree on new steps in Ukraine-Turkey security cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met in Istanbul and agreed on new steps to strengthen security cooperation between Ukraine and Turkey.

stories.title: Ukraine’s big boom FP-2 drones just blew up four Russian Orions inside their Crimean hangar
stories.summary: Ukrainian FP-2 drones struck a hangar in Russian-occupied Crimea, reportedly destroying four Russian Orion reconnaissance drones. The attack reflects Ukraine's expanding use of long-range drone strikes beyond the immediate front lines.

stories.title: Iran leaves door open for peace talks as hunt for missing US pilot continues
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war on Iran entered its sixth week with little prospect of peace talks. Iran has indicated it remains open to negotiations, while the search continues for a missing US pilot.

stories.title: Search for missing airman presents serious test for US
stories.summary: The U.S. military is searching for the weapons system officer of an F-15E Eagle that was downed during operations. Concerns are growing that the missing airman could be captured by Iran, which would significantly raise the stakes of the conflict.

stories.title: Armenia’s parliamentary speaker says country will leave CSTO and Eurasian Economic Union if Russia raises gas price
stories.summary: Armenia's parliamentary speaker Alen Simonyan warned that Armenia would leave the Collective Security Treaty Organization and the Eurasian Economic Union if Russia raises the price of natural gas it supplies to the country.

stories.title: Planning minister advocates for revising market timings to rein in oil import bill
stories.summary: Pakistani Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal proposed revising market operating hours to reduce oil and electricity consumption amid rising import costs linked to the global oil crisis. Speaking in Lahore, he emphasized the need for energy efficiency given Pakistan's reliance on imported fuel for electricity generation.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest antiwar protesters in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Israeli police clashed with and arrested antiwar protesters in Tel Aviv. Demonstrators had gathered to rally against the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike near Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant kills one: State media
stories.summary: A US-Israeli airstrike struck near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, killing at least one person, according to Iranian state media. The strike was the fourth to target the Bushehr area since the war began.

stories.title: Fourth person arrested over arson attack on Jewish ambulances in London
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested a fourth suspect, a 19-year-old man, in connection with the arson attack on Jewish volunteer ambulances in northwest London. He was detained at Westminster Magistrates' Court where three other suspects were being arraigned.

stories.title: Telegram founder says 65 million Russians use app daily via VPN despite blocking attempts
stories.summary: Telegram founder Pavel Durov stated that 65 million Russians use the messaging app daily through VPNs despite government blocking attempts. Durov noted that Russian authorities had spent years trying to ban both Telegram and VPN services.

stories.title: IDF announces Sgt. First Class Guy Ludar died while fighting in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced that Sergeant First Class Guy Ludar, a soldier in the Maglan Unit of the Commando Brigade from Yuvalim, was killed while fighting in Lebanon. His family was notified before his name was released.

stories.title: Ukraine launches probe into violations at Uzhhorod recruitment center
stories.summary: Ukraine's Operational Command West launched a special commission to investigate alleged violations at the Territorial Recruitment and Social Support Center in Uzhhorod.

stories.title: Tehran psychiatric hospital not usable after US-Israeli strike
stories.summary: A psychiatric hospital in Tehran has been rendered non-functional following a U.S.-Israeli military strike, according to the facility's chief. The hospital can no longer provide services to patients.

stories.title: Five EU finance ministers call for tax on energy companies’ windfall profits amid Iran war
stories.summary: Five EU finance ministers called for a tax on windfall profits earned by energy companies amid the Iran war. Oil and gas prices have spiked since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28.

stories.title: The war with Iran is a major setback to China’s Belt and Road Initiative - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion article argues that the war with Iran has undermined core assumptions of China's Belt and Road Initiative, representing a major strategic setback for Beijing.

stories.title: IDF says soldier killed, another seriously hurt by ‘friendly-fire’ in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces reported that Sgt. First Class Guy Ludar, 21, was killed by friendly fire during an overnight raid in southern Lebanon, with another soldier seriously wounded. Separately, the Israeli Air Force struck IRGC and Palestinian Islamic Jihad command centers in Beirut and renewed strikes on Tyre.

stories.title: Israeli forces destroy 17 UNIFIL cameras in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces destroyed 17 UNIFIL cameras in southern Lebanon and are razing buildings in Naqoura, the town that hosts UNIFIL's headquarters.

stories.title: Israel bombs Tyre in Lebanon after ordering residents to flee
stories.summary: Israel's military struck the southern Lebanese city of Tyre on Saturday after ordering residents to evacuate earlier in the day.

stories.title: Thousands of Sadr supporters condemn US, Israel at Baghdad rally
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of supporters of Iraqi Shiite leader Moqtada al-Sadr rallied across Iraq on Saturday to protest the US and Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Mideast war presents 'serious risk' for Africa: report
stories.summary: A joint report by the African Union and the African Development Bank warned that the ongoing Middle East war poses a serious risk to economic growth and living standards across Africa.

stories.title: Five killed, 27 injured as Russia launches over 50 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk кegion
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out over 50 attacks on three districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region on April 4, killing five people and injuring 27. The city of Nikopol suffered the heaviest damage.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy in Istanbul for security talks with Erdogan
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy arrived in Istanbul on Saturday for security talks with Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan. Zelenskiy described the planned discussions as "substantive."

stories.title: What we know so far about the US fighter jet shot down over Iran
stories.summary: A US fighter jet was shot down over Iran. The pilot was safely rescued, but a search and rescue operation continues for the jet's second crew member, according to US media reports.

stories.title: Netzach Yehuda's CNN altercation: Why religion is driving Israel toward extremism - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines the incident involving the IDF's Netzach Yehuda battalion and CNN, arguing that hardline religious influence is driving Israel toward extremism and undermining its democratic character.

stories.title: Three workers wounded in drone strike on Iraq's North Rumaila oilfield, sources say
stories.summary: Two drones struck the BP-operated North Rumaila oilfield in southern Iraq's Basra region on Saturday, wounding three Iraqi workers. Security and energy sources confirmed the attack.

stories.title: Universities hit as US, Israel ramp up attacks on Iran’s infrastructure
stories.summary: At least 30 universities in Iran have been impacted by US and Israeli strikes since the start of the war, according to Iranian authorities.

stories.title: Exhibition 'Target Destroyed: Sky of Kyiv Region' opens in Kyiv
stories.summary: An exhibition titled "Target Destroyed: Sky of Kyiv Region" opened at the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War in Kyiv, showcasing aspects of air defense operations over the Kyiv region.

stories.title: IDF admits air defense failures after Dimona, Arad missile impacts
stories.summary: The IDF acknowledged air defense failures after Iranian missiles impacted near Dimona and Arad. The chief of staff of the IDF's Air Defense Systems said the system, while world-leading, is not hermetic and that malfunctions occurred.

stories.title: Gaza genocide death toll rises to 72,291 amid ongoing Israeli strikes
stories.summary: The Palestinian health ministry reported that the death toll in Gaza has reached 72,291 killed and 172,068 wounded since October 7, 2023. Since an October 11 ceasefire, Israeli forces have killed at least 715 people and wounded 1,968, while rescuers recovered 756 bodies from rubble.

stories.title: Iran’s coastline: architecture of control
stories.summary: An overview of Iran's coastline and strategic islands highlights the country's network of military and defensive infrastructure along its shores.

stories.title: Ukraine peace talks on hold until end of Middle East war – presidential advisor
stories.summary: A Ukrainian presidential advisor said political and military peace negotiations have been paused due to the ongoing war in the Middle East. The humanitarian track of talks continues to function.

stories.title: Vehicle engulfed in flames after Israeli drone strike in central Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli drone struck a vehicle in central Gaza, engulfing it in flames. Palestinians in the area rushed to extinguish the fire following the strike.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills one in central Gaza, several wounded
stories.summary: An Israeli strike killed one Palestinian and wounded several others near the entrance to Maghazi camp in central Gaza. The casualties were transported to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah for treatment.

stories.title: US agents arrest niece, grand niece of Iran's Qassem Soleimani after Rubio revoked green cards
stories.summary: The US State Department confirmed that federal agents arrested Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter after Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked their green cards. The two are the niece and grand-niece of slain Iranian commander Qasem Soleimani and are now in ICE custody.

stories.title: NATO anniversary overshadowed by Trump’s threats
stories.summary: NATO's 76th anniversary on April 4 was marked by growing uncertainty over the alliance's future, as the United States under President Trump has expressed frustration with allies, including over NATO's response to the situation with Iran.

stories.title: Halting $400m White House ballroom project is national security risk, Trump officials say
stories.summary: The Trump administration argued before a federal appeals court that a judge's order halting construction of a $400 million White House ballroom poses a national security risk. US National Park Service lawyers stated the project includes heavily fortified materials meant to protect the president, his family, and staff.

stories.title: Israeli strikes damage hospital in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on buildings near a hospital in Lebanon damaged the medical facility and wounded 11 people.

stories.title: Shahid Khaqan urges govt to deregulate fuel prices, promote electric vehicles
stories.summary: Awaam Pakistan President Shahid Khaqan Abbasi urged the Pakistani government to deregulate petroleum prices and promote electric vehicles to cushion the economic impact of rising oil costs linked to the US-Israel war on Iran. Petrol prices in Pakistan have surged from Rs266.17 to Rs378, and diesel from Rs280.86 to Rs520.35.

stories.title: PMD forecasts countrywide spell of heavy rains from April 5-9
stories.summary: The Pakistan Meteorological Department forecast a spell of heavy rains beginning Sunday night in Balochistan and lasting until April 9 across the country's upper regions. The PMD warned of isolated heavy falls and hailstorms in areas across all provinces.

stories.title: Ukrainian Navy denies involvement in Russian An-26, Su-30 incidents in Crimea
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Navy denied involvement in incidents involving a Russian An-26 transport plane and an Su-30 fighter jet in occupied Crimea. Ukrainian officials suggested the causes may have been accidents or malfunctions within Russia's own systems.

stories.title: Israeli forces destroy UN peacekeeper cameras in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces destroyed 17 surveillance cameras belonging to UN peacekeepers at UNIFIL headquarters in Naqura, southern Lebanon, within 24 hours. A UNIFIL spokesperson said the cameras appeared to have been destroyed by some kind of laser. Israeli soldiers are present in Naqura.

stories.title: IDF recovers remains of soldier killed in War of Independence after 78 years
stories.summary: The IDF recovered the remains of Private Dov Permat, an Israeli soldier killed during the 1948 War of Independence, nearly 78 years after his death. The discovery brought closure to his family.

stories.title: Witkoff and Kushner may make first-ever Kyiv visit, Ukraine’s Presidential Office chief says
stories.summary: Ukraine's Presidential Office chief expects US envoys Keith Witkoff and Jared Kushner, along with Senator Lindsey Graham, to make their first visit to Kyiv after Orthodox Easter on April 12, as security guarantee talks advance.

stories.title: Turkish President Erdogan offers to host Ukraine-Russia-US talks, Zelenskyy says yes
stories.summary: Turkish President Erdogan offered to host Ukraine-Russia-US peace talks, and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy accepted. The two leaders also signed a security cooperation agreement and discussed joint gas development during a meeting on April 4.

stories.title: Iran’s oil exports from Kharg island increase despite war: Media
stories.summary: Iran's oil exports from Kharg Island have reportedly increased despite the ongoing conflict. US President Donald Trump has previously threatened to destroy the island, which serves as a vital oil export terminal.

stories.title: Trump weighs broader Cabinet shake-up as Iran war pressure grows
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is reportedly considering a broader Cabinet shake-up amid growing pressure related to the Iran war, with any reshuffling potentially serving as a White House reset.

stories.title: War update: 55 clashes since morning, fiercest fighting near Kostiantynivka
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 55 attacks on Ukrainian defensive positions since the start of the day, with the fiercest fighting concentrated in the Kostiantynivka sector of the front line.

stories.title: Iraq closes Shalamcheh crossing with Iran after airstrikes kill Iraqi
stories.summary: Iraq closed the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran on April 4 after airstrikes on the Iranian side of the border killed an Iraqi citizen, according to security sources.

stories.title: UAE condemns pro-Palestine protests targeting its embassy in Syria
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine protesters targeted the United Arab Emirates embassy in Damascus, Syria. The UAE condemned the demonstrations, and its foreign ministry called on Syrian authorities to uphold obligations to protect the embassy and its staff.

stories.title: US commits nearly all of stealthy long-range missiles to Iran war
stories.summary: The US military is committing nearly its entire inventory of stealthy JASSM-ER cruise missiles to the war against Iran, drawing from stockpiles designated for other regions including the Pacific. The missiles, valued at $1.5 million each, are being moved to US Central Command bases and RAF Fairford in the UK.

stories.title: Freed Palestinian prisoner dies in Egypt amid neglect concerns
stories.summary: A freed Palestinian prisoner died in Cairo, Egypt, under circumstances that raised concerns about medical negligence. Questions were also raised about the effects of prior Israeli detention on the individual's health.

stories.title: Iran targets Israel, Kuwait after Trump issues 48-hour deadline
stories.summary: Iran struck an oil facility and government offices in Kuwait after rejecting President Trump's 48-hour ultimatum, which Tehran called "stupid." The attacks followed Trump's threat to escalate strikes on Iranian civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to make deal or face 'Hell'
stories.summary: A strike near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant killed a guard, prompting Russia to announce the evacuation of 198 workers from the facility. US President Donald Trump gave Iran a 48-hour deadline to reach a deal or face severe consequences.

stories.title: Zelensky, Erdoğan hold talks in Istanbul
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Istanbul for talks. The meeting took place amid ongoing diplomatic efforts related to the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Italy’s Meloni meets Qatar emir to discuss energy issues amid Iran war
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Qatar's emir to discuss energy issues amid the ongoing war with Iran. Meloni is the first EU and NATO leader to visit the region since the conflict began.

stories.title: 'Gaza, Marseille is with you!': French boats set sail to join international aid flotilla
stories.summary: Approximately 20 French boats departed Marseille on Saturday to join an international flotilla of around 100 vessels planning to sail toward Gaza around April 20. Organizers said the effort aims to break the Israeli naval blockade and deliver humanitarian aid to the territory.

stories.title: Inside Chiburim: Yaron Shane’s mission to help IDF soldiers find Love After War
stories.summary: Yaron Shane discussed his organization Chiburim and its Love After War initiative, which connects Israeli soldiers and veterans with mentors and potential life partners.

stories.title: ‘Never refused to go to Islamabad’: Iran says US media misrepresenting its position on peace talks
