stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated on social media that Tehran never refused to travel to Islamabad for Pakistan-hosted peace talks aimed at ending the US-Israeli war on Iran. Araghchi accused US media of misrepresenting Iran's position and said Tehran seeks terms for a conclusive and lasting end to the conflict.

stories.title: Top diplomat Marco Rubio strips Qassem Soleimani’s niece of US residency
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked the US residency of Hamideh Soleimani Afshar, a niece of slain Iranian general Qassem Soleimani. The State Department accused her of being an outspoken supporter of Iran.

stories.title: Deadly strike on Nikopol market: Injury toll rises to 25, five killed
stories.summary: A Russian morning strike on a market in Nikopol, Ukraine, killed five people and injured at least 25, with the casualty toll rising throughout the day.

stories.title: ‘Like falling out of the sky’: Canadian astronaut describes ‘phenomenal’ Artemis journey
stories.summary: Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen described his experience aboard the Artemis 2 mission, saying the spacecraft's trajectory toward the Moon felt like "falling out of the sky." The four-person crew passed the halfway point between Earth and the Moon on Saturday, more than 150,000 miles from home, marking the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years.

stories.title: US arrests relatives of slain IRGC general Soleimani for supporting Iran’s regime
stories.summary: The US State Department arrested relatives of slain IRGC General Qassem Soleimani, including Hamideh Soleimani Afshar, accusing her of promoting Iranian propaganda while living a lavish lifestyle in Los Angeles. The legal status of relatives of an Iranian official named Larijani was also terminated.

stories.title: Ukrainian USFs strike Russian air defenses, hit radar systems in occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck two radar stations, a Tor surface-to-air missile system, and an anti-aircraft installation belonging to Russian forces. The targets were located in occupied Crimea and occupied parts of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions.

stories.title: New video reveals moment US-Israeli munitions impact Iranian bridge
stories.summary: New video footage shows multiple US-Israeli strikes hitting the B1 bridge in Iran's northern Alborz province on Thursday.

stories.title: Federal judge halts White House effort to collect university data on applicants’ race
stories.summary: US District Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV in Boston issued a preliminary injunction blocking the Trump administration from collecting university data on applicants' race. The ruling followed a lawsuit by 17 Democratic state attorneys general and applies to public universities in the plaintiffs' states.

stories.title: US arrests niece and grandniece of slain Iran general Qassem Soleimani
stories.summary: The Trump administration revoked the green cards or U.S. visas of at least four Iranian nationals connected to the current or former Iranian government. Two individuals, including relatives of slain IRGC commander Qassem Soleimani, were detained by immigration authorities and face deportation. Secretary of State Marco Rubio authorized the actions.

stories.title: ‘Horror movie’: officials investigate after 21 dead dogs wash up on Washington state shore
stories.summary: Authorities in Skagit County, Washington, are investigating after 21 dead dogs washed ashore on Guemes Island, roughly 80 miles north of Seattle, between March 26 and early April. Officials noted the canines appeared to be of similar size.

stories.title: Russian forces use chemical-agent munitions nearly 400 times in March
stories.summary: Russian forces used chemical-agent munitions nearly 400 times in March 2026, according to recorded cases. The munitions were equipped with irritant chemical agents.

stories.title: UAE condemns 'acts of vandalism' at its embassy in Damascus
stories.summary: The UAE's foreign ministry condemned acts of vandalism at its embassy in Damascus, Syria. It called on Syrian authorities to fulfill their obligations to protect the embassy and its diplomatic staff.

stories.title: Iraq closes Shalamcheh crossing with Iran after airstrikes kill Iraqi
stories.summary: Iraq closed the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran after an airstrike on the Iranian side of the crossing killed at least one Iraqi and seriously wounded five others. The strike reportedly hit a passenger reception area.

stories.title: Gaza’s Christians observe Good Friday mass amid Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Christians in Gaza held Good Friday mass services amid ongoing Israeli military operations and a continued siege. Reports indicated daily violations of the ceasefire in the territory.

stories.title: Sirens activated across Israel after attacks from Iran and Lebanon detected
stories.summary: The Israeli Home Front Command activated sirens across Israel after detecting a drone infiltration near the Lebanese border and an Iranian missile attack targeting Jerusalem and Ashdod. Explosions and falling debris were reported in those areas.

stories.title: Khawaja Asif warns India against conducting ‘false-flag operation’
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif accused India of planning a "false-flag operation" to blame Pakistan, warning New Delhi of a strong response. Speaking in Sialkot, Asif alleged India could stage an incident using its own operatives or detained Pakistanis.

stories.title: Trump says Iran has 48 hours to make deal as search for US pilot continues
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening consequences if no deal is reached. The post did not reference reports of a downed US fighter jet.

stories.title: Power outage reported in Haifa following missile debris drop
stories.summary: Israeli media reported a power outage in the Krayot area north of Haifa. Rescue teams received alerts about shrapnel falling in the city, coinciding with the outage.

stories.title: What the Iran-Iraq war can tell us about the US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: An analysis draws parallels between the current US-Israeli military campaign against Iran and the Iran-Iraq war of 1980, suggesting similar strategic miscalculations by leaders pursuing regime assumptions.

stories.title: IAEA says projectile hits near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, killing one
stories.summary: The IAEA reported that a projectile struck near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, killing one physical protection staff member. A building on site was damaged by shock waves and fragments, but no increase in radiation levels was detected.

stories.title: Hundreds protest against Israel in Syria amid death penalty law
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters marched in southern Syria in solidarity with Palestinians, denouncing Israeli incursions. The demonstrations took place amid reports of a new death penalty law in the country.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Naftogaz facilities in Poltava region again
stories.summary: Russian troops struck Naftogaz Group energy facilities in Ukraine's Poltava region. No casualties were reported in the attack.

stories.title: US authorities arrest relatives of late Iranian military commander who were living in Los Angeles
stories.summary: U.S. federal agents arrested Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter in Los Angeles after Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked their lawful permanent resident status. The State Department said the niece and grandniece of late Iranian commander Qassem Soleimani are now in ICE custody.

stories.title: UN watchdog voices 'deep concern' as Iran reports new attacks on nuclear plant
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency expressed deep concern and urged restraint following reported attacks near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, warning of the risk of a nuclear accident.

stories.title: Italian PM in Qatar after Saudi visit
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni arrived in Qatar following a visit to Saudi Arabia, where she held talks with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The trip is part of a diplomatic tour of Gulf states.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike targets food warehouse south of Iran, local media reports
stories.summary: A US-Israeli missile strike hit a food warehouse in the southern Iranian city of Bandar-e-Lengeh, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Displaced in Lebanon: 'Lives turned upside down'
stories.summary: More than 1.1 million people in Lebanon have been displaced by fighting in the south and Israeli airstrikes on Beirut's suburbs. Displaced families are struggling to maintain daily routines amid difficult conditions.

stories.title: US arrests relatives of deceased Iranian ​general Qasem ​Soleimani
stories.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained the niece and grand-niece of deceased Iranian military commander Qasem Soleimani, according to US officials.

stories.title: Fugitive mafia boss wanted for murder arrested at Amalfi coast luxury villa
stories.summary: Italian police arrested Roberto Mazzarella, head of the Mazzarella clan of the Naples-based Camorra organized crime group, at a luxury villa on the Amalfi coast. He had been one of Italy's most wanted fugitives, on the run for over a year on murder charges.

stories.title: Relatives of Qassem Soleimani arrested in US
stories.summary: US federal agents arrested two relatives of the late Iranian military commander Qasem Soleimani — his niece Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter — after Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked their lawful permanent resident status.

stories.title: Iran announces new air defence used to down US fighter jet
stories.summary: Iran announced it had deployed a new air defense system that it claimed was used to shoot down a US fighter jet. Iranian military leaders said they intended to regain control of their airspace from the United States.

stories.title: Ukrainian demining units clear nearly 900 hectares of liberated territories in March – Defense Ministry
stories.summary: Ukrainian demining units cleared 876 hectares of liberated territory during March, according to Ukraine's Defense Ministry.

stories.title: Search for missing US crew member of downed fighter jet enters second day
stories.summary: U.S. search and rescue operations continued for a second day for the missing crew member of an F-15E Strike Eagle downed over Iran. One pilot was rescued on Friday, but the second crew member remained unaccounted for as Iran faced continued heavy bombing and Israel extended operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Senegal bans government travel as Iran war oil shock hits public finances
stories.summary: Senegal banned government travel as an oil price shock caused by the Iran war strained public finances. Prime Minister announced he had already cancelled his own planned trips.

stories.title: Relatives of Qassem Soleimani arrested in the US
stories.summary: The US State Department confirmed that Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter, the niece and grand-niece of late Iranian commander Qasem Soleimani, were arrested and placed in ICE custody after Secretary of State Marco Rubio revoked their green cards.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike kills one in petrochemical plant attack, injures several others
stories.summary: A US-Israeli strike on a petrochemical plant in Mahshahr, southwestern Iran, killed one person and injured several others, according to the governor of Khuzestan province. Authorities said a resulting blaze at the Petrochemical Special Economic Zone was brought under control.

stories.title: Iran says US, Israel belong in Stone Age after Tehran university strike
stories.summary: An Iranian government minister responded to a strike on a Tehran university by stating that the US and Israel are the ones belonging in the Stone Age.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine strikes kill 10 as Zelensky travels to Turkey for talks
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged deadly strikes overnight and Saturday morning, killing 10 people and wounding dozens. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Istanbul for talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and a meeting with Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew.

stories.title: Child injured in Kharkiv as result of Russian drone crash
stories.summary: A child was injured in Kharkiv's Slobidskyi district after a Russian drone crashed in the area.

stories.title: UK charges three men with arson over attack on Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: British authorities charged three men with arson in connection with an attack on Jewish community ambulances. Two of the accused are British nationals, while the third holds dual British-Pakistani citizenship.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy inducts second Milgem-class corvette into fleet
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy inducted PNS Khaibar, its second Milgem-class corvette, built under a 2018 contract with Turkish state-owned firm ASFAT Inc. Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf attended the ceremony. Four corvettes total are being built, two in Turkey and two in Pakistan.

stories.title: UK arrests fourth suspect over arson attack on Jewish ambulances in London
stories.summary: UK counterterrorism police arrested a fourth suspect in connection with an arson attack on Jewish charity ambulances in London. Three others were previously charged with arson and recklessness as to whether life would be endangered.

stories.title: Trump threatens to unleash 'hell' on Iran if no deal made within 48 hours
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran had 48 hours to agree to a deal on opening the Strait of Hormuz or face severe consequences. Trump referenced a previous 10-day deadline he had set for Iran.

stories.title: Russia said coordinating with IDF on evacuation of workers from Iran nuclear plant
stories.summary: Russia's state nuclear company Rosatom announced it was evacuating 198 additional workers from Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant following US-Israeli strikes in the area. A guard at the facility was reportedly killed. Russia said it was coordinating the evacuation with the Israeli military.

stories.title: WATCH: Missile fragments land in Ramat Gan after Iranian missile barrage, one person injured
stories.summary: Missile fragments landed in Ramat Gan after an Iranian missile barrage, injuring one person. Israeli police and IDF sappers were dispatched to impact sites in the Tel Aviv and Sharon areas.

stories.title: Middle East war has caused 'geostrategic impasse', Erdogan says
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told NATO chief Mark Rutte that the military intervention against Iran had created a geostrategic impasse. Erdogan called on the international community to redouble efforts to end the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Police investigate explosion at Israel Centre in the Netherlands
stories.summary: Dutch police in the Netherlands are investigating reports of an overnight explosion at the Israel Centre in the town of Nijkerk. The incident was reported on Saturday, April 4.

stories.title: Three suspects ordered to stay in UK custody over Jewish charity attack
stories.summary: Three men in the United Kingdom were charged with arson after allegedly setting fire to ambulances belonging to a Jewish charity. A London court ordered them to remain in custody. Counter-terrorism police are investigating the incident as a potential antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: Russia slams US-Israeli strike on Iran's nuclear plant as 'evil'
stories.summary: Russia condemned a US-Israeli strike on Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, which hosts Russian staff. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called the attack an "evil deed" that resulted in loss of life and demanded an immediate halt to strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities.

stories.title: Witness records Israeli strike on building in Lebanon’s Tyre
stories.summary: A witness recorded video of an Israeli airstrike hitting a building in Burj Shamali, located in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: President, PM pay tribute to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto on 47th death anniversary
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to former Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto on his 47th death anniversary, emphasizing his contributions to Pakistan's constitution and the importance of justice and due process.

stories.title: Brazilian inmates reduce sentences through reading
stories.summary: Brazil has implemented one of the world's most formalized nationwide programs allowing inmates to reduce their sentences through reading. The initiative addresses challenges posed by the country's high per-capita incarceration rate, one of the largest in Latin America.

stories.title: Second suspect arrested in Brooklyn stray-bullet killing of seven-month-old baby
stories.summary: An 18-year-old suspect, Matthew Rodriguez, was arrested in Pennsylvania in connection with the stray-bullet killing of seven-month-old Kaori Patterson-Moore on a Brooklyn street. NYPD detectives working with U.S. marshals apprehended Rodriguez, the second suspect in the case.

stories.title: Iran has 48 hours to make a deal, says Trump, or US will unleash ‘hell’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Iran on his Truth Social platform, demanding it agree to a deal or open the Strait of Hormuz or face severe consequences. The strait is a critical waterway for global oil and gas trade.

stories.title: US-Israeli onslaught damages 55 libraries across Iran
stories.summary: US and Israeli strikes have damaged 55 libraries across Iran, with two completely destroyed, according to the head of Iran's public libraries' association. Since the war began in late February, at least 30 universities and various heritage sites have also been targeted.

stories.title: Why US and Russia are backing Viktor Orbán in Hungary election
stories.summary: Ahead of Hungary's election, U.S. Vice President JD Vance announced a visit to Budapest seen as an effort to bolster Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who trails in polls. Allegations of Russian interference and overt Washington support have raised questions about foreign influence on the Hungarian vote.

stories.title: Russian forces strike bus stop in Kherson, leaving one dead and several injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a public transport stop in the Korablevskyi district of Kherson at approximately 11:00, killing one person and injuring five others.

stories.title: PPP demands election schedule for Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly amid months-long delay in polls
stories.summary: Pakistan's PPP has demanded the immediate release of an election schedule for the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly, which has been without a sitting legislature for four months. Both general and local government elections were postponed indefinitely due to harsh weather conditions.

stories.title: Strikes rain down on northern Israel from Iran, Hezbollah
stories.summary: A barrage of Iranian missiles triggered sirens across northern Israel. Separately, Hezbollah announced it targeted a gathering of Israeli army vehicles and soldiers in the northern Israeli settlement of Kfar Yuval.

stories.title: Explosion hits pro-Israel centre in the Netherlands
stories.summary: An explosion struck a pro-Israel centre in the Netherlands, following a series of similar night-time attacks targeting Jewish-affiliated sites in the Netherlands and Belgium.

stories.title: 'Iran open to negotiations': Diplomacy shows signs of progress, 'damage to global economy continues'
stories.summary: Diplomatic developments suggest Iran may be open to negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz crisis, though analysts caution the situation remains unstable. A UNIDIR research fellow emphasized the limits of military solutions and the multidimensional nature of ongoing diplomacy. The crisis continues to cause significant damage to the global economy.

stories.title: Iran leaves door open for peace talks as hunt for missing US pilot continues
stories.summary: Iran has signaled openness to peace talks amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, while a search continues for a missing U.S. crew member whose F-15E was downed over Iranian territory. The developments come days after President Trump threatened to bomb Iran "back to the Stone Ages."

stories.title: Former US air force master sergeant pleads guilty to defrauding military out of $37m
stories.summary: Former U.S. Air Force Master Sergeant Alan Hayward James pleaded guilty to defrauding the military of $37 million by rigging bids and inflating costs on Pentagon IT contracts. The scheme ran for nine years beginning in April 2016, with James funneling funds to himself, family members, and co-conspirators.

stories.title: Exiled dissidents say Iran is seizing their family members, friends and property
stories.summary: Exiled Iranian dissidents reported that Tehran has intensified the seizure of family members, friends, and property belonging to opposition figures abroad. Some said the US-Israeli bombing campaign prompted Iranian authorities to worsen conditions for political prisoners.

stories.title: Vehicles burn in Israel after being hit with Iranian projectile debris
stories.summary: Vehicles caught fire in Ramat Gan, central Israel, after debris from an intercepted Iranian projectile struck the area. Video footage showed the burning vehicles.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike two Shahed launch bases in Russia's Kursk and Bryansk regions
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck two Shahed drone launch bases in Russia's Bryansk and Kursk regions. The targeted sites were located in Navlya and at the Khalino airfield.

stories.title: Russia evacuates 198 workers from Iran's Bushehr atomic plant
stories.summary: Russia evacuated 198 workers from Iran's Bushehr atomic plant following a US-Israeli attack on the facility. Rosatom, Russia's nuclear agency, has been gradually removing staff since the war began, with this being the largest evacuation to date. Agency head Alexey Likhachev described the situation as a worst-case scenario.

stories.title: Chinese surveillance tech rolled out in Africa with ZTE, Hikvision and Huawei at the helm
stories.summary: A new survey by the UK-based Institute of Development Studies found that African cities including Nairobi, Lusaka, and Abuja are deploying Chinese surveillance technologies from companies such as ZTE, Hikvision, and Huawei. Chinese banks are funding these "safe city" or "smart city" projects, which include surveillance cameras and command-and-control centers.

stories.title: U.K. charges three men with arson over attack on Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: Three men were charged in the United Kingdom with arson for setting fire to Jewish community ambulances on March 23. British Prime Minister Keir Starmer described the incident as a deeply shocking antisemitic attack.

stories.title: Israel targets southern Lebanon, as Hezbollah launches attacks on Israeli troops
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday. Hezbollah responded by firing missiles at an Israeli army gathering in Qantara and claimed attacks on the settlement of Kiryat Shmona in northern Israel.

stories.title: Russians attempt to cross Zherebets River in Kupiansk-Lyman direction – Trehubov
stories.summary: Russian forces attempted to cross the Zherebets River in the Kupiansk-Lyman direction, according to Ukrainian spokesperson Trehubov. The crossing attempts have not significantly impacted the overall battlefield situation.

stories.title: Three suspects in UK Hatzalah ambulance arson arrested, charged for attack
stories.summary: Three suspects were arrested and charged in connection with an arson attack on UK Hatzalah ambulances. British nationals Hamza Iqbal, 20, and Rehan Khan, 19, along with a 17-year-old British-Pakistani dual citizen, were charged after four ambulances were destroyed.

stories.title: Impact of Iran war in Pakistan: Fuel prices rise by over 50%
stories.summary: Fuel prices in Pakistan have risen by more than 50 percent as a consequence of the war involving Iran. The price surge is straining consumers and the broader economy in the country.

stories.title: Iran says it will not relinquish control over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker declared the country will not relinquish control over the Strait of Hormuz as long as the US-Israel war continues and possibly beyond. The strait is a critical global shipping route.

stories.title: Russian attack on Ukraine market kills five
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a busy market area in a southern Ukrainian town on Saturday morning, killing five people and injuring 21 others.

stories.title: Former IRGC child executioner tells ‘Post’ how he became devout Christian dissident
stories.summary: Iranian dissident Afshin Javid, a former IRGC child executioner, spoke to the Jerusalem Post about his transformation into a Christian dissident. He described how the Iranian regime indoctrinates children to aspire to martyrdom.

stories.title: SSU and Defense Forces strike Alchevsk Metallurgical Plant for second time in one month, halting its operations
stories.summary: Ukraine's SSU and UAV Forces of the Armed Forces conducted a second strike within a month on the Alchevsk Metallurgical Plant in Russian-occupied Luhansk region, halting its operations.

stories.title: Young Israeli voters shifting right, Netanyahu leads as preferred candidate - poll
stories.summary: A recent poll indicates young Israeli voters are shifting toward right-wing political positions. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leads as the preferred candidate among this demographic.

stories.title: Storm Dave expected to cause travel disruption over Easter weekend
stories.summary: Storm Dave is forecast to bring heavy snow and gale-force winds across northern parts of the UK over the Easter weekend. The Met Office issued yellow and amber severe weather warnings for Scotland and northern regions, with up to 30 centimetres of snow possible.

stories.title: Rs20 million fine for a deleted tweet: The cost of irreverence?
stories.summary: Pakistan's Cricket Board fined fast bowler Naseem Shah 20 million rupees for a deleted social media post on X that referenced PCB leadership and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz at a Pakistan Super League event. Shah publicly apologized for the post.

stories.title: Iran announces new air defence system used to target US fighter jet on Friday
stories.summary: Iran announced it used a new air defence system on Friday to shoot down a US fighter jet. A spokesperson for Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya joint military command said Tehran would achieve full control over its airspace.

stories.title: Iran war: Senegal limits foreign visits for ministers as fallout from conflict deepens
stories.summary: Senegal's government banned all non-essential foreign trips for ministers as a cost-saving measure amid an energy crisis linked to the Iran war. The country imports most of its petroleum products, leaving it vulnerable to supply disruptions such as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has driven crude prices higher.

stories.title: Iran executes two linked to opposition group, media say
stories.summary: Iran executed two men on Saturday who were convicted of ties to the People's Mojahedin Organisation of Iran, an opposition group, and of carrying out armed attacks. The executions were reported by Iranian domestic media.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike fuel trains in temporarily occupied Luhansk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces struck railway fuel trains in the Russian-occupied part of the Luhansk region and destroyed a Russian Inokhodets drone at the Kirovske airfield in Crimea.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant kills one
stories.summary: A US-Israeli strike near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant killed one person. It was the fourth strike targeting the Bushehr area since the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes target over 30 universities across Iran, science minister says
stories.summary: Iran's science minister Hossein Simai Sarraf said US-Israeli strikes have hit more than 30 universities across Iran since the war started. He made the remarks during a visit to Shahid Beheshti University in northern Tehran, which was attacked on Friday.

stories.title: After High Court appeal, anti-war protests to be permitted under strict limitations
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court ruled that anti-war protests must be permitted under strict limitations after the Association for Civil Rights filed an urgent appeal. Supreme Court head Isaac Amit stated that wartime conditions do not negate the right to protest.

stories.title: Iran targets US sites in Gulf, amid UAE interception efforts
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it launched attacks on American sites on Kuwait's Bubiyan Island and targeted Bahrain's Patriot missile systems. The UAE defence ministry reported intercepting 79 missiles and drones, including 23 ballistic missiles and 56 drones, in 24 hours.

stories.title: Iran just threatened to attack US companies: Who's on the list?
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened to attack 16 major US companies operating in the region, accusing them of involvement in what it called "terrorist espionage." No specific timeline for potential attacks was given.

stories.title: New Iranian attack on Israel leaves vehicles on fire, buildings damaged
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported another wave of Iranian missiles launched toward Israel. Israeli media said several vehicles caught fire and structures, including a residential building, were damaged in the attack.

stories.title: Drone attack on Kharkiv: Injury toll rises to five
stories.summary: A Russian UAV attack on the Nemyshlianskyi district of Kharkiv injured five people, with the casualty toll rising from initial reports.

stories.title: Qatar and Italy call for de-escalation efforts
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met in Doha and called for de-escalation of the ongoing war. The leaders discussed the conflict's impact on global energy and supply chains.

stories.title: Israeli strikes damage hospital in Lebanon’s Tyre; ground invasion advances
stories.summary: Israeli strikes near the Lebanese Italian Hospital in the southern Lebanese city of Tyre injured at least 11 people and damaged the facility. The attack coincided with an advancing Israeli ground operation in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Russia made nearly no territorial gains in Ukraine in March: Analysis
stories.summary: An analysis found that Russia's military seized only 23 square kilometers across the entire front line in Ukraine during March, with Russian forces losing territory in some areas.

stories.title: Iranian targeting of Israel-linked ship causes fire onboard
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy targeted an Israel-linked vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire onboard, according to Iranian state media.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes target southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel struck the town of Burj al-Shamali in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon on Saturday, along with the areas of Habbouch and Zrariyeh. The attacks followed Israeli-issued expulsion orders for residents in several areas across southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Pakistan rejects media reports of collapse of initiative to facilitate U.S., Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's government rejected media reports suggesting the collapse of its initiative to facilitate negotiations between the United States and Iran. The speculation arose after a Foreign Ministry official briefed journalists on Pakistan's mediation efforts regarding the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Forget democracy, says Burkina Faso military leader Traore
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military leader, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, declared his intention to rule for the long term, publicly dismissing democracy by stating that it "kills."

stories.title: Russians strike Nikopol with drones, leaving five killed and 19 injured
stories.summary: Russian FPV drone strikes on the city of Nikopol killed five people and wounded 19 others, including a 14-year-old girl.

stories.title: China moves to regulate digital humans, bans addictive services for children
stories.summary: China has introduced new regulations governing the digital human industry, including a ban on addictive digital human services targeting children. The rules establish governance guidelines and red lines for the sector's development.

stories.title: Strikes in Lebanon: Israeli army orders evacuation of the city of Tyre
stories.summary: The Israeli army ordered the evacuation of the southern Lebanese city of Tyre amid ongoing strikes in Lebanon. The order came as Israel continued its military operations in the region.

stories.title: Pakistan announces free public transport as energy crisis bites
stories.summary: Pakistan announced that state-run public transport in the capital Islamabad and in Punjab, the country's most populous province, will be free for one month. The measure follows drastic fuel price increases driven by the Iran war.

stories.title: France announces crisis loans for firms hit by fuel-price surge
stories.summary: France announced an emergency loan programme on Friday to assist small and medium-sized businesses affected by soaring fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict. The crisis loans aim to support firms struggling with increased energy costs.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Israel expands operations in Lebanon
stories.summary: The article discusses Israel's expanded military operations in Lebanon, featuring analysis from Simon Mabon, Professor of International Politics and Middle East Studies at Lancaster University.

stories.title: Ukraine hits Crimea drone base: One Inokhodets UAV destroyed, three damaged — each unit worth millions
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Kirovskoe airfield in Crimea, destroying one Inokhodets UAV and damaging three others, each valued at millions of dollars. A separate drone strike halted operations at the Alchevsk steel plant, a supplier of parts for Russian T-90M tanks.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelensky in Istanbul for security talks with Erdogan
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to Istanbul for security talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Ukraine has recently signed security cooperation agreements with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar during similar diplomatic visits.

stories.title: Iran braces as US expected to respond to downing of two aircraft
stories.summary: The US is reportedly preparing a response to Iran's downing of two American aircraft. Israel and the US are planning to extend military operations against Iran for at least two more weeks, with a list of targets already drawn up.

stories.title: 1 dead in Peru football stadium tragedy, dozens injured
stories.summary: At least one person died and 60 others were injured in an apparent crowd crush at Alianza Lima's Alejandro Villanueva Stadium in Lima, Peru, on Friday night. Police said the incident occurred due to a surge of fans in the south stands ahead of a scheduled match against rival club Universitario.

stories.title: AFU adjusts training to counter Russian drones – Syrskyi
stories.summary: Armed Forces of Ukraine Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced that the AFU are adjusting training programs to better counter Russian unmanned aerial vehicles and strengthening technological capabilities.

stories.title: Why China is worried by Japan’s plans to change rules on arms sales
stories.summary: Japan is considering relaxing restrictions on offensive weapons exports, currently limited to five defensive categories including rescue, transport, and surveillance. A draft government document would scrap these categories, prompting concern from China that the change could lead to Japanese arms reaching war zones or Taiwan.

stories.title: IRGC claims attack on Israel-linked vessel in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for targeting an Israel-linked vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. No further details about the vessel or casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: Downed planes spell new peril for Trump as Tehran hunts missing U.S. pilot
stories.summary: Two U.S. warplanes were downed over Iran and the Persian Gulf, leaving one American pilot missing. The prospect of a U.S. service member on the run inside Iran raises the stakes for Washington in a conflict that lacks broad public support domestically.

stories.title: US intel warns Iran won’t budge on Hormuz
stories.summary: US intelligence reports concluded that Iran is unlikely to give up control of the Strait of Hormuz, which carries roughly one-fifth of global oil shipments. Analysts assess the strait represents Tehran's primary leverage over Washington.

stories.title: Hezbollah sees potential win as Israel backs down from disarmament goal - analysis
stories.summary: Hezbollah views Israel's reported retreat from its goal of disarming the group as a strategic victory. The shift is seen as benefiting Hezbollah's long-term survival and influence in Lebanon.

stories.title: Projectile hits near Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, killing one: IAEA
stories.summary: A projectile struck near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, killing one person, according to the IAEA. Tehran stated this was the fourth attack targeting the area around the nuclear facility since the US-Israel war on Iran began.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian attack on Sumy rises to 13
stories.summary: A massive overnight Russian drone attack on the city of Sumy injured 13 people, including one child, with the casualty toll rising from earlier counts.

stories.title: Ukrainian Strikes Hit Southern Russia, Killing 1 and Wounding Several Others
stories.summary: Ukrainian strikes hit targets in southern Russia, killing one person and wounding several others. Unverified reports suggested the attacks targeted chemical plants linked to fertilizer and explosives production.

stories.title: Afghanistan quake kills 12, including 8 members of same family
stories.summary: An earthquake in Afghanistan killed 12 people, including eight members of the same family. A child aged around two was the sole survivor from the household and was injured in the tremor, according to Afghanistan's disaster management agency.

stories.title: One killed, dozens hurt as football stadium event in Peru goes awry
stories.summary: One person was killed and approximately 60 others were injured during a flag-waving event known as Matute at the Alejandro Villanueva Stadium in Lima, Peru.

stories.title: Iranian foreign minister calls for 'conclusive and lasting' terms to end war
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran seeks "conclusive and lasting" terms to end the war, accusing US media of misrepresenting Tehran's stance. He thanked Pakistan for its mediation efforts and affirmed Iran has never refused to visit Islamabad for negotiations.

stories.title: Afghanistan quake kills 12, including 8 from family who had just left Iran
stories.summary: A 5.8-magnitude earthquake struck northeastern Afghanistan's Badakhshan province on Friday evening, killing 12 people. Eight of the dead were members of a single refugee family on the outskirts of Kabul who had recently returned from Iran.

stories.title: ‘Not quite Greggs’: TikTok creators put London’s ‘gentrified’ bakeries to the test
stories.summary: TikTok creators in London have sparked a viral debate by reviewing artisan bakeries across the capital, questioning the cost and cultural accessibility of "gentrified" establishments. The trend began when a young woman posted about her weekend visits to upscale north London bakeries, prompting local residents to say they had never heard of the businesses.

stories.title: Record high ocean temperatures off southern California raise fears of prolonged marine heatwave
stories.summary: Shoreline monitoring stations operated by the Scripps Institution of Oceanography have recorded record-high ocean temperatures off southern California over the past three months. The La Jolla station registered temperatures 10°F above the historical average at one point, raising concerns about a prolonged marine heatwave that could disrupt marine ecosystems.

stories.title: ‘It broke our home’: family demands answers after death of man abandoned by US border agents
stories.summary: Nurul Shah Alam, a nearly blind Rohingya refugee, died after being abandoned by US border agents in a Buffalo, New York parking lot. His death has been ruled a homicide, and his family is demanding answers about the circumstances surrounding his treatment.

stories.title: Angel Studio’s new animated ‘David’ will feel familiar to Israelis – and Christians, too
stories.summary: Angel Studio's animated film "David," a musical retelling of the biblical shepherd who became king of the Israelites, is now playing in Israeli theaters in Hebrew. The dubbing features Israeli performers Sasson Shaulov, Miri Mesika, and Shahar Tavoch.

stories.title: 6 wounded as Iran cluster bombs smash homes in central Israel; IDF hits Iran infrastructure
stories.summary: Six people were wounded in central Israel after Iranian cluster munitions struck residential areas. Israeli jets retaliated by hitting a petrochemical facility in Iran, with additional strikes reported at a cement plant and near the perimeter of the Bushehr nuclear power plant. The US continued searching for its downed pilot in Iran.

stories.title: Klympush-Tsintsadze predicts difficult negotiations for Ukraine's EU membership
stories.summary: Ivanna Klympush-Tsintsadze, chair of the Verkhovna Rada's EU integration committee, stated that Ukraine's negotiations for European Union membership will be difficult.

stories.title: Israel’s unchecked war machine
stories.summary: Israel is engaged in military operations on multiple fronts simultaneously. The ongoing conflicts show no immediate signs of de-escalation.

stories.title: 58 tortillas, five hot sauces and one toilet: life aboard spacecraft Orion
stories.summary: The four-member Artemis II crew aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft is en route to the Moon, carrying supplies including 58 tortillas and five hot sauces. Mission specialist Christina Koch became the first woman to venture into deep space. The crew shares a living space equivalent to two minivans.

stories.title: Hong Kong IP festival Con-Con draws crowds on opening day
stories.summary: The inaugural Con-Con Hong Kong 2026 intellectual property festival opened Saturday at AsiaWorld-Expo, drawing large crowds of fans and cosplayers. The two-day event featured pop culture franchises including Godzilla, along with local designs, licensing showcases, and IP business matching opportunities.

stories.title: Zelensky imposes sanctions on entities supporting Russia's defense industry
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky enacted an NSDC decision imposing sanctions on Russian entities supporting Russia's military-industrial complex, helping circumvent existing sanctions, or conducting illegal business in occupied Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Tehran rejects 48-hour ceasefire proposal from U.S., Iranian media, says Iranian media
stories.summary: Tehran rejected a 48-hour ceasefire proposal from the United States, according to Iranian media reports. The refusal signals a continued hardening of Iran's negotiating position amid the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: Leak reveals Russian campaign to discredit Milei through Argentine media outlets
stories.summary: An investigation based on leaked documents found that a spy group linked to Russian foreign intelligence funded over 250 articles across at least 23 Argentine digital media outlets between June and October 2024. The campaign aimed to discredit Argentine President Javier Milei's government.

stories.title: Israel destroys bridges, kills more civilians in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes targeted bridges, ports, and a hospital in Lebanon, killing at least three more civilians and damaging vital infrastructure.

stories.title: ‘Iran is being destroyed in front of our eyes’: Tehran is gripped by fear
stories.summary: Tehran came under heavy bombardment as the fifth week of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran drew to a close. Residents of the Iranian capital described widespread fear amid ongoing strikes targeting the city.

stories.title: Iran executes two linked to Opposition group: reports
stories.summary: Iran executed two men linked to the banned People's Mojahedin Organisation of Iran (MEK). The men were reportedly arrested in January 2024 and had their death sentences upheld. The executions follow four other MEK-linked executions earlier in the same week.

stories.title: Iran, US race to find crew member of crashed American fighter jet
stories.summary: Iranian and U.S. forces are searching for a missing American pilot after two U.S. warplanes were downed over Iran and the Gulf. Two other airmen were rescued. The incident underscores risks to U.S. and Israeli aircraft as the conflict enters its sixth week.

stories.title: Videos show US missiles being launched from Kuwait into Iran
stories.summary: FRANCE 24 verified and geolocated multiple videos showing US HIMARS missile launchers firing from Kuwaiti territory into Iran on at least two occasions, March 24 and 31. The evidence contradicts denials from Persian Gulf Arab states that their territory is being used in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Red Crescent worker killed in Iran's Isfahan
stories.summary: A US-Israeli airstrike killed a Red Crescent humanitarian worker in Mobarakeh, located in Iran's Isfahan province, according to Iran's Fars News Agency.

stories.title: Drone strike on Rumaila oil field leaves three wounded
stories.summary: A drone strike on the Rumaila oil field in Iraq wounded three people, according to Reuters, citing security and energy sources.

stories.title: Cement plant struck by US-Israeli assault on Iran
stories.summary: A US-Israeli strike hit a cement plant in Bandar Khamir in Iran's southern Hormozgan province. The deputy governor reported no casualties, and the plant continued normal operations.

stories.title: Russian drone attack damages homes, cars in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack overnight damaged residential buildings and vehicles in Ukraine's Cherkasy region.

stories.title: Strike kills one Iraqi PMF fighter near Syria border
stories.summary: A strike near the Syria border killed one fighter from Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF). The PMF has repeatedly blamed such attacks on the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Drone, missile strike kills one in Russia’s Rostov: Governor
stories.summary: A combined drone and missile strike killed one person in Russia's Rostov region, according to the regional governor. Falling drone debris also struck a foreign-flagged cargo vessel in the Sea of Azov, causing a fire. Air defenses intercepted additional drones over Taganrog Bay and other districts.

stories.title: US-Israeli hit on Iraq-Iran border responsible for killing Iraqi citizen: Report
stories.summary: A US-Israeli strike on the Shalamcheh border crossing terminal in Khorramshahr, southwestern Iran, killed one Iraqi citizen and wounded two others, according to Iranian media citing the deputy governor of Khuzestan province.

stories.title: Explosion hits Christian pro-Israel center in the Netherlands
stories.summary: An explosion struck a Christian pro-Israel center in the Netherlands, though no injuries were reported. The incident is part of a recent wave of explosions targeting Jewish and Israel-related institutions across Europe.

stories.title: What we know so far about the search for missing US airman in Iran
stories.summary: US and Iranian forces are conducting a search for a missing American crew member after a US warplane was shot down over or near Iran. Details about the exact location and circumstances of the incident remain under investigation.

stories.title: Lebanese forced to bury their dead twice as war robs them of final goodbyes
stories.summary: As Israel expands its military invasion of southern Lebanon, displaced Lebanese civilians have been forced to bury their dead in temporary graves, unable to perform traditional funeral rites. Communities report being robbed of final goodbyes due to ongoing hostilities.

stories.title: Cubans study oil tanker diplomacy for signs of progress in secret talks with US
stories.summary: A sanctioned Russian oil tanker, the Anatoly Kolodkin, docked at Cuba's Matanzas oil terminal and unloaded 700,000 barrels of crude, apparently passing through the US oil blockade imposed by President Trump. The delivery has prompted speculation in Cuba about possible behind-the-scenes diplomatic progress between Havana and Washington.

stories.title: Strike near Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant kills 1, says IAEA
stories.summary: The IAEA confirmed that a projectile struck near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, killing one site protection staff member and damaging a building with shock waves and fragments. No radiation increase was reported.

stories.title: Israel says it is striking Hezbollah sites in Beirut after destroying bridge
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it was striking Hezbollah sites in Beirut after destroying a bridge in eastern Lebanon. Local media reported two strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs.

stories.title: EU membership by 2027 'unrealistic' for Ukraine – MP Klympush-Tsintsadze
stories.summary: Ukrainian MP Ivanna Klympush-Tsintsadze said that EU membership by 2027 is unrealistic for Ukraine, citing the pace of reforms and the number of procedures still required.

stories.title: The invisible risk: Can you really trust your ‘private’ AI assistant to keep your secrets?
stories.summary: Israeli cybersecurity firm Check Point discovered a vulnerability in ChatGPT's system that could allow data extraction without triggering security alarms.

stories.title: Police investigating explosion at Israel Center in the Netherlands - report
stories.summary: An explosion struck the Israel Center in the Netherlands. Local law enforcement reported no injuries but confirmed the building sustained minor damage. An investigation is underway.

stories.title: Bahrain cracks down on dissent as Iran war reignites internal unrest
stories.summary: Bahrain has arrested dozens of people during the ongoing Iran war for filming strikes and demonstrations, expressing support for Iran, or on suspicion of espionage. The crackdown on dissent comes as the conflict reignites internal unrest in the monarchy, which hosts the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet.

stories.title: Lebanon’s displaced Shia Muslims face rising hostility as airstrikes fuel fear and evictions
stories.summary: Displaced Shia Muslims in Lebanon are facing rising hostility, including evictions, as Israeli airstrikes continue. Sectarian tensions remain a deeply sensitive issue in Lebanon, which fought a 15-year civil war ending in 1990 that largely split along sectarian lines.

stories.title: Three peacekeepers wounded in Lebanon are Indonesian: U.N.
stories.summary: Three United Nations peacekeepers wounded in an explosion in Lebanon were identified as Indonesian nationals. The U.N. Information Centre in Jakarta confirmed their identities but said the origin of the explosion remained unknown.

stories.title: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian market kills five, Moscow intensifies attacks
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a covered market in Nikopol, eastern Ukraine, on Saturday, killing five people and injuring 30 others. The Ukrainian air force reported that Russia launched 286 drones overnight, of which 260 were intercepted.

stories.title: Four civilians killed, 11 injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv region over past day
stories.summary: Four civilians were killed and 11 others injured in Russian shelling across Ukraine's Kharkiv region over a 24-hour period. The attacks targeted multiple locations throughout the region.

stories.title: Iraq closes border crossing with Iran after citizen killed in air strike
stories.summary: Iraq closed the Shalamcheh border crossing on its southern border with Iran after attacks on the Iranian side of the crossing killed an Iraqi citizen, according to security sources.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran hunts crew member of crashed U.S. jet after one reported rescued
stories.summary: President Donald Trump was briefed on the downing of a U.S. F-15 warplane inside Iran, which triggered a major search-and-rescue operation. Iranian and American forces raced to recover the jet's crew, with Iran hunting for one crew member after the other was reportedly rescued.

stories.title: UN says three peacekeepers wounded in Lebanon are Indonesian
stories.summary: The UN Information Centre in Jakarta confirmed that three peacekeepers wounded in Lebanon are Indonesian nationals. The origin of the explosion that injured them remains unknown.

stories.title: Drone attack sparks fires at chemical plants in Russia's Tolyatti
stories.summary: In the early hours of April 4, drones struck the city of Tolyatti in Russia's Samara region, igniting fires near the Tolyattikauchuk and KuibyshevAzot chemical plants. The attack targeted industrial infrastructure in the area.

stories.title: Senegal cuts official travel as high oil prices put new pressure on budget
stories.summary: Senegalese Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko announced cuts to official travel due to budgetary pressure from high oil prices, canceling planned trips to Niger, Spain, and France. He made the announcement at a youth event in Mbour.

stories.title: At least four people killed in Russian attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine killed at least four people, while a Ukrainian strike on Russia's southern Rostov region resulted in at least one death.

stories.title: Israel vows to strike industrial, military sites in latest barrage
stories.summary: The Iranian Revolutionary Guard announced its 94th wave of attacks against Israel, stating it would target industrial and military sites as well as Israeli army commanders and troops.

stories.title: Syrian government understating kidnappings of Alawite women: report
stories.summary: A report alleges the Syrian government has understated the scale of kidnappings of Alawite women and girls, with investigations indicating dozens have disappeared and faced sexual and violent abuse.

stories.title: Iranian drone attack on US embassy in Riyadh more destructive than initially revealed - report
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal report indicated that a recent Iranian drone strike on the US embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, caused significantly more damage than initially disclosed, potentially putting hundreds of people at risk.

stories.title: Hide, find water: Ex-airmen detail how to survive being shot down
stories.summary: Former U.S. Air Force personnel described survival tactics for aviators shot down behind enemy lines, as American and Iranian forces competed to locate a missing crew member in Iran. Retired brigadier general Houston Cantwell explained how SERE (survival, evasion, resistance, and escape) training prepares pilots for such scenarios.

stories.title: Reports of material damage after latest Iranian attack on Israel
stories.summary: Medical emergency teams were dispatched to Bnei Brak and Tel Aviv following an Iranian attack that reportedly damaged buildings. Israeli media reported that cluster missiles were used during the strikes on central Israel.

stories.title: Fire in Kyiv office building after Russian drone strike fully extinguished
stories.summary: A fire caused by a Russian drone strike on a three-story office and warehouse building in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district has been fully extinguished. The blaze broke out following the early morning attack on April 4.

stories.title: Pakistan government slashes petrol price by PKR 80 per litre, day after sharp hike met severe backlash
stories.summary: Pakistan's government announced an unprecedented 42.7 percent increase in petrol prices and a 55 percent increase in diesel prices. Severe public backlash prompted authorities to slash the petrol price by 80 Pakistani rupees per litre the following day.

stories.title: Unions privately voice misgivings over BMA pay demands and doctors’ strikes
stories.summary: Several UK trade unions have privately expressed concerns about the British Medical Association's pay demands and its planned doctors' strikes scheduled for next week. The BMA rejected the government's 3.5% pay rise offer for doctors, which exceeded the offer made to other NHS staff, drawing frustration from senior union figures over the conduct of negotiations.

stories.title: Is Taiwan’s opposition KMT splitting into pro-US and pro-Beijing camps?
stories.summary: Taiwan's main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT), is showing internal divisions ahead of chairwoman Cheng Li-wun's planned April visit to mainland China, which may include a meeting with Xi Jinping. Disagreements over defense spending and ties with Washington and Beijing are fueling the rift.

stories.title: Compound Chinese surnames come from historical figures, ancient states; now fewer than 100 remain
stories.summary: An overview of compound Chinese surnames traces their origins to historical figures and ancient states. Once numbering in the hundreds, fewer than 100 compound surnames remain in use today, with Ouyang being the most common.

stories.title: One dead and dozens injured at Peru football stadium during pre-match event
stories.summary: At the Alejandro Villanueva Stadium in Lima, Peru, one person was killed and dozens were injured during a flag-waving event held on Friday ahead of a derby match between Alianza Lima and Universitario de Deportes. Initial reports suggested a wall collapse, but Alianza Lima stated there were no structural failures at the arena.

stories.title: Incoming missile salvo from Iran, Israeli army says
stories.summary: The Israeli military detected a missile salvo launched from Iran toward Israel. The Home Front Command issued early warnings to areas in central Israel and the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Vietnam's Israel defence ties complicate historic Palestinian solidarity
stories.summary: Vietnam has entered into a series of arms deals with Israel in recent years, complicating Hanoi's historically strong solidarity with the Palestinian cause.

stories.title: Iran demands explanations from Saudis and UAE after Chinese-made drone was shot down
stories.summary: Iran demanded explanations from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates after a Chinese-made Wing Loong II drone was shot down over the city of Shiraz. Both Gulf states are known to possess the reconnaissance and strike-capable drones.

stories.title: Far-right Israeli influencer banned from TikTok for breaking harassment rules
stories.summary: TikTok removed the account of far-right Israeli influencer Roi Star after he was flagged for violating harassment rules. His videos showed him harassing and pepper-spraying left-wing activists in the West Bank.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant kills one
stories.summary: A joint US-Israeli strike hit near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, killing one security staff member and damaging a side building, according to the Iranian Atomic Energy Organization. The main plant was reported unaffected and production continued.

stories.title: Shooting down of US jets marks a potential turning point in the war
stories.summary: The downing of a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle over Iran and an A-10 over the Gulf marks a significant development in the six-week U.S.-Israel-Iran conflict. Analysts describe the incidents as a symbolic and potentially strategic setback for Washington in what had been a largely asymmetric air campaign.

stories.title: Ukraine has no plans to mobilize women, no mechanisms being developed – Ground Forces
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ground Forces stated they have no plans to mobilize women and are not developing any mechanisms for such a process. The announcement addressed public speculation about potential changes to Ukraine's mobilization policies.

stories.title: Costly reliance
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has caused global economic reverberations, with Pakistan hiking fuel prices and shortening school schedules in response. Rising energy costs are affecting countries across the region. Attention is focused on a U.S. deadline of April 6 for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel says striking Hezbollah sites in Beirut after destroying bridge
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on what it described as Hezbollah sites in Beirut, Lebanon, after destroying a bridge in the area. A journalist reported hearing two loud explosions in the capital within half an hour and seeing smoke rising from at least one strike location.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with 'all hell' unless Hormuz Strait opened
stories.summary: Israel launched renewed strikes against Iranian air defense sites as both U.S. and Iranian military forces continued searching for a downed American pilot. President Trump threatened Iran with severe consequences unless the Strait of Hormuz is reopened.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with 'all Hell' unless Hormuz Strait opened
stories.summary: Israel launched renewed strikes against air defense sites in Iran as both the US and Iranian militaries continued searching for a downed US pilot. President Trump threatened Iran with "all Hell" unless the Strait of Hormuz was reopened.

stories.title: Israel strikes Tehran as US continues search for missing pilot
stories.summary: Israel launched renewed strikes targeting air defence sites in Tehran and elsewhere in Iran. Simultaneously, both US and Iranian military forces continued searching for a downed American pilot.

stories.title: European drivers choke on rising diesel prices due to Iran conflict
stories.summary: Diesel prices across Europe have risen by more than 30 percent since the start of the Iran conflict, reaching record levels. The spike highlights Europe's continued dependence on imported energy and the persistent role of diesel in the continent's car market.

stories.title: Benin's main opposition face crisis before presidential elections
stories.summary: Benin is preparing to hold presidential elections on April 12, with the country's main opposition facing an internal crisis ahead of the vote.

stories.title: Legal vs political neutrality
stories.summary: Arab Gulf states face a dilemma over their neutrality in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. While the Gulf nations assert political neutrality, Tehran argues that American military bases on their territories compromise that status. The analysis distinguishes between political neutrality and legal obligations under existing defense pacts with the United States.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Search on for missing crew member after US planes crash
stories.summary: A search is underway for a missing US crew member after American military planes went down during operations related to the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: EU finance ministers urge tax on energy firms’ profits amid Iran war
stories.summary: Finance ministers from Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Austria called on the EU Commission to impose a windfall profit tax on energy companies amid rising fuel prices linked to the Iran war. The joint letter said the measure would demonstrate EU unity and capacity for action.

stories.title: Five dead at Nikopol market after morning drone strike — on top of 286 overnight
stories.summary: Russia launched 286 drones at Ukraine overnight on April 3–4 and subsequently struck a market in Nikopol, killing five people and wounding 19, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: UNSC vote on Strait of Hormuz postponed
stories.summary: A scheduled UN Security Council vote on a draft resolution concerning the Strait of Hormuz was postponed after Iran warned the body against any provocative action.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Israel said it struck military sites and petrochemical plants in Iran's Khuzestan province, including the Mahshahr and Bandar Imam special petrochemical zone, injuring five. Tehran claimed it shot down a US F-15 fighter jet, with one crew member rescued and another still missing.

stories.title: WHO warns about attacks on Iran health facilities, regional threat
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned about attacks on healthcare facilities in Iran and the broader region amid the ongoing conflict. The WHO cited 116 verified attacks on health infrastructure and said the escalating crisis was sharply increasing the risk of communicable disease outbreaks.

stories.title: War in the Middle-East: Israel will reduce French defense imports 'to zero'
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to reduce French defence imports to zero, signaling a significant shift in its military procurement strategy amid the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine downs 260 of 286 Russian drones in overnight attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 260 of 286 Russian drones launched in an overnight attack beginning on the evening of April 3. The large-scale assault involved one of the higher drone counts recorded in recent operations.

stories.title: War in Ukraine: Russian night-time strikes wound at least 14 people
stories.summary: Russian night-time strikes on Ukraine wounded at least 14 people. Separately, air attacks inside Russia killed one person and injured four, according to officials from both sides.

stories.title: Israel’s hospitals are beginning to recognize, empower family caregivers
stories.summary: Israeli hospitals are beginning to formally recognize and support family caregivers, acknowledging their crucial role in patient treatment and recovery. Initiatives are being introduced to empower these caregivers with resources and institutional backing.

stories.title: Slowness: The healing village in Israel's Lower Galilee that restores body and mind
stories.summary: A healing village called Slowness, located in Israel's Lower Galilee, offers a recovery experience combining forest settings, food, and community. The retreat is designed to restore both physical and mental well-being for visitors seeking respite.

stories.title: Another oil shock
stories.summary: Pakistan sharply increased domestic petrol and diesel prices amid global oil price shocks caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The government reduced the petrol price by 80 rupees within 24 hours of the initial hike, reflecting political pressure. Authorities also ordered early market closures and announced targeted subsidies for motorcyclists, farmers, and transporters.

stories.title: In the UK, thieves travel around the country to raid chocolate shelves
stories.summary: Organized theft rings in the United Kingdom have been travelling across the country to systematically steal chocolate from store shelves amid rising chocolate prices.

stories.title: Iran hunts crew member of crashed US jet after one reported rescued
stories.summary: Iranian and American forces are competing to locate a U.S. crew member from a downed F-15 jet in southwestern Iran. Iranian media announced that anyone capturing a U.S. crew member alive would receive a valuable reward. One of the two crew members was reportedly already rescued.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Iran hunts crew member of crashed US jet
stories.summary: One US service member was rescued and at least one remains missing after two American military aircraft went down in separate incidents during the conflict with Iran. Iranian forces are reportedly searching for the missing crew member, in what includes the first US shoot-down since the war began.

stories.title: Russian attacks leave one civilian dead, dozens injured in Kherson region
stories.summary: One person was killed and 25 civilians were injured over the past day in Russian attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region. The strikes caused casualties across the area.

stories.title: Forget euphemism, Trump is using unabashed viciousness in his language against Iran
stories.summary: An analysis examines the Trump administration's use of blunt and graphic language to describe military operations against Iran, contrasting it with traditional political rhetoric and euphemism.

stories.title: War update: 157 combat clashes on frontline over past day, Pokrovsk sector remains hottest
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 157 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front line on April 3. The Pokrovsk sector remained the most active area of engagement.

stories.title: Israel Police decry online defamation campaign against female officer in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israel Police condemned an online defamation campaign targeting a female officer serving in Jerusalem. The posts included comparisons to Nazis and derogatory language. Police stated the behavior "crosses a dangerous red line" and may constitute a criminal offense.

stories.title: Kanye West plays to packed LA stadium as he launches comeback from antisemitism controversies
stories.summary: Kanye West, known as Ye, performed his first major US concert in five years at a packed Los Angeles stadium. The event came 11 months after he released a song titled 'Heil Hitler' and two months after publishing an apology for antisemitic remarks.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill three, injure dozens in Sumy region over past day
stories.summary: Three people were killed and 22 others injured in the Sumy region of Ukraine over the past day due to Russian strikes. The attacks continued a pattern of aggression targeting the northeastern region.

stories.title: Iran executes two convicted members of banned opposition group
stories.summary: Iran executed Abolhassan Montazer and Vahid Baniamerian, both convicted members of a banned opposition group, after the country's Supreme Court upheld their death sentences.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,110 over past day
stories.summary: Russia's total combat personnel losses since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 reached approximately 1,302,370 as of April 4, 2026, with 1,110 casualties reported over the past day.

stories.title: Biometric checks stalled again for cross-Channel travellers
stories.summary: The EU's biometric entry-exit system for cross-Channel travellers has been delayed again, with no facial ID checks planned for Eurotunnel and Eurostar passengers in the coming weeks despite an imminent implementation deadline.

stories.title: ‘Wild west’ reformer pilates boom is causing rise in injuries, experts warn
stories.summary: Experts in the United Kingdom warn that the rapid growth of reformer pilates studios has led to a lack of regulation, with inexperienced instructors contributing to a rise in injuries among fitness enthusiasts.

stories.title: 'Shame on Judaism': Former Israeli president warns against 'Armageddon'
stories.summary: Former interim Israeli president Avraham Burg criticized the use of religion to justify violence, calling rabbinical support for bloodshed "a shame on Judaism." He also rejected the influence of foreign evangelical agendas on Israeli policy and quoted biblical references contrasting King David with idealized images used to promote war.

stories.title: Four ships cross Hormuz as Iran says it is drafting protocol
stories.summary: Four ships, including vessels co-owned by Japanese and French companies, crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday using an Iranian-approved route near Larak Island. Iran announced it is drafting a peacetime protocol with Oman to supervise maritime traffic through the strait. The near-closure of Hormuz due to the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has caused global fuel shortages and soaring energy prices.

stories.title: Israeli military says it hit military sites in Iran
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it conducted air strikes on military sites in Tehran on Friday. Targets included IRGC aerial defense installations reportedly storing missiles, as well as a facility described as responsible for safeguarding weapons research and development and a location linked to ballistic missiles.

stories.title: Russian forces drop nearly 8,000 glide bombs on Ukraine in March – Defense Ministry
stories.summary: In March 2026, Russian forces deployed 7,987 guided aerial bombs (glide bombs) against Ukrainian targets, an increase of more than 1,500 over February, according to Ukraine's Defense Ministry. The escalation marked a significant intensification in the use of this weapon type.

stories.title: UNSC divided as Gulf pushes to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: The UN Security Council remains divided over a Bahrain-led, U.S.-backed resolution to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas passes. Russia and China have raised objections, and the vote has been postponed twice. Iran has warned against what it calls a provocative move.

stories.title: Russian and Egyptian FMs hold talks in Moscow
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov and his Egyptian counterpart held talks in Moscow. Both sides expressed support for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to political and diplomatic processes.

stories.title: Putin, Erdogan call for immediate ceasefire in Middle East war
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called for an immediate ceasefire in the Middle East war during a phone call. Both leaders warned of serious global consequences for energy, trade, and logistics. Their talks also covered coordinated security measures for the Black Sea area.

stories.title: Dream Care: This haredi male nurse is helping redefine private nursing care in Israel
stories.summary: A Haredi male nurse in Israel launched Dream Care, a private nursing service aimed at improving home care for patients who fall through gaps in the healthcare system. The initiative seeks to redefine standards of private nursing care across the country.

stories.title: Transporters raise fares by 30pc as ‘subsidy falls short’
stories.summary: Transporters across Pakistan have raised fares by up to 30 percent following a major fuel price hike, saying government subsidies are insufficient. The increased petroleum costs have also driven up prices of vegetables, fruits, construction materials, and other essential goods. The Lahore Chamber of Commerce warned of reduced export competitiveness.

stories.title: In Kyiv, office building on fire after drone debris falls – Klitschko
stories.summary: Falling debris from a Russian drone caused a fire in an office building in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. Emergency services responded to the incident.

stories.title: Afghanistan earthquake kills eight members of same family
stories.summary: An earthquake in Afghanistan killed eight members of a single family. The only survivor from the household was a young boy who sustained injuries in the tremor. No further details on the quake's magnitude or exact location were provided.

stories.title: No warning as rocket strikes homes in northern Israeli city
stories.summary: A rocket struck homes in a northern Israeli city without warning sirens being activated, according to Israeli media outlets including YNet News and Channel 12. No injuries were reported, but the projectile caused property damage. A photo showed smoke rising over a residential street.

stories.title: Thousands of Hongkongers brave heavy rain for Shenzhen trip on day 2 of Easter
stories.summary: Approximately 153,272 Hong Kong residents crossed the border into Shenzhen on the second day of the Easter holiday despite heavy rain. Travelers cited mainland China's wider selection of shopping, dining, and entertainment options at more affordable prices as key motivations.

stories.title: Russia justifying mass shelling of Zaporizhzhia by claiming ‘almost no civilians left’ there – CCD
stories.summary: Russia's Center for Countering Disinformation reported that Russian propaganda is attempting to justify the systematic shelling of Zaporizhzhia by claiming there are "almost no civilians left" in the city. Ukrainian authorities characterized this as an information campaign to legitimize attacks on civilian areas.

stories.title: Is opposing Israel 'anti-Semitism'? France’s latest attempt to fight hate risks inflaming it
stories.summary: The French government is backing a draft law, known as the "Yadan law," that equates opposition to Israel with anti-Semitism. Critics warn the legislation could suppress legitimate criticism of Israel and potentially fuel further anti-Semitic sentiment in France.

stories.title: UAE squeezes Iranian economic lifeline in retaliation for attacks
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has quietly banned most Iranians from entering the country or transiting its airports in retaliation for Iran's repeated air strikes on UAE industrial infrastructure. The UAE hosts more than half a million Iranians, and the move targets Iran's economic lifeline without signaling broader escalation.

stories.title: Bahrain postpones vote on UN resolution aimed at ending Iran's stranglehold on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Bahrain postponed a UN Security Council vote on a resolution aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively restricted. Diplomats said the vote, originally scheduled for Thursday, would now be held sometime the following week. Council consultations remained private.

stories.title: Canada allocates nearly USD 40 million in humanitarian aid to Ukraine
stories.summary: Canada allocated more than 51 million Canadian dollars (approximately $39 million USD) for humanitarian aid projects in Ukraine. The funding supports various assistance initiatives in the war-affected country.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks continue across Iran overnight
stories.summary: US-Israeli airstrikes continued overnight across Iran, with large explosions reported in western and eastern Tehran as well as heavy bombardment in Isfahan. Additional strikes hit Urmia, Khorramabad, Karaj, and Qom. The death toll from a strike on the B1 bridge rose to at least 13, and attacks appeared to increasingly target Iranian industry.

stories.title: South Sudanese Christians hold Good Friday march for peace
stories.summary: Thousands of people participated in a Good Friday peace march in South Sudan amid intensifying fighting between government and opposition forces. The march reflected growing fears of a return to full-scale civil war in the country.

stories.title: How does a fighter pilot survive being shot down in enemy territory?
stories.summary: A report describes survival, evasion, resistance, and escape (SERE) training that US fighter pilots undergo to prepare for being shot down in hostile territory.
