stories.title: Gaza health minister warns of disease risk as Israeli siege continues
stories.summary: Gaza Health Minister Majid Abu Ramadan warned of mounting disease risks across the Strip as Israel's siege continues. He said widespread destruction, untreated waste, and rubble have fueled a surge in rodents, raising the threat of illnesses including hantavirus, plague, and leptospirosis.

stories.title: Seven injured after train derails in Russia: local media
stories.summary: A train derailed in Russia's Ulyanovsk region, approximately 900 kilometers east of Moscow, injuring seven people. Local media reported the incident, though further details on the cause were not immediately available.

stories.title: Zelensky: Intelligence warns Russia may target railways and water supply systems
stories.summary: President Zelensky disclosed that Ukrainian intelligence has warned Russia may target the country's railway network and water supply infrastructure, including bridges, dams, hydroelectric power plants, and pumping stations. Ukraine is working to strengthen protection of these systems.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post published Shabbat candle lighting times for communities in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: In Sumy, injury toll after Russian strikes climbs to four
stories.summary: The number of people wounded in Russian strikes on the city of Sumy in northeastern Ukraine rose to four following attacks earlier in the day.

stories.title: Overcrowded, understaffed, overpriced: Kyiv’s wartime kiosk wave collapses
stories.summary: Kyiv's wartime boom in commercial kiosks has collapsed due to market oversaturation, declining consumer purchasing power, labor shortages, and rising electricity costs.

stories.title: War crimes are no longer shameful. That should terrify you
stories.summary: Warring parties in the latest Middle East escalation have shown disregard for civilian life, with observers noting that violations of international humanitarian law are increasingly met without accountability or public condemnation.

stories.title: These are Iran’s key islands in the Gulf
stories.summary: Several of Iran's roughly 400 islands hold strategic importance, particularly those located in the Persian Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz. The strait is a vital global chokepoint through which approximately a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passes.

stories.title: MSF condemns 'appalling' attack on Sudan hospital
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières condemned an attack on a hospital in Sudan as "appalling." The organization expressed outrage over repeated and escalating attacks on healthcare facilities in recent weeks.

stories.title: Cuba to pardon more than 2,000 prisoners as US eases fuel blockade
stories.summary: Havana calls releases a Holy Week humanitarian gesture as Russian tanker is allowed to reach oil-starved islandCuba has announced plans to pardon 2,010 prisoners as a “humanitarian” gesture during Hol

stories.title: Suicide car bomb blast kills five in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: A suicide car bomb attack targeted a police station in northwest Pakistan, killing five people. Preliminary information indicates the police station was the primary target of the bombing.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing elected President by pro-military parliament
stories.summary: Myanmar's pro-military parliament elected junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as president. The 69-year-old general led the 2021 coup that ousted Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, triggering mass protests and armed resistance across the country.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges Israel to reopen dialogue to end Iran war
stories.summary: Pope Leo urged Israel to reopen all paths of dialogue to help end the war with Iran during a phone call with Israeli President Isaac Herzog. The pontiff also called for the protection of civilians and respect for international and humanitarian law.

stories.title: Pakistanis face up to 54% rise in fuel prices
stories.summary:
Pakistanis faced record fuel price increases on Friday, as petrol and diesel prices rose by up to 54 per cent driven by the war in the Middle East that has caused global oil prices to surge.
The incre

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains Open for Russian Ships, Kremlin Aide Says
stories.summary: A Kremlin aide stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open for Russian commercial shipping. Russia, China, and India are reportedly among five nations designated as "friendly" that are permitted to use the waterway.

stories.title: China, Europe and why Beijing took a swing at Iran over the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary:
In a rare condemnation of its strategic partner, China has come out in opposition to Iran’s attacks on Gulf nations, calling for a ceasefire and a guarantee of the safety of shipping lanes.
Addressing

stories.title: The Energy Shock Hits Latin America
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving Iran has prompted Latin American governments to recalibrate their economic policies in response to energy market disruptions and broader economic shocks stemming from the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Tencent expands OpenClaw suite with enterprise tool amid China’s ‘lobster’ craze
stories.summary: Tencent Holdings has launched a new OpenClaw tool for enterprises that promises easy deployment of the artificial intelligence agent as part of the Chinese internet giant’s efforts to capitalise on th

stories.title: Marine Corps awards Textron, General Dynamics second rapid ARV prototype contract
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps awarded Textron and General Dynamics a second prototype contract for the Advanced Reconnaissance Vehicle program. The Corps is pursuing a family of ARV variants, each equipped with distinct capabilities to support mobile reconnaissance missions.

stories.title: Massive Russian attack on Kyiv region: One person killed, another wounded
stories.summary: One person was killed and another wounded in the Kyiv region during a massive Russian attack on April 3.

stories.title: The elderly were among the most vulnerable in the Holocaust – and the most overlooked
stories.summary: An exhibition titled "Eldercide" at London's Wiener Holocaust Library examines how elderly Jews were disproportionately vulnerable during the Holocaust. The display, running through April 30, explores how older victims were especially unlikely to survive and faced enormous post-war challenges.

stories.title: International law experts allege violations in Iran war
stories.summary: International law experts have raised allegations of legal violations in the ongoing war involving Iran. The White House has defended its actions, stating the military campaign is intended to eliminate both short- and long-term threats and make the broader region safer.

stories.title: Trump vows 'much more' destruction of Iran's infrastructure
stories.summary: President Trump vowed further destruction of Iran's infrastructure as the US and Israel intensified strikes on civilian targets. The political and economic fallout from the war continues to grow internationally.

stories.title: Todd Blanche takes over justice department after Pam Bondi sacking – US politics live
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump named Todd Blanche, his former personal attorney and deputy attorney general, as acting head of the Justice Department following the sacking of Pam Bondi. Separately, Trump threatened further strikes on Iran's bridges and power plants, while Iran claimed it shot down a second US F-35 fighter jet over its territory.

stories.title: Met Office says no rain expected in Karachi today as death toll rises to six
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department confirmed no further rain was expected in Karachi after torrential downpours caused by a strong westerly system. Rain-related deaths in the city rose to six, including one electrocution in Gulistan-i-Jauhar, prompting city authorities to declare an emergency.

stories.title: US judge rules against deporting man whose murder conviction was overturned after 44 years in prison
stories.summary: A US judge ruled against deporting Subramanyam Vedam, a 64-year-old Indian citizen, after his Pennsylvania murder conviction was overturned following 44 years in prison. Vedam, who was taken into ICE custody last year, maintains he did not kill Thomas Kinser in 1980.

stories.title: Iran Guards recruit children to ‘defend the homeland’, placing them in line of fire
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps launched a recruitment campaign targeting children as young as 12 for homeland defence amid the ongoing US-Israeli war. Rights groups warned that placing minors in military roles constitutes a war crime and poses life-threatening risks to Iranian children.

stories.title: Ireland defence secretary cancels Lebanon troop visit over security fears
stories.summary: Ireland's Defence Minister Helen McEntee cancelled a planned visit to Irish troops serving with the UN Interim Force in Lebanon due to security concerns. The decision followed the killing of three Indonesian peacekeepers in southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces continue to fight Hezbollah.

stories.title: Oxford Brookes’ student racing team target Silverstone win
stories.summary: Oxford Brookes University's student racing team, Oxford Brookes Racing, is designing a race car for the Formula Student competition at Silverstone. Over 100 students are involved in the project at the Headington campus, building on the team's record of design awards in the UK.

stories.title: Operation Task Force East eliminates over 6,500 Russian occupiers in one month, says Shapoval
stories.summary: Ukraine's Operation Task Force East eliminated over 6,500 Russian soldiers in one month, with nearly 4,000 additional enemy casualties recorded, according to Ukrainian commander Shapoval.

stories.title: Lazar Berman: What does the history of airpower tell us about Iran war?
stories.summary: A Times of Israel podcast episode examined over a century of strategic bombing campaigns and what historical precedents suggest about US and Israeli military goals in the ongoing war against Iran. The episode was hosted by Lazar Berman.

stories.title: Trump threatens to strike Iran’s bridges, electric power plants
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to strike Iranian bridges and electric power plants. International law experts warned that U.S. strikes on Iran may amount to war crimes.

stories.title: Nigeria: NSCDC Deploys 57,000 Personnel Nationwide to Secure Easter Celebrations
stories.summary: Nigeria's Security and Civil Defence Corps deployed over 57,000 personnel nationwide to provide security during Easter celebrations and ensure a peaceful holiday period.

stories.title: Iran's former top diplomat Zarif urges deal with US to end war
stories.summary: Iran's former foreign minister Mohammad Javad Zarif urged Tehran to pursue a deal with the United States to end the war. Writing in Foreign Affairs, Zarif claimed Iran held the "upper hand" in its conflict against the US and Israel.

stories.title: Iraq extends airspace closure for another week
stories.summary: Iraq's Civil Aviation Authority announced it has extended the closure of its airspace to all aircraft for an additional week. The closure reflects the ongoing regional security situation.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - Ekid Leaders Withdraw Support for Akwa Ibom Reps Member
stories.summary: Ekid community leaders in Akwa Ibom state, Nigeria, withdrew their support for their federal constituency representative ahead of the 2027 elections, deepening a long-running territorial dispute within the constituency.

stories.title: Malawi: Rural Workers Locked Out of Justice As Malawi's Labour System Struggles to Reach the Majority
stories.summary: Malawi's labour justice system is failing to reach rural workers, with thousands unable to access legal protections due to structural inequalities in the country's legal framework.

stories.title: Iran says it shot down second US F-35 jet over Tehran
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it shot down a second US F-35 fighter jet over Tehran. The IRGC said the aircraft belonged to a squadron stationed at a US Air Force base in eastern England, according to Iranian state-affiliated media.

stories.title: One lightly wounded after Iranian missile barrage targets northern Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile barrage targeted northern Israel, lightly wounding one person. Israel's Channel 12 News reported that emergency services were investigating at least 10 shrapnel impact sites.

stories.title: UN to vote on Hormuz resolution as China opposes authorisation of force
stories.summary: The United Nations Security Council is expected to vote on a resolution regarding the Strait of Hormuz on the morning of April 4. China has voiced opposition to any authorization of the use of force in the resolution.

stories.title: Russian drone hits shopping center in Sumy, injuring several people
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a shopping center in central Sumy, Ukraine, injuring at least two people.

stories.title: When will the Iran war end? Tracing the Trump administration's timelines
stories.summary: Analysts note that multiple US presidents have offered timelines for ending military conflicts, only to repeatedly revise their estimates. The pattern is being examined in the context of the current US war on Iran.

stories.title: ‘I don’t know how we’ll emerge from this’: How much more can Israelis take?
stories.summary: Analysts say years of war have fundamentally altered Israel's politics, economy, and society. Citizens are facing mounting strain as the prolonged conflict reshapes daily life and national priorities.

stories.title: Burkina Faso military leader Traore says ‘forget democracy’
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military leader Ibrahim Traore has abandoned commitments to hold elections and dissolved political parties. Traore publicly declared the country should move away from democracy.

stories.title: Trump’s anger over Iran thrusts NATO into fresh crisis
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli war against Iran has created a major rift within NATO, as European allies have declined American requests to deploy naval forces to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts and diplomats say the dispute has left the 76-year-old alliance in its weakest state since its founding.

stories.title: Casualties reported: Russian forces attack four border communities in Chernihiv region with drones
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked four border communities in Ukraine's Chernihiv region with FPV drones over a 24-hour period, causing extensive damage and resulting in casualties.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says U.S. forces yet to start 'destroying what's left' in Iran
stories.summary: Israel's military activated air defences to intercept missiles fired from Iran, though no immediate casualties or damage were reported. U.S. President Trump stated that American forces had not yet begun fully destroying remaining targets in Iran.

stories.title: French vessel crosses Hormuz as strait remains largely shut
stories.summary: A container ship operated by France's CMA CGM group transited the Strait of Hormuz, according to BFM TV. The strait has been largely closed since the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran began on February 28. Neither CMA CGM nor France's foreign ministry commented on how passage was secured.

stories.title: Kuwait oil refinery units on fire after drone attack: state media
stories.summary: A drone attack struck a Kuwait oil refinery, setting multiple units on fire, according to state media. Emergency teams were deployed to contain the blazes at the facility.

stories.title: Rubble, mud and hair: How to rebuild a home in Gaza
stories.summary: Residents in Gaza are relying on partial rehabilitation and temporary housing solutions rather than full reconstruction. Rebuilding efforts use available materials including rubble and mud amid ongoing devastation in the Strip.

stories.title: Burkina Faso must 'forget' about democracy, military leader says
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military leader Captain Ibrahim Traoré, who seized power in 2023, declared that the country must abandon democratic governance, asserting that democratic rule would not work for Burkina Faso.

stories.title: Malawi: A Nation Taxed to the Bone - Government Must Pause Before It Pushes Malawi Over the Edge
stories.summary: Malawi faces criticism over its heavy tax burden, with calls for the government to reassess fiscal policy as citizens struggle with widespread economic hardship.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'Be Vocal in Supporting Tinubu,' Umahi Tells Southeast Leaders
stories.summary: Nigerian Works Minister David Umahi urged southeastern leaders to vocally support President Bola Tinubu, citing the president's commitment to the region's people.

stories.title: South Sudan: Aid agencies warn of possible war crimes amid deepening humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: Aid agencies operating in South Sudan are warning of possible war crimes amid a deepening humanitarian crisis, calling for urgent international action including increased funding, safe access for aid delivery, and accountability for violations.

stories.title: No more ‘cold peace’ across Taiwan Strait: former KMT chairwoman calls to rebuild trust
stories.summary: Former Kuomintang chairwoman Hung Hsiu-chu called for renewed cross-strait dialogue between Taiwan and mainland China to move beyond the current "cold peace," urging a return to the 1992 consensus to rebuild mutual trust and avoid conflict.

stories.title: Nigeria: Napoli, AC Milan Face Off As Italy Licks World Cup Wounds
stories.summary: Napoli and AC Milan are set to face each other in Serie A on Monday, but domestic football coverage in Italy has been overshadowed by the national team's failure to qualify for another World Cup.

stories.title: Liberia: Fear Grips Business Owners in Bong and Nimba Amid Guinea-Liberia Border Crisis
stories.summary: The border crisis between Guinea and Liberia at the Sorlumah crossing in Lofa County has caused widespread fear among business owners in Bong and Nimba counties, severely disrupting cross-border commerce.

stories.title: Liberia: 'We Were Not Interested in the Details' - Prosecution Star Witness Admits Under Oath in U.S.$6m Tweah Trial
stories.summary: In the corruption trial of former Liberian Finance Minister Samuel Tweah in Monrovia, the prosecution's lead witness admitted under oath that investigators were not interested in the operational details of a controversial US$6 million at the center of the case.

stories.title: Iran outlet publishes images of downed US jet over central Iran
stories.summary: Iran's semi-official Tasnim News Agency published images of what it said was a US fighter jet shot down over central Iran by IRGC air defenses. Markings on the aircraft were identified as belonging to US European Command, linked to a unit based in the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Iraqi leaders face balancing act as Iran conflict exposes deep rifts
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war on Iran has exposed deep political rifts in Iraq, dividing those who hope for an end to Tehran's influence over Iraqi politics from loyalists of the Islamic republic. The conflict cuts through state institutions and armed groups in a country still scarred by previous American military intervention.

stories.title: Washington launches export initiative to ensure ‘future of AI is led by the United States’
stories.summary: The U.S. government unveiled an AI export initiative inviting American companies to form consortiums offering full-stack AI solutions globally, with applications accepted through June. The program aims to cement U.S. technological leadership and counter China's growing influence in artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Xiaomi lifts handset prices as memory chip crunch ripples through supply chain
stories.summary: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi raised prices on several models by about 200 yuan ($29) due to surging memory chip costs, following similar increases by domestic competitors Oppo, Vivo, and Honor in March.

stories.title: China watching ‘like a hawk’ as US Artemis 2 crew fixes toilet on moon trip
stories.summary: Experts say China is closely monitoring the U.S. Artemis 2 lunar fly-by mission, which encountered early challenges including a malfunctioning toilet after launch. The mission represents the first human return to lunar orbit since the Apollo era and could provide Beijing with valuable technical insights.

stories.title: Food prices spiked in March as Middle East conflict drove up energy costs, UN says
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization reported that global food commodity prices rose 2.4 per cent in March, marking a second consecutive monthly increase. Vegetable oil and sugar prices saw the largest jumps, rising 5 per cent and 7 per cent respectively, driven by Middle East conflict-related energy and freight cost increases.

stories.title: Liberia: Sanctioned Fuel Shipment Raises Red Flags for Liberia
stories.summary: A vessel carrying Russian-origin diesel linked to a sanctioned trading network is expected to enter Liberian waters, raising concerns about potential violations of international sanctions regimes and possible diplomatic and economic risks for Liberia.

stories.title: Zelenskyy suggests Ukraine ready to confront Iran in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv is ready to help protect shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz if invited, citing Ukraine's experience maintaining Black Sea routes under Russian attacks. His comments came as Ukraine expands cooperation with Gulf states including Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Russian strikes cause new power outages in six regions
stories.summary: Russian drone attacks and artillery shelling caused new power outages across six Ukrainian regions as of the morning of April 3, according to grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: Over 100 US legal experts condemn strikes on Iran as possible ‘war crimes’
stories.summary: More than 100 US-based legal scholars signed an open letter condemning US strikes on Iran as possible war crimes. The letter raised concerns about the conduct and rhetoric of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: What comes after survival? Sawsan Qaoud answers in Gaza Grad
stories.summary: Film director Sawsan Qaoud discussed her documentary "Gaza Grad," which portrays Palestinians through intimate portraits of displacement and memory. The film aims to reframe Palestinian experiences beyond statistics.

stories.title: ‘Breathtaking’: Artemis astronauts blast towards Moon
stories.summary: Four NASA Artemis 2 astronauts are heading toward the Moon after a successful engine firing of their Orion capsule. The 10-day mission marks the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years. NASA described the engine burn as flawless.

stories.title: Hong Kong documentary pulled from cinemas 3 years ago to be screened in Italy
stories.summary: Hong Kong director Mabel Cheung Yuen-ting's documentary "To My Nineteen-year-old Self," which was pulled from Hong Kong cinemas three years ago over consent issues, will be screened at Italy's Far East Film Festival in Udine between April 24 and May 2.

stories.title: Nigeria: Thank INEC for Timely Derecognition of Your Leaders - Keyamo Tells ADC
stories.summary: Nigerian Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo urged the African Democratic Congress party to appreciate the Independent National Electoral Commission's decision to derecognize factions of the party's leadership.

stories.title: Liberia: Govt Defends Weedor Nomination As Elections Chief
stories.summary: Liberia's Information Minister Jerolinmek Matthew Piah defended the nomination of Jonathan K. Weedor as chairman of the National Elections Commission amid criticism from opposition figures and civil society actors in Monrovia.

stories.title: Ex-police interpreter indicted for sharing missile impact info with foreign agent
stories.summary: Miqdad Natur, a former sign-language interpreter for Israeli police, security services, and courts, has been indicted for sharing missile impact information with a foreign agent. He is accused of providing details on impact sites, casualties, and infrastructure damage.

stories.title: 'This has got me worried': Iranians fear what comes next after US strike on Karaj bridge
stories.summary: Iranians have expressed growing fear following a US strike on a bridge in Karaj. President Trump warned Iran that further strikes on bridges and electric power plants would follow if Iranian leaders did not agree to his terms to end the war.

stories.title: Iran claims second US fighter jet downed over central Iran
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC claimed it shot down a second US F-35 fighter jet over central Iran, reporting the aircraft was completely destroyed. IRGC-affiliated Fars News Agency and Mehr News Agency said the pilot was unlikely to have survived due to a violent explosion on impact.

stories.title: Middle East conflict overshadows migration summit in Egypt
stories.summary: A migration summit held in Egypt's New Administrative Capital brought together African ministers and stakeholders under the International Organization for Migration framework, but discussions were overshadowed by the ongoing Middle East conflict. The meeting preceded a global review forum in New York.

stories.title: Iran warns UNSC against 'provocative action' on Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi warned the UN Security Council against "provocative action" regarding the Strait of Hormuz. His comments came ahead of a scheduled Security Council vote on a draft resolution to mandate a force to protect shipping through the strait.

stories.title: Suicide bombing at Domel police station in Bannu leaves 5 civilians dead, 13 injured
stories.summary: A suicide car bomb attack targeted the Domel Police Station in Bannu, Pakistan, killing at least five civilians from one family and injuring 13 others, including one police officer. The explosives-laden vehicle rammed into the rear of the station, destroying a sentry post.

stories.title: The fight for mineral data in DRC: Belgian museum, US mining firm at odds over archive maps
stories.summary: A dispute has emerged between Belgium's Royal Museum for Central Africa near Brussels and US mining firm KoBold Metals, backed by Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos, over colonial-era archive maps of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The maps detail deposits of cobalt, lithium, coltan, and tungsten critical to the digital and energy transition.

stories.title: Drones attack Moscow and Leningrad region of Russian Federation overnight
stories.summary: Drones attacked Moscow and the Leningrad Region of Russia overnight on April 3 in what appeared to be a Ukrainian long-range strike operation.

stories.title: Weak enforcement blamed for building collapse that killed four in Ghana
stories.summary: An unfinished school building collapsed in Accra, Ghana, killing four children and injuring approximately 30 others. Schools in the region have been suspended, and weak enforcement of building regulations has been blamed for the disaster.

stories.title: New Zealand doctor bills US embassy for rising fuel costs: ‘payment expected within 7 days’
stories.summary: A New Zealand doctor sent the U.S. embassy in Wellington an invoice for NZ$2,790.95 in fuel costs for his clinic staff, blaming the Trump administration for starting a war that caused oil prices to spike.

stories.title: Human remains found on Thai ship attacked by Iran in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Human remains were found aboard the Thai-flagged cargo ship Mayuree Naree, which was struck by Iran while transiting the Strait of Hormuz after departing Khalifa port. Three crew members had been reported missing since the March attack, which followed U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing appointed president after ‘sham’ election
stories.summary: Myanmar's military chief Min Aung Hlaing was appointed president by a parliament dominated by the pro-military party following widely condemned elections. Min Aung Hlaing, who seized power in a 2021 coup, is wanted by the International Criminal Court's prosecutor for crimes against humanity against the Rohingya Muslim minority.

stories.title: Kenya: Fuel Prices Set to Rise in May Dependent On Global Market Pressures
stories.summary: Fuel prices in Kenya are expected to rise in May due to volatility in global oil markets linked to the ongoing Middle East conflict, even as the government sought to reassure the public about the country's economic stability.

stories.title: Rwanda: Experts Flag Lifestyle Factors Behind Rising Infertility
stories.summary: Medical experts in Rwanda are highlighting lifestyle factors including smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, poor sleep, chronic stress, and unhealthy body weight as increasingly significant contributors to rising infertility rates among couples.

stories.title: People of Burkina Faso should forget about democracy, says military ruler
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military ruler Ibrahim Traoré told the state broadcaster that democracy is "not for us" and that people should abandon the concept. Traoré, who took power in a September 2022 coup, has since banned political parties and stifled opposition.

stories.title: Chinese drone downed in Iran, sparking questions about UAE or Saudi Arabian role
stories.summary: Iran reportedly shot down a Chinese-made Wing Loong II drone near Shiraz in southern Iran. Open-source intelligence analysts questioned whether Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia or the UAE may have been operating the drone, though Iranian media initially identified it as a US MQ-9 Reaper.

stories.title: Tzruya ‘Suki’ Lahav, writer, poet and briefly Springsteen’s violinist, dies at 74
stories.summary: Tzruya "Suki" Lahav, an Israeli writer, poet, and Hebrew lyricist, has died at age 74. In her early twenties, she played violin with Bruce Springsteen's E Street Band before pursuing a long career in Hebrew literature.

stories.title: Has Israel dropped its goal of disarming Hezbollah?
stories.summary: The Israeli military has stated that disarming Hezbollah is no longer a war goal in Lebanon. Hezbollah has said it is preparing for a prolonged confrontation with Israeli forces.

stories.title: Artemis II: One giant leap for deep space toiletry
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission preparations drew attention for its deep-space toilet challenges. Separately, French newspapers Libération and Les Échos marked 1,500 days since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, noting an improving outlook for Kyiv despite years of bombardment.

stories.title: Trump claims Starmer is weak as he mocks PM and UK aircraft carriers
stories.summary: Footage emerged of US President Donald Trump mocking UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer during an Easter lunch speech at the White House. Trump accused Starmer of prevaricating over deploying British aircraft carriers to the Middle East, calling the PM weak in a new low for UK-US relations.

stories.title: Kholodnyi Yar commander: The drone war is won at the contact line, but it is decided in the depth
stories.summary: Kholodnyi Yar brigade commander Shamil Krutkov said Ukraine's drone warfare is decided by operations deep in the Russian rear, not just at the front line. He emphasized that the number and quality of available UAVs and enemy positioning are the key variables.

stories.title: US intel contradicts Trump's claims that Iran’s missile and drone arsenal destroyed
stories.summary: US intelligence assessments indicate Iran retains roughly half of its missile launchers and thousands of attack drones despite weeks of US and Israeli strikes, according to CNN sources. The findings contradict President Trump's earlier claims that Iran's military capabilities had been largely dismantled.

stories.title: The death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly acts of terror is unconstitutional
stories.summary: An opinion piece in the Times of Israel argues that Israel's death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly acts of terror is unconstitutional. Critics call the legislation racially discriminatory and legally flawed, urging the High Court to strike it down.

stories.title: Ma Xingrui becomes China’s third Politburo member investigated for corruption
stories.summary: Ma Xingrui, a Chinese Politburo member and former Communist Party chief of Xinjiang, is under investigation by China's anti-corruption watchdog. He is the third Politburo member investigated in the current term beginning in 2022, an unprecedented situation in decades.

stories.title: IDF says disarming Hezbollah unrealistic without full-scale invasion as troops push towards Litani
stories.summary: The IDF stated that fully disarming Hezbollah in southern Lebanon without a full-scale invasion is unrealistic. Israeli forces are expected to finish securing territory eight to ten kilometres from the border within a week to reduce Hezbollah's firing capabilities.

stories.title: Russians attack minibus in Kherson; five people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces used a drone to attack a minibus in the city of Kherson on the morning of April 3, injuring five people.

stories.title: US intel. says half of Iran’s weapons are still intact as Trump, Netanyahu claim otherwise - report
stories.summary: A US intelligence assessment reported by CNN found that roughly half of Iran's weapons remain intact, contradicting claims by President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu. The assessment concluded Trump's prediction of ending the war in two to three weeks was unrealistic.

stories.title: When jail becomes home: Japan's elderly seek refuge behind bars
stories.summary: Japan's demographic crisis is reflected in its prison system, where the number of elderly inmates has quadrupled over 20 years. Around a fifth of Japanese citizens over 65 live below the poverty line, and some deliberately commit petty crimes like shoplifting to access prison's guaranteed meals, housing, and medical care.

stories.title: NATO members boost defence spending to cut reliance on US
stories.summary: NATO member states have significantly increased defence spending and are working to reduce their reliance on US weapons imports amid President Donald Trump's renewed threats to withdraw the United States from the alliance.

stories.title: With an eye on China, Japan looks to kamikaze drones and low-cost missiles
stories.summary: Japan plans to introduce kamikaze drones and low-cost missiles as part of an "integrated attacks" strategy to counter regional threats including China, according to Japanese media citing government sources. The systems would target enemy air defenses.

stories.title: Malaysia urged to take more aggressive action to tackle energy crisis
stories.summary: Experts are urging Malaysia's government to take more aggressive measures to address the regional energy crisis caused by the Iran conflict. Much of Southeast Asia has been severely affected, with fuel shortages and spiraling costs straining economies across the region.

stories.title: Rats versus pets: Hong Kong dog owners want rodent poison in boxes, not bags
stories.summary: Hong Kong dog owners are urging the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department to place rat poison in secure boxes rather than transparent bags, after pets consumed pellets that spilled from broken bags onto pavements.

stories.title: Why ‘dung collector’ was a highly lucrative profession in ancient China
stories.summary: In ancient China, specialized workers known as 'dung collectors' gathered human waste from residents' chamber pots for profit. The profession was highly lucrative and competitive due to the absence of modern sanitation systems, which prohibited residents from freely disposing of waste.

stories.title: Russia conducts massive rolling aerial attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia conducted rolling aerial attacks across Ukraine beginning with overnight drone barrages followed by daytime missile and drone strikes that killed six people. Ukrainian officials noted that Russia has increasingly employed daytime attacks in an effort to penetrate Ukraine's air defences.

stories.title: Does Iran have a path to the bomb?
stories.summary: The article examines Iran's nuclear capabilities and whether it could develop a nuclear weapon in response to a potential Israeli nuclear strike, noting that Iran is considered a nuclear-capable state but questions remain about its timeline for retaliation.

stories.title: US intelligence said to assess around half of Iran’s missile launchers still intact
stories.summary: US intelligence reportedly assesses that around half of Iran's missile launchers remain intact, differing from Israeli estimates. President Trump described Israel as a "team player" on the Iran campaign, saying Israel "will stop when I stop."

stories.title: If Iran unravels
stories.summary: The article analyzes Pakistan's national security concerns regarding a potential collapse of the Iranian regime amid the Gulf conflict. Pakistani officials fear a power vacuum in Tehran could lead to advanced Iranian weapons, particularly kamikaze drones, reaching militant networks like the TTP and BLA.

stories.title: Pentagon shake-up as Hegseth ousts army chief amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth forced Army Chief of Staff General Randy George into immediate retirement during the ongoing war with Iran. Generals David Hodne and William Green were also removed in what media described as one of the most consequential Pentagon leadership upheavals in decades.

stories.title: Ukrinform journalist Olha Zvonariova wins award in Italy
stories.summary: Ukrinform journalist Olha Zvonariova received the 2026 Italian Montecatini Prize for Journalism, recognizing her reporting for the Ukrainian National News Agency.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes destroy Iranian highway bridge
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes on April 2 destroyed a highway bridge approximately 35 kilometres from Tehran, described by Iranian media as the tallest bridge in the Middle East. US President Donald Trump subsequently threatened that Iranian energy plants could be targeted next if Tehran did not agree to a deal.

stories.title: Economic security buffers
stories.summary: The article discusses Pakistan's opportunity to build economic security buffers following international goodwill from its mediation role in the Gulf conflict and a flexible IMF staff-level agreement reached without additional conditions.

stories.title: Wake up to the Mediterranean: Tel Aviv apartments steps from the sea - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored advertisement promotes luxury pre-sale apartments near Tel Aviv's Mediterranean coastline. The development offers sea views and proximity to Tel Aviv's cultural areas.

stories.title: Debris from intercepted threat hits Abu Dhabi gas facility
stories.summary: Debris from an intercepted aerial threat struck gas facilities in Abu Dhabi's Habshan area, forcing a temporary halt to operations and sparking a fire. Authorities reported no injuries as emergency teams worked to contain the blaze.

stories.title: "Is Netanyahu real or AI?" | Generative AI warps truth of West Asia war
stories.summary: The article explores how generative AI is being used to create fabricated content related to the West Asia war, blurring the line between authentic and manipulated imagery, including deepfakes of public figures like Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Hong Kong committed to helping mainland China’s health standards ‘go global’
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Secretary for Health Lo Chung-mau announced the city's commitment to helping mainland China's medical and health standards gain international recognition. Hong Kong hosted its first national medical conference, and the city is pursuing mainland certification for a local stroke centre after a heart disease facility was accredited under national standards.

stories.title: Nepal court extends detention of ex-PM Oli in deadly protest probe
stories.summary: A court in Nepal extended the detention of former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in connection with a probe into deadly protests. Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak were arrested a day after Prime Minister Balendra Shah was sworn in following post-uprising elections.

stories.title: Investigators identify suspects in Dr Malik attack case
stories.summary: Police in Peshawar announced they have identified the suspects who shot urologist Dr. Asif Malik near his residence. Officials said arrests are imminent, though the motive remains unknown. Dr. Malik was reported in stable condition at a hospital.

stories.title: Urumqi meeting
stories.summary: Representatives of Pakistan and Afghanistan met in Urumqi, China, in the first major diplomatic engagement since Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil-Haq against TTP militants in late February. Chinese officials facilitated what Pakistani sources described as exploratory discussions rather than formal mediation.

stories.title: Donald Trump threatens to strike Iran’s bridges and electric power plants
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iran's bridges and electric power plants, posting on social media that the U.S. military had not yet started fully destroying remaining targets in Iran.

stories.title: Israel strikes over 3,500 Lebanon targets in month with 1,000 militants dead: military
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported it had struck more than 3,500 targets across Lebanon over the past month of fighting against Hezbollah and killed approximately 1,000 militants. The conflict escalated after Iran-backed Hezbollah launched rockets at Israel on March 2. Israel responded with extensive airstrikes and a ground offensive.

stories.title: Five people injured in Kharkiv due to overnight enemy attacks, including child
stories.summary: Five people, including an infant, were injured in Kharkiv during overnight Russian attacks on April 3.

stories.title: Iran hunts downed US jet crew as report says one member rescued
stories.summary: Iran launched a search for US aircrew after a jet was reportedly shot down. US media reported that one crew member had already been rescued by American special forces.

stories.title: US scrambles to find downed F-15 pilot, Iran offers bounty
stories.summary: US forces are scrambling to locate the pilot of an F-15 downed over Iran while Iranian authorities have offered a bounty for the crew's capture. President Trump previously threatened to send Iran "back to the Stone Age."

stories.title: US searching for downed pilot as Iran says army also searching
stories.summary: The US military is conducting search operations for a downed pilot over Iran, while Iranian forces said their army is also searching for the same individual. President Trump previously threatened to send Iran "back to the Stone Age."

stories.title: Trump vows more attacks on Iran infrastructure
stories.summary: President Trump vowed additional strikes on Iranian infrastructure, building on earlier threats to send Iran "back to the Stone Age" — rhetoric echoed by other administration officials.

stories.title: French-Palestinian MEP Rima Hassan to be tried for 'advocating terrorism' in X post
stories.summary: European Parliament member Rima Hassan of France's La France Insoumise party will face trial in July on charges of advocating terrorism over a post on X referencing a 1972 Israeli airport attack. Complaints were filed by the International League Against Racism and Anti-Semitism and the European Jewish Organization.

stories.title: Oil prices surge as Trump threatens further strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Global oil prices surged sharply after President Trump renewed threats to strike Iranian infrastructure. Brent crude climbed about 8 percent on Friday to above $109 a barrel, with prices up nearly 50 percent since the war began.

stories.title: IDF official says disarming Hezbollah unrealistic, not a goal of Lebanon operation
stories.summary: A senior IDF official stated that fully disarming Hezbollah is unrealistic and is not a goal of Israel's Lebanon operation. The military plans to present a buffer zone proposal to political leadership involving the demolition of border villages and establishment of army posts in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Cuba to pardon more than 2,000 prisoners amid US pressure
stories.summary: Cuba has announced plans to pardon more than 2,000 prisoners amid ongoing US pressure. The release of political prisoners has long been a core US demand as Washington continues an oil blockade against the island nation.

stories.title: Former Iranian FM urges Iran to declare victory and strike deal to end war
stories.summary: Former Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif urged Tehran to declare victory and negotiate a deal to end the conflict with the United States and Israel. Writing in Foreign Affairs, Zarif proposed limiting Iran's nuclear programme and reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for favorable terms.

stories.title: Storm Erminio lashes much of Greece as Saharan dust blankets Crete
stories.summary: Storm Erminio brought heavy rain, thunderstorms, and hail across much of Greece, with severe flooding in the Attica region around Athens and on Crete. South-east Italy was also affected by heavy rain and snow at higher altitudes. Separately, deadly flooding struck Afghanistan.

stories.title: Helium supply shock threatens Asian chipmakers as economic slowdown fears mount
stories.summary: Damage to Qatar's gas facilities during the Iran war has disrupted global helium supplies, threatening Asian semiconductor manufacturers that rely on the gas for chip production. Analysts, including Deloitte Access Economics, warn the supply shock will have ripple effects across industries from smartphones to medical scanners.

stories.title: War update: 230 clashes on front lines in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defence Forces recorded 230 combat engagements with Russian forces along the front lines on April 2.

stories.title: Kuwait desalination plant, oil refinery hit by missile and drone strikes
stories.summary: A desalination plant and oil refinery in Kuwait were struck by missile and drone attacks. Separately, Oracle and Amazon Web Services data centers in the United Arab Emirates were also reportedly targeted.

stories.title: Four die of electrocution as heavy rain batters Karachi
stories.summary: Heavy rains struck Karachi, killing at least five people — four from electrocution and one from a wall collapse. Nazimabad recorded the highest rainfall at 69.6mm, leaving roads submerged and many areas without electricity for hours.

stories.title: Russian airstrike on Sumy region community kills one, injures three
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out an airstrike on the Shostka community in Ukraine's Sumy region on April 3, killing one person and injuring three others.

stories.title: Hegseth ousts US Army chief of staff
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked General Randy George to step down as chief of staff of the US Army and take immediate retirement. The reason was not officially stated, but reports indicated Hegseth wanted a leader who would implement his and President Trump's vision for the Army.

stories.title: UN Security Council to vote on authorizing force to protect Hormuz
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is set to vote on a Bahrain-sponsored draft resolution to authorize defensive force to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz from Iranian attacks. Iran has disrupted the key shipping lane in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes, threatening global fuel supplies and economic stability.

stories.title: Work from home, but we’re watching: Indonesia, Malaysia geo-track remote civil servants
stories.summary: Indonesia and Malaysia have ordered civil servants to work from home to conserve fuel amid the Iran war, implementing strict digital surveillance measures. Indonesian civil servants must activate location tracking and respond to communications within five minutes, while Malaysian counterparts must log into a geolocation monitoring system hourly, with sanctions for non-compliance.

stories.title: Pakistan's response to any attack would be 'swift, calibrated and decisive': Khawaja Asif on Rajnath Singh’s remarks
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif warned that Pakistan's response to any attack would be swift, calibrated, and decisive, responding to remarks by India's Rajnath Singh. He referenced a previous four-day conflict in May as a reminder of the consequences of miscalculation.

stories.title: Hong Kong set for thunderstorms and showers on Saturday, Observatory says
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory forecast thunderstorms and showers for Saturday, warning of unsettled weather throughout the Easter holiday. A trough of low pressure was expected to bring occasional heavy showers and fast-moving thunderstorms to the territory.

stories.title: Macron snaps back at Trump, reflecting Europe’s growing anger over Iran war
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron publicly criticized President Trump for what he called an "unserious" approach to the Iran war and unhelpful attacks on NATO, reflecting growing European frustration with U.S. policy.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 856 attacks on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 856 strikes targeting 45 settlements across Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region in a single 24-hour period, injuring four people.

stories.title: The greatest threat to Israel is not on the battlefield - it's at home - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the greatest threat to Israel comes from domestic political dynamics rather than external military conflicts. The author contends that Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition choices risk undermining democracy, social cohesion, and long-term stability.

stories.title: 3 reasons Xi-Trump summit won’t be a waste of time for China
stories.summary: A summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled for May 14–15 in Beijing, according to the Trump administration. Beijing has neither confirmed nor denied the meeting, while the article notes contrasts with failed U.S. diplomatic outreach to Iran.

stories.title: Hegseth asks U.S. Army’s top officer to step down while U.S. continues war on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth asked Army Chief of Staff General Randy George to step down during the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Pentagon officials provided no reason for the departure, which comes nearly five weeks into the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine’s ancient Easter egg art helps preserve national identity
stories.summary: Ukrainians are preparing for Easter with pysanky, traditional hand-decorated eggs featuring regionally distinct colors and symbols that carry religious and historical significance, helping preserve national cultural identity.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,230 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost approximately 1,230 troops killed or wounded in a single day, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022 to roughly 1,301,260 personnel as of April 3, 2026.

stories.title: Trump threatens expanded US strikes on Iran civilian infrastructure
stories.summary: President Trump warned that the US military "hasn't even started destroying what's left in Iran," signalling potential escalation of strikes on Iranian infrastructure nearly five weeks into the joint US-Israeli military campaign.

stories.title: Mistakes and slackness do not warrant writ jurisdiction: Federal Constitutional Court
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court ruled that mistakes or negligence by a party in court proceedings do not entitle it to file a challenge under Section 12(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, which allows challenges on grounds of fraud, misrepresentation, or lack of jurisdiction.

stories.title: Fishing nets used in the Mediterranean for millennia — now Italy wants to turn them into drone shields over Ukrainian cities
stories.summary: Italian Senator Scalfarotto introduced a bill to repurpose Mediterranean fishing nets as drone shields over Ukrainian cities. The proposal followed Ukrainian demonstrations that mesh strong enough for fishing can intercept Shahed drones.

stories.title: Seven dead as rains, flash floods ravage Balochistan
stories.summary: Rains and flash floods across Balochistan, Pakistan, killed seven people and injured four, destroying hundreds of homes and submerging farmland. The worst-hit districts include Harnai, Kohlu, Kachhi, and Nasirabad, with major roads and highways washed away.

stories.title: Marble bowl buried 1,300 years ago in Golan church sheds light on ancient baptisms
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered a unique marble bowl in a Golan Heights cathedral destroyed by an earthquake in 749 CE. The liturgical object suggests baptisms there included three moments of anointment, a ritual not previously documented.

stories.title: Iran condemns US-Israeli ‘moral collapse’ after attacks on civilian sites
stories.summary: Iran condemned what it called a US-Israeli "moral collapse" after strikes damaged or destroyed the country's tallest bridge and a century-old medical research centre dedicated to disease prevention.

stories.title: Beijing hails US cooperation as ICE returns suspected drug smuggler to China
stories.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement repatriated a Chinese national suspected of drug smuggling to China, marking the first such case in years. Beijing's Ministry of Public Security said the transfer was carried out through bilateral cooperation channels based on information from Chinese narcotics authorities.

stories.title: While IDF soldiers fight, Israel's government rewards draft dodgers - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion piece discusses frustration among Israeli soldiers serving in combat operations who learned that the government's new budget includes provisions benefiting those who evade military service.

stories.title: Iran says shot down F-35 fighter jet with new defence system
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it shot down a U.S. F-35 fighter jet over Iranian airspace using a new advanced defense system. The United States, which has been conducting military operations against Iran alongside Israel since late February, did not immediately confirm the claim. The IRGC said it was the second F-35 downed.

stories.title: Middle East conflict spiralling into wider regional war, warns UN chief
stories.summary: UN Secretary General António Guterres warned that the Middle East crisis is spiralling into a wider regional war as the conflict enters its second month. He urged the United States and Israel to halt hostilities and called on Iran to cease attacks on neighboring countries.

stories.title: Lebanese PM decries Israel’s  ‘far-reaching’ occupation goals
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam declared there was no end in sight to Israel's war on Lebanon, which has displaced one million people in one month. Eighteen European nations jointly demanded an immediate halt to Israeli military operations and called for respect of Lebanon's sovereignty.

stories.title: Hegseth asked US army chief to step down, Pentagon says
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked the U.S. Army chief to step down, according to the Pentagon. The move occurred as the United States and Israel continue military operations against Iran.

stories.title: US experts say American strikes on Iran may amount to war crimes
stories.summary: U.S. legal and military experts have raised serious concerns that American strikes on Iran may constitute war crimes, citing attacks that hit schools, health facilities, and residential homes.

stories.title: US experts say American strikes on Iran may amount to war crimes
stories.summary: U.S. legal and policy experts expressed serious concern that American strikes on Iran may constitute war crimes, citing attacks that have hit schools, health facilities, and residential homes.

stories.title: Operation Santa Claus: Maxim’s ramps up programmes, fundraising for Tai Po fire victims
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Maxim's Group has expanded its fundraising through Operation Santa Claus, an annual charity initiative run by the South China Morning Post and RTHK, to support victims of a deadly fire in Tai Po. The conglomerate is funding emergency relief and long-term community programs for vulnerable groups.

stories.title: Red Sea arena: Yemen’s Houthis open fourth front in Iran war, with global implications
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces have entered the U.S.-Iran conflict by opening a new front in the Red Sea. Analysts warn the Houthi involvement could disrupt global trade and oil shipments and further destabilize the regional balance of power.

stories.title: Luxury stores take hit in Dubai as Iran war drags on
stories.summary: Luxury retail stores in Dubai are experiencing a significant decline in tourist customers one month into the U.S.-Israeli military offensive against Iran. While local clientele continue to shop, sales staff report noticeably reduced foot traffic in upmarket malls.

stories.title: 3 Chinese nationals arrested in Malaysia over fake US visa passes
stories.summary: Malaysian immigration authorities detained 14 Chinese nationals and one Malaysian man in Kuala Lumpur for various offenses. Three of the Chinese nationals were arrested for using fake passes as supporting documents to obtain U.S. entry visas.

stories.title: Rwanda reintegrates 214 former armed group members from DR Congo
stories.summary: Rwanda officially reintegrated 214 former members of armed groups from the Democratic Republic of Congo this week after they completed several months at the Mutobo demobilization center.

stories.title: UN-backed Haiti mission implicated in four cases of sexual abuse, report finds
stories.summary: United Nations investigations substantiated four allegations of sexual exploitation and abuse in 2024 against personnel in the U.N.-backed security mission in Haiti. The majority of the mission's staff are Kenyan troops deployed to Port-au-Prince.

stories.title: Trump considers cabinet shake-up as several senior officials face possible removal -report
stories.summary: The Atlantic reported that President Trump is considering removing several senior officials, including FBI Director Kash Patel, Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll, and Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer. The timing of any changes remains uncertain.

stories.title: UN delays Hormuz shipping vote as China signals opposition
stories.summary: The UN Security Council postponed a vote on a Bahrain-drafted resolution to safeguard shipping in the Strait of Hormuz after China signalled opposition. The waterway carries roughly a fifth of global oil and gas supplies.

stories.title: Pakistan walks into IMF meetings in DC amid war shocks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb traveled to Washington for the 2026 IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings to seek emergency financing options. The visit gained urgency as the Iran war creates oil and gas volatility threatening Pakistan's reserves and widening its current account gap.

stories.title: Protests erupt in Guinea-Bissau after activist’s killing
stories.summary: Protests erupted in Guinea-Bissau after the killing of an activist. The United Nations condemned the killing as "brutal" and warned of shrinking civic space since the country's 2025 military takeover.

stories.title: How Israel is destroying healthcare infrastructure in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's ongoing attacks on hospitals, medical centres, and healthcare workers in southern Lebanon are driving mass displacement and deepening a public health crisis in the region.

stories.title: SBU exposes draft evasion scheme in Cherkasy involving doctors
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service uncovered and dismantled a large-scale draft evasion operation in the city of Cherkasy. The scheme was organized by local medical workers who helped individuals avoid military conscription.

stories.title: The Limits of Trump’s Regime Capture Strategy from Venezuela to Cuba
stories.summary: The Trump administration reinstated regime change as a U.S. foreign policy tool, reportedly emboldened by the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a January 3 raid. An analysis examines the limits of this leadership decapitation strategy as applied from Venezuela to Cuba.

stories.title: The Limits of Trump’s Regime Capture Strategy from Venezuela to Cuba
stories.summary: The Trump administration has revived regime change as a central tool of U.S. foreign policy, emboldened by the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a January 3 raid. The strategy marks a reversal from Trump's earlier campaign rhetoric against military interventionism abroad.

stories.title: Housing snapshot March 2026: Prices dip again after two-month rise
stories.summary: Israel's housing market saw prices dip again in March 2026 following a brief two-month rise, according to a regular Times of Israel property market report.

stories.title: As Anglo immigration grows, developers rethink ways to cultivate communal roots
stories.summary: As post-October 7 immigration from English-speaking countries to Israel grows, developers are adopting new approaches including rabbi-led neighborhoods and group purchases to help newcomers build community roots.

stories.title: Iranian women footballers reveal ‘enormous pressure’ of the Asian Cup saga
stories.summary: Two Iranian women footballers who initially sought asylum in Australia before reversing their decision spoke to Al Jazeera about the intense pressure they faced during the Asian Cup controversy.

stories.title: US blows up key Iranian bridge, steel plants
stories.summary: The United States and Israel escalated attacks on Iran, striking a century-old medical research centre in Tehran, the B1 bridge near Karaj, and steel plants. President Trump threatened further destruction, while Tehran vowed retaliatory strikes and Iran launched missiles toward Israel.

stories.title: Trump hails destruction of Iranian bridge, warning ‘more to follow’
stories.summary: President Trump praised the destruction of Iran's B1 bridge connecting Tehran and Karaj, warning that further strikes would follow. The attack killed eight people and wounded 95.

stories.title: US defence chief sacks senior army officials amid leadership crises
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Army Chief of Staff General Randy George along with General David Hodne and Major-General William Green Jr, according to reports from The Washington Post and Stars and Stripes.

stories.title: How the War with Iran Ends
stories.summary: Three weeks into the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, debate centers on whether the conflict will lead to a negotiated settlement, prolonged attrition, or internal collapse of the Islamic Republic. The strikes are degrading Tehran's military capacity, but the war's ultimate outcome remains uncertain.

stories.title: How the War with Iran Ends
stories.summary: Three weeks into the joint U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, analysts in Washington are debating whether the conflict will lead to a negotiated settlement, prolonged attrition, or internal collapse of the Islamic Republic. The strikes are reported to be degrading Tehran's military capacity.

stories.title: Hegseth fires US Army chief of staff in reported string of dismissals
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth forced the retirement of Army Chief of Staff General Randy George, the latest in a series of high-profile military dismissals since Hegseth took office in January.

stories.title: Ukraine's State Emergency Service clears nearly 200,000 hectares of landmines since start of war
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service has cleared nearly 200,000 hectares of territory and neutralized 600,000 explosive devices since Russia's full-scale invasion began.

stories.title: Ukraine's State Emergency Service clears nearly 200,000 hectares of landmines since start of war
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service has cleared nearly 200,000 hectares of land and neutralized approximately 600,000 explosive devices since Russia's full-scale invasion began.

stories.title: Iran warns UN action on Hormuz could escalate tensions
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned against any "provocative action" at the UN Security Council ahead of a vote on the possible use of force in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran blocked the waterway after the US-Israeli attack on its territory on February 28.

stories.title: Chinese airlines shed weight, add flights over Russia to trim fuel costs amid Iran war
stories.summary: Chinese airlines are implementing weight-control measures and rerouting European flights through Russian airspace to reduce fuel costs. The changes respond to surging oil prices driven by the Middle East conflict involving Iran, which is squeezing carriers' profit margins.

stories.title: ‘Every night they are bombarding’: at border crossing, some Iranians are fleeing war and some are heading home
stories.summary: At the Kapıköy border crossing between Iran and eastern Turkey, Iranians described the effects of ongoing bombardment and internet blackouts as they fled the war. Some travelers were heading in the opposite direction, returning to Iran to be closer to relatives amid the conflict.

stories.title: Myanmar’s parliament elects coup-leading general as civilian president
stories.summary: Myanmar's pro-military parliament elected Senior General Min Aung Hlaing as civilian president after he relinquished his top military post as constitutionally required. The leader of the 2021 coup transferred military command to the country's former intelligence chief. Monitoring groups dismissed the electoral process as window dressing.

stories.title: Watch: Strike hits major Iranian bridge near Tehran, killing at least 8 civilians
stories.summary: Strikes hit the unfinished B1 bridge in Iran's Alborz province near Tehran, killing at least eight civilians and wounding 95. Families had gathered near the site for Nature Day celebrations when the attack occurred.

stories.title: Trump announces destruction of Iran's tallest bridge
stories.summary: President Trump posted footage on social media showing the destruction of Iran's B1 bridge in Karaj, approximately 35 km from Tehran. He warned of further strikes unless Iran agrees to negotiations to end the five-week war.

stories.title: Trump’s ire at NATO leaves European partners bracing for potential US exit
stories.summary: European partners are bracing for a potential US exit from NATO amid President Trump's growing criticism of the alliance. Tensions over possible Strait of Hormuz operations have deepened concerns that the transatlantic rift may be irreparable.

stories.title: Iran says second US F-35 downed over central Iran
stories.summary: Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency reported that Iranian forces downed a second US F-35 fighter jet over central Iran. State-linked media added that the pilot's survival was considered unlikely.

stories.title: Paris police ban annual French Muslim event over ‘major terrorist risk’ from far-right groups
stories.summary: Paris police banned the Annual Gathering of the Muslims of France, scheduled from Friday to Monday, citing a major terrorist threat from small far-right groups. Authorities noted the event was taking place amid a particularly tense international and national context.

stories.title: Drone strikes disable 40% of Russia's Primorsk port storage – Reuters
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes in March damaged at least 40% of oil storage capacity at Russia's Primorsk port on the Baltic Sea, according to Reuters. The attacks significantly reduced Russian oil export volumes from the facility.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 35 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: On day 35 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, strikes hit a century-old medical research centre and a bridge near Tehran.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Army Behind Most Civilian Deaths - Report
stories.summary: A Human Rights Watch report found that Burkina Faso's army and allied militias are responsible for the majority of civilian deaths in the country, surpassing militant groups in brutality. The Fulani ethnic group has been particularly targeted by security forces.

stories.title: Drone strike sparks fires at Kuwait’s Mina Al-Ahmadi refinery
stories.summary: A drone attack struck Kuwait's Mina Al-Ahmadi refinery, igniting fires across several operational units. The Kuwait Petroleum Corporation confirmed the incident. Authorities reported no casualties.

stories.title: Fossil find reveals primordial burst of evolution
stories.summary: Paleontologists in China unearthed approximately 700 fossils of soft-bodied animals dating from 546 to 539 million years ago during the Ediacaran Period. The discovery reveals that animal life diversified in Earth's seas millions of years earlier than previously documented.

stories.title: US delays Japan’s Tomahawk missile supplies as Iran strikes take priority
stories.summary: The United States has informed Japan that deliveries of hundreds of Tomahawk cruise missiles will be delayed as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran depletes American weapons inventories. The Tomahawks are central to Tokyo's strategy of developing long-range strike capabilities to counter threats from China and North Korea.

stories.title: Four children killed in machete attack at Kampala nursery school
stories.summary: Four children were killed in a machete attack at a nursery school in Kampala, Uganda. Such attacks are rare in the capital and have sparked widespread grief and outrage.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Stone Age’ threats against Iran spark war crimes alarm
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iran's electricity grid and reduce the country to destitution, drawing warnings from experts about potential war crimes. Critics say the threats against a nation of 90 million violate Geneva Convention norms, though Trump faces few near-term consequences as his administration undermines international accountability institutions.

stories.title: Morning recap
stories.summary: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies warned that emergency medical supplies in Iran are at risk of running low. Russia's Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated the Strait of Hormuz remains open to Russian shipping. Yemen's Houthi group also claimed new military operations.

stories.title: Russian mariner held after Houthi Red Sea attack leaves Yemen for home
stories.summary: A Russian mariner detained for approximately eight months after a Houthi attack on a ship in the Red Sea has departed Yemen for Russia. The Houthi-run foreign ministry confirmed the sailor left following medical treatment in Sanaa.

stories.title: Kharkiv hit by four ballistic missiles, residential buildings damaged, woman injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Kharkiv with four ballistic missiles early Friday, damaging residential buildings and injuring one woman.

stories.title: ‘Dancing with the devil’: Nadav Lapid wants his satire film ‘Yes’ to ‘shake souls’
stories.summary: Israeli director Nadav Lapid discussed his new satire film "Yes," set in the aftermath of the October 7 attack. Lapid said the film addresses a global mix of vulgarity, nationalism, and authoritarianism rather than focusing on Israel specifically.

stories.title: Indonesia rebalances energy policy as Iran war spurs new projects
stories.summary: Indonesia is accelerating investments in both renewable energy and fossil fuel projects in response to the global energy crisis triggered by the Middle East conflict. Jakarta signed multiple deals with international partners aimed at strengthening energy security amid heightened geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Myanmar’s coup leader elected president by pro-military parliament
stories.summary: Myanmar's military-backed parliament elected coup leader Min Aung Hlaing as president, with 429 out of 584 votes cast by lawmakers.

stories.title: Russian forces maintain day-long drone barrage of Ukraine's Kharkiv
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted a sustained drone barrage against Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, throughout Thursday. Local officials reported at least two people were injured in the day-long series of strikes.

stories.title: China launches heavyweight rocket to challenge SpaceX’s Falcon 9. It fails
stories.summary: China's Tianlong-3 rocket, developed by Beijing-based startup Space Pioneer as a competitor to SpaceX's Falcon 9, failed during its launch from the Jiuquan facility due to a flight anomaly. The rocket is intended to support China's satellite megaconstellation plans to rival SpaceX's Starlink network.

stories.title: From general to Myanmar president: Min Aung Hlaing’s rebrand dismissed as ‘cosmetic’
stories.summary: Myanmar's pro-military parliament elected former junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as civilian president following an election widely dismissed as a cosmetic rebranding. Critics and analysts say the transition poses a challenge for ASEAN, which has excluded Myanmar from top summits over the military's ongoing war against its own population.

stories.title: Editor's Notes: This Passover, Israeli children deserve a future that's more than sirens
stories.summary: The editorial reflects on the compounding disruptions to Israeli children's lives, from COVID-19 to the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack and its aftermath, and now the current conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Tesla outraces China’s BYD in pure electric car sales to regain world’s top spot
stories.summary: Tesla reclaimed the top global spot in pure electric vehicle sales in the first quarter of 2026, delivering 358,023 units with a 6.5 percent year-on-year increase. China's BYD, which had previously overtaken Tesla, saw a 25.5 percent drop in quarterly EV sales.

stories.title: Chinese man blasts ghost stories over speakers for 10 hours daily to retaliate against neighbour
stories.summary: A man surnamed Lu in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, played ghost stories over loudspeakers for more than 10 hours daily as retaliation against a neighbor, keeping the volume just below China's legal noise limit. The case, publicized by China's Ministry of Justice, drew widespread online ridicule.

stories.title: Trump's contradictory messages on Iran: What comes next? - editorial
stories.summary: The article discusses the contradictory signals from President Trump regarding the U.S. war on Iran, noting that Washington defines its own strategic interests while Israel maintains its security imperatives.

stories.title: How China’s ‘teapot’ refineries are cushioning it from Iran war oil crisis
stories.summary: China's small independent "teapot" refineries are enabling the country to continue importing Iranian oil despite disruptions caused by the US-Iran war, helping cushion Beijing from the broader energy crisis.

stories.title: University town to be fast-tracked, Eric Chan says after mainland China visit
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Secretary Eric Chan pledged to fast-track development of a new university town after visiting similar projects in mainland China. Authorities plan to devise a strategy to attract top institutions from the mainland and overseas to participate in the project under the Northern Metropolis initiative.

stories.title: Man shot dead in Herzliya, another in Rahat, in third killing in town in a week
stories.summary: A man was shot dead in Herzliya and another in Rahat, marking the third killing in Rahat in one week. The death toll from violence in Israel's Arab community has reached 78 since the start of the year.

stories.title: South Africa: Two Killed in N1 Collision Amid Easter Rush - South African News Briefs - April 3, 2026
stories.summary: Two people were killed in a collision on South Africa's N1 highway amid heavy Easter holiday traffic.

stories.title: Groundbreaking Israeli study finds malarial parasites hack RNA to deceive immune system
stories.summary: Israeli researchers discovered that malaria parasites manipulate RNA to confuse the immune system and evade defences. The study could pave the way for new therapies against one of the world's deadliest diseases.

stories.title: ‘Disturbing trend’ of US-Israeli strikes hitting non-military targets in Iran
stories.summary: FRANCE 24 reported from Tehran that U.S.-Israeli strikes have increasingly hit non-military targets across Iran, including civilian airports, hospitals, universities, fuel depots, and pharmaceutical facilities. A strike on Iran's tallest bridge killed eight people and wounded 90 others.

stories.title: Chad: Tine Two Months After Repeated Attacks At the Border
stories.summary: Drone strikes by the Sudanese Armed Forces, Rapid Support Forces, and allied groups continue to hit civilian areas along the Sudan-Chad border near the city of Tine. Since early February 2026, Médecins Sans Frontières has treated 457 people injured in the attacks.

stories.title: Cooperation between Ukraine and the Netherlands becoming more systematic, regular, and deeper – Deputy PM Kachka
stories.summary: Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister Taras Kachka said cooperation between Ukraine and the Netherlands is becoming more systematic following agreements reached at this year's Lviv Conference, held in the Dutch city of Breda.

stories.title: Uganda: Police Name Four Children Killed in Kampala Daycare Stabbing Attack
stories.summary: A man attacked the Ggaba Early Childhood Day Care Centre in Makindye Division, Kampala, Uganda, stabbing and killing four children on Thursday afternoon. Police have identified the victims.

stories.title: Rwanda: IMF Agrees $250m Support to Help Rwanda Handle Economic Shocks
stories.summary: Rwanda reached a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund for a $250 million support program spanning 38 months, designed to help the country manage economic shocks.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump urges Iran to make deal after bridge strike
stories.summary: President Trump urged Iran to negotiate a deal after a U.S. strike destroyed Iran's largest bridge. Separately, Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery was hit by drones, causing fires, and a UN Security Council vote on authorizing defensive force to protect Hormuz shipping was delayed.

stories.title: Central African Republic: Special Prosecutor's Death At Critical Moment in Central African Republic
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch called for the protection of the legacy of Congolese special prosecutor Toussaint Muntazini following his death at a critical juncture in accountability efforts in the Central African Republic.
