While 2026 began with a successful US commando operation to seize Venezuela's president, Trump's first prime-time war address unsettled markets rather than reassuring them, and his responses to energy security concerns drew criticism.

stories.title: Russia’s 14th general killed since war began. His An-26 may have been shot down by Russia’s own air defense
stories.summary: Russia's 14th general killed since the start of the war, the commander of the Northern Fleet's mixed aviation corps, died when his An-26 aircraft may have been shot down by Russia's own air defense systems.

stories.title: President Putin holds talks with Egyptian Foreign Minister Abdelatty in Moscow
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty in Moscow. Their discussions focused on the ongoing war in the Middle East and bilateral economic cooperation between Russia and Egypt.

stories.title: Gulf states seek UN mandate for force to protect Hormuz
stories.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council has called on the UN Security Council to authorize the use of force to protect the Strait of Hormuz from Iranian disruption to maritime traffic.

stories.title: On birthright citizenship, Trump’s restrictive immigration agenda hits a rare roadblock
stories.summary: A U.S. court dealt a setback to President Donald Trump's effort to restrict birthright citizenship. The court indicated that the legal arguments supporting Trump's executive action are invalid, marking a rare obstacle to his immigration agenda.

stories.title: Sadiq Khan warns of ‘zero-tolerance approach’ to any repeat of Clapham disorder
stories.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan warned of a zero-tolerance approach following disorder in Clapham, where young people stormed shops as part of a social media trend. Khan said more arrests would follow and urged against any repeat of the violence over the Easter weekend.

stories.title: Invaders attack Solonytsivka community in Kharkiv region, killing one and wounding others
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Solonytsivka community in the Kharkiv district, killing one man and injuring a woman and a child.

stories.title: Putin calls for end to war in talks with Saudi crown prince
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman discussed the war on Iran by phone, with both sides calling for intensified diplomatic efforts to halt hostilities and pursue a long-term settlement.

stories.title: War update: 127 clashes on front, heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 127 Russian attacks along the front line since the start of the day. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: On the Radar: Brazil’s ‘Escobar,’ Haiti’s Latest Massacre, and Venezuela’s Former First Lady Under Scrutiny
stories.summary: This week's security roundup covers a major drug trafficking figure in Brazil dubbed the country's "Escobar," a recent massacre in Haiti, and legal scrutiny facing Venezuela's former first lady.

stories.title: Azerbaijan upholds conviction of opposition politician, lawyer says
stories.summary: Azerbaijan's Supreme Court in Baku rejected an appeal by a prominent opposition politician serving a nine-year prison sentence. The ruling, issued on Thursday, upholds the politician's original conviction, according to his lawyer.

stories.title: Iran executes man arrested over January protests
stories.summary: Iran executed a man who had been arrested in connection with protests that took place in January. In March, Iran had already executed three men convicted of killing two police officers during the same wave of demonstrations.

stories.title: 'An eye for an eye': Israel’s death penalty law is retaliatory and electorally motivated
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed a law establishing the death penalty for terrorists, which in practice would apply only to Palestinians. The legislation has drawn international condemnation, with critics arguing it is both retaliatory and politically motivated ahead of elections.

stories.title: UN experts urge investigation into Israel’s killing of Lebanese journalists
stories.summary: UN experts called for an investigation into Israel's killing of journalists in Lebanon, Gaza, and the West Bank, saying Israel has been emboldened by impunity for previous attacks on media workers.

stories.title: Lebanese artist files complaint in France against Israeli strike
stories.summary: Lebanese artist Ali Cherri filed a legal complaint in France against Israel over an airstrike. Amnesty International described the case as a rare opportunity to hold Israel accountable for its military actions.

stories.title: Pastor’s White House prayer claims Iranians seek death of all Jews
stories.summary: Evangelical pastor Franklin Graham, speaking at a White House prayer event, claimed Iranians seek to kill all Jews worldwide and asserted that President Trump was chosen by God.

stories.title: French pro-Palestine MEP Rima Hassan arrested over X post
stories.summary: French Member of the European Parliament Rima Hassan was arrested in connection with a social media post on X that allegedly referenced a 1970s airport attack. The detention drew criticism from French politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

stories.title: Space Force plans to establish HQ staff group as surrogate Futures Command
stories.summary: US Space Force Chief of Space Operations Gen. Chance Saltzman signed a memo initiating the creation of a new headquarters staff group, designated SF/S9, to coordinate future force planning. The proposal still requires approval from Air Force Secretary Troy Meink.

stories.title: Regions Calling: Spring Floods Catch Russian Officials Off Guard
stories.summary: The North Caucasus republics of Chechnya and Dagestan are facing catastrophic floods following their heaviest rainfall in decades, catching Russian officials off guard during the spring flood season.

stories.title: Russians carried out 129 attacks on Naftogaz facilities during heating season
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 129 attacks on Naftogaz Group gas infrastructure facilities during the 2025–2026 heating season, targeting Ukraine's energy supply network.

stories.title: Kremlin: Russia is forming new military units for “everyone,” including students
stories.summary: The Kremlin is forming new military units drawing from the general population, including university students. Reports indicate university rectors were instructed to push 2% of students into the army, potentially totaling up to 76,000 soldiers.

stories.title: ‘You have to be serious’: Macron criticises Trump’s mixed messages about Nato and Iran
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron, speaking during a state visit to South Korea, sharply criticized US President Donald Trump's inconsistent messaging on the Iran war and NATO. Macron called for stability and a return to peace, saying the situation required seriousness rather than contradictory daily pronouncements.

stories.title: Graveyard raid in India uncovers hidden cooking gas canisters amid shortage
stories.summary: Indian police seized 414 cooking-gas canisters hidden in a graveyard in Hyderabad and arrested suspects involved in black-market sales. The hoarding was driven by LPG supply shortages caused by shipping disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran. India imports about 60 percent of its LPG demand, mostly from the Middle East.

stories.title: Iran medical needs surge as supplies under threat: Red Cross
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross warned that emergency medical needs in Iran are rising exponentially. Stocks of trauma kits and other medical supplies could run low if the ongoing war continues.

stories.title: Starmer must call energy summit akin to 2008 crisis response, Labour MP says
stories.summary: Labour MP Polly Billington, a former government adviser, urged Prime Minister Keir Starmer to convene a global energy summit modeled on Gordon Brown's 2008 financial crisis response. She warned that economic consequences of the Iran war were imminent and called for Britain to reduce its fossil fuel dependence.

stories.title: Iran, Oman drafting protocol to monitor Hormuz traffic
stories.summary: Iran and Oman are drafting a joint protocol to monitor vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA, citing Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi.

stories.title: The Global Ripple Effect of the War in Iran
stories.summary: As the war with Iran enters its second month, the White House claims significant military achievements while pursuing diplomatic efforts. However, Iran retains the ability to strike Israel and Gulf allies and continues to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: The Global Ripple Effect of the War in Iran
stories.summary: As the US-Iran war enters its second month, the White House publicly touts military achievements, though Iran retains the ability to strike Israel and Gulf allies. Iran's threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continue to cause global economic ripple effects.

stories.title: Argentina expels Iran's diplomatic envoy: foreign ministry
stories.summary: Argentina's government declared Iran's chargé d'affaires, Mohsen Tehrani, persona non grata and expelled him from the country, according to the Argentine foreign ministry.

stories.title: Devastating strikes on Russia: Ukraine’s forces hit five strategic plants, 10 oil facilities in March
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck five strategic factories and 10 oil refining facilities across Russia in March, making it one of the most extensive months for strikes on Russian strategic infrastructure. Targets ranged from occupied Crimea to deep rear areas.

stories.title: Russia says it's ready to help resolve Iran conflict
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia is prepared to help resolve the Iran conflict and that President Vladimir Putin continues consultations with regional leaders.

stories.title: Strikes damage Iran health institute as US, Israel widen assault
stories.summary: US and Israeli forces expanded strikes in Iran on Thursday, hitting the historic Pasteur Institute, a prominent health and research facility, and a major commuter bridge near Tehran.

stories.title: BBC Russia reports Russian Northern Fleet general killed in An-26 crash
stories.summary: BBC Russia reported that Lt. Gen. Alexander Otroshchenko, commander of the Northern Fleet's composite aviation corps, may have been killed in an An-26 military transport plane crash in Crimea on March 31.

stories.title: Al-Aqsa appeal launched as Israel keeps mosque shut for 34th day
stories.summary: A new appeal has been launched over the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, which has remained closed for 34 consecutive days under Israeli restrictions. Advocates warn the prolonged closure could alter the site's status quo and deepen Israeli control over Jerusalem.

stories.title: Three children injured in Kharkiv region in Russian strike
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the Lozova district of Ukraine's Kharkiv region injured three children—girls aged 12, 14, and 15.

stories.title: Macron scoffs at Trump’s mockery of his marriage, says it ‘doesn’t merit a response’
stories.summary: French President Macron dismissed President Trump's public mockery of his marriage, saying it did not merit a response. Macron urged focus on serious matters such as the Iran conflict, stating the situation was not a show.

stories.title: Watch: Trump's shifting deadlines for ending Iran war
stories.summary: The BBC's chief international correspondent reviewed President Trump's repeated shifts in stated deadlines for concluding the US war with Iran, analyzing his latest White House address.

stories.title: Israel imposes curfew on Palestinians over Jewish Passover break
stories.summary: Israel imposed a curfew on Palestinian neighborhoods in the city of Hebron during the Jewish Passover holiday. Simultaneously, Jewish extremists attempted to storm the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Jewish diaspora leaders urge Israeli president to stop West Bank settler violence
stories.summary: Over 3,000 members of the Jewish diaspora, including former UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, signed an open letter urging Israeli President Isaac Herzog to stop settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. The letter was facilitated by the London Initiative, a liberal Zionist network.

stories.title: Qatar says it intercepted Iranian drone attack
stories.summary: Qatar's defence ministry reported that Iranian drones targeted the country, stating that its armed forces successfully intercepted and neutralized all incoming drones.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Army behind most civilian deaths — report
stories.summary: A Human Rights Watch report found that Burkina Faso's security forces and allied militias are responsible for most civilian deaths, describing them as more brutal than militant groups. The Fulani ethnic group has been particularly targeted.

stories.title: Ditch the Camo and Zs, Officials Tell Russians in Border Areas Amid Drone Attacks
stories.summary: Regional officials in Russian border areas are warning civilians not to wear camouflage clothing or drive vehicles marked with military symbols, as they could be mistaken for military targets amid ongoing drone attacks.

stories.title: Moldova’s parliament votes to withdraw from Commonwealth of Independent States
stories.summary: Moldova's parliament voted to denounce key agreements with the Commonwealth of Independent States, with 60 of 101 lawmakers supporting the measure. The vote clears the way for Moldova's withdrawal from the Russia-led organization.

stories.title: Romania weighs cancelling drone contract with Elbit Systems
stories.summary: Romania is considering cancelling a drone procurement contract with Israeli defense firm Elbit Systems due to delivery delays. Bucharest is also exploring closer defense cooperation with Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine’s USFs strike Russian drone depot, aircraft, and radar in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, working with military intelligence, carried out a series of operations against Russian military targets in occupied Crimea on April 2, striking a drone depot, aircraft, and radar installations.

stories.title: Israel's war on Gaza erases autism therapy and support systems
stories.summary: Healthcare and autism therapy services in Gaza have collapsed amid Israel's ongoing military campaign. Autistic children face lost treatment and repeated displacement, reversing years of therapeutic progress.

stories.title: Katz to Hezbollah chief Qassem: You won't live to see Israel’s full response to Passover attacks
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a direct video threat to Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem, warning of a heavy price for attacks on Israeli citizens during Passover Seder celebrations.

stories.title: Argentina expels Iranian diplomat amid rift over blacklisting IRGC
stories.summary: Argentina expelled an Iranian diplomat amid a diplomatic rift after Buenos Aires designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organization. Tehran accused Argentina of making offensive accusations.

stories.title: Pakistan in talks with Afghanistan but Kabul must demonstrate ‘visible and verifiable actions’: FO
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan are holding talks in Urumqi, China, following Pakistan's launch of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan on February 26. Pakistan's Foreign Office said Kabul must demonstrate "visible and verifiable actions" for progress.

stories.title: Iran's two largest steel plants shut down due to strikes, companies say
stories.summary: Iran's two largest steel plants, Mobarakeh Steel Company and Khuzestan Steel Company, have ceased production following strikes that Iran attributes to coordinated U.S.-Israeli military operations, threatening significant damage to the country's economy.

stories.title: Coalition of countries discuss ‘every possible measure’ to pressure Iran into reopening strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: More than 40 countries joined a virtual summit hosted by UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper to discuss coordinated diplomatic and economic measures to pressure Iran into reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Cooper described Iran's actions as reckless efforts to hijack the global economy.

stories.title: Global oil crisis opens ‘window of opportunity’ for renewable energy – expert
stories.summary: Energy experts say the ongoing global oil crisis and shifting geopolitical dynamics in energy markets are creating conditions that accelerate the transition toward renewable energy sources and new economic models.

stories.title: World Cup 2026: Iran and Infantino talks progressing as war darkens US trip
stories.summary: Iranian football officials held their first face-to-face meeting with FIFA President Gianni Infantino since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, discussing Iran's participation in the 2026 World Cup amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike hits newly opened B1 bridge near Tehran, killing two
stories.summary: A U.S.-Israeli airstrike struck the B1 bridge in Karaj, west of Tehran, killing at least two people. The bridge connects the capital to surrounding areas.

stories.title: UK to convene meeting of 40 countries to discuss how to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence confirmed that military planners will convene at the UK's Permanent Joint Headquarters next week with representatives from 40 countries to discuss making the Strait of Hormuz safe for navigation.

stories.title: Ballistic missile strike on facility in Chernihiv kills one, injures young woman
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a facility in Chernihiv with a ballistic missile, killing one person and injuring a young woman.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz says Centre, provinces need to make collective efforts to provide relief amid global oil crisis
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urged the Centre and all four provinces to collectively prioritize relief efforts amid a global oil crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran. He called for curtailing development spending and utilizing resources wisely.

stories.title: ‘A litany of lies’: Trump’s rambling primetime Iran address sparks backlash
stories.summary: President Trump's 19-minute primetime address on the Iran war drew widespread criticism, with commentators expressing bewilderment at his vow to bomb Iran "back to the stone ages." The speech had been expected to signal a winding down of the US military campaign that began on February 28.

stories.title: UK elections: Here's where Greens, Your Party and independents will challenge Labour
stories.summary: Left-wing parties including the Greens and independents are coordinating to challenge Labour and Reform in the UK's May 2026 local elections, seeking to win control of councils across the country.

stories.title: A year after ‘Liberation Day,’ impact of Trump tariffs on defense industry remains muted
stories.summary: One year after the Trump administration's "Liberation Day" tariff announcements, experts and former defense officials say the impact on the defense industrial base has been relatively limited. Exemptions built into the tariff regime have helped blunt the financial effects on defense manufacturers.

stories.title: “The last thread that keeps us anchored in a toxic, bitter past” — Moldova’s parliament votes to leave the post-Soviet CIS bloc
stories.summary: Moldova's parliament voted 60 to 17 on April 2 to leave the post-Soviet Commonwealth of Independent States by denouncing its founding agreements. Only the Communist and Socialist blocs voted against the measure.

stories.title: At least one killed as heavy rain lashes Karachi; city administration declares emergency
stories.summary: At least one person died in Karachi after heavy rain caused a building wall to collapse in Pak Colony, trapping a passerby under debris. City authorities declared an emergency as rain affected multiple areas.

stories.title: Uganda receives first US deportation flight under third-country agreement
stories.summary: A US deportation flight landed in Uganda under a new third-country agreement with the Trump administration. The deported individuals, who have no ties to Uganda, are expected to stay temporarily before potential transfer to other countries. Legal challenges to the scheme are anticipated.

stories.title: Ukraine’s MFA launches 24/7 broadcast to rebut Orbán’s statements
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs launched a 24/7 online broadcast called "Hungarian Radio Ukraine" to counter what it describes as absurd statements by Hungarian officials regarding Ukraine.

stories.title: Streeting hits out at BMA ‘delusion’ as talks to avert resident doctors’ strike fail
stories.summary: Last-ditch talks between the UK government and the British Medical Association failed, meaning resident doctors in England will begin a six-day strike starting Tuesday. Health Secretary Wes Streeting accused the BMA of "delusion" and withdrew an offer of extra training places.

stories.title: IRGC says it has launched attacks on Amazon centre in Bahrain
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it attacked an Amazon cloud computing centre in Bahrain in retaliation for U.S. strikes, warning of more severe actions against companies operating in the region if hostilities continue.

stories.title: Iran army chief tells commanders to prepare for any attack, state media reports
stories.summary: Iran's army commander-in-chief ordered military commanders to prepare for any potential attack, warning that no enemy troops should survive if adversaries attempt a ground operation.

stories.title: Video: Protests in Gaza against Israel’s Palestinian death penalty law
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza held protests against the Israeli government's approval of a law authorizing the death penalty for Palestinian prisoners.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia-China Relations Remain Model of South-South Cooperation, Say Officials
stories.summary: Senior officials from Ethiopia and China reaffirmed that bilateral relations remain a model of South-South cooperation. The officials, speaking in Addis Ababa, emphasized mutual respect and shared development goals as the foundation of the partnership.

stories.title: IRGC tightening grip as Iran faces economic collapse, internal rift – report
stories.summary: A report describes the IRGC as tightening its grip on power as Iran faces economic collapse and internal political rifts. The situation is characterized as the most significant upheaval in Iran since the 1979 revolution.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Green Legacy Initiative Model for Climate Resilience - Zambezi River Basin Secretary General
stories.summary: Zambezi Watercourse Commission Secretary-General Felix Ngamlagosi praised Ethiopia's Green Legacy initiative as an exemplary model for climate resilience. He said the program effectively mitigates climate change impacts and protects the environment.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Eight Years On - Ethiopia's Economic Evolution Toward a Modern and Diversified Economy
stories.summary: Ethiopia's Office of the Prime Minister marked the eighth anniversary of its reform program, highlighting the country's economic transformation. Officials said Ethiopia has shifted from a state-led model to a more market-oriented, diversified, and resilient economy over the past eight years.

stories.title: Latin Patriarch holds limited prayers at Holy Sepulchre after Palm Sunday uproar
stories.summary: Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa held limited Holy Thursday prayers at Jerusalem's Church of the Holy Sepulchre, describing it as a place of peace amid global turmoil following disruptions on Palm Sunday related to the Iran war.

stories.title: PSX tumbles 3,500 points as Trump speech sinks hopes for quick end to war
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell 3,500 points, or 2.25 percent, after a press conference by U.S. President Donald Trump dashed investor hopes for a quick end to the war on Iran. The index closed at 152,011 points.

stories.title: Russia Will Send Second Oil Tanker to Cuba, Energy Minister Says
stories.summary: Russian Energy Minister Sergei Tsivilev announced that Russia will send a second oil tanker to Cuba, stating that the first vessel successfully reached the island and another is being loaded.

stories.title: Mozambique: UK Disbursed 79.9 Million Dollars for Water Supply Systems
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has disbursed 79.9 million US dollars to support water supply systems in Mozambique. The funding is aimed at improving water infrastructure in the country.

stories.title: ‘Israel has been avoiding any diplomacy’ and pursuing escalation
stories.summary: Analysts argue that Israel has avoided diplomatic engagement in favor of military escalation, relying heavily on force as its primary policy tool in the current conflict.

stories.title: Mozambique: Construction of Photovoltaic Power Plant Launched in Tete
stories.summary: The governments of Mozambique and South Korea laid the foundation stone for the Nkantha Photovoltaic Power Plant in Chifunde district, Tete province, on Wednesday. The solar energy project marks a joint development effort between the two countries.

stories.title: Nigeria: 197 Insurgents Surrendered, 813 Hostages Rescued in March - - Defence Headquarters
stories.summary: Nigeria's Defence Headquarters reported that 197 insurgents surrendered and 813 hostages were rescued during military operations in March. The military has consistently publicized operational gains since the start of the year.

stories.title: Trump tariffs cast shadow as US-China trade shrinks ahead of leaders’ meet
stories.summary: New US government data showed direct trade between the United States and China continues to shrink amid ongoing tariff escalations. The figures were released ahead of a planned leaders' meeting in Beijing next month aimed at stabilizing relations. The data coincides with the anniversary of Trump's "Liberation Day" tariff measures.

stories.title: Mozambique: Over 370,000 Expected to Cross Borders During Easter Holiday
stories.summary: Mozambique's Immigration Service estimates that over 370,000 people are expected to cross the country's borders during the Easter holidays.

stories.title: Russia bans gasoline exports until end of July
stories.summary: The Russian government imposed a ban on gasoline exports by producers effective Thursday, with the restriction set to remain in place until the end of July.

stories.title: Russian nuclear missile forces hold drills in Siberia
stories.summary: Russia's strategic missile forces conducted drills in Siberia involving camouflaged movements of Yars intercontinental ballistic missiles, which are capable of carrying nuclear warheads.

stories.title: Some authors refuse to revise books to comply with Russia’s drug ‘propaganda’ law, publisher says
stories.summary: Some rights holders are refusing to revise their books to comply with Russia's law banning the "propaganda" of drugs, according to Yevgeny Kapyev, head of the Eksmo publishing house, as reported by RBC.

stories.title: Iran vows ‘crushing’ attacks on U.S. and Israel after Trump’s threats
stories.summary: Iran vowed "crushing" attacks on the United States and Israel after President Trump warned that strikes would intensify if Tehran did not agree to a negotiated settlement. Trump said the U.S. was "very close" to achieving its objectives.

stories.title: Tehran-Karaj bridge hit again by US-Israeli strike while medics attend to injured
stories.summary: A U.S.-Israeli strike hit a highway bridge in Karaj near Tehran for a second time while rescue workers were treating casualties from the initial attack, killing two people and injuring several others.

stories.title: U.S. Senators from both parties support maintaining NATO membership
stories.summary: U.S. senators from both the Democratic and Republican parties issued a joint statement supporting the continued membership of the United States in NATO.

stories.title: Iran vows ‘crushing’ attacks on US after Trump threats
stories.summary: Iran vowed "crushing" retaliatory attacks on the United States following President Trump's threats to intensify strikes if Tehran does not agree to a negotiated settlement.

stories.title: Seder held underground in Israel as Iran fires missiles after Trump’s address
stories.summary: Iran fired missiles at Israel and Gulf Arab states on Thursday during the Jewish holiday of Passover, with a Seder held underground in Israel. The strikes demonstrated Tehran's continued ability to hit targets despite President Trump's claims that the Iranian threat was nearly eliminated.

stories.title: Russia to send second oil tanker to Cuba, minister says
stories.summary: Russia's Energy Minister Sergei Tsivilev announced Thursday that Moscow is dispatching a second oil tanker to Cuba as the island faces severe energy shortages. The shipment follows an initial delivery earlier in the week, prompted by widespread blackouts after the United States cut off key fuel supplies to Cuba.

stories.title: Ukraine ramps up engineering mines and UAV ammo—Q1 2026 already surpasses 50% of 2025 supply
stories.summary: Ukraine significantly ramped up production of engineering mines and UAV ammunition, with first-quarter 2026 output already surpassing 50% of the total 2025 supply. Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov emphasized the need to continue scaling production.

stories.title: 'I haven't slept for days': Iranians describe mounting desperation after a month of war
stories.summary: Residents across Iran report expanding airstrikes, growing economic hardship, and fear of government repression after a month of ongoing conflict.

stories.title: ‘Dangerous escalation’: 8 Muslim-majority countries, including Pakistan, condemn Israel’s death penalty law
stories.summary: Eight Muslim-majority countries — Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE — jointly condemned Israel's new law making death by hanging the default sentence for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks in military courts.

stories.title: TikTok pulls Israeli ultranationalist’s account for breach of hate speech rules
stories.summary: TikTok removed the account of an ultranationalist pro-settlement Israeli influencer for violating hate speech and bullying rules. The action followed reporting by the Guardian that flagged videos showing harassment of Palestinians and activists in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Middle East war: Few solutions to fuel shortages in Africa
stories.summary: African countries face growing fuel shortages as the U.S.-Israel-Iran war drives global fuel prices sharply higher. Questions are being raised about whether African governments are taking sufficient measures to stabilize their fuel markets.

stories.title: UK says Iran holding world economy 'hostage' with Hormuz attacks
stories.summary: UK Home Secretary Yvette Cooper accused Iran of holding the global economy hostage through attacks disrupting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, calling for coordinated diplomatic and economic measures to reopen the vital waterway.

stories.title: French-Palestinian MEP in custody for 'apology for terrorism' in post on X
stories.summary: French-Palestinian Member of European Parliament Rima Hassan was detained in France on suspicion of "apology for terrorism" after posting on X about Japanese pro-Palestinian activist Kozo Okamoto.

stories.title: Burkina, Mali troops kill more civilians than jihadists do, data shows
stories.summary: A Human Rights Watch report and data tally show that government and allied forces in Burkina Faso have killed more than twice as many civilians as Islamist militants since 2023. Similar patterns were noted in Mali.

stories.title: This Passover, Israel embraces the politics of execution
stories.summary: Israel's government approved a death penalty law targeting Palestinian prisoners, drawing criticism as the measure coincides with the Passover holiday, which celebrates themes of freedom.

stories.title: Romania weighs cancelling drone contract with Israel's Elbit Systems
stories.summary: Romania's Defense Minister Miruta is considering cancelling a 2022 drone contract with Israel's Elbit Systems after the company failed to meet delivery timelines originally set to begin in 2025.

stories.title: Iranian Nobel laureate suffered suspected heart attack in prison, family says
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi reportedly suffered a suspected heart attack while imprisoned. Her brother has warned her life is in imminent danger and called for her immediate transfer to a hospital.

stories.title: Costa Rica strikes deal to accept third country deportees from US
stories.summary: Costa Rica agreed to accept up to 25 deported migrants per week from the United States under a new deal with the Trump administration. The agreement is part of Washington's broader strategy of deporting people to third countries they have no connection to.

stories.title: UN chief to US and Israel: it is ‘high time to stop the war’
stories.summary: UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called on the U.S. and Israel to stop the war on Iran, while also urging Iran to cease attacks on neighboring states, warning that the conflict risks expanding into a wider regional war.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan hold talks in China to end months of conflict
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan held direct talks in China aimed at ending months of bilateral conflict, with Beijing acting as mediator between the two former allies.

stories.title: Russia bans producers from exporting petrol until end-July
stories.summary: Russia has imposed a ban on petrol exports effective until the end of July. The restriction does not apply to countries that have inter-governmental agreements with Russia on fuel supplies.

stories.title: Award-winning Iranian human rights lawyer arrested in Tehran, says her daughter
stories.summary: Award-winning Iranian human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh was arrested at her home in Tehran on Wednesday, according to her daughter Mehraveh Khandan. Sotoudeh's whereabouts remain unknown. Activists accused the Iranian regime of cracking down on civil society under cover of the war with Israel and the US.

stories.title: US may be committing war crimes in Iran, legal experts say
stories.summary: More than 100 legal experts issued a statement expressing profound concern over what they described as serious violations of international law by the US military in Iran, suggesting possible war crimes.

stories.title: Trump’s prime-time speech shows a president torn between escalation and exit
stories.summary: In a prime-time televised address, U.S. President Donald Trump signaled willingness both to escalate military action and to pursue a diplomatic deal with Iran. Analysts noted he intends to enforce stated red lines while remaining open to negotiations with Tehran.

stories.title: Two of Iran’s biggest steel plants put out of service following US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Iran's Mobarakeh Steel Company and Khuzestan Steel Company reported complete shutdowns following U.S.-Israeli airstrikes, with Khuzestan officials estimating at least six months before production can resume.

stories.title: Kherson RMA: Russian forces intensify use of fiber-optic drones
stories.summary: According to the Kherson Regional Military Administration, Russian forces have intensified drone attacks in the Kherson region, with a notable increase in the deployment of fiber-optic-guided drones.

stories.title: Uganda: Four children killed in knife attack at Kampala kindergarten
stories.summary: Four children aged two to three were killed in a knife attack at a kindergarten in Kampala, Uganda. The male suspect reportedly gained access to the daycare by posing as a parent before being apprehended by police.

stories.title: Republican senators McConnell and Tillis break with Trump on Nato withdrawal
stories.summary: Republican Senators Mitch McConnell and Thom Tillis publicly opposed President Trump's consideration of withdrawing from NATO after the alliance declined to join the US-Israeli assault on Iran. They warned that leaving NATO would aid US rivals and threaten national security, noting that Senate approval would be required under a 2024 law.

stories.title: US war on Iran: 'Absolute disaster' for Middle Eastern airlines
stories.summary: Dr. Wouter Dewulf of the University of Antwerp described the impact of the US–Iran war on global airlines as a convergence of geopolitical upheaval and market instability. Rising oil prices driven by the conflict have sharply affected airline costs, while airspace closures and shifting travel patterns have disproportionately hurt Middle Eastern carriers.

stories.title: The War You’re Not Allowed to See: How the UAE Rewrites the Story of Iranian Strikes
stories.summary: Bellingcat identified multiple incidents in which United Arab Emirates authorities downplayed damage from Iranian drone strikes, mischaracterized interceptions, or failed to acknowledge successful hits. A review of official UAE statements found discrepancies between the public narrative and evidence observable through open-source analysis.

stories.title: Attempt to tow drifting Russian LNG tanker to Libyan port fails as vessel breaks free in rough weather
stories.summary: An attempt to tow the drifting Russian LNG tanker Arctic Metagaz to a Libyan port failed after the vessel broke free in rough weather, according to Libya's Ports and Maritime Transport Authority on April 2.

stories.title: US embassy warns nationals to leave Iraq 'immediately'
stories.summary: The US embassy in Baghdad urged all American nationals to leave Iraq immediately, warning that attacks could increase within 24 to 48 hours in central Baghdad.

stories.title: Austria rejects US request to use airspace for Iran operations
stories.summary: Austria's defence ministry rejected multiple U.S. requests to use its airspace for military operations against Iran, citing Austria's longstanding policy of military neutrality. Spain and Italy have taken similar positions.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s Father Says He Held ‘Memorable’ Meeting With Vladimir Putin
stories.summary: Errol Musk, father of Elon Musk, said he held a "memorable" meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin during a two-week trip to Russia focused on research projects with Russian scientists.

stories.title: US reinforcements are coming to the Gulf – but what does victory look like?
stories.summary: Al Jazeera's defence editor examines how the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran has expanded into a broader regional war, as Washington sends additional reinforcements to the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Can the US seize Iran’s enriched uranium – and what are the risks?
stories.summary: Experts say a potential U.S. military operation to seize Iran's enriched uranium would face significant chemical, logistical, and tactical challenges, raising questions about feasibility and risk.

stories.title: Iran releases mocking missile launch video after Trump threats
stories.summary: Iranian state media broadcast footage of missile launches featuring warheads plastered with messages mocking U.S. President Donald Trump, released in response to his recent threats against Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine just doubled rewards for eliminating Russian drone operators — exchangeable for EW equipment and robotics
stories.summary: Ukraine doubled the financial rewards offered for eliminating Russian drone operators before they can launch their aircraft. The bounties can be exchanged for electronic warfare equipment and robotics.

stories.title: Russian sabotage: Poland charges five suspects over arson of Warsaw shopping center
stories.summary: Polish prosecutors charged five individuals, including a Ukrainian citizen, in connection with the 2024 arson of the Marywilska 44 shopping center in Warsaw. Authorities linked the attack to a broader Russian sabotage campaign targeting supporters of Ukraine.

stories.title: Sweden to buy air defence systems for 8.7 billion crowns, defence minister says
stories.summary: Sweden announced the purchase of air defence and anti-drone systems worth 8.7 billion Swedish crowns (approximately $916 million). The contracts involve suppliers including Saab and BAE Systems, according to the Swedish defence minister speaking in Stockholm.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts prepare to leave Earth’s orbit and head towards the moon
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission entered its second day as four astronauts prepared to leave Earth's orbit and head toward the moon. The 10-day voyage aims to mark the first time in over 50 years that humans have traveled to the moon's vicinity. The mission is a critical test ahead of planned lunar surface landings.

stories.title: Man stabs 4 children to death at Uganda kindergarten
stories.summary: A man in his thirties stabbed four children to death at a kindergarten in the Makindye Division of Kampala, Uganda, on Thursday. Police said the suspect gained access to the Ggaba Early Childhood Development Program school by posing as a parent and attacked children aged around two and three with a knife.

stories.title: AOC vows to block future US military aid to Israel, its Iron Dome and defense
stories.summary: US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announced she will oppose any future US military aid to Israel, including funding for Iron Dome and other defensive systems. She cited human rights concerns and said Israel is capable of funding its own defense.

stories.title: Expelled from camp, Palestinian refugees now face Iranian rockets
stories.summary: An estimated 32,000 Palestinian refugees were displaced from their homes in the West Bank by Israeli military operations in 2025. After being expelled from camps, the displaced population now faces additional danger from Iranian rocket attacks.

stories.title: Russia woos students for its drone forces in Ukraine with large financial packages
stories.summary: Russia is recruiting students for its drone units fighting in Ukraine by offering large financial incentive packages. The effort reflects Moscow's strategy to diversify its approaches to replenishing military personnel for the ongoing war.

stories.title: Winning the psychological war: How Israelis endure Iran’s war of nerves
stories.summary: An analysis describes Iran's military strategy against Israel as primarily psychological, arguing that missile attacks are intended to create a pervasive sense of insecurity among the Israeli public beyond physical infrastructure damage.

stories.title: Britain says 40 countries discuss reopening Strait of Hormuz after Iran blockade
stories.summary: Britain hosted a virtual meeting of about 40 countries to discuss joint action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz after Iran's blockade. Participants included France, Germany, Canada, the UAE, and India. British Foreign Minister Yvette Cooper said Iran's blockade was threatening global economic security.

stories.title: Online algorithms are driving Israel’s global reputation crisis - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that online algorithms and short attention spans are driving a global reputation crisis for Israel, while suggesting strategic engagement could improve outcomes.

stories.title: How Ukraine’s defense industry innovates at the speed of modern war
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense industry continues to innovate rapidly to meet the demands of modern warfare. Analysis indicates the key drivers are organizational adaptations rather than purely technological advances.

stories.title: More than 40 countries hold talks on ways to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Diplomats from more than 40 countries held talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global shipping route choked off amid the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. Britain accused Iran of holding the world's economy hostage.

stories.title: Kremlin spokesperson says he has no knowledge of campaigns to recruit students, business employees for war
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated he had no knowledge of reported campaigns to recruit students and employees of Ryazan region businesses to fight in Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Lebanon prime minister: ‘No end in sight’ to Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said there is no end in sight to Israeli attacks on Lebanon, which have displaced a million people, and condemned what he called the significant expansion of Israeli occupation of Lebanese territories.

stories.title: What will the US do next in its war on Iran? Chinese pundits point to a likely path
stories.summary: Chinese analysts suggest the US is likely to pursue an "escalate to de-escalate" strategy in its conflict with Iran, planning more aggressive strikes in the coming weeks to force a resolution. President Trump claimed in a Wednesday address that the US-Israel war on Iran had delivered decisive victories with core military objectives nearly completed.

stories.title: China’s Iran war strategy, Trump’s Hormuz ask: 7 global relations reads
stories.summary: A curated roundup highlighted seven global relations stories, including exiled Iranian prince Reza Pahlavi's plans to reset Tehran's ties with China and Russia, and developments around the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The coverage also addressed China's strategic calculations regarding the Iran war.

stories.title: Ukraine allocates UAH 22B for regional resilience plans, seeks additional funding – Kuleba
stories.summary: Ukraine has allocated 22 billion hryvnias from the state budget for regional resilience plans, according to official Kuleba. Additional funding is being sought to implement priority measures across Ukrainian regions.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kharkiv for second time today; casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv for the second time in a single day, with casualties reported. The attack is part of ongoing Russian aerial assaults targeting Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: Tehran vows ‘crushing’ blows to US after Trump threatens to send Iran to ‘stone age’
stories.summary: Tehran vowed retaliatory "crushing" blows against the United States after President Trump threatened to send Iran to the "stone age." Iran also launched approximately 20 missiles at Israel during Passover, while a major bridge near Tehran was struck by U.S. forces.

stories.title: Money starts flowing for new GCAP fighter, as Britain sorts out finances
stories.summary: A new contract described as a "bridge" arrangement has been signed to keep work on the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) fighter jet moving forward through the end of June. Britain is sorting out its financial commitments to the multinational program.

stories.title: Members of Iran’s Basij militia mount online intimidation campaign to deter protests
stories.summary: Members of Iran's Basij paramilitary force have been posting photos online since early March showing themselves heavily armed and patrolling Tehran's streets with portraits of the new supreme leader. The campaign is intended to intimidate Iranians and discourage renewed anti-regime protests.

stories.title: March from hell: Ukraine hits 10 refineries, 12 air defense systems, 5 Russian factories, halting missile chip supply for 6 months (MAP)
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck a record number of strategic Russian targets in March, hitting 10 oil refineries, 12 air defense systems, and five factories. Officials say the factory strikes disrupted Russian missile chip supply for an estimated six months.

stories.title: EU and democracy at stake in Hungary parliamentary polls
stories.summary: Hungary's upcoming general election could have broad implications for the European Union if Prime Minister Viktor Orbán wins again. Polish and Irish leaders this week condemned leaked phone calls between Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó and Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov, calling Budapest's ties to Moscow "sinister" and "repulsive."

stories.title: Four suspects in foiled Paris bombing put in pre-trial detention
stories.summary: Four suspects linked to a foiled bombing plot in Paris were placed in pre-trial detention on terrorism charges. Investigators are examining possible connections to a suspected pro-Iran network after a powerful explosive device was discovered.

stories.title: India’s new digital rules tighten the noose on freedom of speech
stories.summary: India has introduced new digital regulations that expand executive authority over internet content. Journalists, news outlets, satirists, and cartoonists have been among those targeted under increasingly strict censorship laws. Critics warn the rules signal growing digital authoritarianism in the country.

stories.title: No room to play: A childhood denied to children with autism
stories.summary: The article highlights the systemic lack of structural support for children with autism, noting that despite annual awareness campaigns, families continue to face gaps in services, affordability, and inclusion.

stories.title: Iran's military warns of crushing attacks until adversaries' 'surrender'
stories.summary: Iran's armed forces unified command spokesperson declared Thursday that Tehran would continue military operations until the United States and Israel face "permanent regret and surrender," according to the Tasnim news agency. The statement followed US President Donald Trump's warning that Washington would strike Iran "extremely hard" within weeks.

stories.title: CENTCOM releases video of air strikes in fifth week of war on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command released video footage showing airstrikes conducted during the fifth week of military operations against Iran, including the targeting of drones and tanks.

stories.title: South Africa: Exclusive - the Mystery of Minister Sisisi Tolashe's Missing SUVs
stories.summary: South African Social Development Minister Sisisi Tolashe told Parliament she received two luxury SUVs as donations for the ANC Women's League. The ANC has denied knowledge of the donations, raising questions about the vehicles' origins.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces destroy Russian assault group on Lyman front
stories.summary: Ukrainian Armed Forces destroyed a Russian assault group operating on the Lyman axis of the front line. No further details on casualties or equipment losses were provided.

stories.title: Somalia: Iranian-Flagged Vessel Hijacked Off Somalia
stories.summary: An Iranian-flagged vessel identified as the Al Waseemi 786 was hijacked by suspected pirates off the coast of Somalia, according to maritime security agencies.

stories.title: Germany urges China to help push Iran to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul spoke with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi about the Middle East conflict, with both countries calling for free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and urging a negotiated solution.

stories.title: How international media covered President Trump’s first address to nation on Iran war
stories.summary: International media coverage of President Trump's first national address on the Iran war noted that he failed to outline a clear strategy, while repeating claims of degrading Iran's military and vowing further strikes.

stories.title: US crude tops US$110, Wall Street falls after Trump vows more Iran attacks
stories.summary: US crude oil prices topped $110 per barrel and Wall Street fell sharply after President Trump vowed continued attacks on Iran without offering a clear end-date. The S&P 500 dropped 1.1 percent, the Dow Jones fell 545 points, and the Nasdaq declined 1.6 percent. European and Asian markets also declined.

stories.title: Artist files war crime case in Paris over Israeli strike that killed parents in Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanese-French artist Ali Cherri filed a legal complaint with France's war crimes unit over an Israeli bombing of his family home in Lebanon that killed his parents and a domestic worker. The case is the first time a French court has taken a complaint regarding Israel's bombing campaign in Lebanon.

stories.title: Can Starmer’s 40-nation coalition open the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is leading a 40-nation coalition exploring options to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 20 percent of global oil and gas transits.

stories.title: G7 and GCC countries to meet and discuss Hormuz next week
stories.summary: France, which holds the G7 presidency, announced that G7 and Gulf Cooperation Council countries will meet next week to discuss resolving the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russia paid 206 troops for every Ukrainian square kilometer gained in March. Last summer it paid 61 — expert
stories.summary: Russia lost approximately 31,960 troops in March while gaining 155 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory, equating to roughly 206 casualties per square kilometer. Last summer, the ratio was about 61 troops per square kilometer gained.

stories.title: Iraq begins oil exports on tankers through Syria: ministry
stories.summary: Iraq began exporting crude oil via tanker trucks through Syria after disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Iraqi oil ministry. The shift comes as the regional war continues to destabilize energy markets.

stories.title: As Iran war rages, Europe gears up for energy crisis
stories.summary: The European Union is confronting a developing energy crisis linked to the ongoing Iran war, urging citizens to reduce energy consumption. Energy analysts are calling for increased investment in renewables and concrete policy measures to address potential supply shortages.

stories.title: Why Lebanon should join the International Criminal Court
stories.summary: Advocates argue that Lebanon should join the International Criminal Court, which would enable ICC jurisdiction over alleged Israeli war crimes on Lebanese territory and increase political pressure for accountability.

stories.title: As Hungary blocks Ukraine’s €90 billion, the EU quietly splits into two tiers—one for 27 members, one for 26
stories.summary: Hungary is blocking a €90 billion EU support package for Ukraine, creating a de facto split within the bloc. Analysts suggest this standoff could force the long-avoided emergence of a multi-speed Europe with 26 members proceeding without Hungary.

stories.title: Middle East war creates multi-faceted challenge for airlines
stories.summary: The ongoing war involving Iran has forced the closure of major Middle Eastern aviation hubs, including Dubai, Doha, and Abu Dhabi. Global air travel remains severely disrupted, with many passengers unable to reach their planned destinations.

stories.title: 'People are exhausted': No end in sight as Lebanon enters second month of war
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said Thursday there was no end in sight to the conflict that has displaced a million people over the past month. Israel has pledged to occupy parts of southern Lebanon as a "security zone" amid its ongoing war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

stories.title: Nuclear power: Why did France put the atom at the heart of its energy strategy?
stories.summary: France is one of the world's most nuclear-dependent countries, having placed atomic power at the center of its national energy strategy decades ago. Nuclear energy is viewed as both a key power source and a cornerstone of French national sovereignty, though debate continues over its environmental credentials.

stories.title: Senior military command investigates actions of Skelya regiment near Pokrovsk
stories.summary: Senior Ukrainian military command has launched an investigation into the actions of the 425th Separate Assault Regiment Skelya near Hryshyne in the Donetsk region. The inquiry concerns the conduct of the unit during operations in the Pokrovsk area.

stories.title: France ramps up Paris security after foiled attack on US bank
stories.summary: French authorities tightened security across Paris on Thursday after foiling an attack targeting a US bank amid heightened international tensions. Police increased their presence at sensitive sites, and major US banks including Citigroup instructed staff in Paris and Frankfurt to work from home as a precaution.

stories.title: Libya’s Haftar acquires combat drones despite UN embargo
stories.summary: Reuters reporting found that eastern Libyan military leader Khalifa Haftar has acquired what appear to be Chinese and Turkish combat drones. The acquisitions violate a long-standing UN arms embargo on Libya, which remains politically and militarily divided.

stories.title: A 19th-century drama hit with post-Oct. 7 fallout: Award-winning ‘Yentl’ goes to London
stories.summary: An acclaimed Australian adaptation of Isaac Bashevis Singer's "Yentl" opened in London, running through April 12, despite what its creators describe as international resistance to Jewish artistic works following October 7.

stories.title: UN experts call for investigation into Israel’s targeting of journalists in Lebanon
stories.summary: UN human rights experts condemned Israel's killing of journalists in Lebanon and called for an independent international investigation after three Lebanese journalists were targeted in strikes.

stories.title: Israel shifts strategy in Lebanon amid losses to Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israel is considering intensifying air strikes in Lebanon and adjusting ground tactics after suffering mounting losses in clashes with Hezbollah fighters.

stories.title: Nigeria: Bola Tinubu expected in Jos after deadly gun attack and mob violence
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu is expected to visit Jos in north-central Nigeria following a gun attack on a bar that killed over 30 people during the weekend. Mob violence subsequently erupted in the city on Wednesday.

stories.title: ST Engineering to serve as subcontractor for Kuwaiti navy vessels deal
stories.summary: Singapore-based ST Engineering will serve as a subcontractor on a naval vessels deal for the Kuwaiti navy. The contract is valued at approximately 600 million Singapore dollars, or about 467.6 million US dollars.

stories.title: Iranian tourist ban doesn’t align with the ‘Australian values’ Hedieh signed up to as a citizen
stories.summary: Australia's ban on Iranian tourist visas has drawn criticism from Iranian-Australians. Hedieh Jamshidian, a 32-year-old Iranian-Australian citizen, rushed to bring her mother from Tehran to Sydney before the restrictions took effect, as airstrikes continued in Iran.

stories.title: US banks in Paris ramp up security after cops thwart suspected Iran-linked attack
stories.summary: U.S. banks including Citigroup ramped up security in Paris and Frankfurt after French police detained four people connected to a suspected Iran-linked plot involving an explosive placed outside a Bank of America branch in Paris.

stories.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel after Trump threatens weeks of strikes
stories.summary: Iran launched missiles at Israel following US President Donald Trump's threat to bomb the Islamic republic for weeks. Trump's approval ratings have dropped amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: South Africa: Remembering Steven Gruzd - the Mind That Illuminated Complexity and the Friend Who Shared It
stories.summary: South African political scientist Steven Gruzd has passed away, leaving a noted gap in the country's community of political analysts and researchers.

stories.title: UEFA’s Euro 2032 warning the latest blow to Italy after World Cup exit
stories.summary: Days after failing to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, Italy received a warning from UEFA that its co-hosting of Euro 2032 could be in jeopardy.

stories.title: Kenya: Kindiki Urges Patience As New Gikomba Market Construction Set to Begin
stories.summary: Kenyan Deputy President Kithure Kindiki urged over 6,300 traders at New Gikomba Market in Nairobi to cooperate with relocation plans from the Nairobi River area, as construction of a new market is set to begin.

stories.title: Lithuanian parliament speaker delivers new aid package to Ukraine's military intelligence
stories.summary: Lithuanian parliament speaker Juozas Olekas delivered a new aid package to Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) under the Defense Ministry. The assistance is part of Lithuania's ongoing military support to Ukraine.

stories.title: Fury across Middle East over Israel's 'racist' death penalty law
stories.summary: Widespread protests erupted across Syria and several Arab states issued condemnations of an Israeli law widely described as a racist death penalty measure targeting Palestinians.

stories.title: Burkina Faso military, allies committing ‘horrific’ civilian abuses: HRW
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reports that Burkina Faso's military and allied armed groups have killed more than 1,800 civilians since 2023, describing the abuses as horrific.

stories.title: Gaza baby tortured by Israel traumatised, mother tells New Arab
stories.summary: The mother of Jawad Abu Nasser, a baby released from Israeli detention, told The New Arab that her son showed clear signs of torture and was left traumatized by the experience.

stories.title: Iran's focus on survival means same regime still firmly in place
stories.summary: BBC Persian editor Amir Azimi reports that Tehran's leadership remains firmly in power despite U.S. President Trump's claims of pursuing regime change, with the Iranian government demonstrating resilience under pressure.

stories.title: Karachi authorities declare emergency as westerly wave brings rainfall to city, nearby areas
stories.summary: Karachi authorities declared an emergency as a westerly weather system brought rainfall across the city, affecting areas including Quaidabad, Malir, Gulistan-i-Jauhar, Saddar, Clifton, and Keamari.

stories.title: How attacks on a Christian town test Syria's postwar cohesion
stories.summary: Attacks in the Christian town of Al-Suqaylabiyah in Syria highlight how local grievances can escalate into violence amid weak security and the absence of transitional justice mechanisms.

stories.title: Russia considers tightening telecom licensing rules, critics say the move would reduce competition and raise prices
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry is in preliminary discussions with industry players about tightening licensing rules for telecom operators. Critics warn the proposed changes could reduce competition and drive up consumer prices.

stories.title: Oil prices jump over 7% after Trump vows to continue strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged more than 7 percent after President Trump pledged to continue military strikes on Iran, with markets fearing the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed to shipping.

stories.title: Dust storm turns Israel’s skies gray on Passover, drives up pollution
stories.summary: A dust storm swept across Israel during Passover, turning skies gray and significantly increasing air pollution levels. The Environmental Protection Ministry warned vulnerable populations to limit outdoor physical activity.

stories.title: 'Be serious... don't speak every day': Macron criticises Trump approach to Iran war
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron publicly criticized U.S. President Donald Trump's approach to the war on Iran, calling his sometimes contradictory daily statements unhelpful and urging a more serious diplomatic posture.

stories.title: 'The scale of sexual violence is horrific': MSF head of mission Amande Bazerolle
stories.summary: A new Médecins Sans Frontières report documents widespread sexual violence in Sudan's Darfur region as the country's civil war nears its fourth anniversary. Nearly 3,400 survivors of sexual violence sought care at MSF facilities across northern and southern Darfur in 2024 and 2025, with 97 percent being women and girls.

stories.title: Beeline CEO proposes limiting mobile internet restrictions to subscribers flagged as suspicious
stories.summary: Vimpelcom CEO Sergei Anokhin proposed at the Telecom 2026 conference that mobile internet restrictions in Russia should target only subscribers flagged as suspicious, rather than applying broadly to all users. The company operates under the Beeline brand.

stories.title: Ukraine Renewing Drone Strikes on TurkStream Facilities, Gazprom Says
stories.summary: Gazprom reported that Ukraine renewed drone strikes on TurkStream gas pipeline infrastructure, with three Ukrainian drones targeting a compressor station in Russia's southern Krasnodar region overnight.

stories.title: ICC votes to advance disciplinary measures against prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual assault claims
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court's member states voted to advance disciplinary measures against prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual assault allegations. The vote saw 15 in favor, four against, and two abstentions.

stories.title: How Trump’s plan to take Iran’s Kharg Island could come unhinged
stories.summary: Analysts warned that President Trump's threat to seize Iran's Kharg Island, which handles about 90 percent of Iran's crude exports, poses significant military risks. The island sits close to Iranian missile and drone installations on the mainland and approximately 660 kilometers from the fortified Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Outsource AI Risk to the Right People
stories.summary: An analysis drawing on nuclear history argues that safety-critical decisions in artificial intelligence development benefit from including skeptical voices. The piece emphasizes the importance of involving independent, critical perspectives when assessing and managing AI risks.

stories.title: UK-led coalition of 40 countries vows action on Hormuz Strait gridlock
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer convened a coalition of 40 countries to discuss non-military solutions to the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route.

stories.title: Power Division seeks World Bank support for new power tariff structure for industrial consumers
stories.summary: Pakistan's Power Division is developing a new electricity tariff structure for industrial consumers to shift usage to daytime hours. Federal Minister Sardar Awais Ahmed Leghari discussed the plan with the World Bank Country Director.

stories.title: Trump threatens to halt arms supplies to Ukraine to pressure Europe on Hormuz Strait – FT
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened to stop arms supplies to Ukraine as leverage to pressure European allies into joining a coalition to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Financial Times.

stories.title: Iran executes man allegedly tied to attack on military site during mass protests
stories.summary: Iran executed Amirhossein Hatami, a man allegedly connected to an attack on a military site during mass anti-government protests. He was among 11 men reported to be at imminent risk of execution and who had allegedly been subjected to torture in detention.

stories.title: Pakistan to continue with Iran-US mediation despite ‘obstacles’
stories.summary: Pakistan announced it will continue efforts to mediate between Iran and the United States despite obstacles, following President Trump's threat to bomb Iran "back to the Stone Age."

stories.title: Syria restricts authority of humanitarian organisations
stories.summary: Syria's government issued a decision requiring all memoranda of understanding and agreements with international humanitarian organizations to receive prior approval from the Syrian foreign ministry.

stories.title: Iran war: How long can Tehran's asymmetric strategy hold?
stories.summary: After years of sanctions and weeks of U.S.-Israeli bombing, Iran's regime has been shaken but retains the capacity to threaten the broader Middle East region. Analysts are assessing how long Tehran can sustain its asymmetric military strategy.

stories.title: Italy arrests German-Indian ‘guru’ on child abuse allegations
stories.summary: Italian police arrested a man of German-Indian origin in Sicily on suspicion of aiding and abetting child abuse. The suspect allegedly led an isolated community of 15 people, including two children aged 7 and 11, living in a forest near Cefalù. The children were reportedly unvaccinated and not attending school.

stories.title: Chinese AI giants pivot toward proprietary models to drive revenue, performance
stories.summary: Chinese AI companies including Alibaba Cloud and Zhipu AI have chosen not to open-source some of their latest artificial intelligence models, seeking to capture revenue through official channels. The trend reflects the growing size of the most powerful models, making them increasingly difficult to run on local hardware.

stories.title: Passover, war and faith: Moral clarity matters in Israel’s defense - opinion
stories.summary: A rabbinic commentator responded to Pope Francis's remarks on the conflict, arguing that Jewish ethical tradition demands moral clarity and recognizes the obligation of self-defense. The commentary was published as Passover began amid Israel's ongoing military operations.

stories.title: Freedom under fire: What Passover means in a time of war - comment
stories.summary: As Passover begins during wartime, Jewish communities are reflecting on the holiday's themes of freedom through the lens of ongoing conflict. The observance takes on added meaning as concerns about safety and survival dominate.

stories.title: ‘Bomb back to the Stone Age’: US history of threats and carpet bombing
stories.summary: Analysts note that carpet bombing campaigns constitute war crimes under international law, contextualizing recent U.S. threats against Iran within a broader history of American aerial bombardment tactics.

stories.title: What Trump’s speech says about his war on Iran | Analysis
stories.summary: An analysis of President Trump's national address on the Iran war notes it largely restated previous claims while underscoring his limited options in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Looking for Easter holiday inspiration? Here’s what’s happening in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong begins a five-day long weekend for Easter and the Ching Ming Festival on Friday. Authorities expect heavy inbound and outbound travel during the holiday period. Events such as a coffee festival are among public activities listed for those remaining in the city.

stories.title: With Telegram blocked, Russians turn to cat feeders, classifieds, and robot vacuum cleaners to stay connected
stories.summary: With Russia's Roskomnadzor continuing to block Telegram, Russian users have turned to unconventional workarounds including online games, office tools, cat feeders, classifieds platforms, and robot vacuum cleaners to communicate. Many are avoiding the state-backed messaging app Max.

stories.title: Exclusive: Greek ships secretly supplying Israel with oil and military cargo
stories.summary: Greek shipping companies have been covertly transporting oil and military cargo to Israel, according to an investigation. Shadow ships reportedly disable tracking signals and file false destinations, routing supplies through Turkey to avoid detection.

stories.title: Partisans scout boom barrier defenses in Sevastopol Bay
stories.summary: Partisan operatives conducted reconnaissance of boom barrier defense systems and several piers in Sevastopol Bay, the Russian-controlled naval base in occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Us-Israel war on Iran deepens Gaza's transportation crisis
stories.summary: The US-Israeli military campaign against Iran is worsening Gaza's transportation crisis, with effects from the broader conflict increasingly felt across the besieged Palestinian enclave.

stories.title: France’s Macron says military operation to ‘liberate’ Strait of Hormuz ‘unrealistic’
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said during a visit to South Korea that a military operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is "unrealistic." He criticized the inconsistency of US positions on the Iran war and NATO. Macron stated that a forceful approach was never France's chosen option.

stories.title: Russian court fines man for threatening text message sent to Belarusian security official during 2020 protests
stories.summary: A court in Russia's Smolensk region fined a Russian man for sending a threatening text message to a Belarusian security official during the 2020 protests in Belarus. The case was announced by Belarus's Prosecutor General's Office.

stories.title: Burundi arsenal blasts in Bujumbura kill 13 civilians
stories.summary: Burundi's army confirmed that 13 civilians were killed and 57 others wounded after explosions at a military arsenal in Bujumbura earlier this week. Three soldiers were also reported among the injured.

stories.title: Russians intensify operations in Kharkiv and Sumy regions while simultaneously actively attacking Lyman sector
stories.summary: Russian forces have intensified military operations across the Kharkiv and Sumy regions as well as the strategically significant Lyman sector. Despite the increased pressure on multiple fronts, no territorial advances have been reported.

stories.title: Burkina Army, jihadists killed more than 1,800 civilians since 2023: Human Rights Watch
stories.summary: A Human Rights Watch report found that Burkina Faso's military under Captain Ibrahim Traore and jihadist groups have killed more than 1,800 civilians since 2023, calling for an impartial investigation into military abuses.

stories.title: UAE and Bahrain only Middle East states joining UK coalition to pressure Iran over Hormuz
stories.summary: The UAE and Bahrain are the only Middle Eastern states joining a UK-led coalition aimed at pressuring Iran over the Strait of Hormuz. Key regional players including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey declined to participate in the UK's online summit.

stories.title: Oil surges, stocks fall as Trump vows more Iran attacks
stories.summary: Oil prices surged toward $110 per barrel after President Trump escalated threats of further military action against Iran. Global stock markets fell amid rising fears of inflation and prolonged conflict.

stories.title: Malaysia to roll out work-from-home policy to curb fuel use
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced a new work-from-home policy for government ministries, agencies, and state-linked companies starting April 15. The policy aims to reduce fuel consumption and ensure energy supply sustainability amid global disruptions.

stories.title: Israeli army entrenching Gaza 'Yellow Line' into new border
stories.summary: The Israeli military has been solidifying the so-called Yellow Line in Gaza by establishing permanent military outposts. After months of expanding the boundary, the line is being entrenched as what appears to be a new de facto border within the enclave.

stories.title: PSX tumbles over 4,000 points during intraday trade as Trump speech sinks hopes for quick end to war
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index dropped over 4,000 points during intraday trading after President Trump's address dashed investor hopes for a quick resolution to the war on Iran. The benchmark fell approximately 2.62 percent.

stories.title: Rosatom Prepares Final Staff Evacuation From Bushehr Nuclear Plant
stories.summary: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom is preparing a final staff evacuation from the Bushehr nuclear plant in Iran. Approximately 50 volunteers will remain at the facility to keep it operational.

stories.title: How East Asia is being quietly reordered by the US war on Iran
stories.summary: Analysts say the US war on Iran is reshaping the strategic order in East Asia beyond its impact on oil markets. A month into the conflict, Washington maintains it expects to achieve objectives within weeks, but US and Iranian negotiating positions remain far apart. The war's effects on regional hierarchy and alliances are becoming increasingly significant.

stories.title: Iconic 19th Century painting sets Indian art record with $17.9m sale
stories.summary: Raja Ravi Varma's 19th-century painting "Yashoda and Krishna" sold for $17.9 million, setting a new record for Indian art. The sale surpassed the previous record held by a work by M.F. Husain.

stories.title: Iran army chief orders close monitoring of US, Israeli movements ahead of potential invasion
stories.summary: Iran's Armed Forces chief Amir Hatami ordered commanders to closely monitor US and Israeli military movements, warning of preparations to counter any potential ground invasion. The directive was issued during a meeting with senior military leaders, as reported by Iran's IRNA news agency.

stories.title: Five killed in Ukraine as downed Russian Shahed drones detonate days after impact
stories.summary: In recent days, five people have been killed in Ukraine due to delayed detonations of Russian drones that survived their fall.

stories.title: Hopes dim for swift end to Iran war after Trump speech, oil prices surge anew
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump offered no concrete timeline for ending the war in Iran during a speech that dimmed hopes for a swift conclusion to the conflict. Oil prices surged again amid continued global energy supply disruption.

stories.title: 50% profit tax, no dividends, no new licenses—Eastern European fintechs are buying Ukrainian banks anyway
stories.summary: Eastern European fintech companies are purchasing Ukrainian banks despite wartime conditions including a 50% profit tax, dividend restrictions, and a freeze on new licenses. The firms are betting on Ukraine's post-war reconstruction potential.

stories.title: Russia claims full capture of Luhansk Oblast for the third time — Ukraine’s 3rd Assault Brigade notes it’s still holding the line there
stories.summary: Russia claimed for the third time to have fully captured Luhansk Oblast, but Ukraine's 3rd Assault Brigade says it still holds positions there. The ISW confirmed Ukrainian forces control settlements including Nadiya and Novoyehorivka, comprising 0.16% of the oblast.

stories.title: Eight Muslim nations condemn Israel's 'dangerous' new death penalty law
stories.summary: Eight Muslim-majority nations — Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE — condemned Israel's new death penalty law as dangerous. They urged restraint from measures that could further inflame tensions in the region.

stories.title: Russia offers to help resolve Iran conflict, Kremlin says
stories.summary: The Kremlin said Russia is ready to help resolve the conflict involving Iran, with President Vladimir Putin maintaining contact with regional leaders. Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Moscow remains diplomatically engaged and prepared to assist de-escalation efforts.

stories.title: Sweden to send Tridon anti-air cannon to Ukraine to gain valuable experience for its drone defense
