stories.title: US messages via Witkoff and intermediaries are not negotiations: Araghchi
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that message exchanges with Washington via U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and intermediaries are ongoing but do not constitute formal negotiations. Araghchi said there is no trust between the two sides.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran president asked for ceasefire ahead of address
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed that Iran's president requested a ceasefire, but linked any potential deal to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz for global shipping. The claim was made ahead of a planned presidential address.

stories.title: Houthis claim third attack on Israel as five killed in Beirut
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed a third attack on Israel, while Iranian missile fire reportedly injured 14 people in Israel according to Israeli medics. Separately, five people were killed in Beirut.

stories.title: War update: 171 combat engagements on front line over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces recorded 171 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line over the past day.

stories.title: A Ribbon For Israelis and a Noose for Palestinians
stories.summary: A political cartoon by Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj was published in The New Arab, depicting contrasting symbols for Israelis and Palestinians.

stories.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Crimea, killing all 29 on board
stories.summary: A Russian An-26 military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board, including six crew members and 23 passengers. Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Hong Kong retail sales jump nearly 12% in first 2 months of year
stories.summary: Hong Kong's retail sales rose nearly 12 percent in the first two months of 2026 compared to a year earlier, reaching a combined HK$72.3 billion. Authorities attributed the growth to the local economic expansion, a surge in tourism, and the Chinese New Year holiday.

stories.title: Malaysia ships not paying any toll to pass Strait of Hormuz, government says
stories.summary: Malaysia's government confirmed that its ships waiting to transit the Strait of Hormuz have been allowed to pass without paying any tolls to Iran. Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said reports of toll payments were a misunderstanding.

stories.title: India begins world’s largest population census
stories.summary: India launched its latest population census, deploying more than three million officials to conduct the yearlong count. It is described as the world's largest census exercise.

stories.title: ‘Gerrymandering’ in India’s Assam cuts Muslim representation before vote
stories.summary: Constituency boundary changes in India's Assam state have reduced Muslim-majority seats from approximately 35 to about 20 out of 126 total constituencies ahead of upcoming elections, prompting accusations of gerrymandering.

stories.title: Cubans celebrate arrival of Russian oil tanker amid US energy blockade
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker carrying 730,000 barrels of oil docked at the Cuban port of Matanzas, marking the first oil delivery to the island in three months amid a US energy blockade. Cubans celebrated the arrival.

stories.title: Malaysia denies Anwar delayed disclosure of probe into MACC chief, threatens legal action
stories.summary: Malaysia's government denied allegations that Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim sought to delay disclosure of an investigation into the chief of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission. The government said it would take legal action over the news report making the claim.

stories.title: Antarctica, eco-sail expedition vessels will have a hybrid sail propulsion system
stories.summary: Oceanwide Expeditions, an Arctic and Antarctic cruise operator, announced plans to build two 146-passenger eco-sail expedition vessels. The ships will feature a hybrid sail propulsion system designed to reduce fuel consumption and lower emissions.

stories.title: Macron hails France-Japan ties after talks in Tokyo with PM Takaichi
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron met Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo during a three-day visit that includes a meeting with Japan's emperor. The two leaders pledged to work together to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz amid the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Szijjártó told Russia’s deputy minister he’d removed 72 entities from EU sanctions — then asked Moscow to write his arguments for removing more
stories.summary: Leaked transcripts of a call between Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó and Russia's deputy energy minister revealed that Szijjártó informed Moscow he had removed 72 entities from EU sanctions. He also reportedly asked the Kremlin to draft justifications for further delistings to support Hungary's EU lobbying.

stories.title: Iranian missile hits oil tanker in Qatar, defence ministry says
stories.summary: Qatar's defense ministry reported that three cruise missiles were launched from Iran toward the country. Two were intercepted, while a third struck an oil tanker leased to Qatar Energy; all 21 crew members were evacuated without casualties.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih, other communities in region almost 20 times over past day, leaving two people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 20 attacks on four districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, targeting areas including Dnipro and Kryvyi Rih with drones and artillery. Two people were injured.

stories.title: Haiti gangs keep up attacks in breadbasket region after massacre
stories.summary: Armed gangs launched further attacks in Haiti's Artibonite region on Tuesday, days after a weekend assault in Jean-Denis that killed approximately 70 people according to human rights groups. The Artibonite region is considered Haiti's agricultural breadbasket.

stories.title: Oil price falls and markets rally after Trump says Iran war over in ‘two to three weeks’
stories.summary: Oil prices fell sharply after President Donald Trump said the Iran war could end within two to three weeks. Brent crude dropped more than 15% to $99.78 per barrel, while stock markets rallied across Asia.

stories.title: Aleema asks PTI supporters to take to streets for Imran’s release
stories.summary: Aleema Khan, sister of imprisoned PTI chief Imran Khan, called on party supporters to hold street protests demanding the release of the former Pakistani prime minister, citing his health issues and the family's frustration with the courts.

stories.title: Mainland China, Hong Kong premium office supply to peak as demand lags, Cushman says
stories.summary: Premium office supply across 21 major cities in mainland China and Hong Kong is projected to peak this year, according to Cushman & Wakefield. Demand continues to lag due to economic slowdown and global uncertainties, with total inventory reaching 99.2 million square metres at end of 2025.

stories.title: The surge of global business interest in China’s ‘harbour of stability’
stories.summary: At the China Development Forum, Premier Li Qiang positioned China as a "harbour of stability" amid global war and uncertainty, attracting CEOs from companies including Siemens, Nestlé, and Apple. The messaging reflects growing international business interest in China as a reliable economic partner.

stories.title: War on Iran: Three key takeaways from Araghchi’s interview with Al Jazeera
stories.summary: In an exclusive Al Jazeera interview, Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi confirmed direct talks with U.S. envoy Witkoff but denied these constituted formal negotiations, reiterating a lack of trust between Tehran and Washington.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu's Resignation Deadline Triggers Wave of Exits Ahead of 2027 Elections
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu's cabinet resignation deadline triggered a wave of ministerial departures ahead of the 2027 general elections. Attention is now shifting to how the exits will reshape the federal cabinet and key state-level contests.

stories.title: Fourteen wounded in central Israel after Iran launches cluster munitions
stories.summary: Iran launched cluster munitions at central Israel, wounding fourteen people. One impact site was reported near the US Embassy branch in Tel Aviv, according to Israel's Channel 12 News.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Beat Jamaica, Qualify for First World Cup Since 1974
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo defeated Jamaica 1-0 in extra time to qualify for their first FIFA World Cup since 1974. Defender Axel Tuanzebe scored the decisive goal from close range.

stories.title: English mayor resigns after boosting claim Jewish ambulance arson was ‘false flag’
stories.summary: The mayor of Bath, England, Bharat Pankhania, resigned after promoting claims that the arson of four Hatzola Jewish ambulance vehicles in London was a "false flag" operation. Police are treating the attack as an antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: Debris from Russian drone damages apartment building in Lutsk, strike on industrial facility reported
stories.summary: In the western Ukrainian city of Lutsk, debris from a Russian drone damaged an apartment building. A separate strike hit an industrial facility in the area.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes on Beirut area kill seven
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs and the nearby Jnah area killed at least seven people and wounded 21 others on Wednesday.

stories.title: Hong Kong airport named world’s best at Global Travel Awards 2026
stories.summary: Hong Kong International Airport was named the world's best airport at the Global Travel Awards 2026, organized by the UK-based International Media & News Group. The accolades also recognized the airport's security standards and facilities based on votes from 2.5 million travelers.

stories.title: Lights out, bills up as summer approaches
stories.summary: Pakistan's government is finalizing a plan for scheduled power outages, compulsory conservation measures, and higher electricity tariffs ahead of summer, when peak demand is expected to reach 27–28 GW. The measures stem from disrupted LNG supplies and constrained Thar coal output linked to the broader energy crisis caused by the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Say bye-bye to bitter herbs: Israeli researchers’ work aims to pass over tart tastes
stories.summary: Researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem compiled a compendium of 2,200 bitter molecules and studied the TAS2R14 bitter receptor. Their work aims to reduce bitter tastes in medicine and potentially treat lung diseases.

stories.title: China’s AI Is Spreading Fast. Here’s How to Stop the Security Risks
stories.summary: Chinese AI models surged from one percent of global AI workloads in late 2024 to 30 percent by end of 2025. Alibaba's Qwen family has exceeded 700 million downloads, while labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax are expanding in the global open-source AI marketplace, raising security concerns.

stories.title: China’s AI Is Spreading Fast. Here’s How to Stop the Security Risks
stories.summary: Chinese AI models surged from one percent of global AI workloads in late 2024 to 30 percent by end of 2025, with Alibaba's Qwen family reaching over 700 million downloads. An analysis examines security risks posed by the rapid global spread of Chinese open-source AI systems from labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax.

stories.title: China’s AI Is Spreading Fast. Here’s How to Stop the Security Risks
stories.summary: Chinese AI models surged from one percent of global AI workloads in late 2024 to 30 percent by the end of 2025. Alibaba's Qwen family has exceeded 700 million downloads, becoming the world's largest open-source AI provider, alongside labs such as DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax.

stories.title: As US weighs putting troops in Iran, realities on ground keep Israeli boots closer to home
stories.summary: Experts noted that while debate continues in the U.S. about deploying American troops to Iran, Israel's military role has been pivotal in setting the stage for potential U.S. ground operations, even as Israeli soldiers remain closer to home.

stories.title: UAE said pushing for military op to reopen Strait of Hormuz, is willing to take part
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE is pushing for a military operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and is willing to participate. Abu Dhabi reportedly wants the U.S. to occupy Iranian-held islands in the waterway and is seeking a UN Security Council resolution authorizing force.

stories.title: Anthony Albanese addresses the nation on the Middle East crisis – read the speech in full
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese delivered a national address on the Middle East crisis, warning that the months ahead 'may not be easy.' He urged Australians to support one another, particularly those in rural areas and critical industries.

stories.title: How US’ ‘stupid war’ with Iran torched fuel price stability in America
stories.summary: Surging fuel prices from the Iran war are hitting American consumers hard, with drivers in the Washington, D.C., suburbs confronting sharply higher costs at the pump. The domestic economic impact stems from the U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran and the resulting disruption to global energy markets.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,060 troops, three MLR systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost approximately 1,060 troops killed or wounded in a single 24-hour period, bringing estimated total Russian casualties since February 2022 to roughly 1,298,730.

stories.title: EU condemns Israel’s death penalty law ‘close to apartheid’
stories.summary: The European Union condemned Israel's passage of a death penalty bill applicable to Palestinians convicted of deadly terror attacks but not to Israelis. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the measure a step closer to apartheid.

stories.title: Israeli police inspect damage on the road after missile impact
stories.summary: Israeli police inspected damage in Tel Aviv after a missile struck the city, causing destruction on a roadway. The strike occurred amid ongoing exchanges of fire between Iran and Israel.

stories.title: Iran attacks cause fire in Kuwait, Bahrain; kill man in UAE
stories.summary: Shrapnel from an intercepted Iranian drone killed a Bangladeshi national in Fujairah, UAE. Attacks also caused fires in Kuwait and Bahrain as Iranian strikes affected multiple Gulf states.

stories.title: Nigeria: How Corruption, Overcrowding, Weak Justice Systems Turn Nigerian Prisons Into 'Human Warehouses' - - Report
stories.summary: A report highlighted that Nigerian prisons suffer from severe overcrowding, corruption, and weak justice systems. Officials described custodial centers as "human warehouses," with some facilities exceeding capacity by up to 500%.

stories.title: Nigeria: Enugu On High Alert Over Rabies Outbreak
stories.summary: Health authorities in Enugu, Nigeria, issued an alert over a rabies outbreak, urging all dog owners to vaccinate their pets immediately and to confine animals to prevent free roaming.

stories.title: Nigeria: Misdiagnosed As Malaria - the Hidden Cost of Delayed Lassa Fever Detection in Nigeria
stories.summary: Nigeria is experiencing a severe Lassa fever season, with the WHO warning that clinical symptoms alone are insufficient for diagnosis due to overlap with other diseases such as malaria. Laboratory testing is required to confirm cases.

stories.title: DawnMedia, CVF-V20 partner to accelerate climate investment
stories.summary: The Climate Vulnerable Forum's CVF-V20 Secretariat and DawnMedia's Breathe Pakistan initiative signed an MoU to collaborate on climate action, investment mobilization, and global advocacy efforts in Pakistan.

stories.title: Nigeria: Alkali Resigns As Transport Minister, Eyes Governorship Seat
stories.summary: Nigerian Transport Minister Alkali resigned from his cabinet position to pursue a governorship seat. In his resignation letter, he thanked President Bola Tinubu for the opportunity to serve.

stories.title: Kenya: MPs Push for National Cancer Dialogue As Kenya Faces Rising Death Toll
stories.summary: Kenyan Members of Parliament resolved to engage Ministry of Health officials and other stakeholders to address rising cancer-related deaths in the country through a proposed national cancer dialogue.

stories.title: Four Palestinians said wounded by settler assailants in West Bank village of Tayasir
stories.summary: Four Palestinians were reportedly wounded by settler assailants in the West Bank village of Tayasir. Three of the injured are cousins of Abdullah Daraghmeh, a 75-year-old who was beaten by settlers the previous week. Israeli authorities have not commented.

stories.title: Israel’s war-time injuries rise to 6,286, health ministry says
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported 104 new war-related injuries over the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of wartime injuries to 6,286. Approximately 100 people remain hospitalized.

stories.title: 109 illegal migrants from Pakistan died or went missing last year: International Organisation for Migration
stories.summary: The International Organisation for Migration reported that 109 Pakistani migrants died or went missing in 2025 while attempting illegal border crossings, out of at least 2,722 deaths recorded in the Asia-Pacific region.

stories.title: Russians launch 975 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, leaving four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 975 strikes on 42 settlements across Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region in one day. Four people were wounded in the Zaporizhzhia and Polohy districts.

stories.title: At least seven killed in Israeli strikes in Beirut area, Lebanon says
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in the Beirut area killed at least seven people, according to Lebanese authorities. Israel's military said the strikes targeted a senior Hezbollah commander and another senior member of the organization.

stories.title: The Most Important Deterrent That NATO Needs Is Creativity
stories.summary: An analysis argues that NATO's most critical need is fostering human creativity and innovative mindsets rather than focusing solely on technology like drones, hypersonic missiles, or AI. The piece contends that innovation is a transferable skill that the alliance must cultivate more rapidly across its defense organizations.

stories.title: The Most Important Deterrent That NATO Needs Is Creativity
stories.summary: An analysis argues that NATO's most critical need is fostering human creativity rather than relying solely on advanced technology like drones, hypersonic missiles, or AI. The article contends that innovation as a transferable skill is undervalued within defence organizations and difficult to scale.

stories.title: China’s electric cars and Iran war, BYD’s profit run ends: 7 EV reads
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and associated oil price surges could accelerate global adoption of electric vehicles, potentially widening China's lead in the EV sector. Meanwhile, BYD's profit streak has ended amid shifting market conditions.

stories.title: Buy jet fuel from US or get your own, Trump rails against allies
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump pressured allies to purchase American jet fuel amid the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, while Iranian President Pezeshkian expressed willingness to end the conflict with guarantees. Iranian missiles injured nine in Tel Aviv.

stories.title: Australia and Japan face jet fuel supply crunch as China cuts exports
stories.summary: China has sharply reduced jet fuel exports, cutting shipments nearly 40 percent month-on-month in March amid the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Australia and Japan, major importers of Chinese jet fuel, are scrambling to find alternative suppliers as they face a supply crunch.

stories.title: Confident of air supremacy, US sends B-52 bombers over Iran
stories.summary: The United States sent B-52 bombers over Iran, expressing confidence in its air supremacy over the country. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated the U.S. was "closer than ever before to winning" the conflict.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks Kryvyi Rih, leaving one injured
stories.summary: A Russian Shahed-type drone struck the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, injuring one person and starting a fire in the city.

stories.title: China is trying to play peacemaker in the Iran war - will it work?
stories.summary: China is stepping into a diplomatic role in the Iran conflict after maintaining a muted official response. Analysts are questioning Beijing's motivations and whether its peacemaking efforts can succeed.

stories.title: Systematically crushing Iran, forging alliances with important countries in West Asia: Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel is systematically targeting Iran's capabilities and predicted the Iranian regime will eventually fall. He emphasized that Israel is forging new alliances with countries in West Asia to counter what he described as a shared threat from Tehran.

stories.title: The Arsenal as the Battlefield: The War on Iran and the Return of Counter-Industrial Targeting
stories.summary: The U.S. war against Iran has reignited debates about counter-industrial targeting strategy and defense industrial capacity. Iran's ability to launch repeated salvos of cheap attack drones previews challenges Washington could face in a potential conflict with China over the proliferation of low-cost precision weapons.

stories.title: The Arsenal as the Battlefield: The War on Iran and the Return of Counter-Industrial Targeting
stories.summary: The US war against Iran has reignited debate over counter-industrial targeting strategy and defence industrial capacity. Tehran's ability to launch repeated salvos of inexpensive attack drones previews challenges Washington could face in a potential conflict with China.

stories.title: Death penalty 'a deep stain on the law books of the state of Israel'
stories.summary: Former Israeli hostage negotiator Gershon Baskin criticized the Knesset's newly passed death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of terror charges. He argued the legislation is part of a broader shift in Israel toward exclusionary nationalism and legal inequality.

stories.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Crimea, 29 killed, defence ministry says
stories.summary: A Russian An-26 military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board. Russia's defense ministry confirmed that 23 passengers and six crew members died in the crash.

stories.title: Shipping lines, traders agree on fair pricing, transparency
stories.summary: A committee under Pakistan's Ministry of Maritime Affairs brokered an agreement between shipping lines and traders on fair pricing, advance cost disclosure, and limiting cargo diversions to address complaints about non-transparent shipping practices.

stories.title: Speculation pushes Iranian rial fourfold against rupee
stories.summary: The Iranian rial surged nearly fourfold against the Pakistani rupee during the ongoing war, rising from Rs2,500 to Rs10,000 per 10 million rials, driven by speculative buying and increased cross-border trade demand.

stories.title: Iranian missile attack injures six in central Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile attack on central Israel wounded six people, including an 11-year-old girl and a 13-year-old boy. Impact sites were reported in Bnei Brak, Holon, and Petah Tikva, with damage to an apartment building.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 33 of US-Israel attacks?
stories.summary: On day 33 of U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran, President Trump suggested the U.S. could exit the war within two to three weeks without a deal. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi expressed no faith in ongoing talks.

stories.title: Ganfeng Lithium forecasts strong battery demand amid China-US rivalry in renewable energy
stories.summary: China's Ganfeng Lithium, the world's largest lithium metal producer, forecast explosive growth in the global energy storage market in 2026. Executives cited rising lithium prices and strong demand for renewable energy infrastructure driven by global decarbonization efforts.

stories.title: Third US aircraft carrier heads to Middle East as Iran war continues
stories.summary: A third U.S. aircraft carrier is being deployed to the Middle East as the war in Iran continues. The carrier group is expected to take approximately three weeks to arrive in the region.

stories.title: American journalist Shelly Kittleson kidnapped in Baghdad, US says
stories.summary: American freelance journalist Shelly Kittleson was kidnapped in Baghdad by a suspected Iraqi armed group with ties to Kataib Hezbollah. The US State Department said it was working to secure her release amid deteriorating regional security.

stories.title: Sudan: More Than 9 Million People Displaced in Darfur
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that more than 9 million people remain internally displaced in Sudan, with displacement continuing in Darfur, Kordofan, and Blue Nile states. Approximately 3.8 million people have begun returning home.

stories.title: Occupation administration of Yalta destroys city's historical and cultural heritage – National Resistance Center
stories.summary: According to Ukraine's National Resistance Center, Russian occupation authorities in Yalta, Crimea, are demolishing historical and cultural landmarks and replacing them with closed hotel complexes for Russian elites.

stories.title: Israeli Air Force chases drone for 20 minutes, local media reports
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force pursued a drone over northern Israel for approximately 20 minutes, triggering air raid sirens in towns including Kiryat Shmona, Safed, and surrounding communities. Interception efforts were underway.

stories.title: ‘Blatantly racist’: Death penalty law among 'worst legislation' in Israeli parliamentary history
stories.summary: Bentzi Sykora, Policy Director at the Zulat Institute for Equality and Human Rights, called Israel's new death penalty legislation 'blatantly racist' and among the worst in Israeli parliamentary history. He said the law poses a fundamental challenge to equality before the law and democratic safeguards.

stories.title: Video: Israeli lawmaker condemns death penalty bill as 'genocide law'
stories.summary: Israeli Knesset member Ofer Cassif condemned a newly approved death penalty bill for Palestinian detainees, calling it discriminatory and arguing it was designed to exclude Jewish Israelis from its application.

stories.title: South Sudan: 74 Miners Killed in South Sudan
stories.summary: At least 74 mine workers were killed by gunmen in South Sudan's mineral-rich Jebel Iraq area near Juba. Government and opposition officials have traded accusations over responsibility for the attack.

stories.title: Some Hong Kong taxi drivers unprepared as new e-payments rule takes effect
stories.summary: Hong Kong's new rule mandating electronic payment options in all taxis took effect on Wednesday, but some drivers had not yet installed the required systems. The regulation requires drivers to offer at least a QR code option and one alternative e-payment method.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel will continue to ‘crush Iran's terror regime’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared that Israel will continue its military campaign against Iran, vowing to "crush Iran's terror regime" as operations against Tehran persist.

stories.title: How Israel dodged Hormuz energy crisis while others reel from the blow
stories.summary: Despite the Strait of Hormuz disruption caused by Iran during the ongoing conflict, Israel has remained largely insulated from the energy crisis affecting economies across Asia, Europe, and the United States. Israel's energy infrastructure and planning have allowed it to avoid the surging oil and gas prices hitting other nations.

stories.title: Russian tanker begins unloading oil in Cuba – Reuters
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker began unloading oil at Cuba's Matanzas terminal, marking the first major energy shipment to the island since restrictions were imposed under U.S. President Donald Trump's administration.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A Bangladeshi national was killed by falling shrapnel after a drone interception in the UAE. Separately, a tanker off Qatar was struck by two projectiles, and Dubai-based Emirates airline reported disruptions amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Canada extends its temporary migration program for Ukrainians
stories.summary: Canada extended its Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET) program, which permits Ukrainians to live and work in Canada as the war continues.

stories.title: As US pursues 'maximalist demands', Iran relies on four decades of asymmetric warfare
stories.summary: Ali Vaez of the International Crisis Group examined the US-Israel-Iran confrontation, noting that military escalation risks systemic regional and global consequences. He observed that Iran continues to leverage asymmetric warfare capabilities developed over four decades despite significant internal and external pressure.

stories.title: South Africans react as fuel prices surge despite tax relief
stories.summary: South Africa reduced its general fuel levy by three rand per litre to offset the impact of rising global oil prices linked to the Iran conflict. However, the measure has done little to counter one of the steepest pump price increases on record.

stories.title: US strips citizenship from couple in trade theft case, part of Trump immigration push
stories.summary: The Trump administration revoked the U.S. citizenship of a California couple who emigrated from China after they pleaded guilty to stealing trade secrets, as part of a broader immigration enforcement push.

stories.title: How Canada's double standards on Iran put the world at risk
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney faced criticism for failing to take a stand against the US-Israeli war on Iran, despite earlier rhetoric at Davos about international norms and multilateralism.

stories.title: Trump says US could end war in Iran in two to three weeks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told reporters the U.S. could end the war in Iran within two to three weeks, saying American forces would be "leaving very soon."

stories.title: Empty petrol stations and volatile prices: Australia’s fuel crisis in charts
stories.summary: Hundreds of service stations across Australia have run dry as Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts oil shipments, causing elevated fuel prices and supply cancellations. The Australian federal government has responded by releasing fuel reserves, cutting fuel excise taxes, and implementing a national fuel security plan.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks kill at least 10 nurses in Iran
stories.summary: At least ten nurses were killed in US-Israeli bombings in Iran, according to Iran's Isna news agency. The Iranian Red Crescent Society said civilian areas were targeted, though medical services continued without disruption.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump claims war will end in ‘two or three weeks’; Rubio says US should ‘re-examine’ Nato relationship
stories.summary: President Trump claimed the war on Iran could conclude within two to three weeks and said countries dependent on the Strait of Hormuz must take responsibility for reopening it. Secretary of State Rubio called for a re-examination of the US relationship with NATO. Israel reported an 11-year-old girl seriously injured by Iranian missile strikes.

stories.title: Energy crisis: why ‘keep calm but cut down’ may be a better message for Labour
stories.summary: UK Labour ministers urged calm as oil prices surged due to the Iran war, with Treasury Chief Secretary James Murray encouraging people to continue normal routines. However, analysts suggest the government may need to advise households on reducing energy consumption rather than simply offering reassurance.

stories.title: Passover in the shadow of war: Celebrating freedom amidst strife - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial reflects on the significance of the Passover Seder being observed during wartime, emphasizing themes of family, tradition, and connection amid ongoing conflict.

stories.title: China gains ground in DR Congo’s mining sector as Australian firm loses permits
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Mining Registry canceled mining permits held by Australia's AVZ Minerals for non-payment of surface rights fees, the company's second permit loss in three years. The decisions reflect a broader shift in the DRC's mining sector, where Chinese companies have emerged as preferred partners.

stories.title: Japan solo dining chain surges in popularity in China; hours long wait times lead to scalpers
stories.summary: Japanese conveyor belt sushi chain Sushiro has seen surging popularity in China, tapping into a growing solo dining trend. After opening its first mainland location in Guangzhou in 2021, its Beijing debut in 2024 drew queues of up to 1,500 tables. Its December 2025 Shanghai opening attracted 700 groups before doors opened, with scalpers exploiting demand.

stories.title: Startup takes a different approach to AI assistants
stories.summary: A veteran-founded startup is offering a new approach to AI assistants designed specifically for military use. The tool is positioned as the Pentagon increasingly explores agentic AI capabilities for defence applications.

stories.title: Over 800 strikes, 16,000 munitions: Operation Roaring Lion thus far
stories.summary: The IDF reported conducting over 800 strikes using 16,000 munitions as part of Operation Roaring Lion, a joint effort involving the Operations Directorate, Air Force, and Military Intelligence to target Iranian military infrastructure.

stories.title: Malaysian minister warns of ‘very, very serious’ energy crisis
stories.summary: Malaysia's Transport Minister Anthony Loke warned the country has entered "crisis mode" due to the global energy supply disruption, calling it a "very, very serious matter." He noted energy costs have risen more than 100 percent over the past month as the conflict in the Middle East continues to strain supplies.

stories.title: South Africa: Cape Town Ready to Support Army to Tackle Crime Surge - South African News Briefs - April 1, 2026
stories.summary: Cape Town authorities indicated readiness to support the South African army in addressing a surge in crime in the city.

stories.title: Wednesday briefing: ​How did Russia become the unexpected beneficiary of the Iran war?
stories.summary: Russia has emerged as an unexpected beneficiary of the US-Israeli war on Iran, which began with attacks on Tehran in late February. Soaring energy prices have reversed Moscow's fiscal pressures from the ongoing Ukraine invasion, allowing it to avoid planned budget cuts to education and healthcare.

stories.title: US judge blocks Trump order to strip NPR and PBS funding
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge blocked President Trump's executive order to strip funding from NPR and PBS. However, the ruling's practical impact is limited because congressional Republicans have also voted to rescind funding for the outlets.

stories.title: Bath, UK mayor resigns after amplifying idea that Jewish ambulance arson was ‘false flag' attack
stories.summary: Bharat Pankhania, the mayor of Bath, England, resigned after amplifying suggestions that an antisemitic arson attack on four Hatzolah ambulances in London was a false flag operation carried out by Jews.

stories.title: Finland to introduce air threat alert system modeled on Ukrainian application
stories.summary: Finland announced plans to launch an air threat warning system by the end of 2027, modeled on Ukraine's experience with alert applications developed during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Nigeria: National Assembly Approves Tinubu's Fresh $6bn Loan Request
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Assembly approved President Tinubu's request for a $6 billion loan from the UAE and the UK, earmarked for budget implementation, infrastructure development, and refinancing existing debts.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Apologises to South Africa Over 'Coronation' of Traditional Ruler
stories.summary: Nigeria issued an apology to South Africa over the ceremonial coronation of a traditional ruler, with officials clarifying the event was symbolic and not an installation of a new traditional authority.

stories.title: Pakistan eyes Gulf investment, defence deals in return for playing peacemaker in Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a diplomatic mediator in the US-Israel war on Iran, hoping to leverage a peacemaker role for postwar benefits. Analysts say Islamabad aims to secure defense deals with Gulf monarchies and attract investment to bolster its struggling economy and finance military expansion.

stories.title: Nigeria: Senate Passes 2026 Budget Without Scrutinising Tinubu's Request for Upward Review
stories.summary: Nigeria's Senate passed the 2026 budget after reviewing a report from the Senate Committee on Appropriations, without scrutinizing President Tinubu's request for an upward spending review.

stories.title: Iraq defeat Bolivia 2-1 to qualify for FIFA World Cup 2026
stories.summary: Iraq defeated Bolivia 2-1 in a FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifier, with goals from Ali Al-Hamadi and Aymen Hussein securing Iraq's first World Cup appearance since 1986.

stories.title: Asia stocks jump after Trump suggests Iran war could end in weeks
stories.summary: Asian stock markets surged after U.S. President Trump suggested the Iran war could end within weeks. Brent crude oil prices had risen 64% in March due to conflict-related energy supply disruptions.

stories.title: Iraq secure final World Cup spot with win over Bolivia, join France group
stories.summary: Iraq secured the final 2026 FIFA World Cup berth by defeating Bolivia 2-1 in an intercontinental playoff on Tuesday. The victory marks Iraq's return to the World Cup finals after a 40-year absence. They will compete in Group I alongside France, Senegal, and Norway.

stories.title: DR Congo score extra-time winner to reach first World Cup in half a century
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo defeated Jamaica 1-0 in an intercontinental playoff on Tuesday to qualify for their first FIFA World Cup in 52 years. Former England under-21 international Axel Tuanzebe scored the decisive goal from a corner kick in the 100th minute of extra time.

stories.title: Foreign media group slams Israeli police attack on former AFP photographer
stories.summary: The Foreign Press Association condemned an Israeli police attack on former AFP photographer Menahem Kahana, who was sprayed at close range by a water cannon while covering a protest outside the Knesset in Israel.

stories.title: Israel says missile launched from Yemen
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it was working to intercept a missile launched from Yemen toward its territory. No injuries were immediately reported. Yemen's Houthi group has previously launched missiles at Israel.

stories.title: After meeting in the ICU, these bereaved mothers of IDF troops reunite via new initiative
stories.summary: Two bereaved mothers of fallen IDF soldiers, Hazel Brief and Taly Drori, reunited through a health retreat organized by OneFamily, a nonprofit supporting families of terror victims and fallen soldiers in Israel.

stories.title: Two-thirds of Americans want quick end to Iran war even if goals unachieved, poll finds
stories.summary: A new poll found that two-thirds of Americans favor a quick end to the war in Iran even if military objectives remain unachieved. Among Republican respondents, 40 percent supported ending the conflict quickly.

stories.title: Sirens sound across northern Israel amid drone alerts
stories.summary: Air raid sirens sounded across northern Israel, including in Kiryat Shmona, Safed, and surrounding towns, amid reports of a suspected drone infiltration. Interception attempts were underway.

stories.title: Asia ramps up use of dirty fuels to cover energy shortfall triggered by Iran war
stories.summary: Several Asian governments, including South Korea and the Philippines, are increasing coal-fired power generation to address energy shortfalls caused by the US-Israel war on Iran. South Korea is delaying planned coal plant shutdowns while the Philippines plans to boost coal output. Climate experts warn the shift undermines environmental goals and urge greater investment in renewables.

stories.title: Nigeria: 40 Detained Nigerians Deported From Mozambique
stories.summary: Nigeria's Diaspora Commission confirmed the deportation of 40 of 42 Nigerians who had been arrested and detained for weeks in Mozambique.

stories.title: Fire at Russian petrochemicals plant kills at least three
stories.summary: A large fire erupted at a petrochemicals plant in Russia's Tatarstan region, killing at least three people, including one firefighter, and injuring dozens of others.

stories.title: Writing on the wall: Art UK digitises thousands of murals as street artworks go mainstream
stories.summary: Art UK, a charity, has digitised more than 6,600 murals across the United Kingdom, ranging from medieval church wall paintings to contemporary street art. Notable examples include small public murals on bollards in Shrewsbury, a large work on a 16-storey building in Gosport, and a Cardiff mural reproducing a viral Liam Gallagher social media post.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes hit civilian infrastructure, residential blocks in Tehran
stories.summary: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported US-Israeli airstrikes hit several Tehran districts, including residential areas in Tehransar near Mehrabad International Airport and affluent northern neighborhoods in District 1.

stories.title: IDF strikes Iranian regime chemical manufacturer
stories.summary: The IDF struck a chemical manufacturing factory in Iran owned by the Tofiq Daru Company, which Israel identified as the principal supplier of fentanyl for the Iranian regime's research and development agency.

stories.title: Residents inspect drone damage near Erbil airport
stories.summary: Residents near Erbil's international airport in northern Iraq reported property damage caused by falling drone debris in the area.

stories.title: ‘Harrowing’: Cyclone Narelle leaves graveyard of turtles, dolphins and seabirds in Western Australia
stories.summary: Tropical Cyclone Narelle struck Exmouth in Western Australia, causing flooding and significant wildlife destruction along the coastline. Local resident Brinkley Davies reported finding dead turtles, dolphins, and seabirds at Graveyards beach after the storm subsided.

stories.title: Iran says US-Israeli attack hit passenger dock in Bandar Abbas
stories.summary: Iran said US-Israeli forces bombed the Shahid Haqqani passenger dock in the southern port city of Bandar Abbas. A senior Hormozgan province official condemned the strike but said no casualties were reported.

stories.title: Iran says strike on pharmaceutical facility hits medical supply chain
stories.summary: Iran said a US-Israeli strike destroyed a Tofigh Daru pharmaceutical facility in Tehran, causing what officials described as a significant blow to the national medical supply chain. Deputy Health Minister Mahdi Pirsalehi confirmed total destruction of the production units.

stories.title: Pentagon weighs using anti-drone lasers in Washington airspace
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is considering deploying anti-drone laser systems in the Washington, D.C., airspace following reports of unusual drone activity near Fort McNair.

stories.title: World’s first Chinese-language TV station goes off-air in 2016 – SCMP archive
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Asia Television, described as the world's first Chinese-language TV station, ceased broadcasting on April 1, 2016, after years of financial difficulties. The cash-strapped station aired a rerun of its Miss Asia beauty pageant as its final program before pulling the plug just before midnight.

stories.title: Syria will stay out of Iran conflict unless it faces aggression, president says
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa declared that Syria will remain neutral in the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran unless Syria itself faces aggression and diplomatic options are exhausted. The statement came on Tuesday as the regional conflict continued.

stories.title: Hetmantsev outlines funding sources for Ukraine’s large-scale mortgage program
stories.summary: Ukrainian lawmaker Hetmantsev outlined potential funding sources for a large-scale national mortgage program, including domestic capital markets, banking sector liquidity, partner contributions, and state budget allocations.

stories.title: US military denies strike on Iran sports hall after NYT report
stories.summary: The US military denied carrying out a strike on a sports hall and residential area in the Iranian city of Lamerd, contradicting a New York Times investigation that identified a US Precision Strike Missile as the weapon used. Iran's Fars agency reported roughly 15 people killed.

stories.title: Chancellor meets UK supermarket bosses to discuss cost of living
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves met with bosses of Sainsbury's, Tesco, and Morrisons on Wednesday to discuss potential food price rises and shortages of household essentials. The meeting was prompted by surging energy, fuel, and fertiliser costs linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: China doubles down on chemical plant expansion with tech breakthrough amid Iran war
stories.summary: China began construction of the world's largest coal-to-ethylene glycol project in Xinjiang's Turpan prefecture, expected to produce 2.4 million tonnes per year. The expansion aims to secure key chemicals for green technology manufacturing and scale coal-based production as Middle East conflict disrupts global chemical supply chains.

stories.title: Drone attack sparks fire at airport after fuel tanks hit, Kuwaiti authorities say
stories.summary: Kuwait said its international airport was targeted by drones launched by Iran and allied groups, striking fuel storage tanks and sparking a large fire. No immediate casualties were reported.

stories.title: Anthony Albanese to address nation on Wednesday night as treasurer announces Covid-era support measures
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a national address for Wednesday evening. Treasurer Jim Chalmers unveiled Covid-era-style support measures for businesses facing soaring fuel prices, citing the extreme economic impact of the US-Israel war on Iran on the global economy.

stories.title: Iran says no talks with US, prepared for months of war
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran is prepared for at least six months of war and denied any direct negotiations with Washington, contradicting US President Trump's claim that the conflict could end within weeks.

stories.title: Report: Iran using new methods to enforce internet blackouts
stories.summary: The rights group Access Now reported that Iran is using increasingly sophisticated methods to enforce internet shutdowns, including criminalizing Starlink use and deploying signal jamming to block satellite-based internet since February 28.

stories.title: Kentucky governor: Gaza ‘genocide’ claims shouldn’t be a litmus test for Democrats
stories.summary: Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, stated that claims of genocide in Gaza should not be a litmus test for Democrats, while affirming Israel's right to exist and criticizing both Trump and Netanyahu over the Gaza and Iran wars.

stories.title: Marco Rubio urges US diplomats to use X to fight ‘anti-American propaganda’
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio directed American diplomats to use the social media platform X to counter what he termed "anti-American propaganda." Diplomats were also instructed to coordinate with interagency partners, including the Pentagon's Psychological Operations units.

stories.title: Marco Rubio urges US diplomats to use X to fight 'anti-American propaganda'
stories.summary: WASHINGTON, March 31 - U.S. diplomats should use social media platform X and partner with military psychological operations units in an effort to \"counter foreign anti-American propaganda,\" Secretar

stories.title: Japan begins tax increases to bankroll record US$8 billion military build-up
stories.summary: Japan raised tobacco and corporate taxes on Wednesday to fund its record defense spending buildup, with an income tax increase planned for 2027. The government projects the tax hikes will generate approximately 1.3 trillion yen (US$8 billion) in annual revenue to finance expanding military outlays amid a deteriorating regional security environment.

stories.title: Kremlin reacts skeptically to Zelensky's proposal for Easter truce
stories.summary: The Kremlin responded skeptically to Ukrainian President Zelensky's proposal for an Easter truce, stating it had not received any detailed proposals regarding the ceasefire initiative.

stories.title: Molly the border collie rescued after a week waiting for injured owner in New Zealand’s remote backcountry
stories.summary: A border collie named Molly was rescued from New Zealand's remote alpine backcountry after spending a week near a waterfall where she had been separated from her injured owner. A volunteer team of former helicopter pilots funded by public donations located and brought the dog home.

stories.title: Russian military plane crash kills 29 in Crimea
stories.summary: A Russian An-26 military transport plane crashed into a cliff in Crimea due to a reported technical malfunction, killing all 29 people on board, including six crew members and 23 passengers.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges Trump to find 'off-ramp' to end Iran war
stories.summary: Pope Leo issued a direct appeal to President Donald Trump from Castel Gandolfo, Italy, urging him to seek an "off-ramp" to end the war in Iran as the regional conflict expands.

stories.title: US lawmaker says American families 'paying the price' for 'war of choice'
stories.summary: US Democratic Senator Chris Coons criticized the war with Iran as a "war of choice," saying American families are bearing rising costs in fuel, groceries, and utilities. He called on the Trump administration to clarify the conflict's rationale and timeline.

stories.title: Iraqi armed group warns US against using Kuwait for Iran attack
stories.summary: Iraqi armed group Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada warned the US against using Kuwait as a staging ground for a ground invasion of Iran, saying such action would escalate the conflict into an all-out regional war.

stories.title: China-Pakistan five-point plan to end Iran war
stories.summary: China and Pakistan jointly unveiled a five-point peace plan on Tuesday aimed at restoring stability in the Persian Gulf. The initiative comes after five weeks of US-Israeli military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Hezbollah says 'fierce clashes' ongoing in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah reported fierce clashes with Israeli troops near the town of Chama in southern Lebanon. The group also claimed rocket attacks on Israeli soldiers near El Qantara and strikes on targets in northern Israel, including near Haifa and Safed.

stories.title: Hegseth says ‘no punishment’  for Army pilots who flew near Kid Rock’s house
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said there would be no punishment for Army pilots who flew near musician Kid Rock's residence. The pilots had previously been reported as suspended over the incident.

stories.title: Army suspends helicopter aircrew that flew near Kid Rock's house, official says
stories.summary: March 31 - The U.S. Army has suspended the aircrew of two Apache attack helicopters that flew near the house of singer Kid Rock, seemingly in support of the vocal backer of U.S. President Donald Trump

stories.title: Global protests condemning Israel’s new death penalty law for Palestinians
stories.summary: Protests took place globally against an Israeli bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for certain Palestinian detainees.

stories.title: Iran says Elon Musk’s Starlink now 'legitimate target', state media reports
stories.summary: Iran declared Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet system a legitimate military target, with state media mapping its infrastructure across Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE. Use of Starlink is restricted in Iran and carries prison sentences.

stories.title: US warns Americans in Saudi Arabia to shelter in place after threats
stories.summary: The U.S. government warned American citizens in Saudi Arabia to shelter in place, citing potential threats against hotels, U.S. businesses, and U.S. educational institutions.

stories.title: Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone
stories.summary: Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone after reports emerged that he had briefed Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on efforts to lift EU sanctions on Gulbahor Ismailova, the sister of sanctioned Russian oligarch Alisher Usmanov.

stories.title: Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone
stories.summary: Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone after reports emerged that he had briefed Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov on efforts to lift EU sanctions against Gulbahor Ismailova, sister of sanctioned Russian oligarch Alisher Usmanov.

stories.title: US judge says Trump administration can demand list of Jews at Penn for antisemitism probe
stories.summary: A US federal judge ruled that the Trump administration can request a list of Jewish students at the University of Pennsylvania as part of an antisemitism investigation, finding the request consistent with standard discrimination probes.

stories.title: Tai Po fire hearing: estate management staff tearfully reject failure to help claims
stories.summary: An independent inquiry in Hong Kong is examining the November 26 fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, which killed 168 people and displaced nearly 5,000 residents. Staff from property management firm ISS EastPoint testified, rejecting claims they failed to assist during the blaze that burned through seven of eight towers over 43 hours.

stories.title: U.S. journalist kidnapped in Baghdad, security forces hunt captors, says Iraqi officials
stories.summary: Iraqi officials report that an American female journalist has been kidnapped in Baghdad. Iraqi security forces are actively pursuing the group responsible for the abduction.

stories.title: Al-Sharaa says Syria to stay out of war on Iran unless attacked
stories.summary: Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa stated that Syria will not enter the US-Israeli war on Iran unless Syria itself is attacked, citing 14 years of prior conflict as sufficient.

stories.title: Machado meets Rubio in Washington, says her return to Venezuela is near
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department on Tuesday, saying her return to Venezuela is near. It was their second meeting since the U.S. military operation that captured Nicolás Maduro in Caracas on January 3.

stories.title: Japan races to limit fallout from Chinese embassy break-in
stories.summary: Japan is working to contain diplomatic fallout after a member of its Self-Defence Forces broke into the Chinese embassy in Tokyo on March 24. National Police Agency Commissioner Yoshinobu Kusunoki called the incident "extremely unusual and serious." Observers note Beijing may use the event to reinforce claims of rising Japanese militarism and anti-China sentiment.

stories.title: How China is building faster high-speed railways using vast underwater tunnels
stories.summary: China completed the underwater excavation of a high-speed rail tunnel stretching over 14 kilometers beneath the Yangtze River. The tunnel will connect Shanghai's Chongming Island with Taicang city in Jiangsu province and is expected to be finished by the end of the year.

stories.title: Trump’s order to limit mail-in voting: does he have the authority?
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order seeking to restrict mail-in voting and create a national list of confirmed eligible voters. The order directs the US Postal Service to send mail-in ballots only to those on the list. Critics describe the move as unconstitutional and expect legal challenges.

stories.title: Top Chinese developers’ losses mount as debt overhaul props up operations
stories.summary: Major Chinese property developers including China Vanke reported mounting operating losses in 2025, with Vanke posting a record 88.56 billion yuan loss. Some headline profits were driven mainly by non-cash gains from debt restructuring rather than operational recovery.

stories.title: Jailed Palestinians fear death by hanging without due process under new Israeli law
stories.summary: RAMALLAH/JERUSALEM, March 31 - Palestinians in the occupied West Bank voiced fears on Tuesday that their jailed relatives could be hanged without due process after Israel adopted a new law making the

stories.title: Burundi says explosions in Bujumbura caused by short-circuit at ammunition store
stories.summary: NAIROBI, March 31 - Explosions heard on Tuesday in Bujumbura, Burundi's commercial capital, were caused by an electrical short-circuit at an ammunition store in a military camp, an army spokesperson s

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Iran war could end in 'two weeks, maybe three'
stories.summary: President Trump stated Tuesday that the war with Iran could end within two to three weeks. He also said that responsibility for securing the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil shipping channel, should fall to the countries that depend on it rather than the United States.

stories.title: US war on Iran 'last best chance' to avoid a nuclear Islamic regime, Rubio says
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the war on Iran as the "last best chance" to prevent a nuclear-armed Islamic regime. He said a country run by what he called radical Shia clerics must never possess nuclear weapons.

stories.title: US FDA warns of liver injury cases tied to Amgen’s rare disease drug
stories.summary: The agency has identified 76 cases of drug-induced liver injury with evidence suggesting a causal link to Amgen's Tavneos.

stories.title: Argentina: court demands university salary restoration amid faculty strikes
stories.summary: Argentina's Federal Administrative Litigation Chamber upheld an injunction ordering President Javier Milei's government to enforce Law 27,795 on University Funding. The law mandates salary adjustments for public university staff and restoration of student scholarship programs, amid ongoing faculty strikes.

stories.title: Israel refused normalization with Syria last minute, says Al-Sharaa
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Israel backed away from normalization with Syria at the last minute. He stated that although negotiations had reached promising points, Israel ultimately changed its position.

stories.title: Applying Israel’s death penalty law would be a ‘war crime’: UN
stories.summary: The UN rights chief said that the death penalty is profoundly difficult to reconcile with human dignity.

stories.title: Man wounded during Odesa shelling on March 28 dies in hospital
stories.summary: A 76-year-old man who was severely injured during a Russian attack on Odesa on March 28 has died in hospital.

stories.title: Iran Guards say will target U.S. tech firms if more leaders killed
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to target U.S. technology companies, warning employees at those institutions to leave their workplaces immediately to preserve their lives.

stories.title: Why China is always misunderstood and misrepresented
stories.summary: The article examines longstanding questions about China's historical development, including "Needham's question" about why China did not develop its own scientific and industrial revolutions despite its many early discoveries. It also explores why capitalism did not emerge during the Song dynasty despite favorable economic conditions.

stories.title: Trade war meets tradition: Canadian Jews confront a Manischewitz-free Passover
stories.summary: Canadian Jews faced a Passover without Manischewitz wine due to Canada's ban on American alcohol imposed in response to US tariffs. The ban reportedly created new market opportunities for Israeli wineries in Canada.

stories.title: American journalist kidnapped in Baghdad, police officials say
stories.summary: An American journalist was kidnapped in Baghdad, according to Iraqi police officials. The U.S. State Department confirmed it was aware of the reported abduction.

stories.title: Trump says US could end Iran war in two to three weeks
stories.summary: President Trump told reporters the US could end the war with Iran in two to three weeks. He stated that without a deal, the US could put Iran "into the stone ages" and prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: US Forest Service to move headquarters from Washington DC to Salt Lake City
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it will relocate the US Forest Service headquarters from Washington, DC, to Salt Lake City and close its regional offices. The USDA described the reorganisation as a commonsense approach, while critics called it an attack on science and scientists within the federal land management agency.

stories.title: Scottish man linked to gang arrested in Indonesia’s Bali after Interpol issues red alert
stories.summary: Indonesian authorities arrested Steven Lyons, a 45-year-old Scottish man described as a senior figure in an international crime syndicate, at Ngurah Rai International Airport in Bali. He was detained by immigration officers upon arrival from Singapore after being flagged by an Interpol red notice.

stories.title: Tuanzebe sends DR Congo back to World Cup after 52 years
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo qualified for its first FIFA World Cup since 1974 after Axel Tuanzebe scored the winning goal in a 1-0 play-off victory over Jamaica.

stories.title: Japan’s Shibuya to fine litterbugs on the spot from June as visitor numbers surge
stories.summary: Tokyo's Shibuya ward will begin imposing on-the-spot fines of 2,000 yen (US$12.50) for littering starting June 1, abandoning its previous policy of asking visitors to take rubbish home. The change comes as rising visitor numbers have led to increasing litter problems in the district known for its famous scramble crossing.

stories.title: Why Empress Dowager Cixi and people in ancient China used animal faeces in beauty routines
stories.summary: The article discusses historical beauty practices in ancient China, including the use of animal excrement in skincare routines. Empress Dowager Cixi, who effectively ruled the Qing dynasty for nearly 50 years from 1861 to 1908, reportedly incorporated bird droppings into her lifelong skincare regimen.

stories.title: Emergency workers search for victims of Israeli airstrikes on Beirut
stories.summary: Emergency workers in Beirut searched through rubble in the Jnah neighbourhood after Israeli airstrikes struck the area.

stories.title: ‘A law of death that only applies to Palestinians’
stories.summary: Protesters in the United Kingdom called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to take concrete action against Israel's death penalty legislation targeting Palestinian detainees, rather than merely condemning it.

stories.title: Trump says US will leave Iran in "two or three weeks," claims regime change achieved
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said from the Oval Office that U.S. forces will withdraw from Iran within two to three weeks, claiming the military campaign has achieved its core objectives including regime change.

stories.title: Israel says will reduce French defence imports 'to zero'
stories.summary: Israel announced it will reduce French defence imports to zero, citing disagreements with Paris over policies related to Palestine, airspace restrictions, and defence cooperation.

stories.title: Iran Guards threaten to target US tech firms if more leaders killed
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to target US technology companies including Apple, Google, and Meta if more Iranian leaders are killed. Iran alleged these companies were involved in tracking individuals targeted for assassination during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Russian military plane crashes into Crimea cliff, killing 29 people
stories.summary: A Russian An-26 military transport plane crashed into a cliff in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board. Russia's defense ministry said contact with the aircraft was lost around 6 p.m. local time Tuesday during a planned flight. A possible technical malfunction is suspected as the cause.

stories.title: ‘I’m not dumb’: Hong Kong’s London trade office manager denies running spy network
stories.summary: Bill Yuen Chung-biu, a manager at Hong Kong's trade office in London, denied in a British national security trial that he ran a spy network targeting Hong Kong activists and UK politicians on behalf of China. He challenged prosecution claims that he operated a "shadow" policing operation two years after his arrest.

stories.title: Trump tells allies ‘get your own oil’, says Iran war could end in 2-3 weeks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told allied nations to source their own oil and claimed the war on Iran could conclude within two to three weeks, amid rising domestic petrol prices.

stories.title: Billion-plus people, three million officials, 33 questions - India begins huge census
stories.summary: India launched its massive census exercise, deploying three million officials across the country to count over a billion people using a 33-question survey conducted in two phases.

stories.title: Angela Buchdahl: This Passover, have faith in the story of the Exodus
stories.summary: Rabbi Angela Buchdahl of New York City's Central Synagogue discussed the challenges facing Zionist rabbinic leaders in North America and finding meaning in Passover amid current events.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF strikes, dismantles missile launchers in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military released footage showing strikes on missile launchers in southern Lebanon. The IDF said the launchers were used in a recent barrage against Israel that injured three people, including a six-year-old child.

stories.title: Iran says no decision taken on US talks despite message exchanges
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran has not made any decision on negotiations with the United States and has not responded to any US proposals. He confirmed that messages have been exchanged with Washington but said all communications are handled through official channels.

stories.title: Will surging fuel prices push Filipinos deeper into credit card debt?
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict could push more Filipinos deeper into credit card debt, analysts warn. Although credit card ownership in the Philippines remains relatively low, cardholders are using them more intensively as living costs outpace income growth, with receivables growing consistently.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says conflict to end in 2-3 weeks; Kuwait airport hit
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes continued across Iran, hitting pharmaceutical companies and steel plants in Isfahan and Farokhshar. Separately, Kuwait's international airport was struck during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: War update: 151 clashes on front line, Pokrovsk sector remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 151 combat engagements along the front line, with the Pokrovsk sector seeing the most activity at 51 Russian attacks. Russian forces lost more than 120 troops in the fighting.

stories.title: In Lebanon, UN peacekeepers are caught in the firing line
stories.summary: Three UN peacekeepers were killed in southern Lebanon this week amid the ongoing war between Israel and Hezbollah. The deaths make this conflict one of the deadliest chapters for the UN peacekeeping mission in Lebanon, whose decades-long mandate expires this year.

stories.title: DR Congo beat Jamaica to reach World Cup via intercontinental finals
stories.summary: DR Congo defeated Jamaica 1-0 in an intercontinental World Cup qualifying playoff, with former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe scoring the winning goal in extra time.

stories.title: Syria will stay out of Iran conflict unless it faces aggression
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria will remain out of the Iran-Israel conflict unless directly attacked. He stressed that Damascus seeks to avoid involvement in any new war.

stories.title: Trump says US will be leaving Iran in two to three weeks
stories.summary: Speaking from the Oval Office, US President Donald Trump told reporters that US forces could leave Iran within two to three weeks.

stories.title: Warren Buffett will not commit to more donations to Gates Foundation
stories.summary: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett indicated he would not commit to further donations to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. Buffett said he did not regret past donations but expressed reservations about certain developments at the foundation.

stories.title: Power outage schedules for industrial consumers to be in effect on Wednesday – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that power limitation schedules for industrial consumers would be in effect across all regions on Wednesday, April 1, from 12:00 to 17:00.

stories.title: Power outage schedules for industrial consumers to be in effect on Wednesday – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced power outage schedules for industrial consumers on Wednesday, April 1, from 12:00 to 17:00 across all regions of the country.

stories.title: 11-year-old girl seriously wounded in Iranian cluster bomb impact in Bnei Brak
stories.summary: An 11-year-old girl was seriously wounded by an Iranian cluster munition strike in Bnei Brak, central Israel, with at least 13 others injured. Separately, the IDF intercepted a Houthi projectile targeting southern Israel.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in southern Lebanon within an hour
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon killed at least eight people within one hour. A strike on Jebchit in the Nabatieh district killed a pregnant woman and her husband, while a separate raid in Kafra killed two more people.

stories.title: Hegseth says suspensions lifted for helicopter crews who hovered over Kid Rock home
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth lifted suspensions for the crews of two US Army AH-64 Apache helicopters that hovered near singer Kid Rock's home and swimming pool in Tennessee on Saturday. Hegseth declared there would be no punishment or investigation into the incident.

stories.title: UN says initial findings show roadside blast killed Indonesian peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations said initial findings indicate a roadside blast killed Indonesian peacekeepers serving in Lebanon. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres strongly condemned the attack on the peacekeeping force.

stories.title: 'You're no longer my sister' - rows erupt as war divides Iranian families
stories.summary: Families across Iran are experiencing internal divisions and strained relationships over differing views on the ongoing war, with relatives reportedly cutting ties over political disagreements.

stories.title: Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar junta chief, elected as Vice-Presidentscvnks
stories.summary: The upper house elected Nan Ni Ni Aye, a regional MP from Karen State with the military-aligned Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP), as another V-P, local media reported

stories.title: Zelensky discusses peace talks and security cooperation with Merz
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz about the peace negotiation process and security cooperation with partners to end the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: 'A million things could go wrong' - why seizing Iran's uranium would be so risky for the US
stories.summary: A former US defence official told the BBC that seizing Iran's uranium stockpile would be one of the most complicated special operations in history, citing enormous logistical and security risks.

stories.title: Israel says it struck rocket launch sites in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military spokesperson Avichay Adraee said the army struck rocket launch sites in southern Lebanon that were used in recent barrages toward Israel. Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,268 people, including over 100 children, since March 2.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges Trump to end war on Iran
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV publicly urged US President Donald Trump to find an off-ramp from the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: More than 200,000 fled Lebanon for Syria in March: UNHCR
stories.summary: Lebanon was pulled into the West Asia conflict in early March when Israeli-U.S. strikes killed Iran's supreme leader and Tehran-backed Hezbollah responded by firing rockets at Israel.

stories.title: Lapid: Netanyahu incapable of reaching victory, is dismantling Israel from within
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu, arguing he is incapable of achieving victory, noting Hamas still controls Gaza, Hezbollah continues firing rockets, and Khamenei remains in power in Iran.

stories.title: German chancellor clarifies Syrian refugee comments after backlash
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz walked back comments about the return of Syrian refugees to their homeland after facing backlash. Economists and politicians had warned that a mass departure of Syrian refugees could have a significant negative economic impact on Germany.

stories.title: US exempts Gulf of Mexico oil drillers from endangered species protections
stories.summary: The Trump administration exempted Gulf of Mexico oil drillers from endangered species protections, citing the need to maintain US energy competitiveness during the ongoing war on Iran.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes Nikopol, leaving 11 injured, including one child
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on Nikopol in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region injured 11 people, including one child.

stories.title: On global tensions and India’s economy
stories.summary: In an economy that imports more than four-fifths of its crude oil, external shocks transmitted through energy prices, shipping route, and volatile commodity markets can significantly reshape fiscal ar

stories.title: EU warns oil and gas prices won’t quickly return to normal after Iran war
stories.summary: The EU's energy commissioner warned that oil and gas prices will not return to normal soon, as the war on Iran continues to disrupt global energy markets.

stories.title: Trump says US-Israeli war on Iran ‘coming to an end’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told NBC that the US-Israeli war on Iran is "coming to an end." He suggested the fighting would soon be wrapped up but did not provide a specific timeline.

stories.title: Israeli chess player expected a forfeit, her Iranian opponent showed up
stories.summary: Israeli chess player Yarden Bloch expected her Iranian opponent to forfeit their match, as Iranian athletes have often been prevented from competing against Israelis. Instead, the Iranian player showed up to compete.

stories.title: Funerals held for 3 of the soldiers killed fighting Hezbollah in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Funerals were held in Israel for three soldiers killed fighting Hezbollah in southern Lebanon: Staff Sgt. Maxsim Entis, 21; Cpt. Noam Madmoni, 22; and Staff Sgt. Ben Cohen, 21.

stories.title: Asia's migrant workers debate if Gulf jobs are worth deadly risk of Iran war
stories.summary: Migrant workers from across Asia are reconsidering employment in Gulf states as Iranian strikes on the region raise safety concerns, threatening livelihoods that support families back home.

stories.title: Tunisian journalist sentenced to two years, union denounces systemic attack on media
stories.summary: A Tunisian court sentenced news website editor Ghassen Ben Khelifa to two years in prison. Tunisia's journalists' union denounced the prosecution as part of a systemic attack on press freedom and free speech in the country.

stories.title: Australia politics live: Chalmers announces support package for businesses hit by fuel crisis including tax relief
stories.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers announced a support package including tax relief for businesses affected by a fuel crisis. Separately, AI company Anthropic signed a memorandum of understanding with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to support Australia's national AI plan.

stories.title: EU says 'necessary' to reduce fuel demand to cope with crisis
stories.summary: The EU urged member states to reduce fuel demand amid a crisis caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran. The conflict has practically halted maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries a fifth of global crude supplies.

stories.title: Pentagon declines to reaffirm NATO’s collective defence, says up to Trump
stories.summary: The Pentagon declined to reaffirm NATO's Article 5 collective defense commitment, stating the matter was up to President Trump. The move came as Trump criticized NATO member states for not supporting the US during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses consequences of blockade of Strait of Hormuz and countering Russian propaganda with Tajani
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky, during a meeting with Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Antonio Tajani, discussed the consequences of a potential blockade of the Strait of Ho

stories.title: U.S.-Israel targeted major pharmaceutical company: Iran govt
stories.summary: Iran's government stated that US and Israeli strikes damaged one of the country's largest pharmaceutical companies producing anti-cancer, anesthetic, and specialized medicines. The government said the attack on the civilian facility disrupted drug production lines.

stories.title: Lebanon bracing for long-term displacement crisis amid funding crunch, minister says
