stories.summary: The EU, Spain, Germany, and other governments condemned Israel's new law making the death penalty the default sentence for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis in military courts. Analysts say the law will further damage Israel's diplomatic standing internationally.

stories.title: Kallas and Wadephul state in Bucha that Russia’s crimes must not go unpunished
stories.summary: EU High Representative Kaja Kallas and German politician Johann Wadephul visited Bucha, Ukraine, and reaffirmed the EU's commitment to ensuring accountability for Russian crimes committed there at the start of the full-scale invasion.

stories.title: US defence secretary says next few days in Iran war will be ‘decisive’
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that the coming days in the war with Iran will be "decisive." The remarks signal an anticipated intensification of military operations.

stories.title: PMD forecasts chances of thunderstorms, rain in Karachi, other parts of Sindh on Thursday
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast thunderstorms and rain for Karachi and other parts of Sindh province from April 2–4, driven by a westerly weather system approaching from Balochistan.

stories.title: China pledges ‘strategic coordination’ with Pakistan to help end US war on Iran
stories.summary: China pledged to enhance "strategic coordination" with Pakistan on the Iran crisis to promote dialogue and help end the conflict. Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar visited Beijing for his second trip in three months, following a phone call with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in which Beijing pledged to support Pakistan's mediation role.

stories.title: Soaring fuel prices drive German far-right calls for a turn back to Russia
stories.summary: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has seized on surging energy prices to renew calls for restoring Russian energy imports. The push comes after the party achieved some of its strongest results in two recent state elections.

stories.title: Landlords ‘leveraging up’ by exploiting property tax rules are fuelling Australia’s housing affordability crisis, analysis finds
stories.summary: A new analysis by Australia's e61 Institute found that the combination of capital gains tax discounts and negative gearing rules has fueled debt-driven property speculation, worsening housing affordability. The federal budget is expected to include changes to investor tax breaks.

stories.title: What’s Israel’s death penalty law that only applies to Palestinians?
stories.summary: Israel enacted a death penalty law that rights groups say will primarily apply to Palestinians. Human rights organizations have condemned the legislation as discriminatory.

stories.title: Wolf bites woman in shock German attack in Hamburg shopping street
stories.summary: A wolf attacked and bit a woman on a shopping street in Hamburg, Germany. Authorities believe it is the first wolf attack on a human since wolves began reestablishing populations in Germany decades ago.

stories.title: How India’s Ruling Party is Using AI to Boost Hate Speech in States Near Bangladesh
stories.summary: A Bellingcat investigation reports that a state branch of India's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) shared an AI-manipulated video featuring Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma appearing to target men in Muslim skull caps. The content included anti-immigrant captions such as "Foreigner-free Assam," highlighting the use of AI-generated media to amplify hate speech in Indian states bordering Bangladesh.

stories.title: Replay: Pete Hegseth gives press conference on Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Dan Caine held a press conference addressing the war in Iran. Washington continues to press Tehran to accept a deal to end the conflict.

stories.title: China has ‘room’ for imported inflation, but economic risks rising: PBOC adviser
stories.summary: A monetary policy adviser to the People's Bank of China said the country has sufficient capacity to manage imported inflationary pressures from Middle East instability. However, PBOC adviser Huang Yiping noted that China faces rising price pressures and must balance inflation risks against economic growth concerns, with CPI remaining below the 2 percent target.

stories.title: Satellite images begin to show damage wrought across the region by Iran war
stories.summary: Satellite imagery has revealed significant damage from the Iran war across the region, including burning ships at an Iranian military port near the Strait of Hormuz. Images also show damage to an Iranian military base and destruction at air bases throughout the Gulf.

stories.title: Iran using children in security roles in war, reports and witnesses say
stories.summary: Reports and witness accounts indicate that Iran has been deploying children in security roles during the ongoing conflict. An 11-year-old was reportedly killed in an air strike while manning a checkpoint in Tehran.

stories.title: In Sudan, sexual violence is a "weapon" among many
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders reported that Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and allied militias are using sexual violence as a weapon of war in Darfur to control civilian populations.

stories.title: King Charles to visit US in late April amid Iran war concerns
stories.summary: Buckingham Palace confirmed King Charles III and Queen Camilla will make a state visit to the United States in late April despite calls to cancel the trip amid the Iran war. The visit comes during strained US-UK relations, with President Trump criticizing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's stance on the US-Israel war against Iran.

stories.title: South Africa: Minister Enoch Godongwana Cuts Fuel Tax By R3
stories.summary: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced a R3 cut in fuel taxes to ease costs for consumers. The reduction follows a rise in oil prices after the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: KSE-100 climbs by over 1,800 points during intraday trade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index on the Pakistan Stock Exchange rose by over 1,800 points during intraday trading on Tuesday, partially recovering from a sharp selloff the previous day that had dragged the index below 145,000.

stories.title: Russian oil tanker docks in Cuba ending near-total blockade
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker docked in Cuba, providing temporary relief to the island nation after months of severe fuel shortages that had created a near-total blockade of energy supplies.

stories.title: Soaring fuel prices drive German far-right calls for a turn back to Russia
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices in Germany, exacerbated by the loss of Russian oil and gas supplies after the 2022 Ukraine invasion and Nord Stream shutdown, are fueling far-right calls to restore energy ties with Russia.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Mar. 31 – Israel angers Christian world in another avoidable scandal
stories.summary: The Times of Israel's diplomatic correspondent analyzed Israel's strategy regarding the war with Iran and its ongoing concerns about the former buffer zone in southern Lebanon, amid a controversy that drew criticism from the Christian world.

stories.title: Russian shelling damages train station in Sloviansk; four railway workers wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled railway infrastructure in the city of Sloviansk, damaging a train station. Four railway workers were wounded in the attack, one of whom is in critical condition.

stories.title: At least 70 killed in Haiti massacre, rights group says, far exceeding official toll
stories.summary: A human rights group reported that at least 70 people were killed and 30 injured in a gang attack near Petite-Rivière in Haiti's Artibonite region, far exceeding the official toll of around 16. An estimated 6,000 people were displaced.

stories.title: EU 'must prepare' for energy market disruption from Iran war
stories.summary: The EU energy commissioner urged member states to prepare for potential energy market disruptions resulting from the war with Iran, warning of a possibly prolonged period of supply instability.

stories.title: Why Turkey sees no winners in the US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: Turkey, having attempted to prevent the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, now finds itself caught amid the conflict. Ankara is deeply concerned about economic shocks, security spillover, and broader regional instability.

stories.title: Has Pakistan outplayed India in Iran war diplomacy?
stories.summary: Pakistan has gained diplomatic visibility during the Iran conflict through active engagement, while India's quieter approach has drawn questions about its strategy in the region.

stories.title: ‘A place where music fills the air’: Bangkok to host Eurovision’s first Asia song contest
stories.summary: The Eurovision Broadcasting Union announced that Bangkok, Thailand, will host the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, with the grand final scheduled for November 14. Broadcasters from 10 countries have confirmed participation in the spin-off event.

stories.title: Return of TACO Trump? Gulf states fear Trump may end Iran war without meaningful changes
stories.summary: Gulf states are reportedly concerned that President Trump may end the war with Iran without achieving meaningful strategic changes. Sources said uncertainty about how and when Trump would decide to end hostilities is driving anxiety in the region.

stories.title: How US war in Iran is pushing Philippines closer to China
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. suggested the Iran war could push the Philippines and China toward an agreement on disputed energy resources in the South China Sea. Marcos emphasized the need for a "reset" in relations with Beijing as regional states face economic and foreign policy restructuring due to the conflict.

stories.title: Netanyahu keeps balancing between Russia and Ukraine, even as Moscow arms Iran, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy told Axios that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu continues to balance relations between Russia and Ukraine, even as Moscow reportedly shares information about American military positions with Tehran.

stories.title: Israel’s closure of the Holy Sepulchre is proof that no faith is safe from occupation
stories.summary: Israeli authorities closed the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. The Latin Patriarch was later granted access, but critics say the closure reflects broader threats to Palestinian Christian presence under occupation.

stories.title: Pakistan cricketer Fakhar Zaman handed two-match PSL ban for ball tampering
stories.summary: Pakistan cricketer Fakhar Zaman of Lahore Qalandars received a two-match ban from the Pakistan Super League after being found guilty of ball tampering. The offense occurred during a match against Karachi Kings.

stories.title: How China's propaganda is spinning the Iran war
stories.summary: Chinese state media is framing the United States as a destabilizing force in the Middle East amid the Iran conflict. Coverage includes an AI-generated video depicting a Persian cat and an eagle fighting, symbolizing the war.

stories.title: Iran war: Chinese propaganda casts US as reckless aggressor
stories.summary: Chinese state media is framing the United States as a destabilizing force in the Middle East amid the Iran conflict. One AI-generated propaganda video features a Persian cat and an eagle in combat, symbolizing the war.

stories.title: Unrwa chief seeks probe into killing of hundreds of personnel in Gaza war
stories.summary: Outgoing UNRWA Commissioner-General Philippe Lazzarini called for a high-level independent investigation into the killing of more than 390 UNRWA staff during the war in Gaza. He made the announcement at a press conference in Geneva on his final day in the role.

stories.title: Sudan: UN Alarm At Constraints On Humanitarian Access Across Sudan Amid Ongoing Attacks
stories.summary: The UN Secretary-General's office expressed alarm over attacks on civilians and severe constraints on humanitarian access across Sudan. Drone strikes continue to target civilians, and unsafe roads are making aid delivery nearly impossible.

stories.title: Enemy shells Chernihiv region more than 40 times
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled settlements across Ukraine's Chernihiv region 44 times in a 24-hour period, resulting in 66 recorded explosions.

stories.title: Nigeria's foreign minister Tuggar resigns
stories.summary: Nigerian Foreign Minister Yusuf Tuggar resigned, with the departure confirmed in a statement posted on Facebook by his spokesperson on Monday.

stories.title: Trump urges countries seeking oil sto go to Strait of Hormuz and ‘just take it’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump urged countries not involved in the US-Israeli strikes on Iran to buy American oil and go to the Strait of Hormuz to "just take it." Trump singled out Britain and France as unhelpful during the month-long war that has driven up global energy prices and disrupted tanker traffic through the strait.

stories.title: Woman allegedly gang-raped in moving van near Punjab’s Rawat
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman was allegedly gang-raped by four men inside a moving van near Rawat in Punjab, Pakistan. Police have formed special teams to arrest the accused and are conducting the victim's medical examination.

stories.title: ‘Turf him out tomorrow’: Steve Bannon calls to deport Yair Netanyahu to front lines of Iran war
stories.summary: Steve Bannon publicly called for Yair Netanyahu, son of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, to be sent to the front lines of the Iran war. The broader debate about children of leaders serving in conflicts is not new.

stories.title: Trump administration planning international summit on countering antifa violence
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly planning an international summit focused on countering antifa-related violence. Some U.S. officials have raised concerns that the initiative could divert attention from what they consider a more urgent threat posed by Iran-linked terror groups.

stories.title: Iran executes two more convicted of links to banned opposition
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of links to a banned opposition group, found guilty of attempting rebellion through involvement in what authorities described as multiple terrorist acts.

stories.title: Three Indonesian peacekeepers killed by Israeli attacks in Lebanon
stories.summary: Two Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon killed three Indonesian United Nations peacekeepers within a 48-hour period. The incidents drew international attention to the safety of UN personnel in the conflict zone.

stories.title: Russia putting decoy missiles on Shaheds to distract defenders from real ones
stories.summary: Reports indicate Russia is attaching decoy missiles to Shahed-type drones to distract Ukrainian air defenses from real incoming missiles. Ukrainian defenders are now working on methods to distinguish drones carrying genuine threats from those with fake munitions.

stories.title: The US Navy brought a ‘one-of-a-kind’ laser weapon back from the dead
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy has reactivated its sole 150-kilowatt laser weapon system. The directed-energy weapon, described as one-of-a-kind, had previously been taken out of service.

stories.title: South Africa: 'We Have Not Appointed Any King' - Somali Shop-Owners Targeted in Protests Against Nigerians
stories.summary: Somali shop owners in Buffalo City, South Africa, were targeted in protests sparked by the reported "coronation" of an Igbo Nigerian man. Somali business owners denied appointing any community leader, distancing themselves from the controversy.

stories.title: Stratasys selected for multi‑million‑dollar US Department of Defense manufacturing program
stories.summary: Minnesota-based Stratasys was selected for a multi-million-dollar U.S. Department of Defense additive manufacturing program. The company's 3D printing systems are already deployed across aerospace and defense production environments worldwide.

stories.title: At least 16 killed, thousands displaced by gang attack in rural Haiti
stories.summary: An attack by the Gran Grif gang in Haiti's Artibonite region killed at least 16 people and displaced thousands. The gang has previously targeted residents in the rural area.

stories.title: ‘Diplomacy takes time’: Pak envoy reaffirms Islamabad’s commitment to Iran-US peace amid complex situation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ambassador to the US, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, reaffirmed Islamabad's role in facilitating dialogue between the United States and Iran, stressing that the conflicting parties must create prerequisites for negotiations.

stories.title: Iranian rescuers save two civilians from rubble after US-Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Footage showed Iranian Red Crescent Society rescuers and firefighters pulling two civilians from rubble caused by US-Israeli air strikes on Iran. The rescue effort highlighted the ongoing toll of the strikes on civilian areas.

stories.title: Nigeria: 14.3m Nigerians Abusing Drugs - Sardauna Foundation
stories.summary: The Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation reported that approximately 14.3 million Nigerians are abusing drugs, with youths making up a significant proportion. The foundation raised the alarm about the scale of the drug use problem in Nigeria.

stories.title: Could the energy crisis prompt US and China to ‘sit down and work together’?
stories.summary: Amid the Strait of Hormuz energy crisis, a researcher from a Chinese state-affiliated think tank suggested the U.S. and China could cooperate on solutions. Wang Lining said Washington's shift in energy diplomacy was a reminder that Beijing could play a larger role in global governance.

stories.title: Russia slowly trying to splinter its internet from rest of world, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts say Russia is gradually severing its internet from the global network through escalating mobile internet blackouts, traffic restrictions, and growing blocks on Telegram. Activists compare the piecemeal effort to Iran's internet shutdowns, with steep consequences for millions of Russian users.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill five in Gaza Strip, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least five people in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday in two separate attacks. Three were killed in Jabalia in the north and two in Khan Younis in the south, according to medics, despite an ongoing U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

stories.title: Israel’s use of death penalty law on Palestinians to constitute ‘war crime’
stories.summary: Civil society groups and EU officials have condemned Israel's death penalty law targeting Palestinians, with EU voices expressing "great concern." Protests against the legislation took place across the West Bank.

stories.title: Iran warns of death penalty for 'aiding enemies' amid war
stories.summary: Iran announced an enhanced law that could impose the death penalty for espionage, including for individuals who share videos or photos online deemed to aid the country's enemies during wartime.

stories.title: Russian spy ring planning contract murders of military personnel and volunteers foiled in Kyiv and Kyiv region
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Police and Security Service of Ukraine dismantled a Russian-directed spy ring in Kyiv and the surrounding region that was planning contract killings targeting military personnel and volunteers.

stories.title: Airport congestion eases as TSA workers receive backpay but record DHS shutdown drags on – US politics live
stories.summary: TSA workers received partial backpay, easing airport congestion, though a record Department of Homeland Security shutdown continues. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs chair Dan Caine were set to brief on the military campaign in Iran as President Trump described Iran as "decimated."

stories.title: Iran warns of death penalty, asset seizures for spying, aiding enemies
stories.summary: Iran warned that individuals accused of spying or aiding enemies could face the death penalty and asset seizures. Iranian media reported more than 1,000 arrests in one month, targeting people accused of sharing anti-government content or cooperating with adversaries.

stories.title: 8 lightly hurt by cluster bomb in central Israel as Iranian attacks persist across region
stories.summary: A cluster bomb struck central Israel, lightly injuring eight people, as Iranian attacks continued across the region. Separately, the U.S. launched overnight strikes on Iranian ammunition bunkers near Isfahan, and a drone strike set a crude oil tanker ablaze off Dubai.

stories.title: More than 70 miners killed in South Sudan as government and opposition trade blame
stories.summary: More than 70 miners were killed in an attack in South Sudan. Both government and opposition groups have been accused of responsibility for the deadly incident, with each side trading blame.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drones Damage Ust-Luga Port Again
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Ust-Luga Port on Russia's Baltic Sea coast again, part of a series of attacks over the past week aimed at disrupting Russian oil export infrastructure.

stories.title: Kissing a woman's hand can be sexual assault, Spanish court finds
stories.summary: Spain's Supreme Court ruled that kissing a woman's hand without consent can constitute sexual assault, finding a clear sexual component in the defendant's behavior that went beyond harassment.

stories.title: RSF using sexual violence in Sudan's Darfur as 'war weapon': MSF
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders reported that the Rapid Support Forces are using sexual violence as a weapon of war in Sudan's Darfur region. Survivors have frequently identified RSF militias as their attackers.

stories.title: Macron arrives in Japan on visit dominated by economic consequences of Iran war
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Japan on Tuesday for a visit focused on the economic fallout of the Middle East war. France and Japan stated they are prepared to take all necessary measures to ensure global energy market stability.

stories.title: Four soldiers killed in Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced four soldiers were killed in clashes during Israel's ground operation in southern Lebanon. Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered a deeper push toward the Litani River.

stories.title: From Idlib to Downing Street: Ahmed al-Sharaa meets the UK's prime minister
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa visited 10 Downing Street in London for a meeting with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The UK is expected to announce an export finance scheme for British companies seeking business opportunities in Syria.

stories.title: A Complacent America Shrugs Off New War Technologies
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the United States has not adequately grasped the implications of emerging war technologies, including drones and other evolving threats, with complacency observed from senior leadership down to the broader public.

stories.title: China tests ‘world’s heaviest cargo drone’ suited to high-altitude and island operations
stories.summary: China conducted the maiden flight of the Changying-8, described as the world's heaviest multi-terrain cargo drone. Developed by defense contractor Norinco, the CY-8 is capable of short take-off and landing and operations on high-altitude plateaus and island regions.

stories.title: Russia's Putin and Egypt's Sisi discuss Middle East conflict, Tass says
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi held a phone call to discuss the Middle East conflict, according to Russia's Tass news agency. They also discussed large-scale investment projects in energy and industry.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages in five regions due to new attacks
stories.summary: As of the morning of March 31, Russian attacks on Ukraine's power grid left users in five regions without electricity. Ukrenergo noted that cloudy weather was increasing electricity consumption.

stories.title: Falklands heritage trust takes Endurance replica on first UK tour
stories.summary: The Falklands Maritime Heritage Trust is taking a 3D scale replica of Sir Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance on its first UK tour, beginning April 30 at Discovery Point in Dundee, Scotland. The foundation led the 2022 expedition that located the vessel's remains.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nema, IOM Receive 145 Returnees From Libya
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency and the International Organization for Migration received 145 Nigerian returnees from Benghazi, Libya. The returnees arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos.

stories.title: China prosecutes former regulatory official in graft crackdown
stories.summary: Chinese prosecutors have charged Wang Jianjun, former vice chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, with illegally accepting funds and property and abusing his position to benefit others, as part of China's ongoing anti-corruption campaign.

stories.title: Mongolia names new Prime Minister in bid to end legislative deadlock
stories.summary: Mongolia has appointed Uchral, a former Minister of Digital Development and Communications, as its new Prime Minister in an effort to resolve a legislative deadlock. Before his political career, Uchral was publicly known as a hip-hop artist performing under the stage name "Timon."

stories.title: Chatbot aims to help rescuers defuse acute anxiety, right after traumatic events
stories.summary: A team at Ben-Gurion University in Israel developed a free trilingual AI chatbot designed to help rescue workers manage acute anxiety immediately following traumatic events. The tool is intended for use in Israel, the Diaspora, and the Arabian Gulf.

stories.title: Israel halts defense sales to France, citing 'hostile attitude,' sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Israel has halted defense sales to France, citing what sources described as a hostile French attitude toward Israel over the past two years, according to the Jerusalem Post.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE updates: Israel says four soldiers killed in south Lebanon; power outage in parts of Tehran amid attacks
stories.summary: Israel reported four soldiers killed in southern Lebanon amid ongoing hostilities. Separately, parts of Tehran experienced power outages during attacks, while reports indicate President Trump may be willing to end the war even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed.

stories.title: ‘AI helped pick the first thousand targets in Iran’
stories.summary: Reports indicate that artificial intelligence was used to select the first thousand military targets in Iran, though specific details about the system and operators remain limited.

stories.title: Crypto fuels drone purchases in Russia and Iran: Report
stories.summary: A report by blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis found that procurement networks purchasing drones in Russia and Iran are increasingly using cryptocurrency transactions alongside traditional financial channels.

stories.title: Russians attack three districts in Dnipropetrovsk region more than 30 times; two people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kryvyi Rih, Nikopol, and Synelnykove districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 30 times using drones and artillery, injuring two people.

stories.title: More than 200,000 people have left Lebanon for Syria since the start of the war
stories.summary: The UN refugee agency reported that more than 200,000 people, mostly Syrians, crossed from Lebanon into Syria between March 2 and 27 following the escalation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah in early March.

stories.title: Trump sends mixed signals on war plans, hints may abandon Hormuz
stories.summary: Former President Donald Trump sent mixed signals about U.S. war plans regarding Iran. Tehran accused Washington of attempting to divert attention from what it described as an impending ground assault.

stories.title: No deals on mainland China visit, Taiwan’s Premier Cho Jung-tai warns KMT chairwoman
stories.summary: Taiwan's Premier Cho Jung-tai warned KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun against engaging in government-level talks or agreements during her planned visit to mainland China. The visit has caused friction within and between Taiwan's political parties amid heightened cross-strait tensions.

stories.title: Pakistan, seven other countries condemn Israeli curbs on Muslim and Christian worship in occupied Jerusalem
stories.summary: Pakistan and seven other countries — including Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Indonesia, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia — condemned Israeli restrictions on Muslim and Christian worship at holy sites in occupied Jerusalem, imposed since the start of the Israel-US war with Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Ust-Luga burning again: Ukraine is now hitting this Russian oil port every other day — the shadow fleet tankers that load here keep waiting offshore
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Ust-Luga oil port again, with attacks now occurring roughly every other day. Some drones crossed into Estonian airspace, likely deflected by Russian electronic warfare systems. Shadow fleet tankers that load at the port continue waiting offshore.

stories.title: Israeli invasion turns pregnancy into deadly risk in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in Lebanon have put over 13,500 pregnant women at risk, according to reports. Displacement, food shortages, and damage to healthcare infrastructure have made pregnancy increasingly dangerous across the country.

stories.title: Sudan: MSF Report Reveals 3,396 Cases of Sexual Violence Documented in Darfur
stories.summary: A Médecins Sans Frontières report documented 3,396 cases of sexual violence across Darfur, Sudan. The report found widespread and systematic abuse occurring on roads, in fields, and in displacement camps, both in active conflict zones and far from front lines.

stories.title: Why Trump is eyeing Iran’s Kharg Island oil export hub
stories.summary: The article highlights Kharg Island as a critical Iranian oil export facility, serving as the loading point for approximately 90 percent of Iran's crude oil shipments. It has become a focal point as the Trump administration considers targeting Iran's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Céline Dion announces emotional Paris comeback after health battle
stories.summary: French-Canadian singer Céline Dion announced a comeback concert in Paris near the Eiffel Tower following a prolonged health battle. The announcement marks her return to performing after an extended absence from the stage.

stories.title: Al-Aqsa and the Holy Sepulchre: How has Israel undermined the Status Quo?
stories.summary: Israeli forces have again disrupted access to religious sites in Jerusalem's Old City, including al-Aqsa Mosque and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. Rights observers say the longstanding Status Quo governing these sites is being undermined.

stories.title: Eurovision’s first contest in Asia to be held in Bangkok this year
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest announced its first Asia-based competition, Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026, to be held in Bangkok, Thailand. Artists from at least 10 countries have confirmed participation.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth's broker looked to buy defence fund before Iran attack: report
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported that U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's broker sought to purchase a defense fund before the Iran attack. The report did not confirm whether Hegseth knew of the broker's actions, and the Pentagon has demanded a retraction.

stories.title: 3 Chinese ships exit Strait of Hormuz as PetroChina stresses operations stable
stories.summary: Three Chinese ships exited the Strait of Hormuz as state-owned PetroChina assured that its overall operations remain stable. The company noted that only about 10 percent of its total operating volume passes through the strait, though its Middle East investments have been impacted.

stories.title: Shenzhen activates China’s first 10,000-card AI cluster with domestic chips
stories.summary: Shenzhen activated China's first 10,000-card AI computing cluster, built with Huawei's domestically produced Ascend 910C chips. The cluster features a computing capacity of 11,000 petaflops, marking a milestone in China's push for home-grown computing capabilities.

stories.title: US pump prices hit $5 a gallon as Iran war wreaks havoc on global energy supply
stories.summary: U.S. gasoline prices reached $5 per gallon as the Iran war disrupted global energy supplies. This price level was last seen in August 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel to establish buffer zone in south Lebanon up to Litani River, defence minister says
stories.summary: Israel's defense minister announced plans to establish a buffer zone inside southern Lebanon, with Israeli forces maintaining control over the entire area up to the Litani River.

stories.title: After two years, Gaza's families finally reunite with children
stories.summary: Families in Gaza have reunited with children after two years of separation. Children previously evacuated for medical treatment have returned, with parents describing the reunions as profoundly emotional.

stories.title: Drones strike Russia’s Ust-Luga port again as EU officials visit Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Ust-Luga port again while EU officials were visiting Ukraine. Ukraine's air defenses intercepted 267 of 289 drones launched by Russia in an overnight barrage.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes hit pharmaceutical company producing cancer drugs, Iran says
stories.summary: Iran said U.S.-Israeli strikes on Tuesday damaged one of the country's largest pharmaceutical companies, which produces cancer drugs and anesthetics. The Iranian government described the facility as a civilian target.

stories.title: China bans storing cremated remains in empty 'bone ash apartments'
stories.summary: China has banned the practice of storing cremated remains in vacant apartments, known as "bone ash apartments." Mourners had been using these empty residential units as an alternative to cemeteries for housing urns containing ashes of deceased relatives.

stories.title: A Gaza mother waits in agony: Did Israel kill her daughter, or arrest her?
stories.summary: Tahrir Abu Mady, a mother in Gaza, holds a death certificate for her daughter Malak but has found her name on a prisoner list, leaving uncertainty over whether Israeli forces killed or detained her.

stories.title: Sudan: MSF Report Finds No Safe Places for Women and Girls in Darfur
stories.summary: MSF released a report concluding there are no safe places for women and girls in Darfur, Sudan. The organization documented ongoing sexual violence across the region, both in active conflict areas and beyond front lines. Women in Darfur are demanding protection, care, and justice.

stories.title: 'Dumb judges': Trump heckles Supreme Court ahead of pivotal birthright case
stories.summary: President Donald Trump publicly criticized Supreme Court justices ahead of oral arguments in a pivotal case on his 2025 executive order restricting birthright citizenship. Separately, the Financial Times reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth sought investments in defense companies shortly before the US war on Iran.

stories.title: MoD refutes rumors about draft: Details of territorial recruitment center reform to be presented later
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense denied reports that the mobilization process would shift to a new administrative phase on April 1, stating that a comprehensive reform plan for territorial recruitment centers will be announced at a later date.

stories.title: FM Dar departs on brief visit to China for ‘in-depth’ talks on regional developments
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar departed for a one-day visit to China for talks with counterpart Wang Yi. Discussions are expected to focus on developing a framework for a prospective Iran-United States dialogue to end the war.

stories.title: Giant oil tanker off Dubai hit by Iranian strike after Trump's latest threats
stories.summary: Iran struck and set ablaze a fully loaded crude oil tanker off the coast of Dubai. President Trump responded by warning that the U.S. would destroy Iran's energy plants and oil wells if Iran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Police Foil Human Trafficking Ring Linked to Russia War Effort
stories.summary: Four men appeared at the Harare Magistrates' Court in Zimbabwe on charges of trafficking Zimbabweans to Russia. The victims were reportedly coerced into participating in Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: After uprooting Palestinian hamlets, extremist settlers set sights on purge of entire West Bank
stories.summary: Reports indicate that extremist Israeli settlers have escalated violence against Palestinian communities in the West Bank, apparently under cover of the Iran war. Observers describe what appears to be a deliberate campaign to displace Palestinians from the territory.

stories.title: US average fuel price passes $4 a gallon for first time in four years amid Iran war
stories.summary: The US national average fuel price reached $4.02 per gallon, according to AAA data, the highest level since August 2022. Prices have surged from $2.98 just one month ago, driven by disruptions to oil markets caused by the US-led war on Iran.

stories.title: Russia’s Sanctions-Busting Cryptocurrency Empire
stories.summary: A Kremlin-backed financial technology company has been linked to large-scale cryptocurrency transactions used to circumvent international sanctions, facilitating significant trade in dual-use goods that can serve both civilian and military purposes.

stories.title: Inside the EU parliament: the bloc Ukraine wants to join is already fracturing
stories.summary: A Baltic member of the European Parliament discussed Hungary's use of its veto, growing war fatigue across Europe, and deepening fractures within the EU—the very bloc that Ukraine aspires to join.

stories.title: ‘No weapons, no ammunition’: what the European Parliament can actually do for Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Parliament debated how to increase military support for Ukraine despite limitations on directly supplying weapons and ammunition. An Estonian MEP noted it is technically possible to bypass Hungary's objections, though political challenges remain.

stories.title: ‘No kings’ rallies and a growing anti-war sentiment
stories.summary: The article references growing "no kings" rallies and rising anti-war sentiment in the United States, though no additional details were provided in the available text.

stories.title: Italy denies the US military use of its air bases to attack Iran
stories.summary: Italy reportedly denied the United States permission to use its air bases for operations against Iran. Italian press reported that the government refused to authorize U.S. bombers landing at a base in Sicily.

stories.title: US says respects Israel ‘right’ to determine its laws after death penalty for Palestinian attackers
stories.summary: The United States said it respects Israel's sovereign right to set its own laws after the Israeli parliament introduced the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of killings. European nations and rights groups sharply criticized the measure.

stories.title: At 101, Holocaust survivor credits Spielberg for her ongoing fight against hatred
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Ginette Kolinka, now 101, credits Steven Spielberg's foundation for inspiring her to share her experience surviving Auschwitz. After decades of silence, she began speaking publicly following a 1997 interview with the foundation.

stories.title: PA, rights groups denounce death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly terror
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority and human rights groups condemned a new law imposing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. PA President Abbas said it violates international law, while Hamas threatened retaliatory attacks.

stories.title: Iranian plane damaged in U.S. strike ahead of humanitarian mission to India: report
stories.summary: A Mahan Air aircraft was reportedly damaged during a U.S. strike before it was scheduled to carry out a humanitarian mission to India. The plane had been expected to arrive in New Delhi on April 1.

stories.title: Gunmen force delivery driver to take suspected bomb to County Armagh police station
stories.summary: In Lurgan, County Armagh, Northern Ireland, gunmen hijacked a car, placed a suspected bomb inside, and forced the driver to deliver it to a local police station on Monday. Police evacuated approximately 100 homes and carried out a controlled explosion on the device.

stories.title: As US, Israel and Iran continue fighting, question is how to end 'a war of attrition'
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to destroy Iran's Kharg Island and power grid unless Tehran accepted a US peace deal. The threat was followed by fresh US and Israeli strikes, prompting Iranian retaliatory attacks targeting Gulf nations in what observers describe as a war of attrition.

stories.title: Israel prepared to keep striking Iran for 'weeks to come', military spokesperson says
stories.summary: An Israeli military spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Nadav Shoshani, said Israel is prepared to continue strikes on Iran for weeks, citing sufficient targets, munitions, and manpower. Prime Minister Netanyahu stated the war was beyond its halfway point.

stories.title: Nigeria: Exclusive - Former Nigerian Official Facing Corruption Charges Controls Florida Properties
stories.summary: Former Nigerian education official Dibu Ojerinde, along with three sons and a daughter-in-law, faces corruption charges in Nigeria. They are accused of involvement in the misappropriation of funds during Ojerinde's tenure as an education official, with linked properties identified in Florida.

stories.title: EU ministers commemorate Bucha massacre and reaffirm support to Ukraine
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and several EU foreign ministers traveled to Kyiv on Tuesday to commemorate the fourth anniversary of the Bucha massacre and reaffirm support for Ukraine, amid internal bloc tensions over the scale of EU aid.

stories.title: First Thing: Kuwaiti tanker hit by Iranian drone attack in Dubai port
stories.summary: An Iranian drone attack struck a fully loaded Kuwaiti crude oil tanker at Dubai port, damaging the vessel's hull and sparking a fire that was extinguished within hours with no reported injuries. The strike followed President Trump's threat to destroy Iran's energy infrastructure unless it reopened the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Drones attack Ust-Luga Port in Leningrad region again
stories.summary: On the night of March 31, drones attacked Russia's Leningrad region, damaging facilities at the Ust-Luga Port on the Baltic Sea.

stories.title: Canadian national moves LHC for bail
stories.summary: Canadian-Pakistani PhD scholar Hamza Ahmad Khan has petitioned the Lahore High Court for post-arrest bail in a cybercrime case filed by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency under Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act.

stories.title: Iran fires missiles across Middle East as Trump threatens oil hub
stories.summary: Iran launched missile attacks across the Middle East as President Trump threatened Iranian oil infrastructure. Separately, an Iranian parliamentary committee voted to impose tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli drone strikes kill four in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli drone strikes killed four people in southern Lebanon. Two were killed in a strike on a car near Tyre in the al-Wasita al-Qasimiya area, and two others died in a separate raid on Deir Kifa, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: Nigeria: Governor Confirms 28 Killed in Jos Attack
stories.summary: Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang confirmed that 28 people were killed in a gunmen attack on the Angwan Rukuba community in Jos North Local Government Area, Nigeria.

stories.title: Gulf allies privately tell Trump to keep fighting until Iran is decisively defeated
stories.summary: Gulf allies, including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, have privately urged President Trump to continue military operations until Iran's military capabilities and clerical leadership are decisively weakened, arguing it serves the long-term interests of the Gulf region.

stories.title: War update: 140 clashes on front lines, most clashes occurring in Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors
stories.summary: On March 30, Ukrainian Defense Forces recorded 140 combat engagements with Russian forces along the front lines, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Gaza families reunite years after babies evacuated amid Israel’s war
stories.summary: Infants who were evacuated from al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza during Israel's 2023 siege have returned home, reuniting with their families after years of separation.

stories.title: Apple’s accidental AI feature roll-out in China risks regulatory backlash, expert says
stories.summary: Apple accidentally rolled out its Apple Intelligence feature in mainland China before receiving regulatory approval, then quickly pulled it. Experts warned the brief release may have violated Chinese rules on AI security evaluations, algorithm filings, and data protection, potentially exposing Apple to penalties.

stories.title: How emperors and nobles kept warm without down quilts during winter in ancient China
stories.summary: An article explores how ancient Chinese emperors and nobles kept warm during winter before modern heating. Han dynasty rulers used specially designed "Warm Chambers" with walls plastered with mud and Sichuan peppercorns to insulate against cold.

stories.title: Crude prices whipsaw on mixed signals from Iran war
stories.summary: Crude oil prices fluctuated on Tuesday as conflicting signals emerged from the Iran war. President Trump's threat to destroy Iranian energy infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz stayed closed pushed prices up, while subsequent reports of Trump seeking to end the conflict pulled them back down.

stories.title: Eight wounded, cars catch fire in central Israel following strike from Iranian cluster munition
stories.summary: Eight people were wounded in central Israel after an Iranian cluster munition strike. Cars caught fire at impact sites, and emergency services and police responded to multiple locations where shrapnel fell.

stories.title: Champagne in Knesset as Israel passes 'racist' death penalty law
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a death penalty law that international rights groups condemned as discriminatory and racist. Critics warned the legislation institutionalizes the killing of Palestinians under legal cover. Celebrations were reported inside the Knesset.

stories.title: Somalia: U.S. Lawmaker Pushes Somaliland Recognition After Israel Move
stories.summary: A U.S. congressman introduced legislation that could strengthen ties with Somaliland and potentially support future recognition of the self-declared republic. The move follows Israel's similar recognition of Somaliland.

stories.title: East Africa: Somaliland President Discusses Regional Security With Former IGAD Envoy
stories.summary: [Horn Diplomat] Hargeisa -- The President of the Republic of Somaliland, Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi Irro, held a meeting at the Presidential Palace with former Intergovernmental Authority on Develop

stories.title: Lebanon: 3 peacekeepers killed in 24 hours amid Israeli assault
stories.summary: Three Indonesian UNIFIL peacekeepers were killed in two separate incidents in southern Lebanon within 24 hours amid intensified Israeli military operations. The conflict in the area has escalated since March 2.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says drone interception leaves two injured near Riyadh
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's civil defence reported that debris from intercepting a drone in Al-Kharj province, southeast of Riyadh, caused two minor injuries and limited damage to homes and vehicles. Al-Kharj is home to the Prince Sultan airbase.

stories.title: Ukraine's Bucha commemorates four years since massacre
stories.summary: The Ukrainian town of Bucha marked the fourth anniversary of the massacre discovered after Russian forces withdrew in 2022, when hundreds of civilian bodies were found. An EU ministerial delegation visited to commemorate the dead and discuss further support for Ukraine.

stories.title: ‘Iranians don’t consider Trump’s 15-point plan as beginning of diplomacy’
stories.summary: Iranian officials have reportedly rejected former President Trump's 15-point proposal, stating they do not view it as a credible starting point for diplomatic negotiations.

stories.title: India receives first batch of NEGEV 7.62 LMGs from Israel’s IWI
stories.summary: India received its first batch of NEGEV 7.62mm light machine guns from Israel Weapons Industries. The delivery is part of a larger 41,000-unit order signed in August 2024, with 4,000 more units expected later this year.

stories.title: Gaza's evacuated premature babies return to devastated strip
stories.summary: Eleven premature babies who were evacuated from Gaza to Egypt during the early weeks of the conflict have returned to the devastated strip. The children were moved after the hospital caring for them was besieged by the Israeli military, and their families now face deep uncertainty.

stories.title: Kaja Kallas and delegation of EU ministers arrive in Kyiv
stories.summary: EU High Representative Kaja Kallas and a delegation of EU ministers arrived in Kyiv on March 31 to pay tribute to victims of the Russian occupation in Bucha.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US planes involved in attacks on Iran
stories.summary: Spain closed its airspace to US aircraft involved in attacks on Iran, going beyond its earlier refusal to allow use of jointly operated military bases. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has been among the most vocal European critics of the US and Israeli strikes, calling them reckless and illegal.

stories.title: How FPV drones saved two Ukrainian POWs: isolate, strike, evacuate
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces in Zaporizhzhia Oblast coordinated multiple units and FPV drones to isolate, strike, and evacuate two Ukrainian prisoners of war, establishing control of the area before authorizing direct action.

stories.title: Israel military launches investigation after UN peacekeeper deaths in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched an investigation following two separate incidents in southern Lebanon that killed three United Nations peacekeepers.

stories.title: Wolf bites woman in German city shopping area
stories.summary: A wolf bit a woman in a shopping area in Hamburg, Germany, before being pulled from a nearby lake. Authorities believe it was the first such attack since wolves returned to Germany in 1998.

stories.title: EU diplomats mark Bucha massacre anniversary, affirms support for Ukraine
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and foreign ministers from several member states held a commemoration ceremony in Bucha, a Kyiv suburb, marking the fourth anniversary of the massacre. The event occurred amid tensions within the EU over Hungary blocking an aid package for Ukraine.

stories.title: Vital desalination plant in the Gulf become war targets
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened to destroy Iran's desalination plants if peace talks do not progress. Desalination facilities across the Gulf region have become military targets during the month-old war, with Iran, Israel, and the U.S. all targeting this vital civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: US Pentagon says FT report on bid by Hegseth’s broker to buy defence fund before Iran attack ‘false’
stories.summary: The Pentagon's chief spokesman Sean Parnell called the Financial Times report alleging that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's broker sought to buy a defense fund before the Iran attack "entirely false and fabricated."

stories.title: Syria's al-Sharaa visits Germany to discuss refugee return, war and recovery
stories.summary: Syria's interim leader Ahmed al-Sharaa began a visit to Berlin on March 30 for talks on the Middle East war, post-conflict reconstruction, and refugee returns. The trip marks his first visit to Germany and represents a continuation of efforts to build ties with Western countries after years of isolation under Bashar al-Assad.

stories.title: Filipino singer Matty Juniosa’s Golden Buzzer win stokes #SEAblings’ Southeast Asian pride
stories.summary: Filipino singer Matty Juniosa, 27, earned a Golden Buzzer from judge Simon Cowell on Britain's Got Talent after performing Prince's "Purple Rain," sparking Southeast Asian pride under the #SEAblings social media movement.

stories.title: Former Trump advisor joins board of Ukraine-focused drone tech company Powerus
stories.summary: A former Trump advisor has joined the board of Powerus, a Ukraine-focused drone technology company. The move highlights co-production and commercial ties as a potential path forward for Ukraine amid stalled diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Three UN peacekeepers in Lebanon killed in 24 hours
stories.summary: Two Indonesian UN peacekeepers were killed in southern Lebanon on March 30 when an explosion of unknown origin destroyed their vehicle. A third Indonesian peacekeeper had been killed the day before by a projectile of unknown origin, bringing the toll to three peacekeepers in 24 hours amid ongoing Israeli-Hezbollah hostilities.

stories.title: Russian Forces carry out airstrike on Sloviansk overnight: Three people wounded, including child
stories.summary: A Russian airstrike on the city of Sloviansk overnight on March 31 wounded three people, including a child.

stories.title: Sudan: Airstrike On Funeral Underscores Rising Civilian Toll in Sudan
stories.summary: A deadly airstrike struck a funeral gathering in West Kordofan, Sudan, underscoring the rising civilian toll as fighting between rival military factions intensifies and humanitarian access shrinks.

stories.title: Some 20,000 new immigrants have arrived in Israel since last Passover
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 new immigrants arrived in Israel over the past 11 months since Passover. Among them were 4,119 children and teenagers and 2,426 people over 65.

stories.title: At least four killed, nine injured in highway tunnel blast in southwest China
stories.summary: An explosion inside a highway tunnel in southwestern China killed at least four people and injured nine others. Preliminary investigations suggest the blast may have been caused by flammable gas.

stories.title: Hegseth says next days in Iran will be 'decisive' amid strikes
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the coming days of the campaign in Iran would be "decisive" as American and Israeli strikes continued. He added that diplomatic talks to end the war were "gaining strength."

stories.title: Iran cities bombed, as four Israel soldiers killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes continued against Iran, hitting military sites in central Iran, Tehran, and the northwest. Simultaneously, four Israeli soldiers were killed during ground operations in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Donald Trump willing to end war without reopening Strait of Hormuz, says Wall Street Journal
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump is willing to end the Iran war without reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Aides assessed that a mission to reopen the chokepoint would extend the conflict beyond Trump's preferred four-to-six-week timeline.

stories.title: BMA dismisses Starmer’s 48-hour warning over resident doctors’ strike plan – UK politics live
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer threatened to withdraw NHS training posts if resident doctors do not call off a planned strike. The British Medical Association dismissed the 48-hour warning. Separately, Ofgem's energy price cap is set to decrease from £1,758 to £1,641 starting April 1.

stories.title: Condemnation and outrage: Israelis and world react to Israeli death penalty law
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed a law approving the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. The measure drew widespread international condemnation from rights groups and governments who called it discriminatory.

stories.title: 'Felt close to death': Indian seafarers detained in Iran return home
stories.summary: Indian seafarers who had been detained in Iran after their ship was seized in December were released and returned home, with their release order coming just one day before the war began.

stories.title: Sudan war ‘being fought on women’s bodies’: Survivors detail sexual assault
stories.summary: A Doctors Without Borders report describes sexual violence as a defining feature of the war in Sudan, with survivors detailing widespread sexual assault against women throughout the conflict.

stories.title: EU ministers arrive in Ukraine to mark Bucha massacre anniversary – Europe live
stories.summary: EU foreign ministers arrived in Ukraine on Tuesday to mark the fourth anniversary of the Bucha massacre amid the ongoing Iran war. Separately, a joint media investigation alleged that Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó regularly discussed confidential EU sanctions plans with Russian officials.

stories.title: China plans AI-powered smart shipping system by 2027
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Transport and three other government bodies released an action plan to integrate artificial intelligence into the country's shipping industry by 2027. The roadmap includes establishing at least three pilot zones, launching over five trial routes, and developing more than ten replicable smart-shipping use cases.

stories.title: Oil price steadies for now but cost of petrol soars around the world
stories.summary: Global oil prices have stabilized amid signs the US may seek to end its war against Iran, but petrol prices remain elevated worldwide due to ongoing supply chain disruptions linked to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Lebanon bans Hezbollah's military wing, diplomatic official says
stories.summary: Lebanon formally notified the United Nations that it has criminalized Hezbollah's military wing, according to a diplomatic official cited by Al Hadath. Beirut's letter referenced a March 2 government decision banning all military activity by the group.

stories.title: Iran warns of executions, asset seizures for spying or aiding ‘hostile states’
stories.summary: Iran's judiciary warned that sharing photos or videos that could help enemy targeting may be prosecuted as espionage. The spokesman said penalties could include execution and asset seizure, with no leniency for those aiding hostile states.

stories.title: Lonely battles
stories.summary: The article discusses the challenges and risks faced by human rights advocates in Pakistan, both domestically and abroad. Those who raise human rights concerns are frequently accused of being unpatriotic or treacherous.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF kills dozens of Hezbollah terrorists, seizes weapons in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF reported killing dozens of Hezbollah fighters and seizing weapons during operations in southern Lebanon. Forces also detained a suspect observed monitoring Israeli soldiers, who was transferred for interrogation.

stories.title: ‘Our little savior’: partly blind New Mexico dog hailed for warding off bear
stories.summary: A 12-year-old, partially blind dog named Honey in New Mexico fended off a bear that invaded her family's property, protecting dozens of chickens and other animals. Honey was injured during the confrontation but survived.

stories.title: Palestine: In Nablus 'to survive you can’t think about tomorrow'
stories.summary: The city of Nablus in the occupied West Bank faces daily raids and harassment by Israeli forces. Residents describe deepening despair as the 2026 crisis intensifies, though the city remains a center of Palestinian resistance.

stories.title: Russians attack Poltava overnight, killing one and injuring four
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Poltava on the night of March 31 killed one person and injured four others, including two children.

stories.title: How Iran eyes 100pc success
stories.summary: The article discusses how Israel frames Iran as an existential threat to justify military action, while noting growing divisions among American political figures—both Democratic and Republican—over support for the war against Iran.

stories.title: Kuwait says oil tanker hit in Iranian attack at Dubai port;  crew safe
stories.summary: Kuwait's state oil corporation confirmed that its fully loaded tanker Al Salmi was struck by an Iranian attack at Dubai port, warning of a possible oil spill. The crew was reported safe.

stories.title: China, Pakistan to 'strengthen' cooperation on Iran, Beijing says
stories.summary: China and Pakistan announced plans to strengthen cooperation on the Iran situation during meetings in Beijing. Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning described the two nations as "all-weather" strategic partners working toward peace.

stories.title: UK aviation regulator rejects Heathrow’s plans to significantly raise landing fees
stories.summary: The UK Civil Aviation Authority partially rejected Heathrow Airport's plans to significantly raise landing fees to fund a multi-billion-pound upgrade. The regulator ruled the average charge per passenger should rise only from £28.40 to £28.80 between 2027 and 2031, after airlines warned steep increases would be passed on to passengers.

stories.title: Gas supply to Quetta, other parts of Balochistan suspended
stories.summary: Unidentified armed men blew up an 18-inch main gas pipeline in the Akhtarabad area on the outskirts of Quetta, Balochistan, on Monday night. The explosion disrupted gas supply to the provincial capital and several districts.

stories.title: Air defense downs 267 of 289 drones in overnight Russian attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 267 of 289 drones launched by Russian forces in an overnight attack beginning on the evening of March 30.

stories.title: Iran executes two men convicted of attack on government building, judiciary news outlet says
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of links to the Mujahideen-e Khalq Organisation for involvement in attacks including firing launcher weapons at a government building. Two other men connected to the same opposition group were executed the previous day.

stories.title: Coalition to advance ultra-Orthodox draft exemption bill after pause due to Iran war
stories.summary: Israel's Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee chair Bismuth announced that work on legislation granting ultra-Orthodox draft exemptions would resume after the Iran war ends. The pause came after the IDF chief warned the cabinet about worsening manpower shortages.

stories.title: Three Chinese ships pass through Strait of Hormuz, Chinese ministry says
stories.summary: Three Chinese ships recently transited the Strait of Hormuz, China's foreign ministry confirmed. Spokeswoman Mao Ning expressed gratitude to parties that assisted the vessels' passage through the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Iran sent Russia weapons to kill Ukrainians. Now it’s complaining to the UN that Ukraine is teaching their targets to shoot back
stories.summary: Iran sent a letter to the United Nations accusing Ukraine of providing material and operational support to a US-Israeli war effort, while omitting its own years-long supply of weapons to Russia for use against Ukrainian civilians.

stories.title: Panama Canal sees boost in traffic after Iran war breaks out
stories.summary: The Panama Canal has experienced increased vessel traffic following the outbreak of the Iran war as shipping routes shift. However, a canal official warned that the current rate of approximately 40 daily transits is not sustainable long-term.

stories.title: Malian army denies releasing jihadists to end fuel convoy attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military denied allegations that it released approximately 200 suspected jihadists in mid-March to secure an end to attacks on fuel convoys that have been disrupting the landlocked country's economy.

stories.title: Diplomatic push
stories.summary: Islamabad hosted foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Türkiye over the weekend as regional diplomatic efforts intensified to find a peaceful solution to the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The conflict has entered its second month, with Gulf states caught in the crossfire and the global economy suffering significant disruptions.

stories.title: Man injured in drone attack in Odesa
stories.summary: On the morning of March 31, a Russian attack drone struck the balcony of a third-floor apartment in Odesa, injuring one man.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes damage religious site in Iran's northwest, state media says
stories.summary: US-Israeli air strikes damaged a religious site in the city of Zanjan in northwestern Iran, according to the Fars news agency. Parts of the dome and minarets of the Husseiniya Azam were reported damaged.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Holy sites remain closed as deadly violence spreads
stories.summary: Israeli settlers carried out attacks in the occupied West Bank while authorities in East Jerusalem pursued evictions and closed holy sites. The violence spread across Palestinian territories as Israeli forces tightened control.

stories.title: In age of US-China rivalry, supply chain statecraft counts
stories.summary: An analysis argues that geopolitical competition between the United States and China has shifted from traditional territorial and military dimensions to control over global supply chains. The infrastructure of globalization itself—rather than just the arena it provides—has become a central object of strategic rivalry.

stories.title: Video: Newborns evacuated from Gaza return as toddlers over two years later
stories.summary: A group of children evacuated from Gaza as newborns in 2023 returned over two years later as toddlers, reuniting with their families in emotional scenes.

stories.title: Somali army takes over key city in Southwest as state leader resigns
stories.summary: The Somali federal army took control of the key city of Baidoa in Southwest State after the regional leader resigned. The federal government welcomed the transition and called for peace and unity amid political tensions.

stories.title: Egypt turns to Libya for oil as Iran war chokes Gulf supplies
stories.summary: Egypt secured an agreement with Libya to receive two oil shipments per month, each containing approximately 1.2 million barrels of crude. The deal aims to offset supply disruptions caused by the war on Iran affecting Gulf exports.

stories.title: What does Saudi Arabia want from the Iran war? Will it join the fray?
stories.summary: The article examines Saudi Arabia's strategic interests in the Iran war, noting that Riyadh views itself as the Arab world's economic and political leader and considers Iran a key regional rival.

stories.title: Rescue operations continue in Tehran, Zanjan, Iranian Red Crescent says
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society launched rescue operations in Tehran and the northwestern city of Zanjan following US-Israeli strikes. Injured individuals in Tehran were transferred to hospitals, while relief teams responded to damage at Zanjan's Husseiniya Azam.

stories.title: Grooming gangs inquiry to examine role of ethnicity, culture and religion
stories.summary: A new UK statutory inquiry into grooming gangs will directly examine whether ethnicity, culture, or religion influenced offending and shaped institutional responses in England and Wales. The terms of reference have been published and will be laid before parliament when it returns from recess on April 13.

stories.title: Four soldiers killed, 2 wounded in south Lebanon clash with Hezbollah
stories.summary: Four Israeli soldiers — Captain Noam Madmoni, Staff Sergeants Ben Cohen, Maxsim Entis, and Gilad Harel — were killed and two wounded in a clash with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. The IDF said it captured a Hezbollah operative who had been surveilling troops.

stories.title: Six wounded in Israel following Iranian missile fire
stories.summary: Six people were lightly wounded in Petah Tikva, Israel, after Iran fired ballistic missiles, according to emergency medical services. Impact sites were also reported in Tel Aviv and Bnei Brak in central Israel.

stories.title: Woman allegedly gang-raped in moving van near Rawat
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman was allegedly gang-raped by four men inside a moving van near Rawat in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Police have formed special teams and are conducting raids to arrest the accused.

stories.title: World Bank develops roadmap to modernise wheat sector in Pakistan
stories.summary: The World Bank has developed a roadmap to modernize Pakistan's wheat sector, recommending interventions in five priority areas. The plan aims to stimulate private investment, close yield gaps through better seed systems and water management, and empower smallholder farmers.

stories.title: Daily Quiz: On refugees who sought asylum
stories.summary: A daily quiz references the Dalai Lama's 1959 flight from Tibet to India, where he sought political asylum. The quiz covers other historical refugees who sought asylum in various countries.

stories.title: Dalai Lama warns 'violence begets violence', urges peace in Mideast
stories.summary: The Dalai Lama issued a letter urging peace in the Middle East and Ukraine, warning that violence only leads to more conflict. He called for dialogue and diplomacy as the foundation for lasting resolution.

stories.title: Japan has enough plutonium to make 5,500 nuclear warheads, PLA Daily says
stories.summary: China's PLA Daily published a rare full-page report accusing Japan of "dangerously expanding" its defense industry and crossing a red line. The military newspaper claimed Japan possessed 44.4 tonnes of separated plutonium by the end of 2024, enough to produce approximately 5,500 nuclear warheads.

stories.title: Russian forces lose 970 troops and one air defense system in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported that Russian forces lost 970 troops and one air defense system in the past 24 hours. Total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,297,670 personnel.

stories.title: Safety risks disrupt global aviation amid many wars
stories.summary: Europe's top aviation safety regulator warned that ongoing wars, including the month-old conflict involving Iran, are squeezing global flight corridors and increasing risks from drones. The oil shock from the Middle East conflict is also expected to widen the gap between strong and struggling airlines.

stories.title: Food price rises unlikely before summer, says boss of Sainsbury’s
stories.summary: Sainsbury's CEO Simon Roberts said UK food prices are unlikely to rise before summer and that Easter shopping will be unaffected by the Middle East conflict. He noted it was too early to predict when higher commodity costs might reach supermarket shelves, citing long-term supplier agreements that help protect shoppers.

stories.title: US amphibious assault ship with 1,800 Marines deployed to Indian Ocean
stories.summary: The USS Tripoli, a US amphibious assault ship carrying approximately 1,800 Marines from the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit, is operating in the Indian Ocean. US Central Command confirmed the deployment amid speculation about a possible ground operation against Iran.

stories.title: The U.S. Military Risks Letting Contractors Define How It Sees the Battlefield
stories.summary: An analysis warns that the U.S. military risks ceding control of battlefield intelligence interpretation to private contractors. The piece draws parallels to the film Dr. Strangelove to illustrate dangers of delegating critical command-and-control decisions.

stories.title: The U.S. Military Risks Letting Contractors Define How It Sees the Battlefield
stories.summary: An analysis warns that the U.S. military risks allowing defense contractors to shape how it perceives and interprets the battlefield. The piece draws parallels to institutional control issues, arguing for greater military oversight of the digital tools and platforms that inform operational decision-making.

stories.title: The U.S. Military Risks Letting Contractors Define How It Sees the Battlefield
stories.summary: An analysis warns that the U.S. military risks allowing private contractors to shape how it perceives and interprets the battlefield. The piece draws parallels to the 1964 film Dr. Strangelove to illustrate dangers of delegating critical decision-making authority away from proper command structures.

stories.title: Malaysia raises 2026 growth forecast despite Iran war risks
stories.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia raised its 2026 growth forecast to between 4 and 5 percent, up from the government's earlier 4 to 4.5 percent target. The upgrade reflects stronger-than-expected economic momentum and resilient domestic demand, despite risks stemming from the ongoing Iran war.

stories.title: Iran war wipes $120bn off Dubai, Abu Dhabi stock markets
stories.summary: Stock markets in Dubai and Abu Dhabi lost a combined $120 billion in value due to fallout from the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, making the UAE's financial markets among the hardest hit globally.

stories.title: Iran says it shot down MQ-9 drone near Isfahan
stories.summary: Iran claimed its air defence units shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone near Isfahan, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Iranian officials said it was the 146th drone intercepted during the conflict.

stories.title: Japan deploys long-range missiles to 2 bases amid China tensions, irking locals
stories.summary: Japan's defense ministry announced the deployment of long-range counterstrike missiles at Camp Kengun in Kumamoto prefecture and Camp Fuji in Shizuoka prefecture. The deployment marks a departure from Japan's exclusively defense-oriented policy under its pacifist constitution amid rising tensions with China. Local residents have expressed opposition to the move.

stories.title: Security forces kill 10 terrorists after ‘brief school seizure’ in Bara
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed 10 Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan militants in Bara, Khyber district, after the group briefly seized a government school in the Akkakhel area and hoisted their flag. The operation concluded within hours.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 32 of US-Israel attacks?
stories.summary: On day 32 of US-Israeli strikes on Iran, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Al Jazeera in an exclusive interview that American war objectives would be achieved within weeks.

stories.title: UK decries ‘baseless’ spy charge as Russia expels diplomat
stories.summary: Russia expelled British diplomat Albertus Gerhardus Janse van Rensburg on espionage charges, which Britain dismissed as "complete nonsense." London accused the Kremlin of orchestrating an intimidation campaign against British embassy staff in Moscow.

stories.title: Algeria's former president Liamine Zeroual laid to rest with military honours
stories.summary: Former Algerian President Liamine Zeroual, an 84-year-old retired general, was buried with full military honors in his hometown of Batna on Monday.

stories.title: US says Cuba policy unchanged despite allowing Russian tanker
stories.summary: The White House stated that US policy toward Cuba remains unchanged despite allowing a sanctioned Russian oil tanker to operate. No further details on the reasoning behind the exception were provided.

stories.title: Attack on Iran’s Mahallat kills eleven people
stories.summary: An air strike on the city of Mahallat in Iran's Markazi province killed 11 people and injured 15 others. Three residential units were directly hit by projectiles, causing significant damage, according to Iran's Isna news agency.

stories.title: Israel says four soldiers killed as army pushes deeper into south Lebanon
stories.summary: Four Israeli soldiers were killed as the army pushed deeper into southern Lebanon. Hezbollah has been attempting to make the ground invasion costly for Israeli forces as they continue their advance.

stories.title: After Pope’s remarks, White House defends praying for US troops
stories.summary: The White House defended praying for U.S. troops after Pope Leo XIV warned that God rejects the prayers "of those who wage war."

stories.title: Drone attack in Poltava region kills one, injures three including child
stories.summary: One person was killed and three others, including a child, were injured when debris from a Russian drone fell in Ukraine's Poltava region.

stories.title: Russian attacks kill two, injure dozens
stories.summary: Russian attacks on central and northern Ukrainian regions on Monday killed two people and injured more than 20, according to regional officials.

stories.title: The Trump Administration Had No Plan for the War with Iran
stories.summary: A U.S. legislator with Marine infantry experience in Iraq's Anbar province argues against the war with Iran, contending that the Trump administration entered the conflict without an adequate plan. The piece is part of a War on the Rocks series featuring opposing viewpoints from legislators with military backgrounds.

stories.title: The Trump Administration Had No Plan for the War with Iran
stories.summary: A War on the Rocks article by a legislator with military experience argues against the U.S. war with Iran, drawing on the author's service as a Marine infantryman in Anbar province, Iraq, 21 years ago. The piece contends the Trump administration entered the conflict without an adequate plan.

stories.title: Ukraine attacks on oil and gas to be ‘painful’ for Russian economy: Official
stories.summary: EU Defense and Space Commissioner Andrius Kubilius, speaking to Breaking Defense during a European "missile tour" to Sweden, said Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil and gas infrastructure will be "painful" for the Russian economy. The comments came as an EU official highlighted the strategic impact of targeting Russia's energy sector.

stories.title: Three scenarios for the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Analysts have outlined three possible scenarios for the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran conflict, including two military options and one diplomatic pathway. Pakistan is identified as playing a crucial mediating role.

stories.title: Provinces to share oil subsidy burden under NFC formula
stories.summary: Pakistan's provinces agreed to share the burden of oil subsidies amid global economic disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict.
