President Zardari and Prime Minister Sharif chaired high-level meetings that also included austerity measures such as grounding 60 percent of official vehicles.

stories.title: Trump issues new warning to Tehran, Iran calls US peace proposals ‘unrealistic’
stories.summary: President Trump issued a new warning to Tehran over Iran's continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iranian officials dismissed U.S. peace proposals as "unrealistic." Oil prices are set for a record rise amid the ongoing tensions.

stories.title: South Korean president promises maximum response to energy crisis
stories.summary: South Korean President Myung pledged a maximum response to the energy crisis triggered by the war on Iran, vowing to address fuel supply disruptions to the fullest extent possible.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s Exco approves plans for elevated mass transit system in Kai Tak
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Executive Council approved plans for an elevated smart mass transit railway system in the Kai Tak area. The system will connect the cruise terminal and other major facilities to the local MTR station. The proposal was gazetted in July of the previous year following public consultations.

stories.title: How Israel is waging war on bearing witness in Lebanon
stories.summary: Three journalists were killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon, continuing a pattern of targeting media workers previously documented in Gaza. The killings prompted protests in Beirut against attacks on press freedom.

stories.title: The Cost of Hesitation: Why “Finishing the Mission” is Imperative in Iran
stories.summary: A U.S. legislator with Air Force medical evacuation experience argues for continuing military operations against Iran, framing it as imperative to "finish the mission." The article is part of a War on the Rocks series presenting for-and-against perspectives on the Iran war from legislators with military backgrounds.

stories.title: The Cost of Hesitation: Why “Finishing the Mission” is Imperative in Iran
stories.summary: A War on the Rocks article by a legislator and former Air Force medical crew director argues for continuing U.S. military operations in Iran, framing hesitation as costly. The author draws on combat experience in the Middle East to advocate for completing the mission.

stories.title: Strikes in central Iran hit 'military sites', Iranian media reports
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that initial investigations indicated US-Israeli strikes hit military sites in Isfahan in central Iran. A security official at the Isfahan governor's office confirmed the targeting but said the full extent of damage and casualties remained unclear.

stories.title: Sexual violence part of 'everyday life' in parts of Sudan, charity says
stories.summary: A charity reported that sexual violence has become part of everyday life in parts of Sudan, with victims describing being targeted while carrying out routine daily activities.

stories.title: Video: Bishop Joseph Strickland says Gaza genocide ‘holocaust of our time’
stories.summary: Bishop Joseph Strickland, speaking to Tucker Carlson, described Israel's actions in Gaza as a "holocaust of our time." He also addressed the removal of Carrie Prejean Boller from a Trump administration religious freedom commission for criticizing US support for Israel.

stories.title: Auto sector moves ahead amid uncertainty
stories.summary: Atlas Honda Ltd announced a Rs5.3 billion investment to expand motorcycle operations in Pakistan, while Lucky Motor Corporation partnered with a Chinese company. The moves come amid business uncertainty driven by the ongoing Middle East war.

stories.title: Meta, Tiktok and Google under investigation for allegedly disobeying Australia’s social media ban
stories.summary: The Australian government has accused Meta, TikTok, and Google of failing to comply with the country's ban on social media use by under-16s. A survey of 900 parents found that nearly 70% of children who previously had accounts on platforms like Instagram, Snapchat, or TikTok maintained access after the ban took effect.

stories.title: After backing Iran with Israel strike, Houthis avoid further escalation, for now
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels joined the Iran conflict by striking Israel but have avoided further escalation, reportedly due to fears of retaliation. The group continues to threaten Red Sea shipping lanes and potential attacks on Gulf states.

stories.title: US hits 'ammunition bunkers' near Isfahan, explosions seen in footage
stories.summary: The US military struck what were described as Iranian ammunition bunkers near Isfahan overnight, with footage showing large secondary explosions. President Trump shared clips on Truth Social, though details could not be independently verified.

stories.title: Gulf allies privately pushing Trump to keep up war until Iran decisively defeated
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and the UAE are privately urging the Trump administration to continue the war against Iran until its nuclear capabilities and proxy support networks are eliminated. Oman and Qatar, by contrast, favor diplomatic negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill one in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed one person and destroyed homes in multiple areas of Nabatieh in southern Lebanon overnight. The victim was identified as Shadi Hassan Moallem, and heavy bombardment destroyed the Al-Rous neighbourhood in Doueir.

stories.title: Europe urged to ‘learn to fight for itself’ in case US-China truce collapses
stories.summary: The European Union is being urged to develop contingency plans in case the fragile US-China trade truce, sealed in October, collapses or expires. A breakdown could expose the EU to Chinese export controls on rare earths, potentially undermining European military support for Ukraine and its own defense efforts.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi outlines current stage of army organizational reform
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi outlined the current stage of the Ukrainian Army's organizational reform, stating that restructuring of the military command is now in its second phase.

stories.title: Iran pushing Houthis on Red Sea shipping, officials say
stories.summary: European officials reported that Iran is pushing Yemen's Houthi militants to target shipping in the Red Sea and near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, a move that could severely disrupt global energy markets.

stories.title: After the Iran war, how fast could global trade recover?
stories.summary: Analysts are assessing how quickly global supply chains for energy, fertilizer, and other goods could recover once the Strait of Hormuz reopens following the end of the Iran war.

stories.title: Drone attack sparks fire on Kuwaiti tanker in UAE amid Iran’s Gulf attacks
stories.summary: A drone attack set fire to a Kuwaiti oil tanker in the UAE as part of broader Iranian-linked strikes across the Gulf. Dubai authorities said the blaze was contained with no oil leakage or injuries reported.

stories.title: Fuelling up: the new ‘obsession’ drawing Singaporeans to Malaysia’s Johor
stories.summary: Singaporeans are increasingly crossing into Johor, Malaysia, to purchase cheaper fuel as petrol prices in the city-state have surged due to the Middle East conflict. RON95 petrol in Singapore costs nearly three times the Malaysian price at S$3.41 per litre, though Singapore vehicles may only purchase unsubsidised RON97 fuel in Malaysia.

stories.title: Melbourne girl, 13, allegedly shouted antisemitic remarks, threw eggs and swerved car towards Jewish families
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl in Melbourne has been charged with 52 offences, including allegedly shouting antisemitic remarks, throwing eggs, and swerving a stolen car toward Jewish families in the suburb of Ripponlea. Victorian police said the families narrowly escaped being struck by the vehicle. Two other girls were also allegedly involved.

stories.title: Japan seeks French backing as Macron begins Asia trip in Iran war’s shadow
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is beginning a three-day visit to Tokyo, where Japan is seeking European solidarity amid a crisis in the Strait of Hormuz that has driven up oil prices. The visit comes as Japan navigates a diplomatic falling-out with Beijing. Macron will subsequently travel to South Korea.

stories.title: No oil leakage after Iranian attack on Kuwaiti oil tanker, Dubai media office says
stories.summary: Dubai authorities confirmed that firefighters extinguished a fire on a fully loaded Kuwaiti oil tanker hit in an Iranian attack in Dubai waters. Officials said there was no oil leakage and no injuries were reported.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi: Russians drop 200–300 guided bombs on Ukraine daily
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi reported that Russian military aircraft conduct 70 to 90 strikes on Ukraine daily, deploying between 200 and 300 guided bombs per day.

stories.title: Four soldiers killed, two wounded while fighting in southern Lebanon, IDF confirms
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed four soldiers were killed and two wounded during fighting in southern Lebanon. Three of the fallen were identified as Captain Noam Madmoni, Staff Sergeant Ben Cohen, and Staff Sergeant Maxsim Entis.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Iran war goals achieved ‘beyond halfway point’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed that the war goals against Iran have been achieved "beyond halfway," but he did not provide a timeline for when the conflict would end.

stories.title: Eurovision Song Contest launches first-ever Asia edition
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest announced its first-ever Asia edition, with broadcasters from 10 countries, including South Korea and the Philippines, set to participate.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief elected vice-president, edging closer to becoming president
stories.summary: Myanmar's junta chief Min Aung Hlaing, who led the 2021 coup, was elected vice-president by the lower house of parliament on Tuesday. A second vice-president was elected from a military-aligned party, and a third will be chosen by the military. A parliamentary vote to select the president from among the three is expected later this week.

stories.title: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scores 15-ball fifty for Rajasthan Royals
stories.summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored a half-century off just 15 balls for the Rajasthan Royals in the IPL, his third fifty in the tournament, as Rajasthan defeated the Chennai Super Kings.

stories.title: Gulf allies want Trump to prolong US bombardment of Iran, officials say
stories.summary: Gulf allies led by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are urging U.S. President Donald Trump to continue military operations against Iran, arguing that Tehran has not been sufficiently weakened by the month-long bombing campaign. Gulf states had privately complained about insufficient advance notice of the initial US-Israeli attack.

stories.title: Multiple explosions, airstrikes knock out power in Tehran
stories.summary: Multiple explosions and airstrikes struck Tehran on Tuesday, causing power outages across parts of the Iranian capital. Residents reported hearing airstrikes followed by thundering explosions, with power being knocked out intermittently since Sunday before authorities managed partial restoration in some neighborhoods.

stories.title: Iran war 'shock' is dimming outlook for many economies, IMF says
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that the war in Iran is causing asymmetric economic shocks globally, dimming the outlook for many economies and tightening financial conditions.

stories.title: When faith meets security: Understanding the Palm Sunday incident amid the Iran war - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial addressed the diplomatic tensions surrounding the closure of Jerusalem holy sites on Palm Sunday amid the ongoing Iran war, noting that wartime security restrictions affected access.

stories.title: What can nations do to make up for the ongoing energy shortfall?
stories.summary: The Middle East conflict has disrupted roughly 20 percent of the world's fuel supply, prompting nations globally to scramble for alternative energy sources to address the shortfall.

stories.title: China influencer amasses over 1 million followers in 2 weeks by sharing how to rent a home tips
stories.summary: A Chinese influencer known as Gulumao, based in Xiamen, Fujian province, gained over one million followers in two weeks by posting practical tutorials on how to rent a home. Born in the 1990s, he became one of the fastest-growing creators on a major platform in early 2025.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed five drones in recent hours. The Israeli military reported four soldiers killed in combat with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. Thousands of Iranians marched in Karaj in support of their government and military.

stories.title: Seizing Kharg Island would risk US troops and may not end Iran war, experts say
stories.summary: Military experts warned that a US operation to seize Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal would risk American troops and might not end the war. Tehran could retaliate by mining the Strait of Hormuz and escalating drone strikes.

stories.title: Attack on Michigan synagogue was Hezbollah-inspired ‘act of terrorism’, FBI says
stories.summary: The FBI classified an attack on a synagogue in Michigan as a Hezbollah-inspired "act of terrorism." The suspect, Ayman Ghazali, had consumed pro-Hezbollah ideology prior to carrying out the attack.

stories.title: Attack on Michigan synagogue was Hezbollah-inspired 'act of terrorism,' FBI says
stories.summary: The FBI declared the March attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Michigan — the state's largest Jewish temple — an act of terrorism inspired by the Iran-backed group Hezbollah.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran attacks tanker in Dubai; explosions in Tehran and Jerusalem amid wave of strikes
stories.summary: Iran launched strikes across the Middle East, including an attack on a tanker in Dubai and explosions reported in Tehran and Jerusalem. Kuwait reported a fire on a giant tanker following an Iranian strike at Dubai port; Dubai authorities later confirmed no oil had leaked. US President Trump threatened to destroy Iran's energy grid if a ceasefire is not reached soon.

stories.title: Nadim Houry warns: Israel is no longer just fighting Hezbollah, 'it’s waging war on Lebanon'
stories.summary: Analyst Nadim Houry argued that Israel's current military operations in Lebanon extend beyond fighting Hezbollah and constitute a broader war on Lebanon. He described the conflict as reflecting decades of unresolved tensions and a reconfiguration of Lebanese state sovereignty and strategic options.

stories.title: Tuesday briefing: How to make sense of England’s local elections campaigns
stories.summary: Voters in England will cast ballots in local elections on 7 May, the same day Scotland and Wales hold government elections. Labour under Prime Minister Keir Starmer is expected to face a difficult result, with Nigel Farage's Reform UK, the Green Party, and Plaid Cymru anticipated to make gains.

stories.title: Trump said to tell aides he’s willing to end Iran war without reopening Hormuz
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported President Trump told aides he is willing to end the Iran war without reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's decision-making has reportedly been complicated by the killing of its leadership, hindering potential talks.

stories.title: Indonesia urges respect for international law after peacekeepers killed
stories.summary: Indonesia called on all warring parties in the Middle East to respect international humanitarian law after three Indonesian UN peacekeepers were killed in Lebanon.

stories.title: Wave of bomb threats in Ukraine: Police investigate over half of anonymous reports
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Police reported receiving 1,216 anonymous bomb threats on March 30 targeting state authorities, schools, businesses, and other institutions. Investigators have so far examined 56 percent of the reports.

stories.title: Namibia: U.S. Embassy Warns Namibians of Travel Bans for Visa Overstays
stories.summary: The U.S. Embassy in Namibia issued a warning to Namibian travelers that overstaying visas in the United States can result in travel bans, visa ineligibility, and possible criminal charges.

stories.title: Rubio says US hopeful in private talks after ‘fractures’ in Iran’s leadership
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that internal fractures have emerged within Iran's leadership. He expressed hope that figures with the authority to negotiate and deliver outcomes would assume control, suggesting ongoing private diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Nigeria: Bandits Kill 13, Abduct Several Wedding Guests in Kaduna
stories.summary: Armed bandits attacked a wedding gathering in Nigeria's Kaduna state, killing 13 people and abducting several guests. The attackers arrived in large numbers carrying sophisticated weapons and opened fire on attendees.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tuggar Resigns As Nigeria's Foreign Affairs Minister
stories.summary: Nigeria's Foreign Affairs Minister Yusuf Tuggar resigned from his position. President Bola Tinubu had directed ministers and political appointees intending to contest the 2027 elections to step down from their current roles.

stories.title: Egypt's President al-Sisi calls on Donald Trump to end the war on Iran
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi publicly urged U.S. President Donald Trump to help end the ongoing war involving Iran, now in its second month. The call reflects growing regional pressure for a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s Energy Emergency Begins
stories.summary: The Philippines has experienced one of the world's sharpest increases in petrol prices amid a broader energy crisis affecting Southeast Asia.

stories.title: More drilling in North Sea ‘not the answer’ for UK energy security, say former military leaders
stories.summary: Former UK military leaders argued that increased North Sea drilling would not improve British energy security, citing global supply chain chokepoint vulnerabilities. They urged the government to accelerate a transition to wind, solar, tidal, and nuclear energy, alongside grid modernization and energy efficiency measures.

stories.title: Mozambique: Navy Linked to Killing of Fishermen
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that Mozambique's navy has been linked to the killing of fishermen in conflict-affected areas. The organization called on authorities to adopt protective measures and ensure justice for civilians.

stories.title: South Africa: Government Calls for Calm After Kugompo Erupts Over Crowning of Nigerian 'Igbo King'
stories.summary: A protest erupted in KuGompo (formerly East London), South Africa, over the alleged coronation of a Nigerian 'Igbo king.' The demonstration turned violent, with cars torched, shops looted, and foreign nationals targeted. The South African government called for calm.

stories.title: China to ban storing remains of dead in ‘bone ash apartments’
stories.summary: China is introducing legislation to ban the storage of cremated remains in residential apartments, a practice that has grown as rapid urbanization and an aging population have made cemetery plots scarce and expensive. The new law will also prohibit unauthorized burials and tomb construction outside public cemeteries.

stories.title: Allies sent Ukraine ‘signals’ on reducing strikes on Russian oil, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky revealed that allied nations sent signals urging Ukraine to reduce strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Zelensky said Ukraine is prepared to reciprocate if Russia ceases its attacks on Ukraine's energy system.

stories.title: Breaking Defense announces Breaking Defense Europe, a new, distinct, European edition
stories.summary: Breaking Defense announced the launch of Breaking Defense Europe, a distinct European edition of the defense news outlet, set to debut in early May. Tim Martin and Elisabeth Gosselin-Malo will serve as co-editors.

stories.title: Children in Gaza reenact a funeral procession during play
stories.summary: Children in a Gaza displacement camp were filmed reenacting a funeral procession using a doll during play, reflecting the impact of ongoing conflict on daily life in the territory.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US warplanes involved in war on Iran
stories.summary: Spain denied US warplanes access to its airspace, distancing itself from the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Lithuania plans to create counter-mobility zone along its border with Belarus and Russia
stories.summary: Lithuania's Ministry of Defense proposed establishing a counter-mobility strip along its borders with Belarus and Russia. The plan includes adding 23 engineering counter-mobility parks by the end of 2030.

stories.title: US may reassess Nato ties after Iran war ends, Rubio says
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington may reassess its relationship with NATO after the Iran war, citing what he called the alliance's disappointing lack of support. President Trump previously accused NATO partners of being "cowards" and called the bloc a "paper tiger."

stories.title: Bin bag panic grips South Korea as huge Iran war crisis budget agreed
stories.summary: South Koreans in Seoul panic-bought mandatory pay-as-you-throw bin bags at nearly five times normal volumes, fearing shortages of the naphtha-based products as the Iran war strains global oil supplies. The crisis prompted the government to agree on a large emergency budget.

stories.title: Survey: Most American Jews oppose unconditional aid to Israel
stories.summary: A J Street–commissioned poll found that only 31% of American Jews support unconditional US aid to Israel, while 44% favor conditioning aid on compliance with US law. Sixty percent of respondents opposed US military action against Iran.

stories.title: Outrage and condemnation over Israel’s death penalty law for Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed legislation legalizing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks, drawing widespread international condemnation.

stories.title: CNN: Pentagon to hold first Iran war briefing in weeks
stories.summary: The Pentagon scheduled its first press briefing on the Iran war in nearly two weeks, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine set to speak. Only six briefings have been held since strikes began on February 28.

stories.title: Sanctioned Russian-flagged oil tanker closes in on Cuban port of Matanzas
stories.summary: A sanctioned Russian-flagged oil tanker approached the Cuban port of Matanzas on March 30, according to ship tracking data. The delivery offers relief to Cuba, whose economy has stalled under a de facto oil blockade imposed by Washington.

stories.title: US may ‘re-examine’ NATO’s merit after Iran war snub, Rubio says
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized NATO members for refusing access to military bases for operations related to the Iran conflict. Rubio warned that the United States may re-examine NATO's value in light of the alliance's refusal.

stories.title: Shrapnel damage causes power cuts in Tehran, local media reports
stories.summary: Power outages hit parts of Tehran after shrapnel damaged an electrical substation in the eastern part of the city, according to Iran's Fars news agency. Repair teams were dispatched to restore service.

stories.title: Drone debris damages homes in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Falling debris from a downed drone damaged six homes in Saudi Arabia's al-Kharj province, according to the Saudi Civil Defence. No injuries were reported, and authorities did not identify the drone's origin.

stories.title: Fire extinguished on Kuwaiti tanker hit by Iranian attack in Dubai waters
stories.summary: Firefighters extinguished a blaze on a Kuwaiti oil tanker struck by an Iranian attack in waters near Dubai. The incident is one of several recent assaults on merchant vessels in the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Lawmaker says Australia broke rules deploying troops to UAE
stories.summary: Australian Greens Senator David Shoebridge accused the government of breaching parliamentary oversight rules by deploying troops to the United Arab Emirates without required briefings to both houses of Parliament.

stories.title: Japan PM’s fawning sparks backlash, Philippines’ work-life balance fails: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faced domestic backlash after White House footage showed her behaving in what critics called a sycophantic manner during a visit with President Trump. The article was part of a weekly roundup of Asia-focused stories.

stories.title: Kuwaiti tanker hit by Iranian drone attack in Dubai port
stories.summary: An Iranian drone strike hit the Kuwaiti-flagged Al Salmi tanker, a fully loaded crude oil vessel, at Dubai port, damaging its hull and causing a fire. Dubai authorities said the fire was extinguished early Tuesday and all crew members were safe. The attack is the latest on merchant shipping in the Gulf amid the US-Israel war with Iran.

stories.title: US-based dissident artist put on trial in China over satirical Mao sculptures, says rights group
stories.summary: New York-based Chinese dissident artist Gao Zhen, known for satirical sculptures of Mao Zedong, has been tried in China on charges of "defaming national heroes and martyrs," according to his wife and rights groups. Gao, 69, was detained in 2024 during a family visit to China and faces up to three years in prison.

stories.title: Over 47,000 cabbies adopt Octopus, card readers ahead of e-payment deadline
stories.summary: More than 47,000 taxi drivers in Hong Kong have adopted the commercial Octopus app or installed mobile card readers ahead of new electronic payment regulations taking effect on Wednesday. The new rules require cab drivers to offer at least two e-payment options as part of a government effort to modernize the taxi industry.

stories.title: Trump tells aides he is willing to end Iran war without reopening Hormuz, WSJ reports
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump told aides he is willing to end the Iran war without reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Other military options are being considered but are not his immediate priority.

stories.title: Iraq’s Uniquely Fraught Position in the Iran War
stories.summary: Iraq occupies a precarious position in the Iran conflict, with its northern Kurdistan Region reportedly being struck by both sides in the fighting.

stories.title: Perth man accused of attempted terror attack at Invasion Day rally to plead mental health defence
stories.summary: Lawyers for Liam Alexander Hall, 32, accused of attempting to bomb an Invasion Day rally in Perth, have indicated a possible not guilty by insanity defence. Hall is receiving treatment at Western Australia's most secure psychiatric facility. His court appearance before magistrate Matthew Walton was adjourned until May.

stories.title: Starmer’s immigration rhetoric follows familiar pattern of bold claims but few results, expert says
stories.summary: Madeleine Sumption, director of the University of Oxford's Migration Observatory, said Prime Minister Keir Starmer's pledge to "smash the gangs" behind Channel crossings mirrors the pattern of previous Conservative governments using bold rhetoric on immigration with limited deliverable results.

stories.title: China and Kenya partner to finish ‘most consequential’ rail project
stories.summary: Kenya has revived construction of its stalled Standard Gauge Railway extension in partnership with Chinese firms China Communications Construction Company and China Road and Bridge Corporation. The two remaining sections are estimated to cost US$5.4 billion, financed through renegotiated loan terms with China.

stories.title: Oil tops $114 a barrel as Iran conflict drives record monthly surge
stories.summary: Brent crude oil surpassed $114 per barrel, reaching its highest level since July 2022, driven by the Iran conflict. Oil prices surged roughly 55 percent in March, marking the largest monthly gain since the Brent contract's inception in 1988.

stories.title: US Defense Secretary Hegseth's broker looked to buy defense fund before Iran attack, FT reports
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's Morgan Stanley broker contacted BlackRock in February about a multimillion-dollar defense fund investment. The Pentagon called the report entirely false and fabricated.

stories.title: White House ballroom project to include ‘massive’ military complex
stories.summary: The White House has announced plans for an 8,360-square-meter ballroom that will include a "massive" military complex, replacing the East Wing, which President Trump ordered demolished in October.

stories.title: Fedorov: Private air defense system already operational, initial results discussed
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Mykhailo Fedorov announced that a pilot project involving private-sector participation in Ukraine's air defense system is already operational and producing initial results.

stories.title: Alleged Mossad spy escapes Hezbollah detention thanks to IDF strike in Beirut — report
stories.summary: A suspect allegedly working for Israel's Mossad escaped Hezbollah detention in Beirut after an IDF strike damaged the building where he was held. Lebanon is demanding Ukraine hand over the individual, who reportedly fled to the Ukrainian embassy in Beirut.

stories.title: US doubts Iranian negotiators’ power to approve agreement, CNN reports
stories.summary: US officials expressed doubt that Iranian negotiators involved in indirect talks have the authority to approve or implement a potential agreement, CNN reported. Iranian officials were said to distrust the US due to previous diplomatic failures.

stories.title: Tai Po fire hearing: management company unaware of alarm system shutdown notice
stories.summary: A public hearing into a deadly fire at Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court housing estate revealed that the management company was unaware of a notice to shut down the fire alarm system. The inquiry is in its sixth day, focusing on the alarm deactivation and its consequences.

stories.title: Asian markets fall, oil prices surge amid supply disruptions
stories.summary: Asian stock markets fell as the US-Israeli war on Iran weighed on global sentiment. Oil prices surged, with US benchmark West Texas Intermediate crossing $100 per barrel for the first time since the conflict began, reaching $103.99.

stories.title: WSJ: Trump open to ending Iran war despite Hormuz closure
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Donald Trump told aides he is willing to end the US military campaign against Iran even if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, deferring efforts to reopen the waterway.

stories.title: Report: US carried out major airstrike on Isfahan depot
stories.summary: The United States carried out a large-scale airstrike on a major ammunition depot in Isfahan, Iran, targeting a facility storing munitions including armour-piercing weapons, The Wall Street Journal reported.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says Middle East visit a success, announces accords
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared his Middle East tour a success on March 30, announcing that several security cooperation accords had been finalized or were under discussion with regional partners.

stories.title: Fire on Kuwaiti oil tanker put out, Dubai authorities say
stories.summary: Dubai authorities said firefighters extinguished a blaze on the Kuwaiti oil tanker Al Salmi in Dubai waters following an attack. Response teams continued to assess the situation, with no further details on damage or environmental impact provided.

stories.title: US says Israel free to set laws after death penalty act for Palestinians passed
stories.summary: The United States said it respects Israel's sovereign right to set its own laws after the Israeli parliament approved legislation allowing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks.

stories.title: Three UN peacekeepers killed in Lebanon as Israeli strikes pummel south
stories.summary: Three UN peacekeepers from the UNIFIL mission were killed in southern Lebanon within 24 hours. Two died in an explosion on Monday and a third was killed in a separate blast the previous day. UNIFIL monitors hostilities along the demarcation line with Israel.

stories.title: Trump posts video of explosions amid reported Tehran strikes
stories.summary: President Donald Trump posted a 31-second video on Truth Social showing large explosions amid reports of new strikes on Tehran. Trump did not specify the time or location of the footage.

stories.title: Iran pressuring Houthis to attack Red Sea ships, European officials say
stories.summary: European officials say Iran is pressuring Yemen's Houthi militants to prepare a renewed campaign against Red Sea shipping in the event of further U.S. escalation. Houthi leaders are reportedly weighing more aggressive action after previously launching ballistic missiles at Israel.

stories.title: Iraqi paramilitary says bases hit in US-Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces said US-Israeli airstrikes hit two of its bases—the 45th Brigade in Babil province's Jurf al-Nasr area and the 31st Brigade site in Anbar province's al-Karma. The group said it remains in a high state of readiness.

stories.title: Four soldiers killed, 2 wounded in south Lebanon clash with Hezbollah — IDF
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed four soldiers were killed and two wounded in a clash with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. The IDF identified three of the fallen: Captain Noam Madmoni, Staff Sergeant Ben Cohen, and Staff Sergeant Maxsim Entis.

stories.title: War with Iran casts a shadow as Persian Jews mark Nowruz in New York City
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran cast a shadow over Nowruz celebrations among Persian Jews in New York City. Iranians in the diaspora expressed tentative hope for change, while concern grew for the estimated thousands of Jews still living in Iran.

stories.title: What do Trump’s threats to bomb Iran desalination plants mean for rest of Mideast?
stories.summary: Analysts warned that US threats to bomb Iranian desalination plants could prompt Tehran to retaliate against Gulf states, which depend on desalination for the vast majority of their water supply.

stories.title: Russian agent arrested in Khmelnytskyi for planning to blow up military cars
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service arrested a Russian Federal Security Service agent in the city of Khmelnytskyi. The suspect was planning to blow up vehicles belonging to the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

stories.title: How Pakistan won over Trump to become an unlikely mediator in the Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as an unexpected mediator in the Iran conflict, successfully positioning itself as an intermediary between the United States and Iran. The article examines how Pakistan built credibility with the Trump administration to assume this diplomatic role.

stories.title: Pentagon denies that Hegseth’s broker sought investment before Iran war
stories.summary: The US Department of Defense demanded a retraction of a report alleging that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's broker sought a multimillion-dollar investment before the Iran war, calling the story false.

stories.title: Gulf States pressure Trump to continue war with Iran until fall of Islamic regime - report
stories.summary: Israeli and Gulf officials reported that Gulf states are pressuring President Trump to continue the war with Iran until the Islamic regime falls, believing Iran has not yet been weakened enough to cease being a regional threat.

stories.title: White House says no change in Cuba policy after Russian tanker waiver
stories.summary: The White House stated on March 30 that U.S. policy toward Cuba has not changed despite granting a waiver allowing a sanctioned Russian tanker to deliver fuel to the island. Officials cited humanitarian reasons and said future decisions would be handled on a case-by-case basis.

stories.title: 3 UN observers killed within 24 hours in south Lebanon; IDF says it’s investigating
stories.summary: Three UN observers were killed within 24 hours in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military said it is investigating whether IDF or Hezbollah fire was responsible. Separately, the IDF killed three senior Hezbollah operatives in a strike on Beirut's southern suburbs.

stories.title: California Republican sheriff halts inquiry into alleged voter fraud in Prop 50 election
stories.summary: Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco halted an investigation into alleged voter fraud related to California's Proposition 50 election after seizing approximately 650,000 ballots. The probe had drawn opposition from the state attorney general. Bianco, a prominent Trump supporter, is also a leading Republican candidate for California governor.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Iran fires fresh round of missiles, four Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Iran launched a fresh round of missiles across the Middle East on Tuesday, defying US President Trump's threat to destroy Iranian energy infrastructure unless Tehran accepts a ceasefire. Separately, four Israeli soldiers were killed in clashes with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, according to the Israeli military.

stories.title: Hezbollah, Israel give conflicting accounts of Haifa oil refinery fire
stories.summary: A fire broke out at an oil refinery in Haifa Bay after a strike. Hezbollah claimed responsibility via a rocket attack, while Israeli officials attributed the blaze to debris from an intercepted missile. Authorities said the fire was quickly contained.

stories.title: Chinese flight bookings rise by 20% ahead of April holiday break despite soaring airfares
stories.summary: Flight bookings in China rose 20 percent year-on-year ahead of the Ching Ming Festival holiday, reaching 2.04 million tickets despite higher airfares driven by rising fuel prices. Cross-border bookings also increased.

stories.title: School shooting in Argentina leaves one dead, eight wounded
stories.summary: A 15-year-old student opened fire at a school in Argentina, killing one person and wounding eight others. Authorities said the shooter had no criminal record and was reportedly experiencing a difficult family situation.

stories.title: Trump interested in calling on Arab states to help pay for Iran war, White House says
stories.summary: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that President Trump is interested in asking Arab states to help finance the war in Iran. Leavitt acknowledged it is an idea Trump has been considering.

stories.title: Fearing economic collapse after war, Iran cracks down on dissent
stories.summary: One month into its war with the United States and Israel, Iran is intensifying a crackdown on domestic dissent to prevent unrest amid fears of economic collapse. Security forces have carried out arrests and executions, deployed massively in the streets, and recruited children to staff checkpoints.

stories.title: US Democratic Senator says US 'badly and embarrassingly losing this war'
stories.summary: US Democratic Senator Chris Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said the United States is "badly and embarrassingly losing" the war against Iran and called for an immediate end to the US-Israel military operation.

stories.title: Bus driver arrested in Hong Kong after crashing into stationary taxi, killing 2
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested a 49-year-old Long Win Bus driver on suspicion of dangerous driving causing death after his double-decker bus struck a stationary taxi on the Tsing Yi section of Lantau Link. A 66-year-old taxi driver and his 37-year-old passenger were killed.

stories.title: IRGC navy commander to be buried in Abadan, Fars news reports
stories.summary: IRGC navy commander Admiral Alireza Tangsiri, killed in an Israeli strike, will be buried in Abadan, Khuzestan province, on Friday, according to Iran's Fars news agency.

stories.title: London criticizes Russia’s decision to expel British diplomat
stories.summary: The British Foreign Office criticized Russia's decision to expel a British diplomat accused of espionage. London rejected the spying allegations leveled by Russia's FSB security service.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: allies asked Kyiv about reducing attacks on Russian energy sector, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed that allied nations asked Kyiv to consider reducing strikes on Russia's oil and broader energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy said he is open to scaling back such attacks if Moscow reciprocates with similar restraint. The statement came on day 1,496 of the war.

stories.title: Report: Hegseth’s broker sought to buy defence fund investment before Iran attack
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported that a Morgan Stanley broker for US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth sought a multimillion-dollar investment in BlackRock's Defence Industrials Active ETF in February, shortly before the US-Israeli attack on Iran began.

stories.title: Dubai’s loss could be Hong Kong’s gain, but only if city is ready
stories.summary: InvestHK's director general Alpha Lau stated that companies previously using Dubai as a regional hub have largely shifted to Hong Kong following the outbreak of the Iran war. The article cautions Hong Kong against treating the geopolitical disruption as a guaranteed strategic advantage.

stories.title: Ron DeSantis signs bill renaming Palm Beach airport after Donald Trump
stories.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill renaming Palm Beach International Airport after President Donald Trump. The facility would become the President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The renaming is the latest in a series of buildings, warships, institutions, and currency bearing the president's name.

stories.title: Intense US-Israeli attacks on Iranian city of Isfahan cause column of fire
stories.summary: Witnesses in Isfahan, Iran—a city of 2.3 million—captured footage of intense US-Israeli airstrikes that produced large columns of fire over the city.

stories.title: Mexican president announces ‘protest actions’ after migrant dies in US custody
stories.summary: Mexico's president announced 'protest actions' after another Mexican migrant died in U.S. custody. The death brings the total number of Mexicans who have died in U.S. custody or during immigration raids to fourteen.

stories.title: Argentine microsatellite to fly on NASA's Artemis 2 Moon mission
stories.summary: An Argentine-designed microsatellite will fly as a secondary payload on NASA's crewed Artemis 2 Moon mission, launching from Kennedy Space Center. Argentina is the only Latin American country selected and one of four globally, alongside Germany, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea.

stories.title: Thousands of US Army paratroopers arrive in Middle East as buildup intensifies
stories.summary: Thousands of U.S. Army paratroopers from Fort Bragg, North Carolina, have arrived in the Middle East as the American military buildup in the region continues to intensify. They join thousands of additional forces already deployed to the area.

stories.title: Knife-wielding man shot by Hong Kong police dies after 10 days in critical condition
stories.summary: A 43-year-old knife-wielding man, surnamed Chung and suspected of having mental illness, died at Hong Kong's Princess Margaret Hospital after being shot twice by police in Kwai Chung on March 21. He had been in critical condition for 10 days.

stories.title: Netanyahu: 'Only long-term solution for Hormuz crisis is rerouting pipes to Mediterranean'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told Newsmax that the long-term solution to the Hormuz crisis involves rerouting energy pipelines westward across Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea and Mediterranean, bypassing Iran's geographic chokepoint.

stories.title: NASA begins countdown for first crewed Moon mission in over 50 years
stories.summary: NASA began the countdown for the Artemis 2 mission at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, with liftoff targeted for Wednesday, April 1. The mission will be the first crewed flight toward the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.

stories.title: Zelensky: Putin helping Iran, yet Netanyahu wants to ‘balance’ between Russia and Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky accused Russia of providing Iran with intelligence and criticized Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu for seeking to balance between Russia and Ukraine. Zelensky said he showed Arab leaders proof of Moscow's support for Tehran.

stories.title: Names and games: Taipei hits back over ‘China’ label, but will it pay off?
stories.summary: Taiwan has pushed back against South Korea, Denmark, and Cameroon after those countries relabeled Taiwan as part of China in official systems handling visas, residence permits, and conference credentials. Taipei has taken retaliatory measures, though questions remain about their effectiveness.

stories.title: Chinese mum leaves son, 6, in hotel room for more than 2 weeks; staff act as carers
stories.summary: A six-year-old boy was left alone in a hotel in Zhengzhou, Henan province, for more than two weeks after his 25-year-old mother stopped returning and left no contact information. Hotel staff stepped in to care for the child.

stories.title: Fast bowler Naseem Shah slapped with Rs20m fine after social media post about Punjab CM Maryam
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board fined fast bowler Naseem Shah Rs20 million for breaching his central contract after he posted critical remarks on social media about Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz during the Pakistan Super League.

stories.title: Israeli mothers mourn together after their sons survived the battlefield but not their wounds
stories.summary: The OneFamily organization hosts a bereavement support program for Israeli mothers whose sons died after surviving battlefield injuries. More than a dozen women, aged early 40s to late 70s, participate, including one whose son was killed at the Nova music festival.

stories.title: At least 16 dead, 10 injured in Haiti town, police says
stories.summary: At least 16 people were killed and 10 injured in an attack in Petite-Rivière, located in Haiti's Artibonite region, police in Port-au-Prince reported on Monday. The violence is linked to an ongoing conflict involving the Gran Grif gang.

stories.title: Israel passes law making death penalty default sentence for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law making the death penalty the default sentence for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks against Israelis.

stories.title: Owner of oil tanker seized by Trump administration seeks to block sale
stories.summary: The owner of an oil tanker seized by the Trump administration is seeking a court order to block the vessel's sale. The case highlights the logistical and legal challenges governments face when seizing assets that are costly to maintain and difficult to dispose of.

stories.title: Kuwaiti oil tanker was hit in Iranian attack at Dubai port, alerts raised for possible oil spill
stories.summary: A Kuwaiti oil tanker was struck in a drone attack at the port of Dubai, which authorities linked to Iran's broader military operations. Dubai authorities confirmed maritime firefighting teams were working to control the resulting fire, and alerts were raised over a possible oil spill.

stories.title: Lahore Qalandars imposes ‘voluntary’ fine of Rs1m on captain Shaheen Afridi over security protocol breach
stories.summary: Pakistan Super League franchise Lahore Qalandars imposed a Rs1 million fine on captain Shaheen Shah Afridi for a security protocol breach. The team said the incident arose from a misunderstanding rather than a deliberate violation.

stories.title: Israel passes law making death penalty default sentence for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset voted 62-48 to pass legislation making the death penalty a default sentence for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks in military court. The bill was spearheaded by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir and has drawn sharp international criticism.

stories.title: Africa: Meeks, Jacobs Lead Warning to Rubio Not to End Lifesaving Assistance to 7 African Countries
stories.summary: U.S. Representatives Gregory Meeks and Sara Jacobs led a group of House Democrats in warning Secretary of State Rubio against ending lifesaving assistance to seven African nations: Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Malawi, Mali, Niger, Somalia, and Zimbabwe. They argued the cuts would put millions of lives at risk.

stories.title: At least 70 killed, 30 wounded in Haiti gang attack, rights group says
stories.summary: The Haitian rights group Defenseurs Plus reported at least 70 people killed and 30 wounded in a gang attack in Haiti, far exceeding official estimates of 16 dead.

stories.title: Al Jazeera’s full interview with Marco Rubio on US war on Iran
stories.summary: In an exclusive Al Jazeera interview, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the objectives of the war on Iran would be achieved within weeks.

stories.title: Japan’s wartime past weighs on growing military role in Philippines
stories.summary: Japanese combat troops are set to participate in military exercises in the Philippines next month, marking their first return to Philippine soil since 1945. Some Filipino survivors, activists, and historians have raised concerns about Japan's unresolved wartime legacy, including the lack of a formal state apology.

stories.title: Iran war live: Kuwaiti oil tanker hit in Dubai port; 3 UN soldiers killed
stories.summary: A Kuwaiti oil tanker was struck in Dubai's port and three UN soldiers were killed in Lebanon as Iran retaliated against US-Israeli raids with attacks on Gulf nations. Saudi, Qatari, and Jordanian leaders convened amid the escalation.

stories.title: War update: 120 clashes on front lines, 65 Russian troops eliminated on Pokrovsk axis
stories.summary: On March 30, Ukrainian forces reported 120 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front lines. The Pokrovsk sector saw the heaviest fighting, with 24 Russian attacks and 65 Russian soldiers reportedly eliminated.

stories.title: US formally reopens Caracas embassy as ties with Venezuela warm
stories.summary: The United States formally reopened its embassy in Caracas, Venezuela, on March 30, with the State Department describing it as a new chapter in diplomatic relations. The move comes less than three months after U.S. forces seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a raid on the capital.

stories.title: India planning false flag operation using Pakistani prisoners: security sources
stories.summary: Pakistani security sources alleged that India is planning a false flag operation using Pakistani prisoners, including Kashmiris, who are currently held in Indian jails after inadvertently crossing the border.

stories.title: Ukraine denounces Iran's claims of 'complicity' in US-led war as lies
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry rejected claims by Iran's UN representative Amir Saeid Iravani that Ukraine assisted the US and Israel by sending UAV specialists to Middle Eastern countries, calling the accusations false.

stories.title: New York councilmember and Hochul governor aide investigated for bribery
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors are investigating whether New York City Councilmember Farah Louis, a Brooklyn Democrat, and her sister Debbie Louis, an aide to Governor Kathy Hochul, accepted bribes or kickbacks tied to city funds allocated to a migrant shelter provider. A search warrant dated 19 March was obtained by the Associated Press.

stories.title: Russia overhauls vaccine production after cattle disease triggers mass culling
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on March 30 overhauling animal vaccine production following a cattle disease outbreak in a Siberian region. The outbreak led to mass culling of livestock, a measure that proved deeply unpopular among local populations.

stories.title: Michigan synagogue attack was Hezbollah-inspired terrorism, FBI confirms
stories.summary: The FBI confirmed that the March 12 attack on a synagogue in the Detroit, Michigan, area was Hezbollah-inspired terrorism. Ayman Ghalazi, 41, loaded his truck with fireworks and rammed it into the region's largest synagogue around midday.

stories.title: Huge fires at Russian oil facilities following Ukraine strikes, satellite images show
stories.summary: Satellite imagery analyzed by BBC Verify shows large fires at three Russian oil export facilities near the Baltic Sea following Ukrainian strikes. The damage targeted key infrastructure involved in Russia's oil exports.

stories.title: Chinese coffee brands need more than low prices to compete with global players: analysts
stories.summary: Analysts say Chinese coffee brands seeking overseas expansion must move beyond low-price strategies and develop stronger global brand identities. Experts noted that overseas consumers primarily associate Chinese brands with cost performance rather than quality or innovation.

stories.title: US raises concern over Israel’s closure of Jerusalem holy sites
stories.summary: The White House said the United States raised concerns with Israel over the closure of holy sites in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces to focus on strategic defense and counteroffensives on 'weak' fronts –Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced that Ukraine will focus on strategic defense operations to contain Russian advances in 2026 while pursuing counteroffensives on weaker sections of the front line.

stories.title: Iran war is dimming outlook for many economies, IMF says
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund has warned that the war involving Iran is dimming economic outlooks globally, causing an asymmetric shock across economies and leading to tighter financial conditions worldwide.

stories.title: Iranian Parliament mulls possible exit from nuclear treaty
stories.summary: Iran's parliament is considering a possible withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty amid the ongoing conflict. Iran maintains its nuclear program is peaceful and asserts its right to nuclear enrichment under the NPT.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign ministry rejects US ceasefire demands
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman rejected US ceasefire conditions, describing them as excessive, unrealistic, and unreasonable.

stories.title: White House ballroom project to include 'massive' military complex
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump revealed plans for a large military complex beneath a new White House ballroom that will replace the East Wing. Trump displayed a rendering of the project to reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday.

stories.title: Sybiha: Ukraine receives requests from partners on maritime security and strait unblocking
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said international partners have approached Ukraine for cooperation on maritime security, including potential efforts to unblock the Strait of Hormuz, drawing on Ukraine's experience with the Black Sea grain corridor.

stories.title: Taylor Swift sued for trademark infringement over Life of a Showgirl album title
stories.summary: Las Vegas performer Maren Wade sued Taylor Swift for trademark infringement, alleging that Swift's album "The Life of a Showgirl" creates confusion with Wade's long-running "Confessions of a Showgirl" stage show. Universal Music Group was also named as a defendant.

stories.title: NASA starts countdown for first crewed Moon mission in over 50 years
stories.summary: NASA began a two-day countdown Monday for the Artemis 2 mission, its first crewed lunar flight in over 50 years, targeting a Wednesday launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The four-astronaut crew includes the first woman, person of colour, and non-American assigned to a Moon mission. The flight will orbit the Moon and test the Space Launch System rocket.

stories.title: Rain, storms kill 45 people in Afghanistan and Pakistan
stories.summary: Severe rain and storms across Afghanistan and Pakistan have killed at least 45 people. Officials in central and eastern Afghanistan reported the closure of several highways, with additional rainfall and storms forecast for March 31.

stories.title: Somali national army takes control of part of biggest city in South West state
stories.summary: Somalia's national army has taken control of part of the largest city in South West state, according to local residents on March 30. The move comes two weeks after South West state officials announced they were severing ties with the federal government in Mogadishu.

stories.title: Why most Jewish Israelis back the death penalty for terrorists - analysis
stories.summary: A majority of Jewish Israelis support the death penalty for those convicted of terrorism, according to polling analysis. However, many simultaneously doubt that capital punishment would serve as an effective deterrent against future attacks.

stories.title: Ukraine tests next-generation bomber drones with longer range, secure communication
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry tested a new generation of bomber drones at the Brave1 training ground, featuring extended range and improved secure communications capabilities.

stories.title: Turkey says NATO defences downed fourth inbound Iranian missile
stories.summary: Turkey's defence ministry reported on March 30 that a ballistic missile launched from Iran entered Turkish airspace before being intercepted by NATO air and missile defence systems deployed in the eastern Mediterranean. It was the fourth inbound Iranian missile shot down by NATO defences.

stories.title: Russia ‘glad’ oil cargo reached its ally Cuba amid U.S. blockade
stories.summary: Russia expressed satisfaction that an oil shipment successfully reached its ally Cuba despite the U.S. blockade. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Moscow and Washington had been in communication regarding the delivery.

stories.title: Iran’s Islamic republic will ‘collapse internally’, says Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated his belief that Iran's Islamic republic will eventually "collapse internally" but said regime change is not the stated objective of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign. He said current operations focus on degrading Iran's military, missile, and nuclear capabilities.

stories.title: Facing a resurgent Hezbollah, Israel slouches back to a security zone in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces have established an extended presence in southern Lebanon amid renewed clashes with Hezbollah, drawing comparisons to Israel's previous 18-year security zone in the country. Israeli leaders have spoken of an indefinite stay in a new buffer zone.

stories.title: Key moments from Marco Rubio’s interview with Al Jazeera
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio gave an exclusive interview to Al Jazeera's Hashem Ahelbarra discussing the ongoing war on Iran.

stories.title: Petition targets newly passed death penalty law, calling it discriminatory, unconstitutional
stories.summary: A rights group petitioned Israel's High Court to immediately freeze the newly passed death penalty law, arguing it is discriminatory and unconstitutional. Additional legal challenges are expected.

stories.title: War Diary Day 31: Economic shockwaves deepen in absence of diplomatic off-ramps to Iran war
stories.summary: On day 31 of the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes continued targeting Iranian military, energy, and civilian infrastructure. The conflict's economic shockwaves deepened amid a high-intensity, multi-domain phase with no diplomatic off-ramps in sight.

stories.title: France holding five in custody after foiled Bank of America bombing
stories.summary: French authorities are holding five suspects in custody following a foiled bombing plot targeting Bank of America's offices in Paris. Officials have linked the planned attack to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: France arrests two more suspects on Bank of America's foiled attack
stories.summary: French anti-terrorism prosecutors announced on March 30 that two additional suspects were arrested in connection with a foiled attack on Bank of America's Paris offices. The arrests bring the total number of people detained over the plot to five.

stories.title: Zelensky on security cooperation with Gulf countries: New requests from Bahrain, Oman
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced historic security agreements with Gulf states, including Bahrain and Oman, covering areas such as air defense strengthening and defense industry development.

stories.title: The architect of Iran’s military survival remains defiant
stories.summary: Ahmad Vahidi, a senior Iranian military figure well known to Israel and Western governments, has emerged as a prominent face of Iran's defiant military posture amid ongoing conflict, favoring confrontation over pragmatic diplomacy.

stories.title: Is a peaceful settlement possible in Iran?
stories.summary: Pakistan announced its readiness to host negotiations aimed at ending the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: US says Trump ‘interested’ in asking Arab countries to pay for war on Iran
stories.summary: White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt said President Donald Trump is interested in asking Arab countries to help cover the costs of the war on Iran.

stories.title: US used new ballistic missile in strike that killed teens in Iran sports hall: Report
stories.summary: A report indicates the US military used a new Precision Strike Missile in a strike that hit a sports hall in Lamerd, Iran, killing teenagers. Damage at the site was found to be consistent with the weapon type.

stories.title: Mexican immigrant died in US immigration custody, ICE says, marking 14 deaths in 2026
stories.summary: A Mexican immigrant died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody, marking the 14th such death in 2026. ICE detention numbers have reached record levels, with approximately 68,000 people held as of early February.

stories.title: FBI: Armed man who rammed pickup into Michigan synagogue was inspired by Hezbollah
stories.summary: The FBI said Ayman Ghazali, who rammed a pickup truck into Temple Israel synagogue in Michigan while a preschool was in session, was inspired by Hezbollah. He reportedly declared in a video his intent to kill as many people as possible.

stories.title: Watch: ‘Mr. President, please help us stop the war’: Egyptian President’s plea to Donald Trump
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi publicly appealed to U.S. President Donald Trump to help end the ongoing war in the Middle East during a recorded address.

stories.title: Islamabad businessman succumbs to injuries after being shot during dacoity at farmhouse
stories.summary: Prominent Islamabad businessman Amir Awan was fatally shot during an armed robbery at his farmhouse in the Orchard Scheme area. CCTV footage showed five gunmen armed with submachine guns and wearing bulletproof vests.

stories.title: Long queues in Myanmar as Iran war fuel crisis deepens
stories.summary: Myanmar is experiencing a fuel crisis linked to the ongoing Iran war, with drivers queuing for hours at petrol stations. The conflict's disruption of global energy supplies has sent shockwaves across fuel-importing nations.

stories.title: Defense sources: Trump Hormuz, nuke decisions determine war's end, Israel giving US intel on Strait
stories.summary: Israeli defense sources indicated that decisions by President Trump regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program will determine when the war ends. Sources expressed skepticism that Iran would accept a deal in the coming week, with Israel providing the US intelligence on the Strait situation.

stories.title: Europe’s crisis tourism: how the Iran war swallowed the EU’s geopolitical agenda
stories.summary: In the wake of US and Israeli strikes on Iran, European leaders responded with divergent positions. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz both voiced support for regime change, while questioning the international rules-based order.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces liberate 480 sq km on Oleksandrivka axis – CinC Syrskyi
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Ukrainian forces have liberated 480 square kilometers of territory along the Oleksandrivka axis.

stories.title: Gas pipeline blown up in southern Pakistan by unknown assailants, says official
stories.summary: Unknown assailants blew up a gas pipeline in southern Pakistan, according to officials. The attack disrupted gas supply to several parts of the city and at least five additional districts in the region.

stories.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran’s Kharg Island oil hub if no deal reached
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub and other critical infrastructure unless Tehran agrees to a deal to end the U.S.-Israeli war. The threat rattled global energy markets and raised fears of broader conflict, with Iran signaling potential retaliation near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Born in the USA? China targeted in America’s birthright citizenship fight
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court is set to hear arguments on birthright citizenship, with Chinese nationals at the center of disputed claims. President Trump has framed the issue around alleged abuse of the policy by foreign nationals.

stories.title: Spain denies U.S. permission to use its airspace for ‘illegal’ war on Iran
stories.summary: Spain denied the United States permission to use its airspace for military operations against Iran. Madrid also barred U.S. forces from using jointly operated military bases on Spanish territory, with Defence Minister calling the war 'profoundly illegal and unjust.'

stories.title: Australia politics live: Wong rules out lifting sanctions on Russian oil; Hastie downplays tensions with Taylor
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong ruled out lifting sanctions on Russian oil amid global energy disruptions. Energy Minister Chris Bowen said Australia remains on stage two of its national fuel plan, noting that cancelled fuel shipments have so far been replaced.

stories.title: Fire at superstore located in Karachi’s Zamzama area brought under control
stories.summary: A large fire at Imtiaz Superstore in Karachi's Zamzama shopping district was brought under control after hours of firefighting. CCTV footage indicated the blaze originated at an ATM inside the store.

stories.title: Limited missions, big risks: What a US ground fight in Iran could become
stories.summary: Military analysts outlined potential U.S. ground operations in Iran, including coastal assaults and raids on nuclear sites. Experts warned that even limited missions carry significant risks of escalation in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: 'The hypocrisy was so stark' expert says, as US reverses course on Cuba oil blockade
stories.summary: The White House allowed a sanctioned Russian tanker to deliver fuel to Cuba for humanitarian reasons on a case-by-case basis. Experts highlighted the contradiction between Washington's criticism of Iran restricting maritime movement and its own oil blockade against Cuba.

stories.title: Zelensky holds Staff meeting on air defense issues
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky convened a meeting of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief's Staff focused on air defense issues facing Ukraine.

stories.title: Knesset passes death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly acts of terror
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a death penalty law mandating hanging for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks, with no right to appeal. Security and legal officials opposed the measure, and rights groups plan to petition the High Court to overturn it.

stories.title: Trump administration sues Minnesota for allowing trans athletes in girls’ sports
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice sued Minnesota's education department and the state's high school athletics body for allowing transgender athletes to compete in girls' sports. The lawsuit alleges Minnesota is violating Title IX, the federal law prohibiting sex-based discrimination in federally funded programs.

stories.title: Trump Claims ‘Great Progress’ in Iran Peace Talks
stories.summary: President Trump claimed "great progress" in peace talks with Iran. Simultaneously, the White House threatened to destroy Tehran's energy sector if a deal is not reached soon, sending mixed signals about the status of negotiations.

stories.title: Congo army launches disarmament push against Rwanda genocide-linked militia
stories.summary: Congo's army announced the launch of a disarmament campaign against a militia linked to the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The operation represents a key step toward implementing a U.S.-brokered peace deal between the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighbouring Rwanda.

stories.title: What could Trump achieve by threatening Iran’s Kharg Island?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to obliterate Iran's Kharg Island, the nerve center of Iranian oil exports handling the vast majority of the country's crude shipments. The Pentagon has reportedly eyed the island for potential ground operations.

stories.title: Why India is quietly deepening its engagement with the Taliban
stories.summary: India is quietly expanding its diplomatic engagement with the Taliban government in Afghanistan amid rising Pakistan-Afghanistan border tensions, cross-border strikes, and the persistent threat posed by TTP fighters operating from Afghan territory.

stories.title: How Yemen’s Houthis could worsen the oil crunch
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces have restricted shipping traffic through a key waterway for approximately two years, raising concerns about worsening the global oil supply crunch amid the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Army investigates after two helicopters hovered by Kid Rock’s pool as he saluted
stories.summary: The U.S. Army launched an administrative review after two AH-64 Apache helicopters on a training run hovered near Kid Rock's hillside home in Nashville. The Trump-supporting musician posted videos showing himself saluting and clapping as the helicopters flew alongside his pool.

stories.title: ‘Dangerous escalation’: World reacts to Israel passing death penalty law
stories.summary: International rights groups condemned Israel's newly passed death penalty law as a violation of international law, warning it places Palestinian prisoners at heightened risk.

stories.title: 'It's a prison': Afghans stranded in US camp in Qatar exposed to Iranian strikes
stories.summary: Afghan asylum seekers stranded at Camp As Sayliyah, a US transit facility in Qatar, have been exposed to Iranian strikes. The camp is set to close as a transit hub for vetted Afghans, but residents have not been told where they will be relocated.

stories.title: Israel Knesset set to vote on death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset was set to vote on March 30 on legislation making the death penalty a default sentence for Palestinians convicted in military courts of deadly attacks. The bill fulfils a key pledge made by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition allies.

stories.title: ‘We miss the simplest things’: Tehran residents on edge after month of war
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran are living under fear and uncertainty after a month of war, clinging to daily routines amid ongoing strikes on Iran's capital.

stories.title: Ukraine, Bulgaria sign security cooperation agreement
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Bulgaria's Acting Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov signed a bilateral security cooperation agreement in a meeting between the two countries' leaders.

stories.title: UN condemns killing of Indonesian peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations condemned the killing of three Indonesian peacekeepers in Lebanon, who died in two separate incidents. No further details on the perpetrators were immediately provided.

stories.title: Germany's Merz says Berlin will work with Syria to return refugees
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced on March 30 that Germany and Syria would cooperate to facilitate the return of hundreds of thousands of Syrian refugees. Merz said the refugees had an important role to play in rebuilding their country.

stories.title: Opposition mistakenly approves millions to haredi institutions, A-G halts transfer
stories.summary: Israeli opposition lawmakers mistakenly voted to approve hundreds of millions of shekels in allocations to ultra-Orthodox institutions during a budget maneuver. The Attorney General subsequently halted the fund transfers, as the allocations had previously been blocked by legal advisors. Some opposition members issued public apologies.

stories.title: Trump interested in calling on Arab states to help pay for Iran war, White House says
stories.summary: The White House said President Trump is interested in calling on Arab states to help finance the war against Iran. Press Secretary Leavitt warned that any private commitments made by Iran to Washington would be tested and that Tehran would be held accountable.

stories.title: 'Like a dream': Gaza mother reunited with evacuated baby daughter
stories.summary: Sundus al-Kurd, a Gazan mother, was reunited with her baby daughter after being separated when Shifa Hospital in Gaza was evacuated more than two years ago during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks face death penalty under new Israeli law
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law allowing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks against Israelis. The legislation was championed by far-right Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and approved on Monday.

stories.title: Israeli Knesset approves death penalty for Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset approved legislation permitting the death penalty for Palestinians found guilty of killing Israelis. The measure has drawn widespread controversy domestically and internationally.

stories.title: ‘All roads lead to higher prices and slower growth’: IMF says Iran war is dimming outlook for many economies
stories.summary: The IMF warned that the US-Israeli war on Iran is causing significant global economic disruption, including tighter financial conditions. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and damage to regional infrastructure have caused major energy supply disruptions.

stories.title: Air Canada CEO to quit after furore about crash condolence video
stories.summary: Air Canada's CEO announced his resignation following public backlash over a condolence video he released about a deadly crash. The video, issued only in English, created a significant public relations controversy in Canada.

stories.title: Houthi attacks stoke fears of more shipping disruption
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched attacks on Israeli targets after entering the broader conflict, driving a surge in global oil prices. The Iran-allied group had previously targeted commercial ships near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, raising fears of wider disruption to energy and goods trade between Europe and Asia via the Suez Canal.

stories.title: The war in Iran: Key takeaways from Al Jazeera’s interview with Marco Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed the objectives of the US military campaign against Iran in an interview with Al Jazeera's Hashem Ahelbarra.

stories.title: FBI says man who crashed his truck into Michigan synagogue was inspired by Hezbollah
stories.summary: The FBI announced that Ayman Ghazali, who crashed his pickup truck into Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield Township, Michigan, was inspired by the Iran-backed group Hezbollah and had recorded a video expressing intent to kill.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran one‑week deadline on deal, says US response to Haifa strike coming soon
stories.summary: President Trump gave Iran a one-week deadline to reach a deal and said a US response to the missile strike on Haifa is forthcoming. Trump also stated that Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not been heard from and is believed to be 'very seriously injured.'

stories.title: Syrian army says drone attacks targeted its bases near Iraq
stories.summary: The Syrian army reported on March 30 that drone attacks struck several of its military bases near the Iraqi border. The strikes represent a rare targeting of Syrian positions since U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran a month ago triggered a wider Middle East war.

stories.title: ‘We have to destroy Iran’s ability to launch missiles’, Rubio says
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that eliminating Iran's missile-launch capability is essential for achieving regional stability.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 70 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one and wounding 12
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 70 drone and artillery attacks on the Nikopol and Kryvyi Rih districts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, killing one person and wounding 12 others.

stories.title: Missile hits fuel tanker at Israel's Oil Refineries
stories.summary: Debris from an intercepted missile struck an industrial building and a fuel tanker at Oil Refineries Ltd in Haifa, northern Israel, on March 30. Israel's Fire and Rescue Service confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Israel’s parliament passes death penalty bill targeting Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed a death penalty bill targeting Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks. The Palestinian Authority condemned the legislation as a war crime and a breach of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

stories.title: At least 70 people killed and 30 injured in Haiti gang attack
stories.summary: A gang attack in Haiti's Artibonite region killed at least 70 people and injured 30, according to a human rights group, far exceeding initial official estimates of 16–17 dead. Nearly 6,000 people were forced to flee the area, and the group criticized authorities for abandoning affected communities.

stories.title: War boosts counter-drone sales, joint ventures
stories.summary: The ongoing conflicts have driven a surge in counter-drone technology sales and joint ventures, with defense-technology companies forming new partnerships and nations under threat placing orders in recent weeks.
