stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker has reached Cuba with a much-needed fuel shipment, the first since January when U.S. forces seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. The delivery follows signals from President Trump of a softening stance on the U.S. blockade against Cuba.

stories.title: Ukraine signs defence agreements with Gulf Nations eager to fend off Iranian drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced "historic" defence agreements with Gulf states including the UAE and Saudi Arabia following his regional visit. The deals involve sharing Ukraine's drone-interception expertise with countries facing Iranian drone and missile attacks, in exchange for air defence missiles needed by Kyiv.

stories.title: Ukraine has agreements with Arab countries on maritime drones, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukraine has reached agreements with Arab countries on maritime drone cooperation and the reopening of sea lanes, building on Ukraine's experience with naval drones.

stories.title: Ukraine can help unblock Strait of Hormuz — Kyiv negotiates naval drone with Arab countries after Black Sea success
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine can help unblock the Strait of Hormuz, citing Kyiv's successful use of naval drones in the Black Sea. Ukraine is negotiating naval drone agreements with Arab countries, offering tactical expertise and operational support.

stories.title: Finnish police say stray Ukrainian drone carried warhead
stories.summary: Finnish police confirmed that a stray Ukrainian drone that crashed in southern Finland was carrying a warhead. President Zelenskyy apologized for the incident, and Finland's President Stubb indicated mutual understanding between the two leaders.

stories.title: Iran shows the emerging crisis of the US airborne battle management fleet
stories.summary: U.S. airborne battle management and early-warning aircraft, critical for orchestrating air operations, are facing severe strain amid operations related to the Iran conflict. The fleet is in high demand but short supply, with analysts warning the platforms are approaching a breaking point as requirements continue to grow.

stories.title: Fire alarm, pump systems switched off before tragedy, Tai Po blaze panel told
stories.summary: An investigation into Hong Kong's deadly Tai Po housing estate fire, which killed 168 people on November 26, revealed that fire alarm and firefighting pump systems had been switched off a week before the blaze with no action taken to restore them.

stories.title: Putin’s Persian Problem
stories.summary: Analysts suggest the ongoing conflict involving Iran poses strategic challenges for Russia. Moscow's relationship with Tehran is complicated by the war, which could undermine Russian interests in the region despite their historically close ties.

stories.title: FM Ishaq Dar to embark on official visit to China on March 31: FO
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar will visit China on March 31 at the invitation of Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The visit aims to deepen the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Pakistan and China through discussions on regional and international issues.

stories.title: Ukraine signs ‘historic’ 10-year defense deals with Saudi Arabia, Qatar
stories.summary: Ukraine signed 10-year defense agreements with Saudi Arabia and Qatar, described as historic. The deals were reached as Iran has targeted Gulf countries' bases and energy assets.

stories.title: Zelensky hails 'historic' defence agreements with Gulf states
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on March 30 that he signed defence agreements with Middle Eastern countries during his visit the previous week. The deals include sharing Ukrainian expertise in downing drones with Gulf states targeted by Iranian strikes, with Ukraine proposing to exchange drone interceptors for air defence missiles.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine ready for Easter ceasefire, but with condition
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine is ready for a ceasefire in any form, including during the Easter period. However, he emphasized that any agreement must not compromise Ukraine's dignity or sovereignty.

stories.title: Jerusalem prosecutors indict 23-year-old over alleged contact with Iranian agent
stories.summary: Jerusalem prosecutors indicted a 23-year-old named Jaber for allegedly making contact with an Iranian agent through Telegram. According to the indictment, Jaber connected in January with a user identified as "Joan" while searching for temporary work in a Telegram group.

stories.title: Kharg Island is key to Iran’s oil exports, but targeting it would carry major risks
stories.summary: Kharg Island, located roughly 21 miles off Iran's coast, handles the bulk of Iran's oil exports. A potential U.S. ground operation to seize it would place troops within range of Iranian missiles and drones, posing significant military risks.

stories.title: Nigeria: Foreign Minister Yusuf Tuggar Set to Resign From Tinubu's Cabinet
stories.summary: Nigeria's Foreign Minister Yusuf Tuggar is reportedly set to resign from President Tinubu's cabinet. Supporters say a formal declaration of his governorship bid is imminent.

stories.title: Putin likely to stage another Salisbury-style attack, exiled oil tycoon says
stories.summary: Exiled Russian billionaire Mikhail Khodorkovsky has warned that President Vladimir Putin is likely to stage another attack on UK soil similar to the 2018 Salisbury nerve agent poisoning. Khodorkovsky said Russian security services may seek to create a "sense of vulnerability" in Britain unless the government adopts more aggressive tactics against the Kremlin.

stories.title: Nigeria: Activist Raises Alarm Over Alleged Police 'Abduction,' Extortion of N1.1million
stories.summary: A Nigerian activist has raised alarm over the alleged abduction and extortion of 1.1 million naira by police officers. The case highlights ongoing concerns about police brutality and extrajudicial conduct in Nigeria.

stories.title: Rubio tells Al Jazeera that Strait of Hormuz to reopen ‘one way or another’
stories.summary: In an exclusive Al Jazeera interview, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened "one way or another." He reiterated that Trump seeks a diplomatic path while demanding Iran end its nuclear and missile programs.

stories.title: Trump wants to ‘take Iran’s oil’: Can he, and what would that mean?
stories.summary: President Trump stated that U.S. forces could seize Iran's oil export hub at Kharg Island as the U.S.-Iran war enters its second month. The threat underscores Washington's focus on Iran's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Sheep culls put pressure on Greek feta cheese production
stories.summary: More than 480,000 sheep and goats have been culled in Greece due to an ongoing pox pandemic. The mass culling is putting pressure on the country's feta cheese production.

stories.title: US not 'postured' for another Iraq 2003: Iran maintains vast, 'high-quality military capability'
stories.summary: Military analyst Michael Knights of the Washington Institute assessed that a large-scale U.S. ground invasion of Iran is highly unlikely, noting that Iran maintains a formidable, decentralised military system. He argued that while the U.S. can execute targeted operations, Iran's layered defence strategy presents significant structural resilience.

stories.title: Iran hangs two political prisoners from opposition group, activists say
stories.summary: Iran executed two political prisoners affiliated with the outlawed Mujahedin-e Khalq (MEK) organization at Ghezel Hesar prison outside Tehran. Rights organizations have expressed concern about a surge in executions during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Starmer pledges to tackle new cost of living crisis at May elections campaign launch
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer launched Labour's English local elections campaign in Wolverhampton on March 30, framing the May 7 vote against a backdrop of "war on two fronts" — the ongoing Ukraine conflict and the Iran war. He pledged action to tackle a resurgent cost of living crisis as Labour braces for heavy losses at the polls.

stories.title: Security forces retaliate ‘vigorously’ after Afghan Taliban open fire in KP’s Bajaur sector: sources
stories.summary: Pakistani and Afghan forces exchanged fire in the Bajaur sector of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Monday. Security sources said Pakistan's forces retaliated after Afghan Taliban fighters opened fire with small and heavy weapons, and that Afghan posts used to target Pakistan were destroyed.

stories.title: Keir Starmer says UK will not be 'dragged' into Iran war
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer declared the UK will not be "dragged into" the war on Iran and ruled out deploying troops. He said the UK would still take defensive action to protect British lives and interests and help efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukrainian FM calls on all countries to join agreement on Special Tribunal for Russia’s crimes against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called on all countries to join the Enlarged Partial Agreement establishing a Special Tribunal for Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine. Sybiha stressed that launching the tribunal this year is essential for restoring justice and strengthening international law.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US planes involved in Iran war, defense minister says
stories.summary: Spain's defense minister announced the closure of Spanish airspace to U.S. military aircraft involved in operations against Iran. The restriction forces U.S. planes to bypass Spain en route to Middle Eastern targets but does not apply to emergency situations.

stories.title: Xiaomi, Alibaba ramp up AI recruitment amid global talent war
stories.summary: Chinese tech companies Xiaomi and Alibaba have launched spring recruitment drives targeting AI talent amid intense global competition. Both firms are positioning themselves as AI-first companies as their traditional businesses face growing pressures.

stories.title: Distancing himself from Trump and a badly waged war in Iran might be the smartest move Albanese can make
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has distanced himself from U.S. President Donald Trump's approach to the Iran war, publicly stating that Washington has achieved its original objectives and should end hostilities in the Middle East. Australia is facing economic consequences from the global energy crisis triggered by the conflict.

stories.title: Australians may not see cheaper fuel for weeks despite Labor’s excise cuts
stories.summary: Despite the Australian Labor government's decision to temporarily halve fuel excise starting Wednesday, industry experts warn that cheaper prices may take days or weeks to reach service stations. The delay depends on how quickly stations sell through existing higher-priced fuel stocks ahead of Easter travel.

stories.title: ‘Succulent Chinese meal’ speech added to Australia’s National Film and Sound Archive
stories.summary: Australia's National Film and Sound Archive has added Jack Karlson's 1989 "democracy manifest" speech to its national collection. Karlson delivered the now-famous remarks while being arrested outside a Chinese restaurant in Queensland 35 years ago, and the footage later became a widely shared internet meme.

stories.title: From Mach 0 to 6: this engine may power China’s future fighter jets and missiles
stories.summary: Chinese researchers have completed and experimentally verified a prototype "contra-rotary ramjet engine" designed to operate from standstill to over Mach 6. The engine could power future fighter jets and hypersonic missiles, replacing current combined turbine-ramjet systems.

stories.title: Zelensky responds to Rheinmetall CEO’s remark on Ukrainian housewives building drones
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky responded to remarks by Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger about Ukrainian civilians building drones. Zelensky emphasized that Ukraine demonstrates its defense industry capabilities daily on the battlefield across land, air, and sea domains.

stories.title: Why Iran war makes Red Sea shipping a bigger worry
stories.summary: The Red Sea has become an increasingly important alternative shipping route for transporting crude oil from Saudi Arabia to Asia. The ongoing Iran war has heightened concerns about the security and reliability of this route.

stories.title: Japan’s PM will mull top-level talks with Iran  at ‘appropriate’ time
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she would consider holding talks with Iran's leadership at an appropriate time. Her remarks come amid uncertainty over US-Iran negotiations and renewed threats by President Trump against Iranian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: UAE arrests dozens of British citizens over online posts during Iran war
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has arrested dozens of British citizens for social media posts related to the Iran war. Authorities launched a crackdown targeting posts and videos depicting Iranian missile attacks.

stories.title: Israel strikes Tehran as Trump says Iran deal may be reached ‘soon’
stories.summary: Israel conducted strikes on Tehran while US President Donald Trump suggested an Iran deal may be reached "soon." Trump has not ruled out ground operations against Iran.

stories.title: Explosive Misinformation: A Guide to Mushroom Clouds, ‘Sonic Weapons’ and Disintegration
stories.summary: Bellingcat published a guide addressing common misinformation related to explosions, including misconceptions about mushroom clouds, so-called sonic weapons, and claims of disintegration. The guide references imagery from a Defence Research and Development Canada explosives test to help the public identify misleading conflict-related content.

stories.title: Israel PM restores access after Latin Patriarch blocked from Church of the Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu restored access for the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre after the cleric was blocked from the site. Israel had cited security concerns following Iran's missile strikes near Jerusalem's holy sites.

stories.title: Germany hosts Syria's Al-Sharaa despite human rights issues
stories.summary: Germany hosted interim Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa despite accusations of human rights violations, as Berlin seeks to encourage the return of Syrian refugees to their home country.

stories.title: Israel suspends military unit that assaulted CNN crew in West Bank
stories.summary: The Israeli military suspended the Netzah Yehuda battalion after soldiers were filmed assaulting a CNN crew in the occupied West Bank. The ultra-Orthodox unit has previously been linked to abuses of Palestinian civilians.

stories.title: War on Iran disrupts Asia’s used-car exports to the Middle East
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Israel war on Iran has disrupted Asia's used-car export industry to the Middle East, affecting trade routes and commerce across the region.

stories.title: Japanese destroyer can now fire Tomahawk missiles, extending nation’s combat punch
stories.summary: A Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force destroyer has been equipped to fire Tomahawk cruise missiles, significantly extending Japan's long-range strike capability. Analysts note that Japan's Tomahawk procurement is unlikely to face immediate disruption, though prolonged U.S. military campaigns in the Middle East could create supply delays.

stories.title: Police chief halts incitement department’s operations, complying with High Court
stories.summary: Israel's police chief Danny Levy halted the operations of a social media incitement-monitoring department, complying with a High Court order. The unit had been established by National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, who fiercely objected to the suspension.

stories.title: Asian economies scramble to find solutions to war's impact on oil markets
stories.summary: Iran continues to restrict traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for the U.S.-Israeli military campaign, causing global energy prices to soar. Over 80% of oil and gas typically transiting the strait is destined for Asian markets, leaving the region's economies scrambling for alternative solutions.

stories.title: One Lebanese soldier killed, Israel expands buffer zone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: One Lebanese soldier was killed and others wounded on March 30 when an Israeli air strike hit an army checkpoint in the Tyre region of southern Lebanon. Israel also renewed bombardment of Beirut's southern suburbs while continuing strikes across south Lebanon and expanding its buffer zone.

stories.title: Zelensky on PAC-3 missile shortage: We negotiate with two countries regarding alternatives
stories.summary: President Zelensky acknowledged a global shortage of PAC-3 missiles, noting that most available supplies are currently being directed to the Middle East. He disclosed that Ukraine is negotiating with two countries to secure alternative air defense systems.

stories.title: Israel army withdraws West Bank after CNN journalist assault
stories.summary: Israel withdrew a West Bank battalion after a soldier assaulted a CNN photojournalist. The incident raised concerns over press freedom and the treatment of journalists by Israeli forces in the occupied territories.

stories.title: What Bill Clinton, Netanyahu, McDonald’s and Starbucks reveal about crisis leadership
stories.summary: A new book on crisis management by one of Israel's leading crisis advisers examines leadership decisions by figures including Bill Clinton and Benjamin Netanyahu. The work argues that effective crisis response depends on the leader, timing, and decisiveness.

stories.title: Two Passover initiatives target isolation and safety for Israel’s elderly
stories.summary: Two Passover initiatives were launched in Israel to address isolation and safety concerns among elderly residents. The programs involved collaboration between the Social Equality Ministry, the Israel Association of Community Centers, Tzalir Fund, and Mifal HaPais.

stories.title: AFU deny Russian claims of capturing Kivsharivka in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Armed Forces denied Russian claims of having captured the town of Kivsharivka in the Kharkiv region. Ukrainian forces released footage showing captured Russian soldiers who had been attempting to raise a flag in the town.

stories.title: Why Donald Trump needs a short-term win in Iran before he visits Xi Jinping in China
stories.summary: Chinese military analysts suggest the US is seeking a short-term resolution to the Iran conflict before President Trump's planned May visit to China. The deployment of elite forces, including Army Rangers, indicates efforts to avoid a protracted war.

stories.title: JD Vance says aliens are ‘demons’ and details obsession with UFOs
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance described aliens as "demons" during an appearance on the conservative Benny Show podcast. Vance also discussed his interest in UFOs and promised to investigate reports of government files on unidentified flying objects.

stories.title: The Houthis have entered the Iran war. What could happen next?
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces have entered the war against Israel, launching new attacks on Red Sea shipping. Analysts warn the Houthis could attempt to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, further disrupting global trade.

stories.title: Trump threatens to 'obliterate' Iran's Kharg Island, energy sites
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to "obliterate" Iran's energy infrastructure, including power plants, oil wells, and Kharg Island, if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He framed the threat as a final measure should diplomatic efforts fail.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US planes involved in war on Iran
stories.summary: Spain has closed its airspace to U.S. military aircraft involved in the war on Iran. The move follows Madrid's earlier refusal to allow Washington to use jointly operated military bases on Spanish territory for operations against Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan Foreign Minister sustains ‘hairline fracture’ after fall during Egyptian counterpart’s reception
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar sustained a hairline fracture after falling during a reception for Egyptian counterpart Badr Abdelatty at Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The incident occurred as Dar was calling the Egyptian minister to the stage.

stories.title: The Iran War Has Escaped Its Authors
stories.summary: The military conflict involving Iran has escalated beyond initial expectations set by Washington policymakers. U.S. officials are facing difficulties maintaining control over the trajectory of the confrontation as events on the ground outpace diplomatic and strategic planning.

stories.title: Morocco's Tangier port prepares for spike in traffic driven by Gulf crisis
stories.summary: Morocco's Tangier port, located on the Strait of Gibraltar, is preparing for increased shipping traffic driven by disruptions related to the Gulf crisis. The port serves as a major transit point for Europe-bound container ships.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz expresses gratitude to foreign ministers after quad moot, reiterates Pakistan’s commitment to peace
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif thanked the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Egypt after a quadrilateral meeting in Pakistan focused on de-escalating the US-Iran conflict. The meeting, chaired by Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, was part of a coordinated regional diplomatic push as the war enters its second month.

stories.title: Persian Gulf ships show true locations as signal jamming eases
stories.summary: Ships in the Persian Gulf have begun showing their true locations as GPS signal jamming in the area has eased. However, experts warn the threat from poor signal data in the region remains high.

stories.title: ‘Long live the shah’: Iranian diaspora back war at Washington rally
stories.summary: Members of the Iranian diaspora rallied in Washington in support of the war against Iran. Iran's exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi has positioned himself as a potential transitional leader for a post-war Iran.

stories.title: Zelensky on peace talks: I don’t think we’re at impasse
stories.summary: President Zelensky expressed optimism about ongoing peace negotiations, saying he does not believe talks have reached an impasse. He indicated hope that a trilateral meeting involving Ukraine, the United States, and Russia could take place in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US planes involved in Iran war
stories.summary: Spain closed its airspace to U.S. military aircraft involved in the Iran war. The defense minister said the government refuses to participate in a conflict it considers contrary to international law, requiring U.S. planes to bypass the NATO-member country.

stories.title: PCB charges Fakhar Zaman with ball-tampering in PSL match
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board has charged Lahore Qalandars batter Fakhar Zaman with ball-tampering during a PSL match against Karachi Kings. Umpires awarded five penalty runs to Karachi after Fakhar and bowler Haris Rauf were seen passing the ball between them in the final over.

stories.title: How the Iran war is rewriting the economics of power … and why Pakistan must read the signals first
stories.summary: An analysis describes the 2026 Iran war as the most consequential military conflict since the Gulf War. Iran has launched over 500 ballistic missiles and 2,000 drones, oil prices threaten to breach $200 per barrel, and the Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed to unapproved shipping.

stories.title: Latvia approves new aid package for Ukraine
stories.summary: Latvia's government approved a new aid package for Ukraine worth 6.8 million euros. Foreign Minister Baiba Braže announced the decision as part of Latvia's continued support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Mozambique: World Bank Warns of Social &amp; 'Economic Instability' Which Could Cven Threaten The Gas Projects
stories.summary: The World Bank has issued a stark warning that Mozambique faces rising economic instability that could jeopardize over $50 billion in foreign direct investment, particularly in the country's liquefied natural gas projects.

stories.title: Israel says Latin Patriarch can now access Jerusalem holy sites
stories.summary: Israel restored the Latin Patriarch's access to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem after a Palm Sunday ban drew widespread international criticism. The reversal came amid heightened tensions over religious freedom during the Iran war.

stories.title: Jordan intercepts five missiles, one drone in a day
stories.summary: Jordan's military intercepted and destroyed five missiles and one drone over a 24-hour period. Falling debris from the intercepts injured one woman.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit a shell casing factory in occupied Alchevsk — Russia’s air defense was nowhere to be seen
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck a shell casing factory in Russian-occupied Alchevsk without encountering air defense resistance. The same night, drones also hit Taganrog in what was called the city's worst attack since the war began, as well as a chemical plant in Tolyatti and targets in Krasnodar.

stories.title: Asian economies most vulnerable to impact of Middle east war on oil markets
stories.summary: The war in the Middle East is severely impacting Asian economies, as more than 80% of crude oil and LNG passing through the Strait of Hormuz is bound for Asia. Parts of Southeast Asia are experiencing fuel supply difficulties, with policymakers facing their toughest challenge since the COVID-19 pandemic.

stories.title: West Africa: Sahel Juntas Intensify Crackdown On Journalists - IPI Warns
stories.summary: The International Press Institute (IPI) has warned of an escalating crackdown on journalists across Sahel nations governed by military juntas. The report highlights a growing information blackout with regional and global consequences.

stories.title: Why have the US and Israel bombed more than 75 Iranian police facilities?
stories.summary: An Al Jazeera investigation found that the U.S. and Israel have bombed more than 75 Iranian police and internal security facilities, many located in populated areas. The strikes have heavily targeted law enforcement infrastructure.

stories.title: US military building up in the Middle East as Trump looks for offramp in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump suggested on March 30 that U.S. troops could seize Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub while also claiming a deal with Tehran could come quickly. The New York Times confirmed hundreds of U.S. commandos have arrived in the Middle East, while Iran dismissed reported talks as a cover for military buildup.

stories.title: IDF announces death of Sgt. Liran Ben Zion, 19, killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced the death of 19-year-old Sergeant Liran Ben Zion, who was killed during operations in southern Lebanon. His family has been notified of his death.

stories.title: US used newly developed bomb in Iran school, sports hall strike
stories.summary: The Pentagon used a newly developed short-range ballistic missile in a strike on an elementary school in Lamerd, Iran, on the first day of the war. The weapon was reportedly used uncontested in combat for the first time.

stories.title: Singer-songwriter China Moses on why her music is not on streaming platforms
stories.summary: Franco-American jazz and soul singer China Moses, daughter of Dee Dee Bridgewater and Gilbert Moses, discussed her decision to keep her music off most streaming platforms like Spotify. Her latest album, "It's Complicated," reflects her approach to independent music publishing.

stories.title: Zelensky explains why he did not visit Israel during his Middle East tour
stories.summary: President Zelensky explained that he did not visit Israel during his recent Middle East tour because there had been no prior contact with Israeli officials to arrange the trip. The statement addressed questions about the omission from his itinerary.

stories.title: Apple subsidiary fined by UK government over Moscow sanctions breach
stories.summary: The UK government fined Apple Distribution International, an Ireland-based Apple subsidiary, £390,000 for breaching sanctions against Russia. The company instructed a UK-based bank to make two payments totalling £635,000 to a company owned by a sanctioned Russian entity, linked to a Russian streaming service.

stories.title: China sanctions aide of Japan PM Takaichi for Taiwan ties
stories.summary: China imposed sanctions on a Japanese political aide with ties to Taiwan, barring his entry into China and freezing his assets effective immediately. The sanctioned individual, Furuya, is connected to Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi's office.

stories.title: Ukraine runs out of war funding in June—blocked from outside, inside, and below
stories.summary: Ukraine faces a war funding crisis projected to hit in June due to multiple blockages. Hungary is blocking billions in external aid, Ukraine's parliament is stalling domestic measures, and the government attempted to dismiss an anti-corruption official required by the EU.

stories.title: Iran are now 'calling the shots' over the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump claimed Iran agreed to let 20 ships through the Strait of Hormuz as evidence of progress in talks with Tehran. However, analysts argue the situation actually demonstrates Iran exercising greater sovereignty over the strait, effectively controlling passage through the critical waterway.

stories.title: Holy Sepulchre Easter services to go ahead as Church leaders reach deal with police
stories.summary: Church leaders and Israeli police reached an agreement to allow Easter services at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem to proceed during Holy Week. The ceremonies will include a live broadcast, amid ongoing Iranian missile threats.

stories.title: Palestinian recalls brother’s arrest at the Rafah crossing
stories.summary: A Palestinian man returning to Gaza had his brother detained by Israeli forces at the Rafah crossing. The incident turned his long-awaited homecoming into an ordeal.

stories.title: Sweden charges ‘monster’ man for selling wife to over 120 men
stories.summary: A Swedish prosecutor charged a 62-year-old man with aggravated pimping, multiple rapes, and assault for allegedly selling his wife's sexual services to over 120 men over several years. He was arrested in October after his wife reported him to police in northern Sweden.

stories.title: US mulls over ground offensive in Iran despite claims of talks
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering a ground offensive in Iran to seize the country's nuclear stockpile, which would be one of the riskiest operations in U.S. military history. Thousands of American military personnel arrived in the region over the weekend, as Trump also signalled a possible seizure of Kharg Island.

stories.title: Australia PM Albanese calls for clarity from Trump on objectives of West Asia war
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called on U.S. President Donald Trump to clarify objectives in the West Asia war. Australia has deployed aircraft to help defend the United Arab Emirates but has ruled out sending naval ships to assist in reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Between escalation and engagement: Pakistan keeps hope for peace alive
stories.summary: Pakistan has positioned itself as a diplomatic channel amid the escalating US-Iran crisis. Speculation in Washington has shifted toward possible American ground operations in Iran after President Trump's remarks about "taking the oil," interpreted as a reference to seizing Iran's Kharg Island.

stories.title: Passover hotel programs see mass exodus as war disrupts holiday travel plans
stories.summary: Flight cancellations and security concerns caused by the Iran war have forced mass cancellations of Passover hotel programs in and around Israel. Tens of thousands of travelers found journeys nonviable, dealing a major blow to the kosher-for-Passover hospitality industry.

stories.title: G-7 ministers set to tackle financial fallout of Middle East war
stories.summary: G-7 finance ministers are preparing to address the financial fallout from the Middle East war. The conflict has squeezed global supply chains and pushed oil and natural gas prices higher.

stories.title: US senators visit Taiwan to push defence spending as arms deadlines loom
stories.summary: Four US senators visited Taiwan to press for legislative approval of a NT$1.25 trillion special defence budget stalled by the opposition. The visit comes as Taipei faces payment deadlines for US-approved arms packages amid intensifying military pressure from Beijing.

stories.title: Homes damaged as Iranian missiles trigger sirens across northern Israel
stories.summary: Iranian missile launches triggered air-raid sirens across central and northern Israel. Falling debris struck residential areas, damaging multiple homes.

stories.title: Iran’s Foreign Ministry denies claims of US-Iran negotiations
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry issued a denial of claims that negotiations between Tehran and Washington are taking place, amid ongoing conflict between the two countries.

stories.title: EU seeks new strategy amid Sahel 'influence' rivalries
stories.summary: The EU is developing a new strategy for engagement in the Sahel region following military coups in Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso in 2022–2023. The junta governments turned to Russia, China, and the U.S., prompting the EU to invest more in West African security and economic growth.

stories.title: Iranian lawmakers review possibility of leaving Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
stories.summary: Iran's parliament is reviewing a possible withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, according to foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei, who insisted Tehran has not and will not pursue nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Uganda: Refugees in Uganda Benefit From Empowerment Initiatives
stories.summary: Uganda's refugee communities are set to benefit from two new projects launched by the AVSI Foundation aimed at promoting self-reliance, economic stability, and psychosocial support.

stories.title: Zelensky calls Middle East agreements historic
stories.summary: President Zelensky described newly signed ten-year defense cooperation agreements with Saudi Arabia and Qatar as historic. He noted that Ukraine has never previously had such defense agreements in the Middle East region.

stories.title: Israel is making sure Trump can't find an off-ramp in Iran
stories.summary: Analysis suggests Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is pursuing military escalation against Iran in a way that limits US President Trump's ability to negotiate a diplomatic resolution, drawing parallels to Israel's campaigns in Gaza and against Hezbollah.

stories.title: How the Hormuz attacks stoke oil-shock fears and memories of 1970s stagflation
stories.summary: Attacks disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz amid the US-Israel conflict with Iran have driven oil prices sharply higher. Analysts are drawing comparisons to the 1970s oil shocks and raising concerns about potential stagflation.

stories.title: Let’s be clear: national security law update is not a power grab
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government enacted amended implementation rules for Article 43 of the national security law on March 23. Officials characterized the changes as technical refinements to existing operational procedures rather than an expansion of authority.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US military over Iran war, widening rift with US
stories.summary: Spain has closed its airspace to U.S. military aircraft involved in attacks related to the Iran war. Defence minister confirmed the move, describing the U.S.-Israel campaign against Iran as "profoundly illegal and unjust." Madrid had previously barred the U.S. from using jointly operated military bases for the conflict.

stories.title: Senegal: France Held Responsible for Concealing 1944 African Colonial Soldier's Death
stories.summary: A French administrative court ruled that the French state was at fault for concealing details of the 1944 Thiaroye massacre in Senegal, where the French army killed African colonial soldiers demanding their pay.

stories.title: Don't bottleneck defense-personnel vetting with a small-business set-aside
stories.summary: A commentary argues against imposing small-business set-aside requirements on federal defense-personnel vetting contracts, noting the program screens roughly one million federal employees annually and the workload is expanding.

stories.title: 48-hour curfew imposed after attack on bar in Nigerian city
stories.summary: Authorities imposed a 48-hour curfew in Jos, Nigeria, after an attack on a bar triggered revenge violence. At least 22 people have been reported dead in the volatile Plateau state region.

stories.title: Trump ‘pretty sure’ of Iran deal, but can Pakistan-led efforts end the war?
stories.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt have formed a team to pursue backchannel talks between the U.S. and Iran. President Trump said he is "pretty sure" a deal can be reached, though the war continues.

stories.title: 2026 World Cup: Mexico ramps up security amid threat from cartels
stories.summary: Mexico is ramping up security preparations ahead of the 2026 World Cup amid ongoing cartel violence. The killing of drug lord El Mencho during a special forces operation in late February sparked a nationwide surge in violence, though President Claudia Sheinbaum insists adequate security measures will be in place.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike Alchevsk Metallurgical Plant and Russian echelon
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the Alchevsk Metallurgical Plant in Russian-occupied territory, along with a Russian military convoy. The forces also hit a launcher belonging to Russia's S-400 Triumph mobile surface-to-air missile system.

stories.title: Rocket attack targets Baghdad army base
stories.summary: Rockets fired overnight struck an Iraqi military base inside the Baghdad airport complex, which also houses a US embassy support centre. The base has been repeatedly targeted since the start of the broader Middle East conflict on 28 February.

stories.title: Tai Po fire survivors mourn heroine who alerted neighbours to flames
stories.summary: Survivors of the Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong have mourned Pak Shui-lin, a resident of Wang Tai House who died after knocking on neighbours' doors to warn them of the blaze. Her husband and a neighbour testified at an inquiry, noting that fire alarms in the building failed to activate during the incident.

stories.title: Hezbollah uses ambulances, paramedic uniforms, as disguise for terrorist activity, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces alleged that Hezbollah operatives systematically used ambulances and paramedic uniforms to disguise terrorist activities. The military claimed the group employed these methods to transfer weapons across Lebanon for use in attacks against Israel and IDF soldiers.

stories.title: Donald Trump threatens to 'take the oil' in Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told the Financial Times that the US could seize Iranian oil assets, including the key export hub of Kharg Island, comparing the proposal to US actions regarding Venezuela.

stories.title: Iran claims Israel attacked Kuwaiti desalination plant
stories.summary: Iran's military accused Israel of attacking a desalination plant in Kuwait, with the Revolutionary Guard's operational command Khatam al-Anbiya calling the strike an act of aggression carried out under false pretexts.

stories.title: Netanyahu restores access after Latin Patriarch blocked from Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu restored the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem's access to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre after police blocked Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa from entering on Palm Sunday. Israel cited security concerns related to a ban on religious gatherings during the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan trade fire, readies to host US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan exchanged heavy fire after a truce broke down along their border. Simultaneously, Islamabad signaled plans to host potential US-Iran negotiations amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Hamas Gaza commander abducted as Israel kills man in West Bank
stories.summary: A Hamas Qassam Brigades commander was abducted in Gaza, while Israeli forces killed a Palestinian man in the West Bank. Settler attacks and movement restrictions also intensified across the occupied territory.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks minibus in Kherson, one person injured
stories.summary: Russian forces used a drone to attack a minibus in the center of Kherson, injuring a 62-year-old man. The strike targeted a civilian vehicle in the city center.

stories.title: Nigeria fuel prices surge 65% amid global oil shock
stories.summary: Fuel prices in Nigeria have surged approximately 65%, the steepest increase among major African economies, amid a global oil shock. The country's refinery has failed to reduce reliance on foreign crude imports as expected.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills 1 in Rostov Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on Russia's Rostov region killed one person. Authorities reported that the port city of Taganrog sustained the heaviest damage in the broader aerial assault on the southern region.

stories.title: Authorities rule out smoking areas at construction sites under proposed ban
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Commissioner for Labour Sam Hui Chark-shum announced that a proposed smoking ban at construction sites would apply to all areas, with no designated smoking zones due to enforcement difficulties. Authorities plan to use drones with heat sensors for inspections. The ban was proposed following the deadly Tai Po fire in November.

stories.title: Haifa refinery said hit in latest Iranian missile barrage
stories.summary: Iran launched a missile barrage that reportedly struck the Haifa oil refinery in Israel. Shrapnel from the missiles caused localized damage and temporary power disruptions at the facility, though no casualties were reported.

stories.title: Israel drop more than 80 bombs on Iranian weapons factories
stories.summary: Israeli Air Force jets struck multiple Iranian weapons production facilities during overnight airstrikes in Tehran. The IDF reported dropping more than 80 bombs on the targeted factories.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed in Lebanon; blaze at Haifa refinery after Iran, Hezbollah missile attack
stories.summary: An IDF soldier, Sgt. Liran Ben Zion, 19, was killed by an anti-tank missile in Lebanon, and four other soldiers were seriously wounded. Separately, a missile attack by Iran and Hezbollah struck northern Israel, causing a blaze at the Haifa oil refinery and injuring two people.

stories.title: Nigeria: Ex-VP Atiku Denies Quitting Active Politics
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Vice President Atiku Abubakar has denied reports that he plans to retire from active politics, calling the claims false and part of a coordinated disinformation campaign.

stories.title: Nigeria: Soldiers Repel Iswap Attack in Borno, Kill 38 Insurgents - Official
stories.summary: Nigerian military forces repelled an ISWAP attack in Borno state, killing 38 insurgents in a coordinated offensive-defensive operation that forced the militants to retreat.

stories.title: Africa: Presidential Election in the Republic of the Congo
stories.summary: The African Union Commission chairperson has acknowledged the results of the presidential election in the Republic of the Congo, congratulating Denis Sassou Nguesso on his re-election as announced by the Constitutional Court.

stories.title: Holocaust survivor, descendants urge High Court to allow Gaza children medical access
stories.summary: A Holocaust survivor and descendants submitted a letter to Israel's High Court urging that Gaza children be granted medical access. The letter, read by The Jerusalem Post, invokes Holocaust-era rescue precedent to argue for a "children's exception" in wartime policy.

stories.title: Nigeria: Coronation Insurance, MTN Nigeria, C &amp; I Leasing Top Stock Pick This Week
stories.summary: Nigerian financial analysts have highlighted Coronation Insurance, MTN Nigeria, and C&I Leasing as top stock picks for the week. The guidance is informational and not a formal buy, sell, or hold recommendation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Plateau Attack - Unijos Reschedules Exams for Students
stories.summary: The University of Jos in Plateau State, Nigeria, has rescheduled examinations originally set for Monday and Tuesday following a deadly attack in the area. The postponement was announced to ensure student safety.

stories.title: A month past US-Israel war on Iran, water and power under threat
stories.summary: Residents inside Iran report ongoing daily airstrikes and growing threats to water and power infrastructure roughly one month after the United States and Israel launched military operations against the country. Communications between officials continue, but civilians describe a persistent lack of safety.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda's Impeding Debt Crisis
stories.summary: An analysis warns that Uganda faces a real risk of defaulting on its domestic bonds within two to three years. The assessment argues that debt sustainability should be measured by the ratio of debt service to tax revenues rather than the debt-to-GDP ratio.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Former Minister's Son Faces Court Challenge Over Infant Care
stories.summary: A custody dispute over a 14-month-old child involving a former Zimbabwean minister's son is being heard at the High Court of Zimbabwe in Harare. A woman is challenging a divorce ruling that granted shared custody between her and her former husband.

stories.title: Germany’s FM tells President al-Sharaa ‘We stand with Syria’
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa met with senior German officials during a visit to Berlin. German Foreign Minister expressed support for Syria, and the two sides discussed bilateral cooperation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Hundreds of Delegates Arrive As Wike-Backed PDP Faction Begins Convention
stories.summary: A faction of Nigeria's Peoples Democratic Party backed by FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has begun a national convention. According to reports, approximately 2,632 delegates are participating in the event.

stories.title: China’s massive pig farms spark a supply glut as hog prices hit 8-year low
stories.summary: China's live pig prices have fallen to an eight-year low, averaging 11.05 yuan per kilogram in the third week of March, down 28 percent from a year earlier. The decline is driven by a supply glut caused by the expansion of large industrial pig farms and reduced post-holiday meat consumption.

stories.title: Small number of Russians remain trapped under ruins of hospital in Kupiansk, says Tregubov
stories.summary: According to Ukrainian spokesperson Tregubov, a small number of Russian soldiers remain trapped under the ruins of a hospital in the city of Kupiansk in the Kharkiv region. The soldiers are reportedly surrounded by Ukrainian forces.

stories.title: How North Korea is using Belarus to deepen ties with Russia
stories.summary: Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko made a rare visit to North Korea as part of Pyongyang's broader effort to deepen ties with Russia's sphere of influence.

stories.title: South Sudan: Race Against Time to Stabilise South Sudan As Elections Loom
stories.summary: South Sudan faces a narrowing window to hold meaningful elections as political stabilization efforts continue. Three separate initiatives are underway, though questions remain about whether they can succeed where previous efforts have failed.

stories.title: Spain closes airspace to US planes involved in Iran war, defence minister says
stories.summary: Spain closed its airspace to US aircraft involved in military operations against Iran, going beyond its earlier refusal to allow use of jointly operated military bases, Defence Minister Margarita Robles announced Monday.

stories.title: Russian Oil Tanker Arrives in Cuba After Trump Shrugs Off His Own Fuel Blockade
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker arrived in Cuba after U.S. President Trump indicated Washington would not block oil shipments to the island, including those from Russia. The move effectively relaxed Trump's own earlier fuel blockade against the crisis-stricken nation.

stories.title: Russia’s FSB orders British diplomat’s expulsion, UK rejects ‘intimidation’
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) accused a second secretary at the British Embassy in Moscow of espionage and ordered the diplomat's expulsion. The United Kingdom rejected the move, calling it "intimidation."

stories.title: Donald Trump threatens to 'take the oil' in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump said the U.S. could "take the oil" in Iran, as thousands of American troops have been deployed to the Middle East ahead of a potential ground invasion.

stories.title: Trump says Iran has undergone ‘regime change’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed Iran has undergone "regime change," citing the number of Iranian leaders killed during the month-long war.

stories.title: Taiwan's opposition leader to visit China next month, ahead of Trump
stories.summary: Taiwan's opposition Kuomintang (KMT) chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, elected in October, plans to visit mainland China next month, signaling closer ties with Beijing. Her visit is scheduled ahead of a planned trip by US President Trump.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Indian national killed in Iranian strikes in Kuwait
stories.summary: An Indian national was killed during Iranian strikes in Kuwait, where a service building at a power and water distillation plant was also damaged in the attack.

stories.title: Airport travel chaos continues as DHS funding freeze becomes longest partial shutdown in history – US politics live
stories.summary: U.S. airport disruptions continued as the DHS funding freeze became the longest partial shutdown in history. President Trump ordered pay restored to TSA employees, but the legal authority and funding source for the move remain unclear.

stories.title: Starmer says UK won’t get ‘dragged into Iran war’ as Labour launches its local elections campaign – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Britain would not get "dragged into" the Iran war as he launched Labour's local elections campaign. He planned to chair a meeting Monday on the government's response to the conflict's economic consequences.

stories.title: Iran says US demands for talks are 'excessive'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson said Tehran received US negotiation proposals via intermediaries but deemed them "unrealistic, illogical and excessive." The statement came after foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey met in Islamabad to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Beirut apartment damaged in Israeli strike
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike heavily damaged a residential building in Beirut's southern suburbs, causing significant structural destruction to the area.

stories.title: Sirens heard across Haifa port
stories.summary: Air raid sirens sounded across the port city of Haifa on Monday amid expectations of incoming missile fire targeting the northern Israeli city.

stories.title: Air China resumes flights to North Korea after six-year pause
stories.summary: Air China resumed direct flights between Beijing and Pyongyang after a six-year pause, following the restart of train services between the two capitals weeks earlier. Travel had been heavily restricted since North Korea imposed strict border closures during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz appreciates foreign ministers of Turkiye, Egypt, Saudi Arabia for confidence in Pakistan’s peace efforts
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif thanked the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Egypt following a quadrilateral meeting in Islamabad focused on de-escalating the US-Iran conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Schools, water, industry: What civilian targets have US, Israel, Iran hit?
stories.summary: US and Israeli forces have increasingly struck civilian infrastructure in Iran, including schools, water facilities, and industrial sites, as efforts to end the ongoing weeks-long war continue.

stories.title: IDF drops over 80 explosives on Tehran weapon production sites in latest strike
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces stated that over 80 munitions were dropped on Iranian weapons production, research, and development sites. According to the IDF, these facilities were responsible for manufacturing weapons used in attacks against Israel.

stories.title: As Knesset moves to pay workers furloughed by war, some who returned under fire are passed over
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset moved to compensate workers furloughed due to the war, but the plan drew criticism for excluding employees who returned to work while restrictions were eased, while state workers will receive full wages.

stories.title: China’s sci-fi industry rides a tech wave as revenues hit record high
stories.summary: China's science-fiction industry reached record gross revenues of 126.1 billion yuan (US$18.2 billion) in 2025, a 15.7 percent year-on-year increase. Online search traffic for sci-fi more than tripled last year, according to an annual report released at the China Science Fiction Convention.

stories.title: ‘Not our war’: Europe says no to Trump
stories.summary: European leaders have pushed back against US President Trump's expectations of support in the Iran conflict, wary that antagonizing him could affect US commitments to Ukraine or lead to a deal favoring Moscow.

stories.title: Sudan: Prime Minister and 'Hope Government' Mourn Professor Mohamed Osman Salih
stories.summary: Sudan's Prime Minister Kamil Idris and members of the "Hope Government" have mourned the passing of Professor Mohamed Osman Salih, former head of the Sudanese Scholars Authority. The announcement was made from Khartoum on March 29, 2026.

stories.title: Brazil hit hardest as Latin America adjusts to Trump tariffs after one year
stories.summary: One year after the Trump administration launched tariffs against more than 180 countries, Brazil has been the hardest hit in Latin America. Some regional economies lost U.S. market competitiveness, while others redirected exports or negotiated agreements to mitigate the impact.

stories.title: Trump to revoke protections for endangered species in Gulf of Mexico
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is convening a so-called "God squad" of senior officials to revoke Endangered Species Act protections for wildlife in the Gulf of Mexico. The move aims to expand oil and gas operations and could threaten species including Rice's whales, whooping cranes, and sea turtles.

stories.title: Opportunities and dangers: Opposition to Iran war set to grow in Latin America when prices increase
stories.summary: Opposition to the Iran war is expected to grow in Latin America as rising energy and commodity prices hit the region's economies. Analysts suggest Guyana, an oil producer, may be positioned to benefit most from the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Russian oil tanker arrives in Cuba as Moscow vows to stand by Havana
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker carrying 100,000 tonnes of crude oil arrived in Cuba on Monday, with Moscow pledging further supplies despite a U.S. blockade. The shipment follows Washington's cutoff of Venezuelan oil exports to Cuba after toppling President Nicolás Maduro on January 3.

stories.title: Syria’s al-Sharaa visits Germany to talk reconstruction, return of refugees
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa visited Berlin for high-level meetings with German officials focused on refugee repatriation and Syria's post-conflict reconstruction efforts.

stories.title: Orthopaedist rebuked over performing bunion surgery without informed consent
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Medical Council found orthopaedist Dr. Daniel Wu Yiang guilty of professional misconduct for performing an unconventional soft-tissue bunion surgery at Hong Kong Adventist Hospital without obtaining the patient's informed consent. He was issued a public warning letter and reprimanded.

stories.title: US military building ‘massive complex’ beneath White House ballroom project: Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump disclosed that the US military is constructing a "massive complex" beneath a White House ballroom project. The privately funded budget for the project has doubled from US$200 million to US$400 million.

stories.title: China resumes direct flights to North Korea after six years
stories.summary: Air China resumed direct flights to North Korea after a six-year hiatus. The Chinese Ambassador to North Korea, Wang Yajun, and other diplomats welcomed the flight, according to Chinese state media.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper killed as Israel expands war in Lebanon
stories.summary: A United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded as Israel expanded military operations into Lebanon. Israeli strikes hit targets in Beirut, and soldiers sustained injuries in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Green and Yellow: Two lines that separate me from my land
stories.summary: The article reflects on Israeli-drawn boundaries and their impact on Palestinian land access, discussing the Green Line and other demarcations that restrict Palestinians from their territory.

stories.title: Egypt business curfew sparks concern among traders and tourism sector
stories.summary: Egypt's government has imposed a business curfew, citing surging fuel costs linked to disruptions from regional conflict. Traders and tourism-sector operators have raised concerns about the measure's economic impact as import prices rise and national finances come under strain.

stories.title: Trump says intel chief Tulsi Gabbard ‘softer’ than him on Iran nuclear issue
stories.summary: President Trump said Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard is "softer" than him on the Iran nuclear issue. The Trump administration has sent conflicting messages about the current state of Iran's nuclear programme.

stories.title: Tatreez in Madrid: Stitching culture and resistance
stories.summary: A Palestinian refugee living in Madrid is teaching traditional Palestinian tatreez embroidery, working to preserve cultural heritage and identity in the diaspora.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Seeing More Interest From LNG Buyers for Its Cargoes - NNPC
stories.summary: Nigeria's state oil company NNPC reported growing interest from international LNG buyers for Nigerian cargoes. Simultaneously, the federal government is accelerating permit approvals for oil producers to revive old wells.

stories.title: Nigeria: Conclude Renegotiation Process, Settle All Outstanding Entitlements - SSANU to Govt
stories.summary: The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities has demanded that the federal government reconvene salary renegotiations and settle all outstanding entitlements. SSANU warned of imminent industrial action if salary delays and withheld payments are not addressed.

stories.title: IDF hammers Iranian weapons production sites; Iran files salvos of missiles at south
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck Iranian weapons production sites including an anti-aircraft missile assembly plant in Tehran. Iran launched six missile salvos in response and confirmed the death of IRGC naval chief Tangsiri.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel to seize more Lebanese lands and expand 'buffer zone'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announced plans to seize additional territory in southern Lebanon and expand the military buffer zone, stating the move aims to counter Hezbollah threats and push anti-tank missile fire away from northern Israel.

stories.title: Iranian leaders 'do not take any statements from Donald Trump seriously '
stories.summary: According to FRANCE 24's correspondent in Tehran, Iranian leaders do not take U.S. President Donald Trump's statements seriously, even as U.S. and Israeli attacks continued on March 30. Trump suggested the U.S. could seize Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Mar. 30 – IDF set to vastly expand buffer zone in Lebanon
stories.summary: Military correspondent Emanuel Fabian reported on joint US-Israel operations in Iran, Iranian missile strikes on Israel, and the IDF's plans to significantly expand its buffer zone in southern Lebanon. A West Bank battalion was also pulled for extremist behavior.

stories.title: Fourth suspect arrested in arson attack on Czech factory that made drones and thermal optics for Ukraine
stories.summary: Czech police arrested a fourth suspect in connection with an arson attack on a factory that produced drones and thermal optics for Ukraine. The three previously detained suspects face terrorism charges, and an "anti-Israel" group that claimed responsibility had created its accounts just one day before the attack, despite the factory having no Israeli ties.

stories.title: World Cup 2026 under fire as Amnesty warns of human rights risks for fans
stories.summary: Amnesty International has warned of human rights risks for fans attending the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The organization raised concerns about conditions on the ground despite the tournament being promoted as a celebration of global football.

stories.title: Palestine aIly Ireland under fire for allowing weapons transfers to Israel
stories.summary: Ireland's Shannon Airport is facing renewed scrutiny for serving as a transit hub for US military operations, with critics questioning weapons transfers potentially linked to Israel despite Ireland's pro-Palestinian stance.

stories.title: Latin Patriarch will have access to Jerusalem holy site after police stopped entry
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister stated that Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, was asked not to enter the Church of the Holy Sepulchre over safety concerns. Access to the holy site has since been restored following the incident.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages in seven regions due to new attacks
stories.summary: As of March 30, power outages affected users in seven Ukrainian regions following new Russian attacks on the energy grid. The state energy company Ukrenergo reported the disruptions resulted from the latest wave of strikes.

stories.title: Clitoral nerves mapped for first time, thirty years after male counterpart
stories.summary: Scientists have mapped the nerves of the human clitoris for the first time, approximately thirty years after the equivalent mapping was completed for male anatomy.

stories.title: Iran hangs two convicted of links to banned opposition
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of having links to the banned Mujahedin-e Khalq (MEK) opposition group and allegedly plotting to overthrow the state. The executions come amid continued unrest and international scrutiny over disputed death tolls from recent protests.

stories.title: EU tackles Europe's housing crisis
stories.summary: The European Union adopted an affordable housing plan and appointed a housing commissioner to address soaring purchase and rental prices across Europe. Since 2013, housing costs have risen sharply, with rental supply shrinking and properties increasingly diverted to short-term holiday lets.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits Lebanese army checkpoint in south
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit a Lebanese army checkpoint in southern Lebanon on Monday, wounding at least five soldiers in what officials described as the first direct attack on an active military post since the start of Israel's war on Lebanon.

stories.title: In photos: Aftermath of Israeli strikes on Beirut
stories.summary: Multiple Israeli air strikes hit targets in Beirut on March 30, 2026, damaging residential buildings and sending smoke rising over the city's southern suburbs as the broader US-Israel war on Iran continued.

stories.title: Malaysia’s food prices could rise by 50% as fuel costs soar, traders warn
stories.summary: Trade associations in Malaysia warned that food prices could rise by as much as 50 percent due to soaring fuel costs linked to the Iran war. The Malaysian government's fuel subsidy costs are estimated to spike more than fourfold to about 3.2 billion ringgit (US$795 million).

stories.title: Protesters block Knesset entrance following approval of 2026 state budget
stories.summary: Protesters blocked the entrance to Israel's Knesset following the parliamentary approval of the 2026 state budget. Demonstrators criticized the government for passing the budget while Israeli citizens faced ongoing security threats.

stories.title: Africa: African Court Should Protect People Displaced By Climate Change
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch has called on the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights to protect people displaced by climate change across the continent. The organization said a favorable decision could promote rights-based adaptation and durable solutions for affected populations.

stories.title: Thousands of Lebanese trapped behind Israeli frontlines rely on humanitarian aid
stories.summary: Thousands of Lebanese civilians remain trapped behind Israeli frontlines in southern Lebanon as humanitarian conditions worsen. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu confirmed plans to expand a military buffer zone along the border, while sweeping evacuation orders south of the Litani River have displaced over a million people.

stories.title: Israel’s new immigrants find purpose in volunteering as war continues - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Recent immigrants to Israel are integrating into society by volunteering and helping rebuild communities affected by the ongoing war.

stories.title: Myanmar paves way for junta chief to be civilian president, ruling with ‘iron fist’
stories.summary: Myanmar's parliament nominated coup leader General Min Aung Hlaing as a vice-presidential candidate on Monday, paving the way for him to become civilian president. The junta simultaneously replaced him as military commander. Min Aung Hlaing has ruled since seizing power from Aung San Suu Kyi's government in 2021.

stories.title: Occupying Iran's Kharg island could be 'dangerous and risky' for US forces
stories.summary: The U.S. has amassed its largest military force in the Middle East in over 20 years. While Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested ground operations may not be necessary, President Trump expressed interest in seizing Iran's Kharg Island, the country's primary oil export terminal in the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Israel’s new immigrants find purpose in volunteering as war continues - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Recent immigrants to Israel are volunteering to support communities affected by the ongoing war. The efforts are helping new arrivals integrate into Israeli society while assisting in community rebuilding.

stories.title: ‘To do something nobody’s done’: quantum physicist Zhu Zijie leaves Europe for China
stories.summary: Quantum physicist Zhu Zijie, who published in both Science and Nature by age 30 for work on cold atoms, has left the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH Zurich) to return to China. Zhu originally graduated from Peking University before pursuing graduate studies in Switzerland.

stories.title: In Chernihiv region, kindergarten and enterprises damaged due to Russian attacks; one person injured
stories.summary: Russian attacks on the Chernihiv region on March 29 injured a teenage girl born in 2010. The strikes also damaged residential buildings, a kindergarten, a museum, and local businesses in the area.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing nominated in presidential process
stories.summary: Myanmar's military junta nominated junta chief Min Aung Hlaing for president in a formal process in the capital Naypyidaw. Former spymaster Ye Win Oo was promoted to head the military at a separate ceremony.

stories.title: ‘Transnational repression’: Iranian diaspora faces harassment, death threats, pressure on families
stories.summary: Dr. Roya Boroumand of the Abdorrahman Boroumand Center for Human Rights described Iran's campaign of transnational repression targeting diaspora communities. She stated the strategy began after the 1979 revolution and has since evolved using modern technology to silence dissent, deter political engagement, and reinforce the regime's legitimacy abroad.

stories.title: IDF kills suspected terrorist after attempted vehicle ramming
stories.summary: IDF soldiers killed a suspected terrorist after the individual reportedly attempted a vehicle-ramming attack. The military stated the suspect was accelerating toward soldiers in a manner that posed an immediate threat.

stories.title: Cuba to receive shipment of Russia oil after US lifts pressure
stories.summary: The Russian oil tanker Anatoly Kolodkin is expected to dock at Cuba's western port of Matanzas to deliver crude oil. The shipment follows an apparent reversal of the U.S. blockade on Cuba by President Trump. Havana had faced increasing isolation after Washington arrested Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and intensified pressure on the island.

stories.title: New Israeli defence budget 'another indication of breach between people and government'
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed its annual budget on March 30 in an overnight session, securing Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition through the fall. The opposition criticized increased funding for ultra-Orthodox communities amid rising war costs. Separately, Netanyahu announced an expansion of military operations in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel media reports strike on oil refinery in Haifa
stories.summary: Israeli media reported a strike on an oil refinery in the northern city of Haifa on Monday. The incident followed reports of a fresh salvo of missiles fired from Iran, though the exact cause was not immediately confirmed.

stories.title: Israel, US and Iran exchange airstrikes despite attempted talks
stories.summary: Israel and Iran exchanged airstrikes, with Israeli forces hitting targets in Tehran and Iran's Revolutionary Guards striking an industrial complex in southern Israel. Pakistan announced on March 29 that it would soon host U.S.-Iran talks, though neither Washington nor Tehran immediately confirmed participation.

stories.title: French football team ends American friendlies on high success
stories.summary: France's national football team completed a successful tour in the United States with friendly victories over Brazil and Colombia ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Coach Didier Deschamps used the matches to evaluate players and tactics. The final squad is expected to be announced on May 14.

stories.title: Rob Schneider calls on US to restore military draft
stories.summary: American actor and comedian Rob Schneider called on the U.S. to restore the military draft amid the ongoing war with Iran. Posting on X, Schneider argued the military would teach young people about their country's greatness.

stories.title: Land Day in Gaza: Between memory and the fight for what remains
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza marked Land Day amid ongoing war, siege, and displacement, with the commemoration shifting from historical land rights advocacy to a focus on basic survival.

stories.title: What do we know about the failed bomb attack against Bank of America in Paris?
stories.summary: French investigators suspect Iranian state involvement in a failed bomb attack on a Bank of America branch in Paris on March 29. Three minors have been taken into police custody, including those who attempted to detonate the device. France's interior minister said intermediaries may have acted on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

stories.title: China ‘city work’ new dating trend promotes love on the move as couples earn extra cash
stories.summary: Young couples in Chinese cities have adopted a dating trend called "city work," where they ride e-bikes and deliver takeaway food together during evening outings. The trend offers a low-cost alternative to traditional dates while allowing pairs to earn extra income and combat burnout.

stories.title: College Republicans director made racist and sexist remarks on live streams
stories.summary: A Guardian review revealed that newly appointed College Republicans of America political director Kai Schwemmer made racist, antisemitic, homophobic, and sexist statements on livestreams. He said he would accept legal slavery if abortion were criminalized and described himself as opposed to universal suffrage.

stories.title: Iraq risks Arab ties as Iran-aligned groups strike Gulf nations
stories.summary: Joint Arab condemnation of cross-border attacks by Iran-aligned armed groups operating from Iraqi territory has exposed Baghdad's inability to control proxy militias, straining Iraq's relationships with Gulf Arab nations.

stories.title: Iran strikes Gulf, as Tehran confirms death of IRGC commander
stories.summary: Tehran experienced widespread power outages after Israeli strikes targeted the city's power grids. Iranian authorities confirmed the death of an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) commander in an attack that occurred the previous week.

stories.title: Israel to expand operations in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered an expansion of military operations in southern Lebanon targeting the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group. The Lebanese government reported that approximately 1,200 people have been killed in the country since fighting began in early March.

stories.title: France beat Colombia 3-1 to showcase firepower and squad depth
stories.summary: France defeated Colombia 3-1 in an international football match, with Desire Doue scoring twice and Marcus Thuram adding another goal. Kylian Mbappe came on as a substitute during the match.

stories.title: Trump wants to 'take oil' in Iran as 'tit-for-tat violence' continues
stories.summary: President Trump proposed that U.S. forces seize Iran's Kharg Island, its main oil export terminal in the Persian Gulf. U.S.-Israeli strikes reportedly hit residential areas and non-military targets in Tehran over the weekend, while Iran retaliated by targeting industrial sites in the region.

stories.title: Europe must reinvent warfare for ‘era of shocks,’ NATO’s Vandier says
stories.summary: NATO's top officer for force transformation, Admiral Vandier, urged Europe to reinvent its approach to warfare for what he described as an era of shocks. He emphasized that the alliance must maintain a credible deterrent posture to discourage Russian aggression.

stories.title: Sexual assault survivor calls failure of Travelodge boss to meet MPs ‘shocking’
stories.summary: A woman sexually assaulted at a Travelodge after a man was given a key card to her room criticized CEO Jo Boydell for canceling a meeting with over 20 MPs. The MPs had sought to discuss the chain's security procedures and its offer of a £30 refund to the victim.

stories.title: ‘Hey, Cuba’
stories.summary: The article discusses US President Donald Trump's public remarks about potentially "taking Cuba" and argues Pakistan should pay attention given Cuba's historical support for struggles in Palestine, South Africa, Kashmir, and Vietnam.

stories.title: Eight people injured in Russian strikes in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Kharkiv regional center and 19 other settlements over a 24-hour period, injuring eight people. The strikes targeted multiple locations across the region.

stories.title: Australia to halve fuel tax to keep prices within reach of citizens amid Iran war
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a three-month halving of the country's 52-cent-per-litre fuel tax to help motorists facing surging petrol prices caused by the Middle East war. The measure is expected to cost the government approximately A$2.55 billion.

stories.title: Russian oil tanker reaches Cuba after Trump appears to loosen blockade
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker reached Cuban waters hours after U.S. President Donald Trump signaled he had "no problem" with its arrival. The delivery comes amid a broader U.S. blockade on oil supplies to Cuba.

stories.title: Talk or escalate?
stories.summary: The article examines President Trump's contradictory signals of pursuing peace talks with Iran while simultaneously threatening military escalation. Pakistan emerged as a potential intermediary, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif offering to host US-Iran talks.

stories.title: Algeria mourns former president Liamine Zeroual
stories.summary: Algeria is mourning former President Liamine Zeroual, who has died. Zeroual was widely respected for guiding the country through a period of crisis and laying the groundwork for political reforms before withdrawing from public life.

stories.title: Trump reverses course on Cuban oil blockade, allows Russian tanker to pass
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump appeared to relax a de facto oil blockade on Cuba, allowing a Russian tanker carrying crude to approach the Caribbean island.

stories.title: An in-depth look at Israel's new death penalty law
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law making the death penalty a default sentence for Palestinians convicted in military court of fatal attacks. The legislation was introduced by the far-right coalition and has drawn criticism as discriminatory.

stories.title: Israel poised to pass controversial death penalty bill
stories.summary: Israel's far-right government introduced legislation to expand the death penalty as a deterrence measure. The Knesset is expected to vote on the controversial bill this week.

stories.title: Controversial death penalty bill set to pass in Israel
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset is expected to vote this week on a bill expanding the use of the death penalty. The controversial legislation was introduced by Israel's far-right government coalition.

stories.title: War in Iran and fertiliser security
stories.summary: The war in Iran has disrupted oil and gas supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, sharply raising global energy prices. These shocks have cascaded into the fertiliser sector, threatening nitrogen-based fertiliser production concentrated in the Middle East, including major urea-producing nations like Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Iran.

stories.title: Hong Kong eases rules for Wang Fuk Court residents retrieving belongings
