stories.summary: Hong Kong officials eased retrieval rules for displaced residents of fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court, allowing repeated trips to collect belongings. Deputy Chief Secretary Warner Cheuk Wing-hing said residents could coordinate with designated social workers, responding to an online petition calling for greater flexibility.

stories.title: IDF chief: Detention, alleged assault of CNN crew in West Bank ‘grave ethical incident’
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir called the detention and alleged assault of a CNN crew in the West Bank a "grave ethical incident." A reservist who made far-right remarks during the incident is expected to be dismissed, and the battalion was removed from West Bank service.

stories.title: South Africa: Can Talks Save South Africa's NHI From A Courtroom War?
stories.summary: South African Health Minister Aaron Motsoaledi has met with the South African Medical Association, one of the groups legally challenging the National Health Insurance Act. President Cyril Ramaphosa is also planning further talks with Business Unity South Africa to discuss alternatives to the NHI.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms drench UAE and Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Severe thunderstorms struck the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, delivering up to 150mm of rain in just a few days. An abnormally strong jet stream drove a deep low-pressure system north of Saudi Arabia, pulling moist tropical air from the Indian Ocean into the typically arid region.

stories.title: 'Peace is everything': Women-led festival channels message of peace in Eastern DRC
stories.summary: A women-led festival in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo featured Congolese rapper performances carrying messages of peace. The event highlighted women's roles in promoting peace amid ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 150 of the 164 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 150 of 164 Russian drones launched against the country since the evening of March 29. The drones were part of a large-scale aerial assault by Russian forces.

stories.title: Donald Trump says U.S. negotiating with Iran directly and indirectly
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated the United States is negotiating with Iran both directly and indirectly, suggesting a deal could come soon.

stories.title: Syrian army says drone attacks targeted bases near Iraqi border, studying response options
stories.summary: The Syrian army reported large-scale drone attacks targeting several of its bases near the Iraqi border, stating that most drones were intercepted and that Damascus is assessing response options.

stories.title: Israeli parliament to vote on death penalty for Palestinians
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset is set to debate a bill that would make the death penalty a standard sentence for West Bank Palestinians convicted of killing Israelis. The proposed legislation has drawn significant criticism and faces legal challenges.

stories.title: Trump suggests U.S. could take Iran's Kharg Island
stories.summary: President Trump suggested the US could seize Iran's Kharg Island, a critical oil export terminal. Iran responded by threatening a ground invasion of Gulf Arab countries and new attacks if US troops land on Iranian territory.

stories.title: Afghan truce
stories.summary: Pakistan announced the resumption of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq, which targets terrorist sites in Afghanistan and Afghan Taliban positions, following a temporary Eid al-Fitr truce. Cross-border fire from the Afghan side at Torkham was reported shortly after the truce expired, injuring a Pakistani official.

stories.title: Trump says US could ‘take the oil’ in Iran, seize export hub: Financial Times
stories.summary: President Trump told the Financial Times that his "preference would be to take the oil" in Iran, suggesting the US could seize Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub. Such an operation would require invading and holding the island.

stories.title: Smoke rise from Beirut suburbs following Israeli attack
stories.summary: Smoke was seen rising above buildings in Beirut's southern suburbs following an Israeli air strike on the area.

stories.title: Spain summons Israeli envoy over Latin Patriarch's church access
stories.summary: Spain summoned Israel's top envoy in Madrid after Israeli police blocked Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa from holding Palm Sunday mass at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. An agreement on church access was subsequently reached.

stories.title: Oil rises, stocks fall as Iran war enters fifth week and further escalation looms
stories.summary: Oil prices surged past $115 per barrel as the war in Iran entered its fifth week. Houthi strikes on Israel raised fears of disruption to shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb strait, compounding supply concerns from the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict is affecting global businesses, including used car dealers in Japan and South Korea.

stories.title: IDF suspending Netzach Yehuda, not just company involved, following CNN team debacle
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it is suspending the entire Netzach Yehuda battalion, not just the company directly involved in the alleged assault of a CNN crew. The IDF opposes full disbandment of the unit, which is a flagship project for integrating Haredi soldiers.

stories.title: Russia’s spring offensive has stalled at Ukraine’s Fortress Belt — ISW says it won’t break through in 2026
stories.summary: According to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), Russia's spring offensive has stalled at Ukraine's defensive Fortress Belt and is unlikely to achieve a breakthrough in 2026. The 3rd Combined Arms Army, positioned to advance on Sloviansk, has made no territorial gains in a week after a month of advances east of the city.

stories.title: In Gaza, families are trying to save their children from suicide
stories.summary: Mental health professionals in Gaza describe an entire society experiencing continuous collective trauma rather than isolated cases of depression or anxiety. Families are reportedly struggling to prevent their children from attempting suicide amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: The cost-of-living spillover
stories.summary: The article examines how the Gulf conflict is driving up consumer prices in Pakistan, with petrol and diesel price increases of around 20 percent expected to add over 8 percentage points to domestic inflation, disproportionately affecting everyday expenses for ordinary citizens including over 25 million motorcyclists.

stories.title: Trump wants to invade Iran to seize oil, calls US objectors ‘stupid people’
stories.summary: The Trump administration has deployed US Marines to the Middle East in preparation for a possible takeover of Iran's key oil export infrastructure. Trump called domestic objectors to seizing Iranian oil "stupid people."

stories.title: War update: 147 combat engagements on front line over past day, Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka directions most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces recorded 147 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line on March 29. The Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions saw the heaviest fighting.

stories.title: CORPORATE WINDOW: A new auto policy needed for localisation
stories.summary: Pakistan's imports of CKD/SKD auto assembly kits reached $1.3 billion in the first eight months of FY26, up from $575 million the prior year, driven by strong vehicle demand and low interest rates. The article calls for a new auto policy focused on localisation amid disruptions from the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Gulf instability and remittances’ risk
stories.summary: The article examines risks to Pakistan's economy from the Middle East conflict, noting that 600,000–700,000 Pakistani workers travel annually to Gulf countries for employment. Rising geopolitical tensions threaten both overseas employment opportunities and remittance flows that are critical to Pakistan's economic stability.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper killed in southern Lebanon as Israeli invasion intensifies
stories.summary: An Indonesian UN peacekeeper was confirmed killed by artillery fire in southern Lebanon as Israel's ground invasion of the region intensified.

stories.title: Nigeria: Many Killed in Plateau Attack, Govt Imposes Curfew
stories.summary: An attack in Plateau State, Nigeria, killed an unconfirmed number of residents, prompting the government to impose a curfew. The incident triggered widespread panic and a heavy security deployment in the affected area.

stories.title: South Africa: Ramaphosa Orders Ministers to Ease Pain of April Fuel Price Increase
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has directed ministers to find ways to ease the impact of an April fuel price increase. The rise is linked to global disruptions after Iran shut a key oil shipping route, pushing up fuel and food costs domestically.

stories.title: Ukraine’s intelligence names 51 ships fueling Russia’s war economy through oil exports and occupied port runs
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) expanded its maritime blacklist to 51 vessels allegedly supporting Russia's war economy through oil exports and operations at occupied ports. The agency is now directly warning ship captains that liability for participating in Russia's maritime operations is unavoidable.

stories.title: Iran confirms death of Revolutionary Guard commander Tangsiri, statement says
stories.summary: Iran confirmed the death of Revolutionary Guard Navy Commander Alireza Tangsiri from severe injuries sustained in an earlier attack. Israel had announced his killing along with other senior naval officials on March 26.

stories.title: Trump says he wants Iran oil as Israel continues Tehran strikes
stories.summary: Israel announced it was conducting further military strikes on Tehran on Monday. Simultaneously, U.S. President Donald Trump publicly stated his interest in acquiring Iran's oil resources.

stories.title: Mob retaliates after gunmen kill 12 in Nigeria bar
stories.summary: Gunmen killed at least 12 people at a bar in Jos, the capital of Nigeria's Plateau state. A retaliatory mob subsequently killed 10 more people. Plateau state, in central Nigeria's Middle Belt region, experiences recurring violence often linked to land disputes between farmers and herders.

stories.title: Dar hints at US, Iran talks as quad pushes peace off-ramp
stories.summary: Pakistan signaled it could host direct US-Iran talks after Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar concluded a four-nation meeting in Islamabad with Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Egypt emphasizing dialogue and diplomacy to end Gulf hostilities. Dar was also set to travel to Beijing to meet China's foreign minister.

stories.title: Squeezing the middle class
stories.summary: The article compares Pakistan's and India's personal income tax systems, noting that Pakistani salaried individuals begin paying tax at annual earnings of 600,000 rupees, while India's threshold is higher. Pakistan's tax system disproportionately burdens salaried professionals and entrepreneurs due to a limited tax base.

stories.title: Murder trial opens over alleged masonic lodge crime network in Paris
stories.summary: Twenty-two defendants, including former intelligence agents and police officers, go on trial in Paris on charges of murder and other serious crimes linked to the Athanor masonic lodge in Puteaux. Seven face possible life sentences for alleged murder, attempted murder, and criminal conspiracy.

stories.title: Russian forces strike 25 settlements in Sumy region over past day, leaving three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck 25 settlements in Ukraine's Sumy region over the past day, injuring three people. The attacks targeted multiple locations across the region.

stories.title: One court, ten judges, twenty thousand cases — and a single war crimes verdict in three years
stories.summary: Ukraine has recorded over 217,000 war crimes since Russia's full-scale invasion, but courts have delivered only 245 verdicts, just 23 with the defendant present. A Suspilne investigation found the judiciary operates at roughly half its required staffing, while the ICC focuses only on senior commanders.

stories.title: ‘This is a nightmare scenario if it escalates further.’
stories.summary: Analyst Elisabeth Kendall commented that a Houthi attack on Israel demonstrated the group's willingness to follow through on its threats, warning of a nightmare scenario if the situation escalates further.

stories.title: Japan’s property market is well placed to withstand Iran war energy shock
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Japan's property market is relatively well positioned to withstand the energy shock caused by the Iran war. Traditional safe havens including government bonds and gold have declined, with bonds falling on fears of interest rate hikes and gold dropping about 15 percent this month.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian man near Hebron
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed Palestinian man Ramzi Abdul Hakim al-Awawdeh near the village of Kharsa, southwest of Hebron in the occupied West Bank. Sources reported that soldiers prevented medical personnel from reaching him.

stories.title: What the Claude AI chatbot really does for CENTCOM
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command has integrated the Claude AI chatbot into a broader operational system to assist with military functions. The deployment represents part of a growing trend of incorporating artificial intelligence tools into wartime decision-making, raising concerns about the accelerating speed of military operations.

stories.title: Saudi, Turkey, Egypt urge dialogue after Pakistan-hosted talks
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt concluded talks hosted by Pakistan in Islamabad, calling for diplomacy, an immediate end to Gulf hostilities, and structured negotiations between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Brent crude hits $116 a barrel after Trump says he wants to ‘take the oil in Iran’
stories.summary: Brent crude oil surged to $116 a barrel after U.S. President Donald Trump said he wanted to "take the oil in Iran" and suggested seizing Kharg Island, Iran's main export hub. Asian stock markets dropped sharply on escalation fears.

stories.title: Russian troops shell 38 settlements in Kherson region over past day, leaving one killed, three injured
stories.summary: Russian troops shelled 38 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region over the past 24 hours, killing one person and wounding three others.

stories.title: Three killed as unfinished building collapses on church service in Ghana
stories.summary: Three people were killed when an unfinished building collapsed during a church service in Ghana. Local residents said the structure, located within a school complex, had been in use despite being incomplete for several years.

stories.title: Iranian media says strikes hit park, university and veterinary hospital
stories.summary: Iranian media reported air strikes hit multiple civilian sites across Iran, including an amusement park in Isfahan, a university facility and veterinary hospital in Urmia, and a petrochemical plant in Tabriz.

stories.title: US allows Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba, reversing course on blockade
stories.summary: The United States allowed a Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba, reversing its blockade policy. The US had previously cut off Venezuelan oil exports to Cuba after toppling Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3.

stories.title: Did Israel miscalculate in launching the war on Iran?
stories.summary: The article examines Israel's decision to launch military operations against Iran alongside the United States, questioning whether the campaign proceeded without a realistic political endgame.

stories.title: Fuel stocks sufficient to meet national demand, says PM
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that adequate petroleum reserves are available nationally and urged citizens to avoid unnecessary travel and adopt teleconferencing to conserve fuel amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Trump insists killing of Iran’s leaders ‘truly is regime change,’ deal to end war ‘could be soon’
stories.summary: President Trump claimed the killing of Iranian leaders constitutes regime change, saying their replacements are "very reasonable" and a deal to end the war could come soon, while indicating openness to a ground operation to seize Iran's Kharg Island oil assets.

stories.title: Every Soldier a Software Builder: Governing the Army’s New Digital Workforce
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has expanded internal software development through programs like the Army Software Factory and platforms such as Palantir's Army Vantage and GenAI.mil. An analysis examines governance challenges as the Department of Defense builds a digital workforce among military personnel.

stories.title: Every Soldier a Software Builder: Governing the Army’s New Digital Workforce
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has fielded digital platforms including Palantir's Army Vantage and the Department of Defense's GenAI.mil to improve data analysis and decision-making. An analysis examines governance challenges as the Army builds an internal software development workforce, building on earlier efforts like the Army Software Factory.

stories.title: Every Soldier a Software Builder: Governing the Army’s New Digital Workforce
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense has expanded internal software development through programs like the Air Force's Kessel Run, the Army Software Factory, and the Marine Corps Software Factory. The Army also deployed data platforms including Palantir's Army Vantage and the DoD's GenAI.mil to improve analysis and decision-making across the force.

stories.title: Easter bank holiday expected to be UK’s busiest on roads in four years
stories.summary: The Easter bank holiday weekend is expected to be the busiest on UK roads in four years, with nearly 21 million leisure journeys planned from Thursday to Monday. The travel surge comes despite rising fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Why the Iran war may force countries to rely less on natural gas
stories.summary: The war in Iran is prompting countries to reconsider their reliance on natural gas imports. The conflict underscores the risks of depending on imported gas during periods of geopolitical instability.

stories.title: Russia loses 840 troops, 48 artillery systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost approximately 870 soldiers killed or wounded in the past 24 hours, bringing total estimated Russian casualties since February 2022 to roughly 1,296,700. Additionally, 48 Russian artillery systems were reportedly destroyed.

stories.title: Global food waste crisis undermines climate and security, says UNEP official
stories.summary: A UNEP official highlighted the global food waste crisis, noting that over one billion tonnes of edible food—nearly one-fifth of all food available to consumers—is discarded annually. The statement coincided with the International Day of Zero Waste observed on Monday.

stories.title: WTO talks in Yaounde end in deadlock over e-commerce customs duties
stories.summary: World Trade Organization ministerial talks in Yaoundé, Cameroon, ended early on Monday without reaching an agreement. Deep divisions among member states over e-commerce customs duties blocked a deal, resulting in a deadlock.

stories.title: Displaced families in Sudan struggle as aid falls short
stories.summary: World Food Programme aid disruptions in Sudan's White Nile State have left thousands of displaced families without access to essential supplies, deepening the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: As petrol prices approach US$4 a gallon amid Iran war, Americans rethink holidays
stories.summary: The Iran war, combined with spring break travel demand, has pushed US petrol prices toward US$4 per gallon, levels not seen since 2022. Rising fuel costs are leading Americans to reconsider their holiday plans.

stories.title: Russian tanker heads to Cuba despite U.S. oil blockade
stories.summary: A Russian tanker is heading to Cuba despite a US oil blockade, potentially delivering the island's first oil shipment since January. Cuba, with a population of 9.6 million, has been enduring a deepening energy and economic crisis.

stories.title: Russians carry out 823 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region in one day, leaving one killed, four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 823 strikes on 38 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over a 24-hour period. One person was killed and four were injured in the Zaporizhzhia and Polohy districts.

stories.title: Victorian Liberals to hold another preselection after candidate who defeated Moira Deeming withdraws
stories.summary: The Victorian Liberal Party in Australia will hold a new preselection after candidate Dinesh Gourisetty withdrew. Gourisetty, who had defeated Moira Deeming, was found to have written a court character reference for a friend convicted of sexually assaulting a child.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader accepts Xi's invite to visit China
stories.summary: Taiwan opposition Kuomintang (KMT) leader Cheng Li-wun accepted an invitation from Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit China. The visit, expected in April, would be the first by a sitting leader of Taiwan's main opposition party in a decade.

stories.title: Industry in crosshairs amid no let-up in Iran war
stories.summary: Iran struck aluminium producers in the UAE and Bahrain and a chemical plant in Israel's Neot Hovav industrial zone, triggering a hazardous materials incident. US-Israeli forces bombed an Iranian port city, Isfahan University, and a Tehran media office, killing at least five people. Iran's parliament speaker accused the US of plotting a ground invasion after 3,500 troops arrived in the Middle East.

stories.title: Trump claims ‘regime change’ achieved in Iran war, predicts deal ‘soon’
stories.summary: Israel struck military targets across Tehran on Monday as the Iran war continued, while Iran launched fresh strikes on Israel, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia. U.S. President Donald Trump claimed "regime change" had been achieved and predicted a deal "soon," without ruling out ground operations.

stories.title: Putin Is Not Trapped: Why Regime Survival Does Not Depend on Victory
stories.summary: An analysis challenges the widespread assumption that Russian President Vladimir Putin cannot survive a loss in Ukraine. The piece argues that this framing—central to Biden-era escalation management debates—overstates the existential nature of the war for Putin's regime and misreads his available options.

stories.title: Putin Is Not Trapped: Why Regime Survival Does Not Depend on Victory
stories.summary: An analysis challenges the widely held assumption that Russian President Vladimir Putin cannot survive a loss in Ukraine. The argument that the war is existential for his regime shaped Biden-era debates over escalation management, but the piece questions whether regime survival truly depends on military victory.

stories.title: Drink-driving death in Malaysia spirals into race-baiting, inflames ethnic tensions
stories.summary: A fatal road crash in Klang, Malaysia, on Sunday involving an allegedly speeding Honda City that struck and killed a motorcyclist has sparked racially charged commentary online. Police said the driver, a local man in his twenties, crossed into the opposite lane on Jalan Raya Barat.

stories.title: Govt comes up with hybrid plan to tackle power crisis
stories.summary: Pakistan's government is preparing a hybrid plan combining two to three hours of daily load-shedding, compulsory conservation measures, and tariff hikes to manage summer electricity demand amid disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict. LNG supplies are expected to drop to near zero, and a railways dispute is affecting coal transport to power plants.

stories.title: Indonesian UN peacekeeper killed in Lebanon, origin of the projectile unclear
stories.summary: An Indonesian UN peacekeeper was killed in southern Lebanon, with the origin of the projectile still unknown. UNIFIL launched an investigation to determine the circumstances of the incident near its position.

stories.title: Pro-government Z-channels lose more than 40% of their views in Russia – CCD
stories.summary: According to Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation, pro-government Z-channels in Russia have lost more than 40% of their viewership. The decline is attributed to information-space blockings within the Russian Federation.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran: What’s happening on day 31 of attacks
stories.summary: On day 31 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, fears of a ground invasion grew as additional American troops arrived in the region, despite Trump's stated interest in diplomacy.

stories.title: The Importance of the Raid of Nassau
stories.summary: An analysis of the March 1776 raid on Nassau in the British Bahamas examines the first amphibious landing by U.S. Marines and sailors. While a tactical success, the operation was hampered by inexperience and poor judgment, offering lessons about command and control across distances and the need for adaptability.

stories.title: The Importance of the Raid of Nassau
stories.summary: On March 3, 1776, U.S. Marines and sailors conducted their first amphibious landing at Nassau in the British-controlled Bahamas. Though a tactical success, the raid's broader impact on the American War of Independence was limited by inexperience and poor judgment. The operation offers lessons on command, control, and adaptability for modern naval forces.

stories.title: China steps up North Korea connections as regular Beijing-Pyongyang flights resume
stories.summary: Air China resumed direct flights between Beijing and Pyongyang on Monday, marking a further warming of China–North Korea bilateral ties. The resumption comes weeks after passenger train services between the two countries were restored for the first time in six years.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed five drones, while Kuwait's National Guard downed five more. Air strikes hit multiple sites in Tehran including Mehrabad Airport, and at least three Palestinians were killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza City.

stories.title: 4 lions arrive at Haifa zoo amid species conservation efforts
stories.summary: Four lions arrived at the Haifa zoo as part of species conservation efforts. The three females are named Khitab, Kahale, and Kayana, and the male is called Marty. Keepers move them to protected areas when rocket sirens sound.

stories.title: Israeli Parliament approves 2026 state budget, spokesperson says
stories.summary: The Israeli Parliament approved the 2026 state budget, a spokesperson confirmed. Failure to pass the budget would likely have triggered a snap election within 90 days.

stories.title: Iran war draws attention to US troop presence in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran has drawn renewed attention to the US military presence in Saudi Arabia, placing the close American ally in a difficult position amid the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Fighters of Apachi battalion destroy Russian crossing with drones on Sloviansk axis
stories.summary: Soldiers of the Apachi unmanned systems battalion, part of Ukraine's 81st Separate Airmobile Brigade, destroyed a Russian river crossing over the Bakhmutka River in the Sloviansk direction using drones.

stories.title: Football: France beat Colombia, three days after defeating Brazil before World Cup
stories.summary: France defeated Colombia 3-1 in a friendly match held in the United States. The victory concluded a successful two-game tour for Les Bleus, following their win over Brazil three days earlier, as the team prepares for the 2026 World Cup.

stories.title: US to allow Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba, breaking blockade
stories.summary: The United States will reportedly allow a Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba, breaking the blockade. The ship's arrival could ease a rapidly accelerating energy crisis on the island.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills at least three people in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike southeast of Gaza City killed at least three Palestinians and wounded others near the Al-Shafi Mosque in the Zeitoun neighbourhood. The overall death toll from Israel's war on Gaza has reached 72,278 since October 7, 2023.

stories.title: Indonesian UN peacekeeper killed, some injured in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Indonesian peacekeeper serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) was killed and others were injured in southern Lebanon. UNIFIL is stationed in the region to monitor hostilities along the demarcation line with Israel.

stories.title: Russian troops attack critical infrastructure in Chernihiv
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a critical infrastructure facility in the Ukrainian city of Chernihiv. No further details on casualties or the specific target were immediately provided.

stories.title: Is the EU’s own veto right a leverage tool? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
stories.summary: The European Union's unanimous-vote requirement has been used 48 times since mid-2011 by individual member states to block collective action. Hungary most recently exercised its veto to block a €90 billion financial aid package for Ukraine.

stories.title: Three top Israeli chefs share their winning wartime Passover shortcuts
stories.summary: Three Israeli chefs — Ruhama Shitrit, Adeena Sussman, and Shalom Simcha Elbert — shared simplified Passover recipes suited to wartime conditions, emphasizing tasty but simple food while maintaining holiday traditions.

stories.title: Mohamed Salah warned against US move as MLS clubs eye Egyptian footballer
stories.summary: An Egyptian official warned Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah that a move to Major League Soccer would diminish his career, as San Diego FC reportedly expressed interest in signing the player.

stories.title: Iran war, rogue drones force European aviation safety rethink
stories.summary: Europe's top aviation safety regulator warned that the Iran war and the spread of drones are heightening risks for commercial aviation. The month-old conflict is reshaping Middle Eastern airspace and clogging flight corridors between Asia and Europe that previously transited the region.

stories.title: Under influence of Russian propaganda, occupiers commit suicide increasingly more often – Fedorov
stories.summary: According to Ukrainian official Fedorov, Russian servicemen are increasingly committing suicide after being wounded or while surrounded by drone swarms. He attributed the trend partly to the influence of Russian propaganda on its own troops.

stories.title: Settlers burn vehicles in town near Hebron
stories.summary: Video footage showed Israeli settlers setting vehicles on fire in the town of ad-Dhahiriya near Hebron in the occupied West Bank during an attack on the Palestinian community.

stories.title: Land Day: What happened in Palestine on March 30, 1976?
stories.summary: On March 30, 1976, six unarmed Palestinians were killed and over 100 injured by Israeli forces during protests against land confiscations, an event now commemorated annually as Land Day.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones kill one, damage homes, industry in southern Russia's Taganrog
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on the southern Russian city of Taganrog on March 29 killed one person, triggered fires, and damaged homes and industrial facilities, according to local officials.

stories.title: Oil rises above $115 and Asia shares slide as Iran war enters fifth week
stories.summary: Oil prices climbed above $115 per barrel and Asian equity markets declined as the Iran conflict entered its fifth week, following strikes on Israel by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen over the weekend.

stories.title: Israel says several missile salvos launched from Iran within an hour
stories.summary: Israel reported intercepting multiple missile salvos launched from Iran targeting southern parts of the country within approximately one hour. Sirens sounded across the Negev region, including in Dimona and Arad, as air defences engaged the threats.

stories.title: Hong Kong stocks fall with Asia as Iran conflict drives oil prices higher
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell on Monday as escalating Middle East tensions pushed Brent crude up 3.7 percent to $116.80 per barrel. Yemen's Houthi rebels launched attacks on Israel over the weekend, while the US deployed additional military forces to the region.

stories.title: Palm Sunday brings message of hope to Nigeria's Catholic faithful
stories.summary: Catholics in Lagos, Nigeria, marked Palm Sunday with prayers and processions to begin Holy Week. The celebrations took place against a backdrop of rising living costs and ongoing insecurity affecting many Nigerians.

stories.title: Russian oil tanker nears Cuba, Trump softens de facto blockade rhetoric
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker entered Cuban waters on Monday as US President Donald Trump appeared to relax a de facto oil blockade on Cuba. The delivery could provide a critical lifeline to the Caribbean island's struggling economy.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump says he wants to ‘take the oil’ in Iran and could seize Kharg Island ‘easily’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told the Financial Times he wants to "take the oil" in Iran and suggested seizing Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported Trump is weighing a military operation to extract nearly 1,000 pounds of uranium from Iran.

stories.title: UK savers told to act now before Easter Sunday cash Isa deadline
stories.summary: UK savers are being urged to use their annual cash Isa allowance before the deadline falls on Easter Sunday weekend. Interest rates of up to 4.45% are available, but a significant cut to next year's allowance is expected to drive a last-minute rush of applications.

stories.title: Pessimism takes root in UK as shoppers struggle to afford essentials
stories.summary: A UK survey found that half of households are struggling to afford everyday essentials as the Iran war drives up prices of oil, gas, and raw materials. Millions of Britons are dipping into savings or borrowing to cover costs amid rising pessimism about the economic outlook.

stories.title: China ‘left-behind aunties’, known as senior girl group, gain popularity for charm, dance skills
stories.summary: A group of over 20 rural women averaging 60 years old in Junying village, Henan province, China, have gained online popularity through live-streamed dance performances of viral routines, managed by local Gen Z organizers.

stories.title: Reza Pahlavi’s Iran vision deserves attention, not illusions - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial examined exiled Iranian crown prince Reza Pahlavi's vision for a post-regime Iran aligned with Israel. The piece acknowledged the vision as worth hearing but cautioned it must be weighed against political realities and regional risks.

stories.title: How Australia’s seven-month-long manhunt came to an end
stories.summary: Australian fugitive Dezi Freeman, wanted for fatally shooting two police officers at his rural property in August 2024, was apprehended after a seven-month nationwide manhunt.

stories.title: Video: Netanyahu orders military to ‘further expand’ invasion of Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced in a video statement that he ordered the military to further expand its invasion of southern Lebanon. The directive came amid rising tensions linked to the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: ‘Unconditional Surrender’ Is Always an Illusion
stories.summary: An analysis piece examines the concept of unconditional surrender as it relates to the ongoing war in Iran, arguing that the idea is a recurring American myth that resurfaces during major conflicts.

stories.title: Dezi Freeman shooting live updates: Victorian premier says ‘an evil man is dead and it’s over’ after Australian fugitive killed by police
stories.summary: Victorian Premier stated "an evil man is dead and it's over" after police fatally shot fugitive Dezi Freeman, 56, who had been on the run since allegedly killing two police officers in Porepunkah in the Australian alpine region in August. Victoria's chief commissioner addressed questions about the operation's tactics.

stories.title: By the 50th anniversary of Land Day, Palestinians lose most of their land
stories.summary: By the 50th anniversary of Land Day, Palestinians continue to face ongoing Israeli settlement expansion, land seizures, and restrictions on access to their remaining territory in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: ‘We’re killing them, bro’: Israelis correct Iranian online streamer
stories.summary: An Iranian musician publicly thanked young Israeli women for US-Israeli air strikes on Iran, prompting Israeli respondents online to correct the characterization of the military operations.

stories.title: Israel restores Latin Patriarch’s access to Holy Sepulchre church after international outcry
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed that Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa now has "full and immediate access" to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. The Patriarch had been blocked from holding Palm Sunday Mass at the site, triggering an international outcry.

stories.title: Only 30% of young people in Israel optimistic about future, Aluma survey reveals
stories.summary: A survey conducted by the Israeli nonprofit Aluma found that only 30% of young people in Israel are optimistic about the future. The organization said the findings reflect broader concerns observed in its ongoing fieldwork with Israeli youth.

stories.title: Thai undertaker brings corpse to petrol station to prove fuel need
stories.summary: A Thai undertaker brought a coffin containing a corpse to a petrol station to prove he needed extra fuel for cremation rather than black market resale. Thailand has been affected by fuel supply constraints linked to the US-Israel war on Iran, though Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has said reserves are sufficient for over three months.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer to host industry leaders for Middle East war talks
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer will convene industry leaders at Downing Street for talks on the Middle East war, with participants including executives from energy, shipping, and banking sectors.

stories.title: Report: Iran launched 5,471 attacks on US bases across seven countries
stories.summary: Iran launched at least 5,471 missile and drone attacks targeting US bases across seven Arab countries since late February, according to Anadolu news agency. The UAE recorded the highest number of interceptions, followed by Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and Oman.

stories.title: Israeli military reports multiple Iranian missile interceptions
stories.summary: The Israeli military detected and intercepted multiple ballistic missiles launched from Iran targeting southern Israel. Separate alerts were activated along the northern border due to a suspected drone infiltration from Lebanon, and five rockets aimed at Haifa were also intercepted.

stories.title: Fuel tax halved and free public transport offered as war pushes up prices in Australia
stories.summary: The Australian states of Victoria and Tasmania have introduced halved fuel taxes and free public transport to ease cost-of-living pressures driven by rising energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: UK’s Reeves to warn G-7 against unilateral trade moves during Iran war
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves is expected to warn G-7 counterparts against unilateral trade moves during the Iran war, arguing that protectionism and trade barriers could disrupt supply chains and increase costs.

stories.title: Dezi Freeman shot dead by police after seven-month manhunt
stories.summary: Victoria police confirmed that fugitive Dezi Freeman was fatally shot by officers after a seven-month manhunt in rural Victoria. Police Commissioner Mike Bush described the shooting as "justified" and said it brought closure to the families of the two police officers allegedly killed by Freeman in Porepunkah in August.

stories.title: Six suspected terrorists among 11 killed in Panjgur
stories.summary: Eleven people, including six suspected terrorists, were killed in armed attacks on houses in Panjgur, Balochistan. Separately, one person was killed and 12 others, including police personnel, were injured in firing and grenade attacks across different areas of Quetta.

stories.title: Gwadar Port attains ‘milestone’ with specialised vessel berthing
stories.summary: Pakistan's Maritime Affairs Minister highlighted the berthing of a specialized vessel at Gwadar Port as a milestone, promoting it as a secure alternative amid Gulf war disruptions to global shipping routes. Port Qasim also slashed tariffs by up to 50 percent to attract cargo.

stories.title: More ships arrive from Hormuz
stories.summary: Oil tankers continue arriving at Karachi's ports after Iranian authorities permitted Pakistani vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan National Shipping Company tankers MT Shalimar and MT Khairpur delivered crude oil and diesel, while MT Vienna Wood awaited berthing at Port Qasim with 57,000 tonnes of high-speed diesel.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outage schedules to be in effect for industrial users on Monday
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that power outage schedules will be applied to industrial consumers across all regions of Ukraine on the evening of Monday, March 30.

stories.title: Nigeria: Don't Drag Me Into Boxing Crisis, Adamu Warns Stakeholders
stories.summary: Retired Nigerian National Sports Commission Director General Amos Adamu warned stakeholders in the Nigeria Boxing Federation and the Nigeria Boxing Board of Control not to involve him in their ongoing leadership disputes.

stories.title: Nigeria: CBN Moves to Curb Pre-Election Liquidity Risks, Signals Firm Anti-Inflation Stance
stories.summary: A report by VNL Capital indicates that Nigeria's Central Bank is taking proactive steps to curb inflationary pressures and manage liquidity risks ahead of the 2027 election cycle.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu's Path to Recovery Unstoppable, Stop Playing Games - Presidency to ADC
stories.summary: Nigeria's presidency responded to criticism from the African Democratic Congress party, defending President Tinubu's governance record and economic recovery efforts as requiring difficult trade-offs.

stories.title: 42 arrested in HK$180 million crackdown on triad-linked renovation projects
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities arrested 42 people in a joint ICAC and police operation targeting triad-linked corruption involving a consultancy firm and building maintenance projects worth HK$180 million. Those arrested include the firm's owner, a registered inspector, and middlemen with organized crime ties.

stories.title: Nigeria: 146 Deaths Recorded, 38 Health Workers Infected As Lassa Fever Spreads in Nigeria
stories.summary: Nigeria has recorded 146 deaths from Lassa fever in 2026, with 38 health workers also infected. The disease has spread to 21 states and 82 local government areas across the country.

stories.title: Namibia: Nandi-Ndaitwah Urges Zambezi Residents to Accept Rice Aid, Move to Safety
stories.summary: Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah urged flood-affected residents in the Zambezi region to accept government-provided rice aid totaling over 9,000 bags and to relocate to safer areas.

stories.title: Rockets strike US military base near Baghdad, aircraft destroyed
stories.summary: Rockets struck the Victory Base complex, a US military installation near Baghdad, setting an Iraqi A32B transport aircraft ablaze. Drones were also reportedly launched toward the US Consulate in Erbil amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Kenya: NACADA Seizes 810 Litres of Smuggled Ethanol in Major Blow to Illicit Alcohol Trade
stories.summary: Kenya's National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse (NACADA) seized 810 litres of smuggled ethanol in a major operation targeting the country's illegal alcohol supply chain in Nairobi.

stories.title: Liberia: Liberian Footballer Jesse Francis Dies in Motorcycle Crash
stories.summary: Liberian footballer Jesse Francis, an attacking midfielder for Downtown FC, died in a motorcycle crash late Saturday. His death has prompted widespread mourning across Liberia's football community.

stories.title: Liberia: Liberia Disbursed Just 35.5% of PHC Funds - Report Warns of Widening Health Financing Gap
stories.summary: A report found that Liberia disbursed only 35.5% of approved primary health care funding over a five-year period, highlighting deep budget execution inefficiencies as donor support declines.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing nominated as president
stories.summary: Myanmar's military leader Min Aung Hlaing, who has faced sanctions from Western nations, has been nominated as president and is widely expected to assume the role.

stories.title: 'JD or Marco?’: Iran war raises 2028 stakes as Trump weighs Vance vs. Rubio
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war has intensified discussion about the 2028 US presidential race, with Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both playing key roles in developing negotiations. The pair are widely viewed as potential successors to President Trump.

stories.title: Kenya: Floods Death Toll Hits 110 As Disaster Spreads Across 30 Counties
stories.summary: The death toll from flooding in Kenya has reached 110 as heavy rains continue across the country. The disaster has spread across 30 of Kenya's counties.

stories.title: Indonesian UN peacekeeper killed in Lebanon, ministry confirms
stories.summary: Indonesia confirmed that a UN peacekeeper killed in Lebanon was an Indonesian national, with three other wounded Indonesians from the same incident. The casualties resulted from indirect artillery fire near the UNIFIL position at Adchit al-Qusayr.

stories.title: Trump says Iran’s ‘had regime change’ as he describes ‘boatloads of oil’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed that the US-Israeli war on Iran has effectively achieved regime change, citing the deaths of senior Iranian leaders. He also referenced offers of oil shipments from Iran as part of ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Kenya: I'm Just a Journalist, Says Larry Madowo After Winning Human Rights Defender Award,
stories.summary: CNN International Correspondent Larry Madowo, based in Kenya, was named human rights defender of the year. Madowo stated he considers himself a journalist rather than an activist, focused on holding leaders accountable.

stories.title: Indonesian peacekeeper killed in Lebanon explosion, 2nd critically injured
stories.summary: A UNIFIL peacekeeper from Indonesia was killed and another critically injured in an explosion near the village of Adchit al-Qusayr in southern Lebanon. Both UNIFIL and the Israeli military said they are investigating the origin of the projectile.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's Tuberculosis Deaths Drop By 63% Between 2015 and 2024
stories.summary: Nigeria's tuberculosis mortality rate dropped by 63% between 2015 and 2024, according to Dr. Dan Gadzama, Director of Public Health for the Federal Capital Territory Administration in Abuja.

stories.title: Liberia: Saah Joseph Unveils 'Policy-First' Politics, Pushes Dialogue On Border Tensions At PAP Convention
stories.summary: Liberian Senator Saah Joseph used the People Action Party convention to promote a policy-driven approach to opposition politics, emphasizing dialogue on border tensions and national unity over confrontation.

stories.title: Liberia: Liberia's Untapped Blue Economy Gets Its Defining Moment
stories.summary: Liberia held its National Fisheries Investment Conference 2026, organized by the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority with government backing, to develop the country's underutilized fisheries sector and blue economy potential.

stories.title: Liberia: Liberia Targets Global Investment to Unlock Untapped Fisheries Potential
stories.summary: Liberia convened the National Fisheries Investment Conference 2026 in Farmington, Margibi County, seeking global investment to develop its largely untapped ocean and inland water resources as a driver of economic growth.

stories.title: Nigeria: RCCG Pastor Challenges States, Govt On Communal Healthcare Delivery
stories.summary: Pastor Agbolade Okenla of the Redeemed Christian Church of God called on Nigeria's state and federal governments to ensure the availability and sustainability of quality healthcare services across communities nationwide.

stories.title: Nigeria: Experts List Conditions to Make Nigeria Air Travel Hub in West Africa
stories.summary: Aviation experts in Nigeria outlined conditions necessary for the country to become a major air travel hub for West Africa, addressing infrastructure and regulatory requirements.

stories.title: Nigeria: FCT Records 16,000 TB Cases As Treatment Success Hits 94%
stories.summary: Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory records approximately 16,000 tuberculosis cases annually, with the treatment success rate now reaching 94%, according to local health officials.

stories.title: Nigeria: Bridge Destruction Signals Dangerous Security Shift
stories.summary: Terrorists destroyed a bridge linking Wawa and Luma communities in Borgu Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria, using an improvised explosive device on March 23, 2026, killing eight civilians. The attack signals an expansion of insurgent activity into the north-central region.

stories.title: Nigeria: As Rainy Season Approaches, FCT Community Worries Over Leaking Health Centre
stories.summary: Residents of Ubosharu community in Kwali Area Council of Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory raised concerns about their deteriorating local health centre as the rainy season approaches, citing a leaking roof among other problems.

stories.title: Rwanda: What to Know As MPs Move to Scrutinise Ejoheza Access Bill
stories.summary: Rwanda's parliament has initiated detailed scrutiny of a draft law to amend the legal framework governing the EjoHeza Long-Term Savings Scheme, a national retirement savings program.

stories.title: Five EU governments found to ‘consistently’ dismantle rule of law
stories.summary: The Civil Liberties Union for Europe identified Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Italy, and Slovakia as EU member states "consistently and intentionally" eroding the rule of law. The watchdog, drawing on evidence from over 40 NGOs across 22 countries, also found democratic standards deteriorating in six additional member states.

stories.title: MPs wary of move against Starmer while war is raging
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war is giving many Labour MPs pause about the timing of a potential leadership challenge against Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Despite concerns following electoral difficulties, MPs are wary of moving against the leader while the conflict continues.

stories.title: Number of people helped by RNLI in UK and Channel Islands doubled in 2025
stories.summary: The number of people assisted by RNLI lifeguards on UK and Channel Islands beaches doubled in 2025 to over 35,000, up from about 18,000 in each of the two prior years. The charity believes the Middle East crisis may drive even higher domestic tourism in 2026.

stories.title: Petrochemical facility struck in northern Iran
stories.summary: A petrochemical facility in northern Iran was struck, targeting a plant that processes oil and natural gas into chemical products used in manufacturing plastics and other materials.

stories.title: Wartime Budgets Are an X-Ray of Presidential Priorities
stories.summary: President Lyndon Johnson's decision to escalate the Vietnam War undermined his plan to simultaneously fund military operations and domestic social programs. The article examines how wartime budget choices reveal presidential priorities.

stories.title: Fakhar Zaman charged with ball‑tampering by Pakistan board in PSL
stories.summary: Pakistan Cricket Board charged batsman Fakhar Zaman with ball-tampering during a Pakistan Super League match. The alleged incident reportedly occurred on Sunday.

stories.title: Malaysia jails ex-babysitter for 1 year over toddler’s death
stories.summary: A Malaysian court sentenced former babysitter Khairunnisa Ahmad Damamhuri to one year in jail and fined her 15,000 ringgit for negligence resulting in a toddler's death. She was also ordered to complete 48 hours of community service.

stories.title: Daily Telegraph apologises as dispute reignites between pro-Israel activist and Middle Eastern restaurant Cairo
stories.summary: Australia's Daily Telegraph published an apology to Sydney restaurant Cairo for causing distress after sending pro-Israel activist Ofir Birenbaum to the Middle Eastern eatery as part of an "undercover" story. The apology was part of an agreed joint statement resolving a legal dispute, with Cairo also apologising to the activist.

stories.title: Australia to halve fuel tax as global energy crisis deepens
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a plan to halve the national fuel tax as global crude oil prices surpassed $116 a barrel amid a deepening energy crisis.

stories.title: Israeli military launches attacks on infrastructure in Tehran
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it carried out strikes on Iranian government infrastructure across Tehran. Explosions were reported in multiple areas including the city of Rey south of the capital, as part of an intensifying campaign against strategic sites.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims strikes as Israel intercepts missiles, drone
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it fired missiles at the Israeli community of Dovev and the Ghajar area and launched drone swarms targeting the Shomera barracks in northern Israel. Israeli forces intercepted five missiles fired from Lebanon toward Haifa and shot down a drone over the Western Galilee.

stories.title: Ant smuggling in China, new airport rules in Hong Kong: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: The article summarizes weekend stories from across Asia, including ant smuggling from East Africa to China, new Hong Kong airport rules limiting passengers to two power banks, and a Tang dynasty tablet testing China-Japan cultural restitution.

stories.title: Trump: US will shut down attempt to charge Hormuz passage toll in minutes
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated the US could quickly shut down any Iranian attempt to charge toll fees for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. He suggested the US would act decisively if Iran pursued such a move.

stories.title: University professor in Odesa dismissed for teaching in Russian
stories.summary: A professor at Odesa National University of Technology was dismissed for conducting classes and preparing exam materials in Russian, violating Ukraine's language-in-education requirements.

stories.title: Trump says Iran must give up nuclear weapons
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned that Iran's leaders risk losing their country if they do not abandon nuclear weapons ambitions. Speaking aboard Air Force One, he demanded Tehran comply with US conditions, saying Iran could "have a great country again" if it agrees.

stories.title: Amnesty warns of human rights risks at 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: Amnesty International warned that millions of fans attending the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States face serious human rights risks, raising concerns about conditions for attendees.

stories.title: European nations criticise Israel’s death penalty plans
stories.summary: Several European nations criticized an Israeli legislative proposal that would impose mandatory death sentences for certain offenses. The amendment is backed by Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

stories.title: Big retailers say UK jobs at risk from guaranteed hours reforms
stories.summary: The UK's retail trade body warned that more than half of retail jobs could be affected by new guaranteed working hours reforms taking effect in April under the Employment Rights Act. The industry said the changes could make it harder to employ people in part-time roles, particularly young workers.

stories.title: EU’s flagship Africa project under fire over ties to Chinese state-owned firms
stories.summary: The EU's Lobito Corridor rail project linking the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia to Angola's Atlantic coast, a flagship of the €300 billion Global Gateway initiative, faces scrutiny over ties to Chinese state-owned firms. The project was launched to rival Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative.

stories.title: US lets Russian oil tanker approach Cuba despite blockade
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he had "no problem" with Russia or another country delivering oil to Cuba amid an acute energy crisis on the island. A Russian oil tanker was permitted to approach Cuba despite a broader blockade policy.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones kill one, damage homes, industry in southern Russia's Taganrog
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes killed one person and damaged homes and industrial sites in Taganrog, a city in Russia's Rostov region. Governor Yuri Slyusar reported fires and evacuations following the debris impact.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran 'agreeing' with US on 15-point peace plan
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed Iran is agreeing with the US on a 15-point peace plan sent to Tehran via Pakistan. When asked about Iran's response, Trump said they conceded on most points.

stories.title: Indonesian killed in Lebanon while on UN peacekeeping mission
stories.summary: An Indonesian UN peacekeeper was killed when a projectile struck a UNIFIL position near the southern Lebanese village of Adchit al-Qusayr. Another peacekeeper was critically injured, and three additional Indonesian personnel were wounded by indirect artillery fire.

stories.title: IDF pulls battalion from West Bank action after alleged assault of CNN crew
stories.summary: The Israeli military suspended the Netzach Yehuda battalion from West Bank operations following an investigation into the alleged assault of a CNN crew. The battalion will undergo training to strengthen its professional and ethical standards.

stories.title: Guerrillas burn three electronic warfare antennas near Novgorod
stories.summary: Agents of the ATESH partisan movement reported destroying three mobile communication towers equipped with electronic warfare antennas on Russian territory near Novgorod. The antennas had been disrupting Ukrainian drone operations.

stories.title: Iran’s Mojtaba Khamenei thanks Iraq in latest written message
stories.summary: Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei issued a written message thanking the Iraqi people for their stance against aggression toward Iran. The statement acknowledged Iraq's public support during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Israel says it intercepted two drones launched from Yemen
stories.summary: The Israeli military intercepted two drones launched from Yemen after sirens sounded in the Red Sea city of Eilat. Houthi forces in Yemen have increasingly targeted Israel with drones and missiles amid the widening regional conflict.

stories.title: UK's Reeves to warn G7 against trade moves during Iran war
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves is expected to urge G7 nations against disruptive trade measures during the Iran war. She will argue that cooperation is essential to maintain energy and goods flows and to reduce costs over time.

stories.title: Iranian strike damages US surveillance plane in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: An Iranian strike on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia reportedly destroyed a US Air Force E-3 Sentry early warning aircraft. CNN geolocated photos of the wreckage by comparing them with earlier satellite imagery of the base.

stories.title: Police, Catholic patriarchate reach agreement on prayer at Holy Sepulchre after cardinal blocked
stories.summary: Israeli police and the Latin Patriarchate reached an agreement on prayer access at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre after Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa was barred entry due to wartime restrictions. Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered full and immediate access for the cardinal.

stories.title: Strikes knock out power in Tehran amid US ground invasion fears
stories.summary: Iran's energy ministry reported power outages across Tehran, its surrounding region, and Alborz province following strikes on electricity infrastructure. The blackouts heightened fears of a possible US ground invasion.

stories.title: IDF Chief of Staff suspends battalion that accosted CNN news team in West Bank
stories.summary: The IDF Chief of Staff suspended a battalion after its members accosted a CNN news team operating in the West Bank. The battalion's operational deployment is halted pending a process to reinforce its professional and ethical standards.

stories.title: Tai Po blaze hearing resumes after fire alarm goes off during morning break
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating the Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court estate in Hong Kong, which killed 168 people, entered its fifth day of hearings. The company responsible for fire safety systems at the estate was set to testify, along with seven residents.

stories.title: Beijing sanctions Japanese lawmaker for ‘colluding with Taiwan independence forces’
stories.summary: China imposed sanctions on Japanese lawmaker Keiji Furuya for allegedly colluding with Taiwan independence forces through repeated visits to Taiwan. Beijing's foreign ministry said his actions seriously violated the one-China principle.

stories.title: Afghanistan accuses Pakistan of shelling outskirts of eastern city, killing and wounding civilians
stories.summary: Afghanistan accused Pakistan of shelling the outskirts of Asadabad in Kunar Province on Sunday, using mortars and heavy weaponry against rural areas and civilian homes. Afghan deputy spokesman Hamdullah Fitrat reported civilian casualties.

stories.title: Taiwan’s Kuomintang leader to visit mainland China to aid ‘peaceful’ relations: Beijing
stories.summary: KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun will lead a delegation to mainland China from April 7 to 12, visiting Jiangsu province, Shanghai, and Beijing at Beijing's invitation. Communist Party leader Xi Jinping is expected to welcome the visit aimed at promoting peaceful cross-strait relations.

stories.title: Chinese company to use AI-powered chromosome testing to boost profits and fast-track IVF
stories.summary: Hangzhou-based Diagens Biotechnology plans to use AI-powered chromosome testing to boost IVF success rates and drive profit growth following its Hong Kong listing. China's declining fertility rate is increasing demand for assisted reproduction services.

stories.title: Iran threatens US, Israel-linked universities across Middle East
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reportedly threatened that all Israeli and US-affiliated universities across the Middle East are considered legitimate targets in the ongoing war, according to Rudaw media.

stories.title: Trump says Iran agreed to 'most of' 15-point list of US demands
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said Iran agreed to most of a 15-point list of US demands aimed at ending the war. He described the ongoing negotiations as making significant progress through both direct and indirect channels via intermediaries.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelensky discusses security partnership in Jordan
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed a security partnership during a visit to Jordan. Kyiv has offered its air-defence expertise and drone technology to countries seeking to counter Iranian drone attacks in the region.

stories.title: Where can Japan store its nuclear waste? Island plan raises alarm
stories.summary: Japan is exploring the feasibility of using the remote Pacific island of Minamitorishima, about 1,900 km southeast of Tokyo, as a final disposal site for high-level radioactive waste. An official survey request was presented to the mayor of Ogasawara village, raising concerns domestically and internationally.

stories.title: UN Security Council’s inaction is tearing the world apart
stories.summary: The article criticizes the UN Security Council's inaction across multiple conflicts including Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Syria, Ukraine, Gaza, and Venezuela, arguing that permanent members' use of the veto has blurred the line between permitted and prohibited actions under international law.

stories.title: 'Replicate Gaza model': Netanyahu orders expansion of Lebanon invasion
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered Israeli troops to expand the ground offensive in southern Lebanon, including widening a security buffer zone. He said the move aimed to replicate the "Gaza model," signalling a more entrenched military presence.

stories.title: Israel adds US$10 billion to its war chest with defence budget increase
stories.summary: Israel's parliament approved the 2026 budget with a vote of 62 to 55, including a roughly $10 billion increase in military spending as the country continues fighting on multiple fronts. The vote averted an automatic government collapse and snap elections.

stories.title: Observatory cancels amber rainstorm warning at 11am after heavy rain in Hong Kong
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory issued an amber rainstorm warning at 10am on Monday after heavy rain exceeding 30mm per hour fell across the city. The warning was cancelled approximately one hour later at 11am as conditions eased.

stories.title: 'Dealing with different people': Trump says regime change achieved in Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said the US-Israeli war achieved regime change in Iran, citing the deaths of senior leaders during the conflict. He indicated the US is now negotiating with a different set of Iranian officials and suggested a deal could come soon.

stories.title: European nations criticise Israel's death penalty plans
stories.summary: France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom criticized Israel's proposed death penalty legislation ahead of its second and third readings in the Knesset. The European nations raised concerns about the bill's discriminatory nature.

stories.title: IAEA says Iran’s Khondab heavy water reactor no longer operational
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported that Iran's Khondab heavy water production plant is no longer operational. The facility had been a point of concern in international nuclear monitoring efforts.

stories.title: Israeli military finds no negligence in killing of farmer near Lebanon border
stories.summary: The Israeli military concluded an investigation into the killing of Israeli farmer Ofer Moskovitz near the Lebanese border earlier in March. The inquiry found no negligence or ethical failures by the officers involved in the incident.

stories.title: Israel to allow 'limited prayer' at Holy Sepulchre after outrage
stories.summary: Israeli police reached an agreement with Christian leaders to allow limited prayer at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem after earlier restrictions drew criticism. The arrangement followed talks between police and representatives of the Latin Patriarchate.

stories.title: Pakistan PM appreciates Saudi Arabia for showing 'remarkable restraint' during West Asia tensions
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif praised Saudi Arabia for showing 'remarkable restraint' during escalating tensions in West Asia. The comments came during a meeting with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan in Islamabad.

stories.title: ‘Lighthouses in space’: the Chinese jam-proof satellite network to fill GPS gaps
stories.summary: Chinese researchers have developed an 11-satellite optical navigation network designed to provide jam-resistant, high-accuracy positioning where GPS is unavailable or disrupted. The system is intended for applications ranging from self-driving cars and drones to deep-space missions.

stories.title: Trump: Killing Iran’s leaders is ‘regime change,’ deal to end war ‘could be soon’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump described the killing of Iranian leaders as constituting regime change and suggested a deal to end the war could come soon. He also said Iran agreed to allow 20 more vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, while a UNIFIL peacekeeper was killed in Lebanon.

stories.title: WTO talks on e-commerce duties moratorium deadlocked as reform plan nears deal
stories.summary: World Trade Organization ministerial talks on extending the e-commerce customs duties moratorium have reached a deadlock. Brazil's objection has stalled negotiations on continuing the moratorium beyond two years, even as a broader reform plan nears agreement.

stories.title: Three dead in Russian attack on Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine, police say
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk killed three people and injured 13 on Sunday. Police reported the attack was one of several strikes targeting frontline areas in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: New constitutional affairs chief Janice Tse to lead Hong Kong’s first 5-year plan
stories.summary: Retired civil servant Janice Tse Siu-wa has been appointed Hong Kong's new secretary for constitutional and mainland affairs. Chief Executive John Lee nominated the 61-year-old, citing her 38 years of government experience. Her top priority will be formulating Hong Kong's first five-year plan within the year.

stories.title: Russia sentences three captured Azov fighters to 5.5–19 years in prison
stories.summary: The Southern District Military Court in Rostov-on-Don sentenced three captured Ukrainian fighters from the Azov unit who were taken prisoner during the siege of the Azovstal plant in Mariupol. They received sentences ranging from 5.5 to 19 years in prison.

stories.title: Iranian academic describes US-Israeli attacks on Iran’s universities
stories.summary: An Iranian academic identified as Doutaghi described US-Israeli attacks on Iranian universities, saying they reflect a wider pattern. The strikes raised questions about the boundaries of what constitutes legitimate retaliation in the conflict.

stories.title: Blackouts hit parts of Tehran as Israel conducts strikes in Iran amid peace talks
stories.summary: Parts of Tehran experienced power blackouts as Israel conducted strikes on Iranian infrastructure amid ongoing peace talks. Pakistan offered to host US-Iran negotiations, though it was unclear whether either side agreed to attend.

stories.title: US allows Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba in easing of energy blockade
stories.summary: The United States authorized the passage of a Russian oil tanker loaded with crude bound for Cuba, marking the first easing of Washington's de facto energy blockade on the island imposed since early in the year, according to The New York Times.

stories.title: Amnesty warns 2026 World Cup across North America risks becoming a ‘stage for repression’
stories.summary: Amnesty International warned that the 2026 FIFA World Cup, to be hosted across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, risks becoming a "stage for repression." The organization urged FIFA and host nations to protect the human rights of players and fans.

stories.title: Drug parcels from the US intercepted in Uruguay; two convicted on trafficking charges
stories.summary: Uruguay's National Customs Directorate arrested and secured convictions of two individuals on drug trafficking charges following operations at Carrasco International Airport near Montevideo. The cases involved interception of parcels originating from the United States and passenger screening.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders deeper Israeli invasion into Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to expand its ground invasion in southern Lebanon. The directive comes amid escalating regional hostilities linked to the broader US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says he could seize Iran's Kharg Island as US ramps up troop buildup
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said in a Financial Times interview that he wants to "take the oil in Iran" and could seize the Kharg Island export hub. Approximately 2,500 US Marines have arrived in the region as the US continues its military buildup.

stories.title: Australian police killer shot dead after 7-month manhunt
stories.summary: Australian police fatally shot fugitive Desmond Freeman in Victoria state, ending a seven-month manhunt. Freeman had been wanted for killing two police officers on a rural property in the alpine region in August and had fled into dense bushland, prompting one of Australia's largest-ever manhunts involving hundreds of officers.

stories.title: China woman spends US$1,700 to enrol dog in school for personality testing, training, company
stories.summary: A Shanghai-based woman identified by the pseudonym Taotao spent 12,000 yuan (US$1,700) to enrol her six-month-old Samoyed in a dog kindergarten. The package includes personality testing, behaviour training, social activities, and a school bus service, prompted by her busy work schedule.

stories.title: Oil tops $116 a barrel as Iran accuses US of preparing invasion
stories.summary: Crude oil prices climbed above $116 per barrel as Iran accused the United States of preparing a ground invasion. The surge reflects what analysts describe as the biggest global energy crisis in decades.

stories.title: Maduro calls from prison for "reconciliation, forgiveness, and reunion" in Venezuela
stories.summary: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores issued their first public statement since being captured in Caracas on January 3 during a US military operation. They called for national reconciliation and endorsed acting President Delcy Rodríguez's leadership.

stories.title: Iranian attack damages Kuwait power and desalination plant, kills worker
stories.summary: An Iranian attack struck a power and desalination plant in Kuwait, killing an Indian worker. Kuwaiti authorities reported significant material damage to the facility.

stories.title: Trump news at a glance: Generational divide over Iran war emerges at key conservative conference
stories.summary: A generational divide over the Iran war emerged at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) in Texas. Younger conservatives expressed disappointment and feelings of "betrayal" over President Trump's strikes against Iran, while CPAC leaders urged party unity ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Knesset approves 2026 budget, Israel’s largest ever, sending billions to Haredi institutions
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset approved a record $271 billion budget for 2026 after a marathon filibuster, narrowly avoiding early elections. The wartime budget includes increased defense spending and significant funding for Haredi institutions, with voting interrupted by missile sirens.

stories.title: Russia restricts access to Western social media in occupied territories – National Resistance Center
stories.summary: According to Ukraine's National Resistance Center, Russian forces in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories are systematically restricting residents' access to Western social media platforms.

stories.title: Hong Kong on ‘yellow alert’, Kadoorie says, as Middle East war fuels energy crisis
stories.summary: CLP Group chairman Michael Kadoorie warned that the Middle East conflict has triggered a global energy crisis that poses a "yellow warning" for Hong Kong. While the city has so far avoided severe impacts, Kadoorie said rising fuel costs could affect the territory and urged forward planning.

stories.title: Sketching a recovery: China’s art market puts next-gen buyers in the frame amid slowdown
stories.summary: UBS reports tentative signs of recovery in China's art market despite broader economic pressures, citing increased participation from next-generation wealthy buyers. Amy Lo, chairman of UBS Global Wealth Management Asia, noted a rebound in auction trips and purchases in China.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders Israeli military to ‘further expand’ security zone in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to further expand the security zone in Lebanon, warning that Hezbollah still retained residual capabilities to fire rockets at Israel despite being severely degraded by Israeli operations.

stories.title: Germany, France, Italy, UK express 'deep concern' over Israeli death penalty bill
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Germany, France, Italy, and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement expressing deep concern over an Israeli bill that would introduce the death penalty. The bill could be voted into law as early as next week.

stories.title: Chief rabbi calls for protection of mosques, churches and synagogues after attacks
stories.summary: A chief rabbi called for the protection of mosques, churches, and synagogues following recent attacks on houses of worship. Rabbi Bar stated that religious violence against any faith must be rejected.

stories.title: Israeli national soccer team draws at Georgia in friendly
stories.summary: Israel's national soccer team played Georgia to a 2-2 draw in a friendly match held at Mikheil Meskhi Stadium in Tbilisi. The match took place ahead of Nations League fixtures scheduled for the fall.

stories.title: US sees first combat loss of valuable E-3 jet after Iran targets Saudi base
stories.summary: The United States lost an E-3 Sentry surveillance aircraft, valued at approximately $300 million, after Iran targeted Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. The incident marks the first combat loss of the valuable early-warning jet.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says wants to take Iran’s oil; Kuwait power site hit
stories.summary: Kuwait reported that an Indian worker was killed in an Iranian raid that struck infrastructure in the country. Attacks across Gulf states continued as part of the widening regional conflict.

stories.title: Why revived China-Philippine talks won’t lead to energy cooperation in the South China Sea
stories.summary: Senior diplomats from China and the Philippines met in Quanzhou for two rounds of revived consultations covering oil and gas cooperation in the South China Sea, renewable energy, and coastguard communication. Chinese observers said maritime tensions are likely to persist despite Manila's calls for energy cooperation.

stories.title: War on Iran is about to make clothes more expensive. Here’s why
stories.summary: Clothing manufacturers and analysts are warning consumers to expect price increases of 10 to 15 percent as the war on Iran disrupts South Asia's US$50 billion garment export industry.
