Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has choked natural gas supplies, driving up production costs across the supply chain.

stories.title: China’s ‘teapot’ oil refineries keep economy brewing – but surging crude prices leave them strained
stories.summary: China's small independent "teapot" oil refineries, which buy cheap crude and convert it into fuel, are struggling as surging global oil prices erode their thin profit margins. These refineries are a key part of China's energy security infrastructure.

stories.title: Founder of Free Syrian Army promoted in new military
stories.summary: Riad al-Asaad, a former colonel in the Syrian Air Force who defected to found the rebel Free Syrian Army at the start of the Syrian conflict, has been promoted within Syria's new military structure.

stories.title: Two more apartment buildings restored in Borodianka
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development completed the restoration of two apartment buildings in Borodianka, a town heavily damaged during the war, as part of a broader reconstruction program.

stories.title: Jewish National Fund-USA brotherhood mission shows solidarity with Israel during wartime - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Jewish National Fund-USA organized a volunteer brotherhood mission to Israel during wartime. American participants remained in the country to support communities, soldiers, and recovery efforts as a show of solidarity.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: A United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) peacekeeper was killed when a projectile struck a UN position near Adchit Al Qusayr in southern Lebanon on Sunday night. Another peacekeeper was critically injured in the same incident.

stories.title: In letter to PSL CEO, police detail alleged security protocol breach by Lahore Qalandar’s Shaheen Afridi, Sikandar Raza
stories.summary: Lahore's Deputy Inspector-General of Police reported an alleged breach of security protocols by Lahore Qalandars players Shaheen Shah Afridi and Sikandar Raza during the PSL's 11th edition. The DIG wrote to the PSL CEO urging action to prevent future violations.

stories.title: Iran 30 days into internet blackout, isolating millions amid war
stories.summary: Iran has been under an internet blackout for 30 days, cutting off millions from the global web amid the ongoing war. Domestic intranet services, including local messaging apps and banking platforms, remain operational.

stories.title: Oil prices surge above $100 again
stories.summary: Oil prices surged above $100 per barrel at the start of Asian trading on Monday amid the ongoing Israeli-US war on Iran. West Texas Intermediate rose 3.5 percent to $103.13, while Brent crude climbed nearly 3 percent to $115.93.

stories.title: US to allow Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba in lifeline for Caribbean island
stories.summary: President Donald Trump signalled he would allow a sanctioned Russian oil tanker to deliver crude to Cuba, saying he had "no problem" with countries sending oil to the island. The vessel, part of Russia's "shadow fleet," was expected to reach a Cuban port on Monday, offering a lifeline to the struggling economy.

stories.title: Six-year-old girl wounded in Sumy attack remains in critical condition, authorities say
stories.summary: A six-year-old girl injured during Russia's March 28 shelling of the Znob-Novhorodske community in Ukraine's Sumy region remains in extremely critical condition in hospital.

stories.title: Pakistan will be honoured to facilitate talks between U.S. and Iran: Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said Pakistan would be honored to host talks between the United States and Iran. Dar indicated he briefed visiting foreign dignitaries on the prospects of potential U.S.-Iran dialogue taking place in Islamabad.

stories.title: One month of Israel-U.S. war on Iran: A timeline
stories.summary: A timeline of the first month of conflict between Israel, the United States, and Iran details developments since joint Israeli-U.S. strikes began on February 28. The war has spread across West Asia and significantly affected the global economy.

stories.title: Iran 30 days into internet blackout, isolating millions amid war
stories.summary: Iran has been under an internet blackout for 30 days, severely restricting access to the global internet for millions of citizens amid the ongoing war. The country's domestic intranet remains operational.

stories.title: After Trump said MBS was ‘kissing his ass’, Gulf leaders told to send children to fight Iran
stories.summary: Trump ally Steve Bannon called on Gulf royals' children to lead an assault on Iran, following reports that President Trump made disparaging remarks about Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman during the Future Investment Initiative Summit in Miami Beach.

stories.title: Ukraine’s last friend in the Trump regime just walked away
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, previously seen as a supporter of Ukraine within the Trump administration, has shifted his position on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The development raises concerns about diminishing American diplomatic support for Ukraine and Europe.

stories.title: First PIA direct flight to London in 6 years lands at Heathrow Airport
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines operated its first direct flight from Islamabad to London's Heathrow Airport in six years on Sunday. The airline plans to run four weekly flights on the route, using Heathrow's Terminal 4.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz commends Kingdom’s ‘remarkable restraint’ in meeting with Saudi FM, assures him of Pakistan’s ‘full support’
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised Saudi Arabia's restraint during the Middle East crisis in a meeting with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud in Islamabad. Sharif assured full Pakistani solidarity and support following a quadrilateral ministerial meeting with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey.

stories.title: Li Ka-shing’s CK Life unit eyes China fast track for cancer vaccine pipeline
stories.summary: CK Life Sciences, backed by Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing, plans to fast-track its cancer vaccine candidates into mainland China through investigator-initiated trials. The company has established Sequencio Therapeutics in Hong Kong to support the effort.

stories.title: Why is NASA spending $129 billion to return to the Moon? Depends on who you ask
stories.summary: NASA's $129 billion program to return astronauts to the Moon has drawn questions about its justification. One prominent rationale cited is the desire to stay ahead of China in the space race.

stories.title: 123 clashes on frontline as Ukrainian forces neutralize over 180 Russian troops in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces recorded 123 combat engagements with Russian troops as of the evening of March 29. The heaviest Russian activity occurred in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors, where Ukrainian forces neutralized over 180 Russian soldiers.

stories.title: Fugitive Dezi Freeman shot dead by Australian police after months on the run, reports say
stories.summary: Fugitive Dezi Freeman was shot dead by Australian police after months on the run. Freeman had been wanted since the fatal shooting of two police officers in Porepunkah, Victoria, in August.

stories.title: Tony Blair rejects Gaza genocide charge, says Western leaders are failing to stop antisemitism
stories.summary: Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair rejected claims that Israel's war in Gaza constitutes genocide. He warned that Western leaders are failing to confront the political climate fueling rising antisemitism.

stories.title: Pope Leo says God rejects prayers of leaders who wage wars
stories.summary: Pope Leo stated that God rejects the prayers of leaders who wage wars. The remarks were made in the context of ongoing global conflicts.

stories.title: How will the Houthis’ involvement shape the war?
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi group launched missiles toward Israel in support of Iran, raising questions about how their involvement may shape the broader regional war.

stories.title: Russian tanker nears blockaded Cuba, Trump shrugs off ‘a boat of oil’
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker entered Cuban waters on Monday despite a de facto US fuel blockade on the island. President Trump downplayed the delivery, calling it "a boat of oil" and saying its cargo of 730,000 barrels of crude was "not going to matter."

stories.title: European nations criticise Israel’s death penalty plans
stories.summary: France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom criticized Israel's proposed death penalty legislation, raising concerns about its "de facto discriminatory character." The bill is set for further readings in the Knesset.

stories.title: Iran, US have expressed confidence in Pakistan to facilitate talks; will be honoured to host dialogue ‘in coming days’: FM Dar
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced that both the United States and Iran have expressed confidence in Pakistan to facilitate talks between them. The remarks followed a quadrilateral meeting in Islamabad attended by the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt.

stories.title: US will reportedly allow Russian oil tanker to reach Cuba amid blockade
stories.summary: The Russia-flagged tanker Anatoly Kolodkin, carrying roughly 650,000 barrels of Urals crude from Primorsk, entered Cuba's exclusive economic zone on Sunday. If it discharges at Matanzas port, it would be Cuba's first oil import in over two months.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of plotting ground attack, as Israel steps up bombardment
stories.summary: Iran accused the US of plotting a ground attack as Israel intensified bombardment of Iranian targets. Power was being restored in Tehran after the Iranian Ministry of Energy reported outages following strikes on the capital.

stories.title: Ukraine's president, King of Jordan discuss prospects for security partnership
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Jordan's King Abdullah II held talks on potential cooperation in the security sector. The meeting was part of Zelenskyy's broader regional diplomatic campaign.

stories.title: Israeli PM says ordered military to ‘further expand’ security zone in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, during a visit to northern command, ordered the military to further expand Israel's security zone in Lebanon. He stated that Hezbollah had been severely weakened but still retained residual capabilities to launch rockets at Israel.

stories.title: European countries appeal to Israel to abandon plans to revive death penalty
stories.summary: France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom jointly called on Israel to abandon a bill seeking to revive the death penalty for terrorism convictions. Opponents say the measure would disproportionately target Palestinians. A final Knesset vote is anticipated on Monday.

stories.title: Israeli police block Catholic cardinal from Jerusalem's Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli police blocked Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa and Friar Francesco Ielpo from reaching the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem on Palm Sunday. The Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem confirmed the incident at the site revered as the location of Jesus's crucifixion and resurrection.

stories.title: Gaza receiving over 70,000 cubic meters of water per day, COGAT claims
stories.summary: Israel's Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) claimed that Gaza is receiving over 70,000 cubic meters of water daily, responding to a UNRWA post stating that freshwater supplies in Gaza were severely limited and polluted.

stories.title: American University of Beirut moves online after Iran warns of retaliation over strikes on its universities
stories.summary: The American University of Beirut shifted to remote operations for two days after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened American universities across the region. University President Fadlo Khuri said there was no evidence of a direct threat against the institution.

stories.title: Stubb says no military threat to Finland after drone incident
stories.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb stated there is no military threat to Finland following the detection of several drones over the country on Sunday, March 29.

stories.title: Latest message purportedly from Iran’s new supreme leader thanks Iraq for war support
stories.summary: A third written statement attributed to Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei thanked Iraq for its support in the war. Khamenei has remained out of public view since his appointment, fueling speculation about his health and whereabouts.

stories.title: China protests U.S. alert over security rules change in Hong Kong
stories.summary: China protested a U.S. advisory issued in response to Hong Kong's amended national security enforcement rules. The changes make it an offense in national security cases to refuse to provide passwords or decryption assistance for accessing electronic devices.

stories.title: Why Kenneth Rogoff thinks China’s yuan will be a reserve currency ‘in the next 5 years’
stories.summary: Harvard economist Kenneth Rogoff predicts China's yuan will become a reserve currency within five years. The former IMF chief economist has warned that the US dollar faces a growing crisis of legitimacy in the global financial system.

stories.title: Ways for ‘early and permanent end’ to Middle East war discussed at quadrilateral moot, says Dar
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced that a quadrilateral meeting in Islamabad with counterparts from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt focused on finding an early and permanent end to the Middle East conflict. Dar also held bilateral talks with each foreign minister, who separately met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

stories.title: Life under fire, shifting battle lines, and history’s role in Israel’s present conflicts
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Dispatch podcast discussed daily life in Israel amid ongoing regional conflict, examining shifting battle lines and the strategic implications of the country's present security situation.

stories.title: UK’s PM Starmer to host industry leaders for Middle East war talks on Monday
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer will host senior officials and leaders from the energy, shipping, finance, and insurance sectors at Downing Street on Monday. The roundtable will address the impact of Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz on oil prices and global supply chains.

stories.title: European nations warn over Israel’s planned expansion of death penalty
stories.summary: Britain, France, Germany, and Italy expressed deep concern over Israeli plans to expand the use of the death penalty in a bill expected to be voted on next week. The Council of Europe's rights body also opposed the draft law, warning it would significantly broaden capital punishment.

stories.title: Russia reports fire in new Ukrainian strike on major Baltic port
stories.summary: Ukraine struck a major Russian Baltic port, causing a fire, as part of an intensified campaign targeting Russian infrastructure including refineries, oil depots, and ports. Ukraine has said the strikes aim to reduce revenues funding Russia's military offensive.

stories.title: Israeli police block Catholic cardinal from Jerusalem's Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa from celebrating Palm Sunday at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, citing security concerns related to the Iran war. The Patriarchate said it was the first such restriction in centuries.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces destroy Russian infantry groups near Fedorivka Druha in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces destroyed Russian infantry groups near the village of Fedorivka Druha in the Donetsk region, releasing footage demonstrating their operations against small enemy units.

stories.title: Iran’s supreme leader thanks Iraq for support in war
stories.summary: Iran's newly elected Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei sent a message thanking Iraq's top Shia religious authority Ali al-Sistani and the Iraqi people for supporting Tehran in the war against the United States and Israel. Earlier this month, Sistani had called on all Muslims to denounce what he termed an unjust war against Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts regional powers for Iran talks, with focus on Hormuz proposals
stories.summary: Pakistan hosted a meeting of regional powers focused on the Iran conflict, with discussions centered on proposals related to maritime traffic and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The proposals are intended for presentation to Washington.

stories.title: In Pictures | 'No Kings' protests erupt across the U.S.
stories.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered across U.S. cities in "No Kings" protests opposing the Trump administration's involvement in the Middle East conflict and its domestic policies.

stories.title: Can Hong Kong hitch a ride on China’s commercial aerospace wave?
stories.summary: An analysis examines whether Hong Kong can capitalize on China's 15th five-year plan, which elevates commercial aerospace to a mainstream pillar of national development, integrating satellites and related strategic industries.

stories.title: Keir Starmer to launch local elections campaign with focus on cost of living
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer will launch Labour's local elections campaign with a focus on cost-of-living issues, citing the Iran war as a reason for voters to stay with Labour. The party has adopted the slogan "Pride in Britain" ahead of expected losses in Wales, Scotland, and English councils.

stories.title: Educated and employed but still struggling: India's middle class under strain
stories.summary: India's middle class, despite being educated and employed, is experiencing growing economic strain as opportunities for upward mobility diminish.

stories.title: Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei thanks Iraq in latest written message
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei sent a written message thanking Iraq for its support, delivered after a meeting between the Islamic Supreme Council of Iraq, a Shia political party, and Iran's ambassador in Baghdad.

stories.title: America is not winning Iran war; a ground attack would be complete insanity: Trita Parsi
stories.summary: Analyst Trita Parsi argued that the United States is not winning the war against Iran and called a potential ground attack "complete insanity." He suggested Iran could withstand the conflict for six months to a year, though prolonged war would not serve Tehran's interests.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy arrives in Jordan for next leg of Gulf tour
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy arrived in Jordan as part of a Gulf tour aimed at strengthening defence ties with regional countries amid tensions related to the Iran war.

stories.title: Ukraine's junior team wins 11 medals at Poznan Junior European Cup 2026
stories.summary: Ukraine's junior judo team won 11 medals at the Poznan Junior European Cup 2026, an international tournament held in Poznan, Poland.

stories.title: France detains two more suspects over foiled Paris Bank of America attack
stories.summary: French authorities detained two additional suspects in connection with a foiled attack plot targeting a Bank of America location in Paris, the prosecutor's office confirmed.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1495: Ukraine absorbed 3,000 drone strikes in a week — and spent the weekend setting Baltic ports on fire
stories.summary: Ukraine absorbed more than 3,000 Russian drone strikes in one week and struck the Baltic port of Ust-Luga again. President Zelenskyy traveled to Amman, Jordan, to sign a new defense partnership, while Atesh partisans destroyed Russian electronic warfare towers inside Russian territory.

stories.title: PTI concerned over reports about Bushra Bibi’s health, demands she be taken to hospital for diagnosis, treatment
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf expressed concern over the health of Bushra Bibi, the imprisoned spouse of party founder Imran Khan, and demanded she be transferred to a hospital for proper diagnosis and treatment. The party cited a circulating document indicating she had been examined by a doctor at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences.

stories.title: Knesset approves 2026 state budget in final votes, avoids early elections
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset approved the 2026 state budget in final votes, averting the possibility of early elections. Coalition partners supported the plan despite earlier threats to withhold backing and criticism over spending priorities.

stories.title: Israeli police bar priest from Jerusalem’s Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented the Latin Patriarch from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, as Christians marked Holy Week under wartime restrictions.

stories.title: UAE intercepts 58 missiles and drones launched from Iran
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates' air defense systems intercepted 58 missiles and drones launched from Iran on Sunday, marking a significant aerial engagement between the two countries.

stories.title: Zelenskyy meets Jordan’s king to discuss security partnership – the same Shaheds that hit Kyiv are now hitting Amman’s neighbors
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with Jordan's King Abdullah II to discuss a security partnership. Ukraine already has over 200 specialists deployed across the Gulf region, and Zelenskyy noted that the same Iranian-made Shahed drones striking Kyiv are also threatening Jordan's neighbors.

stories.title: A premature ceasefire risks ‘another round of conflict’ in future
stories.summary: Analysts warn that a premature ceasefire could lead to a renewed round of conflict, arguing that a flawed conclusion to the fighting may carry consequences as severe as continuing the war.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll tops 1,200 as Israel vows to ‘change’ north
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that more than 1,200 people, including 124 children, have been killed over the past four weeks as Israeli strikes intensify across the country. Over 3,500 others have been wounded. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to fundamentally change the situation in northern Israel.

stories.title: Iranian ambassador refuses to leave Lebanon after being declared persona non grata - report
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Lebanon reportedly refused to leave the country after being declared persona non grata, citing the wishes of Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri and Hezbollah, according to AFP.

stories.title: Israel preventing mass by Jerusalem’s Latin Patriarch an ‘offence to the faithful’: Italy
stories.summary: Italy condemned Israeli police actions that prevented Jerusalem's Latin Patriarch from celebrating Palm Sunday mass, calling it an offence to the faithful.

stories.title: Israeli-US war batters UAE economy, wiping $120bn from Abu Dhabi, Dubai markets
stories.summary: The ongoing Israeli-U.S. war on Iran has wiped approximately $120 billion from Abu Dhabi and Dubai stock markets. The conflict has disrupted UAE aviation and property sectors, exposing structural vulnerabilities in the Gulf state's economy.

stories.title: Australia politics live: Jim Chalmers says working from home ‘makes a lot of sense’ during fuel crisis but government will avoid Covid-style measures
stories.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers suggested working from home during a fuel crisis linked to the Middle East war but said the government would avoid Covid-style restrictions. He said the economy is expected to continue growing despite a significant hit from the conflict.

stories.title: A fractured opposition hands Netanyahu a full term - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's government is set to complete its full term as the budget is expected to pass, while opposition infighting continues to undermine efforts to unseat him.

stories.title: Strike on Kramatorsk: Three dead, injury toll climbs to 13
stories.summary: A Russian airstrike on Kramatorsk on March 29 killed three people and injured 13, damaging houses, administrative buildings, and vehicles in the Donetsk region city.

stories.title: IRGC spokesperson says Trump ‘only understands the language of force’
stories.summary: IRGC spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari dismissed threats of U.S. ground operations against Iran, stating that President Trump 'only understands the language of force.'

stories.title: Eisenkot rejects Bennett’s offer to unite parties, says he won’t serve as ‘number two’
stories.summary: Former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar! Party, rejected an offer from Naftali Bennett to merge their parties, stating he would not serve as second-in-command and sees himself as a strong candidate for leadership.

stories.title: Iran’s envoy to remain in Lebanon in defiance of expulsion by Beirut — diplomatic source
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Lebanon is refusing to leave the country despite being declared persona non grata by the Beirut government last week. The expulsion was part of Lebanon's broader moves against Iran and Hezbollah following the group's decision to reignite hostilities with Israel.

stories.title: Israel's Netanyahu orders expansion of south Lebanon invasion
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered an expansion of military operations in southern Lebanon. Defence Minister Israel Katz previously stated that Israeli forces would control remaining bridges and the security zone up to the Litani River.

stories.title: Pakistan offers to host US-Iran talks as Tehran warns ground troops would be 'set on fire'
stories.summary: Pakistan offered to host negotiations between the United States and Iran as fighting in their monthlong war intensifies. Tehran warned that any U.S. ground troops would be 'set on fire,' while fears grow of a broader regional conflict involving Israel, Lebanon, and key maritime chokepoints.

stories.title: Tanker carrying Saudi oil passes through Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reports
stories.summary: The oil tanker P. Aliki, carrying approximately 650,000 barrels of Saudi crude oil destined for Pakistan, passed through the Strait of Hormuz along the Iranian coast, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: US considers Iran operation as Pakistan hosts regional peace talks focused on Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States is considering a potential ground operation against Iran if Tehran does not pursue diplomacy, according to closed-door discussions among U.S. officials. Meanwhile, Pakistan hosted regional peace talks focused on the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Man charged in Germany after fatal stabbing of his 13-year-old son
stories.summary: A 40-year-old German man has been charged with murder after fatally stabbing his 13-year-old son in Witten, western Germany. His wife and daughter were also stabbed in the attack. A judge in Bochum issued an arrest warrant and the suspect has been remanded in custody.

stories.title: Qatari TV station hit in Iran
stories.summary: Qatar's Al Araby television network condemned an attack on its office in Tehran that injured at least 10 people. The network did not identify those responsible for the strike.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz appreciates Kingdom’s ‘remarkable restraint’ in meeting with Saudi FM
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud in Islamabad following a quadrilateral ministerial meeting attended by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey. Sharif praised Saudi Arabia's restraint during the Middle East crisis and outlined Pakistan's diplomatic mediation efforts.

stories.title: Ukraine absorbed 3,000 drone strikes in seven days. Zelenskyy is asking the world to notice.
stories.summary: Ukraine absorbed more than 3,000 drone strikes over seven days. President Zelenskyy called for joint weapons production and shared defense systems, arguing the arsenal targeting Kyiv is the same one being used against Gulf states.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders expansion of “security zone” in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military on March 29 to expand the security zone in southern Lebanon, continuing the deepening Israeli military operation in the area.

stories.title: IDF probe finds ‘no negligence’ by troops in accidental killing of farmer in north
stories.summary: An IDF investigation into the accidental killing of farmer Ofer Moskovitz in a mistaken shelling of Kibbutz Misgav Am in northern Israel found no negligence by troops. The probe attributed the incident to several operational variables and non-optimal firing conditions.

stories.title: Russia’s enormous “giga turtle” tank covered in chains, spines, and mine rollers just attacked Kostiantynivka at 10 km/hr
stories.summary: Russian forces deployed a heavily armored 'giga turtle' tank covered in chains, spines, and mine rollers in an assault on Kostiantynivka in eastern Ukraine. The vehicle advanced at roughly 10 km/h as part of ongoing Russian efforts to capture the city.

stories.title: Iran warns US over ground attack as regional powers meet in Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran warned the United States against launching a ground attack as thousands of US Marines were dispatched to the Middle East. Regional powers convened in Pakistan for mediation talks on ending the conflict.

stories.title: PM says Israel to expand south Lebanon buffer zone as IDF pushes deeper into territory
stories.summary: During a visit to Israel's Northern Command, Prime Minister Netanyahu pledged to expand the security buffer zone in southern Lebanon and to decisively counter the Hezbollah threat. Hezbollah continued launching rockets as the IDF carried out strikes.

stories.title: Iranian missile attack sparks blaze in chemical plant, fears of hazardous leak
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck the Neot Hovav industrial zone in southern Israel, igniting a fire at a chemical plant and raising fears of a hazardous leak. No injuries were reported there, but another missile hit Beersheba, lightly injuring 11 people.

stories.title: High Court orders freeze to proactive monitoring by Ben Gvir’s new ‘anti-incitement’ body
stories.summary: Israel's High Court ordered a freeze on proactive social media monitoring by a new anti-incitement body established under National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, following reports it was tracking citizens' online activity without concrete suspicions.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 30 times; four people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 30 times on March 29, injuring four people and damaging residential buildings across the area.

stories.title: Lebanon’s Catholics observe Palm Sunday under looming threat of war
stories.summary: Lebanese Catholics observed Palm Sunday with prayers amid growing fears of wider war. Worshippers emphasized that hardships are shared across all of Lebanon's communities as Israel's military campaign continues.

stories.title: Cory Booker says Democrats have ‘failed this moment’ and calls for new leaders
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey criticized the Democratic Party, saying it has "failed this moment" and called for generational renewal in party leadership. Booker warned that internal divisions and purity tests are harming the country and benefiting adversaries.

stories.title: Zelensky visits Jordan on Middle East tour to bolster security ties
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Jordan as part of a Middle East tour focused on security cooperation. Kyiv has recently deployed anti-drone experts and signed defense agreements with several Gulf states amid regional tensions related to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: RSF attack on Sudan’s South Kordofan kills at least 14, including children
stories.summary: The Rapid Support Forces and allied militias shelled residential areas in Dilling, South Kordofan, Sudan, for several hours, killing at least 14 people, including children, according to the Sudan Doctors Network.

stories.title: Russian shelling damages monastery of Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate) in Kherson region
stories.summary: Russian shelling on March 29 damaged buildings of the Annunciation Convent in the village of Pryozerne in Ukraine's Kherson region, a monastery affiliated with the Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate).

stories.title: Pro-Ukrainian partisans open drone corridors through Russia by burning the towers that block them, Atesh claims
stories.summary: Pro-Ukrainian partisan group Atesh claimed responsibility for sabotaging electronic warfare towers in Russia's Novgorod region on March 17, creating corridors for Ukrainian drone strikes by neutralizing Russian electronic warfare coverage.

stories.title: France detains two more suspects over foiled Paris Bank of America attack
stories.summary: French authorities detained two more suspects in the foiled attack on Bank of America's Paris offices. The first suspect arrested, a minor, had their custody extended beyond the initial detention on March 28.

stories.title: Finland reports suspected territorial violation by drones
stories.summary: Finland's defence ministry reported a suspected territorial violation after two unidentified drones crashed in the southeastern part of the country on Sunday. Estonia, Lithuania, and Latvia experienced similar drone incidents earlier in the week.

stories.title: Cuba is not alone, deputy FM says as US threats grow
stories.summary: Cuba's deputy foreign minister stated that the island would resist growing United States pressure as sanctions intensify, contributing to worsening blackouts and rising tensions between Havana and Washington.

stories.title: Quadrilateral talks on ME conflict reviews ‘evolving regional situation’
stories.summary: Foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt convened a quadrilateral meeting in Islamabad to review the evolving Middle East situation. The meeting, hosted by Pakistani Deputy PM Ishaq Dar, focused on de-escalation and regional coordination regarding the conflict.

stories.title: HRCP, civil society organisations demand immediate halt to eviction operations in Islamabad’s katchi abadis
stories.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan and several civil society organizations demanded an immediate halt to eviction operations targeting informal settlements and low-income areas in Islamabad. The call was made at a press conference at the National Press Club.

stories.title: Republican Mace says Congress must approve any US troop deployment to Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Representative Nancy Mace and several other Republicans have insisted that any deployment of American ground troops to Iran must receive congressional approval, describing such a move as a significant political threshold for President Trump.

stories.title: Netanyahu announces expansion to Lebanon buffer zone, in bid to safeguard against invasion
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced an expansion of the buffer zone in southern Lebanon, stating that Israel had undergone a paradigm shift in its approach to wars against neighboring countries.

stories.title: Man arrested for attempted murder after car hits pedestrians in Britain
stories.summary: A man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a car struck pedestrians in Britain. Police said the suspect was originally from India. No further details about the location or number of victims were provided in the initial statement.

stories.title: Israel police prevent Jerusalem’s Latin Patriarch from entering Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa and the Custos of the Holy Land from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to celebrate Palm Sunday mass in Jerusalem.

stories.title: War update: Enemy launches 66 attacks, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors see fiercest battles
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 66 attacks against Ukrainian defense positions since the start of the day, with the most intense fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors of the front line.

stories.title: Spain’s PM condemns Israel blocking Latin Patriarch at holy site
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez condemned Israel after authorities blocked the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem from leading Palm Sunday Mass at one of Christianity's holiest sites, calling it a violation of religious freedom.

stories.title: Finland confirms Ukrainian drone in its airspace as Kyiv’s Baltic strike campaign pushes deeper north – Helsinki on alert
stories.summary: Finland confirmed that a Ukrainian drone entered its airspace, with fighter jets tracking the device but standing down over collateral-damage concerns. At least one additional drone is believed to have crashed on Finnish territory.

stories.title: Zelenskyy arrives in Jordan to bolster security ties
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Jordan to strengthen security ties. The visit follows Kyiv's recent defense cooperation agreements with Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Huckabee calls Pizzaballa's blockage from Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday 'unfortunate overreach'
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee criticized Israeli police for blocking Latin Patriarch Pierbattista Pizzaballa from the Church of the Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday, calling the action an "unfortunate overreach" with major global repercussions.

stories.title: In US Supreme Court fight over birthright citizenship, 1898 anti-immigrant sentiment echoes
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court is hearing a challenge by President Donald Trump to birthright citizenship, echoing an 1898 case involving Wong Kim Ark, a US-born man of Chinese descent who was denied re-entry to the country amid anti-Chinese sentiment.

stories.title: What the Houthis’ entry into the Iran war means for the conflict and the wider region
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement has entered the Iran war, raising concerns about potential attacks on Red Sea shipping near the Bab al-Mandab strait. Combined with Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi actions could severely disrupt global commercial shipping routes.

stories.title: Herzog’s office requests additional materials from Justice Ministry on PM’s pardon request
stories.summary: The office of Israeli President Isaac Herzog requested additional materials from the Justice Ministry regarding Prime Minister Netanyahu's pardon request, seeking precedents for pardons granted before conviction as allies of Trump and Netanyahu push to end his criminal trial.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian attack on Kramatorsk climbs to 12
stories.summary: The number of people injured in the Russian attack on Kramatorsk on March 29 rose to 12, as rescue and medical teams continued to respond to the strike on the Donetsk region city.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV rejects claims that God justifies war in Palm Sunday Mass message
stories.summary: During his Palm Sunday message, Pope Leo XIV urged that Christians not forget those suffering around the world during Holy Week, rejecting claims that God justifies war.

stories.title: War Diary Day 30: Multifront attrition deepens, strategic picture getting complicated for US and Israel
stories.summary: By day 30 of the US-Israel war on Iran, the conflict has expanded beyond Iranian territory, with Iran's regional proxies launching coordinated actions and domestic unrest growing in Bahrain. US and Israeli forces continued striking military, industrial, and civilian infrastructure inside Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts talks with Saudi, Turkey, Egypt to push Iran war de-escalation
stories.summary: Pakistan hosted talks in Islamabad with Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt aimed at de-escalating the Israeli-U.S. war on Iran. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said the four nations explored ways to bring a permanent end to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: ‘J.D. or Marco?’: Iran war raises 2028 stakes as Trump weighs Vance v Rubio
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is intensifying speculation about the 2028 U.S. presidential race, with Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio emerging as leading potential successors to President Trump. The conflict is seen as a defining issue that could shape their respective political prospects.

stories.title: Dozens of No Kings protesters arrested in Los Angeles after clash with police
stories.summary: Police in Los Angeles arrested dozens of No Kings protesters and deployed teargas and pepper balls on Saturday night near the Metropolitan detention center. Approximately 150 demonstrators had gathered as part of a broader protest movement against the Trump administration.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel will widen its invasion of southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to widen Israel's military invasion of southern Lebanon. He said Israel would expand its security zone as forces continue operations against Hezbollah, stating the group retains residual rocket-firing capability.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine ready for peace talks anywhere except Russia and Belarus
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is prepared to engage in peace negotiations at any location except Russia and Belarus, affirming that Kyiv would not obstruct the diplomatic process.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders military to expand invasion of southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to expand its invasion into southern Lebanon, with troops advancing toward the Litani River. Meanwhile, mourners attended funerals for three journalists killed during the operation.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei thanks Iraq for support during war in rare message since becoming Supreme Leader
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a rare message thanking Iraq for its support during the war. The message provided no evidence that Khamenei, who has not been publicly seen since the conflict began, is alive.

stories.title: What do we owe the stranger- with Seyla Benhabib - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Political theorist Seyla Benhabib discusses the implications when liberal democracies stop treating human dignity as a universal right and instead reserve it for insiders. This is sponsored content from The Times of Israel.

stories.title: Attacks on Syria’s Christian community fuel distrust of Sharaa regime
stories.summary: Residents of a Christian town in Syria protested after homes and shops were burned in sectarian violence, calling for investigations and stronger state control. The incidents have fueled distrust of the government led by Ahmad al-Sharaa.

stories.title: Bodies found in mass grave near prison in northeast Syria
stories.summary: The bodies of nine people were discovered in a mass grave near a prison in northeast Syria formerly controlled by the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces. The discovery has fueled anger and tribal tensions in the area.

stories.title: The Iran War: the end? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: This sponsored content from The Times of Israel examines whether Israel's closest ally, the United States, will again halt Israeli military operations before they reach their stated objectives in the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: The WHY of this year’s Passover – with Rachel Goldberg-Polin - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: In sponsored content from The Times of Israel, Dan Senor speaks with Rachel Goldberg-Polin ahead of Passover about how the holiday's rituals hold both joy and sorrow and why that duality remains central to the observance.

stories.title: Paramilitary attack kills at least 14 in central Sudan
stories.summary: A paramilitary attack in central Sudan killed at least 14 people. The violence followed an offensive launched by the Rapid Support Forces and allied groups on the capital of South Kordofan state on Saturday.

stories.title: Endless War. Kharg Island. Hormuz. Hezbollah. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: In sponsored content from The Times of Israel, Ya'akov Katz discusses the ongoing war, including unclear military goals, disputed operational data, and questions about whether Israel has meaningfully diminished threats or merely delayed future confrontations.

stories.title: New PIA owners rattled by rising jet fuel costs, worry about sustainability
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines consortium chairman Arif Habib warned that PIA could be forced to shut down due to a 150 percent hike in jet fuel prices. The increase is linked to global supply chain disruptions caused by the US-Iran war.

stories.title: AFU show how they repelled Russian mechanized assault near Mala Tokmachka
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 118th Separate Mechanized Brigade and supporting units repelled a Russian mechanized assault near Mala Tokmachka in Zaporizhzhia region, destroying enemy equipment and killing 20 Russian troops.

stories.title: In Arad, missile blast adds fuel to feud over shelters being used as synagogues
stories.summary: In the southern Israeli city of Arad, a recent missile blast has intensified a dispute over public bomb shelters being converted into synagogues, with residents saying many safe spaces are either decrepit or unusable due to dual-use renovations.

stories.title: PM’s office said to backtrack after tapping controversial Likud activist for key role
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's office reportedly reversed a decision to appoint Likud activist Tal Gilboa as his spokesperson after past anti-Russian and LGBTQ remarks resurfaced publicly.

stories.title: “Nothing has been redirected”: Ukraine’s top diplomat pushes back on fears that Middle East war is eating its weapons
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha pushed back on concerns that the Middle East conflict is diverting weapons from Ukraine, raising the issue with G7 partners in France and reporting the response was unequivocal that nothing had been redirected.

stories.title: US potential ground invasion, Pope Leo speaks out
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post news roundup covered developments including a potential US ground invasion related to the Iran conflict and public statements by Pope Leo on the war.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine French politician banned from Canada, blames 'Israel lobby'
stories.summary: French MEP Rima Hassan, a pro-Palestine politician, said Canada revoked her travel approval ahead of planned events in Montreal. Hassan blamed the "Israel lobby," while Canadian authorities cited undisclosed entry issues and a prior offense.

stories.title: Israeli police block Catholic leaders from Palm Sunday Mass in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Catholic leaders from holding Palm Sunday Mass in Jerusalem, citing safety concerns. Authorities said they had informed the church in advance and noted that large gatherings have been banned since the outbreak of the Iran war.

stories.title: Extreme weather in Afghanistan leaves 17 people dead, authorities say
stories.summary: Extreme weather in Afghanistan killed 17 people, destroyed or damaged 147 homes, wiped out 80 kilometres of roads, and damaged agricultural land and irrigation canals.

stories.title: From the Iran war to the US petrol pumps
stories.summary: Thirty days into the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz remains partially closed, driving up global oil prices. The disruption is significantly affecting businesses and consumers worldwide, with analysts tracking the economic ripple effects.

stories.title: Pope Leo says God rejects prayers of leaders who wage wars
stories.summary: Pope Leo criticized leaders who wage wars, stating that God rejects their prayers. While he did not name specific leaders, his remarks are widely understood as a reference to the ongoing war in Iran, which the head of the Catholic Church has been publicly criticizing.

stories.title: ‘We can insure the ship, but we cannot insure a human life.’
stories.summary: International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez warned that approximately 20,000 seafarers are stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, emphasizing that while ships can be insured, human lives cannot.

stories.title: Iran threatens strikes on US-linked universities in Middle East
stories.summary: Iran warned that US-linked universities in the Middle East could be targeted in retaliation after academic institutions in Tehran were struck by the US and Israel.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia took satellite images of U.S. airbase in Saudi Arabia days before Iranian strike
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia captured satellite images of a U.S. airbase in Saudi Arabia three times in the days before Iran launched an attack on the facility. The strike resulted in injuries to U.S. military personnel stationed at the base.

stories.title: JD or Marco?: Iran war raises 2028 stakes as Trump weighs Vance vs. Rubio
stories.summary: The Iran war is raising the political stakes for Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, both seen as potential 2028 presidential contenders. Vance has taken a cautious stance on prolonged military involvement, while Rubio has aligned with a more hawkish position.

stories.title: ‘Eroding shield’: Iran’s evolving attack strategy aims for interceptor shortage, report reveals
stories.summary: A report by the Jewish Institute for National Security of America warned that Iran's evolving missile attack strategy aims to deplete US and Israeli interceptor stockpiles, identifying an impending shortage as a primary concern in the coming weeks of the war.

stories.title: Ust-Luga on fire again: Drone strikes keep Russia’s Baltic oil ports burning as Ukraine targets war revenues at source
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes hit Russia's Ust-Luga oil port on the Baltic Sea multiple times in recent days, targeting energy export infrastructure whose revenues could grow as global oil prices rise amid the Iran war.

stories.title: Zeeva Bukai on the on the fragments that make us whole - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Author Zeeva Bukai discussed her two recently published novels, Anatomy of Exile and The World Between, both of which draw on her family history.

stories.title: Info ministry refutes reports of ‘complete lockdown’ on weekends as part of fuel-saving measures
stories.summary: Pakistan's information ministry denied reports circulating on social media about a complete weekend lockdown as a fuel-saving measure. The ministry labeled the notification as fake and urged citizens to rely on verified sources.

stories.title: Pentagon reportedly preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran
stories.summary: Reports indicate the Pentagon is preparing for weeks of potential ground operations in Iran as an additional 3,500 U.S. troops arrive in the Middle East. Officials told the Washington Post operations could range from Special Operations raids to larger infantry deployments, though President Trump has not yet approved any plans.

stories.title: Houthis open new front against Israel, is Red Sea shipping at risk?
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces launched their first direct attacks on Israel, opening a new front in the broader regional conflict and raising concerns about the safety of commercial shipping in the Red Sea.

stories.title: What the Iran War reveals about missile warfare - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Missile expert Tal Inbar analyzed the performance of Israel's air defenses during the Iran war, discussing the challenges of intercepting cluster munitions and implications for future Israeli security.

stories.title: Israeli police prevent Catholic leaders from celebrating Palm Sunday mass in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Catholic leaders, including the Latin Patriarch, from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem to celebrate Palm Sunday mass for the first time in centuries. Jerusalem's holy sites have been closed due to the ongoing war with Iran, as the city has faced repeated Iranian missile strikes.

stories.title: Keeping Your Heart Open- Alice Miller - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Alice Miller, a humanitarian leader and aerospace engineer whose petition to the Israeli Supreme Court opened the Israeli Air Force pilot course to women, was featured in a discussion about leadership.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of plotting ground assault while publicly seeking talks
stories.summary: Iran warned the United States it is prepared to confront any ground assault, accusing Washington of secretly planning a land attack while publicly pursuing negotiations. Regional powers met in Pakistan to seek a diplomatic resolution as the war entered its second month with further signs of escalation, including Houthi missile attacks on Israel.

stories.title: Bahrain smelter Alba assesses damage after Iran strikes aluminium plants
stories.summary: Bahrain's Alba aluminium smelter is assessing damage following Iranian strikes targeting aluminium plants in the Gulf region. Most Gulf aluminium producers have been unable to ship products through normal channels due to the disruption caused by the broader conflict.

stories.title: Massive protests against Trump across US
stories.summary: Large-scale "No Kings" protests took place across the United States and in parts of Europe on Saturday, opposing President Trump's policies and the war in Iran. Minnesota drew particularly large crowds rallying against aggressive immigration enforcement.

stories.title: Israeli police bar top Catholic figure in Jerusalem from holding Palm Sunday mass at Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Israeli police barred the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to celebrate Palm Sunday mass. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the incident, though it remains unclear whether the blockade was intentional.

stories.title: Lebanon mourns three journalists killed in Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Hundreds of mourners gathered south of Beirut to attend funerals for journalists Ali Shoeib, Fatima Ftouni, and Mohammed Ftouni, killed in an Israeli airstrike. Israel acknowledged the attack, claiming Shoeib had militant affiliations, while Lebanese officials condemned it as a violation of international law.

stories.title: Iranian missile hit on Ne'ot Hovav factory leads to fear of chemical leakage
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck a factory in the Ne'ot Hovav industrial zone in southern Israel, raising fears of chemical leakage. Israel's Environmental Protection Ministry said it was investigating but found no immediate risk to nearby communities.

stories.title: Funeral held for Lebanese journalists killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Lebanon held funerals for three journalists killed in an Israeli strike on Saturday. The journalists were targeted while reporting in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Drone attacks hit Iraqi Kurdistan amid Iran war
stories.summary: Drone strikes hit multiple targets in Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region, including the residence of the Barzani family and a US-linked military base. The attacks occurred amid escalating violence connected to the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Russia put a hula hoop on its attack drone. Now it flies 50 km into Ukraine’s rear.
stories.summary: Russian forces have added a plastic hula-hoop-shaped ring to attack drones, reportedly enabling them to fly up to 50 kilometers deeper into Ukrainian-held territory to target logistics and supply lines.

stories.title: Iran hits industrial zone in southern Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile barrage struck a chemical plant near Beersheba in southern Israel, causing a fire at the facility.

stories.title: The war with Iran may be ushering in a new nuclear age
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is accelerating nuclear proliferation concerns, as nations increasingly believe that forgoing nuclear weapons leaves them vulnerable. Analysts warn the conflict may be ushering in a new nuclear age driven by a global scramble for atomic deterrence.

stories.title: FM Sybiha: Giving platform to war criminals has nothing to do with free speech
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's appearance on a major French television channel, saying giving a platform to those he characterized as war criminals is not a matter of free speech. The remarks coincided with the G7 summit in France.

stories.title: Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem prevented from entering Church of Holy Sepulchre by Israel Police
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa and Father Francesco Ielpo, Guardian of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, from entering the church to celebrate Palm Sunday Mass in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Elite sports training opens new doors for Hong Kong youth
stories.summary: A youth fencing event was held at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong, featuring national silver medallist Ho Sze-long and junior medallist Chan Lok-hei. Nearly 170 young fencers competed in the Champions Cup for spots in an elite training program.

stories.title: Islamabad to ramp up cooperation with Ankara, Cairo in areas of mutual interest
stories.summary: Foreign ministers of Türkiye and Egypt met with Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad to strengthen bilateral cooperation. The meetings took place ahead of a quadrilateral gathering involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Egypt, which is seen as a diplomatic effort linked to ending regional conflict.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts regional powers for Iran talks, focus on Hormuz
stories.summary: Turkish, Egyptian, and Saudi officials arrived in Islamabad on Sunday for multilateral talks focused on de-escalating Middle East tensions, with a particular emphasis on security around the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Jurgen Habermas' death ends the illusion of a universal European philosophy
stories.summary: German philosopher Jürgen Habermas died on 14 March 2026. His legacy is being reassessed in light of his stance on Gaza, which critics say exposed limitations in European philosophical traditions long considered universal.

stories.title: Russia's Ust-Luga port damaged by Ukrainian drones, fire breaks out
stories.summary: Ukraine launched a drone attack on Russia's Ust-Luga port in the Leningrad region, one of the country's largest petroleum export facilities. Governor Alexander Drozdenko confirmed the port sustained damage and a fire broke out.

stories.title: Israelis told to stay indoors after strike on chemical site
stories.summary: Authorities in southern Israel urged residents to stay indoors after an Iranian missile strike damaged a chemical storage facility in the Neot Hovav industrial zone near Beersheba. No injuries were reported, but fears of a hazardous materials leak prompted shelter-in-place orders.

stories.title: Philippine oil refiner Petron buys Russian crude, eyes alternatives
stories.summary: Petron Corp., the Philippines' sole oil refiner, purchased 2.48 million barrels of Russian crude oil as the country seeks alternative energy suppliers amid disruptions caused by the war in Iran. Parent company San Miguel Corp. said Petron may continue sourcing Russian crude if the crisis persists.

stories.title: How many missiles have fallen on the Pope’s children? - comment
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses the tension between Pope Leo's calls for restraint and condemnation of war and the perspective of Israelis who face daily missile threats from Iran.

stories.title: Iran Parliament Speaker says U.S. plots ground attack despite diplomatic efforts
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged national unity, claiming the United States is plotting a ground attack on Iran despite ongoing diplomatic efforts. He characterized the current situation as a critical stage of what he called a major global war.

stories.title: Russian forces drop aerial bomb on Kramatorsk, killing three and wounding seven
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped an aerial bomb on the city of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine, killing three people including a teenager and wounding seven others.

stories.title: Three arrested in Paris after attempted bomb attack outside Bank of America
stories.summary: Three people were arrested in Paris after an attempted bomb attack outside a Bank of America branch. France's anti-terrorism prosecutor's office immediately assumed control of the investigation.

stories.title: Venezuela’s ousted leader Maduro thanks supporters in first online post from US prison
stories.summary: Venezuela's ousted leader Nicolás Maduro posted his first online message from a US prison, thanking supporters. Maduro and his wife were captured by US forces in January.

stories.title: Renewed air strike targets university in Isfahan
stories.summary: An air strike hit the Isfahan University of Technology in Iran on Sunday, the second attack on the institution in one week. Provincial official Akbar Salehi said the strike damaged several buildings and wounded four staff members. Iran's IRGC warned of possible retaliation.

stories.title: Israeli police block Catholic cardinal from Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented a Catholic cardinal from accessing the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, with authorities citing safety concerns related to the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Funeral held for Lebanese journalists killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Hundreds attended a funeral in Beirut's southern suburbs for three Lebanese journalists killed in an Israeli strike.

stories.title: UK’s Green Party fails to pass ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion after infighting, tech issues
stories.summary: The UK Green Party failed to pass a motion at its conference that would have declared "Zionism is Racism" and called for Israel's replacement with a single Palestinian state. The vote was postponed due to internal disagreements and technical problems.

stories.title: Hundreds in Beirut mourn journalists killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Hundreds of mourners gathered in Beirut for the funerals of three journalists killed by an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon, as reported by the BBC.

stories.title: Israel, US cannot miss the chance to disarm Hezbollah - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel and the United States should seize the opportunity presented by Hezbollah's weakened state to push for its disarmament, urging that the Lebanese state enforce this before 2026.

stories.title: Houthis open new front in Iran war: Will Yemeni group block Bab al-Mandeb?
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement is reportedly considering a blockade of the Bab al-Mandeb strait, one of the world's busiest maritime chokepoints, which could severely disrupt global trade amid the broader Iran conflict.

stories.title: Africa: CAF's Senegal Decision Exposes a Deeper Crisis in African Football
stories.summary: The Confederation of African Football penalized Senegal for walking out of a match, a decision that has drawn criticism as emblematic of deeper institutional governance problems within African football.

stories.title: No tuition, no grades, no power grid: why are people flocking to a ‘college’ in the middle of the desert?
stories.summary: Mars College, an off-grid community located roughly 200 miles from Los Angeles with roots in Burning Man, offers a tuition-free, ungraded educational experience in the desert. The experimental program has been attracting growing interest.

stories.title: Government allocates ₴22.35 billion to protect critical infrastructure, says Kuleba
stories.summary: The Ukrainian government allocated 22.35 billion hryvnias for the construction of protective structures for critical water, heating, electricity, and railway infrastructure, according to official Kuleba.

stories.title: Over 5,000 still in need of food for Pesach - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A charitable appeal highlighted that over 5,000 families in Israel still need food assistance for Passover, with some requesting help for the first time due to school closures preventing parents from working.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl injured in shelling of Mykolaiv region dies in hospital
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl who was wounded during Russian shelling of the Voskresenske community in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region has died in hospital from her injuries.

stories.title: France's Macron condemns Israeli police blocking Jerusalem's Latin Patriarch
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned Israeli police for blocking Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa from celebrating Palm Sunday Mass at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. Macron called it part of a troubling pattern of violations of the status of holy places in the city.

stories.title: 30 Days of War - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jewish People Policy Institute announced a public webinar assessing whether objectives of the current war have been met after 30 days and examining challenges and opportunities ahead.

stories.title: Day of zero waste: International Chef Massimo Bottura speaks to France 24
stories.summary: The UN's International Day of Zero Waste highlighted the issue of food sustainability, noting that roughly one billion tonnes of edible food is discarded annually worldwide. Chef Massimo Bottura, a UN Environment Programme Goodwill Ambassador based in Modena, Italy, discussed efforts to combat food waste.

stories.title: Qatari news channel AI Araby condemns attack on its office
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary speaker warned the United States against a ground invasion, threatening intensified attacks on U.S. allies. Meanwhile, diplomats from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt gathered in Pakistan to push for an end to the Iran conflict as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a 15-point peace proposal. An American-born Israeli soldier was killed in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: How the US memeifies its war on Iran
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondent Linh Nguyen examined how the United States has employed meme-based propaganda techniques in its military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan maintains ‘delicate balancing act’ as it hosts Iran talks
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from multiple countries met in Islamabad, Pakistan, for diplomatic talks aimed at de-escalating the US-Israel war on Iran, as Pakistan navigates a careful balancing act among regional powers.

stories.title: Pentagon reportedly preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran. U.S. military assets, including the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit, continue to deploy to the region.

stories.title: How safe are Israel’s safe rooms? - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines the effectiveness of Israel's residential safe rooms after incidents in Petah Tikva. The Home Front Command acknowledged that safe rooms are not designed to withstand direct missile hits.

stories.title: Iran: 3.500 US troops arrive in the region
stories.summary: Iran's navy chief warned that the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier would be targeted as soon as it enters range. Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Washington of planning a ground attack on Iran while claiming to pursue diplomacy, as approximately 3,500 additional U.S. troops arrived in the region.

stories.title: Pope seems to rebuke Trump in remarks about leaders with ‘hands full of blood’
stories.summary: Pope Leo stated that God ignores the prayers of leaders who wage war and have "hands full of blood," in remarks widely interpreted as directed at the Trump administration. The comments followed U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's public prayer calling for violence against enemies deserving "no mercy."

stories.title: Woman killed and two people wounded in Zaporizhzhia region due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: A woman was killed and two men were wounded by Russian shelling in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Pope Leo condemns using God to justify war in Palm Sunday mass
stories.summary: Pope Leo condemned the use of God to justify warfare during his Palm Sunday Mass, saying God rejects the prayers of those who wage war with "hands full of blood." He also prayed specifically for Christians in the Middle East.

stories.title: ‘Nowhere is really safe’: Iranian dissidents grapple with US war in Iran
stories.summary: Iranian dissidents living in exile say they face dual fears amid the US war on Iran: potential retribution from Iran's government and rising anti-immigrant sentiment in their host countries.

stories.title: Israel army says impact on industrial complex could be from missile shrapnel
stories.summary: The Israeli military said an impact at the Ramat Hovav industrial zone in the Negev desert may have been caused by missile shrapnel following a new barrage fired from Iran. Israeli television showed thick black smoke rising from the site.

stories.title: Pentagon preparing for US ground assault in Iran, says report
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that the Pentagon is preparing options for a ground assault in Iran as thousands of U.S. troops and marines arrive in the Middle East. Officials said any such operation would involve raids rather than a full-scale invasion.

stories.title: First PIA direct flight to London in 6 years takes to the skies
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines resumed direct flights from Islamabad to London's Heathrow Airport for the first time in six years. The inaugural flight, PK-785, was launched at a ceremony attended by Pakistan's Defence Secretary, the British High Commissioner, and PIA Consortium Chairman Arif Habib. Four weekly flights are planned.

stories.title: Knesset set to hold final 2 votes on passing 2026 state budget
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset was set to hold its final two votes on the 2026 state budget ahead of a March 31 deadline. The spending plan increases defense funding amid the war with Iran and includes allocations for ultra-Orthodox constituencies. Failure to pass would trigger early elections.

stories.title: Ukrainian FM: Another country to join agreement on Special Tribunal for Russia’s aggression
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced at the G7 summit in France that another country has indicated readiness to join the agreement establishing a Special Tribunal for Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Arkia cancels Jordan flights after authorities block approvals, limiting alternatives from Israel
stories.summary: Israeli airline Arkia canceled flights to Jordan after Jordanian authorities blocked flight approvals. Some flights were rerouted to Taba, Egypt, where crossing fees have been doubled.

stories.title: Police stop top Catholic figures from reaching Holy Sepulchre for Palm Sunday Mass
stories.summary: Israeli police blocked the Latin Patriarch from reaching the Church of the Holy Sepulchre for Palm Sunday Mass in Jerusalem, citing wartime security. The Prime Minister's office said there was no malicious intent and promised a resolution amid international criticism.

stories.title: A toothless Iran? Missile and drone strikes show it can still inflict pain
stories.summary: Despite sustained US-Israeli strikes, Iran demonstrated a continued capacity to retaliate through a wave of recent missile and drone attacks targeting adversaries in the region.

stories.title: Al Araby TV condemns Israeli attack on Tehran office
stories.summary: Al Araby TV condemned an Israeli strike on the building housing its Tehran office, calling the attack on a civilian commercial building a violation of international law. The Iranian Red Crescent Society said at least 10 people were wounded in the strike.

stories.title: ‘Doctrine of the Mean’: how the US lost a 2-decade race to China in brain implants
stories.summary: A Chinese research team has developed a commercially approved semi-invasive brain-computer interface using a middle-path approach, overtaking the United States in a technology race that Washington had led for two decades.

stories.title: Farmers plead for tax breaks, diesel guarantees and help buying fertiliser as national cabinet meets on fuel crisis
stories.summary: Australian farmers are urging the federal government for tax breaks, diesel supply guarantees, and fertiliser purchasing assistance amid a fuel crisis driven by rising petrol prices. National cabinet was set to meet Monday to discuss broader assistance for affected business sectors.

stories.title: Helplines buzz with alerts from seafarers trapped in war
stories.summary: Over 1,000 emails and messages have been received from seafarers stranded near the Strait of Hormuz as the Middle East conflict disrupts maritime traffic and traps crews aboard their vessels.

stories.title: From appeasement to escalation: Europe's dangerous Iran blind spot - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between Europe's appeasement of hostile ideologies in the 1930s and what it describes as Europe's current failure to confront Iran's stated ambitions.

stories.title: Israel blocks top Catholic leaders from Palm Sunday Mass at Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Israeli forces blocked Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, and Father Francesco Ielpo, custos of the Holy Land, from reaching the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in occupied East Jerusalem to celebrate Palm Sunday Mass.

stories.title: Finland reports drone crashes, alleges territorial violation
stories.summary: Two unidentified drones crashed in southern Finland. Finnish Prime Minister stated the drones may have been Ukrainian drones that strayed into Finnish airspace, and authorities are investigating a possible territorial violation.

stories.title: Enemy attacks Naftogaz facilities for fourth day; damage reported
stories.summary: Russian troops attacked Naftogaz Group production facilities in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones, marking the fourth consecutive day of strikes. Damage to the energy infrastructure was reported.

stories.title: Palestinian economy recedes by 20% over two years amid Gaza War
stories.summary: The Palestinian economy has contracted by approximately 20 percent over two years due to Israel's military operations in Gaza and intensified restrictions in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Israeli footballer’s role in assault on southern Lebanon sparks outrage
stories.summary: Israeli Premier League player Menashe Zalka was filmed firing alongside Israeli army soldiers during an assault in southern Lebanon, generating widespread public backlash.

stories.title: Indonesia cuts free meals to save US$2.3 billion as fuel prices soar
stories.summary: Indonesia announced it will reduce its free school meal program from six to five days per week, aiming to save approximately 40 trillion rupiah (US$2.3 billion). The austerity measure responds to price pressures stemming from the Middle East war.

stories.title: Iran ‘hits’ US AWACS, air tankers: What else has it targeted in past month?
stories.summary: Iran reportedly struck U.S. E-3 Sentry airborne early-warning aircraft, which are used to track drones, missiles, and aircraft from hundreds of kilometers away, as part of a series of Iranian attacks over the past month.

stories.title: Bahrain announces curfew for maritime traffic
stories.summary: Bahrain announced a nighttime maritime curfew from 6:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. local time to protect seafarers and enhance coastal security amid Iranian attacks on the region.

stories.title: Fire Reported After Ukrainian Strike on Ust-Luga Port
stories.summary: A fire was reported at Russia's Ust-Luga port in the northwest after it was targeted by drones in an attack claimed by Ukraine's military.

stories.title: The week in pictures: Massive daytime attack on Ukraine, 'No Kings' and France's adieu to Jospin
stories.summary: France held a national tribute to former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, Russia launched one of its largest daytime attacks on Ukraine, and a third round of "No Kings" protests against President Trump took place across the US and other capitals.

stories.title: Sybiha: Weapons from PURL not to be redirected; another country to join program
stories.summary: At the G7 summit in France, US partners assured Ukraine that weapons allocated under the PURL program would not be redirected. An additional country expressed interest in joining the program to procure weapons for Ukraine, according to Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha.

stories.title: Israeli army kills 6 Palestinians in attack on Gaza police
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least six Palestinians in strikes targeting police checkpoints in the al-Mawasi area near Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Pope Leo says God rejects prayers of leaders who wage wars
stories.summary: Pope Leo used his Palm Sunday address at St. Peter's Square to criticize wars and express concern for Christians in the Middle East, saying God rejects the prayers of leaders who wage wars.

stories.title: Lebanese family launches mobile aid initiative for displaced
stories.summary: A Lebanese family in Beirut launched a mobile aid initiative to provide support to people displaced by the ongoing conflict in Lebanon.

stories.title: Russia wants to legalize cars stolen in EU
stories.summary: Russia is reportedly considering legislation that would allow the legal registration of vehicles stolen from European Union countries, raising concerns among German police that it could incentivize increased car thefts across Europe.

stories.title: DR Congo conflict: M23’s alleged withdrawal shrouded in confusion
stories.summary: Conflicting reports from local sources, rebel leaders, and the Kinshasa government have left it unclear whether M23 fighters in the Democratic Republic of Congo are genuinely withdrawing or simply rotating troops along front lines.

stories.title: One in five UK hospitality businesses fear collapse as costs surge
stories.summary: A UK industry survey found that one in five hospitality businesses fear collapse within the next 12 months. Pubs, restaurants, and hotels face mounting pressure from upcoming increases in business rates and minimum wage thresholds taking effect.

stories.title: ‘No Kings’ flagship protest brings spotlight back to Minneapolis
