stories.summary: Israeli air strikes in Lebanon killed dozens of people, including six paramedics and two journalists, as military operations continued across the country.

stories.title: ‘No dreams, no joy’: Iranians struggle amid war, economic collapse, regime controls
stories.summary: Iranian civilians described explosions, internet blackouts, and deteriorating economic conditions as the ongoing conflict compounds the effects of a January government crackdown. Concerns persist that a US deal could further entrench the regime.

stories.title: Scientists dive beneath Arctic ice to study threatened ecosystems
stories.summary: Scientists completed specialized training in Finland to conduct dives beneath Arctic ice, studying fragile polar ecosystems threatened by climate change. The course provides hands-on skills to explore underwater habitats that robots cannot safely survey, with instructors emphasizing the urgency of further research.

stories.title: Israel kills three journalists in Lebanon air strike
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit a car carrying journalists in southern Lebanon, killing three reporters including Al Manar TV's Ali Shoaib and Al Mayadeen correspondent Fatima Fattouni. Israel claimed Shoaib was a Hezbollah Radwan Force member without providing evidence.

stories.title: 'Divide among men above and under 35': CPAC highlights generational GOP split
stories.summary: At the annual Conservative Political Action Conference, President Trump's absence highlighted a generational divide among Republican men over support for the president and the Iran war. Political analysts noted that men over 35 remain firm Trump supporters, while younger men are increasingly breaking away.

stories.title: Beijing tightens drone rules, citing ‘low-altitude security’ concerns
stories.summary: Beijing's municipal legislature approved strict new regulations on drone sales, storage, and transport, citing low-altitude security concerns. The rules ban the sale or lease of unmanned aerial vehicles and 17 designated core components to any person or organization without public security approval.

stories.title: Death toll after nighttime attack on Odesa climbs to two, more than ten people wounded
stories.summary: A Russian nighttime strike on civilian infrastructure in Odesa killed at least two people and wounded more than ten, including a 9-year-old boy. The death toll rose as rescue operations continued.

stories.title: Trump says US may not be there for NATO if needed
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump suggested the United States may not fulfill its NATO commitments, expressing frustration over Western allies' lack of support since the start of the US-Israeli offensive against Iran a month ago.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Naseem Shah under fire after criticism of politician’s PSL visit
stories.summary: Pakistani fast bowler Naseem Shah faced backlash after publicly criticizing a politician's attendance at a closed-door Pakistan Super League match in Lahore.

stories.title: Missile fired from Yemen as Israel and US target Iran
stories.summary: Israel detected a missile fired from Yemen on Saturday, marking the first such launch since the Iran war began. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington expected to conclude military operations against Iran within weeks rather than months.

stories.title: At least 15 US troops wounded in Iran strike on Saudi airbase: Reports
stories.summary: At least 15 US troops were wounded, with five reported in serious condition, after an Iranian strike on a Saudi airbase that also damaged refuelling aircraft.

stories.title: UNSC holds closed-door session on Iran school bombing
stories.summary: The UN Security Council held a closed-door meeting at Russia's request to discuss US-Israeli strikes on civilian sites in Iran. Pakistan participated as a non-permanent Security Council member. Iran, which is not currently a Council member, was not present at the session.

stories.title: Iran footballers pay tribute to victims of school strike at start of war
stories.summary: Iran's national football team played its first match since the start of the Middle East conflict, losing 2-1 to Nigeria. Players paid tribute to victims of a school strike during the game.

stories.title: Hong Kong police seize 1,600 litres of diesel, arrest 1 in raid of illegal fuel site
stories.summary: Hong Kong police and Fire Services Department officers raided an illegal fuel station in Sai Wan, seizing 1,600 litres of diesel worth approximately HK$50,000. One man was arrested for alleged fire hazard and fuel regulation violations. The crackdown comes amid rising oil prices driven by Middle East conflicts.

stories.title: India approves $25bn defence buys, including Russian S-400 missile systems
stories.summary: India's Defence Acquisition Council, led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, approved defence purchases worth approximately $25 billion, including additional Russian-made S-400 long-range missile systems. The ministry said it signed the highest value of capital procurement contracts in a single fiscal year.

stories.title: Former US defence chief says more war won’t bring peace to Middle East
stories.summary: Former US Secretary of Defense Leon Panetta stated that continued military action will not bring peace to the Middle East, adding that there is no clear end to the war in Iran.

stories.title: USS Gerald Ford docks in Croatia for ‘scheduled visit and maintenance’ after laundry fire
stories.summary: The USS Gerald Ford docked in Split, Croatia, for a scheduled visit and maintenance following a laundry fire on March 12 that injured two sailors and damaged approximately 100 beds.

stories.title: Missile fired from Yemen as Israel and US target Iran
stories.summary: A missile was fired from Yemen toward Israel while U.S. and Israeli forces conducted strikes on Iran. This marked the first missile launch from Yemen since the war began.

stories.title: Israeli military says it identified a launch of a missile from Yemen
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed it identified a missile launch originating from Yemen. This marked the first missile fired from Yemen since the outbreak of the war against Iran.

stories.title: ‘Our assumptions are broken’: how fraudulent church data revealed AI’s threat to polling
stories.summary: Experts have identified a growing threat to polling accuracy from survey participants using AI tools to generate fraudulent responses at scale. The issue came to light partly through questionable church attendance data in Britain, including a 2024 Bible Society report that appeared to show surging congregations.

stories.title: Kuwait Airport attacked by several drones as Iran continues attacking Gulf
stories.summary: Several drones struck Kuwait Airport as part of Iran's ongoing attacks on Gulf targets. The strike followed a drone attack on Oman's Salalah port and a ballistic missile interception over Abu Dhabi on the same weekend.

stories.title: Trump says 'Cuba is next', denies losing MAGA support
stories.summary: President Trump stated that "Cuba is next" while denying any loss of MAGA support. Cuba's government has faced increasing pressure from Trump, who imposed a de facto oil blockade on the island in January.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Chernihiv region 34 times; one man killed
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the Chernihiv region 34 times over 24 hours, killing a 95-year-old man. The attacks also damaged a grain storage facility in the Semenivka community and an energy facility in the Siversk district.

stories.title: Ukraine signs 10-year defence pact with Qatar, eyes broader Gulf cooperation
stories.summary: Ukraine signed a 10-year defence cooperation agreement with Qatar on Saturday as part of President Zelensky's Gulf tour. Kyiv is pursuing a series of deals with Gulf states to counter missile and drone threats, leveraging its battlefield experience to build new partnerships.

stories.title: Pope Leo tells Monaco to use 'gift of smallness' for good
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV visited Monaco and called on the principality's wealthy residents to address the widening gap between rich and poor by channeling their prosperity toward justice.

stories.title: Visiting UAE, Zelensky announces defense cooperation with Abu Dhabi amid Iran attacks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced a defense cooperation agreement with the UAE during a visit to Abu Dhabi, offering anti-drone expertise to Gulf nations facing Iranian attacks. Iran had recently targeted Abu Dhabi and an Omani port.

stories.title: Indonesia begins enforcing social media ban for children under-16s
stories.summary: Indonesia began enforcing a ban on social media use for children under 16 on Saturday. The government cited threats from online pornography, cyberbullying, and internet addiction, with officials warning digital platforms there is "no room for compromise."

stories.title: Cuba holds civilian military drills amid deepening fuel crisis
stories.summary: Cuba conducted nationwide civilian military exercises on Friday involving weapons training and combat drills as part of its "war of the entire people" doctrine. The drills took place amid a deepening humanitarian crisis on the island, including chronic fuel shortages exacerbated by a US oil blockade.

stories.title: Russians attack Odesa with more than 60 combat drones overnight, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian city of Odesa with more than 60 combat drones overnight on March 28.

stories.title: US Congress panel demands full public hearing on Iran war as concerns mount
stories.summary: Democrats on the US House Armed Services Committee, led by Ranking Member Adam Smith, demanded an immediate public hearing on President Trump's war against Iran. The lawmakers urged the Pentagon to testify publicly on strategy, transparency, and the conflict's human and economic costs.

stories.title: Ukraine, UAE seal defence deal: Kyiv’s 'know-how and equipment” gain recognition
stories.summary: Ukraine and the United Arab Emirates signed a defense cooperation agreement focusing on the export of Ukrainian defense technology, including interceptor drones. The deal comes as Middle East countries facing Iranian drone strikes increasingly recognize Ukraine's battlefield-tested expertise.

stories.title: Pakistan, IMF strike deal over disbursement of $1.2 billion fund
stories.summary: Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund reached a deal for the disbursement of approximately $1.2 billion. IMF mission chief Iva Petrova said Pakistan will access about $1.0 billion under the Extended Fund Facility and roughly $210 million under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, subject to IMF board approval.

stories.title: Protests in Yemen against US-Israeli attacks as Houthis warn of action
stories.summary: Protesters in Yemen rallied in support of Iran, Palestine, and Lebanon amid ongoing US and Israeli military operations. The Houthi movement warned of further action in response to the attacks.

stories.title: What Taiwan's imprisonment of opposition figure Ko Wen-je means for its political landscape
stories.summary: Taiwanese opposition figure Ko Wen-je was sentenced to 17 years in prison this week, ending his 2028 presidential bid and removing a prominent centrist from politics. Analysts say the ruling could reshape Taiwan's domestic political alignments and have implications for cross-strait relations with China.

stories.title: How the US and Israel are making the Islamic republic stronger
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that US and Israeli military operations against Iran are strengthening the Islamic Republic by reinforcing a theological narrative of martyrdom and sacrifice among its population.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 4 as deal to end war dims
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Ukraine killed four people as prospects for a peace deal dimmed. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated openness to redirecting weapons to Kyiv to support the US campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 252 of the 273 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 252 of 273 Russian drones launched against Ukraine since the evening of March 27, according to Ukrainian military reports.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis enter Iran war with missile strike on Israel
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces launched missiles at Israel, declaring their formal entry into the regional conflict in support of Iran.

stories.title: AI ‘collusion’ forcing down wages a bigger threat than job-stealing robots: ILO economist
stories.summary: ILO chief macroeconomist Ekkehard Ernst warned at an event in Beijing that AI-driven "algorithmic collusion" quietly eroding wages and workplace safety poses a greater threat than mass job displacement. Ernst said public fears of a robot-driven unemployment wave have overestimated AI's disruptive potential.

stories.title: One month into Iran war, only hard choices for Trump
stories.summary: One month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, President Donald Trump faces difficult options as global energy prices rise and his approval ratings decline. Iran continues to disrupt Gulf oil and gas shipments and launch missile and drone strikes across the Middle East, while diplomatic efforts have so far failed to resolve the widening crisis.

stories.title: Iran says it 'destroyed' Ukrainian air defence depot in Dubai
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they fired missiles that destroyed a Ukrainian air defence depot in Dubai, according to Fars news agency. The claim followed Ukrainian President Zelensky's announcement of a deepened defence cooperation agreement with Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: Zelenskyy in Abu Dhabi: teams to finalize details on defense deal after UAE talks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi and agreed on security and defence cooperation. Ukrainian military specialists had already been deployed in the UAE for several weeks prior to the visit.

stories.title: 12-year-old Israeli girl killed, others injured in bus accident at French ski resort
stories.summary: A 12-year-old Israeli girl was killed at a French ski resort when a bus rolled down a slope after the driver disembarked. Fourteen other Israeli tourists sustained light injuries, with two hospitalized.

stories.title: Pippa Small Jewellery: Where ethics, craft, and culture converge
stories.summary: Pippa Small Jewellery, based in London's Westbourne Grove, collaborates with artisans in Palestine, Colombia, and Afghanistan. The brand combines ethical sourcing with cultural storytelling through gold, glass, and gemstone designs.

stories.title: Rubio raised his voice at EU foreign policy chief — then denied anything happened
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly raised his voice at EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas during a G7 ministerial meeting in France. Kallas had pressed Rubio over Washington's failure to increase pressure on Russia. Rubio later denied the incident occurred.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kryvyi Rih for second time this morning
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih for the second time on the morning of Saturday, March 28.

stories.title: Finland to audit whether US is actually delivering NATO-bought weapons to Ukraine
stories.summary: Finnish Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen announced Finland will audit whether the United States has delivered weapons purchased by European NATO members for Ukraine. Häkkänen stated that what has been promised to Ukraine must reach Ukraine.

stories.title: Hundreds of thousands of people expected at London march against the far right – live
stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to march in central London on Saturday in an anti-far-right demonstration organized by the Together Alliance, proceeding from Park Lane to Trafalgar Square. A separate event organized by the Palestine Coalition also took place. The alliance formed in response to growing far-right sentiment in the UK.

stories.title: Sudanese artist Ahmed Umar and the art of belonging
stories.summary: Sudanese artist Ahmed Umar discussed the influence of Sufi traditions, exile, and revolution on his work. He reflected on how art can preserve memory, dignity, and collective renewal for displaced communities.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits Tehran home, killing several children
stories.summary: A pre-dawn Israeli strike hit a residential building in southern Tehran, killing at least five children. Israeli authorities separately reported that an Iranian missile attack killed a man in Tel Aviv on Friday as Tehran continued retaliatory strikes across the region.

stories.title: Beirut 'holding its breath' as Israel launches strikes across Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel launched strikes across Lebanon, leaving Beirut in a state of heightened anxiety. FRANCE 24 reported that the capital has become a massive refuge for displaced people living out of their vehicles with nowhere to go.

stories.title: Zelensky agrees defence cooperation with UAE, Qatar on Gulf tour
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made an unannounced visit to the UAE and Qatar, agreeing on defence cooperation with both countries. The trip followed a defence agreement signed with Saudi Arabia as Gulf states contend with Iranian drone threats.

stories.title: Zelensky says Ukraine, UAE 'agreed to cooperate' on defence
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made an unannounced visit to the UAE and announced a defence cooperation agreement. The visit followed a similar defence deal with Saudi Arabia, as Gulf states face threats from Iranian drone attacks.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Sumy region 44 times in past 24 hours, two wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 44 strikes on Ukraine's Sumy region over a 24-hour period, wounding two people.

stories.title: The war on Iran faces a MAGA backlash
stories.summary: A significant division has emerged within the MAGA movement over the prospect of a U.S. war with Iran, potentially undermining former President Trump's approach to the conflict.

stories.title: Iran’s football players hold schoolbags wearing black armbands in solidarity with slain girls
stories.summary: Iran's national football players lined up holding pink and purple schoolbags and wearing black armbands in solidarity with victims of the Shajareh Tayyebeh School attack. Tehran says the strike during the first day of joint US-Israeli operations killed more than 175 people, including children and teachers.

stories.title: UN warns: over 10,000 Colombians recruited as mercenaries in the past decade
stories.summary: A United Nations expert group on mercenaries warned that over 10,000 Colombian citizens, mostly former military and police personnel, have been recruited as mercenaries abroad over the past decade. The finding followed an 11-day visit to Colombia. Recruits were reportedly offered between $2,000 and $6,000 per month.

stories.title: Voices from the Arab press: Hezbollah in state of crisis, Strait of Hormuz paralyzed
stories.summary: Arab media commentators highlighted Hezbollah's deepening organizational crisis and the paralysis of the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing regional conflict. The assessments appeared in a weekly roundup of opinions from Arab press outlets.

stories.title: Long-term deradicalization in Gaza faces major hurdles - opinion
stories.summary: Efforts to pursue long-term deradicalization in Gaza face significant geographical and political obstacles. Analysts assess that these barriers make lasting ideological change unlikely in the territory.

stories.title: Peacemaker’s role
stories.summary: Pakistan has positioned itself as a peace broker amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Pakistani military and civilian leaders delivered a 15-point U.S. peace plan to Tehran, which publicly rejected it but is reportedly still reviewing it unofficially. The effort comes as GCC countries are increasingly drawn into the regional conflict.

stories.title: Brazil unveils first supersonic fighter jet manufactured on its soil, a milestone for Latin America
stories.summary: Brazilian manufacturer Embraer unveiled the first F-39E Gripen supersonic fighter jet produced at its facility in Gavião Peixoto, São Paulo state. It is the first of 15 jets Embraer will build under a total contract for 36 aircraft ordered from Sweden's Saab. Brazil's presidency called the milestone unprecedented in Latin America.

stories.title: 2 soldiers seriously hurt in Lebanon clashes as Hezbollah rockets and drones pound north
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were seriously wounded and seven others moderately hurt in clashes in Lebanon. Hezbollah launched rockets and drones at northern Israel. The Israeli military said it killed two senior Hezbollah communications unit members in a Beirut strike.

stories.title: Fitch holds Israel's credit rating at 'A', but debt and war cloud outlook
stories.summary: Fitch Ratings maintained Israel's credit rating at 'A' but flagged concerns over rising debt and ongoing military operations. The agency noted that U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran and domestic political divisions could hinder fiscal consolidation.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis launch first missile strike on Israel since Iran war began
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces launched a missile strike on Israel, their first since the Iran war began. Israel said it intercepted the attack. The Houthis stated they acted in support of Tehran and regional resistance groups.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Israel military says striking 'regime targets' in Tehran; One killed in Tel Aviv amid Iranian missile attack
stories.summary: Israel conducted strikes on what it described as regime targets in Tehran, while Iran launched missiles hitting Tel Aviv and a US military base in Saudi Arabia. Several US service members were wounded and planes were damaged at the Saudi facility.

stories.title: Iranian strikes on Saudi base leave 29 US troops wounded, AP reports
stories.summary: At least 29 U.S. troops were wounded in a series of Iranian missile and drone strikes on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia over the past week, according to AP. The latest attack injured 15 personnel, five of them seriously.

stories.title: Pakistan to host Saudi, Turkey, Egypt for talks on Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan is set to host Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt for diplomatic talks on the Iran war. Islamabad has emerged as a key intermediary, facilitating the exchange of messages between Iran and the United States.

stories.title: Severe floods hit Makhachkala, capital of Russia’s Dagestan region
stories.summary: Severe flooding struck Makhachkala, the capital of Russia's Dagestan region. Footage showed floodwaters submerging vehicles and homes across the city.

stories.title: Irresponsible targeting
stories.summary: The article discusses concerns about US targeting practices in the war on Iran, criticizing strikes on protected persons, civilian infrastructure, and other sites in apparent violation of international humanitarian law standards that the US itself helped develop.

stories.title: Partisans conduct reconnaissance at key Russian armored vehicle plant in Nyzhniy Tagil
stories.summary: Agents of the ATESH partisan movement conducted reconnaissance at Uralvagonzavod, a major Russian armored vehicle manufacturing plant located in Nyzhniy Tagil, Russia.

stories.title: Third No Kings protests to see millions across US push back on Trump administration
stories.summary: Millions of Americans were expected to participate in "No Kings" protests on Saturday against the Trump administration, with over 3,000 events planned across all 50 states and 16 countries. The rallies were organized by a coalition including groups Indivisible and 50501, along with labor unions and grassroots organizations.

stories.title: Cambridge top architect Francois Penz relocates to China from UK
stories.summary: Francois Penz, former head of the University of Cambridge's architecture department, has joined Nanjing University full-time. The school of architecture and urban planning at Nanjing University announced the appointment on March 17. Penz is known for pioneering interdisciplinary work linking architecture and film.

stories.title: Aasiya Andrabi: How India's terror laws turned dissent into life sentences
stories.summary: Aasiya Andrabi, a 64-year-old Kashmiri grandmother, was sentenced to three life terms under India's anti-terror laws. The court reportedly failed to prove she committed, funded, or carried out any acts of violence.

stories.title: Why Chinese pour leftover TCM medicine onto roads, hoping others will walk, drive over it
stories.summary: In parts of China, people deliberately pour leftover Traditional Chinese Medicine herbs onto public roads. A folk superstition holds that when others walk or drive over the remnants, it helps transfer illness away from the patient. The practice is believed to trace back to the Tang dynasty (618–907).

stories.title: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels say launched missile attack on Israel
stories.summary: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for a missile attack on Israel. Military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree announced the strike via the group's Al-Masirah television network. Israel's military said it had intercepted the missile.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis claim missile attack on Israel in expanding conflict
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed their first missile launch toward Israel since the broader Middle East conflict began, firing a projectile that the Israeli military said it intercepted early Saturday. Analysts noted the attack was unexpected, as Israeli authorities had assessed the Houthis would join the conflict only if ceasefire negotiations were underway.

stories.title: Demonstrators gather in Dakar to protest Iran war and show solidarity
stories.summary: Dozens of protesters gathered in Dakar, Senegal, to oppose the ongoing Iran war. Demonstrators voiced opposition to military action and expressed solidarity with countries affected by U.S. and Israeli operations.

stories.title: Singapore’s Lawrence Wong wraps up ‘short but meaningful’ visit to Hong Kong
stories.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong concluded his first official visit to Hong Kong since taking office in 2024, meeting political figures and business leaders including former Chief Justice Andrew Li and Richard Li. Wong described the visit as promoting closer cooperation between the two financial centres.

stories.title: Nepal’s ex-PM Oli detained over alleged role in deadly protest crackdown
stories.summary: Nepal's former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli was detained over his alleged role in a deadly crackdown on protesters. The country's new home minister described the arrest as the beginning of justice.

stories.title: Trump orders TSA agents be paid as Congress still deadlocked over issue that has disrupted airports
stories.summary: President Trump ordered TSA agents to be paid while Congress remained deadlocked over a funding issue. The lapse in funding has caused significant disruptions and long lines at airports across the United States.

stories.title: Senegal to stage AFCON victory celebrations in Paris despite losing title
stories.summary: Senegal's national football team planned victory celebrations in Paris ahead of a friendly match against Peru at the Stade de France on Saturday, despite being stripped of their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title. The Confederation of African Football awarded the title to Morocco, and Senegal's football federation has appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

stories.title: Elon Musk joined Modi-Trump call on West Asia crisis; White House says talks ‘productive’
stories.summary: Elon Musk reportedly joined a phone call between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump discussing the West Asia crisis. The White House described the talks as productive, though it remains unclear why Musk was on the call or whether he spoke.

stories.title: Over 180 clashes reported in past 24 hours, most intense in Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 181 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front lines on March 27, with the most intense fighting occurring in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors.

stories.title: Crisis meeting
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Zardari chaired a high-level meeting with the prime minister, chief of defence forces, and key officials to discuss the US-Israeli war on Iran and its implications for Pakistan. The meeting stressed national consensus and public awareness regarding challenges posed by the conflict on Pakistan's borders.

stories.title: IMF, Pakistan reach staff-level agreement unlocking $1.2bn tranche
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund reached a staff-level agreement with Pakistan to disburse approximately $1.2 billion under the third review of its Extended Fund Facility and the second review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility. The IMF endorsed Islamabad's fuel pricing policy amid the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Russian military loses another 1,300 troops and seven MLRS in war against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reported that Russian forces lost approximately 1,300 troops in a single 24-hour period, along with seven multiple-launch rocket systems. Total Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, are estimated at approximately 1,294,470 personnel.

stories.title: Drone attack damages radar system at Kuwait international airport
stories.summary: Multiple drone strikes hit Kuwait International Airport, severely damaging its radar system. No casualties were reported, according to Kuwait's Civil Aviation Authority via the state news agency.

stories.title: 3 Palestinians, including teen, killed by IDF in West Bank; CNN crew briefly detained
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed three Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, including a 15-year-old shot in Dheisheh refugee camp. The IDF said troops fired at "key instigators" during incidents in Qalandiya. A CNN crew was briefly detained while covering settler violence, with one journalist put in a chokehold.

stories.title: Production at major Iran steel plant halted after Israeli-US strikes, reports say
stories.summary: Production at the Khuzestan Steel Company in southwestern Iran has been halted after US-Israeli strikes damaged several units and steel-making facilities on Friday, according to Iranian media outlet Shargh daily.

stories.title: Iran military says targeted US vessel near Oman port
stories.summary: Iran's military announced it targeted a US logistics vessel at a considerable distance from the Omani port of Salalah. A spokesman for Iran's central military command confirmed the strike in a statement carried by state TV.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Overnight developments across the Middle East include a Houthi missile attack claimed against Israel, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warning Israel of a "heavy price" for strikes on Iranian infrastructure, and continued diplomatic efforts struggling to contain the widening regional conflict.

stories.title: IDF officers, soldiers wounded in separate attacks in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: IDF officers and soldiers were wounded in separate attacks in southern Lebanon. All injured personnel were evacuated to hospitals for treatment, and their families were notified.

stories.title: 4 held as Hong Kong seizes HK$92 million of illicit cigarettes from cargo vessel
stories.summary: Hong Kong customs seized approximately 20 million illicit cigarettes worth an estimated HK$92 million from a cargo vessel during a joint anti-smuggling operation with mainland Chinese authorities. Four people were arrested in connection with the seizure.

stories.title: Israel’s 'Stonehenge’ not alone with near 30 similar sites, satellite imagery reveals - study
stories.summary: A study using satellite imagery revealed nearly 30 circular stone structures similar to Israel's "Stonehenge" site. The newly discovered formations range from approximately 50 to 250 meters in diameter and were built with stones from local basalt fields.

stories.title: UNSC holds closed-door session on school bombing
stories.summary: The UN Security Council held a closed-door meeting at Russia's request to discuss US-Israeli strikes on civilian sites in Iran, including a school bombing on February 28. Pakistan participated as a non-permanent Council member. Iran, not currently on the Council, had separately called for an emergency meeting.

stories.title: US marines arrive in Mideast as Israel, Iran continue strikes
stories.summary: US Marines arrived in the Middle East as Israel and Iran continued exchanging strikes. Yemen's Houthi group, an Iranian-backed movement, launched missile attacks against Israel after previously staying out of the conflict.

stories.title: Iran launches strikes on Israel, Gulf as Houthis enter war
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement, an Iranian-backed group, has entered the conflict by launching missile attacks against Israel. Iran has also carried out strikes targeting Israel and Gulf states as the regional war widens.

stories.title: Hong Kong breaks ground on Northern Metropolis data centre to power AI push
stories.summary: Hong Kong broke ground on a major data centre at the Sandy Ridge site in the Northern Metropolis, spanning over 110,000 square metres. Innovation and Technology Secretary Sun Dong said the facility will boost the city's computing capacity and support national AI development.

stories.title: Who are the Houthis, Iran’s allies in Yemen? - explainer
stories.summary: The Houthis are an Iran-allied armed group based in Yemen capable of striking Gulf neighbors. Their potential involvement in the Iran conflict could cause major disruption to maritime navigation around the Arabian Peninsula.

stories.title: Hundreds of organised protests show resilience of Iranian regime, experts say
stories.summary: Since the start of the war, Iran's government has organized more than 850 pro-regime public demonstrations and detained at least 1,400 people in a crackdown on dissent. Experts say the scale of these efforts underscores the Islamic Republic's resilience despite a month-long US and Israeli airstrike campaign.

stories.title: North Carolina woman forgives mom for disappearing without a word 24 years ago
stories.summary: Amanda Smith of North Carolina reunited with her mother, 62-year-old Michele Hundley Smith, on Thursday after authorities located her alive and well following a 24-year disappearance. Amanda said she forgives her mother, acknowledging the complexity of the situation.

stories.title: Enemy strikes industrial facility in Kryvyi Rih, killing two and injuring others
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an industrial facility in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, on the morning of March 28, killing at least two people and injuring others.

stories.title: US using anti-tank land mines in Iran's Shiraz to neutralize ballistic missile launchers - report
stories.summary: The US military reportedly deployed American BLU-91/B anti-tank land mines in Iran's Shiraz to neutralize ballistic missile launchers. According to The Washington Post, the mines were delivered by aircraft using the Gator mine scattering system.

stories.title: Russian attack on Odesa: one killed, casualties rise to 11
stories.summary: A Russian strike on civilian infrastructure in Odesa, Ukraine, killed one person and injured 11 others, including a child. The attack targeted civilian areas of the port city.

stories.title: Philippine transport strikers say Marcos Jr failing to control oil prices
stories.summary: Transport workers in the Philippines have called on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to impose price caps and take stronger action against oil companies amid rising fuel costs.

stories.title: For Asia, the worst effects of Trump’s war on Iran are yet to come
stories.summary: An analysis warns that the US-led war on Iran will disproportionately harm Asia, the world's most energy-import-dependent region. The consequences may hurt US ally Japan more than China, which could potentially emerge from the crisis with strategic advantages.

stories.title: Pakistan eases trade rules with Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan has permitted exporters to ship food and pharmaceutical products to Iran via land routes without mandatory banking instruments amid disrupted maritime trade from the Gulf crisis. Islamabad also authorized rice exports to Central Asian republics and Azerbaijan through Iran.

stories.title: Belgian ex‑official appeals war crimes trial over 1961 Congo leader's murder
stories.summary: A 93-year-old former Belgian diplomat who was ordered to stand trial over the 1961 assassination of Congolese independence leader Patrice Lumumba has appealed the decision.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran: What’s happening on day 29 of attacks?
stories.summary: Tensions between Israel and Iran continue to escalate on day 29 of Israeli air attacks, with Iran warning that Israel will pay a "heavy price" for the strikes.

stories.title: Strikes on Ukrainian cities kill three, child dies in drone attack on Moscow
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities killed three people and wounded at least 13 overnight Friday into Saturday. Separately, a Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow killed a child, according to local authorities on both sides.

stories.title: IDF finds bombproof room held up to direct hit from cluster munition
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported that a bombproof safe room in Petah Tikva withstood a direct hit from a cluster munition submunition on Tuesday. Those sheltering inside, including two children, were unharmed. It was reportedly the first such direct strike on a bomb-safe room in Israel.

stories.title: Inheritance mutation made thru ‘fictitious will’ annulled
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court annulled an 80-year-old inheritance mutation in a land dispute in Rahim Yar Khan district, ruling that Islamic law prohibits making a will in favor of legal heirs. The case involved land owned by the late Din Muhammad, with petitioners alleging a fictitious will was used to secretly transfer property in 1945.

stories.title: G7 allies press Marco Rubio on US plans for Iran war
stories.summary: G7 allies pressed US Secretary of State Marco Rubio at a meeting near Paris for clarity on American plans for the war in Iran, now nearly one month old. Concerns also centered on cooperation between Russia and Iran. The UK foreign minister urged a swift resolution to restore regional stability.

stories.title: Kryvyi Rih hit by massive enemy drone attack for second time tonight
stories.summary: The Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih was hit by a second massive enemy drone attack overnight, with explosions reported throughout the city.

stories.title: ‘It was bonkers’: Samba the runaway capybara inspires a wild rodent hunt
stories.summary: A nine-month-old capybara named Samba escaped from Marwell Zoo near Winchester, Hampshire, shortly after being transferred from Jimmy's Farm in Suffolk. Specialist dog units and thermal drones have so far failed to locate her, prompting members of the UK public to join the search.

stories.title: Asean countries warned against exploiting US-China tensions for short-term gain
stories.summary: Chinese political scientist Zheng Yongnian, speaking at the Boao Forum for Asia, cautioned Southeast Asian nations against exploiting US-China tensions for short-term gains, warning the strategy could backfire, particularly in the context of South China Sea sovereignty disputes.

stories.title: Rapper Shah sworn in as Nepali prime minister
stories.summary: Balendra Shah, a 35-year-old rapper-turned-politician, was sworn in as Nepal's prime minister after his Rastriya Swatantra Party won the first election since anti-corruption protests toppled the previous government. He named key cabinet posts including appointing a former youth activist as interior minister.

stories.title: By popular demand: Modi standup special and Red Hot Chili Peppers docu
stories.summary: The Times of Israel's entertainment segment highlights viewer-suggested content, including a standup comedy special featuring Indian Prime Minister Modi and a Red Hot Chili Peppers documentary.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis claim missile attack on Israel, say attacks will continue
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed responsibility for a ballistic missile attack targeting what they described as sensitive Israeli military sites in southern Israel. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree warned that operations would continue until their objectives were met. The group said it was their first such strike since the broader Middle East conflict began.

stories.title: Hong Kong defends 3-hour limit for Wang Fuk Court residents to collect belongings
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities defended a three-hour time limit for residents of the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court to retrieve belongings. Deputy Chief Secretary Warner Cheuk said up to four people per household could register, but only one person would be allowed into severely damaged flats due to safety concerns. Discretion would be exercised for those requesting a second entry.

stories.title: Israel has uprooted 370,000 children in Lebanon: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that more than 370,000 children have been displaced in Lebanon within three weeks due to intensified Israeli air strikes and mass evacuation orders. Israel has launched heavy bombardment and a ground assault on Lebanon alongside its operations in Gaza. Hezbollah reported clashes with Israeli forces at villages in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Attempt made to smuggle 39 archaeological artifacts (8th–20th centuries) out of Ukraine by mail
stories.summary: Kyiv customs officials intercepted 39 authentic archaeological artifacts dating from the 8th to the 20th centuries in international mail shipments. The items were being smuggled out of Ukraine to destinations in the United States, France, and Italy.

stories.title: Attacks on Iran’s N-plants, steelworks belie ‘messaging’
stories.summary: The IAEA expressed concern after US-Israeli air strikes hit a uranium processing facility in Arak and a heavy water reactor in Khondab, Iran. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi vowed retaliation, while the IRGC threatened to target industrial sites in the region. The UN formed a task force to keep shipping moving through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran wants to ‘make a deal’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Iran is seeking to negotiate a deal, while praising the strength of the American military. No further details on potential negotiations were provided.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim responsibility for a missile attack on Israel
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for a missile attack targeting Israel, marking an escalation in the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: 🔴 Live: Yemen's Houthis claim first attack on Israel since start of Mideast war
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces claimed their first attack on Israel since the start of the broader Middle East war involving U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran.

stories.title: Provinces look to avoid fuel subsidy burden
stories.summary: Pakistani provinces including Punjab and Sindh are pushing to pass rising global oil prices to consumers rather than absorbing fuel subsidy costs. A national leadership dialogue was planned for late March to develop a unified strategy, with proposals including targeted subsidies and contingency rationing measures.

stories.title: Israel says missile from Yemen intercepted outside its borders
stories.summary: Israel said it detected and intercepted a missile launched from Yemen outside its borders, describing it as the first such attack linked to the ongoing conflict. The incident signals a potential widening of hostilities as Israel conducts operations against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon and faces tensions with Iran.

stories.title: Amid Iran war, Trump says he’d love his legacy to be made as ‘great peacemaker’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed his desire to be remembered as a "great peacemaker" amid the ongoing war with Iran. He referenced his role in halting the India-Pakistan conflict, called the Strait of Hormuz the "Strait of Trump," and dismissed NATO as a "paper tiger."

stories.title: Trump says ‘we don’t have to be there for NATO’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the United States does not have to participate in NATO. His comments raised questions about his willingness to honor NATO's Article 5 mutual defense commitment.

stories.title: Trump says ‘we don’t have to be there for NATO’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the United States does not need to remain committed to NATO, raising questions about his willingness to honor the alliance's mutual-defense obligation under Article 5.

stories.title: First Houthi launch toward Israel since war began triggers alerts across the Negev
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces launched their first projectile toward Israel since the broader war began, triggering alerts across the Negev region. There were no immediate reports of casualties or direct impacts.

stories.title: Iran-linked hackers breach FBI director Kash Patel's personal email, publish photos and documents
stories.summary: An Iranian-linked hacking group called Handala Hack Team claimed to have breached FBI Director Kash Patel's personal Gmail account, publishing photos and documents. Experts say Iranian hackers aim to embarrass US officials as the West Asia war continues.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran gamble falters as war drags on amid concerns of long-term chaos
stories.summary: One month after the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran, the conflict has not followed President Trump's projected four-to-six-week timeline. Despite assassinations of key Iranian political and military leaders, the regime has not collapsed. Continued airstrikes have degraded but not eliminated Iran's ballistic missile and drone capabilities.

stories.title: Kuwait oil price rises above $118 amid Hormuz tensions
stories.summary: The price of Kuwaiti oil rose by $8.10 to reach $118.93 per barrel, according to state news agency KUNA. The increase was driven by disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway handling roughly one-fifth of global energy exports, amid the US-Israeli conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: UK ‘weeks away’ from medicine shortages if Iran war continues, experts say
stories.summary: British experts warn the UK could face medicine shortages within weeks if the Iran war continues, affecting supplies from painkillers to cancer treatments. The conflict has disrupted supply chains for critical raw materials including oil, gas, crop fertilizer, and helium, with health essentials expected to be impacted next. Drug prices could also rise.

stories.title: US-based Iranian’s cloth works at Art Central reflect complex fabric of her identity
stories.summary: Iranian-American artist Elnaz Javani is displaying a series of six coats at the Art Central festival in Hong Kong. Born in Iran in 1985 and now based in the United States, Javani said the works explore themes of memory, identity, and conflict, offering a meditative space for viewers amid the ongoing Middle East war.

stories.title: Nepal's ex-PM arrested over fatal protest crackdown
stories.summary: Nepal's former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli was arrested in connection with a deadly crackdown on protests. More than 70 people were killed during an uprising the previous year that led to the ousting of his government.

stories.title: CCD: Russia shifting blame for environmental destruction in occupied territories onto Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia's Center for Countering Disinformation reports that Russian propaganda is attempting to shift responsibility for environmental destruction in occupied Ukrainian territories onto Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump says 'Cuba is next' in speech touting US military successes
stories.summary: During a speech at an investment forum in Miami, US President Donald Trump declared 'Cuba is next' while touting what he described as US military successes in Venezuela and Iran.

stories.title: US Secretary of State says war could conclude in ‘weeks, not months’
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that Washington aims to conclude the war in a matter of weeks rather than months, signaling a push for a swift resolution to the conflict.

stories.title: ‘Strait of Trump’: US President says Iran must open key waterway
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump called on Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz and suggested renaming the strategic waterway the 'Strait of Trump.' Trump has renamed several Washington buildings after himself during his second term.

stories.title: Iran threatens to seize assets of soccer star Sardar Azmoun over photo with UAE leaders
stories.summary: Iranian authorities threatened to seize the assets of soccer star Sardar Azmoun after he was photographed with UAE leaders. The move follows warnings from Iran's judicial chief that property of celebrities perceived as critical of the government could be confiscated.

stories.title: Detroit school settles lawsuit over student’s anti-Israel Pledge of Allegiance protest
stories.summary: A Detroit-area school settled a lawsuit brought by a student of Palestinian descent who said a teacher humiliated her for refusing to stand during the Pledge of Allegiance in objection to US support for Israel's war in Gaza. The settlement includes a $10,000 payment and staff training.

stories.title: Enemy strikes maternity hospital and residential area in Odesa, child among wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a maternity hospital and residential areas in Odesa, causing fires in the private sector. At least ten people were injured, including a child.

stories.title: Israelis rushed to shelters 18 times overnight, local media says
stories.summary: Sirens sounded across northern Israel, including in Haifa, its bay area, and Acre, with Israeli media reporting residents were sent to shelters 18 times overnight. Three drones that entered Israeli airspace from Lebanon were intercepted, while the military searched for a fourth.

stories.title: Milwaukee rabbi and son ordered to pay $1,000 to muralist who reportedly praised Hamas in court
stories.summary: Rabbi Peter Mehler and his son Zechariah were ordered to pay $1,000 in Milwaukee for destroying a pro-Palestinian mural. Zechariah acknowledged the act was illegal, while noting a strong city response against antisemitism; the muralist reportedly praised Hamas during court proceedings.

stories.title: Russian and Iranian foreign ministers discuss possibility of conflict settlement
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi discussed the possibility of a diplomatic settlement to the Iran conflict during a Friday conversation, according to Russia's foreign ministry.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis warn US and Israel against using Red Sea in attacks
stories.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree declared that Yemeni forces are ready for direct military intervention if the United States and Israel expand their alliance against Iran and its allies. He also warned against the use of the Red Sea for hostile operations.

stories.title: Araghchi warns Israel will pay 'heavy price' for attacks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that Israel would pay a "heavy price" for strikes on Iranian infrastructure, according to state media outlet IRNA. The statement follows a series of Israeli strikes targeting sites in Iran as part of the escalating conflict.

stories.title: Gaza peace doubts deepen as attention shifts to Iran
stories.summary: Growing uncertainty surrounds prospects for a peace agreement in Gaza as international attention has shifted toward the broader Iran conflict. Observers note that diplomatic momentum on Gaza has stalled amid the escalating regional war.

stories.title: 'Our home is gone': BBC speaks to displaced families in Lebanon
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Hugo Bachega reported from Beirut on displaced families, noting that more than one million people have been displaced across Lebanon due to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: New Jersey man arrested for allegedly plotting to firebomb pro-Palestinian activist’s home
stories.summary: A New Jersey man was arrested for allegedly plotting to firebomb the home of Nerdeen Kiswani, a prominent pro-Palestinian activist. The arrest followed a weeks-long investigation by authorities into the planned attack.

stories.title: From rural girl to tycoon: China woman, 55, marries lover, 25, with US$7.3 million dowry
stories.summary: Yu Wenhong, a 55-year-old medical aesthetics tycoon from Dalian, Liaoning province, China, married her 25-year-old husband with a reported dowry of 50 million yuan (US$7.3 million). Yu rose from modest beginnings, starting as an eyebrow tattooing technician at 18 and eventually building her own beauty business empire.

stories.title: Thailand reaches deal with Iran to allow Hormuz oil transit, PM says
stories.summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced an agreement with Iran to allow Thai oil vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to safeguard Thailand's energy supplies. The deal follows an incident in which a Thai-flagged cargo ship was struck by unknown projectiles in the strait.

stories.title: IDF arrests 80 wanted individuals, seizes weapons during West Bank operations
stories.summary: The IDF conducted operations across the West Bank, arresting 80 wanted individuals and seizing firearms and drones. The operations addressed rising violence in the region, including incidents related to settler attacks.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis say 'fingers on the trigger' as US-Israeli war on Iran widens
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement declared on March 27 that it stands ready to intervene militarily if additional countries join the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran or if the Red Sea is used to launch attacks on the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: Military analyst: Russians to focus main attacks on Pokrovsk and Zaporizhzhia sectors
stories.summary: A military analyst reports that Russian forces have intensified attacks along the entire front line to stretch Ukrainian defenses. The main offensive efforts are expected to focus on the Pokrovsk and Zaporizhzhia sectors.

stories.title: One of the most inaccessible art collections in the world awaits liberation in Tehran
stories.summary: The Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art, founded before the 1979 Islamic Revolution, houses an art collection valued at approximately $3 billion. Works from its vault occasionally re-emerge, but the collection's current condition remains unknown amid Iran's ongoing situation.

stories.title: 12 US troops wounded, 2 seriously, in Iranian attack on Saudi base — report
stories.summary: Twelve US troops were wounded, two seriously, in an Iranian attack on a Saudi Arabian base involving ballistic missiles and drones. Several aerial refueling planes were reportedly damaged. Approximately 300 American soldiers have been injured since the start of the war, with most casualties described as minor.

stories.title: Pakistan says holding 'detailed discussions' with leaders in Iran and Gulf
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said Islamabad has held detailed discussions with leaders in Iran and Gulf countries to de-escalate Middle East tensions. In a televised address, Sharif said Pakistan is pursuing diplomatic mediation while also taking measures to shield its economy from rising global oil prices.

stories.title: First MSF medical aid shipment reaches Iran via Turkey, local media reports
stories.summary: Iran's Press TV reported that the first shipment of medical aid from Doctors Without Borders (MSF) arrived in Iran via Turkey and was handed over to the Iranian Red Crescent Society. The shipment included essential pharmaceutical supplies amid disrupted humanitarian supply chains caused by the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Trump plan proposes to disarm Hamas in eight months, destroy tunnels
stories.summary: A disarmament plan presented by US President Donald Trump's "Board of Peace" would require Hamas to surrender weapons in stages over eight months and allow destruction of its Gaza tunnel network. The plan envisions a US-backed committee of Palestinian technocrats taking security control before Israeli forces withdraw.

stories.title: Pakistani ports emerge as safe trade hub
stories.summary: Global shipping lines are diverting container vessels to Karachi ports as risks increase in the Strait of Hormuz due to the Middle East conflict. Pakistan's government has reduced port charges, expedited cargo clearance, and established sub-committees to recommend structural reforms in maritime and logistics sectors.

stories.title: Gulf countries warn of rising threat from Iran-backed militias and proxies
stories.summary: Six Gulf states—Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan—issued a joint statement condemning Iranian attacks on their soil and warning of a rising threat from Iran-backed militias and proxy groups. They expressed concern that Tehran could activate sleeper cells across the Middle East amid its war with the U.S. and Israel.

stories.title: Israel’s unending attacks in Lebanon push country’s population to the brink
stories.summary: Israeli military operations in Lebanon have continued for four weeks, coinciding with a broader US-Israeli campaign against Iran. Many Lebanese civilians are suffering under the sustained bombardment and aggression.

stories.title: FBI confirms Director Kash Patel's email hack claimed by Iran-linked group
stories.summary: The FBI confirmed that Director Kash Patel's personal email account was hacked by an Iran-linked group calling itself the Handala Hack Team. The bureau said the accessed data was historical and contained no government information.

stories.title: Uproar in Bahrain after detainee dies in police custody
stories.summary: A 32-year-old detainee in Bahrain died in police custody after being arrested for opposing the war on Iran. Human rights groups say the man was killed while detained, prompting widespread outrage in the country.

stories.title: Violence in Syria's Druze heartland may be war crimes: UN
stories.summary: UN investigators warned that war crimes and crimes against humanity may have been committed during deadly violence in Syria's Suweida province, a Druze-majority area. The findings highlight ongoing instability and targeted violence in the region.

stories.title: Bank of America settles Epstein case for $72.5 million
stories.summary: Bank of America agreed to pay $72.5 million to settle a lawsuit alleging the bank ignored red flags tied to convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein's operations. The bank denied wrongdoing but chose to settle the case.

stories.title: As Vietnam leads on AI rules, Southeast Asia risks ‘economic own goal’
stories.summary: Vietnam became the first Southeast Asian nation to enact a comprehensive artificial intelligence regulatory law on March 1. Analysts warn that while such data-control measures may offer domestic benefits, the broader regional push risks undermining innovation and deterring foreign investment.

stories.title: Missile debris injures five Indian nationals in Abu Dhabi, officials say
stories.summary: Five Indian nationals were injured in Abu Dhabi by falling debris from intercepted ballistic missiles, with injuries ranging from minor to moderate. Authorities also worked to extinguish two fires caused by missile debris in the Khalifa Economic Zones.

stories.title: Ukraine plans to increase rapeseed oil exports
stories.summary: Ukraine projects rapeseed oil exports of 576,000 tons in the 2025/2026 marketing year, a 2.7-fold increase compared to the previous season.

stories.title: Morocco draw under new coach as Algeria, Egypt win big
stories.summary: Morocco drew in Mohamed Ouahbi's first match as head coach, while Algeria and Egypt both secured dominant victories in World Cup warm-up fixtures.

stories.title: UN warns of humanitarian crisis as Hormuz disruptions risk agriculture
stories.summary: The United Nations established a task force to ensure fertiliser shipments can transit the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing conflict-related disruptions. UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva warned that continued maritime trade interruptions could trigger a massive humanitarian crisis affecting global agricultural production.

stories.title: How the US-Israel war on Iran unfolded in its first four weeks
stories.summary: Al Jazeera published a review of the first four weeks of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, covering major military operations, political developments, and economic impacts during the opening month of the conflict.

stories.title: Trump says ‘Cuba is next’ target of US military
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly threatened Cuba with military action while speaking at a Saudi investment conference. The remarks raised concerns about a potential expansion of US military operations beyond the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Can ‘reliable friend’ China fill the gap as US pressures allies to snub South Africa?
stories.summary: China pledged continued support for South Africa after President Cyril Ramaphosa was disinvited from the G7 summit in France following US threats to boycott the event. The withdrawal of the invitation, originally issued by French President Macron, raised questions about whether Beijing could fill the diplomatic gap.

stories.title: US envoy predicts Iran talks as war enters second month
stories.summary: US envoy Steve Witkoff said talks with Iran could begin this week as the conflict enters its second month. The diplomatic push comes as US-Israeli strikes continue to target Iranian nuclear sites amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis threaten to join war: ‘Our fingers are on the trigger’
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels threatened to militarily intervene in the US-Israeli war on Iran if other countries join the fighting or if the Red Sea is used to attack Iran. The Iran-backed group warned their forces are ready to act.

stories.title: Israel plans 'security zone' in Lebanon as one million face permanent displacement
stories.summary: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs overnight and expanded evacuation orders across large parts of southern Lebanon up to the Zahrani River. Israeli ground forces are operating at multiple locations inside Lebanon, and approximately one million people face potential permanent displacement due to a planned Israeli security zone.

stories.title: EU and CPTPP agree to progress with ‘historic’ digital trade deal, Canada’s international trade minister says
stories.summary: The European Union and the parties to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) agreed in Yaoundé to move forward on a digital trade agreement. Canada's international trade minister described the prospective deal as historic.

stories.title: How mothers raise newborn babies during Israel’s offensive in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on Lebanon forced civilians, including pregnant women, to flee their homes. Hawraa Houmani, 29, was nine months pregnant when she was displaced from her village by the bombing campaign.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent coordinating strikes against AFU artillery in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: The Security Service of Ukraine's counterintelligence unit detained a Russian GRU agent in the Donetsk region. The agent was coordinating Russian airstrikes targeting Ukrainian artillery positions in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: ‘That’s a lie’: US’ Rubio attacks Zelensky, ready to divert Ukraine arms to Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly attacked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, calling his claims false. Zelensky had said in an interview that Washington was pressuring Ukraine to cede its Donbas region to Russia. Rubio also indicated willingness to redirect arms from Ukraine to the Iran campaign.

stories.title: Merz says he will fight for future of Franco-German fighter jet project
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated he is working to salvage the troubled Franco-German-Spanish Future Combat Air System (FCAS) fighter jet program. Merz emphasized the need for greater cooperation within Europe's defense industry.

stories.title: UAE says interception debris caused fires in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi authorities responded to two fires caused by debris from the interception of ballistic missiles in the Khalifa Economic Zones area. Iran's IRGC separately claimed a kamikaze drone struck a hotel in Dubai targeting what it described as US elements in the region.

stories.title: 'If Lebanon won't disarm Hezbollah, the IDF will': Effie Defrin warns against Hezbollah’s rearmamen
stories.summary: Israeli official Effie Defrin warned that the IDF will disarm Hezbollah if the Lebanese government does not act. He stated that Israel will not allow Hezbollah to rearm and will continue operations to protect civilians along the northern border.

stories.title: IAF intercepts over 90% of drones launched by Iran, Hezbollah during Operation Roaring Lion
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force reported intercepting over 90% of drones launched by Iran and Hezbollah during Operation Roaring Lion. The IDF uses multiple interception systems, though the Iron Beam laser has not yet significantly reduced drone intrusions.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli advance toward Litani River
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it attacked Israeli forces that had crossed into Lebanese territory and were advancing toward the Litani River. The operations included rocket, artillery, and drone strikes near the town of Taybeh and targeted two Israeli Merkava tanks near al-Qantara in the Marjayoun district.

stories.title: Cyclone Narelle downgraded to tropical low but severe weather warnings remain for storm-ravaged WA
stories.summary: Cyclone Narelle was downgraded to a tropical low on Saturday after making landfall in Western Australia on Friday. Severe weather warnings remain in effect, with flash flooding threatening the wheatbelt region and Perth as the system moves south-east from Geraldton.

stories.title: Thousands of 'No Kings' protests planned across US in opposition to Iran war
stories.summary: The 'No Kings' protest movement organized more than 3,000 gatherings across the United States for Saturday, with opposition to the Iran war among key grievances. Major demonstrations were expected in Washington, Minneapolis, Chicago, and San Francisco.

stories.title: US’ Rubio urges world to stop Iran imposing tolls in key Hormuz strait
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on the international community to prevent Iran from imposing tolls on shipping through the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Displaced mothers in Lebanon welcome babies' new lives with hope and fear
stories.summary: Hawraa Houmani, a 29-year-old woman nearly nine months pregnant, fled Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon near Nabatieh to a school shelter in Beirut. Displaced mothers in Lebanon are giving birth in difficult conditions, cut off from their regular medical care.

stories.title: More than 400 Hezbollah fighters killed in new war with Israel so far, sources say
stories.summary: More than 400 Hezbollah fighters have been killed since the Lebanese armed group launched a new war with Israel on March 2, according to two sources familiar with Hezbollah's internal count in Beirut.

stories.title: Video shows US missile likely used in deadly strike on Iranian town, experts say
stories.summary: Weapons experts identified a U.S.-made Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) in video footage of a deadly strike on the southern Iranian town of Lamerd. Analysts say the finding points to American munitions being used in the attack.

stories.title: Nepal’s ex-PM K.P. Sharma Oli arrested over alleged role in crackdown on protesters
stories.summary: Former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli and ex-Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak were arrested in Kathmandu over their alleged involvement in a deadly crackdown on protesters in September 2025. The arrests came one day after newly elected Prime Minister Balendra Shah and his cabinet were sworn in.

stories.title: US can only confirm about a third of Iran’s missile arsenal destroyed, sources say
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence indicates that only about one-third of Iran's missile arsenal has been confirmed destroyed nearly one month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign. The status of another third remains uncertain, though bombings may have damaged or buried those missiles in underground facilities. Similar assessments apply to Iran's drone capabilities.

stories.title: UN chief launches task force to aid passage of fertiliser through Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: The United Nations Secretary-General established a task force to facilitate the passage of fertilizer shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative warns that war-related disruptions could worsen global food shortages and humanitarian crises.

stories.title: German Chancellor Merz says he has doubts over Iran war aims
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed doubt that the United States and Israel have a clear strategy for ending the war in Iran. However, Merz said Germany would in principle be prepared to help stabilize the region after hostilities conclude.

stories.title: Northern residents concerned IDF won’t be allowed to ‘finish the job’ against Hezbollah
stories.summary: Evacuated residents of northern Israel expressed concern that the IDF may not be permitted to complete its military campaign against Hezbollah. Residents who remained during the conflict reported struggling to maintain their businesses amid ongoing sirens and limited shelter access.

stories.title: Russia lags in naval drone development and large-scale deployment, says Pletenchuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian spokesperson Pletenchuk stated that Russia lags behind in the development and large-scale deployment of unmanned naval drone systems, despite having available resources and ongoing development efforts.

stories.title: Rubio says war on Iran to last ‘weeks not months’, no US ground troops needed
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated after a G7 meeting in France that the war against Iran is expected to last weeks, not months. Rubio said Washington could achieve its objectives without ground troops but acknowledged deploying some forces to the region to preserve flexibility for President Trump.

stories.title: Intense bombing in Tehran, Isfahan
stories.summary: US-Israeli airstrikes struck Tehran and Isfahan in early morning raids, sending black smoke rising over both Iranian cities. The strikes are part of the ongoing military campaign targeting sites across Iran.

stories.title: US special envoy Witkoff predicts Iran talks as war enters second month
stories.summary: US special envoy Steve Witkoff predicted Iran would hold talks with Washington as the US-Israeli war entered its second month. The conflict began on February 28 with air strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and has since expanded to target Iranian nuclear facilities.

stories.title: Trump pushes Saudi Arabia to join Abraham Accords
stories.summary: President Donald Trump urged Saudi Arabia to join the Abraham Accords at an investment forum in Miami. He said the Middle East is being transformed by the war involving Iran and called the region's future bright.

stories.title: Canada eyes Mercosur pact by autumn
stories.summary: Canada's international trade minister announced on Friday in Yaounde that he aims to finalize a free-trade agreement with the South American Mercosur bloc by autumn. The deal would strengthen trade ties between Canada and Mercosur member states.

stories.title: Iranian media report strike on Tehran university amid attacks
stories.summary: Iran's semi-official Mehr News Agency reported that a US-Israeli airstrike targeted a university in Tehran. The capital has been hit by repeated air strikes in recent weeks as part of the ongoing military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Belgian ex-diplomat appeals order to stand trial in Congo's Lumumba murder
stories.summary: A former senior Belgian diplomat has appealed a court decision ordering him to stand trial over the 1961 assassination of Patrice Lumumba, the Democratic Republic of Congo's first prime minister. The appeal was confirmed by the ex-diplomat's lawyer in Brussels on Friday.

stories.title: How China’s EV makers think they can outrun disastrous price wars
stories.summary: Chinese EV manufacturers are shifting from price competition to a technology-driven contest. BYD unveiled a battery capable of charging from 10 to 70 percent in five minutes, to be deployed in models priced as low as 155,000 yuan, while announcing plans to build 20,000 charging stations.

stories.title: KP Sharma Oli: Nepal’s former prime minister arrested over alleged role in deadly protest crackdown
stories.summary: Nepalese police arrested former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli at his residence near Kathmandu on Saturday over his alleged role in the deadly crackdown on anti-corruption protests in September that killed at least 77 people. Former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak, accused of ordering forces to fire on protesters, was also arrested.

stories.title: US operations in Iran ‘on or ahead of schedule’, says Rubio
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said military operations in Iran are on or ahead of schedule. Washington has deployed two contingents of thousands of Marines to the region to support the campaign.

stories.title: Rubio says US can achieve Iran objectives without ground troops
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the United States can achieve its objectives regarding Iran without deploying ground troops. Rubio indicated he expects U.S. operations in Iran to conclude within a matter of weeks.

stories.title: These pro-Palestine PACs are trying to beat AIPAC at its own game
stories.summary: Several pro-Palestine political action committees are working to elect pro-Palestinian candidates in US elections, seeking to counter AIPAC's influence. The groups are capitalizing on shifting American public sentiment toward Israel, though their electoral results remain mixed so far.

stories.title: From jammed broadcasts to a blocked website: BBC Russian's 80 years of defiance
stories.summary: BBC Russian is marking 80 years of broadcasting, having spent decades fending off signal jammers during the Soviet era. Its website is currently blocked in Russia, but millions of readers continue to access it through other means.

stories.title: Lubinets explains why he continues humanitarian dialogue with Moskalkova
stories.summary: Ukraine's Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets explained that his continued humanitarian dialogue with Russian counterpart Tatyana Moskalkova enables the delivery of letters and parcels to prisoners of war held by both sides.

stories.title: IRGC threatens 'beyond eye for eye' retaliatory strikes on US-Israeli sites in region
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened retaliatory strikes on industrial facilities linked to the US and Israel across the region. The IRGC warned that Tehran's response to attacks on its nuclear and infrastructure sites would exceed proportional retaliation and urged workers at targeted sites to evacuate.

stories.title: Death of South Korean ‘torture expert’ reopens authoritarian era wounds
stories.summary: Lee Geun-an, a former South Korean police officer notorious for torturing political prisoners during the country's authoritarian era, died at age 88 from multiple organ failure. His death revived painful memories as he had never expressed remorse, calling himself a "patriot" and his interrogation methods "art."

stories.title: How to win friends and influence people in ancient China
stories.summary: The article discusses the ancient Chinese text Guiguzi, a work on persuasion and political strategy, drawing parallels to Dale Carnegie's self-help classic on interpersonal influence.

stories.title: Trump demands Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz, slams NATO and warns: “Cuba is next”
stories.summary: President Trump declared at the FII Priority forum in Miami that the Iran military operation is two weeks ahead of schedule and demanded Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He also sharply criticized European NATO allies for not joining the campaign and warned that Cuba could be a future target.

stories.title: Iranian missile, drones strike US airbase Prince Sultan in Saudi Arabia, aircraft damaged - report
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Iranian missiles and drones struck Prince Sultan Air Base, a US facility in Saudi Arabia, damaging aircraft. The attack was confirmed through open-source imagery and data circulating online.

stories.title: Trade deal with India not far-off, but there are still gaps: U.S. official
stories.summary: A US official indicated that a trade deal between the United States and India is close but gaps remain, particularly around pulses. India seeks to protect its domestic market for the agricultural commodity, while the US is pushing for greater access.

stories.title: Trump suggests renaming Hormuz - 'Strait of Trump' during speech confirming negotiations with Iran
stories.summary: During a speech at the FII Priority Summit in Miami, US President Donald Trump suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Strait of Trump' and confirmed that negotiations with Iran are underway, urging Tehran to open the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Beirut again amid Hezbollah clashes
stories.summary: Fresh Israeli airstrikes hit southern Beirut while Hezbollah claimed ground clashes with Israeli forces. Lebanon faces mounting civilian casualties and displacement from the sustained military operations.

stories.title: US to deploy another aircraft carrier near Iran, reports say
stories.summary: The United States is expected to deploy the aircraft carrier USS George H.W. Bush to the Middle East near the ongoing conflict with Iran, according to CBS News and CNN. It is unclear whether the carrier will join or replace two American carriers already operating in the region.

stories.title: 'The gravest crime against humanity': What does the UN vote on slavery mean?
