stories.summary: Ukraine is developing the STRILA-2, an upgraded missile featuring a solid-fuel rocket booster and AI guidance, based on German Jäger technology. Germany previously funded 15,000 units of the original STRILA system and is now investing in the new variant.

stories.title: Whale stranded off Germany swims to freedom after days of efforts to save it
stories.summary: A humpback whale stranded on Germany's Baltic Sea coast since earlier in the week freed itself and swam into deeper waters on Friday. Rescuers had used boats and excavators to guide the 10-metre-long animal, and a flotilla of vessels continued following it at a distance to help direct it toward the North Sea and the Atlantic Ocean.

stories.title: Invaders shell Kostiantynivka with artillery, wounding two civilians
stories.summary: Russian artillery struck the city of Kostiantynivka in Ukraine's Donetsk region, wounding two civilians. No fatalities were reported in the shelling.

stories.title: UN Rights Council set to appoint expert who called Hamas a ‘resistance movement’
stories.summary: The UN Human Rights Council is expected to appoint Palestinian academic Zeina Jallad as a special rapporteur, despite a vetting group's recommendation against her. Jallad has previously referred to Hamas as a resistance movement.

stories.title: China blasts ‘false’ news after report says chipmaker supplying Iran
stories.summary:
China’s foreign ministry accused the media of publishing “false information” on Friday following a report that said the country’s top semiconductor firm has sent chipmaking tools to Iran.
The report,

stories.title: In call with PM, Kuwait crown prince endorses Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between US and Iran
stories.summary: In a phone call with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday, Kuwait’s Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Al Khaled Al Hamad Al Sabah “fully endorsed” Pakistan’s efforts for mediation between Iran and the US,

stories.title: Spanish woman dies by euthanasia in case that drew national spotlight
stories.summary: Noelia Castillo, a 25-year-old Spanish woman, underwent legal euthanasia on Thursday after a nearly two-year legal battle and years of psychiatric illness. Spain legalized euthanasia and medically assisted suicide in 2021 for patients meeting certain conditions. Castillo's case had drawn significant national attention.

stories.title: Kremlin Denies Putin Solicited War Contributions From Russian Billionaires
stories.summary: The Kremlin denied that President Vladimir Putin personally solicited financial contributions for the war effort from Russian billionaires. Officials said an unidentified businessman proposed the idea during a private meeting, but Putin did not make any such request.

stories.title: Russia aiding Iran with targeting data to distract from 'crimes' in Ukraine, German FM says
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul accused Russia of providing Iran with targeting data to divert international attention from Russian actions in Ukraine. Wadephul said Russia is cynically exploiting the Middle East escalation to distract from its war crimes.

stories.title: Ukrainians opened record number of businesses in this European country. Nearest competitor managed 2,000
stories.summary: Ukrainians opened a record number of businesses in an unspecified European country, surpassing the nearest competitor by more than 2,000 registrations. The enterprises span gastronomy, logistics, and IT sectors, mirroring a similar record set in 2024.

stories.title: Ukraine, Saudi Arabia agreed to key defence cooperation: Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in a social media post on Friday (March 27), said the document "lays the foundation for future contracts, technological cooperation, and investment", providing

stories.title: Trump administration sidelines, threatens Europe in Iran war: EU flounders in new world order
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned European countries that failure to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz could have severe consequences for NATO's future. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the U.S. will make its own security decisions regardless of European opinion. The EU's response has been hampered by its inability to present a unified position on the crisis.

stories.title: Death toll in Lebanon from Israeli attacks rises to at least 1,142
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli attacks on the country since March 2 have killed at least 1,142 people and injured 3,315 others.

stories.title: Will the Pentagon have to cut exercises to pay for the Iran war?
stories.summary: Pentagon comptroller office leader Jules Hurst addressed concerns about whether the Department of Defense may need to cut military exercises to fund ongoing operations in Iran. Discussions also covered rising fuel costs and the timeline for a potential supplemental funding request from Congress.

stories.title: U.S. Secretary of State Rubio tries to sell Iran war to sceptical G7 partners after Trump insults allies
stories.summary: Donald Trump complained bitterly about NATO countries not stepping up to help the U.S. and Israel in the Iran war

stories.title: Drones and mines: Why taking Iran’s Kharg Island would pose risks for US troops
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has been weighing whether to use ground forces to seize Iran’s strategic oil hub of Kharg Island, an operation analysts say could be achieved quickly, but leave US troops in

stories.title: Is Europe heading to an energy crisis?
stories.summary: Europe is preparing for potential energy supply shortages and price spikes as the ongoing conflict involving Iran continues to disrupt global energy markets.

stories.title: UN says 1,700 killed during violence in Syria's Suweida
stories.summary: The UN Commission reported that approximately 1,700 people have been killed during violence in Syria's Suweida region. The commission found that violations were committed by all major parties to the conflict, with many potentially constituting war crimes.

stories.title: Jools Holland: The pianist who played with The Beatles and made presidents dance
stories.summary: British musician Jools Holland has spent over five decades in the music industry, known as bandleader of his Rhythm & Blues Orchestra, co-founder of rock group Squeeze, and host of the long-running BBC show "Later... with Jools Holland." He recently achieved a number one album at age 66 with Rod Stewart.

stories.title: Curfews, EVs and ethanol: How African countries are trying to save fuel
stories.summary: Egypt has ordered shops, restaurants, and shopping malls to close from 9:00 PM in an effort to curb energy bills that have more than doubled due to the Iran war. Other African countries are also exploring fuel-saving measures including EVs and ethanol.

stories.title: Ukraine’s interceptor drones set record. Last year, this number would have meant catastrophe
stories.summary: During a large-scale Russian drone attack on 24 March involving 999 drones, Ukrainian forces intercepted more than 94% of incoming threats, setting a new record for interceptor drone operations.

stories.title: Meet the children left without parents under El Salvador’s emergency decree
stories.summary: Four years after El Salvador enacted its state of emergency, families are highlighting the impact of mass arrests on children who have been left without parents.

stories.title: IDF to extend Lebanon rocket warning time as Hezbollah pushed from border zone
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced extended rocket warning times for border towns in northern Israel as Hezbollah forces have been pushed further from the Lebanese border zone. Troops also discovered weapons in a south Lebanon school and tunnels beneath a church.

stories.title: IDF chief warns of potential collapse due to manpower shortage: report
stories.summary: Gen. Zamir’s comments came at a time when Israel is fighting wars on different fronts

stories.title: Paratroopers capture six Russian troops in Sloviansk area
stories.summary: Paratroopers from Ukraine's 81st Separate Slobozhanskyi Airborne Brigade, part of the 7th Airborne Corps, captured six Russian servicemen in the Sloviansk area of Donetsk region.

stories.title: 78% of Jewish Israelis support continuing Iran war — poll
stories.summary: A poll found that 78 percent of Jewish Israelis support continuing the war on Iran. Most Jewish respondents viewed the decision to launch the war as security-driven, while most Arab Israeli respondents saw it as politically motivated. Majorities in both groups said planners underestimated Iran.

stories.title: US rebuilding WWII Pacific airfields amid China threat
stories.summary: U.S. military engineers are refurbishing World War II–era airstrips on the Pacific islands of Tinian and Peleliu. The effort is part of a strategic response to growing rivalry with China in the Indo-Pacific region.

stories.title: Millions expected for third 'No Kings' protest in US on Saturday
stories.summary: Organizers expect millions to attend a third 'No Kings' protest across the United States on Saturday. The main event is planned in Minnesota, featuring speeches by Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont and musician Bruce Springsteen.

stories.title: US 'only certain of having destroyed a third' of Iran's missiles
stories.summary: US officials reportedly acknowledge they can only confirm the destruction of about a third of Iran's missile and drone arsenal, contradicting President Trump's claims that Iran's stockpile has been largely eliminated.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Chernihiv region, spark fire and kill one
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on the Chernihiv region of northern Ukraine killed a 95-year-old man and sparked a fire. The attack was part of ongoing Russian aerial assaults on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Russian shadow war is escalating. NATO railways and sea cables are in the crosshairs.
stories.summary: NATO infrastructure, including railways and undersea cables, faces an escalating Russian shadow war involving deniable attacks. Military supply chain hubs have been identified as especially vulnerable targets.

stories.title: Soviet famine still haunts Moldova, 80 years on
stories.summary: Eighty years ago, a famine struck Moldova that killed more than 150,000 people, a tragedy largely attributed to Soviet authorities. The episode was long shrouded in silence but is gradually being documented through survivor accounts and historical research.

stories.title: Pakistan’s strike on Kabul clinic is a war on Afghan lives
stories.summary: Pakistan conducted an airstrike on a rehabilitation clinic in Kabul, Afghanistan. The attack has drawn criticism for targeting Afghan civilians under the justification of counterterrorism operations.

stories.title: Gabon's eco-rangers battle to help threatened baby sea turtles survive
stories.summary: Eco-rangers in Gabon are working to protect threatened baby sea turtles from predators such as crabs and birds. Nests also face dangers from coastal erosion and human-caused plastic pollution.

stories.title: Iran threatens to target Syrian hotels as part of war with US
stories.summary: Iran threatened to strike Syria's presidential palace and two luxury hotels in Damascus, alleging that US forces are operating from those locations as part of the broader US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia and Ukraine sign defence procurement memorandum
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and Ukraine signed a defence procurement memorandum in Jeddah, as Gulf states increasingly look to Kyiv for assistance in countering Iranian drone and missile threats.

stories.title: US uses hundreds of Tomahawk missiles on Iran, alarming some at Pentagon
stories.summary: The U.S. military has been consuming precision-guided Tomahawk cruise missiles at a rate that has alarmed some Pentagon officials during operations against Iran. The rapid expenditure has raised concerns about maintaining adequate stockpiles.

stories.title: Senate chairman approves surrender of over Rs200m to national exchequer to support govt’s austerity drive
stories.summary:
Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani on Friday approved the surrender of the Rs265 million to the national exchequer in efforts to support the government’s austerity drive.
On March 9, the government an

stories.title: Japan sprinkles fresh missiles across its islands to fend off would-be attackers
stories.summary: Japan is deploying homegrown standoff missiles across its islands as part of a defense capability buildup. The strategy also includes acquiring U.S.-made Tomahawk cruise missiles for launch from Aegis-equipped destroyers to deter potential attackers.

stories.title: Ex-Kursk Governor Testifies Against Predecessor in Border Defense Corruption Trial
stories.summary: Former Kursk region governor Alexei Smirnov testified against his predecessor Roman Starovoit in a border defense corruption trial in Russia. Smirnov entered a plea bargain with prosecutors, alleging Starovoit received millions of rubles through a kickback scheme.

stories.title: Lebanon faces ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ under Israeli assault: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations Refugee Agency warned that displaced Lebanese families are enduring a humanitarian catastrophe, living under constant Israeli bombardment. The UN described conditions in Lebanon as dire.

stories.title: US, Israeli war goals 'not realistic': Regime change in Iran 'can't be achieved' by airstrikes
stories.summary: Former Israeli Health Minister Nitzan Horowitz argued that U.S. and Israeli war goals of regime change and dismantling Iran's military capabilities are unrealistic and unachievable through airstrikes alone. He noted eroding public support due to prolonged insecurity, economic paralysis, and the absence of tangible results, while the Iranian regime's resilience challenges the war's foundational assumptions.

stories.title: Tanzania landslides kill 20 as heavy rains hit East Africa
stories.summary: At least 20 people were killed in landslides in southern Tanzania following days of intense rainfall. The disaster is part of a broader pattern of extreme weather battering parts of East Africa.

stories.title: Financial analysts move to counter Trump’s Middle East war uncertainty with ‘TACO’ index
stories.summary: Financial analysts have created the "TACO" index—standing for "Trump Always Chickens Out"—to model U.S. President Donald Trump's unpredictable policy decisions. The index aims to help mitigate financial shocks caused by uncertainty related to the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: European intelligence agencies believe Russia is supplying drones to Iran, says official
stories.summary: European intelligence agencies believe Russia is in the final stages of preparing to supply explosive-laden drones to Iran for use in its war against the U.S. and Israel, according to a senior European official. Russia has already been sharing intelligence with Tehran to help target U.S. forces. The drone delivery would mark the first evidence of Russian lethal support since the war began.

stories.title: Lawmakers concerned over lack of parking at Huanggang border checkpoint
stories.summary: Hong Kong lawmakers raised concerns about the absence of a car park at the upgraded Huanggang border crossing between Hong Kong and Shenzhen. Security Secretary Chris Tang confirmed the revamped checkpoint on the mainland side would not include public parking or coach bays.

stories.title: Nato to set up new corps in Turkey as Ankara eyes regional deterrence
stories.summary: NATO plans to establish a new multinational corps in Turkey as Ankara seeks to strengthen regional deterrence. While the plans predate recent tensions, Turkey is looking to deepen its defensive capabilities in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine, Saudi Arabia sign air defence deal: senior officials
stories.summary: Ukraine and Saudi Arabia have signed an air defence agreement during President Volodymyr Zelensky’s visit to the kingdom, which is facing Iranian drone attacks, two senior officials told AFP on Friday

stories.title: Israel tightens media restrictions on war coverage
stories.summary: Israel's military censor has tightened restrictions on press coverage of the war, citing national security concerns. Critics, including Israeli journalist Gideon Levy, argue the measures leave audiences with an incomplete picture and warn that self-censorship poses an additional risk to newsrooms.

stories.title: Belarusian leader gifts gun to North Korea's Kim Jong Un
stories.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko gifted a gun to North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during a meeting where the two signed a friendship treaty. Lukashenko is seeking to strengthen ties with Russian allies while also attempting to normalize relations with the United States.

stories.title: EU hopes Hungarian election will bring end to Orban's blockades
stories.summary: BRUSSELS/BUDAPEST, March 27 - Few EU leaders will miss Hungary's Prime Minister Viktor Orban if he loses an April 12 election after he blocked key policies, including vital aid to Ukraine, but they do

stories.title: What does it mean for China if Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin visit back to back?
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is expected to visit China shortly after U.S. President Donald Trump's planned trip to Beijing in mid-May. Chinese analysts say the back-to-back visits reflect Beijing's effort to manage relations with both Washington and Moscow amid global instability.

stories.title: Biker gangs and hired hands: how Iran is increasingly outsourcing its terror campaigns
stories.summary: Experts suspect Iranian involvement in the firebombing of four ambulances in Golders Green, London, as part of an expanding pattern of outsourced terror campaigns. The article details Iran's history of using proxy operatives, including biker gangs and hired individuals, for assassinations and attacks across Europe.

stories.title: IRGC announces Strait of Hormuz closure
stories.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to all maritime traffic. The IRGC warned that any vessels attempting to breach the blockade would face a harsh response.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits southern Beirut with no prior warning
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit Beirut's southern suburb of Tahouitet al-Ghadir on Friday afternoon without any prior warning from the Israeli military, according to Lebanese state media. Earlier strikes on the same district killed two people that day.

stories.title: Why is Russia asking its billionaires to fund a war its $190 billion defense budget should cover?
stories.summary: The Kremlin has asked Russian billionaires to help fund the war effort despite a $190 billion defense budget. Oligarch Suleiman Kerimov pledged $1.2 billion, which the Kremlin characterized as a spontaneous gesture.

stories.title: Russia’s war bill outgrew the budget—so the Kremlin passed a collection plate to its billionaires
stories.summary: The Kremlin turned to Russian billionaires to help cover war costs that have exceeded the national budget. Oligarch Suleiman Kerimov reportedly pledged $1.2 billion, which the Kremlin characterized as a spontaneous gesture.

stories.title: Mohsin Naqvi discusses counter-terrorism and security cooperation with Chinese envoy in Islamabad
stories.summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zedong at the Chinese Embassy in Islamabad on Friday, where the two discussed matters pertaining to counter-terrorism, security coopera

stories.title: Ukraine eyes Middle East deals on countering Iranian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine has been pursuing defense deals across the Middle East focused on countering Iranian drone technology. Discussions have been held with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Jordan, and Oman, with the most advanced talks involving the United Arab Emirates and Qatar.

stories.title: Russia denies intelligence role in Iran’s strikes
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov denied that Moscow is providing intelligence support to Iran, rejecting EU accusations that Russia is helping Tehran target U.S. forces in the Middle East.

stories.title: G7 allies press Rubio on US Iran plans, discuss Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: G7 allies pressed US Secretary of State Marco Rubio for clarity on American plans for Iran at a meeting in France, nearly one month into the Middle East war. Concerns also intensified over cooperation between Russia and Iran, while Rubio urged all G7 nations to push for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran-linked hackers claim breach of FBI director's personal email
stories.summary: Iran-linked hackers publicly claimed to have breached FBI Director Kash Patel's personal email account, publishing photographs and a purported resume. A U.S. Justice Department official confirmed the compromise to Reuters, while the FBI did not immediately comment.

stories.title: Nixon to Trump: Pakistan’s long record as backchannel between rival powers
stories.summary: Pakistan is reprising its historical role as a diplomatic backchannel between rival powers, facilitating communication as the United States and Iran move closer to wider confrontation. Islamabad has served in similar intermediary roles dating back to the Nixon era.

stories.title: Man who allegedly planted bomb at US air force base at large after fleeing to China
stories.summary: US citizen Alen Zheng allegedly planted a bomb at the visitors center of MacDill Air Force Base in Florida, headquarters of US Central Command overseeing the Iran war, where it went undiscovered for a week. Zheng fled to China and remains at large, while his sister Ann Mary Zheng was arrested in the US.

stories.title: Is Saudi Arabia's ambitious 'desert ski resort' dream over?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's planned Trojena ski resort project faces renewed uncertainty after two construction contracts were reportedly cancelled. The ambitious desert ski resort is part of Saudi Arabia's broader development and diversification agenda.

stories.title: Nuclear power in Africa: Big dreams, bigger hurdles
stories.summary: Several African nations are pursuing nuclear energy to expand electricity generation and reduce carbon emissions. However, complex financing requirements, lengthy construction timelines, and stringent safety standards mean only a few countries are likely to bring reactors online in the near term.

stories.title: ‘A Lot of War in Society’: Violent Student Attacks Rock Russian Schools
stories.summary: A rash of stabbings, shootings and other violent incidents involving students in Russian schools has spread across the country. What is going on?

stories.title: A Month of Operation Epstein Fury
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab/Al-Araby Al-Jadeed commenting on one month of operations dubbed "Operation Epstein Fury."

stories.title: Norway to add more than $11bn to defence budget over 10 years
stories.summary: Norway announced plans to increase its defense budget by more than $11 billion over the next ten years. The decision comes amid sustained pressure from the United States on NATO member states to raise their defense spending.

stories.title: China launches investigations into US trade practices. Why now?
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce launched two trade barrier investigations targeting U.S. practices, in response to American Section 301 probes alleging unfair Chinese trade practices. The investigations focus on U.S. measures Beijing says harm global industrial and supply chains, including those obstructing trade in green products.

stories.title: Egypt imposes business curfew to counter soaring fuel costs
stories.summary: Egypt imposed a business curfew requiring shops, restaurants, and malls to close at 9 p.m. on weekdays to curb soaring energy costs linked to the Iran war. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said the measure, effective Saturday, would last at least one month.

stories.title: Russia's Lavrov says US wants to take over Nord Stream gas pipelines
stories.summary: MOSCOW, March 27 - Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said the U.S. has been seeking control over the Nord Stream gas pipelines in the Baltic Sea, which were damaged by mysterious blast in Septemb

stories.title: ‘Trade deal with India not far-off, but there are still gaps’: U.S. official
stories.summary: One of the gaps in India-U.S. discussions, as per the U.S. official, is around pulses, with India seeking to safeguard the market for this agricultural commodity and the U.S. wanting greater access to

stories.title: ‘Raising 10 red flags’: Is Israel’s army exhausted?
stories.summary: Israel's chief of staff has warned that the Israeli military is approaching a state of collapse after years of sustained regional conflict. The assessment reportedly raised multiple serious concerns about the army's readiness and sustainability.

stories.title: Pakistan the peacemaker? Islamabad steps up as US-Iran mediator
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a key mediator between the United States and Iran as the war continues. Analysts note that conflict spillover risks are particularly acute for Pakistan, which is eager to avoid being drawn into the fighting.

stories.title: Thirteen arrested in joint Scotland and Spain gangland raids
stories.summary: Police Scotland and Spain's Guardia Civil arrested 13 people in simultaneous raids targeting organized crime. The coordinated operations were part of a two-year investigation into gangland activity spanning both countries.

stories.title: State Department clears $340M FMS request for hypersonic missile testing support for Japan
stories.summary: The US State Department approved a $340 million foreign military sales request to support Japan's hypersonic missile testing program. Japan has allocated $769 million in its defense budget for development and deployment of its Hyper Velocity Gliding Projectile for the fiscal year beginning April 1.

stories.title: IRGC issues evacuation warning for civilians close to US forces in Gulf States
stories.summary: The IRGC warns civilians to avoid US forces in the Gulf, as tensions rise with threats toward the UAE and Bahrain. Iran also launched drones and missiles at Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Ukraine signs defense pact with Saudi Arabia after its experts spent week finding holes in region’s air defenses
stories.summary: Ukraine signed a defense pact with Saudi Arabia after Ukrainian experts spent a week assessing gaps in the region's air defenses. Ukraine offers combat-tested counter-drone expertise developed over four years and more than 58,000 intercepted drone attacks.

stories.title: Russian and U.S. Lawmakers Meet to Discuss Ukraine War and Bilateral Relations
stories.summary: Members of the State Duma delegation said they also talked about restarting student exchange programs and direct flights.

stories.title: Two oil refining units damaged: General Staff clarifies results of strike on Kirishi Oil Refinery
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff provided updated details on the March 26 strike against the Kirishi Oil Refinery in Russia's Leningrad region. The strike damaged two oil refining units at the facility.

stories.title: Iran war reshapes diplomacy as old dealmakers are sidelined - who replaces them?
stories.summary: NATIONAL AFFAIRS: The month-long war now under way has done more than degrade Iran’s air defenses and cripple parts of its military-industrial complex - it has upended the diplomatic cast.

stories.title: Jewish extremist attacks in the West Bank threaten Israel’s legitimacy - opinion
stories.summary: West Bank violence by extremists threatens Israel’s international standing amid its high-stakes war with Iran.

stories.title: Turkey’s Contested Homefront
stories.summary: The article examines what lessons Turkish President Erdogan may draw about national solidarity from observing the Israel-Iran conflict. It explores implications for Turkey's domestic political dynamics.

stories.title: Pakistan says US-Iran backchannel talks continue despite Tehran rejecting 15-point plan
stories.summary: Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister Dar said Pakistan remains fully committed to promoting peace and is making all possible efforts to ensure stability in the region and beyond

stories.title: US and Israel 'burning through' Tomahawk and interceptor missiles in Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. and Israel have fired more than 850 Tomahawk cruise missiles in four weeks of operations against Iran, alarming Pentagon officials over rapidly depleting stockpiles. Annual production of Tomahawks is limited to a few hundred units, raising concerns about long-term supply.

stories.title: Judge blocks Pentagon's Anthropic ban, calling it illegal retaliation
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge blocked the Pentagon's ban on contracts with AI company Anthropic, ruling that the Trump administration's action was "arbitrary and capricious." The court found the ban constituted illegal retaliation against the company.

stories.title: Scathing UN report demands Syria investigate abuses during deadly clashes with Druze
stories.summary: A UN report demanded that Syria investigate human rights abuses committed during deadly clashes with the Druze community. Investigators found no indication that Damascus had probed violations, documenting widespread looting and systematic burning targeting Druze civilians.

stories.title: Deposed Venezuelan president Maduro makes second NYC court appearance
stories.summary: Deposed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro made his second court appearance in New York City following his capture by US forces in a nighttime raid. A federal judge refused to dismiss the case against Maduro and his wife, noting their apparent inability to afford legal representation without Venezuelan government aid.

stories.title: What the debut of a new air-based missile means for China’s nuclear strategy
stories.summary: China debuted the Jinglei-1, a nuclear-capable air-launched ballistic missile, at last September's World War II Victory Day parade in Beijing. Carried by H-6N strategic bombers, the weapon completes China's nuclear triad capability, which a state-linked military magazine says reinforces its no-first-use policy.

stories.title: BYD’s four-year profit run ends, eyes global markets as next engine of growth
stories.summary: Chinese EV manufacturer BYD reported its first annual profit decline in four years, with 2025 net profit falling 18.97% to 32.6 billion yuan amid intensifying domestic competition. The Shenzhen-based company is now looking to global markets as its next engine of growth.

stories.title: Air China subsidiary to lease 10 Boeing jets in deals worth about US$400 million
stories.summary: Shandong Airlines, a subsidiary of Air China, announced plans to lease 10 Boeing 737 aircraft in deals worth approximately US$405 million. The aircraft will be delivered in batches over two years, signaling China's continued demand for Boeing jets to refresh aging fleets.

stories.title: ‘It’s fired people up’: support grows, including within Labor, for new gas tax to curb wartime profits
stories.summary: Political momentum is growing in Australia, including among Labor MPs, for a new tax on gas producers to curb wartime profits linked to the Middle East conflict. The Australian Energy Producers group is mobilizing against the proposal, arguing it would harm relationships with Asian trading partners.

stories.title: Blink and miss: Trump’s tactic of threats first and U-turn later is proving stale in Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump delayed planned strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, claiming peace talks were going well, even as Israel announced fresh strikes on Tehran. Critics have dubbed this pattern of threats followed by reversals as undermining US credibility in the conflict.

stories.title: Wily coyote? urban canines take more risks compared with rural ones – study
stories.summary: A study found that urban coyotes across the US are bolder and less fearful of new experiences compared to their rural counterparts. Researchers believe the behavioral difference, which may hold true across species, likely results from reduced harassment in city environments.

stories.title: Older Australians in ‘immediate danger’ as fuel crisis affects travel for aged care workers
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs driven by the Middle East war are endangering older Australians by affecting aged care workers' ability to travel. Australian unions and farmers are calling for government intervention as agriculture, construction, and waste industries also face significant impacts from higher prices.

stories.title: Cuba says it will do everything to find aid boats missing on way from Mexico
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel pledged to do everything possible to find two sailing boats that went missing while transporting humanitarian aid from Mexico's Quintana Roo state to Havana. The vessels, carrying food and medicine, were part of a convoy expected to arrive by midweek.

stories.title: Cracks Spread Through Putin’s Power Structure
stories.summary: Growing war setbacks, public protests, and internet shutdowns in Russia are exposing limits to the Kremlin's control. The developments signal widening cracks in President Putin's power structure.

stories.title: Estonian intelligence: Ukraine’s port strikes halt route carrying 40–50% of Russia’s oil exports
stories.summary: Estonia's intelligence chief reported that Ukrainian strikes on Russian port infrastructure have disrupted a route carrying 40–50% of Russia's oil exports. The assessment also noted Russia lost approximately 11,000 troops in a single week with no territorial gains.

stories.title: Pro-Iran hackers claim breach of FBI director’s email
stories.summary: The Iran-linked hacker group Handala Hack Team claimed to have breached FBI Director Kash Patel's personal email account. A person familiar with the matter indicated the leaked materials appear to be authentic.

stories.title: Nepal's new PM inherits India-China-US balancing act
stories.summary: Balendra Shah, a rapper-turned-politician, has taken office as Nepal's new prime minister with a youth-driven mandate for change. He faces the challenge of balancing Nepal's relationships with neighboring India, China, and the United States.

stories.title: SOF release footage of strikes on maritime drone operator base in Sevastopol and Vostochny training ground
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces released footage of strikes on a maritime drone operator base in Russian-occupied Sevastopol and the Vostochny training ground in occupied Zaporizhzhia region. Several other enemy targets were also hit.

stories.title: Proposed anti-crime wall along Cape Town highway divides residents
stories.summary: A proposed anti-crime wall along a major multi-lane highway in Cape Town, South Africa, has divided local residents. The highway, which connects the airport to the city center, has seen a surge in attacks on motorists.

stories.title: 187 years after deadly Iran pogrom, Mashhad crypto-Jews are focus of Jerusalem exhibit
stories.summary: An exhibition at Israel's National Library in Jerusalem spotlights the crypto-Jewish community of Mashhad, Iran, 187 years after a deadly pogrom on March 26, 1839. The display documents how the community outwardly practiced Islam for over a century following the massacre.

stories.title: Exclusive images: Nightly pro-govt rallies spread in Iran
stories.summary: Since the US-Israel war with Iran began on February 28, growing numbers of Iranians have been gathering nightly in Tehran's main squares and across the country to express support for the regime. Exclusive footage captures participants explaining their motivations for attending the rallies.

stories.title: The south in flames of great war: Ukrainian army reclaims 470 square kilometers of land in bloody confrontation
stories.summary: The Ukrainian military reclaimed 470 square kilometers of territory in southern Ukraine during intense fighting. Russian forces responded with record numbers of drone attacks, which analysts characterize as attempts to distract from significant losses and a stalling spring offensive.

stories.title: NATO sees $145B in munitions needs, as members all hit 2 percent GDP for first time
stories.summary: NATO has identified $145 billion in munitions needs as all member nations hit the 2 percent GDP defense spending threshold for the first time. Secretary General Rutte indicated that boosting munitions production will be a primary focus at the next NATO summit.

stories.title: Heraskevych addresses UN panel after IOC banned his tribute helmet at Milan Cortina
stories.summary: Ukrainian skeleton athlete Vladyslav Heraskevych addressed a UN panel after the International Olympic Committee banned his tribute helmet at the Milan Cortina Games. The UN audience gave a standing ovation as the names on the helmet were read aloud.

stories.title: Putin asks oligarchs to donate to Russia's budget as cost of Ukraine war soars, The Bell media reports
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has asked oligarchs to contribute to the national budget to help stabilize finances strained by the ongoing invasion of Ukraine, according to The Bell media outlet citing unnamed sources.

stories.title: Rubio attends G7 meeting in France for talks on Iran, Ukraine
stories.summary: European foreign ministers used a G7 meeting in France with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to argue that Russia was helping Iran target US forces in the Middle East. The gathering took place amid wars in Iran and Ukraine, economic uncertainty, and growing unease over unpredictable US foreign policy under President Trump.

stories.title: 'Conflicting and confusing statements from Trump': The latest from Iran
stories.summary: President Trump postponed his deadline for strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, claiming peace negotiations were progressing well. Meanwhile, Israel announced fresh strikes on Tehran, and Iran responded coolly to an American peace plan. Trump denied being desperate for a deal to end the conflict.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Asia hit hard by disruptions to energy markets
stories.summary: Countries across Asia are being hit particularly hard by energy market disruptions in the fourth week of the Middle East war, given their dependence on Persian Gulf energy supplies. Governments and populations are seeking ways to adapt to ongoing fuel shortages.

stories.title: Why Philippines may face ‘strategic dilemma’ over Nato partnership, US demands
stories.summary: The Philippines is pursuing broader defense cooperation with NATO's European members while maintaining its longstanding security alliance with the United States. Observers note Manila could face a strategic dilemma if its NATO ties conflict with U.S. positions, particularly as President Trump criticizes the alliance over its Middle East involvement.

stories.title: Saudi, UAE, Iraq: Can three pipelines help oil escape Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Iraq have accelerated oil exports via pipeline routes to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The three countries are seeking to mitigate disruption risks to global energy supplies amid regional tensions.

stories.title: Ministry of Economy: Ukraine's GDP drops by approximately 1.2% in first two months of this year
stories.summary: In the first two months of this year, GDP decreased by about 1.2%, but the government expects economic activity to recover soon.

stories.title: UN human rights chief calls on US to conclude probe into Iran school strike
stories.summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk urged the United States to complete its investigation into a strike on a school in Iran that killed at least 168 people, most of them children. Türk described the attack as evoking "visceral horror."

stories.title: Bloomberg: Ukraine to sign air defense cooperation deal with Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as part of an unannounced Gulf tour. Ukraine is expected to sign an air defense cooperation deal with Saudi Arabia, offering drone interception expertise in exchange for U.S.-made missile supplies.

stories.title: Is Trump's pause on attacking Iranian energy for diplomacy or an escalation?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has paused strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, with BBC diplomatic editor James Landale analyzing whether the move signals a diplomatic opening or preparation for further escalation. Trump's use of deadlines is described as fluid but purposeful.

stories.title: Qatari PM and US officials discuss strategic ties amid Iran war
stories.summary: Qatar's Prime Minister met with U.S. officials to discuss strategic ties during the ongoing Iran war. Qatar's foreign ministry described the talks as a review of close strategic cooperation between Doha and Washington.

stories.title: As Americans drink much less wine, kosher demand stays strong
stories.summary: Despite a significant decline in overall U.S. wine consumption, demand for kosher wine remains strong. A built-in ritual market and an evolving consumer base are helping kosher wine producers outperform the broader industry.

stories.title: Iran expert says US ground invasion could cause a global economic meltdown
stories.summary: Iran expert Ali Vaez warned that a U.S. ground invasion of Iran could trigger a global economic meltdown. He assessed that the U.S. and Iran have reached a military stalemate in which further escalation by either side risks catastrophic consequences.

stories.title: #MeToo and the French farming sector
stories.summary: French farmer Laura Chalendard launched a #MeToo movement in the agricultural sector after reporting a sexual assault in 2023 that led to no charges. The segment also covers how perimenopause and menopause are worsening Germany's labor shortage.

stories.title: France slams return of Olympic gender testing as 'a step backwards'
stories.summary: French Sports Minister Marina Ferrari criticized the International Olympic Committee's decision to reintroduce gender testing for the first time since 1999, calling it a step backwards. She argued that genetic testing would unfairly exclude many athletes with differences in sexual development.

stories.title: Afghan asylum seeker jailed for raping and abducting 12-year-old girl
stories.summary: Ahmad Mulakhil, an Afghan asylum seeker, was jailed for 15 years in the UK for abducting and raping a 12-year-old girl in Nuneaton. He filmed himself during the assault and was found guilty of rape, child abduction, and multiple sexual assault charges.

stories.title: Hamas disarmament plan sees Gaza's tunnels destroyed, arms given up in stages, text shows
stories.summary: The plan follows an eight-month timeline that begins with a US-backed committee of Palestinian technocrats taking security control of Gaza and concludes with Israeli forces withdrawing completely.

stories.title: Iran releases strike images from US–Israeli attacks as war fears escalate
stories.summary: Iran released images showing damage at two sites in Tehran and a northwestern province following overnight U.S.-Israeli strikes. The publication of the images came as fears of further military escalation intensified.

stories.title: Ukraine sent air defense experts to Saudi Arabia. They delivered results in a week
stories.summary: Ukraine has deployed air defense specialists to Saudi Arabia, leveraging four years of combat experience during which Ukrainian forces intercepted over 57,000 Iranian-designed drones. Reports indicate the experts delivered measurable results within one week of arrival.

stories.title: Cryptocurrencies aiding Iran during war
stories.summary: Between February 28 and March 2, over $12.85 million worth of cryptocurrency left Iran as the country reportedly turned to digital currencies amid wartime conditions. The use of crypto highlights efforts to circumvent financial constraints during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Pain at the pump fuels EV rush in China, driving a timely boost for carmakers
stories.summary: Rising oil prices driven by the Middle East conflict are boosting demand for electric vehicles in China. With Brent crude trading above US$110 per barrel, Chinese consumers are increasingly switching from petrol vehicles to battery-powered cars, providing a timely lift for domestic EV manufacturers.

stories.title: Leading Chinese hypersonic aviation scientist Yan Hong dies at 56
stories.summary: Yan Hong, a leading Chinese researcher in hypersonic and high-speed propulsion technologies, died at age 56 at a hospital in Nanjing. She was a professor at Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi'an, an institution placed on U.S. sanctions lists for alleged ties to military research.

stories.title: Chinese market regulator tells firms to focus on healthy competition overseas
stories.summary: China's State Administration for Market Regulation urged major companies including BYD and CATL to maintain healthy competitive practices in overseas markets. The directive comes amid growing international accusations of unfair competition, subsidies, and dumping by Chinese firms.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces strike Valday radar complex and drone control station in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck the Russian Valday radar complex and the Forpost ground-based drone control station in the temporarily occupied Crimea, as well as several other enemy targets in the te

stories.title: Rain, thunderstorms likely in Karachi, other parts of Sindh tomorrow: PMD
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast chances of rain and thunderstorms in Karachi and across Sindh on Saturday, as a westerly wave continues to affect the country.
According to it

stories.title: ‘Policing thought’: French bill to fight antisemitism accused of silencing Israel critics
stories.summary: A proposed French law aimed at combating antisemitism would sanction public statements presenting terrorism as legitimate resistance and create an offense for incitement to the destruction or denial of a state. Critics accuse the bill of silencing criticism of Israel and policing thought.

stories.title: IDF soldier, combat officer severely wounded during operational accident in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The soldiers have been taken to a hospital, and their families have been notified.

stories.title: Israel launches new wave of strikes on Iran with no sign of diplomatic breakthrough
stories.summary: Israel’s attack on targets “in the heart of Tehran” came after the country said it would be “intensifying” its strikes on Iranian weapons production facilities

stories.title: Czech Police Investigating Firebomb Attack on Russian Culture Center in Prague
stories.summary: Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called the attack on the Russian House "barbaric."

stories.title: Gas production facility in Poltava region shuts down following Russian attack
stories.summary: A gas production facility in the Poltava region has suspended operations due to a Russian attack.

stories.title: Man jailed for assaulting woman in London attack witnessed by Barron Trump
stories.summary: Matvei Rumiantsev, a 23-year-old Russian man, was sentenced to four years in a British prison for assaulting a woman in London. The attack occurred after Rumiantsev became jealous of her friendship with Barron Trump, who witnessed the assault via video call and alerted police.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit all three Baltic States − did Russia redirect them?
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck locations in all three Baltic States, raising questions about whether Russia actively redirected them. It remains unclear if the incursions resulted from deliberate Russian action or were a byproduct of electronic warfare defenses and flight distances.

stories.title: Le Monde: 'Majority' of ICC bureau members support Karim Khan exoneration report
stories.summary: According to Le Monde, a majority of International Criminal Court bureau members support the exoneration report concerning ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan. Khan has been on a leave of absence since May 2025 pending the outcome of an investigation.

stories.title: US Republicans reject Senate bill to end shutdown, fund TSA
stories.summary: US House Republicans rejected a Senate bill aimed at ending the partial government shutdown and funding the TSA. With Congress deadlocked, President Trump signed an executive action to ensure airport security officers continue to be paid.

stories.title: Escalation in Middle East possible in coming days, Polish prime minister says
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that a further escalation in the Middle East conflict is possible in the coming days. Tusk said the assessment was based on intelligence shared by allied nations, stating that stabilization was unlikely.

stories.title: Top US AI conference apologises after sanctions policy sparks backlash in China
stories.summary: Organizers of a leading U.S. artificial intelligence conference apologized after a new policy appeared to bar U.S.-sanctioned entities from participating, sparking backlash in China. Several major Chinese professional bodies had urged domestic researchers to boycott the event over concerns that companies like Huawei would be excluded.

stories.title: What do China’s new ‘correct view’ rules for local Communist Party officials mean?
stories.summary: China's ruling Communist Party Politburo met in Beijing under President Xi Jinping to review new regulations for local party committees. The rules call for upholding a "correct view" of political performance, emphasizing alignment of regional governance with central leadership priorities.

stories.title: Palestinian man killed as death toll from West Bank settler violence climbs
stories.summary: Mohammad al-Malhi, a Palestinian man, was killed by an Israeli settler in the occupied West Bank, bringing the total number of Palestinians killed by settlers to seven since the outbreak of the war with Iran. The violence represents a surge in settler attacks.

stories.title: Time to confront folly of Iran war and irrational US spending
stories.summary: The article discusses the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fourth year, alongside an escalating US-Israel conflict with Iran. Key developments include the reported death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and surging oil prices.

stories.title: Ukraine and Saudi Arabia sign defense cooperation agreement
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine and Saudi Arabia have signed a defense cooperation agreement, which strengthens Ukraine’s international role as a security provider.

stories.title: Afghan repatriations suspended after border security official injured at Torkham
stories.summary: PESHAWAR: Repatriation of undocumented Afghan nationals was abruptly suspended on Friday after a border security official was injured in a late evening cross-border attack from the Afghan side on Thur

stories.title: Ukraine announces ‘mutually beneficial’ defence deal with Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Ukraine announced a defense cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia, described by Kyiv as mutually beneficial. The deal leverages Ukraine's combat-tested expertise in countering drone warfare, developed during its own conflict involving Iranian-designed drones.

stories.title: Sudan: Global Fund Approves Emergency TB Funding for Conflict-Affected Sudan
stories.summary: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria approved US$1,607,729 in emergency funding for tuberculosis diagnosis and treatment in conflict-affected Sudan. The program, running through December 2026, will be implemented by UNDP in collaboration with Sudan's National TB Programme to serve internally displaced persons and host communities.

stories.title: Text of Board of Peace Gaza plan calls for Hamas to disarm over period of eight months
stories.summary: The Board of Peace's Gaza plan calls for Hamas to disarm over an eight-month period and agree to the destruction of its tunnel network. Under the plan, the IDF would fully withdraw only after verification that Gaza is free of weaponry.

stories.title: IDF destroys regime's missile, sea mine production site in Yazd amid nationwide airstrikes
stories.summary: The IDF hit Iran's missile and sea mine production site in Yazd, targeting key regime infrastructure across the country, including Tehran and Isfahan, as part of ongoing operations.

stories.title: Palestinian killed as Jewish settlers rampage through West Bank
stories.summary: One Palestinian was shot dead and 14 others wounded during Israeli settler raids across the occupied West Bank. Five new settler outposts were established overnight, including four in Area A, which is nominally under full Palestinian Authority control.

stories.title: Israeli forces prevent Friday prayer on Salah al-Din Street in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli forces prevented Palestinians from conducting Friday prayers on Salah al-Din Street in occupied Jerusalem, dispersing worshippers and the imam within minutes. The incident occurred as Israeli authorities continued to keep Al-Aqsa Mosque closed for the 28th consecutive day.

stories.title: Donald Trump takes credit for transgender ban at LA's 2028 Olympics
stories.summary: The International Olympic Committee ruled to ban transgender female athletes from competing in female events starting with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. President Trump took credit for the decision, while India's parliament approved a controversial law that critics say curtails transgender rights.

stories.title: Two killed in Israeli attack in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli attack on Hawta al-Ghadir in Beirut's southern suburbs killed two people at dawn, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Lebanon's health ministry reported that at least 1,116 people were killed and 3,229 injured in Israeli attacks on Lebanon between March 2 and March 20.

stories.title: IDF Home Front Command to extend siren warning times for Hezbollah rockets
stories.summary: This could double the amount of time that Israelis have to reach a sheltered area in the event of Hezbollah terrorists launching rockets towards Israeli civilian locations.

stories.title: Iran war tests MAGA's 'America first' credo
stories.summary: As the US-Iran conflict approaches its first month, support among MAGA supporters for President Trump remains high but some cracks are appearing. The war is testing the movement's core 'America first' principle of avoiding foreign conflicts.

stories.title: Namibia: First Gentleman Ndaitwah Calls for Critical, Forward-Thinking Leadership
stories.summary: Namibia's first gentleman Denga Ndaitwah called on leaders to adopt self-critical and forward-thinking approaches, emphasizing the need to reflect, adapt, and focus on present challenges for effective leadership.

stories.title: France calls IOC sex testing a ‘step backwards’ while Trump praises move
stories.summary: France criticized the International Olympic Committee's new sex-testing eligibility policy as a "step backwards," while U.S. President Trump praised the move. The IOC's updated policy excludes transgender women athletes from competing in female events at the Olympics.

stories.title: Oil rises, stocks mixed as investors worry over Trump's Iran war
stories.summary: Oil prices rose while stock markets showed mixed results as investors expressed concern over the trajectory of the U.S.-Iran war. Market uncertainty was driven by inconsistent White House messaging, with President Trump alternating between threats and peace rhetoric.

stories.title: Spanish woman who died through euthanasia failed by state, say critics
stories.summary: Noelia Castillo, a Spanish woman, died by euthanasia on Thursday evening at a Barcelona hospital following a prolonged legal battle with her father. Critics say the state failed her throughout the process.

stories.title: Nigeria: Army Intensifies Offensives, Records Gains Against Iswap, Boko Haram in Northast
stories.summary: The Nigerian Army, under Operation Hadin Kai, has intensified offensives against ISWAP and Boko Haram in the North-East. The military reported major gains targeting key leaders and insurgent strongholds.

stories.title: Rubio, G7 diplomats duel over wars in Iran and Ukraine
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clashed with G7 counterparts over the wars in Iran and Ukraine at a gathering outside Paris. Rubio criticized European allies for not supporting US military efforts in the Gulf, while European nations rebuffed President Trump's request for military assistance in the region.

stories.title: Africa: Can the Iran War Shift the Dial On Climate Action?
stories.summary: An analysis from the Institute for Security Studies examines how the Iran war's impact on Africa could be profound, while suggesting that lessons from the conflict might accelerate the continent's energy transition.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Escalating Violence and Influx of Returnees in DR Congo Fuel Regional Instability
stories.summary: The humanitarian crisis in the Democratic Republic of Congo has worsened following the reopening of the Burundi-DRC border, with returning Congolese refugees facing overcrowded conditions. Escalating clashes between AFC, M23 rebels, and government-affiliated forces, including drone strikes, are fueling regional instability.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: See Shabbat times for your area.

stories.title: Opinion: Iran's way of warfare is being tested to its limits
stories.summary: An analysis examines how Iran's layered warfare strategy of forward defense through allied non-state partners and long-range missiles is being tested under current hostilities. The piece notes that Iranian military commander Hossein Salami, who had vowed overwhelming defensive power, was killed in an Israeli air strike.

stories.title: Africa: Africa Is Forging Its Own Green Future
stories.summary: African institutions are developing their own frameworks for a green energy transition, aiming to advance both economic development and climate resilience. The push comes despite long-standing shortfalls in international climate financing for the continent.

stories.title: Latin American Countries Boost Ties to Africa
stories.summary: Latin American countries are strengthening ties with African nations in a new era of south-south cooperation. The article questions whether these partnerships can outlast the current leftist leadership in the region.

stories.title: China’s economy big enough to absorb Iran war shocks, says Justin Lin
stories.summary: Economist Justin Lin Yifu, dean of Peking University's Institute of New Structural Economics, stated that China's economy has sufficient capacity to absorb shocks from the Iran war and still meet its growth targets. He also noted China is preparing for the possibility that Washington might renege on trade deals.

stories.title: The end of ‘win-lose’? China-backed mediation body makes pitch at Boao Forum
stories.summary: Teresa Cheng Yeuk-wah, secretary general of the newly launched International Organisation for Mediation, promoted the China-backed body at the Boao Forum for Asia. She described mediation as a flexible alternative to arbitration and litigation for resolving commercial and state-level disputes involving long-term investment.

stories.title: Protection against Iranian attacks: Zelensky meets with Ukrainian military experts in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Ukrainian military experts currently in Saudi Arabia to discuss key requirements for strengthening air defense in the region.

stories.title: West Africa: Ecowas Marks 50 Years With Academic Quiz Competition for Liberian Students

stories.title: Hong Kong Kai Tak Cruise Terminal tender deadline extended by 1 month
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities extended the tender deadline for the next Kai Tak Cruise Terminal operator by one month, from May 22 to June 26. The Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau granted the extension after prospective bidders requested additional time to prepare for new management requirements and key performance indicators.

stories.title: At Turkish border town, Iranians seek respite from ‘endless’ war at home
stories.summary: Iranian civilians, particularly young people, have been crossing into the Turkish border town seeking temporary refuge from the ongoing war. Iranians expressed divided opinions about the regime and uncertainty about their future regardless of the conflict's outcome.

stories.title: China team builds first silicon chip with elements for fault-tolerant quantum computing
stories.summary: Researchers from Shenzhen, China, demonstrated the first silicon quantum chip capable of performing a full set of error-detecting logical operations, a milestone published in Nature Nanotechnology. This achievement, previously accomplished only in superconducting circuits, represents a key advance toward building fault-tolerant quantum computers using silicon technology.

stories.title: World Bank to provide financial aid to countries affected by war
stories.summary: The World Bank announced it will provide financial relief to countries affected by the Middle East war, which has disrupted global energy prices and created economic challenges for multiple nations.

stories.title: Over 8,000 litres of illicit fuel worth HK$250,000 seized, driver arrested in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities arrested a 61-year-old driver and seized over 8,000 litres of illicit fuel valued at HK$250,000 in a joint operation involving police, Fire Services, and Customs. The seizure is part of a growing trend of illegal fuel cases linked to rising global oil prices driven by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Nigeria: Air Traffic Controllers Lament Obsolete Equipment, Low Morale of Personnel
stories.summary: Nigerian air traffic controllers have warned that obsolete equipment and low personnel morale are threatening the safety of the country's airspace. Controllers described escalating operational pressures that endanger national flight security.

stories.title: Nigeria: NCAA, Army Collaborate for Improved Aviation Security At Abuja Airport
stories.summary: The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority and the Nigerian Army are collaborating to improve security at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja. The joint effort aims to advance aviation security at the capital's main airport.

stories.title: US creates fund to help return displaced Ukrainian children
stories.summary: The United States has established a fund to support the return of Ukrainian children who were forcibly deported to Russia. Nearly 20,000 Ukrainian children have been taken since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: War on Iran could usher the end of US petrodollar, Deutsche Bank says
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank issued a report warning that the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran could undermine the petrodollar system, a key pillar of the U.S. dollar's status as the world's reserve currency.

stories.title: Trump weaves from Sharpies to Bessent’s glasses in cabinet meeting
stories.summary: During a Cabinet meeting focused on the US-Israeli war with Iran—now in its fourth week and causing a historic energy shock—President Trump digressed into topics including Sharpie pens, Treasury Secretary Bessent's glasses, and jokes about running for president of Venezuela.

stories.title: Hong Kong must look beyond mainland China talent to stay global, experts say
stories.summary: Experts warned that Hong Kong's heavy reliance on mainland Chinese talent—94.5 percent of successful top talent scheme applicants—could undermine its status as an international hub. Industry veterans and lawmakers called for a strategic shift toward recruiting from the Middle East and ASEAN, though challenges remain regarding Muslim-friendly workplaces.

stories.title: Mexican navy says petroleum tanker, natural seabed likely caused Gulf coast spill
stories.summary: Mexican naval officials stated that an oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico was caused by both natural seabed seepage and a petroleum tanker that authorities are still working to identify.

stories.title: Iran war risks, Southeast Asia’s fuel crisis, Xinjiang’s ‘salmon’: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post highlighted seven key stories of the week, including Chinese experts analyzing risks of potential U.S. ground operations in Iran, Southeast Asia's fuel crisis, and other regional developments. Topics spanned the Strait of Hormuz uncertainty and various issues across Hong Kong, mainland China, and broader Asia.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Violence Intensifies As UN Mission Pledges Continued Support
stories.summary: A senior UN official told the Security Council that the security and political situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains extremely tense. The UN mission pledged continued support as violence intensifies in the DRC.

stories.title: Five more children returned from temporarily occupied Kherson region
stories.summary: Five more children have been returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory from the temporarily occupied part of the Kherson region. Four of the five children are without parental care.

stories.title: As Philippines battles fuel crisis, will Marcos postpone Asean summit?
stories.summary: Philippine lawmakers urged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to postpone the 2025 ASEAN summit as the country struggles with soaring fuel prices amid the global energy crisis. Analysts cautioned that postponement could undermine Manila's chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

stories.title: Malaysia’s ships allowed to pass Strait of Hormuz, PM Anwar says
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Iran has granted clearance for Malaysian oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The Malaysian government is also introducing domestic fuel conservation measures.

stories.title: First responders rescue man from Tehran building hit by air strike
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society released footage showing first responders in Tehran rescuing a man trapped in a building damaged by an air strike.

stories.title: Trump says he was told Mojtaba Khamenei may be gay, spotlighting Iran’s brutal anti-gay persecution
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump publicly claimed he was told that Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Iran's supreme leader, may be gay. Same-sex relations are criminalized in Iran and can carry the death penalty under the Islamic regime's systematic persecution of LGBTQ+ individuals.

stories.title: US considers sending additional 10,000 ground troops to Middle East amid Iran talks - report
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering deploying an additional 10,000 ground troops to the Middle East during ongoing Iran talks. The force would likely include infantry and armored vehicles, supplementing the 82nd Airborne Division already in the region, according to the Wall Street Journal.

stories.title: Palestinians flee tear gas as Israeli settlers arrive in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: The Israeli army fired tear gas at Palestinian residents of Beit Imrin village in the occupied West Bank as Israeli settlers arrived in the area.

stories.title: Envoy to Britain warns against cancelling king’s US visit
stories.summary: A diplomatic envoy to Britain has warned against cancelling the king's planned visit to the United States. Buckingham Palace has not yet officially confirmed the trip.

stories.title: Hong Kong home prices surge to near 2-year high, but Iran war clouds outlook
stories.summary: Hong Kong's second-hand home prices rose 1.6 percent in February, marking 11 consecutive months of growth and pushing the official index to a 22-month high. Since reversing a downward trend in April, prices have climbed nearly 8 percent, though the ongoing Iran conflict clouds the market outlook.

stories.title: A way out for the US and Iran? The diplomatic path that could prove China right
stories.summary: Chinese Middle East expert Niu Xinchun of Ningxia University suggested nuclear containment and regional ceasefires as the most viable starting points for U.S.-Iran negotiations. He argued the escalating conflict has validated China's longstanding insistence on diplomatic and political solutions to the crisis.

stories.title: Albanese government says fuel supply ‘same, if not higher’ in coming weeks as Coalition calls for halving of excise
stories.summary: The Australian government sought to reassure the public that fuel supply levels would remain normal or increase in coming weeks amid rising prices. The ACCC reported diesel and unleaded petrol prices rose roughly 10% and 8% respectively across Australia's five largest cities. The Coalition called for the fuel excise to be halved.

stories.title: Iran bars its sports teams from traveling to ‘hostile’ countries
stories.summary: Iran announced a ban on its sports teams traveling to countries deemed "hostile," citing security concerns. The decision affects an upcoming club soccer match in Saudi Arabia and prompted efforts to relocate Iran's World Cup matches from the U.S. to Mexico.

stories.title: Australia will be left with no submarines if it abandons Aukus, senior defence official warns
stories.summary: A senior Australian defence official warned that Australia would have no submarines if it abandons the Aukus partnership with the US and UK. The official declined to outline an alternative plan if the promised Virginia-class and Aukus-class nuclear-powered submarines do not arrive under Australian command.

stories.title: Red Crescent video shows aftermath of strike on homes in Iran’s Urmia
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent released video showing damage to a residential area in Urmia, the capital of West Azerbaijan province, following a strike.

stories.title: Albanese says Australia playing “constructive” role in the war on Iran
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated that his government has played a "constructive" role in the war on Iran, though he did not specify the nature of Australia's contribution.

stories.title: Ukraine says ‘no indication’ US weapons to be diverted to Middle East
stories.summary: Ukraine stated there is no indication that US-supplied weapons will be diverted to the Middle East. The PURL programme enables Ukraine to receive US military equipment financed by European countries.

stories.title: Google’s Gemini AI app debuts in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Google launched its Gemini AI chatbot mobile app in Hong Kong, where it quickly topped Apple's app store chart. The rollout followed Google's announcement of a gradual introduction of generative AI services to the city, beginning with web-based access before the mobile version.

stories.title: Cheap and elusive, drones put incessant pressure on Israel’s evolving air defenses
stories.summary: Iran and Hezbollah are deploying waves of low-cost drones that challenge Israel's air defenses. Israel is responding with layered defense systems and emerging technologies, drawing on lessons from Ukraine's experience with drone warfare.

stories.title: Wild autumn weather delivers snow, storms and power cuts to eastern Australia
stories.summary: Severe autumn storms struck eastern Australia on Thursday night, leaving thousands without power across multiple states and delivering the first major snowfall of 2026 to highland areas. Tropical Cyclone Narelle was also expected to make landfall near Perth, bringing potential flash flooding to Western Australia.

stories.title: At least six killed in Iran's Qom, as Tehran announces hits across region
stories.summary: A U.S.-Israeli strike on a residential area in Qom, Iran, killed at least six people, with the number of wounded still unknown. The Red Crescent said rescue operations continue in both Tehran and Qom to find people trapped under rubble.

stories.title: Who is Hasan Piker, the US left-wing streamer critics say the Democrats should reject?
stories.summary: U.S. left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has drawn scrutiny as Democratic politicians appear on his show. Critics accuse him of antisemitism and warn that engagement with him risks centering bigotry within the party.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to sell defense systems in surplus to partners – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to sell surplus defense systems to partner nations. The Ukrainian defense industry is currently operating at half capacity due to insufficient funding, and proceeds would help increase domestic drone production.

stories.title: Hong Kong slams UK for undermining city’s rule of law with calls to release Jimmy Lai
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government condemned the United Kingdom for undermining the city's rule of law after British authorities pledged to press for the release of Jimmy Lai, the former media executive sentenced to 20 years for national security offences. Hong Kong dismissed London's comments as misleading and irresponsible.

stories.title: Over 1,000 Diaspora leaders urge action against ‘Jewish-extremist terror in West Bank’
stories.summary: Over 1,000 Diaspora Jewish leaders sent a letter to Israeli President Herzog condemning settler violence in the West Bank as morally and strategically damaging. They called on the president to intervene given the government's lack of action.

stories.title: Iran recruiting teenagers for Tehran checkpoints amid war
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly recruiting children as young as 12 to staff checkpoints in Tehran amid the ongoing war. The minors are being tasked with collecting security data and conducting operational patrols.

stories.title: Hezbollah attacks Israeli forces attempting to advance into southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced multiple attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, including detonating explosive devices and launching missiles, claiming confirmed casualties. The assaults came as Israel attempted to advance deeper into Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Two aid boats go missing en route to Cuba, says Mexico
stories.summary: Two humanitarian aid boats carrying nine people went missing after departing Mexico bound for Havana, Cuba. The Mexican navy has launched a search and rescue operation.

stories.title: Middle East live: Iran launches strikes on Israel and Gulf sites
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced they carried out missile and drone strikes against targets in Israel and US-linked military facilities across the Gulf on Thursday. Strikes reportedly hit sites in the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain, including a Patriot air-defence maintenance facility.

stories.title: Russia says Britain's decision to detain its vessels is hostile, vows response
stories.summary: Russia's embassy in the United Kingdom called Britain's plan to detain Russian vessels a hostile act, as reported by the TASS news agency. Moscow vowed to respond with political, legal, and asymmetric measures against the decision.

stories.title: Belarus leader gifts rifle to North Korea's Kim as they sign friendship treaty
stories.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko visited Pyongyang and gifted a rifle to North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as the two signed a friendship treaty. Both leaders are key supporters of Russia's war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Two Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon combat, military says
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced that two of its soldiers were killed during combat operations in southern Lebanon on Thursday. The clashes occurred amid ongoing fighting with Hezbollah along the Israeli-Lebanese border.

stories.title: Trump suggests that Iran let ten oil tankers through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump suggested during a White House Cabinet meeting that Iran allow ten oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing blockade.

stories.title: As haze returns to Singapore, is crisis ‘quietly accepted’ by Asean as inevitable?
stories.summary: Recurring transboundary haze has returned to Singapore, with residents reporting worsening air quality during evening hours. The article examines whether ASEAN member states have quietly accepted the annual haze crisis—driven largely by land-clearing fires in the region—as an inevitable occurrence.

stories.title: China’s top chip foundry SMIC unveils action plan for seizing new growth opportunities
stories.summary: China's largest contract chipmaker, SMIC, released an action plan alongside its 2025 annual report aimed at enhancing existing operations and pursuing new growth opportunities through 2026. The strategy focuses on optimizing current capabilities while supporting China's semiconductor self-sufficiency drive.

stories.title: Iran’s harder-to-hunt long-range missiles are taking greater toll
stories.summary: Despite nearly four weeks of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes that have significantly degraded Iran's military capability, Tehran continues to deploy long-range missiles from hard-to-reach bases in eastern Iran. Recent strikes against Israel, likely involving Khorramshahr missiles, hit targets near Dimona's nuclear research facility and injured over 100 people.

stories.title: Ukraine using strikes to pressure Russia after oil sanctions eased, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is using strikes to pressure Russia after the US issued a 30-day waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products.

stories.title: Mexico launches search for two missing aid boats bound for Cuba
stories.summary: Mexico's navy launched a search operation after two boats carrying humanitarian aid to Cuba went missing en route from Mexican waters.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent who attempted to cut off power to Kropyvnytskyi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SSU) counterintelligence officers detained a Russian FSB agent in Kropyvnytskyi. The agent was allegedly attempting to sabotage power supply infrastructure in the central Ukrainian city.

stories.title: US judge temporarily halts Trump-era sanctions on AI firm Anthropic
stories.summary: A US federal judge temporarily blocked Trump administration sanctions imposed on AI company Anthropic, finding the measures likely violated the law. The ruling freezes a Pentagon designation of the firm as a national security risk while the government considers an emergency appeal.

stories.title: War Diary Day 27: Multifront escalation in US-Israeli war on Iran appears imminent
stories.summary: On day 27 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, strikes intensified inside Iran with multiple explosions reported across Tehran and Khorramabad. Air defence systems were activated in the capital, and the conflict showed no signs of de-escalation as President Trump's five-day pause expired.
