stories.title: More than one million displaced by Israel’s evacuations in Lebanon
stories.summary: More than 250,000 people fled Lebanon over a two-week period due to Israeli-ordered evacuations, with approximately 125,000 crossing into Syria, including around 7,000 Lebanese citizens. The total displaced exceeds one million.

stories.title: Death toll in Lebanon increases to over 1,110
stories.summary: Lebanon's National News Agency reported that Israeli attacks have killed over 1,116 people and wounded 3,229 in Lebanon, while forcibly displacing more than 136,000 people into shelters.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia weathering Iran war, but Red Sea attacks could force its hand
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has so far weathered the economic effects of the Iran war, but escalating Red Sea attacks could force Riyadh into a more active role. A new Red Sea front would likely draw Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen into the conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky arrives in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Saudi Arabia for an official visit to meet with Saudi leadership.

stories.title: After four years of war, Ukraine formally tears up its last legal ties to Russia and the CIS
stories.summary: Ukraine formally terminated its remaining legal agreements with Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said 116 agreements are being terminated, denounced, or withdrawn from after four years of war.

stories.title: 'Tehran assumes war is behind them:  Iran will not capitulate, Trump has it all wrong'
stories.summary: Senior researcher Danny Citrinowicz of Israel's Institute for National Security Studies assessed that Iran interprets its endurance in the war as strategic success. He argued Tehran believes the conflict is largely behind it and is unlikely to capitulate despite US military superiority.

stories.title: The delusion of easy victory from the air may have seduced the US into another war
stories.summary: An analysis examines the historical pattern of overconfidence in air power delivering quick military victories, drawing parallels to the current US military strategy in Iran. The piece traces the concept back to Italian General Giulio Douhet's 1921 theory on air superiority.

stories.title: Italy police warn reptiles being used by crooks as weapons after snakes found behind false wall
stories.summary: Police in Bari, southern Italy, discovered anacondas, boa constrictors, and a spectacled caiman hidden behind a false wall in an apartment block. Authorities warned that dangerous reptiles are increasingly being used by criminals to intimidate victims.

stories.title: Pentagon weighs diverting Ukraine military aid to the Middle East, Washington Post reports
stories.summary: The Pentagon is considering diverting military aid originally allocated for Ukraine to the Middle East, according to the Washington Post. The consideration comes as US military operations in the region intensify amid the Iran conflict.

stories.title: MEPs back plans for ‘return hubs’, raising fears of ‘human rights black holes’
stories.summary: The European Parliament voted to allow detention of refused asylum seekers for up to two years or their transfer to offshore "return hubs." An alliance of centre-right and far-right lawmakers backed the proposal, which experts warn could create "human rights black holes."

stories.title: Wes Streeting accused of dog whistle politics over campaign letter
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting faced accusations of dog-whistle politics over a campaign letter that described independent candidates as "divisive" and "focused on foreign conflicts."

stories.title: Kallas says US should pressure Russia to end wars in Ukraine and Middle East
stories.summary: EU High Representative Kaja Kallas called on the United States to pressure Russia into making concessions to end the war in Ukraine, emphasizing the need for coordinated US-European efforts on Moscow.

stories.title: Spanish woman wins legal battle to end her life under euthanasia law
stories.summary: Noelia Castillo, a 25-year-old Spanish woman, won a legal battle against her father for the right to euthanasia under Spain's 2021 law. Castillo became paraplegic after a suicide attempt following a sexual assault and has suffered from psychiatric illness and constant pain.

stories.title: Iran war complicates WHO's emergency medical supply routes
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has rerouted emergency medical supplies from Dubai to Lebanon via overland routes as the Iran war disrupts supply chains. Rising fuel costs are further threatening medical shipments to conflict zones.

stories.title: Iran's chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz: Fertiliser supply chains under strain
stories.summary: Disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz due to US-Israel-Iran hostilities are straining global fertiliser supply chains. UN Conference on Trade and Development officials warned of rising prices and food insecurity risks, particularly for the world's poorest economies.

stories.title: National Defense Strategy ‘falls short’ on nuclear, space threat: SASC chair
stories.summary: The chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee stated that the National Defense Strategy falls short in addressing nuclear and space threats. The head of US Strategic Command described a Russian space weapon as a very significant concern.

stories.title: Gulf countries seeking seat at negotiation table following Iranian attacks
stories.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council emphasized the importance of Gulf states participating in any negotiations between Iran and the United States aimed at ending the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Trump says UK’s aircraft carriers are just ‘toys’, repeating complaint about lack of support for US in Iran – UK politics live
stories.summary: President Trump called the UK's aircraft carriers "toys" during a broader address criticizing NATO allies for insufficient support in the Iran war. The remarks highlighted ongoing transatlantic tensions over allied contributions to US-led military operations.

stories.title: Forget Discounts – Russian Oil Is Now Selling at a Premium, Deputy PM Novak Says
stories.summary: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak stated that Russian oil is no longer selling at a discount on global markets. Novak told reporters that prices have shifted to parity or, in some cases, a partial premium compared to international benchmarks.

stories.title: Violence against journalists surges in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported a surge in violence against journalists in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo as armed conflict intensifies in the region. The organization warned that the DRC has become one of the most dangerous countries for media workers in Africa's Great Lakes region.

stories.title: LIVE: Brazil vs France – FIFA World Cup 2026 warm up
stories.summary: Brazil and France are set to play a warm-up match ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026. Full team news and live text commentary are expected.

stories.title: US plans 'final blow' against Iran as Trump demands Tehran make a deal
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of War is reportedly drafting plans for a "final blow" against Iran, including options such as ground troops, a bombing campaign, and seizing or blockading Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90 percent of Iran's oil exports.

stories.title: 'They were trying to dehumanise me': Palestine Action hunger strikers allege mistreatment in prison
stories.summary: Former Palestine Action members who conducted hunger strikes in UK prisons allege they suffered medical neglect and dehumanizing treatment. The former inmates plan to pursue legal action.

stories.title: Uganda military chief suggests could join Israel in Iran war
stories.summary: Ugandan military chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba suggested on social media that Uganda could join Israel's war against Iran. Kainerugaba is known for his outspoken public statements.

stories.title: Hezbollah rocket attack kills one person in Israel
stories.summary: A Hezbollah rocket struck Nahariya in northern Israel, killing one person and seriously wounding another. Iranian and Hezbollah strikes also triggered sirens across Tel Aviv, central Israel, and West Jerusalem, with 25 people reported wounded.

stories.title: Bears take control as PSX plunges over 5,000 points
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index on the Pakistan Stock Exchange fell 5,405.48 points, or 3.41 per cent, closing at 152,907.96. The index hit an intraday low of 152,668.07 points before recovering slightly. The sharp decline followed a previous session's gains driven by cautious optimism over Middle East geopolitical developments.

stories.title: Rationing power and diluting petrol - how African countries are coping with effects of Iran war
stories.summary: Several African countries are experiencing oil supply disruptions linked to the Iran war, leading to fuel shortages. Governments are resorting to measures including power rationing and diluting petrol to cope with reduced supplies.

stories.title: NGO counts over 10 settler attacks a day amid Iran war; 14 said hurt in latest violence
stories.summary: Israeli human rights organization Yesh Din reported 257 incidents of extremist settler violence and land seizures in the West Bank during the first 25 days of the Iran war, averaging over 10 attacks per day. Fourteen people were reportedly hurt in the latest violence.

stories.title: Unable to shut down Kan, coalition maneuvers to control public broadcaster’s budget
stories.summary: Israel's ruling coalition advanced a bill removing legal safeguards protecting public broadcaster Kan from political interference. The legislation was moved to a Knesset committee headed by a Netanyahu loyalist.

stories.title: Chinese Envoy assures Pakistan of 'continued support' in meeting with PM Shehbaz Sharif
stories.summary: Chinese Ambassador Jiang met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and commended Pakistan's economic resilience and reform efforts. The envoy reaffirmed China's continued support for Pakistan, particularly in trade and investment.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war 'way ahead of schedule', doubts deal despite claims of talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the conflict with Iran was progressing "way ahead of schedule" but expressed doubt about reaching a deal, stating he would "see if they want to do it."

stories.title: British police release on bail men arrested over Jewish ambulance attack
stories.summary: British police released on bail men arrested in connection with an attack on Jewish ambulances in the UK. The attack targeted ambulances operated by Hatzola, a volunteer emergency medical organization.

stories.title: US plans 'final blow' against Iran as Trump demands Tehran make a deal
stories.summary: The US Department of War is reportedly drafting plans for a 'final blow' against Iran, with options including seizing Iranian islands or capturing oil tankers, as President Trump pressures Tehran to negotiate a deal.

stories.title: Senate reportedly makes progress on DHS funding deal amid turmoil at US airports – live
stories.summary: US Senate leaders reportedly made progress on a Department of Homeland Security funding deal amid widespread airport disruptions caused by unpaid security staff. The Pentagon is also reportedly preparing plans for a potential escalation in the Iran war, including possible ground troop deployment.

stories.title: High-level meeting chaired by president stresses national consensus, institutional coordination amid regional volatility
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari chaired a meeting at Aiwan-i-Sadr in Islamabad with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir. The meeting emphasized national consensus and institutional coordination in response to regional challenges stemming from the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Tensions build in Lebanon as Hezbollah targets church, some close doors to displaced Shi'ites
stories.summary: Tensions are rising in Lebanon after Hezbollah reportedly targeted a church. Some Lebanese communities have closed their doors to displaced Shi'ite civilians. A Lebanese media source denied that soldiers had taken refuge in the church.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Baltic energy blitz: KINEF refinery struck as Kyiv targets Russia’s northwestern export corridor
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's KINEF refinery in Kirishi as part of a broader campaign targeting Baltic energy export infrastructure, following recent attacks on facilities at Ust-Luga and Primorsk.

stories.title: Russia says report it is sending drones to Iran 'lies'
stories.summary: The Kremlin denied a Financial Times report that Russia was close to completing a drone shipment to Iran, calling it "lies." Russia, a close ally of Iran, has denied sending military aid to Tehran since the US and Israel began attacking the country in February.

stories.title: Soaring oil prices could bring the Kremlin billions — but they still won’t fix the Russian economy
stories.summary: Rising oil prices driven by the Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz blockade could provide Russia's federal budget with additional revenue, potentially helping the Kremlin meet its deficit target. However, analysts say the windfall will not address deep structural problems in the Russian economy.

stories.title: US passengers enraged by hours-long lines and missed flights: ‘Absolutely insane’
stories.summary: US airline passengers reported hours-long security and customs lines and missed flights due to DHS staffing shortages caused by employees going weeks without pay. Some travelers said they were opting not to fly at all, calling the situation a manufactured crisis by the Trump administration.

stories.title: Trump insists Iran operations 'extremely' ahead of schedule
stories.summary: President Trump declared the Iran war "extremely" ahead of schedule during his first cabinet meeting since the conflict began nearly a month ago. He reiterated his original four-to-six-week timeline for the US-Israeli military offensive as Tehran publicly rebuffed negotiations.

stories.title: US claims 'strong signs' for deal with Iran
stories.summary: The Trump administration claimed during a cabinet meeting that there were strong signs a ceasefire deal with Iran could soon be reached. The statements came amid ongoing US-Israeli military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Details revealed of Board of Peace plan for Gaza disarmament
stories.summary: Board of Peace head Nikolay Mladenov has submitted a plan calling for the gradual disarmament of Gaza over an eight-month period. Details of the proposal have been made public.

stories.title: Ukraine could be useful in future European Security Council's work - MEP
stories.summary: A member of the European Parliament argued that Ukraine's wartime experience would be valuable to a future European Security Council, should the body be established to strengthen continental defense.

stories.title: One killed, eleven injured in Nahariya by Hezbollah rocket fire
stories.summary: Hezbollah rocket fire struck the city of Nahariya in northern Israel, killing one person and injuring eleven others. A Magen David Adom spokesperson said a man in his fifties was in critical condition.

stories.title: Israel took Iran's Araghchi, Qalibaf off hit list on Pakistan request: report
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly reviewing a 15-point proposal from US President Donald Trump, transmitted through Pakistan, aimed at ending the war. According to the report, Israel removed Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi and parliament speaker Qalibaf from its hit list at Pakistan's request.

stories.title: Nicolás Maduro appears again in New York court on ‘narco-terrorism’ charges
stories.summary: Deposed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in a Manhattan federal court for his narco-terrorism case after his capture by US military forces in January. The hearing featured arguments over whether Maduro should be allowed to use Venezuelan government funds for his legal defense. Both Maduro and his wife have pleaded not guilty.

stories.title: Pentagon reportedly weighs diverting Ukraine military aid to Middle East
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly considering redirecting military aid originally designated for Ukraine to operations in the Middle East, according to the Washington Post. The weapons under consideration include air-defense interceptor missiles procured through a NATO initiative.

stories.title: More Africans die fighting for Russia on the frontline of its war in Ukraine
stories.summary: Zimbabwe has confirmed that 15 of its nationals died fighting for Russia on the frontlines of the war in Ukraine. The country is the latest African nation to report casualties among citizens recruited to serve in the conflict.

stories.title: Israel Defence Minister claims Iran Guards navy commander killed in strike
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz claimed that Alireza Tangsiri, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy, was killed alongside other senior naval commanders in an overnight strike. Iran did not immediately acknowledge Tangsiri's death.

stories.title: Labour vows to ban trail hunting as it opens public consultation
stories.summary: The UK government announced plans to ban trail hunting, opening a public consultation on the practice. Police and animal rights activists have long accused trail hunting of being a smokescreen for illegal foxhunting.

stories.title: Zelensky to ink air security deal with Saudi Arabia on visit
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Saudi Arabia to sign an air security deal. The agreement focuses on air defence cooperation, with Ukraine sharing anti-drone expertise with Gulf states.

stories.title: Lebanese resistance music pioneer Ahmad Kaabour dies at 70
stories.summary: Lebanese resistance music pioneer Ahmad Kaabour died at age 70. He was best known for the song "Ounadikom," written as a tribute to resistance against Israel.

stories.title: Pentagon boss claims Iran now has ‘no navy, no navy leader’
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed that Iran now has "no navy, no navy leader," characterizing the war with Iran as historic in scale.

stories.title: Trump: Iran asked me to be Supreme Leader, but I said no thanks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed that Iran asked him to serve as the country's Supreme Leader, an assertion he said he declined. The remark was made amid a series of controversial statements during the Iran war.

stories.title: DPM Dar says US-Iran ‘indirect talks’ taking place through messages being relayed by Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar confirmed that indirect talks between the United States and Iran are being conducted through messages relayed by Pakistan. Dar stated that the U.S. has shared 15 points currently being deliberated by Iran.

stories.title: National Security Council advises Israelis abroad to avoid public Passover events during Iran war
stories.summary: Israel's National Security Council advised Israeli citizens abroad to avoid public Passover gatherings during the Iran conflict, citing recent attacks in Belgium and the Netherlands as evidence of heightened threats.

stories.title: Revolutionary find: Hoard of century old gold coins discovered under a house in western Russia
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered a hoard of pre-revolution gold coins beneath a house in western Russia. The 10-ruble coins, approximately 90% gold, have an estimated total melt value of around half a million dollars.

stories.title: Iran War tests European unity amid German economic slowdown and fears over Ukraine support
stories.summary: EU member states remain divided in their stance on the Iran conflict as Europe faces economic slowdown and rising energy prices. Germany fears that opposing US-Israel actions could prompt Washington to withdraw support for Ukraine, while the war threatens to further damage its already struggling economy.

stories.title: Man who murdered pregnant girlfriend has 42-year term increased to whole-life order
stories.summary: The UK Court of Appeal increased Shaine March's sentence to a whole-life order for murdering his pregnant girlfriend Alana Odysseos in Walthamstow, east London, in July 2025. March, who had been released on licence after killing a teenager in 2000, inflicted 23 stab wounds on the 32-year-old victim.

stories.title: Iran Is Putting a ‘Toll Booth’ in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has imposed selective passage controls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, effectively operating a toll system on the critical waterway. Some vessels are reportedly being allowed through based on payments or alignment with Tehran's interests.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ‘lousy fighters but great negotiators’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump described Iran as "lousy fighters but great negotiators" and stated that Tehran is "begging to make a deal" amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: G7 meets in France to mend rupture with US on Middle East war
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers convened for a two-day meeting outside Paris to address differences with the US over the Middle East war. The gathering also covered the Ukraine and Gaza crises, as President Trump threatened to "unleash hell" if Iran rejects a deal.

stories.title: French armed forces chief held video call with 35 countries on Hormuz strait
stories.summary: France's armed forces chief General Fabien Mandon held a video conference with representatives from 35 countries to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The French defence ministry described the initiative as strictly defensive and independent of ongoing military operations.

stories.title: Russian oil tanker nears Cuba in test of US resolve on blockade
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker is approaching Cuba in what Moscow describes as a humanitarian fuel delivery, testing US enforcement of its oil blockade against Havana. The shipment comes as Cuba faces a worsening energy crisis and humanitarian disaster due to US efforts to cut off oil supplies.

stories.title: No US-Iran talks ‘appear realistic’ at the moment, senior Iranian official tells Reuters
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran reviewed a 15-point US proposal for ending the Middle East war and rejected it as "one-sided and unfair," saying it served only US and Israeli interests.

stories.title: Fact check: Imran’s son Kasim did not demand the suspension of Pakistan’s GSP+ status at UNHRC
stories.summary: Claims circulating on social media that Kasim Khan, son of imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan, demanded the suspension of Pakistan's GSP+ trade status at the UNHRC were found to be false by iVerify Pakistan. Multiple PML-N supporters and media outlets shared two misleading videos since March 25.

stories.title: Iran Guards navy commander Alireza Tangsiri killed in strike
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed IRGC Navy commander Alireza Tangsiri, with the U.S. confirming his death. The strike further escalated tensions in the ongoing war against Iran.

stories.title: REPLAY: US President Donald Trump holds cabinet meeting
stories.summary: During a White House cabinet meeting, President Trump urged Iran to abandon its nuclear ambitions and accept a deal to end US and Israeli bombing. Trump warned of continued strikes if Tehran does not agree to a new diplomatic path forward.

stories.title: Golan resident convicted of spying for Iran after passing tank movement, missile-impact data
stories.summary: A resident of the Israeli-controlled Golan Heights was convicted of espionage for Iran after passing information about tank movements and missile-impact locations. The court rejected claims that his confessions were obtained under improper pressure by Shin Bet and police.

stories.title: Zelenskyy lands in Saudi Arabia, taking Ukraine’s drone war experience to the Gulf and pitching air defense cooperation across six countries
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Saudi Arabia on March 26 to meet with Gulf leaders, aiming to discuss drone warfare experience and air defense cooperation across multiple countries.

stories.title: Ahmed Fouad Alkhatib: Hamas triggered the Iran war. Now it may outlast the Islamic Republic
stories.summary: Ahmed Fouad Alkhatib, head of Realign for Palestine, commented on the Board of Peace's disarmament principles, arguing that Hamas triggered the Iran war but may ultimately outlast the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: Houthis threaten to join Mideast war, raising specter of renewed Red Sea attacks
stories.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement threatened to join the broader Middle East war, raising the possibility of renewed attacks on shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical chokepoint near the Suez Canal already strained by the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Tehran’s’tollbooth’: How Iran picks who to let through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has blocked vessel passage through the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting an estimated 20 percent of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies transiting the waterway.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces repel four-direction Russian assault in Kostiantynivka
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces successfully repelled a combined Russian assault launched from four directions in Kostiantynivka, a city in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Hegseth prays at Pentagon service for ‘overwhelming violence’ against enemies
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth prayed during a Pentagon worship service for "overwhelming violence of action" against enemies. The Christian service, held before military and civilian personnel, was Hegseth's first since the Iran war began.

stories.title: Somalia football slowly becomes a women's game
stories.summary: Women's football is gaining unprecedented public support in Somalia, with hundreds of spectators attending matches between young women's teams at a stadium in Mogadishu. The development marks a significant cultural shift in the conservative, conflict-affected country.

stories.title: Arizona gun dealer accused of selling firearms to two Mexican cartels
stories.summary: Arizona-based licensed gun dealer Laurence Gray was charged with attempting to provide material support to terrorist organizations after allegedly selling rifles and firearms to two Mexican cartels. The case comes amid longstanding Mexican government pressure on the US to curb the flow of weapons across the border.

stories.title: West Bank Palestinians face Israel's interceptor debris with no protection
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank are being struck by debris from Israeli interceptor missiles without access to sirens or shelters, while nearby settlements are protected by the Iron Dome system. Towns near Hebron have been hit by deadly shrapnel.

stories.title: Cubans face darkest hour as US blockade strangles island
stories.summary: Cuba is facing severe shortages as a U.S. blockade tightens around the island. Solidarity flotillas are delivering emergency supplies to Havana as Cubans brace for further escalation.

stories.title: PMD forecasts isolated rain, thunderstorms in Karachi over next three days
stories.summary: The Pakistan Meteorological Department forecast partly cloudy weather for Karachi with chances of thunderstorms and rain on March 26 and 28. A westerly wave is affecting most of the country, with Karachi's maximum temperature expected to reach 30–32°C and humidity around 45–55 per cent.

stories.title: Senegal appeals to get AFCON title from Morocco at CAS
stories.summary: Senegal filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport after the Confederation of African Football stripped the country of its Africa Cup of Nations title and awarded it to Morocco following a disputed ruling over a controversial final.

stories.title: MBDA to double Aster air-defense missile output in 2026
stories.summary: European missile manufacturer MBDA announced plans to double production of its Aster family of air-defense missiles by 2026. The Aster missiles are used in the SAMP/T air-defense system, which is the only European-made counterpart to the U.S. Patriot system.

stories.title: Fighting may intensify in Kupiansk, Southern Slobozhanshchyna sectors – National Guard Spokesman
stories.summary: A Ukrainian National Guard spokesman warned that Russian forces remain active along certain front-line sectors, with potential intensification expected in the Kupiansk and Southern Slobozhanshchyna areas as warmer weather arrives.

stories.title: European NATO defense spending rose by almost 20% in 2025
stories.summary: European NATO members and Canada collectively raised defense spending by 19.6% in 2025, matching the previous year's growth rate. Germany's defense budget reached 2.4% of GDP, a notable increase for a country long criticized for sluggish military spending.

stories.title: ‘Jury’s still out’ on future of Army’s mobile prepositioned stock: AMC head
stories.summary: The head of U.S. Army Materiel Command said the future of the Army's mobile prepositioned stock program remains uncertain. So far, the Army has offloaded equipment from its APS-3 afloat prepositioned stocks to bases in South Korea and the Philippines.

stories.title: Pakistan says it is mediating US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan announced it is mediating indirect talks between the United States and Iran with the aim of ending the ongoing war between the two countries.

stories.title: Hungary to block gas transit to Ukraine from July
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ordered a halt to natural gas transit through Hungary to Ukraine starting in July, potentially disrupting one of Kyiv's energy supply routes.

stories.title: Why was a £1.5bn Chinese plan to invest in a Highland yard blocked?
stories.summary: The UK government blocked a £1.5 billion proposal by Chinese company Ming Yang to build a wind turbine manufacturing plant at the Ardersier port facility in the Scottish Highlands.

stories.title: Venezuela's Maduro back in US court after stunning capture
stories.summary: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro made his second court appearance in New York following his capture by US forces in a nighttime raid. Maduro, who led Venezuela since 2013, faces charges as the oil-rich country increasingly falls under US pressure from President Trump.

stories.title: Israel says it has killed Iran's navy chief overseeing Strait of Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Israel's defence minister said a number of other "senior Navy command officials" have also been killed. Iran has not yet commented.

stories.title: Kremlin Denies Report It’s Sending Iran Attack Drones
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov denied reports that Russia is sending attack drones to Iran, calling the claims "fake." The denial addresses allegations of military drone shipments from Moscow to Tehran.

stories.title: Iran war is a test the Gulf cannot afford to fail
stories.summary: A drone attack struck Kuwait City in March 2026 as analysts warn the Iran war threatens to destabilize Gulf states economically and militarily, potentially rendering the region inhospitable to future industries.

stories.title: Ukraine ready for full membership in Joint Expeditionary Force – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine, currently an enhanced partner in the Joint Expeditionary Force, is prepared to become a full member of the UK-led multinational military coalition.

stories.title: Nigeria: Why We Promised Support for Soldier Accused of N114 Million Fraud - Abia Govt
stories.summary: The Abia State Government in Nigeria said Governor Alex Otti's earlier promises of support to a soldier now accused of N114 million fraud were made on compassionate grounds, before the fraud allegations emerged.

stories.title: Uganda: Kampala Youth Pledge Individual Responsibility in Climate Change Fight
stories.summary: Young people in Kampala, Uganda, pledged individual responsibility in addressing climate change during a youth climate governance dialogue. The event brought together international students, media professionals, local leaders, and environmental advocates to develop practical solutions.

stories.title: Nigeria: Ondo Community Petitions Aiyedatiwa Over Abandoned World Bank Projects
stories.summary: Leaders of the Yaba Community in Idanre, Ondo State, Nigeria, petitioned Governor Aiyedatiwa over the alleged abandonment and mismanagement of World Bank-funded projects worth billions of naira in their area.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Orders Arrest of Turaki, Factional PDP Chairman
stories.summary: A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory in Abuja, Nigeria, issued a bench warrant for the arrest of Kabiru Turaki, a Senior Advocate and factional National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda Urges De-Escalation Amid Middle East Tensions
stories.summary: Rwanda called for de-escalation of hostilities in the Middle East, emphasizing civilian protection, respect for state sovereignty, and renewed diplomatic efforts to prevent further bloodshed.

stories.title: Meloni vows to boost cooperation with Algeria on gas deliveries
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni pledged to strengthen gas cooperation with Algeria during a meeting aimed at increasing deliveries. Italy is seeking to fill supply gaps caused by limited options for replacing lost LNG imports amid broader energy disruptions.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia PM Dismisses Two State Ministers in Cabinet Reshuffle
stories.summary: Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre dismissed two state ministers in a cabinet reshuffle aimed at improving government performance. The move was announced through an official statement from the prime minister's office in Mogadishu.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda Military Chief Says Country Would Join War If Israel Faces Defeat
stories.summary: Uganda's military chief stated that while the country seeks an end to the Middle East conflict, Uganda would side with Israel if it faced defeat. The remarks signal Kampala's alignment with Israel amid ongoing regional hostilities.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Govt Launches $552m Programme to Reform Basic Education
stories.summary: Nigeria's government launched a $552 million education reform programme supported by the World Bank and the Global Partnership for Education. The initiative aims to benefit over 29 million children, train 500,000 teachers, and deliver 13,000 new classrooms nationwide.

stories.title: UAE envoy to US says ‘ceasefire not enough’ and calls for escalation in Iran war
stories.summary: UAE Ambassador to the U.S. Yousef al-Otaiba wrote in the Wall Street Journal that a ceasefire in the Iran war is insufficient, calling instead for a "conclusive outcome" against Tehran and framing the UAE as being on the conflict's front line.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis warn of 'military response' to US-Israeli attacks if required
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi warned in a televised statement that the group would launch a "military response" to US-Israeli attacks if required by Iran, pledging to "repay loyalty with loyalty."

stories.title: Can Donald Trump end his war on Iran in time for rescheduled China trip?
stories.summary: Chinese analysts suggest Donald Trump's rescheduled visit to China on May 14-15 may reveal the U.S. road map for ending the war with Iran. The trip was delayed from late March so Trump could focus on the conflict. China has not yet confirmed the dates.

stories.title: Knife-wielding man kills woman at Tokyo Pokemon shop before taking his own life
stories.summary: A man armed with a knife fatally stabbed a woman in her 20s, believed to be an employee, at a Pokemon store inside the Sunshine City shopping center in downtown Tokyo before killing himself. Police responded after receiving an emergency call.

stories.title: 'Toppling a regime is an art, not a science,' security sources say on Iran - exclusive
stories.summary: Security sources disclosed that Mossad Director David Barnea launched an AI-driven intelligence overhaul in 2021, which they say could eventually support efforts to destabilize the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Zelensky: Pressure on Russia insufficient from both U.S. and Europe
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the West is not putting enough pressure on Russia and warned of the risk of diminishing international support for Ukraine as attention shifts to escalating tensions in the Middle East.

stories.title: France sets up ‘urgent’ $9.8B munitions top-up package
stories.summary: France announced a €9.8 billion emergency munitions procurement package to replenish military stockpiles. Paris also plans to create a new platform called France Munitions, which will serve as a centralized wholesale buyer of weapons for both the French Armed Forces and export clients.

stories.title: Ghana: IGP Deploys Reinforcement to Nkwanta After Violent Attacks
stories.summary: Ghana's Inspector General of Police deployed additional security personnel to Nkwanta in the Oti Region following renewed violent attacks in the area.

stories.title: US said mulling ‘final blow’ options if Iran talks fail, including sending troops to seize key assets
stories.summary: According to an Axios report, the U.S. is considering "final blow" military options against Iran if negotiations fail, including seizing islands in the Strait of Hormuz, blockading Iranian oil shipments, and sending troops to capture Iran's stockpile of 60-percent enriched uranium.

stories.title: UAE envoy to US says ‘ceasefire not enough’ and calls for escalation in Iran war
stories.summary: UAE Ambassador to the US Yousef al-Otaiba stated that a ceasefire with Iran would be insufficient and called for escalation in the conflict. Analysts warned the stance could antagonize Tehran while seeking favor with Washington's hardliners.

stories.title: Nigeria takes its place on world stage in quest to become regional superpower
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu visited the United Kingdom for a state visit as both nations seek to strengthen trade and economic ties. King Charles acknowledged painful chapters in the countries' shared history amid growing calls from African and Caribbean nations for reparative justice.

stories.title: Pakistan continuing military operations against Afghanistan
stories.summary: Renewed military clashes along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border have killed civilians and heightened tensions after a ceasefire between the Taliban and Pakistani forces expired.

stories.title: Iran awaiting response from US after responding to plan via intermediaries
stories.summary: Iran responded through unnamed intermediaries to a 15-point U.S. proposal to end the war, conveyed via Pakistan. Tehran's state news agency Tasnim reported that Iran is now awaiting Washington's reply.

stories.title: Iranian American Leila Namvar runs for California Assembly
stories.summary: Iranian American candidate Leila Namvar is running for the California State Assembly in District 47, currently held by Republican Greg Wallace.

stories.title: Navy nixes MASC program, unveils new MUSV ‘marketplace’ amid Golden Fleet push
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy has canceled its MASC program and announced a new medium unmanned surface vessel marketplace as part of its Golden Fleet initiative. The replacement effort will prioritize production-ready, mission-capable platforms with potential deliveries beginning in fiscal year 2027.

stories.title: Muzychuk: Russians deploy up to 200 “Molniia” drones daily in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian National Guard units reported that Russian forces are deploying up to 200 "Molniia" drones per day in the Pokrovsk direction on the eastern front line.

stories.title: Can France really broker peace between Israel and Lebanon?
stories.summary: France is pursuing a diplomatic initiative to broker peace between Israel and Lebanon, but faces questions about the limits of its influence amid the rising costs of the conflict.

stories.title: Iraq caught between US and Iran, facing attacks from both warring sides & Iran-aligned actors within
stories.summary: Iraq finds itself caught between the US and Iran as the war between the two increasingly unfolds on Iraqi territory. Chatham House researcher Hayder Al-Shakeri described Iraq's position as structurally constrained by economic dependence, security arrangements, and geographic ties to both Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Middle East conflict and fuel prices: Who is the Pakistani govt really protecting?
stories.summary: Global oil prices have risen approximately 50 per cent since the US-Israel war with Iran began on February 28. Pakistan's government raised regulated petroleum product prices by 20 per cent, or Rs55 per litre, leading to higher transport fares and rising food prices across the country.

stories.title: REPLAY: NATO Secretary General annual report for 2025
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte reported that European allies and Canada increased defense spending by 20% in real terms in 2025. Rutte urged members to continue toward the 5% spending objective ahead of the next NATO summit in Ankara.

stories.title: Go to sleep in France, wake up in Germany: Paris-Berlin night train restarts
stories.summary: A Paris-to-Berlin overnight sleeper train service is being relaunched by a new operator. The route was previously revived by SNCF in 2023 after nearly a decade but ceased operations in December 2025.

stories.title: Iran, US harden positions as Tehran tightens grip on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran and the United States reached an impasse over negotiations as both sides escalated tensions in the Middle East. Washington deployed thousands of additional troops toward the region while Tehran tightened control over the Strait of Hormuz. Sirens sounded across Israel amid Iranian missile barrages, and Gulf nations attempted intercepts as heavy strikes hit Tehran and other Iranian cities.

stories.title: War in the Mideast: Iranian cluster ballistic missiles test Israel’s defences
stories.summary: Iran has deployed cluster ballistic missiles against Israeli civilian areas, introducing a new challenge for Israel's air-defense systems. Unlike conventional single-warhead missiles, these munitions release hundreds of submunitions that can turn neighborhoods into minefields long after impact. FRANCE 24 reported on how this banned weapon type is testing the limits of Israeli defenses during the escalating regional conflict.

stories.title: NATO's European allies and Canada boosted military spending by 20% in 2025
stories.summary: A NATO report released Thursday showed that European allies and Canada increased military spending by 20 percent in 2025. The boost follows sustained pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump for NATO members to raise defense expenditures. Alliance leaders agreed at a summit last year to reach 5 percent of GDP on defense and related investments by 2035.

stories.title: In Lebanon, paramedics mourn their own killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: In the southern Lebanese town of Nabatieh, paramedics gathered to bury colleagues Ali Jaber and Joud Sleiman, who were killed in an Israeli strike on Tuesday. According to Lebanon's health ministry, the two were on a rescue mission riding a clearly marked ambulance motorcycle and wearing paramedic uniforms when they were hit.

stories.title: Chelyabinsk Judge Bans Distribution of Oscar-Winning ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ in Russia
stories.summary: A judge in Chelyabinsk, Russia, banned the distribution of the Oscar-winning documentary 'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' after the state prosecutor's office requested its removal from three online video platforms.

stories.title: Nigeria’s return to Windsor castle signals new era in UK economic partnership
stories.summary: Nigeria's delegation visited Windsor Castle for the first time in nearly four decades, signaling a diplomatic reset and expanded economic partnership with the United Kingdom. Separately, investors in Uganda are shifting toward Treasury yields of up to 18%.

stories.title: Australia urged to swap diesel for electric buses as fuel costs soar
stories.summary: Transport advocates in Australia are urging a faster rollout of electric buses as diesel prices exceed $3 per litre amid fuel security concerns from the Iran war. Electric buses currently make up just 1% of Australia's fleet, compared with 80% of urban buses in China.

stories.title: Australian petrol stations report 25% surge in demand as governments plan for ‘biggest energy crisis in history’
stories.summary: Australian petrol stations have reported a 25% surge in fuel demand over two weeks amid the Iran war's impact on global energy supplies. Hundreds of retailers have reported being without one or more fuel types, putting pressure on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to develop a national energy crisis plan.

stories.title: Ukraine barters with Gulf states: Patriot missiles for anti-drone capabilities
stories.summary: Ukraine is exploring exchanges with Gulf states, offering anti-drone expertise in return for Patriot missile systems. Ukrainian anti-drone specialists have already been deployed to at least six countries.

stories.title: Israel extends Al-Aqsa Mosque closure until mid-April
stories.summary: Israeli authorities extended the closure of Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem until mid-April. Palestinians have warned of escalating restrictions at the holy site.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi meets frontline commanders on “hot” southern fronts
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief General Oleksandr Syrskyi visited the Southern Operational Zone and met with frontline unit commanders to discuss improving conditions and planning further military actions.

stories.title: Air Canada chief apologizes after English-only message to plane crash victims
stories.summary: Air Canada CEO Michael Rousseau apologized after his condolence message to victims of a deadly plane crash in New York was delivered almost entirely in English. The four-minute video included only two French words, prompting criticism from Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Quebec officials, with some calling for his resignation.

stories.title: The military’s fabled ‘human in the loop’ for AI is dangerously misleading
stories.summary: Mikey Dickerson argues that the concept of a "human in the loop" in military AI systems is misleading and insufficient as a safeguard. He contends that a human whose only role is to approve a machine's recommendations represents a design failure rather than meaningful oversight.

stories.title: State asks High Court to reject challenge to anti-UNRWA laws ahead of Monday hearing
stories.summary: Israel's state attorney asked the High Court to reject a legal challenge to two laws passed by the Knesset in October 2024 that restrict UNRWA operations. One of the laws bars UNRWA activity in sovereign Israeli territory, with a hearing scheduled for Monday.

stories.title: US and Israel vote against UN resolution recognising slavery as 'gravest' crime against humanity
stories.summary: The United States and Israel voted against a UN resolution, tabled by Ghana, recognizing the African slave trade as the "gravest" crime against humanity. European states and Japan abstained from the vote.

stories.title: 2 bid-rigging syndicates ‘potentially linked’ to estate destroyed in Tai Po fire
stories.summary: At least two bid-rigging syndicates may be linked to a HK$336 million renovation contract for a Hong Kong housing estate destroyed in the territory's deadliest fire in decades. The Competition Commission revealed the potential connection during an evidential hearing.

stories.title: UK authorises military to board Russian shadow fleet tankers
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer authorized the military to board and detain Russian ships believed to be part of Moscow's shadow fleet used to export oil in violation of Western sanctions. The decision aligns with broader European efforts to disrupt Russia's sanction-evading tanker network that funds its war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Social media platform X back up after brief international outage
stories.summary: Social media platform X experienced a brief international outage on Thursday afternoon. Internet monitor NetBlocks confirmed the disruption was not related to country-level filtering. Downdetector recorded a sharp spike in user-reported problems in Pakistan, with issues primarily affecting the timeline and other features.

stories.title: Arab-Israeli educator Suleiman Suleiman advocates shared responsibility and coexistence
stories.summary: Suleiman Suleiman, CEO of the organization Atidna, called for strengthened cooperation between Arab and Jewish communities in Israel, emphasizing education as the foundation for coexistence.

stories.title: Drone Hits Turkish Tanker Carrying Russian Oil in Black Sea
stories.summary: The Sierra Leone-flagged tanker Altura was struck by a drone in the Black Sea after departing Russia's port of Novorossiysk carrying approximately one million barrels of crude oil. The vessel was carrying Russian oil at the time of the attack.

stories.title: US deploys 82nd Airborne as Trump warns Iran to pursue diplomacy or face force
stories.summary: The US deployed the 82nd Airborne Division and two amphibious ready groups to the region as President Trump warned Iran to pursue diplomacy or face military force. Experts say the buildup targets Iranian strategic interests.

stories.title: Russian officials meet US counterparts as Moscow denies aiding Iran
stories.summary: Russian officials held talks with U.S. counterparts while the Kremlin denied aiding Iran. A Kremlin spokesperson described the discussions as "necessary dialogue" with Washington as the war in Ukraine continues.

stories.title: SDA hopes to bring satellite laser links into use within next 6 months
stories.summary: The Space Development Agency is taking a strategic pause in launching its Tranche 1 data-relay and missile-tracking satellites to resolve technical issues found in the 42 satellites already in orbit. SDA Director GP Sandhoo indicated the agency hopes to bring satellite laser communication links into operational use within the next six months.

stories.title: UK blocks China wind turbine project on ‘national security’ amid tense business climate
stories.summary: Britain blocked a £1.5 billion plan by Chinese clean energy company Mingyang to build the UK's largest wind turbine factory in Scotland, citing national security concerns. Analysts said the decision likely resulted from U.S. pressure, despite the energy crisis from the Iran war raising hopes for the project.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine could produce 2,000 interceptor drones daily with sufficient funding
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has the capacity to produce 2,000 interceptor drones per day if sufficient funding is provided. The claim underscores Kyiv's growing domestic defense-production ambitions.

stories.title: EU greenlights controversial mandate to deport refugees
stories.summary: The European Union has approved a bloc-wide mandate aimed at streamlining deportation procedures, expanding policing powers, and establishing dedicated deportation centers for refugees.

stories.title: Iranian naval chief killed in attack, Israel says
stories.summary: Israel announced it killed IRGC naval commander Alireza Tangsiri in a strike near Bandar Abbas, close to the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Teen volunteer paramedic killed in Israeli strike in Lebanon
stories.summary: A 15-year-old volunteer paramedic was killed along with a colleague in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon.

stories.title: Russia bans Oscar-winning film 'Mr Nobody Against Putin'
stories.summary: A Russian court banned the Oscar-winning documentary "Mr Nobody Against Putin," alleging it promoted negative attitudes toward the Russian government and the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Damage in Israel from Iranian attacks
stories.summary: Video footage showed damage across several Israeli cities resulting from Iranian attacks.

stories.title: Major Oil Refinery in Leningrad Region Reportedly Damaged in Ukrainian Drone Strike
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Leningrad region reported damage to an industrial site in the Kirishky district following a Ukrainian drone strike. The district hosts the Kirishinefteorgsintez oil refinery, one of Russia's major refining facilities.

stories.title: Army commander convicted of Guinea stadium massacre dies in prison
stories.summary: Aboubacar Sidiki Diakité, a Guinean army commander convicted for his role in the 2009 stadium massacre in Conakry that killed more than 150 people, has died in prison.

stories.title: ‘My phone is a brick’: Russians scramble for information as data blocked
stories.summary: Russian authorities imposed data blackouts citing security concerns as Ukrainian drones continued to strike, leaving citizens scrambling for information.

stories.title: Israel bombs Gaza camps, forcibly expels Jerusalem families
stories.summary: An explosion in a Gaza camp killed one person and wounded seven others. Meanwhile, Israeli authorities continued forcible expulsions of Palestinian families in East Jerusalem.

stories.title: US delaying Iran ceasefire for one key reason - analysis
stories.summary: Analysis suggests the US is delaying a ceasefire with Iran based on a strategic calculation guiding behind-the-scenes decisions. Former Israeli National Security Adviser Eyal Hulata noted that Trump's conduct is difficult to interpret but purposeful.

stories.title: Heavy downpour floods roads in Egypt
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall struck several parts of Egypt, including New Cairo, flooding roads across the country. Local authorities warned of two days of continued heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms, strong winds, and lower temperatures.

stories.title: Trump eyes China deal, but dragging out talks risks backlash, warns former diplomat
stories.summary: Former US Deputy Secretary of State Stephen Biegun said President Trump is seeking an economic deal with China during a planned Beijing visit. Biegun warned that if Beijing drags out trade negotiations too long, Trump could adopt a much tougher stance against China.

stories.title: DJI unveils its first 360-degree drone amid patent dispute with crosstown rival Insta360
stories.summary: Chinese drone manufacturer DJI launched its first 360-degree drone, the DJI Avata 360, featuring an 8K omnidirectional camera. The product directly challenges domestic rival Insta360 amid an escalating patent dispute between the two Shenzhen-based companies.

stories.title: Trump: Iran ‘begging’ for deal as pressure mounts on Tehran
stories.summary: President Trump claimed on Truth Social that Iran is "begging" for a deal as pressure mounts on Tehran. He described the Iranian delegation as "strange" and asserted that Iran has been "militarily obliterated" with no chance of recovery.

stories.title: Sanctioned Russian shadow fleet tanker struck by drone near Istanbul, 140,000 tons of oil on board
stories.summary: A drone struck the sanctioned Russian shadow-fleet tanker ALTURA near Istanbul while it was carrying approximately 140,000 tons of oil. The vessel had previously transported millions of barrels of Russian crude to India and China.

stories.title: Is Europe heading to an energy crisis?
stories.summary: Europe is bracing for an energy supply crunch and price shock as the ongoing Iran conflict disrupts global energy markets.

stories.title: Zelensky: EU will resolve issue of granting Ukraine loan
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is awaiting the release of a €90 billion EU loan or an alternative financing mechanism. The funds are intended to support Ukraine's military operations.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia stoic amid Iran war, but attacks on Red Sea ports could change that
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has maintained a restrained stance during the Iran war, but experts warn that any Iranian attack on the Bab al-Mandeb Strait — Riyadh's remaining oil export shipping route — would likely trigger an immediate Saudi retaliation.

stories.title: 2 men released on bail after arson attack on London Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: Two men were released on bail in London after being arrested for an arson attack on Jewish community ambulances. Police said the suspects face strict conditions and the incident is being investigated as an antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: Volkswagen in talks to make Iron Dome parts at struggling German auto plant: report
stories.summary: Volkswagen is reportedly in discussions to manufacture components for Israel's Iron Dome air-defense system at an underperforming German automotive plant. The move reflects a broader trend of European automakers pivoting toward defense production as the German auto industry faces significant economic challenges.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires over 600 times at Israel, IDF troops over last 24 hours
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched over 600 attacks on Israel and IDF forces within a 24-hour period. Analysts suggest the surge in attacks may be aimed at pressuring Israel and the US into agreeing to a ceasefire on all fronts.

stories.title: Domestic helper held over death of baby found in rubbish bin at Hong Kong plaza
stories.summary: A 34-year-old Indonesian domestic helper was arrested in Hong Kong on suspicion of concealing a child's birth. A newborn boy with his umbilical cord still attached was found by a cleaner in a rubbish bin at Lee Theatre Plaza in Causeway Bay and was later declared dead at hospital.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Mar. 26 – Premature ceasefire will not neutralize Iran’s potent threat
stories.summary: Times of Israel editor David Horovitz discussed U.S. efforts to initiate high-level negotiations with Iran, warning that a premature ceasefire could fail to neutralize Iran's threat to the region and the world.

stories.title: US war in Iran: China casts itself as savior of SE Asia
stories.summary: Beijing is positioning itself as a more reliable partner for Southeast Asian nations as the US-Israeli war with Iran drives fuel prices higher across the region. China is leveraging the crisis to contrast its stability with Washington's military engagements.

stories.title: The limits of military might: Thoughts on the wars in Iran, Lebanon, and Gaza - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that military force in the conflicts involving Iran, Lebanon, and Gaza can weaken adversaries but cannot eliminate them or resolve the underlying disputes driving the violence.

stories.title: Iranian press review: Reports of US backchannel to Ghalibaf cause backlash in Tehran
stories.summary: Reports of a U.S. backchannel to Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf sparked a political backlash in Tehran. Meanwhile, Iranian cancer patients face treatment difficulties and opposition figures have condemned attacks on national infrastructure.

stories.title: Video: GCC chief says Iran charging for ships to pass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: GCC Secretary-General Jasem al-Budaiwi accused Iran of charging fees for ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, effectively imposing a toll on maritime traffic.

stories.title: Defense forces halt major Russian offensive in Pokrovsk area
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported halting a major Russian offensive near the city of Pokrovsk in eastern Ukraine. No further details on casualties or territorial changes were provided.

stories.title: China’s CNOOC to boost oil and gas output amid Middle East strife
stories.summary: China National Offshore Oil Corporation announced plans to further boost oil and gas production in 2025 amid geopolitical tensions. The state-backed company reported an 11.5 percent drop in net profit to 122.08 billion yuan despite record-high production volumes, owing to low oil prices.

stories.title: Palestinian prisoners' families fear Israel's death penalty law
stories.summary: Families of Palestinian prisoners have expressed fear over Israel's proposed death penalty legislation. One mother told reporters she now worries her imprisoned son could face execution.

stories.title: Trump stays popular in Philippines despite Iran war fuel crisis
stories.summary: Despite an energy crisis in the Philippines driven by the US-Israel war on Iran, Filipino public opinion remains largely favorable toward President Trump. Public anger has instead focused on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s administration for failing to control soaring fuel prices across the archipelago.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed in Hezbollah gunfight; terror group fires rockets, drones at north
stories.summary: An IDF soldier was killed in a gunfight with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, while the group fired rockets and drones at northern Israel. Separately, an 11-year-old girl was in serious condition after suffering heart failure during a rocket attack, and 15 troops were hospitalized with suspected hypothermia.

stories.title: ‘We’ll go 40%’: Army wants good-enough tech it can reshape for battle
stories.summary: The commander of the U.S. Army's 4th Infantry Division stated the service prefers fielding technology at roughly 40 percent maturity that can be adapted and refined during operations. The approach prioritizes speed of deployment over perfection, embracing good-enough solutions that can be reshaped for battlefield conditions.

stories.title: Israel says IRGC Navy’s commander, other chiefs killed; Qalibaf said removed from hit list
stories.summary: Israel confirmed it killed IRGC Navy commander Alireza Tangsiri and other senior Iranian military officials. Israeli authorities reportedly removed Iranian FM Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf from their target list at Pakistan's request to facilitate ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: As oil-shocked world turns to renewables, China will reap the rewards
stories.summary: The oil shock from the Iran war is accelerating global investment in renewable energy, with analysts predicting China will be the largest beneficiary. China's renewable energy exports are expected to perform strongly, offsetting costs from higher-priced oil imports.

stories.title: India sees spike in social media censorship amid Iran war
stories.summary: Activists in India are raising concerns about increased social media censorship, particularly targeting posts critical of the Indian government and its stance on the Iran war. Content removals have reportedly spiked amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: “You think of only one thing: is your person’s name there” — the Mariupol marine who came home after 1,400 days
stories.summary: Ukrainian marine Ruslan Kurtmallaiev, who defended Mariupol with the 36th Separate Brigade, was released after approximately 1,400 days in Russian captivity, including over two years in solitary confinement. He received only one letter and one phone call from family during his detention.

stories.title: Israel ramps up attacks on Iran, fearing US 'truce' deal
stories.summary: Israel has intensified strikes against Iran, with reports suggesting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is acting pre-emptively ahead of a potential US announcement of a temporary truce with Tehran.

stories.title: As a Palestinian, I stand in solidarity with the Iranian people. Here’s why
stories.summary: A Palestinian writer expressed solidarity with the Iranian people, arguing that Western promises of freedom are undermined by imperialism's pursuit of control.

stories.title: Iran to allow Malaysian vessels to pass in Strait of Hormuz: Anwar
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Iran has agreed to allow Malaysian vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Anwar said he spoke with Iranian and other regional leaders, and efforts are underway to release detained Malaysian oil tankers and their crews.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim meets Lukashenko, slams ‘pressure ​on Belarus from West’
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un met Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko in Pyongyang, where the two allies of Russia signed a friendship treaty and criticized Western pressure on Belarus.

stories.title: Netanyahu vows to seize more of Lebanon amid annexation fears
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has pledged to seize additional territory in southern Lebanon, amid calls from far-right government ministers to annex areas largely depopulated by Israel's military campaign.

stories.title: At least 15 IDF soldiers evacuated from Lebanon with hypothermia symptoms
stories.summary: At least 15 IDF soldiers operating in Lebanon were evacuated after developing hypothermia symptoms. One soldier was in moderate condition, while 14 others, including an officer, sustained light injuries.

stories.title: Meet Karin Prien, who could become Germany’s first president of Jewish descent
stories.summary: German federal minister Karin Prien, a granddaughter of Holocaust survivors, is being considered as a candidate for Germany's presidency. If selected, she would become the country's first president of Jewish descent.

stories.title: Oil prices jump 5 percent on Iran-US talks uncertainty
stories.summary: Oil prices surged approximately 5 percent amid uncertainty surrounding ongoing US-Iran negotiations, raising concerns about potential supply disruptions. Brent crude reached $107 per barrel.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Teachers Issue Ultimatum Over Pay and Conditions
stories.summary: Teachers represented by the Amalgamated Rural Teachers Union of Zimbabwe (ARTUZ) issued a petition to the government threatening industrial action. The union cited long-standing grievances over pay and working conditions.

stories.title: Namibia: Nandi-Ndaitwah Assesses Zambezi Floods As School Close, Communities Refuse to Relocate
stories.summary: Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah assessed flood conditions in the Zambezi region, where rising waters have forced school closures. Some affected communities have reportedly refused to relocate despite the flooding.

stories.title: NATO 2025 Annual Report warns energy infrastructure is primary target in any Russian attack on the Alliance
stories.summary: NATO's 2025 annual report, presented by Secretary General Mark Rutte on 26 March, identified energy infrastructure as the primary target in any potential Russian attack on the Alliance. The report noted that Russia's strikes on Ukrainian power grids informed NATO's defensive training priorities.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz floats EU-China trade deal as capitals soften on Beijing
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in parliament he could envision a future EU trade deal with China, signaling a softening European stance toward Beijing. The remarks reflect how rising trade and geopolitical tensions with Washington are prompting European capitals to reconsider their relationship with China.

stories.title: Pro-Israel Democrats decry settler violence in West Bank amid attacks on Palestinians
stories.summary: Several pro-Israel Democratic lawmakers in the US have publicly denounced escalating settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. Dozens of Israeli settlers have conducted apparently coordinated attacks, torching homes and vehicles, with at least 10 Palestinian civilians killed by settlers and police since the start of the month.

stories.title: AI rift widens as China urges boycott of top US conference over sanctions ban
stories.summary: The China Computer Federation urged Chinese researchers to boycott a major AI conference after organizers barred submissions from US-sanctioned institutions, including Huawei Technologies. The move marks a new flashpoint in deepening US-China tensions over artificial intelligence development.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine and US assess Putin's intentions to end war differently
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv and Washington differ in their assessments of Russian President Vladimir Putin's willingness to end the war. Zelenskyy argued that only additional international pressure can compel Putin to pursue peace.

stories.title: In mixed Haifa, weary residents face near-constant Iranian and Hezbollah missile fire
stories.summary: Residents of the mixed Jewish, Christian, and Muslim city of Haifa are enduring near-constant missile fire from Iran and Hezbollah. Local businesses across all communities are suffering as customers stay away.

stories.title: Venezuela’s Maduro set to again appear in US court: How strong is the case?
stories.summary: Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is scheduled to appear in a U.S. court on March 26 for a second hearing since his abduction by U.S. military forces on January 3.

stories.title: Egypt's Cairo businesses hit with energy crunch amid Iran war
stories.summary: Egypt announced energy-saving measures to reduce natural gas consumption as its ongoing energy crisis worsens due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Businesses in Cairo are being affected by the energy crunch.

stories.title: Octopus reports sharp rise in solar panel sales since start of Iran war
stories.summary: UK energy company Octopus Energy reported a 54 per cent increase in solar panel sales this month compared to the same period last month, driven by the Iran war's impact on oil prices. Good Energy also reported a doubling of consumer interest in solar installations following the latest energy price shock.

stories.title: EU advances trade deal with US with safeguards - Europe live
stories.summary: The European Union advanced a trade deal with the United States that includes safeguards, following months of delays over tariff legality concerns. Separately, President Trump criticized NATO allies on social media for doing "absolutely nothing" to support the US campaign in Iran.

stories.title: Libya tows damaged Russian LNG tanker from its coast
stories.summary: Libya's coast guard towed a damaged Russian LNG tanker away from the shores near Zuwara after a drone attack. Mediterranean nations have raised concerns about potential environmental risks from the incident.

stories.title: Ukraine struggles to find more NATO donors to pay for US weapons, Bloombeg reports
stories.summary: Ukraine is struggling to secure additional NATO allies willing to fund purchases of U.S. weapons. Only a few countries currently contribute, with the UK being the latest donor. Kyiv estimates it needs $15 billion in 2026 but received just $4.3 billion for 2025, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: Libya, Iran, and the Limits of Airpower
stories.summary: An analysis examines the 2011 NATO air campaign in Libya as a lens for understanding the constraints of airpower in the current Middle East situation. The piece highlights the difficult strategic choices facing U.S. President Donald Trump regarding military options involving Iran.

stories.title: Malaysia says its tankers allowed through Hormuz
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister announced that Iranian authorities have permitted Malaysian oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz, signaling a limited easing of passage restrictions for selected vessels.

stories.title: Britain moves from sanctions lists to tanker seizures – navy can now board Russia’s shadow fleet
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has expanded its enforcement against Russia's shadow fleet beyond sanctions to include naval authority to board tankers. Approximately 75% of Russian crude exports are transported via the shadow fleet, and the UK and allies have sanctioned more than 500 vessels.

stories.title: Drone attacks sanctioned Russian oil tanker in Black Sea – media
stories.summary: A drone struck the oil tanker Altura in the Black Sea approximately 14 miles from the Bosporus strait. The Altura is subject to sanctions by the EU, Switzerland, Ukraine, and the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Iran to Lebanon: Four million people displaced by US-Israeli war
stories.summary: According to reports, approximately three million Iranians and at least one million Lebanese have been displaced from their homes as a result of US-Israeli military attacks on both countries.

stories.title: Finland’s president says Ukraine talks may be at ‘end of the road’
stories.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said he fears US-led Ukraine peace talks may have reached a dead end. Stubb, who has close ties with both President Trump and President Zelensky, suggested the Iran war may be diverting attention from Ukraine negotiations, or that talks have simply stalled.

stories.title: Cape Town mayor campaigns for leadership of Democratic Alliance
stories.summary: Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis announced his campaign for the leadership of South Africa's Democratic Alliance, the second-largest party in the ruling coalition. He said he aims to build voter trust and expand the party's support base.

stories.title: Royal Navy leads NATO maritime force from German flagship; HMS Dragon in Cyprus
stories.summary: Royal Navy personnel will command one of NATO's maritime immediate response forces from a German flagship vessel. HMS Dragon, originally slated to lead the force, is no longer available and is currently deployed near Cyprus.

stories.title: At least 28 civilians killed in Sudan drone strikes
stories.summary: Drone strikes in Sudan killed at least 28 civilians in the Darfur and Kordofan regions amid the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces. The attacks have worsened the country's displacement crisis.

stories.title: China’s Pony AI to launch robotaxi service in Europe with Uber, local start-up
stories.summary: Chinese self-driving firm Pony AI announced plans to launch robotaxi services in Zagreb, Croatia, in partnership with Uber and local start-up Verne. The companies aim to operate thousands of autonomous taxis across multiple European cities in the coming years.

stories.title: Turkey, Pakistan emerge as key brokers, shaping post-war order amid Iran conflict- analysis
stories.summary: Turkey and Pakistan are positioning themselves as key mediators in the Iran conflict, seeking to ease tensions and influence the post-war regional order. Both countries are working to establish diplomatic roles amid the broader crisis.

stories.title: Russians strike Dnipro, high-rise building damaged, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro in central Ukraine, damaging a multi-story residential building. Casualties were reported, though specific numbers were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Iran rejects US ceasefire plan and submits its own | First Thing
stories.summary: Iran rejected a US ceasefire proposal and submitted its own negotiation plan, with Foreign Minister stating Tehran has no intention of negotiating for now. Intermediaries are working to keep diplomatic channels open. The conflict has killed over 1,000 people in Lebanon, more than 1,500 in Iran, and 16 in Israel, according to respective authorities.

stories.title: Ukraine drafts its first Africa strategy — targeting Maghreb and sub-Saharan states as geopolitical rivals
stories.summary: Ukraine is drafting its first comprehensive Africa strategy, targeting Maghreb and sub-Saharan states. Lieutenant General Kyrylo Budanov chaired an interagency meeting that produced a draft plan, which is now headed to the Cabinet of Ministers for approval.

stories.title: Germany warns of world economic ‘catastrophe’; OECD cuts UK growth forecast
stories.summary: European officials and the OECD have issued warnings of severe economic fallout as the war on Iran approaches its one-month mark. The OECD has cut its growth forecast for the United Kingdom amid broader concerns about global economic stability.

stories.title: Russian troops regroup and prepare for larger-scale offensive actions – Trehubov
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Trehubov reported that Russian troops are regrouping and preparing for larger-scale offensive operations. The anticipated intensification may coincide with spring vegetation growth, which provides concealment for infiltration groups.

stories.title: Iranian naval commander Alireza Tangsiri killed in attack, Israel says
stories.summary: Israel's defence minister announced that Alireza Tangsiri, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy, was killed in an Israeli strike. Israel cited Tangsiri's role in blocking the Strait of Hormuz as justification for the attack.

stories.title: Prominent scholar Tariq Ramadan sentenced to 18 years for rape
stories.summary: Swiss scholar Tariq Ramadan, a former Oxford University lecturer, was sentenced in absentia to 18 years in prison for the sexual assault of three women. The sentencing took place in a French court.

stories.title: WTO members gather in Yaounde amid deep divisions and calls for reform
stories.summary: The World Trade Organization's 166 members convened a ministerial conference in Yaoundé, Cameroon, amid sharp divisions over institutional reform. Geopolitical tensions, rising protectionism, and the Middle East conflict overshadowed the trade discussions.

stories.title: SpaceX reportedly set to launch IPO valuing firm at $1.75 trillion
stories.summary: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, is reportedly preparing an IPO that would value the rocket and satellite internet company at approximately $1.75 trillion, seeking to raise $75 billion on public equity markets. The move comes as its subsidiary xAI continues to consume significant cash.

stories.title: Travelers flock to Clear security app to bypass TSA lines amid US airport chaos
stories.summary: Clear Secure, a biometric security company, has seen a surge in new sign-ups as travelers seek to bypass long TSA lines at more than 60 US airports. The increased demand comes amid a partial Department of Homeland Security shutdown that has left TSA workers unpaid.

stories.title: Nepal’s probe into deadly uprising finds ex-prime minister, officials ‘reckless’
stories.summary: A high-level probe in Nepal found former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli and senior officials criminally negligent over shootings during last year's youth uprising that killed 76 people. The committee, led by former judge Gauri Bahadur Karki, recommended investigation and prosecution of Oli and other officials.

stories.title: Taiwanese court jails former Taipei mayor Ko Wen-je for 17 years for corruption
stories.summary: A Taiwanese court sentenced former Taipei mayor Ko Wen-je to 17 years in prison for taking bribes and misusing political donations. Ko founded the Taiwan People's Party in 2019 and finished third in the 2024 presidential election. He did not plead guilty.

stories.title: UN adopts Ghana slavery resolution despite Israel, US opposition
stories.summary: UN adopts Ghana-led resolution recognising transatlantic slavery as a crime against humanity and calls for reparations despite US and EU opposition.
