stories.title: Zimbabwe says 15 nationals killed after being lured to fight for Russia
stories.summary: Zimbabwe confirmed that 15 of its nationals were killed after being recruited to fight for Russia under false pretenses. The Zimbabwean government said it is engaging Moscow to repatriate remains and bring surviving citizens home.

stories.title: Adopt a Bomb Shelter. Give Israelis a Safer Passover. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jewish Joint Distribution Committee is soliciting donations to equip bomb shelters in Israel with Wi-Fi and resilience kits ahead of Passover, aimed at communities facing ongoing attacks.

stories.title: Russia's largest oil refineries in Leningrad region under drone attack
stories.summary: The Kirishinefteorgsintez (KINEF) oil refinery in Kirishi, Leningrad region, was attacked by drones. KINEF is one of Russia's largest refining facilities.

stories.title: Anger mounts in northern communities as Netanyahu urges residents stay put
stories.summary: Municipal leaders in northern Israel have criticized the government's response to relentless Hezbollah rocket attacks that are driving residents to flee. Prime Minister Netanyahu has urged local officials to discourage outward migration from the affected communities.

stories.title: Israelis set to lose even more sleep as clocks to move forward for daylight saving
stories.summary: Israel is set to move clocks forward one hour for daylight saving time, with 2 a.m. becoming 3 a.m. in the early hours of Friday. Daylight saving time is scheduled to end on October 25.

stories.title: Co-op boss Shirine Khoury-Haq to step down after difficult year for group
stories.summary: Co-op Group chief executive Shirine Khoury-Haq will step down on 29 March following a year marked by a cyber-security attack that contributed to a £125 million loss and allegations of a toxic workplace culture. Board member Kate Allum will serve as interim CEO while a permanent successor is sought.

stories.title: Tamtam: The Saudi pop star nurturing Saudi Arabia's music scene
stories.summary: Saudi pop singer Tamtam discussed her music career, identity, and return to Riyadh in an interview, reflecting on feminism, diaspora experiences, and creative freedom in Saudi Arabia's growing music scene.

stories.title: Video: Storms wash away vehicles and flood homes across Middle East
stories.summary: Severe storms swept across parts of the Middle East, washing away vehicles in Oman and flooding homes in Syria. The extreme weather caused widespread disruption across the region.

stories.title: Yale report ties Russian energy giants to kidnapping and military training of Ukrainian children
stories.summary: A Yale School of Public Health Humanitarian Research Lab report found that Russian energy companies Gazprom and Rosneft transported and indoctrinated at least 2,158 Ukrainian children at camps in Russia and occupied territories between 2022 and 2025.

stories.title: Pakistan says it is relaying messages between US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar confirmed that Islamabad is relaying messages between the United States and Iran as part of indirect mediation efforts. Dar said Washington has presented 15 points that Iran is currently reviewing, with Turkey and Egypt also supporting the initiative.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Grants Speedy Hearing As Terror Suspects Admit Spying On U.S., Israeli Embassies
stories.summary: A Federal High Court in Abuja, Nigeria, granted an accelerated hearing in the trial of three terror suspects. The accused are charged with spying on U.S. and Israeli embassies in Nigeria on behalf of individuals linked to Iran.

stories.title: Niger: Boa Niger Suspends Dividend After Profit Collapse in 2025
stories.summary: Bank of Africa Niger (BOAN) announced it will not pay a dividend for the 2025 financial year following a sharp decline in earnings. The decision breaks several years of regular dividend distributions by the bank.

stories.title: Oil prices could hit $120 as war risks escalate, analyst warns
stories.summary: An analyst has warned that oil prices could reach $120 per barrel as risks from the ongoing Middle East conflict escalate. Prices are expected to remain elevated amid continued uncertainty over supply disruptions.

stories.title: 9 injured as Iran fires 6 missile salvos at Israel within hours, many with cluster warheads
stories.summary: Iran launched six missile salvos at Israel within a 24-hour period, some carrying cluster warheads, injuring at least nine people. Two people were killed by an intercepted missile in Abu Dhabi, and the Israeli Air Force conducted extensive retaliatory strikes on Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump lashes out at Nato, says it has done ‘nothing’ on Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized NATO allies on Truth Social, accusing them of doing "absolutely nothing" to assist with the situation involving Iran. He stated that the US needs nothing from the alliance.

stories.title: VW pulls Skoda brand from China after years of falling sales
stories.summary: Volkswagen announced it will withdraw its Skoda brand from mainland China following years of declining sales. The Czech automaker is realigning its global strategy to focus on growth markets including India and the ASEAN region, as international car brands continue losing ground in China's automotive market.

stories.title: Moldova court cases reveal Russia’s transnational network to recruit, train and deploy spies and saboteurs
stories.summary: Moldovan court cases have revealed a Russian-linked transnational network that recruited Moldovan citizens for drone training camps in the Balkans. The same recruiter also organized the painting of Stars of David on buildings in Paris following the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks.

stories.title: Four injured in Tel Aviv by missile debris
stories.summary: Four people were wounded in Tel Aviv after shrapnel from an Iranian missile fell across the city, landing in at least six locations. Israeli media reported injuries and property damage from the debris.

stories.title: Italy's Meloni says to boost cooperation with Algeria on gas deliveries
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni visited Algeria on Wednesday and announced plans to boost cooperation on gas deliveries to Italy. Meloni and Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune agreed to collaborate on projects including shale gas extraction and offshore exploration.

stories.title: Dozens dead in Bangladesh as passenger bus plunges into Padma River
stories.summary: A passenger bus carrying approximately 40 people plunged into the Padma River in Bangladesh while attempting to board a ferry. Dozens were killed, including children.

stories.title: Two drone strikes on civilian targets kill 28 people in Sudan
stories.summary: At least 28 civilians were killed in two drone strikes in Sudan as the civil war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces nears its fourth year. One strike hit a market in Saraf Omra, North Darfur, killing 22 people including an infant, while another struck a truck carrying civilians in North Kordofan.

stories.title: France pays national tribute to former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin
stories.summary: France held a national tribute on Thursday for former Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who died on Sunday. President Emmanuel Macron led the ceremony honoring Jospin, who headed the "plural left" coalition government from 1997 to 2002.

stories.title: Israel, US diverging timelines on possible negotiation for end of war
stories.summary: A US plan to end the Middle East war was conveyed to Tehran through Pakistani mediators, but Iran rejected the proposal and put forward its own conditions. Despite these indirect diplomatic exchanges, Israel has continued large-scale military strikes against Iran.

stories.title: Colombia Hercules crash aftermath: political clash over causes intensifies days after tragedy
stories.summary: The crash of a Hercules C-130 military aircraft in Putumayo, Colombia, on March 23 killed 70 people and has triggered a political confrontation between President Gustavo Petro, military leadership, and the opposition. The dispute centers on the causes of the disaster and the state of Colombia's defence capabilities ahead of May 31 presidential elections.

stories.title: Hungary moves to restrict gas supplies to Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungary has banned its gas transmission system operator from holding auctions for shipments to Ukraine in the third quarter, moving to wind down gas supplies. Hungary and Slovakia blame Kyiv for an outage on the Druzhba pipeline that carries Russian crude through Ukraine to their refineries.

stories.title: ‘Missile hit’ flips car in Israel
stories.summary: Surveillance footage from central Israel captured a car being flipped over by debris from an incoming rocket or missile strike. The incident highlighted the ongoing threat from projectile attacks on Israeli territory.

stories.title: WHO alarmed by health turmoil in Cuba
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Wednesday that Cuba's health situation is "deeply concerning" as a US fuel blockade worsens the island's energy crisis. He called for health to be protected from geopolitics, energy blockades, and power outages.

stories.title: South Africa: Mantashe Tells South Africans Not to Panic Over Fuel Shortages
stories.summary: South African Mineral Resources and Energy Minister Gwede Mantashe urged citizens not to panic over fuel shortages linked to the US-Israel-Iran war. Petrol and diesel prices are expected to rise sharply on April 1, with diesel set to increase by R9.50 per litre.

stories.title: Five weapons, 57 days: how Budapest escalated against Ukraine after one Russian drone strike
stories.summary: Tensions between Budapest and Kyiv escalated over 57 days following a Russian drone strike, with Hungary deploying five diplomatic or economic measures against Ukraine. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry noted that Hungarian gas imports have not stopped and that Kyiv has contingency plans prepared.

stories.title: UN adopts Ghana's slavery resolution, defying resistance from US, Israel
stories.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted a Ghana-proposed resolution recognizing transatlantic slavery as the "gravest crime against humanity" and calling for reparations. The non-binding resolution passed with 123 votes in favor, three opposed—including the US and Israel—and 52 abstentions, including EU members and Britain.

stories.title: Europe can’t rely on US for air-defense missiles, top EU official says
stories.summary: A top EU official, Kubilius, is conducting a "missile tour" across Europe to discuss air-defense missile production with manufacturers. The effort underscores concerns that Europe cannot rely on the United States for air-defense missile supplies and that the European Commission must support domestic production.

stories.title: Israeli judge closes case of Palestinian teen's death in prison
stories.summary: An Israeli judge closed the investigation into the death of a Palestinian teenager in Israeli prison, despite evidence suggesting starvation and an unclear cause of death. The decision has raised concerns about the treatment of Palestinian detainees.

stories.title: Strike kills IRGC Navy chief Tangsiri in Strait of Hormuz, Israeli official tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli sources confirmed the IDF carried out a strike that killed IRGC Navy commander Alireza Tangsiri in the Strait of Hormuz. Several of Tangsiri's top naval aides were also reported killed in the same attack.

stories.title: Residents injured after blast in Israeli home amid new Iranian barrage
stories.summary: Five people were injured after a blast struck a residential area in Kafr Qasim, central Israel, during a new Iranian missile and projectile barrage. Medics responded to the scene as fears of further Iranian strikes intensified.

stories.title: Ex-Taiwan presidential hopeful sentenced to 17 years for corruption
stories.summary: Former Taiwan presidential candidate Ko Wen-je was sentenced to 17 years in prison on corruption charges. His supporters had previously described the prosecution as politically motivated.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's Broadband Demand May Spike By 2030
stories.summary: Nigeria's broadband demand is projected to grow significantly as the country's population is expected to reach 245 million by 2030. The forecast highlights increasing pressure on the country's telecommunications infrastructure.

stories.title: Australian growth forecasts slashed as global economy faces inflation spike
stories.summary: The OECD warned that the US-Israel war on Iran threatens a major global inflationary spike as soaring fuel prices endanger growth in European and Asian nations. Australian growth forecasts have been slashed, with economists expecting higher interest rates and inflation driven by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: OECD cuts eurozone growth outlook as war drives inflation
stories.summary: The OECD downgraded its eurozone growth forecast by 0.4 percentage points to 0.8 percent, citing rising energy prices and inflation driven by the Middle East war. Growth projections for Germany and France were each cut by 0.2 points.

stories.title: US links security guarantees to Ukraine giving up Donbas, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a Reuters interview that the United States is conditioning security guarantees on Ukraine relinquishing all of Donbas. The disclosure highlights a key point of contention in ongoing negotiations over Ukraine's future security framework.

stories.title: Middle East conflict will damage UK’s economy ‘more than any other’
stories.summary: The OECD warned that the Middle East conflict will hurt the UK economy more than any other industrialised nation, cutting its 2026 growth forecast from 1.2% to 0.7%. The organisation also cautioned about rising inflation linked to the regional instability.

stories.title: What can the Iran war tell China about missile interception?
stories.summary: A Chinese military magazine urged Beijing to develop an air-based missile interceptor system, citing lessons from the Iran war. The analysis highlighted how Iran's ballistic missiles posed severe challenges to Israel's existing midcourse and terminal-phase missile defence systems.

stories.title: Once a poor village boy, famous China educational guru Zhang Xuefeng dies at 41 after a run
stories.summary: Zhang Xuefeng, a prominent Chinese education influencer with over 30 million online followers, died on March 24 at age 41 after suffering cardiac arrest following a run. CCTV News reported he felt unwell after exercising and was rushed to the hospital, where doctors were unable to revive him.

stories.title: Help us reach our goal of 4,500 Seder boxes for Tel Aviv-Yafo families in need - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jaffa Institute is seeking support to provide 4,500 Seder boxes to underprivileged families in Tel Aviv-Yafo ahead of Passover.

stories.title: Bangladesh recovers 24 bodies after bus plunges into river
stories.summary: Rescue teams including navy divers recovered 24 bodies, including five children, from a bus that plunged into the Padma River at Goalanda, Bangladesh, about 65 km west of Dhaka. The bus sank on Wednesday with approximately 50 passengers on board; many managed to escape.

stories.title: Israel hinders repair of damaged water infra deepening Gaza’s health crisis
stories.summary: Palestinian engineers in Gaza are struggling to repair water infrastructure damaged by Israeli military operations. Contamination of the water system is deepening the health crisis facing Gaza's population.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso Leads the Way in Culturally Inspired Ai
stories.summary: Burkina Faso is integrating local languages into its artificial intelligence development as part of a push for digital sovereignty. The initiative positions the country as a leader in culturally inspired AI on the continent.

stories.title: Nigeria: Maiduguri Bombings Show New Threat to Civilians
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch called on Nigerian authorities to ensure civilian protection and investigate bombings in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno state. The attacks highlighted a new threat to civilians in the region.

stories.title: Amid US-Israel war, Iran football team trains in Turkiye before World Cup
stories.summary: Iran's national football team has traveled to Turkey for training and two friendly matches ahead of the FIFA World Cup, scheduled to be held in the US, Canada, and Mexico.

stories.title: ECOWAS appoints veteran diplomat to mediate with Sahel States
stories.summary: ECOWAS appointed former Guinean Prime Minister Lansana Kouyaté to mediate with Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso. The three Sahel states withdrew from the regional bloc last year, and Kouyaté is tasked with re-establishing dialogue.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in gunfight with Hezbollah terrorists in southern Lebanon, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that 21-year-old Staff Sergeant Ori Greenberg of the Golani Brigade was killed in a gunfight with Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon. Another Israeli soldier was injured in the same engagement.

stories.title: Drone hits Russian oil tanker in Black Sea near Turkey
stories.summary: A drone struck a Russian oil tanker carrying crude in the Black Sea near the Bosphorus strait close to Turkey. The crew was reported safe after the explosion damaged the vessel, amid rising tensions in the region.

stories.title: Ex-NSA leaders say Americans are becoming ‘numb’ to cyber threats
stories.summary: Former National Security Agency leaders warned that Americans are becoming desensitized to cybersecurity threats. One former NSA director said that serious cyberattacks have not prompted sufficiently strong policy responses or public awareness.

stories.title: Cathay to increase fuel surcharge for all flights by 34% from April
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways announced a 34 per cent increase in fuel surcharges for all flights starting in April, its second increase in two weeks. The airline cited rising jet fuel prices driven by the Middle East war, noting its fuel hedging measures were insufficient to offset costs.

stories.title: How much junk is in South China Sea? Beijing flexes surveillance muscle with survey
stories.summary: A Chinese survey estimated approximately 93 million pieces of debris are floating on the surface of the South China Sea. Using fixed-ship monitoring, underway surveys, and satellite remote sensing, marine scientists audited 26 locations in the central and southern portions of the disputed waters.

stories.title: Gaza: Strike near Deir al‑Balāḥ tents kills at least one
stories.summary: An airstrike near tents in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, killed at least one person. Video from the scene showed an explosion triggering a fire as residents and medics rushed to assist the wounded.

stories.title: Turkey-operated tanker carrying Russian oil struck by naval drone in Black Sea
stories.summary: A crude oil tanker traveling from Russia's Novorossiysk port to Istanbul was struck by a naval drone near the Bosphorus strait on Thursday morning, according to Turkish Transportation Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu. The attack targeted the ship's engine room, but no injuries were reported.

stories.title: Pakistan steps in as Iran mediator while India watches from the wings
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a backchannel mediator between Tehran and Washington as the Iran war reshapes West Asian geopolitics. India, despite growing partnerships with the US, Israel, and Gulf states, has been absent from meaningful conflict-resolution efforts regarding Iran.

stories.title: Iran says 87,000 civilian sites damaged in war
stories.summary: Iran's Red Crescent reported that more than 87,000 non-military sites have been damaged or destroyed across the country since the start of Israeli-US strikes. The organization described widespread harm to civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: China’s lidar giants pivot to robotics as Jensen Huang praises Chinese supply chain
stories.summary: Chinese lidar sensor manufacturers Hesai Group and RoboSense Technology are expanding into robotics products. Shanghai-based Hesai plans to invest 200 million yuan this year to design and manufacture sensor and actuator components for robots, seeking new growth as China strengthens its global robotics supply chain.

stories.title: Israel medics say Iranian missile attack leaves six wounded
stories.summary: Iranian missile attacks on Israel wounded six people and caused damage to homes, according to Israeli medics. Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon has also escalated, with one Israeli soldier killed.

stories.title: Cuban president says Raul Castro involved in US talks amid oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel stated that former leader Raúl Castro is involved in ongoing talks with the United States. The discussions come amid rising tensions, including a US oil blockade and remarks by President Trump about taking over Cuba.

stories.title: New India bill to amend transgender rights sparks protests
stories.summary: India's government has introduced a bill that would amend the existing Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, altering how transgender individuals are legally recognised and their right to self-identify, prompting public protests.

stories.title: Singapore leader sees China helping small groups realise big results for Asia
stories.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said at the Boao Forum for Asia that China could lead plurilateral cooperation among smaller groups of like-minded Asian countries. He also suggested Beijing could spearhead AI governance efforts and play a larger role in promoting regional economic prosperity.

stories.title: Trump sets new China visit date as Iran war stokes economic risks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced he would visit China on May 14–15 for a meeting with President Xi Jinping, after delaying the trip by about six weeks due to the Iran war. The revised schedule is one day shorter than the originally planned three-day visit starting March 31.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Joins Ghana, 121 Others Urging Reparations for Slavery's Historical Wrongs
stories.summary: Nigeria joined Ghana and 121 other UN member states in adopting a resolution declaring the transatlantic slave trade the gravest crime against humanity. The resolution calls for reparations for slavery's historical wrongs.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda to Withdraw Troops From Some Positions in Eastern DR Congo, Says Gen Muhoozi
stories.summary: Uganda announced plans to withdraw some of its troops deployed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Chief of Defence Forces General Muhoozi Kainerugaba confirmed the planned partial drawdown.

stories.title: ‘He will call me Mama’: The Gaza ‘grandmother’ raising an orphaned baby
stories.summary: A woman named Maha in Gaza adopted an infant named Hamza after an Israeli air strike killed his parents on the day he was born. She had previously been known as 'Grandmother' within her family.

stories.title: G7 meets in France to narrow transatlantic Iran split
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers convened near Paris to discuss Middle East tensions, the Ukraine war, and other global crises. The meeting aimed to bridge differences between European allies and the United States on Iran policy.

stories.title: Helium hitch: Why US-Israel war on Iran could cause MRI scan delays
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran is disrupting global helium supplies, which could lead to delays in MRI scans and affect other medical and industrial applications that depend on the gas.

stories.title: US embassy urges citizens to leave Iraq over attacks
stories.summary: The US embassy in Iraq issued a security alert warning of escalating attacks by Iran-aligned armed groups targeting American citizens and interests. The embassy urged US nationals to leave Iraq immediately, recommending overland travel via Jordan.

stories.title: One house, two faiths, one fasting season
stories.summary: In Nigeria, couples like Olanrewaju and Kaosara are observing Ramadan and Lent together as the two fasting periods overlap for the first time since 1993.

stories.title: Inside Ethiopia's 'smart' police station
stories.summary: Ethiopia unveiled its first unmanned "smart" police station, where citizens can report crimes using automated touch screens without the need for in-person officer interaction.

stories.title: El-Sisi says Egypt in ‘state of near-emergency’ as war threatens economy
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi declared on Thursday that Egypt is in an economic "state of near-emergency" due to the Middle East war. He warned of runaway inflation, noting that the conflict has paralyzed trade through the Strait of Hormuz and affected Egypt's Gulf allies.

stories.title: How Israel’s ‘buffer zone’ plan could redraw the map of southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel announced a ground incursion into southern Lebanon with the aim of establishing a permanent "security zone" along the border. The operation was triggered after Hezbollah launched attacks on Israeli forces from positions south and north of the Litani River, prompting renewed Israeli air and ground campaigns.

stories.title: Israel decided to kill Khamenei in November, defense minister says
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz revealed that Israel decided in November to assassinate Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and planned to carry out the operation roughly six months later. Khamenei was killed in the opening hours of the US-Israeli air campaign that began on Saturday.

stories.title: Macron calls on Israel, Iran and Hezbollah to prevent Lebanon being embroiled in conflict
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron called on Israel, Iran, and Hezbollah not to embroil Lebanon in the wider Middle East conflict. He proposed a plan to end hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah, including military aid to the Lebanese army, as Israel ordered evacuations in Beirut's southern suburbs and the Bekaa region.

stories.title: Trump fires homeland security chief Kristi Noem
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump fired Kristi Noem as Secretary of Homeland Security after she testified that he had approved a $220 million DHS advertising campaign featuring herself. Trump announced that Republican Senator Markwayne Mullen of Oklahoma would replace Noem effective March 31.

stories.title: Jordan’s king condemns Iranian attacks in region during talks with Syrian president
stories.summary: King Abdullah of Jordan and Syrian President Ahmad Al-Sharaa discussed the regional crisis following US and Israeli strikes against Iran in a telephone call on Thursday. Both leaders emphasized the need for dialogue to prevent further escalation.

stories.title: Europol warns Iran crisis raises threat of terror, extremism and cyberattacks
stories.summary: Europol warned that the Middle East conflict will have immediate repercussions for EU security, including increased risks of terrorism, violent extremism, and cyberattacks. Spokesperson Jan Op Gen Oorth said the agency expects more cyberattacks on European infrastructure and a rise in AI-driven online fraud exploiting the conflict.

stories.title: Swedish intelligence warns of increased Middle East war fallout
stories.summary: Sweden's security service warned of increased threats against American and Israeli interests, as well as Iranian dissidents, in Sweden due to the Middle East war. Sapo operations chief Fredrik Hallstrom said the country's security situation, already strained by Russia's invasion of Ukraine, has worsened since US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Kane to miss Bayern game against Gladbach with calf knock
stories.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane will miss the Bundesliga match against Borussia Moenchengladbach due to a calf injury. Coach Vincent Kompany said Kane is expected to recover in time for the Champions League last-16 first leg at Atalanta next Tuesday.

stories.title: PSG prepare for Chelsea clash with Monaco rematch
stories.summary: Paris Saint-Germain face Monaco on Friday as preparation for their upcoming Champions League last-16 clash against Chelsea. Coach Luis Enrique expressed enthusiasm for the next phase of the season as PSG remain in contention to retain both their French and European titles.

stories.title: At the scene: Muslims killed 'over rejection of extremist ideology' in Nigeria
stories.summary: At least 78 people were buried and more than 170 are feared killed in attacks targeting Muslims in Nigeria. The victims were reportedly killed over their rejection of extremist ideology.

stories.title: From the front lines to the future: Israeli society and the Jewish people in 2036
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Conference, IDF veterans and civil-society leaders discussed service, dignity, and Diaspora responsibility as key pillars for Israel's future through 2036.

stories.title: How TALMA turns English education into social mobility and a Zionist mission
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Conference, TALMA CEO Ido Mahatzri presented the organization's work using English education to promote social mobility in Israel's peripheral communities.

stories.title: 'Over 90% of Iranians hate the regime,' INSS’s Beni Sabti reveals from leaked Iran survey
stories.summary: A leaked survey discussed by INSS researcher Beni Sabti indicates that approximately 92% of Iranians oppose their regime. Sabti described it as a secret poll, with findings shared at a Jerusalem Post event.

stories.title: Alshareef: Israel, Jews, should help Iranians seek liberty to ‘repay debt to Cyrus’
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Summit, speaker Alshareef called on Israel and the Jewish people to support Iranians seeking freedom, framing it as repaying a historical debt to the ancient Persian king Cyrus. Prime Minister Netanyahu also voiced solidarity with Iranian protesters.

stories.title: Watch: The Jerusalem Post Miami Summit
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post Miami Summit served as a platform for discussions on geopolitics and Diaspora-Israel relations, featuring speakers addressing a range of global and regional issues.

stories.title: The gifts I have been given: Survival as a collective act in Sudan
stories.summary: The article discusses survival as a collective act in Sudan, focusing on mutual aid and community resilience amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Hope and resistance: Slam poets capture the weight of war in DR Congo
stories.summary: Slam poets in the Democratic Republic of Congo are using their art to capture the weight of war, expressing themes of hope and resistance amid the country's ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Beware the AI efficiency messiah
stories.summary: The article examines concerns about over-reliance on artificial intelligence as a solution for efficiency, cautioning against uncritical adoption of AI-driven approaches.

stories.title: Israeli bombing exposes critical shortages in Iran’s healthcare system
stories.summary: Israeli bombing campaigns have exposed critical shortages in Iran's healthcare system, highlighting the strain on medical infrastructure and supply chains during the conflict.

stories.title: Myanmar in-depth: Slow earthquake response underlines need to overhaul long-flawed international aid efforts
stories.summary: The article examines how the slow international response to Myanmar's earthquake underscored longstanding flaws in global humanitarian aid delivery and the need for systemic reform.

stories.title: As Sudan army gains drive mass returns, mutual aid groups begin to rebuild
stories.summary: Sudanese army territorial gains are driving mass civilian returns to recaptured areas, where mutual aid groups have begun rebuilding communities and providing essential services.
